data.title: Kerron Stark
data.text:
Kerron Stark is an actor, television producer, teaching artist, musician, and author based in Omaha, Nebraska. He is the creator and host of Mister K's Clubhouse, a live-action educational children's television series that premiered in 2021. [ref: Omaha’s Kerron Stark may be the new face of educational children’s TV, The Reader] [ref: Mister K's Clubhouse aims to be a place of 'love, learning and imagination' for kids, KMTV 3 News Now] [ref: Omaha Wolf Trap Teaching Artists, Omaha Performing Arts]

== Background ==
Stark attended Omaha South High School, where he participated in theater and film productions. After graduating, he moved to Los Angeles to pursue acting. He later returned to Omaha and performed with local theater companies, including Radio Theatre Omaha, Blue Barn Theatre, Chanticleer, and SNAP! Productions.

== Career ==

=== Mister K's Clubhouse ===
Stark conceived the idea for his own children's television program in 2018. Mister K's Clubhouse debuted in 2021, with early episodes recorded in his basement. Production subsequently moved to KPAO, a public-access television station in Omaha.

Stark hosts the series as Mister K. The program uses songs, puppetry, dancing, and stories to introduce educational topics to young children. It features local children, puppets, and adult supporting characters, with episodes addressing themes such as feelings and friendship. Stark has cited children's programs including Mister Rogers' Neighborhood, Sesame Street, and Barney & Friends as influences on his work.

Stark personally financed the production of the pilot. In 2021, he received a Black American Artist Support Grant from Amplify Arts. The grant helped fund production of the series' first season. [ref: 2021 Annual Report, Amplify Arts] Amplify Arts' annual report also documented his performance of Mister K's Clubhouse LIVE! at Joslyn Art Museum. Stark also established the nonprofit organization Dreams V Reality.

In 2024, Stark presented Mister K's Toy Chest of Dreams, an interactive stage production based on the series, at Benson Theatre in Omaha.

=== Theater and arts education ===
Stark appeared in Witness for the Prosecution with Chanticleer Theater. His other theater credits include A Very Die Hard Christmas with Blue Barn Theatre and The Last Supper with SNAP! Productions. He has also worked with the touring theater organization RESPECT.

With Radio Theatre Omaha, Stark played Brad Wormrun in The Grinch Who Came to Dinner and Louis Wilkinson in Shadow Point in 2019. In 2020, he played Payload in the company's production of Atlas Slugged. [ref: Past Productions, Radio Theatre Omaha]

Stark has worked as a teaching artist providing social and emotional learning lessons in middle schools, as well as elementary schools. Omaha Performing Arts lists him among its Omaha Wolf Trap teaching artists. He has also served as a teaching artist for the organization's Disney Musicals in Schools program. [ref: Disney Musicals in Schools Teaching Artists, Omaha Performing Arts]

=== Writing ===
Stark is the author of the children's book Being Different Is Simply Amazing, illustrated by Marcus Murray. The educational organization RESPECT includes the book in its RESPECT Reads collection of recorded readings for teachers and parents. [ref: RESPECT Reads, RESPECT]

Stark co-wrote Carey the Car with Jenn Pollard, with illustrations by ARTPORTRA. A dramatized reading appeared on Mister K's Storybook Station in February 2024. [ref: Mister K's Storybook Station, Apple Podcasts] He also co-wrote The Adventures of Captain Epic with Mark Terrett, with illustrations by Tracie Mauk.

In 2022, Concordia University, Nebraska named Stark among the authors and illustrators scheduled to appear at its 26th annual Plum Creek Literacy Festival. [ref: Concordia University, Nebraska to host 26th annual Plum Creek Literacy Festival, Concordia University, Nebraska]

=== Music and audio productions ===
Stark began writing music during his senior year of high school. In a 2025 interview with The Reader, he described spending approximately ten years singing, rapping, songwriting, and performing before creating Mister K's Clubhouse.

Stark hosts Mister K's Storybook Station, a podcast featuring dramatized readings of children's stories. Its earliest listed episode was released in December 2023. In March 2024, author and former Romper Room presenter Karen Robbins joined him for a reading of her book I Think I Can.

He is also the creator of Do With That What You Will, a podcast whose introductory episode was released in December 2025. [ref: Do With That What You Will, Apple Podcasts]

== Barney fandom ==
Stark is an administrator and founding member of Barney History Fans, an online community focused on the children's television franchise. In a 2025 interview with The Pop Insider, he discussed his involvement in the community and his collection of Barney memorabilia. [ref: Barney's Tee-rific Comeback, The Pop Insider] The group was highlighted in the Peacock documentary I Love You, You Hate Me.

Stark hosts the Barney History Fans podcast Spots of Love!, which features interviews with fans and people involved in the franchise's production. Guests have included original Barney body performer David Voss, designer Jamie Ruth Connor, director and camera operator Dwin Towell, and assistant director Larry Baker. [ref: Spots of Love!, Apple Podcasts] Other guests have included director Fred Holmes, writer Stephen White, and music director Bob Singleton.

In December 2024, Stark appeared as an interviewee in "Kid Bopz" and "Purple-Colored Glasses", two episodes of Connecticut Public's documentary podcast Generation: Barney. [ref: Generation: Barney: Kid Bopz, Connecticut Public] [ref: Generation: Barney: Purple-Colored Glasses, Connecticut Public]

== Community work ==
In 2023, Stark served as a mentor for UNeTech Institute's Opportunity Corps: Bell-Jewell program, which supports Black and African American entrepreneurs. [ref: Bell-Jewell 2023, UNeTech Institute]

== Awards and nominations ==
For the 19th Omaha Entertainment & Arts Awards, held in 2025, Stark received nominations for Outstanding Director, Musical and Outstanding Actor, Musical for Mister K's Toy Chest of Dreams at Benson Theatre. The production, written by Stark, was also nominated for Outstanding Premiere of a New, Original, Local Script. [ref: Announcing nominees to the 19th Omaha Entertainment & Arts Awards, Omaha Entertainment & Arts Awards]

data.title: Felicia Arigo
data.text:
Felicia Arigo (born 13 March 1969) is a Nigerian entrepreneur, humanitarian, and retired civil servant. She is the President and Founder of the BLESSED2BLESS GLOBAL EMPOWERMENT FOUNDATION (B2BG) and was profiled in the book 100 Audacious Nigerian Women.

== Early life ==
Arigo was born on 13 March 1969 in Ibedeni, Ndokwa East Local Government Area, Delta State, Nigeria. She is based in Lagos, Nigeria.

== Education ==
* M.Sc. Information Technology – National Open University of Nigeria, Naval Base, Apapa (2016)
* B.Sc. Data Management (Second Class Lower) – National Open University of Nigeria (2006–2012)
* Advanced Diploma and Diploma in Computing – University of Lagos (1994–1997)

== Career ==
Arigo served as a civil servant with the Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS), Nigeria from 1991 to 2026, and is now retired.

She is also a business owner:
* CEO, D'FOCUS WORLDWIDE COMPANY LTD.
* CEO, OKERICHA FARMS
* CEO, DESTINED FARMERS MULTIPURPOSE COOPERATIVE SOCIETY LIMITED

== Humanitarian work ==
Arigo is the President and Founder of BLESSED2BLESS GLOBAL EMPOWERMENT FOUNDATION (B2BG), a non-governmental organization focused on empowerment.

== Professional memberships and certifications ==
* Fellow, Institute of Management Consultants (FIMC) and Chartered Management Consultant (CMC) – 2019, upgraded 2021
* Chartered Institute of Management Consultants (ChMC)
* Member, Nigeria Institute of Management (MNIM 2020, AMNIM 2016)
* ITIL v3 Foundation, ACE, GMNCS
* Member, ISACA

== Honors and recognition ==
* Honorary Doctorate (D.Sc) in Leadership & Corporate Governance – European-American University (21 June 2021)
* United Nations Eminent Peace Ambassador and Global Diplomat – Inducted into UN Hall of Fame as Global Citizen (6 February 2021)
* African Leadership Award as "Beacon of Hope For African's Development" (23 September 2021)
* Climate Change Training & Certification (2024)
* United Nations Global SDGs Advocate Award for Community & Human Development (11 January 2025)
* Listed among Nigeria's 100 Audacious Women – Accolade Communications

== Titles ==
Pst., Amb. (Dr.), JP – Pastor, Ambassador, Doctor (Honorary), Justice of the Peace.

== References ==

[ref: Okojie, Luke. 100 Audacious Nigerian Women: A Compendium of Outstanding and Formidable 100 Nigerian Women. Accolade Communications, 2026. Profile: Amb. (Dr.) Felicia Arigo JP – President and Founder, BLESSED2BLESS GLOBAL EMPOWERMENT FOUNDATION (B2BG).]

data.title: Knifetwister records
data.text:
Knifetwister Records (stylized as knifetwister records) is an American independent record label and online music publication based in New York [ref: Pool Halls, Punk, and a Dog With a Grudge: Inside the World of Knifetwister Records with Raph Copeland, The MIC Magazine]. Founded by Raph Copeland in 2025, it focuses primarily on punk, hardcore, ska and metal, with an emphasis on independent and emerging artists. [ref: Single Use - Knifetwister Records, WRIR-LP 97.3 FM]

== History ==
Copeland established Knifetwister Records after previously working with musicians through music-video production and band management [ref: Punk Is Not Dead: How Knifetwister Records Is Keeping New York Loud, Mixed Alt Mag] [ref: Interview with Raph Copeland of knifetwister records, Racket Magazine]. The publication initially concentrated on the New York music scene before expanding its coverage beyond the region [ref: 2025 Recap, We Might Die]. Its interviews have included both established musicians and lesser-known independent acts [ref: Gallery 1, DOLL FEST], including interviews with War on Women, Dance Hall Crashers, 18fevers, Ryan Cassata and Angelo Moore of Fishbone. [ref: NY DIY Label Spotlight, In Effect Hardcore]

== Benefit compilations ==
The label's released the compilation Not in Our City in late 2025 [ref: Read a track-by-track breakdown for Knifetwister Records' new benefit comp, 'Not In Our City'!, www.punknews.org], which featured 21 bands with all proceeds toward The Bowery Mission, a New York City organization serving people experiencing homelessness. [ref: Knifetwister Records Compilation, coventrycarols.com] [ref: Current Reviews – In Effect Hardcore, ineffecthardcore.com] [ref: OfficialSoda - Releases, officialsoda.com]

A sequel, Not in Our City 2, followed in 2026 and benefited immigrant-rights organization Make the Road New York. [ref: Not in Our City 2 Charges for Compassion, In Spite Magazine] The compilation featured 22 bands from eight countries and included music spanning several punk subgenres. [ref: Music Review: Knifetwister Records' Not in Our City 2, A Punk Rock Compilation to Benefit Immigrant Rights, Rock DNA Magazine] [ref: Press - Saints of Lorain, saintsoflorain.com] [ref: Current Reviews – In Effect Hardcore, ineffecthardcore.com] [ref: Press, Skip The Needle]

A third compilation, Trans Riot!, to benefit the Transgender Law Center and Trans Closet Hudson Valley, is scheduled for release on November 20, 2026 [ref: ]

== Approach ==
Knifetwister's editorial coverage is centered largely on independent and underground music. [ref: Pool Halls, Punk, and a Dog With a Grudge: Inside the World of Knifetwister Records with Raph Copeland, THE MIC MG] [ref: knifetwister records’ Birthday Bash Show 7/26/2026!, Uncharted Music] Copeland has described providing exposure to smaller artists as one of the publication's primary goals and has stated that the magazine makes a particular effort to interview female-fronted and transgender bands.

data.title: Hüseyin Bulut
data.text:
Hüseyin Bulut (born 29 March 1999) is a Turkish professional footballer who plays as a right-back or winger for Süper Lig club Çorum. Born in Dortmund, Germany, he spent most of his youth career with Borussia Dortmund before beginning his senior career with Borussia Dortmund II. He has represented Turkey at under-16 and under-17 level. [ref: Hüseyin Bulut – Player Details, Turkish Football Federation]

==Club career==

===Borussia Dortmund===
Bulut was born in Dortmund, Germany, and played youth football for TuS Eving-Lindenhorst before joining the youth system of Borussia Dortmund in 2010. [ref: Hoş geldin Hüseyin Bulut, Altınordu F.K.]

He progressed through Borussia Dortmund's youth teams. His development was interrupted by a hip injury during the 2016–17 season, which caused him to miss much of the campaign. [ref: Hüseyin Bulut: Das türkische Talent in den Reihen von Borussia Dortmund, [[Goal (website)] He returned to feature in the final stages of Borussia Dortmund's German under-19 championship-winning campaign.

In September 2017, Bulut attracted attention after scoring twice for Borussia Dortmund's under-19 team in a 5–3 victory over Real Madrid in the UEFA Youth League. A profile published by Goal.com following the match examined his development at Dortmund, injury history, technical ability and positional versatility.

Bulut later progressed to Borussia Dortmund II. During the 2018–19 Regionalliga West season, he made nine league appearances and scored three goals. [ref: Huseyin Bulut – Player profile, German Football Association]

In 2019, Turkish sports outlet Ajansspor published a separate profile and analysis of Bulut, discussing his development at Borussia Dortmund, positional versatility and playing characteristics. [ref: Hüseyin Bulut Analizi, Ajansspor]

===Göztepe and return to Germany===
Bulut moved to Turkey in July 2019 and joined Göztepe. He did not make a league appearance for the club, but appeared twice in the Turkish Cup, scoring once. [ref: Gel de kahrolma!, Yeni Asır]

Yeni Asır reported in July 2020 that Bulut had struggled for first-team opportunities under managers Tamer Tuna and İlhan Palut and had requested permission to leave the club in order to continue his career in Germany. His contract with Göztepe was terminated by mutual consent on 14 July 2020.

He subsequently returned to Germany and joined Sportfreunde Lotte, making 11 Regionalliga West appearances and scoring once. In January 2021 he moved to Rot-Weiß Oberhausen, where he made 28 league appearances over two seasons and scored one goal.

Bulut joined Rot Weiss Ahlen for the 2022–23 season, scoring seven goals in 29 Regionalliga West appearances. The following season he played for Wuppertaler SV, recording four goals in 25 league appearances.

===Altınordu===
In May 2024, Bulut returned to Turkey and signed a three-year contract with Altınordu. He became one of the club's leading attacking players during the 2024–25 TFF Second League season.

By May 2025, Bulut had scored 13 goals during the regular league season. Demirören News Agency described him as Altınordu's leading scorer and reported that his goals had played an important role in the club qualifying for the promotion play-offs. [ref: Altınordu'nun kozu Hüseyin Bulut, Demirören News Agency]

He finished the campaign with 15 goals in 36 appearances across the league and promotion play-offs. [ref: Hüseyin Bulut, Maçkolik] In June 2025, DHA reported that his performances had attracted transfer interest and that Altınordu had placed a reported €600,000 valuation on him. [ref: Altınordu'da Hüseyin değerini katladı, Demirören News Agency]

===Keçiörengücü===
Bulut joined Keçiörengücü in September 2025. He made 29 appearances and scored four goals in the TFF First League during the 2025–26 season.

During his time with Keçiörengücü, he increasingly featured in a defensive role on the right side, having spent much of his earlier career in attacking wide positions.

===Çorum===
On 11 July 2026, newly promoted Süper Lig club Çorum signed Bulut from Keçiörengücü on a two-year contract with an option for a further season. [ref: Çorum FK, Hüseyin Bulut'u kadrosuna kattı, Demirören News Agency] The transfer was announced with Bulut described as a right-back.

His registration with Çorum took effect on 14 July 2026, with the Turkish Football Federation listing his contract as running until 30 June 2028.

==International career==
Bulut represented Turkey at youth international level. He made three appearances for the Turkey under-16 team in 2015. He scored for Turkey in a 3–1 defeat against Mexico at the Montaigu Tournament on 4 April 2015. [ref: U16 Milli Takımı, Meksika'ya 3-1 mağlup oldu, Turkish Football Federation]

Later that year, Bulut represented the Turkey under-17 team, making three appearances. He was part of the Turkey squad that competed at the St George's Park Tournament in England in August 2015. [ref: U17 Milli Takımı İtalya'ya 2-0 yenildi, Turkish Football Federation]

==Playing style==
During his youth career, Bulut was primarily used as an attacking player. In its 2017 profile, Goal.com described him as capable of playing on either wing or through the centre, highlighting his technical ability, dribbling, movement and work rate.

A 2019 analysis by Ajansspor also noted his ability to play in several attacking and midfield positions and emphasised his one-on-one ability, pace and dribbling. Later in his senior career he was also deployed as a right-back, the position in which he was described when he joined Çorum in 2026.

==References==

data.title: David Sinclair
data.text:
----

David Sinclair is an American professional athlete competing in Nordic skiing, ski mountaineering, and trail running.

Sinclair has represented Team USA in ski mountaineering (skimo) and trail running. [ref: David Sinclair, Team USA] [ref: Nordic Skiing, Ultrarunning Prepared David Sinclair To Take A Shot At A Lifelong Olympic Dream In Skimo, Team USA]

== Early life and career ==
Sinclair was on the skiing team at Dartmouth College, specializing in Nordic. [ref: Dartmouth Skiing, 2013-14 Skiing Roster] While at Dartmouth, running was primarily cross-training for ski racing. Despite this, he ran a 2:42 marathon as a college junior. [ref: David Sinclair, US Olympic Team Trials Athlete Bios]

Following college, Sinclair transitioned to elite trail running and ultramarathons. In 2018, he won the USATF 50-km Trail Championships. [ref: Vermonters Enman and Sinclair win rain-soaked Ragged 50K, Trail Running, Ultrarunning, USATF, USATF Championships] He has represented Team USA at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships in 2018, 2019, 2022 and 2025. [ref: Catching Up with David Sinclair About Trail Running and Ski Mountaineering, Trail Runner Magazine]

Despite primarily competing in trail running, Sinclair qualified for the 2020 US Olympic Marathon Trials with a time of 2:16:18 at the 2016 California International Marathon. [ref: David Sinclair, US Olympic Team Trials Athlete Bios]

He was rated Ultra Running Magazine's number 3 men's ultrarunner of 2024. [ref: David Sinclair Named #3 Ultrarunner of the Year, Ultrarunners of the Year]

In 2025, he joined the Craft Elite Run Team as a sponsored athlete. [ref: Craft Sportswear Welcomes New Trail Athletes to Its Elite Run Team, Outdoor Industry Association]

data.title: Will Markeith Green
data.text:
Will Green (born February 10, 1979) is an American entrepreneur and event promoter from Louisville, Kentucky. He founded Just Lit Candle Co., a scented candle business established in 2020, and created Trap-N-Candles, an event concept combining candle making with hip-hop and R&B music. Green has also participated in school supply fundraising in Louisville. [ref: Viral post sparks community effort to meet JCPS students' needs, The Courier-Journal]

== Early life ==

Green was born on February 10, 1979, in Louisville, Kentucky, where he grew up.Green was born on February 10, 1979, in Louisville, Kentucky, where he grew up. He later became involved in the local entertainment industry, working as an event promoter and planner.

== Career ==

=== Event promotion (2010–2020) ===

Green began working as an event promoter and planner in 2010. For approximately ten years, he organized and promoted parties, nightlife events, and other social gatherings.

In 2020, restrictions associated with the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States affected in-person entertainment events. During this period, Green began exploring other business opportunities.

=== Just Lit Candle Co. (2020–present) ===

In 2020, Green founded Just Lit Candle Co., a scented candle business based in Louisville, Kentucky. During the pandemic, he began learning to make candles through instructional videos on YouTube and experimented with ingredients and fragrances before starting the business.

Green used marketing methods from his work in event promotion. The company's advertising has incorporated humor, popular culture, and suggestive themes.

According to Green, the company generated approximately $50,000 in sales during its first year, with sales increasing in later years. These figures have not been independently verified.

The company's fragrances have included Grey Sweatpants, Sunday Morning Mimosas, and Mr Teakwood.

=== Trap-N-Candles (2023–present) ===

In 2023, Green created Trap-N-Candles, an event concept combining candle making with music and entertainment. The events include candle-making activities, hip-hop, R&B, live DJs, and a nightclub-style setting. Some events include alcoholic beverages.

The concept combines Green's event promotion work with his candle business.

== Community involvement ==

Green has participated in efforts to provide school supplies to children in Louisville. In September 2026, The Courier-Journal published an article discussing his involvement in backpack fundraising and distribution efforts for local students. The article reported that he had been involved in backpack fundraising for approximately ten years and helped collect more than 3,000 backpacks ahead of the school year.

data.title: Epistle Communications
data.text:
Epistle is an Indian public relations and communications consultancy headquartered in New Delhi, India. Founded in 2011 by architect Tanya Khanna, the firm specialises in strategic communications, brand development, and media relations for clients in the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry. It is recognised as South Asia's first and largest communications consultancy dedicated exclusively to the built environment sector. [ref: Alumni Q&As: Tanya Khanna is putting Indian design on the global map, UCL Bartlett Faculty of the Built Environment]

=== History ===

==== Founding ====
Epistle was founded in New Delhi in 2011 by Tanya Khanna, an architect trained at Sushant School of Art and Architecture and The Bartlett School of Architecture, University College London. Khanna established the firm with the aim of developing a professional communications infrastructure for architecture and design practices in India, a sector that lacked dedicated communications services at the time. [ref: The less-spoken field of architectural journalism, The Hindu]

==== Growth and expansion ====
From its founding as a sole proprietorship, Epistle expanded over the following decade into a multi-city operation. The firm grew to a team of over 80 professionals across six Indian cities. It has provided communications services to over 150 client organisations across the architecture, interior design, real estate, and design manufacturing sectors, with clients spanning twelve countries.

Epistle has been credited with pioneering the field of architectural communications in South Asia, developing editorial, public relations, content, and brand strategy services specifically for built environment practitioners.

=== Services ===
Epistle provides communications services exclusively to clients in the built environment sector. Its services include: [ref: ]

* Strategic communications: Development of communications strategies for architecture firms, design studios, real estate developers, and building product brands.
* Brand development: Positioning, identity, and messaging strategy for design practices and organisations.
* Media relations: Press outreach, project placement, and relationship management with architecture and design publications in India and internationally.
* Editorial services: Project documentation, architectural writing, award submissions, and content development.
* Digital communications: Online presence strategy, social media, and digital content for design practices.
* Education and training: The Epistle Academy offers structured training in design communication for architecture and design professionals. The Epistle Writing Prize is an open international competition for writing about architecture, design, and urbanism, which received 195 entries from 18 countries in its 2024 edition.

=== Leadership ===
Epistle is led by its founder, Tanya Khanna, who serves as Chief Executive Officer. The firm's senior leadership includes:

* Tanya Khanna — Founder and Chief Executive Officer
* Suneet Zishan Langar — Director, Editorial and Brand Strategy
* Mariyam Hassan — Director, Strategic Partnerships
* Sana Jhamb — Director, Public Relations

=== Recognition ===
Tanya Khanna and Epistle have received recognition from several industry organisations and publications:

* Khanna served as a juror for the Dezeen Awards in 2021. [ref: Tanya Khanna, Dezeen]
* Khanna served as a juror for the Frame Awards in 2022. [ref: The 15 design professionals leading May's Frame Awards jury, frameweb.com]
* Khanna was a speaker at NeoCon, Chicago, in June 2024. [ref: NeoCon Talks, NeoCon]
* Epistle and its work have been covered in The Hindu (February 2024) and the Journal of the Indian Institute of Architects (May–June 2023).

data.title: Louie Bradbury
data.text:
----

Louie Bradbury (born 16 September 2008) is a Welsh professional footballer who plays as a forward for the Under-18 squad of Premier League club Manchester United [ref: Louie Bradbury Player Profile - Men U18s, ManUtd.com] and represents the Wales national under-19 team internationally.

== Early life ==
Bradbury was born in Shrewsbury, England. He spent his early youth development within the academy structure at Shrewsbury Town, before transferring to the Manchester United Academy at Under-14 level in early 2023. [ref: Former Corwen junior signs for mighty Manchester United, North Wales Sport] [ref: Manchester United academy star Louie Bradbury continues impressive goalscoring form, Daily Mirror]

== Club career ==
=== Manchester United ===
After rising through the youth ranks at the Trafford Training Centre, Bradbury made his Under-18s debut for Manchester United on 17 January 2025, appearing as a late substitute in a FA Youth Cup tie against Preston North End. [ref: Louie Bradbury: The 17-year-old forward with Javier Hernandez-like instincts currently on fire for Man Utd U18s, United In Focus / Yahoo Sports] He scored his first goal at Under-18 level on 18 February 2025 during his first start against Wolverhampton Wanderers. In the summer of 2025, Bradbury signed a formal scholarship agreement with Manchester United. During the 2025–26 season, he integrated fully into the under-18 system under Darren Fletcher and made development appearances for the Under-21 side in Premier League 2. [ref: Everton 0 Under-18s 3 Match Report, ManUtd.com] Bradbury signed his first professional contract with Manchester United on 1 July 2026.

== International career ==
Bradbury is a youth international for Wales. [ref: Oswestry: Future football star Louie gets Wales call-up, Border Counties Advertizer] After representing the nation at Under-15, Under-16, Under-17 and Under-18 level, he was called up a year early to the Wales Under-19 squad for the 2026 UEFA European Under-19 Championship finals hosted in North Wales. [ref: Louie Bradbury relishing first Cymru U19 EURO call-up, FAW.cymru] He scored his first goal for the Under-19 team during international training camps in a fixture against Sweden in June 2026.

data.title: Emmanuel Magembe Silburn
data.text:
----

Emmanuel Magembe (born 25 December 1992) is a Ugandan former footballer who played as an attacking midfielder and winger. He is also known for his fox sprints and speed, free kick specialist and a dribbler. He was regarded as a highly talented attacking midfielder/winger, capable of playing centrally or on either flank. He developed through youth football in Uganda, including the Kampala Kids League, and later played for several Ugandan and European clubs. His senior career included spells with Victors FC, KJT, Vipers SC, KCCA FC, Proline FC, Franö FK and Ishavsbyen FK

== Early life and youth career ==
Emmanuel Magembe was born on 25 December 1992 in Kampala, Uganda. He began playing football at a young age in Mutundwe, in Rubaga South Division. He played football while attending primary school, where his ability in the sport helped him obtain a bursary to continue his education.

Magembe began his early academy football in Nalukolongo. He played for Super Cubs before moving to Young Express, also known as Wembley. He later joined the Kampala Kids League (KKL), where he developed as a youth footballer and gained opportunities to participate in international youth tournaments.Magembe later joined the Kampala Kids League (KKL), where he developed as a youth footballer and gained experience in international youth competitions. By 2007, he was listed among players produced by KKL, which had won tournaments including the Gothia and Tivoli Cups in Europe. [ref: https://www.newvision.co.ug/news/1518522/kkl-transformed-ugandan-football]

Magembe represented KKL in international youth competitions in Europe. He travelled with the team to tournaments in Denmark, England, Peru, Spain, Sweden and Norway and was among the players who gained international experience through KKL. [ref: KKL transformed Ugandan football, New Vision] [ref: KKL Tivoli Cup, New Vision] [ref: KKL roll on at Gothia Cup, New Vision]

In 2005, Magembe joined Old Kampala Senior Secondary School as a student and footballer. He initially developed with the school before progressing to the senior team. During this period, he continued to develop through school and youth football. [ref: Ali finds gift in unbreakable spirit, Daily Monitor] [ref: Magembe ready to revive career at Proline, Kawowo Sports] [ref: Old Kampala SSS are the U-16 Secondary School Champions, Uganda Radio Network]

Magembe later transferred from Old Kampala Senior Secondary School to St. Mary's Kitende, where he continued his education while playing football for the school team. In 2010, he was part of the St. Mary's Kitende team that travelled to Nakuru, Kenya, for the Federation of East Africa Secondary Schools Sports Association (FEASSA) competition, which Kitende won.

== Senior career ==
In 2011, Magembe joined Victors FC in the Uganda Premier League. He later moved to PDRM in Malaysia, where he played during the 2012–13 period. [ref: Express faces player exodus, New Vision] [ref: Hippos Prepare as Opponent Win 3-Nation tourney, Uganda Radio Network]

In 2012, Magembe was summoned to the Uganda Hippos under-21 team. He subsequently spent a period away from active football following a contractual dispute involving a football agent.In 2012, Magembe was summoned to the Uganda Hippos under-21 team. [ref: Afrikansk landslagsspiller klar for norsk 3.-divisjon, Aftenposten] [ref: 2012/13 Super League Club Preview: Vipers Sports Club, Kawowo Sports]

== International career ==
Magembe was involved with the Uganda under-21 national team. In 2012, he was listed among the players in the Uganda Hippos camp preparing for the African Youth Championship qualifying campaign. [ref: Hippos Prepare as Opponent Win 3-Nation tourney, Uganda Radio Network] In 2015, a Norwegian report stated that Magembe had made under-21 international appearances for Uganda and had played against Ghana. [ref: Afrikansk landslagsspiller klar for norsk 3.-divisjon, Aftenposten]

In 2014, Magembe joined Rwenshama/KJT, a club competing in the FUFA Big League. He was part of the team that earned promotion to the Uganda Premier League and contributed goals and assists during the campaign. [ref: KJT / Rwenshama dumps Mutundwe out, faces Jinja S.S / Kirinya, Kawowo Sports] [ref: Rwenshama Books Slot In FUFA Super League, ChimpReports]

Magembe later continued his career in Europe. He played for Franö FK in Sweden before moving to northern Norway, where he joined Ishavsbyen FK. During his time in Norway, he played under the name "Em" and scored goals for the club. [ref: Afrikansk landslagsspiller klar for norsk 3.-divisjon, iTromsø] [ref: Afrikansk landslagsspiller klar for norsk 3.-divisjon, iTromsø]

In 2016, Magembe joined KCCA FC under coach Mike Mutebi. He was part of the KCCA team that won the 2015–16 Uganda Premier League title. He later moved to Proline FC, but injuries, including knee and ankle problems, limited his ability to play.In 2016, Magembe joined KCCA FC and was part of the club's 2015–16 league-winning side. [ref: https://www.monitor.co.ug/uganda/magazines/score/kcca-triumph-amidst-mediocrity-1651940] He later joined Proline FC on a two-year deal. [ref: https://kawowo.com/2016/09/01/magembe-ready-to-revive-career-at-proline/] Magembe left Proline in 2017 after limited playing time, with injury contributing to his lack of game time. [ref: https://kawowo.com/2017/06/14/magembe-confirms-departure-proline/]

Magembe retired from active football in 2017. [ref: Magembe confirms departure from Proline, Kawowo Sports]

data.title: Hayden High School (Alabama)
data.text:
Hayden High School is a public secondary school located in Hayden, Alabama, United States. Operated by Blount County Schools, the school serves students in grades eight through twelve. The school offers academic instruction, extracurricular activities, and interscholastic athletics.

The school's mascot is the Wildcats, and its school colors are black and Vegas gold.

== History ==

=== Early schools ===

The history of public education in Hayden, Alabama, predates the development of the present high school. According to the Encyclopedia of Alabama, the community's earliest school was a one-room log building. As the population grew, the school was expanded to a two-room, two-story building and later a four-room facility. [ref: Hayden, Encyclopedia of Alabama]

The Town of Hayden's historical account describes the earliest schoolhouse as a crude log structure with a dirt floor. School was initially held during the summer, when children were less needed for agricultural work. Winter classes were introduced later, and a fireplace was added to provide heat. As demand for education increased, the community constructed larger school buildings. [ref: Town History, Town of Hayden]

Following the construction of a four-room schoolhouse after World War I, additional rooms were added as enrollment increased. In the early 1920s, a larger site was acquired across the railroad, and a twelve-grade school building was constructed. The development marked an important stage in the expansion of educational facilities in the Hayden community. [ref: Town History, Town of Hayden]

=== Twentieth-century campus ===

According to Hayden High School's official website, a school building occupied by the institution had been in use since 1937. The building remained in use for decades, during which the campus expanded to include portable classroom trailers. [ref: About Us, Hayden High School]

=== New campus ===

On March 31, 2003, students, teachers, and staff moved from the older campus into a newly constructed school facility. The move ended the school's use of the building that had been occupied since 1937 and replaced a campus that included portable classrooms. The school described the new facility as a modern educational complex. [ref: About Us, Hayden High School]

== Academics ==

Hayden High School provides secondary education for students in grades eight through twelve. Its academic program includes academic support services, career and technical education, dual enrollment opportunities, and graduation planning. [ref: Academics, Hayden High School]

The school's educational mission emphasizes preparing students to become responsible, productive, successful lifelong learners. The school describes its educational approach as emphasizing cooperation, commitment, academic development, and preparation for participation in the wider community. [ref: Home, Hayden High School]

=== Academic support ===

Academic support is one of the services identified in the school's academic program. The school maintains a dedicated section for academic support to provide information about assistance available to students. Further details about specific interventions and services require additional documentation. [ref: Academics, Hayden High School]

=== Career and technical education ===

Career and technical education is part of Hayden High School's academic offerings. These programs provide a pathway for students interested in career-oriented learning alongside their broader secondary education. The school maintains a dedicated career and technical education page for program information. [ref: Career and Technical Education, Hayden High School]

=== Dual enrollment ===

Hayden High School lists dual enrollment as an academic opportunity for its students. Dual enrollment programs generally allow eligible high school students to take approved postsecondary courses while completing their high school education. Participation requirements, available courses, and arrangements with postsecondary institutions may vary. [ref: Dual Enrollment, Hayden High School]

=== Graduation requirements ===

The school publishes information about graduation requirements to guide students in completing the academic credits and other requirements necessary to graduate. These requirements are subject to applicable Alabama education regulations and local school district policies. [ref: Graduation Requirements, Hayden High School]

== Extracurricular activities ==

Hayden High School offers extracurricular programs intended to provide students with opportunities for leadership, academic competition, music, and service outside the classroom. The school's official extracurricular directory lists the Ambassadors program, Key Club, National Beta Club, the Pride of Hayden Band, and Scholars Bowl. [ref: Extracurriculars, Hayden High School]

=== Student leadership and service ===

The school's Ambassadors program provides an extracurricular opportunity associated with student representation and leadership. Key Club is a student service organization that emphasizes community service and volunteerism. The school also lists the National Beta Club, an organization that promotes academic achievement, leadership, character, and service among students. [ref: Extracurriculars, Hayden High School]

=== Music ===

The Pride of Hayden Band is the school's band program. It provides students with opportunities to participate in instrumental music and school performances. The program is part of the school's extracurricular offerings and contributes to musical activities within the school community. [ref: Pride of Hayden Band, Hayden High School]

=== Academic competition ===

Hayden High School lists Scholars Bowl among its extracurricular programs. Scholars Bowl is an academic competition in which students answer questions across a range of subject areas. Participation provides opportunities for students to demonstrate academic knowledge and work collaboratively in a competitive setting. [ref: Extracurriculars, Hayden High School]

== Athletics ==

Hayden High School competes in interscholastic athletics under the Wildcats name. The school's teams have competed in a range of sports, including football, basketball, baseball, softball, volleyball, track and field, and wrestling. The school uses black and Vegas gold as its athletic colors. [ref: Hayden Wildcats Sports History, Alabama High School Football and Sports History]

=== Football ===

The Hayden Wildcats football program dates to 1933, when the school fielded its first football team. The team temporarily ceased competing during the 1940s before returning to competition. [ref: Hayden Wildcats Football Team History, Alabama High School Football and Sports History]

In 1954, Hayden completed its first undefeated season. The team was recognized in contemporary newspaper-based championship listings, although this historical designation predates the modern Alabama High School Athletic Association playoff championship system. [ref: Hayden Wildcats Football Team History, Alabama High School Football and Sports History]

Hayden made its first football playoff appearance in 1975, the same year it won its first recorded region championship. The program subsequently won region championships in 1990, 1991, and 1992. [ref: Hayden Wildcats Football Team History, Alabama High School Football and Sports History]

The 1991 season marked the program's first playoff victory and its first season with at least ten wins. In 1992, Hayden recorded an 11-win season and completed a 10–0 regular season, establishing one of the strongest seasons in the program's documented history. [ref: Hayden Wildcats Football Team History, Alabama High School Football and Sports History]

=== Softball ===

Hayden's fast-pitch softball program has won three Alabama state championships in Class 5A, in 2013, 2019, and 2022, according to historical records of Alabama high school athletics. [ref: Hayden Wildcats Sports History, Alabama High School Football and Sports History]

These championships represent major achievements for the school's athletic program. Additional season-by-season records and contemporary reports would provide further detail about the teams' postseason runs and championship games.

=== Other sports ===

In addition to football and softball, Hayden fields teams in baseball, boys' and girls' basketball, volleyball, track and field, and wrestling, among other athletic activities. Historical databases document postseason participation and season records across several of these programs. [ref: Hayden Wildcats Sports History, Alabama High School Football and Sports History]

== Enrollment ==
The National Center for Education Statistics reported an enrollment of 798 students for the 2024–2025 school year. [ref: Hayden High School: School Directory Information, National Center for Education Statistics]

data.title: Red Rising (series)
data.text:
Red Rising is a dystopian science fiction series written by American author Pierce Brown. Set in a technologically advanced society organized around a rigid, color-coded social hierarchy, the series follows characters who challenge the political, social, and military systems governing humanity. The story begins on Mars and expands across the solar system as conflicts over oppression, revolution, power, loyalty, and freedom intensify. [ref: Red Rising by Pierce Brown, Penguin Random House]

The series began with Red Rising, published in 2014. The original trilogy consists of Red Rising, Golden Son (2015), and Morning Star (2016). [ref: Golden Son by Pierce Brown, Penguin Random House] [ref: Morning Star by Pierce Brown, Penguin Random House] Brown subsequently expanded the story with Iron Gold (2018), followed by Dark Age (2019) and Light Bringer (2023). [ref: Iron Gold by Pierce Brown, Penguin Random House] [ref: Dark Age by Pierce Brown, Penguin Random House] [ref: Light Bringer by Pierce Brown, Penguin Random House] The seventh novel, Red God, is planned to conclude the saga.

==Setting and themes==
The series takes place in a future in which humanity has colonized the solar system and society is divided into genetically and socially stratified groups known as Colors. Golds occupy the ruling class, while Reds occupy the lowest levels of the hierarchy, performing labor under conditions designed to preserve the established order.

The novels explore revolution, authoritarianism, class conflict, political legitimacy, military strategy, friendship, sacrifice, and the moral consequences of pursuing power. As the story progresses, the conflict expands from an uprising against an oppressive social order into a broader struggle over the future of human civilization.

==Plot==
===Original trilogy===
The original trilogy follows Darrow, a Red miner on Mars who discovers that the society he serves is built on deception. After undergoing a transformation that allows him to infiltrate the ruling Gold class, Darrow enters the institutions that govern the Society and works to undermine them from within.

In Red Rising, Darrow enters the Institute, a brutal proving ground where young Golds compete for status and power. Golden Son follows his rise through the political and military establishment, while Morning Star depicts the escalating conflict between the Rising and the Society.

===Second series===
The second series takes place approximately ten years after the events of Morning Star. The Rising has overthrown the old regime, but establishing a lasting political order proves more difficult than winning the war.

Iron Gold broadens the narrative through multiple perspectives, examining the consequences of revolution and the challenges of governing a fractured solar system. Dark Age depicts the escalating military and political crises confronting the Republic, while Light Bringer continues the struggle among rival powers as the future of the solar system remains uncertain.

Red God is intended to conclude the overarching story.

==Characters==
* Darrow — A Red-born revolutionary who infiltrates the Gold ruling class and becomes a central military and political figure in the Rising.
* Virginia au Augustus — Commonly known as Mustang, a Gold leader whose political judgment and commitment to the Republic shape the conflict.
* Sevro au Barca — Darrow's close ally and a prominent member of the Howlers.
* Cassius au Bellona — A Gold swordsman whose loyalties, relationships, and personal code place him at the center of several major conflicts.
* Adrius au Augustus — Known as the Jackal, he is a calculating political strategist and one of Darrow's most dangerous adversaries.
* Lysander au Lune — A central character in the second series whose competing ideals and ambitions influence the struggle over the solar system's future.
* Lyria of Lagalos — A Red whose experiences provide a perspective on the lives of ordinary people affected by the Rising and its aftermath.
* Ephraim ti Horn — A former soldier and criminal whose storyline explores survival, loss, and the consequences of political upheaval.

==Adaptations==
===Audiobooks===
The novels have been released in audiobook editions. The series' audio editions feature narrated performances that bring its extensive cast of characters, political conflicts, and military action to life.

===Board game===
A tabletop board game based on Red Rising was published by Stonemaier Games in 2021. The game uses characters and factions from the novels as the basis for a competitive card-driven strategy experience. [ref: Red Rising Standard Version, Stonemaier Games]

===Screen adaptation===
A screen adaptation of Red Rising has been pursued at various points. In October 2026, reports described renewed film development involving Paramount Pictures, with Francis Lawrence attached to direct and Justin Rhodes to write the screenplay. Pierce Brown was also reported to be involved as an executive producer. [ref: The Red Rising Movie Is Going To Be Really Hard To Get Right, For A Few Reasons, CinemaBlend]

data.title: Meta Akita
data.text:
----

Meta Akita Inc. (Japanese: ) is a Japanese research and consulting firm based in Akita, Akita Prefecture. Its principal activities include research, regional development strategy, policy formulation, new business development, and the development and implementation of artificial intelligence and blockchain technologies. [ref: 事業内容：地域戦略、イノベーション支援、AI導入, Meta Akita]

In 2022, the company partnered with the Akita Inu Preservation Society to develop an international community of Akita dog enthusiasts using non-fungible tokens (NFTs) and metaverse platforms. [ref: 秋田犬で経済圏を 保存会公認 「メタ秋田」が設立 世界のファン拡大へ 地方創生目指す, Hokuroku Shimbun] [ref: 「秋田犬」がデジタルアートに 保存会×メタ秋田で１３日発売, Akita Sakigake Shimpo]

The company's stated philosophy includes the use of regional resources in domestic and international markets, the development of clients' businesses, and "strategic disruption and creation", which it describes as reconsidering existing structures and developing new industries. It also states that its approach combines data analysis and field research with support extending from strategy development to technology implementation.

== Business ==
=== Research and consulting ===
Meta Akita supports local governments and businesses in regional strategy, policy formulation and business development through research in Japan and overseas. Its work includes statistical analysis of regional economies, industrial structures and demographic trends, studies of initiatives in Japan and overseas, and stakeholder interviews. These inform its analysis of regional issues, business conditions, stakeholder needs and practical constraints, and the preparation of strategies, policies and business plans. [ref: 実績：政策提言、先端技術の社会実装、自治体・大学連携, Meta Akita]

Its services for businesses include planning new ventures, preparing business plans, commercialising regional resources and intellectual property, and supporting business development through collaboration among industry, universities and government.

In technology implementation, the company supports the design, deployment and adoption of AI, data applications and blockchain systems. Its services also cover business process digitalisation and workforce training.

=== AgeTech ===
The company conducts research and develops policy proposals concerning AgeTech, technology that supports the health, daily lives and social participation of older people. Its initiative covers four areas: health, daily living, social participation, and family and community. These include health management, dementia support, housing, mobility, learning, employment, social interaction, care and monitoring. [ref: AgeTech × 地方創生：秋田AgeTechHub構想, Meta Akita]

==== Akita AgeTech Hub Initiative ====
In August 2025, Meta Akita developed the Akita AgeTech Hub Initiative and submitted it to the Akita Prefectural Government. The proposal aims to establish the prefecture as a centre for AgeTech research and business development, addressing population decline and ageing while supporting local businesses and industrial development. [ref: Akita AgeTech Hub Initiative formulated and submitted to Akita Prefecture, Meta Akita]

Based on studies of initiatives in Japan and overseas, including industry support centres abroad, the proposal seeks to connect companies and researchers in Japan and abroad with businesses, local governments and universities in Akita. It identifies three functions:
* International conferences and information sharing to support business and research collaboration.
* Test sites in care and medical settings and local businesses to assess products and services and users' needs.
* Commercialisation and financing support, including a proposed public–private venture capital fund for businesses whose products and services have been evaluated through pilot projects. [ref: Our proposal selected for Akita Prefecture's longevity society conference project, Meta Akita]

==== Akita Prefecture conference project ====
In August 2026, the Akita Prefectural Government selected Meta Akita as the preferred contractor for a project to organise a conference on longevity and well-being. According to the company, it is responsible for planning and operating a prefecture-hosted symposium scheduled for January 2027, with keynote lectures and panel discussions on AgeTech.

The company describes the symposium as an initial stage of the Akita AgeTech Hub Initiative, intended to establish a shared understanding of ageing-related issues among residents and local businesses. Its proposed subsequent activities include recurring conferences, pilot projects in care and medical settings, and financing for businesses evaluated through those projects.

=== University collaboration ===
Meta Akita collaborates with Akita International University on the Tohoku Digital Archive initiative. Its corporate history dates the start of this joint research to October 2025. The company describes the initiative as using AI and blockchain technology to document and preserve regional folk culture for use in education, research and tourism.

=== Digital pedigree certificates ===
Meta Akita and the US company Heirloom Inc. jointly developed digital pedigree certificates for the Akita Inu Preservation Society. [ref: Japan Akita dog society issues digital pedigrees to combat forgery, Kyodo News] The company announced the system in February 2024, with introduction scheduled for March that year.

The system was developed to address forged paper pedigrees and documents lost in the post. It uses decentralised identifiers (DIDs) and verifiable credentials (VCs) to verify issuers and allows owners to receive certificates through a smartphone application and present them to third parties. It also associates dogs' microchip numbers with pedigree information.

=== Akita dog-related activities ===
Through its Akita Inu Partnership programme with companies and organisations, Meta Akita develops Akita dog-themed NFTs, tourism projects and products. [ref: 秋田犬プロモーションと秋田犬事業開発のための秋田犬パートナーシップを募集中。秋田犬NFTやメタバース開発を手がける、「秋田犬保存会」公認企業「Meta Akita」。, Meta Akita] In 2023, it developed an NFT and sake set commemorating the centenary of Hachikō's birth as a return gift for donations to Ōdate under Japan's furusato nōzei programme. Designs submitted through public calls were used for the NFTs and sake labels. [ref: 秋田県大館市のふるさと納税返礼品に、ハチ公生誕100年を記念した限定NFTとオリジナル日本酒のセットが登場, Meta Akita] [ref: 秋田県大館市ふるさと納税「ハチ公100年NFT」の第２回デザイン公募を開始。採用作品はNFTや日本酒ラベルに。, Meta Akita]

The company's services also include support for international business expansion.

data.title: Karen Ocamb
data.text:
----

Karen Ocamb is an American journalist, editor, and photographer whose reporting has focused on LGBTQ+ civil rights, the HIV/AIDS epidemic, and LGBTQ+ political history. She began her career in broadcast journalism at CBS News before entering LGBTQ+ journalism in 1988. [ref: Frontiers news editor Karen Ocamb laid off by new owners – Press Pass Q, blog.presspassq.gay] [ref: ]

Ocamb worked for nearly three decades with Frontiers, a Los Angeles-based LGBTQ+ publication, and later became the founding news editor of the Los Angeles Blade in 2017. Her reporting has documented the AIDS epidemic, LGBTQ+ political movements, civil rights campaigns, and the development of LGBTQ+ organizations in Southern California and nationally. [ref: ] [ref: Lesbian reporter fired by prominent queer publication for being too old, LGBTQ Nation] [ref: Frontiers news editor Karen Ocamb laid off by new owners – Press Pass Q, blog.presspassq.gay]

Her work has received recognition from the California Legislative LGBT Caucus, GLAAD, the Los Angeles Press Club, and the City of West Hollywood. In 2020, she received a Special Recognition honor at the GLAAD Media Awards. She was also named the Los Angeles Press Club’s 2020 Print Journalist of the Year in the under-50,000-circulation category, with the award presented in October 2021. [ref: ] [ref: ] [ref: Former LA Blade Editor Karen Ocamb, journalist of the year awardee, Los Angeles Blade: LGBTQ News, Rights, Politics, Entertainment]

== Early Life ==
Karen Ocamb was born on January 24, 1950, at Maxwell Air Force Base in Montgomery, Alabama. Her father served in the United States Air Force, and her family moved several times before settling in Westport, Connecticut. [ref: Karen Ocamb: A Proud Eyewitness to LA AIDS/LGBTQ History, Los Angeles Blade: LGBTQ News, Rights, Politics, Entertainment]

During the 1960s, Ocamb participated in demonstrations against the Vietnam War and became involved in the civil rights and women’s liberation movements. She attended Skidmore College before beginning her journalism career in New York City. [ref: Karen Ocamb: A Proud Eyewitness to LA AIDS/LGBTQ History, Los Angeles Blade: LGBTQ News, Rights, Politics, Entertainment] [ref: Former LA Blade Editor Karen Ocamb, journalist of the year awardee, Los Angeles Blade: LGBTQ News, Rights, Politics, Entertainment]

== Journalism Career ==

=== CBS News & Early Career ===
Ocamb began her journalism career at CBS News in New York City in 1973. During her time with the network, she worked in broadcast production and editorial roles. Her career at CBS culminated in work producing coverage of the 1984 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles for CBS affiliates. [ref: ] [ref: Former LA Blade Editor Karen Ocamb, journalist of the year awardee, Los Angeles Blade: LGBTQ News, Rights, Politics, Entertainment]

Following her work in network journalism, Ocamb pursued theater and volunteered in the campaign for West Hollywood’s incorporation as an independent city. She subsequently worked for a Hollywood public relations firm. [ref: ]

== LGBTQ+ Journalism and AIDS Reporting ==
In 1988, Ocamb began reporting for Frontiers, a Los Angeles-based LGBTQ+ publication. Her first article concerned ACT UP’s October 1988 protests demanding expanded access to experimental AIDS treatments, including demonstrations directed at the Food and Drug Administration. [ref: Frontiers news editor Karen Ocamb laid off by new owners – Press Pass Q, blog.presspassq.gay]

Ocamb has described the deaths of friends during the AIDS epidemic as a major influence on her decision to enter LGBTQ+ journalism. Her reporting subsequently focused on HIV/AIDS, public health, LGBTQ+ political organizing, civil rights, and community organizations. [ref: Frontiers news editor Karen Ocamb laid off by new owners – Press Pass Q, blog.presspassq.gay] [ref: ]

Over the following decades, Ocamb reported on LGBTQ+ political developments in California and nationally. Her coverage included the 1994 election of Sheila Kuehl to the California State Assembly, the establishment of the California Legislative LGBT Caucus, and the election of John A. Pérez and Toni Atkins as speakers of the California State Assembly. [ref: ]

Ocamb also appeared as a commentator on radio programs discussing LGBTQ+ political and legal developments. She participated in coverage of California’s same-sex marriage litigation on KCRW’s public affairs program Which Way, L.A.?, hosted by Warren Olney. [ref: ]

Ocamb also contributed to other LGBTQ+ and progressive publications, including The Pride LA, Bay Area Reporter, Windy City Times, The Bilerico Project, and HuffPost. She established the LGBTQ+ news and commentary blog LGBT POV. [ref: Karen Ocamb: A Proud Eyewitness to LA AIDS/LGBTQ History, Los Angeles Blade: LGBTQ News, Rights, Politics, Entertainment] [ref: ]

In 2012, Ocamb contributed two chapters to Gay Press, Gay Power: The Growth of LGBT Community Newspapers in America, a historical collection edited by journalist Tracy Baim. Her contributions, “Headlines, Heroes and History” and “Frontiers Magazine,” examined LGBTQ+ journalism and the history of the Los Angeles publication Frontiers. [ref: ]

In addition to her work in LGBTQ+ publications, Ocamb contributed reporting to mainstream newspapers. In September 1996, the Los Angeles Times published her profile of Judy Wieder, the first female editor-in-chief of The Advocate. The article examined Wieder’s editorial priorities and the changing landscape of LGBTQ+ news publishing. [ref: In News, in History: First Female Editor of the Advocate Defines Her Mission, Los Angeles Times]

Ocamb’s firsthand knowledge of Southern California LGBTQ+ history has also been cited in mainstream news reporting. In 2018, the Los Angeles Times quoted her recollections of former Los Angeles County assessor Kenneth P. Hahn and his participation in West Hollywood’s public commitment ceremonies during the early 1990s. [ref: Kenneth P. Hahn, former L.A. County assessor who became an accidental LGBTQ trailblazer, dies at 78, Los Angeles Times]

=== Books and Historical Writing ===
Ocamb is the author of Representation Matters: How Victory Fund, Victory Institute, and LGBT Leaders Are Transforming America (2016), a book documenting the development of LGBTQ+ political representation in the United States. The book examines the history of the LGBTQ+ Victory Fund and Victory Institute and the role of LGBTQ+ elected officials in American politics. [ref: ]

Her research was subsequently incorporated into Pride & Progress, a historical project documenting LGBTQ+ political leadership. According to the project’s editors, major portions of its historical material were adapted from Ocamb’s book. [ref: ]

=== Frontiers and professional recognition ===
Ocamb became a full-time staff member of Frontiers in 2002 and eventually served as its news editor. The publication covered LGBTQ+ politics, culture, public health, and community affairs in Southern California. [ref: Lesbian reporter fired by prominent queer publication for being too old, LGBTQ Nation] [ref: Frontiers news editor Karen Ocamb laid off by new owners – Press Pass Q, blog.presspassq.gay]

In February 2016, Ocamb was laid off during a restructuring by the publication’s parent company, Multimedia Platforms Worldwide. The decision attracted attention from journalists and editors working in LGBTQ+ media. [ref: Lesbian reporter fired by prominent queer publication for being too old, LGBTQ Nation] [ref: Frontiers news editor Karen Ocamb laid off by new owners – Press Pass Q, blog.presspassq.gay]

In an article for Press Pass Q, journalist Chuck Colbert examined the restructuring and interviewed Ocamb, company executives, and journalists from other LGBTQ+ publications. The article included commentary from Cynthia Laird of the Bay Area Reporter, Michael K. Lavers of the Washington Blade, and other media professionals discussing Ocamb’s contributions to LGBTQ+ reporting. [ref: Frontiers news editor Karen Ocamb laid off by new owners – Press Pass Q, blog.presspassq.gay]

The reporting also addressed broader changes in LGBTQ+ journalism, including the financial pressures facing print publications and the shift toward digital publishing and entertainment-oriented coverage. [ref: Frontiers news editor Karen Ocamb laid off by new owners – Press Pass Q, blog.presspassq.gay]

In March 2017, The Advocate reported that Ocamb had filed an age and gender discrimination lawsuit against her former employer. The article examined her career and the circumstances surrounding her departure from Frontiers. [ref: ]

Ocamb was also involved in professional journalism organizations, serving on the board of the Los Angeles Press Club. During her board service, she participated in organizing the club’s annual journalism awards ceremony. [ref: https://lapressclub.org/3424-2/, Los Angeles Press Club]

=== Los Angeles Blade ===
In July 2017, Ocamb was appointed founding news editor of the Los Angeles Blade, a newly established LGBTQ+ newspaper affiliated with the Washington Blade. Her responsibilities included reporting on LGBTQ+ issues in Southern California and overseeing the publication’s news coverage. [ref: Los Angeles Blade names Karen Ocamb news editor, Los Angeles Blade: LGBTQ News, Rights, Politics, Entertainment]

During her tenure, Ocamb reported on LGBTQ+ civil rights, political developments, public policy, and issues affecting LGBTQ+ communities. Her work included coverage of the Trump administration’s restrictions on transgender military service and the COVID-19 pandemic. [ref: Former LA Blade Editor Karen Ocamb, journalist of the year awardee, Los Angeles Blade: LGBTQ News, Rights, Politics, Entertainment]

Ocamb left the Los Angeles Blade in March 2021 to join Public Justice, a nonprofit legal advocacy organization, where she worked in communications and storytelling. [ref: Karen Ocamb leaves LGBTQ press for Public Justice advocacy, Los Angeles Blade: LGBTQ News, Rights, Politics, Entertainment]

== Later Work ==
Following her departure from the Los Angeles Blade, Ocamb worked with Public Justice, a national nonprofit organization involved in civil rights, environmental protection, and consumer and workers’ rights litigation. [ref: ] [ref: Karen Ocamb leaves LGBTQ press for Public Justice advocacy, Los Angeles Blade: LGBTQ News, Rights, Politics, Entertainment]

In 2026, Ocamb established LGBTQ+ Freedom Fighters, an independent journalism project published through Substack. The publication features interviews, historical reporting, and commentary concerning LGBTQ+ activists, civil rights organizations, and political developments. [ref: Veteran journalist Karen Ocamb continues the good fight with the launch of her podcast, Los Angeles Blade: LGBTQ News, Rights, Politics, Entertainment]

Ocamb also launched the podcast LGBTQ+ Freedom Fighters with Karen Ocamb, featuring interviews with activists and community figures involved in LGBTQ+ history and contemporary political movements. [ref: Veteran journalist Karen Ocamb continues the good fight with the launch of her podcast, Los Angeles Blade: LGBTQ News, Rights, Politics, Entertainment]

Ocamb continued reporting on LGBTQ+ cultural history through LGBTQ+ Freedom Fighters. Her reporting on the death of actor and activist Michael Kearns in October 2026 was subsequently cited by Entertainment Weekly. [ref: Michael Kearns, barrier-breaking gay actor and activist, dies at 76, EW.com]

== Awards & Recognition ==

=== Early journalism recognition ===
In 2004, the Los Angeles chapter of the National Lesbian and Gay Journalists Association announced plans to honor Ocamb for her contributions to LGBTQ+ journalism. [ref: NLGJA Announces 2004 Excellence in Journalism Award Winners, groups.google.com]

A 2004 Los Angeles Press Club publication also identified Ocamb as a recipient of Christopher Street West’s Woman of the Year recognition. [ref: https://lapressclub.org/3424-2/, Los Angeles Press Club]

In 2006, Ocamb received third place in the Sarah Pettit Memorial Award for Excellence in LGBT Media category at the National Lesbian and Gay Journalists Association’s Excellence in Journalism Awards. She was recognized for her work at IN Los Angeles Magazine. [ref: 2006 Excellence in Journalism Award Winners: NLGJA]

=== Rainbow Key Award ===
Ocamb received a Rainbow Key Award from the City of West Hollywood in recognition of her contributions to the LGBTQ+ community. A 2013 article published by WEHOonline identified her among previous recipients. [ref: WeHo Council Criticizes Rainbow Key Award Selection Process, WEHOonline.com]

=== Women in Leadership Award ===
In March 2016, Ocamb was among the recipients of West Hollywood’s annual Women in Leadership Awards. The awards recognized women who had made contributions to the city’s community, civic life, and professional organizations. [ref: Annual Women in Leadership Awards on Wednesday, WEHOonline.com]

=== California Legislative LGBT Caucus ===
On August 8, 2016, Ocamb was among six Californians honored by the California Legislative LGBT Caucus during its annual Pride ceremony at the State Capitol. The honorees received legislative resolutions recognizing their contributions to LGBTQ+ equality. [ref: ]

The Legislature’s announcement described Ocamb’s career in LGBTQ+ journalism, including her coverage of the AIDS epidemic, political developments, and civil rights issues. The other honorees included former and serving California elected officials Christine Kehoe, John Laird, and Mark Leno. [ref: ]

=== GLAAD Media Awards ===
In 2020, GLAAD presented Ocamb with a Special Recognition honor at its 31st annual Media Awards, acknowledging her journalism career and reporting on LGBTQ+ communities. [ref: ] [ref: ]

=== Los Angeles Press Club ===
In October 2021, Ocamb received the 2020 Print Journalist of the Year award in the under-50,000-circulation category at the Los Angeles Press Club’s 63rd Southern California Journalism Awards. [ref: Former LA Blade Editor Karen Ocamb, journalist of the year awardee, Los Angeles Blade: LGBTQ News, Rights, Politics, Entertainment] [ref: Past Winners, Los Angeles Press Club]

== References ==

== External Links ==
[https://karenocamb.substack.com/about LGTQ+ Freedom Fighters]

data.title: Lamin Sillah
data.text:
Lamin Sillah (born 6 June 2006) is a Gambian professional footballer who plays as a striker for EFL League Two club Gillingham, on loan from Nottingham Forest. He previously played for Steve Biko in The Gambia and the under-19 side of Greek club Olympiacos, and has represented The Gambia at under-20 level.

==Club career==

===Early career===
Sillah began his career with Steve Biko in the Gambian First Division. He made a strong start to the 2023–24 season, scoring nine goals in his first ten league appearances and providing three assists. [ref: Sillah, Mustapha open up on GFF Division 1 Golden boot race, The Alkamba Times] Sillah said that he had taken on greater goalscoring responsibility following the departure of Adama Bojang from the club.

He finished the season as the league's top goalscorer with 14 goals. [ref: Title favorites, new signing, drop in goal ratio and relegation battle, The Alkamba Times] In May 2024, Sillah also scored as Steve Biko beat Elite United 2–0 to reach the semi-finals of the Gambia Football Federation Cup. [ref: Medina Utd, Steve Biko, Team Rhino cruise to FF Cup semis, The Point]

Sillah subsequently moved to Greece, signing a four-year contract with Olympiacos in October 2024. Three days after signing, he scored the winning goal on his debut for the club's under-19 side in a 2–1 victory over Panathinaikos. [ref: Λαμίν Σιλά: Υπέγραψε την Πέμπτη 4ετές συμβόλαιο στον Ολυμπιακό και την Κυριακή έκρινε το ντέρμπι «αιωνίων» Κ19, Sportal]

Sillah scored nine goals and provided five assists in 17 U19 Super League appearances during his season with Olympiacos. [ref: Forest sign Sillah, Nottingham Forest F.C.] He was also part of the club's squad in the 2024–25 UEFA Youth League. [ref: UEFA Youth League 2024–2025 – Knockout Round 32, Olympiacos F.C.]

===Nottingham Forest===
On 16 July 2025, Sillah moved to England to sign for Nottingham Forest on a contract until the summer of 2028, initially joining the club's B team.

He became a regular in Forest's development side during the 2025–26 season and also made three appearances for the club's under-21 team in the EFL Trophy. [ref: Gills snap up striker on loan, Kent Sports News] On 24 May 2026, Sillah was named in a Nottingham Forest senior matchday squad for the first time, remaining an unused substitute in a 1–1 Premier League draw with Bournemouth. [ref: Nottingham Forest vs. Bournemouth Match Report – Sunday May 24, 2026, FBref]

===Loan to Gillingham===
On 27 August 2026, Sillah joined EFL League Two club Gillingham on loan for the remainder of the 2026–27 season. He had scored in both of Forest B's opening two matches of the season prior to the move, including an equaliser against Gateshead in the National League Cup.

Sillah made his English Football League debut two days after signing, replacing Ronan Hale in the 81st minute of a 1–1 draw with Northampton Town at Priestfield. [ref: Live Commentary – Gillingham vs Northampton, Sky Sports] On 5 September 2026, Sillah scored his first goal in the EFL in a 4–1 away win against Rochdale. [ref: Rochdale 1-4 Gillingham Report, Gillingham F.C]

==International career==
Sillah was selected for the Gambia under-20 squad for the 2024 WAFU Zone A U20 tournament in Liberia. [ref: Gambia U-20 gaffer announces squad ahead of WAFU U-20 tourney, The Point]

He scored as Gambia came from behind to draw 2–2 with defending champions Senegal in the group stage. [ref: Gambia draws Senegal at Wafu U-20 tourney, The Standard] Sillah scored again in a 3–0 victory over Guinea in the third-place play-off as Gambia finished the tournament in third place. [ref: Gambia U20 vs Guinea U20, Global Sports Archive]

data.title: Thomson K. Mathew (1951-)
data.text:
Thomson K. Mathew (1951 - ) is an American Pentecostal academic, author, and a globally recognized theological educator. He is professor emeritus and former Dean of the College of Theology and Ministry at Oral Roberts University ([https://oru.edu oru.edu]) and well-known conference speaker within the Spirit-empowered movement.

Career

Mathew began his career as the 16th pastor (1976-1981) of the historic Gospel Tabernacle of New Haven, CT (now Hope Christian Church) and later served as a chaplain at the (former) City of Faith Medical and Research Center in Tulsa, OK (1981-1989). In 1989, he joined the graduate (seminary) faculty of the College of Theology and Ministry at Oral Roberts University (ORU).

After thirty years of service at ORU as professor of pastoral care and concurrently holing various offices as Dean of Students, Director of Field Education and Assessment, Dean of Doctoral Studies, and Associate Dean of Academic Affairs at various times, he became the fifth Dean of the institution, serving sixteen years (2000-2016). He became professor emeritus in 2018 and has been serving as a volunteer academic consultant, doctoral program guide, and guest professor at several seminaries, including three in India - India Bible College, Kumbanad, Kerala; New Life College, Bangalore, Karnataka; and Filadelfia Institute of Global Studies, Udaipur, Rajasthan.

During his deanship, ORU Theological faculty was commissioned to help theological schools within the Spirit-empowered movement in England (Peniel College), Sweden (Livets Old, now Scandinavian School of Theology), Korea (Foursquare Gospel Theological Seminary, now Asia Life University), etc., modeling teaching courses from a Pentecostal/charismatic perspective and assisting to gain accreditation from their own regional jurisdictions.

Mathew has spoken at mega churches and major Pentecostal conferences in various parts of the world, including Sweden, Singapore, India, Russia, El Salvador, USA, UK, and Czech Republic.

Contributions to Theology and Theological Education

A major scholarly contribution was systematizing, clarifying, and historically interpreting Oral Roberts' theology for a new generation of scholars and ministry leaders. His work helped move Roberts' ideas from popular preaching into academically articulated theology. Rather than treating Roberts' theology as static, Mathew argued that it developed through three identifiable stages.

As dean, Mathew encouraged scholarship that remained faithful to Spirit-empowered perspective while engaging the wider evangelical and academic community. In this regard, he developed a new model of pastoral care by reframing pastoral care as "ministry between miracles."

Early Education and Family

Thomson K. Mathew was born in India as the eldest of six children. His parents (K. T. Mathew and Aleyamma Mathew) and grandparents (K. M. Thomas and Mariamma Thomas) were Pentecostal ministers in India. He attended CMS Primary School and St Thomas High School in Vechoochira and graduated from St Mary's High School, Niranam, all in Kerala. He migrated to the United States in 1972. He is married to Molly (George) Mathew. They are parents to two daughters.

Education and professional association

Thomson K. Mathew is a graduate of Bishop Moore College (Kerala University), India (BS, 1971), Yale University Divinity School (MDiv, 1975 and STM, 1977), Oral Roberts University (DMin, 1986), and Oklahoma State University (EdD, 1992). He is a professional member of the Association of Professional Chaplains (APC), Association for Clinical Pastoral Education (ACPE), and a charter member of the Association for Doctor of Ministry Education (ADME).

Books

Thomson K. Mathew is a prolific writer. His works include:

Ministry Between Miracles, revised edition: A Biblical Model of Spirit-led Pastoral Care

Spirit-led Ministry in the 21st Century, 3rd edition: Essentials of Ministry for Human Pastors Serving the AI Generation

Spiritual Identity and Spirit-empowered Life: Discover Your Identity in God's Family, Purpose in God's Call, and Power in God's Spirit

Spiritual Identity and Spirit-empowered Life Leader's Guide

What Will Your Tombstone Say? 52 Short Essays on Spirit-filled Church, Spirit-led Ministry, and Spirit-Empowered Discipleship

Membership to Discipleship: A Path to Spiritual Formation and World-Impacting Life

Prayer, Medicine and Healing: Why Ministers, Medical Professionals, and All Followers of Jesus Should Pray for the Sick

A Seminary Dean's Experiment with Servant Leadership: Stories and Lessons from My Journey Through Ivy League to Whole Person Education

Anatomy of a DMin Dissertation: A Guide to Develop, Implement, and Report a Doctor of Ministry Project

Small Group Ministry in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: A Guide to Extend Pastoral Care and Lead from Membership to Discipleship

Spirit-led Ministry in the 21st Century and Spiritual Identity and Spirit-empowered Live have been translated into Korean language, Spirit-led Ministry in the 21st Century has also been translated into Malayalam. He has written two other books in Malayalam.

== References ==

https://digitalshowcase.oru.edu/theo_history/1

Mathew, Thomson, "Oral Roberts’ Theology of Healing: A Journey from Pentecostal “Divine Healing” to Charismatic “Signs and Wonders” to Spirit-empowered “Whole Person Healing”" Spiritus: ORU Journal of Theology Vol. 3, no. 2 (2018): -. [https://digitalshowcase.oru.edu/spiritus/vol3/iss2/13 10.31380/2573-6345.1092]

[https://thomsonkmathew.com www.thomsonkmathew.com]

data.title: Ehrigite
data.text:
----

Ehrigite is a sub-microscopic bismuth telluride mineral with the chemical formula. Formally approved by the International Mineralogical Association (IMA) in 2024, it is a member of the tetradymite group of minerals. [ref: Ehrigite, a new mineral from the tetradymite group, Mineralogical Magazine] The mineral is named in honor of Dr. Kathy Ehrig, a prominent chief geologist at BHP, recognizing her contributions to geometallurgy and ore microscopy. [ref: New mineral named after BHP geologist Dr Kathy Ehrig, Mining Weekly] [ref: New mineral named after BHP geologist Dr Kathy Ehrig, BHP] [ref: World-first new mineral identified using electron microscopy, Microscopy Australia]

== Properties ==
Due to its sub-microscopic nature, ehrigite is rarely seen as discrete macro-crystals. Under reflected light microscopy, it appears opaque and pale gray, resembling other native bismuth and bismuth telluride minerals. Grains isolated by researchers are typically smaller than 100 microns.

== Discovery ==
The mineral was discovered by a research team led by scientists at the University of Adelaide, including Associate Professor Cristiana Ciobanu and Professor Nigel Cook. The type locality for ehrigite is the abandoned Good Hope gold mine in Hedley, British Columbia, Canada, where it occurs alongside other bismuth-rich minerals. [ref: https://resourcesreview.com.au/news_article/new-mineral-ehrigite-recognised-by-international-authority-honouring-bhp-scientists-legacy/]
