data.title: Hygglo
data.text:
Hygglo is Swedish Peer-to-peer rental marketplace for individuals to rent various items from each other. It was founded in Stockholm in 2016 by Ola Degerfors, Axel Hellström and Henrik Fräsén. Hygglo vill få folk att hyra grejer – nu ökar de efter uppköp: “Har lång väg kvar”, Impact Loop

Hygglo is part of the Sharing economy and has been used in many case studies in academic research regarding the environmental and social effects of peer-to-peer sharing. [ref: Assessing the Environmental Potential of Collaborative Consumption: Peer-to-Peer Product Sharing in Hammarby Sjöstad, Sweden, Sustainability] [ref: Ethics and Sustainability in Digital Cultures, Routledge]

== History ==
Hygglo was founded in Stockholm in 2016.

In 2019 and 2020, Hygglo was included in Swedish technology publication ‘’Computer Sweden’’s Topp100 selection of Swedish websites and online services. The service was included in the sustainability category in 2019 and the sharing-services category in 2020. [ref: Topp100 2019: Här är Sveriges 100 bästa sajter och nättjänster, Computer Sweden] [ref: Topp100 2020: Här är Sveriges 100 bästa sajter och nättjänster, Computer Sweden]

In 2022, Hygglo acquired British competitor Fat Llama. [ref: ‘A cricket bat to the face’: The story of one startup’s ‘gruelling’ road to acquisition, Sifted] [ref: Swedish Hygglo fattens peer-to-peer rental portfolio with Fat Llama buy for $41.5 million, Tech.eu]

== Academic research ==
Hygglo has been part of a case study in research examining both the environmental and social effects of the sharing economy.

A 2019 peer-reviewed study by Michael Martin, David Lazarevic and Charlie Gullström, published in the journal ‘‘Sustainability’’, investigated peer-to-peer sharing using transaction data from Hygglo in Hammarby Sjöstad, Stockholm. The authors researched the environmental effects of sharing consumer items compared with scenarios in which products would be purchased instead. The study found that product sharing reduces co2 emissions in the scenarios examined, main due to a reduced need for additional manufactured products.

Hygglo was also used as a case study by researchers Per Fors and Tina Ringenson in a book chapter examining the relationship between the sharing economy, social sustainability and local communities. The researchers examined how peer-to-peer sharing platforms could affect relationships between people in local communities. They discussed the potential for such platforms to strengthen local social connections while also considering limitations related to factors including user homogeneity and residential segregation in Stockholm.

In 2026, ‘’The Washington Post’’ discussed Hygglo as part of a examination of peer-to-peer sharing and community-based alternatives to purchasing consumer goods. The reporter used Hygglo while researching the challenges associated with sharing items between individuals. [ref: I wanted to buy less stuff. I ended up bonding with my neighbors., The Washington Post]

data.title: VolDex
data.text:
----

VolDex is a family of financial indices measuring implied volatility, developed by Nations Indexes, Inc., a Chicago-based index provider. The principal index, VOLI, tracks the implied volatility of the S&P 500 over a 30-calendar-day period using at-the-money options on the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (ticker: SPY). [ref: Vix challenged by new volatility index, [[Risk (magazine)] Nations Indexes calculates VolDex on a wide variety of underlyings including the Nasdaq-100, Russell 2000, Gold, Silver, Treasury Notes, Treasury Bonds, High-yield bonds, Volatility itself, Bitcoin, and several equities including Apple, Tesla, Microsoft, SpaceX, and others.

VolDex indices are most often compared with the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX). The primary methodological distinction is that the VIX uses a variance swap-based calculation drawing on a broad range of strike prices, while VolDex is a closed-form calculation using only options near the current market price of the underlying asset. [ref: Self-Regulatory Organizations; International Securities Exchange, LLC; Notice of Filing of Proposed Rule Change To List Options on the Nations VolDex Index, Federal Register]

==History==
Nations Indexes, Inc. was founded by Scott Nations, a former Chicago-based proprietary options trader. The company introduced VolDex in June 2013. Writing in the financial trade journal Risk, journalist Yakob Peterseil described the launch as a challenge to the VIX's two-decade market position, noting that VolDex "only looks at the implied volatility of a precisely at-the-money option due to expire in precisely 30 days," contrasting this with the VIX, which "prices future S&P 500 variance."

In August 2013, the International Securities Exchange (ISE) filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission a proposed rule change to list options on the Nations VolDex index. The SEC published notice of proceedings in November 2013 [ref: Self-Regulatory Organizations; International Securities Exchange, LLC; Order Instituting Proceedings To Determine Whether To Approve or Disapprove a Proposed Rule Change, as Modified by Amendment No. 1, To List Options on the Nations VolDex Index, Federal Register] and approved the rule change on January 28, 2014 (Exchange Act Release No. 71365, 79 FR 4512). [ref: ISE Gets Green Light to List VolDex Options, The Wall Street Journal]

In 2018, Crain's Chicago Business identified VolDex as one of several products seeking to challenge Cboe's dominance in volatility products following controversy surrounding the VIX. [ref: VIX woes open up opportunities for Cboe rivals, Crain's Chicago Business]

In 2019, Nasdaq licensed the VolDex methodology from Nations Indexes to create the Nasdaq-100 Volatility Index (VOLQ). [ref: Nasdaq nearing launch of its own volatility index, S&P Global Market Intelligence] CME Group announced futures on VOLQ in August 2020 [ref: CME Group to Launch Futures on Nasdaq-100 Volatility Index (VOLQ), CME Group] and launched the contracts on October 5, 2020. [ref: CME to launch volatility index futures contract, Crain's Chicago Business]

==Methodology==
VolDex is a closed-form measure of at-the-money implied volatility. The calculation uses the first in-the-money and first out-of-the-money call and put options for expirations that bracket the target tenor. For the 30-day index, this means one expiration before and one after 30 calendar days (43,200 minutes) from the moment of calculation.

Forward prices for each expiration are derived from put-call parity. These define the at-the-money level; option prices are then interpolated to yield hypothetical at-the-money put and call prices, which are combined to produce the VolDex value.

The methodology can be applied to multiple tenors and asset classes. Tenors include zero days-to-expiration (0DTE), one day, seven days, thirty days, and periods through 360 days. Asset classes include the S&P 500, Nasdaq-100, Russell 2000, U.S. Treasury bonds, gold, silver, and individual equities. [ref: VOLQ: How to Measure Nasdaq-100 Volatility, Traders Magazine]

The component expirations for the 30-day index roll each Thursday morning to the Friday expirations that are approximately 29 and 36 days in the future.

==Indices==

===VOLI (S&P 500)===

VOLI is the original VolDex index, measuring 30-day implied volatility from at-the-money options on SPY, the S&P 500 ETF. It is disseminated in real time under the ticker symbol VOLI, and historical data maintained by Nasdaq covers a period beginning January 31, 2005.

* Implied volatility
* S&P 500
* Nasdaq-100

data.title: Teneo Online School
data.text:
Teneo Online School (also trading internationally as Teneo International School) is a British international online school headquartered in London, England, delivering Pearson Edexcel qualifications to learners aged 11 to 19. The school operates entirely online, with no physical campus, and serves families across the United Kingdom, South Africa, the United Arab Emirates, Singapore, Hong Kong, Qatar, Kenya, Nigeria, and other countries.

== History ==
Teneo Online School was founded by Saul Geffen, who also developed the school's proprietary Smart School System. The school initially focused on the South African market, operating at teneoschool.co.za, before expanding internationally under the brand Teneo International School at teneoschool.com. The school offers curriculum pathways aligned to South African qualifications including CAPS and IEB, as well as the Pearson Edexcel British International curriculum.

== Curriculum and qualifications ==
Teneo delivers the Pearson Edexcel British International curriculum from Key Stage 3 (Years 7–9) through to International GCSEs (Years 10–11) and International AS and A Levels (Years 12–13). Pearson Edexcel International Advanced Level qualifications are recognised for entry by more than 1,000 universities worldwide, including institutions in the United Kingdom, North America, Asia, and the Middle East. [ref: Teneo Online School offers global families more than ever, GlobeNewswire]

In South Africa, the school additionally offers the Curriculum and Assessment Policy Statement (CAPS), the Independent Examinations Board (IEB) pathway, and the South African Comprehensive Assessment Institute (SACAI) Matric pathway. Students sit final examinations in person at approved examination centres. Teneo holds Pearson Edexcel Centre Number 94897.

== Smart School System ==
The Smart School System is Teneo's proprietary learning platform developed by founder Saul Geffen. The system combines live teaching, real-time analytics, behavioural science, and artificial intelligence to monitor learner engagement and academic progress, generating alerts when a learner's engagement changes so that teachers can intervene early.

== Research and public interest work ==

=== School safety ===
In 2026, Teneo International School submitted Freedom of Information requests to police forces across the United Kingdom, seeking data on sexual offences recorded at school premises over three years. Of 35 forces contacted, 19 were able to provide offence data. The data showed that reported sexual offences at schools rose from 1,789 to 2,066 over the period, an increase of more than 15 per cent. The sharpest rises were recorded in Nottinghamshire (50 per cent), Devon and Cornwall (49 per cent), and Greater Manchester (31 per cent). Several forces, including the Metropolitan Police and West Yorkshire, cited the cost of retrieving the data as a reason for not responding. [ref: Sexual offence reports at schools up by more than 15 per cent over three years, Daily Mirror]

Taryn Jankes, Chief Marketing Officer of Teneo International School, told the Daily Mirror that a rise in reported offences did not necessarily mean more offences were taking place, and that increased reporting could reflect stronger safeguarding culture and greater willingness among young people to come forward.

=== Matric study resources ===
In September 2026, Tracey Clayton, Phase Head at Teneo Online School, was quoted in The Citizen regarding free study resources available to South African matric pupils. Clayton recommended past papers published by the Department of Basic Education, free platforms including Siyavula and Khan Academy, and small study groups as alternatives to private tutoring. She noted that while free educational material had narrowed the gap between learners who could afford additional academic support and those who could not, access to a device, data, and a suitable study environment remained barriers for many families. [ref: Writing matric? Here's where to find free study tools, The Citizen]

== Recognition ==
In 2026, Teneo was named a finalist in the Trendsetter Awards' Product or Service Setting a Trend category at The EdTech Awards 2026, the world's largest awards programme for education technology presented by EdTech Digest. Saul Geffen was simultaneously named a finalist in the School Leader category. [ref: Teneo International School Named a Global Finalist in the World's Largest EdTech Awards, GlobeNewswire]

Also in 2026, Teneo received the Educational Establishment of the Year award at the Education Resources Awards.

== Delivery model ==
Teneo operates through three delivery formats: live online lessons taught in real time, a hybrid model combining live and recorded sessions, and a fully recorded format. All live sessions are recorded and made permanently available for revision and catch-up. The school reports having educated more than 20,000 learners and produced over 4,000 graduates.

data.title: Ajay B Harish
data.text:
----

Ajay B. Harish is a British-Indian computational engineer and Associate Professor in Computational Mechanics at the University of Manchester. His research aims at the development of numerical methods for computational mechanics, with applications in biomechanics and biomedical engineering. [ref: Ajay Harish, Research Explorer]

==Early life and education==
Harish graduated with a B.Tech in mechanical engineering from the National Institute of Technology Karnataka in 2007. He subsequently undertook masters' study in aeronautics at the California Institute of Technology and completed an engineer's thesis titled "simulation of dynamic interface fracture using a spectral boundary integral method", supervised by Nadia Lapusta in 2009. [ref: Simulation of Dynamic Interface Fracture Using Spectral Boundary Integral Method, CaltechTHESIS]. Subsequently he received a Dr.-Ing. from Leibniz University Hannover in 2018 under the supervision of Peter Wriggers. [ref: Micromechanics, fracture and contact behavior of nanoparticle reinforced polymers, Leibniz University Hannover Research Portal]. Harish was a group leader in Nanotribology at the Institute of Continuum Mechanics in Leibniz University Hannover between 2018-20. He joined the University of California, Berkeley in 2020 as a postdoctoral researcher with NHERI SimCenter. In 2022, he joined the University of Manchester as a lecturer in engineering simulation and data science and was later promoted to senior lecturer in 2025. Since Sep-2025, he serves as the Discipline Head of Education (Aerospace) / Deputy Head of Department (Mechanical & Aerospace engineering) at Manchester.

==Research and career==
Harish's work has spanned the development of numerical methods for modelling of tendon structures, abdominal aortic aneurysms and haemodynamics of the carotid.

== Recognition ==
Harish ss a recipient of a Ramanujan Fellowship in 2022 [ref: Ramanujan Fellowship, Research Explorer] and the UK-Italy Turing award by the Alan Turing Institute in 2024.

data.title: Vishnu Govindhan
data.text:
----

Vishnu Govindhan (also credited as Vishnu Govindan) is an Indian actor and film director known for his work in the Malayalam film industry. He is popularly known among Malayalam film audiences by the nickname "Jomy", after a supporting character he played in the 2017 film Oru Mexican Aparatha. [ref: History of Jomy, Deccan Chronicle] [ref: Director Vinayan's son Vishnu Vinay turns an actor; Oru Mexican Aparatha fame Vishnu Govindan to direct the movie, Onlookers Media]

== Early life ==
Govindhan is from Kottayam, Kerala. He moved to Kochi to pursue a B.Tech degree at the Cochin University of Science and Technology (CUSAT), a move that exposed him to the theatre and film community in the city and set him on the path toward acting, assistant direction, and later filmmaking.

== Career ==

=== Theatre and early film work ===
Before entering films, Govindhan worked as a theatre artiste in Kochi. He later worked as an assistant to filmmaker Tom Emmatty, having first met him during the making of Lord Livingstone 7000 Kandi, in which Govindhan had a small role. He went on to work with Emmatty on advertising films and later assisted him during the writing of Oru Mexican Aparatha. He had earlier had a minor acting role in Amal Neerad's Iyobinte Pusthakam.

=== Acting ===
Govindhan gained wider recognition for playing "Jomy" — a supporting, comic-relief role as the friend of the lead character — in Oru Mexican Aparatha (2017), starring Tovino Thomas. The role gave him his popular nickname.

=== Direction ===
Govindhan made his directorial debut with History of Joy (2017), a Malayalam coming-of-age drama produced under the banner of Sivaparvathi Films. He also co-wrote the film's story with Anoop P. [ref: Songs of 'History Of Joy', starring director Vinayan's son Vishnu Vinay, released, Onmanorama] The film starred Vishnu Vinay — son of director Vinayan — in his acting debut, alongside Vinay Forrt, Sai Kumar and Joju George. [ref: 'History of Joy' review: a take on second chances, Onmanorama] In its review, Onmanorama described the film as centring on a former convict's attempts to move past his history, and called Govindhan's work "commendable" for a directorial debut.

data.title: Marique B. Moss
data.text:
== Marique B. Moss ==
Marique B. Moss (born June 29,1993) is an American Afro-Indigenous author, poet, educator, and community organizer. She is an enrolled citizen of the Mandan, Hidatsa and Arikara Nation (MHA) and is of African American, and Dakota ancestry. Based in Minneapolis, MN, she is nationally known for her work in Afro-Indignous literature, cultural education, Indigenous food sovereignty, and community orginizing. she is the author of Sweetgrass and Soul Food: A Memoir in Poems (2025). Sweetgrass and Soul Work: A Seld-Guided Journal for Reflection and Renewal (2026), and My Afro-Indigenous Superpower(2026).

She is also the co-founder of Mashkiki Studios, an Indigenous cultural education and creative business.

== Early life and family ==
Marique was born on June 29, 1993, in Rio Rancho, New Mexico. She is of African American ancestry through her father and Hidatsa an Dakota ancestry through her mother. She is the daughter of Dr. Margaret P. Moss, and Indigenous nursing scholar and professor at the university of Minnesota. Margaret P. Moss is known for her research in Indigenous health, nursing Education, aging, and health policy. Her Traditional Hidatsa name is Mirgua Miash, meaning "Woman in the Water". She is an enrolled citizen of MHA Nation, also know as the Three Affiliated Tribes.

== Education ==
Marique B. Moss attended Fort Lewis College in Durango, Colorodo, earnin a bacholor of arts in Native American and Indigenous studies.

In 2019, she received the college's Outstanding Student r of the year recognition in Native American and Indigenous Studies.During her undergraduate studies, she co-founded the Black Student Union and established the Black Student Resource Center, supporting initiatives related to student retention, campus inclusion and educational equity. In 2020, she earned a Master of Legal Studies in Indigeous Peoples Law from the University of Oklahoma College of Law. She has also served as vice president of the Native American alumni chapter at Fort Lewis College.

== Literary career ==
In 2025, Marique B. Moss published her debut poetry memoir, Sweetgrass and Soul Food: A Memoir in Poems.

The collection examines Afro-Indigenous identity, family history, cultural belonging, relationships, and personal experiences through poetry. The book has been incorporated into university curricula, including coursework examining Indigenous literature, identity, and cultural representation. It has also been distributed through independent bookstores, educational institutions, museums, and cultural organizations. The publication received coverage from Sahan Journal and Minnesota Native News. Sahan Journal profiled the author and discussed the cultural intersections explored in her writing, including the concept of "Blindian Country."

===== Sweetgrass and Soul Work: A Self-Guided Journal for Reflection and Renewal =====
In 2026, she published Sweetgrass and Soul Work: A Self-Guided Journal for Reflection and Renewal. The companion publication to her debut poetry memoir includes guided writing prompts and reflective exercises exploring personal identity, grief, emotional well-being, and renewal.

===== My Afro-Indigenous Superpower =====
In 2026, Marique B. Moss published My Afro-Indigenous Superpower, a children's book illustrated by Adair Carroll. The story follows Meeka, a young Afro-Indigenous girl exploring her African American and Indigenous heritage through family stories, cultural traditions, and intergenerational knowledge.

My Afro-Indigenous Superpower is one of fewer than five children's books written by Afro-Indigenous authors specifically about Afro-Indigenous identity and the experiences of Afro-Indigenous children. The publication received coverage from Minnesota Public Radio in February 2026, highlighting its focus on identity, representation, and the importance of children seeing their experiences reflected in literature.

== Indigenous education and cultural preservation ==
Marique B. Moss co-founded Mashkiki Studios with Theodore Marcil. The Minneapolis-based business focuses on Indigenous cultural education, traditional plant knowledge, arts programming, storytelling, and community-based learning. The studio provides educational workshops involving Indigenous foodways, herbal preparations, traditional crafts, plant identification, and cultural practices. Her work includes developing and facilitating programs for schools, community organizations, and cultural institutions, with an emphasis on connecting Indigenous knowledge with contemporary education.

===== University of Minnesota Landscape Arboretum =====
In 2026, she participated in the co-curation of the Hidatsa Earth Lodge Agriculture exhibit and the Original People's Garden at the University of Minnesota Landscape Arboretum. The exhibitions examine Indigenous food systems, agricultural traditions, and relationships between land, culture, and community. The Hidatsa Earth Lodge Agriculture exhibit incorporates traditional planting methods, including mound-based agriculture and the cultivation of corn, beans, squash, and sunflowers. Her work at the Arboretum was featured in a July 2026 article highlighting Indigenous agricultural knowledge and the preservation of ancestral traditions.

===== The Story Lodge: An Indigenous Literary & Book Fair =====
In August 2026, she organized the inaugural The Story Lodge: An Indigenous Literary & Book Fair, presented by The Dreaded Hidatsa and Mashkiki Studios in partnership with Indigenous Roots Cultural Arts Center in Saint Paul, Minnesota.

Held on August 1, 2026, the free public event brought together Indigenous authors, publishers, illustrators, poets, artists, and educators. Programming included literary discussions, author panels, poetry readings, children's storytelling, book signings, and cultural workshops. The event featured conversations with Indigenous food advocate Sean Sherman and author Kate Nelson, alongside programming focused on Indigenous storytelling, publishing, and literary sovereignty. The event's cultural theme, Máagada Aru Óodi Mirísh ("When the Berries Ripen Moon"), reflected the Hidatsa seasonal calendar and the importance of storytelling and community gathering.

== Public Speaking and National Engagements ==
In September 2026, Marique B. Moss participated in a Google-hosted gathering in New York City marking the first anniversary of the Food Talks Network. Her participation included conversations concerning food, cultural storytelling, community, and representation. She has participated in public speaking engagements related to Afro-Indigenous identity, literature, cultural education, and Indigenous sovereignty.

In March 2026, she served as a featured alumni speaker during Fort Lewis College's Hozhoni Days Powwow alumni breakfast.

== Selected publications ==

data.title: Chamisa Elementary School
data.text:
Chamisa Elementary School is one of the five elementary schools in the Los Alamos Public Schools district, and is the second one in the community of White Rock after Piñon Elementary [ref: Los Alamos Public School Sites, Los Alamos Public Schools]. The school was founded in 1968.

Unlike the other four elementary schools in the district, Chamisa had an open pod design, as opposed to an individual classroom layout. There were two main circular pods consisting of seven classrooms apiece and an open area in the center for various activities. The classrooms could be used in any combination or individually [ref: https://www.usmodernist.org/AW/AW-1967-05.pdf].

In 2024, construction began at Chamisa to replace the aging building on campus [ref: Groundbreaking Ceremony Held At Site Of New Chamisa Elementary School]. A new building was built next to the old one, and opened in time for the 2025-2026 academic year [ref: Brand New Chamisa Elementary School Welcomes Students]; and soon after the start of the school year, the old building was demolished [ref: Demolition Scenes Wednesday At Old Chamisa School, Los Alamos Daily Post].

data.text:
= Jay Stratton =
John "Jay" Stratton is a former American intelligence official and senior civilian official within the United States Department of Defense. He is best known for his role as the director and senior leader of several official military programs investigating Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP), formerly referred to as UFOs. Stratton served as the first director of the Pentagon's Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force (UAPTF).

== Early Life and Career ==
Stratton has an extensive background in the United States Armed Forces and intelligence community. During his tenure with the Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA), he served as a senior executive, including as the Subject Matter Expert for Air and Space Warfare.

Throughout his government career, Stratton played a central role in initiating and managing three successive U.S. government UAP research efforts:

* AAWSAP (Advanced Aerospace Weapons System Applications Program)
* AATIP (Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program)
* UAPTF (Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force)

As head of these initiatives, Stratton led the initial internal Department of Defense investigation into the 2004 USS Nimitz "Tic Tac" incident. He was also instrumental in transitioning official terminology from "UFO" to "UAP" within government and defense policy contexts to reduce stigma and encourage formal reporting.

After retiring from government service, Stratton entered the private sector as an executive and consultant.

== Media Appearances and Claims ==
In October 2026, Stratton released his memoir, Out of the Shadows: Revealing the Truth About Non-Human Intelligence. In the book and subsequent public interviews, he stated that elements of the U.S. government and defense contractors have long been in possession of technology and material of non-human origin.

Official spokespersons for the Department of Defense and the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) have maintained that there is no verifiable evidence to support claims that the U.S. government possesses extraterrestrial technology or off-world craft.

data.title: Thomas Dörner
data.text:
Thomas Dörner

German physician-scientist and rheumatologist

Overview

Thomas Dörner is a German physician-scientist specializing in rheumatology, clinical immunology, hemostaseology, and autoimmune diseases. He is Professor of Innovative Therapies for Autoimmune Diseases at Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin, where he also leads Clinical Hemostaseology, and heads the B-Cell Memory research group at the German Rheumatism Research Center Berlin (DRFZ).

Education and career

Dörner studied medicine at Humboldt University and Charité in Berlin, receiving his medical doctorate in 1991 and completing his habilitation in rheumatology and clinical immunology in 1998. From 1996 to 1998, he conducted postdoctoral research at the University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center in Dallas. His specialist qualifications include internal medicine, rheumatology, hemostaseology, and transfusion medicine.

He has held senior academic and clinical positions at Charité and served as Professor and Head of Rheumatology at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich. Since 2009, he has held a professorship focused on innovative therapies for autoimmune diseases at Charité and has led its Clinical Hemostaseology service. His research group operates as a liaison between Charité and the DRFZ.

Research

Dörner’s research examines the roles of B lymphocytes, memory B cells, plasmablasts, and long-lived plasma cells in systemic autoimmune diseases, particularly systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), Sjögren’s disease, rheumatoid arthritis, and antiphospholipid syndrome. His early work used single-cell and immunoglobulin-gene methods to study B-cell receptor repertoires, receptor editing, and abnormal B-cell selection in lupus and Sjögren disease.

His group subsequently contributed to the characterization of circulating plasmablasts as correlates of disease activity, antigen-specific memory B-cell responses, extrafollicular immune activation, and distinct plasma-cell populations in human bone marrow. Later research addressed post-activated or functionally anergic B cells, immune-checkpoint pathways, plasma-cell heterogeneity, and CRISPR/Cas9-based manipulation of primary human B cells.

Clinical and translational work

Dörner has participated in the development and clinical evaluation of several B-cell- and immune-directed treatments. These include rituximab, epratuzumab, ianalumab, remibrutinib, baricitinib, iberdomide, and emerging approaches involving bispecific antibodies and CD19-directed CAR-T cells. He was the lead author of the initial clinical study of epratuzumab in patients with moderately active SLE, ianalumab (anti-BAFF-R) in Sjögren’s disease and led or contributed to other randomized studies of targeted therapies in lupus and Sjögren disease.

His clinical and translational work also encompasses autoimmune coagulation disorders, immune thrombocytopenia, antiphospholipid syndrome, vaccination responses in immunosuppressed patients, biomarker-guided monitoring, and the concept of deep B-cell targeting or “immune recalibration” in treatment-refractory autoimmune disease.

International collaborations and clinical standards

Dörner has contributed to international efforts to standardize the classification, assessment, and treatment of autoimmune disease. These activities include work on the 2019 EULAR/ACR classification criteria for SLE; the 2016 criteria followed by ESSDAI and ESSPRI disease-assessment instruments for Sjögren disease; the 2023 criteria for antiphospholipid syndrome; international definitions of remission and treat-to-target principles in lupus; and European treatment recommendations for SLE, Sjögren disease, antiphospholipid syndrome and related immune-mediated disorders.

Publications and recognition

Dörner has authored or co-authored an extensive body of original research, clinical studies, consensus statements, and review articles. His publications have addressed B-cell biology, autoantibody diagnostics, plasma-cell survival, biologic and targeted therapies, immune checkpoints, vaccination responses, and advanced cell-based treatments for autoimmune disease.

His honors include the American College of Rheumatology Senior Scholar Award, the Rudolf Schoen Prize of the German Society for Rheumatology, the Wolfgang Schultze Foundation Prize, and the Randy Fischer Prize. In 2023, he was named an Honorary Member of the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) for his contributions to rheumatology research, education, and international collaboration.

data.title: Duck, Duck, Gray Duck
data.text:
Duck, Duck, Gray Duck (also spelled Duck, Duck, Grey Duck) is a traditional children's game played primarily in the U.S. state of Minnesota. It is a regional variation of Duck, Duck, Goose, a children's chasing game played in schools, playgrounds, and recreational settings.

Although the two games share similar rules, the Minnesota variation commonly incorporates different duck colors, adding an element of anticipation and wordplay. The game has become a recognizable feature of Minnesota's regional culture and identity.

== Gameplay ==
Duck, Duck, Gray Duck is typically played by a group of children seated in a circle, facing inward. One player, designated as "it," walks around the outside of the circle, lightly tapping the other players on the head or shoulder while identifying them as ducks.

In the Minnesota variation, the player may use descriptive colors, such as "red duck," "blue duck," or "green duck," before selecting another player by saying "gray duck."

The player identified as the gray duck stands and attempts to catch the person who selected them before that person completes a circuit of the circle and occupies the empty space.

If the selecting player reaches the empty space without being caught, the selected player becomes the new person who is "it." Rules concerning what happens when the selecting player is caught may vary.

The use of different colors distinguishes this variation from the more widespread Duck, Duck, Goose game. Players may deliberately emphasize the beginning of a color, particularly the similar sounds of "green" and "gray," to create suspense.

== History and origins ==
The precise origins of Duck, Duck, Gray Duck are uncertain.

One theory attributes the Minnesota variation to Scandinavian immigration, particularly Swedish settlers who established communities throughout Minnesota during the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

Accounts of the game's possible Swedish origins describe two versions: Anka, Anka, Gås ("Duck, Duck, Goose") and Anka, Anka, Grå Anka ("Duck, Duck, Gray Duck"). According to this explanation, Swedish immigrants may have introduced the gray duck variation to Minnesota.

However, a direct historical connection between Swedish immigration and the Minnesota game's terminology has not been conclusively established.

A documented reference to "Duck, Duck, Grey Duck" appears in the 1936 educational publication Education in the Kindergarten, by Foster and Headley, both associated with kindergarten education in Minnesota. The book describes a circle game in which a player selects another child by saying "Grey Duck," prompting a chase.

This reference establishes that the gray duck terminology was in use in Minnesota educational settings by at least the 1930s, although it does not establish when or where the variation originated.

== Cultural significance in Minnesota ==
Duck, Duck, Gray Duck has become closely associated with Minnesota's cultural identity.

While most of the United States knows the game as Duck, Duck, Goose, many Minnesotans recognize Duck, Duck, Gray Duck as the familiar name from childhood. The distinction has become a subject of regional humor and friendly debate.

In March 2014, the Star Tribune published an article by Jeff Strickler examining the Minnesota variation and the public attention surrounding a map created by Christopher Pollard, a Minneapolis-area digital strategist. The map highlighted Minnesota's unusual terminology and gained attention through online sharing and coverage by BuzzFeed.

The discussion reflected the extent to which the game had become a symbol of Minnesota's regional distinctiveness.

The game has also been cited in discussions of Minnesota identity, alongside other regional traditions, expressions, and foods.

== Popular culture ==
The distinction between Duck, Duck, Gray Duck and Duck, Duck, Goose has appeared in Minnesota sports and popular media.

On October 9, 2017, Minnesota Vikings players performed a celebration based on the children's game following a touchdown against the Chicago Bears. The celebration attracted attention because the players used the more widely known "goose" terminology rather than Minnesota's "gray duck."

The event prompted renewed public discussion about the regional variation and inspired commemorative merchandise from a Minnesota apparel company.

Duck, Duck, Gray Duck has also appeared as a symbol of Minnesota identity in discussions surrounding the state's flag redesign. Some proposed flag designs submitted in 2023 incorporated references to the game.

== Relationship to Duck, Duck, Goose ==
Duck, Duck, Gray Duck and Duck, Duck, Goose share the same basic structure: players sit in a circle while one player walks around selecting another to give chase.

The primary differences are the terminology used to select the chasing player and the optional use of descriptive colors.

In Duck, Duck, Goose, the selecting player generally repeats "duck" until saying "goose." In Duck, Duck, Gray Duck, the selecting player may name differently colored ducks until announcing "gray duck."

The color-based variation allows for additional verbal misdirection and anticipation. Despite these differences, both games serve similar recreational purposes and involve running, listening, and group participation.

== See also ==

* Duck, Duck, Goose
* Culture of Minnesota
* Traditional children's games
* Scandinavian American culture

== References ==

# Brown, Heather. "Why Do Minnesotans Say 'Duck, Duck, Gray Duck?'" CBS Minnesota. 2017.
# "Duck, duck, goose." Wordorigins.org. Discussion of the historical terminology and a 1936 published reference.
# Rand, Michael. "Hey, Kyle Rudolph: Around here we say, 'duck, duck, gray duck.'" Star Tribune. October 9, 2017.
# Harlow, Tim. "No goose here: Minneapolis company markets Vikings 'Duck, Duck, Gray Duck' shirt." Star Tribune. October 11, 2017.
# Yuen, Laura. "Duck, duck, what? The moments you knew your kid was Minnesotan." Star Tribune. September 28, 2021.

data.title: Mufti Khalil ur Rehman
data.text:
----

Mufti Khalil ur Rehman (1923 – 1977) was a Pakistani publishing administrator who served as the General Manager of the Taj Company in Lahore, a major publisher of Quranic literature in South Asia. He managed the company's executive administration and editorial operations.

== Early life and education ==
He was born in 1923 in Lohianwala, Gujranwala, British India. He did a Bachelor of Arts degree and a Munshi Fazil (Persian Honors) qualification from the University of the Punjab in 1945.

== Career ==
He joined the Taj Company in 1946, spending a professional career of 31 years with the firm, where he primarily served as General Manager based in Lahore. During his tenure, he traveled to various Arab and European countries to study Arabic calligraphy methods and modern printing technologies, focusing particularly on updates from Germany.

From 1966 to 1976, the publishing house undertook a multi-year project under his administrative guidance to produce a standardized 30-para collection of embroidered Quranic textiles crafted with gold and silver thread work, costing a total of 239,831 rupees. The project utilized 1,228 yards of green velvet across 1,228 pages, featuring threadwork containing 5% gold and 95% silver produced by United Industries Hyderabad. The primary calligraphy was executed by Hafiz Muhammad Azam of Mozang between July 1966 and November 1967, under the supervision of Hafiz Nazeer Ahmad and Mian Ata Muhammad. Following its completion, the embroidered collection was transitioned to permanent public display within the Tabarrukat-e-Qur'an Gallery located at the Badshahi Mosque museum in Lahore.

data.text:

Ros Nwar (formerly known as Sediem) is a Mauritian electronic music producer and DJ. Initially gaining recognition under his alias Sediem within the Moombahton genre—receiving support from major international acts such as Diplo and Afro Bros—he later transitioned into producing House, Afro House, and Tech House under the moniker Ros Nwar.

=== Career ===

==== Early Career as Sediem (Moombahton Era) ====
Beginning his career under the artist name Sediem, he focused on Moombahton, a fusion genre combining Dutch house and reggaeton. During this period, his productions gained traction within the global dance music scene and earned early support from prominent figures in the industry, including American producer and DJ Diplo, as well as the Dutch production duo Afro Bros.

==== Rebranding to Ros Nwar and House Music ====
After establishing a foundation in Moombahton, he rebranded under the stage name Ros Nwar, shifting his musical direction toward House, Afro House, and Tech House. Incorporating rhythmic percussion, deep basslines, and melodic electronic elements, his work under Ros Nwar reflects the evolving sounds of modern underground and melodic house scenes.

In October 2026, Ros Nwar collaborated with fellow producer Mahé to release an unofficial remix of ANOTR's track "Talk To You". [ref: ]

=== Musical Style and Influences ===
Ros Nwar’s sound is characterized by a blend of groove-driven House beats, Afro House rhythms, and Tech House arrangements. His transition from Moombahton to House music represents an evolution toward deeper, dancefloor-oriented club tracks while maintaining energetic rhythmic roots.

data.title: Flamingo (Youtuber)
data.text:
Albert Spencer Aretz (Born June 11th, 1997), more known as Flamingo or MrFlimFlam, is an Amarican YouTuber. His videos focus on Gaming and Comedy.

== Early life and education ==
Albert Spencer Aretz was born on 11 June 1997. He was born in New Jersey and raised in Sarasota, Florida. He has kept his parents private only revealing his dad's name that is Ronald Gerard Aretz. Albert started to play videogames at the age of 10. [ref: Albert Aretz, Albertsstuff Wiki]

== YouTube career ==

=== Early years ===
Aretz initially uploaded Roblox videos under the name ROBLOXHub. In July 2012, he created the AlbertsStuff YouTube channel. He began regularly uploading to the channel in 2014. The AlbertsStuff channel became known for Roblox gameplay, commentary, dark humor, and unscripted interactions with other players. The channel eventually gained more than one million subscribers. Aretz's early content helped establish the style that would later become associated with his Flamingo channel. [ref: The Flamingo / Albert Q&A, Shorty]

=== Flamingo ===
In July 2017, Aretz created the Flamingo YouTube channel. The channel allowed him to focus on a more advertiser-friendly style of content while continuing to make Roblox videos. As Flamingo grew, Aretz gradually stopped regularly uploading to AlbertsStuff and focused his attention on Flamingo. The Flamingo channel reached one million subscribers in early 2018. It continued growing rapidly and passed 11 million subscribers in 2021. The channel has since grown to more than 14 million subscribers and billions of views. [ref: Flamingo (channel), Albertsstuff Wiki]

=== Content and style ===
Flamingo primarily produces Roblox gaming videos. His videos often combine gameplay with comedy and commentary. Common elements of his videos include:

* Roblox gameplay
* Comedy
* Roleplay
* Challenges
* Player interactions
* Reactions
* Memes
* Improvised situations

Aretz is known for changing his approach depending on the Roblox game he is playing. His videos can range from playing popular Roblox experiences to testing unusual games and interacting with random players. His style relies heavily on spontaneous humor and exaggerated reactions.

=== AlbertsStuff ===
AlbertsStuff was one of Aretz's earliest major YouTube channels. The channel became popular for its Roblox videos and more mature style of comedy. As Aretz's career developed, he shifted his focus toward Flamingo. In 2020, he removed or made private much of the older AlbertsStuff content because he no longer wanted the older material publicly available. The change allowed Aretz to concentrate on Flamingo and its more family-friendly style.

=== Flamingo's growth ===
Flamingo became one of the largest Roblox-focused YouTube channels. The channel's growth was helped by Aretz's frequent uploads and his focus on entertainment rather than competitive Roblox gameplay. In 2020, Flamingo was recognized as one of YouTube's top ten most-viewed gaming creators. The channel continued to gain millions of subscribers during the following years. By 2026, third-party tracking sites listed Flamingo at more than 14 million subscribers and over 12 billion views.

=== Face reveal ===
Aretz initially created videos without showing his face. He later began appearing on camera, with his face reveal becoming part of his transition toward the modern Flamingo channel. His videos have since included both gameplay footage and footage of himself.

=== Roblox ===
Roblox has remained the main focus of Aretz's online career. He began playing the platform in 2008 and has continued creating Roblox content for more than a decade. His videos have covered a wide range of Roblox experiences, including roleplay games, obstacle courses, social games, horror games, simulators, and games created by members of the Roblox community. Aretz has also used Roblox to create recurring characters and comedic situations that appear throughout his videos.

== Collaborations ==
Aretz has collaborated with other Roblox creators throughout his career. One of his notable recurring collaborators is Jayingee, who has appeared in videos with him. In November 2021, Aretz also appeared as a guard in MrBeast's real-life recreation of Squid Game.

data.title: Kristian Bainey
data.text:
Kristian Bainey is an author, educator, and information technology consultant based in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada. He is the founder of K-PIC Systems Inc. and the author of AI-Driven Project Management (2024), a book on applying artificial intelligence and ChatGPT to project management, published by Wiley. The book was reviewed in PM World Journal and by the IEEE Professional Communication Society, among others. [ref: Sadeghi, Soheila. [https://pmworldjournal.com/article/ai-driven-project-management Book review, "AI-Driven Project Management"], PM World Journal, June 2024.] [ref: Tiandini, Novian. [https://procomm.ieee.org/book-reviews-ai-emerging-technologies/ Book review of AI-Driven Project Management], in "Book Reviews: AI and Emerging Technologies", IEEE Professional Communication Society.] In 2025, he won an ASTech Award in the Social Innovation and Educational Technologies category [ref: ASTech Awards. [https://astech.ca/2025-astech-award-finalists-collage "2025 ASTech Award Winners and Finalists"] (Social Innovation and Educational Technologies: winner, Kristian Bainey of K-PIC Systems Inc).] and received an honorary diploma from NorQuest College. [ref: NorQuest College. [https://www.norquest.ca/about-us/news-and-events/stories/norquest-announces-2025-honorary-diploma-recipients/ "NorQuest announces 2025 Honorary Diploma recipients"], May 15, 2025.]

== Career ==

Bainey has more than 15 years of experience in information technology, digital transformation, and artificial intelligence, according to NorQuest College. He is the founder and principal consultant of K-PIC Systems, an Edmonton company working in artificial intelligence, technology, project management, and education. [ref: K-PIC Systems. [https://k-picsystems.com/about "About K-PIC Systems"] (Kristian Bainey, Founder and Principal Consultant).] NorQuest describes him as the company's chief executive officer.

He served as president of the PMI Northern Alberta Chapter in 2023 to 2024. [ref: Wiley-VCH. [https://www.wiley-vch.de/en/areas-interest/finance-economics-law/ai-driven-project-management-978-1-394-23221-5 "AI-Driven Project Management"] (publisher book page, including author biography).] [ref: ASTech Awards. [https://astech.ca/archives/indexofpastwinners "Index of Past Winners"] (entry: Leadership in AI-Driven Project Management Innovation, Kristian Bainey).] According to his speaker biography for DAMA Edmonton's 2025 conference, he co-authored the Project Management Institute's AI Essentials for Project Professionals guide, contributed to PMI's first global generative AI course in 2023, and has appeared on PMI's Projectified podcast. [ref: DAMA Edmonton. [https://www.dama-edmonton.org/_files/ugd/7ef714_6427e53f9c6048839c46b6c7e142d708.pdf "DAMA 2025 Conference Speakers and Biographies"] (Kristian Bainey speaker biography and workshop listing).]

ASTech states that Bainey created an artificial intelligence in project management curriculum that is taught at the Northern Alberta Institute of Technology (NAIT). His book is listed as a required learning resource in NAIT course outlines for its artificial intelligence project management courses. [ref: Northern Alberta Institute of Technology. [https://academictools.nait.ca/CourseOutline/DownloadCourseOutline?id=49695 Course outline] listing AI-Driven Project Management by Kristian Bainey as a required learning resource.] He also teaches management information systems (MSYS 200) at MacEwan University's School of Business. He presented a workshop on AI-driven project management at DAMA Edmonton's 2025 conference.

== Books ==

=== AI-Driven Project Management (2024) ===

AI-Driven Project Management: Harnessing the Power of Artificial Intelligence and ChatGPT to Achieve Peak Productivity and Success was published by Wiley in April 2024 (384 pages, ISBN 978-1394232215). [ref: Google Books. [https://books.google.com/books/about/AI_Driven_Project_Management.html?id=BBAg0AEACAAJ "AI-Driven Project Management: Harnessing the Power of Artificial Intelligence and ChatGPT to Achieve Peak Productivity and Success"].] The book covers the use of AI and ChatGPT across predictive, agile, and hybrid project approaches, and focuses on four areas: decision making and risk management, optimization and efficiency, innovation and strategic insights, and ethics, bias reduction, and quality control.

The book was reviewed by Soheila Sadeghi in PM World Journal in June 2024, by Novian Tiandini for the IEEE Professional Communication Society, by Samant Kumar in AI Time Journal, [ref: Kumar, Samant. [https://aitimejournal.com/ai-driven-project-management Book review, "AI Driven Project Management"], AI Time Journal.] and by Ipek Bozkurt for the American Society for Engineering Management. [ref: Bozkurt, Ipek. [https://www.asem.org/blog/13448246 Book review, "AI-Driven Project Management by Kristian Bainey"], American Society for Engineering Management.]

A Chinese edition, AI qudong de xiangmu guanli (ISBN 978-7-121-50786-1), translated by Zhao Hong, was published by the Publishing House of Electronics Industry in 2025. [ref: Douban Books. [https://book.douban.com/subject/37471420/ Chinese edition listing, AI qudong de xiangmu guanli], Publishing House of Electronics Industry, 2025, ISBN 978-7-121-50786-1.]

=== PMP Project Management Professional Exam Study Guide, 11th edition ===

Bainey is the sole author of the 11th edition of the PMP Project Management Professional Exam Study Guide: 2026 Exam Update, published by Sybex, an imprint of Wiley. Kim Heldman authored the earlier editions of the guide. The edition is aligned with the 2026 PMP Examination Content Outline and the eighth edition of the PMBOK Guide. [ref: Bookshop.org UK. [https://uk.bookshop.org/p/books/pmp-project-management-professional-exam-study-guide-2026-exam-update-kristian-bainey/c37cb1501fdf1937 "PMP Project Management Professional Exam Study Guide, 2026 Exam Update, a book by Kristian Bainey"].]

=== Other writing ===

He contributed a chapter on generative AI prompts for environmental impact assessment to Green PMO: Leading the Sustainable Project Revolution (2024).

== Awards and recognition ==

In 2025, Bainey won the ASTech Award in the Social Innovation and Educational Technologies category for "Leadership in AI-Driven Project Management Innovation", entered under K-PIC Systems Inc.

Also in 2025, NorQuest College conferred an honorary diploma on Bainey. He was one of four recipients that year. [ref: NorQuest College. [http://www.norquest.ca/student-resources/convocation/honorary-diploma/ "Honorary Diploma"] (past winners list, 2025 recipient Kristian Bainey).]

data.title: Lubna Speitan
data.text:
Lubna Speitan is a British-Palestinian award winning contemporary artist and activist. She is a founding member of the Greenwich Palestine Alliance and a long-standing campaigner for Palestinian rights [ref: ] [ref: GREENWICH PALESTINE ALLIANCE, GREENWICH PALESTINE ALLIANCE]. She has been involved in a legal campaign concerning Greenwich Council's investments and Palestine [ref: Campaigner takes Greenwich Council to court over Israel investments, The Greenwich Wire].

Speitan is based in London and is specialising in Abstracts, Landscapes, Seascapes, Nightscapes and Portraits although she has put her painting career largely on hold for more than two years while undertaking activism [ref: Biography, lubnaspeitan].

== Activism ==

=== Greenwich Palestine Alliance ===
Speitan is a founding member of the Greenwich Palestine Alliance, a London-based grassroots organisation campaigning on Palestinian issues. The organisation has organised political education, demonstrations and campaigns directed at institutions in the Royal Borough of Greenwich [ref: ].

=== Pension-fund campaign ===
In December 2024, Speitan submitted a public question to Greenwich Council concerning support for Palestinian residents affected by the conflict in the Middle East. In 2025 and 2026, Speitan pursued a judicial review backed by the Public Interest Law Centre concerning the investment policy of Greenwich Council’s pension fund. By early 2026, the council conceded that its stance on lacking legal power for divestment was unlawful, leading to a policy review [ref: Greenwich Council concedes pension fund investment policy was “unlawful” following Israel divestment challenge: law centre, www.localgovernmentlawyer.co.uk] [ref: Greenwich Council admits pension investments in Israel are unlawful following legal challenge, Morning Star] [ref: Gaza activist taking Greenwich Council to court claiming it unlawfully invested £60m in Israel, The Jewish Chronicle] [ref: ].

The dispute concerned a clause in Greenwich Council’s Local Government Pension Scheme investment strategy that stated that the council could not exclude investments in order to pursue boycotts, divestment and sanctions against foreign countries and UK defence industries. According to data from the Palestine Solidarity Campaign, Greenwich’s pension fund has invested more than £61.8m in companies with Israeli interests. Following the legal challenge, the council accepted that the relevant provision was legally erroneous and agreed to remove it and consult on its responsible-investment policy [ref: Greenwich Council concedes pension fund investment policy was “unlawful” following Israel divestment challenge: law centre, www.localgovernmentlawyer.co.uk].

Speitan said that the campaign arose partly from her family’s experience in Gaza and the West Bank. In an interview with the Public Interest Law Centre, she described the campaign as an attempt to apply consistent human-rights principles to local-government investment decisions and drew comparisons with local-government divestment campaigns during the South African anti-apartheid movement: "Our own local history proves this: divestment from South Africa was a crucial, tangible step Greenwich council took against apartheid. It showed local government can be a powerful lever for global justice" [ref: ].

=== Art ===
Speitan is a contemporary artist whose work has been exhibited in London. Her website records participation in the FLUX Exhibition in London in 2023, an exhibition involving dozens of contemporary artists [ref: Biography, lubnaspeitan].

In December 2025, she held what her website described as her “final studio exhibition” at Thames-Side Studios in Woolwich. The exhibition presented remaining works from her artistic career, with proceeds intended to support her campaigning through the Greenwich Palestine Alliance and Trade Unionists for Palestine.

data.title: Murad Teymurov
data.text:
Murad Teymurov is an Azerbaijani academic, researcher, lecturer, and civil servant specializing in economic sciences, labor relations, and labor and social policy. He is a PhD candidate at Sapienza University of Rome and is currently a lecturer at Azerbaijan State University of Economics, as well as a researcher at the University of Chicago. Teymurov has published over 10 academic articles and contributed to public policy analysis, financial education program development, public-private partnership initiatives, and policy research on AI integration in governance.

==Early Life and Education==

Murad Teymurov was born on January 3, 1997, in Azerbaijan. He completed his early education in Baku before enrolling at Azerbaijan State University of Economics, where he earned a BA in Management in 2018. During his undergraduate studies, he participated in the SABAH program, a specialized initiative for talented students. He was also recognized among the Rector's TOP 15 academic excellence awardees and received internships and scholarships from leading companies in Azerbaijan.

In 2021, he completed a Master of Public Administration (MPP) from the Public Administration Academy of Azerbaijan, graduating with honors. He then pursued a Master of Science in Economics and Communication for Management and Innovation at Sapienza University of Rome, graduating in 2022. During his time at Sapienza, he was awarded a scholarship from Italy's Ministry of University and Research and was selected for double degree programs with the University of Bucharest and MiGIMO University.

Additionally, Teymurov participated in the Erasmus Exchange Program, studying economics and finance at Charles University in Prague. Currently, he is pursuing a PhD in Economics at Sapienza University of Rome while simultaneously studying for a Master of Public Policy (MPP) at the Harris School of Public Policy, University of Chicago.

==Career==

Teymurov began his career in the private sector, working at well-known companies such as Azerbaijan Supermarket LLC (Bravo), Azercell LLC, and Ekvita LLC.

In 2021, he transitioned to the public sector, working at the Azerbaijan State Labor Inspectorate Service.

Since 2022, Teymurov has been a lecturer and dissertation supervisor at Azerbaijan State University of Economics, teaching MBA students in the areas of Human Resource Management (HRM), Human Resource Information Systems (HRIS), Innovation and Product Development, and Labor Legislation. Under his academic supervision, several students have successfully defended their theses.

Currently, he is a researcher at the University of Chicago, Simultaneously, he is pursuing his PhD at Sapienza University of Rome and studying for a Master of Public Policy at the University of Chicago's Harris School of Public Policy. Teymurov has published over 10 academic articles and contributed to public policy analysis, financial education program development, public-private partnership initiatives, and policy research on AI integration in governance

==Research and publications==

* Teymurov has published over 10 academic articles, with a primary focus on public-private partnerships, labor policy, and economic development. His notable publications include:
* 'The Role of Public-Private Partnerships in Social Economic Development: Case Azerbaijan,' published in Ekonomicheskie Nauki, Moscow, Russia (2023).
* 'Application of Artificial Intelligence in Public-Private Sector Partnerships,' published in Science and Innovative Technologies, Baku, Azerbaijan (2023).
* 'Public-Private Sector Partnership in the Energy Sector: Case Europe,' presented at the III International Scientific-Practical Conference, Saratov, Russia (2024).
* 'Public-Private Sector Synergy for Promoting Development in Social Endeavors,' published in Economy of Ukraine (2024).
* 'Cooperation of the State and Private Sector in Social Projects: A Perspective for Development,' published in Journal of Labor and Social Relations, Baku, Azerbaijan (2024).
* Additionally, he has contributed to policy analysis on labor legislation and innovation management, aligning his research with his academic focus in economics and public policy.

data.title: Bomma Venu Goud
data.text:
Bomma Venu Goud is an Indian film director, screenwriter and producer associated with Telugu-language cinema. He is credited with directing and producing the historical film project Yedu Tharala Yudham, which explores the Telangana armed struggle. His filmmaking credits also include the Telugu short film Andhera – The Darkness.

== Early life ==
According to his FilmFreeway profile, Bomma Venu Goud was born on 29 December 1990 in Nirmal, in present-day Telangana, India.

== Career ==

=== Early work ===
Venu Goud's IMDb biography states that he began his career in the direction department of filmmaker Ram Gopal Varma. [ref: Bomma Venu Goud, IMDb] It lists his involvement in projects including Attack, Secret and Mogilipuvvu. These reported credits require confirmation from independent reporting or official film credits.

His FilmFreeway profile identifies him as the writer and director of the Telugu short film Andhera – The Darkness.

=== Bomma Cinema Company ===
Venu Goud is associated with Bomma Cinema Company, a Telugu film production banner.

In September 2023, 10TV Telugu reported that the historical filmYedu Tharala Yudham was being produced under the banner, with Venu Goud serving as both director and producer. [ref: ]

=== Yedu Tharala Yudham ===
Yedu Tharala Yudham (Telugu: ఏడుతరాల యుద్ధం) is a Telugu-language historical film project set against the background of the Telangana armed struggle.

The film's narrative concerns the political and social conflicts associated with the late Nizam period and the events surrounding 1948.

On 18 September 2023, 10TV Telugu reported the release of a promotional glimpse of the film. The report identified Venu Goud as its director and producer and stated that the first shooting schedule had been completed.

The reported cast included Kiran Sharma, Arun, Suresh Bheemagani, Shiva Varkala, Navaneeth Jha, Anil, Yashika and Karan Singh Tagore, among others. The report also identified Pawan Kumar as the music director.

On 17 September 2025, NTV Telugu published another report concerning the film's announcement on Telangana Liberation Day. The article described the project as a historical drama set in 1948 and reported that Venu Goud would also undertake editing and visual-effects work. [ref: Yedu-Tarala-Yuddham: తెలంగాణ విమోచన దినోత్సవం నాడు ‘ఏడు తరాల యుద్ధం’ అనౌన్స్మెంట్, NTV Telugu]

The 2025 report identified Subhash Anand as the music composer and described the project as being in pre-production at that time.

== Filmography ==
Andhera – The Darkness

A Telugu-language short film credited to Bomma Venu Goud as writer and director in his FilmFreeway profile. The film is reported to have been released in 2018.

Yedu Tharala Yudham

A Telugu-language historical film project directed and produced by Bomma Venu Goud. Its development and promotional activities were reported by 10TV Telugu in 2023 and NTV Telugu in 2025.

data.title: UserFerry – WordPress User Export and Import Plugin
data.text:
----

UserFerry is a WordPress plugin designed to export, import, and manage WordPress user data, including standard user information and custom profile fields. It supports multiple file formats and provides tools for transferring user records between WordPress installations, maintaining backups, and performing bulk user data operations.

The plugin includes user filtering, custom field detection, reusable export templates, import field mapping, batch processing, and export/import history management.

== Overview ==
{| class="wikitable"
!Information
!Details
|-
|Plugin Name
|UserFerry
|-
|Category

|Version

|-

|-
|Contributor
|[user]
|}

== Features and Functionality ==

=== 1. WordPress User Export ===
UserFerry allows administrators to export WordPress user information into structured files. [ref: ]

Users can be selected based on their assigned roles, registration dates, or individual accounts. The export interface also includes search, sorting, and a live user counter. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

Administrators can select which fields to include and arrange their order before generating the export file.

=== 2. Multiple Export Formats ===
The plugin supports four data export formats:

* CSV: Suitable for spreadsheets, databases, and bulk data management.
* Excel (XLSX): Provides formatted worksheets with frozen headers and filtering options.
* JSON: Suitable for structured data exchange and development workflows.
* XML: Supports structured information exchange between systems.

=== 3. Custom User Field Support ===
UserFerry detects custom profile fields stored in WordPress user metadata. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

The plugin is designed to work with fields created by systems such as Advanced Custom Fields (ACF), Ultimate Member, WooCommerce, BuddyPress, Meta Box, and JetEngine. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

Administrators can scan available custom fields and select which information should be included in exported files. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

=== 4. User Import and Migration ===
UserFerry provides functionality for importing user information from CSV, XLSX, JSON, and XML files. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

Its import interface supports automatic column matching and manual field mapping. Administrators can create new users, update existing records, or skip matching users. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

Existing accounts can be identified through email addresses, usernames, or user IDs. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

This functionality can be used when transferring user records between WordPress websites or updating user information in bulk. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

=== 5. Reusable Export Templates ===
The plugin includes a template management system that allows administrators to save export configurations. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

Templates preserve selected fields and export settings, reducing the need to repeat the same configuration for recurring exports. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

Saved templates can be edited, duplicated, deleted, or used to start another export. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

=== 6. Batch Processing ===
UserFerry processes import and export operations in batches. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

This approach is intended to reduce server timeouts and memory consumption when working with large numbers of WordPress users. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

The administration interface displays progress information during these operations. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

=== 7. Export and Import History ===
The plugin maintains a history of completed export and import operations. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

Administrators can review previous operations and download retained export files. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

Automatic file cleanup settings are available to manage stored export data. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

=== 8. Security and Data Protection ===
UserFerry includes several safeguards for handling WordPress user information. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

These include permission-based access, protected export file storage, import validation, role assignment restrictions, and spreadsheet formula injection protection. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

The plugin also includes a configuration check intended to identify situations where exported files might be publicly accessible. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

== Installation ==
UserFerry can be installed through the WordPress administration dashboard. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

# Log in to the WordPress administration panel.
# Navigate to Plugins → Add New Plugin → Upload Plugin.
# Upload the UserFerry ZIP file.
# Click Install Now.
# Activate the plugin.
# Open the UserFerry menu in the WordPress dashboard.

After activation, administrators can access the Dashboard, Export Users, Import Users, Templates, History, Settings, and Documentation sections. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

== Video Tutorial ==
A video tutorial is available demonstrating the UserFerry plugin. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

Watch the UserFerry tutorial on YouTube:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TNJCre6AAvk

The plugin also includes a video guide within its Documentation interface. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

== Applications ==
UserFerry may be used for several WordPress administration tasks, including: [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

* Migrating registered users between WordPress installations.
* Exporting WooCommerce customer profile information.
* Maintaining structured backups of user records.
* Updating user information through spreadsheet files.
* Transferring custom user metadata.
* Generating recurring user data reports.

== Technical Information ==
UserFerry is distributed under the GNU General Public License version 2 or later. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

The plugin requires WordPress 6.2 or later and PHP 7.4 or later, according to its included documentation. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

The supplied plugin package identifies version 1.0.0 as its stable release. [ref: UserFerry – Export & Import Users, WordPress.org]

data.title: Sakibphobia
data.text:
----

Sakibphobia is a social and psychological construct that refers to the constant fear, distaste, or hostility against people who seem to be better, more talented, more skilled, or more successful than the self. According to the Bangladeshi interdisciplinary scholar S M Nazmuz Sakib, the phenomenon derives from toxic comparative theory. He came up with the term and defined it as a form of phobia in his working paper titled S M Nazmuz Sakib's Toxic Comparative Theory: An Analysis of Sakibphobia that was published on the Cambridge University Press website on 12 April 2023.

In toxic comparative theory, which Sakib proposed as an alternative to normal social comparison theory, the victim is caught in a cycle of self-hatred and anxiety because of comparing him/herself to a person that seems to be better in terms of success. Contemporary societies, social media, education system, and business environment encourage this type of social competition, thus provoking feelings of inadequacy in individuals. To provide his theory with mathematical support, Sakib formulated an equation for estimating the extent of Sakibphobia in an individual or community.

Following the publication of the working paper, numerous peer-reviewed and preprint papers were published that addressed different aspects of Sakibphobia. In 2024, a journal article published at SSRN investigated the phenomenon's effects on people's mental health using the paradigms of structural functionalism, symbolic interactionism, and conflict theories. A study published in 2025 used qualitative data collection techniques to test whether toxic comparison fits into sociological models. In 2026, another paper discussed similarities between Sakibphobia, Emersonian self-reliance, and Sankara's Advaita Vedanta.

There have been critics of the concept since its inception. They claim that it pathologises a normal psychological process that can be explained with existing psychological disorders such as social anxiety disorder or low self-esteem. Moreover, some people find fault with the use of Sakib's name for the newly invented condition, arguing that it makes it difficult to separate scientific research from promoting the scholar himself. However, supporters say that there is a need for new terminology in this case.

SINQU Esports is a Finnish esports organization based in Kannus, Central Ostrobothnia, Finland. Founded in 2025, the organization competes in Counter-Strike 2 and operates a main team and a junior team, SINQU REHTI. [ref: E-urheilu kärvistelee talousvaikeuksissa, mutta pikkuinen seura Kannuksesta tähtää silti maailmalle, Yle]

SINQU Esports was founded in Kannus in 2025. The organization focuses on Counter-Strike 2 and has competed in domestic and international tournaments.

In December 2025, SINQU participated in the DraculaN 4 tournament in Romania. According to Yle, the team defeated the European team Nexus during the event.

The organization has also developed a junior programme. In 2026, its junior team, SINQU REHTI, won the second season of NUKE-Liiga and participated in Urban Riga Open Season 5 in Latvia. [ref: NUKE-Liiga Season 2, Liquipedia] [ref: Urban Riga Open Season 5, HLTV]
