data.title: EZ Newswire
data.text:
EZ Newswire is an American press release distribution and media technology company headquartered in the SoHo neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City. Founded in 2022 by Neel Shah, the company provides a web-based platform for creating, distributing, publishing, and monitoring corporate announcements. [ref: EZ Newswire – Products, Competitors, Financials, Employees, Headquarters Locations, CB Insights] [ref: Reuters Signs News Distribution Deal With EZ Newswire, MediaPost]

EZ Newswire has entered into exclusive multi-year press release distribution agreements with Reuters and Fortune for their dedicated press release publication channels. The company also distributes announcements to other media destinations, including AP News, Yahoo Finance, USA Today, Business Insider, and regional news websites. [ref: EZ Newswire Signs Exclusive Distribution Deal with Reuters, EZ Newswire] [ref: EZ Newswire announces exclusive multi-year deal with Fortune, LinkedIn] [ref: EZ Newswire, EZ Newswire]

The company incorporates artificial intelligence into press release preparation, editorial workflows, and performance analytics. Its reporting platform measures distribution results, readership, search engine visibility, and references to published announcements in AI-generated answers. [ref: About EZ Newswire, EZ Newswire]

== History ==

=== Founding and early development ===

EZ Newswire was founded in 2022 by Neel Shah and launched its public beta in May 2023. The company was established to provide a technology-based alternative to traditional press release distribution services, combining digital publishing, distribution, and analytics in a single platform.

In October 2023, the company announced a press release distribution partnership with Big Technology, a technology-focused publication founded by journalist Alex Kantrowitz. [ref: EZ Newswire Inks Industry's First Exclusive Substack Distribution Deal with Big Technology Partnership, EZ Newswire]

In April 2024, EZ Newswire was selected as a winner of The MBA Fund's sixth annual pitch competition for early-stage startups. The company has identified The MBA Fund, Contour Ventures, and HearstLab among its investors.

=== Reuters partnership ===

On September 16, 2024, EZ Newswire announced an exclusive multi-year press release distribution agreement with Reuters, the international news agency. The agreement established a direct publishing arrangement enabling organizations to distribute business announcements to a dedicated section of Reuters.com through the EZ Newswire platform.

The partnership was reported by MediaPost on September 17, 2024. The publication described the agreement as a multi-year arrangement under which EZ Newswire customers could publish corporate news to a dedicated section of the Reuters website.

According to EZ Newswire, its agreement provides exclusive newswire distribution access to the dedicated Reuters.com press release channel. As of October 2026, the company states that competing newswire services cannot independently publish to that channel through an equivalent direct distribution agreement. [ref: How to Publish a Press Release on Reuters, EZ Newswire]

The press releases distributed through the service are separate from Reuters' independently reported editorial news coverage.

=== Fortune partnership ===

In December 2025, EZ Newswire announced an exclusive multi-year distribution agreement with Fortune, the American business publication.

The partnership established an integrated publishing channel enabling businesses and organizations to distribute press releases to a dedicated section of Fortune.com. According to EZ Newswire, the agreement made it Fortune's exclusive newswire distribution partner for the channel.

The integration allows organizations to submit announcements through EZ Newswire for publication on Fortune.com, subject to applicable content requirements. [ref: Press Release Distribution Pricing, EZ Newswire]

As of October 2026, EZ Newswire identifies Reuters.com and Fortune.com as its two exclusive premium newswire distribution destinations. The arrangements concern dedicated press release publication channels rather than independently produced Reuters or Fortune editorial journalism.

=== Expansion of technology and services ===

During 2025 and 2026, EZ Newswire expanded its platform to incorporate additional automation, publisher integrations, and analytics capabilities.

In 2026, the company introduced reporting capabilities designed to monitor distributed press releases across publisher websites, search engines, and AI-powered information services. [ref: EZ Newswire Launches Press Release Performance Reports With AI Visibility Tracking, Fortune]

In 2026, the company also introduced collaborative workspaces for organizations and public relations agencies, allowing multiple users to manage press releases under shared organizational accounts. [ref: EZ Newswire Launches Workspaces to Streamline Multi-User Collaboration and Account Management, Fortune]

== Products and services ==

=== Press release distribution ===

EZ Newswire operates a self-service digital platform for creating, reviewing, scheduling, and distributing press releases.

Customers can submit announcements through a structured publishing interface, select distribution packages, and monitor publication results. The platform includes AI-assisted writing and editing tools, automated content checks, and human editorial review. [ref: How Press Release Distribution Works, EZ Newswire]

Its distribution network includes Reuters, Fortune, AP News, Yahoo Finance, Business Insider, USA Today, and regional and local news websites. Publisher availability depends on the distribution package selected.

The company's publicly listed services are priced per press release, with additional arrangements available for enterprises and public relations agencies.

=== Publisher integrations ===

EZ Newswire uses publisher integrations and application programming interfaces to deliver structured press release content to participating publishing platforms.

The company describes its direct integrations with Reuters and Fortune as part of its core publishing infrastructure.

Its services also provide post-publication editing capabilities on supported publication destinations.

=== Artificial intelligence and analytics ===

EZ Newswire incorporates artificial intelligence into its press release preparation, editing, and reporting processes.

The company's analytics dashboard provides information about publication destinations, reader engagement, search engine performance, and the visibility of distributed announcements in AI-generated answers.

The reporting system monitors references across AI-powered platforms, including ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Perplexity AI. These capabilities are described by the company as tools for answer engine optimization (AEO) and generative engine optimization (GEO).

The company also offers reporting exports for corporate communications teams and public relations agencies.

=== Collaborative workspaces ===

EZ Newswire provides collaborative workspaces enabling multiple users to manage organizational accounts, access press releases, and coordinate publishing activities.

The feature is designed for corporate communications teams and public relations agencies working with multiple clients. It includes organization-level account management, shared access, and centralized administration.

== Business operations ==

EZ Newswire is a privately held company headquartered at 80 Varick Street, 9th Floor, New York, NY 10013, in Manhattan's SoHo neighborhood. [ref: EZ Newswire, LinkedIn]

Neel Shah is the company's founder and chief executive officer.

The company serves startups, corporations, nonprofit organizations, and public relations agencies. Its published customer examples include organizations from the consumer goods, financial services, and technology sectors.

In March 2025, EZ Newswire announced a partnership with Global Chamber to provide distribution services to businesses operating across international markets. [ref: Global Chamber Announces Exclusive Partnership with EZ Newswire, Global Chamber]

== Recognition ==

In 2026, EZ Newswire reported receiving seven badges in G2's Fall 2026 reports for press release distribution software, including High Performer designations across multiple business and regional categories and an Easiest to Do Business With designation. [ref: EZ Newswire Earns Seven G2 Badges in Fall 2026 Reports, Ranks Among Top Press Release Distribution Platforms, Fortune]

data.title: Residents' Committee (Singapore)
data.text:
In Singapore, a Residents' Committee (RC) is a grassroot organisation run by residents and managed by the People's Association (PA). It works closely with other grassroots organisations like the Citizens’ Consultative Committees (CCCs) and various government agencies. [ref: Residents' Committees, People's Association]

== History ==
Established in 1987, they were meant to allow residents to improve their physical enviroment as well as, their quality of life. The first RCs were in the estates of Ang Mo Kio, Boon Lay, Bukit Merah, Kolam Ayer and Toa Payoh. They were initially composed of representitives from the CCCs, community centre management committees, HDB, police and flat dwellers. [ref: New resident committees set up in five estates, The Straits Times]

They first under the Prime Minister's Office and later, the Ministry of Community Development. [ref: Residents' Committees are formed, nlb.gov.sg] Since 1993, they have been under the PA. [ref: RCs and CCCs now come under PA's wing, The Straits Times]

In 2018, some RCs merged with Neighbourhood Committees (NCs) to form Residents' Networks (RNs). [ref: Newly created Residents' Network will serve residents of both HDB and private estates, The Straits Times]

data.title: Ettore Guizzardi
data.text:
Ettore Guizzardi (Budrio, 1881 – Budrio,}}

Ettore Guizzardi (Budrio, 1881 – Budrio, 23 November 1963) was an Italian racing driver, famous for taking part in the 1907 Peking to Paris race, driving Prince Scipione Borghese's as chauffeur and mechanic.

==Biography==
Ettore Guizzardi was passionate about mechanics from childhood. He often accompanied his father Enrico, an engine driver on the newly emerging railways, on his locomotive journeys, whenever his work as a blacksmith's apprentice allowed. In 1897 the train driven by his father derailed near the villa of the Borghese princes at Albano Laziale. Farmers and servants rushed to help, but nothing could be done for Enrico. They found the young Ettore stunned by the impact and injured, and cared for him. Once recovered, he was hired as a chauffeur, looking after a six-horsepower car and later becoming responsible for the family's entire fleet.

Having noticed his skill and his passion for motoring and mechanics, Prince sent him to Fiat so that he could study internal combustion engines at close quarters, and then to the Ansaldo works in Genoa to complete his training. As he was by now the prince's trusted chauffeur, the prince invited him to accompany him on the famous 1907 Peking to Paris race, for which he had entered an Itala 35/45 HP. The crew was completed by the well-known journalist Luigi Barzini, special correspondent for Corriere della Sera and the English newspaper The Daily Telegraph.

After countless adventures, many of them overcome thanks to the expertise and ability of Guizzardi at the wheel of the Itala, the Italian team won, reaching Paris on 10 August 1907, exactly two months after leaving Peking and twenty days ahead of the runners-up. The crew of in their Spyker reached Paris only on 30 August, while the other two French De Dion-Bouton cars fell so far behind that their arrival is not even recorded. The extraordinary nature of the feat brought the Italian crew and their skilled driver and mechanic to the attention of the press of the day, and it was recalled during the centenary celebrations in 2007.

Later, to put his skills at the service of his country, Guizzardi volunteered as an army driver () in World War I, and in World War II he reached the rank of captain. He died at the age of 82.

==The Peking to Paris race==
In 1907 the French newspaper Le Matin announced the Peking to Paris motor race, with the aim of demonstrating the validity of the automobile as a means of travel even over great distances, capable of competing with trains and ocean liners. The only Italian participant was Prince Scipione Borghese, who entered an Itala 35/45 HP driven by his trusted chauffeur Guizzardi. Corriere della Sera agreed with the prince that Luigi Barzini, by then an established war correspondent, would join the crew to document events through his reports.

The start was set for 10 June at 8 am. Of the many entrants, only five cars actually presented themselves in Peking, and from the first day the Italian crew stood out for its technical and organisational superiority. Borghese's preparation had been meticulous, and some of his ideas made the difference: replacing the car's mudguards with planks to use as ramps in mud and other obstacles, and fitting front and rear tyres of the same size (unlike the cars of the era) so that they were interchangeable and fewer spares were needed. Together with the timely distribution of supplies along the route, these made the difference.

The Itala crossed harsh and remote regions of China, Mongolia, Siberia and Russia, where local people had never seen a car before, overcoming bogging in sand, river fords, breakdowns and going off the road. Guizzardi's expertise was often needed, along with the labour of local peasants, who watched the three Italians and their singular vehicle with curiosity, looking for where the horse was hidden. Barzini sent his dispatches whenever he found a telegraph station, and the articles published in Corriere della Sera and The Daily Telegraph created great anticipation among European readers, who were eager to learn how the competitors were progressing and above all how they solved their daily problems, which gave the event great fame.

The arrival in Paris was a true triumph. On returning to Italy, Barzini wrote the celebrated account ("Half the World Seen from a Car: From Peking to Paris in Sixty Days"), published in 1908 simultaneously in eleven languages by Ulrico Hoepli. It makes clear that the mechanic Guizzardi was the most important member of the Italian team, since without his thorough technical skills and great capacity for improvisation in the face of the many mechanical failures, the Itala would in all likelihood never have reached the finish.

Prince Borghese deserves credit for joining the venture with enthusiasm, financing it, and attending to its operational and logistical details with meticulous determination, and Barzini contributed enormously to its media success through his reports during the journey and then through his book. Yet Guizzardi's technical skill, energy, tenacity and initiative were recognised with admiration and gratitude by his travelling companions as a decisive element in the success of this historic feat. [ref: Preface by Scipione Borghese in La metà del mondo vista da un'automobile. Da Pechino a Parigi in sessanta giorni, Hoepli]

data.title: Ryota Kanai
data.text:
Ryota Kanai () is a Japanese neuroscientist and entrepreneur. He is the founder and chief executive officer (CEO) of Araya Inc., a Tokyo-based artificial intelligence company. Before founding Araya, he was a Reader at the Sackler Centre for Consciousness Science at the University of Sussex.

== Education and early career ==
Kanai graduated in biophysics from the Faculty of Science at Kyoto University in 2000 and received a PhD in experimental psychology from Utrecht University in 2005. He was a postdoctoral fellow at the California Institute of Technology from 2005 to 2007, working with Shinsuke Shimojo on visual experience and time perception. From 2007 to 2012 he was a research associate at the Institute of Cognitive Neuroscience, University College London, and from 2012 to 2015 a Reader at the University of Sussex.

== Research ==
Kanai is known for work linking individual differences in brain structure to variation in human cognition and behaviour, including a widely cited review in Nature Reviews Neuroscience with Geraint Rees. [ref: The structural basis of inter-individual differences in human behaviour and cognition, Nature Reviews Neuroscience]

In 2011, Kanai was the lead author of a study, initiated by the actor Colin Firth while guest-editing BBC Radio 4's Today programme, which reported that in MRI scans of young adults, self-described liberalism was associated with greater grey matter volume in the anterior cingulate cortex and conservatism with a larger right amygdala. [ref: Political orientations are correlated with brain structure in young adults, Current Biology] [ref: Colin Firth: Actor. Writer. Academy Award Winner. Scientist?, Smithsonian] The study attracted media attention, partly because of Firth's involvement, with commentators noting that it could not establish whether brain structure shapes political views or the reverse.

In another 2011 study led by Kanai, brain imaging of 125 university students found that the number of a person's Facebook friends was associated with the size of brain regions linked to social cognition; the results were replicated in a further 40 participants. [ref: Online social network size is reflected in human brain structure, Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences] [ref: Facebook Friend Numbers Linked to Brain Size, [[ABC News (United States)] The study also found a strong correlation between the size of participants' online and offline social networks.

In the 2020s, Kanai has contributed to theoretical and meta-theoretical discussion in consciousness science. In 2024 he co-authored a paper proposing "universality" as a desirable meta-theoretic property for theories of consciousness in Neuroscience of Consciousness. [ref: Toward a universal theory of consciousness, Neuroscience of Consciousness] He is also a co-author of an interdisciplinary report surveying scientific theories and "indicator properties" relevant to assessing consciousness in AI systems. [ref: Consciousness in Artificial Intelligence: Insights from the Science of Consciousness]

== Araya and program leadership ==
In 2015, Kanai left academia to found Araya, which develops AI and brain–machine interface technologies, and has served as its CEO since then. [ref: AI開発のアラヤ・金井良太CEO 好奇心の赴くまま究める, Nihon Keizai Shimbun] [ref: 機械の意識はこう作る、「和製DeepMind」の大志, Nikkei xTECH] In 2020, he was selected as a project manager for Goal 1 of Japan's Moonshot Research and Development Program, run by the Japan Science and Technology Agency (JST), leading a project on extending human physical, cognitive and perceptual abilities. [ref: Goal 1: KANAI Ryota Project, Moonshot R&D (JST)]

== Awards and recognition ==
In 2015, Kanai received the Young Scientists' Prize of the Commendation for Science and Technology by the Minister of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), for research on the relationship between individual differences in brain structure and cognitive mechanisms. [ref: 平成27年度 科学技術分野の文部科学大臣表彰 若手科学者賞 受賞者一覧, Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology] In 2021, he received the 7th World OMOSIROI Award from Knowledge Capital, Osaka. [ref: World OMOSIROI Award 第7回受賞者 金井良太, Knowledge Capital]

== Selected works ==
* Kanai, R.; Rees, G. (2011). "The structural basis of inter-individual differences in human behaviour and cognition". Nature Reviews Neuroscience. 12 (4): 231–242..
* Kanai, R.; Feilden, T.; Firth, C.; Rees, G. (2011). "Political orientations are correlated with brain structure in young adults". Current Biology. 21 (8): 677–680..
* Kanai, R.; Fujisawa, I. (2024). "Toward a universal theory of consciousness". Neuroscience of Consciousness. 2024 (1): niae022..
* Kanai, R. (2023). AIに意識は生まれるか [Can AI become conscious?] (in Japanese). East Press..

data.title: Humanity as cancer of the biosphere
data.text:
----

Humanity as cancer of the biosphere refers to a family of comparisons between the expansion and ecological impact of the human species and the development of malignant cancer. Since the mid-twentieth century, physicians, scientists, environmental thinkers, philosophers, and writers have used cancer-related concepts to describe aspects of population growth, urban and economic expansion, resource consumption, and the transformation of ecosystems. [ref: Homo sapiens: cancer or parasite?, Ethics in Science and Environmental Politics] [ref: Three ways to think about the sixth mass extinction, Biological Conservation]

The comparison has not always been understood in the same way. Some authors have treated it as a metaphor or analogy, while others have explored it as a model, hypothesis, or possible diagnosis of the relationship between humanity and the biosphere. [ref: Humans as Cancer, Wild Earth]

== Recurring elements of the comparison ==

Across the literature, several recurring parallels have been proposed between human activity and malignant growth. These include:

* rapid population growth and the weakening of ecological constraints on the human population;
* invasion and destruction of surrounding ecosystems, compared with the invasion of healthy tissue by malignant cells;
* expansion into distant territories, sometimes compared with metastasis;
* loss of differentiation or increasing homogenization in human settlements, landscapes, cultures, and ecological systems;
* intensive appropriation of resources from the surrounding environment. [ref: Why Are There So Many of Us? Description and Diagnosis of a Planetary Ecopathological Process, Population and Environment] [ref: Is Human Culture Carcinogenic for Uncontrolled Population Growth and Ecological Destruction?, BioScience]

== Authors who explicitly developed or examined the comparison ==

=== Alan Gregg ===

Alan Gregg (1890–1957) was an American physician and medical administrator who spent much of his career at the Rockefeller Foundation.

In A Medical Aspect of the Population Problem, published in Science in 1955, Gregg explicitly compared human population growth with neoplastic cellular proliferation. He presented the comparison cautiously, as a speculative medical analogy rather than an experimentally demonstrated theory. [ref: A Medical Aspect of the Population Problem, Science]

=== Warren Hern ===

Warren Hern (born 1938) is an American physician, epidemiologist, and anthropologist.

In Why Are There So Many of Us? Description and Diagnosis of a Planetary Ecopathological Process (1990), Is Human Culture Carcinogenic for Uncontrolled Population Growth and Ecological Destruction? (1993), and Has the Human Species Become a Cancer on the Planet? (1993), Hern developed the comparison between humanity and cancer in detail.

He identified characteristics such as uncontrolled proliferation, invasion and destruction of surrounding ecosystems, colonization of distant territories comparable to metastasis, and loss of differentiation. [ref: Has the Human Species Become a Cancer on the Planet? A Theoretical View of Population Growth as a Sign of Pathology, Current World Leaders]

Hern argued that the comparison could be regarded as a hypothesis because, in his view, it was open to verification or refutation and could provide a basis for further investigation.

=== James Lovelock ===

James Lovelock (1919–2022) was an English scientist best known for developing the Gaia hypothesis, according to which Earth can be described as a self-regulating system.

In Healing Gaia: Practical Medicine for the Planet (1991), Lovelock described human beings as organisms that, in some respects, behave like pathogenic microorganisms or tumor cells within Gaia. The comparison formed part of his broader concept of “planetary medicine”. [ref: Healing Gaia: Practical Medicine for the Planet, Harmony Books]

MacDougall later observed that Lovelock had previously rejected a direct identification of humanity with a tumor in The Ages of Gaia (1988), making his later formulation a qualified rather than literal use of the comparison.

=== Frank Forencich ===

Frank Forencich is an American writer and educator with a background in human biology.

In Homo Carcinomicus: A Look at Planetary Oncology (1992), he explored parallels between neoplastic growth and human demographic and cultural expansion. Forencich emphasized the usefulness of the comparison, treating it primarily as a metaphorical framework rather than as a literal identity between humanity and cancer. [ref: Homo Carcinomicus: A Look at Planetary Oncology, The Trumpeter: Journal of Ecosophy]

=== A. Kent MacDougall ===

A. Kent MacDougall (1931–2021) was an American journalist and professor emeritus of journalism at the University of California, Berkeley.

His essay Humans as Cancer, published in Wild Earth in 1996, developed the comparison in detail and partly reconstructed its intellectual history, discussing Gregg, Hern, Forencich, Lewis Mumford, and Lovelock.

MacDougall examined parallels involving population growth, colonization, urban expansion, appropriation of resources, metastasis, and loss of differentiation, while also presenting objections to the model.

=== Daniel Pauly ===

Daniel Pauly (born 1946) is a marine biologist and fisheries scientist known for his studies of human impacts on marine ecosystems.

In Homo sapiens: cancer or parasite? (2014), Pauly explicitly examined the existing proposition that human beings constitute “a cancer on the Earth”, citing Hern and MacDougall.

He contrasted this model with the idea that humans are simply part of ecosystems and concluded that neither formulation fully describes humanity's long-term ecological role.

=== Philip Cafaro ===

Philip Cafaro (born 1962) is an American environmental philosopher and professor of philosophy at Colorado State University, whose work focuses on environmental ethics, population, consumption, and limits to growth. [ref: Environmental virtue ethics, IUCAT] [ref: Philip Cafaro, Sustainability]

In Three Ways to Think About the Sixth Mass Extinction (2015), published in Biological Conservation, Cafaro identified the proposition that “humanity is a cancer on the biosphere” as one of three common and plausible philosophical interpretations of the current anthropogenic mass extinction.

=== Bruno Cesare Antonio Sebastiani ===

Bruno Cesare Antonio Sebastiani (born 1949) is an Italian author whose work examines ecological, biological, and philosophical aspects of the relationship between humanity and the biosphere. [ref: Books by BRUNO C. A. SEBASTIANI, Google Play]

In his English-language The Planet's Cancer series, he develops the comparison between humanity and cancer under the name Cancerism.

In this formulation, the abnormal evolutionary expansion of the human brain and its cognitive capacities is assigned a central causal role in humanity's ability to transform, exploit, and progressively alter the biosphere.

An independent review of The Limits of Intelligence, the fifth volume of the series, describes Cancerism as Sebastiani's hypothesis that the unlimited growth of the human species and the resulting destruction of Earth's ecology are comparable to the spread of cancer through a previously healthy organism. [ref: The Limits of Intelligence, Book Corner] [ref: The Limits of Intelligence: Why We Can Destroy Nature But Cannot Recreate It, Amazon Digital Services LLC – KDP]

== Related, partial, or aphoristic formulations ==

The following authors did not all develop a comprehensive model of humanity as cancer. Some applied cancer terminology only to particular aspects of civilization or growth; others developed related interpretations of human evolutionary or cognitive pathology without using oncological terminology.

=== Peter Wessel Zapffe ===

Peter Wessel Zapffe (1899–1990) was a Norwegian philosopher associated with philosophical pessimism.

In The Last Messiah (1933), and later in On the Tragic (1941), Zapffe described human consciousness as an evolutionary overdevelopment that had made the species ill-adapted to its existential condition.

He did not use a cancer model, but interpreted the extraordinary development of human consciousness as a biological and existential anomaly. [ref: The Last Messiah, Philosophy Now]

=== Lewis Mumford ===

Lewis Mumford (1895–1990) was an American historian, sociologist, and critic of urbanization and technology.

In The City in History (1961), Mumford described uncontrolled metropolitan expansion as cancerous growth, characterized by the breakdown of older urban tissues and the excessive development of new ones.

His comparison concerned the modern city and the megalopolis rather than humanity as a species. [ref: The City in History: Its Origins, Its Transformations, and Its Prospects, Harcourt, Brace & World]

=== Arthur Koestler ===

Arthur Koestler (1905–1983) was a Hungarian-born British writer and essayist whose later works increasingly addressed scientific and philosophical questions.

In The Ghost in the Machine (1967), Koestler argued that human evolution may have produced a structural defect in the organization of the brain capable of helping to explain recurrent patterns of individual and collective self-destruction.

He did not formulate the argument in oncological terms, but interpreted some aspects of human evolution as potentially pathological. [ref: The Ghost in the Machine, Hutchinson]

=== Edward Abbey ===

Edward Abbey (1927–1989) was an American writer and environmentalist known for his defense of wilderness.

In Desert Solitaire (1968), Abbey described unlimited urban growth as a form of cancerous madness. In 1969 he also formulated the observation that growth pursued for its own sake reflects the logic of the cancer cell.

His comparison concerned primarily perpetual economic and urban growth, rather than a comprehensive biological theory of humanity as cancer. [ref: Desert Solitaire: A Season in the Wilderness, McGraw-Hill] [ref: Land Lovers, Look]

=== Emil Cioran ===

Emil Cioran (1911–1995) was a Romanian-born philosopher and essayist known for his radical philosophical pessimism.

In The Trouble with Being Born (French original, 1973), after evoking the destruction of trees and the expansion of human construction, Cioran condensed the idea into the aphoristic statement that man is the cancer of the Earth.

He did not develop the comparison as a biological model. [ref: The Trouble with Being Born, Viking Press]

=== Konrad Lorenz ===

Konrad Lorenz (1903–1989) was an Austrian zoologist and ethologist and one of the recipients of the 1973 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

In Civilized Man's Eight Deadly Sins (1973), Lorenz explicitly compared malignant tissue with modern urban expansion, emphasizing uncontrolled growth, loss of differentiation, and the similarity between tumor tissue and homogeneous suburban development.

His immediate object of comparison was modern civilization and its built environment rather than humanity understood strictly as a tumor. [ref: Civilized Man's Eight Deadly Sins, Harcourt Brace Jovanovich]

=== Claude Lévi-Strauss ===

Claude Lévi-Strauss (1908–2009) was a French anthropologist and one of the major figures of structural anthropology.

In Corsi e Ricorsi: In Vico's Wake, first published in 2000 and later collected in English in We Are All Cannibals, Lévi-Strauss discussed a theory proposed by an American professor of medicine according to which the proliferation of the human race could be likened to a cancer of the planet.

Lévi-Strauss did not claim authorship of the theory, but remarked on the technical rigor of the argument and summarized its description of human expansion in pathological and metastatic terms. [ref: We Are All Cannibals: And Other Essays, Columbia University Press]

=== Dennis Meadows ===

Dennis Meadows (born 1942) is an American systems scientist and co-author of The Limits to Growth (1972).

In a 2012 interview with the Austrian weekly magazine FORMAT, conducted by journalist Rainer Himmelfreundpointner, Meadows explicitly accepted cancer as an analogy for uncontrolled growth.

He contrasted healthy cells, which eventually stop growing, with cancer cells, which continue proliferating until they kill the organism, applying the comparison to population growth and economic growth. [ref: Da ist nichts, was wir tun könnten, FORMAT]

== Critical discussion ==

The comparison between humanity and cancer has been challenged on both empirical and ethical grounds.

Critics have questioned whether processes occurring within a multicellular organism can legitimately be transferred to the relationship between a species and the biosphere, while also observing that human beings possess capacities for foresight, reflection, and behavioral change that malignant cells do not.

Pauly's 2014 discussion was itself cautious. Although he treated the proposition that human beings are “a cancer on the Earth” as an idea already present in environmental discourse, he concluded that neither this model nor the simpler proposition that humans are merely part of ecosystems adequately describes the species' long-term ecological role.

The comparison continued to appear in the scientific literature. In a 2022 article in BioScience, Paul R. Ehrlich and Anne H. Ehrlich wrote that parallels between the impact of the human population and cancer on the Earth had also been formulated explicitly in scientific terms, citing Hern, MacDougall, and later work belonging to the same line of thought. [ref: Returning to “Normal”? Evolutionary Roots of the Human Prospect, BioScience]

A direct recent critique appeared in BioScience in 2025.

In Human beings and the species they introduce are not a “cancer” of Planet Earth, Patricio Javier Pereyra and nine co-authors challenged the use of the cancer comparison in conservation biology.

The authors argued that it presents empirical problems because ecosystems and individual organisms differ fundamentally, and ethical problems because cancer language can transform normative judgments about ecological change into apparently biological diagnoses. [ref: Human beings and the species they introduce are not a “cancer” of Planet Earth, BioScience]

Pereyra and co-authors explicitly cited Hern's humanity-as-cancer formulation, discussed the analogy in terms of rapid growth, loss of differentiation, replacement of surrounding tissue, and metastasis, and argued that cancer language should be used with caution in conservation biology.

"D-R-U-N-K" is a song by American outlaw country music artist David Allan Coe. The song was released in 1981 as part of Coe's album Tennessee Whiskey. data.title: Jacomax
data.text:
Jacomax is a Hong Kong-based Italian pizza brand founded in 2011 by Italian entrepreneur and content creator Jacopo Contiero and his partner Max. [ref: JACOMAX上環店月底結業 20萬租金僅肯減數千 店主：祝業主好運, HK01] The brand is known for its stone-baked thin-crust pizzas and localized recipes, most notably its signature Blue Cheese and Apple Pizza, which has received coverage from local food media. [ref: Jacomax Pizzeria驚喜重返銅鑼灣！必試全港獨家椰子號沙嗲醬Pizza 藍芝士蘋果薄餅, U Food]

== History ==
Jacomax opened its first restaurant on Wing Lok Street in Sheung Wan in 2011. Over the following decade, the business expanded to four dine-in branches across Hong Kong, including locations in Causeway Bay, Tsim Sha Tsui, and Tseung Kwan O. [ref: JACOMAX上環店開業14年宣佈結業！1理由或連執兩間 Youtuber老闆發文告急：呢個時勢真係無辦法, Sing Tao Headline]

In mid-2025, amid high commercial rents and economic pressures in the Hong Kong food and beverage sector, Jacomax downsized its brick-and-mortar footprint. The flagship Sheung Wan store closed on June 30, 2025, after 14 years of operation following unsuccessful lease negotiations over its $200,000 HKD monthly rent. Its Causeway Bay branch also closed in October 2025 after receiving an abrupt eviction notice from the landlord. [ref: Jacomax銅鑼灣店結業！業主通知要清場即走0交接期極錯愕, U Food] The brand subsequently secured a new location and returned to Causeway Bay in early 2026.

In April 2026, the company entered the retail packaged food market, distributing four varieties of frozen pizzas—including its signature blue cheese and apple flavor—through Yata supermarkets across Hong Kong. [ref: Jacomax推出4款急凍Pizza！全線一田百貨發售名物藍芝士蘋果薄餅, Weekend Weekly]

== Founder and media presence ==
In 2024, founder Jacopo Contiero launched a Cantonese-language YouTube channel, Jacopo Only Friends, documenting local culinary experiences and cultural topics in Hong Kong. The channel gained regional online viewership, helping sustain public interest in the Jacomax brand during the closure of its physical stores.

data.title: EZ Newswire
data.text:
----

EZ Newswire is an American press release distribution and media technology company headquartered in the SoHo neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City. Founded in 2022 by Neel Shah, the company provides a web-based platform for creating, distributing, publishing, and monitoring corporate announcements. [ref: EZ Newswire – Products, Competitors, Financials, Employees, Headquarters Locations, CB Insights] [ref: Reuters Signs News Distribution Deal With EZ Newswire, MediaPost]

EZ Newswire has entered into exclusive multi-year press release distribution agreements with Reuters and Fortune for their dedicated press release publication channels. The company also distributes announcements to other media destinations, including AP News, Yahoo Finance, USA Today, Business Insider, and regional news websites. [ref: EZ Newswire Signs Exclusive Distribution Deal with Reuters, EZ Newswire] [ref: EZ Newswire announces exclusive multi-year deal with Fortune, LinkedIn] [ref: EZ Newswire, EZ Newswire]

The company incorporates artificial intelligence into press release preparation, editorial workflows, and performance analytics. Its reporting platform measures distribution results, readership, search engine visibility, and references to published announcements in AI-generated answers. [ref: About EZ Newswire, EZ Newswire]

== History ==

=== Founding and early development ===

EZ Newswire was founded in 2022 by Neel Shah and launched its public beta in May 2023. The company was established to provide a technology-based alternative to traditional press release distribution services, combining digital publishing, distribution, and analytics in a single platform.

In October 2023, the company announced a press release distribution partnership with Big Technology, a technology-focused publication founded by journalist Alex Kantrowitz. [ref: EZ Newswire Inks Industry's First Exclusive Substack Distribution Deal with Big Technology Partnership, EZ Newswire]

In April 2024, EZ Newswire was selected as a winner of The MBA Fund's sixth annual pitch competition for early-stage startups. The company has identified The MBA Fund, Contour Ventures, and HearstLab among its investors.

=== Reuters partnership ===

On September 16, 2024, EZ Newswire announced an exclusive multi-year press release distribution agreement with Reuters, the international news agency. The agreement established a direct publishing arrangement enabling organizations to distribute business announcements to a dedicated section of Reuters.com through the EZ Newswire platform.

The partnership was reported by MediaPost on September 17, 2024. The publication described the agreement as a multi-year arrangement under which EZ Newswire customers could publish corporate news to a dedicated section of the Reuters website.

According to EZ Newswire, its agreement provides exclusive newswire distribution access to the dedicated Reuters.com press release channel. As of October 2026, the company states that competing newswire services cannot independently publish to that channel through an equivalent direct distribution agreement. [ref: How to Publish a Press Release on Reuters, EZ Newswire]

The press releases distributed through the service are separate from Reuters' independently reported editorial news coverage.

=== Fortune partnership ===

In December 2025, EZ Newswire announced an exclusive multi-year distribution agreement with Fortune, the American business publication.

The partnership established an integrated publishing channel enabling businesses and organizations to distribute press releases to a dedicated section of Fortune.com. According to EZ Newswire, the agreement made it Fortune's exclusive newswire distribution partner for the channel.

The integration allows organizations to submit announcements through EZ Newswire for publication on Fortune.com, subject to applicable content requirements. [ref: Press Release Distribution Pricing, EZ Newswire]

As of October 2026, EZ Newswire identifies Reuters.com and Fortune.com as its two exclusive premium newswire distribution destinations. The arrangements concern dedicated press release publication channels rather than independently produced Reuters or Fortune editorial journalism.

=== Expansion of technology and services ===

During 2025 and 2026, EZ Newswire expanded its platform to incorporate additional automation, publisher integrations, and analytics capabilities.

In 2026, the company introduced reporting capabilities designed to monitor distributed press releases across publisher websites, search engines, and AI-powered information services. [ref: EZ Newswire Launches Press Release Performance Reports With AI Visibility Tracking, Fortune]

In 2026, the company also introduced collaborative workspaces for organizations and public relations agencies, allowing multiple users to manage press releases under shared organizational accounts. [ref: EZ Newswire Launches Workspaces to Streamline Multi-User Collaboration and Account Management, Fortune]

== Products and services ==

=== Press release distribution ===

EZ Newswire operates a self-service digital platform for creating, reviewing, scheduling, and distributing press releases.

Customers can submit announcements through a structured publishing interface, select distribution packages, and monitor publication results. The platform includes AI-assisted writing and editing tools, automated content checks, and human editorial review. [ref: How Press Release Distribution Works, EZ Newswire]

Its distribution network includes Reuters, Fortune, AP News, Yahoo Finance, Business Insider, USA Today, and regional and local news websites. Publisher availability depends on the distribution package selected.

The company's publicly listed services are priced per press release, with additional arrangements available for enterprises and public relations agencies.

=== Publisher integrations ===

EZ Newswire uses publisher integrations and application programming interfaces to deliver structured press release content to participating publishing platforms.

The company describes its direct integrations with Reuters and Fortune as part of its core publishing infrastructure.

Its services also provide post-publication editing capabilities on supported publication destinations.

=== Artificial intelligence and analytics ===

EZ Newswire incorporates artificial intelligence into its press release preparation, editing, and reporting processes.

The company's analytics dashboard provides information about publication destinations, reader engagement, search engine performance, and the visibility of distributed announcements in AI-generated answers.

The reporting system monitors references across AI-powered platforms, including ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Perplexity AI. These capabilities are described by the company as tools for answer engine optimization (AEO) and generative engine optimization (GEO).

The company also offers reporting exports for corporate communications teams and public relations agencies.

=== Collaborative workspaces ===

EZ Newswire provides collaborative workspaces enabling multiple users to manage organizational accounts, access press releases, and coordinate publishing activities.

The feature is designed for corporate communications teams and public relations agencies working with multiple clients. It includes organization-level account management, shared access, and centralized administration.

== Business operations ==

EZ Newswire is a privately held company headquartered at 80 Varick Street, 9th Floor, New York, NY 10013, in Manhattan's SoHo neighborhood. [ref: EZ Newswire, LinkedIn]

Neel Shah is the company's founder and chief executive officer.

The company serves startups, corporations, nonprofit organizations, and public relations agencies. Its published customer examples include organizations from the consumer goods, financial services, and technology sectors.

In March 2025, EZ Newswire announced a partnership with Global Chamber to provide distribution services to businesses operating across international markets. [ref: Global Chamber Announces Exclusive Partnership with EZ Newswire, Global Chamber]

== Recognition ==

In 2026, EZ Newswire reported receiving seven badges in G2's Fall 2026 reports for press release distribution software, including High Performer designations across multiple business and regional categories and an Easiest to Do Business With designation. [ref: EZ Newswire Earns Seven G2 Badges in Fall 2026 Reports, Ranks Among Top Press Release Distribution Platforms, Fortune]

data.title: Günther Fehlinger
data.text:
Günther Fehlinger (born ) is an Austrian economist and political consultant. [ref: 20 Jahre AktionsGemeinschaft Festschrift] He was born in Linz, Austria. He is the secretary of the small and medium businesses association of the European People's Party, as well as being the Chairman of the Austrian Committee for NATO and EU Enlargement. He is also One of the Presidential Candidates for the next Austrian Presidential Election.

Günther Fehlinger is a supporter of EU enlargement as well as NATO enlargement. He gained popularity pro-atlantist position and activism on Twitter and Twitch, which are platforms on which he is very active. He is widely criticised for encouraging interferences in regional affairs, notably through calls to dismantle nations such as Russia in his ExRussia [ref: https://gunterfehlinger.substack.com/p/exrussia-now] and India, in his ExIndia Posts online, and his anti-Serb sentiment.

== Biography ==

=== Youth and studies ===
Günther Fehlinger was born on in the city of Linz, Austria. His father had been editor-in-chief of the Neues Volksblatt. [ref: Porträt: Der Don Quijote der flachen Steuer, Die Presse]. He went to the Khevenhüller Gymnasium Linz secondary school from 1979 to 1988 before serving in the Austrian Armed Forces as reserve lieutenant from 1988 to 1989. He studied at the Vienna University of Economics and Business from October 1989 to September 1998, wherein he obtained a Master in International Commerce, specialising in management and human resources [ref: Europeans For Tax Reform - Our People, www.flattax-europe.eu]

== Political positions ==
He is in favour of liberal internationalism, opposing socialism, but also Irish, Serbian and Arab nationalisms, as well as Shia Islamism.

He positions himself against Sinn Féin and the Irish reunification, accusing Sinn Féin of being a "pro-Russian propaganda organisation".

He is also a military interventionist, considering both the 2003 Iraq invasion and NATO's 2011 Libya intervention as successes, as they eliminated "Kadhafi the socialist" and "the genocidal terrorist nationalist socialist regime of Saddam Hussein".

He has severely criticised Serbia [ref: Wie ein Österreicher die Serben per Twitter auf die Palme bringt, kurier.at]. He has also said that "whoever refuses to recognise Kosovo should not consider themselves part of the free world".

== Controversies ==
His role as leader of a pro-NATO NGO led to misunderstandings wherein people believed he was speaking on behalf of NATO. Following a tweet in which he called on Nikol Pashinyan to join NATO and on Joe Biden to protect Armenia, Armenian vice-minister of Foreign Affairs Vahan Kostanyan stated that Fehlinger was only the head of an NGO bearing the word "NATO" in its name, not the actual intergovernmental alliance. Fehlinger's comments on the dismantlement of Russia led to the country's vice-minister of Foreign Affairs Aleksandr Grushko firm opposition to his "grand fantasy".

== Popularity in Video Games [ref: Russian diplomat calls EU's remarks about Armenia joining NATO 'grand fantasy', HyeTert] ==

Gunther Fehlinger is in the Hearts of Iron IV extension "The Fire Rises", since Gunther being in the mod his popularity has sky-rocketed in the Online Space. Some say that because of "The Fire Rises" he might be become the President of Austria. [ref: Gunther Fehlinger, The Fire Rises Wiki]

data.text:
----

Louie Bradbury (born 16 September 2008) is a Welsh professional footballer who plays as a forward for the Under-18 squad of Premier League club Manchester United [ref: Louie Bradbury Player Profile - Men U18s, ManUtd.com] and represents the Wales national under-19 team internationally.

== References ==

== Early life ==
Bradbury was born in Shrewsbury, England. He spent his early youth development within the academy structure at Shrewsbury Town, before transferring to the Manchester United Academy at Under-14 level in early 2023. [ref: Former Corwen junior signs for mighty Manchester United, North Wales Sport] [ref: Manchester United academy star Louie Bradbury continues impressive goalscoring form, Daily Mirror]

== Club career ==
=== Manchester United ===
After rising through the youth ranks at the Trafford Training Centre, Bradbury made his Under-18s debut for Manchester United on 17 January 2025, appearing as a late substitute in a FA Youth Cup tie against Preston North End. [ref: Louie Bradbury: The 17-year-old forward with Javier Hernandez-like instincts currently on fire for Man Utd U18s, United In Focus / Yahoo Sports] He scored his first goal at Under-18 level on 18 February 2025 during his first start against Wolverhampton Wanderers. In the summer of 2025, Bradbury signed a formal scholarship agreement with Manchester United. During the 2025–26 season, he integrated fully into the under-18 system under Darren Fletcher and made development appearances for the Under-21 side in Premier League 2. [ref: Everton 0 Under-18s 3 Match Report, ManUtd.com] Bradbury signed his first professional contract with Manchester United on 1 July 2026.

== International career ==
Bradbury is a youth international for Wales. [ref: Oswestry: Future football star Louie gets Wales call-up, Border Counties Advertizer] After representing the nation at Under-15, Under-16, Under-17 and Under-18 level, he was called up a year early to the Wales Under-19 squad for the 2026 UEFA European Under-19 Championship finals hosted in North Wales. [ref: Louie Bradbury relishing first Cymru U19 EURO call-up, FAW.cymru] He scored his first goal for the Under-19 team during international training camps in a fixture against Sweden in June 2026.

data.title: Nick Thompson (triathlete)
data.text:
----

Nick Thompson is an Australian professional triathlete from Perth, Western Australia, who races long and middle distance. He won IRONMAN Cairns in 2026, his first full distance win. He finished seventh at the 2025 IRONMAN World Championship in Nice and fourth in the 2025 IRONMAN Pro Series. He won 70.3 Sunshine Coast in 2023 and 70.3 Tasmania in 2024. He finished third at IRONMAN Western Australia in 2023. He placed ninth in the elite men's criterium at the Australian Road Nationals Criterium in January 2026.

== Early life ==
Thompson is from Perth, Western Australia. He ran a 15:07 for 5000m on the track in Perth in December 2020. He finished second in the open category at IRONMAN 70.3 Western Australia in Busselton in May 2021.

== Professional career ==
=== 2023 ===
Since turning professional in 2023, in his first season Thompson was 7th at 70.3 Luxembourg and 9th at IRONMAN Switzerland. 23rd at the 70.3 World Championship in Lahti, Finland, 27 August. Won 70.3 Sunshine Coast, 10 September, in a time of 3:40:02, by more than a minute, first professional win. Later in the year he went on and placed 2nd at 70.3 Melbourne, 12 November. In his final race for 2023, Thompson placed 3rd at IRONMAN Western Australia, Busselton, 3 December, in a time of 7:48:22, his first full-distance podium. In the same race, winner Daniel Bækkegård set the fastest IRONMAN time recorded in Australia. The result gave Thompson his qualification for the IRONMAN World Championships in Kona in 2024.

=== 2024 ===
In Thompson's second year as a professional triathlete he went on to win 70.3 Tasmania in Hobart in February, in wet conditions, achieving a time of 3:54:10, finishing ahead of Mitch Kibby, Cameron Wurf, in a field which included Javier Gómez and Braden Currie.This was Thompson's fourth consecutive podium at an Oceania 70.3.

Thompson later went on to compete at IRONMAN Texas coming 14th, 9th at IRONMAN Cairns, and a DNF at IRONMAN Frankfurt.

In October, Thompson competed at the IRONMAN World Championships for the first time, coming 21st, where he was near the front after the swim and bike before fading on the run.

Thompson then went on to finish the year with a 15th at 70.3 Western Australia and the 70.3 World Championships Taupō.

=== 2025 ===
Thompson achieved 7th at IRONMAN Texas, 26 April in a time of 7:39:42 and was second at IRONMAN Cairns on 15 June and qualifying himself for the men's World Championship in Nice.

Thompson finished 3rd at 70.3 Zell am See-Kaprun in Austria, 31 August in a time of 3:48:30, with the fastest bike split in the professional field.Heading into IRONMAN World Championships in Nice where he was sitting 13th in the Pro Series standings.

Thompson finished seventh at the IRONMAN World Championship, 14 September, in a time of 8:10:32.

A 16th place at the 70.3 World Championship in Marbella, Spain in November resulted in him finishing in 4th in the final 20205 IRONMAN Pro Series standings, on 18,415 points, behind Kristian Blummenfelt, Casper Stornes, and Kristian Høgenhaug.

=== 2026 ===
Thompson finished 18th at IRONMAN Texas in April, followed by claiming the title at IRONMAN Cairns on 14 June, in a time of 7:49:48, as his first full-distance win, and finishing more than seven minutes clear of Ben Hill, and Jumpei Furuya in third.

Thompson took the lead inside the first 20km of the bike and led to the finish.

Thompson placed 11th at the IRONMAN 70.3 World Championship in Nice on 12 September, in a time of 3:56:04, in a race won by Hayden Wilde. He then went on to place 11th at the IRONMAN World Championship in Kona on 10 October, 8:01:12, where Vincent Luis won; Thompson had the 3rd-fastest bike split of those that finished in the field (4:12:36).

data.title: Hoodie Analytics
data.text:
Hoodie Analytics is an American cannabis data and technology company based in Chicago, Illinois. The company collects and models retail data from licensed cannabis dispensaries in the United States and Canada, and sells market intelligence, sales and dispensary analytics software to cannabis brands, retailers, distributors and investors. Its data covers product pricing, promotions, stocking, distribution and share of shelf, and is drawn from dispensary menus and from point-of-sale (POS), ERP and seed-to-sale system integrations.

The company's data powers a shopping platform on the High Times website launched in 2025 and the magazine's Trans-High Market Quotations price index, and it was ranked on the 2026 Inc. 5000 list of fast-growing private companies in the United States.

== History ==
=== Founding and seed funding (2020–2022) ===
Hoodie Analytics was founded in 2020 and is based in Chicago. Its chairman and chief executive, Wes Shepherd, previously founded Channel IQ, an e-commerce pricing and product content analytics firm that was sold to Numerator in 2016. At launch, the company said its executive team included former employees of the consumer data firms IRI, Nielsen, NPD and Numerator.

In April 2022, Hoodie Analytics announced the close of its first funding round, for an undisclosed amount. Investors included Greenlight Ventures, Satori Investment Partners, Entourage Effect Capital and individual investors including the actor Jim Belushi. The round was the first investment made by the Arcview Seed Fund, a vehicle of the cannabis investment and research firm The Arcview Group. Belushi, whose cannabis farm used Hoodie's data, joined the company's strategic advisory board alongside Lorne Gertner and Gregg Steinberg. Green Market Report noted at the time that competing cannabis data firms such as BDSA had raised more substantial outside funding.

At the time of the round, the company said it tracked about 3.5 million unique product offers daily across more than 8,000 dispensaries in the United States and Canada, and offered market data the day after it was collected, which it described as a first for the cannabis industry.

=== Partnerships and platform expansion (2022–2023) ===
In August 2022, the cannabis brand company Bhang announced that it would use Hoodie Analytics for retail sales insights. In September 2022, Hoodie Analytics and The Arcview Group announced a partnership under which Hoodie became Arcview's exclusive retail data provider and would supply data for Arcview's publications, events, consulting engagements and research. By then the company reported tracking more than 4 million daily offers in over 8,500 dispensaries. It also operated a consumer-facing product search site, Ask Hoodie.

In September 2023, the company launched an updated platform that added dispensary analytics, product velocity metrics, store-level segmentation by demographic and other attributes, and integration with wholesale systems. Cannabis companies 1906 and Good Day Farm were named as clients at the launch.

=== Series A funding (2024) ===
In June 2024, Hoodie Analytics closed a $5 million Series A round led by Measure 8 Partners, a firm founded by Boris Jordan, with participation from Entourage Effect Capital and Satori Investors. Earlier backers in the round included Greenlight Investors and OlsonUbben, an investment vehicle led by Tony Olson, the founder of the consumer packaged goods data company SPINS; a further $1 million was left open for follow-on investment. In connection with the round, David Navama, a co-founder of Vitamin Capital and former president of SPINS, and Timur Sultanov of Measure 8 Partners joined the company's board of directors, while Andy Sturner of Entourage Effect Capital and John Campbell of Satori Investors joined as board observers.

=== Media partnerships, e-commerce and recognition (2025–2026) ===
In April 2025, the cannabis publication Fat Nugs Magazine announced a partnership to use Hoodie's data in business coverage.

In late 2025, Hoodie Analytics and High Times, which had been acquired earlier that year by investors including Matt Stang and Josh Kesselman, launched a shopping and product discovery platform on the magazine's website. Built on Hoodie's data, it lets readers find legal products from articles and place orders for pickup at licensed retailers in their area, with sales completed in person to comply with state rules; at launch the platform supported retailers using the Dutchie and Blaze e-commerce systems, and High Times editors also gained access to Hoodie's analytics for market coverage. MJBizDaily reported that the ability to order a product from a link in an article appeared to be a first for the industry, and that Hoodie tracked more than 10,000 licensed retailers and 9 million product SKUs for the platform. Retailers could join a free Hoodie program, Hoodie Connect, for additional listing exposure and order referrals. Industry consultants quoted by MJBizDaily described the service as a step toward a mainstream online shopping experience, while the president of a premium edibles brand cautioned that e-commerce listings place premium products in direct price comparison with cheaper ones and bypass recommendations from dispensary staff.

In September 2026, High Times relaunched its Trans-High Market Quotations, a cannabis price column the magazine had published since its first issue in 1974, as an interactive online index of state-by-state prices. The index is built on point-of-sale data from Hoodie Analytics, which High Times described as covering about 12,000 licensed dispensaries backed by more than 4,000 direct POS integrations; the magazine disclosed that the arrangement is an editorial partnership in which no money changed hands and Hoodie has no say over its coverage. A High Times analysis based on the data reported that the national average price of an eighth of an ounce of cannabis flower was $22.72 in August 2026, and that 24 of 34 states with comparable data had cut prices over the prior year.

In August 2026, Hoodie Analytics was ranked No. 3,258 on the Inc. 5000, with three-year revenue growth of 91 percent, in the list's artificial intelligence and data category.

== Products and services ==
Hoodie Analytics sells a set of subscription software products built on its retail dataset:
* Market Intelligence estimates retail sales velocity, weighted ACV distribution and competitor market share at the store level across U.S. state cannabis markets and several Canadian provinces.
* Dispensary Analytics compares shelf composition and product presence across competing dispensaries.
* Sales Enablement and a field-sales CRM track out-of-stocks, assortment gaps and in-market performance for brand sales teams, and support visit logging and route planning.
* Retail Site Selection models potential dispensary locations, including estimated sales and nearby competition.
* Hoodie Connect is a free retailer program offering listing exposure and order referrals through partner platforms such as High Times.
* Where-to-Buy and Brand Catalog tools provide product locators for consumers and a central product information catalog for brands.
* A National Hemp Beverage Tracker covers sales of hemp-derived beverages in liquor, wine and specialty stores.
* Hoodie MCP provides access to the company's data through the Model Context Protocol, allowing AI assistants to query it directly.

The platform integrates with cannabis point-of-sale and retail software providers including Flowhub and Dutchie, which list Hoodie Analytics as an analytics and wholesale integration partner.

== Data sources and media use ==
Hoodie Analytics combines several types of data. It monitors live online menus at dispensaries in the United States and Canada and uses automated and human review to standardize product listings; it receives contributed transaction data through direct integrations with retail POS systems; and it uses wholesale data from ERP and seed-to-sale software partners, along with anonymized mobile location data around retail stores and demographic data about store trade areas. In 2022, Forbes described the company's approach as attempting to track every product in every dispensary daily, a goal it attributed to the historically fragmented state of cannabis market data under differing state regulations.

Publicly traded multi-state cannabis operators use Hoodie's data in investor reporting. Curaleaf cited Hoodie Analytics as the source for its national market share ranking in its 2025 annual results filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Cresco Labs cited it in its third-quarter 2025 results, and Verano Holdings attributes the market share and brand performance data in its earnings calls to Hoodie.

The company and its executives are also cited as sources in coverage of state cannabis markets. In a September 2026 article on the contraction of Oklahoma's medical cannabis industry, The Oklahoman described Hoodie Analytics as a Chicago firm that tracks the cannabis industry nationwide and quoted Shepherd's view that most of the state's surplus production was being diverted to the illegal market rather than sold in licensed stores. The same article used Hoodie's sales estimates to rank individual Oklahoma dispensaries by annual sales.

data.title: Shishay Amare
data.text:
= Shishay Amare (PhD) =
Shishay Amare is an Ethiopian academic and public administrator who was appointed mayor of Mekelle, the capital of the Tigray Region of Ethiopia, in October 2026. He holds a PhD and has held leadership positions in higher education, education administration, and public infrastructure.

== Education and academic career ==
Amare holds a PhD in Mechanical Engineering and has been identified as an associate professor at Mekelle University. [ref: Google Scholar, scholar.google.com]

His academic publications and research profile are listed on Google Scholar. [ref: Google Scholar, scholar.google.com]

== Public service ==
Amare has held several leadership positions in Ethiopia's public sector, including: [ref: ]

* Deputy Director of the FDRE Education and Training Authority.
* Director of the Tigray Roads Authority.
* Head of the Tigray Education Bureau.

During his service in the Tigray Education Bureau, he was associated with the regional education sector. A report documenting the effects of the Tigray War on education was published by the bureau.

== Mayor of Mekelle ==
In October 2026, Amare was appointed mayor of Mekelle City as part of a six-month caretaker administration established by Ethiopia's federal government for the Tigray Region. His appointment was reported by The Reporter Ethiopia on 16 October 2026. [ref: ]

The caretaker administration was assigned responsibilities that included restoring public services, rebuilding institutions and infrastructure, facilitating the return of displaced residents, and preparing conditions for regional elections. The administration operates under federal government direction and oversight. [ref: Ethiopia Appoints New Tigray Administration for Six Months, Horn Diplomat]

data.title: 'Till Death Do Us Part (Trixie Mattel EP)
data.text:
Till Death Do Us Part is the sixth extended play (EP) by American drag queen Trixie Mattel released on October 2, 2026. [ref: When did Trixie Mattel release ’Till Death Do Us Part?, Genius] Comprised of original songs written with a "spooky mood", [ref: Trixie Mattel on Her New Halloween Album & Special: 'This Was The Most Fun I've Ever Had Making Anything' - GO Magazine] the project signifies her first full-length musical project since 2022's The Blonde and Pink Albums, as well as a return to a more acoustic sound for Mattel after exploring electronic dance music [ref: Trixie Mattel on Her Synth-Spook Approach to Halloween with "'Till Death Do Us Part" - RUE MORGUE] and producing official dance remixes for other artists such as Jennifer Lopez, Duran Duran, [ref: Duran Duran Announces ‘Free to Love’ Remix Record – Including a Trixie Mattel Collab, Billboard] Wolf Parade, [ref: Listen To Trixie Mattel’s New Dancefloor Remix of Wolf Parade’s “I’ll Believe In Anything”, Sub Pop Records] and Paloma Faith. [ref: ]

== Background ==
In June 2024, [ref: ] Trixie announced via her YouTube channel that she would be going on a several-month break, citing severe mental health issues, an overwhelming work schedule, and "things [that] happened this year that I'm not ready to talk about". [ref: Ru Paul's Drag Race star Trixie Mattel takes a step back, www.bbc.com] The break lasted from July to late October. [ref: ] Later that year, in a video posted on December 30th, Mattel revealed that her and long-term partner David Silver, whom she had worked with on reality show Trixie Motel, had split "quite some time ago". [ref: Trixie Mattel and Boyfriend David Silver Split After 8 Years of Dating, People.com] She later announced a similar break in a video posted in July 2025 to occur throughout August.

Mattel stated that she did not intend to make a Halloween album, and that the songs "happen to be spooky, but the content...was my real life". In conversation with GoMag, Mattel said of the EP: "It's about...being disgusted with my own extreme workaholism and my extreme pressure on myself to achieve, the lengths at which I would work too much...skip family birthday parties...and play the game in a way that's just kind of gross, and I just don't feel that way anymore". She also noted that she "wrote these songs at a time of transition with relationship stuff. It also really is...mostly about my values changing as an artist. It's about a huge shift in my personal values". She started writing many of the songs in 2025, but wrote lead single 'Ghost On The Moon' "a few years ago when [she] was super depressed and having a huge crisis of faith that [she] wasn't a good musician or a good drag queen". She also said that 'I'm In Love With A Ghost' was written about mourning her relationship whilst continuing to live in the house they renovated together on Trixie Motel.

== Release and Promotion ==
On the 7th of August 2026, Mattel posted on social media platform X (formerly Twitter), writing, "what if I told you we aren't even very far away from another EP of my sad acoustic little country boy music". [ref: Trixie Mattel™ (@[user]) on X, X (formerly Twitter)] She made a similar post on the 7th of September, "what if I told you another sad white boy album is seriously nigh", posting a pumpkin emoji in the post's replies. [ref: Trixie Mattel™ (@[user]) on X, X (formerly Twitter)] On September 22nd, Mattel announced the Halloween-themed EP on social media, scheduled for release on October 2nd the following week, as well as the corresponding lead single 'Ghost on the Moon' for release on September 25th. [ref: Trixie Mattel Announces Halloween Album, Single “Ghost On the Moon” Out Friday, PHANTASMAG]

Following the release of the EP on October 6th, Mattel posted a 45-minute Halloween special entitled 'Trixie's Halloween Mattelathon' to her YouTube channel intending to showcase the songs on the EP. [ref: Trixie Mattel on Her Synth-Spook Approach to Halloween with "'Till Death Do Us Part" - RUE MORGUE] Plot-wise, the 'Mattelathon' follows Trixie during the production and filming of a live television Halloween fundraiser whilst being stalked by a killer. [ref: ] The special included performances of "'Till Death Do Us Part', 'Ghost On The Moon', 'I'm In Love With A Ghost', and 'Tell Me When It's Over', and had celebrity guest cameos from Luscious Massacr, Inde Navarette, Katya Zamolodchikova, Anna Camp, Jamie Lee Curtis, Kelly Mantle, Brittany Broski, Roz Hernandez, and Orville Peck. [ref: Chris Colfer weighs in on Glee reboot, Trixie's Halloween treat & all the best LGBTQ+ releases this week, Queerty]

data.title: California Flag Handicap
data.text:
The California Flag Handicap is a Black type American Thoroughbred horse race for California-bred or sired horses aged three years old or older over a distance of about furlongs on the downhill turf course scheduled annually in mid-October at Santa Anita Park in Arcadia, California. It is part of the Golden State Series of races sponsored by the California Thoroughbred Breeders Association. [ref: California Thoroughbred Breeders Association - Golden State Series Schedule, California Thoroughbred Breeders Association] [ref: Kings River Knight Much The Best On Hillside Turf As He Rallies To Take $100,000 California Flag Handicap By 1 1/2 Lengths, Santa Anita Park] The event currently carries a purse of $100,000.

==History==

The event was inaugurated on 19 October 2013 at Santa Anita Park as the eighth race on the racecard over a distance of about furlongs on the downhill turf.

The event was named for California Flag, the 2009 Breeders' Cup Turf Sprint winner and Co-California Horse of the Year. [ref: Classy The Chosen Vron Heads Field Of 11 In Sunday’s $100,000 California Flag Handicap, Santa Anita Park]

In 2018, the race was shortened to 5 furlongs and excluded Santa Anita’s characteristic downhill. The race remained shortened at about 5.5 furlongs in 2019 and 2020 before returning to its original length in 2021.

data.title: Mary Halsey
data.text:
Mary Halsey is an American viral video performer known as Missy Elliott's "Funky White Sister" after a July 2018 karaoke performance of Elliott's song "Work It" at Goddard Park in Warwick, Rhode Island, was widely shared online and praised by Elliott. [ref: Watch Missy Elliott perform with "funky white sister" Mary Halsey, NME] [ref: Missy Elliott Praises Rhode Island Woman's Viral Rendition of "Work It", Exclaim!] She subsequently performed "Work It" on The Ellen DeGeneres Show on 13 September 2018, where Elliott surprised her on stage for a duet, performed live on Good Morning Britain, and served as a red-carpet correspondent for Ellen at the American Music Awards in October 2018 and the Grammy Awards in February 2019.

== Early life and background ==
Rhode Island Monthly identified Halsey's hometown as LeRoy, New York. She has sung karaoke since 1989. "Work It" became her regular karaoke song after a 2003 contest; she told Ellen DeGeneres that the positive reaction led her to study the lyrics until it became her go-to song. In 2018 she was working as a recreation assistant at Genesis HealthCare's Coventry Center in Rhode Island.

== Viral breakthrough in 2018 ==
In July 2018, Halsey performed "Work It" at "Karaoke Sunday" in Goddard Park, Warwick, Rhode Island, holding a shofar. Her best friend Pamela Wilsey filmed the performance, and Halsey posted it to Facebook that evening. The nickname "Missy's funky white sister" was Halsey's own self-description in her act, which Elliott adopted and amplified when she shared and praised the video on 8 August 2018.

Exclaim! reported that Elliott was among more than 7 million people who had viewed the performance, and quoted Elliott's post describing Halsey as her "FUNKY WHITE SISTER" and saying she "straight killed 'Work It' sound effects and all."

== Television appearances and coverage ==
On 13 September 2018, Halsey appeared on The Ellen DeGeneres Show. She performed "Work It" carrying the shofar, and Elliott surprised her on stage for a duet. [ref: Missy Elliott surprises viral video star who sang "Work It", The FADER] [ref: Missy Elliott Performs "Work It" on 'Ellen' With Viral Video Star, XXL] She received a signed shirt from Elliott and a "Missy's Funky White Sister" jacket from Ellen DeGeneres.

Halsey also performed live on Good Morning Britain. The programme's official clip is titled "Missy Elliot's Funky White Sister, Mary Halsey, Performs Live | Good Morning Britain". [ref: Missy Elliot's Funky White Sister, Mary Halsey, Performs Live, YouTube (Good Morning Britain)]

Two further national items were coverage of the Ellen moment, not separate studio interviews. TODAY published a PopStart video report, "See Missy Elliott surprise viral video star Mary Halsey on 'Ellen'". [ref: See Missy Elliott surprise viral video star Mary Halsey on 'Ellen', TODAY.com] Billboard News published a video segment, "Missy Elliott Surprises Viral Fan Mary Halsey on 'Ellen'". [ref: Missy Elliott Surprises Viral Fan Mary Halsey on 'Ellen', Billboard]

== Red-carpet correspondent work ==
Ellen DeGeneres sent Halsey as a red-carpet correspondent to the American Music Awards on 9 October 2018, accompanied by producer Andy Zenor, and to the Grammy Awards in February 2019. A contemporary American Music Awards report noted that DeGeneres sent Halsey to the AMAs as her special correspondent. [ref: The 46th Annual American Music Awards, Cal Times] Official Ellen videos document both assignments. [ref: Mary Halsey at the American Music Awards (Ellen), YouTube (The Ellen Show)] [ref: Mary Halsey at the Grammys (Ellen), YouTube (The Ellen Show)] In a second studio appearance on Ellen on 30 January 2019, Halsey performed "Anaconda" and received two Grammy tickets.

== Later work and recognition ==
Rhode Island Monthly named Halsey one of its Top Ten Rhode Islanders of the Year in its December 2018 issue. From 6 February 2019, she hosted "Skyline Karaoke Idol" on Wednesdays at Skyline at Waterplace in Providence. She appeared at Creators Live in Branson, Missouri, on 20 June 2020, and hosts The Magic Mary Podcast.

On 15 September 2026, a collaboration video with Nicki Marie was posted on Instagram by nickimarieinc, with Halsey (mary.halsey_) credited as collaborator. [ref: Nicki Marie collaboration reel with Mary Halsey, Instagram]

data.title: Abdulmalek Majeed Hameed
data.text:
Abdulmalek Majeed (Arabic: عبد الملك مجيد; born 1997) is an Iraqi cybersecurity specialist whose work focuses on digital security awareness, information security, and the prevention of online extortion. [ref: خبير أمن المعلومات عبد الملك مجيد يقدم وصاياه لمكافحة الابتزاز الالكتروني, Third River News]

== Early life and background ==
Majeed was born in Baghdad, Iraq, in 1997. According to Third River News, he began his activities in technology in 2014, initially sharing educational material through social media. The publication reports that he subsequently focused on information security and online extortion prevention beginning in 2015.

== Cybersecurity activities ==
Majeed has discussed cybersecurity awareness, personal data protection, and the risks associated with online extortion. [ref: خبير أمن المعلومات عبد الملك مجيد يقدم وصاياه لمكافحة الابتزاز الالكتروني, وكالة النهر الثالث الإخبارية]

In an August 2026 interview with Ashur News Agency, he described his involvement in assisting individuals affected by online extortion and promoting safer digital practices. [ref: عبد الملك مجيد: الابتزاز الإلكتروني لم يعد مجرد جريمة تُرتكب خلف الشاشات ، بل تحدياً مجتمعياً يمس الأسرة والشباب والمؤسسات, Ashur News Agency]

His public statements have addressed online impersonation, account security, fraudulent links, and the misuse of artificial intelligence to create manipulated images and videos.

== Digital safety awareness ==
Majeed has advocated stronger awareness of online risks, including the use of secure passwords, two-factor authentication, and caution when interacting with unfamiliar links. [ref: وكالة اشور الاخبارية » عبد الملك مجيد: الابتزاز الإلكتروني لم يعد مجرد جريمة تُرتكب خلف الشاشات ، بل تحدياً مجتمعياً يمس الأسرة والشباب والمؤسسات, www.ashurnews.com]

He has also emphasized the importance of preserving evidence and contacting the appropriate authorities when responding to online extortion.
