data.title: Will Markeith Green
data.text:
Will Green (born February 10, 1979) is an American entrepreneur and event promoter from Louisville, Kentucky. He founded Just Lit Candle Co., a scented candle business established in 2020, and created Trap-N-Candles, an event concept combining candle making with hip-hop and R&B music. Green has also participated in school supply fundraising in Louisville. [ref: Viral post sparks community effort to meet JCPS students' needs, The Courier-Journal]

== Early life ==

Green was born on February 10, 1979, in Louisville, Kentucky, where he grew up. He later became involved in the local entertainment industry, working as an event promoter and planner.

== Career ==

=== Event promotion (2010–2020) ===

Green began working as an event promoter and planner in 2010. For approximately ten years, he organized and promoted parties, nightlife events, and other social gatherings.

In 2020, restrictions associated with the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States affected in-person entertainment events. During this period, Green began exploring other business opportunities.

=== Just Lit Candle Co. (2020–present) ===

In 2020, Green founded Just Lit Candle Co., a scented candle business based in Louisville, Kentucky. During the pandemic, he began learning to make candles through instructional videos on YouTube and experimented with ingredients and fragrances before starting the business.

Green used marketing methods from his work in event promotion. The company's advertising has incorporated humor, popular culture, and suggestive themes.

According to Green, the company generated approximately $50,000 in sales during its first year, with sales increasing in later years. These figures have not been independently verified.

The company's fragrances have included Grey Sweatpants, Sunday Morning Mimosas, and Mr Teakwood.

=== Trap-N-Candles (2023–present) ===

In 2023, Green created Trap-N-Candles, an event concept combining candle making with music and entertainment. The events include candle-making activities, hip-hop, R&B, live DJs, and a nightclub-style setting. Some events include alcoholic beverages.

The concept combines Green's event promotion work with his candle business.

== Community involvement ==

Green has participated in efforts to provide school supplies to children in Louisville. In September 2026, The Courier-Journal published an article discussing his involvement in backpack fundraising and distribution efforts for local students. The article reported that he had been involved in backpack fundraising for approximately ten years and helped collect more than 3,000 backpacks ahead of the school year.

data.title: Kyōkaku
data.text:
Kyōkaku (, also read Gyōkaku; 1395 – 19 September 1473) was a Japanese Buddhist monk of the Hossō school in the Muromachi period. He was born in the 2nd year of the Ōei era and died on the 27th day of the 8th month of Bunmei 5. His father was the kampaku Kujō Tsunenori, [ref: コンサイス日本人名事典 第5版, 三省堂] and his mother came from the of Jōdo Shinshū (later the ). Through this maternal connection he took in Rennyo, who later became the 8th head of the Hongan-ji, as his disciple, and the two remained teacher and pupil for life despite belonging to different schools. He is also known for having served four times as bettō, the head of Kōfuku-ji (the great temple of Nara), with the rank of. His posthumous name was.

== Life ==
Records confirm that Kyōkaku's mother (Horikawa no Tsubone, Buddhist name ) came from the Hongan-ji, but her exact identity is unclear. Based on Kyōkaku's year of birth, however, she is generally considered to have been a daughter of the 5th head; if so, Rennyo's father was Kyōkaku's cousin. At the time the Hongan-ji was in a state of decline and, to obtain the protection of the Kujō family, one of the regent houses, it performed services for the family somewhat like those of a. Kyōkaku's mother is thought to have attracted Tsunenori's attention while she was in service with the Kujō family.

At the age of 13 he took Buddhist vows under at the of Kōfuku-ji. The abbacy (monzeki) of the Daijō-in was customarily held by members of the Kujō family, and at that time his elder brother occupied it. When died young, Kyōkaku succeeded him as abbot at the age of 16.

He was appointed bettō of Kōfuku-ji on the 7th day of the 2nd month of Ōei 33 (1426), and was later appointed three more times, in Eikyō 3 (1431), Kanshō 2 (1461) and Bunmei 1 (1469). He had close ties with the central government and was on friendly terms with leading figures of the Muromachi shogunate, including the 6th shōgun Ashikaga Yoshinori. In Eikyō 10 (1438), however, he incurred Yoshinori's displeasure by asking for a reduction of the contributions owed to the shogunate, and was expelled from the Daijō-in. There was no direct master–disciple relationship between him and, who was appointed abbot in his place, and after Kyōkaku's restoration following Yoshinori's death the two waged a long, covert struggle for control of the Daijō-in.

When Yoshinori was killed in the Kakitsu incident, Kyōkaku, with the support of the (local warrior families) of Yamato such as and, entered and resumed his activities. He contested the office of deputy administrator of the, toll barriers on the Yodo River system, with the brothers and. In Kakitsu 3 (1443), through the good offices of the kanrei (both men had been banished by Yoshinori), he was granted an audience with the 7th shōgun Ashikaga Yoshikatsu. [ref: 田中慶治「和泉国上守護代宇高氏と興福寺官符衆徒棟梁古市氏」（小山靖憲 編『戦国期畿内の政治社会構造』（和泉書院、2006年） ISBN 978-4-7576-0374-5 および田中慶治『中世後期畿内近国の権力構造』（清文堂、2013年） ISBN 978-4-7924-0978-4 所収] With Mochikuni's backing Kōsen was driven out, and under Kyōkaku, Furuichi Insen, and were entrusted with the control of Yamato.

In Kakitsu 4 (1444) he gathered the kokujin of Yamato and ordered them to attack Kōsen and his brother, but they were defeated, and he in turn came under attack from Jun'ei. He then built Kionzan Castle on the hill within the precincts of the Daijō-in and held out there, but the castle fell the following year and he fled to in.

In the 4th month of Bun'an 4 (1447), Furuichi Insen brought him by force to Furuichi, the base of his family. Kyōkaku tried several times afterwards to return to An'i-ji, but each time Insen stopped him, and he was compelled to stay in Furuichi. [ref: Kyōgaku Shiyōshō (), entries for Bun'an 4, 4th month 13th day; 5th month 23rd day; and 6th month 27th day.] Behind this lay Insen's wish, troubled as he was by his struggle with the Tsutsui clan and by defections within his own kin, to preserve the cohesion of the main line of the by keeping Kyōkaku under his protection; Kyōkaku, for his part, needed the military strength of the Furuichi to maintain his own authority and so could not refuse the demands of Insen and the Furuichi. As a result Kyōkaku remained in Furuichi until his death, a stay that lasted 27 years until he died in Bunmei 5. [ref: 田中慶治「中世後期畿内国人層の動向と家臣団編成 -大和国古市氏を中心に-」（初出:『日本史研究』406号（1996年）/所収:田中『中世後期畿内近国の権力構造』（清文堂、2013年） ISBN 978-4-7924-0978-4）] [ref: 田中慶治「国人古市氏の馬借・関支配について ―南山城を中心にして―」『高円史学』13号、高円史学会、1997年、62-79頁。]

In the 7th month of the same year, when an uprising of bashaku (packhorse drivers) broke out in Yamato, Ōmi, Kawachi, Yamashiro and elsewhere, a rumour spread that Kyōkaku and Insen had set the bashaku in motion in order to destroy Nara, and the (the assembly of Kōfuku-ji's monk-warriors) placed the two under the sanction known as. Kyōkaku condemned the uprising in his diary, and the charge against him was false; but the historian Tanaka Keiji holds that Insen, who was closely tied to the bashaku, can be regarded as having organized and supported the uprising.

Afterwards, however, Kyōkaku was again restored, reappointed bettō of Kōfuku-ji, and wielded great influence over the whole of Yamato.

In the 10th month of Bun'an 5 (1448) he was summoned by his ailing elder brother Kujō Mitsuie and asked who should succeed as head of the Kujō family: the 10-year-old son (Kujō Masatada) of, Mitsuie's sickly heir (who was 28 but had still not come of age), or Mitsuie's own 4-year-old son (Kujō Masamoto). After some thought, Kyōkaku suggested that the 10-year-old be made head of the house for the time being, on the understanding that he would later pass the headship to. This was adopted: the 10-year-old became Mitsuie's adopted son and succeeded to the house, and Kakamaru took the tonsure. [ref: 酒井紀美『経覚』p150-p154]

When Kujō Mitsuie died in Hōtoku 1 (1449), Kyōkaku acted as guardian of his orphaned sons, the brothers Masatada and Masamoto.

On the 27th day of the 7th month of Hōtoku 2 (1450) he received an imperial decree naming him senior daisōjō. When the Tsutsui clan and the shuto who supported them obstructed his pilgrimage to the Kasuga Shrine to report the appointment, Furuichi Insen and in the 8th month demolished the residences of members of the Tsutsui faction (an act signifying ).

After Furuichi Insen died in Kyōtoku 2 (1453), Kyōkaku made peace with Kōsen in the following year, Kyōtoku 3 (1454).

From Kōshō 2 (1456) onward he was relied upon to the point of annoyance by, a grandson of his brother Mitsuie who had become monzeki of the, a sub-temple of Tōdai-ji. Kakujin did almost none of the duties expected of the abbot of the Tōnan-in and turned to Kyōkaku for everything, which made him a constant source of worry for Kyōkaku. [ref: 酒井紀美『経覚』p165-p168]

He died at on the 27th day of the 8th month of Bunmei 5 (1473).

== Family tree ==
His father Kujō Tsunenori was a son of Nijō Michihira and succeeded to the Kujō family after becoming the of Kujō Michinori. Kyōkaku was his youngest child. The family relationships at the time of his birth can be traced from the (autograph testament) that Tsunenori left in Ōei 3 (1396). The eldest brother Tadamoto, who should have become head of the family, died before his father, and the second brother Noritsugu inherited the Kujō house. Among the brothers, had already entered the Daijō-in, and there was an elder brother one year older, Mitsunori (later Mitsuie).

Regarding the headship of the Kujō family, in the 10th month of Bun'an 5 (1448) the bedridden Mitsuie consulted him about the succession (see above).

== Character ==
The historian compares Kyōkaku with his rival Jinson, author of the. In her assessment, Jinson wrote about events from a distance, in a calm and objective manner, and did not side with either of two opposing forces; Kyōkaku, by contrast, was curious and active, ready to involve himself even where he was not wanted. Faced with two opposing forces, he would side with one on his own judgement and stand by it to the end, and he was a man full of chivalrous spirit who sought to repay good faith with good faith. [ref: 酒井紀美『夢から探る中世』角川書店、2005年] According to the entry in Jinson's Daijōin Jisha Zōjiki for the 21st day of the 6th month of Ōnin 1, Kyōkaku visited Jinson that day and said that he would go up to the capital to watch. This was just after news reached Nara that the Ōnin War had broken out in Kyoto, so Kyōkaku was going to "watch" the battles of the Ōnin War. Jinson described his conduct as "improper" (). [ref: 瀬戸祐規「『大乗院寺社雑事記』『文正記』に見る長禄・寛正の内訌」（初出:大乗院寺社雑事記研究会 編『大乗院寺社雑事記研究論集 第三巻』（和泉書院、2006年）/木下聡 編著『シリーズ・室町幕府の研究 第一巻 管領斯波氏』（戒光祥出版、2015年）ISBN 978-4-86403-146-2）]

His diary is the Kyōgaku Shiyōshō (see below).

== Relationship with Rennyo ==
Although they belonged to different schools, Kyōkaku had close ties with the Ōtani Hongan-ji, his mother's family. When the 7th head Zonnyo died, he sent an envoy to the Hongan-ji to offer condolences, saying that Zonnyo had been "an acquaintance of fifty years and a benefactor without equal" (), and later visited the Hongan-ji in person to offer his condolences.

Rennyo, born as an illegitimate son of Zonnyo, was placed in Kyōkaku's care as a child and studied under him, and afterwards the two supported each other as teacher and pupil whenever either faced a crisis. In addition, Kyōkaku appointed, the head priest of, a branch temple of the Hongan-ji, as deputy of Hosorogi-gō (also written ) in the in Echizen, a manor of the Daijō-in under his control.

When the Hongan-ji faced a threat to its very survival through persecution by Enryaku-ji in the, it was to Kyōkaku that Rennyo first came for advice. Kyōkaku proposed that he move to Yoshizaki in the Kawaguchi estate, which he had entrusted to, and make a fresh start there. Echizen was home to many followers of Jōdo Shinshū and of other Pure Land schools, which made it ideal for Rennyo's missionary work; from Kyōkaku's side, the manor was then suffering continued usurpation by the, the shugodai of Echizen, and by Asakura Toshikage as a result of their conflict, and he is said to have hoped that Rennyo, a trusted "nephew", would serve as a kind of deputy for the Kawaguchi estate.

With Kyōkaku's advice and 's support, Rennyo founded the Yoshizaki Gobō at Yoshizaki and began his missionary activity there. At the same time he never neglected to see that the of the Kawaguchi estate reached Kyōkaku safely. It was shortly after Kyōkaku's death that the Hongan-ji grew into a major power in the Hokuriku region.

== Kyōgaku Shiyōshō ==
The diary that Kyōkaku left is called the (). It is also known as and. The original, in 82 volumes, is held by the National Archives of Japan () and was designated an Important Cultural Property in 2003 (one of the volumes has been found to be a diary of Jinson that was handed down by mistake). [ref: [http://www.archives.go.jp/news/030322.html 「経覚私要鈔」等が、国の重要文化財に指定] - 国立公文書館] The surviving entries run from the 10th month of Ōei 22 (1415) to the 9th month of Bunmei 4 (1472), the year before his death.

It records in detail matters ranging from temple administration and the management of temple estates within Kōfuku-ji to the movements of the kokujin of Yamato, the central political world in Kyoto, and the affairs of his relatives the Kujō family and the Hongan-ji, and it is a source for the politics, economy, society and religion of the Muromachi period. Little of the earlier part survives, however. It was lost when, on the 14th day of the 9th month of Bun'an 2 (1445), Kyōkaku set fire to Kionzan Castle (written; also ) himself and fled from the. Kyōkaku himself noted: "As for my diary, the part before Bun'an was lost and scattered when it burned at the Zenjō-in; it survives from Bun'an 2 onward" ().

data.title: Marco Zappone
data.text:
----

Marco Zappone, né en 1966 à Rome [ref: Marco Zappone, Les Rencontres d'Arles], en Italie, est un auteur [ref: Zappone] éditeur [ref: Champs de bataille, Éditions Photosynthèses] franco-italien installé à Arles, en Provence, depuis 1998.

=== Biographie ===
Après une enfance passée entre la France, l’Italie, l’Afrique et le Moyen-Orient, [ref: Marco Zappone, Les Rencontres d'Arles] il étudie l’anthropologie et le cinéma à l’université La Sapienza de Rome et à l’École des hautes études en sciences sociales (EHESS), à Paris. Après plusieurs années consacrées à la bibliophilie et au collectionnisme, il fonde la maison d’édition Photosynthèses, spécialisée dans la publication de beaux livres, ainsi que de textes et d’essais sur la photographie et les arts visuels [ref: ]. Rattachée au groupe Libella, la maison d’édition est située au 12, rue Vernon, à Arles [ref: ].

Bien qu’il ait envisagé dès son plus jeune âge de faire de la photographie son métier, cette passion devient finalement le fil conducteur du projet éditorial de la maison. Il participe notamment à la réalisation, avec Yan Morvan, de Champs de bataille, [ref: Yan Morvan: entretien avec Marco Zappone, L'Œil de la Photographie Magazine] un ouvrage consacré aux paysages de champs de bataille à travers le monde. L’ouvrage reçoit le Grand Prix du jury de la Nuit du livre en 2016 [ref: La Nuit du livre 2016 dévoile ses 13 lauréats, Livres Hebdo]. Après une tentative infructueuse de reconversion dans la tauromachie, passion qui l’anime toujours, Marco Zappone met fin à ses activités au sein des éditions Photosynthèses en 2023. Il est père de deux enfants, Niccolò et Giulietta.

data.text:
Trade Intelligence Global Pte. Ltd. is a Singapore-based software and data company focused on international [ref: What is TradeInt?, TradeInt]
trade intelligence. Its main product, TradeInt, is a platform that provides access to global import and export data including shipment information and tools for analyzing trade activity. The company was incorporated in Singapore November 2018, and its public company information identifies its business activity as providing a platform with global trade data information. TradeInt is designed to help businesses research international markets, identify buyers and suppliers, monitor trade flows, and analyze market opportunities using trade and shipment data.

data.title: Darling Causeway
data.text:
----

The Darling Causeway is a 10km (6.2 mi) major road connecting the Great Western Highway at Mount Victoria to the Bells Line of Road at Bell in the Blue Mountains of New South Wales, Australia.

The road is two lanes in each direction, with the occasional overtaking lane, but can get narrow in some sections, and many sections have no shoulders. The road gained unexpected importance as a result of the sudden closure of the Mitchell's Causeway on the Great Western Highway in March 2026 [ref: ] [ref: ] due to the discovery of deep cracks in the pavement as the result of the internal fill deteriorating. [ref: ]

As a result, Transport for NSW has been conducting roadworks along the route to strengthen and replace the pavement due to the increase in traffic volume along the route. [ref: ]

The road is classified as Main Road 184 for its entire length.

== Route ==
The Darling Causeway begins as Station Street at the intersection with the Great Western Highway at Mount Victoria, and heads north as the road changes name to the Darling Causeway as it passes the Mount Victoria railway station. The road follows a ridge in the Blue Mountains that it shares with the Blue Mountains Line, which the road parallels for its entire length. The road then terminates at an intersection with the Bells Line of Road and Chifley Road at Bell.

data.title: R. K. Mishra
data.text:
Rakesh Kumar Mishra, also known as R. K. Mishra, is an Indian politician and retired Indian Police Service (IPS) officer. A member of the 1986 batch of the Bihar cadre, he served in the Bihar Police and several central armed police forces, including the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) and Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP). He was also Director General-cum-Commandant General of Home Guards and Fire Services in Bihar.

Mishra joined the Jan Suraaj movement after retiring from the police service. He contested the 2025 Bihar Legislative Assembly election from Darbhanga as a Jan Suraaj Party candidate.

== Early life and education ==

Mishra is from Saharsa district in Bihar. He studied civil engineering at Banaras Hindu University, where he received a gold medal. According to his election affidavit, he graduated in 1983.

== Police career ==

Mishra joined the Indian Police Service in August 1986 and was assigned to the Bihar cadre.

Among his early postings was Bhagalpur, where he served as an Assistant Superintendent of Police during the communal riots of 1989.

He subsequently held district policing appointments in Bihar and the region that later became Jharkhand, before moving to central police organisations.

=== Central police organisations ===

Mishra served in the CISF in several capacities. In December 2016, his appointment as Additional Director General of the force was reported.

He also served in the CRPF, including as Inspector General of its Jharkhand sector. He was identified in that position in June 2015, when the force was involved in operations against Maoist insurgents in the state.

Mishra later became Additional Director General of the ITBP. The 2019 IPS civil list records his appointment to that position in July 2017.

=== Bihar Police and Home Guards ===

Mishra also held senior positions in the Bihar Police. In October 2012, he was promoted to Additional Director General and assigned responsibility for police modernisation.

After returning from central deputation, he took charge as Director General-cum-Commandant General of Bihar Home Guards and Fire Services on 27 August 2019.

During his tenure, the department announced measures concerning Home Guard personnel, including the processing of retirement benefits and the payment of allowances. In January 2020, Mishra described arrangements for more timely payments and settlement of retirement benefits.

In March 2020, Prabhat Khabar reported that the department had issued 18 standing orders governing service conditions, duty allocation, payments and grievance procedures.

The department was also involved in the deployment of trained Home Guards for the security of Reserve Bank of India currency chests in Bihar.

== Political career ==

Following his retirement, Mishra became associated with the Jan Suraaj movement led by Prashant Kishor.

In May 2023, he was among a group of retired IPS officers who joined the movement at an event in Patna. The Indian Express reported his participation alongside other former police and administrative officers.

Mishra remained associated with Jan Suraaj as it developed into a political party in October 2024.

In October 2025, the party selected him to contest the Darbhanga constituency in the Bihar Legislative Assembly election.

He finished third, receiving 11,758 votes. The seat was won by Sanjay Saraogi of the Bharatiya Janata Party, while Umesh Sahani of the Vikassheel Insaan Party finished second.

== Awards and honours ==

Mishra received the Police Medal for Meritorious Service in 2003, according to the Ministry of Home Affairs' IPS civil list.

He was awarded the President's Police Medal for Distinguished Service on Republic Day in 2010.

data.title: Interior Design Society of Kenya
data.text:
The Interior Design Society of Kenya (IDSK) is a professional association representing interior designers, spatial planners, design studios, material suppliers, and allied manufacturers in Kenya. [ref: About Us – Interior Design Society of Kenya (IDSK), Interior Design Society of Kenya] Headquartered in Nairobi, the society advocates for formal industry regulation, professional accreditation, ethical practice, and sustainable interior architecture across residential, commercial, and public sectors in Kenya. [ref: IDSk Supports New Bill With Amendments and Demands Legal Recognition, Jicho News]

== History and Governance ==
The organization was established to serve as a unified voice for practitioners in Kenya's built-environment sector, where interior design had historically operated without a dedicated statutory framework.

IDSK is governed by an executive board led by President Cecilia Nakhungu Mbati. [ref: Architects' alliance opposes bill on regulation of built environment professions, Kenya News Agency] The society engages with national educational bodies, TVET institutions, and universities to ensure academic curricula align with evolving professional standards, spatial safety regulations, accessibility requirements, and building codes. [ref: IDSK Industry Integration Programme, Interior Design Society of Kenya]

== Key Objectives and Programs ==
The society's core mandate includes regulating professional practice, protecting consumers from unqualified operators, and facilitating professional development. Its main initiatives include:

* Industry Integration Programme (IIP): A structured transition and mentorship framework designed to connect interior design graduates and emerging professionals with practical studio experience, site mentorship, and industry network opportunities.
* Workforce Placement Programme: A professional pathway program matching qualified interior designers with employment opportunities across corporate fit-out firms, architectural practices, and design agencies.
* Circular Design and Sustainability: Advocacy initiatives promoting eco-friendly spatial planning, energy efficiency, acoustic design, indoor air quality, biophilic elements, and the sourcing of local timber, stone, and sustainable materials.
* Interior Design Summit: An annual flagship convention uniting design professionals, policy leaders, suppliers, and real estate developers. The 2026 summit took place at the Sarit Expo Centre in Nairobi under the theme "Building the Interior Design Economy." [ref: Interior Design Summit 2026: Building the Interior Design Economy, Interior Design Society of Kenya]

== Legislative Advocacy ==
In 2026, IDSK actively participated in legislative discussions before the National Assembly Committee on Housing, Urban Planning and Public Works regarding the Architectural and Quantity Surveying Practitioners Bill, 2026 (National Assembly Bill No. 47 of 2026), which sought to replace the colonial-era Architects and Quantity Surveyors Act (Cap. 525). [ref: Parliament Seeks Stakeholders’ Views on Bill to Regulate Architects and Quantity Surveyors, KTN News Kenya]

During parliamentary stakeholder submissions, IDSK President Cecilia Mbati expressed general support for statutory regulation while submitting clause-by-clause amendments aimed at safeguarding the independence of interior design practitioners:

1. Title and Scope Expansion: Requesting that the legislation be renamed the Built Environment Practitioners Act to explicitly encompass interior designers, landscape architects, and construction project managers.
2. Regulatory Council Representation: Advocating for dedicated statutory representation for interior designers on the proposed joint regulatory board under Clause 71D.
3. Transitional Grandfathering Provisions: Demanding clear grandfathering mechanisms under Part X (Clause 58) to register existing interior design professionals with over five years of verified experience who had operated legally prior to statutory enactment.
4. Stamping Authority for Fit-Out Documentation: Requesting statutory recognition under Clause 46(1) for technical documents, spatial planning layouts, material specifications, and interior fit-out drawings stamped by registered interior designers.

data.title: CMoMa
data.text:
thumb|Schematic distribution of the three cell lines in a cMoMa individual. Cells with variant 1 are violet, cells with variant two are pink and wildtype cells are orange.

Clustered monoallelic mosaicism (abbreviated cMoMa) is a term in the field of human genetics describing a rare form of mosaicism. cMoMa individuals carry two distinct, closely spaced genetic variants (e.g. single nucleotide deletions). Both located on the same parental allele but mutually exclusive on the level of individual sequencing reads. Thus resulting in three distinct cell lines (the two variants and the remaining wildtype allele).

The term, as well as the postulated mechanism, originates from a 2026 publication by the group of Christian Schaaf at the Institute of Human Genetics at Heidelberg University Hospital, in Human Genetics and Genomics Advances (HGG Advances). The team first observed the specific genetic constellation in two monozygotic twins with HNRNPU-associated neurodevelopmental disorder.

== Background ==

=== Recurrent, surprising genotype constellations ===
In diagnostic human genetics, cases have repeatedly been described in which two distinct variants lie conspicuously close to each other on the same gene or allele, even though there was no indication that they shared a common origin (they behave like two independent mutational events). Such spatial proximity is statistically unlikely, although it is difficult to calculate exactly how unlikely.

Examples of such constellations that were retrospectively attributed to the cMoMa pattern can be found in several published case reports:

* WAS gene: two different mutations in a single male germ cell, resulting in a female carrier who was mosaic for two different variants.
* ACVRL1 gene: germline mosaicism with two distinct mutant alleles in hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia with pulmonary arterial hypertension.
* AHDC1 gene (Xia-Gibbs syndrome): two adjacent mosaic deletions that likewise never occurred together on the same sequencing read.

=== Genetic diagnostics in the Heidelberg twins ===
In the two twins in Heidelberg, two de novo 1-bp deletions (c.1463del, c.1466del; allele fractions ~20–39 %) were identified in the HNRNPU gene. The mosaicism was subsequently confirmed by Sanger sequencing in leukocytes and buccal mucosa. The two variants never occurred together on the same sequencing read, yet according to long-read sequencing both were located on the paternal allele; the maternal allele was wild-type throughout.

The diagnostic workup – whole-genome, long-read and Sanger sequencing as well as the molecular phasing analysis – was carried out largely by Julia Dennig.

== Definition ==

# Two closely adjacent genetic variants in the same gene.
# Located on the same parental allele.
# The variants are mutually exclusive at the read level.

== Proposed mechanism ==
Böhnlein and Maaß weighed two models against each other. Model 1 (two independent mutational events) would have required both deletions to arise independently within the same ±3-bp window before the twins separated – i.e. within roughly the first eight cell divisions; the calculated probability of this was 10⁻⁷ to 10⁻¹⁰, and the model was rejected as unlikely.

Model 2 (favoured) assumes a single mutational event, followed by divergent, error-prone repair on the two sister chromatids: one chromatid acquires deletion A, the other deletion B; after cell division, the two segregate into separate daughter cell lineages. This model explains both the mutual exclusivity and the shared paternal phase with only one mutational event.

== Relevance for genetic counseling ==
It is proposed, that the recurrence risc for parents with a cMoMa child is not elevated above baseline as the proposed mechanism is incompatible with a germline mosaicism.

[https://www.youtube.com/@[user] Relap5e] is a Philippine-Based rock band formed in Angeles City, Pampanga in January 2026. The band is known for its relapse-esque music style.

data.title: Cliffords (Band)
data.text:
Cliffords are an Irish alternative/indie guitar band from Cork in Ireland. Bringing guitar-driven arrangements and the vocals of lead singer Iona Lynch at the centre. The band emerged from Cork's prolific independent music scene and developed a strong live following through performances across Ireland, the Uk and Europe.

History

Cliffords formed in Ballincollig while the band members were still at school. Within a year of forming they won University College Cork's Battle of the Bands competition in 2022.

The band released their debut EP, Strawberry Scented, independently in 2024, following up that release with Salt of the Lee in May 2025. The lyrics, written by singer Iona Lynch, explore themes of identity, relationships and growing up in Cork.

Cliffords have performed at festivals including Glastonbury and The Great Escape, alongside touring in Ireland and the United Kingdom.

Their music has been featured in NME, Rolling Stone UK and Hot Press, with critics drawing comparisons to Wolf Alice and The Cranberries.

Members

* Iona Lynch – lead vocals, rhythm guitar
* Gavin Dawkins – bass guitar, trumpet, backing vocals
* Harry Menton – lead guitar, backing vocals
* Locon O'Toole – keyboards

data.title: 681 (genre)
data.text:
681 is the genre of music that consist of exactly vocals and percussion instruments. It combines a capella with minimalist dance music. An example is the song Crabapples by Bruce Peninsula. [ref: Bruce Peninsula climbing the musical ladder, Interrobang]

This is the artificial name of minimalist vocal dance music.

Many main genres have a given artificial name. For example, an artificial name trance is given to usually minimalist ambient rhythmic dance music with tempo between 120 and 150 BPM.

== Etymology ==

The name 681 originates from the list of natural numbers. We have a=1 and skip 2 to get b=3 as the next notable number. The formula of the square of a binomial is (a+b)^2=a^2+2\cdot a\cdot b+b^2. If we square the exponents of b in each addend, we get the addends a^2, 2\cdot a \cdot b and b^4, respectively. The addends are equal to 1, 6 and 81, respectively. The ratio when the second addend is divided by the first addend is 6/1=6, while the ratio when the third addend is divided by the first addend is 81/1=81. Its concatenation gives 681.

data.title: Stanisław Jabłonowski
data.text:
Stanisław Jabłonowski of the Prus III coat of arms (born 10 March 1799, died 15 August 1878 in Kraków) – prince in the Congress Kingdom of Poland in 1820, participant in the November Uprising, pioneer of the oil industry, and knight of the Order of Virtuti Militari.

He was a direct descendant of the hetmans Stanisław Jan Jabłonowski and Paweł Jan Sapieha, and the son of Prince Stanisław Paweł Jabłonowski and Teodora née Walewska. He received his early education abroad, at an aristocratic boarding school in Paris and at Pastor Gerlach’s educational institution in Switzerland. When he finally returned to the country in 1815, he spoke Polish only with difficulty. In 1814, at a ball given by his mother, he was introduced to Emperor Alexander I; the young prince then declared his desire to enter military service. In 1816 he volunteered for an examination, after which he was accepted as a cadet into the positional battery of the mounted artillery of the Guard. Thanks to his background, he was promoted to the rank of second lieutenant after only two years. Having come into conflict with Grand Duke Konstantin Pavlovich, he resigned in 1821.

After the outbreak of the November Uprising he returned to the army. He served in the 4th Battery of Light Horse Artillery. He took part in the skirmish at Miłosna (18 February 1831), the First Battle of Wawer (19 February), and the Battle of Grochów (25 February), for which he received the Golden Cross of the Order of Virtuti Militari on 16 March 1831. He later fought in the Battle of Domanice and the Battle of Iganie (10 April). Immediately after the latter engagement he was promoted to the rank of captain. He took part in the expedition against the imperial guards. On 26 May 1831 he fought in the Battle of Ostrołęka. When the corps of Tomasz Łubieński crossed the Narew, the position of his battery became threatened. Warned of this, he reacted to the proposal of retreat with the words:

“Then I shall remain here alone. For the first time I am commanding a battery; I will not withdraw without an order.”

After Józef Bem assumed command of all Polish artillery, Jabłonowski became his chief of staff. He took part in the fortification of Warsaw and then took command of the 2nd Battery of Light Horse Artillery, which formed part of the Reserve Artillery Corps commanded by Colonel Chorzewski. He participated in the defence of Warsaw, fighting first near the Mokotów tollgates and later near the Jerusalem tollgates.

He is the author of memoirs of his participation in the November Uprising, entitled Recollections of the Positional Battery of the Mounted Artillery of the Royal Polish Guard.

He was a pioneer of the oil industry in Poland. In 1852, in the Empty Forest (Pusty Las) in Siary, he founded the first industrial-scale mine of so-called rock oil (crude oil seeping from the mountains) in the world [citation needed]. Near the palace in Kobylanka he owned an asphalt factory.

He was married twice. His first wife was Maria Gonzaga-Myszkowska-Wielopolska; his second, in 1875 (when he was already 76 years old), was her mother, Wanda née Ossolińska, secundo voto Potocka. He had no children. He is buried at the Rakowicki Cemetery.

data.title: Okonkwo Christopher Asah
data.text:
Christopher Asah Okonkwo (16 January 1943 – September 1978), popularly known as Seven Seven, was a Nigerian singer-songwriter, music teacher, composer and performer. He's among the revolutionary of Egwu Ekpili traditional Igbo music genre. [ref: Okonkwo Asah (Seven Seven) Biography, Career, Age, Networth, Death [Highlife Musician], Throwback Times Nigeria] [ref: Profile: Okonkwo Asah, African Music Library] [ref: Awka Journal of Research in Music and the Arts (AJRMA), Volume 17, June 2024, Nigerian Journals Online]

He was known for combining traditional instruments with guitars and for using his songs to promote Enugwu Ukwu, his hometown in Anambra State, Nigeria. [ref: Long John — Christopher Asah and his Group of Enugwu Ukwu, Apple Music]

During his musical career, Seven Seven released several albums, including Long John, and performed in different countries. [ref: Long John, Amazon Music] [ref: 51 Lex Presents Tour Africa (feat. Group of Enugwu Ukwu) — EP, Apple Music] He was also involved in music education, teaching at educational institutions in Nigeria. He was known among his admirers by the title "Eze Egwu Ekpili", meaning "King of Egwu Ekpili".

== Early life and education ==

Okonkwo was born on 16 January 1943 into the family of Pa Okoye Asah and Madam Mmankwo Asah of Uruogbo village in Enugwu Ukwu, present-day Njikoka Local Government Area of Anambra State, Nigeria. His parents were musicians. His father played a local guitar, while his mother sang with women's groups. Their musical activities influenced his early interest in music.

He began his primary education in 1949 at St Anthony's Catholic Mission School in Enugwu Ukwu. After losing both parents in 1950, he was taken to Enugu by his uncle, Mathew Ekwedike Asah, where he completed his primary education.

Following his schooling, Okonkwo moved to Nzam in present-day Anambra West Local Government Area. There, he lived with Eze Okoye, who taught him bricklaying. He later worked as a bricklayer for Ronasco, a construction company owned by Chief R. O. Nkwocha, the Ide of Enugwu Ukwu. He became a senior worker who also trained other apprentices.

data.title: Darlington Onyeagoro
data.text:
Darlington Onyeagoro is a Nigerian financial-technology executive and entrepreneur. He held senior operations and management roles at OPay and OKash before co-founding the digital-finance company Aladdin in 2020. [ref: SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION] [ref: Behold, Nigeria’s Leading Techpreneurs] He is also the author of the 2013 book It's Okay to Have a Bad Boss. [ref: Events This Weekend, BellaNaija]

== Early life and education ==
Onyeagoro was born on 22 June 1982 to George and Comfort Onyeagoro.[citation needed] He studied mechanical engineering at the Federal University of Technology, Owerri.

== Career ==

=== Banking and OPay ===
Onyeagoro began his career in Nigerian banking, working at Guaranty Trust Bank and Diamond Bank. In 2023, TechCabal reported that he had about 15 years of experience across those banks and the fintech firms OKash and OPay. [ref: techcabal.com]

At OPay, he served as Director of Operations. [ref: techcabal.com] A 2022 regulatory filing describes the role as Director of Operations and Procurement.

=== OKash ===
Onyeagoro later led OKash, a digital lending company. The 2022 filing lists him as its former managing director,[9] while Techpoint Africa described him as its former chief executive. [ref: Lendsqr is building the infrastructure to power lending in Africa] He left OKash in 2020. [ref: techcabal.com]

=== Aladdin and other ventures ===
After leaving OKash in 2020, Onyeagoro co-founded Aladdin, a Nigerian digital-finance company, and became its chief executive. [ref: techcabal.com] The company launched its mobile banking app in April 2021. [ref: Digital bank unveils revolutionary app, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News] [ref: Aladdin unveil digital bank app, Punch Newspapers] In 2021, Arise News and THISDAY included him in a feature on Nigerian technology entrepreneurs. [ref: Tech, Nigeria’s New Oil – THISDAYLIVE] In a 2023 interview with Nairametrics, he argued that the Nigerian fintech market was close to saturation. [ref: “Nigerian fintech market is almost saturated” - Darlington Onyeagoro, Nairametrics]

Also in 2020, he created Blacklist, a platform for sharing borrower data among lenders. [ref: Lendsqr is building the infrastructure to power lending in Africa] That year he worked as a strategy consultant on Rapid Trace, a product Cadnetwork developed in response to COVID-19. [ref: History as Nigerian firm develops rapid trace to tackle COVID-19, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News]

== Writing and public speaking ==
Onyeagoro's book It's Okay to Have a Bad Boss was launched at Terra Kulture, Lagos, on 28 June 2013.[12] In February 2024, he delivered a lecture titled "Creativity and Innovation in a Digital World" at Igbinedion University, Okada.[10] He was a panellist at the university's artificial-intelligence summit in February 2026.[11]

== Personal life ==
Onyeagoro is married to Vivian Chinonye Onyeagoro; they have four children.[citation needed]

data.title: Ana Khunjua
data.text:
----

Ana Khunjua is a Georgian boxer who represents Belgium in international amateur boxing. She previously represented Georgia. In 2019, she became the first Georgian female boxer to win a medal at a European boxing championship after taking bronze at the European Under-22 Boxing Championships. [ref: პირველი ქართველი მოკრივე ქალი ევროპის ჩემპიონატის მედლით, Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty]

== Early life ==
Khunjua grew up in the village of Sajijao in Khobi Municipality, Georgia. She began training in boxing at the age of 12. According to Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty, she trained in a small local gym and was the only female boxer training there at the time.

== Boxing career ==

=== Georgia ===
In March 2019, Khunjua represented Georgia at the European Under-22 Boxing Championships in Vladikavkaz, Russia. Competing in the women's 54 kg division, she defeated Belarusian boxer Aliaksandra Karpovich by a 5–0 decision in the quarter-final. [ref: EUBC U22 European Boxing Championships Vladikavkaz 2019, European Boxing Confederation] She finished the tournament with a bronze medal, becoming the first Georgian female boxer to win a medal at a European boxing championship.

=== Belgium ===
Khunjua later began representing Belgium in international competition. In April 2025, she competed in the women's 54 kg division at the Brussels Capital Tournament in La Hulpe, Belgium. She defeated France's Kaelya Mopin in the semi-final. [ref: Les Bleu(e)s au tournoi de Bruxelles, Fédération Française de Boxe] In the final, she defeated Italy's Michel Nicol Vescovini to win the tournament. [ref: Brussels Capital Tournament – Brussels, Belgium – April 25–27 2025]

In 2026, Khunjua represented Belgium at the Gee-Bee Tournament in Helsinki, Finland. She competed in the women's 57 kg division against American boxer Deborah Grant. [ref: Brackets Set for USA Boxing Elite High Performance Squad at 2026 Gee Bee Boxing Tournament, USA Boxing] European Boxing reported that Khunjua had previously represented Georgia before switching to Belgium and had won international tournament titles for Belgium. [ref: News, European Boxing]

== Selected achievements ==
* 2019 European Under-22 Boxing Championships — Bronze medal, 54 kg (Georgia)
* 2025 Brussels Capital Tournament — Gold medal, 54 kg (Belgium) [ref: Brussels Capital Tournament – Brussels, Belgium – April 25–27 2025]

data.title: Mohamed Sliten
data.text:
Mohamed Sliten (25 January 1945 – 31 August 2026), also referred to in contemporary sources as Mohamed Slitane, was a Moroccan professional association football player who played as a winger.

During the 1960s, Sliten played in Europe for Belgian club Standard de Liège and Swiss club BSC Young Boys. [ref: Football: Décès de Mohamed Sliten, le roi du dribble, Maroc Hebdo] He later returned to Morocco to play for Union Sportive de Sidi Kacem in the Botola, where the club finished as league runners-up in 1970, and represented the Morocco national football team. [ref: Décès de l'ancien international Mohamed Sliten, "Le Roi du Dribble", L'Économiste] [ref: Morocco 1969/70, Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation]

== Early life ==
Sliten was born on 25 January 1945 in Marrakech. He developed as a youth player with local club Mouloudia Club de Marrakech in the Riad Zitoun quarter before moving abroad in 1963.

== Club career ==
=== Europe (1963–1968) ===
In 1963, Sliten moved to Europe and joined Belgian club Standard de Liège. In 1964, he transferred to Swiss Nationalliga A side BSC Young Boys. With Young Boys, he finished as runner-up in the 1964–65 Nationalliga A championship behind Lausanne-Sports. [ref: Switzerland 1964/65, Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation] During his tenure in Switzerland, he was nicknamed « Le Roi du Dribble » by the regional sports press in reference to his dribbling ability. [ref: أحد رواد الاحتراف المغربي في أوروبا "محمد سليتن" في ذمة الله, MFM Sport]

In the mid-1960s, during an international friendly fixture playing for Young Boys against English club Manchester United, Sliten scored three goals in a single match. [ref: Décès de l'ancien international Mohamed Sliten, Le Site Info]

=== Return to Morocco (1969–1978) ===
Sliten returned to the Moroccan domestic championship in 1969, signing with Union Sportive de Sidi Kacem (USK). During the 1969–70 Botola season, USK finished second in the Moroccan first division with 64 points (10 wins, 14 draws, 6 defeats), two points behind champions FAR Rabat, marking the highest league placement in the club's history. Sliten also competed with USK in the Coupe du Trône, reaching the semi-finals in 1971 and 1972. [ref: Morocco - List of Cup Finals, Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation]

== International career ==
Sliten represented the Morocco national football team during the late 1960s and early 1970s. He took part in qualification matches for the 1970 FIFA World Cup, but was excluded from the final tournament squad in Mexico due to a knee injury sustained during domestic competition.

== Death ==
Sliten died in Marrakech on 31 August 2026, at the age of 81. His death was officially confirmed by the Fondation Mohammed VI des Champions Sportifs.

* Nationalliga A runner-up: 1964–65

; USK Sidi Kacem
* Botola runner-up: 1969–70

data.title: Lewis G. Burton
data.text:
----

Lewis G. Burton is a London-based performance artist, DJ, cultural producer and activist. They are the founder of INFERNO, a queer techno rave and performance-art platform established in 2015, and a founding organiser of London Trans+ Pride. Burton's work combines performance, club culture and community organising. [ref: Lewis G. Burton on the Magic of Change, Mission Magazine] [ref: 5 photographers on INFERNO, London's most 'chaotic, beautiful' rave, Dazed] [ref: The right to dance: Queer nightlife in 2026, [[Time Out (magazine)]

==Career==

===Performance art===
Burton began working as a performance artist in the early 2010s. In 2014, Burton collaborated with artist Victor Ivanov on FLESH, a performance project centred on a bodysuit constructed from preserved chicken skins. The project received coverage in the Evening Standard, which reported on Burton performing in the suit in public spaces across London. [ref: Video: man in chicken flesh gimp suit shocks London commuters, Evening Standard]

In December 2022, Burton presented TRANSPHORIA, an interdisciplinary performance work combining theatre, performance art and club culture, at the Institute of Contemporary Arts in London. [ref: TRANSPHORIA, Institute of Contemporary Arts]

===INFERNO===
Burton founded INFERNO in London in 2015 as a club night combining techno with performance art. In a 2024 feature, Dazed examined INFERNO's influence on London's queer techno-rave culture through the work of photographers who had documented the night over nine years.

INFERNO subsequently developed programming beyond its regular club nights. In 2022, it staged a late-night takeover at the Institute of Contemporary Arts alongside an INFERNO Summit focused on queer and trans artists and nightlife culture. [ref: INFERNO Rave, Institute of Contemporary Arts] In July 2026, Dazed reported that INFERNO was operating at The Distillery in London and continued to provide a space for artists and designers within the city's nightlife scene. [ref: London's dying nightlife is killing the fashion club kid, Dazed]

===London Trans+ Pride===
Burton is a founding member and organiser of London Trans+ Pride. [ref: 'We have the right to live with dignity': More than 55,000 people march for London Trans+ Pride, The Big Issue] At the 2026 march, which ended at Trafalgar Square for the first time, organisers estimated attendance at 150,000. ITV News identified Burton as a founding member and reported their remarks at the event. [ref: 150,000 march through London in 'world's largest trans pride', organisers say, ITV News]

data.title: Dillon Leacock
data.text:
== Early life and high school ==

Leacock attended Millbrook High School in Raleigh, North Carolina, where he competed in sprint and hurdle events. During his high school career, he won the boys' 400-meter hurdles championship at The Outdoor Nationals, presented by Nike, in 2021, running 52.284 seconds at Hayward Field in Eugene, Oregon. DyeStat reported that Leacock became the first male athlete from North Carolina to win the 400-meter hurdles title at the meet since 2008. [ref: Dillon Leacock 1st Place Boys 400m Hurdles Championship - The Outdoor Nationals, Presented by Nike 2021, DyeStat]

His University of Houston biography lists victories in the 400-meter hurdles at Nike Outdoor Nationals, the NACAC Championships and the USATF Outdoor Nationals, as well as a North Carolina state championship in the 300-meter hurdles. He was also runner-up in the North Carolina state 110-meter hurdles. [ref: Dillon Leacock - Track and Field, University of Houston Athletics]

== International career ==

In 2021, Leacock won the 400-meter hurdles at the NACAC Championships in San José, Costa Rica, in 53.45 seconds. Trinidad and Tobago Newsday reported that Leacock was among Trinidad and Tobago's gold medalists at the championships. [ref: Clement Campbell, Iantha Wright earn NACAC medals on final day, Trinidad and Tobago Newsday] [ref: NACAC U20 Championships, World Athletics]

The Trinidad Guardian later included Leacock's victory among Trinidad and Tobago's track and field highlights of 2021, reporting that he won the 400-meter hurdles in 53.45 seconds. [ref: Daniel, Horsford, Gittens and Warren track and fields bright spots for 2021, Trinidad Guardian]

Leacock was selected to represent Trinidad and Tobago at the 2021 World Athletics U20 Championships in Nairobi, Kenya. He was scheduled to compete in the men's 400-meter hurdles but withdrew before his heat after experiencing discomfort in training. [ref: Three-member Trinidad and Tobago team for World Athletics Under-20 Champs, Trinidad and Tobago Newsday] [ref: No medals for Trinidad and Tobago at U-20 World Championships, Trinidad and Tobago Newsday]

In 2025, Leacock represented Trinidad and Tobago at the 2025 Junior Pan American Games in Asunción, Paraguay. He competed in the men's 400-meter hurdles and was part of Trinidad and Tobago's men's 4 × 400-meter relay team, which finished fourth. [ref: Junior Pan American Games, World Athletics] [ref: Trinidad and Tobago men stumble to fourth in 4x400m final at Jr Pan Am, Trinidad and Tobago Newsday]

In June 2026, Leacock recorded a personal best of 49.83 seconds in the 400-meter hurdles at the LA Sprint Series at Notre Dame High School in Sherman Oaks, California. He finished second in the event. [ref: Leacock, Harrison shine in LA series, Trinidad Express] [ref: Dillon LEACOCK, World Athletics]

Later that month, Leacock won the men's 400-meter hurdles at the Trinidad and Tobago Championships, running 51.24 seconds. [ref: Trinidad & Tobago Championship, World Athletics]

== Collegiate career ==

=== Houston ===

Leacock competed collegiately for the Houston Cougars.

As a freshman in 2022, he finished eighth in the 400-meter hurdles at the American Athletic Conference Championships and recorded a personal best of 52.48 seconds. He also set a personal best of 49.70 seconds in the 400 meters at the Charlie Thomas Invitational. [ref: Dillon Leacock - Track and Field, University of Houston Athletics]

In 2023, Leacock qualified for the NCAA West Preliminary Round in the 400-meter hurdles. He finished seventh in the event at the American Athletic Conference Championships with a personal best of 52.15 seconds. During the indoor season, he ran 49.64 seconds in the 400 meters at the American Indoor Championships. [ref: Dillon Leacock - Track and Field, University of Houston Athletics]

In 2024, Leacock won the 400-meter hurdles at the Victor Lopez Classic in 51.33 seconds. At the Big 12 Outdoor Championships, he finished fifth in the 400-meter hurdles in 50.62 seconds and helped Houston finish seventh in the 4 × 400-meter relay. He subsequently qualified for the NCAA West First Round in both events. [ref: Dillon Leacock - Track and Field, University of Houston Athletics]

Leacock did not compete for Houston during the 2025 season. [ref: Dillon Leacock - Track and Field, University of Houston Athletics]

=== Missouri ===

Leacock transferred to the Missouri Tigers for the 2026 season. [ref: Dillon Leacock - 2026 Track & Field Roster, University of Missouri Athletics]

During the 2026 indoor season, he established a collegiate personal best of 47.61 seconds in the 400 meters at the Tyson Invitational. He also competed in the 60-meter hurdles and was part of Missouri's distance medley relay team. [ref: Dillon Leacock – Track and Field Results & Statistics, TFRRS]

At the Drake Relays in Des Moines, Iowa, Leacock won the men's 400-meter hurdles in 50.68 seconds, defeating a field of 20 competitors. The performance ranked third on Missouri's all-time list in the event. [ref: Track and Field Notches Three Champion Titles During Day Three of Drake Relays, University of Missouri Athletics] [ref: 116th Drake Relays - 400m Hurdles, TFRRS]

His Drake Relays performance qualified him for the NCAA West First Round. [ref: Fifteen Tigers Qualify for NCAA Track & Field West Regional Championships, University of Missouri Athletics]

At the NCAA West First Round in Fayetteville, Arkansas, Leacock ran 50.33 seconds in the 400-meter hurdles to finish seventh in his heat and advance to the quarterfinals. The performance was a collegiate personal best at the time and improved his position on Missouri's all-time list. [ref: Track and Field's Innes Advances to NCAA Championship Final, Leacock Qualifies for Quarterfinals, University of Missouri Athletics]

Leacock's 2026 Missouri season received coverage from the independent Missouri sports publication Rock M Nation, which highlighted his Drake Relays victory, NCAA regional qualification, 50.33-second performance and position on Missouri's all-time list. [ref: 2025-26 Rock M’mys: Newcomer of the Year, Rock M Nation]

data.title: Nate Hodges
data.text:
Nate Hodges (born 1984) is an American professional timbersports competitor. He won the STIHL Timbersports Individual World Championship in 2024 [ref: North Fork native Nate Hodges crowned Timbersports world champion, ABC30] and the U.S. championship in 2024 and 2025. [ref: U.S. Championships Delivers World Records, Title Defenses, and Rising Stars, STIHL Timbersports] In 2025, he set a world record of 4.28 seconds in the Hot Saw discipline.

== Early life ==
Hodges grew up in North Fork, California, in Madera County. His family has a long involvement in the Mid-Sierra Loggers Jamboree; his father Patrick, mother Cathey, brother Jerry, and sister Amanda have also competed in the event. [ref: Hodges Carves Out Runner Up Finish At 2019 Stihl Timbersports Championships, Sierra News Online]

Hodges began competing at the Jamboree as a young adult, entering the axe throw. He tied for first place in his first competition and won a tiebreaker throw-off. [ref: Hodges Defends Title At 60th North Fork Loggers Jamboree, Sierra News Online]

== Career ==
Hodges entered the STIHL Timbersports national circuit in 2019. That July, he finished second at the U.S. Pro Championship in Milwaukee, one point behind Cassidy Scheer. Later that year, he competed for the United States at the World Championships in Prague. [ref: Hodges to Compete Next Month at Timbersports World Championships in Prague, Sierra News Online]

In 2022, Hodges was part of the U.S. team that won the silver medal at the Team World Championship in Gothenburg, Sweden. [ref: Australia dominate World Championships in Sweden, STIHL Timbersports] He won another team silver medal at the 2024 World Championships in Toulouse, France. [ref: Australia defend world title in Toulouse, STIHL Timbersports]

Hodges won his first U.S. championship in July 2024, defeating Matt Cogar by one point. [ref: STIHL Timbersports brings the heat to the U.S. Championship, STIHL Timbersports] The victory qualified him for the Individual World Championship in Toulouse, where he scored 67 points to win the title ahead of Jack Jordan of New Zealand and Ben Cumberland of Canada. [ref: Check-Nate! USA's Nate Hodges scoops his first STIHL Timbersports Individual World Championship, STIHL Timbersports]

In July 2025, Hodges won his second consecutive U.S. championship. During the semifinals, he set a world record of 4.28 seconds in the Hot Saw discipline. He finished sixth while defending his title at the 2025 Individual World Championship in Milan, after being disqualified in the Hot Saw for cutting outside the marked line. [ref: Wood you believe it?! New Zealand's Jack Jordan snatches his first solo world title, STIHL Timbersports]

In 2026, Hodges finished second at the North American Trophy and was runner-up to Matt Cogar at the U.S. Men's Pro Championship in Milwaukee. [ref: North American Trophy 2026, STIHL Timbersports] [ref: Breakthrough Champions, Record-Breaking Cuts and an Eight-Time Winner: STIHL Timbersports Crowns 2026 U.S. Champions, STIHL]

== Personal life ==
Hodges lives near North Fork, California, and has worked as a general contractor. In 2019, he opened Yosemite Axe Throwing in Oakhurst, California. [ref: Timber! New Axe Throwing Club Opening in Oakhurst, Sierra News Online]

data.title: Alessandro Giannì
data.text:
Alessandro Giannì (born 12 August 1989) is an Italian contemporary artist whose work encompasses painting, sculpture and multimedia art. [ref: Alessandro Giannì, Quadriennale di Roma] [ref: La Cina come ponte visivo tra pittura e AI. Intervista all'artista Alessandro Giannì, Artribune]

== Biography and work ==
As a painter, sculptor and multimedia artist, Giannì works across traditional media and digital forms, exploring the relationships between painting, sculpture, artificial intelligence and new technologies. A central concern of his practice is the image as an element in continual transformation, moving between physical and virtual states. His work also examines the relationship between contemporary images and historical iconography, reinterpreted through technological tools and digital processes. [ref: Le visioni in transizione di Alessandro Giannì sono in mostra a Modena, Artribune]

In 2014, he participated in Ñewpressionism, an exhibition introduced by Miltos Manetas at the Istituto Svizzero in Milan. Other participating artists included Sylvie Fleury, Olivier Mosset, Petra Cortright, Amalia Ulman, Luca Pozzi and Jon Rafman. [ref: Ñewpressionism in Milan, 1,11,111. From screen to nature and back again, Istituto Svizzero] During the 73rd Venice International Film Festival in 2016, he worked as art director on EGH, a project by Enrico Ghezzi and Emiliano Montanari. [ref: Alessandro Giannì, Tang Contemporary Art]

In 2019, Giannì began developing a custom artificial-intelligence system named VASARI, intended to emulate aspects of his creative and compositional process by generating digital sketches that he would subsequently develop into oil paintings. [ref: Lo squarcio: luci e ombre nella pittura di Alessandro Giannì, Balloon Project] [ref: Alessandro Giannì “Due to the Image”, Italian Cultural Institute of New York]

He was among the founders of Spaziomensa in 2020, an independent artist-run cultural space in Rome. [ref: Nuovi artist run space: nasce a Roma spaziomensa, Artribune] [ref: Vera: Roma, 8 spazi, 54 studi, Quodlibet]

In 2021, he presented the solo exhibition Due to the Image at Postmasters Gallery in New York City. It included paintings developed with the aid of VASARI and was accompanied by a publication featuring a critical text by Renato Miracco.

He held his first solo exhibition in Asia in 2023, Breaking Darkness, at Tang Contemporary Art in Bangkok. [ref: Alessandro Giannì: Breaking Darkness, Tang Contemporary Art] In 2024, he participated in The Power of Painting at the ENNOVA Art Museum in Langfang, China, exhibiting alongside artists including Marlene Dumas, Anish Kapoor, Bernard Frize, Christopher Le Brun and Jörg Immendorff. [ref: Alessandro Giannì, Tang Contemporary Art]

In 2025, Giannì held his second solo exhibition in Asia, Multiple Unrealities, at Tang Contemporary Art in Hong Kong. [ref: Alessandro Giannì Solo Exhibition: Multiple Unrealities, Tang Contemporary Art] Later that year, he opened a solo exhibition at Galleria Mazzoli in Modena, founded by gallerist Emilio Mazzoli.

During this period, his work increasingly explored painting as a means of seeing and as a kind of "screen" on which images are generated and reworked through processes combining pictorial language, visual memory and digital systems. The perceptual dimension of images and the use of algorithmic tools became particular areas of interest. [ref: Per Alessandro Giannì, la pittura accade quando l'immagine incontra lo sguardo, Exibart]

In 2026, Giannì presented the solo exhibition Eterno Antico at the Aurora Art Museum in Shanghai. [ref: Mostra “Eterno Antico” di Alessandro Giannì all'Aurora Art Museum di Shanghai, Italian Cultural Institute of Shanghai] In the same year, he exhibited Eco dal confine at the Complesso Monumentale del Purgatorio ad Arco in Naples. [ref: ECO DAL CONFINE di Alessandro Giannì, Complesso Monumentale Purgatorio ad Arco]

data.title: ADA KATE UCHEGBU
data.text:
Ada Kate Uchegbu (born September 30, 1982) is a Nigerian journalist, author, media entrepreneur, and political figure. She is the founder and publisher of Distinguished Africans Magazine and the CEO of ADA Consolidated Nigeria Limited. In 2025, she declared her intention to run for the presidency of Nigeria in the 2027 general elections under the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), advocating for structural reforms, gender inclusion, and generational shifts in governance.

== Early life and education ==
Ada Kate Uchegbu was born on September 30, 1982, in Nigeria. She completed her higher education at the National Open University of Nigeria. Seeking further specialization in communications and language, she attended the National Broadcast Academy in Lagos and studied at Alliance Française in Lagos. She holds the traditional title of Iyom Omelorah.

== Career ==
=== Journalism and media ===
Uchegbu began her career in writing and media, focusing on investigative reporting across West Africa. Her coverage frequently addresses governance, systemic inequality, economic issues, and national insecurity. Notable among her editorial works is "Roads of Blood – The Kidnap Highway," an investigative piece dealing with kidnapping incidents in Nigeria.

She established the media firm ADA Consolidated Nigeria Limited and subsequently founded Distinguished Africans Magazine, serving as its Editor-in-Chief. The publication acts as a pan-African platform focused on celebrating local achievements, cultural promotion, and documenting the profiles of African leaders and innovators.

=== Literary works ===
As an author, Uchegbu has written across both non-fiction political commentary and creative fiction:
* Wings of Destiny: My Journey Through Power, Politics and the Dream of Nigeria's First Female President (2026) – A political memoir evaluating her experiences within the Nigerian political space and advocating for female political participation.
* Ada the Future President – A children's book series focusing on civic responsibility and leadership.
* Kidnapped and The Dark Testament – Fiction books exploring contemporary socio-political anxieties.
* African Short Horror Stories (Volume 1 and 2) – Fiction collections utilizing traditional African folklore, superstitions, and supernatural motifs.

== Political activism and 2027 presidential campaign ==
Uchegbu's political career spans over a decade of continuous participation, during which she contested positions including the Anambra State House of Assembly, the PDP National Women Leadership, and an APC gubernatorial primary in Anambra State.

In June 2025, Uchegbu officially declared her intention to run for the President of Nigeria in the 2027 general election under the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). Running under the campaign blueprint titled "The New Covenant," she argues that Nigeria's recurring socio-economic challenges stem from heavily recycled leadership and structural stagnation. She stands prominently as an advocate against the exclusion of women from major political party tickets, arguing that true democracy cannot be achieved without fair gender representation at the highest executive levels.

Her key campaign policy promises include:
* The establishment of a ₦150 billion Youth Enterprise Fund.
* Fully digitized public administration systems to counter institutional corruption.
* Standardized community health reforms and community-oriented policing.
* Increased representation of youth and women in the national cabinet.

data.title: Rick Robertson
data.text:
Richardson Robertson III, professionally known as Rick Robertson, is an American architect and principal of Robertson Partners Architects. His work encompasses private residences and proposals for large-scale urban development drawing on Neoclassical, Beaux-Arts, and other classical architectural traditions. His projects include the Fleur de Lys estate in Los Angeles and proposed developments in California and New York.

== Career and residential architecture ==
Robertson designed Fleur de Lys, a French-inspired estate in Los Angeles featured in Matt Tyrnauer's 2002 Vanity Fair article "Versailles on the Pacific". [ref: Tyrnauer, Matt. "Versailles on the Pacific." Vanity Fair, April 2002.] The Los Angeles Times also covered the estate and Robertson's work. [ref: "Now Anchored in Hollywood." Los Angeles Times, December 13, 1998.]

Jeff Hyland's The Legendary Estates of Beverly Hills includes a chapter on Fleur de Lys describing its site, architecture, construction, and landscape. [ref: Hyland, Jeff. The Legendary Estates of Beverly Hills. New York: Rizzoli, 2008. Chapter: "Carolwood Drive: Fleur de Lys."] The property was assembled from six adjacent parcels to create a site of approximately five acres.

In 2014, the Los Angeles Times reported that Fleur de Lys had sold for $102 million, identifying Robertson as its architect and quoting his description of the house as a Neoclassical design conceived as a decorative arts museum rather than a traditional French floor plan. [ref: "Westside mansion sells for $102 million, highest Southland price." Los Angeles Times, April 1, 2014.]

In 2013, the Los Angeles Times reported on Robertson's design for a proposed 25,000-square-foot penthouse at the W Hollywood, with four bedrooms, a ballroom, a screening room, a trophy room, a fitness center, and a beauty parlor. [ref: Lelyveld, Nita. "Above it all in Hollywood." Los Angeles Times, May 19, 2013.]

In April 2007, C Magazine published Degen Pener's profile "Classical Artist," examining Robertson's career, architectural philosophy, and use of classical precedents in residential and urban design. [ref: Pener, Degen. "Classical Artist." C Magazine, April 2007.]

Robertson designed a Mediterranean-style house in Tulsa, Oklahoma, for Bobby and Leslie Lorton. Southern Accents featured the residence in its May–June 2007 issue in "Together in Tulsa," discussing its limestone exterior, classical detailing, and the clients' interest in historical architectural accuracy. [ref: "Together in Tulsa." Southern Accents, May–June 2007.]

In January–February 2014, Veranda published "Glamorous Texas Home," featuring a Dallas residence designed by Robertson, with interiors by Beverly Field, text by Nancy Perot, and photography by Max Kim-Bee. [ref: Perot, Nancy. "Glamorous Texas Home." Veranda, January–February 2014.]

The Los Angeles Times featured a French Normandy-style residence designed by Robertson at Lake Arrowhead, California, in 2010. [ref: Marshutz, Scott. "Home of the Week: Chateau on Lake Arrowhead." Los Angeles Times, September 5, 2010.] In 2019, the newspaper identified him as the architect of a Mediterranean-style residence in Los Angeles's Bird Streets neighborhood offered for sale by former motorcycle racer John Kocinski. [ref: Flemming, Jack. "Retired motorcycle racer John Kocinski asks $30 million for Bird Streets abode." Los Angeles Times, January 16, 2019.]

== Urban design and planning ==
In May 2003, Urban Land published Brad Berton's "Northern Gateway" about Las Lomas, a proposed master-planned community in Los Angeles County, identifying Robertson as the project's architect. [ref: Berton, Brad. "Northern Gateway." Urban Land, May 2003, pp. 74–78.]

Robertson developed the Setauket Village Center proposal to redevelop the Route 25A retail district in Setauket, Long Island. [ref: Mastrosimone, Peter C. "A New Vision of Setauket Unveiled: Village center and park could remake Route 25A." The Village Times Herald, October 9, 2003, pp. A1, A13.] In October 2003, The Village Times Herald described his plan to unite three shopping plazas with apartments or condominiums above shops, a village green, gardens, a pond, and an amphitheater. The article characterized the design as a Beaux-Arts reinterpretation of early American architecture incorporating Tudor and shingle-style elements, and quoted Robertson on modern architecture and Long Island's changing development pattern.

In November 2003, Newsday published the editorial "A Model for Revitalizing LI Towns," presenting the proposal's combination of housing above retail space and a community park as a potential model for downtown revitalization. [ref: "A Model for Revitalizing LI Towns." Newsday, November 28, 2003, p. A42.]

In 2006, David Brussat discussed Robertson's proposed downtown Los Angeles residential towers, City House and the Olympic, in The Providence Journal, considering their designs in the context of classical architecture in contemporary American cities. [ref: Brussat, David. "Angeleno inspiration for Providence." The Providence Journal, May 18, 2006, p. B5.]

Steve Cutler's "New York Living Goes Global," published in New York Living Magazine in December 2006–January 2007, described plans for the Olympic, a proposed 49-story tower with 150 condominium apartments, and City House, a proposed 60-story tower with 180 units. The article discussed their limestone exteriors and classical detailing, Robertson's references to several New York museums and the former Pennsylvania Station, and his comments on the projects. [ref: Cutler, Steve. "New York Living Goes Global." New York Living Magazine, December 2006–January 2007, pp. 34–35.]

== Awards and honors ==
A 2007 C Magazine profile reported that Robertson received the Stars of Design award, a Los Angeles design honor, in 2003.

The profile also associated Fleur de Lys with recognition from the French government for contributions to French-style architecture.

== Architectural commentary ==
In a 2008 article about Château Élysée in Los Angeles, The New Yorker included Robertson's observations on the building and its architectural character. [ref: Goodyear, Dana. "Château Scientology." The New Yorker, January 14, 2008.]

data.title: Counterfactual measurement of marketing effectiveness
data.text:
Counterfactual measurement of marketing effectiveness is the estimation of the causal effect of a marketing activity by comparing an observed outcome with a counterfactual, meaning the outcome that would have occurred without the activity. It is also called incrementality measurement, because the quantity estimated is the incremental outcome attributable to the marketing. The methods include randomised controlled experiments in which a treatment group is exposed to the marketing and a control group is withheld from it, holdout tests, and geographic experiments in which regions are assigned to treatment or control.

Counterfactual measurement is distinguished from methods that infer effect from observed associations between marketing exposure and outcomes, such as attribution models and marketing mix modeling, which typically use observational data.

== Concept ==
The central quantity in counterfactual measurement is incremental outcome: the sales, conversions or other results that occurred because of the marketing and would not have occurred otherwise. Outcomes that follow marketing exposure but would have happened anyway are not incremental. A customer who was already planning to purchase and later clicked an advertisement is an example.
Randomisation of exposure is intended to make the treatment and control groups comparable on all characteristics except exposure, so that a difference in outcomes can be attributed to the marketing.

== Methods ==
; Randomised controlled experiments
: Users, households or other units are randomly assigned to a group that can be shown the marketing and a group that cannot, and outcomes are compared between the groups.
; Geographic experiments
: Regions rather than individuals are assigned to treatment or control, for example by withholding advertising in selected regions.
; Calibration of other models
: Results from experiments can be used to check or adjust estimates from observational models.

== Empirical comparisons with observational methods ==
Several field studies have compared experimental estimates of advertising effect with estimates from observational methods applied to the same campaigns.

In a large-scale field experiment at eBay, Blake, Nosko and Tadelis found that returns from paid search advertising were a fraction of the returns suggested by conventional non-experimental estimates. For eBay, a large and well-known brand, advertising on brand keywords had no measurable short-term benefit.

Gordon, Zettelmeyer, Bhargava and Chapsky compared experimental results from 15 Facebook advertising campaigns with the results of observational methods. They reported that the observational methods often did not reproduce the experimental result, that they generally overstated advertising effectiveness, and that in some cases they understated it.

In a 2023 study of 663 Facebook experiments, Gordon, Moakler and Zettelmeyer reported median absolute differences between observational and experimental estimates of lift of 115 percent for upper-funnel outcomes, 107 percent for mid-funnel outcomes and 62 percent for lower-funnel outcomes. The authors concluded that the tested observational methods could not reliably recover the causal effect in their setting.

A 2026 working paper by the same group, covering 2,226 Meta advertising experiments, reported that a model calibrated on experimental results predicted incremental conversions per dollar with an out-of-sample R-squared of 0.88, compared with 0.19 for seven-day last-click attribution. The paper had not been peer reviewed at the time of retrieval.

The scope of these findings is specific to the studied platforms, methods and, in the eBay case, a single brand.

== Use in marketing decisions ==
Hanssens and colleagues state that return on marketing investment is interpreted and used in varied ways, which causes ambiguity and suboptimal marketing decisions. Incrementality estimates provide one way of defining the return attributable to marketing spend, because they compare spend with outcomes that would not have occurred without it.

JBL Colours is an independent colouring-book project founded by British creator and author Jack Barrow, who publishes under the name Jack S. Barrow. The project produces colouring books and illustrated stories for children and adults. Its catalogue includes fantasy, animals, family activities and hospital-themed stories.

JBL Colours publishes books for different age groups and interests. Children’s titles include fantasy and animal-themed colouring books, as well as longer collections such as The Great Big Colouring Adventure. The project has also developed story-based books, including the hospital adventure, and titles for adult readers under the JBL Colours After Dark label.

The project has promoted free printable colouring pages alongside its books. Barrow has used these pages to introduce the artwork and invite readers to offer feedback.

== Publishing and promotion ==
The books are marketed under the JBL Colours name through a dedicated website and social media accounts. Some titles are distributed through Amazon’s Kindle Direct Publishing platform.
