data.title: Proxy Foods
data.text:
Proxy Foods AI is an American food technology company that develops artificial intelligence software for food and beverage formulation. It was founded in 2022 by Panos Kostopoulos, a chemical engineer and food biotechnologist, and four co-founders, [ref: Proxy Foods: Τα σχέδια της startup που φέρνει την ΑΙ στην ανάπτυξη τροφίμων μετά τη χρηματοδότηση $2,5 εκατ., Capital.gr] and grew out of Georgetown University’s biotechnology program. [ref: Georgetown’s Bark Tank Competition: MS in Biotechnology Student Takes 1st Prize with Proxy Foods, Master of Science in Biotechnology] The company has raised $8.3 million across two funding rounds. [ref: Business Wire (5 August 2026). [https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260805888751/en/Proxy-Foods-AI-Raises-%246M-Seed-Round-to-Accelerate-AI-Native-Food-and-Beverage-Development-Platform "Proxy Foods AI Raises $6M Seed Round to Accelerate AI-Native Food and Beverage Development Platform"]. Business Wire. Retrieved 28 September 2026.] Its platform applies predictive machine learning models to recipe formulation, regulatory compliance, and sensory evaluation, with an initial focus on alternative proteins. [ref: ] Its clients include Barilla, CAVA, and MISTA, a food innovation center owned by Givaudan.

== History ==
Proxy Foods was conceived by Panagiotis (Panos) Kostopoulos while he was completing a master’s degree in biotechnology at Georgetown University in Washington, D.C. Kostopoulos, who also holds an integrated master’s degree in chemical engineering from the National Technical University of Athens, developed the initial concept around applying artificial intelligence to food formulation, with a focus on alternative proteins, including plant-based, fermentation-derived, and cultivated products. The company was co-founded in 2022 with Petros Mandalis, Dimitris Zisis, Sid Mitroo, and Ted Leonsis, with technical operations based in Athens and business operations in Washington, D.C. According to the company, its mission is to transform food and beverage product development by integrating artificial intelligence with food science and culinary knowledge.

In 2022, the concept was presented at Georgetown’s annual Bark Tank entrepreneurship competition, formally known as the Leonsis Family Entrepreneurship Prize, a joint initiative of the university’s biotechnology program and its McDonough School of Business. Kostopoulos and his team took first place and a $30,000 cash prize, which served as the company’s initial capital. [ref: Entrepreneurs Split $100,000 in Annual Bark Tank Competition, The Hoya] [ref: Georgetown Entrepreneurs Take Home $145,000 in Prizes During Annual ‘Bark Tank’ Pitch Competition, McDonough School of Business] The competition is named for and supported by Ted Leonsis, a Georgetown alumnus and founder and CEO of Monumental Sports & Entertainment, who later became a co-founder and lead investor in the company. [ref: Proxy Foods raises $2.3m to grow AI-based recipe formulation platform, FoodNavigator.com]

== Technology ==
Proxy Foods develops a cloud-based platform for food and beverage research and development. Kostopoulos, the company’s CEO, has described the platform’s role as analogous to design software in other creative industries: a tool that allows food scientists to model and iterate formulations digitally before any physical testing, much as a graphic designer works with visual elements on screen. [ref: Proxy Foods CEO on AI’s potential in alt-protein market, creating ‘Canva... for the food scientist', FoodNavigator.com]

The platform incorporates predictive formulation models that use machine learning to anticipate a recipe’s performance across dimensions such as taste, texture, nutrition, and production cost, before laboratory trials are conducted. It also addresses regulatory compliance across multiple jurisdictions and includes sensory evaluation simulation capabilities. One of its design goals is to integrate the institutional knowledge held by food companies — historical R&D data, supplier records, and process documentation — into a unified AI interface.

In June 2026, the company was named a collaborating partner in the launch of the Food Intelligence Lab, an initiative of Food System Innovations (FSI) supported by a $2 million grant from the Bezos Earth Fund. Working with FSI and Stanford University computer scientist Anna Thomas, Proxy Foods co-developed an expert-guided Bayesian optimization (EGBO) system that improved the sensory performance of a dairy-free Greek yogurt by 29 percent over ten formulation iterations across five days, matching the animal-derived benchmark on three of four key sensory attributes. [ref: This Bezos-Funded Lab Wants to Use AI to Make Better Vegan Burgers, Green Queen]

== Funding and recognition ==
In March 2024, Proxy Foods announced a $2.3 million seed round led by Ted Leonsis, with participation from CAVA Group co-founders Ike Grigoropoulos, Ted Xenohristos, and Dimitri Moshovitis, as well as SWaN & Legend Venture Partners, Robert G. Hisaoka of RGH Capital, and food industry veteran Richard Ware, who had retired after a 35-year career at Mars, Inc. In August 2026, the company announced a second $6 million round, again led by Leonsis, with additional participation from Hisaoka, SWaN & Legend, and individual investors including Jeff Skoll, Roger W. Ferguson Jr. (former President and CEO of TIAA), Michelle Freeman, Howard Eisenberg, Grant Verstandig, George P. Stamas, Yiannis Gavrielides, Chris Goulakos, and Evee and Alexander Georgiadis of Krinos Foods Canada. The round brought total funding to $8.3 million. [ref: Ted Leonsis Backs $6M Seed Round for Proxy Foods AI, citybiz] Proceeds from both rounds were directed toward expanding the platform’s capabilities in food science, regulatory compliance, and commercialization, as well as growing the company’s enterprise client base internationally.

In 2025, Proxy Foods was selected as one of six resident startups at Tyson Foods’ annual Demo Day, an event at which Tyson evaluates food technology startups for potential collaboration and partnership. [ref: Meat+Poultry (2025). [https://talkbusiness.net/2025/07/tyson-foods-selects-six-ai-startups-at-demo-day-event/ "Tyson Selects Six AI Startups from Demo Day"]. Meat+Poultry. Retrieved 28 September 2026.] [ref: ] That same year, Endeavor Greece, the local affiliate of the global entrepreneurship network Endeavor, selected the company for its portfolio of high-impact, high-growth businesses, following a selection process that includes evaluation by experienced entrepreneurs from its global network. [ref: ] In May 2026, the company announced a technology partnership with Aperio Global focused on adding quantum-resistant security infrastructure to its platform. [ref: Mridul, Anay (25 June 2026). [https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260519916301/en/Proxy-Foods-AI-and-Aperio-Global-Partner-to-Deliver-Secure-AI-Driven-Food-Innovation-at-Enterprise-Quantum-Resilient-Scale "This Bezos-Funded Lab Wants to Use AI to Make Tastier Plant-Based Meat"]. Green Queen. Retrieved 28 September 2026.]

data.title: Jarno Zaffelli
data.text:
----

Jarno Zaffelli is an Italian motor-racing circuit designer and the founder of Dromo Circuit Design. [ref: Jarno Zaffelli, un reggiano sulle piste di mezzo mondo, Corriere di Bologna] [ref: Jarno Zaffelli, progettista delle piste: 'Autodromi migliori grazie a noi', Il Resto del Carlino] His work has included the redesign or resurfacing of circuits such as Silverstone, Zandvoort and the Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps, as well as the original design of the Madring circuit in Madrid. [ref: Architect Zaffelli: 'Bouwen aan Circuit Zandvoort is als spelen in het zand', [[Nederlandse Omroep Stichting] [ref: El diseñador del circuito semiurbano de F1 en Madrid: «Que la gente esté tranquila; Madrid no será como Valencia», El País]

== Early life and career ==

Zaffelli trained as an industrial technician in experimental mechanics and briefly studied management engineering. In 2000 he began developing a proposal for a motor-racing circuit near Reggio Emilia. Although that circuit was not built, the research led him to travel internationally to study existing tracks and ultimately to establish Dromo Circuit Design. Italian publications subsequently profiled his development from the Reggio Emilia project into an international circuit-design career. [ref: Jarno Zaffelli, il progettista italiano che sfida Hermann Tilke, FormulaPassion.it] [ref: Dalla Malesia ad Abu Dhabi, progetti ad alta velocità, Gazzetta di Reggio]

Zaffelli developed a crash-prediction model based on eleven years of accident and circuit data. The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile reported that the model was used during Dromo's 2012 reconstruction of the Autódromo Termas de Río Hondo in Argentina. [ref: Crashing the numbers, FIA Auto+Medical] At the 2017 FIA Sport Conference, he presented the use of data analysis in circuit design and safety work. [ref: How the art of circuit design can improve safety while increasing the entertainment factor, Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile]

Following the cancellation of the 2018 British motorcycle Grand Prix because of drainage and surface problems, Zaffelli was appointed to take part in the technical investigation at Silverstone. [ref: MotoGP, Silverstone: Jarno Zaffelli condurrà l'indagine tecnica, FormulaPassion.it] Dromo subsequently worked on the circuit's complete resurfacing in 2019. [ref: Silverstone's Brooklands bump set to be fixed for MotoGP, Motorsport.com]

Between 2019 and 2020, Zaffelli led design work for the renovation of Zandvoort ahead of the return of the Dutch Grand Prix to Formula One. The project included the banked Hugenholtz and Arie Luyendyk corners. [ref: Development of the Zandvoort GP circuit, Professional Motorsport World] In 2021 and 2022, Zaffelli and Dromo worked on the renovation of Spa-Francorchamps, including changes to the three-dimensional geometry and surface of Eau Rouge–Raidillon while retaining its plan-view alignment. [ref: Jarno Zaffelli: «Il y avait l'option de changer l'Eau Rouge», L'Équipe]

In January 2024, Zaffelli was presented as the designer of the semi-permanent Formula One circuit planned around the IFEMA exhibition complex in Madrid. [ref: Why Madrid F1 critics have it wrong – 'It's a real test of driver & machine', [[Motor Sport (magazine)] In 2025, IFEMA terminated its implementation-support contract with Dromo and appointed companies from the German group founded by circuit designer Hermann Tilke to continue the project. In 2026, the Cologne Regional Court granted Dromo interim relief limited to Germany, prohibiting two Tilke companies from reproducing specified protected materials there. [ref: Landgericht Köln, judgment in case no. 14 O 62/26, following the hearing of 2 April 2026, pp. 1–4 and 61–64 ([https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Landgericht_K%C3%B6ln_judgment_14_O_62-26_(redacted).pdf redacted copy], in German).] El País reported that IFEMA maintained that the contract had been terminated because of documented breaches and that it was entitled to provide the material to third parties; Dromo disputed that account. The German order was preliminary and did not determine the wider contractual dispute in Spain. [ref: El diseño del circuito de F1 de Madrid desata un conflicto millonario con frentes en Alemania y España, El País] [ref: Ifema moviliza a la Comunidad de Madrid en su pulso millonario por el diseño del circuito de la F1, El País]

data.title: Mid Devon CC
data.text:
Mid Devon Cycling Club (MDCC) is an amateur cycling club based at Abbrook Park in Kingsteignton, near Newton Abbot, Devon, England. Founded in 1930, it is one of the largest cycling clubs in South West England, with a membership of around 585 as of 2018, and has developed several riders who went on to national and professional honours.

== History ==
The club was formed in 1930 with 17 members under the name Newton Abbot Wheelers. [ref: Ride With... Mid Devon Cycling Club, Cycling Weekly] It is registered with British Cycling and organises competitive events across several disciplines in the local region, including time trials, hill climbs and road races, promoting the Totnes-Vire stage race and six open time trials as of 2018. [ref: 2025 Totnes Vire: day one report and results, The British Continental]

Since 2007 the club has organised the Dartmoor Classic sportive, an event started by then club vice-president Ron Keegan. [ref: GALLERY: More than 1,500 cyclists battle hills and changeable weather to take part in the Dartmoor Classic Sportive, plymouthsportsgazette.com] A 2009 review in Cycling Weekly described it as having become "the best organised sportive in the UK" within its first three years, citing its marshalling, signage and organisation, and it has continued to feature regularly in lists of the UK's leading sportives. [ref: Cyclo-Sportive: The Dartmoor Classic, Cycling Weekly]

MDCC runs a youth development programme and is the host club for coaching sessions at the Torbay Velopark; in March 2018 it hosted the opening round of the Youth National Circuit Series. As of 2018, five club riders had won British national titles across various age groups and disciplines.

== Notable alumni and members ==
Mid Devon Cycling Club has served as the development club or early team for several riders who went on to professional or international careers.

Colin Lewis (1942–2022) joined the club as a teenager and rode as an amateur for MDCC from 1958 to 1966 before turning professional, riding the Tour de France in 1967 and 1968 and winning the British National Road Race Championship in successive years (1967 and 1968). [ref: Obituary: GB Tour Rider Colin Lewis RIP, PezCycling News] He later served as MDCC president, a role he held from around 1998.

Jeremy Hunt, a two-time winner of the British National Road Race Championship (1997 and 2001) who went on to ride for professional teams including Banesto and Team Sky, was coached as a teenager in Devon by Colin Lewis. [ref: About cycling coach Jeremy Hunt, Formfinder]

Yanto Barker joined the club at 15 and won the Junior British National Road Race Championship in 1998 while riding for MDCC, before turning professional and later founding the cycling apparel brand Le Col. [ref: Yanto Barker, ProCyclingStats]

Harrison Wood became the club's first member in over a decade to sign a UCI WorldTour contract when he joined Cofidis in 2023, having previously taken a national championship podium in the junior 25-mile time trial while riding for MDCC. [ref: The next step for pro cyclist Harrison Wood, torbayweekly.co.uk]

data.title: William Gill (surgeon)
data.text:
----

William Gill (1795 – 14 September 1863) was a British-born surgeon and naturalist who practiced in the Cape Colony. He is best known for the large bequest in his will that established Gill College in Somerset East (today KwaNojoli), one of the older educational institutions in the Eastern Cape province of South Africa [ref: Gedenkboek van die Nederduits-Gereformeerde Kerk Somerset Oos, Cape Times Beperk].

== Early life and training ==
Gill was born in Market Harborough, Leicestershire, in 1795. He completed a five-year medical apprenticeship (1810–1815) with Thomas Peck in Wellingborough, Northamptonshire, and studied medicine at the University of Glasgow. In 1818 he was admitted as a Member of the Royal College of Surgeons of England (MRCS) and as a licentiate of the Society of Apothecaries. He spent a year travelling in continental Europe, during which he developed a lasting interest in botany [ref: S2A3 Biographical Database of Southern African Science, www.s2a3.org.za].

== Career in the Cape Colony ==
Gill arrived at the Cape in June 1818 and was licensed to practise as a surgeon, accoucheur and apothecary later that year. He first served as district surgeon at Caledon and later settled in the Zwartland district (near present-day Malmesbury) in 1822, where he was noted for his work during a typhoid outbreak. [ref: South Africa: its medical history 1652-1898; a medical and social study, Struik]

In 1826 he undertook an expedition northward for hunting and natural-history collecting, reaching as far as Kuruman, where he met the explorer and geologist Andrew Geddes Bain. He suffered heavy losses when his wagons were destroyed and returned to Cape Town in 1827. Around the same period he collected plant and shell fossils along the Sundays River east of Uitenhage. [ref: Botanical Exploration of Southern Africa, SANBI]

On the recommendation of the Rev. George Thom, Gill was appointed district surgeon of the newly established settlement of Somerset (later Somerset East) in 1829. He maintained a private practice there for many years and became a respected member of the local community. When the district surgeoncy was abolished in 1845, Gill declined an alternative appointment as resident surgeon on Robben Island, instead continuing to practicing medicine in the town. He also acquired a number of farms in the district and became a wealthy merino sheep farmer.

He co-founded the Somerset Reading Society in 1832 and was a member of the Literary, Scientific and Medical Society of Grahamstown [ref: Grahamstown Journal, 15 March 1856, p. 2, "Literary, Scientific and Medical Society"]. He continued to collect botanical specimens, particularly orchids, and sold approximately 400 specimens that eventually reached the Herbarium at Kew Gardens. Several plant species, including Myrsine gillianus [ref: [https://redlist.sanbi.org/species.php?species=2565-2 Threatened Species Programme | SANBI Red List of South African Plants]], Aspalathus gillii [ref: ] and Erica gillii [ref: ], were named in his honor.

== Death and legacy ==
Gill, unmarried, died of oedema on 14 September 1863 in Somerset East, aged 68 [ref: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSQF-XS99-P?view=index&personArk=%2Fark%3A%2F61903%2F1%3A1%3AQGLF-GL2N&action=view&lang=en Cape Province. Probate Records 1861–1862, 1863]]. In his will dated 19 January 1863 he left the bulk of his estate, approximately £23,000, to “found and maintain an institution of higher education in the Eastern Province.” Local residents raised money for the buildings. The Gill College Corporation was formed, land was granted in 1867, and the college opened on 18 March 1869. Its architecture was modelled on that of the University of Glasgow. Originally intended as a university college, it later became a high school (from 1903) and continues today as a co-educational dual-medium school.

Gill’s remains were reinterred in front of the college in 1916.

data.title: ADA KATE UCHEGBU
data.text:
Ada Kate Uchegbu (born September 30, 1982) is a Nigerian journalist, author, media entrepreneur, and political figure. She is the founder and publisher of Distinguished Africans Magazine and the CEO of ADA Consolidated Nigeria Limited. In 2025, she declared her intention to run for the presidency of Nigeria in the 2027 general elections under the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), advocating for structural reforms, gender inclusion, and generational shifts in governance.

== Early life and education ==
Ada Kate Uchegbu was born on September 30, 1982, in Nigeria. She completed her higher education at the National Open University of Nigeria. Seeking further specialization in communications and language, she attended the National Broadcast Academy in Lagos and studied at Alliance Française in Lagos. She holds the traditional Igbo title of Iyom Omelorah.

== Career ==
=== Journalism and media ===
Uchegbu began her career in writing and media, focusing on investigative reporting across West Africa. Her coverage frequently addresses governance, systemic inequality, economic issues, and national insecurity. Notable among her editorial works is "Roads of Blood – The Kidnap Highway," an investigative piece dealing with kidnapping incidents in Nigeria.

She established the media firm ADA Consolidated Nigeria Limited and subsequently founded Distinguished Africans Magazine, serving as its Editor-in-Chief. The publication acts as a pan-African platform focused on celebrating local achievements, cultural promotion, and documenting the profiles of African leaders and innovators.

=== Literary works ===
As an author, Uchegbu has written across both non-fiction political commentary and creative fiction:
* Wings of Destiny: My Journey Through Power, Politics and the Dream of Nigeria's First Female President (2026) – A political memoir evaluating her experiences within the Nigerian political space and advocating for female political participation.
* Ada the Future President – A children's book series focusing on civic responsibility and leadership.
* Kidnapped and The Dark Testament – Fiction books exploring contemporary socio-political anxieties.
* African Short Horror Stories (Volume 1 and 2) – Fiction collections utilizing traditional African folklore, superstitions, and supernatural motifs.

== Political activism and 2027 presidential campaign ==
Uchegbu's political career spans over a decade of continuous participation, during which she contested positions including the Anambra State House of Assembly, the PDP National Women Leadership, and an APC gubernatorial primary in Anambra State.

In June 2025, Uchegbu officially declared her intention to run for the President of Nigeria in the 2027 general election under the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). Running under the campaign blueprint titled "The New Covenant," she argues that Nigeria's recurring socio-economic challenges stem from heavily recycled leadership and structural stagnation. She stands prominently as an advocate against the exclusion of women from major political party tickets, arguing that true democracy cannot be achieved without fair gender representation at the highest executive levels.

Her key campaign policy promises include:
* The establishment of a ₦150 billion Youth Enterprise Fund.
* Fully digitized public administration systems to counter institutional corruption.
* Standardized community health reforms and community-oriented policing.
* Increased representation of youth and women in the national cabinet.

== Media appearances ==
Uchegbu has utilized broadcast media platforms to advocate for structural reforms and greater inclusion of women within Nigeria's executive governance. Between late 2025 and 2026, she made several appearances on Silverbird Television and Radio Nigeria network news broadcasts. During these sessions, she argued against the political recycling of leadership and detailed her policy platform, "The Mother's Care," which calls for community-focused national safety nets and structural shifts in party primary nomination processes.

data.title: Malek Alshammari
data.text:
Malek Alshammari (Arabic: مالك عويد الشمري) is an orthopedic surgeon practising in Kuwait, specializing in hip and knee surgery. Al Salam Hospitals lists him as a consultant orthopedic surgeon whose clinical interests include hip and knee joint replacement, robotic-assisted knee replacement, arthroscopy, and the treatment of sports injuries and degenerative joint conditions. [ref: Dr. Malek Alshammari, Al Salam Hospitals]

== Education and postgraduate training ==
According to his official biography, Alshammari graduated from the Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland. He subsequently completed specialty training and board qualification in orthopedic surgery before undertaking further clinical training in Canada. [ref: ]

His website describes three fellowships completed at McGill University in Montreal and the University of British Columbia in Vancouver. These covered hip and knee arthroplasty, joint reconstruction, arthroscopy, and sports surgery.

=== McGill University ===
Alshammari's official biography states that he completed a fellowship in hip and knee arthroplasty at McGill University, with clinical training at the Jewish General Hospital in Montreal. The training encompassed adult joint reconstruction, including primary hip and knee replacement and complex revision procedures.

The stated scope also included the management of infections associated with joint replacements and fractures around prosthetic joints.

=== University of British Columbia ===
According to the same biography, Alshammari subsequently completed a fellowship in hip and knee arthroplasty at the University of British Columbia. This training focused on adult reconstruction, complex revision joint replacement, and the management of bone loss.

He then undertook an additional fellowship in hip and knee arthroscopy, reconstructive procedures, and sports surgery. His biography describes training in hip preservation, femoroacetabular impingement, acetabular labral injuries, knee ligament reconstruction, and injuries involving multiple knee ligaments. It also lists training in meniscal surgery and the treatment of patellar conditions.

== Clinical practice ==
Al Salam Hospitals identifies Alshammari as a consultant orthopedic surgeon within its Orthopedic, Spinal Surgery and Sports Injuries Center. Its professional profile lists hip and knee replacement, robotic-assisted knee replacement, and hip and knee arthroscopy among his principal areas of practice.

His official website identifies his clinic as being at Al Salam Al Assima Hospital in Kuwait.

=== Joint replacement and reconstruction ===
The hospital profile lists hip and knee arthroplasty among Alshammari's specialties, together with robotic-assisted knee replacement. It identifies hip and knee osteoarthritis as conditions within his clinical practice.

His official biography additionally describes a practice encompassing both primary and revision hip and knee replacement. The revision component is consistent with the areas of postgraduate training described on his website.

=== Arthroscopy and hip preservation ===
Alshammari's hospital profile lists arthroscopy of both the hip and knee. It also identifies hip pain and femoroacetabular impingement among the conditions he treats.

His website describes further interests in hip preservation and the treatment of acetabular labral injuries. These areas are included in its account of his arthroscopy and sports surgery fellowship training.

=== Knee ligament and meniscal surgery ===
Al Salam Hospitals lists knee ligament injuries, meniscal injuries, patellar disorders, and patellar instability among his clinical interests.

His official biography describes a scope of practice that includes reconstruction of the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments, collateral ligament reconstruction, and treatment of injuries involving multiple knee ligaments. It also lists high tibial osteotomy and procedures addressing patellar disorders.

== Professional activities ==
Alshammari is included on the published speaker list of the 4th Kuwait Orthopedic Conference. [ref: 4th Kuwait Orthopedic Conference, kworthoconf.com]

== Selected Publications ==

* Alshammari MO, de Petrillo G, Epure LM, Huk OL, Zukor DJ, Antoniou J. (2023). "Outcomes of Ceramic-On-Ceramic Bearing Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Minimum 10-Year Follow-Up Study." The Journal of Arthroplasty. 38 (7S): S146–S151. doi:10.1016/j.arth.2023.04.018. PMID:37084924. [ref: Outcomes of Ceramic-On-Ceramic Bearing Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Minimum 10-Year Follow-Up Study, The Journal of Arthroplasty]

data.title: European Taekwondo Club Championships
data.text:
The European Taekwondo Club Championships is an annual competition featuring Europe's leading taekwondo clubs, with national teams also permitted to participate. The event was first held in Athens in 2013.

Unlike other European club competitions in combat sports such as judo, wrestling, and karate, the championships do not feature direct team matches between clubs. Instead, the competition follows the format of a regular taekwondo tournament, with athletes competing in separate weight categories. Clubs are subsequently ranked in a medal table, with trophies awarded to the top three.

Depending on the organization of each edition, trophies have been awarded across several age and gender categories. This page presents results exclusively for the senior divisions. The awards have varied over the years and have included the following categories:
1) senior men,
2) senior women,
3) overall seniors (senior men and women combined),
4) overall male competitors (senior men and male youth competitors combined),
5) overall female competitors (senior women and female youth competitors combined), and
6) overall team standings.

The results table below presents the available standings for these categories.

data.title: Katseye discography
data.text:
Girl group Katseye has released three three extended plays (EPs), one compilation album, ten singles, and two promotional singles. Formed in 2023 by Hybe and Geffen Records through the reality competition show The Debut: Dream Academy, [ref: The Business of Katseye, [[Vogue (magazine)] [ref: Sophia Laforteza Joins Final Lineup of The Debut: Dream Academy Girl Group, Billboard Philippines] the group officially debuted on June 28, 2024, with the single "Debut". [ref: Hybe's global girl group Katseye launches with debut single, Yonhap News Agency]

Following "Debut", the group released the single "Touch" on August 5, 2024. [ref: KATSEYE Long For Connection In New Single "Touch" – Listen, Billboard Philippines] On August 16 of the same year, the group released their debut EP, SIS (Soft Is Strong), which peaked at number 119 on the Billboard 200 and entered several international charts. [ref: KATSEYE Roar with Empowering Debut EP 'SIS (Soft Is Strong)', Billboard Philippines]

In 2025, the group released their second EP, Beautiful Chaos, which was preceded by the single "Gnarly" and later supported by "Gabriela". [ref: KATSEYE announce new EP 'Beautiful Chaos', NME] [ref: KATSEYE Unveil New Single 'Gabriela', [[Clash (magazine)] The EP debuted at number four on the Billboard 200, outperforming its predecessor and becoming the group's first top-five entry on the chart. [ref: Morgan Wallen’s ‘I’m the Problem’ No. 1 for Seventh Week on Billboard 200, [[Billboard (magazine)]

In the first half of 2026, the group released the singles "Internet Girl" and "Pinky Up", [ref: Katseye charts career-best with ‘Internet Girl’, The Korea Herald] [ref: KATSEYE Releases 'Pinky Up' Without Manon, Forbes] and collaborated with Le Sserafim and Illit on the track "Iconic by Mistake". [ref: HYBE Girl Groups Unite for ‘Iconic by Mistake,’ Featuring Katseye, Le Sserafim, and Illit, L'Officiel] On August 14, they released their third EP, Wild, [ref: KATSEYE Releases 'WILD' EP with Global Artists, The Chosun Daily] [ref: KATSEYE Release New EP 'WILD' via HYBE x Geffen Records, Billboard Philippines] which debuted atop the Billboard 200, marking their first number-one entry on the chart. [ref: KATSEYE's 'WILD' Debuts at No. 1 on Billboard 200, [[Billboard (magazine)] The release also yielded the group's highest peak on the UK charts to date, with its single "Animal" peaking at number 12 on the UK Singles Chart, while tracks "Hootie Frutti" and "Bel Air" also entered the chart. [ref: Katseye Scores Its Biggest Hit Ever As A New Single Climbs, Forbes]

data.title: U!REKA European University
data.text:
----

U!REKA European University is a European university alliance. The name U!REKA stands for ‘Urban Research and Education Knowledge Alliance’. The alliance brings together higher education institutions with a focus on applied sciences, professional education, and cooperation in teaching, research, and innovation.

=== Member institutions ===
As of 2024, the alliance comprises eleven member institutions:

* Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences (The Netherlands),

* Edinburgh Napier University (Scotland),
* Frankfurt University of Applied Sciences (Germany),
* HOGENT University of Applied Sciences and Arts (Belgium),
* Metropolia University of Applied Sciences (Finland),
* New Bulgarian University (Bulgaria),
* Odessa National Economic University (Ukraine),
* UAS BFI Vienna (Austria),
* Universidade Politécnica de Lisboa (Portugal),
* University of Bari Aldo Moro (Italy)
* VSB Technical University of Ostrava (Czech Republic).

Together, the member institutions represent approximately 123,000 students and 13,000 staff members.

=== Funding ===
The alliance is supported through the European Union's Erasmus+ programme [ref: The European Universities alliances in action - European Education Area, education.ec.europa.eu], which funds cooperation in higher education, research, innovation, and societal engagement. Following its designation as a European University alliance, the U!REKA SHIFT project received co-funding from the European Union [ref: European Universities alliances and their partners - European Education Area, education.ec.europa.eu] for an initial four-year period. The programme also provides opportunities for transitional funding between EU budget periods.

=== Objectives and activities ===
U!REKA promotes cooperation among its member institutions in the fields of teaching, research, innovation, and academic mobility. The alliance develops joint initiatives and projects related to urban challenges, including the Urban Commons Lab [ref: U!REKA Lab: Urban Commons – Collaborative Challenge Based European University Education] and the U!REKA Change Agents programme [ref: U!REKA Change Agents engage students in challenge-based learning to develop skills for innovation, Metrospective]. It also organizes an annual networking event known as U!REKA Connects. [ref: EURASHE at the U!REKA Connects meeting, EURASHE]

The alliance's activities are centred on supporting the transition towards climate-neutral and smart cities. This focus is linked to the European Union's Mission Climate-Neutral and Smart Cities, which aims to support 100 European cities in achieving climate neutrality by 2030 [ref: EU Mission: Climate-Neutral and Smart Cities, research-and-innovation.ec.europa.eu]. Several cities associated with member institutions, including Amsterdam, Helsinki, and Lisbon, participate in the mission. [ref: 112 Mission Cities striving for climate neutrality by 2030, NetZeroCities]

=== History ===

==== Formation ====
U!REKA was established in Amsterdam in November 2016 by six higher education institutions [ref: Explore our journey, U!REKA]:

* Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences (Netherlands)
* HOGENT University of Applied Sciences and Arts (Belgium)
* Frankfurt University of Applied Sciences (Germany)
* Metropolia University of Applied Sciences (Finland)
* Edinburgh Napier University (Scotland, United Kingdom)
* Oslo and Akershus University College of Applied Sciences (Norway; later renamed OsloMet)

In 2020, the alliance expanded with the addition of Politécnico de Lisboa (Portugal) and VSB Technical University of Ostrava (Czech Republic). OsloMet subsequently withdrew from the consortium in 2021.

=== Recognition as a European University Alliance ===
In 2023, U!REKA was selected by the European Commission under the third call of the European Universities Initiative, obtaining official recognition as a European University alliance. [ref: ]

In January 2024, four additional institutions joined the alliance:

* UAS BFI Vienna (Austria)
* University of Bari Aldo Moro (Italy)
* Odessa National Economic University (Ukraine)
* New Bulgarian University (Bulgaria)

=== Partnerships ===
U!REKA cooperates with regional authorities, municipalities, European networks, and other organizations. Its partners include [ref: Our U!REKA Moment: Co-Creating Sustainability Education Across Urban European Contexts, UAS Journal]:

==== Cities and municipalities ====
* Amsterdam
* Cascais

data.title: CarOlé Flamenco
data.text:
CarOlé Flamenco (full name CarOlé Tachíria Acuña Flamenco; also credited as CarOlé Acuña and Tachíria Flamenco) is a fifth-generation flamenco and Spanish dancer, as well as a union actor, stand-up comedian, and mezzo-soprano singer. She is the director and principal artist of CarOlé Flamenco's Compañía FSDT (Flamenco Spanish Dance Theatre), carrying forward her family's Gitano flamenco legacy that began in 1894, as well as the professional company lineage, which Lola Montes started in 1955 and passed to her mother, Carolina Lugo, in succession in 1995 — the oldest flamenco and Spanish dance company lineage in the Americas. [ref: 'The healing power' of flamenco: How dancers are persisting amid a challenging arts landscape, San Francisco Chronicle] [ref: Fourth to Fifth Generation: What My Mother Gave to Me Lives on Through Me, In Dance]

== Early life and family ==

An essay published in In Dance traces her family flamenco tradition that began in 1894 and was practiced at home, running from her great-great-grandmother Domitila Herrera, through her great-grandmother Romelia and her grandmother Dora, to her mother, Carolina Lugo; Ms. Flamenco is the fifth generation.

== Early career and training ==

As a dancer, Ms. Flamenco turned professional at fourteen with Rosa Montoya's Bailes Flamencos. At seventeen, she joined her mother's company as co-director and principal artist, while also building her own solo career as a dancer and actor. In Seville, she was chosen as a private protégée of Pepa Montes, entering the lineage of Matilde Coral and Pastora Imperio; flamenco guitarist Gino D'Auri, who had toured with Lola Montes' company alongside her mother, brought her to Pepa. She trained in acting at the American Conservatory Theater and at the Meisner Technique Studio, where she completed a two-year Meisner program with Jim Jarrett, Sanford Meisner's last teaching protégée. At twenty-two, she became a professional actor, singer, and stand-up comedian. She holds a Bachelor of Arts in theatre and dance from San Francisco State University [ref: Commencement 2025, San Francisco State University] and is a Master of Fine Arts candidate at Saint Mary's College of California. [ref: CarOlé Flamenco, IMDb]

== Career ==

Ms. Flamenco is a professional union actor. She works in film, television, and live theatre, in both dramatic and comedic roles. Her film credits include the Academy Award-winning Milk, Wolf Mother, and Collisions, to name a few.

Sunset magazine profiled Ms. Flamenco, writing that she "brings the soul of Spain to San Francisco." [ref: Dance fever: flamenco star Carole Acuna brings the soul of Spain to San Francisco, Sunset] She was nominated for an Isadora Duncan Dance Award for Outstanding Achievement in Performance – Individual, for Unidad/Unity. [ref: 2016 Award Winners and Nominees, The Isadora Duncan Dance Awards] The San Francisco Chronicles Datebook section opened its feature "'The healing power' of flamenco" with her work reviving flamenco performance in San Francisco.

Her theatre work includes Lady Macbeth in The Dark Season; multiple lead roles at the San Francisco Dungeon; I Love You San Francisco; and Chardonnay Comedy at PianoFight, among others. As a stand-up comedian, she has performed at the Punch Line in San Francisco and Sacramento, Caroline's in New York, and the San Jose Improv, among others.

Following her mother's passing, Ms. Flamenco became director of Compañía FSDT. The company received a Cultural Dance Catalyst Fund grant through World Arts West, supported by the Wallace Foundation. [ref: WAW Cultural Dance Catalyst Fund 2026 Grantees, World Arts West] [ref: Wallace Foundation Provides Boost for Small Minority Art Groups, San Francisco Classical Voice]

== Reception ==

Ms. Flamenco performed with her mother as a mother-daughter duo. Reviewing the two of them dancing together, Oakland Tribune dance critic Ann Murphy wrote: "It is when Lugo and her daughter Carolé Acuña dance together that the women unearth a new dimension in dance…" [ref: Oakland Tribune] Of Ms. Flamenco's own dancing, Murphy wrote that she is "a mesmerizing young woman and a sensuous, generous dancer, as gifted in classical Spanish dance as in gypsy Flamenco." [ref: Oakland Tribune]

data.title: R. K. Mishra
data.text:
Rakesh Kumar Mishra, also known as R. K. Mishra, is an Indian politician and retired Indian Police Service (IPS) officer. A member of the 1986 batch of the Bihar cadre, he served in the Bihar Police and several central armed police forces, including the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) and Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP). He was also Director General-cum-Commandant General of Home Guards and Fire Services in Bihar.

Mishra joined the Jan Suraaj movement after retiring from the police service. He contested the 2025 Bihar Legislative Assembly election from Darbhanga as a Jan Suraaj Party candidate.

== Early life and education ==

Mishra is from Saharsa district in Bihar. He studied civil engineering at Banaras Hindu University, where he received a gold medal. According to his election affidavit, he graduated in 1983.

== Police career ==

Mishra joined the Indian Police Service in August 1986 and was assigned to the Bihar cadre.

Among his early postings was Bhagalpur, where he served as an Assistant Superintendent of Police during the communal riots of 1989.

He subsequently held district policing appointments in Bihar and the region that later became Jharkhand, before moving to central police organisations.

=== Central police organisations ===

Mishra served in the CISF in several capacities. In December 2016, his appointment as Additional Director General of the force was reported.

He also served in the CRPF, including as Inspector General of its Jharkhand sector. He was identified in that position in June 2015, when the force was involved in operations against Maoist insurgents in the state.

Mishra later became Additional Director General of the ITBP. The 2019 IPS civil list records his appointment to that position in July 2017.

=== Bihar Police and Home Guards ===

Mishra also held senior positions in the Bihar Police. In October 2012, he was promoted to Additional Director General and assigned responsibility for police modernisation.

After returning from central deputation, he took charge as Director General-cum-Commandant General of Bihar Home Guards and Fire Services on 27 August 2019.

During his tenure, the department announced measures concerning Home Guard personnel, including the processing of retirement benefits and the payment of allowances. In January 2020, Mishra described arrangements for more timely payments and settlement of retirement benefits.

In March 2020, Prabhat Khabar reported that the department had issued 18 standing orders governing service conditions, duty allocation, payments and grievance procedures.

The department was also involved in the deployment of trained Home Guards for the security of Reserve Bank of India currency chests in Bihar.

== Political career ==

Following his retirement, Mishra became associated with the Jan Suraaj movement led by Prashant Kishor.

In May 2023, he was among a group of retired IPS officers who joined the movement at an event in Patna. The Indian Express reported his participation alongside other former police and administrative officers.

Mishra remained associated with Jan Suraaj as it developed into a political party in October 2024.

In October 2025, the party selected him to contest the Darbhanga constituency in the Bihar Legislative Assembly election.

He finished third, receiving 11,758 votes. The seat was won by Sanjay Saraogi of the Bharatiya Janata Party, while Umesh Sahani of the Vikassheel Insaan Party finished second.

== Awards and honours ==

Mishra received the Police Medal for Meritorious Service in 2003, according to the Ministry of Home Affairs' IPS civil list.

He was awarded the President's Police Medal for Distinguished Service on Republic Day in 2010.

data.title: Bahamas Airways
data.text:
----

Bahamas Airways was an airline based out of Nassau that operated from 1936 to 1970. It was a part of the BOAC group of companies and was one of the first airlines based out of the Bahamas. The company had a large impact during an important period in the development of tourism in the country. It was sold to the John Swire & Sons in 1968 but went out of business 2 years later.

== History ==

=== Establishment ===
Bahamas Airways was founded in 1936 [ref: Bahamas Air Holdings Ltd., Encyclopedia.com] by Charles Collar. [ref: Origins of Bahamian Aviation, The Nassau Institute] Collar was an American who had served in the US Naval Reserve and flown with Pan Am.

The airline took over the routes of Inter-Island Charter Services which had gone out of business after just three years. Millionaire Harry Oakes, one of Collar's customers, invested in the airline, allowing it to buy a Douglas Dolphin.

=== Operations (1941–1970) ===
In 1941, Collar returned to the US and sold the airline to Pan Am. In 1944, American Airways also took an interest in the fledgling airline. [ref: Index to vol. XLVI: July to December 1944, Flight and Aircraft Engineer] In 1947, the airline started flying to a cluster of islands nicknamed the French Leave islands.

In January 1949, the airline was acquired by H. G. Christie's British South American Airways. [ref: B.S.A.A. Acquire Bahamas Line, Gloucestershire Echo] [ref: ] In March 1956, the airline started flying to Grand Turk in the Turks and Caicos Islands via San Salvador, Mayaguana and Great Inagua. [ref: Bahamas Airways '59, Bluegrass Airlines]

In the 1950s, the government subsidised the airline. [ref: Air, Colonial Office Report on the Bahamas for the Years 1952 and 1953] [ref: Air, Colonial Office Report for the Bahamas for the Years 1954 and 1955] [ref: Air, Colonial Office Report for the Bahamas for the years 1956 and 1957]

In April 1959, the new Skyways (Bahamas) purchased a stake in the airline.

Bahamas Airways tried to break into the market flying to Florida, however, it didn't have a lot of success. It acquired bigger airplanes but American passengers still didn't fly with them and opted instead to fly with Pan Am and Mackey Airlines. In addition, the airline had to pay nearly double the cost of maintenance as other carriers. [ref: Flight 24 May 1962 (Britten-Norman Hovercraft Cutaway, Aurora, Bahamas Airways)] In 1958, the airline was also affected by the General Strike. [ref: B. O. A. C. 1957–58, Flight and Aircraft Engineer]

Several other airlines like Pan Am and British Eagle would propose replacements for Bahamas Airways around the same time as the crisis at Bahamas Airways.

However, the airline remained competitive in the domestic market with flights often being overbooked. [ref: ]

Parent company BOAC looked for a buyer for the airline. [ref: Bahamas Airways Pt2: Swire’s Flamingo -, Yesterday's Airlines] In 1961, questions were asked in the House of Commons when Bahamas Airways was sold by BOAC to Eric Rylands and David Brown and then bought back by BOAC in 1960. [ref: Air Commerce... Clearing the Bahamas Air, Flight (magazine)] MPs wanted to know the amount of money that exchanged hands.

The Bahamian government refused to take and interest and, in 1969, BOAC approached John Swire & Sons, which owned Cathay Pacific and had purchased Hong Kong Airways during the 1950s.

=== Collapse ===
In 1968, John Swire & Sons took an 80% stake in the airline, [ref: ] [ref: ] and set about rebranding the airline. [ref: New Image, Twin Falls Times News] The new flamingo motif and flight attendant uniforms, reminiscent of the Royal Bahamas Police Force, attracted attention. The airline ordered a couple of BAC 1-11s to allow it to carry more passengers and fly further. However, it was still bested by competitors flying Boeing 727. A long range BAC 1-11-500 was created by BAC especially for the airline. The airline took on 35 more flight attendants and, in July 1970, the airline announced that it was planning jet services to the Cayman Islands. [ref: Bahamas Airways to Introduce Jet Service, The Caymanian] In total, John Swire spent $30 million dollars. [ref: ]

On 9 October 1970, Bahamas Airways abruptly ceased operations, [ref: Airline going into liquidation, Shropspire Star] $35 million in debt.

The company cited the impact of a US recession on tourism; it had also failed to convince the Bahamian Government to invest in the airline. [ref: Bahamas Airways Ends Operation, Citing Recession, The New York Times] However, the Minister for Transport countered that the government had been been prepared to take a 51% interest in the carrier but the company insisted on a non-negotiable term that was unacceptable to the government and an immediate injection of cash. [ref: ] When the airline went out of business, 600 employees lost their jobs, including 80 pilots.

The airline was eventually wound up in 1973. The same year, the national carrier Bahamasair was born taking over the routes of Flamingo Airlines and Out Island Airways.

== Fleet ==
The airline would utilize a number of airlines during its lifetime:

* a Loening Air Yacht was the first aircraft in the Bahamas Airways fleet
* Douglas Dolphin in the 1930s and 1940s.
* six Vickers Viscounts. All of them removed from the fleet by the end of 1968.
* four Hawker Siddely HS 748; none of them the fleet by 1970 when the airline ceased operations.
* single Canadian Vickers Catalina was removed from the fleet in 1956.

* a couple of Hawker Siddeley Heron until 1959.
* In 1964, it leased a Handley Page Herald
* a small fleet of 3 Handley Page Hermes but, in 1961, the airline would stop using the type
* a PBY-5A Catalina [ref: Civil Aviation, Colonial Office Report on the Bahamas for the Year 1949]
* a Seabee
* the Douglas DC 3s were for a time, a mainstay in the fleet
* similarly, the Grunmann G-21 was one of the most common aircraft in the fleet
* the BAC 1-11s were the last aircraft type to be utilized by Bahamas Airways. There was an aircraft bound for the airline when it ceased operations in October 1970. [ref: MEXICO BERMUDA & THE CARIBBEAN (section Bahamas Airways)]

== Accidents and incidents ==
On 26 February 1938, a Bahamas Airways airplane went to the aid of a stranded yacht at Joulters Cay near Andros. [ref: ]

On 17 March 1947, a Bahamas Airways Grunmann G 21 A Goose went out of control and crashed, there were no fatalities. [ref: Crash of a Grumman G-21A Goose off Nassau | Bureau of Aircraft Accidents Archives, Bureau of Aircraft Accidents Archives]

On 26 August 1949, a Consolidated 16 Commodore would be destroyed in a hurricane. [ref: Other Friday 26 August 1949 Consolidated 16 Commodore]

On 7 December 1959, the Grumman Goose registered as VP-BAP would be involved in a forced landing. [ref: Incident Grumman G-21A GOOSE]

On 20 November 1960, a Douglas DC 3 of Bahamas Airways would suffer an engine fire for unknown reasons, the crew of the aircraft were unable to extinguish the fire and the crew ended up crash landing. [ref: Crash of a Douglas C-47B-30-DK in Nassau, Bureau of Aircraft Accidents Archives]

data.title: Hannah Lew
data.text:
----

Hannah Lew is a Bay Area-based musician, filmmaker, and visual artist best known as the bassist and co-vocalist of the post-punk trio Grass Widow (2007–2013) and as the founder of darkwave group Cold Beat (~2012-present). [ref: WAMU's Bandwidth Presents: Cold Beat, NPR] She also runs a record label, Crime on the Moon, and co-founded Contact Records, a record store in Oakland, California. Her self-titled solo album was released on April 10, 2026.

== Early life ==
Hannah Lew is the daughter of Rabbi Alan Lew. Her family moved often when she was a child. At one point, her family lived in New York City during the week, went to Monroe, New York on weekends, and "lived in the basement for Shabbat." [ref: With dad’s legacy as inspiration, rabbi’s daughter uses music to heal] Her family moved to San Francisco when Hannah was 11, just after the Loma Prieta earthquake. Alan Lew later became the leader of Congregation Beth Sholom in San Francisco, California.

Lew started her first band at age 19. She worked as a visual artist until the September 11 attacks changed her perspective. Lew wanted to "do something that was accessible, that everyone could have." Early in her career, Lew worked at a video store called Lost Weekend. In her twenties, she played moog synthesizer in a band, The Insides, where she was the only girl.

== Grass Widow ==

Lew co-founded Grass Widow with Raven Mahon and Lillian Maring in 2007. [ref: Grass Window: Past Time, Pitchfork]
[ref: Grass Widow, a band in perfect harmony, Washington Post] In one interview, Lew described the band's process as highly collaborative, adding, "We collaborate on songs, each writing parts and all singing. We have band meetings where we make decisions together. We don't have a band leader. It's a very empowering project and it takes a lot of work." Songs were created together in their San Francisco practice space and all members contributed equally to the work of the band. [ref: Grass Widow interview: "Our own internal logic", Dummy] They would often tour for two weeks at a time, in order to remain connected to their friends and family. [ref: Grass Widow [band], The Believer]

Members of the band were often asked about the fact that the band is all-women and about their feminism, and responded with a quote from Gina Birch: "And you ask me if I’m a Feminist? Why the hell would I not be?!" [ref: Grass Widow, Interview] They cited influences like Neo Boys, Kleenex, The Move, and The Kinks as major sources of inspiration. [ref: Grass Widow, Kill Rock Stars]

The band dissolved circa 2013, with members moving on to pursue other projects. [ref: Cold Beat [band], BOMB Magazine] [ref: On figuring out how to do whatever you want, The Creative Independent]

== Cold Beat ==

Lew started Cold Beat after the death of her father, when she felt the collaborative style of Grass Widow (which was already on hiatus) would not work for her. [ref: Grass Widow's Hannah Lew formed new group Cold Beat, releasing debut album in July, BrooklynVegan]
Cold Beat's name comes from a song by the British post-punk group The Sound. The project began as a solo vehicle for Lew, and evolved into a four-piece band. [ref: Cold Beat Dodges the Ghosts of San Francisco, Dives Into Surf-Kissed Post-Punk, Spin] Cold Beat has released five studio albums and two EPs on Crime on the Moon (Lew's own label), Dark Entries Records, DFA Records, and Like LTD. [ref: Cold Beat's Dreamy Synth-Pop Song '62 Moons' Takes Off, NPR All Songs Considered] [ref: Cold Beat discuss the inspirations behind their new album 'War Garden', BrooklynVegan] The album Mother (2020) was recorded while Lew was pregnant. [ref: Indie Basement (2/28): Caribou, Real Estate, Juniore, The Orielles, Cold Beat, Pictish Trail, David Roback's Rainy Day, BrooklynVegan]

== Filmmaking ==
Lew has directed dozens of music videos for her own bands and other acts, including Erase Errata, Tony Molina, and The Mantles. [ref: Music Videos, HannahLew.com] She has also made and released several short films. In 2009, she received both the Leo Diner and Robin Eichman Awards for her short films Stoplight and Over the Hill. [ref: Hannah Lew and Chris Stewart Just Want to Connect., Talkhouse]

== Other projects ==
Lew released San Francisco is Doomed, an anthology of local bands, on her label Crime on the Moon. She released a self-titled album in April 2026, which was named Bandcamp's "Album of the Day" and positively reviewed in The Guardian and BrooklynVegan. [ref: Add to playlist: the maximalist melancholy of Hannah Lew and the week’s best tracks, The Guardian] [ref: Indie Basement (4/10): Squarepusher, My New Band Believe, more]

data.title: Josh Pacewicz
data.text:
Josh Pacewicz is an American sociologist, who is an Associate Professor of Sociology and Urban Studies at Brown University and a 2020 Guggenheim Fellow. [ref: ] His research interests are in the areas of political sociology, historical sociology, urban sociology, the sociology of law, and American political development. [ref: Pacewicz, Josh, vivo.brown.edu]

== Education and Career ==
Pacewicz holds a bachelor’s degree from The University of Texas-Austin, Plan II Honors program. He graduated from the University of Chicago with a Ph.D in Sociology in 2010. [ref: Pacewicz, Josh, vivo.brown.edu] His dissertation was supervised by Andrew Abbott, Elisabeth Clemens, Andreas Glaeser, and Susan Gal. [ref: Pacewicz, Josh, vivo.brown.edu]

From 2010 to 2012, Pacewicz was an ASA Postdoctoral Fellow on the Current Economic Crisis at Stanford University, under the supervision of Mark Granovetter. [ref: Pacewicz, Josh, vivo.brown.edu] He joined the faculty at Brown University in 2012. [ref: Pacewicz, Josh, vivo.brown.edu]

== Research Areas and Books ==
Pacewicz’s research focuses on American statecraft and subnational governance, especially the interplay between federal policy and party politics, municipal finance, political advocacy and expertise, and more generally the democratic process. His research relies primarily on interviews with legislators, state agency employees, municipal officials, and other policy workers. Pacewicz has written about qualitative case selection and comparison [ref: What Can You Do With a Single Case? How to Think About Ethnographic Case Selection Like a Historical Sociologist, Sociological Methods & Research] [ref: After Positivism: New Approaches to Comparison in Historical Sociology, Columbia University Press], and he is the author of two books about American political development and federalism.

In his 2016 book Partisans and Partners: The Politics of the post-Keynesian Society, Pacewicz examines municipal and partisan politics in two Rust Belt cities during the 2008 and 2012 election cycles. [ref: Partisans and Partners: The Politics of the Post-Keynesian Society, University of Chicago Press] The book shows how changes in American federalism—the corporate merger waves that followed 1970s-era financial deregulation and changes in the prevailing logics of inter-governmental finance—eroded the traditional base of both political parties, thus creating an opening for activists to take over grassroots politics, especially within the GOP. Partisans and Partners was a co-winner of the American Sociological Association’s Theory prize. [ref: Past Awards, ASA Theory Section]

His 2027 book, Divided States: Doing Federalism in Red and Blue America, centers officials who interpret and administer federal rights and programs in the states and documents their ongoing efforts to make real the promises of flagship social programs and civil rights guarantees. [ref: global.oup.com] In Republican states, this resulted in policies that were less extreme than legislators’ frontstage rhetoric, but also contributed to an extremist and antidemocratic reorientation among Republicans, who used the architecture of state government to decouple legislative initiatives from their street-level consequences.

== Awards ==
Pacewicz’s articles have received prizes from the American Sociological Association’s Historical-Comparative Section (2016) and Community and Urban Sociology Section (2015 and 2021). [ref: ] [ref: ] He has won an award from the Society for the Advancement of Socio-Economics (SASE) and was a 2020 Guggenheim Fellow. [ref: annual prize, Oxford Academic] [ref: Guggenheim Fellowships: Supporting Artists, Scholars, & Scientists, www.gf.org]

== References ==

data.title: Kutcho deposit
data.text:
The Kutcho deposit (also Kutcho Creek deposit) is a copper–zinc volcanogenic massive sulphide (VMS) deposit in the Cassiar Mountains of northern British Columbia, Canada, about from Dease Lake. [ref: MINFILE No. 104I 060: Kutcho, Main, Sumac, Kutcho Creek, Esso West, MINFILE Mineral Inventory] Discovered in the early 1970s, it has been the subject of exploration and mine proposals by a succession of companies, and of geological research because its host rocks record a primitive Permo-Triassic island arc unlike other VMS settings in the Canadian Cordillera.

==Geology==
The deposit lies within the Kutcho Assemblage (formerly Kutcho Formation), a latest Permian to Early Triassic volcano-sedimentary sequence within the fault-bounded King Salmon allochthon. [ref: Geological setting, U–Pb geochronology, and radiogenic isotopic characteristics of the Permo-Triassic Kutcho Assemblage, north-central British Columbia, Canadian Journal of Earth Sciences] The assemblage comprises basaltic to basaltic andesite flows and tuffs and rhyodacitic to rhyolitic flows, mass flows and pyroclastic flows, intruded by gabbro, diorite, trondhjemite and quartz–plagioclase porphyry. The ore is hosted by rhyolite mass flows near the top of the assemblage; rhyolites from the hanging wall and footwall have U–Pb ages of about 242 million years, and a nearby porphyry intrusion is dated at 244 ± 6 million years. Lead and neodymium isotope signatures indicate formation in an intra-oceanic island arc, probably on oceanic crust, and are inconsistent with the adjacent Stikine or Quesnel terranes. The stratigraphic, lithogeochemical and tectonic setting of the deposit was described by Barrett, Thompson and Sherlock in 1996. [ref: Stratigraphic, lithogeochemical and tectonic setting of the Kutcho Creek massive sulfide deposit, northern British Columbia, Exploration and Mining Geology]

Mineralization occurs in three stratabound, lenticular lenses — Main (Kutcho), Sumac and Esso (Esso West) — along about of a single stratigraphic horizon. The lenses strike about 280° and dip north at 40 to 45°. Sulphides include pyrite, sphalerite, chalcopyrite and bornite, with minor chalcocite and traces of tennantite and galena; the lenses have copper-rich cores and zinc-rich margins. They are surrounded by an alteration halo depleted in sodium and enriched in potassium that extends about 300 metres into the footwall.

Childe and colleagues (1998) interpreted Kutcho as a distinct type of Cordilleran VMS deposit formed in a primitive intra-oceanic arc, and noted similarities with the Sitlika assemblage and the Venables Valley–Red Hill area, which they considered prospective for similar deposits. [ref: Primitive Permo-Triassic volcanism in the Canadian Cordillera: tectonic and metallogenic implications, Economic Geology]

==History==
Sumac Mines Ltd. (controlled by Sumitomo Metal Mining) and Esso Minerals of Canada staked the deposit in 1972 and 1973 respectively, and carried out more than 50,000 metres of drilling and a bulk-sampling crosscut. Esso sold its interest to Homestake Mining (Canada) in 1989; Teck-Cominco held an option from 1992. Western Keltic Mines acquired the property from Barrick Gold and Sumitomo in 2004 and was purchased in 2008 by Sherwood Copper, which merged with Capstone Mining later that year. In June 2017 Desert Star Resources agreed to acquire the project from Capstone, and renamed itself Kutcho Copper Corp. in December 2017.

===Resource and reserve estimates===
All figures below are as reported by the companies and compiled by MINFILE:
* 1986 (published estimate, CIM Special Volume 37): Kutcho lens 17 million tonnes at 1.62% Cu and 2.32% Zn; Sumac about 10 million tonnes at 1.0% Cu and 1.2% Zn.
* 2017 (Desert Star Resources pre-feasibility study): probable reserves of 10.4 million tonnes at 2.01% Cu, 3.19% Zn, 0.37 g/t gold and 34.61 g/t silver.
* March 2019 (Kutcho Copper Corp.): measured and indicated resources (Main, Esso and Sumac combined) of 17.26 million tonnes at 1.85% Cu and 2.72% Zn, plus 10.7 million tonnes inferred.

===Environmental assessment===
A proposal for a 2,500-tonne-per-day underground mine in the Andrea Creek watershed, a tributary of Kutcho Creek, was assessed federally; in 2011 the assessment was downgraded from a comprehensive study to a screening after a redesign, and it was terminated on 20 June 2016. [ref: Kutcho Copper Zinc Silver Gold Mine Project, Dease Lake (Registry 36352), Canadian Impact Assessment Registry] A revised proposal for an underground copper–zinc mine of about 3,500 tonnes of ore per day with a mine life of up to 14 years entered British Columbia's environmental assessment process under the 2018 Environmental Assessment Act in December 2019. [ref: Kutcho, EAO Project Information Centre (EPIC)]

data.title: Copyright Office (India)
data.text:
Established in 1957, the Copyright Office is an official department of the Government of India dedicated to protecting original creative works. The office is directed by the Registrar of Copyrights. It functions within a broader government network (Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade) that oversees patents and business development under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (India) [ref: https://www.dpiit.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/06/3d9c9c2daeefb97bb9ce964370938b71.pdf].

The Copyright Office is the main national authority in India for registering copyrights and overseeing copyright societies. Its headquarters is located at Boudhik Sampada Bhawan in Dwarka,New Delhi.

==History ==

Before India passed its own laws after independence, it followed British copyright rules. The modern Copyright Office was officially opened in 1958. Its main purpose was to create a national record to protect books, plays, music, and art.

From 1958 to 2016, the Ministry of Education managed the office. In 2016, the government transferred it to the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT). This change was made to manage all of India's intellectual property rights in a single department. During this reorganization, the headquarters also moved to Dwarka. [ref: https://dohe-education.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/09/224f8f774f420af628dec35932ffee5c.pdf]

To make registration easier and more modern, the office launched an online "E-filing" system in September 2009. [ref: https://ipindia.gov.in/storage/uploads/media/English_Annual_Report_2024-25.pdf]
[ref: History of Copyright Law in India | Intellepedia]

== Registrar of Copyrights ==
*Jurisdiction
The office is led by the Registrar of Copyrights, who is chosen by the central government. Since 2016, the official who manages India's patents and trademarks also serves in this role.
The Registrar has strong legal powers. When investigating a case, they have the same authority as a civil court judge. For example, they can order people to appear in front of them, make them swear to tell the truth, and require them to provide important documents. [ref: Hand Book of Copyright Law]

*Appellate mechanism
In the past, special groups like the Copyright Board handled copyright arguments. However, the system changed in 2021. Today, if someone disagrees with a final decision made by the Registrar, they must take their appeal directly to a High Court judge. Other issues about business fees and licenses are now handled by Commercial Courts. [ref: https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/acts_parliament/2021/The%20Tribunals%20Reforms%20Act,%202021.pdf]

== Functions and services ==
The primary functions of the Copyright Office include:

* Maintenance of the Register of Copyrights: The office maintains the statutory Register of Copyrights, which records the titles of works and the details of authors, publishers, and copyright owners. [ref: The Copyright Act, 1957]
* Registration and Examination: Processing applications for copyright registration and modifications. Applications undergo a mandatory 30-day waiting period for third-party objections before formal examination. [ref: Copyright Application Workflow, Intellectual Property India]
* Regulation of Copyright Societies: The Registrar monitors and processes applications for collective administration societies (such as the Indian Performing Right Society) and ensures their statutory compliance.
* International Cooperation: Facilitating India's compliance with multilateral copyright treaties administered by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), including the Berne Convention, the TRIPS Agreement, and the Marrakesh VIP Treaty.
[ref: Working of Copyright Board in India]

* Registrar of Copyrights (India)
* Intellectual property in India

data.title: Anthony Chow
data.text:
Anthony K. Chow (Chinese: 鄒果慶) is a Malaysian-born businessman who has served as chief executive officer of Newegg Commerce, Inc. (NASDAQ: NEGG) since 2019. [ref: Honoree: Anthony Chow, Los Angeles Times] [ref: How did Taiwan help Newegg make its comeback?, CommonWealth Magazine] He previously held executive roles at Newegg from 2006 to 2011, and later worked at OTTO Group's China business and Haier Group before rejoining Newegg.

== Education ==
Chow holds a bachelor's degree in electrical and electronics engineering from the University of Toledo and an Executive Master of Business Administration from the UCLA Anderson School of Management. [ref: Newegg CEO Anthony Chow Receives the Los Angeles Times CEO Leadership Award, citybiz] [ref: Form 6-K, www.sec.gov]

== Career ==
Chow first joined Newegg in an executive capacity in 2006, overseeing North American operations and later the company's China operations, including its OZZO Logistics subsidiary, until 2011. [ref: Newegg’s CEO Unifies a Multinational Workforce, UCLA Anderson School of Management]He then worked as an executive at OTTO Group's China business and at Haier Group Corporation.

Chow rejoined Newegg as chief executive officer in 2019, when the company's annual sales had fallen to about $2 billion. He negotiated new supply agreements with Taiwan-based component manufacturers Asus, Gigabyte, MSI, and ASRock. Newegg reported sales growth of approximately 38 percent in 2020. In May 2021, Newegg completed a reverse merger with Lianluo Smart Limited and began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol NEGG, at a reported valuation of approximately $3.9 billion. [ref: Electronics Retailer Newegg Goes Public, Los Angeles Business Journal]

During the COVID-19 pandemic, Newegg continued fulfilling customer orders while several competitors experienced shipping delays; trade publications attributed this to the company's geographically distributed supply chain. [ref: How to Buy PCs (and Parts) That Ship Now: Newegg CEO, Others Explain How They're Maintaining Stock, Tom's Hardware] [ref: The best alternatives to Amazon for buying tech right now, PCWorld] The company also reported increased customer demand during this period for products such as webcams and laptop computers used for remote work.

== Recognition ==
In 2021, Chow received the Los Angeles Times B2B Publishing CEO of a Public Company Leadership Award.

== Professional affiliations ==
Chow was elected to Newegg Commerce, Inc.'s board of directors on August 9, 2025, filling a vacancy created by the resignation of company founder Fred Chang. He is listed as a member of the UCLA Anderson Forecast Board of Advisors. [ref: Board of Advisors, UCLA Anderson School of Management]

== Corporate developments ==
Under Chow, Newegg repositioned its in-house Advanced Battlestations (ABS) brand of pre-built computers toward the gaming market. [ref: Newegg Reinvents the ABS Brand to Focus on the Gaming Community, TechPower Up] In 2025, the trade publication TechPowerUp reported that most of Newegg's initial stock of Nvidia GeForce RTX 50-series graphics cards sold within minutes of release. [ref: Newegg Sold Out Most NVIDIA RTX 50 Series GPUs in Just 5 Minutes, Entire Stock Cleared in 20 Minutes, TechPower Up]

According to the Chinese business publication PEdaily, Newegg's China-based subsidiary, the e-commerce platform SellingPilot, received an industry award in 2025. [ref: 新蛋SellingPilot斩获“2025 新锐奖”，以 AI 智能ERP领跑跨境电商数字化新赛道_行业动态, 投资界] Newegg's China operations were also named an outstanding cross-border e-commerce enterprise by the Shanghai Cross-Border E-Commerce Association in 2022, [ref: ] and received a foreign-trade enterprise award at a national cross-border e-commerce forum, according to a report republished on the Baidu Baijiahao platform. [ref: 新蛋斩获第三届中国对外贸易合作发展论坛 “对外贸易先锋企业”大奖, baijiahao.baidu.com]
