data.title: Kh. Asadul Islam
data.text:
Kh. Asadul Islam, also known as Kh. Asadul Islam Ripon, is a Bangladeshi financial executive and capital-market professional. He has served as the managing director and chief executive officer of Alliance Capital Asset Management Limited since June 2014. His previous positions include chief executive officer of IDLC Securities Limited, executive vice president and head of brokerage at The City Bank Limited, and managing director and chief executive officer of City Brokerage Limited. [ref: ]

His professional activities have included securities brokerage, investment management, institutional investor services, and commentary on Bangladesh's capital-market development. He also briefly served as a non-executive director of Asia Frontier Capital in 2013–2014. [ref: Asia Frontier Capital (AFC) - Asia Frontier Capital, www.asiafrontiercapital.com]

== Career ==

=== Early career ===
Islam began his professional career at Premium Securities Limited before moving to Peregrine Capital Limited and Union Capital Limited. In 2002, he became a director of SES Company Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of Union Capital, where he remained until 2006. He subsequently joined IDLC Securities Limited, serving as its chief executive officer. [ref: Kh Asadul joins City Bank as Head of Brokerage, today.thefinancialexpress.com.bd]

In July 2009, Islam joined The City Bank Limited as executive vice president and head of brokerage, following his tenure at IDLC Securities.

=== City Brokerage Limited ===
On 24 November 2010, The Financial Express reported Islam's appointment as chief executive officer of City Brokerage Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of The City Bank Limited. He was also described in subsequent reporting as the company's founding managing director and CEO. [ref: City Brokerage Limited appoints new CEO, today.thefinancialexpress.com.bd]

During his tenure, City Brokerage provided securities brokerage services to local and foreign investors. In January 2014, The Daily Star quoted Islam on the growth of foreign portfolio investment in Bangladesh during 2013. He attributed the increase partly to macroeconomic indicators and discussed the influence of interest rates, exchange rates, and international market conditions on foreign investment. [ref: ]

=== Alliance Capital Asset Management Limited ===
In June 2014, Islam was appointed managing director and chief executive officer of Alliance Capital Asset Management Limited, an investment management company operating in Bangladesh's mutual-fund industry. [ref: ]

In November 2014, Alliance Capital announced plans to introduce a Shariah-based equity index for institutional investors. The proposed index, developed using research from S&P Dow Jones Indices, was intended to help institutional investors identify Shariah-compliant investment opportunities. Islam discussed the proposed product and its investment objectives in an interview with The Daily Star. The announcement concerned a planned launch rather than a confirmed launch of the index. [ref: ]

In October 2022, Alliance Capital received second place in the asset-management category of the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission's Golden Jubilee of Bangladesh awards, which recognized market intermediaries for their performance in 2021. The award was presented to the company during Islam's tenure as its managing director and CEO. [ref: ]

== International financial activities ==
In October 2013, Asia Frontier Capital, an investment firm focused on frontier markets, announced Islam's appointment as a non-executive director. At the time, he was serving as the managing director and CEO of City Brokerage Limited. [ref: Asia Frontier Capital — October 2013 Newsletter, www.asiafrontiercapital.com]

In February 2014, Asia Frontier Capital's newsletter featured an interview with Islam concerning Bangladesh's economic conditions, investment environment, and opportunities for international investors. [ref: Asia Frontier Capital (AFC) - February 2014 Newsletter - Asia Frontier Capital, www.asiafrontiercapital.com]

In April 2014, Asia Frontier Capital announced that Islam had stepped down from his directorship for personal reasons. [ref: Asia Frontier Capital (AFC) - October 2013 Newsletter - Asia Frontier Capital, www.asiafrontiercapital.com]

His international professional involvement also included discussions of foreign portfolio investment in Bangladesh's securities market through his roles in brokerage and asset management. [ref: ]

== Contributions to capital-market discussions ==
Islam has participated in public discussions on Bangladesh's securities market, investment-product diversification, regulatory coordination, and the participation of institutional and foreign investors.

In December 2011, The Daily Star published his article "Stockmarket: what next?", which examined market instability following the 2010–2011 stock-market decline. The article advocated greater coordination between financial regulators, more transparent supervision, and the introduction of diversified investment instruments, including bonds and index-traded funds. [ref: ]

In December 2016, The Daily Star quoted Islam on the performance of Bangladesh's stock market and the need to address financial indiscipline and limited investment-product diversification. [ref: ]

In October 2021, he participated in a seminar on the institutional role in sustainable financing, organized by the Association of Asset Management Companies and Mutual Funds of Bangladesh as part of World Investor Week. [ref: ]

=== Artificial intelligence in capital markets ===
On 3 October 2026, The Business Standard published Islam's article "Preparing Bangladesh's capital market for AI".

The article examined potential applications of artificial intelligence in financial research, portfolio analysis, investment advisory services, market surveillance, and regulatory compliance. Islam argued that effective adoption would require improvements in market-data infrastructure, cybersecurity, professional training, institutional coordination, and governance.

He also emphasized the importance of human judgment, accountability, and verification when using AI-generated financial analysis. [ref: Artificial intelligence in capital markets]

=== Proposals for capital-market reform ===
On 8 October 2026, Times of Bangladesh published Islam's article "A roadmap to revive the capital market" in its city edition.

The article proposed establishing a Financial Sector Stability Council to coordinate policy among Bangladesh's financial regulators and relevant government agencies. Islam also recommended increasing institutional investment, introducing differentiated capital-gains taxation, simplifying procedures for foreign portfolio investors, expanding stock-market indices, and developing secondary-market trading in government Treasury bonds.

These proposals represented his views on capital-market reform; their publication did not establish that they had been adopted by the government or financial regulators. [ref: A roadmap to revive the capital market, Daily Times Of Bangladesh]

== Regulatory scrutiny ==
In March 2023, the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (BSEC) requested police authorities to restrict Islam's departure from Bangladesh following a regulatory inquiry concerning two mutual funds managed by Alliance Capital Asset Management Limited.

According to reporting by The Daily Star and The Business Standard, the BSEC inquiry committee alleged that approximately Tk 45.07 crore had been transferred from the mutual funds to the asset management company's bank accounts between July 2021 and December 2022 and subsequently withdrawn or transferred elsewhere. [ref: Award-winning asset manager launders Tk45cr, The Business Standard]

Islam disputed the characterization of the transactions as money laundering. He told The Business Standard that the funds had been invested outside the stock market to generate returns and said that the company intended to return the money to the mutual funds. In comments to The Daily Star, he said that the funds had been invested in unlisted companies and that steps had been taken to recall them. [ref: BSEC fines Alliance Capital Asset Tk5 lakh for reporting lapses, The Business Standard]

In August 2026, BSEC imposed a Tk 5 lakh fine on Alliance Capital Asset Management Limited for failing to submit audited financial statements within statutory deadlines. According to The Business Standard, Islam and another company executive attributed the delays to operational restrictions arising from an ongoing regulatory inquiry. BSEC rejected the company's explanation. The financial penalty was imposed on the company. [ref: BSEC fines Alliance Capital Asset Tk5 lakh for reporting lapses, The Business Standard]

== Selected publications ==
Islam has authored commentary concerning financial-market development, investment policy, and technological change. His published writings include:

* "Stockmarket: what next?" — The Daily Star, 20 December 2011. https://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-214951 The Daily Star — Stockmarket: what next?
* "Preparing Bangladesh's capital market for AI" — The Business Standard, 3 October 2026. https://www.tbsnews.net/thoughts/preparing-bangladeshs-capital-market-ai-1561156 The Business Standard — Preparing Bangladesh's capital market for AI
* "A roadmap to revive the capital market" — Times of Bangladesh, 8 October 2026. https://tob.news/a-roadmap-to-revive-the-capital-market/ Times of Bangladesh — A roadmap to revive the capital market

== External links ==
* Official website: https://khasadulislam.com
* Alliance Capital Asset Management Limited: https://www.acaml.com/khasadul

== References ==

[ref: BSEC fines Alliance Capital Asset Tk5 lakh for reporting lapses, The Business Standard]

In August 2026, BSEC imposed a Tk 5 lakh fine on Alliance Capital Asset Management Limited for failing to submit audited financial statements within statutory deadlines. According to The Business Standard, Islam and another company executive attributed the delays to operational restrictions arising from an ongoing regulatory inquiry. BSEC rejected the company's explanation. The financial penalty was imposed on the company. [ref: BSEC fines Alliance Capital Asset Tk5 lakh for reporting lapses, The Business Standard]

Islam has authored commentary concerning financial-market development, investment policy, and technological change. His published writings include:

data.title: Klarita Gerxhani
data.text:
----

\

Klarita Gërxhani is an Albanian-Dutch interdisciplinary economist. She is Professor of Behavioral Socio-Economics at the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (VU Amsterdam) School of Business and Economics, where she serves as Associate Dean of Diversity, Equity and Inclusion. [ref: prof. dr. Klarita Gërxhani, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam] She is a lifelong member of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences (KNAW) and holds the title of Knight of the Order of the Academic Oak, a state decoration conferred by the President of the Republic of Albania in April 2026. [ref: Academy selects 17 new members, Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]

== Early life and education ==
Gërxhani began her academic studies in Tirana, Albania, where she completed an M.A. at the Faculty of Economics, University of Tirana. She moved to the Netherlands, where she earned an M.Phil. and a Ph.D. in Economics through the Tinbergen Institute and the University of Amsterdam, completing her doctorate in 2002 with her thesis "The informal sector in transition: Tax evasion in an institutional vacuum".

== Career ==
Gërxhani began her academic career at the University of Amsterdam, holding successive positions as postdoctoral researcher, assistant professor, and associate professor. She subsequently held a full professorship in the Department of Political and Social Sciences at the European University Institute in Florence, Italy, from 2015 to 2022. She joined VU Amsterdam as Professor of Behavioral Socio-Economics in January 2023. From 2023 to 2025 she served as Head of the Department of Ethics, Governance and Society and from 2026, as Associate Dean of Diversity, Equity and Inclusion at the School of Business and Economics. [ref: Klarita Gërxhani, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam] She is also a research fellow at the Tinbergen Institute. [ref: New Research Fellow: Klarita Gërxhani, Tinbergen Institute]

Gërxhani has supervised fourteen doctoral students to completion, with one ongoing, and has mentored seven postdoctoral researchers.
== Research ==
Gërxhani's research lies at the intersection of behavioral economics and economic sociology, combining laboratory experiments, field experiments, vignette studies, and traditional surveys. Her work spans several interconnected themes.

Her early research examined the informal economy and tax evasion in post-communist countries, particularly Albania. Using surveys and experiments, she showed how a clash between formal institutions and rules on the one hand and informal institutions on the other drives informal economic activity, with tax evasion varying systematically by income source, gender, and institutional context.

A related strand of her work investigates how formal and informal institutions shape individual behavior and how social norms evolve and change over time. In the more than two decades since the start of her career, she has also studied norm compliance, institutional change, and the relationship between social values and collective decision-making.

Her most prominent recent work examines how competitive settings generate gender inequality. Her experiments demonstrate that men and women perform equally well when there is no competition, but that status-ranking competition against peers improves men's outcomes while worsening women's. This effect is observed even when men and women do not differ in ability; it is driven by gendered expectations. [ref: Academy selects 17 new members, Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences] This research was the subject of a feature interview in Het Financieele Dagblad, referenced on the newspaper's front page. [ref: Hoogleraar Gërxhani: 'Meritocratie is een fabel, weten we nu', Het Financieele Dagblad]

She has also studied employer behavior extensively, including how firms recruit workers, how social networks and contacts influence hiring decisions, and how gender and intersectional biases shape the evaluation of job candidates. This work combines laboratory experiments with field and vignette studies to isolate the mechanisms behind labor market discrimination.

An earlier strand of her research explored the role of social capital in post-communist societies, examining how trust and informal networks differ between Eastern and Western Europe and how they relate to economic participation, welfare attitudes, and political behavior.

Gërxhani's work has been covered by De Telegraaf, NPO Radio 1, [ref: Bar weinig vrouwen zijn hoogleraar economie, NPO Radio 1] ABC News Albania, [ref: Interview with Klarita Gërxhani, ABC News Albania] and A2 Business CNN Albania, [ref: Interview with Klarita Gërxhani, A2 Business CNN Albania] and she has been invited by corporations including KPMG and Heineken to discuss the application of her research to workplace inclusion. She has delivered keynote lectures at institutions including the MIT Summer School, the German Institute for Employment Research (IAB), the Leibniz Centre for European Economic Research (ZEW), and the European University Institute.

== Honours and recognition ==
* Elected lifelong member, Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences (2024) [ref: Academy selects 17 new members, Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]
* Knight of the Order of the Academic Oak, conferred by the President of the Republic of Albania (2026)
* NWO Open Competition M grant (2025–2029), Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research [ref: Klarita Gërxhani, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam]
* Aspasia grant, Dutch Research Council (2011) [ref: Aspasia grant, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam]
* VENI grant, Dutch Research Council (2005) [ref: VENI grant, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam]
* Wicksell Prize, European Public Choice Society (2003), for best paper by a researcher under 30 [ref: European Public Choice Society 2003 Wicksell Prize, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam]

== Selected publications ==

=== Books ===
* Barrera, D., Gërxhani, K., Kittel, B., Miller, L., & Wolbring, T. (2024). Experimental Sociology: Outline of a Scientific Field. Cambridge University Press.
* Gërxhani, K., de Graaf, N.D., & Raub, W. (eds.) (2022). Handbook of Sociological Science: Contributions to Rigorous Sociology. Edward Elgar.

=== Journal articles ===
* Gërxhani, K., Brandts, J., & Schram, A. (2023). Competition and gender inequality: A comprehensive analysis of effects and mechanisms. American Journal of Sociology 129(3): 715–752.
* Gërxhani, K. (2021). How ranking performance can hurt women. Harvard Business Review, December 13, 2021.
* Sarsons, H., Gërxhani, K., Reuben, E., & Schram, A. (2021). Gender differences in recognition for group work. Journal of Political Economy 129(1): 101–147.
* Schram, A., Brandts, J., & Gërxhani, K. (2019). Social-status ranking: A hidden channel to gender inequality under competition. Experimental Economics 22(2): 396–418.
* Bills, D.B., & Di Stasio, V., & Gërxhani, K. (2017). The demand side of the hiring process: Employers in the labor market. Annual Review of Sociology 43: 6.1–6.20.
* Gërxhani, K. (2004). Tax evasion in transition: Outcome of an institutional clash? Testing Feige's conjecture in Albania. European Economic Review 48(4): 729–745.

data.title: Londrim Mekaj
data.text:
Londrim Mekaj (born 5 November 2000) is a Kosovan Albanian singer, model and television personality. He is known for his music releases, including the extended play El Divo and the single "Prek", and for winning the fourth season of Big Brother VIP Kosova in 2026. [ref: Londrim Mekaj wins Big Brother VIP Kosovo 4, BalkanWeb] [ref: Përfundon Big Brother VIP Kosova 4 me Londrimin fitues, Telegrafi]

== Early life and education ==

Mekaj grew up in Peja, Kosovo. [ref: Nga kasa e Massimo Dutti-t te fama – Londrim Mekaj, Zë me Mirën Podcast]

Before pursuing a career in entertainment, Mekaj worked at Massimo Dutti, initially as a cashier and later as a manager. [ref: Nga kasa e Massimo Dutti-t te fama – Londrim Mekaj, Zë me Mirën Podcast]

Mekaj studied musicology at the Faculty of Arts. [ref: Nga kasa e Massimo Dutti-t te fama – Londrim Mekaj, Zë me Mirën Podcast]

== Music career ==

Mekaj began releasing music under his own name. His releases include "M'lujti", "Zemër", "Helem", "Prek", "Paramendo", "Exit" and "Je ka mdjeg". [ref: Londrim Mekaj, Apple Music]

In June 2026, he released his extended play El Divo. The EP consists of five tracks: "Bonasera", "Ngom", "My Baby", "Falma" and "Afterparty". [ref: El Divo - EP by Londrim Mekaj, Apple Music]

Following his participation in Big Brother VIP Kosova, Mekaj continued releasing music and performing live. In June 2026, he performed at the Alba Festival in Zürich, Switzerland. [ref: Alba Festival brachte die Kaserne zum Kochen, Zürich 24]

data.title: Remzi Gokdag
data.text:

Remzi Gökdağ (born 1968 in Istanbul) is a Turkish journalist and author.

==Journalism career==

Gökdağ was born in Istanbul in 1968. [ref: Following Footsteps] While studying journalism at Istanbul University, he began his journalism career as a reporter for Cumhuriyet in 1989. [ref: Efsane isimlerin izinde 'Başka Şehirler', Aydınlık] He covered Istanbul's urban development and municipal affairs. [ref: Belediye muhabiri gökdelene karşı, EP Medya] [ref: Bir kent suçunun belgesel öyküsü, Cumhuriyet Kitap Eki]

In the early 1990s, Gökdağ reported for Cumhuriyet on the controversies surrounding the Park Hotel and the Süzer Building, known as "Gökkafes." [ref: Gökkafes haberi suç değil, Cumhuriyet] A lawsuit seeking 2 billion lira in damages was filed against Gökdağ and other defendants over the reporting. The court dismissed the case. [ref: Gökkafes'in sahibinin açtığı dava reddedildi, Cumhuriyet]

In 1993, he received an award from the Contemporary Journalists Association [ref: ÇGD ödülleri sahiplerini buldu, Cumhuriyet] and an honorable mention in the Çetin Emeç Journalism Encouragement Awards [ref: Emeç Ödülleri sahiplerini buldu, Cumhuriyet] for his story about "Matmazel," an elderly member of Istanbul's Rum community living alone in Beyoğlu. [ref: Son sahneyi oynuyor matmazel, Cumhuriyet]

Gökdağ later worked abroad, serving as the Moscow correspondent for Kanal D and Radikal. [ref: Kaliforniya'da Bir Türk Gazetesi, VOA Türkçe] In Los Angeles, he continued reporting for Cumhuriyet [ref: Başka şehirlere zaman yolculuğu, Diken]; by 2005 he had become editor-in-chief of the newly launched California Turkish Times, a Turkish-language newspaper based in California. [ref: ABD'de yeni Türk gazetesi, Cumhuriyet] Cumhuriyet later published his reporting from Zurich [ref: Avrupalı göçmenlerin ekmek kapısı, Cumhuriyet] and Dubai. [ref: Remzi Gökdağ / BAE (Dubai), Cumhuriyet]

Nicholas Bakalar is an American author and editor. [ref: Bakalar, Nicholas, Encyclopedia.com]

== Early life and career ==

Nicholas Bakalar was an editor at Doubleday, HarperCollins, and other publishing houses from 1976 to 1991, acquiring both fiction and a wide range of nonfiction books. His column, called “Vital Signs” and later “In Brief,” appeared weekly. [ref: Mr Nicholas J Bakalar, Healthed]

== Journalism ==

Bakalar wrote more than 2,200 articles for The New York Times between 2004 and 2023, covering health, medicine, science, sports, and other subjects. [ref: Below the Fold: A New York Times X-Ray Dashboard, Below the Fold]

His writing has also appeared in Discover, National Geographic News, and Wildlife Conservation.

data.title: Sunset Paradise
data.text:
Sunset Paradise is an Australian independent-animated action-adventure comedy web series created by Kevin and Luke Lerdwichagul, produced and animated by Glitch Productions, and funded by Screen Australia for YouTube. Serving as a spinoff of the sketch comedy machinima web series SMG4, it focuses on Meggy Spletzer, a character from said series, who decides to take a vacation in order to find the calling she needs, while also fighting a variety of criminals and her inner demon, Shadow Meggy. Unlike Meta Runner, which focuses on Tari as the protagonist but is set in a separate continuity, Sunset Paradise is set within the SMG4 continuity, but remains in a standalone nature to put sole focus on Meggy's ongoing character arc.

Prio to the series, Meggy Spletzer first appeared as a major character in the machinima parody web series SMG4, also created by Luke Lerdwichagul. The series premiered on the GLITCH YouTube channel on 26 March 2021, with new episodes being released weekly from 4 June to 30 July of that year.

== Sypnosis ==
Sometime after winning the final Splatfest and fulfilling her promise to her friend Desti in the first SMG4 feature-length movie, "Meggy's Destiny," Meggy has found it increasingly hard to figure out what she wants to do with her life that gives her a purpose. To help sort herself out with some much-needed relaxation, she takes a vacation to Port Aurora, the island paradise home of the Aura Boras, and host to all manner of colorful tourists, leaving her dear friends behind. Unfortunately for her, the town has become plagued with criminal activity in the lead-up to its Phoenix Festival which takes place once every 100 years, and the closest thing the island has to an authority figure is the inept deputy Auri Bori who Meggy meets and befriends. If she wants to get any peace and quiet, Meggy will need to team up with Auri and lay down the law and bring justice as Port Aurora's new sheriff, leading to one heck of a crazy misadventure. Along the way, she not only has to battle a diverse cast of criminals including the Spud Buds, a rowdy gang of potato thugs, Whisk, a sly, but shy cat burglar, the Funky Fource, a team of super villainous robotic dancers, and the infamous criminal mastermind leading them, Sir Benedict Cumbersnatch, but also dealing with her inner demon self, Shadow Meggy.

== Characters ==

=== Main ===
* Meggy Speltzer (voiced by Lizzie Freeman) is an inkling-turned human and the main protagonist of the series. She goes on a vacation to Port Aurora to figure out what to do next in life, while also helping to fight criminals on the island. Freeman reprises her role as Meggy from SMG4.
* Auri Bori (voiced by Aimee Smith) is the secondary protagonist of the series, who is a young inept, but well-intentioned Aura Bora who is the self-proclaimed deputy of Port Aurora. In the penultimate episode, he sacrificed himself to save Meggy from the laser shot by Benedict at the top of the tower, but was later revived in the series finale.
* Mayora Bora (voiced by Jasmine Yang) is the tritagonist of the series. He is the mayor of Port Aurora. In "Mad Meggy", he was ultimately killed by the Funky Fource when he sacrificed himself to save Meggy and Auri.

=== Villains ===
* Benedict Cumbersnatch (voiced by Edwyn Tiong) is the main antagonist of the series. He is the crime boss of Port Aurora's criminal underworld who, after a confrontation with Auri's grandfather which resulted in the latter’s death, Benedict was cursed to be reduced into an egg-shaped form, forcing him to rely on the Goonies, alongside the Spud Buds, Whisk, and the Funky Fource. He wants to utilize Aloysius's ashes to bring him back to his original form, gain the Phoenix Egg to harness its power, and rule Port Aurora. However, he is defeated for good by Meggy and Auri.
* The Spud Buds (voiced by Kevin Lerdwichagul, Luke Lerdwichagul & Jasmine Yang) are major antagonists in the series. They are a gang of anthropomorphic potato bandits terrorizing Port Aurora and contribute to the crime occurring on the island, and are under the command of Benedict. Their names are Yam, Mash, Duke, & Russet.
* Whisk (voiced by Amber May) is the secondary antagonist in the series. She is a world-class cat thief who's always brimming with confidence and skill, whenever she's wearing her mask, that is. Without it, she turns into a literal scaredy-cat, and is under the command of Benedict.
* The Funky Fource (all voiced by Anthony Sardinha) are major antagonists in the series. They are a "funkalicious foursome of crime-fighting superheroes" who crush evil through the power of dance...or so they claim. In truth, they're frauds who harbor a dark secret behind their acts of derring-do, and are under the command of Benedict. After the fall of benedict, they are forced to fix the damage they caused. Their names are Frank Fresh, Freddy Fresh, Felix Fresh & Phil Fresh.
* Goonies - The recurring antagonsists of the series. They are silent, hulking Aura Boras serving under Benedict's whim as his army of henchmen. They are now working as ice-cream vendors with Aziz.
* Shadow Meggy (voiced by Lizzie Freeman) is one of the two overarching antagonists of the series. She is a mysterious entity and the dark counterpart of Meggy, who exists in her subconscious mind, serving as the manifestation of her negative thoughts and emotions, and the reason Meggy is even visiting Port Aurora in the first place.
* Froy and Doy Maloy (both voiced by Anthony Sardinha) are two minor antagonists in the series. They are a pair of big time magician brothers in Port Aurora who love to con and scam their way to the top. They also owned a pet tiger as their guard named Tig Tig. They only appear in Cat-sino Royale.

=== Supporting ===
* Aziz Youshi (voiced by James Bailey) is a Arab-American ice cream vendor in Port Aurora, who pretends that he is happy with his customers, but in fact he is very unhappy to serve customers and instead, rather unenthusiastic and grumpy.
* Chet (voiced by Anthony Sardinha) is a room cleaner of Hotel Aurora, who has some feelings toward Whisk.
* Aloysius Bori (voiced by Jason Marnocha) is the posthumous overarching protagonist of the series. He was Auri's late Grandfather and the previous sheriff of Port Aurora, who was murdered by Benedict, but not before cursing him into his current form.

== Episodes ==
NOTE: Every episode title–besides the first and last episodes–is a pun or reference to a movie, book, song, and/or video game title.

=== Crossover ===
On 21 May 2021, to promote the series' viral momentum, Glitch produced an animated, non-canon crossover video to hype fans of Friday Night Funkin and to announce the release of the additional episodes on their YouTube channel, as well as introducing major antagonists, "The Funky Force". [ref: If Friday Night Funkin Was 3D - ANIMATION, GLITCH]

== Background and production ==
Sunset Paradise was created by brothers Kevin and Luke Lerdwichagul, who were known for their work on the Super Mario machinima parody web series SMG4, created by Luke Lerdwichagul in 2011.

The series protagonist, Meggy Spletzer, made her debut in an episode titled "If Mario Was In... Splatoon," which was released on the SMG4 YouTube channel on 25 July 2017. [ref: If Mario Was In... Splatoon, SMG4] Initially introduced as a competitive Inkling athlete who participates in the annual Splatfest arena, she quickly became a recurring major protagonist who would protect her friends throughout the web series. On 8 June 2019, her character underwent a permanent transformation from an Inkling into an anime-influenced human in the episode "Final Hours," which served as the finale to SMG4's Anime Arc series–where she also played a central role. [ref: Final Hours, SMG4] At the end of the first episode, co-creators Kevin and Luke Lerdwichagul revealed that they began conceptualizing Sunset Paradise in the spring of 2020, shortly after the release of the first SMG4 feature-length movie, "Meggy's Destiny," and during production for the second season of Meta Runner. [ref: SUNSET PARADISE - EP 1: PILOT, GLITCH] The brothers first revealed the project at the end of the SMG4 episode, "War of the Fat Italians 2020", [ref: War of the Fat Italians 2020, SMG4] where it was later elaborated in a now-deleted update video that they were working on a pilot for a new animation series that would focus entirely on Meggy.

In an "ask me anything"-type Reddit post for the series, co-creator Luke Lerdwichagul stated that they took inspiration from video games such as Super Mario Sunshine and A Hat in Time, in terms of the environment and character concepts. [ref: We took inspiration from games like a Hat in time and Mario sunshine! We studied how they built their environments and built our own version from there!, Reddit] On 12 May 2021, it was announced by various news sources that Screen Australia agreed to provide $1.3 million in funding production for the remaining episodes of Sunset Paradise, alongside other original projects. [ref: Screen Australia Commits to 5 Online Originals; ACTF Welcomes Federal Budget Commitment, Animation Magazine] [ref: Screen Australia announces $1.3 million in online production funding across five projects, IF Magazine] [ref: SCREEN AUSTRALIA announces $1.3 million for 5 online originals, TV Blackbox] [ref: Screen Australia announces $1.3 million in funding for five online originals, [[Mediaweek (Australia)] [ref: Screen Australia invests $1.3 million across five online originals, including one about the Emu War, ScreenHub Australia]

data.title: Three-Phase Design Model
data.text:
The Three-Phase Design Model is an instructional design model for online learning developed by Rob Sims and Deborah Jones in 2002. [ref: Continuous improvement through shared understanding: Reconceptualising instructional design for online learning, Winds of Change in the Sea of Learning: Proceedings of the 19th ASCILITE Conference] The model was developed in response to the limitations of traditional instructional design approaches when applied to online learning environments. Some traditional instructional designs, particularly, those based on a step-by-step process from print-based distance education, offered limited flexibility to change aspects of the course during the delivery. The model offers flexibility in evaluating and improving learning materials, instructional activities and teaching strategies continuously.

The three phases of the model are Functionality, Enhancement and Maintenance. The phases provide direction for the preparation of the course, improvement during delivery and continued maintenance of the online learning environment. At the functionality phase all essential components such as learning materials, instructional activities and technological devices are established to facilitate the beginning of teaching. The Enhancement phase focuses on making improvements during course delivery. This allows for changes to be made after an evaluation is done. The final phase, Maintenance, updates the necessary components for the course after it is taught, making improvements in preparation for future offerings.

The 3PD Model includes collaboration and feedback. Academic staff, instructional designers and technical personnel work together, bringing their different skills and knowledge to the development of the course. Feedback is important in helping to identify areas of the course that need improvement. Information gathered from learners, instructors and development teams can reveal problems with course components such as learning materials, activities and technological resources. [ref: Enhancing Quality in Online Learning: Scaffolding Planning and Design Through Proactive Evaluation, Distance Education]

==Background and Development==

Online learning in higher education was becoming increasingly popular around the time the 3PD Model was developed. The groups involved in creating and delivering course content faced challenges with existing approaches. These challenges included limited time for developing online courses and insufficient consultation between academic staff and development teams. Consequently, some of the resources developed were not completely suitable for the intended teaching and learning activities. Additionally, some of the instructional materials were prepared before they were delivered to students. This posed a problem because it was difficult to introduce changes when needs or problems emerged during the delivery of the course. These challenges highlighted the need for a different approach that would allow interaction, feedback and changes to take place during course delivery.

In 2002, Rod Sims, Graeme Dobbs and Tim Hand published a study examining the planning, design and evaluation of online learning resources. The focal point was the need to consider both educational and technological factors when developing online resources. The authors explained that technology alone was not adequate for the purpose of supporting teaching and learning. The suggestion was to use proactive evaluation, which would embed evaluation into the early stages of planning and designing online learning resources. The aim was not to depend on evaluation only after instructional materials had been developed but instead encourage designers to establish evaluation criteria during planning. The research reflected the wider concerns about instructional design around the same time the 3PD Model was introduced.
==The Three- Phase Model Phases==

===Functionality Phase===

Functionality is the first phase of the 3PD Model. The development team may conduct a preliminary needs analysis to identify what is necessary for the course. Appropriate instructional materials, technological resources, and teaching arrangements are then selected. [ref: E-Learning Development in Higher Education: Maximising Efficiency—Maintaining Quality, ERIC (Education Resources Information Center)] [ref: In search of an Instructional Material Design Model to Support the Implementation of IQF Oriented Curriculum at HEIs, Proceedings of the 1st International Conference on Education Innovation (ICEI 2017)] During this phase, the course is developed as a functional prototype. The essential components of the course must be prepared before teaching begins, leaving further improvements in the other phases. Learners must also be able to access the online course and its learning materials.

The faculty team and support team contribute their different expertise to support the first phase of the model. The faculty team, which includes academic staff, provides subject knowledge and determines the course content along with learning outcomes and assessment requirements. The support team, which includes educational designers, interactive architects, information specialists, and technical personnel focuses on how learners will interact with the learning platform, provides guidance and instructional approaches, and assists with organising learning resources and establishing the technological environment. The professionals coordinate to support the development of the course.

Professional development for academic staff is another aspect of the functionality phase provided to academic staff. Instructors may have limited experience with online teaching and require guidance in using new technologies. Scaffolding is used in the model to help academic staff develop the knowledge and skills needed to teach in the online environment. Support given includes assistance in using online tools, managing digital learning activities, and becoming familiar with different instructional approaches. Continuous support and guidance in this area are given beyond this phase as new challenges arise during course delivery.

===Enhancement Phase===

The Enhancement phase is the second phase of the model. It monitors and evaluates course delivery. The development team performs this task by assessing how the initial design functions during the teaching and learning process. This aspect of the model is called shadowing. Revising instructional plans and making adjustments to course components and delivery arrangements are important activities in this phase. Feedback from both the learners and teachers is used to determine which areas of the course need changes. Learners may also participate in testing instructional activities and evaluating the online environment.

There are three forms of interaction emphasised during this phase:

* Teacher-learner interaction: Instructors and learners communicate through discussions, questions, feedback and academic support
* Learner-content interaction: Learners interact with course materials and learning activities to develop their understanding of the subject
* Learner-learner interaction: Learners participate in group discussions and collaborative activities that allow them to share knowledge and learn from one another

Collaboration continues at this stage among academic staff, educational designers and technical personnel. Academic staff share their experiences of delivering the course and identify areas where additional support or changes may be needed. Educational designers work with instructors to improve learning activities, while technical personnel assist with adjustments to the online environment. Through this cooperation, the team combines its different areas of expertise to address difficulties that may arise during course delivery. As academic staff gain experience, they may take greater responsibility for managing the online course while continuing to receive specialist support.

===Maintenance Phase===

The Maintenance Phase allows for preparation for future course delivery. This is the final stage of the 3PD Model, and different activities occur to ensure that the course remains functional. Any feedback given about the course is then reviewed to identify areas that may need further development. If necessary, course material and other resources are updated to ensure relevance to the course and technical issues are also addressed. There is continued support from academic and technical staff to maintain the learning environment. All of this is done after the course has been taught.

==Developers of the 3PD Model==

===Rob Sims===

Rob Sims, also known as Roderick C.H. Sims, is an Australian academic and researcher in educational multimedia, instructional design and interactive learning. With more than 15 years of experience in developing interactive learning systems, he worked as an Associate Professor of Educational Multimedia at Southern Cross University, Australia, in 1998. [ref: Designing effective interactions for online learning, EdTech'98 – Australian Society for Educational Technology]

Prior to the development of the 3PD Model, Sims undertook research on the use of technology and interactivity in education. Several publications reflected his work in the field. His 1997 publication, Interactive Learning as An "Emerging" Technology, explored approaches to designing interactive learning environments. [ref: Interactive learning as an "emerging" technology: A reassessment of interactive and instructional design strategies, Australasian Journal of Educational Technology] Another publication in 2000, An Interactive Conundrum: Constructs of Interactivity and Learning Theory, investigated the relationship between interactivity and learning theory. [ref: An interactive conundrum: Constructs of interactivity and learning theory, Australasian Journal of Educational Technology]

The development of the 3PD Model resulted from a collaboration with Deborah Jones in 2002. Their work underscored the importance of collaboration and continuous improvement in the design and delivery of online courses.

===Deborah Jones===

Deborah Jones has experience in the field of instructional design and online learning in Australian higher education. Her professional work encompassed the development of online resources and collaboration with academic staff and course-development teams. She worked in the Teaching and Learning Unit at RMIT Business Online in Australia in 2002. [ref: A team-based approach to the production of online courseware (case study), ASCILITE 2002 Conference Proceedings]

One of her contributions involved research on team-based approaches, and in 2002 she co-authored A Team Based Approach to the Production of Online Courseware with Lyn Atkinson and Mary Toohey. In the publication, the authors investigated the contribution of teamwork to the development of an online Commercial Law course.

==Applications and Adaptations of the 3PD Model==

===Applications===

Since its introduction in 2002, the model has been used in various educational environments to guide online course development. The model was used to guide the development of an online Poultry Production course in Australia in 2008. The project involved adapting a course originally designed for distance education into an online format within a restricted development period. [ref: Poultry production online: Where broilers and layers encounter virtual pedagogy, ASCILITE Publications] In 2010, the University of New England in Australia used the model as a part of a curriculum-renewal initiative. It provided a framework for introducing course improvements gradually and supporting collaboration among academic staff and course-development personnel. [ref: Managing Projects for Change: Contextualised Project Management, Journal of Distance Education] Earlier in 2007, the model was used outside Australia to support the development of online courses at Georgia Virtual School in the United States. The project involved developing courses using the Desire2Learn learning management system, including Advanced Placement courses. [ref: The Design of a Computer-Supported Collaborative Learning Environment that Promotes Interaction, 2014 International Conference on Teaching and Learning in Computing and Engineering]

===Adaptations===

Several adaptations of the 3PD Model have been made to meet the needs of different online environments. Backward Design was combined with the Three-Phase Design Model to develop an online doctoral course. This adaptation, implemented by Neal and Hampton, used the 3PD Model to guide the ongoing development of the course, while Backward Design was used to establish the learning outcomes and assessment requirements. [ref: Developing a Challenging Online Doctoral Course Using Backward and Three-Phase Design Models, The Journal of Aviation/Aerospace Education and Research] Another modification was used by Cuevas and Neal in an online doctoral aviation course. Some improvements were made while the course was being taught, but the learning management system limited the scope of these changes. [ref: Informing Online Doctoral Course Development Using Student Feedback, Journal of Online Graduate Education] Aini used the model in German-language instruction in Indonesia. The purpose was to develop learning materials using Adobe Presenter. The three phases of the model were maintained while incorporating needs analysis, expert review and testing of the learning materials. [ref: Variants of Adobe Presenter E-Learning to Effectively Optimize the Teaching of German Language at Universities in Malang, Indonesian, Research on Humanities and Social Sciences]

==Limitations of the 3PD Model==

The Three-Phase Model may present challenges, particularly for institutions with limited staff and resources. The model requires continued collaboration among academic staff, educational designers and technical personnel throughout course development and delivery. This may require considerable staff involvement and institutional resources. [ref: Survey of Instructional Design Models, Association for Educational Communications and Technology]

Technological restrictions may also limit the changes that can be made while a course is being taught. Neal and Hampton documented difficulties in making changes during the teaching of the course. The issue was that some changes could only be made when the course was offered again and not during course delivery.

data.title: The Last Letter
data.text:
The Last Letter is a romance novel including tragic elements by Rebecca Yarros, published by Entangled Publishing. The book came out in 2019 and alternates between letters and first-person viewpoints. Rebecca Yarros has written a lot of romance books, but her most popular work is the New York Times bestselling Empyrean Series, which is a romantic fantasy series.

== Plot description ==
Ella is a single mother of the twins Masie and Colt, and they live together at the Bed & Breakfast called Solitude, in Telluride, Colorado, which Ella runs. Chaos' whole life circles the military, and he’s in the same unit as Ella’s brother Ryan. Therefore he and Ella start having written correspondence, and they immediately find a connection, and ultimately fall in love.

Unfortunately Maise gets diagnosed with advanced neuroblastoma, and only has a 10 percent chance of surviving the year. Ella’s crushed and shortly after, she finds out that her brother died during a mission. When she doesn’t hear from Chaos, she believes that he died alongside her brother. But Chaos isn’t dead, he just couldn’t bring himself to answer Ella. When Ryan’s last wish is for him to go to Telluride and help Ella, he leaves the Army. But when he arrives at Solitude, he introduces him as Beckett Gentry, his real name, not revealing he’s Chaos. Ella's first response is to shut him out. She tells herself that she doesn’t need his help. But Beckett refuses to leave, and starts working with a search and rescue team in the mountains. Over time Ella let him in more and more, and when he meets the children, they immediately connect. With time Beckett earns her trust, and they eventually fall in love. Together they fight Maise’s cancer and take care of the twins.

But Masie’s treatments are expensive, and the insurance Ella signed for the kids isn’t enough to cover everything. Eventually they discover that Becketts' insurance is enough, and therefore Ella allows him to adopt the kids. But shortly after the papers are signed, the insurance company starts questioning the adoption. For them to believe that the adoption was an act of love, Beckett and Ella need evidence that Beckett knew the twins before Masie got sick. Beckett realises that the only way for his insurance to cover Maise’s treatments, is to show the company his and Ella’s letters. This is the evidence they need, but it also means that Ella will discover his lie.

Ella’s whole world breaks down once again. Beckett apologises deeply and tries to explain that his love isn’t a lie. But Ella doesn’t ever want to see his face again. The twins are incredibly sad that Beckett no longer is a part of their life. But when Beckett one afternoon needs to pick Colt up from suspension, since Ella is at the hospital with Masie, everyone realises how much the kids miss Beckett. Therefore he and Ella find a way to coexist, and they eventually find their way back together. At the same time, they find out that Masie is cancer free, which makes everyone unbelievably happy.

Unfortunately the unthinkable happens. During one of the twins’ field trips, Beckett and his rescue team find out that Colt is missing. While walking on the trail, he and his classmate Emma tripped off a steep cliff, and Colt risked himself to save Emma. They eventually find Colt in very bad condition, and there’s nothing Beckett can do to save him. Words can’t describe how big his, Ella’s and Masie’s grief are and together they mourn him. But with time that loss gets easier to carry, and in the end they manage to live through the pain.

== Major themes ==

=== Learning to trust ===
During her life, Ella has had a lot of experience with men leaving her behind. First her father and then her brother, who often promised to soon be out of the Army, but then ended up dead instead. Her ex husband Jeff, who she met at 18 years old and decided to marry in great haste, also left her after discovering that she was pregnant. Because of her trusting issues she also has a hard time with forgiving lies, and she doesn’t tolerate them. So when Beckett first arrives at Solitude, she believes that he’s the same as her brother and father, too restless to settle down and leaving as soon as reality gets too boring. But because Beckett already is in love with her, because of their written correspondence, and also promised Ryan to help her, he stays in Telluride. One step at a time he  finally earns her trust. But it takes a while, and she has a really hard time with letting him in and admitting to herself that she really is in love with him. But when the big lie is out, when Ella realises that Beckett and Chaos are the same person, and that Beckett has been lying to her during the eleven months that he’s been living at Solitude, her trust is broken. She’s mad at herself for letting Beckett in and believing and trusting him, since he was just like everyone else.

As readers we get to follow along on this inner fight, both before and after the lie is out. In the beginning she starts to have troubles with trusting Beckett and if she should let him in. In the end of the novel, she has the same problem. Can she really trust him again and be sure that he won’t lie another time? After some time she understands how much he fights for her and that the risk of him lying again is worth taking because she loves him so much. To get to understand all of Ella’s consideration about Beckett and their relationship, and to see how she in the end leaves all of her experience behind and embraces their love is so inspiring and wonderful to see.

=== The Reality of Living with a sick child ===
The entire novel is shaped by Masie’s cancer and all of the treatments she has to go through. Right from the start, Ella and her family find out that Masie has advanced neuroblastoma, and has a low percentage of surviving the year. To understand that your child is sick and probably won't grow up is the last thing a parent wants to hear. And to still keep your life together, and live with the fear of losing your child is extremely hard. During the whole book, we get to follow along on that journey, where Ella and her little family need to battle everything going on because of Masie’s cancer. To understand all of the little pieces that a family with a sick child has to handle, make the readers more aware of how hard it actually is. Everyone knows how incredibly sad it is to receive a cancer diagnosis, but most people don’t realise how difficult it is to live everyday with it over your head. Therefore this novel helps to increase that knowledge, and it’s also a big inspiration to all of the moms that have children with cancer. To understand that you’re in this together and that it’s possible to still have a little sparkle in a life that's so full of darkness, must be a big relief.

=== Love as a source of hope and happiness ===
Jeff, Masie and Colts’ dad, left Ella when he found out that she was pregnant, and from that moment Ella had to handle everything regarding the kids by herself. This also meant that she had to fight Maise’s cancer all by herself and it really took a toll on her when she needed to be there both for Masie and Colt. She wasn’t that happy mom that she used to be, instead she laid almost all of her time on Masie’s cancer, plus everything else that needed to be done, like handling the Bed & Breakfast, or sorting out the economy. She felt like a really bad mom, and was incredibly disappointed at herself.

So when she got to know Beckett, who was unbelievably helpful to her and the kids, something changed. This change became even more significant when she realised that she had fallen in love with him. Once they started to explore their love, she felt a happiness which she hadn’t felt since before Masie got diagnosed. For Ella, this happiness was especially important because so much of her life had been consumed by Masie’s illness, leaving little room for her own needs and feelings. Her relationship with Beckett reminded her that she could experience love and joy even while facing one of the most difficult periods of her life. Through the novel, readers are shown how important love is in helping people find that spark, even when reality feels like a nightmare. The novel shows that love does not make difficult circumstances disappear, but it can make them easier to face. Even the toughest periods can feel lighter at times because of the people you surround yourself with.

== Development history ==
Rebecca Yarros mostly writes romance novels, and in an interview with Angel Reads she got asked what made her start writing romance novels. Her answer was: “I love the intricacies of relationships and how one person can really change us for the rest of our lives, and man does romance fit that bill! I love falling in love, and since I’ve loved my husband for the last twenty-one years, I get to feel that head-over-heels feeling with every new book.” [ref: ]

When The Last Letter first came out, she also got interviewed by Publishers Weekly about her new book. The novel includes a lot of cancer treatments for Masie’s advanced neuroblastoma. Yarros described that one of her friends from flight school went through the same thing with her son as Ella in The Last Letter did, which meant that Yarros could get a hold of treatment records and good resources. “He was one of the first kids to actually survive using the same treatment that Maisie was given. He’s four years cancer-free right now.” Publishers Weekly also got told that she didn’t want to overwhelm the reader by putting too much sadness in all of the chapters. Because it’s a heavy book Yarros wanted to make Beckett the one to help Ella go through her sadness. She means that a mother to a child with cancer can’t live with all the emotions by herself, and therefore need someone near. Rebecca Yarros also wanted the reader to feel a rollercoaster of emotions, “the highest high of falling in love” and “the depth of sadness that’s possible”. Gratefulness is also an emotion Yarros hoped to evoke from the book. “When you witness someone else’s tragedy, when you love that person, even if it’s through a character in a book, it makes you grateful for the things that you have when you close the pages. I hope that when they come out of it, they can look at their kids and know every mom is just doing the best she can.” [ref: ]

== Publication history ==

* Initial Release (February 26, 2019): Released in paperback and ebook formats by Entangled Publishing, as well as editions via Penguin Books.

* Kindle Editions (January 28, 2020 / May 2024): Digital re-releases and updates on Amazon Kindle.

* UK / International Paperback (November 24, 2022): Published in the United Kingdom by Transworld Publishers (Penguin imprint).

* Translations: Has been translated to 4 different international languages, including French (Chère Ella, Nov 2019), German (Alles, was ich geben kann, Aug 2024), Spanish (La última carta, Apr 2025), and Portuguese (A última carta, Aug 2025).

* Deluxe / Signed Collector's Editions (2025): Re-released as a jacket-less foiled hardcover with stenciled edges and a new letter to readers. [ref: Editions of The Last Letter by Rebecca Yarros, www.goodreads.com]

== Literary significance and reception ==
In October 2025, The Last Letter appeared in third place on the New York Times bestseller list as hardcover fiction. [ref: Hardcover Fiction Books - Best Sellers - Books - Oct. 5, 2025 - The New York Times, The New York Times]

In 2019, the book received a Kirkus Star and made it onto Kirkus Reviews Best Indie Books of the Year. [ref: Best of 2019, Kirkus Reviews]In the review it said: “Yarros’ writing is crisp and sharp, with passages that are poetic without being florid. For example, in a letter to Beckett, Ella writes of motherhood: ‘But I’m not the center of their universe. I’m more like their gravity.’ While the love story is the book’s focus, the subplot involving Maisie’s illness is equally well-developed, and the link between Beckett and the twins is heartfelt and sincere. A thoughtful and pensive tale with intelligent characters and a satisfying romance.” [ref: ]

The Last Letter also got a Publishers Weekly star in 2019, and Louise Fury stated that: “Thanks to Yarros’s beautiful, immersive writing, readers will feel every deep heartbreak and each moment of uplifting love in this tearjerker romance.” [ref: The Last Letter by, www.publishersweekly.com]

= MSA =
The MSA is an organization founded by Liechtenstein, who serves as its chief executive officer (CEO) and founder. The organization consists of founding members and later members who hold various roles, including financial management, law enforcement, diplomacy, debate, and general organizational work.

== History ==
The MSA was established by Liechtenstein and co-founded by Wolf Strashny. Its original membership included individuals responsible for the organization's leadership, financial affairs, enforcement, diplomatic relations, and debate activities. The organization later expanded its membership to include additional participants.

== Leadership and membership ==

=== Founding members ===
The original members of the MSA are:

* Liechtenstein — Founder and CEO (Chief executive officer) of the MSA.
* Wolf Strashny — Co-founder of the MSA.
* John Gornour — Responsible for law enforcement within the organization and serves as an ambassador from TOF II. [ref: TOFII is from the book "The Dawn of Fleivenshtein" which is scheduled to release some time in 2027.]
* Fishy the Plishti — CFO (Chief financial officer), responsible for the organization's financial affairs.
* Ezra Rosenfeld — Head debater and organizational worker.
* Samson Roth — Debater and organizational worker.

=== Non-founding members ===
The MSA also includes members who joined after its founding. These include:

* Louie Heching — Debater and organizational worker.

== Organization and responsibilities ==
The MSA's membership is organized around several areas of responsibility. Its executive leadership is headed by Liechtenstein, while Wolf Strashny holds the role of co-founder. Financial responsibilities are assigned to Fishy the Plishti, and John Gornour is responsible for law enforcement and diplomatic representation from TOF II.

Debate and general organizational work are carried out by Ezra Rosenfeld, Samson Roth, and Louie Heching.

== Membership ==
The MSA distinguishes between its original founding members and individuals who joined the organization later. Founding members include Liechtenstein, Wolf Strashny, John Gornour, Fishy the Plishti, Ezra Rosenfeld, and Samson Roth. Louie Heching is identified as a non-founding member.

data.title: Cecelia (band)
data.text:
Cecelia (Band) is an American hard rock and glam metal band featuring singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Cecelia Casso. The band performs original music influenced by the sound and style of 1980s hair metal and hard rock. Originally based in Denver, Colorado, the band is now based in Las Vegas, Nevada. [ref: Cecelia Band, Cecelia Band]

= History =
Cecelia Casso began developing her musical career in Denver Colorado and began playing guitar in 2013. She began performing live in the Denver area in 2016. Her musical interests center on rock music of the 1960s, 1970s and 1980s, with a particular focus on hair metal and hard rock.

Cecelia (Band) developed as a vehicle for Casso’s original music and live performances. The band’s repertoire and recordings combine original material with the musical style and aesthetic associated with 1980s hair metal and hard rock. The Denver Post has described the Denver-based band as combining hard-rock covers with original songs in the style of 1980s hair metal. [ref: Colorado's cover bands and tribute acts make old music new again, The Denver Post]

Cecelia (Band) has performed the most throughout Colorado during 2021-2025, including appearances at Lost Lake in Denver [ref: Cecelia w/ Pocket Sauce, Twisted Escape + Anti- Omega, www.etix.com], the Rickhouse in Denver [ref: The Social Divide Tour CRASHING WAYWARD, THE ALMAS @ Francisco Studio Denver, CO - April 2nd 2025 7:30 pm, holdmyticket.com], and Moe’s Original BBQ in Englewood. [ref: Cecelia Band, Cecelia Band] The biggest show Cecelia (Band) has performed so far was July 18, 2025 at the Whisky a Go Go in West Hollywood, California, as part of a bill headlined by L.A. Guns. [ref: Whisky A Go Go L.A. Guns, Leila Harlac, Hooligan's Holiday (Motley Crue Tribute), Philthy Rych, Cutt, Tokyo Riot and Cecelia]

In July 2026, Casso relocated from Denver to Las Vegas, where she continued developing Cecelia (Band), writing original music and recording the band’s second release. [ref: Conversations With Cecelia Casso]

= Musical style and influences =
Cecelia (Band)’s music is rooted in 1980s hair metal and hard rock. Casso has cited bands including Stryper, Bon Jovi, Kiss, Def Leppard, Van Halen, Whitesnake, Journey, Europe, Y&T, Mötley Crüe, Dokken and Steelheart among her influences. She has also cited 1960s and 1970s rock artists including the Beatles, the Eagles and Queen as influences and the modern bands My Chemical Romance, the Struts and Pierce The Veil. [ref: Cecelia Band, Cecelia Band]

The band’s original material is characterized by its deliberate use of the musical style associated with 1980s hair metal. Casso told the Denver Post that she writes music to emulate the genre because of her longstanding affinity for it.

= Music And Discography =

Cecelia (Band) released its debut EP, ‘‘Let’s Keep It Goin’’, on February 9, 2024. The five-track EP marked the band’s first official release and is available through major digital music platforms.

data.title: TriTopic
data.text:
TriTopic is an open-source method and Python library for topic modeling of text collections. It was introduced by Roman Egger in 2026. [ref: TriTopic: Tri-Modal Graph-Based Topic Modeling with Iterative Refinement and Archetypes] The method combines semantic text representations based on sentence embeddings with lexical information from tf–idf weighting and, optionally, document metadata in a single document graph. Topics are then identified through repeated graph-based community detection and consensus clustering. [ref: TriTopic – Graph-Based Topic Modeling, SmartVisions]

== Background ==
Topic modeling aims to discover recurring themes in large collections of text. Classical approaches include latent semantic analysis, non-negative matrix factorization and latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA). [ref: Applied Data Science in Tourism: Interdisciplinary Approaches, Methodologies, and Applications, Springer] More recent methods such as BERTopic and Top2Vec cluster documents based on transformer-based text embeddings. [ref: A Topic Modeling Comparison Between LDA, NMF, Top2Vec, and BERTopic to Demystify Twitter Posts, Frontiers in Sociology]

TriTopic belongs to the embedding- and graph-based approaches. Unlike probabilistic models such as LDA, it does not rely on a generative model but represents similarities between documents as a graph. The original publication motivates the method with three limitations it attributes to existing embedding-based approaches: results that vary between runs, a loss of lexical precision, and reliance on a single view of the data.

== Method ==

=== Document representations ===
Documents are first encoded with a sentence embedding model, and the dimensionality of the embeddings is reduced with UMAP. In addition, a lexical representation based on tf–idf captures the actual vocabulary used. Optionally, metadata such as source or date can be included; according to the documentation, metadata only strengthens links between documents that are already similar in content and does not create new ones.

=== Graph construction ===
The representations are fused into a weighted document graph in which documents are nodes and similarities are edges. Neighbourhoods are determined using mutual k-nearest neighbors and shared nearest neighbors, and links that appear in more than one view receive a higher weight.

=== Consensus clustering ===
Communities in the graph are detected with the Leiden algorithm. [ref: From Louvain to Leiden: guaranteeing well-connected communities, Scientific Reports] Because the result depends on random initialisation, TriTopic runs the clustering several times and builds a consensus graph in which document pairs that are frequently assigned to the same community receive stronger links. This is intended to make the results more reproducible.

=== Number of topics and refinement ===
The number of topics can be specified or determined automatically. In automatic mode, several resolution parameters are tested and compared by the coherence of the resulting keywords. The document representations are then iteratively moved towards the centre of their topic and re-clustered until consecutive partitions agree.

=== Topic representation ===
Topics are described by characteristic keywords and representative documents; keyword selection takes into account both how frequent a term is within a topic and how many of the topic's documents contain it. The publication also describes an archetype-based topic representation that considers boundary cases in addition to central documents. Unlike density-based clustering methods such as HDBSCAN, every document is assigned to a topic.

== Further features ==
The library supports partially guided topic modeling, in which known categories are supplied as seed topics while further topics can still emerge from the data. It also provides functions for analysing how topics change over time, hierarchical topic structures, and analysis tools aimed at empirical research, such as topic stability under resampling, thematic saturation and group comparisons.

Large language models are not required to form the topics. They can optionally be used after clustering to name and describe topics.

== Evaluation ==
In the original publication, TriTopic was compared with LDA, non-negative matrix factorization and BERTopic on the 20 Newsgroups, BBC News, AG News and arXiv datasets. The author reports a mean normalized mutual information (NMI) of 0.575 for TriTopic, compared with 0.513 for BERTopic, 0.416 for NMF and 0.299 for LDA. No independent comparative evaluations have been published so far.

== Applications and limitations ==
The documentation lists open-ended survey responses, interviews, customer reviews, news articles, social media posts and support tickets as typical applications, for collections ranging from a few hundred to tens of thousands of texts. It describes the method as less suitable for very short text snippets, for long documents covering many themes (which should be split into sections first) and for corpora of millions of documents.

* Natural language processing

data.title: Magdalen College choir
data.text:
Magdalen College choir is the collegiate chapel choir of Magdalen College, Oxford, a constituent college of the University of Oxford. Established under the college statutes of 1480, it sings services in Magdalen College Chapel and also undertakes concerts and recordings. [ref: The Choir, Magdalen College, Oxford]

The choir is directed by the Informator Choristarum, the historical title of the college's director of music; since 2017 the post has been held by Mark Williams. [ref: People, Magdalen College Choir] Its membership consists of choristers, undergraduate singers known as Academical Clerks, and organ scholars. The choir has appeared at the BBC Proms [ref: Oxford's Magdalen College Choir Admits Girl Choristers for First Time, The Violin Channel] and toured Europe, Japan and the United States. [ref: Magdalen College Choir, Oxford – Biography, AllMusic] The choir is particularly associated with Oxford's annual May Morning celebrations, during which it sings from Magdalen Tower at 6 a.m. on 1 May.

== History ==

=== Foundation and early history ===

The choir was established under the college statutes of 1480, which provided for sixteen boy choristers, eight Academical Clerks and four chaplains. The foundation formed part of the religious and educational establishment of the college, founded by William Waynflete, Bishop of Winchester. Musical direction was entrusted to an Informator Choristarum, a title that remains in use.

The earliest recorded holders of the office included John Clavering, John Hardy, Alexander Bell and Richard Marbrooke, and the early succession also included the composer Richard Davy. In the sixteenth century the office was held by the Tudor composer John Sheppard. Research by Roger Bowers places Sheppard's tenure as one continuous appointment from September 1543 to early 1548, correcting an earlier chronology that divided it into two periods. [ref: John Sheppard (c.1514–1558/59) at Oxford and the Chapel Royal: exculpation and clarification, Early Music]

=== Seventeenth to nineteenth centuries ===

Several composers held the office in the seventeenth century, including Richard Nicolson, Arthur Phillips, Benjamin Rogers and Daniel Purcell. Rogers, appointed in 1665 according to the chapel's commemorative succession board, wrote the Hymnus Eucharisticus that is still sung at May Morning. [ref: Rogers, Benjamin, Dictionary of National Biography, 1885–1900]

In the eighteenth century the post passed from William Hayes to his son Philip Hayes. The nineteenth-century succession included Walter Vicary, Benjamin Blyth, John Stainer (1859), Walter Parratt (1872) and John Varley Roberts (1882).

=== Twentieth and twenty-first centuries ===

Twentieth-century holders of the office included Haldane Campbell Stewart (appointed 1919 and again in 1941, with William McKie in post in between), Philip Taylor, Bernard Rose (1957), John Harper (1981) and Grayston Ives (1991). The college's archives identify Rose's appointment as a change in the status of the post, since the Organist and Informator Choristarum had not previously been a Fellow of the college. [ref: Administration and Chapel Records, Magdalen College Archives] Daniel Hyde was appointed in 2009 and was succeeded by Mark Williams in 2017.

In 2010 the college established the Consort of Voices, a separate ensemble giving female students the opportunity to take part in chapel music. The choir welcomed its first female Academical Clerk in 2020. [ref: Music for May Morning, Opus Arte] In March 2026 the college announced that girls would be admitted as choristers from September 2027, following plans for Magdalen College School to become co-educational; the change was reported by national and student media as ending an all-male chorister tradition dating to the choir's foundation. [ref: Oxford's Magdalen College Choir will admit girl choristers for first time in over 500 years, [[Classic FM (UK)] [ref: Magdalen College Choir to admit girls for first time in 500-year history, [[Cherwell (newspaper)] The number of chorister places is to rise from sixteen to eighteen, with a fully mixed treble line expected by 2031. [ref: Magdalen College Choir to admit girls as choristers, Magdalen College, Oxford]

== Organisation and services ==

The trebles are choristers educated at Magdalen College School. The adult voices are the Academical Clerks, who are undergraduate members of the university, and the organ scholars play for services and accompany the choir.

During university terms the choir sings Evensong at 6 p.m. every day except Monday, together with the Sunday morning Eucharist. Its repertoire ranges from Renaissance polyphony and Anglican church music to contemporary commissions.

=== Recordings and reception ===
The choir has recorded for labels including Harmonia Mundi, Opus Arte and Coro. Gramophone named its 2024 album Voices of Thunder, which marked the installation of the chapel's new organ, an Editor's Choice in January 2025, [ref: Choir of Magdalen College Oxford, Presto Music] and reviewed the 2019 album The Pillar of the Cloud favourably.

== May Morning ==

[[File:William Holman Hunt - May Morning on Magdalen Tower.jpg|thumb|upright=1.2|May Morning on Magdalen Tower (1890) by William Holman Hunt]]

At 6 a.m. on 1 May the choir sings from the top of Magdalen Tower as part of Oxford's May Morning celebrations. The ceremony includes Hymnus Eucharisticus by Benjamin Rogers, and forms part of a longer tradition of May Day observance at the college. The precise origins of the custom are uncertain: the tower was built between 1492 and 1509, and the surviving evidence points to singing from it on May Morning by at least the late seventeenth century. [ref: May Morning and Magdalen College, Oxford, Folklore] [ref: The history of May Morning] In 2026 the event, which is organised by Oxford City Council, drew a crowd of about 18,500. [ref: 18,500 people celebrate May Morning in Oxford, Oxford City Council]

The ceremony was depicted by the Pre-Raphaelite painter William Holman Hunt in May Morning on Magdalen Tower (1890), which shows choristers and adult singers assembled on the tower. Two versions of the composition survive, one of them in the Lady Lever Art Gallery. [ref: William Holman Hunt and May Morning at Magdalen College, Magdalen College, Oxford]

In 2020, when public gatherings were restricted during the COVID-19 pandemic, the choir produced a virtual May Morning performance, with members recording their parts remotely. In 2021 a performance was pre-recorded at the top of the tower, and in 2022 the choir held its first live May Morning since 2019. [ref: Magdalen's May Morning tradition returns, [[Gramophone (magazine)] [ref: Virtual May Morning, Magdalen College, Oxford]

== Directors of music ==

The musical direction of the chapel has historically been entrusted to the Informator Choristarum and the organist, offices that have often been held by the same person. The following list follows the commemorative board in the organ loft of Magdalen College Chapel. Dates are those inscribed on the board; where only a year of appointment is given, no end date has been inferred. data.title: Mary Muriel Ludidi-Gaobepe
data.text:
Mary Muriel Ludidi-Gaobepe is a South African-born educator, researcher, and activist who contributed significantly to women's vocational education and community development during her time in exile in Zambia.

== Early Life and Education ==
Mary Muriel Ludidi was born in Gwadu Village, Willowvale District, Eastern Cape to her parents, James Jubilee Ludidi and Dinah Siphunzi Ludidi. She grew up within the prominent Gaobepe and Ludidi family structures in the Eastern Cape. She pursued her primary and higher education in South Africa, qualifying as a professional educator before entering into political exile.

== Career and Exile in Zambia ==
During the South African liberation struggle, Ludidi-Gaobepe relocated to Zambia, which served as a major urban hub for the exiled liberation movement. She became a prominent lecturer at the Teachers' Training College in Kitwe, helping shape the landscape of regional education.

In the early 1970s, she participated in an international study visit to Australia sponsored by UNESCO to examine educational frameworks. [ref: UNESCO Study Visit: South African Educator in Australia, National Library of Australia (Trove)] In 1973, she co-authored and published a comprehensive country report on the social, educational, and economic conditions of women in Zambia for the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa. [ref: Zambia, United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (Open Library / WorldCat)] During this period in exile, her home in Zambia also functioned as an important node of hospitality and support for active liberation leaders, including African National Congress (ANC) President Oliver Tambo.

== Personal Life ==
She was married to her husband, Godisang Au-Rheims Gaobepe. Together, they raised a family that included three children born in South Africa and during their time in Zambia. Her legacy continues through her children: Soga, Nomsa, and Neo. Her grandchildren, including Thandiwe Gaobepe, Godisang Nzo, Naledi Gaobepe, Nkululeko Nzo, Moranodi Gaobepe, Odueste Gaobepe, and Mthunziwabantu Alfred Nzo, maintain her archival history.

== Publications ==

data.title: Cogitopic Principle
data.text:
The “Cogitopic Principle” is a formal logical constraint expressing the necessary structural conditions for faithfully representing a cogito-capable Observer. Its starting premise is the assertion that “at least one experience occurs”. Experience is treated as a primitive predicate on Observer states: it holds for at least one state, but not for every state, and no further defining criterion is required for this formulation. With no assumed “prohibitor,” all finitely describable structures -including descriptions of noise- remain available without privileged status. A description represents a given cogito-registration only where its registered distinctions and specified continuation relations are in place. A description lacking that structure remains available but is cogito-incapable with respect to that registration. The principle is an analogue of the “Anthropic Principle” directed at the registering Observer. Its conditioning consists entirely in structural compatibility: no agent chooses descriptions, and no external process filters or removes them. Its formal content concerns the presence or absence of the structure identifying a registration, without requiring a philosophical interpretation of consciousness, an ontology of the Observer or an account of its physical constitution.
