data.title: Sim Shagaya
data.text:
Simdul  Shagaya (born 1975) known as Sim Shagaya is a Nigerian electrical engineer and technology business executive. He is the founder and chancellor of Miva Open University, a digital and distance learning higher institution,  uLesson - an educational technology company offering e-learning resources to African students, and  Konga, a Nigeria e-commerce company. [ref: How uLesson's present and past employees perceive Sim Shagaya's leadership style] [ref: ] [ref: "I look back now and I think I could have built this very differently." — Sim Shagaya on lessons learnt building Konga] [ref: Sim Shagaya: Entrepreneur Transforming Commerce, Education In Africa, Leadership] [ref: Konga ex-boss, Sim Shagaya started and failed at these 4 projects before finding success] [ref: Why ex-Konga boss, Sim Shagaya is now venturing into education with ed-tech startup, uLesson]

== Early life and education ==
Sim Shagaya was born in 1975 to John Nanzip Shagaya. His father was a Brigadier General in the Nigerian Army and served as commander of ECOMOG force in Liberia in 1993. [ref: Brig-General John Shagaya 1942-2018, Daily Trust] He was elected Senator for Plateau South Senatorial District in 2007 to the 6th Senate of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. Senator Shagaya died on 11 February 2018 in a fatal auto crash in his home state of Plateau. [ref: UPDATED: Ex-senator John Shagaya dies in road accident, www.premiumtimesng.com]

Shagaya received his secondary school education at the Nigerian Military School, Zaria, and enlisted in the Nigerian Army where he had a stint before leaving to further his studies in the United States. [ref: The 9 companies Sim Shagaya built: From early failures to rewriting Nigeria's tech rules] He studied Electrical Engineering at George Washington University where he earned a bachelor of science degree. He attended Thayer School of Engineering, Dartmouth College for his master of science degree in Engineering Management, and Harvard Business School where he obtained a master of business administration (MBA) in 2003.

== Career ==
Shagaya’s career started in the late 1990s with several failed start-ups. In 2005, he founded his first successful company, E-Motion Advertising - an outdoor advertising agency. [ref: Business leaders who built empires from unlikely beginnings, Punch Newspapers] He ran the  company until 2019 when it was  acquired by Loatsad Promomedia. [ref: Konga founder Sim Shagaya's earliest company, E-Motion Advertising acquired by Seyi Tinubu's Loatsad Promomedia] [ref: Sim Shagaya enters venture capital space with “The Honey Badger Fund”] In 2011, Shagaya founded his second company, DealDey - a shopping website that tracks online discounts on popular goods and services for consumers. [ref: Ringier Africa acquires DealDey from Konga’s Sim Shagaya, Financial Nigeria International Limited]

In 2012, relying on his experience from the DealDey company, Shagaya diversified into e-commerce. He founded Konga, an online retail marketplace selling a wide range of consumer products. Konga was one of the early e-commerce start-ups in Nigeria and was initially impacted by lack of trust in online transactions, payment security, poor delivery infrastructure and low internet penetration. The company later became one of the popular online shopping companies in Nigeria. [ref: Konga Founder Had To Pay A Debt Of NGN 60 Mn That Wasn't His & Fake A Heart Attack To Save The Business, WeeTracker]  Shagaya stepped down from the company as its chief executive officer in 2016. In 2018, it was acquired by Zinox Group - a Nigerian technology company. [ref: Konga's former CEO, Sim Shagaya, establishes a new company 'uLesson', Nairametrics] [ref: Fall and rise of 48-year-old Sim Shagaya, brain behind Miva Open University, uLesson Group – Businessday NG]

Edtech

In 2019, Shagaya switched interest from e-commerce to education and founded uLesson Group - an educational technology company focused on making learning material accessible to African students online. uLesson's e-learning platform went live in 2020, initially focusing on primary and secondary school education offering curriculum based learning resources through digital devices such as recorded video lessons, quizzes, and assessments. [ref: With uLesson, Sim Shagaya is now top of the class, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News] [ref: Sim Shagaya the Serial Entrepreneur Behind Konga, Ulesson, Business Elites Africa]

In 2023, Shagaya founded Miva Open University under the uLesson Group. He is the chancellor of the university. [ref: ]

data.title: P & R Ginger Jo R
data.text:
----

P & R Ginger Jo R (I.F.S.B. No. 127252; whelped 18 November 1973) was an American Foxhound owned and handled by Jacob “Jackie” Ryals of McRae, Georgia. In 1976 she won the United States Open (U.S.O.) and the National Field Trial Championship. The Chase and The Lumber City Log described those two titles, won in the same year, as unmatched in the sport. She remains the only foxhound, male or female, to win both events in the same calendar year.

== Early life and background ==
Ginger Jo R was whelped on 18 November 1973. She was sired by Allegany Ringo and out of Pittman Snow Bird. She was produced through a collaborative breeding program between Dr. C.W. Pittman of Raleigh, North Carolina and Ryals.  Ryals took the pick of the litter and raised her at his kennels in McRae.

The Chase quoted Ryals as saying she was “the sorriest looking little female you ever saw, but when she was turned loose at six months with older hounds that would not run a deer, she took right to foxhunting. At nine months of age she could hold her own with the other packs".

== Competitive career ==
At fifteen months age she was loaned to E. M. Cannon for the Mid-South Open and was scratched for running a deer.[2]

At the Western Hills field trial she did not have a score going into the last day, then came from behind to be crowned Western Hill Dual Champion.

In 1976 Ginger Jo R won the United States Open at Laurinburg, North Carolina, and the National Field Trial Championship at Panama City, Florida. Contemporary reports said more than 600 hounds were entered at the National. The Chase said she finished first in hunting, trailing, speed and drive, and endurance.

The Lumber City Log reported that the National win brought eight trophies, including challenge trophies, the Jasper Maupin Memorial Trophy, and the James Trophy.

In December of the same calendar year, she was entered into the U.S. Open Field Trial in Laurinburg, North Carolina. Despite freezing temperatures and frozen ground during the first two days of the event, she outperformed 353 other hounds to capture the High General Average (HGA) title and secure the U.S.O. championship. With this victory, she became the only hound in history to win both the National and the U.S. Open in the same calendar year [ref: List of National and U.S. Open Champions, The Chase]. [ref: N FCh Ginger Jo R. Wins Top USO Honors, The Chase]

== Sale and later life ==
In February 1977 Paul May purchased Ginger Jo R for $10,000, setting a record at the time for the highest price paid for a field trial hound. In 1978 she returned to the Ryals kennels in McRae. She was retired from field trial competition to be utilized for breeding with notable studs at the Ryals Kennels.

The Ryals kennels produced other champion hounds, including Jackie’s Scout, winner of the 1980 National Field Trial Championship. Ryals and that hound appeared on the cover of The Chase.[1]

== Burial ==
She is buried at the National Hall of Fame Cemetery of Fox Hounds at Boles Field in the Sabine National Forest, Shelby County, Texas. The headstone lists Western Hill Dual Champion, National Champion, and U.S.O. Champion.

data.title: Humankind 2 (video game)
data.text:
Humankind 2 is a turn-based strategy 4X video game currently in development by Amplitude Studios. A sequel to Humankind (2021), the game will be released for Windows in 2027.

== Gameplay ==
Humankind 2 is a 4X game similar to its predecessor. Like its predecessor, players are able to select whichever civilizations to play as across six eras of human history, from the nomadic age to the modern day, ultimately deciding how their civilizations evolve over time. The game introduces a new system called First Tales, which are founding myths that affect the development of civilizations in-game. [ref: Humankind 2 Rethinks One of Its Predecessor’s Most Divisive Ideas, Which May Solve The Great Culture-Switching Debate, IGN]

Players can also choose to keep playing as the civilization they chose at the start of the game, unlike its predecessor. Every civilization also has a new culture tree, which provides bonuses related to the chosen civilization's history and culture. A new system called Adaptations is introduced. Adaptations provide bonuses depending on which biomes your cities are located in on the world map. [ref: After Civ 7 stumbled, Humankind 2 looks like it's making smart choices to pick up the 4X torch, PC Gamer]For example, a city in the desert can adopt methods to gather water and protect against the heat, while a city in the forest can specialize in hunting animals and foraging fruit. Players can also adopt advancements from other civilizations they interact with in-game. [ref: 4X strategy sequel Humankind 2 gets its first extended in-game footage, rich in era-spanning, culture-shaping, history-rewriting action, Rock, Paper, Shotgun]

== Development ==
Humankind 2 is currently being developed by Amplitude Studios. [ref: Humankind 2 Forces You To Deal With The Consequences Of Climate Change, GameSpot] It was revealed at the 2026 Gamescom Opening Night Live with a live action trailer. [ref: Humankind 2 announced, coming 2027, and promises climate change and "a new take on historical strategy", Eurogamer] The trailer was produced by Nu Boyana Film Studios, which was based in Sofia. The game is set to be released for Windows in 2027. [ref: Humankind 2 trailer accused of being 'AI slop,' studio says nope: 'real actors, practical sets, and custom-made props', PC Gamer]

data.title: Zoopunk
data.text:
----

Zoopunk is an upcoming action role-playing video game developed and published by the Chinese studio TiGames. The game is a prequel to F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch (2021), and changes the earlier game's side-scrolling Metroidvania format into a three-dimensional, third-person action role-playing game.

==Gameplay==
The game is played from a third-person perspective and combines melee and ranged combat with exploration. TiGames has described its areas as wider and more vertically layered than those in F.I.S.T., but not as a seamless open world. [ref: Zoopunk and the revival of wildness beyond wasteland aesthetics, IGN China] Three playable characters were announced: Rayton, an agile rabbit who specializes in close-range attacks; Braton, a rhinoceros who fights with heavy attacks and a large flame sword; and Trixie, a chipmunk who relies on acrobatics and hit-and-run tactics. Each character has a distinct combat role. [ref: Zoopunk shown in a spectacular new trailer, Gamereactor] [ref: ZOOPUNK Gamescom 2026 trailer screenshots, Gematsu]

== Premise ==
The story is set decades before F.I.S.T.: Forged In Shadow Torch, during the origins of Torch City. The discovery of Fire Seed energy accelerates technological development but also awakens mechanical debris, which becomes a self-aware mechanical empire. [ref: ZOOPUNK confirmed for PS5, Xbox Series, and PC; reveal trailer, Gematsu] [ref: Enter the Dieselpunk Chaos of Torch City in ZOOPUNK Coming to Xbox and PC, TheXboxHub] Rayton, Braton, and Trixie travel through territories controlled by competing animal factions as the First Torch War begins, with the characters shown pursuing an object called the Spark. [ref: Xbox Partner Preview November 2025 Everything Announced From Our Amazing Partners, Xbox Wire] [ref: 動物たちによるド派手なアクション『Zoopunk（ズーパンク）』の発売が決定。発売時期は明かされず【Xbox Partner Preview】, Dengeki Online]

== Development and release ==
TiGames began informal discussions about the project in early 2023 and began prototype development in 2024. Studio chief executive Tao Zhang said that the development team had grown from about 20 people to approximately 50, while retaining members of the earlier game's action-design team and composer Caisheng Bo. Chinese concept artist Su Jian was invited to contribute to the visual design. The game is being made with Unreal Engine 5, replacing the predecessor's use of Unreal Engine 4. TiGames cited the newer engine's handling of fur, feathers, lighting, and larger environments as reasons for the change. The term animal punk was used by the developers to describe the combination of anthropomorphic characters, industrial machinery, ruins, and resistance to technological domination.

The January 2025 Nvidia technology demonstration was the first public announcement of the game, which was then described as a project in the same setting as F.I.S.T. [ref: TiGames announces ZOOPUNK for console PC, Gematsu] In an interview published during CES 2025, Zhang called Zoopunk a provisional title and described it as a conventional PC and console game rather than an AI-focused experiment. [ref: Interview with TiGames CEO Tao Zhang on expanding the Animal Punk universe, TapTap] However, following the November 2025 gameplay reveal, the game's visual assets and an in-game tool allowing players to use generative AI for creating content sparked online discussion. TiGames publicly clarified that the core game is entirely human-made. [ref: Zoopunk Says The Game Is All Human Made But Lets Players Use Gen AI To Make Stuff, Kotaku] [ref: Rabbit action game Zoopunk was made by humans not AI says Chinese dev TiGames, Eurogamer]

TiGames formally revealed the game with a gameplay trailer during the Xbox Partner Preview on November 20, 2025. [ref: Every big announcement from the Xbox Partner Preview, Polygon] A second trailer premiered during Gamescom Opening Night Live on August 25, 2026, followed by an extended five-minute gameplay presentation. [ref: Animal Punk action RPG Zoopunk is coming to PC and consoles, RPG Site] [ref: All the Xbox and PC game announcements at Gamescom 2026 Opening Night Live, Windows Central] The game is set to be released for Windows, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X and Series S in 2027.

== Reception ==
Writing after the 2025 reveal, Alberto Zaragoza Lerma of MeriStation characterized the move from a Metroidvania to a three-dimensional action role-playing game as a substantial change from F.I.S.T.. [ref: A standout Chinese game makes the leap to 3D action in its prequel, MeriStation] Michael Hoglund of Windows Central praised the game's "grizzled combat and wondrous colors" but noted that certain visual elements felt off. [ref: ZOOPUNK showcases grizzled combat and wondrous colors but something feels off, Windows Central]

At Gamescom 2026, GamesRadar+ compared the presentation's premise and large-machine combat to other third-person action games, but commented that the density of the trailer made the action difficult to follow. [ref: Gamescom Opening Night Live 2026 Everything announced, GamesRadar+] Fabiano Uslenghi of GameStar called it his action game "surprise" of the event. [ref: Zoopunk was my action surprise of Opening Night Live, GameStar]

Edmund Bibbesworth (died ) was an English politician. He sat as MP for Middlesex in December 1421. [ref: BIBBESWORTH, Edmund (d.c.1445), of Bibbesworth in Kimpton, Herts. and Latton, Essex., History of Parliament Online]

data.title: Uri Shanas
data.text:
Uri Shanas (born April 16, 1961) is an Israeli professor of zoology and nature conservation Oranim College, and founder and CEO of the international nonprofit conservation organization This Is My Earth (TiME). [ref: Prof. Uri Shanas, Biology and Environment - Oranim campus] [ref: Israeli conservationist launching new platform to save at-risk global hotspots, Jerusalem Post]

== Biography ==
Uri was born in Beersheba, Israel, one of four children of Leib and Shoshana Shanas, environmental activists who initiated the fight against the construction of the nuclear reactor between Ashkelon and Ashdod in the 1970s. [ref: The activists who prevented the construction of a reactor in Nitzanim, Haaretz] [ref: Death Wants to Be Your Neighbor, Davar] His father worked for Mekorot, Israel’s national water company, and therefore, the family moved around the country when Uri was a child. From the age of 16, Uri and his family spent two years in Thailand, where his dad worked for Tahal, helping develop the water supply infrastructure in northeastern Thailand. When they returned to Israel, Uri enlisted in the Nahal, was a member of the Scouts' group that lived on Kibbutz Ketura, and participated in the establishment of Shizafon (now Neot-Smadar). [ref: Against Time: The Israeli Trying to Prevent the Greatest Disaster in History, NRG, Makor Rishon]

Shanas received a bachelor's degree in life sciences [ref: The George S. Wise Faculty of Life Sciences, en-lifesci.tau.ac.il] (1988), a master's degree in zoology (1991) and a doctorate with distinction in zoology (1997), all from Tel Aviv University. [ref: Israeli's crowdfunding effort seeks to save forests by buying a piece of them, The Times of Israel] The master's thesis was on the reproduction of the blind mole rat. [ref: Aspects of reproductive behavior of the mole rat Spalax ehrenbergi.] The doctoral thesis dealt with the morphology, chemistry, and pheromonal properties of the harderian gland of the blind mole rat. [ref: The morphology, chemistry, and pheromonal properties of the Harderian gland of the mole rat.]

In 1998, he did a postdoctoral fellowship at Columbia University and then joined the University of Haifa in 2001. From 2009 to 2013, he was head of the Biology and Environment department at the University of Haifa on the Oranim College campus.

Uri is married with three children and lives in Givat Ada, Israel.

== Environmental activism ==
In 2000, Shanas warned about the environmental impacts of the construction of the Trans-Israel Highway: the fragmentation of habitats, destruction of open spaces, roadkill, damage to vegetation, contamination of groundwater and air pollution. [ref: Amateur planning bordering on criminal negligence!, Green, Blue, and White: The Journal of the Economic and Business Forum for Environmental Quality] He pointed out shortcomings in the environmental-impact assessment phase and emphasized the difficulty of predicting in advance the true impacts of projects of this magnitude, warning that the damage could be irreversible. Shanas submitted a petition to the Supreme Court of Israel against the Trans-Israel Highway Company and the State of Israel in a lawsuit to address road runoff and protect the sources of the Yarkon River and water aquifers.

Shanas co-founded the Green Movement party. Two years later, he led the Green Movement’s submission of a petition to the Supreme Court of Israel demanding that the Turkel Committee reconsider Yoav Galant’s suitability for the position of the Israeli Defense Forces’ chief of staff, due to suspicions of land misappropriation. [ref: Green Movement Chief of Staff: Uri Shaines - the man behind the High Court of Justice Gallant, NRG, Makor Rishon] [ref: ] The Green Movement questioned “who gave Galant the extra 35 dunams [of public open space] and why no one else received it.” [ref: Turkel C'tee refuses to question Galant over land deal, The Jerusalem Post]

In 2011, Shanas was involved in research and the fight to protect the Samar Sands in the southern Arava, an area that is a unique habitat for rare and endemic species. [ref: Head to Head: Spiders Versus Tractors in the Samar Sands, Ynet] He worked to raise awareness of the ecological importance of the site and its biodiversity and warned against the harm caused by sand mining and habitat loss. As part of the conservation efforts, Shanas initiated the purchase of land by Israel Nature and Parks Authority, where he was a board member, to help save the last dunes in the area.

In 2015, he co-founded with Alon Tal the international nonprofit organization This is My Earth (TiME), [ref: About us, TiME · This is My Earth] which works to slow the rate of species extinction, combat climate change, and preserve areas of high biodiversity around the world. [ref: Israeli professor hopes to purchase 1.4% of the planet, i24 News] Shanas is TiME’s CEO. The organization operates through an international crowdfunding model, allowing the public to participate in both funding the purchase and long-term protection of natural areas by local organizations and communities and selecting target areas for conservation among a shortlist chosen by TiME’s international scientific advisory committee, on which Shanas sits. [ref: Meet the Israeli Buying Land Across the Globe to Keep It Green, Haaretz]  By 2025, the organization had given grants to local conservation organizations and communities to acquire 13 natural habitats in various countries, including Peru, Colombia, Ecuador, Brazil, Kenya, and the Philippines. [ref: Crowdsourcing NGO purchases 700 acres in Brazil, Kenya for conservation, The Jerusalem Post]  TiME funded the conservation of over 14,000,000 m2 of ecologically critical areas, the protection of hundreds of endangered animal and plant species, and the reduction of carbon-dioxide emissions.

Shanas has served as a member of the board of directors of the Society for the Protection of Nature and a plenary member and chair of the professional scientific committee at the Israel Nature and Parks Authority, and was a co-founder and board member of the environmental organization Adam Teva Ve Din.

== Research ==
Shanas specializes in conservation biology. He is particularly interested in the biodiversity and ecology the Arava desert, and is affiliated with the Arava Institute of Environmental Studies, where he teaches courses and supervises field studies in ecology. [ref: Dr. Uri Shanas, Arava Institute for Environmental Studies]

Notably, Shanas helped discover a new species of huntsman spider, Cerbalus aravensis. [ref: Desert Spider Discovery on Jordan-Israel Border, The New York Times] [ref: New spider species is largest of its type in Middle East, Science Daily] The species was first discovered in 2003 during a study conducted on both sides of the Israeli-Jordanian border by Shanas and a team of Israeli and Jordanian researchers in the southern Arava region, north of Eilat. Shanas also studied rare and endangered species in this area, including the Middle Eastern short fingered gecko and the Lesser Egyptian gerbil and pointed out the genetic uniqueness of local populations.

Shanas was involved in preliminary studies on the reintroduction of the Carmel deer to Israel.  These studies showed the importance of the deer as a herbivore and leaf eater in the Mediterranean forest [ref: Feeding activity and dietary composition of roe deer at the southern edge of their range, European Journal of Wildlife Research] and its need for a regular source of water in its habitat. [ref: Water requirements as a bottleneck in the reintroduction of European roe deer to the southern edge of its range, Canadian Journal of Zoology]

In 2018, Shanas studied the impact of hunting and land use on the behavior, social structure, and physiology of wild boars in the Carmel region, together with his student Dr. Achiad Davidson. [ref: Wild boar foraging and risk perception—variation among urban, natural, and agricultural areas, Journal of Mammalogy] [ref: Age- and sex-dependent vigilance behaviour modifies social structure of hunted wild boar populations, Wildlife Research] The study examined differences between areas with a lot of hunting and those with minimal hunting, and findings showed that hunting increases progesterone hormone levels in females, advances the age of sexual maturity, increases the boar’s vigilance, changes foraging patterns, and affects herd structure. [ref: The influence of hunting on the social structure and behavior of wild boars in agricultural areas, Ramat Hanadiv] [ref: Research: More Hunting – More Wild Boars, Ynet] However, hunting pressure was not found to cause chronic stress. The findings also revealed that hunting does not reduce the wild boar population and may even contribute to its increase. The results of the study contributed to understanding the biology of wild boars and developing approaches to population management and reducing conflicts between humans and wildlife.

data.title: Showaddywaddy (album)
data.text:
Showaddywaddy is the eponymous debut studio album by English rock and roll revival group Showaddywaddy. Released on 8 November 1974 through Bell, the album peaked at number 9 on the UK Albums Chart and remained in the charts for 19 weeks, [ref: Showaddywaddy by Showaddywaddy, Official Charts] certifying Silver with the British Phonographic Industry (BPI) on 1st February 1975. [ref: BRIT Certified Award – Showaddywaddy – Showaddywaddy, British Phonographic Industry] The album was released and distributed in several European countries, as well as Australia, New Zealand, and Japan.

Unlike the group's later reputation as primarily a covers band, the album features nine original compositions alongside three covers of classic 1950s and 1960s tracks. [ref: Hey Rock 'n' Roll!, Isolation Records] It spawned two successful UK singles: "Hey Rock 'n' Roll" (which reached number 2) and "Rock 'n' Roll Lady" (which reached number 15). Prior to the album’s release the band appeared 5 times [ref: Showaddywaddy Artist Profile, Top of the Pops Archive] on the national British tv show Top of the Pops, miming to the 2 singles from the album.

== Critical reception ==

Record Mirror rated the album a good debut in its review on 16 November 1974, noting "a very solid side one" and that side two was "well played and sung". In a retrospective review for AllMusic, critic Dave Thompson awarded the album four out of five stars, praising the group as one of the finest and most enduring rock & roll revival bands of the 1970s. Thompson noted that while they emerged alongside other glam-era retro groups, their run of early material sounded remarkably pure and authentic, effectively balancing commercial pop appeal with true energy. The Encyclopedia of Popular Music gave the album a three-star rating, meaning the album was "good" by the groups "usual standards."

== Track listing ==
All tracks are written by Buddy Gask, Trevor Oakes, Al James, Romeo Challenger, Dave Bartram, Russ Field, Rod Deas, and Malcolm Allured, except where noted. Track lengths via MusicBrainz. [ref: Showaddywaddy release entry, MusicBrainz]

=== 2000 CD reissue bonus tracks ===
The 2000 reissue on 7T’s Records (GLAM CD 2) included the following bonus tracks, both written by Showaddywaddy:

# “You Will Lose Your Love Tomorrow” (first released on b-side of “Hey Rock ‘n’ Roll”)
# “I’m a Traveller” (first released on b-side of “Rock ‘n’ Roll Lady”)

== Personnel ==
Showaddywaddy
* Dave Bartram – vocals
* Buddy Gask – vocals
* Russ Field – guitar
* Trevor Oakes – guitar
* Al James – bass
* Rod Deas – bass
* Malcolm Allured – drums

data.title: John Biddulph (MP)
data.text:
John Biddulph of Newcastle-under-Lyme, Staffordshire () was an English politician. He sat as MP for Newcastle-under-Lyme in 1419 and May 1421. [ref: BIDDULPH, John, of Newcastle-under-Lyme, Staffs., History of Parliament Online]

He also served as bailiff of Newcastle-under-Lyme from Michaelmas 1408 till 1409; mayor of Newcastle-under-Lyme from 1418 till 1419; probably escheator in Staffordshire from 9 December 1408 till 7 November 1409; and commissioner of inquiry in Staffordshire in February 1422 concerning counterfeiting.

He was the son of Roger Biddulph of Newcastle-under-Lyme. By Michaelmas 1403, he married Margery, the widow of Richard Buntable (died ) of Newcastle-under-Lyme.

data.title: Before You Break My Heart
data.text:
"Before You Break My Heart" is a song by the English singer Jade. It was released through RCA Records on 12 September 2025 as part of her first solo studio album That's Showbiz Baby!. The song was written by Jade, along with Pablo Bowman, and Mike Sabath, the latter of whom also produced it. Additional credits were given to songwriting and production team Holland–Dozier–Holland due to the song's interpolation of "Stop! In the Name of Love" (1965) by the Supremes.

==Background and composition==
[[File:The_Supremes_1966.JPG|thumb|"Before You Break My Heart" interpolates "Stop! In the Name of Love" by the Supremes (pictured).]]
"Before You Break My Heart" is described as a contemporary electronic pop song. [ref: Interview: Jade launches debut album That's Showbiz Baby: "I wanted this album to sound like chaos...I wanted you to listen to every track and be like oh god, what's coming next?", Women in Pop] The song samples vocals from 8-year-old Jade's audition for Stars in Their Eyes singing "Stop! In the Name of Love" by the Supremes. [ref: Curtain Call: Jade Steals the Spotlight on That's Showbiz Baby, The Honey Pop] [ref: Jade Thirlwall interview: life after Little Mix, [[Harper's Bazaar]

Following the song's release, Jade revealed that she is not receiving royalties from the song after being asked about how she was given permission to interpolate the Supremes' song on the track. [ref: Jade won't get royalties from 'Before You Break My Heart' due to Supremes sample, NME] She also explained that the song pays homage to Diana Ross, whom she described as her favorite artist, by prominently featuring the sample throughout the track. [ref: Jade Releases Debut Solo Album That's Showbiz Baby, PM Studio] [ref: Jade Thirlwall forfeits royalties to sample The Supremes on solo album, [[Contactmusic.com]

==Reception==
Puah Ziwei of NME described the song as "groovy" and noted Jade's vocal delivery as "oft-vulnerable." [ref: Jade – That's Showbiz Baby review: pop's star student is ready for the big leagues, NME] David Cobbald of The Line of Best Fit described the song as "more than well worth the listen" and highlighted its interpolation of "Stop! In the Name of Love", calling it a "perfect example of good sampling." [ref: Jade is the star of the show on That's Showbiz Baby, The Line of Best Fit] Jett Tattersall of Women in Pop praised the song for not being overly reliant on its interpolation and called it "an album highlight."

==Live performances==
On 25 July 2025, Jade performed an orchestral concert for BBC Proms at the Glasshouse, accompanied by the Royal Northern Sinfonia. [ref: Jade and Northern Sinfonia give packed crowd a musical masterpiece at BBC Proms in Gateshead, [[Evening Chronicle] After the show's radio broadcast, Jade was joined by her niece Amara to perform "Before You Break My Heart" before the song's release. [ref: A Northern Proms Debut: Jade Thirlwall and Finn Forster at The Glasshouse @ The BBC Proms, Classical Source] The performance was later broadcast as part of the BBC Two special Jade at the Proms: A Homecoming on 8 November 2025. [ref: TV tonight: Cynthia Erivo and Ariana Grande’s big Wicked night in, The Guardian]
It was also part of the setlist of Jade's first solo concert tour, That's Showbiz Baby: the Tour. [ref: The It Girl has arrived: Jade embodies showbiz perfection, Manchester Evening News]

==Visualiser==
On 12 September 2025, Jade premiered a compilation of visualisers for all tracks on That's Showbiz Baby, describing it as a visual album. [ref: Jade shines on debut solo album That’s Showbiz Baby, CelebMix] The visualiser for "Before You Break My Heart" features Jade and her niece, Amara, portraying a younger version of the singer. It was shot in South Shields by director Niyadre on the same day as Jade's BBC Proms show. [ref: Jade 'Before You Break My Heart' by Niyadre, Promonews.tv] [ref: Everything you need to know about Jade's solo music, [[Rayo (streaming)]

==Personnel==
Credits adapted from Apple Music. [ref: Before You Break My Heart]

* Jade Thirlwall – vocals, composition, lyrics
* Ramera Abraham – vocal recording engineer
* Pablo Bowman – composition, lyrics

data.title: Old Tram Bridge
data.text:
The Old Tram Bridge is a now demolished crossing over the River Ribble. Built in 1802 by the Lancaster Canal Company, it was opened in 1804 to carry goods by horse drawn carriages. Following several rebuildings, it was completely demolished in 2024 and replaced by the Preston Tram Bridge which opened in May 2026.

==History==
There has been a bridge crossing the river Ribble since Roman times, the road from Luguvalium to Mamucium (now Carlisle to Manchester) crossed the River Ribble at Walton-le-Dale, south-east of the centre of Preston, and a Roman camp or station may also have been here. [ref: William Dobson, Rambles by the Ribble, Volume 3, "[https://books.google.com/books?id=qu4-AAAAYAAJ&pg=RA2-PA78 Ch. 8, Walton-le-Dale] ", Publisher: W. and J. Dobson, 1864]

The Lancaster Canal Company obtained an act of Parliament, the Westmoreland Canals Act 1792 (32 Geo. 3. c. 101) in 1792 to construct a canal linking the towns of Kendal, Lancaster and Preston to the coalfields around Wigan. [ref: The "First" Tram Road, www.wyrearchaeology.org.uk] The original plan was to build an aqueduct but as a temporary measure, the canal company constructed a tramroad to allow revenue traffic to start flowing. Construction took three years. In 1794, the canal company engaged the services of engineer William Cartwright, first to supervise the construction of the foundations for an Aqueduct and later as Resident Engineer. The five-mile-long tramroad comprised a double-track plateway and was designed to transport wagons carrying coal from the Wigan Coalfields. Wagons were pulled by horses, up to six at a time, and each wagon had a capacity of two tons. Originally there were three inclined planes where the wagons were hauled by stationary steam engines and a continuous chain.

The Old Tram Bridge itself began construction in 1802 out of timber, finishing the following year and opened to the public in 1804. [ref: Old Tram Road] The bridge operated for around 40 years until falling into disrepair until ultimately being closed in 1858; Preston Corporation purchased the bridge from the Lancaster Canal Company in 1872. During the 1890s a chicken shack had floated down the river in a flood and destroyed some of the bridge supports, and so the bridge was reconstructed entirely during the 1890s at which point stone pilasters were installed.

In December 1935, high flood waters caused high levels of damage to the bridge resulting in the timber supports to be replaced in concrete and the replacement of the timber walkway. During World War Two, the timber walkway was removed to hinder a potential enemy advancement in the event of an Invasion. Restoration followed in the 1950s however during the 1960s, the bridge began to fail. A 1960 inspection learned that the concrete supports were beginning to fail and the timber was rotting; as a result, the bridge was closed in November 1964 to await repair. A loan was granted for the necessary work by the Ministry of Housing and Local Government in April 1965, along £17,725 being given by Matthews and Mumby's and work began to replace the concrete and timber by October 1965.

The 1965 bridge served as a vital public link between Avenham Park and Penwortham for over 55 years. However, by the 2010s, the structure began to exhibit signs of critical fatigue. A formal inspection conducted in 2019 identified more than 200 defects including severe fractures in the pre-stressed beams and "spalling" (the degrading and crumbling of concrete supports). These findings and the fear of collapse led to an immediate closure of the bridge on safety grounds. [ref: Preston's Old Tram Bridge closed over 'risk of sudden collapse', BBC News] [ref: REVEALED: The cost of replacing Preston's old tram bridge – and why there is no sign of it happening, Lancashire Evening Post]

The replacement Tram Bridge was funded through Preston City Council's £20 million Levelling Up grant. [ref: Preston's Tram Bridge - What's next?, Preston City Council] The new 125-metre weathering steel bridge was designed by Studio John Bridge and DYSE Structural Engineers, and was lifted into place in December 2025. It opened to the public on 22 May 2026, restoring the active travel link between Avenham Park and South Ribble. [ref: Memories shared as city's £6.6m tram bridge opens]

[[File:Preston Tram Bridge.jpg|thumb|Preston Tram Bridge, the replacement of the Old Tram Bridge as seen from Avenham Park]]

Adenekan is of Nigerian heritage with his family immigrating to Scotland in the 1990s. [ref: REVIEW: Ayo Adenekan: Black Mediocrity, Brass Tacks Comedy, EdFringe 2025 ★★★★★ – Binge Fringe Magazine] He is bisexual, with his show Homeland Insecurity exploring his experiences dating both women and men. data.title: Spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia, Guo–Campeau type
data.text:
----

Spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia, Guo–Campeau type (SEMDGC) is an inherited skeletal dysplasia associated with pathogenic variants in ERI1. It causes pronounced short stature and abnormalities affecting the spine, pelvis, hips, and limbs. Fingers or toes may be shortened, underdeveloped, or absent, and facial features vary between affected individuals. [ref: Spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia, Guo-Campeau type (Concept ID: C5882737), MedGen] The disorder follows an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern. [ref: ERI1, PanelApp]

== Signs and symptoms ==
Skeletal manifestations include limb shortening and abnormalities of the hands and feet. Reported findings include short digits, joined digits, curved fingers, absent toes, restricted elbow extension, and dislocation of the radial head. Hydronephrosis and vesicoureteral reflux have also been recorded.

Radiographs show flattened vertebral bodies, irregular vertebral endplates, and scoliosis in affected individuals. Severity varies: two siblings are alive into their twenties, whereas three other individuals with the severe skeletal phenotype died in infancy or early childhood. These observations describe the initial series rather than an established survival estimate. [ref: Null and missense mutations of ERI1 cause a recessive phenotypic dichotomy in humans, The American Journal of Human Genetics]

== Genetics ==
ERI1 is located on chromosome 8p23.1. It encodes a 3′-to-5′ exoribonuclease involved in RNA processing. Reported severe cases have carried at least one pathogenic missense variant. By contrast, individuals with two null alleles have generally shown milder skeletal involvement. [ref: Congenital Bone Disorders Associated with ERI1-Mediated RNA Metabolism Dysfunction: Spondylo-Epi-Metaphyseal Dysplasia Guo-Campeau Type and Beyond, Current Osteoporosis Reports] The latter presentation, involving digital abnormalities and mild intellectual disability, is classified separately as Hoxha–Aliu syndrome (OMIM 620662).

== Diagnosis ==
The original study combined clinical and radiographic assessment with exome or genome sequencing. Candidate variants were investigated by Sanger sequencing and where parental samples were available, family studies.

== History ==
Guo and colleagues described the disorder in 2023. Their study included eight individuals from seven families with ERI1 variants; five individuals from four families had the severe skeletal phenotype.
==Research==
Cell experiments linked the missense variants to impaired exonuclease activity, abnormal 5.8S ribosomal RNA processing, and reduced histone messenger RNA degradation. Patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells also showed impaired cartilage differentiation.

A 2025 review emphasized that the mechanism connecting altered RNA metabolism to the skeletal abnormalities remains incompletely understood. It also noted that Eri1-knockout mice do not reproduce the full human phenotype, limiting their usefulness as a model of the severe disorder.

data.title: John Bidewell
data.text:
John Bidewell of Barnstaple, Devon () was an English politician. He sat as MP for Barnstaple in February 1383, 1386, 1394, and 1395. [ref: BIDEWELL, John, of Barnstaple, Devon., History of Parliament Online]

He also served as mayor of Barnstaple from Michaelmas 1382 till 1383, 1395 till 1397, and 1399 till 1400; and tax collector of Devon in November 1382, December 1385, and 1398.

By 1386, he was married to Margery, the daughter and heiress of Thomas Hunnacott by his wife Agnes, the widow of Nicholas Reygnee of Barnstaple. He then married his second wife, Isabel.

data.title: Polish Parliament Youth Council
data.text:
The Polish Parliament Youth Council is an official advisory body of the Polish Parliamentary Group for Youth Affairs, established in 2024 to address the underrepresentation of young people in the legislative process.

The Council has over 300 members from across Poland, making it the largest youth advisory body in Polish history.

== History ==
On 10 May 2024, the Polish Parliamentary Group for Youth Affairs appointed the leadership of its Youth Council and tasked it with developing the framework for a parliamentary youth advisory body, organising recruitment, drafting the Council’s rules of procedure, and establishing its organisational structure.

The Council officially began its work on 8 November 2024, during an inaugural session at the Senate of the Republic of Poland. Participants included Marshal of the Senate Małgorzata Kidawa-Błońska, Senators Jerzy Wcisła and Krzysztof Kwiatkowski, former Commissioner for Children’s Rights Marek Michalak, and Deputy Commissioner for Children’s Rights Adam Chmura. With 304 members, the Council became the largest youth advisory body in Polish history. [ref: Obrady Rady Młodzieżowej przy Parlamentarnym Zespole ds. Młodzieży, senat.gov.pl]

On 18 October 2024, the Council organised a conference on children’s rights, during which it called on Prime Minister Donald Tusk to ratify the Third Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of the Child. [ref: W Senacie konferencja poświęcona prawom dziecka, senat.gov.pl]

On 22 October 2024, the Council organised an event on additional educational programmes for schools funded through Poland’s National Recovery Plan, bringing together representatives of the Ministry of Education, local authorities, and NGOs. [ref: W Senacie o dodatkowych programach edukacyjnych, senat.gov.pl]

The Council held its second plenary session on 22 April 2025 at the Silesian Stadium in Chorzów. The session brought together regional government representatives and members of parliament, including Joanna Bojczuk, Member of the Board of the Silesian Voivodeship; Senators Joanna Sekuła, Halina Bieda, and Jerzy Wcisła; and Members of the Sejm Urszula Koszutska and Aleksandra Kot. The discussion focused on encouraging greater civic engagement among young people in Poland. [ref: Głos młodego pokolenia na Stadionie Śląskim, Aktualności i wiadomości * Zabrze, Chorzów, Bytom]

On 15 May 2025, at a press conference in the Senate of the Republic of Poland, the Council concluded its six-month “YouthVote” voter mobilisation campaign, which aimed to encourage young people to participate in the upcoming presidential election. [ref: Apel Rady Młodzieżowej o udział w wyborach prezydenckich, senat.gov.pl]

Together with the Commissioner for Children’s Rights, the Council contributed to drafting legislation aimed at lowering the age at which young people can independently access psychological support from 18 to 13. After being passed by the Sejm and the Senate in June and July 2025, the bill was submitted to President Andrzej Duda for signature. The President instead referred it to the Constitutional Tribunal, citing concerns relating to parental authority. [ref: Co w Zdrowiu, cowzdrowiu.pl]

On 21 November 2025, the Council co-organised a conference on necessary reforms to the Polish government’s housing policy. Young people presented their proposals to representatives of the Ministry of Economic Development and Technology, Ministry of Development Funds and Regional Policy, and Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development. [ref: Młodzi o polityce mieszkaniowej w Senacie RP, senat.gov.pl]

On 27 November 2025, the Council submitted to parliamentarians a comprehensive position paper on proposed changes to Poland’s 2026 state budget. [ref: W Senacie posiedzenie Parlamentarnego Zespołu ds. Młodzieży, senat.gov.pl]

On 26 March 2026, Commissioner for Children’s Rights Monika Horna-Cieślak, together with representatives of the Council and other youth organisations, presented at the Sejm a jointly developed proposal to amend the Social Assistance Act. The proposed amendment would exempt minors from the obligation to cover the costs of an adult’s stay in a social assistance home. [ref: Dzieciństwo bez długów. Konferencja Rzeczniczki Praw Dziecka, Rzecznik Praw Dziecka]

The Council held its fourth plenary session at the Senate of the Republic of Poland on 10 April 2026. Participants included Deputy Marshal of the Senate Rafał Grupiński; Senators Jerzy Wcisła, Jolanta Piotrowska, Agnieszka Gorgoń-Komor, and Krzysztof Kwiatkowski, as well as other parliamentarians; Commissioner for Children’s Rights Monika Horna-Cieślak; Deputy Minister of Education Paulina Piechna-Więckiewicz; and representatives of the Youth Council under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine and the Chancellery of the President of the Republic of Poland. [ref: 4. posiedzenie Rady Młodzieżowej przy Parlamentarnym Zespole ds. Młodzieży, senat.gov.pl]

The Council’s fifth plenary session took place on 25 June 2026 in the Column Hall of the Sejm of the Republic of Poland. Participants included Deputy Marshal of the Senate Magdalena Biejat, Deputy Minister of National Education Paulina Piechna-Więckiewicz, and representatives of the Ministry of Economic Development and Technology, National Labour Inspectorate, Ministry of National Education, and National Centre for Nuclear Research. [ref: V posiedzenie Rady Młodzieżowej przy Parlamentarnym Zespole ds. Młodzieży]

On 9 July 2026, the Polish Parliamentary Group for Youth Affairs met in the Senate to review the Council’s activities and discuss proposals for its future work. The Council’s coordinators presented a summary of its work during the 2025/2026 term, highlighting more than 70 advisory documents adopted during that period, including proposed amendments, draft legislation, and legislative opinions. They also reported on the launch of international initiatives through the Youth Lublin Triangle coalition, cooperation with the UK Youth Parliament and the European Commission, and dozens of new partnerships with NGOs and public institutions.

At the request of the Council’s President, the Parliamentary Group decided to rename the advisory body the “Polish Parliament Youth Council”.

== Objectives ==
The Council focuses primarily on legislative advice and civic engagement. Its main objective is to address the underrepresentation of young people in the legislative process.

Through policy positions and proposals, reports, proposed amendments, and draft legislation, the Council seeks to ensure that young people’s views are represented in the law-making process, working with parliamentarians from across the political spectrum.

The Council also works closely with other youth representative and advisory bodies in Poland, NGOs, and public institutions.

== Structure ==
The Polish Parliament Youth Council consists of 17 thematic committees, which draft advisory documents regarding legislation, as well as of standing committees within departments, which support the work of the committees. Among others, the Council also contains an international department, where teams responsible for different regions build relations with youth advisory bodies from all over the world. [ref: Parlamentarna Rada Młodzieżowa, www.radamlodziezowa.pl]

Councillors working within thematic committees create advisory documents - including amendments to bills, legislative opinions or bills - and consult them with relevant standing committees.

The work of thematic and standing committees is overseen by coordinators of the Council, appointed by the Polish Parliamentary Group for Youth Affairs. Their responsibilities also include organising recruitment for the Council, managing the departments (each is responsible for a different area, e.g. communications, advocacy, law) and acting as intermediaries between the Councillors and the Parliamentary Group for Youth Affairs. All the aforementioned points are fastened together by the Chief Coordinator, who is responsible for the Council’s day-to-day operations.

The Council’s decision-making body for strategic matters and the coherence of the organisation’s operation is the Coordination Committee, composed of representatives of the committees, as well as the Council’s coordinators and the Chief Coordinator, who leads the Coordination Committee’s work.

== Successes and achievements ==

* The Polish Parliament Youth Council represents Poland in the Youth Lublin Triangle - the youth-oriented version of the Lublin Triangle. [ref: Działalność Rady Młodzieżowej tematem Parlamentarnego Zespołu ds. Młodzieży, senat.gov.pl]
* The Polish Parliament Youth Council has led to the submission of numerous bills, including a bill lowering the age for independent access to psychological help, a bill reforming the Fund for Combating Communication Exclusion, and a bill excluding minors from the responsibility for financial obligations of persons residing in social welfare homes. [ref: Parlamentarna Rada Młodzieżowa, www.radamlodziezowa.pl]
* The Polish Parliament Youth Council coordinated the #WylęgarniaDOBRA campaign - a coalition of 47 youth organizations and over 170 youth councilors in response to media coverage targeting young people engaged in the work of youth councils nationwide. [ref: List otwarty ws. odpowiedzialności mediów za przekaz opisujący zaangażowanie publiczne młodego pokolenia - Rada Młodzieżowa przy Parlamentarnym Zespole ds. Młodzieży, www.radamlodziezowa.pl]
* In the 2025/2026 work year, the Council prepared over 70 advisory documents - draft bills, amendments, legislative opinions, analyses, and more.

== Partnerships ==

* Office of the Ombudsman for Children of Poland [ref: Rada Młodzieżowa przy Parlamentarnym Zespole ds. Młodzieży z udziałem RPD, Rzecznik Praw Dziecka]
* Youth Council under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine [ref: 4. posiedzenie Rady Młodzieżowej przy Parlamentarnym Zespole ds. Młodzieży, senat.gov.pl]
* Polish National Centre for Nuclear Research
* State Labour Inspection of Poland
* The European Parliament Representation in Poland
* The European Commission Representation in Poland

data.title: Dyala Khodary
data.text:
----

Dyala Khodary (Arabic: ديالا خضري; born 1979) is a Lebanese contemporary painter based in Beirut [ref: Dyala Khodary - Biography, Art on 56th]. Her work explores the city's people, architecture, infrastructure, and urban landscape through paintings depicting portraits, façades, tiled floors, manhole covers, electrical cables, and other elements of Beirut's environment. Although rooted in recognizable Beiruti scenery, her paintings often move toward abstraction through repetition, decorative pattern, and unusual perspectives [ref: Dyala Khodary répète Beyrouth à l’infini, L'Orient-Le Jour] [ref: Dyala Khodary, un regard sur les formes de Beyrouth, L'Orient-Le Jour].

Education and early career

Khodary graduated from the Lebanese University in 2002 with a degree in Plastic Arts.

Following her studies, she worked professionally in decorative painting. She has described this experience as influential in developing her approach to texture, material behavior, craftsmanship, and painted surfaces, elements that later became defining characteristics of her artistic practice [ref: Des bouches d'égout de Beyrouth à Menart Fair Paris: Le parcours artistique de Dyala Khodary, www.arabnews.fr].

Career

Before her first solo exhibition, Khodary participated in collective exhibitions, including three editions of the Salon d'Automne organized by Beirut's Sursock Museum.

Tailor-Made

Khodary's first solo exhibition, Tailor-Made, was held in 2015 in Beirut at Art on 56th, the gallery that has represented her since. The exhibition presented portraits drawn from the artist’s local surroundings, combining figurative painting with techniques influenced by her background in decorative painting, including patterns, collage, and layered surfaces [ref: ديالا خضري في "غاليري آرت أون 56" الفنانة الشابة ماهرة بتراكيبها ونضارة وجوهها الأنثوية, annahar.com] [ref: La mise en lumière de Dyala Khodary, L'Orient-Le Jour] [ref: " T a i l o r - M a d e " by Dyala Khodary, Lamasat Future TV].

Beirut in Patterns

Her second solo exhibition, Beirut in Patterns, opened in 2018 and marked a shift toward making Beirut's architecture the central subject of her work. Rather than depicting panoramic city views, the exhibition focused on architectural fragments such as balconies, façades, tiled floors, and abandoned buildings [ref: ] [ref: معرض ديالا خضري لدى غاليري 'آرت أون 56' إعادة اعتبار معمارية إلى بيروت أخرى بعيدة المنال, annahar.com].

Critics read the exhibition as a reflection on the disappearance of Beirut's historic architecture and the transformation of the city's urban identity. L'Orient-Le Jour described Beirut as the central subject of the series, while Annahar, Al-Akhbar, and Al Araby Al Jadeed emphasized architectural memory and the contrast between traditional and contemporary urban development [ref: مرثية لعمارات الزمن الوديع: ديالا خضري... الهمجية الزاحفة على بيروت, الأخبار] [ref: ديالا خضري: شبّاك قديم فتحه الهواء, العربي الجديد] [ref: ديالا خضري.. زوايا بيروت وانفعالاتها البصرية, العربي الجديد].

Le Corbeau et le Regard

In 2023, Khodary presented Le Corbeau et le Regard: Beyrouth en Motifs II (Corbels and Manholes: Beirut in Patterns II), a continuation of her investigation of Beirut's visual identity. The exhibition expanded her architectural vocabulary to include corbels, rooftops, staircases, pavements, drainage systems, and manhole covers. Around the same period, she also developed the Portals series, in which manhole covers became symbolic entrances to hidden layers of the city [ref: ].

Critics discussed the exhibition's relationship between realism and abstraction, as well as its use of overlooked urban details. Al Modon highlighted its elevated viewpoints and absence of human figures, while Al Mayadeen interpreted ordinary architectural objects as central components of Khodary's visual language [ref: Le Corbeau et le Regard by Dyala Khodary: Shades of Hyperrealism] [ref: ديالا الخضري: رحلة عابرة من تراث "الكوربو" إلى واقع "الريغار", شبكة الميادين] [ref: معرض «الغراب والنظرة» مجازية التعبير على طريقة لافونتين, aawsat.com].

Off the Grid / اشتراك

Khodary's fourth solo exhibition, Off the Grid / اشتراك, was presented in 2026. The exhibition focused on Lebanon's electricity crisis and the dense networks of electrical cables associated with privately operated neighborhood generators [ref: ] [ref: ]. Rather than functioning only as documentary representations, the cables became layered visual systems that moved between observation and abstraction. In some works, the cables remained recognizable as parts of the urban landscape. In others, they became lines, knots, grids, and overlapping forms that could be read independently of their original function [ref: معرض «اشتراك»... توصيلات المولّدات الكهربائية ندوب على وجه بيروت, aawsat.com] [ref: ] [ref: غابة الأسلاك والحلول المؤقتة بين الواقعية والتجريد: ديالا خضري... يوميات فوضى اسمها بيروت, الأخبار] [ref: OFF THE GRID by Dyala Khodary on MTV Sar El Wa2et] [ref: ].

L'Orient-Le Jour’s coverage emphasized that the exhibition did not simply document infrastructural failure. Instead, Khodary transformed temporary and improvised electrical arrangements into a visual language through which the city could be interpreted [ref: À Art on 56th, « Off the grid » transforme la crise de l’électricité en œuvre d’art, L'Orient-Le Jour] [ref: Dyala Khodary a transformé les câbles de ces générateurs en matériau artistique.].

Artistic practice

Architecture and infrastructure are central subjects throughout Khodary's recent work. Beginning with recognizable elements of Beirut, she reorganizes buildings, pavements, electrical systems, and urban surfaces through repetition, cropping, patterning, shifts in scale, and unusual viewpoints.

Her background in decorative painting is reflected in her attention to textured, weathered, and repaired surfaces. She primarily uses acrylic paint, while also working with oil paint and epoxy resin. Her choice of supports ranges from canvas and paper to wood and oxidized metal [ref: La liberté guidant l’art, L'Orient-Le Jour] [ref: Dyala Khodary - Works, Art on 56th].

data.title: Dave Kerpen
data.text:
Dave Kerpen is a New York based author and entrepreneur [ref: From Sponsored Wedding to Sponsored Content: How One Man Uses Likability to Get What He Wants, Fast Company] [ref: Dave Kerpen runs for North Hempstead town supervisor, Long Island Press]. Kerpen authored several books including Likeable Social Media (2011), [ref: Likeable Social Media: How to Delight Your Customers, Create an Irresistible Brand, and Be Generally Amazing on Facebook (& Other Social Networks), McGraw Hill Professional] Likeable Business [ref: Likeable Business: Why Today's Consumers Demand More and How Leaders Can Deliver, McGraw Hill Professional] (2012) published by McGraw-Hill. The Art of People (Crown Business) [ref: ] came later in 2016 followed by Get Over Yourself (BenBella Books) in 2024. [ref: Get Over Yourself: How to Lead and Delegate Effectively for More Time, More Freedom, and More Success, BenBella Books] He cofounded a social media company Likeable Media with his wife Carrie that he later sold. Kerpen also appeared on Paradise Hotel on Fox in 2003. [ref: Good Company; When 'Reality' Ends And Reality Begins, The New York Times]

== Early life and education ==
After growing up in Brooklyn in a "typical dysfunctional Jewish" family, he went to Hunter College High School and then to Boston University. Kerpen began working as a vendor at Fenway Park in the summer of 1996, before his junior year at Boston University, and at the FleetCenter that fall, where he sold Crunch 'n Munch on commission. [ref: Vendor tries new song and dance: Concession king lands sales job, Boston Herald] His sales routine of shouting, singing and dancing in the aisles earned him the nickname "the Crunch 'n Munch Guy". [ref: Vendor tries new song and dance: Concession king lands sales job, Boston Herald] Clay Siegert of the Herald wrote in 1998 that the routine had made him "a local celebrity", [ref: Vendor tries new song and dance: Concession king lands sales job, Boston Herald] and Richard C. Whiteley, in his 2001 book Love the Work You're With, wrote that Kerpen had "turned a routine sales job into high-flying, first-class entertainment". [ref: Love the Work You're With, Henry Holt]

After graduating from Boston University, Kerpen worked as a financial counselor at Merrimack Estate and Business Planning Group in North Andover, Massachusetts, while continuing to work as a vendor at night. He had joined the firm as an intern after its managing director saw him vending at a Bruins game in 1996.

== Reality TV and other events ==
In 2003 Kerpen was a contestant on Paradise Hotel, a dating reality show on Fox filmed at a resort in Acapulco. [ref: This Wedding Is Brought to You by..., The New York Times] Andrew Goldman of The New York Times wrote that he "politicked and double-dealt for three months" to reach the last four contestants. Heather Havrilesky of Salon described him as the "smart, regular-looking guy" who became "the driving force" behind a group of contestants known as the Barbies. [ref: Lord of the 'hotel' flies, Salon] In the finale his game partner was given the option of splitting a $250,000 prize with him and kept the full amount, which left him the only finalist without prize money.

Kerpen married Caroline (Carrie) Fisher in July 2006 on the field at KeySpan Park in Brooklyn, after a Brooklyn Cyclones game. [ref: How to Score a Sponsored Wedding, CBS News] [ref: Hoping for extra innings: Couple ties the knot on field after Cyclones game, The Brooklyn Paper] The two had met while working at Radio Disney in Boston, and Kerpen was then an eighth-grade teacher in Queens. Unable to afford the wedding they wanted, they persuaded companies including 1-800-Flowers.com and Entenmann's to cover much of the cost in return for publicity. [ref: James Bernstein column, Newsday] [ref: Marriage Proposal, World News Tonight] The New York Times put the value of the wedding at $100,000, of which the couple paid $25,000, and CBS News reported that they donated $20,000 to the David Wright Foundation. Gersh Kuntzman of The Brooklyn Paper wrote that a sponsor video shown on the stadium screen "did elicit a groan from the sellout crowd".

== Likeable media ==
After their 2006 wedding, Dave and Carrie Kerpen started a company called Likeable Media that operated in the social media and word-of-mouth marketing space. Two of the wedding's sponsors, 1-800-Flowers.com and Entenmann's, became its clients. [ref: 10Pearls Acquires Creative Social Media Agency Likeable, Adweek] It was based in New York City and Kerpen was the chief executive. [ref: A Review of Likeable Social Media: How to Delight Your Customers, Create an Irresistible Brand, and Be Generally Amazing on Facebook (and Other Social Networks), Journal of Applied Communications] The technology company 10Pearls acquired Likeable in 2021.

== Publications and critical reception ==
Kerpen wrote two books under the Likeable name, both published by McGraw-Hill. Likeable Social Media set out 18 concepts for businesses using social media, with case studies of companies applying them. [ref: 2012 Book Review: 'Likeable Social Media' by Dave Kerpen, Oakland University News Archive] Likeable Business set out 11 goals for organizations, among them listening, storytelling, authenticity, transparency, responsiveness and gratefulness. [ref: Do they really like you?, CMA Magazine] He also wrote about eleven principles of what he called likeable leadership.

=== The Art of People ===
Linda White, writing in the Toronto Sun, summarized the 2016 book as 53 "bite-sized skills" in 11 categories. [ref: People Skills Win The Day; Be the person others like, respect and trust, Toronto Sun] A Recruiter.com interview carried by Fox Business gave one of its main ideas as the claim that the people who succeed are those with the best people skills, "not the cutthroat competitive types". [ref: Nice Guys Finish First: Dave Kerpen on the Power of People Skills, Fox Business] Helena Escalante, reviewing it for the New York Public Library's blog, called it "a very easy and enjoyable read" built from stories of Kerpen's life and business career, and wrote that she admired the author. [ref: Book Review: The Art of People by Dave Kerpen, New York Public Library]

=== Get Over Yourself ===
AudioFile magazine, reviewing the audiobook in 2024, said it draws on Kerpen's experience of starting and growing several businesses and argues that leaders should concentrate on the most important matters and delegate the rest. The reviewer described his narration as "spotty" at first, with pauses that made some sentences hard to follow. [ref: Get Over Yourself: How to Lead and Delegate Effectively for More Time, More Freedom, and More Success, AudioFile]

== Politics ==
In 2008 Kerpen, then living in Little Neck, Queens, was a candidate for a New York City Council seat. [ref: Little Neck resident seeks Weprin's seat, TimesLedger Newspapers] He later served on the Port Washington Board of Education. In February 2025 he announced his candidacy as a Democrat for supervisor of the Town of North Hempstead, campaigning on revitalizing downtowns, government efficiency and a more "likable" town government. In the November 2025 election the incumbent, Jennifer DeSena, was re-elected with 55.62 percent of the vote. [ref: DeSena Fends Off Challenge From Kerpen To Remain North Hempstead Supervisor, Patch]

== Personal life ==
As of 2025 Kerpen had lived in Port Washington, New York, for 16 years with his wife, Carrie Kerpen. On 8 July 2026, their 20th wedding anniversary, the couple officiated a vow renewal ceremony for more than a dozen couples at the Brooklyn stadium where they had married. [ref: Through the wins and losses: couples renew vows, wed at Coney Island stadium in tribute to 2006 sponsored wedding, Long Island Press]
