Fakhrian made his senior debut with Aluminium Arak F.C. during the 2022–23 Persian Gulf Pro League season. According to FBref, he made three league appearances for the club. [ref: Mojtaba Fakhrian Stats, Goals, Records, Assists, Cups and more, FBref]

In January 2026, Fakhrian joined Malavan F.C. on loan from Persepolis. Transfermarkt records the loan as beginning on 17 January 2026 and ending on 30 June 2026. [ref: Mojtaba Fakhrian - Player profile 25/26, Transfermarkt]

He made four league appearances and scored one goal for Malavan during the 2025–26 season.

===Gol Gohar===

After returning to Persepolis, Fakhrian joined Gol Gohar on loan for the 2026–27 season. Transfermarkt lists the move as a loan transfer from Persepolis. [ref: Persepolis FC - Transfers 26/27, Transfermarkt]

data.title: Monastery of Saint Petka in Bijeljina
data.text:
The Monastery of Saint Petka is a Serbian Orthodox monastery for women. It is dedicated to Saint Paraskeva of the Balkans and is located near the Pet Jezera urban settlement in Bijeljina, Bosnia and Herzegovina. [ref: „Манастир Свете Петке, Пет Језера у Бијељини“, Namjesništvo bijeljinsko.]

Construction of the monastery began in 2001 during the tenure of Vasilije Kačavenda, Bishop of Zvornik and Tuzla. The monastery is situated at the entrance to Bijeljina from the direction of Sremska Rača. The land on which the monastery was built was donated by the City of Bijeljina. It was consecrated in 2003, while construction of the main building began in 2005. [ref: Mitrić, V. (7 November 2015). „Српски храм као руски“. Večernje novosti.]

The monastery was built of solid brick in a Russian architectural style and consists of two churches. The lower church, located in the crypt, is dedicated to Saint Sergius of Radonezh. Its walls are decorated with depictions of Russian saints, and the crypt contains a reliquary with the relics of Hieromartyr John Knjazev. [ref: „Бијељина: Српски храм као из срца Русије“. Radio-televizija BN, 7 November 2015.]

The upper church is dedicated to Saint Petka and is decorated with Serbian-Byzantine compositions. The monastery has five domes and a roof covered with gold-coloured sheet metal. Its iconostasis is carved from oak. [ref: „Бијељина: Српски храм као из срца Русије“. Radio-televizija BN, 7 November 2015.]

The monastery has been led by Abbess Stefanida (Stević), who has lived there since 2006. Church services are held in the crypt. [ref: „Празнично бденије у манастиру Свете Петке у Бијељини“. Српска православна црква, 28 October 2008.]

An adjacent five-storey building provides accommodation for elderly and infirm people. The building is notable for its ornate appearance and is informally known as "Little Versailles". [ref: „ZLATO, MERMER, KULE I GRADOVI Pogledajte u kakvoj raskoši Kačavenda „okajava” svoje grehe“. Blic, 9 February 2016.]

data.text:
(your article name) is... (description)When the city commission approved the Brentwood Hills Addition plans on June 1, 1953, it created the city of Kansas City, Kansas' first subdivision in Wyandotte County established for African Americans (west of 18th street). The stakeholders formed a Land Investors Group guided by Douglass State Bank.

Dr. Charles.W. Alexander and Dr. William M. Blount, both physicians in KCK; Harold Robbins and Wendell Robbins of Robbins & Robbins Construction Company; Henry W. Sewing, President of Douglass State Bank; Earl D. Thomas, an educator and Principal at Lincoln High School, KCMO;  Isadore Gross, a real estate broker and taxicab company owner in KCMO; Ernest W. Robbins, a retired railway mail clerk;  Atty. Elmer G. Jackson; Mrs. J.A. Hibbler; widow of a physician from KCMO and Rev. Isaiah H. Henderson Sr., pastor of Eighth Street Baptist Church, came together and brought their vision to life.

In total, 54 acres was purchased from Judge Norman B. Sorter. The original boundaries of the subdivision sat between 34th and Farrow and 38th and Farrow to 34th and Bell Crossing and 38th and Oak. It consisted of 143 homes.

According to the April 16, 1954 edition of the KC Call, 1200 people attended the open house. The official dedication was held on the Sunday afternoon of April 11, 1954 in Quindaro Park. Dr. George W. Snowden and William F. McKinney, both federal officials with the Federal Housing Administration, were in attendance.

The neighborhood became a village for the families that lived there. It consisted of doctors, teachers, beauticians and small business owners. It even had its own baseball team, The Quindaro Dragons, with Mr. Harold Rucker, as the coach and a Cub Scout Troop with Mrs. Lorraine Robinson as troop leader.

Missouri submitted Interstate 635 to the American Association of State Highway Officials (AASHO) as part of its proposed Urban Route Numbering on July 31, 1958 and it was approved on November 10, 1958. Construction of I635 began in 1969. Fourteen of the Brentwood Hills homes on 34th Street were acquired which changed the landscape of the subdivision, but not the pride of the people.

data.title: Pidiya (festival)
data.text:
Pidiya is a traditional Hindu festival celebrated in the Bhojpuri region of India and Nepal. [ref: R̥tugīta: svara aura svarūpa, Ayana Prakāśana] [ref: Bihar Ke Paryatan Stahal Aur Sanskritik Dharohar: Demanding Ebook Book, Prabhat Prakashan] It is observed mainly by girls and women for the well-being, longevity and prosperity of their brothers. [ref: भोजपुरी संस्कृति का अनूठा पर्व: पीड़िया धर्म, परंपरा और भाई–बहन के प्रेम का पवित्र संगम - peediya festival celebrating bhojpuri culture brothersister bond, Jagran] [ref: Pañcāmr̥ta: Bhojapurī lekha saṅgraha, Santosha Prinṭarsa] The festival begins around Godhan (Govardhan Puja) and continues for about a month. [ref: Bhojapurī bhāshā kā itihāsa, Loka-Sāhitya-Saṅgama] It involves making pidiya figures from cow dung, creating Pidiya paintings, singing traditional folk songs, listening to ritual stories, fasting and immersing the pidiya in a river, pond, or other water body. [ref: भोजपुरी कहावतें: एक सांस्कृतिक अध्ययन, Vaṇī Prakāśana]

In the Bhojpuri region, Pidiya is traditionally associated with the bond between brothers and sisters and family unity. The observance connects religious practice with traditional family values and customs. Traditionally observed after the paddy harvest, the festival has remained an important part of Bhojpuri cultural traditions, particularly reflecting the affection, respect and close bond shared between sisters and brothers. [ref: Bonded Labour (Kamaiya) in Nepal, Trilij Counselling Centre]

==Name and observance==
Pidiya is also known as Rudravrata. [ref: Trends in Social Science Research, Chitra Srivastava] It is traditionally observed by the Bhojpuriya people during the months of Kartik and Agahan. The observance begins around Godhan (Govardhan Puja) and continues until the second day of the bright fortnight of Agahan.

==Ritual practices==
On Godhan (Govardhan Puja), sisters begin the rituals by making pidiya from the cow dung left after the Godhan ritual and attaching them to the walls of their houses. [ref: Loka sāhitya, Prakāśana Kendra] In some traditions, cow dung from a female calf is also mixed with the cow dung used for making the pidiya. Sisters traditionally make sixteen pidiya for each brother, with the number of sets corresponding to the number of brothers.

The pidiya are removed and made again at different stages of the observance. The first pidiya are removed on Kartik Purnima and another set is made again on the same day. The pidiya are later removed on Agahan Shukla Pratipada, marking the end of the month-long period of their display on the walls. As part of the observance, two ritual stories are traditionally heard: the chhotki katha (small story) from Godhan to Kartik Purnima and the badki katha (long story) from Agahan Krishna Ekam (Pratipada) to Agahan Amavasya. They are narrated by elderly women of the family. The sisters traditionally listen to the stories after completing their daily activities and only then consume food and water. On Agahan Shukla Pratipada, the sisters observe the special Rudravrat Pidiya, a one-day fast associated with the concluding ritual and involving distinct fasting and ritual practices. On this day, both the chhotki katha and badki katha are heard. On Agahan Shukla Dwitiya, the pidiya are taken to a river, pond or other water body and immersed, marking the completion of the ritual cycle. [ref: आज मनाया जाएगा पीड़िया व्रत, जानें इस व्रत का महत्व और विधि- विधान, www.livehindustan.com]

The observance also includes exchanges between brothers and sisters. Sisters may give sweets and gram to their brothers, while brothers may give their sisters money, clothes or ornaments. Sisters also exchange ghee-based sweets and chiura (flattened rice) with one another, a practice known as mutth dalal. [ref: Indian Philosophy & Culture, The Institute]

The sixteen pidiya made for each other are associated with Shodash Maatri puja (worship of sixteen mother goddesses). [ref: Bihar Ke Parva-Tyohar Aur Khanpan: Bestseller Book by Subodh Kumar Nandan: Bihar Ke Parva-Tyohar Aur Khanpan, Prabhat Prakashan] The pidiya are also described as symbolic representations of Lord Shiva, resembling the pind-like form used to represent Lord Shiva in certain Hindu rituals. [ref: पीड़िया के भोजपुरी गीत - कवन फूलवा फूलेला अधि अधि रे रतिया, News18 India]

==Rudravrat Pidiya==
Agahan Shukla Ekam (Pratipada) is the main day of the Pidiya observance and is known as Rudravrat Pidiya. [ref: भाई के लिए बहनों के प्‍यार का त्‍योहार रुद्र व्रत पीड़िया - Know the importance of Rudra vrat pidiya, Jagran] It marks the principal day of the vrat and it's concluding rituals.

On the day before the fast, Agahan Amavasya, the sisters observe Nahay-Khay as a preparatory ritual. [ref: नहाय-खाय के साथ पारंपरिक पीड़िया पर्व की शुरुआत, www.livehindustan.com] On Agahan Shukla Pratipada, the sisters observe a day-long fast. In the morning, they remove the pidiya from the walls and place them in a chhitni (khachiya), a traditional basket. They prepare rasiyav, a sweet preparation made from new rice and jaggery without milk, and decorate their courtyards with traditional chowk-aipan (alpana) designs. After fasting throughout the day, the sisters consume the rasiyav in the evening along with Sorahiya. For each brother, sixteen grains of paddy are taken and peeled by hand using the fingernails to obtain the rice. The rice obtained from these grains is then consumed with the rasiyav, with sixteen grains used for each brother. It is traditionally believed that no sound should be heard while eating, and therefore sisters may put cotton in their ears.

The sisters also apply tilak to their brothers, perform aarti and give them blessings, while the brothers express their commitment to protect and respect their sisters. On the same day, both chhotki katha and badki katha are heard. During the night, the sisters remain awake and sing traditional Pidiya songs.

On Agahan Shukla Dwitiya, the brother carries the khachiya on his head to a river, pond, or other water body, where the pidiya are immersed. The sisters accompany him while singing traditional Pidiya songs. [ref: Lokagītoṃ ke sandarbha aura āyāma, Viśvavidyālya Prakāśana] After the immersion, the girls exchange chiura and sweets with one another, and then perform paran to break their fast.

==Pidiya painting==
Pidiya painting is an ancient and traditional style of Bhojpuri folk painting associated with the Pidiya festival in the wider Bhojpuri region, including Purvanchal. [ref: 2026-27 Bihar STET Class IX-X Fine Art Solved Papers & Practice Book 216 395. This book contains 16 sets of the previous solved papers and practice book., Youth Competition Times] [ref: बिहार: कोरोनाकाल में भोजपुरी चित्रशैली को मिल रही नयी पहचान, मास्क पर बन रहे पेंटिंग ने खोला नया बाजार Bhojpuri painting style getting New identity in Corona period opened new market brvj, News18 India] The practice of making these paintings is known as Pidiya lekhan. Traditionally, Pidiya paintings are made using cow dung, clay, sem leaves, rice paste, plant-based colours and other natural materials. [ref: नई दिल्ली से दुनिया तक पहुंची पीड़िया कला; GI टैग से मिला नया सम्मान, भोजपुरी संस्कृति की बड़ी उपलब्धि - peedia painting gets gi tag global recognition for bhojpuri art, Jagran]

The walls are first prepared with a coating of cow dung and clay. After the surface dries, a green colour made by grinding sem leaves is applied as a base, followed by white designs made with rice paste. The designs are drawn using the fingers, rengni thorns (tungal) and traditional painting brushes known as koonchi. The painting features motifs such as the sun, moon, palanquins, bearers, birds, fruits, flowers, trees, and human figures, reflecting elements of local culture, nature and everyday life. Sisters traditionally create the paintings while singing Pidiya folk songs.

In 2026, the Pidiya painting was registered as a geographical indication (GI) handicraft, giving the traditional art form of the Bhojpuri region formal recognition under India's geographical indications system. [ref: Bawan Buti Sari, Pattharkatti StoneCraft & Pidhiya Painting get GI tag, The Times of India]

== Pidiya songs ==
The Pidiya observance includes traditional Pidiya songs (Pidiya Geet), which form part of the broader tradition of Bhojpuri music. These traditional Bhojpuri folk songs are sung by women and girls while making, removing and immersing the pidiya, as well as during night-time vigils throughout the observance. The songs express themes of brother-sister affection, family well-being and wishes for prosperity.

=== Songs sung while making the pidiya ===
Pidiya songs while making and placing the pidiya reflect the colour of folk life and everyday struggles, while expressing affection and concern for brothers.

Sample song:

कवन बहिना जागसु भिनुसार ए हरि
पूरूब जइहऽ भइया पछिम जइहऽ
ले अइहऽ ए भइया टिकरी मिठइया
नइखे मिलत ए बहिनि टिकरी मिठइया
पुरूब गइनी बहिनि पछिम गइनीं
जनि भूखऽ ए बहिनि पीड़िया बरतिया
कइसे छोड़िं भइया तोहरे बरतिया
मंगिया के जुड़ हउए, कोखि के जियछिया
ई तऽ हउए तहरो बरहिया

English translation:

Which sister wakes before dawn, O Hari?
Go east, brother, then go west,
Bring me some tikri sweets, O brother.
Sister, tikri sweets cannot be found.
I went east, sister, and I went west.
Do not go hungry, sister, for the Pidiya fast.
How can I give up the fast, brother? I am observing it for you.
Through this fast, a married woman's sindoor remains auspicious and her womb remains fruitful.
This observance is for you too.

=== Songs sung while removing the pidiya ===
Songs are also sung while the pidiya are being removed from the walls. Their themes vary; one such song describes the emotions of a married sister who is called back to her in-laws around the time of the pidiya removal.

Sample song:

लावे के त लवनी पीड़ियावा
राम छोड़ावहिं के बेरिया
असकहिं ससुर अकुतइल हो
राम छोड़ावहिं के बेरिया
भेजि दिहलन एकम दूजि दिनवा हो
राम छोड़ावहिं के बेरिया
असकहिं अकुतइल हो राम
छोड़ावहिं के बेरिया

English translation:

I have made the pidiya; now comes the time to remove them.
The in-laws grow restless and call me back.
O Ram, it is time to remove the pidiya.
On Ekam and Dooj, they send me back to my in-laws.
O Ram, it is time to remove the pidiya.
Restless hearts stir, O Ram,
for it is time to remove the pidiya.

=== Songs sung during the Rudravrat Pidiya night vigil ===

On the night of Rudravrat Pidiya, the fasting sisters stay awake throughout the night, singing Pidiya songs that express their affection for their brothers, their wishes for their well-being, and their anticipation of the morning immersion.

Sample song:

सांझ के पहरा, सुरूज जाले बहरा
उगहु ए सुरूज, बारब दियरा
उगे के त उगबो फलाना भइया के अंगना
सांझ के पहरा, सुरूज जाले बहरा

English translation:

As evening falls, the sun sets away,
Rise, O Sun, and I shall light the lamp.
When you rise, may you shine upon my brother’s courtyard,
As evening falls, the sun sets away.

=== Songs sung during the immersion of the pidiya ===

During the immersion of the pidiya, the brothers walk ahead carrying the daura, followed by the fasting sisters who sing songs along the way. These songs also express the emotional bond between brothers and sisters.

Sample song:

नदिया किनारे धोबिया लुगा धोवे जालें
मलहवा नइया खेवलें
से केकरि बहिनिया दहल जाली ए हरि
रोवेलन फलाना भइया मुख धरि गमछिया
से हमरी बहिनिया दहल जाली ए हरि
हंसेलन फलाना जीजा मुख धरि गमछिया
से फलाना के बहिनिया दहल जाली ए हरि

English translation:

By the riverside, the washerman goes to wash his clothes,
The boatman rows his boat along.
Whose sister is drifting away, O Hari?
So-and-so Bhaiya weeps, his face covered with a cloth.
My sister is drifting away, O Hari.
So-and-so Jija smiles, his face covered with a cloth.
The sister of so-and-so is drifting away, O Hari.

== Ritual Stories ==
The Pidiya observance includes two traditional ritual stories, known as the Chhotki Katha (small story) and the Badki Katha (long story). The stories are traditionally narrated in the Bhojpuri language by elderly women of the family. Sisters traditionally listen to the stories as part of the observance and do not eat or drink until the day's story has been heard.

===Chhotki katha===
The Chhotki Katha is traditionally heard from the day of Godhan until Kartik Purnima.

The story concerns two friends. One is the daughter of a bhant, while the other is the daughter of a king, or a princess. The story begins with this introduction. In the story, the princess eats something before listening to the katha each day, whereas the bhant's daughter listens to it every day. As a result, the bhant's daughter's brother faces no danger, while the princess's brother comes under threat. In the end, when the princess also begins listening to the katha, the danger threatening her brother is averted.

===Badki katha===
The Badki Katha is traditionally heard from Agahan Krishna Ekam until Agahan Amavasya.

It also tells the story of two friends, one a queen and the other a maidservant. In the story, the queen’s children die, while the maidservant’s children remain alive. The queen eats before listening to the katha, whereas the maidservant listens to it before beginning her daily work. The story thus associates listening to the katha and having faith in it with the well-being of one’s children and brothers and with prosperity.

data.title: Priyalal Sirisena
data.text:
Priyalal Sirisena (born 25 May 1979) is a Sri Lankan attorney-at-law and author who practices constitutional law and fundamental rights litigation in Sri Lanka. [ref: Lawyer sues cops for stifling his professional rights, Daily Mirror] In addition to his legal practice, he is a novelist whose literary work was shortlisted for the Swarna Pusthaka Awards. [ref: Swarna Pusthaka Awards 2025: Shortlisted Novels Announced, The Island]

== Early life and education ==
Sirisena was born in Kurunegala, Sri Lanka. He studied law at the University of Colombo, graduating with a Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.) in 2004, and was subsequently admitted to the bar as an Attorney-at-Law of the Supreme Court of Sri Lanka. He later completed a Master of Laws (LL.M.) at the same university.

== Legal career and human rights petitions ==
Sirisena has been involved in constitutional law and human rights cases in Sri Lanka. In June 2018, he filed a Fundamental Rights petition in the Supreme Court of Sri Lanka against senior police officers, alleging interference with his professional duties and rights as a legal counsel.

In May 2023, Sirisena filed formal complaints regarding intimidation and threats related to his ongoing legal proceedings in Kurunegala, which received coverage in national print media. [ref: 'Withdraw case or face the consequences': Lawyer files complaint, The Island] He has also represented clients in public interest litigations concerning administrative oversight and police accountability.

== Literary career ==
Sirisena is also active in Sinhala literature. He authored the Sinhala novel Deyyange Atha (The Elephant of the Gods). In 2025, the novel gained critical recognition and was selected among the shortlisted nominees for the prestigious Swarna Pusthaka Awards, one of Sri Lanka's primary literary honors for novel writing. [ref: Contemporary Sinhala Literature and the Swarna Pusthaka Nominees, Ceylon Today]

data.title: Regalias Digitales
data.text:
----

Regalias Digitales LLC is a Bay Area-based independent music publishing administration and royalty collection company founded in 2014. The company provides royalty collection, publishing administration, and rights management services for songwriters, recording artists, producers, and music publishers. [ref: Josh Norek Is on a Mission to Help Musicians, Hispanic Executive] Regalias Digitales was the leading representative of artist and songwriter victims whose royalties were stolen in the $23 million Mediamuv scandal. [ref: YouTube Thieves Ordered to Pay $3M of Stolen Royalties Back to Bad Bunny, Julio Iglesias & Other Latin Musicians, Billboard]

Regalias Digitales was founded by music executive Josh Arón Norek, a former vice president of Nacional Records, co-founder of the Latin Alternative Music Conference (LAMC), [ref: Latin Alternative Music's Movers and Shakers Meet, The New York Times] and co-host of the syndicated public radio program The Latin Alternative. [ref: Josh Norek shines a light on alternative Latino music, Times Union] Although Regalias Digitales initially focused on representing Latin music creators and rights holders, the company subsequently expanded its roster to include artists and publishers across multiple musical genres.

Regalias Digitales' music publishing clients include hip-hop artists like Big Boi (Outkast), Lloyd Banks, Lil Gnar, OMB Peezy, Eric Bobo (Cypress Hill, Beastie Boys) [ref: Publishing Briefs: Reservoir Makes a 'Key' Move in Egypt, Plus Concord Signs Wyoming Rapper, Billboard] and SOB x RBE; rock acts like Primus, Ween, The Warning [ref: Publishing Briefs: Foreigner's Mick Jones Signs to WCM, Barry Weiss Announces Bossy Songs, Billboard] and The Used; Latin artists such as Daddy Yankee, Los Tigres del Norte, Los Tucanes de Tijuana, Grupo Codiciado, Canserbero [ref: Publishing Briefs: Kacey Musgraves On Another 'Merry Go 'Round' With Warner Chappell, Billboard]); EDM acts Said The Sky and Bonnie X Clyde; and the publishing catalogs of Regional Mexican labels like Afinarte. Regalias Digitales also represents reggae acts SOJA, Stick Figure, Collie Buddz, Steel Pulse, Tribal Seeds and Mo'Kalamity [ref: Publishing Briefs: UMPG Signs 'Poor Things' Composer Jerskin Fendrix, Billboard]; and popular Caribbean / dancehall artists such as KES The Band, Machel Montano, Travis World and Destra.

Norek's ties with the Argentine music industry date back to the 1990's, [ref: Josh Norek Is on a Mission to Help Musicians, Hispanic Executive] and the company represents the heirs of many of the country's most iconic tango, rock and folkloric artists including Astor Piazzolla, Soda Stereo, Carlos Gardel and Mercedes Sosa.

In recent years Regalias Digitales has acquired the music publishing catalogs of several artists, including Likybo, Juan Gotti, J Swey, Bill $aber, Beeda Weeda, producer Branden Cox (Icewear Vezzo, Young Thug) and Swifty Blue. [ref: Publishing Briefs: Laufey Renews Deal With Warner Chappell Music, Plus Claudia Brant & More, Billboard]

data.title: Camerun Pippin
data.text:
Camerun L. Pippin is an American former police officer and firefighter from Summerville, South Carolina. He served with the law enforcement and fire services for nearly sixteen years, rising to the rank of sergeant with the Summerville Police Department, where he was named Officer of the Year in 2016. He has been profiled in local newspaper features covering his public service career.

== Early life and public service beginnings ==
Pippin began his path in public service as a teenager with the Summerville Police Explorer Post #751, where he eventually served as Cadet Chief. [ref: Citizens learn more about use of force, The Summerville Journal Scene] At age 17, he became a volunteer firefighter with the Pine Ridge Fire Department, and at 18 he was hired full-time with the Summerville Fire Department. [ref: 'I prefer being on the streets': Meet Summerville officer Camerun Pippin, The Summerville Journal Scene]

== Law enforcement career ==
Pippin joined the Summerville Police Department as a street patrol officer after turning 21. He later became a certified drug interdiction officer, one of two with the department. In 2016, he was named the Summerville Police Department's Officer of the Year. He was promoted to the rank of sergeant in April 2018. [ref: Summerville Police Department, Facebook]

In total, Pippin served nearly sixteen years across law enforcement and firefighting.

== Later activities ==
Pippin is the author of The Momentum Method, a self-published motivational book available on Amazon Kindle. data.title: ChessMoon
data.text:
Chess Moon is an online chess platform offering live multiplayer chess games, variant game modes, interactive instructional lessons, tactics training, and organized team leagues. [ref: Linksammlung: Online-Schach, Deutscher Schachbund] [ref: Cờ Vua Online, Cờ Vua Cao Cấp] [ref: Kendinizi test edin - 2 (1200 - 1700), Satranç Okulu] [ref: Chess Moon, Satranc.net] [ref: Online Chess Links Directory, ChessStar] The platform provides browser-based access for casual and competitive players, along with social features and post-game engine analysis.

== Features ==
Chess Moon provides various modes and tools for online play, learning, and community engagement:

* Lessons & Training: Features live interactive instruction where chess coaches and instructors can teach multiple students simultaneously on an interactive chessboard. Lessons feature real-time move demonstration, step-by-step replays, and integrated chat.
* Puzzles: Interactive tactics training featuring four distinct puzzle modes: Classic, Streak (where a run ends on the first incorrect move), Storm (a timed 3-minute challenge), and a unified Daily Puzzle. Puzzles are user-submitted, undergo community review, and are published to the global puzzle database.
* Live Matchmaking: Real-time chess games with configurable time controls (bullet, blitz, rapid) and premove support.
* Chess Variants: Support for non-standard variants including Crazyhouse, Three-Check, Chess960, and custom thematic starting positions.
* Tournaments: Automated round-robin and Swiss-system tournament engines featuring dedicated event pages, standings, crosstables, and PGN archives.
* Team Leagues: Structured team competitions designed around over-the-board (OTB) club league formats. Teams progress through seasonal divisions with head-to-head board-matching across 2 to 20 boards per match.
* Game Analysis & Archives: Post-game engine evaluations detailing move accuracy percentages, blunder tracking, live evaluation graphs, and full historical game archives.
* Social Features: Personal and team activity feeds ("The Wall") for posting chess games, images, and videos, alongside direct messaging and friend lists.

== Technology ==
Chess Moon operates on a WebSocket web architecture for real-time game state synchronization and low-latency move transmission. It includes server-side network lag compensation (Timeseal) and compatibility with desktop chess interfaces via the XFCC protocol.

data.title: Supratit Banerjee
data.text:
----

Supratit Banerjee (born 23 February 2014) is an English chess player who holds the title of International Master (IM). He represented Scotland in international competition until February 2024, when he transferred to England.

In August 2026, at the age of 12, Banerjee completed his third IM norm and met the accompanying rating requirement, making him the youngest International Master in the United Kingdom. [ref: Chess prodigy Supratit Banerjee becomes Britain's youngest-ever International Master, ChessBase India] [ref: Genius Sutton boy, 12, becomes youngest Brit to get chess master title despite 'limited coaching', MyLondon]

== Early life and chess career ==
Banerjee began playing chess in Scotland in 2020, at the age of six, and continued with online chess lessons and inter-club matches. [ref: Supratit Banerjee, ChessKid] His first international tournament was the 2021 European Youth Chess Championship, where he represented Scotland in the Under-8 category. [ref: European Youth Chess Championship 2021 – Open 08, Chess-Results.com]

At the 2022 British Under-8 Championship, Banerjee won the title with a score of 6/7. [ref: Prizewinners' list 2022, British Chess Championships] Later that year, he also won the Under-8 section of the Delancey UK Schools' Chess Challenge Terafinal, scoring 10/11 to take first place on tiebreak. [ref: Terafinal 2022, Delancey UK Schools' Chess Challenge]

In 2023, Banerjee was named Chess Maestro at the BYITC Inspire Awards, recognising his early chess achievements. [ref: Sport Category Winners of BYITC Inspire Award 2023, British Youth International College] [ref: Edinburgh youngsters honoured at Holyrood in inaugural Inspire Awards, The NEN – North Edinburgh News] He was part of the Scotland team that won the Glorney Cup in 2023, the country's first victory in the event in 58 years. [ref: Scotland Win Glorney Cup, Chess Scotland] He was awarded the Candidate Master (CM) title that year. [ref: A New Titled Player – Supratit Banerjee, Chess Scotland]

Banerjee transferred his FIDE federation from Scotland to England in February 2024. [ref: FIDE federation transfer list 2024, FIDE] He played club chess for Coulsdon Chess Academy before joining Kingston Chess Club. [ref: David Maycock (Kingston) v Supratit Banerjee (Coulsdon), Kingston Chess Club] [ref: Supratit Banerjee v Simon Williams, Kingston Chess Club] In October 2024, he won the Under-10 section of the Delancey UK Schools' Chess Challenge Terafinal, scoring 9.5/11. [ref: 2024 Results, Delancey UK Schools' Chess Challenge] He plays for CSC/Kingston, the club's combined team in the 4NCL, and was a member of the squad promoted to the league's first division for the 2024–25 season. A review of that season named him the team's most valuable contributor. [ref: Measuring how individuals contribute to a team, Kingston Chess Club]

Banerjee received the FIDE Master (FM) title in 2025, at the age of 11. [ref: Banerjee, Supratit – FIDE Chess Profile, FIDE]

At the 2025 UK Chess Blitz Championship final, Banerjee qualified through a regional heat and finished eighth out of 16 players, in a field that included grandmasters, international masters and FIDE masters. [ref: Year 7 Student Shines at UK Chess Blitz Final, Sutton Grammar School]

At the 2026 British Rapid Championship in March, he finished joint third on points. [ref: Outstanding chess success for Supratit, Sutton Grammar School] Following his results in 4NCL matches, he was featured in a Financial Times article by Leonard Barden.

In 2026, he was invited through the English Chess Federation to training camps run by the Kasparov Chess Foundation in Munich and Zagreb, where he met Garry Kasparov. He also defeated Grandmaster Artem Uskov at the Menorca Chess Open. [ref: Supratit Banerjee: UK's Youngest International Master at 12, The Global Indian]

== International Master title ==
Banerjee earned his three IM norms between 2025 and 2026. The first came at the 2025 British Chess Championship in Liverpool, at the age of 11, where he scored 6/9. [ref: Supratit Banerjee Becomes UK's Youngest International Master at 12, ChessEver] [ref: 2025 Prizewinners, British Chess Championships] [ref: Michael Adams wins his ninth British Chess Championship; Yao and Mirzoeva tie for Women's title, FIDE] The second came in July 2026 at an IM norm tournament in Sheffield, where he scored 6.5/9 and finished joint first. [ref: Supratit Continues Remarkable Rise, Sutton Grammar School] The third came at the 2026 British Chess Championship in Coventry, where he scored 6/9 with a performance rating of 2503. Two days later, at the Stockholm GM Norm Invitation in Sweden, he crossed the 2400 FIDE rating threshold required for the title. [ref: Shreyas Royal, 17, is youngest ever British chess champion as new generation takes over, AOL]

== ChessKid Under-13 Youth Championship ==
In February 2026, Banerjee won the Under-13 section of the ChessKid Youth Championship, winning the final 3.5–1.5 a day before his 12th birthday. [ref: Supratit Banerjee Stops Bodhana Sivanandan To Win ChessKid U13 Youth Championship, Chess.com]

== Personal life ==
Banerjee was born in Ranchi, India. The family moved to London in 2015, to Glasgow in 2017, and back to London in 2022. He is a pupil at Sutton Grammar School in Sutton, London.

data.title: Subuola Fasoyiro
data.text:
Subuola Fasoyiro is a Nigerian food scientist and academic. She is a professor of Food Science and Technology and a researcher at the Institute of Agricultural Research and Training (IAR&T), affiliated with Obafemi Awolowo University, Ibadan. [ref: Subuola Bosede Fasoyiro - About me, OWSD] [ref: Professor Subuola Fasoyiro, Bowen University] [ref: Prof. Subuola Bosede Fasoyiro, Institute of Agricultural Research and Training] Her work focuses on food processing, food safety, nutrition quality, product development, food preservation, and the utilization of underutilized legumes for food security.

== Early life and education ==

Subuola Fasoyiro was born on August 1, 1971, in Lagos State, Nigeria. She studied Food Science and Technology at the Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta, where she obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in 1994. [ref: Why I chose career path in Food Science and Technology: Prof. Subuola Fasoyiro reflects on academic journey, The Nation] She later earned a Master of Science degree in Food Technology in 1997 and a Doctor of Philosophy degree in Food Technology in 2004 from the University of Ibadan.

[ref: FUNAAB Matriculates 6,356 Students, Highest intake in 4 decades, The Whistler]

== Career ==

Fasoyiro began research work at the Institute of Agricultural Research and Training (IAR&T) in 1998. She became a professor in 2014. She has also served as a professor in the Food Science and Technology Programme of Bowen University. Her academic and research work has been associated with food processing, product development, food preservation, food safety, and nutrition quality for food and nutrition security.

At IAR&T, her work has included research and extension activities in food processing technologies, value addition to agricultural produce, and training in food safety and processing for rural communities and extension personnel.

== Research ==

Fasoyiro's research interests include food processing, food preservation, food safety, food and nutrition quality, and food product development for food security. Specific areas of focus in her work include the processing and utilization of underutilized legumes, the nutritional improvement of indigenous staple crops through value addition, and the development of low-cost food technologies and natural food preservatives.

Her research, academic work and community service led to the delivery of the 372nd inaugural lecture at Obafemi Awolowo University in 2023. [ref: Hidden Treasures in Plants: For Food Security, Healthy and Wealthy Life, Obafemi Awolowo University Institutional Repository]

== Lectures ==

=== 372nd inaugural lecture of Obafemi Awolowo University ===

On 13 June 2023, Fasoyiro delivered the 372nd inaugural lecture of Obafemi Awolowo University, titled The Hidden Treasures in Plants: For Food Security, Healthy and Wealthy Life.

In the lecture, she discussed the role of food processing, value addition, and the use of underutilized plant resources in addressing hunger, malnutrition, and food insecurity. The lecture was reported by CEOAfrica, Independent and Nigerian Tribune. [ref: Prof. Subuola Fasoyiro is set to deliver 372nd Inauguration Lecture in OAU, CEOAfrica] [ref: OAU 372nd Inaugural Lecture: Prof Fasoyiro advocates for food security, healthy and wealthy life, CEOAfrica] [ref: Expert shares discoveries on reducing hunger, increasing food processing, Independent Newspaper Nigeria] [ref: How Nigeria can achieve sustainable food security by 2030 - Prof Fasoyiro, Tribune Online]

=== 13th commencement lecture, Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta ===

On 19 November 2025, Fasoyiro delivered the 13th commencement lecture of the Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta during the institution's 2025/2026 matriculation ceremony. [ref: FUNAAB’s 2025/2026 Matriculation Ceremony: Prof. Fasoyiro to Deliver 13th Commencement Lecture, Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta] The lecture was titled Future Leaders of Character in Agriculture: Building Capacity Today for National and Global Impact Tomorrow. [ref: Future Leaders of Character in Agriculture: Building Capacity Today for National and Global Impact Tomorrow, ResearchGate] The event was also reported by The Whistler. [ref: FUNAAB Matriculates 6,356 Students, Highest intake in 4 decades, The Whistler]

== Community and institutional service ==

Fasoyiro has been involved in extension and community-based food technology work through IAR&T. Her institutional service has included technology transfer to adopted villages, training of extension agents and food vendors on food safety practices, and training of unemployed youth and processors in pigeon pea, soybean, cassava, and roselle processing technologies. She also mentors early career researchers.

She is the co-founder and vice-chairperson of Grace Reachfill Development Foundation (GRDF), an organization involved in education and empowerment initiatives for girls, youth and women. [ref: Prof Subuola Fasoyiro, Grace Reachfill Development Foundation]

== Honours and fellowships ==

Fasoyiro has received fellowships and professional development opportunities including the Netherlands Fellowship Programme, the African Nutrition Leadership Programme, the Norman Borlaug Women in Science programme, and the Schlumberger Foundation Faculty for the Future programme. She has also been associated with the African Women in Agricultural Research and Development (AWARD) programme as a fellow and mentor. [ref: Subuola Fasoyiro, African Women in Agricultural Research and Development (AWARD)]

She was listed among fellows inducted by the Centre for Public Service Productivity and Development (CeProd). [ref: CeProd Inducts 23 New Members, Charges Professionals on Smart Productivity for Income Growth, Centre for Public Service Productivity and Development]

Honors associated with Fasoyiro include Gamma Delta Membership in 2015, a Best Paper Award at ICPP in 2018, an Award of Excellence by NIEEE in 2021, the Jericho Business Panelist Award in 2023, the FUNAAB Alumni Humanitarian Award in 2024, and the FUNAAB Award of Honour in 2025. [ref: Hidden Treasures in Plants: for Food Security, Healthy and Wealthy Life. OAU 372nd Inaugural Lecture Series, ResearchGate]

== Grants ==

Fasoyiro has received research support and grants associated with organizations including the International Foundation for Science and the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA).

== Selected works ==

* Fasoyiro, S. B. (2023). The Hidden Treasures in Plants: for Food Security, Healthy and Wealthy Life. 372nd Inaugural Lecture, Obafemi Awolowo University. [ref: The Hidden Treasures in Plants: for Food Security, Healthy and Wealthy Life, Obafemi Awolowo University Institutional Repository]

* Fasoyiro, S. B. (2025). Future Leaders of Character in Agriculture: Building Capacity Today for National and Global Impact Tomorrow. 13th Matriculation Commencement Lecture, Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta.

* Fasoyiro, S. B., Hovingh, R., Gourama, H. G. and Cutter, C. N. (2020). "Influence of Seed: Water Ratio and Shredding Time on Dehulling Process of Pigeon Pea". Journal of Food Science and Nutrition, 6: 083. DOI: [https://doi.org/10.24966/FSN-1076/100083 10.24966/FSN-1076/100083]. [ref: Influence of Seed: Water Ratio and Shredding Time on Dehulling Process of Pigeon Pea, HSOA Journal of Food Science and Nutrition]

* Fasoyiro, S. B., Farinde, E. O., Arowora, K. A., Ajani, A. O., Adeola, A., Olanipekun, O. T., Ejigbo, E., Oyedokun, M. O., Adebayo, A. K. and Ashaye, O. A. (2019). Pigeon Pea Utilization: A Recipe Book (for Home Use and Cottage Industries). IAR&T Publication Unit, Ibadan, Oyo State, Nigeria. 71 pp. ISBN 978-978-50216-6-0. [ref: Pigeon pea Utilization: A Recipe Book (for home use and cottage industries), ResearchGate]

* Fasoyiro, S. B., Gourama, H. and Cutter, C. N. (2017). "Stability and Safety of Maize–Legume-Fortified Flours Stored in Various Packaging Materials". European Food Research and Technology, 243(10): 1861–1868. DOI: [https://doi.org/10.1007/s00217-017-2892-4 10.1007/s00217-017-2892-4]. [ref: Stability and safety of maize–legume-fortified flours stored in various packaging materials, Penn State]

* Fasoyiro, S. B., Arowora, K. A. and Ajani, A. O. (2017). "Storage and Sensory Qualities of Extrudate-Like Maize–Pigeon Pea Snacks Processed by Low-Cost Technology". Journal of Food Processing and Preservation, 41(4): e13000. DOI: [https://doi.org/10.1111/jfpp.13000 10.1111/jfpp.13000]. [ref: Storage and Sensory Qualities of Extrudate-Like Maize–Pigeon Pea Snacks Processed by Low-Cost Technology, Wiley Online Library]

* Fasoyiro, S. B., Hovingh, R., Gourama, H. and Cutter, C. (2016). "Change in Water Activity and Fungal Counts of Maize-Pigeon Pea Flour During Storage Utilizing Various Packaging Materials". Procedia Engineering, 159: 72–76. DOI: [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.proeng.2016.08.066 10.1016/j.proeng.2016.08.066]. [ref: Change in water activity and fungal counts of maize-pigeon pea flour during storage utilizing various packaging materials, Penn State]

* Fasoyiro, S. B., Obatolu, V. A., Ashaye, O. A. and Lawal, B. O. (2010). "Knowledge Assessment, Improved Storage Techniques, and Training of Local Processors and Vendors of Soy Products on Food Safety Practices in South West Nigeria". Journal of Agricultural & Food Information, 11(4): 340–350. DOI: [https://doi.org/10.1080/10496505.2010.512855 10.1080/10496505.2010.512855]. [ref: Knowledge Assessment, Improved Storage Techniques, and Training of Local Processors and Vendors of Soy Products on Food Safety Practices in South West Nigeria, Taylor & Francis]

data.title: Kochchikade
data.text:
Kochchikade (; also spelled Kochchikada) is a town and locality in Negombo Divisional Secretariat, Gampaha District, Western Province, Sri Lanka.

Kochchikade is situated north of Negombo and forms part of an important road and railway corridor between the Colombo metropolitan area and north-western Sri Lanka. The locality is associated with the Colombo–Puttalam road, the Puttalam railway line, the Kochchikade railway station, and the Maha Oya bridge. [ref: [https://www.railway.gov.lk/web/index.php?Itemid=191&id=165&lang=en&option=com_content&view=article Sri Lanka Railways — Station Details]] [ref: [https://www.sundaytimes.lk/190324/news/pm-opens-new-maha-oya-bridge-342340.html The Sunday Times — PM opens new Maha Oya bridge]]

The official administrative code for Kochchikade is 1203015, and it is identified as Grama Niladhari Division 78 under the Negombo Divisional Secretariat and Negombo Municipal Council. [ref: [https://www.statistics.gov.lk/qlink/AdminDivCodes Department of Census and Statistics — Administrative Division Codes]]

The 2024 Census of Population and Housing recorded a population of 2,499 for Kochchikade GN Division, comprising 1,206 males and 1,293 females.

The locality should be distinguished from Kochchikade North and Kochchikade South in the Colombo municipal area, which have the same name but are separate localities.

== Name ==

The Sinhala name of the locality is කොච්චිකඩේ.

The English spelling Kochchikade is used in official administrative, railway, postal and municipal records. The alternative spelling Kochchikada also occurs in English-language material.

The locality has postal code 11540. [ref: [https://www.slpost.gov.lk/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/POST-CODE-BOOK-.pdf Sri Lanka Post — Post Code Directory]]

== Administrative status ==

Kochchikade is GN Division No. 78 within the Negombo Divisional Secretariat of Gampaha District.

The Department of Census and Statistics assigns Kochchikade the administrative code 1203015 and places it under Negombo DS Division and Negombo Municipal Council.

The 2012 Gampaha District GN atlas also lists Kochchikade as GN Division 78 of Negombo DS Division. [ref: [https://www.statistics.gov.lk/Resource/en/Population/DistrictAtlases/DCS_Population_Atlas_2012_D12_GampahaDistrict.pdf Department of Census and Statistics — Grama Niladhari Level Population Atlas of Gampaha District, 2012]]

== Negombo Municipal Council ==

Kochchikade is within the administrative area of Negombo Municipal Council.

The municipal council operates a Kochchikade Sub-Office as one of its two sub-offices. The council lists an officer-in-charge and identifies the Kochchikade sub-office as part of its local administrative service network. [ref: [https://www.negombo.mc.gov.lk/?lang=en&page_id=5540 Negombo Municipal Council — Sub-Offices]]

The council's published contact information lists the Kochchikade Sub-Office telephone number as 031-2277276. [ref: [https://www.negombo.mc.gov.lk/?lang=en&page_id=1643 Negombo Municipal Council — Contact Us]]

The council also lists a Kochchikade Ayurveda dispensary within its municipal health-service network.

== Population ==

The 2024 GN-level census records a population of 2,499 for Kochchikade GN Division 78.

The figures apply specifically to GN Division 78 and do not represent the combined population of the wider Kochchikade area, including Pallansena, Thoppuwa, Manaveriya, Welihena and other neighbouring settlements.

For comparison, the 2012 GN population atlas recorded 2,777 people in Kochchikade GN Division 78.

== Location and geography ==

Kochchikade is situated at approximately, at an elevation of about 12 metres above sea level. [ref: [https://www.geonames.org/1239882/kochchikade.html GeoNames — Kochchikade]]

The locality lies north of Negombo and close to the lower reaches of the Maha Oya. Its landscape contains a mixture of built-up areas, residential neighbourhoods, roads, small agricultural plots, waterways and areas connected with the coastal economy.

The locality is also close to the transition between the urbanised Negombo coastal belt and the more rural areas of Katana.

== Nearby localities ==

Places associated with the wider Kochchikade area include:

* Negombo
* Pallansena
* Palangathure
* Poruthota
* Duwana
* Manaveriya
* Udangawa
* Thoppuwa
* Bambukuliya
* Muruthana
* Welihena
* Ethgala
* Mahaththogala
* Adikkandiya
* Katana
* Dankotuwa
* Waikkala

Not all of these places form part of Kochchikade GN Division 78. Several are separate GN divisions, and some are administered by Katana Divisional Secretariat. [ref: [https://www.statistics.gov.lk/Resource/en/Population/DistrictAtlases/DCS_Population_Atlas_2012_D12_GampahaDistrict.pdf Department of Census and Statistics — Gampaha District Population Atlas]]

== Relationship with Negombo ==

Negombo is the principal city and service centre associated with Kochchikade.

Kochchikade lies north of the main Negombo urban area and is connected to the city by road and railway.

Negombo provides major commercial, health, education, government, tourism and transport services for the surrounding coastal and inland communities.

Main article: Negombo

== Relationship with Pallansena ==

Pallansena is one of the principal settlements immediately associated with Kochchikade.

DCS administrative data identify Pallansena North as GN Division 77 and Pallansena South as GN Division 76, both under Negombo DS Division and Negombo Municipal Council.

Pallansena is connected to Kochchikade through roads, schools, churches, commercial activity and residential development.

Main article: Pallansena

== Palangathure ==

Palangathure is a coastal locality within the Negombo municipal area and is closely associated with Kochchikade in addresses and local commercial use.

DCS data identify Palangathure as GN Division 75A under Negombo DS Division and Negombo Municipal Council.

The locality is part of the wider Negombo beach and tourism landscape.

Sri Lankan excise licensing records have included tourism businesses and hotels using addresses such as Palangathure, Kochchikade, Negombo. [ref: [https://excise.gov.lk/images/license/englishall.pdf Sri Lanka Excise Department — Licensed Establishments]]

== Poruthota ==

Poruthota is a coastal locality associated with the northern Negombo tourism belt.

The area contains hotels, restaurants, guesthouses and other tourism-related businesses and is connected with Kochchikade and Negombo by the coastal road network.

The proximity of Poruthota and Palangathure to Kochchikade gives the locality a role as a transport gateway to northern Negombo's coastal tourism area.

== Duwana ==

Duwana is a settlement in the wider Kochchikade–Pallansena area.

The Ministry of Education lists Duwana Sinhala Mixed Vidyalaya within the Negombo education network. [ref: [https://moe.gov.lk/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/01i-2024-En.pdf Ministry of Education, Sri Lanka — School List 2024]]

The Department of Christian Affairs also lists Holy Trinity Church, Duwana, Kochchikade in its Gampaha District church records. [ref: [https://www.christian.gov.lk/churches/gampaha-district.html Department of Christian Affairs — Gampaha District Churches]]

== Manaveriya ==

Manaveriya is a nearby locality northeast of Kochchikade.

Although Manaveriya is frequently associated with the wider Kochchikade area in local addresses and geographic descriptions, it is administratively separate from Kochchikade GN Division 78 and belongs to the Katana Divisional Secretariat.

Manaveriya forms part of the rural transition between Kochchikade and the Katana interior.

== Udangawa ==

Udangawa is another settlement in the wider Kochchikade–Katana landscape.

It is administered separately from Kochchikade GN Division 78 and forms part of the Katana-side settlement network.

== Thoppuwa ==

Thoppuwa is a settlement north of Kochchikade and is part of the Katana administrative area.

DCS records identify Thoppuwa as GN Division 65A within Katana DS Division.

The Ministry of Education lists:

* Thoppuwa St. Philip Neri's K.V.; and
* Thoppu R.C. Tamil M.V.

within the relevant education network.

The Department of Christian Affairs lists St. Philip Neri's Church, Thoppuwa and St. John the Baptist Church among churches associated with the area.

The official Sunday-school records also list St. Philip Neri's Sunday School at Thoppuwa in both English and Tamil. [ref: [https://christian.gov.lk/sunday-schools/gampaha-district.html Department of Christian Affairs — Gampaha District Sunday Schools]]

== Muruthana ==

Muruthana is a nearby settlement within the Katana-side rural network.

The Ministry of Education's 2024 school list includes Muruthana K.V..

The Department of Christian Affairs lists St. Anthony's Church, Muruthana among the churches of the Gampaha District.

== Bambukuliya ==

Bambukuliya is a settlement associated with the Thoppuwa–Katana side of the Kochchikade region.

DCS administrative data place Bambukuliya within the Katana Divisional Secretariat rather than Kochchikade GN Division 78.

The area is connected to Kochchikade through local roads, schools and religious institutions.

== Welihena ==

Welihena is a larger settlement area on the Katana side of the Kochchikade region.

The area includes separate northern and southern GN divisions and forms part of the rural and educational network north and east of Kochchikade.

The Ministry of Education's 2024 school list includes:

* Welihena Sinhala Mixed K.V.; and
* Welihena R.C. Tamil V.

These schools illustrate the Sinhala- and Tamil-medium educational presence in the wider locality.

== Ethgala and Mahaththogala ==

Ethgala and Mahaththogala are settlements in the broader Katana-side rural landscape.

The 2024 school list includes Ethgala Roman Catholic K.V. within the local education network.

They are connected with Kochchikade through the wider road and service network rather than being part of GN Division 78 itself.

== Adikkandiya ==

Adikkandiya is a rural locality associated with the Welihena–Ethgala side of the wider Kochchikade region.

It belongs to the Katana administrative network rather than Kochchikade GN Division 78.

== Maha Oya ==

The Maha Oya is the principal river associated with the northern side of Kochchikade.

The Central Environmental Authority states that Maha Oya has a catchment of about 1,538 km² and a river length of approximately 130 km. It flows through several districts before reaching its lower reaches near the Gampaha coastal plain. [ref: [https://www.cea.lk/web/2013-05-07-07-51-07/environmental-pollution-contorl-division/water-quality-unit?lang=en Central Environmental Authority — Water Quality Monitoring Laboratory Unit]]

The CEA includes Maha Oya among the inland water bodies subject to regular surface-water quality monitoring.

The authority's published water-quality material notes that organic pollution is a significant pressure on Maha Oya, including elevated biological and chemical indicators at monitored sites. [ref: [https://www.cea.lk/web/water?id=160&lang=en Central Environmental Authority — Water Quality Monitoring]]

The river is therefore important to Kochchikade not only as a geographical feature but also as an environmental and water-management concern.

== Kochchikade Maha Oya bridge ==

The Maha Oya bridge at Kochchikade is one of the locality's most important transport structures.

The former bridge was approximately 83 years old when it was replaced because of deterioration and traffic congestion. [ref: [https://www.sundaytimes.lk/190324/news/pm-opens-new-maha-oya-bridge-342340.html The Sunday Times — PM opens new Maha Oya bridge]]

The replacement bridge is approximately 105 metres long and has four lanes. Construction began on 24 June 2016 and was completed on 24 January 2019.

The project cost approximately Rs. 651.9 million and was funded with Australian government assistance, according to the report on its opening.

The bridge was opened in March 2019 and was described as important for road users travelling from northern and north-eastern parts of Sri Lanka towards Colombo.

The same report described the new bridge as a tourist attraction for visitors to Negombo.

== Colombo–Puttalam road ==

Kochchikade is situated along the principal northbound road corridor between Colombo and the north-western part of Sri Lanka.

The A3 route connects the Colombo metropolitan area with Negombo and continues towards the Puttalam side of the country.

The replacement Maha Oya bridge was designed to address increasing traffic volumes and congestion on this corridor.

The road is important for:

* passenger transport;
* freight movement;
* local commerce;
* access to Negombo;
* access to north-western districts; and
* tourism.

== Railway ==

Kochchikade railway station is on the Puttalam railway line of Sri Lanka Railways.

Official Sri Lanka Railways station data place Kochchikade at 45.048 km from Colombo Fort and list the station telephone number as 031-2277271.

The station lies north of Negombo railway station and south of Waikkala railway station.

Rail services provide connections for commuters travelling between Kochchikade, Negombo, Colombo and settlements farther north on the Puttalam line.

== Road transport ==

Kochchikade's main road network connects it with:

* Negombo;
* Colombo;
* Katana;
* Dankotuwa;
* Waikkala;
* Pallansena;
* Palangathure;
* Poruthota;
* Thoppuwa; and
* surrounding villages.

The Maha Oya bridge is the main north–south road crossing at Kochchikade.

The road network also connects the locality with the coastal tourism belt around northern Negombo.

== Postal services ==

The postal code of Kochchikade is 11540. [ref: [https://www.slpost.gov.lk/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/POST-CODE-BOOK-.pdf Department of Posts — Post Code Directory]]

The Department of Posts lists a Kochchikade postmaster and Kochchikade Post Office in its official Main Offices Directorate information. [ref: [https://slpost.gov.lk/information/main-offices-directorate/ Department of Posts — Main Offices Directorate]]

The official listing gives:

* Postmaster — 031-2277250
* Post Office — 031-2277252

== Police services ==

Kochchikade Police Station provides policing services for the locality and surrounding areas.

The official Sri Lanka Police telephone index lists:

* General telephone — 031-2277222
* Mobile — 071-8591631
* Email — [email] [ref: [https://www.police.lk/?page_id=1301 Sri Lanka Police — Telephone Index]]

== Education ==

Kochchikade and its surrounding localities are served by the Negombo education zone and nearby education networks.

The Ministry of Education's 2024 school directory records schools in the Kochchikade, Pallansena, Thoppuwa and surrounding areas.

Schools associated with the wider Kochchikade area include:

* Kochchikade Maha Vidyalaya;
* Duwana Sinhala Mixed Vidyalaya;
* Palangathuraya Sinhala Mixed K.V.;
* Pallansena R.C.P.V.;
* Thoppuwa St. Philip Neri's K.V.;
* Thoppu R.C. Tamil M.V.;
* Muruthana K.V.;
* Welihena Sinhala Mixed K.V.;
* Welihena R.C. Tamil V.; and
* Ethgala Roman Catholic K.V..

Some of these schools are outside Kochchikade GN Division 78 and are included here because they form part of the wider local education network.

== Religious and cultural landscape ==

Kochchikade and the surrounding Negombo–Katana region have a multi-religious and culturally diverse population.

The Department of Christian Affairs' Gampaha District church table lists several churches associated with Kochchikade and neighbouring areas, including:

* St. Anne's Church, Palangathurai, Kochchikade;
* Holy Spirit Church, Kochchikade;
* Our Lady of Sorrows Church, Pallansena, Kochchikade;
* Holy Trinity Church, Duwana, Kochchikade;
* St. Sebastian's Church, Poruthata, Kochchikade;
* Our Lady of Conception Church, Pallasena, Kochchikade;
* St. Philip Neri's Church, Thoppuwa, Kochchikade;
* St. John the Baptist Church; and
* St. Anthony's Church, Muruthana, Kochchikade.

The official Sunday-school records also list St. Philip Neri's Sunday School at Thoppuwa in English and Tamil.

These institutions illustrate the long-standing Christian cultural presence within the wider Negombo coastal settlement network.

== Economic geography ==

Kochchikade's economy is influenced by its location on a major transport corridor and its proximity to Negombo's commercial and tourism economy.

Economic activities include:

* retail trade;
* food and hospitality;
* transport services;
* vehicle and mechanical services;
* banking;
* education;
* public services;
* small and medium-sized enterprises; and
* tourism-related activity.

The surrounding coastal settlements additionally have links with fishing, hotels, restaurants and the wider Negombo tourism economy.

Sri Lankan excise licensing records include tourism and hospitality establishments using Kochchikade and Palangathure addresses.

== Tourism ==

Kochchikade is not itself the principal tourism centre of the district, but it functions as an important northern gateway to the Negombo tourism area.

Tourism destinations accessible through the Kochchikade road network include:

* Negombo;
* Palangathure;
* Poruthota;
* Pallansena;
* Negombo Lagoon;
* northern coastal beaches; and
* settlements towards Waikkala and Dankotuwa.

The 2019 report on the Maha Oya bridge described the new structure as a tourist attraction for visitors travelling to Negombo.

Hospitality establishments in Palangathure and nearby Poruthota are part of the wider Negombo tourism economy.

== Maha Oya and environmental importance ==

Maha Oya is the principal natural waterway associated with Kochchikade.

The Central Environmental Authority states that it monitors the surface-water quality of Maha Oya as part of its national water-quality programme.

Published CEA water-quality information identifies organic pollution as a major pressure on Maha Oya and reports exceedances of several monitored parameters at sampling locations. [ref: [https://www.cea.lk/web/water?id=160&lang=en Central Environmental Authority — Surface Water Quality Monitoring]]

The Kochchikade bridge is therefore an important reference location for both transport and the monitoring of the river's lower catchment.

== Climate ==

Kochchikade is in the low-elevation western coastal plain of Sri Lanka.

Its climate is warm and humid compared with the central highlands of the island, and rainfall is strongly influenced by the southwest monsoon and inter-monsoonal conditions.

The Maha Oya and surrounding drainage network can influence local water levels and surface-water conditions during periods of heavy rainfall.

== Urban and social landscape ==

Kochchikade is characterised by a mixture of commercial, residential, transport and religious land uses.

The central area contains shops, service businesses, transport facilities, schools and religious institutions, while the surrounding areas become progressively more residential and rural.

The locality's social geography extends beyond its GN boundary because nearby settlements use Kochchikade for transport, commerce, education and municipal services.

== Relationship with the wider Kochchikade area ==

In everyday address and geographic usage, Kochchikade can refer to a wider area than GN Division 78.

This broader area includes:

* Pallansena;
* Palangathure;
* Poruthota;
* Duwana;
* Manaveriya;
* Udangawa;
* Thoppuwa;
* Bambukuliya;
* Muruthana;
* Welihena;
* Ethgala; and
* Adikkandiya.

Administratively, however, these places are divided between Negombo and Katana Divisional Secretariat areas.

This distinction is important when interpreting population statistics, government services and GN-level boundaries.

== Regional relationship tree ==

The following diagram represents geographic, transport, education, religious and service connections rather than a formal administrative hierarchy.

Negombo
│
▼
Kochchikade
│
├── Pallansena
│ ├── Poruthota
│ ├── Palangathure
│ └── Duwana
│
├── Thoppuwa
│ ├── Bambukuliya
│ ├── Muruthana
│ └── Manaveriya
│
└── Welihena
├── Ethgala
├── Mahaththogala
└── Adikkandiya

== Transport network ==

The principal transport network can be represented as:

Colombo
│
▼
Negombo
│
▼
Kochchikade
│
├── Railway → Colombo / Negombo / Puttalam direction
│
├── A3 road → Negombo / Colombo
│
├── A3 road → Thoppuwa / Dankotuwa / north-west
│
└── Local roads
├── Pallansena
├── Poruthota
├── Palangathure
├── Manaveriya
└── Welihena

== Historical development ==

The modern development of Kochchikade has been closely associated with road and railway transport.

The older Maha Oya bridge served the main road for many decades before being replaced because of deterioration and increasing traffic requirements.

The Puttalam railway line also established Kochchikade as a transport stop between Colombo, Negombo and communities farther north.

The combination of road, bridge and railway infrastructure contributed to Kochchikade's development as a commercial and service locality.

== Maha Oya bridge replacement ==

The replacement of the Maha Oya bridge was a major infrastructure project for Kochchikade.

The new bridge cost approximately Rs. 651.9 million, was funded with Australian government assistance, and was opened in March 2019.

The project replaced the older bridge and provided four lanes across the river.

The bridge was intended to improve road capacity and reduce congestion on the Colombo–Puttalam corridor.

== Current urban issues ==

A 2024 report in The Sunday Times described continuing traffic congestion and infrastructure issues in Kochchikade despite the new bridge.

The report discussed road conditions, drainage, pedestrian conditions and parking problems around the railway station. [ref: [https://www.sundaytimes.lk/240324/news/kochchikade-far-from-the-great-expectations-the-new-bridge-held-552847.html The Sunday Times — Kochchikade: Far from the great expectations the new bridge held]]

These observations describe conditions reported in 2024 and should not be treated as a timeless description of the locality.

== Religious heritage ==

The churches and Sunday schools recorded around Kochchikade, Pallansena, Palangathure, Poruthota, Duwana and Thoppuwa form part of the religious heritage of the northern Negombo region.

The concentration of churches, schools and coastal settlements reflects the historical development of Catholic and other Christian communities in and around Negombo.

== Public services ==

Kochchikade provides several local public services, including:

* municipal administration;
* police services;
* postal services;
* railway transport;
* education;
* Ayurveda health services; and
* access to larger services in Negombo.

The Negombo Municipal Council lists a Kochchikade Ayurveda Medical Officer among its municipal health personnel.

The council's sub-office provides a further local-government access point for residents.

== Main places ==

Important places within or closely associated with Kochchikade include:

* Kochchikade Sub-Office, Negombo Municipal Council;
* Kochchikade railway station;
* Kochchikade Post Office;
* Kochchikade Police Station;
* Kochchikade Maha Vidyalaya;
* Kochchikade Ayurveda Dispensary;
* the Maha Oya bridge;
* Holy Spirit Church, Kochchikade; and
* the road corridor connecting Negombo with Palangathure, Pallansena and Thoppuwa.

data.text:
The 2026–27 UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball team will represent the University of Nevada, Las Vegas during the 2026–27 NCAA Division I men's basketball season. The Runnin' Rebels, will be led by second-year head coach josh Pastner, playing their home games at the Thomas & Mack Center in Paradise, Nevada as a member of the Mountain West Conference (MW).

== Previous season ==

The Runnin' Rebels finished the 2025–26 season 18–17, 11–9 in Mountain West play to finish tied for seventh (but got eighth place due to losing the tiebreaker to Colorado State) in the conference. As the 8th seed in the Mountain West Tournament they would beat (9th seed Wyoming) 73–70 in the First Round, but would lose to (1st Seed Utah State) 80–60 in the Quarterfinals. As they were not selected to participate in the NCAA Tournament, they were selected and played in the NIT Tournament, at they were played in the Tulsa Regional, where they would beat (4th seed UC Irvine) 75–72 in the First Round, but would lose to (1st seed Tulsa) 77–66 in the Second round, witch would end their season with an overall record of 18–17.

data.title: Kelley Dennison
data.text:
Kelley Anne Dennison is an American political candidate, licensed massage therapist, small-business owner, and activist from Colorado.She became the Republican nominee for Colorado's 2nd congressional district int he 2026 United States House of Representatives election.Her campaign has focused on economic affordability, environmental conservation, family policy, education reform, and constitutional rights.

== Early life and education ==
Dennison is a Colorado native who has described growing up in a family where political issues andpublicaffairs were openly discussed. According to her campaign interviews, her interest in politicsdevelopedpartly through high school civics and history classes and concerns about the rising cost of living.

She attended Estes Park High School and completed professional training in massage therapy at the Academy of Natural Therapy, receiving a certificate in 2023.

== Career ==

=== Business and massage therapy ===
Before entering electoral politics, Dennison worked as a licensed massage therapist and small-business owner. Her professional background includes operating Wind Bear Holistic Healing, abusiness associated with massage and holistic wellness services.

She has presented her experience working directly with clients and running a small business as a basis for understanding the financial pressures faced by ordinary workers, families, and entrepreneurs.

=== Entry into politics ===
Dennison's first reported involvement in electoral politics included working as a campaign staffer for Republican congressional candidate Adam DeRito. She subsequently decided to run for Congress herself,citing concerns about affordability, government accountability,and the limited participationof younger Americans in politics.

Her candidacy attracted attention because she entered a high-profile congressional race withouthaving previously held elected public office.

== Political career ==

=== 2026 congressional campaign ===
In 2026, Dennison sought the Republican nomination for Colorado's2nd congressional district. She won the Republican primary on June 30, 2026, defeating Christina Blunt and becoming the party's nominee for the general election against Democratic incumbent Joe Neguse.

The race drew attention because the district had historically favoured Democrats. In the 2024 election, Neguse won nearly 70% of the vote, making Dennison's campaign a challenge in a district where Republicans faced a significant electoral disadvantage.

Dennison promoted a grassroots campaign aimed at engaging younger voters and residents of Colorado's mountain communities. She also advocated for greater participation by members of Generation Z in political life.

== Political positions ==
Dennison's campaign platform includes several major policy areas. The following summarizes positions she has publicly expressed; it does not imply that the proposals have been enacted.

=== Economic affordability ===
Dennison has advocated increasing the supply of housing, reducing regulations that she believes increase construction costs, and limiting large corporate investors' purchases of starter homes. Shehas also emphasized the cost of living for working families and younger Coloradans.

=== Environmental conservation ===
She supports responsible land use, conservation of forests and headwater ecosystems, and protection of watersheds. She has also emphasized the relationship between environmental stewardship, water security, and Colorado's outdoor recreation economy.

=== Family and education policy ===
Her campaign supports pro-family policies, greater parental involvement in education, and efforts to improve educational quality and practical career preparation. She also identifies veterans and senior citizens as groups deserving stronger support.

=== Constitutional rights and term limits ===
Dennison supports Second Amendment rights and has signed the U.S. Term Limits pledge, committing to support a constitutional amendment limiting congressional service. Her campaign frames these positions around individual liberty and government accountability.

=== Immigration and government accountability ===
She supports secure borders, enforcement of immigration laws, and more efficient legal immigration pathways. She has also called for greater transparency in government and cooperation across party lines.

== Public image and political significance ==
Dennison has been described in media coverage as an unconventional, younger Republican candidate. Her candidacy combines conservative positions on gun rights and government regulation with an emphasis on housing affordability, environmental conservation, and outreach to younger voters.

Her background as a small-business owner rather than a career politician has been a prominent part of her campaign identity. She has argued that ordinary citizens should participate more actively in public affairs instead of leaving political leadership exclusively to established politicians.

== Electoral status ==
As of October 18, 2026, Dennison is the Republican nominee in the 2026 general election for Colorado's 2nd congressional district.

data.title: Turbo (Dutch band)
data.text:
Turbo is a Dutch hard rock band from Arnhem, formed in early 1979 by former members of Dutch bands including Metal Voices, Long Tall Ernie and The Shakers, and the Speedtwins. The band released two albums on CBS Netherlands, Turbo (1979) and You Girl (1980).

== History ==

=== Formation ===
The line-up was singer and guitarist Leen "Lain" Barbier, guitarist Jos Jaspers, bassist Charles Schutters and drummer Eugène Arts. Jaspers, Schutters and Arts had previously played together in the science-fiction rock band Metal Voices; Barbier had been in the punk group Speedtwins and Splinterfunk, and Arts and Jaspers in Long Tall Ernie and The Shakers. According to regional press coverage, the band took a demo to CBS, whose staff at first believed it was an existing record, and the label signed them.

=== Turbo (1979) ===
Their self-titled debut album was completed in ten days and released on CBS in June 1979. Barbier wrote most of the lyrics, and some songs were by Floris Kolvenbach, a former Metal Voices member; "Time Traveller" dated from the Metal Voices period. A review in de Volkskrant of a concert at Amsterdam's Jaap Edenhal, where Turbo and Ted Nugent both played, described the band as playing "melodic hard rock" with more variety than ordinary "beton" (hard rock) and called them "a promise for the future", singling out Barbier's voice. A Groningen newspaper described the band as having been "heavily hyped" by CBS. The debut was also released in France, Germany and Canada.

A regional newspaper reported that the album's cover, showing the band appearing to steal a Porsche Turbo, was copied by another band, The Roadrunners, using a DAF, and that the car in the photograph was removed by someone else two days after the shoot.

=== You Girl (1980) ===
The second album, You Girl, appeared in early 1980, produced by the radio DJ Alfred Lagarde and including a cover of Jimi Hendrix's "Stone Free". Bassist Charles Schutters left after the recording sessions. “Algemeen Dagblad praised the album’s natural, carefully played rock, but found the title song somewhat forced, praising Barbier's singing, Jaspers' guitar solos and Lagarde's production, and noting that CBS Netherlands was actively developing Dutch talent with releases by Turbo, The Nits and White Honey.

=== Later activity ===
Turbo has continued to perform in the Netherlands in recent years under Barbier, with Dick Kemper and drummer Willem van der Aa. [ref: Dampend optreden Lain Barbier, Arnhemse Koerier] A planned show in Arnhem in July 2024 was cancelled when the drummer was injured.

== Discography ==
; Studio albums
* Turbo (CBS, 1979)
* You Girl (CBS, 1980)

; Live albums
* Turbolence (2002) [ref: Turbo – The legendary rock formation, turbo-rock.nl]

The Sweet Potato King of Colorado is the honorary title awarded annually to the winner of the sweet potato competition at the Colorado State Fair. The individual who produces the highest-scoring sweet potato entry is ceremonially crowned "Sweet Potato King" and serves as the symbolic ambassador for sweet potato cultivation in Colorado for the following year.

Contest entries are evaluated by fair judges based on criteria including:

* Size and uniformity
* Appearance
* Color and texture
* Overall quality
* Agricultural presentation

The entrant receiving the highest overall score is declared the Sweet Potato King and is awarded a ceremonial crown.

data.title: Leonard Harvey Lynn
data.text:
Leonard Harvey Lynn is an American academic and Professor Emeritus at Case Western Reserve University. [ref: https://people.ucsc.edu/~boxjenk/Economics,%20Management,%20and%20Financial%20Markets%205(2),%202010.pdf] His research focuses on technology innovation, international business systems, and the comparative analysis of technological development across countries, particularly the United States and Japan. [ref: ]

== Early life and education ==
Lynn completed his undergraduate and master’s studies in Asian Studies at the University of Oregon, earning a B.A. in 1966 and an M.A. in 1967. He received a Certificate in Mandarin Chinese from the U.S. Defense Language Institute in 1962 and undertook Japanese language studies in Tokyo from 1968 to 1973. [ref: ] [ref: https://pacificaffairs.ubc.ca/files/2011/07/Volume75.pdf]

He later pursued graduate studies at the University of Michigan, earning an M.A. in Sociology (1976) and a Ph.D. in Sociology (1980). His doctoral dissertation examined the social sources of technological innovation in oxygen steelmaking in Japan and the United States.

== Career ==
Lynn joined Carnegie Mellon University in 1980 as an assistant professor in the Department of Social and Decision Sciences, where he worked until 1987. [ref: How Japan Innovates: A Comparison With The U.s. In The Case Of Oxygen Steelmaking, Routledge & CRC Press] During this period, he conducted comparative research on engineering careers and industrial technology systems in the United States and Japan [ref: Japanese Technology at a Turning Point, Current History], supported by the National Science Foundation. He also collaborated with Timothy McKeown on a study of trade associations in the two countries funded by the U.S. Department of Commerce. [ref: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=894348]

In 1987, Lynn joined Case Western Reserve University as an associate professor of management policy and later became a full professor. He chaired the Department of Marketing and Policy Studies from 1995 to 2005 and became professor emeritus in 2010. [ref: ] From 1993 to 1994, he served as a visiting professor at Hitotsubashi University in Japan under a program supported by Japan's Ministry of Education. He also participated in executive education programs in Japan and the United States, including the University of Hawaii–Japan Executive MBA program. [ref: https://www.jpf.go.jp/Assets/Volumes/Volume%202.pdf]

Lynn's research has examined the social, institutional, and organizational factors influencing technological innovation and international industrial competition. His early work compared innovation in the steel industries of Japan and the United States. [ref: Institutions, Organizations, and Technological Innovation: Oxygen Steelmaking in the U.S. and Japan, University of Michigan] [ref: ]

At Case Western Reserve University, Lynn served on the Faculty Senate Executive Committee, provost and dean search committees, and other university advisory bodies. [ref: ] He was president of the Association of Japanese Business Studies from 1995 to 1997 and also served as its treasurer and program chair. [ref: Client Challenge, link.springer.com]
