A record can carry more than one format value, so the rows do not add up exactly to the total. By sector, libraries account for about 13.1 million records, archives for 4.2 million, museums for 2.3 million and other organisations for 170,000. About 4.8 million records have digital content available online.

The most-used material providers in 2022 and 2023 were the National Board of Antiquities (Finnish Heritage Agency), the National Library of Finland, KAVI, the Helsinki City Museum, the National Museum of Finland, the University of Jyväskylä, Lusto, Vapriikki Museum Centre, the 3AMK libraries (Haaga-Helia, Laurea and Metropolia) and the Helmet libraries.

== Finna platform ==
Besides the national Finna.fi site, the National Library offers Finna as a platform service. Organisations use it to build their own search services ("Finna views"), such as public library online libraries, university library catalogues, museum collection sites and archive portals, under addresses of the form organisation.finna.fi. Each organisation customises the appearance and features of its view with a management tool. More than 130 organisations used the platform in 2026, and there were 131 Finna search services at the end of 2024. Organisations can also add shared material, such as Finnish scholarly journals from the Journal.fi platform or open learning materials, to their own views.

The views listed on Finna.fi include archive services such as those of the Central Archives for Finnish Business Records and the Finnish Literature Society, museum sites such as those of the Finnish Heritage Agency, Helsinki City Museum and the Sámi Museum Siida, public library consortia such as Helmet, PIKI and Vaski, and the libraries of universities and universities of applied sciences.

== Technology ==
Finna's search service is built on VuFind, an open-source discovery system that uses the Apache Solr search platform. The National Library publishes its fork as NDL-VuFind2 under the GNU General Public License version 2, and the metadata harvesting and processing system RecordManager as a separate open-source project. The National Library extended VuFind for museum and archive material, adding support for several metadata formats and media types.

Contributing organisations deliver metadata mainly over OAI-PMH in EAD, LIDO, MARC 21, Dublin Core and Forward formats. Finna supports the International Image Interoperability Framework (IIIF), enriches metadata with vocabularies from the Finto ontology service, geocodes material with OpenStreetMap data, and imports organisation details from the Kirkanta library directory and the museum database of the Finnish Museums Association. A new version is released about once a month.

== Access and usage rights ==
Finna separates three layers of access: use of the website, reuse of the descriptive metadata, and reuse of the digital objects (images, documents, recordings and video) that the metadata describes. Each layer has its own rules.

=== Using the website ===
Anyone can search Finna.fi, view records and view digital content without an account and without charge. A user who logs in can save favourites and searches, add tags, comments and reviews, receive alerts about new records, and use library services. In participating libraries, logged-in users can view loans, renew them, place holds, and pay fines and fees online.

Finna supports four login methods:
* a library card number and PIN of a participating library;
* Haka credentials of Finnish higher education institutions;
* a Finna ID created on the site, which needs an email address (users under 13 need the permission of a legal guardian);
* a one-time login link sent to the email address in the user's library patron record.

Accounts created with different methods are separate, even when they share an identifier. Some Finna views also search indexes outside Finna, such as the article indexes CDI, EDS and Summon, alongside Finna's own index.

The general terms of the service prohibit using the service "for any purposes out of the ordinary" and forbid automated tools such as robots, spiders, scrapers and offline readers on functions that require login. The National Library reserves the right to restrict access, for example to secure maintenance or the functioning of the service.

=== Usage rights of digital material ===
Each contributing organisation sets the usage rights of its own material and is responsible for it. Finna displays those rights on every record and asks users to check and observe them before reuse. Most digital material carries either a Creative Commons licence or a statement from RightsStatements.org.

{| class="wikitable"
|+ Rights marks used on Finna and what they allow
! Mark !! Reuse allowed
|-
| Public Domain Mark || Copyright has expired; free use.
|-
| CC0 || Free use; the rights holder has waived copyright.
|-
| CC BY 4.0 || Any use, including commercial use and modification, with attribution of the author and other named parties (such as the holding organisation), a link to the licence, and a note of changes.
|-
| CC BY-SA 4.0 || As CC BY; derived works must use the same licence.
|-
| CC BY-ND 4.0 || Commercial use allowed; no modification (for example, no cropping).
|-
| CC BY-NC 4.0 || Non-commercial use only, including in education; modification allowed.
|-
| CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 || Non-commercial use; derived works under the same licence.
|-
| CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 || Non-commercial use; no modification.
|-
| In Copyright || View, link and save to favourites only; no reuse, modification, presentation or commercial use without permission.
|-
| In Copyright – Educational Use Permitted || As In Copyright, but educational reuse is allowed without permission.
|-
| Copyright Not Evaluated || View, link and save; ask the provider before any reuse.
|-
| No Known Copyright || View, link and save; ask the provider before any reuse.
|}

When a record shows no rights information, or the user is unsure, Finna directs the user to the providing organisation through a "Contact us" form attached to each record. Without known rights, users may still view the material, share links to it, save searches and add it to public or private lists.

Finna's usage-rights page stresses that these marks cover copyright only. The user remains responsible for privacy and other laws; for example, photographs of living people may not be used in marketing or advertising without the subjects' consent.

The search interface and the API offer a usage-rights filter with six categories. The categories are filters by permitted use, so the counts overlap and do not add up to the total.

{| class="wikitable" style="text-align:right"
|+ Records matching each usage-rights filter
! style="text-align:left" | Filter !! Records
|-
| style="text-align:left" | Free use || 475,636
|-
| style="text-align:left" | Derivatives, also commercial || 1,986,980
|-
| style="text-align:left" | No derivatives, also commercial || 2,057,820
|-
| style="text-align:left" | Derivatives, non-commercial || 2,135,594
|-
| style="text-align:left" | No derivatives, non-commercial || 2,552,028
|-
| style="text-align:left" | Permission required / unknown || 3,050,445
|}

=== Descriptions and cover images ===
As a general rule, users may freely reuse the descriptions shown in Finna search results. Exceptions are abstracts within descriptions, back-cover texts of books and descriptions written by Finna users, which may be under third-party copyright. Other Finna views and online libraries may apply their own restrictions. Many book cover images shown on Finna are protected by copyright; their use must be agreed separately, for example with the publisher.

=== Open API ===
Finna's REST API at api.finna.fi gives read-only access to the search index. It opened on 3 February 2016, when it exposed the metadata of almost 9 million records. The National Library's Library Network Services unit maintains it.

Its terms of use set these rules:
* No registration or API key is needed. The National Library may introduce registration if it must restrict use, for example to avoid excessive server load.
* The metadata is licensed under the CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication.
* CC0 does not cover the resources linked from the metadata, such as images, which appear in the urls, onlineUrls and images fields. Reuse of those resources follows the terms shown with the resource or in the imageRights and accessRestrictions fields. If no terms are shown, the user must ask the providing organisation for permission.
* Because of third-party copyright, the API does not expose all the metadata visible on Finna.fi, and CC0 does not apply to metadata outside the API.
* The National Library is not the rights holder of the metadata or the linked resources, does not guarantee the accuracy of the metadata, and accepts no liability for its use. The providing organisations are responsible for their right to supply data on these terms. Data is provided "as is" and may change at any time.

The terms also recommend, without requiring, that users credit Finna.fi and the organisations that produced the data. Library metadata may include records from OCLC, and users are asked to credit OCLC under its WorldCat community norms.

Technically, the API returns JSON (or JSONP with a callback parameter) and allows cross-origin resource sharing from any origin. It offers record and search endpoints for the main index and for an authority index, and an endpoint for public user lists. A query returns at most 100 records per page and at most 100,000 records in total; larger sets must be fetched in batches with a resumption token. A search returns at most 20 images per record. Full-resolution image links are delivered through the API's image service. The National Library announces API changes in the GitHub Discussions of the NDL-VuFind2 project.

Finna also runs an OAI-PMH repository at api.finna.fi/OAI/Server.

=== Personal data ===
The National Library of Finland is the data controller for Finna's user register, with CSC as a co-provider of the service. Depending on the login method, Finna stores the user's name, email address, library card number, PIN and home library, and data the user saves, such as favourites, tags, comments, reviews, saved searches and holds. Loan and hold data stays in each library's own system; Finna stores only what it needs to send optional due-date reminders. Accounts and their data are deleted automatically 18 months after the last login, or when the user closes the account; comments left by a closed account remain but are anonymised.

Finna collects usage statistics with Matomo, hosted at CSC, only with the user's consent, and anonymises IP addresses. Cloudflare processes technical log data of the traffic to Finna sites to keep the services running. Cloudflare processes data in the European Economic Area and the United States, under the standard contractual clauses approved by the European Commission. Finna transfers no other personal data outside the EU and EEA.

Records and digital objects may themselves contain personal data, such as names or photographs. Requests to correct or remove such data go to the organisation that provided the material.

=== Accessibility ===
Finna.fi publishes an accessibility statement under Finnish law. Annanpura Oy assessed the site in June 2019, and the statement was last updated on 1 October 2025. The National Library is responsible for the accessibility of the user interface, and the contributing organisations for the accessibility of their material. Unresolved complaints go to the Digital Accessibility Supervision Unit of Traficom.

data.title: Priyalal Sirisena
data.text:
----

Priyalal Sirisena (born 25 May 1979) is a Sri Lankan attorney-at-law, human rights lawyer, and novelist. [ref: Priyalal Sirisena Profile, Front Line Defenders] He practices constitutional law and fundamental rights litigation in Sri Lanka and is the author of the Sinhala novel Deyyange Atha. [ref: Echoes of the Past: A Conversation with Priyalal Sirisena, The Island]

== Early life and education ==
Sirisena was born on 25 May 1979 in Kurunegala, Sri Lanka. He studied law at the University of Colombo, graduating with a Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.) in 2006, and was admitted to the bar as an Attorney-at-Law of the Supreme Court of Sri Lanka. He later earned a Master of Laws (LL.M.) from the same university.

== Legal career ==
Sirisena works on legal cases involving fundamental rights, police misconduct, and custodial torture in Sri Lanka. He has contributed to civil society reports submitted for Sri Lanka's Universal Periodic Review at the United Nations.

In June 2018, Sirisena filed a Fundamental Rights petition in the Supreme Court of Sri Lanka against police officers, alleging interference with his duties as legal counsel. [ref: Lawyer sues cops for stifling his professional rights, Daily Mirror] In May 2023, Front Line Defenders reported that Sirisena faced threats and intimidation related to his legal work in Kurunegala.

== Literary work ==
Sirisena worked as a journalist for The Island newspaper before writing fiction. He authored the Sinhala novel Deyyange Atha (The Elephant of the Gods), published by Vidarshana Publishers. [ref: Deiyange Etha by Priyalal Sirisena, Katha.lk] The book was shortlisted for the Swarna Pusthaka Awards in 2025.

data.title: Jace Shim
data.text:
Jace Shim (born Shim Jun-Kyu; ) is a South Korean management consultant, business executive and author. He is the chief executive officer of The Solution Company B (TSCB Group), a consulting firm specializing in environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategy and the assurance of sustainability reports, and an adjunct professor in the Department of Business Administration at Inha University. [ref: [신간] 심준규 박사, 스테이블코인 프로토콜 출간, Mustnews] [ref: [신간소개] 녹색금융으로 읽는 ESG 이야기: 브랜드의 미래를 결정하는 ESG와 녹색금융, ESGKO] [ref: [MD포토] 심준규 대표 '회복과 성장을 위한 ESG 정책', My Daily]

He is the author of FVS Marketing (2015), which proposed a marketing framework built on frame, value and story, [ref: [신간 리뷰] 고객 지향형 마케팅의 새 기준, 'FVS 마케팅', Money Today Network (MTN)] and of several books on ESG and stablecoins, including Dollar on Chain (2026). [ref: Dollar on Chain, Kyobo Book Centre] In 2026, he proposed four strategy models for generative engine optimization (GEO) in AI 승자독식 (AI Winner-Takes-All) and its English edition, Winner Takes the Answer. [ref: AI 승자독식: 생성형 AI가 단 하나의 브랜드를 추천하는 시대의 GEO 마케팅 전략, Raonbook Plus] [ref: Winner Takes the Answer, Raonbook Plus]

== Education ==
Shim earned a Master of Business Administration with a concentration in marketing from the University of Liverpool Management School in 2014, with a dissertation on online consumer purchase decision-making. [ref: 심준규 작가 정보, Kyobo Book Centre] [ref: What decision making choices do online shoppers make, when deciding to purchase goods from the Internet?, University of Liverpool] He received a doctorate in ESG management from the Graduate School of Inha University in 2024. His doctoral dissertation examined how buyer-perceived ESG management affects social capital and supply chain performance. [ref: 구매자가 인식한 ESG 경영이 사회적 자본과 공급사슬 성과에 미치는 영향, Inha University]

== Career ==
Shim worked in marketing and brand management at E-Land Group, including as an expatriate employee at the group's China headquarters in Shanghai from 2010 to 2013. [ref: [전문가 기고] 유커 관광 콘텐츠 개발, 가치 설계가 우선, Money Today] While posted in Shanghai, he first encountered Bitcoin in 2011; after returning to South Korea, he took part in initial coin offerings and operated a cryptocurrency mining business. He later handled product planning and brand launches for the Chinese market at CJ IMC, and worked on online expansion strategy in China for Kolon Industries FnC. [ref: 심준규 저자 소개, Aladin]

He founded The Solution Company B, which initially provided marketing and new-business consulting with a focus on the Chinese market. In December 2015, he was a panelist at a seminar held at the National Assembly on fintech and the overseas spread of Korean Wave content, where he argued that Korean Wave culture needed to be reinterpreted from a marketing perspective. [ref: 홍문종 "한류 콘텐츠 확산 위해 금융산업 변화해야", Gukje News] At a textile and fashion industry seminar in December 2016, he presented on Chinese consumers' mobile-based lifestyles and online-to-offline strategies for entering the Chinese market, stressing that "the core of communication is truthful content". [ref: 섬유·패션기업간 교류회 지상중계 – 불가분 소재와 디자인…"서로 교류하는 플랫폼 구축 시급하다", Korea Textile News]

The company later shifted its focus to sustainability, and it now advises companies on ESG strategy and sustainability reporting and provides third-party assurance of sustainability reports. Shim holds the Certified Sustainability Assurance Practitioner (CSAP) qualification from AccountAbility, and The Solution Company B is listed by AccountAbility as an AA1000 Licensed Assurance Provider. [ref: AA1000 Qualified Individuals, AccountAbility] [ref: AA1000 Licensed Assurance Providers, AccountAbility] In July 2025, he lectured on "ESG policy for recovery and growth" at the My Daily Business Forum in Seoul, held to mark the newspaper's 21st anniversary. [ref: [MD포토] 마이데일리 비즈포럼에서 강의하는 심준규 대표, My Daily]

Shim is an adjunct professor in the Department of Business Administration at Inha University, where he teaches business model innovation and marketing strategy. His research covers marketing strategy, sustainable management and ESG management. He has written ESG columns for several Korean media outlets, including the series Shim Jun-Kyu's ESG Green Book for Mustnews. [ref: [심준규의 ESG 그린북] AI 시대, 비즈니스 모델링의 재정의가 필요한 이유, Mustnews]

== Major works ==
=== FVS Marketing ===
In FVS Marketing (2015), Shim proposed that marketing consists of three elements applied in sequence: frame, value and story. According to a review by Money Today Network, the frame stage asks marketers to adopt the customer's first-person perspective, the value stage identifies the customer's core needs and builds a platform to deliver them, and the story stage combines history, issues and creation. The book illustrates the framework with cases including Uniqlo's Heattech in China and Xiaomi's value-for-money strategy, and argues that social media should not be used only as a one-way promotional channel.

=== ESG Stories Told through Green Finance ===
ESG Stories Told through Green Finance (2026), co-written with Inha University professor Nam Doo-woo, explains ESG through capital flows and financial change rather than as an abstract ideal. The book describes how climate risk has become a financial risk that affects bank lending, investment decisions and corporate valuation. It also covers supply-chain carbon data requests and ESG evaluation by financial institutions, and argues that these pressures extend to small firms, startups and regional companies as well as large corporations.

=== Stablecoin books ===
Shim's books on stablecoins examine how dollar-pegged stablecoins are restructuring monetary infrastructure, approaching the subject through management and geopolitics rather than price analysis or short-term trading. Dollar on Chain (2026), published by Raonbook, is a revised English edition of his Korean book 스테이블코인 부의 기회 (Stablecoin: The Wealth Opportunity), with added international case studies and updated coverage of regulation.

The books describe how stablecoins may replace SWIFT-based international remittances, how smart contracts change trade settlement and how real-world asset tokenization opens new asset access for small investors. Shim interprets the United States' GENIUS Act, which requires dollar stablecoin issuers to hold reserves in short-term U.S. Treasury securities, as a strategic design to channel global private liquidity into the U.S. Treasury market and extend dollar dominance into digital finance. He compares U.S. legislation with the European Union's Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation and South Korea's Virtual Asset User Protection Act, and argues for a Korean stablecoin strategy in light of South Korea's separation of banking and commerce.

=== Generative engine optimization models ===
In AI 승자독식 (2026), Shim argued that generative AI is changing search from a list of links into a single synthesized answer that names only a few brands. He introduced the term citation gap to describe the difference between a company's actual competitiveness and the competitiveness conveyed in AI-generated answers. To address this gap, he proposed four models, each extending an established management or marketing framework with one additional element. He described them as analytical tools for companies rather than criteria used by any search engine or AI provider.

{| class="wikitable"
|+ Models proposed by Shim (2026)
! Model !! Framework extended !! Original author !! Element added
|-
| 3C-AI || 3C analysis (Company, Customer, Competitor) || Kenichi Ohmae || AI as an information intermediary
|-
| VRIO-D || VRIO (Value, Rarity, Inimitability, Organization) || Jay B. Barney || Discoverability
|-
| STQP || STP (Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning) || Philip Kotler and Kevin Lane Keller || Question Mapping
|-
| E-E-A-T-C || E-E-A-T (Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness) || Google || Citability
|}

* 3C-AI retains the three elements of Ohmae's 3C analysis and treats AI not as a fourth competitor but as an intermediary that determines which alternatives are compared and on which criteria.
* VRIO-D adds discoverability to Barney's VRIO framework, asking whether the value of a firm's resources can be accessed, understood and verified by customers searching through AI-mediated information.
* STQP inserts question mapping between the targeting and positioning stages of the STP model, linking target customers' decision questions and conditions to the company's claims and evidence.
* E-E-A-T-C adds citability to the E-E-A-T perspectives in Google's search quality guidance, defined as the property that allows a passage to retain its meaning, conditions and source when excerpted into an AI-generated answer.

Shim combined the four models into a cycle he called the Winner Takes the Answer Framework, and the book closes with a 90-day implementation plan.

== Selected works ==
=== Books ===
* FVS 마케팅: 심플하고 명쾌한 마케팅의 기준, Human Cube
* 실천으로 완성하는 ESG 전략, Hankyungsa
* 그린북: ESG로 성과 내는 사람들, Provence
* 녹색금융으로 읽는 ESG 이야기
* 스테이블코인 부의 기회
* Dollar on Chain, Raonbook
* AI 승자독식, Raonbook Plus
* Winner Takes the Answer, Raonbook Plus

=== Selected articles ===
* 구매자 관점에서 본 ESG활동이 사회적 자본을 매개로 공급사슬 성과에 미치는 영향: 중소 제조기업을 중심으로, The Journal of International Trade & Commerce
* "꽌시에 기초한 기업 네트워크가 정보공유와 기업성과에 미치는 영향에 관한 연구" [A study on the effect of guanxi-based networks on information sharing and firm performance]. Journal of China Studies. 2023. [https://www.riss.kr/search/detail/DetailView.do?p_mat_type=1a0202e37d52c72d&control_no=6a13124fc4df914ab7998d826d417196 RISS]
* "성과평가 시스템이 구성원의 지식 창출 및 업무성과에 미치는 영향: 공공기관을 대상으로" [The effects of performance evaluation systems on employee knowledge creation and performance in public organizations]. Korean Academy of Business Administration. 2023. [https://www.riss.kr/search/detail/DetailView.do?p_mat_type=1a0202e37d52c72d&control_no=5a07055a78752d33d18150b21a227875 RISS]

data.title: Murder of Jeanie Seton
data.text:
The murder of Jeanie Seton, also known as the Ratho murder, was committed at Ratho in Midlothian, Scotland, on 16 April 1864 by George Bryce.

Bryce was convicted of murder at the High Court of Justiciary and publicly executed on 21 June 1864. His execution was the last public execution to take place in Edinburgh.

== Background ==
Jeanie Seton – also known as Jane or Janie Watt – born 1841, was a nurse (nanny), working for the family of the grain merchant Robert Tod and his wife Margaret in Ratho, Midlothian. [ref: Cowan H. Report of the Trial of George Bryce for Murder. Edinb Med J. 1864 Jul;10(1):76-92. PMID: 29646165; PMCID: PMC5311517.] [ref: Cunningham, S. (1899). Inverkeithing, North Queensferry, Limekilns, Charlestown & The Ferry Hills (1st ed.). Dunfermline: W. Clark & Son.]

George Bryce, born 1829, lived in Ratho and was the romantic interest of Isabella Brown, neighbour of Jeanie Seton. In March 1863, Brown distanced herself from Bryce. Bryce believed Seton was behind this.

== The murder ==

On 16 April, at approximately 7 am, Bryce entered the Tod's house. He asked the house cook for the whereabouts of Jeanie Seaton; the cook told him that Seaton was in the nursery and that he could not see her. Bryce ignored the cook, entered the nursery, and attacked Seton. Her screams attracted the attention of the cook and Mrs Tod, who attempted to intervene. The cook was bitten by Bryce while trying to help Seaton. [ref: The Ratho Murder, www.thegenealogist.co.uk]

Seaton escaped the Tods' house but was followed by Bryce. She was found outside the neighbouring house with her throat cut. She died from her injuries. Witnesses reported that Bryce had stomped on her body.

Bryce fled the area. He later asked an acquaintance, Davidson, to cut his throat, claiming that he had attempted to do so himself. Davidson refused and, having learned of the murder, pursued Bryce with a group of local quarrymen. Bryce reached the railway line near Ratho station, where he was intercepted by railway navvies. He was restrained and taken to Ratho police station.

== The trial ==
Bryce was tried at the High Court of Justiciary in Edinburgh in June 1864. His defence argued that he was insane; evidence was given that Bryce had been known locally as "Daft Geordie Bryce". The jury found him guilty, but recommended leniency, citing the "low organisation of his mental faculties".

Included in trial evidence was the razor used in Seton's murder. [ref: NRS Catalogue - browse - details of record, catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk]

The court sentenced him to death, with the execution scheduled for 21 June 1864. [ref: NRS Catalogue - catalogue record, catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk]

== Execution ==
Before his execution, Bryce reportedly acknowledged that murder was a crime and that he should be punished.

Bryce was hanged at Edinburgh on 21 June 1864 at approximately 8:20am. His body was removed from the scaffold at about 9am. His execution took place on the corner of the present-day George VI Bridge and The Royal Mile, now the site of the French Consulate. [ref: The Maiden: The Scottish beheading machine, National Museums Scotland] [ref: The Hidden History of Public Executions in Edinburgh, www.escapethepast.co.uk] [ref: Site of the Last Public Execution in Edinburgh Historical Marker, www.hmdb.org]

The execution attracted a large crowd; contemporary reports describe disorderly behaviour among the spectators, including singing, drinking and fighting.
File:Post execution of George Bryce, the Ratho Murderer, by Dr John Smith.jpg|Post execution sketch of George Bryce by Dr John Smith of the Royal College of Surgeons, Edinburgh.
File:Brass tile of the site of the last public execution in Edinburgh.jpg|Commemorative plaque on the Royal Mile for the site of the execution.
File:The Death Mask of George Bryce, 1864.jpg|George Bryce death mask, from the Royal College of Surgeons of Edinburgh archives.

=== Newspaper reports ===
The Dunfermline Saturday Press of 25 June, 1864 p.4 reported: ″On making the fatal plunge, the body remained in perfect stillness for the space of about thirty seconds, after which a slight tremor of the spinal cord, a clutching of the fingers, and a slight drawing in of the foot were the only movements perceptible. There was no struggle whatsoever indicative of suffering".

The Dundee Courier of June 22nd, 1864 reported: “The body fell three feet, and entirely disappeared from the view of the public.″

The Southern Reporter of June 23rd, 1864 reported: “Only the rope being seen, the vast crowd began immediately to disappear.″

“The Times of June 22, 1864 reported: ”The executioner drew the bolt, and, with a few slight struggles, the convict expired".

== Aftermath ==
Following Bryce's arrest, Seaton's mother had reportedly been so distressed by her daughter's death that she was taken to an asylum.

Jane Seton is buried at Hope Street Cemetery, Inverkeithing. Her memorial stone reads:JANE SEATON, aged 23 years.

I know O Lord that Thy judgements are right

Into thine hand I commit my spirit, Thou hast redeemed me O Lord God of Truth, Psalm XXXI, 5.
Erected by the children to whom she was nurse as a mark of their love.George Bryce would be the last person hung in public in Edinburgh. Hanging as a form of punishment continued in Edinburgh until 1954. [ref: hiddenscotland.com]

== References ==

data.title: Lyadh
data.text:
[[File:Edward Bird (1772-1819) - Idleness - FA.246(O) - Victoria and Albert Museum.jpg|upright=1.15|thumb|Idleness by Edward Bird, –1819]]

Lyadh (Bengali: ল্যাদ) is a word or concept in Bengali that describes the act of doing nothing, being relaxed, and lazing around. [ref: Panta Bhaat: How the humble fermented rice has become a summer weekend staple for me, Wion] [ref: The ultimate A to Z Bengali dictionary, [[The Telegraph (India)] [ref: On The Occasion Of Mahalaya, Here Are A Few Ways To Celebrate Durga Puja Like A Bengali, iDiva] Depending on the context, it can be translated as 'indolence', [ref: 2024 Reporter Diaries: A laid-back Bong finds love in the languid charm of domestic cricket - Santadeep Dey, Sportstar] 'sloth', [ref: Letters to the Editor: Oxford's Word of the Year 2022, [[The Telegraph (India)] [ref: ‘Lyadh’!, Varta Trust] 'sleepiness', [ref: Why Pradipta Bhattacharya’s musical short 'LYAD' is unique?, The Times of India] or a state of inactivity. It can also refer to a state of intentional unproductivity, lackadaisicalness, getting some rest, idling around, dawdling, or procrastinating. [ref: Untranslatable Words From Languages Across India, Homegrown] [ref: Tilottama at a glance, Ukiyoto Publishing] The Bengali expression lyadh khawa (Bengali: ল্যাদ খাওয়া; literally, 'consuming laziness' [ref: Review: In Praise of Laziness and Other Essays by Indrajit Hazra, Hindustan Times]) is often used to denote the act of experiencing, indulging in, or enjoying a state of idleness and relaxation. [ref: A true-blue Bengali guide to spending a ‘productive’ weekend, [[The Telegraph (India)] [ref: Please Remove Your Shoes: A Judgmental Guide to Surviving the World and the 30 United States of India]

Lyadh is an example of an untranslatable word, due to the lexical gap that prevents it from having a perfect equivalent in other languages.

== Etymology ==
Unlike the majority of words in the Bengali language, the etymology of lyadh is uncertain. It does not find mention in traditional Bengali dictionaries, and does not appear to share any roots or cognates with Sanskrit, Persian, or Arabic. The word, used as a slang or expression in Bengali, is believed to have originated during the late 2000s–early 2010s; it is possibly a corruption or adaptation of the English words 'laidback' or 'lethargy', albeit this is speculative and remains unconfirmed. [ref: ‘ল্যাদ’ পুজো, Eisamay Online]

== Culture and use ==
In Bengali culture, lyadh is considered an emotion or a state of mind, and a certain fondness for 'laziness' has become embedded in Bengali society. [ref: Lyaad -- A universal feeling, [[The Telegraph (India)] Unlike somnolence and lethargy, which sometimes carry negative connotations and are often associated with depression, apathy and weakness, lyadh is more intentional and guilt-free, and is usually associated with joy, pleasure and recreation. It is often described as the "art of doing nothing". [ref: Kolkata to Kurseong: Of mist and lazy days, mint] Bengalis tend to link indolence and idleness with the motto, "simple living, high thinking"; according to some, this inclination, however, arguably has adversely affected Bengal's economic output and entrepreneurial ethos. [ref: Poor, Lazy and Loving It, Open Magazine]

Lyadh can indicate a plethora of situations, such as lying on one's sofa, leisurely reading a book, taking a siesta, listening to music, and gazing out one's window, among others. It is also associated with adda culture, an informal Bengali tradition involving long, casual and unstructured conversations as part of a hang-out. [ref: This Bengali ritual is a cure for loneliness, 360]

== In popular culture ==
In 2020, Lyaad, a musical short film based on the concept was released. It was directed by Pradipta Bhattacharyya and stars Ritwick Chakraborty. [ref: শীতকালটা ‘ল্যাদ’ খেয়েই কাটালেন ঋত্বিক, Anandabazar Patrika]

== Similar words ==

* The Italian expression dolce far niente (literally, 'the sweetness of doing nothing') is close in meaning to lyadh, and refers to the joy derived from being idle, slowing down, or relaxing.
* The Dutch word niksen (literally, 'nothinging' or 'doing nothing') refers to the art of doing nothing and being idle, and has been explored as a method to combat work-related health problems such as stress and burnout.

Hostino is a Moroccan web hosting and domain registration company based at Technopark Tanger in Tangier, Morocco. It was founded in 2022 by Aniss Kiassi. The company is listed by Morocco's Agence Nationale de Réglementation des Télécommunications (ANRT) as an accredited registrar for the.ma domain. data.title: Open systems theory
data.text:
----

Open systems theory (OST) is a conceptual framework for active socioecological adaptation and democratic self-management developed by the social scientists Fred Emery and Merrelyn Emery. It provides both a theoretical view of organizations and their environments and practical methods for organisational and community design and planning. It is an amalgamation of research on sociotechnical system by the Tavistock Institute of Human Relations, Ludwig von Bertalanffy's general systems theory (GST), and the conceptualisation of the environment as Causal Textures by Fred Emery and Eric Trist.

== Core concepts ==
Two concepts are central: the genotypical organizational design principles, which describe two different places where the responsibility for control and coordination lies: over the work (known as DP1) or with the people doing it (known as DP2). DP1 produces dominant hierarchies while DP2 produces self-managing groups.

The other is the ecological view in which people and their environments co-evolve, so that active adaptation requires changing the system and environment together.

==Applications==
The framework is used for organizational unified design and change, using methods like the Search Conference for strategic planning and the Participative Design Workshop to design a DP2-based organisational structure. These can be combined to form a two-stage method for active adaptation. OST has been applied in democracy programmes in both the private and public sectors, in community planning, and in a wide range of research projects.

==Reception==
Baburoğlu tracks the development of the framework from the 60s through the mid-1990s. Mike Jackson places OST within the wider systems thinking tradition. OST methods are also treated in surveys of Dialogic Organization Development.

== See also ==

* Sociotechnical system
* Tavistock Institute
* Fred Emery
* Merrelyn Emery
* Eric Trist

[ref: Emery, F. E. & Trist, E. L. (1965). [https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/001872676501800103 "The Causal Texture of Organizational Environments"]. Human Relations. 18 (1): 21–32..]

data.title: Chinmay Pandya
data.text:
Chinmay Pandya (born 9 April 1976) is an Indian psychiatrist, educationist, and academic administrator serving as the Pro Vice-Chancellor (Vice-President) of Dev Sanskriti Vishwavidyalaya (DSVV) in Haridwar, Uttarakhand. He represents the All World Gayatri Pariwar (AWGP), an organization founded by his grandfather, Shriram Sharma Acharya. His work and public engagements span psychiatric medicine, yoga, Indian knowledge systems, interfaith dialogue, and the ethical governance of artificial intelligence.

== Early life and education ==
Pandya was born on 9 April 1976 in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, India. He grew up at Shantikunj, the global headquarters of the All World Gayatri Pariwar in Haridwar.

He pursued medical studies at the Himalayan Institute of Medical Sciences in Dehradun, graduating with a Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) degree. He later moved to the United Kingdom for postgraduate psychiatric training, earning a postgraduate diploma in Public Health and obtaining Membership of the Royal College of Psychiatrists (MRCPsych).

== Medical career ==
Between 2002 and 2010, Pandya worked within the United Kingdom's National Health Service (NHS) across various psychiatric posts. His concluding clinical appointment was as an associate specialist in older adult psychiatric services at West London Mental Health Trust, focusing on the diagnosis and management of neurocognitive disorders, including Alzheimer's disease and other dementias.

In 2010, he relocated to India to join the leadership and voluntary initiatives of Dev Sanskriti Vishwavidyalaya and All World Gayatri Pariwar in Haridwar.

== Academic leadership and institutional roles ==
Pandya serves as the Pro Vice-Chancellor / Vice-President of Dev Sanskriti Vishwavidyalaya (DSVV), overseeing academic policy development, interdisciplinary curriculums, and global academic partnerships.

=== Academic and editorial work ===

* Editor of Dev Sanskriti: Interdisciplinary International Journal, an academic journal covering Indian philosophy, psychology, education, and Ayurveda.
* Chairperson and co-founder of the Centre for Baltic Culture and Studies at DSVV.
* Chairperson of the South Asian Institute of Peace and Reconciliation (SAIPR), established at DSVV in partnership with the University of Winchester.
* Founder Patron and Board of Founders member at Rishihood University.

=== Government and advisory committees ===
Pandya has served on several national statutory and advisory bodies in India, including:

* Governing Body of the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR).
* Advisory Council of the Ministry of Ayush.
* Syllabus restructuring committee of the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE).
* Board of Trustees of the India Development Foundation of Overseas Indians.
* General Council of the National Culture Fund under the Ministry of Culture.

== Representation and public engagements ==
As a senior representative of the All World Gayatri Pariwar, Pandya represents the organisation at national and international forums on youth development, social reform, and cultural preservation. [ref: Three Jyoti Kalash Chariots depart from Shantikunj to spread message of centenary celebrations, ANI News] [ref: Gayatri Parivar's Jyoti Kalash chariots begin yatra for centenary, Asianet Newsable] [ref: Three Jyoti Kalash Chariots depart from Shantikunj to spread message of centenary celebrations, Lokmat Times]

=== International engagements and interfaith dialogue ===
Pandya has addressed global conferences on cultural dialogue, spirituality, and peacebuilding:

* Addressed discussions at the United Nations Office at Vienna and UNESCO forums concerning intangible cultural heritage.
* Attended the COP24 climate summit and delivered guest lectures at various global institutions including the University of Cambridge, as well as Indian institutes such as the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs), and Bhabha Atomic Research Centre.
* Serves as a director of the Global Covenant of Religions and participated in the Parliamentary Conferences on Interfaith Dialogue in Marrakesh (Morocco) and Rome (Italy).

=== Artificial intelligence and ethics ===
Pandya has been active in international consultations focusing on the ethical governance of artificial intelligence (AI):

* In July 2024, participated in the interfaith summit "AI Ethics for Peace: World Religions Commit to the Rome Call" in Hiroshima, Japan.
* Appointed as an Associate member of the AI Faith and Civil Society Commission in Abu Dhabi.
* Speaker at the India AI Impact Summit in New Delhi (February 2026) and chaired discussions on AI and democratic governance.
* In July 2026, contributed to panels during UN-affiliated events in Geneva, including the Geneva Centre for Security Policy session on extreme AI risks and the ITU's AI for Good Global Summit.
* Member of the HumAIn Capital's Global South Leadership Council on responsible AI.

=== Yoga and wellness ===

* Served as Vice-President of the Indian Yoga Association.
* Chairperson of the International Festival of Yoga, Culture and Spirituality organized by DSVV.
* Speaker at the International Yoga Festival in Rishikesh, addressing psychological well-being and contemplative practices.

== Awards and recognitions ==

* Bharat Gaurav Award (2023): Presented at the Palace of Westminster, London.
* Civic Honour from Wrocław: Awarded by the City of Wrocław, Poland, for advancing cultural and academic cooperation.
* Vivekananda International Relations Peace Award (2024): Conferred by the Tarpan Foundation in Mumbai for educational and intercultural initiatives.
* Karma Yoga Honour (2025): Conferred by the Hindu Spiritual Care Institute, California.

=== Jury and international appointments ===

* Served on the international judging panel for the Templeton Prize for three consecutive years.
* Appointed to the judging committee of the King Hamad Award for Peaceful Coexistence in Bahrain.
* Honorary member of the Senate of the University of Latvia.

== Personal life ==
Pandya is the son of Pranav Pandya and Sailbala Pandya. He is married to Shefali Pandya, and they have two children.

data.title: College of Engineering Technology Janzour
data.text:
The College of Engineering Technology - Janzour (CETJ; ) is a public technical higher-education institution in Janzour, Libya. The college assumed its current institutional status in 2010, when the Higher Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Professions - Janzour was reorganized as the College of Engineering Technology - Janzour. [ref: الكليات التقنية, National Center for Quality Assurance and Accreditation of Educational and Training Institutions] The National Center for Quality Assurance and Accreditation of Educational and Training Institutions lists the college among Libya's recognized governmental technical colleges. [ref: المؤسسات الحكومية المعترف بها, National Center for Quality Assurance and Accreditation of Educational and Training Institutions]

The college provides technical engineering education through five academic departments and also offers postgraduate study in engineering fields. [ref: نبذة عن الكلية, College of Engineering Technology - Janzour]

== History ==
Technical and industrial education at Janzour predates the establishment of the present college. The college traces its educational antecedents to the Nasser El-Din Al-Qummi Institute, an industrial technical institution in Janzour. According to the college's institutional history, the institute was established in 1957 to provide industrial technical education and was authorized to award intermediate diplomas.

In 1989, the antecedent institution was authorized to award higher diplomas. The institution immediately preceding the present college was the Higher Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Professions - Janzour. Libya's National Center for Quality Assurance and Accreditation of Educational and Training Institutions records the transition from the Higher Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Professions - Janzour to the College of Engineering Technology - Janzour in 2010.

In 2010, the college was authorized to award technical bachelor's degrees. In 2016, it received authorization under Decision No. 734 to offer master's-level postgraduate study in mechanical and industrial engineering.

== Academics ==
The college is organized into five academic departments:
* Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering
* Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering
* Department of Chemical and Environmental Engineering
* Department of Petroleum Operations Engineering
* Department of Computer Technology Engineering

The departments provide technical bachelor's degree education in engineering and technology fields. The college also offers postgraduate engineering study.

== Student life ==
The college hosts an active student chapter of the Society of Petroleum Engineers (SPE Chapter 6415). This international affiliation provides engineering students with academic networking opportunities, industry resources, and professional development within the global oil and gas sector. [ref: College of Engineering Technology - Janzour Chapter, Society of Petroleum Engineers]

== Research and publishing ==
The college publishes the Libya Journal of Applied Sciences and Technology (LJAST), a peer-reviewed, biannual academic journal covering engineering, applied sciences, technology and interdisciplinary research. [ref: About the Journal, Libya Journal of Applied Sciences and Technology] The Libyan Electronic Directory of Scientific Journals lists the College of Engineering Technology - Janzour as the journal's publishing institution. [ref: الدليل الليبي الإلكتروني للمجلات العلمية, الدليل الليبي الإلكتروني للمجلات العلمية]

The college also acts as a key academic organizer and participant in national scientific conferences, including the International Renewable Energy, Gas, Oil, and Climate Change (IREGO) Conference and Exhibition. [ref: IREGO Conference Committees, IREGO Conference and Exhibition]

== Identifiers ==
The college is registered in the Research Organization Registry (ROR) under the identifier [https://ror.org/02str6y02 02str6y02]. [ref: College Of Engineering Technology Janzour, Research Organization Registry]

data.title: Syed Muhammad Ali Naqvi
data.text:
Shaheed Dr Syed Muhammad Ali Naqvi (28 September 1952 – 07 March 1995) was a prominent Pakistani Shia leader, medical practitioner, and community organizer from Lahore. He is widely recognized as the principal founder of the Imamia Students Organization (ISO) Pakistan, the largest student organization for Shia youth in Pakistan. [ref: Rieck, Andreas. The Shia of Pakistan: An Assertive Minority. Oxford University Press, 2015, pp. 214–225. ISBN 978-0190240967.] [ref: Khan, Tasleem Raza. Safeer-e-Inqilab: Biography of Shaheed Dr. Muhammad Ali Naqvi. Youth Progressive Publications, 2002.] He was also a key figure in the formation of Tehreek-e-Jafaria Pakistan (TJP) and a close associate of Allama Arif Hussain Hussaini. He played an instrumental role in shaping Shia student activism, anti-imperialist awareness, and socio-religious reforms in Pakistan. [ref: Fuchs, Simon Wolfgang. Inverted World: Shi'i Thought and Activism in Modern South Asia. Harvard University Press, 2019, pp. 165–170. ISBN 978-0674980792.] [ref: ISO founder Dr Naqvi remembered, Dawn]

== Early life and education ==
Dr. Syed Muhammad Ali Naqvi was born in Ali Raza Abad, Lahore on 28 September 1952. He received his early education in Lahore and spent parts of his childhood in East Africa, where his father served as a preacher. [ref: Khan, Tasleem Raza. Safeer-e-Inqilab: Biography of Shaheed Dr. Muhammad Ali Naqvi. Youth Progressive Publications, 2002.] He completed his higher secondary education at Government College, Lahore before enrolling at King Edward Medical University, where he earned his Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) degree. [ref: ISO founder Dr Naqvi remembered, Dawn]

== Founding of ISO Pakistan and activism ==
On 22 May 1972, while studying at King Edward Medical College, Dr. Naqvi alongside fellow Shia students founded the Imamia Students Organization (ISO Pakistan) to unify Shia youth, promote religious literacy, and provide educational and social assistance. [ref: Remembering Dr Muhammad Ali Naqvi: Tribute paid to ISO founder, The Express Tribune] Under his leadership, ISO grew into a nationwide network across Pakistani universities, colleges, and schools. [ref: Dr Naqvi remembered on anniversary, The Nation]

He was a staunch follower of Ruhollah Khomeini and the ideology of the Islamic Revolution, advocating for Islamic unity and social justice while actively organizing anti-imperialist rallies and educational workshops across the country. [ref: Fuchs, Simon Wolfgang. Inverted World: Shi'i Thought and Activism in Modern South Asia. Harvard University Press, 2019, pp. 165–170. ISBN 978-0674980792.]

== Political activism and major events ==
During his student life and medical practice, Dr. Muhammad Ali Naqvi was deeply involved in grassroots political organizing and public mobilizations in Pakistan:

* 1980 Islamabad Demonstration: In July 1980, when the Shia community organized a massive sit-in in Islamabad against Zakat and Ushr Ordinance enforcement under General Zia-ul-Haq's regime, Dr. Naqvi played a crucial role on the ground in organizing logistics, student volunteers, and medical first-aid teams. [ref: Rieck, Andreas. The Shia of Pakistan: An Assertive Minority. Oxford University Press, 2015, pp. 214–225. ISBN 978-0190240967.]
* Formation of Tehreek-e-Jafaria (TJP): Dr. Naqvi was key in connecting student activism with national religious leadership, working closely with Allama Arif Hussain Hussaini to organize political awareness rallies across Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa during the 1980s. [ref: Fuchs, Simon Wolfgang. Inverted World: Shi'i Thought and Activism in Modern South Asia. Harvard University Press, 2019, pp. 165–170. ISBN 978-0674980792.]
* Establishing Free Healthcare: Alongside political rallies, he operated healthcare clinics and free medical outreach programs in Lahore for underprivileged communities. [ref: Khan, Tasleem Raza. Safeer-e-Inqilab: Biography of Shaheed Dr. Muhammad Ali Naqvi. Youth Progressive Publications, 2002.]

== Death ==
On 7 March 1995, Dr. Syed Muhammad Ali Naqvi was assassinated at Yateem Khana Chowk in Lahore. [ref: Remembering Dr Muhammad Ali Naqvi: Tribute paid to ISO founder, The Express Tribune] He was laid to rest in his ancestral cemetery at Ali Raza Abad, Lahore. [ref: Dr Naqvi remembered on anniversary, The Nation]

== References ==

data.title: Daddy B. Nice
data.text:
Daddy B. Nice is the pseudonym for Bruno Niceswanger (born November 2, 1946), an American writer and music critic who according to The Village Voice indispensably chronicles, reviews, and aggregates Southern Soul music's subculture from the inside. [ref: Southern Soul Guide: Sweet Angel, Mel Waiters, and Luther Lackey, The Village Voice] In 2005, he launched the website SouthernSoulRnB.com with the determination to "spread the word" about the genre of music. [ref: An Apostle for Southern Soul, Jackson Free Press] The Jackson Free Press has called Daddy B. Nice "The Apostle of Southern Soul," [ref: An Apostle for Southern Soul, Jackson Free Press] and Jefferson Blues Magazine has described him as "The Southern Soul Oracle." [ref: STEVIE J / KÌNG GEORGE / SUMMER WOLFE / CURT THE COUNTRYMAN ft. COUNTRYBOII TYE, Jefferson Blues Magazine] Before his work in music criticism, he was an editor for underground newspapers and a participant in radical student activism at the University of Northern Iowa in the 1960s, and later published articles as a freelance journalist in Boulder, CO. [ref: An Apostle for Southern Soul, Jackson Free Press] [ref: The Crest of the High Wave: Radical Studnets and the Underground Press at UNI, Midwestern Marx Institute] [ref: Showdown in Boulder: Tate, Fuller and civic pride, The Rocky Mountain News]

== Early life, writings, and underground press ==

Niceswanger was born in Carroll, Iowa on November 2, 1946. [ref: An Apostle for Southern Soul, Jackson Free Press] While attending the University of Northern Iowa in 1965, he published a poem titled "The Way Bruno Feels About Writing" in the literary review Midwest. [ref: The Way Bruno Feels About Writing, Scholarworks.uni.edu] He was given an award and named an outstanding journalist by the university in 1966. [ref: Awards given to outstanding SCI journalists, IndexUNI] In 1968, he was recruited by publisher Doug Warrington to edit Campus Underground, an underground newspaper based in Cedar Falls, Iowa that Warrington had aspired to make a national newspaper. [ref: Everything You Ever Wanted To Know About The Primer, Index UNI] [ref: The Crest of the High Wave: Radical Studnets and the Underground Press at UNI, Midwestern Marx Institute] Niceswanger was chosen to be the first editor after a search among interested students in the three Iowa state universities. [ref: Everything You Ever Wanted To Know About The Primer, Index UNI] When that publication folded due to financial issues, he edited its successor, The New Prairie Primer, from 1969 to 1970. [ref: The Crest of the High Wave: Radical Studnets and the Underground Press at UNI, Midwestern Marx Institute]

The first issue of the The New Prairie Primer featured a highly popular, multi-page article by Niceswanger covering his experience of going to the Woodstock Music & Art Festival titled "Going Up to Meat County." [ref: The Crest of the High Wave: Radical Studnets and the Underground Press at UNI, Midwestern Marx Institute] [ref: Everything You Ever Wanted To Know About The Primer, Index UNI] In the wake of the success of the first issue, the Primer received enough donations to make their second issue about the Vietnam War, free to readers. The Vietnam issue featured the first publication anywhere of the entire list of Iowa's war dead, and featured a story by UNI student, Dick Simpson, who was under indictment for refusing induction into the armed forces. [ref: Everything You Ever Wanted To Know About The Primer, Index UNI] [ref: Underground Newspaper In Circulation Under New Name, Index UNI] The second issue of the Primer also brought attention to the notable cooperation that was happening between the anti-war hippies of the radical left and various statewide church ministries. [ref: The Crest of the High Wave: Radical Studnets and the Underground Press at UNI, Midwestern Marx Institute] The paper did receive support from the United Christian Ministry and was headquartered in the basement of the Bethany House, which caused some community opposition. [ref: Everything You Ever Wanted To Know About The Primer, Index UNI] [ref: Underground Newspaper In Circulation Under New Name, Index UNI]

During his time as an editor, he participated in radical student activism, including the anti-Vietnam war movement and protests related to the "UNI7." [ref: The Crest of the High Wave: Radical Studnets and the Underground Press at UNI, Midwestern Marx Institute] In 1970, he edited a tabloid exposé titled "Special Report: The Military-Industrial Complex in Iowa," detailing defense contracts held by local companies. [ref: Campus Underground [with] The New Prairie Primer (12 issues) [with] Special Report: The Military-Industrial Complex in Iowa, AbeBooks] [ref: The Crest of the High Wave: Radical Studnets and the Underground Press at UNI, Midwestern Marx Institute] Niceswanger also published "The Conspiracy To Undermine The Freaks" in The North American Review in 1969, which analyzed the systemic harassment of the counterculture. [ref: The Conspiracy to Undermine the Freaks, The North American Review] Sometime in the mid-1970s, Niceswanger moved to Boulder, CO, and as a free-lance writer was published in the regional newspaper, The Rocky Mountain News. [ref: Showdown in Boulder: Tate, Fuller and civic pride, The Rocky Mountain News]

== Southern Soul advocacy ==

Daddy B. Nice became interested in Southern Soul and the music of the Chitlin' Circuit in the late 1990s while traveling through the Deep South. [ref: An Apostle for Southern Soul, Jackson Free Press] He began recording songs from local radio stations on a portable recorder, particularly the Jackson, Mississippi station WMPR-FM. [ref: An Apostle for Southern Soul, Jackson Free Press] Nice became determined to spread awareness about the genre, and invested heavily in computer equipment, and spent 2 years learning the code and programming necessary for a website. [ref: An Apostle for Southern Soul, Jackson Free Press] In 2005, he launched SouthernSoulRnB.com to promote what he described as "today's extension of classic rhythm and blues." [ref: An Apostle for Southern Soul, Jackson Free Press] The website aims to provide a platform for an entire generation of black rhythm and blues artists who have matured in obscurity and are largely overlooked or marginalized by mainstream media. [ref: The Website the Southern Soul Professionals Read, Southern Soul RnB]

== Style and influence ==

The Village Voice has called his website an "indispensable" aggregator of the southern soul subculture. [ref: Southern Soul Guide: Sweet Angel, Mel Waiters, and Luther Lackey, The Village Voice] Music journalists and performers use his reporting to track scene updates, such as artist news, concert dates, and obituaries. [ref: Q&A with electrifying singer Val McKnight - a mixture of Gospel, Soul and Blues with a raw back in the day Mississippi flavor, Blues.GR] [ref: Daddy B Nice - 2019: The Year In Southern Soul, Jefferson Blues Magazine] The Swedish publication Jefferson Blues Magazine has described Daddy B. Nice as "The Southern Soul Oracle." [ref: STEVIE J / KÌNG GEORGE / SUMMER WOLFE / CURT THE COUNTRYMAN ft. COUNTRYBOII TYE, Jefferson Blues Magazine] Dylann DeAnna, aka Blues Critic, owner of CDS Records and the longrunning website SoulBluesMusic.com has deemed Daddy B. Nice's website, "The definitive guide to Southern Soul!" [ref: Looking For More Info On Southern Soul?, Soul Blues Music]

His website includes monthly top 10 charts and annual "Year of Southern Soul" rankings. [ref: An Apostle for Southern Soul, Jackson Free Press] These rankings cover 15 categories, including "Best Album," "Best Male/Female Artist," and "Best Producer." [ref: Daddy B Nice - 2019: The Year In Southern Soul, Jefferson Blues Magazine]

A signature element of Nice's work is the use of his own original, hand-drawn sketches of musicians instead of promotional photographs. This style choice was based on the art seen in The New Yorker magazine. [ref: An Apostle for Southern Soul, Jackson Free Press]

== References ==

data.title: Ashirbek Muminov
data.text:
Ashirbek Kurbanovich Muminov (Kazakh: Әшірбек Құрбанұлы Муминов; born 18 July 1959) is a historian specializing in medieval Islam in Central Asia. His research includes Hanafi scholarship, Islamic manuscripts and the history of Islamic education.⁠[1]⁠[2]⁠[10]

= Early life and education =
Muminov grew up in Tashkent and attended Secondary School No. 1, where he studied Arabic from the second grade. He completed school in 1976 with a gold medal.⁠[1]⁠[10]

He entered the Arabic section of the Faculty of Oriental Languages at Tashkent State University in 1976 and graduated with honours in 1982. He qualified as an Arabic philologist and a teacher of Arabic and English languages and literature.⁠[7]

From 1987 to 1990, he undertook postgraduate research at the Leningrad branch of the Institute of Oriental Studies of the USSR Academy of Sciences under Stanislav Mikhailovich Prozorov. He defended his Candidate of Historical Sciences dissertation in Leningrad on 29 March 1991. It examined al-Kafawi’s Kata’ib a‘lam al-akhyar as a source for the history of Islam in Transoxiana.⁠[7] [ref: ИВР РАН (Санкт-Петербург) - Personalia, www.orientalstudies.ru]

On 24 June 2003, he defended his Doctor of Historical Sciences dissertation at Tashkent Islamic University. The study examined the significance of Hanafi scholars in the urban life of central Transoxiana.⁠[7]

= Academic career =
Muminov began his research career in 1982 at the Abu Rayhan Beruni Institute of Oriental Studies in Tashkent, working in the department responsible for source studies and cataloguing Oriental manuscripts. Detailed biographical accounts record research employment in 1982–1985 and 1990–1991.⁠[10] [ref: Ташкент-Алматы-Астана-Стамбул: Путь исламоведа, Qojalar.kz]

From 1991 to 1993, he headed the Department of Oriental Philology at Ahmed Yasawi University in Turkestan.⁠[10] He was an associate professor in the Department of Islamic Studies at Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies from 1993 to 2005.⁠[8] [ref: ]

In 2005, he became deputy director of the R. B. Suleymenov Institute of Oriental Studies in Almaty, serving until 2013.⁠[8]⁠[10] From 2013 to 2016, he headed the Department of Religious Studies at L. N. Gumilyov Eurasian National University in Astana.⁠[8] In 2016, IRCICA identified him as consultant to its director general on Central Asian studies.⁠[2] [ref: ]

= International research appointments =
In 1998, Muminov was a visiting professor in the Fourth Section of the École pratique des hautes études (EPHE), at the Sorbonne in Paris, working with F. Déroche. He returned to the institution in 2002 as a visiting professor in its Fifth Section, working with D. Aigle.⁠[8]

The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation records a research fellowship at Ruhr University Bochum, hosted by Stefan Reichmuth, with sponsorship beginning on 1 October 1999. Muminov’s CV dates the research visit to 1999–2001.⁠[8]⁠[9]

In 2006, he was a visiting scholar at Indiana University, researching Islamization and sacred genealogies in Central Asia. He also held a visiting professorship at Zentrum Moderner Orient in Berlin in 2011.⁠[8]

He was a Fulbright Visiting Scholar at Indiana University Bloomington from September 2011 to June 2012. From September 2012 to June 2013, he held a senior fellowship at Koç University’s Research Center for Anatolian Civilizations in Istanbul.⁠[8]

In April–June 2015, he was a visiting scholar at Nanjing University in China.⁠[8]

= Research =
From 2001 to 2008, he participated in the “Manuscript heritage of Central Asia” project at CNRS in Paris, directed by Maria Szuppe. He subsequently participated in the project “Manuscript traditions of Iran, India and Central Asia” (2009–2012), directed by Szuppe and Nalini Balbir.⁠[8]

Muminov collaborated with Bakhtiyar Babadjanov and Anke von Kügelgen on the 2007 volume Disputes on Muslim Authority in Central Asia (20th Century). The collection presents texts documenting religious debates in Soviet Central Asia. In a 2008 review, Canat Mahaşeva discussed its use of manuscripts and printed works preserved in private collections.⁠[4] [ref: (XX.yy. Orta Asya Müslüman Din Adamlarýnýn Polemikleri: Kritik Edisyon ve Kaynak Araþtýrmasý),, Ankara Üniversitesi İlahiyat Fakültesi Dergisi]

He also conducted research with Devin DeWeese on the Islamization of Central Asia and sacred lineages, published in the two-volume work Islamization and Sacred Lineages in Central Asia (2008 and 2013).

He co-edited Saduaqas Ghïlmani’s biographical collection with Allen Frank and Aitzhan Nurmanova. Published by IRCICA in 2018, the two-volume edition contains the Arabic-script Kazakh text and an English translation.⁠[5] In 2026, he edited Galiya Kambarbekova’s catalogue of Turkic manuscripts in Kazakhstan’s National Library.⁠[6] [ref: Biographies of the Islamic Scholars of Our Times, shop.ircica.org]

= Recognition =
In 2016, his book Hanafi Madhhab in the History of Central Asia won first place in the Islam category of the regional Book of the Year competition for Russian-language scholarship on Islam and Iran. The award was presented on 1 December 2016.⁠[3] [ref: ]

= Languages =
His CV lists Kazakh, Uzbek and Russian as native languages, and Arabic, Turkish and English as fluent languages. It also records reading knowledge of German, French, Persian and the Turkic languages of Central Asia.⁠[8]

data.title: Yamamoto Kakuyoshi
data.text:
----

Yamamoto Kakuyoshi (山本角義, March 3, 1914 – January 30, 1982) was a Japanese martial artist.
He was a direct disciple of Takeda Sōkaku, the reviver of Daitō-ryū Aiki-jūjutsu, and the founder of Mugenshintō-ryū Iaijutsu. [ref: 合気、その源流山本角義伝, 月刊秘伝] [ref: [https://www.aikidosangenkai.org/blog/aiki-rentai-conditioned-body-yukiyoshi-sagawa-part-2/ Aiki Sangenkai – "Aiki Rentai: The Conditioned Body of Yukiyoshi Sagawa (Part 2)"], retrieved 2025.]

== Biography ==
Yamamoto was born in Akita Prefecture under the name Yamamoto Tumekichi (山本留吉).
While working as a cook, he met Takeda Sōkaku in 1937, when the latter frequented the restaurant where Yamamoto was employed. Yamamoto soon began training under Takeda.

According to Takeda's records, Yamamoto formally enrolled in Daitō-ryū in 1941. That same year, he received the Hiden Okugi no Koto certificate, and in 1942 he was licensed as kyōju dairi (teaching representative).
Takeda Sōkaku died in 1943, making Yamamoto the final disciple to receive such formal recognition. For this reason, he is often described as the “last student” of Takeda—not simply in terms of chronology, but as the last to have mastered the art to the level of advanced transmission. [ref: Stanley Pranin, Conversations with Daitō-ryū Masters, p. 184 (Seigo Okamoto interview).]

After World War II, Yamamoto lived in Hakodate, Hokkaidō, and later established the Jūshinkan Dōjō in Tomakomai, Hokkaidō. There he taught:
* Daitō-ryū Aiki-jūjutsu (Yamamoto-ha)
* Mugenshintō-ryū Iaijutsu (sword drawing / real-sword methods)
* Ono-ha Ittō-ryū kenjutsu as transmitted through the Aizu domain [ref: [https://calgaryrakushinkan.com/mugenshinto-ryu Calgary Rakushinkan – Mugenshintō-ryū page]]

== Mugenshintō-ryū Iaijutsu ==
Yamamoto is credited with creating the style known as Mugenshintō-ryū Iaijutsu (無限神刀流居合術). [ref: [https://calgaryrakushinkan.com/mugenshinto-ryu Calgary Rakushinkan – Mugenshintō-ryū page]]
The system drew on Yamamoto's training in Ono-ha Ittō-ryū kenjutsu under Takeda, combined with the principles of Daitō-ryū Aiki-jūjutsu. Its practice centers on sword-drawing (iai) with an emphasis on real-sword methods (shinken tōhō), integrating sword and unarmed principles into a unified pedagogy.

The creation of Mugenshintō-ryū represented a continuation of Takeda's efforts to connect the sword traditions of Aizu with the aiki-based body methods of Daitō-ryū. The school has been transmitted through Yamamoto's successors, and remains part of the curriculum at branches of the Yamamoto-ha lineage. [ref: [https://webhiden.jp/master/yamamoto_kakuyoshi/ Web Hiden – "Yamamoto Kakuyoshi"]]

== Legacy and continuation ==

The Jūshinkan dōjō, founded by Yamamoto Kakuyoshi, continues to operate in Japan. [ref: [https://jushinkan.shin-gen.jp/ "柔進館 流派／伝承系譜／理念" – Jūshinkan official website]]
It is affiliated with the Shintō Jūshin Kai (神刀柔進会), an organization that maintains Yamamoto's martial legacy. The group emphasizes preserving what Yamamoto and his teacher Takeda Sōkaku regarded as the core of Daitō-ryū Aiki-jūjutsu—its grounding in bujutsu (martial techniques) and its orientation toward protection without unnecessary injury. [ref: [https://daito-ryu.jp/ Shintō Jūshin Kai official website]]

Martial arts historian Stanley Pranin recorded references to Yamamoto in his book Conversations with Daitō-ryū Masters. Katsuyuki Kondō stated that he studied with Yamamoto for two days in 1972. [ref: Stanley Pranin, Conversations with Daitō-ryū Masters, p. 165.]
Seigo Okamoto recalled participating in a demonstration with Yamamoto, referring to him as “the last student of Sokaku Sensei” and remembering his distinctive sword drawing methods. [ref: Stanley Pranin, Conversations with Daitō-ryū Masters, p. 184.]
Yamamoto is also mentioned in Kondō’s book Daitō-ryū Aikijūjutsu Hiden Mokuroku Ikkajo (p. 33).
Yamamoto is discussed in Satō Kinbei's 1991 memoir "Jū to Ken to Dō", where he is described as Takeda Sōkaku's “last disciple” and as an active participant in postwar Daitō-ryū demonstrations. Satō recounts correspondence with Yamamoto and cites him as a source regarding Takeda's training methods. [ref: 林檎プロモーション]

data.title: Ashendye
data.text:
----

Ashendye (Amharic: አሸንድዬ) is a religious festival celebrated in Lasta, Lalibela, and Gondar of the Amhara region of Ethiopia. [ref: Bete Amhara: A Journey Through Wollo’s Living Heritage, Landscapes, and Seasonal Festivals, Rex Clarke Adventures] In different localities of Amhara, the festival is also known as Shadey (ሻደይ) or Solel (ሶለል). It explicitly commemorates the Old Testament story of Moses and the reed basket in which he was saved. In contrast, Ashenda in Tigray (ኣሸንዳ) is a secularized civic festival that centers on female social autonomy, gendered freedom, and modern regional political expression. [ref: Tigrayans in North Texas preserve culture, tradition through Ashenda, a day to honor women, www.keranews.org/]

== Historical and Cultural Roots ==

The Amhara highlands of Bete Amhara and Gondar serve as the foundational cradle of the Ashendye festival due to the region's ancient roots in early Jewish tradition. [ref: Falasha anthology, New Haven, Conn.; London: Yale University Press] This deep Hebraic heritage is preserved through the historic use of the Tabot (Ark covenant replica) ceremony. This celebration predates the Aksumite Christian era and goes back before the spread of Christianity.

Girls participating in Ashendye traditionally wear fresh green Cyperus sedge grass, known as Ashenda (Amharic: አሸንዳ), woven and tied around their waist. This grass is prepared as a thick, layered belt or skirt and serves as one of the festival's most recognizable elements.

Within this historical framework, the connection centers on the symbolism of the reed basket. In Amhara tradition, the primary reason young women weave and wear the native green Cyperus sedge grass around their waists is to symbolise the papyrus reed basket that saved the infant Moses on the Nile. According to the Old Testament narrative, Moses's mother placed him in a basket hidden among the reeds of the Nile River to protect him from Pharaoh's decree. The fresh river grass used in the festival acts as a living monument to this biblical event of preservation and divine protection. [ref: Travels to discover the source of the Nile, in the years 1768, 1769, 1770, 1771, 1772, and 1773, Edinburgh, Printed by J. Ruthven, for G. G. J. and J. Robinson, London]

data.title: Highly Optimized Object-oriented Many-particle Dynamics
data.text:
[https://hoomd-blue.readthedocs.io/en/v7.1.2/ HOOMD-blue] (Highly Optimized Object-oriented Many-particle Dynamics—blue edition) is a general-purpose particle simulation engine designed primarily for nano- and colloidal-scale modeling. It serves the scientific purpose of probing the structure, dynamics, and self-assembly of complex matter. The software executes on single or multi-core central processing units (CPUs) as well as graphics processing unit (GPU) hardware architectures. Its principal research fields focus on soft matter physics, polymers, colloids, self-assembly, and active matter. [ref: HOOMD-blue: A Python package for high-performance molecular dynamics and hard particle Monte Carlo simulations, Computational Materials Science] It is also enlisted in the list of different tools for molecular modelling in the table.

== History and development ==
Development began in March 2007 at Iowa State University to explore the computational potential of graphics processing units for coarse-grained polymer simulations. The initial implementation achieved accelerated execution using C++ and CUDA code targeting single NVIDIA GPUs. In published benchmark evaluations, single-GPU execution produced computational performance comparable to approximately 30 CPU cores for equivalent benchmark systems. [ref: General purpose molecular dynamics simulations fully implemented on graphics processing units, Journal of Computational Physics] In August 2008, HOOMD was released as open-source software. Shortly after, developers added a high-level Python scripting interface, transforming HOOMD-blue into an extensible Python package that integrates natively into the scientific Python ecosystem. [ref: HOOMD-blue version 3.0 A Modern, Extensible, Flexible, Object-Oriented API for Molecular Simulations, SciPy 2020]

== Capabilities ==
HOOMD-blue supports molecular dynamics (MD) simulations in constant-volume (NVE, NVT) and constant-pressure (NPT, NPH) thermodynamic ensembles. For particle motion, the software provides separate equations of motion, including Langevin, Brownian, and overdamped dynamics. It evaluates interaction potentials such as short-range pair cutoffs, angular or dihedral force fields, embedded-atom method (EAM) potentials, and Finnis-Sinclair (FS) metallic terms. [ref: Implementation of metal-friendly EAM/FS-type semi-empirical potentials in HOOMD-blue: A GPU-accelerated molecular dynamics software, Journal of Computational Physics] Additionally, the Hard Particle Monte Carlo (HPMC) framework supports two-dimensional and three-dimensional simulations in constant-volume (NVT) and constant-pressure (NPT) ensembles. [ref: Scalable Metropolis Monte Carlo for simulation of hard shapes, Computer Physics Communications] Supported HPMC shape classes include disks, spheres, convex polygons, concave polyhedra, spheropolygons, and ellipsoids. The high-level Python interface completely decouples simulation setup, particle initialization, and control loops from the low-level compiled backend.

== Architecture and performance ==
The engine pairs a user-facing Python API with a compiled C++/CUDA backend optimized for hardware execution. While early versions were restricted to single-GPU workstations, the engine transitioned to distributed-memory execution using spatial MPI domain decomposition. This spatial decomposition divides the global simulation box across multiple parallel processor targets. Performance evaluations demonstrate scaling across parallel supercomputing architectures. For molecular dynamics, published benchmark studies tested simulations on up to 3,375 GPUs and systems containing as many as 108 million particles. [ref: Strong scaling of general-purpose molecular dynamics simulations on GPUs, Computer Physics Communications] For Hard Particle Monte Carlo simulations, multi-GPU scaling tests demonstrated performance across up to 2,048 GPUs for systems containing 16.8 million hard polyhedra.

== Distribution and licensing ==
HOOMD-blue is distributed as open-source software under the permissive BSD 3-Clause licence, which permits free use, modification, and redistribution. [ref: License - HOOMD-blue 7.1.2 documentation, hoomd-blue.readthedocs.io] The source code repository, documentation, and user tutorials are publicly hosted online. Researchers can extend the software by writing separately compiled C++ and Python plugins. This plugin system allows developers to introduce custom pair forces, novel particle shapes, constraint algorithms, and external potential fields without modifying the core codebase.

data.title: Leaveland
data.text:
Leaveland is a metropolitan outdoor leisure brand originating from Milan, Italy. In the early 1950s, Whitaman Hill, a Canadian-Italian, inherited his father's Emil shoe store in Milan, Italy. The brand was established in Milan, Italy, in 1952. [ref: 嘉隆商贸获意大利枫叶中国区独家运营权]

== History ==
In 1970, Leaveland established its base in Italy and gradually expanded into other European countries, as well as the Canadian and U.S. markets in North America. In 1982, Leaveland began entering the Asian market, first launching in Hong Kong, and over the next decade, expanded into markets across the Asia-Pacific region, including Malaysia, Japan, Singapore, South Korea, and Australia. In 1990, Leaveland officially entered China and became the sponsor of the Chinese delegation for the 1990 Beijing Asian Games. In 1992, Leaveland provided sponsorship to the Chinese Football Association, with its products designated as the official products of the association. Through market expansion, it has now secured a certain market share in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and the East China region. In 2017, Leaveland was appointed by Maple Leaf International Investment Co., Ltd. as the sole authorized Maple Leaf International Commercial Co., Ltd. for global brand management and operations, specializing in footwear, apparel, leather goods, socks, and underwear.

data.title: KinitoPET
data.text:
----

KinitoPET is a 2024 psychological horror video game developed by troy_en. It was released to steam on January 9th, 2024. The game is presented as an early-2000s virtual desktop assistant named Kinito, an axolotl who interacts directly with the player's computer. The game combines metafiction, simulated desktop interaction, and psychological horror.

==Gameplay==
The game takes place through a simulated desktop interface where the player interacts with Kinito, a virtual assistant. As you play the game Kinito starts to get a too nosy asking you about your personal life opening up different programs and giving you lots of little games and puzzles to solve. What you do in the game affects how it ends. There are many different endings, to Kinito depending on what you decide to do with Kinito.

==Plot==
The player downloads KinitoPET, a virtual assistant designed to become their best friend. At the start, he is friendly and helpful, but Kinito gradually reveals obsessive behavior as the story progresses, blurring the line between the game and the player's computer.

==Development==
KinitoPET was developed by the indie developer troy_en using the Godot Engine. An interview with the developer confirmed the game was made entirely using free software, such as the 3D models being made using Blender, and the artwork being made using Paint.NET. [ref: https://www.reddit.com/r/KinitoPET/comments/1b6p85n/interview_with_troy_en_developer_of_kinitopet/] One of the biggest issues he suffered when developing KinitoPET was procrastination. As he states, "Procrastination can kill dreams. It's never perfect and always needs changes - (To be honest I still don't like KinitoPET - I would have changed a lot if I were to redo it)". It was released for Microsoft Windows and macOS on January 9, 2024.

==Reception==
KinitoPET received generally positive reviews. On steam, the game has a total of 9,122 "Very Positive" reviews, and 138 "Overwhelmingly Positive" reviews. [ref: https://store.steampowered.com/app/2075070/KinitoPET/#app_reviews_hash] According to the review aggregate website Metacritic, the game recieved many "generally favoriable reviews" by users, with praise directed toward its atmosphere, and very good experience. [ref: https://www.metacritic.com/game/kinitopet/user-reviews/?platform=pc]
