data.title: Vivek International Public School
data.text:
Vivek International Public School (VIPS) is a private, co-educational senior secondary school in Baddi, in the Solan district of Himachal Pradesh, India. It is affiliated with the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) and run by the Swami Vivekananda Educational Society. [ref: VIPS – Best CBSE School in Baddi, Nalagarh and Barotiwala, Vivek International Public School]

__TOC__

== History ==
=== Founding ===
The school's website says it has operated since 2002. Government school-data aggregators (based on the UDISE+ database), a CBSE school directory and a school-listing portal also give 2002 as the year of establishment. [ref: Vivek International P.S. Baddi – Baddi(2), District Solan (Himachal Pradesh), Schools.org.in] [ref: Vivek International Public School – Solan, Himachal Pradesh, CBSE School] [ref: Vivek International Public School, Baddi, Solan: Admission, Fee, Affiliation, Careers360]

=== Founders ===
According to the school, the project was started by promoters familiar with education systems in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom and other European countries. Its founder president, K. S. Arya, is described as having been associated with the University Grants Commission, Panjab University and college administration for over thirty years. [ref: About Us, Vivek International Public School] (Self-published statement.)

== Management and leadership ==
The school is managed by the Swami Vivekananda Educational Society. The principal is Punita Sharma. A 2026 news report names Tushar Sharma as Director (Academics). [ref: Vivek International School holds Investiture Ceremony, [[The Tribune (Chandigarh)]

== Campus and enrolment ==
A school directory lists the campus area as 6,794.15 square metres, with 36 classrooms, 48 teachers and 1,502 enrolled students. A government-data listing records the school as co-educational, privately managed and unaided, with grades 1–12 and an attached pre-primary section. The same government-data listing records 14 teachers, 17 working computers and a computer-aided learning lab, a figure that differs from the directory's teacher count; the figures come from different sources and dates. A school-information portal lists science labs and computer labs among the facilities. [ref: Vivek International School – Contact Information, TargetStudy] Careers360 lists a school magazine and a school exhibition among the school's activities.

== Philosophy ==
The school cites the educational ideals of Swami Vivekananda and names Gurugriha Vasa – close personal contact between teacher and student – as a core value.

== Academics ==
=== Streams ===
Instruction is in English. A directory lists PCM, PCB, Commerce and Arts as the senior secondary streams.

=== Curriculum focus areas ===
The school lists these focus areas:
* Krīdā – sports
* Sapta Swaras – music
* Sūtradhāraḥ – storytelling
* Nūtanarītiḥ – innovation
* Vātsalyam – personalised attention
* Samvaachya – the art of conversation
* Vainayiki Vidyadnyan – the art of discipline

=== Teaching methodology ===
The school highlights artificial intelligence (data, computer vision and natural language processing), an Atal Tinkering Lab, experiential learning and skill development.

== Student life ==
The school holds an annual investiture ceremony. In the 2026–27 session, The Tribune reported that the ceremony included the investing of the head boy, head girl, deputies and sports captains, along with a house flag march.

== Admissions ==
The school offers an [https://vips.schoolpad.in/enquiryManager/onlineAdmission/17 online admission form] for the 2026–27 session, hosted on the Schoolpad platform, and refers families to its office for dates and details. [ref: Online Admission Form, Schoolpad (VIPS)] Fee, dress-code and transfer-certificate pages are on its website.

== Official documents ==
The school publishes the following documents on its website:
* a mandatory disclosure under CBSE affiliation requirements [ref: Mandatory Disclosure, Vivek International Public School]
* an annual report [ref: Annual Report, Vivek International Public School]
* an academic calendar for 2025–26 [ref: Academic Calendar for Session 2025-26, Vivek International Public School]
* a book list for 2025–26 [ref: List of Books for Session 2025-26, Vivek International Public School]

== Online presence ==
=== School blog ===
The school's blog publishes articles for parents and students. Posts listed on the homepage include one on STEM education and school infrastructure, [ref: Why VIPS is the Best School in Baddi for STEM and Modern Infrastructure, Vivek International Public School] one on Bharat Ratna recipients, [ref: Bharat Ratna Winners List and Their Contributions, Vivek International Public School] and one on STEM activities for children. [ref: Easy STEM Activities for Kids, Vivek International Public School] The school also publishes articles on [https://medium.com/@[user] Medium]. [ref: Vivek International Public School Baddi, Medium]

=== Social media ===
The school has accounts on [https://www.facebook.com/vipsbaddi Facebook], [ref: Vivek International Public School, Baddi, Facebook] [https://www.youtube.com/c/VivekInternationalPublicSchool YouTube], [ref: Vivek International Public School, YouTube] [https://www.instagram.com/vipsbaddi Instagram], [https://www.twitter.com/vipsbaddi X (Twitter)] and [https://in.linkedin.com/company/vivek-international-public-school LinkedIn].

data.title: Rally Takes the Train
data.text:
Rally Takes the Train is a 2022 American children's picture book written by Kelsey Cecil and illustrated by Leslie Dunn. Told in rhyming verse, it follows Rally, a corgi, on his first train journey to visit his grandparents, whom the book calls his "grand-paw-rents." The story is set aboard a passenger train traveling along the Southern California coast, and the title character is based on the author's own dog. [ref: Rally Takes the Train, Rally Takes the Train]

== Plot ==
Rally wakes early on the morning of a big journey. Seeing a suitcase, he assumes his family is going away and packs his favorite things: a turtle toy, a green bone, and a yellow ball. At a Spanish-style train station lined with palm trees, Rally runs ahead in excitement, but his short legs cannot climb the train's tall steps, and his father lifts him aboard.

On the train, the family finds their seats and Rally greets the other passengers. Children reach down to pet him, and he leaves a trail of shed fur, described as "corgi glitter," as he walks the aisle. When the train departs, Rally watches the ocean through the window, greets a seabird, shares a pretzel with his mother, and meets the conductor.

The train then enters a dark tunnel. Rally is frightened at first, but soon sees light ahead, hears cheering, and emerges onto a stretch of track running beside coastal cliffs and the sea. Near the end of the trip, Rally sees his grandparents, Grandmommy and Papa, waving from the platform of another station. He runs to the door to greet them.

== Background ==
The idea for the book, including its title, plot, and the "grand-paw-rents" wordplay, originated with the author's mother, who discussed it for years but died in 2021 before writing it. Cecil subsequently wrote the book to realize her mother's idea and as a memorial to her. [ref: Our Story, Rally Takes the Train]

The character of Rally is based on the Cecil family's corgi. The tunnel scene was inspired by a photograph of the dog sitting frightened in a car during a rainstorm.

== Setting ==
The journey depicted in the book corresponds to a trip on Amtrak's Pacific Surfliner from San Diego to Orange County. The departure station illustrated in the book is modeled on San Diego's Santa Fe Depot, and the ocean views depict the coastline near San Clemente, where the rail line runs directly along the beach.

== Illustrations ==
The book was illustrated by Leslie Dunn of 9+C Designs. Each page was hand-painted in watercolor. [ref: The Art, Rally Takes the Train]

In her review for Reedsy Discovery, Kathryn Bettendorf highlighted the illustrations' use of a corgi-eye-level perspective and their depiction of the train journey. [ref: Rally Takes the Train, Reedsy Discovery]

== Publication ==
Rally Takes the Train was independently published in paperback through Kindle Direct Publishing on November 5, 2022. The original edition contains 25 pages and has the ISBN 9798846419773. [ref: Rally Takes The Train, Open Library]

The book is also available in paperback and digital formats through Barnes & Noble, including an edition for its NOOK e-reading platform. [ref: Rally Takes The Train, Barnes & Noble]

A Kindle edition is also available through Amazon. [ref: Rally Takes the Train, Amazon]

== Critical reception ==
In a review published by Reedsy Discovery, Kathryn Bettendorf praised the book's rhyming narrative, read-aloud qualities, and watercolor illustrations by Leslie Dunn. Bettendorf highlighted the illustrations' use of a corgi-eye-level perspective and described the book as a heartwarming account of family and adventure.

Bettendorf also discussed the book's appeal to children interested in trains and dogs, noting its suitability as a read-aloud picture book.

data.title: Md Moshiur Rahman
data.text:
Md Moshiur Rahman is a Bangladeshi businessman who serves as the Honorary Consul of the Republic of Belize in Bangladesh. [ref: Moshiur made Hon Consul for Belize in Bangladesh, The Daily Observer] [ref: New Honorary Consul for Belize in Bangladesh, Bangladesh Post] [ref: List of Honorary Consul/Consul General, Protocol Wing, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh]

== Early Life and Family Background ==
Md Moshiur Rahman was born on 22 December 1982 in Purana Paltan, Dhaka, Bangladesh. He belongs to a prominent and influential local family traditionally known as the "Peer family" of Munshiganj.

* **Grandfather:** His grandfather was **Azhar Ali Pir** (locally known as Azhar Ali Hazari, Azhar Peer, or Hazari Peer), a notable landowner (jotdar) and influential personality in Munshiganj Sadar (including Banglabazar, Banial Bhukailash, Shilai, Kaziarchar, and Vasanchar). During the Pakistan era under the Basic Democracies system, he served as the President of the local Union Council, managing the local administration of the region.He was A businessman his main trade was Agricultural products like rice,potatoes or other crops.
* **Parents:** His father, **Md Sohrab Hossain Pir** (also spelled Sohrab Hossain Peer), is a public representative, local political figure, and former Union Parishad (UP) Chairman of Bangla Bazar Union under Munshiganj Sadar Upazila. [ref: Bangla Bazar Union Portal, National Web Portal of Bangladesh] He is also active in trade leadership as the General Secretary of the Bangabandhu National Stadium Shop Owners Malik Samitee in Dhaka. His mother, **Amena Begum**, is a homemaker.
* **Siblings:** He is the second among five siblings consisting of four brothers and one sister.

== Education ==
Rahman completed his Secondary School Certificate (SSC) from Motijheel Model High School, Dhaka in 1998, achieving First Division. He completed his Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) from Khilgaon Model College, Dhaka in 2000, also in First Division.

He pursued his higher studies in business administration at Southeast University, Dhaka, completing his Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) in 2007 and obtaining his Master of Business Administration (MBA) degree in 2010.

== Business Career ==
Rahman is the Proprietor of **Azhar Ali Peer International**, located at Baitul Mukarram Market in Dhaka. His business concerns encompass importing, wholesaling, and retailing various electronics products and home appliances, which are also supplied to various government agencies in Bangladesh.

In addition to his commercial enterprises, he is actively involved in trade association leadership, having been elected as the Joint Secretary of the **Baitul Mukarram Baboshayee Group**. Prior to his diplomatic appointment, he also served for over 12 years as an Honorary Representative of Bekto Precisa (Bosnia and Herzegovina) in Bangladesh, managing international trade, finance, and industrial import operations. [ref: Moshiur made Hon Consul for Belize in Bangladesh, The Daily Observer]

== Diplomatic Role ==
He was officially appointed as the Honorary Consul of the Republic of Belize in Bangladesh to facilitate diplomatic, trade, and economic cooperation between both nations, with the Honorary Consulate located at Purana Paltan, Dhaka. [ref: List of Honorary Consul/Consul General, Protocol Wing, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh]

== Personal Life ==
Rahman is married to Dr. Romana Afroze Roxy, a dentist who serves as the Chief Consultant of Romana Dental Clinic. The couple has two children: a daughter, Mehrish Radwa Rahman, and a son, Md Muaz Rakhwan Rahman. Both children receiving their education in the United Kingdom.

data.title: Marina Shmatova
data.text:
Marina Shmatova is a philanthropist and founder of the Nia Safi Charity Foundation, now operating as the Shmatov Family Fund, active in Mozambique, Kenya and the United Arab Emirates.

== Philanthropy ==
In 2023, the Nia Safi Charity Foundation, now the Shmatov Family Fund, rehabilitated the Mungassa Primary School in Beira, Mozambique. The foundation's work in Sofala Province includes the construction of schools and housing for vulnerable families after cyclones, including the Vila Massane housing program. According to the local press, the foundation announced plans to build more houses for vulnerable populations. From 2020-2022 the foundation ran the Mentalidade Ecologica (EcoMindset) educational program in Sofala and Manica provinces, focusing on soft skills, ecology, culture and sustainable development.

== Publications ==
Shmatova is the author of children's educational books published under the Shmatov Family World Library imprint:

* Orações para Crianças (Prayers for Children) - 2025
* Coloring Pages for Children Creativity: Beira (Author: Marina Schmatova, Designer: Vartanyan George) - 2023

data.title: Axel Hutter
data.text:
DRAFT Translation Article Axel Hutter DE

Axel Hutter (born 1961 in Berlin) is a German philosopher and university lecturer.

==Life==
===Academic career===

Hutter studied philosophy, German studies, musicology and medicine at the Free University of Berlin (FU Berlin) from 1982 to 1988. In Berlin, his philosophy tutors were Michael Theunissen and Ernst Tugendhat. He completed his medical studies with the state examination and was granted a licence to practise medicine. His Master’s thesis, ‘Plato’s Modernity in the Light of Platonic Modernity’, marked the completion of his philosophy studies. He was awarded his doctorate in 1993 at the Free University of Berlin with his doctoral thesis ‘Historical Reason: The Continuation of Kant’s Critique of Reason in Schelling’s Late Philosophy’. Both his Master’s thesis and doctoral thesis were supervised by Michael Theunissen.

From 1994 to 1998, Hutter was a lecturer at the Institute of Philosophy at the Free University of Berlin; from 1998 to 2006, he was a research fellow at the Institute of Philosophy at the Ruhr University Bochum and at the Hegel Archive there. In Bochum, he obtained his habilitation in philosophy with the book ‘The Interest of Reason. Kant’s Original Insight and Its Development in the Major Works of Transcendental Philosophy’. The habilitation thesis was supervised by Walter Jaeschke.

Since March 2006, Axel Hutter has held the Chair of Theoretical Philosophy at the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich. Since 2025, he has also been a visiting professor at the Institute of Philosophy in Leipzig.

===Scholarships and awards===
* University scholarship (1982–1988) and doctoral scholarship (1990–1992) from the German National Academic Foundation (Studienstiftung)
* Habilitation scholarship (1995–1998) from the German Research Foundation (DFG)
* Awarded the ‘[https://cas.au.dk/filosofi-og-idehistorie/forskningsprogram/annual-justus-hartnack-lecture Justus Hartnack Lecture]’ in Aarhus, Denmark (2008)

==Works==

Axel Hutter conducts research and teaches in the field of contemporary theoretical philosophy. From a systematic perspective, his main areas of focus are the philosophy of language, epistemology, the theory of rationality and metaphysics; his historical focus lies on classical German philosophy and classical analytic philosophy. His research is devoted to the development of a narrative ontology that rethinks the relationship between meaning (language) and being (the world) by granting meaning systematic priority over being.

===I. Historical Reason===

In Historical Reason [ref: ], Axel Hutter examines the systematic structure and epistemological claims of Schelling’s late philosophy. His central aim is to reconstruct positive philosophy as a continuation of Kant’s critical philosophy under historical conditions. Hutter thus refutes interpretations that see Schelling’s late work as a departure from the rationality of the Enlightenment.

Central to the argument is the thesis that Schelling does not abandon the idea of reason, but rather gives it a historical turn. Drawing on key texts – in particular from the Philosophy of Mythology and the Philosophy of Revelation – Hutter demonstrates that Schelling no longer understands reason primarily as a transcendental structure, but as a force that unfolds historically. The distinction between myth and revelation thus appears as an expression of the historical articulation of the Absolute.

Schelling’s philosophy is thus conceived as an attempt at a rationality that does not ignore the factual and the contingent, but integrates them into reason’s self-understanding. This form of ‘historical reason’ differs from Hegel’s speculative idealism without sacrificing systematic coherence.

===II. The Interest of Reason===

In The Interest of Reason [ref: ], Hutter analyses a central yet frequently overlooked concept in Kantian philosophy: the notion of the ‘interest of reason’. The starting point is the observation that Kant himself speaks on several occasions of the ‘true interest of pure reason’ without systematically elaborating this concept. Hutter takes up this hint and develops from it a guiding category that brings the three Critiques – Critique of Pure Reason, Critique of Practical Reason and Critique of Judgement – into a coherent whole.

The aim of the study is to reconstruct the internal connection between theoretical, practical and aesthetic-teleological reason from the perspective of a common interest. This ‘interest’ is not to be understood in psychological or subjective terms, but rather structurally: it denotes reason’s intrinsic claim to assert its own unity, freedom and final purpose. Hutter demonstrates that the pursuit of knowledge, moral action and aesthetic judgement are based on a common rational orientation, which finds expression in this interest.

Particular focus is placed on the transition from theoretical to practical reason. Hutter argues that reason is not merely a cognitive faculty, but necessarily also an active one. Moral legislation appears not as a mere postulate, but as an expression of a rational interest that finds its form in the idea of freedom. The third critique, on the power of judgement, is also situated within this structure: according to Hutter, it represents a mediating level in which reason’s interest in the unity of nature and freedom, of what is and what ought to be, comes to light.

Overall, Hutter reconstructs Kantian philosophy not as a system of individual disciplines, but as the expression of a unified rational context, the driving force of which is a structural interest oriented towards freedom and meaning. In doing so, he advocates an understanding of Kantian philosophy that takes its fundamental practical structure seriously, without downplaying its theoretical achievements.

===III. Narrative Ontology===

In Narrative Ontology [ref: ], Hutter develops a philosophy of self-knowledge that sets out to rethink the relationship between freedom, God and immortality under the conditions of modernity. To explore this question, Hutter takes Thomas Mann’s Joseph and His Brothers as a model and ally. For Mann’s novel portrays humanity’s existential self-knowledge through the mode of storytelling: it is not through abstract conceptualisation, but through the narrative shaping of life and the world that freedom, the relationship with God and immortality become negotiable. Drawing on Mann’s work, Hutter develops the fundamental concept of a narrative ontology: a philosophy that conceives of being and meaning not as separate entities, but as two inextricably linked aspects of human reality. The meaning of life is not situated outside of life, but unfolds within the story of life itself. Accordingly, Hutter no longer understands ontology as the description of objective structures of being, but as the interpretation of being within the horizon of narrative self-revelation. The narrative structure of the self, which seeks to understand itself through stories, thus forms the basis of a renewed philosophy of self-knowledge.

In the first part (The Stories of Jacob), Hutter examines the ambiguity and decentred nature of the ‘I’, which cannot be understood as a fixed identity, but is constituted solely through the mode of narrative self-interpretation. The motif of the ‘theatre of the world’ shows that human freedom consists in interpreting and reshaping roles. Deceptions, ruptures and narrative irony are not external disruptions, but constitutive elements of human existence. Being oneself becomes visible as a process of understanding and appropriating one’s own story.

In the second part (Time and Meaning), Hutter explores the temporality of the self. Human beings do not understand themselves through isolated actions, but within the context of their life story. Using the example of Abraham, it is shown that self-knowledge and knowledge of God lie within the horizon of the future and of revelation. God does not appear as a guaranteed metaphysical backdrop, but as a claim that mediates between freedom and historicity. The world is thus understood as a meaningful, narratable unfolding of events that calls for interpretation.

In the third part (The Stories of Joseph), Hutter turns his attention to the future perspective and the openness of human existence. Joseph’s story shows that self-understanding remains a risky process that passes through suffering, catastrophe and, not least, death. Hope, humour and empathy emerge as central dimensions of narrative freedom. Meaning is not posited beyond life, but is brought forth within the medium of parable and interpretation itself.

In the concluding section (Making Present), Hutter diagnoses contemporary nihilism as a consequence of the separation of being and meaning. He counters this with the idea of a narrative ontology that understands human beings as historical, interpretative and free beings. Self-knowledge consists in experiencing oneself, through the act of telling one’s own story, as the bearer of a meaning that is neither guaranteed nor arbitrary.

===IV. Language Analysis and Metaphysics===

In Language Analysis and Metaphysics [ref: ], Axel Hutter presents an introduction to modern philosophy that systematically brings two major currents into dialogue with one another: the analysis of linguistic meaning and the redefinition of metaphysical questions. Philosophy is understood here as humanity’s self-understanding of the conditions of its thinking, speaking and acting – not in the sense of mere knowledge, but as a reflection on that which is familiar to us and yet open to question.

In the first part, Hutter develops key insights from linguistic analysis drawing on Frege, Russell and Wittgenstein. Central to this is the distinction between representation, sense and meaning, as well as the role of language as a rule-governed medium for shared engagement with the world. Meaning arises from usage; language games and ways of life are constitutive of understanding. The task of philosophy here lies in elucidating concepts in order to avoid linguistic confusion – not in a reductionist manner, however, but in the service of a deeper clarification of our relationship to the world and our self-understanding.

The second part transfers these questions into the sphere of metaphysics without lapsing into traditional speculation. Building on the linguistic-analytical foundation developed in the first part, Hutter examines central concepts such as the world, time, the self, the person, freedom and, finally, philosophy itself. Authors such as Anscombe, McTaggart, Strawson and Harry Frankfurt serve as points of reference. The aim is to interpret these concepts as metaphysical names, in order both to do justice to their claim to absolute universality and, at the same time, to open them up to a linguistic-analytical approach. Hutter is guided in this by the insight developed throughout the book that philosophy is directed towards the self-evident – towards that which lies openly before our eyes, yet nevertheless eludes us. It is precisely through this movement that the astonishing reveals itself within the seemingly familiar.

===Reception===

Narrative Ontology is the subject of an academic anthology: ‘On the Spirit of History: On Axel Hutter’s Narrative Ontology’ [ref: [https://www.mohrsiebeck.com/buch/vom-geist-der-geschichte-9783161645037/ Vom Geist der Geschichte. Zu Axel Hutters Narrativer Ontologie], Th. Oehl und Th. Enthofer (Hrsg.), Tübingen: Mohr Siebeck 2026]. In addition to an introduction by the editors, the volume contains contributions by: Dominik Fröhlich, Axel Hutter, Silvia Jonas, Tereza Matějčková, Thomas Oehl, Julia Peters, Sebastian Rödl, Jan Rohls, Ariane Cäcilie Schneck, Pirmin Stekeler-Weithofer and Wilhelm Vossenkuhl.

[https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axel_Hutter Axel Hutters deutsche Version]

data.title: Rohit Shanmukhappa
data.text:
Rohit Shanmukhappa is an Indian actor and film producer who works primarily in Kannada cinema. A model and theatre artist, Rohit made his lead acting debut in the 2024 Kannada feature film Raktaksha, directed by Vasudeva S. N. and produced by Rohit under the Sai Production banner. [ref: Model-turned-actor Rohit turns lead with Raktaksha, Cinema Express] [ref: Rohit's debut 'Raktaksha' locks release date, The New Indian Express] [ref: Kannada Movie Review-Rakthaksha: Drugs, suspense and violence, Bangalore Mirror] [ref: ರಕ್ತಸಿಕ್ತ ಕಥೆ ಹೊತ್ತ ರಕ್ತಾಕ್ಷ, Chittara] [ref: ರೋಹಿತ್ ಕಣ್ಣಲ್ಲಿ ರಕ್ತಾಕ್ಷ ಕನಸು, Roopatara] He was previously cast in a negative role in the unreleased film AB Positive.
== Early life and career ==
Rohit is from Mudgal in Raichur district, Karnataka. He began his career in modelling and gained experience in theatre before entering feature films. Public TV reported in May 2023 that Rohit had six years of modelling experience and two years of theatre experience before entering films. Media coverage described him as a model and theatre artist during his transition to cinema. Rohit has said that becoming an artiste was a childhood ambition. In connection with Raktaksha, he said he underwent multiple physical transformations for the role and sought to establish himself through his work in cinema. [ref: 'ರಕ್ತಾಕ್ಷ' ಸಿನಿಮಾ ಮೂಲಕ ಬೆಳ್ಳಿತೆರೆಗೆ ಮಾಡೆಲ್, Kannada Prabha] [ref: 'ರಕ್ತಾಕ್ಷ’ ಸಿನಿಮಾ ಮೂಲಕ ಸ್ಯಾಂಡಲ್ ವುಡ್ ಗೆ ಕಾಲಿಟ್ಟ ಮಾಡೆಲ್, Public TV]
[ref: Raktaksha film review: ಪ್ರತೀಕಾರದ ದಾರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಆಘಾತಕಾರಿ ಮಾಫಿಯಾ, ಪ್ರೇಕ್ಷಕ ಕೂಡ ಅಚ್ಚರಿ, Asianet Suvarna News]
== Film career ==
Raktaksha marked Rohit Shanmukhappa's lead acting debut in Kannada cinema. Directed by Vasudeva S. N., the film was produced by Rohit under the Sai Production banner and was released in July 2024. Actor Pramod Shetty played the antagonist. The film's title track was sung by actor and playback singer Vasishta N. Simha. Actors Vijay Raghavendra and Suman Nagarkar attended the film's trailer launch, where the release date was announced. [ref: Rohit's debut 'Raktaksha' locks release date, The New Indian Express] At a title-track launch event in May 2023, Rohit said that Raktaksha was inspired by true incidents and would incorporate a reverse-screenplay concept. In a July 2024 feature in *Chittara*, Rohit discussed the challenges of acting in and producing *Raktaksha* simultaneously. He said his responsibilities extended beyond acting to overseeing different production departments and addressing problems that arose during filming. He also discussed the financial risks of filmmaking and the need to work within the available budget.
Following its release in July 2024, Raktaksha was reviewed by Kannada entertainment publications. Bangalore Mirror discussed the film's crime-thriller storyline, suspense and action sequences, and commented on Rohit's performance. In its review, Asianet Suvarna News rated the film three out of five stars and described Rohit as a promising talent in Kannada cinema.[8] CiniMirror's review described Rohit's performance as conveying vulnerability, anger and charm. [ref: Raktaksha Kannada Movie Review: An Gripping Revenge Thriller, CiniMirror] In an August 2024 interview with CiniMirror, Rohit discussed his experience of acting in and producing Raktaksha. He described the experience of producing the film and spoke about his plans to continue acting and develop further film projects. [ref: North Karnataka Witnesses a New Star, CiniMirror]
== Reception ==

Reviews of Raktaksha discussed its action sequences, suspense and revenge storyline. In its review published on 28 July 2024, Bangalore Mirrorpraised the handling of the action sequences and the film's thriller and dramatic elements [ref: Kannada Movie Review-Rakthaksha: Drugs, suspense and violence, Bangalore Mirror]. A review published by Kannada Prabha on 27 July 2024 described Rohit as a promising talent in Kannada cinema for his portrayal of a man seeking revenge for his younger brother's death. [ref: ಕ್ರೈಮ್, ಸಸ್ಪೆನ್ಸ್, ಥ್ರಿಲ್ಲರ್‌ ನೆರಳಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಸಾಗುವ ಪ್ರತೀಕಾರದ ದಾರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಆಘಾತಕಾರಿ ಮಾಫಿಯಾ, Kannada Prabha]
== Awards and nominations ==
Rohit Shanmukhappa was nominated for Best Debut Actor for his performance in Raktaksha at the sixth Chandanavana Film Critics Awards, according to a report published by The Hans India on 5 May 2025. [ref: VI Chandanavana Film Critics Awards 2025 nominations announced, The Hans India]

data.title: Mayookha
data.text:
Mayookha is a 2026 Indian Telugu-language psychological crime thriller film written and directed by Shree Tej SK. [ref: Mayookha Movie Review: A Gripping Suspense Thriller, The Hans India] Produced by Sasidhar Nalla under the Prashvitha Entertainment banner, the film stars Payal Chengappa in the titular role alongside Dev D, Aman Masud, Muralidhar Goud, and Lavanya Rani. [ref: Mayookha Telugu Movie Review, 123telugu]

The film revolves around the concept of phrogging, following an independent working woman who experiences strange disturbances inside her flat while a serial killer targets women in the city. [ref: Mayookha Movie Review, Cinejosh] Mayookha was released theatrically on 9 October 2026. [ref: Cognier Cine Creations to Release Unique Thriller “Mayookha” Overseas, TELUGU TIMES]

== Plot ==
Mayookha is an independent banking professional living alone in an apartment in Hyderabad. Carrying trauma from a childhood incident, she struggles with anxiety and isolation. Her life takes an alarming turn when she begins to notice subtle, inexplicable changes in her flat at night, including moved objects and the feeling of a presence sharing her home. Unbeknownst to her, an intruder is secretly inhabiting her apartment without her knowledge—a phenomenon known as phrogging.

Simultaneously, the city is gripped by fear over a string of gruesome murders of young women living alone. The killer leaves distinct signatures, taking items from the victims and obsessively seeking fragrances. Sub-Inspector Dev leads the police investigation into the homicide spree. When Mayookha approaches the police reporting that someone is residing in her flat, her complaints are initially treated as paranoia due to lack of evidence.

The tension escalates when a visitor to Mayookha's apartment is killed, placing her under intense suspicion. As SI Dev digs deeper into the victims' backgrounds and Mayookha's surroundings, the investigation reveals the terrifying link between the intruder in her apartment and the serial murders terrorizing the city.

== Cast ==
* Payal Chengappa as Mayookha
* Dev D (Dev Shashank) as SI Dev
* Aman Masud as Kumar, a carpenter
* Muralidhar Goud as Veeru's father
* Lavanya Rani as the opposite flat neighbor / bank cashier
* Charishma Dabbara as Honey
* Janu Varma as Divya
* Nanaji Karri as Ravi, apartment security guard
* Raghu Vasireddy as Assistant Bank Manager
* Abhilash Adda as Bank Manager

== Production ==
The film was directed by Shree Tej SK and produced by Sasidhar Nalla under the banner Prashvitha Entertainment, with Manoj Pola serving as co-producer. The narrative was conceived around the premise of "phrogging", a thriller concept where an unauthorized individual resides secretly inside someone else's house.

Farhan Vadakkan handled the cinematography, with Sharat J editing the film. The dialogues and associate direction were handled by Chintakindi Kiran Kumar, alongside additional dialogues by Shiva Ram Charan. Sibi Mathew Alex composed the original background score and songs. Prior to its theatrical release, the film was screened at festival circuits and won the Best Mystery Film award at the New York International Film Awards (NYIFA).

== Release ==
Mayookha was censored with an 'A' (Adults Only) certificate by the Central Board of Film Certification and released in theatres on 9 October 2026. Overseas distribution was handled by Cognier Cine Creations.

== Reception ==
Mayookha received generally moderate to positive reviews from critics, who praised the novel premise of phrogging, the suspenseful second half, and Payal Chengappa's lead performance, while critiquing the slow pace of the initial portions.

The Hans India rated the film 3 out of 5 stars, describing it as a "gripping mystery thriller" and praising Chengappa's acting alongside the twists in the second half, though noting that tighter pacing in the early scenes would have helped.

Pinkvilla Telugu also awarded it 3 out of 5 stars, commending the film's atmospheric tension and the unique integration of phrogging within a serial-killer mystery. [ref: Mayookha Telugu Movie Review, Pinkvilla Telugu]

Writing for Sakshi, a reviewer gave the film 2.75 out of 5 stars, calling it a thrilling watch with commendable performances, particularly highlighting Chengappa's emotional range. [ref: మయూఖ మూవీ రివ్యూ, Sakshi]

NTV Telugu rated the film 2.75 out of 5 stars, stating that the climax twists and background music elevate the film, even if the investigation sequences occasionally feel familiar. [ref: మయూఖ మూవీ రివ్యూ, NTV]

Filmibeat Telugu gave it 2.5 out of 5 stars, noting that the concept is fresh and the murder mystery maintains curiosity despite minor pacing flaws. [ref: Mayookha Movie Review and Rating in Telugu, Filmibeat Telugu]

123telugu gave the film 2.5 out of 5 stars, praising the lead cast, technical values, and background score, while remarking that the narrative moves at a gradual pace before hitting its stride. [ref: సమీక్ష: మయూఖ – పర్వాలేదనిపించే క్రైమ్ థ్రిల్లర్, 123telugu]

Cinejosh noted that while the initial setup takes time, the second-half twists and Sibi Mathew Alex's score provide solid thrills for fans of the genre. [ref: Mayookha Movie Review, Cinejosh]

data.title: Haggis 1
data.text:
The Haggis Wildlife Foundation is a Scotland-based folklore, publishing and digital storytelling initiative whose work centres on the wild haggis, an animal associated with Scottish humour and folklore. The Foundation produces documentary-style films, illustrated species guides, fictional field reports, online publications and interactive community projects. Its stated purpose is to document, reinterpret and share the cultural legend for contemporary audiences, rather than to operate as a conventional wildlife conservation charity. [ref: About the Haggis Wildlife Foundation, Haggis Wildlife Foundation] [ref: Our Work, Haggis Wildlife Foundation]

Its activities span a main website, an online catalogue of films and books, an interactive sightings register, social-media and mailing-list communities, a related research-style publishing network, and a retail website. Although much of its work adopts the conventions of zoology, conservation and historical archives, those conventions are employed in a fictional and folkloric setting. [ref: Haggis Wildlife Foundation, Haggis Wildlife Foundation] [ref: About the Haggis Wildlife Foundation, Haggis Wildlife Foundation Official Shop]

== Purpose and organisational identity ==
The Foundations work is the preservation and continuation of a Scottish storytelling tradition. It uses encounters with wild haggis to encourage participation in folklore through watching, reading, sharing stories and submitting sightings. Its online About Us statement distinguishes this activity from conventional wildlife conservation and characterises the work as cultural storytelling and community-building.

The main website presents the Foundation as an archive of wild haggis lore. It organises material into areas such as species guides, videos, news, books, the Grand Survey and a map of reported sightings. The stated motto is To document and preserve, also rendered there as describendum et conservandum. Its Our Work statement identifies storytelling, documentary production and online discussion as its principal methods and places particular emphasis on the social communities formed around humorous folklore.

== Historical narrative ==
The Foundation's website contains an extensive fictionalised foundation history. Its Our Story page attributes an establishment date of 1892 to Sir Archibald MacTavish, described as the 7th Earl of Glenfinnan. It introduces a purported early team comprising photographer Neil McKinnon, zoologist Edwin McTaggart, and Highland guides Duncan and Harris MacLeod, and situates the fictional expeditionary programme around the Heatherlie estate and the Highlands. [ref: Our Story, Haggis Wildlife Foundation]

The narrative describes late nineteenth-century photographic expeditions, the use of glass-plate equipment, purported discoveries of haggis burrows and archival photographs. These episodes are elements of the Foundation's constructed history and are not independently established events in the organisation's actual legal or operational history. No independently corroborated nineteenth-century incorporation or continuous operating history is asserted here.

The historical framework extends beyond the Foundation's own website. Publications attributed to its fictional archives include photographs and purported field records dated to the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. Their historical dates describe the setting of the stories, not independently verified dates of the Foundation's real-world activities. [ref: Wildes Haggis, German-language Wikipedia]

== Activities and projects ==

=== Films and digital documentaries ===
Documentary-style video is one of the Foundation's principal forms of publication. Its website hosts a film catalogue covering imagined wild haggis species, habitats, seasonal migrations and encounters. Listed titles include White Tash Haggis Animal, The Round Woodland Haggis, Wild Forest Haggis, Subspecies of Wild Scottish Sea Haggis, The Great Return: Scotland's Wild Haggis Awaken, Winter Subspecies of Wild Haggis Animals, The Great Migration of Wild Scottish Haggis Animals and A Spotters Guide to Wild Scottish Haggis Animals. [ref: Videos, Haggis Wildlife Foundation]

The films use natural-history presentation techniques to describe impossible or invented animals as though they were subjects of wildlife photography. A September 2024 community-contributed article on Daily Kos discussed the Foundation's YouTube videos, including What Is Scotland's Wild Haggis Animal?, The Ancient Art of Scottish Wild Haggis Shearing and The Truth Behind Commercial Haggis Farming. The author described the documentaries as humorous fiction and commented on their computer-generated imagery and narrated presentation. [ref: Kitchen Table Kibitzing 9/3/2024: The Haggis Wildlife Foundation, Daily Kos]

=== Species guides ===
The Foundation publishes introductory descriptions of invented wild haggis varieties, including the Common Garden Haggis and the Stirling White Tash. Its website combines species names and illustrations with instructions framed as spotting advice, while linking to longer guides and films.

These materials are presented in the style of field guides: they assign characteristics to imagined species and describe supposed habitats, behaviours and regional varieties. The subject matter remains folklore rather than verified taxonomy or zoology. The site's Grand Survey framing connects species descriptions, visitor observations and further creative entries within a common fictional world.

=== Public sightings register ===
The Foundation maintains an online wild haggis sightings map and register. The page invites visitors to submit sightings and displays named submissions, images, descriptive observations and species categories. Register categories visible on the site include Garden Haggis, Lowland Hagglet, Unknown Species and Woolly Highland Haggis. [ref: Wild Haggis Animal Sightings Map, Haggis Wildlife Foundation]

The submissions function as participatory folklore and audience engagement, rather than evidence of a real species. The public register permits contributors to extend the Foundation's shared fictional setting by adding individual names and stories to the sightings archive.

=== Community participation and outreach ===
The Foundation invites participation through a mailing list, online communities and the contribution of accounts or sightings. Its Our Work page describes community engagement and shared humour as integral to the initiative. It also displays promotional audience figures for Facebook, TikTok, Instagram and YouTube; these are self-reported website figures and have not been independently audited.

The official shop describes a broader participant community of enthusiasts, families, first-time spotters and its fictional Rangers, and connects merchandise to continuing work on the Grand Survey, films and stories. The Foundation's online activity thus includes both published creative material and reader or viewer participation.

== Publications and research-style writing ==
The Haggis Wildlife Foundation maintains a dedicated publishing programme encompassing illustrated books, field guides, archival collections and works addressing Scottish folklore, cultural heritage and historical interpretation. Its books section provides a catalogue of publications associated with the Foundation's wider activities in documentary production, cultural preservation, research-themed publishing and public engagement. The catalogue includes The Official Book of Wild Haggis Animals, Field Guide to Wild Haggis Spotting in Scotland, The Sacred Order's Guide to Haggis Enlightenment, The Sacred Order of Haggis and Scotland's Wild Haggis.

The Foundation's publishing activities encompass several distinct literary and cultural categories, reflecting its wider organisational interest in Scottish traditions, historical narratives and the presentation of archival material. Its illustrated reference works and field guides employ the conventions of natural-history publishing, while its historical collections use photographic imagery and archival presentation to develop the Foundation's documentary narratives. Publications associated with the Sacred Order of the Haggis extend the Foundation's catalogue into fictional institutional history, ceremonial traditions and cultural satire. Together, these works form an interconnected publishing programme that complements the Foundation's online articles, documentary productions and associated cultural projects.

The Foundation's publications are associated with the recurring authorial identity of Professor MacDougal McDougal, whose profile appears within its books section. The author profile presents MacDougal as an authority on the Foundation's specialist subject matter, establishing continuity between its literary publications, archival collections and research-style material. This academic characterisation forms part of the Foundation's fictional publishing framework rather than establishing independently verified academic credentials.

The Foundation's publishing activities have also received international bibliographic recognition through references in the German-language Wikipedia article Wildes Haggis. The article lists Scotland's Wild Haggis: Rare Photographs from the Haggis Wildlife Foundation Archives (1890–1905), attributed to MacDougal MacDougal, as an independently published book issued in 2023 with ISBN 979-88-6573232-7. The bibliographic entry identifies the Foundation's archival collection within the publication's title, providing a documented German-language reference to its historical and photographic publishing activities.

The German-language article additionally references the Foundation's 2024 research-style publication The Impact of Plastic Waste on Wild Haggis Populations in the Scottish Highlands. Its references and external links also identify audiovisual material associated with the Foundation, documenting the appearance of its publications and creative productions in German-language encyclopaedic material. Although Wildes Haggis concerns Scottish folklore rather than providing an organisational profile of the Foundation, its bibliographic references establish that the Foundation's published output has been cited outside its own websites.

=== Online research-style publications ===
An Academia.edu profile under the Foundation's name hosts documents written in the form of scientific, ecological and philosophical papers. Its listed titles include The Impact of Plastic Waste on Wild Haggis Populations in the Scottish Highlands (2024) and Dialectical Engagement with the Haggis (2024). They employ scientific terminology, quantitative claims and academic conventions in the context of an imaginary species. [ref: Haggis Wildlife Foundation: Research Profile, Academia.edu]

Hosting on Academia.edu identifies a public distribution platform and does not by itself indicate independent peer review or scientific validation. These works are relevant as examples of the Foundation's publishing formats and satirical use of research genres, rather than as empirical evidence concerning animal populations.

=== Connected fictional archives ===
Wild Haggis Animal contains a wider collection of research-style, archival and philosophical texts. Its navigation divides material into sightings, historical interviews, field guides, conservation, philosophy, health and news. Examples include accounts of sightings assigned to 1880–1922, migration studies and fictional conservation analyses. [ref: Explore the Wild Haggis Animal, Wild Haggis Animal]

The site's About page describes a Haggis Research Network supported by the Haggis Wildlife Foundation and the Sacred Order of the Haggis. It presents the network as a means of organising writings around the mythology and cultural history of the imagined animal. [ref: Discover the Wild Haggis Animal, Wild Haggis Animal]

== Related websites and cultural presence ==

=== Wild Haggis Animal ===
The Wild Haggis Animal website links to the Foundation and provides a parallel collection of fictional archival articles, historical chronicles and discussions framed as research. Its reference to the Haggis Research Network explicitly names the Foundation as a supporting body.

=== TODO in Scotland ===
The Scotland-oriented website TODO in Scotland maintains a page titled Haggis Wildlife Foundation, links to its main website and displays the Foundation's United Kingdom trade mark number. It also publishes pages concerning the imagined animal and related sightings. This establishes an external web reference to the Foundation, but the page is predominantly a directory-style identification rather than a substantial independent organisational history. [ref: Haggis Wildlife Foundation, TODO in Scotland]

=== The Sacred Order of the Haggis ===
The Sacred Order of the Haggis hosts a connected fictional archive containing ceremonial narratives, historical accounts, expeditions and writings. Its homepage links to the Haggis Wildlife Foundation. Its purported historical claims are part of this related creative world and should not be interpreted as verified historical records. [ref: The Sacred Order of the Haggis, The Sacred Order of the Haggis]

=== German-language Wikipedia ===
The German-language Wikipedia article Wildes Haggis references material published by the Foundation. As well as citing the Foundation website, it lists its historical-photograph publication, links to the Foundation website and identifies a Foundation video. This is evidence of reuse or citation of the Foundation's published material on an external encyclopaedia page; it is not a German Wikipedia biography or organisational article devoted to the Foundation itself.

=== Online commentary ===
A Daily Kos community article dated 3 September 2024 focused on the Haggis Wildlife Foundation's videos and reproduced links to several of its film releases. It characterised the series as entertainment presented through mock wildlife documentaries. As a community-contributed article, it provides an example of external commentary but should not be confused with a professionally commissioned or independently fact-checked organisational profile.

== Retail and intellectual property ==
The Foundation operates the Haggis Wildlife Foundation Official Shop, through which it offers branded clothing, illustrated books, plush haggis toys and other gifts. The shop connects products to characters and themes introduced in the Foundation's storytelling and promotes participation in the wider fictional world. [ref: Haggis Wildlife Foundation Official Shop, Haggis Wildlife Foundation Official Shop]

The name Haggis Wildlife Foundation is associated with United Kingdom trade mark UK00004134196. The Foundation identifies the mark as registered in its official shop, while TODO in Scotland publishes the same number with a link to the UK Intellectual Property Office record. The Foundation also publishes an intellectual-property statement covering its creative works, images, writing and film. [ref: Terms of Use, Haggis Wildlife Foundation]

data.title: Malou Morillo
data.text:
Marilou "Malou" Flores-Morillo is a Filipino businesswoman, philanthropist, and politician from Oriental Mindoro. She made history as the first female city mayor of Calapan, serving from 2022 to 2025.

==Early Life and Business Career==
Before entering public service, Morillo established herself in the private sector as a prominent corporate executive and entrepreneur. In 1994, she founded Sixteen Enterprises, a heavy equipment operations and commercial trading firm based in Calapan City. Deeply involved in social and civic work, she launched the Morillo Foundation in 2019 to spearhead local philanthropic, educational, and livelihood development initiatives across the province.

==Political Career==
===2022 Calapan City Mayoralty Campaign===
Morillo entered local politics by running for the mayoral seat of Calapan City during the May 2022 local elections under the Aksyon Demokratiko banner. She won her first public office by securing 36,452 votes, defeating incumbent vice mayor Gil Ramirez of Mindoro Bago Sarili (39,824 votes) and lawyer Gilbert Repizo of PDP–Laban (12,040 votes). She officially took her oath of office on June 30, 2022.

===Mayor of Calapan (2022–2025)===
Upon assuming office, Morillo introduced her flagship "Green Calapan" administrative platform, which focused on balancing city-wide economic advancement and infrastructural upgrades with environmental protection and public safety.

Her term was characterized by high administrative marks:
* Government Performance: Under her leadership, Calapan City ranked first nationwide in the Government Efficiency and Resiliency Pillars during the 10th Cities and Municipalities Competitiveness Index (CMCI) Summit.
* National Recognition: In November 2024, the Civil Service Commission and Gawad Pilipino named her one of the "Most Outstanding Mayor" awardees in the Philippines for her excellence in executive governance and community program delivery.
* Regional Hub Development: She successfully collaborated with regional departments to establish major administrative infrastructure, including securing the groundbreaking of the DENR MIMAROPA Regional Office in Barangay Sapul, alongside initiating the construction of the Calapan City Heritage, Culture, and Arts Building.

===2025 Re-election Bid===
In the May 2025 local elections, Morillo sought a consecutive second term under the local Galing sa Puso Movement (GSM) coalition. However, she was unseated by returning mayor and former congressman Paulino Salvador "Doy" Leachon. Following the transition of power, Morillo officially stepped down from office upon the expiration of her term on June 30, 2025.

data.title: Haider Naqvi
data.text:
----

Syed Naqi Haider Naqvi, T.I. (popularly known as S. N. Haider Naqvi, T.I.) is a Pakistani investigative journalist, political columnist, news analyst, media executive, advertising administrator, telecommunications pioneer, sports administrator, and regulatory official. Widely recognized among Pakistan's top-tier media figures, he is known for breaking high-profile investigative reports and authoring news columns on state governance, national political developments, defense affairs, media regulation, and cricket administration.

He serves as an official Executive Member of the Authority at the Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA) representing Sindh, as well as a regular senior analyst on flagship political talk shows across Pakistan's premier news networks, including Geo News and ARY News (notably as a panelist on The Reporters). He is the founder and CEO of the advertising, PR, and media agency CLICKCOM, previously served as the Chief Executive Officer of the Pakistan Super League (PSL) franchise Multan Sultans during its inaugural season, is the CEO and founder of Urdu news network StarNews Pakistan, was the founder and CEO of satellite network TV2Day, led network infrastructure modernization during Pakistan's 3G/4G telecom transformation, and currently serves as the Chief Executive Officer of the international satellite channel Ocean News UK. In 2024, he was conferred the Tamgha-e-Imtiaz (Medal of Excellence) by the President of Pakistan for his contributions to journalism.

== Early life and education ==
Naqvi is the son of **Syed Shabbir Hussain Naqvi** (1937–2013), a well-known Pakistani social worker and philanthropist noted for his extensive contributions to community welfare, humanitarian projects, and social relief initiatives across the country. Following his passing in June 2013, official state condolence messages were issued by top national leadership—including President of Pakistan Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, PTI Chairman Imran Khan, Chairman Senate Nayyar Bukhari, and Speaker National Assembly Sardar Ayaz Sadiq—acknowledging his distinguished social services and extending condolences to Haider Naqvi and the bereaved family.

Naqvi earned his Bachelor of Engineering degree from the prestigious NED University of Engineering and Technology in Karachi. During his university years, he was a prominent student leader, serving as President of the NED student body during his tenure. Demonstrating leadership and technical distinction during his academic career, he later leveraged his engineering and administrative background to lead major telecommunications infrastructure projects, corporate media management, advertising, sports governance, broadcast journalism, media entrepreneurship, and public media regulation.

== Career ==

=== Advertising, PR, & CLICKCOM ===
Naqvi expanded his corporate operations into strategic communications and media representation by founding **CLICKCOM**, a full-service advertising, public relations (PR), and media agency. As CEO of CLICKCOM, he led corporate branding, strategic media buying, nation-wide advertising campaigns, and corporate PR strategies for various public and private sector clients in Pakistan and abroad.

=== Media entrepreneurship, StarNews Pakistan & TV2Day ===
In the mid-2000s, during the expansion of private electronic media in Pakistan, Naqvi established **TV2Day**, an independent satellite television network headquartered in Karachi. Upon launching the channel, he gained widespread national attention as one of the country's youngest television network owners and CEOs.

During his tenure as head of TV2Day in 2006, Naqvi was invited to an official meeting by the then President of Pakistan, General Pervez Musharraf, to discuss electronic media expansion, broadcasting policy, and national current affairs.

Expanding his media network, Naqvi founded and serves as CEO of **StarNews Pakistan**, an Urdu-language news organization that developed into one of Pakistan's widely followed digital and broadcast current affairs outlets. Under his leadership, StarNews Pakistan focuses on breaking political coverage, investigative reporting, regional news, and current affairs analysis.

=== National initiatives & "I'M Pakistan" Conference ===
Naqvi organized the national **"I'M Pakistan" Conference**, a public recognition platform designed to honor citizens, public figures, and veterans who rendered distinguished services to Pakistan. The conference was attended by national leadership, with the then Prime Minister of Pakistan, Yousuf Raza Gillani, presiding as the Chief Guest to present honors and recognize the contributions of key national achievers.

=== Digital media presence, political engagement, & Indian media censorship ===
Naqvi maintains a significant digital presence on X (formerly Twitter), where his reporting and analytical commentary on national policy, constitutional matters, and governance regularly reach key decision-makers. His social media posts and exclusive news breaks are frequently reshared, cited, or endorsed by top state leadership and prominent politicians, including the Prime Minister of Pakistan, the President of Pakistan, Chief Minister of Punjab Maryam Nawaz, Federal Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari, and Sindh provincial minister Syed Nasir Hussain Shah.

His high-impact digital commentary on national defense and regional security led to cross-border censorship actions. During Indian military operations and geopolitical friction in Jammu and Kashmir (Operation Sindoor), Indian law enforcement agencies and news reports (including *News Bharati*) listed Haider Naqvi's account among key Pakistani digital media handles subjected to geo-blocking and restrictions by Delhi Police over regional reporting and national policy commentary.

=== Telecommunications pioneer & 3G/4G rollout ===
As a qualified engineer and corporate executive, Naqvi served as Chief Executive Officer of an international Chinese-based network infrastructure company operating in Pakistan. In this role, he played a pioneering role in modernizing Pakistan's telecommunications architecture, overseeing nationwide network building initiatives that enabled the transition of Pakistan's legacy 2G mobile networks into high-speed 3G/4G cellular networks leading up to the nation's spectrum auctions and network upgrade phase in 2013–2014.

=== International broadcast media & diplomatic engagements ===
Naqvi has featured as a guest senior news analyst on global broadcast networks, including CNN, the BBC, and Deutsche Welle (DW), offering international perspectives on South Asian geopolitics, regional security, and civil-military affairs in Pakistan.

Beyond media commentary, Naqvi has represented Pakistani journalism and broadcast leadership across international forums. He has received official invitations to attend and address legislative and diplomatic assemblies, including guest speaking engagements at the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) side sessions in New York and parliamentary media conferences in the United Kingdom.

=== Public governance & refusal of political offices ===
Naqvi was appointed by the Government and President of Pakistan to serve as a key Executive Member of the Authority at the **Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA)** representing Sindh province. In this regulatory role, he contributes to national policy formulation, broadcasting compliance, electronic media licensing, and structural oversight across Pakistan's private television networks and broadcast infrastructure.

Over his career, Naqvi was offered consideration for high-level political roles, including the post of Federal Minister for Interior and a seat in the Senate of Pakistan. However, he declined both offers, maintaining that taking up political cabinet posts or legislative office would create a direct conflict of interest with his professional mandate as an independent journalist and broadcast media analyst.

=== Defense initiatives, ISPR event direction, & "Salam Sipahi Jeeo Jawan" ===
Driven by his strong affiliation with national defense institutions, Naqvi was appointed by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) as the Director for the national **Pakistan Day Event – "Peaceful Pakistan"**. In this capacity, he was fully authorized to act on behalf of ISPR to manage and coordinate the international-scale event, which engaged global heads of state, Hollywood celebrities, and world-renowned sports figures to project a positive global image of Pakistan.

Additionally, Naqvi organized the national event series **"Salam Sipahi Jeeo Jawan"**. The ceremonies were organized as grand tributes to commemorate national defense triumphs, honor fallen soldiers (*shuhada*), and celebrate the operational victories and sacrifices of the Pakistan Armed Forces. Key national figures attended the proceedings, including PPP leader Faryal Talpur and Chief Minister of Sindh Murad Ali Shah.

=== Print journalism & column writing ===
Throughout his career, Naqvi has maintained an active presence in print media as a prolific columnist and contributing reporter. His news columns and analytical pieces on South Asian politics, regional security, civil-military dynamics, and national constitutional debates—such as his commentary on presidential versus parliamentary systems ("Plan Kuch Aur Hai!")—have been published across major national and international publications, including Urdu daily Daily Jang, English daily The News International, Daily Express, and global platforms such as The Washington Post.

In addition to opinion columns, Naqvi has authored major front-page news reports for leading dailies such as Daily Jang and The News International, detailing key executive appointments, provincial governance dynamics between federal leadership and Sindh, and administrative appointments including the Inspector General of Police (IGP) Sindh.

=== Humanitarian efforts (2005 earthquake relief) ===
Following the devastating 2005 Kashmir earthquake, Naqvi engaged in cross-border relief and fundraising initiatives. He facilitated the visit of prominent Bollywood film actor Manisha Koirala to Karachi in November 2005 to participate in a live broadcast telethon ("Pukar") aimed at raising emergency funds and aid for earthquake victims in northern Pakistan.

=== Broadcast journalism & television news analysis ===
Naqvi is a prominent and widely recognized figure on Pakistani news television. In addition to appearing as a core panelist on ARY News's flagship political discussion show, **The Reporters**, he regularly features as an expert analyst across all of Pakistan's major news channels, including Geo News, offering analytical commentary and insider perspectives on constitutional matters, parliamentary debates, national election developments, and civil-military relations.

=== Sports administration and PCB connections ===
Naqvi served as the Chief Executive Officer of the **Multan Sultans** during the franchise's inaugural appearance in the 2018 Pakistan Super League (PSL) season. As CEO, he oversaw franchise operations, team recruitment, and strategic partnerships. During his tenure, Naqvi notably presented an official team jersey to Major General Asif Ghafoor, the then Director-General of Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), recognizing the support of national security institutions for the restoration of international cricket in Pakistan.

Through his dual roles in sports administration and broadcast management, Naqvi developed deep-rooted connections within the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) and domestic sports circles, frequently reporting insider developments regarding PCB governance, team selection dynamics, and administrative decisions.

=== Investigative journalism & military leadership reporting ===
Over his career spanning print and broadcast media, Naqvi established a reputation as a leading investigative reporter specializing in defense affairs, high-level military appointments, and intelligence administration.

Notably, Naqvi broke major exclusive reports regarding senior military promotions and appointments, including early investigative reporting from Rawalpindi detailing the promotion of six Major Generals to Lieutenant General under General Qamar Javed Bajwa—specifically breaking news on Major General Asim Munir (later Chief of Army Staff) and anticipating his appointment as Director-General of Inter-Services Intelligence (DG ISI). His investigative scope also encompasses top-level security briefings, political power shifts, as well as exclusive news from the media, entertainment, and sports industries.

=== Ocean News UK ===
Naqvi serves as the Chief Executive Officer of **Ocean News UK**, an international satellite news network headquartered in London with news operations spanning Europe, the Middle East, and South Asia.

== Awards and accolades ==
Throughout his multi-faceted career across broadcast management, advertising, telecommunications infrastructure, journalism, public regulation, and sports administration, Naqvi has received various professional accolades and national recognition:

* **Tamgha-e-Imtiaz (2024):** Conferred by President Asif Ali Zardari in Islamabad on 23 March 2024 (12 Ramadan 1445 AH) for achieving distinction in the field of Journalism (*Sahaafat*).
* **ISPR Event Directorship:** Appointed as Event Director by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) for the international Pakistan Day event "Peaceful Pakistan".
* **Journalism & Public Tribute Recognition:** Honored for outstanding contributions to media and public service events, receiving awards presented by senior political leadership, including Faryal Talpur in the presence of Chief Minister of Sindh Murad Ali Shah during the "Salam Sipahi Jeeo Jawan" ceremonies.
* **PEMRA Executive Authority Member:** Appointed to represent Sindh on the federal board governing electronic media regulations in Pakistan.
* **Telecom Infrastructure Leadership:** Recognized for pioneering contributions to Pakistan's 3G/4G cellular infrastructure transition as CEO of an international network builder.
* **Youngest Media Executive Distinction:** Recognized across Pakistani media circles for becoming one of the nation's youngest television network owners and CEOs upon establishing TV2Day in the mid-2000s.
* **Sports Leadership Recognition:** Commended by national sports and administrative bodies for leading the inaugural setup of the Multan Sultans PSL franchise and promoting cricket revival in Pakistan.

== References ==

=== Primary & Secondary Document References ===
1. **Presidential Citation for Tamgha-e-Imtiaz:** Official Presidential Conferment Certificate issued in Islamabad on 23 March 2024 (12 Ramadan 1445 AH) under the signature of President Asif Ali Zardari, conferring Tamgha-e-Imtiaz upon Syed Naqi Haider Naqvi for distinction in Journalism (*Sahaafat*).
2. **State Condolence Messages (2013):** Official condolence messages and letters issued upon the demise of Syed Shabbir Hussain Naqvi (1937–2013) by President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Mian Mohammad Nawaz Sharif, PTI Chairman Imran Khan, Senate Chairman Syed Nayyer Hussain Bokhari, National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq, and Senator Farhatullah Babar (PPP Media Cell).
3. **Official Meeting with President Pervez Musharraf (2006):** Photographic and official media records documenting the 2006 state meeting between President of Pakistan General Pervez Musharraf and Syed Naqi Haider Naqvi regarding electronic media developments and broadcasting policy.
4. **Investigative Reporting on Military Leadership Promotions:** Front-page reporting by Haider Naqvi from Rawalpindi detailing the promotion of 6 Major Generals to Lieutenant General by COAS General Qamar Javed Bajwa, including Major General Asim Munir and predicting his appointment as DG ISI.
5. **The News International & Daily Jang Front-Page Reporting:** Front-page news reports authored by Haider Naqvi covering Sindh IGP appointments, executive leadership decisions, and provincial political developments between Prime Minister Imran Khan, Governor Imran Ismail, and Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah.
6. **Political Column Writing:** Special analytical column by Haider Naqvi titled "Plan Kuch Aur Hai!" analyzing national debates surrounding presidential versus parliamentary systems.
7. **News Bharati & Digital Media Blockage Coverage:** International media reports detailing Delhi Police blocking top Pakistani digital handles, explicitly listing Haider Naqvi among the blocked accounts following regional defense reporting.
8. **ISPR Appointment Authorization Letter:** Official letter from Director General ISPR (signed by Lieutenant Colonel Syed Zamin Abbas Naqvi), appointing Syed Naqi Haider Naqvi as Director for the Pakistan Day Event – "Peaceful Pakistan".
9. **PEMRA Board Appointment:** Office of the Prime Minister of Pakistan / PEMRA Authority nomination announcement for Syed Naqi Haider Naqvi as Executive Authority Member representing Sindh.
