data.title: Justian Suhandinata
data.text:
----

Dr. Ir. Justian Suhandinata, SE (20 November 1946 – 4 November 2022) was an Indonesian badminton administrator, businessman, and author. He held the position of Vice President of the International Badminton Federation (IBF), now known as the Badminton World Federation, across multiple terms from 1992 to 2002. In 2017, he became the tenth person in history — and the only Indonesian — to receive the Badminton World Federation Honorary Life Vice President award. [ref: https://bwfbadminton.com/news-single/2022/11/06/bwf-mourns-passing-of-justian-suhandinata Badminton World Federation, "BWF Mourns Passing of Justian Suhandinata", 6 November 2022] He is also credited with laying the groundwork for what became the Badminton World Federation World Junior Championships. [ref: https://www.antaranews.com/berita/3224965/justian-suhandinata-seorang-organisator-bulu-tangkis-kelas-dunia ANTARA News, "Justian Suhandinata, Organisator Bulu Tangkis Kelas Dunia", 2022]

== Early Life and Family ==

Justian Suhandinata was born on 20 November 1946 in Bandung, West Java. He was one of four sons of Suharso Suhandinata and his wife Sri Pandaliana (also known as Phan Tjoe Lian), who married in Bandung in 1941. [ref: [https://validnews.id/kultura/Suharso-Suhandinata--Diplomat-Pemersatu-Bulu-Tangkis-Dunia---cWD ValidNews, "Suharso Suhandinata, Diplomat Pemersatu Bulu Tangkis Dunia", 3 December 2018]] Suharso, together with Dick Sudirman, was instrumental in uniting the world's divided badminton bodies into a single organisation — a process that culminated in a landmark meeting in Tokyo in 1981. [ref: [https://www.kompas.com/badminton/read/2022/11/05/15000088/profil-justian-suhandinata-tokoh-bulu-tangkis-yang-bergelar-doktor-dari Kompas.com, "Profil Justian Suhandinata", 5 November 2022]]

He married Poppy Tumengkol, who represented Indonesia in the Uber Cup in 1969 and 1972. They had four children and seven grandchildren. [ref: https://golfmagz.id/dr-ir-justian-suhandinata-se/ GolfMagz, "Dr. Ir. Justian Suhandinata SE"]

== Education ==

Justian earned a degree in Engineering (Ir.) and a degree in Economics (SE) from Indonesian universities. He later completed a doctorate (Dr.) at Washington International University in Pennsylvania, United States, graduating in September 2002. [ref: https://golfmagz.id/dr-ir-justian-suhandinata-se/ GolfMagz, "Dr. Ir. Justian Suhandinata SE"]

== Badminton Playing Career ==

Justian took up badminton in 1957 and joined PB Tangkas as a club member the following year. [ref: https://www.antaranews.com/berita/3224965/justian-suhandinata-seorang-organisator-bulu-tangkis-kelas-dunia ANTARA News, "Justian Suhandinata, Organisator Bulu Tangkis Kelas Dunia", 2022] In 1964, he won the junior championship of DKI Jakarta and was subsequently selected for the national training centre (Pelatnas) of the Indonesian Badminton Association (PBSI). He was named to the Thomas Cup shadow squad in 1967 and represented DKI Jakarta at the Pekan Olahraga Nasional (National Sports Week) in Surabaya in 1969. [ref: https://www.kompas.com/badminton/read/2022/11/05/15000088/profil-justian-suhandinata-tokoh-bulu-tangkis-yang-bergelar-doktor-dari Kompas.com, "Profil Justian Suhandinata", 5 November 2022]

== Administrative Career ==

=== Domestic (PBSI) ===

Justian began his administrative work as Secretary of PB Tangkas. He progressed through PBSI's regional structure, serving as Head of Development and later Chairman of PBSI South Jakarta, before becoming Provincial Chairman of PBSI DKI Jakarta. At the national level, he served as Head of the Organisation Division of PP PBSI from 1985 to 1989, and as Vice Chairman General of PP PBSI from 1986. He later served as Secretary of the PP PBSI Supervisory Board from 1997 to 2001, and remained on the PP PBSI Advisory Board until his death. [ref: https://www.antaranews.com/berita/3224965/justian-suhandinata-seorang-organisator-bulu-tangkis-kelas-dunia ANTARA News, "Justian Suhandinata, Organisator Bulu Tangkis Kelas Dunia", 2022] He served as Chairman of PB Tangkas until 2022. [ref: https://bwfbadminton.com/news-single/2022/11/06/bwf-mourns-passing-of-justian-suhandinata Badminton World Federation, "BWF Mourns Passing of Justian Suhandinata", 6 November 2022]

=== International (IBF/Badminton World Federation) ===

Justian first joined the International Badminton Federation (IBF) as a Council Member in 1986. [ref: https://www.kompas.com/badminton/read/2022/11/05/15000088/profil-justian-suhandinata-tokoh-bulu-tangkis-yang-bergelar-doktor-dari Kompas.com, "Profil Justian Suhandinata", 5 November 2022] He went on to serve as Vice President of the IBF — later renamed the Badminton World Federation — across three consecutive terms: 1993–1995, 1996–1999, and 1999–2001. [ref: https://www.antaranews.com/berita/3224965/justian-suhandinata-seorang-organisator-bulu-tangkis-kelas-dunia ANTARA News, "Justian Suhandinata, Organisator Bulu Tangkis Kelas Dunia", 2022] During this period he also chaired the Development Committee during the establishment of the Badminton World Federation World Academy. He remained a Badminton World Federation Council Member until his passing. [ref: https://bwfbadminton.com/news-single/2022/11/06/bwf-mourns-passing-of-justian-suhandinata Badminton World Federation, "BWF Mourns Passing of Justian Suhandinata", 6 November 2022]

== Key Contributions ==

=== Badminton World Federation World Junior Championships ===

In 1984, Justian organised the Jakarta Open Junior, an invitational tournament for junior players from across the world. [ref: https://www.kompas.id/artikel/justian-suhandinata-pahlawan-bulutangkis-1 Kompas.id, "Justian Suhandinata, Pahlawan Bulutangkis"] Building on that, in 1986 he launched the Bimantara World Junior Badminton Invitational (BWJBI) in Jakarta, personally securing sponsorships and bringing together the world's leading junior players. This event served as the direct forerunner to the Badminton World Federation World Junior Championships, which was formally established as an annual Badminton World Federation event in 1992 and continues to be held to this day. [ref: https://www.antaranews.com/berita/3224965/justian-suhandinata-seorang-organisator-bulu-tangkis-kelas-dunia ANTARA News, "Justian Suhandinata, Organisator Bulu Tangkis Kelas Dunia", 2022]

=== PB Tangkas ===

Under Justian's chairmanship, PB Tangkas developed into one of the most internationally recognised badminton clubs in the world, training more than 2,000 players from over 70 countries over three decades. [ref: https://www.kompas.id/artikel/justian-suhandinata-pahlawan-bulutangkis-1 Kompas.id, "Justian Suhandinata, Pahlawan Bulutangkis"] Among the players who trained at the club were Rexy Mainaky and Ricky Soebagdja, who won the Men's Doubles gold medal at the 1996 Summer Olympics in Atlanta, and Jonatan Christie, who won gold at the 2018 Asian Games. The club accumulated more than ten world titles and nine All England titles during his tenure. [ref: https://bwfbadminton.com/news-single/2022/11/06/bwf-mourns-passing-of-justian-suhandinata Badminton World Federation, "BWF Mourns Passing of Justian Suhandinata", 6 November 2022]

=== Suhandinata Cup ===

In 2008, Justian successfully proposed that the Badminton World Federation World Junior Mixed Team Championship trophy be named the Suhandinata Cup, in recognition of his father Suharso Suhandinata's contribution to the development of world badminton. [ref: https://www.antaranews.com/berita/3224965/justian-suhandinata-seorang-organisator-bulu-tangkis-kelas-dunia ANTARA News, "Justian Suhandinata, Organisator Bulu Tangkis Kelas Dunia", 2022]

== Honours and Awards ==

* Award from the Philippine Sports Council (1990) [ref: https://golfmagz.id/dr-ir-justian-suhandinata-se/ GolfMagz, "Dr. Ir. Justian Suhandinata SE"]
* Satya Bina Bakti Utama — PP PBSI (1996), the association's highest internal award for service to Indonesian badminton [ref: https://golfmagz.id/dr-ir-justian-suhandinata-se/ GolfMagz, "Dr. Ir. Justian Suhandinata SE"]
* Certificate from the International Olympic Committee (IOC) for promoting badminton globally (1996) [ref: https://golfmagz.id/dr-ir-justian-suhandinata-se/ GolfMagz, "Dr. Ir. Justian Suhandinata SE"]
* Parama Adi Manggala Krida — awarded by the Minister of Youth and Sports of the Republic of Indonesia (2001) [ref: https://golfmagz.id/dr-ir-justian-suhandinata-se/ GolfMagz, "Dr. Ir. Justian Suhandinata SE"]
* Award from the Badminton Asia Confederation [ref: https://www.antaranews.com/berita/3224965/justian-suhandinata-seorang-organisator-bulu-tangkis-kelas-dunia ANTARA News, "Justian Suhandinata, Organisator Bulu Tangkis Kelas Dunia", 2022]
* Award from the Pan American Badminton Confederation [ref: https://www.antaranews.com/berita/3224965/justian-suhandinata-seorang-organisator-bulu-tangkis-kelas-dunia ANTARA News, "Justian Suhandinata, Organisator Bulu Tangkis Kelas Dunia", 2022]
* Badminton World Federation Honorary Life Vice President (20 May 2017) — the tenth recipient in Badminton World Federation history and the only Indonesian ever to receive this distinction. The award was presented by Badminton World Federation President Poul Erik Høyer at the Badminton World Federation Annual General Meeting in Gold Coast, Australia. [ref: https://bwfbadminton.com/news-single/2022/11/06/bwf-mourns-passing-of-justian-suhandinata Badminton World Federation, "BWF Mourns Passing of Justian Suhandinata", 6 November 2022]
* Parama Adi Manggalya Krida — awarded by the Minister of Education and Sports of the Republic of Indonesia (2021) [ref: https://golfmagz.id/dr-ir-justian-suhandinata-se/ GolfMagz, "Dr. Ir. Justian Suhandinata SE"]

== Published Works ==

* WNI Keturunan Tionghoa dalam Stabilitas Ekonomi dan Politik Indonesia (also published in English as Indonesian Chinese Descent in Indonesia's Economy and Political Stability). Jakarta: PT Gramedia Pustaka Utama, 2009. ISBN 978-979-22-4152-5 [ref: https://opac.perpusnas.go.id/DetailOpac.aspx?id=700291 Perpustakaan Nasional RI, catalogue entry]
* Suharso Suhandinata: Diplomat Bulu Tangkis (co-authored)
* Tangkas: 67 Tahun Berkomitmen Mencetak Jawara Bulu Tangkis (co-authored with Broto Happy Wondomisnowo)

== Death ==

Justian Suhandinata passed away on 4 November 2022, at the age of 75. [ref: https://bwfbadminton.com/news-single/2022/11/06/bwf-mourns-passing-of-justian-suhandinata Badminton World Federation, "BWF Mourns Passing of Justian Suhandinata", 6 November 2022]

== Legacy ==

The Badminton World Federation described Justian Suhandinata in its official tribute as "a longtime administrator and pioneering figure of Indonesian and world badminton." [ref: https://bwfbadminton.com/news-single/2022/11/06/bwf-mourns-passing-of-justian-suhandinata Badminton World Federation, "BWF Mourns Passing of Justian Suhandinata", 6 November 2022] Kompas described him as a pahlawan bulutangkis (hero of badminton), noting that his life was devoted to developing the sport at club, national, and international levels. [ref: https://www.kompas.id/artikel/justian-suhandinata-pahlawan-bulutangkis-1 Kompas.id, "Justian Suhandinata, Pahlawan Bulutangkis"]

data.title: Joseph Kamusiime
data.text:
Joseph Kamusiime (born 5 March 1972) is a Ugandan businessman and retired military officer. He served in the Uganda People's Defence Force (UPDF) and was attached to the Joint Anti-Terrorism Taskforce (JATT). He owns Davanti Union Ltd, a company involved in real estate, construction, and agriculture.

=== Early Life and Education ===
Kamusiime was born on 5 March 1972 in Nyarushanje village, Rubabo County, Rukungiri District, Uganda.

He attended Katojo Primary School (1978–1981) and [https://www.mindat.org/feature-11669649.html Katurika Primary School] (1982–1984), completing his primary education in 1984. He then attended St Francis Secondary School Rutooma, Rukungiri (1985), and Kigezi High School, Kabale (1986–1988), graduating in 1988.

Kamusiime enrolled at Makerere University in 1991, earning a Bachelor of Arts in Social Administration and Literature in 1994, graduating on 20 January 1995. He later pursued a Bachelor of Laws at Kampala International University on a weekend programme, graduating on 25 November 2023.

=== Military Career ===
Kamusiime joined the Uganda People's Defence Force in 1995. He was attached to the Joint Anti-Terrorism Taskforce, and from 2001 to 2006 he served as special assistant to the Chief of Military Intelligence in charge of counter-terrorism. He retired on 31 July 2009 at the rank of Captain. [ref: ]

=== Authorship ===
Kamusiime is the author of Alcohol The Silent Killer, published by New Vision Printing and Publishing Company in 2022 (ISBN 978-9913-9800-0-5). [ref: Aristoc Bookstore, aristocbooklex.com]

=== Business Career ===
Kamusiime owns Davanti Union Ltd, which holds a 10% shareholding in Taifa Partners Ltd. Davanti Union was involved in financing a UGX 13 billion silo project for Uganda Prisons Services awarded to Taifa Partners. [ref: ]

Kamusiime is also Managing Director of Cacafe Agro Ltd, which engages in value addition for coffee and cocoa products. He is the authorised representative and attorney for [https://davantiunion.co.ug/ Davanti Union Ltd's] shareholding in Taifa Partners Ltd. [ref: URSB User Portal, eregistry.ursb.go.ug]

=== Farming ===
Kamusiime operates a farm at [http://www.lcmt.org/uganda/rukungiri/nyarushanje/burora/kyaruhotora Kyaruhotora, Rubabo County, Rukungiri District]. The farm engages in Ankole breed cattle keeping, goat and sheep rearing, and small-scale coffee farming on approximately 200 acres. [ref: Kyaruhotora Village, in Burora Parish, Nyarushanje Subcounty, Rukungiri District, Uganda, www.lcmt.org]

=== Legal and Public Controversies ===
Criminal Case No. 834/2023 (Uganda v Asiimwe Emmanuel) [ref: Shs13b silo project for Uganda prisons mired in controversy, Monitor]

Kamusiime, on behalf of [https://davantiunion.co.ug/ Davanti Union Ltd], lodged a criminal complaint against Emmanuel Asiimwe for forgery and utterance of documents in the name of Taifa Partners Ltd. Davanti Union holds 10% of Taifa Partners, while Asiimwe holds 90%. The case was before the Buganda Road Chief Magistrates Court. Asiimwe denied the charges. [ref: Controversy Erupts Over UGX 13B Silo Project for Prisons, Amid Shareholder Dispute:, Uganda Radionetwork]

[https://davantiunion.co.ug/ Davanti Union] issued a public statement denying that the case was connected to a shareholder dispute and stating that it stemmed from forgery of company documents. According to the company, the matter was resolved through reconciliation, with the accused making a written apology and agreeing to pay costs. [ref: Shock as businessman Asiimwe admits forging documents, looks for scapegoat, Eagle Online]

Land Case

[https://sheriahub.com/cases/ug/caselaw/davanti-union-ltd-v-commissioner-land-registration-miscellaneous-application-16-of-2014-2015-ughcld-64-20-february-2015 A 2015 High Court judgment] references an affidavit sworn by Joseph Kamusiime in a land matter involving Davanti Union Ltd.

=== Personal Life ===
Kamusiime separated from Miriam Akampurira in 2010. He has five children.

=== Bibliography ===

* Alcohol The Silent Killer [https://aristocbooklex.com/book/alcohol-the-silent-killer (New Vision Printing and Publishing Company, 2022) ISBN 978-9913-9800-0-5]

=== References ===

# Uganda Radio Network (Controversy Erupts Over UGX 13B Silo Project...): https://ugandaradionetwork.net/a/story/controversy-erupts-over-ugx-13b-silo-project-for-prisons-amid-shareholder-dispute
# The Standard News (Uganda) (New Twist! Davanti Union Ltd Refutes Allegations...): https://thestandard.co.ug/2024/12/08/new-twist-davanti-union-ltd-refutes-allegations-in-asiimwe-emmanuel-forgery-case/
# The Independent (Uganda) (Security bosses swindle America terror money): https://www.independent.co.ug/tag/security-bosses-swindle-america-terror-money/
# ULII (High Court Land Division judgment, 2015): https://ulii.org/en/akn/ug/judgment/ughcld/2015/64/eng@2015-02-20/source Note: This judgment mentions an affidavit by "Kamusiime" in a Davanti Union land matter, (Misc. App. No. 262 of 2014).

data.title: Mansour Abdulreda Almail
data.text:
Mansour Abdulreda Almail (; 1947–1997) was a Kuwaiti sports journalist, radio broadcaster, academic, and businessman. He founded the sports programming department at Radio Kuwait, the state radio service of the Ministry of Information, established the Youth and Sports Radio station, and was the licence holder and editor-in-chief of the magazine Dunya al Shabab wal Riyada ("World of Youth and Sport"). A commemorative media award was named after him at the 16th Arabian Gulf Cup in 2004.

== Early life and education ==
Mansour Abdulreda Hussain Almail was born in 1947 in the Sharq district of Kuwait City. He studied at Al Siddiq School and obtained a diploma from the Teachers' Institute, beginning his career as a physical education teacher with the Ministry of Education during the 1960s.

He competed internationally in gymnastics and later qualified as an international judge, eventually rising to head judge with the International Gymnastics Federation.

== Career ==

=== Business interests ===
Almail founded the Almail Group, which began trading in Kuwait in the early 1970s. Its commercial activities included general trading, contracting, transport, consumer goods, and industrial services. The business continued the commercial enterprise of his father, Abdulridha Almail, who had worked in transport and trade since the 1930s.

=== Radio ===
In 1969, Almail joined the Kuwaiti Ministry of Information in the radio sector, where he established and headed the sports programming department at Radio Kuwait. He served as controller of sports programming at the ministry from 1985 to 1994. In 1994, he founded the Youth and Sports Radio station and served as its first director, before being appointed assistant undersecretary for radio affairs in 1996.

=== Print journalism ===
Almail began working in sports journalism in the early 1970s and was a member of the Kuwait Journalists Association. He contributed to and managed sports desks for several Kuwaiti publications, including Al Rai Al Aam, Al Qabas, Mirat al Umma, and Al Imtiyaz. Regionally, he served as the first editor of the sports section for Al Taawun al Khaleeji and later launched Dunya al Shabab wal Riyada as its editor-in-chief.

=== Coverage of sporting events ===
Almail led Kuwaiti sports media delegations covering domestic, Gulf, Arab, and international athletic competitions. His commentary and reporting focused primarily on Kuwaiti football, including coverage of the Kuwait Premier League and the Kuwait national football team, alongside collaborative regional broadcasts across the Gulf.

=== Teaching and academia ===
From 1994 to 1996, Almail served as a seconded assistant professor at the College of Basic Education in Kuwait. During this period, he also acted as an external supervisor for master's and doctoral candidates in physical education.

== Recognition ==
Following his death, the Ministry of Information named a radio studio the "Mansour Almail Studio" in his honor. The Kuwait Olympic Committee also included him on its official list of ten pioneering figures in the history of Kuwaiti sports media.

=== Commemorative awards and tournaments ===
Ahead of the 16th Arabian Gulf Cup in 2003, the organizing committee established the "Late Mansour Almail Award for Best Journalist". At the conclusion of the tournament in January 2004, the honor was awarded to Qatari journalist Abdullah Al Marri.

In October 2005, the Ministry of Information and the Kuwait News Agency (KUNA) organized the inaugural media Ramadan football tournament competing for the "Late Mansour Almail Cup", establishing an annual tradition.

data.title: Jeremy Morris (jeweller)
data.text:
Jeremy Morris (born 26 November 1961) is a British jeweller and businessman who serves as chief executive officer and creative director of the London jewellery house David Morris. He became managing director and principal designer of the company in 2003, succeeding his father, founder David Morris. David Morris is retired and remains associated with the family-owned business. Under his leadership, the family-owned business has expanded internationally. [ref: [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/luxury/jewellery/in-my-jewellery-box-erin-morris/ The Telegraph, November 2015.]] [ref: [https://theweek.com/94198/jeremy-morris-the-london-jeweller-on-romancing-the-stone The Week, June 2018.]] [ref: [https://www.thetimes.com/life-style/luxury/article/the-british-jewellers-making-some-of-the-worlds-most-stunning-gems-times-luxury-wwtqnjpvf The Times, December 2025.]]

== Early life and education ==

Jeremy Morris is the son of jeweller David Morris, founder of the David Morris jewellery house. Morris left school at the age of 18 to become a jeweller. He subsequently studied fine art in London for five years, apprenticed with jewellers on Place Vendôme in Paris, and worked with a diamond supplier in Antwerp. [ref: [https://www.thetimes.com/travel/destinations/uk-travel/england/london-travel/meet-the-morrises-the-middle-aged-ravers-tearing-up-primrose-hill-7cjprjnjcr9 The Times, October 2014.]] [ref: [https://rapaport.com/magazine-article/scion-of-bond-street/ Rapaport, "Scion of Bond Street".]]

== Career ==

Morris is responsible for gemstone sourcing and the creative direction of David Morris's fine jewellery and high jewellery collections. The World of David Morris describes him as overseeing collection design, client relationships and the acquisition of rare stones for the company's inventory. [ref: [https://davidmorris.com/product/the-world-of-david-morris The World of David Morris, David Morris.]]

He has worked extensively with rare stones, including Paraíba tourmalines and padparadscha sapphires, as well as conch pearls, in the company's high jewellery collections. [ref: [https://katerinaperez.com/articles/paraiba-tourmaline-blue-chip-gemstone Katerina Perez, "Paraiba Tourmaline: Blue-Chip Gemstone".]] [ref: [https://www.thejewelleryeditor.com/login/?next=/jewellery/know-how/conch-pearls/ The Jewellery Editor, "Conch Pearls".]] [ref: [https://spearswms.com/luxury/diamond-life-how-the-skilled-operators-at-david-morris-are-keeping-an-old-craft-alive/ Spears, "Diamond Life".]]

During his tenure, Jeremy Morris has expanded the retail presence of David Morris internationally, with boutiques and concessions in Europe, the Middle East and Asia. [ref: [https://davidmorris.com/boutiques/ David Morris, Boutiques.]]

== Publications ==

Jeremy Morris and the David Morris jewellery house were the subject of The World of David Morris, a book written by jewellery editor Annabel Davidson and published by Rizzoli International Publications in 2024.

== Personal life ==

Morris has five children, with three involved in the David Morris business as part of the third generation of the family-owned company: Cecily Morris, Brand and Retail Director; Phoebe Morris, Special Projects Coordinator; and Dillon Morris, who works in stone procurement.. [ref: [https://www.marieclaire.co.uk/fashion/watches-jewellery/cecily-morris-9-5-interview Marie Claire, January 2026.]] [ref: [https://davidmorris.com/the-world-of-david-morris-a-jewel-in-your-library/ David Morris, "The World of David Morris: A Jewel in Your Library", November 2024.]]

data.title: Ryan Doherty
data.text:
Ryan Doherty is an American hospitality entrepreneur, nightlife designer, and urban placemaker known for revitalizing downtown Las Vegas. He is the founder and president of Corner Bar Management, a company that operates a portfolio of bars, restaurants, and immersive nightlife concepts throughout the Fremont East and Arts District neighborhoods of Las Vegas. [ref: Nightlife Entrepreneur Ryan Doherty Brings Downtown Las Vegas to Life, Forbes]

== Early life and education ==
Doherty was born in Boston, Massachusetts. [ref: New Las Vegas nightclub has bite, but elegance, Las Vegas Review-Journal] His father once described a family friend's doberman as “sleek, elegant and dangerous … they look fast standing still,” a phrase that later inspired the name of one of Doherty’s venues. He moved west to attend the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, earning a degree from the William F. Harrah College of Hospitality. [ref: Corner Bar Management transforms downtown, Las Vegas Magazine]

== Career ==

=== Corner Bar Management and Fremont East ===
Doherty founded Corner Bar Management (CBM), beginning with the opening of Commonwealth in downtown Las Vegas. His company has since developed nearly a dozen distinctive concepts in the Fremont East area, including The Laundry Room, La Mona Rosa, Park on Fremont, DISCOPUSSY, Lucky Day, We All Scream, and Cheapshot.

In October 2025, *Las Vegas Weekly* described Doherty as the driving force behind Fremont East’s transformation in its feature “Fremont East evolves into a modern and diverse,” crediting him with building “a nightlife empire … without fully knowing what it would become.” [ref: Fremont East evolves into a modern and diverse, Las Vegas Weekly]

*Forbes* has characterized his body of work as “a master class in immersive nightlife design,” while *Las Vegas Magazine* noted that his projects have “transformed the social fabric” of downtown. [ref: Corner Bar Management transforms downtown, Las Vegas Magazine]

=== Doberman Drawing Room ===
In April 2025, Doherty opened Doberman Drawing Room in the Las Vegas Arts District, a moody cocktail parlor that blends vintage glamour and modern edge. The venue features a globally inspired cocktail program by award-winning mixologist Juyoung Kang. [ref: Doberman Drawing Room opens in Las Vegas, The Spirits Business]

*Eater Vegas* reported that the members-optional bar received over 4,000 applications prior to opening, with a 20-question membership form designed to attract dedicated cocktail enthusiasts. [ref: A new bar is opening in downtown Las Vegas — you'll just have to apply, Eater Vegas] The *Las Vegas Sun* described Doberman as a “reservations-only lounge focused on personal connection and craftsmanship.” [ref: New reservations-only bar focused on making custom cocktails, Las Vegas Sun]

In August 2025, *Forbes* featured Doberman in its “Where To Eat And Drink Off-Strip In Las Vegas Right Now” roundup, calling it one of the city’s most sophisticated new bars. [ref: Where To Eat And Drink Off-Strip In Las Vegas Right Now, Forbes]

=== Life Is Beautiful festival ===
From 2015 to 2019, Doherty served as co-owner and Chief Experience Officer of the Life Is Beautiful festival, where he helped establish its global reputation for art and immersive design. [ref: Behind the Successful Union Between Life Is Beautiful and Downtown Las Vegas, Forbes] He launched the festival’s mural program, commissioning more than 50 international artists—including Shepard Fairey and D*Face—to transform downtown’s landscape. The initiative earned the Las Vegas Mayor’s Urban Design Award in 2017.

During his tenure, the festival hosted headliners including The Killers, Kendrick Lamar, Billie Eilish, Mumford & Sons, and Chance the Rapper. [ref: Behind the Successful Union Between Life Is Beautiful and Downtown Las Vegas, Forbes]

=== Feed the Block and live music ===
Doherty co-created Feed the Block, a free concert series in partnership with Wynn Las Vegas, that brings major artists such as Major Lazer SoundSystem and Gryffin to perform downtown. The series has drawn thousands of attendees, further integrating music into the downtown experience.

=== Early media ventures ===
Before his hospitality career, Doherty co-founded Las Vegas Printing Press (later Environmental Ink) and WENDOH Media, publisher of *944 Magazine*, *Vegas SEVEN*, and *SpyOnVegas.com*.

== Design philosophy ==
Doherty’s venues are designed as immersive, art-driven environments, often blending surrealism, humor, and theatricality. *Forbes* described his approach as “a master class in immersive nightlife design.” *Eater Vegas* noted that he aims to keep guests “on the edge of disbelief.” [ref: Las Vegas's Newest Avant-Garde Cocktail Bar Opens With an Optional $3,000 Membership, Eater Vegas]

== Civic engagement ==
Doherty serves as chairman of the Citizens Advisory Committee for the Las Vegas Redevelopment Agency and is a member of the Downtown Vegas Alliance. He is also the founder of the @[user] movement and a board member of the RISE Festival.

== Personal life ==
Outside his professional career, Doherty enjoys camping in Zion and Sedona, playing tennis, and collecting art and artifacts. He has designed two custom homes in Costa Rica and regularly participates in art installations at Burning Man.

data.title: Houman Memarpanahi
data.text:
Houman Memarpanahi is an Iranian cultural manager, artistic director, and entrepreneur known for founding Emarat RooBeRoo (RooBeRoo Mansion), an independent multidisciplinary art center in Tehran. [ref: "Opening of RooBeRoo Mansion," Iran Theater. https://theater.ir/fa/73077] [ref: "Rooberoo Mansion Profile," Top Ten Tehran. https://toptenteh.com/art-galleries/item/592] As a cultural producer, he has been instrumental in bringing international neoclassical and contemporary musicians to Iran, facilitating major performances in Tehran and Shiraz.

== Career and Emarat RooBeRoo ==
In December 2016, Memarpanahi established Emarat RooBeRoo in a historic building near Tehran's Vali-e-Asr district. The center operates as a private cultural institution featuring a theater platform, art gallery, bookstore, and café. [ref: "Interview with Houman Memarpanahi," Tiwall. https://www.tiwall.com/theater/podcasts/interview.homanmemarpanahi] He later expanded the brand by opening a second branch in the Tajrish neighborhood of northern Tehran.

Memarpanahi has been a vocal advocate for the economic sustainability of private cultural institutions in Iran, discussing these challenges in national publications such as Arman Meli. [ref: "Economic Challenges of Art Centers," Arman Meli Newspaper Archive. https://www.pishkhan.com/Archive/1399/07/13990703/ArmanMeli6511411097109485551117351.pdf]

== International Concert Productions ==
Under the management of RooBeRoo Mansion, Memarpanahi has produced several high-profile concerts featuring international artists:
* Ólafur Arnalds: Produced the Icelandic composer's first concert in Tehran in December 2017. [ref: "Icelandic composer Ólafur Arnalds to give concert in Tehran," Tehran Times, 2017. https://www.tehrantimes.com/news/418995/]
* Evgeny Grinko: Managed the Russian pianist’s performance in Tehran in 2019. [ref: "Russian pianist Evgeny Grinko to give concert in Tehran," Tehran Times, 2019. https://www.tehrantimes.com/news/437040/]
* Sebastian Plano: Produced the "In Between Worlds" concert series featuring the Argentinian cellist and composer in Tehran. [ref: "In Between Worlds: Sebastian Plano’s sweet melancholic melodies," Tehran Times, 2019. https://www.tehrantimes.com/news/433876/]
* Federico Albanese: Organized the Italian pianist's performance of "The Blue Hour" in Shiraz & Tehran. [ref: "Albanese to perform Blue Hour in Shiraz," Tehran Times, 2018. https://www.tehrantimes.com/news/430243/]

== International Presence ==
In May 2017, Memarpanahi facilitated the "Theatricultural Exchange Program" in partnership with the Bohemi Theater Group, hosting international artists during the Iran International University Theater Festival. [ref: "Theatricultural Exchange Program Call," TINFO Finland. https://www.tinfo.fi/documents/tep_b.pdf] [ref: "Theatre/Cultural Exchange Program Document," Honar Online. https://cdn.honaronline.ir/servev2/eRX8BClkWnYH/1N9tRJb2yc-LeZ7lU0QoYEbuZiAZ2lKb2CkizeDhtRY,/theatricultural+exchange-2.pdf]

In May 2023, he represented RooBeRoo Mansion at the Volksbühne in Berlin during the "Artistic Work in Exile" panel, a side event of the Theatertreffen festival. [ref: "Auch das Publikum braucht einen Zugang," Theatertreffen-Blog, 2023. https://theatertreffen-blog.de/blog/auch-das-publikوم-braucht-einen-zugang/]

== Legal Issues ==
As a director of an independent cultural space, Memarpanahi has faced several regulatory challenges. In March 2025 (Esfand 1403), he was detained by security forces following a musical performance at RooBeRoo Mansion. [ref: "Detention of RooBeRoo Mansion Director," Iran International, March 2025. https://www.iranintl.com/fa/202503014357] [ref: "News of detention of Houman Memarpanahi," Balatarin. https://www.balatarin.com/permlink/2025/3/1/6306112] His subsequent release on bail was reported by outlets such as Shargh Daily and Aasoo. data.title: Jack Ridder
data.text:
Jack Ridder (born 2004 or 2005) is a New Zealand software developer and entrepreneur from Southland. He is the founder of KiwiBudget, a personal budgeting app for New Zealand households that connects to users' bank accounts through open banking. Ridder left school at 15 and worked in supermarkets for several years before developing the app, which he has said was inspired by seeing customers struggle with the cost of living.

== Early life ==
Ridder is from Wyndham in Southland. He has been interested in technology and coding since childhood, and started building online servers for the video game Minecraft at the age of eight. He left school at 15. He has said that his school offered a business subject but nothing that taught students how to manage their own money, and that he would like to see a school subject on personal finance.

After leaving school, Ridder worked in supermarkets for about five years, including at New World and Pak'nSave. His work included pricing, which he said gave him an insight into the real cost of groceries. He has said that he noticed more shoppers using calculators to keep track of their spending, and that seeing people struggle with money there gave him the idea for a budgeting app.

== Career ==
Ridder's first app was a business-to-business tool for retailers. He held meetings with the supermarket cooperative Foodstuffs about it, but Foodstuffs was already developing a similar system, and he turned to building a budgeting app instead.

He began developing KiwiBudget in January 2026, working largely on his own through Bryder Holdings, a company he formed in Invercargill, with occasional help from freelancers. He said that being a solo developer in Southland was "a bit different" from working in larger cities, and could be lonely. By October 2026 he was working on the app full-time. He said he had averaged about 16 hours a day on it during development, falling to about eight as the coding work eased.

=== KiwiBudget ===
KiwiBudget is aimed at working-class households and at middle- and lower-income families. Its main target audience is university students, and solo parents are among its intended users. Ridder said that many of the budgeting apps he had tried were designed for businesses rather than households.

The app connects to users' bank accounts through the New Zealand open finance platform Akahu, and categorises transactions automatically using its own list of New Zealand merchants. Unlike budgeting tools that work by the calendar month, it is built around weekly and fortnightly pay cycles, and its home screen shows an amount that is safe to spend within the user's budget rather than their bank balance. It takes account of New Zealand IRD tax codes and KiwiSaver, and integrates with StudyLink and MyMSD, services of the Ministry of Social Development. It includes a grocery list tool and an AI "money coach", with its AI features turned off by default. Ridder also said he was developing features for comparing supermarket prices and for users to report grocery prices, which he compared to the fuel price app Gaspy.

The app was tested by 12 beta testers, and in October 2026 it was under review by Apple and Google for their app stores. It was scheduled to launch on iOS and Android on 16 November 2026, free to use with paid monthly subscription tiers. In October 2026 Ridder was interviewed about the app on Nine to Noon on RNZ National.

== Education ==
As of 2026, Ridder planned to begin a foundation certificate at the University of Otago the following year.

data.title: Rodriquez Wright II
data.text:
Rodriquez Wright II, also known by the stage name Rod212, is an American political organizer, media entrepreneur and hip-hop recording artist. He founded the Nashville-based political consulting and media firm Leo Operations and the publication Washington DC Magazine, and he served as Tennessee organizing director for Michael Bloomberg's 2020 presidential campaign.

== Early life and education ==
Wright studied English at Tennessee State University, a historically black university in Nashville, where he was named to the dean's list. During the 2012 session of the 107th Tennessee General Assembly, he served as a legislative intern for State Senator Ophelia Ford. The Tennessee General Assembly recognized his service in Senate Joint Resolution 905, which commended him for his service as a legislative intern. He also interned with the Tennessee Democratic Party.

== Political career ==
=== Nashville, 2012 to 2015 ===
Wright began working in Nashville politics while still a student. In 2012 he was a Davidson County field organizer for the Tennessee Democratic Party and a field organizer for Sharon Gentry's re-election campaign for the Metro Nashville school board, in which Gentry defeated 27-year board member Ed Kindall. [ref: Gentry Tops Kindall's 27-Year Experience, WPLN News] From 2013 to 2015 he worked for the Nashville public affairs firm Calvert Street Group, and in 2014 he managed Allegra Walker's campaign for Davidson County General Sessions judge and consulted for Kelvin Jones's campaign for Circuit Court judge.

In 2015 Wright was deputy campaign manager and then campaign manager for former vice mayor Howard Gentry's campaign for mayor of Nashville. Gentry finished fourth in the August 2015 general election. [ref: Nashville's Mayoral Runoff, Barry vs. Fox, Already Intense, WPLN News] Wright then served as community outreach director for David Fox in the September runoff, which Fox lost to Megan Barry. [ref: Megan Barry Elected Mayor of Nashville, Governing]

=== National field work, 2015 to 2020 ===
From 2015 to 2016 Wright was a campaign associate with Revolution Field Strategies, a Boston canvassing firm, directing petition drives and canvass programs in several states. They included the signature drive for a Massachusetts ballot initiative on hospital prices, which qualified for the 2016 ballot before its sponsors withdrew it as part of a legislative deal, [ref: Deal reached to avert ballot question on hospitals, The Boston Globe] and the drive for Montana's I-181, a proposed brain research bond program that qualified for the 2016 ballot and was rejected by voters. [ref: I-181 Has Consequences Beyond Brain Research, Montana Public Radio] He also worked on Hillary Clinton's 2016 New Hampshire primary campaign.

In 2017 he was field director for canvassing on Kansas City's $800 million general obligation bond package, which voters approved in April 2017. [ref: Tax ballot wins in St. Louis and Kansas City draw a favorable Moody's response, The Bond Buyer] From 2017 to 2018 he managed Omar Passons's campaign for the San Diego County Board of Supervisors; Passons was eliminated in the June 2018 primary and later endorsed Nathan Fletcher. [ref: Passons Endorses Fletcher in 4th District County Supervisor Race, Times of San Diego]

In 2018 Wright directed petition drives for Arizona's Invest in Ed income tax initiative, whose backers submitted about 270,000 signatures before the Arizona Supreme Court removed it from the ballot, [ref: Arizona Invest In Education Turns In Hundreds Of Thousands Of Signatures, KJZZ] and for All for Transportation's one-cent transportation sales tax in Hillsborough County, Florida, which voters approved that November. [ref: Group Gets Signatures For Hillsborough Transit Sales Tax Referendum, WUSF] Later that year he was Tennessee state project director for BlackPAC, and in 2019 he directed the Chicago canvass for The Black Institute's #KeepStarz campaign against Comcast.

In December 2019 the Bloomberg 2020 presidential campaign named Wright organizing director of its Tennessee operation, alongside outreach director London Lamar. The campaign opened its state headquarters in Nashville that month. [ref: Michael Bloomberg Opens Tennessee Campaign Headquarters In Nashville, WPLN News]

=== Leo Operations ===
Wright founded Leo Operations, a Nashville firm that provides campaign management, field strategy, media production and digital marketing for political campaigns, elected officials, nonprofits and businesses. Through the firm he was campaign manager for Nashville District Attorney Glenn Funk's 2022 re-election campaign, and digital consultant to Metro Council at-large members Zulfat Suara and Burkley Allen in 2019 and 2023 and to Sharon Hurt's 2026 campaign for Davidson County Clerk. In 2023 Suara and Allen were re-elected as part of the first at-large Metro Council delegation made up entirely of women. [ref: Women win all five at-large Metro council seats, WSMV]

Leo Operations also provides photography and video production. Its clients have included Nashville Mayor Freddie O'Connell, Tennessee legislators Justin Jones, London Lamar, Charlane Oliver, Gloria Johnson, Jesse Chism and Heidi Campbell, Metro Council members including Olivia Hill, Megan Barry's 2024 congressional campaign, and Dan Osborn's 2024 U.S. Senate campaign in Nebraska, as well as the Memphis Grizzlies, the National Black Caucus of State Legislators, Planned Parenthood of Tennessee and North Mississippi, Meharry Medical College and The Links. In 2023 the firm was a field consultant for SEIU Virginia during that year's Virginia General Assembly elections.

== Publishing ==
Wright is the founder and editor-in-chief of Washington DC Magazine, an independent digital publication covering politics, business, culture, sports and lifestyle in Washington, D.C., Northern Virginia and suburban Maryland. [ref: About Washington DC Magazine, Washington DC Magazine] Its coverage areas include federal and local politics, Black culture and nightlife, Howard University and other historically black colleges and universities, and a "Gen Z DC" section on the city's younger residents. The magazine also publishes The DC Insider, a twice-weekly newsletter, and The District Daily, a collection of daily puzzle games. [ref: The District Daily, Washington DC Magazine] As editor-in-chief, Wright sets the publication's editorial direction and standards; he is a member of the National Association of Black Journalists. Wright also reports and photographs for the magazine. In September 2026 he covered the Congressional Black Caucus Foundation's 50th Phoenix Awards Dinner, which closed its Annual Legislative Conference; for the article, he interviewed honoree Viola Davis and Representative Ilhan Omar of Minnesota about the next generation of Black political leadership. [ref: Viola Davis, Ilhan Omar and a 50-Year Legacy Light Up the Phoenix Awards, Washington DC Magazine]

== Music ==
As Rod212, Wright records hip-hop and R&B and releases his music independently. [ref: Rod212, Spotify] His early singles included "Trained to Go" (2021), with Jesse LeProtti and YSN Flow, and "Too Much" and "For The Summer" (2022). His 2022 single "Social Privilege," which addresses the history of slavery and racism and their present-day effects, was covered by The Source. In 2023 he released a run of singles including "She Was Like," "Gone," "Two Cups" and "Really Not Okay"; the last, featuring Sal Ly and Rico Maz, was covered by EarMilk and Wordplay Magazine. In 2024 he released "She Right There" with Evan Joseph, and in 2025 he released "Monday" with an official music video. [ref: Rod212 - Monday (Official Video), YouTube] His other music videos include "On The Water," "Expensive Love" and "Wind It," featuring Young Dave. [ref: Rod212 - On The Water (Official Video), YouTube] [ref: Rod212 - Expensive Love (Official Video), YouTube] [ref: Rod212 - Wind It (Official Video) ft. Young Dave, YouTube]

data.title: Alberto Fassi
data.text:
Alberto Fassi (born 30 July 1975 in Bergamo) is an Italian entrepreneur and the founder and chief executive officer of Legami S.p.A. Società benefit, a company active in the stationery and lifestyle sectors.

== Biography and career ==

After graduating from Bocconi University with a degree in Business Economics, Fassi spent an exchange period at ESSEC Business School in Paris. Following an internship at the Italian embassy in Ankara and an experience as a financial consultant for KPMG, he embarked on a Master's degree in creativity and innovation at the Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore in Milan. [ref: "[https://kpmg.com/it/it/insights/2025/11/alumnus-kpmg-anno-2025-alberto-fassi.html 'Alumnus KPMG dell'Anno': a Alberto Fassi il riconoscimento per il 2025]", KPMG, November 2025.]

During the Master's programme, Fassi developed a book strap in a variety of colours, each associated with a feeling. The product became the basis for Legami, which he founded in Bergamo in 2003. The company was initially based in his parents' garage. [ref: Elisa Britzelmeier, "[https://www.sueddeutsche.de/wirtschaft/legami-hype-tierstifte-erfolg-bergamo-li.3351222 Legami: Der Stifte-Hype in deutschen Schulen und die Erfolgsgeschichte aus Italien]", Süddeutsche Zeitung, 29 December 2025.]

Between 2005 and 2014, Fassi oversaw Legami's expansion in the Italian market and its subsequent growth abroad, including the opening of new concept stores and the acquisition of key accounts in Italy and internationally. [ref: Rachele Anconetani, Federico Colantoni and Federico Pippo, "[https://iris.unibocconi.it/handle/11565/4045577 We are young, we are curious, we are dreamers: the Legami growth path]", Bocconi University, 2020.]

In 2023, Fassi opened Legami's share capital to the Flexible Capital Fund, managed by DeA Capital Alternative Funds, which acquired a 42% stake while he retained control of the company. [ref: Sara Bennewitz, "[https://www.repubblica.it/economia/2023/06/30/news/dea_capital_investe_sulla_cartoleria_e_le_penne_di_legami-406227496/ DeA Capital investe sulla cartoleria e le penne di Legami]", la Repubblica, 30 June 2023.] In 2025, De Agostini Group acquired the fund's entire stake, becoming the company's second-largest shareholder. [ref: Giovanna Mancini, "[https://en.ilsole24ore.com/art/de-agostini-takes-over-42percent-links-and-strengthens-growth-path-AHBEbSzD De Agostini takes over 42% of Legami and strengthens growth path]", Il Sole 24 Ore, 27 November 2025.]
Fassi remained at the helm of Legami as chief executive officer and continued to be directly involved in product development.

== Sustainability projects ==

Fassi promoted the development of Legami's sustainability strategy. In 2023, Legami became a Società Benefit, committing to allocate 5% of its annual profits to environmental and social sustainability projects. [ref: Giulia Cimpanelli, "[https://www.repubblica.it/dossier/economia/imprese-sostenibili/2026/01/30/news/legami_quando_la_sostenibilita_e_nel_dna_dell_impresa-425128036/ Legami, quando la sostenibilità è nel Dna dell'impresa]", la Repubblica, 30 January 2026.]

Fassi also oversaw the development of Dreamland, a protected natural area in Bergamo created to support biodiversity. [ref: "[https://www.compromisorse.com/rse/2026/06/04/dreamland-el-parque-natural-protegido-de-legami-cumple-tres-anos/ Dreamland, el parque natural protegido de Legami, cumple tres años]", Compromiso RSE, 4 June 2026.] Established in 2023 on approximately three hectares, the project subsequently expanded to more than 30 hectares. [ref: "[https://www.ansa.it/sito/notizie/economia/2026/05/27/legami-fa-crescere-dreamland-oltre-30-ettari-di-parco-natura-protetta-a-bergamo_1a471b99-9149-4d9a-bae0-5d59bdca90d9.html Legami fa crescere Dreamland, oltre 30 ettari di parco natura protetta a Bergamo]", ANSA, 27 May 2026.]

== Writing ==

In 2026, Fassi published his debut novel, We Are Dreamers - La battaglia delle fragole, an adventure novel for young readers released by Magazzini Salani. [ref: "[https://www.huffingtonpost.it/life/2026/05/23/news/un_mondo_senza_sbavature_quattro_ragazzi_pieni_di_difetti_il_romanzo_desordio_del_fondatore_di_legami-21978902/ Un mondo senza sbavature, quattro ragazzi pieni di difetti: il romanzo d'esordio del fondatore di Legami]", HuffPost Italia, 23 May 2026.] The novel debuted in the weekly top ten of children's books published by la Repubblica. [ref: Ilaria Zaffino, "[https://www.repubblica.it/robinson/2026/05/24/news/libri_per_ragazzi_un_romanzo_che_celebra_i_legami-425364157/ Libri per ragazzi, un romanzo che celebra i Legami]", la Repubblica, 24 May 2026.]

== Recognition ==

In 2025, Fassi received the Alumnus KPMG dell'Anno award from KPMG.

data.title: Vissoth Nam
data.text:
== Vissoth Nam ==

is a Cambodian business executive and entrepreneur serving as Chief Executive Officer of AirAsia Cambodia [ref: VISSOTH NAM, AirAsia Newsroom] since its inception in 2022 [ref: Capital A to launch AirAsia Cambodia as it resumes growth, Reuters]. He previously worked in macroeconomic research for the National Bank of Cambodia and the International Monetary Fund (IMF), and was named a Young Global Leader [ref: Meet the Young Global Leaders Class of 2026, World Economic Forum] by the World Economic Forum in 2026.

== Early life and education ==
Born in Phnom Penh and raised in France, Vissoth completed his higher education in Paris, studying law and economics at Université Paris-Panthéon-Assas from 2009 to 2012. He subsequently earned a Master’s degree in Management with a specialization in Global Financial Management from ESCEMBusiness School.

== Career ==

=== Economic research ===
Early in his career, Vissoth specialized in central banking and macroeconomic policy. He served as Deputy Section Chief in Economic Research at the National Bank of Cambodia (NBC), focusing on monetary policy, national financial stability, and macroeconomic indicators. He later joined the International Monetary Fund (IMF) as an economist, where he co-authored research analyzing domestic credit growth, banking sector leverage, and financial cycles in Cambodia. [ref: https://www.imf.org/-/media/Files/Countries/ResRep/BGD/2018/032018.ashx]

=== Entrepreneurship and hospitality ===
In 2017, Vissoth transitioned into the private sector, founding Sivilai Asia, a Cambodia-based investment and holding firm focused on hospitality and strategic local ventures [ref: Capital A Forms AirAsia Cambodia As Budget Carrier Seeks New Growth Markets, Forbes]. Through Sivilai Asia, he led development and management projects aimed at elevating Cambodia's regional hospitality and commercial ecosystem.

=== AirAsia Cambodia ===
In December 2022, Capital A (AirAsia Group) partnered with Sivilai Asia in a joint venture to establish AirAsia Cambodia, with Capital A holding a 51% stake and Sivilai Asia holding 49%. As Director of Sivilai Asia, Vissoth was appointed Chief Executive Officer of the new low cost airline.

Under his executive leadership, the airline navigated regulatory approvals with the State Secretariat of Civil Aviation (SSCA), securing its Air Operator Certificate (AOC) in April 2024 [ref: ]. AirAsia Cambodia launched domestic operations on 2 May 2024, connecting Phnom Penh, Siem Reap, and Sihanoukville [ref: AirAsia Cambodia Takes Off!, AirAsia Newsroom], before expanding to international regional routes [ref: AirAsia Cambodia launches first int’l flight to Kuala Lumpur] to boost tourism and economic integration within ASEAN.

=== Recognition ===
- World Economic Forum: Named to the WEF Young Global Leaders Class of 2026 under the Business category

- [https://ctb.gov.kh/about-ctb Cambodia Tourism Board] (CTB): Appointed to the Board of Directors in 2026 to advise on national tourism strategy, aviation policy, and destination marketing [ref: Cambodia Tourism Board]

data.title: Filippo Ghirelli
data.text:
Filippo Ghirelli (born 23 January 1980) [ref: My Heritage, My Heritage] is an Italian entrepreneur whose business activities include energy efficiency, infrastructure, artificial intelligence and aerospace technology. [ref: Filippo Ghirelli, Forbes] He founded Genera Group and Infracorp, and operates the family office Sophrance Global. In December 2025, he entered Forbes Italias ranking of Italian billionaires in 62nd place, with an estimated net worth of US$1.5 billion. [ref: Crescono i miliardari italiani: sono 79. Ferrero sempre in testa, Forbes Italia]

== Early life and education ==

Ghirelli was born in Rome in 1980. [ref: This Italian Entrepreneur Became A Billionaire Investing In India. Up Next: Space And AI, Forbes] He studied civil engineering at the University of Rome. [ref: Filippo Ghirelli, Confassociazioni] He earned an MBA and a master's degree in Financial Markets from LUISS Business School and completed a specialization at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.[ [ref: TEDxYouth@ISMonaco: Meet our speakers, International School of Monaco]

== Career ==

=== Infrastructure and Genera Group ===

Ghirelli began his career working as a project engineer on infrastructure projects in West Africa, including Guinea, Ghana and Mali, and Turkey for multinational enterprises such as Astaldi. He came back to Italy in 2006 for high-speed rail projects and became general manager at De Angelis Group in 2007

In 2009, Ghirelli established a construction and project development business, which evolved into Genera Group, later integrated into Mareterra Group Holding. He invested in projects in Italy, Morocco and Egypt. Political unrest in Egypt in 2013 affected those projects, and he shifted the company's focus to industrial energy efficiency in Italy. In 2013, he also co-founded the sustainable energy trading platform OV Energy in partnership with UniCredit and WWF's Officinae Verdi. [ref: Interview, YouTube]

In 2017, Ghirelli sold 49% of the company to the German investment group IKAV, but bought it back in 2020. He then sold a 75% share to the Swiss manager SUSI Partners. SUSI bought the remaining 25% in December 2024, after which Ghirelli resigned from Genera's board. [ref: SUSI Partners Acquires Remaining Stake in Italian Energy Service Company Genera Group, SUSI Partners]

=== Nayara Energy and Infracorp ===

In January 2023, Hara Capital (a part of Mareterra Group) bought a 24.5% share in Nayara Energy, an Indian company with a refinery in Vadinar. [ref: Hara Capital Sarl completes purchase of Trafigura's interest in Nayara Energy, Trafigura] The investment initially included plans to develop biofuel production for aviation, although these plans did not proceed.

In 2024, Ghirelli founded Infracorp, a global tech-infrastructure holding firm, and acquired Riviera Airport in northern Italy to develop it for private aviation and logistics. [ref: Villanova, aeroporto ceduto da Toussaint al gruppo Infracorp, Il Secolo XIX] [ref: Aeroporto di Villanova d’Albenga: Infracorp compra la maggioranza da Clemens Toussaint, Eco di Savona]

== Sport ==
In 2014, Filippo Ghirelli was in talks to buy the Mallorca football club. [ref: Filippo Ghirelli está dispuesto a comprar el Mallorca, MARCA.com] [ref: 'Quiero pensar que llego al Mallorca para quedarme', ELMUNDO]

== Personal life and other activities ==

Ghirelli resides in Monaco with his wife Daniela and their two children. [ref: Pictures: Venice collides with Monaco at Dreaming in Azur charity gala, Monaco Life] The couple founded the Venetian Arts Foundation, which held a charity gala in support of the Prince Albert II of Monaco Foundation.

He is a former vice-president of environment and energy at Confassociazioni. In July 2024, he was named co-chair of the Monaco Ambassadors Club alongside Christian Moore. [ref: Brazil in the spotlight at Monaco Ambassadors Club’s annual Summer Party, Monaco Life] An International School of Monaco speaker profile lists him as a member of the Prince Albert II of Monaco Foundation. He is also a TEDx speaker. [ref: ISM holds third TEDxYouth event, International School of Monaco]

data.title: David Elkington
data.text:
David Elkington is an entrepreneur and technology executive. He co-founded InsideSales.com with Ken Krogue and Rob Christensen in 2004 and served as the company's chief executive officer. [ref: The Bottom Line: David Elkington, InsideSales CEO, KCPW] InsideSales developed predictive-analytics software intended to help salespeople decide which prospects to contact and when. [ref: InsideSales.com Raises $100M to Predict Sales; Valuation Close to $1 Billion, The Wall Street Journal]

==Early life and education==
Elkington studied philosophy as an undergraduate and computer science at the graduate level at Brigham Young University. He also worked in banking before founding InsideSales. [ref: An inside look at InsideSales, Deseret News] [ref: Dave Elkington Creates Insidesales.com Machine Learning Platform To Accelerate Sales, Forbes]

==Career==
Before InsideSales, Elkington founded Integr8ted Technology Solutions, a consulting and application-development firm. [ref: The 2017 CRM Market Influential Leaders: David Elkington, Founder and CEO, InsideSales.com, destinationCRM] He launched InsideSales with Krogue and Rob Christensen in 2004. The company's early product was a dialer system that collected data from sales interactions; it later used that data in predictive models for sales teams. The company was initially bootstrapped, including a period when Elkington and his wife took nighttime janitorial work to help cover expenses.

In April 2014, The Wall Street Journal reported that InsideSales had raised $100 million at a valuation of nearly $1 billion. The newspaper described the company's software as using predictive analytics to help salespeople determine whom to call and when. In 2017, Deseret News reported that the company had raised more than $250 million in investment and had been valued at $1.5 billion.

Elkington also co-founded Silicon Slopes, a Utah technology and startup community. [ref: Innovation Plaza Founder Series: Dave Elkington, Founder of InsideSales.com, Trailblazer Bulletin] In February 2026, Nasdaq identified him as the founder and chief executive officer of Atonom. [ref: Dave Elkington Founder & CEO, Atonom, Nasdaq]

Elkington's work in sales technology was profiled by destinationCRM in 2017. The publication described him as a contributor to sales-industry thought leadership and technological innovation, and reported that he served on the advisory board of the American Association of Inside Sales Professionals.

The film stars Madhumitha Das, Jeeva Rav and Regin Rose. The film was released on 4 September 2026. [ref: ] [ref: “ஏன் என்னை ஏதோ செய்தாய்” படத்தின் ரிலீஸ் தேதி அறிவிப்பு, Daily Thanthi]

Maalai Malar wrote "D. Anthony, who has handled the writing, direction, and editing, has moved the story around the loneliness of modern you... [ref: ஏன் என்னை ஏதோ செய்தாய்- திரை விமர்சனம், Maalai Malar] [ref: ]

data.title: Carlos Brucal
data.text:
Carlos "Caloy" B. Brucal (October 4, 1946 – December 24, 2011) was a veteran Filipino politician and lawyer who played an instrumental role in the foundational growth and early governance of Calapan City, Oriental Mindoro. Alongside Arnan Panaligan and Doy Leachon, he is recognized as one of the co-founding city mayors who steered Calapan during its developmental years following its transition from a municipality.

==Early Political Career and Vice Mayoralty (1995–2004)==
Brucal served as the Vice Mayor of Calapan under then-Municipal Mayor Arnan Panaligan. When Republic Act No. 8475 was ratified on March 21, 1998, converting Calapan into a component city, Brucal made local history by becoming the first City Vice Mayor of Calapan. As the presiding officer of the last Sangguniang Bayan and the inaugural Sangguniang Panlungsod, he led the first generation of city councilors through the legislative transitions required for early cityhood.

==Mayor of Calapan (2004–2007)==
Following his vice mayoral tenure, Brucal successfully ran for the local chief executive position and served as the Mayor of Calapan from June 30, 2004, to June 30, 2007.
His mayoral administration was marked by several local milestones:
* The City College of Calapan (CCC): While the original vision for a local government-managed tertiary institution was conceived under the Panaligan administration, Mayor Brucal drove the actual groundwork. In 2005, Brucal formed the technical working group that conducted structural feasibility studies, directly laying the foundations for the official establishment of the institution.
* Crisis Management: In December 2005, his administration led emergency relief and infrastructure response efforts when severe flash floods submerged 48 out of Calapan's 62 barangays, prompting the local government to place the city under a state of calamity.
* Administrative Strategy: His term introduced localized corporate management practices to the local government unit through his "8-Point Agenda" structural program.
Upon the expiration of his term in 2007, he was succeeded in office by Paulino Salvador Leachon.

==Personal and Family Life==
Brucal was married to Luzviminda S. Brucal. His family remains active in public service in the province; his son, C. Voltaire "Bong" S. Brucal, entered local politics and served as a multi-term city councilor, Vice Mayor of Calapan (2013–2016), and currently serves as a Member of the Provincial Board representing the 1st District of Oriental Mindoro.

data.title: Johnny O'Reilly
data.text:
----

Johnny O'Reilly (born 22 October 1970) is an Irish filmmaker and journalist. He wrote and directed the Russian-language feature films Moscow Never Sleeps (2016) and The Weather Station (2010), and the short film The Terms (2002), which was shortlisted for the 74th Academy Awards. Following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, O'Reilly began developing a documentary project about events in Kherson and the surrounding region. [ref: Our man in Moscow, The Irish Times] [ref: 'I want to see out the war': Irish filmmaker moved to Ukraine from Russia when 'the pessimists were proved right', The Irish Times] [ref: Red Letter Day, The Sunday Times] As a journalist, he has covered politics and culture in Russia, Belarus, and Ukraine for publications including The Sunday Times, The Times, and The Irish Times.

== Early life and education ==
O'Reilly grew up in Dublin, Ireland. He studied Russian and Classics at Trinity College Dublin. In 1993, while still a student, he worked in Moscow as a freelance reporter covering the Russian constitutional crisis. In 1996, he completed graduate film studies at New York University. He worked at The Sunday Times for two years before pursuing a career in filmmaking. In 2006, he relocated to Moscow, where he lived for ten years.

== Career ==

=== Filmmaking ===

==== The Terms (2002) ====
O'Reilly directed the short film The Terms (2002). Based on a short story by Irish writer Mike McCormack, the film was shortlisted for the 74th Academy Awards and received multiple international festival awards. [ref: The Terms Shortlisted for Oscars, IFTN]

==== The Weather Station (2010) ====
O’Reilly’s feature directorial debut was the Russian-language thriller The Weather Station (2010). Described by Variety as a “whodunit straight out of the Agatha Christie school”, the film was set in an arctic meteorological outpost and filmed near Simferopol in Crimea, Ukraine. [ref: The Weather Station, Variety]

==== Moscow Never Sleeps (2016) ====
O’Reilly wrote and directed Moscow Never Sleeps (2016), an ensemble drama set during Moscow City Day celebrations. The film follows several interconnected stories over a single day and features actors including Mikhail Yefremov, Lyubov Aksyonova, and Aleksei Serebryakov.

==== Kherson ====
O'Reilly subsequently began developing a documentary project about events in Kherson and the surrounding region.

=== Journalism and cultural initiatives ===
O'Reilly has reported from Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, and the wider former Soviet region, covering politics, culture, society, and conflict across Eastern Europe. His journalism has appeared in international media outlets, including The Sunday Times, The Times, and The Irish Times.

In 2008, he co-founded the Irish Film Festival in Moscow. According to The Sunday Times, the festival continued for eleven years and expanded to other Russian cities.

=== Russian television incident ===
In August 2015, O'Reilly appeared live on Russian state television to discuss Moscow Never Sleeps. During the interview, he described Ukrainian filmmaker Oleg Sentsov as a political prisoner, after which the broadcast was abruptly cut short. The incident received international media coverage in outlets such as The Irish Times and The Hollywood Reporter. [ref: Russian TV Cuts Away After Irish Director Backs Jailed Ukrainian Filmmaker Oleg Sentsov, The Hollywood Reporter] [ref: Russian TV cuts off Irish director after backing jailed filmmaker, The Irish Times]

== Filmography ==
=== Feature Films ===
* CO/MA (2004) – Writer, Director
* The Weather Station (2010) — Writer, Director
* Moscow Never Sleeps (2016) — Writer, Director
* Kherson — Writer, Director, Producer

=== Short Films ===
* The Terms (2002) — Writer, Director

== Awards and Nominations ==
* **2001** – Ajijic International Film Festival: Winner, Los Charales Award for Best Short Film (under 16 minutes) — *The Terms*
* **2001** – Palm Springs International ShortFest: Second Place, Jury Award for Best Live Action Film (15 minutes and under) — *The Terms*
* **2001** – Woodstock Film Festival: Winner, Jury Prize for Best Short Film — *The Terms*
* **2001** – Terezín Fort Film Festival: Winner, Terezín Brick for Best Short Film — *The Terms*
* **2001** – FIKE – Évora International Short Film Festival: Winner, Best European Short Film — *The Terms* (Shared with Mike McCormack)
* **2002** – San Francisco International Film Festival: Winner, Certificate of Merit for Film and Video – Short Narrative — *The Terms*
* **2002** – Temecula Valley International Film Festival: Winner, Jury Award for Best Short Film — *The Terms*
* **2002** – Chlotrudis Awards: Nominee, Chlotrudis Award for Best Short Film — *The Terms*
* **2005** – Locarno Film Festival: Nominee, Golden Leopard – Video — *CO/MA* (Shared with Jovan Arsenic, Steve Hudson, Hanna Slak, and Mike Figgis)
* **2016** – Golden Unicorn Awards: Nominee, Best Screenplay — *Moscow Never Sleeps*

data.title: International Engineering and Technology Institute
data.text:
----

The International Engineering and Technology Institute (IETI) is an international academic organization founded in 2015 and based in Hong Kong. It is involved in academic collaboration, research activities, conferences, fellowships and awards in science, engineering and technology. [ref: SSUET VC honored with prestigious global award, Business Recorder]

== History ==

IETI was founded in 2015. In 2020, the Department of Statistics and Data Science at Tsinghua University described IETI as a non-profit organization established in 2015 that promoted research and collaboration in science, engineering and technology, with activities extending into mathematics, statistics, economics and related fields. [ref: Professor Lijian Yang was Elected as Distinguished Fellow of the International Engineering and Technology Institute, Tsinghua University]

In 2026, the Pakistani newspaper Business Recorder described IETI as a non-profit and non-political academic organization founded in 2015 and reported on one of its international awards.

== Activities ==

IETI's activities include academic conferences, research collaboration, fellowships and academic awards. Universities in several countries have reported appointments and awards involving the organization.

In 2020, Tsinghua University reported the election of statistician Lijian Yang as an IETI Distinguished Fellow and described the institute's research scope and fellowship program.

In December 2025, the University of California, Santa Barbara reported that computer scientist Linda Petzold had been elected a Distinguished Fellow of IETI. The university described the fellowship as an honor recognizing Petzold's contributions to computational science and engineering. [ref: UCSB Professor Linda Petzold Elected Fellow of IETI, University of California, Santa Barbara]

In 2025, the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology reported that environmental engineer Irene Man Chi Lo had been elected an IETI Distinguished Fellow. [ref: Prof. Irene LO Elected Distinguished Fellow of IETI and Honored with Career Award at International Conference, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology]

IETI has also participated in the organization of international academic conferences. In May 2026, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University reported that IETI co-organized the fifth International Symposium on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence for Education Transformation (ISBDAI 2026). The event included a keynote address by Nobel Prize in Physics laureate Ferenc Krausz. [ref: Nobel Laureate Prof. Ferenc KRAUSZ shares insights at PolyU to shape the AI-Powered future during the ISBDAI 2026, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University]

== Fellowships ==

IETI operates a fellowship program that includes Fellow and Distinguished Fellow categories. The organization also has a Laureate Distinguished Fellow category. [ref: About IETI, International Engineering and Technology Institute]

The fellowship program has been reported by universities including Tsinghua University, the University of California, Santa Barbara, and the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology.

IETI's fellowship lists include academics who have received major international awards. However, the individual distinction of a fellow is separate from the organizational status of IETI.

== Awards ==

IETI administers academic awards and honors, including awards related to scientific research, leadership and young researchers. [ref: IETI Awards, International Engineering and Technology Institute]

In July 2026, Business Recorder reported that Muhammad Afzal Haque, vice chancellor of Sir Syed University of Engineering & Technology, received an IETI Global Leadership Award. The newspaper described the award as an international recognition for contributions to engineering education, research and international collaboration.

== International activities ==

IETI's activities involve academic institutions in several countries. Its collaboration with The Hong Kong Polytechnic University on ISBDAI 2026 was reported by the university in connection with a keynote presentation by Nobel laureate Ferenc Krausz.

The organization has also been referenced in university reports concerning individual academics and their appointments to IETI fellowship positions.
