data.title: Pocket FM
data.text:
= Pocket FM =

Pocket FM is an Indian audio entertainment platform that distributes serialized fiction and other audio content. It was founded in 2018 by Rohan Nayak, Prateek Dixit and Nishanth Srinivas. [ref: Pocket FM raises $22.4 million in Series B funding led by Lightspeed, The Economic Times] [ref: Rohan Nayak, Prateek Dixit, Nishant KS, Fortune India]

The platform uses a freemium model in which some episodes are available without charge while subsequent episodes can be unlocked using virtual currency purchased through in-app transactions. The company is actively incorporating artificial intelligence for audio production as well as translation into other languages. [ref: Pocket FM partners with ElevenLabs to convert scripts into audio content quickly, TechCrunch] [ref: Pocket FM wants to be the Netflix of long-form audio, www.forbesindia.com]

As of 2026, The Pocket FM website claims the company is serving 20+ countries in 15 international languages. [ref: Pocket FM: The home of the world's best audio dramas, pocketfm.com]

== History ==
Pocket FM began offering content across multiple formats like audiobooks, podcasts and other spoken-word content before shifting its focus toward serialized fiction. [ref: Pocket FM: The Startup that Pioneered Audio Series and Made the Entertainment Industry Follow in Its Footsteps, OK Magazine] By 2021, the platform was describing itself primarily as a community of content creators, and an audio entertainment service serving fictional content in an episodic story format. [ref: Audio OTT app Pocket FM raises $22.4mn funding in round led by Lightspeed, Business Standard]

In December 2021, Pocket FM raised $22.4 million in a Series B funding round led by Lightspeed, with participation from Tanglin Venture Partners and existing investor Times Group. The company said the funding would be used to expand its operations, creator community and geographical presence.

In September 2023, the company announced that its Android application had surpassed 100 million downloads on Google Play. The company attributed the growth to its serialized-fiction format and expansion across languages and genres. [ref: Pocket FM crosses over 100 million downloads on Google Play Store, The Times of India]

In March 2024, Pocket FM raised $103 million in a Series D funding round led by Lightspeed, with participation from StepStone Group. TechCrunch reported that the round brought the company's total funding to approximately $196 million and valued it at $750 million. The company said the funding would support expansion into Europe and Latin America following growth in the United States. [ref: Audio platform Pocket FM bags $103M in funding as it eyes global expansion, TechCrunch]

== Content and business model ==
Pocket FM's principal offering is serialized audio fiction. The platform hosts stories released in episodes, with content spanning genres including romance, fantasy, science fiction, thriller and drama. Pocket FM uses a freemium, pay-as-you-go model in which users can listen to some episodes for free and unlock additional episodes by purchasing virtual coins. [ref: Out of Pocket, The Verge]

The company expanded into the United States in 2022. By March 2024, the company said it had generated more than $150 million in annual recurring revenue, including $100 million from the United States, and was expanding into Europe and Latin America.

Pocket FM's revenue stood at ₹1,768 crore for the financial year 2024–25, an increase of 68 percent from the previous year. More than half of the company's revenue came from user payments through microtransactions, with the remainder coming from advertising. In April 2026, Pocket FM said it had reached approximately $450 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR). The company said it had reached approximately $200 million ARR in the fourth quarter of financial year 2025 and approximately $400 million in the fourth quarter of financial year 2026. [ref: Pocket FM hits $450 million ARR in April after accelerating AI-led content creation, The Economic Times]

== Notable series ==
According to play counts displayed by Pocket FM, Insta Millionaire and Super Yoddha have each accumulated approximately 1.4 billion plays, Ek Ladki Ko Dekha To approximately 1.3 billion, Secret Ameerzaada approximately 885 million, and Insta Empire approximately 556.4 million. [ref: Pocket FM: The home of the world's best audio dramas, pocketfm.com]

== Creator ecosystem ==
Pocket FM relies upon its community of writers and voice artists to produce content for the platform. In 2021, the company reported working with more than 17,000 writers and voice artists for content production. In February 2026, The Economic Times reported that Pocket FM said more than 20 percent of its monetized creators earned more than ₹1 lakh per month and that total creator payouts had exceeded ₹300 crore.

== Artificial intelligence ==
Pocket FM has increasingly incorporated artificial intelligence into the production of its audio content. In June 2024, the company announced a partnership with ElevenLabs to convert written scripts into audio using AI-generated voices. Pocket FM reported produceding 30,000 hours of audio series using ElevenLabs' technology during a testing phase, and planned to make the technology available to its creators in the future.

Subsequently, the company expanded use of artificial intelligence beyond voice generation, incorporating it deeper into writing assistance, content production, translation, and localization. By April 2026, the company reported more than 300,000 creators producing over 80,000 hours of content on a monthly basis. [ref: Pocket FM gives its writers an AI tool to transform narratives, write cliffhangers, and more, TechCrunch]

== Partnerships ==
Pocket FM has entered into partnerships involving established entertainment properties as it has expanded its audio catalogue. In 2025, the company partnered with Arka Mediaworks, the production company behind the Baahubali films, on an audio series based on the Baahubali universe. The planned series was reported to comprise 250 episodes. [ref: Pocket FM, Arka Mediaworks to launch new Baahubali audio series, The Economic Times]

== References ==

data.title: Haider Naqvi
data.text:
----

Syed Naqi Haider Naqvi, T.I. (popularly known as S. N. Haider Naqvi, T.I.) is a Pakistani investigative journalist, political columnist, news analyst, media executive, advertising administrator, telecommunications pioneer, sports administrator, and regulatory official. Widely recognized among Pakistan's top-tier media figures, he is known for breaking high-profile investigative reports and authoring news columns on state governance, national political developments, defense affairs, media regulation, and cricket administration.

He serves as an official Executive Member of the Authority at the Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA) representing Sindh, as well as a regular senior analyst on flagship political talk shows across Pakistan's premier news networks, including Geo News and ARY News (notably as a panelist on The Reporters). He is the founder and CEO of the advertising, PR, and media agency CLICKCOM, previously served as the Chief Executive Officer of the Pakistan Super League (PSL) franchise Multan Sultans during its inaugural season, is the CEO and founder of Urdu news network StarNews Pakistan, was the founder and CEO of satellite network TV2Day, led network infrastructure modernization during Pakistan's 3G/4G telecom transformation, and currently serves as the Chief Executive Officer of the international satellite channel Ocean News UK. In 2024, he was conferred the Tamgha-e-Imtiaz (Medal of Excellence) by the President of Pakistan for his contributions to journalism.

== Early life and education ==
Naqvi is the son of **Syed Shabbir Hussain Naqvi** (1937–2013), a well-known Pakistani social worker and philanthropist noted for his extensive contributions to community welfare, humanitarian projects, and social relief initiatives across the country. Following his passing in June 2013, official state condolence messages were issued by top national leadership—including President of Pakistan Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, PTI Chairman Imran Khan, Chairman Senate Nayyar Bukhari, and Speaker National Assembly Sardar Ayaz Sadiq—acknowledging his distinguished social services and extending condolences to Haider Naqvi and the bereaved family.

Naqvi earned his Bachelor of Engineering degree from the prestigious NED University of Engineering and Technology in Karachi. During his university years, he was a prominent student leader, serving as President of the NED student body during his tenure. Demonstrating leadership and technical distinction during his academic career, he later leveraged his engineering and administrative background to lead major telecommunications infrastructure projects, corporate media management, advertising, sports governance, broadcast journalism, media entrepreneurship, and public media regulation.

== Career ==

=== Advertising, PR, & CLICKCOM ===
Naqvi expanded his corporate operations into strategic communications and media representation by founding **CLICKCOM**, a full-service advertising, public relations (PR), and media agency. As CEO of CLICKCOM, he led corporate branding, strategic media buying, nation-wide advertising campaigns, and corporate PR strategies for various public and private sector clients in Pakistan and abroad.

=== Media entrepreneurship, StarNews Pakistan & TV2Day ===
In the mid-2000s, during the expansion of private electronic media in Pakistan, Naqvi established **TV2Day**, an independent satellite television network headquartered in Karachi. Upon launching the channel, he gained widespread national attention as one of the country's youngest television network owners and CEOs.

During his tenure as head of TV2Day in 2006, Naqvi was invited to an official meeting by the then President of Pakistan, General Pervez Musharraf, to discuss electronic media expansion, broadcasting policy, and national current affairs.

Expanding his media network, Naqvi founded and serves as CEO of **StarNews Pakistan**, an Urdu-language news organization that developed into one of Pakistan's widely followed digital and broadcast current affairs outlets. Under his leadership, StarNews Pakistan focuses on breaking political coverage, investigative reporting, regional news, and current affairs analysis.

=== National initiatives & "I'M Pakistan" Conference ===
Naqvi organized the national **"I'M Pakistan" Conference**, a public recognition platform designed to honor citizens, public figures, and veterans who rendered distinguished services to Pakistan. The conference was attended by national leadership, with the then Prime Minister of Pakistan, Yousuf Raza Gillani, presiding as the Chief Guest to present honors and recognize the contributions of key national achievers.

=== Digital media presence, political engagement, & Indian media censorship ===
Naqvi maintains a significant digital presence on X (formerly Twitter), where his reporting and analytical commentary on national policy, constitutional matters, and governance regularly reach key decision-makers. His social media posts and exclusive news breaks are frequently reshared, cited, or endorsed by top state leadership and prominent politicians, including the Prime Minister of Pakistan, the President of Pakistan, Chief Minister of Punjab Maryam Nawaz, Federal Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari, and Sindh provincial minister Syed Nasir Hussain Shah.

His high-impact digital commentary on national defense and regional security led to cross-border censorship actions. During Indian military operations and geopolitical friction in Jammu and Kashmir (Operation Sindoor), Indian law enforcement agencies and news reports (including *News Bharati*) listed Haider Naqvi's account among key Pakistani digital media handles subjected to geo-blocking and restrictions by Delhi Police over regional reporting and national policy commentary.

=== Telecommunications pioneer & 3G/4G rollout ===
As a qualified engineer and corporate executive, Naqvi served as Chief Executive Officer of an international Chinese-based network infrastructure company operating in Pakistan. In this role, he played a pioneering role in modernizing Pakistan's telecommunications architecture, overseeing nationwide network building initiatives that enabled the transition of Pakistan's legacy 2G mobile networks into high-speed 3G/4G cellular networks leading up to the nation's spectrum auctions and network upgrade phase in 2013–2014.

=== International broadcast media & diplomatic engagements ===
Naqvi has featured as a guest senior news analyst on global broadcast networks, including CNN, the BBC, and Deutsche Welle (DW), offering international perspectives on South Asian geopolitics, regional security, and civil-military affairs in Pakistan.

Beyond media commentary, Naqvi has represented Pakistani journalism and broadcast leadership across international forums. He has received official invitations to attend and address legislative and diplomatic assemblies, including guest speaking engagements at the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) side sessions in New York and parliamentary media conferences in the United Kingdom.

=== Public governance & refusal of political offices ===
Naqvi was appointed by the Government and President of Pakistan to serve as a key Executive Member of the Authority at the **Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA)** representing Sindh province. In this regulatory role, he contributes to national policy formulation, broadcasting compliance, electronic media licensing, and structural oversight across Pakistan's private television networks and broadcast infrastructure.

Over his career, Naqvi was offered consideration for high-level political roles, including the post of Federal Minister for Interior and a seat in the Senate of Pakistan. However, he declined both offers, maintaining that taking up political cabinet posts or legislative office would create a direct conflict of interest with his professional mandate as an independent journalist and broadcast media analyst.

=== Defense initiatives, ISPR event direction, & "Salam Sipahi Jeeo Jawan" ===
Driven by his strong affiliation with national defense institutions, Naqvi was appointed by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) as the Director for the national **Pakistan Day Event – "Peaceful Pakistan"**. In this capacity, he was fully authorized to act on behalf of ISPR to manage and coordinate the international-scale event, which engaged global heads of state, Hollywood celebrities, and world-renowned sports figures to project a positive global image of Pakistan.

Additionally, Naqvi organized the national event series **"Salam Sipahi Jeeo Jawan"**. The ceremonies were organized as grand tributes to commemorate national defense triumphs, honor fallen soldiers (*shuhada*), and celebrate the operational victories and sacrifices of the Pakistan Armed Forces. Key national figures attended the proceedings, including PPP leader Faryal Talpur and Chief Minister of Sindh Murad Ali Shah.

=== Print journalism & column writing ===
Throughout his career, Naqvi has maintained an active presence in print media as a prolific columnist and contributing reporter. His news columns and analytical pieces on South Asian politics, regional security, civil-military dynamics, and national constitutional debates—such as his commentary on presidential versus parliamentary systems ("Plan Kuch Aur Hai!")—have been published across major national and international publications, including Urdu daily Daily Jang, English daily The News International, Daily Express, and global platforms such as The Washington Post.

In addition to opinion columns, Naqvi has authored major front-page news reports for leading dailies such as Daily Jang and The News International, detailing key executive appointments, provincial governance dynamics between federal leadership and Sindh, and administrative appointments including the Inspector General of Police (IGP) Sindh.

=== Humanitarian efforts (2005 earthquake relief) ===
Following the devastating 2005 Kashmir earthquake, Naqvi engaged in cross-border relief and fundraising initiatives. He facilitated the visit of prominent Bollywood film actor Manisha Koirala to Karachi in November 2005 to participate in a live broadcast telethon ("Pukar") aimed at raising emergency funds and aid for earthquake victims in northern Pakistan.

=== Broadcast journalism & television news analysis ===
Naqvi is a prominent and widely recognized figure on Pakistani news television. In addition to appearing as a core panelist on ARY News's flagship political discussion show, **The Reporters**, he regularly features as an expert analyst across all of Pakistan's major news channels, including Geo News, offering analytical commentary and insider perspectives on constitutional matters, parliamentary debates, national election developments, and civil-military relations.

=== Sports administration and PCB connections ===
Naqvi served as the Chief Executive Officer of the **Multan Sultans** during the franchise's inaugural appearance in the 2018 Pakistan Super League (PSL) season. As CEO, he oversaw franchise operations, team recruitment, and strategic partnerships. During his tenure, Naqvi notably presented an official team jersey to Major General Asif Ghafoor, the then Director-General of Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), recognizing the support of national security institutions for the restoration of international cricket in Pakistan.

Through his dual roles in sports administration and broadcast management, Naqvi developed deep-rooted connections within the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) and domestic sports circles, frequently reporting insider developments regarding PCB governance, team selection dynamics, and administrative decisions.

=== Investigative journalism & military leadership reporting ===
Over his career spanning print and broadcast media, Naqvi established a reputation as a leading investigative reporter specializing in defense affairs, high-level military appointments, and intelligence administration.

Notably, Naqvi broke major exclusive reports regarding senior military promotions and appointments, including early investigative reporting from Rawalpindi detailing the promotion of six Major Generals to Lieutenant General under General Qamar Javed Bajwa—specifically breaking news on Major General Asim Munir (later Chief of Army Staff) and anticipating his appointment as Director-General of Inter-Services Intelligence (DG ISI). His investigative scope also encompasses top-level security briefings, political power shifts, as well as exclusive news from the media, entertainment, and sports industries.

=== Ocean News UK ===
Naqvi serves as the Chief Executive Officer of **Ocean News UK**, an international satellite news network headquartered in London with news operations spanning Europe, the Middle East, and South Asia.

== Awards and accolades ==
Throughout his multi-faceted career across broadcast management, advertising, telecommunications infrastructure, journalism, public regulation, and sports administration, Naqvi has received various professional accolades and national recognition:

* **Tamgha-e-Imtiaz (2024):** Conferred by President Asif Ali Zardari in Islamabad on 23 March 2024 (12 Ramadan 1445 AH) for achieving distinction in the field of Journalism (*Sahaafat*).
* **ISPR Event Directorship:** Appointed as Event Director by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) for the international Pakistan Day event "Peaceful Pakistan".
* **Journalism & Public Tribute Recognition:** Honored for outstanding contributions to media and public service events, receiving awards presented by senior political leadership, including Faryal Talpur in the presence of Chief Minister of Sindh Murad Ali Shah during the "Salam Sipahi Jeeo Jawan" ceremonies.
* **PEMRA Executive Authority Member:** Appointed to represent Sindh on the federal board governing electronic media regulations in Pakistan.
* **Telecom Infrastructure Leadership:** Recognized for pioneering contributions to Pakistan's 3G/4G cellular infrastructure transition as CEO of an international network builder.
* **Youngest Media Executive Distinction:** Recognized across Pakistani media circles for becoming one of the nation's youngest television network owners and CEOs upon establishing TV2Day in the mid-2000s.
* **Sports Leadership Recognition:** Commended by national sports and administrative bodies for leading the inaugural setup of the Multan Sultans PSL franchise and promoting cricket revival in Pakistan.

== References ==

=== Primary & Secondary Document References ===
1. **Presidential Citation for Tamgha-e-Imtiaz:** Official Presidential Conferment Certificate issued in Islamabad on 23 March 2024 (12 Ramadan 1445 AH) under the signature of President Asif Ali Zardari, conferring Tamgha-e-Imtiaz upon Syed Naqi Haider Naqvi for distinction in Journalism (*Sahaafat*).
2. **State Condolence Messages (2013):** Official condolence messages and letters issued upon the demise of Syed Shabbir Hussain Naqvi (1937–2013) by President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Mian Mohammad Nawaz Sharif, PTI Chairman Imran Khan, Senate Chairman Syed Nayyer Hussain Bokhari, National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq, and Senator Farhatullah Babar (PPP Media Cell).
3. **Official Meeting with President Pervez Musharraf (2006):** Photographic and official media records documenting the 2006 state meeting between President of Pakistan General Pervez Musharraf and Syed Naqi Haider Naqvi regarding electronic media developments and broadcasting policy.
4. **Investigative Reporting on Military Leadership Promotions:** Front-page reporting by Haider Naqvi from Rawalpindi detailing the promotion of 6 Major Generals to Lieutenant General by COAS General Qamar Javed Bajwa, including Major General Asim Munir and predicting his appointment as DG ISI.
5. **The News International & Daily Jang Front-Page Reporting:** Front-page news reports authored by Haider Naqvi covering Sindh IGP appointments, executive leadership decisions, and provincial political developments between Prime Minister Imran Khan, Governor Imran Ismail, and Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah.
6. **Political Column Writing:** Special analytical column by Haider Naqvi titled "Plan Kuch Aur Hai!" analyzing national debates surrounding presidential versus parliamentary systems.

data.title: Ronen Taieb
data.text:
Ronen Taieb is an Israeli entrepreneur and business executive, the founder and owner of Integrity Cyber, a company operating in cybersecurity, information security, cyber risk management, data privacy, corporate governance, and cyber incident preparedness.

Taieb has more than a decade of professional experience in risk management, information security, and strategic consulting. His professional activities encompass cybersecurity services, regulatory compliance, technological risk management, and corporate governance. [ref: זירות המסחר היזהרו, המחוקק בדרך, Calcalist] [ref: External Directors Club Conference on Cyber Risks and the Role of Board of Directors, Bar-Ilan University]

== Professional expertise ==

Taieb's professional activities encompass a holistic approach to information security, connecting technological risks, business implications, executive responsibility, and regulatory requirements.

His principal areas of expertise and professional activity include:

* Cybersecurity Governance: Cybersecurity strategy, risk management, corporate governance, and CISO services.

* Incident Response and Cyber Resilience: Cyber incident preparedness, incident response, crisis management, and organizational resilience.

* Security Operations: Security Operations Center (SOC) services, threat detection, vulnerability management, and security assessments.

* Data Protection and Privacy: Data Protection Officer (DPO) services, personal data protection, regulatory compliance, and privacy management.

* AI and Cybersecurity Innovation: Entrepreneurship and the development of artificial intelligence-based solutions for cyber threat detection, investigation, and incident response.

* Business Strategy and International Partnerships: Business development, strategic partnerships, and expansion into international markets.

In July 2017, Taieb published a professional article through the Israeli Directors Union examining cyber threats, organizational preparedness, and the responsibilities of corporate leadership and boards of directors in addressing cybersecurity risks. [ref: מאמרו של רונן טייב למידעון 07/2017, Israeli Directors Union]

== Leadership and entrepreneurship ==

As the founder of Integrity Cyber, Taieb works to develop an end-to-end cybersecurity services framework combining professional expertise, established risk management methodologies, and advanced security technologies.

His management philosophy emphasizes professional responsibility, measurable performance, the reduction of business exposure, and the delivery of tangible value to clients.

Taieb served as chairman of Integrity Consulting and Risk Management in 2015.

By 2018, he was serving as president of Integrity Consulting and Risk Management. He was a participant in a professional conference program organized by Bar-Ilan University's Chair in Israeli Corporate Governance, addressing cybersecurity risks and the responsibilities of corporate boards.

In addition to his involvement in cybersecurity services, Taieb is engaged in technological entrepreneurship in information security and artificial intelligence, including the activities of the separate product company AiCY and its AIIR solutions.

== International activities ==

Taieb is involved in promoting business relationships and strategic partnerships in cybersecurity and technology across international markets, including Europe, Latin America, and the United States.

These activities focus on expanding access to cybersecurity services, developing international cooperation, and creating business models that combine managed security services with innovative technologies.

== Religious and community activities ==

Alongside his business career, Rabbi Ronen Taieb is involved in Torah education, delivering religious lessons, and community activities.

He is active within the religious community of Modi'in, including at the Nitzotz HaKedusha synagogue, combining business activities, community leadership, and the promotion of Torah study.

== Professional vision ==

The following statement is attributed to Taieb in his executive profile:

== Professional publications and appearances ==

Taieb has published professional articles on risk management, financial regulation, cybersecurity, and corporate governance.

In May 2015, he co-authored an article with Inga Eisenberg in Calcalist concerning the regulation of financial trading platforms in Israel.

In 2017, he published an article through the Israeli Directors Union addressing the organizational and managerial implications of cyberattacks.

In May 2018, he was listed as a participant in a panel discussing cybersecurity risks and the responsibilities of corporate boards at Bar-Ilan University.

In February 2025, Taieb was scheduled to deliver a presentation on cybersecurity threats and the importance of ISO 27001 at the annual conference of the Israeli Lighting Association. [ref: הכינוס השנתי של האגודה פברואר 2025, Israeli Lighting Association]

data.title: Horatio George Powys Townshend
data.text:
Sir Horatio George Powys Townshend (6 February 1780 – 25 May 1843) KCH was a British politician and soldier. He sat as MP for Whitchurch from 13 August 1816 till 1826, and 25 February 1831 till 1832. [ref: TOWNSHEND, Hon. Horatio George Powys (1780-1843)., History of Parliament Online]

He was knighted and appointed Knight Commander of the Royal Guelphic Order (KCH) on 25 September 1835. At the time of his death, he served as lieutenant-governor of Windsor Castle.

== Military career ==
He served as ensign for the 1st Regiment of Foot Guards in 1795; he was promoted to lieutenant and captain in 1799; promoted to captain and lieutenant-colonel in 1809; promoted to brevet colonel in 1819; promoted to lieutenant-colonel of the 1st Regiment of Foot Guards in 1821.

== Family and education ==
He was the third son of Thomas Townshend, 1st Viscount Sydney by Elizabeth, the daughter and co-heiress of Richard Powys of Hintlesham, Suffolk. He was the brother of John Thomas Townshend and William Augustus Townshend. He was educated at Eton College from 1787 till 1791. He never married.

data.title: Urine (band)
data.text:
----

URINE is an American band from Albany, New York, formed in 2018. The band was founded by members Nick Hauprich and Jacob Roberts. initially as a joke project intended to release a single song. URINE's music incorporates elements of slam metal, grindcore, beatdown hardcore, industrial metal, death metal and electronic music. The band has released several recordings, including "NIGHT OF THE PISSING DEAD" (2021), "EXCRETA LOTIUM MIASMA" (2023) and "PEEMOCRACY" (2025).
[ref: Urine - An Interview with Liam Sweeny]

== History ==

=== Formation And Early Years ===

URINE officially debuted with the release of their first song "F*** Mike Pence" on December 26th, 2018. After a couple of attempts to start a death metal band. Vocalist Nick Hauprich (Also known as Postal Malone) and drummer and producer Jacob Roberts (Also known as The Artist Formally Known As Sir Kix Alot, Casually Known As Jean Claude Van Damnation) made the first song with a laptop, and a USB microphone. Originally starting as a two-piece, in the upcoming months they would have more members join within the next couple of months. Very shortly after releasing their first song, they began working on their first EP, "URINE FOURSOME SHIT"
[ref: Urine - An Interview with Liam Sweeny]
[ref: Metal Horror Pi*score!!!! Come take a bathroom break with us! We’re got urine!]

=== "URINE FOURSOME SHIT" & "URINE FOURSOME SHIT II: THE TRICKLING" ===
After the release of "F*** Mike Pence" in late 2018, the two founding members decided to go for a much more raw and sloppy sound with their next release. Very consistently stating that they originally did not take the project seriously, their first EP, named "URINE FOURSOME SHIT" opted out of using guitars, and instead had cello VST's ran through distortion effects to create the sound of the project. Everything was done for as cheap as possible, with most of the vocal recordings taking place in closets, and inside cars. "URINE FOURSOME SHIT" while very much non-serious in musical production, was political in message. It also featured future members, Stephen Harrington and Brandon Collins (Also known as his nickname Breo) on vocals for a song. The project was released in mid March of 2019.
Shortly after the release of "URINE FOURSOME SHIT" Breo (Known as PISS BARNES) joined as a full time vocalist alongside Nick. The three of them began work on what was supposed to be the first full length. A 53 song long concept album named "PISS INFUSED GUTTURAL TRASH. They switched from cellos, over to a multitude of guitar plugins and VST's and began writing the album, about a creature who comes to life after people starting urinating radioactive material on a garbage heap after a nuclear apocalypse. It was around this time that BJ Patrignani IV joined the band as his first character: 'Lord Diabeticus'.
However, after about 43 songs were completely instrumentally, and only a handful with recorded vocals, the laptop that Jacob was using became unusable, thus making the album completely lost media. Although a couple years later, a handful of them would be found in an email, and released on their first compilation album "GREATEST PISSES VOL. 1".
After a new laptop was obtained, a very immediate production came on the next release which would be called "URINE FOURSOME SHIT II: THE TRICKLING'. This EP would be much more serious in sound, but was much less politically driven. The EP would feature future URINE vocalist Frank Cogliando (Also known as DANK SINATRA). The EP was released in early October of 2019, just 7 months after the first. During this time URINE played its first shows, calling themselves 'death metal karaoke' and performing with Nick and Breo using microphones, and Jacob playing instrumentals over his laptop. They would perform twice with this set up.

[ref: Urine - An Interview with Liam Sweeny]

=== "NIGHT OF THE PISSING DEAD" ===

After the loss of "PISS INFUSED GUTTURAL TRASH" and the subsequent release of "URINE FOURSOME SHIT II:THE TRICKLING", the now four manned URINE started their work on another full length album. Taking the name from classic horror movie "Night Of The Living Dead" they named this new project "NIGHT OF THE PISSING DEAD".
At this point, Frank Cogliando had joined, marking 4 vocalists (Nick, Breo, Frank and BJ) and Jacob continued to do production with DAWs. BJ's character 'Lord Diabeticus' was killed off, and his new character 'Gint Eastwood' took over.
Shortly after production began, COVID-19 swept through the world. This gave the members more time to work on the album. Going for a more sludgy and heavy sound, they started using more down-tuned tunings on the plugins, and taking inspiration from Vinnie Paul, Jacob and Nick used a lot of reverb on the drums.
During production, another issue came about with the computer being used to make the album. Unlike "PISS INFUSED GUTTURAL TRASH", they had taken precaution by emailing an almost finished version to themselves. They would not end up releasing "NIGHT OFTHE PISSING DEAD" until July, 21st, 2021. This would be the last album to include non-real guitars and bass. It would also be the last album to feature BJ Patrignani as a full time vocalist, as his character was killed off and he left the band in late 2021.
[ref: Urine - An Interview with Liam Sweeny]

=== First Live URINE Shows & "EXCRETA LOTIUM MIASMA" ===
In late 2021, the first actual guitar player, Joseph Grecco (Also known as BLAKK MYLDE) joined the band, Breo switched from vocalist to bassist, and Jacob went from producing everything on a DAW to playing Drums, and Nick stayed as a vocalist with Frank. They had accepted a one time only live show at a friends wedding and started practicing old songs, while also beginning to write new ones. It was also during this time they starting writing their next album, which would eventually be named "EXCRETA LOTIUM MIASMA".

The writing process for "EXCRETA..." was very different than any other album they had done before. By early 2022, Joseph Grecco ended up recording 2 songs with URINE, before he ended up moving to a different state. This led URINE to recruit Stephen Harrington, who had previously lent vocals for on the "URINE FOURSOME SHIT" EP to join as the band's now longest term guitar player. It was during this time as well, that URINE started playing their first live shows as an actual band.

Stephen took over recording the rest of "EXCRETA...", and did so at Baphometric Studios in Ballston Spa, NY.
By the summer of 2022, URINE had picked up doing more shows, including for opening for Bonginator, Abraded, and good amount local term bands. It was around this time that URINE picked up it's first second guitar player, Nick Schuyler. Nick was URINE's shortest term member, only being in the band for a couple months. He was never featured on any recordings.
In 2022, URINE released a compilation album featuring a bunch of unreleased songs that were supposed to be on "PISS INFUSED GUTTURAL TRASH". Originally released as singles on Bandcamp, "GREATEST PISSES VOL. 1" was filled with a bunch of songs not yet released on streaming platforms, including 2 songs never released before. It also includes the first 2 URINE songs ever released, and their cover of the Primus song "Too Many Puppies"
In early 2023, URINE was close to finishing the writing and recording process for their sophomore full length, and focused more of their energy on playing shows locally, gaining a pretty good following. Known for their non-serious antics, like costumes, bubble guns, and a inflatable items passed around to the crowd, URINE continued to play local smaller shows until they finally released "EXCRETA LOTIUM MIASMA" on September 23rd, 2023. They also has opened for 'Born Dead Fest' earlier that month.

"EXCRETA LOTIUM MIASMA" became a major key in URINE's discography, mostly thanks to the single "Starr Sacrifice" featuring Scott Savaria of [https://www.metal-archives.com/bands/dysentery/19021 Dysentery] which also became a staple for their lives shows for many years to come. It was also right after this, that another second guitarist by the name of Ben Godin (Also known as Crusty Chodes) from the bands x5x1x8x and Coquette joined the band, making them a five piece.
[ref: Urine - An Interview with Liam Sweeny]
[ref: Dysentery - Encyclopaedia Metallum: The Metal Archives, www.metal-archives.com]

=== Hiatus and "GREATEST PISSES VOL. 2" ===

During the beginning months of 2024, the vocalist of URINE announced that the band was splitting up. While no reason was officially given, people close to URINE state that it was most likely due to substance abuse by members, as well as other irreconcilable differences. Vocalist Nick Hauprich joined local metalcore outfit MARROW, and guitarist Stephen Harrington joined local thrash band Vaexus.
While broken up, URINE released a second "GREATEST PISSES" this time, including their most popular live versions of songs, as well as the most popular songs for "NIGHT OF THE PISSING DEAD" and "EXCRETA LOTIUM MIASMA"
Along with the release of the album, URINE released their first music video. It was for their song "Starr Sacrifice" and featured a bunch of live cuts from different shows over the years that URINE has performed. It is currently their most viewed music video.

[ref: Urine - An Interview with Liam Sweeny]
=== Reunion & "PEEMOCRACY" ===

In later 2024, URINE made a surprise reunion to play a benefit show for a friend wo had recently passed away. Although they stated they were not going to do anything beyond that one show, by January of 2025 they had announced they were doing a 'semi-reunion' to release a few songs but nothing beyond that. The first song they released was a cover of The Dead Kennedys Nazi Punks Fuck Off
Later that month, they announced a string of actual reunion shows. It was at this time that drummer and producer Jacob had admitted the reason for the hiatus was due to his addictions with alcohol amongst other things, and that he'd stayed sober for a long enough time for he other guys to be around him again. It was also during this time, vocalist Frank Cogliando would silently step down referring to his busy home life as the reasoning.

Towards the middle of 2025, URINE announced they'd be starting to work on their third full length album. It was birthed from a very hot political climate, with the band voicing their opinion on things like the United States Government, war in the Middle East, and their own distrust for police. This was the first album that Stephen and Ben recorded at "Allison Sound" under executive producer Dana Allison.
"PEEMOCRACY" was officially released on August 16th, 2025. It included 5 brand new songs, as well as a Metallica, Chappell Roan and a Dying Fetus cover.

With the release, URINE also released their second music video, this time for a song named "F*** J.D Vance"
The video was filmed in the apartment of vocalist Nick Hauprich. It was given an old school filter, and made to look like an old VH1 music video.

In November of 2025, URINE embarked on their first short tour with to other New York bands: Piss Guzzler and Blind Tyrant. They played a 4 day run, in multiple places in New York State. The tour was named "The New York Piss Tour". The vocalist of New York state band Flatwounds also came along for half of the tour to help URINE out.

After the short run, Stephen and Jacob started working on what would become the next URINE release.

[ref: Urine - An Interview with Liam Sweeny]

=== "6 SHOTS OF HATE" ===

In early 2026, URINE began working on a new release. Stephen again got with Dana Allison of Allison Sound, making this his second release as an executive producer for the band.
Originally the idea was for a more groove filled album in comparison to the more straight up death metal vibe that "PEEMOCRACY" had, but after writing had began, URINE eventually decided to team up with local Albany band Self-Inflicted to do a split.

After months of decisions being made, the two bands finally decided on a name: "6 SHOTS OF HATE" which came from one of Ben's old bands, and was an idea given by a member of Self Inflicted,. They decided to do three songs each, and release the split on cassette. Self Inflicted recorded their side at Pacemaker Audio by Tyler Krupsky. Tyler ended up mastering the whole split, even though URINE recorded at Allison Sound.
In May of 2026, URINE released their third music video, for the single "Headline Empathy" that was recorded for the split. The video was recorded and edited by Tristan Marler of TMMedia. The video was filmed at No Fun in Troy for URINE opening up for Two Piece.

On July 2nd, URINE and Self Inflicted finally released "6 SHOTS OF HATE". It was released on all platforms.

[ref: Urine - An Interview with Liam Sweeny]

data.title: A.M. Glazer
data.text:
----

Anthony Michael Glazer (born 1 May 1943) is a British crystallographer and Emeritus Professor of Physics at the University of Oxford. He is best known for developing the internationally adopted Glazer notation for octahedral tilting in perovskite structures. Glazer is also co‑founder of Oxford Cryosystems, a leading manufacturer of low‑temperature equipment for X‑ray crystallography.

Early life and education Glazer attended Christ’s College Finchley from 1954 to 1964. He earned a B.Sc. (Hons) in Physics from Queen’s College (University of St Andrews, Dundee) in 1965. He completed his Ph.D. in Crystallography at University College London under Kathleen Lonsdale between 1965 and 1968, working on mixed organic crystals. He later received M.A. degrees from the University of Cambridge (1974) and the University of Oxford (1976).

Academic career After a research fellowship at Harvard University (1968–1969) and research posts at the Cavendish Laboratory (1969–1976), Glazer joined the Clarendon Laboratory at Oxford in 1976 as Lecturer in Physics. He simultaneously became Official Fellow and Tutor in Physics at Jesus College, Oxford, positions he held until his retirement in 2010. He was appointed Professor of Physics in 1996 and is now Emeritus Professor of Physics at Oxford and Emeritus Fellow of Jesus College.

Research Glazer’s research focuses on the relationship between crystal structure and physical properties, particularly in ferroelectrics, perovskites, and phase transitions.

In 1972, he introduced a systematic classification of octahedral tilting in perovskite structures, now known as the Glazer tilt system. The notation is widely used in solid‑state physics, crystallography, and materials science.

In 1986, Glazer co‑founded Oxford Cryosystems with J. Cosier to commercialize cryogenic cooling systems for crystallography. Their Cryostream instrument became a standard tool for low‑temperature X‑ray diffraction worldwide.

He has also worked extensively on synchrotron radiation methods for X‑ray diffraction, birefringence measurement instrumentation, ferroelectric and antiferroelectric phase transitions, and crystallographic computing. He has delivered public lectures, including the Royal Institution Bragg Lecture on perovskites.

Publications Glazer is the author of several books, including:

* A Journey into Reciprocal Space (2nd ed., 2021)
* Crystallography: A Very Short Introduction (2016)
* Crystal Clear: The Autobiographies of Sir Lawrence and Lady Bragg (2015)
* Space Groups for Solid State Scientists (3rd ed., 2013)

He is also General Editor of the IUCr Newsletter.

Awards and honours Glazer has received numerous distinctions, including:

* National Medal of Polish Education (1992)
* Czochralski Medal, European Materials Research Society (2012)
* Spriggs Award, American Ceramic Society (2015)
* Vice President, International Union of Crystallography (2014–2017)
* President, British Crystallographic Association (1996–2000)

A nitrogen-gas-stream cryostat for general X-ray diffraction studies. J. Appl. Cryst., 19, 105. N. Zhang, H. Yokota, A. M. Glazer, Z. Ren, D. A. Keen, D. S. Keeble, P. A. Thomas & Z.-G. The 2026–27 George Mason Patriots Men's basketball team represents George Mason University during the 2026–27 NCAA Division I men's basketball season. The season marks the 61st for the program, the fourth under head coach Tony Skinn, and the fourteenth as members of the Atlantic 10 Conference (A-10). The Patriots play their home games at EagleBank Arena in Fairfax, Virginia.

The Patriots finished the previous season 23–10, 11–7 in A-10 play, to finish in fifth place. They lost to St. Bonaventure in the second round of the A-10 tournament. Their season ended with a first round loss to Liberty in the 2026 National Invitation Tournament.

data.title: Monex Global
data.text:
Monex Global is part of Monex S.A.P.I. de C.V. ("Monex"). [ref: Monex 40+ Years of FX Expertise, Monex Global]

Monex Global specializes in foreign exchange (FX) risk management and international payments for corporate and institutional clients.

Monex reports combined annual foreign-exchange volume of more than $198 billion and approximately $16.1 billion in total assets. The company reports serving more than 73,000 individuals and corporate clients worldwide.

Monex operates in Mexico, the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Spain, the Netherlands and Singapore. [ref: ]

=== History ===
Monex was founded in 1985 and is headquartered in Mexico City. [ref: ] According to the company, Monex was established to address the payment and currency exchange needs of companies conducting business internationally.

Monex expanded its international foreign-exchange operations through acquisitions in North America and Europe. Monex's corporate history states that the group acquired Tempus Consulting in 2010. [ref: ] [ref: Monex Acquisition of Tempus Consulting, BGL] The US business was later rebranded as Monex USA in January 2022.

In July 2012, Monex group acquired London-based Schneider Foreign Exchange. [ref: Monex Group acquires Schneider Foreign Exchange, Euromoney] The company subsequently became Monex Europe. Monex later developed additional operations in European markets, including Spain and the Netherlands.

=== Operations ===
Monex Global comprises the international operations of the Monex group through entities established in several jurisdictions.

==== North America ====
The group's North America operations include Monex Inc. in the United States and Monex Canada Inc. in Canada.

==== Europe ====
In Europe, Monex operates through entities including Monex Europe Limited and Monex Europe Markets Limited in the United Kingdom and Monex Europa S.L.U. and Monex Europe Markets, S.V., S.A.U. in Spain.

==== Asia ====
Monex's international operations in Asia include MonFX Pte. Ltd. in Singapore.

=== Products and Services ===
Monex Global's principal activities relate to foreign exchange and cross-border financial transactions.

The business provides services including:

* Foreign exchange
* International payments
* FX risk management/hedging
* Cross-border financial transactions

data.title: Electronic Business One-Stop Shop in the Philippines
data.text:
----

= Electronic Business One-Stop Shop in the Philippines =

== Overview ==
The Electronic Business One-Stop Shop (eBOSS) is an online system used by local government units (LGUs) in the Philippines to process business permit applications and related transactions. It allows business owners to submit documents, pay fees, and receive permits through an online platform. The system aims to simplify business registration and reduce the need for applicants to visit government offices in person. [ref: ARTA sets Nov. 1 deadline for LGUs to shift to online business permit processing – Philippine Information Agency]

== Legal basis ==
Republic Act No. 11032, also known as the Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act of 2018, requires cities and municipalities to automate their business permitting and licensing systems or establish an electronic Business One-Stop Shop. Its implementing rules provide guidelines for setting up electronic business permitting systems and issuing electronic permits. [ref: Republic Act No. 11032, lawphil.net]

Republic Act No. 12254, or the E-Governance Act, was signed in 2025. It provides a broader legal framework for digital government services and is relevant to the implementation of eBOSS in local government units. [ref: REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11032 - AN ACT PROMOTING EASE OF DOING BUSINESS AND EFFICIENT DELI VERY OF GOVERNMENT SERVICES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9485, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE ANTI-RED TAPE ACT OF 2007, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES - Supreme Court E-Library, elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph]

== Implementation ==
The Anti-Red Tape Authority (ARTA) works with other government agencies to promote the implementation of eBOSS. The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) also provides support for the digitalization of local government services. [ref: ARTA sets Nov. 1 deadline for LGUs to shift to online business permit processing – Philippine Information Agency]

According to the Philippine Information Agency, only 127 out of 1,642 local government units were fully compliant with eBOSS requirements as of December 31, 2025. In June 2026, ARTA announced efforts to require all LGUs to process business permits online by November 1, 2026. [ref: ARTA sets Nov. 1 deadline for LGUs to shift to online business permit processing – Philippine Information Agency]

== Challenges ==
The implementation of eBOSS faces challenges related to resources, technical capacity, and coordination among government systems. A 2026 study by the Philippine Institute for Development Studies examined the relationship between automated business permitting and local government revenue. The study identified limitations involving resources, willingness to adopt the systems, and system functionality. It also discussed the need for better integration between local and national government systems. [ref: PIDS study finds fully automated business permitting boosts local tax revenues, pids.gov.ph]

The study recommended improving information and communications technology infrastructure, strengthening the technical capacity of local governments, and integrating local systems with the DICT's eLGU platform. These measures may help local governments improve their digital services and make online business transactions more accessible. [ref: PIDS study finds fully automated business permitting boosts local tax revenues, pids.gov.ph]

== References ==

Irr republic act no. 11032 (CSC, Arta, DTI joint memorandum circular no. 2019-001) - the implementing rules and regulations of republic act no. 11032 otherwise known as the “ease of doing business and efficient government service delivery act of 2018” - supreme court e-library. (2019). Judiciary.Gov.Ph. https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/96391

More LGUs urged to fully automate biz registration, licensing processes. (2026). Pids.Gov.Ph. https://serp-p.pids.gov.ph/publication/public/view?slug=more-lgus-urged-to-fully-automate-biz-registration-licensing-processes

PIDS study finds fully automated business permitting boosts local tax revenues. (2026). Mysite. http://pids.gov.ph/details/news/press-releases/pids-study-finds-fully-automated-business-permitting-boosts-local-tax-revenues

data.title: August Nimtz
data.text:
----

August H. Nimtz (born 1942) is an American political scientist. He is a professor of political science and of African American and African studies at the University of Minnesota.

His first book, Islam and Politics in East Africa (1980), based on fieldwork in the Tanzanian town of Bagamoyo, focused on the political role of its Sufi brotherhoods. Since 2000 Nimtz has written mainly about Karl Marx, Friedrich Engels and Vladimir Lenin. His books include Marx and Engels: Their Contribution to the Democratic Breakthrough (2000), a two-volume study of Lenin's electoral strategy (2014), a comparison of Marx and Frederick Douglass written with Kyle A. Edwards (2024), and a reply to Cedric Robinson's Black Marxism (2026).

== Early life and career ==
Born in 1942 [ref: August Nimtz: History and Contingency in the Making of a Black Communist, Minneapolis Interview Project] to a New Orleans family, [ref: Double Ring Ceremony Unites Nimtz-Towns In New York City, The Louisiana Weekly] Nimtz grew up under Jim Crow laws, attending schools that were segregated by law. [ref: "Black Marxism" Under Debate, 40 Years On, Cosmonaut] He took a Bachelor of Arts at Purdue University in 1963 [ref: Receiving Degrees, New Orleans States-Item] and a Ph.D. in political science at Indiana University in 1973. [ref: August H. Nimtz, jr. Islam and Politics in East Africa: The Sufi Order in Tanzania. Minneapolis: University of Minnesota Press. 1980. Pp. xvi, 234. $20.00, The American Historical Review] His doctoral research was based on fieldwork in the Tanzanian coastal town of Bagamoyo, where he lived in 1969 and 1970 and later visited. [ref: Islam in Tanzania - Islam and Politics in East Africa. The Sufi Order in Tanzania. By August H. Nimtz Jr. Minneapolis: University of Minnesota Press, 1980. Pp. xvi + 234, The Journal of African History] His first book was a shortened and revised version of the thesis.

Nimtz has taught at the University of Minnesota since 1971. He is a professor of political science and of African American and African studies there. [ref: August Nimtz, College of Liberal Arts, University of Minnesota] In 2002 he received the Horace T. Morse-University of Minnesota Alumni Association Award for Outstanding Contributions to Undergraduate Education. [ref: Distinguished Teachers Morse-Alumni, Scholars Walk]

Nimtz was a member of the Socialist Workers Party (SWP) from 1972 to 1995. He co-chaired the Minnesota Committee on Southern Africa from 1976 to 1978 and the Twin Cities chapter of the National Black Independent Political Party from 1981 to 1983. [ref: Voter's guide: City primary election, Minneapolis Star and Tribune] He twice ran for office for the SWP: for mayor of Minneapolis in 1985, [ref: Mayor, Minneapolis Star and Tribune] and the next year as running mate to Tom Jaax, its candidate for governor of Minnesota. [ref: Socialist candidate for governor wants public steel control, The Duluth News-Tribune]

== Works ==
Nimtz's first book came out of his doctoral fieldwork and was about Islam and politics in Tanzania. His later books are about Marx, Engels and Lenin, and several of them are about race and slavery in the United States.

=== Islam and politics in East Africa ===
Nimtz's first book Islam and Politics in East Africa: The Sufi Order in Tanzania came out in 1980. It examines the political role of the tariqa, or Sufi brotherhood, in East Africa under German and British colonial rule and through independence. [ref: Review of Islam and Politics in East Africa: The Sufi Order in Tanzania, The International Journal of African Historical Studies] Nimtz argues that the reason the brotherhoods grew was because they gave leadership roles to African Muslims, which they could not get within mainstream Islam. [ref: Review of Islam and Politics in East Africa: The Sufi Order in Tanzania, The American Political Science Review] The book ends with thirteen propositions meant to apply beyond East Africa. Norman R. Bennett reviewed the book in the American Historical Review and called it a major contribution that went well beyond earlier guesswork about the brotherhoods. Ibrahim Abu-Lughod called the book an important study in the American Political Science Review and C. C. Stewart wrote that the book opened a debate that had not been possible before in East Africa.

Bennet and Stewart felt the thirteen propositions at the end of the book were weak. Bennett wrote that they were commonsense conclusions from evidence and the latter called several of the propositions circular. Abu-Lughod wrote that the book stopped at the independence struggle and did not cover what happened to the brotherhoods afterwards. Marguerite Ylvisaker reviewed the book in the International Journal of African Historical Studies and wrote that she doubted Nimtz's claim that the split between "black" and "white" was the basic division in Swahili society. She also added that women's membership got only a brief mention.

=== Marx scholarship ===
Marx and Engels: Their Contribution to the Democratic Breakthrough was published in 2000. It argues that Marx and Engels were leading figures in the democratic movement of the nineteenth century and that what they went through in the revolutions of 1848 and 1849 shaped their later ideas. [ref: Review of Marx and Engels: Their Contribution to the Democratic Breakthrough, Science & Society] [ref: The Philosophy and Politics of Freedom, Monthly Review] The book follows their work in the Communist League, the revolutions themselves as well as Engels's work after Marx died. It includes a chapter that compares Marx with Alexis de Tocqueville. Paul Le Blanc reviewed the book in Monthly Review and wrote that it works both as a guide to the Marx/Engels Collected Works and as a political biography. Reviewing the book in Science & Society Mehmet Tabak called it a full account of their party work. Bradley J. Macdonald reviewed the book in Perspectives on Politics and credited Nimtz with putting their ideas back into the working-class struggles of the time. [ref: Review of Marx and Engels: Their Contribution to the Democratic Breakthrough, Perspectives on Politics]

Tabak, Le Blanc and Macdonald all thought that Nimtz claimed more than his evidence supported. Tabak said working-class organisation came before Marx and Engels and was developed largely independently of them. Le Blanc objected to the book's definition of the working class and also disagreed with what it says about the dictatorship of the proletariat. Macdonald said Nimtz had mistaken what Marx and Engels meant to do for what they actually achieved. He further wrote that his case against the "Marxologists" only works if books such as the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 and Capital are left out.

Marx, Tocqueville, and Race in America: The 'Absolute Democracy' or 'Defiled Republic (2003) grows out of the comparison in the earlier book. The book compares Tocqueville's writings on the United States with Marx's on slavery and the Civil War. [ref: Marx, Tocqueville, and race in America: the "absolute democracy" or "defiled republic", Berkeley Law Library catalogue] In a survey of Marx scholarship in English, Paul Blackledge described the book as an expansion of one chapter of Marx and Engels, and summed up its argument as being that Marx and Engels understood the American democracy of their day better than Tocqueville because they saw how much slavery and racism mattered. [ref: Marx for Today, Routledge] Richard Boyd, in Perspectives on Politics, praised the chapters on Marx and Engels. He called them detailed, and wrote that Nimtz recounts Marx's support for the Union cause with grace and passion. [ref: Review of Marx, Tocqueville and Race in America: The "Absolute Democracy" or "Defiled Republic", Perspectives on Politics] Boyd was much harder on the treatment of Tocqueville, which he called a straw man. In his opinion Nimtz attacks Tocqueville for views he did not hold. He also wrote that Democracy in America is treated as though it were only concerned with political institutions. He further objected that Nimtz applies a double standard on race, excusing Marx's racial insults while calling Tocqueville's views straightforwardly racist.

Nimtz wrote The Communist and the Revolutionary Liberal in the Second American Revolution: Comparing Karl Marx and Frederick Douglass in Real-Time (2024) with Kyle A. Edwards. The book traces Douglass from Garrisonian abolitionism to what the authors call revolutionary liberalism, and Marx from radical democracy to communism. It argues that the two converged during the Civil War and then diverged again. [ref: Marx and Douglass in Their Time, Against the Current] Jason Dawsey wrote a review of the book in Against the Current. He singled out the attention the book gives to Marx's journalism in the New York Daily Tribune and Die Presse, which he thought a useful corrective to recent scholarship's focus on the Grundrisse and Capital. Dawsey disliked the authors' talk of a "mind-meld" between the two men. He also wanted more on what was happening elsewhere in the world at the time.

"Black Marxism": A Marxist Critique (2026) is a reply to Cedric Robinson's Black Marxism: The Making of the Black Radical Tradition (1983). It gathers work Nimtz published over four decades, along with autobiographical writing and new essays. The centrepiece is his 1984 review of Robinson in the Journal of African Marxists, one of the first responses to that book. A 2002 essay answers the charge that Marx was Eurocentric. The volume closes with a new essay, "Revisiting Black Marxism Four Decades Later". Reviewing the book in Cosmonaut, Gary Levi called it the strongest available answer to charges about Marx's views on race. However, he wrote that Nimtz's strengths as a political historian do not carry over into the account of the years since the 1970s. He also found the claim that the United States is less racist and more tolerant than ever to be one-sided. Seth Sandronsky reviewed it in CounterPunch. For him the core of the book was its reading of what Marx and Engels wrote about the divisions between English and Irish workers, and between black and white workers in the United States. [ref: On Cedric Robinson's "Black Marxism", CounterPunch]

=== Lenin scholarship ===
Lenin's Electoral Strategy from Marx and Engels through the Revolution of 1905 and Lenin's Electoral Strategy from 1907 to the October Revolution of 1917 appeared in 2014. Both are subtitled The Ballot, the Streets or Both, and both deal with Lenin's leadership of the Bolshevik wing of the Russian Social Democratic Labour Party in the four Russian state Dumas. [ref: Vladimir Lenin as Democratic Vanguard Revolutionary, New Political Science] According to Nimtz Lenin used elections and parliaments for revolutionary ends more than anyone else, and that he took his lead from Marx and Engels. He describes Lenin's position as revolutionary parliamentarism: standing in elections while rejecting what Engels called parliamentary cretinism, the belief that winning seats could replace struggle outside parliament. [ref: Review of Lenin's Electoral Strategy from Marx and Engels through the Revolution of 1905 and Lenin's Electoral Strategy from 1907 to the October Revolution of 1917, Perspectives on Politics]

William W. Sokoloff, writing in New Political Science, called the books politically relevant. Bradley J. Macdonald in Perspectives on Politics contrasted the two volumes favorably against the stereotypical image of Lenin as a Jacobin, a believer in willpower and a hero of the anti-liberal crowd. Derrick Morrison, in Against the Current, called the books handbooks for anti-austerity activists. [ref: Election and Revolution, Against the Current] Sokoloff and Macdonald each had reservations. Sokoloff found Nimtz needlessly harsh towards other scholars. He also said Nimtz identifies too closely with Lenin so that the resulting Lenin is never wrong. Macdonald thought there was too much quotation of Lenin and also found the case for Lenin's present-day relevance weak. Todd Chretien said Nimtz was too absolute in tracing the split in the Second International mainly to disagreements about elections. [ref: Revolutionary parliamentarism? Lenin, the Bolsheviks, and the electoral arena, International Socialist Review]

=== Other works ===
In Marxism versus Liberalism: Comparative Real-Time Political Analysis (2019) Nimtz applies a method he calls comparative real-time political analysis. It compares rival figures against each other over the same events, and asks three questions of each: what they wrote, what their actions achieved as those events unfolded, and how accurately they read them. The book pairs Marx and Engels with Tocqueville on the French side of the European Spring, Marx with John Stuart Mill on the American Civil War, Lenin with Max Weber on the Russian Revolution of 1905, and Lenin with Woodrow Wilson on 1917 and the end of the First World War. [ref: The Democratic Quest: Marxism Versus Liberalism, New Politics] Matthew E. Strauss reviewed it in New Politics. The method, he thought, worked best in the comparison chapters and credited Nimtz with being open about its limits. He pointed out that Nimtz treats Domenico Losurdo's Liberalism: A Counter-History as an opponent when the two books complement each other.

Nimtz has also authored articles in academic journals. He wrote an article in Science & Society in 2015 on the first clash between Marxism and anarchism. He argued that the popular account, which traces the split to the debates of the First International, exaggerates their importance of those debates. He wrote that Marx and Engels never publicly confronted Mikhail Bakunin on what divided them. [ref: V. I. Lenin's Struggle Against Anarchism, International Critical Thought] There was a symposium on the article the following year. [ref: Revisiting Marxism and Anarchism, Science & Society]

== Selected publications ==
*Islam and Politics in East Africa: The Sufi Order in Tanzania, University of Minnesota Press
*Marx and Engels: Their Contribution to the Democratic Breakthrough, State University of New York Press
*Marx, Tocqueville, and Race in America: The "Absolute Democracy" or "Defiled Republic", Lexington Books
*Lenin's Electoral Strategy from Marx and Engels through the Revolution of 1905: The Ballot, the Streets or Both, Palgrave Macmillan
*Lenin's Electoral Strategy from 1907 to the October Revolution of 1917: The Ballot, the Streets or Both, Palgrave Macmillan
*The Ballot, the Streets or Both: From Marx and Engels to Lenin and the October Revolution, Haymarket Books
*Marxism versus Liberalism: Comparative Real-Time Political Analysis, Palgrave Macmillan
*The Communist and the Revolutionary Liberal in the Second American Revolution: Comparing Karl Marx and Frederick Douglass in Real-Time, Brill
*"Black Marxism": A Marxist Critique, Monthly Review Press

== References ==

== External links ==
* [https://cla.umn.edu/about/directory/profile/animtz Faculty page] at the University of Minnesota

data.title: Gilberto Conchas
data.text:
----

Gilberto Q. Conchas is an American sociologist of education. He is the Wayne K. and Anita Woolfolk Hoy Endowed Professor of Education at Pennsylvania State University.

Conchas's first book, The Color of Success (2006), compared academies within an urban high school in northern California to examine the academic success of low-income students of color. His other books include Small Schools and Urban Youth (2008), on small learning communities; Streetsmart Schoolsmart (2012), on gangs and street socialization among boys; and The Chicana/o/x Dream (2020), on first-generation Chicana/o/x college students. He has also edited volumes on race and education policy, including When School Policies Backfire (2016) and Race Frames in Education (2022).

In 2022, Conchas received the Sylvia Hurtado University Faculty Award from the American Association of Hispanics in Higher Education.

==Early life and education==
Conchas is the son of Mexican immigrant farmworkers. [ref: Education as a Tool for Breaking the Cycles of Poverty, Teachers College, Columbia University] [ref: The Interview: Gil Conchas, The Boston Globe Magazine] After attending public schools in Ventura and graduating from Ventura High School in 1988, [ref: New Ventura schools chief begins year with pep talk, Thousand Oaks Star] he received a bachelor's degree in sociology from the University of California, Berkeley, and a master's degree and doctorate in sociology from the University of Michigan. [ref: Gilberto Q. Conchas To Give Talk, "Complicating Urban Success among Black and Chicano High School Boys: 1999, 2009, and 2019", Education and Inequality Workshop, University of Pennsylvania]

==Career==
Conchas was an assistant professor at the Harvard Graduate School of Education, [ref: Keynote speaker, Ventura County Star] where in 2001 he received a National Academy of Education/Spencer Postdoctoral Fellowship. [ref: Gilberto Conchas: Promoting Minority Academic Success: Understanding the Role of Institutional Mechanisms in Distinct School Contexts, National Academy of Education] He later moved to the University of California, Irvine, where by 2008 he was an associate professor of education and chancellor's fellow. [ref: Gates Program Officer to Speak on Breaking the Intergenerational Cycle of Poverty, Teachers College, Columbia University] During the same period he was a senior program officer at the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation in its postsecondary education program for low-income young people. He left UC Irvine as a full professor, [ref: Education professor's book recognized for focus on Hispanic issues, Penn State News] and in 2020 joined Pennsylvania State University as the Wayne K. and Anita Woolfolk Hoy Endowed Professor of Education. [ref: Education researcher outlines pathways for success for minoritized students, Penn State News] In 2022 he received the Sylvia Hurtado University Faculty Award from the American Association of Hispanics in Higher Education. [ref: Sylvia Hurtado Receives Major Awards from AIR and the University of Pennsylvania, UCLA School of Education & Information Studies]

==Research and work ==
===Student success in urban schools===
In his first book, The Color of Success: Race and High-Achieving Urban Youth (2006), Conchas studied low-income Black, Latina/o and Vietnamese American students at an urban high school in northern California, which the book calls Baldwin High School. He interviewed students and compared two academies within the school and its Advanced Placement track. [ref: A review of: The Color of Success: Race and High-Achieving Urban Youth. Gilberto Q. Conchas, Journal of Education for Students Placed at Risk] The school's medical academy, which recruited "high-potential" students, produced cooperation across racial lines, while its more selective graphics academy produced competition. Conchas argued that social capital from peers and teachers shapes engagement and achievement, [ref: Book review: The Color of Success: Race and High-Achieving Urban Youth, Urban Education] and recommended small school-within-a-school programs. In Urban Education, Vichet Chhuon and Francisco D. Carranza recommended it for courses on minority education and school reform. D. Brent Edwards Jr. and Derek Tyler found it refreshing for showing that low-income minority students can achieve at high levels and recommended it as an example of context-specific research. However, they wrote that the book did not define success. Mei-Ling N. Malone called it an important resource for educators. She argued, however, that exclusive programs of the kind it recommends perpetuate tracking. [ref: Review: The Color of Success: Race and High-Achieving Urban Youth by Gilberto Q. Conchas, InterActions: UCLA Journal of Education and Information Studies] Conchas published a revised edition, The Color of Success 2.0, in 2024.

In Small Schools and Urban Youth (2008), co-authored with Louie F. Rodriguez, Conchas again studied Baldwin High School and compared its academies with small learning communities in Boston. The authors argued that relationships between students and teachers matter more to student success than school size, and that culture should take priority over size in urban school reform. [ref: Editor's review: Small Schools and Urban Youth: Using the Power of School Culture to Engage Students, Harvard Educational Review] Writing in the Harvard Educational Review, James P. Huguley called the book's evidence compelling, but pointed out that it was not a proof of a causal link. P. L. Yoder's review in Choice recommended the book as an introduction to restructuring large urban schools, but found little new thinking in its findings. [ref: Small schools and urban youth: using the power of school culture to engage students, Choice]

Streetsmart Schoolsmart was published in 2012. In it, Conchas and James Diego Vigil studied gangs and street socialization among low-income boys in Southern California. They argued that social capital gained from school and community can offset the effects of street socialization. [ref: Book review: Streetsmart Schoolsmart: Urban Poverty and the Education of Adolescent Boys, Urban Education] Laurie A. Garo called the book a timely contribution. She recommended it for training teachers and administrators. However, she wrote that its interventions mainly served students already identified as capable. In the Journal of Youth and Adolescence, Alexander C. Howell wrote that he found its account of the pressures on urban boys convincing and useful for the study of adolescence. However, he saw little empirical evidence that the programs worked. [ref: Gilberto Q. Conchas and James Diego Vigil: Streetsmart Schoolsmart: Urban Poverty and the Education of Adolescent Boys, Journal of Youth and Adolescence]

===Latina/o students===
Conchas's early work includes a 2001 Harvard Educational Review article arguing that cultural-ecological theory could not explain the wide variation in Latina/o students' school performance. [ref: Hispanic Achievement, Education Commission of the States] He later edited Cracks in the Schoolyard (2016) with Briana M. Hinga, a collection of case studies of Latina/o educational success in California written by Latina/o scholars. [ref: Cracks in the schoolyard: confronting Latino educational inequality, Choice] In the introduction he argued that such scholars are well placed to understand Latina/o students. [ref: Book review: Cracks in the Schoolyard: Confronting Latino Educational Inequality, Journal of Latinos and Education] Billie Gastic wrote in the Journal of Latinos and Education that the book avoids simple solutions. D. L. Norland wrote that the book rejected deficit models and rated it highly recommended in Choice.

Conchas wrote The Chicana/o/x Dream with Nancy Acevedo. It is based on first-person accounts of first-generation Chicana/o/x students at community colleges and four-year universities. [ref: The Chicana/o/x dream: hope, resistance, and educational success, Choice] J. E. Perez in Choice and Diane Wu Chang in the Journal of College Student Retention wrote that the book would be useful to practitioners. [ref: Book review: The Chicana/o/x Dream: Hope, Resistance, and Educational Success, Journal of College Student Retention: Research, Theory & Practice] Emily Ramos and Pedro E. Nava in their review of the book suggested that future work should include Afro-Chicanx, Indigenous and non-Californian students. [ref: The Chicana/o/x Dream: Hope, Resistance, and Educational Success, Association of Mexican American Educators Journal] The book received the American Association of Hispanics in Higher Education's 2021 Book of the Year award in the senior scholar category.

===Race in education policy===
Conchas and Michael A. Gottfried edited When School Policies Backfire (2016). It examines education policies that produced the opposite of their intended effect on disadvantaged students. [ref: When school policies backfire: how well-intended measures can harm our most vulnerable students, Choice] In Public Administration Review, James V. Shuls called the editors' definition of backfire instructive but wrote that most contributors did not apply the definition consistently. He recommended the book for courses in education policy and public administration. [ref: Review of When School Policies Backfire: How Well-Intended Measures Can Harm Our Most Vulnerable Students, Public Administration Review] P. M. Del Prado Hill, reviewing the book in Choice, recommended it to decision makers. [ref: When School Policies Backfire: How Well-Intended Measures Can Harm Our Most Vulnerable Students, Principal]

Conchas edited Race Frames in Education (2022) with Sophia Rodriguez. In the book, they apply Michael Omi and Howard Winant's racial formation theory to examine how education policies to promote equity can reproduce racial inequality. [ref: Race Frames in Education: Structuring Inequality and Opportunity in a Changing Society, Teachers College Record] [ref: Race frames in education: structuring inequality and opportunity in a changing society, Choice] He edited Transforming Education for Social Justice (2025) with Mahmoud F. Suleiman and Victor DeAlba. [ref: Transforming Education for Social Justice: Empirical Insights from Leadership, Equity, and Research in Action, ERIC] In his co-authored chapter in the volume, based on interviews with first-generation Chinese, Korean and Vietnamese American college students, Conchas found that students' views of inequality varied with migration history and gender. Transforming Education for Social Justice received the 2026 Outstanding Book Award from the Society of Professors of Education. [ref: Education chair's book on advancing equity earns national award, Penn State News]

===Youth resistance===
In 2025 Conchas and Miguel N. Abad edited two books on youth resistance. Youth Resistance for Educational Justice collects studies of how young people from racialized communities organize against injustice. [ref: Youth resistance for educational justice: pedagogical dreaming from the classroom to the streets, International Studies in Sociology of Education] Repertoires of Racial Resistance: Pedagogical Dreaming in Transborder Educational Spaces received the 2025 Critics' Choice Book Award from American Educational Studies Association. [ref: Critics' Choice Book Awards, American Educational Studies Association]

==Selected publications==
