data.title: Juste McKeown
data.text:
Justė McKeown (née Juozapaitytė), also known professionally as Juste Juozapaityte, is a Lithuanian model and entrepreneur based in London. She won the Miss Photogenic title at Miss Lithuania 2007 and the international Miss Fashion TV 2007 competition. [ref: Realybės šou ir užkulisiuose?, Lrytas.lt] [ref: Cả nước vui đón năm mới, Tuổi Trẻ]

She subsequently finished as runner-up in the seventh series of Britain's Next Top Model in 2011 and the fifth season of Top Model po-russki in 2014. [ref: Teased redhead is Top Model, Sky News] [ref: Названа новая топ-модель по-русски, Дни.ру]

Her later work has included founding London Social Media Agency and the sports coaching platform Trainow.

== Beauty pageants ==

=== Miss Lithuania 2007 ===
In 2007, McKeown, then known as Justė Juozapaitytė, participated in Grožio mokykla (Beauty School), a Lithuanian reality television programme broadcast on LNK. The programme formed part of the selection process for the Miss Lithuania 2007 beauty pageant. [ref: „Grožio mokykla“: Nerijaus Juškos laimės valanda, TV3.lt]

McKeown joined the reality programme in April 2007 and subsequently advanced to the national pageant final. The Miss Lithuania competition was held on 12 May 2007 and was won by Jurgita Jurkutė. McKeown received the Miss Foto (Miss Photogenic) title. [ref: „Mis Lietuva 2007“ karūna pasipuošė plungiškė J. Jurkutė, Lrytas.lt]

=== Miss Fashion TV 2007 ===
Later in 2007, McKeown represented Lithuania in the international Miss Fashion TV competition organised by the fashion television network FashionTV.

The final took place aboard the Fashion TV yacht F-Diamond in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, during New Year's celebrations. According to Vietnamese newspaper Tuổi Trẻ, McKeown won the Miss FTV 2007 title, with contestants from Vietnam and China finishing second and third respectively.

Her victory was subsequently covered by Lithuanian media. In April 2008, 15min published an interview discussing her pageant achievements and international modelling career. [ref: Justė Juozapaitytė – šiemet tapo „Mis Fashion TV“, 15min]

In July 2008, Lithuanian newspaper Klaipėdos diena reported that McKeown had attended the subsequent Fashion TV competition in Aqaba, Jordan, as a guest and previous titleholder. [ref: Osamos deimantinis papuošalas – lietuvei, Klaipėdos diena]

== Television career ==

=== Britain's & Ireland's Next Top Model ===
In 2011, McKeown participated in the seventh series of Britain's Next Top Model, broadcast on Sky Living and presented by Elle Macpherson.

During the competition, her makeover and photographic performances were discussed in television reviews published by Irish broadcaster RTÉ. [ref: Britain & Ireland's Next Top Model, RTÉ] [ref: Britain & Ireland's Next Top Model, RTÉ]

McKeown advanced to the final alongside Jade Thompson, finishing as runner-up in September 2011. The result was reported by Sky News and the Evening Standard. [ref: Bullied Jade Thompson wins Britain's and Ireland's Next Top Model, Evening Standard]

Her participation and final result also attracted coverage in Lithuanian media. [ref: Britų konkurse Next Top Model lietuvaitei laimėti sutrukdė kilmė?, TV3.lt]

=== Russia's Next Top Model ===
In 2014, McKeown participated in the fifth season of Top Model po-russki (Топ-модель по-русски), known as the International Season, broadcast on Russian television channel Yu-TV.

Russian entertainment publication Vokrug TV published a profile discussing her Lithuanian background, modelling experience and earlier participation in the British version of Next Top Model. [ref: Юстэ Юзапайтитэ, Вокруг ТВ]

The publication also included McKeown in its editorial analysis of the season's contestants. [ref: Топ-модель по-русски. Международный сезон: самые яркие, самые смелые и самые слабые участницы шоу, Вокруг ТВ]

McKeown reached the final alongside Evgeniya Nekrasova and Tatyana Rumyantseva. Nekrasova won the competition, while McKeown finished as runner-up. [ref: Кемеровчанка победила в шоу Топ-модель по-русски, Сибдепо]

== Modelling career ==
McKeown began working internationally as a fashion model following her participation in Miss Lithuania 2007.

In an interview published by 15min in April 2008, she described being approached by modelling agency Modilina during rehearsals for Miss Lithuania and subsequently travelling to Milan for modelling assignments. The interview also discussed photographic work in Thailand, China, Vietnam and Hong Kong.

In 2010, 15min included McKeown in a feature about models, referring to her previous Miss Fashion TV title and runway work in Italy. [ref: Ryškiausi pasaulio modeliai (nuotraukos), 15min]

Her professional modelling portfolio lists television commercial credits for Nike, Rimmel, Vodafone, Lynx, McDonald's and Very, and advertising work associated with Revlon, HTC, Ford Fiesta and Alfa Romeo. It also lists showroom assignments for Versace and Armani Jeans. [ref: Juste Juozapaityte – Female Model Profile, Model Mayhem]

The same portfolio lists photographic or editorial work for publications including Look, Time Out, Company, Volt and Cosmopolitan Lithuania, as well as an appearance in the music video for Matt Cardle's 2011 single Starlight.

== Entrepreneurship ==

=== London Social Media Agency ===
McKeown founded London Social Media Agency, a London-based digital marketing business specialising in social media management, content creation and influencer marketing.

In 2024, the agency received the Best Social Media Agency – London title in LUXlife Magazine's Creative & Visual Arts Awards. [ref: London Social Media Agency, LUXlife Magazine]

=== Trainow ===
McKeown subsequently founded Trainow, a sports coaching marketplace connecting users with sports coaches for individual training sessions.

In 2026, Trainow received the Most Innovative SaaS Marketplace 2026 title in Acquisition International's SaaS-ies awards. [ref: TRAINOW, Acquisition International]

data.title: Sripur, Malda
data.text:
Sripur is a rural area in the Malda district of West Bengal, India. It falls under the Ratua II community development block and the Chanchal subdivision. The wider Sripur area is large and includes two gram panchayats, Sripur I and Sripur II. This article focuses on a specific locality also known as Sripur, located near Sripur Halt railway station (SRPU).

== Geography and location ==

The locality extends along the road connecting Sripur bus stand to Gangadevi via GSA Road. Sripur is located approximately 42 km from Malda Town. The nearby town of Samsi provides access to educational institutions and healthcare facilities.

== Education ==

=== G.S.A. High Madrasah ===

G.S.A. High Madrasah is an educational institution located in Sripur. It is affiliated with the West Bengal Board of Madrasah Education (WBBME) and the West Bengal Council of Higher Secondary Education (WBCHSE). Students can study from Class V to Class XII. After Class X, the institution offers Arts subjects, with no Science department at the higher secondary level.

=== KGBV Girls' Hostel ===

A girls' hostel named KGBV Girls' Hostel is located under G.S.A. High Madrasah. It provides residential facilities for girls from disadvantaged backgrounds and families below the poverty line who study in Classes V to VIII. The hostel has a capacity of 100 students and approximately 20 staff members involved in cooking, management, cleaning and other duties.

=== Sripur Primary School ===

Sripur Primary School is another educational institution in the locality. Students can study from Class I to Class IV.

== Transport ==

Sripur is connected to nearby towns and areas by road and railway. National Highway 12 (NH 12) and state highways provide road connectivity between the locality and Malda Town. Railway services also connect the area with Malda Town and Malda Court. Sripur Halt railway station, with the station code SRPU, serves the locality.

== Healthcare ==

Samsi Rural Hospital is the nearby hospital serving the locality and surrounding rural areas.

== Economy ==

Agriculture is one of the main occupations of the people living in Sripur. Farming provides a livelihood for a significant part of the local population.

== Nearby educational institutions ==

Samsi College is located in the nearby town of Samsi and serves students from the surrounding areas.

data.title: Rico Africa
data.text:
Rico Africa (born Robert Berry; 1964 – 2022) was an American painter, collagist, sculptor and performance artist active in the Cass Corridor art scene of Detroit, Michigan.

== Career ==
Africa emerged in the Cass Corridor art scene in the 1980s. He was self-taught, and was described by the Detroit News as well-versed in art theory, trends and criticism. His friend, the artist and curator Dave Roberts, described him as an outsider to art-school circles whose sociability gave him wide influence among other artists. Detroit singer-songwriter Audra Kubat credited Africa, whom she described as the host of a gathering at the Foyer House, a former artists' commune, with encouraging her first public performance.

His work was shown at the Motor City Brewing Works in Detroit, whose owner, artist John Linardos, exhibited the paintings under black light. In the 1990s Africa also worked as a performance artist; his project Transgendered Frankenstein combined spoken-word poetry with a live band.

== Style and themes ==
The Detroit News characterized Africa's style as pop-influenced expressionism. He worked in acrylic on canvas, collage, works on paper and welded steel sculpture. Many works combine collage with oil painting and use bright, almost radioactive color. Recurring subjects include consumerism and corporate America, Detroit politics and society, current events, and pure abstraction. Many of his paintings are self-portraits that address his identity as a Black and mixed-race man in America.

== Death and retrospective ==
Africa died of cancer in early 2022, aged 57. A posthumous retrospective of about 50 works, mostly dating from the 1990s to the 2010s, was held at the Cass Cafe in Detroit from April 23 to May 27, 2022, curated by Dave Roberts.

data.title: LabHost
data.text:
LabHost was a subscription-based phishing-as-a-service platform that operated from 2021 until April 2024, when it was shut down in an international police operation led by London's Metropolitan Police Service and coordinated by Europol. The service sold users templates for fake websites imitating banks, postal services and other organisations, along with hosting and tools for running SMS phishing campaigns. The Metropolitan Police said the platform had about 2,000 paying users who created some 40,000 fraudulent websites, and that it had been used to obtain about 480,000 payment card numbers, 64,000 PINs and more than one million passwords worldwide.

Between 14 and 17 April 2024, police in several countries searched about 70 addresses and arrested 37 people, including the service's original developer in the United Kingdom. In April 2025 the developer was sentenced to eight and a half years' imprisonment after pleading guilty to fraud and money-laundering offences. Prosecutions of individual users followed in other countries, including Canada and the Netherlands.

== Background ==
According to the Associated Press, LabHost was set up in 2021 and charged its users a monthly fee. Trend Micro, a security company that assisted the investigation, said the service appeared in late 2021 and mainly targeted customers of organisations in Canada, the United States and the United Kingdom. Australian police said the platform started in Canada before spreading to the UK, Ireland and elsewhere.

Subscriptions were paid in cryptocurrency. Trend Micro reported three membership tiers costing between US$179 and US$300 a month, the cheapest covering Canadian institutions and the most expensive covering more than 70 institutions in other countries. Users could choose among templates impersonating about 170 organisations, 47 of them based in the UK, according to police figures reported by the Press Association. The service also supplied tutorial videos.

Trend Micro described two built-in tools: "LabSend", for sending phishing text messages from customisable templates, and "LabRat", which used adversary-in-the-middle techniques to intercept credentials and two-factor authentication codes while a victim was entering them.

== Investigation and takedown ==
The Metropolitan Police investigation, named Operation Stargrew, began in June 2022 after the force received intelligence from the Cyber Defence Alliance, an information-sharing body of UK banks. Trend Micro said it began assisting the Metropolitan Police in June 2023. Europol's European Cybercrime Centre and the Joint Cybercrime Action Taskforce supported the case, and law enforcement agencies from 19 countries took part. In Australia, investigators began work on the platform's local users in October 2023.

Searches took place from 14 to 17 April 2024 at about 70 addresses worldwide, and 37 suspects were arrested. Europol said four of those arrested in the UK were linked to running the site, among them its original developer. UK arrests were reported at Manchester and Luton airports, in Essex and in London. On 18 April 2024 the Metropolitan Police replaced the LabHost website with a police notice.

In Australia, about 200 officers from the Australian Federal Police and four state police forces executed 22 search warrants in five states; two men from Melbourne and Adelaide were arrested and charged over alleged use of LabHost, and three others were arrested on drug charges during the searches. In Ireland, the Garda Síochána carried out 12 searches in Dublin, Kildare and Waterford, arrested two men and said it had linked 116 LabHost users to the country.

Private companies that assisted investigators included Trend Micro and Microsoft. The blockchain analysis company Chainalysis said wallets linked to LabHost received more than US$1.1 million in cryptocurrency between August 2021 and April 2024.

== Results ==
The Metropolitan Police said that up to 70,000 people in the UK had been victims of LabHost-based phishing. Police said they had contacted up to 25,000 UK victims to tell them their data had been compromised. About 800 LabHost users received a message from the police stating that their identities were known to investigators. The force said the platform had received just under £1 million in payments from users.

Australian police said the personal details of about 94,000 Australians had been obtained through the service, and estimated that it could have caused up to A$28 million in losses in Australia.

== Prosecutions ==
In September 2024 LabHost's developer, a man from Huddersfield, pleaded guilty to making or supplying articles for use in fraud, encouraging or assisting the commission of an offence, and transferring criminal property. On 14 April 2025 he was sentenced at Manchester Crown Court to eight and a half years' imprisonment. The Crown Prosecution Service said he had received about US$230,000 in cryptocurrency for creating and running the site between August 2021 and October 2023, and that it would seek confiscation of his assets.

In April 2025 the Sûreté du Québec and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police arrested 87 people in the Montreal area accused of carrying out phishing attacks with LabHost, following on from a server seized during the 2024 takedown. In November 2025 a court in the Netherlands convicted a LabHost user of phishing offences and imposed a partly suspended prison sentence and community service.

== Reliability of figures ==
Published figures for the platform's scale vary between sources. The Metropolitan Police reported about 2,000 registered users, while Europol and Australian police cited a figure of about 10,000 users. Estimates of losses also changed over time: police in 2024 said the service had earned just under £1 million from subscriptions, while at sentencing in 2025 the Crown Prosecution Service estimated that LabHost had enabled at least £100 million in fraud losses worldwide, including more than £32 million in the UK. Infosecurity Magazine noted that the prosecution's loss estimate was far higher than the earlier police figure. Reported numbers of participating countries ranged from 17 to 19.

data.title: Friendly Captcha
data.text:
Friendly Captcha is a German computer security company based in Wörthsee, Bavaria, and the name of its CAPTCHA service. Founded in 2020 by Benedict Padberg and Guido Zuidhof, the company offers a service that, instead of asking visitors to solve image or text puzzles, has the visitor's browser complete a proof of work calculation in the background. Government accessibility guidance in Germany and Luxembourg has cited it as an example of proof-of-work CAPTCHAs. The company won the start-up category of the in 2023.

== History ==
Friendly Captcha was founded at the end of 2020 by Benedict Padberg and Guido Zuidhof. According to a 2024 profile in the magazine of the Munich and Upper Bavaria chamber of commerce, the founders financed the company from their own funds and from revenue rather than outside investment.

== Technology ==
When a user loads a page that embeds the Friendly Captcha widget, the widget presents the user's browser with a cryptographic puzzle. Solving it takes the browser a few seconds and usually requires no action from the user, while making automated mass submissions slower and more costly. The difficulty of the puzzle escalates when requests appear more likely to come from a bot. The underlying principle, proof of work, had been in use for decades before the company adopted it for CAPTCHAs.

== Reception ==
A guide published by the, the German federal body that monitors the accessibility of public-sector IT, lists proof-of-work methods among accessible alternatives to conventional CAPTCHAs, naming Friendly Captcha as an example. According to the guide, because the calculation runs in the background, such CAPTCHAs help users who are disadvantaged by incomprehensible, visual or audio tasks. A 2025 article on the Luxembourg government's accessibility portal likewise named Friendly Captcha as an example of proof-of-work CAPTCHAs, a family it said generally performs well on both accessibility and privacy and requires little or no user interaction. In a September 2025 survey of 821 Luxembourg public-sector websites, the same portal found Friendly Captcha on two sites, compared with reCAPTCHA on 98.

A 2024 article in Communications of the ACM, written by the developers of the competing mCaptcha system, included Friendly Captcha in a table comparing CAPTCHA services. The table noted that Friendly Captcha works over the Tor network and is accessible to screen reader users, but that it is not open source and its validation mechanism is undocumented. It listed application-specific integrated circuits and very large botnets as possible ways to bypass it.

== Awards ==
In September 2023, Friendly Captcha won the start-up category of the Deutscher Gründerpreis, a German award for founders, at a ceremony held at the ZDF capital studio in Berlin. The other finalists in the category were Edurino and Klim.

data.title: GradeX
data.text:
----

GradeX is an Uzbekistan-based human resources consulting and technology company specializing in job evaluation, organizational design, compensation management, and the automation of human resources processes. The company combines HR consulting services, recruitment services, with the development of proprietary software for HR automation, that includes, job grading, performance management, flexible benefits, applicant tracking system, annual leaves management. [ref: Job Grading & HR Consulting, GradeX] [ref: Job Grading & HR Consulting, GradeX]

GradeX provides consulting services related to organizational structures, job architecture, compensation frameworks, and the implementation of HR management systems. Its software platform, also named GradeX, is designed to support these processes through integrated data management, workflow automation, and artificial intelligence. [ref: Job Grading & Performance Management Software, GradeX]

==== Activities Human resources consulting ====
GradeX operates in the field of human resources and organizational management consulting. Its activities include job evaluation, the development of grading systems, organizational design, compensation management, and HR process optimization.

The company's consulting approach involves assessing organizational requirements, developing evaluation frameworks, and supporting their implementation. Its services address the relationships between organizational roles, responsibilities, compensation, and employee performance.

==== HR technology and automation ====
In addition to consulting, GradeX develops software intended to automate human resources processes. Its technology activities focus on connecting organizational data with HR workflows and reducing the need for manual administration. [ref: GradeX - AI-powered Job Evaluation & Grading Platform, app.gradex.uz]

The company incorporates artificial intelligence into selected processes, including the collection of job information and the preparation of job evaluation recommendations. The platform retains human review and approval of AI-generated recommendations.

==== GradeX platform ====
The GradeX platform is a web-based human resources management system developed by the company. It uses a shared organizational data structure connecting employees, positions, departments, reporting relationships, and job grades.

==== Publications ====
GradeX publishes educational and analytical content concerning human resources management, organizational behavior, workplace psychology, and compensation practices. [ref: Blog, GradeX] [ref: ] [ref: Instagram, www.instagram.com] [ref: GradeX, Telegram]

Its online publication, GradeX Journal, features articles on management research and behavioral phenomena affecting organizational decision-making. Content is published in Russian, English, and Uzbek.

data.title: Anuradha Pathak
data.text:
----

Dr.Anuradha Pathak (born August 1, 1985) is an Indian academic and philosopher specializing in Advaita Vedanta. She currently serves as the Head and Assistant Professor in the Department of Philosophy at R.D.S. College, Muzaffarpur, Bihar, under B.R.A. Bihar University.She is also heavily involved in the National Service Scheme (N.S.S.), notably leading the Bihar and Jharkhand state N.S.S. volunteer team at the 2023 Republic Day parade in New Delhi.

== Early life and education ==
Anuradha Pathak was born on August 1, 1985.She completed her higher education at Banaras Hindu University (B.H.U.) in Varanasi.She earned her Bachelor of Arts in 2004, a Master of Arts in Philosophy in 2006, and was awarded her Ph.D. in Philosophy in 2010.Her doctoral thesis was focused on Advaita Vedanta (अद्वैत वेदान्त में सुषुप्ति).From 2015 to 2018, she completed a Post-Doctoral Fellowship sponsored by the University Grants Commission (UGC), researching dreams in Indian philosophy.

== Academic career ==
Pathak began her teaching career as a temporary lecturer at Bareilly College in 2011, later serving as a Post-Doctoral Fellow in the Faculty of Arts at B.H.U. in 2015 and 2016.

In May 2017, she was appointed as an Assistant Professor at M.J.K. College in Bettiah, West Champaran, where she subsequently served as the Head of the Department of Philosophy from June 2017 until January 2024. [ref: MJK College Updates, Prabhat Khabar]

In January 2024, she transferred to R.D.S.College, Muzaffarpur, as an Assistant Professor of Philosophy, and was appointed Head of the Department in July 2024. [ref: Teachers Details: Dr. Anuradha Pathak, B.R.A. Bihar University]

== Administrative and community leadership ==

Pathak has held numerous administrative and community-focused roles, primarily through the National Service Scheme (N.S.S.). She served as an N.S.S. Program Officer at M.J.K.College and was the Nodal Officer for the West Champaran district in 2020–2021.In January 2023, she was selected as the team leader for the N.S.S. volunteer contingent representing Bihar and Jharkhand at the Republic Day parade on the Kartavya Path in New Delhi. [ref: पहल: परेड में बिहार- झारखंड की एनएसएस टीम का नेतृत्व करेंगी डॉ. अनुराधा पाठक, Dainik Bhaskar]

In April 2025, she was appointed as the N.S.S. Coordinator for Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University, where she initiated regular campus cleanliness awareness programs. She has also served as an Assistant Controller of Examination at R.D.S. College

== Publications ==
Pathak has authored over 30 academic research papers and has contributed to university-level curricula.Notably, she authored a textbook chapter titled "भगवान की अवधारणा और स्वरूप" (Concept and Nature of Bhagavan) for the Indira Gandhi National Open University (IGNOU) M.A. Hindu Adhyayan program. [ref: इकाई-2 भगवान की अवधारणा और स्वरूप, IGNOU eGyanKosh] She also edited the book आधुनिक भारतीय दार्शनिक-भाग - 1 (Modern Indian Philosophers - Part 1), published in 2025.
Some of her selected publications include:

1. बौद्ध- न्याय विमर्श: एक दार्शनिक विश्लेषण, Darshnik Traimasik,oct.-dec. 2023, ISSN:0974-8849,SI.No. 4, year-69,page no. 69-76 [ref: बौद्ध - न्याय विमर्श: एक दार्शनिक विश्लेषण, darshanik traimasik]

2. Kabir Ke Chintan Mein Anekta Mein Ekta Ka Darshan", Shodh Drishti, Vol. 2, No. 4, April-June 2011, Published by Srijan Samiti, Varanasi (ISSN-0976-6650), Pg. No. 183-184. [ref: Kabir Ke Chintan Mein Anekta Mein Ekta Ka Darshan, Shodh Drishti]

3. अद्वैतीय दृष्टिकोण से स्वचेतना पर विमर्श, Darshnik Triamasik, 2021,jan-march, ISSN:0974-8849 [ref: अद्वैतीय दृष्टिकोण से स्वचेतना पर विमर्श, Darshnik Triamasik]

4. Gandhi ka swaraj darshan: Bharat ki punarkhoj" Darshanik Traimasik, year -66, No.01, Jan-Mar 2020, ISSSN 0974-8849. Pg.no. 129-141 [ref: Gandhi ka swaraj darshan: Bharat ki punarkhoj, Darshanik Traimasik]

5. Aarambhik Vaidik Sahitya Mein Swapna-Awastha', Darshanik Traimasik, Year 64, No. 1, Jan-March, 2018, ISSN: 0974-8849, p. 116-123. [ref: Aarambhik Vaidik Sahitya Mein Swapna-Awastha, Darshanik Traimasik]

== Awards and honors ==
* Vijaya Shri Smriti Yuva Puraskar (2017): Awarded by the Akhil Bhartiya Darshan Parishad for her paper presentation on "Vaidik Sahitya Mein Swapna" at Jai Narayan Vyas University, Jodhpur.

data.title: GoMore
data.text:
GoMore is a Danish car-sharing company based in Copenhagen. It runs an online platform on which private individuals and businesses rent out cars, and it also offers car leasing. In Spain it operates under the brand Amovens. [ref: Getaround Europe and GoMore merge to create Europe's largest peer-to-peer carsharing network, Tech.eu] In 2026 it acquired the European operations of Getaround; the combined business reported more than five million users in 11 European countries. [ref: GoMore Becomes Europe's Largest Peer-to-Peer Car-Sharing Platform After Acquiring Getaround Europe, Øresund Startups]

== History ==
GoMore was started in 2005 by Matias Møl Dalsgaard and Søren Riis and was relaunched in 2011 when further partners joined. [ref: Gomore: fem år og to millioner brugere senere, TechSavvy] It expanded to Sweden in 2014. [ref: Så blir bilsemestern billig, Dagens Nyheter] In March 2015 it acquired the Spanish ride-sharing service Amovens, founded in 2009 by Diego Hidalgo. [ref: Spanish car sharing platform Amovens acquired by GoMore, Novobrief] Later launches included Switzerland (2021) [ref: Geld verdienen mit dem eigenen Auto?, Luzerner Zeitung], Austria (2022) [ref: GoMore: So funktioniert die neue private Autovermietung in Österreich, Trending Topics] and Estonia (2024). [ref: Eestis alustab inimeselt inimesele autode jagamise platvorm GoMore, Raamatupidamisuudised] In 2021 the Swiss insurer Baloise invested about €5 million in the company. [ref: Baloise kauft sich bei dänischer Carsharing-Firma GoMore ein, cash.ch]

In February 2026 GoMore closed its ride-sharing service in Denmark, by then the only country where it was offered, to concentrate on car rental and leasing. [ref: Tak for turen, GoMore] [ref: GoMore dropper samkørsel i Danmark, TV 2]

In May 2026 GoMore acquired Getaround Europe, the European business of the US company Getaround, which operates mainly in France, Norway, Belgium and Germany. The purchase was financed with equity from existing investors and loans from EIFO and Nordea. The combined business reported about 70,000 shared cars, about 1.5 million rentals a year and net revenue of more than €50 million. [ref: GoMore übernimmt Getaround Europe und wird größte Carsharing-Plattform Europas, Trending Topics] Getaround continued as a separate platform after the purchase. [ref: Getaround and GoMore: a new chapter for carsharing in Europe, Getaround] In Austria, Getaround's cars later moved to the GoMore platform. [ref: Unsere Autos in Österreich sind jetzt bei GoMore, Getaround]

== Services ==
Car owners list cars on the GoMore website or app and renters book them. Many cars can be unlocked with the app, without a key handover. GoMore also offers leasing and a subscription, GoMore+, which gives a discount on rentals. [ref: New: Get a discount every time you rent a car with GoMore+, GoMore]

data.title: Moyo Ogunseinde
data.text:
Moyo Ogunseinde is a Nigerian architect, real estate developer, designer, and hospitality entrepreneur. She is the founder and Group Chief Executive Officer of Club Concierge Africa, a travel and hospitality group whose brands include Club Concierge International, GoTravelCC, GoPartnerCC and MyTravelCC. Trained at University College London, Moyo Ogunseinde designed the Radisson Blu Anchorage Hotel in Lagos and sits on the board of its owner, Anchorage Leisures. Earlier in her career she was an executive director of Uraga Real Estate, a member of the Honeywell Group, where she led the development of the Upbeat Recreation Centre, described in the Nigerian press as West Africa's first trampoline park. She has chaired the Lagos State Gymnastics Association since 2018.

== Early life and education ==
Moyo Ogunseinde is from Ibadan, Nigeria. She has cited the city's markets, colours and cultural life as an influence on her later design work. She trained as an architect at University College London and later undertook executive education at Harvard Business School. She is a chartered architect.

== Career ==

=== Architecture and real estate ===
Moyo Ogunseinde began her career in architecture before moving into real estate development in Nigeria. She designed the Radisson Blu Anchorage Hotel on Victoria Island, Lagos, which opened in 2011, and later oversaw the renovation of its rooms and business lounge. She became an executive director of Uraga Real Estate Limited, a subsidiary of the Honeywell Group, contributing to design, land acquisition and planning.

=== Upbeat Recreation Centre ===
As an executive director of Uraga Real Estate, Moyo Ogunseinde led the development of the Upbeat Recreation Centre, a multi-purpose leisure facility on Admiralty Road, Lekki, which opened in December 2017 and was reported in the Nigerian media as West Africa's first trampoline park. The project was conceived during Nigeria's 2016 recession as a diversification into recreational real estate, aimed at the country's young population. The centre set up a gymnastics club in February 2018 and held its first trampoline gymnastics competition in October 2018. In 2024 it hosted a fun day for underprivileged children in Lekki.

=== Aga Culture ===
In 2017 Moyo Ogunseinde founded Aga Culture (originally Àga Concept), an African lifestyle and design brand based in Lagos, and serves as its creative director. The name derives from the Yoruba word àga, meaning a chair or functional object. The brand produces clothing, furniture and homeware that combine Yoruba and wider African traditions with a contemporary, minimalist aesthetic, and emphasises slow fashion and ethically sourced materials such as Adire cotton and linen. Its furniture includes the Oko chair, drawn from traditional farming tools, and the Egungun accessories collection, inspired by Egungun masquerades; in 2020 the American trade magazine Hospitality Design named Moyo Ogunseinde one of six rising product designers. The brand's Mmanwu chair featured in Cultured magazine's 2021 survey of the Lagos design scene. Its work has also included the AADA clothing collection and participation in design exhibitions.

=== Hospitality ===
Moyo Ogunseinde has served as executive director of Anchorage Leisures Limited, owner of the Radisson Blu Anchorage Hotel, and sits on its board. She is also a board member of the Honeywell Group and an advisory board member of Wavecrest College of Hospitality, Lagos. In a 2022 interview she argued that Nigeria could develop world-class tourism by investing in local infrastructure and emphasised local content in the hotel's operations, art and food sourcing. In November 2025 she accepted the Best Corporate Hotel award at the World Luxury Awards in Barcelona on behalf of the Radisson Blu Anchorage, where she was described as a board member and key owner of the property. In 2025 she was included in a Nigerian trade listing of "Top 100 Women in Hospitality".

=== Club Concierge Africa ===

Moyo Ogunseinde founded Club Concierge Africa (CCA) during the COVID-19 pandemic, building a travel, hospitality and lifestyle group intended to serve African travellers. The group offers travel membership, travel management, hospitality partnerships and concierge services. Its brands are:
* Club Concierge International (CCI), a travel club offering vacation-ownership membership for leisure travellers and, through Club Concierge for Business, corporate travel membership;
* GoTravelCC, a travel-management company offering flights, hotels and related services;
* MyTravelCC, a flights-first travel booking brand;
* GoPartnerCC, the group's partnership brand;
* Concierge Resort, which manages resort destinations; and
* CSolute, a business-to-business travel affiliate arm.

As Group CEO, Moyo Ogunseinde oversees operations across several African and international markets. In September 2026 she spoke on a panel on cross-border payments at the 22nd Akwaaba African Travel Market in Lagos, calling for closer cooperation between regulators, payment providers and tourism operators to reduce the cost of travel within Africa.

== Sports administration ==
On 3 December 2018 Moyo Ogunseinde was inaugurated as chair of the Lagos State Gymnastics Association by Kweku Tandoh, executive chairman of the Lagos State Sports Commission. Her first duty was supporting the Lagos team at the 19th National Sports Festival in Abuja, where it won two gold and two bronze medals. In April 2019 the association partnered with the International Gymnastics Federation, and she unveiled a four-year development plan for the sport in Lagos and called for gymnastics to be added to school curricula. She has also served on the board of the Lagos State Sports Trust Fund. In 2021 she was named among nominees for induction into the African Sports Tourism Hall of Fame.

Moyo Ogunseinde is the founder of WANAMKE, a non-governmental organisation focused on the development of women in sport.

== Other activities ==
Moyo Ogunseinde has been associated with Artclip Africa, a gallery promoting Nigerian contemporary art in partnership with the Radisson Blu Anchorage Hotel. In August 2026 she was a speaker at The Borderless Experience, a travel and hospitality event held in Lagos and organised by Condia.

== Recognition ==
According to BusinessDay, Moyo Ogunseinde has received the Nigerian Institute of Architects' Best Qualified Registered Architect award and the Interior Design Excellence Award for Best Hospitality Designer.

data.title: Sam Slater (composer)
data.text:
Sam Slater is a British composer, music producer and sound designer based in Berlin. His work includes experimental recordings, solo work, film and television scores, video-game music and audiovisual performance. [ref: Sam Slater, CTM Festival] He collaborated with Hildur Guðnadóttir as score producer on Chernobyl and Joker, and as co-composer on Battlefield 2042. [ref: Chaos and Climate: Hildur Guðnadóttir and Sam Slater on scoring the near-future world of Battlefield 2042, MusicTech] The Recording Academy credits him with two Grammy wins, for Chernobyl in 2020 and Joker in 2021. [ref: Sam Slater, Recording Academy]

== Background and early career ==
Slater began producing recordings as a teenager and studied experimental composition at the University of Leeds. He moved to Germany in 2013. His early professional work included musical sound design and creative engineering for the Icelandic composer Jóhann Jóhannsson.

== Career ==

=== Film, television and video games ===
Slater worked with Guðnadóttir on the scores for the 2019 television miniseries Chernobyl and the film Joker, serving as score producer and musical sound designer. For the 2021 video game Battlefield 2042, the pair co-composed a score built around distorted textures and experimental sound-making. They received the Society of Composers & Lyricists award for Outstanding Original Score for Interactive Media in 2022. [ref: 3rd SCL Awards Held, Winners Announced, Society of Composers & Lyricists]

He composed the score for the Netflix series The Railway Men (2023), which concerns the 1984 Bhopal disaster. In an interview with Rolling Stone India, he discussed drawing on memories of the ravanahatha and railway sounds while developing the music. [ref: ‘The Railway Men’ Music Composer Sam Slater Takes Us Behind His Process, Rolling Stone India] The score won the Filmfare OTT Award for Best Background Music (Series) in 2024. [ref: Filmfare OTT Awards 2024: Who won maximum awards?, Filmfare]

His documentary work includes Mstyslav Chernov's 2000 Meters to Andriivka and Dmytro Hreshko's Divia, both released in 2025. [ref: 10th Annual Critics Choice Documentary Awards – List of Nominees and Winners (2025), Critics Choice Association] [ref: Exclusive: Trailer From Dmytro Hreshko’s Karlovy Vary-Premiering ‘Divia’, International Documentary Association] Chernov described how Slater incorporated battlefield recordings into the former's score, using gunfire and radio transmissions as musical material. [ref: Metric of Loss: Mstyslav Chernov Discusses the Ethical Responsibility of ‘2000 Meters to Andriivka’, International Documentary Association]

In 2026, Slater composed the music for Housemarque's Saros, combining electronic music with drone-metal influences. [ref: Saros, drone metal and the year's most stressful game soundtrack, NME]

=== Recordings and performance ===
Slater released Wrong Airport Ghost through Bedroom Community in 2018. Its development followed his work with musician Krishna Bhopa in Rajasthan and experiments with the sonic possibilities of a single string. [ref: Sam Slater Details Bedroom Community LP, ‘Wrong Airport Ghost’, XLR8R]

His second solo album, I Do Not Wish to Be Known as a Vandal, followed on the same label in 2022. The album assembled contributions from instrumentalists and vocalists. [ref: Sam Slater on bringing emotion into experimental composition, Composer] A related audiovisual work was developed with visual artist Theresa Baumgartner and dancer and choreographer Lukas Malkowski. [ref: I Do Not Wish To Be Known As A Vandal, Bedroom Community]

He is a member of Osmium with Guðnadóttir, James Ginzburg and Rully Shabara. The ensemble performs with custom-built instruments.

Slater's third solo album, Lunng (2026), features collaborators including Bendik Giske, Maria W. Horn, Adam Betts and Yair Glotman. Reviewing the album for The Quietus, Bernie Brooks highlighted its mixture of heavy textures and more delicate passages, and the integration of its contributors into Slater's arrangements. [ref: Sam Slater: Lunng, The Quietus]

Slater co-founded the record label Mt. Brings Death with guitarist Mason Lindahl in 2025. [ref: About, Sam Slater]

data.title: Citizens State Bank (Edmond, Oklahoma)
data.text:
Citizens State Bank is a historic building in downtown Edmond, Oklahoma. It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The bank was founded April 18, 1901. [ref: 125-year mark Edmond’s oldest operating business still meeting community needs, edmondlifeandleisure.com]

The red sandstone building is at 102 South Broadway was originally called Citizens Bank. [ref: Historic Citizens’ State Bank: Edmond, OK] The stone was quartied nearby. [ref: Edmond Historic Sites - Edmond Historic Preservation Trust] W. H. Tuttle its first president followed by co-founder W. J. Huffman in 1907, the same year Oklahoma became a state, and Edwin A. == Early Life and Education ==
Ahmed Gadalla [ref: ], or Ahmed Alushibe, is a Libyan businessman chairing Alushibe Holding Group and sitting at the top of several industrial companies in Libya.

He studied industrial engineering at the University of Garyounis, now the University of Benghazi.

In 2025, Gadalla completed a Master of Business Administration at International Business University in Toronto, Canada [ref: ].

== Business Career ==
In 2008, Ahmed Gadalla founded the Alushibe Holding Group [ref: ALUSHIBE – Holding, alushibe.com]. The company began as an automative-parts business in Benghazi, Libya. Currently Alushibe Holding group covers consumer goods, industrial manufacturing, engineering, healthcare and retail.

During Gadalla's tenure as chair of the Libyan Cement Company, Alushibe Holding Group announced a program to rehabilitate and expand the company's cement plants, aiming for 3 million tons of annual capacity.

Gadalla is associated with the food sector through Zulfa Food Industries [ref: Zulfa Factory Close to Completion, www.alushibenews.com]. This company is building milk and juice facilities in Benghazi together with Tetra Pak [ref: Libya’s Food-Processing Opportunity Is Bigger Than Agriculture - Markets & Companies - Business, Ahram Online].

The largest project is in steel. As chairman of Libya United Steel Company [ref: Tosyalı Sulb Steel Industries Joint Company, Tosyalı Holding] (SULB), Gadalla oversaw a partnership with the Turkish producer Tosyalı Holding [ref: Home Page, Tosyalı Holding] to build a $2.5B direct-reduced iron complex near Benghazi. The project was announced in 2024 and, across all its phases, is planned to produce roughly 8.1 million tons a year [ref: The Vietnam Trap: Why Libya’s Industrial Mega-Projects Must Build Supply Chains, Not Just Factories – OpEd, www.eurasiareview.com] [ref: What Asia’s Industrialization Lessons Can Teach Fragmented States] [ref: From Libya to the world: How international business can strengthen libya’s economy, Gulf Times].

data.text:
WeFixmoney.com is a family owned American online loan marketplace and financial lead generator headquartered in Lorton, Virginia. Founded in 2008, the platform is a free connection service matching potential customers seeling short term personal loans, cash advances, or installment loans with direct lenders in its network.

== History ==

WeFixMoney.com was officially launched in 2008 as a web-based financial portal to assist consumers in obtaining short-term liquidity. [ref: ]

* 2013: The platform expanded its network to include its 100th direct lending partner
* 2014: WeFixMoney.com reached a milestone of over 1 million total customers served.
* 2015: The company was recognized by the Online Lenders Alliance (OLA), recieving the Extraordinary Contribution Award for its work within the online lending marketplace ecosystem
* 2025: The company reported serving over [https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7417513467890319360 8 million customers] since inception.

== Services & Business Model ==
WeFixMoney.com operates as a non-bank financial connection platform rather than a direct lender. The service is free to use and operates entirely online: [ref: ]

# Application: Applicats fill out a single online form specifying desired funding amount (typically between $100 and $5000), monthly income, and basic personal details.
# Matching: The platform evaluates applicat data against criteria provided by its network of independent third-party lenders.
# Redirection & Disbursement: If a match is found, appliants are redirected to the respective lender's portal to review and finalize loan terms, with funding discbuersed as soon as the same business day.

The company states its primary mission is providing accessible liquidity options for consumers, including individuals with bad or limited credit histories who may not qualify for standard bank products. [ref: ]

== Industry Accrediations & Memberships ==

* Online Lenders Alliance (OLA): Member of the [https://onlinelendersalliance.org/ OLA], adhering to industry standards for best practices and fair online lending principles.
* Better Business Bureau (BBB): Holds an [https://www.bbb.org/us/va/lorton/profile/payday-loans/fix-media-llc-0241-5717809 "A" rating] from the Better Business Bureau.

== User Feedback ==

=== Posetive Feedback ===
Users often cite the platform's rapid approval process, ease of application, and availability to borrowers with subprime credit profiles as primary advantages. The matching service is completely free to applicants. who remain under no onlihation to accept any loan offer or terms presented by direct lenders. Operating 24/7, the platform allows users to complete applications from mobile devices in the comfort of home, backed by responsive customer support. [ref: ]

=== Market Considerations ===
As an intermediary, WeFixMoney.com does not set interest rates, loan terms, or fees. Industry analysts and consumer reviews note that third-party lenders within online loan networks can charge High Annual Percentage Rate (APRs), often associated with short-term installment and payday loans. Additiional criticisms focus on variable transparency dependent on individual matched lenders. [ref: ]

data.text:
----

MUGnet is a Japanese fan-based circle that creates visual novels.

== Overview ==
Under the slogan "Questioning the World," the circle creates works that explore philosophical themes such as perspectives on life and happiness. Its works are characterized by a fusion of story-driven scenarios and graphic expressions that enhance immersion. Through the visual novels it produces, the circle offers players a different perspective on the world.

The circle's name, "MUGnet," is a portmanteau combining English slang, the nature of the circle's activities, and the homonym "magnet." Zakinu, one of the founders, revealed in an official note post that the name was derived from the following two elements. [ref: MUGnetについて語る, note]

* MUG： English slang meaning a "fool" or "gullible person."
* net：Derived from the internet-based nature of their activities.

Although the spelling differs from the actual English word "magnet," this is intentional rather than a typo.

It conveys the meaning that "fools (MUG) active on the internet (net) attract or involve people like a magnet."

== History ==

* July 17, 2024 – Established for creative activities. [ref: MUGnet 1周年記念特設サイト, mugnet.jp]
* December 30, 2024 – Released their debut work, Journey to die, at Comic Market 105 (C105).
* May 2025 – Featured in an interview by the indie game event DREAMSCAPE, discussing the circle's origins and production structure.
* July 17 – 31, 2025 – Offered Journey to die at a 50% discount on the official BOOTH store to commemorate the circle's 1st anniversary.
* August 17, 2025 – Participated in Comic Market 106 (C106).
* September 11, 2025 – Began streaming/releasing music related to Journey to die.
* December 31, 2025 – Released Bonten Sekai no Kowashikata at Comic Market 107 (C107). [ref: ]
* April 2026 – Bonten Sekai no Kowashikata was featured in the serial column "Mirai no Game ni Tsuite Ohanashi Shimasu" by Kosaku Akano in the April 2026 issue of S-F Magazine.
* July 17, 2026 – Opened a special website to commemorate the circle's 2nd anniversary, featuring statements from MUGnet members.
* August 16, 2026 – Participated in Comic Market 108 (C108).

== Media ==
In May 2025, an interview with MUGnet's representative members, Zakinu and Usagi Moto, was published as part of a serialized feature in the indie game media outlet DREAMSCAPE. The interview covered topics such as the circle being composed primarily of junior and senior high school students, the background behind the production of Journey to die, and the division of roles in scenario writing and system development.

According to the interview, the circle is mainly composed of junior and senior high school students, and the members discussed the production background of Journey to die along with their division of roles in scenario and system development. [ref: DREAMSCAPE JOURNAL#20 【MUGnet】｜DREAMSCAPE, note（ノート）]

In 2026, Bonten Sekai no Kowashikata was featured in Kosaku Akano's serialized column "Mirai no Game ni Tsuite Ohanashi Shimasu" in the April 2026 issue of S-F Magazine. Akano praised the work for tackling the theme of juvenile fiction head-on within a science fiction worldview. [ref: ＳＦマガジン 2026年 4月号, 株式会社早川書房]

: The circle's debut work, themed around "death" and depicting what one thinks about at the very end of life.

data.title: Tommy Beavers
data.text:
----

William Thomas "Tommy" Beavers (December 14, 1949 – October 29, 2023) was an American drummer best known as a member of the Western swing band Asleep at the Wheel. He performed on the band's 1993 album Tribute to the Music of Bob Wills and the Texas Playboys and was credited by the Recording Academy with one Grammy Award win and two nominations. Earlier in his career, Beavers performed with Tommy Shaw in the Montgomery, Alabama-based band Harvest.

==Career==

===Harvest and Harmony===
During the 1970s, Beavers played drums in the Montgomery-based band Harvest with bassist Jimbo Jones, keyboardist Eddie Wohlford and guitarist and vocalist Tommy Shaw. [ref: The Quaz Q&A: Tommy Shaw, Jeff Pearlman]

In a 2011 interview, Shaw recalled his time with Harvest and specifically praised Beavers's drumming, noting his ability to control his dynamics while performing in the group's small venue.

After Shaw left Harvest to join Styx, the group continued as Harmony. Singer-songwriter Beth Nielsen Chapman subsequently joined the lineup. [ref: Tommy Beavers, Encyclopedia of Alabama]

===Asleep at the Wheel===
Beavers joined Asleep at the Wheel in the early 1990s, replacing drummer David Sanger. He was part of the lineup that recorded the 1993 album Tribute to the Music of Bob Wills and the Texas Playboys. [ref: Tommy Beavers – Biography, Discography, Albums & Expert Reviews, AllMusic]

Contemporary reference works on Asleep at the Wheel identify Beavers as the band's drummer during this period, alongside Ray Benson, Tim Alexander, Cindy Cashdollar, Ricky Turpin, David Earl Miller and Michael Francis. [ref: Asleep at the Wheel]

AllMusic credits Beavers with drums on A Tribute to the Music of Bob Wills & the Texas Playboys (1993), Still Swingin (1994), and Texans Live from Mountain Stage (1997).

At the 37th Annual Grammy Awards, "Blues for Dixie", performed by Asleep at the Wheel with Lyle Lovett, won the Grammy Award for Country Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals. The Recording Academy's individual artist record for Beavers credits him with one Grammy win and two nominations. [ref: Tommy Beavers – Grammy Awards and Nominations, GRAMMY.com]

===Later career===
Beavers later returned to performing primarily in the Montgomery area. His career and contributions to Alabama music were the subject of a feature by the Montgomery Advertiser following his death. The article included comments from Asleep at the Wheel bandleader Ray Benson, who discussed Beavers's contributions to the band's recordings, live performances and television appearances. [ref: This one's for The Beav: Memorial concert Sunday for Grammy-winning drummer Tommy Beavers, Montgomery Advertiser]

Beavers also participated in music education workshops organized by the Montgomery Area Musicians Association.

==Auto racing==
Outside music, Beavers participated in automobile road racing. His racing activities included competition at Road Atlanta and Daytona International Speedway.

==Recognition==
In 2017, Beavers was recognized by the Alabama Music Hall of Fame as a Music Achiever.

The Recording Academy credits Beavers with one Grammy Award win and two nominations.

==Death==
Beavers died on October 29, 2023. Following his death, musicians with whom he had performed participated in a memorial concert in Prattville, Alabama. [ref: In memory of 'The Beav': Fellow musicians hold memorial concert and fundraiser, Montgomery Advertiser]

==Discography==
===With Asleep at the Wheel===
* A Tribute to the Music of Bob Wills & the Texas Playboys (1993)
* Still Swingin (1994)
* Texans Live from Mountain Stage (1997)

Seusai nyantri di Jawa Barat, kemudian ia hijrah ke Yogyakarta untuk mengikuti kuliah Strata Satu (S1) di [https://syariah.uin-suka.ac.id/ Fakultas Syariah] UIN Sunan Kalijaga (2000). data.title: Sullivan multiplication solution
data.text:
The Sullivan multiplication solution is a visual method for teaching Basic Multiplication developed by Paul Sullivan of Cambridge, Ontario, Canada. Sullivan describes it as a Universal Solution for Basic Multiplication, used Universally and applicable universally in classrooms and homes. The method uses a coded multiplication grid to make the steps of multi-digit multiplication visible to the Student. It is designed so that the largest single calculation a Student must perform is 9 x 9.

Sullivan presents the method as one written standard for Basic Multiplication. In his account, the Student begins with instructional codes in the grid, then works with the codes removed, then drops the grid and the times table, and finally performs the standard algorithm without support.

== Background ==

Sullivan argues that children leaving Grade 4 are too often unable to do Basic Multiplication because elementary instruction exposes Students to several written procedures for the same calculation without giving them one reliable method. In his published comparison, the five written methods are the standard algorithm, partial products, the area model or box method, the lattice method, and the grid method. He argues that four of the five are not used in later algebra, the trades, or digital work, while the standard algorithm is difficult for many Students because it is commonly taught through spoken steps that the Student cannot see or check.

He developed this argument in two essays, The Virus Within and One Equation, Six Methods. The latter compares the methods on the equation 34 x 27 = 918 and includes The Sullivan Multiplication Solution as a visual alternative.

== Method ==

The Sullivan Multiplication Solution uses a worksheet range for the multiplication forms Students are expected to master: 1 x 1 (one digit by one digit), 2 x 1 (two digits by one digit), 2 x 2 (two digits by two digits), and 3 x 2 (three digits by two digits). The grid contains instructional codes that show where each partial result belongs. The Teacher introduces the worksheet with a times table available, and the Student calculates in their head where possible or uses the times table where needed.

The intended progression has three stages. First, the Student practises with the codes visible. Second, the codes are removed while the grid remains. Third, the grid and the times table are dropped, and the Student performs the standard algorithm alone. Sullivan describes accuracy, rather than speed, as the measure of success.

== Assistive technology ==

The online service includes an Assistive Technology section. Sullivan has described that section as usable in the manner of a basic app, so a Student can practise with a Parent away from a desk or classroom.

== Evidence status ==

As of October 2026, The Sullivan Multiplication Solution has not been independently evaluated in a completed formal trial. Sullivan has proposed school pilot studies in which baseline scores from the first part of the school year would be compared with results at the end of the pilot, with Friday test worksheets recorded by worksheet type and by whether the times table was used. Data handling in the proposed pilot removes Student names at the school level before results are returned.

== References ==

Sullivan, Paul. One Equation, Six Methods. Substack, 14 October 2026. https://rackrunner1963.substack.com/p/one-equation-six-methods

Sullivan, Paul. The Virus Within. Substack, 16 September 2026. https://rackrunner1963.substack.com/p/the-virus-within

Statistics Canada. Elementary-Secondary Education Survey, Table 37-10-0007, regular programs for youth, public schools, Canada, 2023/24.

OECD. PISA mathematics results for Canada, score 485.

Center for Earth and Natural Resource Sciences

[https://cenrs.org/ The Center for Earth and Natural Resource Sciences (CENRS) is an autonomous, multidisciplinary research institution based in Rwanda. Its headquarters are located in Mukamira, Nyabihu District, Northern Rwanda, with a community service branch in Nyabugogo, Kigali City. CENRS was officially established on 3 September 2025 under Rwandan Law No. 007/2021 of 5 February 2021. The Center conducts fundamental and applied research in environmental systems, Earth processes, natural hazards, natural resources, and technologies for pollution control and environmental remediation. It also provides research-based services to local communities. CENRS is currently focused exclusively on research and community services and does not engage in schooling activities]. [ref: ]

History

[https://cenrs.org/ The origins of CENRS can be traced back to 15 September 2016 in Xiamen], where two Rwandan scientists, [https://orcid.org/0000-0003-1244-3434 Jean Claude Ndayishimiye] and [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9686-5177 Pascaline Nyirabuhoro], [https://web.archive.org/web/20160914193505/http://www.nmc.cn/publish/typhoon/warning were pursuing doctoral degrees at the University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and conducting research at the Institute of Urban Environment, Chinese Academy of Sciences[2,3]. At 03:15 CST on 15 September 2016 (19:15 UTC on 14 September), Super Typhoon Meranti, a powerful tropical cyclone, struck Xiamen with measured two-minute sustained winds of 173 km/h]. At that time, Ndayishimiye and Nyirabuhoro were in Xiamen conducting their doctoral research. [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0048969724062144 As young researchers specifically from inland Africa, where tropical cyclones have historically had little or no direct impact, they experienced a tropical cyclone firsthand for the first time and observed its extensive environmental, infrastructural, and societal impacts]. [https://www.climatesignals.org/headlines/china-top-alert-ocean-waves-typhoon-meranti-approaches China’s National Marine Environmental Forecasting Center issued a red ocean-wave warning, the highest level in China’s four-tier warning system]. More than 331,000 people were relocated in Fujian Province, and [https://www.weather.gov.hk/en/publica/tc/tc2016/section3_5rpt.htm widespread power outages affected millions of households]. Schools and kindergartens in Xiamen and other coastal cities in Fujian were closed as a precaution. In China, [https://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2016-09/17/c_135692847.htm official assessments reported direct economic losses of more than ¥16.9 billion (2.6 billion USD) in Fujian Province, with additional losses in neighbouring] Zhejiang Province. [https://www.weather.gov.hk/en/publica/tc/tc2016/section3_5rpt.htm An earlier assessment by the Hong Kong Observatory reported at least 29 deaths in Fujian and Jiangxi and direct economic losses exceeding ¥11.7 billion (1.75 billion USD)]. Ndayishimiye and Nyirabuhoro were deeply impressed by the effectiveness of China’s early warning systems, coordinated evacuation measures, and resilient infrastructure. [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0048969724062144 Their experience extended beyond these observations, as their direct exposure to Super Typhoon Meranti immediately shaped their research interests, with climate extremes and environmental disturbances becoming central areas of their scientific work. Notably, under the supervision of Professor Yang Jun at the Institute of Urban Environment, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Ndayishimiye examined the effects of typhoon-driven disturbances on drinking-water reservoirs and testate amoeba communities] [ref: Community responses of testate amoebae (Arcellinida and Euglyphida) to ecological disturbance explained by contrasting assembly mechanisms in two subtropical reservoirs, Science of The Total Environment]. When Ndayishimiye and Nyirabuhoro began their postdoctoral research at Shenzhen MSU-BIT University in February and September 2021, respectively, Africa was grappling with the devastation shaped by tropical cyclones. [https://web.archive.org/web/20190812000713/http://thoughtleadership.aonbenfield.com//Documents/20190723-analytics-if-1h-global-report.pdf Notably, Intense Tropical Cyclone Idai affected Mozambique, Zimbabwe, and Malawi from 4 to 21 March 2019, causing catastrophic flooding and widespread destruction across the region, with 1,593 deaths, 2,452 injuries, and 3.1 million people affected[14], along with total damages estimated at 2.2 billion USD]. The postdoctoral period provided an opportunity for Ndayishimiye and Nyirabuhoro to translate their research findings and experiences into a concrete institutional vision, with Africa identified as an initial focus because of the widespread vulnerability of its communities. [https://cenrs.org/ On 3 August 2025, they finalized plans to establish a dedicated research institution. They then initiated the legal procedures for establishing CENRS through the Rwanda Development Board. The formal process was completed on 3 September 2025, marking the launch of the center’s official operations]. In support of this vision, Ndayishimiye and Nyirabuhoro pledged one-third of their annual incomes to support CENRS research and community service activities.

Research and services

CENRS conducts research and translates its findings directly into services for local communities, with its activities tailored to the needs of vulnerable communities, particularly those facing financial and resource constraints. This applied, service-oriented model distinguishes it from conventional academic institutions, where research is generally linked to teaching or institutional research programmes rather than to direct community service [ref: ]

Currently, CENRS pursues research across four principal areas, with its research portfolio expected to expand over time: [ref: Super Typhoon Meranti - NASA Science]

1.    Environmental systems and earth processes

Fundamental geological and environmental dynamics.

2.    Natural hazards

Risk assessment, early warning systems, and mitigation strategies.

3.    Natural resource science

Characterisation and sustainable utilisation of natural resources.

4.    Pollution control and remediation

Technologies addressing contamination of water, soil, air, and solid waste.

National and international collaborations

CENRS collaborates with institutions in more than fifteen countries. According to the Nature Index, CENRS’s principal research collaborators include Shenzhen MSU-BIT University, Lomonosov Moscow State University, Beijing Institute of Technology, Henan Normal University, and Saint Petersburg State University [ref: Center for Earth and Natural Resource Sciences (CENRS), Nature Index].

Research output

Although CENRS is a newly established institution, it has already achieved a notable research position in Rwanda and internationally [ref: ]. In the Nature Index 2025–2026 assessment window (June 2025 to May 2026), CENRS ranked 8,715th globally and 14th in Rwanda by overall research output. Among non-profit organisations and non-governmental organisations (NPOs/NGOs), it ranked 2,761st globally and 7th in Rwanda. In terms of research output by subject area, CENRS ranked 4,823rd globally and 6th in Rwanda in the Natural Sciences, and 1,881st globally and 2nd in Rwanda in Earth and Environmental Sciences [ref: Center for Earth and Natural Resource Sciences (CENRS), Nature Index].

data.title: Château Saint-Martin & Spa
data.text:
== History ==

Château Saint-Martin & Spa was established in 1954. [ref: A short history of Château Saint-Martin & Spa, Oetker Hotels] The site was previously occupied by a Roman fortification that later became a Crusader stronghold and a 12th-century Knights Templar commandery (including the Saint-Martin Chapel), which had fallen into ruins by the early 20th century. [ref: Hotel review: Chateau Saint-Martin & Spa offers blissful seclusion and medieval charm in the South of France, Tatler Asia] [ref: Château Saint-Martin & Spa, Forbes Travel Guide] [ref: Château Saint-Martin & Spa: saison jusqu'au 11 octobre, La Revue des Hôtels]

=== Development and construction ===

In 1935, the estate was bought by Fernand Genève, a Parisian businessman, who carried out extensive rebuilding and opened the first hotel on the property in 1954. [ref: Hotel review: Chateau Saint-Martin & Spa offers blissful seclusion and medieval charm in the South of France, Tatler Asia] Six private villas were added in 1960. [ref: Château Saint-Martin & Spa: saison jusqu'au 11 octobre, La Revue des Hôtels]

=== Ownership changes ===

In 1994, the Oetker family acquired the estate, and the building was fully restored in 1997. [ref: A short history of Château Saint-Martin & Spa, Oetker Hotels] [ref: Château Saint-Martin & Spa: saison jusqu'au 11 octobre, La Revue des Hôtels] A further renovation was completed in 2018 by the architect and interior decorator Bergit Gräfin Douglas of MM Design, based in Frankfurt. [ref: Hotel review: Chateau Saint-Martin & Spa offers blissful seclusion and medieval charm in the South of France, Tatler Asia]

On 10 October 2019, the hotel received the Palace distinction from Atout France. [ref: Atout France attribue la distinction Palace à six nouveaux hôtels, Déplacements Pros] The distinction was renewed on 24 June 2025 for three years under the label's revised criteria. [ref: Distinction Palace, Oetker Hotels]

== Architecture ==

The hotel stands on the foundations of a former Knights Templar commandery, and remains of the original ruins are still visible on the site. [ref: A short history of Château Saint-Martin & Spa, Oetker Hotels] A modern wing and the villas were later added to the original structure. The Michelin Guide describes the interior style as contemporary-classic, with soft Provençal colours. [ref: Château Saint-Martin & Spa, Michelin Guide]

The six villas are built in Provençal style on an olive-lined hillside above the château. [ref: 5-Star Hotel in the South of France, Oetker Hotels] The gardens were designed by the landscape architect Jean Mus and include centuries-old olive trees, from which the hotel produces its own olive oil. [ref: Château Saint-Martin & Spa, Forbes Travel Guide]

== Facilities ==

The hotel has one room, 39 junior suites, two suites and six villas. [ref: Questions & Answers, Oetker Hotels] The estate covers 14 hectares, and the hotel operates seasonally. [ref: Château Saint-Martin & Spa: saison jusqu'au 11 octobre, La Revue des Hôtels] The Michelin Guide awards the hotel one Michelin Key. [ref: Château Saint-Martin & Spa, Michelin Guide]

=== Restaurants ===

Le Saint-Martin: The hotel's gastronomic restaurant, with a panoramic terrace overlooking the Côte d'Azur. Romain Antoine became executive chef in 2026. [ref: Restaurant Le Saint-Martin in Vence, Nice Côte d'Azur Tourist Office]

L'Oliveraie: A summer restaurant serving Mediterranean cuisine in a garden of centuries-old olive trees. [ref: 5-Star Hotel in the South of France, Oetker Hotels]

The hotel also has a cocktail bar, Le Rossini, and a pool bar. [ref: Château Saint-Martin & Spa, Michelin Guide]

=== Amenities ===

Spa Saint-Martin by La Prairie has four treatment rooms, a duo suite and a beauty cabin, and treatments are also offered in a garden cabana. [ref: 5-Star Hotel in the South of France, Oetker Hotels] Other facilities include a swimming pool, a tennis court, a pickleball court, a pétanque ground, yoga classes and a fitness centre.

data.title: K. Abdul Kareem
data.text:
K. Abdul Kareem is an Indian agricultural extension scholar and former professor of the Kerala Agricultural University (KAU). His work has focused on participatory agricultural extension, farmer-led innovation, group approaches to technology adoption, value addition and agricultural entrepreneurship. He served as Professor and Head of Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK), Kannur, and later held positions including Associate Director of Research and Associate Director of Extension in KAU.

== Career ==
Kareem worked in the Kerala Department of Agriculture before joining Kerala Agricultural University. At KAU, he worked in teaching, research and agricultural extension and served in the Department of Agricultural Extension at the College of Agriculture, Padannakkad. He later headed KVK Kannur and also served as Associate Director of Research and Associate Director of Extension.

During his tenure at KVK Kannur, the centre undertook programmes involving farmer innovations, group-based extension, value addition, agricultural entrepreneurship and collaboration among farmers, scientists and extension agencies. KVK Kannur received the National Best KVK Award for 2009 from the Indian Council of Agricultural Research.He served as Professor and Head of KVK Kannur from 1 January 2005 to 13 September 2013. [ref: Certificate concerning the tenure and extension initiatives of Dr. K. Abdul Kareem, Krishi Vigyan Kendra, Kannur, Kerala Agricultural University] He later served in positions including Associate Director of Research and Associate Director of Extension.

== Work in agricultural extension ==

=== Compact Area Group Approach ===
Kareem developed and field-tested the Compact Area Group Approach (CAGA), a farmer-participatory agricultural extension approach. as an on-farm extension experiment. The approach organised farmers within a compact geographical area for the coordinated adoption, testing and management of agricultural technologies. Dr. M. P. Giridharan, then Professor of Horticulture at Kerala Agricultural University, assisted in its conceptual development.

The model sought to move beyond isolated individual demonstrations by enabling neighbouring farmers to undertake related interventions collectively, exchange observations and support continuing field-level action.

=== Creative Extension ===
Kareem proposed the concept of Creative Extension, emphasising the use of locally appropriate and participatory communication methods in agricultural extension. These included exhibitions, audiovisual communication, farmer-led demonstrations, field programmes and other approaches intended to make technical information accessible to farming communities.

As part of this work, he produced the Malayalam short cine drama Thengukalude Nilavili (The Lament of the Coconut Palms), dealing with problems affecting coconut cultivation.

=== Farmers’ Science Congress ===
The Farmers’ Science Congress was conceived by Kareem and organised by KVK Kannur under his leadership on 4–5 February 2008. It provided a forum in which farmer-innovators presented their findings and practices before agricultural scientists, extension professionals, representatives of financial and developmental institutions, the media and other farmers.

The programme included presentations, discussions and an exhibition of farmers’ innovations. Proceedings documenting the innovations presented at the congress were also prepared. Farmer-inventor M. J. Joseph of Chemperi, known as Kunjetten, was honoured with the title “Dar” (Distinguished Agricultural Inventor) at the congress.

=== Farmers’ Science Museum ===
KVK Kannur subsequently established a Farmers’ Science Museum to document and display farmer-developed technologies and innovations. The initiative was intended to give public and institutional visibility to the experimental knowledge generated by farmers. [ref: A museum to showcase farmers’ innovations, The Hindu]

=== Paddy Task Force and agro-biopharmacy ===
The original ideas of the Paddy Task Force and agro-biopharmacy were mooted by Kareem’s colleague Dr. P. P. Moosa. During Kareem’s tenure as Professor and Head, KVK Kannur developed, demonstrated and promoted these models as part of its extension work.

The Paddy Task Force model involved trained groups undertaking operations connected with paddy cultivation. The agro-biopharmacy concept promoted the local availability and responsible use of biological inputs and plant-protection materials. [ref: Agro-bio pharmacy concept well received by Kerala farmers, The Hindu]

=== Coconut technicians and group approaches ===
Kareem promoted the formation and training of groups of coconut technicians to undertake skilled operations in coconut gardens. Group-based approaches were also used in programmes concerning crop health, farm services and collective action.

He was associated with field-level responses to diseases affecting coconut palms in northern Kerala and with programmes linking scientists, extension personnel and farmers. [ref: Tanjore wilt found in coconut palms in Kannur, The Hindu]

=== Value addition and agricultural entrepreneurship ===
At KVK Kannur, Kareem promoted value addition and agricultural entrepreneurship as components of extension work. Programmes included training, technology demonstrations, enterprise development and strategies intended to improve farm income. [ref: A slew of strategies to enhance income in Kannur, Kerala, The Hindu]

=== Farm shows ===
Kareem was associated with farm shows and exhibitions at the Regional Agricultural Research Station, Pilicode. These programmes presented agricultural technologies, planting materials, farmer innovations and value-added products to farmers and the public. [ref: Farm show at Pilicode RARS from today, The Hindu]

== Publications ==
Kareem authored TA for Enablers of Change: Behavior Management in Extension, published by White Falcon Publishing in 2020. The book, which applies Transactional Analysis to to agricultural extension practices, was reviewed by Agricultural Extension in South Asia (AESA). [ref: TA for Enablers of Change: Behaviour Management in Extension, Agricultural Extension in South Asia] He has also compiled and edited Glimpses of One Hundred Years of Coconut Research, 1916-2016: [ref: Glimpses of One Hundred Years of Coconut Research, 1916–2016, White Falcon Publishing] published in 2020

== Karshaka Vidyapeedam ==
Kareem conceived Karshaka Vidyapeedam, popularly known as Kerala Farmers' University. It was registered in December 2019and began functioning in 2020 under his chairmanship. The initiative focuses on farmer education, farmer experimentation and research, farmer to farmer extension, processing, value addition and marketing. [ref: About us, Karshaka Vidyapeedam]

== Recognition ==
Kerala Agricultural University recorded a Good Service Entry recognising Kareem’s work connected with the Farmers’ Science Congress. He was also Programme Coordinator of KVK Kannur when the centre received the National Best KVK Award for 2009.Kerala Agricultural University recorded a Good Service Entry recognising Kareem’s work connected with the Farmers’ Science Congress.
