data.title: Ronen Taieb
data.text:
Ronen Taieb is an Israeli entrepreneur and business executive, the founder and owner of Integrity Cyber, a company operating in cybersecurity, information security, cyber risk management, data privacy, corporate governance, and cyber incident preparedness for organizations in Israel and international markets.

Taieb has more than a decade of professional experience in risk management, information security, and strategic consulting, alongside involvement in business and technological activities with complex organizations, financial institutions, commercial companies, and public-sector entities.

== Professional expertise ==

Taieb's professional approach to information security connects technological risks, business implications, executive responsibility, and regulatory requirements.

His areas of professional activity include:

* Cybersecurity Governance: Cybersecurity strategy, risk management, corporate governance, and CISO services.
* Incident Response and Cyber Resilience: Cyber incident preparedness, incident response, crisis management, and organizational resilience.
* Security Operations: Security Operations Center (SOC) services, threat detection, vulnerability management, and security assessments.
* Data Protection and Privacy: Data Protection Officer (DPO) services, personal data protection, privacy regulation, and compliance.
* AI and Cybersecurity Innovation: Entrepreneurship and the development of artificial intelligence-based solutions for detecting, investigating, and responding to cyber incidents.
* Business Strategy and International Partnerships: Business development, strategic partnerships, and expansion into international markets.

In July 2017, Taieb published a professional article through the Israeli Directors Union examining cybersecurity threats, organizational preparedness, and the responsibilities of corporate management and boards of directors in addressing cyber risks. [ref: מאמרו של רונן טייב למידעון 07/2017, Israeli Directors Union]

== Leadership and entrepreneurship ==

As the founder of Integrity Cyber, Taieb works to develop an end-to-end cybersecurity services framework combining professional expertise, established methodologies, and advanced security technologies.

His management philosophy emphasizes professional accountability, performance measurement, the reduction of business exposure, and the creation of tangible value for clients.

Taieb served as chairman of Integrity Consulting and Risk Management in 2015. [ref: זירות המסחר היזהרו, המחוקק בדרך, Calcalist]

By 2018, he was serving as president of Integrity Consulting and Risk Management. In May of that year, he was included in the program of a professional conference organized by Bar-Ilan University's Chair in Israeli Corporate Governance, addressing cybersecurity risks and the role of corporate boards. [ref: External Directors Club Conference on Cyber Risks and the Role of Board of Directors, Bar-Ilan University]

Alongside his activities in cybersecurity services, Taieb is involved in technological entrepreneurship in information security and artificial intelligence, including the activities of the separate product company AiCY and its AIIR solutions.

== International activities ==

Taieb promotes business relationships and strategic partnerships in cybersecurity and technology across international markets, including Europe, Latin America, and the United States.

These activities focus on expanding access to cybersecurity services, developing international cooperation, and creating business models combining managed services with innovative technologies.

== Religious and community activities ==

Alongside his business activities, Rabbi Ronen Taieb is involved in Torah education, delivering religious lessons, and community activities.

He is active in the religious community of Modi'in, including at the Nitzotz HaKedusha synagogue, combining business activities, community leadership, and efforts to strengthen Torah study.

== Professional publications and appearances ==

Taieb has published professional articles addressing risk management, financial regulation, cybersecurity, and corporate governance.

In May 2015, he co-authored an article with Inga Eisenberg in Calcalist concerning the regulation of financial trading platforms in Israel.

In July 2017, he published an article through the Israeli Directors Union addressing organizational preparedness for cyberattacks and the implications for corporate management.

In May 2018, he was included in the program of a conference at Bar-Ilan University concerning cybersecurity risks and corporate board responsibilities.

data.title: Synopsys VCS
data.text:
Synopsys Verilog Compiler Simulator (VCS) [ref: EE 382N: VCS Manual, users.ece.utexas.edu] is a proprietary functional verification and Verilog simulator [ref: ] maintained by Synopsys. It also has integration with a GUI based waveform viewer called Synopsys Verdi [ref: Higher Productivity with Integrated MATLAB and Synopsys VCS Verification Workflows, in.mathworks.com], which superseded VirSim.
[[File:Synopsys-verdi-21mux.png|alt=Synopsys Verdi displaying a two-to-one multiplexer.|thumb|Synopsys Verdi displaying a two-to-one mux written in Verilog with its test waveform generated after simulating.]]

== History ==

VCS was developed by John Sanguinetti as part of Chronologic Simulation in 1992. Created from the ground up, VCS was developed by four people. Sun Microsystems gave the team a model called the "tsunami model", which, after 13 months of development on VCS, did not run. After ironing out the bugs, VCS was able to run the model successfully. Because of this, Sun Microsystems formed a contract with the team, promising an extra $480,000 of funding in three stages. [ref: [https://archive.computerhistory.org/resources/access/text/2015/06/102702042-05-01-acc.pdf Oral History of John Sanguinetti]. Computer History Museum. 26 February 2009.]

In November 1992, VCS was formally announced at the Tech Museum in San Jose. In January of 1993, the company received a $400,000 check from Cyrix, which allowed the company to further work on VCS.

Chronologic Simulation was acquired by ViewLogic in 1994 for $26.5mn, though there were complications with lawsuits until 1995 [ref: Chronologic Simulation, Inc. v. Sanguinetti, 892 F. Supp. 318 (D. Mass. 1995), Justia Law]. In 1997, ViewLogic as bought out by Synopsys for $500mn [ref: SYNOPSYS ACQUIRES VIEWLOGIC FOR $500M - Tech Monitor, Tech Monitor].

data.title: Skura Style
data.text:
== Skura Style ==
Skura Style is an American company that sells kitchen cleaning products. Founded in 2017 by Linda Sawyer and Alison Matz, the company initially focused on kitchen sponges and later expanded its product range to include scouring pads, microfiber cloths, and kitchen towels. [ref: Two Rockland Natives Rethink The Kitchen Sponge, Daily Voice]

=== History ===
Skura Style was founded by Linda Sawyer, a former advertising executive, and Alison Matz, a media and publishing executive. The company launched in October 2017 with a kitchen sponge as its first product. Sawyer's previous career included serving as CEO and Chairman of the advertising agency Deutsch, while Matz spent the majority of her career as a media executive, serving as Publisher at Condé Nast and Meredith. Independent trade publication Digiday covered the founders' transition from advertising and publishing to consumer products in January 2018. [ref: Life After Advertising: From Deutsch CEO to cleaning supplies startup founder, Digiday]

In May 2022, actress Eva Mendes acquired an ownership stake in the company and became a co-owner and brand ambassador. Her involvement included collaboration on product design and marketing. The partnership subsequently expanded to include a collection of kitchen cleaning products associated with Mendes. [ref: Eva Mendes comes clean, Forbes Australia]

=== Products ===
The company's product range includes kitchen sponges, scouring pads, microfiber cleaning cloths, Swedish dishcloths, and cotton kitchen towels.

Its Skrubby Sponge incorporates a printed pattern that fades with use, providing a visual indication of when the sponge may need replacing. The product is also treated with an antimicrobial agent, according to descriptions of the product published by the company and media outlets.

Other products include Very Skrubby, a double-sided scouring pad; Wipe Envy, a microfiber cleaning cloth; and Towel Ta-Da, a cotton kitchen towel. The company has also released products in collaboration with Eva Mendes. [ref: Allow Eva Mendes to Explain Why She’s Bubbly Over Sponges These Days, Architectural Digest]

data.title: Framework for Responsible use of AI in Monitoring and Evaluation
data.text:
Assessment in the era of artificial intelligence

In the modern era of artificial intelligence (AI), evaluation means both using AI tools in evaluation and evaluating programmes, services or systems that use AI. Artificial intelligence can help with tasks such as sorting large datasets, analysing text and summarising documents. Its use also raises issues around the quality of evidence, bias, privacy, transparency and accountability. [ref: Artificial intelligence and big data-driven evaluation research and practices: A systematic literature review, Evaluation] Applications Machine-learning and artificial intelligence techniques have been used to analyse large data sets and detect trends in text and other information. Generative artificial intelligence can also assist with tasks at various stages of evaluation, including design, data structuring, analysis and reporting. Case studies of these applications and shifts in evaluation methods and practitioner skills are presented in the edited volume From Algorithms to Evidence: Using GenAI in Evaluation Practice. [ref: From Algorithms to Evidence: Using GenAI in Evaluation Practice, Routledge]

Methodological and ethical considerations: AI-assisted analysis may allow evaluators to work with more information or to perform some tasks more quickly. Outputs still need to be checked for accuracy, validity and relevance to the evaluation questions. A systematic review of the use of AI and big data in evaluation found unresolved methodological, ethical and data-ownership issues and recommended the combination of these tools with traditional approaches. [1] Researchers have also explored the possible effects of AI use on evaluation standards such as rigour, utility, fairness and independence. [ref: Sage Journals: Discover world-class research, Sage Journals] Responsible use guidelines on responsible AI use in evaluation typically encompass oversight by humans, transparency, sensitive data, and representation of different perspectives. In 2025, the United Nations Evaluation Group published ethical principles for the use of AI in United Nations evaluations. [ref: ]

The [https://www.taylorfrancis.com/chapters/oa-edit/10.4324/9781003799139-33/frame-valentine-joseph-gandhi-kerry-bruce-steffen-bohni-nielsen?context=ubx&refId=eb11a85b-b358-4419-8ad1-0dc1e02d21a9 FRAME] framework (Framework for Responsible AI in Monitoring and Evaluation) offers guidance across seven phases of evaluation. It sets out five principles: accountability architecture; stakeholder engagement; epistemic integrity; transparency; and proportionality. The framework emphasises human responsibility for decisions and provides a checklist to record the use of AI in evaluation activities. [ref: ]]AI System Evaluation The evaluation of an AI system is a related but different task from the use of AI to perform an evaluation. It is about evaluating the system’s performance and effects in context. Evaluation researchers have also suggested criteria for thinking about how AI is used in evaluation practice and what its use leads to. [ref: Evaluation criteria for artificial intelligence, New Directions for Evaluation]

data.title: Liz Tripodi
data.text:
Liz Tripodi is an Australian vocal coach, music educator, songwriter, podcast host and surrogacy advocate. She founded the Melbourne-based music school Vocal Art Studios and has worked in music education, performance and entertainment. She later became involved in international surrogacy advocacy following her experience of having children through surrogacy in Georgia. [ref: Georgia's surrogacy clinics attract hundreds of Australians but ethical questions remain, ABC News]

== Music career ==

Tripodi founded Vocal Art Studios in Melbourne in 2003. Australian Business Register records show Vocal Art Studios operating as a trading name from May 2003. [ref: Historical details for ABN 15 429 044 569, Australian Business Register]

Her work as Founder and Director from 2003-2023 through Vocal Art Studios included vocal coaching, music education, performance training and involvement in the Melbourne music and entertainment industry as well as work in America and Europe.

Tripodi has also worked as a mc, speaker, performer, adjudicator and judge at music competitions and eisteddfods. She has been heavily involved in Italian-Australian musical and cultural events, including festival and community performances as well as in Canada, America and Italy.

The Moonee Valley Foundation lists Tripodi among its past recipients, describing her as an "Italian musical producer". [ref: Past Winners, Moonee Valley Foundation]

== Songwriting ==

Tripodi has also worked as a songwriter. In 2019, her song Family placed ninth in the Folk/Acoustic category of the Australian Songwriting Contest. [ref: 2019 Top 10 List, Australian Songwriters Association]

The placing was also published in the December 2019 edition of The Australian Songwriter, the magazine of the Australian Songwriters Association. [ref: 2019 Australian Songwriting Contest Top 10, The Australian Songwriter]

== Awards and recognition ==

Tripodi was an individual recipient in the Service Delivery to Multicultural Victoria category of the Victorian Multicultural Commission's Multicultural Awards for Excellence. [ref: Annual Report 2008–09, Victorian Multicultural Commission]

In 2017, she received the Women's Small Business Champion award at the Northern Multicultural Small Business Awards for her work with Vocal Art Studios. [ref: Northern Multicultural Small Business Awards winners announced, Brotherhood of St Laurence]

Tripodi was also listed as a Westfield Airport West Local Heroes nominee in 2018. [ref: Recognising all of our 2018 Nominees, Westfield Local Heroes]

== Media and broadcasting ==

Tripodi has appeared in Australian media in connection with her work in music, business and surrogacy. Her media work has also included music broadcasting and interviews.

She has been featured in reporting concerning Italian-Australian cultural activities and has participated in radio and entertainment programs.

== Surrogacy advocacy ==

Tripodi and her husband experienced infertility for approximately 13 years before pursuing surrogacy in Georgia. Their twin daughters were born in Georgia through a surrogate.

ABC News reported in 2025 that Tripodi subsequently started a podcast about surrogacy in Georgia and became involved in supporting others considering international surrogacy.

The Georgian Surrogacy Podcast, hosted by Tripodi, began in 2022 and discusses international surrogacy, particularly surrogacy in Georgia. [ref: The Georgian Surrogacy, Great Australian Pods]

Tripodi has also participated in Australian surrogacy events. Growing Families has identified her as an Australian representative of Chachava Clinic in Georgia. [ref: Sydney Surrogacy and Donor Event, Growing Families]

She has contributed to public discussion concerning surrogacy regulation, including making a submission to the Australian Law Reform Commission. [ref: Submission – Liz Tripodi, Australian Law Reform Commission]

data.title: TakeMe2Space
data.text:
TakeMe2Space is a space company based in Hyderabad, India. It develops satellite payloads and subsystems and offers remote access to computing hardware on its spacecraft, so users can run software in orbit, including AI inference on imagery. The company plans to build an orbital data centre.

The company flew its first experiment, RSEM, aboard ISRO's PSLV-C58 on 1 January 2024. In November 2024, it announced MOI-TD, an AI payload, which was launched on PSLV-C60 on 30 December 2024. Its first satellite, MOI-1, was aboard PSLV-C62 on 12 January 2026; the rocket failed during ascent, and all 16 satellites on board, including MOI-1, were lost. A replacement, MOI-1a, was launched on 1 October 2026 aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9.

== History ==

Ronak Kumar Samantray co-founded NowFloats, a software firm acquired by Reliance in 2019. When he turned to space technology, he found there was no satellite to rent, so he decided to build one. He conceived the idea in 2022, and in June 2023, he and three friends started TakeMe2Space in Hyderabad.

To extend the lifespan of satellite electronics, the company tested a tantalum coating as a low-cost radiation shield. The experiment, the Radiation Shielding Experimental Module (RSEM), flew on 1 January 2024 on PSLV-C58, mounted on POEM-3, the rocket's fourth stage used as an orbital platform.

The company announced its first mission, MOI-TD (My Orbital Infrastructure – Technology Demonstrator), in November 2024. It was launched on 30 December 2024 from Sriharikota. MOI-TD carried an onboard computer and an AI accelerator to test AI inference, sensor fusion, and high-speed data handling in low Earth orbit. This allowed users to upload AI models that could run on the payload through a web-based console called OrbitLab. Uses included environmental monitoring and tracking deforestation, among others. Samantray told ThePrint that his goal was to make space accessible to any researcher, student, educator, or start-up that wanted to be part of it. Its first research partners were a Malaysian university and a group of Class 9 and 10 students from an Indian school. The founder said a Class 9 student was among the company's first customers.

Chiratae Ventures led a seed round in which TakeMe2Space raised US$5 million in January 2026. The company said it would use the money to expand its constellation to six spacecraft and to scale real-time AI inferencing in orbit. It also said it planned to build an orbital data centre in Telangana.

=== PSLV-C62 and MOI-1 ===

MOI-1 was a 14 kg CubeSat developed by TakeMe2Space. It gave developers and organisations the opportunity to run AI workloads in space without needing to own or operate a satellite, and the company said the mission would demonstrate an AI-powered orbital image laboratory. Integrated with MOI-1 was MIRA, an electro-optical Earth-observation payload built by EON Space Labs, with an optical system carved from a single block of fused silica; it weighed 502 g and supported multispectral imaging across nine bands. The PSLV-C62, carrying Anvesha, a DRDO-designed Earth observation satellite, was to launch from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.

A flight-ready CubeSat payload built by 17 students aged 12 to 15 at Blue Blocks Montessori School was also on the launch. The payload included real-time telemetry and commercial off-the-shelf sensors to study thermal behaviour in space, transmitting raw data on temperature, humidity and other weather parameters from an altitude of 450 km. Scientists from TakeMe2Space guided them, and the students executed the plan.

PSLV-C62 was launched on 12 January 2026 at 10:17 am IST and encountered a failure during ascent due to an anomaly in the rocket's third stage. MOI-1 was lost, along with all 16 satellites on the mission.

After the loss of MOI-1, the company booked the earliest available launch slot with SpaceX. The replacement, MOI-1a, was launched on 1 October 2026 aboard SpaceX's Transporter-18 mission. The satellite allows customers to collect Earth observation data and process it in space. It weighs 14 kg, has 117 TOPS of onboard computing and 2 TB of storage, and has a nine-band multispectral imager. At launch, MOI-1a had 23 customers. ThePrint reported it as the first of five planned satellites, and the company described the mission as a step towards building an orbital data centre in space.

== Technology and products ==

OrbitLab, the company's web-based platform, was used by customers to rent satellite processing time. Initial reports put the price at $2 (₹180) per minute.

TakeMe2Space also produces PowerBank-50, a satellite battery pack designed to power a satellite while it passes through Earth's shadow. Weighing 380 g and storing around 50 Wh, it was onboard Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-1 first flight, Mission "Aagaman", launched on 18 July 2026, powering an experimental payload from Cosmoserve Space at approximately 450 km altitude. Samantray said the battery was "now space proven, made in India, and ready for every satellite builder in the world".

data.title: Luxcara
data.text:
Luxcara is an investment management company based in Hamburg, Germany. It manages investments in European energy infrastructure for institutional investors, including wind and solar power and hydrogen production. [ref: Hamburger Asset Manager übernimmt Anlagevermittler, Private Banking Magazin] It also invests in battery storage projects. [ref: Consortium kicks off 1.8GWh 'Battery Park' development in Germany, Energy-Storage.news] In 2024, its project company Waterekke Energy secured a 1.5 GW offshore wind concession in the German North Sea. [ref: RWE, Luxcara Winners of German 5.5 GW Offshore Wind Tender, OffshoreWIND.biz]

== Background and fund management ==

Alexandra von Bernstorff and Kathrin Oechtering established Luxcara in 2009. The business is owned by its management. Bernstorff, Marc Brehm and Philip Sander are its managing partners. [ref: The Team, Luxcara]

Flaveo I, one of Luxcara's early funds, closed in April 2010. [ref: Luxcara: Institution Profile, Infrastructure Investor] Its Luxembourg-based Flaveo S.A., SICAV-FIS fund held a solar power plant in France in 2012. [ref: Luxcara acquires 12MW PV plant in Aquitaine, France, PV Tech]

The company's funds receive capital from institutional investors, including insurance companies and pension funds. In 2023, the pension fund for Siemens employees in Switzerland committed capital to Luxcara's Flaveo IV Green Energy fund as part of its allocation to infrastructure. [ref: Swiss Siemens Pensionskasse commits to infrastructure via Aquila, Luxcara, Partners Group, IPE Real Assets] In 2024, the insurer Gothaer provided capital to a Luxcara fund, following a €150 million commitment made in 2022. [ref: Gothaer beteiligt sich an Luxcara-Fonds, dpn] [ref: Gothaer investiert in Offshore-Windpark und Wasserstoff-Projekt, Private Banking Magazin] In August 2024, Luxcara acquired Convexity, a Berlin financial services company authorised to provide investment brokerage, investment advice and asset management. The acquisition received approval from Germany's Federal Financial Supervisory Authority.

== Wind and solar investments ==

In May 2018, Facebook entered into a power purchase agreement with Luxcara for electricity from the Bjerkreim wind farm cluster in south-western Norway. The three projects covered by the agreement had a combined design capacity of 294 MW. Vattenfall contracted to provide electricity balancing and integration services. [ref: Facebook buys Norwegian wind power, Windpower Monthly] In 2019, Luxcara and MEAG arranged project bonds for two of the cluster's wind farms, Skinansfjellet and Gravdal. Investors in the bonds included Munich Re group companies and Uniqa Insurance Group, while a Luxcara fund provided equity financing. [ref: Munich Re and Luxcara create bond to finance Norwegian wind farms, IPE Real Assets]

Luxcara acquired the Guillena-Salteras solar project north of Seville, Spain, on behalf of institutional investors in January 2019. [ref: Greencoat, Sonnedix and Luxcara each expand solar portfolio via acquisition, IPE Real Assets] In April that year, it bought the Önusberget wind project in Sweden from Svevind for an undisclosed sum. [ref: Luxcara expands Scandinavian portfolio with Swedish wind farm project deal, IPE Real Assets] The wind farm forms part of the Markbygden wind power area near Piteå and has a capacity of 753 MW. [ref: Vindkraft vid Markbygden pressas av miljardförluster, ENERGInyheter.se] [ref: Windpower Intelligence Global Forecast: October 2023, Windpower Monthly]

Its German offshore investments include Waterkant and Waterekke. In August 2024, the Federal Network Agency awarded the N-9.3 North Sea site, with a capacity of 1.5 GW, to Luxcara.

== Waterkant turbine procurement ==

Waterkant is a 300 MW offshore wind development. [ref: Asset manager Luxcara shies away from using Chinese offshore wind turbines, Riviera Maritime Media] Its site lies approximately 90 km from the island of Borkum. [ref: Subventionierte China-Windräder vor Borkum geplant, Tagesschau]

In July 2024, Luxcara selected Ming Yang Smart Energy as the preferred turbine supplier for Waterkant. The agreement covered 16 turbines rated at up to 18.5 MW each. Germany's economy ministry announced that it would examine the implications for critical infrastructure and competition. The industry association WindEurope also criticised the agreement. [ref: Germany to examine security, competition impact of Chinese wind turbine deal, Reuters]

In August 2025, Luxcara entered a capacity into a reservation agreement with Siemens Gamesa for 97 turbines rated at 15.5 MW each for Waterekke. It also reserved 19 turbines of the same type for Waterkant. It attributed the possible supplier change to operational efficiencies between the projects and told Reuters that political debate had not been decisive. Ming Yang confirmed that it was no longer involved in Waterkant. [ref: German company is set to scrap politically sensitive Chinese turbine deal, Reuters]

== Hydrogen and battery storage ==

Luxcara holds a 74.9% interest in the Hamburg Green Hydrogen Hub, a joint venture with the municipal utility Hamburger Energiewerke. The venture is building a 100 MW electrolyser at the former Moorburg power station in Hamburg. The foundation stone was laid in December 2025. [ref: Grundsteinlegung in Moorburg: Hamburg setzt auf Wasserstoff, Logistik Heute] The European Commission classified the development as an Important Project of Common European Interest (IPCEI) in February 2024. Federal and Hamburg state funding was approved later that year. [ref: Hamburg Green Hydrogen Hub bestellt 100-Megawatt-Elektrolyseur bei Siemens Energy, pv magazine Deutschland]

In June 2025, Luxcara acquired a stake in a battery storage development in Waltrop, North Rhine-Westphalia. The development is a consortium project with BKW and the municipal utility group Trianel. The first development phase has a design capacity of 900 MW and 1,800 MWh of storage, with 520 MW allocated to Luxcara. The site was originally reserved for Trianel's Lünen coal-fired power station, which was built nearby instead. Construction began in September 2026, with a groundbreaking ceremony on 21 September. [ref: Stadtwerke starten Bau eines 900-MW-Batterieparks, Energie Informationsdienst]

In February 2026, Luxcara bought the Tuisku battery storage project near Keminmaa, Finland, from the developer Pohjan Voima. The purchase price was not disclosed. [ref: Luxcara acquires 125MW Finnish battery storage project from Pohjan Voima, IPE Real Assets]

data.title: Andrea Monath Schumacher
data.text:
Andrea Monath Schumacher is an American interior designer and author. She is the founder of Andrea Schumacher Interiors, an interior design firm established in Denver, Colorado, in 1999. Her work is known for its use of color, pattern, antiques and globally influenced decorative arts. Schumacher has been featured in publications including Galerie, House Beautiful and 1stDibs, and was selected as a designer for the 50th Kips Bay Decorator Show House New York in 2025. [ref: Meet the Kips Bay Designer: Andrea Schumacher, Galerie Magazine]

=== Early life and education ===
Schumacher grew up in several locations in the United States and abroad, including Nigeria. Her father worked as a virologist for the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and Schumacher has cited her childhood travel as an influence on her approach to interior design. She earned a bachelor's degree in interior design from Colorado State University and later studied universal design at the Harvard Graduate School of Design. [ref: Fashion and Travel Inspire This Former TV Set Designer’s Gutsy Interiors, 1stDibs Introspective]

=== Career ===
Schumacher began her career working in television set design in Los Angeles, including work associated with the NBC daytime series Days of Our Lives. She later returned to Colorado and established Andrea Schumacher Interiors in 1999. [ref: The Houzz Blog]

Her residential interiors have been characterized by layered combinations of color, pattern, vintage furnishings and objects collected through travel. Schumacher operates from Denver and Santa Barbara and has completed residential and hospitality projects in multiple regions of the United States. [ref: Meet Interior Designer Andrea Schumacher, Home & Garden Colorado]

In 2025, Schumacher participated in the 50th annual Kips Bay Decorator Show House New York, where she designed a guest apartment, kitchen and bathroom. [ref: Meet the Kips Bay Designer: Andrea Schumacher, Galerie Magazine]

=== Publications ===
Schumacher is the author of Vibrant Interiors: Living Large at Home, published by Gibbs Smith. The book received a Colorado Book Award in the pictorial category. [ref: Meet Interior Designer Andrea Schumacher, Home & Garden Colorado]

data.title: Haitham Al-Jadaani
data.text:
Haitham bin Shunayf bin Raddad Al-Jadaani (; 1979 – 22 April 2011) was a Saudi Quran reciter, imam, and khatib from Jeddah. He was known for his murattal recitation in the Hafs 'an Asim narration and for holding ijazahs in a number of Quranic readings. [ref: هيثم بن شنيف الجدعاني, midad.com] [ref: الترجمة الشخصية للشيخ هيثم بن شنيف الجدعاني, ar.islamway.net]

== Biography ==
Al-Jadaani was born in Jeddah on 8 Rajab 1399 AH (1979). He completed his primary, intermediate, and secondary education in the city, then studied at the Qassim branch of Imam Mohammad Ibn Saud Islamic University, graduating from it. [ref: القارئ الشيخ هيثم الجدعاني رحمه الله, haithamaljadani.com] He married twice and had five children.

== Education and ijazahs ==
He began memorising the Quran in the Quranic study circles of Jeddah as a child under Sheikh Muhammad Bafil and a group of students of knowledge, until he was granted an ijazah in it. He then travelled to the Qassim region in pursuit of knowledge, where he attended the lessons of Sheikh Muhammad ibn Salih al-Uthaymeen, and after al-Uthaymeen's death he continued studying with his students.

He travelled outside Saudi Arabia to receive the Quran from those proficient in its narrations, obtaining ijazahs in several readings, including Hafs 'an Asim, Shu'bah 'an Asim, Al-Bazzi and Qunbul from Ibn Kathir, and Qalun from Nafi'.

== Career ==
He served as imam and khatib of Noor Al-Rahman Mosque in the Al-Salamah district of Jeddah until his death. He was already listed among the well-known reciters of Jeddah several years before his death. [ref: المساجد التي سيؤم بها قراء العالم الإسلامي هذا العام, mazameer.com]

== Recitations ==
Al-Jadaani recorded the complete murattal Quran in the Hafs 'an Asim narration, and also recorded recitations in the Al-Bazzi 'an Ibn Kathir narration as well as recordings of the tarawih and tahajjud prayers. [ref: مصاحف هيثم بن شنيف الجدعاني, midad.com] His recitations remain available on a number of Quran audio platforms and download archives. [ref: تلاوات القارئ هيثم الجدعاني, audio.islamweb.net] [ref: هيثم بن شنيف الجدعاني: تلاوات القرآن الكريم بصوته, ar.assabile.com] [ref: القارئ هيثم الجدعاني, tahaquran.com]

== Death ==
On Friday 22 April 2011, Al-Jadaani drowned in the sea near the shore of Dhahban, north of Jeddah, during a family outing on a boat. When his nine-year-old nephew Abdulaziz fell from the boat, his father Abdulrahim and his uncle Haitham entered the water to rescue him; the boat's captain succeeded in saving the child, but the two brothers drowned. [ref: وفاة الشيخ هيثم الجدعاني إمام وخطيب جامع نور الرحمن بجدة, dd-sunnah.net]

The funeral prayer was offered for the two brothers after the Fajr prayer on Saturday 23 April 2011 at Al-Thunayan Mosque in Jeddah, and they were buried in the Dhahban cemetery.

== Legacy ==
After his death, Saudi Arabia's Quran Radio broadcast selections of his recitations, and his recordings continued to circulate among listeners. Several Quran audio platforms have kept his complete murattal recitation available for streaming and download.

data.title: Wes Parker (Musician)
data.text:
----

Wes Parker is an American musician and songwriter from Richmond, Virginia. He wrote and performed with the indie rock band Camp Howard and recorded with his brother Jonathan Parker as the duo Ruth Good before releasing solo music under his own name in 2024. His solo releases include the EPs Splinter (2025) and fantom (2025), and the album Super Rare (2026). Parker also creates online comedy sketches featuring a recurring character named Skunk. [ref: From Band Life to Big Dreams: Wes Parker's Solo Journey, RVA Magazine] [ref: The many faces of Wes Parker, VPM] [ref: Yes, Wes Parker Can Feel Something Shifting Too, Zany Waves]

== Early life ==
Parker grew up in Richmond in a musical family. His father and older brothers played guitar, and Parker began learning the instrument as a child. He later played in a middle school band with Nicholás Perea, who would become his bandmate in Camp Howard. Parker has described a one-chord composition called "The Salamander Song" as his first song.

== Career ==
=== Camp Howard ===
Parker and Perea became songwriters in Camp Howard, a Richmond indie rock band that began performing in 2015. The group also included Matt Benson and Brian Larson. Parker played guitar and bass and contributed vocals. [ref: RVA #29: From house shows to Egghunt Records, a look at the rise of Camp Howard, RVA Magazine]

Camp Howard released a self-titled album in 2016 and the Juice EP through Egghunt Records in 2017. A live session recorded for Audiotree was released in 2018, followed by the band's second studio album, Cañón, in 2019. Camp Howard toured outside Richmond and reunited for a performance in 2023. [ref: Camp Howard - Audiotree Live, Bandcamp] [ref: Early Listen: Richmond's Camp Howard Unveils "Cañón", POND Magazine]

=== Ruth Good ===
Parker and his brother Jonathan, known as JP, formed the Richmond duo Ruth Good. Their seven-track Spliff EP was released through Citrus City Records in 2017. The brothers largely wrote and recorded their respective contributions separately, while their brother Alan played additional instruments on two tracks. All three brothers also played in the Richmond band Poser. [ref: Brothers from Richmond's Ruth Good Discuss Debut EP 'Spliff' Ahead of Smatter Show Tonight, RVA Magazine]

=== Solo recordings ===
Parker began releasing singles under his own name in 2024, including "Why Won't You Pick Up the Phone?", "Annie Moore", "Burn the House", "Tattoo" and "Den". He played every instrument on the recording of "Annie Moore". [ref: New Single "Den" By Wes Parker, Social Casualty] Reviewing "Den" for Social Casualty, Claire Johnson discussed its country-influenced guitar melody and changes in tempo.

His first solo EP, Splinter, was released in January 2025. Writing for The Auricular, a Richmond music publication, the reviewer connected Parker's earlier work with Camp Howard to Splinter, describing the EP's melodic pop-rock songwriting and retro-influenced arrangements. [ref: RVA Shows You Must See This Week: July 16 – July 22, The Auricular] RVA Magazine's "Sound Check!" column described Splinter as blending alternative country with indie rock, contrasting the title track's energetic sound with the country-influenced "Deadbolt". [ref: Sound Check! Wes Parker, Rubblebucket, Sweet Bahs, RVA Magazine] Parker followed it with fantom in October 2025. He described fantom as a fictional narrative inspired by the fall of Lucifer. [ref: Freedom and Fallen Angels: Journey into the World of Wes Parker's 'fantom', Atwood Magazine] In a review of the EP, Rachel Leong of Atwood Magazine discussed its alternative rock and early-2000s influences and the narrative connecting its songs. [ref: The Rise and Fall of an Angel: Wes Parker's EP 'fantom' & Defiant Artistry, Atwood Magazine] Leo Edworthy of EARMILK described the fantom single "Neck" as combining grunge influences, indie rock and falsetto vocals. [ref: Wes Parker tunes up his grunge sensibilities on "Neck", EARMILK] "Neck" appeared on filmmaker James Gunn's Spotify playlist of favorite songs from 2025, which he shared on Threads. [ref: Just a few of my favorite songs from 2025, Threads] [ref: James Gunn's favorite songs of 2025, Spotify]

Parker released his debut solo album, Super Rare, on June 5, 2026, through Big Machine Rock. It includes "Little Birdie", "Bad Doggie" and "Cut the Grass", the last of which features Jessica Lea Mayfield. [ref: New Music Mondays: Evanescence, Red Clay Strays and More!, Overtone] Overtone rated the album seven out of ten, discussing its mix of indie rock, folk and country and its radio-show framing.

In 2026, Parker placed second in the singer-songwriter category of Style Weekly Readers' Winners poll. [ref: Readers' Winners: Arts + Culture, Style Weekly]

=== Live performances ===
In 2025, Parker toured as a solo artist, including a 16-stop run noted by Flagpole ahead of a show in Athens, Georgia. [ref: Calendar Pick: Wes Parker, Flagpole] Parker also performed an in-studio set for WNRN's 2025 Holiday Showcase, playing original songs and a cover of "Last Christmas". The station published video and audio recordings of the session. [ref: 2025 WNRN Holiday Showcase, WNRN]

In May 2026, Parker and his band performed before a live audience at the DC101 Sound Stage in Rockville, Maryland. The appearance also included an interview with radio host Mike Jones. [ref: Wes Parker - DC101 Artist Session, DC101] [ref: INTERVIEW: Mike Jones Talks With Wes Parker!, ALT 107.3]

In 2026, he opened for Liz Cooper on West Coast dates, played a headlining tour on the East Coast and supported Shakey Graves for several shows. Reviewing a Shakey Graves concert at the Coronado Theatre in Rockford, Illinois, Music Scene Media described Parker's opening performance as a three-piece set drawing from his EPs and Super Rare. [ref: A Foot-Stomping Evening With Shakey Graves and Wes Parker, Music Scene Media]

Parker performed at the All Things Go Music Festival at Merriweather Post Pavilion in Columbia, Maryland, on September 27, 2026. [ref: All Things Go Music Festival: Sunday, Merriweather Post Pavilion] [ref: Photos: All Things Go DC Set Times Announced for Hayley Williams, Mitski, Brandi Carlile, BroadwayWorld] The festival shared a [https://www.facebook.com/allthingsgomusic/videos/4441262686095060/ video clip of his performance]. [ref: Wes Parker performance clip, Facebook]

=== Comedy and video work ===
Parker has created short online comedy sketches, including sketches featuring his recurring character Skunk. He developed the character after taking a virtual sketch-writing class. Parker and his band have also performed for the music video series Jam in the Van. [ref: Wes Parker, Jam in the Van] Parker appeared twice on The 8-Bit Show, in segments covering Splinter and Super Rare. [ref: The 8-Bit Show: Wes Parker, YouTube] [ref: The 8-Bit Show: Wes Parker, YouTube]

Parker has also released music videos for several solo songs. Colin Earner directed the videos for "Tattoo", "Splinter" and "fantom".

== Discography ==
=== Solo releases ===

* Splinter (EP, 2025)
* fantom (EP, 2025)
* Super Rare (album, 2026)

=== With Camp Howard ===

* Camp Howard (album, 2016)
* Juice (EP, 2017)
* Camp Howard - Audiotree Live (live session, 2018)
* Cañón (album, 2019)

=== With Ruth Good ===

* Spliff (EP, 2017)

Fátima Lianes (born 6 August 1977) is a Spanish film director. Her work has been broadcast by Al Jazeera English, Movistar Plus+, and HBO Max. Her credits include The Iraqi 8 [ref: ‘Los 8 de Irak’, un documental reconstruye la mayor tragedia del servicio secreto español casi 20 años después, El País] for Movistar Plus+ and Battle of Culiacán: Heirs of the Cartel for HBO MAX [ref: La Jornada: Culiacanazo: Herederos del narco narra el antes y después de la seguridad en México, www.jornada.com.mx].

Lianes has worked primarily in observational documentary filmmaking. Her productions have used interviews and on location footage rather than narrator led exposition, with participants’ accounts forming a central part of the narrative. data.title: Mindbreeze Overview 10192026
data.text:
----

Mindbreeze GmbH is an Austrian enterprise software company that develops enterprise search, knowledge management and artificial intelligence software. It was founded in Linz in 2005 by Daniel Fallmann and Jakob Praher. [ref: [https://www.mindbreeze.com/management "Management". Mindbreeze. Accessed 7 October 2026.]] [ref: [https://kompany.ie/p/at/262155y "Mindbreeze GmbH, FN 262155y". Austrian commercial register extract via kompany. Accessed 7 October 2026.]] The company operates in Austria and the United States. [ref: [https://www.mindbreeze.com/company "Company". Mindbreeze. Accessed 7 October 2026.]] It is majority-owned by the Austrian software company Fabasoft AG. [ref: [https://at.cloud.fabasoft.com/folio/public/0s5n1dd48kq2w2vz00fbpdjvw3/download "Fabasoft AG has increased its stake in Mindbreeze GmbH". Fabasoft AG, 20 April 2021.]]

== History ==

Mindbreeze was entered in the Austrian commercial register as a limited liability company (GmbH) on 13 April 2005. Its early software was marketed under the Fabasoft name, including Fabasoft Mindbreeze Enterprise, which searched information across corporate file systems, email and document management systems. [ref: [https://www.kmworld.com/Articles/Editorial/Features/Trend-Setting-Products-of-2010Fabasoft-and-FTI-Technology-69607.aspx "Trend-Setting Products of 2010: Fabasoft and FTI Technology". KMWorld, 2010.]]

Mindbreeze subsequently developed Mindbreeze InSpire, initially offered as enterprise search software preinstalled on dedicated hardware. The company later expanded its offerings to cloud and hybrid deployment. In May 2024, InSpire became available through Google Cloud Marketplace. [ref: [https://www.destinationcrm.com/Articles/CRM-News/CRM-Across-the-Wire/Mindbreeze-InSpire-Available-on-Google-Cloud-Marketplace-164213.aspx "Mindbreeze InSpire Available on Google Cloud Marketplace". Destination CRM, 24 May 2024.]]

In April 2021, Fabasoft increased its ownership interest in Mindbreeze from 76% to 85.5%. In a May 2026 article, Diginomica reported that Mindbreeze worked directly with approximately 2,000 large companies, with partners serving smaller customers. [ref: [https://diginomica.com/cast-setting-sail-enterprise-scale-ai-mindbreeze Ring, Katy. "Cast off! Setting sail for enterprise scale AI with Mindbreeze". Diginomica, 13 May 2026.]]

In 2024 the company introduced Mindbreeze Insight Workplace, a product built on its enterprise search technology. In August 2025, the company added multimodal large-language-model capabilities to InSpire, including processing of audio, video and image content. [ref: [https://www.destinationcrm.com/Articles/CRM-News/CRM-Across-the-Wire/Mindbreeze-Adds-Multimodal-LLM-Integration-to-InSpire-170822.aspx "Mindbreeze Adds Multimodal LLM Integration to InSpire". Destination CRM, 5 August 2025.]] [ref: [https://www.kmworld.com/Articles/News/News/Mindbreeze-adds-multimodal-LLM-integration-to-refine-enterprise-data-intelligence-171064.aspx Simone, Stephanie. "Mindbreeze adds multimodal LLM integration to refine enterprise data intelligence". KMWorld, 19 August 2025.]]

== Products ==

=== Mindbreeze InSpire ===

Mindbreeze InSpire is enterprise search and information-retrieval software designed to index structured and unstructured information from multiple business systems. The software supports search and question answering across connected sources and can be deployed on premises or through cloud infrastructure. Its newer functions use retrieval-augmented generation and multimodal large language models.

=== Mindbreeze Insight Workplace ===

Mindbreeze Insight Workplace is a software interface built on InSpire for accessing enterprise information and configuring AI-assisted workflows. Diginomica reported that its Insight Touchpoints can be configured by subject-matter experts through an Insight App Designer and that the software records information about user requests and responses.

== GenAI Confidence Index ==

Mindbreeze publishes a survey series called the GenAI Confidence Index, which examines business attitudes toward generative AI. In February 2026, Crowdfund Insider reported on findings from the company's survey, including differences in confidence between executive and implementation-focused roles. [ref: [https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2026/02/264243-genai-focus-narrowing-mindbreeze-survey/ Zerucha, Tony. "GenAI Focus Narrowing: Mindbreeze Survey". Crowdfund Insider, 27 February 2026.]]

== Industry recognition ==

Mindbreeze appeared in KMWorld’s AI 100 lists in 2023, 2025 and 2026. [ref: [https://kmworld.com/Articles/Editorial/Features/The-KMWorld-AI-100-The-Companies-Empowering-Intelligent-Knowledge-Management-158690.aspx Ojala, Marydee. "The KMWorld AI 100: The Companies Empowering Intelligent Knowledge Management". KMWorld, 12 July 2023.]] [ref: [https://www.kmworld.com/Articles/Editorial/Features/2025-The-KMWorld-AI-100-The-Companies-Empowering-Intelligent-Knowledge-Management-169468.aspx Ojala, Marydee. "2025 The KMWorld AI 100: The Companies Empowering Intelligent Knowledge Management". KMWorld, 7 July 2025.]] [ref: [https://www.kmworld.com/Articles/Editorial/Features/2026-The-KMWorld-AI-100-The-Impact-of-AI-on-KM-is-Inescapable-174988.aspx Ojala, Marydee. "2026 The KMWorld AI 100: The Impact of AI on KM is Inescapable". KMWorld, 6 July 2026.]] InSpire was also included in the publication's 2024 Trend-Setting Products list. [ref: [https://kmworld.com/Articles/Editorial/Features/KMWorld-Trend-Setting-Products-of-2024-165019.aspx Ojala, Marydee. "KMWorld Trend-Setting Products of 2024". KMWorld, 9 September 2024.]]

Angry Birds Slingshot Stories is a Finnish computer-animated 3D web series based on the Angry Birds franchise created by Rovio Entertainment. The short-form series is produced in collaboration with Indian animation studio Cosmos-Maya. [ref: Rovio Teams with Cosmos-Maya for 'Angry Birds Slingshot Stories', Animation Magazine]

== Premise ==
The series focuses on short, non-verbal slapstick scenarios involving the Birds and the Pigs. Set behind the scenes of the games, episodes explore comedic hypothetical situations between the characters on Piggy Island. [ref: Rovio and Cosmos-Maya Partner on 'Angry Birds Slingshot Stories', Animation Xpress]

== Production and release ==
The first season premiered on YouTube on May 9, 2020. Subsequent seasons were released, with the third season launching in October 2023 and the fourth season debuting in May 2025. [ref: Angry Birds Slingshot Stories, IMDb]

data.title: Cut the Rope: Magic
data.text:
Cut the Rope: Magic is a puzzle video game developed and published by ZeptoLab. The fifth main installment of the Cut the Rope franchise, the game's plot involves Om Nom travelling inside a magical book after a spider wizard inside the book steals his candy supply.

== Gameplay ==
Like other titles in the franchise, the game's goal is to cut ropes in order to feed candy to Om Nom. A new feature in this game allows Om Nom to transform into different creatures, each with their own unique abilities, in order to solve certain puzzles. [ref: Zeptolab Goes Back To The Well With Cut The Rope: Magic, Now Available For Free In The Play Store, Android Police] In some levels, the player must face off against the spider wizard, who will forcefully attempt to bring the candy to his direction; the player will lose the level if the wizard eats the candy. [ref: Cut the Rope: Magic Review, Trusted Reviews]

== Development and Release ==
In October 2015, five years after the release of the first Cut the Rope game, ZeptoLab announced a brand new game for the franchise entitled Cut the Rope: Magic, which was slated for a December release, although few details of the game were given at the time. [ref: Om Nom is back, and still hungry: New ‘Cut the Rope’ set for December, GeekWire] [ref: Cut the Rope: Magic swinging into Android devices this December, Android Authority] The game was later released on December 17, introducing six different transformations for Om Nom, including a bird form, a baby form, a fish form, a mouse form, a ghost form, and a dragon form. The game was free for Android, while the iOS version costed $1.

== Reception ==
According to the review aggregation website Metacritic, the game has received "generally positive reviews" from critics. [ref: Cut the Rope: Magic Reviews - Metacritic, www.metacritic.com] Nadia Oxford of Gamezebo in particular praised the game for its graphics and blending of old and new mechanics. [ref: Cut the Rope: Magic Review - My Magical Om Nom, Gamezebo] Michael Crider of Android Police positively compared the game's addition of magical transformations to that of the Super Mario franchise and, while noting the game's use of in-app purchases and advertisements, stated that the core gameplay would make these flaws easy to ignore.

== References ==

data.title: Achyuth GS
data.text:
Achyuth GS (also known as Achyuth Gudla) [ref: Achyuth GS – Movies, Reviews, and Filmography, The Review Monk] is an Indian actor, theatre artist, filmmaker, and line producer who works primarily in Telugu cinema and theatre. He portrayed Venkat and served as the line producer for the independent drama film Sanjeev (2026). [ref: Sanjeev Movie 2026: Review, Cast, Trailer, Posters, Watch Online at Aha, The Times of India]

== Early life ==

Achyuth GS was born on 10 November 1999 in Rayaparthy, located in the Warangal district of Telangana, India.

== Career ==

=== Theatre ===

Achyuth began his acting career in Hyderabad theatre, working with the Creative Theatre group. In October 2021, he performed in the stage production Asamardhudu, written by Mercy Margaret and directed by Ajay Makenapalli, which was staged at Ravindra Bharathi. [ref: "అసమర్థుడు" నాటక ప్రదర్శన -]

=== Film ===

In 2024, Achyuth appeared as Allrounder Achyuth in Bandi Saroj Kumar's Telugu feature film Parakramam.

In 2026, he co-starred as Venkat in the independent Telugu drama film Sanjeev, directed by Anil Nakka, starring alongside Hareesh Palakurthi and Laya Miryala. [ref: Sanjeev Movie Review: సంజీవ్ సినిమా రివ్యూ.. కల కోసం పోరాడే యువకుడి కథ.. ప్రతి కుర్రాడి మనసును తాకే మూవీ, [[TV9 (Telugu)] Achyuth also served as the film's line producer under Team APPAH. [ref: హీరో కావాలంటే ఇన్ని అవమానాలా? ఒక్క అవకాశం కోసం జీవితాన్నే పణంగా పెట్టిన యువకుడి కథ, BIG TV] The film's promotional roll-out received regional media attention, [ref: సంజీవ్ మూవీ ఫస్ట్ లుక్ పోస్టర్ విడుదల.. సినిమా ప్రత్యేకత ఏంటంటే?, BIG TV] [ref: సంజీవ్ ఫస్ట్ లుక్ పోస్టర్ విడుదల, Nava Telangana] including coverage of its official trailer [ref: Sanjeev – Official Trailer, The Times of India] and a soundtrack single launched by filmmaker Sailesh Kolanu. [ref: ‘సంజీవ్’ నుంచి ఎమోషనల్ మెలోడీ ‘కలలకే’.. మూడో సింగిల్‌ను విడుదల చేసిన శైలేష్ కొలను, [[TV9 (Telugu)] The film was subsequently released for digital streaming on Aha on 21 August 2026. [ref: నాలుగు రోజుల్లోనే షూటింగ్... 7 నేషనల్ అవార్డ్స్ – ఆహాలో 'సంజీవ్' స్ట్రీమింగ్, ABP Live Telugu] [ref: Sanjeev OTT Release: 4 రోజుల్లో సినిమా.. ఏడు అవార్డులు.. ఓటీటీలోకి వస్తున్న ‘సంజీవ్’, NTV Telugu]

== List of ferns of West Virginia==
The term "Ferns" is here used in the historical sense and includes Ferns, Spikemosses, Clubmosses, and Quillworts.

This checklist was compiled from the following sources: WVU Herbarium, SERNEC, iNaturalist, USDA Plants and PteridoPortal records. For the most part, the nomenclature used in this list follows that in "Ferns, Spikemosses, Clubmosses, and Quillworts of Eastern North America" by Emily Sessa.

West Virginia's diverse geology and forest types, along with elevations ranging from 274 to 4,863 feet, supports a rich fern flora of 22 Families, 46 Genera and 109 Taxa.
Amongst West Virginia's ferns are the ubiquitous Christmas Fern (Polystichum acrostichoides) and the very rare Alternate-leaved Spleenwort ([https://castaneajournal.com/article/first-records-of-alternate-leaved-spleenwort-asplenium-%E2%9C%95alternifolium-in-the-new-world/ Asplenium ×alternifolium]).

Although this list is specific to West Virginia, the majority of the species can be found throughout the Central Appalachian Mountains.

* Pellaea glabella subsp. glabella — Smooth Cliff Brake

data.title: World Youth Choir
data.text:
The World Youth Choir (WYC) is an international youth choir. The choir was created in 1989. it is a project choir reformed through auditions each year, consisting of singers aged between 17 and 26 from up to 75 different countries.

The choir is organised by the WYC Foundation [ref: Stichting World Youth Choir, KVK], based in Amsterdam, which is a cooperation between Jeunesses Musicales International, the International Federation for Choral Music, and since 2002 Europa Cantat [ref: World Youth Choir, World Youth Choir], which merged into the European Choral Association.

In 1996, the World Youth Choir was names UNESCO Artist for Peace [ref: UNESCO Artists for Peace, portal.unesco.org]. The choir performed at a number of notable events, including twice at the Olympic Games (Summer 1992, 2008) and the Nobel Peace Prize Ceremony (2011) [ref: Video - The 2011 Nobel Peace Prize Award Ceremony, NobelPrize.org].

data.title: Team, Inc.
data.text:
----

Team, Inc. (stylized in all caps) is a global industrial services company with its headquarters located in Sugar Land, Texas. Founded in 1973, the company provides specialty maintenance, inspection, and mechanical integrity services to facilities in the refining, petrochemical, power generation, and manufacturing sectors. The company's common stock is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol TISI.

== History ==
The company was founded in 1973 as an industrial maintenance services contractor primarily for petrochemical plants along the Texas Gulf Coast.

The company went public on the Nasdaq exchange in 1995, and moved its listing to the New York Stock Exchange in 2001, under the ticker symbol TISI.

In the 2000s and 2010s, TEAM, Inc. extended its geographic footprint and technical capabilities by acquiring regional inspection and specialty service providers. In February 2016, the Company acquired Furmanite Corporation, a leading competitor in specialized on-site industrial services and leak sealing, in an all-stock transaction.

The company had operational reorganization programs in the early 2020s to consolidate service lines and deal with debt from major transactions. In December 2022, the company completed a 1-for-10 reverse stock split to stay in compliance with exchange listing rules.

== Operations and services ==
TEAM, Inc. is a provider of asset integrity, inspection, maintenance and repair, and rope access services for industrial facilities and equipment. The company provides six core areas of service, including inspection, detection, repair, heat treating, digital services via OneInsight, and advanced asset and project solutions. [ref: Industrial Asset Integrity Services, TEAM, Inc.]

=== Inspection ===
TEAM performs traditional and advanced non-destructive testing, tank inspections and valve testing. It also possesses inspection capabilities, including robotics and drones, computed and digital radiography, laser inspection, infrared thermography, 3D imaging, and data collection to assess the state of industrial equipment and structures.Inspection and Testing (NDT/NDE), TEAM, Inc.

=== Detection ===
Detection services are designed to find and quantify leaks and emissions. These include: leak detection and repair (LDAR) programs, greenhouse gas measurement and control, methane emission reduction, and optical gas imaging. These services support emissions monitoring, repair coordination and environmental compliance reporting. [ref: Detection and Emissions Reduction, TEAM, Inc.]

=== Repair ===
TEAM offers specialty mechanical repair services including leak sealing on operating equipment, hot tapping and line stops, field machining, controlled bolting, valve repair and insertion, welding services and engineered composite repairs. It also provides vapor barrier and hydrostatic weld testing.On-Stream Mechanical Repair & Online Leak Sealing Services, TEAM, Inc.

=== Heat treating ===
Services include pre and post weld heat treatment, dehydrogenation, solution annealing, normalizing and curing of coatings and refractory materials. TEAM also provides equipment for thawing, expansion heating, temperature monitoring and mobile heat treatment.Heat Treating, TEAM, Inc.

=== OneInsight ===
OneInsight is TEAM’s digital platform for the collection, management and reporting of information associated with inspection, maintenance and repair activities. Its tools support field service management, remote monitoring, asset integrity records, repair documentation and turnaround co-ordination. The platform also includes dashboards, audit logs and mobile reporting.
OneInsight, TEAM, Inc.

=== Advanced asset and project solutions ===
TEAM provides industrial project support for maintenance, fabrication, shutdowns and asset integrity management Services include IRATA certified rope access for inspection & repair in hard to reach areas, custom component manufacturing, turnaround planning & execution and engineered line lifts to provide access to pipes and supports. Asset-integrity management services aid in risk assessment and maintenance planning. [ref: Industrial Project Support Services, TEAM, Inc.]

== Corporate affairs ==
Team, Inc. operates service locations across the United States, Canada, Europe, and Latin America. The company is governed by a board of directors and executive management led by Chief Executive Officer Gary L. Hill. As a publicly traded entity, it files annual (10-K) and quarterly (10-Q) reports with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

data.title: LVCRFT
data.text:
LVCRFT (pronounced "Lovecraft") is an American Halloween music group formed in Los Angeles in 2019 by songwriter Evan Bogart, songwriter and producer Amanda "MNDR" Warner, and producer Peter Wade. The group has released an album of Halloween-themed songs each year since its debut, This Is Halloween Vol. 1 (2019), and had written more than 100 Halloween songs by 2024. Its song "Skeleton Sam" was featured in the Disney+ film Hocus Pocus 2 (2022).

==History==
===Formation and early albums (2019–2021)===
LVCRFT was founded by Bogart, Warner and Wade, pop songwriters and producers whose credits include songs for Beyoncé, Rihanna, Charli XCX, Mark Ronson and Kylie Minogue. Members perform under pseudonyms, including "Lil Punkin" (Bogart), "DeepKutz" (Warner) and "Norman Crates" (Wade). Warner told Nylon that the group began in reaction to the same small set of classic Halloween songs being played every October.

The group's debut album, This Is Halloween Vol. 1, was released in 2019. Its second album, The Sequel (2020), contained 15 original songs and featured guest vocalists including Uffie, Bonnie McKee and Sarah Hudson, each credited under a horror-themed alias. Its lead single, a version of "Spooky Scary Skeletons", was used as the theme for Freeform's 31 Nights of Halloween programming block. The group's third album, The Return, followed in 2021, led by the single "Every Night". The song's music video, the group's first, was filmed inside a Spirit Halloween store.

===Hocus Pocus 2 and Scream Warriors (2022)===
"Skeleton Sam", sung by Sarah Barrios, is the first song heard in the present-day portion of Hocus Pocus 2 (2022). According to Luminate data reported by The New York Times, the song's U.S. streams nearly doubled between October 2022 and October 2023, and it had reached 14.3 million U.S. streams by October 2024. Later in 2022 the group released Scream Warriors, a 15-track album made in collaboration with film composer Christopher Young. Nylon described the album as darker and more immersive than the group's earlier work.

===V and Under the Covers (2023–2024)===
The group's fifth album, V, was released in 2023 and followed a "found audio" storyline about the character Skeleton Sam. In 2024 LVCRFT released Under the Covers, an album of Halloween-themed cover versions, preceded by the single "Halloween Hop" featuring actor David Dastmalchian.

===Skeleton Sam's Deadtime Stories (2026)===
The group's eighth album, Skeleton Sam's Deadtime Stories, was released on October 1, 2026, on the group's Spooky Never Sleeps label. Structured as a late-night horror broadcast with skits and fictional film trailers, it is hosted by Roger L. Jackson and features Robert Englund, Heather Langenkamp, Mick Garris, Robert Rodriguez, Bruce Campbell, Ernie Hudson, John Kassir, Jasmin Savoy Brown, Katharine Isabelle and Alyssa Sutherland, among others. A music video for "My Boo", featuring Brown, was released alongside the album. The group said an anthology series based on the album is in development.

==Other work==
LVCRFT's music has been used in Chilling Adventures of Sabrina, Hubie Halloween, Flack and Chucky. On October 31, 2023, Charity Lawson and Artem Chigvintsev performed a jive to "Skeleton Sam" on the "Monster Night" episode of Dancing with the Stars. The group scores mazes and live entertainment for the Queen Mary's Dark Harbor, and writes music for the LA Haunted Hayride. The group also creates ambient loops and custom scores for haunted attractions under the name Nightmare Soundworks.
The members also formed Spooky Never Sleeps, a company that serves as the group's record label and produces scores and immersive experiences; Bogart told The New York Times that the group hoped it would become a musical counterpart to the horror studio Blumhouse.

data.title: Jacques Cory
data.text:
----

Jacques Cory (Hebrew: יעקב קורי; born 1944) is an Israeli businessman, author, and lecturer on business ethics and corporate social responsibility. His publications address corporate governance and the protection of minority shareholders. He also helped initiate and edit a Ladino translation of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. [ref: משוגעים, תרדו, Globes] [ref: Jacques Cory, Magnes Press] [ref: Deklarasion Universal de Derechos Umanos, El Amaneser]

== Early life and education ==

Cory was born in Cairo, Egypt, in 1944 and moved to Israel as a child. He studied economics and political science at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and earned an MBA at INSEAD in France. [ref: About Jacques Cory, Business Ethics Cory]

In 2004, he completed a doctorate in management sciences at the Conservatoire national des arts et métiers (CNAM) in Paris, supervised by Yvon Pesqueux. His thesis, L’éthique des affaires et les actionnaires minoritaires, examined business ethics and the protection of minority shareholders. It was based on his two books published by Kluwer Academic Publishers in 2001. [ref: L’éthique des affaires et les actionnaires minoritaires, Theses.fr]

== Business and academic career ==

Cory worked at Elbit for fourteen years and held senior positions in the high technology industry. From 1987, he worked independently in international mergers and acquisitions.

He lectured at the University of Haifa on business ethics, corporate social responsibility, sustainability, globalization, and business administration. A contributor biography published in Sephardic Horizons also records teaching at INSEAD in 2006, the Technion in 2009–2010, and Tel Aviv University in 2010–2011. A 2013 notice from the University of Haifa’s junior academic staff organization identifies him as a teaching fellow. [ref: Komo deskuvri la sinagoga de Coria, Sephardic Horizons] [ref: University of Haifa junior academic staff newsletter, University of Haifa junior academic staff organization]

== Research and writing ==

In Business Ethics: The Ethical Revolution of Minority Shareholders, Cory examines the limitations of conventional safeguards for minority investors, including regulation, corporate boards, auditors, and financial intermediaries. He argues for greater transparency, investor associations, and ethical investment funds as additional means of protecting shareholders. The book includes case studies involving companies in France, Israel, and the United States. [ref: Business Ethics: The Ethical Revolution of Minority Shareholders, Springer Nature]

Reviewing Business Ethics in Transparency International Germany’s newsletter, Irene Wiegand praised its detailed case evidence and use of literature, while questioning its novelty and its analysis of ethical investment funds. [ref: Jacques Cory: Business Ethics. The Ethical Revolution of Minority Shareholders, Rundbrief]

His second book, Activist Business Ethics, develops an approach based on cooperation among businesspeople, academics, stakeholders, and minority shareholders to address unethical corporate conduct. [ref: Activist Business Ethics, Springer Nature]

His Hebrew book Selected Issues in Business Ethics and Social Responsibility was published by Magnes Press in 2008. It combines theoretical discussion and business cases with analyses of literary works, plays, and films. Its subjects include whistleblowing, corporate governance, corruption, environmental responsibility, and ethical questions in Israeli business. [ref: סוגיות נבחרות באתיקה עסקית ובאחריות חברתית, Magnes Press]

In a 2008 Globes discussion of business education, Cory advocated including integrity assessments in admissions to MBA programs. He proposed using simulations, case discussions, and role playing to examine applicants’ responses to conflicts between ethics and profitability. [ref: תסננו אותם, Globes]

In 2012, Cory and Eran Vigoda-Gadot contributed a chapter on the public responsibility of government and public administration to Public Responsibility in Israel, edited by Raphael Cohen-Almagor, Ori Arbel-Ganz, and Asa Kasher. [ref: Public Responsibility in Israel, Kotar]

== Literature and Ladino ==

Cory’s literary works include the play Nelly’s Choice, written with Amalia Eyal, and the Hebrew novel הישמרו מדורון יווני [Beware of Greeks’ Presents], published by Bimat Kedem in 2001. The novel concerns a businessman navigating a corrupt business environment. Cory has also published an essay in Ladino in Sephardic Horizons. [ref: הישמרו מדורון יווני, Bimat Kedem]

In 2011, Cory initiated a Ladinokomunita project to translate the Universal Declaration of Human Rights into Ladino. According to project participant Rachel Amado Bortnick, he and Bortnick co-edited the contributors’ translations, and Cory liaised with United Nations officials about submission. Her account was published in El Amaneser and on eSefarad. A Ladino translation is listed in the United Nations Regional Information Centre’s guide to translations of the Declaration. [ref: Deklarasion Universal de Derechos Umanos – en ladino, eSefarad] [ref: The Declaration in your language, United Nations Regional Information Centre]

== Recognition and personal life ==

In October 2015, News1 reported that Cory had been selected to receive Ometz’s Exemplar Decoration (עיטור מופת), among the organization’s awards recognizing contributions to its campaign against public corruption. [ref: אותות אומץ 2015 יוענקו לכמה אישים, News1]

Cory is married to Ruthy and has three children.

== Selected publications ==

* Business Ethics: The Ethical Revolution of Minority Shareholders. Kluwer Academic Publishers, 2001.
* Activist Business Ethics. Kluwer Academic Publishers, 2001.
* הישמרו מדורון יווני [Beware of Greeks’ Presents]. Bimat Kedem, 2001. Hebrew novel.
* סוגיות נבחרות באתיקה עסקית ובאחריות חברתית [Selected Issues in Business Ethics and Social Responsibility]. Magnes Press, 2008. Hebrew.

== References ==

data.title: Andrew Forde
data.text:
Dr. Andrew Nathaniel Forde (born January 21, 1987) is a Canadian engineer, artificial intelligence researcher, management consultant, and violinist. He is a partner at KPMG and, since March 2026, the firm's inaugural head of AI research, a national role the firm described as the first of its kind in Canada's professional services industry.

Dr. Forde began his career as a materials scientist at NASA's Langley Research Center and later held roles at Boston Consulting Group, Deloitte, CGI, and IBM Consulting before joining KPMG in 2023. He is also an adjunct professor in the Faculty of Applied Science and Engineering at the University of Toronto, and testified before the Senate of Canada in 2026 as an expert witness on artificial intelligence.

Trained on the violin from early childhood, Dr. Forde has performed for United States presidents Bill Clinton and George W. Bush and has shared stages with Sting, Justin Bieber, Mary J. Blige, and Pitbull. His 2018 multimedia work Ideas of North, a reinterpretation of Glenn Gould's radio documentary The Idea of North, premiered to a sold-out audience at Koerner Hall in Toronto. He serves on the board of directors of the Tafelmusik Baroque Orchestra.

== Early life and education ==
Dr. Forde was born and raised in Toronto, Ontario, to a Jamaican mother and a Bajan father, and has credited his Caribbean family foundation with shaping his path toward higher education. He holds Canadian and Bajan citizenship. He was introduced to the violin at age three after watching an orchestral performance, and received his first instrument at age four.

He earned a Bachelor of Applied Science in materials science and engineering from the University of Toronto in 2011, and completed a PhD in industrial engineering and machine learning at the same institution in 2020 under the supervision of Mark S. Fox. His doctoral thesis, An Ontological Framework & Data Driven Approach for Measuring Radicalness, developed an innovation ontology for classifying radical and incremental innovation and for selecting ideas in the front end of innovation management. Fox, a Professor Emeritus of Industrial Engineering at Toronto and one of the first researchers to apply artificial intelligence to industrial systems, was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada in 2026. In 2014 Dr. Forde received a fellowship award from Mitacs (Mathematics of Information Technology and Complex Systems). While a graduate student, he was also chief executive of Sommerlink Solutions, a big-data consulting firm.

== Career ==

=== NASA and consulting ===
Dr. Forde began his professional career as a materials scientist conducting research at NASA's Langley Research Center. He subsequently worked as an associate at Boston Consulting Group, as global innovation lead for strategic modelling and analytics at Deloitte, and as a managing director at CGI, before becoming an associate partner in the data, AI, and technology transformation practice at IBM Consulting.

=== KPMG ===
Dr. Forde joined KPMG in 2023 as a partner in the firm's technology strategy and digital transformation practice, with a focus on digital healthcare, enterprise AI strategy, and large-scale transformation for clients across government, energy and utilities, healthcare, telecommunications, and financial services.

On March 24, 2026, KPMG Canada announced Dr. Forde's appointment as its first head of AI research, a newly established national role that the firm described as the first of its kind in Canada's professional services industry. The mandate focuses on bridging the gap between Canadian AI research and commercialization, building relationships with universities and research labs, and serving as the firm's leading voice on AI research and policy. Announcing the role, Dr. Forde argued that Canada helped pioneer modern AI research but has too often seen its breakthroughs commercialized elsewhere.

In April 2026, Dr. Forde appeared as an expert witness before the Standing Senate Committee on Transport and Communications, testifying on the opportunities and challenges of artificial intelligence in the information and communications technology sector. He has contributed to policy submissions to the Government of Canada on AI transparency, sovereign compute, and national AI strategy.

Dr. Forde is a frequent commentator on artificial intelligence in Canadian media. The Logic profiled him in May 2026 as KPMG's "AI whisperer", and in the Financial Post he has discussed the economics of enterprise AI token consumption and the competitive significance of Moonshot AI's open-weight Kimi K3 model. He has also spoken on AI trust and governance in The Logic and in an interview with Circuit Cellar at Web Summit Vancouver.

=== Academic work ===
Dr. Forde is an adjunct professor in the Faculty of Applied Science and Engineering at the University of Toronto, where he has taught since 2022. He has published in scientific journals and business literature on quantitative innovation and decision making under ambiguity.

== Music ==
A concert-trained violinist, Dr. Forde has performed for United States presidents Bill Clinton and George W. Bush, has performed alongside Sting, Justin Bieber, Mary J. Blige, and Pitbull, and has composed for film and commercial projects.

In 2017, marking what would have been Glenn Gould's 85th birthday, he released "Branches", a collaboration with rapper Shad that combined classical composition with hip hop, inspired by Gould's 1967 CBC radio documentary The Idea of North. The project grew into Ideas of North, a full-length multimedia reinterpretation of Gould's work performed with his band the Ghost Tapes, singer-songwriter iskwē, and trumpeter William Leathers, which premiered during Black History Month in February 2018 and played to a sold-out audience of roughly 1,000 at Koerner Hall in Toronto before touring internationally.

Dr. Forde serves on the board of directors of Tafelmusik, the Toronto-based period-instrument orchestra.

== Philanthropy ==
Through the Forde Foundation, in 2012 Dr. Forde established the Andrew Forde Polymath Award at the University of Toronto, an annual scholarship for an undergraduate engineering student who is active in the Afro-Caribbean community and excels in multiple areas of life beyond academics.

== Writing and speaking ==
Dr. Forde served as master of ceremonies and delivered the opening remarks of the Corporate Innovation Summit at Web Summit Vancouver in May 2026. He has delivered keynotes at Upper Bound in Edmonton, AICON in Halifax, the AMD Canada Leadership Summit, and the SMPS Pinnacle Experience in Las Vegas, and gave the June 2026 convocation address to the University of Toronto's Faculty of Applied Science and Engineering. He was announced as a speaker at the 2026 AfroTech Conference.

His essays and opinion writing include "Renting Intelligence Is a Risky Way to Run a Business", an op-ed published by Digital Journal in April 2026 on the strategic risks of dependence on externally supplied AI capability, and "Only a Revolution Will Solve Canada's Healthcare Crisis" for TheFutureEconomy.ca. His longer-form projects include The Human Standard, an academic manuscript; Technology or Revolution, a seven-essay manifesto on the design, infrastructure, ownership, and governance of the AI age; and AI and the Debasement of Human Judgment.

He is a member of the Forbes Technology Council, through which he contributes commentary on artificial intelligence and technology leadership to Forbes.

== Selected publications ==
* Forde, A.; Fox, M. S. (2015). "A Telecommunications and Innovation Ontology for Global City Indicators (ISO 37120)". Working Paper, Enterprise Integration Laboratory, University of Toronto.
* Forde, Andrew N.; Fox, Mark S. (2023). "An innovation ontology for idea forecasting and measurement". International Journal of Industrial and Systems Engineering. 44 (2): 141-185.
* Forde, Andrew (October 2025). "Only a Revolution Will Solve Canada's Healthcare Crisis". TheFutureEconomy.ca. Op-ed.
* Forde, Andrew (April 16, 2026). "[https://www.digitaljournal.com/article/renting-intelligence-is-a-risky-way-to-run-a-business/ Renting Intelligence Is a Risky Way to Run a Business]". Digital Journal. Op-ed; republished by KPMG in Canada, May 2026.
* Forde, Andrew; Elzeki, Karim (June 2026). "Death of a Data Scientist: The Counterfeit on the Farm". Long-form essay.
* Forde, Andrew (September 2026). "The Doomsday Faction". Essay on the AI existential-risk debate.
* KPMG in Canada (2026). Response to the Government of Canada consultation on artificial intelligence transparency. Policy submission (principal author).

== Recognition ==
Dr. Forde received a Mitacs fellowship award, presented by the Government of Canada, in 2014. He has been recognized as one of Canada's 40 emerging leaders under the age of 40.
