data.title: Benjamin Riley
data.text:
= Benjamin Riley =

Benjamin Riley is an American education writer, policy advocate and former government lawyer. He is the founder of Cognitive Resonance, a self-described "think-and-do tank" that examines generative artificial intelligence through the lens of cognitive science.[1][3] Before that, he founded and for nearly a decade led Deans for Impact, a nonprofit that works to bring findings from the science of learning into teacher preparation programs.[1][6]

Riley is one of the more widely cited skeptics of AI in schools. He argues that large language models imitate the communicative side of human language without doing the thinking that language usually reports, and that heavy student reliance on chatbots can erode the mental effort learning depends on.[11][13] His writing on cognitive science, AI and education has appeared in outlets including The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, The Washington Post, Le Monde, The Guardian, Education Week, Education Next, The 74 and NPR.[1]

Contents
# Education and legal career
# Education policy work
# Deans for Impact
# Cognitive Resonance
## Education Hazards of Generative AI
## Language and intelligence
## "Cognitive hot dog"
# Views
# Reception and criticism
# Selected works
# Media appearances
# References

== Education and legal career ==
Riley earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Washington and a Juris Doctor from Yale Law School.[1] His early career included about four years in private legal practice, a short period on Wall Street, and a summer clerkship with the Land Claims Court of South Africa.[5]

He later served as a deputy attorney general in the California Department of Justice. In that post he advised then–Attorney General Jerry Brown on California's first Race to the Top application and related education policy, helped draft legislation connected to the program, and represented the California State Board of Education, including a stint as the board's interim chief counsel. A Northern California legal publication named him one of two "Rising Stars" in education law in 2009.[5]

== Education policy work ==
After leaving state government, Riley became director of policy and advocacy at NewSchools Venture Fund, where he worked from Washington, D.C., on a policy agenda aimed at supporting education entrepreneurs.[5] He also carried out research on the New Zealand education system.[4]

== Deans for Impact ==
Riley founded Deans for Impact in 2015 and served as its executive director. Based in Austin, Texas, the organization brought together leaders of U.S. educator-preparation programs who wanted teacher training to draw more directly on research-backed principles of how students learn.[7][6]

The group's best-known early publication, The Science of Learning (2015), condensed findings from cognitive psychology into six questions every new teacher should be able to answer, each paired with classroom implications. It was produced by the organization's member deans with University of Virginia cognitive scientist Daniel Willingham and former middle-school science teacher Paul Bruno.[8] At its public launch, Riley urged educators to reconsider teaching one concept to mastery before moving on, and pointed to research-dissemination bodies in the United Kingdom as a model.[9] British education writer David Didau praised the document as clearer than comparable summaries.[10]

In April 2022, Deans for Impact announced that Riley would step down later that year, ending almost ten years with the organization. Board chair David Chard credited him with bold and creative leadership.[6]

== Cognitive Resonance ==
Riley has said his move into AI grew out of his own interest in deep learning in the years before ChatGPT, and from the view that AI belongs alongside psychology, neuroscience, linguistics and philosophy as one of the cognitive sciences.[12] He founded Cognitive Resonance to help people understand both human cognition and generative AI, and to replace hype with a clearer picture of how the systems work.[3][16] The venture publishes the Substack newsletter Build Cognitive Resonance, which had passed 3,000 subscribers, and runs a YouTube channel.[2][15]

=== Education Hazards of Generative AI ===
The organization's first publication, Education Hazards of Generative AI, was released on 7 August 2024 and co-written with Paul Bruno of the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.[11][14] Aimed at teachers, administrators, parents and policymakers, it gives a plain-language overview of how large language models work and draws out practical consequences for classrooms. The report does not reject classroom AI outright but warns that the hype around it obscures real risks.[14] Riley told Education Week that schools need not adopt the technology simply because it exists.[11]

=== Language and intelligence ===
In late November 2025, The Verge published Riley's essay arguing that the AI boom rests on a basic error: treating fluency in language as if it were intelligence.[17] Drawing on a 2024 Nature paper by Evelina Fedorenko and colleagues, which concluded that language is primarily a tool for communication rather than thought, he argued that human reasoning depends largely on brain systems separate from language. On that view, scaling up language models would yield ever better text generation but not general intelligence or new scientific discoveries.[16][17] The piece drew wide international coverage.

=== "Cognitive hot dog" ===
In a second Verge essay in 2026, Riley compared AI to junk food for the mind: harmless as an occasional treat, damaging as a daily diet. He argued that the industry underestimates the harm because its leaders, including Demis Hassabis and Elon Musk, describe the brain as a kind of computer.[13] He cited a working paper on more than 26,000 Chinese secondary students in which homework scores rose after AI adoption while exam scores fell, along with new restrictions on student AI use in Norway and in the New York City and Los Angeles school districts. He also noted a Harvard trial in which purpose-built AI physics tutors outperformed strong active-learning classes.[13] In interviews around the essay, he said human intelligence grows from action, direct experience and cultural transmission rather than data processing.[18]

== Views ==

* AI will not revolutionize education. At the 2025 ASU+GSV Summit, a major ed-tech investment conference, Riley presented himself as a dissenter and told attendees to stop believing claims that AI would transform schooling.[15]
* Language is not thought. Large language models, in his account, reproduce the communicative function of language without the separate processes of reasoning.[16]
* Effort is how people learn. Consistent with his Deans for Impact work, he argues that tools which remove the effort of recall and reasoning can raise short-term output while weakening learning.[13]
* Teachers should decide. Because educators bear responsibility for instruction, he argues they should judge whether and how to use AI, informed by an accurate understanding of its limits.[14]

== Reception and criticism ==
Interviewers have generally described Riley as a careful, well-reasoned skeptic. Michael B. Horn introduced him on the Class Disrupted podcast as one of the AI skeptics the show sought out alongside optimists.[12]

His language essay also drew pushback. Commentators noted that it was a personal synthesis rather than peer-reviewed work, and that many researchers see language and reasoning as more intertwined than he allows.[16] One Substack rebuttal, titled "The Larger Language Mistake," argued that Riley read more into the Fedorenko findings than they support and that his conclusion that language-based systems cannot reason does not follow.[19]

== Selected works ==

* Deans for Impact (2015). The Science of Learning. Austin, TX: Deans for Impact. (Riley was founding executive director.)
* Riley, B. & Anderson, C. (2018). "The Science of Learning." researchED.
* Riley, B. & Bruno, P. (2024). Education Hazards of Generative AI. Cognitive Resonance.
* Riley, B. (2025). "AI will not revolutionize education." Build Cognitive Resonance.
* Riley, B. (2025). "Large Language Mistake" (published as "The AI boom is based on a fundamental mistake"). The Verge.
* Riley, B. (2026). "Our minds aren't equipped to handle AI." The Verge.

== Media appearances ==

* Class Disrupted (The 74), "Ben Riley on Why AI Doesn't Think Like Us," with Michael B. Horn and Diane Tavenner.[12]
* ERRR podcast, episode 102, "Benjamin Riley on the dangers of AI in Education," May 2025.[3]
* What's the Big Idea?, "Ben Riley: We Should Be Skeptical of AI."[20]
* Transforming Teaching, episode 3, on The Science of Learning with Daniel Willingham.

data.title: Legs On Wheels
data.text:
Legs on Wheels is a five-piece progressive rock band from Manchester, UK. Formed in 2017, their musical style blends progressive rock, psychedelic rock, jazz, Canterbury rock, and punk [ref: LEGS ON WHEELS, Prog Archives]. They note their highest influences are King Crimson, Cardiacs, and Frank Zappa. The band is made up of 5 members; Danny Murgatroyd (guitar, vocals), George Roberts (Keys, vocals), Alex Crumbie (Guitar, vocals), Dean Stolloff (bass), and Jamie (Drums).

The band received high praise from Stuart Maconie on his BBC radio 6 show Freak Zone, commenting that their album second Gobble (2026) was a knotty, funky, and adventurous release, calling them one of the best acts he has heard in years [ref: Home, Legs On Wheels].

"Gobble is an absolute masterpiece...this is 45 minutes that will change your musical perceptions if you just let it." I Don't Hear A Single [ref: I Don't Hear A Single: Legs On Wheels - Gobble, I Don't Hear A Single]

"This is truly bonkers...an original and inventive journey" Classic Album Review [ref: NEW ALBUMS - How Many of these do you Own?]

Legs On Wheels have released numerous music videos: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dnFv1F8BOow Winner Winner], [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L1ivqF2m9Lc Peekaboo], [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tyjtQy5QUts A.P.E.S], [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yVyPPzLkCTM The Big Squeeze], [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IWi8JDyb6JQ Heaven's Gaze],the 19 minute epic [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fZSxAQqO6nc Arnold the Slime King], and [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FuPee2d5niM Milktop Mandy].

data.title: Barak Bussel
data.text:
Barak Bussel is an American venture capital investor and entrepreneur whose work focuses on emerging technologies, including quantum computing, semiconductors, and artificial intelligence. He is the managing partner of 7i Capital and chair of the strategic board of the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) Center for Quantum Science and Engineering. [ref: CQSE Strategic Board, UCLA Center for Quantum Science and Engineering]

== Education ==

Bussel received a Bachelor of Science in theoretical and mathematical physics from Harvey Mudd College. He subsequently earned a Master of Science in theoretical physics from UCLA in 1993 and a Master of Business Administration from the UCLA Anderson School of Management in 1995.

== Career ==

Bussel is the founder and managing partner of 7i Capital, a venture capital firm investing in early-stage technology companies in fields including quantum computing, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, semiconductors, robotics, energy, and space.

He has also served as a managing partner at Third Wave Ventures, a Los Angeles-based venture capital firm. From 2016 to 2019, Bussel was president of a photonics technology company in Third Wave Ventures' investment portfolio. Earlier in his career, he served on the board of Neven Vision, a machine-vision company subsequently acquired by Google.

== Academic and quantum technology activities ==

Bussel chairs the strategic board of UCLA's Center for Quantum Science and Engineering. He has participated in efforts to establish the UCLA Quantum Innovation Hub, an initiative associated with the university's Research Park and focused on quantum information science and technology.

In 2017, Bussel delivered an address at UCLA's Department of Physics and Astronomy commencement ceremony. [ref: UCLA College Magazine, Summer 2017, UCLA College]

In August 2026, Bussel appeared on The New Quantum Era podcast to discuss venture investment in quantum computing, fault-tolerant quantum technologies, and collaboration between universities and industry. [ref: Investing in the Quantum Frontier and the Road to Fault Tolerance with Barak Bussel, The New Quantum Era]

== References ==

data.title: Ouijdane QACAMI
data.text:
Ouijdane Qacami is an entrepreneur, researcher and engineer based in France, of Moroccan origin, whose work focuses on concrete durability. [ref: Remise du Prix Pépite 2025: 30 lauréats, dont cinq alumni, récompensés, Campus France Maroc] She is the founder of Strucmedica, a startup developing non-destructive assessment and predictive maintenance tools for concrete infrastructure. [ref: How Moroccan Engineer Ouijdane Qacami Is Using Technology to ‘Listen’ to Buildings, Morocco World News] Her supplied professional record identifies her as its chief executive officer.

Her work brings together materials research, non-destructive measurement and software-assisted interpretation of structural deterioration. [ref: Entretien avec Ouijdane Qacami: « Il est essentiel de valoriser davantage la présence des femmes dans les métiers techniques et industriels », La Nouvelle Tribune] She was a national Prix Pépite laureate in 2025 and was included in Forbes Afrique’s 30 Under 30 selection in 2026. [ref: Moroccan Engineer Ouijdane Qacami Wins France’s Top Student Innovation Prize, Morocco World News] [ref: La Jeunesse Africaine, Moteur de Transformation, Forbes Afrique]

== Education ==
Her supplied professional record lists mathematics preparatory studies (CPGE) in Morocco and civil-engineering studies at the Mohammadia School of Engineers. She subsequently obtained a civil-engineering qualification at the École nationale des ponts et chaussées. She also undertook parallel master’s-level studies in construction-material durability. [ref: Félicitations à Ouijdane Qacami (CIV 22), Lauréate du Prix National Pépite, Ponts Alumni]

Her supplied qualifications are described as “Master of Engineering (MEng), Civil Engineering” and “Master of Science (MS), Sustainable building materials”, the latter also titled “Sciences des Matériaux pour la Construction Durable”, with Mention Bien.

La Rochelle University identifies her as a member of its 2024–2025 D2E student-entrepreneur cohort. [ref: Deux distinctions pour nos étudiants entrepreneurs !, La Rochelle Université] She pursued an executive programme at HEC Paris alongside doctoral research. The programme is described in her supplied materials as DeepTech Startup Leadership.

Her education also includes climate-resilience studies and entrepreneurship training. The climate-resilience course is identified in her supplied materials as RESCUE at La Rochelle, described as an “International diploma of EU policies and initiatives that support resilience”. Its reported topics include climate risks; EU environmental, energy, maritime and social policies; European cooperation and external partnerships; and tools for societal transformation. Her supplied professional record also lists AI and machine-learning accelerator mentorship through Holcim University.

== Business and engineering career ==
=== Engineering experience ===
Her supplied professional record lists a placement with Marchica Med in Nador Province, contributing to urban development, artificial-beach and road projects, pavement-condition assessment and work in the Atalayoun area. It also lists work with BIOUI Travaux in Oujda on the RP6011 road between Berkane and Saïdia, including roadway dimensioning, pavement works, drainage and sanitation, an access bridge, crossing structures and drinking-water connections.

She undertook a placement with STFA Construction Group on the stability of a caisson breakwater at Nador West Med port. The port work was reported by Morocco World News in December 2025. Her supplied professional record identifies STFA, SGTM and JDN as consortium participants and STFA as her placement employer.

Her supplied professional record lists work at Bouygues Construction in Yvelines on BYFLU calculation software for concrete creep and time-dependent tower behaviour, with an application to Triangle Tower in Paris. It also lists structural modelling and design calculations at Ingérop in Rueil-Malmaison for the HHI building at Hinkley Point C, including work she describes as nuclear-waste storage dimensioning. The record describes the Bouygues and Ingérop roles as permanent-contract positions and the Moroccan placements as internships.

Qacami worked as a research-and-development engineer at the Holcim Innovation Center. Her work at Holcim provided the basis for Strucmedica.

Her supplied professional record describes research-and-development project engineering in Saint-Quentin-Fallavier on concrete durability, carbonation, non-destructive measurement and low-carbon materials. It also lists an end-of-studies placement developing a non-destructive carbonation measurement method alongside engineering and master’s studies, and business-plan development among her professional skills.

=== Strucmedica ===
Qacami reports creating earlier startups before founding Strucmedica. She founded Strucmedica to develop non-invasive assessment of concrete structures and support maintenance, repair and continued use. Her supplied professional record lists a founder and chief executive role in France from 2025.

Qacami describes Strucmedica’s proposed system as combining connected sensors, physical materials models and AI-assisted software to interpret concrete condition and anticipate deterioration. Its intended applications include prioritising repairs, estimating carbon dioxide fixed through carbonation and supporting life-cycle assessment of low-carbon concrete. The proposed users include infrastructure owners, operators, consulting engineers and asset managers.

=== Incubation and startup support ===
Her supplied professional record lists Station F incubation/residence support, more than a year of NEOMA Business School incubator support and NEOMA accelerator participation for Strucmedica. Its reported support network also includes WILLA; Deloitte strategic, legal and innovation support; HEC Paris/HEC Challenge; Campus Innov; Pépite France; SATT Nouvelle-Aquitaine; and Bpifrance.

She also reports startup and technical support from GitHub, AWS, Microsoft, Vercel and Anthropic. Her materials identify La French Tech and Le Coq Créa as ecosystem associations and VentureDays Luxembourg as a waitlist lead.

The GEF Start-up Weekend first-prize package included six months of NEOMA incubation, six months of access to WILLA group workshops, legal and tax support from Deloitte Société d’Avocats and Creative Valley mentoring. [ref: Edition 2025, GEF Start-up Weekend]

== Research ==
=== Doctoral research ===
Qacami conducted doctoral research on concrete durability through collaboration between La Rochelle University, the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology and Holcim Innovation Center. Her supplied professional record lists concurrent contractual research appointments at La Rochelle and KIT’s IMB/MPA/CMM, with work in La Rochelle and Karlsruhe.

La Rochelle University announced a public defence scheduled for 23 June 2026 of her thesis on non-destructive evaluation of carbonation in concrete and low-carbon systems through flux measurement. The notice names Abdelkarim Aït-Mokhtar as thesis director, Frank Dehn as co-director and Philippe Turcry as co-supervisor, within joint doctoral supervision with KIT. [ref: Avis de Soutenance: Madame Ouijdane QACAMI, La Rochelle Université]

Her professional description uses “PhD” for the research experience and describes her as a PhD engineer and expert in concrete durability, non-destructive assessment and predictive infrastructure maintenance.

=== Concrete carbonation ===
Qacami is the first author of a paper published in Materials and Structures in 2026 proposing a non-destructive method for assessing concrete carbonation. The Carbonation Flux Test measures carbon dioxide flux using a sealed cell on the concrete surface. The paper reports numerical and experimental testing on low-clinker concrete mixtures and identifies cell sealing as an area for further improvement. [ref: Non-destructive assessment of concrete carbonation based on the CO2 diffusion resistance factor, Materials and Structures]

The paper lists affiliations with Holcim Innovation Center, KIT and La Rochelle’s LaSIE laboratory (CNRS UMR 7356). Co-authors are Bruno Huet, Philippe Turcry, Abdelkarim Aït-Mokhtar, Ravi Ajitbhai Patel and Frank Dehn. Her research also addresses CO₂ transport, carbonation-related uptake and environmental assessment of low-clinker materials.

=== Publications and conferences ===
Qacami’s verified publications and conference records include:
* “Non-destructive assessment of concrete carbonation based on the CO₂ diffusion resistance factor” (2026), a journal article in Materials and Structures, volume 59, article 160.
* “Diffusive method for measuring carbonation properties of concrete under natural laboratory conditions” (2025), a proceedings paper in the fib International Symposium on Concrete Structures in Antibes, pp. 1968–1979. [ref: Diffusive method for measuring carbonation properties of concrete under natural laboratory conditions, KITopen]
* “Numerical study and inverse analysis of a non distructive measurement method for oxygen diffusivity in partially carbonated concrete” (2023), an oral-contribution record and abstract for the Journées d’Etudes des Milieux Poreux (JEMP), with Qacami, Bruno Huet, Philippe Turcry, Abdelkarim Aït-Mokhtar, Ravi Ajitbhai Patel and Frank Dehn listed as authors. [ref: Numerical study and inverse analysis of a non distructive measurement method for oxygen diffusivity in partially carbonated concrete, 16e Journées d’Etudes des Milieux Poreux (JEMP 2023)]

Her supplied research materials list additional conference contributions including “Field evaluation of oxygen diffusion in partially carbonated concrete by numerical calculation” at AUGC–CFGC 2023; “Validation of a non-destructive method for assessing instantaneous carbonation of coated concrete” at the 78th RILEM Annual Week in 2024; and “Assessing CO₂ uptake by cementitious materials for life cycle analysis: flux measurement and thermogravimetric analysis” at ICSBM 2025. The RILEM presentation was also reported by Morocco World News. She reports three fib contributions overall, of which two additional citations remain unidentified.

Her other reported research works include “Non destructive diffusive method for assessing carbonation: influencing factors”; “Evaluating carbonation and CO₂ uptake in low-clinker cementitious concretes through flux testing and conventional methods”; “Experimental study of hygroscopic and gas transport properties of calcined clay and portland concretes under carbonation and curing effects”; “Experimental based modeling of moisture transport in partially carbonated low-carbon concrete under wetting drying cycles”; and “Impact of wetting drying cycles on CO₂ flux and diffusive properties evolution in concrete: comparative study under natural and controlled conditions for low-carbon concretes”. Publication and acceptance status for these works remain unverified.

Qacami is listed in her supplied event materials as a Tech&Fest 2026 speaker and in Meet & Fabrik/i-Factory coverage in Tribune de Lyon. Strucmedica is also listed as a 2026 Viva Technology exhibitor/delegation participant.

== Associations and volunteering ==
=== Morocco and student initiatives ===
Qacami participated in Enactus and Solar Decathlon and helped found a sustainable civil-engineering association.

Her supplied professional record lists communications leadership for EMIGreen and co-founding CLUB EMI Génie Civil. It also lists construction-unit leadership with THRIVE-HOUSE SDA and engineering and operations leadership through Enactus and Solar Decathlon Africa. She describes leading a multidisciplinary team of approximately 13 on Thrive, an energy-autonomous building, and selection among ten global projects for Solar Decathlon Africa 2019.

=== France and professional associations ===
Qacami reports involvement in establishing associations in Morocco and France. Her supplied professional record lists social-media and events coordination with ADO–Les Ailes de Demain in Lyon, in an Erasmus+ context involving youth leadership, social justice, workshops, training and international exchanges. It also lists rescue volunteering with FFSS 75–AMNS, AFGC membership and fib young membership.

== Awards and recognition ==

* 2025: First prize awarded by Alter Egales at the GEF Start-up Weekend, with Strucmedica.
* 2025: National Prix Pépite laureate, one of 30 selected projects, representing Pépite ECA with Strucmedica in the category Les matériaux dans tous leurs états, following regional selection. [ref: 12ᵉ édition du Prix Pépite, Pépite France] The award was also reported by Femmes du Maroc and H24info, the latter crediting MAP. [ref: La Marocaine Ouijdane Qacami primée en France pour sa startup Strucmedica, Femmes du Maroc] [ref: France: la Marocaine Ouijdane Qacami reçoit le Prix Pépite dédié aux jeunes startups, H24info]
* CLAP prize recipient, identified by La Rochelle University. Her reported categories are CLAP Innovation and CLAP Coup de Cœur; she also lists Innovation and Public’s Choice at “J’peux pas, j’entreprends!”.
* 2026: Forbes Afrique 30 Under 30 selection.
* 2026: Strucmedica’s selection for TechCrunch’s Startup Battlefield 200 cohort. [ref: The 2026 Startup Battlefield 200 is here: see who made the cut, TechCrunch]
* 2026: i-PhD laureate for the Strucmedica project in France’s state innovation competition, operated by Bpifrance under the France 2030 programme. [ref: Concours d’innovation de l’État 2026: 8 projets IP Paris parmi les lauréats i-PhD et i-Lab, Institut Polytechnique de Paris] Campus France lists Qacami among the award-winning alumni, and Institut Polytechnique de Paris identifies Strucmedica among the i-PhD laureate projects. [ref: Concours d’innovation de l'Etat: deux alumni décrochent un Grand Prix, Campus France]
* Reported Prix Enedis/Meet & Fabrik, Prix AAPIC, Forbes Tech for Change, NeoTerra/Neo Terra Greentech and Pepitizy distinctions.
* Reported sixth place in Startup World Cup Paris, Top 30 finalist status in Construction Startup Competition, laureate status in Tech for Construction and finalist status for Prix Gabriel/Live for Good.

The Spartanburg Youth Theatre is a community theatre founded in 1972 by Mary Nicholson. It operates on a “for youth, by youth,” principle. [ref: ]

Its productions are almost entirely produced by children. Children in the 3rd-12th grades can audition to be cast, and 7th-12th graders can apply to work as crew. It received the South Carolina Theatre of Distinction recognition in 2023 [ref: Previous Recipients, South Carolina Theatre Association].

== History ==
Founded in 1972, SYT originally performed in the Camp Croft Playhouse [ref: David W. Reid, Spartanburg Herald Journal] (later named the David W. Reid Playhouse) with its sister company, Spartanburg Little Theatre. Both companies moved to the Chapman Cultural Center in 2007.

The Youth Theatre is an extension of the Spartanburg Little Theatre, which was founded in 1964 [ref: ]. Their productions and offices reside entirely in the Chapman Cultural Center theatre building.

== Community Impact ==
SYT is highly involved in the local Spartanburg community, primarily in their outreach programs with local Title I schools. SYT board and educational members perform shows in Title I schools so as to curate an accessible introduction into the performing arts at a young age. They have performed True Story of the 3 Little Pigs, The Rainbow Fish, and more in these performances.

The theatre also provides school-time performances, in which local classes are able to come watch a show in the morning as an arts field trip [ref: ]. They average seven school time performances per Youth production.

Cast members have been featured on local news stations in order to advertise the show [ref: Spartanburg Youth Theatre Puts on 3 Little Pigs, Your Carolina].

== Productions ==
The theatre is currently producing their 2026-2027 season. Their performances take place consistently in October, December, February, and April. They also produce summer blackbox shows. SLT alternates between these months with their season averaging six shows, as opposed to the Youth Theatre’s four.

data.title: Warren Davis (video game designer)
data.text:
Warren Davis is an American video game designer, programmer, actor and author. He designed and programmed the 1982 arcade game Q*bert at Gottlieb, working with artist Jeff Lee. He later worked on video digitizing tools used in arcade games including Mortal Kombat and NBA Jam. He has also worked as an actor, mainly in guest television roles, and in 2022 published a memoir about his career in the arcade industry.

== Early life and education ==
Davis attended high school in Brooklyn, New York, where he first learned to program in the 1970s. He earned a bachelor's degree in computer and systems engineering from Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and a master's degree in electrical engineering from Ohio State University. He then worked at Bell Labs in Naperville, Illinois, leaving in 1981; afterwards he studied improvisational theatre in Chicago.

== Video game career ==
=== Gottlieb ===
Davis joined Gottlieb as a video game programmer at the start of 1982, after answering a newspaper job advertisement. Q*bert was his first game. It began as a programming exercise with bouncing balls, to which Davis added a player character, collision detection and the ability to jump off the pyramid. In Davis's account, the game's pyramid of cubes grew out of a cube-patterned screen Lee had drawn, and Davis wrote all of the game's code and made its design decisions; Lee designed the characters and is credited by Davis as a close collaborator, and David Thiel created the sound. Davis removed an early idea in which the main character shot at enemies, and rotated the joystick 45 degrees to match the game's diagonal movement, keeping the design despite objections from other staff.

Before release, Davis lowered the game's difficulty at management's request, which he later regretted. In 1983 he made a harder version, Faster, Harder, More Challenging Q*bert, which tested poorly and was not released; he later made its program available to the public. Davis declined Gottlieb's request to make a Q*bert sequel, and the follow-up, Q*bert's Qubes, was made by another programmer.

At Mylstar Electronics, as Gottlieb had been renamed, Davis was programmer and video editor on Us vs. Them (1984), a laserdisc video game combining live-action footage with game graphics. The finished game was smaller in scope than first planned, and laserdisc hardware proved too fragile for arcade use.

=== Williams, Midway and later work ===
At Williams Electronics Davis co-programmed Joust 2: Survival of the Fittest (1986) and began developing a system for bringing videotaped images into games, first used for NARC. At Williams he typically worked as part of larger teams rather than as lead designer. After leaving to develop the arcade game Exterminator for Premier Technology, he returned to Williams to work on Terminator 2: Judgment Day (1991). His digitizing work was used in Williams/Bally/Midway games including Mortal Kombat and NBA Jam, and he also worked on Revolution X (1994). In the late 1990s he worked at Disney Interactive.

== Acting ==
Davis later turned to acting. His television guest roles include episodes of The Practice (1999), ER (2002), House (2005), Criminal Minds (2005) and The Middle (2015). He has also appeared as himself in documentaries about video games, including Video Games: The Movie (2014) and Insert Coin (2020), a film about Midway's arcade studio.

== Writing ==
Davis self-published a memoir, You Can't Call It @!#?@!, in 2019. Santa Monica Press then published it in 2022 as Creating Q*bert and Other Classic Video Arcade Games, with a foreword by Ed Boon and an afterword by John Newcomer. Publishers Weekly described the book as an entertaining debut that would fascinate gamers.

== Recognition ==
Davis was inducted into the International Video Game Hall of Fame as part of its class of 2017, in a ceremony in Ottumwa, Iowa, on October 6, 2018. In February 2019 he was one of twelve fans inducted into the White Castle restaurant chain's Cravers Hall of Fame, in its 18th annual class; his entry described eating the chain's burgers late at night while developing Q*bert.

data.title: Kyle Correya
data.text:
Kyle Correya is an Australian Catholic worship leader, singer-songwriter and youth minister based in Melbourne, Victoria. He is the organiser of Awaken Night, a recurring Catholic worship event series run in partnership with New Dawn Ministry and Raconteur, and leads a schools and youth ministry program offering retreat days, student workshops and staff sessions to Catholic schools. In 2026 he began releasing original worship music, starting with the single "Stuffed Up".

== Early life ==
Kyle grew up in Melbourne.

== Ministry ==
=== Awaken Night ===
Kyle organises and leads worship at Awaken Night, a Catholic evening of worship run with New Dawn Ministry and Raconteur. The series is held at parishes around Melbourne; one edition took place at St Peter's Catholic Church, Epping, on 22 August 2026.

=== Schools and youth ministry ===
Kyle runs a schools and youth ministry program for Catholic schools, offering retreat days, student workshops and staff formation sessions. He also speaks to student groups; in June 2026 he travelled to Sydney with Icon Ministry to address a large gathering of students.

== Music ==
Kyle writes and records original contemporary worship songs. He began releasing them as singles in October 2026, with a further original and a Christmas single scheduled for later that year.

data.title: Trudy Tanzillo
data.text:
Trudy Tanzillo (born Trudy Ann Cauthen, 1946) is an American former beauty pageant titleholder and hereditary society officer. She was crowned Miss North Carolina USA in 1963 and represented North Carolina at Miss USA 1963. Since 2025 she has served as President General of the Descendants of American Prisoners of War (DAPOW), a national lineage society.

== Pageantry ==
Cauthen, of Newton, North Carolina, was crowned Miss North Carolina USA in 1963; contemporary newspaper coverage styled her "Miss N. C. Universe" and photographed her in a white ball gown waving from a flower-decked float. [ref: Contemporary newspaper photograph, 1963, captioned "MISS N. C. UNIVERSE, TRUDY CAUTHEN" (family collection).] She succeeded Brenda Smith of Charlotte in the title. As state titleholder she represented North Carolina at the Miss USA 1963 pageant, held in Miami Beach, Florida, on 17 July 1963. North Carolina sent no delegate to Miss USA in 1964; the next recorded state titleholder was Sandra Farmer of Greensboro in 1965.

== Education and career ==
Tanzillo earned a Bachelor of Arts in social sciences at Western Carolina University (1962–1966), where she was a member of Sigma Kappa and head cheerleader, and a Master of Arts in reading at Rider University (1979–1981), followed by certification in supervision and administration at Rutgers University (1984). [ref: Tanzillo, Trudy. Professional profile. LinkedIn.] Her career was in New Jersey public education: she taught in the Bordentown Township, East Windsor Regional, and Manalapan-Englishtown Regional school districts, served as assistant principal of West Windsor-Plainsboro High School South (1998–2002), and was an adjunct professor at Rider University (2002).

== Hereditary society leadership ==
Tanzillo has held office in several American hereditary and lineage societies. She was an officer of the Descendants of American Prisoners of War from its first administration, serving as Corresponding Secretary General (2021–2023), [ref: "Captive Thoughts" (DAPOW newsletter), Issue 2, 2022. Officer listing: "Corresponding Secretary General — Trudy Cauthen Tanzillo."] and in 2025 was elected the society's third President General, for the 2025–2027 term, succeeding Kimberly Ormsby Nagy. [ref: Descendants of American Prisoners of War (DAPOW) "President General (2025–2027): Trudy Cauthen Tanzillo."] [ref: Officers, Descendants of American Prisoners of War] She took office at the society's Fourth Annual Assembly on 6 April 2025 in Alexandria, Virginia. [ref: News & Photos, Descendants of American Prisoners of War]

She has also served as president of the Virginia Society of the National Society Southern Dames of America (2018–2020), [ref: "Virginia Society, Trudy Tanzillo, President 2018–2020." The Journal, National Society Southern Dames of America, Spring 2018.] president of the District of Columbia society of the National Society Daughters of Founders and Patriots of America (2019), [ref: CMM Past President Addresses Joint Meeting of DC OFPA and DC DFPA, Culpeper Minute Men Photo caption: "DC President, Daughters of Founders and Patriots, Trudy Tanzillo."] and chairman of the finance committee of the Sons and Daughters of Virginia Founding Fathers (2019–2021). She is a member of the Daughters of the American Revolution (from 2008), serving as Assistant Registrar of its Fairfax County Chapter in 2019, [ref: "Fairfax County Chapter Attends Turning Point Suffragist Memorial Groundbreaking." The Virginia View (Virginia Society DAR), Vol. V, Issue 2, November 2019.] a member of The National Society of the Colonial Dames of America (from 2017), and is recorded as an attendee at annual assemblies of the Order of the Steel Magnolias in 2019 and 2023. [ref: History, Order of the Steel Magnolias]

== Personal life ==
Tanzillo was born in Newton, North Carolina, in 1946.

data.title: SOCIAL AND MEDIA STUDIES INSTITUTE
data.text:
The **Social and Media Studies Institute** (French: Institut d'Études Sociales et Médiatiques; Arabic: معهد الدراسات الاجتماعية والإعلامية, acronym: SMS Institute) is an independent, non-profit think tank and research center headquartered in Casablanca, Kingdom of Morocco. Founded in mid-2019 by a collective of Moroccan researchers and academics specializing in economic, legal, political, and social sciences.

The institute produces field analyses and scientific public opinion polls on social, economic, and political transformations in Morocco, the Maghreb region, and Africa, as well as evaluations of public policies and the development of field observation tools.

== Creation and Objectives ==
The institute was founded with the aim of bridging theoretical academic research with public policy evaluation and providing empirical data for decision-makers and civil society actors. Its core statutory objectives include:
* Conducting quantitative and qualitative field studies on societal and media dynamics.
* Organizing public opinion polls on current political, economic, and social issues.
* Publishing peer-reviewed scientific journals and academic works via its publishing house, "African Academic Press". [ref: يوسف الحفيرة يقارب "الهوية السياسية", Hespress]
* Developing strategic notes and recommendations aimed at improving legislation and public policies. [ref: معهد الدراسات الاجتماعية يصدر مذكرة استراتيجية جديدة: نحو نموذج سياسي مغربي يقود التنمية, Journal 24]
* Promoting the values of transparency, combating discrimination, and anchoring ethics in media and scientific research.

== Structure and Governance ==
The governance of the institute relies on an executive management team and a scientific council composed of doctors and university professors affiliated with various Moroccan and international universities (including Mohammed V University in Rabat, Hassan II University in Casablanca, Cadi Ayyad University in Marrakech, Sidi Mohamed Ben Abdellah University in Fes, Chouaib Doukkali University in El Jadida, Ibn Zohr University in Agadir, Mohammed I University in Oujda, as well as associate researchers from the University of Douala in Cameroon and Abderrahmane Mira University in Béjaïa, Algeria).

* Scientific Presidency: The institute is chaired by Dr. Younes Bennane, an economist and researcher specializing in public policies and geopolitics. [ref: Global South researchers to offer solutions to key world problems at ‘Future of the World’ Open Dialogue]
* Executive Management: Executive leadership and the development of international partnerships are overseen by Canadian researcher Dr. Brahim Meddeb. [ref: تنصيب الكندي براهيم مداب على رأس الادارة التنفيذية لمعهد الدراسات الاجتماعية و الإعلامية بالمغرب, Press Medias]

== Research Axes and Strategic Observatories ==

=== Political Sociology and Electoral Observation ===
The institute established the Interactive Legislative Election Results Observatory to monitor shifts in the electoral map, voting behavior in Morocco, and parliamentary performance [ref: المرصد التفاعلي للنتائج البرلمانية, BENNANE], while also formulating strategic memorandums containing proposals to reform the electoral system. [ref: معهد مغربي ينادي بإنشاء مجلس وطني مستقل للإشراف على الانتخابات, Hespress]

=== Public Policy and Institutional Evaluation ===
In its studies, the institute addresses the efficiency of national and constitutional institutions. It published an analytical report on the decisions of the Competition Council between 2020 and 2021 to assess its role in market regulation and the implementation of the New Development Model. [ref: دراسة: مجلس المنافسة لم يقبل أيّا من الإحالات المعروضة عليه باستثناء طلب رأي من وزير المالية, Lakome2] [ref: ] On the legislative front, the institute published a study addressing obstacles hindering parliamentary oversight of state budget execution within the framework of the organic law on finance laws. [ref: ] The institute has also conducted a study on the evolution of civil society functions in Morocco and its relationship with the state since independence.

=== Economic Foresight and Energy Security ===
The institute develops strategic dashboards, including a report dedicated to energy security [ref: ], shipping flows in Moroccan ports, and economic impact scenarios of closing the Strait of Hormuz. [ref: Google Scholar, scholar.google.com] In the summer of 2026, the institute published a critical study of the High Commission for Planning's (HCP) methodology regarding the labor market, demonstrating that the statistical decline in the unemployment rate does not necessarily reflect a reduction in social pressures and real precarity. [ref: ]

=== Social and Educational Issues ===
The institute has conducted several field opinion polls covering citizen trust in political parties (2021), Moroccan youth trust in the future and migration issues (2023), as well as a survey revealing that 80% of surveyed PhD holders doubt the transparency of selection criteria for assistant professor-researchers in Moroccan universities (2023).

== Media Coverage and International Notoriety ==
The institute's reports and polls benefit from extensive national and international media coverage:
* International Coverage: An episode of the international channel France 24 (part of the Vis-à-vis program) was dedicated to analyzing and debating the results of the institute's poll regarding Moroccan youth trust in the future and emigration. [ref: ] The institute also participates in international conferences, notably the 14th International Conference on Foresight and Innovation Policy organized by the Higher School of Economics (HSE) in Moscow, as well as the proceedings of the international "Open Dialogue" forum. [ref: ]
* National Coverage: The institute's work is regularly relayed by prominent official and independent reference media such as the Maghreb Arabe Presse (MAP / RIM Radio), Le360, Hespress, Lakome2, Anfas Press, and specialized websites like Albahr News.

== Periodicals and Scientific Publications ==
The institute publishes several peer-reviewed scientific journals registered with the international ISSN network:

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Journal Title !! Scientific Field !! International Identifier (ISSN)
|-
| Revue Droit et Société (مجلة القانون والمجتمع) || Legal, political, and social sciences || ISSN: 2737-8101 / P-ISSN: 2737-8152
|-
| Revue Économie et Société (مجلة الاقتصاد والمجتمع) || Economic sciences, management, and development || ISSN: 2820-6991 / P-ISSN: 2820-7211
|-
| Insaniyat (مجلة إنسانيات) || Humanities and media sociology || Peer-reviewed academic edition
|}

Additionally, the publishing house affiliated with the institute, "African Academic Press", has published several monographs and academic works equipped with a legal deposit and an ISBN number:
* Santé et protection sociale au Maroc - Dr. Younes Bennane and Sanaa Haouata (ISBN: 978-9920-9209-4-0).
* Méthodologie de la recherche sur le terrain - Dr. Fawzi Boukhriss (ISBN: 978-9920-9209-3-3).
* Introduction à la sociologie des organisations - Dr. Fawzi Boukhriss (ISBN: 978-9920-9209-2-6).
* Le contrôle de la société anonyme - Dra. Asmaa Boukhima (ISBN: 978-9920-42-212-3).
* Le droit de grève et la continuité du service public - Moustafa Jai (ISBN: 978-9920-9209-5-7).
* Les dispositions de la prénotation dans la législation marocaine - Yassine Hosni (ISBN: 978-9920-9209-1-9).

== Distinctions and Institutional Differentiation ==
To avoid any conceptual or institutional confusion, the institute is clearly distinct from the following structures:
* MENASSAT Center for Social Research and Studies: A non-governmental organization based in Casablanca focused on fundamental sociological research and individual freedoms.
* Institute of Higher Economic and Social Studies (IHEES): A private higher education institution founded in 1984 in Casablanca.
* Higher Institute of Information and Communication (ISIC): A public university establishment in Rabat specializing in initial journalism training.
* School of Information Sciences (ESI): A public institution located in Rabat specializing in knowledge engineering and data management.

data.title: Peace, Death!
data.text:
Peace, Death! is a pixel art simulation game developed and published for PC on March 24, 2017, by the Russian studio AZAMATIKA. The player controls Reaper, a novice worker of Death, who must guide people to their correct afterlife. [ref: Peace, Death! para PC - Linux, 3DJuegos] [ref: インディーズゲームの小部屋：Room＃474「Peace, Death!」, 4Gamer.net] [ref: Безумные игры: смартфонный президент, пес-суперагент и русские в Steam — Игромания, Igromania.ru] [ref: «Мир! Труд! Май!» — подборка игр, в которых можно попробовать необычные профессии, iXBT.games]. The game is currently available on PC, Android, iOS and Nintendo Switch.

== Gameplay ==
The gameplay consists of selecting who goes to Hell, Heaven or Purgatory, within a time limit. [ref: ]

In order to do it properly, the player must examine each individual and see what criteria they meet. [ref: SwitchArcade Round-Up: ‘SEGA AGES Out Run’ Releases January 10th, Upcoming NEOGEO Titles, the Latest Releases, a Huge List of Sales, and More – TouchArcade, TouchArcade] Initially it is as simple as sending demons down to Hell on the left elevator and humans up to Heaven on the right elevator. However, new rules are added every day and the process of checking them gets increasingly more complex. The player can be asked, for example, to verify if someone is carrying a weapon or if their body is stained with blood, with both cases meaning the character is meant to be sent to Hell. Some crucial elements might be hidden with objects such as hats or glasses, which must be removed in order to make a proper judgement.

Each day has a set number of people to verify, after which the player receives rewards depending on their performance. If enough mistakes are made, a day can be failed midway.

After a certain point, Purgatory is added as a third destination for those who cannot go to either Heaven or Hell. The criteria include, for example, letting go of a weapon (which would otherwise result in Hell) or renouncing holy text (which would otherwise lead to Heaven) when the player left-clicks the corresponding character.

During work, the player might answer phone calls from colleagues asking for advice on certain decisions. They receive the description of an individual and must discern what is important and what is superfluous.

The game often presents bizarre visitors, including celebrity references.

== Plot ==
The protagonist, a Grim Reaper, realizes they have no food to eat and decides to apply for a job at Apocalypse Corporation, working for Death. After successfully completing seven weeks of a trial period, they get paid and hired for a full-time job. [ref: Peace, Death!, Steam]

== Development ==
The head of the AZAMATIKA studio, Azamat Baizulaev (also known as Azamat Zage), revealed his original plan was to make a sequel to his Western game Gun Done, with the same hero, but it didn't work out. At the same time, he came across an online comment sarcastically asking his next game to not be called Peace, Death! (a Russian swear pun). [ref: «В играх я беру ник ULTRAG4Y». Интервью с создателем Peace, Death и Draw Chilly, DTF] The developer, instead, was motivated by the comment and began working on the title.

According to the creator, the central idea of the game remained mostly the same over the course of development. He highlights, however, how Reaper would originally give orders with a lever instead of his hands, which became visually problematic when Purgatory was added. [ref: Интервью с создателем игры Peace, Death! «А еще мы выпустили Gun Done» — Игромания, Igromania.ru]

When asked about comparisons to Papers, Please, Azamat described the similarities as coincidental, while acknowledging it helped boost the popularity of Peace, Death!

The game was localized in French by Sébastien Sosa and Mate Lichtle, in German by Thomas H. (also known as Kyron) and in Brazilian Portuguese by Ruffles, HDD and Fire Borealis. [ref: [Peace, Death! news and announcements], Steam]

Its Nintendo Switch edition, called Peace, Death: Complete Edition, was published by HypeTrain Digital. [ref: Nintendo Download: 22nd November (Europe), Nintendo Life]

== Reception ==
Peace, Death! was often compared to Papers, Please due to its similar gameplay loop.

Shaun Musgrave, writing for TouchArcade, praised the game's concept and the gameplay itself. However, he also drew attention to the humor, with some jokes he described as "a bit lame" and references he predicted might become dated.

An Igromania review, from Lena Pi, described the game as a rather entertaining time-killer.

== References ==

Scott Frenzel is an American musician, songwriter, and digital content creator known for his pop music releases and online video content. He gained an audience through videos on YouTube, including comedic content about nostalgia and childhood trends. [ref: Road to 1 million subscribers with Scott Frenzel, blog.youtube]
== Early career and internet presence ==
Frenzel began creating videos after losing his restaurant job during the COVID-19 pandemic. His content included nostalgic comedy, reaction videos, and recurring series such as “That Kid” and “Embarrassing Mistakes Every College Freshman Makes.” [ref: Road to 1 million subscribers with Scott Frenzel, blog.youtube]

== Music career ==
Frenzel released the single “Sugar High” in 2023. In 2024, the song appeared on YouTube's list of the most-used songs in Shorts in the United Kingdom for that year, ranking sixth. [ref: Central Cee and Charli XCX among domestic acts on YouTube UK rankings for 2024, www.musicweek.com]

Following the success of “Sugar High,” he released several singles, including:

* “Key Lime Pie”
* “Someone on the Radio”
* “Ghost Stories”

These releases and Frenzel's subsequent music career are discussed in [https://www.bmi.com/spotlight/scott-frenzel BMI's artist profile of Scott Frenzel.]

On February 20, 2025, Frenzel released his debut EP Postcards, which included previously released singles, the title track, and an additional demo track titled “Burnout”, which was never released on streaming platforms. Later in 2025, Frenzel released the single “Streetlights.” In November 2025, he released the holiday single “Reindeer Games.”

== Style and themes ==
Frenzel's music combines pop influences, nostalgic sounds, and lyrics focused on relatable experiences. BMI's [https://www.bmi.com/spotlight/scott-frenzel artist profile] identifies Katy Perry's Teenage Dream and Troye Sivan's earlier music among his influences.

data.title: Jackpot.com
data.text:
----

Jackpot.com is an American lottery courier based in San Francisco. It has a website and app for ordering tickets for lottery draw games such as Powerball and Mega Millions, along with scratch cards, in seven US states as of January 2026. [ref: Jackpot.com secures $10m financing to fuel expansion, NEXT.io]

== History ==
In 2017, the Malta Gaming Authority approved the addition of a lottery messenger proposition to Jackpot.com's license. [ref: Jackpot.com secures secondary Maltese lottery licence, iGB] The company later began operating as a lottery courier in the United States. Its co-founders include chief executive Akshay Khanna, Roi More, and Yariv Ron. [ref: With New Jersey ties, Jackpot.com continues its rapid growth, NJBIZ]

In January 2023, Jackpot.com launched in Texas. [ref: The Couriers’ Race – La Fleur's Lottery World, lafleurs.com] Following its initial Series A funding round of $35 million in June 2022, [ref: Jackpot raises $35m to fund US expansion, Gaming Intelligence] [ref: Arctos, Kraft, Rubin Among Heavy Hitters in $35M Jackpot Raise, Yahoo Finance] the company secured an additional $7 million, [ref: Jackpot.com receives $42m investment to expand to Texas - SBC Americas] bringing total funding to $42 million. Investors included Bettor Capital, Aurum Partners, Detroit Venture Partners, the Tisch family, and the Dallas Cowboys and New York Yankees.

In 2023, Jackpot.com expanded its courier operations. It launched in Ohio in May [ref: Lottery site Jackpot.com launches in Ohio with help from Cleveland's three pro sports teams, Crains Cleveland] New York in August. [ref: Jackpot brings its lottery app, online ticket sales to NY, PIX11 News] In 2024 it continued its expansion, becoming available in Massachusetts in January, [ref: Jackpot.com enters fourth US market with Massachusetts launch - EGR North America] Arkansas in March, [ref: ] New Jersey in May, [ref: Lottery courier Jackpot.com launches in NJ, NJBIZ] and Colorado in November. [ref: Jackpot.com Launches in Colorado, Expanding To Seventh State] On January 7, 2025, Jackpot.com launched in Arizona, its eighth state. [ref: Arizona Now Eighth Market for Lottery Courier Jackpot.com]

In February 2025, the Texas Lottery Commission announced that it would prohibit lottery courier services. By early April 2025, Jackpot.com had suspended its operations in the state. [ref: How couriers changed the playing field of the Texas Lottery, The Texas Tribune] In June 2025, Texas enacted Senate Bill 3070, which made it a criminal offense to sale lottery tickets online or through apps, effectively banning courier services, and abolished the Texas Lottery Commission. [ref: Texas Lottery Commission to be disbanded as state game gets new restrictions, The Texas Tribune]

In January 2026, the company secured a $10 million revolving credit facility from Discerning Capital’s House Advantage Fund and PvX Capital.

In March 2026, the company introduced a loyalty program, Jackpot Rewards. [ref: Loyalty 360 - Jackpot.com Launches Loyalty Program to Reward Lottery Players]

== Operations ==

=== Courier service ===
Customers order lottery tickets through the Jackpot.com website or app. The company subsequently buys a physical ticket from a licensed retailers on the customer's behalf and uploads a scan of it to their account.

Winnings under $600 are credited directly to the customer's account. For larger prizes, the ticket is delivered to the player to claim from the state lottery.

In November 2024, 7-Eleven named Jackpot.com as its official lottery partner at more than 600 stores in Ohio and Massachusetts [ref: Jackpot.com named lottery partner of 7-Eleven, Gaming Intelligence].

data.title: Benjamin Basire
data.text:
Benjamin Basire is an Iranian-American legal and compliance professional, political analyst, writer, and media commentator based in Malibu, California. He writes articles and political analysis for media and academic outlets, specializing in Iran and Middle Eastern affairs, denuclearization, nuclear energy policy, and Iran's future democratic constitutional design. [ref: Integrating Denuclearization and Energy Accessibility: Policy Frameworks for a Sustainable Transition, SSRN] [ref: Rekindling the Discussion About Nuclear Power Usage, SSRN]

He has appeared multiple times on Fox News, on programs hosted by Trace Gallagher and Jonathan Hunter, and on Italy's RAI TG3 Mondo. He was the first political analyst in media to compare Secretary of State Marco Rubio's leadership style to that of Winston Churchill. [ref: Rubio's leadership is similar to Churchill, political analyst says, Fox News Video] Basire is also an active LGBT rights advocate and has worked with refugee populations.

He belongs to the Basire family, whose Sephardic branch resettled in Izmir (Smyrna) in the 15th century and later migrated to Persia (modern-day Iran), and whose British branch produced four generations of celebrated copper-plate engravers, including James Basire (1730–1802), the master of William Blake. [ref: James Basire, Wikipedia] [ref: James Basire, The Worshipful Company of Stationers and Newspaper Makers]

== Early life and family ==

Basire was born in Tehran, Iran to a Jewish family and grew up in Larnaca, Cyprus, where he was educated before relocating to the United States. He speaks six languages professionally and fluently: English, Persian (Farsi), Turkish, Greek, French, and Hebrew.

=== Sephardic heritage and the Basire dynasty ===

The Basire family is a Sephardic Jewish dynasty with branches across the Mediterranean, the Middle East, and Europe. The branch to which Benjamin belongs resettled in Izmir (Smyrna) in the Ottoman Empire during the 15th century, part of the broader wave of Jewish migration following the expulsions from the Iberian Peninsula. The family later migrated eastward to Persia (modern-day Iran), where they became established within the country's ancient Jewish community, one of the oldest in the world, with roots extending to the Babylonian captivity of the 6th century BCE. [ref: Persian Jews]

On his mother's side, Basire comes from a well-respected Persian Jewish family.

=== The Basire dynasty ===

The British branch of the Basire family produced four generations of distinguished copper-plate engravers and is among the most prominent artistic dynasties in British history.

The dynasty began with Isaac Basire (1704–1768), the son of Jacques Basire, a Huguenot emigrant from Rouen, Normandy, who settled in Soho, London. Isaac trained as a silversmith before turning to copper-plate engraving, becoming renowned for his cartographic work. [ref: Isaac Basire (engraver), Wikipedia] [ref: BASIRE, Isaac, The Huguenots of Spitalfields]

His son James Basire I (1730–1802) became the most celebrated member of the dynasty. He served as Engraver to both the Royal Society and the Society of Antiquaries of London, and is best known for apprenticing the young William Blake at his Great Queen Street studio beginning 4 August 1772. His major works included the copperplate for the Field of the Cloth of Gold and extensive contributions to Vetusta Monumenta. [ref: James Basire, Royal Academy of Arts]

The tradition continued through James Basire II (1769–1822), who engraved the Oxford Almanack, and James Basire III (1796–1869), who expanded into lithography and produced scientific illustrations for the Philosophical Transactions and journals of the Royal Astronomical Society and Zoological Society of London. [ref: Drawing on Copper: The Basire family of copper-plate engravers and their works, Universitaire Pers Maastricht]

The broader Basire family also produced Claude Basire (1764–1794), a French Revolutionary politician from Dijon. He served as a deputy for the Côte-d'Or in the Legislative Assembly and the National Convention, where he voted for the execution of Louis XVI. He was tried before the Revolutionary Tribunal alongside Georges Danton and Camille Desmoulins and was guillotined in Paris in 1794. [ref: Claude Basire, Wikipedia]

== Education ==

Basire earned his Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) in International Affairs and Global Studies from Portland State University in Portland, Oregon. He then completed his LL.B./J.D. at Queen's University Belfast in Northern Ireland, followed by a Master of Laws (LL.M.) in Energy, Environment, and Natural Resources Law at Lewis & Clark Law School, also in Portland. He later enrolled at Pepperdine Caruso School of Law's Straus Institute for Dispute Resolution, where he is pursuing a second LL.M. in Dispute Resolution and completing a thesis on post-theocratic Iranian constitutional design. [ref: Straus Institute for Dispute Resolution, Pepperdine Caruso School of Law]

== Career ==

=== Legal and compliance ===

Basire has built a career in the legal and compliance field, with experience spanning litigation, regulatory compliance, dispute resolution, and enforcement matters in the United States. His work draws on his multilingual capabilities and international legal training across multiple jurisdictions.

=== Writing and political analysis ===

Basire writes articles and political analysis for media and academic outlets. His research focuses on Iranian geopolitics, nuclear nonproliferation, constitutional reform, and Iran-Israel relations. He was notably the first political analyst in media to compare Secretary of State Marco Rubio's leadership to that of Winston Churchill, a characterization he offered during a Fox News panel discussion.

== Advocacy and humanitarian work ==

Basire is an active member of the LGBT community and has advocated for LGBT rights, particularly within Middle Eastern and diaspora contexts. His visibility as an openly LGBT Iranian-American commentator places him at the intersection of identity, politics, and human rights in communities where these issues remain deeply contested. He has also worked with refugee populations, drawing on his multilingual abilities and personal experience within the Iranian diaspora.

=== Fight against antisemitism ===

In May 2026, Basire played a prominent public role in advocating for justice after an antisemitic attack near the Third Street Promenade in Santa Monica. On May 24, 2026, a man named Nay Min Tar allegedly stalked a Jewish couple who were wearing Star of David necklaces, threatened to kill them using antisemitic slurs, brandished a baseball bat from his car, and set his Italian mastiff on the male victim, who sustained dog bites. [ref: Man and his dog allegedly chase couple down Santa Monica street, CBS News Los Angeles] [ref: After Santa Monica attack, setting dog to bite Jewish victim, man charged but not with hate crime, The Jerusalem Post]

Basire, identified as a friend of the victims and a legal scholar, published video of the incident and spoke out in major media outlets. In an interview with the Jerusalem Post, he stated that Tar had targeted the couple specifically for their Star of David necklaces and followed them for nearly two blocks before attacking. He argued that the circumstances "clearly support a hate crime modifier" and expressed outrage that the Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office charged Tar with felony criminal threats and misdemeanor battery but declined to add a hate crime enhancement. In a report by CBS News Los Angeles, Basire was quoted describing the attacker's use of "antisemitic slogans and rhetoric."

The case drew widespread media attention, with coverage from the New York Post, [ref: Bat-wielding driver and dog terrorize shoppers in Santa Monica as city struggles to control crime crisis, New York Post] KTLA, and the City of Santa Monica, whose police chief stated that "hate has no place in Santa Monica."

== Academic publications ==

Basire has authored two policy research papers published on the Social Science Research Network (SSRN):

* Integrating Denuclearization and Energy Accessibility: Policy Frameworks for a Sustainable Transition (April 2025). Examines the intersection of global nuclear disarmament and sustainable energy access, proposing solutions for security dilemmas, proliferation risks, and energy poverty.
* Rekindling the Discussion About Nuclear Power Usage: How Implementing Robust Policies is Essential for Fulfilling Tomorrow's Energy Needs and Decreasing Oregon's [Carbon Emissions] (December 2024). Argues for reconsidering nuclear power in Oregon's clean energy strategy to meet its 2050 net zero target.

== Media appearances ==

Basire has appeared multiple times on Fox News as a guest panelist and commentator, and on RAI TG3 Mondo, Italian national television's international affairs program. Notable appearances include:

* Rubio-Churchill comparison (February 2026): During a Fox News @ Night panel reacting to Iran's foreign minister dismissing claims of high death tolls, Basire became the first political analyst in media to compare Secretary of State Marco Rubio's leadership to that of Winston Churchill.
* Iranians celebrate after Khamenei's death (March 2026): Discussed the emotional reaction of Iranians worldwide to the reported death of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in an airstrike, analyzing Iran's future trajectory. [ref: Iranians celebrate worldwide after supreme leader is killed in airstrike, Fox News Video]
* Operation Epic Fury panel (March 2026): Appeared on a Fox News @ Night panel analyzing Operation Epic Fury and its aftermath. [ref: Real question is if the objectives behind 'Operation Epic Fury' are in the best interest of the US, Fox News Video]
* RAI TG3 Mondo (14 March 2026): Featured on Italy's state-owned Rai 3 network's TG3 Mondo international affairs program. [ref: TG3 Mondo del 14/03/2026, Rai News]

Basire has also contributed analysis on European-American relations regarding Iran, arguing that Europe's failure to support U.S.-Israeli military operations against Iran's nuclear program undermines transatlantic alliance values. [ref: No more restraint: Europe must stand with America on Iran, Fox News Opinion]

* Santa Monica antisemitic attack (May 2026): Interviewed by CBS News Los Angeles and the Jerusalem Post as a legal scholar and advocate after a Jewish couple was attacked near the Third Street Promenade in Santa Monica. Basire published video of the incident and called for hate crime charges.

data.title: Brunel Medical School
data.text:
Brunel Medical School (BMS) is the medical school of Brunel University of London, a public research university in Uxbridge, west London, England. It offers a five-year Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) programme.

== History ==
Brunel Medical School was established as part of Brunel University of London's expansion into undergraduate medical education. Its MBBS programme began recruiting students for entry in 2022.

== Academic programmes ==
=== Undergraduate medicine ===
The school's principal programme is the five-year MBBS degree. The curriculum combines biomedical sciences, clinical skills, professional development and clinical placements.

== Teaching and learning ==
=== Team-based learning ===
Team-based learning is a principal teaching approach at the school. Students work in groups to apply medical knowledge and discuss clinical problems.

=== Clinical skills ===
Clinical and communication skills are incorporated throughout the programme, alongside simulation and supervised patient contact.

== Clinical training ==
Clinical placements take place in hospitals, general practices and community healthcare settings. The programme includes primary-care experiences and hospital-based clinical training.

== Facilities ==
Medical teaching takes place on Brunel University's campus, using anatomy teaching facilities, clinical skills laboratories and simulated hospital wards.

== Student support ==
The school operates a House system, with students allocated to one of five Houses.

== Accreditation and regulation ==
Medical education in the United Kingdom is regulated by the General Medical Council. The programme's current regulatory status should be verified against the latest published GMC and university information.

Carlos Jurado

Carlos Jurado is an American immigration attorney and the founder of The Jurado Firm. His practice focuses on family-based immigration, asylum, deportation defense, immigration waivers, and employment-related immigration matters. [ref: Meet Our Immigration Attorneys in Long Beach, The Jurado Firm]

Early life

Jurado was born in Los Angeles, California, to Mexican immigrant parents. His mother worked in a factory, and his father was a mariachi musician. He grew up in South Central Los Angeles, Long Beach, and Compton.

Jurado has described his family’s experiences with immigration and the passage of California’s Proposition 187 during his childhood as influences on his decision to pursue a legal career. He recalled the fear and uncertainty the measure created among his family and neighbors.

Education

Jurado earned an undergraduate degree in rhetoric from the University of California, Berkeley. He subsequently worked as a staff member in the United States House of Representatives in Washington, D.C.

He earned his law degree from the University of California, Hastings College of the Law. During his legal studies, he participated in community legal clinics serving small businesses, nonprofit organizations, and immigrant families.

Jurado also participated in a training program at Yale Law School’s Center for Community and Economic Development, where he provided legal assistance to mission-driven organizations.

Legal career

Jurado founded The Jurado Firm, an immigration law practice serving individuals, families, and employers. He is licensed to practice law in Michigan. [ref: Carlos Jurado, State Bar of Michigan Attorney Directory]

His practice includes family petitions, immigration waivers, asylum applications, deportation defense, and employment visas. He also represents artists, musicians, and athletes in immigration matters.

Selected cases

Carlitos Ricardo Parias

Jurado represented Carlitos Ricardo Parias, a Los Angeles citizen journalist known online as “Richard LA” and “Richard Noticias LA.” Parias was shot and wounded by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer during an attempted arrest on October 21, 2025. The U.S. Press Freedom Tracker identified Jurado as Parias’s attorney and reported his statements concerning the government’s treatment of his client. [ref: Journalist shot by federal agents in LA, taken into ICE custody]

José Mejía Hernández

Jurado also represented José Mejía Hernández, a Mexican immigrant who alleged that ICE officers seriously injured him during an encounter in Arlington, Virginia, on August 11, 2026. Working alongside civil rights attorney Denisse Gastélum, Jurado sought a criminal investigation into the incident. On August 28, Hernández appeared at Arlington County Police headquarters to report the alleged assault. His attorneys requested an investigation and preservation of evidence. The Department of Homeland Security disputed key elements of their account. data.title: Netchex
data.text:
Netchex is an American human capital management and payroll software company headquartered in Covington, Louisiana. Founded in 2003 in Mandeville, Louisiana, by Will Boudreaux and Stuart Ethridge, the company provides cloud-based payroll processing, human resources administration, benefits management, time and attendance tracking, and recruiting services, primarily to employers with hourly and frontline workforces.

The company operated without outside investment until 2016, when it received a growth investment from Primus Capital. In June 2023, Netchex was acquired by the New York–based private equity firm GrowthCurve Capital, at which point it reported annual revenue of more than US$50 million, over 6,400 clients, and approximately 340 employees.

== History ==

=== Founding and early years ===
Boudreaux and Ethridge were roommates at Louisiana State University and later worked together for about twelve years in payroll and financial outsourcing at ADP. Following the collapse of the dot-com bubble, they founded Netchex in Mandeville in 2003 to offer payroll services over the web, financing the business with personal savings and a loan from the U.S. Small Business Administration. Boudreaux later said the two spent the early years "knocking on doors" along the Gulf Coast and bootstrapped the company for its first thirteen years before taking outside capital.

The company recorded first-year sales of between $600,000 and $700,000 against an initial target of $250,000. It concentrated on mid-market employers in sectors with large hourly workforces—restaurants, hotels, retailers, healthcare practices and automotive dealerships—which the founders considered underserved by payroll providers designed for corporate finance departments.

Netchex appeared on the Inc. 5000 list of fast-growing private companies in 2010 and 2016, and was included in the inaugural NOLA100 list in 2015 and in several editions of the LSU 100 list of fastest-growing businesses led by LSU graduates.

=== Louisiana expansion ===
In June 2015, Louisiana Governor Bobby Jindal and Boudreaux announced a US$5.3 million expansion of the company's headquarters, supported by an incentive package from Louisiana Economic Development. The plan called for leasing 30,000 square feet of office space, retaining 86 existing jobs and creating 240 new positions at an average salary of $43,800 in St. Tammany Parish. Louisiana was selected over competing sites in Texas and Florida.

At the time, Netchex employed about 120 people, served more than 3,000 clients, and maintained offices in Dallas, Atlanta and Jackson, Mississippi. By 2016 the company reported annual revenue of about $14 million and 115 employees. The expansion took the company from its original offices on North Causeway Boulevard in Mandeville to a larger facility on U.S. Highway 190 in Covington, which remains its headquarters.

=== Primus Capital investment ===
In March 2016, Primus Capital, a private equity firm based in Cleveland, made a growth investment in Netchex for an undisclosed amount. The company then served more than 2,500 employers, concentrated in the southeastern United States.

=== Acquisition by GrowthCurve Capital ===
In June 2023, GrowthCurve Capital acquired a majority stake in Netchex from Primus Capital. Terms were not disclosed. Netchex reported annual revenue exceeding $50 million, more than 6,400 clients and approximately 340 employees, of whom about 200 worked at the Covington office. Boudreaux and Ethridge each retained an ownership stake and remained in executive roles.

=== Leadership ===
In September 2024, Boudreaux stepped down as chief executive after twenty-one years and joined the company's board of directors. He was succeeded by David Giannetto, previously chief executive of WorkWave. According to the company, Abhinav Agrawal, who had joined Netchex in 2023 as chief product and technology officer, became chief executive officer in 2025.

As of 2025 the company employed about 375 people, roughly 200 of them in the New Orleans metropolitan area, and reported serving more than 7,300 customers across all fifty states.

=== Mesh.ai acquisition and AI products ===
In 2025, Netchex acquired Mesh.ai, a Y Combinator-backed startup founded in 2020 that developed artificial-intelligence tools for performance management and employee engagement. Mesh.ai co-founder Saurabh Nangia joined Netchex as chief product officer.

In July 2026, Netchex launched Mesh, a set of six artificial intelligence assistants built on that technology and aimed at employers with deskless workforces. The company said the assistants identify issues such as missing timecards, expiring certifications and payroll discrepancies, that human approval is required before sensitive actions are completed, and that employees can access the platform through ChatGPT and Claude.

== Products and services ==
Netchex provides a cloud-based platform covering payroll processing and tax filing, human resources administration, benefits enrollment and Affordable Care Act reporting, time and attendance tracking, recruiting and onboarding, learning and performance management, and reporting and analytics. The company holds Nacha certification for ACH payment processing.

The company markets primarily to employers with large hourly or frontline workforces in hospitality, retail, healthcare and automotive retail. In October 2024, Netchex announced an integration with the hotel management software provider Inn-Flow, intended to connect labor-cost accounting with payroll data for hotel operators.
