data.title: Wolfgang Vogt
data.text:
Wolfgang Vogt (1 December 1929 – 12 December 2006) was a German economist, journalist and politician of the Christian Democratic Union (CDU). He was a member of the Bundestag from 1969 to 1998, representing the Düren constituency by direct mandate from 1972 to 1994 and North Rhine-Westphalia via the state list in his other terms. He was mayor of Düren from 1972 to 1983 and Parliamentary State Secretary at the Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs under Norbert Blüm from 1982 to 1991. From 1975 to 1995 he chaired the Christian Democratic Employees' Association (CDA) at state level in North Rhine-Westphalia.

== Early life and education ==

Vogt was born in Schirgiswalde in the Bautzen district of Saxony. He joined the CDU in the Soviet occupation zone and, after completing his Abitur in 1949, worked for the party in Bautzen until he fled to West Berlin in 1950. He studied economics and social sciences at the University of Cologne, graduating as a Diplom-Volkswirt in 1956, and worked as a research assistant at the university's sociology seminar until 1959.

== Early career ==

Vogt was an education officer for the Katholische Arbeitnehmer-Bewegung (KAB), the Catholic workers' movement, and a lecturer at the Katholisch-Soziales Institut in Bad Honnef. In 1959 he became editor-in-chief of the Ketteler-Wacht, the KAB's weekly newspaper. He belonged to the trade union IG Bau-Steine-Erden and was vice-president of the Arbeitsgemeinschaft der Verbraucherverbände (AgV), the umbrella organisation of West German consumer associations. He moved to Düren in 1970.

== Political career ==

=== Local politics ===

After the death of Oberbürgermeister Heinz Kotthaus in March 1972, Vogt was elected to the Düren town council on 23 April 1972 and chosen as Oberbürgermeister on 9 May. He was re-elected in 1975 and 1979. During his tenure the title of the office was changed to Bürgermeister, after a 1975 decree by the state interior minister restricted the title Oberbürgermeister to independent cities; the town amended its charter in 1977. Vogt resigned as mayor on 13 December 1983 and was succeeded by Hans Becker. He was again a member of the town council from 1984 to 1989.

=== Member of the Bundestag ===

Vogt was elected to the Bundestag in the 1969 federal election on the CDU's North Rhine-Westphalia state list and won the Düren constituency directly from 1972 to 1990. Before the 1994 election he faced a rival candidate within the party; Thomas Rachel won the Düren seat for the CDU, and Vogt returned via the state list. He left the Bundestag in 1998 after eight terms.

In May 1971 he asked the Brandt government in question time whether the price target in its annual economic report could be met, and about a forecast of the cost-of-living index by the consumer associations. His main field was social policy. In 1982 he opposed cuts to housing benefit proposed by Gerhard Stoltenberg, arguing that housing benefit could not be reduced if the party accepted rising rents to encourage housebuilding. He chaired the employees' group (Arbeitnehmergruppe) of the CDU/CSU parliamentary group. In August 1996 he proposed a tiered value-added tax, with a rate of 20 per cent on luxury goods, a general rate of 17 per cent, and 7 per cent on food and cultural goods.

In his last term he was a member of the Committee on Labour and Social Affairs, the Committee on Economic Cooperation and Development, and the Mediation Committee, and a deputy member of the Health Committee.

=== Parliamentary State Secretary ===

Vogt was Parliamentary State Secretary at the Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs under Minister Norbert Blüm in the government of Chancellor Helmut Kohl from October 1982 to 24 January 1991. He left office when a new cabinet was formed after the 1990 German federal election. In November 1982 he said that a supplementary income tax, which the trade unions and the Social Democrats had demanded, was politically spent for the new coalition; the coalition introduced a repayable compulsory loan, the investment aid levy, instead. He remained mayor of Düren until December 1983.

In 1984 Vogt was one of twenty serving and three former members of the Bundestag investigated by tax investigators and prosecutors on suspicion of aiding tax evasion in connection with donations to political parties, as part of the party donations affair. The proceedings against him were discontinued in 1988 for lack of sufficient suspicion.

=== Christian Democratic Employees' Association ===

From 1975 Vogt chaired the CDA's Rhineland association and, after its merger with the Westphalian association, the CDA in North Rhine-Westphalia, until 1995. He was a member of the CDU's state executive, first in the Rhineland and later in North Rhine-Westphalia.

After the CDU's defeat in the 1980 state election, he rejected the view of the CSU leader and chancellor candidate Franz Josef Strauß that the state party's campaign had caused the loss. In 1981, as treasurer of the CDA under Blüm, he supported a Bundestag resolution calling on the government to secure codetermination in the coal and steel industry. In 1985, during the debate on merging the Rhineland and Westphalian CDU associations, he opposed Kurt Biedenkopf.

By 1987 Vogt was a deputy federal chairman of the CDA. When Blüm stepped down as federal chairman that year, Vogt did not stand for the post, as his government office bound him to cabinet discipline; Heinz Soenius was chosen instead.

In January 1993, during the negotiations on the Solidarity Pact to finance reconstruction in eastern Germany, he published a position paper opposing further cuts in social benefits. He argued that the share of national income going to employees had fallen from 76.9 to 70.8 per cent between 1982 and 1991, and that a proposed three per cent cut in social assistance would be unconstitutional. He proposed reducing contributions to the Federal Labour Office (now the Federal Employment Agency) by two percentage points, financed by a temporary surcharge on income and corporation tax.

He helped establish the Stiftung Christlich-Soziale Politik and its conference centre, the Arbeitnehmer-Zentrum Königswinter, which opened in Königswinter in 1986. The CDA in North Rhine-Westphalia later made him its honorary chairman.

== Personal life and death ==

Vogt was a Catholic, was married and had two children. He died in Düren on 12 December 2006, aged 77, after a long illness. His memoirs, Bohrer und Brett, edited by Karl-Albert Eßer, were published in 2007.

== Honours ==

* Commander's Cross of the Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany
* Heinrich Brauns Prize of the Diocese of Essen (1998)
* Ring of Honour of the town of Düren (2004)

== Selected works ==

* Der Staat in der Soziallehre der Kirche, Pattloch
* Geschichte wiederholt sich nicht, Geschichten schon – Ein Querdenker erinnert sich, Soziale Ordnung
* Bohrer und Brett: Erinnern und Reflektieren, Porschen & Bergsch

data.title: The Story of Birds
data.text:
The Story of Birds: A New History from Their Dinosaur Origins to the Present is a 2026 popular science book by American paleontologist Steve Brusatte. It presents a chronological account of the evolution of birds, from their origins among theropod dinosaurs to the diversity of living birds. [ref: The Story of Birds: An Evolutionary History of the Dinosaurs that Live Among Us, British Trust for Ornithology]

The book was published in the United States by Mariner Books on April 28, 2026. [ref: The Story of Birds, HarperCollins] A British edition was published by Picador on June 11, 2026, under the subtitle An Evolutionary History of the Dinosaurs That Live Among Us. [ref: The Story of Birds, Pan Macmillan]

==Background and writing==
Brusatte wrote The Story of Birds over several years alongside his work as a university teacher, laboratory manager, student supervisor and grant writer. In the acknowledgements, he described fitting the project around his professional and family responsibilities. His wife, Anne, a children's author and former teacher, read the complete manuscript and suggested revisions intended to make it more accessible to a general readership. [ref: The Story of Birds: A New History from Their Dinosaur Origins to the Present, Mariner Books]

Members of Brusatte's palaeontology group at the University of Edinburgh read portions or complete drafts of the book during weekly meetings, while students in his third-year palaeontology and sedimentology course commented on its opening chapters. Palaeontologist Daniel Field and members of his Cambridge research group read the complete manuscript and assisted with fact-checking its treatment of bird classification, anatomy and behaviour. Researchers associated with the "Deep Time Cognition" project reviewed the material concerning avian brains, neurons and cognition.

==Publication==
The American hardcover edition contains 448 pages and was published with the subtitle A New History from Their Dinosaur Origins to the Present. The British hardcover edition, also 448 pages, was published by Picador with a different subtitle.

An audiobook narrated by Patrick Lawlor was released by Harper Audio on April 28, 2026. [ref: The Story of Birds, Kirkus Reviews]

The first edition is illustrated throughout in black and white, combining drawings, photographs and diagrams. It contains illustrations by Cordula Marks Venters, Sarah Shelley and Todd Marshall, and photographs credited to palaeontologist Daniel Field. [ref: The Story of Birds: A New History from Their Dinosaur Origins to the Present, Mariner Books] Marshall also created the book's cover artwork. The front matter includes a chronological timeline of bird evolution and a simplified phylogenetic tree showing the principal relationships between dinosaurs, early birds and the major groups of living birds. [ref: The Story of Birds: A New History from Their Dinosaur Origins to the Present, Mariner Books]

==Contents==
The book is structured as a chronological history of birds and their ancestors. The main text comprises a prologue, nine numbered chapters and an epilogue. A timeline of bird evolution and a bird family tree precede the prologue, while notes on sources and an index follow the epilogue. [ref: The Story of Birds: A New History from Their Dinosaur Origins to the Present, Mariner Books]
[[File:Dinornis1387.jpg|thumb|right|upright=0.7|Richard Owen beside a reconstructed moa skeleton in 1879. The photograph is reproduced in chapter 7, which discusses birds that lost the ability to fly.]]

The first four chapters trace the evolutionary origin of birds among theropod dinosaurs and the gradual development of characteristics associated with birds. These include small body size, feathers, wings, eggs, flight, changes to the digestive system, adaptations for living in trees, beaks, rapid growth, endothermy and bird sounds. [ref: The Story of Birds: A New History from Their Dinosaur Origins to the Present, Mariner Books]

Chapters five to seven examine the survival of some bird lineages during the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event, the establishment and subsequent diversification of the modern bird family tree, and the repeated loss of flight in groups including ratites and penguins.

Chapter eight surveys extinct groups and species including terror birds, dromornithids, giant seabirds, the dodo, the passenger pigeon and the great auk. Chapter nine discusses bird intelligence, cognition, tool use, birdsong and continuing evolution among living species.

The epilogue turns to the human-driven decline of bird populations, discussing threats including habitat destruction, pesticides, invasive species, climate change, domestic cats and collisions with glass. It concludes on a cautiously optimistic note, emphasizing birds' evolutionary adaptability and resilience.

==Reception==
James Heywood, reviewing the book for the British Trust for Ornithology, gave it a highly positive assessment. He described Brusatte as one of the foremost palaeontologists working in the United Kingdom and praised his ability to make the subject exciting and engaging, as well as the book's engagement with recent research and its extensive notes. Heywood's only reservation concerned the illustrations: he suggested that additional phylogenetic diagrams and colour plates would have been useful, while noting that the book followed the same general approach as Brusatte's two preceding works.

A review in The New Yorker highlighted Brusatte's use of narrative vignettes alongside accounts of fossil discoveries, describing the book as combining scientific precision with enthusiasm for birds and their evolution. [ref: Briefly Noted, The New Yorker]

Kirkus Reviews, reviewing the audiobook edition, praised Patrick Lawlor's narration and the book's explanations of flight, adaptation and the relationship between birds and dinosaurs.

The book reached number ten on The New York Times hardcover nonfiction bestseller list for the week ending May 2, 2026.

==Press coverage==
In a pre-publication review and feature for The Guardian, science correspondent Nicola Davis discussed the book's account of bird evolution and its use of research on living birds to investigate the cognition and behaviour of extinct dinosaurs. She highlighted several of the animals covered in the book, including Archaeopteryx, dromornithids, the dodo and the hoatzin. Davis also noted Brusatte's concern about contemporary threats to birds, while presenting the book's conclusion as ultimately optimistic about their adaptability and evolutionary resilience. [ref: Scientists believe birds' skulls hold clues to inner lives of long-extinct dinosaurs, The Guardian]

==See also==
* The Rise and Fall of the Dinosaurs (2018)
* The Rise and Reign of the Mammals (2022)

data.title: Abuqatrania
data.text:
Abuqatrania is an extinct genus of parapithecid primates known from the Paleogene of North Africa. It was established in 2001 by Elwyn L. Simons, Erik R. Seiffert, Prithijit S. Chatrath and Yousry Attia for the type species Abuqatrania basiodontos, based on fossils from the late Eocene of the Fayum Depression in Egypt. [ref: Earliest record of a parapithecid anthropoid from the Jebel Qatrani Formation, northern Egypt, Folia Primatologica]

Its taxonomic status has been debated, as some authors have treated it as a synonym of the related genus Qatrania. [ref: A Companion to Paleoanthropology, Wiley-Blackwell] In 2024, isolated teeth from the earliest Oligocene of southern Morocco were tentatively referred to Abuqatrania cf. basiodontos.

== Discovery and occurrence ==

The original fossils of Abuqatrania basiodontos came from Quarry L-41 in the Jebel Qatrani Formation of the Fayum Depression, northern Egypt. The species was described as a late Eocene anthropoid and provided evidence for the presence of Parapithecidae in the oldest productive vertebrate-bearing deposits of the formation.

A second, tentative occurrence was reported in 2024 from the Samlat Formation in the Dakhla region of southern Morocco, near the northern border of Mauritania. The material comes from locality DAK C2, in the uppermost part of the formation along the Atlantic margin of the Rio de Oro, east of the Dakhla peninsula. The fossil-bearing deposits date to the earliest Oligocene, approximately 33.5 million years ago. The specimens were recovered from estuarine sediments using wet-screening techniques. [ref: A new primate community from the earliest Oligocene of the Atlantic margin of Northwest Africa: Systematic, paleobiogeographic, and paleoenvironmental implications, Journal of Human Evolution]

== Description ==

The original description characterized Abuqatrania basiodontos as a parapithecid with no clear autapomorphies, or derived characteristics exclusive to the species. Its most parsimonious phylogenetic interpretation placed it as the sister taxon of a clade containing Qatrania, Parapithecus and Apidium.

Body mass estimates for specimens tentatively assigned to Abuqatrania cf. basiodontos range from approximately 371 to 561 grams. These estimates were calculated from the dimensions of an isolated first lower molar and an isolated third lower molar from the earliest Oligocene of Morocco. This mass range is similar to that of New World Monkeys of the genus Callithrix. [ref: Quantitative assessment of grasping strength in platyrrhine monkeys, American Journal of Biological Anthropology]

The Moroccan material referred to Abuqatrania cf. basiodontos consists of isolated teeth rather than an associated skeleton. The published specimen records include a lower canine, lower molars, an upper molar identified as either the first or second molar, a lower incisor tentatively identified as either the first or second incisor, two lower second premolars and an upper third molar. Some of the teeth are worn, corroded or broken. [ref: 3D models related to the publication: A new primate community from the earliest Oligocene of the Atlantic margin of Northwest Africa: Systematic, paleobiogeographic and paleoenvironmental implications, MorphoMuseuM]

== Taxonomic history ==

Simons and colleagues established Abuqatrania as a distinct genus in 2001. They interpreted A. basiodontos as closely related to other early parapithecids, particularly a clade containing Qatrania, Parapithecus and Apidium.

In their review of Paleogene anthropoids, Seiffert and colleagues (2010) recognized Abuqatrania separately from Qatrania. They also discussed the possibility that Abuqatrania basiodontos was close to the ancestry of other parapithecids, noting that its fossils were approximately one million years older than those of Qatrania wingi. [ref: Cenozoic Mammals of Africa, University of California Press]

The distinction between Abuqatrania and Qatrania was not accepted by all authors. In 2013, K. Christopher Beard treated Abuqatrania as a synonym of Qatrania, using the combination Qatrania basiodontos for the species. Under this classification, the species belongs to the same genus as Qatrania wingi and Qatrania fleaglei.

The name has continued to be used in subsequent scientific literature. Marivaux and colleagues (2024), for example, tentatively assigned the Moroccan material to Abuqatrania cf. basiodontos.

== Paleobiogeography ==

The Moroccan locality DAK C2 preserves a diverse primate community from the Eocene–Oligocene transition. Marivaux and colleagues identified at least eight primate species, including anthropoids assigned to Oligopithecidae, Propliopithecidae, Parapithecidae and Afrotarsiidae, as well as several strepsirrhine groups.

Comparisons between the primates and rodents from Dakhla and those from the Jebel Qatrani Formation in Egypt led the authors to propose that an east–west environmental connection existed across North Africa during the latest Eocene and earliest Oligocene. They also suggested that tropical habitats along the northwestern margin of Africa may have acted as refuges during the cooling associated with the Eocene–Oligocene transition. These interpretations concern the broader fossil assemblage and its environment, rather than Abuqatrania alone.

== See also ==

* Qatrania
* Parapithecidae

data.title: Arshad Pappu
data.text:
Arshad Pappu (c. 1972 – 16 March 2013) was a Pakistani underworld figure and gang leader based in Lyari, Karachi. [ref: Lyari 'gangster' Arshad Pappu, brother killed, [[Dawn (newspaper)] He led an influential criminal syndicate during the Lyari gang war, clashing primarily with factions led by Rehman Dakait and Uzair Baloch. [ref: Tortured to death: Gangster Arshad Pappu's body found in Lyari, The Express Tribune]

== Early life and background ==
Arshad Pappu was the son of Haji Lal Mohammad (known as Haji Laloo), a prominent drug dealer in Lyari. His brother was Yasir Arafat. Through family marriages, Pappu was connected to rival gang leader Rehman Dakait, as Dakait and Pappu's brother Arafat were married to sisters. [ref: Special report: Lords of misrule, [[Dawn (newspaper)]

== Criminal activities and gang war ==
During the 1990s, Pappu and Rehman Dakait operated together in Lyari before having a violent falling out over ransom money from an abduction. Following the split, Pappu established an independent syndicate.

A major turning point in the Lyari gang war occurred when Pappu was implicated in the kidnapping and murder of Faiz Mohammad (known as "Mama Faizu"), a local transporter and father of Uzair Baloch. After his father's death, Uzair Baloch allied with Rehman Dakait to launch a protracted feud against Pappu's faction.

Pappu was booked by police in over 50 criminal cases involving homicide, extortion, and narcotics. [ref: Uzair Baloch indicted in Arshad Pappu murder case, [[Dawn (newspaper)] He was imprisoned for five years in Karachi and the Gadani prison in Balochistan. Due to a lack of testifying witnesses, he was acquitted in all cases—including the murder of Faiz Mohammad—and released in early 2012. Following his release, he operated between Karachi and border areas of Balochistan.

== Death ==
On the night of 16 March 2013, Pappu, his brother Yasir Arafat, and an associate named Juma Shera (alias Shera Pathan) visited a flat in the Defence Housing Authority (DHA), where they were abducted by armed men. [ref: Key figure in Arshad Pappu's murder killed, The Express Tribune]

They were transported to Lyari, where all three were tortured and killed. [ref: Arshad Pappu murder: Police ordered to seize Uzair Baloch's properties within 10 days, The Express Tribune] Following orders from the Supreme Court of Pakistan, police registered a triple-murder case that indicted Uzair Baloch, Noor Muhammad (alias Baba Ladla), and several police personnel.

== In popular culture ==

* In Aditya Dhar's 2025 Hindi spy thriller film Dhurandhar, Arshad Pappu was portrayed by actor Ashwin Dhar. [ref: Ashwin Dhar on Arshad Pappu's viral 'football' scene in Dhurandhar, India TV]

== References ==

data.title: Limington-Harmon Airport
data.text:
----

Limington-Harmon Airport (IATA: none; ICAO: none; FAA LID: 63B) is a privately-owned, public-use general aviation airport located 3 miles (2.6 nautical miles (4.8 kilometers)) north of the center of Limington, a town in York County, Maine, United States. It is owned by Starkweather Airport Authority, LLC and managed by Kyle Starkweather, both based in Rochester, New Hampshire. [ref: LIMINGTON-HARMON, FAA] [ref: AirNav: 63B - Limington-Harmon Airport, AirNav] [ref: Limington-Harmon Airport, Limington-Harmon Airport]

== Facilities ==
Limington-Harmon Airport is located at an elevation of 292.3 feet (89.1 meters) above mean sea level. It has one asphalt paved runway in poor condition (severely cracked, shallow potholes, and loose aggregate on the runway) designated 11/29 (true alignment of 93° for Runway 11 and 273° for Runway 29), which measures 2,973 feet long by 50 feet wide (906 x 15 meters). The airport has a left traffic pattern, has basic markings in poor condition, and no lights or instrument landing system (ILS). The airport has no air traffic control (ATC) tower. [ref: AirNav: 63B - Limington Harmon Airport, AirNav] [ref: LIMINGTON-HARMON, FAA] [ref: 63B - Limington [Limington-Harmon Airport], ME, US - Airport - Great Circle Mapper, Great Circle Mapper]
== Accidents and incidents ==
* On August 30, 2013, a 56-year-old four-seat Cessna aircraft (built in 1957) crashed while attempting to take off from Runway 29 at around 1:40 PM. Witnesses reported hearing loud noises just before the plane crashed. The pilot and only person on board, 58-year-old Anthony Longley from Naples, was killed in the crash. The crash caused a fuel leak that had to be cleaned up by a hazardous-materials crew. [ref: 1 killed in Limington plane crash - WMTW, WMTW] [ref: Limington reacts to fatal plane crash, WMTW]
* On July 12, 2014, a Culver LFA took off at around 4:45 PM headed for Twitchell Airport in Turner. According to witnesses, the plane stalled and crashed into trees, reporting that they heard the engine sputter and then regain power before the crash, that the aircraft waas lower than usual at the end of the runway, and banked sharply to the left and went down after takeoff. The wreckage of the plane was located around 200 yards from the runway. 52-year-old Clarke Tate from Gray, the pilot and only person on board, was killed in the crash. [ref: Pilot identified in Limington plane crash - WMTW, WMTW] [ref: Preliminary report issued in fatal Limington plane crash - WMTW, WMTW] [ref: Photos: Limington plane crash - WMTW, WMTW]
* On April 14, 2019, a gust of wind caused a small plane to crash after landing. According to officials, the pilot was uninjured. [ref: Wind causes plane to crash after landing, officials say - WMTW, WMTW]
* On November 16, 2023 at around 12:30 PM, a small yellow plane crashed nose-first into a wooded area less than a mile west of the airport after experiencing an engine failure shortly after takeoff. The pilot and only person on board, 62-year-old Bradley Marston of Windham, survived with only minor injuries and was treated at a local hospital. [ref: Minor injuries reported after small plane crashes in Limington - WMTW, WMTW]

data.title: Olivia Liang
data.text:
Olivia Faith Liang (born May 11, [ref: ] 1993) [ref: Kung Fu's Olivia Liang on Reclaiming the Martial-Arts Stereotype, Popsugar] is an American actress. She is known for her roles as Alyssa Chang in the television series Legacies [ref: Legacies Recap: Another Saltzman Birthday Ends In Death And Betrayal, TVLine] and Nicky Shen in Kung Fu. [ref: ‘Kung Fu’: Olivia Liang Cast As The Lead Of the CW Reboot Pilot, Deadline] Liang has also appeared in television series including Grey's Anatomy, Into the Dark, and One Day at a Time.

== Life and career ==
Olivia Faith Liang was born on 11 May 1993, She grew up in Diamond Bar, California. [ref: Olivia Liang Is the Role Model She Wishes She Had, Cero Magazine] Liang became interested in acting at a young age and also trained in dance. [ref: Olivia Liang On How The 'Kung Fu' Reboot Rewrites The Show's Problematic Legacy, Bustle] She studied ballet, jazz and hip-hop and later described dance as her first form of storytelling. [ref: 'Kung Fu's' Olivia Liang Says She Struggled With Anorexia As A Young Dancer, Women's Health]

She attended the University of California, San Diego, where she studied communications. [ref: Heroic Hugs, Television Academy] [ref: Olivia Liang, The CW] After graduating, she attended an acting program at the University of California, Los Angeles.

Liang began her television career with guest roles, including appearances in One Day at a Time and Grey's Anatomy. [ref: Kung Fu: Gender-Flipped CW Reboot Adds Legacies Actress In Lead Role, TVLine] In 2017, she was selected for the ABC Discovers Talent Showcase. Thereafter, she appeared in Hulu's Into the Dark and The CW's Legacies. [ref: Meet Olivia Liang, star of CW’s new Kung Fu reboot, South China Morning Post] [ref: Interview: Olivia Liang Talks Into The Dark: Crawlers (Exclusive)]

In 2020, she was cast in The CW's Kung Fu. [ref: 'Kung Fu' Star Olivia Liang is Fighting on Her Own Terms – The Nerds of Color] [ref: ‘Kung Fu’: Olivia Liang Cast As The Lead Of the CW Reboot Pilot, Deadline] After more than 150 actresses auditioned for the role. At the time, she was appearing as Alyssa Chang on Legacies. [ref: ‘Kung Fu’ Rights the Wrongs of Its Ancestor, The New York Times] [ref: Legacies season 2 star lands lead role in The CW's Kung Fu, Digital Spy] Liang had not studied martial arts before being cast in Kung Fu. After being cast as Nicky Shen, she began training for the role. [ref: Why Kung Fu's Olivia Liang Was "Anti-Learning Martial Arts" Before Landing Her Role, E! Online] The series premiered in April 2021 and ran for three seasons, ending in 2023. [ref: ‘Kung Fu’ Star Olivia Liang Bids Show Farewell In Emotional Instagram Post, Deadline] In May 2021, Liang appeared on The Kelly Clarkson Show to promote Kung Fu. [ref: Olivia Liang to Appear on ‘The Kelly Clarkson Show’, Nerds and Beyond]

In 2023, Liang joined the cast of Paper Flowers, an independent film directed by Karan Soni. [ref: Kapil Talwalkar, Olivia Liang, Karan Soni & Tom Everett Scott Join Inspirational Indie ‘Paper Flowers’ Based On Viral HuffPost Article, Deadline]

== Personal life ==
Liang has spoken about having anorexia as a teenager. She said that her experience with dance contributed to the pressure she felt about her body and appearance. She later discussed the experience in an interview with Women's Health.

data.title: Ol' Lonely
data.text:
----

Ol' Lonely, or "the lonely repairman", is a character in Maytag advertisements, created in 1967 by copywriter Vincent R. Vassolo of the Leo Burnett advertising agency for Maytag.

==History==
His character was initially played by Jesse White, who retained the role until 1988. [ref: North, Gary, What To Learn From Maytag, LewRockwell.com (2007)] [ref: [http://brandculturetalk.com/2009/01/09/maytags-brand-blunder-a-focus-group-of-one/ Early Maytag Repairman TV Commercial] Maytag's Brand Blunder, BrandCultureTalk.com, 9 January 2009]

In a time in which the laundry appliances of major manufacturers had reached maturity, differing mostly in minor details, the campaign was designed to remind consumers of the perceived added value in Maytag products derived from the brand's reputation for dependability. Maytag advertisements stated “Ol' Lonely’s predicament is testimony to the durability and reliability of Maytag appliances. Now if only he had something to do with his days.” Other ads stated, "Not all Maytag repairmen are this lonely, but we're trying." The campaign proved a huge success, allowing Maytag to set a substantial price premium, as well as strongly influencing consumer preference at the higher end of the laundry appliance market. [ref: Maytag's Brand Blunder, BrandCultureTalk.com, 9 January 2009]

In 1986, the repairman was joined by Newton, a Basset Hound named for Maytag's headquarters in Newton, Iowa. In 1989, after Jesse White retired from acting in 1988, character actor Gordon Jump first appeared as Ol' Lonely in the advertisement "Biker". [ref: Advertising: Been Lonely Too Long, Time] In total, Jump appeared in more than 77 Maytag commercials and print advertisements. He made appearances at events for employees and customers and also was actively involved in several philanthropic and charitable causes.

In January 2001, Maytag shifted the direction of its iconic "Ol' Lonely" campaign by hiring actor Mark Devine (which played the younger repairman known as the "Maytag Apprentice" from 2001 to 2007), while actor Gordon Jump continued playing the iconic senior repairman. [ref: The long-suffering and lonely Maytag repairman will get a new repairman, The New York Times]

Actor Hardy Rawls was hired to play Ol' Lonely after Jump's retirement in July 2003, although he appeared only in print advertising and personal appearances. [ref: Jump Retires as Maytag's 'Lonely' Repairman, ADWEEK] [ref: HE'S THE NEW MAYTAG MAN, New York Post] Gordon Jump died two months later on September 22, 2003. [ref: Gordon Jump, 71, 'WKRP' Actor Who Played Maytag's Repairman, The New York Times] [ref: [http://www.maytag.com/GJbiography.htm] ] In French-speaking Quebec, Ol' Lonely was played by Paul Berval. [ref: Paul Berval – Artisans — Emissions.ca, Archives.emissions.ca] However, in 2005 Maytag cancelled his contract. Maytag also elected not to renew Rawls' contract, instead holding open auditions. Indianapolis Colts backup quarterback Jim Sorgi was among those who auditioned. [ref: Maytag Casting for New 'Ol Lonely, The Washington Post] On April 2, 2007, Maytag announced that Clay Earl Jackson of Richmond, Virginia had been selected to fill the role of Ol' Lonely. [ref: Maytag Introduces New "Lonely" Repairman, CBS News] [ref: A Winning Audition for Maytag Repairman, The New York Times] [ref: Virginia man beats out 1500 for role of Maytag repairman, Sarasota Herald-Tribune]

By the end of the twentieth century, the "Maytag repairman" character had become an iconic metaphor for a professional whose services are rarely needed. Times were changing however, and events at Maytag and within the industry began to diminish the effectiveness of the long-lived Maytag repairman campaign. Consumer demand for innovative, expensive, and increasingly complex electronically controlled and computerized appliances, coupled with higher labor costs and complaints over Maytag product quality and service, influenced a decline in Maytag sales and profit margins. By 2004, the Maytag repairman character had become to some consumers a symbol of misplaced trust in aging marketing campaigns. [ref: Maytag's Brand Blunder (a focus group of one), Brand Culture Company] [ref: Rob Frankel – Branding Expert: The Maytag Repairman Gets Even Lonelier, Robfrankel.blogspot.com] As one commentator noted, "Unfortunately things change, and, after some major quality hiccups, now it's the Maytag salesman who is bemoaning his loneliness. Maytag's reputation has plunged to the bottom with costly consumer class action lawsuits and numerous quality complaints." [ref: Continental Quality Engineering, "The High Cost of Low Quality"; Anderson IA: The Continental Quality Newsletter] As a partial result of Maytag's quality problems, the company reported a loss of $9 million in 2004, according to Industry Week.

In January 2014, Maytag announced a "Generation Five" of the Maytag Repairman, currently played by Colin Ferguson. [ref: Maytag Ads Ditch That Old, Bored Repairman for a Younger Model, Business Week] But instead of commercials showing the repairman waiting around his shop for a Maytag appliance to break, he is playing the part of the actual appliance.

In March 2023, the Maytag Repairman made a highly publicized return from a multi-year hiatus. Colin Ferguson appeared live and in uniform at the BrandSource Summit 2023 in Las Vegas. At the event, Whirlpool hosted a kitchen-vignette photo booth where retail members could take pictures with him. [ref: He's Back! Maytag Man Makes Live Appearance, YourSource News]

John Newsham of Chadshunt, Warwickshire (15 April 1673 – 21 November 1724) was an English politician. He sat as MP for Lostwithiel from 25 June 1720 till 1722. [ref: NEWSHAM, John (1673-1724), of Chadshunt, Warws., History of Parliament Online]

He was the first surviving son of Charles Newsham (died 1705) of Chadshunt by Elizabeth, the daughter and heiress of John Hide of East Greenwich, Kent. William Augustus Townshend (10 March 1776 – 3 July 1816) was a British politician and soldier. He sat as MP for Whitchurch from 15 July 1800 till his death on 3 July 1816. [ref: TOWNSHEND, Hon. William Augustus (1776-1816)., History of Parliament Online]

data.title: Matthias Faes
data.text:
----

Matthias G. R. Faes (born 15 October 1991) is a Belgian engineer and academic who works on uncertainty quantification and reliability engineering. Since February 2022 he has been a full professor at TU Dortmund University, where he heads the Chair for Reliability Engineering (CRE) in the Department of Mechanical Engineering.

== Early life and education ==
Faes was born in Lier, Belgium. He studied engineering technology at the De Nayer campus in Sint-Katelijne-Waver, obtaining a bachelor's degree in 2012 and a master's degree in engineering technology with a specialization in manufacturing engineering in 2013, which he completed summa cum laude.

He then carried out his doctoral research in the Department of Mechanical Engineering of KU Leuven under the supervision of David Moens. He obtained his PhD in engineering technology in 2017 with a dissertation on interval methods for the identification and quantification of inhomogeneous uncertainty in finite element models.

== Career ==
From 2013 to 2017 Faes worked as a scientific and teaching assistant at KU Leuven. After completing his doctorate he remained there as a postdoctoral researcher, from 2019 to 2022 as a postdoctoral fellow of the Research Foundation – Flanders (FWO). In 2020 he received a postdoctoral research fellowship from the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation, which he held at the Institute for Risk and Reliability of Leibniz University Hannover.

In February 2022 he was appointed full professor (W3) of Reliability Engineering at TU Dortmund University.

== Research ==
Faes's research concerns computational methods for uncertainty quantification and reliability analysis of engineering structures and systems. The main areas of his work are positioned in the reliability analysis of complex structures, uncertainty quantification under scarce data and the extension of numerical models with scientific machine learning and artificial intelligence tools. [ref: Matthias Faes, ORCID]

His doctoral and early postdoctoral work developed interval field methods, which represent spatially varying non-probabilistic uncertainty in finite element models, together with inverse methods to identify such uncertainty from measurement data. His later work addresses the efficient estimation of small failure probabilities, including first-passage problems in stochastic structural dynamics, Bayesian active learning with Gaussian process surrogate models, the propagation of imprecise probabilities such as probability boxes, and reliability-based design optimization of complex systems.

== Awards and honours ==

* 2018: ECCOMAS Award for the best PhD theses of 2017 on computational methods in applied sciences and engineering, one of two winners selected from 17 nominated theses.
* 2018: Second laureate of the award of the Belgian National Committee on Theoretical and Applied Mechanics for the best PhD thesis of 2017.
* 2019: IJAR Young Researcher Award of the International Symposium on Imprecise Probabilities: Theories and Applications (ISIPTA), shared with Arthur Van Camp.
* 2023: Junior Research Prize in the area of Development of Methodologies for Structural Dynamics of the European Association for Structural Dynamics (EASD).
* 2026: Olgierd Cecil Zienkiewicz Young Investigator Award of the European Community on Computational Methods in Applied Sciences (ECCOMAS), presented at the WCCM-ECCOMAS 2026 Congress in Munich.

== Professional service ==
Faes is an associate editor of the journals Reliability Engineering & System Safety and Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing, and associate managing editor of the ASCE-ASME Journal of Risk and Uncertainty in Engineering Systems.

data.title: Morgantown Mall
data.text:
Morgantown Mall is a shopping mall located in Westover, West Virginia, at the intersection of Interstate 79 and U.S. Route 19. It is the newer of the two malls located in Morgantown, the other being the Mountaineer Mall. Anchors are JCPenney, Dunham's Sports, Burkes Outlet, Home Centric, Ollie’s Bargain Outlet, and AMC Classic. The former Sears is used as a logistics and distribution center for WVU Medicine. [ref: 2 new anchor stores coming to Morgantown Mall, [[WBOY-TV] To the north lies The Morgantown Commons.

== History ==
Plans for the mall were announced in 1989 by Glimcher Realty Trust and site work began on June 12. [ref: Morgantown mall work under way, Cumberland Times News] It opened on September 13, 1990, with Elder-Beerman, JCPenney, Sears, and K-Mart (later Proffitt's) as anchors. The mall was a newer alternative to the Mountaineer Mall located across town along Greenbag Road. [ref: Morgantown complex poses no challenge, merchants say, The Pittsburgh Press] Due to its popularity, many anchors abandoned the Mountaineer Mall and began moving to the Morgantown Mall. [ref: Mountaineer Mall, more than just stores, The Dominion Post] Elder Beerman operated two stores in Morgantown in each mall before the closure of the Mountaineer Mall location in January 2008, due to lease expiry. [ref: Elder-Beerman to close its doors in January, Morgantown Dominion Post]

Proffitt's was converted to Belk on March 1, 2006. [ref: Proffitt's at Morgantown changes to Belk today, Morgantown Dominion Post] On November 1, Gabriel Brothers opened. [ref: Hosanna for bargain-hunters, Morgantown Dominion Post]

In 2016, The Gap and Hollister left the mall due to their owner companies restructuring. The Hollister was planned to be replaced with a Rue21. [ref: Morgantown Mall fills spaces fit for community needs, WV News] On October 15, 2018, Sears was announced to close as part of its national closure of 142 stores due to Chapter 11 Bankruptcy. [ref: Sears closing these 142 stores in bankruptcy filing and liquidation sale, CBS News] This followed the closures of Belk and Elder-Beerman the same year. [ref: Sears to close Morgantown Mall store as retailer continues to struggle, The Dominion Post] In 2020, AMC was renovated and Ollie’s Bargain Outlet and Dunham's Sports opened. In 2025, ownership was transferred from Washington Prime Group to Kohan Retail Investment Group. [ref: New ownership represents ‘pivotal moment’ for Morgantown Mall, [[The Dominion Post (Morgantown)] Their previous owner filed for Chapter 11 Bankruptcy protection after the COVID-19 pandemic. [ref: Morgantown Mall’s parent company files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, WBOY]

=== morgantownmall.com ===
On June 1, 2001, the domain name "morgantownmall.com" was disputed between Morgantown Mall Associates LTD. Partnership of Columbus, Ohio and the former domain holder located in Rio, Brazil via arbitration. Morgantown Mall Associates (owner of Morgantown Mall) stated that the domain name was identical to their current website and that it was used in "bad faith". It was decided that the domain name would be transferred to Morgantown Mall Associates. [ref: Morgantown Mall Assoc. Ltd. P’ship v. morgantownmall.com, adrforum.com]

data.title: Dan Pinchbeck
data.text:
----

Dan Pinchbeck is a author, scriptwriter, and game developer. He is best known as co-creator of the video games Dear Esther and Everybody's Gone to the Rapture. Both games were nominated for several British Academy Games Awards with Everybody's Gone to the Rapture winning three along with winning the Writers' Guild of Great Britain Best Writing in a Videogame award. He is the co-founder of the British video game development studio The Chinese Room where he was creative director until 2023.

== Career ==
Pinchbeck started making games whilst undertaking a PhD and working as a lecturer at the University of Portsmouth. [ref: A very British disaster: How The Chinese Room made one of 2015's best video games, The Telegraph] After receiving a grant from the Arts & Humanities Research Council. [ref: UK Research and Innovation Gateway, UK Research & Innovation Gateway], he led a team that made a series of experimental game mods exploring different aspects of game design. Pinchbeck worked closely with the composer Jessica Curry on the development of the mods, which were released for free on the Moddb website. One of the mods, Dear Esther, was a breakout, if controversial, hit that has gone on to be a frequently cited title in conversations about the definition of games and the relationship between games and art. [ref: Game of the Week: Dear Esther, Eurogamer.net] [ref: ModDB Dear Esther, Moddb] [ref: Touched By The Hand of Mod, Rock, Paper, Shotgun].

In 2009, Pinchbeck and Curry were approached by game artist Robert Briscoe about creating a commercial version of Dear Esther. They secured investment from the US backer Indie Fund and the game was launched in 2012, paying back its investment in less than six hours [ref: Dear Esther has reached profitability, Indie Fund]. The game was an overnight cult hit. In his review for The Telegraph, Tom Hoggins described it as "oil painting, poetry, eulogy and video game all at once" [ref: Dear Esther review, The Telegraph]. For IGN, Keza MacDonald noted that "Dear Esther doesn't need puzzles or mechanics to draw you in. The strength of the writing and the world alone is enough", praising the writing's depth: "I can't give away anything of Dear Esther's story and premise without spoiling it, but it's layered enough to support multiple playthroughs. The writing is dense with intertextual references, most of them biblical, and there are clues and allusions in the narrator's musings that you won't notice the first time you play through.". She concluded that "Dear Esther can change your perspective on what games could be doing." [ref: Dear Esther review, IGN.com]. Dear Esther "is generally regarded as kick-starting the walking simulator sub-genre." [ref: Clash of Realities, Clash of Realities] It won an IndieCade award in 2012 for Best World/Story [ref: University of Portsmouth - Game, set and match, Times Higher Education (THE)] and was nominated for five British Academy Games Awards (BATFA).

At that point, under the brand name The Chinese Room, the development team had begun working on a sequel to Frictional Games' Amnesia: The Dark Descent.. The game, Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs was released in 2013 [ref: How the Amnesia Sequel's sausage was made, www.eurogamer.net]. Pinchbeck stated that his aim with the game was to create a horror without simple morality and strong thematic links to 20th Century history. [ref: Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs writer Dan Pinchbeck talks about horror, genocide, and the scene so disgusting he had to cut it, Killscreen]

In his review of the game, Kirk Hamilton stated "Writer Dan Pinchbeck has stitched together literary influences both obvious and surprising, and the result is a wonderfully macabre indictment of the industrial revolution: Upton Sinclair‘s The Jungle meets H.G. Wells’ The Island of Doctor Moreau.” [ref: Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs review, Kotaku.com] The New York Times stated, "The game's writer, Dan Pinchbeck, is colorful and creative in the cruelty he describes" [ref: Rayman Legends, Total War: Rome II, Plants vs. Zombies 2, Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs and Puppeteer, The New York Times]

By the time of Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs release, The Chinese Room were working on a prototype for the openworld game Everybody's Gone to the Rapture. The story was inspired in part by Pinchbeck's experience of the Great storm of 1987 while growing up in a small village in Kent during the Cold War. In their review of the game, The Washington Post credited his "moxie" as creative director in helping The Chinese Room become a "vanguard in the industry." [ref: ‘Everybody’s Gone to the Rapture’ review: An arthouse movie in video game form, The Washington Post]

Everybody's Gone to the Rapture was released in 2015 and was a critical and commercial hit with Pinchbeck's writing frequently cited as major factor in its success.In his review for IGN, Marty Sliva wrote "For a span of five hours, Everybody’s Gone to the Rapture transported me to one of the most detailed, fully realized worlds I’ve ever experienced in a video game. Even the most earth shattering of these revelations are presented in a way that’s painfully melancholy, but I wholly appreciated that Rapture made me actually feel connected to these characters and this place in a way that stirred something in me, which is a task not very many video game stories have managed to accomplish." [ref: Everybody's Gone to the Rapture review, IGN.com]. Andy Kelly in PC Gamer picked up on the deliberate literary skew of the story, writing that "Apocalyptic fiction rarely focuses on how normal, everyday people would cope when faced with the end of the world, which makes Rapture’s story all the more powerful. I couldn’t help but see myself and my loved ones in the people living in the valley, which gave it an extra resonance". [ref: Everybody's Gone to the Rapture review, PCGamer]. The game went on to win 3 BAFTAs,and was nominated for another seven, including Best Story. [ref: ] The BAFTA-winning score by studio co-founder and composer Jessica Curry was also singled out as critical to the game's success, with Pinchbeck writing the lyrics to the original songs. [ref: Everybody's Gone to the Rapture: writing a score for the end of the world, The Guardian]

During this period, Dear Esther was also ported to console with the publisher Curve Digital. [ref: Dear Esther: how the 'walking simulator' made it to PlayStation 4 and Xbox One, The Guardian]

Following the release of the mobile VR title So Let Us Melt in 2017, The Chinese Room became a subsidiary studio of Sumo Digital. Pinchbeck led the studio through acquisition and the development of 2020's Little Orpheus. The game saw Pinchbeck expand his writing and directing into comedy [ref: ] and once again, this was picked out as a central plank in the game's success. In Eurogamer, Vikki Blake called it "a captivating yarn, and a glorious adventure to boot" [ref: Little Orpheus Review, Eurogamer.net] and Thomas Hughes in The Sixth Axis described the game as setting "a new bar in mobile gaming experiences" with "Its rich, lush world is only surpassed by the fantastic narrative and voice acting". [ref: Little Orpheus Review, The Sixth Axis]. Writing for Switch Player, Joe Westcott said "It really is the story that makes Little Orpheus as enjoyable as it is... The juxtaposition between the fumbling, bumbling Ivan and the stoic General doesn’t portray a pairing that inspires anything new, but the writing is so sharp that the story feels fresh regardless. Unlikely relationships such as theirs have been mined for every shred of comedy they’re worth for years, so for me to still find enjoyment and laughter in what could have been a very stale scenario speaks to the strength of both the writing and the acting." [ref: Little Orpheus Review, Switch Player]. In 2021, Little Orpheus won an Apple Design award for Delight & Fun, citing it's "excellent storytelling". [ref: Apple Design Awards - Apple Developer, developer.apple.com]

Pinchbeck's last game for The Chinese Room was the original horror title Still Wakes the Deep. Pitched as "The Thing Meets Boys From the Black Stuff on an oil rig. Oil Rig sinks" [ref: From Half Life 2 Mods to Vampire: The Masquerade, The Goth Boss podcast] [ref: "The Thing on an oil rig" is one hell of a pitch, but Still Wakes the Deep's unshakable terror is driven by its unheroic characters, GamesRadar+], Still Wakes the Deep saw Pinchbeck return to the blend of social drama and horror of Machine for Pigs and Everybody's Gone to the Rapture. James Stephanie Sterling described it as "an impeccable horror production, a gorgeously sickening nightmare in a rarely used setting propelled by stellar acting and sublimely nasty body horror. It’s more than just “The Thing on an oil rig,” though it makes good on that elevator pitch too. It's going to  remain with me for a long time. A true genre classic." [ref: Still Wakes the Deep review, thejimquisition]. It went on to win 3 BAFTAs for Best New Intellectual Property and Best Performer wins for Alec Newman and Karen Dunbar. [ref: 21st BAFTA Games Awards: Winners Announced, Bafta]

In 2023, Pinchbeck stepped down as co-studio head and creative director of The Chinese Room. [ref: ‘Trauma is messy, but music will come of it’: Jessica Curry on her new album, Shielding Songs, The Guardian] Since leaving the games industry, Pinchbeck has focused on being a full-time writer.

== Academic Work ==

Prior to starting The Chinese Room, Pinchbeck was a Reader in Computer Games at the University of Portsmouth where he lectured and researched game design and game narrative. [ref: ]

In 2009, Pinchbeck completed his PhD, entitled Story as a function of gameplay in First Person Shooters and an analysis of FPS diegetic content 1998-2007. [ref: Story and Recall in First‐Person Shooters, International Journal of Computer Games Technology] [ref: Cyber Games and Interactive Entertainment, International Journal of Computer Games Technology]

He is the author of Doom: ScaryDarkFast, an academic analysis of the 1993 video game Doom. [ref: Doom: scarydarkfast, University of Michigan Press] [ref: From the Presupposition of Doom to the Manifestation of Code: Using Emulated Citation in the Study of Games and Cultural Software, Digital Humanities Quarterly]

== Awards ==

Pinchbeck's games have been nominated for 23 BAFTAs and won 6. Other notable awards include 2 Apple Design Award nominations and 1 win [ref: Apple Design Awards 2021, developer.apple.com/], 4 DICE nominations [ref: 2025 DICE Awards Winners, ign.com/] [ref: 19th DICE Awards Winners, interactive.org/] [ref: 24th DICE Awards Winners, interactive.org/], 4 Develop awards [ref: Develop Awards 2012, mcvuk.com/] [ref: MCV Develop 2025 Winners, mcvdevelopawards.com/] [ref: MCV Develop 2021 Winners, mcvuk.com/], 8 TIGA awards [ref: 2024 TIGA awards, tiga.org/] [ref: 2015 TIGA awards, tiga.org/] [ref: 2012 TIGA awards, tiga.org/], an IGF award [ref: IGF Winners 2012 Winners, polygon.com] and nominations and wins at GDC Choice [ref: GDC 2016 Nominations Winners, gamechoiceawards.com], South by South West (SXSW) [ref: SXSW 2016 Finalists Announced s, austinchronicle.com], Golden Joystick [ref: Golden Joysticks 2020 Nominees announced s, gonintendo.com] and NAVGTR [ref: NAVGTR Awards 2015 s, navgtr.org]

data.title: Gerald Jonas
data.text:
Gerald Jonas (born 1935) is an American writer, journalist, and literary critic. He was a staff writer for The New Yorker for approximately 30 years and a science fiction book critic for The New York Times Book Review. [ref: Selected Shorts: Anything But Politics with Tony Hale, Symphony Space] He wrote a number of nonfiction books, and his science fiction novelette The Shaker Revival was nominated for a Nebula Award in 1970. [ref: 1970 Nebula Awards, Nebula Awards]

== Early life and education ==
Jonas was born in 1935 [ref: Stuttering: the disorder of many theories - NLM Catalog - NCBI, www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov]. He attended the Horace Mann School in New York [ref: My Grandfather, the Writer, The Science Survey] and Yale University where he wrote for the Yale Daily News [ref: Elected to Yale News Board, The New York Times], graduating in 1957. He subsequently held a Henry Fellowship at the University of Cambridge, a Guggenheim Fellowship, and a Rockefeller Fellowship.

== Career ==
Jonas spent approximately three decades as a staff writer for The New Yorker [ref: Gerald Jonas, The New Yorker], writing about science, technology, psychology, and medicine. He served as a science fiction book critic for The New York Times Book Review for approximately 30 years, reviewing more than 900 works of science fiction and related literature. [ref: Science Fiction, archive.nytimes.com]

In 1977, science fiction critic John D. Berry criticised Jonas's New York Times column in the fanzine Karass. Berry considered Jonas a competent but unexceptional reviewer. [ref: Hot Corn, Cold Corn, Karass]

In a review of the second edition of The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction published in Fantasy Commentator, A. Langley Searles identified Jonas as one of several figures he believed warranted an entry. [ref: The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction, Fantasy Commentator]

In a 2006 discussion of science fiction reviewing in Publishers Weekly, Jonas' science fiction column was described as a near-monthly, one-page feature of capsule reviews that had become less frequent after Sam Tanenhaus became editor of The New York Times Book Review. [ref: ]

His later journalism included obituaries of science fiction writers Arthur C. Clarke [ref: Arthur C. Clarke, Author Who Saw Science Fiction Become Real, Dies at 90, The New York Times], Ray Bradbury [ref: Ray Bradbury, Who Brought Mars to Earth With a Lyrical Mastery, Dies at 91, The New York Times], and Ursula K. Le Guin [ref: Ursula K. Le Guin, Acclaimed for Her Fantasy Fiction, Is Dead at 88, The New York Times] for The New York Times.

=== Nonfiction books ===
Jonas has written six nonfiction books on subjects ranging from religion and psychology to scientific research, dance and natural history.

His first book, On Doing Good: The Quaker Experiment (1971), examined the history and principles of the Religious Society of Friends. Reviewing the book, Kirkus Reviews described it as "refreshingly objective". [ref: Book Reviews, Sites, Romance, Fantasy, Fiction, Kirkus Reviews]

His second book, Visceral Learning: Toward a Science of Self-Control (1973), concerned research into the control of physiological processes. It was reviewed by Bob Samples in The American Biology Teacher. [ref: Review: Visceral Learning: Toward a Science of Self-Control, by Gerald Jonas and The Psychology of the Consciousness, by Robert E. Ornstein, The American Biology Teacher]

Jonas's Stuttering: The Disorder of Many Theories (1977) combined scientific theories about stuttering with his personal experiences. A contemporary review in Kirkus Reviews praised the book's combination of personal experience and scientific investigation. [ref: Stuttering: The Disorder of Many Theories, Kirkus Reviews] In a 2012 essay in The New York Review of Books, Francine du Plessix Gray described the work as a "splendid memoir". [ref: The Paralysis of Stuttering, The New York Review of Books]

His 1989 book, The Circuit Riders: Rockefeller Money and the Rise of Modern Science, examined the role of Rockefeller Foundation philanthropy in the development of scientific research. The book was reviewed in several publications, including JAMA [ref: The Circuit Riders: Rockefeller Money and the Rise of Modern Science, JAMA], The New York Times Book Review [ref: BIG MONEY MEETS BIG SCIENCE, The New York Times], Science [ref: Modes and Agendas of Patronage: The Politics of Philanthropy. Abraham Flexner and Medical Education. Steven C. Wheatley. University of Wisconsin Press, Madison, 1989. xx, 249 pp. + plates. $37.50; paper, $14.95.; The Circuit Riders. Rockefeller Money and the Rise of Modern Science. Gerald Jonas. Norton, New York, 1989. 430 pp., illus. $22.95., Science], the Los Angeles Times [ref: Book Review: 'Circuit Riders': Giving Away Research Money Is an Art, Los Angeles Times], and The Quarterly Review of Biology. [ref: The Rockefeller Foundation: Warren Weaver and the Launching of Molecular Biology The Circuit Riders: Rockefeller Money and the Rise of Modern Science. Gerald Jonas, The Quarterly Review of Biology]

Jonas wrote Dancing: The Pleasure, Power, and Art of Movement (1992) as a companion to an eight-part television documentary series. The book and television series were reviewed in the Dance Research Journal. [ref: Dancing: The Pleasure, Power, and Art of Movement, byGerald Jonas. New York: Harry N. Abrams, 1992. 256pp., photographs, Bibliography, Index. 199.95., Dance Research Journal]

His sixth nonfiction book, The Living Earth Book of North American Trees (1993), examined the history of North American trees and their relationship with human settlement and conservation. [ref: The living earth book of North American trees, Reader's Digest living earth] The book was reviewed in the journal Economic Botany in 1994. [ref: The living earth book of North American trees, Economic Botany]

=== Fiction and poetry ===
In addition to his nonfiction and journalism, Jonas has published short fiction and poetry. His work has appeared in The New Yorker, The Atlantic, Poetry, The Nation, The New Republic and The Paris Review.

His science fiction novelette The Shaker Revival, published in Galaxy Science Fiction in 1970, was nominated for the Nebula Award for Best Novelette for that year.

Jonas also collaborated with writer Renata Adler, writing under the pseudonym Jean Marple, on the short story "The Stand-in", which appeared in the summer 1969 issue of The Paris Review. [ref: The Stand-in, The Paris Review]

== Selected Bibliography ==

=== Nonfiction books ===
* On Doing Good: The Quaker Experiment, Scribners
* Visceral learning; toward a science of self-control., Viking Press
* Stuttering, the disorder of many theories, Farrar, Straus & Giroux
* The circuit riders: Rockefeller money and the rise of modern science, Norton
* Dancing: the pleasure, power, and art of movement, Harry N. Abrams in association with Thirteen/WNET
* The living earth book of North American trees, Reader's Digest Association

=== Other works ===

* The Shaker Revival, Galaxy Science Fiction
* The Art of Reviewing Science Books, The Sciences

data.title: Marcos da Matta
data.text:
Marcos da Matta Meira (born March 18, 1973), known as Parrumpinha or Parrumpa, is a Brazilian Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt, retired mixed martial artist and mixed martial arts coach. A black belt under Carlson Gracie, he won the first IBJJF World Championship at purple belt in 1996 and the Brazilian national title at black belt in 2000. [ref: World Jiu-Jitsu IBJJF Championship 1996 – Results, International Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Federation] [ref: Campeonato Brasileiro de Jiu-Jitsu 2000 – Resultados, Confederação Brasileira de Jiu-Jitsu] He moved to the United States in 2002 and is the head Brazilian jiu-jitsu coach of the American Top Team professional team in Coconut Creek, Florida. [ref: Pro Coaches, American Top Team] [ref: Inside American Top Team, Fighters Only]

He made his professional MMA debut at 34 and went 12–3 between 2007 and 2018, fighting for Strikeforce and Bellator. [ref: Treinador da ATT, Parrumpinha vence luta de despedida do MMA aos 45 anos, Combate] As a coach he has led Alexandre Pantoja since 2018, including Pantoja's run as UFC Flyweight Champion, and has worked with Petr Yan, Arman Tsarukyan, Renato Moicano, Amanda Nunes and Mayra Bueno Silva, among others. [ref: Marcos Parrumpinha condena polêmicas do MMA nas redes sociais: "Desrespeitam pessoas e nada acontece", ge]

==Early life==
Da Matta grew up in Copacabana, where he spent his days playing beach soccer and footvolley. [ref: Marcos da Matta "Parrumpinha", BJJ Heroes] Carlson Gracie's academy was in the same neighborhood, on Rua Figueiredo Magalhães. [ref: Num encontro marcante, pupilos lembram Carlson Gracie, Graciemag] By his account, Gracie met him on the beach when he was 11 or 12 and kept pushing him to train. He went "for a week or two to prove to him that I don't like it" and stayed. He began training regularly in 1987 and remained with Gracie until 2000. [ref: Interview with Marcos da Matta, American Top Team BJJ instructor, Bloody Elbow] [ref: Legendary Gym Stories: When Liborio Wiped Out The Carlson Gracie Competition Team, BJJEE]

His nickname reportedly comes from a well-known Copacabana local called "Parrumpa", whom he resembled, so friends called him "Parrumpinha" (little Parrumpa). Because of the number of Russian fighters he later began to coach, the Brazilian MMA community also took to calling him "Parrumpov". [ref: ATT Coach: Sean O'Malley Has Never Faced a Challenge Like Pedro Munhoz, Sherdog]

==Brazilian jiu-jitsu career==
===Carlson Gracie academy===
At Gracie's academy, one of his main influences was Amaury Bitetti, who got him to cross-train in judo and work on guard passing. He also practiced Álvaro Romano's Ginástica Natural, which he credits with helping him recover from injuries. [ref: Benefits of Ginastica Natural for Jiu-Jitsu, BJJEE] He calls Ricardo Libório his mentor, and names Renato Tavares as his most frequent training partner.

He was promoted to purple belt on January 1, 1994, and his first match at the new rank was against Leonardo Vieira, who was still unbeaten at purple belt. [ref: Parrumpinha - 100% Carlson Gracie, MMA Debate] The 20-minute match was part of a challenge between Carlson Gracie's academy and Romero "Jacaré" Cavalcanti's Academia Master, held at a nightclub in Leblon in February 1994. [ref: EP#25 Mente Blindada com Marcos "Parrumpinha" Da Matta, Gustavo Dantas] [ref: Exclusivo! Parrumpinha fala de seu início no jiu-jitsu e o começo da American Top Team, Só Papos MMA] Da Matta says he won by a wide margin on points. He had been a little-known blue belt until then and calls it the fight that most shaped his life, since the jiu-jitsu community began to take him seriously afterward. The two met again later, and each won once. [ref: Marcos Parrumpinha - Resenha PVT, Portal do Vale Tudo]

In 1996 he won the first IBJJF World Championship at purple belt, featherweight, entered as "Marcos Da Mata", with Fredson Junior taking silver. Gracie promoted him to black belt in 1997. [ref: It's Time! 'Parrumpinha' participa do podcast do Super Lutas, Super Lutas] At black belt he took silver at the 1999 Pan American Championship in the 70 kg division, losing the final to Royler Gracie on advantage. [ref: Marcos da Matta, Let's BJJ] During those years he also refereed as a center official for the Confederação Brasileira de Jiu-Jitsu. [ref: Parrumpinha comenta estreia no Strikeforce e lembra rivalidade com Robinho, Graciemag]

===Brazilian Top Team and the Robson Moura rivalry===
When Carlson Gracie's leading black belts broke with him in 2000, da Matta left with Libório and Bitetti for the newly founded Brazilian Top Team. Under the BTT banner he won the 2000 Brazilian Nationals at black belt featherweight, ahead of Marcos Loureiro. The same year he reached the featherweight final of the World Championship at the Tijuca Tênis Clube and lost 2–0 to Robson Moura. [ref: World Jiu-Jitsu IBJJF Championship 2000 – Results, International Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Federation] [ref: Jiu-Jitsu: relembre Robinho Moura x Parrumpinha no Mundial de 2000, no Tijuca, Graciemag]

In 2010 da Matta said Moura had beaten him twice and that their rivalry "was good for stirring up the fans, but it never went beyond the dojo"; after both moved to the United States they trained together. They met a third time on October 18, 2014, in a 15-minute gi superfight at the World Jiu-Jitsu Expo in Long Beach, California, where Moura won by clock choke at around the four-minute mark. [ref: Jiu-Jitsu Expo 2014: Vitor Shaolin e Robson Moura voltam a brilhar em noite de superlutas, Graciemag] [ref: 2014 Jiu-Jitsu World Expo Superfights & BJJ Pro League Recap & Results, BJJEE]

===In the United States===
He competed at the 2005 ADCC World Championship in Long Beach and lost in the first round of the under-66 kg division to Urijah Faber. [ref: ADCC 2005: a serious look back, ADCombat] American Top Team lists him as a ten-time NAGA superfight champion.

Competing in the masters divisions at super-heavyweight, he won the 2014 Boca Raton Open and the 2015 Miami Open, took bronze at the 2017 World Master Championship and silver in 2020, when he lost the master 4 final to Roberto Godoi. [ref: Boca Raton Open: Cyborg wins absolute, other results, Graciemag] [ref: Miami International Open IBJJF Jiu-Jitsu Championship 2015 – Results, International Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Federation] [ref: Megaton, Mario Sperry, Titi and more winners from day 2 of the World Master Championship, Graciemag] His own academy lists him as a sixth-degree black belt; American Top Team's coaches page gives fifth degree. [ref: American Top Team WPB – Parrumpa BJJ, American Top Team West Palm Beach]

==Mixed martial arts career==
After moving to the United States, da Matta's job was to help Libório run jiu-jitsu at American Top Team; he gradually moved into MMA coaching and, past 30, into competing. He debuted on March 31, 2007, at 34, submitting Dan Funes in the first round at PFL: Genesis in Miami, and won his first seven fights on Florida regional cards. [ref: Marcos Meira – Fighter Record, CombatReg]

Still unbeaten, he signed with Strikeforce; he said he had also talked to Dream and the WEC, but Strikeforce made the firm offer. At Strikeforce: Miami on January 30, 2010, at the BankAtlantic Center in Sunrise, he lost to Pablo Alfonso by armbar at 1:47 of the first round, for a disclosed purse of $2,500. [ref: Strikeforce paydays and salaries, MMAmania]

His Bellator debut came against Shah Bobonis at Bellator 50 on September 17, 2011, in Hollywood; he controlled the first two rounds with armbar and choke attempts before being knocked out by a right hand in the third. [ref: Cooper Clobbers Araujo in Bellator 50 Undercard Showstealer, Sherdog] Three straight armbar wins followed in 2013 and 2014, before Solon Staley knocked him out at AFC 24 in January 2016.

After more than two years away, he took one more fight so as not to retire on a loss. On July 21, 2018, aged 45, he faced Jordan Mackin, 20 years his junior, at UCFC 1 in West Palm Beach, where he runs his academy, and finished him with a kata-gatame early in the second round, with student Pedro Munhoz in his corner. He said he had fainted during his weight cut and retired afterward, saying he could no longer balance fighting with travel, his athletes and his family.

==Coaching career==
===American Top Team===
Da Matta moved to the United States in 2002 at the invitation of Ricardo Libório, one of American Top Team's founders, and in 2024 described himself as having been at ATT "since the beginning". [ref: Parrumpinha explica desabafo no UFC 300: "Não foi para o Charles", Ag. Fight] He worked his first corner in 1998 and his first UFC corner in 2006. [ref: Protetor, treinador Parrumpa exalta relação com Pantoja como "irmão mais velho", UOL] By 2009 the fighters he trained included Mike Brown, Thiago Alves, Marcus Aurélio, Gesias Cavalcante, Luigi Fioravanti, Steve Bruno and Cole Miller. He also owns ATT West Palm Beach.

He is the head jiu-jitsu instructor of ATT's professional team in Coconut Creek. According to da Matta, fighters at ATT pick their own coaches, and on busy weekends he has cornered five fighters across separate events. [ref: A Man in High Demand: Following the Whirlwind Weekend of ATT Coach 'Parrumpa', Sherdog] A positive COVID-19 test in June 2020 kept him out of the corners of Pantoja, Tsarukyan, Amanda Ribas and Luis Peña for a run of UFC events. [ref: Coach 'Parrumpinha' tests positive for COVID-19, MMA Fighting] At the time, Brazilian outlet Super Lutas described him as the man in charge of the jiu-jitsu of Amanda Nunes, Junior dos Santos and Edson Barboza. [ref: Técnico de Amanda Nunes é diagnosticado com Covid-19, mas mira retorno no UFC 251, Super Lutas]

===Alexandre Pantoja===
Pantoja approached da Matta in early 2018, after losing to Dustin Ortiz at UFC 220; both are from Rio, and Pantoja has said he wanted to be coached by a Carlson Gracie black belt. Pantoja won the UFC Flyweight Championship from Brandon Moreno at UFC 290 on July 8, 2023, and defended it four times before losing it at UFC 323 in December 2025, when he injured tendons and ligaments in his arm early in the fight with Joshua Van. He stayed with da Matta through his recovery. [ref: Coach Speak: ATT Trainer 'Parrumpa' Reveals Pantoja's Successful Strategy at UFC 290, Sherdog] [ref: Ex-Champ Alexandre Pantoja Returns to Sparring, Targets May Comeback, Sherdog]

Da Matta coached Pantoja to approach every title defense as a challenger. After three title fights in ten months, he insisted that Pantoja rest until the end of 2024 and told the UFC that, once rested, Pantoja would finish whoever they matched him with; Pantoja then submitted Kai Asakura at UFC 310. Pantoja compares the relationship to the film Whiplash: "I'm the drummer and 'Parrumpa' is the maestro." Da Matta calls himself Pantoja's "older brother".

===Russian fighters and other athletes===
From the late 2010s da Matta began coaching a large group of Russian and Caucasian fighters, starting with Omari Akhmedov and followed by Movsar Evloev, Petr Yan, Sergey Morozov, Zhalgas Zhumagulov, Damir Ismagulov, Muhammad Mokaev, Alexandr Shabliy, Movlid Khaybulaev, Magomed Magomedkerimov and Magomed Umalatov. He also cornered Kayla Harrison in the PFL. In 2023 Mokaev stopped training at ATT after Pantoja won the title; da Matta said he understood: "Pantoja is like a son to me, and it would be complicated for me to train two guys with the same goal." [ref: ATT Coach Expects Nothing to Change with New UFC Anti-Doping Policy, Sherdog]

He also coaches Tsarukyan, Moicano and Bia Mesquita, and was part of Tsarukyan's camp for his scheduled fight with Islam Makhachev at UFC 311. Mesquita, a jiu-jitsu world champion, moved to Florida in 2023 to make the switch to MMA under him. [ref: BJJ legend Bia Mesquita ready for MMA debut, MMA Fighting] He cornered Mayra Bueno Silva for the women's bantamweight title at UFC 297 in January 2024, calling it a chance to bring Amanda Nunes's old belt back to ATT. [ref: Mayra Bueno Silva coach happy to win back Amanda Nunes' old UFC belt for ATT: 'It's very special', MMA Fighting]

He was nominated for the Shawn Tompkins Coach of the Year award at the 2024 World MMA Awards. [ref: Indicado ao Oscar do MMA, Parrumpinha é entrevistado do Conexão PVT, Portal do Vale Tudo]

==Controversies==
===1998 World Championship===
At the 1998 World Championship at the Tijuca Tênis Clube, da Matta refereed the purple belt open-weight final between Fernando Tererê and Rolls Gracie, son of the late Rolls Gracie. Tererê was down by an advantage when he locked in a triangle choke; to escape, Gracie lifted him and slammed him to the mat, an illegal move, and da Matta disqualified him. Gracie then attacked the referee. By da Matta's account, he was punched while bending down to tie his shoe and hit three more times on the ground, and was dazed for two hours afterward. He filed a police complaint at the 19th precinct in Tijuca, underwent a forensic examination and sued for physical and moral damages. Gracie was arrested at the scene, and Confederation president Carlos Gracie Jr. expelled him from the tournament and docked Gracie Barra twenty points in the team standings. [ref: 3º Mundial de Jiu-Jitsu: o show de Sperry e Saulo e as homenagens a Hélio e Carlson, Kimê]

===UFC 259===
Da Matta was in Petr Yan's corner at UFC 259 on March 6, 2021, when Yan lost the UFC Bantamweight Championship by disqualification for an illegal knee to a downed Aljamain Sterling. On the broadcast, Joe Rogan and Daniel Cormier suggested someone in the corner had told Yan to throw it. Da Matta denied it, saying he twice told Yan "just punch", [ref: Treinador nega interferência do corner em golpe ilegal aplicado por Petr Yan no UFC 259, Ag. Fight] that the referee had gone over that exact rule in the locker room, and that he could not follow what the other cornermen said in Russian. Of Sterling's decision not to continue, he said "only he truly knows" whether he could have gone on. [ref: Petr Yan cornerman Marcos 'Parrumpinha' da Matta discusses illegal knee, DQ loss at UFC 259, MMA Fighting]

===UFC 300===
After Tsarukyan beat Charles Oliveira at UFC 300 on April 13, 2024, da Matta went to the broadcast camera, mimed crying and shouted "respect me" in Portuguese. Brazilian fans accused him of disrespecting a national idol. He later said he and his wife had received abusive messages and threats in the preceding months, some aimed at his family, that the outburst was meant for those people rather than Oliveira or his coach Diego Lima, and apologized to those it had hurt.

===Mayra Bueno Silva doping case===
In 2023 Bueno Silva's win over Holly Holm was overturned to a no contest after she tested positive for ritalinic acid from an ADHD medication she had taken since childhood. Da Matta criticized the Nevada State Athletic Commission for punishing something USADA had cleared and publicly thanked UFC executive Hunter Campbell for keeping her ranked. In the same interview he said he gives private lessons to George Piro, a former FBI official and a director at the company taking over the UFC's anti-doping program, and dismissed jokes that ATT would benefit: in his view, ATT fighters would be tested even more.

===Comments on other fighters===
In October 2025 he criticized Jhonata Diniz for bringing businessman Luciano Hang into his corner at UFC Rio, where Diniz lost by TKO to Mário Pinto. "If you're a professional and you take your career seriously, you can't do something like that," he said, suggesting guests buy a front-row ticket instead. [ref: Parrumpinha detonates the presence of the 'Old Man of Havan' in the corner of the Brazilian at UFC Rio, Super Lutas] [ref: UFC Rio: Com 'Véio da Havan' no corner, Jhonata Diniz é dominado por Mario Pinto, Ag. Fight] Earlier that year he questioned a training video Alex Pereira released before UFC 320, arguing that the partners shooting takedowns on him had no real wrestling pedigree: "Poatan is defending takedowns like nobody else, perfect, but who's attacking him?" [ref: Parrumpinha questiona treinos de Alex Poatan em preparação para enfrentar Magomed Ankalaev no UFC 320, Super Lutas]

In April 2026 he said he would not coach Carlos Prates because of the fighter's lifestyle, as Prates often appears in videos drinking and smoking, adding that he liked watching Prates fight but did not consider him an example for young people. Online, some fans pointed to aggressive incidents involving Tsarukyan, one of da Matta's own fighters. [ref: Marcos Parrumpinha critica estilo de vida e farras de Carlos Prates: 'Não é exemplo', Super Lutas] That month, on the Mundo da Luta podcast, he called some MMA social media pages "gossip channels" that disrespect athletes without consequence, and suggested a trip to the police station for bullying would stop them. On Moicano's and Tsarukyan's own online provocations, he said: "Sometimes I don't agree with either one's attitude, but I'm not their father."

==Personal life==
Da Matta says he has never drunk alcohol, smoked or used drugs. He is married and has two children. Calling himself "an extremely superstitious person", he avoids naming his fighters as favorites before a bout.

==Championships and accomplishments==
===Brazilian jiu-jitsu===
*International Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Federation
**World Championship gold (1996, purple belt, featherweight)
**World Championship silver (2000, black belt, featherweight)
**Pan American Championship silver (1999, black belt, 70 kg)
**World Master Championship bronze (2017, master 3, super-heavyweight)
**World Master Championship silver (2020, master 4, super-heavyweight)
