data.title: Clash of the Thundermans
data.text:
----

Clash of the Thundermans is a 2026 American superhero comedy film directed by Trevor Kirschner and written by Jed Spingarn, Sean W. Cunningham and Mark Dworkin. It is the second film in The Thundermans franchise, following The Thundermans Return (2024). The film stars Kira Kosarin, Jack Griffo, Maya Le Clark, Chris Tallman, Rosa Blasi, Addison Riecke and Diego Velazquez reprising their roles as the Thunderman family, with Ariel Winter joining the cast.

Clash of the Thundermans premiered simultaneously on Nickelodeon and Paramount+ on September 3, 2026.

== Plot ==
As the Thundermans are being rewarded at the Hall of Heroes by Super President Kickbutt, the Replicator, a villain Hank locked up years ago, crashes the ceremony. As the family fight off his various duplicates, Chloe has a sudden power surge which blows the family away. Not thinking too much of it yet, Max scans the duplicates to find the real Replicator and Phoebe freezes him.

Afterwards, Barb takes Chloe to the super doctor to determine what happened. When they return home, Chloe announces that she is developing a new power: enerkinesis, the power to manipulate energy; however, she can't control the power yet. On the Superhero Evening News, it is announced that Kickbutt may be stepping down and Phoebe may be taking her place. Kickbutt later calls the team and tells them to meet her in her office.

At her office, Kickbutt discusses Chloe's new power and its potential danger. Because of her inability to control her power, Kickbutt wants to send Chloe to Top Secret Hero League School for Gifted Supes (T.S.H.L.S.F.G.S.) so she can learn to control it. Kickbutt introduces the family to Cognita, the school's principal with hyper-intelligence, who shows them a presentation of the school's offerings.

After they return home, the family discuss the prospect of sending Chloe to the school. While Chloe goes upstairs, the family becomes split on the decision: Phoebe, Billy, and Barb want Chloe to stay while Max, Nora, and Hank feel she should go. An argument breaks out, and when Chloe breaks it up, her powers activate and destroy most the house. Kickbutt and Cognita show up for Chloe, the latter giving her a numbing agent to temporarily stop her powers. Phoebe refuses to give Chloe up, joined by Billy and Barb. Phoebe freezes Kickbutt, Cognita, Max, Nora, and Hank before making an escape with Billy, Barb, and Chloe.

Dr. Colosso unfreezes Max using a hair dryer, the latter unfreezing the rest of them. The escapees are declared fugitives of the Hero League, and Max is directed to lead what's left of the T-Force to retrieve Chloe. Meanwhile, Phoebe, Billy, Barb, and Chloe go to the Hall of Heroes Museum to retrieve Antidote Man's Lasso of Healing to undo the numbing of Chloe's powers. They are almost apprehended by Max, Nora, and Chloe, but Dr. Colosso crashes the Thunder Van into the wall, inadvertently giving them an escape route.

They go to the barn of Mee-Maw, Barb's mother whose power is sonic screaming, and she successfully uses the Lasso of Healing on Chloe, restoring her powers. Meanwhile, Max invents a quasiparticle thermo-energy detector to detect Chloe's power and track her location, which Chloe inadvertently reveals while Phoebe tries to teach her to control her power. After failing to control her power multiple times, cooking a chicken (that Dr. Colosso was flirting with) and destroying a tractor in the process, the other half of the family arrive for Chloe, but they are still denied her; this results in a fight between the two halves, with Phoebe facing Max, Barb facing Hank, and Billy facing Nora. Mee-Maw uses her sonic scream to halt the fighting, and Chloe announces she will go to the school.

She teleports into Kickbutt's office, resigning herself. One of Cognita's students, Granite Girl, enters and calcifies Kickbutt into a statue of stone. Afterwards, Cognita reveals her true intentions to utilize Chloe's power and Granite Girl takes her away. Back at home, the rest of the family are trying to clean up their destroyed home when two Hero League officials show up with news of an incident. Kickbutt, half-freed from the stone, and Captain Chisel appear. The family learns that Cognita is evil and took Chloe and six of her other students off the grid, but don't yet know her intentions.

Chloe is taken to Facility X, Cognita's lair, where she is introduced to Cognita's six students: Granite Girl, Magneteen, Toxic Todd, Sludgerella, and Desk Boy, all of whom are brainwashed. She reveals her full intentions to use Chloe's enerkinesis to obliterate all of Metroburg. Back in Hiddenville, the family realize they must come back together as a team to rescue Chloe; Max and Phoebe do so reluctantly. Meanwhile, Chloe is handcuffed and a headnamd is attached to her head. However, her legs aren't restricted, allowing her to kick Cognita into Magneteen, who gets stuck. As Cognita and the other students free her, Chloe uses the time to teleport to her wristwatch and send a distress signal to her family, allowing them to pinpoint her location.

When they arrive at Facility X, they are confronted by Cognita's students, who were directed to fight them. Meanwhile, Cognita brainwashes Chloe and then uses her power to create an energy storm. After the rest of the family defeat Cognita's students, they confront Cognita directly. Cognita uses Chloe against the family, and Hank grabs a table to hide behind when Chloe tries to use her enerkinesis on them. Per Billy's idea to focus on Cognita, Max tries to get Cognita's headband off with his telekinesis, to no avail as it is lined with Thundertanium. When Cognita tries to shoot Max with a blaster, Phoebe jumps in the way to save him and she is shot unconscious.

Angered, Max dodges Cognita's next shots and unscrews her headband, dumbing her down and allowing him to grab the blaster and shoot her and freeze her. Barb uses the Lasso of Healing to revive Phoebe, and they head outside to deal with the energy storm. They urge Chloe to control her enerkinesis stop the energy storm, and she succeeds. When they arrive at home, it is revealed that Colosso had gotten the house fixed up, using Hank's money. Kickbutt calls, offering Phoebe the position of Super President, which she declines to focus on her bettering relationship with Max, to everyone's surprise.

Afterwards, Phoebe goes down to Max's lair to talk to him, but it is revealed through a hologram he made that he had left for the sake of Phoebe becoming Super President, which she revokes her previous decision and takes on the position. Meanwhile, an unnamed hero in black stops three men from stealing a kid's bike. Noticing his freeze breath, the kid immediately assumes he is Max, to which he denies, and he flies away with a jetpack. At the end of the film, Dr. Colosso is shown to be back at Mee-Maw's barn, using the Lasso of Healing to bring back the chicken.

== Cast ==

* Kira Kosarin as Phoebe Thunderman [ref: Nickelodeon Greenlights ‘Clash Of The Thundermans’ Movie; Ariel Winter Joins Cast, [[Deadline Hollywood]
* Jack Griffo as Max Thunderman
* Maya Le Clark as Chloe Thunderman
* Chris Tallman as Hank Thunderman
* Rosa Blasi as Barb Thunderman
* Addison Riecke as Nora Thunderman
* Diego Velazquez as Billy Thunderman
* Ariel Winter as Cognita
* Daniele Gaither as Super President Kickbutt
* Robyn Bradley as Mee-Maw
* Ben Van Huis as Replicator
* Clifton Murray as the Newsflash
* Peyton Feltham as Granite Girl
* Marco Walker-Ng as Captain Chisel
* Tatyana Decker as Lieutenant #1
* Paul Almedia as Lieutenant #2
* Keith Dallas as Ralph Riggins
* Kingston Chan as Mangateen
* Sebastian Billingsley-Rodriguez as Kid Ricochet
* Liam Louis as Desk Boy
* Grace Sunar as Sludgerella
* Rajan Lalli as Toxic Todd

=== Voices ===
* Dana Snyder as Dr. Colosso
* Piotr Michael as Replicator
* Shelby Young as Slideshow Narrator

== Production ==
=== Development ===
Prior to the film's official announcement, Production Weekly confirmed that Clash of the Thundermans was in the works on June 19, 2025. [ref: Production Weekly – Issue 1458 – Thursday, June 19, 2025 / 142 Listings – 32 Pages, Production Weekly] Nickelodeon officially announced the film the following month on July 31.

=== Casting ===
Upon the film's announcement, it was reported that Kira Kosarin, Jack Griffo, Maya Le Clark, Chris Tallman, Rosa Blasi, Addison Riecke, and Diego Velazquez would reprise their roles as the Thunderman family, with Ariel Winter joining the cast as a new character named Cognita. Dana Snyder and Daniele Gaither would later be reported to be reprising their roles as Dr. Colosso and Super President Kickbutt respectively, alongside newcomer Robyn Bradley, starring as Mee-Maw. [ref: Clash of the Thundermans Premiere Date and Key Art Unveiled, Vital Thrills]

=== Filming ===
Principal photography began on July 31, 2025, in Vancouver, British Columbia. On August 10, filming suffered a temporary delay due to a bomb threat, [ref: Nickelodeon Movie's Production Shut Down After Bomb Threat, PopCulture.com] which was proven false. Filming wrapped in September. [ref: 1. CLASH OF THE THUNDERMANS is wrapped and will premiere on Paramount Plus 2026 ⚡️...]

== Soundtrack ==
An official soundtrack was released on September 3, 2026, featuring 21 songs from the film, composed by Frederik Wiedmann. [ref: ‘Clash of the Thundermans’ Soundtrack Album Details, Film Music Reporter]

== Release ==
On July 22, 2026, it was announced that Clash of the Thundermans would release on September 3, 2026 on Nickelodeon and Paramount+ simultaneously. [ref: Paramount+'s 13-Year Superhero Franchise Officially Sets 2026 Return With First Poster For New Movie, Screen Rant] The trailer for the film was released on August 6, 2026. [ref: 8 Years Later, Nickelodeon’s Bonkers Superhero Family Returns in New Trailer [Exclusive], [[Collider.com]

== Reception ==
=== Critical response ===
Mama's Geekys Tessa Smith gave Clash of the Thundermans a very positive review, praising its humor, relatable family conflict, nostalgic charm, and unpredictable story, especially enjoying how Chloe’s new powers serve as a metaphor for growing up and how the family’s disagreement over her future gives the movie genuine emotional stakes. [ref: The Clash of the Thundermans Movie Review, Mama's Geeky] Common Sense Media reviewer Ashley Moulton rated the film a 3-out-of-5 stars, arguing that the film is an unoriginal, trope-heavy superhero comedy with unnecessary fights, but fans may enjoy its silly humor and heartfelt ending. [ref: Clash of the Thundermans, Common Sense Media]

data.title: Doin' Damage
data.text:
Doin' Damage is the debut LP by American hip-hop group JVC Force, released in 1988 through B-Boy Records. The album includes the song "Strong Island", one of the group's best-known recordings. The group consisted of MC's AJ Rok and B-Luv and DJ Curt Cazal. [ref: J.V.C. Force:: Doin' Damage, RapReviews]

== Reception ==

=== Contemporary ===

In its September 24, 1988 issue, Cash Box reviewed Doin' Damage in its "independant way" column. The review characterized JVC Force's approach as informal and humorous, highlighting the variety of vocal styles on the album. It also praised the range of its samples and beats, and described B-Boy Records as a promising independent label in the contemporary rap scene. [ref: The Independent Way, Cash Box]

=== Retrospective ===

In a 2008 review for RapReviews, Steve "Flash" Juon gave the album a score of 7.5 out of 10. He praised the chemistry between the group's members and the album's sampling and production, while noting that some of its rhymes could sound simplistic to modern listeners. Juon also discussed the later reissue of the album by Traffic Entertainment Group in 2005.

data.title: Rodney Zelenka
data.text:
Rodney Zelenka (born 1953) is a Panamanian painter and visual artist whose figurative and mixed-media work explores migration, violence, social exclusion and the exercise of power. He represented Panama at the centennial Venice Biennale in 1995, as part of the Istituto Italo-Latino Americano exhibition, and at the 23rd São Paulo Art Biennial in 1996. He was one of fourteen artists in Crosscurrents: Contemporary Painting from Panama 1968–1998 at the Americas Society in New York, and has since exhibited in Panama, the United States, Mexico and elsewhere.

== Early life and education ==
Zelenka was born in Panama City in 1953. He has said that his parents came to Panama from Europe to escape the Holocaust. From 1962 to 1969 he took courses with the painters Alfredo Sinclair and Guillermo Trujillo at Panama's Escuela de Bellas Artes. He studied at Cornell University in Ithaca, New York, from 1971 to 1977, majoring in economics with a minor in Latin American politics and taking courses in studio art. According to his published curriculum vitae, he spent extended periods between 1979 and 1989 working alongside the artists Julio Zachrisson in Madrid, Rodolfo Abularach in New York and Jessy Patrick Allen in California.

== Career ==
=== Early exhibitions and international biennials ===
In 1979 Zelenka received a prize at the Gulf Oil Exhibition at Panama's Museo de Arte Contemporáneo, and in 1980 he held his first solo exhibition at Galería Arte 80 in Panama City. Writing in La Estrella de Panamá, the artist and writer Arístides Ureña Ramos placed Zelenka alongside Brooke Alfaro and Tabo Toral among the Panamanian artists who had spent time in New York in the 1970s and joined the local exhibition scene in the early 1980s.

In the late 1980s and early 1990s he exhibited at New York galleries such as Gallery Revel (1987) and Cast Iron Gallery (1993), and in Japan at Shone Okuda Gallery in Tokyo (1989) and at venues in Osaka and Nagoya (1990). In 1994 he took part in the Bienal de Cuenca in Ecuador and the Caribbean Biennial in Santo Domingo.

In 1995 Zelenka represented Panama at the 46th Venice Biennale, the centennial edition of the exhibition. He was one of nine artists from nine countries in the exhibition organized by the Istituto Italo-Latino Americano (IILA) at the Chiesa di San Giovanni Novo in Venice, for which Fernando Macotela served as commissioner, assisted by Alessandra Bonanni.

The following year he represented Panama at the 23rd São Paulo Art Biennial, held from 5 October to 8 December 1996 under the general curator Nelson Aguilar. The official catalogue devoted several pages to Zelenka and reproduced paintings including Asesino del Tiempo (1996), El Color de la Supervivencia (1996) and Escape en Cámara Lenta de Hueco Negro (1995). In an accompanying essay, the art critic Phyllis Braff described how the work combined tightly ordered patterns, figurative scenes and psychological tension.

Also in 1996, Zelenka held exhibitions at the Museo de la Nación in Lima, the Casa de la Cultura Ecuatoriana in Quito and the Museo Municipal de Arte Moderno in Cuenca. He later recalled that the Lima exhibition, Canto a la guerra y el fuego, used suspended mattresses to evoke the possessions carried by people fleeing disasters. His exhibition Tensión was shown at Panama's Museo de Arte Contemporáneo in 1997 and at the Museo de Arte Moderno in Santo Domingo in 1998.

In 1998 Zelenka took part in Crosscurrents: Contemporary Painting from Panama 1968–1998, curated by Mónica E. Kupfer and Edward J. Sullivan, which ran at the Americas Society in New York from 2 May to 31 July. The survey brought together fourteen Panamanian painters whose work had developed amid the political and cultural changes the country had undergone since 1968. His exhibition record also lists Panamanian art biennials up to 2002 and an international biennial in Buenos Aires that year.

=== Exhibitions since 2020 ===
In 2020 Zelenka took part in Everything Is Art, Everything Is Politics, an online group exhibition organized by Elga Wimmer PCC and curated by Wimmer and Berta Sichel. Writing about his paintings, Mark Bloch reported that the curators had compared Zelenka's treatment of the human body to the work of Leon Golub. According to the artist's exhibition history, the show was later presented at the Museo Casa Pintada of the Fundación Cristóbal Gabarrón in Mula, Spain, in 2021–2022.

Dominion and Frailty, curated by Wimmer and Thalia Vrachopoulos, was shown at the Tenri Cultural Institute in New York in November and December 2022. The paintings dealt with displacement, poverty and unequal relations of power. In their reviews, Mary Hrbacek and Bloch discussed how the show set grey human figures against brightly colored everyday belongings, and the journalist Lucy Komisar interviewed Zelenka about his use of suitcases and his concern with abusive power.

In Mexico, a run of exhibitions began in 2022 with Mística social at the Centro Estatal de las Artes in Tecate, Baja California, which later traveled to Ensenada and Tijuana. In 2023 the Museo de Arte de Ciudad Juárez showed A ras de suelo, about 50 works dealing with migration, homelessness, violence and abuses of authority.

Also in 2023, Zelenka showed Rivers of Babylon at Lichtundfire in New York, co-curated by Wimmer and Priska Juschka. Reviewing the show, the art critic Robert C. Morgan related its works on paper to imagery of mass migration and discarded possessions.

In 2024 he took part in No Trespassing: Artists Comment on the Migration Crisis, curated by Vrachopoulos at the Anya and Andrew Shiva Gallery of John Jay College of Criminal Justice. He contributed ten paintings on war and the abuse of power, which he said were prompted by Andy Warhol's electric-chair imagery. From 31 May to 18 August that year, the Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Querétaro presented Realidades incomprensibles, curated by Francisco "Pancho" López: more than forty works in painting, drawing, sculpture and installation, arranged around migration and the exercise of power.

Suitcase Stories, curated by Gladys Turner Bosso, was shown at the Galería Juan Manuel Cedeño in Panama City in 2024 and explored the belongings and experiences of people displaced by war and hunger. At Lichtundfire, Semiotics of a Spider (2024), curated by Wimmer and Juschka, developed the artist's recurring spider motif across paintings, sculpture, video and drawings.

In March 2025 Zelenka opened two exhibitions in Mexico City, both curated by López: Estéticas de la coerción, with work made between 2022 and 2024, at the Casa de la Primera Imprenta de América of the Universidad Autónoma Metropolitana; and Personalidades desubicadas, with works dating from 1997 to 2021, in the cultural display cases of the Zócalo/Tenochtitlan station of the Mexico City Metro. Later that year, Suitcase Stories was presented again at the Centro Cultural Teatro García Carrillo during the Fiesta Internacional de las Artes in Saltillo.

Night Travelers, Zelenka's third solo exhibition at Lichtundfire, ran from 4 to 28 March 2026 and was curated by Juschka.

== Artistic practice and critical reception ==
Zelenka works in painting, drawing, sculpture, installation and video. His pictures often set carefully rendered figures or ordinary objects against comparatively abstract fields. In her essay for the 1996 São Paulo Biennial, Braff described images of prisoners, isolated individuals and fish within strict, sometimes mosaic-like patterned spaces, and linked their spatial arrangement to psychological pressure and fantastical narrative. Reviewing Dominion and Frailty in 2022, Hrbacek characterized his approach as "merging realism with abstract non-descriptive pictorial space". Mexican coverage of his exhibitions has associated his imagery with Latin American surrealism.

Displacement has become a recurring subject: his canvases and works on paper include suitcases, furniture, clothes and other belongings that can stand in for the people forced to abandon them. Bloch noted his use of striped clothing reminiscent of concentration-camp uniforms and his recurring animals, among them cranes, turkeys, fish and spiders. The works on paper in Rivers of Babylon combined acrylic and ink with metal pins and 22-karat gold leaf. In Semiotics of a Spider, he used the spider and its web to explore barriers, entrapment and border crossings.

Bloch has also connected Zelenka's subject matter to Panama's years of military rule, relating the artist's political imagery in 2020 to his experience of the regime established in 1968 and the later rule of Manuel Noriega. In a 2022 interview with Komisar, Zelenka described his aim as denunciation rather than changing viewers' minds: "I just feel very uncomfortable with abusive power."

== Selected works ==
* Orange Carps in a Water Lily Pond (1994), acrylic on canvas
* Escape en Cámara Lenta de Hueco Negro (1995), acrylic on canvas
* Asesino del Tiempo (1996), acrylic on canvas
* Manhole (2020), acrylic on canvas
* Waiting Has a Price (2021), acrylic on canvas
* Web Masters (2021), acrylic on canvas
* Golden Wall (2022), gold leaf, acrylic, ink and metal pins on paper
* Migration Road (2023), acrylic, gold leaf, ink and metal pins on paper
* Three Sunsets (2026), acrylic and aluminum foil on canvas

== Awards ==
* 1979 – Prize, Gulf Oil Exhibition, Museo de Arte Contemporáneo, Panama
* 1986 – Honorable mention, national art competition, Instituto Nacional de Cultura, Panama
* 1997 – Honorable mention, 2nd Egyptian International Print Triennale, Giza

data.title: James Newsham
data.text:
James Newsham of Chadshunt, Warwickshire ( – November 1769) was an British politician. He sat as MP for St Germans from 1741 till 1747 and St Mawes from 10 December 1754 till 1761. [ref: NEWSHAM, James (1715-69), of Chadshunt, Warws., History of Parliament Online]

He was the oldest son of John Newsham of Chadshunt by his second wife. He was educated privately under David Mallet. He went on a Grand Tour in 1735. He died unmarried. He succeeded to estates at Chadshunt in 1724, to the Kentish property of his mother in 1756, and to the property of his aunt Elizabeth Eliot in 1765.

John Birken of Kingston upon Hull, Yorkshire () was an English politician. He sat as MP for Kingston upon Hull in 1402. [ref: BIRKEN, John, of Kingston-upon-Hull, Yorks., History of Parliament Online]

He also served as bailiff of Kingston upon Hull from Michaelmas 1379 till 1380; and mayor of Kingston upon Hull from 1386 till 1387, and 1400 till 1401.

By March 1408, he was married to Margery.

data.text:
The 2026–27 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team will represent Gonzaga University during the 2026–27 NCAA Division I men's basketball season. The Bulldogs, also unofficially nicknamed the "Zags", will be led by twenty-eighth-year head coach Mark Few and will play their home games at the McCarthey Athletic Center in Spokane, Washington as a member of the Pac-12 Conference. This will mark Gonzaga's first season as members of the Pac-12 Conference after spending the previous forty-seven seasons as members of the West Coast Conference. [ref: Gonzaga Officially Joins Pac-12 Conference, Finds Out Tournament Details, The Slipper Still Fits] [ref: Gonzaga officially joins the Pac-12 as new era begins, Gonzaga Bulldogs On SI] [ref: GU officially joins Pac-12, emphasizing regionality and elite basketball competition, The Gonzaga Bulletin]

==Previous season==
Gonzaga finished the 2025-26 season 31–4, 16–2 in the West Coast Conference to finish tied for first in the conference. As the top seed in the WCC Tournament they would defeat 4-seed Oregon State in the Semifinal to advance to the Championship against 3-seed Santa Clara. [ref: Gonzaga beats Oregon State to advance to WCC championship game, Gonzaga Bulldogs On SI] [ref: Gonzaga men's hoops defeat Oregon State, advance to WCC tournament championship, KXLY kxly.com] The Zags defeated the Broncos 79–68 to claim the tournament championship. [ref: Gonzaga secures final WCC Tournament championship with gritty win over Santa Clara, Gonzaga Bulldogs On SI] [ref: No. 12 Gonzaga beats Santa Clara 79-68 to win the WCC tournament in its final appearance, AP News] As a result, they received the conference's autobid to the NCAA Tournament as the 3-seed in the West region. [ref: Gonzaga Earns No. 3 Seed in West Region, The Slipper Still Fits] Gonzaga defeated 14-seed Kennesaw State in the First round before falling to 11-seed Texas 68–74 in the Second round to end their season. [ref: Texas Longhorns advance in NCAA tournament after beating Gonzaga, FOX Local] [ref: Gonzaga men shocked by Texas in second round of NCAA tournament, The Seattle Times]

data.title: LOT Polish Airlines Flight 6883
data.text:
LOT Polish Airlines Flight 6883 was a scheduled cargo flight from Warsaw, Poland to Beirut, Lebanon with a stopover in Varna, Bulgaria. [ref: Tragedy An-12 SP-LZA on 13.05.1977. – Polot, polot.net] [ref: ] On 14 May 1977, the aircraft operating the flight crashed into terrain near Aramoun, Lebanon, while attempting to land at Beirut International Airport in poor weather conditions. All nine crew members on board were killed.

== Background ==

=== Aircraft ===
The aircraft involved was an Antonov An-12BP registered as SP-LZA, delivered to LOT Polish Airlines in 1966, flying with the company from June to July 1967 and again from August 1976 until the accident flight. It was powered by four Ivchenko AI-20M engines. [ref: Accident Antonov An-12BP SP-LZA, Friday 13 May 1977, Aviation Safety Network] The aircraft was leased by LOT Polish Airlines from Poland's 13th Transport Aviation Regiment. [ref: Katastrofy wojskowych transportowców, TVN24] The aircraft was operated by military pilots in civilian uniforms. [ref: 1977 Zapomniany lot 6883, Newsweek Polska] This facilitated the passage of the aircraft over countries that barred military aircraft from using their airspace. [ref: Samolot z Polakami rozbił się o górę. Bliscy nie wierzą władzom, Fakt] The cargo onboard consisted of food, industrial products, medicine, and weapons. [ref: Brawurowy lot ku wolności na skrzydłach „Wiedeńczyka”, Dziennik Polski]

=== Crew members ===
The crew consisted of captain Henryk Bajer who had accumulated a total of 6,200 flight hours.

The first officer, Tadeusz Florek, had accumulated a total of 5,800 flight hours.

The remaining crew members which included flight navigator Jan Kowalik, Jerzy Grzywalski, Adam Rybak, Janusz Lech, Kazimierz Krupa and two unidentified crew members had between 3,000 - 5,500 flight hours.
== Accident ==
The flight departed from Varna Airport at 05:30 AM local time. On approach to Beirut Airport, the crew asked for clearance to land on runway 21 and a request to descend to 1,500 feet. Moments later, the aircraft struck power lines, trees, and stone terraces at 2,100 feet before crashing into Mount Douair near Aramoun, Lebanon, 8 kilometers southeast of Beirut Airport at 08:45 AM local time.All 9 occupants onboard were killed.

== Investigation ==
The investigation proposed that the most probable cause of the crash was difficulty by the crew in interpreting the messages transmitted by air traffic control, possibly due to a language barrier. It was found that the controller had to repeat his instructions to the crew while on approach twice for them to understand but the crew failed to acknowledge them.

Disputes from various agencies debated about the cause of the crash due to having no records of the crash and were assumed locked away, labelled as "TOP SECRET" (due to Poland being under socialist ideologies in 1977 until 1991). It was first thought that the weather had something to do with the crash, however, examination of the photos in the documents recovered showed that weather was not a cause of the crash.

In 1977, Lebanon was ravaged by war, and many feared that the aircraft had been shot down. Also, the plane was carrying cargo that included weapons, which hinted at political unrest between Poland and Lebanon and the Lebanese thought the plane was a threat and about to attack. Two weeks earlier, while taking off from Beirut, the aircraft had been shot at, causing in damage to the airframe.

The investigation team was not able to definitively determine the cause of the crash due to the documents being locked away, even after the fall of the Soviet Union in 1991. The crash remains unsolved to this day.

data.title: Chrysolepicynips
data.text:
Chrysolepicynips is a genus of gall wasp. The genus was erected in 2026 and encompasses former members of the genus Dryocosmus which use chinquapins as their hosts. [ref: Confirmation, consequences and causes of extensive polyphyly in the oak gall wasp genus Dryocosmus (Hymenoptera: Cynipidae: Cynipini), Insect Systematics and Diversity] [ref: Genus Chrysolepicynips, Gallformers] [ref: Not All Oak Gall Wasps Gall Oaks: The Description of Dryocosmus rileypokei, A New, Apostate Species of Cynipini from California, Proceedings of the Entomological Society of Washington] [ref: New species of Dryocosmus Giraud gallwasps from California (Hymenoptera: Cynipidae: Cynipini) galling Chrysolepis Hjelmq. (Fagaceae), Zootaxa] It can be separated from Dryocosmus based on the following characteristics: Presence of white setae on head and mesosoma; mesoscutellar foveae divided by an elevated narrow central carina; and lateral propodeal carinae being sub-parallel.

==Species==
* Chrysolepicynips castanopsidis (Beutenmüller, 1917) (Chinquapin flower gall wasp)
* Chrysolepicynips demartinii (Melika, Nicholls & Stone, 2018)
* Chrysolepicynips juliae (Melika, Nicholls & Stone, 2018)
* Chrysolepicynips rileypokei (Morita & Buffington, 2009)

data.title: 2026–27 Utah State Aggies men's basketball team
data.text:
The 2026–27 Utah State Aggies men's basketball team will represent Utah State University during the 2026–27 NCAA Division I men's basketball season. The Aggies will be led by first-year head coach Ben Jacobson and will play their home games at the Smith Spectrum in Logan, Utah as a member of the Pac-12 Conference. This will mark Utah State's first season as members of the Pac-12 Conference after spending the previous thirteen seasons as members of the Mountain West Conference. [ref: After nearly two years of waiting, Utah State's Pac-12 era begins, The Herald Journal] [ref: Utah State officially begins Pac-12 era, ABC4 Utah (KTVX)] [ref: Utah State celebrates its new era of Pac-12 membership, Deseret News]

==Previous season==
Utah State finished the 2025-26 season 29–7, 15–5 in the Mountain West Conference to finish first in the conference. As the top seed in the Mountain West Tournament they would defeat 8-seed UNLV in the Quarterfinals and 5-seed Nevada in the Semifinals to advance to the Championship against 2-seed San Diego State. The Aggies defeated the Aztecs 73-62 to win claim the tournament championship. [ref: SDSU busts in Mountain West championship, falling to No. 1-seed Utah State, The Daily Aztec] [ref: Utah State beats San Diego State to win the Mountain West tournament title, Deseret News] As a result, they received the conference's autobid to the NCAA Tournament as the 9-seed in the West region. Utah State defeated 8-seed Villanova in the First round before falling to top-seeded Arizona 66–78 in the Second round to end their season. [ref: Arizona withstands Utah State comeback to reach Sweet 16 Utah State proves its toughness in Round of 32 loss to Arizona, KSL Sports] [ref: Bradley scores 18 points to lead No. 1-seeded Arizona past Utah State 78-66 to reach Sweet 16, AP News]

Two days after the season's conclusion, head coach Jerrod Calhoun left to take the same position at his alma mater, Cincinnati. [ref: Cincinnati hires Jerrod Calhoun: Utah State coach leaving after two years to guide his alma mater, CBS Sports] [ref: Utah State's Jerrod Calhoun returns to Cincinnati as coach, www.espn.com] On March 30, 2026, the school named Northern Iowa head coach Ben Jacobson as the team's new head coach. [ref: Utah State hires Ben Jacobson as new men’s basketball head coach, The Utah Statesman] [ref: Utah State hires Northern Iowa's Ben Jacobson as coach, www.espn.com]

The 2026–27 New Mexico Lobos men's basketball team will represent the University of New Mexico during the 2026–27 NCAA Division I men's basketball season. The Lobos, led by second-year head coach Eric Olen, will play their home games at The Pit in Albuquerque, New Mexico, as members of the Mountain West Conference.

==Previous season==
The Lobos finished the 2025–26 season 26–11 overall and 13–7 in Mountain West play, finishing third in the conference standings. [ref: Eric Olen and UNM Agree to New Five-Year Deal, New Mexico Lobos] As the No. 3 seed in the Mountain West tournament, New Mexico defeated 11th-seeded San Jose State in the quarterfinals before falling to second-seeded San Diego State in the semifinals.

New Mexico received a bid to the National Invitation Tournament, where the Lobos defeated Sam Houston, George Washington and Saint Joseph's to advance to the NIT semifinals. The Lobos' season ended with a 74–69 loss to Tulsa at Hinkle Fieldhouse. The appearance was New Mexico's first trip to the NIT semifinals since 1990.

Following the season, Olen agreed to a new five-year contract that will keep him at New Mexico through the 2030–31 season. [ref: Eric Olen and UNM Agree to New Five-Year Deal, New Mexico Lobos]

data.title: John Bexle
data.text:
John Bexle was an English politician. He sat as MP for Hastings in 1406. [ref: BEXLE, John., History of Parliament Online]

He was perhaps the son of the portsman William Bexle, who had held land at Wilting near Hastings in the 1370s. John had claimed exemption from taxation during the early years of Henry IV's reign in the same place where William held land. He had also once been a tenant on the manor of Knelle.

data.title: Michelle Cook (sheriff)
data.text:
Michelle Cook is an American law enforcement officer serving as Sheriff of Clay County, Florida since September 2020. She is the first woman to hold the office in the county's history and, as of 2026, is one of two women serving as sheriff in Florida, alongside Miami-Dade County Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz. [ref: She's the Sheriff: Michelle Cook starts early in Clay County, Florida Politics] [ref: Florida Sheriffs Association Celebrates Graduation of 2nd Annual Women's Leadership Academy, Florida Sheriffs Association] She was elected in 2020 after defeating incumbent Darryl Daniels, who had been suspended from office by Governor Ron DeSantis following his arrest, and was reelected in 2024 with about 80 percent of the vote. [ref: Daniels suspended as Clay County sheriff following arrest, Clay Today] [ref: Gov. DeSantis appoints temporary replacement for Florida sheriff, ABC Action News] [ref: Michelle Cook reelected as Clay County sheriff after defeating Darryl Daniels again, News4Jax]

== Early life and education ==
Cook is a native of Green Cove Springs, Florida, in Clay County, and a graduate of Clay High School. [ref: Clay Sheriff Michelle Cook lists her priorities for 2nd term, Jacksonville Today] She holds a bachelor's degree in criminal justice with a minor in public administration, and a master's degree in criminal justice, both from the University of North Florida, and is a graduate of the FBI-LEEDA Command Leadership Institute. [ref: Sheriff Michelle Cook, Clay County Sheriff's Office]

== Law enforcement career ==
Cook joined the Jacksonville Sheriff's Office in 1992. In 2016, she was promoted to head the agency's Department of Patrol and Enforcement. [ref: Michelle Cook leads by example at Sheriff's Office; recently promoted to run patrol and enforcement, Jacksonville Daily Record] She retired from the agency as director of patrol and enforcement in 2017, and became chief of the Atlantic Beach Police Department in 2017.

== 2020 sheriff election ==
Cook left the Atlantic Beach Police Department in early 2020 to run for Sheriff of Clay County. [ref: Michelle Cook launches bid for Clay County Sheriff, Florida Politics] The incumbent, Darryl Daniels, was arrested on August 13, 2020, and charged with tampering with evidence and giving false reports to law enforcement, charges that stemmed from an investigation into his relationship with a subordinate. Governor DeSantis suspended him the next day and appointed Florida Department of Law Enforcement agent Matt Walsh as interim sheriff. [ref: DeSantis names FDLE's Matt Walsh as interim sheriff of Clay County, News4Jax] Cook won the August 18, 2020, Republican primary, with Daniels finishing second with 29 percent of the vote. A write-in candidate withdrew from the general election race, leaving Cook as the next sheriff. [ref: Cook to be Clay County's next sheriff as write-in candidate withdraws, WJCT News] DeSantis asked Cook to take office ahead of the normal January inauguration date, and she was sworn in as Sheriff of Clay County on September 1, 2020, becoming the first woman to hold the office.

== Tenure as sheriff ==
In March 2021, the National Sheriffs' Association recognized Cook, at the time the only woman serving as sheriff in Florida, for Women's History Month. [ref: National Sheriff's Association recognizes Florida's only current woman sheriff: Michelle Cook, News4Jax] In 2023, she helped launch the Signal 35 Fund, a nonprofit that provides emergency financial assistance to first responders in Clay County. [ref: Clay County leaders announce launch of public safety initiative to help first responders facing personal emergencies, News4Jax] Cook and the Clay County Sheriff's Office are also founding partners of the Northeast Florida Inter-Agency Child Exploitation and Persons Trafficking (INTERCEPT) Task Force, a multi-agency initiative combating human trafficking and child exploitation. [ref: Leaders examine sex trafficking awareness, Clay Today]

Clay Today reported that crime rates in the county fell even as its population grew. [ref: Clay crime rates drop as county grows, Clay Today] In 2025, her office announced a collaboration with the state to help solve cold cases. [ref: Clay County Sheriff's Office announces collaboration with state to help solve cold cases, News4Jax]

In March 2026, Cook was recognized by President Donald Trump during a Women's History Month event at the White House. [ref: Clay County Sheriff Michelle Cook honored by President Trump at Women's History Month event at White House, News4Jax] [ref: Trump recognizes Clay County Sheriff Cook for Women's History Month, First Coast News]

== 2024 re-election ==
Cook filed for re-election in May 2023 and ran unopposed in the Republican primary. [ref: Michelle Cook files for re-election for Clay County Sheriff, Action News Jax] In the November 2024 general election, she again faced Daniels, who had been acquitted of all charges in 2022, and won with around 80 percent of the vote. [ref: Former Clay County sheriff acquitted of crimes against his mistress will be on 2024 ballot, First Coast News] [ref: Incumbent Clay County Sheriff Michelle Cook secures reelection, First Coast News]

== Boards and affiliations ==
Cook serves as the District 2 representative on the Florida Sheriffs Association's board of directors, and chairs its Cold Case Advisory Commission. She also sits on the association's Legislative and Research committees. [ref: Sheriff Michelle Cook, Florida Sheriffs Association] Other affiliations include the Florida Department of Law Enforcement's Regional Domestic Security Task Force, the Northeast Florida High-Intensity Drug Trafficking Area executive board, and the Florida Commission for Law Enforcement Accreditation, where she serves as a commissioner.

data.text:
----

Coral Edge LRT station is a Light Rail Transit station in Punggol, Singapore. Coral Edge LRT station serves the east loop of the Punggol LRT line (PGLRT). Coral Edge is located along Punggol East, between Meridian and Riviera stations. Coral Edge station is designated [ref: https://www.lta.gov.sg/content/dam/ltagov/getting_around/public_transport/rail_network/pdf/SM_TEL4_Eng.pdf].

= History =

=== Punggol LRT line ===
Coral Edge station was first built as part of the LRT system that serves the Punggol area. The contract for designing and building the 13‑kilometre Punggol LRT system was awarded to a group that included Singapore Technologies Industrial Corporation [ref: https://www.sgpbusiness.com/company/Singapore-Technologies-Industrial-Corporation-Ltd], Mitsubishi Heavy Industries and Mitsubishi Corporation for S$656 million. The contract also covered the Sengkang LRT line.

Coral Edge station opened on 29 January 2005 along with the east loop stations of the Punggol LRT. Coral Edge station is located inside the Coral Edge precinct, which gives it its name.

=== Incidents ===
On 9 January 2020 a crack was found on one of the plinths between Coral Edge and Riviera stations. Coral Edge station closed one platform early for maintenance while trains kept using the platform. [ref: https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/transport/punggol-east-lrt-platform-closes-early-for-urgent-maintenance-works-after-crack?ref=search-results]

=== Details ===
Coral Edge station serves the east loop of the PGLRT Coral Edge station is located between Meridian and Riviera stations.

Like the stations on the Sengkang‑Punggol LRT [ref: https://www.lta.gov.sg/content/ltagov/en/getting_around/public_transport/rail_network/sengkang_punggol_lrt.html], Coral Edge station is wheelchair friendly. It has accessibility features such as lifts, wider fare gates [ref: https://www.sgtrains.com/technology-faregates.html] and tactile flooring.

data.title: Jace Shim
data.text:
Jace Shim (; also romanized Shim Jun-Kyu; born 1981) is a South Korean management consultant and author. He is the chief executive of TSCB Group (The Solution Company B), a consulting firm specializing in environmental, social, and governance (ESG) management, and an adjunct professor at Inha University. [ref: 교수소개: 심준규, Inha University] [ref: About B, TSCB Group] [ref: 【ESG 신간】그린북 THE GREEN BOOK / AI와 지속 가능성, Impact On] [ref: [신간] 그린북: ESG로 성과내는 사람들, Must News] He has written books on marketing, business models, ESG strategy, and digital currencies.

== Education ==
Shim received a Master of Business Administration from the University of Liverpool. He earned a doctorate in business administration from the Graduate School of Inha University in February 2025 with a dissertation on how buyers' perceptions of suppliers' ESG management affect social capital and supply chain performance. [ref: 구매자가 인식한 ESG 경영이 사회적 자본과 공급사슬 성과에 미치는 영향, Inha University Graduate School, Department of Business Administration]

== Career ==
Shim began his career at E-Land, where he worked in company-wide marketing planning and fashion brand management before leading brand management at the company's Chinese subsidiary. He later worked on product planning for the Chinese market at CJ IMC, part of CJ Group, and on strategy for entering Chinese online channels at Kolon FnC, part of Kolon Group.

He is the chief executive of TSCB Group, which provides ESG management strategy, sustainability reporting, third-party assurance of sustainability reports as an AccountAbility AA1000 licensed assurance provider, and support for companies entering overseas markets. At Inha University, he teaches business model innovation and digital marketing strategy.

== Writing ==
Shim's first book, FVS Marketing, was published in 2015 by Humancube, an imprint of the Munhakdongne publishing group. [ref: (좀 더 쉽고, 명쾌하고, 가치 있는,) FVS 마케팅, Humancube] His later books focus on ESG management, including ESG Strategy (2024), co-authored with Park Seung-wook and Kim Mi-hwa, [ref: 실천으로 완성하는 ESG 전략 = ESG way: traditional way, Hankyungsa] and The Green Book (2025), published by Provence. The ESG news outlet Impact On described The Green Book as focusing on how individual departments and job functions can turn ESG into concrete business results.

In 2026 he published several books on marketing and corporate strategy in the context of artificial intelligence and digital platforms, as well as books on stablecoins and digital currencies. [ref: AI 마케팅 패러다임: 검색에서 에이전트로 AI 시대를 이끄는 새로운 마케팅 전략, Raonbook] [ref: 비즈니스 모델 혁신 = Business model innovation: AI, 플랫폼, 데이터, ESG로 읽는 새로운 기업 전략, Raonbook] His book Winner Takes the Answer, published in Korean and English editions in October 2026, addresses generative engine optimization and proposes frameworks adapting established management models to AI-generated search results. [ref: Winner Takes the Answer: Marketing Strategy for the Age of Generative Engine Optimization, Raonbook Plus]

data.text:

= Goudy Text =

Goudy Text is a blackletter typeface designed by American type designer Frederic W. Goudy and released in 1928. Goudy based it on an earlier alphabet called Goudy Black, which he had drawn for his 1922 book Elements of Lettering. He designed it in the tradition of the early blackletter used by Johannes Gutenberg, rather than the more decorative styles common in the 19th century. The name “Goudy Text” was suggested by the Lanston Monotype company. [ref: Anatomy of a Typeface, Godine]

Goudy Text follows the Textura style of blackletter. Type historian Alexander S. Lawson describes it as similar to Textura letters from 15th-century Italy, with some French influence. Goudy also designed Lombardic Capitals as an alternative set of capitals for the typeface.

A digital version of Goudy Text is available from Lanston through Adobe Fonts. [ref: ]

data.text:
----

Vangiliya Yotana Ribeiro Filipe, affectionately known as Vânya Filipe, is an Angolan engineer working at the Ministry of Telecommunications, Information Technologies and Social Communication ([https://minttics.gov.ao/ao/ MINTTICS]) and holding the position of Deputy Director-General of Angola's National Space Program Management Office (GGPEN). [ref: Vangiliya Pereira, World Economic Forum] She is recognized as one of the 100 most influential women in Africa and for contributing to the advancement of knowledge, research, and technological innovation, especially in the Angolan space sector. [ref: Instagram, www.instagram.com]

== Biography ==
Vangiliya was born in the municipality of Sambizanga in Luanda, on December 17, 1984. She has been an employee of [https://minttics.gov.ao/ao/ MINTTICS] since March 2011. In July 2018, she began her duties as Deputy Director-General for the Technical and Scientific Area of ​​GGPEN. She holds a Bachelor's degree in Electronics and Telecommunications Engineering and a Master's degree in Mobile and Satellite Communications from the University of Glamorgan in Wales, United Kingdom. She specializes in Satellite Design, Architecture and Operating Principles and is certified by the Russian Space Agency as a Satellite Operator, having previously served as Flight Director for the Satellite Control and Mission Center Shift. She has worked in several telecommunications companies, specifically in the area of ​​supervision and installation of WiMAX, SHDL and ADSL network services. [ref: ]

She also served as a consultant for the State Secretariat for Telecommunications between March 2011 and 2014, and contributed to the training and capacity building of more than 60 specialists at GGPEN and in the launch of the AngoSat-1 and Angosat-2 telecommunications satellites. She was named one of the 100 Most Influential Women Engineers in Africa by the Federation of African Engineering Organisations ([https://faeo.org/ FAEO]) in 2021, in recognition of her contributions to engineering on the continent.

She, along with her ex-husband, has founded the angolan company [https://firmoper.ao/ FIRMOPER - SOCIEDADE COMERCIAL E INDUSTRIAL, Lda.] On May 7, 2026, she launched the book [https://www.facebook.com/platinaline/posts/lan%C3%A7ado-oficialmente-a-obra-biogr%C3%A1fica-uma-vida-servindo-vidas-o-legado-do-dr-ne/1449981070502593/ "UMA VIDA SERVINDO VIDAS - O LEGADO DO DR. NENÉ FILIPE"], a biographical work about her father, António Pedro Filipe Jr. (Nené Filipe), along with her company, FIRMOPER EDITORA. [ref: Instagram, www.instagram.com]

== Family ==
Vangiliya Filipe is the daughter of Angolan cardiologist and nationalist Dr. Nené Filipe and Member of Parliament and businesswoman Carla de Sousa. She has three children: Janira Hidianeth Filipe Pereira (November 28, 2004, Cunene, Angola), Jadiel Luciano Filipe Pereira (December 25, 2012, Lisbon, Portugal), and António Pedro Filipe Pereira (November 8, 2015, Lisbon, Portugal). Vangiliya is the younger sister of Ossanda Filipe and the older sister of the twins Jeice and Elionaro Filipe, her paternal siblings, and the first of Carla de Sousa's daughters: Cinthya do Prado, Daniela Silvestre, Débora Francisco, and Cássia Rabelais.

Thanos Hotels & Resorts is a Cypriot hospitality group founded in 1971 by Alekos Michaelides. It is active in the ownership, development and management of hotel properties in Cyprus and Greece, including Anassa, Almyra, Annabelle and the Amyth Hotels collection. [ref: Thanos Hotels and Resorts: Από το βομβαρδισμένο Paphos Beach Hotel, στο στόχο για 10 ξενοδοχεία στην Ελλάδα, Οικονομικός Ταχυδρόμος] [ref: Thanos Hotels & Resorts: Πώς προχωρούν οι επενδύσεις σε ξενοδοχεία σε Ελλάδα και Κύπρο, Forbes Greece]

== History ==

Thanos Hotels & Resorts was founded in 1971 by Alekos Michaelides, later expanding its hotel activities in Cyprus, including Almyra, Annabelle and Anassa. Almyra originally operated as the Paphos Beach Hotel, which opened during the 1972–73 season and was expanded and renovated in 2003 before being relaunched as Almyra. [ref: Αναγνωρίζεις ποιο γνωστό ξενοδοχείο της Πάφου απεικονίζεται στη φωτογραφία;, SigmaLive] Annabelle opened in 1987, while Anassa has operated since the 1990s. Following his death in 2008, leadership of the group passed to Michaelides' children. [ref: Thanos Hotels and Resorts, Χρυσές Εταιρείες / Philenews] [ref: Απόβαση στην ελληνική ξενοδοχειακή αγορά κάνει η κυπριακή αλυσίδα Thanos Hotels and Resorts, Insider]

== Operations ==

Thanos Hotels & Resorts is active in hotel management and consulting for hospitality properties. It operates and manages hotel properties in Cyprus and Greece. It is also involved in hotel development and redevelopment projects in Cyprus and Greece.

data.title: Letizia Murat
data.text:
Letizia Murat (25 April 1802 - 3 December 1859) was a French noblewoman, notable for her salon at Palazzo Pepoli Campogrande or Palazzo Pepoli Vecchio on via Castiglione in Bologna, which led to her being nicknamed the Regina di Bologna ('Queen of Bologna').

Several portraits of her by notable artists such as Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres (Harvard University Art Museum [ref: Letizia Murat]), Benjamin Rolland (Reggia di Caserta) and
Louis Ducis (Musée de l'Histoire de France [ref: Musée de l'histoire de France]) survive.

== Life ==
[[File:Caroline_Murat_by_Vigee-Lebrun.jpg|thumb|left|Letizia as a child with her mother by Élisabeth Vigée-Lebrun.]]
Born in Paris to Joachim Murat and Caroline Bonaparte (the eldest of their four children), she had one sister, Luisa Giulia, and two brothers, Achille and Lucien. She was named after her mother's mother Letizia Bonaparte. She was made an imperial and royal prince of the First French Empire in 1804. [ref: Genealogische Tafeln zur Staatengeschichte des 19. Jahrhunderts, nebst einer genealogisch-statistischen Einleitung, F.A. Brockhaus]

Even after her father was made Grand Duke of Cleves and Burg by Caroline's brother Napoleon in 1806 the family remained in Paris. The same year she was made a princess of the Grand Duchy and on 28 October by imperial decree abbess of Elten, [ref: Das fürstliche Stift Elten: aus authentischen Quellen, Heberle'sche Buchhandlung] a former imperial territory annexed by the Grand Duchy. In 1808 her father was made King of Naples, making her princess of Naples. The family thus left the palais de l'Élysée in Paris for the Royal Palace of Naples. There she learned how to run a salon and received an education befitting her rank, learning singing, music, English, German and several other languages.

Her father was shot for his failed attempt to regain the Kingdom after Napoleon's second abdication and so she, her mother and her brothers moved to Trieste, where they benefitted from Metternich's support (Caroline had had a love affair with him years before while he was an ambassador in Paris [ref: Caroline Bonaparte: Princesse Murat, Reine de Naples, France-Empire.]). They lived near the town in villa Campo Marzo for a time before moving to Graz then to a suburb of Vienna and finally to Tuscany, where Caroline's sister Élisa lived.

The 1815 Congress of Vienna stripped them of the right to use their titles and banned them from returning to France and so in 1817 Caroline acquired the Frohsdorf Castle in Lower Austria, living there until 1819. [ref: Il était une fois...le château de Frohsdorf et le couvent de Kostanjevica, leretourdecharlesx.com] Although a liberal, Letizia later pushed her brother Lucien to claim his right to their father's throne in Naples. [ref: Pèpoli, Letìzia Murat, marchésa, www.sapere.it]

After her marriage she supported her husband's political career through her salon, travelled widely, wrote to figures all over Europe and wrote travel diaries. As well as their city residence, the couple also lived at Villa della Palata near the city. Her salon discussed art, culture and politics. In Rome she met the French salon-holder Julie Récamier, who wrote of the meeting "We were fascinated by Marquise Pepoli; I found her beautiful, spiritual and a perfect natural". [ref: Murat Letizia, www.storiaememoriadibologna.it]

[[File:Murat Bologna.JPG|thumb|upright|Her tomb monument, one of the masterpieces of the Certosa di Bologna.]]
She died in Bologna in 1859 after a long illness and was buried in the Certosa di Bologna cemetery there. Her tomb monument by Vincenzo Vela next to the Sala del Colombario is surmounted by a statue of her father.

== Marriage and issue ==
On 27 October 1823 she married Bolognese marquess Guido Taddeo Pepoli (1789-1852), count of Castiglione, who was from an ancient noble family from the city of Bologna. They had four children:

* Carolina (Bologna, 21 August 1824 – Bologna, 23 August 1892), married 1) count Angelo Tattini (1823-1878), with whom she had three children: Laetizia Guida (1846-1924) who married Francesco Isolani-Lupari, Giovanni Gioacchino (1846-1877) and Napoleone (1849-1870)
* Gioacchino Napoleone (Bologna, 1825 - Bologna, 1881) (Mayor of Bologna from 1866 to 1868), in 1844 married princess Friederike von Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen, with whom he had three daughters: Letizia (1846-1902), in 1868 married count Antonio Gaddi (1842-1914), Antonietta (1849-1887), in 1872 married count Carlo Taveggi (1836-1902), and Napoleona Luisa (1853-1929), in 1872 married count Guarini Dominico-Mar Castelfalcino Matteucci (1848-1905)
* Elisabetta (1829-1892) married Ippolito Ruspoli, with whom he had two daughters: Laetizia (1849-1944; married Mario Rappini di Casteldelfino and then the Marquis di Casteldelfino); and Giacenta (1861-1862)
* Paolina (1831-1916), married for the first time to Gian Mauro Zucchini Solimei (1825-1854) and had one son 1) Giuseppe Gioacchino Zucchini (1854-1902) who married Carmelita Cagnola (1854-1936); second marriage to Tancredi Mosti Estense Trotti (1826-1903) by whom she had four children:1) Ercole (1864-?) married Rachel Verset and then Iole Fabbri (by whom he had a son called Tancredi); 2) Giovanna (1867-1945) married Alfonso Costabili Containi, with whom he had two children: Gian Battista and Maria Letizia; 3) Maria Letizia (1873-1951) married Andrea Carlo Guidi di Bagno, with whom she had one son, Guido Novello; 4) Ercole Guelfo (born 1876-1896)

data.title: The Party at Boles (2025 film)
data.text:
The Party at Boles is a 2025 western film directed and written by Soul Rees. It is the debut film of Rees's directing and acting career. It stars Mateo Belmarez, River VanBerg, Cyrus Kuhr, and Noreen Lucas. The plot follows three friends, Alejandra, Nacho and Ese along with a bounty hunter Gargulio on a journey to get back a totem that was stolen from them by a mob boss Chancho. However, Chancho seems to have more up his sleeve than it first seems.

The film debuted to critical acclaim, grossing an incredible $1 USD within it's opening week. It's also credited with being the most successful student film to be produced from Kohala High School, being shown as an example film to Spanish 2 students.

Rees has stated that "A sequel isn't out of the picture."

data.title: Nura Space
data.text:
Nura Space is an Australian software as a service company that develops a workplace management platform for hybrid work. Founded in Melbourne in 2017, the company is a subsidiary of the Schiavello Group, a privately owned Australian furniture manufacturing, construction and property business. The platform combines booking of desks, meeting rooms, lockers and car spaces with occupancy analytics, visitor management and space planning tools, and is supported by proprietary IoT hardware.

== History ==
Nura Space was established in 2017 within the Schiavello Group, led by Anton Schiavello, a member of the founding family. The platform was developed from insights gathered during Schiavello's workplace change-management programmes and was initially trialled in a small number of enterprise environments.

The product was publicly launched as a standalone offering in late 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic, with the Schiavello Group planning to deploy it across its own seven Australian offices. At launch the company said it would target medium and large enterprises in Australia before expanding to the United States, United Kingdom and Asia, and that the software was hosted on Microsoft Azure with an integration to Microsoft Teams scheduled for early 2021.

In 2023, Schiavello Furniture released NEXUS, a range of technology-integrated furniture including height-adjustable workstations, locker storage and meeting room booking panels that operate through the Nura Space platform.

== Products ==
The Nura Space platform is delivered through a web dashboard and mobile applications for iOS and Android. Its functions include desk, room, locker and car park booking, team and neighbourhood zoning, mobile check-in, visitor management, real-time occupancy analytics and block-and-stack scenario planning for office portfolios. The platform integrates with Microsoft 365, Azure Active Directory and Microsoft Teams, as well as third-party systems such as Vecos smart lockers and occupancy sensors.

The company also designs its own hardware, including the Nura Vision above-desk device, which combines a touchscreen with NFC and presence sensing to provide check-in, desk status indication and ambient availability signalling, and a power control module and remote sit-stand controller for height-adjustable desks.

== Awards ==
In June 2025 Nura Vision, developed by Nura Space and exhibited by its parent company Schiavello, won the Gold award in the Technology – Integrated Solutions category at the Best of NeoCon awards, judged by a 42-member jury at the NeoCon commercial interiors show at The Merchandise Mart, Chicago.

== Ownership ==
Nura Space operates through Nura Space Technology Services Pty Ltd and is backed by the Schiavello Group, whose managing director Peter Schiavello is a co-founder of the company. Schiavello Group has stated it continues to provide support and funding for the platform's development.

data.title: Kaylene Peoples
data.text:
== Professional Overview & Global Footprint ==
* Kaylene Peoples is an award-winning recording artist, music composer, multi-instrumentalist, publisher, and filmmaker. [ref: Kaylene Peoples Official Website. https://kaylenepeoples.com/kaylene-peoples-a-renaissance-woman/]
* As a media entrepreneur, she serves as the co-founder and executive editor of KL Publishing Group alongside the late Lee L. Peoples, specializing in print book periodicals (mooks) including flagship titles AGENDA and Virtuoso Bass. [ref: AGENDA Official Website. https://www.agendamag.com/]
* A former international fashion and commercial model whose career encompassed runway, print advertising, and television campaigns, Peoples has experienced a resurgence in fashion and editorial modeling, appearing on the covers of numerous publications, including international editions of Vogue, Vanity Fair, Variety, and Cosmopolitan.

== Discography, Charting Hits, Tours & Musical Collaborations ==
* As a vocalist with a rare five-octave range, multi-instrumentalist, and composer, Peoples has recorded, performed, and toured extensively across the globe. [ref: Pandora Artist Profile. https://www.pandora.com/artist/kaylene-peoples/ARxvcXq3756c9m9] Her musical journey includes close associations with the premier jazz-fusion supergroup CAB (featuring Bunny Brunel, Virgil Donati, and stellar guest artists), alongside historic recorded credits across landmark collaborative projects such as Bass Ball, Bass Ball 2, Invent Your Future, and Fusion Holidays.

=== Official Solo & Feature Discography ===
* All Jazzed Up! (2005)
* The Meaning of Christmas (2013)
* My Man (2015) — Official 2015 Grammy Ballot Contender [ref: First Take PR Milestones. https://firsttakepr.com]
* A New Rite of Passage (2016) — Featuring Grammy-winner Mark Hammond
* Carol of the Bells (2017)
* Romantic Bossa-Nova (2020) — Album of the Week on Smooth.fm Portugal
* Vampire Odyssey (2024) — Award-winning feature film score; won Composer of the Year at the 2024 Olympia Arts Awards [ref: Vampire Odyssey Awards & Bio. https://kaylenepeoples.com/music-bio/] [ref: GoldPoster Redemption Awards. https://www.goldposter.com/movie/2464933/]

* Chart-Topping Success & Sustained No. 1 Hits: Secured major No. 1 hit songs, with "Do You Remember?" hitting the top spot globally. Her single "Run Away with Me" achieved extraordinary, sustained dominance by holding the No. 1 position for five consecutive months (September 2025 – February 2026). Her single "Corcovado" also hit No. 1 and peaked at No. 2 globally, while her single "Giant Steps" (featuring Hubert Laws, Bunny Brunel, Mark Hammond, and Bobby Lyle) won the Akademia Award for Best Jazz Song (2015).
* International & Festival Tours:
* Touch of Fire Tour (Early Career — Southeast Asia & Jakarta, Indonesia)
* Madajazzcar (2016)
* Oxnard Jazz Festival (2022)
* Fusion Holidays Tour (Russia, 2023)
* Collaborations & Advocacy: Maintained a close artistic partnership with actress and activist Chase Masterson, who has served as master of ceremonies and concert host for many of her live performances. [ref: AGENDA Advocacy Feature. https://www.agendamag.com/breaking-barriers-and-rewriting-the-narrative-kaylene-peoples-is-the-force-changing-jazz-and-publishing/] Expanding this collaboration into advocacy through music, Peoples contributed powerful recordings of "Beautiful" and "Imagine" to the compilation CD for Masterson’s Pop Culture Hero Coalition. Supported the launch of Artemis Women Powered Music with a formal proposal to the Culver City Chamber of Commerce introduced by legendary bassist John B. Williams.
* Elite Musical Roster: Her extensive recordings and live performances feature an elite roster of music icons, including Stanley Clarke, Larry Dunn (Earth, Wind & Fire), Jeff Goldblum, John Beasley, Hubert Laws, Bobby Lyle, Patrice Rushen, and Armand Sabal-Lecco. [ref: AllMusic Credits. https://www.allmusic.com/artist/kaylene-peoples-mn0000371694]
* The Mouse House Studio: Much of her core discography was developed, recorded, and produced at The Mouse House production facility in Altadena, California. Peoples played a central role in finding, designing, and decorating the legendary studio space, which served as the creative incubator and birthplace for most of her albums before it ultimately burned down. Her sessions and recordings have been permanently preserved in photo and media history, including archival features on Getty Images.

== Early Years: Modeling, Commercials & Pageantry ==
* Modeling & Commercial Campaigns: Worked internationally as an international runway model signed with LA Models, and starred in prominent commercial campaigns, including print and television ads for Miller's Outpost.
The Dove Campaign ("Kaylene's People"): Selected out of a massive nationwide competition featuring thousands of women to star in a prominent campaign/commercial centering entirely on her life, story, and personal journey, titled "Kaylene's People"*.
Pageantry Milestones & Leadership: Achieved major titles, including being crowned Miss Anaheim America (performing an original piano composition for her talent). [ref: Miss Anaheim Forever Team Titleholders. https://www.missanaheimpageant.org/forever-team-anaheim-titleholders/kaylene-peoples] Competed on the fierce Miss California America state stage as one of the first two Black contestants to ever compete in the pageant, delivering a powerhouse performance where she played “Flight of the Bumblebee” and the “William Tell Overture” on flute and piano (orchestrating the arrangement entirely herself). Entered Miss California Young Miss competing against a vast field of 1,000 girls, winning the crown by singing “New York, New York”. Additional state titles include Miss Golden State (won concurrently in the same system and division competed in by Eva La Rue of CSI: Miami*). Returning to her pageantry roots with deep distinction, she served as a Performer and Judge in 2016, and as Head Judge for the Miss Anaheim Pageant in 2017.

== Classical Training, Orchestral Works & Major Label Conducting ==
* Classical Foundation & Instructors: Developed a rigorous classical foundation from an early age, training as a prodigy in flute, piano, and composition under master instructors including Walter Scharf, Henry Mancini, David Raksin, and Sheridan Stokes.
* Historic UCLA Composition Pioneer: Graduated from the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Composition and Ethnomusicology, making history as the first Black person (and one of two women) to graduate with a degree in composition from the institution. At her UCLA graduation, Peoples met film composer Jerry Goldsmith, the keynote speaker. She later recalled that Goldsmith invited her to his suite, where they played piano together and he offered advice on composing. [ref: Miss Anaheim official program (2017). https://www.missanaheimpageant.org/_files/ugd/12792c_117a124fc86f4390bbdc12a938af53b5.pdf] [ref: KL Publishing Group biography (2023). https://kaylenepeoples.com/storage/2023/08/About-KL-Publishing-Group-AUG-2023.pdf]
* Elite Film Scoring Master's Program: Achieved the extraordinary distinction of being selected 2nd out of 5,000 applicants for the elite Master's Program in Film Scoring under the direction of Academy Award-winning composer Walter Scharf.
Symphonies & Major Label Conducting: Composed hundreds of orchestral arrangements, including three neoclassical symphonies (with her first symphony, "For God", receiving critical acclaim in Europe). Built an extensive career as a master conductor and notable string arranger for major labels including Capitol Records (arranging and conducting for Tracie Spencer’s Music Box), Polygram, Warner Bros., and Universal Republic. Her large-scale classical works also include composing and conducting Apocaliptica, a 10-act ballet that enjoyed a month-long run at Santa Monica College.

== Film Scoring, Filmmaking, TV Ghostwriting & Awards ==
Film Scoring, Apprenticeship & Ghostwriting: Began her professional career in film composition during the 1990s, composing and orchestrating original scores for feature films, including Making the Rules. [ref: IMDb Making the Rules. https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2205562/fullcredits] Apprenticed with legendary composer Barry Goldberg, serving as his trusted ghostwriter and arranging strings for projects including the feature film Ruby (starring Danny Aiello). Contributed orchestral scoring and arrangements to prominent prime-time television series. Expanding her narrative work into full-scale filmmaking, she wrote, directed, produced, and scored the critically acclaimed feature film Redemption, starring Ali Saam (Argo*) and Jordan Murphy.
* Festival Accolades:
* Best First-Time Director (HUFFY Award): Presented personally by legendary director Arthur Hiller at the Hollywood Underground Film Festival (2002).
* Best Picture: Florida Film Festival.
* Best Picture & Grand Prize Jury Award: Goldie Film Awards (2003).
Composer of the Year (2024): Won at the Olympia Arts Awards for her original feature score to Vampire Odyssey*.

== Rock, Pop & Punk Orchestral & String Arrangements ==
Oleander's Sole Orchestrator: Served as the sole orchestrator and string arranger for the post-grunge band Oleander across all of their albums except the first one (including their album Unwind), with her arrangements heard worldwide—featuring prominent placements in the closing credits of American Pie 2* ("Halo"), television broadcasts for the Super Bowl, and major feature films. [ref: IMDb American Pie 2. https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0252866/fullcredits]
Cinematic & Punk Arrangements: Orchestrated the title track "Always Something There to Remind Me" for the feature film Serendipity. [ref: IMDb Serendipity. https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0240890/fullcredits] Famously wrote and conducted the string arrangements for the punk band The Generators' single Destroy Hollywood*, alongside custom string arrangements for countless other prominent artists across genres.

== Advocacy, Bella Composers & The Artemis Competition ==
Launched Bella Composers in April 2015 during a landmark dual CD release concert for her album MY MAN and Bunny Brunel's Invent Your Future*—hosted by Chase Masterson and featuring legendary pianist Patrice Rushen.
Bella Composers sponsored groundbreaking initiatives, culminating in 2019 with the launch of Artemis Women Powered Music—sponsored by Bella Composers as the first international competition for women composers, drawing participants from all over the globe and documented extensively in Agenda Collector's Issue 2*.

== Publishing, Media Ventures & Board Leadership ==
* KL Publishing Group & Board Roles: Directs editorial operations and multi-media production as co-founder and executive editor alongside the late Lee L. Peoples. Serves as a distinguished member of the Advisory Board for the Black Design Collective, headed by President Kevan Hall.
Periodicals & Mooks: KL Publishing Group specializes in print book periodicals (mooks)—including flagship titles AGENDA (recognized 3 separate times by Feedspot as a top Los Angeles magazine) and Virtuoso Bass—while also publishing impactful memoirs such as Levy Lee Simon's Odyssey Towards the Light*, specialized photography, and art books.

== Honors, Awards & Cover Features ==
* Music Industry & Production Honors:
Composer of the Year (2024): Awarded by the Olympia Arts Awards for her feature score to Vampire Odyssey*.
Grammy Ballot Contender (2015): Her album MY MAN* officially made the Grammy Ballot.
LA Music Awards Best R&B Album & Artist of the Year (2001): Won for producing Christina Fasano's critically acclaimed album Spiritually Wet*.
* Akademia Award for Best Jazz Song (2015): Won for "Giant Steps" (feat. Hubert Laws, Bunny Brunel, Mark Hammond, and Bobby Lyle).
Album of the Week: Romantic Bossa-Nova* honored by Smooth.fm Portugal.
* LA Music Awards Official Sponsor (2009): Named the official sponsor for the event.
* Cover Modeling & Print Milestones:
Feature Cover Model & Major Magazine Milestones: Accomplished high-profile cover model appearing across prominent publications, including Insider Travel, New York Verve, Blur, Ur Spirit, LA Lifestyle, Monaco Muse, Celebrity Feature, and The Hollywood Magazine, alongside features in flagship independent periodicals such as AGENDA and Virtuoso Bass. [ref: Vogue Monaco Feature. https://voguemonaco.co/2024/12/27/title-kaylene-peoples-a-renaissance-woman-redefining-excellence/] Highlighted as a featured headlining artist and residency staple at Hollywood's legendary Catalina Jazz Club for her "A Journey Through Jazz"* series. [ref: Bonetto and Bender, Los Angeles Pocket, 5th Italian ed. (2024), ISBN 9788859290667. https://shop.lonelyplanetitalia.it/prodotto/guida-di-viaggio-los-angeles-pocket]
* Government & Community Recognition:
* Senator’s Award (Women of Distinction): Presented by State Senator Roderick D. Wright for the 35th Senate District, recognizing outstanding community leadership and artistic achievement.
* National Media & Leadership Accolades:
* MSN Top Ten Women Leaders (2026): Honored as one of the Top Ten Most Inspiring Women Leaders.
* MSN Trailblazing Entrepreneurs (2025): Named to the Top 10 Trailblazing Entrepreneurs to Follow list.
* Executive & Professional Biographies:
* Covington's Who's Who, Cambridge Who's Who (Executive Professionals and Entrepreneurs), Who's Who Publishers (19th Edition), and Stanford Who's Who.
* National & Institutional Honors:
* United States National Achievement Award.

data.title: Chandanbati Shiva Mandir
data.text:
----

Chandanbati Shiva Mandir (locally known as Chandaneshwar Shib Mandir) is a Hindu temple located in Chandanbati village within the Sagardighi Community Development Block of Murshidabad district, West Bengal, India. [ref: District Statistical Handbook 2014: Murshidabad, Department of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Government of West Bengal] The site features a modern superstructure enclosing a basalt stone Shiva lingam, which local tradition associates with the regional Pala Empire heritage of the area. [ref: Bengal District Gazetteers: Murshidabad, Bengal Secretariat Book Depot]

== Location ==
The temple is situated in Chandanbati village in the Jangipur subdivision of Murshidabad district (PIN: 742226). It is located approximately 1.78 kilometres (1.11 mi) from Sagardighi railway station and roughly 7.52 kilometres (4.67 mi) from the Morgram junction connecting NH-12 and NH-114A. [ref: District Census Handbook: Murshidabad, Directorate of Census Operations, West Bengal]

== Historical context ==
The site reflects the historical settlement patterns of the Northern Rarh region, where early medieval ritual sites transitioned into rural community centers following regional trade realignments and shifts in river courses. [ref: Banglar Mandir Sthapatya O Bhaskarya, Pustak Bipani] The basalt lingam has remained under continuous local religious worship.

== Architecture ==
The temple consists of a single-chamber masonry sanctum topped with a stepped pyramidal shikhara. Over time, the structure has undergone multiple renovations:
* Earlier phase: A monolithic masonry sanctum finished in lime plaster, featuring hand-painted devotional murals flanking the entrance under a stepped tower.
* Modern phase: Renovation with ceramic tiles, an updated stepped pyramidal shikhara with an ornamental brass kalasha (finial), and a perimeter boundary railing.

== Governance and festivals ==
The site's physical infrastructure, civil maintenance, and religious observances are managed by the Chandanbati Shib Mandir Parichalana Committee. The temple serves as a focal point for regional religious gatherings, with peak congregations occurring during Maha Shivaratri and throughout the Bengali month of Shraavana.

data.title: Monireh Baradaran
data.text:
Monireh Baradaran Khosroshahi (born 1954–1955 in Tabriz) is an Iranian women's rights activist, political activist, and former political prisoner. [ref: Monireh Baradaran, Iran Academia] [ref: WomenList: Frankfurt Book Fair 2018, International Alliance of Independent Publishers] [ref: منیره برادران، با سابقه ۹ سال زندان در دهه ۶۰: «رئیسی سمبل جنایت‌های جمهوری اسلامی است», Center for Human Rights in Iran] After emigrating from Iran, she published A Simple Truth, a memoir of her years in prison. [ref: Biography, Forough Book]

== Life and activities ==

Baradaran attended school in Tehran and graduated from the University of Tehran with a degree in sociology. She later continued her studies at the University of Hanover in Germany. She was imprisoned in Evin Prison during the mass executions of Iranian political prisoners in the summer of 1988.

== Arrests and imprisonment ==

Baradaran was first arrested in June 1978 and released in December that year. Following the Iranian Revolution of 1979, she was arrested again in October 1981, alongside her brother and sister-in-law. Her brother was executed 40 days later. Baradaran remained imprisoned for nine years and was released in October 1990. [ref: Monireh Baradaran, Abdorrahman Boroumand Foundation] She witnessed the events surrounding the 1988 prison executions and subsequently published an account of her imprisonment.

data.title: Kyle Correya
data.text:
Kyle Correya is an Australian Catholic musician and worship leader from Melbourne. He was director of music for the Archdiocese of Melbourne at World Youth Day 2023, and in 2024 was Australia's official youth representative at the International Congress on Youth Ministry in Rome.

== Early life ==
Correya grew up in a Catholic family in Melbourne; his parents are both singers and his father leads a prayer group. He began playing music with his father at the age of six. He has also worked as an electrician, undertaking an electrical apprenticeship.

== Ministry ==
Correya is involved at St Peter's parish in Epping, where he has led the youth band and taken part in youth ministry. He has led worship at Eucharistic adoration.

At World Youth Day 2023 in Lisbon he served as director of music for the Archdiocese of Melbourne's pilgrims. In 2024 he was nominated as Australia's representative to the International Congress on Youth Ministry, hosted by the Dicastery for Laity, Family and Life in Ciampino, near Rome, from 19 to 28 May 2024. More than 300 young people from over 100 countries attended. Correya played guitar at the congress's daily Mass and adoration, and met Pope Francis.

He leads a ministry called Awaken Ministry, under the motto "Awakening Young Hearts", which aims to host worship nights and other events for young people across Australia.

== Music ==
Correya sings and plays drums, keyboard, organ, piano, bass and electric guitar. He released his debut EP, GateKeeper, at the age of 18.
