== Background ==

SMiB (Korean: 스미브) is a hair-care brand that sells products intended for scalp care, hair cleansing and the management of hair-loss concerns. The brand is associated with hair care products originated in South Korea and is distributed in Singapore and Malaysia through SMIB SINGAPORE PTE LTD. Its product range is marketed towards consumers experiencing concerns including oily scalp, dandruff, scalp itchiness, thinning hair and hair fall. [ref: SMIB SINGAPORE PTE. LTD. (201919778Z), SGPBusiness]

A central part of SMiB’s product identity is its use of coral calcium, an ingredient used in its shampoo, hair treatment and scalp-essence products. According to the company, its Coral Calcium range was developed to support scalp care and improve the condition of the hair and scalp. The range includes the Coral Calcium Shampoo, Coral Calcium Treatment, Hair Scalp Essence and a plasma scalp massager. [ref: Most Effective Anti Hair Loss / Fall Shampoo SMiB Singapore & Malaysia, SMiB 스미브]

SMiB describes its product approach as “DEVICOS”, a term referring to the combined use of cosmetic hair-care products and a scalp-care device. The plasma scalp massager is intended to be used alongside the company’s topical products as part of a home hair-care routine. In addition to its anti-hair-loss products, SMiB sells anti-ageing and anti-frizz hair-care products, including colour-change shampoo for grey hair and repair-focused products.

== Products ==
SMiB markets hair & scalp-care products through several product ranges. The brand’s products are primarily sold as shampoo, hair treatment, scalp essence, hair masks, scalp-cleansing products and home-use scalp-care devices. [ref: SMiB Products Review: This Iconic Brand Changed My Hair!] Its product line is aimed at consumers seeking products for general hair maintenance and scalp-related concerns, including oily scalp, dandruff, dryness, frizz, thinning hair and hair fall. [ref: About us - SMIB SINGAPORE PTE LTD, SMiB 스미브]

Coral Calcium Anti Hair Loss range

The Coral Calcium Anti Hair Loss range is SMiB’s principal product line. [ref: SMiB Anti Hair Loss Series - 500ML Coral Calcium Shampoo, SMiB 스미브] It includes Coral Calcium Shampoo, Coral Calcium Treatment, Hair Scalp Essence and a Plasma Scalp Massager. The products are sold individually and as bundled sets.

According to SMiB, the range uses coral calcium as a key ingredient, together with ingredients including biotin, niacinamide, dexpanthenol and zinc pyrithione. The company markets the products towards users with oily scalps, thinning hair, hair fall and postpartum hair fall. These uses are product-marketing claims made by the company and should not be presented as medical treatment claims.

The Plasma Scalp Massager is a handheld device intended for use alongside the shampoo, treatment and scalp essence. SMiB describes it as part of its “DEVICOS” approach, combining a device with cosmetic hair-care products. The company states that the device is intended to support scalp cleansing and product application as part of a home-use hair-care routine.

LactoBio Anti-Frizz & Repair range

SMiB also sells the LactoBio Anti-Frizz & Repair range. The range includes LactoBio shampoo, hair-mask treatment and scalp-scaler products. It is marketed for people with dry, damaged or frizzy hair, and is positioned by the company as a hair-maintenance range rather than a hair-loss line. [ref: SMiB Anti-Frizz & Repair Series - LactoBio Shampoo, SMiB 스미브]

The LactoBio range is sold in Singapore and Malaysia through SMiB’s regional online store. Product descriptions refer to probiotic-based hair-care ingredients, though specific performance claims should be attributed to the company unless supported by independent scientific sources.

Anti-Aging range

SMiB’s Anti-Aging range includes a Colour Change Shampoo and associated bundled products. The shampoo is marketed as a gradual colour-depositing product designed to blend or reduce the visibility of grey hair through repeated use. [ref: SMiB Anti-Aging Series - Colour Change Shampoo for Grey Hair, SMiB 스미브] Unlike conventional permanent hair dyes, the product is marketed as part of a regular shampoo routine.

According to SMiB, the Colour Change Shampoo was developed by its research and development team in South Korea. The product is available through the company’s Singapore and Malaysia distribution channels, while Korean SMiB online stores list additional hair-care products for the domestic South Korean market.

Sales and availability

SMiB products are sold through its official Singapore website and selected online retail platforms. The Singapore site lists delivery within Singapore and Malaysia, as well as shipping options to selected international destinations. Separate SMiB online stores in South Korea offer products for the Korean market. [ref: 스미브 온라인 스토어, 스미브]

== Availability ==
SMiB products are sold in South Korea through the brand’s Korean online stores. The company’s Korean product listings include hair-care products such as LactoBio shampoo, colour-change shampoo and other scalp-care products.

In Singapore, products are distributed through SMIB SINGAPORE PTE. LTD., a Singapore-incorporated company. The company was incorporated on 19 June 2019 and lists wholesale and retail of cosmetics and toiletries among its business activities.

SMiB’s Singapore website sells products to customers in Singapore and Malaysia. Its delivery information also lists shipping options for selected overseas destinations, including Australia, India, Japan, South Korea and New Zealand. The availability of shipping to these countries does not necessarily indicate that SMiB has local distributors, offices or physical retail stores in each market.

data.title: Vincent Roscigno
data.text:
----

Vincent J. Roscigno is a sociologist and Distinguished Professor of Arts & Sciences in Sociology at The Ohio State University. His research is comprised of topics ranging from social inequality to workplace discrimination, the sociology of work and education, collective behavior and social movements. Roscigno has served as the Co-Editor of the American Sociological Review, as President of the Southern Sociological Society, and as an elected Council Member of the American Sociological Association. In 2026, he received the American Sociological Association's Distinguished Contributions to Teaching Award. [ref: 2026 ASA Award Winners, American Sociological Association] [ref: American Sociological Association Announces 2026 Award Recipients, [www.newswise.com](https://www.newswise.com)]

==Education and career==

Roscigno received his B.A. in sociology from the University of Arizona in 1989. He attended North Carolina State University, where he earned his M.S. in 1991 and his Ph.D. in 1996. [ref: American Sociological Association. "Roscigno, Hodson Are Incoming Editors of American Sociological Review." Footnotes, July/August 2006, Vol. 34, No. 6. https://www.asanet.org/wp-content/uploads/fn_2006_06.pdf] His early scholarship, while at North Carolina State, included a co-authored study with sociologist Donald Tomaskovic-Devey on racial economic inequality in the U.S. South. [ref: Tomaskovic-Devey, Donald and Vincent J. Roscigno. "Racial Economic Subordination and White Gain in the U.S. South." American Sociological Review 61 (1996): 565–589.]

Roscigno began teaching at The Ohio State University in 1996. He was promoted to associate professor in 2001 and to full Professor in 2005; he was named Distinguished Professor of Arts & Sciences in Sociology in 2012, the same year he received the university's Distinguished University Scholar Award. [ref: Vincent J. Roscigno, Curriculum Vita (June 2026). The Ohio State University Department of Sociology. https://u.osu.edu/roscigno.1/files/2026/06/VJRVITA__6-9-26.pdf] [ref: ]

From 2007 to 2009, Roscigno served as the Co-Editor of the American Sociological Review alongside the late sociologist Randy Hodson. [ref: ] From 2013 to 2018, he was the founding Co-Editor (with Toni Calasanti of Virginia Tech) of Social Currents, the official journal of the Southern Sociological Society. [ref: Social Currents, and the Prospects and Promise of Sociology, Social Currents]

==Research==

Roscigno's research addresses inequalities through various methodological procedures ranging from quantitative, qualitative, and historical methods. [ref: ] As of 2026, his publications have accumulated more than 14,000 citations. [ref: Vincent J. Roscigno, scholar.google.com]

===Workplace and organizational inequality===

In one area of research, Roscigno's work examines how race, gender, and age discrimination operates within organizations and labor markets, through his 2007 book The Face of Discrimination: How Race and Gender Impact Work and Home Lives, which draws on discrimination complaints filed with the Ohio Civil Rights Commission. [ref: The Face of Discrimination: How Race and Gender Impact Work and Home Lives] His 2011 article "Power, Revisited," delivered as his Presidential Address to the Southern Sociological Society, presents a theoretical framework for understanding power within organizations. [ref: Roscigno, Vincent J. "Power, Revisited." Social Forces 90 (2011): 349–374.]

===Labor movements, music, and culture===

Roscigno's earlier research explored culture, media, and labor mobilization in the American South. His 2004 book The Voice of Southern Labor: Radio, Music, and Textile Strikes, 1929–1934 (co-authored with William F. Danaher) examines how southern textile mill workers used radio broadcasts and music to build solidarity, sustaining labor insurgencies during the strikes of 1929 and 1934. [ref: Roscigno, Vincent J. and William F. Danaher. The Voice of Southern Labor: Radio, Music, and Textile Strikes, 1929–1934. Minneapolis: University of Minnesota Press, 2004. https://www.upress.umn.edu/book-division/books/the-voice-of-southern-labor] The book was reviewed in both academic and government publications, including the Journal of Interdisciplinary History, [ref: The Voice of Southern Labor: Radio, Music, and Textile Strikes, 1929–1934. By Vincent Roscigno and William F. Danaher (Minneapolis, University of Minnesota Press, 2004) 177 pp. $19.95, The Journal of Interdisciplinary History] and the International Review of Social History. [ref: Roscigno, Vincent J. and William F. Danaher, The Voice of Southern Labor. Radio, Music, and Textile Strikes, 1929–1934. [Social Movements, Protest, and Contention, vol. 19.] University of Minnesota Press, Minneapolis [etc.] 2004. xxviii, 177 pp. $59.95, International Review of Social History] It was also reviewed by the Bureau of Labor Statistics in its Monthly Labor Review. [ref: Music for the people: the role of music in the southern textile strikes of 1929–34: Monthly Labor Review: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Bureau of Labor Statistics]

===Education and first-generation students===

Roscigno has also contributed to the sociology of education, leading a longitudinal study on first-generation college students at Ohio State University, specifically examining the structural and social barriers across various outcomes like persistence, campus integration and social mobility. [ref: First-Generation Student Study, cssl.osu.edu]

==Professional leadership and honors==

Roscigno served as the President of the Southern Sociological Society in 2010–2011, having served as the President-Elect from 2009 to 2010. [ref: Presidents of the Southern Sociological Society, Southern Sociological Society] He was elected to membership in the Sociological Research Association in 2004, then elected to its executive committee in 2022 [ref: Current SRA Officers, Sociological Research Association], and is scheduled to serve as its president in 2027.

He served as an elected Council Member of the American Sociological Association from 2019 to 2022 [ref: ] and served on the ASA Publications Committee from 2012 to 2015. [ref: American Sociological Association. "Publications Committee Summary," August 2015. https://www.asanet.org/wp-content/uploads/savvy/journals/August2015PCSummary.pdf] He has served on the advisory board of the General Social Survey since 2024. [ref: ]

Among his major awards are the Distinguished University Scholar Award from Ohio State University (2012), the W. Richard Scott Distinguished Article Award from the ASA's Organizations, Occupations & Work Section (2005), [ref: Scott Award, Organizations, Occupations and Work] the Joan Huber Faculty Fellow for Research Excellence (2007–2009), [ref: ] the Harlan Hatcher Arts & Sciences Distinguished Faculty Award (2020), the Alumni Award for Distinguished Teaching from Ohio State University (2023), [ref: ] and the Donald MacNamara Distinguished Article Award from the Academy of Criminal Justice Sciences (2022). [ref: Past Award Winners, Academy of Criminal Justice Sciences] He was also co-recipient of the Best Paper Award from the International Sociological Association's Research Committee on Logic and Methodology (RC33) in 2025 for an article first authored by his colleague Michael Vuolo. [ref: 11ICSSM Awards, rc33.org]

data.title: Shubha V. Iyengar
data.text:
Shubha V. Iyengar also known as Shubha Venkatesha Iyengar is an Indian scientist. She is best known for her contributions to civil aviation, defence and indigenous technology sectors in India. She served at the CSIR-National Aerospace Laboratories for a period of approximately five decades (46 years). [ref: A Bengaluru Aerospace Scientist Built the Made-in-India System That Reads Fog for Pilots, thebetterindia.com] [ref: Who is Dr. Shubha V Iyengar? Meet the unsung Indian hero who guides thousands of flights through fog every day by giving runways 'Drishti', The Times of India]

== Biography ==
She was born in Bengaluru as the youngest in a family of nine children. She faced barriers to continue her higher studies in science, at a time when girls in India had severe societal restrictions to pursue their education and career choices. [ref: This Indian woman scientist’s research was published by NASA and her technology now guides flights across India, The Times of India] However, she was encouraged by her father to pursue her studies in science.

== Career ==

Iyengar was a batch topper in academics during her higher studies by achieving distinction in both her graduation and post-graduation studies at the Bangalore University. She also received gold medals in the field of Physics and obtained first rank in MSc physics examination in 1974. Following her distinction pass, she subsequently received a Government of India merit scholarship. [ref: https://www.news18.com/amp/india/one-has-to-persevere-scientist-behind-indias-indigenous-aircraft-landing-system-shares-her-journey-at-news18-amrit-ratna-ws-l-10156554.html] She joined as a research scientist at the National Aerospace Laboratories in 1974, where she was assigned at Material Science Division and Airport Instrument Division. [ref: Meet Padma Shri Shubha V Iyengar, the scientist behind India’s aviation safety tech, India Today] During her stint with, National Aerospace Laboratories, her job role was emphasised heavily on designing and improving devices that support safer aircraft operations. She also focused mainly in developing gadgets to combat challenging weather and low-visibility conditions, which were central to the aviation industry. She also engaged in creating devices incorporating portable, FPGA-based humidity and temperature sensors.

In 2011, Shubha collaborated with the Indian Meteorological Department and conceptualised a unique model to monitor aviation weather and runway visibility measurement, which was later named as "Drishti". Her innovative model "Drishti" transmissometer has since been approved by the Government of India and has been predominantly used in across various international airports in India as well as by the Indian Air Force. [ref: Meet Dr. Shubha Venkatesh Iyengar, Agni missile scientist, whose tech is now being used by every international airport in India, The Economic Times] Prior to her innovation, the aviation industry had faced the longstanding issue with regards to making arrangements to fly the aircraft safely onto fog-covered runways. [ref: 'She helps planes land through fog': Anand Mahindra calls Indian scientist his motivation. Who is Dr Shubha V Iyengar? - The Economic Times, m.economictimes.com] Shubha pioneered to build a cost-effective, indigeneous homegrown system which could measure runway visibility and weather conditions, as well as to detect possibilities for aeroplanes to land safely even when issues pertaining to poor visibility exist. Prior to the introduction of "Drishti", Indian airports had long practiced the approach of purchasing expensive runway visibility measuring instruments from Finland and Australia. Over the years, Drishti also gained widespread international attention, where prominent organizations such as World Meteorological Organization and the International Civil Aviation Organization had recommended the usage of Drishti. She also actively involved in India's defense system and during an occasion, she served as a chief architect to solve complex technical issue that had prevented the Agni missile from reaching its intended target.

She devised a blueprint to develop indigenous components which could withstand temperatures of 3000K, while operating at optimum speed levels of Mach 5. Eventually the indigenous components developed by Iyengar had been mandatorily used for missile systems and ramjet-scramjet engines. Those components have also been vital in India's satellite launch initiatives which have been carried out over the years. Some of her research papers were also published as official reports by NASA, taking insights from Iyengar's technical knowledge on aviation and space.

In 2015, she was conferred with the "Make in India" award, in recognition of her contributions in indigenous technological development and self-reliance. She retired from National Aerospace Laboratories in 2020 after having served for 46 years. [ref: Eight from Karnataka to be honoured with 2026 Padma awards, The Hindu] Shubha was also conferred with the Padma Shri award, India’s fourth-highest civilian honour, in the category of Science and Engineering in 2026, in recognition of her contributions to aerospace technology. [ref: They started small, but left lasting impact: from Anke Gowda to Shubha Iyengar, meet Karnataka’s Padma Shri winners, The Indian Express] [ref: Eight luminaries from Karnataka win Padma awards, The New Indian Express]

data.title: Chinmay Pandya
data.text:
Chinmay Pandya (born 9 April 1976) is an Indian psychiatrist and academic administrator. He serves as the Pro Vice-Chancellor of Dev Sanskriti Vishwavidyalaya (DSVV) in Haridwar, Uttarakhand, and is a senior representative of the All World Gayatri Pariwar (AWGP), founded by his grandfather Shriram Sharma. His public work focuses on education, youth development, and interfaith dialogue.

== Early life and medical training ==
Pandya was born on 9 April 1976 in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, and was raised at Shantikunj in Haridwar. He completed his Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) from the Himalayan Institute of Medical Sciences in Dehradun. He subsequently pursued postgraduate medical training in the United Kingdom, obtaining a postgraduate diploma in Public Health and becoming a member of the Royal College of Psychiatrists (MRCPsych).

Between 2002 and 2010, Pandya practiced within the United Kingdom's National Health Service (NHS). His clinical appointments included work as an associate specialist in older adult psychiatric services with the West London Mental Health Trust, focusing on neurocognitive disorders and dementia management. In 2010, he returned to India to take up institutional responsibilities at Shantikunj and DSVV.

== Academic and public roles ==
As Pro Vice-Chancellor of Dev Sanskriti Vishwavidyalaya, Pandya oversees institutional administration, international partnerships, and academic development. In his capacity as a representative of All World Gayatri Pariwar, he coordinates various national and global outreach programs, including cultural awareness and centenary campaigns. [ref: Three Jyoti Kalash Chariots depart from Shantikunj to spread message of centenary celebrations, Asian News International] [ref: Gayatri Parivar’s Jyoti Kalash Chariots begin Yatra for centenary, Asianet News]

He has participated in interfaith and international dialogues, speaking on ethics, mental health, and Indian philosophy at academic and intergovernmental forums. He has also served in advisory capacities for statutory bodies, including the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR).

== Personal life ==
Pandya is married to Shefali Pandya, and they have two children. He is the son of Pranav Pandya and Sailbala Pandya.

data.title: Danphone A-S
data.text:
Danphone A/S is a Danish telecommunications and hardware company that manufactures coastal radio systems, NAVTEX equipment, AIS shore infrastructure, and testing devices for the Global Maritime Distress and Safety System (GMDSS). [ref: [https://profiler.dk/13640378 Danphone A/S Unternehmensprofil], Profiler.dk.] [ref: [https://oceannews.com/news/defense/danphone-selected-to-deliver-navtex-solution-to-ccg/ Danphone Selected To Deliver NAVTEX Solution To CCG], Ocean News & Technology, 26 August 2024.] The company is headquartered in Nørresundby, Denmark.

== History ==
Founded in 1990 in northern Denmark, Danphone initially focused on radio communication technology and has since expanded into complete maritime communication systems. [ref: [https://elek-data.dk/artikel/kommunikation-iot-og-cybersikkerhed/danske-danphone-skal-sikre-verdens-lngste-kystlinje Danske Danphone skal sikre verdens længste kystlinje], Elek-data.dk, 27 August 2024.] Over subsequent decades, the company shifted its primary operational focus toward shore-based maritime safety infrastructure and GMDSS-compliant testing equipment.

The company operates on an export model, supplying coastal infrastructure and radio testing equipment to national maritime authorities through public procurement contracts and regional infrastructure upgrades. [ref: [https://nordjyske.dk/erhverv/claus-falk-navigerer-i-en-branche-hvor-forretning-er-som-at-kaste-med-terninger/ Claus Falk navigerer i en branche, hvor forretning er "som at kaste med terninger"], Nordjyske.dk.]

== Operations and systems ==
Danphone manufactures shore-based maritime communication systems, coastal radio infrastructure, and radio inspection equipment designed to comply with standards set by the International Maritime Organization (IMO) and International Telecommunication Union (ITU).

=== Coastal radio systems ===
IP-based GMDSS communication platforms configured for coast stations, ports, and offshore facilities. These systems support Voice over IP (VoIP), automated logging, and remote management across VHF and MF/HF radio frequencies. [ref: [https://automatik.nu/artikel/navtex-udstyr-sikrer-canadas-kystlinjer/ Navtex-udstyr sikrer Canadas kystlinjer], Automatik.nu.]

=== GMDSS test equipment ===
Portable test devices, such as the Futronic series, used by maritime radio surveyors during mandatory inspections of shipborne radio equipment, emergency beacons, and Search and Rescue Transponders (SART). [ref: [https://www.samsa.org.za/api/api/File/view/Uh7apBvciUWErMv55gbYgg%3D%3D Calibration and Battery Replacement – Futronic MKII GMDSS Test Box], South African Maritime Safety Authority (SAMSA), 2026.]

=== Maritime safety information & NAVTEX ===
Transmitter installations used by maritime authorities to broadcast weather alerts and navigational warnings to vessels. The company also produces NAVDAT (Navigational Data) transmitters operating in the 500 kHz band. [ref: [https://elek-data.dk/artikel/branche-og-teknologi/danske-firmaer-samarbejder-om-ny-teknologi-til-sfartssikkerhed Danske firmaer samarbejder om ny teknologi til søfartssikkerhed], Elek-data.dk, 4 November 2024.]

=== AIS shore infrastructure & VDES ===
Physical Shore Stations (PSS) for the Automatic Identification System (AIS) used in coastal vessel traffic tracking, alongside VHF Data Exchange System (VDES) technology. [ref: [https://digitallead.dk/viden/nyheder/dansk-maritim-foererposition-styrkes-med-nyt-projekt-for-sikkerhedsmeddelelser-til-soes/ Dansk maritim førerposition styrkes med nyt projekt for sikkerhedsmeddelelser til søs], DigitalLead.]

== Major contracts and deployments ==
The company supplies coastal communication systems and safety equipment to national maritime authorities globally:
* Canada: The Canadian Coast Guard (CCG) selected Danphone to replace Canada's nationwide NAVTEX infrastructure, delivering 24 1 kW transmitters and 21 automatic antenna tuning units along the Canadian coastline.
* Africa: The company has supplied coastal radio communication networks, port systems, and safety infrastructure under contracts with regional maritime authorities in several African nations. [ref: [https://www.electronic-supply.dk/article/view/1056930/nordjysk_kommunikationsspecialist_far_vigtig_afrikansk_ordre Nordjysk kommunikationsspecialist får vigtig afrikansk ordre], Electronic Supply DK.]

data.title: Professor Hayder Al Hamdany
data.text:
Hayder Al Hamdany

Hayder Kareem Al Hamdany is an Iraqi-Australian academic, researcher and higher-education leader. Born in Iraq, he developed his academic career across Iraq and Australia, where he has lived, studied and worked in higher education.

His career spans more than two decades in higher education, combining academic scholarship with senior university leadership, academic governance, quality assurance, postgraduate education, internationalisation and international higher-education projects.

His research has developed from applied linguistics and English for Academic Purposes into broader work on education, identity, belonging, intercultural relations and higher education.

Early life and education

Al Hamdany was born in Iraq, where he completed his early education before undertaking university study in the field of education, English language and literature.

He subsequently moved into postgraduate study and developed an academic career connecting Iraqi and Australian higher education.

He completed a Bachelor’s degree in Education, English and Literature at the University of Thi Qar in Iraq.

He later undertook postgraduate study in Australia, completing an MA in Education/TESOL at the University of South Australia and an MPhil at the University of Adelaide.

He subsequently completed a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Education, specialising in Applied Linguistics, at the University of Adelaide.

His doctoral thesis, An Exploration of Perceptions and Applications of Spoken Register: Iraqi Students at a South Australian University, examined the experiences of Iraqi students using spoken academic English in Australian higher education.

Career in Iraq

University of Kufa

Al Hamdany established a substantial part of his academic and leadership career at the University of Kufa in Iraq.

His work at the university has encompassed teaching, research, postgraduate education, university governance, international scholarships, academic development and international cooperation.

During his career at the University of Kufa, he held a number of leadership and institutional responsibilities, including:

* Secretary of the University Council;
* Director of Missions and Scholarships;
* UNESCO Chair;
* Founding Director of Graduate Studies; and
* academic and research leadership responsibilities within the university.

These positions placed his work at the intersection of academic governance, postgraduate education, international mobility, research development and institutional strategy.

University governance

As Secretary of the University Council, Al Hamdany was involved in university-level governance and institutional decision-making.

His responsibilities included supporting the operation of university governance processes and contributing to the coordination of academic and administrative matters at institutional level.

The position formed an important part of his transition from an academic and researcher into broader higher-education leadership.

Scholarships and international mobility

As Director of Missions and Scholarships, Al Hamdany worked in an area central to the internationalisation of Iraqi higher education.

His responsibilities included matters relating to international scholarships, academic mobility and the development of overseas study opportunities for Iraqi academics and students.

This experience subsequently contributed to his involvement in international university partnerships and European higher-education projects.

Postgraduate education

Al Hamdany also served as Founding Director of Graduate Studies, contributing to the development and coordination of postgraduate education and research at the University of Kufa.

His postgraduate leadership has included academic-program development, research coordination, supervision structures and institutional processes associated with graduate education.

Career in Australia

Al Hamdany subsequently developed a significant academic career in Australia, particularly in South Australia.

His Australian academic experience includes work with the University of Adelaide and the University of South Australia.

His Australian career has combined teaching, research and academic development with an ongoing focus on international students, English language education, higher education and academic quality.

His experience working across Iraqi and Australian universities has provided a comparative perspective on higher-education systems, academic standards, internationalisation and institutional development.

2000s–2010s: Applied linguistics and English language education

During the earlier stage of his research career, Al Hamdany focused primarily on applied linguistics, English language education and English for Academic Purposes.

His research examined how Iraqi students and other English-as-an-additional-language learners develop the language practices required for successful participation in higher education.

His work particularly examined spoken academic register, a relatively underexplored dimension of academic English compared with written academic language.

2013: Research on Iraqi students and academic register

In 2013, Al Hamdany, Michelle Picard, Nina Maadad and Indrawati Darmawan published research examining the perceptions and use of spoken academic register among Iraqi students participating in an English for Academic Purposes program at an Australian university.

The study involved 52 Iraqi students and examined their experiences of academic spoken language and the role of pre-enrolment English programs in preparing students for university study.

The research established one of the central themes of Al Hamdany’s scholarship: the relationship between language preparedness, educational transition and successful participation in higher education.

2015: Doctoral research

In 2015, Al Hamdany completed his PhD at the University of Adelaide.

His thesis, An Exploration of Perceptions and Applications of Spoken Register: Iraqi Students at a South Australian University, investigated how Iraqi students perceived and applied different forms of spoken academic language.

The doctoral research contributed to understanding the challenges faced by English-as-an-additional-language students transitioning into Australian higher education.

2015: Adult learners and English for Academic Purposes

Also in 2015, Al Hamdany and Michelle Picard published research in the Journal of Adult and Continuing Education examining Iraqi adult learners’ experiences of spoken register in English for Academic Purposes programs at an Australian university.

The research extended his earlier work on academic language by considering how adult Iraqi learners negotiated academic and non-academic registers in an Australian educational environment.

2010s: International higher-education leadership

During the 2010s, Al Hamdany’s professional activities increasingly incorporated international higher education, university partnerships and institutional development.

His work connected Iraqi higher education with Australian and European institutions and involved international scholarships, academic mobility, institutional partnerships and capacity building.

This period marked a transition from a primarily applied-linguistics profile towards a broader higher-education leadership and internationalisation profile.

European higher-education projects

Al Hamdany subsequently participated in a number of European collaborative projects involving Iraqi and European universities.

These projects expanded his professional experience into:

* international project management;
* institutional capacity building;
* curriculum development;
* academic quality;
* communication and dissemination;
* research collaboration;
* cultural heritage and education;
* internationalisation; and
* European–Iraqi university cooperation.

EDUU

Al Hamdany was a member of the University of Kufa team participating in the EDUU – Education and Cultural Heritage Enhancement for Social Cohesion in Iraq project.

The project involved collaboration between Iraqi and European universities and addressed the relationship between higher education, cultural heritage and social cohesion.

His participation contributed to the development of international academic networks connecting Iraqi higher education with European institutions.

WALADU

He also participated in WALADU – Development and Structuring of BA Courses in Archaeology in Iraq, a European university cooperation initiative involving Iraqi and European higher-education institutions.

The project focused on the development and restructuring of university-level archaeology education and strengthening academic cooperation between Iraqi and European institutions.

BANUU

Al Hamdany was also involved in the BANUU project.

Project documentation records his involvement in the University of Kufa team and his contribution to communication and dissemination activities.

The project included formal arrangements for project management and quality control, giving Al Hamdany additional experience within international higher-education project structures.

Quality assurance

A major component of Al Hamdany’s professional profile is higher-education quality assurance.

His experience encompasses academic standards, curriculum quality, program development, quality processes, benchmarking, continuous improvement and institutional development.

He has undertaken professional development and engagement associated with international quality-assurance frameworks, including the Quality Assurance Agency for Higher Education (QAA) in the United Kingdom.

His professional experience across Iraq and Australia has allowed him to work with higher-education systems operating under different regulatory and quality-assurance environments.

His quality-assurance philosophy emphasises the use of quality systems not merely for compliance but as mechanisms for:

* academic enhancement;
* institutional improvement;
* evidence-based decision-making;
* curriculum quality;
* student outcomes;
* international benchmarking; and
* institutional competitiveness.

Academic governance and leadership

Al Hamdany’s leadership experience encompasses several levels of university governance.

His responsibilities have included:

University governance — participation in university-level decision-making and council processes.

Postgraduate leadership — development and coordination of graduate education and research.

International scholarships — management and coordination of international academic mobility.

Academic quality — engagement with quality assurance, standards and academic development.

Internationalisation — development of international partnerships and collaborative projects.

Research — development of research networks and participation in international research projects.

This combination gives his professional profile a multidisciplinary character extending beyond his original specialisation in applied linguistics.

2024: Curriculum and critical discourse research

In 2024, Al Hamdany and Michelle Picard published research on the critical discourse analysis of pre-enrolment English-program curriculum documents.

The research examined how curriculum documents construct academic language expectations and prepare English-as-an-additional-language students for university registers.

The publication extended Al Hamdany’s earlier work on academic English into curriculum analysis, discourse and educational policy.

2026: World Englishes

In 2026, Al Hamdany and Michelle Picard contributed the entry “Iraq, English in” to The Wiley Blackwell Encyclopedia of World Englishes.

The publication represents an expansion of his scholarship into the study of English in Iraq and its relationship to language, education and sociocultural contexts.

The encyclopedia is an international scholarly reference work published by Wiley.

Muslim identity, belonging and intergroup relations

Al Hamdany’s more recent research has expanded beyond applied linguistics into identity formation, belonging and intergroup relations in education.

His research examines the experiences of Muslim secondary-school students in Australia and investigates how students negotiate religious, cultural and national identities within different educational environments.

The research considers:

* Muslim identity;
* Australian identity;
* religious and cultural belonging;
* Sunni–Shiʿite identity;
* intergroup relations;
* educational context;
* identity negotiation; and
* the relationship between institutional environments and young people’s sense of belonging.

The work uses a mixed-methods research design, combining quantitative survey research with qualitative interviews.

Internationalisation of higher education

Internationalisation has remained a consistent component of Al Hamdany’s professional career.

His international work has involved cooperation among universities in:

* Australia;
* Iraq;
* Europe; and
* the wider Middle East.

His activities have included international partnerships, mobility, scholarships, research collaboration, curriculum development, quality assurance and institutional capacity building.

His experience in both Iraqi and Australian higher education has enabled him to work across different institutional and regulatory environments.

Higher-education reform and institutional development

Al Hamdany’s broader professional interests include higher-education reform and institutional development.

He has worked on issues involving:

* university quality;
* academic standards;
* graduate employability;
* curriculum relevance;
* vocational education and training;
* university–industry engagement;
* innovation;
* entrepreneurship;
* technology incubation;
* research capacity;
* international rankings;
* internationalisation; and
* institutional competitiveness.

He has argued for closer integration between universities, technical and vocational education, industry and national economic development.

Research interests

Professional service

Al Hamdany has participated in professional and scholarly activities associated with education, applied linguistics, translation and higher education.

His professional activities have included academic peer review, editorial work, professional associations, international conferences and academic project committees.

He has also undertaken professional work in translation and interpreting, complementing his academic expertise in language and intercultural communication.

Academic and professional identity

Al Hamdany’s career can be characterised by the intersection of four fields:

University governance, postgraduate education, academic development and institutional leadership.

His experience across Iraq and Australia, combined with his engagement with European higher-education projects, provides an international dimension to his academic and leadership profile.

Geographic and professional trajectory

Al Hamdany’s professional trajectory can be broadly understood in three stages:

data.title: Bloxdio
data.text:
Bloxd.io is a free online video game, released in January of 2021 by an independent developer, Arthur Benedict Baker. It is a sandbox game inspired by the games Minecraft, and Roblox. The game features blocky 3D graphics all ran on a web browser, needing no download. As of 2026 Bloxd.io has 461 million plays on Crazy Games and an average player count of 21,000 people.

== Gamemodes ==
Bloxd.io has many gamemodes to choose from. The gamemodes range from being Open world, games such as survival, creative, and Bloxdsmp where you can gather resources, farm, and build houses. Another genre of gamemodes is PvP. PvP gamemodes include bedwars, Skyblock, and cube warfare. In these gamemodes, it is fast paced, and player will need to utilize their material to the max. Skill games are another type of gamemode mostly including parkour, where you would have to jump over obstacles to make it to the end. Bloxd.io also has a feature where you can create a new world where you have the power of using commands and code blocks to make your own mini games. None of the gamemodes contain a pay-wall [ref: Bloxd.io Wiki, bloxd-io.fandom.com]

== Ranks ==
Bloxd.io has only 1 rank, Super Rank. Super Rank Is a 30 days paid rank added on December 18, 2024. The rank is not pay-to-win because it doesn't give the user any gameplay advantage. The rank's perks are cosmetics. Spending $10 on Super Rank would give you the following, visual badges, name colors (would allow you to change the color of your username), capes, and remove all advertisements. The only free way of getting Super Rank is through winning it through a YouTube giveaway, or reporting a bug. [ref: Bloxd.io Wiki, bloxd-io.fandom.com]

data.title: MTW Agency

MTW Agency, also known as More Than Words, is a culture marketing agency based in Los Angeles. Founded by Matt Ferrigno and Diana Dotel, the company specializes in talent and brand partnerships, influencer marketing, entertainment marketing, and experiential activations. [ref: Our Services, MTW Agency] [ref: ] [ref: Latinos in Music Q&A: Diana Dotel, MTW, Hispanic Executive] [ref: MTW Agency Helps Create Brand Strategies Which Are More Than Words, Forbes]

=== History ===
Ferrigno and Dotel established MTW to develop partnerships between brands and talent. Before co-founding the agency, Dotel worked in concert promotion and live entertainment. The agency's early work included collaborations involving music artists and consumer brands.

In 2022, MTW was named culture agency of record for Patrón Tequila. The appointment included work on the brand's cultural strategy and audience connections. [ref: ]

=== Operations and selected work ===
MTW's services include influencer partnerships, cultural marketing strategy, music and film partnerships, creative development, and campaign measurement. The agency describes its influencer selection approach as talent-agnostic, selecting partners according to the brand and intended audience.

In a 2025 Pollstar interview, Ferrigno discussed influencer marketing alongside festival activations and tour sponsorships. Examples included HBO Max's sponsorship of Sueños and Patrón's sponsorship of Becky G's tour, with influencers attending events and sharing their experiences through social content. [ref: Branding Survey 2025: On Brand And In Command - Pollstar News]

MTW has also worked on brand partnerships involving Bad Bunny and adidas, Becky G and Patrón, SZA and Grey Goose, and Carín León and Cash App. A 2024 Forbes contributor profile discussed the agency's role in developing partnerships between brands and recording artists.

For HBO Max's Romeo Santos: King of Bachata campaign, a Shorty Awards entry credits Ferrigno, Dotel, and MTW account executive Natalia Saavedra. The entry describes experiential activity in New York, a festival partnership in Los Angeles, an influencer screening in Miami, and social activations. [ref: Romeo Santos: King of Bachata - The Shorty Awards, shortyawards.com]

=== Recognition ===
At the 2026 SABRE Awards North America, More Than Words (MTW) was credited alongside BBH USA, M Booth, and OMD on the Patrón campaign, "How PATRÓN Tequila Turned Censorship into the Campaign." The campaign received the Platinum SABRE Award for Best in Show and the Integrated Marketing award. [ref: 2026 Winners, PRovoke Media]

data.text:
----

Hazrat Khawaja Pir Ghulam Ahmed Chishti Sabri is a Sufi saint of the Chishtiya Sabriya order based in Matli, District Badin, Sindh, Pakistan.

== Biography ==
Pir Ghulam Ahmed Chishti Sabri was associated with the Chishti Sabri spiritual lineage. His teachings focused on love, peace, and service to humanity in accordance with Sufi traditions.

== Shrine ==
His shrine (Dargah) is located in Matli, Sindh. Devotees from across Sindh visit the shrine to pay respects.

== Urs ==
The annual Urs (death anniversary) of Hazrat Pir Ghulam Ahmed Chishti Sabri is observed every year on 6th March at his shrine in Matli. The Urs is observed with religious devotion. The gathering includes recitation of the Holy Quran, Naat Khwani, and Mehfil-e-Sama. A large number of devotees, scholars and spiritual leaders attend the Urs. Langar is also distributed among attendees.

== Legacy ==
He is remembered for his contributions to promoting Sufi teachings, interfaith harmony, and spiritual guidance in the region of Matli and lower Sindh.

= Grass Patch =
Grass Patch was an American rock band from Fort Lauderdale, Florida, active during the 1990s. The band was associated with South Florida’s independent music scene and released a track on the 1995 split 7-inch A Field Guide to Crop Circle Activity, shared with Milk-Shed and released by Space Cadette Records.[1][2]

== History ==
Grass Patch was part of the South Florida underground music scene during the 1990s. In a September 1996 article, Miami New Times described the band as working in a heavier musical style than local punk band Milk-Shed and noted the two groups’ split single on Space Cadette Records.[1]

The band’s documented release, A Field Guide to Crop Circle Activity, was issued in 1995. The record paired Grass Patch with fellow Florida band Milk-Shed and featured elaborate artwork and packaging.[1][2] Grass Patch’s credited track on the split was “Xenogamy.” The tracks “Whoa” and “Live” were credited to Milk-Shed, not Grass Patch.[2]

In an April 2002 article about the Fort Lauderdale band the Remedy Session, Miami New Times described Grass Patch as a noisecore band and reported that it had split up before drummer Alex Osuna and guitarist Chris Polito began working on a new musical project.[3]

== Members ==
The band’s lineup was:

* Ray Sousa – guitar, vocals
* Josh Gibbs – guitar
* Scott Hanzlik – bass
* Alex Osuna – drums[2]

== Discography ==

=== Split releases ===

* A Field Guide to Crop Circle Activity (1995, split 7-inch with Milk-Shed; Space Cadette Records)[1][2]

Grass Patch track

* “Xenogamy”[2]

The other tracks on the split, “Whoa” and “Live,” were credited to Milk-Shed.[2]

A cassette associated with the band has the following handwritten tracklist, transcribed from the cassette cover:

The cassette’s title, release date, and release status have not been independently established.

data.title: Blockmec
data.text:
Blockmec Technology is a Nigerian technology company founded in 2019 that develops digital products and software solutions for commerce, payments, product verification, and enterprise operations. Its product portfolio includes Blockmec Verify, a product authentication initiative, and BinPay, a digital initiative focused on waste-management bill payments.

== History ==

Founded in 2019, Blockmec Technology was established to develop technology-based solutions for business and operational challenges. Its areas of interest include digital verification, payment systems, and software platforms intended to improve the management of transactions and services.

The company develops digital products intended to address needs across the private and public sectors. Its broader ambition is to support the adoption of digital tools that can improve record-keeping, transaction transparency, and operational efficiency.

== Products and services ==

=== Blockmec Verify ===

Blockmec Verify is a product authentication and verification initiative within Blockmec Technology's product portfolio. It is designed to help users verify product information and address risks associated with counterfeit goods.

The product focuses on digital verification and its potential applications in product identification, consumer protection, and counterfeit-risk detection.

=== BinPay ===

BinPay is a digital payment initiative focused on waste-management billing and collection processes. It aims to support the digitization of waste bills and provide a more organized approach to recording payments.

The initiative is intended to make waste-management payments more accessible and support transparency in billing and collection processes. Its potential users include residents, waste-management operators, and public institutions responsible for environmental services.

=== Other products ===

Blockmec's listed products also include Moonsource, Close Network, Soundspec, OS Square, Blockmec Chain and 1base. Further descriptions of these products should be added where reliable published sources are available.

== Areas of focus ==

Blockmec Technology's stated areas of focus include:

* Product verification: Digital tools designed to support product authentication and address counterfeit-related risks.
* Digital payments: Software solutions intended to simplify payment processes and improve transaction records.
* Enterprise software: Digital platforms designed to support business operations and administrative processes.
* Public-sector technology: Solutions intended to assist institutions with service administration, billing, and collection processes.
* Digital transformation: The application of software to improve processes traditionally managed through manual or less integrated systems.

== Business objectives ==

Blockmec Technology aims to develop software products that address operational challenges and can be adapted to different markets. Its stated objectives include improving access to digital services, supporting more transparent transactions, and helping organizations adopt technology in their operations.

The company has expressed an ambition to expand its solutions beyond Nigeria into other African countries and emerging markets. Its potential growth will depend on factors including product adoption, technical development, partnerships, and the requirements of the markets in which its solutions operate.

== Market focus ==

Blockmec Technology's products address potential needs across sectors including consumer goods authentication, payment services, waste management, and enterprise operations.

Digital product verification can help businesses and consumers assess product information, while digital billing and payment systems can support the administration of service charges and the recording of collections.

data.title: Faith, Commerce, and Cultural Exchange in the World of Ibn Battuta
data.text:
Faith, Commerce, and Cultural Exchange in the World of Ibn Battuta: Travelling Islam is an edited academic book edited by Abbas Panakkal and published by Palgrave Macmillan in 2026. It examines the travels of the fourteenth-century Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta and the historical relationships between Islam, commerce and cultural exchange across Africa, Asia and Europe. [ref: Faith, Commerce, and Cultural Exchange in the World of Ibn Battuta: Travelling Islam, Palgrave Macmillan]

== Contents ==

The volume consists of fifteen (15) chapters arranged in three sections: "Historical Accounts of Travel and Tradition", "Textual Tradition, Jurisprudence and Cultural Exchange", and "Pilgrimage, Faith, and Identity Across Borders". The chapters examine Ibn Battuta's accounts of African societies, religious and commercial networks in South and Southeast Asia, Islamic finance in the Maldives, the history of Calicut, and Muslim communities in precolonial Malabar. Other subjects include the transmission of cultural traditions between India and Southeast Asia, women and religion in Ibn Battuta's accounts of India, and pilgrimage and religious revivalism in West Africa. [ref: Faith, Commerce, and Cultural Exchange in the World of Ibn Battuta: Travelling Islam, Palgrave Macmillan]

The contributions approach Ibn Battuta's travel narrative, commonly known as the Rihla, from historical, archaeological, religious, legal and cultural perspectives. The final chapter examines encounters between travelling musicians and Indian performers in nineteenth-century Australia.

== Publication ==

The book was published by Palgrave Macmillan, an imprint of Springer Nature, as part of the Palgrave Series in Indian Ocean World Studies.

The pront edition has ISBN 978-3-031-97882-1, and the electronic edition has ISBN 978-3-031-97883-8. [ref: Faith, Commerce, and Cultural Exchange in the World of Ibn Battuta: Travelling Islam, Palgrave Macmillan]

data.title: Vino Volta Winery
data.text:
----

Vino Volta is an Australian Wine producer based in the Swan Valley (Western Australia) Wine Region. It was founded by winemaker Garth Cliff and Kristen McGann, and it released its first wines in 2019 [ref: WA Wine Review 2026, Ray Jordan Wine] [ref: Vino Volta, Wine Companion]. Vino Volta is known mainly for producing Chenin Blanc and Grenache from Swan Valley fruit and has been associated with renewed interest in the region's wines. [ref: The Best Swan Valley Wineries Featured in the 2020 YGOW Top 50, Young Gun of Wine] [ref: What to Know About Swan Valley, the Birthplace of Western Australian Wine?, Vino Joy News]

== History ==
Cliff began working in the wine industry around 2000. He held winemaking roles in the Hunter Valley wine region and at the South Australian wineries Stonehaven and Tintara, and worked vintages in Napa Valley and on California's Central Coast before joining Houghton Wines in the Swan Valley. He was a winemaker at Houghton for about ten years.

Cliff began developing the Vino Volta label in 2018, and its first wines were released in 2019. Cliff and McGann also established a wine import business, Wine Terroirists.

In 2020, Vino Volta was named in the Young Gun of Wine Top 50.

== Vineyards and Winemaking ==
Vino Volta sources fruit from leased vineyards and independent growers, mainly in the Swan Valley, with some fruit from the Geographe wine region and the Perth Hills. The producer focuses on varieties suited to warm climates, particularly Chenin Blanc and Grenache, alongside other varieties including Dolcetto, Vermentino and Fiano, and a fortified Verdelho.

The Vino Volta winemaking process uses wild yeast fermentation and no added enzymes, with techniques such as skin contact, whole-bunch fermentation and maturation in older oak. Production is around 2,800 dozen per year, and the wines are sold locally and exported to the United States, Japan, Singapore and Sweden.

== Reception ==
Wine writer Ray Jordan profiled Vino Volta in his WA Wine Review 2026, describing Cliff as an advocate for the Swan Valley as a warm-climate wine region. He rated the producer's Intimations of Immortality Liqueur Verdelho 98 out of 100. The producer has also been reviewed in Business News, [ref: Review: Elements in balance at Vino Volta, www.businessnews.com.au] The West Australian, [ref: Looking back to the future with chenin blanc, The West Australian] and Gourmet Traveller. [ref: Wine country: Swan Valley wineries to know about, Gourmet Traveller]

data.title: Julius Grafton
data.text:
----

Julius Grafton (born 1957) is an Australian entertainment technology publisher, journalist and trade show organiser. He founded the trade magazine CX and the ENTECH exhibition for the professional audio, lighting and audiovisual industry, and is the subject of a chapter in Stuart Coupe's 2018 history Roadies.

== Early career ==
Grafton was born in Melbourne in 1957. He began in the Australian live production industry in the early 1970s, running psychedelic light shows for bands before moving into stage and theatre lighting. Based in Sydney, he started his own lighting company in 1974 and in 1980 opened a production company, Grafton's Sound and Lighting, touring as a sound engineer with Australian rock bands; the first band he worked with regularly was the ska revival group The Allniters. He also founded the loudspeaker manufacturer Australian Monitor. His years on the road, and his views on the working conditions and welfare of road crews, are the subject of a chapter in Stuart Coupe's Roadies: The Secret History of Australian Rock'n'Roll (Hachette, 2018).

== Publishing ==
Grafton moved into publishing in 1990 and edited and published CX Magazine, a trade journal for the entertainment, sound and lighting industry, for almost thirty years. He sold the magazine in January 2020 to VCS Creative Publishing, owned by its then editor Jason Allen, and has continued to contribute articles.

He has written opinion pieces for the general press, including a 2019 Sydney Morning Herald column opposing the New South Wales government's interim music festival guidelines, which he argued would restrict live performance beyond dance festivals.

== ENTECH and other events ==
Grafton founded the ENTECH entertainment technology trade show in Sydney in 1993. It grew into a multi-day exhibition occupying more than 10,000 square metres at the Sydney and Melbourne exhibition centres. In 2003 he sold the event to Exhibitions and Trade Fairs Pty Ltd, a trade show organiser backed by Publishing and Broadcasting Limited, with CX remaining the official show publication. He returned to run the educational program for the 2010 edition under its new owners.

Grafton later reacquired the ENTECH name and relaunched it as the ENTECH Roadshow, a one-day touring format staged annually in Australian capital cities and every second year in New Zealand. A planned United States edition was abandoned before launch ahead of the COVID-19 pandemic. In 2014 he founded SECTECH, a companion roadshow for the security technology industry, which he operated in partnership with a publishing house until 2022, when the partnership broke down and the company was placed in voluntary liquidation.

In 2025 Grafton stepped aside from ENTECH, with Kate McKenzie appointed chief executive, and acquired Sydney PA Hire, a corporate audiovisual rental company. In 2026 Mumbrella reported on his public rejection of an influencer agency's request for about $16,000 of audiovisual services in exchange for exposure.

== Training and industry involvement ==
From about 2001 to 2010 Grafton ran Julius Events College, a privately funded registered training organisation in Sydney offering full-time technical production courses, with scholarships funded by industry suppliers. He has served on the board of CrewCare, a charity for Australian live production workers.

== Book ==
Grafton self-published a memoir, This Could Be Serious, in 2020, with proceeds directed to CrewCare.

Viktor Sukau is a businessman in the agricultural inputs industry. He is the founder of Natural Green, a mineral-based fertiliser company, and is associated with MNG, a farming-system brand developed through a partnership between Natural Green and Jordan's Manaseer Group. [ref: How natural fertilisers can benefit farmers, Farmer's Weekly]

== Career ==
Sukau founded Natural Green in Germany; according to the company, its headquarters later moved to Switzerland. [ref: Our story, Manaseer Natural Green]

In March 2023, AgriBusiness Global published an article on the Manaseer Natural Green joint venture that quoted Sukau, described as CSO and founder of Natural Green, on the lower carbon footprint of mineral-based fertilisers compared with conventional NPK fertilisers. [ref: Manaseer Natural Green: How a Fertilizer Joint Venture is Making Great Strides in the Agricultural Market, AgriBusiness Global]

In June 2023, Farmer's Weekly published an interview with Sukau, identified as "CSO" of Manaseer Natural Green, and the company's CEO, Anton Prysiazhniuk. Sukau argued that farmers should move from synthetic fertilisers towards environmentally friendly alternatives, citing reduced pollution and improved soil health. The article described MNG as a joint venture between Natural Green and the Manaseer Group.

According to Manaseer MNG, MNG was established in September 2022 as a joint venture between Sukau and the Manaseer Group, and is operated by Manaseer Trade House L.L.C. [ref: About, Manaseer MNG]

As of 2026, Forbes Middle East Events lists Sukau as co-founder and chief sustainability officer of DAR Manaseer Trade House. [ref: Viktor Sukau, Forbes Middle East Events]

== Agricultural projects ==
In October 2026, Roya News reported on a rice-cultivation trial by the Manaseer Group in the Qatrana area of Jordan, using drip irrigation and locally produced natural fertilisers. data.title: Henry Martin
data.text:
Henry Martin is an American media personality known for his high-profile relationship with model and television personality Kendall Jenner.

== Public profile and media ==
In contrast to many public figures, Martin maintains a very low profile on social media. His only official personal account is on Snapchat under the username `@[user]_henryy`, and he is notably absent from other major social media platforms such as Instagram and X (formerly Twitter).

== Personal life ==
Since 2022, Martin has been in a relationship with Kendall Jenner. The couple has kept their relationship out of the public eye and away from media scrutiny, reportedly on the advice of Jenner's mother and manager, Kris Jenner, who encouraged them to maintain privacy regarding their personal life.

data.title: Jahed Al-Hasan
data.text:
----

Jahed Al-Hasan (also reported as Jahed Ahmed) is a Bangladeshi youth involved in child protection and digital safety initiatives. He is the founder of iSafe BD, a youth-led initiative focused on online safety education and support for children and teenagers. In 2026, he was listed as a nominee for the International Children's Peace Prize by the Netherlands-based organisation KidsRights. [ref: Jahed Ahmed, KidsRights]

== Work ==
Al-Hasan founded iSafe BD to address issues including cyberbullying, online harassment, fraud and online exploitation affecting children and teenagers. According to his KidsRights profile, he also developed a pilot model of a digital missing-child alert system intended to circulate verified information about missing children. The same profile states that he conducted digital-safety awareness programmes at more than 20 schools and colleges in Bangladesh.

== Recognition ==
In 2026, KidsRights listed Al-Hasan, under the name Jahed Ahmed, among the nominees for the International Children's Peace Prize. The organisation identifies child protection and digital safety among the themes of his work.

A June 2025 report by Jainta Barta also covered his work in cybersecurity and recognition associated with his activities. [ref: সাইবার সুরক্ষায় জাতীয় স্বীকৃতি পেলেন ওসমানীনগরের জাহেদ, Jainta Barta]

data.text:
Shai Diego Hope (born 10 November 1993) is a Barbadian cricketer who has played for the West Indies cricket team. A right-handed batsman and wicket-keeper, he has scored 28 centuries in international cricket: 5 in Test cricket, 21 in One Day International (ODI) cricket and 2 in Twenty20 International (T20I) cricket.

Hope made his Test debut against England on 1 May 2015 at Kensington Oval in Bridgetown, Barbados. [ref: Shai Hope, International Cricket Council] He scored his maiden Test century during the 2017 tour of England, making 147 and an unbeaten 118 in the second Test at Headingley. [ref: Brathwaite, Hope reach career-best rankings, International Cricket Council] His two centuries made him the first batsman to score a century in each innings of a first-class match at Headingley. The West Indies won the match by five wickets after successfully chasing 322. [ref: Windies Test match defeat 'fresh in the minds' of England players - Trevor Bayliss, International Cricket Council] His highest Test score is 147.

Hope made his ODI debut against Sri Lanka in November 2016. [ref: 'If I had to open the bowling for West Indies, I'd do it' – Shai Hope, International Cricket Council] He scored his maiden ODI century against Zimbabwe in Bulawayo, scoring 101. [ref: Shai Hope, International Cricket Council] His highest ODI score is an unbeaten 170, which he scored against Ireland in 2019. [ref: Hope could be 'one of our best ODI players ever' – Jason Holder, International Cricket Council] In August 2022, Hope scored a century in his 100th ODI against India, becoming the tenth West Indies player to score a century in his 100th ODI. [ref: Axar keeps his cool to guide India to series-clinching victory, International Cricket Council] In February 2023, he was appointed captain of the West Indies ODI team. [ref: West Indies announce Pooran's replacements as ODI and T20I captain, International Cricket Council]

data.title: Shepherd's Bush Cricket Club
data.text:
Shepherd's Bush Cricket Club is an English cricket club based in west London. It plays in the Premier Division of the Middlesex County Cricket League and is one of the closest clubs to the centre of London.

In 2026 Shepherd’s Bush CC won the ECB National Club Cricket Championship, [ref: Shepherd's Bush win National Cup] the most prestigious competition in English club cricket. They have also won the Middlesex Cup three times, in 1981, 1994 and 2024, [ref: Middlesex Cup Winners] as well as the Middlesex T20 Cup (2024). [ref: MCCL-T20-2024-Winners:Shepherds Bush]

The club was founded in 1882 [ref: History of Shepherd's Bush Cricket Club] by young men from the Shepherd's Bush parish church, St Stephen's, under the presidency of the vicar. Initially called St Stephen’s CC, they played first in a field just west of Old Oak Road in East Acton, then on a nearby tree-lined ground on East Acton Lane, remaining there for almost 120 years. In 1893, the club became known as Shepherd's Bush.

The first pavilion was erected in 1909, then replaced with a larger structure in 1935, after which the ground developed a reputation as one of the prettiest in London. [ref: History of Shepherd's Bush Cricket Club]

Among the earliest of more than 20 first class players to have played for the club were Manek Bajana of Somerset and Charles Burgess of Sussex, both in the early 1900s.

Shepherd’s Bush CC was one of the 16 founding members of the Middlesex County Cricket League in 1972. Having enjoyed a reputation as a sociable and hospitable club, during the 1980s and 1990s it became renowned for having a strong contingent of players from the Caribbean diaspora, [ref: We Were Pioneers] including Martin Jean-Jacques, who went on to play for Derbyshire and Hampshire, and Kervin Marc, who played for Middlesex. During that era, Jamaican-born Alf Langley, who is now the club’s president, had three spells as club captain. [ref: Interview with Alf Langley]

In the early 2000s the Goldsmiths company, which owned the East Acton Lane ground, declined to renew the club's lease and sold the land to developers, forcing the club to build a new facility just a few yards to the south in Bromyard Avenue, East Acton. It moved there in 2004. [ref: History of Shepherd's Bush Cricket Club]

Since then the club has been active in coaching initiatives in local primary schools. It has in excess of 250 boy and girl juniors, as well as three women's teams, five Saturday men’s teams and a Sunday team. It is one of the few clubs in the UK still maintaining the tradition of holding a Cricket Week each summer, with five midweek home matches against invited sides in July. [ref: Shepherd's Bush Cricket Club narrowly lose to Marylebone]

Shepherd's Bush's victory in the National Knockout Competition in 2026 came against the Bradford Premier League side New Farnley, [ref: New Farnley Cricket Club] of Leeds. They became the first Middlesex County Cricket League club to lift the national trophy since 1991.

data.title: Robert Peckham (MP)
data.text:
Sir Robert Peckham (by 1516 – 10 September 1569) was an English politician. He sat as MP for Buckinghamshire in April 1554. [ref: PECKHAM, Sir Robert (by 1516-69), of London, Biddlesden and Denham, Bucks., History of Parliament Online]

He was knighted on 2 October 1553.

== Family and education ==
He was the first son of Sir Edmund Peckham of Denham by Anne, the daughter of John Cheyne of Chesham Bois, Buckinghamshire. He was the brother of Henry Peckham (MP for Wycombe). He was admitted into Gray's Inn in 1533., he married Mary, the daughter of Edmund Braye, 1st Baron Braye.

== Political career ==
He also served as clerk comptroller of the counting house by 1540 till 1543; justice of the peace for Buckinghamshire from 1542 till 1547, quorum in 1558/59; commissioner of subsidy in 1543, commissioner of relief in 1550; escheator in Bedfordshire and Buckinghamshire from 1545 till 1546; sheriff from 1556 till 1557; member of the Privy Council from August 1553 till November 1558.
