data.title: Charles de Loupoigne
data.text:
Charles de Loupoigne (14 March 1761 - 30 July 1799) was a man from the Southern Netherlands known for his resistance to the French occupation of that area. His acts of resistance inspired the Peasants' War. He was also known by the nom de guerre Charles François Jacqmin and the nicknames Cousin Charles or Charlepoeng.

== Family==
His father Jean Joseph Jacqmin was an eau de vie and brandy merchant, a gin distiller and corporal in Brussels' garde-bourgeoise. He was a son of Marie Virly and Jean Antoine Jacqmin, both based in Brussels. They were both buried in the parish of Saint Géry, Marie in 1758 and Jean Antoine in 1762. Almost all the Jacqmin family moved to live in Brussels. Jean Joseph and his two brothers were all born in Braine-l'Alleud and all three gained promotion to become Bourgeois of Brussels, Jean Joseph in 1752, Bartholomée in 1753 and Nicolas in 1772.

In 1752 Jean Joseph married Brigitte Josèphe Quertenmont in Saint-Nicolas parish in Brussels - she died in the parish of Saint-Géry in 1759. Again in the parish of Saint-Géry, Jean Joseph married Marie Josèphe De Glain or De Glin four months after his first wife's death. Charles François Jacqmin was born eighteen months after the marriage, followed by a second son, François Chrisostôme Jacqmin, in 1765. François later became a musician at the Théâtre des Arts in Rouen and had two marriages, one in Paris and another in Canteleu, both of which had issue. Jean Joseph Jacqmin died in Brussels on 21 May 1797. - Charles Francois's mother was still alive at the time.

A record from 1767 mentions Jean Joseph as an eau de vie maker at 30 Rue de l'Étuve, at its junction with Rue de l'Amigo, in section 30 of the city (Saint-Nicolas). Another from 1776 has him requesting a 'tolbrief' and giving his address as at the sign of 'Aen Sint Jan'.

==Life==
===Armed resistance===
He was born in Brussels and baptised at Saint-Géry church in the city on 14 March 1761. His family spoke French, but he learned Flemish with his playmates. He began but did not complete studies in surgery and unsuccessfully attempted to become a wine merchant on Rue du Lombard in Brussels.

In July 1789 he was made an excise officer in Brussels but lost that job on the outbreak of the Brabant Revolution and the French driving the Austrians out of the Southern Nerthlands, instead becoming a recruiting sergeant for the Franc Corps of Grün-Laudon, an Austrian regiment. When the Austrian forces crossed the Rhine at Neuss on 5 November 1794 he was captured and taken to Charleville.

He escaped in late December and headed for Brabant, but was arrested in his hiding place on 6 March 1795 and this time sent to the citadel in Doullens. He was freed a few months later in return for a security deposit. In June that year he was sheltered by Antoine Bève in Loupoigne. There Jacqmin took on the nickname Charles de Loupoigne, which misspelling transformed into Charlepoeng. He decided to oppose the French occupation of the Southern Netherlands and formed a group of forty armed men, calling it "The Belgian Army". His second-in-command was a distant relation, Antoine Lecoq, a slate worker in Baulers.

His force attacked a French-held foundry with an attached arms factory in Genappe on 3 January 1796, even though France and Austria had signed an armistice on 21 December the previous year. It was therefore a complete surprise to the French troops, who were all captured. The Tree of Liberty planted in front of the 'Le Roy d'Espagne' inn was cut down and the successful attack drew in new volunteers. The following day he and his force ambushed more French troops, this time at the Quatre Bras crossroads near Charleroi, capturing twenty-four men and 104 army horses. Near Gosselies he robbed a mail coach between Charleroi and Brussels, capturing three French travellers. One other traveller, Chapel, escaped and informed the French authorities in Brussels what had happened.

Those authorities immediately sent a garrison under commander Carette from Brussels to Gosselies. It attacked Charles' troops by night and - finding them asleep or drunk - easily defeated them. Lecoq was captured and interrogated, telling the French the true identity of 'Charlepoeng'. Lecoq was condemned to death and on 17 January shot in Place de la Liberté. The same sentence was passed on in absentia on 25 February on Charles and on Dom Guillaume de Chentinne, prior of the Cistercian abbey in Villers which sheltered Charles for a long period. de Chentinne was hidden in Charleroi by his brother and finally given an amnesty, dying a natural death in Jauche on 6 November 1811.

=== Peasants' War and death ===
From then on Charles lived a more clandestine life and changed tactics, terrorising and disarming French soldiers and stealing from the municipal coffers. On 18 April 1797 Austria and French agreed a treaty and Charles stopped his acts of resistance, failing to take an active part in the Peasants' War.

He took up arms again on 19 July 1799 and near Blanden captured Van Billioen, an old municipal agent in the village who had previously helped the brigands but had then been arrested for that supported. Charles avenged himself on him and on 23 July captured and for the same reason executed the former brigand Guilliam Bartholomeus, who had betrayed Charles and his troops and frequently given away their hiding places.

His force grew significantly and was able to carry out armed resistance against the French Army itself. On 30 July, at Neerijse, he forced two former brigands to join his army. This pair escaped and were captured by a French mobile column, to which they revealed Charles' location. His forces were encircled in a wood, the Margijsbos, [ref: Het Margijsbos aan de Ijse in Loonbeek, op zoek naar natuur, het kasteel, Charlepoeng en de watermolen by Ernst Gülcher] also known as the Marghys Bosch or the Bois de Marie Ghys, behind the castle at Loonbeek. He was killed in battle by a sabre cut from a mounted chasseur, despite surrendering after being wounded and asking to be captured alive.

According to Alphonse Wauters four of Charles' companions died with him - his servant Amand André Vanermen from Neerijse, Pierre Vandevelde from Brusseghem, Jacques Abeloos from Vossem, and a fourth unnamed man. They were buried in the forest. The same day three more peasants were killed, Pierre De Waels and François De Both from the Kauhof or Keyhof farm near Huldenbergh and Pierre Nys from Neerijse. Charles' other companions were captured or fled - as it was held that he had forced them to take up arms they were not pursued. The French brought Charles' head back to Brussels and displayed it in the Grand-Place for three hours.

==Marriages and issue==
On 8 January 1786, at the église des Chartreux, he married Marie Anne Parys, a widow from Saint-Gudule parish, as mentioned by the registers of the Church of St. Catherine. She was a little older than him but very rich, though he was still a minor. His signature on the act of marriage showed good penmanship, unlike those of his wife and his father. They were ill-suited and very soon gained a religious divorce, with Marie Anne dying at Woluwe-Saint-Pierre only a year after the marriage, leading to several court cases on her succession. [ref: Archives de la ville de Bruxelles, catalogue numérique, Carolus Fr. Jacqmin contre Joannes Roebaert pour Maria Anna Parijs, 1787, Procès 3949] [ref: Matheus Parijs et Maria Candijs (héritiers de Maria Anna Parijs, divorcée de Jacqmin) contre Joannes Roobaert, 1787, Procès 5513] [ref: Joannes Roobaert pour la succession de Maria Anna Parijs contre Carolus Franciscus Jacqmin, 1787, Procès 6281] [ref: Joannes Roubaert comme exécuteur testamentaire de Maria Anna Parijs contre Carolus Franciscus Jacqmin, 1787, Procès 7651.]

On 29 September 1787 Charles then married nineteen-year-old Jeanne Josèphe Deinsman or Deinsmans of Brussels at the église de la Chapelle She was then living on rue des Tanneurs and he on rue du Poinçon, with the young couple settling in the marital home. Jeanne had Jeanne Marie in 1788 then Jean Jacques Henri in 1790, both on the rue du Poinçon and both baptised at the église de la Chapelle.

In 1813 Jeanne Marie married Josse Contempré, whilst in 1812 Jean Jacques Henri married Marie Gertrude Van Delen of Antwerp - both marriages were in Brussels. Van Delen died in 1833, by which time her widower was a police officer, and later that year he married Anne Catherine Willems, a widow and businesswoman, again in Brussels. She died on 15 September 1834 in Brussels, which the death record giving her widower as a retired police agent. [ref: Bruxelles, acte de décès n° 2840 of 17 September 1834]

After Charles François's death, his widow Jeanne Josèphe remarried to Nicolas Dachsbek in Brussels in 1805, she then being thirty-six and he twenty-four. She died on 16 September 1846 in Brussels, [ref: Bruxelles, acte de décès n° 3494 of 17 September 1846.] with her death registered by Nicolas Joseph Verhulst and commissioner Philippe Joseph Dachsbeck, both Brussels residents, and by Jean Baptiste Dieudonné Dachsbeck, employed in Brussels.

==Legacy==
He was discussed at a Société d’Archéologie de Bruxelles meeting on 8 July 1890 [ref: Annales de la Société d'archéologie de Bruxelles, vol. 4, 1890, pp. 433 à 436, minutes of the 8 July 1890 meeting.] by Paul Verhaegen (author of La Belgique sous la domination française, 1792-1814. [ref: Paul Verhaegen, La Belgique sous la domination française, 1792-1814., Bruxelles, Goemaere, Paris, Plon, 1922-1924. Vol. I (1792-1795) and Vol. II (1795-1797). In-8°, 666 and 509 pp.]) and Henri Van Havermaet (who was presenting his research on Charles). Verhaegen stated that Charles had:

Van Havermaet replied that - in his research into the violent actions of which the French authorities accused Charles de Loupoigne and his force - "he was able to see for himself how unfounded these accusations appear to be". He admitted Bartholomees' execution but stated that he was "a traitor who had often betrayed the conscripts' hiding places". As for accusations of pillaging, these "were never formulated locally - by contrast the farmers voluntarily gave these young men supplies". For this reason Van Havermaet stated that he "sought to rescue from oblivion the memory of a Brussels man, a man vilified by contemporary French or French-inspired writers".

A few years later, in 1928, Verhagen put up a granite cross in Klein Waver near Loonbeek, near the wood where Charles de Loupoigne was killed, with a Latin inscription that translated as "Not far from here Charles Jacqmin (known as de Loupoigne) and his companions died for the fatherland, 30 July 1799". On 14 July 1940 another memorial cross to him was set up in Loonbeek - it is now against the wall of the Scouts en Gidsen Vlaanderen estate chapel of Le Kluis in Weert-Saint-Georges.

There is a chemin du Cousin Châles and a promenade Charles de Loupoigne in Loupoigne, whilst there is also a rue Charles de Loupoigne in Ottignies-Louvain-la-Neuve. In the Zita op de planken issue of the Dutch comic Bakelandt he is an antagonist of the Bakelandt gang.

data.title: Steffen Klamt
data.text:
Steffen Klamt (born February 4, 1972 in Magdeburg) is a German researcher in computational and systems biology. Since 2009 he is a research group leader at the Max Planck Institute for Dynamics of Complex Technical Systems in Magdeburg.

=Education and professional career=

Steffen Klamt studied Applied Systems Science at the University of Osnabrück and received his Diploma degree in 1998. From 1998-2005 he was a PhD student at the Max Planck Institute for Dynamics of Complex Technical Systems in Magdeburg and received his doctoral degree (Dr.-Ing.) with a thesis on Metabolic Network Modeling at the University of Stuttgart. Since 2009 he heads the research group Analysis and Redesign of Biological Networks [ref: ARB Group, Max-Planck-Institut Für Dynamik Komplexer Technischer Systeme Magdeburg] at the Max Planck Institute in Magdeburg.

=Research=

Steffen Klamt’s research focuses on systems and computational biology, with a particular emphasis on metabolic networks and metabolic engineering. His research group develops algorithms and mathematical modeling approaches to analyze cellular metabolism at the systems level and to enable the rational engineering of microbial cell factories for biotechnological applications. Theoretical investigations are frequently combined with experimental studies, particularly using Escherichia coli and other bacterial model organisms.

===Major research contributions===

* Metabolic network analysis: Klamt and coworkers have developed computational methods for the analysis of metabolic networks based on stoichiometric and constraint-based modeling approaches. This work includes the theory and application of elementary modes for metabolic pathway analysis, [ref: Von der Information zur Funktion, Deutschlandfunk] [ref: Metabolic network structure determines key aspects of functionality and regulation, Nature] [ref: Computation of elementary modes: a unifying framework and the new binary approach, BMC Bioinformatics] [ref: From elementary flux modes to elementary flux vectors: Metabolic pathway analysis with arbitrary linear flux constraints, PLoS Computational Biology] concepts for analyzing the effects of thermodynamic constraints on metabolism, [ref: OptMDFpathway: Identification of metabolic pathways with maximal thermodynamic driving force and its application for analyzing the endogenous CO2 fixation potential of Escherichia coli, PLoS Computational Biology] [ref: Network-wide thermodynamic constraints shape NAD(P)H cofactor specificity of biochemical reactions, Nature Communications] and methods for efficiently constructing metabolic models with enzyme-capacity constraints. [ref: Automatic construction of metabolic models with enzyme constraints, BMC Bioinformatics]

* Integration of constraint-based and kinetic modeling (COBRA-k): Klamt’s group introduced the COBRA-k framework, which integrates constraint-based and kinetic metabolic modeling to predict enzyme abundances, metabolite concentrations, and metabolic fluxes in cellular metabolism. [ref: COBRA-k: A powerful framework bridging constraint-based and kinetic metabolic modeling, Science Advances]

* Minimal cut sets and metabolic engineering: Klamt developed the computational framework of minimal cut sets for metabolic networks. [ref: Minimal cut sets in biochemical reaction networks, Bioinformatics] [ref: Enumeration of smallest intervention strategies in genome-scale metabolic networks, PLoS Computational Biology] [ref: ) An extended and generalized framework for the calculation of metabolic intervention strategies based on minimal cut sets, PLOS Computational Biology] [ref: Minimal cut sets in metabolic networks: from conceptual foundations to applications in metabolic engineering and biomedicine, Briefings in Bioinformatics] The approach can be used to identify combinations of metabolic interventions for redirecting cellular metabolism towards the production of desired compounds. [ref: Growth-coupled overproduction is feasible for almost all metabolites in five major production organisms, Nature Communications] The methodology was applied to guide the metabolic engineering of an E. coli strain for high-yield production of itaconic acid. [ref: Model-Based metabolic engineering enables high yield itaconic acid production by Escherichia coli, Metabolic Engineering]

* Bioprocess design: His research also includes concepts and strategies for the design and optimization of biotechnological production processes. [ref: When do two-stage processes outperform one-stage processes?, Biotechnology Journal] [ref: Design of microbial catalysts for two-stage processes, Nature Reviews Bioengineering] [ref: Model-based optimization of cell-free enzyme cascades exemplified for the production of GDP-fucose, Metabolic Engineering]

* Increasing ATP turnover for metabolic engineering: In 2017, Klamt was awarded an ERC Consolidator Grant, which supported research on metabolic engineering strategies based on increasing cellular ATP turnover to enhance the production of (bio)chemicals. [ref: StrainBooster, StrainBooster project website] [ref: Increasing ATP turnover boosts productivity of 2,3-butanediol synthesis in Escherichia coli, Microbial Cell Factories] [ref: Deciphering the physiological response of Escherichia coli under high ATP demand, Molecular Systems Biology] [ref: Max-Planck-Institut für Dynamik komplexer technischer Systeme Magdeburg, Renewable Carbon] [ref: Praxistest für optimierte Zellfabriken, Bioökonomie.de]

* Cellular signaling and regulatory networks: In earlier work, Klamt developed mathematical modeling approaches for the analysis of cellular signal-transduction and gene-regulatory networks, [ref: A methodology for the structural amd functional analysis of signaling and regulatory networks, BMC Bioinformatics] [ref: The logic of EGFR/ErbB signaling: Theoretical properties and analysis of high-throughput data, PLoS Computational Biology] as well as methods for inferring biological network structures from experimental data. [ref: TRANSWESD: inferring cellular networks with transitive reduction, Bioinformatics] [ref: Detecting and Removing Inconsistencies between Experimental Data and Signaling Network Topologies Using Integer Linear Programming on Interaction Graphs, PLoS Computational Biology]
* Software development: His group developed CellNetAnalyzer [ref: Structural and functional analysis of cellular networks with CellNetAnalyzer, BMC Systems Biology] [ref: CellNetAnalyzer] and CNApy [ref: CNApy: a CellNetAnalyzer GUI in Python for analyzing and designing metabolic networks, Bioinformatics] [ref: CNApy], which are software packages for the modeling and analysis of biological networks, implemented in MATLAB and Python, respectively.

Overall, Klamt's research combines approaches from biology, mathematics, computer science, and engineering to analyze and engineer complex biological networks.

As of 2026, Klamt has authored or co-authored more than 120 peer-reviewed publications [ref: Google Scholar citations, Google Scholar] and is listed in the Research.com database of ranked scientists in the field "Engineering and Technology". [ref: Best Scientists - Engineering and Technology Steffen Klamt, Research.com]

data.title: ID) Model
data.text:
----

== Introduction ==
The Four Component Instructional Design (4C/ID) Model is an instructional design framework created to help students learn difficult cognitive skills and professional competencies. Jeroen J. G. van Merriënboer, Otto Jelsma, and Fred Paas established the concept in 1992 and it offers a systematic to constructing or building educational programs that integrate information and skills, inside authentic learning experiences.

Neek et al. (2025) states that "The four-component instructional design (4C/ID) model is designed to support complex learning by the facilitation of the transfer of theoretical knowledge into practice [ref: Implementing the four-component instructional design model in professional development programs: a systematic review with a focus on teachers, Frontiers in Education]." The 4C/ID paradigm provides a theoretical foundation for developing learning environments and training programs. The model's four components closely match the qualitative characteristics of good and effective training programs. As such, it is believed that 4C/ID can be extremely imperative in the development of high quality teacher training programs, especially for in-service training, when professionals already have both an educational background and personal experience with their specialized real-world activities.

Unlike instructional approaches that focus on isolated objectives or specific abilities, the 4C/ID Model prioritizes whole task learning and the continual development of competence. It is made up of four interconnected components:

# learning tasks
# supportive information
# procedural knowledge
# part task practice. [ref: Blueprints for complex learning: The 4C/ID-model, Educational Technology Research and Development](van Merriënboer et al. (2002)

It is noteworthy, that this model has been applied in educational and professional training contexts where learners must integrate multiple skills, solve problems, and transfer their learning to uncommon or unfamiliar situations. Its principals are backed by research on cognitive load, acquisition of skills and the development of expertise with special emphasis on promoting effective learning and the transfer of complex cognitive skills [ref: Training for reflective expertise: A four-component instructional design model for complex cognitive skills, Educational Technology Research and Development] (van Merriënboer et al., 1992, 2002).

A meta analysis by Costa et al. (2022) reported positive effects on learning performance [ref: Four-component instructional design (4C/ID) model: a meta-analysis on use and effect, Learning Environments Research], while a systematic review by Qi et al. (2026) identified promising outcomes relating to skill development and knowledge transfer [ref: The Four-Component Instructional Design (4C/ID) Model in Higher Education: A Systematic Literature Review, Journal of University Teaching and Learning Practice], although limitations in the available research remain. Together, these findings articulate the model's relevance to instructional environments requiring learners to integrate and apply complex skills.

== Origins and Development of the 4C/ID Model ==
The Four Component Instructional Design Model emerged in the late 1980s as a response to the constraints of instructional approaches that focused on teaching skills separately. Jeroen J. G. van Merriënboer, Otto Jelsma, and Fred Paas created a framework to help learners build complex cognitive skills that integrate knowledge, procedures and decision making abilities. van Merriënboer et al. published "Training for Reflective Expertise: A Four Component Instructional Design Paradigm for Complex Cognitive Skills [ref: Training Complex Cognitive Skills: A Four-Component Instructional Design Model for Technical Training, Educational Technology] in 1992, which formally established the paradigm.

== Theoretical Foundations of the 4C/ID Model ==

* Cognitive Load Theory

The 4C/ID Model is closely related to cognitive load theory, which investigates how limitations in working memory affect learning. Complex tasks frequently need learners to comprehend many interacting elements at the same time, which might strain their cognitive resources. The model addresses this difficulty by carefully structing learning activities, providing appropriate instructional guidance, and gradually reducing support as learners gain experience (Sweller et al., 2019) [ref: Cognitive Architecture and Instructional Design: 20 Years Later, Educational Psychology Review]

* Whole Task Learning

Whole task learning is a key component of the 4C/ID Model, emphasizing the development of integrated competencies rather than teaching individual skills separately. Learners participate in authentic tasks that simulate real world professional scenarios, allowing them to synchronize their knowledge, abilities and attitudes. Instruction proceeds from simple activities to more complicated scenarios, with help gradually reduced as students gain independence (Frerejean et al., 2019) [ref: Ten steps to 4C/ID: training differentiation skills in a professional development program for teachers, Instructional Science]

* Routine and Non-Routine Skills

The model also differentiates between recurring and non-recurring aspects of performance. Recurrent abilities are procedures that may be automated with repeated practice, but non-recurrent skills require reasoning, problem solving, and adaptation to new contexts. The 4C/ID paradigm combines learning activities with supportive information, procedural guidance and concentrated practice opportunities. (van Merriënboer & Kirschner, 2018)

== The Four Components of the 4C/ID Model ==
The Four Component Instructional Design Model is made up of four interconnected components that facilitate the acquisition of complex skills. These components integrate authentic learning experiences with instructional guidance and targeted practice, allowing students to gain both conceptual comprehension and practical competence [ref: Vocational Training in Virtual Reality: A Case Study Using the 4C/ID Model, Multimodal Technologies and Interaction], as seen in Frerejean et al. (2019) and Mulders (2022)

Learning Tasks

The Model's foundation is built around learning tasks. They include authentic activities such as projects, simulations, and case studies which encourage students to integrate their knowledge, abilities, skills and attitudes. According to Mulders (2022), tasks progress from simpler to more complicated levels, with instructional help gradually decreasing as students develop proficiency. This strategy promotes independent performance and the application of knowledge in real world situations. (Frerejean et al., 2021)

Supportive Information

This presents the conceptual understanding and the cognitive methods required to complete the non-routine components of intricate tasks. It essentially enables learners to understand basic ideas, analyze situations and make informed judgments. Drugova et al. (2023) asserts that this information can be conveyed through readings, explanations, examples or other learning tools, helping students to relate new knowledge to prior knowledge. [ref: Learning Design Using the Four-Component Instructional Design Model (4C/ID) in Higher Education: Review of Studies, RUDN Journal of Psychology and Pedagogics]

Procedural Information

Procedural information offers instant assistance for routine components of task execution. Instructions, prompts and corrective feedback are sent, when learners need them, which makes it commonly referred to as "just in time" information. Mulders (2022) and Frerejean et al. (2019) also states that as learners gain competence, this coaching is gradually eliminated to encourage independent performance.

Part-Task Practice

This involves repeated exercises meant to enhance specific regular abilities so that they can be executed with higher precision and automaticity. Unlike whole learning tasks, which necessitate the integration of several competencies, part task practice essentially focuses on distinct procedures that require more repetition. It enhances rather than replaces actual learning experiences. (Frerejean et al., 2021)

== Research and Applications of the 4C/ID Model ==
The Four Component Instructional Design Model has been researched for its usefulness in higher education, professional developments and vocational training. A meta analysis conducted by Costa et al. (2022) found a favorable overall effect on learning performance (d=0.79), implying that instructional programs built using the model can aid in the acquisition of knowledge and complicated abilities. The researchers also found educational level as an important determinant with notably positive results in higher education.

In teacher professional development, Neck et al. (2025) conducted a systematic review of 55 papers on the implementation of the 4C/ID. In a quantitative sub analysis, they discovered applications across several professional training contexts and found a moderate beneficial influence on learning outcomes (g=0.76). However, the researchers observed that many studies offered little information about how the model's components were applied, limiting prospects for replication and evaluation.

The model has also been used in technologically supported vocational education. Mulders (2022) investigated its application in creating a virtual reality training program that was used for automobile painting. The study showed how authentic learning activities, instructional guidance and targeted practice may be combined in a simulated professional setting. Although the findings validated the model's utility as a design framework, the study focused on instructional development rather than determining changes in learner accomplishment.

Collectively, these students indicate that 4C/ID provides a structured method to building complex professional competencies in a variety of educational settings. Nonetheless, discrepancies in research methodology and implementation approaches suggest that further study is needed to determine its effectiveness across varied learner demographics and instructional situations.

== Strengths and Limitations of the 4C/ID Model ==
Strengths

One of the 4C/ID Model's main merits is its emphasis on real, whole task learning, which encourages students to integrate knowledge and abilities rather than acquire them separately. This method encourages the development of skills that are practical in real-world circumstances. In an experimental investigation of university physics students, Guo et al. (2024) discovered that instruction based on the 4C/ID Model provided superior results in knowledge acquisition and learning transfer than standard teaching approaches [ref: EMPIRICAL RESEARCH ON INTEGRATIVE LEARNING BASED ON 4C/ID MODEL, Physics and Engineering].

== References ==

data.title: Moyo Ogunseinde
data.text:
Moyo Ogunseinde is a Nigerian architect, real estate developer, designer, and hospitality entrepreneur. She is the founder and Group Chief Executive Officer of Club Concierge Africa, a travel and hospitality group whose brands include Club Concierge International, GoTravelCC, GoPartnerCC and MyTravelCC.

Trained at University College London, Moyo Ogunseinde designed the Radisson Blu Anchorage Hotel in Lagos and sits on the board of its owner, Anchorage Leisures. Earlier in her career, the architect was an executive director of Uraga Real Estate, a member of the Honeywell Group, where she led the development of the Upbeat Recreation Centre, described as West Africa's first trampoline park.

Moyo has chaired the Lagos State Gymnastics Association since 2018.

== Early life and education ==
Moyo Ogunseinde is from Ibadan, Nigeria. She has cited the city's markets, colours and cultural life as an influence on her later design work. She trained as an architect at University College London and later undertook executive education at Harvard Business School. She is a chartered architect.

== Career ==

=== Architecture and real estate ===
Moyo Ogunseinde began her career in architecture before moving into real estate development in Nigeria. She designed the Radisson Blu Anchorage Hotel on Victoria Island, Lagos, which opened in 2011, and later oversaw the renovation of its rooms and business lounge.

Moyo became an executive director of Uraga Real Estate Limited, a subsidiary of the Honeywell Group, contributing to design, land acquisition and planning.

=== Upbeat Recreation Centre ===
As an executive director of Uraga Real Estate, Moyo Ogunseinde led the development of the Upbeat Recreation Centre, a multi-purpose leisure facility on Admiralty Road, Lekki, which opened in December 2017 and was reported in the Nigerian media as West Africa's first trampoline park. The project was conceived during Nigeria's 2016 recession as a diversification into recreational real estate, aimed at the country's young population.

The centre set up a gymnastics club in February 2018 and held its first trampoline gymnastics competition in October 2018. In 2024 it hosted a fun day for underprivileged children in Lekki.

=== Aga Culture ===
In 2017 Moyo Ogunseinde founded Aga Culture (originally Àga Concept), an African lifestyle and design brand based in Lagos, and serves as its creative director. The name derives from the Yoruba word àga, meaning a chair or functional object. The brand produces clothing, furniture and homeware that combine Yoruba and wider African traditions with a contemporary, minimalist aesthetic, and emphasises slow fashion and ethically sourced materials such as Adire cotton and linen. Its furniture includes the Oko chair, drawn from traditional farming tools, and the Egungun accessories collection, inspired by Egungun masquerades; in 2020 the American trade magazine Hospitality Design named Moyo Ogunseinde one of six rising product designers. The brand's Mmanwu chair featured in Cultured magazine's 2021 survey of the Lagos design scene. Its work has also included the AADA clothing collection and participation in design exhibitions.

=== Hospitality ===
Moyo Ogunseinde has served as executive director of Anchorage Leisures Limited, owner of the Radisson Blu Anchorage Hotel, and sits on its board. She is also a board member of the Honeywell Group and an advisory board member of Wavecrest College of Hospitality, Lagos. In a 2022 interview, she argued that Nigeria could develop world-class tourism by investing in local infrastructure and emphasized local content in the hotel's operations, art and food sourcing.

In November 2025, she accepted the Best Corporate Hotel award at the World Luxury Awards in Barcelona on behalf of the Radisson Blu Anchorage, where she was described as a board member and key owner of the property. In 2025 she was included in a Nigerian trade listing of "Top 100 Women in Hospitality".

=== Club Concierge Africa ===

Moyo Ogunseinde founded Club Concierge Africa (CCA) during the COVID-19 pandemic, building a travel, hospitality and lifestyle group intended to serve African travellers. The group offers travel membership, travel management, hospitality partnerships and concierge services.

Its brands are:
* Club Concierge International (CCI), a travel club offering vacation-ownership membership for leisure travellers and, through Club Concierge for Business, corporate accommodation membership;
* GoTravelCC, a travel-management company offering flights, hotels and related travel services;
* MyTravelCC, a flights-first travel booking company for individuals;
* GoPartnerCC, the group's partnership brand;
* Concierge Resort, which manages resort destinations; and
* CSolute, a business-to-business travel affiliate arm.

As Group CEO, Moyo Ogunseinde oversees operations across several African and international markets.

In September 2026, she spoke on a panel on cross-border payments at the 22nd Akwaaba African Travel Market in Lagos, calling for closer cooperation between regulators, payment providers and tourism operators to reduce the cost of travel within Africa.

== Sports administration ==
On 3 December 2018 Moyo Ogunseinde was inaugurated as chair of the Lagos State Gymnastics Association by Kweku Tandoh, executive chairman of the Lagos State Sports Commission. Her first duty was supporting the Lagos team at the 19th National Sports Festival in Abuja, where it won two gold and two bronze medals.

In April 2019, the association partnered with the International Gymnastics Federation, and she unveiled a four-year development plan for the sport in Lagos and called for gymnastics to be added to school curricula. She has also served on the board of the Lagos State Sports Trust Fund. In 2021, she was named among nominees for induction into the African Sports Tourism Hall of Fame.

Moyo Ogunseinde is the founder of WANAMKE, a non-governmental organisation focused on the development of women in sport.

== Other activities ==
Moyo Ogunseinde has been associated with Artclip Africa, a gallery promoting Nigerian contemporary art in partnership with the Radisson Blu Anchorage Hotel. In August 2026, she was a speaker at The Borderless Experience, a travel and hospitality event held in Lagos and organised by Condia.

== Recognition ==
According to BusinessDay, Moyo Ogunseinde has received the Nigerian Institute of Architects' Best Qualified Registered Architect award and the Interior Design Excellence Award for Best Hospitality Designer.

data.title: Bareeze Ahmad
data.text:
----

Writer | FinTech Student | Theatre Enthusiast | Digital Content Creator

Lahore, Pakistan

=== Introduction ===
Bareeze Ahmad (born 14 May 2006) is a Pakistani writer, student, and creative professional based in Lahore. She is pursuing a degree in Financial Technology (FinTech) at FAST-NUCES, where she combines technical and business studies with a sustained commitment to literature, theatre, and visual communication. She is a published author whose poetry, reflective prose, and short fiction have appeared in several books and anthologies, including collections published in India, in which she was the only Pakistani contributor.

=== Education ===
Ahmad completed her early schooling at Convent School and her intermediate education at Kinnaird College, Lahore. She is currently studying FinTech at FAST-NUCES, a field that applies technology to financial services, digital payments, and financial systems.

=== Literary Work ===
Ahmad writes poetry, short fiction, reflective prose, and cultural and theatre reviews. Her work explores identity, silence, memory, emotional experience, and the gap between outward appearance and private thought.

Her writing has been included in several anthologies, some of them published in India. Her first anthology featured one of her short stories, and she has since contributed to further collections. Her titles listed by Literacy Gardeners include: [ref: The Invisible Me]

* The Invisible Me
* The Fracture of Time

She has also written the poetry and reflective prose pieces The Cage I Call Mine and The Things We Bury Alive, which deal with concealed identity, suppressed memory, and unspoken words. She shares her writing journey, including novel writing, creative essays, and reviews, through her writer platform on Instagram (@[user]). [ref: Instagram, www.instagram.com]

=== Theatre and Performing Arts ===
Ahmad is an active participant in Pakistan’s theatre scene and has worked with Ajoka Theatre, an organization known for socially engaged performance in Urdu and Punjabi. She is also known for her cultural and theatre reviews, including a widely shared review of Ajoka’s production Jhalley Kithay Jave at PILAC, which examined women’s emotional struggles and domestic compliance. [ref: Instagram, www.instagram.com]

Her theatre involvement includes:

* Taking part in dramatic readings. In September 2026 she portrayed Ruttie Jinnah in a dramatic reading about Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
* Social media management, audition coordination, and promotional material for Ajoka activities and a film project.
* Developing mood boards and creative plans for theatrical projects.
* Writing reviews of stage productions.

=== Leadership and Student Activities ===
At FAST-NUCES, Ahmad has been involved in student societies and events connected with SOFTEC and FINTEC. She has held deputy-head and head-level leadership roles, coordinated teams, organized events, and worked on promotional and communications material. She has served as a director of graphics in a university society, drawing on her skills in design and visual storytelling.

Her other activities include:

* Debating and hosting debates.
* Event organization and student society management.
* Community-oriented initiatives, including blood donation drives.

=== Professional Experience ===
People and Communications Intern, Daftarkhwan (six weeks)

Ahmad interned at Daftarkhwan, a Pakistani coworking and workspace company. Her work included administrative coordination, spreadsheet management, data organization, budget-related tasks, purchase-order records, internal communications, and operational reporting. The role gave her practical experience in business administration and data management.

=== Digital Content Creation ===
Ahmad is an emerging digital content creator with interests in social media, branding, and visual storytelling. She develops promotional content, product-focused video concepts, and campaign ideas, with a focus on beauty and skincare. She has also received a public-relations package connected to L’Oréal’s Eye Star campaign.

=== Skills and Interests ===

* Creative writing: poetry, short fiction, reflective prose, reviews
* Theatre, dramatic reading, and cultural storytelling
* Public speaking, debating, and hosting
* Graphic design, mood boards, and branding
* Social media and content creation
* Event management and team leadership
* Spreadsheet management and data organization
* Financial technology and digital financial systems

=== Summary ===
Ahmad brings together technical study, creative writing, performing arts, and student leadership. Her published work, theatre involvement, leadership roles, and professional experience reflect a person who works comfortably across analytical and creative fields.

data.title: Tapas Chakraborty
data.text:
Tapas Chakraborty is an Indian computer scientist, researcher, and deep-tech entrepreneur. [ref: Can AI fix India's land record problem? This startup believes so, The Economic Times] He is the founder of Vixplor and its automated document intelligence platform, DocXplor. [ref: DocXplor extracts medical record, speeds up process in hospitals, insurance cos, The Hindu BusinessLine] His career spans a decade in the multinational software industry, peer-reviewed computational research in bioinformatics, and the deployment of artificial intelligence tools for public sector governance and healthcare infrastructure.

== Early life and education ==
Chakraborty completed his primary and secondary schooling at the historic Hindu School, Kolkata in Kolkata. He demonstrated early academic distinction under the West Bengal state boards, securing the 34th state rank in the Madhyamik examinations in 2001, and subsequently the 63rd state rank in the Higher Secondary examinations in 2003. He was named a recipient of the National Scholarship for his performances in both board tiers. Additionally, during his Higher Secondary board exam, he was awarded a Gold Medal from the Government of West Bengal for attaining a perfect score (200 out of 200) in mathematics.

He then attended Jadavpur University, graduating with a Bachelor of Engineering (BE) degree in 2007. Following a decade in corporate technology enterprises, Chakraborty returned to academia at Jadavpur University to pursue advanced computational research.

He completed his Master of Engineering (ME) degree in 2019. His master's research specialized in audio signal processing using deep learning frameworks, culminating in his thesis titled "Speaker identification on multimodal environment using deep learning" (2019). In 2026, he was awarded a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Computer Science from Jadavpur University. His doctoral work specialized in structural bioinformatics and computational biology. His dissertation, titled "Computational studies on protein protein interaction" (2026), proposed a series of deep neural network architectures introducing innovative approaches for predicting protein-protein interactions (PPI), protein self-interactions, and protein residue-residue proximity frameworks.

== Career ==
=== Enterprise technology (2007–2017) ===
After earning his engineering degree, Chakraborty spent ten years working within the enterprise software and technology consulting sectors. During this period, he held corporate engineering roles at global technology consulting firms, including IBM and PwC (PricewaterhouseCoopers), where he designed enterprise application architectures and automated software data flows.

While at IBM, Chakraborty was assigned to highly specialized corporate optimization and data analytics projects:
* Severn Trent Water (Predictive Analytics): He contributed to the data analytics and predictive framework infrastructure for the UK-based water utility company Severn Trent. His work centered on building analytical modules to identify geographical "hot spots" in water distribution networks to isolate areas requiring immediate infrastructural intervention or targeted pipeline replacements.
* Philip Morris International (Research Infrastructure): He was integrated into the specialized technological research and development infrastructure team for Philip Morris International (PMI), assisting in building backend systems mapping data flows for their IQOS electronic nicotine delivery research programs.

=== Entrepreneurship and public sector utility (2017–present) ===
In 2017, Chakraborty left the multinational technology sector to establish his deep-tech startup, Vixplor, focusing on intelligent automation and character recognition. Under Vixplor, he developed **DocXplor**, an artificial intelligence platform utilizing specialized Deep Learning models and Large Language Models (LLMs) to read, interpret, and digitize highly variable printed and handwritten text records without requiring static templates.

The platform has been deployed in several public public infrastructure and private enterprise use cases:
* Land Records Digitization: The Finance Department of the Government of West Bengal contracted the platform to process, extract, and digitize legacy handwritten municipal registries and land deed repositories, algorithmically stitching together "chain deeds" to map real estate ownership lineage across multiple decades.
* Healthcare and Insurance Automation: The platform is used by national healthcare facilities and over a dozen insurance providers to instantly extract structured digital data from handwritten medical prescriptions and clinical invoices, reducing manual data entry delays and accelerating claim pre-authorizations.

In 2026, Chakraborty presented his document intelligence platform on zee TV Zee 24 Ghanta's startup program, Tigers Pitch (Season 1), securing institutional validation and ecosystem funding.. [ref: Tigers Pitch Season 1, Zee 24 Ghanta] He has also been invited as a domain specialist on state television networks, including Doordarshan DD Bangla's flagship economic and entrepreneurship programs, to speak on sustainable scaling and AI integration bottlenecks within emerging industrial corridors. [ref: Pratyasha: 2025-er Safalya 2026-er Pratashya, DD Bangla] and [ref: BARTAMAN ARTHONOITIK ABOSTHA EBONG START-UP BUSINESS, DD Bangla]

=== Ecosystem leadership ===
Chakraborty acts as an industry ecosystem advocate in Eastern India. He is an elected member of the Confederation of Indian Industry Eastern Regional Council and serves on the CII Startup Subcommittee. In this administrative capacity, he acts alongside corporate executives and state policy advisors to frame systemic recommendations aimed at scaling capital access and infrastructure development for early-stage deep-tech companies throughout the region.

== Selected publications ==
Chakraborty's computational research has been featured in major international journals, covering neural network applications and bioinformatics:
* Chakraborty, T., et al. "DensePPI-2: a bio-inspired update for sequence-based PPI prediction leveraging mutation rates." Briefings in Bioinformatics, Oxford University Press. [ref: DensePPI-2: a bio-inspired update for sequence-based PPI prediction leveraging mutation rates, Briefings in Bioinformatics]
* Chakraborty, T. "DensePPI: A Novel Image-Based Deep Learning Method for Prediction of Protein–Protein Interactions" IEEE Xplore / IEEE Journals. [ref: DensePPI: A Novel Image-Based Deep Learning Method for Prediction of Protein–Protein Interactions, IEEE Xplore]
* Chakraborty, T. "MAuD: a multivariate audio database of samples collected from benchmark conferencing platforms." Multimedia Tools and Applications, Springer. [ref: MAuD: a multivariate audio database of samples collected from benchmark conferencing platforms, Multimedia Tools and Applications]
* Chakraborty, T. "Closed-set speaker identification using VQ and GMM based models." International Journal of Speech Technology, Springer. [ref: Closed-set speaker identification using VQ and GMM based models, International Journal of Speech Technology]

== Works ==
Outside of his technology career and computer science research, Chakraborty is an essayist whose personal travel philosophies focus on cross-cultural interactions and urban exploration.
* Chakraborty, Tapas. Itiuti Europe (ইতিউতি ইউরোপ). Kolkata: Boighar, 2018.
:: Note: A travel memoir documenting European cities, geographic exploration, and sociolinguistic interactions with foreign cultures. The preface of the memoir was authored by the prominent Bengali novelist and litterateur Sanjib Chattopadhyay.

= Rebel Reid =

Rebel Reid is a Māori musician, guitarist, songwriter and producer from Aotearoa New Zealand. She is known for her work with the South Auckland band Valkyrie and her solo music, including the 2023 EP Hiria. Her music draws on pop rock, blues, soul, folk and country, while her solo work incorporates te reo Māori and English. [ref: Silke Hartung, “Q & A: Catch Up With Valkyrie’s Rebel Reid”. NZ Musician.] [ref: Conor Lochrie, “On ‘Hiria’, Rebel Reid Beautifully Memorialises Her Beloved Mum”. Rolling Stone Australia/New Zealand, 9 August 2023.]

== Early life ==
Rebel Reid was born on 4 June 1987 in Auckland, New Zealand, and grew up in Papatoetoe, South Auckland, with her mother, Leia Reid, who raised her as a solo parent. She attended Papatoetoe High School.

Her mother’s influence continued to shape Reid’s music throughout her career. In 2023, she released the solo EP Hiria in memory of her late mother. The project explores love, loss and remembrance, with the song “Leia” serving as a personal musical tribute to the woman who helped shape her life.

== Career ==

=== Valkyrie ===
Reid is the guitarist and songwriter for Valkyrie, a New Zealand band associated with South Auckland. The group developed a sound combining pop rock and alternative influences with a theatrical performance style. [ref: Sam Carswell, “Vallkyrie: Stirring the Pot”. NZ Musician.]

Reid and vocalist Omer Gilroy had known each other since childhood and later reconnected to pursue music together. Valkyrie subsequently developed its live performance profile and released its debut album, Joyride, in November 2022. [ref: “Aotearoa’s Valkyrie release smash debut album JOYRIDE”. Music Managers Forum Aotearoa, November 2022.]

In October 2023, Reid was included in the lineup for Aotearoa House at SXSW Sydney, a showcase featuring 30 New Zealand artists and supported by Creative New Zealand, Te Māngai Pāho and the New Zealand Music Commission. [ref: Levi Hartnett, “Aotearoa House to Bring 30 Kiwi Artists to SXSW Sydney”. Rolling Stone Australia/New Zealand, 3 October 2023.]

=== Solo career and Hiria ===
In July 2023, Reid released her debut solo EP, Hiria, coinciding with Matariki. The three-track project was dedicated to her late mother and features the songs “Leia”, “Cry Cry Cry” and “Dancing in the Stars”. [ref: “Rebel Reid shines on debut solo EP, ‘Hiria’, in memory of her beloved mum”. Muzic.NZ, 14 July 2023.]

In an interview with Rolling Stone Australia/New Zealand, Reid discussed her mother’s influence on her musical tastes and the personal significance of making Hiria. She described the EP as a gift to her mother and to her people and culture, connecting the release to Matariki and her experience of grief.

The EP blends English and te reo Māori with musical influences including blues, country, folk, pop and rock. Reid also discussed the influence of Witi Ihimaera’s book Navigating the Stars on the songwriting process.

The release received coverage from Rolling Stone Australia/New Zealand, Te Ao Māori News and Muzic.NZ. [ref: Mārena Mane, “Māori musician Rebel Reid releases new EP, an ode to her late mother”. Te Ao Māori News, July 2023.]

=== PROMISELAND ===
Reid is developing a music project titled PROMISELAND, drawing on blues and soul influences. In an August 2026 review of a Play It Strange fundraising concert at Auckland’s Tuning Fork, music journalist Paul Marshall described the blues and soul qualities of Reid’s voice and reported that she performed a song titled “Promised Land”. The review also quoted Reid expressing her ambition to record an album at Sun Records in Memphis, Tennessee. [ref: Paul Marshall, “Play It Strange”. Write Said Paul, 26 August 2026.]

The project’s wider concept, including its planned bilingual songwriting and cinematic elements, has not yet been independently documented in the sources identified for this article.

== Musical style and influences ==
Reid’s musical influences include blues, soul, country, folk, pop and rock. In coverage of Hiria, she discussed growing up listening to artists including Elvis Presley, David Bowie, Billy Idol, Pink Floyd, Queen and Prince. She also cited film composer Hans Zimmer among the music she listened to while recording the EP.

Her work with Valkyrie combines rock and pop influences with theatrical performance, while her solo work explores more personal themes through bilingual songwriting and acoustic arrangements.

data.title: BillingPlatform
data.text:
----

BillingPlatform is an enterprise software company headquartered in Englewood, Colorado, that provides billing and revenue management software. [ref: BillingPlatform raises capital, names new CEO] Its platform enables businesses to automate billing, invoicing, and revenue recognition workflows across pricing models that include subscriptions, usage-based billing, and hybrid arrangements, including AI monetization models.

The company was founded in 2012 by Leonid Solomonik and Nathan Shinn and operated as a self-funded startup before raising external funding in 2017. [ref: BillingPlatform raises capital, names new CEO] As of January 2024, it has raised a total of $104 million from Columbia Capital and FTV Capital. [ref: BillingPlatform lands $90m growth equity investment from FTV Capital]

==History and Founding==

BillingPlatform was founded in 2012 by Leonid Solomonik and Nathan Shinn in Englewood, Colorado. Shinn serves as chief strategy officer and has more than 20 years of experience in high-volume enterprise information systems; Solomonik serves as chief technology officer, with more than 20 years of software industry experience, including extensive experience in high-capacity billing information systems. [ref: Englewood-based BillingPlatform raises $18M Series A, announces new CEO]

The company grew organically for several years before seeking external funding, expanding its client base primarily through direct sales and word-of-mouth referrals.

In January 2026, Chris Bishop was named Chief Executive Officer, with Dennis Wall remaining on the company's board of directors. [ref: Chris Bishiop Named CEO of BillingPlatform]

==Funding==

In August 2017, BillingPlatform announced a $4 million Series A round led by Columbia Capital and Dennis Wall was named CEO. [ref: Englewood-based BillingPlatform raises $18M Series A, announces new CEO] Wall had previously co-founded Cloud Sherpas, a cloud advisory firm acquired by Accenture in 2015. [ref: Englewood-based BillingPlatform raises $18M Series A, announces new CEO]

In December 2019, BillingPlatform raised a $10 million Series B round from Columbia Capital. [ref: BillingPlatform Raises $10M in Series B Funding]
BillingPlatform announced a $90 million growth equity investment from FTV Capital, in January 2024. [ref: BillingPlatform lands $90m growth equity investment from FTV Capital] FTV Capital joined Columbia Capital as a minority institutional investor, and FTV Capital partners Kyle Griswold and Richard Liu joined the company's board of directors. [ref: BillingPlatform raises $90M growth round from FTV]

==Platform==
BillingPlatform's cloud-based software is built on a metadata-driven architecture that allows billing configurations to be defined through settings rather than custom code. It supports functions related to the order-to-cash process, including product catalog management, order intake, billing, invoicing, revenue recognition, payment processing, and collections.

The software supports several billing models, including one-time charges, subscriptions, usage-based pricing, and tiered pricing, as well as combinations of these models. It integrates with third-party payment gateways and enterprise systems such as ERP and CRM platforms, and includes functionality for ingesting usage data for consumption-based billing. [ref: BillingPlatform Enables Deployment of Pricing Models Designed for AI Services]

==Customers==
Notable customers include Carrier, DIRECTV, Instacart, J.P. Morgan and Panera. [ref: Auctane streamlines billing with expanded BillingPlatform use]

In November 2023, BillingPlatform announced a partnership with J.P. Morgan Payments to support billing needs across J.P. Morgan's Treasury Services and Trade Finance businesses, as part of J.P. Morgan's broader billing and pricing transformation. [ref: J.P. Morgan Payments integrates with BillingPlatform, IBS Intelligence]

data.title: Apoorva Gokhale
data.text:
----

Apoorva Gokhale (born 5 December 1973) is an Indian Hindustani classical vocalist associated with the Gwalior gharana. She was born into a family of traditional musicians and is the granddaughter of vocalist Gajananrao Joshi and the great granddaughter of musician Antubua Joshi, who served as a court musician in the erstwhile state of Aundh. [ref: ]

== Early life and training ==
Gokhale began learning Hindustani classical music at the age of five under the guidance of her grandfather, Gajananrao Joshi. She later received training from her uncle, Madhukar Joshi. She also received guidance from her father, Manohar Joshi, her aunt Sucheta Bidkar, and vocalist Ulhas Kashalkar. [ref: A Khayal Recital by Apoorva Gokhale, NCPA]

She later received guidance from Pt. Shankar Abhyankar, Manik Bhide, Ashwini Bhide-Deshpande, Pt. Yashwant Mahale and Pt. Arun Kashalkar. [ref: Apoorva Gokhale & Pallavi Joshi Official Website, www.apoorvapallavi.com]

== Musical style ==
Gokhale's approach to khayal singing incorporates lyrical and evocative expression while maintaining the traditional structure of the form. Her performances emphasise the development of the raga through alaap and improvisation, along with attention to swara and laya (rhythm). [ref: Ghan Garaje: Monsoon Melodies, NCPA]

She has been described as presenting khayal through a systematic development of the raga, combining melodic expression with rhythmic structure. [ref: Ghan Garaje: Monsoon Melodies, NCPA]

== Awards and recognition ==

* Government of India fellowship in Indian music [ref: ]
* Surmani title from Sur Singar Sansad, Mumbai
* Vidyasagar Award from Music Forum, Mumbai
* Acharya S. N. Ratanjankar and Pt. K. G. Ginde Award and Scholarship
* Pandit Ramkrishnabuwa Vaze Yuva Puraskar
* Pandit Basavraj Rajguru Yuva Puraskar (2014)
* Sangeet Bhushan, Pandit Ram Marathe Yuva Puraskar [ref: A Voice That Resonates Beyond Thane – Apoorva Gokhale]

data.title: Claudio Kaya
data.text:
Claudio Kaya is a Greek-Albanian actor, writer, director, and contemporary dancer. He works across feature films, television, and theater. He is best known for his breakthrough leading film role as Argiris in the 2024 psychological mystery thriller film Buzzheart, directed by Dennis Iliadis.

== Early life and education ==
Kaya was born in Albania and relocated to Greece with his family at the age of four, growing up in Athens. He pursued a professional career in the performing arts, earning a Bachelor of Arts degree in Acting and Performance. During his academic studies, he completed intensive on-camera performance training under the mentorship of the prominent Greek television and film director Manousos Manousakis.

== Career ==
=== Film and Television ===
In 2024, Kaya made his feature film debut starring as Argiris, the central protagonist in the psychological thriller Buzzheart (original Greek title: Akouo tin Kardia sou). Directed by Hollywood genre filmmaker Dennis Iliadis, the film premiered in the Official Competition at the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival. Kaya's performance as an introverted young man subjected to violent parental psychological screenings received favorable reviews from Greek cinematic publications such as Flix.gr.

Following his cinematic breakthrough, Kaya transitioned into television, securing guest roles on Greek National Television (ERT). He appeared as Vasilis Stefanidis in the comedy-drama series Mama sta Kryfa (Hidden Mother).

=== Theater and Other Work ===
Active within the independent Athens theater circuit, Kaya has expanded his work into writing and directing. He wrote and directed the original stage play Horny Fans, produced by Independent Artists in Athens. In addition to his acting career, Kaya is trained in contemporary dance and physical theater, and regularly participates in screenwriting workshops for stage and cinema.

data.title: EnglishCentral
data.text:
EnglishCentral is a provider of video-based English language learning tools, founded in 2009 by Alan Schwartz and based in Burlington, Massachusetts. The platform uses automated speech recognition with one-on-one live tutoring options to help non-native speakers practice speaking and listening.

== History ==
The company started operations in 2009 with funding from Google Ventures. It later expanded to schools and universities, mainly across East Asia and Europe, by partnering with educational institutions.

== Platform and Technology ==
The system offers video lessons paired with voice analysis tools. When users speak into the system, the speech recognition engine compares their pronunciation and fluency against target models to deliver feedback. Additionally, users can participate in live video sessions with tutors for direct conversational practice.

== Reception and Academic Evaluation ==
Scholars in computer-assisted language learning have studied the platform. A 2021 review by G. Strong in Language Learning & Technology noted that while the video and voice recognition setup helps practice speaking and listening, it has limited capacity for open conversational practice. Other journal studies have looked at its use in university settings regarding student engagement and pronunciation practice.

data.title: Rethink Space
data.text:
Rethink Space (stylized up all caps) is an international space technology and infrastructure venture founded by German scientist and entrepreneur Karl Johannes Lierfeld. The organization develops architectural, neuro-technological, and robotic frameworks for the New Space Economy, focusing on long-term human presence in cis-lunar space and sustainable lunar habitats.

== History and Overview ==
Rethink Space was established as an interdisciplinary research and development project bridging artificial intelligence, brain-computer interfaces (BCI), robotics, and space architecture. Operating as Rethink Space Inc. (Delaware C-Corporation / foundation pending) with research activities in Germany, the venture collaborates with international academic and industrial partners.

The project addresses the key operational challenges of permanent human settlement on the Moon and deep-space environments. Rather than relying solely on terrestrial supply lines, Rethink Space focuses on in-situ resource utilization (ISRU), autonomous swarm robotics, and modular habitats.

== Research Areas ==

=== Lunar Habitat Design & Architecture ===
Rethink Space designs modular lunar habitats engineered to withstand extreme environmental hazards, including solar radiation, micro-meteorite impacts, and severe thermal fluctuations. The architectural concepts incorporate human-centered cognitive principles to mitigate psychological and physiological stressors during long-duration lunar missions.

=== Brain-Computer Interfaces & Neuro-AI ===
Drawing on founder Johannes Lierfeld's research in neurotechnology and artificial intelligence, Rethink Space explores brain–computer interface (BCI) applications in extreme environments. Focus areas include real-time neuro-monitoring of astronaut cognitive states and direct BCI systems for the teleoperation of surface robotics.

=== Swarm Robotics & ISRU ===
The project develops autonomous swarm robotics architectures designed for pre-deployment lunar operations, including regolith excavation, automated site preparation, and resource extraction prior to crew arrival.

== Collaborative Network ==
Rethink Space collaborates with academic researchers, space technology institutions, and start-up hubs, including:

* Valentina Sumini (Politecnico di Torino / MIT Media Lab) – Space architecture and swarm robotics.
* Tommy Nilsson (Fraunhofer FIT / European Space Agency) – Human-computer interaction and lunar digital twins.
* German Accelerator/Start2Group (selected Rethink Space for their "market discovery" and "market access" programs)
* ESA / ESTEC (selected Rethink Space for "Strategy forum on Space-Based Data Centers")

== Key Figures ==

* Karl Johannes Lierfeld – Founder and CEO. Lierfeld is a scientific author and entrepreneur working across artificial intelligence, cognitive neuroscience, and space technology.

data.title: Falcon 23-4M Lightning
data.text:
The Falcon 23-4M Lightning, also styled FDI Falcon-23/4M Lightning, is a trailer-mounted short-range air defense and counter-unmanned aircraft system combining four ZU-23-2 twin-barrel 23 mm anti-aircraft gun mounts with radar, electro-optical sensors and centralized fire control.

Azerbaijani reporting attributes the design, development and manufacture of the system's main platform to FDI Falcon Dynamic Systems Azerbaijan. Other defence publications describe FDI Technology (Falcon Dynamic Systems) as a Turkish defence enterprise. These descriptions refer to the manufacturer and its reported national affiliations; they do not, by themselves, establish joint governmental development of the weapon.

The system was displayed at the ADEX 2026 defence exhibition in Baku, Azerbaijan, which took place from 30 September to 2 October 2026.

== Development ==

According to information supplied by the manufacturer and published by Editor.az, the main platform was designed and produced by FDI Falcon Dynamic Systems Azerbaijan, with BIRD radar components integrated as a separate technological module. The manufacturer said that integration, evaluation, proving-ground activity and live-fire trials were being carried out with support from Azerbaijan's Ministry of Defence. The company reiterated this account in an October 2026 announcement; these statements have not been presented as independently verified test results.

Times of Defence and Defence.Tech reported that a version of the system had been delivered to Azerbaijan in 2025 for integration and testing, describing the information as originating from the company. The reports do not establish the extent of any subsequent operational deployment.

== Design ==

The ADEX configuration mounts four ZU-23-2 gun assemblies on a multi-axle semi-trailer. Each assembly has two 23 mm cannon barrels, for a total of eight. Published descriptions also identify hydraulic stabilizing outriggers fitted to the carrier.

The concept reuses existing ZU-23-2 armament in a system intended for point defence, including the protection of airfields, logistics sites, command posts and other fixed or semi-fixed infrastructure. Defence reports list standard 23×152 mmB ammunition and a nominal combined cyclic rate of approximately 3,200–4,000 rounds per minute; these figures describe the weapon configuration, not a measured combat success rate.

AsiaToday described the displayed system as having a mast-mounted electro-optical station and a separate remote-control position with monitors. Azerbaijan's Ordu.az also published a feature about the four-mount arrangement in October 2026; its account closely resembles reporting by Army Recognition.

== Sensors and fire control ==

Reports describe the BIRD radar as providing surveillance and target cueing, while electro-optical and infrared equipment supports observation and target tracking. These inputs are reported to feed the FDI Falcon Eye Air Guard centralized fire-control system, allowing the four gun mounts to be directed as a coordinated installation.

The system has been described as using automated target tracking and computerized ballistic calculations while retaining remote operator control. In a report titled На ADEX в Баку представили Falcon-23M: ИИ следит, оператор стреляет, the Russian technology site Modelora used the designation Falcon-23M Lightning and, citing a NEWS.ru correspondent and an attributed developer statement, reported that artificial intelligence identifies and follows targets while the operator makes the decision to fire. The same report mentioned a radar detection range of up to 10 km and asserted that the underlying artificial-intelligence technology had been in development for seven years. Those details are uncorroborated descriptions of a differently designated system, not independently established specifications for the 23-4M variant; radar detection range is also distinct from weapon engagement range.

== Reported performance ==

Published manufacturer figures specify engagement against aerial targets travelling at speeds of up to 650 km/h, at ranges of up to 2.5 km and altitudes of up to 1,000 metres. Army Recognition, Defence Arabia and Vietnamese coverage note that the figures are manufacturer-stated or remain subject to validation; they are not verified here as achieved operational performance.

== Exhibition and media coverage ==

The Falcon 23-4M Lightning was depicted or discussed in ADEX 2026 coverage by NEWS.ru, AsiaToday and the Azerbaijani publication Ordu.az. Further Russian-language reporting included a brief item on Pressa24, which credited the Telegram channel @[user], and a comparative article in Conflictora discussing the Falcon alongside modernized ZU-23-family systems. Modelora also published a report on AI-related tracking and operator control.

Defence Review, Times of Defence, Army Recognition, Defence Arabia and Defence.Tech covered the system in specialist or defence-industry reporting. Defence.Tech explicitly credited Army Recognition for some of its information, while several reports repeated manufacturer technical figures.

In Vietnam, coverage included features in VietNamNet and the People's Army Newspaper (QDND). The QDND article was republished by Báo Mới, while the VietNamNet article was reproduced by TinCongNghe, ThongTinTrucTuyen, VNBizNews and Báo Mới. These are republications of the respective original stories rather than separate investigations.

data.text:

David Elkington, also known as Dave Elkington, is an entrepreneur who co-founded InsideSales.com and served as its chief executive officer. He co-founded the company with Ken Krogue and Rob Christensen in 2004. [ref: From Cash-Strapped to Fast-Growth: How InsideSales.com Survived an Early Crisis, Inc.] [ref: An inside look at InsideSales, Deseret News]

==Career==

A 2017 profile in Deseret News reported that Elkington worked in banking and later studied computer science at the graduate level at Brigham Young University. The profile connected his technical studies with the development of InsideSales.com's data-driven sales software.

In a 2015 account of InsideSales.com's early financial difficulties, Inc. reported that a problem with the company's credit line threatened its ability to meet payroll in 2008. The article described Elkington's response, including discussions with vendors and customers, and characterized the episode as a formative crisis for the company. It also reported that Elkington and his wife had worked overnight cleaning shifts during the company's early bootstrapping period.

Deseret News later described Elkington's role in InsideSales.com's product strategy and company leadership. The article discussed the company's growth, its use of data to guide sales activity, and decisions made during a period of workforce reduction. In a separate 2015 article, Inc. reported on Elkington's role in selecting investors and retaining control of the company during its fundraising period. [ref: How InsideSales.com Raised $140 Million Without Ceding Control, Inc.]

data.title: Muisbertus
data.text:
Muisbertus

== Achtergrond ==

Muisbertus is een internetmeme verspreid op Nederlandse meme pagina's vanaf 2025. De meme wordt veelal in verband gebracht met de memepagina [https://rtvvannelle.nl/ RTVVanNelle], hoewel niet met zekerheid gezegd kan worden of de meme hier ook voor het eerst is geplaatst.

De meme toont een karakter wat doorgaans half mens en half muis is, hoewel het visueel vooral een mannelijk, menselijk gedaante is met wat kenmerken van een muis zoals:

- Meer (grijs) haar dan natuurlijk voor een mens

- Een duidelijke verticale spleet in de bovenlip

- Oren in de vorm van die van een muis

Verder toont de meme een klein deel van een menselijk lichaam met overwegend overgewicht, een oud aandoende huidstextuur en neutraal starende ogen van achter een bril. In de originele afbeelding draagt Muisbertus een blauw t-shirt, hoewel vooral hierin veel variatie is aangebracht in latere memes.

== Verhaal ==

Verschillende verhalen rondom Muisbertus doen de ronde sinds de introductie in 2025, waarin vaak wordt beweerd dat Muisbertus zich bezighoudt met de productie en verspreiding van harddrugs op een manier die vooral doet denken aan de hitserie Breaking Bad.

Muisbertus komt volgens het verhaal uit Hoogeveen en heeft verschillende vijanden, dan wel kennissen die ook in verband worden gebracht met de onderwereld, zoals Kakeltinus, Miauwtinus en Grombertus.

data.title: Tobe Asikoko
data.text:
Tobechukwu "Tobe" Asikoko (born 16 February 1986) is a Nigerian fashion designer and creative director. He is the founder of the namesake fashion brand Tobe Asikoko, which focuses on integrating traditional African textiles and narrative concepts into contemporary couture. [ref: Nigerian Designer Tobe Asikoko Gains Attention for Storytelling Through Fashion – THISDAYLIVE, ThisDay]

== Early life and education ==
Asikoko was born on 16 February 1986 and hails from Delta State, Nigeria. He pursued higher education in the performing arts and design across Nigeria and the United Kingdom where he moved into specialized design. Asikoko completed a Master of Arts (MA) in Design (Fashion) with Advanced Practice at Teesside University in Middlesbrough, United Kingdom [ref: Across Africa and Europe, Tobe Asikoko blends heritage with contemporary fashion, The Nigerian Xpress]. As part of his advanced practice, he completed an internship at the Ferrari Fashion School in Milan, Italy, in 2024. [ref: My fashion internship in Milan, blogs.tees.ac.uk]

== Career ==
Asikoko established his fashion label, Tobe Asikoko, incorporating techniques from his theatrical background into fashion design and garment construction with his work been presented on runways including the GT Fashion Week in Lagos, Nigeria. In 2025, he showcased a collection at the Gambia International Fashion Week. [ref: How I'm turning African culture into contemporary fashion — Tobe Asikoko, Vanguard News]

== Design style ==
Asikoko's fashion collections combine elements of African craftsmanship with European tailoring techniques using fashion as a medium for storytelling and cultural preservation. [ref: Tobe Asikoko and the Art of Turning Fashion Into Cultural Memory, The Poise Nigeria]

data.title: Navin Manjooran
data.text:
----

Navin Manjooran is an American nanotechnology expert, [ref: Nanotech Industry Panel, NIMET: Nanoscience Institute for Medical & Engineering Technology] healthcare professional, business executive and author who serves as the President of ASM International, [ref: Dr. Navin Manjooran Appointed as President of ASM International, ASM International] a global professional society for nanotechnology, materials scientists and professionals in healthcare and energy. He is the chairman of Solve a technology and research company focused on cancer, healthcare and energy headquartered in Florida. [ref: ]

== Education ==
Manjooran holds an MBA from the Booth School of Business at the University of Chicago and has his EE from Harvard University. He earned a BTech from the National Institute of Technology. He has his MS from the University of Florida and a doctorate in MSE (cancer and nanotechnology) from Virginia Tech. [ref: Five alumni inducted into Academy of Engineering Excellence, news.vt.edu] [ref: Academy of Engineering Excellence, eng.vt.edu]

== Career ==
Manjooran worked at Siemens AG for nearly a decade as part of the company's global leadership team. During his tenure, he managed international collaborations and strategic development across the company's technology portfolio.

In 2020, he became chairman of Solve, a company that provides research services addressing challenges in energy, industry, medicine, and infrastructure. [ref: ]

Since 2010, Manjooran has served as a professor adjunct in materials science [ref: Material science all set to create wonders in future: Dr Manjooran, The Times of India] and engineering at Virginia Tech. He also serves as chairman of the advisory board for the Materials Science and Engineering Department and the College of Engineering at the University of Florida. [ref: People, Department of Materials Science & Engineering] [ref: ]

== ASM International ==
Manjooran has been active in ASM International, which describes itself as the world's largest materials professional society. He served on the board of trustees beginning in 2020, became senior vice president in 2023–2024, and assumed the presidency on October 1, 2024.

He has co-organized more than 50 international symposia and more than 150 sessions for the society and other professional organizations. [ref: AMP 01 January-February 2025, static.asminternational.org]

== Recognition ==
Manjooran is a fellow of seven professional technical and leadership societies, including ASM International, [ref: 2020 Fellows, ASM International] the American Ceramic Society, the Institute of Materials, Minerals and Mining, and the Indian Institute of Metals. [ref: ACerS announces 2024 Class of Fellows - The American Ceramic Society, The American Ceramic Society] He has been inducted into academic and leadership honor societies, including Alpha Sigma Mu. [ref: Alpha Sigma Mu inducts new class of Fellows – Alpha Sigma Mu, alphasigmamu.org]

In April 2025, he was inducted into the Virginia Tech Hall of Fame - Virginia Tech Academy of Engineering Excellence [ref: Five alumni inducted into Academy of Engineering Excellence, news.vt.edu], which has recognized only 190 graduates out of more than 82,000 living alumni and 250,000 total alumni of the College of Engineering at Virginia Tech.

== Publication ==
Manjooran has authored or edited 12 books on advanced nanotechnology and materials published by Wiley and the Royal Society of Chemistry. [ref: Issn Ser.: Nanofabrication and Its Application in Renewable Energy by Navin Manjooran (2014, Hardcover) for sale online, eBay] His books include Nanofabrication and Its Application in Renewable Energy (Royal Society of Chemistry, 2014) and Advances in Energy Materials (Wiley, 2009).
