data.title: Street Fighter (2026 soundtrack)
data.text:
Street Fighter (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack) is the soundtrack album to the 2026 film Street Fighter directed by Kitao Sakurai which is based on the Street Fighter video game series by Capcom. The album features original score composed by Leo Birenberg and Zach Robinson and two original songs by the industrial rock band Health. The album was released through Milan Records and Paramount Music on October 16, 2026.

== Background ==
Leo Birenberg and Zach Robinson composed the score for Street Fighter renewing his association with Sakurai after their collaboration in Twisted Metal. The composers admitted that the music for the video game has been their core musical foundation that shaped their career as composers, having listened to "Guile's Theme" composed by Yoko Shimomura for the video game. The newer version of "Guile's Theme" served as a nod to the original theme, and had attempted the reinterpretation to be heavily substantial for the film. [ref: ‘Street Fighter’ Soundtrack Takes ‘Guile’s Theme’ From Arcade to Big Screen: See the Full Tracklist, [[Billboard (magazine)]

The composers added that the primary goal for them was to present each character with a unique musical identity, and they went ahead with a fan-pleasing approach by creating distinct sounds for the characters and had incorporated most of them for nostalgic moments. He also admitted the action choreography for E. Honda was the most unique segments to score for and praised the director for allowing unconventional experimentations with the music. The duo also expressed on incorporating the music of 50 Cent to create a seamless "dovetail" between the licensed pre-existing music and original compositions. [ref: Cobra Kai Composers Zach Robinson and Leo Birenberg on pleasing fans in Street Fighter]

Besides the score, the industrial rock band "Health" contributed two original songs—"Negative Edge" [ref: EXCLUSIVE: Health Drops New Street Fighter Film Track, Bleeding Cool] and "Brainrot". [ref: Listen: HEALTH Drops Two New Songs Written For 'Street Fighter' Movie, Metal Injection] [ref: HEALTH Share Two New Songs From The 'Street Fighter' Soundtrack, Stereogum] Guitarist Charlie Robbins also worked on few of the musical pieces as one of the featured soloists. [ref: “A dream come true”: Street Fighter soundtrack guitarist has been revealed, Guitar World]

== Release ==
The new adaptation of "Guile's Theme" was released as a single on September 30, 2026. [ref: First Track from ‘Street Fighter’ Soundtrack Released, Film Music Reporter] The soundtrack album featuring the songs and score was released through Milan Records and Paramount Music on October 16, 2026. [ref: ‘Street Fighter’ Soundtrack Album Details, Film Music Reporter] [ref: Street Fighter (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack), Apple Music]

== Reception ==
Zanobard Reviews assigned the score 7.5/10 saying, "The sheer enthusiasm of Leo Birenberg and Zach Robinson’s bombastically electric guitar-led score for Street Fighter is a thing to behold by itself, so that combined with a killer ’90s-styled orchestral/electronic sound and countless references to iconic themes makes it so worth a listen." [ref: Street Fighter (2026) – Soundtrack Review, Zanobard Reviews] Ayaan Paul Chowdhury of The Hindu added that "few composers are better equipped to soundtrack men punching through their feelings than Leo Birenberg and Zach Robinson of Cobra Kai fame". [ref: ‘Street Fighter’ movie review: Fists, fetishes and a fighting chance at cult status, The Hindu] Kristy Puchko of Mashable India wrote "The score by composers Leo Birenberg and Zach Robinson leans on electric guitar and synth keyboards that throw back to '90s action-movie sensibilities." [ref: 'Street Fighter' Review: What If It's Giving Super Mario Bros Live-Action, But I Love That?, [[Mashable] Dan Bayer of Next Best Picture called it "a kinetic techno score by Leo Birenberg and Zach Robinson". [ref: "STREET FIGHTER" - Review, Next Best Picture]

data.title: Kirk T. McDonald
data.text:
----

Kirk T. McDonald is an American experimental physicist specializing in high-energy physics and strong-field quantum electrodynamics. He is a professor emeritus in the Department of Physics at Princeton University.

== Biography ==

=== Education ===
McDonald first studied at the University of Arizona, where he earned his Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree in physics in 1966. He pursued his graduate studies at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), completing his PhD titled Inelastic Photoproduction of Pi Mesons from Hydrogen and Deuterium at Energies Between 1.3 and 1.8 GeV in 1972 under the supervision of Clemens A. Heusch. [ref: Inelastic Photoproduction of Pi Mesons from Hydrogen and Deuterium at Energies Between 1.3 and 1.8 GeV, Caltech / ProQuest Dissertations]

=== Academic career ===
From 1973 to 1975, he conducted postdoctoral research as a Fellow at CERN in Geneva, before becoming a researcher at the Enrico Fermi Institute at the University of Chicago.

In 1976, he joined the faculty of Princeton University as an assistant professor. He was granted tenure in 1980 and spent the remainder of his academic career there at the Joseph Henry Laboratories. [ref: Kirk McDonald's Research Interests, Princeton University] He is currently a professor emeritus.

== Research and contributions ==
McDonald's research focuses on major international experimental programs in particle physics and the development of innovative detectors.

=== Strong-field quantum electrodynamics (QED) ===
In the 1990s, he led the notable SLAC E-144 experiment at the Stanford Linear Accelerator Center (SLAC). This experiment successfully produced matter directly from light-by-light collisions (nonlinear Breit–Wheeler process) by colliding a 46.6 GeV electron beam with an ultra-intense picosecond laser pulse, [ref: Observation of Nonlinear Effects in Compton Scattering, Physical Review Letters] thereby validating fundamental predictions of strong-field quantum electrodynamics. [ref: Positron Production in Multiphoton Light-by-Light Scattering, Physical Review Letters]

=== Neutrino physics and flavor ===
McDonald has been heavily involved in the study of neutrinos and CP violation:
* He participated in the Daya Bay Reactor Neutrino Experiment in China, which precisely measured the neutrino mixing angle θ13. [ref: Observation of Electron-Antineutrino Disappearance at Daya Bay, Physical Review Letters] This contribution led to him sharing the 2016 Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics with the rest of the collaboration. [ref: Laureates: Daya Bay Collaboration, Breakthrough Prize]
* He collaborated on the BaBar experiment at SLAC, dedicated to the study of CP violation in B meson decays. [ref: Observation of CP Violation in the $B^0$ Meson System, Physical Review Letters]
* He also contributed to cutting-edge research programs on neutrino factories, high-power targetry for muon production, [ref: High-Power Targets for Muon (and Neutrino) Production, arXiv] and the international Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE, formerly LBNE/LANNDD).

=== Electromagnetism pedagogy ===
Beyond his experimental research, McDonald is globally renowned in the physics community for his extensive collection of problems, pedagogical notes, and technical clarifications in classical electromagnetism. He has authored over 1,200 scientific notes resolving complex paradoxes related to Maxwell's equations, radiation reaction forces, and the dynamics of relativistic charges.

== Awards ==
* 2016: Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics (as a member of the Daya Bay collaboration).

== Selected publications ==

* Kirk T. McDonald, The Relation Between Expressions for Time-Dependent Electromagnetic Fields Given by Jefimenko and by Panofsky and Phillips, Joseph Henry Laboratories, Princeton University (1996; updated 2018).
* Kirk T. McDonald, On the History of the Radiation Reaction, Princeton University (2017).
* Kirk T. McDonald, On the “Helmholtz” Decomposition, Joseph Henry Laboratories, Princeton University (2023).

data.title: Puruesh Chaudhary
data.text:
Puruesh Chaudhary is a Pakistani media development practitioner and futures researcher. She is the founder of Agahi, a Pakistani non-profit organisation, and of its journalism awards programme. [ref: The Media in Pakistan, The Diplomat]

== Career ==
Chaudhary began her career at the Pakistani television channels Dawn News and Samaa TV. In 2010 the Center for International Media Ethics named her its ambassador to Pakistan on media ethics, and in 2012 the World Economic Forum recognised her as a Global Shaper. Between 2011 and 2012 she worked with press clubs in Sindh, Punjab, Azad Kashmir and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to run training courses in investigative journalism and media ethics.

Through Agahi she launched the Agahi Awards, which The Diplomat described as Pakistan's first annual journalism awards. In 2014 the magazine interviewed her about media ethics and the state of investigative journalism in Pakistan. In August 2015 she was the featured guest on Cafe DC, a Voice of America Urdu interview programme hosted by Faiz Rehman. [ref: Cafe DC: Puruesh Chaudhary, Founder/President of AGAHI, Voice of America Urdu]

Chaudhary has served as a director of Mishal Pakistan, the World Economic Forum's partner institute in the country. In 2020 she briefed a meeting with Pakistan's Board of Investment on the forum's forthcoming Global Competitiveness Report. [ref: World Economic Forum asks Pakistan to build institutions, The News International] In 2015 the futurist Ross Dawson included her in his list of the world's leading female futurists. [ref: List of the world's top female futurists, rossdawson.com]

Etac is a Swedish‑founded multinational group that develops, designs, and sells medical devices such as mobility aids and patient handling equipment. The company was founded in 1973 and is owned by the investment company Nordstjernan. [ref: ]

The group is known for its innovative and ergonomic product design for people with reduced mobility. [ref: Why We Think the Etac Shower Commode is the Best On the Market, Limon Attire] [ref: TAKHEIS fra Etac Molift, Produktfakta] [ref: Konferanse om tekologi i helse og omsorgsektoren – Rauma kommune, www.rauma.kommune.no] [ref: Rauma Helsehus, Rauma Kommune] The products are used in healthcare as well as in home environments and are intended for children, adults, and older people with varying needs for support in everyday life, and for healthcare professionals. [ref: ] [ref: Nordstjernan's subsidiary Etac invests in Ki Mobility, a US manual complex rehab company, Nordstjernan]

== History ==
Etac has its origins in RFSU Rehab, an organisation founded in 1973 by RFSU to develop and sell assistive devices as part of its social work. [ref: Penna för reumatiker, DigitaltMuseum] [ref: History – Etac, Etac] The early development of RFSU Rehab was shaped by Sverker Göthberg, who introduced industrial design as a central element in their product development. [ref: Dödsfall: Sverker Göthberg, Dagens Nyheter]

In 1985, RFSU acquired the company Enco Miljö and the Etac brand. In 1999, Enco Miljö was merged with RFSU Rehab, after which the company was renamed Etac. [ref: Årsrapport 2023, RFSU] [ref: History – Etac, Etac] Since 2008, Etac has continued to expand through a number of acquisitions in the assistive devices and patient handling segment. [ref: ] [ref: Nordstjernan's subsidiary Etac invests in Ki Mobility, Private Equity Wire]

In 2006, the Ax:son Johnson family's investment company Nordstjernan became the majority owner of Etac. [ref: RFSU och Nordstjernan i långsiktigt partnerskap om Etac, Cision News] In 2011, Nordstjernan acquired the remaining shares in Etac and became the sole owner. [ref: Nordstjernan takes the next step in building a global mobility Group – Etac acquires Convaid, Cision News]

Etac has received several design awards, including the Red Dot Award, Excellent Swedish Design, the Good Design Award, and the Award for Excellence. [ref: ] Some of Etac's products have also been shown at international exhibitions, such as the Museum of Modern Art in New York. [ref: Designs for Independent Living: Museum of Modern Art, New York, April 16–June 7, 1988, Museum of Modern Art (MoMA)]

== Product brands ==
The product brands within Etac include Etac, Immedia, Molift, R82, Convaid, Star, HoverTech [ref: Nordstjernan's subsidiary Etac invests in HoverTech, a US patient handling company, Nordstjernan], Ki [ref: Nordstjernan's subsidiary Etac invests in Ki Mobility, Private Equity Wire], Axiom, and Klaxon. [ref: Gernandt & Danielsson advises Nordstjernan and Etac in connection with its acquisition of KLAXON Mobility GmbH, Mynewsdesk] [ref: Our product brands, www.etac.com]

== Manufacturing and distribution ==
Etac's products are designed and/or manufactured in Scandinavia, North America, Austria, and Poland, and distributed from regional warehouses. [ref: About us, Etac]

The Etac group has sales subsidiaries in ten countries: Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Germany, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, Italy, France, North America, and Australia. Etac also sells through distributors in many parts of the world. [ref: ]

Etac has its own manufacturing facilities in the following locations; [ref: ] [ref: ] [ref: ] [ref: ] [ref: ] [ref: Immedia - Bloomberg] [ref: ]

* Anderstorp, Sweden
* Gedved, Denmark
* Arnoldstein, Austria
* Tczew, Poland
* Torrance, CA, United States
* Allentown, PA, United States
* Stevens Point, WI, USA

data.title: HEF Group
data.text:
HEF Group is a private surface engineering company, founded in 1953 by Jacques-Jean-Caubet. It was founded in the city of Saint-Chamond near Saint-Étienne (France) in the Loire department [ref: ]. In 2025, the group operates in 23 countries in Europe, North America, South America and Asia.

Since 1973, HEF is employee-owned, with 75% distributed among employees while the remaining shares are held by the founding family [ref: HEF, ingénierie des matériaux de surface et traitement de surface, HEF] [ref: HEF Group Acquires Abrisa Technologies, Abrisa Technologies].

== Sectors of activity ==
HEF Group's sectors of activity are the following:

* Surface finishing in ionic liquid;
* PVD and PECVD vacuum deposition technologies;
* The manufacturing of mechanical components such as bushings, pins and joints intended for industrial applications;
* Tribology and surface degradation mechanisms (wear, friction, corrosion and more);
* Hydrogen technologies (fuel cell [ref: A Saint-Etienne, HEF investit dans la production de matériaux pour piles à combustible, L'Usine Nouvelle]) since 2024 [ref: Saint-Etienne. Cette entreprise crée une usine unique au monde: 100 emplois prévus, actu.fr];
* Photonics (lasers, optical filters) since 2023 [ref: Une nouvelle usine stéphanoise pour HEF, www.brefeco.com].
The group develops and sells surface coating services through processes such as nitriding or vacuum deposition [ref: HEF GROUPE, Hydrogen and Carbon Capture Technology World Expo 2026].

HEF manufactures friction components, notably metal and composite bushings. Depending on the intended application, these products can provide resistance to wear, friction, abrasion or corrosion, which serves industries such as mobility, energy, manufacturing and aeronautics [ref: HEF PEL Bushings, Agriculture XPRT] [ref: PEL 4.0].

== Acquisitions and diversification ==
As part of its strategy to extend its field of activity, HEF Group has acquired companies in the sectors of tribology, surface engineering and photonics.

In the friction components sector, the group acquired companies such as ACM Composite Bearings from the United Kingdom in 2024 and Drie-D from the Netherlands in 2026 [ref: ].

Beginning in 2021, HEF expanded into the photonics industry through acquisitions, and now owns the French companies Fichou (2021) [ref: Fichou, spécialiste de l’optique militaire demeure française, Portail de l'IE] [ref: Le fonds d'investissement du ministère des Armées se désengage de Fichou, spécialiste de l'optique de haute précision, Zone Militaire] [ref: Le ligérien HEF accélère sa diversification en reprenant des PME en Bretagne et en région parisienne - Le Journal des Entreprises, www.lejournaldesentreprises.com], Kerdry (2021) [ref: HEF becomes a major actor in the fields of photonics and defense] [ref: Le ligérien HEF accélère sa diversification en reprenant des PME en Bretagne et en région parisienne - Le Journal des Entreprises, www.lejournaldesentreprises.com], Acerde (October 2021) [ref: Startup ACERDE Anodes légères tournantes pour tubes à rayons X, www.myfrenchstartup.com] and Neyco (21 July 2022) [ref: ], as well as the American companies Abrisa Technologies (2021) [ref: Abrisa Technologies Joins HEF Photonics Business Unit, www.photonicsonline.com] [ref: ] and The Telic Company (2025) [ref: HEF Groupe annonce le rachat de la société TELIC by HEF GROUPEDirectIndustry, trends.directindustry.fr].

In 2024, the group invested €40 million into developing a new plant dedicated to the development of surface treatments for fuel cells, with the intention of providing an alternative to materials such as gold and platinum [ref: Hydrogène: le groupe HEF contraint de revoir sa copie faute d'un marché suffisant, www.latribune.fr] [ref: Plaques bipolaires: fabrication avancée, usinage CNC et revêtements de surface pour les piles à combustible de nouvelle génération, Shenzhen Tuofa Technology Co., Ltd.].

data.title: Patriot Pit Stop
data.text:
Patriot Pit Stop

Patriot Pit Stop is an independently operated automotive repair and maintenance business located at Hill Air Force Base in Davis County, Utah, United States. The business operates adjacent to the Exchange Mini Mall at 7440 6th Street, providing automotive maintenance, diagnostic services, and mechanical repairs to military personnel, civilian employees, retirees, and other authorized visitors to the installation. [ref: https://patriotpitstophill.com/]

History

The automotive repair facility now known as Patriot Pit Stop, since Nov. 2025, originally operated as the separate company, Firestone automotive service center, before transitioning to Kwik Kar Complete Auto Care in July 2017. The location serves the Hill Air Force Base community as an automotive maintenance and repair facility. ref>https://www.loc8nearme.com/utah/hill-air-force-base/kwik-kar/4531611/

The Hill Air Force Base location subsequently transitioned from the Kwik Kar name to Patriot Pit Stop, establishing a distinct local identity while continuing to provide automotive maintenance and repair services. The facility retained its established location on the installation and continued serving the surrounding military community.

In September 2026, ownership of Patriot Pit Stop LLC transferred to Aaron Cleveland, marking a new chapter in the business's operations. The company continued operating as Patriot Pit Stop following the ownership transition.

Location

Patriot Pit Stop is situated at 7440 6th Street on Hill Air Force Base, near Ogden and Layton, Utah. The repair facility is attached to the Hill Air Force Base Exchange Mini Mall, a retail and service complex serving the installation's military and civilian population. [ref: https://www.loc8nearme.com/utah/hill-afb/hill-afb-mini-mall/7340475/]

Its location provides convenient access to automotive services for individuals working or conducting business on the installation. Because the facility is located within an active military installation, customer access is subject to Hill Air Force Base entry requirements.

Automotive services

Patriot Pit Stop provides general automotive repair, preventive maintenance, and vehicle diagnostic services for domestic and imported vehicles. Its operations include routine maintenance as well as more extensive mechanical repairs. [ref: https://patriotpitstophill.com/]

Services offered include oil and filter changes, brake inspection and repair, battery replacement, engine diagnostics, scheduled maintenance, tire rotation, wheel alignment, suspension and steering repairs, heating and air conditioning service, electrical system repairs, and replacement of starters, alternators, and timing belts. The staff has even been reported to drop off and pick up customers at their work.

The facility also provides vehicle inspections and fleet maintenance services. Its preventive maintenance program includes multipoint vehicle inspections intended to identify potential mechanical issues and support long-term vehicle reliability.

Operations

Patriot Pit Stop operates as a locally managed automotive service business serving the Hill Air Force Base community. The facility employs automotive technicians and service personnel responsible for vehicle diagnostics, maintenance, repairs, and customer assistance.

The business generally operates Monday through Friday, 8AM - 4PM, with scheduled appointments and repair services available during regular business hours. Its location within the Exchange Mini Mall area allows customers to access automotive maintenance services while they work without leaving the military installation.

No Brainer Agency is a UK-based digital marketing and public relations agency headquartered in Warrington, Cheshire. Founded in 2015 by Gary Jenkins and Lee Cullen, [ref: Where we work: No Brainer, Warrington, Prolific North] the agency specialises in services including search engine optimisation (SEO), digital PR, and content marketing. [ref: No Brainer Agency Profile, The Drum]

== Operations and Corporate Status ==
The agency operates primarily within the United Kingdom and provides digital search and visibility services across sectors including e-commerce, healthcare, and financial services. Notable client campaigns have included work for Checkatrade, AO.com, Places for People, Kids Planet, and PillTime. The firm operates as an independent agency under the ownership of its original co-founders. [ref: No Brainer: The co-founders proving purpose-led business possible, City A.M.]

In December 2023, No Brainer Agency became a Certified B Corporation, earning an overall B Impact Score of 87.4, which recognises the company's verified social and environmental performance. [ref: No Brainer Agency - B Corp Directory, B Lab]

In early 2026, the agency integrated artificial intelligence into its operations following a partnership and training program with AI consultancy NoCodeLab.ai. [ref: Warrington PR agency puts AI at the heart of its business, Warrington Guardian] As part of this initiative, the agency launched Seer, a proprietary digital tool designed to consolidate SEO, social discovery, and digital PR data for marketing analysis. [ref: Agency News: No Brainer, One Black Bear, SHC Digital and more, New Digital Age]

== Recognition ==
The agency has been featured in industry media and regional press. The regional media publication Prolific North ranked No Brainer Agency 18th in its annual "Top 50 PR Agencies" list for 2023 and 2024, and 28th in 2025. [ref: Where we work: No Brainer, Warrington, Prolific North] [ref: The Prolific North Top 50 PR Agencies 2025, Prolific North] In 2026, when the publication consolidated its sector-specific rankings into a single pan-agency list, No Brainer Agency was included in the "Top 150 Agencies" ranking. [ref: The Prolific North Top 150 Agencies 2026: Full list revealed, Prolific North] In September 2026, the Warrington Guardian reported that the agency was included in the "UK's Best Workplaces in Advertising, Media & Marketing" list within the Small & Medium category. data.title: Hakeem Babar
data.text:
Hakeem Babar (also spelled Hakim Babar) is a Pakistani herbal practitioner based in Rawalpindi, Pakistan. He attracted media attention in February 2026 after videos of his marriage circulated on social media. His marriage and subsequent statements were reported by Pakistani and international news outlets. [ref: 60-year-old herbal practitioner marries 26-year-old woman in Rawalpindi. Couple gets trolled, Moneycontrol]

== Career ==

Babar has been identified in news reports as the owner of Al-Noor Dawakhana, a traditional medicine establishment in Rawalpindi. Media reports describe him as a hakeem, a practitioner of traditional herbal medicine. [ref: 60-year-old Hakeem from Rawalpindi marries young woman, video goes viral, MM News] Published coverage reviewed for this article provides limited independently verified information about his early life, education, or professional training.

== Media attention ==

=== Marriage and public reaction ===

In February 2026, videos and photographs of Babar's marriage circulated on social media and attracted public discussion about the age difference between the couple. Reports described mixed reactions, including criticism and support for the couple. [ref: Rawalpindi groom, 60, hits back at critics over marriage, Aaj English TV] [ref: 60-year-old herbal practitioner marries 26-year-old woman in Rawalpindi. Couple gets trolled, Moneycontrol]

Babar described the marriage as both a love marriage and an arranged marriage, saying that the couple had developed an interest in each other before deciding to marry. He also responded to criticism of their age difference, arguing that age was less important than feeling young at heart. [ref: راولپنڈی کے 60 سالہ حکیم کا شادی پر غلط تبصرے کرنے والوں کو جواب, Aaj News]

=== Public statement and apology ===

On 28 February 2026, Aaj News reported that Babar and his wife had released a video message asking the public for forgiveness following the circulation of their wedding videos. In the statement, Babar referred to Ramadan as a month of mercy and forgiveness and said he hoped people would forgive them. His wife also asked the public for forgiveness. [ref: حکیم بابر اور ان کی اہلیہ نے معافی مانگ لی, Aaj News]

data.title: Metamorphic solar cell
data.text:
Metamorphic (MM) solar cells, also called lattice-mismatched solar cells are multijunction solar cells that incorporate materials with different lattice constants. These are contrasted with lattice-matched (LM) solar cells in which all subcells have the same crystal lattice constant. The main advantage of MM cells is the ability to optimize the band gaps of each subcell for maximum efficiency, a process known as band-gap engineering. Although band gaps can be modified in all multijunction solar cells, metamorphic semiconductors allow for greatly increased flexibility. [ref: ]

Having different lattice constants causes elastic deformation. To mitigate this, dislocations are purposefully created in the structure. This in turn increases the nonradiative recombination rate, which can decrease performance of the cell. A buffer layer can be used to relieve strain and reduce the dislocations. Another method is to grow the higher band gap subcells first and then grow the lower band gap subcells with a lattice-mismatch. Such cells are known as inverted metamorphic (IMM) cells. This also necessitates that the substrate is removed, which is done either through etching or epitaxial lift-off. [ref: ] The term upright metamorphic (UMM) cell is sometimes used to refer to cells that aren't inverted. [ref: ] [ref: ]

data.title: Salah El Moncef
data.text:
Salah El Moncef (also written Salah el Moncef; full name Salah el Moncef bin Khalifa) is a writer, literary scholar, editor and visual artist born in Kuwait City and based in France. His publications include Atopian Limits (2002), The Offering (2015), Now and Then (2022), Benghazi (2022), The Woman from Warsaw (2026), and the long-form study Art as Pharmakon (2021). Independent criticism of his fiction has focused on memory, traumatic loss, diaspora and the effects of colonial and fascist violence. [ref: Nantes Université, "Salah EL MONCEF BIN KHALIFA," faculty profile, updated 12 May 2026.] [ref: Jean-Yves Pellegrin, review of Atopian Limits, Transatlantica (2004), DOI 10.4000/transatlantica.707.] [ref: Stephen Watt, "Memory, Trauma, and the Diasporic Subject," Los Angeles Review of Books, 4 April 2015.] [ref: Stephen Watt, "An Enormous, Enigmatic Signifier: Salah el Moncef's Benghazi," Michigan Quarterly Review, January 2023.] [ref: Stephen Watt, "The Art of World-Building: Salah el Moncef's The Woman from Warsaw," Michigan Quarterly Review, 20 February 2026.] [ref: Salah El Moncef, official author site (used only for routine biographical and publication data).]

At Nantes Université, Moncef is a Maître de Conférences in English studies and creative writing, with research interests in contemporary American literature and culture, diasporic literatures, migration and transnational identities. He is the General Issue Editor of Angelaki: Journal of the Theoretical Humanities and an editor of the associated Routledge series Angelaki: New Work in the Theoretical Humanities. Several Angelaki general issues have also used his paintings as cover and interior art. [ref: Nantes Université, institutional profile/CV: maître de conférences in English studies and creative writing; research on diasporic literatures, migration, and transnational identities.] [ref: Taylor & Francis, Angelaki: Journal of the Theoretical Humanities, "About this journal" (editorial team).] [ref: Routledge, Angelaki: New Work in the Theoretical Humanities, series page.] [ref: Moncef, Salah el. "Editorial Introduction: General Issue I 2024." Angelaki 29.5 (2024), artwork list and acknowledgements.] [ref: Moncef, Salah el. "Editorial Introduction: General Issue II 2025." Angelaki 30.6 (2025), artwork list and acknowledgements.]

== Education and academic career ==
A contributor biography published in the academic collection The Matrix in Theory records that Moncef received a Presidential Prize for Distinction in the Humanities in 1987 and was a Fulbright fellow at Indiana University Bloomington from 1988 to 1993. Indiana University lists him among its English PhD alumni, while a University of Colorado contributor profile likewise identifies him as a former Fulbright doctoral fellow there. [ref: University of Colorado Boulder, Genders archive, "Salah El Moncef" contributor profile.] [ref: Myriam Diocaretz and Stefan Herbrechter, eds., The Matrix in Theory (Rodopi, 2006), contributor note for Salah el Moncef bin Khalifa.] [ref: Indiana University Bloomington, Department of English, PhD alumni publications pages.]

Moncef later joined Nantes Université. The university's public profile lists him as a Maître de Conférences in the Department of English and identifies contemporary American literature and culture as his teaching and research field. A more detailed institutional profile describes his work as extending to creative writing, diasporic literature, migration and transnational identities.

== Scholarship and editorial work ==
Moncef's scholarship brings literary and cultural theory to modernist and postmodern American writing. His articles of the 1990s examined Ezra Pound in boundary 2, John Updike's Rabbit at Rest in Arizona Quarterly, Paul Auster's Moon Palace in Angelaki and Thomas Harris's Hannibal Lecter novels in Genders. This line of research was developed in Atopian Limits: Questions of Self, Complexity, and Contingency in Postmodern American Narrative (2002). [ref: Moncef, Salah el. "Gold, Representation, and the Reversible Dynamic of Symptomatic Return in Ezra Pound." boundary 2 22.1 (1995): 117–142.] [ref: Moncef, Salah el. "Sounding the Black Box: Linear Reproduction and Chance Bifurcations in Rabbit at Rest." Arizona Quarterly 51.4 (1995): 69–108.] [ref: Moncef, Salah el. "Lecter Knows Worst: Justice, Marginal Value, and the Law in the Series of Thomas Harris's Silence of the Lambs." Genders, 5 July 1999.] [ref: Moncef, Salah el. "Figures in (De)composition: The Genesis of the Paradoxical Self in Paul Auster's Moon Palace." Angelaki 4.3 (1999): 75–91.]

Reviewing Atopian Limits in Transatlantica, Jean-Yves Pellegrin described it as a wide-ranging study of postmodern American narrative organized around systems, limits, ethics and complexity, discussing writers including Paul Auster, Ken Kesey, John Updike, Thomas Harris, Gore Vidal and Kathy Acker. Moncef subsequently co-edited Présence et représentation (2005) with Jacques Gilbert and Borderline Identities in Chicano Culture (2006) with Michele Bottalico. In Aztlán, Antonio C. Márquez reviewed the latter as a collection on border identity and discussed Moncef's concluding contribution, "The Hybrid Self at the Crossroads." [ref: Antonio C. Márquez, review of Borderline Identities in Chicano Culture, Aztlán 32.2 (2007): 213–216.] [ref: WorldCat, bibliographic record for Présence et représentation, Jacques Gilbert and Salah El Moncef (Peter Lang, 2005).]

Later work ranged across film, transnational identity and Don DeLillo, including chapters on mestiza and cyborg identities and on The Matrix trilogy; essays on The Truman Show, Gloria Anzaldúa, DeLillo's Underworld and Falling Man; and the Oxford Encyclopedia of Literary Theory article on Minor Literature. His 2016 study Literature as Antidote reads Falling Man through trauma, grief and post-traumatic healing. The 32-page Art as Pharmakon: Viral Terror, Trauma, and Healing in the DeLillian Age, published in Angelaki in 2021, extends that inquiry into art, terror and recovery. [ref: Moncef, Salah el. "Minor Literature." Oxford Research Encyclopedia of Literature, published 29 May 2020.] [ref: Moncef, Salah el. "Art as Pharmakon: Viral Terror, Trauma, and Healing in the DeLillian Age." Angelaki 26.6 (2021): 144–175.] [ref: Moncef, Salah el. "Literature as Antidote: Reflections on Don DeLillo's Falling Man." International Journal of Humanities and Social Science Research 2 (2016): 87–113.] [ref: Moncef, Salah el. "Life after 'Truman'?" Revue française d'études américaines 102 (2004): 117–125.] [ref: Moncef, Salah el. "The Matrix Trilogy and the Triumph of Virtual Reason." In The Matrix in Theory (Rodopi, 2006): 227–248.] [ref: Moncef, Salah el. "Mestizas and Cyborgs R Us." In (Re)Mapping the Centres (2000): 125–136.] [ref: Moncef, Salah el. "Übermenschen, Mestizas, Nomads." Angelaki 8.3 (2003): 41–57.] [ref: Moncef, Salah el. "Don DeLillo's Underworld and the Inscriptions of the Commonplace." Angelaki 13.1 (2008): 149–165.] [ref: Moncef, Salah el. "Nomadismes et identités transfrontalières (première partie)." Amerika 2 (2010).] [ref: Moncef, Salah el. "Nomadismes et identités transfrontalières (deuxième partie)." Amerika 2 (2010).]

Moncef's scholarship has also generated independent academic citation over more than two decades. Hungarian scholar Pál Hegyi's 2010 essay on Paul Auster's Moon Palace, published in AMERICANA: E-Journal of American Studies in Hungary, relies extensively on Moncef's Lacanian reading of the novel in "Figures in (De)composition," using his terms "monadic unfolding" and "nomadic self-containment" as an interpretive framework. Joshua M. Hall's 2023 article on Gloria Anzaldúa, "Anzaldúa's Snake-Bridge as Alternative to Mestizaje," summarizes and builds on the Anzaldúa–Nietzsche argument Moncef developed in "Übermenschen, Mestizas, Nomads." Yvonne Liao, Julia T. S. Binter, Olivia Irena Durand and Helena F. S. Lopes cite Moncef's "Minor Literature" entry alongside Deleuze and Guattari's concept of minor literature in their 2026 Journal of Global History article on colonial port cities, published by Cambridge University Press. [ref: Pál Hegyi, "Extended mise-en-abyme in Paul Auster's Moon Palace," AMERICANA: E-Journal of American Studies in Hungary (2010).] [ref: Joshua M. Hall, "Anzaldúa's Snake-Bridge as Alternative to Mestizaje" (2023).] [ref: Yvonne Liao, Julia T. S. Binter, Olivia Irena Durand and Helena F. S. Lopes, "Port cities storytelling: Drawing on materials of neglect," Journal of Global History (Cambridge University Press, 2026).]

=== Scholarly reception ===
Moncef's scholarship has received attention in subsequent studies of contemporary American literature and cultural theory. Literary theorist Cary Wolfe contributed the preface, "Total Systems and Dense Instances," to Atopian Limits, discussing the book's use of systems theory, complexity and contingency in its readings of contemporary American fiction. Jean-Yves Pellegrin reviewed Atopian Limits in the academic journal Transatlantica, examining its treatment of works by Paul Auster, Ken Kesey, John Updike, Thomas Harris, Gore Vidal and Kathy Acker. [ref: Cary Wolfe, "Total Systems and Dense Instances," preface to Salah El Moncef, Atopian Limits: Questions of Self, Complexity, and Contingency in Postmodern American Narrative (Peter Lang, 2003).]

Individual arguments from Moncef's work have also been taken up in later scholarship. C. Parker Krieg's study of Updike's fiction in Studies in American Fiction discusses aspects of Moncef's interpretation of Rabbit at Rest. Alan Lopez, writing in Textual Practice, states that his own reading of a sequence in Frantz Fanon's work "owes a great deal to" Moncef's earlier analysis of Peter Weir's The Truman Show. [ref: C. Parker Krieg, "Energy Futures: John Updike's Petrofictions," Studies in American Fiction 44.1 (2017): 87–112.] [ref: Alan Lopez, "Kindred spirits: Fanon's postcolonialism," Textual Practice 29.5 (2015): 949–972, note 37.]

Moncef has edited Angelaki general issues since at least 2008, when he was credited for General issue 2008 I, and his name has appeared on the journal's masthead as General Issue Editor for each subsequent general issue through 2025. Routledge lists him among the editors of Angelaki: New Work in the Theoretical Humanities. [ref: Moncef, Salah el. "General issue 2008 I." Angelaki 13.1 (2008): 1.]

== Fiction ==

=== The Offering ===
The Offering, first published in 2015, follows Tariq Abbassi, a Tunisian poet and restaurateur living in France, through a fractured retrospective account of migration, artistic ambition, marital breakdown, grief and memory. The novel carries an independent introduction by scholar Mari Ruti. In a review essay in Angelaki, Stefan Mattesich offers an extended scholarly reading of the novel. Stephen Watt's Los Angeles Review of Books essay reads the novel through trauma and diaspora, emphasizing what he calls the impossibility of "happy forgetting" and the pressure that remembrance places on the diasporic subject. In Moderna Språk, Wade A. Bell Jr. similarly treated Tariq as a fractured transnational or "diasporic body-subject." [ref: Wade A. Bell Jr., review of The Offering, Moderna Språk 111.1 (2017): 206–208.] [ref: Stefan Mattesich, review essay on The Offering, Angelaki 20.4 (2015).] [ref: Mari Ruti, introduction to The Offering, by Salah El Moncef.]

=== Now and Then and Benghazi ===
Now and Then (2022) combines two works of fiction — Benghazi and The Night Visitor — with the essays "A Bridge Too Near" and "The Voice of Exile." Amy O'Loughlin's Foreword Clarion review interpreted the volume through identity beyond the nation-state, diaspora, nationalism and transnationalism. A BlueInk review praised its descriptive prose while arguing that the volume's fiction and theory did not always form a cohesive whole. [ref: Amy O'Loughlin, review of Now and Then, Foreword Clarion Reviews, 4 October 2022.] [ref: BlueInk Review, review of Now and Then, October 2022.]

Benghazi was also published separately as a novella in 2022. Narrated by Mariam Khaldoon, it recalls her family and her friendship with Esther Sanz against the background of Italian colonial rule in Libya and Benito Mussolini's 1937 visit to Benghazi. In Michigan Quarterly Review, Watt used Paul Ricœur's work on memory and Mari Ruti's framing of the novella to interpret its characters as diasporic subjects who are never fully at home. Kirkus Reviews praised the evocation of place and the father–daughter relationship but considered the narrative slow and overextended in places. [ref: Kirkus Reviews, review of Benghazi, posted 30 December 2022.]

An earlier novelette, Sleepwalking, appeared in the academic journal Short Story in 2011. [ref: Moncef, Salah el. "Sleepwalking." Short Story 19.1 (2011): 30–53, University of Northern Iowa ScholarWorks.]

=== The Woman from Warsaw ===
The Woman from Warsaw, published by Atopon Books in 2026, is a historical novel set principally in Benghazi during the Second World War. Mariam narrates her adolescence under Italian Fascist rule and her relationship with Esther, a Jewish émigrée. The novel incorporates Benghazi as the first of four narrative sections and expands the earlier novella's family and wartime setting. [ref: Atopon Books, catalogue page for The Woman from Warsaw (2026).]

In Michigan Quarterly Review, Watt interprets the novel as an act of "right remembering": Mariam's reconstruction of Fascist racial laws, wartime bombing and Esther's experiences places private feeling within the pressures of history. He also emphasizes Esther's independence and the novel's representation of Benghazi as a cosmopolitan city.

== Visual art ==
Angelaki has reproduced Moncef's paintings on journal covers and as interior illustrations. General Issue I 2024 used Birth 3 on its cover and included works such as Three Flights Up and Fantasy Rhino; General Issue II 2024 used Phoenician Mask 3 and included Humpty Dumpty, Iris Out and Passage Pommeraye. General Issue I 2025 used Fantasy Rhino 3 (Kinderszenen), while General Issue II 2025 used Strange Attractors 9 (Space). The publisher's issue documentation identifies the works and records permission for their reproduction. [ref: Moncef, Salah el. "Editorial Introduction: General Issue II 2024." Angelaki 29.6 (2024), artwork list and acknowledgements.] [ref: Moncef, Salah el. "Editorial Introduction: General Issue I 2025." Angelaki 30.5 (2025), artwork list and acknowledgements.]

== Selected works ==

=== Fiction ===

Algamus Recovery Centers (also known as Algamus Gambling Treatment Services) is a residential treatment facility for gambling addiction located in Goodyear, Arizona, United States. It was founded in 1992 by Rick Benson.

== History ==
Algamus was founded by Rick Benson, a recovering compulsive gambler. Benson established the organization in 1992 after experiencing difficulties finding residential treatment specifically for gambling addiction.

== Program ==
Algamus offers a residential program typically lasting four to six weeks, incorporating individual and group therapy, cognitive behavioral therapy, and aftercare planning.

== Media coverage ==
In 2026, Algamus and founder Rick Benson were profiled by Fast Company in an article examining gaps in U.S. gambling addiction treatment infrastructure amid the rise of online sports betting. The facility also received coverage from FOX 10 Phoenix and Yahoo Sports in connection with reporting on a college athlete gambling scandal. Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby publicly acknowledged receiving treatment at Algamus in a statement reported by NBC Sports.

data.title: Claudiu Popa
data.text:
Claudiu Popa is a Canadian cybersecurity consultant, author and educator whose work has focused on cybersecurity, information security, privacy and cyberfraud. He is a co-founder of the KnowledgeFlow Cybersafety Foundation and the author of books on information security, privacy and cyberfraud. [ref: RBC customer loses $10,000 after falling victim to bank draft fraud, Global News] [ref: uXperience - Think Privacy, University of Waterloo]

== Career and public work ==

Popa operates a Toronto-based risk-management consultancy focused on security and privacy. In February 2015, he appeared before the House of Commons Standing Committee on Access to Information, Privacy and Ethics during its study of identity theft and its economic impact. [ref: Evidence - ETHI (41-2) - No. 33, House of Commons of Canada] [ref: Minutes - ETHI (41-2) - No. 33, House of Commons of Canada]

The committee's subsequent report, The Growing Problem of Identity Theft and Its Economic and Social Impact, included a subsection devoted to Popa's testimony. The report summarized his evidence concerning the evolution of identity theft, phishing and spear-phishing, data breaches, credit-monitoring services and approaches to detecting and preventing identity-related fraud. [ref: The Growing Problem of Identity Theft and Its Economic and Social Impact, Standing Committee on Access to Information, Privacy and Ethics, House of Commons of Canada]

In 2019, The Toronto Star reported on privacy and security concerns raised by Popa and other parents regarding the York Region District School Board's use of the Edsby educational platform. [ref: Stouffville parents fear potential breach, want kids' information off education app, Toronto Star]

Popa is a founder of the KnowledgeFlow Foundation, an organization involved in cybersafety and digital-literacy education. The University of Waterloo identified him as the foundation's founder in materials for its 2020 Think Privacy event, while Global News has described him as a co-founder.

The Canadian Research Insights Council has credited Popa with developing its Information Security Toolkit. According to CRIC, the toolkit provides guidance for member companies and presents a standardized framework for information-security policies and procedures. [ref: New CRIC Toolkits Guide Members toward best Privacy and Information Security Practices, Canadian Research Insights Council]

== Media commentary ==
Popa has provided commentary to Canadian media on cybersecurity, fraud and data protection. Global News has interviewed him about digital fraud, data breaches and financial fraud, [ref: Top 10 Scams in Canada and How to Spot Them, CAA Magazine]

== Publications ==

data.title: Johnny O'Reilly
data.text:
----

Johnny O'Reilly (born 22 October 1970) is an Irish filmmaker and journalist. He wrote and directed the Russian-language feature films Moscow Never Sleeps (2016) and The Weather Station (2010), and the short film The Terms (2002), which was shortlisted for the 74th Academy Awards. [ref: Our man in Moscow, The Irish Times] [ref: 'I want to see out the war': Irish filmmaker moved to Ukraine from Russia when 'the pessimists were proved right', The Irish Times] [ref: Red Letter Day, The Sunday Times] As a journalist, he has reported from Russia, Belarus, and Ukraine for publications including The Sunday Times, The Times, and The Irish Times.

== Early life and education ==
O'Reilly grew up in Dublin, Ireland. He studied Russian and Classics at Trinity College Dublin. In 1993, while a student, he worked in Moscow as a freelance reporter covering the Russian constitutional crisis. In 1996, he completed graduate film studies at New York University. He worked at The Sunday Times for two years before focusing on filmmaking. In 2006, he moved to Moscow, where he lived for ten years.

== Career ==

=== Filmmaking ===

==== The Terms (2002) ====
O'Reilly directed the short film The Terms (2002), based on a short story by Irish writer Mike McCormack. The film was shortlisted for the 74th Academy Awards. [ref: The Terms Shortlisted for Oscars, IFTN]

==== The Weather Station (2010) ====
His feature directorial debut was the Russian-language thriller The Weather Station (2010). The film was set in an arctic meteorological outpost and filmed near Simferopol in Crimea. [ref: The Weather Station, Variety]

==== Moscow Never Sleeps (2016) ====
O’Reilly wrote and directed Moscow Never Sleeps (2016), an ensemble drama set during Moscow City Day celebrations. The film follows interconnected stories over a single day.

==== Kherson ====
O'Reilly subsequently began work on a documentary project focused on events in Kherson and the surrounding region.

=== Journalism and cultural initiatives ===
O'Reilly has reported on politics and culture in Eastern Europe. His reporting has appeared in outlets including The Sunday Times, The Times, and The Irish Times.

In 2008, he co-founded the Irish Film Festival in Moscow, which ran for eleven years and held events in multiple Russian cities.

=== Russian television incident ===
In August 2015, O'Reilly appeared live on Russian state television to discuss Moscow Never Sleeps. During the interview, he described Ukrainian filmmaker Oleg Sentsov as a political prisoner, after which the broadcast was cut short. [ref: Russian TV Cuts Away After Irish Director Backs Jailed Ukrainian Filmmaker Oleg Sentsov, The Hollywood Reporter] [ref: Russian TV cuts off Irish director after backing jailed filmmaker, The Irish Times]

data.title: Lawrence Chamurwa Mudzinganyama
data.text:
Lawrence Chamurwa Mudzinganyama is a Zimbabwean-born businessman who has businesses in South Africa. He made headlines after appering on a viral video threatening to kill women at a restaurant after they rejected his romance advances. [ref: Is 'abusive' Zim businessman in SA legally? Man arrested as police minister joins calls for probes, The Citizen] [ref: ] [ref: Zimbabwean businessman arrested after viral Sandton restaurant threats, African Insider]

== Vlamo resturant incident ==
Mudzinganyama is a businessman in South Africa who is the founder of Moriel Infrastructure Group. [ref: Zimbabwean businessman under fire: Sanral probe ordered after viral Sandton restaurant threat, bnknews.co.za] His company has a tender with SANRAL.On September 18, 2026, Mudzinganyama was filmed at Vlamo Restaurant in Sandton Gate, Johannesburg, threatening to kill the women who had rejected his romantic advances. [ref: Vlamo opens criminal case, adds 'visible security' after viral threat video, The Citizen] In the video, which is circulating on the internet and social media, Mudzinganuyama could be heard shouting:“I could put a bullet in you now. I do not play. I will murder you now and walk.” He also went on to say, "I'm a wealthy man. You guys are poor ladies. “You’re a cheap b***h and you will remain that.”. [ref: SA govt probes Zimbabwe born businessman Mudzinganyama 's source of wealth, awarding of multi-million rand state contracts, Express Mail Zim] [ref: South Africa's road agency instructed to investigate Zimbabwean businessman who threatened women with ‘bullets’ after ‘being rejected’, NewZimbabwe.com] Mudzinganyama also told the women that he was the owner of the restaurant.

== Aftermath ==
After the incident, the restaurant opened a case against Mudzinganyama and denied his claims of being the owner or part of its management. The women in the viral video also opened a case of intimidation, and the suspect is expected to appear in court on 01 October 2026. [ref: https://news.pindula.co.zw/2026/09/20/zimbabwean-businessman-under-scrutiny-in-sa-after-threatening-to-kill-women-in-restaurant/?amp=1]

South Africans called for Mudzinganyama to be investigated and also as to how his company got to get tenders, as he was a Zimbabwean. His immigrant status was also called to be investigated. [ref: Is 'abusive' Zim businessman in SA legally? Man arrested as police minister joins calls for probes, The Citizen] SANRAL issued a statement and is investigating Mudzinganyama for his conduct. [ref: Caught on camera: the threat that triggered a SANRAL probe (Video), The South African] [ref: Transport Minister Orders Probe Into Contractor After Viral Sandton Restaurant Incident - Briefly.co.za, briefly.co.za] The Board of Moriel Infrastructure Group has since resolved to terminate its association with Mudzinganyama. His lease at his residential place in Steyn City was also terminated. [ref: Steyn City to Sun City? Lawrence Mudzinganyama's lease TERMINATED, The South African]

Mudzinganyama has issued an apology and has appeared in court on charges of intimidation in October 2026, where he received bail of R15 000. [ref: Man says sorry after threat against women at Sandton restaurant goes viral, Sowetan] [ref: ‘Wealthy man’ apologises for threatening to ‘put a bullet in the head’ of young women] [ref: Zimbabwean businessman ‘sorry’ for threatening to murder women at South African restaurant, NewZimbabwe.com] [ref: Mudzinganyama granted R15 000 bail as NPA warns more charges possible, Mail & Guardian] [ref: Businessman Lawrence Mudzinganyama’s bathroom rage case on hold for trial preparation, News24] Mudzinganyama faces 10 charges, including fraud, intimidation, criminal injuria, and assault with intent to grievously bodily harm. [ref: South African prosecutors lay 10 charges against Zimbabwean businessman after threats to kill women in Sandton, NewZimbabwe.com]

data.title: Sharky Laguana
data.text:
----

Sharky Laguana (born 1970) is an American musician and entrepreneur based in San Francisco, California. He is founding member of the indie rock band Creeper Lagoon, founder of the van rental company, Bandago. [ref: He Survived the ‘Knife Fight’ of SF Politics. What’s Sharky Laguana’s Next Act?, The San Francisco Standard] [ref: Sharky Laguana profile, City and County of San Francisco]

== Early life ==
Laguana was born in 1970. He spent part of his childhood as a foster youth, and experienced periods of homelessness as a young adult, [ref: SF homelessness advisor has first-hand experience with life on the street - CBS San Francisco, www.cbsnews.com] living in single-room occupancy hotels and working as a street performer in San Francisco. He later credited these experiences with shaping his later public service work. [ref: From street performer and ‘drifter’ to small business champion, San Francisco Examiner]

== Music career ==
In the mid-1990s, Laguana co-founded the indie rock band Creeper Lagoon in San Francisco. He played multiple instruments and contributed to the band's songwriting. Creeper Lagoon released two studio albums: I Become Small and Go (1998) on the Dust Brothers' NickelBag label, and Take Back the Universe and Give Me Yesterday (2001) on DreamWorks Records. [ref: Tonight Was Fun: The Quiet Odyssey of Creeper Lagoon, Under the Radar Magazine] The band received a Spin magazine Best New Artist award in 1998. [ref: 40 minutes to fame at Texas music fest, SFGATE] Their music appeared in films including Orange County, Vanilla Sky, and Hellboy, and in the television series The Sopranos. [ref: Sharky Laguana: Creeper Lagoon reunion 'feels right', Pass The Aux]

== Business career ==
Following the end of Creeper Lagoon, Laguana founded Bandago in 2003, [ref: Luxe van rental business Bandago makes sure all customers get the rock star experience, www.bizjournals.com] a van rental company marketed toward touring musicians. [ref: Bandago: Rock Star Van Rental, Forbes] The company expanded to U.S. locations and later transitioned to employee ownership in 2023. [ref: Bandago, Bandago]

He was also elected as president of American car rental association (ACRA) in 2020. [ref: Sharky Laguana – American Car Rental Assocation] [ref: ]

== Public service ==
In 2018, after a series of rental van thefts from his company. Liguana posted about thefts, [ref: SF man’s tweetstorm over stolen van leads to new state law, San Francisco Chronicle] lawmakers introduced AB 2620, which allowed rental companies to use GPS tracking to recover stolen vehicles under certain conditions. [ref: Can GPS tracking stop customers from stealing rental cars? In California, a new debate over privacy begins., The Washington Post] [ref: Twitter tale of SF van theft gets elected officials’ attention, San Francisco Chronicle]

Laguana was appointed to the San Francisco Small Business Commission in 2019 and served as its president from 2020 to 2022. During his tenure, he contributed drafting the city's Venue Recovery Fund, established in 2020 to support music and entertainment venues affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. He advocated for Proposition H [ref: He Survived the ‘Knife Fight’ of SF Politics. What’s Sharky Laguana’s Next Act?, The San Francisco Standard], a 2020 ballot measure make it easy for small businesses and community-serving organizations to operate in San Francisco, the “First Year Free” program that waived fees for new small businesses. [ref: SF Supervisor Proposes Pilot Program That Waives City Fees for New Small Businesses, NBC Bay Area]

In 2023, Laguana was appointed to the San Francisco Homeless Oversight Commission. [ref: Think you can solve SF’s homelessness crisis? Give it a try, The San Francisco Standard] [ref: New San Francisco study looks at data about homelessness with a different approach - CBS San Francisco, www.cbsnews.com]

== Personal life ==
Laguana lives in San Francisco. In 2000 He married Naomi Putterman; they have two sons. He has discussed his past experiences with homelessness and foster care in interviews and public appearances. [ref: Twitter tale of SF van theft gets elected officials' attention, San Francisco Chronicle]

data.title: Pass Logistics
data.text:
== Pass Logistics==
Pass Logistics is a British transport and logistics business based in Doncaster, South Yorkshire. Its services include road haulage, same day transport, warehousing and distribution.

The business developed from ParcelPass Transport Ltd, which was launched by Adrian Sullivan in 2017. [ref: Doncaster logistics firm scoops prestigious top prize at London business awards, Doncaster Free Press] The company was rebranded as Pass Logistics in 2020 alongside an acquisition of their logistics hub in Harworth, Nottinghamshire.

== History ==
Adrian Sullivan founded ParcelPass Transport Ltd in 2017 after previously working in the electrical wholesale industry. An independent profile published in 2022 reported that the business began with one van and £1,500 and subsequently developed into a multi-site logistics operation. [ref: #DNBusinessTalks – Adrian Sullivan (Owner – Pass Logistics), Be More]

Pass Logistics was incorporated as a private limited company on 17 December 2020. Companies House lists its registered office at Suite 7, Spinner Point, Lakeside Boulevard, Doncaster. [ref: Adrian James SULLIVAN personal appointments - Find and update company information - GOV.UK, find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk]

In November 2024, Pass Logistics received the Customer Experience and Loyalty Award in the medium or large business category at the Growing Business Awards. The result was reported by the Doncaster Free Press and Business Doncaster. The same coverage reported the business had previously received the Start Up Business of the Year at the 2018 Doncaster Chamber Business Awards and the SME Business of the Year Award in 2022. [ref: Doncaster logistics firm scoops prestigious top prize at London business awards, Doncaster Free Press]

In March 2025, the company added twelve DAF XF tractor units to their fleet through contract-hire and rental agreements with Fraikin. At the time, industry publication Commercial Motor reported that the vehicles formed part of a program concerning the companies fleet of 18 trucks. [ref: A dozen new DAF XF tractor units for Pass Logistics, www.commercialmotor.com]

In September 2026, Pass Logistics acquired additional warehousing in Carcroft, Doncaster to support growing demand.

== Operations ==
Pass Logistics is a leading provider of transportation, warehousing and logistics services, serving clients across multiple sectors including retail, manufacturing and e-commerce. Known for its innovative approach to logistics solutions and its commitment to sustainability, Pass Logistics has grown rapidly in recent years, establishing a strong presence across the UK and beyond from its Doncaster base. [ref: Pass Logistics confirmed as Doncaster Rovers shirt sponsor, Yorkshire Post]

Pass Logistics provides transport, warehousing and logistics services. Reporting by Business Doncaster states that the company serves corporate and logistics customers in the United Kingdom and Europe. [ref: Doncaster logistics business scoops prestigious top prize at London business awards, Invest Doncaster]

== Doncaster Rovers Sponsorship ==
In December 2024, Pass Logistics entered a two-year agreement to become the front-of-shirt sponsor of Doncaster Rovers FC beginning with the 2025/26 season. The agreement covered the 2025/26 and 2026/27 EFL League One seasons.

Bdaily reported that the agreement followed an earlier relationship between the company and the club that began in 2023 when Pass Logistics sponsored the North Stand at the Club Doncaster Sports Village Stadium. The sponsorship announcement was also covered by The Yorkshire Post. [ref: Pass Logistics named Doncaster Rovers sponsor, Bdaily Business News]

Six HGV tractor units introduced in 2025 were given the names of former Doncaster Rovers legends [ref: PASS LOGISTICS TURNS TO FRAIKIN FOR THE FIRST TIME WITH BESPOKE CONTRACT HIRE AND RENTAL PACKAGE, Fraikin] as part of a campaign run by Pass Logistics' Marketing Manager, Harvey Travis. Trucks named include: Alick Jeffery, Billy Sharp, Brian Stock, Colin Douglas, Francis Tierney and James Coppinger.

== Community Activities ==

==== PassTheParcel ====
Pass Logistics supported the PassTheParcel Christmas donation campaign in partnership with Doncaster Rovers FC and Club Doncaster Foundation.

In December 2025, Doncaster Rovers reported that the campaign was collecting presents for children, as well as food and hygiene products for local food banks. The club stated that the campaign delivered presents to organisations including the children's ward at Doncaster Royal Infirmary, Foster for Doncaster and the Bluebell Wood Children's Hospice. [ref: www.doncasterroversfc.co.uk]

The 2025 campaign utilised Pass Logistics HGV's to support the collection and distribution operation.

Pass Logistics were recognised for their efforts as they were named finalist of Campaign of The Year at the 2026 Doncaster Business Awards.

==== Harworth Colliery FC ====
In 2025, Pass Logistics became front-of-shirt sponsor of Harworth Colliery FC's away kit under a sponsorship agreement covering the 2025/27 and 2026/27 seasons. Public statements from Pass Logistics noted the company's connection to the Harworth area through its warehousing operations and employees with linked to football club and community.

The sponsorship forms part of the company's wider involvement in local sports within South Yorkshire. Harworth Colliery FC also lists Pass Logistics among its club sponsors. [ref: Links, www.pitchero.com]

data.title: Paul Woodward (filmmaker)
data.text:
Paul Woodward is an actor, producer, writer and director from Skelmersdale, Lancashire, North West England. In 2019 he co-founded Old Swan Films alongside his best friend, producer, director and writer, Thomas Elliott Griffiths. Together they created the feature documentary The Little Things which gained global distribution through Buffalo 8 on Amazon Prime. The Little Things takes you on a journey through the doors of a UK children's hospice showing you the love hope and beauty within. Paul became a Patron of Derian House after producing this documentary and is now a spokesperson for the media organisation HEARD when it comes to child palliative care. [ref: A local dad behind an acclaimed Amazon Prime documentary becomes patron of the children's hospice that cared for his son, Wigan Today]

== Early life and education ==
Paul went to Latham high school in Skelmersdale and then attended Wigan and Leigh College where he studied electrical engineering. It was a year later that he decided drama would be his chosen path so he switched to St Helens College to study theatre performance and then eventually gained a degree under the University of Central Lancashire UCLAN. Early is his acting career, Paul starred in two British independent feature films The Treasure of Albion 2006 and The School that Roared in 2009. Those films were produced by the co-operative British film Academy or the BYFA. [ref: Paul Woodward, Derian House Children's Hospice]

Paul stepped away from the creative industries for several years to care for his son who needed 24/7 care at the time. In 2017, Paul decided to join the Academy of Live and Recorded Arts ALRA in Wigan, where he gained a masters in professional acting, this was the start of his journey creating Old Swan Films.

== Career ==
Early in his career, Paul cut his teeth in many disciplines from cabaret to UK stage tours and short films, after gaining his master’s in 2018 he created Old Swan Films with Thomas Elliott Griffiths. Old Swan Films is a Liverpool based film production company, the pair often work on socially impactful films and also work towards developing talent behind the camera.

In 2025 Paul produced The Little Things feature documentary which was directed by Thomas Elliott Griffiths and saw multi-BAFTA winning actor and writer Steve Pemberton joint as an executive Producer. The film was created from Paul's own experience after his son attended Derian House Children's Hospice for several years. The film was picked up by American distribution company Buffalo 8 and then was globally released on Amazon Prime. In early 2026 Paul then produced and directed Voice Again an 18 minute documentary which was in support of other father's who had lost a child, as-well as men's mental health charities, this short documentary took Paul to the BBC morning sofa.

Paul also produced the satirical feminist thriller Time to Go which was directed by Thomas Elliott Griffiths this film was in support of RASA Merseyside, a sexual abuse charity. The film has gone on to win multiple awards and be seen on the film festival circuit across the UK. Paul also had a support role in the film. [ref: Thomas Elliott Griffiths, Edge Hill University]

== Advocacy and philanthropy ==
Paul was made a patron of Derian House Children's Hospice after creating The Little Things, it is very much a place close to his heart as his son spent several years at the hospice before passing away in 2019. This experience has inspired much of his documentary work to date and Paul continues to look for powerful stories to tell. [ref: BBC News] [ref: BBC News]

Since becoming a Patron, Paul has had many opportunities to speak and share his work at major health events across the country, early in 2026 Paul was able to show The Little Things at the 2026 Royal College of Nursing annual conference in Liverpool. [ref: Derian House documentary moves healthcare workers to tears, Lancashire Telegraph]

There was also a special screening by Hospice UK at the Everyman Cinema at Kings Cross, London in September 2026. [ref: Derian House documentary screened at London cinema, Lancashire Telegraph]

In June 2026, during Children’s Hospice Week and in partnership with Together for short Lives, Paul gave a speech at the All-Party Parliamentary Group (APPG) in Westminster and spoke about the vital need for more funding for our UK children's hospices. [ref: Paul’s story: Our most precious moments, Together for Short Lives]

data.title: EuroNatur
data.text:
EuroNatur is a German foundation based in Radolfzell that supports nature conservation projects in Europe. The foundation was established in 1987 by Bund für Umwelt und Naturschutz Deutschland (BUND), Environmental Action Germany (DUH) and Naturschutzbund Deutschland (NABU). EuroNatur is a member of the Deutschen Naturschutzring.

== Mission ==
The foundation's mission is to protect Europe's diverse natural heritage. Its projects focus on wild animals such as wolves, brown bears, lynxes and endangered migratory birds, as well as valuable natural and cultural sites. The foundation's motto is “connecting nature and people”, which reflects its belief that restoring nature, conserving wildlife and improving biodiversity are fundamental to human quality of life. Working with local people helps ensure the long-term success of their projects to protect endangered animals and their habitats in Europe.

EuroNatur is heavily involved with the European Green Belt initiative, a collaborative cross-border project which aims to create a wild, biodiverse corridor along the route of the former Iron Curtain. Since 2004, EuroNatur has coordinated the conservation efforts along the Balkan Green Belt, the southernmost section of the European Green Belt. [ref: EGB: Home, www.europeangreenbelt.org]

== Operations and administration ==
The foundation works with scientists, conservationists, farmers, politicians and entrepreneurs from across Europe. A key part of the foundation’s work takes place in the Balkans, for which they work with local conservationists and volunteers to plan and establish a large network of nature reserves, along with species conservation projects for wolves, bears, lynxes and migratory birds based on scientific research. EuroNatur organises workshops, seminars and training programmes to share knowledge and experiences that help protect Europe’s wild animals. EuroNatur also engages in political lobbying in EU institutions.

EuroNatur's first president was Claus-Peter Hutter, followed by Hartmut Vogtmann between January 2008 and early July 2011. Christel Schroeder served from October 2011 to the end of 2019, and Thomas Potthast has been president since 1 January 2020. Gabriel Schwaderer is the executive director of EuroNatur. [ref: Gabriel Schwaderer, EuroNatur]

== Funding ==
The foundation is funded through donations, third-party funding and income from foundation capital. EuroNatur has been awarded the DZI Donation Seal by the German Central Institute for Social Issues (DZI).

== European Stork Villages ==
The European Stork Village network was set up by EuroNatur in 1994 as a way of publicly recognising communities across Europe that are making a significant contribution to protecting their local white stork populations. Representatives from each of the Stork Villages meet every year in one of the member villages to discuss and develop solutions for the conservation of white storks. There are currently 16 recognised European Stork Villages. [ref: “European Stork Villages” initiative, EuroNatur]

The most recent village to be recognised and added to the network was Knepp Wildland and Storrington in 2025, the first and only Stork Village in the UK. [ref: European Stork Villages Network, White Stork Project] The village was honoured in recognition of its conservation and rewilding programme which led to the return of the white stork to the area. The village of Storrington holds its White Stork and Nature Festival each year to celebrate its conservation efforts and the return of its white stork population.

== Awards ==
The foundation has been running its EuroNatur Award since 1992. [ref: Award for Environmental Excellence, EuroNatur]

EuroNatur runs an annual photography competition called European Treasures of Nature in partnership with the NaturVision film festival, Natur magazine and German utility company Gelsenwasser. The winning entries are displayed in a year-long touring exhibition titled Fascinating Nature and featured in the next year's EuroNatur calendar. [ref: European Treasures of Nature, EuroNatur]

data.title: Unciv
data.text:
Unciv is a free and open source 4X strategy game based heavily on Civilization V. Developed by Yair Morgenstern, it tries to incorporate every feature of the original game under the libGDX framework and aims to be small and moddable with low hardware requirements. [ref: Unciv is a free, open-source take on Civilization 5 that's coming to Steam, Rock, Paper, Shotgun] The gameplay will be exactly like Civilization V, [ref: Fans basteln kostenloses Remake von Civilization 5 für PC und Android, GameStar] but it does not recreate the soundtrack, graphics, or animation. [ref: Unciv the open source remake of Civilization V is heading to Steam, GamingOnLinux] The game is available on Windows, macOS, Android, and Linux, and through itch.io, but while it was planned to be released on Steam, [ref: Free Alternative to Civilization 5 Coming Soon to Steam, Gamepressure.com] it was removed because the platform did not want to handle potential legal issues. [ref: ]

It has a multiplayer mode using Dropbox for gameplay synchronization, and the game uses a 2D style that can be edited with asset packs. Frequent updates are published. There are no microtransactions and the developer does not accept donations. [ref: Wirklich Free2Play: 44 kostenlose PC-Spiele ohne Echtgeldkäufe 2023, GameStar]

As of 2023, all of Civilization V's game mechanics up to Gods & Kings expansion, except espionage, have been reimplemented.

data.title: Avid Interplay
data.text:
Avid Interplay is a media asset management system developed by Avid Technology for the Microsoft Windows platform [ref: https://resources.avid.com/SupportFiles/attach/InterplayEngineInstallGuide_v1_0.pdf], designed for video and audio post-production workflows. Interplay is generally regarded as the first nonlinear "Workflow Engine" [ref: https://digitalproduction.com/2006/04/25/nab-avid-nonlinear-workflow-engine-und-viel-mehr/]. The main two components are Interplay Engine, the backend, and Interplay Access, which serves as the client that assets are accessed through.

== Features ==
Interplay's main features are:
* Management and organization of media assets
* Native integration with Avid Media Composer and Pro Tools for easy asset access
* Asset transcoding (Interplay Transcode)
* Tape ingest (Interplay Low-Res Encode)
* Archives management with low-resolution proxy generation (Interplay Archive)
* Asset transfers over WAN (Interplay Transfer)

== Initial release ==

Avid Interplay was released and presented at NAB 2006 [ref: https://digitalproduction.com/2006/10/02/avid-interplay-verfuegbar/], with a starting price of €16,700, depending on configuration.

data.title: Birger Corleis
data.text:
Birger Corleis (20 October 1955 in Harsefeld-30 October 2012 at the same place) was a musician and a musical educator. He was most known for being one of the vocalists of Modern Talking forming the falsetto parts and singing the chorus of the song "There's too much blue in missing you". He has worked for artists like Rolf Köhler, Mary Roos and Taco. He has played in bands like Springflut, Straightflush, Junkband, Me & The Duckdivers and Kentucky.

==Early Life==
Birger Corleis was born and grew up in Harsefeld in Lower Saxony. In his youth he played in diffrent school bands. After his youth he studied to become a typesetter. [ref: Birger Corleis – early life]

==Career==
After his studies he devoted entirely to his music career. From the mid 1970s till the early 1990s he played in diffrent bands as a singer, bassist or guitarist. He played in bands such as Straight Flush, Springflut and Junkband. He also played in the band Kentucky. Kentucky was a popular live cover band in Germany. [ref: Birger Corleis with Kentucky] Together with Walter Vagts he wrote "Back in the highlands" for Rolf Köhler under his pseudonym "Marc De Ville" in 1978. In 1984 together with Rolf and Michael Scholz he created the band Straight Flush and released the single "Dancing In The Sunlight". Later he would create the band Junkband with Michael Scholz. He was also in the band Springflut together with Rolf, Michael and Detlef Wiedeke. [ref: The discography of Birger Corleis]

From 1984 till 1987 Corleis sang the and falsetto vocals for Modern Talking together with Köhler Scholz and Wiedeke. The falsettos became a iconic part of the sound of Modern Talking. Dieter Bohlen pretended to sing them in videos and concerts. Corleis also sang the chorus of "There's Too Much Blue In Missing You" in which Bohlen sang the verses. This only got revealed in 2001, due to some legal disputes with Dieter Bohlen. [ref: The real voices behind Modern Talking]
Modern Talking would sell 65 million records their first era and top the charts in many countries.Notably, Modern Talking were one of the first Western bloc bands sale of whose records was allowed in the Soviet Union. After four decades of Cold War censorship and import restrictions, Chairman Mikhail Gorbachev's glasnost reforms in the USSR in 1986 opened up the Soviet sphere to western bands, including Modern Talking at the height of their popularity. As a result, they have gotten a large, enduring fanbase in Eastern Europe. Other Euro Disco acts that entered the Soviet sphere are Joy, C.C.Catch and Silent Circle. [ref: Die Russen mögen's Anders, Der Spiegel] The Euro Disco acts Bad Boys Blue and Patty Ryan also entered the Soviet sphere and were inspired by Modern Talking. [ref: You're My Heart, You're My Soul vs You're A Woman] Popular tracks from Modern Talking which Corleis sang on were You're My Heart, You're My Soul, Cheri Cheri Lady, You Can Win If You Want, Brother Louie and Atlantis Is Calling (S.O.S. for Love).

He sang backing vocals for Mary Roos's album Leben Spür'n in 1987. He also sang backing vocals for Taco's album Swing Classics: In The Mood Of Glen Miller.

From the mid-1990s onwards, Corleis worked primarily as a musical educator, instructing at various music schools for almost two decades. [ref: Birger Corleis educator]He formed the band Me & The Duckdivers in 2007 with other members. [ref: Me & The Duckdivers]

==Lawsuit against Bohlen==
In 2001 Corleis sued Bohlen claiming he deserved more money for his contibutions to Modern Talking and for using recordings from the old Modern Talking albums for the 1998 album Back For Good Bohlen called it "typical parasitic behaviour" and told him that he would not get a cent. Corleis lost the lawsuit and had to pay the costs of the trial himself. [ref: Lawsuit against Bohlen]

==Death and Legacy==
In 2012 he died 10 days after his 57th birthday. He left behind one daughter. [ref: Death of Corleis] People on the internet started spreading tribute videos about his work. [ref: Tributes]
