data.title: HURR (company)
data.text:
HURR is a UK fashion rental and resale platform founded by Victoria Prew in 2018 [ref: How HURR Became The Go-To Place To Create The Perfect Vacation Wardrobe, Forbes]. The platform supports peer-to-peer rentals between users as well as managed rentals, with garments supplied by fashion brands and retailers. Lauren Roberts is HURR's current CEO after Prew stepped away from her role [ref: Hurr co-founder Victoria Prew steps down as CEO, Drapers].

History

HURR was founded by Victoria Prew in 2018, who said the idea for the company came from the growth of sharing-economy businesses such as Airbnb and Uber. The platform launched during the 2018 Christmas period as a peer-to-peer fashion rental service.

In 2020, HURR opened a rental pop-up at Selfridges in London. The pop-up stocked around 200 garments from brands including Rixo, Ganni, Mara Hoffman and Gucci, that customers could rent for either 4 or 8 days. [ref: Hurr Collective is launching the first in-store wardrobe rental pop-up at Selfridges, The Standard].

HURR later began providing rental services for fashion brands and retailers. In 2021, the company developed a white-label service called HURR Enterprise where retailers could operate rental services under their own brands. Selfridges Rental was an early client of the service

Forbes included founder Victoria Prew in its 30 Under 30 list and in 2021, HURR was named among the world's top 50 retail technology start-ups [ref: HURR: The Tech Start-Up Leading The UK’s Fashion Rental Revolution, Forbes]. The company has also received venture capital investment as part of its growth within this industry (fashion technology and circular fashion) [ref: Leading UK fashion rental platform HURR joins our portfolio, Praetura Ventures]. They secured £7.9m in a fundraising round led by Praetura Ventures [ref: Hurr secures $10m in funding, Drapers].

By 2022, HURR was working with more than 130 fashion brands and operating rental services for retailers including Selfridges, John Lewis and Matches Fashion [ref: ‘It’s more sustainable – and I still get to wear something new every weekend’: how rental fashion became big business, The Guardian]. In the same year, the company became the first fashion rental platform to achieve B Corporation certification [ref: Hurr co-founder Victoria Prew steps down as CEO, Drapers].

Business Model

HURR operates a fashion rental marketplace with brands such as Fendi, Ganni and The Row having been listed as available to rent through the platform [ref: 20 pledges for 2020: Renting clothes could be the trick to help me curb my fast fashion habits, Independent].

The company offers peer-to-peer (P2P) rentals, where users can rent their clothing directly to other users, and managed rentals, where stock is supplied by fashion brands and partners. Customers can rent items for 4, 8, 16 or 30-day options [ref: Hurr launches bundle rental service, Drapers].

In May 2024, HURR Flex launched, a credit-based rental service. Customers can purchase bundles of rental credits to use on items available through the marketplace by spending £99 for £170 credit points or £125 for £225 [ref: Hurr launches bundle rental service, Drapers].

Alongside P2P rentals, HURR provides rental services to fashion brands and retailers through HURR Enterprise. The service allows brands to operate rental platforms under their own branding, with HURR providing the technology and operational services.

HURR launched a resale service in 2023 where users could make offers to purchase garments listed on the platform [ref: Rental platform Hurr launches resale, Drapers].

Partnerships

Vogue has reported that HURR works with more than 100 brands and retailers. Its retail partnerships have included Selfridges, John Lewis, Matches Fashion and Flannels [ref: The 6 Best Fashion Rental Sites In The UK, British Vogue].

In 2023, HURR partnered with Depop to launch “The Loop by HURR”, where the collection consisted of previously rented garments offered for resale. In the same year, Net-a-Porter also launched its first rental edit on the platform [ref: Net-A-Porter debuts rental collection with By Rotation and Hurr, Drapers].

In November 2024, HURR partnered with Deliveroo on a rental delivery service within central London where customers could receive their rental orders in under 20 minutes by bike couriers [ref: HURR teams up with Deliveroo to deliver dresses in just 20 minutes, The Industry Fashion] [ref: Hurr taps Deliveroo for same-day fashion rental delivery, Drapers].

Reaction and Impact

A HURR user has earned more than £100 000 from renting clothing through the platform after starting to list items in 2021 [ref: How fashion became the go-to side hustle for working mothers, Bazaar].

In October 2026, HURR partnered with Sky to allow customers to rent original designer pieces worn by Sienna Miller and other cast members in the drama series, War [ref: Want to Dress Like Sienna Miller in the New Sky Series ‘War’? Hurr Rentals Can Make It Happen, WWD].

data.title: TREE Innovative Foundation
data.text:
TREE Innovative Foundation (TREEI) is a not-for-profit company based in Pune, Maharashtra, India. It was founded in 2018 by mechanical engineer Tanveer Inamdar. [ref: Taking Electricity, Wherever They Go: Engineer's Portable Solar Units Power Huts of Tribal Migrants in Maharashtra, The Better India] The organisation works in Pune city and Pune district on clean energy, school education, women's livelihoods and health, nutrition and river restoration. [ref: About TREE Innovative Foundation, TREE Innovative Foundation] Its best-known project, Mission Urja, installs solar power systems in tribal hamlets that are not connected to the electricity grid, and since 2025 has installed solar lighting and CCTV cameras at hill forts in the Sahyadri. [ref: Forgotten Pune forts set to be solar-lit in effort to illuminate history, The Indian Express]

== History ==
Inamdar started the organisation in 2018 after working for multinational companies. The name TREE stands for "Technology Reuse Environment Empowerment". [ref: Neer Chakra helps rural women in fetching water, The Bridge Chronicle] It was formally registered in 2019 and was incorporated as a Section 8 company under the Companies Act, 2013 in 2023. [ref: Company master data: TREE Innovative Foundation (CIN U72200PN2023NPL220779), Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India]

Its first project was the Neer Chakra, a three-wheeled cart for carrying water over hilly ground. The cart holds 80 litres and has a filter and a tap. After a pilot in May 2019, carts were given to 25 families in Zhende Wadi, a village about 30 km from Pune, in August 2019. According to Inamdar, the water project showed that many of the same villages had no electricity, which led to Mission Urja in 2022.

The organisation started a school programme, Program Dhruv, in 2020. A river restoration programme and an integrated village development programme followed in 2026. [ref: Program DHARA, TREE Innovative Foundation]

== Programmes ==

=== Mission Urja ===
Mission Urja works mainly with the Katkari community in Haveli, Maval and Mulshi talukas of Pune district. [ref: Mission URJA: Village Edition, TREE Innovative Foundation] It uses two types of system: centralised solar installations of 15–20 kW that supply huts through individual meters, and portable foldable solar units of about 3 kg for migrant families without permanent homes. Small hydroelectric units are used where streams allow.

Each village forms a committee of three men and two women to manage its system. Households pay 10–50 a month into the committee's bank account to cover maintenance after the five-year equipment warranty, and local young people are trained to maintain the equipment.

In November 2024 the organisation began a project with Netcracker Technology and the Imerys group to supply solar and hydroelectric power to three Katkari villages, starting at Velvani. [ref: Mission Urja: TREEI Foundation's Green Power Initiative Reaches Underserved Villages, The Bridge Chronicle] The Better India reported in October 2025 that the programme had reached 945 households. [ref: Diwali Special: How 7 Indians Are Lighting Up Villages Across India With Solar, The Better India] The Marathi daily Sakal covered the programme in March 2026. [ref: Mission Urja Project: दुर्गम आदिवासी पाड्यांत सौरऊर्जेचा उजेड, Sakal] The organisation reported 41 villages and 1,398 households electrified, with 1,432 kW installed, as of 2026. [ref: Our Programs, TREE Innovative Foundation]

=== Hill forts ===
In April 2025 the organisation announced plans to light hill forts in Pune district that are not maintained by the state, starting with Tikona and Ghangad. The plan included solar street lights, floodlights, solar-powered CCTV cameras with footage shared with local police, and mobile charging points for trekkers. The organisation lists Tikona and Sudhagad as completed, with work under way at about ten other forts. [ref: Mission URJA: Fort Edition, TREE Innovative Foundation] In October 2026 Marathi newspapers reported that solar lighting and eight CCTV cameras had been installed at Asherigad. [ref: अशेरी गडावर सौर दिव्यांचा प्रकाश: सुरक्षेलाही बळकटी; आठ सीसीटीव्ही कॅमेऱ्यांची नजर, Sakal] [ref: अशेरी गडाच्या संरक्षणासाठी सोलर सीसीटीव्ही आणि एलईडी दिव्यांची सुविधा, Dainik Bhaskar]

=== Education ===
Program Dhruv, started in 2020, runs life-skills, counselling and career sessions for students in classes 5 to 12. According to the organisation, it works in about 80 government and rural schools in Mulshi, Maval, Purandar and Baramati talukas and in Pune city. [ref: Program DHRUV, TREE Innovative Foundation]

=== Women's livelihoods and health ===
Project Eklavya supports women-led small businesses in food processing and crafts. A production unit at Velhe, near Pune, was set up with support from Persistent Foundation; according to Persistent Foundation's 2023–24 annual report, the unit had 55 members and recorded a turnover of 18.94 lakh that year. [ref: 15th Annual Report 2023–24, Persistent Foundation] The same report describes a nutrition project addressing anaemia among women using locally made food. Project Garima provides counselling and support for women.

=== Environment and village development ===
Program Dhara works on the Mula-Mutha River in Pune using interception barriers, aeration, floating wetlands and bank planting. Its first phase, covering four sites in the Pune and Pimpri-Chinchwad municipal areas, was launched on World Rivers Day, 27 September 2026. Program Utthan, started in 2026, combines the organisation's energy, water, education, health and livelihood work in four tribal villages in Mulshi taluka. [ref: Program UTTHAN, TREE Innovative Foundation] Project Sahyog provides relief and other support, such as flood relief and wheelchair distribution.

== Organisation ==
The organisation is led by Tanveer Inamdar as managing director, with Tamanna Inamdar as co-founder and advisory director. It is registered for corporate social responsibility funding with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and under sections 12A and 80G of the Income Tax Act, 1961. Companies that have funded its projects include Netcracker Technology, Imerys and Persistent Foundation.

data.title: Kids Renee Show
data.text:
----

== Kids Renee Show ==
Kids Renee Show (/kɪdz ˈɹɛni ʃoʊ/ [ref: ], stylised as Kids Renee Show) is a children's YouTube [ref: ]channel owned by FIGPPE Entertainment [ref: HOME -, kidsreneeshow.com], a subsidiary of FIGPPE Holdings [ref: Figppe Holdings Ltd - Company Profile - Endole, open.endole.co.uk]. Created by Ada Prior, the channel features children's songs [ref: ], nursery rhymes [ref: ], 3D animated videos [ref: ] and educational entertainment for toddlers and preschoolers.

== History ==
The YouTube [ref: Kids Renee Show, YouTube]channel launched on September 2024, following the birth of Prior's daughter. Initially, it was created as a way for Prior to keep her personal YouTube recommendations separate from baby songs and children's content. However, after noticing limited representation of Black [ref: ] mothers [ref: ], white [ref: ] fathers [ref: ] and their biracial children [ref: ] in children's cartoons [ref: ] [ref: ], Prior identified an opportunity to create content that reflected her own family. She wanted her daughter to see characters and family relationships that resembled her own experiences.

In March 2026, Prior began publishing original songs, videos and animated children's content under the Kids Renee Show name. The channel aims to combine early learning, music [ref: Kids Renee Show Amazon Artist Profile, music.amazon.co.uk], storytelling and family-centred entertainment with an emphasis on diversity and representation.

== Characters ==

* Renée (voiced by Bernadine Chinwe) is the main protagonist of Kids Renee Show. She is an outgoing three-year-old biracial British girl who wears a green dress and green Crocs [ref: ]. She is the eldest of two children in her family.
* Zara (voiced by Edith Pho) is a three-year-old Black British [ref: ] girl who wears a red floral dress, blue leggings and a green rucksack. Her hairstyle features cornrows [ref: ], reflecting the show's representation of Black hairstyles and cultural identity. She enjoys reading stories about Paddington Bear [ref: ].
* Hunter (voiced by Andrew George) is a three-year-old British Indian [ref: ] boy who wears a multicoloured striped shirt, jeans and blue trainers. He enjoys playing with toy trucks.

* Tobias (voiced by Anthony Gert) is a White British [ref: ] boy who wears a blue-and-white striped shirt, jeans and green trainers. He carries a rucksack and enjoys playing with toy dinosaurs [ref: ].

== Music and educational content ==
Kids Renee Show produces children's music [ref: ] and animated educational content aimed primarily at toddlers [ref: ] and preschool [ref: ]-aged children (one to five year olds). Its catalogue includes original songs, nursery rhymes and themed musical releases. By October 2026, its published music catalogue included albums such as Music and Stories [ref: 'Music and Stories' Album on Anghami], featuring nine tracks, and Phonics for Kids [ref: Phonics for Kids Album on amazon], featuring eight tracks. These releases cover a range of subjects, including the alphabet [ref: ], phonics [ref: ], counting [ref: ], animals [ref: ], personal hygiene [ref: ], greetings [ref: ]and early social interaction. The catalogue also includes seasonal music, such as Halloween [ref: ], Easter [ref: ] and Christmas songs [ref: ], alongside songs designed to support everyday learning and routines.

The channel's musical style combines children's music, nursery rhymes, educational pop and playful, rhythm-led songs. Its content uses repetition [ref: ], simple lyrics, memorable melodies and animated storytelling to introduce concepts in an engaging format. Songs can be used by parents, carers and early-years [ref: ] educators as supplementary learning resources to encourage children to sing along, practise new vocabulary [ref: ], recognise letters and numbers [ref: ], explore sounds and participate in movement-based activities.

Kids Renee Show also places an emphasis on cultural diversity [ref: ] and family representation [ref: ] in children's media. Its animated world features a biracial lead character and an interracial family, reflecting the experiences of children growing up in multicultural households. The channel aims to broaden the range of family structures and backgrounds represented in children's entertainment, allowing children from mixed-heritage and interracial families to encounter characters with whom they may identify, while introducing other young viewers to different family experiences.

Through music, recurring characters and familiar everyday situations, the channel seeks to encourage curiosity, language development [ref: ], early numeracy, social interaction and an appreciation of diversity. Its content can complement activities at home and in early-years settings, providing opportunities for shared singing, discussion and play. These are intended educational uses rather than independently verified developmental outcomes.

== Rise in popularity ==
Kids Renee Show increased its online presence following the regular publication of songs and videos beginning in March 2026. By October 2026, the channel had gained approximately 8,000 followers and 1Million Views [ref: Kids Renee Show, YouTube] across its online audience, supported by frequent uploads of children's music [ref: ], nursery rhymes [ref: ] and animated educational content. [ref: ]

One of the channel's popular releases is The Good Morning Train [ref: ], a nursery song designed for circle time [ref: ] and morning routines. The song has attracted approximately 600,000 streams [ref: Good Morning Train], reflecting interest in music that incorporates familiar Montessori [ref: ] preschool activities [ref: ], movement and early learning [ref: ].

The channel's educational content uses British English pronunciation [ref: ] and a British accent, with the aim of exposing young viewers to spoken English through songs, repetition and everyday vocabulary. This approach is intended to support early language exposure, listening skills and pronunciation practice, particularly among children learning English as an additional language.

Cultural diversity is another feature of the channel's music catalogue. Its album Foods Around the World [ref: ] introduces children to foods associated with different cultural traditions, including fufu [ref: ], pie and mash [ref: ], curry, [ref: ] and plantain [ref: ]. By incorporating foods from African [ref: ], Caribbean [ref: ], South Asian [ref: ]and British culinary traditions [ref: ], the project aims to familiarise young audiences with a wider range of cultural experiences through music and children's entertainment.

The channel's content reflects an approach to preschool media [ref: TikTok - Make Your Day, www.tiktok.com] that combines language learning, music and cultural representation. Through regular releases and the inclusion of diverse characters, family backgrounds and everyday experiences, Kids Renee Show seeks to create educational entertainment for children growing up in an increasingly interconnected world.

Clade [ip]b (H5N1)

Nomenclature & Classification

Full Name: H5N1 influenza virus, clade [ip]b

Virus Family: Orthomyxoviridae (influenza)

Genetic Lineage: Emerged from H5N8 (clade [ip]) during 2016–2020 H5N8 outbreak

Timeline

2020: Clade [ip]b first detected; marks beginning of 2020–2026 global outbreak

2020–2023: Rapid global expansion across avian populations

2023–2026: Spillover into mammalian species; expanded ecological range

2024: Detected in Antarctica (Danger Islands penguin deaths)

Geographic Distribution

Primary: Asia, Europe, North America, Africa

Recent: South America, Antarctic region

Status: Pandemic strain; circulating on all inhabited continents

Key Characteristics

Dominance: Primary circulating H5N1 clade globally since 2020

Adaptation: Enhanced capacity to infect diverse bird species and mammals

Severity: High mortality rates in poultry and wild birds; increasing mammalian spillover

Transmission: Primarily via direct contact and contaminated environments; limited human-to-human transmission

Affected Species

Primary: Domestic poultry (chickens, turkeys, ducks); wild waterfowl

Secondary: Penguins, seabirds, marine mammals (seals, sea lions)

Spillover: Terrestrial mammals (minks, foxes, raccoons); occasional human infections

Public Health Impact

Human Cases: Sporadic, rare; limited human-to-human transmission documented

Mortality (Human): High case fatality rate when infections occur (~50%)

Economic: Billions in poultry culling and trade losses

Pandemic Risk: Monitored by WHO; intermediate zoonotic threat (lower than pandemic influenza risk)

Detection & Monitoring

Surveillance: WHO, FAO, OIE coordinate global monitoring

Diagnostics: Reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR) for rapid detection

Genomic Tracking: Continuous sequencing reveals sub-lineage evolution

Current Outbreak Scale (as of October 2026)

Affected Countries: 50+

Poultry Deaths/Culls: Hundreds of millions

Wildlife Deaths: Millions documented (particularly seabirds)

Status: Ongoing endemic circulation in wild populations

Molecular & Genetic Features

Surface Proteins:

Hemagglutinin (HA): H5 subtype; contains multiple basic amino acids at cleavage site (high pathogenicity marker)

Neuraminidase (NA): N1 subtype

Key Mutations: Polybasic cleavage site; N66S and other residues linked to mammalian adaptation

Genetic Stability: Relatively stable compared to seasonal influenza; limited reassortment risk with human seasonal strains

Species-Specific Mortality Rates

Species Mortality Rate Notes

Domestic chickens 90–100% Highly susceptible; rapid spread in flocks

Wild waterfowl 30–70% Variable by species; some tolerance

Penguins 70–90%+ High impact in Antarctica colonies

Humans ~50% Rare infections; high case fatality

Prevention & Control

Culling Operations:

Preemptive and reactive depopulation of infected flocks

Billions of birds culled globally since 2020

Farm quarantine protocols

Equipment disinfection; movement restrictions

Personal protective equipment (PPE) for handlers

Limited intervention; monitoring and surveillance primary strategy

Environmental sampling in high-risk ecosystems

Vaccines:

Human vaccine candidates under development; limited stockpiles available

Veterinary vaccines exist but variable efficacy against [ip]b

Antivirals:

Neuraminidase inhibitors (oseltamivir, zanamivir) effective in vitro; clinical efficacy in human cases variable

Monoclonal antibody treatments in research phase

Status: No specific therapeutic proven highly effective; supportive care primary treatment

Fecal-oral: Primary route in birds (contaminated water, feed, surfaces)

Respiratory droplets: Airborne transmission among closely housed birds

Direct contact: Predation, physical contact between species

Indirect: Contaminated equipment, vehicles, human clothing

data.title: Ouijdane QACAMI
data.text:
Ouijdane Qacami is an entrepreneur, researcher and engineer based in France, of Moroccan origin, whose work focuses on concrete durability. [ref: Remise du Prix Pépite 2025: 30 lauréats, dont cinq alumni, récompensés, Campus France Maroc] She is the founder of Strucmedica, a startup developing non-destructive assessment and predictive maintenance tools for concrete infrastructure. [ref: How Moroccan Engineer Ouijdane Qacami Is Using Technology to ‘Listen’ to Buildings, Morocco World News] Her supplied professional record identifies her as its chief executive officer.

Her work brings together materials research, non-destructive measurement and software-assisted interpretation of structural deterioration. [ref: Entretien avec Ouijdane Qacami: « Il est essentiel de valoriser davantage la présence des femmes dans les métiers techniques et industriels », La Nouvelle Tribune] She was a national Prix Pépite laureate in 2025 and was included in Forbes Afrique’s 30 Under 30 selection in 2026. [ref: Moroccan Engineer Ouijdane Qacami Wins France’s Top Student Innovation Prize, Morocco World News] [ref: La Jeunesse Africaine, Moteur de Transformation, Forbes Afrique]

== Education ==
Her supplied professional record lists mathematics preparatory studies (CPGE) in Morocco and civil-engineering studies at the Mohammadia School of Engineers. She subsequently obtained a civil-engineering qualification at the École nationale des ponts et chaussées. She also undertook parallel master’s-level studies in construction-material durability. [ref: Félicitations à Ouijdane Qacami (CIV 22), Lauréate du Prix National Pépite, Ponts Alumni]

Her supplied qualifications are described as “Master of Engineering (MEng), Civil Engineering” and “Master of Science (MS), Sustainable building materials”, the latter also titled “Sciences des Matériaux pour la Construction Durable”, with Mention Bien.

La Rochelle University identifies her as a member of its 2024–2025 D2E student-entrepreneur cohort. [ref: Deux distinctions pour nos étudiants entrepreneurs !, La Rochelle Université] She pursued an executive programme at HEC Paris alongside doctoral research. The programme is described in her supplied materials as DeepTech Startup Leadership.

Her education also includes climate-resilience studies and entrepreneurship training. The climate-resilience course is identified in her supplied materials as RESCUE at La Rochelle, described as an “International diploma of EU policies and initiatives that support resilience”. Its reported topics include climate risks; EU environmental, energy, maritime and social policies; European cooperation and external partnerships; and tools for societal transformation. Her supplied professional record also lists AI and machine-learning accelerator mentorship through Holcim University.

== Business and engineering career ==
=== Engineering experience ===
Her supplied professional record lists a placement with Marchica Med in Nador Province, contributing to urban development, artificial-beach and road projects, pavement-condition assessment and work in the Atalayoun area. It also lists work with BIOUI Travaux in Oujda on the RP6011 road between Berkane and Saïdia, including roadway dimensioning, pavement works, drainage and sanitation, an access bridge, crossing structures and drinking-water connections.

She undertook a placement with STFA Construction Group on the stability of a caisson breakwater at Nador West Med port. The port work was reported by Morocco World News in December 2025. Her supplied professional record identifies STFA, SGTM and JDN as consortium participants and STFA as her placement employer.

Her supplied professional record lists work at Bouygues Construction in Yvelines on BYFLU calculation software for concrete creep and time-dependent tower behaviour, with an application to Triangle Tower in Paris. It also lists structural modelling and design calculations at Ingérop in Rueil-Malmaison for the HHI building at Hinkley Point C, including work she describes as nuclear-waste storage dimensioning. The record describes the Bouygues and Ingérop roles as permanent-contract positions and the Moroccan placements as internships.

Qacami worked as a research-and-development engineer at the Holcim Innovation Center. Her work at Holcim provided the basis for Strucmedica.

Her supplied professional record describes research-and-development project engineering in Saint-Quentin-Fallavier on concrete durability, carbonation, non-destructive measurement and low-carbon materials. It also lists an end-of-studies placement developing a non-destructive carbonation measurement method alongside engineering and master’s studies, and business-plan development among her professional skills.

=== Strucmedica ===
Qacami reports creating earlier startups before founding Strucmedica. She founded Strucmedica to develop non-invasive assessment of concrete structures and support maintenance, repair and continued use. Her supplied professional record lists a founder and chief executive role in France from 2025.

Qacami describes Strucmedica’s proposed system as combining connected sensors, physical materials models and AI-assisted software to interpret concrete condition and anticipate deterioration. Its intended applications include prioritising repairs, estimating carbon dioxide fixed through carbonation and supporting life-cycle assessment of low-carbon concrete. The proposed users include infrastructure owners, operators, consulting engineers and asset managers.

=== Incubation and startup support ===
Her supplied professional record lists Station F incubation/residence support, more than a year of NEOMA Business School incubator support and NEOMA accelerator participation for Strucmedica. Its reported support network also includes WILLA; Deloitte strategic, legal and innovation support; HEC Paris/HEC Challenge; Campus Innov; Pépite France; SATT Nouvelle-Aquitaine; and Bpifrance.

She also reports startup and technical support from GitHub, AWS, Microsoft, Vercel and Anthropic. Her materials identify La French Tech and Le Coq Créa as ecosystem associations and VentureDays Luxembourg as a waitlist lead.

The GEF Start-up Weekend first-prize package included six months of NEOMA incubation, six months of access to WILLA group workshops, legal and tax support from Deloitte Société d’Avocats and Creative Valley mentoring. [ref: Edition 2025, GEF Start-up Weekend]

== Research ==
=== Doctoral research ===
Qacami conducted doctoral research on concrete durability through collaboration between La Rochelle University, the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology and Holcim Innovation Center. Her supplied professional record lists concurrent contractual research appointments at La Rochelle and KIT’s IMB/MPA/CMM, with work in La Rochelle and Karlsruhe.

La Rochelle University announced a public defence scheduled for 23 June 2026 of her thesis on non-destructive evaluation of carbonation in concrete and low-carbon systems through flux measurement. The notice names Abdelkarim Aït-Mokhtar as thesis director, Frank Dehn as co-director and Philippe Turcry as co-supervisor, within joint doctoral supervision with KIT. [ref: Avis de Soutenance: Madame Ouijdane QACAMI, La Rochelle Université]

Her professional description uses “PhD” for the research experience and describes her as a PhD engineer and expert in concrete durability, non-destructive assessment and predictive infrastructure maintenance.

=== Concrete carbonation ===
Qacami is the first author of a paper published in Materials and Structures in 2026 proposing a non-destructive method for assessing concrete carbonation. The Carbonation Flux Test measures carbon dioxide flux using a sealed cell on the concrete surface. The paper reports numerical and experimental testing on low-clinker concrete mixtures and identifies cell sealing as an area for further improvement. [ref: Non-destructive assessment of concrete carbonation based on the CO2 diffusion resistance factor, Materials and Structures]

The paper lists affiliations with Holcim Innovation Center, KIT and La Rochelle’s LaSIE laboratory (CNRS UMR 7356). Co-authors are Bruno Huet, Philippe Turcry, Abdelkarim Aït-Mokhtar, Ravi Ajitbhai Patel and Frank Dehn. Her research also addresses CO₂ transport, carbonation-related uptake and environmental assessment of low-clinker materials.

=== Publications and conferences ===
Qacami’s verified publications and conference records include:
* “Non-destructive assessment of concrete carbonation based on the CO₂ diffusion resistance factor” (2026), a journal article in Materials and Structures, volume 59, article 160.
* “Diffusive method for measuring carbonation properties of concrete under natural laboratory conditions” (2025), a proceedings paper in the fib International Symposium on Concrete Structures in Antibes, pp. 1968–1979. [ref: Diffusive method for measuring carbonation properties of concrete under natural laboratory conditions, KITopen]
* “Numerical study and inverse analysis of a non distructive measurement method for oxygen diffusivity in partially carbonated concrete” (2023), an oral-contribution record and abstract for the Journées d’Etudes des Milieux Poreux (JEMP), with Qacami, Bruno Huet, Philippe Turcry, Abdelkarim Aït-Mokhtar, Ravi Ajitbhai Patel and Frank Dehn listed as authors. [ref: Numerical study and inverse analysis of a non distructive measurement method for oxygen diffusivity in partially carbonated concrete, 16e Journées d’Etudes des Milieux Poreux (JEMP 2023)]

Her supplied research materials list additional conference contributions including “Field evaluation of oxygen diffusion in partially carbonated concrete by numerical calculation” at AUGC–CFGC 2023; “Validation of a non-destructive method for assessing instantaneous carbonation of coated concrete” at the 78th RILEM Annual Week in 2024; and “Assessing CO₂ uptake by cementitious materials for life cycle analysis: flux measurement and thermogravimetric analysis” at ICSBM 2025. The RILEM presentation was also reported by Morocco World News. She reports three fib contributions overall, of which two additional citations remain unidentified.

Her other reported research works include “Non destructive diffusive method for assessing carbonation: influencing factors”; “Evaluating carbonation and CO₂ uptake in low-clinker cementitious concretes through flux testing and conventional methods”; “Experimental study of hygroscopic and gas transport properties of calcined clay and portland concretes under carbonation and curing effects”; “Experimental based modeling of moisture transport in partially carbonated low-carbon concrete under wetting drying cycles”; and “Impact of wetting drying cycles on CO₂ flux and diffusive properties evolution in concrete: comparative study under natural and controlled conditions for low-carbon concretes”. Publication and acceptance status for these works remain unverified.

Qacami is listed in her supplied event materials as a Tech&Fest 2026 speaker and in Meet & Fabrik/i-Factory coverage in Tribune de Lyon. Strucmedica is also listed as a 2026 Viva Technology exhibitor/delegation participant.

== Associations and volunteering ==
=== Morocco and student initiatives ===
Qacami participated in Enactus and Solar Decathlon and helped found a sustainable civil-engineering association.

Her supplied professional record lists communications leadership for EMIGreen and co-founding CLUB EMI Génie Civil. It also lists construction-unit leadership with THRIVE-HOUSE SDA and engineering and operations leadership through Enactus and Solar Decathlon Africa. She describes leading a multidisciplinary team of approximately 13 on Thrive, an energy-autonomous building, and selection among ten global projects for Solar Decathlon Africa 2019.

=== France and professional associations ===
Qacami reports involvement in establishing associations in Morocco and France. Her supplied professional record lists social-media and events coordination with ADO–Les Ailes de Demain in Lyon, in an Erasmus+ context involving youth leadership, social justice, workshops, training and international exchanges. It also lists rescue volunteering with FFSS 75–AMNS, AFGC membership and fib young membership.

== Awards and recognition ==

* 2025: First prize awarded by Alter Egales at the GEF Start-up Weekend, with Strucmedica.
* 2025: National Prix Pépite laureate, one of 30 selected projects, representing Pépite ECA with Strucmedica in the category Les matériaux dans tous leurs états, following regional selection. [ref: 12ᵉ édition du Prix Pépite, Pépite France] The award was also reported by Femmes du Maroc and H24info, the latter crediting MAP. [ref: La Marocaine Ouijdane Qacami primée en France pour sa startup Strucmedica, Femmes du Maroc] [ref: France: la Marocaine Ouijdane Qacami reçoit le Prix Pépite dédié aux jeunes startups, H24info]

[ref: Concours d’innovation de l’État 2026: 8 projets IP Paris parmi les lauréats i-PhD et i-Lab, Institut Polytechnique de Paris] Campus France lists Qacami among the award-winning alumni, and Institut Polytechnique de Paris identifies Strucmedica among the i-PhD laureate projects. The platform was developed around a model intended to prioritize user expression and chronological content visibility. [ref: RAW Social Pitch Deck, RAW Social]

* Anonymous posting
* Topic discussion rooms
* Direct messaging
* Voice posts
* Temporary posts and stories
* Reaction systems
* Referral tools
* User profile customization
* Creator tipping tools
* Long form profile biography sections [ref: About RAW Social, RAW Social]

----

Beta Systems Software AG is a German software provider that develops intelligent automation and orchestration solutions for IT operations. [ref: Key Takeaways: 2024 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Service Orchestration and Automation Platforms, Solutions Review] [ref: Beta Systems erweitert SSO-System, Computerwoche] The company develops products that can be accessed through the cloud, on-premises, and through a software as a service (SaaS) model. [ref: Beta Systems: Comprehensive IT Products & Solutions, Beta Systems]

The company is headquartered in Berlin, in the Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf borough, and has subsidiaries in other countries. [ref: Beta Systems zieht an den Berliner Ernst-Reuter-Platz, IZ]

== History ==

Beta Systems was founded in 1983 by Alfred Tauchnitz, Bill Schmidt, and James Henderson. [ref: Die Lage der Firma war dramatisch, Berliner Morgenpost] [ref: Beta Systems geht in den Neuen Markt, Der Tagesspiegel] In the same year, the company introduced its first product, the Beta 91 Quality Management System, for quality assurance of input data. [ref: Beta Systems hat das Angebot für Rechenzentren aufpoliert, Computerwoche] This was followed by Beta 92 Process History Manager, a product for controlling and archiving job logs. [ref: Moderne Verknüpfung von Mainframe mit offener Serverwelt, eGovernment] In 1987, Beta Systems released Beta 93, its report distribution and print management system. [ref: Beta Systems, Computerwoche]

In 1991, Beta Systems was converted into a stock corporation. [ref: Beta Systems jetzt eine AG, Computerwoche] The company became one of the first companies in its industry to have an initial public offering on the Neuer Markt in 1997. [ref: Beta Systems geht in den Neuen Markt, Der Tagesspiegel] [ref: Beta Systems: Teilrückzug des Firmengründers, Computerwoche] A year later, Beta Systems acquired Harbor Systems Management. [ref: One-time charges drive Beta Systems further into the red, Tech Monitor] [ref: Neuer Firmenchef will Beta Systems aus der Krise führen, Computerwoche]

In April 2000, Harbor's storage division was transferred to Beta Systems' Boulder, Colorado-based subsidiary, Tantia Technologies.

Beta Systems acquired Systor Security Solutions in 2003. [ref: Systor sells security business to Beta Systems, Tech Monitor] The following year, it acquired a majority stake in Kleindienst Datentechnik AG. [ref: Beta Systems greift nach Kleindienst Datentechnik, Computerwoche]

Beta Systems acquired SI Software Innovation in 2008. [ref: Beta Systems übernimmt SI Software Innovation, Finance Magazin] In 2009, the company acquired Detec Decision Technology Software and Detec Software Products. [ref: Beta Systems übernimmt Detec, IT-Times] In the same year, Beta Systems chief executive officer Kamyar Niroumand was dismissed from his position. No reason was given for his dismissal. [ref: Neuer Firmenchef will Beta Systems aus der Krise führen, Computerwoche]

In 2012, Beta Systems sold Detec Software to Unicorn Systems. [ref: Beta Systems Software AG verkauft Tochtergesellschaft DETEC Software GmbH an UNICOM Systems, Inc., PresseBox] Beta Systems also acquired the Munich-based software developer Horizont Software. [ref: Beta Systems acquires Horizont Software GmbH, Conectronica]

At the end of 2017, Beta Systems acquired Lynet Kommunikation AG. [ref: Beta Systems Software AG: Acquisition of LYNET Kommunikation AG, EQS Group AG] In February 2018, the company also acquired Auconet / Asdis GmbH. [ref: Beta Systems acquires Auconet / Asdis GmbH, PresseBox]

In 2019, Beta Systems acquired a majority stake in the Habel / Akzentum Group with the assistance of Oppenhoff & Partner. [ref: Oppenhoff & Partner berät Beta Systems Software beim Erwerb der Habel/Akzentum-Gruppe, RWS Verlag] Beta Systems also acquired a majority stake in the Polish company infinIT Codelab through a subsidiary. [ref: Beta Systems Software AG: Acquisition of infinIT Codelab Sp. z o.o., EQS Group AG]

In October 2023, the company sold its shares in Proxess Holding GmbH to Easy Software AG. [ref: Easy Software übernimmt Proxess, IT-ZOOM] In the same year, Beta Systems donated a z14 mainframe computer to Leipzig University for use in training junior staff. [ref: Beta Systems Software spendet z14 Mainframe an Uni Leipzig, DataCenter-Insider]

In 2024, Beta Systems was included in Gartner's Magic Quadrant for Service Orchestration and Automation Platforms. [ref: Key Takeaways: 2024 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Service Orchestration and Automation Platforms, Solutions Review]

data.title: These Smiths
data.text:
These Smiths are an English tribute band based in Manchester that perform the music of the Smiths and Morrissey. Formed in 2015 by original vocalist Jim Thompson following his appearance on the television programme Stars in Their Eyes, the band has performed throughout the United Kingdom and internationally. The current line-up consists of Roy Barrow (vocals), Zander Sumner (guitar), Nigel Clare (bass) and Lee Summers (drums).

The band recreates the sound and stage presentation of the Smiths, including the guitar arrangements of Johnny Marr and the vocal style of Morrissey. The approach was discussed in a 2026 interview with the Spanish newspaper Última Hora.

== History ==

=== Formation and early years ===
These Smiths were formed in 2015 after original vocalist Jim Thompson performed as Morrissey on ITV's Stars in Their Eyes. His appearance was reported by the Manchester Evening News in February of that year.

The band's media archive lists subsequent press and radio appearances, including an interview with Thompson and guitarist Josh Smith in the Oldham Chronicle in 2016, a 2024 Bolton News review, a 2025 interview with the Polish publication Fakt, and a Radio Tameside interview with Roy Barrow and Zander Sumner. The group was also featured in a 2023 Dee Radio interview. [ref: Videos & media, These Smiths] [ref: These Smiths – The Smiths Tribute Band, Dee Radio]

In 2026, the group was profiled ahead of performances in Majorca and Galicia. The Majorca Daily Bulletin described its origins and current members, while El Ideal Gallego previewed a concert in A Coruña.

=== Line-up changes ===
The founding line-up consisted of vocalist Jim Thompson, guitarist Barry Eaton, bassist Nigel Clare and drummer Luke Williams. Josh Smith replaced Eaton in September 2016, remaining until January 2022, when Zander Sumner joined as guitarist. Thompson left in October 2024 and Roy Barrow succeeded him, making his first live appearance with the group in December 2024. Luke Williams departed in 2025; Dan Hough subsequently joined on drums and remained until November 2025. Lee Summers became the permanent drummer in December 2025, having previously performed as a deputy.

As in the original band, whose best-known line-up included Morrissey, Johnny Marr, Andy Rourke and Mike Joyce, each performer takes the corresponding role in the tribute group's stage presentation. [ref: Meet the band, These Smiths]

=== Zander Sumner's 2025 accident ===
In February 2025, guitarist Zander Sumner was seriously injured in a road collision on the A49 in Lancashire. Reports by Lancs Live and ITV News described injuries including a broken hip, broken collarbone and injuries to his hands, which affected his ability to perform during his recovery. [ref: The Smiths tribute guitarist left crawling from written-off car after hit-and-run crash, Lancs Live] [ref: Lancashire teenager spared jail after 'horror smash' leaves Smiths tribute act unable to perform, ITV News]

The band also used substitute performers during other members' absences, including bassist Kris Perry, who covered for Nigel Clare during March–May 2025 and at a performance in Germany in 2026.

=== Performances and touring ===
These Smiths perform at venues and festivals in the United Kingdom and abroad. British appearances have included The Cavern Club in Liverpool, Shepherd's Bush Empire in London and HMV Empire in Coventry. The band was included in the programme for the 2023 Made in Manchester festival. [ref: These Smiths – Live at The Cavern Club Liverpool, The Cavern Club] [ref: These Smiths at hmv Empire, Coventry, Eventim] [ref: Crowds enjoyed live music at Dukinfield's Made in Manchester festival, Tameside Reporter]

In 2026, Spanish newspaper reports previewed concerts in Santander, Ponferrada, A Coruña and Palma de Mallorca. The group performed at the Trui Teatre in Palma on 17 July 2026, with interviews and profiles appearing in the Majorca Daily Bulletin and Última Hora ahead of the concert.

The band also performed at Landei Lugau in Germany on 27 June 2026. [ref: These Smiths in Lugau, Eventim]

== Meeting members of the Smiths ==
In a July 2026 interview with the Spanish newspaper Última Hora, Sumner described meeting former Smiths guitarist Johnny Marr on two occasions and telling him about These Smiths. According to Sumner, Marr was aware of the band and had wished them well. Sumner also said members of These Smiths had met former Smiths drummer Mike Joyce at Christmas and had a photograph taken with him.

== 2026: The Queen Is Dead 40th anniversary ==
In 2026, These Smiths programmed performances marking 40 years since the release of The Queen Is Dead, the Smiths' third studio album. A June listing for the Marrs Bar in Worcester advertised a performance of the album in full, while a November concert at the Boileroom in Guildford was billed as an anniversary celebration. [ref: These Smiths, WeGotTickets] [ref: A celebration of The Smiths: 40 Years of The Queen Is Dead – These Smiths, The Boileroom]

== Band members ==

=== Current members ===

* Roy Barrow (Morrissey) – vocals (2024–present)
* Zander Sumner (Johnny Marr) – guitar (January 2022–present)
* Nigel Clare (Andy Rourke) – bass guitar (2015–present)
* Lee Summers (Mike Joyce) – drums (December 2025–present)

Before joining These Smiths, Roy Barrow performed in original-music groups including Otiks, The Selftonic and Vacant Joy. Otiks released the singles Deadlights and Low Profile, and the four-track EP Contrast in 2014.

Roy Barrow has also worked as an actor, singer and voice-over performer. His professional profile lists background and walk-on work in the television series The Bill, Peaky Blinders and Emmerdale. Other credits include the independent screen production Luna Demise and the audio drama Piercing Time Podcast.

Zander Sumner previously performed with the re-formed Blackburn post-punk band Some Now Are, joining its line-up in 2017 during a period of renewed live performances and recording. Sumner also provides private guitar tuition through Ribble Valley Guitar Lessons.

Nigel Clare is the only member of the band's original 2015 line-up who remains with the group. Lee Summers previously performed with the Manchester-based Morrissey tribute act Viva Morrissey before joining These Smiths permanently in December 2025.

The group Viva Morrissey was reviewed in The Guardian in 2024, although that article did not identify the individual players at the reviewed show.

=== Former members ===

* Jim Thompson (Morrissey) – vocals (2015–October 2024)
* Barry Eaton (Johnny Marr) – guitar (2015–September 2016)
* Josh Smith (Johnny Marr) – guitar (September 2016–January 2022)
* Luke Williams (Mike Joyce) – drums (2015–2025)
* Dan Hough (Mike Joyce) – drums (2025)

=== Other performers ===
The following musicians have stood in for the core members. The dates and roles are based on band-supplied history and require independent published verification.

* Steve Williams – guitar, portraying Johnny Marr or Craig Gannon (dates not established)
* Gary Minor – drums, portraying Mike Joyce (dates not established)
* Kris Perry – bass guitar, portraying Andy Rourke (temporary cover March–May 2025 and Germany 2026)
* Liam Nykolyszyn – drums, portraying Mike Joyce (stand-in, 2025)

data.title: Signal and Image Processing Institute
data.text:
The USC Signal and Image Processing Institute (SIPI) is a research institute within the Ming Hsieh Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering in the USC Viterbi School of Engineering, focused on signal and image processing.

==History and research==

SIPI was established in 1972 (initially as the USC Image Processing Institute, or IPI) by Professors William K. Pratt and Harry C. Andrews with support from ARPA. [ref: Image Processing Research Semiannual Technical Report: 3 August 1971 through 29 February 1972, Defense Technical Information Center] Image processing was in the early stages of development in the 1960s and 1970s, and SIPI/IPI was one of the first university groups in the world dedicated to image processing research [ref: 40 Years at SIPI: The Past, Present and Beyond] [ref: USC Living History Project - Dr. Alexander A. Sawchuk (2022)]. In addition to performing fundamental early research that helped lay the foundation for the JPEG and MPEG image and video compression standards [ref: Machine vision: The past, the present and the future See also [https://www.vision-systems.com/knowledge-zone/article/14069209/the-history-of-machine-vision adapted online version, “The history of machine vision” (2019)].] [ref: Culture, Communication, and an Information Age Madonna, IEEE Professional Communication Society Newsletter] [ref: Nearly Every JPEG on Earth Runs on Math a Reviewer Called Too Simple to Fund in 1972, Fstoppers], SIPI/IPI was also a key member of the ARPANET (the precursor to the Internet) where it provided image processing hardware and software services for other members of the network [ref: IMAGE PROCESSING OVER THE ARPA COMPUTER NETWORK, University of Arizona Libraries Campus Repository].

In the early 1970s, SIPI/IPI research focused on the basic theory of image processing with applications to image compression and image transmission/communication (including pioneering work on transform coding [ref: Origins of the zigzag scan in transform-based picture coding, SPIE] [ref: How I came up with the discrete cosine transform, Digital Signal Processing]), image restoration and enhancement (including topics such as denoising, super-resolution, and color enhancement), image analysis, and display.

In 1977, SIPI released the first version of the USC-SIPI image database [ref: The USC - Image Processing Institute Data Base, Defense Technical Information Center] [ref: The USC-SIPI Image Database]. The database provides a large collection of standard test images that were scanned and digitized using SIPI's image acquisition hardware. Many of these images have been influential in image processing research [ref: Data Compression: The Complete Reference, Springer] [ref: Image Restoration: Fundamentals and Advances, CRC Press] [ref: Forty years of color quantization: a modern, algorithmic survey, Artificial Intelligence Review], including the widely-used, Peppers, and Lenna test images.

Over the years, SIPI's scope expanded beyond just image processing to involve a broader range of signal processing applications, including audio signal processing, speech processing, video processing, and the processing of data from a variety of sensors, imaging systems, and other information sources. [ref: USC Signal and Image Processing Institute]

data.title: Deep Structure Theory
data.text:
----

Deep Structure Theory (DST), also known as Neuropsychological Deep Structure Theory, is a unifying analytical framework that models how mental states emerge as compiled electromagnetic oscillatory activity relating to the structure and function of underlying neural circuitry. It is a local instance of dynamic complex systems theory that applies to how the brain generates the mind and was introduced by the cognitive neuroscientist and psychotherapy researcher Oliver Boxell. [ref: Deep Structure Theory: An introduction to a unifying theoretical framework for the analysis of human neuropsychology., Journal of Mind and Behavior]

The term "deep structure" was popularized in formal linguistics by Noam Chomsky in his theory of generative grammar, although this referred only to a core syntactic structure that could be expressed as different surface sentence forms. Boxell radically extends and deepens the idea in DST by developing it into a standard model for the entirety of the mind in which core conceptual meaning representations can be re-coded into integrated language, mathematics, music and sound patterns, or visuospatial and sensorimotor patterns. Furthermore, while Chomsky viewed mental representation in isolation, DST describes deep structure as the product of integrated, co-evolved representational and real-time processing subsystems. As such, the DST paradigm is able to stipulate systems for memory, learning, and sustained developmental patterns over time, in which the emergence of consciousness appears and plays a mediating role. The relationship between micro- and macro- neural circuits and compiled oscillations as the encoding of deep structure also makes DST more explicit about how the mind emerges from the structure and function of the brain, although generative grammar also more loosely viewed deep structure as somehow relating to the structure of the brain.

== Basic technical outline ==
===Universal deep structure algorithms===
Boxell imports three core algorithms from X-Bar Theory (namely the complement, specifier, and adjunct rules), as well as binary switches, but views them as domain-general faculty for core meaning rather than a language-specific one. As such, in DST these formal algorithms derive abstract mental information structure as encoded by compiled neural oscillations. In common with dynamic complex systems theories generally, these neurosymbolic structures are computed as branching computations of nodes (units of information) that form binary tree representations.

===Phase transitions===
The domain-general faculty for core meaning occurs in the Information-Phase (I-Phase) of deep structural computation. One of the main functions of the I-Phase is conceptual or thematic role assignment, in which the deep structural tree incorporates theta theory and predicate logic. As some of these I-Phase computations reach a neural activation threshold filter known as theta (Φ) they transition into the Spellout-Phase (S-Phase), where the core meaning derivations are re-rendered into modality-specific deep structural forms through the addition of abstract features to the nodes, producing language, mathematics, music and sound patterning, and visuospatial and sensorimotor patterning. The I-to-S phase transitions in DST subsume transformations and phase analysis from the Minimalist Program and extend it as per-propositional chunking to all neurocognitive domains as a general computational working memory constraint.

===Linearization===
Some I-Phase and especially S-Phase computations reach another neural threshold filter called omega (Ω) that precipitates the deletion of branches from the deep structural tree representations to create a linear string of nodes. Subsets of deep structures that undergo this transition become self-aware or conscious, in-line with fundamental neurobiological research on consciousness that finds it appears when activation thresholds are reached in conjunction with highly distributed macrocircuits. [ref: What is the readiness potential?, Trends in Cognitive Sciences] [ref: Unconscious determinants of free decisions in the human brain, Nature Neuroscience] [ref: Piercing of Consciousness as a Threshold-Crossing Operation, Current Biology] [ref: Neural correlates of evidence accumulation during value-based decisions revealed via simultaneous EEG-fMRI, Nature Communications]

===Memory===
The sustained strength of transient neural circuit structures upregulates the strength of branch connections between nodes in deep structural tree derivations. Using Marvin Minsky's typology, Boxell calls the strength of branch connections "k-lines" (knowledge lines). [ref: K-Lines: A theory of memory, Cognitive Science] Just as neural circuits upregulate k-lines, k-line strengths can downregulate neural circuit connectivity strength; at both the neurobiological and emergent neuropsychological levels, frequency, recency, and saliency are proposed as the main filters that determine connectivity strengths. The ephemeral nature of k-lines show how the processing subsystem is instrumental in forming part of the nature of the deep structures that are built along with the actual representational algorithms that constrain their nature.

===Learning and development===
A real-time episode of learning involves the re-weighting of k-line branch attachments between nodes of deep structural trees. These can be transient but if frequency, recency, and saliency build up these learned connections to a critical mass threshold known as alpha (α), then the deep structural tree derivations involved become entrained into the developmental trajectory of the individual and further episodes of learning and development can build on them. Cycles of the α, Φ, and Ω thresholds running through I-Phase, S-Phase, and linearization process developmental curves over time, which Boxell (2025) relates to neuroconstructivism and its preceding models such as Piaget's cognitive development theory and Mahoney's cognitive constructivism. This mechanism also accounts for highly entrained components of human nature such as personality and identity.

===Bidirectional crosstalk with natural systems===
Direct two-directional interactions between neuronal cells and circuits, immune cells, endocrine molecules, microbiota and their metabolites, and the central nervous system mean that emergent deep structural mental states from these circuits' activity can influence — and be influenced by — a range of biological and biochemical systems. [ref: Neuropsychological Deep Structure: The Electromagnetic Emergence of Human Nature, Psychopathology, and the Scope of Clinical Mental Health Intervention., University of Rochester] This accounts for placebo effects and somatoform conditions, for example. Additionally, Piattelli-Palmarini and Vitielo identify a mathematical isomorphism between Quantum Field Theory and the features of Chomskyan X-Bar Theory and the Minimalist Program that are in turn incorporated into DST. [ref: Quantum field theory and the linguistic Minimalist Program: a remarkable isomorphism, Journal of Physics: Conference Series] Boxell (2025) suggests that this isomorphism may therefore transitively apply to DST as well, which is in-keeping with Piatelli and Vitielo's suggestion that it relates to electromagnetic oscillatory activity and could be connected to a more general neural phenomenon than language in isolation. If so, then the isomorphism may provide evidence of a high level of parsimony between the deep structural account of neuropsychology and quantum electrodynamics.

== Psychopathology ==
DST views psychopathology as a form of "oscillopathy" or "rhythmopathy," terms introduced by Buzsáki and Vöröslakos (2023, p.926). [ref: Brain rhythms have come of age, Neuron] Boxell identifies four main etiological pathways, as follows:
* Genetically predetermined: When the genome codes for protein synthesis that impacts key neural circuit formations, clinically diagnosable mental states emerge in the form of neurodevelopmental disorders. Examples include intellectual disability disorders, Down's syndrome, or Williams Syndrome.
* Chemically induced: The introduction of substances that can impact synaptic or neural transmission will influence the structure and function of neural circuits and in turn the emergent deep structural mental states. Most psychiatric conditions have a chemically induced version.
* Neurodegenerative: Molecular or cellular pathologies that impact the structure and function of neural circuits will in turn produce pathological emergent deep structural states. Examples include Alzheimer's disease, Lewy Bodies dementia, other dementias, and traumatic brain injuries.
* Epigenetic predispositions/trauma-induced: The genome has code that is switched on or off by interaction with environmental stimuli. When the I-Phase encodes interpersonal-emotive trauma, the associated pain expresses phenotypes for neural circuits responsible for the S-Phase that use its neurocognitive modalities (such as language or visuospatial patterns) to produce symptomatic narratives — namely, defensive patterns of deep structural information processing that redirect the underlying I-Phase to "anesthetize" the pain of the trauma. There are a variety of such responses, each corresponding to a psychiatric disorder. Additionally, bidirectional crosstalk between relevant neural circuits and other biological systems mean that microbiota and their metabolites, endocrine responses, immunological responses, central nervous system responses may all impact neural structure and function directly or indirectly via interfacing with the genes that express them.
The deep structural account of psychopathology is predicted by findings that psychometric, genomic, neurocognitive, and neural circuit data across mental disorders all load onto a common latent variable known as the p-factor. [ref: The Hierarchical Taxonomy of Psychopathology (HiTOP): A Quantitative Nosology Based on Consensus of Evidence, Annual Review of Clinical Psychology] [ref: Toward the future of psychiatric diagnosis: the seven pillars of RDoC, BMC Medicine] As such, Boxell argues that mental disorders are different variants of the same core set of underlying neuropsychological representational and processing systems.

The Deep Structure Psychotherapy Model, also formulated by Oliver Boxell, provides a framework to apply these etiological pathways to clinical diagnosis and treatment. [ref: Deep Structure Psychotherapy. In B. Owens & K. Campbell (eds). The Encyclopedia of Mental Health Trainings, Certifications, and Credentials, Vol. 3., ONB] For measurement of deep structural states to enhance psychometrics, different technologies are used including reaction time latencies, eye-tracking, and electroencephalography (EEG). The model itself establishes some key principles of emergent neuropsychology that can be used to integrate efficacious components of traditional forms of psychotherapy together and it also enables the formulation of augmentative techniques to prime clinical target deep structures into their antidotes additively alongside the traditional interventions to boost efficacy further.

data.title: Green Mountain Gringo
data.text:
----

== Green Mountain Gringo ==
Green Mountain Gringo is an American brand of salsa and tortilla strips owned by TW Garner Food Company, also known as Garner Foods, a food manufacturer based in Winston-Salem, North Carolina. The brand was founded in Vermont in 1989 and is known primarily for its line of all-natural jarred salsas made with ingredients including tomatoes, tomatillos, onions, peppers, garlic, herbs and spices. [ref: Our Story, Green Mountain Gringo]

Green Mountain Gringo products include traditional, roasted and cantina-style salsas in multiple heat levels, as well as corn tortilla strips. The brand's products are sold through grocery retailers in the United States and through its online store.

=== History: ===
Green Mountain Gringo was founded in 1989 in Vermont by Christine and David Hume. [ref: Green Mountain Gringo, Vermont Roots, Inc]

The Humes developed the original Green Mountain Gringo salsa recipe at their farm in Chester, Vermont, initially making salsa in small batches using produce and a simple combination of vegetables, herbs and spices. As demand increased, the brand expanded beyond its local origins. [ref: Green Mountain Gringo, Vermont Roots, Inc]

Green Mountain Gringo was subsequently acquired by TW Garner Food Company, a family-owned food manufacturer headquartered in Winston-Salem, North Carolina. TW Garner Food Company is also the maker of the Texas Pete brand of hot sauces and condiments. [ref: Our Story, Green Mountain Gringo]

Following the acquisition, production of Green Mountain Gringo expanded and the brand developed national retail distribution while retaining salsa as its primary product category.

== Products: ==
Green Mountain Gringo's principal product line is jarred salsa. Its salsa portfolio has included:

* Mild Salsa
* Medium Salsa
* Hot Salsa
* Roasted Garlic Medium Salsa
* Roasted Chile Pepper Medium Salsa
* Cantina Mild Salsa
* Cantina Medium Salsa
* Cantina Roasted Garlic Salsa
* Cantina Salsa Verde Salsa
* Mango Habanero Hot Salsa

The brand also produces tortilla strips, including yellow corn, multigrain, blue corn and white corn varieties. Some varieties of its tortilla strips are made with organic corn. [ref: All Products - Complete Product Listing, Green Mountain Gringo]

Green Mountain Gringo salsa varieties range from mild to hot. The brand uses combinations of jalapeño, pasilla and serrano peppers to produce different heat profiles.

=== Ingredients and certifications: ===
Green Mountain Gringo positions its salsa around relatively simple ingredient formulations. Ingredients found across its salsa varieties include tomatoes, onions, tomatillos, apple cider vinegar, jalapeño peppers, pasilla peppers, serrano peppers, cilantro, parsley, garlic, sea salt and cumin. [ref: Medium Salsa, Green Mountain Gringo]

Green Mountain Gringo salsas are Certified Gluten-Free, Non-GMO Project Verified, and certified kosher. The company's salsas are also certified by the American Vegetarian Association. [ref: FAQs, Green Mountain Gringo]

The company's salsa products do not contain the major food allergens identified on their ingredient labels, although they are manufactured on a line that also produces products containing soy. [ref: FAQs, Green Mountain Gringo]

=== Ownership and manufacturing ===
Green Mountain Gringo is owned by TW Garner Food Company, which operates under the Garner Foods name and is headquartered in Winston-Salem, North Carolina. [ref: Our Story, Green Mountain Gringo]

Garner Foods traces its history to 1929 and is best known as the manufacturer of Texas Pete hot sauce. The company manufactures and markets products under both the Texas Pete and Green Mountain Gringo brands.

Green Mountain Gringo products are manufactured in Winston-Salem, North Carolina. [ref: Our Story, Green Mountain Gringo]

=== Brand development ===
In 2025, Green Mountain Gringo introduced redesigned packaging and a broader brand refresh. The redesign included updated salsa and tortilla-strip packaging, a redesigned website, new retail materials and a marketing campaign using the phrase "Let's Gringo!"

The company also expanded its salsa portfolio with a line of Cantina salsas, developed to provide a smoother, restaurant-style consistency than the brand's traditional salsa varieties.

The Cantina range includes mild, medium, hot and roasted garlic varieties. [ref: All Products - Complete Product Listing, Green Mountain Gringo]

=== Distribution ===
Green Mountain Gringo products are distributed through grocery and food retailers in the United States as well as through [https://Greenmountaingringo.com Greenmountaingringo.com] and Amazon.

At the introduction of its expanded Cantina salsa line in 2025, the company reported that the products were available through more than 2,600 retail stores nationwide.

data.title: EuroNatur
data.text:
EuroNatur is a German foundation based in Radolfzell that supports nature conservation projects in Europe. The foundation was established in 1987 by Bund für Umwelt und Naturschutz Deutschland (BUND), Environmental Action Germany (DUH) and Naturschutzbund Deutschland (NABU). EuroNatur is a member of the Deutschen Naturschutzring.

== Mission ==
The foundation's mission is to protect Europe's diverse natural heritage. Its projects focus on wild animals such as wolves, brown bears, lynxes and endangered migratory birds, as well as valuable natural and cultural sites. The foundation's motto is "connecting nature and people", which reflects its belief that restoring nature, conserving wildlife and improving biodiversity are fundamental to human quality of life. Working with local people helps ensure the long-term success of their projects to protect endangered animals and their habitats in Europe.

EuroNatur is heavily involved with the European Green Belt initiative, a collaborative cross-border project which aims to create a wild, biodiverse corridor along the route of the former Iron Curtain. Since 2004, EuroNatur has coordinated the conservation efforts along the Balkan Green Belt, the southernmost section of the European Green Belt. [ref: EGB: Home, www.europeangreenbelt.org]

== Operations and administration ==
The foundation works with scientists, conservationists, farmers, politicians and entrepreneurs from across Europe. A key part of the foundation's work takes place in the Balkans, for which they work with local conservationists and volunteers to plan and establish a large network of nature reserves, along with species conservation projects for wolves, bears, lynxes and migratory birds based on scientific research. EuroNatur organises workshops, seminars and training programmes to share knowledge and experiences that help protect Europe's wild animals. EuroNatur also engages in political lobbying in EU institutions.

EuroNatur's first president was Claus-Peter Hutter, followed by Hartmut Vogtmann between January 2008 and early July 2011. Christel Schroeder served from October 2011 to the end of 2019, and Thomas Potthast has been president since 1 January 2020. Gabriel Schwaderer is the executive director of EuroNatur.

== Funding ==
The foundation is funded through donations, third-party funding and income from foundation capital. EuroNatur has been awarded the DZI Donation Seal by the German Central Institute for Social Issues (DZI).

== European Stork Villages ==
The European Stork Village network was set up by EuroNatur in 1994 as a way of publicly recognising communities across Europe that are making a significant contribution to protecting their local white stork populations. [ref: Ferger, Stefan & Schwaderer, Gabriel. (2016). The European Stork Villages - a successful combination of nature conservation and sustainable development of rural areas.] Representatives from each of the Stork Villages meet every year in one of the member villages to discuss and develop solutions for the conservation of white storks. There are currently 16 recognised European Stork Villages.

The most recent village to be recognised and added to the network was Knepp Wildland and Storrington in 2025, the first and only Stork Village in the UK. [ref: European Stork Villages Network, White Stork Project] The village was honoured in recognition of its conservation and rewilding programme which led to the return of the white stork to the area. The village of Storrington holds its White Stork and Nature Festival each year to celebrate its conservation efforts and the return of its white stork population.

== Awards ==
The foundation has been running its EuroNatur Award since 1992. [ref: Award for Environmental Excellence, EuroNatur]

EuroNatur runs an annual photography competition called European Treasures of Nature in partnership with the NaturVision film festival, Natur magazine and German utility company Gelsenwasser. The winning entries are displayed in a year-long touring exhibition titled Fascinating Nature and featured in the next year's EuroNatur calendar.

data.title: Isima
data.text:
Isima is a hair care brand founded by Colombian singer-songwriter Shakira. Launched in July 2025, the brand was developed to cater primarily to wavy, curly, coily, and highly porous hair types.

The brand's name is derived from the Spanish feminine suffix -ísima, which translates to "extra" or "maximum". Isima's initial product line includes shampoos, conditioners, curl creams, and scalp treatments formulated with Latin American-sourced botanicals, such as Peruvian maca root extract, Brazilian sugarcane, and Mexican aloe. Upon its launch, the brand debuted exclusively through its direct-to-consumer website and the United States cosmetics retailer Ulta Beauty.

== History ==
Before launching, the Isima brand was in development for three to four years, a process inspired by Shakira's personal struggles managing her naturally curly, thick hair, which had become highly porous and damaged from frequent styling, coloring, and heat treatments throughout her career. [ref: Isima, Isima: Shakira is Serving Hair Care con Amor, American Salon] [ref: Exclusiva: Shakira pone a ritmo tu melena con Ísima su nueva línea de productos para el cabello. ¡Enamórate de sus productos!, People en Español] [ref: ¡Ahora empresaria! Shakira lanza Ísima, su nueva línea para el cabello, así puedes adquirirla - Telemax] To address the lack of products catering to the complex hair textures of the Latin community and the industry's reliance on oversimplification, she partnered with Sid Katari, who serves as the brand's CEO and founding member. [ref: I Tried Shakira’s Curly Hair Care Line Isima On My Type 4 Hair—Here’s What Happened, Forbes] The brand's identity and packaging were designed by the agency Established, utilizing a "joyful maximalism" aesthetic based on the brand's "más es más" (more is more) philosophy. [ref: How Shakira's Hair Care Brand Isima Breaks the Celebrity Brand Mold, Dieline]

Isima announced its launch in June 2025. [ref: Shakira launches haircare brand isima, Fashion and Beauty Monitor] The brand officially debuted its initial eight-product lineup through its direct-to-consumer website on June 16, 2025, followed by an exclusive physical retail launch at Ulta Beauty on July 6, 2025. The initial collection included items designed to target the health of the scalp, cortex, and cuticle, utilizing Latin American-sourced botanicals such as Peruvian maca root extract, Brazilian sugarcane, and Mexican aloe. Following its United States retail rollout, the brand expanded to flagship locations in Mexico in August 2025. The brand expanded to the UK in October 2025. [ref: Shakira conquista Europa, pero ahora como empresaria: su marca de cuidado capilar debuta en el Reino Unido, infobae] [ref: Shakira desembarca en Europa con isima, su línea de cosmética capilar, La Razón]

== Products ==
Upon its launch in June 2025, Isima introduced an initial lineup of eight products intended to create a comprehensive wash day routine for diverse hair textures and porosities. [ref: Latin-Rooted, Clinically-Proven Haircare Brand isima, Ignited by Shakira Mebarak, Promises To Give Hair What It Deserves: More, PR Newswire] The brand utilizes culturally inspired Spanish names for several of its formulas, reflecting the Shakira's heritage. [ref: I Tried Shakira's New Haircare Line—Here's How My Curls Held Up, Who What Wear] Isima's products are all vegan, cruelty-free and use susainable packaging. [ref: Colombian singer Shakira enters the beauty space with new hair care line, isima, Premium Beauty News] [ref: Meet Isima, Shakira’s Most Personal Project Yet, WWD]

The inaugural collection includes:

* Reset Clarifying Shampoo – A deeply cleansing shampoo designed to strip away product buildup and detoxify the hair and scalp. [ref: Here Are the Five Best Products to Shop from Shakira's Haircare Brand Isima, Billboard]
* Riquísima Hydrating Shampoo – A daily moisturizing cleanser.
* Suavísima Hydrating Conditioner – A hydrating and detangling daily conditioner.
* Súperbomba Triple Repair Peptide Mask – A protein-rich, restorative deep conditioning treatment designed to repair damaged hair.
* All In Restorative Leave-In Conditioner – A softening cream that doubles as a thermal heat protectant (up to 450°F).
* Curls Don't Lie Curl Perfector – A curl-defining styling cream named in reference to Shakira's hit song "Hips Don't Lie".
* Iconic Densifying Scalp Serum – A targeted treatment intended to promote a healthy scalp and encourage thicker, fuller hair density.
* Delicia Reparative Hair Oil – A nourishing hair oil designed for moisture retention and shine.

== Reception ==
Within its first few months of availability, Isima became the top-selling hair care line at Ulta Beauty in the United States, as well as the retailer's third best-selling brand overall. [ref: Isima, la marca capilar de Shakira, logra su cuarto premio internacional de belleza en solo tres meses, Infobae] Following its initial launch, the brand expanded its retail presence in Mexico, opening physical retail spaces in shopping centers such as Antara in Polanco and Galerías Metepec in Toluca.

Isima also received industry recognition for its product formulations, winning four international beauty awards within three months of its debut. In October 2025, the brand was included in NewBeauty magazine's "NB100" list, an annual round-up that highlights innovative companies in the beauty sector. The publication commended Isima for successfully integrating Shakira's cultural heritage with clinical formulations to create effective products for a wide variety of hair types.

data.text:
----

Gedius is the stage name of Tilen Kolbe, a Slovenian singer and online music creator. He initially gained an audience through online performances and covers of popular songs before releasing original music.

The rise behind that reputation is hard to overstate. In under six months, Gedius has amassed more than 120 million views and grown past 460,000 followers across his platforms (TikTok & Instagram), adding roughly 15,000 new followers every week. He is currently the most-followed artist from Slovenia and one of the fastest-growing channels on social media for his niche — with the engagement to match, making him a natural fit for brands and campaigns looking to reach younger audiences authentically.

That momentum carries beyond the screen. Gedius has taken his sound to the stage across a growing run of live shows — opening for Silente, one of the region’s biggest rock bands, and performing at Zagreb’s Fuliranje summer festival — while steadily stepping into headline shows of his own.

While known for his interpretations of major hits, Gedius is now channeling that momentum into original music, with his first releases on the way. His sound pairs modern production with real emotional weight and a distinctive vocal quality — the foundation of an artist who is only beginning to show what he’s capable of.

== Career ==

Kolbe performs under the name Gedius. His online content includes vocal and guitar covers of popular songs. In September 2026, he released "HOME", his debut original single. The song explores the idea of home as a sense of belonging associated with people rather than a particular place. [ref: Louder - Official Booking Website, Louder.hr]
