== Rahul Dhandlaniya ==
Rahul Dhandlaniya is an Indian social media personality and fitness content creator from Haryana, known for promoting traditional exercise practices, rural lifestyle content and Haryanvi cultural identity. He has gained recognition for his demonstrations of spatte, a traditional physical exercise, and is sometimes referred to online as the "Spate King". His content combines fitness, humour, motivational themes and everyday village life. [ref: == Career and fitness == Rahul Dhandlaniya is associated with Haryana's traditional fitness movement, which combines rural lifestyles, traditional exercise practices and regional cultural identity. In January 2026, The Federal included him in its coverage of the growth of desi fitness creators in Haryana, noting his social-media career and background in Dhandalan village, Jhajjar district.How 'desi fitness' is changing workout goals and life aspirations in Haryana, The Federal]

On 10 September 2023, Dhandlaniya's YouTube channel published a video titled Rahul Dhandlaniya 5005spate world Record, documenting his performance of 5,005 sapate, a traditional physical exercise. The performance has been associated with his online identity as a fitness creator. [ref: Rahul Dhandlaniya 5005spate world Record, Rahul Dhandlaniya] [ref: घर पर चलता रहा बुलडोजर, इधर लगाते रहे सपाटे, कौन हैं राहुल ढंडलानिया?, Khabargaon]

In addition to creating online fitness and lifestyle content, Dhandlaniya has appeared in Haryanvi entertainment productions. The episode covered his career, personal outlook, fitness practices, commercial offers and views on protein. The interview provides a primary source for his own statements on these subjects. == May 2025 incident == On 10 May 2025, two youths reportedly opened fire outside Dhandlaniya's home in Dhandhlan village, Jhajjar district, Haryana, following an alleged dispute involving social-media posts. According to The Tribune, Dhandlaniya was not at home at the time. Police confirmed the arrests of both suspects and stated that further investigation was underway. ==References== ]

His approach to fitness is associated with a preference for conventional exercise routines and traditional food rather than an exclusive focus on commercial fitness products. His content has contributed to the visibility of traditional Haryanvi exercise practices among younger audiences.

=== Personality and public image ===
A defining feature of Dhandlaniya's online presence is his association with traditional Haryanvi culture. His conversational manner, regional expressions and light-hearted humour distinguish his content from more formal fitness programming. Comedy and an informal, jovial presentation are recurring elements of his videos.

His continued association with village life is also an important part of his public image. Rather than separating his online identity from his rural background, his content regularly incorporates familiar surroundings, local traditions and everyday experiences. This connection to his roots has helped establish his identity as a regional creator whose appeal extends beyond fitness alone.

=== Commercial endorsements and personal values ===
As his audience has grown, Dhandlaniya has become part of a social media environment in which fitness creators receive commercial collaboration opportunities, including offers involving fitness-related products.

His reported reluctance to promote certain supplements, despite potentially lucrative commercial opportunities, has been presented by supporters as an indication of his preference for personal principles over commercial gain. Claims concerning specific financial offers, however, require confirmation through a reliable published interview or another verifiable source.

Similarly, accounts suggesting that he has chosen to remain in his village despite opportunities to purchase large amounts of land.

=== Cultural significance ===
Dhandlaniya's online identity reflects a wider trend in which regional creators have built audiences by presenting local culture through digital platforms. His combination of traditional fitness, Haryanvi humour and rural lifestyle content illustrates how social media can bring locally rooted personalities to a broader audience.

His public persona is closely associated with physical discipline, regional identity and an informal style of communication. Through this combination, he has become a recognisable figure within Haryana's social media fitness community.

=== Physical feats ===
In 2023, Rahul Dhandlaniya published a video on his YouTube channel titled Rahul Dhandlaniya 5005spate world Record, documenting his performance of 5,005 sapate, a traditional exercise associated with Indian physical training. The feat subsequently became associated with his online identity as a fitness creator. His performances have also featured in coverage of Haryana's traditional fitness culture.

=== Music and entertainment ===
Beyond digital content creation, Dhandlaniya has appeared in Haryanvi music productions. In May 2025, Dainik Tribune reported that he had appeared in Knife Brown, a song by Haryanvi rapper Dhanda Nyoliwala.

His screen-related credits also include Baba Ki Daya Tey (2024) and 12 Gaam, according to IMDb. These credits should be independently verified through reliable entertainment sources before being added to the article.

=== Digital milestones ===
Dhandlaniya created his YouTube channel, operating under the handle @[user], on 6 August 2017. The channel publishes fitness demonstrations, personal vlogs and videos documenting aspects of his everyday life.

By October 2026, third-party channel statistics reported that the account had approximately 1.52 million subscribers and more than one billion cumulative views. These figures represent a snapshot of the channel's growth and may change over time.

=== 2025 incident ===
On 10 May 2025, two youths reportedly opened fire outside Dhandlaniya's home in Dhandhlan village, Jhajjar district, Haryana, following an alleged dispute connected to social-media posts. According to The Tribune, Dhandlaniya was away from home when the incident occurred. His brother filed a police complaint, and the two suspects were apprehended. Police confirmed their arrest and stated that the matter was under investigation.

The incident received coverage in several news outlets, including The Tribune and Dainik Tribune.

data.title: Schiavello Group
data.text:
Schiavello Group is a privately owned Australian company engaged in commercial furniture design and manufacturing, interior construction and fit-out, property development and workplace technology. It was founded in Melbourne in 1966 by Italian-born furniture maker Tony Schiavello with his younger brother Joe, initially as a partitioning and joinery business. The group is headquartered in Tullamarine, employs around 1,100 people and reported revenue of approximately A$700 million in 2025. It has been described as one of Australia's oldest manufacturers of high-end furniture and is ranked among the country's top 100 private companies.

== History ==

=== Founding and early years (1966–1979) ===
Tony Schiavello, a furniture maker by trade, migrated to Australia from Calabria, southern Italy, in the 1950s. In 1966 he secured a labour-only subcontract to install toilet partitions at 15 William Street, Melbourne, and registered the partnership TT&G with his brother Joe Schiavello and friend Tony Cipollone. Schiavello Bros Pty Ltd was established two years later.

The company's early product was MK1, a series of demountable partitions, and its first large-scale partition project was completed for Victoria Insurance in 1968. Growth led to new factory premises in Airport West from 1970. In 1971 the company produced more than 8,000 voting booths for the Australian Electoral Office ahead of the 1972 Australian federal election. The office furniture operation was established in 1978 with the Series 35 and Series 45 foldable desk collections.

=== Office furniture and expansion (1980s–1990s) ===
In 1982 Schiavello designed its first ergonomic, height-adjustable desks to meet Federal Government requirements for computer desks; the resulting Primatic desk, launched in 1983, was among the first ergonomic desks with a fully user-adjustable main worktop. The company's first workstation system, Interstat, was exhibited at the Orgatec furniture fair in Cologne in 1986, its first international trade show. Interstate offices opened in New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory in the late 1980s, with Queensland, Western Australia and South Australia following by 1993.

In 1990 Tony Schiavello won the National Australia Bank Ethnic Business Award, broadcast live on SBS. In 1992 the company won a contract to supply more than 20,000 workstations to the World Bank headquarters in Washington, D.C., which the company describes as the start of its significant international presence. The following year it completed one of its largest interior construction projects as head contractor for Clayton Utz in Sydney, and launched the Sesto desking system with a worktop height-adjustment design.

In 1995 the Newtech height-adjustable workstation received an award for excellence in design and manufacture of systems furniture at the Australian Furniture Fair, and Schiavello developed the "Hot Desk" concept, described as Australia's first mobile workplace, in collaboration with RMIT's federally funded EcoReDesign programme. Schiavello carried out interior construction and joinery for the opening of Crown Melbourne in 1997, beginning a long-term relationship that included hotel refurbishments in 2007. The company also obtained ISO 14001 environmental management accreditation in the late 1990s.

=== Diversification (2000s) ===
Schiavello established bathroomware company Omvivo and, in 2003, Italian architect Mario Bellini commissioned the company to manufacture the NGV bench for the reopening of the National Gallery of Victoria. In 2005 Victorian Premier Steve Bracks opened the group's purpose-built 70,000 square metre headquarters and factory in Tullamarine, which consolidated the group's divisions on one site. The project was recognised with the 2005 Victorian Master Builder of the Year award. Tony Schiavello was inducted into the Victorian Manufacturing Hall of Fame in 2008.

The group entered property development in 2007 with The Artist, a multi-residential building in Fitzroy developed in joint venture with PDG and completed in 2011. In the same year it took a shareholding in Melbourne hospitality operator Atlantic Group, founded by Hatem Saleh, in which Schiavello (Vic) Pty Ltd became a joint shareholder and Tony Schiavello a director. The group's venues and contracts expanded from Central Pier in Docklands to The Atlantic restaurant at Crown Melbourne, opened in 2011, catering at the Melbourne Cup Carnival from 2011 and the Australian Grand Prix from 2013, Gardens House in the Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria and the Port Melbourne Yacht Club. By 2019 Atlantic Group was Central Pier's anchor tenant; the pier was closed by Development Victoria that year on safety grounds, and Atlantic Group led tenants in a A$100 million Federal Court claim against the agency. Peter Schiavello, Tony's eldest son, who had run the furniture operation since 1982 and served as Deputy Managing Director from 1992, was appointed Managing Director of the group in 2009.

=== Recent history (2010–present) ===
In 2010 the company released Climate, a workstation system designed around the concept of "malleability", in which electronics, shelving and panels are housed in a channel independent of the work table so that layouts can be reconfigured without rebuilding. Schiavello was appointed head contractor for the Sydney Commonwealth Parliament Offices in the early 2010s.

Tony Schiavello (Antonino Schiavello) was appointed a Member of the Order of Australia in the 2013 Australia Day Honours "for significant service to business, particularly in the manufacturing and construction industries, and to the community of Victoria". Also in 2013 the company launched Krossi, an electric sit-stand workstation developed and manufactured in Australia; the company describes it as the first Australian-designed and manufactured sit-stand workstation.

International projects in this period included furnishing the Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi, the company's largest healthcare project, and supplying more than 5,500 pieces of furniture to the 31-storey Harbin Bank headquarters in China, with the majority of manufacturing carried out in Australia. The company opened a logistics operation in Malaysia to support expansion in the Asia-Pacific region. In 2013 Anton Schiavello, grandson of the founder, was appointed to lead the group's South-East Asian business from Singapore, where the company had maintained a showroom for 15 years.

In property, the group developed Prima Tower, a 70-storey residential tower in Southbank, and Abode318 in Melbourne, both in joint venture with PDG. In construction, the group's redevelopment of the Garden State Hotel in Flinders Lane, Melbourne, designed by Techne Architecture, was completed in 2016 and won the 2017 Master Builders Award for Excellence in Construction of Commercial Buildings in the A$5–10 million category. The company also delivered a 15,000 square metre workplace for the South Australian Department of Environment, Water and Natural Resources in Adelaide targeting a 6 Star Green Star rating.

In 2016 Tony Schiavello published a memoir, Anything is Possible, the phrase the company uses as its motto. In 2017 Christopher Schiavello, son of co-founder Joe Schiavello, was appointed Director of the group's New South Wales construction operation.

The group's largest property project, M-City in Clayton, was developed in a 50–50 joint venture with developer Nick Saraceno on a 3.5-hectare site opposite Monash University that Saraceno had owned since 1992. Announced by Tony Schiavello and Saraceno in 2017 and led for the group by Managing Director Peter Schiavello, the A$1 billion mixed-use precinct was designed by Buchan and built by Multiplex from July 2018, and was completed in 2020 as one of the largest single-stage master-planned developments in Victoria. It comprises 665 apartments in four buildings, a 250-room Park Royal hotel, an eight-level office tower of 14,000 square metres and a 30,450 square metre retail centre anchored by Woolworths, Kmart and a Village cinema. The joint venture partners retained ownership of the office, hotel and retail components. The Focus Quiet Room collection of demountable acoustic rooms was released in 2019, and in 2023 the company released NEXUS, a range of furniture integrated with workplace management software developed by its subsidiary Nura Space. In June 2025 Nura Vision, an above-desk workplace device developed by Nura Space and exhibited by Schiavello, won the Gold award in the Technology – Integrated Solutions category at the Best of NeoCon awards in Chicago. The group marks its 60th anniversary in 2026.

== Operations ==
The group operates through several divisions:

* Schiavello Furniture designs and manufactures commercial furniture, including workstations, seating, storage and acoustic rooms, at its Tullamarine facility. The company has stated that it manufactures around 95 per cent of its products in Australia. Products have been developed with Australian and international designers including Mario Bellini, Helen Kontouris and Doshi Levien.
* Schiavello Construction provides interior fit-out, refurbishment, heritage restoration and commercial construction services, and holds Office of the Federal Safety Commissioner (OFSC) accreditation.
* Schiavello Property develops residential and commercial buildings, primarily in Melbourne, and holds the office, hotel and retail assets at M-City.
* Nura Space is a workplace management software and hardware business established within the group in 2017 and publicly launched in 2020. The platform provides desk, room and locker booking, occupancy analytics and space planning for hybrid workplaces, and was first deployed across the Schiavello Group's own Australian offices.
* Omvivo is a bathroomware brand established within the group.

Schiavello publishes an in-house magazine, Details, and from the early 2000s has hosted "Future Ways of Working" forums on workplace design.

== Leadership ==
Tony Schiavello remains Governing Director and Executive Chairman, and his brother Joe Schiavello a director.

Peter Schiavello, Tony's eldest son, has led the group as Managing Director since 2009. He joined the family business in 1982, taking responsibility for the furniture operation, and was appointed Deputy Managing Director in 1992, having been mentored by his father. His tenure as Managing Director has seen the group's expansion into large-scale property development, including the A$1 billion M-City precinct, and into workplace technology through Nura Space, which he co-founded in 2017 and for which he serves as an advisor.

Second-generation family members in the business also include Christopher Schiavello, Joe's youngest son, who is Director and State Manager of the group's Victorian and New South Wales construction operations. The third generation includes Anton Schiavello, Peter's son and grandson of the founder, who is co-founder and chief executive of Nura Space.

Vangiliya Yotana Ribeiro Filipe, affectionately known as Vânya Filipe, is an Angolan engineer working at the Ministry of Telecommunications, Information Technologies and Social Communication (MINTTICS) and holding the position of Deputy Director-General of Angola's National Space Program Management Office (GGPEN). [ref: Vangiliya Pereira, World Economic Forum] She is recognized as one of the 100 most influential women in Africa and for contributing to the advancement of knowledge, research, and technological innovation, especially in the Angolan space sector. [ref: Instagram, www.instagram.com]

== Biography ==
Vangiliya was born in the municipality of Sambizanga in Luanda, on December 17, 1984. She has been an employee of MINTTICS since March 2011. In July 2018, she began her duties as Deputy Director-General for the Technical and Scientific Area of ​​GGPEN. She holds a Bachelor's degree in Electronics and Telecommunications Engineering and a Master's degree in Mobile and Satellite Communications from the University of Glamorgan in Wales, United Kingdom. She specializes in Satellite Design, Architecture and Operating Principles and is certified by the Russian Space Agency as a Satellite Operator, having previously served as Flight Director for the Satellite Control and Mission Center Shift. She has worked in several telecommunications companies, specifically in the area of ​​supervision and installation of WiMAX, SHDL and ADSL network services. [ref: ]

She also served as a consultant for the State Secretariat for Telecommunications between March 2011 and 2014, and contributed to the training and capacity building of more than 60 specialists at GGPEN and in the launch of the AngoSat-1 and Angosat-2 telecommunications satellites. She was named one of the 100 Most Influential Women Engineers in Africa by the Federation of African Engineering Organisations (FAEO) in 2021, in recognition of her contributions to engineering on the continent.

She, along with her ex-husband, has founded the angolan company FIRMOPER - SOCIEDADE COMERCIAL E INDUSTRIAL, Lda. On May 7, 2026, she launched the book "UMA VIDA SERVINDO VIDAS - O LEGADO DO DR. NENÉ FILIPE", a biographical work about her father, António Pedro Filipe Jr. (Nené Filipe), along with her company, FIRMOPER EDITORA. [ref: Instagram, www.instagram.com]

== Family ==
Vangiliya Filipe is the daughter of Angolan cardiologist and nationalist Dr. Nené Filipe and Member of Parliament and businesswoman Carla de Sousa. Vanya is mother of 3: Janira Hidianeth Filipe Pereira (November 28, 2004, Cunene, Angola), Jadiel Luciano Filipe Pereira (December 25, 2012, Lisbon, Portugal), and António Pedro Filipe Pereira (November 8, 2015, Lisbon, Portugal). Vangiliya is the younger sister of Ossanda Filipe and the older sister of the twins Jeice and Elionaro Filipe, her paternal siblings, and the first of Carla de Sousa's daughters: Cinthya do Prado, Daniela Silvestre, Débora Francisco, and Cássia Rabelais.

Sitka Engineering is a boat design and manufacturing business based in Grants Pass, Oregon. It supplies aluminum jet boat hull kits for assembly and outfitting by customers and professional boat builders. Its product range includes mini jet boats and the Creekboat. [ref: Sitka Engineering, Sitka Engineering]

In 2026, the company manufactured components for boats assembled by welding and metal fabrication students at Grants Pass High School, North Valley High School, Hidden Valley High School, and Illinois Valley High School in Josephine County. The boats were built for the Cal-Ore Junior River Racing Club, with two scheduled to debut at that year's Boatnik festival. [ref: Josephine County high school students build jet boats, Grants Pass Daily Courier] [ref: Forged on the Rogue: Grants Pass Students Keep Boatnik’s Junior Racing Tradition Alive, Grants Pass Tribune] Reporting on the project, the Grants Pass Daily Courier identified the manufacturer as Matt Richardson's company, Sitka Marine Engineering & Exploration.

Deputy Under Secretary of the Army

The Deputy Under Secretary of the Army (DUSA) is a principal civilian advisor to the Secretary of the Army and Under Secretary of the Army and oversees special projects and policy initiatives as delegated by the Secretary of the Army. [ref: Army Publishing Directorate, armypubs.army.mil]The DUSA is a 3-Star Equivalent member of the Senior Executive Service (SES) and works alongside other senior members of Headquarters Department of the Army. The DUSA is assigned responsibility for:

a. assisting the Secretary of the Army in directing and supervising Army-wide transformation and reform initiatives

b. recommending to the Secretary of the Army policies, methodologies, and measurement criteria developed in consultation with the Secretariat and Army Staff to incorporate artificial intelligence (AI) into Army operations to synchronize, integrate, and coordinate optimal alignment in support of Department of War and Army missions

c. directing and supervising Civilian Senior Leader Management Office (CLSMO), as directed by the Under Secretary of the Army

The Position of Deputy Under Secretary of the Army (DUSA) was created in 1953, and at times multiple DUSA positions existed simultaneously. Although the mission for this role has changed throughout the decades, the DUSA’s portfolio adjusts according to the needs of the Army, directly supporting the Secretary of the Army’s oversight functions and Title 10 responsibilities.

Historical roles of the office include international affairs, manpower and reserve affairs, personnel management, operations research, and business transformation. In recent years, the portfolio of the Deputy Under Secretary of the Army included:

a.        Strategic Capital Initiative (SCI): Created in 2026, the Strategic Capital Initiative seeks strategic partners to co-invest in Army installations, technology, energy infrastructure, and the industrial base. The Army seeks to use creative financial and partnership models, such as joint ventures, long-term leases, and service agreements to create “value for value” exchanges in which the Army offers secure land and stable demand signal in return for resilient energy, re-shored supply chains, and modern facilities without relying solely on taxpayer dollars. The effort spans six pillars (energy resilience, the organic industrial base, logistics and supply chains, advanced manufacturing, real estate and facilities, and critical minerals). [ref: Strategic Capital Initiative, www.army.mil]

b.        Project ARIA (Army Rapid Integration of Artificial Intelligence): Announced March 5, 2026, Project ARIA pairs Army leaders with top private-sector firms to rapidly field cutting-edge technolgy to Army formations. The initaitve is organizaed into multiple teams, each of which is tasked rapidly prototype and field AI-solutions to solve specific Army problems, including both tactical and enterprise-level use cases. [ref: Harnessing AI for the future: Army unveils Project ARIA, www.army.mil]

Previous Deputy Under Secretaries of the Army Included:

1.        Harold L. Pearson: c. 1953

2.        Frank H. Higgins: c.1954-1955

3.        Howard E. Haugerud: c. 1961-1963

4.        Harry C. McPherson: c. 1964

data.title: Matty Mayhem
data.text:
Terry Overton (born 6 December 1990), better known by his ring name Matty Mayhem, is an English professional wrestler who competes on the British independent wrestling circuit. He is a former Rapid Action Wrestling (RAW) Heavyweight Champion and Firestar Championship Wrestling (FCW) Tag Team Champion.

Mayhem began his involvement in professional wrestling in 2007 and made his in-ring debut in 2015. His career has included appearances for 5 Star Wrestling and a long-running tag team partnership with Ryan Roode, known as Anarchy Ink. In May 2025, he returned from a six-month injury absence to win the RAW Heavyweight Championship. [ref: North Shields wrestler Matty Mayhem crowned RAW champion in Blyth after injury comeback, Northumberland Gazette]

== Early life ==
Overton was raised in North Shields, North Tyneside, England. He attended John Spence Community High School, where he was a schoolmate of singer-songwriter Sam Fender. [ref: Matty Mayhem 'North Shields' Own Wrestling Star, I Love North Shields]

== Professional wrestling career ==

=== Early career (2007–2017) ===
Overton began his involvement in professional wrestling in 2007 with the Independent Wrestling Federation (IWF) in Newcastle upon Tyne, where he worked as a referee while also undertaking wrestling training.

In 2012, he continued training with RAD:PRO in South Shields under professional wrestler Vulture. He made his in-ring debut in 2015 at a RAD:PRO event, competing in an eight-man tag team match under the ring name Matty Mayhem.

During his early career, Mayhem competed regularly for RAD:PRO and Maximum Pro Wrestling (MPW), primarily as a singles wrestler. He subsequently made appearances outside North East England, including for World Wide Wrestling League (W3L) in Scotland.

=== 5 Star Wrestling (2018) ===
In 2018, Mayhem appeared for 5 Star Wrestling, a British professional wrestling promotion that organised arena events across the United Kingdom.

On 15 February 2018, Mayhem defeated HT Drake and Alex Young in a three-way match at Sheffield Arena. [ref: 5 Star Wrestling Live Review – 15th February 2018, Across The Pond Wrestling]

The following week, Mayhem faced Flash Morgan Webster in a non-televised match in Plymouth.

On 1 March 2018, Mayhem faced HT Drake in a singles match at a 5 Star Wrestling event in Belfast, Northern Ireland. [ref: 5 Star Wrestling Review – 1st March 2018, Across The Pond Wrestling]

=== Anarchy Ink (2018–2026) ===
In 2018, Mayhem began teaming with Ryan Roode for Classic UK Pro Wrestling (CUKPW). Their partnership developed following an unexpected change to an event's scheduled matches, when Roode replaced another competitor in a triple-threat match.

The pair adopted the name Anarchy Ink, which Mayhem had previously used as part of a wrestling stable in RAD:PRO. They subsequently became regular competitors on the British independent wrestling circuit.

Following Mayhem's return to wrestling in October 2023, the pair resumed their partnership.

On 12 October 2024, Anarchy Ink defeated The Denizen (Bo Carter and Caleb Carter) at Firestar Championship Wrestling's A Cold Night in Hell event in Ripponden, West Yorkshire, to capture the FCW Tag Team Championship. [ref: FCW A Cold Night in Hell, Cagematch]

During their championship reign, Anarchy Ink became involved in an extended rivalry with Reform Wrestling, consisting of Ryan Ace and Kendoll.

On 26 September 2026, Anarchy Ink lost the FCW Tag Team Championship to Reform Wrestling in a ladder match at September Showdown in Greetland, Halifax. The result ended a championship reign lasting nearly two years. [ref: Firestar Championship Wrestling, BritWresEvents]

=== Hiatus and return (2020–2023) ===
Mayhem stepped away from professional wrestling in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic and personal circumstances.

He remained absent from active competition for approximately three years before returning in October 2023 for Rapid Action Wrestling, facing Asylum in his comeback match.

Following his return, Mayhem continued to compete in singles competition while also resuming his tag team partnership with Ryan Roode.

=== Injury and comeback (2024–2025) ===
On 7 December 2024, Mayhem suffered a broken right collarbone during a match involving Anarchy Ink and Reform Wrestling in Ripponden, West Yorkshire. The injury occurred following an awkward landing during the match and required surgery, during which a metal plate and eight screws were fitted to stabilise the fracture.

The injury forced Mayhem out of in-ring competition for approximately six months. During his recovery, the ongoing rivalry between Anarchy Ink and Reform Wrestling continued.

On 24 May 2025, Mayhem returned to competition at a Rapid Action Wrestling event in Blyth, Northumberland, defeating X-Jack to win the RAW Heavyweight Championship. The victory ended X-Jack's 819-day championship reign.

The match had originally been scheduled before Mayhem's injury but had been postponed following an injury to X-Jack.

=== RAW Heavyweight Championship (2025–2026) ===
Following his return from injury, Mayhem competed as RAW Heavyweight Champion.

On 19 September 2025, he defeated Brandon Prince at a Rapid Action Wrestling event in Cramlington, Northumberland. [ref: Rapid Action Wrestling, BritWresEvents]

On 16 May 2026, Mayhem defeated veteran British professional wrestler Jonny Storm in a RAW Heavyweight Championship match in Cramlington.

On 12 September 2026, Mayhem lost the RAW Heavyweight Championship to Eazy-B in Cramlington, ending his first reign with the title.

=== Wrestling training and coaching ===
Mayhem has also been involved in training other professional wrestlers. He previously assisted with coaching at RAD:PRO's Lair of Lucha wrestling school.

In April 2026, Mayhem became head trainer at Ultimate Wrestling Alliance (UWA), succeeding Chris Cannon following his retirement from professional wrestling. Mayhem had faced Cannon in his retirement match.

His responsibilities include training beginners and experienced wrestlers, concentrating on technical fundamentals and in-ring performance.

== Wrestling persona ==
In 2025, Mayhem adopted the nickname "Blacklisted", incorporating it into his existing wrestling persona rather than portraying a separate character.

His finishing moves include the Go to Sleep (GTS) and a headlock driver.

== Championships and accomplishments ==

* Firestar Championship Wrestling
** FCW Tag Team Championship (1 time) – with Ryan Roode

* Rapid Action Wrestling
** RAW Heavyweight Championship (1 time)

* Maximum Pro Wrestling
** MPW Chaos Championship (2 times)

* Classic UK Pro Wrestling
** CUKPW Heavyweight Championship (2 times)
** CUKPW Tag Trophy (1 time) – with Ryan Roode

* Sovereign Nation Wrestling
** SNW Heavyweight Championship (1 time)

* Leeds Pro Wrestling
** LPW Heavyweight Championship (1 time)

Taylah Hasaballah (b.1994, Melbourne) is an Australian artist living and working in Paris. Her practice centres around the concept of entropy through chemically driven paintings that investigate transformation, matter, and time. Working across painting, digital media, and sound installation - she has presented solo exhibitions and large-scale public works is Australia and Europe. Her work is held in public and private collections across Australia and the United States. She holds a degree in science from the University of Queensland, Brisbane and certificate in painting from the National Art School, Sydney [ref: Taylah Hasaballah's paintings are built to decay, The Australian] [ref: saliva.live] [ref: Everything You Missed From the Australian Fashion Week Resort 2025 Collections, Vogue] [ref: INDICATRIX - The Italian Art Guide].

data.title: Johnny Britt (musician)
data.text:
Johnny Britt is an American singer, trumpeter, songwriter, producer, musical director and author. He is known as a founding member of the Motown/MoJazz R&B and jazz duo Impromp2, for his work as musical director for the Temptations, and for songwriting and recording collaborations with saxophonist Boney James. [ref: Impromp2, AllMusic] [ref: Johnny Britt, SoulTracks] [ref: Ride – Boney James, AllMusic]

== Early life and education ==
Britt was born in Louisville, Kentucky, and raised in Cleveland, Ohio, where he attended Cathedral Latin High School. [ref: Johnny Britt biographical materials.] [ref: Johnny Britt, WBSS Media] [ref: A Former Clevelander, Contemporary Jazz Star Johnny Britt to Perform in Cleveland This Weekend, Cleveland Scene] Gospel music was an early influence; he began singing in his uncle's church as a child and took up the trumpet at age 12.

As a teenager, Britt became friends with future television host Arsenio Hall, who was then a drummer, and the two played music together. Hall later discussed Britt and their long-standing friendship in his memoir. [ref: Arsenio: A Memoir] According to a photograph and caption reproduced in the book, the two met as students at R. H. Jamison Junior High School in Cleveland and started their first band together at age thirteen; Britt and Hall went on to play together in a group called the Soul Sophistications.

During a visit to France while still in high school, Britt attended a performance by French classical trumpeter Maurice André. Britt has described the experience as influencing his decision to pursue trumpet more seriously. [ref: 10 Questions with Johnny Britt, Connect Brazil]

Britt later returned to France and studied classical trumpet at the Conservatoire de Versailles under Roger Delmotte of the Paris Opera. In an interview with Connect Brazil, Britt said that during his time in France he became fluent in French, signed his first recording contract in Paris, and appeared on French radio and television.

After returning to the United States, Britt continued his music studies at Governors State University in the Chicago area, where he earned a bachelor's degree in music and received the Gerald Myrow Award for Outstanding Composer.

== Career ==

=== The Temptations ===
Britt's association with the Temptations began after meeting the group's founding member Otis Williams. Britt has recounted approaching Williams after a performance and presenting him with original songs; Williams subsequently hired Britt as the group's musical director.

Britt served as musical director for the Temptations for approximately three years. Multiple published profiles have described him as the group's youngest-ever musical director. [ref: Johnny Britt, EFG London Jazz Festival] [ref: Sitemap, EFG London Jazz Festival] [ref: Johnny Britt '75: A Multifaceted Talent Making Waves Across Industries, Latin Alumnotes] Arsenio Hall's memoir independently corroborates the general timing of the hire: Hall recounts that Britt, after the two reconnected following several years apart, told him that Williams had just hired him for the role.

Britt also worked as a songwriter and producer for the Temptations. He later served as a co-music producer on the NBC television miniseries The Temptations.

Britt subsequently worked as a co-music producer on the television film Little Richard, directed by Robert Townsend.

=== Impromp2 ===
After his work with the Temptations, Britt developed the concept for Impromp2 in Los Angeles, combining his vocals and trumpet with hip-hop and contemporary R&B influences. He partnered with rapper Sean E. Mac, and Impromp2 was formed in Los Angeles in 1993.

The duo signed with Motown's MoJazz label and released its debut album, You're Gonna Love It, in 1995, followed by Can't Get Enough in 1997.

After MoJazz was discontinued, Impromp2 released The Definition of Love through Big3 Records in 2003. JazzTimes described the group's combination of Britt's singing and trumpet with Sean E. Mac's rapping and singing; the album included guest appearances by Boney James and George Duke. [ref: Musicians find originality in mix of different styles, The Vindicator] [ref: Impromp2: The Definition of Love, JazzTimes]

The duo's fourth studio album, It Is What It Is, followed in 2008.

=== Songwriting, recording and solo career ===
As a songwriter, vocalist and musician, Britt contributed to several recordings by saxophonist Boney James. On James's 2001 album Ride, Britt co-wrote "Heaven" and "Grand Central" and contributed background vocals; AllMusic credits "Grand Central" to Johnny Britt and Boney James. [ref: Boney James Takes Guest Artists for a Ride, Billboard]

On James's 2004 album Pure, Britt co-wrote "Break of Dawn" (featuring Dwele) with James and Andwele Gardner, and co-wrote "It's On" with James. [ref: Pure – Boney James, AllMusic] "Grand Central" later received substantial smooth-jazz radio airplay, reaching the top 10 of the Radio & Records Smooth Jazz chart and finishing at No. 11 on the publication's 2003 year-end Smooth Jazz chart. [ref: Smooth Jazz airplay chart, Radio & Records] [ref: Year-End Smooth Jazz chart, Radio & Records]

Britt later co-wrote "The Total Experience," recorded by Boney James featuring George Duke; the song became James's first No. 1 on Billboards Smooth Jazz Airplay chart, spending four weeks at No. 1 in 2006. [ref: Shine – Boney James, AllMusic] [ref: Smooth Jazz Airplay chart, Billboard]

Britt also co-wrote "Contact," the title track of James's 2011 album Contact; the song reached No. 1 on Billboards Smooth Jazz Airplay chart, remaining at the top for five consecutive chart weeks beginning in May 2011. [ref: Contact – Boney James, AllMusic] [ref: Smooth Jazz Airplay chart, Billboard]

Following his work with groups and other artists, Britt increasingly focused on his solo recording career. His solo releases include Feels So Good (2012), Marvin Meets Miles (2016), So Hot (2018), MoJazzin (2020), After We Play (2023), and Midnight in Paris (2025). [ref: Johnny Britt – After We Play, Smooth Jazz Daily]

In 2020, Britt was nominated for Instrumentalist of the Year in the SoulTracks Readers' Choice Awards. [ref: See the Nominees: 2020 SoulTracks Readers' Choice Awards, SoulTracks]

Britt wrote ten original songs and produced all 13 tracks on After We Play. The album included collaborations with Peter White, Will Downing, George Benson, Little Anthony, Tom Browne, Gerald Albright, Ricky Peterson and Nils; the title track, featuring White, reached No. 1 on both the Mediabase and Smooth Jazz Network charts. [ref: The Pulse of Entertainment: Johnny Britt Releases After We Play with Peter White, Will Downing, Gerald Albright, George Benson, The Baltimore Times] [ref: Trumpeter/Vocalist Johnny Britt Release New Album "After We Play", TheUrbanMusicScene.com]

SoulTracks featured a world premiere of Britt's recording of "Goin' Out of My Head," featuring Little Anthony and George Benson. [ref: World Premiere: Little Anthony, Johnny Britt and George Benson Re-create a Classic Together, SoulTracks]

Britt released Midnight in Paris in 2025; the album reflected his longstanding connection with France and the musical influences he encountered while studying there. Later that year, Britt performed at the EFG London Jazz Festival in London.

=== Little Anthony and the Imperials ===
Britt has also performed as a first-tenor singer with Little Anthony and the Imperials. Published biographical material places the beginning of his association with the group in 2012. His association with Little Anthony continued into his solo recording career: Little Anthony appeared with Britt on "Goin' Out of My Head" from After We Play, along with guitarist George Benson.

=== Film and television work ===
Britt has performed on the scores of several major motion pictures.

On Hidden Figures (2016), composed by Hans Zimmer, Pharrell Williams and Benjamin Wallfisch, soundtrack credits identify Britt as a solo trumpeter. [ref: Hidden Figures (Original Motion Picture Score)] [ref: Hidden Figures [Original Motion Picture Score], AllMusic] [ref: Hidden Figures, Hans Zimmer (official store)] The film received several Academy Award nominations at the 89th Academy Awards, including Best Picture; because more than two composers worked on it, the score itself was ruled ineligible for Best Original Score consideration that year. [ref: 89th Academy Awards (2017), Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]

Britt and Jon Lewis were credited as trumpet soloists on Hans Zimmer's score for Dunkirk (2017). [ref: Dunkirk: Original Motion Picture Soundtrack, WaterTower Music] [ref: Dunkirk, Hans Zimmer (official store)] Zimmer's score for the film was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Original Score at the 90th Academy Awards; the nomination recognized Zimmer as composer, with Britt credited as a trumpet soloist on the recording itself. [ref: 90th Academy Awards (2018), Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]

Britt also performed as a trumpet musician on La La Land (2016). [ref: La La Land (2016) – Full Credits, Metacritic]

Britt is also credited as a trumpet musician on the score of Marshall (2017). [ref: Marshall (2017) – Full Credits, Metacritic] He is credited among the vocalists on "Circle of Life," the opening track of The Lion King (1994). He also performed as a member of the film's Sideshow Band on the soundtrack of Water for Elephants (2011), alongside musicians Beresford Bennett, Garnett Brown, George Harper and Bobby Haynes.

Britt served as trumpet coach for actor Damson Idris, who plays Miles Davis in the upcoming film Miles & Juliette.

== Author ==
Britt is the co-author, with Arlene Krieger, of the autobiography The Soloist, which recounts his life and musical career. [ref: The Soloist] [ref: Johnny Britt (Author of The Soloist), Goodreads]

== Personal life ==
Britt has been married to Arlene Britt since 1986. The couple has two children, Joshua and Mariah, and lives in West Hills, California, in the San Fernando Valley, where Britt maintains a recording studio.

== Awards and honors ==
In 2024, the Cathedral Latin Alumni Association named Britt one of its two "Men of the Year," recognizing alumni described by the association as having distinguished themselves in their chosen field. [ref: Man of the Year Inductees, Cathedral Latin Alumni Association]

Britt is a recipient of the President's Lifetime Achievement Award, presented in 2023 by AmeriCorps and the Office of the President of the United States for lifetime volunteer service.

Britt received the Soul Café Radio Indie Soul Award for Group or Duo of the Year in 2024 for "Butterflies," a duet with Will Downing.

Britt received the Soul Café Radio Indie Soul Award for Smooth Jazz Single of the Year in 2025 for "Ocean Waves." [ref: Johnny Britt Wins 2025 Indie Soul Award, Latin Alumnotes]

data.text:
# Raj Gond

The **Raj Gond** (also spelled **Rajgond** or **Raj-Gond**; Hindi: राजगोंड; Telugu: రాజ్ గోండ్) are the historically dominant, aristocratic lineage and ethnolinguistic branch of the Gondi people, an Adivasi community primarily inhabiting the Gondwana region of Central India. They are distributed across the states of Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra (chiefly in Vidarbha), Telangana (concentrated in Adilabad and Kumuram Bheem Asifabad district), Chhattisgarh, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, and Karnataka.

Between the 14th and 18th centuries, Raj Gond dynastic houses established four major sovereign kingdoms in Central India: Garha-Mandla, Chanda (Chandrapur), Deogarh, and Kherla. The ruling houses adopted aspects of Rajput court culture, statecraft, and ritual patronage—a sociopolitical process often cited in anthropological literature as a classic example of "Rajputisation" or "Kshatriyaisation"—while retaining their distinct Dravidian language, religious system, and totemic clan organization.

Raj Gond society is internationally renowned in anthropology due to the foundational field ethnographies of Austrian anthropologist Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf, whose works, including *The Raj Gonds of Adilabad* (1948) and *The Gonds of Andhra Pradesh* (1979), documented their four-phratry social structure (*sagas*), the ritual veneration of clan deities (*Persa Pen*), and their symbiotic relationship with the Pardhan hereditary bards. In modern India, the Raj Gond are constitutionally recognized as a Scheduled Tribe under the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950.

---

## Infobox

| **Raj Gond (राजगोंड / రాజ్ గోండ్)** | |:--- | | **Total population:** Approx. 4–5 million (sub-group of the ~13 million Gondi population) | | **Regions with significant populations:** India: Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Karnataka | | **Languages:** Gondi language (Adilabad Gondi, Northern Gondi), Hindi, Marathi, Telugu | | **Writing systems:** Historically Gunjala Gondi script, Masaram Gondi script; modern usage in Devanagari and Telugu script | | **Religion:** Gondi Punem (worship of *Persa Pen*, *Aki Pen*, ancestral *Sanal*), alongside syncretic Hinduism | | **Related ethnic groups:** Gondi people, Pardhan, Kolam, Maria, Muria, Baiga |

---

## Etymology and Identity

The compound name *Raj Gond* derives from Sanskrit/Hindi *Rājā* (राजा, meaning "king", "royal", or "ruling") and *Gond*, literally signifying the "Royal Gonds" or "Ruling Gonds." Historically, the term denoted the landed nobility, hereditary chieftains (*zamindars*), village headmen (*patels* or *mokashis*), and royal houses of Gondwana, distinguishing them from ordinary cultivators and pastoralists (frequently termed *Dhur Gond*, literally "dust Gonds" or commoners, in colonial-era gazetteers).

Like other branches of the Gond confederation, the Raj Gond refer to themselves endonymously as ***Kōītōr*** (or *Koitur*, *Koya*), which translates in the Gondi language to "human beings" or "people of the hills/earth."

During the height of their political power in the medieval era, Gond rulers patronized Brahmin scholars and genealogists, observed ritual dietary codes, adopted the sacred thread (*janeu*), and contracted political marriages with established Rajput ruling houses—most notably illustrated by the marriage of King Dalpat Shah of Garha-Mandla to the Chandel Rajput princess Rani Durgavati. Despite these outer adoptions of Hindu martial norms, the Raj Gonds remained endogamous within the broader Gond social fabric, maintaining ancestral clan totems, village shrines, and customary laws outside the orthodox fourfold varna system.

---

## History

### Medieval Origins and Rise of Gondwana

Prior to the 12th century, the Central Indian highlands—geographically dominated by the Satpura Range, Vindhya Range, and the basins of the Narmada River and Godavari River—were sparsely documented in imperial Sanskrit and Persian chronicles. As regional empires such as the Kalachuris of Tripuri and the Paramaras fragmented, indigenous Gond chieftains consolidated territorial bastions (*garhs* or hill forts) and established political authority over the region, which came to be known as **Gondwana** ("Country of the Gonds").

Muslim historians of the Delhi Sultanate and Mughal Empire noted the rise of substantial Gond kingdoms by the 14th century, documenting their fortified capital cities, standing armies, cavalry, and extensive agricultural revenue systems.

data.title: Adebola Akinola
data.text:
----

Adebola Akinola is a Nigerian gospel singer, songwriter, performer and choir director based in the United Kingdom. She began releasing recorded music in 2022 with the single “Wonderful God” and has also performed in theatrical and cultural productions incorporating Yoruba folklore. [ref: Adebola Akinola takes 'Wonderful God' global, Punch]

Akinola's performance work has included The Woman Whose Womb Carried the Village, a live music and storytelling piece presented at a Soap Box Spotlight event at the Showroom Cinema in Sheffield in March 2026. The work draws on Yoruba folklore and centres on a woman subjected to rejection because of infertility. A review in The Guardian Nigeria discussed Akinola's vocal delivery and the treatment of the story's themes of love, forgiveness and community judgment. [ref: Adebola Akinola delivers a Yoruba tale of love, hatred, forgiveness at soap box spotlight, The Guardian Nigeria]

== Early life and education ==

Akinola was born on the 7th of August in Lagos, Nigeria. She studied Music Education at Adeniran Ogunsanya College of Education and later studied Library and Information Science at Kwara State University, Malete. She also received musical training through the Musical Society of Nigeria (MUSON). [ref: About, Adebola Akinola]

Before relocating to the United Kingdom, Akinola was involved in church music in Nigeria, including work as a worship leader, choir director and music minister. [ref: About, Adebola Akinola]

== Music career ==

Akinola released “Wonderful God” in 2022. According to The Punch, the song was initially released on Boomplay and was subsequently made available on additional digital music services in 2026. The newspaper reported that the song had accumulated more than 8,000 listeners on Boomplay before its wider release. [ref: Adebola Akinola takes 'Wonderful God' global, Punch]

In May 2026, Vanguard reported on the wider release of “Wonderful God” and described Akinola as a UK-based Nigerian gospel artist, worship minister and choir director. The article also reported the 2023 release of the album Sovereignty. [ref: UK-based gospel artist Adebola takes worship global with 'Wonderful God', Vanguard]

New Telegraph likewise reported in May 2026 that “Wonderful God”, initially released in 2022, had subsequently been made available internationally. The article also described Sovereignty as an album released in 2023. [ref: Nigerian Gospel Artist, Adebola Akinola, Goes Global With Wonderful God, New Telegraph]

== Performance work ==

In March 2026, Akinola participated in The Woman Whose Womb Carried The Village, a live music work presented as part of Soap Box Spotlight at the Showroom Cinema in Sheffield. The production was created and performed by Akinola together with Toby Williams, Gideon Olajide and Segun Lawal. The programme was presented by SBC Theatre and was supported by Showroom Cinema, the Paul Hamlyn Foundation and Arts Council England. [ref: Soap Box Spotlight, SBC Theatre]

The performance draws on Yoruba folklore and tells the story of Morẹnikẹ, a woman who is rejected by her community because she is unable to have children. Reviewing the performance for The Guardian Nigeria, Michael Kolawole discussed Akinola's restrained and intense delivery, while also criticising the treatment of some elements of the story, including the character's unanswered prayer and the village's accountability. [ref: Adebola Akinola delivers a Yoruba tale of love, hatred, forgiveness at Soap Box spotlight, The Guardian Nigeria]

New Telegraph also reported on the Sheffield Soapbox event in April 2026, describing Akinola among the performers at the Showroom Cinema event. [ref: Standing Ovation At Sheffield Soapbox As Mayor Safiya Saeed Praises Adebola Akinola, New Telegraph]

== Awards and recognition ==

In 2023, Akinola received an Award of Excellence at the Kwara Province 1 Music Competition, where Punch reported that she was named Overall Best Winner and Best Vocalist. The information was included in the newspaper's coverage of the subsequent release of “Wonderful God”. [ref: Adebola Akinola takes 'Wonderful God' global, Punch]

In September 2026, THISDAY reported that Akinola received the Eko Best Female Vocalist / Best Vocal Performance Award at the sixth Eko Heritage Awards, held at the Lagos Oriental Hotel in Lagos. [ref: Adebola Akinola Wins Eko Best Female Vocalist Award at 2026 Eko Heritage Awards, THISDAY]

data.title: Narcrisha Norman
data.text:
----

Narcrisha Norman, PhD is an American aerospace engineer, educator, and federal program director at the National Science Foundation (NSF). She currently serves as the inaugural lead of the NSF EPSCoR Graduate Fellowship Program and is a program director for the NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program.

=== Education ===
Narcrisha Norman earned her Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering from Southern Illinois University Carbondale in 2004. She completed her Master of Science in Mechanical Engineering at the same institution in 2006. She received her Ph.D. in Aerospace Engineering from Old Dominion University in 2012. Her dissertation was on modeling Martian planetary entry, descent, and landing using Monte Carlo-driven response surface methodology.

== Career ==

=== National Science Foundation ===
She joined the [https://www.nsf.gov/edu NSF's Division of Graduate Education] in September 2019. In May 2024, she became the inaugural lead of the NSF EPSCoR Graduate Fellowship Program (EGFP), managing a $25 million budget.

Since September 2022, Narcrisha Norman has served as the expert contact for the NSF-Wide Supplemental Funding for [https://www.nsf.gov/funding/opportunities/dcl-supplemental-funding-space-related-preparation-awareness/nsf22-123 Space-Related Preparation and Awareness for Career Equity (SPACE) Dear Colleague Letter], representing NSF on the Vice President's White House Space Council Interagency Working Group.

From April 2020 to March 2021, she co-led the EDU Racial Equity in STEM Education Program, managing a $30 million budget with a team of 12 program directors.

=== Academic Positions ===
Narcrisha Norman served as Associate Professor and Chair of the Engineering Fundamentals program at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University Worldwide from 2015 to 2023.

She held positions as Senior Research Associate at Howard University (2014–2023), where she conducted research in the Applied Fluids-Thermal Engineering Research Laboratory, and served in various teaching and research roles at institutions including J.S. Reynolds Community College, Clemson University, and ECPI University.

Narcrisha Norman was a Fulbright Scholar in Trinidad and Tobago (2018–2019), where she worked with the University of Trinidad and Tobago's Aviation Program to develop research strategies.

=== NASA and USPTO ===
She worked as a Patent Examiner for turbomachinery at the United States Patent and Trademark Office (2011–2012) and participated in NASA's Career Exploration Program at Johnson Space Center (2010) where she analyzed data for mission simulation and instrument modeling for lunar landing flight projects.

== Awards and Honors ==

* 2024: Cash Award for EGFP leadership (NSF)
* 2023: Commendable Service Award (NSF GRFP)
* 2023: Agency Priority Goal Performance Award (NSF)
* 2022: Director's Award (NSF Racial Equity Team)
* 2018: Fulbright Award, Trinidad and Tobago
* 2015: Presidential Management Fellows Finalist
* 2010: NASA Student Ambassador

== Research ==
Narcrisha Norman's research focuses on aerospace engineering, aerodynamics, thermodynamics, and STEM education.

She is a Senior PoSSUM (Polar Suborbital Science in the Upper Mesosphere) Scientist-Astronaut Training Graduate and has been developing expertise in aeronomy and space physics data.

Her technical expertise includes hypersonic, cryogenic system analysis, experimental design, and data analysis.

She has mentored numerous undergraduate and graduate students in research projects ranging from drone intelligence to material characterization for superconducting circuits.

== Publications ==
Narcrisha Norman has published research on aerospace engineering, STEM education, and thermal systems. [ref: Narcrisha Norman, PhD, scholar.google.com] She has also published a book. Some of her notable works include:

* [https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0C2DHH7NN The Suicide Journal (1st ed.)] from [https://doodlepublishinghouse.weebly.com/#/ Doodle Publishing House.] published in 2023
* Her dissertation about Modeling Martian planetary entry descent and landing using Monte Carlo driven response surface methodology, published in 2013 [ref: ‪Modeling Martian planetary entry descent and landing using Monte Carlo driven response surface methodology‬, scholar.google.com]
*Her thesis on Catalytic coal gasification using calcium oxide, published in 2006 [ref: Catalytic coal gasification using calcium oxide, proquest]
*An article titled, Examining the Needs of Adjunct Faculty in a Distance Education Framework in Higher Education, authored with Federica Robinson-Bryant and Yuetong Lin, published in 2020 [ref: Examining the Needs of Adjunct Faculty in a Distance Education Framework in Higher Education, 2020 ASEE Virtual Annual Conference Content Access]

data.title: Ispmanager
data.text:
ispmanager is a commercial web hosting control panel for Linux-based servers. It provides a web interface for administering web, apss, database and mail services without using the command line, and can be installed on physical servers or virtual machines.

Through its interface the panel manages common server software, including the Apache HTTP Server, Nginx and LiteSpeed/OpenLiteSpeed web servers; the MySQL, MariaDB, Percona and PostgreSQL database servers; and an Exim/Dovecot mail server.

== History ==
The first public release of the control panel appeared in 2004. [ref: ISPmanager 2004 announcement]

Version 5 was released in 2014, built on the developer's proprietary COREmanager framework and distributed as deb/rpm packages with data stored in SQLite or MySQL.

Version 6 was released in 2021, adding interface and update improvements, resource monitoring, an updated APS repository and Ansible support. [ref: New versions of the ispmanager panel are available, Introserv]

In March 2022 the product was spun off from its original developer, ISPsystem, into a separate company that focuses solely on the control panel. [ref: ISPmanager separates from ISPsystem and becomes an independent company, ispmanager]

== Editions ==
ispmanager is offered in three editions that differ mainly by the number of supported sites and the availability of features such as Docker virtualization and CloudLinux limits: lite (up to 10 sites), pro (up to 50 sites, with Docker and CloudLinux support) and host (unlimited sites). A 14-day free trial is available.

== Features ==
The panel can configure Apache, Nginx and LiteSpeed/OpenLiteSpeed web servers with per-site version selection for PHP, Python and Node.js. It supports one-click installation of content management systems such as WordPress, Drupal and Joomla, and works with the MySQL, MariaDB, Percona and PostgreSQL databases.

Security and maintenance functions include automatic issuing of Let's Encrypt SSL certificates, scheduled and manual backups to local or external storage, a configurable firewall, Fail2ban, WireGuard VPN, DNSSEC and integrations with third-party protection services. Mail functions cover mail domains, mailboxes, aliases, the Roundcube webmail client and spam/virus filtering.

The panel exposes an API and offers integration with billing systems including HostBill, [ref: ispmanager integration, HostBill] WiseCP, Blesta, ClientExec, WHMCS and BILLmanager. [ref: ispmanager shared hosting provisioning for WHMCS, WHMCS Marketplace] It can restore cPanel and Plesk backup files and transfer users between ispmanager installations.

== Supported operating systems ==
ispmanager supports current versions of Debian, Ubuntu, AlmaLinux and Rocky Linux.

data.title: What Part of Get Thee Gone Don't You Understand?
data.text:
What Part of "Get Thee Gone" Don't You Understand? is a 1997 compilation/reissue by The Geraldine Fibbers, the Los Angeles alt-country band fronted by Carla Bozulich.

It originated as an expanded reissue of the band's self-titled 1994 EP, which featured their early signature song "Get Thee Gone." The reissue was put out in 1997 to showcase the band's earliest days staking out their elegant, often intense country-rock sound.

It was released on February 11, 1997, on Sympathy for the Record Industry (catalog SFTRI 481).

The album contains 16 tracks, and draws from several sources:

Tracks 1–7 were originally released as the earlier EP Get Thee Gone.

Tracks 8–9 come from the Big Jesus 7".

Track 10 is an unreleased demo from November 1994.

Tracks 11–13 were recorded live on KCRW-FM in Santa Monica, and

Tracks 14–15 were recorded live at the El Rey Theatre in Los Angeles in June 1996.

Track 16 was recorded live at the Foothill Club, Long Beach in September 1996

data.title: BarCode Security
data.text:
BarCode is an American cybersecurity media organization founded in 2020 by cybersecurity practitioner and filmmaker Chris Glanden. It began as the BarCode podcast and later expanded into live events, documentary filmmaking, cybersecurity consulting, and other media projects. Its productions include the documentaries Inhuman (2024) and I Am Machine (2025), both directed by Glanden, and the narrative podcast FALLOUT, launched in 2026. [ref: From IT Help Desk to Cyber Storyteller: How Chris Glanden Built a Creative Career in Cybersecurity, CYBR.SEC.Media]

== History ==

=== 2020–2022: Podcast launch ===

BarCode launched as a podcast in September 2020, hosted by Newark, Delaware-based cybersecurity practitioner Chris Glanden. [ref: The BarCode podcast serves cybersecurity talk with a happy hour feel, Technical.ly] The show was created during the COVID-19 pandemic, when many in-person security conferences and networking events had been canceled. Glanden modeled the program after the informal conversations that take place at conference bars and hotel lobbies.

Early episodes included a recurring segment featuring Glanden and a fictional bartender named "Tony", who introduced a cocktail connected to the theme of the episode before the guest interview.

Within its first several months, the podcast featured guests including web security researcher Troy Hunt, cryptographer Bruce Schneier, Metasploit creator H.D. Moore, and former Tenable chief executive Ron Gula.

In 2021, BarCode won the Technology category at the People's Choice Podcast Awards. [ref: Past Winners, People's Choice Podcast Awards]

By 2022, BarCode was also producing live podcast and networking events in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Delaware. [ref: 'Physical cybersecurity' is a thing, and other lessons from off the industry's beaten path, Technical.ly]

=== 2023–present: Expansion ===

In May 2023, Glanden announced Inhuman, a documentary examining the weaponization of artificial intelligence. The independently financed production marked BarCode's expansion into documentary filmmaking. [ref: This Delaware podcaster is behind 'Inhuman,' a documentary on AI weaponization, Technical.ly]

Later that year, Glanden left his cybersecurity consulting role to establish BarCode Security as a consulting business alongside the media operation. [ref: Delaware's BarCode expands into consulting, Technical.ly]

BarCode also continued recording podcasts in front of live audiences. In April 2023, it recorded CISOs Riff on the Latest in Cybersecurity at SecureWorld Philadelphia, featuring cybersecurity executives Krista Arndt, David Lingenfelter, and Bistra Lutz. [ref: InfoSec Leaders Share in Podcast Interview at SecureWorld Philadelphia, SecureWorld]

In 2024, Glanden co-founded the Cyber Circus Network, a collective of independent cybersecurity media creators and organizations.

The podcast recorded its 100th episode during a live event in Las Vegas in 2024. BarCode has also produced live programs in conjunction with cybersecurity events and conferences including BSides Philadelphia, SecureWorld, Hacker Halted, and events held during the annual Black Hat and DEF CON conference period in Las Vegas.

== BarCode podcast ==

The BarCode podcast consists primarily of long-form interviews with people working in cybersecurity and related fields, including security researchers, chief information security officers, penetration testers, social engineers, hackers, and technology executives.

The program combines technical discussions with personal interviews and elements drawn from Glanden's original conference "happy hour" concept. Many episodes have included a cocktail created around the episode's guest or subject.

Guests have included Bruce Schneier, Troy Hunt, H.D. Moore, Ron Gula, Jenny Radcliffe, Joe Grand, Graham Cluley, Sherri Davidoff, Ric Prado, Vivek Ramachandran, Anahi Santiago, John Kindervag, Jack Rhysider, Len Noe, and Higinio "W0rmer" Ochoa.

=== Selected episodes ===

* "SafeHouse" — Troy Hunt (October 6, 2020), founder of the data-breach notification service Have I Been Pwned?.
* "Full Disclosure" — Bruce Schneier (December 18, 2020), cryptographer, security technologist, and author.
* "Rumble" — H.D. Moore (January 22, 2021), founder of the Metasploit Project.
* "Checkmate" — Graham Cluley (May 14, 2021), cybersecurity writer and commentator.
* "Kingpin" — Joe Grand (June 4, 2021), hardware hacker and former member of L0pht Heavy Industries.

== Films ==

=== Inhuman ===

Inhuman is a 2024 documentary directed by Glanden about the weaponization and potential misuse of artificial intelligence. The documentary examines subjects including deepfakes, synthetic voices, generative artificial intelligence, autonomous vehicles, biometric tracking, and algorithmic bias.

=== I Am Machine ===

I Am Machine is a 2025 documentary directed by Glanden that profiles cybersecurity researcher Len Noe and examines the security, privacy, and ethical implications of human-machine augmentation.

The film was screened in several U.S. cities during 2025, including Philadelphia, Austin, Las Vegas, Houston, Grapevine, Texas, and Atlanta.

== Live events ==

Live events have been a recurring part of BarCode since 2022, when the organization began holding podcast recordings and cybersecurity networking events in the Delaware Valley.

The BarCode Live format places podcast interviews in bar and social-event settings rather than traditional studios.

An annual Las Vegas event, BarCode @ BarCode Vegas, began in 2023 during the summer cybersecurity conference season. The 2024 event included the recording of the podcast's 100th episode. The 2025 edition, titled SynCity Soundtrack, combined podcast interviews with live music.

== Other projects ==

=== FALLOUT ===

FALLOUT is a narrative podcast launched in 2026 under the BarCode Studios name and hosted by Chris Glanden and Robert Bradley. Unlike the interview format used by BarCode, FALLOUT uses scripted narration, dramatized scenes, sound design, voice acting, and music to tell stories based on documented technology incidents.

=== GhostLine ===

In 2026, BarCode introduced GhostLine, a browser-based video-interview tool intended to allow interview subjects to conceal their appearance and voice while speaking with a host.

GhostLine uses browser-based video and audio processing to alter a participant's appearance and voice during an interview.

== Chris Glanden ==

Chris Glanden is a cybersecurity practitioner, podcast host, and filmmaker who founded BarCode in 2020. Before launching BarCode full-time, Glanden worked in information technology, security operations, and cybersecurity consulting.

He directed the documentaries Inhuman and I Am Machine and is a co-founder of the Cyber Circus Network.

data.title: Jaeyeol Han
data.text:
Jaeyeol Han (; born 1983) is a South Korean painter who works between Seoul and Berlin. His principal bodies of work include Passersby, based on anonymous people encountered in cities, and Bystanders, which focuses on images of crowds. [ref: 선과 색의 총성, 한재열이 그리는 '얼굴 없는 얼굴', The Korea Economic Daily]

==Life and career==
In 2010, while serving in the South Korean military, Han volunteered for deployment to Haiti for earthquake-recovery work following the 2010 Haiti earthquake. After completing his service, he lived in Ireland and began drawing pedestrians, an activity that developed into the Passersby series.

In 2013, Han received an Excellence Award at the Seoul Digital University Art Awards for Passers-by, Repassage. [ref: '서울디지털대학교 미술상'에 이윤성, Kyunghyang Shinmun] In 2021, he presented the solo exhibition The Gathering, Bystanders at Gallery BK in Seoul, showing work that expanded his earlier individual figures into crowd imagery. [ref: 연말에 놓치면 안 될 회화 전시 4, Esquire Korea]

Han moved his main base to Berlin around the end of 2019 and has since maintained studios in Berlin and Seoul. His work appeared in the Schema Art Museum exhibition SM-Smash#1: Data Material in 2022. [ref: SM-Smash#1: Data Material, Schema Art Museum] Han participated in the group exhibition UNBOXING PROJECT 6: Reading, held at New Spring Project in Seoul from 23 October to 23 November 2025. [ref: Reading, UNBOXING PROJECT] He was selected for the VIRTUAL VITAL special exhibition at Kiaf SEOUL in 2026. [ref: '5년째 동행' 키아프·프리즈 “분리 개최해도 협력 유지…상생하며 발전”, Herald Business]

==Work and technique==
Han removes identifying facial features and indicators of age, gender, and race in order to emphasize anonymity. In a 2015 feature, the Korean art magazine Art in Culture described his use of oil sticks without brushes, noting the physical force of his mark-making and the thick masses of paint that give the work both painterly and sculptural qualities. [ref: [New Look] 한재열: 무명의 얼굴들, Art in Culture]

===Pigment bars===
Han makes and uses solid oil paint sticks that he calls "pigment bars" to obtain particular colors and textures. He holds the material directly against the canvas, applying friction and pressure rather than using a conventional brush; this produces heavily worked, sculptural surfaces. The pigment bars are used in both the Passersby and Bystanders series.

==Major series==
* Passersby: a series based on people observed in the streets of several cities, with individual identifying features broken down or removed.
* Bystanders: a series using montaged images of crowds associated with historical events, disasters, and wars to examine relationships between individuals and groups.

data.title: Jamon Jordan
data.text:
----

= Jamon Jordan =
Jamon “Baba Jamon” Jordan (born January 19, 1971) is an American historian and educator and is the official historian of the City of Detroit. [ref: Jamon Jordan, Detroit’s unofficial historian, is now its official one, BridgeDetroit] He is also the founder of the Black Scroll Network, a Detroit-based organization which offers tours of African American historical sites throughout the city, and is also a lecturer at the University of Michigan, teaching a course in the university’s Semester in Detroit program called “From the Underground to Motown: A Course on Detroit’s History.” [ref: ] [ref: ]

== Early Life and Education ==
Jordan was born and raised in Highland Park and developed an early interest in Detroit’s Black architectural history through stories his grandmother told as a child. He learned about places such as Black Bottom, Paradise Valley, Gotham Hotel, Forest Club, and the Flame Show Bar, all of which weren’t well-documented at the time, though the stories gave him a vibrant picture of the places and people that inhabited these spaces. He was also raised in a household that valued reading, being introduced to works such as The Autobiography of Malcolm X at a young age, which furthered his interest in Black history as a child. [ref: A Storied History: Detroit’s African American Architectural History Lives on Through the Tours of Jamon Jordan, Michigan Architectural Foundation]

He became engaged in the intersection between activism and education during his time at Highland Park High School, where he and other students recognized the inadequate education they were receiving from their teacher. He and these other students would protest against their teacher's poor teaching job in-class, and as a result of this experience, he realized that he wanted to be more proactive as a student. [ref: Jordan, Jamon, Voices from the Grassroots]

He triple-majored in Black Studies, American Studies, and Sociology at Western Michigan University, gaining a more comprehensive view of Black history in the United States and Detroit’s role in it. Outside of class, he challenged racism on campus, joining clubs involved in African American culture and African American resistance to white supremacy, and began a newspaper called The Black Scroll. He graduated with a Bachelor of Science in Black Americana Studies and Sociology.

== Career ==

=== Educator ===
Jordan's first teaching job after returning to Detroit, following a brief stint in Kalamazoo, was at the Ben Carson Academy, a charter school within the Wayne County juvenile detention facility. This position was short-lived though, as he and everyone else who worked there lost their job after the privately-owned school lost their contract with the county.

After working briefly at another charter school in Inkster, he turned to the Nsoroma Institute, an African-centered school. Having read about it in the Michigan Citizen in high school, he saw Nsoroma as a natural fit as he thought his own approach to education was similarly African-centered. While there wasn’t an opening at the time of his interview, he returned two weeks later to follow up, and after teaching a class for another instructor who thought he already worked there, he quickly earned himself a position as a teaching assistant, with a job as a full-time instructor following shortly after. He worked at the Nsoroma Institute for 12 years until it closed in 2013.

Jordan has been part of the University of Michigan's faculty since the Fall 2021 semester, teaching the course “From the Underground to Motown: A Course on Detroit's History," part of the Semester in Detroit program.

=== Black Scroll Network, History & Tours ===
Jordan founded the Black Scroll Network later in 2013 following Nsoroma Institute's closure after providing years of educational tours to students and parents, offering the general public the same experience with African American history in Detroit that his students received. [ref: Jamon Jordan teaches the hidden Black histories of Detroit, Detroit Metro Times] The Black Scroll Network provides guided, educational tours to sites important to Black history in Detroit, with popular sites being Black Bottom, Paradise Valley, the Berry Gordy House, the Motown Museum, and the homes of Aretha Franklin and Rosa Parks. [ref: Historian Jamon Jordan shares the legacy of Black Detroit: "I'm just telling their story" - CBS Detroit, www.cbsnews.com] In the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic, Jordan contracted COVID and lost his mother, promptly ceasing in-person tours. It later shifted to a virtual format [ref: Local historian relaunches Detroit tour company after battling COVID-19, losing mom in 2020, WXYZ 7 News Detroit], with in-person tours returning in mid-2023.

=== Historian of Detroit ===
On October 25, 2021, former Detroit mayor Mike Duggan and City Director of Arts, Culture & Entrepreneurship Rochelle Riley announced that Jordan would be named the first official historian of Detroit.

As city historian, he has been appointed with the job of scouring the archives of Detroit's history and educating people about the stories that haven't been told, as well as reminding the citizens of the importance of the city's history. [ref: Detroit's first historian appointed to tell city's story, FOX 2 Detroit]

He has delivered annual lectures in celebration of Black History Month since 2022 [ref: Jamon Jordan Annual Black History Month Lecture, Detroit Arts, Culture, & Entrepreneurship] among other formal appearances, and is often involved in projects related to Detroit's history. [ref: ] Jordan was the historical consultant for the 2021 film No Sudden Move [ref: ‘No Sudden Move’ Writer Ed Solomon on Drawing From Real History to Craft a 50s Crime Thriller, Collider] and also appears in the documentaries Highland Park 100 Year Anniversary and Legacy Lives On.

Jordan was appointed to the Michigan Historical Commission for a term starting October 12, 2026 by governor Gretchen Whitmer, succeeding Nubia Wardford Polk. This term is due to expire May 21, 2028. [ref: governor-whitmer-makes-appointments-to-boards-and-commissions]

== Personal Life ==
Jordan has been married to Annamarie Jordan since 1997.

data.title: Peach and Goma
data.text:
== Origin: How Peach and Goma Were Created ==
Peach and Goma are fictional cats created by Bu Jue Xiao Xiao, a Chinese artist inspired by her daily life and relationship with her boyfriend. [ref: Who Created Peach and Goma - Story Behind the Adorable Cat Duo, Get Bubu Dudu] First introduced to the world as a sticker series called "Peach Cat", Goma and Peach quickly earned many followings after their fame extended into not only WeChat (the first area they were used as stickers) but Instagram, Twitter (now X), and Youtube.

== Relationship with other characters ==
Despite being created by different artists, [https://english.mathrubhumi.com/lifestyle/who-are-bubu-and-dudu-the-internets-favourite-couple-m1olonjq Bubu and Dudu] are often compared with Peach and Goma. Because of their similar drawing styles and ways of expressing love, Bubu and Dudu are constantly confused with the cat characters. It is notable that the artists of the characters continue to sell merchandise in the same websites. Bubu and Dudu are sometimes expressed as "overshadowed by Goma and Peach" [ref: Why is Bubu and Dudu overshadowed by peach and goma] on media platforms such as Reddit.

== Media appearances/Merchandise (Daily Appearances) ==
This cat couple is often found on animated Youtube clips/songs or social media platforms. They were recently used in a yogurt ad for Chunzhen's Craving Yogurt (Nut&Berry Oat Crunch) [ref: Peach and Goma] and are available as memes on messenger apps such as Kakaotalk(recreated into a Korean version by a Kakaotalk artist, quan, on the app), WeChat, and Telegram. Peach and Goma are also found in online shops such as Peach and Goma Shop or Buy Bubu Dudu, etc. as plushies and mug cups [ref: About Peach and Goma Cat: The Adorable Cat Couple, Peach Goma Official Shop]. Even more than their simple drawing style, Peach and Goma are earning more and more fame from their everyday interactions that show humor and affection people can relate to easily. Couples continue to support and empathize to Peach & Goma, the everyday couple.

== About the Characters ==

=== Appearance & Personality ===
Peach is a fluffy white cat with large eyes and an energetic, playful, and mischievous personality while Goma has gray fur and a gentle personality that contrasts with Peach’s. [ref: About Peach and Goma Cat: The Adorable Cat Couple, Peach Goma Official Shop]

=== Relationship ===
Whether Goma and Peach are a couple or not is currently not revealed by the artist, whereas Netizens continue to guess the two cats' relation. Their relationship is often interpreted as best friends, roommates, or a couple from their humorous and heartwarming gestures and playful interactions. [ref: Are Peach and Goma a Couple? Peach Goma Relationship Explained, Get Bubu Dudu]
