data.title: Progressive Democratic Students' Union (PDSU)
data.text:
= Progressive Democratic Students' Union (PDSU) =
The Progressive Democratic Students' Union (PDSU) is a leftist student organisation in India. George Reddy is considered the founder of PDSU, [ref: 'PDSU founder George Reddy was AP’s Che Guevara', The New Indian Express] although PDSU's official formation happened after George Reddy's death. [ref: ‘George was fearless and continues to be an inspiration', The Hindu]

=== History ===
George Reddy, a student leader and activist, used to publish pamphlets under the label of PDS, which became a state-level organisation following his assassination in 1972. PDS formally changed its name in 1974, leading to the formation of PDSU. [ref: Keeping the Dream Alive: In Memory of George Reddy, Mission Telangana] PDSU is active in Telangana (particularly in Nizamabad and Khammam), Andhra Pradesh and New Delhi. [ref: Progressive Democratic Students Union holds 22nd conference in Nizamabad, Countercurrents] [ref: PDSU lays siege to Bhatti, Thummala offices over Rs. 8,200 crore student dues, Telangana Today] [ref: PDSU protests against privatisation of medical colleges in Andhra, The Hindu] [ref: PDSU alleges linguistic discrimination against non-Hindi-speaking student at JNU, theprint.in] [ref: JNU Student Alleges Linguistic Discrimination and Academic Harassment, dailypioneer.com]

=== Activism ===

==== 2024 protest against delay in release of scholarships and fee reimbursement ====
PDSU Telangana protested outside the State Legislative Assembly in Hyderabad demanding release of scholarships and fee reimbursements. The demands also included allocation of 30% of the state budget to education, justice for the victims of the NEET UG question paper leak, and filling up of the vacant teaching and non-teaching positions in the universities. [ref: Hyderabad: PDSU activists stage protests outside Assembly demanding release of scholarships, fee reimbursement, Telangana Today]

==== 2025 protest against privatisation of medical colleges in Andhra Pradesh ====
In 2025, PDSU demanded that the Andhra Pradesh government revoke the steps taken towards privatisation of medical education. It said that the increasing rate of privatisation of medical colleges would affect students from SC, ST and OBC minority communities. [ref: PDSU protests against privatisation of medical colleges in Andhra, The Hindu]

==== 2026 campaign against academic harassment and linguistic imposition ====
In 2026, PDSU accused an assistant professor at the Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi, of academic harassment and Hindi imposition and demanded an impartial, time-bound inquiry into the assistant professor's actions to ensure a safe learning environment for students. [ref: JNU Student Alleges Linguistic Discrimination and Academic Harassment, dailypioneer.com] [ref: Delhi NCR News: जेएनयू में गैर हिंदी भाषी छात्रा के उत्पीड़न का सहायक प्रोफेसर पर लगा आरोप, Amar Ujala]

data.title: TelaVets
data.text:
TelaVets is an American veterinary telehealth company that provides remote consultations between pet owners and veterinarians. The company was founded by Christine Naoum Long and offers virtual veterinary appointments for animal health concerns. [ref: TelaVets.com founder explains virtual medicine for your pet, FOX 11 Los Angeles] [ref: TelaVets Launches Virtual Vet Platform: Affordable Online Veterinary Care Nationwide, Newsfile Corp.]

== History ==

TelaVets was established by Christine Naoum Long in 2024. In a segment published by FOX 11 Los Angeles in May 2026, Long discussed the experience that inspired her to develop a service through which animals could be assessed by a veterinarian without leaving home.

A launch announcement distributed by Newsfile Corp. and republished on Yahoo Finance on 10 July 2025 described TelaVets as an online veterinary platform offering remote consultations. The announcement identified Long as the company's founder and described its pricing and medication services. Because the item was distributed as a company announcement, it is a primary publicity source rather than independent reporting.

== Services ==

TelaVets offers virtual veterinary consultations through its online platform. The company's website describes remote appointments with veterinarians and states that prescriptions may be provided when clinically appropriate and permitted by applicable law. [ref: About TelaVets, TelaVets]

The company's website lists services for dogs, cats and chickens and describes consultations for common animal health concerns. The suitability of a virtual appointment depends on the condition being assessed and the veterinarian's clinical judgement.

The company also describes medication-related services, including prescriptions and delivery arrangements. Availability depends on the medication, pharmacy arrangements and applicable regulations. [ref: Terms and Conditions, TelaVets]

== Telehealth model ==

Veterinary telehealth enables pet owners to communicate remotely with veterinary professionals. TelaVets uses this model to provide consultations without requiring every initial interaction to take place at a physical clinic.

Remote consultations have limitations. Some conditions require a physical examination, laboratory testing, imaging or other in-person procedures. TelaVets' terms describe the limitations of its service and the circumstances in which remote care may not be appropriate.

== Media coverage ==

In May 2026, FOX 11 Los Angeles published a video segment featuring TelaVets founder Christine Naoum Long. The segment discussed her experience and the idea of providing veterinary consultations remotely.

In July 2025, Newsfile Corp. distributed a company announcement about TelaVets' virtual veterinary platform. The announcement was reproduced on Yahoo Finance and described the company's advertised pricing, consultations and medication-delivery services.

AnimalHealthX published an interview with Long about the company's approach to veterinary telemedicine. The interview discussed the need for timely access to veterinary advice and the intended role of remote consultations in animal care. [ref: Telemedicine Meets Pet Care: Chris Long on TelaVets’ Vision for Healthier Pets, AnimalHealthX]

data.title: Ivan M. Buzurović
data.text:
----

Ivan M. Buzurović is a Serbian-American medical physicist and scientist who works in radiation oncology and medical physics. He is a professor in the Department of Radiation Oncology at Harvard Medical School and Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston, Massachusetts. His research focuses on brachytherapy, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-guided radiation treatment, radiation dosimetry, and methods for improving the accuracy of radiation therapy.

== Academic career ==
Buzurović has conducted research in medical physics and radiation oncology at academic medical institutions in the United States, including Thomas Jefferson University and the Dana-Farber/Brigham and Women's Cancer Center, affiliated with Harvard Medical School. His work combines imaging, computational methods, radiation physics, and clinical treatment planning. [ref: ]Buzurović serves as a clinical mentor in the Harvard Medical Physics Residency Program [ref: Clinical Mentors at BWH: Harvard Medical Physics Residency Program].

== Research ==
Buzurović's research has addressed the development and evaluation of imaging-based methods for planning and verifying brachytherapy treatments. Brachytherapy is a form of radiation therapy in which a radioactive source is placed inside or near a tumor to deliver a prescribed radiation dose. [ref: Brachytherapy for Cancer - NCI, www.cancer.gov]

In 2011, while working as a medical physics resident and researcher in the Department of Radiation Oncology at Thomas Jefferson University, Buzurović co-authored research on a dynamic tumor-tracking technique for radiation therapy.The approach used computer algorithms to predict tumor motion and coordinate the movement of a treatment couch with a linear accelerator, with the aim of improving radiation delivery to moving tumors while reducing exposure to nearby healthy tissue. The research, evaluated through computer simulations, was reported in RSNA News in May 2011. [ref: ]

In 2021, Buzurović and colleagues investigated the feasibility of using MRI alone for high-dose-rate surface brachytherapy, a technique used to treat selected superficial tumors. Their study evaluated whether MRI-based treatment planning could replace conventional computed tomography (CT)-based planning in an appropriate clinical workflow.[2] [ref: Feasibility of magnetic resonance-only high-dose-rate surface brachytherapy for clinical application, Medical Physics]

In 2023, he co-authored research examining catheter reconstruction and dosimetric verification in MRI-only treatment planning for interstitial high-dose-rate brachytherapy. The study investigated the use of a pointwise encoding time reduction with radial acquisition (PETRA) MRI sequence in the treatment of gynecological cancers. [ref: Selection criteria for high-dose-rate surface brachytherapy and electron beam therapy in cutaneous oncology, Journal of Contemporary Brachytherapy]

Buzurović has also contributed to research on treatment selection for cutaneous oncology. A 2021 study published in the Journal of Contemporary Brachytherapy examined criteria for selecting high-dose-rate surface brachytherapy or electron beam therapy for skin cancer treatment. [ref: Selection criteria for high-dose-rate surface brachytherapy and electron beam therapy in cutaneous oncology, Journal of Contemporary Brachytherapy]

In 2023, he co-authored an American Association of Physicists in Medicine (AAPM) medical physics practice guideline on high-dose-rate brachytherapy, addressing technical and clinical practice considerations in the field. [ref: AAPM medical physics practice guideline 13.a: HDR brachytherapy, part A, Journal of Applied Clinical Medical Physics]

His subsequent work has included research on the clinical implementation of MRI-guided surface brachytherapy, optimization of MRI sequences for patient-specific treatment planning, and the geometric accuracy of brachytherapy applicators and catheters. [ref: Feasibility and clinical implementation of MRI-guided surface brachytherapy, Journal of Contemporary Brachytherapy]

In 2026, Buzurović co-authored a study evaluating an adjustable tandem-and-ring applicator intended to improve radiation dose distribution in high-dose-rate brachytherapy for cervical cancer. [ref: A Novel Adjustable Tandem and Ring Applicator for Improved Dosimetry in Cervical Cancer HDR Brachytherapy, Technology in Cancer Research & Treatment]

== Selected publications ==

* Lee, C. Y.; Kaza, E.; Devlin, P. M.; Cormack, R. A.; Buzurović, I. M. (2021). "Feasibility of magnetic resonance-only high-dose-rate surface brachytherapy for clinical application." Medical Physics, 48(11), 7313–7322. doi:10.1002/mp.15224.
* Buzurović, I. M., et al. (2021). "Selection criteria for high-dose-rate surface brachytherapy and electron beam therapy in cutaneous oncology." Journal of Contemporary Brachytherapy, 13(2), 195–204. doi:10.5114/jcb.2021.105288.
* Lee, C. Y., et al. (2023). "Catheter reconstruction and dosimetric verification of MRI-only treatment planning (MRTP) for interstitial HDR brachytherapy using PETRA sequence." Physics in Medicine & Biology, 68(3). doi:10.1088/1361-6560/acaf48.
* Richardson, S. L., et al. (2023). "AAPM medical physics practice guideline 13.a: HDR brachytherapy, part A." Journal of Applied Clinical Medical Physics, 24(3). doi:10.1002/acm2.13829.
* Lavelle, M. J., et al. (2024). "Feasibility and clinical implementation of MRI-guided surface brachytherapy." Journal of Contemporary Brachytherapy, 16(1), 48–56. doi:10.5114/jcb.2024.135647.[7]
* Lavelle, M. J., Kaza, E., Devlin, P. M., and Buzurović, I. M. (2025). "Comparison of optimized magnetic resonance sequences for patient-specific treatment planning in surface brachytherapy." Medical Physics, 52(10), e70031. doi:10.1002/mp.70031.
* Kaza, E., and Buzurović, I. M. (2026). "Geometric accuracy of surface high-dose rate brachytherapy applicator and catheters identified using Dixon volumetric interpolated breath-hold examination magnetic resonance images." Physics and Imaging in Radiation Oncology, 38, 100955. doi:10.1016/j.phro.2026.100955.

data.title: Manju Shivraj Singh
data.text:
Manju Shivraj Singh (also published as Manju Kumari Singh) was an Indian cookery writer. She was the author of The Spice Box (1981), Royal Indian Cookery: A Taste of Palace Life (1987) and Shaakaahaari: Indian Vegetarian Cookery (1997).

== Early life ==
In 1964 she married Shiv Raj Singh, an entomologist then at the Indian Agricultural Research Institute; his career took the family to Ibadan, Nigeria, where he worked at the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture from 1973 to 1990, to Ithaca, New York in 1979–80, and to Washington, D.C., where he joined the World Bank in 1991. [ref: Shiv Raj Singh, Prabook]

== Writing ==
Her first book, The Spice Box: Vegetarian Indian Cookbook, was published by the Crossing Press of Trumansburg, New York, in 1981. [ref: The Spice Box: Vegetarian Indian Cookbook, Crossing Press]

Royal Indian Cookery: A Taste of Palace Life followed in 1987, published by Windward in Britain and McGraw-Hill in the United States. [ref: Royal Indian Cookery: A Taste of Palace Life, Windward] [ref: Royal Indian Cookery: A Taste of Palace Life, McGraw-Hill] It was reissued in India by Zaika, Mumbai, in 2002. [ref: Royal Indian Cookery: A Taste of Palace Life, Zaika]

Writing as Manju Kumari Singh, she published Shaakaahaari: Indian Vegetarian Cookery with HarperCollins India in 1997, [ref: Shaakaahaari: Indian Vegetarian Cookery, HarperCollins Publishers India] and Vegetarian Indian Cooking with India Research Press, New Delhi, in 2002. [ref: Vegetarian Indian Cooking, India Research Press]

== Death ==
Manju Shivraj Singh died in 2020. Her husband survived her and died in Jaipur on 13 December 2022. [ref: Obituary: Dr. Shivraj Singh, The Times of India]

== Bibliography ==

* Royal Indian Cookery: A Taste of Palace Life. Leicester: Windward, 1987.; New York: McGraw-Hill, 1987.; Mumbai: Zaika, 2002..

OHL (ONE HUNDRED LIMINAL) is a seven-member Japanese dance and vocal group, also known as Wanlimi (ワンリミ). Its official fan name is PIECE (ピース). The group is managed by 1NE Entertainment. [ref: MUSICIAN, 1NE Entertainment]

== Overview ==
In 2021, leader JUNYA brought together KTA, RYUSEI, SHURU and GEN to perform with him. They later decided that the performances they wanted to create called for a seven-member group, and formed the current line-up with NAO and KANNA.

When the COVID-19 pandemic caused their previous agency's plans to be cancelled, the youngest member, GEN, initiated the establishment of a company to keep the group together and preserve its freedom of expression, and the group resumed its activities.

The members operate as a DIY group, handling their own music, choreography, costumes and live-show production.

The group has three units: OHL-D, focused on dance; OHL-R, focused on rap; and OHL-V, focused on vocals.

The group's name expresses the idea of "unlocking a hundred forms of potential and creating a supernatural phenomenon in society".

The group aims to perform at the Nippon Budokan.

The fan name PIECE reflects the idea that "each person who supports us is an essential piece in the story of OHL. Together, we will build on the story we began from zero and complete one big puzzle".

data.title: Catherine Lezer
data.text:
Catherine Lezer is an Australian local government politician, property investor, and businessperson who has served as an independent Councillor for the City of Perth since 2020. [ref: Elected Members, City of Perth Official Website] Alongside her council duties, Lezer holds roles in strata property advocacy and state heritage governance. [ref: Catherine Lezer Official Website]

== Early Life and Education ==
Born and raised in Perth, Western Australia, Lezer's professional background is in business and corporate governance. She holds a Bachelor of Business, a Master of Business Administration (MBA), and qualifications from the Australian Institute of Company Directors (AICD).

== Professional Career ==
Prior to entering local government, Lezer built a career as a property investor, mortgage broker, and advocate for inner-city and strata living. Since 2015, she has been involved with the Strata Community Association (SCA), previously serving on both the New South Wales and Western Australia boards. [ref: SCA WA President Report 2022, Strata Community Association] [ref: SCA WA President Report 2023, Strata Community Association] She remains active within the organization, including hosting and presenting at events such as the CHU SCA (WA) 2026 Owners Conference. [ref: CHU SCA (WA) 2026 Owners Conference, Strata Community Association (WA)]

In 2021, Lezer was appointed to the board of the Heritage Council of Western Australia, where she advises on state heritage planning and preservation. [ref: New Chair and members appointed to the Heritage Council of WA, Government of Western Australia] [ref: Heritage Council of Western Australia Annual Report 2025-26, Government of Western Australia] She has also served on audit and risk committees for both the SCA and the Department of Planning, Lands and Heritage.

== Political Career ==

=== City of Perth Council ===
Running as an independent candidate advocating for apartment residents and sustainable urban design, Lezer was first elected to the City of Perth Council in 2020, placing third with 6.34% of the vote under the first-past-the-post system. [ref: Lord Mayor Basil Zempilas unveils the team driving new-look City of Perth, The West Australian]

She was re-elected in 2023, being the first candidate to reach quota with 16.57% of the vote under the newly introduced optional preferential voting system, securing a term running until October 2027. Within the council, she serves as Chair of the Audit, Risk and Improvement Committee.

=== Mayoral Candidacy ===
Following the departure of Lord Mayor Basil Zempilas to State Parliament in early 2025, Lezer was the first candidate to announce her candidacy for Lord Mayor, running under the campaign slogan "independent, proven, ethical". [ref: Perth councillor Catherine Lezer first to put hand up to replace Basil Zempilas as Perth Lord Mayor, The West Australian] During her campaign, she completed the national Pathways to Politics Program for Women as part of the 2025 Western Australian cohort. [ref: Recommendations for your pathway to politics: Cr Catherine Lezer, Pathways to Politics] She narrowly lost the election by 70 votes.

=== Council Initiatives ===
During her tenure on the council, Lezer initiated and supported various urban policy proposals:
* 2021: Initiated targeted grant programs to assist strata complexes with sustainability upgrades, waste management, and building reports.
* 2021: Introduced an apartment recycling yellow bag initiative.
* 2022: Passed a motion to install a rainbow street crossing to celebrate diversity. [ref: Northbridge gets new bold rainbow street art, OUTinPerth]
* 2024: Passed a motion advocating for additional green open space and pocket parks.
* 2025: Initiated a program encouraging the conversion of vacant spaces into residential homes.
* 2025: Passed a motion regarding security enhancements on Central Area Transit (CAT) buses.
* 2025: Unsuccessfully proposed a motion to install playground fencing to enhance public safety. [ref: Request to fence inner city kids playground after anti social behaviour knocked back, PerthNow]
* 2026: Passed a motion for modifications and extensions to CAT bus routes to improve precinct connectivity. [ref: CAT bus route extension needed for struggling East Perth businesses, PerthNow]
* 2026: Passed a motion to install public lighting along Langley Park and Riverside Drive. [ref: Let there be light: call to install lighting along Perth riverfront, PerthNow]
* 2026: Unsuccessfully introduced a motion proposing a cost-saving budget review package. [ref: City of Perth councillor wants art project binned as $168m of projects left unbudgeted, PerthNow]

=== Council Voting and Positions ===
* E-scooters: In 2025, Lezer voted against continuing the city's e-scooter hire scheme citing safety concerns; the motion was defeated, though the scheme was later suspended following a major incident in May 2025. [ref: City of Perth votes to continue e-scooter scheme despite calls for deferral ahead of medical report, The West Australian]
* Night Parking: In 2025, she voted to retain free night parking in the CBD, but was in the minority as the council reintroduced paid night parking. [ref: City of Perth council ends free night parking in the CBD and increases parking fees, PerthNow]
* Workplace Culture Review: In 2025, Lezer successfully moved to overturn a council workplace culture review motion, citing procedural flaws. [ref: Perth acting CEO calls council's decision to undertake workplace culture review as unlawful and flawed, quits, The West Australian]
* Infrastructure Projects: In 2025, she voted in favour of a proposed helicopter landing pad in West Perth, which was rejected by the broader council. [ref: Perth council grounds Rinehart's helipad plans for $270m Hancock headquarters, The Sydney Morning Herald]
* Travel Restrictions: In 2026, Lezer twice proposed motions to suspend ratepayer-funded council travel during ongoing Local Government Inspector investigations and the state fuel emergency; both motions failed to pass. [ref: Calls to immediately suspend ratepayer-funded travel over fears of City of Perth debt, The West Australian] [ref: Business class travel for Perth council members immediately suspended as city tries to avoid serious debt, The West Australian] [ref: Lord Mayor calls proposed council travel ban during fuel crisis more symbolic than practical, The West Australian]
* Executive Leadership Dispute: In 2026, following the sudden departure of Chief Executive Officer Michelle Reynolds, Lezer publicly criticized council leadership's process and introduced a motion calling for Reynolds' reinstatement. [ref: Tensions run high at Perth council meeting over former CEO's sacking, WAtoday] [ref: Perth council blocks CEO return as investigation continues, WAtoday] [ref: City of Perth councillor calls for sacked CEO reinstatement, Business News WA] [ref: Perth Mornings, ABC Radio Perth]

data.title: Jochi Ritz-Olewski
data.text:
----

Jochi (Jocheved) Ritz-Olewski (15 March 1947 – 10 February 2024) was an Israeli activist involved in preserving the memory of the Holocaust and the heritage of Bergen-Belsen. She served as chair of the Bergen-Belsen Survivors Organization in Israel from January 2022 until her death in February 2024. She was the first woman, and the first person born in the Bergen-Belsen displaced persons camp, to chair the organization. She was also editor-in-chief of the organization's international journal, Our Voice. [ref: History in the Belsen organization in Israel: Jochi Ritz-Olewski, born in Bergen-Belsen, elected chairperson of the organization, Bergen-Belsen Survivors Organization in Israel]

== Early life ==
Ritz-Olewski was born Jocheved-Rivka Olewski on 15 March 1947 at the Glyn Hughes Hospital in the Bergen-Belsen displaced persons camp in Germany. [ref: שורדת השואה האהובה והפעילה החברתית יוכי ריץ-אולבסקי הלכה לעולמה, mynet Ra'anana] [ref: Babyboom in Bergen-Belsen, Jüdische Allgemeine]

Her parents, Rachela Zelmanowicz-Olewski and Rafael Gershon Olewski, were Holocaust survivors. Her mother had been imprisoned at Auschwitz, where she played the mandolin in the Women's Orchestra of Auschwitz. Her father survived Auschwitz III–Monowitz (Buna) and Bergen-Belsen and later became a journalist, writer and one of the founders and chairmen of the Bergen-Belsen Survivors Organization in Israel.

Her parents met after liberation and married in Celle, Germany, in 1946. In April 1949 the family immigrated to Israel. They initially lived in Bnei Brak and later moved to Ramat Gan.

She served in an intelligence unit of the Israel Defense Forces, where she acquired the nickname "Jochi".

== Education and career ==
Ritz-Olewski studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, earning a bachelor's degree in English and French as well as a teaching certificate. She later earned a master's degree with distinction in public administration from Bar-Ilan University.

Early in her career, she worked at the Technion – Israel Institute of Technology, where she coordinated a pre-academic preparatory program.

In 1978 she joined the Open University of Israel. During her career there she held administrative positions in the Dean of Academic Studies' office and served for many years as deputy dean of academic studies. [ref: University authorities, Open University of Israel] [ref: סוגרת מעגל: תושבת רעננה שנולדה בברגן בבלזן חנכה השבוע במקום מרכז הנצחה, mynet Ra'anana]

She retired from the Open University in 2014.

== Holocaust remembrance and Bergen-Belsen activities ==
Alongside her professional career, Ritz-Olewski was active in the Bergen-Belsen Survivors Organization in Israel. She joined its leadership after people born in the displaced persons camp and members of subsequent generations became involved in the organization, and later served as deputy chair.

She represented the Israeli organization in the international advisory framework associated with the Lower Saxony Memorials Foundation in Germany.

In 2012 Ritz-Olewski signed a declaration calling for the preservation of the former Bergen-Belsen displaced persons camp area, historically significant buildings and the Jewish cemetery, and for their incorporation into the Bergen-Belsen memorial landscape. [ref: Jahresbericht 2012, Stiftung niedersächsische Gedenkstätten]

In 2019 she participated in efforts that led to the transfer of five historic buildings in the former displaced persons camp area to the Lower Saxony Memorials Foundation for preservation and educational use.

That year she was also involved in the organization's campaign against the auction of a historic Bergen-Belsen rabbinical court ledger, arguing that documents of Holocaust-era historical significance should remain accessible to the public. [ref: Bergen-Belsen survivors petition court to halt sale of camp ledger, The Jerusalem Post]

== Our Voice ==
Ritz-Olewski and her brother Arie Olewski revived Our Voice, the journal of the Bergen-Belsen Survivors Organization in Israel. The publication continued the tradition of the Yiddish newspaper Unzer Sztyme, which had been published in the Bergen-Belsen displaced persons camp after the Second World War and with which their father Rafael Olewski had been involved.

Ritz-Olewski served as editor-in-chief of Our Voice, which covered Bergen-Belsen survivors, the displaced persons camp, later generations and the preservation of the community's historical memory.

== Chair of the Bergen-Belsen Survivors Organization in Israel ==
Ritz-Olewski was elected chair of the Bergen-Belsen Survivors Organization in Israel and began serving on 1 January 2022, succeeding Shraga Milstein.

She remained chair until her death in February 2024. In March 2024 her brother, Arie Olewski, was elected chair of the organization. [ref: Arie Olewski is the new Chairman, Bergen-Belsen Survivors Organization in Israel]

== Personal life ==
Ritz-Olewski married Oded Ritz in 1969. They initially lived in Haifa and moved to Ra'anana in 1978. They had three children. Oded Ritz died in 2020.

Ritz-Olewski died on 10 February 2024 at the age of 76. [ref: Jochi Ritz-Olewski, chair, passed away, Bergen-Belsen Survivors Organization in Israel]

data.title: Kotaro Horiuchi
data.text:
----

is a Japanese architect and urban planner. He is the founder and chief executive of Kotaro Horiuchi Corp. (stylised KOTARO HORIUCHI; ), and works from Paris, Tokyo and Ishigaki Island across architecture, interior design, furniture and spatial design. [ref: X-Knowledge Includes a one-page profile of Horiuchi with several of his projects.] His early work in Paris was published in the European and Japanese design press, [ref: kotaro horiuchi architecture: salon du fromage, Designboom] [ref: Shōtenkenchiku] and in 2019 he was the only Japanese finalist in the international open competition to reimagine the roof of Notre-Dame de Paris. [ref: Forest Roof — The People's Notre-Dame Design Competition, GoArchitect]

== Biography ==

=== Education and early career ===
Kotaro Horiuchi was born in Nagoya, Aichi Prefecture, and studied architecture and urban design at the graduate school of Meiji University, completing his master's degree in 2004. [ref: Nikkan Sugoi Hito! The outlet's name translates roughly as "Daily Amazing Person!", a Japanese web magazine of interview profiles.] While a student he represented Japan at the 1st International Architecture Biennale Rotterdam (2003) with a work on Tokyo, "Tokyo Ring Project / Visible Area Map".

During the same period he gained experience at several European offices: in 2003 at Mecanoo in Delft, the Netherlands, led by Francine Houben, and as an assistant at the summer school of the Architectural Association in London; in 2004 at PPAG in Vienna; and from 2005 to 2009 at the office of Dominique Perrault in Paris, known for the Bibliothèque nationale de France. [ref: Dominique Perrault Architecture, Éditions HYX / Centre Pompidou Exhibition catalogue, Centre Pompidou, Paris, 11 June – 22 September 2008.] According to Nikkan Sugoi Hito!, this itinerary across the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Austria and France left him working in six languages.

=== Practice ===
In 2005 Horiuchi founded his own practice, Kotaroo Architecture, in Paris. He incorporated the firm in 2009 as Kotaro Horiuchi Architecture Inc., reorganised it in 2015 under the name Kotaro Horiuchi, [ref: Kotaro Horiuchi, France News Digest] [ref: Kotaro Horiuchi, Japanese architect in France, French Code] and established Kotaro Horiuchi Corp. in Tokyo in 2020. [ref: JIA Bulletin Self-authored; used only for uncontroversial biographical detail.] He now works from Paris, Tokyo and Ishigaki Island, and holds a first-class registered architect qualification (, ikkyū kenchikushi); he is also a PADI Master Instructor.

One of his best-known early built works is the Paris cheese shop salon du fromage HISADA (2010), at 47 Rue de Richelieu. Working within an existing 18th-century building on a narrow site, he clad the interior and exterior in graded aluminium studs and arranged a ground-floor sales area beneath an upper floor used for cooking classes, wine-and-cheese gatherings and events. [ref: Bamboo Media] The project was published in the Japanese trade magazine Shōtenkenchiku in 2011. It was followed by The Roof Residence (2011) in Maintenon, France, where three dwellings and a restaurant are gathered beneath a single perforated roof that opens the interior toward the surrounding landscape. [ref: kotaro horiuchi architecture: the roof residence, Designboom]

=== Notre-Dame competition ===
In 2019 Horiuchi was selected as a finalist (second place) in "The People's Notre-Dame Cathedral Design Competition", an open, participatory competition organised by GoArchitect of the United States that invited the public to imagine the future of Notre-Dame de Paris after the 2019 fire. From 226 entries submitted from 56 countries, six finalist teams were chosen by a public vote of more than 30,000 people; the finalists came from five countries, and the only Japanese-led entry was "Forest Roof", a proposal to crown the cathedral with a garden-like canopy. [ref: Results of the People's Notre-Dame competition, Pragmatika] The finalist proposals, including "Forest Roof", were later collected in the book Top 50 Visions of Notre Dame (2019). [ref: Top 50 Visions of Notre Dame A compilation of the competition's finalist proposals, including the "Forest Roof" entry led by Horiuchi.]

=== One Sapporo Station Tower ===
Horiuchi provided design supervision for the main-entrance façade and common areas of One Sapporo Station Tower, a residential high-rise (48 storeys, about 175 m) directly connected to Sapporo Station as part of the Kita-8 Nishi-1 urban-redevelopment project. Completed in 2023, it is the tallest building in Hokkaido; its developers include Daiwa House, Sumitomo Realty & Development and Tokyu Land. [ref: Sora no Ma — Skyscape for All, Houzee Awards / Architecture Collection] The project received a Platinum award at the 2024 Houzee Awards [ref: Platinum Winner 2024 — One Sapporo Station Tower, Houzee Awards / Architecture Collection] and six Gold certifications at the 2026 Grands Prix du Design (organised by Agence PID, Canada), where it also received the jury's Grand Prize and the public People's Choice Award. [ref: One Sapporo Station Tower — Urban Thresholds, Grands Prix du Design (Agence PID)] In 2027 the project received a German Design Award from the German Design Council. [ref: One Sapporo Station Tower — Urban Thresholds, German Design Council]

== Design approach ==
Since the beginning of his career, Horiuchi has pursued research into perforation — openings he calls ana ("hole" in Japanese) — in façades. [ref: ANA Glass by Kotaro Horiuchi, Sky Design Awards The project statement notes that ana means "hole" in Japanese and likens looking through the glass's opening to glimpsing the lattice of a Kyoto machiya.] Drawing on the reversal of visibility seen in the timber lattices (kōshi) of Kyoto townhouses — where an interior barely visible from outside by day is revealed by light at night — he studies the light, shadow, depth and moiré effects produced by the shape, density and layering of openings, using physical models and computer imagery. Extending the idea from façades to furniture, lighting, glassware and jewellery, he presents much of this research through annual solo exhibitions conceived as installations that visitors enter and experience physically rather than as displays of drawings and models. [ref: Kotaro Horiuchi, monographs kotaro horiuchi 2010, kotaro horiuchi 2012 and kotaro horiuchi 2014.]

== Selected projects ==

* 2025–: The Ubufuru Ishigaki, Ishigaki Island, Japan — ongoing renovation of the former Ishigaki Resort Hotel, which was acquired in 2025 by Hirugi LLC, a vehicle of Ryukyu Capital's Ryukyu Fund No. 2, [ref: Okinawa Times] and operates under the PDS HOTELS brand of Plan Do See; [ref: Ryukyu Shimpo] Horiuchi provides project management and construction-design supervision. [ref: The Ubufuru Ishigaki Official website.]
* 2024: One Sapporo Station Tower (Kita-8 Nishi-1 district, Sapporo), design supervision, Japan
* 2024: Jewelrscape (scenography for the LARICH jewellery exhibition), SAA SPACE, Osaka, Japan [ref: Rosway Co., Ltd. (PR TIMES)]
* 2019: ANA Glass (perforated wine glass whose name refers to ana, Japanese for "hole"; made by Sugahara Glassworks) [ref: ANA Glass — Gold Winner 2022, Architecture & Design Collection Awards] [ref: ANA Glass by Kotaro Horiuchi, MUSE Design Awards]
* 2019: Forest Roof (the "Floating Forest" proposal for the Notre-Dame de Paris competition), Paris, France
* 2014: Fusionner 3.0, Paper Cave and Fusionner (installations), Nagoya, Japan [ref: Kotaro Horiuchi creates a paper hideout for Fusionner 3.0 installation, Dezeen] [ref: Kotaro Horiuchi creates a Paper Cave inside his architecture studio, Dezeen] [ref: Kotaro Horiuchi creates human Whac-A-Mole with membrane installation, Dezeen]
* 2012: Membrane in Stratum, Nagoya, Japan [ref: kotaro horiuchi architecture: membrane in stratum, Designboom]
* 2011: The Roof Residence, Maintenon, France
* 2010: salon du fromage HISADA, 47 Rue de Richelieu, Paris
* 2009: Taipei Music Center (competition entry), Taipei, Taiwan [ref: B1 Magazine, 2010.]
* 2008: Nagoya Funeral Hall, Nagoya, Japan [ref: architecturephoto.net]

== Exhibitions ==

* 2024: Jewelrscape, LARICH exhibition (scenography), SAA SPACE, Osaka
* 2010: Flottant, Galerie Grand E'terna, Paris [ref: Événements, Galerie Grand E'terna]

== Awards ==

* 2027: German Design Award, Winner, for One Sapporo Station Tower (Germany)
* 2026: Grands Prix du Design (19th edition), six Gold certifications plus the jury Grand Prize and the People's Choice Award, for One Sapporo Station Tower (Canada)

data.title: Advanta IRA
data.text:
----

== Advanta IRA ==
Headquartered in Clearwater, Florida, Advanta IRA Services, LLC is a private U.S.-based company that provides administrative and recordkeeping services for self-directed individual retirement arrangements (IRAs) and other qualified plans and savings accounts. [ref: Tampa Bay Business Journal, Tampa Bay Business Journal]

In 2024, the Tampa Bay Business Journal described Advanta IRA as a multibillion-dollar self-directed retirement account administrator. As of mid 2026, the company reports holding approximately $4 billion in assets under administration. [ref: Why Advanta IRA, Advanta IRA]

== History ==
Jack Callahan is the founder and president of Advanta IRA. With decades of experience in financial services and real estate, Callahan has spoken on self-directed retirement strategies and regulatory compliance. [ref: ]

Advanta IRA was originally founded in 2003 and began operating as an affiliate of The Entrust Group under the name Entrust of Tampa Bay. Callahan added another location, Entrust of Georgia, located in Atlanta, in January 2009. [ref: ADVANTA IRA SERVICES, LLC - LEI: 254900VLUCG2CCN7N325, Bloomberg LEI]

The company changed its name to Advanta IRA Services, LLC in December 2011. It became independent of The Entrust Group’s franchise program in January 2012. [ref: The Entrust Group Announces the Dissolution of its Franchise Program, www.theentrustgroup.com]

Throughout its 20+ year history, Advanta IRA has grown in both client base and assets under administration. Advanta IRA was named to Florida State University's Seminole 100 list of fastest-growing alumni-owned or alumni-led businesses in 2020, 2021, and 2022, ranking 58th, 71st, and 55th, respectively. [ref: ] [ref: ] [ref: ] The Seminole 100 list, which recognizes the fastest-growing companies owned or led by alumni of Florida State University, is presented annually by the Jim Moran Institute for Global Entrepreneurship at Florida State University.

In 2024, the company relocated its corporate headquarters from Largo to Clearwater, Florida. According to the Tampa Bay Business Journal, the move followed a period of operational growth.

In 2025, Callahan formed Advanta Trust Company, Inc., a Nevada-chartered trust company established to serve as a qualified custodian for self-directed accounts. [ref: Retail Trust Companies as of April 20, 2026, Nevada Financial Institutions Division] As of 2026, client assets administered by Advanta IRA are held in custody by Advanta Trust Company. [ref: Advanta Trust Company Launches as Nationwide Custodian for Self-Directed IRAs and Tax-Advantaged Accounts, Yahoo Finance]

== Services ==
Advanta IRA provides administrative services for self-directed IRAs and other retirement and savings plans. These accounts include traditional IRAs, Roth IRAs, SEP and SIMPLE IRAs, solo 401(k)s, health savings accounts (HSAs), and Coverdell education savings accounts (ESAs). [ref: Types of Self-Directed IRA Accounts, Advanta IRA]

The firm administers accounts used for alternative investments in real estate, gold, private placements, private lending, and limited liability company (LLC) structures (commonly referred to as checkbook IRAs). [ref: IRA Alternative Investments, Advanta IRA]

Advanta IRA facilitates account setup, documentation, and compliance reporting in accordance with Internal Revenue Service (IRS) regulations. The company does not offer investment advice or sell investments. Clients maintain full control over their investment choices and decisions. [ref: Beyond Stocks and Bonds: Is a Self-Directed IRA Right for You?, pro.thestreet.com]

== Educational Resources and Outreach ==
Advanta IRA produces educational content related to self-directed accounts and  alternative investments, including webinars, podcasts, articles, and frequently asked questions addressing investment structures and IRS regulations. Representatives of the company participate as speakers on third-party podcasts and webinars focused on alternative investments and self-directed accounts. [ref: ] [ref: Retiring soon? Expert explains how IRAs and 401(k) work, The Independent] [ref: REIAGC Speaker Profile for Larissa Greene, www.cincinnatireia.com] [ref: Bitcoin Q&A for Business Owners – Tax, Mining, and Retirement]

== Regulatory Compliance ==
Self-directed accounts administered by Advanta IRA are subject to federal tax laws and regulations governing individual retirement accounts and qualified plans, including contribution limits, required minimum distributions (RMDs), prohibited transactions, and reporting obligations. [ref: ] [ref: ]

In an interview with TheStreet, Advanta IRA’s Vice President of Sales, Scott Maurer, stated that Advanta IRA performs administrative functions in accordance with these regulations, but does not sell or vet investments. Account holders and their financial team are responsible for due diligence and compliance.

== References ==

data.title: Charlie Matthews
data.text:
----

Charlie Matthews (born May 10, 1991) is an American fashion model and social media personality. He is known for his advertising campaigns with GUESS, including the brand’s Seductive Noir fragrance campaign, and for his work in fashion publications including DAMAN, Wonderland, and MMSCENE.

Early life

Matthews was born in Los Angeles, California, and grew up in Anaheim. He is a first-generation Serbian American.

Before pursuing modeling, Matthews participated in competitive video gaming tournaments during his teenage years.

Matthews was discovered by a modeling scout while working at a grocery store in California. He subsequently moved to New York City to pursue professional modeling.

Career

Modeling

Matthews began his professional modeling career in the 2010s. His early work included a national advertising campaign for Nautica and an appearance in Arena Homme Plus.

He subsequently worked on campaigns for Calvin Klein, Skechers, Target, Adidas, and Jeremy Scott.

In 2017, Matthews began a professional association with American fashion brand GUESS. He appeared in advertising for the company’s clothing, accessories, eyewear, and fragrances.

In 2019, Matthews appeared alongside Kelsie Smeby in the GUESS Seductive Noir fragrance advertising campaign, photographed by Josh Ryan and directed by Paul Marciano.

In 2022, he appeared in GUESS’s spring/summer clothing and accessories campaigns, photographed by Yasmine Kateb. That year, Wonderland published an interview with Matthews discussing his five-year association with the brand.

Editorial and magazine appearances

Matthews has appeared in fashion editorials and interviews for international publications.

In September 2017, he was interviewed by MMSCENE for its eighteenth issue.

In 2021, Matthews appeared in a cover story for the June/July issue of DAMAN, which discussed his modeling career and work with GUESS and Calvin Klein.

His career was also profiled by Socialite Life in 2019 and Wonderland in 2022.

Social media and gaming

Alongside his modeling career, Matthews has maintained a presence on Instagram and TikTok, publishing content related to fashion, entertainment, and his personal interests.

Matthews has also discussed his background in competitive video gaming in media interviews. His interest in gaming predates his professional modeling career.

Personal life

Matthews is of Serbian descent and was raised in Southern California. In interviews, he has discussed his interest in video games and fashion.

data.text:

Alan Dolan is a British breathwork practitioner and founder of Breathguru, an organisation dedicated to teaching Conscious Connected Breathing. He conducts individual sessions and workshops in London and online, residential retreats in Lanzarote, and professional training programmes for breathwork practitioners. [ref: 'I feel totally seen': John Crace on how guided breathing soothed a lifetime of anxiety, The Guardian] [ref: Jeremy Clarkson, Claudia Winkleman and India Knight amongst others review the best treatments from around the world, The Sunday Times]

== Career ==

Originally from Manchester, Dolan worked in corporate communications before changing careers and training as a breathwork practitioner. He subsequently established a base in Lanzarote, Spain, where he conducts residential breathwork retreats. [ref: Meet Alan Dolan, the Breath Guru, The Sunday Times]

Dolan began working as a breathing coach in 2005. His work focuses on Conscious Connected Breathing, a technique involving continuous breathing without pauses between inhalation and exhalation. [ref: Are breathing techniques good for your health?, The Guardian] [ref: Breathwork With Alan Dolan, West London Living]

In addition to working with individual clients, Dolan trains other practitioners in breathwork facilitation. By 2020, he had trained 24 practitioners to lead breathing sessions.

Through Breathguru, Dolan offers a 12-month, 400-hour professional training and mentoring programme, delivered with fellow practitioner Natalia Blake. The programme combines online teaching and supervised practice with residential training modules in Lanzarote. [ref: Breathguru Training & Mentoring Programme, Breathguru]

data.title: Vanessa Ragland
data.text:
----

Vanessa Ragland is an American comedian, actress and theater producer. She is the co-owner and co-artistic director of Dynasty Typewriter, a comedy and performance venue in the Westlake neighborhood of Los Angeles, and co-hosts the podcast Pop My Culture.

== Early life and education ==
Ragland grew up in a rural area with little access to the arts. She earned a bachelor's degree in acting from Virginia Tech and briefly studied toward an MFA in poetry at the University of North Carolina Wilmington before moving to Los Angeles.

== Career ==
=== Performing ===
Ragland performed with The Groundlings, including as a member of its Sunday Company. Her television credits include The Office, Men of a Certain Age and New Girl. She played Chastity, a teacher's assistant, in the 2010 independent comedy Jeffie Was Here; a review from the Phoenix Film Festival singled out her brief comic performance. She played Jenny in The Late Bloomer (2016), a comedy directed by Kevin Pollak. In October 2014, several outlets reported on similarities between a Tina Turner impersonator sketch Ragland and Kimberly Condict had written and performed with the Groundlings and a Saturday Night Live sketch that aired that month; an unnamed source close to SNL attributed the resemblance to parallel thinking. With Cole Stratton she co-hosts Pop My Culture, an interview podcast about film, television and music; in 2011 Rolling Stone ranked it second on its list of the ten best comedy podcasts. She has also co-hosted Totally Mommy, a comedic parenting podcast that The Washington Post included in a 2016 list of recommended parenting podcasts.

=== Dynasty Typewriter ===
Ragland met Jamie Flam more than a decade before founding the venue, when she interned at the comedy theater where he worked and the two joined the same improv team. In 2010 they staged a comedy benefit at the Hayworth Theatre for the Leukemia & Lymphoma Society. Over about a year and a half, they wrote a business plan, negotiated a lease on the Hayworth Theatre, and ran a $100,000 Kickstarter campaign to open Dynasty Typewriter, which held its first performance on November 16, 2017. Ragland and Flam co-own the venue and serve as co-artistic directors, curating its programming together.

In 2019, The New York Times reported that the venue had established itself within two years as a home for unconventional comedy programming, hosting performers including Sarah Silverman, Bob Odenkirk and Margaret Cho, with residencies by Marc Maron, Eddie Izzard and Hannah Gadsby. In 2022 the Los Angeles Times featured Ragland among women booking the city's stand-up venues, noting her role in booking the club and growing it into a leading local comedy venue.

data.title: Memorygram
data.text:
Memorygram is an American company that produces printed memoir books from personal stories collected through written, recorded, and telephone responses to guided questions. It also sells memorial products that link to online memorial pages.

== History ==
According to a 2022 interview published by The Ancestor Hunt, Memorygram began operating in August 2021 and launched its service in November 2021. The founder interviewed, Sara Damiano, described herself as a clinical social worker and gerontologist and said the company was created as a legacy-building tool for individuals and families. Later coverage credits childhood friends Paul Damiano and Larry Scharra with creating the company.

== Products ==
=== Legacy Book ===
The Legacy Book is a service in which a storyteller answers questions about their life, family, and experiences. Responses can be typed, recorded in a web browser, sent by text message, or given during an automated, AI-based telephone interview. Spoken answers are transcribed and edited into written prose, and users can attach photographs to each story. The finished stories are printed as an 8.5 by 11 inch hardcover book that includes a QR code linking to the original audio recordings. More than one storyteller can contribute to a single book, and a Spanish-language version is offered.

=== Memorial Medallion ===
The Memorial Medallion is a custom-engraved medallion bearing a person's name, birth year, and year of death, designed to be placed on a headstone, urn, or indoor memorial. Scanning its QR code opens an online memorial page where visitors can view photos and videos, leave memories, and listen to recordings from the Legacy Book. The medallion also includes a feature that uses a voice sample and information about the deceased to generate a conversational recreation of the person's voice.

=== Other products ===
Memorygram also offers Tribute Books for occasions such as graduations, retirements, weddings, and memorials.

data.title: Novak (2025 film)
data.text:
Novak (Greek: Νόβακ) is a 2025 Greek-Swiss science fiction drama film written and directed by Harry Lagoussis in his feature directorial debut. The film stars Zlatko Burić as a former neuroscientist whose abandoned research attracts the attention of a group of young scientists and activists in Athens. Ella Rumpf, Yannis Papadopoulos and Elena Topalidou also star. [ref: 'Novak' review: Zlatko Buric's convincing mad scientist elevates this offbeat Greek debut, Screen Daily] [ref: Novak (2025), IMDb]

The film had its world premiere in competition at the Edinburgh International Film Festival on 17 August 2025. It subsequently screened at the Thessaloniki International Film Festival in November 2025. It was theatrically released in Greece on 25 June 2026. [ref: Edinburgh International Film Festival 2025 Official Guide, Edinburgh International Film Festival] [ref: Novak, Move It]

== Plot ==

Dr. Nikola Novak, a Croatian former neuroscientist, lives in isolation in Athens, haunted by a mysterious past. His secluded existence is interrupted when a group of idealistic young scientists and activists becomes interested in his forgotten research into electromagnetic fields.

Novak is drawn into their collective, which aims to create a community protected from electromagnetic pollution. The group offers him an opportunity to resume his scientific experiments and regain a sense of purpose and belonging.

However, tensions begin to emerge within the commune as ideological differences and personal conflicts threaten the group's cohesion. As Novak becomes increasingly immersed in the collective's ambitions, his pursuit of a scientific breakthrough places his own stability and the future of the community at risk.

== Cast ==

* Zlatko Burić as Dr. Nikola Novak
* Ella Rumpf as Louise
* Yannis Papadopoulos as Petros
* Elena Topalidou as Maria

== Production ==

Novak was written and directed by Greek filmmaker Harry Lagoussis as his first feature film. It is a co-production involving Greece, Switzerland and India, with the production companies Heretic, Cloud Fog Haze Pictures and Stone Bench Films. [ref: Novak, Heretic] [ref: Novak (2025), Letterboxd]

The film was produced by Giorgos Karnavas, Michael Graf, Sara Bonakdar, Kaarthekeyen S and Danae Spathara.

The cinematography was handled by Yorgos Koutsaliaris, with production design by Elena Vardava, editing by Dimitris Polyzos and an original score composed by Haris Neilas. [ref: Novak, Thessaloniki International Film Festival]

=== Music ===

The film's original score was composed by Haris Neilas. Its soundtrack also features a selection of existing recordings, including by Tiny Tim, The Fiery Furnaces, The Seeds, Hardy Fox and Richard Wagner. [ref: Novak (2025) – Soundtracks, IMDb]

== Release ==

Novak had its world premiere on 17 August 2025 in the feature competition at the Edinburgh International Film Festival.

The film subsequently had its Greek premiere at the 66th Thessaloniki International Film Festival.

The film was theatrically released in Greece on 25 June 2026.

data.title: Awasi (company)
data.text:
Awasi is a Chilean hospitality company, headquartered in Santiago, that operates five small lodges in Chile, Argentina and Brazil. Founded in 2007 with the opening of Awasi Atacama in San Pedro de Atacama, it built lodges near Torres del Paine National Park (2013) and Iguazu Falls (2018), and acquired existing hotels in Santa Catarina, Brazil, in 2024 and in Mendoza, Argentina, in 2025. Each room is assigned its own guide and four-wheel-drive vehicle, and excursions are planned individually rather than on a fixed schedule. All five lodges hold Michelin Keys, with Awasi Patagonia holding three.

== History ==
The name Awasi derives from the Quechua word wasi, meaning "house". The company was founded by Matías de Cristóbal, an Argentine former banker. Its first lodge, Awasi Atacama, opened in 2007 as one of the first high-end hotels in the area, followed by Awasi Patagonia in November 2013 and Awasi Iguazú in 2018, the company's first property in Argentina. Since 2024, Awasi has been owned by the Argentine group Grupo Faro Verde.

At the end of 2024 Awasi acquired Ponta dos Ganchos, a resort that opened in 2002 in Governador Celso Ramos, Santa Catarina, and had been a Relais & Châteaux member from 2005 to 2014, and renamed it Awasi Santa Catarina. In 2025 it took over Cavas Wine Lodge in Luján de Cuyo, Mendoza, which had opened in 2005 as one of the first hotels built within a winery, and renamed it Awasi Mendoza. Both properties adopted Awasi's fully hosted model, which includes meals, beverages and private guided excursions.

In 2025–2026 the company invested about R$20 million (US$4 million) in Awasi Santa Catarina, moving the pool to the cliff edge and adding a spa, gym, boats and a larger guiding team, and renewed vehicles and facilities at its other lodges.

== Properties ==
{| class="wikitable sortable"
! Lodge !! Location !! Country !! Opened !! Units !! Michelin Keys
|-
| Awasi Atacama || San Pedro de Atacama || Chile || 2007 || 12 || 2
|-
| Awasi Patagonia || Torres del Paine || Chile || 2013 || 16 || 3
|-
| Awasi Iguazú || Puerto Iguazú, Misiones || Argentina || 2018 || 14 || 2
|-
| Awasi Santa Catarina || Governador Celso Ramos || Brazil || 2002; Awasi since 2024 || 25 || 2
|-
| Awasi Mendoza || Luján de Cuyo, Mendoza || Argentina || 2005; Awasi since 2025 || 17 || 2
|}

Awasi Atacama has 12 rooms built of stone, adobe and thatch in San Pedro de Atacama, a town at about 2,400 m at the foot of the Licancabur volcano; its architect worked with a local historian to model the rounded buildings on nearby pre-Inca ruins.

Awasi Patagonia, designed by Chilean architect Felipe Assadi, consists of 16 villas and a main lodge built of native lenga wood on a private conservation area northeast of Torres del Paine National Park, on a hillside above Lake Sarmiento facing the Torres del Paine peaks.

Awasi Iguazú has 14 villas on stilts, each with a private pool, set on a slope above the Iguazú River in a private Atlantic Forest reserve about 20 minutes from the falls. The lodge was designed by Argentine designer Eugenia Chorén with the Awasi team, using local stone and wood and decoration by nearby Guaraní communities.

Awasi Santa Catarina occupies a peninsula on the Emerald Coast, about 45 km from Florianópolis, with 25 standalone villas.

Awasi Mendoza has 17 villas on a vineyard estate in the Agrelo wine district, at the foot of the Andes.

== Operations ==
Awasi assigns each room a private guide and a four-wheel-drive vehicle, so guests set their own itineraries instead of joining group excursions. All five lodges are members of Relais & Châteaux. Awasi Santa Catarina, Awasi Iguazú and Awasi Mendoza offer guests the choice between a fully hosted stay and a bed-and-breakfast rate.

== Conservation and community ==
Awasi Iguazú and Awasi Patagonia together protect about 340 hectares of native forest, and the company describes its operations as carbon neutral. Awasi Patagonia runs on a combination of solar and diesel power, reuses wastewater for irrigation, and leases part of the surrounding ranch to move livestock off the land and restore wildlife habitat. In Misiones, the Iguazú lodge runs workshops with a local Guaraní community and sells its crafts to guests; in Patagonia, guides run nature and outdoor-skills workshops in rural schools. Awasi Santa Catarina keeps hives of native stingless bees, grows its own leafy greens and uses no pesticides on the property.

== Recognition ==
* Michelin Guide (2026 edition): three Keys for Awasi Patagonia and two Keys for each of the other four lodges; Awasi Santa Catarina rose from one Key to two in 2026. The guide lists Awasi Patagonia as one of two Three-Key hotels in Torres del Paine.
* Condé Nast Traveler: Readers' Choice Awards (2017) and Gold List (2019) for Awasi Atacama.
* Condé Nast Traveller Triple Crown (2026), awarded to hotels on its Hot List, Gold List and Readers' Choice Awards: Awasi Patagonia and Awasi Mendoza.
* Travel + Leisure World's Best Awards (2026): Awasi Atacama, Awasi Iguazú and Awasi Santa Catarina among the World's 100 Best Hotels; all five lodges among the Best Resorts in South America.
* Travel + Leisure Most Luxurious New Hotels in the World (2025): Awasi Santa Catarina.
* Travel + Leisure It List: Awasi Iguazú (2019) and Awasi Santa Catarina (2026).
* The Telegraph World's 50 Greatest Hotels (2024): Awasi Patagonia.
* La Liste Top 1000 Hotels (2026): Awasi Patagonia, with a score of 99.

data.title: Suzanne Scott (scholar)
data.text:
Suzanne Scott is an American media scholar is an associate professor in the Department of Radio-TV-Film at the University of Texas at Austin. [ref: Suzanne Scott, The University of Texas at Austin: Moody College of Communication] Previously, Scott previously taught Film and Media Studies in the Department of English at Arizona State University, as well as undergraduate and graduate courses at University of California, Santa Cruz, University of California, Los Angeles, and the University of Southern California. She also served as a Mellon Digital Scholarship Postdoctoral Fellow in the Center of Digital Learning + Research at Occidental College.

Scott is the author of Fake Geek Girls: Fandom, Gender, and the Convergence Culture Industry (2019). She has also co-edited a number of books including The Routledge Companion to Media Fandom (2018) and Sartorial Fandom: Fashion, Beauty Culture, and Identity (2023).

== Education and personal life ==
Scott graduated from New York University with a B.F.A. in Cinema Studies and Journalism, she then earned her M.A. and Ph.D. in Critical Studies from the University of Southern California. Scott's doctoral dissertation, Revenge of the Fanboy: Convergence Culture and The Politics of Incorporation (2011) was supervised by Ellen Seiter, Tara McPherson, and Henry Jenkins.

== Books Published ==

data.title: Hitmarker
data.text:
----

Hitmarker is a British online recruitment platform for the video game industry, esports and related
creator and entertainment businesses. Founded in Newcastle upon Tyne in 2017, it lists jobs from game
studios, publishers, esports organisations and content creators, and describes itself as the largest jobs
platform for gaming and esports.

== History ==
Hitmarker was founded by Philip Huggan and launched in mid-2017 as a jobs platform for the esports industry;
his brother Richard Huggan joined later that year and became managing director.
It later broadened from esports to the wider games industry.

In 2019 the company ran an equity crowdfunding campaign on Crowdcube, seeking a minimum of £80,000 for
4% of its equity, and reached 207% of that target within seven days.
A second Crowdcube round in December 2020 raised approximately €568,000 to fund expansion into new markets.
The company states that both rounds were led by Ironmonger360, the investment vehicle of Duncan Ironmonger,
co-founder and former chief executive of the controller maker Scuf Gaming, and that Ironmonger Properties made a
further strategic investment in 2025.

In April 2026 Hitmarker launched Hitmarker Pro, a subscription hiring product for games companies with
applicant tracking, AI-assisted candidate matching and automation.

== Platform ==
Employers post vacancies, and candidates create profiles and apply. Roles span game development (engineering,
art, design, audio, production), esports, community and content, marketing and business functions.
According to the company, more than 200,000 jobs have been posted on the platform, and by 2024 it had over
300,000 registered members and around one million annual users.

data.title: Deafness in Sweden
data.text:
== Deafness In Sweden ==

Sweden is home to around 8,000 deaf sign language users and 600 Swedish Sign Language interpreters. [ref: Sweden, European Union of the Deaf] Sweden was one of the first countries to recognize their official sign language, Swedish Sign Language (also known as SSL or STS). The country did so in 1981 and implemented bilingual education soon after in 1983. Sweden signed onto the UN Committee on Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD) in 2007 and it was ratified it a year later. Their own law is sufficient in following the rules outlined in the UN CRPD but is continuing to implement more policies outlined in the CRPD as time goes on. Sweden has good infrastructure to facilitate early intervention for deaf or hard of hearing children as around 95% of children are screened for hearing loss at birth and those children are referred to rehabilitation centers that facilitate access to hearing technology and other necessary therapies. Sweden has a bilingual education system as outlined in their national curriculum which is applied in both deaf schools and mainstream schools. Today, around 90% of Swedish deaf or hard of hearing children receive cochlear implants which impacts where they are sent to school, however placement in deaf schools is still recommended by the Swedish government.

=== Human/Civil Rights ===
The World Federation for the Deaf is an organization that focuses on ensuring the human and civil rights for all Deaf people are protected by their individual legislatures. [ref: Human Rights - World Federation of the Deaf, https://wfdeaf.org/] They do this by referring to the UN Committee on Rights for Persons with Disabilities (UN CRPD) which addresses some key areas of concern for disabled persons across the world. [ref: Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, OHCHR] They specifically focus on the following sections:

* Article 2 – Definition
* Article 9 – Accessibility
* Article 21 – Freedom of expression, opinion, and access to information
* Article 24 – Education
* Article 30 – Participation in cultural life, recreation leisure and sport

These are all detailed in the UN CRPD which is why the following section refers to that document to assess the state of human and civil rights for the deaf in Sweden.

The UN CRPD was signed in Sweden in 2007 and ratified in 2008. Sweden's law was found to be in good accordance with the UN CRPD so not much changed as far as the state legislation or the available resources [ref: Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities - Combined second and third periodic reports submitted by Sweden under article 35 of the Convention pursuant to the optional reporting procedure, due in 2019]. However, parts of the UNCRPD have been adopted into Swedish law, for example, as of 2013, the European Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms (ECHR) and as of 1 January 2020 the Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC). These have both been signed into law in Sweden. These are considered preemptive efforts and the Swedish government plans to continue to evaluate the effects of incorporating these conventions before continuing to incorporate the UNCRPD in its entirety into law.

Despite the amount of legal protections, Swedish citizens have voiced that there is still room for improvement in the disability rights of deaf and hard of hearing people in Sweden [ref: Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities - List of issues in relation to the initial report of Sweden, adopted by the Committee at its tenth session (2–13 September 2013)]. The most recent report from 2023 replies to complaints that the implementation of disability policy has been a particular shortcoming saying that the Swedish government has many systems in place to observe implementation on state, local and regional levels. Swedish citizens have also asked for the Swedish government disclose the specific parts of the Swedish disability legislation to see if it falls in line with the things outlined in the UN CRPD as they feel as though it is not being appropriately implemented and that the UN CRPD does in fact need to be adopted in it's entirety. The point being made in these reports is that despite the fact the Swedish government has most of their bases covered legally, they are not actually implementing policy in the ways they should be.

=== Sign Languages ===
Swedish Sign language is the recognized sign language in the state of Sweden and has about 8,000 scattered speakers making up about.1% of the population [ref: ]. It is a deaf community sign language used since 1800 with the first deaf school established in 1809. Swedish sign language is sometimes referred to as SSL and sometimes referred to as STS. Sweden recognized sign language first in 1981 giving Swedish signers access to interpretation in public places as well as access to Swedish Sign Language use in school [ref: ]. The Language Law of 2009 recognizes SSL in a way similar to the other 5 minority languages (Sámi, Finnish, Meänkieli, Romani Chib, and Yiddish) making it a more official recognition that requires its promotion and encouragement and makes acquisition of deaf education easier.

Finland- Swedish Sign Language also known as FinnSSL is another sign language present in Sweden despite its emergence at a deaf school in Finland [ref: Finland-Swedish Sign Language]. The language is much less popular and is actually considered an endangered language with only about 300 speakers remaining. The language borrows from Finnish Sign Language (FinSL), Swedish Sign Language (SSL), and Swedish. It is a deaf community sign language that developed in conjunction with the founding of the first deaf school in Porvoo, Finland. The school closed in 1993 and the language died out with it. Most people switched to FinSL after its popularity dwindled despite the fact that is was mainly developed from SSL.

=== Newborn Hearing Screening ===
Newborn hearing screenings are not mandated but, over 95% of newborns in Sweden are screened for hearing at birth. [ref: A Survey on the Global Status of Newborn and Infant Hearing Screening, Journal of Early Hearing Detection and Intervention] 2.1% of newborns screened fail their screening and 1.8% of kids screened are determined to have hearing loss. For those newborns who do get screened, receiving a diagnosis happens between 1-14 months of age with the mean age being 6 months old and receiving treatment happens around the same time. For those who do not get screened, receiving a diagnosis happens most at 38 months (3 years) and receiving treatment happens around the same time. 90% of screenings take place at birth facilities and 2% take place at ENT/Audiology Clinics. However, 30% of screenings are done by audiologists, 30% are done by nurses and 40% are done by midwives.

=== Early Intervention ===
In Sweden, children have access through the medical system to rehabilitation centers that connect them with the necessary resources to be referred to audiologists and possibly receive hearing aids or cochlear implants as well as state-sponsored introductory sign language courses for families [ref: Communication, Information, and Support for Swedish Parents with Deaf or Hard-of-Hearing Children, Scandinavian Journal of Disability Research].

There are two main perspectives on the development of DHH children that are widely accepted in Sweden; cultural-linguistic and medical. Parents are often met with the medical perspective first and due to this, the wide access that Swedish DHH children have to hearing aids and cochlear implants is the first and therefore best intervention that parents hear about.

There are many organizations that serve DHH children in Sweden, some adopting the cultural-linguistic perspective and some adopting the medical perspective, these organizations are often at odds with each other as one camp believes the other is not informing parents enough of their options.

Parents note that professionals from both camps (cultural-linguistic and medical) introduce them to the importance of SSL and give them resources to take courses in the language. However, most families stop taking courses after an introductory course offered by the County Council.

=== Deaf Education ===
The state of Sweden has a public, compulsory education for children aged 7-16 [ref: ]. These schools are inclusive of students with all abilities as required by the state including visual and hearing disorders. There was a large scale school reform in 1962 that was not fully recognized until 1980 that supported children with special education needs being in class with their non-disabled peers.

As Swedish Sign Language (SSL) was recognized as an official language in Sweden in 1981, access to bilingual education in both Swedish and SSL began to spread across the country as early as 1983 [ref: Bilingual education for deaf children in Sweden, International Journal of Bilingual Education and Bilingualism]. This education model existed mainly in specialty schools for the deaf where SSL is the primary language of instruction and Swedish is taught mainly as a written language. However, as the state encourages all schools to be inclusive of deaf and hard of hearing students, this model also exists for deaf students in mainstream public schools. Later, the national curriculum was revised to require the bilingual model as opposed to recommending it and added that deaf children gain proficiency in written English as well.

Today, Swedish families have more autonomy with where their child goes to school. It was at one time assumed that all deaf children would prefer to go to a special school but with the popularization of Cochlear Implants in Sweden (around 90% of children born deaf are implanted), fewer deaf or hard of hearing children attend specialty schools for the deaf. However, regardless of the kind of school a deaf or hard of hearing student attends, the Swedish government stresses the importance of bilingual education.

data.title: A. Jordan Wright
data.text:
Andrew Jordan Wright, who publishes as A. Jordan Wright, is an American clinical psychologist known for his work on psychological assessment, including assessment training, tele-assessment, and the role of culture in assessment. He is a clinical associate professor at NYU Steinhardt [ref: Jordan Wright, New York University Steinhardt] and served as president of the Society of Clinical Psychology (American Psychological Association Division 12) in 2025. [ref: The Clinical Psychologist, The Clinical Psychologist]

== Education ==
Wright received a master's degree in psychology in education from Teachers College, Columbia University in 2001 and a PhD in clinical psychology from Columbia University in 2005. [ref: Andrew Jordan Wright, Society for Personality Assessment]

== Career ==
From 2006 to 2011, Wright was on the faculty of Teachers College, Columbia University, where he coordinated training in psychological assessment. From 2007 to 2011 he also directed the mental health department of The HOPE Program, a workforce development organization in Brooklyn. From 2011 to 2017 he was on the faculty of SUNY Empire State College, where he served as statewide chair of psychology.

Wright joined NYU Steinhardt in 2017. He is a clinical associate professor in the Department of Applied Psychology, directs the combined clinical and counseling psychology PhD program, and is the founding director of the program's training clinic, the Center for Counseling and Community Wellbeing.

Wright joined Parallel Learning, a company that provides virtual special education and related services to schools, as an advisor in 2021 and became its chief clinical officer in 2022. [ref: Dr. Jordan Wright, Parallel Learning]

== Professional service ==
Wright was president of the Society of Clinical Psychology's assessment section in 2017, president-elect of the Society of Clinical Psychology in 2024, and its president in 2025. In 2021 he chaired the APA Board of Educational Affairs. [ref: Board of Educational Affairs 2021 Annual Report, American Psychological Association] He chaired the APA task force that developed guidelines for education and training in psychological assessment in health service psychology, published in American Psychologist in 2020.

He is president of the American Board of Psychological Assessment (formerly the American Board of Assessment Psychology) and serves on the executive board of the Society for Personality Assessment (2025–2027 term). Since 2024 he has been an associate editor of the journal Professional Psychology: Research and Practice. [ref: Editorial Board for Professional Psychology: Research and Practice, American Psychological Association]

== Recognition ==
Wright is a fellow of the American Psychological Association through Division 12 (Society of Clinical Psychology, 2022) and Division 17 (Society of Counseling Psychology, 2025), and a fellow of the Society for Personality Assessment (2015). He is board certified by the American Board of Psychological Assessment (2012) and by the American Board of Professional Psychology in clinical psychology (2022).

He received the Association of Psychology Training Clinics' Spruill Award in 2024 [ref: APTC Bulletin: Practicum Education & Training Announcements, Association of Psychology Training Clinics] and the Society for Personality Assessment's Distinguished Service and Contribution to Personality Assessment Award in 2025. [ref: Distinguished Service and Contribution to Personality Assessment Award, Society for Personality Assessment]

== Research ==
Wright's research covers training and supervision in psychological assessment, the equivalence of remote and in-person cognitive testing, cultural factors in assessment, and the measurement of microaggressions experienced by LGBTQ people. With K. Constantine, he developed the Wright–Constantine Structured Cultural Interview (WCSCI), a free structured interview for evaluating the cultural context of an individual. [ref: Wright-Constantine Structured Cultural Interview (WCSCI), NYU Steinhardt]

== Selected books ==

* Handbook of Psychological Assessment, Wiley
* Essentials of Psychological Assessment Supervision, Wiley
* Essentials of Psychological Tele-Assessment, Wiley
* Essentials of Culture in Psychological Assessment, Wiley
