data.title: Samantha Storr
data.text:
Samantha Storr is an American producer known for her work in virtual reality, augmented reality, and immersive media. She has served as Head of Content at Meta Reality Labs, overseeing the virtual reality fitness application Supernatural, and previously held leadership roles at Within and Here Be Dragons (formerly Vrse.works).

== Early life and education ==

Storr lives in Los Angeles with her husband and son. She attended the Hewitt School in New York City and earned a degree in Communications from Boston University. [ref: Samantha Storr – LinkedIn]

== Career ==

Storr began her career producing music videos and commercials, working with artists including the Beastie Boys and collaborating with film and commercial directors. Her early producing credits include Last Day Dream (2009), a short film directed by Chris Milk for the 42 Second Dream Film Festival; [ref: Last Day Dream, Vimeo] Fight for Your Right Revisited (2011), a short film directed by Adam Yauch that premiered at the Sundance Film Festival; [ref: Beastie Boys: Fight for Your Right Revisited, Radio Times] [ref: The House That Yauch Built, uDiscoverMusic] the Beastie Boys' "Don't Play No Game That I Can't Win" featuring Santigold (2011), directed by Spike Jonze; [ref: Advertising Age — 2011 to 2012, Advertising Age (via Internet Archive)] their "Make Some Noise" (2011), directed by Adam Yauch; [ref: 2011 MTV VMA Nominee List, HipHopWired] Demi Lovato: Stay Strong (2012), a documentary produced by RadicalMedia; [ref: Demi Lovato to Participate in Live Q&A Tuesday on MTV, NBC Today] The Legend of Hallowdega (2010), directed by Terry Gilliam; [ref: Craig DeLeon — Selected Credits, Evolution Music Partners] the 2013 YouTube Music Awards, directed by Spike Jonze; and Cathedrals of Culture (2013), a documentary series executive produced by Wim Wenders with an episode directed by Robert Redford. [ref: Cathedrals of Culture — Cast, TV Guide] [ref: Cathedrals of Culture — Credits, Box Office Mojo]

She also produced branded entertainment, including Toyota's "Project Endeavour" (2012), in which a Toyota Tundra towed the Space Shuttle Endeavour to the California Science Center; [ref: Tundra Endeavour 'Ultimate Journey', The One Club] Sony and Intel's "Project Shiphunt" (2011), an online adventure series; [ref: An @[user] Departure For 180LA: High School Students Go On Nautical Adventure For Sony VAIO, SHOOTonline] and the second season of GT Academy USA (2012), a Nissan and PlayStation reality competition series, on which she served as showrunner. [ref: Lauded Branded Entertainment, Part 2: GT Academy, SHOOTonline]

In 2013, Storr collaborated with director Chris Milk on Hello, Again, a virtual reality project featuring Beck. The interactive 360-degree concert film was commissioned by Lincoln and produced by RadicalMedia. [ref: A New Vision For Sound: Chris Milk Breaks Down How 'Beck: Hello, Again' Was Made, Fast Company] The project won two Cannes Gold Lions and one Bronze Lion in 2013, along with two Webby Awards. [ref: Beck "Hello, Again" — Awards, Zachary Richter] [ref: The Man Behind Beck's 360-Degree Sound and Vision, Billboard]

In 2014, Storr and Milk co-founded Vrse.works, a virtual reality production company that later became Here Be Dragons. She served as Vice President of Content from 2014 to 2017, overseeing documentary, branded, and narrative virtual reality productions. [ref: Evolution of Vrse, Webby Awards] [ref: FutureHero Samantha Storr: The heroine of virtual reality, Atlas of the Future] [ref: Vrse — Atlas of the Future, Atlas of the Future]

Projects produced during this period include Clouds Over Sidra (2015), created in collaboration with the United Nations and premiered at the World Economic Forum in Davos. The film, produced by Storr and directed by Gabo Arora and Chris Milk, follows a twelve-year-old Syrian girl in Jordan's Za'atari camp and was the first virtual reality film made for the UN. [ref: UN Launches Powerful, First Ever, VR Film following Syrian Refugee Girl, TechCrunch] [ref: UN Agencies team up to bring voices of Syrian refugees to world leaders through Virtual Reality, ReliefWeb (United Nations)] It won the Interactive Award at Sheffield Doc/Fest in 2015. [ref: 'Syrian Love Story' wins Sheffield Doc/Fest prize, Screen Daily]

She was also a key collaborator on Waves of Grace (2015), a virtual reality experience by Gabo Arora and Chris Milk following Ebola survivor Decontee Davis in Liberia, featured in the New Frontier program at the 2016 Sundance Film Festival. [ref: Sundance Institute Celebrates New Frontier 10th Anniversary at 2016 Festival, Sundance Institute]

Storr also executive produced The Displaced (2015), a virtual reality documentary produced in collaboration with The New York Times that followed the lives of three refugee children from South Sudan, Ukraine, and Syria. [ref: NY Times teams with Google on virtual reality project, Associated Press] The project won the Entertainment Lions Grand Prix at the Cannes Lions in 2016, the first such award given in the Entertainment category. [ref: Cannes Lions Entertainment Grand Prix Bestowed Upon NY Times' 'The Displaced', SHOOTonline] [ref: Times Virtual Reality Film Wins World Press Photo Award, The New York Times (Lens Blog)] [ref: New York Times VR Project Displaced Takes Best in Show AICP Next Awards, SHOOTonline] [ref: Virtual Reality Journalism Puts You Inside the Refugee Crisis, VICE] [ref: 37th News & Documentary Emmy Nominations, Deadline (via National Academy of Television Arts & Sciences)]

In 2017, Storr joined Within as Vice President of Content. There, she oversaw the launch of projects including Wonderscope (2018), an augmented reality storytelling app for children, and Supernatural, a virtual reality fitness application developed for the Meta Quest platform. [ref: VR Fitness App Supernatural on UMG Licensing Deal Impact, Billboard] [ref: Supernatural: Feel The Real, Ads of the World]

Wonderscope won the Children's BAFTA for Digital in 2019 for its inaugural story "A Brief History of Stunts by Astounding People." [ref: Within Makes Wonderscope AR Kids Story Library Available for Free, Animation Magazine] [ref: Bafta Children's Award winners announced, Televisual]

Supernatural was named one of TIME magazine's Best Inventions of 2020 [ref: The 100 Best Inventions of 2020, IP CloseUp (reproducing TIME list)] and received Fast Company's Innovation by Design Award in the Apps and Games category. [ref: Supernatural — Innovation by Design 2020, Fast Company]

In February 2023, Meta completed its acquisition of Within after a FTC antitrust challenge was resolved in Meta's favor. [ref: Meta acquires Within despite FTC concerns, TechCrunch] Storr continued in her role as Head of Content at Meta's Reality Labs, overseeing creative direction and production for Supernatural VR, until January 2026.

data.title: Dromeryda Agyapong
data.text:
----

Dromeryda Agyapong is a Ghanaian entrepreneur, designer and philanthropist.She is the founder and CEO of Turq-Stones Limited, a company involved in construction, architectural and spacial interior design and business consultancy.She also established Turq-Design Studios, a creative agency specializing in branding, visual identity and digital experiences [ref: Turq Design - We Design Brands People Remember, www.turqdesign.com]and La mere Foundation, an initiative focused on supporting post natal mothers and women entrepreneurs [ref: Turq-Stones CEO Dromeryda Agyapong named 'Ghana’s Best in Construction' at Forty Under 40 Awards - MyJoyOnline]

== Early Life and Education ==
Agyapong was born on 3 July 1996 to Seth Agyapong and Joyce Otiwah. She attended Holy Child School in Ghana for her secondary education before continuing her studies at the tertiary level. She later obtained a masters degree from Coventry University in the United Kingdom [ref: My Family Pushed Me To Take Part In Miss Malaika- Dromeryda, DailyGuide Network]

She is one of five siblings

== Career ==

=== Turq-Stones LImited ===
Dromeryda founded Turq-Stones Limited, a company operating in construction architectural and interior designs and business consultancy. Its activities span theft environment and business services

=== Turq Design Studios ===
Agyapong established Turq Design Studios, a creative agency specializing in branding, visual identity and digital experiences.The Studio's work extends her business interests into creative services and digital design [ref: Turq Design - We Design Brands People Remember, www.turqdesign.com]

Through these ventures, Agyapong has pursued business activities across construction, interior design, consultancy and the creative industry. [ref: Dromeryda Agyapong named among 100 most influential African Leaders 2026 - MyJoyOnline]

== Philanthropy ==

=== La Mére Foundation ===
Agyapong founded La Mere Foundation, an initiative focus on supporting pos natal mothers, promoting opportunities for women entrepreneurs and undertaking community-oriented activities

The foundation's activities include initiatives intended to assist mothers following childbirth and support women pursuing entrepreneurial ventures. [ref: La Mere Foundation support for nursing mothers, Graphic Online]

== Pageantry and Public Recognition ==

=== Pageantry ===
In 2016, Agyapong participated in the Miss Malaika Ghana pageant, where she was among the top 5 finalist. During the competition, she received the titles of Miss Congeniality and Most Down-To-Earth [ref: CypressGH.COM: PHOTOS OF 2016 MISS MALAIKA GHANA TOP 5 DELEGATES VACATION TRIP TO DUBAI, CypressGH.COM]

=== Awards and Recognitions ===
Agyapong has received recognition is areas including entrepreneurship, education, leadership and women's empowerment.

At the Ghana Tertiary Awards, she was named Student Model Of the Year 2017,2018 and 2019. In 2019 she was also associated with the International Aids Society as a Youth Ambassador.

Her subsequent recognitions include Best Student in Supply Management in 2024, Forty under Forty Ghana in 2025 and the Global Entrepreneurship Award in 2025.

In 2026, she was associated with Forty Under Forty Africa and other recognition programs, including the Triumph Women Awards, The Global 100 League of Individuals and 50 Under 50 women.

OC Japan Fair is a Japanese cultural festival held in Orange County, California, United States, since 2009. The event showcases traditional Japanese culture alongside contemporary Japanese popular culture. It is primarily held at the OC Fair & Event Center in Costa Mesa, California. [ref: ABOUT US / CONTACT, OC Japan Fair] [ref: OC Japan Fair: a festival of tradition with a pop culture twist, Daily Pilot]

== Overview ==

OC Japan Fair presents various aspects of Japanese culture, including cuisine, traditional performing arts, music, anime, manga, and fashion. The festival features live performances, food vendors, merchandise exhibitions, and cultural activities.

The event is organized by Japan Product Promotion and operated by Adentope, Inc. Its programming combines traditional Japanese cultural activities with contemporary entertainment, attracting local residents and visitors interested in Japanese culture. [ref: Traditional and contemporary Japanese culture celebrated at OC Japan Fair in Costa Mesa, Daily Pilot]

== History ==

OC Japan Fair was established in 2009 in Orange County, California, under the organization of Japan Product Promotion.

The ninth edition was held in October 2018, featuring Japanese cultural activities such as Awa Odori dancing, taiko drumming, and tea ceremonies. The event was covered by the Daily Pilot, a regional publication of the Los Angeles Times. [ref: OC Japan Fair brings slices of culture to Costa Mesa fairgrounds, Daily Pilot]

The 13th OC Japan Fair was held from October 27 to 29, 2023. According to the organizers, approximately 220 booths were planned, with an anticipated attendance of 45,000 visitors. The announced performers included Japanese boy band Travis Japan, singer Chris Hart, entertainer Ai Haruna, and comedian Tonikaku Akarui Yasumura. [ref: The 13th OC JAPAN FAIR is bringing Japan to SoCal October 27th to 29th, 2023, Japan Product Promotion]

The 18th edition took place from April 3 to 5, 2026, featuring more than 200 booths. The spring festival was held alongside the Japanese music event Freedom LA, whose announced performers included Minmi, Naoto Inti Raymi, Genki Iwahashi, and Yuriyan Retriever.

== Festival activities ==

=== Traditional Japanese culture ===

The festival features demonstrations and performances of traditional Japanese arts, including tea ceremonies, taiko drumming, traditional dance, and kimono-related activities.

During the spring 2026 event, an area inspired by Nakamise Street in Tokyo's Asakusa district featured Bon Odori dancing, koto performances, calligraphy, and ikebana demonstrations. The autumn 2026 event included naginata martial arts demonstrations and traditional Japanese dance performances.

=== Music and live entertainment ===

The festival hosts live performances featuring Japanese pop music, traditional performing arts, dance, and comedy. In 2023, Travis Japan was among the announced performers, drawing attention to the festival's entertainment lineup.

In spring 2026, the event was held alongside Freedom LA, a Japanese music festival featuring artists including MINMI.

=== Anime and cosplay ===

Japanese anime, manga, and video game culture are represented through themed activities, merchandise vendors, and cosplay competitions.

In spring 2026, an area called "Akihabara Electric Town", inspired by Tokyo's Akihabara district, featured a maid café and vendors selling anime-related merchandise.

=== Food and merchandise ===

Food vendors offer a variety of Japanese dishes, including yakitori, takoyaki, ramen, and wagyu beef. The festival has also featured tuna-cutting demonstrations.

Merchandise vendors sell Japanese traditional crafts, accessories, and anime- and manga-related products.

== Organization ==

OC Japan Fair is organized by Japan Product Promotion and operated by Adentope, Inc., doing business as Japan Product Promotion. According to the festival's official website, the company's president is Masataka Taguchi and its producer is Ryuji Yamakita.

== Venue ==

The festival is primarily held at the OC Fair & Event Center, located at 88 Fair Drive in Costa Mesa, California.

The event uses several areas of the fairgrounds, including the Anaheim Building, Los Alamitos Building, Main Mall, and OC Promenade. [ref: OC Japan Fair, OC Fair & Event Center]

data.title: Beige flag
data.text:
[[File:Solid beige.svg|thumb|300x300px|The color beige]]
A beige flag is an Internet slang term for an unusual habit or characteristic considered neither clearly positive nor negative, especially in a romantic relationship. [ref: Why Beige Flags Are TikTok's Latest Obsession, [[Time (magazine)] The term is derived from the terms "red flag" for negative or worrying behavior and "green flag" for positive or desirable qualities in a romantic partner. [ref: beige flag, Dictionary.com] In 2023, users shared videos describing their partners' beige flags as part of a TikTok trend, often with jazz music in the background.

In May 2022, TikTok user @[user] coined the term to indicate signs that someone might be "very boring". Her examples included cliché discussions of food, and references to mainstream television programs on dating profiles. [ref: Beige Flags Are the Latest Dating Phenomenon Dividing the Internet, [[Glamour (magazine)] In early 2023, the meaning of the term underwent a semantic shift to refer to generally harmless habits.

In 2023, Oxford University Press included beige flag on its shortlist for the Oxford Word of the Year. [ref: Eight words go head-to-head for Oxford Word of the Year 2023, Oxford University Press] A 2024 analysis published in Contexts found that according to Google Trends, search interest in the term peaked in June 2023 and fell sharply by the end of that year. [ref: It's Still Complicated, Contexts]

data.title: Jake Dunning (physician)
data.text:
William Jake Dunning MBE is a British physician and clinical researcher specialising in emerging and high-consequence infectious diseases (HCIDs). He is a senior clinical research fellow at the Pandemic Sciences Institute, University of Oxford, and a consultant in infectious diseases at the Royal Free Hospital in London. He is NHS England's National Clinical Lead for Contact HCIDs and leads the HCID service at the Royal Free Hospital. [ref: Jake Dunning, Pandemic Sciences Institute] [ref: Britain's terrifying isolation tent for the world's deadliest diseases, The Daily Telegraph]

Dunning was the field lead for two clinical trials of experimental treatments during the 2014–2016 West African Ebola epidemic. The trials were devised and led by Peter Horby. His work on the trials in Liberia and Sierra Leone was documented in a 2015 Guardian Long Read on experimental Ebola treatments. [ref: Ebola: the race to find a cure, The Guardian] His subsequent clinical and research work has encompassed Ebola virus disease, Lassa fever, mpox, influenza, MERS, COVID-19 and other emerging infectious diseases.

He is a co-director of the National Institute for Health and Care Research Health Protection Research Unit in Emerging and Zoonotic Infections, [ref: NIHR Health Protection Research Unit in Emerging and Zoonotic Infections, HPRU EZI] leads Oxford's clinically focused research contributions to the UK Public Health Rapid Support Team, and has served on World Health Organization (WHO) emergency committees and guideline-development groups. [ref: Who We Are, NIHR Health Protection Research Unit in Emerging and Zoonotic Infections] [ref: PSI's continued involvement in UK-PHRST to reinforce epidemic preparedness globally, Pandemic Sciences Institute]

Dunning received the Ebola Medal for Service in West Africa following his work during the West African Ebola epidemic and was appointed a Member of the Order of the British Empire (MBE) in the 2018 New Year Honours for services to clinical research. [ref: Uni honours staff who tackled Ebola, Oxford Mail] [ref: Dr Jake Dunning recognised in 2018 New Year's Honours list, University of Oxford]

==Career and research==

Between 2009 and 2013, Dunning worked on the Mechanisms of Severe Acute Influenza Consortium (MOSAIC). He undertook doctoral research in viral immunology at Imperial College London, under the supervision of Peter Openshaw, Jonathan Weber, and Anne O'Garra, and was awarded a PhD by Imperial. [ref: Determinants of severity in patients with pandemic influenza]

A principal output from this research was a first-author study published in Nature Immunology in 2018 examining whole-blood transcriptional responses in adults hospitalised with influenza. [ref: Progression of whole-blood transcriptional signatures from interferon-induced to neutrophil-associated patterns in severe influenza, Nature Immunology]

In 2014, Dunning joined the Epidemic diseases Research Group Oxford (ERGO) to work on clinical trials of potential treatments for Ebola virus disease in West Africa. During 2014 and 2015, he was clinical lead for Ebola treatment trials conducted by the Oxford group. The Guardian reported extensively on Dunning and the Oxford team's efforts to establish treatment trials across Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone, including his leadership of clinical trial teams in Liberia and Sierra Leone.

The research included trials of brincidofovir and TKM-130803, for which Dunning was lead author of the published reports. [ref: Experimental Treatment of Ebola Virus Disease with Brincidofovir, PLOS ONE] [ref: Experimental Treatment of Ebola Virus Disease with TKM-130803: A Single-Arm Phase 2 Clinical Trial, PLOS Medicine]

From January 2016 to April 2018, Dunning served as deputy lead of the NHS England High Consequence Infectious Diseases Programme, working with Sir Michael Jacobs. [ref: Second witness statement of Dr Michael Charles Prentice, UK Covid-19 Inquiry]

From 2015 until 2021, Dunning was a consultant at Public Health England (PHE), initially in the Respiratory Virus Unit and later becoming Head of the Enteric Virus Unit and Head of Emerging Infections and Zoonoses. He served as a national incident director, including during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom. In 2019, The Guardian identified him as PHE's head of emerging infections and zoonoses while reporting on the repatriation of British healthcare workers following potential exposure to Lassa fever in Sierra Leone. [ref: Three Britons brought back from Sierra Leone over Ebola-like virus, The Guardian]

During the COVID-19 pandemic, Dunning was co-lead of the NIHR-funded Assessment of Transmission and Contagiousness of COVID-19 in Contacts (ATACCC) study from 2020 to 2022, alongside Prof Ajit Lalvani at Imperial College London. [ref: Responsive Research, NIHR Health Protection Research Unit in Respiratory Infections] The prospective community study investigated SARS-CoV-2 transmission and infectiousness in UK households. Research arising from ATACCC included studies of infectiousness, viral-load kinetics and household transmission. [ref: Onset and window of SARS-CoV-2 infectiousness and temporal correlation with symptom onset: a prospective, longitudinal, community cohort study, The Lancet Respiratory Medicine]

Dunning returned to Oxford's ERGO group in 2021. His research focuses on the pathogenesis, transmission, diagnosis and clinical characterisation of emerging infections and clinical trials of potential treatments. In 2021 he was also made an Honorary Clinical Associate Professor in the Division of Infection and Immunity at University College London. [ref: Jake Dunning, UCL Profiles]

==High-consequence infectious diseases==

Dunning is a consultant in infectious diseases at the Royal Free Hospital and leads its High Consequence Infectious Diseases service. The Royal Free houses a nationally commissioned Airborne HCID treatment centre and its High Level Isolation Unit (HLIU), a specialist facility for managing contact HCIDs (transmissible viral haemorrhagic fevers) including Ebola, Lassa fever and Crimean–Congo haemorrhagic fever. [ref: Dr Jake Dunning MBE, Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust]

During the West African Ebola epidemic, the Royal Free HLIU treated healthcare workers evacuated to the United Kingdom with Ebola; contemporary reporting in The Guardian described it as a state-of-the-art specialist isolation facility. [ref: Treating Ebola: inside the Royal Free hospital's high-level isolation unit, The Guardian]

In 2022, the work of the HLIU was featured in the BBC Two documentary Hospital: Road to Recovery. The episode featured Dunning and the HLIU team during the transfer and treatment of a patient with Lassa fever. [ref: 'Road to Recovery' – BBC Hospital returns, Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust] [ref: Road to Recovery]

In 2023, The Daily Telegraph profiled the Royal Free's HLIU and Dunning's work there, discussing his clinical experience managing cases of Lassa fever and Crimean–Congo haemorrhagic fever and identifying him as the Royal Free's lead consultant for high-consequence infectious diseases.

Dunning is NHS England's national clinical lead for contact HCIDs and director of the NHS England contact HCID network. He is also an honorary clinical associate professor of infectious diseases at University College London and an honorary consultant at the UK Health Security Agency.

==Public health advisory roles==

Dunning is a member of the UK Advisory Committee on Dangerous Pathogens. [ref: Advisory Committee on Dangerous Pathogens, UK Government]

He is also a member of the Emerging Infections Sub-committee of the Joint Committee on Vaccination and Immunisation.

===World Health Organization===

Dunning has served on several World Health Organization (WHO) committees concerning emerging infectious diseases.

In 2022, he was appointed a member of the International Health Regulations Emergency Committee concerning the multi-country outbreak of mpox. [ref: IHR Emergency Committee regarding the multi-country outbreak of monkeypox, World Health Organization] He was again appointed to the WHO IHR Emergency Committee established in response to the international upsurge of mpox in 2024. [ref: Mpox IHR Emergency Committee 2024, World Health Organization]

In 2026, Dunning was appointed a member and rapporteur of the WHO IHR Emergency Committee concerning the epidemic of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda. [ref: List of members, advisers and country representatives: IHR Emergency Committee regarding epidemic of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, World Health Organization]

Dunning has also contributed to WHO guideline development for MERS, COVID-19 and mpox. [ref: Public notice and comments on the Guideline Development Group for WHO Guideline on testing and testing strategies for mpox, World Health Organization] His contributions have included MERS clinical-management guidance, COVID-19 clinical-management and therapeutics guidelines, and WHO guideline development on clinical management and infection prevention and control for mpox. [ref: Clinical management of severe acute respiratory infection when Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) infection is suspected, World Health Organization] [ref: WHO Guideline Development Group for living clinical practice guidelines for COVID-19: therapeutics and clinical management, World Health Organization] [ref: Clinical management and infection prevention and control for monkeypox: Guideline Development Group biographies, World Health Organization]

==Research programmes==

Dunning is a co-director of the NIHR Health Protection Research Unit in Emerging and Zoonotic Infections, representing the University of Oxford. He also leads Oxford's clinically focused research contributions to the UK Public Health Rapid Support Team, including research on mpox in Nigeria, Lassa fever in west Africa, and capacity strengthening efforts for outbreak research in low- and middle-income countries.

==Research on mpox==

Dunning has participated in clinical and public-health responses to mpox in the United Kingdom and internationally.

In 2018, he helped diagnose the first travel-associated case of mpox identified in the United Kingdom, according to subsequent BBC reporting. [ref: Monkeypox: How UK hospitals are tackling the outbreak, BBC News]

During the 2022 international outbreak, Dunning was senior author of a UK multicentre cohort study examining patients hospitalised with more severe mpox. The study was published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. [ref: Clinical features and management of individuals admitted to hospital with monkeypox and associated complications across the UK: a retrospective cohort study, The Lancet Infectious Diseases]

His other published work has included studies of clinical features and environmental contamination in mpox. [ref: Clinical features and management of human monkeypox: a retrospective observational study in the UK, The Lancet Infectious Diseases] [ref: Air and surface sampling for monkeypox virus in a UK hospital: an observational study, The Lancet Microbe]

==Honours==

Dunning was awarded the Ebola Medal for Service in West Africa for his work during the West African Ebola epidemic.

He was appointed Member of the Order of the British Empire (MBE) in the 2018 New Year Honours for services to clinical research.

==Media appearances==

Dunning has appeared in BBC television and radio coverage as an infectious-diseases expert. He was also a guest judge on BBC Two's Great British Menu in 2018 during its NHS 70th anniversary-themed series. [ref: North West – Judging]

During the early stages of the COVID-19 pandemic, he contributed to BBC Newsround coverage of infectious-disease control. [ref: Coronavirus: Why are people wearing masks and do they work?, Newsround]

In 2022, Dunning and the Royal Free HLIU featured in the BBC Two documentary Hospital: Road to Recovery, which followed the HLIU team during the treatment of a patient with Lassa fever. [ref: Hospital (2022), IMDb]

In 2023, Dunning appeared on BBC Radio 4's Inside Health in an episode examining the 2022 mpox outbreak. [ref: What happened to mpox?]

==Selected publications==

* Dunning J, Kennedy SB, Antierens A, et al. "Experimental Treatment of Ebola Virus Disease with Brincidofovir." PLOS ONE. 2016;11(9):e0162199..
* Dunning J, Sahr F, Rojek A, et al. "Experimental Treatment of Ebola Virus Disease with TKM-130803: A Single-Arm Phase 2 Clinical Trial." PLOS Medicine. 2016;13(4):e1001997..
* Dunning J, Blankley S, Hoang LT, et al. "Progression of whole-blood transcriptional signatures from interferon-induced to neutrophil-associated patterns in severe influenza." Nature Immunology. 2018;19:625–635..
* Singanayagam A, Hakki S, Dunning J, et al. "Community transmission and viral load kinetics of the SARS-CoV-2 delta variant in vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals in the UK: a prospective, longitudinal, cohort study." The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 2022;22(2):183–195..
* Hakki S, Zhou J, Jonnerby J, et al. "Onset and window of SARS-CoV-2 infectiousness and temporal correlation with symptom onset: a prospective, longitudinal, community cohort study." The Lancet Respiratory Medicine. 2022;10(11):1061–1073..
* Adler H, Gould S, Hine P, et al. "Clinical features and management of human monkeypox: a retrospective observational study in the UK." The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 2022;22(8):1153–1162..
* Fink DL, Callaby H, Luintel A, et al. "Clinical features and management of individuals admitted to hospital with monkeypox and associated complications across the UK: a retrospective cohort study." The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 2023;23(5):589–597..
* Rojek A, Fieggen J, Apiyo P, et al. "Ebola disease: bridging scientific discoveries and clinical application." The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 2025;25(3):e165–e176..

==References==

==External links==

* [https://www.psi.ox.ac.uk/our-team/jake-dunning Jake Dunning] at the Pandemic Sciences Institute, University of Oxford
* [https://www.royalfree.nhs.uk/services/consultants/dr-jake-dunning Jake Dunning] at the Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust

data.title: Rajesh Gadia
data.text:
----

Rajesh Gadia is a consultant in general medicine at K.E.M. Hospital, Pune. [ref: Rajesh Gadia, K.E.M. Hospital Pune] He was the project director of the hospital's dengue research project in 2018. [ref: Pune study states dengue has grown 100-fold in the past two decades]

== Career ==

Hindustan Times identified him as project director of dengue research project of K.E.M. hospital. The 2018 Hindustan Times article identified Gadia as the doctor who has detected Pune's first dengue case in 1994. He stated that some of the contributing factors increasing risk of dengue in pune localities were waterlogging, construction activity and stagnant water. [ref: No dengue outbreak in city: Hospital, PMC, The Times of India] In 2006, Dr. Gadia was handling dengue project in K.E.M. Hospital, Pune. According to Times of India, he treated around 70 dengue patients in preceding three months. [ref: Youth dies of dengue in Pune, The Times of India] The Indian Express quoted him as a doctor who has been examining dengue cases since 1998 and he planned to study the changes in the virus. [ref: PMC plan to make mosquitoes vanish]

== Research ==

Gadia was co author in Clinical findings and pro-inflammatory cytokines in dengue patients in Western India: a facility-based study, published in PLOS ONE in 2010. [ref: Clinical findings and pro-inflammatory cytokines in dengue patients in Western India: a facility-based study, PLOS ONE]

data.title: Grzegorz Zwoliński
data.text:
Grzegorz Zwoliński is a Polish technology entrepreneur. He is the founder and chief executive officer of ARES Shield, a company developing high-power microwave (HPM) systems intended to protect satellites. [ref: Polish startup ARES Shield hired to protect data center satellites with high-power microwave weapons, Space.com] [ref: Ares Shield has a big ambition – and a long way to go, XYZ] He previously co-founded and led the satellite manufacturer SatRev (formerly SatRevolution) [ref: Polish space startup puts first nanosats into orbit, eyes satellite constellation and production facility, SpaceNews] and co-founded the mobile-game developer T-Bull. [ref: Producent gier mobilnych z Wrocławia wkrótce zadebiutuje na giełdzie, Gazeta Wyborcza]

== Career ==

=== T-Bull ===
In 2010 Zwoliński co-founded T-Bull, a mobile-game developer, together with Damian Fijałkowski and Radosław Łapczyński. The company debuted on the NewConnect alternative market in Warsaw in November 2016 [ref: Doskonały debiut T-BULL na NewConnect, Polskie Radio Jedynka] and moved to the main market of the Warsaw Stock Exchange in August 2018.

=== SatRev ===
In 2016 Zwoliński co-founded the nanosatellite company SatRevolution, later renamed SatRev, and served as its chief executive officer. The company designed and manufactured nanosatellites for Earth observation and commercial missions. In 2019 it launched Światowid, described by the Polish Press Agency as Poland's first commercial Earth-observation satellite. [ref: Two Polish satellites have left the International Space Station, Science in Poland ([[Polish Press Agency] SatRevolution announced plans for an Earth-imaging constellation and in December 2021 received a Series B investment from Virgin Orbit. [ref: Virgin Orbit Invests in Customers Hypersat, SatRevolution to Expand Markets, Via Satellite]

In January 2023 the company's STORK-6 satellite was lost in the failure of Virgin Orbit's first LauncherOne mission from the United Kingdom. [ref: First Virgin Orbit U.K. launch fails, SpaceNews] Following Virgin Orbit's collapse later that year, SatRev came under financial and operational pressure. In 2025 investor January Ciszewski took control of the company; Zwoliński sold his shares and stepped down as chief executive. [ref: Kolejne zmiany w SatRev. Odchodzi CEO firmy, Evertiq] [ref: Jeszcze więcej Ciszewskiego w SatRev. Inwestor przejmuje 42% akcji spółki i chce budować kosmiczny ekosystem, MamStartup] He later acknowledged that SatRev's communication about the scale of its plans had at times run ahead of the company's ability to deliver, describing this as a lesson for his subsequent work.

=== ARES Shield ===
Zwoliński founded ARES Shield around the turn of 2025 and 2026. According to the company, its system combines sensors, AI-based analytics and a high-power microwave emitter in a module attached to a client satellite, designed to disable threatening spacecraft electronically without creating space debris. Zwoliński said the company initially raised 1 million PLN and later a further 1.4 million PLN from private investors.

In August 2026 the American company Lonestar Data Holdings contracted ARES Shield to protect its orbital data-storage satellites, in a deal reported to be worth up to US$6 million (about 22 million PLN). The agreement initially covers three satellites, with the first systems expected to be delivered in 2028 or 2029. At the time, the technology was at Technology Readiness Level 4, having been tested only under laboratory conditions, and Zwoliński estimated that around 80 million PLN in further funding would be needed to bring it to operational use. Industry commentators described the concept as technically plausible but subject to high technological risk, noting a long path from a laboratory demonstrator to an operational system in orbit, and Polish space-industry observers said they were following the venture with interest but caution in light of SatRev's record.

Zwoliński has also co-founded other Polish ventures, including the airborne wind energy startup Njord Energy [ref: Latawiec, który generuje prąd. Polski start-up walczy o rynek w USA, Gramwzielone.pl] and the artificial-intelligence startup GrantBot.AI. [ref: GrantBot.AI kończy męki przedsiębiorców związane z wnioskami o dotacje, 300Gospodarka]

== References ==

data.title: Narrative intelligence
data.text:
Narrative intelligence refers to the ability to create, tell, and understand stories and to respond to them emotionally. Research on computational narrative intelligence examines these abilities in artificial intelligence systems. [ref: Computational Narrative Intelligence: A Human-Centered Goal for Artificial Intelligence, arXiv]

In information warfare, the term narrative intelligence, or NARINT, is used to analyze narratives, their circulation, and their influence on perceptions and behavior. [ref: Inteligencia narrativa en la era de la IA: análisis de la desinformación antiucraniana de Rusia, Ministerio de Defensa]

This analysis examines how people interpret events through stories, how ideas gain attention, who promotes them, and how they change over time. Analysts connect individual posts to recurring themes and the networks that spread them to help identify emerging narratives and potential influence campaigns.

== Background ==
Michael Mateas and Phoebe Sengers co-chaired the 1999 AAAI Fall Symposium on Narrative Intelligence. The symposium's call for participation covered story generation and understanding, interactive storytelling, and autonomous agents, alongside contributions from psychology, cultural studies, and art. [ref: Call for Participation: Narrative Intelligence, Carnegie Mellon University]

Mateas and Sengers later edited the 2003 collection Narrative Intelligence. It examined how people use stories to make sense of the world and how this could inform computer design, with chapters on narrative generation, agents participating in stories, and tools for storytellers. [ref: Narrative Intelligence, John Benjamins]

== Computational narrative research ==
Stories often leave characters' motives and connections between events unstated. In a 2016 position paper, Mark O. Riedl identified the background knowledge and causal inferences needed to understand such stories as obstacles for computational systems.

Story generation also requires attention to characters' motives. In their 2010 paper Narrative Planning: Balancing Plot and Character, Mark O. Riedl and R. Michael Young developed a planning method that incorporated character goals into plot generation. They evaluated it by testing readers' understanding of the characters' intentions. [ref: Narrative Planning: Balancing Plot and Character, Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research]

In his 2016 paper, Riedl proposed applications in entertainment and training, as well as using stories to explain AI decisions and teach machines social norms. His paper also discussed difficulties with figurative language and causal connections across long passages.

In a 2023 study of visual storytelling, Brett A. Halperin and Stephanie M. Lukin analyzed 100 stories composed from image sequences, examining characterization, visual grounding, and narrative bias. [ref: Envisioning Narrative Intelligence: A Creative Visual Storytelling Anthology, Association for Computing Machinery]

== Information operations and disinformation ==
In information operations, narratives connect events and actors to explain what is happening. They are not necessarily deceptive or hostile. Strategic narratives can support democratic communication or be used to manipulate audiences.

In a study published by Spain's Ministry of Defence, Viktoriia Romaniuk and Yevhen Fedchenko examined recurring narratives in Russian disinformation about Ukraine and how they are adapted to events and audiences. For example, the portrayal of Ukraine as a failed state recurs across different messages, giving otherwise separate claims a common interpretation. They also discussed identifying influential sources and mapping the connections between them.

Analysts can draw on open-source intelligence to trace narratives across news outlets and social media. In a 2024 Foreign Policy Research Institute article, EdgeTheory chief executive Joe Stradinger illustrated theme tracing, source mapping, and changes in amplification using coverage of NATO and the war in Ukraine. [ref: Narrative Intelligence: Detecting Chinese and Russian Information Operations to Disrupt NATO Unity, Foreign Policy Research Institute]

DARPA's completed Narrative Networks program investigated how narratives influence cognition and behavior through quantitative analysis, neurobiological research, and modeling. [ref: Narrative Networks, DARPA] A Joint Special Operations University study by Troy Troublefield examined narrative intelligence in internet-based military information support operations, with attention to emotional connection, contextualization, and counternarratives. [ref: Narrative Intelligence in Internet-Based Military Information Support Operations: A Cyberpsychology Perspective Under the Irregular Warfare Construct, Joint Special Operations University]

=== AI methods ===
One approach to disinformation narrative mining combines large language models with clustering methods: models extract claims from text, and clustering groups them by similarity in meaning to identify shared narratives.

DiNaM, presented by Witold Sosnowski and colleagues at EMNLP in 2025, applies this approach to false claims extracted from fact-checking articles. It generates descriptions of the resulting groups, which the authors evaluated against narratives compiled by experts. [ref: DiNaM: Disinformation Narrative Mining with Large Language Models, Association for Computational Linguistics]

=== Commercial use ===
Gartner defines a category of narrative intelligence tools on its Peer Insights website. The category covers monitoring narratives across news and social media, tracking their spread, and analyzing adversarial intent. [ref: Narrative Intelligence Reviews and Ratings, Gartner Peer Insights]

Agentic AI enables users to investigate online conversations through natural-language dialogue, allowing those with limited expertise in intelligence analysis to conduct intelligence investigations. [ref: Brinker's agentic intelligence analyst, Brinker]

In an October 2025 article in Haaretz, Omer Benjakob reported that Brinker uses AI to scan online discourse for signs of influence campaigns. These signs include repeated wording promoted simultaneously by different accounts and narratives recurring across posts. Discussing the multi-industry application of narrative inteligenc technology Daniel Ravner, said: "There's a big question about who should be your ideal client: whether to target disinformation - then the natural clients are governments and security agencies - or to approach companies through the world of 'brand reputation'". [ref: From Charlie Kirk Rumors to AI Scams: How Online Wars Turned Israel Into an Anti-fake News Powerhouse, Haaretz]

In a January 2026 ITKeyMedia interview, Repsense representatives described combining automated clustering and network mapping with human review. In this workflow, human analysts interpret the findings and assess their relevance. [ref: EUR 2M for Repsense’s Narrative Intelligence and Influence Forecasting, ITKeyMedia]

Vendors describe several applications of narrative intelligence. Blackbird.AI emphasizes actors and amplification networks, [ref: What is Narrative Intelligence?, Blackbird.AI] while EdgeTheory describes tracing thematic similarities across media and over time. [ref: Narrative Intelligence Features, EdgeTheory] Brinker promotes agentic narrative intelligence focusing on autonous and pro active inevstigations. [ref: What is Agentic OSINT?, Brinker] PeakMetrics describes tracking claims across news and social media. [ref: Narrative intelligence: Definition and Examples, PeakMetrics] LetsData describes Vantage as monitoring emerging narratives and coordinated amplification. [ref: Vantage, LetsData] Repsense describes Havel as analyzing narratives in text, broadcast media, and video. [ref: The Havel Platform, Repsense]

=== Limitations ===
Stradinger notes that the volume of social-media content prevents comprehensive coverage. PeakMetrics distinguishes tracing dissemination from establishing attribution: the earliest appearance found in a dataset may not be the actual origin of a narrative.

The DiNaM authors identify two sources of error: confusion between similar narratives and unsupported content generated by language models. Reliance on published fact-checking articles also limits the system's ability to detect emerging narratives.

A narrative's reach does not, by itself, establish its effect on attitudes or behavior. In a study published in Nature Communications in 2023, Gregory Eady and colleagues linked survey responses to Twitter exposure during the 2016 US election. They found no meaningful relationship between exposure to Russian influence accounts and changes in attitudes, polarization, or voting behavior. The researchers cautioned that this finding did not rule out other effects, including changes in trust in electoral integrity. [ref: Exposure to the Russian Internet Research Agency foreign influence campaign on Twitter in the 2016 US election and its relationship to attitudes and voting behavior, Nature Communications]

data.title: Gildas Loaëc
data.text:
----

== Gildas Loaëc ==
Gildas Loaëc (born 1973) is a French entrepreneur and music producer. He is best known as co-founder of the lifestyle brand Maison Kitsuné. In the mid-1990s he became closely involved with the electronic duo Daft Punk. He later turned Kitsuné into a record label, fashion brand, and café chain that mixes Japanese and French influences. [ref: Gildas Loaëc, le roman du renard, Libération] [ref: In Bali, a House That Taught a Fashion Executive How to Relax, The New York Times]

== Early life ==
Loaëc was born in 1973 in Lesneven, in the Finistère department of Brittany. At lycée he became friends with Loïc Prigent, who went on to become a fashion journalist. The two made fanzines, ran a radio show, and went to some of the early raves in France and the UK.

== Career ==
=== Street Sounds ===
In 1995 Loaëc opened a vinyl record shop called Street Sounds near the rue de Rivoli in Paris. It specialized in house and techno and quickly turned into a hangout spot for DJs and musicians in the French electronic scene. Regular customers included Thomas Bangalter and Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo (who later formed Daft Punk) as well as the Japanese designer Masaya Kuroki, who later became Loaëc's business partner.

=== Association with Daft Punk ===
From the mid-1990s onward Loaëc was part of Daft Punk's inner circle and stayed involved with the duo for about fifteen years. He has called himself an “homme à tout faire," describing his role as someone who did a bit of everything. He is credited as artistic director on several of the group’s album covers and also ran their individual labels: Roulé (founded by Bangalter) and Crydamoure (founded by de Homem-Christo). Both labels put out a number of French house records during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

=== Maison Kitsuné ===
In 2002 Loaëc and Kuroki started Kitsuné (later Maison Kitsuné) as a record label. The name means “fox” in Japanese and points to the brand’s Franco-Japanese identity. What began as a label later added fashion and cafés and eventually opened stores and locations in several countries. [ref: How Kitsuné Cultivated a Loyal Fashion Fanbase Through Music, The Business of Fashion]

Fashion accounts for the large majority of the brand’s revenue. By the mid-2020s the company operated more than 75 fashion boutiques worldwide, with particularly strong sales in Asia.

=== Café Kitsuné and later expansion ===
The first Café Kitsuné opened in Tokyo in 2013. Later it expanded to Paris and other cities, becoming an integral part of the brand’s lifestyle offering. By the mid-2020s there were approximately 35 cafés worldwide.

== Personal life ==
Loaëc is based in Tokyo.

data.title: Green Interventions for Sustainable Towns
data.text:
= Green Interventions for Sustainable Towns (GIST) Kenya =
Green Interventions for Sustainable Towns (GIST) Kenya is a nonprofit organization based in Kisumu, Kenya, working at the intersection of climate justice, health equity and inclusive governance. Its programs focus on tackling the triple planetary crisis with a central focus on Climate change. [ref: GIST Kenya - Green Interventions for Sustainable Towns, www.gist-ke.org] [ref: Seeding Climate-Smart Food Systems in Kenya, The Pollination Project] [ref: Day of the African Child: B-Ball for Life introduced in Kenya, sportanddev]

== History and organizational background ==
The organization is registered in Kenya under the Public Benefit Organizations Regulatory Authority registration number NGO-[https://pbora.go.ke/pbos GDUQJRG] and was founded in 2025 to drive sustainable development by integrating climate action, health, economic empowerment, and human rights advocacy into community interventions envisioning a future where all communities thrive in well-being and resilience, with inclusive solutions that promote green practices and equitable access to sexual and reproductive health for all. [ref: The Ground-Level Changemaker: How Emmanuel Is Rebuilding Communities From the Inside Out - Peace First] In its early work in Kisumu County, GIST Kenya has focused on sustainable waste management and environmental health, including research on healthcare sharps waste and the safety of informal waste workers. [ref: Sharps – Green Medical Waste Management Situational Analysis of Healthcare Waste Management Practices, Occupational Safety, and Health System Readiness in Peri-Urban Health Facilities in Kisumu Central Sub-County]

data.title: 10 Pujaan Malindo Vol. 1
data.text:
10 Pujaan Malindo Vol.1 [ref: ] is Noraniza Idris’s debut studio album, and the songs she performs are cover versions of tracks previously popularised by local artists as well as those from neighbouring countries (Indonesia). The album 10 Pujaan Malindo was recorded in two volumes, released in 1986 and 1987. This album series was launched in 1986 by Life Records (Hup Hup Sdn. Bhd.).

== Background ==
After taking part in an audition organised by RTM, the winner of the 1985 RTM Bintang competition, Noraniza Idris, was approached by Hamidi, the publisher and producer at Life Records, who wanted her to become a recording artist because he was captivated by the sweetness of her voice; The offer first arose whilst she was still participating in the 1985 RTM Star competition, which had not yet concluded. At the time, she was with her father, Idris Ahmad, enjoying a meal at the Angkasapuri canteen—the venue where she had taken the RTM talent test. Eventually, after much consideration, she agreed to sign a contract with Life Records on 1 January 1986 and officially became a recording artist – marking the first recording contract of her career. She also released her debut album, a compilation titled Melayu Deli, alongside a legendary singer of the 1980s on 1 January 1986. Meanwhile, he had taken part in the 1985 Bintang RTM competition, though he only reached the semi-finals; however, he remained resilient, and perhaps Hamidi’s arrival and his official status as a recording artist served as the remedy he had been seeking all along. [ref: NORANIZA IDRIS: 12 LAGU PALING POPULAR SEPANJANG ZAMAN, GALAKSIVIRAL]

The release of the album 10 Pujaan Malindo Vol.1 in 1986 on the Life Records label (Hup Hup Sdn. Bhd.) marked a highly significant milestone in Noraniza Idris’s professional discography. This major project was released at a time when the regional music market was witnessing a vibrant wave of cultural exchange between Malaysia and Indonesia (the acronym for ‘Malindo’). As a new singer establishing her name in the 1980s, Noraniza was sent to Jakarta, Indonesia, to undertake the vocal recording and musical arrangement process on location. This strategic move by the record company was taken to ensure that the resulting archipelago-inspired music possessed authentic aesthetic value and high production standards. The album’s extraordinary success in the market not only placed her on the mainstream industry’s radar but also paved the way for the production of its sequel, 10 Pujaan Malindo Vol.2, which was released the following year. [ref: ]

data.title: Ido Naor
data.text:
Ido Naor () is an Israeli cybersecurity executive, former security researcher, and author. He is the co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of the cybersecurity company Security Joes, which he established in 2020 after leaving Kaspersky Lab's Global Research and Analysis Team. [ref: Ido Naor, Cyber Week 2025] [ref: Ido Naor — Experience, LinkedIn] He previously co-founded the malware-research platform VirusBay. [ref: VirusBay Aims To Make Malware Analysis More Social, BleepingComputer] His earlier research included banking malware, information exposed through online services, industrial control software, and threat actors targeting Israeli organizations. [ref: Zombies and mules: The inside story of the first-ever shekel bank hack, The Times of Israel] [ref: Flaws in Gas Station Software Let Hackers Change Prices, Steal Fuel, Erase Evidence, Vice]

== Early life and education ==
Naor was born in Kabri and raised in Afula. He served in Unit 504 of the Israel Defense Forces. [ref: האקר סטנדרטי, e-vrit] After active service he worked in security operations for the Israel Airports Authority at Ben Gurion Airport from 2009 to 2011.

During this period, Naor studied Computer Science at the College of Management Academic Studies. He graduated and returned as lecturer for cybersecurity studies between 2013–2015. [ref: מה אתם באמת יודעים על האקרים? הצצה לחייו של האקר, College of Management Academic Studies]

== Career ==
=== Early cybersecurity career ===
Naor began his cybersecurity career as an application-security researcher at CYCL, formerly known as Bugsec, in 2011. He subsequently worked as a security researcher at Cisco from 2012 to 2013 and at McAfee from 2013 to 2015. His earliest located magazine article, about the security of connected medical devices, appeared in the Israeli cybersecurity magazine Digital Whisper in June 2011, however prior to that he practiced Bug Bounty and was featured in Hall of Fame lists. [ref: Medical Hazardous Implants, Digital Whisper]

Naor maintained a personal security blog from 2011 to 2015. It included security-challenge walkthroughs and reports of web vulnerabilities that he disclosed to companies including LinkedIn, Google and Waze, eBay, AliExpress, and Meta's Facebook. [ref: Ido Naor, Blogger] Two posts from early 2014 display Naor's name in Google's application-security Hall of Fame for the fourth quarter of 2013; one of the posts focuses on multiple reported vulnerabilities in Waze, followed by Hall of Fame name appearance. [ref: Google Hall Of Fame – Multiple vulnerabilities in Google Waze GPS, Blogger] [ref: Google Hall Of Fame – Vulnerability in Google, Blogger]

=== Kaspersky ===
Naor joined Kaspersky's Global Research and Analysis Team in 2015. He worked as a senior security researcher and, from 2019 until leaving the company in August 2020, as a principal security researcher. His early work there included research into Grabit, an espionage campaign that targeted small and medium-sized organizations, [ref: Small-To-Mid-Sized Organizations Targeted By 'Grabit' Cyberspies, Dark Reading] and ATMZombie, a banking trojan used to steal money from Israeli accounts. [ref: כך גנבו האקרים מאות אלפי שקלים מחשבונות בנק בישראל, People and Computers]

In 2015, Naor disclosed a flaw in LinkedIn's mobile-comment and email-notification handling that could have facilitated targeted phishing. LinkedIn fixed the issue before publication. [ref: Kaspersky researchers warns Linkedin from potential spear phishing, Securelist] That year he also served as a mentor in Kaspersky's Security Startup Challenge, whose finals were held at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in Cambridge, Massachusetts. [ref: Taking A Break From Research To Accelerate Startups: SSC 2015, Securelist] [ref: Kaspersky Lab names the best startups of its first acceleration program, Kaspersky]

In June 2016, Naor investigated a Facebook-spreading malware campaign for which Kaspersky recorded almost 10,000 attempted infections in 48 hours. [ref: Facebook malware: tag me if you can, Securelist] He presented the research at CODE BLUE in Tokyo that October. [ref: Facebook Malware: Tag Me If You Can, CODE BLUE 2016]

In February 2017, Naor and the IDF's C4I and Information Security units published Breaking the Weakest Link of the Strongest Chain, an investigation of malicious Android applications and social engineering used to spy on more than 100 Israeli soldiers. [ref: Breaking The Weakest Link Of The Strongest Chain, Securelist] [ref: Israeli soldiers' personal Android phones hacked by spies, researchers say, CyberScoop] Initial media reports associated the campaign with Hamas. [ref: ViperRat – Mobile APT Targeting Israeli Defense Force, Lookout]

In mid-2017, Naor investigated an Instagram application programming interface flaw that exposed users' contact information. He reported the issue to the company and later demonstrated how information obtained through the flaw was being offered for sale. [ref: בין קורבנות הפריצה לאינסטגרם: בר רפאלי וגל גדות, Calcalist] [ref: Hackers Sell Celebrity Info Obtained in Instagram Hack, SecurityWeek]

Naor also reported six vulnerabilities in fuel-station management software. The flaws could have allowed an attacker to alter fuel prices, stop pumps, or obtain payment information. [ref: Automation Software Flaws Expose Gas Stations to Hacker Attacks, SecurityWeek]

In 2019, the United States Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency issued an advisory crediting both researchers. One of the vulnerabilities, CVE-2017-14728, was assigned a CVSS score of 9.8. [ref: Orpak SiteOmat, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency]

That year, GReAT published an investigation of ViceLeaker, Android spyware used against Israeli and other Middle Eastern targets. The report described spyware embedded in legitimate applications, distribution through Telegram and WhatsApp, and application detections in Iran; it was credited collectively to GReAT rather than to an individual author. Ido and an additional researcher, Alexey F., were behind the research, also speaking about it publicly during SAS (Kaspersky's Security Analysts Summit) 2019. [ref: ViceLeaker Operation: mobile espionage targeting Middle East, Securelist] [ref: ViceLeaker Android spyware targets users in the Middle East, Security Affairs]

=== VirusBay ===
In 2017, Naor and fellow researcher developed VirusBay, a community for malware researchers that combined a Telegram bot with a web application, Yara rule generator and free malware binary uploads, which was missing at the time. The platform launched in November 2017 and had more than 1,000 beta users by March 2018. In August 2018, VirusBay reported that the community had reached over 2,000 researchers. [ref: Ready for next year, as currently #2019 researchers are using #VirusBay, X] A crowdfunding campaign raised approximately US$15,000 in April 2018. [ref: VirusBay, Startup Nation Finder] The project ceased operating in May 2019 due to life-changing decisions with an investment opportunity. Ido and his co-founder decided to pass the offer and closed the joint venture.

That year, Naor also presented research at Black Hat USA about confidential files that organizations had inadvertently uploaded to public malware-scanning services. [ref: Dissecting Non-Malicious Artifacts: One IP at a Time, Black Hat USA 2018]

=== Security Joes ===
After leaving Kaspersky in August 2020, Naor co-founded together with his wife, Ortal, Security Joes and became its chief executive. The company provides incident-response, managed detection-and-response and red team services. [ref: Our Story, Security Joes]

In 2021, Security Joes incident-response investigations associated ransomware attacks against gambling companies with infrastructure and techniques previously used by APT27, and reconstructed the toolchain of the Ever101 ransomware. [ref: State-sponsored Chinese hackers turning to financially motivated attacks, Israeli researchers find, CTech] [ref: China's APT hackers move to ransomware attacks, BleepingComputer] [ref: Mysterious ransomware payment traced to a sensual massage site, BleepingComputer]

In 2022, Naor and researchers at the company documented an intrusion involving Sockbot, a customized version of the Ligolo reverse-tunnelling tool, and a previously undocumented credential dumper. [ref: Russian Ransomware Gang Retool Custom Hacking Tools of Other APT Groups, The Hacker News] [ref: Hackers fork open-source reverse tunneling tool for persistence, BleepingComputer]

In early 2023, the company reported a more complex variant of the Raspberry Robin worm targeting financial and insurance organizations in Europe; the company report led the investigation with Naor. [ref: Raspberry Robin Worm Evolves to Attack Financial and Insurance Sectors in Europe, The Hacker News] [ref: Raspberry Robin Detected ITW Targeting Insurance & Financial Institutes In Europe, Security Joes] The company subsequently described Ice Breaker, a social-engineering campaign against gaming and gambling companies that delivered a previously undocumented Node.js backdoor. [ref: Hackers use new IceBreaker malware to breach gaming companies, BleepingComputer]

That same year, Naor, and fellow researchers disclosed Mockingjay, a Process Injection technique that used an existing read-write-execute section in a legitimate DLL to avoid several actions commonly monitored by endpoint security products. [ref: New Mockingjay process injection technique evades EDR detection, BleepingComputer] [ref: New Mockingjay Process Injection Technique Could Let Malware Evade Detection, The Hacker News]

Later that year, Security Joes incident responders together with Naor, documented attackers exploiting MinIO vulnerabilities and replacing the storage service with a backdoored version. [ref: Hackers exploit MinIO storage system to breach corporate networks, BleepingComputer] [ref: Hackers Exploit MinIO Storage System Vulnerabilities to Compromise Servers, The Hacker News]

The team also volunteered to assist Israeli organizations, during operation Swords of Iron, which led them to discover BiBi-Linux, a destructive Wiper used against Israeli organizations, and later connected it to a broader data-destruction campaign that included a Windows variant. [ref: New BiBi-Linux wiper malware targets Israeli orgs in destructive attacks, BleepingComputer] [ref: Israel warns of BiBi wiper attacks targeting Linux and Windows, BleepingComputer]

In January 2024, Security Joes published research into a DLL Search-Order Hijacking method that used executables in the Windows WinSxS directory, allowing malicious code to be loaded without bringing a separate vulnerable executable onto the target system. [ref: New Variant of DLL Search Order Hijacking Bypasses Windows 10 and 11 Protections, The Hacker News] [ref: New DLL Search Order Hijacking Technique Targets WinSxS Folder, SecurityWeek]

In mid-2026, the company disclosed Naor's work around a sandbox-escape vulnerability in the n8n workflow-automation platform that could allow authenticated workflow editors to execute operating-system commands; the issue was fixed in n8n versions 2.31.5 and 2.32.1 and credited Naor's Github profile. [ref: n8n Sandbox Escape Lets Workflow Editors Run OS Commands as the n8n Process, The Hacker News]

In October 2026, Security Joes launched JOES AIR (Autonomous Investigations & Response), an agentic operating layer for security operations that coordinates investigations and response across connected security tools, maintains context across workflows, and retains human approval gates. [ref: Today, Security Joes is reaching another milestone!, LinkedIn]

== Writing and media ==

Naor wrote Standard Hacker (), a Hebrew-language autobiographical book published by Sagol in 2020. In January 2021, the Israeli television network Keshet 12 devoted an episode of its Private Lesson series to Naor and his work. [ref: שיעור פרטי, פרק 16: עידן נאור, Keshet 12]

== Personal life ==

data.title: 681 (genre)
data.text:
----

681 is the genre of music that consist of exactly vocals and percussion instruments. It combines a capella with minimalist dance music. An example is the song Crabapples by Bruce Peninsula. [ref: Bruce Peninsula climbing the musical ladder, Interrobang]

It follows that this is the alternative name of the genre of minimalist vocal dance music.

Many genres have a given alternative name. For example, an alternative name trance is given to usually minimalist ambient rhythmic dance music with tempo between 120 and 150 BPM.

== Name origin ==

The name 681 originates from the list of natural numbers. We have a=1 because of the existence of vocals as the primary element of most vocal songs. [ref: Musical Texture, Fundamentals: Music in World Cultures] Then we skip 2 because there are no instruments other than percussion in this genre to function as the secondary element of most vocal songs. Hence we take b=3 as the next notable number because there is percussion in this genre and is the tertiary element of most vocal songs. The formula of the square of a binomial is (a+b)^2=a^2+2\cdot a\cdot b+b^2. If we square the exponents of b in each addend, i.e., raise them to the 2nd power, because 2 is the skipped natural number, we get the addends a^2, 2\cdot a \cdot b and b^4, respectively. The addends are equal to 1, 6 and 81, respectively. The ratio when the second addend is divided by the first addend is 6/1=6, while the ratio when the third addend is divided by the first addend is 81/1=81. Its concatenation gives 681.

data.title: The African insurance organization (AIO)
data.text:
The African Insurance Organization (AIO) is a nongovernmental organization [ref: Organisation des Assurances Africains (OAA), MFW4A - Making Finance Work for Africa] representing Africa’s insurance and reinsurance industry. It was established in 1972 in Port Louis, Mauritius [ref: ], and its headquarters are in Douala, Cameroon [ref: ].

== Activities and role ==
The AIO organizes an annual conference and General Assembly, holds specialized meetings and seminars, and publishes studies on African insurance markets [ref: 52nd AIO conference kicks off in Cairo with more than 2,000 attendees] [ref: African Insurance Organization (AIO), Financial Afrik] [ref: ].

In 2026, its Africa Insurance Pulse report examined how limited insurance data contributes to the insurance protection gap in African markets [ref: Africa Insurance Pulse 2026 - Data-driven insurance catalyses inclusive growth in Africa, Africa Insurance Pulse]. An analysis discussed the challenges facing the AIO, including its limited financial resources, lack of regulatory authority and the diversity of insurance markets across Africa.

== History ==
In the early 1970s, insurance executives in Mauritius, including Robert Woodthorpe Browne [ref: Africa Insurance Organisation, The Paddy Ashdown Forum], proposed creating a forum where heads of African insurance companies could meet. The Insurers’ Association of Mauritius and Mauritius Re approached the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) to organize a conference in Mauritius.

The first meeting was held from 5 to 9 June 1972 [ref: Report by the Board of Direction of the African Reinsurance Corporation covering the period from 1st April, 1977 to 31st December, 1978, Report by the Board of Direction of the African Reinsurance Corporation covering the period from 1st April, 1977 to 31st December, 1978] at Le Réduit, Mauritius, with the support of the Mauritian government. It brought together 77 delegates from 28 African countries, including insurance companies, supervisory bodies and European observers. A sponsorship committee included René Adam, Sheikh S. M. Balala, Hedi Ennifer, Ephrem Marie Mba and Anthony Kobina Woode.

Discussions covered cooperation among insurance markets, insurance capacity, a possible African insurance congress and a proposed African reinsurance company. The meeting also considered the establishment of technical and training committees.

A second meeting, held in Nairobi, Kenya, from 25 to 29 June 1973, led to the formal establishment of the AIO. Tomas Okelo-Odongo, chairman of the board of Kenya Re, became its Secretary-General.

At the third conference, held in Yaoundé, Cameroon, in 1974, the AIO’s statutes were adopted. Kabisi Pene Yemba Milanga, Managing Director of the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s National Insurance Company (SONAS), was appointed the organization’s first Honorary Secretary-General.

=== The 1980s ===
Yosef Assefa was appointed Secretary-General in 1981 and held the position for 24 years. In July 1983, the AIO established its first insurance pool, the African Aviation Pool [ref: African Aviation Insurance Pool, pools.africa-re.com], in Libreville, Gabon. The organization’s headquarters moved from Nairobi to Douala in 1984. In June 1986, the AIO decided to establish the African Oil and Energy Pool [ref: African Oil and Energy Pool, pools.africa-re.com]. The pool began operations in January 1989.
=== The 1990s ===
The first African Reinsurance Forum was held in Lomé, Togo, in 1995.

=== The 2000s ===
After Assefa stepped down, Abdallah Badaoui became Secretary-General in July 2005 but left the position later that year. Roland Rasamoely served as acting Secretary-General until Prisca Soares was appointed in 2007; she served for 12 years [ref: AIO 2021: PILA Honours Prisca Soares With Award, businessstandardsng.com].

In 2005, the AIO, UNCTAD and the World Bank established the African Centre for Catastrophe Risks (ACCR), headquartered in Casablanca, Morocco.

=== The 2010s ===
In 2012, the AIO marked its 40th anniversary in Mauritius.

In 2016, the AIO published its first research report, Africa Reinsurance Pulse [ref: Africa Reinsurance Pulse - 2016, Africa Reinsurance Pulse], on trends and prospects in the African insurance market.

=== The 2020s ===
Jean Baptiste Ntukamazina became Secretary-General in 2019 [ref: New Secretary General for the African Insurance Organisation, www.cover.co.za]. In 2022, the AIO signed the Nairobi Declaration on Sustainable Insurance [ref: The Nairobi Declaration on Sustainable Insurance - EXPLAINER, The Nairobi Declaration on Sustainable Insurance].

== Members ==
According to the AIO’s 2025 annual report, as of June 2025 the organization had 421 corporate and institutional members from 47 African countries and 13 countries outside Africa [ref: African Insurance Organisation - Annual Report 2025, African Insurance Organisation - Annual Report]. The report lists insurers, brokers, reinsurers, regulators, associations, training institutions and InsurTech or support-service organizations among its members.

== Leadership ==
At the AIO’s 52nd Conference and Annual General Assembly in Cairo, Egypt, held from 5 to 9 June 2026, Alaa El-Zoheiry [ref: Alaa El-Zoheiry elected President of African Insurance Organisation for 2026-2027 term, Dailynewsegypt] was elected president for the 2026-2027 term.

== Insurance pools==

=== The African Aviation Pool ===
Established in July 1983, the African Aviation Pool was the AIO’s first insurance pool. It is managed by Africa Re.

=== African Oil and Energy Pool ===
The AIO approved the creation of the African Oil and Energy Pool at its 13th General Assembly; operations began in January 1989. The pool is managed by Africa Re.
