data.title: Void Vibration
data.text:
Void Vibration is the second studio album by Düsseldorf Neo-psychedelic and Neo-Kraut Rock band Vibravoid. The album was released in September 2002 by Berlin independent record label Nasoni Records. The album was named "CD of the Month" by major German music magazine Eclipsed. [ref: Vibravoid – Void Vibration, Eclipsed]

== Recording and production ==

The album was initially recorded on analogue tape at the Düsseldorf studio "Das Kleine Analoge" in November and December 2001 with a Fostex G24S 24-track tape recorder (1-inch). However, most of these recordings did not make it onto the album but were released later on Triptamine E.P. Volume 1. [ref: Triptamine E.P. Volume 1, Nasoni Records] The version of the title track Void Vibration from these sessions remains unreleased and is considered lost. [ref: Void Vibration (10th Anniversary Deluxe Edition), Krauted Mind Records] [ref: Eine kleine Reise ins elektrische Bewusstsein, eclipsed Rock Magazin]

The band re-recorded all tracks except Echovoid and Electrovoid in 2002 at the Institut für Wohlklangforschung in Hanover, assisted by Willi Dammeier on a Telefunken M15A 2-inch 24-track tape recorder and an Amek Angela mixing console. The album was mastered by Michael Schwabe at the Monoposto Studios. The album was produced in Dolby Surround quadraphonic sound. For the track Echovoid, two separate tape echo units were used, a Roland Space Echo and a Dynacord echo unit. [ref: Let's Take A Trip With… Nasoni Records, Rumble Skunk]

== Style and sound ==
Void Vibration is intended as an analogue counterpoint to the digital revolution in music production emerging in the 1990s. Stylistically, the album combines the experimental electronic influences of the Düsseldorf School with elements of classic flower power psychedelia and Kraut Rock. The overall sound is characterised by the use of analogue vintage effects, tape echo units, synthesizer and sitar sounds. Alongside psychedelic passages are noise-heavy walls of guitar sound that display influences from the early sound of Pink Floyd.

== Historical context of the songs ==
Void Vibration is retrospectively regarded as a document of the German underground of the 1990s and the emerging vinyl revival. [ref: Vibravoid, Slam] Other official releases of alternative versions date the songs during that decade. The track Adjustment was composed as early as 1992 and first recorded on 10 February 1994 at Potter's Work Studio in Essen, using a Fostex B16 reel-to-reel recorder and an ACE Audio Engineering mixing console. The original 1994 recording was first released on the demo tape One Nation Underground in the same year before appearing on the album Turned On Acid in 2003. [ref: Turned on Acid, Moonhead Records] A new recording of the song was released as a 7-inch single on Nasoni Records in 2001. This version had been recorded at the Düsseldorf studio "Das Kleine Analoge" using a Tascam 8-track tape recorder and was reviewed by contemporary press coverage. The single was released on grey marbled vinyl. [ref: Vibravoid – Void Vibration (review), Gew Gaw] [ref: Vibravoid – Adjustment, Prinz] Since this particular recording had already been released as a single, the band re-recorded the song in Hanover for the LP version of Void Vibration but included both songs from the 7” single as bonus tracks on the 2002 edition of the CD. [ref: Vibravoid – Void Vibration, Bad Acid Magazine]

The title track Void Vibration dates back to 1995 and is documented by historical demo tapes, live recordings from the period in which it was created and contemporary radio broadcasts. While the track Vivid Vision dates to 1996, the record credits identify Black And White and Creepy People as new compositions from 2001. [ref: Vibravoid Feature, Timemazine]

== Release and special editions ==
The CD edition was released in September 2002 on Nasoni Records and distributed by Swamp Room Distribution. The official record release party followed in December 2002 with a Vibravoid concert at the Duncker Club in Berlin. A recording of this show was released as Live At Duncker Berlin 2002 in 2025. [ref: Live At Duncker Berlin 2002 (Triptamine EP Vol. 8), Tonzonen Records] The vinyl edition of Void Vibration was released at the worldwide low point for vinyl records in 2003. [ref: Vinyl Revival, Journal of Popular Music Studies] The CD edition came in a black cover, while the LP was released in a white gatefold sleeve with blind embossing and a custom die-cut to be used for an optical effect. The LP was released in four different editions, including a DMM pressing in Dolby Surround quadraphonic sound on black 180-gram virgin vinyl, a white vinyl version, a regular black vinyl version and a black-and-white picture disc featuring an Op Art motif. This record is visually matched to the transparent inner sleeve printed with another Op Art graphic and being placed underneath the die cut opening. If the record is rotated inside the sleeve, moving Op Art effects are created. Production problems caused by an error during the die-cutting process delayed the regular delivery of the gatefold sleeves until February 2003. [ref: Vibravoid – Void Vibration (Master Release), Discogs]

== Reissues ==
In 2007, a remastered CD version was released by Nasoni Records. In 2012, a limited "10th Anniversary Deluxe Edition" was released by Krauted Mind Records as a double LP featuring a kinetic Op Art lenticular sleeve and as a double kinetic Op Art picture disc set in a PVC sleeve. Another limited vinyl edition was released in 2016 for the band's 25th anniversary on red-and-black marbled vinyl and included a construction kit for a cardboard pyramid named by the band the "Psychedelic Power Pyramid". [ref: Vibravoid – Void Vibration (Master Release), Discogs]

== Reception ==
The music magazine Visions described the album as an "atmospherically dense album somewhere between psychedelia, art rock and new wave", whose wide song structures are flooded with synthesizer and sitar streams. It also noted parallels to Pink Floyd, New Order and the noisy moments of Monster Magnet. [ref: Vibravoid: Void Vibration (review), Visions]

Ox-Fanzine praised the album as a successful development that surpassed the innovative psychedelic sound of its predecessor. [ref: Vibravoid – Void Vibration, Ox-Fanzine (issue 49)]

The magazine Guitar Galore described the album as "a journey through the world of psychedelic sound" and as "truly pure sound". [ref: Vibravoid – Void Vibration, Guitar Galore]

Music critic Mark Pause noted in Coolibri that the album was a more minimalistic approach and more firmly rooted in psychedelic rock. He also wrote that the record "makes even genre heavyweights such as Monster Magnet look like harmless schoolchildren" and that "Vibravoid is the most innovative Düsseldorf band since Kraftwerk". [ref: Vibravoid – Void Vibration (review), Coolibri]

# Adjustment – 3:20
# Echovoid – 5:28
# Vivid Vision – 3:34
# Electrovoid – 0:58

András Lénárd (born 6 September 1977 in Miercurea Ciuc) is a Szekler Hungarian businessman and investor from Szeklerland. He has been involved in the creation and development of businesses in several sectors, including property development, energy, food manufacturing and technology. [ref: Csinta, Samu. Háromszék. 27 August 2016. Retrieved 15 July 2026.] [ref: Kozán, István. [https://szekelyhon.ro/aktualis/lenard-andras-kiszallt-a-csiki-sorbol Lénárd András kiszállt a Csíki Sörből]. Székelyhon. 20 September 2024. Retrieved 15 July 2026.] [ref: [https://www.libertatea.ro/stiri/cine-este-lenard-andras-miliardarul-harghitean-care-a-fondat-fabrica-de-bere-csiki-sor-5072843 Cine este Lénárd András, omul de afaceri din Harghita care a fondat fabrica de bere Csíki Sör]. Libertatea. 7 November 2024. Retrieved 15 July 2026.] [ref: Felseghi, Bianca. [https://pressone.ro/suveica-prin-care-guvernul-orban-finanteaza-campania-de-identitate-a-secuilor Suveica prin care guvernul Orbán finanţează campania de identitate a secuilor]. PressOne. 28 January 2018. Retrieved 6 September 2026.] [ref: Bőtös, Botond; Sipos, Zoltán. [https://atlatszo.ro/nerdely/befektetesek/igazi-csiki-sor-ki-lehet-lenard-andras-csendestarsa/ Igazi Csíki Sör: ki lehet Lénárd András csendestársa?]. Átlátszó Erdély. 13 February 2017. Retrieved 6 September 2026.]

His best-known business has been the Csíki Sör Manufactory in Sânsimion, which gained international attention through its trademark dispute with the Romanian subsidiary of Heineken. [ref: Karasz, Palko. [https://www.nytimes.com/2017/08/04/business/heineken-transylvania-beer.html Small Transylvania Brewer Stood Up to an Industry Giant, and Survived]. The New York Times. 4 August 2017. Retrieved 15 July 2026.] Some of Lénárd's ventures in the energy sector were acquired by Magyar Villamos Művek. In 2024, he sold his 50 per cent interest in the corporate group that included the Csíki Sör and Csíki Csipsz production units founded by him. [ref: [https://mvm.hu/-/media/MVMHu/Documents/Media/Mediatartalmak/Jelentesek/EN/Archive/MVM_Group_Consolidated_Annual_Report_2014.pdf MVM Group Consolidated Annual Report 2014]. Section concerning the acquisition of the Valea Uzului hydropower project. Retrieved 15 July 2026.] Székelyhon reported, citing market information, that the buyout may have taken place at a corporate valuation of approximately €50 million.

== Early years and property development ==

Lénárd moved to the United States in the second half of the 1990s. In a 2020 interview, he said that he initially worked as a house painter before moving on to production and organisational roles in a sportswear company. He returned to Romania in 2001. [ref: Nagy, József. [https://24.hu/belfold/2020/06/19/lenard-andras-csiki-sor-interju/ Lénárd András: Elég sok bicskám van. S elég sok történetem]. 24.hu. 19 June 2020. Retrieved 15 July 2026.]

Starting in 2005, he was involved in property development in and around Miercurea Ciuc. Press reports have linked him to residential developments in the Jigodin and Șumuleu Ciuc areas and to the Hét vezér residential project. According to a Romanian press profile published in 2024, he was also involved in developing a four-star hotel in Budapest in 2015, which he later sold.

== Hydropower investments ==

Starting in the late 2000s, Lénárd became involved in hydropower projects. HydroEnergy Zrt., in which he held a majority interest, and related Romanian project companies developed power plants on the Vârghiș River and in the Valea Uzului area. [ref: Sipos, Zoltán. [https://atlatszo.ro/klimavalsag/torpe-vizeromu-oriasi-buktaval-a-magyar-allam-finanszirozza-a-csodot/ Törpe vízerőmű óriási buktával: a magyar állam finanszírozza a csődöt]. Átlátszó Erdély. 26 July 2019. Retrieved 15 July 2026.]

In January 2015, MVM completed the acquisition of a 90 per cent interest in Hivatalos SRL, the company that owned the Valea Uzului hydropower complex, from Winsland Holding Ltd. and HydroEnergy Zrt. MVM reported the total transaction value as €27.8 million.

The projects drew criticism regarding their environmental and economic aspects. Átlátszó Erdély reported that the Valea Uzului complex generated less electricity than initially estimated and that riverbed interventions raised environmental concerns. Lénárd responded that the projects had the required permits and that their environmental impact was limited.

The run-of-river hydropower technology used at Valea Uzului is commonly used in Europe. According to the European Small Hydropower Association, approximately 14,000 small hydropower plants operated in the old member states of the European Union, a further 2,800 in the new member states and approximately 400 in candidate countries, meaning that nearly 17,000 such facilities operated in Europe in total. [ref: [https://www.globalccsinstitute.com/archive/hub/publications/138218/State-art-small-hydropower-EU-25.pdf The State of the Art of Small Hydropower in the European Union]. European Small Hydropower Association. Retrieved 15 July 2026.]

The European Commission published separate guidance on how hydropower developments may be reconciled with the Natura 2000 nature-conservation framework and the requirements of the Water Framework Directive. According to the guidance, construction of hydropower plants is not prohibited, but an investment must be preceded by an environmental assessment and permitting procedure. [ref: [https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/9d8c1c3d-b7c7-11e8-99ee-01aa75ed71a1/language-en Hydropower and Natura 2000 – Guidance Document]. European Commission. Retrieved 15 July 2026.]

The electricity output of run-of-river hydropower plants depends directly on the hydrological conditions of the catchment area, including precipitation, snowmelt and water-flow conditions. As a result, annual energy production may vary naturally, and data from individual years may not necessarily be suitable for assessing the long-term performance of a facility. [ref: [https://www.eia.gov/energyexplained/hydropower/ Hydropower explained]. U.S. Energy Information Administration. Retrieved 15 July 2026.] [ref: [https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=2650 U.S. hydropower output varies dramatically from year to year]. U.S. Energy Information Administration. Retrieved 15 July 2026.] [ref: [https://www.iea.org/reports/climate-impacts-on-south-and-southeast-asian-hydropower Climate impacts on hydropower]. International Energy Agency. Retrieved 15 July 2026.]

== Csíki Sör and food production ==

In 2013, Lénárd acquired a former distillery in Sânsimion and converted it into a brewery. Production began in 2014 through Lixid Project SRL, with Lénárd serving as a major shareholder, business manager and public representative of the brand. [ref: [https://transylvanianow.com/brewery-group-as-integrator-for-the-csik-region/ Brewery group as integrator for the Csík region]. Transylvania Now. 14 October 2019. Retrieved 15 July 2026.]

The Csíki Sör and Igazi Csíki Sör trademarks led to several Romanian and European trademark disputes between Lixid Project and Heineken's Romanian subsidiary. Heineken argued that the trademarks could be confused with its Ciuc Premium brand. The proceedings produced differing rulings before the parties reached an amicable settlement in March 2017, allowing the Ciuc and Csíki trademarks to coexist and ending the related litigation. [ref: [https://www.portfolio.hu/gazdasag/20170327/megegyezett-a-heineken-es-a-csiki-sor-246110 Megegyezett a Heineken és a Csíki Sör]. Portfolio. 27 March 2017. Retrieved 15 July 2026.] [ref: [https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/economie/consumatori/povestea-unei-beri-locale-din-romania-care-s-a-luat-la-tranta-in-tribunal-cu-gigantul-heineken-772497 Povestea unei beri locale din România care s-a luat la „trântă” în tribunal cu gigantul Heineken]. Digi24. 7 August 2017. Retrieved 6 September 2026.] The New York Times covered the dispute in the context of local identity, economic nationalism and distrust of multinational companies in the region.

A wider corporate group later developed around the brewery, including distribution, hospitality and food-production businesses. Pityóka Gyár SRL was established in 2017, and production of Csíki Csipsz began in 2020. According to the Pro Economica Foundation, the potato-processing investment, valued at almost 4.5 billion Hungarian forints, received 1.7 billion forints in non-repayable support from the Hungarian government. [ref: [https://444.hu/2020/05/08/diplomatautlevele-van-a-tiltott-csiki-sort-gyarto-szekelyfoldi-ceg-vezetojenek Diplomataútlevele van a Tiltott Csíki Sört gyártó székelyföldi cég vezetőjének]. 444.hu. 8 May 2020. Retrieved 15 July 2026.]

In September 2024, Lénárd stated that he had sold 50 per cent of his shares in the Csíki Group to his partner. The transaction included the brewery and snack factory as well as restaurants, distribution and event companies. [ref: [https://telex.hu/gazdasag/2024/10/09/vilagi-oszkar-csiki-sor-lenard-andras-szlovakia-romania Szlovákiai magyar milliárdoshoz került a székelyföldi Csíki Sör]. Telex. 9 October 2024. Retrieved 15 July 2026.]

Subsequent court proceedings showed that the insolvency proceedings had been initiated by Lixid Holding BV, a Netherlands-registered company holding a 50 per cent interest in Lixid Project SRL. The proceedings ended before a decision on the merits after the applicant withdrew its petition, and no insolvency proceedings were ultimately ordered against the company.

== Technology ventures ==

Lénárd participated in the development of the drone-technology company Spider Drone Security together with engineer Attila Bustya, who was responsible for the technical development, while Lénárd was involved in financing and business organisation. [ref: Molnár, Rajmond. [https://szekelyhon.ro/aktualis/csikszek/dron-vilagrekord-szuletett-csikszentsimonban Drónvilágrekord született Csíkszentsimonban]. Székelyhon. 30 October 2015. Retrieved 15 July 2026.]

On 30 October 2015, a multirotor drone designed by Bustya completed a flight lasting 2 hours, 6 minutes and 7 seconds at Sânsimion, setting a Guinness World Record for the duration of a remotely controlled model multicopter flight. [ref: [https://www.digi24.ro/regional/digi24-brasov/record-de-zbor-al-unei-drone-452994 Record de zbor al unei drone]. Digi24. 30 October 2015. Retrieved 15 July 2026.] In 2016, Lénárd and Bustya were included as founders of Spider Drone Security in the New Europe 100 list compiled by the Res Publica Foundation with the Financial Times, Google and the International Visegrad Fund. [ref: [https://www.ft.com/content/ece06f66-90a7-11e6-a72e-b428cb934b78 New Europe 100 – changemakers in central and eastern Europe]. Financial Times. 2016. Retrieved 15 July 2026.]

Lénárd's technology ventures also included Swiss Message Bank, a service designed to store encrypted voice messages for long periods and deliver them later to designated recipients. [ref: [https://novekedes.hu/hirek/jon-az-elso-karpat-medencei-kriptovaluta Jön az első Kárpát-medencei kriptovaluta]. Növekedés.hu. 2017. Retrieved 15 July 2026.]

== Industry organisation ==

Lénárd is a founder and president of the Association of Factory Owners and Industrialists of Szeklerland. The stated objectives of the association include cooperation between industrial companies, professional representation, job creation, economic development and vocational education in the region. [ref: Statute of the Association of Factory Owners and Industrialists of Szeklerland, Sânsimion, 6 April 2021, pp. 1–8.] [ref: [https://szekelyhon.ro/aktualis/borboly-csaba-valaszara-var-lenard-andras Borboly Csaba válaszára vár Lénárd András]. Székelyhon. 27 March 2023. Retrieved 15 July 2026.]

As president of the association, he initiated public discussions in 2023 on the economic situation of Szeklerland and the need for a regional economic-development strategy.

== Dracula Park Transylvania ==

In June 2025, Lénárd announced plans for Dracula Park Transylvania, a proposed theme park in the Jigodin Baths area of Miercurea Ciuc. The announced budget for the first phase was €56 million, and the Italian company Antonio Zamperla Spa was named as the project's technology partner. [ref: [https://szereda.ro/hirek/vilagszinvonalu-elmenypark-letesul-csikszeredaban/333 Világszínvonalú élménypark létesül Csíkszeredában]. Municipality of Miercurea Ciuc. 2 June 2025. Retrieved 15 July 2026.] [ref: Kovács, Andrea. [https://hargitanepe.ro/hirek/csikszek/erdelyi-disneyland-epulhet-csikszeredaban Erdélyi Disneyland épülhet Csíkszeredában]. Hargita Népe. 3 June 2025. Retrieved 15 July 2026.]

At the beginning of 2026, the project remained in the planning stage. Investor communications described a site of nearly 30 hectares, more than 50 themed buildings and a proposed opening in 2027, subject to detailed design, permitting and financing. [ref: [https://transtelex.ro/transtelex/2026/01/31/lenard-andras-csikszereda-drakula-park Sokat ígérő látványtervekkel jelentkezett Lénárd András csíkszeredai Drakula Parkja]. Transtelex. 31 January 2026. Retrieved 15 July 2026.] [ref: [https://draculaparktransylvania.com/hu/rolunk/ About Dracula Park Transylvania]. Official project website. Retrieved 15 July 2026.]

== Legal and public controversies ==

=== Criminal case in the United States ===

News reports published in 2018, based on United States court records, stated that Lénárd was detained in 2001 near the border between the United States and Canada. A single federal charge relating to the unlawful bringing of foreign nationals into the United States was filed in the United States District Court for the Northern District of New York. He was released on bail but later failed to appear in court after returning to Romania and being unable to return to the United States. [ref: [https://444.hu/2018/01/03/embercsempeszet-miatt-keresik-az-usa-ban-a-csiki-sor-tulajdonosat Embercsempészet miatt keresik az USA-ban a Csíki Sör tulajdonosát]. 444.hu. 3 January 2018. Retrieved 15 July 2026.] [ref: [https://www.scribd.com/document/368433039/Case-title-USA-v-Lenard USA v. Andras Lenard – Criminal Case Details], 1:01-cr-00048-LEK, court-docket extract. Retrieved 15 July 2026.]

In 2023, under the Speedy Trial Act, the United States Attorney's Office for the Northern District of New York dismissed the charge. On 1 August 2023, federal judge Lawrence E. Kahn approved the dismissal of the single count with prejudice. [ref: United States District Court for the Northern District of New York. United States of America v. Andras Lenard, Criminal No. 1:01-CR-048 (LEK), Document 44, Order for Dismissal, 1 August 2023.]

=== Diplomatic passport ===

According to a parliamentary response by Hungary's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, Lénárd had been issued a diplomatic passport “to promote the success of foreign economic activity”. Foreign minister Péter Szijjártó withdrew the passport in 2024. [ref: [https://telex.hu/belfold/2024/02/24/lenard-andras-csiki-sor-diplomata-utlevel-oka-kulugyminiszterium „A külgazdasági tevékenység sikeres előremozdítása” miatt kapott diplomata-útlevelet a Csíki Sör tulajdonosa]. Telex. 24 February 2024. Retrieved 15 July 2026.] [ref: [https://telex.hu/belfold/2024/02/05/lenard-andras-csiki-sor-szijjarto-peter-diplomata-utlevel-visszavonas-kulugyminiszterium Szijjártó Péter visszavonta a Csíki Sör tulajdonosának diplomata-útlevelét]. Telex. 5 February 2024. Retrieved 15 July 2026.]

data.title: Edmund Verney (1528–1558)
data.text:
Edmund Verney (25 July 1528 – 13 December 1558) was an English politician. He sat as MP for Buckinghamshire in March 1553 and 1555. [ref: VERNEY, Edmund (1528-58), of Pendley in Tring, Herts., History of Parliament Online]

He was the first son of Sir Ralph Verney (died April 1546) of Pendley by Elizabeth, the daughter of Edmund Braye, 1st Baron Braye and the brother of Francis Verney. In 1546, he married Dorothy, daughter of Sir Edmund Peckham of Denham, Buckinghamshire. By 1555, he was married to Alice.

data.title: Rhinoceros dolphin
data.text:
The rhinoceros dolphin (Delphinus rhinoceros) is an alleged species of dolphin first discovered by French naval surgeons Jean René Constant Quoy and Joseph Paul Gaimard on the 19th of October, 1819, in the Pacific ocean while sailing between the Sandwich Islands (now the Hawaiian Islands) and New South Wales, Australia (5°28' N). [ref: Voyage Autour de Monde, Fait Par Ordere du Roi, Pillet Aîné, Printer-Bookseller, Rue Christine] It was formally described in Voyage Autour de Monde, Fait Par Ordere du Roi, a compendium of the scientific observations and accounts of the Uranie voyage around the world under the rule of Louis de Freycinet in 1824. The species is widely considered dubious. [ref: Delphinus rhinoceros, Quoy & Gaimard, 1824, World Cetacea Database]

== Morphology and discovery ==
The rhinoceros dolphin was described to have been dark in overall colour with sporadic white blotching along the dorsum which ceased around or soon after the dorsal fin closest to the fluke. The first dorsal fin was located close to or on the neck, and the species' head and face were not visible due to a hesitance to breach, a detail noted as being unlike the other dolphins encountered on the voyage. During interactions with the Uranie, the dolphins passed close to the prow of the vessel, though they did not surface frequently enough to be photographed. Consequently, the morphology of any potential beak or snout, was impossible to deduce. The cetaceans were encountered in a pod [ref: Mysterious Creatures: A Guide to Cryptozoology, ABC-CLIO] and individuals were said to have been double the length of a porpoise. Though the specific species of porpoise being referenced is not mentioned, if the size comparison was made in reference to the common porpoise (Phocoena phocoena), the rhinoceros dolphin would measure close to 3m (10ft) in length. Another two dorsal-finned cetacean resembling a dolphin was sighted breaching and playing amongst common dolphins (Delphinus delphinus) off Lantivet Bay, Cornwall, Wales, in April of 1856 by British naturalist Johnathan Couch who claimed them to have been a maximum of 2.4m (8ft) in length.

== Taxonomy and naming ==
The rhinoceros dolphin was named in reference to its frontal dorsal fin, a defining structure located close to or on the neck in superficial resemblence to the horn of a rhinoceros. [ref: The Natural History of the Ordinary Cetacea or Whales, Lizars] The species is not known from a type specimen or holotype, and is widely considered to be dubious altogether due to a lack of evidence supporting its existence beyond the description by Quoy and Gaimard. Upon description, Quoy and Gaimard suggested the taxonomic classification; (Delphinus rhinoceros), placing the species in the same genus as the common dolphin, though this conclusion was founded on little evidence. [ref: Cetaceans with two dorsal fins, Aquatic Mammals]

Later revisions of the taxonomy of the rhinoceros dolphin by French naturalist René Lesson in his 1828 book, Historie Naturelle Mammiferes place the species instead in the genus (Oxypterus). [ref: Historie Naturelle des Animaux Rares, Baudouin Brothers] This genus had been previously used by French naturalist and polymath Constantine Samuel Rafinesque in 1814 to refer to a large odotocete characterised by possessing two dorsal fins that had stranded itself 10km (6.2 miles) off Licata, Sicily in the September of 1741, which he had classified as O. mongitore. This specimen was said to have measured 13.2m (45ft) in length with a forked tail, a hole in its head that was leaking water, and a mouth equipped with strong teeth by Italian presbyter Antonio Mongitore, who illustrated the specimen along with two other whales, D. dalippus and Physeter urganantus. [ref: "Monstri Marini": Constantine S. Rafinesque's names for three of Antonio Montigore's Sicillian Whales, Archives of Natural History] Lesson refers to Oxypterus as a "subgenus" that he only gives serious attention to at all in light of the rhinoceros dolphin account. In Cetaceans with two dorsal fins, an article published as part of the seventeeth volume of the Aquatic Mammals journal in 1991, Michel Raynal dismissed this account as a misidentified basking shark (Cetorhinus maximus) rather than a newly undiscovered species of Mediterranean two dorsal-finned cetacean akin to the rhinoceros dolphin. Within the same article, Raynal proposed the hypothetical binomial name for the rhinoceros dolphin; (Cetodipterus rhinoceros), constituting a new genus within the family Delphinidae.

== Consensus in scientific literarure ==

=== In cryptozoology ===
Contemporary discussions of the rhinoceros dolphin occassionally refer to the species as a cryptid, an animal yet to be scientifically recognised due to a lack of substatiated evidence of its existence. It appeared in George M. Eberhart's 2002 book Mysterious Creatures: A Guide to Cryptozoology, where he described it as an "Unknown cetacean of the North Pacific Ocean" and discussed it alongside Couch's account of the two dorsal-finned dolphin spotted off Cornwall.

=== In cetology ===
The rhinoceros dolphin was consistently regarded as being a valid species for a short period, being included in cetological publications such as Robert Hamilton's The Natural History of the Ordinary Cetacea or Whales (1864-65) and mammologist Phillip Hershkovitz's Catalog of Living Whales (1966). [ref: Catalog of Living Whales, Smithsonian Institution] This is perhaps due to the fact that the hourglass dolphin (Cephalorhynchus cruciger), then (D. cruciger), was discovered and described by Quoy and Gaimard on the same expedition and was similarly treated as a legitimate species. Unlike the rhinoceros dolphin, the hourglass dolphin remains a valid species that has since been subsequently encountered and photographed, as well as evaluated in the context of conservation.

It has been proposed that the rhinoceros dolphin was a misidentification on Quoy and Gaimard's part, and that the description of two dorsal fins matched the profile of a mother and calf swimming tightly together and causing their silhouettes to overlap. Alternatively, the sighting may have been of a pod of any of the various species of beaked whale, many of which were not well known at the time of the encounter. Both Cuvier's and Blainville's beaked whales (Ziphius cavirostris) and (Mesoplodon densirostris) respectively possess dark bodies with white or light grey mottling of various intensities between individuals, and are known to travel in small groups of mothers and calves.

In the event that the rhinoceros dolphin does constitute a new species, the presence of a second dorsal fin is not particularly unreasonable. Raynal notes that the presence of a second fin is entirely within the realms of cetacean biology due to the nature of dorsal fin structure as a cartilaginous protrusion and the biological function they serve as stabilisation while swimming. The existing diversity among cetaceans in dorsal stabilisation biomechanisms -singular dorsal fins, no dorsal fins, or dorsal ridges, suggest that the exhibition of a second dorsal fin is not entirely impossible though it has not yet been found to exist among valid species.

data.title: Hopecore
data.text:
Hopecore is a social media trend where participants share content intended to inspire hope and optimism. [ref: What is TikTok's new 'hopecore' trend and is it exactly what we need right now?, The Independent] It typically features montages or slideshows of inspirational quotations and images, often accompanied with music. Common hopecore-themed videos include acts of kindness, personal achievements, and scenes from nature. [ref: Is Hopecore the Last Gasp of a Less-Toxic Internet?, GQ]

Hopecore was started on TikTok as an optimistic offshoot of corecore. After gaining popularity on TikTok, it spread to Instagram, YouTube, Reddit, and X. By 2024, it was also being used ironically for videos that paired cheerful imagery and music with captions about personal problems. [ref: TikTok's 'hopecore' trend shows the best-and worst-of internet optimism, Fast Company]

A 2026 study in the Journal of Documentation examined hopecore posts and user comments on Instagram. [ref: "Needed this": understanding hopecore content and engagement on Instagram, Journal of Documentation]

== Reception ==
Kieran Press-Reynolds of GQ criticised hopecore's simplistic reassurances and its commercial exploitation by influencers: "In a godless internet landscape full of dodgy influencers and grifters, it has morphed into the algorithmic equivalent of a role model for kids, who comment about how the videos have changed their mindset and leave praise like, 'This video is cleaning my ["For You" Page]!'"

data.title: Thomas Slade (MP)
data.text:
Thomas Slade of Huntingdon (died 1580) was an English lawyer and politician. He sat as MP for Huntingdon in 1572. [ref: SLADE, Thomas (d.1580), of Huntingdon and the Middle Temple, London., History of Parliament Online]

He also served as counsel to Huntingdon by 1572; and justice of the peace for Huntingdonshire from.

He was the first son of Richard Slade (died 1557) of Huntingdon by Elizabeth, the daughter of John Spencer of Bedfordshire. He was admitted into the Middle Temple in 1558 and called to the bar by 1567. He married Clayes Bellikin Clampe, who was possibly the daughter of Philip Clampe (died 1559) of Huntingdon and Brampton, Huntingdonshire. They had two daughters.

data.title: Parsamian 21
data.text:
Parsamian 21 (also spelled Parsamyan 21) is a cometary reflection nebula approximately 400 pc (1,304 ly) away in the constellation Aquila. The was discovered by Armenian astronomer Elma Parsamian in 1965 and is one out of 23 cometary nebulae discovered by her. [ref: Catalogue of Cometary Nebulae Discovered on Palomar Maps, Izvestiya Akademiya Nauk Armyanskoi SSR]

Parsamian 21 is highly polarized and illuminated by its central star designated as HBC 687. The nebula exhibits a fan-like structure with two highly illuminated bands on both sides. Two parallel bands also extend across the head of the nebula and the central star, these bands formed by aligned grains in the circumstellar disc surrounding the central star. The polarization structure of Parsamian 21 is very similar to well-studied cometary nebulae like NGC 2261 and NGC 6729. [ref: A polarization study of the cometary nebula Parsamyan 21, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society] A study utilizing an F814W filter revealed a faint southern structure. The northern structure that makes up most of Parsamian 21 features a compact northern knot and a bowed shaped southern knot. [ref: The FU Orionis--Type Spectrum and Bipolar Outflow of Parsamyan 21, Astrophysical Journal] A study reported 2-3 mag brightness fluctuations in the B band between 1966 and 1990, most of the time, Parsamian 21 barely or does not fluctuate and has remained constant at roughly 15 per cent, this leads to no significant flux have been detected in longer wavelengths. [ref: Spectroscopic observations of parsamian 21, Astronomy and Astrophysics]

Cental star HBC 687 is a low-mass, pre-main sequence FU Orionis star with an edge-on circumstellar disc. The disc appears to be flat, extending between 48 and 360 au from the central star. [ref: High-resolution polarimetry of Parsamian 21: revealing the structure of an edge-on FU Ori disc, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society] [ref: Massive Compact Disks around FU Orionis–type Young Eruptive Stars Revealed by ALMA, The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series] An of gas with a solar mass of approximately surrounds HBC 687. This envelope is expanding at about 120 km/sec away from the central star. [ref: Investigation of the cometary nebula Parsamyan 21, Astrofizika]

data.title: Is mathematics invented or discovered?
data.text:
Is mathematics invented or discovered? is a question in the philosophy of mathematics concerning whether mathematical objects, concepts, and truths exist independently of human thought, and are therefore discoveries to be found, or are products of human intellectual activity, and are therefore inventions to be made. The question invokes related debates about mathematical realism and broader questions on the nature of mathematical knowledge and the relationship between mathematics and the physical world. [ref: Philosophy of Mathematics, Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University] [ref: Why Math Works, Scientific American] [ref: Mathematics: Art and Science, The Mathematical Intelligencer]

==Overview==
The epistemological question of whether mathematical knowledge is a priori, capable of being justified independently of experience, or a posteriori, dependent upon empirical experience, is distinct from the question of whether mathematical objects exist independently of human thought. The former concerns the justification of mathematical knowledge, while the latter concerns the nature and existence of the objects of that knowledge. [ref: A Priori Justification and Knowledge, Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University]

The distinction between invention and discovery can also be applied separately to the foundations of mathematics, including the concept of natural numbers, the formulation of axioms, the development of logical systems, and the nature of mathematical proof. Whether the birth of mathematics was by chance or induced by necessity during the development of similar subjects, such as physics, remains an area of contention. [ref: Is Mathematics Discovered or Invented?, Philosophy of Mathematics Education] [ref: Math: Discovered, Invented, or Both?, pbs.org] Different philosophical approaches do not necessarily regard each of these components of mathematics in the same way. For example, mathematical Platonism holds that abstract mathematical objects exist independently of human thought, while other approaches emphasize mathematical objects or systems as constructions dependent upon human intellectual activity. [ref: Platonism in the Philosophy of Mathematics, Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University]

At least as early as 1969, the question was being explicitly formulated in terms of invention versus discovery. In Extending Understandings of Mathematics, [ref: Extending Understandings of Mathematics] published that year, Roger Osborn wrote:

Osborn thereby described the debate as a centuries-old controversy, asking whether mathematics was invented or discovered and contrasting mathematics as a creation of the human mind with mathematics as an independently existing structure awaiting discovery.

==Philosophical approaches==

The question of whether mathematics is invented or discovered depends in part on what is understood to constitute a mathematical object. A mathematical object is an abstract entity arising in mathematics. Commonly encountered mathematical objects include numbers, expressions, shapes, functions, and sets. Mathematical objects can be very complex; for example, theorems, proofs, and even formal theories are considered as mathematical objects in proof theory. Philosophers debate whether such objects have an independent existence outside of human thought or whether their existence is dependent on mental constructs or language. [ref: Abstract Objects, Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University]

Mathematical Platonism is a form of realism that holds that mathematical objects exist independently of human thought, language, and practices. Such objects are understood to be abstract, lacking spatiotemporal or causal properties. Under this view, mathematical truths are discovered rather than invented, just as scientific investigation discovers properties of independently existing physical objects. The position is associated with Plato's theory of forms, although contemporary mathematical Platonism is distinguished from Plato's own philosophical doctrines. Prominent proponents have included Kurt Gödel, who argued for a form of mathematical intuition through which mathematical objects could be apprehended.

One objection to mathematical Platonism concerns how human beings could acquire knowledge of mathematical objects if those objects exist independently of human minds and cannot be encountered through sensory experience. This difficulty, associated particularly with philosopher Paul Benacerraf, raises questions about the relationship between accounts of mathematical truth and explanations of mathematical knowledge. [ref: Mathematical Truth, The Journal of Philosophy]

By contrast, mathematical nominalism denies the existence of abstract mathematical objects. Nominalist approaches include mathematical fictionalism, which regards mathematical discourse as useful without requiring that the abstract objects to which it apparently refers actually exist. [ref: Nominalism in the Philosophy of Mathematics, Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University] Other approaches, including formalism, emphasize the manipulation of symbols according to the rules of formal systems rather than the investigation of independently existing mathematical entities. [ref: Formalism in the Philosophy of Mathematics, Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University]

Mathematical constructivism emphasizes the construction of mathematical objects and proofs, and generally requires constructive justification for claims that mathematical objects exist. Such approaches differ from classical mathematics in their treatment of certain non-constructive proofs. [ref: Constructive Mathematics, Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University] Mathematical structuralism, meanwhile, emphasizes the relationships of mathematical objects within structures rather than their individual identities. Structuralist approaches differ over whether mathematical structures exist independently of human thought, and therefore do not necessarily imply either an exclusively inventionist or discovery-based understanding of mathematics. [ref: Structuralism in the Philosophy of Mathematics, Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University]

==Arguments==
Astrophysicist Mario Livio, in his 2011 article, "Why Math Works", argues that the distinction between mathematical invention and discovery is not exhaustive, and that people develop mathematical concepts through processes of abstraction and then discover relationships among those concepts, distinguishing human selection and construction of mathematical frameworks from the consequences that mathematicians uncover within them.

Philosopher of mathematics education Paul Ernest's 1999 article, "Is Mathematics Discovered or Invented?", distinguishes between absolutist and fallibilist conceptions of mathematics. The absolutist perspective regards mathematical knowledge as universal, objective, and certain, with mathematical truths existing independently of human activity and being discovered through intuition and established through proof. Ernest identifies Roger Penrose and John D. Barrow as proponents. By contrast, the fallibilist perspective treats mathematics as a historically evolving body of knowledge, with its concepts, definitions, and proofs being subject to development and revision. Ernest associates this perspective with later Ludwig Wittgenstein, Imre Lakatos, and Philip Kitcher.

Ernest argues that the historical development of mathematics supports the fallibilist interpretation, and that mathematical disciplines have tended to emerge in response to practical problems. Examples of external circumstances influencing mathematical developments he cites include development of written arithmetic for commerce and taxation, trigonometry and spherical geometry for astronomy and navigation, and statistics for insurance and actuarial calculation. He also argues that the invention of mathematical systems does not make their conclusions arbitrary, since mathematical reasoning remains constrained by established rules and accepted assumptions. According to Ernest, the invention of mathematical systems is compatible with the subsequent recognition of mathematical relationships unanticipated at the time that the systems themselves were formulated. He compares mathematics to chess, in which the rules are human inventions but their implications may be complex and unexpected, and consequently argues that the discovery of surprising mathematical relationships does not necessarily establish underlying mathematical systems existing independently of human thought.

Mathematician Armand Borel's 1983 essay, "Mathematics: Art and Science", also examines whether mathematical theories exist independently of human thought or are created by mathematicians, and observes that a belief in the independent existence of mathematical reality is widespread among mathematicians, citing G. H. Hardy, who regarded mathematical theorems as discoveries about an external reality, and Charles Hermite, who regarded mathematical truths as existing independently of humanity through divine creation. Borel questions whether the distinction is necessarily meaningful, observing that mathematicians may experience mathematical objects as independently existing, even as they recognize "mathematics" as a human creation. Borel notes the apparent objectivity of mathematics arising from the shared intellectual experience of mathematicians. Mathematical concepts become objective in the sense that they can be understood, communicated, and investigated by different individuals, and "the language of mathematics is so precise, it is ideally suited to defining concepts for which such a consensus exist". Borel considers this sufficient to account for the perception of an independently existing mathematical reality, without requiring a conclusion about whether such a reality exists apart from human thought. Borel further characterizes mathematics as both an intellectual creation and a theoretical and experimental science, with mathematicians investigating a shared body of mathematical objects, theories, and unsolved problems, using the examination of particular cases to develop conjectures and discover general relationships. He emphasizes the coherence and unity of mathematics, by which mathematicians working independently can establish the same theorem, and separately developed mathematical theories potentially later having unexpected connections.

Mathematics educator David Tall, in his 2011 article "Crystalline Concepts in Long-Term Mathematical Invention and Discovery", argues that the two perspectives need not be in conflict, distinguishing choices made in developing mathematical representations and theories from the relationships that necessarily follow within them. For example, he says that different civilizations have devised different numeral systems and methods of calculation, but the numerical relationships they represent are not matters of arbitrary choice. Tall also discusses the development of new mathematical contexts, including non-Euclidean geometry, in which mathematicians choose definitions and assumptions and subsequently uncover their consequences. [ref: Crystalline Concepts in Long-Term Mathematical Invention and Discovery, For the Learning of Mathematics] Tall coined the phrase crystalline concept to describe a mathematical concept with an internally constrained structure of necessary relationships, applying this idea to mathematical thinking developed through the perception of shapes and space, through operations and symbols in arithmetic and algebra, and through axiomatic definitions and proofs. [ref: Crystalline Concepts in Long-Term Mathematical Invention and Discovery, For the Learning of Mathematics] On this account, mathematical concepts are constructed through human thought, but their interrelated properties can still appear inevitable and independent of any particular thinker. Tall cites the view of mathematician Christopher Zeeman, in particular, that mathematical work involves both invention and the discovery of unexpected results, and does not regard this apparent independence as requiring the existence of a separate Platonic mathematical realm.

===Indispensability of mathematics===

An argument for the independent existence of mathematical objects arises from the apparent indispensability of mathematics to the natural sciences. The Quine–Putnam indispensability argument, associated with philosophers Willard Van Orman Quine and Hilary Putnam, maintains that mathematical entities should be accepted as existing insofar as they are indispensable to our best scientific theories. The argument holds that because scientific theories depend upon mathematical objects and structures, acceptance of those theories entails an ontological commitment to the mathematical entities upon which they depend. [ref: Indispensability Arguments in the Philosophy of Mathematics, Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University]

The argument is related to questions concerning the "unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics", a phrase associated with physicist Eugene Wigner's 1960 essay on the unexpected success of mathematical theories in describing natural phenomena. [ref: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Mathematics in the Natural Sciences, Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics] Borel similarly discusses mathematical theories developed through abstract reasoning that later acquired important scientific applications, including the use of group theory and matrix algebra in quantum mechanics. The usefulness of mathematics in describing physical reality does not, however, by itself resolve the philosophical question of whether mathematical objects exist independently of human thought.

===Significance to mathematical practice===

The distinction between mathematical invention and discovery does not necessarily determine how mathematicians conduct their research. The concept of working realism describes the methodological position that mathematics may be practiced as though mathematical objects exist independently of human thought, without necessarily accepting mathematical Platonism as a metaphysical doctrine. This approach supports the use of classical mathematical reasoning, including certain non-constructive methods, without requiring resolution of the ontological question.

The question nevertheless has philosophical significance because different understandings of mathematical existence and truth can influence views about which methods of mathematical reasoning are justified. The debate also concerns the possibility of knowledge about abstract objects, the status of mathematical truths, and the relationship between the human creation of mathematical theories and the discovery of their consequences.

data.title: John Williams (legal scholar)
data.text:
John Matthew Williams (born 1967) is an Australian legal scholar specialising in constitutional law, federalism and legal history. He serves as the deputy vice-chancellor (academic) of Adelaide University, where he also holds the Dame Roma Mitchell Chair of Law. His interests are centered on the Australian Constitution and the High Court of Australia.

Williams pursued political science and industrial relations at the University of New South Wales and later continued his education in law at the same university. He graduated from the University of Tasmania with the first-class honours Bachelor of Arts in 1991 and a graduate diploma in legal practice from the University of Technology Sydney in 1993. He earned his doctorate degree in law at the Australian National University (ANU) in 1997 after writing a thesis on the Protection of Rights Under the Australian Constitution: A Republican Analysis.

In 1997, Williams joined University of Adelaide (UofA) as a lecturer in law and later became a senior lecturer in 1999. From 2004 to 2005, he worked as a reader in law at ANU and returned to Adelaide to work as a professor of law in 2006. He was appointed founding director of the South Australian Law Reform Institute in 2010 and served as the dean of law from 2011 to 2016. He worked in several other important university administrative positions, including provost at UofA from 2023 to 2025.

== Early life and education ==
John Matthew Williams was born in 1967. [ref: Judicial federalism in Australia: history, theory, doctrine and practice, Catalogue] He was the first member of his family to attend university as his mother, Judith M. Williams, was a social justice activist who has volunteered with many councils and charities throughout her life. [ref: Judith M Williams OAM Scholarship for Humanities and Social Sciences, Adelaide University]

Williams joined the University of New South Wales between 1986 and 1988 and graduated with a Bachelor of Arts in political science and industrial relations. After that, he joined the same university for law between 1989 and 1992 and taught at Basser College in 1989 and 1990. In 1991, he earned a Bachelor of Arts in first-class honours from the University of Tasmania. [ref: Prof John Williams, Researcher Profiles]

== Academic career ==
=== Early career (1992–2003) ===
Between 1992 and 1993, Williams was a deputy dean of Basser College. In 1993, Williams attained a Graduate Diploma in Legal Practice from the University of Technology Sydney and enrolled for PhD at the Australian National University (ANU). He got an ANU postgraduate scholarship and became a research assistant to Philip Pettit in 1994. In 1995, he tutored in constitutional law via the Aboriginal Tutorial Assistance Scheme. He later worked as a consultant to the National Archives of Australia (NAA) from 1996 to 1997.

In May 1997, Williams graduated with his PhD in the Law Program at the Research School of Social Sciences of ANU and his thesis title was The Protection of Rights under the Australian Constitution: A Republican Analysis. [ref: Winterton’s Australian Federal Constitutional Law: Commentary and Materials, Third Edition — Select Bibliography, Lawbook Co.] Later that year, he became a lecturer in law at the University of Adelaide (UofA) and rose to the position of senior lecturer in 1999. He was the editor of the Australian Journal of Legal History between 1997 and 2001 and founded The New Federalist: The Journal of Australian Federation History, which he edited between 1998 and 2002.

Williams was an ambassador for the South Australian "Yes" campaign in the referendum about the 1999 Australian republic referendum. In 2000, he took part in a senior fellowship at the University of Melbourne and became a member of the Don Dunstan Foundation's management board. [ref: Member (AM) in the General Division of the Order of Australia: Media Notes (M–Z), Governor-General of the Commonwealth of Australia] Additionally, he assisted the NAA in developing its Documenting a Democracy website project, which was an electronic collection of documents relating to the legislation and constitution of Australia launched in June 2000. [ref: New website documents Australia's founding charters, Government of Western Australia]

Williams was an appointed professor at the University of Cape Town in 2001 and had the position of a Menzies Foundation Fellow at King's College London from 2002 to 2003. [ref: 'Swelling the ranks of the peripatetic unemployed': the first decade of the High Court of Australia, High Court of Australia] Moreover, he was on the council of the Australian Association of Constitutional Law (AACL) from 2001 to 2008 and associate dean of research at UofA from 2003 to 2004.

=== Professorship and law reform (2004–2014) ===
Between 2004 and 2005, Williams was a reader in law at ANU. He returned to UofA as a professor of law in 2006, serving as an associate dean for research till 2010. From 2006 till 2011, he edited the Adelaide Law Review while serving as the secretary of the Judicial Conference of Australia from 2006 to 2009. He had a visiting appointment at the University of Victoria in British Columbia in 2007.

From 2008 to 2014, Williams served as a member of the NAA Advisory Council. In 2008, he joined the South Australian selection committee of the Fulbright Commission while chairing the same from 2010 to 2014. In 2009, he served as a consultant to the Good Offices Mission that assisted the United Nations in its peace process in Cyprus. He also acted as the vice-president of AACL from 2009 till 2010.

Williams was appointed as the first director of the South Australian Law Reform Institute (SALRI) in 2010. From 2011 to 2018, he was responsible for its review of succession law in South Australia. The Jay Weatherill-led government commissioned this review, which resulted in seven reports as a result of the research and consultation with the public, legal practitioners and other interested parties. [ref: Recommendations lead to landmark Succession Act reform, University of Adelaide]

Williams was the dean of law at UofA from 2011 to 2016. He and Margaret Nyland created the Dean of Law's Fund in 2014 to assist law students in financial distress. [ref: Nyland, Margaret, The Australian Women's Register] Williams was also the Harold White Fellow at the National Library of Australia.

=== University leadership (2015–present) ===
[[File:March 2026 Graduation Ceremonies (University of Adelaide) - 33.jpg|thumb|Williams, Peter Høj and John Hill at the final UofA graduation ceremonies following Høj's tenure as vice-chancellor, March 2026]]
In 2015, Williams was appointed to the position of Dame Roma Mitchell Chair in Law. He was also made the pro-vice-chancellor for research operations and dean of graduate studies, a combined role, which he held until 2018. He also became a member of the board of Adelaide Festival of Ideas. Williams was the chair of the university's Academic Board from 2016 to 2021.

In November 2016, Williams restated SALRI's proposal that the provocation defence, also called the "gay panic defence", be abolished. [ref: Weatherill's "premature" apology to LGBTIQ community, InDaily] During 2017, he collaborated with Morry Bailes and a colleague from UofA to design a preferential ballot system for choosing the Law Council of Australia's executive.

Williams was appointed associate provost and executive dean of the Faculty of the Professions in 2018, serving as executive dean from then until 2022. He returned as a member of the NAA Advisory Council from 2018 until 2021. [ref: ]

In 2019, Williams advocated for the review of abortion laws in South Australia, as suggested by Attorney-General Vickie Chapman. [ref: Independent SA body to undertake examination of state abortion laws, Lawyers Weekly] The resulting SALRI report recommended that abortion be decriminalised and regulated through health laws. The report proposed 66 reforms and considered over 3,000 submissions. [ref: How your views will affect abortion law change, CityMag]

Williams held several positions as acting and interim provost during 2020 and 2021. He was named the first executive dean of the Faculty of Arts, Business, Law and Economics after the merger of the Faculty of Arts and the Faculty of the Professions in March 2022.

The South Australian Parliament enacted the Succession Act 2023 in September 2023, which put into effect 107 of the 113 recommendations of the SALRI report on the succession law review. Williams acted as the provost of UofA from 2023 to 2025.

On 30 September 2024, Williams became the deputy vice-chancellor (academic) of Adelaide University, created by the merger of UofA and the University of South Australia. He took up his position on 1 October 2024 before the establishment of the new university in January 2026. [ref: Adelaide University names deputy vice-chancellors, InDaily] Following the merger, on 6 August 2026, Arts Minister Kyam Maher appointed Williams a member of the board of the Art Gallery of South Australia for a three-year term. [ref: New appointments to Art Gallery of SA board, InDaily]

== Honours and awards ==
Williams was honoured with the W. Townsley Award from the University of Tasmania in 1991 and the Best Academic Award from the Adelaide Law School in 1997. The Centenary Medal was bestowed on him in 2003.

The Australian Academy of Law conferred him with a fellowship (FAAL) in 2012. In the 2022 Australia Day Honours, [ref: UNSW Sydney community celebrates recipients of Australia Day Honours, UNSW Sydney] Williams was made a Member of the Order of Australia (AM) for his contribution to tertiary education, law and professional bodies.

On 26 October 2025, Williams became a Fellow of the Academy of the Social Sciences in Australia (FASSA) due to his contributions to the field of Australian constitutional law. [ref: Shaping Australia’s policy and future: Academy appoints 22 distinguished social science leaders as new Fellows, Academy of the Social Sciences in Australia]

== Selected publications ==
=== Books ===
==== Authored ====
* One Hundred Years of the High Court of Australia, Menzies Centre for Australian Studies
* The Australian Constitution: A Documentary History, Melbourne University Press

==== Edited ====
* Makers of Miracles: The Cast of the Federation Story, Melbourne University Press

data.title: Edmund Peckham
data.text:
Sir Edmund Peckham (by 1495 – 29 March 1564) was an English politician. He sat as MP for Buckinghamshire in October 1553, and November 1554. [ref: PECKHAM, Sir Edmund (by 1495-1564), of the Blackfriars, London and Denham, Bucks., History of Parliament Online]

He was knighted on 18 May 1542.

== Political career ==
He also served as clerk of the counting house by 1520; treasurer of the chamber from 1 May 1522 till 1 January 1524; cofferer of the Household from January 1524 till 31 March 1547; justice of the peace for Buckinghamshire from 1525 till 1543, for Middlesex from 1537 till 1543, quorum Buckinghamshire, and Middlesex from 1554 till 1558/59; constable of Scarborough Castle in Yorkshire from 1529 till 1537; high treasurer of all the mints from 25 March 1544 till his death; member of the Privy Council from 6 till 30 October 1549, and 29 July 1553 till November 1558; commissioner of relief in Buckinghamshire, and Middlesex in 1550, commissioner of goods of churches and fraternities in 1553, commissioner of subsidy in Buckinghamshire in 1558; and receiver-general of the Exchequer on 1 December 1553.

== Family ==
He was the second son of Peter Peckham of London and Denham by his second wife Elizabeth, the daughter of Henry Eburton of London. By 1516, he was married to Anne, the daughter of John Cheyne of Chesham Bois, Buckinghamshire and they had four sons (including Henry and Sir Robert Peckham) and two daughters.

data.title: Francesca Cordelia Merlan
data.text:
Francesca Cordelia Merlan is an American-born Australian anthropologist whose research focuses on Indigenous-settler relations [ref: Dynamics of difference in Australia: indigenous past and present in a settler country, by Merlan, Francesca, HAL (Le Centre pour la Communication Scientifique Directe)], social transformation, land claims, gender, and linguistic documentation. [ref: Settlers and their land rights: Francesca Merlan, ‘Anthropology and change over the ‘land rights era’: Towards treaties?’ Australian Journal of Anthropology, 2025, settler colonial studies blog] [ref: Francesca Merlan, "Dynamics of Difference in Australia: Indigenous Past and Present in a Settler Country" (U Pennsylvania Press, 2018), New Books Network] in northern Australia [ref: ], Papua New Guinea [ref: Ku Waru: Language and segmentary politics in the western Nebilyer Valley, Papua New Guinea. By Francesca Merlan and Alan Rumsey. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1991. Pp. xviii, 387. Cloth $59.50., Language], and Germany. She is professor emeritus of Anthropology at the Australian National University (ANU) and Fellow of the Academy of the Social Sciences in Australia. [ref: ] In 2003 she was awarded the Centenary Medal from Department of Prime Minister and Cabinet, Australia. [ref: ]

== Education and career ==
She completed her MA and PhD in anthropology at the University of New Mexico in 1975, conducting doctoral research on Native American and settler communities in the North American Plains. [ref: Moscow High School... Class of 1965, Francesca Merlan, www.mhs1965.com]

In 1976, Merlan was awarded a research grant from the Australian Institute of Aboriginal Studies, bringing her to northern Australia for fieldwork that lasted from 1976 to 1979.

She joined the Australian National University as Professor of Anthropology in 1995 and has since been appointed professor emeritus. [ref: ] She has held a visiting fellowship at the Institute of Advanced Study, Princeton (2015–16). [ref: ]

== Scholarly works ==
Merlan's research focuses three geographic regions. In northern Australia, she has investigated the effects of Aboriginal people's movement into regional towns; Indigenous-settler relations [ref: Relative Autonomy Revisited: Reply to Francesca Merlan, American Anthropologist]; Aboriginal languages, socio-cultural significance and land claims. [ref: Power and Recognition: Australia's Indigenous People Today, University of Pennsylvania Press] Her book Caging the Rainbow: Places, Politics and Aborigines in a North Australian Town (1998), which examined the lives of Aboriginal people in Katherine, Northern Territory.

Her later book Dynamics of Difference in Australia: Indigenous Past and Present in a Settler Country (2018) investigated relations between Indigenous and non-Indigenous Australians from first contact to the present. [ref: Merlan, Francesca. 2018. Dynamics of difference in Australia: indigenous past and present in a settler country. Philadelphia, PA: University of Pennsylvania Press. 320 pp. Hb.: US$59.95. ISBN: 9780812250008., Social Anthropology] [ref: ]

Her co-authored work Ku Waru: Language and Segmentary Politics in the Western Nebilyer Valley, Papua New Guinea (1991) examined segmentary sociality, language, and politics. [ref: Gender as a Dimension in Changing Hegemonies, History of Anthropology Review] [ref: Children's Language Learning and the Making of Human Lifeworlds, School of Culture, History & Language]

Her other works include Mangarayi (1982), Ngalakan Grammar, Texts, and Vocabulary (1983) and A Grammar of Wardaman (1993). [ref: Review of A Grammar of Wardaman, a Language of the Northern Territory of Australia, Language]

data.title: SCenTRLE
data.text:
== Student-Centered, Technology-Rich Learning Environments (SCenTRLE)==
Student-Centered, Technology-Rich Learning Environments (SCenTRLE) is an instructional design model developed by educational researcher Atsusi Hirumi. Developed in the 1990s and formally described in a 2002 publication, the model uses eight instructional events to support student-centred learning based on constructivist principles. It focuses on active participation, knowledge construction and learner independence, and uses technology to support the learning process. [ref: Student-Centered, Technology-Rich Learning Environments (SCenTRLE): Operationalizing Constructivist Approaches to Teaching and Learning, Journal of Technology and Teacher Education]

== Theoretical background ==

The SCenTRLE model is grounded in constructivist learning theory, which positions learners as active participants in the development of knowledge. Hirumi identified four foundations for the model: societal, psychological, epistemological and pedagogical. These principles are also discussed in wider research on technology-enhanced student-centred learning environments. [ref: The Foundations and Assumptions of Technology-Enhanced Student-Centered Learning Environments, Instructional Science]

Hirumi posits that the societal foundation is based on the growing role of information and technology in education. He argued that greater access to information requires learners to develop competences beyond subject knowledge, including problem-solving, communication and independent learning.

Secondly, the psychological foundation draws on constructivist perspectives, particularly those of Jean Piaget, Jerome Bruner and Lev Vygotsky. It explains how learners acquire knowledge through experience, cognitive development and social interaction.

Thirdly, the epistemological foundation is rooted in pragmatism. While recognising an external reality, this perspective claims that individuals construct knowledge through experience, prior understanding and interaction with others.

Finally, the pedagogical foundation integrates student-centred learning, generative learning, situated cognition, problem-based learning and performance assessment. Together, they foster active participation, authentic learning and the practical application of knowledge. In SCenTRLE, learners contribute to decisions about their learning, while instructors provide ongoing guidance and feedback.

== The eight instructional events ==

The SCenTRLE model comprises eight instructional events that guide student-centred learning. These events provide a framework in which learners help establish objectives, select learning strategies and assess their progress. Although the events are presented sequentially, learners may revisit earlier activities as their understanding develops. [ref: Vicarious Interactions and Self-Directed Learning of Students by Course Delivery Strategy, Texas A&M University]

# Set Learning Challenge: The instructor establishes a learning challenge that defines what students should be able to accomplish and provides the overall direction.
# Negotiate Learning Goals and Objectives: Learners collaborate with the instructor to determine the knowledge and skills required to meet the challenge. This includes assessing prior knowledge, identifying areas for improvement and developing individual learning objectives.
# Negotiate Learning Strategies: Students identify the activities and resources they will use to achieve their learning objectives. The instructor provides guidance while encouraging learners to determine which approaches best address their needs.
# Construct Knowledge: Learners apply their selected strategies, individually or collaboratively, to develop knowledge and skills. The instructor monitors progress and provides support when needed.
# Negotiate Performance Criteria: Learners and instructors establish criteria for determining whether the learning objectives have been achieved. Assessment rubrics may be developed to help learners evaluate the quality of their work.
# Conduct Self, Peer and Expert Assessments: Students evaluate their work against the agreed performance criteria and receive feedback from peers and individuals with relevant expertise.
# Monitor Performance and Provide Feedback: Monitoring and feedback occur throughout the learning process rather than at a single stage. Instructors review students' work, respond to questions and provide feedback on their progress and students monitor their own progress.
# Communicate Results: The final event involves formally presenting the outcomes of learning. Students may use portfolios, presentations or other work samples to demonstrate their achievements.

The eight events promote learner independence while preserving the instructor's role as a facilitator.

== Applications and case studies ==

=== Initial implementation in higher education ===

Hirumi reported an initial field test of SCenTRLE in a 15-week undergraduate course on the educational applications of computer technology. The course included 30 students with varying levels of computer experience: seven novice users, 17 apprentices and six more proficient users. The model was introduced to address these differences and enable students to pursue learning objectives aligned with their existing knowledge and interests.

Students negotiated their learning goals and strategies with the instructor and developed portfolios to demonstrate their progress. The portfolios included assessment rubrics, work samples and reflections on learning. Students were assessed on their progress across five course standards and were given opportunities to revise their work in response to feedback.

Of the 28 students who completed the course, 12 received an A, 13 received a B, two received a C and one received an F. Hirumi reported that most students improved their computer-related skills. However, the findings were drawn from a single course, and Hirumi acknowledged that they were insufficient to establish the model's effectiveness in other educational settings.

=== Application in secondary mathematics education ===

Mlotshwa, Tunjera and Chigona (2020) used SCenTRLE as a framework for integrating Moodle into Grade 10 mathematics teaching in South Africa. They selected the model because it combines constructivist learning principles with the use of technology. Their intervention followed three levels involving teacher guidance, interaction with peers and learning materials, and independent learning through Moodle. [ref: Integration of MOODLE into the classroom for better conceptual understanding of functions in Mathematics, South African Journal of Education]

The researchers found that students who used Moodle performed better than those who received conventional classroom instruction. They recommended integrating Moodle into mathematics teaching and considering SCenTRLE for teacher training.

== Reception and criticism ==

The implementation of SCenTRLE raises concerns about learner readiness, instructional support and assessment. Barksdale (2018) discusses the challenges students may face when transitioning from teacher-directed to student-centred learning, including anxiety, confusion and frustration. Drawing on Hirumi's initial field test, she notes that learners may find it difficult to assume greater responsibility for managing their own learning. [ref: Assessment with Technology Integrated Menus: Creating a Bridge Between Traditional and Student-Centered Learning]

Assessment presents a further challenge. Barksdale (2018) highlights the importance of aligning assessment with student-centred instruction, including greater learner participation in establishing performance criteria and evaluating work. Similarly, Hirumi reported that students in his initial study sought clearer feedback on their progress, even though they regarded portfolio assessment as fair.

Miró i Fuentes (2009) examined SCenTRLE alongside Jonassen's Mindtools and considered the challenges of adapting educational methods to technology-rich environments. He distinguished between the approaches by describing SCenTRLE as a model concerned with organising learning processes in response to the educational and technological context. [ref: Reseña sobre los nuevos métodos pedagógicos colaborativos, Cuadernos de Educación y Desarrollo]

data.title: Social Health
data.text:
----

What is Social Health?

Social health is a person’s overall well-being, including relationships, social support systems, and community. It studies how people establish links with family, friends and their place of work. Physical health relates to physical health, mental health and psychological well-being. Social health relates to the quality and importance of human interaction that affects overall health.

The concept of social health is not new and has been researched for a long time before the establishment of modern educational programs. The term has been used frequently by public health experts and researchers to explain how a person’s well-being is affected by involvement in the community and relationships. Over the years, a variety of frameworks have been developed.

The concept of social health is not new, and has been studied long before modern educational programs were created. Researchers and public health experts have often used the term to explain how relationships and community participation shape an individual's well-being. Over time, different frameworks have placed social health alongside physical and mental health as an integral part of overall wellness. Social health is a crucial component of overall health, alongside physical and mental health, and has been so throughout history, albeit in different frameworks.

There is a lot of research that shows that stronger relationships and social connections are related to better overall health. Feeling lonely and isolated is linked to poor physical and mental health, while feeling connected and supported is linked to lower risk of depression and anxiety. This can be a two-way thing, experts say, with mental health problems also making it more difficult to sustain relationships.

Because social connections have health effects, educators and therapists wonder if the skills that make them possible can be taught directly. Relationships are a natural thing. Communication can be taught using a skill based approach.A skill-based approach can teach communication, listening, and working through difficult conversations/conflict, rather than taking relationships as something that happens naturally.

Therapist David Koslowski, who spent years working with teens in his private practice and running free community support groups, created a social health class. In Utah, at Herriman High School, he created a program called Level Up to teach students practical communication and relationship skills. Koslowski has said he did not create the idea of social health, but formed the class as a practical use of it to be taught in schools.

data.title: Taxonomy of Significant Learning
data.text:
== Background and Development ==
L. Dee Fink, an American scholar and consultant  whose work focuses on higher education and instructional  design,  which  mainly concentrates on the significant learning experience. He served as director of the Instructional Development Program at the University of Oklahoma and has written about faculty development and approaches to improving teaching in higher education. [ref: Becoming a Professional Engineering Educator: A New Role for a New Era, Journal of Engineering Education] [ref: Toward learning‐centered education in colleges and universities, New Directions for Teaching and Learning]

Fink is particularly interested in the types of learning that have significant and lasting effects on students. He moved beyond the belief which places emphasis on planning courses around the content and skills that students are required to obtain at the end of the unit. Fink argued that  learning outcome should not only include learning goals but also apply know knowledge, make connection across subjects, understand others, develop different interest and continue to learn independently [ref: 7: Higher–Level Learning: The First Step toward More Significant Learning, To Improve the Academy] [ref: Creating Significant Learning Experiences: An Integrated Approach to Designing College Courses, Canadian Journal of University Continuing Education]

"Higher-Level Learning: The First Step toward More Significant Learning," was a taxonomy presented in 2001 to help educators develop more rigorous learning goals. He expanded this methodology in his 2003 Creating Significant Learning Experiences connecting the taxonomy to an integrated process for designing and developing courses in higher education. This approach requires higher education educator to not only present the content of the course but facilitate how students apply it in academic, professional and personal contexts, therefore integrating course design, teaching strategies and assessment within a single process.
