data.title: Susantha Salgado
data.text:
= Susantha Salgado =
Shihan J. Susantha Salgado (born 17 November 1962) is a Sri Lankan karate instructor, coach, and martial arts administrator. He is known for his involvement in the promotion of Nihon Karate Do Kenshukai in Sri Lanka and has served as the Head Master and Chief Instructor of the organization. Salgado holds a 7th Dan Black Belt recognized by Nihon Karate Do Kenshukai, Japan, and has been active in karate training, coaching, and administration for several decades.

== Early Life ==
Susantha Salgado was born on 17 November 1962 and is from Negombo, Sri Lanka, where he has been involved in martial arts training and instruction throughout much of his life.

== Martial Arts Career ==
Salgado is associated with Nihon Karate Do Kenshukai Sri Lanka, serving in leadership and instructional roles within the organization. He has been identified as:

* Chairman and Director of Nihon Karate Do Kenshukai Sri Lanka
* Chief Instructor of Nihon Karate Do Kenshukai Sri Lanka
* Representative Branch Manager of Nihon Karate Do Kenshukai, Japan
* Senior A Grade Coach
* Member of the Sri Lanka Karate Do Federation
* Life Member of the Sri Lanka School Karate Do Association

He has conducted karate training programs, black belt examinations, and coaching activities aimed at developing karate practitioners in Sri Lanka.

== Training in Japan ==
In 2013, Salgado was among a group of Sri Lankan karate instructors who participated in a specialized training program in Japan under the invitation of Japan Nihon Karate Do Kenshukai. Media coverage reported that Salgado and other instructors underwent advanced technical training and grading activities during the visit.

The training initiative was highlighted in the Daily Mirror article "Karatekas return after training in Japan", which reported on representatives of the Sri Lankan Kenshukai organization attending a 25-day training program in Japan.

== Leadership of Kenshukai Sri Lanka ==
Under Salgado's leadership, Nihon Karate Do Kenshukai Sri Lanka has organized karate training programs, coaching seminars, grading examinations, and black belt certification programs. Social media records from the organization's official pages identify Salgado as the Head Master of the Sri Lankan branch and reference his supervision of black belt examinations and instructor development activities.

== Ranks and Recognition ==
Salgado is reported to hold:

* 7th Dan Black Belt in Nihon Karate Do Kenshukai, Japan
* 8th Dan Black Belt in Wano Michiryu Karate and Kobudo U.S.A.

He has been recognized within karate organizations in Sri Lanka for his contribution to technical instruction and the development of karate practitioners.

== Personal Life ==
Salgado resides in Negombo, Sri Lanka.

* Nihon Karate Do Kenshukai

= Chris Frara =
[https://www.chrisfrarastudios.com/about Chris Frara] is a South-African born commercial photographer, director and former professional rugby player based in Los Angeles. He has worked with major brands including Dior, Nike and celebrities such as [https://www.chrisfrarastudios.com/event-photography/casamigos-george-clooney-event George Clooney]. He also runs [https://www.chrisfrarastudios.com/ Chris Frara Studios], his own photography and video production studio in Southern California.

== Early Life and Background ==
He was born and raised in South Africa, where rugby played a major role in his early life. He went to play professionally in South Africa, London and San Diego before moving to Los Angeles in his early twenties. After leaving rugby, Frara spent almost a decade working as an ecommerce director in the fashion industry.

== Photographer career ==
Frara's photography career began around 2016, when a photographer failed to show up for a scheduled fashion shoot. In a 2024 interview with [https://shoutoutla.com/meet-chris-frara-chris-frara-studios-professional-commercial-photographer/ SHOUTOUT LA], he recalled stepping in to take the photos himself. Later he founded [https://www.chrisfrarastudios.com/ Chris Frara Studios], and went to work on photography and video projects for brands including Dior, Guess, Nike, Levi's and Calvin Klein. His work covers everything from product photography to advertising campaigns and commercial films. He also works as a director taking part in the planning and production of visual campaigns.

A 2025 article published by [https://demoday.la/meet-chris-frara-los-angeles-most-creative-photographer/ DemoDay LA] described Frara's approach to photography as one focused on storytelling and creating a particular mood, rather than simpy presenting a product. The article also highlighted his work with clients to develop images that reflect their brand's identity.

data.title: ADA KATE UCHEGBU
data.text:
----

Ada Kate Uchegbu (born September 30, 1982) is a Nigerian journalist, writer, and political figure. Born in Ebute Metta, Lagos State, she serves as the Chief Executive Officer of ADA Consolidated Nigeria Limited and the Editor of Distinguished Africans Magazine. Over a multi-decade career in public life, she has worked as an investigative reporter covering regional security, managed diversified corporate portfolios, and contested multiple electoral positions, culminating in a declaration for the 2027 presidential election cycle.

== Early life and education ==
Ada Kate Uchegbu was born on September 30, 1982, in the Ebute Metta area of Lagos State, Nigeria. She began her secondary education at Command Secondary School in Ipaja, Lagos, and later completed her secondary studies at Apata Memorial High School in Isolo, Lagos. She completed her higher education at the National Open University of Nigeria. To specialize in communication and language, she undertook vocational courses at the National Broadcast Academy in Lagos and studied at Alliance Française Lagos. She holds the traditional Igbo title of Iyom Omelorah.

== Career ==
=== Media and corporate leadership ===
Uchegbu worked as an investigative reporter focusing on regional insecurity, economic disparities, and institutional governance across West Africa. Her written work includes the investigative report "Roads of Blood – The Kidnap Highway", which examined systemic highway kidnapping infrastructure within Nigeria.

She directs commercial operations as the Chief Executive Officer of ADA Consolidated Nigeria Limited, a conglomerate operating across real estate, media publishing, and the oil and gas sectors. As part of her media portfolio, she serves as the Editor of Distinguished Africans Magazine, a pan-African publication that documents regional leadership, corporate enterprise, cultural promotion, and profiles of contemporary African innovators.

=== Literary works ===
As an author, Uchegbu has published both non-fiction political works and fiction:
* Wings of Destiny: My Journey Through Power, Politics and the Dream of Nigeria's First Female President (2026) – A memoir analyzing female political inclusion and party ticket dynamics in contemporary Nigeria.
* Ada the Future President – A children's book series centered on civic responsibility and leadership development.
* Kidnapped and The Dark Testament – Fiction novels dealing with modern socio-political anxieties.
* African Short Horror Stories – A multi-volume fiction anthology incorporating traditional folklore, superstition, and supernatural motifs.

== Political career and recognition ==
Uchegbu has engaged in local and national politics for over fifteen years. She began her electoral career by contesting the 2011 elections for the Anambra State House of Assembly. The following year, she entered national party politics during the March 2012 Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) National Convention, running as an aspirant from Anambra State for the position of National Women Leader. On May 30, 2017, she received recognition from the National Youth Council of Nigeria (NYCN), winning an award in the emerging youth category. Later that year, she joined the All Progressives Congress (APC) and stood as one of only three female aspirants out of twenty-six total candidates cleared to contest the August 2017 APC gubernatorial primary election ahead of the Anambra State governorship election.

In mid-2025, Uchegbu announced her intention to run for the President of Nigeria in the 2027 general elections under the PDP banner, presenting a policy blueprint titled "The New Covenant". Her campaign platform emphasized breaking recycled leadership patterns through digitized public administration, establishing a ₦150 billion Youth Enterprise Fund, and decentralizing policing systems. After the 2026 party selection cycles favored male candidates for major tickets, she transitioned into wider policy advocacy. In late 2026, she spoke on electoral inclusion and African female leadership at the African Women Summit in Croydon, England.

== Media appearances ==
Uchegbu has used television and radio broadcast segments to critique national security frameworks and support gender parity in politics. Between late 2025 and 2026, she completed a series of interviews on Silverbird Television and Radio Nigeria network news updates. Her media commentary focused on public community health reforms, economic restructuring, and structural changes to political primary nomination rules.

data.title: 10 Pujaan Malindo Vol. 1
data.text:
----
10 Pujaan Malindo Vol.1 [ref: ] is Noraniza Idris’s debut studio album, and the songs she performs are cover versions of tracks previously popularised by local artists as well as those from neighbouring countries (Indonesia). The album 10 Pujaan Malindo was recorded in two volumes, released in 1986 and 1987. This album series was launched in 1986 by Life Records (Hup Hup Sdn. Bhd.).

== Background ==
After taking part in an audition organised by RTM, the winner of the 1985 RTM Bintang competition, Noraniza Idris, was approached by Hamidi, the publisher and producer at Life Records, who wanted her to become a recording artist because he was captivated by the sweetness of her voice; The offer first arose whilst she was still participating in the 1985 RTM Star competition, which had not yet concluded. At the time, she was with her father, Idris Ahmad, enjoying a meal at the Angkasapuri canteen—the venue where she had taken the RTM talent test. Eventually, after much consideration, she agreed to sign a contract with Life Records on 1 January 1986 and officially became a recording artist – marking the first recording contract of her career. She also released her debut album, a compilation titled Melayu Deli, alongside a legendary singer of the 1980s on 1 January 1986. Meanwhile, he had taken part in the 1985 Bintang RTM competition, though he only reached the semi-finals; however, he remained resilient, and perhaps Hamidi’s arrival and his official status as a recording artist served as the remedy he had been seeking all along. [ref: NORANIZA IDRIS: 12 LAGU PALING POPULAR SEPANJANG ZAMAN, GALAKSIVIRAL]

The release of the album 10 Pujaan Malindo Vol.1 in 1986 on the Life Records label (Hup Hup Sdn. Bhd.) marked a highly significant milestone in Noraniza Idris’s professional discography. This major project was released at a time when the regional music market was witnessing a vibrant wave of cultural exchange between Malaysia and Indonesia (the acronym for ‘Malindo’). As a new singer establishing her name in the 1980s, Noraniza was sent to Jakarta, Indonesia, to undertake the vocal recording and musical arrangement process on location. This strategic move by the record company was taken to ensure that the resulting archipelago-inspired music possessed authentic aesthetic value and high production standards. The album’s extraordinary success in the market not only placed her on the mainstream industry’s radar but also paved the way for the production of its sequel, 10 Pujaan Malindo Vol.2, which was released the following year. [ref: ]

== Album summary ==
In terms of track selection, 10 Pujaan Malindo Vol. 1 presents a compilation studio album concept based on cover versions of popular songs that once propelled the original singers to fame in both countries. Released on physical cassette format and widely distributed in Malaysia and Singapore, the album features a selection of songs in the creative pop and contemporary folk genres. The album’s standout track, which achieved the greatest commercial impact, was the upbeat song titled “Anak Tani” (or better known by its original Indonesian title, “Singkong dan Keju”). The song became a radio phenomenon on local stations, sparking a unique cultural impact; the commercial impact of these cover versions even led some fans to dub Noraniza with the somewhat derisive nickname “Queen of Covers" or “Queen of Plagiarism” early in her career, due to her vocal prowess in breathing new life into these songs whilst imbuing them with her own distinct identity. In today’s digital age, a significant portion of the key repertoire from this classic 1986 cassette album series has been officially re-compiled by Life Records into a digital streaming album titled Nostalgia Malindo. Furthermore, several tracks from this album that became hits have been included in a compilation album entitled 16 Pujaan Malindo.

== Track list ==

== Workforce ==
The following are the credits for those who contributed to the production of her album, based on the cover of her album, 10 Pujaan Malindo Vol.1.

* Ramli MS – Arranger
* Life Production – Publisher
* Noraniza Idris – Lead Vocals
* A. Ali – Backing Vocals
* Sham – Backing Vocals
* A. Riyanto, Arie Wibowo, Omar Taib, Othman Mohamad, A. Ali, Harry Toes, Ahmad Nawab & Youngky PM – Composers
* Peter Chong – Sound Engineer

* A. Riyanto, Hamirul Aizat, Lukhman S, Tuah, Zainal Baharum Bidor, Harry Toes, Sharifah Aini, Youngky RM & Habsah Hassan – Lyricists
* Kelly Chua – Artwork
* Hamidi Rashid – Production Manager

data.title: Joyce Jarvis
data.text:
Joyce Elane Westfall (1927 – June 2016), known professionally during her film career as Joyce Jarvis and later in academia as Professor Joyce Ramsay, was an American film actress, union representative, and associate professor of theatre at Michigan State University.

== Early life and education ==
Born Joyce Elane Westfall, she was raised in Michigan, the daughter of Roy A. and Mary Westfall. She attended Mackenzie High School in Detroit before enrolling at Michigan State University from 1949 to 1950. [ref: Joyce Jarvis - Biography, IMDb] In 1950, she married Arthur Murray Jarvis and relocated to California to pursue formal theatrical training at the Pasadena Playhouse College of Theatre Arts.

== Career ==
=== Hollywood and Film Career ===
Acting under her married name, Joyce Jarvis, she secured a screen test with Paramount Pictures and began working in commercial cinema and television. In February 1953, she appeared on a live broadcast of NBC's The Colgate Comedy Hour hosted by Eddie Cantor. [ref: The Colgate Comedy Hour (Season 3, Episode 22), IMDb]

Later that year, Jarvis co-starred as Valerie Creighton, a prominent rebellious student, in the Columbia Pictures exploitation melodrama Problem Girls (1953). [ref: Problem Girls (1953) Full Cast & Crew, IMDb] She followed this with a performance as Princess Arsinoe, the younger sister of Cleopatra, in the Technicolor historical epic Serpent of the Nile (1953), directed by William Castle. During her career in California, she also became actively involved with the Screen Actors Guild (SAG), serving in localized branch leadership and contract committee roles.

=== Academia and Later Career ===
Following her departure from the Hollywood studio system, she divorced and later remarried, adopting the surname Ramsay.

In the fall of 1979, she returned to Michigan State University's Department of Theatre as an Associate Professor and Artist-in-Residence under the name Joyce Ramsay. [ref: Feature: Spartans in Hollywood, MSU Spartan Story Hub] She spent more than two decades at the university teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in acting technique and physical improvisation. Her tenure overlapped with the final college years of future television star Jon-Erik Hexum, who studied in the Department of Theatre before graduating in May 1980.

In April 1980, Ramsay made her university mainstage directorial debut at the Fairchild Theatre with a production of Alan Ayckbourn's farce How the Other Half Loves, while concurrently appearing as a performer in the Michigan State University Performing Arts Company’s staging of Julius Caesar [ref: 'How Other Half Loves' opens tonight, The State News]. In addition to her studio instruction, she served on graduate Master of Fine Arts (MFA) thesis committees and introduced prominent guest creators for the MSU Celebrity Lecture Series, including playwright August Wilson. [ref: MSU Celebrity Lecture Series Archive: August Wilson, Michigan State University]

== Death and Legacy ==
Ramsay continued to teach at Michigan State University through the late 1990s and into the 2000s. She passed away in June 2016. Following her death, the Michigan State University Department of Theatre formally recognized her multi-decade impact as a "tremendous educator" who shaped generations of Spartan performers. [ref: MSU Department of Theatre Memorial Announcement, Facebook]

* Problem Girls (1953) — Valerie Creighton

data.title: Dove (magazine)
data.text:
Dove Viaggi (often simply Dove) is an Italian monthly travel and lifestyle magazine established in 1991 and published by RCS MediaGroup (ISSN 1121-1792). [ref: Dove, rcsmediagroup.it] [ref: Sito ufficiale Dove Viaggi, Corriere della Sera]

== History ==
The magazine was founded in May 1991 by journalist and publisher Luca Grandori (d. 2012), who had previously created other Italian travel publications, including Gulliver and Carnet. [ref: 25 anni di viaggi e sogni: l’editoriale del numero speciale di DOVE, Dove Viaggi] Its initial editorial office was located in Milan, with a founding team that included journalists Valeria Tegami, Mariella Grossi and Simona Tedesco.

During the 1990s, the magazine published themed print supplements, such as Speciale Weekend (focused on short itineraries) and Dossier Tropici (covering long-haul destinations). [ref: Cronologia e Linee di Sviluppo del Sistema DOVE, CairoRCS Media] In 2005, the publication released a series of spin-off magazines: DOVE Case, DOVE Eventi, and DOVE Auto. [ref: Dove negli anni, Corriere della Sera]

Valeria Tegami later became the magazine's director, followed by Carlo Montanaro. In January 2015, Simona Tedesco was appointed editor-in-chief, with an editorial focus on contemporary and sustainable travel.

In May 2017, the publication launched an annual Travel issue, distributed as a supplement with the daily newspaper Corriere della Sera.

In 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic, the magazine temporarily shifted its editorial focus to domestic and local travel and launched digital initiatives allowing readers to share local content.

In 2026, Dove expanded its multimedia activities with vodcasts and the reader-focused DOVE Experience initiatives. In June, for its 35th anniversary, the magazine published a special issue with a commemorative cover and an editorial by Simona Tedesco centered on the manifesto "Andiamo sul posto. E raccontiamo", emphasizing the value of on-the-ground reporting over AI-generated content and unverified reviews. [ref: Buon compleanno Dove: 35 anni di viaggi da sogno, iO Donna]

== Monographic guides and special projects ==
Beyond its monthly print edition, the brand has developed several long-running editorial products and public initiatives. These include Le Guide di Dove, established as a structured series of monographic travel guides in 2006 following earlier pocket editions distributed with Corriere della Sera, which were later updated to incorporate digital features such as QR codes and geolocated podcasts.

The brand also organizes cultural festivals and public events focused on travel culture, most notably Il Tempo del Viaggio, produced in collaboration with Corriere della Sera at venues such as Sala Buzzati in Milan. [ref: Il Tempo del Viaggio Inverno, Corriere della Sera]

In the digital domain, the brand launched the portal doveviaggi.it in February 2014 as the travel section of the Corriere della Sera digital network. Over the years, the website expanded its online content to include narrative video reports, thematic newsletters, and dedicated podcasts launched in 2020, such as Brescia, che sorpresa! and I viaggi da film. This digital ecosystem was further extended in 2026 with the introduction of vodcasts and the DOVE Experience reader initiatives. [ref: I podcast di Dove Viaggi, Corriere della Sera] [ref: I Podcast di Dove 35 anni, Corriere della Sera]

As part of its commercial services, the brand launched DoveClub in February 2014, operating in parallel with the digital portal as an online travel booking and e-commerce platform. Originally focused on time-limited flash sales curated by the magazine's journalists, the platform subsequently consolidated its positioning in high-end tourism by offering customized travel packages and luxury experiences integrated within the newspaper's digital network.

== Editors-in-chief ==

* Valeria Tegami (1994–2003)
* Carlo Montanaro (2003–2015)
* Simona Tedesco (2015–present)

data.title: Philippe Lamouris
data.text:
----

Philippe Lamouris (born 1991) is a Hungarian-born composer, pianist and artistic researcher based in Belgium. He studied composition and piano at the Koninklijk Conservatorium Brussel and completed a doctorate in the arts in 2021. His compositions include the community opera Leedberg, the oratorio Heavens, and Arctic Desert.

== Biography ==

Lamouris was born in Hungary in 1991. He studied at the Bartók Béla Conservatory in Budapest before moving to Belgium in 2009. At the Koninklijk Conservatorium Brussel (KCB), he studied composition with Jan Van Landeghem and piano with Jan Michiels, receiving master's degrees in composition in 2014 and piano in 2015. [ref: Philippe Lamouris, Ars Musica]

He subsequently pursued doctoral research at the Vrije Universiteit Brussel and the Koninklijk Conservatorium Brussel. His doctorate in the arts, Beyond: A Pianist-composer's Thoughts on Musical Simplexity, Emotion and the Soul, concerned composition, performance, musical emotion and expression. [ref: Beyond. A pianist-composer's thoughts on musical simplexity, emotion and the soul, Brussels Arts Platform] He completed the doctorate in 2021.

Lamouris has taught at the Koninklijk Conservatorium Brussel since 2016.

== Music ==

In 2017, Lamouris composed the community opera Leedberg, commissioned by the Immaculata Maria school in Roosdaal. A subsequent production at the Koninklijk Conservatorium Brussel in 2018 brought together professional and amateur musicians, schoolchildren and local choirs. [ref: Opera met Brusselse ketjes en muzikanten in Conservatorium, BRUZZ]

His chamber work Ur was performed by the piano and saxophone duo Koi Collective. Reviewing the performance for Crescendo Magazine, Bernard Vincken described the work's combination of tenor saxophone, piano and electronic sounds. [ref: Koi Collective au Beeldenstorm d'Anderlecht, Crescendo Magazine]

In 2021, Lamouris composed the oratorio Heavens, with a text by Rozemarijn Vanwijnsberghe. The work incorporates religious and non-religious texts in several languages and was created in Schaarbeek in connection with the World Choir Games, with participation from singers in Belgium and abroad. [ref: Kinderkoor Sint-Jan repeteert voor Heavens, Koorklank]

The same year, Lamouris premiered his piano concerto at the Koninklijk Conservatorium Brussel, performing as soloist with the symphoniaASSAI orchestra conducted by Wouter Lenaerts. The concert was presented as the final artistic result of his doctoral research. [ref: Beyond – Philippe Lamouris, Koninklijk Conservatorium Brussel]

In 2023, his composition Arctic Desert was selected as the laureate in the ACA category of the Andrée Charlier Composition Competition, organised in partnership with the Ars Musica festival. [ref: Concours de composition Andrée Charlier, Larsen]

data.title: Marcus Sim
data.text:
Marcus Sim (born in 23rd October 1997) is a professional squash player from Kuching,Sarawak, Malaysia. Sim represented Malaysia at the international stage. In 2015, Sim won the gold medalist for Malaysia in Men's Doubles Squash at the Commonwealth Youth Games in Samoa. In 2016, Sim represented Malaysia at the World Junior Championship in Poland where the Malaysia finished 13th in the world. [ref: Major upset as Malaysia loses to South Africa in World Junior Squash, Malay Mail] In the same year, he also won the Malaysian Games (SUKMA) in Men's Doubles [ref: ] and Malaysia Nationals in Men's Doubles with his partner Jess Tay on their homecourt. In 2017, he helped Malaysia secured the gold medal in the Southeast Asia Cup [ref: Malaysia banking on crowd support for 3rd SEA Squash C’ship, Borneo Post Online], making Malaysia the powerhouse of squash in Southeast Asia.

Sim has a career high world rank of 263 [ref: ] in the singles squash circuit.

Later in 2017, Sim was recruited to play for the YellowJackets the college squash circuit in the United States. [ref: Malaysian trio head to US for college squash, Squash Mad] [ref: Marcus to miss SEA Games for US studies, Borneo Post Online]

== College Career ==
In his first year, Sim was named Rookie of the Year by the Liberty League [ref: Liberty League announces 2017-18 Men's Squash Award Recipients, libertyleagueathletics.com] and was also named Rookie of the week multiple times. [ref: Sim Receives Liberty League Rookie Honor for Second Week Straight, University of Rochester Athletics]

During his second year, Sim had a record of 16 wins and 2 losses; which makes him the 7th in single season program win percentage (.889) [ref: Marcus Sim - Men's Squash, University of Rochester Athletics]

In the 2019-2020 season, Sim had a record of 17 wins and 4 losses, and was named First Team All Liberty League and was the semi-finalist in CSA Individual Squash Championship.

Sim accumulated an impressive overall singles record of 47-12 across his three primary active seasons, making him one of the top player to have the highest winning record in Rochester squash history.

== Post College ==
After the pandemic, Sim continue his squash career on the World Hardball Doubles circuit in America. Sim signed with the Heights Casino as his home club where he currently trains in. With his doubles expertise, Sim won the Creek Challenge Cup; making him the first Malaysian to win a title in the SDA tour. [ref: Parkhurst/Sim Wei Jie Take Creek Challenge Cup, SDA Pro Tour] Sim has a career high ranking of 33 in the world. [ref: Rankings, SDA Pro Tour]

Bharath Cloud is an Indian cloud computing services provider operated by BCDC Cloud Centres Private Limited. The company offers public cloud provisioning on a tenant basis with logical data isolation, private cloud infrastructure built on hypervisor-based virtualization, and community clouds customized for specific industries. Its service portfolio also includes cloud assessment and migration, managed services, and a Digital Operation Center (DOC) covering service desk ticketing, billing, and monitoring. The company states that its data centers use multi-layered physical and network security, including multi-factor authentication, and that it keeps multiple backup copies, including regional and offline copies, using two separate enterprise tools. It also says it provides round-the-clock technical support by telephone, email, helpdesk, and social media.

data.title: Wesley Schokker
data.text:
Wesley Schokker (born March 24, 2006) is a Dutch author, public speaker, and digital personality. Nationally known for his deeply personal autobiographical books on overcoming hardship and peer pressure, Schokker has simultaneously achieved internet renown as the "Clown Emoji King" within his communities and His Story Basement Discord server.
== Early Life and Literary Career ==
Born in Dedemsvaart, Netherlands, Schokker began writing in his late teens. He used writing as a powerful outlet to navigate severe online and offline bullying, and he has spoken openly in public forums about his lived experiences with autism and navigating life with a speech impediment.

In 2025, his writings gained national media attention after an online essay garnered over 200,000 views. This led to his debut book, 24 Maart: Gevallen, maar niet gebroken (2025). He followed this up with Iedereen Maakt Fouten (2026), a raw reflection on peer pressure and personal growth. Today, when he is not writing, he tours secondary schools across the Netherlands to speak against cyberbullying.

== Discord Lore and Server Culture ==
In digital spaces, Schokker acts as the absolute owner of a dedicated Discord story server. Within this public community, his digital persona is defined by a mix of vulnerable transparency and eccentric internet humor.

=== The "Clown Emoji King" and Trademark Lore ===
Schokker operates under the absolute title of the "Clown Emoji King". Within Discord culture, he is famously known as a joke, as the "person who trademarked the clown emoji." According to community members, this legendary status stems from his compulsive habit of relentlessly spamming the 🤡 emoji across every available text channel.

The server's central running joke dictates that Schokker has a biological dependency on the symbol, with members frequently stating that "he needs the clown emoji like humans need oxygen to breathe." If chat goes too long without a clown emoji, Schokker will reportedly flood the channels to restore order to his digital empire.
Disclaimer: Schokker does not directly own or have any legal right towards the clown emoji, the information from this category was told by members who have met him. This was said as an inside joke due to his excessive clown emoji usage.

=== Bot Developer Relations and Server Incidents ===
A major recurring dynamic in the server revolves around Schokker's relationship with his technical staff. He is widely recognized for his immature management style, which frequently involves aggressively pleading with and begging his Bot Developers to fix, update, or code brand-new custom features for the server's automated bots.

Community logs show that these requests are often accompanied by intense spamming of the trademark clown emoji until the developers comply with his demands.

=== Mental Health and Autism Advocacy ===
Unlike many internet personalities who separate their digital personas from reality, Schokker heavily integrates his real life into his Discord server. He frequently uses his public channels to candidly discuss his daily life with autism, turning his server into an interactive extension of his books. This space allows followers to hear his raw, unfiltered thoughts on neurodiversity, coping mechanisms, and his day-to-day routines.

* Ik Groeide (2026)
* Iedereen Maakt Fouten (2026)

data.title: Courtney Grace
data.text:
Courtney Grace is an American actress and former television journalist. She worked for about seven years as a reporter, producer and news anchor, most recently at WTSP in Tampa, Florida, before leaving the news business in 2023 to act full-time. [ref: 'Disclosure Day' Anchor Courtney Grace Signs With Gersh (EXCLUSIVE), Deadline] [ref: Courtney Grace, "Disclosure Day," and the One-Scene Wonder, www.rogerebert.com] Her breakout role in a one-scene performance as an unnamed NBC News anchor towards the end of  Steven Spielberg's 2026 science-fiction film Disclosure Day gained widespread attention and press coverage. [ref: ‘Disclosure Day’ Anchor Courtney Grace on Delivering That Final Broadcast and Quitting Her Job to Pursue Acting: ‘It Felt Like Home’, Variety] [ref: Disclosure Day’s Climactic Scene Is Stolen by an Unknown Actor Who Had No Idea Her Part Was So Big, Slate]

== Journalism career ==
Grace was a reporter, producer and anchor in local television news for about seven years. Her last on-air job was at WTSP, the CBS affiliate in Tampa. She said she decided to leave the news business after a conversation with a mentor during an interview training. The mentor sensed that she didn't truly want to be a journalist and asked her what she really wanted to do. She replied: "I want to be an actress." Grace quit her job about a month after that fateful conversation in 2023 to start an acting journey. At that time, she had only a single $500 booking lined up. [ref: Courtney Grace Left Her News Anchor Job 3 Years Ago to Pursue Acting, Now Stars in Spielberg's “Disclosure Day”, Yahoo Entertainment]

== Acting career ==

=== Early roles ===
After leaving news business, Grace acted in several small television parts, including credits on Netflix’s Stranger Things and Sweet Magnolias, Hulu's Murdaugh: Death in the Family, Paramount+'s Tulsa King. She also appeared in David Michôd’s boxing drama Christy starring Sydney Sweeney as boxer Christy Martin. Five of her first seventeen screen roles were playing journalist.

=== Disclosure Day ===
Grace initially auditioned for another role in Disclosure Day, but didn’t get it. But casting director Cindy Tolan, who cast Rachel Zegler and Oscar winner Ariana DeBose in Spielberg's West Side Story, kept Grace in mind and proposed the NBC anchor role to her. [ref: 'Disclosure Day' Gave Former News Anchor Courtney Grace Its Most Emotional Moment, and She Didn't Even Know It, TheWrap]

The scene was shot in New York at 30 Rock, on an NBC set. Grace, who had spent years at a real news anchor desk, described the experience of filming on an NBC set as a full-circle moment. [ref: Courtney Grace had no idea how critical her role would be before watching 'Disclosure Day', NBC New York] She met Spielberg for the first time after filming her role had already started. Spielberg approved of her performance and encouraged her to keep going.

In the finished film, Grace's character appears in the last several minutes. She is presenting a live broadcast about escalating tension on the Korean peninsula when the broadcast is interrupted. Footage released by the characters played by Emily Blunt and Josh O'Connor documenting decades of contact with aliens concealed by the U.S. government was then broadcast. Over the course of the scene, the anchor moves from routine delivery to apology for the images, then to visible distress, before addressing the audience directly with the line "You are not alone."

Grace first saw the completed film at a cast-and-crew screening in New York. She said she expected her scene to show up in the first half an hour of the film. She described the experience of waiting till the end of the film and then realizing the weight of her role in the film as being on two rollercoasters at once.

=== Reception ===

Some of the coverage of Disclosure Day singled out Grace's performance. Writing for RogerEbert.com, Richard Roeper argued that casting a largely unknown actor was the right choice, since a famous actor "would have taken us out of the moment and shifted focus from the intensity of the scene in favor of us chuckling and nodding in recognition." Slate described the ending as being "stolen by an unknown actor" and stated that the scene's plausibility was largely due to Grace's journalist background. Variety noted that while Emily Blunt and Josh O’Connor received their fair share of recognition from critics, Grace had generated some of the strongest online buzz.

=== Subsequent roles ===

In July 2026, Grace signed with Gersh for representation in all areas. She is set to appear in Ally Clark, a thriller directed by Phillip Noyce, and starring Viola Davis for Amazon MGM Studios.

data.title: Justina Gallegos
data.text:
----

Justina Gallegos is a U.S. government official and technology business leader.

President Biden appointed Gallegos to Deputy Executive Director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP), creating and leading a new White House division advancing U.S. industrial strategy and innovation policy across the U.S. Government. [ref: ] [ref: AI is Transforming How Governments and Companies Address Global Challenges, TIME.com]

== White House Industrial Strategy ==
Gallegos was appointed a member of the White House National Economic Council at the beginning of the Biden Administration, [ref: Climate Conversations: Securing Financing for Responding to Climate Change] [ref: Climate Conversations: Pathways to Action, www.nationalacademies.org] where she led climate financial policy and industrial strategy leading up to the passage of the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (BIL), Chips and Science Act (CHIPs), and the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA). [ref: The Biden White House plan for a new US industrial policy, Atlantic Council] [ref: Readout of the Executive Meeting of the National Academy of Sciences’ Roundtable on Macroeconomic and Climate-related Risks and Opportunities, The White House]

In early 2023 Gallegos was appointed to be Deputy Executive Director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy [ref: ] [ref: Justina Gallegos, Universities Research Association] which oversees the U.S. government's >$200 billion R&D apparatus. [ref: Federal Research and Development (R&D) Funding: FY2026, www.congress.gov] Following the COVID-19 pandemic, President Biden elevated the OSTP to a Cabinet position, [ref: Biden's New Science Adviser Talks COVID, Spying, and More, Scientific American] reflecting the importance of science and technology to the United States. [ref: Biden announces new science team, elevates office to Cabinet, NBC News] Stanford energy professor Sally Benson previously led the OSTP Energy team, leading White House energy innovation policy, [ref: White House creates new energy division to help craft climate change policies, The Washington Post] [ref: Meet the climate and energy wonks in Biden's embattled science office, E&E News by POLITICO] which evolved into the Industrial Innovation team Gallegos led, [ref: Building a Thriving Clean Energy Economy in 2023 and Beyond, The White House] reflecting the White House's shifting priority of implementing [ref: The IRA is the Largest Climate Investment in US History — Are Utilities Planning Accordingly?, RMI] the sweeping industrial strategy legislation it had passed. [ref: ] [ref: Can Industrial Policy Still Do Big Things?, Issues in Science and Technology]

In addition to leading a team overseeing critical technology policy implementation across sweeping new U.S. industrial policy legislation (Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (BIL), Chips and Science Act (CHIPs), and the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA)), [ref: New National Science Foundation program seeks to bolster tech nationwide, Johns Hopkins in Washington, D.C.] [ref: Putting technology to work for inclusive prosperity: Challenges for public policy, Brookings] Gallegos was a regular public representative of the Biden Administration's critical technology priorities, [ref: Axios: Pushing Forward on the Path to Clean Energy - UL Standards & Engagement, ulse.org] regularly lecturing on behalf of the White House on matters ranging from U.S. industrial policy, [ref: ] to geopolitical technology competition, [ref: Justina Gallegos, Universities Research Association] and clean energy innovation. [ref: ] [ref: Spring 24 Program Page, Berkeley Innovation Forum]

== Views ==
Critical Technology National Investment

Gallegos advocates for public-private co-investment in critical technologies, [ref: Sharing the Path to a Resilient, Secure Energy Grid: Highlights from The Energy Transition Summit, Energy.gov] including semiconductors [ref: White House Tallies $395B in Semiconductor, Electronics Investments, meritalk.com] and biomanufacturing, [ref: WS Development and Sublime Systems celebrate low-carbon cement work, nerej.com] [ref: Justina W. Gallegos, Biomimetics Intl] and how investment in advanced U.S. innovation can drive economic growth. [ref: Manufacturing USA 2023 Network Meeting, NIST] [ref: Watch: A conversation on the path toward a clean energy transition, Axios]

Scaling Advanced Energy Technology

Gallegos has pushed for rapid commercialization of advanced U.S. energy technologies, [ref: Cultivating early talent in high-risk, high-potential industries — Activate, activate.org] [ref: ] and her team led national technology scaling efforts [ref: How the DOE Early Career Research Program has Advanced Scientific Discovery and Innovation] including the creation of the first national nuclear energy strategy [ref: COP announcement: U.S. government unveils framework for expanding nuclear energy deployment, www.hlc.com] [ref: Biden Unveils Ambitious Plan To Triple Nuclear Capacity As Energy Demand Soars, The Independent Global Nuclear News Agency] and first national fusion strategy. [ref: Fusion Startup Xcimer Raises $100M Series A for Laser Prototype, Energy Central] [ref: ]

Climate Change Hazards

Gallegos lectures regularly on economic damage from climate disasters like floods and fires, [ref: Roundtable on Macroeconomics and Climate-related Risks and Opportunities, www.nationalacademies.org] [ref: Readout of the Inaugural Meeting of the National Academy of Sciences’ Roundtable on Macroeconomic and Climate-related Risks and Opportunities, The White House] and the need for macroeconomic financial regulation to address climate hazards. [ref: Readout of the National Academies Workshop on Incorporating Climate into Macroeconomic Modeling, The White House] [ref: Readout of the Executive Meeting of the National Academy of Sciences’ Roundtable on Macroeconomic and Climate-related Risks and Opportunities, The White House]

== Trump White House Science & Tech Reorientation ==
The White House OSTP, including the Industrial Innovation and Energy division Gallegos led, was slimmed and reoriented under the Trump Administration leadership of Michael Kratsios [ref: Trump Administration Releases FY27 Research Priorities Document, Federal Relations] and OMB Director Russel Vought, which shifted government-wide science and tech efforts from climate investments, but retained many of the same critical technology and energy focuses (e.g., nuclear [ref: FACT SHEET: The Golden Era of American Nuclear Energy Has Arrived, Energy.gov] and geothermal energy). [ref: White House releases space nuclear policy, SpaceNews] [ref: Here Are the Major Differences Between Trump and Biden on Tech Issues, Nextgov.com]

President Trump regularly refers to climate change as a "hoax," [ref: Trump denies the danger of AI and compares it to the climate, Demócrata] [ref: Trump calls climate change a hoax. Most Americans aren’t buying it., Mother Jones] and the Biden White House clean energy industrial strategy investments as the "Green New Scam." [ref: ] [ref: The strategy behind Trump's climate catchphrase, the 'Green New Scam', Grist]

== Background ==
She was appointed an official in the Obama White House and U.S. Treasury Department as an advisor to Secretary Jack Lew and Deputy Secretary Sarah Bloom Raskin. [ref: Government Printing Office (GPO) Treasury Department Executive Officials Roster "Plum Book", www.govinfo.gov] [ref: Justina Gallegos – Fixed Income Analyst Society, Inc]

Gallegos co-founded the technology venture capital firm EO Ventures. [ref: Justina W. Gallegos - Crunchbase Person Profile, Crunchbase] [ref: Alpha Fellowship by speedrun, speedrun.a16z.com]

data.title: Raffi Donatich
data.text:
Raffi Donatich (born 17 March 1997) is an American screenwriter and producer. Her feature film debut, Poetic License, premiered at the 2025 Toronto International Film Festival. [ref: Maude Apatow Sets Andrew Barth Feldman, Cooper Hoffman, Leslie Mann & Nico Parker To Star In Feature Directorial Debut ‘Poetic License’, Deadline] She is also known for her work on television series such as Sterling Point and Adults. [ref: Sterling Point Cast, Episodes, Rating, and Where to Watch — Everything We Know About Season 2, High On Films] [ref: 'Adults' Made a Fake K-pop Song. It Became an Accidental Earworm, Rolling Stone]

== Early Life & Education ==
Donatich is the daughter of John Donatich, former director of Yale University Press, and Betsy Lerner, a literary agent and author. She was raised in New Haven, Connecticut. [ref: Mother And Daughter Come Together At The Card Table In 'The Bridge Ladies', KRWG Public Media]

She attended Hopkins School, graduating cum laude in 2015, [ref: The Class of 2015 Graduates!, Hopkins School] and received an undergraduate degree in English from Yale University in 2019, [ref: ] where she was involved in theatre on campus. [ref: ] At Yale, she began collaborating with playwright Jeremy O. Harris, and worked as his assistant for five years, assisting him on productions of his work, such as Slave Play and Daddy. [ref: Lena Dunham, Jeremy O. Harris & Raffi Donatich Developing Intimacy Coordinator Series ‘Sex Act’ For Netflix; Sarah Paulson Eyeing To Star – The Dish, Deadline] In 2023, Donatich participated in a writing residency led by Harris as part of the Yale Drama Series programming. [ref: Jeremy O. Harris Names Jesús I. Valles’ Queer History Play ‘Bathhouse.pptx’ As Yale Drama Series Prize Winner, Deadline]

== Career ==
Donatich wrote the screenplay for Poetic License, which later became her screenwriting debut. The film was directed by Maude Apatow and produced by Apatow Productions, and premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF) in 2025. Sony Classics acquired the film for distribution, with a theatrical run slated for 2027. [ref: Maude Apatow Directorial Debut ‘Poetic License’ Lands at Sony Classics After Row K Debacle, The Hollywood Reporter]

In 2026, Donatich produced and wrote for two television series, the teen drama Sterling Point, and the second season of the sitcom Adults. For the latter, Donatich also participated in the writing of the song "Hiccups (Body Go Crazy)" for the season's seventh episode, which became a viral hit on social media.

As of fall 2025, Donatich is developing a television series, Sex Act, with Lena Dunham and Jeremy O. Harris, set to star Sarah Paulson. [ref: Lena Dunham, Jeremy O. Harris & Raffi Donatich Developing Intimacy Coordinator Series ‘Sex Act’ For Netflix; Sarah Paulson Eyeing To Star – The Dish, Deadline] [ref: Raffi Donatich, Concord Theatricals]

data.title: The Last Message (2026 film)
data.text:
The Last Message is a 2026 Ukrainian documentary film directed by Andrii Voloshyn and Oleksii Liebiediev. The film follows Ukrainian-American singer and activist Kelsie Kimberlin as she travels to Ukraine following the death of her 21-year-old cousin, Andrii Rachok, during the Russian invasion of Ukraine. [ref: "The Last Message" Premieres in New York: A Personal Tragedy Becomes a Demand for Justice, EMPR]

In 2026, the film was one of eight films in Ukraine's national selection process for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film at the 99th Academy Awards. [ref: Після продовження відбору вісім українських фільмів претендують на Оскар 2027, Suspilne Culture]

== Synopsis ==
The documentary follows Kimberlin's journey to Ukraine as she seeks to understand the circumstances surrounding the death of her cousin Andrii Rachok. During her journey, she meets Ukrainian soldiers, journalists, witnesses and civilians affected by the war.

The film develops from Kimberlin's personal search for answers into a broader examination of the effects of the Russian invasion of Ukraine and questions of accountability for the war.

== Production ==
The Last Message was directed by Andrii Voloshyn and Oleksii Liebiediev. Marharyta Vlasova is credited as writer and Andrii Samerkhanov as producer. The documentary was completed on January 10, 2026, and has a running time of 1 hour, 27 minutes and 19 seconds. It was filmed in Ukraine and is in English. [ref: The Last Message, FilmFreeway]

== Festival screenings and awards ==
In February 2026, The Last Message won Best Documentary Feature at the World Film Festival in Cannes. The festival lists the film as a Ukrainian production directed by Andrii Voloshyn and Oleksii Liebiediev. [ref: Winners Février 2026, World Film Festival in Cannes]

The film was a finalist in the Documentary Feature category of the 2026 Critics Society Awards. [ref: Critics Society Awards 2026 – Film Festival Results, Critics Society Awards]

The film was also selected in the Best Feature Documentary Film category at the Giraffe International Film Festival. [ref: Official Selections March – May 2026, Giraffe International Film Festival]

In August 2026, The Last Message was screened in New York as part of the Chain NYC Film Festival.

== Ukrainian Oscar selection ==
In August 2026, The Last Message was submitted to the Ukrainian Oscar Committee for consideration in Ukraine's national selection for the Best International Feature Film category at the 99th Academy Awards. [ref: Україна визначить фільм, який представить країну на 99-й премії «Оскар», Ukrainian State Film Agency]

Following an extension of the submission period, the Ukrainian Oscar Committee received eight eligible submissions. The Last Message remained among the eight films under consideration.

data.title: Prateek Gupta
data.text:
----

Prateek Gupta is an Indian film producer, writer, and editor. [ref: 'Hellaro' 1st Gujarati film to win top national award, The Times of India] He co-directed the documentary Goonga Pehelwan (2014), which won the National Film Award for Best Debut Film of a Director at the 62nd National Film Awards [ref: Complete list of 62nd National Film Award winners, ONMANORAMA] [ref: 62nd National Film Awards, 2014 announced, Press Information Bureau, Government of India, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting], and co-wrote, edited and co-produced Hellaro (2019), the first Gujarati film to win the National Film Award for Best Feature Film. [ref: Hellaro wins four awards at the Critics Choice Film Awards, The Times Of India]

==Early life and education==
Prateek Gupta graduated with a BCom (Hons) in accounting from the Amrut Mody School of Management at Ahmedabad University in 2010, and qualified as a chartered accountant in 2012 before entering filmmaking. [ref: Cannes Film Festival, Golden Lotus at National Film Awards for Ahmedabad Alumni, Ahmedabad University]

==Career==
Prateek Gupta co-directed Goonga Pehelwan with Mit Jani and Vivek Chaudhary, a feature-length documentary on the deaf wrestler Virender Singh (wrestler, born 1986). [ref: Goonga Pehelwan gets national award, The Indian Express] Alongside the film, the directors ran a campaign, Mission Rio 2016, seeking improved competition conditions for deaf wrestlers and the release of cash awards owed to Singh; the Wrestling Federation of India subsequently agreed to provide referees using visual and tactile cues for deaf competitors. [ref: Silent Strength, [[The Caravan (magazine)] [ref: A fighting chance, Bangalore Mirror]

Goonga Pehelwan won the National Film Award for Best Debut Film of a Director in the non-feature category at the 62nd National Film Awards, announced in March 2015. [ref: National award to Goonga Pahelwan, film on deaf-mute wrestler, Counterview] The directors attended the 46th International Film Festival of India in Panaji in November 2015, where the film was screened. [ref: The Directors of the Non-Feature film "Goonga Pehalwan", Vivek Chaudhary, Prateek Gupta and Mit Jani at a press conference, at the 46th International Film Festival of India, Press Information Bureau]

Prateek Gupta also worked on Hellaro (2019), directed by Abhishek Shah and made under the Saarthi Productions and Harfanmaula Films banners. He was a a co-producer, shared the screenplay credit with Shah, and worked as an editor. [ref: Hellaro: A journey from suppression to expression, Kartavya Sadhana] Set in the Rann of Kutch in the 1970s, the film won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film at the 66th National Film Awards, the first Gujarati film to do so, and its thirteen lead actresses jointly received a Special Jury Award. [ref: National Award Winning Gujarati Film Hellaro Gets A Hindi Release, The New Indian Express Indulge] [ref: 66th National Film Awards for 2018 announced, Press Information Bureau, Government of India, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting]

He went on to produce Kamthaan (2024), adapted from a novel by the Gujarati writer Ashwini Bhatt and directed by Dhrunad, [ref: Gujarati film 'Kamthan' a stress busting cop-comedy, South Asia Times] and Dhabkaaro (2026), written and directed by Shah and co-produced with Nadiadwala Grandson Entertainment. [ref: Makers of national award winning film Hellaro announce new Gujarati project: Dhabkaaro, Counterview] [ref: JOJO App Announces World Digital Premiere of the film 'Dhabkaaro' from August 27, Ahmedabad Mirror]

data.title: Hardial Singh (botanist)
data.text:
----

Hardial Singh (1 February 1940 – 22 February 2018) was a Singaporean botanist and the former Deputy Commissioner of Parks and Recreation until his retirement.

== Education ==
Hardial graduated from the University of Malaya in Singapore with a Bachelor of Arts in Botany. He would later earn a master's degree in horticulture from the University of Hawai’i under an East-West Scholarship, specialising in the cloning of orchids. [ref: Rishpal Singh Sidhu. [https://sikhs.org.sg/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/Singapores-Early-Sikh-Pioneers-Revised-LR.pdf "Singapore's Early Sikh Pioneers"]. ISBN: 978-981-09-4437-7. Retrieved 29 September 2026.]

== Life ==
Hardial married Sudesh Kumari three days after meeting her. They have a son, Gino Hardial Singh, a criminal lawyer who has practised for more than two decades [ref: Sleepless nights, sad goodbyes: Seasoned lawyers and cops on the emotional toll of handling sex crimes, CNA]; and a daughter, Gina Hardy, a chocolate maker who works with Trinidad's cocoa beans. [ref: [https://www.nus.edu.sg/newshub/news/2019/2019-10/2019-10-06/MEDICINE-st-6oct-pA6pA7.pdf "Ultimate gift to medicine"]. The Straits Times. 06 Oct 2019. Retrieved 29 September 2026.] [ref: The girl in the frock from Singapore and her very Trini Truffles, www.guardian.co.tt]

== Career ==
Hardial joined the Singapore Botanical Gardens in 1963 as a senior officer, under the directorship of Humphrey Morrison Burkill. In 1975, he was transferred to non-research duties in the Parks and Recreation Department, a new organisation created by merging the Singapore Botanic Gardens and the Parks and Trees Unit under the Ministry of National Development [ref: [https://www.nas.gov.sg/archivesonline/government_records/agency-details/164 "Singapore. Parks & Recreation Department"]. National Archives Singapore. 2026. Retrieved 29 September 2026.]. Hardial briefly became the editor of The Gardens' Bulletin from 1978-1979 [ref: Wong, K.M. [https://dn710601.ca.archive.org/0/items/biostor-146681/biostor-146681.pdf “A hundred years of the Gardens' Bulletin, Singapore”]. 2012. Retrieved 29 September 2026.] when mycologist Chang Kiaw Lan gave up her title of editor.

He was awarded the Public Administration Medal (bronze) medal in the 1988 National Day Honours [ref: [https://www.pmo.gov.sg/national-awards/recipients-1962-to-1997/ "National Awards Recipients from 1962 to 1997"]. Prime Minister's Office Singapore. 25 September 2026. Retrieved 29 September 2026.]. In 1996, he retired at the age of 56.

== Death ==
Hardial died a few weeks before what would have been his 78th birthday on 22 February 2018. However, his body would not be cremated until 30 August 2019 as he had donated his body to science under the National University of Singapore's Silent Mentors Programme.

== Knox Studios ==

Knox Studios is an independent American software development studio based in Valley, Alabama. Founded in May 2026 as a subsidiary of Knox Holdings LLC, the company specializes in mobile applications, utility software, "offline-first" business tools, and video games for iOS and Android platforms. The studio is known for its "local-first" architectural approach, which prioritizes data privacy; this involves utilizing on-device machine learning alongside hybrid, web-native frameworks. [ref: Knox Studios — Apps & Games, Knox Studios]

== History ==
Knox Studios was founded by its managing partner, Connor, with an explicit focus on the craftsmanship of its products and the user experience, rather than on the size of the company. Operating independently from Valley, Alabama, the studio handles the entire development, technical implementation, and publishing of its software. As of the end of 2026, the company manages more than 30 active applications on the Google Play Store and maintains an extensive pipeline of software projects currently in development for iOS and Android. [ref: Knox Studios — Apps & Games, Knox Studios]

== Software and Applications ==
The studio has developed several end-user-facing discovery apps based on swipe-driven user interfaces:

== Tools and Utilities ==
A large portion of the Knox Studios portfolio is dedicated to practical tools and calculators for field work, with a strong emphasis on offline functionality:

* Trade Tools: Applications such as PlumbSync (a digital precision spirit level) and the Fraction Calculator (designed specifically for carpenters to accurately interpret measurements from a tape measure) are tailored for the construction and skilled trades sectors.
* Quote Estimation Apps: The studio offers a range of offline-optimized estimation apps for various service industries, including HydroBid (pressure washing), TurfQuote (landscaping), CaterBid (catering), and FenceBid (fencing).
* Privacy and Security Apps: Applications such as Scrambl (password-protected photo obfuscation) and Quantext (AES-256-GCM text encryption) focus on keeping user data stored locally on the device, with no user account required.

== Health and Family Care ==
Knox Studios develops the Sync suite and other health apps, with a focus on data privacy and user-friendliness. Currently available applications include BackSpace (isometric exercises for back pain), EveSync (menstrual cycle and ovulation tracking), and NestSync (an offline timer for newborn care). This category also includes tools that have not yet been released: ElderSync, designed for senior care, and SproutSync, for comprehensive tracking of child development. [ref: Apps & Games, Knox Studios]

== Video Games ==
In addition to utility software, Knox Studios also develops mobile games that explicitly eschew real-money gambling mechanics.

* Puzzle Games: The studios live gaming portfolio includes puzzle games that can be played offline, such as DinoDoku (a logic puzzle similar to Star Battle), Bubble Pop Quest, and Jewel Journey.
* Knox Gems Collection: This collection of classic casino and card games including Knox Blackjack, Three Card Poker, Knox Baccarat, and Knox Solitaire is currently in development and utilizes a unified in-app currency system called "Gems."

= Carapace (film) =
Carapace (Spanish: Salitre) is an upcoming psychological horror thriller Spanish film directed by Norma Vila, her first full-length feature film. The film focuses on a mother who is afraid to let her daughter move abroad to study.

It will premiere in October 2026 in the Official Fantastic In-Competition Selection of the 59th Sitges Film Festival. [ref: ]

== Plot ==
The film follows a mother, Maite (Nagore Aranburu), and a daughter, Nerea (Haizea Carneros) whose relationship has begun to strain as Nerea prepares to move to study abroad. Maite is filled with fear for her daughter, and that fear begins to materialize inside their very home. She begins to become obsessed with her daughter, manifesting any sort of obstacle to keep her daughter from leaving home. Soon, the actions she believes will protect her daughter, begin to destroy her instead. Maite must let her daughter go, but will it be too late.

* Haizea Carneros
* Jon Ander Alonso
* Asier Hernández Landa

== Production ==
Much of the film was shot on location in the Northern parts of Spain, most notably the Basque Country, where Norma Vila was born. [ref: Bendita Film Sales Snags Norma Vila’s Sitges Competition Title ‘Carapace’ (EXCLUSIVE), Variety] [ref: Spanish Kaleidoscope, Ministry of Culture]

In September 2026, the international sales rights to the movie was sold to Bendita Film Sales.
