data.title: Lloyd Czaplewski
data.text:
Lloyd Czaplewski is a British scientist working in antibacterial drug discovery and development. He was an author of a 2008 study in Science describing inhibitors of the bacterial cell-division protein FtsZ, and lead author of a 2016 review in The Lancet Infectious Diseases assessing non-traditional approaches to treating bacterial infection.

== Education ==
Czaplewski received a first-class B.Sc. in biological sciences from the University of East Anglia and a Ph.D. in molecular genetics from the University of Glasgow, where his research concerned Streptomyces molecular genetics. [ref: Streptomyces molecular genetics thesis record, University of Glasgow] He subsequently held a postdoctoral position at the University of Leeds studying gene regulation in Bacillus subtilis. [ref: Biography for Lloyd Czaplewski, World Health Organization]

== Career ==
Czaplewski has held research and development roles at British Biotech, Prolysis, Biota Europe and Persica Pharmaceuticals. He was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry. [ref: Lloyd Czaplewski, CF AMR Syndicate] [ref: Lloyd Czaplewski, REVIVE, Global Antibiotic Research and Development Partnership]

== Antibacterial drug discovery ==
Czaplewski was one of the authors of a 2008 study in Science describing a class of synthetic antibacterials, exemplified by the compound PC190723, that inhibit FtsZ and prevent bacterial cell division. The compounds showed bactericidal activity against staphylococci, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. [ref: An inhibitor of FtsZ with potent and selective anti-staphylococcal activity, [[Science (journal)] The work arose from antibacterial research at Prolysis, [ref: New approaches to overcoming antimicrobial resistance, The Pharmaceutical Journal] which subsequently received funding for antibacterial discovery research through the Wellcome Trust's Seeding Drug Discovery initiative. [ref: Wellcome Trust issues first grants to encourage drug discovery, Pharmafile]

== Antimicrobial resistance research and policy ==
From around 2010 Czaplewski worked on initiatives concerning antimicrobial resistance. He took part in activities associated with the British Society for Antimicrobial Chemotherapy's "The Urgent Need" programme, which examined challenges in antibacterial research and development. [ref: Antibiotic resistance: what, why, where, when and how?, British Medical Bulletin] He chaired a review commissioned by the UK Department of Health and the Wellcome Trust examining alternatives to conventional antibiotics, including bacteriophages, antimicrobial peptides and host-directed approaches. The review was published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2016 as "Alternatives to antibiotics—a pipeline portfolio review", with Czaplewski as lead author. [ref: Alternatives to antibiotics—a pipeline portfolio review, The Lancet Infectious Diseases] Its findings informed the alternatives-to-antibiotics section of the Review on Antimicrobial Resistance chaired by Jim O'Neill; Czaplewski is listed among the report's acknowledged contributors.< [ref: Tackling Drug-Resistant Infections Globally: Final Report and Recommendations, Review on Antimicrobial Resistance)] He was lead author of a study of global public and philanthropic investment in antibacterial therapeutic research from 2017 to 2023, published in The Lancet Microbe in 2026. The analysis, based on data from the Global AMR R&D Hub, found that 130 funders had invested US$2.51 billion over the period, that funding was concentrated among a small number of sources, and that it had declined since 2020. [ref: An overview of global public and philanthropic investments into antibacterial therapeutics (2017–23), The Lancet Microbe]

== Later translational research ==
Czaplewski is chief scientific officer of Persica Pharmaceuticals, which developed PP353, an intradiscal antibiotic therapy for chronic low back pain associated with Modic change type 1. A phase 1b randomised, sham-controlled trial reported in eClinicalMedicine in 2026 found that two intradiscal administrations of PP353 were well tolerated and reduced pain and disability relative to the sham procedure at twelve months. [ref: Intradiscal linezolid (PP353) treatment for chronic low back pain associated with Modic change type 1: an international, first-in-human, randomised, sham procedure-controlled, double-blind, phase 1b clinical trial, eClinicalMedicine] [ref: New drug for lower back pain could be ‘a gamechanger’, The Guardian] [ref: Therapeutic approach could treat chronic low back pain, Drug Discovery World (DDW)].

== Advisory roles ==
Czaplewski has served on advisory bodies concerned with antimicrobial resistance research and funding, including the World Health Organization's Antibiotic Advisory Group and advisory panels for CARB-X [ref: Advisory Board, Carb-X] and the Global Antibiotic Research and Development Partnership. He served on the scientific selection board of the Novo REPAIR Impact Fund and later chaired it, and has chaired an advisory group of the Pathways to Antimicrobial Clinical Efficacy (PACE) programme. [ref: PACE Scientific Projects Advisory Group, PACE] Since 2021 he has been a non-executive director of Curza. [ref: Curza leadership and board information, Curza]

== Research impact ==
As of October 2026, Czaplewski's publications had received over 6,000 citations with an h-index of 32, according to Google Scholar. [ref: Lloyd Czaplewski, Google Scholar]

== Selected publications ==

* Haydon DJ, Stokes NR, Ure R, et al. [https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1159961 An inhibitor of FtsZ with potent and selective anti-staphylococcal activity]. Science. 2008;321(5896):1673–1675.
* Czaplewski L, Bax R, Clokie M, et al. Alternatives to antibiotics—a pipeline portfolio review. The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 2016;16(2):239–251.
* Jackson N, Czaplewski L, Piddock LJV. Discovery and development of new antibacterial drugs: learning from experience? Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy. 2018;73(6):1452–1459.
* Czaplewski L, Lamichhane U, Sudbrak R, et al. An overview of global public and philanthropic investments into antibacterial therapeutics (2017–23). The Lancet Microbe. 2026;7(3):101288.

data.title: Kawanthissa Tusker
data.text:
Kawanthissa (also spelled Kavanthissa or Kavantissa) was a wild Sri Lankan elephant associated with the Galgamuwa area of Sri Lanka's North Western Province. He was known for his prominent tusks and attracted public attention.

== Background ==

Kawanthissa was known in the Galgamuwa area and received attention from residents and wildlife enthusiasts. News reports described public concern about his welfare following an injury in 2026. [ref: Outrage and calls for investigation following tragic death of iconic Kawanthissa, The Sunday Times]

== Injury and death ==

In September 2026, Kawanthissa was reportedly found with an injury to his right foreleg in the Galgamuwa area. Wildlife officials and veterinarians treated the injury and monitored his condition. [ref: Ailing tusker Kavanthissa in critical condition, public urged to stay away, Daily Mirror]

Subsequent reports described a deterioration in the elephant's condition, including reduced food intake and diarrhoea, while veterinary treatment continued. [ref: Ailing tusker Kavanthissa in critical condition, public urged to stay away, Daily Mirror]

Kawanthissa died in October 2026 while receiving veterinary care. His death prompted public concern and calls for an investigation into the circumstances surrounding his treatment. [ref: Outrage and calls for investigation following tragic death of iconic Kawanthissa, The Sunday Times]

== Investigation ==

Following Kawanthissa's death, Sri Lanka's Environment Ministry announced an independent investigation into the circumstances of his treatment and whether any errors or deliberate wrongdoing had occurred. [ref: Independent probe into tusker Kawanthissa's death, Daily Mirror]

On 19 October 2026, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake appointed an expert committee to investigate the elephant's death, examine its possible causes, and determine whether lapses or negligence had occurred during treatment. The committee was also tasked with making recommendations concerning wild elephant welfare and conservation. [ref: President appoints committee to probe Kavanthissa's death, Daily Mirror]

The committee was expected to submit its findings and recommendations to the President within 30 days. The appointment of the committee did not establish the cause of death or prove that negligence had occurred. [ref: President appoints committee to probe Kavanthissa's death, Daily Mirror]

data.title: SCenTRLE
data.text:
== Student-Centered, Technology-Rich Learning Environments (SCenTRLE)==
Student-Centered, Technology-Rich Learning Environments (SCenTRLE) is an instructional design model developed by educational researcher Atsusi Hirumi. Hirumi developed the model in the 1990s and formally published it in 2002. Hirumi's model uses eight instructional events to facilitate student-centred learning grounded in constructivist principles. The model largely focuses on active participation, knowledge construction and learner independence, and uses technology to support the learning process. [ref: Student-Centered, Technology-Rich Learning Environments (SCenTRLE): Operationalizing Constructivist Approaches to Teaching and Learning, Journal of Technology and Teacher Education]

== Theoretical background ==

The SCenTRLE model is rooted in constructivist learning theory, which depicts learners as active participants in the expansion of knowledge. Hirumi identified four foundations for the model: societal, psychological, epistemological and pedagogical. These four principles are also addressed in other research on technology-enhanced student-centred learning environments.. [ref: The Foundations and Assumptions of Technology-Enhanced Student-Centered Learning Environments, Instructional Science]

Hirumi posits that the societal foundation is based on the growing role of information and technology in education. He argued that increased access to information requires learners to develop various competences other than subject knowledge such as problem-solving skills, communication and independent learning.

Secondly, the psychological foundation draws on constructivist perspectives of Jean Piaget, Jerome Bruner and Lev Vygotsky. It explains how learners acquire knowledge through experience, cognitive development and social interaction.

Thirdly, the epistemological foundation is rooted in pragmatism. This perspective claims that individuals construct knowledge through experience, prior understanding and interaction with others while recognising an external reality.

Finally, the pedagogical foundation integrates student-centred learning, generative learning, situated cognition, problem-based learning and performance assessment. Together, they foster active participation, authentic learning and the practical application of knowledge.

In SCenTRLE, learners contribute to decisions about their learning, while instructors provide continuous guidance and feedback.

== The eight instructional events ==

The SCenTRLE model comprises eight instructional events that guide student-centred learning. The events provide a framework that learners use to establish objectives, select learning strategies and assess their progress. The events are presented sequentially but learners may revisit earlier activities as their understanding develops. [ref: Vicarious Interactions and Self-Directed Learning of Students by Course Delivery Strategy, Texas A&M University]

# Set Learning Challenge:The instructor sets a learning challenge that identifies what students should be able to accomplish and provides the overall direction.
# Negotiate Learning Goals and Objectives: Learners collaborate with the instructor to determine the knowledge and skills needed to complete the challenge. This may include assessing prior knowledge, identifying areas for improvement and creating individual learning objectives.
# Negotiate Learning Strategies: Students identify the activities and resources they will use to achieve their learning objectives while instructors provide guidance and encourages learners to determine which activities best address their needs.
# Construct Knowledge: Learners then apply their strategies, individually or collaboratively, to develop knowledge and skills. The instructor monitors progress and provides support when needed.
# Negotiate Performance Criteria: Learners and instructors establish criteria for assessing whether the learning objectives have been met. Assessment rubrics may be developed to help learners review the quality of their work.
# Conduct Self, Peer and Expert Assessments: Students evaluate their work based on the agreed rubrics and receive feedback from peers and individuals with relevant expertise.
# Monitor Performance and Provide Feedback: Monitoring and feedback occur throughout the learning process. Instructors review students' work, respond to questions, provide feedback on their progress while students monitor their own progress.
# Communicate Results: The final event involves presenting the outcomes of learning. Students may use portfolios, presentations or other samples to demonstrate their achievements.

The eight events promote learner independence while preserving the instructor's role as a facilitator.

== Applications and case studies ==

=== Initial implementation in higher education ===

Hirumi's first field test of SCenTRLE was a 15-week undergraduate course on the educational applications of computer technology. The course included 30 students with different levels of computer experience: seven novice users, 17 apprentices and six more proficient users. The model was introduced to address these differences and allow students to pursue learning objectives aligned with their existing knowledge and interests.

Students discussed their learning goals and strategies with the instructor and developed portfolios to demonstrate their progress. The portfolios included rubrics, work samples and reflections on learning. Students were evaluated on their progress across five course standards and were allowed to revise their work in response to feedback.

Of the 28 students who finished the course, 12 received an A, 13 received a B, two received a C and one received an F. Hirumi stated that most students improved their computer-related skills. However, the findings were drawn from a single course, and Hirumi believed that they were insufficient to establish the model's effectiveness in other educational settings.

=== Application in Curriculum Design ===
Tynan investigated the use of SCenTRLE in designing an online learning environment for a proposed Master of Arts (Arts Education) programme at LASALLE-SIA College of the Arts in Singapore. The programme was intended for educators and professionals working in arts education. Given that many prospective students were employed, the institution sought to combine online learning with face-to-face tutorials and adopted SCenTRLE as a framework for applying constructivist learning principles. [ref: Tynan, B. (2005). How do we go beyond the affordances of what we already do on campus? A case of supporting staff in developing a constructivist learning environment. In Proceedings of the 22nd ASCILITE Conference: Balance, Fidelity, Mobility: Maintaining the Momentum? (pp. 685–691). https://www.ascilite.org/conferences/brisbane05/blogs/proceedings/79_Tynan.pdf]

The development team used the model's eight instructional events to plan a module titled Interpreting Contemporary Art. Students would participate in establishing their learning goals and selecting learning strategies, while activities would encourage independent and collaborative knowledge construction. Students would also negotiate assessment criteria and use portfolios to demonstrate their learning. Facilitators would monitor students' progress and provide ongoing feedback, with online activities supported by face-to-face tutorials.

The development team found the model useful for structuring discussions during curriculum design. The study highlighted the use of SCenTRLE as a framework for curriculum development rather than an evaluation of student learning outcomes.

=== Application in secondary mathematics education ===

One application of SCenTRLE was done in 2020 in South Africa. Mlotshwa, Tunjera and Chigona used SCenTRLE as a framework for integrating Moodle into Grade 10 mathematics teaching in South Africa. The authors posit that the model was selected because it combines constructivist learning principles with the use of technology. Their intervention depicted three levels involving teacher guidance, interaction with peers and learning materials, and independent learning through Moodle. [ref: Integration of MOODLE into the classroom for better conceptual understanding of functions in Mathematics, South African Journal of Education]

The researchers found that students who used Moodle performed better than those who received conventional classroom instruction. They recommended integrating Moodle into mathematics teaching and considering SCenTRLE for teacher training.

== Reception and criticism ==

While the model was recommended by some authors, its implementation raised concerns about learner readiness, instructional support and assessment. From the 2005 study by Tynan, several challenges arising during the curriculum design process were identified. These include students' ability to establish their own learning goals, the expertise required of facilitators to provide guidance without directing the learning process, and the use of portfolio assessments. The model's instructional events also needed to be integrated into existing curriculum planning practices.

Similarly, Barksdale also discusses the challenges students may encounter when moving from teacher-directed to student-centred learning, including anxiety, confusion and frustration. Drawing on Hirumi's initial field test, she notes that learners may find it difficult to shoulder increased responsibility for directing their own learning. [ref: Assessment with Technology Integrated Menus: Creating a Bridge Between Traditional and Student-Centered Learning]

Barksdale also noted assessment as another challenge and highlights the importance of aligning assessment with student-centred instruction. This includes greater learner participation in determining performance measures and assessing work. Likewise, Hirumi reported that students in the initial study sought clearer feedback on their progress, even though they considered the portfolio assessment as fair..

Additionally, Miró i Fuentes examined SCenTRLE together with Jonassen's Mindtools and considered the challenges of adapting educational methods to technology-rich environments. He separated the approaches by explaining SCenTRLE as a model concerned with organising learning processes in response to the educational and technological context.. [ref: Reseña sobre los nuevos métodos pedagógicos colaborativos, Cuadernos de Educación y Desarrollo]

== Conflict of interest ==
I am the subject of the biographical article I am drafting. I am disclosing this connection and will submit the draft through Wikipedia’s Articles for Creation process for independent review.

Matthew Bernard Laur (born February 14, 1999), is an American football player, with most of his professional snaps being at wide receiver. Born in Minneapolis, Minnesota, Laur played college football for the University of Minnesota Morris Cougars. After graduating in December, 2021, he continued his football career in Germany. He is the first player in the history of the Minnesota Morris Cougars football program to be a member of the XFL draft pool.

== Early years ==
Matthew Laur was born in Minneapolis, Minnesota. He attended Irondale High School in New Brighton, Minnesota from the fall of 2013 until graduating in the spring of 2017, where he was a letterman in football and weight lifting. In football, he played wide receiver and outside linebacker for the Knights football team. Laur played center as a freshman, but changed to wide receiver and outside linebacker his sophomore season, when he started practicing with JV and varsity. After going 0-10 as a freshman, his sophomore year didn't go any better, as both varsity and junior varsity went winless. Laur started receiving more playing time on special teams units, especially kickoff. As a junior, he became a full time starter for junior varsity going both ways as a wide receiver and outside linebacker. At the end of his junior season (2015), Laur received the Most Improved JV Player award from the team. In the fall of 2016, Laur's senior year of high school, he was placed back on junior varsity instead of being promoted to varsity. He would never start a high school varsity football game, outside of special teams, only getting to start the second half of his senior night at outside linebacker. Laur recorded 1 tackle and 1 fumble recovery as a member of the kickoff team against Park Center Senior High School during his senior night. He would only add a handful more tackles to his high school varsity career stats, all from special teams.

Laur was also a member of his high school's track and field team during his freshman and sophomore years. He competed in the 100m, 800m, shotput, and discus during his two years with the team.

During his junior year of high school, Laur went out for the tennis team. He participated in both singles and doubles during the season for the junior varsity team. This would be his only season of high school tennis.

As a high school senior, Laur joined the Mounds View rugby club. Laur played lock during the rugby season, and wing during the rugby sevens season. Rugby is where Laur learned how to drop kick field goals.

Laur enrolled in the delayed entry program for the Marine Corps during the summer of 2016, wanting to pursue military police. In March of 2017, Matthew was called by the University of Minnesota Morris, and they recruited him to play football for them as a wide receiver. He committed to Morris shortly after to be a student athlete and get his Bachelor of Arts degree in human services: criminal justice. Minnesota Morris was the only school to recruit Laur for athletics.

== College career ==
Laur played his entire college career [ref: Matt Laur - Football, University of Minnesota Morris Athletics] for the University of Minnesota Morris. From the fall of 2017 to the fall of 2021, Laur attended the University of Minnesota Morris as a student athlete. He played wide receiver and special teams for their football program, while earning his bachelor's degree in human services: criminal justice.

In addition to playing football during his time at the University of Minnesota Morris, Laur also played for their tennis team. [ref: Matt Laur - Men's Tennis, University of Minnesota Morris Athletics] He participated in both singles and doubles for his college tennis team. Laur finished his collegiate tennis career with a record of 2-1 in singles, and 1-1 in doubles, for a 3-2 (.600) overall record.

Laur was also a member of the rugby club at Minnesota Morris. He participated in an alumni match his freshman year and played the wing position. After a rugby tournament was canceled during his freshman year, Laur decided to step away from rugby to focus more on football.

=== 2017 season ===
As a freshman at the University of Minnesota Morris, Matthew Laur appeared in 4 games of 10 games. He made his collegiate debut on September 9th, 2017 at Westminster College. The following week on September 16th, 2017, Laur would get his first snaps on offense during a home game against Eureka College. The following week, September 23rd, 2017, Laur recorded his first collegiate reception playing at the College of St. Scholastica, for a seven yard gain and a first down. The cougars would finish this season 1-9 overall, only winning their homecoming game against Crown College.

=== 2018 Season ===
As a Sophomore in 2018, Laur appeared in eight out of ten games, mostly on special teams. Laur racked up 3 tackles (1 solo) on kickoff, all coming against Crown College on October 6th, 2018. Laur earned his first collegiate start at wide receiver against Martin Luther College on October 27th, 2018. Although he didn't see much of an increase in game time on offense, he started making plays as a scout player in practice, and started gaining the attention of his coaches. Minnesota Morris would finish the season 3-7, earning their final win of the season against Greenville University in a snow storm on November 10th, 2018.

=== 2019 season ===
As a junior in 2019, Laur appeared in all ten games, starting four of them at wide receiver. He recorded seven catches for fifty receiving yards, with his longest reception of the season on September 7th, 2019, for 12 yards. His season high for receptions and receiving yards both came on homecoming on September 21st, 2019 against Macmurray College. Laur finished homecoming with 4 receptions for 23 receiving yards. Laur also had two tackles on the season from kickoff, coming against Valley City State University, and Crown College. Morris would finish the season 1-9, with their lone win coming against Iowa Wesleyan University.

=== 2020-2021 (Covid-19) season ===
When his university announced that fall sports were being cancelled due to COVID-19, Laur took the fall semester off from school so he would have eligibility to play in the fall of 2021 and have a senior season. He returned in the spring of 2021 to play a four game "covid season." Before the spring season started, The College of St. Scholastica switched from the UMAC to the MIAC, withdrawing from this shortened UMAC season. The final game against Crown College on April 16th, 2021, was cancelled due to some Crown players in the U.S. National Guard being deployed to protests in Minneapolis that were going on after the murder of George Floyd.

Laur started both spring games, recording 2 catches for 24 yards and a touchdown, all coming against University of Northwestern - St. Paul on April 3rd, 2021. That would end up being the only touchdown of Laur's collegiate career. Minnesota Morris finished the shortened spring season 0-2.

=== 2021 season ===
Finally a senior season during the fall 2021 season, Laur started all ten games of the season, and was also a team captain. Laur caught 19 passes for 291 yards, with his season high for catches in a game coming on September 18th, 2021 against Hamline University, and again on November 13th, 2021 against Greenville University in the UMAC conference championship game, with 4 catches in each of those contests. Laur's season and career high for receiving yards in a game, came against Greenville University as well, with 80 receiving yards in the conference championship game. Laur also added five tackles on kickoff during the season, two being solo. Both solo tackles occurred during a game at Macalester College on September 4th, 2021. The Cougars went 5-5 overall (4-2 in conference play), and lost in the conference championship game against Greenville University. This would be the first time since 2006 that the Cougars would win 4 games in a row. Laur would receive the coaches award at the end of the season, for his improvement as a player and person, on and off the field, and his contributions to the team.

After using all his college eligibility, Laur started contacting teams all over the world looking to continue his football career after college.

== Professional career ==

=== 2022 Season ===
After graduating from the University of Minnesota Morris in December, 2021, Laur signed a one year contract to play football overseas as a wide receiver for the Giessen Golden Dragons in the German Football League 2 in March of 2022. During the 2022 GFL2 season, Laur played in all ten games, recording 54 catches, for 715 receiving yards, 12 receiving touchdowns, and a two-point conversion. Laur also tallied 13 tackles, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery as a member of the kickoff unit during the ten game season. The Golden Dragons finished the season 6-4 overall, finishing in 4th place in the GFL2 South. [https://europlayers.com/ViewProfilePlayer.aspx?ProfileId=66162 Film and stats] from the 2022 GFL2 season earned Laur an [https://www.americanfootballinternational.com/strong-international-influence-found-in-the-xfl-draft-pool/ invite to the 2023 XFL draft pool] without attending a combine.

=== 2023 Season ===
After going undrafted in the 2023 XFL draft, [https://www.facebook.com/share/p/1AaeBayq9Z/?mibextid=wwXIfr Laur spent training camp] with the Salina Liberty in the Champions Indoor Football league during the spring of 2023 in Salina, Kansas. Laur was released at the end of training camp, but [https://podtail.se/podcast/balltime-football-made-in-germany/matt-laur-wr-tollense-sharks-oberliga-ost/ signed with the Tollense Sharks], located in Neubrandenburg, Germany, in the fourth tier of the German Football League system. While mainly playing wide receiver for the Sharks, he also played tight end, running back, quarterback, and returned punts and kicks. Laur was not only signed by the Sharks to play however, as he was also their offensive coordinator and offensive play caller. Under Laur as offensive coordinator and play caller, the Sharks offense went 8-0, with the number one offense in the league. Due to issues surrounding the extension of import player visas, Laur had to end his season earlier than expected, and miss the final two games. The Sharks still finished 10-0 on the season, winning their ninth game without imports, and winning their tenth game due to a forfeit from the other team. This would be Laur's first career championship, dominating the Oberliga Ost. Laur played the eighth game at quarterback after the original import quarterback abandoned the team upon hearing the news about being unable to expand visas through the end of the season, skipping the eighth game. In only [https://europlayers.com/ViewProfilePlayer.aspx?ProfileId=66162 seven games] at wide receiver, Laur racked up 64 catches, for 1,100 receiving yards (1,374 all-purpose yards), 15 receiving touchdowns, 3 rushing touchdowns, and 1 passing touchdown.

=== 2024 Season ===
Going into the following year, [https://www.instagram.com/p/C0XDS_uIOm0/?igsh=enB4bjM1eW1rbjYy Laur signed with Baller Sports Agency]. Following his success during his first season as a player and coach, the Munich Rangers [https://www.instagram.com/p/C3LBrYBsykN/?igsh=MW9xeDIwcHN5c2w4OQ== signed Laur] as a wide receiver and offensive coordinator for the 2024 season. The Rangers played in the 3rd tier of the German Football League system for the 2024 season. As their offensive coordinator, Laur was responsible for installing his playbook in the offense, and creating opening drive scripts for games. Laur played in [https://europlayers.com/ViewProfilePlayer.aspx?ProfileId=66162 eight games], recording 57 catches, for 526 receiving yards, and 7 receiving touchdowns.

=== 2025 Season ===
[https://www.instagram.com/p/DAkKjotvVmv/ Signed to training camp] with the Alabama Beavers of the International Football Alliance but was released before the season started. Laur [https://www.facebook.com/share/p/15y14aZE33/ signed with] the Coralville Chaos of the American Indoor Football League (AIF) and played his first professional arena football game on February 14th, 2025 against the West Michigan Ironmen. In April 2025, Laur [https://www.instagram.com/p/DKCsfv4MYbX/ signed to training camp] with the Chihuahua Rebelión of the International Football Alliance. Laur made the active 43-man roster and competed in the first ever IFA football game, [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=msoNMqL3RWE playing for the Chihuahua Rebelión against the Dallas Prime on May 31st, 2025]. Laur would not only rotate at receiver throughout the game but was the team's punter, as well as being on kickoff and kickoff return units.

In July of 2025, [https://www.instagram.com/p/DN8c2WjkdK8/?igsh=c2loZDh5cGh3cjlh Laur signed with the Hot Springs Wise Guys] of The Arena League (TAL). He was not active for any of the 4 games he spent with the team. They would go on to [https://www.northernnewsnow.com/2025/08/10/duluth-harbor-monsters-repeat-arena-league-champions-with-56-27-win-arenamania-ii/?outputType=amp lose in the championship game, Arena Mania 2].

During the fall of 2025, [https://cdn2.sportngin.com/attachments/document/37c2-3462675/Roster-FB-V-25-26_New_LOGO.pdf?_gl=1*1dbj3z1*_ga*MTMwNjA1NDExNy4xNzY3OTcyMTkw*_ga_PQ25JN9PJ8*czE3Njc5NzIyMDIkbzEkZzAkdDE3Njc5NzIyMDIkajYwJGwwJGgw#_ga=2.240333827.1853474165.1767972190-1306054117.1767972190 Laur would be an assistant defensive backs coach] at Rogers High School where he also assisted in coaching the punters.

=== 2026 Season ===
Laur would sign a contract with the Wyoming Cavalry of the AIF to play wide receiver to start off 2026. [ref: ] He would play in 3 games, totaling 4 catches, 51 yards, 2 TD, and 3 tackles. The Cavalry would go on to finish their season 6-0.

After the end of the AIF season, Laur would sign to training camp with the Eau Claire Axemen of the TAL to play wide receiver for them. During week 1, just before halftime, Laur dislocated his knee during a two point conversion. This resulted in a torn ACL, PCL, and LCL, ending his season after recording 2 catches for 8 yards.

data.text:
Shaz Saleem – Full Biography

Shaz Saleem

British community leader, charity founder and former local politician

Shaz Saleem is known for his involvement in local government, charitable fundraising, youth development and community initiatives across Dudley, Kingswinford and the wider West Midlands.

1. Early life and personal background

Shaz Saleem has strong connections to the Black Country, particularly Kingswinford and the Dudley borough. He was the Chairman of Dudley Private Hire and Taxi Association which had over 2000 members.

Family and community have played an important role in shaping his public activities. One particularly significant influence was his grandfather, whose memory inspired the establishment of The Saleem Foundation in 2019.

His public profile has centred on helping others, bringing communities together and encouraging young people to get involved in positive activities.

Detailed information about his age, education and early childhood is not widely documented in reliable public sources.

2. Education and professional background

Saleem's public LinkedIn profile lists the University of Wolverhampton as his place of study between 2006 and 2009.

His profile also identifies experience in the taxi industry, business enterprise advice and community organisations.

3. Political career

Saleem became involved in local politics through the Conservative Party.

# 2021 – Elected councillor

Elected as a Conservative representative for Kingswinford North and Wall Heath on Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council.

# 2022 – Cabinet appointment

Appointed cabinet member for highways and public realm, with responsibilities relating to local roads, highways and public spaces.

# 2023 – Departure from Conservative group

Following his suspension from the Conservative Party in February 2023, he left his cabinet position and continued serving as an independent councillor.

# 2025 – Court proceedings

Saleem stood trial over two charges concerning messages allegedly sent over a public communications network. He denied both charges and was found not guilty by the district judge in March 2025.

# 2026 – Return to Conservatives

He announced his return to the Conservative Party and indicated that he would support candidates rather than stand in the 2026 local elections.

4. The Saleem Foundation

The Saleem Foundation was established in 2019 in memory of Saleem's grandfather, Al-Haj Master Mohammad Saleem, who died in 2016.

The organisation supports people experiencing financial hardship, disability, illness, social isolation and other difficulties across Birmingham and the Black Country.

Its registered charity number is 1183167, according to the Charity Commission.

Its community initiatives have included:

* TSF Youth Club: Activities and opportunities for local young people.
* TSF Kuppa Club: Social gatherings intended to reduce loneliness, particularly among older residents.
* Kingswinford and Wall Heath Litter Pick Group: Volunteer-led environmental improvements. They won the Black Country Heroes Award for Environment in 2026.
* Mental health awareness: Campaigns, films and support for community conversations.
* Emergency and charitable assistance: Food deliveries, food banks and fundraising for other charities.

In an interview published by the University of Derby's StoryHub in March 2026, Saleem explained that his grandfather's death had been a major turning point in his life. He described how establishing the charity helped him turn personal difficulties into community action.

5. Fundraising and charitable achievements

£240,000+

Reported cumulative fundraising for various charitable causes

2019

Year The Saleem Foundation was established

Saleem's fundraising activities have included a 15,000-foot skydive, bungee jumping, abseiling and charity boxing. Local reporting credits him with raising more than £240,000 for various charitable causes, although that figure is not an independently audited lifetime total.

The Foundation has also supported West Midlands Air Ambulance and organised smaller community fundraising events, including coffee afternoons.

6. Awards and recognition

One of his notable honours was the High Sheriff Award in 2025, recognising his contribution to community life.

The award was presented by Douglas Wright MBE DL at a West Midlands ceremony in Sutton Coldfield.

The recognition highlighted his voluntary activities, community groups, charitable fundraising and work supporting local residents.

7. Community values and public profile

A recurring theme in Saleem's interviews is his belief that residents share responsibility for improving the places where they live.

He has spoken about the importance of helping people who experience loneliness, supporting mental wellbeing, engaging young people and encouraging residents to volunteer.

His work combines grassroots community activity with political experience, although the two are distinct parts of his public career.

8. Recent activities in 2026

In 2026, Saleem continued to be publicly associated with charitable fundraising and community projects.

Dudley Council also publicised a charity boxing event involving Saleem and council leader Patrick Harley, planned to raise money for the Mayor of Dudley's charities. The council's announcement set a fundraising target of £30,000, which should not be confused with a confirmed amount raised.

9. Overall profile

Shaz Saleem is best described as a former local politician who has developed a prominent community and charitable role in the Black Country.

His public story has several defining elements: his grandfather's influence, the creation of The Saleem Foundation, his election to Dudley Council, his period as a cabinet member, his departure and return to the Conservatives, and recognition for his voluntary work.

== References ==

* University of Derby StoryHub – Shaz Saleem's personal story
* Charity Commission – The Saleem Foundation
* Dudley Council – Cabinet appointment, 2022
* Express & Star – Return to the Conservative Party

data.title: Blue Alto Farewell 2026
data.text:
----

= Blue Alto Farewell 2026 =
[https://youtube.com/@[user] Blue Alto Farewell 2026] is a proposed name for an alleged incident associated with a school farewell held on 23 April 2026 in Rawalpindi, Punjab, Pakistan. Accounts provided by a student describing the incident concern a disagreement among friends over transportation to an after-party and the reported departure of a group in a blue Suzuki Alto. The circumstances surrounding the incident have not been independently verified, and the proposed name has not been established as a widely used or officially recognized title.

== Background ==
The account places the alleged incident at or near the parking area by the gate of Army Public School and College (APSAC), Ordnance Road, in Rawalpindi. The event was reportedly associated with a Grade 12 farewell.

According to the account, a group of four friends planned to attend an after-party following the farewell [ref: SSC Farewell APSAC Ordinance Road]. The account alleges that three members of the group left in a blue Suzuki Alto while the fourth, identified in the account as Unas Rizwan, was left behind.

== Alleged incident ==
The account [ref: Account: Blue Alto] further alleges that the circumstances surrounding the group’s departure became disputed. It describes disagreement over whether the friends had arrived at the agreed time and whether they had seen or collected the student who was reportedly left behind.

The account also claims that injuries were observed afterward. However, no independent documentation has been provided to establish how the injuries occurred or whether they were connected to the alleged incident. The available information does not establish that an assault took place or determine responsibility for any harm.

== Disputed accounts and online discussion ==
According to the account, the students involved gave differing explanations of the events, including disagreements about their timing and whether they had seen the student in question. The account also describes discussion and speculation among students on social media.

A YouTube channel using the name “Blue Alto [ref: Blue Alto Account]” has been identified by the person providing the account as a possible source of related material. The channel’s content, the context of any relevant videos, and claims that material was subsequently deleted have not been independently verified.

== Documentation and investigation ==
The person providing the account reports having photographs, chat records, timestamps, and written statements related to the alleged incident. These materials have not been independently examined for this draft.

No independently verifiable news reports or publicly available official investigation documenting the alleged incident were identified during the research conducted for this draft. The official school website confirms the institution’s identity but does not, by itself, establish that the alleged incident occurred.

== Sources ==

# Army Public School & College (Boys), Ordnance Road, Rawalpindi. Official website: https://apsordrd.edu.pk/ This source provides institutional information; it has not been identified as documenting the alleged incident.
# “Blue Alto” YouTube channel. https://youtube.com/@[user] Identified by the person providing the account as a possible source for further research. The relevance and reliability of its content have not been independently established.

data.title: Ben Mora
data.text:
Ben Mora (b. 1994) is an American game show host, podcaster, and former political organizer. He created and hosts Interior Motives, a YouTube game show with the tagline, "You show us your bed and we guess who's been in it," and co-hosts the comedy podcast Seeking Derangements. [ref: ] [ref: The YouTube Game Show That Judges You by Your Bedroom, Dwell] He is known for his large bright blue eyes, causing him to suffer frequent comparisons to a memefied photograph of the pop singer Miley Cyrus. [ref: Please Stop This Miley Cyrus Meme, W Magazine]

== Early Life and Education ==
Mora grew up in Des Moines, Iowa, in a house built partly by his father, a contractor from Costa Rica. His mother was an occupational therapist for Des Moines Public Schools. He said that he was a difficult teenager, a heavy marijuana smoker who often fought with his parents. [ref: Interior Motives Host Ben Mora Knows You by Your Stuff, Curbed] At seventeen, he moved to Denver, where he worked in restaurants as a maid. He has said that when he first moved out, he slept for a year and a half on a pile of clothes that he molded into a makeshift mattress with a fitted sheet. [ref: Ben Mora, TANKtv] According to Mora's longtime friend Chloe Truong-Jones, he left Colorado after falling out with a group of Buffalo Exchange employees who accused him of being "the [[Osama bin Laden|[O]sama bin Laden]] of the Denver Arts Community." [ref: chlobuchar (@[user]_im_chloe) on X, X (formerly Twitter)]

== Career ==

===== Politcal Organizing =====
In 2019, Mora, now living in Iowa again, began volunteering for Bernie Sanders's presidential campaign. He was hired full time on the basis of his door knocking prowess, and went on to organize events for service workers in Des Moines. After the Iowa caucuses, the campaign sent him to Michigan, where by February 2020 he had been promoted to regional field director. [ref: ] Mora has said that during the campaign he slept in the campaign office, a former Office Max store in Dearborn. He was fired that first month (see Controversies). [ref: Bernie Sanders Staffer Fired for Mocking Warren, Buttigieg on Private Twitter Account, The Daily Beast]

===== Seeking Derangements =====
After his dismissal, Mora received hate mail from some strangers and donations from others, the latter of which he called his "Venmo severance package." He felt to New York City in March 2020 and by his own account, arrived as "an instant microcelebrity," with invitations to appear on "dirtbag left" podcasts; he was a guest on Red Scare that month. [ref: Red Scare Podcast: Corona Crush w/ Ben Mora, redscarepodcast.libsyn.com] He also started his own comedy podcast, Seeking Derangements, with friends, among them Hesse Deni and Jacques Gonsoulin. In December 2020, he and journalist Glenn Greenwald started a weekly podcast on Substack, Ben and Glenn's After Hours. [ref: ] The podcast later ended over creative differences. [ref: New: Ben And Glenn's After Hours, Podcast Business Journal]

===== Interior Motives =====
In 2025, while scrolling through TikTok, Mora came across a video of a messy room and wondered who lived there. He said that he then looked around his own room, where he was lying on a mattress with no bed frame, and thought, "This room looks really gay." He tested the idea as a game on Seeking Derangements. Listeners responded at once; in the summer of 2025, Mora relaunched the game as a separate YouTube show, recording from his childhood bedroom in Des Moines. He has named the online games GeoGuessr, in which players guess a location from street-level photographs, and the television series Queer Eye as influences: "What if you did GeuGuessr for gender? For sexuality?" He has also said that the show draws on his own experience of poor housing and that "the show is in some ways about the housing crisis." [ref: The YouTube Game Show That Judges You by Your Bedroom, Dwell]

In each episode, which runs about an hour, Mora and guest contestants join a remote call and examine photographs of three bedrooms submitted by viewers, along with a photograph of another space, such as the inside of a refrigerator or a medicine cabinet, a car, a workplace, or an Instagram Explore page. The contestants guess the age, gender, sexuality, and location of the person who lives in room and receive a point for each correct guess. Mora opens each episode by asking the contestants which object in their own rooms might give away where they are calling from. Mora releases two episodes a week, some of which are devoted to submissions from outside the United States. Mora edits each episode himself, with emoji captions, satirical sponsorships, canned applause, and an opening sequence in retro graphics. Subscribers on Patreon pay $7 a month for extra episodes, some of them R-rated, and the change to play the game live against one another. [ref: Interior Motives Host Ben Mora Knows You by Your Stuff, Curbed]

Contestants have included Courtney Love, Margaret Cho, Kim Petras, John Early, Kate Berlant, Julio Torres, Hari Nef, Juliana Huxtable, Gregg Araki, Jeremy O. Harris, and Hasan Piker. Mora said in 2026 that he received more than 5,000 room submissions. In September 2026, the Youtube channel had 140,000 subscribers and more than 6.9 million views. By October 2026, Mora had hosted nearly 75 episodes. [ref: Ben Mora wants to see your bedroom, Dazed]

In a profile of Mora, New York magazine described some of the contestants as "surprisingly astute in ways that are mesmerizing to watch and occasionally informative." Mora has said that the contestants, himself among them, usually guess wrong; he has also said that the clearest differences among the submitted rooms are between generations rather then between genders, sexualities, or places. [ref: Ben Mora, TANKtv]

== Controversies ==
On February 24, 2020, The Daily Beast reported that Mora, "a regional field director for Sanders's campaign based in Michigan," had used a private Twitter account, which had about 4,000 followers, to mock candidates in the Democratic presidential primary. [ref: A Brief Guide to the Pettiest Scandal of Campaign 2020, Slate] In his tweets, Mora wrote that Pete Buttigieg "is what happens when the therapist botches the conversion," that Buttigieg was untrustworthy "because he combined the natural devious disposition inherent in gay men with a bloodthirsty careerist drive," and that Buttigieg's husband, Chasten, "has the vibes of a housewife whose slow burning repression is leading to an inevitable psychotic break" and would "go missing and then resurface in Ft. Lauderdale after getting busted for running a meth racket with a bunch of Guatemalan twinks." He was also running an account named @[user], which Twitter suspended. He referred to Elizabeth Warren as a "dumb Okie" and "an adult diaper fetishist" and opined that she "looks like shit." He compared the appearance of Amy Klobuchar to "that optical illusion where it's an old lady but also a young woman depending on how you look at it but with her it's just two different old ladies" He suggested that "Hillary Clinton should literally be catapulted off the planet." He urged his followers to volunteer for phone banks for Michael Bloomberg, a candidate in the primary, in order to enter false data and "totally sink" the Bloomberg campaign.

After the report appeared, Mora was fired. Mike Casca, the communications director of the Sanders campaign, said: "We are running a multiracial, multigenerational campaign for justice where disgusting behavior and ugly personal attacks by our staff will not be tolerated." In a 2026 interview, Mora confirmed the firing and said: "I'm not ashamed of it. In fact, with hindsight, it's the best thing that ever happened to me." [ref: ]

== Personal Life ==
Mora is gay. [ref: Gay Sanders staffer busted running anon Twitter account slurring Buttigieg & other candidates, LGBTQ Nation] He describes himself as a leftist. Since March 2025, he has led what he calls "a bit of a drifter lifestyle," living alternatively between Des Moines and other cities like New York City, Los Angeles, and New Orleans. In 2026, he said he is single and does not use dating apps.

data.title: Ekonómia ľudskou rečou
data.text:
Ekonómia ľudskou rečou () is a Slovak educational media project that explains economics, personal finance and economic policy in non-technical language. It was started in April 2020 by analyst Martin Lindák as a YouTube channel and later expanded into a podcast, a website and an Instagram account. [ref: Slovákom na Youtube vysvetľuje ekonomické témy. Jeho rady odoberajú najmä muži, Forbes Slovensko] [ref: Analytik Lindák: Na YouTube sa dá zarobiť, ale s mojimi témami sa človek neuživí, Forbes Slovensko]

== History ==
Martin Lindák, a native of Rožňava, studied finance, banking and investment at the University of Economics in Bratislava. He was an external contributor to the F. A. Hayek Foundation, worked at Index, the business section of the daily SME, and as an analyst at the Slovak Business Agency, and later became an analyst at the business-information company FinStat. [ref: Martin Lindák – Rebríček 30 pod 30: Forbes predstavuje členov pre rok 2024, Forbes Slovensko]

He launched the channel during the COVID-19 pandemic while working from home. He cited Slovak popular-history and popular-science channels such as Dejepis Inak and Vedátor as inspiration, saying that nobody in Slovakia had done something similar for economics.

The channel grew fastest during the 2020–2023 global chip shortage and after the start of the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022, when it published videos on the Russian economy, sanctions, the SWIFT system and whether Europe could replace Russian gas. In April 2023, Forbes Slovakia reported that the channel had about 45,000 subscribers, more than 120 videos and 4.6 million views, with almost 16,000 followers on Instagram.

== Content ==
The project covers macroeconomics, public finance, taxes and social contributions, pensions, housing and mortgages, investing, inflation, entrepreneurship and the world economy. [ref: Ekonomika a osobné financie ľudskou rečou, Ekonómia ľudskou rečou] Its most-watched videos have included an overview of the Russian economy published on 22 February 2022 (over 350,000 views), a video on the chip shortage, two videos on the economy of Vatican City released around Pope Francis's 2021 visit to Slovakia, and a documentary-style video on the economic history of the Gemer region.

=== Podcast ===
A podcast of the same name has been produced since 2022 by the Slovak podcast network skpodcasty.sk. Besides Lindák, it has been hosted by Nikola Šuliková Bajánová and Jana Kubalová. As of October 2026, Apple Podcasts listed 188 episodes. [ref: Ekonómia ľudskou rečou, Apple Podcasts]

== Audience and funding ==
According to Lindák, the audience is mostly aged 25 to 50; on YouTube it is predominantly male and includes a significant share of pensioners, while the Instagram audience is balanced by gender. The project is funded through YouTube advertising, sponsored segments and supporter contributions. Lindák has said he does not provide investment advice.

== Reception ==
In 2024, Lindák was included in the Forbes Slovakia 30 Under 30 list in the Science and Education category for the project, and appeared as a guest on episode 29 of the Forbes 30 pod 30 podcast. As the channel's author he appears in Slovak media as a commentator on economic issues. In March 2022, shortly after the Russian invasion began, the news site Startitup interviewed him about the state of the Russian economy, [ref: Putinovo Rusko môže o 2 týždne zbankrotovať, hovorí Martin z kanálu Ekonómia ľudskou rečou, Startitup] and in May 2026 he was a guest on Startitup's interview show Dírerov filter, discussing the sustainability of the Slovak pension system and housing affordability for young people. [ref: Lindák: Sme na tom horšie ako Rumuni, na dôchodky nemáme, Startitup] [ref: „Slováci sú na tom horšie ako Rumuni, na dôchodky jednoducho nemáme," hovorí Lindák, Startitup] In September 2026, Denník N quoted him as an economist "known from the YouTube channel Ekonómia ľudskou rečou" on the risks of buy-to-let apartments and on spotting investment fraud. [ref: Ekonóm a youtuber Martin Lindák upozorňuje, ako si všimnúť podvod, ktorý nás láka na vysoké zhodnotenie peňazí, Denník N] [ref: Investičné byty sa prezentujú ako priama cesta k bohatstvu. Mám s tým problém, vraví ekonóm Martin Lindák, známy z youtubového kanála Ekonómia ľudskou rečou, Denník N]

data.title: Robilant
data.text:
Robilant is an art gallery based in London, founded in 2026 by art dealer Edmondo di Robilant. The gallery was founded following the separation of the gallery Robilant+Voena, and specialises in European Old Masters, 20th Century art with a focus on the Italian Post-War period, and Contemporary art. [ref: Robilant, Robilant]

The gallery is located on Dover Street, in Mayfair, the former premises of Robilant+Voena. Robilant offers a varied exhibition programme, presenting curated shows on art from the 16th century to the present. The gallery also participates in fairs internationally, including TEFAF Maastricht and TEFAF New York, Frieze Masters in London, NOMAD in St. Moritz and its inaugural edition in the Hamptons.

=== Exhibitions ===
Robilant launched its exhibition programme with a group show of five contemporary artists in May 2026, titled Nor here, Nor there. The artists represented in the exhibition were Yoan Capote, Isaac Chong Wai, Hung Fai, Raya Kassisieh and Vittorio Marella. [ref: ]

In October 2026, the gallery opened a survey of 400 years of still life painting, Still Life, Then and Now. The exhibition featured paintings from the 16th century to the present, by artists such as Osias Beert the Elder, Willem Claesz. Heda, Sebastian Stoskopff, Michelangelo Cerquozzi, Francisco de Zurbarán, Giovanni Battista Recco, Anne Vallayer-Coster, Giovanni Segantini, Henri Fantin-Latour, Victoria Dubourg, Odilon Redon, Pablo Picasso, Juan Gris, Pierre Bonnard, Nicolas de Staël, Andy Warhol, Poppy Jones and Asher Liftin. [ref: ] The exhibition was featured by ARTNews and House & Garden as one of the top exhibitions to see in London in October 2026. [ref: 7 Exhibitions to See in London During Frieze Week, From Shocking ’90s Artworks to Renoir Masterpieces, ARTnews.com] [ref: The art exhibitions you need to see in London in October 2026, House & Garden]

data.title: Frédéric Worms
data.text:
----

Frédéric Worms was born on 30 January 1964 [ref: Connaissez-vous Frédéric Worms ?, www.marianne.net] in Boulogne-Billancourt, Hauts-de-Seine, Île-de-France. Worms is a French contemporary philosopher, a professor at the University of Lille and director of the École normale supérieure since 2022. He is known for his specialization in the history and thought of Henri Bergson. He is the author of several books and periodicals, and has directed much editorial work. In 2018, he was awarded the Prix Moron for his entire body of work.

== Education ==
Worms received his education at École normale supérieure in Paris from 1982-1986, at which time and place he earned the Agrégation in Philosophy. [ref: Frédéric Worms: “Le refus de la mort sous toutes ses formes est la seule façon de fonder la morale”, philomag] He completed a doctoral thesis in 1995 at Blaise Pascal University, a that is titled in English translation, "The problem of mind: psychology, koowledge theory, and metaphysics in the philosophy of Bergson," and researched under the supervision of Jean-Claude Pariente. [ref: Le problème de l'esprit: psychologie, théorie de la connaissance et métaphysique dans l'oeuvre de Bergson, Theses] He also obtained a Habilitation to direct research in 2004. His work for that qualification was published as Bergson ou Les deux sens de la vie: étude inédite by Presses Universitaires de France (PUF) in 2004. [ref: Bergson ou les deux sens de la vie: étude inédite, Presses universitaires de France]

== Academic career ==
He is a professor at the University of Lille since 2004, director of the ENS since 2022, [ref: Frédéric Worms: "Bien organisé, notre emploi du temps est un instrument contre la panique qui menace le monde", L'Express] [ref: Décret du 12 mars 2022 portant nomination du directeur de l'Ecole normale supérieure - M. WORMS (Frédéric), Journal officiel de la République française] [ref: « L’urgence la plus vitale »: quand tout devient urgent, que faut-il sauver d’abord ?, up-magazine] and a visiting professor at several institutions in the United States and United Kingdom, including: Worms is a visiting professor at several institutions, including UC Berkeley, UCLA, the University of Chicago, Ritsumeikan University, and the University of Essex. [ref: Entretien avec Frédéric Worms - Philosophe et professeur de philosophie contemporaine à l’École normale supérieure, membre du Comité consultatif national d’éthique pour les sciences de la vie et de la santé Marie Gaille and Jean-Luc Teillaud Med Sci (Paris), 35 2 (2019) 157-162 DOI: https://doi.org/10.1051/medsci/2019012]

Since 2006, he has been the founding honorary president of the (Society of Friends of Bergson). He co-authored a biography of the philosopher with Philippe Soulez. He directed the first critical edition of Bergson's works for Presses Universitaires de France (2007–2012)—a collection comprising all of lectures, articles, correspondence, and previously unpublished lectures from the Collège de France. [ref: La première édition critique de Bergson, www.puf.com] It included volumes of the Annales bergsoniennes in the "Épiméthée" series directed by Jean-Luc Marion. Worms directed the Annales bergsoniennes, a PUF collection, and also currently directs the "Questions de soin" [ref: Questions de soin, www.puf.com] and "Philosophie française contemporaine" book series. [ref: Philosophie française contemporaine, www.puf.com] He is a co-editor of the journal Bergsoniana.

Since 2004, he is the director of the (International Center for the Study of Contemporary French Philosophy, abbreviated as CIEPFC), a component of the "Republic of Knowledge: Letters, Sciences, Philosophy" research unit (UMR 3608 ENS / CNRS / Collège de France). [ref: Frédéric Worms – République des Savoirs, republique-des-savoirs] [ref: Approches de l’individuel: Épistémologie, logique, métaphysique. France: Éditions Rue d’Ulm via OpenEdition, 2022.]

In 2007, at the University of Lille III, he established the "Ethics of the Living" Master's program, which he directed until 2013. [ref: Frédéric Worms Institut-ENS, institutens]

From 2012 to 2014, he served as director of the USR 3308 Cirphles (ENS / CNRS). In September 2015, he became the deputy director of the École normale supérieure. [ref: Frédéric Worms, Philomonaco]

From 2013-2021, he served on the Comité consultatif national d'éthique (National Ethics Advisory Committee, [ref: Arrêté du 26 décembre 2017 portant nomination au comité consulta, ccne-ethique] investigating bioethical issues in the sciences.

Prior to his appointment as director at the ENS, he was the institution's deputy director (from 2015) under the directorship of Marc Mézard.

== Research and reception ==
The philosopher and critic Jean-Hugues Barthélémy considers Worms to be a leading Bergson scholar. In La philosophie en France au xxe siècle. Moments (Gallimard, 2009), Worms developed a general hypothesis regarding the history of philosophy that, according to Barthélémy, can be
applied to the timeline of 20th-century French philosophy. [ref: Barthélémy, Jean-Hugues. « Frédéric Worms, La philosophie en France au xxe siècle. Moments, Paris, Gallimard, 2009, 650 p. ». Revue philosophique de la France et de l'étranger, 2010/2 Tome 135, 2010. p.257z-289z. https://doi.org/10.3917/rphi.102.0257z] Barthélémy explains that Worms's theory is divided into three "moments": the 1900 moment, the Second World War moment, and the 1960 moment. The first, he wrote, is defined by the problem of the mind (or spirit), the second by the problem of existence, and the third by the problem of structure. In his work, Worms places the philosophers Bergson, Brunschvicg and Alain predominantly in the 1900 moment. However, Barthélémy stresses, Worms identifies throughout the work many approaches shared by Bergson and the major contemporary philosophers such as Freud, Husserl, and James. Barthélémy cites the work (Moments, p.37) as explaining at the first "moment" (the 1900 moment) is interested in the duality of experience: subjective and other

Barthélémy explains Worms's second "moment" as emerging from World War II, and as one that shifts philosophy from a meditation on the mind to one of existence. He suggested one fault in Worms's theory was the failure to explain Merleau-Ponty's determination, in contrast to Sartre's split approach, not to be either realist or idealist. Otherwise, Barthélémy credits Worms for a thorough exploration of Merleau-Ponty's work. Worms, rather, demonstrates that it was Gaston Bachelard who ushered in the real transition through his critique of Bergsonian theory of Duration. Finally, Worms concludes his theory of this "moment" by comparing Merleau-Ponty, Canguilhem, and on the problem of the figure of "the hero."

According to Barthélémy, the third of Worms's "moments" is about structural thought. Worms asserts that it is defined by its duality-structure and difference. The 1960 moment is, thus, a "system of differences" (Moments, p.469), with tension between "system" and "difference." Derrida, more than Levinas, Worms wrote, questioned the "system" in the name of "difference" in its post-Heideggerian dimension--in other words, ontological difference. Derrida, Worms writes, carried the "moment" deeper into the question of human life and "animal" life, as well as into the realm of morality and the life "worthy of being lived" (Moments, p.506) but it is ultimately Paul Ricœur, as Barthélémy notes, who gets the more extensive treatment by Worms.

Worms carries the history of philosophy through the 20th century thinkers Jean Cavaillès, Jean Wahl, Albert Camus, Simone Weil, Vladimir Jankélévitch, and Jean-François Lyotard. Barthélémy asserts that Worms's work is notable for moving beyond Hegel's notion of "epochs" in history and conceiving of a discontinuous movement from individuation to the multidimensional "transindividual."

=== Chapters and prefaces ===

data.title: Reconomy
data.text:
Reconomy is a British circular economy and waste management company headquartered in Telford, Shropshire, England. Founded in 1994 as an outsourced waste management business, it expanded through a series of acquisitions in the United Kingdom, mainland Europe and North America, and provides waste and resource management, extended producer responsibility (EPR) compliance, take-back and reverse logistics services. It operates through a number of specialist brands, including Valpak, Reverse Logistics Group (RLG), Noventiz, Advanced Supply Chain, ReBound and Lincoln Waste Solutions.

The company has been owned by the private equity firm EMK Capital since 2017. Its revenue grew from about £111 million in 2016 to more than £1 billion in 2022, largely through acquisitions.

== History ==

=== 1994 to 2016: Founding and early growth ===
The company's main UK trading entity, Reconomy (UK) Limited, was incorporated on 22 July 1994 as Critical Resource Limited and adopted its current name in 2012. The business provided outsourced waste management services for commercial customers, delivering a national service through a network of independent local waste operators.

In July 2006 the private equity firm Bregal Capital acquired a majority stake in the business. In 2015 Reconomy bought Countrywide Waste Management in January and Just Hire UK, which traded as Network Waste, in October. At that time it employed about 180 people, worked mainly in the construction and business and industrial sectors, and expected annual turnover of about £90 million. It acquired Skippy Nationwide in 2016.

=== 2017 to 2021: EMK Capital ownership and diversification ===
In August 2017 Reconomy was acquired by EMK Capital, a London-based private equity firm founded by Bregal's former managing partner Edmund Lazarus. The company then employed about 300 people, had sales of £111 million in the previous year and managed about three million tonnes of waste a year. In 2018 it refinanced its debt with a £70.7 million facility from Macquarie Bank, reporting turnover of £122 million for 2017.

During 2018 Reconomy acquired the waste broker Waste Check, the resource management consultancy Helistrat and, in December, Valpak, which it described as the UK's largest compliance scheme provider, which continued to operate under its own brand. Group revenue was forecast to exceed £250 million in 2019.

The company began to expand outside the UK in 2020. It acquired Noventiz, a waste disposal provider based in Cologne, Germany, in October 2020, and agreed in December 2020 to acquire Reverse Logistics Group, a Munich-based provider of outsourced resource management and environmental services operating in more than 80 countries. The RLG deal took the group's pro-forma revenue for 2020 to more than £465 million. In late 2021 it bought the British recycling businesses Casepak and Oceala.

=== 2022 to present: Further acquisitions and North America ===
In 2022 Reconomy and RLG acquired Rene AG, a German compliance services provider for electronics, packaging and batteries. Group revenue more than doubled to over £1 billion in 2022, from £490 million in 2021, through a combination of organic growth and acquisitions.

Guy Wakeley succeeded Paul Cox as chief executive on 1 January 2023, with Cox moving to the role of founder director on the group board. In 2023 the company acquired the Danish recycling and waste management company Combineering and the Newark-based waste broker UK Waste Solutions, whose brands included Novati, AMA, Click Waste and Evolution.

In the first half of 2024 Reconomy made four acquisitions, including its first two in North America (Lincoln Waste Solutions of Windsor, Connecticut, and Vermilion), the German metal recovery business Sudamin Rohstoff and the UK waste management provider Circle Waste. It continued to expand in the United States through Lincoln Waste Solutions, acquiring Complete Solutions & Sourcing and Waste Focus in January 2025, American Outsourced Waste and Recycling in April 2025, and Integrated Waste Analysts and National Waste Associates later that year. In 2026 it acquired the German industrial waste management company GfAW and, in its ninth North American acquisition, Waste Disposal Solutions of Greensboro, North Carolina.

== Operations ==
Reconomy organises its services into three areas, which it calls loops: Recycle, covering outsourced waste and resource management; Comply, covering producer responsibility and environmental compliance; and Re-use, covering returns management, reverse logistics and supply chain services. The Re-use loop includes the specialist brands Advanced Supply Chain and ReBound. The group's businesses are based in locations including Telford and Stratford-upon-Avon in England, Munich and Cologne in Germany, Denmark, and Connecticut and North Carolina in the United States.

According to the company, it served more than 25,000 customers in over 175 countries in 2025, with about 32% of revenue from the UK, 42% from the European Union and 23% from North America.

== Sustainability reporting ==
Reconomy publishes an annual group sustainability report. Its report for 2022 stated that 97.5% of the waste it managed was diverted from landfill and that 67% of its electricity came from renewable sources, while its absolute carbon emissions rose by 28%, which the company attributed to acquired UK sites. Its near-term and net-zero emissions targets have been validated by the Science Based Targets initiative.

In 2024 the company published a framework of ten proposals for reforming the UK waste system, developed with the consultancy Sancroft.

data.text:
----

Bix Pix Entertainment is an American animation studio specializing in stop-motion animation, based in Burbank, California and was founded in 1998. [ref: Local Stories - Meet Kelli Bixler of Burbank, CA, VoyageLA]

== History and Work ==
Bix Pix Entertainment has provided original and work-for-hire production services across new media, television, commercials and short films for clients including Disney, NBC, Cartoon Network, Hasbro, Amazon Studios and Applet TV+. [ref: Bix Pix Clicks with Amazon, Kidscreen Magazine] [ref: Podcast: Creating Stop Motion Animation, WAMC Northeast Public Radio] The studio's credits include several award-winning productions, among them the preschool series Tumble Leaf, which received a BAFTA, an Annecy International Animation Film Festival Jury Award, Annie Awards, Emmy Awards and a Peabody nomination; Adventure Time episode "Bad Jubies," which earned an Annie Award; and Apple TV+'s Shape Island which received an Annecy Jury Award and nominations for a Peabody and an Emmy Award.

Founder, Kelli Bixler discovered stop motion while working as a live-action director in Chicago, IL and Bix Pix was established shortly after that. [ref: Reel Chicago, Reel Chicago] The studio's early productions were created in traditional clay animation and included a 23-minute video Doh-Doh Island Adventures for Hasbro, the "NBC Memories" commercial, and Miss Twiggley's Tree, based on Dorothea Warren Fox's children's book. [ref: The Big Picture, Animation Magazine] In 2005, the studio produced a Saturday Night Live "TV Funhouse" segment Christmastime for the Jews. [ref: (https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0694918/companycredits/?ref_=tt_dt_cmpyv)] [ref: Stop-Motion ‘Community’ Special Airs Thursday, Animation Magazine]

The studio relocated to Los Angeles in 2006 and began production on the ABC special Holiday: The Christmas That Almost Didn't Happen. [ref: Wal-Mart Taps Bix Pix for Holiday Toons, Animation Magazine] In 2013, Bix Pix developed the preschool show Tumble Leaf for Amazon Studios. [ref: Bix Pix Brings Handcrafted Approach to Amazon's Tumble Leaf, Animation World Magazine] In between seasons, Bix Pix worked with director Kirsten Lepore to produce her stop-motion episode "Bad Jubies" for Cartoon Network's Adventure Time [ref: Kirsten Lepore Lends Stop-Motion Skill to Tonight’s ‘Adventure Time’, Cartoon Brew] [ref: Adventure Time: Good Jubies – Making Of Bad Jubies, Stop Motion Magazine]and in 2017, they worked with Fred Rogers Productions and The Fred Rogers Center to create the Google Doodle "Celebrating Mister Rogers." [ref: Watch Google's beautiful tribute to Mister Rogers, USA Today] In 2021, Bix Pix moved to Burbank, CA to create Shape Island for Apple TV+, adapting Mac Barnett and Jon Klassen's Shape books. [ref: Bix Pix Brings Great ‘Form’ to Apple TV+’s ‘Shape Island’ Kids’ Series, Animation World Network]

Tien Bolt is a 2026 comedy short film listed on [[https://letterboxd.com/film/tien-bolt/](https://letterboxd.com/film/tien-bolt/) Letterboxd].\ [ref: Tien Bolt, Letterboxd\] The film stars Tien Ho as the title character, Tien Bolt, and Ammaar Liaqat as his rival, Ammaar Blake.

\== Plot == Tien Bolt attempts to break the world record in the 100-metre dash while competing against his intense and competitive rival, Ammaar Blake. Their rivalry develops into a high-pressure athletic showdown, with Tien's preparations complicated by comedic mishaps.

After Tien loses a race, his girlfriend breaks up with him and begins a relationship with Ammaar. Despite these personal setbacks, Tien ultimately wins the race and breaks the 100-metre world record.

Paul F La Franca (born 15 August 1959) is an Information Technology Engineer and Author of children books. Paul loves to travel, and play soccer with his friends.

Born in Villabate, a small town near Palermo, Paul emigrated with his mother Caterina, father Giuseppe, and sister Patricia on October 12, 1972 to search for a better life. He has been blessed with a family, a career, and his love for travel. His latest accomplishment is the publishing of his book Coconut’s Amazing Adventures.

Education: Paul studied Computer Engineering at New York Institute of Technology in Old Westbury, NY where he graduated in 1983

Career: Paul worked as an information technologist for most of his career for a computer dealer, and then later in a large American insurance company.

Political Views: Paul is centric, he believes that elected officials should work for their votes and, and he will not commit to any party.

Relationships: Paul married Maria Randazzo on 24 of May 1984. They have two Children Lauren, and Dana, and also four Grandchildren Lucas, Gianna, Paul, and Vinny.
