data.title: Network discovery and reconciliation
data.text:
----

Network discovery and reconciliation is a set of operational practices used by telecommunications network operators to keep a network inventory system aligned with the actual physical and logical state of the network it is supposed to describe. [ref: TM Forum. "TMFC045 Resource Discovery and Reconciliation v1.0.0." https://www.tmforum.org/resources/technical-specification/tmfc045-resource-discovery-and-reconciliation-v1-0-0/] In practice this means two things happen in sequence: automated tools collect data directly from network equipment and from the management systems that oversee it, and that data is then compared, record by record, against whatever already exists in the operator's inventory database. [ref: Breitbart, Y., Garofalakis, M., Jai, B., Martin, C., Rastogi, R., Silberschatz, A. "Topology Discovery in Heterogeneous IP Networks." Proc. IEEE INFOCOM, 2000, pp. 265–274. Extended version: "Topology discovery in heterogeneous IP networks: the NetInventory system," IEEE/ACM Transactions on Networking, vol. 12, no. 3, 2004, pp. 401–414. https://doi.org/10.1109/TNET.2004.828963] Where the two disagree, the discrepancy is either corrected automatically or set aside for a person to review, depending on how the operator has configured the process.

The practice exists because large telecommunications networks are rarely static. [ref: TM Forum Inform. "Introducing TM Forum's Autonomous Network Mission: The roadmap to true autonomy in telecom." July 2025. https://inform.tmforum.org/features-and-opinion/introducing-tm-forums-autonomous-network-mission-the-roadmap-to-true-autonomy-in-telecom] A typical operator's network combines equipment from many vendors, mixes physical hardware with virtualized and cloud-hosted functions, and changes continuously as equipment is installed, links are re-patched, and old hardware is retired. Under these conditions, an inventory record maintained only by hand tends to become more inaccurate over time, from what is deployed. [ref: Donnet, B., Friedman, T. "Internet topology discovery: a survey." IEEE Communications Surveys & Tutorials, vol. 9, no. 4, 2007, pp. 56–69. https://doi.org/10.1109/COMST.2007.4444750] Network discovery and reconciliation was developed to close that gap, by treating the network's own reported state, rather than a person's notes about the network, as the source of truth.

The process is applied across most of the domains a modern operator runs, including IP and MPLS networks, optical transport networks, passive optical and DSL access networks, mobile radio access networks, and software-defined wide area networks. [ref: TM Forum. "TIP (Operations Management) Interfaces." https://www.tmforum.org/standards/standarized-interfaces-apis/operations-management-interfaces/] It has also been formalized as a named, standardized function, Resource Discovery and Reconciliation, within TM Forum's Open Digital Architecture, an industry reference architecture used across the telecommunications sector by both network operators and their equipment and software suppliers.

== Background ==

Before automated discovery tools became common, telecommunications operators generally relied on manually maintained inventory databases: engineers recorded what equipment was installed, where it was connected, and how it was configured, and updated those records whenever a change was made in the field. This worked reasonably well while networks were smaller and changed infrequently, but it scales poorly. A large operator's network can span tens of thousands of physical elements across multiple vendors and technology generations, and any of them can be touched during a routine maintenance window, an outage repair, or a planned upgrade. Every one of those changes is an opportunity for the paper or database record to fall out of sync with reality.

The consequences of that inaccuracy are practical, not abstract. Plan a network expansion around a stale inventory record and the numbers can be wrong in either direction: capacity that looks available may already be gone, or capacity that exists may never make it into the plan at all. Fault investigations run into the same wall from the other side, time lost hunting for a piece of equipment the inventory places in one location when it was physically moved months earlier. Neither failure mode is unusual. It's the accumulation of small, ordinary mismatches like these, more than any single dramatic outage, that pushed discovery and reconciliation from a niche tool used by a handful of large operators into a standard part of telecommunications operations generally.

== Historical background ==

The practice grew out of two separate lines of development that only later converged: internet-standard network management protocols on one side, and telecommunications-industry efforts to standardize operational support systems (OSS) on the other.

1988 - The OSI/Network Management Forum is founded by eight companies, including AT&T, British Telecom, and Hewlett-Packard, to address operational management problems in OSI-based networks. It is renamed the TeleManagement Forum in 1998 and TM Forum in 2008; this organization later standardizes the OSS interfaces that discovery-and-reconciliation systems commonly implement. [ref: Embry, J., Manson, P., Milham, D. "An Open Network Management Architecture: OSI/NM Forum Architecture and Concepts." IEEE Network, vol. 4, no. 4, July 1990, pp. 14–22. https://doi.org/10.1109/65.56547; TM Forum. "About Us." https://www.tmforum.org/about/]

1990 - The Internet Engineering Task Force publishes RFC 1157, defining the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP). SNMP becomes the basis for most of the automated network discovery tools that follow. [ref: Internet Engineering Task Force. "RFC 1157: A Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP)." 1990. https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1157]

2000 - 2004 - Breitbart, Garofalakis, Jai, Martin, Rastogi, and Silberschatz present the NetIn -entory system at IEEE INFOCOM in 2000, with an extended version published in IEEE/ACM Transactions on Networking in 2004. It describes algorithms for reconstructing the complete physical topology of a heterogeneous, multi-vendor IP network from the partial address-forwarding data available on individual switches, one of the first rigorous treatments of the discovery problem at network scale.

2005 - The IEEE standardizes the Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP) as IEEE 802.1AB, giving vendors a common, non-proprietary way for directly connected devices to announce themselves to one another. [ref: IEEE Standards Association. "IEEE Standard for Local and Metropolitan Area Networks – Station and Media Access Control Connectivity Discovery (802.1AB-2005)." 2005. https://standards.ieee.org/standard/802_1AB-2005.html]

2007 - Donnet and Friedman publish a survey of internet topology discovery techniques in IEEE Communications Surveys & Tutorials, cataloguing the range of active and passive methods developed up to that point and comparing their accuracy and cost.

2017 - Azodi, Cheng, and Meinel publish REAMS in Wireless Personal Communications, an event-driven, passive approach to topology discovery and inventory listing intended for networks too sensitive for active probing, such as industrial control systems. [ref: Azodi, A., Cheng, F., Meinel, C. "Event Driven Network Topology Discovery and Inventory Listing Using REAMS." Wireless Personal Communications, vol. 94, 2017, pp. 415–430. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11277-015-3061-3]

== How discovery works ==

Discovery is the "data collection half" of the process: gathering information about what equipment exists, how it is configured, and how it is connected. No single method covers every situation, so operators and tool vendors typically combine several.

=== Protocol-based discovery ===

The earliest and still most widely used approach queries network elements using SNMP, reading standard management information base (MIB) tables such as interface tables and address-forwarding tables. Because no individual switch has a complete view of the network it sits in, the NetInventory algorithms combine the partial forwarding-table data collected from many switches into one consistent physical topology, using consistency checks to work around devices that only partially support SNMP or that return incomplete information. Other protocol-based methods draw on the Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) for reachability probing, the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) for mapping IP addresses to hardware addresses, and link-state data taken directly from routing protocols such as OSPF.

=== Link-layer discovery protocols ===

Rather than inferring adjacency indirectly from forwarding tables, some devices announce their own identity and capabilities directly to their neighbors. The IEEE's Link Layer Discovery Protocol and Cisco's proprietary Cisco Discovery Protocol both work this way: each device periodically transmits a frame describing itself, and neighboring devices record what they receive. This produces very accurate immediate-neighbor data, but only for devices that support the protocol, and only for direct physical adjacency rather than the network as a whole. It answers what is connected to this specific port, rather than what the whole network looks like.

=== Management-system-based discovery ===

In telecommunications operations specifically, discovery tools more often query a network management system (NMS) or element management system (EMS) that has already aggregated data from many devices, rather than polling individual elements one at a time. This is done through a range of interface types, including REST APIs, TL1, the Common Object Request Broker Architecture (CORBA), the Multi-Technology Operations Systems Interface (MTOSI), XML-based interfaces, and vendor-specific proprietary protocols. When an NMS is unavailable, or exposes only partial data, discovery tools fall back to querying network elements directly over SNMP or a command-line interface, at the cost of more overhead per element.

=== Passive versus active discovery ===

Most of the methods above are active: they send queries or probes to the network and read the responses. In networks where active probing risks disturbing time-sensitive traffic, such as industrial control systems built on hierarchical, cyber-physical networks, passive methods are used instead, observing management-plane traffic as it naturally occurs rather than generating new traffic to elicit a response. The REAMS system is a documented example of this approach; its authors note that passive methods introduce their own accuracy trade-offs relative to an idealized active mapping process, since they can only see what traffic happens to occur rather than what they choose to ask for.

=== Data normalization ===

Different vendors and technologies describe the same physical reality in different formats, so discovered data is normally translated into a common data model before it can be meaningfully compared against inventory records. TM Forum's Information Framework, better known by its earlier name, the Shared Information/Data model (SID), is the reference data model most widely used for this purpose in telecommunications OSS. [ref: TM Forum. "Information Framework (SID)." https://www.tmforum.org/open-digital-architecture/information-framework-sid/] It defines a common vocabulary and structure for entities such as physical devices, logical resources, and services, independent of any single vendor's data format.

Normalization is what allows a router's SNMP-reported interface table and an optical platform's proprietary configuration export to be represented, and compared, using the same underlying object model, rather than requiring a bespoke comparison for every combination of vendor and technology an operator happens to run.

== How reconciliation works ==

Once discovery data has been normalized, it is compared item by item against the existing inventory records. This comparison tends to surface a few recognizable categories of discrepancy: equipment or connections that are present on the network but absent from the inventory, sometimes described as undocumented or "ghost" assets; inventory records that refer to equipment that has since been removed or replaced; and records whose details, such as a serial number, a port assignment, or a cable route, no longer match what the network reports.

How a discrepancy is handled once it is found is generally a policy decision made by the operator rather than something fixed by the tooling itself. Some categories of discrepancy can be corrected in the inventory system automatically; others are held in a review queue for a person to confirm before any change is committed, particularly where the correction would affect billing or service records downstream. Because a network keeps changing after any given comparison is made, reconciliation is not a one-time event but is run repeatedly, continuously in some deployments and on a fixed schedule in others, with historical snapshots retained so that past and current network states can be compared against each other.

== Standardization ==

TM Forum defines resource discovery and reconciliation as a distinct, named component, TMFC045, within its Open Digital Architecture, a reference architecture adopted by network operators and their equipment and software suppliers. This sits within a broader family of standards TM Forum maintains for OSS and BSS interoperability, including the eTOM business process framework and the Information Framework (SID) data model referenced above; discovery and reconciliation, in this context, is one operational component built to interoperate with the others rather than a standalone specification.

The component is designed to work alongside other ODA-defined interfaces, notably the Product Inventory Management API (TMF637), which standardizes how inventory records are created, retrieved, updated, and queried across a telecommunications operator's products and services. [ref: TM Forum. "TMF637 Product Inventory Management API User Guide, v5.0.0." https://www.tmforum.org/resources/specifications/tmf637-product-inventory-management-api-user-guide-v5-0-0/] Because these are open, vendor-neutral specifications, an operator can in principle combine a discovery tool from one supplier with an inventory system from another, provided both conform to the same TM Forum interfaces.

== Comparison with related network management practices ==

Network discovery and reconciliation overlaps with several adjacent practices without being identical to any of them. Link-layer discovery protocols such as LLDP or CDP establish adjacency between directly connected devices, but they do not, by themselves, compare that information against a separate inventory record; reconciliation is a further step applied on top of whatever discovery method supplies the raw data, and a network can run LLDP everywhere without ever reconciling the results against an inventory system at all.

It is also distinct from fault and performance monitoring, even though the two are easy to lump together. Monitoring evaluates the operational health of network elements that a management system already knows about: is this port up? Is this link congested? Has this device stopped responding? Discovery and reconciliation asks a more basic question first, one that has to be answered before any of those make sense: what exists on the network, and does the inventory's record of it still hold? A device can be perfectly healthy and fully monitored while still being completely undocumented in the inventory system. That gap, invisible to monitoring by definition, is exactly what discovery and reconciliation is built to catch.

Compared with periodic manual network audits, an automated process can run far more frequently, which shortens the window during which inventory records may be wrong. A manual audit conducted once a year, however thorough, still leaves the inventory exposed to drift for the months in between; a continuously or frequently scheduled reconciliation process narrows that exposure considerably, at the cost of the engineering effort needed to build and maintain the automation in the first place.

== Role in network operations ==

The output of discovery and reconciliation is generally consumed by other OSS and business support system (BSS) processes rather than being an end in itself. An inventory known to be reconciled against the live network is used as an input to network planning and design, so that engineers do not need to separately verify live network status before planning changes, and to service orchestration and fulfilment workflows, so that provisioning a new service can rely on an accurate map of available resources rather than an assumed one.

Because it produces a synchronized, queryable record of the network, it can also reduce how often planners and engineers need direct, live access to network equipment for the sole purpose of checking its current configuration, since the same information is available through the inventory system instead.

== Technical challenges ==

Two problems keep showing up across the literature and standards on this topic, and neither has a clean fix. The first is heterogeneity. Vendors implement management interfaces differently enough that operators and tool vendors end up maintaining a small zoo of adapters, separate handling for REST, CORBA, SNMP, and whatever proprietary interface a given vendor happens to ship, just to cover a realistic multi-vendor network. The second is incompleteness: older or lower-tier management systems often expose only partial data about the equipment underneath them. This is the specific gap the NetInventory stitching algorithms and passive methods such as REAMS were built to work around, and it's worth being clear that neither approach solves it outright, they narrow the gap rather than close it.

== Ron Lynch ==
Known professionally as Ron Lynch, Ronald Eugene Lynch II (born 1966) is an American direct response marketer, advertising professional, author, filmmaker, actor, entrepreneur and founder of faith based and non-profit organizations. [ref: https://baconwrappedbusiness.com/ron-lynch/] [ref: https://www.newswire.ca/news-releases/tut-fitness-group-expands-strategic-advisory-board-864862148.html] [ref: https://smwatx.com/speakers/ron-lynch/] [ref: https://lifestyleinvestor.com/ron-lynch/] [ref: https://miraclemorning.com/ron-lynch/] [ref: https://conversionengineering.co/lessons-learned-from-the-marketing-mercenary/] [ref: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0ufMEbSO8WI]

=== Intellihelp ===
Lynch founded Intellihelp during the COVID-19 pandemic. [ref: Want to help your neighbor during COVID-19? Here’s how] Intellihelp is a peer-to-peer crisis relief initiative that was created to connect people facing food shortages and hardships with basic needs. Intellihelp's sourced nearby volunteers willing to help those in need.

As global shutdowns began in March 2020 and unemployment and food supply shortages began to rise [ref: WHO Director-General's opening remarks at the media briefing on COVID-19 - 11 March 2020, www.who.int], many households were left without reliable access to food and basic necessities. [ref: ] Intellihelp connected those in need with volunteers who could respond with food, delivery assistance, hygiene products, diapers, baby formula, over-the-counter supplies, transportation, and other urgent care needs. [ref: Seattle native's Facebook group matches volunteers to thousands in need, Seattle Refined]

Intellihelp was built to move quickly enough to meet immediate urgent needs by allowing direct exchanges between the people in need, and the people able to provide help, while protecting the dignity of those asking for help.

Intellihelp's initiative grew beyond its original municipal scale and became associated with broader crisis assistance, utilizing volunteer-based help during the pandemic.

== Filmmaking ==
Ron was the director and producer of the documentary film  Polé Polé. The film followed Rebecca Dufek's Mount Kilimanjaro climb, which Lynch became involved in after Dufek's husband visited Cesari Direct’s studios to make a commercial. [ref: The Slow Walk: Redmond Woman Takes on Illness One Step At a Time, Redmond, WA Patch]

== Marketing ==
At a marketing event in Austin, Texas, the In Business Madison columnist described Lynch as someone who helped in the building of the GoPro brand. [ref: The mindset of millionaires]

== Books ==

data.title: Vercaa
data.text:
----

Vercaa is a web hosting provider offering general web hosting, cloud hosting, WordPress hosting and managed WordPress hosting. Its related services include domain registration and transfers, business email, website backup, monitoring and cybersecurity. As of October 2026, the company advertises 16 cloud-hosting plans with RAM allowances ranging from 1 GB to 16 GB per hosting account, managed through cPanel. [ref: Vercaa — Web Hosting, Domain Search & Website Security, Vercaa] [ref: Hosting Features: cPanel, Security and Domains, Vercaa]

== Products and services ==

=== Web and cloud hosting ===

Vercaa's general web hosting uses cPanel for account management and includes SSL certificates and Imunify360 malware and firewall protection. The company advertises support for PHP, Python and Node.js applications. Its hosting catalogue distinguishes plans by their RAM allowance, storage allocation and number of permitted websites. [ref: Web Hosting, Vercaa]

Its cloud-hosting line retains the cPanel account model while offering a wider range of resources. The 16 advertised plans span RAM allowances from 1 GB to 16 GB, increasing in 1 GB steps. The largest listed allowance is 16 GB for an individual hosting account. Customers manage their websites through that account without taking on administration of a standalone VPS or dedicated server. The figure refers to the account's RAM allowance, rather than the total physical memory of an underlying server. [ref: Cloud Hosting with cPanel and Imunify360, Vercaa]

=== Application hosting ===

The company also markets hosting for Laravel, Node.js and Python applications. These offerings use the same plans and pricing as its Cloud Hosting line. The Laravel service describes support for Composer and Artisan commands; the Node.js service lists npm, process management and WebSockets; and the Python service lists pip, virtual environments and WSGI or ASGI applications, including frameworks such as Django and Flask. [ref: Laravel Hosting, Vercaa] [ref: Node.js Hosting, Vercaa] [ref: Python Hosting, Vercaa]

=== WordPress hosting ===

Vercaa's WordPress services include installation and site-management tools. Its client-area WordPress panel provides interfaces for plugins, themes, backups, staging, security and updates. The company describes tools for creating a staging copy, managing installed components and checking a site's maintenance status. These functions are presented within the customer dashboard alongside access to cPanel. [ref: WordPress Hosting, Vercaa]

Managed WordPress adds scheduled core and plugin updates, daily backups and priority support. This service places recurring WordPress maintenance with the provider while leaving customers access to their site's themes and plugins. A migration tool transfers an existing WordPress installation's database and files through an exporter and importer, with progress displayed in the client area. [ref: Managed WordPress Hosting with Daily Backups, Vercaa]

=== Domains and related services ===

Vercaa provides domain registration, renewal and transfer services through ConnectReseller, identified in its terms as its registrar partner. Its website offers domain-availability searches and transfer initiation. DNS management, email forwarding and WHOIS or ID protection are available for supported extensions. Customers can manage domains alongside hosting services through the company's account platform. Available features and transfer requirements depend on the relevant extension and registry. [ref: Terms of Service for Hosting, Domains and Add-ons, Vercaa] [ref: Domain Registration Policy: Renewals and Transfers, Vercaa] [ref: Domains, Vercaa]

=== Website security, certificates and backup ===

Alongside protection included with hosting, Vercaa resells SiteLock website-security products. The advertised options cover malware scanning, cleanup, firewall protection and content delivery, with inclusions varying by plan. Its certificate catalogue includes domain-validation, organization-validation, extended-validation and wildcard SSL certificates issued by external certificate authorities. The company also resells NordVPN subscriptions for private network access. [ref: Website Security with Malware Scanning and Removal, Vercaa] [ref: SSL Certificates, Vercaa] [ref: VPN, Vercaa]

Website and database backup is offered through CodeGuard. The service includes automated daily backups stored separately from the hosting account, file-change alerts and restoration of individual files or an entire website. Its advertised features also include testing a backup in a staging environment before restoring it. Backup capacity varies by the selected storage tier. [ref: CodeGuard Backup, Vercaa]

=== Business email and email security ===

Vercaa's business email service uses OX App Suite for mailboxes on a customer's own domain. It combines webmail with calendars, contacts, tasks and access from desktop or mobile email clients. A Productivity option adds OX Drive file storage and browser-based document, spreadsheet and presentation tools. A migration facility supports moving existing email into the service. [ref: Professional Email Hosting with OX App Suite, Vercaa]

SpamExperts is offered separately for incoming and outgoing email filtering. Incoming filtering screens messages addressed to a domain, while outgoing filtering monitors mail sent from it. Available bundles add searchable, encrypted email archiving to one or both filtering directions. The service includes quarantine and log-search interfaces for reviewing messages caught by the filters. [ref: Email Security and Spam Filtering with SpamExperts, Vercaa]

=== Monitoring ===

Vercaa resells 360 Monitoring for websites, servers and SSL certificates. Its advertised checks cover availability, response times, certificate expiration, page keywords and network ports. Server monitoring tracks resource use, including CPU, memory, disk and network activity. Alerting options notify customers when a configured check detects a problem. This customer monitoring product is separate from Vercaa's own public service-status page. [ref: Website and Server Monitoring with 360 Monitoring, Vercaa] [ref: System Status, Vercaa]

=== Customer support and account management ===

Vercaa provides a client area for managing services, orders, invoices and support requests. Its public Help Center contains tutorials covering hosting administration, cPanel, WordPress and application-related topics. The company also publishes an operational-status page and incident history. That page records the provider's own service-status reporting. [ref: Knowledgebase, Vercaa]

== Cyber security ==

Vercaa advertises a cyber security division covering assessment, recovery and ongoing protection for websites and systems. Its services are grouped into three areas. [ref: Enterprise Cyber Security Services, Vercaa]

* Security audits and penetration testing: automated vulnerability scanning and manual testing aligned with OWASP web-application risks. The advertised scope includes access control, authentication, security configuration, injection vulnerabilities and outdated software dependencies. Deliverables include findings with severity, impact, evidence and remediation guidance, followed by fixes or assistance with remediation and retesting. [ref: Security Audit & Penetration Testing, Vercaa]
* Hacked-website recovery and incident response: investigation and containment of a compromise, removal of malware and backdoors, identification of the entry point, patching and measures to harden the affected site. The process also includes review requests to services such as Google Safe Browsing when a cleaned website remains flagged. Those external services control the timing and outcome of delisting. [ref: Hacked Website Recovery & Incident Response, Vercaa]
* Annual managed protection: a yearly contract combining continuous security monitoring, management of a web application firewall, quarterly vulnerability re-audits, patch coordination and an incident-response retainer. A dedicated security manager provides a point of contact and reporting. Major infrastructure migrations, extensive forensic investigations and formal certification work are scoped separately from the standard contract. [ref: Managed Protection — Yearly Cyber Security Contract, Vercaa]

The company's compliance material describes alignment with frameworks including ISO/IEC 27001 and PCI DSS, alongside regional security and data-protection requirements. It expressly distinguishes this methodological alignment from holding formal third-party certification. [ref: Compliance & Standards — Vercaa Cyber Security, Vercaa]

== Reception ==

A Website Planet review by Caitlin Greyling, first published on 4 March 2024, examined account creation, website setup, features, support and performance. Greyling praised the assistance provided by support staff but reported slower loading speeds outside Europe. These findings concern the service and configuration tested for that review. Some specifications in the review differ from Vercaa's current catalogue, including the RAM range. Website Planet discloses affiliate links and says commercial agreements are considered in its vendor rankings. [ref: Vercaa Hosting Review [2026]: Is It Worth Your Money?, Website Planet]

data.title: Larivaar
data.text:
Larivaar () is the traditional style of writing the Gurmukhi script in which words are written continuously, without spaces between them. It is a form of scriptio continua. Larivaar was the standard form of Sikh scriptural manuscripts, including handwritten copies of the Guru Granth Sahib, and of the scripture's early printed editions. The contrasting style, in which words are separated by spaces, is called pad chhed (). Printed editions of the Guru Granth Sahib switched to word-separated text in the early 1970s, a change that met strong opposition before it was accepted. Some Sikhs continue to learn to read scripture in larivaar.

== Characteristics ==
In larivaar text, letters run on continuously, and whitespace is used only to separate a heading from the text beneath it. Verses are divided by the double danda (॥), and it is left to the reader to work out where one word ends and the next begins. Word boundaries are therefore not marked on the page and are realised only when the text is read aloud.

In historical larivaar manuscripts, the double danda was not written as a free-standing pair of strokes. Its first stroke was joined to the last letter of the preceding verse, and, if another verse followed in the same block of text, its second stroke was joined to the first letter of that verse. According to a 2020 proposal to the Unicode Consortium, this way of writing the double danda disappeared with the introduction of lithography and the printing press in India.

The opening verse of the Guru Granth Sahib, the Mul Mantar, illustrates the difference between the two styles:

{| class="wikitable"
! Style !! Text
|-
| Larivaar ||
|-
| Pad chhed ||
|}

== History ==

=== Printed editions ===
The first printed edition of the Adi Granth appeared in 1865. Single-volume printed editions continued the manuscript tradition of writing words without breaks between them. In the early twentieth century, the printed text was collated against the Kartarpur Pothi, a process that lasted several decades and culminated in the standard 1,430-page edition published by the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) in 1951.

=== Transition to pad chhed ===
According to the historian Gurinder Singh Mann, the connected style of writing was given up in printed editions of the Guru Granth Sahib in the early 1970s. The change was strongly opposed, and some critics saw it as "tearing apart the body of the Guru". Supporters of the change argued that separating the words would make the text easier to read for those not trained in reading continuous script, and would help readers make the correct breaks between words. After a period of controversy, the word-separated text was accepted, and it is now the version in use in Sikh homes and gurdwaras around the world, retaining the standard pagination of 1,430 pages.

== Reading and study ==
Because word divisions are not indicated, reading larivaar requires the reader to determine where each word begins and ends. Instruction in the correct reading and pronunciation of Gurbani is known as santhiya. Writing in 2020, the authors of a Unicode proposal stated that many Sikhs studying the scriptures were learning to read them in larivaar.

== Digital encoding ==
Larivaar text can be represented in Unicode by omitting spaces between words, or by using the zero-width space. In a 2020 proposal to the Unicode Consortium, Manvir Singh and Irvanjit Singh argued that standard fonts rendered the double danda incorrectly in larivaar text, because they display it as two detached strokes rather than joining it to the adjacent letters as in historical manuscripts. They described the detached form as a departure from the written tradition and as an example of Western or British influence on the script. They proposed either encoding new Gurmukhi double danda characters at reserved code points (U+0A64 and U+0A65) or adding guidance on contextual rendering to the Unicode Standard.

* Santhiya

data.title: Frederick Louis Pache
data.text:
Frederick Louis Pache (9 May 1871 - 19 March 1910) was an Ocularist and heir of the prominent and award winning family firm Pache & Son [ref: The Ophthalmic Review, [Volume XII, Page 4], November 1893], which provided major UK hospitals with artificial glass eyes as well as the perfected Snellen "Reformed Eye". [ref: https://eyemuseum.ranzco.edu/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/History_V4_2.pdf ] [ref: {{Cite web|url=https://www.college-optometrists.org/professional-development/college-journals/acuity/all-issues/summer-2025/an-art-and-a-science] [ref: A short history of the artificial eye by H.E Henkes & G K Van Leersum]

==Early Life==
Frederick was born in Birmingham in 1871, and the son of pioneering Ocularist Thomas Pache, during the city's booming industrial era. He was of Swiss-Huguenot ancestry, descending from an old historic bourgeoisie family of Morges in the Canton of Vaud, Switzerland. The family having ancestral records dating back centuries involving local artisans, merchants, and businessmen. [ref: {{Cite web|url=https://www.pastellists.com/Articles/Pache.pdf}] [ref: https://www.pastellists.com/Genealogies/Pache.pdf ]

His Grandfather Charles Lewis Pache, patriarch of the family, was the first to start the family business of Glassblowing during the late 1840's, specialising in artificial glass eyes, as well as Syringes, test tubes, foreign bird skins and insects. [ref: https://uncletomstales.com/a-virtual-tour-of-the-back-to-backs/a-virtual-tour-of-the-back-to-backs-part-25/] [ref: Slater's Business Directory for Birmingham 1852] He was also related to Charles Henry-Pache, his great-great Uncle, who was a famous Pastellist and supplier to the Royal Society of Arts.

As heir to the company Pache & Son, Frederick started working for the family firm when he was around 18 years old, learning the complex craftsmanship and skills involved in manufacturing and creating artificial glass eyes. [ref: The National Archives of the UK (TNA); Kew, Surrey, England; Census Returns of England and Wales, 1891; Class: RG12; Piece: 2408; Folio: 57; Page: 19; GSU roll: 6097518] [ref: The London Medical Record; Volume XII; Smith Elder & Co.; 15 Waterloo Place; 1884]

During the 1890's the family business had consolidated it's position as one of the countries leading artificial glass eye makers, and by 1900 had a complete monopoly in providing them to all major hospitals in the UK. This was mainly thanks to the quality manufacturing of their eyes and artistic details, as well as his father Thomas perfecting Snellen's "Reformed Eye" using English Glass, which at the time was considered extremely hard to achieve. [ref: Prosthetic Body Parts in Literature and Culture, 1832 to 1908 - Ryan Craig Sweet to the University of Exeter as a thesis for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy in English] [ref: http://ndl.ethernet.edu.et/bitstream/123456789/12586/1/H.E.%20Henkes%20%282%29.pdf - History of Ophthalmology by H.E Henkes (Page 353)]

By this time, the firm had upwards of 4,000 eyes in stock and ready to be delivered to any of their principal hospitals. They created glass eyes in various colours, sizes, and even morbid conditions. Due to their exquisite design and detail, they even supplied models to universities so that the various examples of diseases and conditions of the eye could be examined by the students. [ref: The American Journal of Photography 1892 titled "ARTIFICIAL HUMAN EYES"] [ref: Showell's Dictionary of Birmingham, by Walter Showell.]

==Death==
It was between 1908 to 1910 that Frederick contracted Pulmonary Tuberculosis, commonly known as Phthisis during this era. This was probably the result of living and working in the densely populated urban areas of Birmingham, where this disease spread rapidly. [ref: Birmingham, England, All Saints Hospital Records, 1845-1931]

This lead to his rapid decline in mental and physical health during the next two years, being susceptible to bouts of delusion and aggression as his condition worsened, unfortunately resulting in a break-down of his marriage to Edith. [ref: Library of Birmingham, Birmingham City Council; Birmingham, England, UK; Court records: Quarter and Petty sessions; Reference: PS B/1/1/4/9]

It was in early 1910 that he had become profoundly emancipated, bedridden, and suffering from delusional insanity as a result of late-stage tuberculosis. It was because of this he was administered to the All Saints Hospital (Winson Green Asylum) on the 10th March 1910. However, he only survived for a further 9 days and passed away on the 19th March, aged only 38 years old. [ref: Library of Birmingham; Birmingham, England, UK; All Saints Hospital Records, 1845-1920; Reference Number: HC AS/10/1; Finding Number: MS 344/10/1]

Once Frederick had passed away, Thomas disinherited Frederick's family from the company fortune, because of him disapproving of his marriage to a "commoner", leaving Edith widowed with 6 children. However, Frederick's children eventually all received a sizable inheritance from their Aunt Ella Pache, who had taken over the company for a time after Thomas' death in 1918 until it ceased to exist sometime in the 1940's. [ref: Probate Record; 10 May 1919; Birmingham; and, hardcopy photocopy of Thomas Pache will.] [ref: Probate Record; Birmingham; 24 May 1930; to Ella Beatrice Grimson, widow; Effects £528 2s 8d.]

== References ==

data.title: Richard Mund
data.text:
RICHARD MUND POTTERY
Richard Mund is a Canadian ceramic artist and production potter based in Neustadt, Ontario. He is known for functional pottery designed for everyday use, including stoneware vessels and decorated ceramics.
== Biography ==
Mund studied ceramics at Georgian College in Barrie, Ontario, where he took electives with ceramic artist Roger Kerslake. He began working full-time with clay in 1994 while apprenticing at Cunningham Pottery in Des Moines, Iowa. He subsequently earned a Bachelor of Fine Arts degree from the Nova Scotia College of Art and Design (NSCAD University) in Halifax, where he studied ceramics, including wheel throwing, mould making and maiolica surface decoration. [ref: Artist Profile: Richard Mund, Grey-Bruce Boomers]
After working as a ceramics technician, production potter and continuing education instructor, Mund established his own pottery studio in Neustadt in 1997. [ref: About, Richard Mund Pottery]
Artistic practice
Mund's work focuses on functional pottery intended for domestic use. His approach combines simple forms with attention to weight, ergonomics, surface decoration and the relationship between form and finish. His work draws on historical pottery traditions while incorporating contemporary design ideas. [ref: Richard Mund, Owen Sound Artists' Co-op]
His work includes wheel-thrown stoneware, decorated ceramics using maiolica glazing techniques, and practical objects for the home and garden. His product designs have included flower holders made to fit standard Mason jars. [ref: Gallery of Images, Richard Mund Pottery]
=Exhibitions and events
In 2025, Mund was named the featured artist at the Hamilton Potters Guild's fall sale in Dundas, Ontario. The event brought together more than 100 potters and included the guild's annual Empty Bowl fundraiser for Hamilton Food Share. [ref: Hamilton Potters Guild Fall Sale returns, DundasToday]

Mund also participates in the Autumn Leaves Studio Tour, an annual event featuring artists and studios in Grey and Bruce counties, Ontario. [ref: Richard Mund, Autumn Leaves Studio Tour]

data.title: Indoor Skydancing
data.text:
Indoor skydancing is the performing art of choreographed bodyflight to music within a vertical wind tunnel, as well as a specific musical format within the sport of indoor skydiving. [ref: Indoor Skydancing: The Big Bang!, SkydiveMag] Rather than existing as a standalone sport with its own governing body, skydancing refers specifically to the artistic free routines where solo or group athletes—such as those in freestyle or dynamic disciplines—synchronize their aerial maneuvers to musical accompaniment. [ref: Indoor Solo Freestyle Competition Rules - 2025 Edition, Fédération Aéronautique Internationale (FAI)] The term was coined by Mexican-Canadian competitor Lise Hernandez Girouard as a tribute to outdoor freestyle pioneer Deanna Kent, who was widely known as "Skydancer". [ref: Deana Kent "Skydancer", International Skydiving Museum Hall of Fame]

== History ==
=== Acoustic challenges and hardware integration ===
Before the integration of music, competitive indoor freestyle vertical wind tunnel (historically referred to as "Neo-Freestyle") was evaluated strictly on technical body positions, speed, and acrobatic maneuvers. [ref: Neo-freestyle competition at iFLY Hollywood, Extreme66] A primary barrier to incorporating music was the acoustic environment of vertical wind tunnels, which generate background noise exceeding 100 decibels at airspeeds over 200 km/h. [ref: Catching up with Lise Hernandez, SkydiveMag] Standard audio playback was inaudible to athletes, and extended exposure to such noise requires hearing protection.

To solve this, Hernandez Girouard developed a technical setup utilizing custom-moulded ear seals with integrated monitors, earmuffs, and a modified flight helmet. She also implemented a wireless multi-channel distribution system that transmitted the audio directly to the athlete's in-ear monitors, the on-site spectators, and the live broadcast feed simultaneously. The equipment was first successfully tested at the Aerokart wind tunnel in France in 2013. [ref: Lise Hernandez pionnière pour faire des figures au rythme d'une musique, Actu.fr]

=== Early performances and FAI rule updates (2014–2015) ===
The first public performance of indoor freestyle synchronized with live music occurred on March 23, 2014, during the 2nd Canadian Indoor Skydiving Championships at SkyVenture Montreal, where Hernandez Girouard competed in the Freestyle category. [ref: Music is in the Air, CanPara Magazine] In November 2014, she demonstrated the musical format internationally at the 1st Fédération Aéronautique Internationale (FAI) World Cup of Indoor Skydiving in Austin, Texas, acting as the only competitor using musical accompaniment. [ref: 1st World Cup in Indoor Skydiving - Day 2, FAI]

Prompted by these proof-of-concept performances, the FAI officially updated its global competitive regulations to permit music as an optional element in freestyle routines. However, at the inaugural FAI World Indoor Skydiving Championships held in Prague the following year in 2015, the option remained unused, and no freestyle competitors performed their routines to music.

=== The 2016 Wind Games ===
The integration of music gained significant global traction at the third edition of the Wind Games in January 2016 in Empuriabrava, Spain. Anne Maxwell, creator of the Wind Games, invited Hernandez Girouard to organize the event's first freestyle competition and mandated that it include a compulsory musical interpretation round.

Hernandez Girouard authored the new scoring criteria and served as Head Judge. The format required athletes to perform three rounds: low-speed flow, high-speed flight, and a mandatory musical interpretation round. To score the musical round fairly across both technical flight mechanics and choreographic expression, the judging panel was hybridized to include technical freeflyer Adam Mattacola, professional dance choreographer Dolo Yglesias, and Hernandez Girouard.

The 2016 musical routines achieved unprecedented viral publicity for the sport. Russian athlete Leonid Volkov won first place with a highly theatrical routine, while Polish athlete Maja Kuczyńska won second place. [ref: Wind Games winner will blow you away with astounding aerial dance moves, Today] [ref: Watch: Athlete dances in a wind tunnel, defies gravity, NBC News]. Volkov's routine went immediately viral, grabbing the media's attention. [ref: Watch: Athlete dances in a wind tunnel, defies gravity] A video of Kuczyńska's performance set to the song "Chandelier" amassed over 100 million views on social media, directly leading to her becoming the first indoor skydiving athlete sponsored by Red Bull, which subsequently became the primary title sponsor for the Wind Games. [ref: Maja Kuczyńska - Red Bull Athlete Profile, Red Bull] [ref: The Return of the Wind Games!, SkydiveMag]

== Formats and disciplines ==
Following the popularization of the musical round, indoor skydancing developed into two distinct branches: standardized competitive disciplines and theatrical performing arts exhibitions.

=== Competitive branches ===
In sanctioned indoor skydiving competitions, the musical format is integrated into specific artistic events, heavily weighting technical flow, artistic superiority, and synchronization:
* Solo Freestyle: Competitors perform compulsory routines (without music) and free routines (where music is an optional but heavily utilized element to score artistic points).
* Pairs / Dance Couples: A codified partner format introduced for national competitions, such as by the Russian Sports Federation in 2024. [ref: New discipline of indoor skydiving (Russian Championship 2024) DANCE COUPLES, YouTube]
* Dynamic Free Rounds: Teams of two or four flyers have 60 to 90 seconds to showcase original, synchronized choreography, frequently flown to music.

=== Theatrical exhibitions ===
Separate from scored competitive sports, indoor skydancing is utilized as a purely theatrical performance art. These exhibitions throw out competitive rulebooks to focus on entertainment, allowing for the use of theatrical costumes, specialized lighting, and complex production elements. In 2017, a 30-minute opening show at the Weembi wind tunnel pioneered the integration of wind tunnel flyers with floor dancers and synchronized lighting outside the chamber. [ref: Soirée WEEMBI, Indoor Skydiving Source] Other notable developments in this branch include the launch of "The Space Theater" in Moscow in 2017 and various high-profile international showcases such as "Three Dragons of My Soul." [ref: The Russian Space Theater, Youtube]

Paul F La Franca (born 15 August 1959) is an Information Technology Engineer and Author of children books. Paul loves to travel, and play soccer with his friends.

Born in Villabate, a small town near Palermo, Paul emigrated with his mother Caterina, father Giuseppe, and sister Patricia on October 10, 1972 to search for a better life. He has been blessed with a family, a career, and his love for travel. His latest accomplishment is the publishing of his book Coconut’s Amazing Adventures.

Education: Paul studied Computer Engineering at New York Institute of Technology in Old Westbury, NY where he graduated in 1983

Career: Paul worked as an information technologist for most of his career for a computer dealer, and then later in a large American insurance company.

Political Views: Paul is centric, he believes that elected officials should work for their votes and he will not commit to any party.

Relationships: Paul married Maria Randazzo on the 27th of May 1984. They have two Children Lauren, and Dana, and four grandchildren Lucas, Gianna, Paul, and Vinny.

data.title: Lauren Caster
data.text:
Lauren Caster is a filmmaker and actress who wrote, directed, and starred in Rhythm Is a Dancer. Her work also includes the story concept for the Lifetime television film You're Not Supposed to Be Here. [ref: ] [ref: How an Isolated Camping Trip Inspired Lifetime Lesbian Thriller ‘You’re Not Supposed to Be Here’, TheWrap]

== Career ==
Caster's debut short film, Donor Baby, was acquired by Amazon. She subsequently made the short film Plan C.

In 2021, Caster won the inaugural PitchFest for Emerging Female Filmmakers, presented by WrapWomen and Lifetime, with You're Not Supposed to Be Here. The prize included a development deal with Lifetime. [ref: WrapWomen and Lifetime Name Winner of PitchFest for Emerging Female Filmmakers, TheWrap] The concept became a television film written by Erica Lane and directed by Nicole L. Thompson, which premiered on Lifetime on November 4, 2023.

In 2022, Caster earned a Grand Jury Honorable Mention for Bold and Honest Filmmaking for Plan C at the Utah Arts Festival's Fear No Film program. [ref: Focus on two independent short films with Utah significance: Arthur Veenema’s The Atomic Spawn and Lauren Caster’s Plan C, The Utah Review]

Caster made her feature directorial debut with Rhythm Is a Dancer, in which she plays Ro, a dancer who returns home to meet her biological father. The cast includes Amy Aquino and Tate Donovan. [ref: Austin Film Fest 2025 Interview: Lauren Caster, Amy Aquino, Tate Donovan and Marianne Mullerleile on Finding a Real Groove Together in “Rhythm is a Dancer”, The Moveable Fest] The film had its world premiere in competition at the Austin Film Festival in 2025. [ref: Austin Film Festival Debuts First Wave of Films and 2025 Writer’s Writer Award, Austin Film Festival] Its story was loosely inspired by Caster's experience of meeting her biological father.

In November 2025, the film was presented at the American Film Market to seek international sales representation and distribution. [ref: Austin Film Festival Hit ‘Rhythm Is a Dancer’ Heads to American Film Market for Worldwide Sales (EXCLUSIVE), Variety] It was subsequently released in the United States by Circle Collective, an imprint of Utopia, in July 2026. [ref: Exclusive Trailer for Rhythm Is a Dancer Finds Lauren Caster Making a Family Discovery, The Film Stage]

In September 2026, following the film’s limited theatrical release and availability on video on demand, Caster began a 30-day Instagram video diary campaign to find an audience for the film. Jim Hemphill reported in IndieWire that her first video received approximately 130,000 views and was shared by actors Vincent D’Onofrio and Juliette Lewis. [ref: Filmmaker Lauren Caster Is Spending 30 Days on the Internet Convincing People to Watch Her Indie, IndieWire]

data.title: Cayosoft
data.text:
Cayosoft is a privately held software company based in the Columbus, Ohio, area. The company develops software for administering, monitoring, and recovering Microsoft identity environments, including Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft 365, Exchange, Microsoft Teams, and Intune. [ref: Cayosoft Inc. transaction profile, KPMG Corporate Finance] [ref: Cayosoft company profile, CB Insights]

== History ==
Cayosoft was founded in 2013 by Robert Bobel and Andrey Polevoy, who had previously worked in identity and systems-management software. The company was established to develop administration and automation software for organizations operating Microsoft directory services across on-premises and cloud environments. [ref: Cayosoft company profile, PitchBook] [ref: An Interview With Robert Bobel, CEO & Founder Of Cayosoft, Tech Company News]

The company’s initial products focused on automating user, group, and Microsoft 365 administration in hybrid Active Directory environments. It later added change auditing, rollback, threat detection, and recovery capabilities, broadening its focus from routine administration to identity security and operational resilience. [ref: Cayosoft company profile, CB Insights]

In November 2021, Cayosoft launched Guardian Forest Recovery, extending its Guardian product with automated recovery for Active Directory objects, domain controllers, and forests. The product used continuous change monitoring and a standby recovery environment to reduce the time required to restore directory services after corruption, operational errors, or cyberattacks. [ref: Cayosoft Launches Innovative, All-In-One Active Directory Recovery Software, Cayosoft Guardian Forest Recovery, PR Newswire]

In March 2024, Cayosoft received a $22.5 million minority investment from Centana Growth Partners. The company said the financing would support product development, sales and marketing, and international expansion. [ref: Cayosoft Raises $22.5M in Funding, FinSMEs] [ref: Cayosoft attracts $22.5m from Centana Growth Partners, FinTech Global] In September 2024, the company announced that it had received a United States patent covering its directory-service backup and recovery technology. [ref: Cayosoft Wins Patent for Revolutionary Instant Active Directory Recovery Solution, AI-TechPark]

In February 2025, Cayosoft acquired the Petri IT Knowledgebase, a technology publication founded in 1999 that covers Microsoft enterprise products and related IT topics. Petri Media LLC was established as an independent subsidiary, and Petri stated that it would retain editorial independence. [ref: Cayosoft acquires the Petri IT Knowledgebase, Cayosoft] [ref: About Petri.com, Petri IT Knowledgebase]

== Products ==

=== Cayosoft Administrator ===
Cayosoft Administrator automates identity lifecycle tasks and delegated administration across hybrid Microsoft environments. Its functions include user and group administration, provisioning and deprovisioning, Microsoft 365 license management, policy enforcement, reporting, and auditing. [ref: Cayosoft Administrator, Microsoft Marketplace]

=== Cayosoft Guardian ===
Cayosoft Guardian provides identity-change monitoring, audit history, threat detection, rollback, and recovery. The product includes tools for restoring objects and attributes and recovering an Active Directory forest through a preconfigured standby environment. The standby recovery is called Cayosoft Guardian Instant Forest Recovery and it is the first and only patent for standby active directory recovery [ref: Cayosoft Guardian, Microsoft Marketplace] [ref: Forest Recovery Overview, Cayosoft Support] [ref: Intellectual Property, Cayosoft]

== Patents ==
Cayosoft is the assignee of United States patents covering directory-service recovery and administrative-unit management. U.S. Patent Nos. 12,093,141, 12,399,791, and 12,743,349, granted between September 2024 and September 2026, are related patents in a continuation family titled “Systems and methods for directory service backup and recovery.” They describe maintaining a standby directory service that can be implemented when a host directory service is interrupted. U.S. Patent No. 12,254,107, granted in March 2025, is titled “Orchestration of administrative unit management” and covers methods for evaluating and implementing directory-object membership changes across administrative units. [ref: Patents Assigned to Cayosoft, Inc., Justia Patents]

== Gartner research mentions ==
Since 2024, Cayosoft has appeared in Gartner research concerning Microsoft identity administration, governance, backup, rollback, and recovery. Inclusion in Gartner research does not constitute an endorsement, ranking, or product recommendation.

=== 2024 ===

* Address Top IAM Hygiene Issues to Enhance Security and Reduce Risk (10 December 2024), which discussed specialized management tools for Active Directory Domain Services and Microsoft Entra ID. [ref: Address Top IAM Hygiene Issues to Enhance Security and Reduce Risk, Gartner]

=== 2025 ===

* A Well-Run Active Directory Requires Strong Identity Controls (8 May 2025), concerning specialized Active Directory management and backup tools. [ref: A Well-Run Active Directory Requires Strong Identity Controls, Gartner]

=== 2026 ===

data.title: Iê Bentes Fernandez
data.text:
----

Iê Bentes Fernandez, also known as Iê Regina Bentes Fernandez, is a Brazilian physician specializing in hematology, hemotherapy, and transfusion medicine. Her professional activities include hospital transfusion services, medical research, institutional management, and the implementation of Patient Blood Management (PBM) programs in Brazil. [ref: Hospital de Clínicas reúne especialistas para discutir cuidado com o sangue, Agência Pará]

== Education and medical training ==

Fernandez graduated in medicine from the Federal University of Pará (UFPA) in 1996. She completed her residency in internal medicine at Hospital Universitário João de Barros Barreto in 2000 and her residency in hematology and hemotherapy at Hospital Universitário Professor Edgard Santos in 2002.

In 2022, she obtained a master's degree from the Federal University of Pará in the graduate program Health, Environment and Society in the Amazon. Her academic work addressed the rational use of blood components in high-complexity hospitals in the metropolitan region of Belém. [ref: Iê Regina Bentes Fernandez, Escavador]

== Medical career and institutional leadership ==

Fernandez has worked in hematology and hemotherapy services in the Brazilian state of Pará, including public hospitals and specialized transfusion services.

At the Fundação Hospital de Clínicas Gaspar Vianna (FHCGV), in Belém, she held responsibilities in hemotherapy and transfusion medicine and participated in institutional initiatives concerning transfusion safety and the rational use of blood components.

In 2024, the institution officially launched its Patient Blood Management program, following approximately two years of multidisciplinary preparation. Fernandez was among the physicians involved in its development and implementation. [ref: Hospital de Clínicas Gaspar Vianna lança programa inovador de Manejo do Sangue do Paciente, Agência Pará]

In September 2026, Agência Pará identified Fernandez as the hospital's hemotherapy coordinator and as responsible for the implementation of PBM. She also presided over the International Conference on Hemotherapy and Patient Blood Management, held in Belém on 9–10 September 2026.

Fernandez has also worked in hemotherapy at Hospital Regional Dr. Abelardo Santos. In February 2022, she was identified by Agência Pará as a hematologist at the hospital in a report about initiatives to increase blood donation. [ref: Hospital Abelardo Santos usa telecaptação para ampliar doação de sangue, Agência Pará]

At Hospital Oncológico Infantil Octávio Lobo (HOIOL), she participated in hemotherapy activities involving pediatric oncology patients. In 2025, she was part of a team that presented research on the rational use of blood components in pediatric oncology at the Brazilian Congress of Hematology, Hemotherapy and Cell Therapy (HEMO 2025). [ref: Equipe do HOIOL aborda sobre segurança transfusional durante congresso em São Paulo, Agência Pará]

Her professional activities also include technical and administrative responsibilities at PROHEMO Serviços Médicos, a company providing hematology and hemotherapy services in Pará.

== Patient Blood Management ==

Fernandez has been involved in the institutional implementation of Patient Blood Management, a multidisciplinary approach to improving patient blood health, diagnosing and treating anemia, reducing blood loss, and supporting appropriate transfusion decisions.

At Fundação Hospital de Clínicas Gaspar Vianna, she coordinated the PBM program officially launched in October 2024. [ref: Programa de Gerenciamento do Uso do Sangue completa um ano de implantação no Hospital de Clínicas, Agência Pará]

According to an institutional report published in October 2025, the hospital recorded an approximate 25% reduction in the use of red blood cell concentrates and a 60% reduction in the use of fresh frozen plasma during surgical procedures in the program's first year. These figures were reported as institutional results of the multidisciplinary program.

In September 2026, Fernandez presided over the International Conference on Hemotherapy and Patient Blood Management at FHCGV. The event brought together approximately 180 participants, including healthcare professionals, researchers, and administrators, to discuss the implementation of PBM in clinical practice and public healthcare.

== Scientific research ==

Fernandez has contributed to research concerning chronic myeloid leukemia, molecular responses to imatinib treatment, and transfusion medicine.

In 2005, she was a co-author of a study published in Genetics and Molecular Research investigating the molecular response of BCR-ABL transcript variants to imatinib mesylate in patients with chronic myeloid leukemia. [ref: Differential molecular response of the transcripts B2A2 and B3A2 to imatinib mesylate in chronic myeloid leukemia, Genetics and Molecular Research]

In 2009, she participated in a study published in Clinics examining the relationship between delayed treatment and responses to imatinib in patients with chronic myeloid leukemia. [ref: Influence of late treatment on how chronic myeloid leukemia responds to imatinib, Clinics]

== Publications ==

In 2026, Fernandez published PBM Essencial: Transformando o Cuidado, Salvando Vidas, a Portuguese-language book addressing the scientific foundations, clinical applications, and institutional implementation of Patient Blood Management.

The book discusses anemia management, blood-loss prevention, transfusion decision-making, institutional governance, patient safety, and the implementation of multidisciplinary PBM programs.

The publication includes a foreword by Axel Hofmann, a researcher involved in the international development and implementation of Patient Blood Management. In the foreword, Hofmann examines the book's coverage of PBM principles, scientific evidence, clinical applications, and institutional strategies. [ref: PBM Essencial: Transformando o Cuidado, Salvando Vidas]

The book's publication was also mentioned in the Repórter 70 column of the Brazilian newspaper O Liberal in July 2026. [ref: R70: 'Não vamos ficar chorando', diz Lula sobre Tarifaço de 25%, O Liberal]

data.title: Dhaval Bhanusali
data.text:
----

Dhaval G. Bhanusali is an American dermatologist and entrepreneur based in New York City. He is the founder of Hudson Dermatology & Laser Surgery, a medical and cosmetic dermatology practice in Manhattan, [ref: How These A-List Dermatologists Are Making New York City The Destination For Beauty Innovation, Forbes] and of the prescription-dermatology technology platforms Skin Medicinals, HairStim Labs, and Aire Health. [ref: Meet The Doctor Disrupting The $100 Billion Skincare Industry And Empowering Celebrities Like Hailey Bieber And Martha Stewart, Forbes] [ref: Meet the Dermatologist Behind Rhode, Hailey Bieber's Hit Skin Care Brand, Entrepreneur] [ref: Celebrity Dermatologists Launch Platform Aire Health To Transform How Dermatologists Recommend And Sell Skincare, Beauty Independent]

Bhanusali served as the founding dermatologist for Rhode, the skin-care brand launched by Hailey Bieber in 2022 and acquired by e.l.f. Beauty in 2025 in a transaction valued at up to $1 billion, [ref: Meet Rhode, Hailey Bieber’s Minimalist Beauty Brand, WWD] [ref: Rhode, Femfounded] and co-founded Elm Biosciences with Martha Stewart, where he serves as chief medical officer. [ref: After Five Years in Development, Martha Stewart Is Launching Her Own Skin Care Line Elm Biosciences, WWD] [ref: Martha Stewart, 84, Is Now A Skincare Founder, Launching Elm Biosciences With Dermatologist Dr. Dhaval Bhanusali: ‘People Remark On The Vibrancy Of My Skin All The Time’, Forbes] In 2024 he was named one of Neutrogena's first Global Innovation Partners, [ref: Neutrogena® launches breakthrough collaboration with two of world’s most recognizable dermatologists, Kenvue] [ref: Neutrogena Taps Drs. Bhanusali & Shah As Global Innovation Partners, Happi] and in 2026 he was appointed the first chief dermatologist of Therabody. [ref: /C O R R E C T I O N -- Therabody/, www.prnewswire.com] [ref: Therabody Names Dr. Dhaval Bhanusali as First Chief Dermatologist, LATF USA NEWS]

In 2020 the American Academy of Dermatology named him a Patient Care Hero for providing pro bono scar treatment to Bridger Walker, a six-year-old who was injured protecting his younger sister from a dog attack. [ref: AAD Names Drs. Daval Bhanusali and Cory Maughan Patient Care Heroes for Treating Young Dog Bite Victim, PracticalDermatology] [ref: Dermatologists receive accolades for helping Cheyenne hero Bridger Walker with scars, Cap City News] [ref: ]

== Early Life and Education ==
Bhanusali was accepted into medical school at age 17 through the Michigan State University Medical Scholars Program. [ref: ] He completed his medical degree through Michigan State University before a dermatology residency at Mount Sinai Hospital in New York City. [ref: Dhaval Bhanusali - Skin of Color Society, skinofcolorsociety.org]

In 2019, Michigan State University's College of Human Medicine honored him with its alumni award as a Distinguished Scholar and Alumni of the Year. [ref: Home Page, myhumanmedicine.msu.edu] He has since worked with the university's Burgess Institute on programs connecting medicine and entrepreneurship, and has invested in MSU student innovation programs. [ref: This Spartan health entrepreneur is investing in MSU’s future innovators, MSUToday]

== Medical Career ==
Bhanusali founded Hudson Dermatology & Laser Surgery, located near Hudson Yards in Manhattan. His clinical practice covers medical and cosmetic dermatology, laser surgery, scar revision, and hair loss. [ref: How These A-List Dermatologists Are Making New York City The Destination For Beauty Innovation, Forbes] [ref: Dr. Dhaval Bhanusali Treats Scar And Hair Loss Patients With Compassion And Gently-Priced Products, Forbes]Forbes has described him as among the New York dermatologists shaping the city into a center of beauty innovation.

Through the Aesthetica Research Center at his practice, he conducts clinical research on dermatologic therapeutics, devices, and skincare products. [ref: Celebrity Derm Dhaval Bhanusali And TikTok Derm Muneeb Shah Partner At NYC Medical Practice, Set Out To Make Facials More Science-Driven, Beauty Independent] He is regularly cited as an expert source in consumer and trade press, is included in Allure's A-List of leading dermatologists, and has served on expert panels including InStyle's Best Beauty Buys. [ref: This “Celebrity Dermatologist” Wants to Be Known for More Than Treating Famous Faces, Allure]

== Pro Bono Work ==
Bhanusali has received national coverage for providing free scar treatment to patients recovering from violent injuries. In 2017 he treated a New York City knife-attack survivor at no cost, performing a series of laser procedures documented in a widely shared before-and-after recovery. [ref: NYC Slashing Victim Undergoes an Amazing Transformation 6 Months After Incident, NewBeauty] [ref: Life-changing treatment for slashing victim, FOX 5 New York]

In 2020, he and dermatologist Cory Maughan treated Bridger Walker, a six-year-old Wyoming boy whose story went viral after he shielded his younger sister from a charging dog and required dozens of stitches to his face. Bhanusali flew to treat the boy's scars pro bono, and the American Academy of Dermatology named both physicians Patient Care Heroes for the work. [ref: AAD Names Drs. Daval Bhanusali and Cory Maughan Patient Care Heroes for Treating Young Dog Bite Victim, PracticalDermatology] [ref: Dermatologists receive accolades for helping Cheyenne hero Bridger Walker with scars, Cap City News] [ref: ]

== Health Technology Ventures ==

=== Skin Medicinals ===
Bhanusali founded Skin Medicinals, a platform that works with physicians and compounding pharmacies to provide customized prescription dermatologic formulations at lower cost than many brand-name equivalents. He has cited the price of commonly prescribed dermatology medications as the motivation for the company, [ref: Meet the Dermatologist Behind Rhode, Hailey Bieber's Hit Skin Care Brand, Entrepreneur] which has grown to serve prescribers across the United States. [ref: Meet The Doctor Disrupting The $100 Billion Skincare Industry And Empowering Celebrities Like Hailey Bieber And Martha Stewart, Forbes]

=== HairStim Labs ===
He later founded HairStim Labs, a physician-directed platform for customized compounded treatments for hair loss, building on his clinical work in the area. [ref: Dr. Dhaval Bhanusali Treats Scar And Hair Loss Patients With Compassion And Gently-Priced Products, Forbes]

=== Aire Health ===
In 2024 Bhanusali launched Aire Health, a platform through which dermatology practices recommend and dispense professional skincare to patients. [ref: Celebrity Dermatologists Launch Platform Aire Health To Transform How Dermatologists Recommend And Sell Skincare, Beauty Independent]

== Brand and product development ==

=== Rhode ===
Bhanusali was recruited during the development of Rhode, Hailey Bieber's skin-care company, contributing dermatologic and formulation expertise alongside cosmetic chemist Ron Robinson, and subsequently served as the brand's dermatologist. [ref: Dr. Dhaval Bhanusali on dermatology, serial entrepreneurship and working on Rhode with Hailey Bieber, Glossy] [ref: Meet Rhode, Hailey Bieber’s Minimalist Beauty Brand, WWD] Rhode launched in 2022; in 2025, e.l.f. Beauty agreed to acquire the company in a transaction valued at up to $1 billion. [ref: Rhode, Femfounded]

=== Elm Biosciences ===
Bhanusali co-founded Elm Biosciences with Martha Stewart and serves as its chief medical officer. The company, developed over roughly five years and launched in 2025, focuses on skin longevity and drew on an advisory network of dermatologists and researchers. [ref: After Five Years in Development, Martha Stewart Is Launching Her Own Skin Care Line Elm Biosciences, WWD] [ref: Martha Stewart, 84, Is Now A Skincare Founder, Launching Elm Biosciences With Dermatologist Dr. Dhaval Bhanusali: ‘People Remark On The Vibrancy Of My Skin All The Time’, Forbes] [ref: Martha Stewart launches science‑led skincare brand amid celebrity beauty boom, FashionUnited]

=== Neutrogena ===
In October 2024, Neutrogena named Bhanusali and dermatologist Muneeb Shah its first Global Innovation Partners in a multi-year product development collaboration. [ref: Neutrogena® launches breakthrough collaboration with two of world’s most recognizable dermatologists, Kenvue] [ref: Neutrogena Taps Drs. Bhanusali & Shah As Global Innovation Partners, Happi] [ref: Neutrogena Recruits 2 Renowned Dermatologists as Global Innovation Partners, Beauty Packaging] His work with the brand has included development on core franchises such as Hydro Boost and the co-created Evenly Clear collection. [ref: Kenvue turns to science in skin health category, Drug Store News]

=== Aesthetica Skin Lab ===
In 2023 Bhanusali and Shah opened Aesthetica Skin Lab within Hudson Dermatology, pairing dermatologic assessment with science-driven aesthetic treatment;[22] [ref: Celebrity Derm Dhaval Bhanusali And TikTok Derm Muneeb Shah Partner At NYC Medical Practice, Set Out To Make Facials More Science-Driven, Beauty Independent] its flagship facial has been profiled in Forbes. [ref: Is This New York City’s Most Exclusive Facial?, Forbes]

=== Therabody ===
In April 2026 Therabody appointed Bhanusali its first chief dermatologist, with a role spanning dermatologic innovation and the company's beauty-device portfolio; he also serves on its scientific advisory board. [ref: Therabody Names Dr. Dhaval Bhanusali as First Chief Dermatologist, LATF USA NEWS] [ref: /C O R R E C T I O N -- Therabody/, www.prnewswire.com]

== Other activities ==
Bhanusali advised Ephemeral Tattoo, the maker of biodegradable made-to-fade tattoo ink, on ink development for medical applications. The ink was studied in a 2023 clinical trial at Henry Ford Health as an alternative to the permanent alignment-mark tattoos used in radiation therapy for cancer patients; the trial of 44 tattoos in 15 patients reported no adverse effects. [ref: Henry Ford Health and Ephemeral Tattoo Partner to Study Made-to-Fade Tattoo Ink for Medical Markings, www.henryford.com] [ref: www.eurekalert.org]

== Awards and recognition ==

* American Academy of Dermatology and Patient Care Hero (2020) [ref: AAD Names Drs. Daval Bhanusali and Cory Maughan Patient Care Heroes for Treating Young Dog Bite Victim, PracticalDermatology] [ref: Dermatologists receive accolades for helping Cheyenne hero Bridger Walker with scars, Cap City News]
* Neutrogena Global Innovation Partner (2024)
* Michigan State University College of Human Medicine, Distinguished Scholar / Alumni of the Year (2019) [ref: Home Page, myhumanmedicine.msu.edu] [ref: ]
* Allure A-List [ref: This “Celebrity Dermatologist” Wants to Be Known for More Than Treating Famous Faces, Allure]
* National Minority Quality Forum, 40 Under 40 Leaders in Minority Health (2018) [ref: National Minority Quality Forum Announces 2018 40 Under 40 Leaders in Minority Health Award Winners, www.diversityplus.com]
* American Academy of Dermatology Presidential Citations [ref: Dhaval Bhanusali - Skin of Color Society, skinofcolorsociety.org]

data.title: Riesbri
data.text:
Riesbri (born Alexandra Riesemberg Britez) is a Paraguayan-born visual artist based in Montreal, Canada. She works across painting, sculpture, ceramics, woodworking and metalwork, and her practice draws on her Guaraní heritage to address identity, migration and climate change. [ref: La tierra que busca saciar el alma, La Nación] [ref: "A Day in the Life" with Montreal Visual Artist Alexandra Riesbri, Montreal Guardian]

== Early life and education ==
Riesbri was born in Asunción, Paraguay, and raised in Brazil before settling in Montreal. Her artist name combines shortened forms of her two surnames, Riesemberg and Britez, adopted as a gender-neutral signature. She earned a Bachelor of Fine Arts in sculpture from Concordia University in 2024, graduating with great distinction as the valedictorian of the Faculty of Fine Arts. [ref: Meet the 2024 Faculty of Fine Arts valedictorians, Concordia University]

== Career ==
In 2023 she created a temporary public sculpture for Montreal's REM light-rail network in the Griffintown district, as part of an interuniversity public art cohort. [ref: An interuniversity cohort of 19 students installs 4 temporary artworks at Griffintown's Place des Aiguilleurs, Concordia University] Her first major solo exhibition, Techaga'u, was presented at Galería Arte Actual in Asunción in 2024. In 2025, her solo exhibition Haku Porã at POPOP Gallery in Montreal, curated by India-Lynn Upshaw-Ruffner, filled a gallery heated to roughly 35 °C with painted radiators and wooden cow sculptures in a critique of mass production, consumption and human intervention in the climate. [ref: POPOP Gallery: Haku Pora, The Cujah] In 2026 she was among the artists who hand-painted bicycles for L'art en mouvement, an open-air gallery project by BIXI and Loto-Québec. [ref: BIXI et Loto-Québec dévoilent L'art en mouvement: des vélos transformés par des artistes et une galerie à ciel ouvert dans le réseau BIXI cet été, CNW Telbec]

She has received a Research and Creation grant from the Canada Council for the Arts (2025) and project support from the Conseil des arts de Montréal, and has completed residencies in Montreal, Asunción and Mexico City.

== Selected exhibitions ==
=== Solo ===
* 2024 — Techaga'u, Galería Arte Actual, Asunción
* 2025 — Haku Porã, POPOP Gallery, Montreal

=== Group and fairs ===
* 2024 — Chromatic Reveries, Galerie JANO, Montreal
* 2024, 2025 — Art Toronto (with Galerie JANO)

== Awards and honours ==
* 2021 — Perseverance Award, Quebec Ministry of Higher Education
* 2024 — Valedictorian, Faculty of Fine Arts, Concordia University
* 2025 — Research and Creation grant, Canada Council for the Arts
