data.title: The Reclassified "NEGRO" aka "African American"
data.text:
The Memory of the Nations is a historical research project examining Indigenous identity, territorial sovereignty, racial classification, slavery, emancipation, colonial administration, and cultural continuity. It brings together historical maps, treaties, census instructions, land records, legal decisions, photographs, books, and cultural symbols to investigate how governments and institutions have influenced the recognition of peoples and the interpretation of history.

The project connects case studies from North America and other regions, including Indigenous communities in the United States, colonial racial classifications, and historical debates concerning Moorish identity. Its central theme is the relationship between the authority to define identity, control territory, and establish official historical narratives.

1. Indigenous geography and historical names

Indigenous nations across the Americas developed distinct languages, political systems, traditions, territories, and relationships to the land before the formation of modern national borders. These nations included the Muscogee, Cherokee, Chickasaw, Choctaw, Seminole, Lenape, Nanticoke, Catawba, Caddo, Quapaw, Haudenosaunee, and Shawnee, among many others.

Maps associated with the Native Niiji videos identify Indigenous nation names across the Southeast, Great Lakes, Plains, Southwest, Mexico, and Gulf Coast. Examples include Mvskoke, Chickasha, Chahta, Ani’yunwi’ya, Lenni-Lenape, Nanticoke, Shawano, Quapaw, and Caddo.

These maps provide starting points for examining Indigenous geography, migration, settlement, and political relationships. However, historical names may vary between Indigenous languages, colonial records, missionary accounts, treaties, and later publications. Maps must therefore be evaluated alongside archaeological findings, community histories, treaties, and other primary sources.

Lenape and Nanticoke histories are associated with the Mid-Atlantic region, including present-day Delaware. Chickasaw and Choctaw histories connect to the southeastern United States and later settlement in Indian Territory. Seminole history includes Florida, connections with Muscogee communities, forced removal, and continuing questions of sovereignty.

2. Texas, Galveston, land ownership, and slavery

The Akokisa and Karankawa have documented histories along the Texas coast before the establishment of the Republic of Texas.

In February 1836, Sam Houston negotiated a treaty with Cherokee and other East Texas communities. The Convention of 1836 did not ratify the agreement. Texas authorities subsequently relied on the absence of recognized land titles in decisions affecting Indigenous territorial claims and removal.

On June 13, 1837, the Telegraph and Texas Register published legislation concerning the relinquishment of one league and one labor of land at the eastern end of Galveston Island to Michael B. Menard and associates, subject to specified conditions. Texas General Land Office records preserve documents concerning land transactions, certificates, purchasers, and patents.

Galveston also participated in the domestic slave trade. Rosenberg Library preserves manifests associated with enslaved people transported aboard the steamships Galveston and Texas. The records include one manifest listing eight enslaved people and another listing 63. A bill of sale dated May 13, 1865, documents the sale of Louise, an eight-year-old child, and a six-month-old infant.

Together, these sources provide evidence of systems through which land and human beings were transferred under legal and commercial arrangements. They also offer opportunities for research into individual property transactions, enslaved families, and the consequences of slavery.

Sources: "Texas State Library and Archives Commission" (https://www.tsl.texas.gov/arc/local/galveston.html); "Texas State Historical Association" (https://www.tshaonline.org/); "Rosenberg Library African American history resources" (https://www.galvestonhistorycenter.org/research/african-american-history-resources-from-slavery-to-juneteenth).

3. The American Civil War and emancipation

The American Civil War lasted from 1861 to 1865. The Confederacy seceded to preserve slavery, which Confederate leaders identified as central to their social and economic order. The conflict involved enslaved people seeking freedom, free Black communities, Union soldiers, Indigenous nations, abolitionists, and political leaders.

The Emancipation Proclamation, effective January 1, 1863, declared enslaved people in designated areas still in rebellion against the United States to be free. It did not immediately abolish slavery throughout the entire country. As Union forces advanced, enslaved people escaped bondage, sought refuge, resisted plantation labor, and joined the military struggle. Black military service became an important component of Union victory.

On June 19, 1865, Union Major General Gordon Granger issued General Order No. 3 in Galveston, Texas, announcing freedom for enslaved people in Texas under the authority of the Emancipation Proclamation. The event became known as Juneteenth.

The Thirteenth Amendment, ratified on December 6, 1865, abolished slavery throughout the United States, except as punishment for a crime following conviction. Emancipation did not end racial discrimination, violence, or disputes over labor, land, and citizenship.

Sources: "National Archives: Emancipation Proclamation" (https://www.archives.gov/milestone-documents/emancipation-proclamation); "National Archives: Thirteenth Amendment" (https://www.archives.gov/milestone-documents/13th-amendment); "National Archives: Juneteenth" (https://www.archives.gov/news/topics/juneteenth).

4. Indigenous nations during and after the Civil War

The Civil War divided Indigenous communities in Indian Territory. Some leaders allied with the Confederacy, others supported the Union, and many communities faced displacement, damaged settlements, and internal political divisions.

Cherokee Confederate brigadier general Stand Watie continued fighting until June 1865 and became the last Confederate general to surrender. Muscogee, Seminole, Chickasaw, Choctaw, and Cherokee communities also experienced the consequences of changing military alliances and federal policy.

After the war, the United States negotiated new treaties with the Five Tribes. The 1866 treaties addressed emancipation, the rights of formerly enslaved people, citizenship, land, railroad access, and federal authority. These agreements connected the consequences of the Civil War with continuing disputes over Indigenous sovereignty.

The Chickasaw Nation's Great Seal was adopted on March 4, 1856. Depicting a Chickasaw warrior, the seal served as a symbol of the Nation's political identity. Federal authorities took custody of it after Oklahoma statehood in 1907, and it was returned to the Chickasaw Nation in 1984.

The Treaty with the Choctaw and Chickasaw Nations of April 28, 1866, addressed slavery, freed people, and land allotments. Later disputes over Freedmen's rights were examined in United States v. Choctaw Nation and Chickasaw Nation (1904). Federal enrollment systems, including the Dawes Rolls, classified people under categories that affected allotment and legal recognition.

The Oklahoma Historical Society preserves photographs catalogued as Chickasaw Freedmen, including images identified with Carrie William Hall and Claude Devoyd Hall. These records provide evidence for researching family histories and the contested legal status of African-descended people within the Chickasaw Nation.

Sources: "Chickasaw Nation: The Great Seal" (https://www.chickasaw.net/Our-Nation/Government/The-Great-Seal-of-the-Chickasaw-Nation); "Oklahoma Historical Society: Carrie William Hall" (https://gateway.okhistory.org/ark:/67531/metadc1595311/); "Claude Devoyd Hall" (https://gateway.okhistory.org/ark:/67531/metadc1596297/); "National Archives: Dawes Rolls" (https://www.archives.gov/research/native-americans/dawes).

5. Government classification and Indigenous identity

Government classification systems have influenced how Indigenous people were recorded, recognized, and treated under law.

Virginia

The Virginia Racial Integrity Act of 1924 strengthened racial classification requirements. Walter Ashby Plecker, registrar of vital statistics, challenged Indigenous identity claims under the state's racial definitions. Records held by the Library of Virginia include documents in which the designation “Ind” was crossed out and replaced with “colored,” as well as correspondence involving Rappahannock Chief George L. Nelson.

Federal census rules

The 1930 United States census instructions generally classified people of mixed Indian and Negro ancestry as Negro unless Indigenous ancestry predominated and the individual was generally accepted as Indian within the community. These instructions demonstrate how federal administrative criteria influenced recorded racial identity.

Delaware

Delaware laws enacted during the 1930s addressed school eligibility for children identified as Moors or Indians. A 1937 statute established a committee to resolve eligibility disputes. Later state legislation records the historical identification of the Lenape community as Moors and the use of “M” on certain state documents.

Nanticoke and Lenape communities maintained their identities while navigating official classifications and educational restrictions. Legislation, archival records, and community histories provide evidence for examining these developments.

The Dawes Act

The Dawes Act of 1887 divided communal tribal lands into individual allotments and permitted surplus land to pass into non-Indigenous ownership. Although the policy was presented as a means of promoting individual landownership and assimilation, it contributed to extensive transfers of Indigenous land.

Together, these cases illustrate how administrative rules could influence identity, education, citizenship, landownership, and recognition.

Sources: "Library of Virginia: Records of a Paper Genocide" (https://uncommonwealth.lva.virginia.gov/blog/2024/11/13/records-of-a-paper-genocide/); "1930 Census Instructions" (https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/decennial-census/technical-documentation/questionnaires/1930/1930-instructions.html); "Delaware's 1937 school law" (https://legis.delaware.gov/SessionLaws/Chapter?id=35663); "National Archives: Dawes Act" (https://www.archives.gov/milestone-documents/dawes-act).

6. International examples of colonial classification

Similar questions concerning identity, land, education, and cultural continuity arose in colonial systems around the world, although their histories and consequences differed.

- Canada: The Indian Act of 1876 established federal legal definitions of Indian status. Sex-based provisions caused some First Nations women who married men without status to lose their status and affected their descendants.
- Australia: Amendments to New South Wales' Aborigines Protection Act in 1915 expanded the authority to remove Aboriginal children from their families. These policies contributed to the history known as the Stolen Generations.
- South Africa: The Population Registration Act of 1950 formalized racial classification under apartheid. Its repeal began in 1991 as apartheid legislation was dismantled.
- Brazil and Guatemala: Census categories and national narratives influenced the statistical representation of Indigenous and mixed-ancestry populations. Brazil restored a distinct Indigenous census category in 1991.
- Rwanda: Belgian colonial administration formalized Hutu, Tutsi, and Twa classifications through identity documentation during the 1930s. These classifications formed part of the wider political history preceding later violence.
- Japan: The Hokkaido Former Aborigines Protection Act of 1899 advanced policies of Ainu assimilation.
- Norway: Norwegianization policies restricted Sámi language and culture. Norway's Truth and Reconciliation Commission reported in 2023.
- Fiji and French West Africa: Colonial administrations influenced the legal recognition of customary landholding and distinguished between different categories of colonial subjects and citizens.
- Namibia: German colonial forces committed genocide against the Herero and Nama peoples between 1904 and 1908.
- The Caribbean: European invasion caused catastrophic losses among Indigenous Caribbean populations. However, demographic collapse does not establish complete cultural extinction. Indigenous traditions, family histories, and contemporary identities have persisted, and the Smithsonian's National Museum of the American Indian has challenged claims that Caribbean Indigenous peoples became entirely extinct.

These examples provide comparative contexts for examining the effects of colonial administration on identity, land, legal status, and cultural continuity.

7. Moorish identity and historical literature

Historical research into Moorish identity involves examining the changing meanings of the term Moor, the history of North Africa and Muslim Iberia, and modern works that connect Moorish identity with religion, language, symbolism, and political history.

Josiah Priest

Josiah Priest's Slavery, as It Relates to the Negro, or African Race, Examined in the Light of Circumstances, History and the Holy Scriptures, published in 1843, used historical and scriptural arguments to defend slavery. The book is a primary source for studying nineteenth-century proslavery ideology. Its publication demonstrates that the arguments circulated, not that those arguments were historically or scientifically correct.

Source: "Internet Archive: 1843 edition" (https://archive.org/details/slaveryasitrela00priegoog).

C. M. Bey and Clock of Destiny

Clock of Destiny: Your Master Key of Civilization, associated with C. M. Bey, is catalogued in editions identified with 1947, 1951, 1973, and 2010. The work connects Moorish identity with religion, language, number symbolism, calendars, the Zodiac, political organization, and monetary systems.

Its claims can be investigated by comparing its historical references with primary documents, dated maps, religious records, and the history of mathematics and astronomy.

Source: "Clock of Destiny" (https://www.moorishcircleeducationcenter.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Clock-of-Destiny-Part-1-2.pdf).

Moor and Moabite terminology

The term Moor has a long history in European and Mediterranean sources, particularly in reference to North African peoples and Muslim Iberia. Its meaning has varied across periods and contexts.

Ancient Moab, by contrast, was a kingdom east of the Dead Sea, known through biblical sources and archaeological evidence, including the Mesha Stele. Similarity between the terms Moor and Moabite is a subject for linguistic and historical investigation, but a direct relationship requires evidence from language, chronology, geography, and historical usage.

North African and Iberian Muslim civilizations contributed to mathematics, medicine, astronomy, architecture, philosophy, and scholarship through interactions among diverse cultural and religious communities.

Historical census instructions, vital records, and enrollment categories demonstrate how institutions assigned identities according to particular rules. Nutrients support normal physiological functions, but diet cannot reliably manufacture ancestral identity or precisely control inherited skin pigmentation.

9. Themes and historical interpretation

The cases examined in The Memory of the Nations converge around several themes:

1. Naming and classification: Census rules, enrollment systems, and racial-integrity laws determined how people were recorded in official documents.
2. Territory and ownership: Treaties, land grants, allotment policies, and colonial property systems shaped the legal recognition of land rights.
3. Cultural continuity: School laws, language restrictions, child-removal policies, and assimilation programs affected the transmission of identity between generations.
4. Historical narratives: Books, government documents, community histories, and contemporary interpretations present different accounts of the past and must be evaluated in context.
5. Symbols and political identity: Flags, seals, stars, numbers, directions, and calendars can express cultural identity and political authority. Their meanings require investigation within the communities and periods in which they were used.

These themes connect the histories of Indigenous classification in Virginia, Delaware's Moor and Indian school laws, Chickasaw Freedmen disputes, Texas land transfers and slavery, Canadian status laws, Australian child removals, and South African apartheid. The cases are historically distinct but offer comparative evidence about the relationship between administrative power and cultural continuity.

10. Reconstructing history through evidence

Reconstructing history requires bringing together maps, photographs, treaties, archaeology, legal decisions, family histories, Indigenous languages, community records, and surviving objects. No single book, flag, seal, census column, or historical theory can establish the full account of a people or civilization.

The project emphasizes the importance of recovering original records, restoring historical names, tracing land transactions, contextualizing symbols, and comparing interpretations with documentary evidence. It also emphasizes that Indigenous history cannot be reduced to descriptions imposed by outside governments; Indigenous political memory, community histories, and continuing cultural identities are essential to historical research.

The central argument is that a fuller understanding of the past emerges when records and memories are examined together, with attention to their origins, limitations, and historical contexts.

data.title: VOdds
data.text:
VOdds is an online sports betting broker that gives customers access to several bookmakers and betting exchanges through one account. It is operated by Ole Group International B.V., a company registered in Willemstad, Curaçao.

==History==
VOdds was launched in 2016 as a platform giving bettors access to several Asian sports bookmakers through one account. [ref: About Us VOdds Trading Platform] A 2019 study of odds across 11 European leagues found that selecting the best available odds across bookmakers affected assessments of market efficiency, with three leagues showing inefficiencies that implied potential profit opportunities. [ref: Efficiency of online football betting markets, International Journal of Forecasting]

In February 2026, VOdds announced Odds Scanner, a tool that compares the odds different bookmakers offer on the same outcome in football, tennis, basketball and other sports. [ref: VOdds Introduces Advanced Odds Checker Tool to Help Bettors Find the Best Odds]

==Operations==
Its operator holds a licence from the Curaçao Gaming Control Board, reference OGL/2024/1358/1233. [ref: Certificate of Operation] It provides an application programming interface (API), the UNITY API, for integrating automated trading and monitoring odds in real time, and an online casino with games from Pragmatic Play and PG Soft.

data.title: JBOY (artist)
data.text:
----

JBOY is a street artist based in London. In 2010, JBOY changed a Banksy artwork in Bermondsey to include a reference to The Simpsons. [ref: Banksy's artwork gets Simpsons makeover, ShortList] [ref: Simpsons Themed Parody of Bansky [sic] by JBOY, Laughing Squid] More recent work has appeared in group exhibitions in London and on outdoor screens abroad.

== Early work ==
In October 2010, JBOY made a Simpsons-themed version of Banksy’s tribute to Keith Haring in Bermondsey, south London. This happened shortly after Banksy made the opening sequence for an episode of The Simpsons. ShortList covered the piece and described JBOY as a London street art group. JBOY told the magazine that the work had received complaints as well as compliments.

== Later work ==
In July 2024, JBOY took part in Let’s Live With Less Plastic, organised by Le Good Society for Plastic Free July. The exhibition showed work on outdoor screens in Times Square in New York and across the Netherlands. [ref: 'Let's Live With Less Plastic' Art Exhibition Inspires Global Action, The Ethicalist] JBOY returned in 2025 with Seafood, a work about plastic pollution. That year, the exhibition ran in New York, the Netherlands and London. FAD Magazine included a photograph of Seafood on a screen in Chelsea. [ref: Global Exhibition aims to help tackle Plastic Pollution, FAD Magazine] [ref: Pixels for the Planet: Global Outdoor Art Exhibition Tackles Plastic Pollution, The Ethicalist] In October 2026, JBOY took part in Wrestle Room, a group exhibition about British wrestling at Atom Gallery in Stoke Newington. Other artists in the exhibition included Peter Blake and Luke Haines. [ref: Wrestle Room, Atom Gallery]

== Style ==
On the artist’s website, JBOY describes working mainly with charcoal, pencil and paint. The work is often black and white with one strong colour. JBOY names cartoonist Gary Larson and illustrator Guy Billout as influences, and says the idea behind a piece matters more than its style or finish. The website also describes using tags, stickers and other forms of street writing, with humour that is often directed at the artist’s own work. JBOY uses the term détournement to describe changing familiar images or everyday things to give them a different meaning. [ref: About JBOY, JBOY] A series called Drip Works uses uncontrolled paint drips as the basis of the work. [ref: Drip Works, JBOY]

== Auctions ==
JBOY’s prints have appeared at auctions in the United States and the UK. In 2019, Heritage Auctions offered Selfie (Silver), a print from 2018, and Very Little Helper, which was released in 2010. [ref: Jboy, Selfie (Silver), 2018, Artsy] [ref: Jboy, Very Little Helper, 2010, Artsy] A copy of Very Little Helper was sold at Chiswick Auctions in London in March 2021. [ref: Very little helper, MutualArt] The prints Blinky and Yoots were also offered by Adam Partridge Auctioneers in September 2024. [ref: Blinky, MutualArt] [ref: JBoy, MutualArt] In October 2026, the painting The Standard was sold at McTear’s in Glasgow. It was included in a charity auction raising money for Glasgow Children’s Hospital Charity. [ref: Lot 40 – JBOY, The Standard, McTear's]

Lichon Kithan.

Lichon Kithan (born 31 January 1998) is an Indian Naga Student leader from Wokha district, Nagaland. He serves as the Present Education and Statistical Secretary of the Lotha Students' Union (LSU) for the 2026–2029 term.
He previously served as General Secretary of the Lotha Middle Range Students' Union (LMRSU) from 2024 to 2025 and as president of his native village from 2023 to 2025.

Early life and education

Kithan was born on 31 January 1998 in Wokha, Nagaland, India. He completed his Bachelor of Arts degree in History from Mount Tiyi College, Wokha, in 2021.

Family

Kithan is the eldest of four siblings.
He has two brothers and one sister.

Student leadership

Kithan serves as the Present Education and Statistical Secretary of the Lotha Students' Union for the 2026–2029 term.

In September 2026, the Lotha Students' Union directed its constituent units to monitor government schools in their respective areas. The initiative addressed concerns regarding teacher absenteeism, irregular classes and proxy teaching through field assessments and verification of school records. The initiative was reported by Nagaland Post on 17 September 2026.

Kithan previously served as General Secretary of the Lotha Middle Range Students' Union from 2024 to 2025. During his tenure, the organization raised concerns about regional issues, including human-elephant conflict and agricultural crop damage.

He also served as president of his native village from 2022 to 2025.

data.title: Silky (streamer)
data.text:
Bryan "Silky" Francisque (born October 21, 1997), known professionally and online as Silky. [ref: Who’s in FaZe Clan? Full roster and all members who quit in 2025 exodus, Dexerto] [ref: Who Is In FaZe Clan? Here's Every Member of The Popular Streamer Group, Complex] [ref: FaZe Clan reveals four new members as organization “reboots”, Dexerto], Jerry Woo [ref: Who’s in FaZe Clan? Full roster and all members who quit in 2025 exodus, Dexerto], or Rico [ref: When did Silky (USA) start making music?, Genius], is an American online streamer, YouTuber, and Internet personality who specializes in comedic live streams and videos. He is a member of the streamer collective CORE "Create, Own, Run, Everything." [ref: Former FaZe Clan creators rebrand under new ‘CORE’ group with $20M content house, Dexerto] [ref: Ex-FaZe Clan Members Form New Streaming Group, CORE, Complex] [ref: FaZe Clan alumni see rapid fan uptake with launch of CORE collective, The Drop]

He began his streaming career on Twitch in 2019. He gained mainstream attention in 2024 following his joining of the esports and entertainment organization FaZe Clan. [ref: Who Is In FaZe Clan? Here's Every Member of The Popular Streamer Group, Complex] [ref: Who’s in FaZe Clan? Full roster and all members who quit in 2025 exodus, Dexerto] [ref: FaZe Clan reveals four new members as organization “reboots”, Dexerto] On April 30, 2026, following his departure from FaZe Clan [ref: Former FaZe Clan CEO Banks Calls PlaqueBoyMax ‘Fake,’ Denies Role in Mass Departure, Complex] [ref: What’s Going On With FaZe Clan? They Just Lost 5 Members, Yahoo Entertainment], Silky became one of the six founding members of CORE, a content collective formed alongside other top content creators such as Adapt, Stable Ronaldo, JasonTheWeen, and Marlon. [ref: FaZe Clan alumni see rapid fan uptake with launch of CORE collective, The Drop] [ref: Ex-FaZe Clan Members Form New Streaming Group, CORE, Complex] [ref: Former FaZe Clan creators rebrand under new ‘CORE’ group with $20M content house, Dexerto]

Regarded as one of the most popular online streamers, Silky pioneered and helped popularize the highly successful "e-dating" content format on Twitch [ref: FaZe Silky on Beef with Adin Ross, Almost Losing His Life, Joining Faze Clan]. This style of e-dating content later became a staple across Twitch, heavily popularized by creators like Adin Ross and Kai Cenat. [ref: FaZe Silky on Beef with Adin Ross, Almost Losing His Life, Joining Faze Clan] [ref: FaZe Silky on Beef with Adin Ross, Almost Losing His Life, Joining Faze Clan]

With over 1.4 million followers on Twitch [ref: About Silky - Twitch] [ref: Silky - Streamer Overview & Stats, TwitchTracker], Silky has achieved significant milestones in the streaming community, notably becoming the third black Twitch streamer ever to surpass 100,000 Twitch subscribers [ref: Twitch All-time Streamers With Most Active Subscribers, TwitchTracker] during his FaZe subathon in October 2025. [ref: ]

== Early Life and Education ==
Silky was born as Bryan Francisque on October 21, 1997, in Canarsie, Brooklyn, New York City [ref: FaZe Silky on Beef with Adin Ross, Almost Losing His Life, Joining Faze Clan], to a mother of Haitian descent and a father of Guyanese and Nepali descent. Silky was raised by his mother along with his three other siblings, an older sister and two younger sisters.

Silky attended high school in Brooklyn, New York City. He graduated from high school in 2015 and received his bachelor's degree in computer science from The City College of New York in New York. He is a Christian. [ref: FaZe Silky on Beef with Adin Ross, Almost Losing His Life, Joining Faze Clan]

== Career ==

=== 2019–2020: Early career ===
Before streaming full-time, Silky began playing and grinding NBA 2K17 directly from his Xbox, pulling in an average audience of 100 to 300 viewers. [ref: FaZe Silky on Beef with Adin Ross, Almost Losing His Life, Joining Faze Clan] [ref: Silky - Stream Nov 22, 2019 - Stats on viewers, followers, subscribers; VOD and clips, TwitchTracker]

In July 2019, he officially created his Twitch Channel [ref: Silky - Twitch Stats, Analytics] while working normal jobs and attending school.

In 2020, Silky began regular streaming, rapidly shifting his primary focus to NBA 2K, Grand Theft Auto V (GTA RP), and "Just Chatting" content. [ref: Who’s in FaZe Clan? Full roster and all members who quit in 2025 exodus, Dexerto] [ref: FaZe Clan reveals four new members as organization “reboots”, Dexerto] [ref: How Silky Started Streaming]

His roleplaying content on the "GTA RP" servers acted as his first major breakout, pushing his average viewership into the thousands [ref: FaZe Silky on Beef with Adin Ross, Almost Losing His Life, Joining Faze Clan].

=== 2021: Initial Popularity ===
In 2021, Silky experienced a breakthrough year, transitioning from a growing gaming streamer into a major personality-driven, "Just Chatting" powerhouse.

Silky was also known for his reactions to Brooklyn and New York drill music. [ref: Silky Reacts To Dthang x Bando x Tdot - Talk Facts ( Official Music Video )] [ref: FIREE!! Silky Reacts To CHII WVTTZ X SET DA TREND X CBLU X DOUGIE B - GEEKED] [ref: Silky Reacts TO Off The Radar Cypher: Kyle Richh, Jenn Carter & Tata] [ref: Silky Reacts To Say Drilly x E-Wuu x Nesty Floxks x Lee Drilly - “Deadly” (Shot By Borleone)] [ref: Silky Reacts To Pop Smoke Album w/Quelly Woo, Snaggymo,Pat & Geesice] His animated, high-energy breakdowns of drill beats, samples, and music videos became a staple of his channel during his 2021–2023 streaming era.

Moving away from GTA RP servers, Silky pioneered the highly popular online "e-dating" and matchmaking concepts on Twitch — a format later popularized on a massive scale by Adin Ross, in which Silky was a recurring participant. [ref: Adin Ross Hosts Edate with KKVSH FT. Kai Cenat, Silky, & iShowSpeed... *FULL E-DATE*] [ref: Silky's Full Edate With Rubi Rose ft.Kai Cenat, Adin & More]

In mid-2021, he completed his first-ever subathon. He capped off the year with a highly successful "25 Days of Silkmas" campaign, streaming every single day of December to cement his core community.

In later years, the phrase "2021 Silky" [ref: How Silky Started Streaming] actually became a running joke and meme within his community and on TikTok. [ref: 2021 Silky Meme explained 🤣] Viewers frequently look back at his 2021 era as a time when his streams were uniquely chaotic, experimental, and unhinged compared to his later, highly structured eras. [ref: Silky's Still On Top 8 Years Later...]

=== 2022–2023: Nation house and firework accident ===
Following rapid growth in 2021, Silky suffered heavy burnout. Consequently, he disappeared from the internet entirely for six months in 2022 to step away and mentally reset [ref: FaZe Silky on Beef with Adin Ross, Almost Losing His Life, Joining Faze Clan]

Silky was a prominent part of and leader of Nation content house from mid-to-late 2023 until joining FaZe Clan in early 2024. [ref: Twitch partner Silky becomes the second member to join FaZe Clan after recent layoffs, www.sportskeeda.com] [ref: Silky Joins FaZe Clan...] [ref: Silky Joins FaZe Clan...]

On July 4, 2023, while celebrating Independence Day, Silky tried to shoot a heavy mortar firework shell out of a thick cardboard tube to mimic a rocket launcher. At the last second, he moved the tube away from his head, and it instantly exploded in his hand. The blast split his hand open to the bone, causing second-degree burns and severe lacerations. Silky had to undergo multiple major surgeries to repair the extensive tissue damage on his hand. [ref: FaZe Silky on Beef with Adin Ross, Almost Losing His Life, Joining Faze Clan] [ref: Silky Tells The Story Of The Firework Incident That Sent Him To The ER]

=== 2024: FaZe Clan ===
In April 2024, following a brief two-month hiatus, Silky was recruited into the newly revamped FaZe Clan roster under the leadership of FaZe Banks [ref: Who Is In FaZe Clan? Here's Every Member of The Popular Streamer Group, Complex] [ref: FaZe Clan reveals four new members as organization “reboots”, Dexerto] [ref: Who’s in FaZe Clan? Full roster and all members who quit in 2025 exodus, Dexerto]. He moved into the FaZe Miami house alongside PlaqueBoyMax, YourRage, and FaZe Kaysan. [ref: Kaysan tells his associate to terminate the FaZe House in Miami after watching YourRaage, Plaqueboymax, and Silky trash his room, www.sportskeeda.com] [ref: We Destroyed The Miami FaZe House...] [ref: i moved into the faze house]

In September 2024, Silky was a part of FaZe Clan’s first highly successful subathon [ref: FaZe Clan Subathon] [ref: Plaqueboymax claims FaZe clan earned $2 million during their subathon on Twitch this month, www.sportskeeda.com].

=== 2025–2026: Departure from FaZe Clan and Start of CORE ===
In December 2025, Silky parted ways with FaZe Clan [ref: Former FaZe Clan CEO Banks Calls PlaqueBoyMax ‘Fake,’ Denies Role in Mass Departure, Complex] [ref: ] [ref: What’s Going On With FaZe Clan? They Just Lost 5 Members, Yahoo Entertainment] and co-founded the content group CORE [ref: Former FaZe Clan creators rebrand under new ‘CORE’ group with $20M content house, Dexerto] continuing close collaborations with the same inner circle of massive internet personalities. [ref: Ex-FaZe Clan Members Form New Streaming Group, CORE, Complex]

In late 2025, his explosive momentum pushed him past 100,000 active Twitch subscribers, landing him a spot on the historical list of the most-subscribed Twitch channels of all time. [ref: ] [ref: Silky Hits 100,000 Twitch Subscribers!]

Today, Silky sits at over 1.4 million Twitch followers. He remains one of the top English-speaking "Just Chatting" creators worldwide, regularly pulling massive concurrent viewership during major events and collaborative streams. [ref: Silky - Streamer Overview & Stats, TwitchTracker]

In July 2026, Silky participated as a student in the second installment of Kai Cenat's Streamer University. He was officially announced as part of the 2026 class alongside other notable creators like PlaqueBoyMax and Stable Ronaldo. [ref: Kai Cenat Reveals Streamer University Class Of 2026] [ref: Silky Arrives At Streamer University!] Since Streamer University, Silky has been one of the top streamers on Twitch, consistently streaming every day. [ref: Silky - Streamer Overview & Stats, TwitchTracker] [ref: Twitch Top Streamers, October 2026, English, TwitchTracker]

In early September 2026, Silky went viral after a video showed him helping a woman who approached him and his friend on the street, revealing that an unknown man had been following her. Silky stayed beside the woman and calmly handled the situation by approaching the man following her and encouraging him to pass them. [ref: Silky and BigEx help woman allegedly followed during Los Angeles livestream, viewers praise their calm response, The Times of India]

In October 2026, Silky earned his first individual Streamer Awards nomination for Best Just Chatting Streamer ("President of Chat"). [ref: ] [ref: All The Nominees For The Streamer Awards 2026, THE MAGIC RAIN] [ref: Streamer Awards 2026 Reveals All Nominees As IShowSpeed, Jynxzi And CaseOh Lead The Race, NDTV Sports] [ref: The Streamer Awards, The Streamer Awards]

data.title: Mr. Universe (1988 film)
data.text:
Mr. Universe is a 1988 American-Hungarian documentary film directed by György Szomjas. [ref: https://kronika.hu/cikk/a-kobanyai-ferfi-akit-schwarzenegger-alakitott-a-vasznon]

==Synopsis==
Two drifting, half-swindler Hungarian characters decide to make a documentary about their old friend and compatriot, Mickey Hargitay, the bodybuilding champion who has since become a world star in the United States and was the husband of Jayne Mansfield. Although they have not been in contact with him for some fifteen years, they are certain that Mickey will be flattered by the idea and will even support the penniless production financially. They cross America in their battered car and look him up. Mickey lives quietly in his enormous villa beneath the "Hollywood" sign, running his businesses and raising his children. Although he welcomes his old friends warmly, he shows no interest whatsoever in their crazy film idea.

data.title: SOMOS Productions
data.text:
SOMOS Productions LLC is an independent audiovisual content producer focused on the production of Television content headquartered in Miami, Florida. The company concentrates in Spanish language content, and it is involved in concept creation and development, production management, consulting, technical production of multi-camera events in several genres (fiction, drama, variety shows, and documentaries, among others). SOMOS Productions is headed by Luis Villanueva, an executive in the Hispanic media and entertainment industry, President and CEO of SOMOS Group, entity that includes SOMOSTV, SOMOS Distribution, SOMOS Next, SOMOS Fast, SOMOS Show and SOMOS Films.

SOMOS Productions participates in co-production with international partnering companies in several countries.

== History ==

Founded in 2011. [ref: Luis Villanueva launches Somos Productions, PRODU], SOMOS Productions started its production catalog with two teen series 11-11: En mi cuadra nada cuadra [ref: Nickelodeon Latin America Producing Tween Novela ’11 11′ (Exclusive), The Hollywood Reporter], written by Luis Llosa and Pablo Vasquez (75 episodes) and directed by Cary Delgado, Diego Salazar, and Cusi Barrio. The company produced as well Vikki RPM (60 episodes), based on an original idea by Eduardo Jiménez-Pons, written by Catharina Ledeboer and Rocio Lara, directed by William Barragan, Maria Eugenia Herrera, Tito Rojas, and Diego Salazar. These series were produced for Nickelodeon (Latin America) [ref: Nickelodeon Latin America orders new tween novela] [ref: ESTRENOS, NOTICIAS Y ENTRETENIMIENTO: VIKKI RPM lo nuevo de Nickelodeon Latino América, ESTRENOS, NOTICIAS Y ENTRETENIMIENTO]and successfully broadcast in the region [ref: Nickelodeon estrena este lunes su nueva novela «11 11 – En mi cuadra nada cuadra», Prensaescenario]

The company has also produced TV formats for Telemundo. In 2013, SOMOS Productions produced Todos Somos Héroes [ref: Somos Productions realiza 'Todos Somos Héroes' para Telemundo, Newsline Report] (Duration: 2 hours). The format highlights the stories of ordinary people who have made a difference in their families, friends, communities, and countries. It also produced the Premios Billboard de la Musica Mexicana [ref: "Anuncian nominaciones a los Premios Billboard de la Música Mexicana", Peple en Espanol] [ref: "Jenni Rivera, máxima ganadora de Premios Billboard de la Música Mexicana; lista de ganadores aquí", People en Espanol](Duration: 2 hours), devoted to the best-selling Latin music genre in the United States: Regional Mexican. SOMOS Productions has been the producer of the Latin American Music Awards [ref: Who Should Win Latin AMAs Artist Of the Year? Vote!, Billboard] [ref: Maluma to Receive The Extraordinary Evolution Award at 2018 Latin American Music Awards, Billboard](years 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2021, 2022), a 3-hour live show honoring today's most influential and iconic Latin artists, voted for by fans. The awards honor artists in Pop rock, Regional Mexican music, Urban music, and Tropical music genres.

In 2016, SOMOS Productions co-produced one of its most successful series Hasta que te conocí (TV series), a biographical tv-series that follows the footsteps of "Juan Gabriel" toward his dream of fame. A tour of 14 episodes based on unpublished testimonies produced by Juan Gabriel in collaboration with SOMOS Productions, BET Media Group, and Disney Media Distribution and written by Abe Panes, Edgar Cuevas, Mary Black, Camilo Hernandez, Sergio Jablon. The series narrate how Alberto Aguilera Valadez and his talent led him to defy fate and overcome poverty, betrayal, and prejudice.

In 2020, the company followed on these steps with "Súbete a Mi Moto (2020 TV series) [ref: Mipcom: Endemol Shine Latino Co-produces Drama Series on Latin Boy Band, Menudo, Variety] [ref: A Menudo Series Is In the Works: Here’s What to Know About ‘Súbete a Mi Moto’, Billboard](15 episodes) in coproduction with Endemol Shine Boomdog (Mexico) and Piñolywood (Puerto Rico). told the story of the famous boyband Menudo (group), a musical group that laid the foundations for the "boybands" that still exist today. The band was the beginning of the solo careers of many important figures and continues to be the reference for all other Hispanic youth bands. The series premiered [ref: Por fin se estrena la controversial serie musical 'Súbete a mi Moto' en los Estados Unidos, Los Angeles Times en Español] [ref: HOY ESTRENA. ¿Logrará la serie 'Súbete mi a moto' despertar la Menudomanía con su estreno en EE,UU.?, Los Angeles Times en Español] successfully on Amazon Prime Video on October 9, 2020, in Mexico, Latin America, and Spain. Súbete a Mi Moto was directed by Raul Garcia and Javier Solar.

The company continued its production of musical youth series with "[[@[user] Yei: WithAllMyHeartAndMore]] [ref: "Somos Productions y Piñolywood Studios preproducen “Lucy es el 7” - Señal News", senalnews.com] [ref: Somos Distribution presenta Gina Yei y Lucy es el 7 – Prensario Zone] [ref: [i]GinaYei[/i], producción de Somos Productions y Piñolywood, culmina rodaje, www.thedailytelevision.com](12 episodes). This is the story of a young woman that thanks to her talent for lyrics, won a scholarship at an Institute located on the island of Puerto Encantado, considered the best place in the world to study Latin music and the cradle of Reggaeton. The story was written by Vladimir Pérez, Nailys Sánchez, Edgar Cuevas and Miguel A Medina. The series was co-produced with Piñolywood Studios for the Walt Disney Company, premiering worldwide on Disney+ [ref: SOMOS PRODUCTIONS LICENSES "@[user]" TO DISNEY+ - Señal News, senalnews.com]

SOMOS Productions finished in 2025 its production Lucy es el 7 (12 episodes). Lucy's imagination is very particular, she sees the people around her as if they were characters from an oriental anime and is in love with a boy. This forces her to disguise herself as a boy to become the seventh member of his band. The series premiered in May 2026 in HBO Max [ref: Lucy Is The 7 Premieres on HBO Max in Latam, TTV News]

data.title: Thomas Barrington (1530–1581)
data.text:
Sir Thomas Barrington (1530 – 1581) was an English politician. He sat as MP for Essex in 1572. [ref: BARRINGTON, Sir Thomas (1530-81), of Hatfield Broad Oak, Essex., History of Parliament Online]

He was knighted in 1571.

== Family and education ==
He was the only son of John Barrington (died 1537) of Hatfield Broad Oak by Elizabeth, the daughter of Thomas Bonham. He was admitted into Gray's Inn in 1554. He married Alice, the daughter of Sir Henry Parker (probably 10th) Lord Morley and they had one son (who predeceased him) and one daughter. he married Winifred, the daughter of Sir Henry Pole, 1st Baron Montagu and widow of Sir Thomas Hastings and they had two sons (Francis and Henry Barrington) and one daughter.

== Offices held ==
He served as chief forester of Hatfield forest; captain of levies in Hertfordshire in 1562; Sheriff of Hertfordshire, and Essex in 1562; commissioner of musters in Essex in 1563; commissioner to raise a benevolence in Essex in 1564; commissioner of restraint of victuals in Essex in 1573; commissioner of grain in Essex in 1579; justice of the peace for Essex from 1564; and sheriff of Essex from 1580 till 1581.

data.title: Joshua's Confusion
data.text:
Joshua’s Confusion is a 1977 children's television special produced by Multimedia Program Productions. It is part of a series called Young People's Specials, a series of specials locally produced in Cincinnati [ref: Young People's Specials - Joshua's Confusion entry form, letters, study guide, press release, clipping, and photos, 1977, University of Georgia] that tackled cultural issues through the lenses of children. The special originally aired on WLWT-TV, but would be syndicated in other areas, including on Nickelodeon's Special Delivery. [ref: Monday Movie Ratings, Eugene Register-Guard] [ref: Sunday TV, Mohave Daily Miner] [ref: Daily TV Time Table, Williamson Daily News] The film was produced with help from the Amish community of Berlin, Ohio.

==Plot==
The special follows Joshua, an Amish boy who gets invited to a sleepover by one of his friends at school. His parents forbid Joshua from going since it goes against their beliefs. Joshua sneaks out of his bedroom window and goes to the party anyway. Throughout the party, Joshua thinks about what his father told him as he plays with the kids. Joshua’s parents find out Joshua left and pick him up. On the way home, Joshua jumps out of their buggy and retreats into the woods. Joshua sleeps in the woods and the special ends with him returning home the next day.

==Awards==
In 1977, Joshua's Confusion won a Peabody Award for Children's & Youth. [ref: Joshua's Confusion - Peabody Awards, peabodyawards.com] Charles Goetz won a regional Emmy for his role as Joshua's Father. [ref: 42nd Street Lights Up Stage, The Western Star] [ref: Charles Joseph Goetz Jr. Obituary, weilkahnfuneralhome.com]

data.title: Tara Hernandez (writer)
data.text:
Tara Hernandez is an American television writer, producer and showrunner. She served as producer and wrote for the CBS sitcom The Big Bang Theory and its spin-off Young Sheldon. [ref: 'Big Bang Theory' EP Tara Hernandez Sets 19th-Century Sitcom Pilot Order at CBS, TheWrap] [ref: "Mrs. Davis" Receives New Series Order from Peacock, Warner Bros. Television] She co-created the Peacock science-fiction series Mrs. Davis (2023) with Damon Lindelof and served as its showrunner. [ref: Meet the cast and creators of Peacock's sci-fi series 'Mrs. Davis', Syfy Wire] She is writing a live-action adaptation of Captain Planet and the Planeteers for Netflix. [ref: CBS orders Tara Hernandez comedy pilot Regency, Deadline Hollywood]

== Early life and education ==
Hernandez graduated from Chapman University's Dodge College of Film and Media Arts in 2010 with a Bachelor of Fine Arts in film production. [ref: Alumni Spotlight – Tara Hernandez, Dodge College of Film and Media Arts]

== Career ==
=== The Big Bang Theory and Young Sheldon ===
After graduating, Hernandez was offered an interview with the executive producer and showrunner of The Big Bang Theory. She has said she was initially uninterested in television, describing herself as a "film snob". She was hired as an assistant to the show's executive producers, a role she held for two and a half seasons, during which she learned to pitch stories. After several of her pitches were produced, she was promoted to staff writer, and by early 2017 had become a co-producer.

Over her nine-year tenure on the series she progressed from assistant to writer and producer, eventually serving as a co-executive producer. She subsequently wrote for and co-executive produced the spin-off Young Sheldon from 2018 to 2021. By the time she left network comedy, she had written close to 200 episodes across the two series. [ref: "Mrs. Davis" – Wacky, Unpredictable, and Full of All Kinds of Surprises, Golden Globes] Hernandez also wrote an episode of the Nickelodeon series Henry Danger in 2015. [ref: Tara Hernandez, IMDb]

=== Mrs. Davis ===
Mrs. Davis grew out of a comedic spec script Hernandez had written about post-apocalyptic nuns. The script reached Susan Rovner, then an executive at Warner Bros. Television, who suggested Hernandez meet Lindelof; the pair met shortly before the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic and developed the project together during that period. [ref: Mrs. Davis Co-Creator Tara Hernandez On Crafting Peacock's Wild New Sci-Fi Series [Exclusive Interview], /Film]

Rovner later brought the project with her to Peacock after leaving Warner Bros. to become chair of NBCUniversal's television and streaming division. [ref: Tara Hernandez, Variety500] In May 2021, Peacock gave the series a straight-to-series order of ten episodes in a competitive situation, with Hernandez as showrunner and executive producer; both she and Lindelof were then under overall deals with Warner Bros. Television. Starring Betty Gilpin as a nun set on destroying an all-powerful artificial intelligence, the series premiered at SXSW in March 2023 before its first four episodes were released on Peacock on 20 April 2023. It ran for a single season of eight episodes, [ref: Peacock Submits Genre-Bending Mrs. Davis as Limited/Anthology Series for 2023 Emmy Awards, Syfy Wire] and Peacock submitted it in the limited/anthology categories for the 75th Primetime Emmy Awards. The series was well received by critics. It was nominated for the TCA Award for Outstanding New Program. [ref: Mrs. Davis, TV Guide] Hernandez was named to the Variety500 for 2023.

=== Captain Planet and the Planeteers ===
As of 2025, Hernandez was writing a live-action series adaptation of the animated series Captain Planet and the Planeteers for Netflix, in development with Greg Berlanti's Berlanti Productions, Leonardo DiCaprio's Appian Way and Warner Bros. Television.
=== The Tillbrooks ===
In December 2025, CBS ordered a pilot for Regency, a multi-camera family sitcom written and executive produced by Hernandez for Warner Bros. Television, placing it in contention for the 2026–27 broadcast season. [ref: CBS comedy pilot Regency from Tara Hernandez, [[Variety (magazine)] The project put a period twist on the traditional family sitcom, following the upper-middle-class Tillbrooks family in 19th-century England. It was the network's second comedy pilot order of the cycle, after the single-camera Eternally Yours from Ghosts showrunners Joe Port and Joe Wiseman. Rhys Darby was cast as patriarch Arthur Tillbrook, [ref: Rhys Darby to Star in CBS Comedy Pilot 'Regency', [[Variety (magazine)] and Kate Walsh joined as matriarch Jocelyn after the project was retitled The Tillbrooks. [ref: Kate Walsh ("Grey's Anatomy") mit neuem Comedy-Projekt in der "Bridgerton"-Ära, Wunschliste] In April 2026, CBS declined to order the pilot to series, opting instead for the comedy Eternally Yours. [ref: Kate Walsh's new sitcom canceled at CBS, ARY News] [ref: CBS Orders Eternally Yours to Series, Passes on The Tillbrooks, The TV Ratings Guide]

data.title: Detlef Kleinert
data.text:
Detlef Kleinert (26 July 1932 – 17 June 2016) was a German lawyer and politician of the Free Democratic Party (FDP). He was a member of the Bundestag from 20 October 1969 to 26 October 1998, representing Lower Saxony via the FDP state list, and worked on legal policy. From 1967 to 1996 he chaired the FDP district association for the city of Hanover.

== Early life and education ==

Kleinert was born in Essen and grew up in Schöningen, near the inner German border, and in Hanover. His father, a trained merchant, was a senior official of the Reichsbank and last headed its branch in Schöningen. He passed his Abitur in Schöningen in 1951 and studied law at the universities of Erlangen and Munich. He took the first state law examination in 1955 and the second in 1960. In Munich he joined a student corps. In 1952 he became a member of the Liberal Student Federation of Germany (Liberaler Studentenbund Deutschlands, LSD).

== Legal and business career ==

Kleinert began practising as a lawyer in Hanover in 1960 and later worked as a notary. During his time in parliament he was a board member of Wert-Garantie Technische Versicherung AG, an insurance company in Hanover. He was honorary chairman of the Vereinigung Liberaler Juristen (Association of Liberal Lawyers).

Kurt Jodexnis, a Hanover insurance businessman and a long-standing business associate of Kleinert, held a 20 per cent share in the casino company of Bad Bentheim and Bad Zwischenahn, which received its licence in 1975 from the FDP state interior minister Rötger Groß. In 1982 Jodexnis transferred half of this share to Kleinert. In August 1988 Kleinert testified about the stake before the Landtag of Lower Saxony's casino inquiry committee. He stated that he had received the share, with a nominal value of 300,000 Deutsche Mark, free of charge as compensation for a business deal with Jodexnis twelve years earlier. He also stated that he had only advised Jodexnis on the selection of the other partners, had never discussed the licence with Groß and had not donated any casino income to the party. Jodexnis largely confirmed his account.

== Political career ==

=== Party offices ===

Kleinert joined the FDP in 1957. From 1967 to 1996 he was chairman of the party's district association for the city of Hanover. In 1970 he became treasurer of the Lower Saxony FDP, a post he still held in 1988; during this time he consolidated the state party's finances. He took part in the FDP's 1974 coalition negotiations with the Social Democrats in Lower Saxony, whose delegation was led by Alfred Kubel. In November 1976 he was elected to the party's federal executive.

=== Member of the Bundestag ===

Kleinert was elected to the Bundestag in the 1969 federal election on the FDP's state list for Lower Saxony and was re-elected at each subsequent election until 1994. He sat from 20 October 1969 to 26 October 1998, from the 6th to the 13th legislative term.

From the end of 1969 he chaired the FDP parliamentary group's Working Group IV, which covered home affairs and law and, at times, education and the environment. His work there included data protection, bureaucracy and the volume of legislation. In his last term he was a full member of the Legal Affairs Committee, the Judicial Selection Committee and the committee that elects judges of the Federal Constitutional Court, and a deputy member of the Committee on Internal Affairs. He supported the repeal of Paragraph 175, the criminal provision against homosexual acts between men, and took part in drafting the reform of divorce law.

In July 1979 the Bundestag debated the abolition of the statute of limitations for murder, prompted by the approaching expiry of the limitation period for Nazi-era murders. Kleinert spoke for the majority of the FDP parliamentary group in favour of retaining the existing law. He argued that criminal justice should be kept separate from the country's responsibility for its history, that few unidentified perpetrators remained, and that the Majdanek trial had shown that fair trials were no longer possible after so long a period.

In May 1989, in a Bundestag debate on the conviction of the Memmingen gynaecologist Horst Theissen for illegal abortions, Kleinert criticised the conduct of the trial and described the women concerned as more victims than offenders.

On 23 November 1994, in the debate on Chancellor Helmut Kohl's government statement, Kleinert gave a short speech on legal and home-affairs policy while under the influence of alcohol. He spoke on whether electronic surveillance of private homes should be permitted, a question on which the FDP had not yet reached a decision, and his remarks drew repeated laughter from the opposition benches.

During the dispute over the German orthography reform of 1996, Kleinert, Norbert Geis and other members tabled a motion on German spelling, which the Bundestag debated on 18 April 1997.

In January 1998 Kleinert was one of the Legal Affairs Committee's rapporteurs on the amendment to Article 13 of the Basic Law that permitted electronic surveillance of private homes for criminal prosecution, and he took part in the cross-party negotiations on it for the FDP. In the Bundestag debate on 16 January 1998 he supported the amendment. He argued that its safeguards, including authorisation by a panel of judges, would limit surveillance to a small number of serious cases, and that the offices of lawyers and other professionals bound by confidentiality could not be fully exempted from surveillance.

=== Political positions ===

Kleinert belonged to the right wing of the FDP and was critical of the party's left-leaning currents. In 1995 the party's conservative wing, centred on Kleinert and the parliamentary group leader Hermann Otto Solms, was in conflict with the civil-liberties wing of the party and with the Federal Minister of Justice, Sabine Leutheusser-Schnarrenberger, who opposed electronic surveillance of private homes and supported dual citizenship. He also received negative press coverage over a dispute in a pub.

== Personal life and death ==

Kleinert had one child. He died in Hanover on 17 June 2016 at the age of 83. [ref: Trauerfeier für FDP-Politiker Detlef Kleinert, HAZ – Hannoversche Allgemeine]

data.title: Friedrich Vogel (politician)
data.text:
Friedrich Vogel (2 June 1929 – 9 December 2005) was a German judge and politician of the Christian Democratic Union (CDU). He was a member of the Bundestag from 1965 to 1966 and from 1969 to 1994. He was Minister of Justice of North Rhine-Westphalia in 1966 and Minister of State to the Federal Chancellor from 1982 to 1987.

== Early life and education ==

Vogel was born in Hahnenknoop, then in the district of Wesermünde and now part of Loxstedt in Lower Saxony. His father was an estate manager and later the farm manager at Handorf airfield near Münster. At the end of the Second World War, aged 15, Vogel served with a Luftwaffe unit in Denmark.

He attended the Ratsgymnasium in Münster and, from 1945, the Gymnasium Laurentianum in Warendorf, where he completed his Abitur in 1949. From 1949 to 1952 he studied law and political science at the University of Münster. He passed the first state law examination in 1952 and the second in 1956.

== Legal career ==

Vogel became a judge in July 1956. In April 1960 he was appointed Landgerichtsrat at the regional court (Landgericht) in Münster. He was a member of the Deutscher Richterbund, the German association of judges. From 1977 he practised as a lawyer in Warendorf, and from 1980 also as a notary.

== Political career ==

Vogel joined the Junge Union in 1952 and the CDU in 1953. He was deputy federal chairman of the Junge Union from 1963 to 1967. He was a co-opted member of the federal board of the CDU/CSU association for local politics and deputy regional chairman of the party's Protestant Working Group (Evangelischer Arbeitskreis) in Westphalia-Lippe. He was deputy federal chairman of the Protestant Working Group from 1978 to 1993. From 1956 to 1972 he was a member of the Warendorf town council.

From 1970 to 1986 he chaired the Federal Working Group of Christian Democratic Lawyers (Bundesarbeitskreis Christlich-Demokratischer Juristen, BACDJ). During this period the group held legal policy congresses in Karlsruhe under the title Recht sichert die Freiheit ("Law secures freedom") in 1975, 1978, 1983 and 1986.

=== Minister of Justice of North Rhine-Westphalia ===

On 5 October 1966 Minister-President Franz Meyers appointed Vogel Minister of Justice of North Rhine-Westphalia. After the coalition between the CDU and the FDP ended, the FDP and the SPD elected Heinz Kühn Minister-President. Vogel left office on 8 December 1966.

=== Member of the Bundestag ===

Vogel was elected to the Bundestag in the 1965 federal election. He left parliament on 6 October 1966 on joining the state government of North Rhine-Westphalia. He was elected again in 1969 and remained a member until 1994. He entered the Bundestag each time through the CDU state list in North Rhine-Westphalia and stood as the party's candidate in the Ennepe-Ruhr-Kreis. Bundestag records list him as "Vogel (Ennepetal)".

From 1968 to 1969 he was a member of the commission under the Article 10 Act, which oversees restrictions on the privacy of correspondence and telecommunications. From 1971 to 1977 he chaired the CDU/CSU parliamentary group's working group on home affairs and legal policy.

From 1977 to 1982 he chaired the Mediation Committee of the Bundestag and Bundesrat. As chairman he signed the committee's notices to the President of the Bundestag, including those on an amendment to the law on public assemblies in September 1978 and on the Tax Amendment Act 1979 in November 1978. He presented the committee's recommendations to the plenary.

=== Minister of State to the Federal Chancellor ===

Following the election of Helmut Kohl as Chancellor, Vogel was appointed Minister of State to the Federal Chancellor on 4 October 1982. He was responsible for the government's relations with the Bundesrat. He left office on 12 March 1987, after the 1987 federal election.

=== Human rights subcommittee ===

From 1987 to 1994 Vogel chaired the Subcommittee on Human Rights and Humanitarian Aid of the Bundestag's Foreign Affairs Committee. On 22 February 1988 the subcommittee held a public hearing on whether German citizens were held against their will and under conditions violating human rights in Colonia Dignidad in Chile. Former members of the colony, their relatives and the colony's doctor Hartmut Hopp took part. The hearing was not a committee of inquiry, and those invited did not appear as witnesses. The public prosecutor's office in Bonn investigated Hopp from at least the time of the hearing.

=== Committee of inquiry on Kommerzielle Koordinierung ===

In the 12th Bundestag (1990–1994) Vogel chaired the first committee of inquiry, which examined the Kommerzielle Koordinierung (KoKo), the East German foreign-currency organisation headed by Alexander Schalck-Golodkowski. The committee issued interim reports in 1992, a final report in May 1994 and a supplementary report in November 1994. He did not stand in the 1994 federal election.

== Personal life ==

Vogel was a Protestant. He was married and had five children. He died in Warendorf on 9 December 2005. His papers are held by the Archive for Christian Democratic Policy in Sankt Augustin.

== Selected works ==

* "Wie geht die Politik der Erneuerung weiter? Außen-, Sicherheits- und Deutschlandpolitik". In: Evangelischer Arbeitskreis der CDU und CSU (ed.): Politik der Erneuerung. Bonn 1986, pp. 26–44.
* (ed., with Hartmut Bühl): Wehrdienst aus Gewissensgründen. Zur politischen und ethischen Legitimation der Verteidigung. Herford 1987.
* "Möglichkeiten und Grenzen 'christlicher Politik' unter der Geltung des Grundgesetzes der Bundesrepublik Deutschland". In: Stefan Smid, Norbert Fehl (eds.): Recht und Pluralismus. Hans-Martin Pawlowski zum 65. Geburtstag. Berlin 1997, pp. 77–94.

data.title: Brent Bokovoy
data.text:
Brent Bokovoy is an American filmmaker and screenwriter. He is known for the feature film Ronald's Little Factory (2023) and for the short horror film Monster in My Swimming Pool (2011), which won Universal's Halloween Horror Nights Short Film Competition in 2011. [ref: The Essential A&E Picks for Aug 3 - 9: Ronald's Little Factory, Park City Kimball Arts Festival, Ogden Pride, and more., Salt Lake City Weekly] [ref: Rants and Raves: Vote for San Diego Filmmakers, KPBS Public Media]

==Career==

In 2011, Bokovoy directed the horror short Monster in My Swimming Pool starring Lia Marie Johnson. [ref: The Sound of San Diego is...Kids' Music??, San Diego Reader] Bokovoy won Universal's Halloween Horror Nights Short Film Competition, and the film was screened during the Eyegore Awards at Universal Studios Hollywood. [ref: Stars, Screams And Scares At The 2011 “Eyegore” Awards, Neon Tommy] [ref: Event Report: The 2011 Eyegore Awards Celebrate the Best and Brightest of the Horror Genre, Dread Central] JoBlo.com described it as "curiously cute". [ref: EVENT: Universal's Hollywood Halloween Horror Nights 2011, JoBlo.com] KPBS arts reporter Beth Accomando wrote that the film was "smartly shot".

Bokovoy later wrote and directed Ronald's Little Factory, a dark comedy set within the culture of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. His use of a late-1980s horror aesthetic and the challenges of expanding the premise into a feature-length film were discussed in the Salt Lake City Weekly. Bokovoy made the film during the COVID-19 pandemic.

In a 2024 essay about contemporary Mormon cinema for the Association for Mormon Letters, film scholar Randy Astle examined Ronald's Little Factory alongside films including Heretic and Plan 10 from Outer Space. He conferred on the film's exaggerated performances, its throwback setting, and its theology on sexuality. [ref: Heretic, Humanism, and the Modern Transcendental Mormon Film, Association for Mormon Letters] In 2025, Bokovoy directed the mockumentary short Deathline – The Juicy Hidden Truth Behind the Killer Tomatoes, a tribute to the cult film Attack of the Killer Tomatoes. [ref: San Diego arts roundup: Arsenio Hall brings stand-up show to Sycuan Casino, San Diego Union-Tribune]

data.title: Thomas Bonham (died 1532)
data.text:
Thomas Bonham (by 1482 – 1532) was an English politician. He sat as MP for Essex in 1529. [ref: BONHAM, Thomas (by 1482-1532), of Stanway, Essex., History of Parliament Online]

== Family and education ==
He was educated at the Inner Temple. In 1508/9, he married Catherine, the daughter of Henry Marney, 1st Baron Marney, the widow of Edward Knyvet and they had five sons (including William Bonham) and two daughters.

== Offices held ==
He served as receiver-general of the Duchy of Lancaster from 1509 till his death, and steward of Savoy manor from 1523 till his death; justice of the peace for Essex from 1510 till possibly his death; recorder of Colchester from 1511 till 1529; commissioner of subsidy in Essex in 1512, 1514, 1515, 1523, 1524, and in Colchester in 1523, and 1524; he served in other commissions from 1512 till 1530; as keeper of writs and rolls, captain of common pleas in 1520; Sheriff of Essex and Hertfordshire from 1520 till February 1522, 1526 till 1527; and bencher of the Inner Temple in 1530.

== References ==

data.title: William James (MP, 1589)
data.text:
William James was an English politician. He sat as MP in 1589, though it is not known which constituency he sat for. [ref: JAMES, William., History of Parliament Online]

According to Simonds d'Ewes in 1682, he was appointed to the subsidy committee on 11 February 1589. [ref: The Journals of All the Parliaments during the Reign of Queen Elizabeth, John Starkey]
