data.title: Duncan A. Buell
data.text:
Duncan A. Buell (born October 17, 1950) is an American mathematician and computer scientist whose research and professional work have included computational number theory, high-performance computing, information retrieval, digital humanities, and election data analysis. He is Professor Emeritus at the University of South Carolina, where he previously held the NCR Chair in Computer Science and Engineering. [ref: ] He has also worked in government research environments, including the Institute for Defense Analyses’ Center for Computing Sciences. [ref: https://www.purplebreezepress.com/duncan-buell] [ref: Frontiers of Supercomputing II: A National Reassessment, University of California Press]

== Early life and education ==
Duncan A. Buell was born in Detroit, Michigan, United States. He received a Bachelor of Science in mathematics from the University of Arizona in 1971 [ref: https://www.fitsnews.com/wp-content/uploads/securepdfs/2024/12/Report_of_Dr_Duncan_Buell_on_Senate_District_29_Results_for_2024_General_Election.pdf], a Master of Arts in mathematics from the University of Michigan in 1972, and a Ph.D. in mathematics from the University of Illinois Chicago in 1976. His doctoral specialization was in number theory. [ref: ] [ref: ]

== Career ==
After completing his Ph.D., Buell worked as a research associate at Carleton University from 1976 to 1977. He then held assistant professor positions at Bowling Green State University from 1977 to 1979 and Louisiana State University from 1979 to 1985, where he subsequently became a tenured associate professor. [ref: https://www.amazon.in/Duncan-Buell/e/B005LYRXXW/ref=dp_byline_cont_book_1]

During this period, his research focused on number theory, algebraic structures, and computational methods in mathematics. His publications addressed topics including quadratic fields, class numbers, and computational aspects of algebraic number theory. [ref: Algorithmic Number Theory: 6th International Symposium, ANTS-VI, Burlington, VT, USA, June 13-18, 2004, Proceedings, Springer Berlin Heidelberg] [ref: Duncan Buell, scholar.google.com]

From 1986 to 2000, Buell worked at the Center for Computing Sciences, an institution operated by the Institute for Defense Analyses. The center, formerly known as the Supercomputing Research Center, conducted computational research in support of the U.S. National Security Agency.

His work involved high-performance computing, parallel computation, and large-scale algorithmic implementations. He also participated in research projects involving large-scale computations, including one described as the largest computation performed in the history of the U.S. intelligence community. [ref: Duncan A Buell, ACM Digital Library]

In 2000, Buell joined the University of South Carolina as Professor of Computer Science and Engineering. He served as department chair for nine years and as interim dean of the College of Engineering and Information Technology (2005–2006). [ref: https://www.hpcwire.com/2006/01/06/thats_why_its_called_research-1/]

== Selected Publications ==

* Binary Quadratic Forms: Classical Theory and Modern Computations [ref: https://www.amazon.de/-/en/Duncan-Buell/dp/1461245435]
* Fundamentals of Cryptography [ref: Fundamentals of Cryptography: Introducing Mathematical and Algorithmic Foundations, Springer International Publishing]
* Multiple peer-reviewed articles in journals including Journal of Number Theory, Information Processing and Management, and Fuzzy Sets and Systems (1979–present)

data.title: Linscp
data.text:
linscp (Linux Secure Copy) is a cross-platform file manager and SSH File Transfer Protocol (SFTP), File Transfer Protocol (FTP), WebDAV, Amazon S3, and Secure copy protocol (SCP) client for Linux and Microsoft Windows. Its source code is publicly available on [https://github.com/99ecarvalho/linscp GitHub]. The software is distributed under the GNU General Public License, version 3. [ref: linscp, linscp.org]

==Program==
linscp transfers files between a local computer and remote servers. It also provides tools to browse and manage remote files, compare directories, and synchronize their contents. SFTP and SCP connections use the Secure Shell (SSH) protocol.

The application provides two graphical layouts. Its Commander layout displays local and remote files in side-by-side panels, while the Explorer layout displays the remote files with a folder tree. The client can queue transfers and edit remote files using an internal or external editor.

The separate linscp-cli console client supports scripting and automation. The graphical and console clients share sites, settings and scripts across Linux and Windows. The project distributes packages for 64-bit Linux and for 64-bit Windows 10 and 11. [ref: linscp, GitHub]

linscp uses WinSCP's core for sessions, transfers, scripting and messages, with an interface built using Qt. Its SSH, SFTP and SCP support uses components from PuTTY; FTP and FTPS use FileZilla's FTP engine; WebDAV uses neon; and Amazon S3 support uses libs3. OpenSSL provides TLS and cryptographic functions. linscp is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by WinSCP. [ref: Licence and credits, linscp]

==Features==
* Support for SFTP and SCP over SSH, FTP and FTPS, WebDAV, and Amazon S3-compatible storage.
* Commander and Explorer graphical layouts.
* A site manager for saved connections, session URLs, and imports from PuTTY and KiTTY sessions, OpenSSH configuration, FileZilla, and WinSCP INI files. [ref: Site Manager, linscp]
* Queued and resumable transfers, transfer presets, and speed limits.
* Preservation of file modification timestamps during transfers. [ref: Transfer settings, linscp]
* Directory comparison and synchronization, including keeping a remote directory up to date.
* Remote file editing with automatic upload after saving.
* Command-line automation through linscp-cli, including script generation from a session.
* SSH password, public-key, keyboard-interactive, and Kerberos authentication; support for Pageant and OpenSSH agents; host-key and TLS-certificate checks; and an optional master password for saved passwords. [ref: Authentication, linscp]
* Windows integration with File Explorer, including Send To uploads, drag and drop, the local file context menu, URL handlers, and a taskbar jump list. [ref: Windows shell integration, linscp]
* A.NET assembly for C# and PowerShell that can control linscp-cli on Linux and Windows. [ref: WinSCP.NET assembly and PowerShell, linscp]
* Interface translations in 53 languages and a portable mode.

==History==
The first published pre-release, version 0.2.0, appeared on 15 October 2026. [ref: linscp 0.2.0, GitHub] The first official release, version 0.7.0, was published on 19 October 2026. [ref: linscp 0.7.0, GitHub]

data.title: Kajeneri Mugenzi Christian
data.text:
----

Kajeneri Mugenzi Christian is a Rwandan fintech executive and public official. He serves as the Chief Executive Officer of MTN MoMo Congo Brazzaville and as the Chairperson of the City of Kigali Council. [ref: Christian Mugenzi elected chair of City of Kigali council, [[The New Times (Rwanda)]

== Early life and education ==
Christian was born in Niamey, Niger, and spent his early childhood in West Africa before relocating with his family to Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo. He later moved to Kigali, Rwanda, where he completed his studies.

He graduated from the Science College of the University of Rwanda and completed post-graduate business management studies at the African Leadership University (ALU) School of Business.

== Career ==

=== Financial technology and banking ===
Christian has over 15 years of leadership experience in banking, telecommunications, and fintech across multiple African markets. He held senior positions at MTN Mobile Money Rwanda, Equity Bank, Airtel, and Ericsson.

He served as the Director of Payment Systems at the National Bank of Rwanda (BNR), where he led national payment system initiatives, financial inclusion strategies, and interoperability frameworks. [ref: National Bank of Rwanda Payment Systems Overview, [[The New Times (Rwanda)] He was later appointed Chief Executive Officer of MTN MoMo Congo Brazzaville, overseeing mobile money services and financial inclusion operations in Central Africa.

=== Public service ===
On 21 August 2024, Christian was appointed by President Paul Kagame as a councillor for the City of Kigali. [ref: President Kagame appoints six Kigali City councilors, IGIHE] On 22 August 2024, the council elected him as its Chairperson, succeeding Didas Kayihura Muganga. In this capacity, he oversees council governance, urban infrastructure policies, and the implementation of the Kigali City Master Plan. [ref: End of the City Council's five-year term: Key achievements in infrastructure and urbanisation, City of Kigali]

data.title: János Farkas
data.text:
----

== Early life and Studies ==
János Farkas's family history is rooted in political tragedy and noble secrecy. Following the war of independence in 1848, his maternal

great grandparents. [ref: Love story a szobor talpán, VAOL] participated in a conspiracy against the Viennese court. When the plot was uncovered, they were convicted and executed. Their orphaned daughter, Mária Szigeti was raised in the house of count Batthyány and his wife with the count's son in Zalacsány. When they grew up, they fell in love, but the Countess did not approve. They had a son József (adopted name Farkas). János Farkas, the sculpture, was the son of József, the grandson of the count. He was born in a small village in [https://savoly.hu/ Sávoly] (Somogysávoly) in western Hungary. He had a sister, Aranka and a brother Lajos.

[Name change: Although Farkas had a noble lineage, due to the situation, the child could not carry on the Batthyány name as Lajos Batthyány, in the extended family, was Hungary's first prime minister in 1848. A wealthy agricultural property owner, István Farkas married his biological mother Magda Szigeti, and adopted [ref: Love story a szobor talpán, Love story a szobor talpán] the boy, hence the name Farkas instead of Batthyány.]

Janos Farkas was born shortly after Worlds War I. He entered the world during a period of national despair, when the country lost 80% its territories. Political uncertainty peeked with a brief rise of communist flair of Hungarian Soviet Republic (Tanácsköztársaság) in 1919. [ref: Visit Szombathely]

Despite these turbulent times, his abilities were recognized early. He began school at age four at Keszthely, later moved to Balatonlelle, where he attended upper school (polgári). He completed the curriculum in two years, instead of four.

His artistic abilities caught the attention of the local priest who encouraged the youngster who started to sculpt at age 8. By age 11, he created a portrait of Christ [ref: Tizennégyéves szobrász zseni, Tolnai világlapja] and at fourteen, an industrialist [https://www.vaol.hu/kultura/2009/07/love-story-a-szobor-talpan? Nándor Rott] [ref: Titokzatos szobrok, rejtélyes üzenetek Farkas Jánostól, VAOL Vas vármegyei Hírportál], took the youngster to study at the Budapest School of Applied Arts (Országos Magyar Királyi Képzőművészeti Iskola), where he studied under Imre Simai. Farkas received recognition from János Pásztor, an established sculptor at the time. In his teen years, Farkas worked on private commissions to support his stay in Vienna where he was a frequent at the Art Gallery and enjoyed guiding visitors (unofficially). He passed his matura exams at 16 (customarily 18) [https://www.kozterkep.hu/adattar/lexikon_szocikk/1216? 1935-37]. His education was further sponsored by Baron Paul Szunyogh [ref: László Gyula: Farkas János (1920-1994), Hungaricana - Életünk 1997 (35. évfolyam 8. szám)]. Media coverage of Farkas's work began as early as age twelve and continued to gain attention including the supplementary section of Pesti Napló in 1936 [ref: Egy 14 éves szobrásztehetség útja a világhír felé, Uj Somogy].

The young sculptor continued his studies at the Academy of Fine Arts (Képzőművészeti Főiskola) a six-year institution, where he was formed by master artists Ferenc Medgyessy and Ferenc Sidló. Sidló remarked about Farkas: "We have embraced a talent such as the Hungarian land gives birth to just one or two every century" [ref: Látogatás Farkas Jancsinál az Epreskertben, Balatoni kurir] and Medgyessy similarly considered Farkas a "natural talent of his generation". The respect was mutual, Medgyessy was an important artistic influence. Farkas's nude sculpture Combing Hair, [ref: Fésülködő leány, Farkas János, Nemzeti Galéria] was submitted to the Szinyei competition and was accepted to the collection of the Museum of Fine Arts. Farkas won most competitions held for young artists. He started to read about art and sculptors at a very early age, finding the Museum of Fine Arts in Budapest to be perfect setting, where he could offer visitors his contextual interpretations.

Farkas spent his post-college scholarship years to study further in Vienna in 1941 and in Rome 1942-43. Rome was transformative, this was where he solidified his artistic style, devotion to renaissance. He worked in multiple mediums, but he had a preference to marble.

In 1947, he finally got his diploma.

== Family Life and Final Illness ==
Farkas met his first wife, Ilona Görgey ([https://www.myheritage.hu/family-trees/farkas/OYYV7RFEJWOJUIHMH7OOHJ37BE3DYBY?familyTreeID=0 1919-]2009) in college at the Budapest School of Fine Arts from where she graduated as a goldsmith. She had quite a historic prominent family background.

[Ilona (görgői és toporczi) Görgey belonged to the extended family of General Artúr Görgey, a hero who fought against the Austrian army in 1848 for Hungary's independence, while her mother Békássy Antónia, also came from an aristocratic background. Ilona's uncle [https://hlo.hu/portrait/ferenc_bekassy.html Ferenc Békássy], a poet, studied in Cambridge in Bedales School and Kings College as other members of the family. In these intellectual circles, Ferenc formed close friendships with Virginia Woolf - who published his poems in English - and John Maynard Keynes who later played a foundational role in establishing the World [https://orszagut.com/kornyezet/epiteszet-muemlekvedelem-zsennye-alkotohaz-sennyey-bezeredj-bekassy-kastelysors-6463 Bank].] [ref: Kastélysors, Orszagut]

Farkas and Ilona lived in his wife's family estate in Zsennye. He loved his mother-in-law, Békássy Antonia, and made a sculpture of her. They had a daughter, Zsófia, an architect and a son, András, who became sea captain.

In 1947 the Zsennye property was ceased by the communists, where an agricultural cooperative dried grain on the parquet floors. The family was forced to share the gardener's cottage with another couple. The living situation became increasingly strained and Farkas moved the family to his artist studio in Szombathely. There, Farkas and Ilona became deeply embedded in the local art community and pulled all strings imaginable to salvage the Zsennye residence. Unable to regain ownership, they managed to transfer the tenancy to Hungarian Republic Artist Foundation (later MANK), which used it as an artists' retreat. It was always Farkas's dream to buy back the castle at Zsennye, the opportunity never came.

From his second marriage with Zsuzsa Kovács had twin boys, Peter and Pál. They lived in Nemeskolta (Kolta). In the wake the failed 1956 anti-communist revolution, Farkas defected, as many others, awaited Zsuzsa and the boys in Yugoslavia for a year, in vain. To sustain himself, he worked in a ceramics factory in Zagreb sculpting multiple portraits of Michelangelo. Displaced once again as a refugee, he left Yugoslavia and permanently relocated in Pierrefonds neighborhood of Montreal, Canada in 1957. Leaving his family behind caused a profound emotional scar.

In 1974, Farkas married Claudette Gagnon, in Canada. After moving to the United States he was diagnosed with a throat cancer and underwent a laryngectomy. Farkas disliked the artificial sounding electrolarynx and avoided using it. Due to the surgery his verbal communication was severely limited. His vocal impairment led him to immerge in reading, searching for the origin of the Hungarian language alongside always working a sculpture. His dedication to his art remained a priority, on one occasion he modified the ceiling by cutting an opening into the attic just to fit the oversized clay study.

While physical distance, he cherished rare visits from his granddaughter and kept in touch with his children. He hosted nieces with his traditional Hungarian food.

János Farkas was diagnosed with lung cancer and died in 1994, in Greensboro, NC from complications of the disease.

== Select portfolio ==
WORKS in HUNGARY

* 1938 - Julika - Bronze head - First prize, Szinyei Társaság Tavaszi Szalon - in National Gallery (Nemzeti Galéria)
* 1938 - Little girl - bronze - First prize of Jelzálog Hitelbank - The portrait of Anikó Rott, the daughter of Nándor Rott. This piece was singled out as "exceptional, outstanding from other entries" by Esti Újság. [ref: A legfiatalabb művésznemzedék az Ernst Múzeum tavaszi szalonján, Esti Ujság]
* 1939 - [https://mng.hu/mutargyak/87806/ Combing hair] - Life size bronze - National Gallery (Nemzeti Galéria)
* 1940 - Madonna - Szilágyi Sándor prize - First place
* 1940 - Babszem - Leányfej paster - Museum of Fine Art Exhibit
* 1943 - Petőfi - Kolta

* 1946-47 - After WWII, Szombathely's cathedral suffered serious bombing damage. [ref: farkas – Magyar Katolikus Lexikon, lexikon.katolikus.hu] One scholarly resource estimates about 60 cathedral sculptures bear his mark of his restoration reconstruction work. Other works were in the cities of Szentgotthárd, Komló and Ajka.
* 1948 - Magyar összefogás (Hungarian Unity) - centenary monument, it commemorates the 1848-49 revolution, a war of independence from (from Austria). Inscription: "Együtt a jobb jövőért" (Together for a better future.) This piece has a particular significance in the sculpture's life as his grandfather lost his life for Hungary's freedom.

* 1948 - Derkovits Gyula relief - A Gyula Derkovits memorial plaques at his residence in Szombathely, Mátyás kir. u. 4. [ref: Derkovits Gyula utóélete Szombathelyen, Művészet]
* 1950 - Puskin [ref: Puskin, www.kozterkep.hu]- Located in Brenner Park, Szombathely. In the lime stone bust, the inscription has dual meaning. It could address Puskin's first love also a daughter of a Count at the same time can be to Farkas's muse, his first wife, Ilona in Latin Helena: "Parata est in tempore nativitatis amatae primae helena nominatur." could be largely interpreted as "It was created from the birth of his first love, Helena."
* 1954 - [https://www.kozterkep.hu/33515/vajar#fotolista Vájár / Miner] - in the city Komló. It is a limestone sculpture for the city's mining community. Originally stood beside the Kossuth mine bath building. In 2010 was moved to a small park at the corner of Kossuth Lajos Street and Berek Street. This is an example how a classical figurative style was adopted to the socialist/era subject matter. [ref: Előterjesztés - Komló Város Önkormányzat Képviselő-testületének 2023. április 26-án tartandó ülésére 104. oldal, www.komloonk.hu]
* 1956 - Erdély domborművek - Transylvania relieves - These are series of decorative arts on Kerepes úti housing estate buildings.

WORKS in CANADA

* 1957-58 - Beethoven - Double life size marble in Montreal (800 lbs)
* ? - [https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Teracotta_torso.jpg/120px-Teracotta_torso.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail Torso] - 3 ft - Glazed terracotta - signed top left shoulder. Raised on a square wood base.
* 1958-74 - Private collection portraits in marble, Carrara, terracotta torso [ref: Teracotta Torso, icollector]

WORKS in USA

* 1979 - The Student - 6 ft bronze [ref: The Student, Smithsonian Art Inventories Catalogue]- Greensboro, NC - life size bronze in Bicentennial Garden commemorating Dr. Caldwell's academy in 1767-1811, a log cabin that stood in the same park as the statue. Farkas argued the historical figure should be barefoot in order to represent early frontier students arriving from far away and grounded them to North Carolina. His technique was rare, he went beyond anatomy - he used a real model - he had an extraordinary talent to make bronze weightless.
* 1979-81 - Private work
* 1981-83 - Hinshaw - Life size private commission in marble - Hinshaw Memorial Garden, in Yadkinville, NC - Farkas worked on this piece for a couple of years simultaneously with other works. The statue was commissioned by Lucy Hinshaw Crater of her father Sylvester Hinshaw in 1983. She offered the garden to the town of Yadkinville which the town accepted in 1985. [ref: Hinshaw Garden, Town of Yadkinville]
* 1983 - Otway Burns - 12 ft bronze - Sea captain, senator fought to give more democratic rights to the poor and ease some hardships for slaves (however he was not an abolitionist) It was dedicated on May 6, 1983 on the 200th anniversary of the town of Swansboro [ref: Otway Burns (sculpture), Smithsonian, American Art Museum]
* 1985 - Josephus Daniels - 8 ft bronze [ref: Josephus Daniels, (sculpture), Smithsonian Art Inventories Catalogue]- Raleigh, NC - Farkas chose a deliberate pose, waving with right hand raised toward the sky while his left hand held his hat down at this side. He was shown in his trademark attire thigh length tail coat, a vest trousers and a shirt fastened with a bowtie. Daniels was a highly influential newspaper publisher. The statue was removed on June 6, 2020, when Daniels' supremacist background resurfaced. The family relocated the statue to private grounds.[https://www.newsobserver.com/news/local/article243559272.html] Statue of Josephus Daniels
* 1987 - Dr. Ronald E. McNair [ref: Dr. Ron McNair, Ronald E. McNair - NCA&T LibGuide: A&T Tributes and Honors] - 1.5 life size bronze bust - NC A&T State University, Greensboro, NC - Unique feature of the piece that Farkas detailed the NASA flight suit with a zipper. It is displayed on a granite pedestal outside McNair Hall. - McNair was an Astronaut who lost his life in the Challenger disaster. He was a scientist and a humanitarian. The statue was donated by Ralph Clay and Janice Pace [https://www.hmdb.org/m.asp?m=221866 Price]. Ronald McNair
* ? - Baby Beethoven - bronzed plaster

== Art Colonies ==
In Hungary art colonies, were popular collaborative spaces for specific disciplines such as painting, sculpting and literature. In the 1940s Farkas and his wife Ilona, hosted many artists at their estate in Zsennye. Active in Szombathely art circles, Farkas also drew his contemporaries to [https://www.flickr.com/photos/nora-meszoly/albums/72157626755876564/with/5736443902 Zsennye] gatherings. These colonies were hubs for intellectual conversations, a refuge from conformity and intimidation of the communist regime. Farkas rejected the state enforced style of socialist realism.

* Zsennye - prior to 1947
* Szombathely

== Legacy ==
János Farkas explored multiple mediums: plaster, porcelain, bronze and marble influenced by the renaissance. In North Carolina and in Hungary he was known primarily for his classical monuments. While he worked in professional independence in Canada and USA, he did so in relative isolation following his relocation from his intellectual and art communities in Hungary.

== Gallery ==

File:Otway Burns - Janos Farkas.jpg|Otway Burns - Janos Farkas
File:Ron McNair - Janos Farkas.jpg|Ron McNair Bust - Janos Farkas

data.title: User Needs for News
data.text:
== User Needs for News ==
User needs for news is a strategic and planning framework used by newsrooms and journalists to maximise audience engagement. As the name suggests, this approach is used to ensure that news articles, videos and other content is commissioned, created and published from angles which address the specific needs of the audience.

It draws from principles of human-centred design and User-centered design, in which the needs of the audience, or end user influence how the product or design is developed and created.

Proponents argue that if done correctly, newsrooms can create content that is more relevant for audiences [ref: [https://www.journalism.co.uk/why-user-needs-model-has-the-power-to-transform-your-newsrooms-beyond-traditional-reporting/] "Why user needs have the power to stop audiences feeling overwhelmed by the news". Journalism UK. 2025-03-19. Retrieved 2026-09-02] - and audiences will engage for longer, and with more regularity.

== Origins and background in news media ==
While news is most often associated with the relaying of facts, consumers have long read, watched or listened to news for a wide variety of reasons.

"Back in the 1940s, Bernard Berelson (1949) described how people living in New York felt a sense of companionship and connectedness from reading the newspaper, and from the 1970s onwards, researchers have detailed a wide range of ‘uses and gratifications’ – such as entertainment and escapism – that people can find through news or other forms of media use." [ref: [https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/more-just-facts-how-news-audiences-think-about-user-needs] "More than 'just the facts': How news audiences think about 'user needs' | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism". reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk. Retrieved 2026-09-02.]

News outlets had - and have - different ways of communicating information to publishing simple updates. Opinion pieces bring a personal perspective to any issue or subject; interviews allow readers to feel inspired or moved by a direct experience. Concise explainers provide context and background to unfolding events.

In short, before user needs was named thus, they mostly certainly existed.

The BBC was among the first to formalise a user needs approach, and in 2016 it developed the first user needs model [ref: [https://theaudiencers.com/9-the-model-that-transformed-the-bbc/] White, Madeleine (2023-03-15). "#9. The model that transformed the BBC". Audiencers. Retrieved 2026-09-02.], from which many subsequent frameworks have evolved. In this, the BBC identified six core reasons (needs) readers sought out news:

# Update me
# Keep me on Trend
# Educate me
# Give me Perspective
# Inspire me
# Divert me

These were not selected from inside the newsroom: it followed a thorough analysis of audience engagement and came from cues from the audience themselves. They discovered, for example, that while 70% of their published content on one of their news sites (BBC Russia) could be classed as updates, but in fact Update Me content accounted for only 7% of page views.

Data analysis is a key part of the user needs process: those applying this framework to their own newsrooms must combine audience-centric planning with post-publication data analysis in order to ascertain what works, what doesn't - and why.

== Development and versions ==
Since 2016, many other news organisations have adopted, adapted or created their own user needs framework. These organisations include (but are not limited to) The Conversation [ref: [https://smartocto.com/client-case/identifying-brand-specific-user-needs-the-conversation/]"Identifying brand-specific user needs with The Conversation". smartocto. Retrieved 2026-09-02.], The Atlantic [ref: [https://www.editorandpublisher.com/stories/the-atlantic-spent-two-years-studying-what-readers-and-listeners-need-heres-what-they-found,216143] Lab, Emily Goligoski "The Atlantic spent two years studying what readers and listeners need. Here's what they found". Editor and Publisher. data.title: Mübeccel Akdis
data.text:
Mübeccel Akdis, is a Turkish physician and immunologist based in Switzerland. She is a professor at the University of Zurich and leads the Immune Regulation research group at the Swiss Institute of Allergy and Asthma Research (SIAF) in Davos. Her research focuses on mechanisms of immune tolerance in allergic diseases, allergen-specific immunotherapy, and regulatory immune-cell populations. [ref: Editorial: Women in primary immunodeficiencies, Frontiers in Immunology]

== Education and career ==
Akdis graduated from the Faculty of Medicine at Uludağ University in Bursa, Turkey, in 1985. She joined the Swiss Institute of Allergy and Asthma Research in 1995, where she received a PhD in immunology, worked as a postdoctoral scientist and became a group leader in 2003. [ref: Board Member Biographies – Mübeccel Akdis, European Journal of Immunology]

She completed her habilitation (Venia Legendi) in experimental immunology at the Faculty of Medicine of the University of Zurich in 2005 and later became a professor at the university.

== Research ==
Akdis's research has addressed the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying immune tolerance and allergic inflammation. A 2023 editorial in Frontiers in Immunology described her as having contributed to understanding skin allergy and atopic dermatitis and as having played a leading role in research on immune-tolerance mechanisms.

Her research has included studies of allergen tolerance, high-dose allergen exposure in humans, mechanisms of allergen-specific immunotherapy, regulatory T cells, regulatory natural killer cells and IL-10-producing regulatory B cells.

More recently, her research has examined allergen-specific B-cell responses and their roles in food allergy and the development of immune tolerance. [ref: FEBS Datta Lecture – Mechanisms of food allergy and the role of allergen-specific B cells, 49th FEBS Congress]

== Awards and recognition ==
In 2006, Akdis received the Sedat Simavi Medicine Award.

In 2018, the American College of Allergy, Asthma and Immunology (ACAAI) presented Akdis with its International Distinguished Fellow Award. [ref: 2018 Award Winners, ACAAI Annual Scientific Meeting] The award is given to an individual living outside the United States and Canada who has demonstrated scholarly achievement, leadership or an outstanding professional reputation, or has participated in ACAAI's international activities. [ref: Awards and Lectureships, American College of Allergy, Asthma and Immunology]

In 2020, she received the Paul Ehrlich Award for Experimental Research from the European Academy of Allergy and Clinical Immunology. The University of Zurich reported that the award recognized her long-term research on allergy, immune regulation and skin immunology. [ref: Research Awards 2020, University of Zurich]

In the same year, the Government of the Canton of Graubünden presented Mübeccel Akdis and Cezmi Akdis with a Recognition Award for their research on human immune regulation. [ref: Anerkennungspreis an Mübeccel und Cezmi Akdis, Faculty of Medicine, University of Zurich]

Akdis received the Medical Science Award of the Dr. Nejat F. Eczacıbaşı Medical Awards in 2021. The Turkish Academy of Sciences reported that the award was given for her research in human immunology and noted that the Medical Science Award recognizes scientists whose body of research has made contributions to science at an international level. [ref: TÜBA-GEBİP Ödülü Sahibi Prof. Çadırcı'ya "Dr. Nejat F. Eczacıbaşı Tıp Ödülü", Turkish Academy of Sciences]

In 2025, Akdis received the FEBS Datta Medal from the Federation of European Biochemical Societies. She delivered the Datta Lecture, titled "Mechanisms of food allergy and the role of allergen-specific B cells", at the 49th FEBS Congress. [ref: Plenary Lectures, 49th FEBS Congress]

In 2026, the Austrian Society for Allergology and Immunology (ÖGAI) awarded Akdis the Karl Landsteiner Medal. The society describes the medal as recognizing scientists who have made important contributions to immunology. [ref: ÖGAI Medals – awardees 2026, Austrian Society for Allergology and Immunology]

data.title: GoMore
data.text:
----

GoMore is a Danish car-sharing company based in Copenhagen. It provides a platform for private individuals to rent out cars and also offers car leasing. In Spain, it operates under the name Amovens. [ref: Getaround Europe and GoMore merge to create Europe's largest peer-to-peer carsharing network, Tech.eu]

In May 2026, GoMore acquired the European operations of the American car-sharing company Getaround. The two businesses reported a combined total of more than five million users across 11 European countries. [ref: GoMore Becomes Europe's Largest Peer-to-Peer Car-Sharing Platform After Acquiring Getaround Europe, Øresund Startups]

== History ==

GoMore began in 2005 as a non-profit ride-sharing website, founded by Matias Møl Dalsgaard and Søren Riis. [ref: Gomore: fem år og to millioner brugere senere, TechSavvy] It became a for-profit business in 2011 and introduced peer-to-peer car rental and leasing services in 2014. [ref: Business model diversification in the sharing economy: The case of GoMore, Journal of Cleaner Production]

GoMore expanded into Sweden in 2014. [ref: Så blir bilsemestern billig, Dagens Nyheter] In March 2015, it acquired Amovens, a Spanish ride-sharing service founded by Diego Hidalgo in 2009. [ref: Spanish car sharing platform Amovens acquired by GoMore, Novobrief] It launched in France in 2016.

By 2017, GoMore had become Denmark's largest ride-sharing service, with more than 645,000 Danish members. [ref: Deleøkonomien i Danmark]

GoMore launched in Finland in late 2020. [ref: Oman auton voi vuokrata tuntemattomalle jopa ilman, että on itse paikalla, Yle] In April 2021, the Swiss insurance company Baloise invested approximately €5 million in GoMore. [ref: Baloise kauft sich bei dänischer Carsharing-Firma GoMore ein, cash.ch] GoMore launched in Switzerland in October 2021, [ref: Geld verdienen mit dem eigenen Auto?, Luzerner Zeitung] Austria in 2022 [ref: GoMore: So funktioniert die neue private Autovermietung in Österreich, Trending Topics] and Estonia in March 2024. [ref: Eestis alustab inimeselt inimesele autode jagamise platvorm GoMore, Raamatupidamisuudised]

GoMore closed its ride-sharing service in Denmark in February 2026. By then, Denmark was the only country where GoMore still offered ride-sharing. The company said it would focus on car rental and leasing. [ref: GoMore dropper samkørsel i Danmark, TV 2] [ref: GoMore dropper samkørsel: Ikke nok opbakning til idéen, Ingeniøren]

In May 2026, GoMore acquired Getaround's European business, which operated in several countries, including France, Norway, Belgium and Germany. The purchase was financed through investments from existing shareholders and loans from EIFO and Nordea.

At the time of the acquisition, the companies reported approximately 70,000 shared cars, 1.5 million annual rentals and net revenue exceeding €50 million. [ref: GoMore übernimmt Getaround Europe und wird größte Carsharing-Plattform Europas, Trending Topics] Getaround continued to operate as a separate platform. [ref: Getaround and GoMore: a new chapter for carsharing in Europe, Getaround]

== Services ==

GoMore allows private individuals to list cars for rent through its website and app. Renters can book available cars, some of which can be unlocked through the app without meeting the owner.

The company also offers car leasing. [ref: Nya tjänster för delad mobilitet, Trafikanalys] Its GoMore+ subscription provides discounts on car rentals. [ref: New: Get a discount every time you rent a car with GoMore+, GoMore]

data.title: Fox on Ice
data.text:
----

Fox On Ice is the joint artistic project of writer and performer Anna Luca Poloni and composer and musician Christian Mair. The shows are Performing Arts Concerts which combine original music, lyrics and film with performance.

Recent works are Orlando Trip (after Ludovico Ariosto and Virginia Woolf) and Polyxena – Female Voices of Troy (based on narratives surrounding the Trojan War). [ref: Mit Orlando auf Reisen, Die Presse] [ref: Macherin der Wortwiege mit Projekt in der Türkei, Kurier]

Fox On Ice is Vienna-based and touring internationally.

== Background and artistic work ==

Fox On Ice is the artistic project of Anna Luca Poloni and Christian Mair, which combines literary and mythological sources with original music, text, film and performance.

Currently, Fox On Ice is working on the trilogy “FE.MALE MYTH”, which consists of Orlando Trip (touring since 2022) [ref: Thomas Maurer ++ Fox On Ice, Ö1 Kulturjournal], Polyxena – Female Voices of Troy (premiered in 2026) and Joanna’s Love (planned for 2028).

== Orlando Trip ==

The Performing Arts Concert Orlando Trip is the first part of FE.MALE MYTH and deals with themes of transformation, identity, gender, travel and freedom.

It is based on Ludovico Ariosto’s epic poem Orlando furioso and Virginia Woolf’s novel Orlando: A Biography. Original songs and intermezzi are telling the story of the key moments in Orlando’s life. Film is an integral part of the show.

The music is characterised by Die Presse as incorporating indie, punk, chanson and spoken poetry.

Orlando Trip has been presented internationally since 2022, including the United States, Canada, Europe, Turkey and Sri Lanka. [ref: ORLANDO TRIP - Performing Arts Concert by Fox On Ice, Austrian Embassy Ottawa] [ref: Orlando Trip, Austrian Cultural Forum Washington DC]

In 2024, a studio concept album Orlando Trip was released. [ref: Musikalischer Tribut an Orlando auf Virginia Wolfs Spuren, Kronen Zeitung]

== Polyxena – Female Voices of Troy ==

Polyxena – Female Voices of Troy is the second part of FE.MALE MYTH and premiered on 13 August 2026 at the Troy Museum in Çanakkale, Turkey. [ref: POLYXENA – Female Voices of Troy, Austrian Cultural Forum Istanbul]

Drawing on literary and mythological traditions surrounding the Trojan War, including Homer, Euripides and Ovid, Polyxena approaches the material from female perspectives.

The work combines music, literature, film and live performance.

On October 7, 2026 Austrian Radio Ö1 broadcasted a radiosession of Polyxena. [ref: Neue Lesarten überlieferter Mythen: Fox On Ice, Ö1]

data.title: Brickflow
data.text:
Key Facts
Full legal company name: Property Funding Hub Limited
Incorporation / founding year: 17 July 2019
Founders: Ian Humphreys, Robert Lange, Frazer Campbell
Headquarters: Floor 1, 1-3 Worship St, London EC2A 2AB
Industry: Financial technology
Services: Online marketplace for bridging loans, commercial mortgages and development finance
Website: Brickflow.com
Companies house number: 12109370
Lead section
Brickflow is a British online marketplace for specialist property finance. Its platform allows brokers, property developers and investors to search for and compare bridging loans, commercial mortgages and development finance from a panel of lenders, with applications made on the platform, through brokers.[5][6] Brickflow is a trading name of Property Funding Hub Limited, a London-based company registered in England and Wales [incorporation year 2020].[8] It was co-founded by Ian Humphreys and Robert Lange, and the platform launched in November 2020.[1] In 2026 the company stated that its panel included more than 160 lenders.[6]
History
Brickflow was co-founded by Ian Humphreys, a property finance professional, and software developer Robert Lange.[1] [Incorporation year TO CONFIRM – Companies House.] The platform launched in November 2020 as an online search engine for development finance loans, initially giving access to 18 lenders.[1]
In 2023 Brickflow became a partner of the National Association of Commercial Finance Brokers (NACFB) and began adding bridging lenders to its panel.[9] In October 2023 it published Solving the UK's Housing Shortage, a 58-page white paper that criticised government housing policy and proposed a 10-stage framework for increasing housebuilding; it was covered by FT Adviser, Sky News [17] and regional radio.[10][16] In the first quarter of 2024 it added 11 lenders and reported completing a £16.85 million development finance loan for a 103-flat scheme in Hastings, its largest completed loan at that time.[4] Later in 2024 it partnered with Deallocker, a second-charge and equity funding platform,[2] and integrated its tool with auction house websites through broker partners.[3]
In 2026 Brickflow added property data from Sprift to its appraisals,[11] launched a joint distressed-property service with Revcore Asset Management,[6] and introduced automated decisions in principle with the lender Together.[12] It reported more than £520 million in loan offers on the platform in the second quarter of 2026.[5]
Platform and services
Brickflow operates an online marketplace that connects borrowers and their brokers with specialist property lenders.[5][6] Users enter the details of a proposed loan, and the platform returns matching products from lenders on its panel.[1] Brokers can then apply to selected lenders through the platform and request a decision in principle.[6]
The platform covers bridging loans, commercial mortgages and development finance. In the second quarter of 2026, bridging finance accounted for the largest share of loan offers by value.[5] Brickflow also offers a version of the platform that brokers and partner businesses, such as auction houses, can embed on their own websites.[3][7]
Reception and recognition
Brickflow has won two awards at the NACFB Commercial Lender Awards, run by the National Association of Commercial Finance Brokers: Technological Innovation of the Year in 2023[15] and Industry Supplier of the Year in 2024.[13] At the 2025 awards it was shortlisted for Industry Supplier of the Year and Pioneers of the Year.[14]

data.title: Andrea Monath Schumacher
data.text:
----

Andrea Monath Schumacher is an American interior designer and author based in Denver, Colorado. She founded Andrea Schumacher Interiors in 1999. Her work has received regional and national design recognition, including inclusion in 5280’s 2021 list of Colorado home-industry influencers, and her book Vibrant Interiors: Living Large at Home won the 2023 Colorado Book Award in the pictorial category. [ref: Meet Colorado's Top 15 Home Industry Influencers of 2021, 5280] In 2026, Colorado State University named her an Outstanding Alumna. [ref: Designing a career: Andrea Schumacher, a 2026 CHHS Outstanding Alumni]

=== Early life and education ===
Schumacher grew up in several locations in the United States and abroad, including Nigeria. She studied interior design at Colorado State University. Before establishing her design practice, she worked in television set design in Los Angeles, including on the NBC soap opera Days of Our Lives. [ref: Fashion and Travel Inspire This Former TV Set Designer’s Gutsy Interiors, 1stDibs Introspective]

=== Career ===
Schumacher founded Andrea Schumacher Interiors in Denver in 1999. A 2019 profile in Colorado Homes & Lifestyles discussed the development of her practice, her use of color and pattern, and the influence of her grandmother, artist Elizabeth Monath, on her interest in art and design. [ref: 2019 Circle of Excellence: Interior Designer Andrea Schumacher, Colorado Homes & Lifestyles]

Schumacher’s residential work has appeared in editorial coverage in Colorado Homes & Lifestyles. In 2010, a residence she designed was selected as the magazine’s “Home of the Year.” [ref: 2010 Home of the Year, Colorado Homes & Lifestyles]

A 2021 profile in 1stDibs Introspective discussed Schumacher’s work as influenced by travel, fashion, and her childhood experiences abroad. The publication also covered her transition from television set design to residential interior design and the growth of her Denver-based firm.

In 2021, 5280 included Schumacher in its list of Colorado’s top home-industry influencers, citing her long-running Denver practice, expansion beyond Colorado, and development of wallpaper and textile collections.

In 2022, Andrea Schumacher Interiors received a regional Luxe RED Award for interior design for a Denver Tudor Revival residence. [ref: Andrea Schumacher Interiors, Luxe RED Awards]

In 2025, Schumacher participated in the 50th Kips Bay Decorator Show House New York. [ref: Design, Drama, and Deadlines at the Kips Bay Decorator Show House New York 2025, Architectural Digest]

In 2026, Luxe Interiors + Design featured a Cherry Hills Village residence designed by Schumacher, highlighting her use of color, vintage furnishings, art, and custom interior architectural details. [ref: Andrea Monath Schumacher Designs A Colorful Colorado Abode, LUXE Interiors + Design]

In 2026, Schumacher was named a Leader in Small Business by the Denver Business Journal, which recognizes leaders of locally owned companies in the Denver region. [ref: Special Report: The DBJ honors Leaders in Small Business award winners, Denver Business Journal]

=== Publications ===
Schumacher is the author of Vibrant Interiors: Living Large at Home, published by Gibbs Smith in 2022. Foreword Reviews published an independent review of the book, describing its focus on Schumacher’s interiors, design approach, and use of color and multicultural influences.

The book won the 2023 Colorado Book Award in the pictorial category, awarded by Colorado Humanities. [ref: 2023 Colorado Book Awards honor winners in 16 categories at Colorado Springs celebration, The Colorado Sun]

Gould Property Company is associated with the Gould family, an American family whose prominence dates to the 19th century through the railroad and financial activities of Jay Gould [ref: ]. Earlier generations of the Gould family were associated with railroad and financial enterprises, while later generations became involved in real estate and related businesses. The family lineage relevant to the company runs from Jay Gould to his son George Jay Gould, his grandson Kingdon Gould Sr., and his great-grandson Kingdon Gould Jr. [ref: About, Gould Property Company] [ref: DC's Top 10 Real Estate Dynasties, Bisnow] The Gould family's business interests have extended beyond Gould Property Company. Earlier generations were associated with railroad and financial enterprises, while later generations developed interests in real estate and related businesses.

Kingdon Gould Jr. established Gould Property Company in the 1950s. The company subsequently became one of the family's principal real estate businesses in the Washington, D.C., and Baltimore metropolitan areas. The company's own history identifies Gould Jr. as its founder and traces its origins to land acquisitions made during the 1950s.

Kingdon Gould III, the son of Kingdon Gould Jr., subsequently became owner and vice president of Gould Property Company [ref: DC's Top 10 Real Estate Dynasties, Bisnow]. He has also served in leadership roles with the DowntownDC Business Improvement District [ref: Our Team, Downtown DC].

Gould Property Company's real estate activities have included development, ownership, investment, and management of commercial and residential properties. Its portfolio has included office buildings, residential properties, hospitality, retail, industrial, and mixed-use developments.

Notable projects and properties associated with the company include:

Konterra

Konterra is a mixed-use development encompassing approximately 1,400 acres in Prince George's County, Maryland, near Laurel, and the intersection of Interstate 95 and Maryland Route 200. The development includes 17 existing office buildings and has frontage along I-95 and MD 200. It is located near the National Security Agency, Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory, Goddard Space Flight Center, and the University of Maryland. Development of Konterra has proceeded in phases, with construction on the current phase beginning in April 2026 and a groundbreaking ceremony held on May 14, 2026, in anticipation of the future Konterra Town Center East, an approximately 400-acre mixed-use district withing Konterra [ref: Konterra breaks ground on first residential project » The Business Monthly, The Business Monthly]. The development plan calls for approximately 1.5 million square feet of retail, dining, and entertainment space; 3.8 million square feet of office space; 600 hotel rooms; and approximately 4,500 residential units. Plans also call for approximately 8.5 miles of parks, trails, and public plazas. The first residential phase of Town Center East is The Marais, a townhome community being developed by Caruso Homes [ref: ] [ref: The Downtown Of A Mini-City 40 Years In The Making Breaks Ground, Bisnow].

600 Massachusetts Avenue NW is an approximately 400,000-square-foot office building in downtown Washington, D.C., near the Walter E. Washington Convention Center and the Gallery Place and Chinatown neighborhoods. The 10-story building was completed in 2016. Gould Property Company developed the project in partnership with Oxford Properties Group. [ref: Oxford, Gould Celebrate Opening Of 600 Mass Ave, Bisnow] [ref: 600 Massachusetts Avenue, SK&A]

[ref: More Good News for CityCenterDC, Downtown DC] [ref: Gould kicks off his ‘next generation’, Washington Business Journal]

401 on Ninth, at 401 9th Street NW in Washington, D.C., is a mixed-use development associated with Gould Property Company. Gould Property Company identifies the property as a completed project undergoing reinvestment. [ref: Groundbreaking at 600 Massachusetts Ave, Downtown DC] [ref: ] [ref: 401 on Ninth, Gould Property Company]

1616 Rhode Island Avenue

data.title: Frutiger Eco
data.text:
Frutiger Eco is a design trend that dominated as a subgenre to Frutiger Aero between the mid 2000s and early 2010s.

== It's start ==
Frutiger Eco was first seen in 2004-2005. It's first appearance was most likely in Microsoft's Windows Vista's aero interface. It also appeared in gOS and Wallpapers in Android (2.3-4.0).

== It's Fame ==
In 2007-2014, this design trend was most used. It was used in ads like the The 3rd-Gen Toyota Prius (2009), The Nissan Leaf (2010) launch, [https://www.sourcewatch.org/index.php/General_Electric's_Ecomagination_Campaign GE's "Ecomagination" Campaign], and also in Bottled water Packaging like Poland spring, Nestlé Pure Life, and [https://www.aquafina.com/en-US/ Aguafina] (Eco-Fina).

== It's downfall ==
It got slowly less popular as people switched to Flat Design, Apple went on the new Flat Trend with iOS 7 and Microsoft too with Windows 8. More and more company's started going to Flat design. People didn't want Frutiger Eco gone, but as less and less people used stuff with Frutiger Eco, as more and more company's changed to flat design, It died off around early 2020s when Microsoft discontinued Windows 7.

== Coming back ==
Apple made a shocking suprise by anouncing Liquid Glass in 2025, that resembles Frutiger Eco (and aero), and now slowly, Frutiger Eco is coming back. Everything is slowly getting more rounded and colorful.

The design & user interface are heavily inspired by Apple's designs, including its Liquid Glass design, the lock screen taking the looks of an Apple iPad, and the main operating system heavily inspired by Apple's macOS. After developer testing when the operating system is publicly released, it is aimed as a general-purpose system designed for minimalists and productivity enthusiasts.

data.title: Cara Korhonen
data.text:
Cara Korhonen (born 29 September 2005) [ref: Cara Korhonen, www.tennis.com] is a Finnish-Australian tennis player who competes primarily on the ITF Women's World Tennis Tour. [ref: Cara Korhonen – ITF Tennis, International Tennis Federation] She has reached a career high WTA singles ranking of No. 1038 on 20 July 2026.

She joined Brigham Young University (BYU), BYU Cougars, as a graduate student athlete in 2026, combining NCAA Division I tennis with postgraduate studies.

== Early life and background ==

Korhonen began playing tennis at around the age of four.  She developed through junior tennis programs in Australia.

As a junior, she won the NSW Age 10-and-under 2015 Medibank Age. [ref: 2015 Medibank Age (Gold JT) – Winners, Tennis Australia Tournaments] She was also selected as an ANZ Tennis Hot Shots of the Year participant, earning a trip to the Australian Open. [ref: Stanhope Gardens local wins VIP trip to Australian Open 2016, Hills to Hawkesbury Living] [ref: Congratulations to our April ANZ Australia Tennis Hotshot of the Year nominee, Cara Korhonen, Facebook]

In 2017, Korhonen was a member of the Metropolitan Green Dynamite team that won the 2017 Jan O’Neill Cup at the New South Wales 12-and-under State Teams Championships. [ref: 12u-State Teams Champions crowned]

In 2022, Korhonen competed in the girls’ singles qualifying event at the Australian Open Junior Championships in Melbourne. [ref: Australian Open Junior Championships 2022 – Draws and Results, International Tennis Federation]

In December 2023, Korhonen competed at the Australian 18-and-under Championships at Melbourne Park, reaching the girls’ doubles quarterfinals. [ref: Stevens shining at 2023 18/u Australian Championships, www.tennis.com.au]

== Education ==
Alongside her tennis career, Korhonen completed a Bachelor of Science in Psychology in University of Southern Queensland, Australia, in approximately 17 months while competing internationally. [ref: Tenniksen vuoksi Australiasta kisaan Savitaipaleelle, Etelä-Saimaa] [ref: Tough times in Wagga Wagga as young tennis stars chase grand slam dreams, ABC News] In 2026 she began postgraduate studies at Brigham Young University (BYU), pursuing a master’s degree in Nutritional Science while competing for the university's NCAA Division I women's tennis team. [ref: Cara Korhonen – Women's Tennis, BYU Athletics] [ref: How BYU tennis player Cara Korhonen balances school, sports, BYU Daily Universe]

== Collegiate and Professional tennis ==
Korhonen has competed on the ITF Women’s World Tennis Tour, participating in tournaments in Australia and internationally.

Korhonen achieved a career-high WTA singles ranking of world No. 1038 on 20 July 2026 and doubles No. 1470 on 26 December 2022. [ref: ]

Korhonen joined BYU women’s tennis program in 2026, competing in NCAA Division I.

In September 2026, Korhonen and her BYU teammate Sue Yan Tan reached the women’s doubles quarterfinals at the USTA Southern California Championships in San Diego. [ref: Cougars make strong showing at USTA SoCal Championships, BYU Athletics - Official Athletics Website - BYU Cougars] The following month the pair advanced to the doubles semifinals at the ITA Mountain Regional Championships in Provo, Utah. [ref: Bergeson qualifies for NCAA Individual Nationals as BYU hosts ITA Mountain Regional Championships, BYU Athletics - Official Athletics Website - BYU Cougars]

data.title: Kovur Annon
data.text:
Kouvr Annon (born May 31, 2000) is an American social media personality and model. Originally from Oahu, Hawaii, she became known for her content on TikTok and Instagram and her involvement in the Los Angeles-based creator collective the Hype House. She appeared in the Netflix reality series Hype House (2022), which followed members of the group and their lives as online creators [ref: Kouvr Annon - Influencer, Model, YouTuber, TV Insider].

Annon married singer-songwriter and fellow former Hype House member Alex Warren on June 22, 2024, in Escondido, California.

== Early life ==
Kouvr Annon was born in Oahu, Hawaii. She has four sisters.

Annon spent her childhood in Hawaii and lived there until graduating from high school in 2018 [ref: Time to Meet Kouvr Annon, Who Inspired Alex Warren’s Hit Song “Ordinary”, Cosmopolitan]. In July of that year, she began posting modelling photographs on Instagram.

Also in 2018, she connected with Alex Warren through Snapchat. Within four months of meeting online, Annon moved from Hawaii to California to be with him. The couple briefly lived in a car before establishing themselves as social media creators.

== Career ==

=== Early Social Media Activity ===
Annon began sharing modelling photographs on Instagram in July 2018. Her content expanded to include fashion, travel and promotional posts, alongside collaborations with Alex Warren [ref: Kouvr Annon’s biography: age, height, birthday, net worth, siblings - Legit.ng, www.legit.ng].

She also developed a presence on YouTube, publishing videos featuring activities and challenges with Warren, including “We Did Couples Yoga.” On TikTok, she became known for short lip-sync and dance videos, frequently featuring Warren and other creators [ref: Kouvr Annon - Agent, Manager, Publicist Contact Info, Booking Agent Info].

=== Hype House ===
In 2019, Annon joined the Hype House, a collective of social media creators whose early members included Charli D’Amelio and Addison Rae. Her participation in the group helped expand her public profile through collaborative content.

Annon appeared in the Netflix reality series Hype House, which premiered on January 7, 2022 [ref: See The First Look at the TikTok Reality Show Hype House and When It’s Coming to Netflix, E! Online]. The series followed the creators’ personal relationships, shared living arrangements and work producing online content. Annon’s relationship with Warren featured in the programme.

After filming concluded in spring 2021, Annon and Warren moved out of the shared residence in October that year. In a subsequent update, Hype House co-founder Thomas Petrou said that they remained members of the collective and had moved because they wanted their own space. Later reporting described the couple as leaving the group in 2022, as Warren increasingly pursued a music career.

=== Subsequent Work ===
Annon continued creating content for her individual social media accounts, including modelling, travel and sponsored Instagram posts, as well as TikTok videos featuring Warren.

On October 2, 2023, MGA Entertainment announced Annon as one of the guest judges for Bite Size, a TikTok reality competition series featuring miniature-food challenges based on the company’s Miniverse products.

In 2025, she appeared in the music video for Warren’s single “Ordinary,” a song inspired by their relationship.

== Personal Life ==

=== Relationship & Marriage ===
Annon began a relationship with Alex Warren in 2018 after they connected through Snapchat via a mutual friend. Four months later, she moved from Hawaii to California to live with him. The couple experienced housing insecurity early in their relationship and spent time living together in a car [ref: All About Alex Warren and Kouvr Annon's Relationship (Which Inspired His Hit Song 'Ordinary'!), People].

Their relationship became a recurring subject of their online content. Warren proposed on December 31, 2022, during a trip to the mountains, which he described as Annon’s first experience of snow [ref: Alex Warren and Kouvr Annon’s Relationship Timeline: From Snapchat Friends to ‘Ordinary’ Soulmates, Us].

The couple married on June 22, 2024, at Ethereal Gardens in Escondido, California, with 275 guests. John Bigelow, who had previously provided them with a car to sleep in, officiated. Warren’s suit incorporated sunflower and pelican designs in tribute to his late parents. Annon changed into a Milla Nova corset-and-skirt ensemble for the reception, and the couple danced to Taylor Swift’s “Lover.” [ref: All the Details from Musician Alex Warren and Kouvr Annon's Romantic Garden Wedding (Exclusive)]

For the ceremony, Annon wore Galia Lahav’s Abbey gown, a strapless dress featuring an embroidered bodice and a pleated silk-tulle skirt [ref: Hype House’s Kouvr Annon Stuns in Galia Lahav at Wedding to Alex Warren, Galia Lahav].

Their relationship inspired Warren’s single “Ordinary,” released in February 2025. Annon also appeared in the song’s music video [ref: ALEX WARREN ASCENDS EVEN HIGHER WITH “ORDINARY” OFFICIAL MUSIC VIDEO, Warner Music Ireland].

=== Health & Body Image ===
Annon has publicly discussed difficulties with body image and online harassment. In August 2020, after a TikTok video mocking her appearance circulated, she described longstanding insecurities and the effect of negative comments on her self-confidence. She condemned body-shaming and encouraged people to consider the impact of their words. Fellow creator Charli D’Amelio publicly supported her [ref: Charli D’Amelio Tweets Out Against Body Shaming After a TikTok About Kouvr Annon Goes Viral, Seventeen].

In a July 2022 appearance alongside Warren on the podcast Not Gonna Make It, Annon discussed diagnoses of endometriosis and polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) [ref: Why Alex Warren Quit Vlogging. (ft. Alex Warren & Kouvr) EP. 32, Apple Podcasts]. In a 2024 interview on Just Trish, Warren described her seeking medical care and adopting healthier eating habits [ref: ].

Following their June 2024 wedding, the couple began trying to conceive. During his 2026 Finding Family on the Road tour, Warren told an audience that they were trying for a baby that year.

=== Interests ===
Annon has shared horse-related content on social media, alongside interests including knitting and interior design. A January 2026 summary of a TODAY profile noted that her posts featured a newly acquired horse.

== References ==
