== Characters ==

=== Hosts ===
* Announcer is the host of the first and sixth seasons of Battle for Dream Island, who also secretly hosted the first five episodes of Battle for Dream Island Again before making his return as the final antagonist in Battle for B.F.B. He is a gray rectangular speaker box from outer space, who offered the contestants Dream Island in the first season and frequently gets concerned over budget cuts, which often effects on how he runs the show. He was put up for rejoin in BFDI:TPOT 25 despite having never competed before.

===Algebraliens===
These creatures are extraterrestrial beings shaped like mathematical symbols (usually numbers) that originate from a place called the “Equation Playground”. They are major characters in Season 4 and 5 of BFDI and jacknjellify’s subscriber milestone videos. Algebraliens tend to have reality-warping powers, though not all of them are shown to have said powers.
* Zero (voiced by Xander Archibald) is a gray Algebralien representing the number zero.
* One (voiced by Emily Pitcher) is a blue Algebralien representing the number one. The first canonical appearance of One shows her as a lonely, self-conscious person who constantly seeks to interact with others but is dismissed or ignored. One's own mental health is shown to be deteriorating from the lack of communication with anyone, which causes her to become more aggressive around people. When she is locked inside the Moon, she turns more psychologically unstable and starts a revenge plot against the Algebraliens to repair Three but Three killed her and turns to pieces.
* Two (voiced by Niall Burns) is a green Algebralien representing the number two. They were the host of Battle for Dream Island: The Power of Two up until "Seasonal Shift".
* Three (voiced by Em Mintz-Kreyns) is a red Algebralien representing the number three. They often act kind and social and want to include everyone the majority of the time. They are shattered and killed by One in TPOT 20, and are revived in an unstable state.
* Four (voiced by Michael Huang) is the host of the fourth season of Battle for Dream Island: Battle for B.F.D.I. They are a blue Algebralien representing the number four. They are chaotic and mischievous, often torturing contestants for fun and, when provoked in the first half of BFB, also not tolerating criticism. In the second half, he becomes more calm, friendly and humble. They are shown to have god-like powers with which he can warp reality and teleport and eliminate contestants by sending them to a classroom called the "E.X.I.T.", which itself is in a pocket dimension he made in his body called the "Fourest". He also frequently screeches at contestants and shoots beams at them when provoked.
* Five (voiced by Dane Trent) is a purple Algebralien representing the number five. They are Three’s best friend and are very irritable and a stickler for the rules.
* Six (voiced by Florence Chapell) is a light blue colored Algebralien representing the number six.
* Seven (voiced by Griffin Weber) is a dark gray colored Algebralien representing the number seven. They like to tell jokes and make them funny but they usually fall flat and no one will eventually like them.
* Eight (voiced by Sam Thornbury) is a gray colored Algebralien representing the number eight.
* Nine (voiced by Sam Thornbury) is a white colored Algebralien representing the number nine. They own glasses and a yellow and blue skateboard and usually act like they’re “cool”.
* Ten (voiced by Bryan Ndubisi) is an orange colored Algebralien representing the number ten. In “Thanks for 2,000,000 subscribers!”, their skin gets eaten up by a green seven (which was actually Fourteen in disguise).
* Fourteen (voiced by Ivan Maslov) is a dark green colored Algebralien representing the number fourteen. They are a cannibal who like to eat people’s skin. In “Thanks for 2,000,000 subscribers!”, they split into two dark green sevens, one of them eventually going to Ten’s house and eating their skin.
* Fifteen (voiced by Joseph Pak) is a dark red colored Algebralien representing the number fifteen. She is very strict and lives in a cabin in the forest and also has a crush on Zero.
* X (voiced by Cary Huang) is the co-host of the fourth season of Battle for Dream Island: Battle for B.F.D.I. They are a yellow Algebralien representing the variable X and Four’s best friend.

=== Contestants ===
The contestants are characters (often objects) that compete for a prize.
==== Debuted in Battle for Dream Island ====
* Blocky (voiced by Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFDI, and BFB. He is a wooden red block who likes to pull pranks on other characters. In each of the Blocky's Funny Doings International segments, he demonstrates how a contestant's recovery center can be booby-trapped so that they die repeatedly.
* Bubble (voiced by Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFDI, and BFB. She is a kindhearted and happy soap bubble that gets popped a lot. But in later seasons, she has become more anxious and sensitive.
* Coiny (voiced by Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFDI, BFDIA, BFB and BFDI:TPOT. He is a nice but rude penny that has a rivalry with Firey, with whom he shares a mutual history of slapping each other. In later seasons, he becomes nicer and more thoughtful to people. He has a friendship with Pin and liked competing with her in BFDIA.
* David (voiced by Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFDI, BFB, and BFDIE. He is a mysterious poorly-drawn stick-figure who only says "Aw, Seriously?" being his catchphrase and only phrase he can say. He can also be quite antisocial, often refusing to follow directions of others. He is allergic to sunrises.
* Eraser (voiced by Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFDI, BFB and BFDI:TPOT. He is a grumpy, bored and impatient pink eraser, who has a close friendship with Pen and Blocky. He likes having rivalries and often tries to form them with characters like Teardrop and Bottle.
* Firey (voiced by Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFDI, BFDIA, and BFB. He is a competitive, loyal and gullible flame, who has a rivalry with Coiny, having a history of slapping each other. He’s also the best friend of Leafy. He was the winner of Battle for Dream Island.
* Flower (voiced by Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFDI, and BFB. She is a Zeltnera venusta flowering plant. She started off in BFDI as a mean, nasty and short-tempered person who was extremely disliked by all of the other contestants, always wanting people to call her beautiful. In BFB, she becomes more friendly and upbeat. She was the winner for Battle for B.F.B.
* Golf Ball (voiced by Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFDI, BFDIA, BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is an intelligent and bossy golf ball. She has a good friendship with Tennis Ball, and she always tries to assert herself as a leader.
* Ice Cube (voiced by Cary Huang in BFDI; Satomi Hinatsu in BFB 1 and 13-30; and by Pokey in BFB 2-12, TPOT, and BFDIA 6+) is a contestant in BFDI, BFDIA, BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is an outwardly kind ice cube always seeking revenge for people who disobey her.
* Leafy (voiced by Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFDI and BFB. She is a kind-hearted, generous, impulsive, green leaf who tries to be a people-pleaser.
* Match (voiced by Cary Huang) is a contestant in BFDI, BFDIA, and BFB. She has a close friendship with Pencil. She is friendly to specific contestants and will be mean and exclude most others, usually following and agreeing with whatever Pencil wants to do. She feels guilt for how she treated some others and becomes kinder in her limited screen-time throughout the show.
* Needle (voiced by Cary Huang in BFDI, BFDIA 1-5, and IDFB, Satomi Hinatsu in BFB 1, and Pokey in BFB 2+, TPOT, and BFDIA 6+) is a contestant in BFDI, BFDIA, BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is an assertive, resourceful and vengeful gray sewing needle. She will become angry and slap anyone who calls her "Needy".
* Pen (voiced by Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFDI, BFB and BFDI:TPOT. He is a kind, loyal, empathetic and considerate white and blue ballpoint pen. He is good friends with contestants Blocky and Eraser, but he often shows to be the kindest out of the three.
* Pencil (voiced by Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFDI, BFDIA, BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is a lazy, serious and brash pencil. She is caring to her friends and often sticks up for them if anyone is mean to them. She becomes a controlling and manipulative figure in BFB. In TPOT, she becomes more mentally unstable due to the events and trauma she faced in the E.X.I.T.
* Pin (voiced by Cary Huang) is a contestant in BFDI, BFDIA, BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is a confident and fierce red thumbtack who bosses people around in an attempt to become a “heroic team leader”. In later seasons, she displays more self-righteousness and integrity.
* Rocky (voiced by Cary Huang in BFDI and Satomi Hinatsu in TPOT) is a contestant in BFDI, BFDIA, BFB and BFDI:TPOT. He is a bizarre and erratic rock who can barely speak and only produces and throws up vomit.
* Snowball (voiced by Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFDI, BFDIA, BFB and BFDI:TPOT. He is a competitive, jock-like, egoistical snowball who tries to act tough around people and regards anyone he does not like as weaklings.
* Spongy (voiced by Cary Huang and briefly Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFDI, BFDIA, and BFB. He is a gentle and sensitive fat yellow kitchen sponge who is not well-received among many contestants, with most of them considering him dead-weight for challenges due to his weight.
* Teardrop is a contestant in BFDI, BFDIA, BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is a mischievous, rebellious and deadly blue teardrop. She is mute, meaning she cannot speak.
* Tennis Ball (voiced by Cary Huang) is a contestant in BFDI, BFDIA, BFB, and BFDI:TPOT. He is a clumsy and intelligent tennis ball who is very close friends with Golf Ball, and is even implied to have a crush on her. He is good at inventing and robotics.
* Woody (voiced by Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFDI, BFDIA, and BFB. He is a piece of balsa wood who often gets nervous over things. He has panophobia.

==== Debuted in Battle for Dream Island Again ====
* Bomby (voiced by Michael Huang in BFDI, BFDIA 1-5, and IDFB; and by Satomi Hinatsu in BFB, TPOT, and BFDIA 6+) is a contestant in BFDIA, BFB and BFDI:TPOT. He is a jumpy and easily scared bomb who explodes often when his fuse is lit. He constantly snacks on bananas.
* Book (voiced by Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFDIA, BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is a determined, loyal and gullible green and blue hardcover book. She has a hard time controlling herself when angered, as shown in BFB, in which she marked another contestant, Taco, as a traitor. She was the winner for Battle for Dream Island Again.
* Donut (voiced by Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFDIA, BFB and BFDI:TPOT. He is a considerate, thoughtful and arrogant jelly-filled donut who displays his rational side when he shows care for his teammates and acts as a team leader. He hosted BFB episodes 6 through 9.
* Dora is a contestant in BFDIA, and BFB. She is a calm, collected and mysterious stick figure similar to David. She is obsessed with eating islands, which is all she talks about. Like David, she also speaks a few words being "Dadadada". She is implied to be a parody of Dora the Explorer.
* Fries (voiced by Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFDIA, BFB and BFDI:TPOT. He is a grumpy, sarcastic and antipathetic cardboard cup of French fries. Fries believes that people who take the mantle of leadership are valuable.
* Gelatin (voiced by Graham Taylor in BFDIA 1-5 and BFB 1-23; Ian Woodside in BFB 24-30, TPOT 1–19; and BFDIA 6–22; and Alem Hadzic in TPOT 20+ and BFDIA 23+) is a contestant in BFDIA, and BFB. He is a laid-back, childish and immature block of carved lime-flavored gelatin, who runs a steakhouse called Gelatin's Steakhouse.
* Nickel (voiced by Adam Katz) is a contestant in BFDIA, BFB and BFDI:TPOT. He is a goofy, happy-go-lucky American nickel who shouts random erratic and nonsensical phrases.
* Puffball (voiced by Michael Huang with a vocoder) is a contestant in BFDIA, BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is a calm, bubbly, fuzzy pink ball who has a vocoded voice and fur that changes color when she talks. She has the ability to fly and float, and she is usually calm except when she is wronged.
* Ruby (voiced by Michael Huang in BFDI, BFDIA 1-5, and IDFB; and Cary Huang in BFB, TPOT and BFDIA 6+) is a contestant in BFDIA, and BFB. She is a bubbly, silly and curious diamond-cut ruby. She enjoys playing around with other contestants and is shown to look up to contestants with leadership roles, such as Pencil.
* Yellow Face (voiced by Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFDIA, BFB, and BFDI:TPOT. He is a loud and erratic poorly-drawn yellow cartoon head that appears in mock commercial segments where he sells outlandish products. He is shown to largely hate contestants that oppose his ads or products. He runs a company called Yellow Face Inc.

==== Debuted in Battle for B.F.D.I/Battle for B.F.B. ====
* 8-Ball (voiced by Cary Huang) is a contestant in BFB. He is a black "8" billiard ball from the game eight-ball who always wants everyone to know that he does not have a favorite number.
* Balloony (voiced by Satomi Hinatsu) is a contestant in BFB. He is a green rubber balloon.
* Barf Bag (voiced by Pokey) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is a sickness bag half full with vomit. Her strength varies depending on how full and the type of liquid she contains.
* Basketball (voiced by Satomi Hinatsu) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is a basketball who has a passion for creating inventions and has a friendship with Robot Flower.
* Bell (voiced by Pokey) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is a bell suspended from a long string, and dislikes when people climb it, which leads to Bandland.
* Black Hole (voiced by Satomi Hinatsu) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. He is a black hole who is immensely powerful, and is steadfast in his desire to not cause death.
* Bottle (voiced by Satomi Hinatsu) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is a glass bottle who acts carefree and sometimes oblivious to her surroundings.
* Bracelety (voiced by Cary Huang) is a contestant in BFB. She is a cyan-colored silicone ring who is often shown obsessing over Ice Cube.
* Cake (voiced by Pokey) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. He is a slice of chocolate cake with white and red icing on top. He acts shy and dependent on others, especially to Loser, who he is loyal to.
* Clock (voiced by Satomi Hinatsu) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. He is a blue and white clock. He often acts self-righteously and an enforcer of rules.
* Cloudy (voiced by Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. He is a cumulus cloud able to fly. He speaks with an accent in which voiced and unvoiced consonants are swapped. He likes to collect items and keep them to himself.
* Eggy (voiced by Katherine Sun) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is a white egg with yellow spots.
* Fanny (voiced by Satomi Hinatsu) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is a blue fan who expresses her hatred for everything, though is quite reasonable and does what she believes is right. In early BFB, She is apathetic and eccentric.
* Firey Jr. (voiced by Satomi Hinatsu) is a contestant in BFB. He is a small version of Firey. Unlike Firey, he acts more insensitive and bluntly.
* Foldy (voiced by Cindy Jiang) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is a folded sheet of origami paper shaped like a pentagon. She tends to act friendly to others, but she is enemies with Liy and can act aggressive towards people who go against her or Stapy.
* Gaty (voiced by Satomi Hinatsu) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is a painted wooden fence gate with metal hinges. She often acts as the voice of reason, criticizing the actions of others. She later develops a friendship with Two. She is confirmed to be transgender.
* Grassy (voiced by Cary Huang) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. He is a green tuft of grass. He acts the most childish of the cast, and relies on others for help. He later on learns to become stronger and independent.
* Lightning (voiced by Sabrina) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. He is a lightning bolt able to electrocute anyone he touches.
* Liy (voiced by Sabrina) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is a periwinkle light switch who claims to have had a murderous past. If her switch is flipped, she can go on a killing spree.
* Lollipop (voiced by Sam Lee) is a contestant in BFB. She a grape-flavored lollipop who acts snide and above others. She tries to sell an aerosol spray can able to deflect forks. She often acts as a competitor to Yellow Face in marketing.
* Loser (voiced by Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFB. He is a yellow cube popular among the contestants due to having a celebrity status. He loses his popularity in BFB 7, after claiming he “used to play with” toys that had been invented hours prior.
* Marker (voiced by Cary Huang) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. He is a purple washable marker pen with a chisel tip. He likes playing a game about tossing dirt over his head.
* Naily (voiced by Katherine Sun) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is a metal nail who commonly makes puns about 'nailing it'.
* Pie (voiced by Sam Lee) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is a friendly blueberry pie in a pie tin. She has the ability to explode when experiencing physical trauma. Despite this, she acts apathetic and relaxed.
* Pillow (voiced by Cindy Jiang) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is a psychopathic pillow who wants to research killing people. She often does things without caring and kills people whenever she can.
* Profily (voiced by Niall Burns) is a blue-colored default profile picture who first appears in BFB. They claim to have been competing since BFDI 1a, much to the contestants' (and Four's) chagrin. They also make minor appearances in BFDI:TPOT, dropping Teardrop off to the competition site so she can join, and offering Balloony the same. They were put up for rejoin in BFDI:TPOT 25 despite having never actually competed before.
* Remote is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is a black plastic remote control. She talks with a speech synthesis voice, and is able to use her buttons to control TV.
* Robot Flower (voiced by Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is a robot copy of Flower, and shares similar behaviors as her. However, Robot Flower is able to be reprogrammed, and experience glitches.
* Roboty is a contestant in BFB. He is an immobile red-colored robot who speaks in morse code. He is often dismissive of most contestants, and is usually left behind due to his lack of movement ability.
* Saw (voiced by Satomi Hinatsu) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. She is a metal ripsaw with a pink wooden handle. In BFB 8, she gets an illness causing her to involuntarily say the number eight while speaking.
* Stapy (voiced by Sam Lee) is a contestant in BFB. He is a red office stapler who doesn’t have legs. He hops around and uses his body to crush and staple things. He calls these actions his “stapler instincts.”
* Taco (voiced by Pokey) is a contestant in BFB. She is a soft shell fish taco. She is incorrectly accused of abandoning her team after being stuck in a large, hollow jawbreaker.
* Tree (voiced by Thomas Chick) is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. He is a tree who often acts like the leader of his team or as the voice of reason. He has the ability to be resurrected and grow into a larger tree when in contact in water. Other contestants are also able to control his body when inside his leaves and branches.
* TV is a contestant in BFB and BFDI:TPOT. He is a flatscreen plasma television able to display videos and infographics on his screen.

==== Debuted in Battle for Dream Island: The Power of Two ====
* Price Tag (voiced by B. Oktavio Wolfmann) is a contestant in BFDI:TPOT. They are a red price tag who uses emoticons for a face.
* Winner (voiced by Schazer) is a contestant in BFDI:TPOT. They are a purple blob with one retractable hand that can come out of their body. They were a former celebrity along with Loser. The two parted ways when Loser became more popular.

==== Debuted in Battle for Dream Island Elsewhere ====
* Beach Ball (voiced by Joseph Pak) is a contestant in BFDIE. They are an inflated beach ball.
* Fern (voiced by Pokey) is a contestant in BFDIE. He is a fern. He is the winner for Battle for Dream Island Elsewhere.
* Hot Dog (voiced by Peter Ruette) is a contestant in BFDIE. He is a hot dog topped with mustard and chopped onions.
* Jammy (voiced by Katherine Sun) is a contestant in BFDIE. She is a jar of peach jam.
* Money (voiced by Michael Huang) is a contestant in BFDIE. She is a bundle of folded dollars held within a money clip.
* Needy (voiced by Bella Reeves) is a contestant in BFDIE. She is a syringe containing a purple fluid.
* Rose (voiced by Gooseworx) is a contestant in BFDIE. She is a red rose.
* Ruler (voiced by Thomas Ridgewell) is a contestant in BFDIE. He is a wooden ruler.
* Sidewalky (voiced by Adam Katz) is a contestant in BFDIE. He is a segment of a concrete sidewalk.
* Sticker (voiced by Xander Archibald) is a contestant in BFDIE. They are a square adhesive sticker.
* Toothpaste (voiced by Satomi Hinatsu) is a contestant in BFDIE. She is a mean white tube of toothpaste.

=== Other recurring characters ===
* Evil Leafy is a red, demonic, and hostile version of Leafy. When contestants are near, she teleports to chase after them. If she gets the contestants, she eats them alive. She is recovered from Leafy when she feels high levels of distress.
* Nonexisty doesn't exist, as his name would imply. He was up for debut in BFDI, where he didn't get enough votes to join, and BFDI:TPOT, where he got the second-most votes to join, almost making it in but being replaced by Price Tag due to his aforementioned nonexistence.
* Pan Flute (voiced by Kevin MacLeod) is a pan flute, a successful musician who leads a orchestra whose instruments get poisoned in BFDIA 12.
* Purple Face (voiced by Justin Chapman and later Benjamin Cross) is a poorly-drawn purple face. He has an immense hatred towards Yellow Face. He was put up for rejoin in BFDI:TPOT 25 despite having never competed before.
* The Fourse is a blue horse resemblant of Four, which first appeared in BFDI:TPOT 11 as a minor antagonist. It then became a recurring character starting in BFDI:TPOT 17, holding a cartoony grudge against Tennis Ball. It was put up for rejoin in BFDI:TPOT 25 despite having never competed before.

data.title: Victor Murgatroyd
data.text:
Victor Murgatroyd is an American record producer, A&R executive and musician. He was production supervisor on Evanescence's Grammy Award-winning debut album Fallen (2003), and has worked with J Records founder Clive Davis and with artists including The Cult, Ian Astbury, Incubus, Seether, Finger Eleven, Drowning Pool, Buckcherry, Escape the Fate and Mother Tongue.

== Early life and music career ==
Murgatroyd grew up in New York. He performed with The Cult and played bass in The Four Horsemen. He formed Zen Mafia with Chris Johnson, and co-produced, co-wrote and played guitar and bass on the band's 1999 debut album California, released by RCA.

== Career ==
Murgatroyd joined Epic Records as director of A&R for the West Coast in 1993. He later worked in A&R at Wind-up Records, J Records and Better Noise Music. While at Epic, he produced tracks by Mother Tongue and Kate Gibson for the soundtracks of two James Cameron productions, True Lies (1994), starring Arnold Schwarzenegger, and Strange Days (1995), starring Ralph Fiennes and Angela Bassett, on which he also played piano and Chamberlin. His other production credits from the 1990s include Mother Tongue's self-titled album (1994), co-produced with Beastie Boys producer Mario Caldato Jr., and Kate Gibson's Weary Remedy (1996). He was executive producer of Ian Astbury's solo album Spirit\Light\Speed (1999).

As an A&R executive at Wind-up, he oversaw Drowning Pool's debut album Sinner (2001) and albums by Seether and 12 Stones, and was production supervisor on records by Evanescence, Finger Eleven and Boysetsfire. Fallen peaked at No. 3 on the Billboard 200, reached No. 1 in the UK and Canada, and was certified Diamond by the RIAA for 10 million units in the US; it has sold more than 17 million copies worldwide. It won Evanescence two Grammy Awards in 2004, and the album and its songs received six nominations in total, including Album of the Year. Sinner peaked at No. 14 on the Billboard 200 and was certified platinum, and its single "Bodies" also went platinum. Finger Eleven was certified gold in the US and platinum in Canada, and its single "One Thing" reached No. 16 on the Billboard Hot 100. Disclaimer was certified gold in the US.

In 2007 he brought Nickelback singer and songwriter Chad Kroeger and producer Joey Moi to Clive Davis and mediated their joint-venture label deal with J Records. He founded Five K Entertainment Group, which in 2008 formed a publishing venture with the Canadian publisher ole and developed artists under an agreement with J Records. He later worked as A&R on Escape the Fate's Chemical Warfare (2021).

== Personal life ==
Murgatroyd has been sober since 1991 and runs an independent private-client advisory practice in Los Angeles. He had a major stroke in 2014, from which he recovered. He is a friend of the musician Jesse Malin.

data.title: Solace Health
data.text:
----

Solace Health is a healthtech platform that matches patients with healthcare advocates who help them navigate the U.S. healthcare system. Established in 2022, the privately held company is based in Redwood City, California.
== History ==
Jeremy Gurewitz and Sara Sargent co-founded Solace Health in 2022 after Gurewitz watched his mother struggle to navigate the healthcare system while she battled pancreatic cancer. His mother had difficulty even though she was a radiologist with an understanding of the medical system [ref: Solace Health expands care navigation services to commercially insured patients, Fierce Healthcare] who led a women's imaging center in Long Island, New York. [ref: Medicare Coverage Fuels Solace’s $60 Million Series B, Wall Street Journal]

Patients initially paid for Solace services out-of-pocket. This changed in 2024 when Medicare started covering patient advocacy services for chronic and complicated health conditions. [ref: VCs Give Solace Health $1 Billion Valuation for Patient Advocacy Tech, Bloomberg] Gurewitz told the Wall Street Journal that investor interest increased once patient advocacy was covered by Medicare. In April 2025, Solace announced a $60 million Series B, which was twice the amount they intended to raise. In February 2026, Business Insider reported that the need for help navigating the U.S. medical system had propelled the company to a $1 billion valuation.

In 2026, Solace announced additional insurance coverage from major health plans, including United Healthcare and Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield. Fierce Healthcare quoted Gurewitz that this expanded coverage extended the opportunity for patient advocacy to millions of Americans. The company also partnered with Disabled American Veterans (DAV) [ref: DAV announces new partnership with Solace Health supporting veterans’ care, DAV] and the American Legion [ref: Solace Health, American Legion announce partnership to help veterans navigate healthcare system, American Legion] to help U.S. military veterans navigate healthcare. They announced a partnership with Walmart’s Better Care Services in September 2026. [ref: Solace Health Expands Access to Healthcare Advocacy Through Walmart’s Better Care Services Platform, Businesswire]

== Advocacy services ==
Solace advocates include registered nurses and other healthcare professionals who, according to a 2026 press release have 16 years of experience on average. When Medicare reimburses advocates, Solace receives a share in exchange for use of its platform. In early 2026, Solace had more than 2,000 participating advocates providing services to more than 20,000 patients each month.

Advocate services include helping clients understand medical bills and treatment plans, as well as finding physicians, scheduling appointments, and coordinating care across multiple providers. Advocates can also go to appointments with patients, either virtually or in person. Gurewitz told MedCity News in 2026 that Solace advocates specialize in doing the work for patients, rather than simply providing advice on what patients should do.

Patients interact with advocates through text and phone calls as well as video calls embedded in the Solace platform. [ref: Solace Health Reaches Unicorn Status by Taking the ‘Homework’ Out of Care Navigation, MedCityNews] Solace's proprietary electronic health records system assembles a patient's health history. The platform also handles Medicare billing. Gurewitz informed Founder Brew in a 2026 interview that while the Solace platform incorporates AI to help advocates do their jobs, many aspects of the U.S. healthcare system cannot be completed by AI and still require human interaction.

data.text:
----

K-AL is the professional moniker of Kevin Earl Allen Jr., an American musical artist, music producer, songwriter, and audio engineer. Specializing in independent hip-hop and contemporary urban music, K-AL manages multiple facets of the production pipeline, operating as a performing rap artist, record producer, and mixing and mastering engineer. His work focuses on integrating individual creative composition with distinct sonic architecture, establishing an independent presence within the music industry.

Early Life and Education

Allen pursued formal training in the technical and commercial aspects of the music industry. In 2004, following his graduation from high school, he enrolled at San Jacinto College in Texas. During his time at the institution, he completed focused coursework in recording engineering and music business administration. This academic background provided the foundation for his subsequent technical work in studio tracking, signal processing, and independent label operations.

Career and Performance Rights

Operating under the stylized stage name K-AL, Allen handles the end-to-end production of his musical catalog, tracking vocals, composing instrumental arrangements, and executing final studio mixes. As a songwriter and publisher, K-AL is professionally affiliated with Broadcast Music, Inc. (BMI), the performing rights organization that manages the licensing, tracking, and distribution of public performance royalties for his musical works.

data.title: John R. Woznicki
data.text:
John R. Woznicki is a literary scholar and academic administrator whose scholarly work primarily involves twentieth-century American poetry and poetics. Woznicki is the author of Ideological Content and Political Significance of Twentieth-Century American Poetry [ref: John R. Woznicki. Ideological Content and Political Significance of Twentieth-Century American Poetry. Edwin Mellen Press. 2002.] and the edited collection The New American Poetry: Fifty Years Later. [ref: John R. Woznicki ed. The New American Poetry: Fifty Years Later. Lehigh University Press. 2013.]

== Scholarship ==

Woznicki’s first monograph, Ideological Content and Political Significance of Twentieth-Century American Poetry [ref: John R. Woznicki. Ideological Content and Political Significance of Twentieth-Century American Poetry. Edwin Mellen Press. 2002,] is an interdisciplinary examination of politics and ideology in twentieth-century American poetry, drawing upon philosophy, sociology, literary criticism, and cultural studies. It examines the work of Ezra Pound, Charles Olson and the L=A=N=G=U=A=G=E poets, with particular attention to totalitarianism, utopian thought, and political consciousness.

He then edited a collection of essays and wrote the introductory chapter for The New American Poetry: Fifty Years Later, [ref: John R. Woznicki ed. The New American Poetry: Fifty Years Later. Lehigh University Press. 2013,] a collection of scholarly essays reassessing Donald Allen’s influential 1960 anthology The New American Poetry 1945–1960. [ref: Donald Allen ed. The New American Poetry 1945–1960. Grove Press. 1960.] Woznicki’s collection considers the anthology's formation, its modernist antecedents, poets and movements represented in it, and its subsequent literary and cultural influence. A paperback edition was subsequently published in 2015. [ref: John R. Woznicki ed. The New American Poetry: Fifty Years Later. Lehigh University Press. 2015.]

== Reception ==

Orchid Tierney reviewed Woznicki’s volume in the Journal of Modern Literature. [ref: Orchid Tierney. “Back to the Future of Poetry? A Review of The New American Poetry: Fifty Years Later." Journal of Modern Literature, vol. 40, no. 1, 2016, pp. 164–168. DOI:10.2979/jmodelite.40.1.09.]  Tierney characterizes the collection more broadly as an investigation of tradition-building and the reasons Allen's anthology remained relevant to poets, readers, and scholars of innovative writing.

Choice Reviews recommended The New American Poetry: Fifty Years Later. The review discusses aspects of the legacy of Allen’s anthology, including women poets, the British avant-garde, the long poem, and Language poetry. [ref: John. R Woznicki.The New American Poetry: Fifty Years Later. Bloomsbury Book Page. Bloomsbury Publishing. https://www.bloomsbury.com/us/new-american-poetry-9781611462142/.]

Patrick James Dunagan reviewed The New American Poetry: Fifty Years Later in the journal Your Impossible Voice. [ref: Patrick James Dunagan. Review: The New American Poetry: Fifty Years Later, edited by John R. Woznicki. Your Impossible Voice. ISSN #2327-381X. https://yourimpossiblevoice.com/review-new-american-poetry-fifty-years-later-john-r-woznicki-ed/.] Dunagan considers Woznicki’s introductory argument and the volume's attempt to move critical discussion beyond the original construction of Allen's anthology toward questions concerning its reception, cultural influence, and continuing relationship to contemporary poetry.

In discussing Donald Allen and the historical significance of The New American Poetry, Stephanie Anderson directs readers to scholarship concerning Allen's anthology and includes Woznicki's collection alongside work by Alan Golding and Stephan Delbos. [ref: Stephanie Anderson. “‘It's Only Vanity if It's Not Good’: Daisy Aldan and Women Midcentury Small Press Publishers.” Post45, 2024.]

In his book titled The New American Poetry and Cold War Nationalism, Delbos identifies Woznicki’s volume in his discussion of prior scholarship on Allen’s anthology, citing essays from the collection throughout his study. Delbos engages Woznicki’s own interpretation of Charles Olson. In the chapter “This Thing Is Most National: Nationalism and Assimilation in The New American Poetry,” Delbos discusses Woznicki's interpretation of correspondence from Olson as revealing Olson's conception of his American poetic identity in relation to the European cosmopolitan tradition associated with figures such as Ezra Pound and T. S. Eliot. Delbos argues that the passage can be taken further by examining the nationalism underlying Olson's position. [ref: Stephan Delbos.The New American Poetry and Cold War Nationalism. Modern and Contemporary Poetry and Poetics series. Palgrave Macmillan, 2021. p. 135.]

== Academic Career ==

John R. Woznicki is associate provost and dean of Arts and Sciences at Misericordia University, following his service as dean at Delaware Valley University. [ref: Misericordia University Welcomes Two New Deans. 06/16/2022. https://www.misericordia.edu/news/news-postpage/~board/news/post/misericordia-university-welcomes-two-deans.] Prior to this, he was dean at Thomas Edison State University, provost and assistant vice president of academic affairs at Union County College, and division head for Arts, Communications and Humanities at Holy Family University. He had earlier academic appointments at Georgian Court University, Community College of Philadelphia, and Fairmont State University. [ref: Jessica Perry. NJBIZ. June 30, 2014. https://njbiz.com/close-up-robert-daber/.]

== Selected Works ==

*John R. Woznicki ed. The New American Poetry: Fifty Years Later. Lehigh University Press. 2013.

*John R. Woznicki. “Wallace Stevens and ‘The Glass of Water.’” The Explicator, vol. 53, no. 4, 1995, pp. 224–227.

*John R. Woznicki. “Poetry of Play, Poetry of Purpose: The Continuity of American Language Poetry.” Moria: A Poetry Journal, 2000.

*John R. Woznicki. “Keep Cujo Unleashed.” In Censored Books, vol. 2. Scarecrow Press, 2002.

data.title: Bieler School of Environment (BSE)
data.text:
The Bieler School of Environment (BSE), known until 2020 as the McGill School of Environment (MSE), is an interfaculty undergraduate teaching and research unit of McGill University in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. Founded in 1998, it offers interdisciplinary environment programs on both McGill's Downtown campus and its Macdonald Campus. [ref: About the McGill Bieler School of Environment, McGill University] The school was renamed in 2020 in recognition of a $15-million gift commitment from McGill alumnus and agri-food entrepreneur Marc Bieler. [ref: McGill receives $15-million gift commitment from agri-food entrepreneur Marc Bieler, McGill University Newsroom]

== History ==
=== McGill School of Environment (1998–2020) ===
The school was established in 1998 as a joint initiative of three McGill faculties: Agricultural and Environmental Sciences, Arts, and Science. [ref: Bieler School of Environment welcomes new director, McGill University] [ref: The MSE Newsletter, Issue 3, McGill School of Environment] The Faculty of Law later joined as a partner faculty. [ref: McGill School of Environment, Programs, Courses and University Regulations 2015–2016]

Its first full-time director was Peter G. Brown, an environmental ethicist and former founding director of the School of Public Affairs at the University of Maryland. [ref: McGill School of Environment: A new director takes the helm, McGill Reporter] Later directors included parasitologist Marilyn Scott, who led the school in the early 2010s. [ref: McGill School of Environment Newsletter, Spring 2012, McGill School of Environment] The school marked its 20th anniversary in 2018 with a homecoming lecture and alumni events. [ref: MSE 20th Anniversary Homecoming Newsletter, McGill School of Environment]

=== Renaming and the Bieler gift (2020) ===
In October 2020, McGill announced a $15-million gift commitment from Marc Bieler (DipAgr'58, BA'64) and his wife Marie Bieler (BSc(Agr)'80), and renamed the school the Bieler School of Environment. [ref: The cranberry king donates $15M to McGill University's school of the environment, CTV News Montreal] The gift consists of an initial cash contribution followed by a 25-year commitment from Bieler and his estate, and was described as the largest ever made by a graduate of the Macdonald Campus. [ref: A new chapter for Environmental Studies at McGill, McGill University Advancement] According to McGill, the funds were directed at three areas: expanding academic programs (particularly graduate training and doctoral recruitment); strengthening interdisciplinary research capacity, visiting scholars and international partnerships; and expanding internships, mobility awards and other experiential-learning opportunities.

At the time of the gift, the school was described as a joint initiative of the Faculties of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences, Arts, Engineering, Law and Science, with 18 jointly appointed faculty members and 53 associate members. Administratively, it reports through the Dean of the Faculty of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences. [ref: 00408 – Bieler School of Environment, McGill University Academic Personnel Board]

=== Recent developments ===
Atmospheric scientist Frédéric Fabry served as director from 2020 to 2025. In January 2025, invasion ecologist Anthony Ricciardi, a member of the school since 2001, was appointed director; directors serve five-year terms.

== Academic programs ==
The school's approach is to expose students to a broad range of disciplines early in their studies before they specialize. [ref: Environment, Bieler School of, McGill Course Catalogue] Many programs can be taken entirely on either campus or across both.

=== Undergraduate ===
Programs offered include: [ref: Université McGill – Programmes offerts en environnement, Gouvernement du Québec]
* B.Sc. Major in Environment, with concentrations including Atmospheric Environment and Air Quality; Biodiversity and Conservation; Earth Sciences and Economics; Ecological Determinants of Health; Environmetrics; Food Production and Environment; Land Surface Processes and Environmental Change; Renewable Resource Management; and Water Environments and Ecosystems
* B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.) Major in Environment (Macdonald Campus)
* B.A. Faculty Program in Environment, with concentrations including Economics and the Earth's Environment, Environment and Development, and Ecological Determinants of Health in Society
* B.A. & Sc. Interfaculty Program in Environment
* Honours and Joint Honours options
* Minor in Environment and Diploma in Environment

=== Graduate ===
The school administers a graduate Environment option that can be added to master's and doctoral programs in participating departments, including Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences, Biology, Bioresource Engineering, Geography and Philosophy. Students in the option must be supervised or co-supervised by a BSE faculty or associate member. [ref: Environment, Bieler School of (Graduate), McGill Course Catalogue]

=== Field studies and experiential learning ===
Environment students may take field semesters abroad, including in Panama, Barbados and East Africa. [ref: B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.) Major in Environment, McGill University]
* The Panama Field Study Semester is a joint venture between McGill and the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute, a 15-credit winter-term program built around internship and research projects on Panamanian environmental issues. [ref: Field Studies, McGill Course Catalogue] Its research course, ENVR 451, places groups of four to six students with Panamanian universities, government agencies and NGOs on topics such as protection of the Panama Canal watershed and alternatives to deforestation. [ref: ENVR 451 Research in Panama, eCalendar 2024–2025]
* The Barbados Field Study Semester is based at McGill's Bellairs Research Institute, and the Africa Field Study Semester is held in East Africa each January.
* The Bieler Environment Learning Fund (BELF) supports student experiential-learning activities. [ref: BSE Students Named Valedictorians, Bieler School of Environment]

== Research ==
The school's faculty and associate members work across climate science, biodiversity, water resources, sustainable development, environmental policy and law. Members hold appointments jointly with departments such as Biology, Geography, Natural Resource Sciences, Bioresource Engineering, Civil Engineering, Economics and Law, and with units including the Brace Water Centre and the Redpath Museum. [ref: Experts: Environment, McGill University Newsroom]

=== Endowed chairs ===
* Bieler Chair in Northern Climate Change and Sustainability – announced in October 2023 following a gift from Marc and Marie Bieler, the chair is housed jointly in the BSE and the Department of Natural Resource Sciences. It focuses on climate change in Canada's North, where sea-ice loss and permafrost change threaten livelihoods, Indigenous culture, food security and community health. [ref: McGill establishes research chair to address climate change in the North, McGill University Advancement]
* Bieler Chair in St. Lawrence River Ecology – supported by a $1-million gift from Philippe Bieler (BEng'55), the chair investigates how climate change and invasive species, individually and together, affect freshwater biodiversity and food webs in the St. Lawrence River. [ref: From Douglas Hall to the sheep farm – my entrepreneurial journey, McGill University Advancement] Director Anthony Ricciardi is the inaugural chairholder, with a mandate to work with government agencies, community groups and First Nations authorities on monitoring the river. [ref: A message from our new Director, Bieler School of Environment]

=== Outreach ===
The school hosts an annual public environment lecture and produces The Bieler Broadcast: Environmental Research Unplugged, a podcast featuring research by faculty, students and alumni. [ref: Bieler School of Environment Welcomes New Director, Bieler School of Environment]

== Philanthropy ==
The Bieler family, four generations of whom attended McGill, are the school's principal benefactors.
{| class="wikitable"
! Year !! Donor(s) !! Gift !! Purpose
|-
| 2009 || Marc Bieler and family || $1 million || Bieler Family Internship Program, Faculty of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences [ref: Canada's "Cranberry King" donates $1 million to Macdonald Campus, McGill University]
|-
| 2020 || Marc and Marie Bieler || $15 million (gift commitment) || Naming gift; graduate programs, research and experiential learning
|-
| 2026 || Philippe Bieler || $1 million || Bieler Chair in St. Lawrence River Ecology
|}

Marc Bieler founded Atoka Cranberries and Bieler Cranberries in Saint-Louis-de-Blandford, Quebec, in partnership with his brother Philippe; Atoka's processing business was acquired by Ocean Spray in 2018. [ref: Ocean Spray acquires Quebec cranberry grower, Food in Canada]

== Alumni ==

Graduates of the school's programs have gone on to careers in environmental law, research, government and the non-profit sector.

data.title: Holtzman Vogel
data.text:
Holtzman Vogel Baran Torchinsky & Josefiak PLLC (operating primarily as Holtzman Vogel) is an American boutique law firm specializing in political law, election compliance, government ethics, and constitutional litigation. [ref: Holtzman Vogel Baran Torchinsky & Josefiak PLLC, USA 2026, Chambers and Partners] Founded by attorney and former Virginia State Senator Jill Holtzman Vogel, the firm advises political campaigns, national party committees, political action committees (PACs), and non-profit organizations. [ref: ‘Dark-money’ superlawyer bills herself as advocate for charities in Va. lieutenant governor’s race, The Washington Post] [ref: These GOP-Aligned Law Firms, Lobbying Shops Are Growing in Market Share, The National Law Journal] Alongside its core campaign and election practice, the firm manages complex appellate litigation, white-collar defense, corporate political compliance, and congressional investigation counseling.

== History ==

The firm was established in 2001 in Virginia by Jill Holtzman Vogel, who previously had served as chief counsel to the Republican National Committee (RNC). [ref:.Defamation lawyer turns up heat on Va. state senator over anonymous emails, The Washington Post] Originally established in northern Virginia, the firm opened offices in Washington, D.C., Florida, Arizona, New York, Utah, and Tennessee. [ref: Political Law Specialist Holtzman Vogel Expands to Nashville With Former Top Aide to 2 Governors, The National Law Journal] It now has eight offices, and 63 attorneys.

In 2025, Holtzman Vogel opened a Nashville, Tennessee office to focus on commercial and political regulatory law, appointing Brandon Smith, the former chief of staff to the Tennessee Attorney General, to lead the branch. [ref: Holtzman Vogel Expands to Tennessee with Nashville Office, TBA Law Blog] [ref: Holtzman Vogel expands Nashville office in move to Broadwest, Nashville Business Journal] [ref: Holtzman Vogel relocates to Broadwest, Nashville Post] The firm also expanded its constitutional and appellate practices by bringing in academic and legal experts, including constitutional law professor Elizabeth Price Foley, to its Miami and Washington offices. [ref: Holtzman Vogel Taps Former Assistant US Attorney for Further Growth in Miami, Daily Business Review] [ref: Holtzman Vogel Adds Constitutional Law Pro In DC And Miami, Law360] The firm recruits senior personnel exiting federal service and the United States Department of Justice (DOJ). [ref: Ex-DOJ Enviro Deputy AG Lands At Holtzman Vogel, Law360] [ref: 'We're Recruiting': Amid DOJ Hires, Holtzman Vogel Looks to Grow, The National Law Journal]

== Notable attorneys ==
*Sean Cairncross, U.S. national cyber director, former CEO of the Millennium Challenge Corporation and chief counsel for the Republican National Committee
*Jonathan Fahey, former Deputy Assistant Secretary of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security and senior official performing the duties of the director of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement
*Elizabeth Price Foley (born 1965), legal theorist in the fields of constitutional law, bioethics, and health care law, and professor at Florida International University College of Law
*Andrew Gould (born 1963), former justice of the Arizona Supreme Court
* Saritha Komatireddy (born 1984 or 1985), former federal prosecutor, and chief of staff of the Drug Enforcement Administration, currently the Republican nominee for attorney general of New York in the 2026 election.
*Matthew S. Petersen (born 1970), formerly a member of the U.S. Federal Election Commission
*Jill Holtzman Vogel (born 1970), formerly a Virginia State Senator

data.title: Prime Educational and Social Trust
data.text:
Prime Educational and Social Trust, commonly known as Prime Trust, is a non-governmental organisation based in Puducherry, India. It runs Janani Home, a shelter for girls and women who have experienced violence or abuse. [ref: À Pondichéry, un foyer pour « exister autrement », Mediapart] [ref: Die Schattenkämpferinnen, Der Spiegel]

== History ==
Prime Trust was founded in 2002. Its founder and director is S. M. Arasu. [ref: Prime Trust – Home, Prime Educational and Social Trust] According to Der Spiegel, the trust established Janani Home in 2012.

== Janani Home ==
Janani Home is located in Puducherry. It takes in minors placed by the local police, and women and girls who have experienced violence or abuse stay there under police protection. The organisation works closely with local authorities, and Mediapart reported that it relies on the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act) in assisting girls in distress. The home provides psychological support and education for minors, as well as retraining and job placement for older women.

== Other activities ==
According to the trust, its other activities include women's self-help groups, after-school education programmes and health camps in Puducherry and neighbouring districts of Tamil Nadu. It describes the Akshaya SHG Confederation and India Volunteer Care as sister organisations.

== Media coverage ==
In 2025, Janani Home was the subject of a photo story by the Indian-French photographer Jennifer Carlos. The story was published by Mediapart in March 2025, and by Der Spiegel later that month with text by Maria Stöhr.

The [https://www.sugarhousehotel.com/ Sugar House Hotel] is a new boutique hotel in Winooski, Vermont anticipated to make history as Marriott’s first all-electric, net-zero energy and LEED Platinum property in the world [ref: ]. The 115-room Tribute Portfolio hotel draws inspiration from Vermont’s maple-sugaring history while putting guests within walking distance of the city’s downtown rotary, restaurants, and riverfront paths. It has a rooftop restaurant and bar, [https://www.instagram.com/treetopsrooftop/ Treetops], with views of the surrounding Winooski River and the 104-acre preserve [https://downtownwinooski.org/ Casavant Nature Area]. [ref: Sugar House Hotel in Winooski to Open Restaurant and Café-Bar, Seven Days].

Inspired by Vermont’s indigenous maple traditions and a deep respect for the Earth, the eight-floor hotel is crafted from reclaimed materials and shaped by local metalworkers, glassblowers and sugarmakers. Every level of the property is designed to be a love letter to Vermont craftsmanship through artisan-crafted details. By blending the creative pulse of Winooski with the tranquility of the adjacent woods, the design reflects a place shaped by the rugged spirit of Vermont.

data.title: SēmonBarai
data.text:
Seimon Harai is an annual event held in Kyoto, Japan, in which people's lies from that year are wiped away. Participants are said to be forgiven for their lies by paying their respects at a shrine called "Kanjaden Shrine."

**History**

Seimon Harai is held every year on October 20 at Kanjaden Shrine on Shijo-dori Street. The festival originates from the story of a man named "Tosa no Bo Shoshun." On orders from his lord, he tried to assassinate a military commander, but was discovered by the commander, who had sensed the plot. Although he was released after promising not to carry out the assassination, he attacked anyway. Just before he was killed, he said, "I will become a god who forgives those who lie." He was then enshrined at the shrine as a deity.

**Recent Years**

Seimon Harai once fell into decline, but it was revived in 2003 by the Otabi-cho neighborhood association and has continued to this day. There have also been changes since it came under the association's management, such as the Otabi-cho neighborhood association starting a ritual called the "Shiraishi Arai Kiyome Shinji" (a purification ritual) for the festival.

data.text:
----

Faswell Sdn. Bhd.

Faswell Sdn. Bhd. is a Malaysian health-products company that develops wound-care, skinhealth and metabolic-health products, marketed through e-commerce and social media.

[https://www.orientaldaily.com.my/news/nation/2026/10/15/855338 Oriental Daily] · [https://faswell.my/ Faswell.my]

History

The company was founded by Dr. Salehin, described on the company website as a medical practitioner who has dedicated his expertise to chronic wound care innovation. In several podcast interviews, he has shared his journey from a Ministry of Health Malaysia doctor to the founder of Faswell, including his experience developing wound-care product formulations.

[https://faswell.my/ Faswell.my] ·

Products

Faswell Nano Silver & Manuka Honey Spray — a wound-care spray. [https://faswell.my/faswell-spray Faswell.my]

Glunova — a probiotic powder. [https://faswell.my/glunova-original Faswell.my]

Faswell Cream — an herbal cream. [https://faswell.my/faswell-cream Faswell.my]

The product descriptions above are manufacturer descriptions from the company website; they are not independent assessments of product safety or efficacy.

Sales channels

Faswell markets its products through its official website [https://faswell.my/ faswell.my] and an online storefront on [https://shopee.com.my/salehinkornain Shopee].

In 2026, Faswell was selected as one of eight finalists in the Retail-X track of the Selangor Triple Accelerator Programme, an accelerator run by the Selangor Information Technology and Digital Economy Corporation (Sidec). data.title: Kamelia Stankova Allow
data.text:
Kamelia Stankova Allow is a Bulgarian author, business consultant and entrepreneur based in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Her professional career has included accounting, corporate services, business advisory and financial technology. She founded My Business Consulting DMCC in 2009 and later became involved in the development of BookBI, an accounting software application. [ref: Емирствата са рай без партии и данъци - Свят — Новини Стандарт, www.standartnews.com] [ref: How Kamelia Allow built a life and a business in the UAE] [ref: Камелия Аллоу: Академията остава за мен на върха, Actualno Svishtov]

In 2018, Allow received the Leading Woman in Business award at the Dubai Multi Commodities Centre (DMCC) Member Awards.[4]

== Early life and education ==
Allow was born in Haskovo, Bulgaria, and raised in Simeonovgrad.[3] She attended the D. A. Tsenov Academy of Economics in Svishtov from 1994 to 1999. She moved to the United Arab Emirates in 1999.

== Career ==

=== Early career ===
Allow began her professional career in Bulgaria before relocating to the United Arab Emirates in 1999. In an interview with Dubai Newsweek, she described beginning her career in Abu Dhabi while developing her English-language and professional skills.

During the following decade, she worked in accounting, finance and administrative positions in the UAE, including roles in hospitality, aviation services, investment and precious-metals trading.

A 2014 article in the Bulgarian newspaper Standart identified Allow as a Bulgarian expatriate who had been living in Dubai since 1999. The article included her observations about living and working in the United Arab Emirates.

=== My Business Consulting DMCC ===
In June 2009, Allow founded My Business Consulting DMCC, a Dubai-based company providing corporate services, business consulting, accounting and company formation assistance.

The business expanded during the following decade. In a 2025 interview with Dubai Newsweek, Allow stated that the company had grown from an initial team of two employees and one client to serving more than 3,000 clients before her departure.

In June 2019, the UAE business publication SME10X published an interview with Allow and Keren Jadhav discussing business and life following an acquisition involving My Business Consulting DMCC. [ref: #10XTakeover: My Business Consulting DMCC, www.sme10x.com]

During Allow's association with the company, My Business Consulting DMCC received recognition at the DMCC Member Awards, including the Best Marketing Campaign award in 2018. [ref: Winners Announced for the DMCC Member Awards 2018, dmcc.ae]

=== Subsequent business activities ===
In October 2021, Allow established Bowarr Management Ltd, a Dubai International Financial Centre-based business advisory company focused on business valuations, due diligence and feasibility studies. She served as its chief executive until March 2023. [ref: Bowarr Management Ltd – Arabian Business Directory, Arabian Business Community] [ref: ]

In May 2024, Allow founded Numtrex for Accounting & Bookkeeping Co LLC, a Dubai-based company providing accounting and advisory services. [ref: NUMTREX FOR ACCOUNTING & BOOKKEEPING CO. LLC — ملف المخاطر والرخصة والسجل في الإمارات · Counterscope, Counterscope] [ref: Kamelia Allow - Chief Executive Officer at Numtrex Accounting & Bookkeeping LLC, THE ORG]

In January 2025, she established BookBI AI FZCO, a financial technology company developing an AI-assisted accounting application. In an interview published by Actualno Svishtov in January 2026, Allow discussed the launch of BookBI in August 2025 and its intended use by entrepreneurs without formal accounting training.

Allow has been listed as a board member of the Bulgarian Business Council in Dubai. [ref: Leadership, Bulgarian Business Council - Dubai]

==Publications==
===Books===
Allow has authored two books addressing entrepreneurship and her professional experiences.

* 5 to 25: Take Your Business to the Next Level (2022). A business management book discussing organizational growth, business processes and operational systems. [ref: 5 TO 25, Dubai library distributors] [ref: 5 to 25: Take Your Business to the Next Level, Amazon UAE]
* From Eastern Shadows to Desert Gold: My Unlikely Rise as a Woman in the Arab Business World (2024). An autobiographical account of her experiences and career in the United Arab Emirates. [ref: From Eastern Shadows to Desert Gold: My Unlikely Rise as a Woman in the Arab Business World, Amazon]

==Speaking engagements==
Allow spoke at the INNOWAVE 2017 Business & Startup Forum in Varna, Bulgaria, where she discussed financial management for new businesses. [ref: An overview of Innowave 2017 Business & Startup Forum, Dyaksov.com]

In June 2026, she was listed as a speaker at a Bulgarian Business Council event titled UAE's Resilience: Unlocking New Business Opportunities in a Changing Landscape. [ref: UAE’s Resilience: Unlocking New Business Opportunities in a Changing Landscape, Bulgarian Business Council - Dubai]

== Awards and recognition ==
Allow has received awards relating to business leadership and entrepreneurship.

In 2017, she was listed among the recipients of the Influential Businesswoman Awards organized by Acquisition International, in connection with My Business Consulting DMCC. [ref: My Business Consulting DMCC – Kamelia Allow, Acquisition International]

In 2018, she received the Leading Woman in Business award at the DMCC Member Awards. The awards were organized by the Dubai Multi Commodities Centre to recognize achievements among its member companies.

In March 2019, she was named the female recipient of the Stars of Business Leadership Award, according to coverage published by BizToday News. [ref: Winners of Stars of Business Leadership Awards 2019 announced, Biz Today] [ref: Who are the Winners of Stars of Business Leadership Awards?, Day of Dubai]

== References ==

data.text:
----

Our Cycle

OurCycle is a mobile application for tracking the menstrual cycle that is designed to be shared with a partner. It is available for iOS, watchOS, and Android, and was founded by [user], with Andrius Steponavičius as technical co-founder. [ref]

History

* May 2026: OurCycle was releasedon the App Store as a cycle tracker that one person keeos and a partner can follow.[ref]
* September 2026:
** An Android version was released on Google Play.[ref]
** The app added partner invitations by link and "mutual" tracking, in which both partners track a cycle.
** It added "Our Picture", a shared puzzle that fills as both partners check in.
** Spanish and Portuguese versions were released.[ref]
* October 2026:
** German and French versions were added.[ref]
** The daily check-in was extended so users can select several feelings and cravings at once.[ref]
** The company announced Body", described below.[ref]
** It began testing a wider set of women's health tools.[ref]

Features

* Cycle tracking: the user records period days and a daily check-in covering energy, mood, stress, pain and symptoms. The app estimates cycle phases from her own history, not a fixed 28-day model, and refines its estimates as more cycles are logged.[ref]
* Partner features: a paired partner receives a daily summary of the information she chooses to share, and can send short "signals" in return. The app supports couples of any gender, including female couples.[ref]
* Body: a page that summarises how the user's body is doing on a given day compared with her own usual pattern for the same part of her cycle. It combines the daily check-in with data from Apple Health on iPhone, and from Health Connect on Android (including Samsung Health). It reads sleep, resting heart rate, heart rate variability and skin temperature from wearables such as Apple Watch, Galaxy Watch, Oura, WHOOP, Garmin and Fitbit. Users can also log exercise, basal body temperature and ovulation test results. Health data read from these sources is processed on the device.[ref]
* Women's health tools (announced, in testing):
** Logging of sexual activity and contraception method
** Additional symptioms.
** Life-stage modes for trying to conceive, pregnancy and premenopause.
** Medication reminders
** A PDF report of cycles and symptoms for medical appointments.[ref]
* Apple Watch: app with cycle information and partner signals.[ref]

Privacy

Each category of information is shared with the partner only if the tracking user turns it on. [ref]

Business model

OurCycle is free to download, with an optional subscription, OurCycle Plus.[ref]

data.title: Raman Raheja
data.text:
Raman Raheja is an Indian sports and media entrepreneur. He is the co-founder of Legends League Cricket (LLC), a T20 cricket league featuring former international cricketers. Before this, he was founding CEO of the World Kabaddi League (WKL) and founder of the sports-media company Sports Flashes. [ref: IPL-style kabaddi league launched, Al Jazeera] [ref: ITV Network to buy out Sports Flashes' radio business in an all-stock deal, The Economic Times]

Notably all the three initiatives were unique and first of its kind in Sports Business. LLC created a new category of Cricket format, [ref: Legends League Cricket, Times of India] WKL launched and promoted a 4000 year old indigenous sport on global stage [ref: World Kabaddi League, NDTV] and Sports Flashes was the first Digital Sports Radio platform of India [ref: 1st 24x7 Sports Radio Channel of India, Exchange4Media]

Raheja has worked in the entertainment and events industry and later contributed in development of sports leagues, sports media, marketing and research in India. [ref: Exclusive: Sports Flashes raises pre-Series A funding, TechCircle]

Through LLC, he was also involved in hosting some noteworthy cricket matches featuring former international players in Jammu and Srinagar, cities which were deprived of international cricket for several decades. [ref: After 35 years, Jammu witnesses return of international cricket, The Indian Express] [ref: Legends League brings back cricketing action to Kashmir after 38 years, Hindustan Times]

==Career==

===World Kabaddi League===

Raheja served as the founding chief executive officer of the World Kabaddi League (WKL), a professional circle-style kabaddi competition launched in 2014. The league was part of Kabaddi's growth in India along with Pro Kabaddi League

The competition was conceived as an international touring sports property as its structure had been modelled on Formula One, with plans for teams to compete in cities across several countries. The inaugural season began in London before subsequently staging matches in India. [ref: World Kabaddi League, Times of India]

===Sports research===

In 2016, Raheja was part of sports research organisation Super Insight, and was instrumental in the launch of Indian Sports Salaries Report 2016. Media stories described it as India's first sports salaries report [ref: India's first ever Sports Salary Report reveals startling facts, The Sports Mirror] with compensation details across eight professional sports leagues in India, including the Indian Premier League, Indian Super League, Pro Kabaddi League, Hockey India League, International Premier Tennis League, Premier Badminton League, Champions Tennis League and Pro Wrestling League. [ref: Foreign players pocket major chunk of money in Indian leagues, The Economic Times]

=== Athlete management ===

Raheja was also involved in athlete management and marketing. He handled commercial interests of Indian wrestler and two-time Olympic medallist Sushil Kumar. [ref: After Great Khali, Olympian Sushil Kumar may join WWE, Hindustan Times] Raheja was involved in discussions about Kumar's possible move into professional wrestling, including talks with representatives of WWE. [ref: Sushil Kumar considers WWE in bid to extend wrestling career, The Indian Express] There were some reports on Kumar's meeting with WWE representatives and Raheja's involvement in the same. [ref: Sushil on WWE SmackDown?, The Tribune]

===Sports Flashes===

In 2017, Raheja founded Sports Flashes, a sports content and media business that subsequently developed a sports-radio app. [ref: Sports Flashes raises angel round, VCCircle]

Sports Flashes acquired audio broadcast rights for a number of sporting events. In 2018, it acquired the live audio broadcast rights in India for all 380 matches of the English Premier League, under a four-year agreement with talkSPORT. [ref: Alexa to broadcast live commentary of English Premier League, The Economic Times]

The same year, Sports Flashes obtained global audio rights for Indian cricket matches played in India, for outside India territories. [ref: Sports Flashes gets audio rights for Indian cricket, The Economic Times] It also acquired audio broadcast rights for the 2019 Cricket World Cup, and distributed commentary through digital platforms, radio stations and telecommunications partners. [ref: Multi-sport app Sports Flashes acquires ICC World Cup audio rights, The Economic Times]

During the 2019 Cricket World Cup, Sports Flashes was in news for dispute with original rights holder Channel 2 group regarding the production and payment arrangements for the tournament's global audio feed. Media reported allegations of payment defaults between the companies involved and disruption of the audio feed. [ref: ICC struck by bouncer as radio feed for World Cup falls silent, The Times of India]

In 2021, ITV Network, an Indian media house, acquired the radio business of Sports Flashes in an all-stock transaction.

===Legends League Cricket===

Raheja co-founded Legends League Cricket with Vivek Khushalani. The competition was established as a platform for former international cricketers to continue playing competitive cricket after retiring from the international game. [ref: Exclusive: 'Dhoni should play till he's 50 and beyond that' - How Legends League Cricket aspires to extend players' careers, The Times of India]

The first edition was staged in Oman in 2022. LLC subsequently introduced a franchise-based competition in India. Former India coach Ravi Shastri joined the competition as commissioner ahead of its first edition. [ref: Ravi Shastri joins upcoming Legends League as Commissioner, The Indian Express]

The League's management described its objective as providing retired international cricketers with an additional competitive platform to their playing careers.
The league also adopted a strategy of staging matches in Indian cities that had received relatively little international cricket. [ref: Peak wedding season left us scrambling to accommodate 120 players: LLC CEO on struggles of hosting in tier-II cities, Hindustan Times]

In 2022, Legends League Cricket became the subject of an ownership dispute concerning an earlier memorandum of understanding relating to the establishment and operation of the league. Some media reports mentioned that the matter reached the Delhi High Court following a petition seeking arbitration. [ref: Uncertain times: Legends League Cricket caught in 'ownership' row, The New Indian Express]

====Jammu and Srinagar====

In November 2023, LLC hosted matches at the Maulana Azad Stadium in Jammu, which had not hosted international cricket for 35 years. As per media reports, Raheja said the league was seeking to stage matches in smaller cities that had been deprived of international cricket and that Jammu and Kashmir had been high on its list of prospective locations.

In October 2024, LLC subsequently staged seven matches at Bakshi Stadium in Srinagar, bringing former international cricketers to the Kashmir Valley nearly four decades after the region had last hosted international cricket. [ref: Legends League allows long-deprived fans to enjoy cricket again in Kashmir, Al Jazeera]

The Indian Express reported on the return of cricket to Srinagar and quoted Raheja on the league's objective of promoting cricket and inspiring younger audiences. [ref: 'You can't miss Chris Gayle or Irfan Pathan': Cricket comes back to Srinagar, four decades after last international match, The Indian Express]

Al Jazeera examined the wider significance of the event, reporting enthusiasm among spectators while also noting criticism from some local players and observers who questioned whether a short tournament would contribute to the long-term development of cricket in Kashmir.

===Film and media===

In 2026, Raheja was credited as a co-producer of the Hindi crime-comedy film Jeevan Ya Bheema Con?, directed by Abhishek Dogra and starring Arshad Warsi, Sanjeeda Shaikh and Vijay Raaz. The film had earlier been announced under the title Jeevan Bheema Yojana. [ref: Director Abhishek Dogra says Arshad Warsi surprised all with his double role in 'Jeevan Bheema Yojana', India Tribune]

==References==

data.title: Gamivo
data.text:
Gamivo S.A. (stylized as GAMIVO) is a Polish technology company based in Szczecin that develops Gamivo.com, an online platform for digital gaming products. The platform connects suppliers of digital goods with customers worldwide, most of them in Europe and North America. As of June 30, 2026, Gamivo.com had 7.24 million registered users, according to the company's quarterly report. The company was founded in 2017, and its shares have been traded on NewConnect, an alternative trading system for smaller issuers, since April 2021. In a change of business model in December 2023, Gamivo sold its stake in the platform's operator, which continues to run the platform as a separate company under a license from Gamivo; from then on, the company's revenue has come primarily from licensing fees. In articles on game key resale sites that mentioned Gamivo, CNET France described key reselling as legal on paper, and Polygon wrote that it was not always clear whether keys offered on such sites had been obtained legitimately. [ref: Instant Gaming, G2A, Kinguin, Gamivo: du gaming low cost au trafic de clés, CNET France] [ref: The Day Before Steam keys are going for big bucks on gray market sites, Polygon]

== History ==
=== Founding and listing ===
Gamivo was founded in 2017, with the investment fund Tar Heel Capital Pathfinder among its founders. The company's shares debuted on NewConnect on April 22, 2021. In an interview with Parkiet at the time of the debut, management said the company planned to add physical products, such as gaming and computer accessories, to the platform. [ref: Gamivo: Specjalizacja pozwala konkurować z gigantami, Parkiet] In early July 2021, the number of users passed 3 million, up from almost 2.4 million at the start of the year. [ref: GAMIVO poszerza ofertę o akcesoria gamingowe i gry w wersji fizycznej, Wirtualnemedia.pl] By August 2021, the platform linked those users with more than 1,000 suppliers offering over 50,000 products. [ref: Platforma Gamivo notuje 4-krotny wzrost zysku brutto w II kwartale 2021, Wirtualnemedia.pl] Gaming accessories and boxed games were added to the platform on October 1, 2021. That month, Gamivo also began a joint promotion with the game developer Plarium. [ref: GAMIVO kontynuuje współpracę z izraelskim producentem gier Plarium, Wirtualnemedia.pl] The Gamivo group recorded consolidated sales revenue of PLN 28.33 million and a net profit of PLN 4.37 million in the first three quarters of 2021. [ref: Prawie 4,4 mln zł zysku netto odnotowało Gamivo w trzech kwartałach br., Wirtualnemedia.pl] [ref: Quarterly report of GAMIVO S.A. for the period of 01.07.2021 - 30.09.2021, GAMIVO S.A.] The company announced plans in 2021 and 2022 to move its shares to the Main Market of the Warsaw Stock Exchange; as of mid-2026, they were still listed on NewConnect. [ref: GAMIVO ogłasza plany na 2022 rok. Spółka skoncentruje się na skalowaniu oraz automatyzacji ścieżki zakupowej, Wirtualnemedia.pl]

=== 2023 change of business model ===
In December 2023, according to a company press release reported by PAP Biznes, Gamivo adopted a new strategy under which it would simplify its structure and prepare the platform for licensing to other entities; the plan also provided for the sale of the company that operated the platform and handled payment processing. [ref: Gamivo zmienia strategię biznesową, chce m.in. uprościć strukturę i wejść na nowe rynki, Bankier.pl] Under the new model, Gamivo retained ownership of the platform, including its know-how, technology, software, logo, domain, website and other intellectual property, while the company to be sold continued as the platform operator, responsible mainly for processing payments and delivering digital products to buyers. The sale took place in December 2023, and on December 5, 2023, the two companies amended the licensing agreement they had signed on October 29, 2020, raising the license fee. The company said that its revenue would come mainly from licensing fees paid by platform operators, a change that could lower both its consolidated revenue and its costs.

=== Since 2024 ===
On March 20, 2024, Parkiet reported that Gamivo's shares had risen by more than a third that day after the company published its results, presented its plans and announced a dividend. [ref: Euforia na akcjach Gamivo, Parkiet] For the second quarter of 2026, the Gamivo group reported revenue of PLN 3.9 million and a net profit of PLN 1.2 million. The company acquired 127,629 of its own shares at PLN 35 per share in a buyback whose subscription period ran from May 19 to June 1, 2026, after which it held treasury shares representing 12.97% of the total voting rights. Tar Heel Capital Pathfinder MT Limited, the principal shareholder, held 58.09% of the total voting rights after the buyback.

== Business model ==
Gamivo owns the intellectual property rights to the Gamivo.com platform. The platform offers games, gift cards and other digital goods. Since the December 2023 change of business model, the company has concentrated on developing the platform's technology and the Gamivo brand, while transaction processing, payments and digital product delivery are handled by the platform operator. In addition to the parent company, the Gamivo group includes Omnigate, a subsidiary that provides customer support, IT and business administration services. As of June 30, 2026, the Gamivo group had 70 employees and contractors. In its NC Focus summary for the second quarter of 2026, the brokerage Dom Maklerski BOŚ described the expansion of the platform's top-up category and the use of artificial intelligence in customer support as growth opportunities whose financial contribution was still to be confirmed in future reports.

== Reception ==
In March 2021, CNET France included Gamivo, together with Instant Gaming, G2A, Kinguin and Eneba, in an article on low-cost game key sites; the article described the key-reselling business on such sites as legal on paper. According to the article, these sites connect vendors, often private individuals, with buyers, and keys bought cheaply during official sales were later relisted on G2A or Gamivo at higher prices.

In December 2023, Polygon reported that Steam keys for The Day Before were listed for more than $200 on resale sites, citing a price tracker that showed the keys on sites including Kinguin, K4G and Gamivo. Such sites, the outlet wrote, generally had high customer ratings on Trustpilot, but "it's not always clear that keys sold through them were obtained legitimately". Some of those keys, it added, could have been obtained through honest methods, for example from owners of extra Steam keys.

As of October 2026, Gamivo's terms and conditions define a supplier as a user that is "a duly registered business, including a company, partnership or sole trader" and sells products on the platform in the course of its business activity. [ref: Terms & Conditions, Gamivo]
