data.title: K. B. M. Saiful Islam
data.text:
K. B. M. Saiful Islam () is a Bangladeshi academic and professor of veterinary medicine and public health at Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University (SAU) in Dhaka, Bangladesh. [ref: Faculty Profile - Prof. Dr. K. B. M. Saiful Islam, Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University] KBM Saiful Islam previously served as Dean of the Faculty of Animal Science and Veterinary Medicine at SAU and was appointed a Global PR Ambassador for Hokkaido University, Japan. [ref: Veterinarian Dr K B M Saiful Islam appointed Dean of Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University, The Daily Star] [ref: HUPRA Global Ambassador Network - Bangladesh, Hokkaido University]

== Early life and education ==
KBM Saiful completed a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) degree at the University of Chittagong in 2001 and earned a Master of Science (MS) in Medicine from Bangladesh Agricultural University in 2005.

Under a Monbukagakusho (MEXT) scholarship, he pursued graduate studies at Hokkaido University in Sapporo, Japan, earning an MS in 2008 and a PhD in Bio-systems Sustainability in 2011. His doctoral research investigated the role of host bile acids in regulating cecal microbiota composition. [ref: Bile acid is a host factor that regulates the composition of rat cecal microbiota, Gastroenterology] He also completed postgraduate diplomas at the Royal Veterinary and Agricultural University in Denmark (2006) and École Nationale Vétérinaire d'Alfort in France (2017), as well as clinical training at Tufts University in 2024.

== Career ==
KBM Saiful began his career in 2005 as a scientist at the Bangladesh Livestock Research Institute. In May 2013, he joined the Department of Medicine and Public Health at Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University as an Assistant Professor, becoming a Full Professor in September 2020. He served as Chairman of the Department of Medicine and Public Health from 2013 to 2024 and as Dean of the Faculty of Animal Science and Veterinary Medicine from April 2023 to September 2024.

He helped establish the Zoonotic Diseases Research & Information Center (ZDRIC) at SAU, conducting epidemiological research on zoonotic pathogens and food safety. [ref: One Health Day Event Listing 2016 - Asia, One Health Commission] He coordinated international continuing professional development (CPD) workshops for veterinary medicine and pathology in partnership with foreign bodies. [ref: CPD Training for Academic Veterinarians on Animal Disease, Davis-Thompson Foundation] He has served as a technical expert on antimicrobial resistance and food safety advisory committees for Bangladeshi government agencies, including the Bangladesh Standards and Testing Institution.

== Public policy and commentary ==
KBM Saiful regularly contributes policy op-eds and commentary on public health, food safety, dengue control strategies, and One Health initiatives in national daily newspapers. [ref: Controlling dengue requires a national strategy, Dhaka Tribune] [ref: Opinion - Saiful Islam, Prothom Alo] His columns address systemic challenges in health governance and vector-borne disease management. [ref: Author Profile - Prof. Dr. K. B. M. Saiful Islam, The Daily Star] [ref: Author Profile - KBM Saiful Islam, New Age]

data.title: Jonas Dahlberg Strand
data.text:
Jonas Dahlberg Strand (født 2008) er en norsk fotballspiller som spiller i ungdomsavdelingen til den italienske fotballklubben Inter Milan.

== Klubbkarriere ==
Strand begynte å spille fotball for FK Bodø/Glimt som treåring og ble tatt inn i klubbens akademi som 12-åring. I juli 2025, 16 år gammel, signerte han en treårskontrakt med den italienske klubben Inter Milan. [ref: [https://www.an.no/jonas-16-signerte-for-inter-milan-na-blir-det-flytting-tidligere-enn-planlagt/s/5-4-2205489 «Jonas (16) signerte for Inter Milan – nå blir det flytting tidligere enn planlagt»]. Avisa Nordland.] [ref: [https://www.inter.it/en/news/youth-sector-all-transfer-deals Youth sector, all transfer deals]. Inter.] [ref: [https://www.transfermarkt.com/jonas-dahlberg-strand/profil/spieler/1253754 Jonas Dahlberg Strand – spillerprofil]. Transfermarkt.]

I sesongen 2025–2026 spilte Strand for Inters U18-lag, som vant det italienske U18-mesterskapet. Prestasjonene hans i løpet av sesongen ble omtalt i norske og italienske sportsmedier. [ref: [https://www.bodonu.no/jonas-17-ble-seriemester-i-italia-sammenlignes-med-zlatan/s/80-159-16339 «Jonas (17) ble seriemester i Italia: Sammenlignes med Zlatan»]. Bodø Nu.] [ref: [https://www.sprintesport.it/nazionali/2026/06/12/news/inter-nella-notte-piu-calda-la-firma-e-glaciale-il-gigante-del-nord-cambia-il-destino-allo-scadere-756002/ «Inter, nella notte più calda la firma è glaciale: il gigante del Nord cambia il destino allo scadere»]. Sprint e Sport, 12. juni 2026.]

Som 16-åring fikk Strand også trene med Inters førstelag. [ref: [https://www.bodonu.no/jonas-fikk-trene-med-a-laget-til-inter/s/5-159-209907 «Jonas (16) fikk trene med A-laget til Inter: – En helt annen verden»]. Bodø Nu.] [ref: [https://www.an.no/16-aringen-fra-bodo-imponerer-i-italia/s/5-4-2263664 «16-åringen fra Bodø imponerer i Italia»]. Avisa Nordland.]

Ifølge statistikk fra Norges Fotballforbund spilte Strand for flere av ungdomslagene til Bodø/Glimt, samt Bodø/Glimt 2. I 2025 scoret han fire mål på fire kamper for Bodø/Glimt 2 i 4. divisjon menn, tilsvarende et målsnitt på ett mål per kamp. [ref: [https://www.fotball.no/fotballdata/person/profil/?fiksId=3866856&underside=statistikk Jonas Dahlberg Strand – statistikk]. Norges Fotballforbund.]

== Landslagskarriere ==
Strand deltok på Norges Fotballforbunds Equinor Talentleir to ganger i 2022, som en del av Landslagsskolens talentutvikling. [ref: [https://www.fotball.no/barn-og-ungdom/landslagsskolen/2022/uttak-equinor-talentleir-gutter/ Uttak til Equinor Talentleir for gutter]. Norges Fotballforbund.] [ref: [https://www.fotball.no/landslag/norge-gutter-15/2022/uttak-equinor-talentleir/ Uttak til Equinor Talentleir]. Norges Fotballforbund.] [ref: [https://www.glimt.no/nyheter/tre-spillere-er-klare-for-nasjonal-talentleir Tre spillere er klare for nasjonal talentleir]. FK Bodø/Glimt, 25. mars 2022.] [ref: [https://xn--bodposten-n8a.no/fotballtalenter-fra-bodo-glimt-folger-i-haaland-og-odegaard-sine-fotspor/ Fotballtalenter fra Bodø/Glimt følger i Haaland og Ødegaard sine fotspor]. Bodøposten, 29. juni 2022.]

Strand har representert Norge på aldersbestemt landslagsnivå. I september 2026 ble han tatt ut i Norges G18-landslagstropp til privatlandskamper mot England, Wales og USA. [ref: [https://www.fotball.no/landslag/norge-gutter-18/2026/g18-tropp-til-privatlandskamper/ G18-tropp til privatlandskamper]. Norges Fotballforbund.]

data.title: Colonial Narrative
data.text:
Colonial narratives are the stories, myths, and official histories constructed by imperial and settler powers to justify the conquest, dispossession, and governance of colonized lands and peoples. These frameworks typically frame colonizers as bringers of "civilization" and modernity while erasing or misrepresenting Indigenous populations. [ref: https://www.griffithreview.com/articles/disrupting-the-colonial-narrative/]

== History ==
Since the Age of Exploration there have been narratives from the perspectives of the colonists which have attempted to misinform or ignore information of natives. One example is the myth/idea of Terra Nullius used for Australia, to falsely claim the land belonged to no one prior to European arrival, thereby legalising dispossession. [ref: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/ajcp.70075]

== Regions ==
=== Oceania ===

Australia

Colonial narratives of Australia center on the arrival of the First Fleet in 1788 [ref: https://www.britannica.com/topic/colonization-of-Australia] and the foundational myth of Terra Nullius, which erased Indigenous sovereignty. These stories span penal transportation, pastoral expansion, bushranger folklore, and the violent displacement of First Nations peoples. [ref: https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/abs/cambridge-history-of-the-australian-novel/colonial-adventure-novels/EDEACDECF91073DCA95A0AE50121E2A7]

New Zealand

=== North America ===

United States

Mexico

=== South America ===

Brazil

=== Africa ===

South Africa

=== Asia ===

India

data.title: Francesco Siccardo
data.text:
Francesco Siccardo (14 January 1920 – 16 January 2011) was an Italian linguist and lexicographer who taught French language in the Faculty of Political Science of the University of Genoa. He specialised in the lexicology of French political vocabulary, tracing the history of words such as république, républicain, police, intégrisme and nationalisme. His work is cited in the Trésor de la langue française [ref: Intégrisme, Trésor de la langue française informatisé See also the entries nation, prévôt and républicain.] and was reviewed in several French journals. [ref: Francesco Siccardo, « Nationalisme ». Contributo linguistico. Contributo storico-letterario, Mots. Les Langages du politique] [ref: Review of: Francesco Siccardo, « Intégriste » e « intégrisme ». Stratigrafia di due vocaboli francesi, Archives de sciences sociales des religions]

== Life ==
=== Education ===
Siccardo was born in Savona into a farming family. After obtaining a teaching diploma (diploma magistrale), he began teaching in primary school at the age of eighteen while continuing his studies. [ref: Francesco Siccardo, Società Universitaria per gli Studi di Lingua e Letteratura Francese (SUSLLF)] He graduated in modern languages from the University of Turin (Faculty of Magistero), where he studied under Franco Simone, with a thesis on "Madame Bovary and the realist novel of its time" (academic year 1944). [ref: Francesco Siccardo – scheda n. 11046, Tesi d'Archivio (title: "Madame Bovary" e il romanzo realista del tempo; Faculty of Magistero; academic year 1944).] He later took a second degree, in philosophy, at the University of Genoa under.

=== Second World War ===
Called up in August 1942, he attended the infantry reserve officer cadet school in Avellino and was commissioned as a second lieutenant with effect from 5 September 1943, at the depot of the 83rd Infantry Regiment in Pistoia. [ref: State Archive of Savona (Archivio di Stato di Savona), Military District of Savona, service record (foglio matricolare) no. 5186, class of 1920, and personal file of Francesco Siccardo.] After the armistice he was captured by the Germans and deported as an Italian military internee to the camp at Beniaminów, in occupied Poland, where he spent many months in captivity; he returned to Italy in April 1944. In 1971 he was awarded the War Merit Cross for his internment.

=== Academic career ===
After a year of study and teaching in France, in 1956 he won the national competition for teaching foreign languages in Italian secondary schools (licei). In 1968 he was appointed lecturer (professore incaricato) in French language for the political science programme at the University of Genoa – the Faculty of Political Science was formally established by decree of 31 October 1969 [ref: Scienze Politiche a Genova, Genova University Press] – and in 1982 he became holder of the chair as professore straordinario (a full professor in his probationary period); [ref: Scritti in onore del prof. Paolo Emilio Taviani, ECIG The author is described as "Professore Straordinario di Lingua Francese, Università di Genova".] he later became full professor (ordinario) of French language at the same university. [ref: Rivista di storia della Chiesa in Italia 55 (2001), p. 569:.] [ref: Scienze Politiche a Genova, Genova University Press]

He advocated the autonomy of linguistic studies from literary studies and promoted the creation of an autonomous Institute of Languages (Istituto di Lingue) within the Faculty of Political Science, which he directed for many years. In 1998 the University of Genoa named him honorary professor. He died at his home in Savona on 16 January 2011.

=== Correspondence ===
Letters by Siccardo are held in the Jacques and Raïssa Maritain papers at the National and University Library of Strasbourg (1959), [ref: National and University Library of Strasbourg, Fonds Jacques et Raïssa Maritain. Inventaire, correspondence, entry "Siccardo Francesco" (two letters: 13 March 1959 and undated).] in the Henry Bordeaux papers at the Departmental Archives of Savoie (1963) [ref: Lettre de Francesco Siccardo à Henry Bordeaux, 1963, Catalogue collectif de France] and in the papers of the poet Luciano Erba (1981). [ref: Siccardo, Francesco (1981 febbraio 27), ArchiVista – Lombardia Archivi] His French correspondents included Georges Simenon, who in a letter to him dated 24 March 1959 described himself as ("entirely apolitical"). [ref: Per un racconto dello scacco. Simenon e Sciascia venticinque anni dopo, Nerosubianco, citing Georges Simenon, "Je suis a-politique", in Laurent Demoulin (ed.), Georges Simenon, Les Cahiers de L'Herne 102 (2013), p. 73.]

== Research ==
His earliest papers, in the early 1950s, dealt with the religious thought of Jean-Jacques Rousseau and the concept of "virtue" in Voltaire. He then turned to the lexicology and lexicography of French, making specialised language – and political vocabulary in particular – the main object of his research at a time when literary studies predominated over linguistic ones in Italian French studies.

He also worked on political and religious history, the history of education, comparative literature (Dante e Victor Hugo, 1965; Cristoforo Colombo nella letteratura francese del XVI secolo, 1986) and the local history of Savona, publishing in the Atti e Memorie of the Società savonese di storia patria. [ref: Atti e Memorie, nuova serie (1967–2026), Società savonese di storia patria (vol. III, 1969, and vol. XI, 1977).]

=== Reception ===
In 1982 named him among the scholars of political vocabulary, alongside Jost Trier, and Émile Benveniste. [ref: Les vocabulaires politiques à l'étude, aujourd'hui (1962–1982), Raison présente] Reviewing Nationalisme (1984) in the journal Mots, Tournier praised its prose, "transparent, elegant and sober Italian that reads like classical French", and its erudition; reviewing «Intégriste» e «intégrisme» (1979), he called it a "little book […] marvellous in its erudition in all languages". [ref: Francesco Siccardo, « Intégriste » e « intégrisme ». Stratigrafia di due vocaboli francesi, Mots. Les Langages du politique Reprinted in Des mots en politique, Klincksieck] The same book was reviewed by Émile Poulat, who described it as a "valuable, well-documented semantic study", by Claude Savart in the Revue d'histoire de l'Église de France [ref: Claude Savart, review, Revue d'histoire de l'Église de France, vol. 66, no. 176 (1980), p. 107 (per the Table du tome LXVI, Persée).] and by Ian Short and Richard Griffiths in French Studies. The historian cites his "erudite lexicographical study", in which Siccardo identified the modernist priest Albert Houtin as the first, in 1902, to use intégrisme in a pejorative sense. [ref: Histoire des traditionalistes, Tallandier]

The historian Jacques Godechot wrote that Siccardo had "set out to follow the fate of this word" (nationalisme), showing how bonapartisme and patriotisme turned into nationalisme in the first half of the 19th century. [ref: La période révolutionnaire et impériale (suite), Revue historique, p. 192 and note 64.] His paper on citoyen, camarade and compagnon (1980) is cited by Philippe Corcuff [ref: Le catégoriel, le professionnel et la classe: usages contemporains de formes historiques, Genèses, note 63.] and discussed by Marc Angenot, who called it "the only work that deals specifically with the questions raised" by his own study while disputing its conclusion that citoyen and camarade were interchangeable. [ref: Citoyen, Camarade, Compagnon: sur les formules d'allocution de la Deuxième Internationale, marcangenot.com, p. 23.] Three of his works appear in Gabrielle Drigeard's bibliography of the political vocabulary of the Third Republic. [ref: Bibliographie sur le vocabulaire et le discours politique de la Troisième République (1879–1914), Mots. Les Langages du politique]

The Trésor de la langue française lists his work in the bibliographies of several entries, including intégrisme, nation, prévôt and républicain; for intégrisme his 1979 book is the only bibliographical source given.

== Selected works ==

* "Quelques difficultés lexicologiques du français moderne pour les Italiens", Le Français moderne 24 (2), 1956, pp. 97–101.
* "Dante e Victor Hugo", Revue de littérature comparée 39, July–September 1965, pp. 427–433.
* "République et républicain: contribution à l'histoire de deux mots", Annali della Facoltà di Scienze politiche dell'Università di Genova 2, 1974, pp. 569–617.
* "Survivance de la langue française aux îles anglo-normandes", Annali della Facoltà di Scienze politiche dell'Università di Genova 3, 1975, pp. 405–452.
* Petit dictionnaire de la politique en France. CLU, 1976; new ed. Genoa: ECIG, 1979.
* "La lingua politica dell'«Ancien Régime» (1660–1789). Progetto lessicografico", Annali della Facoltà di Scienze politiche dell'Università di Genova 4–5 (1976–1977), pp. 439–495.
* «Intégriste» e «intégrisme»: stratigrafia di due vocaboli francesi. Genoa: Il Melangolo, 1979.
* «Police»: profilo di una parola nella storia della lingua francese. Genoa: ECIG, 1979.
* "Citoyen, camarade et compagnon en période de IIIe République triomphante (1889–1913)", in Actes du 2e colloque de lexicologie politique (Saint-Cloud, 1980), vol. 2. Paris: Klincksieck, 1982, pp. 507–519.
* «Nationalisme»: contributo linguistico, contributo storico-letterario. Genoa: ECIG, 1984..
* "Alla ricerca di un neologismo: «Nationalisme»", in La letteratura e l'immaginario. Problemi di semantica e di storia del lessico franco-italiano. Milan: Cisalpino-Goliardica, 1984, pp. 393–399.
* "Cristoforo Colombo nella letteratura francese del XVI secolo", in Scritti in onore del prof. Paolo Emilio Taviani, vol. 3. Genoa: ECIG, 1986, pp. 287–307.
* "1917. La guerre, la paix et le pape dans un sermon du père Sertillanges", Mots. Les Langages du politique 24, September 1990, pp. 102–116..
* "«La Democrazia in America» di Alexis de Tocqueville", Vita e Pensiero 76 (3), March 1993, pp. 172–185.

== References ==

data.title: Kenneth Akiti
data.text:
----

Kenneth Tetteh Akiti

Kenneth Tetteh Akiti is a Ghanaian electrical and electronics engineer, researcher, and inventor whose work encompasses embedded systems, magnetic-field measurement, and battery energy storage technologies. He is a doctoral researcher at Edith Cowan University in Western Australia, where his research focuses on the reuse of retired electric mining vehicle batteries in stationary energy storage applications. [ref: Kenneth Tetteh Akiti, ECU] [ref: Responsible management of retired mining vehicle batteries to address environmental and economic challenges ​, Minerals Research Institute of WA]

In 2025, Akiti was awarded the Odwyn Jones PhD Scholarship by the [https://www.mriwa.wa.gov.au/ Minerals Research Institute of Western Australia (MRIWA)] for research into the responsible management of retired mining vehicle batteries. He is also a named co-inventor of a patented optical-pumping-based magnetic-field measurement device. [ref: Device and method for measuring scalar magnetic field based on pulsed optical pumping]

Early life and education

Akiti was born in Ghana and attended Presbyterian Boys' Senior High School in Accra, where he studied General Science and joined the robotics club.

He studied Electronics and Communication Engineering at All Nations University in Koforidua, Ghana, graduating with a Bachelor of Engineering degree with First Class Honours in 2017.

He subsequently studied at Zhejiang University of Science and Technology in Hangzhou, China, where he obtained a master's degree in Intelligent Manufacturing and Control Engineering. His postgraduate work included research on laser stabilization and magnetic-field measurement systems. [ref: A kilohertz bandwidth and sensitive scalar atomic magnetometer using an optical multipass cell, Measurement]

Akiti later enrolled in a doctoral programme in Electrical and Electronic Engineering at Edith Cowan University in Perth, Australia. His doctoral research concerns battery management, optimization, and the repurposing of retired electric vehicle batteries for secondary energy storage applications.

Engineering career

Akiti has worked in embedded systems engineering, electronic circuit design, and autonomous systems development.

During his early career in Ghana, he worked at Syngle Electronics Bay, where his engineering activities included microcontroller-based systems, electronic prototyping, and embedded hardware development.

He subsequently worked at Robsense Technology in Hangzhou, China, developing embedded systems for unmanned aerial vehicles and related control technologies.

His professional and research interests include microcontroller programming, autonomous systems, electronic instrumentation, and energy storage system design.

ResearchMagnetic-field measurement and instrumentation

During his postgraduate studies in China, Akiti participated in research involving atomic magnetometers and optical instrumentation.

He co-authored the 2022 paper "A kilohertz bandwidth and sensitive scalar atomic magnetometer using an optical multipass cell", published in the journal "Measurement". The study investigated a scalar atomic magnetometer designed to achieve high measurement bandwidth and sensitivity through an optical multipass cell.

Akiti is also listed as a co-inventor of United States patent US11486945B1, "Device and method for measuring scalar magnetic field based on pulsed optical pumping", granted on 1 November 2022. The patent describes an optical-pumping-based system for measuring magnetic fields.

Second-life battery systems

At Edith Cowan University, Akiti's doctoral research examines the technical challenges associated with reusing retired batteries from electrically powered mining vehicles.

The project, titled "Responsible management of retired mining vehicle batteries to address environmental and economic challenges", investigates methods of repurposing batteries for stationary battery energy storage systems.

His research includes predictive modelling, battery-cell performance assessment, and dynamic reconfiguration of electrical connections within battery packs. These approaches are intended to address cell heterogeneity, performance degradation, and the operational limitations of conventional fixed-configuration battery systems.

The project has potential applications in renewable energy integration and energy storage for mining operations and remote communities.

In 2026, Akiti and colleagues authored "Switching configurations for reconfigurable battery packs: A review", a study examining switching architectures used in reconfigurable battery systems, including their complexity, fault tolerance, and implementation characteristics. [ref: Switching Configurations for reconfigurable battery packs: A review, Journal of Energy Storage]

Awards and recognition

In 2025, Akiti received the MRIWA Odwyn Jones PhD Scholarship, supporting his research at Edith Cowan University.

The award and associated research project were documented in the Minerals Research Institute of Western Australia's 2024–25 annual report, which identified his project as part of the institute's research and workforce development programme.

Akiti was also featured among the researchers presenting at MRIWA's 2025 scholarship programme events. [ref: Speakers 2025, Minerals Research Institute of WA]

data.title: Atomos Wealth
data.text:
Atomos Wealth is a British wealth management and financial planning company headquartered in London and Bristol. It was formed in 2022 following the acquisition of the UK wealth business of the Sanlam Group by funds managed by Oaktree Capital Management, and trades under the brand "atomos". The firm provides advice-led financial planning alongside discretionary investment management, and is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA).

== History ==
The business has its origins in the UK expansion of the South African financial services group Sanlam, which built a wealth advisory and asset management presence in Britain over a period of around two decades. In September 2021, Sanlam agreed to sell its UK wealth management business to funds managed by Oaktree Capital Management in a transaction reported at around £140 million. The deal completed in 2022, after which the business was rebranded from Sanlam Wealth to atomos.

The rebrand was announced in 2022, with the business commencing trading under the atomos name. Jonathan Polin, who had been chief executive of Sanlam's UK group, continued to lead the company following the change of ownership.

== Corporate structure ==
Atomos Wealth operates through several regulated and non-regulated entities registered at Companies House in England and Wales. Regulated activities are carried out principally through Atomos Investments Limited, which holds FCA permissions for discretionary investment management (FCA firm reference number 122588), and Atomos Financial Planning Limited, which is authorised to arrange and advise on regulated financial products (FCA firm reference number 193503).

The group is owned by funds managed by Oaktree Capital Management, which took control following the 2022 carve-out from Sanlam. In October 2024, the professional-services and advisory firm Willis Towers Watson (WTW) acquired a minority equity stake in the business.

== Operations ==
The company describes its model as advice-led, combining face-to-face financial planning with discretionary fund management and a client-facing digital platform. It operates from offices in London and Bristol alongside a network of regional offices across England.

In November 2022, Atomos entered a sub-advisory arrangement under which Willis Towers Watson took over management of the firm's retail multi-asset portfolios. The commercial relationship between the two firms was extended when WTW took its minority stake in 2024.

== Acquisitions ==
Following its separation from Sanlam, Atomos pursued a programme of acquiring regional financial advisory firms. Acquisitions have included Shore Financial Planning in Devon and Define Wealth in Surrey, both in 2023, and the City of London advisory firm Cartlidge Morland in 2026.

In September 2026, Atomos acquired MWA Financial from its founder and the private equity firm Coniston Capital, in a transaction reported to add almost £1 billion in assets. According to trade press, the acquisition brought the group's total assets under administration to around £8.7 billion.

== Recognition ==
Atomos has been named in the WealthBriefing Wealth for Good Awards. Coverage of the firm and its transactions has appeared in financial trade publications including Professional Adviser, Investment Week and International Adviser.

data.title: Eliangiringa Kaale
data.text:
|

Eliangiringa Amos Kaale (born 4 March 1971) is a Tanzanian pharmacist, researcher, and expert in pharmaceutical regulatory science. [ref: Professor Eliangiringa Kaale, Infectious Diseases Data Observatory] His work and research focus primarily on drug quality assurance, pharmaceutical analysis, post-marketing surveillance, and the strengthening of medicine regulatory systems and health supply chains in developing countries, particularly across Africa.

He is a Professor of Medicinal Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs at the School of Pharmacy at Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences (MUHAS). [ref: MUHAS na wadau wajadili mtaala mpya wa usimamizi na ugavi wa bidhaa za afya, Mwananchi] He has also served as an Africa Oxford Initiative (AfOx) research fellow collaborating with the Infectious Diseases Data Observatory (IDDO) drug quality group at the University of Oxford, as well as a Georg Forster Research Fellow with the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation in Germany. [ref: Prof. Dr. Eliangiringa Kaale - Profile, Alexander von Humboldt-Stiftung]

== Early life and education ==
Kaale began his higher education in pharmacy at the University of Dar es Salaam (UDSM), earning a Bachelor of Pharmacy (B.Pharm.) degree in 1997. He pursued postgraduate studies in Belgium at KU Leuven, where he obtained a Master of Science in Pharmaceutical Sciences in 1999 and a Ph.D. in Pharmaceutical Sciences in 2003. [ref: Kaale - Academic Qualifications, African Scientists Directory]

In 2007, he earned a postgraduate diploma in Monitoring and Evaluation from Stellenbosch University in South Africa. Between 2012 and 2014, he served as a senior Georg Forster research fellow at the Institute of Pharmacy and Food Chemistry at the University of Würzburg in Germany.

== Academic and leadership career ==
Following his doctoral studies, Kaale joined the MUHAS School of Pharmacy, rising through the academic ranks to become a Full Professor of Pharmacy in 2018. [ref: Serenus Biotherapeutics Names Accomplished Group Of Researchers To Scientific Advisory Board, BioSpace]

Throughout his career, he has held several administrative and technical leadership positions:
* Head of the Department of Medicinal Chemistry: Overseeing academic training and research in pharmaceutical chemistry and analysis at MUHAS.
* Founder and Director of the Pharmaceutical Research and Development Laboratory: Establishing a regional center in Tanzania for high-level drug quality testing and pharmaceutical formulation development.
* Coordinator of the TMDA-MUHAS Regional Centre of Regulatory Excellence (RCORE): Partnering with the Tanzania Medicines and Medical Devices Authority (TMDA) to build regulatory oversight capacity across various African nations.
* Visiting Lecturer: Teaching and conducting research collaborations with international institutions, including the University of Rwanda and the University of Würzburg.

== Professional contributions ==

=== National and regional ===
* Chairman of the Medicines Technical Committee at TMDA: Heading the technical body responsible for evaluating the safety, efficacy, and quality of human medicines prior to national registration in Tanzania. [ref: Medicine Technical Committee, Tanzania Medicines and Medical Devices Authority]
* Chairman of the Pharmacy Standards Committee: Leading the technical team at the Tanzania Bureau of Standards (TBS) addressing pharmaceutical products.
* Coordinator of the EAC External Quality Assurance Scheme: Coordinating regional initiatives under the East African Community (EAC) to assist drug testing laboratories in maintaining international analytical standards.

=== International ===
* Member of the World Health Organization (WHO) Expert Panel on International Pharmacopoeia and Pharmaceutical Preparations.
* Member of the United States Pharmacopeial Convention (USP) Expert Panel on Surveillance and Quality Monitoring Technologies (2015–2020). [ref: Volunteer Award Winners 2017, United States Pharmacopeial Convention]
* Board Member of PharmaConnect Africa.
* Advisor and Expert on Substandard and Falsified Medical Products (SFMPs) for the African Union Development Agency (AUDA-NEPAD). [ref: Call for Expression of Interest to join the African Working Group on Substandard and Falsified Medical Products, AUDA-NEPAD] [ref: The six critical actions Africa must take to stop the deadly trade in fake, substandard medicines, IOL]

== Awards and honors ==
* Pharmacist of the Year Award – Tanzania Health Summit (2023)
* Partnership Grant for Pharmacy Education and Research – Joint collaboration between MUHAS and the University of Bergen (2019)
* USP Award for Outstanding Contribution to Standards – United States Pharmacopeial Convention (2018)
* Research Infrastructure Grant – Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences (2018)
* Georg Forster Research Fellowship – Alexander von Humboldt Foundation, Germany (2012)

== Research and publications ==
Kaale's research focuses on pharmaceutical analysis, formulation science, quality assurance, post-marketing surveillance, and proficiency testing. According to IDDO, his work includes developing pediatric HIV formulations, generic drug evaluations, and low-cost digital tools for assessing medicine quality in resource-constrained environments.

He has authored numerous studies on the quality of medicines sold in pharmacies and Accredited Drug Dispensing Outlets (ADDOs) in Tanzania:
* The Quality of Selected Essential Medicines Sold in Accredited Drug Dispensing Outlets and Pharmacies in Tanzania, PLOS ONE
* Characterization of drug authenticity using thin-layer chromatography imaging with a mobile phone, Journal of Pharmaceutical and Biomedical Analysis

data.title: RigER
data.text:
RigER (RigER Inc.) is a software company that makes operations management software for oilfield service and equipment rental companies. It was started in Calgary, Alberta, in 2012 by Michael Maltsev, who had worked as chief financial officer of an oilfield rentals company. The company later moved to Texas, and since February 2026 its headquarters has been in Bee Cave, a suburb of Austin. The name stands for "Rig Equipment Rental".
== History ==
Before starting RigER, Michael Maltsev spent three years as chief financial officer of an oilfield rentals company. In a 2014 interview with the Calgary Herald, he said the software available to such companies was expensive and complicated, and that spreadsheets did not work well when many people needed to share data and reports. He said the first prototype took about two months to build, and the first full version was ready about six months later. The Calgary Herald featured the company that year in its "Startup of the Week" column, describing it as software for small and medium-sized energy services companies.

In April 2016, Alberta Oil magazine profiled RigER and Maltsev, whom it described as a former oilfield financial officer with a background in technology. It described RigER's software as cloud-based, usable through mobile apps and designed for small and medium-sized oilfield rental and energy service companies. The magazine reported that RigER had decided to make its software available to other equipment rental firms rather than keep it only for the in-house rental fleet it was first built for. The firm said it had 10 client companies at the end of February 2016. It noted that while other invoice-management software firms operated in Canada, none appeared to focus as closely on oilfield rentals.

In October 2018 the Odessa American put Maltsev on its front page in its coverage of the Permian Basin International Oil Show, where RigER was exhibiting. The paper described RigER as a company operating out of western Canada that makes software for equipment rentals, field tickets and invoicing. Maltsev told the paper that the company had three or four competitors in North America.

In December 2020, Permian Basin Oil & Gas Magazine described RigER as an Alberta-based company in an article about oilfield firms adopting software after the economic crash of spring 2020. Maltsev told the magazine that the COVID-19 pandemic had pushed more oilfield companies to go digital, and that RigER had added new modules.

By 2022 the company was based in Fort Worth, Texas. In June of that year it announced a partnership with CashLine Solutions, a company that provides order-to-cash services to the oil and gas industry. In July, the Midland television station KMID reported that RigER was marking its tenth anniversary and planned to set up a presence in the Midland area.

According to the company, RigER has exhibited at oil and gas trade shows in Canada, the United States and the Middle East since 2017. At ADIPEC in Abu Dhabi in November 2024, the event's official daily newspaper carried a profile of the company. Maltsev spoke at Offshore Europe in September 2025.

In February 2026 RigER moved its headquarters to Bee Cave, Texas. Maltsev said the Austin area's mix of energy and technology companies made it a good fit for the business.
== Products ==
RigER's main product is a cloud-based system with mobile apps. It covers sales, dispatching, field operations, equipment maintenance, asset tracking, safety records, field tickets, invoicing and billing. The company says its software is used in the Americas, Europe and the Middle East.

In 2019 the company presented version 6.5, "Houston", at the Offshore Technology Conference and version 7.0, "Oklahoma", at the Oklahoma Oil & Gas Expo. Version 8.0, called "Odessa", came out in December 2020. It added mobile apps that work offline, customer relationship management tools, a built-in email client and barcode scanning for checking equipment in and out. Version 9.0, "Greeley", was announced in October 2021. It added a web portal for customers, QR-code check-in and check-out of equipment, and a direct link to the OpenInvoice billing platform.

In April 2026 the company released RigER PRO, a separate mobile-first app for field ticketing aimed at small and mid-sized oilfield service companies. Version 2.0, shown at Oil Sands Canada in Calgary in June 2026, added syncing with QuickBooks Online.
== Recognition ==
In 2022 RigER was one of three winners in the digitalization category of E&P magazine's Meritorious Awards for Engineering Innovation, run by Hart Energy. Entries were judged by a panel of engineers and scientists from operating and consulting companies.

data.title: Mulkanoor Cooperative Rural Credit and Marketing Society
data.text:
History

Mulkanoor Cooperative Rural Credit and Marketing Society Ltd. (MCRCMS) is a farmer-owned cooperative society based in Mulkanoor village in Hanumakonda district, Telangana, India. Established on 27 July 1956 under the Hyderabad Cooperative Societies Act, 1952, it was initially known as Mulkanoor Cooperative Rural Bank and was later renamed Mulkanoor Cooperative Rural Credit and Marketing Society. [ref: The Story of Mulkanoor cooperative Rural credit and marketing society, International cooperative Alliance Asia and Pacific]

The society was formed to improve the socio-economic conditions of farmers in Mulkanoor and surrounding villages. It was established in response to challenges faced by cultivators, including limited irrigation facilities, high interest rates on loans, inadequate access to agricultural inputs, distress sales of agricultural produce and dependence on moneylenders. Initially, the cooperative was  established with a membership of 373 farmers.with a share capital of ₹2,300. [ref: New Member: Mulkanoor Cooperative Rural Credit and Marketing Society, International Cooperative Alliance Asia and Pacific]

Its services include agricultural credit, agricultural inputs, agricultural produce procurement and marketing, consumer services and welfare-related activities. Over the following decades, it expanded its membership and developed integrated services in agricultural credit, agricultural production, finance, marketing, value addition and rural development, with the objectives of improving agricultural productivity, increasing farmers' incomes and reducing dependence on moneylenders and intermediaries. [ref: Mulkanoor Light of Indian's Cooperative Movement]

== Area of operation ==
The society's area of operation covers 14 revenue villages across the Bheemadevarapally, Elkathurthy and Velair mandals. These include Mulkanoor, Mutharam, Bheemadevarapally, Gatla Narsingapur, Kothapally, Koppur, Vangara, Rathnagiri, Mallaram, Kothakonda, Mustafapur, Gopalpur, Jeelugula and Errabelly. [ref: The Harvest of Trust, International Cooperative Alliance Asia and Pacific]

Historical government material has also described the cooperative as operating across 14 revenue villages surrounding Mulkanoor and providing agricultural credit, agricultural supplies and agricultural marketing services. [ref: The Harvest of Trust - The Story of Mulkanoor Cooperative Rural Credit and Marketing Society, International Cooperative Alliance Asia and Pacific]

Objectives

The cooperative was established primarily to provide financial and agricultural services to its farmer members. Its activities developed around the following objectives:

* Agriculture credit to members [ref: Agriculture input services, Mulkanoor Cooperative Rural Credit and Marketing Society]
* Procuring and marketing agricultural produce value-addition facilities [ref: Agri Produce Procurement, Mulkanoor Cooperative Rural Credit and Marketing Society]
* Assisting members with agricultural production extension services [ref: Title: Mulkanoor Cooperative Society: A Model of Member - Centric Rural Development Publication: Hindu Dhayashankar Author: Dr.S.L.N.T. Srinivas Date: 20 May 2026]
* Providing consumer and welfare activities [ref: Impact of Institutions on Economy of Farmers-A Case Study of Mulkanoor Co-operative Rural Bank and Marketing Society in Telangana, Indianjournals.com]
* Supplying agricultural inputs
* Supporting agricultural extension and farmer education.

These activities have allowed the society to operate across several stages of the agricultural value chain

== Services ==

=== Agricultural credit ===
MCRCMS provides agricultural and other forms of credit to its members. Its lending activities include short-term seasonal crop loans, medium-term agricultural loans, long-term loans and general-term loans for specified purposes. Agricultural finance supports crop cultivation, the purchase of farm machinery, irrigation facilities and other agricultural activities. The society also provides loans for allied agricultural activities, including dairy farming, poultry farming, sheep rearing, horticulture, sericulture and protected cultivation. [ref: Impact of Institutions on Economy of Farmers-A Case Study of Mulkanoor Cooperative Rural Bank and Marketing Society in Telangana, Researchgate]

The society also provides loans to support the purchase of agricultural equipment and the development of irrigation infrastructure [ref: Impact of Institutions on Economy of Farmers – A Case Study of Mulkanoor Cooperative Rural Bank and Marketing Society in Telangana, Research Gate]

=== Agricultural inputs and extension ===
The cooperative supplies agricultural inputs and provides technical and extension-related assistance to its members. Its agricultural services include the supply of seeds, fertilizers, pesticides and other farming inputs intended to support farm productivity. The International Cooperative Alliance describes the society's agricultural input and extension services as being supported by technical experts. [ref: Agriculture Input Services, Mulkanoor Cooperative Rural Credit and Marketing Society]

=== Procurement and marketing ===
The society purchases agricultural produce from member farmers and undertakes marketing and value-addition activities, helping farmers reach distant markets on a larger scale. Its marketed agricultural products include rice, paddy and cotton [ref: Agri Produce Procurement, Mulkanoor Cooperative Rural Credit and Marketing Society]

The cooperative also operates rice-related processing and marketing activities. Its product portfolio includes varieties such as Sona Masoori, Jai Sri Ram and Telangana RNR. [ref: Mulkanoor Co-op Set to Export Telangana Rice to Us, indiancooperative.com]

Its cotton division includes cotton lint and cotton seed-related activities. [ref: Cotton Division, Mulkanoor Cooperative Rural Credit and Marketing Society]

== Leadership ==
The society was founded by A. K. Vishwanatha Reddy, who played a central role in its establishment in 1956. Historical and institutional sources identify him as the founder of the Mulkanoor cooperative. [ref: Aligireddy Kasi Viswanath Reddy, Mulkanoor Cooperative Rural Credit and Marketing Society]

Aligireddy Praveen Reddy, son of A. K. Vishwanatha Reddy, has served as president of the society. [ref: Aligireddy Praveen Reddy, Wikipedia]

Recognition and external coverage

* Manager of the year award – 1981 – to founder president Shri Aligireddy Kasi Vishwanatha Reddy for best management and outstanding achievement. Only person to receive  this award from the Cooperative sector. [ref: Manager of the Year 1981, Mulkanoor Cooperative Rural Credit and Marketing Society]

* Model Cooperative and best Cooperator – 2004, Government of Andhra Pradesh – for outstanding contribution to cooperative movement on centenary celebration of cooperative movement in India [ref: Best Cooperative Award 2004, Mulkanoor Cooperative Rural Credit and Marketing Society]

* Biennial award for cooperative excellence – 2014, National Cooperative development corporation – Govt. of India corporation – for society’s excellent performance and contribution to cooperative development [ref: Biennial Award for Cooperative Excellence – 2014, Mulkanoor Cooperative Rural Credit and Marketing Society]

*  The Hindu – May 2016 – Mulkanoor Cooperative Society to the rescue of drought ridden villages in Karimnagar [ref: At Mulkanoor, farmers reap the benefits of dairy farming]

* Agriculture Today – July 2014 – Mulkanoor Cooperative Society’s Socio-Economic impact on farmers.

*  International Cooperative Alliance magazine – January 1982, Mulkanoor Cooperative story of self-reliance and rural upliftment. [ref: The Harvest of Trust, International Cooperative Alliance Asia and Pacific]

* The Cooperator – August 1981 – Mulkanoor Cooperative Society’s inspiring success story [ref: Manager of the year 1981, Mulkanoor Cooperative Rural Credit and Marketing Society]

== References ==

data.title: List of Middle Eastern tornadoes in 2026
data.text:
The 2026 Middle Eastern tornado season is the current season of tornadoes and tornado outbreaks across the Middle East and the Caucasus in 2026. As of October, there have been 160 confirmed tornadoes across several countries, resulting in 1 fatalities and at least 30 injuries. [ref: European Severe Weather Database, ESWD]
*Note: Some tornadoes have been rated using different scales. They are counted as their closest IF-Scale equivalent on this table.

Many different meteorological organizations across the Middle East document tornado events, often using different tornado intensity scales, including the Enhanced Fujita (EF) scale, and the International Fujita (IF) scale. [ref: Tornado Rating in Europe with the EF-scale, Keraunos] For consistency, this list primarily uses the IF-scale, the preferred scale of the European Severe Storms Laboratory (ESSL) and its database, the European Severe Weather Database (ESWD). [ref: International Fujita (IF) Scale, European Severe Storms Laboratory]

==Climatology==

The Middle East sees significantly fewer tornadoes than the United States and Europe. Geography plays a major role in this discrepancy, with the unique features in North America making areas like Tornado Alley ideal for severe weather, while the Middle East relies on the heat from the Mediterranean, and the instability from the extreme heat of the deserts. However, the under-reporting of weaker tornadoes across the continent also contributes to this. [ref: Here's why the US has more tornadoes than any other country, CNN] [ref: A Climatology of Tornadoes in Europe: Results from the European Severe Weather Database, Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society] This under-reporting primarily stems from a lack of Middle Eastern collaboration in monitoring tornadoes, and most tornadoes only being tracked by one database, resulting in less public awareness of them or their danger or the real threat they pose. [ref: Tornadoes in Europe: An Underestimated Threat, Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society]

Tornado activity in the Middle East typically peaks in the spring, and is usually lowest during autumn, winter, and sometimes summer months. More specifically, Turkish and Syrian coastal areas peak in the spring and early summer, and most other coastal countries peak in months like January. Tornadoes over land most often occur in the late afternoon and early evening hours. On the other hand, waterspouts, which sometimes move ashore in coastal areas and become tornadoes, peak in late spring and typically occur earlier in the day.

==Season summary==

January was somewhat active, with 17 tornadoes confirmed, and 2 IF2 tornadoes reported. The first half of the month was very active, with 12 of the 17 tornadoes occurring in the first half. On January 8th, a strong IF2 struck Karacalar, Turkey, and a day later a waterspout in Bat Yam, Israel that made landfall, impacted 3 kitesurfers, one being killed after being thrown 150 meters and being struck by a large rock. The second half of the month was shockingly inactive, with only 5 tornadoes occurring, with most being part of a tornado outbreak lasting from January 26 to January 27. On January 26th, a strong IF2 struck Kumköy, Turkey. To end the season off, an IF1.5 tornado impacted Sarıçam and Ahatlar, Turkey.

February and March were both relatively inactive, with 11 tornadoes occurring in February and 12 in March. February was very inactive, with nearly every event being waterspouts. March was significantly more active in tornadic events, but still relatively inactive. On March 29th, an IF1.5 tornado impacted towns north of Aleppo, Syria.

April was slightly active, with 14 confirmed events occurring. The first half of the month was very active, with 12 of the 14 tornadoes occurring in the first half. An IF1.5 tornado struck Uzuncuk, Turkey. The second half was inactive, with 2 tornadoes occurring in the second half of the month. A long funnel cloud was observed in Nicosia, N. Cyprus, with touchdown being considered very likely.

May was an incredibly active month by a large margin, with 27 tornadoes being confirmed, with 8 IF2 rated tornadoes occuring. On May 3rd, a violent tornado outbreak tore parts of Turkey and Syria, with an extremely rare and violent IF4 tornado striking multiple villages along the Syria-Turkey border, and nearly striking a large city in the district of Oğuzeli, with the highest intensity being reported around Akçamezra, Turkey, with mansory houses being destroyed, and mature pistachio trees being entirely debarked. On the same day, 7 out of the 8 IF2 tornadoes occured on this day, and an IF2.5 struck a small rural village in southwestern Viranşehir, Turkey. This tornado outbreak holds multiple records, including strongest tornado in the Middle Eastern region and both Syria and Turkey, and first IF4 rated tornado to ever occur in an European country since 2021.

June and July are tied to be the most inactive months in this season, with both having 8 tornadoes. No significant events occured in the months, with nearly every tornado on this page being waterspouts. August and September were nearly as inactive as February, with 11 tornadoes occurring in August and 16 in September, with 24 of the 26 total events combined being waterspouts. No significant events occured in August or September.

The construction was also solid brick and stone masonry around 30-40cm thick, though connections within the walls seemed weak and were not reinforced. The tornado moved through rural areas and crop fields until it reached east of Kayacık, where it damaged the roof of some farm buildings before crossing a highway. data.title: Zheng Xin
data.text:
wikitext

Zheng Xin (; 1905 – November 1974), originally named Zheng Bingbi (), was a prominent Chinese philosopher, Marxist scholar, and a leading figure in the Department of Philosophy at Peking University. He served as the chair of the department from 1949 to 1952 and again from 1956 to 1966. [ref: Peking University Department of Philosophy history records.] He is recognized for his extensive research on Immanuel Kant's transcendental philosophy and his active participation in the ideological transformations of the early People's Republic of China (PRC), notably his systematic critique of the philosopher Zhang Dongsun. [ref: Information regarding his philosophical debates and works.]

== Early life and education ==
Zheng was born in Lujiang County, Hefei, Anhui Province in 1905. He graduated from the Department of Philosophy at Nankai University in 1926. During his youth, he participated in the Northern Expedition following the communist revolutionary Sun Bingwen. Following the Shanghai massacre of 1927, he fled to Germany to escape political persecution.
While in Europe, he studied as a research student in philosophy at the University of Berlin (1927) and Jena University (1928), before registering at Yale University in the United States as a non-degree special student in 1929. His academic focus during this period was primarily on Kantian transcendental philosophy and realism. Consequently, in his later academic career in China, Zheng focused almost exclusively on traditional German Kantianism and Marxist historical materialism, failing to properly or comprehensively introduce the development of modern American philosophical thought to the Chinese academic community.

== Academic career and ideological role ==
In 1932, Hu Shi, then the Dean of the College of Arts and Letters at National Peking University, appointed Zheng as a professor of philosophy. This appointment was viewed as a strategic move to counter the influence of Carsun Chang (Zhang Junmai), a liberal philosopher of the Research Clique. During the Second Sino-Japanese War, Zheng taught at the National Southwestern United University in Yunnan before returning to Peking University after the war.
Following the establishment of the PRC in 1949, Zheng became a close political and ideological ally of Mao Zedong and Zhou Enlai. He was appointed Chair of the Philosophy Department at Peking University (1949–1952). From 1952 to 1956, he directed the Marxist-Leninist Teaching and Research Office, playing a leading role in restructuring higher education toward historical and dialectical materialism.
In 1956, following the removal of the logician Jin Yuelin from the departmental leadership, Zheng reinstated his position as the Chair of the Philosophy Department, serving until the onset of the Cultural Revolution in 1966. He also held several political positions, including a member of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (Philosophy section) and a representative to the National People's Congress. He passed away due to illness in Beijing in November 1974.

== Critique of Zhang Dongsun ==
Zheng played a pivotal role in the early PRC's intellectual purges, most notably targeting Zhang Dongsun, a highly influential philosopher and political figure who attempted to synthesize Western epistemology with Chinese thought. After Zhang became a major political target and fell into severe distress in late 1951, during the "Anti-America and Aid North Korea" campaign—a movement launched in response to the intervention of the US-led United Nations forces in the Korean War—Zheng authored "Critique of Zhang Dongsun's Reactionary Philosophical Thought" (张东荪的反动哲学批判). This work served as a definitive text in the state-led campaign to systematically dismantle Zhang's pluralist epistemology and cultural philosophy, replacing it with orthodox Marxist-Leninist materialism.

== Major works ==
* "Truth and Reality" (真理与实在)
* "An Exposition of Kantianism" (康德学述)
* "The Dissolution of Idealism" (解决唯心主义)
* "Critique of Kant's Philosophy" (康德哲学批判)
* "Critique of Zhang Dongsun's Reactionary Philosophical Thought" (张东荪的反动哲学批判)

data.title: Roofing calculator
data.text:
== Roofing calculator ==
A [https://roofertx.net/tools/ roofing calculator] is a calculation tool used to estimate roof surface area, roofing material quantities, or project costs. Depending on its purpose, it may use measurements supplied by the user or property information processed by an estimating system. Area calculators can account for roof slope and overhangs, while cost estimators may incorporate location, roof size, and complexity. [ref: https://www.gaf.com/en-us/plan-design/homeowner-education/roof-cost/calculator]
== Area estimation ==
Roof surface area differs from the horizontal area covered by a building. On a sloping roof, the surface follows the incline rather than the horizontal projection.

Some roofing calculators estimate this surface using a building’s base area, roof pitch, and eave dimensions. A slope correction factor converts horizontal measurements into an estimated sloping area. [ref: https://roofertx.net/tools/roof-area-calculator/]

For roofs with several sections or different slopes, the individual sections may be measured separately and their areas added together. A single base-area measurement cannot fully describe a complex roof.
== Material estimation ==
Material calculators use an estimated or measured roof area to calculate quantities of roofing products. Their outputs depend on the material assumptions built into the tool.

In roofing estimates, area may be expressed in square feet or roofing squares. A roofing square represents 100 square feet of roof surface. This unit is also used when describing material and installation costs.
== Cost estimation ==
Roofing cost calculators produce estimates using selected project characteristics. For example, GAF describes its residential replacement-cost calculator as using information including property address, roof size, slope, and complexity to generate a non-binding estimate. [ref: https://www.gaf.com/en-us/plan-design/homeowner-education/roof-cost]

Roof replacement costs also depend on the selected materials and the circumstances of the project. Roof slope can affect installation labor, while location influences local costs and applicable requirements.

A calculator’s estimated price and a contractor’s final price may differ. Existing roof layers or damaged decking can require additional work that becomes apparent during removal.

=== Limitations ===
The usefulness of a roofing calculation depends on the measurements and assumptions supplied to it. A calculator based on a simplified roof shape may not account adequately for a roof with multiple intersecting sections. Calculator.net’s documentation recommends measuring individual sections when estimating more complex roofs.

Cost estimates also have a defined scope. GAF characterizes its calculator results as informational and non-binding; they do not constitute a project-specific contract price. [ref: https://www.gaf.com/en-us/plan-design/homeowner-education/roof-cost]

data.text:
Mealzo is a Glasgow-based online food-ordering company. It operates the ordering platform mealzo.co.uk, which lists takeaways and restaurants, and provides hospitality businesses with ordering technology. [ref: Glasgow food ordering app set to expand into England, Insider.co.uk]

== History ==
The company began as a technology business providing payment systems and website building for takeaways and restaurants, and later developed this into a single ordering portal, which was established during the COVID-19 pandemic. According to the company, it operated under the name WeeTech before being renamed Mealzo. [ref: WEETECH UK LIMITED, Mealzo] Mealzo Ltd was incorporated on 27 July 2021, with Pedram Peroz listed as a director. [ref: MEALZO LTD – Officers, Companies House] In 2022, Reza Peroz was managing director.

== Operations ==
Mealzo's platform charges participating restaurants no commission on orders; in 2022, Insider reported that more than 1,000 takeaways and restaurants had signed up. That year the company opened an office in Manchester and a team in London as it expanded beyond Scotland. The company also offers white-label websites and apps under a client's own branding, and states that it has offices in the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United Arab Emirates and Turkey. [ref: ]

== Corporate affairs ==
Mealzo is certified as a B Corp. [ref: Mealzo, B Lab]

== Recognition ==
In 2025, Mealzo won the Best Marketing Campaign category at the World Catering Technology Awards for its "Mealzo Mega Munch" campaign. [ref: World Catering Technology Awards 2025: Winners announced!, Hotel, Restaurant & Catering (HRC)]

data.title: Murder of Samuel Bird
data.text:
Samuel Bird was a 14-year-old member of Paul First Nation who disappeared in Edmonton, Alberta, on June 1, 2025, after leaving his home to visit a friend. His remains were discovered in a rural area outside Edmonton on October 16, 2025. [ref: Mother of Samuel Bird calls for more awareness of all missing, murdered Indigenous children, CBC News]

On October 15, 2025, Edmonton police arrested Bryan Farrell, 38, and charged him with second-degree murder and interfering with a body in connection with Bird's death.

== Disappearance ==
On June 1, 2025, Samuel Bird left his home in west Edmonton to visit a friend. According to police, surveillance footage recorded him at approximately 8:30 p.m. walking through the grounds of Holy Cross School, near 151 Street and 104 Avenue. He subsequently went to a friend's residence near 150 Street and 106 Avenue in the Canora neighbourhood, where investigators said he was last seen. [ref: Man charged with murder as remains of Samuel Bird located outside Edmonton, Yahoo News Malaysia] [ref: Search for Samuel Bird: New information leads police to wooded area 160km west of Edmonton, CityNews Toronto]

In the months following his disappearance, Bird's family and volunteers searched Edmonton and surrounding areas. Missing-person posters were distributed throughout the city, and his mother, Alanna Bird, helped organize community searches. In August, searchers from Manitoba joined efforts to examine the shores and waters of the North Saskatchewan River. [ref: Missing Edmonton teen Samuel Bird presumed dead; police deem death criminal in nature, CityNews Toronto]

Police searched the residence where Bird was last seen on September 18. On September 29, emergency crews responded to a fire at the same property, which investigators described as suspicious. [ref: Family of missing Edmonton teen Samuel Bird pushes to expand search before winter, CityNews Toronto]

On October 1, Edmonton police announced that Bird was presumed dead and that they believed his death was criminal in nature. Investigators said his body might have been concealed in a rural area west of Edmonton and appealed to landowners, hunters and other members of the public for information. His family subsequently redirected its volunteer search efforts toward the area identified by police.

== Search efforts ==
The Evelyn Memorial Search Team from Manitoba assisted with searches of the North Saskatchewan River, using an AquaEye handheld sonar device to scan underwater. [ref: Manitoba group helping search for missing Edmonton teen Samuel Bird, Raven Radio Network] Volunteers with diving experience and underwater cameras also participated, while a community crisis team supplied food and water to searchers. [ref: ]

A Facebook group named Bring Samuel Bird Home supported the search by sharing notices about upcoming searches and gatherings. A fundraiser organized by Samantha Dornbusch on behalf of Alanna Bird directed supporters to the group and sought donations for search supplies, boat rentals, licensed drone operators and specialist water-search teams.

The Confederacy of Treaty No. 6 First Nations supported the family and sought additional assistance from regional and external partners. In an August statement, it acknowledged responders, volunteers and community members searching within Edmonton and neighbouring First Nations, noting that many were using personal resources. [ref: Confederacy of Treaty No. 6 First Nations asks EPS to designate Samuel Bird case as Search and Recovery, Treatysix]

Police-led searches also covered wooded and agricultural land near Carrot Creek, approximately 160 kilometres west of Edmonton. These efforts involved professional ground searchers, cadaver dogs, civilian search dogs and drones.

== Discovery of Remains ==
On the morning of October 16, 2025, Edmonton police located Samuel Bird's remains in a rural area outside the city, more than four months after his disappearance. Police Chief Warren Driechel said developments in the investigation the previous day had led to searches continuing overnight and the recovery the following morning. Police notified Bird's family before publicly announcing the discovery. [ref: Edmonton teen Samuel Bird's body found, arrest made, CityNews Toronto]

The following day, investigators disclosed that the remains had been found in a treed area near a farmer's field south of Stony Plain, west of Edmonton. The location was separate from the area near Carrot Creek where police had concentrated search efforts the previous week. [ref: False tips, narratives complicate difficult investigation death of Samuel Bird: EPS, CityNews Edmonton]

Bird's mother, Alanna Bird, acknowledged the discovery in a social media post and thanked police, volunteer searchers and those who had donated to support the search. [ref: ]

== Perpetrator ==
On October 15, 2025, Edmonton police arrested Bryan Farrell, who was 38 at the time, and charged him with second-degree murder and interfering with a body in connection with Samuel Bird's death. Police stated that Farrell was the only person charged in the homicide and that they were not seeking additional suspects at that time. [ref: REMAINS LOCATED, CHARGES LAID IN SAMUEL BIRD HOMICIDE – EDMONTON POLICE SERVICE - MissingPeople.ca, Missing People Canada]

Farrell was also charged with 13 additional offences, including aggravated assault, arson, firearms and weapons offences, assaulting peace officers with a weapon, uttering threats and fraud over $5,000. According to court documents cited by CityNews, his arson charges related to the September 29 fire at the Canora residence where Bird was last seen. [ref: Samuel Bird: Bail hearing adjourned for man accused of killing teen, CityNews Toronto]

A bail hearing scheduled for October 20, 2025, was postponed until November 10 because the Crown had not yet provided disclosure documents to Farrell's lawyer. On November 10, the hearing was postponed again, to December 17. The charges remained unproven at the time of that reporting [ref: Bail hearing rescheduled for man accused of killing Samuel Bird, APTN News].

== Aftermath ==
Following the discovery of Bird's remains, Assembly of First Nations National Chief Cindy Woodhouse Nepinak expressed condolences to his family and Paul First Nation. In a statement dated October 16, 2025, she called for coordinated action to protect First Nations people and address violence against Indigenous men and boys, including implementation of an existing AFN resolution supporting advocacy and a working group on the issue. [ref: National Chief Cindy Woodhouse Nepinak Extends Condolences on the Tragic Death of Samuel Bird - Assembly of First Nations]

Funeral arrangements included a service at Connelly-McKinley Downtown Funeral Home in Edmonton on November 8, followed by a two-day wake at Paul First Nation. Bird was laid to rest on November 10, 2025. Family supporters also gathered outside the Edmonton courthouse that day as proceedings against the man accused in his death continued. [ref: ] [ref: Family and friends lay Samuel Bird to rest as suspect's bail hearing rescheduled., APTN News]

On June 1, 2026, the first anniversary of Bird's disappearance, community members held a memorial walk from Sir Winston Churchill Square to Dawson Park, where a feast was held. His mother, Alanna Bird, said the gathering was intended both to honour her son and to bring attention to missing and murdered Indigenous children. She also emphasized the importance of community support for grieving families. [ref: Community Members Unite at Samuel Bird Memorial Walk at Churchill Square, CFWE Northern Alberta]

data.title: Abdallah Bostaji
data.text:
Abdallah Bostaji is a Jordanian communications and development cooperation professional whose work has focused on strategic communications, digital media, public diplomacy, and international development. His professional experience includes roles with the Embassy of Sweden in Amman, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), CARE International, and organizations in the private sector.

Bostaji holds a Master of Science in Digital Media and Society from Uppsala University in Sweden, with a minor in Peace and Conflict Studies. His academic and professional interests include digital communication, media analysis, development cooperation, and misinformation in conflict reporting.

Career

Bostaji began his professional career in Jordan, working in marketing, customer service, and digital communications. From 2017 to 2019, he worked at Zain, where his responsibilities included customer communications, digital content, and marketing campaigns.

From 2019 to 2021, he worked as a content manager at The Online Project, a digital communications company based in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. His work included content strategy, brand identity development, campaign management, and digital publishing.

He subsequently worked as a user management adviser at BIGO in Singapore and as a creative director on a production projects in Jordan and Saudi.

Humanitarian and development communications

In 2022, Bostaji joined CARE International in Jordan as an Advocacy and Communications Assistant. His responsibilities included advocacy campaigns, digital content production, and communications supporting humanitarian programmes.

Later that year, he joined the United Nations Development Programme in Jordan as a Communications Associate. His work included developing communication strategies, coordinating multimedia production, preparing publications and briefing materials, and supporting communications for donor-funded development projects. He also contributed to public outreach initiatives related to youth political engagement.

From September 2023 to October 2024, Bostaji worked as a Communications and Programme Officer with the Regional Development Cooperation Section of the Embassy of Sweden in Amman.

His responsibilities covered programme coordination, monitoring and evaluation, partner relations, and communications for development cooperation funded by Sweden and the European Union. He also worked on public diplomacy and bilingual Arabic- and English-language communications, including digital campaigns, publications, photography, and video production.

His role involved coordination with regional partners, civil society organisations, government counterparts, and European institutions on development cooperation activities across the Middle East and North Africa.

Research interests

Bostaji's postgraduate research examined misinformation on social media during conflicts from the perspective of journalists. The research explored the relationship between digital media, conflict reporting, and responses to misinformation.

His academic background combines digital media studies with peace and conflict studies, alongside professional experience in communications for development and humanitarian programmes.

Publications

Bostaji's professional portfolio includes communications materials and articles associated with development and public outreach initiatives. These include:

[https://www.undp.org/jordan/blog/accelerator-lab-jordan-unlocks-power-play The Accelerator Lab Jordan Unlocks the Power of Play]

[https://www.undp.org/jordan/blog/project-based-portfolio-powered-undp-jordan-learns-about-new-way-working From Project-Based to Portfolio-Powered]

[https://www.undp.org/jordan/blog/jordan-accelerator-lab-goes-orange-understand-role-safe-public-transportation-womens-economic-empowerment The Role of Safe Public Transportation in Women's Economic Empowerment] [ref: The Jordan Accelerator Lab Goes Orange 🟠 to understand the role of safe public transportation in women's economic empowerment, UNDP]

[https://www.undp.org/jordan/blog/how-could-open-air-exhibition-improve-tourists-experience-madaba How Could an Open-Air Exhibition Improve Tourists' Experience] [ref: How could an open-air exhibition improve tourists’ experience in Madaba?, UNDP]

Sweden Package of Solutions

Scholarships and awards

Bostaji has received scholarship awards from international educational and cultural organisations, including:

data.title: Nipah Virus: A One Health Perspective
data.text:
Introduction

Nipah virus is a zoonotic paramyxovirus belonging to the genus Henipavirus (Lo & Rota, 2008). It was first identified during an outbreak in Malaysia from September 1998 to June 1999, when it was implicated as the etiological agent of severe encephalitis in people with close exposure to pigs (Lo & Rota, 2008). The virus is primarily maintained in wild populations of fruit bats of the genus Pteropus. The broad tropism of Nipah virus and the lack of therapeutics result in high mean case mortality ranging from 40 to 75% in humans and livestock (Liu et al., 2015; Yadav et al., 2025). For this reason, the World Health Organisation has classified Nipah Virus as a priority pathogen with epidemic potential, and the risks it poses exemplify a One Health public challenge (Yadav et al., 2025).

The complex transmission dynamics across the One Health pillars are particularly difficult with Nipah virus. Transmission usually occurs through direct contact with infected wildlife reservoirs, consumption of contaminated food products with bat excreta or close person-to-person contact (Epstein et al., 2020). A reduction in spillover events requires a multifaceted One Health approach spanning anthropological public health changes, enhanced agricultural biosecurity and wildlife ecology interventions (Yadav et al., 2025). Since its initial detection in Malaysia, the virus has spread throughout South Asia, particularly in Bangladesh and India, often without an intermediate host.

One Health Analysis of Nipah Virus

The Animal Reservoir

The natural reservoir hosts of the Nipah virus are Pteropus fruit bats, which are commonly known as flying foxes (Chua et al., 2000). Natural reservoirs for the virus are asymptomatic, which favours persistent endemicity in wild bat populations (Wacharapluesadee et al., 2010). This is because the intrinsic immune systems of bats favour viral persistence due to the constant production of interferon-alpha, which keeps viral replication suppressed at low, non-lethal levels (Subudhi et al., 2019). Virus shedding occurs via saliva, urine, faeces, and reproductive fluids secreted by the bats. Several events linked to disturbances in bat foraging behaviours have forced the colonies into closer encounters with human settlements and agricultural zones, including habitat destruction, deforestation and extreme weather conditions (Yadav et al., 2025).

Intermediate Hosts and Agricultural Pathways during Spillover Events

During the 1998 Malaysian outbreak, domestic pigs served as the amplifying intermediate hosts (Epstein et al., 2020). The cascade of events occurred when intensified swine farming adjacent to orchards created an interface where bats dropped partially eaten, contaminated fruit into pig enclosures (Epstein et al., 2020). Since the innate immune system of pigs is not like that of bats, upon contracting the virus through the contaminated fruit, virion particle production was amplified, followed by copious shedding (Subudhi et al., 2019). Consequently, occupational transmission events among farm and slaughterhouse workers led to dissemination throughout the farm. Other animals such as horses, goats, and cats tested positive for antibodies or active Nipah virus infection.

Environmental Vectors and Foodborne Pathways

The primary environmental vector is raw date palm sap, which is harvested during winter. During the harvesting season, fruit bats drink sap collected from tapped date palm trees, thereby contaminating the liquid with saliva or urine (Khan et al., 2012). Transmission of Nipah virus occurs in Bangladesh and India, where raw date palm syrup is often consumed raw as khejur rosh, a practice denoted as one of severe public health risk because of the potential to contract the virus (Khan et al., 2012; Yeasmin et al., 2025). This transmission method is most often observed in South Asia.

Disease Occurrence and Clinical Features

* Incubation Period: Typically ranges from 5 to 15 days, though incubation periods up to 45 days have been documented (Nikolay et al., 2019).
* Human Symptoms: Initial symptoms include fever, headache, myalgia, vomiting, and sore throat. Progression can lead to acute respiratory distress and severe encephalitis characterised by drowsiness, disorientation, seizures, and coma within 24 to 48 hours (Nikolay et al., 2019).
* Case Fatality Rate: Estimated between 40% and 75%, varying by outbreak severity, viral strain (Malaysia vs. Bangladesh strain), and local public health infrastructure (Lo & Rota, 2008).
* Secondary Transmission: Person-to-person transmission occurs primarily in household and healthcare settings through close exposure to bodily fluids of infected patients (Nikolay et al., 2019).

Prevention Strategies and One Health Interventions

A multisectoral, One Health approach is required to address the dangers associated with transmission of Nipah virus. It requires multiple, concomitant efforts from all of the One Health Pillars to limit exposure to the viral reservoir: the flying foxes.

Environmental and Wildlife Interventions

* Habitat Preservation: Protecting natural bat habitats reduces stress-induced viral shedding and minimises bat encroachment into agricultural and residential areas.
* Seasonal Surveillance Activities: Early warnings of seasonal spillover risks could be monitored through ecological movements of Pteropus spp. roosting sites and viral surveillance.

Agricultural and Veterinary Interventions

* Biosecurity Measures: Increased biosecurity measures could be enforced in swine holdings where physical barriers (such as netting or roofs over enclosures) prevent fruit bats from accessing livestock feeding areas and fruit orchards.
* Livestock Surveillance: Early clinical detection of respiratory and neurological symptoms in livestock ("barking pig syndrome") allows rapid quarantine, preventing farm-to-human spillover (Mohd Nor et al., 2000).

Community and Anthropological Interventions

* Safe Harvesting Practices: Deploying bamboo skirts or protective mesh over date palm tree taps prevents bats from contacting or contaminating the sap during collection (Khan et al., 2012).
* Public Education Campaigns: Community awareness initiatives advise against consuming raw date palm sap, eating partially bitten fruits, or having unprotected contact with sick animals or individuals (Yeasmin et al., 2025).
* Infection Prevention and Control (IPC): Standardising barrier nursing techniques and personal protective equipment (PPE) in healthcare facilities prevents nosocomial clusters during localised outbreaks.
