Center for Earth and Natural Resource Sciences

[https://cenrs.org/ The Center for Earth and Natural Resource Sciences (CENRS) is an autonomous, multidisciplinary research institution based in Rwanda. Its headquarters are located in Mukamira, Nyabihu District, Northern Rwanda, with a community service branch in Nyabugogo, Kigali City. CENRS was officially established on 3 September 2025 under Rwandan Law No. 007/2021 of 5 February 2021. The Center conducts fundamental and applied research in environmental systems, Earth processes, natural hazards, natural resources, and technologies for pollution control and environmental remediation. It also provides research-based services to local communities. CENRS is currently focused exclusively on research and community services and does not engage in schooling activities].. [ref: ]

History

[https://cenrs.org/ The origins of CENRS can be traced back to 15 September 2016 in Xiamen], where two Rwandan scientists, [https://orcid.org/0000-0003-1244-3434 Jean Claude Ndayishimiye] and [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9686-5177 Pascaline Nyirabuhoro], [https://web.archive.org/web/20160914193505/http://www.nmc.cn/publish/typhoon/warning were pursuing doctoral degrees at the University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and conducting research at the Institute of Urban Environment, Chinese Academy of Sciences[2,3]. At 03:15 CST on 15 September 2016 (19:15 UTC on 14 September), Super Typhoon Meranti, a powerful tropical cyclone, struck Xiamen with measured two-minute sustained winds of 173 km/h]. At that time, Ndayishimiye and Nyirabuhoro were in Xiamen conducting their doctoral research. [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0048969724062144 As young researchers specifically from inland Africa, where tropical cyclones have historically had little or no direct impact, they experienced a tropical cyclone firsthand for the first time and observed its extensive environmental, infrastructural, and societal impacts]. [https://www.climatesignals.org/headlines/china-top-alert-ocean-waves-typhoon-meranti-approaches China’s National Marine Environmental Forecasting Center issued a red ocean-wave warning, the highest level in China’s four-tier warning system]. More than 331,000 people were relocated in Fujian Province, and [https://www.weather.gov.hk/en/publica/tc/tc2016/section3_5rpt.htm widespread power outages affected millions of households]. Schools and kindergartens in Xiamen and other coastal cities in Fujian were closed as a precaution. In China, [https://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2016-09/17/c_135692847.htm official assessments reported direct economic losses of more than ¥16.9 billion (2.6 billion USD) in Fujian Province, with additional losses in neighbouring] Zhejiang Province. [https://www.weather.gov.hk/en/publica/tc/tc2016/section3_5rpt.htm An earlier assessment by the Hong Kong Observatory reported at least 29 deaths in Fujian and Jiangxi and direct economic losses exceeding ¥11.7 billion (1.75 billion USD)]. Ndayishimiye and Nyirabuhoro were deeply impressed by the effectiveness of China’s early warning systems, coordinated evacuation measures, and resilient infrastructure. [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0048969724062144 Their experience extended beyond these observations, as their direct exposure to Super Typhoon Meranti immediately shaped their research interests, with climate extremes and environmental disturbances becoming central areas of their scientific work. Notably, under the supervision of Professor Yang Jun at the Institute of Urban Environment, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Ndayishimiye examined the effects of typhoon-driven disturbances on drinking-water reservoirs and testate amoeba communities] [ref: Community responses of testate amoebae (Arcellinida and Euglyphida) to ecological disturbance explained by contrasting assembly mechanisms in two subtropical reservoirs, Science of the Total Environment]. When Ndayishimiye and Nyirabuhoro began their postdoctoral research at Shenzhen MSU-BIT University in February and September 2021, respectively, Africa was grappling with the devastation shaped by tropical cyclones. [https://web.archive.org/web/20190812000713/http://thoughtleadership.aonbenfield.com//Documents/20190723-analytics-if-1h-global-report.pdf Notably, Intense Tropical Cyclone Idai affected Mozambique, Zimbabwe, and Malawi from 4 to 21 March 2019, causing catastrophic flooding and widespread destruction across the region, with 1,593 deaths, 2,452 injuries, and 3.1 million people affected[14], along with total damages estimated at 2.2 billion USD]. The postdoctoral period provided an opportunity for Ndayishimiye and Nyirabuhoro to translate their research findings and experiences into a concrete institutional vision, with Africa identified as an initial focus because of the widespread vulnerability of its communities. [https://cenrs.org/ On 3 August 2025, they finalized plans to establish a dedicated research institution. They then initiated the legal procedures for establishing CENRS through the Rwanda Development Board. The formal process was completed on 3 September 2025, marking the launch of the center’s official operations]. In support of this vision, Ndayishimiye and Nyirabuhoro pledged one-third of their annual incomes to support CENRS research and community service activities.

Research and services

CENRS conducts research and translates its findings directly into services for local communities, with its activities tailored to the needs of vulnerable communities, particularly those facing financial and resource constraints. This applied, service-oriented model distinguishes it from conventional academic institutions, where research is generally linked to teaching or institutional research programmes rather than to direct community service [ref: ]

Currently, CENRS pursues research across four principal areas, with its research portfolio expected to expand over time: [ref: Super Typhoon Meranti - NASA Science]

1.    Environmental systems and earth processes

Fundamental geological and environmental dynamics.

2.    Natural hazards

Risk assessment, early warning systems, and mitigation strategies.

3.    Natural resource science

Characterisation and sustainable utilisation of natural resources.

4.    Pollution control and remediation

Technologies addressing contamination of water, soil, air, and solid waste.

National and international collaborations

CENRS collaborates with institutions in more than fifteen countries. According to the Nature Index, CENRS’s principal research collaborators include Shenzhen MSU-BIT University, Lomonosov Moscow State University, Beijing Institute of Technology, Henan Normal University, and Saint Petersburg State University [ref: Center for Earth and Natural Resource Sciences (CENRS), Nature Index].

Research output

Although CENRS is a newly established institution, it has already achieved a notable research position in Rwanda and internationally [ref: ]. In the Nature Index 2025–2026 assessment window (June 2025 to May 2026), CENRS ranked 8,715th globally and 14th in Rwanda by overall research output. Among non-profit organisations and non-governmental organisations (NPOs/NGOs), it ranked 2,761st globally and 7th in Rwanda. In terms of research output by subject area, CENRS ranked 4,823rd globally and 6th in Rwanda in the Natural Sciences, and 1,881st globally and 2nd in Rwanda in Earth and Environmental Sciences [ref: Center for Earth and Natural Resource Sciences (CENRS), Nature Index]

Selected publications

In Jagaba AH, Mu’azu ND, Isa MH, Lübken M, Usman AK (Eds.), Biochar Applications Advances in Environmental Remediation and Resource Recovery; Elsevier: Amsterdam, Netherlands, pp. 279‒307. https://doi.org/10.1016/B978-0-443-44581-1.00019-3 [ref: ]

In: Doon RA (Ed.), Transitioning to Climate Action; MDPI: Basel, Switzerland, pp. 163–214. https://doi.org/10.3390/books978-3-03897-875-6 [ref: Transitioning to Climate Action, MDPI]

Water Research. 286, 124248. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.watres.2025.124248 [ref: Determinants of testate amoeba community dynamics in urban waters: Effects of heatwave, air pollution, and hydrological gradient, Water Research]

4.  Nyirabuhoro P, Ndayishimiye JC, Rui N, Saldaev D, Mazei Y, Gao XF. 2025. Biodiversity and water conservation challenges in urban blue-green infrastructure under climate extremes. Water Science and Engineering. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.wse.2025.11.004 [ref: Biodiversity and water conservation challenges in urban blue–green infrastructure under climate extremes, Water Science and Engineering]

5.  Varatharajan GR, Ndayishimiye JC, Nyirabuhoro P. 2025. Emerging contaminants: a rising threat to urban water and a barrier to achieving SDG-aligned planetary protection. Water. 17, 2367. https://doi.org/10.3390/w17162367 [ref: Emerging Contaminants: A Rising Threat to Urban Water and a Barrier to Achieving SDG-Aligned Planetary Protection, Water]

6.  Ndayishimiye JC, Nyirajana J, Nyirabuhoro P, Nacumuyiki PI, Coker AO, Akintayo FO, Mazei Y, Saldaev D, Nkinahamira F, Habumugisha T, Murwanashyaka T. data.title: Ahmad's HotChicken
data.text:
Ahmad's HotChicken, formerly known as Ahmad's Fried Chicken, is a Malaysian fast-food restaurant brand established in 2024. The brand specialises in fried chicken, chicken burgers and other fast-food dishes. It was co-founded by Lailatul Sarahjana Mohd Ismail and Mohd Taufik Khairuddin. The company initially expanded through restaurants, mini-restaurants and kiosks in Malaysia. [ref: Ahmad's Fried Chicken Wants To Give Choices In Local Fast Food Market, Bernama]

In July 2026, the brand introduced a new identity under the name Ahmad's HotChicken. The rebranding was accompanied by changes to its product presentation, chicken recipes and menu offerings. [ref: Ahmad's Official Website, Ahmad's]

== History ==

=== Founding ===

Ahmad's Fried Chicken was established in Malaysia in 2024 by Lailatul Sarahjana Mohd Ismail and her husband, Mohd Taufik Khairuddin. Before entering the fast-food business, the founders had experience operating an online bakery business. Difficulties during the COVID-19 pandemic prompted them to explore other business opportunities.

The founders subsequently developed a business concept focused on fried chicken and the Malaysian fast-food market. Their aim was to establish a local brand that could offer consumers an alternative to established international fast-food chains.

The business initially operated from a small stall at Mydin Senawang in Negeri Sembilan. After receiving a response from customers, the founders moved towards establishing restaurant outlets. The brand's name was derived from the nickname of co-founder Mohd Taufik Khairuddin, according to a report by Bernama.

Lailatul Sarahjana Mohd Ismail was involved in product development and recipe preparation, while Mohd Taufik Khairuddin contributed to market research and branding.

=== Expansion in Malaysia ===

The company expanded its presence through a combination of full-service outlets, smaller restaurant formats and kiosks.

In June 2025, a report published by New Straits Times stated that the company had 30 outlets and planned to open additional locations during the year. [ref: Ahmad's Fried Chicken aims to open 66 new outlets, New Straits Times]

A report published by Bernama in July 2025 subsequently referred to 38 outlets operated by the brand.

These figures reflected the company's expansion during 2025. They should not be interpreted as the number of outlets currently operating, because the company later acknowledged operational challenges and the closure of some locations.

=== Business expansion plans ===

During 2025, Ahmad's Fried Chicken pursued further expansion through business partnerships. Its business model included arrangements intended to allow local entrepreneurs to operate outlets under the brand.

According to Bernama, the estimated investment required to establish an outlet ranged from RM700,000 to RM1 million, depending on its size and location.

The company also expressed ambitions to expand beyond its existing Malaysian market. However, plans for additional outlets or international operations should not be treated as completed developments unless supported by evidence of actual openings.

== Rebranding as Ahmad's HotChicken ==

In July 2026, the company introduced the name Ahmad's HotChicken as part of a rebranding initiative.

The new identity placed greater emphasis on fried chicken, different spice levels and additional menu offerings. The company promoted chicken prepared with a mixture of 13 spices and a selection of five heat levels.

The rebranding also included changes to the presentation of the brand and its customer-facing products. The company used its official website to promote its updated menu and related offerings.

=== Operational challenges ===

In its published communications, the company acknowledged that its rapid expansion had not been accompanied by sufficiently strong operational support systems. It reported that some outlets had closed and some business partners had chosen not to continue operating under the brand.

The company subsequently emphasised improvements to its operating structure, product quality and customer service. Its current operating footprint may therefore differ from the outlet counts reported during the expansion period in 2025.

== Products ==

The brand's principal product is fried chicken. Its menu has included chicken tenders, chicken burgers, rice-based meals and other fast-food dishes.

Products promoted under the newer brand identity include:

* Fried chicken
* Hot tenders
* Spicy Mad Crunch Burger
* Ayam Gepok sets
* Nasi Lemak meals
* Macaroni and cheese dishes

The availability of individual items and their prices may vary by outlet and over time. The company's official website publishes information about its current offerings.

=== Spice levels ===

As part of its 2026 branding, Ahmad's HotChicken promoted five levels of spiciness. The levels were presented under the names Scaredy Cat, Lowkey, Mid, Nocap Hot and Reaper.

The system was intended to allow customers to select a level of heat according to their preferences.

== Business model ==

Ahmad's Fried Chicken expanded through a combination of company operations and business partnerships. In 2025, the company discussed a licensing-based approach to outlet expansion and opportunities for small and medium-sized businesses to participate in its network.

The investment required for an outlet depended on its size and location. The figures reported during 2025 described the anticipated cost of establishing an outlet and should not be confused with the price of a licensing agreement or the company's total operating costs.

The operational difficulties acknowledged by the company in 2026 highlighted the challenges associated with rapid expansion, including the need for consistent operating standards and support for business partners.

== Founders ==

=== Lailatul Sarahjana Mohd Ismail ===

Lailatul Sarahjana Mohd Ismail is a co-founder of Ahmad's Fried Chicken. Before entering the restaurant industry, she worked in the banking sector. She subsequently contributed to the development of the company's food products and recipes.

=== Mohd Taufik Khairuddin ===

Mohd Taufik Khairuddin is a co-founder of the brand. His work included market research and branding. According to Bernama, the brand's name originated from his nickname.

== Market context ==

Ahmad's Fried Chicken emerged in Malaysia's competitive fast-food market, where local restaurant brands operate alongside international chains. Its founders presented the business as a local alternative offering products adapted to the preferences of Malaysian consumers.

The founders also discussed the role of consumer interest in local food brands in the context of public discussions about boycotts of international companies. The brand's long-term competitiveness, however, depends on factors such as food quality, pricing, customer service and operational consistency.

data.title: Udrive Car Sharing/Rental
data.text:
----

== Udrive ==
Udrive [ref: ] is a Dubai-based car-sharing and car-rental company that operates a smartphone-app-based fleet in the United Arab Emirates. Founded in 2016, it describes itself as the first pay-per-minute car-sharing service in the Middle East, and is licensed by Dubai's Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) [ref: Udrive — the UAE’s first pay-per-minute car rental concept, Khaleej Times] [ref: Free petrol, free parking: U-Drive offers cheap, convenient car rental in the UAE, Gulf News: Latest UAE news, Dubai news, Business, travel news, Dubai Gold rate, prayer time, cinema]. Users locate, unlock, and pay for vehicles entirely through the Udrive mobile app, with rentals available by the minute, hour, day, week, or month; fuel, parking, and insurance are included in the price. [ref: Udrive - Car Sharing & Rental App, App Store] [ref: Udrive - Car Sharing & Rental - Apps on Google Play, play.google.com]

Udrive was founded by Hasib Khan, who previously operated a traditional car rental company in Dubai; he has said the idea for Udrive came from repeatedly being unable to offer customers short, ad-hoc rentals under that traditional model [ref: The SME Story: Hasib Khan, founder and CEO of Udrive, gulfbusiness.com] [ref: Money & Me: ‘I never look at how much I own or what my fortune is’, The National] [ref: Thought Leader Interview: Hasib Khan – Bizpreneur Middle East]. Khan is identified as founder and chief executive of Udrive in independent press coverage. [ref: Udrive Data Highlights Growing Role of Car-Sharing in UAE Daily Mobility - Construction Business News Middle East]

== History ==
Udrive launched in Dubai in 2016, marketed as the UAE's first pay-per-minute car rental concept. [ref: Udrive — the UAE’s first pay-per-minute car rental concept, Khaleej Times] By 2017 the company reported more than 20,000 registered customers and over 100,000 trips recorded that year. [ref: Free petrol, free parking: U-Drive offers cheap, convenient car rental in the UAE, Gulf News: Latest UAE news, Dubai news, Business, travel news, Dubai Gold rate, prayer time, cinema]

In 2018, Udrive expanded to Abu Dhabi following a permit from the Abu Dhabi Department of Transport; at that point the company said it had recorded 150,000 rides and 25,000 registered customers in Dubai. [ref: Car-sharing service launched in Abu Dhabi, Gulf News: Latest UAE news, Dubai news, Business, travel news, Dubai Gold rate, prayer time, cinema]

In November 2025, Udrive announced a partnership with BYD and Al-Futtaim Group to add New Energy Vehicles (hybrid models) to its fleet, starting with BYD Song Plus and Qin Plus units with plans to expand to 500. [ref: ] [ref: ] [ref: Udrive’s hybrid pivot is here, and BYD is driving, Tbreak Media UAE] In February 2026, Udrive signed a memorandum of understanding with AGMC, the official MINI importer for Dubai, Sharjah and the Northern Emirates, to add MINI vehicles — including convertibles — to its shared fleet. [ref: Udrive partners with AGMC to introduce MINI vehicles to its car-sharing fleet in the UAE, gulftoday] [ref: Udrive partners with AGMC to introduce MINI vehicles to its car-sharing fleet in the UAE - Biz Today, Biz Today] [ref: ] [ref: تُشارك “يو درايف” مع “AGMC” لإدخال سيارات “MINI” إلى أسطول المشاركة بالسيارات في الإمارات, جريدة الوطن] In July 2026, the company said it had added new "Business Zones" across Dubai, Sharjah, and Ajman as part of continued network expansion. [ref: Udrive Company Overview, Contact Details & Competitors, LeadIQ] [ref: Udrive customers cross 45mln kilometres as UAE demand for car sharing accelerates, ZAWYA] [ref: Dubai car-sharing hotspots revealed: The neighbourhoods where demand is highest - Arabian Business: Latest News on the Middle East, Real Estate, Finance, and More]

== Services ==

=== How it works ===
Users register through the Udrive mobile app (iOS and Android), providing identity documents — an Emirates ID for residents or a passport and international driving licence for tourists — for verification. [ref: ] Once registered, the app displays a map of nearby available vehicles. A user selects a car, chooses a rental package, and unlocks the vehicle via the app without needing to collect a physical key or visit a rental office. [ref: ] At the end of a trip, the rental is ended in the app and the vehicle is left in an approved parking area within the operating zone.

=== Packages and pricing ===
Udrive offers rental packages ranging from short pay-per-minute bookings up to fixed-duration packages of one hour, several hours, one day, and up to one week or longer, with monthly and long-term subscription options also available.

Fuel, parking, and comprehensive insurance are included in the rental price rather than charged separately. The company has stated that its included-parking coverage extends to most public parking zones within its operating areas.

=== Fleet and coverage ===
Udrive's fleet has historically included economy models such as the Toyota Yaris, Peugeot 208, Nissan Sunny, Ford EcoSport, and Kia Picanto, and as of 2026 the company reported operating a fleet of more than 2,000 vehicles, expanding to include hybrid and premium models through partnerships with BYD and MINI. Operating areas include Dubai (including Dubai Marina, Downtown Dubai, Business Bay, DIFC, JBR, Barsha Heights, and Dubai Silicon Oasis), Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, and Ajman.

== How Udrive differs from traditional car rental ==
Udrive's operating model differs from traditional car rental companies in the UAE in several structural respects, according to company and press descriptions of the service: [ref: Udrive’s data reveals how freedom of choice is shaping UAE Millennials’ mobility habits] [ref: Udrive’s data reveals how freedom of choice is shaping UAE Millennials’ mobility habits, menafn.com]

* No counter visit or physical handover. Traditional rental requires visiting a branch, waiting at a counter, and returning the car during branch hours. Udrive's app-based model lets users locate, unlock, and return a vehicle through the app without staff interaction.
* Flexible, granular rental duration. Where traditional rental is typically priced and booked in full-day increments, Udrive offers per-minute and per-hour billing in addition to daily and weekly packages, allowing shorter or less-planned use.
* Bundled costs. Fuel, parking, and insurance are included in Udrive's rental price; traditional rental agreements more commonly bill these separately or require the renter to return the vehicle with a full tank. [ref: ]
* No security deposit. Udrive rentals do not require a security deposit; users link a credit or debit card at registration instead of paying a refundable hold, in contrast to the deposit common at traditional rental counters. [ref: No Deposit Car Rentals in Dubai: Are They Worth It?, Udrive] [ref: How Udrive Car Sharing Works in Dubai: Costs & Zones 2026, First Choice Cars] [ref: Udrive UAE: Complete Guide to Dubai’s Car Sharing Service - driveuae.ae]
* Decentralized vehicle locations. Traditional rental fleets are typically based at a limited number of branch locations (airports, city offices); Udrive vehicles are distributed across street parking and residential/commercial areas within its operating zones, reducing distance to a vehicle for users already in those areas.

This operating model places Udrive within a broader global category of app-based "free-floating" or station-based car-sharing services — a category that also includes operators such as Zipcar and Getaround in other markets — which is generally distinguished from traditional car rental by its use of keyless, app-mediated access and by not requiring a branch visit.

== Reception ==
Media coverage of Udrive, largely from UAE regional outlets, has generally framed the service positively, highlighting its convenience relative to traditional car rental — citing the absence of counter visits, security deposits, and paperwork, along with bundled fuel, parking, and insurance as differentiators. [ref: Essential Dubai Apps to make life easier (...or lazier), Gulf News: Latest UAE news, Dubai news, Business, travel news, Dubai Gold rate, prayer time, cinema] [ref: Is Gen Z Choosing Access Over Ownership When It Comes to Cars?, lofficielarabia.com] Local lifestyle and expat-focused publications have listed the app among recommended tools for getting around Dubai.

App store ratings for Udrive have generally been positive. On the UAE App Store, the app holds a rating of 4.4 out of 5 from approximately 8,800 ratings as of September 2026. On Google Play, the app holds a rating of 4.6 out of 5 from approximately 8,650–8,710 reviews as of the same period (the total shown varies slightly by page section, e.g. 8.71K in the summary vs. 8.65K beside the review breakdown).

Udrive is also listed on Tripadvisor under the "Things to Do" / Transportation category as "Udrive Car Sharing Experience," holding a rating of 4.6 out of 5 bubbles from two reviews as of September 2026 (ranked #755 of 1,862 transportation listings for Dubai on the platform). [ref: Udrive Car Sharing Experience - All You SHOULD Know Before Going (2026 Reviews), Tripadvisor]

data.title: The way I used to be
data.text:
The way I used to be is a 2016 young adult realistic fiction novel with themes of romance and sexual assault. It’s written by Amber Smith [ref: Amber Smith – bestselling author of young adult & middle grade books] and is published by Margaret K. McElderry Books. The novel is about a girl, named Eden, who gets sexually assaulted and how her life gets affected by that. This is a book series with two other books after this one.

== Plot summery ==
The novel begins right after Eden, who is the main character, wakes up after she got raped and sexually abused by Kevin who is her brothers best friend, a person close to her family. She wants it to be a dream, but it’s not. She starts questioning herself for example she think “I don’t know why I didn’t hear the door click shut, why I didn’t lock the damn door to begin with, why I didn’t scream when I opened my eyes and saw him crawling between my sheets, or why I didn’t try to fight him when I still stood a chance”. Eden's mom came into her room in the morning and saw the blood in the bed but she just thought Eden got her period, so she didn’t make a big deal about it. Eden knew in her mind that she should tell somebody, but she couldn’t, instead she kept it a secret. She tries to continue her normal life at school, but she struggles with her feelings and becomes a different person. In school Eden and her friends Mara and Stephen are seen as “nobodys” and are bullied. To get away from that she starts a bookclub, not just because she’s bullied but also because she thinks it will help her get over her trauma. Which it doesn’t.

During the middle part, she starts sophomore year and some time has passed since she was raped and sexually assaulted. Now Eden has changed her looks, it’s like she has become a new person. She doesn’t want to be the shy, “dorky” girl anymore. Instead she tries to appear self-confident and like nothing has happened.

She tries to get control over her life after what Kevin did to her. She still doesn't tell the truth though about what happened and she tries to hide how bad she feels. She has important people around her but still feels lonely and can't tell anyone what happened.

Eden starts talking to a boy in her school who is one year older than her, Josh Miller. He is one of the “popular” boys and they get interested in each other. But she finds it hard to trust others, difficult managing her emotions and letting anyone get close to her. She tries to keep the relationship on her own terms and does not want to show how vulnerable she is. She lies about things, her terms leads to a difficult relationship between them and even though Josh shows love to her she still feels alone. She still continues to keep the abuse a secret.

As the book goes on Eden grows up, she's in senior year and she has become even more emotionally shut off. Eden tries to cope with her pain by partying, drinking alcohol, smoking cigarettes and having casual sexual relationships. But all she wants, even though the abuse was several years ago, is still for someone to ask her if she’s doing fine and to acknowledge her. But no one does and she can’t bear to tell people either. Eden's relationship with her best friend Mara is falling apart, because Eden feels left out, has it hard to show what she needs and behaves kinda bad.

Close to the end, Eden finds out that Kevin has been accused of rape by another girl and the police get involved. Eden then calls Josh again after years of not talking and meets him again and tells him everything about the abuse. Then she also tells her brother Caelin and the book ends with her going to the police and telling them what happened and report Kevin for rape. In the end, she chose to make her voice heard and don't carry this all by herself anymore. She regained control of her life again.

== Major themes ==
There is quite a lot of major themes in the book The way I used to be, but the biggest theme that the whole plot relies on is that Eden gets raped by her older brothers best friend Kevin. This becomes a big theme not only because it's an awful thing but also because Eden doesn’t tell anyone, not even her best friend, and we get to read how much this affects her life considering she changes herself to a completely different person than she was before it all happened and she even starts hating herself.

The book is therefore not just about the assault itself, it’s also very much about what happens to Eden afterwards. The trauma affects her self-image, sexuality, schooling, way of handling emotions and relationships. It affects her for a very long time and we get to read about the consequences that follow her.

Another major theme in this book is Eden’s silence about the assault. The fear, shame and anxiety she feels causes her to keep it to herself instead of telling anyone and get the help she deserves, which causes the isolation and it forces her to navigate this trauma on her own. The author wants to show by this, how important it is to talk to someone if something like this happens. It doesn’t matter who, it could be a parent, a friend, the police or someone you don’t know, but just telling and asking for help is important!

== Development history ==
Smith says in a magazine article that she has always felt a need to explore tough subjects and that’s what fuels her creativity. She wants to understand and in some way make a difference and sexual abuse is also something that always has been “close to her heart”. She first worked with visual art with the themes of sexual violence and trauma, because that was a way for her to work with her thought and emotions surrounding the topic. But then she realised that the things she has tried to accomplish by her visual art would be better to show and tell through words. The writing also opened up her creative world even more. Through the years of Smith's writing, she got more and more compassion for her own inner teenager. She got more respect for her own experiences and problems she had when she was a teenager. Because Smith had faced some abusive situations during her own teenage years. The book The way I used to be, is written with emotional truth, reflection and compassion. But one thing Smith wanted to mark with this book is the message that young people who are sexually violated or abused need to know: you are and always will be worthy, speak out, stand up for yourself and you deserve to be seen and heard no matter how hard it is. She wants to inspire and find one’s own voice, hope, light in the darkness and freedom in truth. [ref: The Story Behind ‘The Way I Used to Be’: An Essay by Author Amber Smith]

== Publication history ==
The way I used to be by Amber Smith was originally published by Margaret K. McElderry Books on March 22, 2016 and was an imprint of Simon and Schuster. It was also published by imprints such as Rock the Boat and OneWorld Publications in international markets.

Smith's book is translated into multiple languages, such as German, French, Spanish, Polish, Swedish and a lot of other languages. [ref: The Way I Used to Be Series by Amber Smith, www.goodreads.com]

== Literary significance and reception ==
The Public Library District says in a review from November 2023, by Alexa Duncan, that it’s an excellent book, but also brutal, powerful and with a strong message. She was moved when she was done reading the book. [ref: In Case You Missed It – The Way I Used to Be by Amber Smith – Argenta-Oreana Public Library District]

A reviewer at the IONIAN college, from February 2026, also gave a review on how she felt when she read the book. She said her heart felt heavy and that she was enthralled in it. She also speaks about the process of what a rape-victime goes thru. [ref: ‘The Way I Used to Be’: Book Recommendation, The Ionian] Another reviewer from SLJ, Mars 2016, does a similar review of the book as the other two reviews. She said that “it was a rough read” with a lot of deep context. [ref: Book Review: The Way I Used To Be by Amber Smith, School Library Journal]

== Awards and nominations ==

* Goodreads choice award nominee 2016 [ref: Announcing the Goodreads Choice Winner in Best Young Adult Fiction!, Goodreads]
* A New York Times bestseller [ref: Young Adult Paperback Books - Best Sellers - Books - March 5, 2023 - The New York Times, The New York Times]

data.title: Ceylon Examiner
data.text:
----

The Ceylon Examiner (originally The Examiner) was an English-language bi-weekly newspaper published in Colombo, British Ceylon. After it was bought in 1859 by a syndicate led by the lawyer Charles Ambrose Lorenz, it has been described as arguably the island's first genuinely local newspaper. [ref: In search of Charles Ambrose Lorenz, [[The Sunday Times (Sri Lanka)]

== History ==
=== Founding ===
The paper was founded in 1846 as The Examiner. [ref: Newspaper publishing in Sri Lanka, [[Sunday Observer (Sri Lanka)] Accounts differ on the exact date: the Sunday Observer places its launch in January 1846, while another account gives 7 September 1846, with Bessell as editor and John Capper as chief contributor. [ref: John Capper: A life in old Ceylon, [[The Sunday Times (Sri Lanka)] Along with the Observer and the Times, it was one of only three English-language newspapers on the island at the time. [ref: Some Notable Burgher Personalities of the Past, VMSL Library]

=== Lorenz era (1859–1871) ===
In 1850–52, a group of Burgher intellectuals, including Lorenz, George and Frederick Nell, John Prins and Charles Ferdinands, published the literary magazine Young Ceylon. [ref: People Inbetween: Ethnic and Class Prejudices in British Ceylon, Thuppahi's Blog] In 1859 the same circle organised the purchase of an English newspaper to serve as a critical voice against the colonial government. Under Lorenz's syndicate, The Examiner was renamed the Ceylon Examiner.

Francis Beven became a co-proprietor at the age of 23, alongside Lorenz and Leopold Ludovici. In 1861 Lorenz succeeded Louis Nell as editor. Until his death in 1871, he edited and largely wrote the paper. He used it to argue for social reform and democratic causes, and to criticise the Governor and the Executive Council. [ref: Some Burgher personalities of the past in the arenas of public debate and politics, WorldGenWeb Sri Lanka]

=== Later years ===
Leopold Ludovici, formerly of the Ceylon Survey Department, later became editor and then proprietor of the paper. [ref: Ludovici, Leopold, Persons of Indian Studies] Robert Farrance also served as its editor, for ten years. [ref: List of Inscriptions on Tombstones and Monuments in Ceylon, of Historical or Local Interest, Government Printer]

== Legacy ==
The Ceylon Examiner has been described as carrying forward the Young Ceylon circle's idea of a shared "Ceylonese" identity from 1859 onwards. [ref: The Cricketing Universe of Sri Lanka: A Short History written in 2007, Thuppahi's Blog] Lorenz himself is credited with coining the term "Ceylonese". The paper was known as a lawyers' paper, and George Wille was among its regular contributors.

data.title: Devicenow
data.text:
devicenow GmbH is a German information technology services company that rents end-user IT hardware to businesses under a device-as-a-service (DaaS) model. It was founded in 2022 as a subsidiary of the technology leasing company CHG-Meridian and is headquartered in Weingarten, Baden-Württemberg.

== History ==
CHG-Meridian announced the formation of devicenow in April 2022, alongside a second new company, the Berlin-based refurbished-hardware reseller circulee. According to a report by the Deutsche Presse-Agentur, the parent company expected that the increase in home working during the COVID-19 pandemic had raised demand for IT equipment, and that short product cycles would lead many companies to prefer renting devices over buying them. At launch, CHG-Meridian stated that the service would be available in 190 countries and would operate on a non-captive basis, that is, independently of specific hardware manufacturers.

The Nuremberg-based IT service company Hemmersbach acted as the service and logistics partner for the offering from its launch. The trade magazine DV-Dialog described devicenow as having been established together with Hemmersbach. In August 2022 the Federal Cartel Office listed a notification (file no. B7-75/22) under which CHG-Meridian planned to acquire shares in, and joint control of, Hemmersbach Holding GmbH and Hemmersbach Worldwide GmbH.

In February 2024 the Norwegian company Techstep announced a partnership with devicenow to offer Techstep's device lifecycle management software to devicenow customers; Techstep reported in October 2024 that the first devicenow customer had been onboarded to the platform.

== Services ==
devicenow rents laptops, desktop computers, tablets and smartphones to companies for a fixed monthly fee per device. The contracts bundle the hardware with services across the device lifecycle, including procurement, pre-configuration, international logistics, a next-business-day replacement service for defective devices, certified data erasure and the reuse of returned devices. According to DV-Dialog, the service is aimed primarily at multinational corporations and larger Mittelstand companies.

Within the CHG-Meridian group, devicenow is operated as a separate brand from the parent company's individually structured leasing business, offering a standardized rental product for workplace IT.

data.title: Flag of Montgomery, Alabama
data.text:
The flag of Montgomery, Alabama is the current flag for Montgomery, Alabama, the capital city of the state of Alabama. It was adopted on October 1st 2026. [ref: City of Montgomery hoists new city flag, WAKA Action 8 News]

==Design==
The flag of Montgomery, Alabama is a diagonal vertical triband with white in the middle and red on the sides. The red bands on the side represent the momentum, movement, and Montgomery's evolving story. The center of the flag has a blue ribbon for renewal, unity, and new beginnings with nine stars on it representing the nine City Council districts. A central outlined star sits on top for unity and leadership, and it's surrounded by two olive branches to represent peace, resilience, growth, and goodwill. [ref: City of Montgomery hoists new city flag, WAKA Action 8 News]

==History==

The old flag of Montgomery, Alabama was created from a contest for a new flag hosted by the Montgomery Chamber of Commerce. The winning entry, which was designed by Robert S. Ryan, was adopted on the 19th of April, 1952. It was divided diagonally at the center of the flag. It had two main colors: red and gray. There was a diagonal strip of blue with a white border and seven white stars at the center of the flag. The two words “city of” was located on the top left corner of the flag, and the name of Alabama’s capital city was at the bottom right corner. There was a gold laurel wreath at the direct center of the flag. [ref: American City Flags: 150 Flags from Akron to Yonkers, North American Vexillological Association]

data.title: William Egerton (1649–1691)
data.text:
Sir William Egerton KB (15 August 1649 – 1691) was an English politician. He sat as MP for Brackley from October 1679 till January 1681, Aylesbury from 1685 till 1687, and Brackley from 1690 till before 24 December 1691. [ref: EGERTON, Hon. Sir William (1649-91)., History of Parliament Online]

In March 1690, he was returned unopposed for Brackley on his family's interest, at that time he was noted by Sir Thomas Osborne, 1st Duke of Leeds as a Whig.

He became a Knight of the Bath on 23 April 1661 and freeman of Chipping Wycombe in 1672.

== Family and education ==
He was the second son of John Egerton, 2nd Earl of Bridgewater and the brother of Charles Egerton. He was admitted into the Inner Temple in 1673. On 23 September 1674, he married Honora, the daughter of Sir Thomas Leigh and they had one son (whom predeceased him) and four daughters.

data.title: Kishan Dholakia
data.text:
----

Kishan Dholakia (FAA) is a physicist and professor specialising in optics and photonics. He holds positions at the Adelaide University in Australia and the University of St Andrews in Scotland. His research centres on the development of optical manipulation techniques, including optical tweezers and structured light beams, and their applications in biology and medicine.

In 2026, Dholakia was elected a Fellow of the Australian Academy of Science [ref: Photonics leader named Australian Academy of Science Fellow, University of Adelaide]. He is an Australian Research Council (ARC) Laureate Fellow (2021-2026) and is a Node Leader and Chief Investigator for the Australian Research Council [https://www.combs.org.au/ Centre of Excellence Optical Microcombs for Breakthrough Science (COMBS)]. He also Director for the [https://www.adelaide.edu.au/centre-of-light-for-life/ Centre of Light for Life] at Adelaide University.

== Early Life and Education ==
Dholakia completed his Bachelor of Arts in Natural Sciences (Physics) from Churchill College, University of Cambridge, in 1988. He then pursued postgraduate studies at Imperial College London, obtaining an MSc with distinction in Applied Optics in 1990, followed by a PhD in Laser Physics in 1993, focusing on laser cooling and trapping of ions [ref: Kishan Dholakia CV].

== Career ==

=== University of St Andrews ===
In 1997, Dholakia joined the University of St Andrews as a Royal Society of Edinburgh Research Fellow. He was a lecturer in the School of Physics and Astronomy in 2000 and became a full Professor of Physics in 2003. At St Andrews, he established the [https://biology.st-andrews.ac.uk/biophotonics/ Centre of Biophotonics] and founded the James Mackenzie Institute for Early Diagnosis in 2019 [ref: Sir James Mackenzie Institute for Early Diagnosis]. He is the head of the [https://opticalmanipulationgroup.wp.st-andrews.ac.uk/ Optical Manipulation Group], with Graham Bruce. The group specialises in many areas of optics, namely Raman spectroscopy, speckle metrology, structured light fields, bioimaging, optical tweezers and levitated optomechanics.

=== Adelaide University ===
In 2020, he joined the University of Adelaide as a Visiting Professor. In 2022, he became a full Professor and the Director for the Centre of Light for Life, together with Deputy Director Associate Professor Kylie Dunning. The Centre vision is "To use light to reveal, measure and understand life and the world around us, and translate these insights into meaningful impact." [ref: Centre of Light for Life Vision Statement, University of Adelaide]. The Centre laboratories house numerous specialised optics, including light sheet fluorescence microscopy, speckle metrology, levitated optomechanics, optical tweezers, quantum imaging, digital holographic microscopy, optical coherence tomography, and Raman spectroscopy. The group consists of approximately 20 researchers, ranging from undergraduate to graduate students, and postdoctoral researchers [ref: Centre of Light for Life researchers, adelaide.edu.au]. The Centre also collaborates with researchers from institutes with Adelaide University: the [https://adelaide.edu.au/research/institute-for-photonics-advanced-sensing-and-quantum-technologies/ Institute of Advanced Sensing and Quantum Technologies] and the [https://adelaide.edu.au/research/robinson-research-institute/ Robinson Research Institute]. Dholakia is Chief Investigator for the Australian Research Council [https://www.combs.org.au/ Centre of Excellence Optical Microcombs for Breakthrough Science (COMBS)], the Australian Research Council [https://arcquantumcentre.com.au/ Training Centre for Current and Emergent Quantum Technologies (QuTech)], and Australian Research Council [https://ai-grainhub.org/researchthemes Industrial Transformation Research Hub in Responsible AI for a Sustainable Grain Industry (grAIn)].

== Research ==
Dholakia's research is widely cited (over 49,000 citations, [https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=OlD7pJoAAAAJ& Google Scholar]) and encompasses:

* Optical Manipulation: Developing optical tweezers which use lasers to trap and manipulate matter at microscopic scales, such as microscopic particles, biological specimens, and molecules [ref: Shaping the future of manipulation, Nature Photonics] [ref: Roadmap for optical tweezers, Journal of Physics: Photonics].
* Structured Light: Exploring Bessel beams [ref: Bessel beams: Diffraction in a new light, Contemporary Physics], Airy beams [ref: Light-sheet microscopy using an Airy beam, Nature Methods], and Laguerre-Gaussian beams [ref: Second-harmonic generation and the conservation of orbital angular momentum with high-order Laguerre-Gaussian modes, Physical Review A] for applications in biological imaging and material analysis, such as multiphoton imaging to improve imaging at depth [ref: All-Optical Methods to Study Neuronal Function: Widefield Multiphoton Imaging at Depth with Temporal Focusing, Springer].
* Biophotonics: Advancing light-sheet fluorescence microscopy for biomedical imaging [ref: Wavefront Shaping for Biomedical Imaging: Shaped Beams for Light Sheet Imaging and Optical Manipulation, Cambridge University Press], notably its use in metabolic imaging of mouse embryos [ref: UVA Hyperspectral Light-Sheet Microscopy for Volumetric Metabolic Imaging: Application to Preimplantation Embryo Development, ACS photonics] and Raman spectroscopy for through-the-bottle whisky detection [ref: Raman spectroscopy using shaped laser light for through-bottle whisky detection, Frontiers in Optics + Laser Science 2023 (FiO, LS) (2023), paper JTu4A.19] and methanol quantification [ref: Non-invasive Raman spectroscopy with wavefront shaping and wavelength modulation to quantify methanol in bottled spirits, Journal of Physics: Photonics].
* Speckle metrology: Using the orbital angular momentum of light beams to generate speckle patterns [ref: Wavelength sensitivity of the speckle patterns produced by an integrating sphere, Journal of Physics: Photonics] for use in precision measurement of biological samples [ref: Speckle-based measurement of the fractional azimuthal index of orbital angular momentum beams for refractive index sensing, Nature Communications].

== Awards and recognition ==
* Fellow of the [https://science.org.au/ Australian Academy of Science] (2026) [ref: Photonics leader named Australian Academy of Science Fellow, University of Adelaide] [ref: Kishan Dholakia, Australian Academy of Science] [ref: Renowned professor elected Fellow of the Australian Academy of Science, University of St Andrews]
* [https://scienceawards.sa.gov.au/ South Australian Science Awards] Scientist of the Year (2025) [ref: Winners announced for the 2025 SA Science Excellence and Innovation Awards, Government of South Australia] [ref: Kishan Dholakia named SA Scientist of the Year 2025, ARC Quantum Centre]
* [https://spie.org/ SPIE] Board of Directors (2025-2027 term) [ref: SPIE Board of Directors 2025-2027, spie.org]
* [https://scienceawards.sa.gov.au/ South Australian Science Awards] Scientist of the Year - Finalist (2023) [ref: Past Winners and Finalists, SA Science Excellence and Innovation Awards]
* SPIE Dennis Gabor Award (2018) [ref: 2018 SPIE Dennis Gabor Award, University of St Andrews]
* Institute of Physics Thomas Young Medal (2017) [ref: The Institute of Physics Awards 2017: Thomas Young Medal and Prize to Kishan Dholakia, SPIE] [ref: St. Andrews’ Dholakia Receives 2017 IOP Thomas Young Medal and Prize, Photonics Media]
* Optica R. W. Wood Prize (2016) [ref: R. W. Wood Prize, Optica] [ref: R. W. Wood Prize, University of St Andrews]
* Fellow of Optica (2008) [ref: Optica Fellows, Optica]
* Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh (2007) [ref: Professor Kishan Dholakia, Royal Society of Edinburgh]

=== Media recognition ===
* ABC news - Raman spectroscopy for methanol detection [ref: Researchers develop laser technology to test drinks for methanol, ABC News]
* 2013 Guiness World Record for fastest man-made rotation of a microscopic object [ref: Scientists create fastest rotating man-made object ever, Financial Express]

== Patents and Industry Collaborations ==
Dholakia holds over 27 patent families, with 23 licensed ([https://patents.google.com/?inventor=Kishan+Dholakia Google Patents]), contributing to technologies such as high-value light-sheet microscopes and optical trapping instruments. His collaborations include partnerships with Boeing USA, M Squared Lasers [ref: University of St. Andrews and M Squared Lasers form partnership for biophotonics research, Laser Focus World], and Elliot Scientific Ltd [ref: Commercial optical traps emerge from biophysics labs, PHYSICS TODAY].

Evan White is a publicist and marketing executive. [ref: The Business of 'Me', The Wall Street Journal] [ref: Viddy, which helps users make and share videos, is a hit at SXSW, Los Angeles Times] He worked as a publicist for Kyle MacDonald, whose One red paperclip project involved a series of trades. White served as Viddy’s chief marketing officer in 2012 and attended South by Southwest in Austin with founder JJ Aguhob that March. data.title: Jon Gluyas
data.text:
Jon Gluyas (born Jonathan Gluyas) is a British geoscientist and energy entrepreneur. He is Emeritus Professor of Geoenergy, Carbon Capture and Storage at Durham University, and was President of the Geological Society of London from 2024 to 2026.

Gluyas spent around fifteen years at BP before moving into the independent oil sector and later academia. In 2015 he worked with Chris Ballentine of the University of Oxford to develop an exploration model used to confirm a large helium gas field in Tanzania, reported at the time as an unusual case of helium being found by deliberate exploration rather than discovered incidentally during oil and gas drilling.

== Early life and education ==
Gluyas traced his interest in geology to a Scout trip to the Yorkshire Dales as a schoolboy. He studied geology at the University of Sheffield and completed a PhD in geochemistry at the University of Liverpool in 1983.

== Career ==
Gluyas joined BP in 1981 as a sedimentologist and research geologist, holding technical and leadership roles in the UK, Norway, Venezuela and China over about fifteen years. He later worked at Monument Oil & Gas and Lasmo, before co-founding Acorn Oil & Gas in 2001, which redeveloped the previously abandoned Argyll/Ardmore oilfield in the North Sea. After Acorn was sold in 2005, he co-founded Fairfield Energy to redevelop mature North Sea assets, and has since founded or co-founded several further energy and earth-observation companies, including Geoptic, a muon-imaging spin-out from Durham, Sheffield and St Mary's University, Twickenham, which won a King's Award for Enterprise in 2025.

He joined Durham University in 2009 as the first holder of a chair in geoenergy, carbon capture and storage in Europe, later serving as Head of the Department of Earth Sciences (2011–2014) and Executive Director of the Durham Energy Institute.

== Research ==
Gluyas's early work focused on sedimentary diagenesis and its effects on sandstone reservoir quality, including a 1992 Nature paper co-authored with Michael Coleman. He has since worked on UK carbon capture and storage research and on deep geothermal energy, co-founding the BritGeothermal research consortium and later serving on the board of the UK National Geothermal Centre.

His 2015 helium work was followed by further research on nitrogen–helium gas field formation, published in Nature in 2023, and a 2025 review of natural hydrogen resource accumulation in Nature Reviews Earth & Environment. Gluyas has also contributed to research on human-induced earthquakes linked to hydraulic fracturing and geothermal operations, including work on the HiQuake database.

== Awards and honours ==
* Aberconway Medal, Geological Society of London (2000), for distinction in applied or economic geoscience.
* Industry Expert Award, SPE Aberdeen Offshore Achievement Awards (2025).
* King's Award for Enterprise, Innovation category (2025), awarded to Geoptic.
* Honorary Fellow, Geological Society of India (2023).

== Selected publications ==
* Gluyas, J. G., & Swarbrick, R. E. Petroleum Geoscience. Wiley-Blackwell.

data.title: The BLCK Madonna
data.text:
----

The BLCK Madonna is the professional name of Ana Hoffman, a New York-based vocalist and recording artist. Hoffman worked professionally as a singer before beginning to record under The BLCK Madonna name. In March of 2026, she released her debut album, Between the Lines, built around seven jazz standards reimagined through new arrangements and fresh interpretations. [ref: Meet the BLCK Madonna: Jazz singer Ana Hoffman redefining reverence and Black womanhood, amNewYork] The album reached a peak of number 37 on JazzWeek’s multiweek jazz chart. [ref: JazzWeek Multiweek Chart, JazzWeek]

== Early life and career ==

Hoffman grew up between Ghana and Texas. [ref: Meet The BLCK Madonna: Jazz singer Ana Hoffman redefining reverence and BLCK womanhood, amNewYork] While attending college in Texas, she was initially planning on a career as a pharmacist until she joined the classical and jazz choirs, where she was first introduced to jazz standards. That experience led her to pursue a professional career in music. [ref: Ana's Life of Jazz, The Royal Gazette]

Her early work included the national tour of Dreamgirls that opened at the Apollo Theatre in New York, where she performed as Michelle Morris and understudied Deena Jones. [ref: THE CITY CLUB Announces Cast; Will star Kristen Martin, Peter Bradbury, Emily Tyra & More, BroadwayWorld] In 2012, she appeared as Maddy in the Off-Broadway production of The City Club at the Minetta Lane Theatre. [ref: THE CITY CLUB Announces Cast; Will star Kristen Martin, Peter Bradbury, Emily Tyra & More, BroadwayWorld]

Following her early theater work, Hoffman stepped away from performing for a period and returned to Ghana where she was born. After moving back to the United States in 2018, she shifted her focus exclusively to music, performing as a lead vocalist and developing her own musical projects. One of those projects, Life Is Jazz, was based upon music associated with the Harlem Renaissance and was commissioned by Holland America Line. Hoffman performed the show as a featured guest artist aboard Holland America voyages until the COVID-19 pandemic interrupted live performances in 2020. [ref: Ana's Life of Jazz, The Royal Gazette]

During the pandemic, Hoffman concentrated on her music, developing her voice, repertoire and approach to jazz standards. In 2022, she also returned to the stage as Josephine Baker in Barry Manilow and Bruce Sussman's Harmony. [ref: Watch Highlights From Opening of Barry Manilow and Bruce Sussman's Harmony Musical, Playbill] Later that year, Life Is Jazz was expanded into a full concert and was selected to open the Bermuda Festival of the Performing Arts. In the years that followed, Hoffman performed regularly in New York [ref: Ana Hoffman, New York Music Month] while continuing to develop the arrangements and sound that would eventually lead to her debut album Between the Lines. [ref: Ana's Life of Jazz, The Royal Gazette]

== The BLCK Madonna ==

In 2025, Hoffman began using the stage name The BLCK Madonna, bringing her recording and live performances together under a new artistic identity. She has described Ana Hoffman and The BLCK Madonna as “two sides of the same coin.” [ref: Meet the BLCK Madonna: Jazz singer Ana Hoffman redefining reverence and Black womanhood, amNewYork]

Her debut album, Between the Lines, was released on March 27, 2026. [ref: BLCK Madonna – Between the Lines, Paris Move] The album consisted of seven jazz standards that Hoffman reworked with new arrangements and soulful interpretations. The repertoire included “Afro Blue,” “‘Round Midnight,” “Body and Soul,” “Night and Day,” “My Funny Valentine,” “Pick Yourself Up” and “Love Is Here to Stay.” [ref: Between the Lines, Apple Music]

Between the Lines received recognition following its release. Jazz Weekly selected it as its “Ringer of the Week,” [ref: Ringer of the Week: The BLCK Madonna – Between the Lines, Jazz Weekly] and French broadcaster TSF Jazz named it one of its Disques du Jour. [ref: The BLCK Madonna, Levi Harvey, Louis Billette, Mario Canonge: voici vos disques du jour, TSF Jazz] T.S. Monk, commenting on Hoffman's recording of “‘Round Midnight,” called it “one of the most beautiful and passionate versions” he had heard. [ref: “Between the Lines”: The BLCK Madonna and the Art of Becoming, Uptown Magazine] The album reached a peak of number 37 on the JazzWeek radio chart and has continued to appear on JazzWeek's multiweek chart. [ref: JazzWeek Multiweek Chart, JazzWeek]

data.title: Sulley (Monsters, Inc.)
data.text:
----

James Patrick "Jimmy" Sullivan, [ref: Powerless] [ref: See the Voices Behind Your Favorite 'Monsters, Inc.' Characters, Entertainment Weekly] often nicknamed Sulley, is a fictional character and one of the main protagonist of the Disney/Pixar's Monsters Inc. franchise, alongside Mike Wazowski. He is primarily voiced by John Goodman. Sulley was a former student at Monsters University before getting expelled, but was able to work at Monsters Incorporated, going from a mailroom worker, to the top scarer, to CEO.

Sulley has been generally well received by critics and audiences for his character, his kind-hearted nature from the first film, and Goodman's performance.

== Creation ==
Throughout production of 2001's Monster, Inc., Sulley had received numerous revisions. In an early concept for the film, Sulley, originally named Johnson, was an up-and-comer at Monsters, Inc., nervous about the possibility of him losing his job after his boss announces a downsizing. Johnson also feels envious due to another scarer, Ned (later renamed Randall), being the company's top performer. Throughout various drafts, Johnson's occupation went back and forth between scarer and some other position such as a janitor, a refinery worker or an assistant to Ned, until eventually given his final incarnation as the top scarer of Monsters, Inc. [ref: ]

Sulley had also received various redesigns. He originally had tentacles, but were scrapped due to them them being too difficult to animate for the time and to avoid distracting the audiences. [ref: Early Tests. Commentary by Thomas Porter, Steve May and Michael Fong, Monsters Inc. 2002 DVD.] He was also planned to wear glasses throughout the film, with test footage depicting the character with them already created. However, the creators abandoned the idea as they found the eyes were perfectly readable and a clear way of expressing a character's personality.

Bill Murray was considered for the voice role of Sulley. [ref: Bill Murray And the Roles that Got Away, Best Movies by Farr] [ref: 3 Comedians Who Screen Tested For Famous Animated Movies, VICE] While Murray had screen-tested for the role and was interested, Pete Docter, director of Monsters, Inc., among other filmmakers, were unable to make contact with him to formally offer the part. [ref: That Time Bill Murray Was Offered the Role of Sulley in Monsters Inc., TVovermind] [ref: Spotlight on Bill Murray & my Top Five Favorite Roles, FLIXCHATTER FILM BLOG] [ref: Monsters, Inc., Blonde Episodes] [ref: 10 Not-So-Scary Facts About Monsters, Inc., Mental Floss] The role for Sulley was ultimately given to John Goodman, who had previously appeared in a number of Disney-released films, including Hollywood Pictures' Arachnophobia (1990) as Delbert McClintock, and Disney Animation's The Emperor's New Groove (2000) as Pacha. [ref: Eight Legs, Two Fangs and an Attitude: ‘Arachnophobia’ Turns 35, Bloody Disgusting!] [ref: ‘We’ll Never Make That Kind of Movie Again’, Vulture] John Kahrs, animator of Sulley, found that the "bearlike quality" of Goodman's voice provided an exceptionally good fit with the character, while Goodman compared him to an National Football League player, describing him as an "seasoned lineman in the tenth year of his career," and a "total pro."

== Role in the Monsters, Inc. series ==

=== Background ===
In Monsters, Inc., Sulley's best friend, roommate, and assistant, Mike Wazowski, mentioned to Sulley that he [Sulley] had been jealous of his looks since fourth grade, implying that they'd knew each other since childhood. While Monsters University retconned Mike's statement by establishing the two first meeting in the titular university, an deleted scene for the film had shown that the two did met in school. The scene was originally set to be the opening for the film before getting cut. [ref: Monsters University Deleted Scenes, Behind The Voice Actors] Another retconed statement from the first film was from the teaser trailer, in which Sulley reminds Mike of one time at fifth grade when Mike was putting notes while Sulley and the rest of their class was studying geography. [ref: Monsters, Inc. Trailer]

=== Monsters University ===

Sulley was accepted into the titular university's scaring program. In the film, he was initially portrayed as lazy and careless about school studies for the program. Sulley was also initially accepted as member of the Roar Omega Roar (RΩR) fraternity after its leader, Johnny Worthington III, noticed his skills for steeling and chasing a pig mascot named Archie from another school called Fear Tech. He was eventually kicked out from both the scaring program and RΩR for clashing with another program student, Mike, during the final exam and was moved to can designs, along with Mike. The two decides to join another fraternity, the Oozma Kappa (OK), so they can compete in the university's Scare Games as a way to rejoin the scaring program. Throughout all the training the competing for the game events, Mike and Sulley gotten along better as time gone. Ultimately, the Oozma Kappa became the champions of the year's Scare Games after winning the Simulated Scare event against RΩR, giving Sulley, Mike, and the rest of the Oozma Kappa, the opportunity to join the scaring program. However, Mike discovers that his scare simulator level was lowed down to easy. Sulley admitted that he tempered the simulator to ensure that Mike can get a high score.

Mike, being in denial of the fact that he isn't scary, leaves Sulley behind after realising that he doesn't truly believe in him, and decides to break into the university's door lab and head into the human world to scare real human kids to prove that he is scary, only to be proven otherwise. Sulley, after admitting that he cheated to dean of Monsters University and renown scarer, Abigail Hardscrabble, hears that Mike entered the human world, and decides to also head into the world to find and rescue Mike. As they reconcile, Hardscrabble deactivates the door to keep any humans from passing through. As a result, Mike and Sulley decide to collaborate to scare a group of park rangers, creating enough energy to power the door from their side, and pass through just before it explodes. Mike and Sulley are expelled from Monsters University for their actions, while the other Oozma Kappa members are reinstated into the scaring program. As Mike and Sulley leave the university, Hardscrabble, impressed by the two, wishes them well, and orders them to keep surprising people as they did to her. The two begin working for Monsters Incorporated in the mailroom, and over the years work their way up through the company's ranks until Sulley becomes a scarer, with Mike as his scare assistant.

=== Monsters, Inc. ===
Years after the events of Monsters University, Sulley became the top scarer of Monsters, Inc., getting close to achieving the all time scare record. With the exception of rival Randall Boggs, he gets along with a majority of the workers at Monsters, Inc., including the chief executive officer of the company, Henry J. Waternoose III. One evening, while starting to file Mike's papers, Sulley discovered an active door left at Randall's station. While inspecting the door, he accidentally lets a toddler girl (canonically named Mary [ref: Monsters Inc: What Is Boo's Real Name?, ScreenRant]) into the factory. Horrified, Sulley unsuccessfully tries to return the girl to her room, who escapes into Monstropolis, interrupting Mike on a date at a sushi restaurant with Celia Mae. Chaos erupts when other monsters discovered the girl; Sulley and Mike escape with her as the Child Detection Agency (CDA) arrives and quarantines the restaurant. Forced to keep the girl hidden in their apartment for the night, Sulley and Mike realize that she isn't toxic despite the rumors and her laughter can generate more energy than screams.

Sulley grown attached to to the girl and nicknames her "Boo". The next day, Sulley and Mike disguise the girl as a monster out of Sulley's chair from their apartment and attempt to send her home. Randall, waiting in ambush for the girl, accidentally kidnaps Mike and reveals his plan to kidnap children and force screams from them using a machine called a scream extractor and than proceed to test it on Mike. Sulley rescues Mike, and they head to the simulator room to alert Waternoose of Randall's plot. However, Waternoose makes Sulley give a scare demonstration to some recruits, which frightens Boo. Seeing Boo terrified by him, Sulley now realizes how children truly feel when scared. Boo inadvertently reveals herself to Waternoose, who turns out to be in league with Randall. Waternoose abducts Boo and banishes Mike and Sulley to the Himalayas in the human world. Mike and Sulley are found by the Abominable Snowman, who takes them to his lair and reveals a village Sulley realizes he could use to get back to the monster world, but Mike initially refuses to go with him. Sulley returns to the factory and rescues Boo from the scream extractor. Mike returns to reconcile with Sulley, and Randall chases them through the enormous door vault as the trio searches for Boo's door. Randall eventually grabs Boo and almost killed Sulley, but Boo overcomes her fear of him and attacks him. Mike and Sulley banish Randall to the human world and destroy the door used to do so.

Mike and Sulley locate Boo's door, but Waternoose calls it down to the scare floor, intending to have the CDA arrest them. Mike distracts the CDA while Sulley and Boo lure Waternoose into the simulator room. Sulley tricks Waternoose into revealing his conspiracy to kidnap thousands of children to solve the energy crisis. Mike records the conversation, and replays it to the CDA, who arrest him. Scare floor administrator Roz reveals herself as an undercover CDA agent, and allows Sulley to send Boo home, but orders her door destroyed. Since then, Sulley becomes new CEO of Monsters, Inc., and retools the factory to harvest children's laughs rather than screams, due to laughter being ten times more powerful, solving the energy crisis in Monstroplis. [ref: Disney Television Turns Scares into Laughs in ‘Monsters at Work’, Animation World Network] [ref: The Science Behind Monsters, Inc's Scream Extractor Machine, ScreenRant] Mike, now an comedian in the company, then reveals to Sulley that he has rebuilt Boo's door, allowing Sulley to reunite with Boo.

=== Monsters at Work ===

Season 1 takes place before the epilogue of the first movie, showcasing Sulley's beginnings as new CEO of Monsters, Inc.

== Reception ==
[[File:John Goodman 2000.jpg|thumb|John Goodman, voice of Sulley, received critical acclaim.|268x268px]]
Along with Mike, Sulley is regraded as one of the best fictional characters from Pixar Animation Studios. Rolling Stone ranked Sulley as the 16th best Pixar character, calling him a "top-notch monster, and a true American hero." [ref: 25 Best Pixar Movie Characters, Rolling Stone] Chloe Gronow on Screen Rant consider Sulley to be one of the best Pixar characters, stating that "Sully proves to be the type of fatherly figure anyone would want in their life and it’s this fact that has left him in such high regard with many fans. While he may seem like a terrifying monster at first glance, he’s really just as soft as his fur suggests." [ref: 10 Best Pixar Characters Of All-Time, According To Ranker, ScreenRant] Kyle Phillippi of Yardbarker listed Sulley as the 13th best Pixar characters, claiming that he's "as good-hearted as any Pixar character." [ref: Ranking the 25 all-time greatest Disney Pixar characters, Yardbarker] William Thomas of Empire describe both Sulley and Mike as "bickering buddies in the Eric and Ernie mould", declaring the two characters "Funny, loveable and, above all, inseparable." [ref: Monsters, Inc., Empire]

Goodman's performance as Sulley, is often considered one of his best role. Amanda Bruce of Screen Rant ranked Monsters, Inc. as the 4th best film/TV series starring Goodman, stating "The warmth of Goodman’s Sulley was a big part in making the characters likeable and giving them such great staying power among other legendary Disney figures." [ref: John Goodman's 10 Best Movies And TV Shows, ScreenRant] Luc Haasbroek of Collider considered the same film to be an essential Goodman film, claiming that he "gave Pixar one of its most enduring characters." and "doesn't just make Sulley lovable, he makes him human", while also prising his chemistry with Mike's actor, Billy Crystal. [ref: 10 Essential John Goodman Movies, Ranked, Collider] Robert Keeling of Den of Geek ranked Sulley as Goodman's fourth best role, stating "He imbues Sully with a caring and affectionate demeanour, despite being rightfully considered the company’s scariest Monster. There’s something about Goodman’s deep yet relaxing vocals that lends itself perfectly to this gentle giant." [ref: The Top 25 John Goodman Roles, Den of Geek]

== In other media ==
Sulley, along with Mike, appeared in the short film, Mike's New Car, released as a bonus feature on the original DVD and VHS release of Monsters, Inc. in September 17, 2002, with Goodman returning as Sulley. [ref: Monsters, Inc. Blu-ray (Blu-ray + DVD)]

Sulley and Mike, returned as car variants in 2006's Cars, during an credits sequence featuring automobile spoofs of Monsters, Inc, and the two other Pixar films; Toy Story (1995) and A Bug's Life (1998), with Goodman reprising his role as Sulley. [ref: Celebrities That Did Voice Acting in Cars, Voices]

=== Video games ===
As one of the two main characters of the Monsters, Inc. franchise, Sulley has made regular appearances in the video games of the franchise, usually as the main playable character. [ref: Disney•Pixar Monsters, Inc. (2002), MobyGames] [ref: Monsters, Inc. Scream Team, IGN]

He also made appearances in other Disney crossover video games, such as the Disney Infinity series (2013-2015; voiced by Joel McCrary), where as with the other playable characters in the game a tie-in figure for him was also released, [ref: Exclusive Disney Infinity Wave 1 Hands-On, WIRED] Kingdom Hearts III (2019; voiced by Christopher Swindle), [ref: Monsters Inc Confirmed in New Kingdom Hearts 3 Trailer, WellPlayed] appearing as one of Sora's party members, and Disney Mirrorverse (2022). [ref: Disney-mirrorverse-mcfarlane-toys-monsters-inc-sulley-action-figure, MiceChat] [ref: Kabam Creates a New RPG World of Beloved Characters in 'Disney Mirrorverse', Animation Magazine] [ref: Disney favorites become Guardians in the Disney Mirrorverse!, Gaming Age]

== References ==

== Bibliography ==

* The Pixar Touch, Alfred A. Knopf

data.title: Legends League Cricket
data.text:
Legends League Cricket (LLC) is a Twenty20 cricket competition featuring former international cricketers. The competition began in January 2022 with an international-format tournament and later expanded to include a franchise-based competition in India.

The league was co-founded by Raman Raheja and Vivek Khushalani and is organised by Absolute Legends Sports Private Limited. [ref: Uncertain times: Legends League Cricket caught in 'ownership' row, The New Indian Express]

== History ==

=== Establishment and Ravi Shastri's appointment ===

In November 2021, former India cricketer and national team head coach Ravi Shastri was appointed commissioner of Legends League Cricket ahead of its inaugural tournament. The competition was planned as an international event involving former players from India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Australia, England and other cricket-playing nations. [ref: Ravi Shastri joins upcoming Legends League as Commissioner, The Indian Express]

The first edition was staged in Muscat, Oman, in January 2022. It featured India Maharajas, Asia Lions and World Giants, with World Giants winning the tournament. [ref: Legends League Cricket 2022: Full list of players signed up for season two of LLC T20, Wisden]

The international-format competition subsequently operated under the name LLC Masters, while a separate franchise-based tournament was established in India.

=== Franchise competition ===

The franchise tournament began in September 2022 with four teams: India Capitals, Manipal Tigers, Bhilwara Kings and Gujarat Giants. The inaugural season featured former India cricketers Virender Sehwag, Gautam Gambhir, Harbhajan Singh and Irfan Pathan as team captains. [ref: Virender Sehwag, Irfan Pathan, Gautam Gambhir and Harbhajan Singh appointed captains in Legends League Cricket, Hindustan Times]

India Capitals won the first franchise championship, defeating Bhilwara Kings by 104 runs in the final in Jaipur. [ref: Legends League Cricket: India Capitals Champions After Ross Taylor, Mitchell Johnson Fireworks, NDTV Sports]

The competition expanded to six teams in 2023. Manipal Tigers won the championship, defeating Urbanrisers Hyderabad in the final. [ref: Harbhajan Singh's Manipal Tigers clinch LLC T20 2023 title after beating Suresh Raina's side, The Times of India]

The 2024 season was won by Southern Super Stars, who defeated Konark Suryas Odisha in a Super Over at Bakshi Stadium, Srinagar. [ref: Southern Super Stars vs Konark Suryas Odisha, Final, Legends League Cricket 2024, Cricbuzz]

The fourth franchise season took place in March 2026. Royal Riders Punjab defeated Konark Suryas Odisha by 41 runs in the final at Haldwani. [ref: Legends League Cricket 2026, Cricbuzz]

== Notable participants ==

The league has featured former international cricketers from India, Australia, England, Sri Lanka, South Africa, New Zealand, Pakistan, the West Indies and other cricket-playing nations.

Among the former Indian players associated with the competition are Virender Sehwag, Gautam Gambhir, Harbhajan Singh, Suresh Raina, Irfan Pathan, Yusuf Pathan, Mohammad Kaif and Robin Uthappa.

International participants have included Chris Gayle, Jacques Kallis, Brett Lee, Shane Watson, Muttiah Muralitharan, Dale Steyn, Eoin Morgan, Mitchell Johnson, Ross Taylor and Darren Sammy. [ref: Legends League Cricket press releases, Legends League Cricket]

== Matches in Jammu and Kashmir ==

In November 2023, Legends League Cricket staged matches at Maulana Azad Stadium in Jammu. The event brought former international players to a venue that had not hosted international cricket for approximately 35 years. [ref: After 35 years, Jammu witnesses return of international cricket, The Indian Express]

In October 2024, the league held matches at Bakshi Stadium in Srinagar. The tournament received international media coverage for bringing former international players to Kashmir after nearly four decades. Al Jazeera reported both enthusiasm among spectators and concerns expressed by some local observers about the long-term development of cricket in the region. [ref: Legends League allows long-deprived fans to enjoy cricket again in Kashmir, Al Jazeera]

== Commercial and legal developments ==

In 2022, the league became involved in an ownership dispute concerning an earlier memorandum of understanding. The New Indian Express reported that the matter reached the Delhi High Court following a petition seeking arbitration. The league's representatives disputed the validity of the agreement.
