data.title: DJ Narain
data.text:
----

Dharmendra Jai Narain, also known as DJ Narain, is an Indian musician, singer, composer and also a former civil servant. Started as the lead singer and composer of the Indian pop-rock band Aryans. The group became popular in the late 90 and 2000s with popular songs including Aankhon Mein Tera Hi Chehra, Yeh Hawa Kehti Hai Kya and Dekha Hai Teri Aankhon Ko. [ref: Aryans: Bald and the dutiful!, The Times of India] [ref: Tera Naam: Aryans' DJ Narain makes a grand comeback with soulful number, Hindustan Times]

Besides being a musician, he has been a civil servant with Government of India. Alongside his music career, Narain had a career in the Indian Information Service for long and served as director of the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII) from 2011 to 2015. [ref: D J Narain takes charge as director of FTII, The Times of India] [ref: Ex-NFAI director Prashant Pathrabe appointed as director of FTII Pune, The Indian Express] His last few months as director of FTII were eventful and in news for the students strike over appointments to the institute's governing bodies. [ref: FTII director draws hard line to students: End strike or face rustication, The Indian Express]

After taking voluntary retirement from government service, Narain returned to releasing music as a solo artist and musician in 2022. [ref: DJ Narain is back, to shoot a song in hometown Lucknow, Hindustan Times]

==Early life and music==

Narain studied at the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur. [ref: Aryans: Striking the right notes, The Times of India]

He was involved with music before the formation of Aryans and was associated with the Lucknow student music scene and was a member of the band Dreams in 1988 who later became DJ Narain of Aryans. [ref: Bands which had a bond with LU, The Times of India]

Narain subsequently became associated with Aryans while also pursuing a professional career as a Civil servant outside music. In 2003 while being part of the band Aryans, he was also working with the Directorate of Film Festivals in New Delhi.

==Music career==

===Aryans===

Aryans emerged as part of India's independent-pop scene around the turn of the century. Narain was one of the principal members of the group and was widely known for being its lead singer.

The group produced songs including Aankhon Mein Tera Hi Chehra, Yeh Hawa Kehti Hai Kya and Dekha Hai Teri Aankhon Ko. The music video for Aankhon Mein Tera Hi Chehra featured Shahid Kapoor before his emergence as a Hindi film actor.

Narain continued to pursue music while working in government as a civil servant. Early 2000s, various media reports profiled Aryans lead singer Narain's connection with the music and his simultaneous professional career. There were Reports about the band's music and international performances. Aryans had also contributed the song Kyun to the Hindi film Woodstock Villa in 2008.

The band later went off the radar as the members pursued individual career and DJ Narain focusses on his professional career as a Civil Servant with goverment.

===Solo return===

He spent more than a decade being away from music, and after his voluntary retirement from government service, Narain returned as a solo artist in 2022.

His single Tera Naam was released by Times Music. Narain wrote, composed and sang the song.

==Civil service career==

Before joining the civil services, Narain worked in advertising inductry. He subsequently joined the Indian Information Service as part of its 1990 batch.

His association with FTII began in 1993, when he undertook a film and television production course at the institute as part of his Indian Information Service training.

During his government career, Narain served as the spokesperson for the Southern Command, Ministry of Defence in 1997–98 and later taught mass communication at the Indian Institute of Mass Communication.

===Film and Television Institute of India===

Narain took charge as director of the Film and Television Institute of India in July 2011, succeeding Pankaj Rag.

After an inatial three-year term, he subsequently received a one-year extension. [ref: FTII director to be picked in July 13 meet, The Indian Express]

====2015 FTII strike====

The final months of Narain's tenure coincided with a major dispute at FTII following the appointment of actor Gajendra Chauhan as chairman of the institute's governing council and the appointment of other members of the FTII Society. Students began an indefinite strike in June 2015 opposing the appointments.

Narain, as director, became actively involved in a bid to manage the dispute. As the strike continued into its second month, he issued a formal notice directing students to resume academic activities and warning that continued defiance could result in disciplinary action, including rustication. But the students rejected the warning and continued their protest, publicly criticising the administration's response. [ref: Now, FTII director comes under criticism for rustication threat, The Indian Express]

The relationship between Narain and the protesting students was quite complex considering the continued agitation but before his tenure ended, students had expressed support for extending his term, saying that his four years at the institute gave him an understanding of their concerns and that he had acted as a channel of communication between them and the Information and Broadcasting Ministry. [ref: FTII students hope D J Narain gets another extension, The Indian Express]

While the strike continued, Narain's tenure ended in July 2015. The Economic Times reported about the controversies around the dispute. [ref: Government decides to change FTII director, Prashant Pathrabe to replace DJ Narain, The Economic Times] Dj Narain was preceded by Prashant Pathrabe, then director of the Press Information Bureau in Pune and a former director of the National Film Archive of India, was given additional charge as FTII director.

data.title: Rohan Rajbhar
data.text:
Rohan Rajbhar (born 6 February 2006) is an Indian cricketer, who plays as a opening batter. He plays for Rajasthan in domestic cricket.

= Mudu Vishwamitra Chouhan =
Mudu Vishwamitra Chouhan is an Indian child environmental activist from Telangana, India, known for his efforts to promote tree planting and environmental conservation. He has been involved in planting saplings and collecting seeds of native tree species as part of efforts to increase green cover.

== Early life ==
Chouhan is from Chunchupalli, in Bhadradri Kothagudem district, Telangana. He is the son of Jayaram and Anusha. His interest in environmental conservation was inspired in part by the work of Daripalli Ramaiah, a Padma Shri award recipient known for his tree-planting activities.

== Environmental activities ==
Chouhan has participated in planting saplings and collecting seeds from forest areas. His activities focus on native tree species and supporting afforestation initiatives.

On 2 June 2022, he began an initiative called Walk for Trees, through which he pledged to plant at least one sapling every day. His work has included planting saplings in public spaces and supplying seeds to support tree-planting programmes.

== Recognition ==
Daripalli Ramaiah reportedly encouraged Chouhan's environmental work and expressed the view that he could carry forward the legacy associated with the title Vanajeevi.

data.title: Somasekhar Sundaresan
data.text:
Somasekhar Sundaresan (born 23 December 1972) is an Indian jurist serving as a Permanent Judge of the Bombay High Court. After his appointment as an Additional Judge to that high court in November 2023, Sundaresan was confirmed as a Permanent Judge in September 2025. [ref: Hon'ble Sitting Judges: Somasekhar Sundaresan, J., High Court of Bombay] [ref: Advocate Somasekhar Sundaresan sworn in as additional judge of Bombay HC, The Indian Express] [ref: President appoints 6 Permanent Judges for Bombay High Court, SCC Online] He has also practiced as a regulatory and commercial lawyer giving advice on takeovers, securities laws and corporate insolvency rules in Mumbai. [ref: Somasekshar Sundaresan of JSA leaves the firm to begin counsel practice, The Economic Times]

== Early life and education ==
Sundaresan graduated with a Bachelor of Commerce from RA Podar College of Commerce & Economics in 1993. He then earned his law degree from Government Law College, Mumbai in 1996. While pursuing his law degree, Sundaresan worked in finance journalism as a business editor for The Times of India from 1994 to 1998. [ref: Somasekhar Sundaresan, Partner, J. Sagar Associates, on work of a transactional lawyer, responsibilites of a Partner, and his transition from Journalism to Law, SuperLawyer]

== Career ==

=== Legal ===
In 1999, Sundaresan joined Udwadia, Udeshi & Berjis (now Argus Partners) as a partner, advising on company law and foreign exchange regulations. From 2002 until August 2016, he served as a partner at J. Sagar Associates. Sundaresan's practice there had a focus on transactional governance and regulatory litigation before the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the Competition Commission of India and the Securities Appellate Tribunal.

=== Public policy and regulatory committees ===
Sundaresan has served on multiple Indian government advisory committees. He was a part of the SEBI Takeover Regulations Advisory Committee in 2010 to draft the revised substantial acquisition code. [ref: SEBI appoints committee to revamp Takeover Code; Achutan, Somasekhar Sundaresan and Kumar Desai represent the legal community, Bar and Bench] [ref: Report of the Takeover Regulations Advisory Committee, Securities and Exchange Board of India] Sundaresan provided advice to the Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission under Justice B.N. Srikrishna between 2011 and 2013, which prepared the draft Indian Financial Code. [ref: Who tried to clip the RBI governor's wings?, Mint] He was also a member of SEBI's High-Level Committee on Insider Trading Regulations in 2013, chaired by Justice N.K. Sodhi. [ref: Report of the High Level Committee to Review the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 1992, Securities and Exchange Board of India] Sundaresan was appointed by the Supreme Court of India to a six-member expert panel, reviewing securities market regulatory mechanisms after allegations against the Adani Group in 2023. [ref: Supreme Court forms expert panel to probe any regulatory failure on Adani issue, The Hindu]

=== Judicial ===
Sundaresan was recommended for elevation to the bench by the Bombay High Court Collegium in October 2021. The file was returned for reconsideration by the Union Government due to views expressed by Sundaresan on social media regarding pending court matters. In January 2023, the Supreme Court Collegium, headed by Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud, strongly reiterated his name, stating that airing critical views on government policy does not compromise judicial independence or imply bias. [ref: Advocate Somasekhar Sundaresan appointed as an Additional Judge of the Bombay High Court, The Hindu] Sundaresan was then sworn in as an Additional Judge on 28 November 2023, before becoming a Permanent Judge on 18 September 2025.

data.title: Pioneertown International Film Festival
data.text:
----

The Pioneertown International Film Festival, also known as the Pioneertown Film Festival, was a one-off film festival devoted to the Western genre, held in Pioneertown, California, a former film-set town in the high desert of San Bernardino County near Joshua Tree National Park. The festival was co-founded by filmmaker Julian T. Pinder and artist Keely King, who also served as its creative director.

Its first edition took place over Memorial Day weekend, May 27–29, 2022, after a planned August 2021 debut was postponed because of the COVID-19 pandemic. The inaugural program, curated by head programmer Todd Luoto, a former Sundance programmer, combined premieres of new Westerns with restored classics from the Paramount Pictures archive, anniversary screenings, short-film programs, panels and live music. It opened with the world premiere of the Jason Momoa–produced The Last Manhunt.

The festival was presented by Fistful of Bourbon and organized in partnership with the Autry Museum of the American West in Los Angeles, the archive and restoration division of Paramount Pictures, and the Palm Springs Art Museum.

== History ==

=== Background ===
Pioneertown was established in 1946 by a group that included actor Dick Curtis and Roy Rogers, as a working town that doubled as a Western film set. Productions shot there included The Cisco Kid, The Gene Autry Show and Annie Oakley.

Pinder, a documentary and film director who grew up in rural Canada, had lived on a ranch outside Pioneertown for about a decade. His credits include the Netflix series Fire Chasers, executive produced by Leonardo DiCaprio, and the films Jesus Town, USA, Trouble In The Peace, and Population Zero, among others. He said he conceived the festival to mark the town's role in the history of Western film, and to celebrate it through film and music.

=== Development ===
Todd Luoto, a former programmer for the Sundance, CineVegas, Newport Beach and Silver Lake film festivals, came on during the development of the film festival as head of programming. The organizers were initially unsure whether enough new Westerns were being made to sustain a genre-specific festival. Luoto and Pinder spent nearly two years canvassing other festivals and distributors for titles, and the team adopted a broad definition of the genre that included films following Western story archetypes. Artist Keely King, the festival's creative director, developed the unique branding, artwork, and posters, including a limited screen-print run.

Organizers launched the festival in late February 2020, shortly before the COVID-19 pandemic. The first edition was scheduled for August 27–29, 2021, but was postponed after a rise in COVID-19 cases and moved to May 27–29, 2022. During the delay, members of the community non-profit group Friends of Pioneertown helped maintain a drive-in theater that had been built as one of the festival's venues.

== Venues and format ==
Pioneertown has no movie theater, so organizers converted the town's historic soundstage, where interiors for Roy Rogers and Gene Autry productions were filmed, and a nearby ranch barn into temporary cinemas with 4K digital projection and Dolby sound. Other historic sites, including Desert Willow Ranch, the Pioneertown Motel, the Red Dog Saloon and Super X Ranch, served as screening venues, lounges and bars.

The 2022 edition had capacity for about 1200 attendees. It ran 20 to 25 screenings in two screening rooms over three days, including two blocks of short films. Pinder said the festival intended to stay small and improve the quality of its program rather than grow its audience.

== 2022 festival ==
The festival opened on May 27, 2022, with a performance by The Dandy Warhols and the world premiere of The Last Manhunt. The feature film, directed by Christian Camargo and produced by Jason Momoa, dramatizes the 1909 pursuit of Willie Boy, a Chemehuevi man, based on the Chemehuevi oral account of the events. The Autry Museum presented the screening. Two days earlier, on May 25, the Palm Springs Art Museum hosted a screening of the film in association with the festival, attended by members of the Twenty-Nine Palms Band of Mission Indians and descendants of the Mike family. The band The Dandy Warhols played the Opening Night show.

New films in the program came from the United States, Ukraine, Australia, Italy and Spain. They included Roman Perfilyev's Ukrainian action Western The Inglorious Serfs, whose director attended after relocating to the United States because of the war in Ukraine, and Tim Kirk's documentary The Mystery of Durango!.

Retrospective programming included:

* a series of recently restored Westerns presented by Paramount Pictures' archive and restoration department, which also gave a masterclass on film restoration;
* an anniversary screening of An American Tail: Fievel Goes West, attended by director Phil Nibbelink;
* an anniversary screening of From Dusk till Dawn, presented by co-producer Robert Kurtzman;
* a tribute to Monte Hellman, with The Shooting and Ride in the Whirlwind presented by Melissa Hellman and Jennifer Nicholson, daughters of Hellman and Jack Nicholson;
* Heartworn Highways and Heartworn Highways Revisited, presented by producer Graham Leader.

A program titled Stupid F*cking White Man: The Indigenous Image in Westerns, curated by Adam Piron (Kiowa/Mohawk) of the Sundance Institute's Indigenous Program, centered on Jim Jarmusch's Dead Man. Pinder and Luoto said the festival set out to confront the genre's history of racist portrayals of Indigenous and other non-white characters. Director Joe Dante and screenwriter Josh Olson recorded their podcast The Movies That Made Me live during the festival.

The closing night on May 29 featured Alexandre O. Philippe's documentary The Taking, about Monument Valley and its use in Western films, and a performance by the Sons of the Pioneers, which included Dusty Rogers, whose father Roy Rogers co-founded the town with Gene Autry.

== Organization and partners ==
Pinder co-founded the festival with artist Keely King, who served as its creative director. King also created the festival's artwork and unique graphic identity. Local filmmaker Mike Bruce was also initially in a founding role until stepping back when the festival was postponed due to COVID. Todd Luoto led programming, Bonnie Brooks handled physical and production design, and Stephanie Blank served as festival coordinator.

Partners and sponsors:

* Fistful of Bourbon, presenting sponsor.
* Autry Museum of the American West, which co-presented the festival, presented The Last Manhunt and talks at the festival, held a members' screening of the film in Los Angeles, and gave festival attendees free museum admission through the end of 2022.
* Paramount Pictures archive and restoration division, which supplied restored Westerns and sent staff to present them.
* Palm Springs Art Museum, which hosted an associated screening of The Last Manhunt for local tribal community members on May 25, 2022.

== Recognition ==
San Bernardino County awarded the festival a Certificate of Recognition for community enrichment, presented at the festival's closing ceremony on May 29, 2022.

== Future plans ==
After the hugely successful 2022 edition, there has been some talk of re-igniting it as an annual event, although nothing confirmed.

data.title: Roofing calculator
data.text:
----

== Roofing calculator ==
A [https://roofertx.net/tools/ roofing calculator] is a tool that estimates roof surface area, roofing material quantities, or project costs. Depending on its purpose, it may use user-supplied measurements or property information processed by an estimating system. Area calculators can account for roof slope and overhangs, while cost estimators may incorporate location, roof size, and complexity.
[ref: https://www.gaf.com/en-us/plan-design/homeowner-education/roof-cost/calculator]
== Area estimation ==
Roof surface area is different from the horizontal area covered by a building. On a sloping roof, the surface follows the incline instead of the horizontal projection.

Some roofing calculators evaluate this surface using a building’s base area, roof pitch, and eave dimensions. A slope correction factor converts horizontal measurements into an approximate slope area. [ref: https://roofertx.net/tools/roof-area-calculator/]

The individual sections may be measured separately and their areas added together for roofs with several sections or different slopes. A single base-area measurement cannot fully define a complex roof.

== Material estimation ==
Material calculators use a measured roof area to quantify roofing products. Their outputs are dependent on the material assumptions built into the tool.

In roofing estimates, area might be expressed in square feet or roofing squares. A roofing square represents roof surface of 100 square feet. This unit is also used when defining material and installation costs.

== Cost estimation ==
Roofing cost calculators produce estimates using selected project characteristics. For example, GAF uses its residential replacement-cost calculator to illustrate information including property address, roof size, slope, and complexity to generate a non-binding estimate. [ref: https://www.gaf.com/en-us/plan-design/homeowner-education/roof-cost]

Roof replacement costs also depend on the selected materials and the consequences of the project. Roof slope may affect installation labor, while location influences local costs and applicable requirements.

A calculator’s estimated price and a contractor’s final price may differ.When removing a roof, it's important to be aware that existing roof layers or damaged decking may necessitate additional work. This need often becomes evident during the removal process.

=== Limitations ===
The usefulness of a roofing calculation depends on the measurements and assumptions built into the project. A calculator based on a simplified roof shape may not account adequately for a roof with multiple intersecting sections.

Cost estimates also have a defined scope. GAF characterizes its calculator results as informational and non-binding; they do not constitute a project-specified contract price. [ref: https://www.gaf.com/en-us/plan-design/homeowner-education/roof-cost]

data.title: European Association of CCP Clearing Houses (EACH)
data.text:
----

== Overview ==
The [https://eachccp.eu/ European Association of CCP Clearing Houses (EACH)] is a Belgian not-for-profit organisation that represents the interests of Central Counterparty Clearing Houses (CCPs) across Europe. Established in 1992, the association contributes to the safety, transparency, and efficiency of financial markets by coordinating policy engagement, developing standards, and supporting the role of CCPs in reducing systemic risk.

EACH acts as the collective voice of European CCPs, representing 19 members from 15 European countries as of 2026 [ref: About us, EACH - European Association of CCP Clearing Houses]. The organisation is registered in the EU Transparency Register under the number 36897011311-96.

CCPs play a crucial role in modern financial systems by interposing themselves between buyers and sellers in financial transactions and managing counterparty credit risk [ref: Central Clearing of OTC Derivatives: bilateral vs multilateral netting, Statistics & Risk Modeling]. EACH supports these institutions by facilitating dialogue with regulators, providing industry expertise, encouraging harmonisation of best practices and representing them in discussions concerning financial market infrastructure, clearing, risk management and financial regulation with several entities in the EU bubble [ref: The European central counterparty (CCP) ecosystem] [ref: Standards of Risk Management Controls used by Central Counterparty Clearing Houses].

== History ==
EACH was established in 1992 to facilitate and strengthen cooperation among European CCPs and contribute to a more resilient financial system. In 2001, the association published a set of risk management standards for CCPs. According to EACH, these standards contributed to later international work on CCP regulation, including discussions leading to the development of international standards for financial market infrastructures by the Committee on Payment and Settlement Systems (CPSS, now CPMI) and the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO).

Following the 2007–2008 global financial crisis and the adoption of the European Market Infrastructure Regulation (EMIR), EACH became a regular participant in consultations conducted by the European Commission, the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the European Banking Authority (EBA), the European Central Bank (ECB) and international standard-setting bodies like CPMI, IOSCO and Financial Stability Board (FSB) on the regulation and supervision of central counterparties [ref: Setting EU CCP policy – much more than meets the eye] [ref: CCP Policy, www.esma.europa.eu], which has lead to the association subsequently contributing to consultations relating to EMIR reviews, CCP recovery and resolution, operational resilience, cyber security, digital assets and the transition to T+1 securities settlement [ref: ESMA CONSULTS ON EMIR REPORTING GUIDELINES, www.esma.europa.eu] [ref: ].

== Activities ==
* Preparing industry responses to consultations issued by European and international authorities.
* Facilitating cooperation among member CCPs on technical and regulatory issues.
* Organising working groups on legal, operational, technological and risk-management matters.
* Publishing reports, position papers and technical guidance relating to clearing and market infrastructure.

EACH's consultation responses are part of the broader stakeholder input considered by [https://www.esrb.europa.eu/about/orga/list/html/index.en.html European macroprudential authorities] when reviewing financial market infrastructure regulation [ref: A system-wide approach to macroprudential policy].

== Governance ==
As stated on their website, EACH is governed by its General Assembly, Board and a number of specialised committees and working groups [ref: Governance, EACH - European Association of CCP Clearing Houses].

=== General Assembly ===
The General Assembly is the association's highest decision-making body. It approves amendments to the Articles of Association, elects the Board, approves the annual accounts and decides on the admission of new members.

=== Board ===
The Board is responsible for overseeing the implementation of the association's strategic objectives and supervising its activities between meetings of the General Assembly [ref: Board, EACH - European Association of CCP Clearing Houses].

=== Committees and Working Groups ===
EACH maintains permanent committees and working groups [ref: Committees, EACH - European Association of CCP Clearing Houses] covering regulatory, legal, operational and technical matters. These include:

* Policy Committee
* Risk Committee
* Legal Committee
* Energy Clearing Working Group
* EMIR Trade Reporting Working Group
* EMIR Risk-Free Rates Working Group
* Securities Operations Working Group
* DORA Task Force
* Cyber Security Task Force

These bodies internally coordinate technical analysis and prepare common industry positions on regulatory developments affecting CCPs.

== Membership ==
As of 2026, EACH's members comprise:

* BME Clearing
* Cboe Clear Europe
* [https://www.ccpa.at/en/ CCP Austria]
* [https://www.ccpro.ro/ CCP.RO]
* [https://www.eccbelgium.be/ ECC]
* [https://www.enexgroup.gr/web/guest/home EnExClear]
* Eurex Clearing
* Euronext Clearing
* ICE Clear Europe
* [https://irgit.pl/en IRGiT]
* [https://www.kdpwccp.pl/en/index.html KDPW_CCP]
* KELER CCP
* LCH Ltd
* LCH S.A.
* LME Clear
* [https://www.nasdaq.com/solutions/nasdaq-clearing-offering Nasdaq Clearing]
* [https://www.omiclear.pt/en OMIClear]
* [https://www.six-group.com/en/products-services/securities-services/clearing/info-center.html SIX x‑clear]
* [https://www.takasbank.com.tr/en Takasbank]

Membership information is published on the association's official website [ref: Members, EACH - European Association of CCP Clearing Houses].

== Publications and Key Issues ==
EACH publishes in their website and social media position papers [ref: Position papers, EACH - European Association of CCP Clearing Houses], consultation responses [ref: Responses, EACH - European Association of CCP Clearing Houses], technical reports and press releases [ref: Press releases, EACH - European Association of CCP Clearing Houses] concerning financial market infrastructure and clearing.

Its publications have addressed subjects including:

* EMIR implementation and review
* Anti-procyclicality of margin requirements
* Interoperability between CCPs
* Operational resilience
* Cyber security
* Digital assets and tokenisation
* Capital markets integration
* AI and Clearing
* Sustainability considerations affecting CCPs

They also include initiatives such as the [https://www.linkedin.com/groups/12789353/ "Women in Clearing"] series, highlighting industry professionals.

== Reception and influence ==
Coverage of the association's activities has appeared in specialist financial publications including Securities Finance Times, particularly regarding EMIR reform, capital markets policy and consultation responses [ref: ].

The association has participated in numerous consultations conducted by European and international authorities, including the European Commission, ESMA, the ECB, the Bank of England and the FSB [ref: Central clearing: three lessons and a path forward − speech by Christina Segal-Knowles, www.bankofengland.co.uk] [ref: Publications, Financial Stability Board].

data.text:
= Chef Nepal (TV series) =
Chef Nepal is a Nepalese cooking competition reality television series produced by Dharma Pictures and created by Dharma Raj Pandey. The programme premiered on Kantipur Television on 8 September 2023. It featured amateur cooks and culinary enthusiasts competing in cooking challenges evaluated by a panel of professional chefs, including Masterchef Santosh Shah, Bhanse Laxman Prasad Bhandari and Chef Ganesh Bahadur Dhakal. [ref: ‘Chef Nepal’ to air on Kantipur Television, kathmandupost.com] [ref: ‘Chef Nepal’ to air from today on Kantipur Television, kathmandupost.com] [ref: Chef Nepal: So Happy to Finally See a Cooking Reality Television Show, NeoStuffs]

The series was developed as an original Nepalese cooking competition, with a format incorporating competitive cooking, elimination rounds and judging by culinary professionals.

== Background and development ==
Plans for Chef Nepal were publicly reported in October 2022, when Onlinekhabar announced that Nepali chef Santosh Shah had joined the programme as its master judge. Shah, who had appeared on the BBC cooking competition MasterChef: The Professionals, joined fellow judges Bhanse Laxman Bhandari and Chef Ganesh Dhakal. Early reports identified Himalayan Television as the intended broadcaster. [ref: टीभी रियालिटी शो ‘सेफ नेपाल’को मास्टर जजमा सन्तोष साह अनुबन्धित, Online Khabar]

The programme was conceptualised and produced by Dharma Raj Pandey under the banner of Dharma Pictures. A purpose-built cooking competition set was established at Royal Thai Hospitality in Thimi, Bhaktapur. The set was unveiled in early January 2023 in an event attended by Shah. [ref: पाककलाको रियालिटी शो ‘सेफ नेपाल’को छायांकन सेट सार्वजनिक (तस्वीर), Online Khabar]

In July 2023, Kantipur Television and Dharma Pictures signed an agreement to broadcast the programme. The agreement was announced at Kantipur Television's office in Tinkune, Kathmandu, with producer Dharma Raj Pandey and members of the judging panel involved in the event.

== Production ==
Chef Nepal was produced by Dharma Pictures, with Dharma Raj Pandey serving as founder, producer and creative director of Chef Nepal. Siddhartha Pudasaini directed the first 6 episodes. Kedar Bhusal of Flicker Arts directed another 10 episodes and last 4 episodes are produced and directed by Kantipur Television team.

The competition was filmed at a cooking studio which was created at Royal Thai Hospitality in Bhaktapur. Participants prepared dishes for evaluation by the judges during different rounds of the competition.

The production experienced delays before its television premiere. Writing for NeoStuffs following the broadcast of the first episode, Neeraj Pun reported that financial limitations had contributed to the delayed launch.

== Format and contestants ==
The series was designed as a cooking competition for amateur cooks, home cooks and other eligible culinary enthusiasts. Professional chefs were excluded from the initial competition, according to reporting published ahead of the premiere.

More than 500 people applied during the initial audition process. The judges shortlisted approximately 100 applicants for the competition.

Contestants prepared dishes that were assessed by the judging panel, with elimination rounds determining progression through the competition.

The final stage of the first season involved eight remaining contestants, as reported in July 2024. [ref: नेपालको पहिलो फुड रियालिटी शो 'सेफ नेपाल' ग्रान्ड फिनाले तयारीमा, नेपालको पहिलो फुड रियालिटी शो 'सेफ नेपाल' ग्रान्ड फिनाले तयारीमा]

== Judges and presentation ==
The principal judging panel consisted of:

* Masterchef Santosh Shah — Nepali chef and former contestant on BBC's MasterChef: The Professionals, serving as master judge.
* Bhanse Laxman Prasad Bhandari — Nepali culinary practitioner, known as Bhanse Laxman.
* Chef Ganesh Bahadur Dhakal — Chef and hospitality entrepreneur associated with Royal Thai Hospitality and Baan Thai Restaurants.

Actress Priyanka Karki was involved during the programme's development and early presentation.

Media presenter Rakchya Upreti was announced as host for the programme's concluding episodes in July 2024.

== Broadcast ==
Chef Nepal premiered on Kantipur Television on 8 September 2023, with an initial Friday evening broadcast schedule.

Ahead of the premiere, producers announced plans for an 18-episode run. The programme's broadcast extended into 2024, with the concluding episodes reported to be scheduled for July 2024 following interruptions.

The series was also made available through Chef Nepal's online video platforms. [ref: ]

== Season 1 results ==
The first season concluded in 2024, with Ajuehang Rai of Udayapur winning the competition. Bikesh Manandhar finished as first runner-up, while Ingwa Subba was second runner-up. [ref: Australian ambassador congratulates winners of Chef Nepal, www.myrepublica.nagariknetwork.com]

In August 2024, Australian Ambassador to Nepal Felicity Volk congratulated the competition's participants and production team. Volk had previously appeared as a guest on the programme's fourteenth episode.

== Reception and media coverage ==
Following the television premiere, entertainment website NeoStuffs published a review of the first episode. Writer Neeraj Pun welcomed the introduction of an original Nepalese cooking competition and commented on its production quality. While praising aspects of the presentation, he suggested that more detailed close-up shots of the contestants' dishes would have improved the programme.

The series also received coverage from Nepalese news organisations including The Kathmandu Post, Onlinekhabar, Capital Nepal and Republica, which reported on its development, judges, broadcast and competition results.

== Related activities ==
Following the first season, Dharma Pictures continued developing culinary media projects under the Chef Nepal name. The organisation's official website describes activities involving culinary media production, professional recognition and a community of Nepali culinary professionals.

These activities are distinct from the original television competition.

data.title: Sai Shipping Company Private Limited
data.text:
Sai Shipping Company Private Limited is a privately owned Indian ship agency and shipbroking company based in Mumbai. Established in 1977, it is the parent company of the SAI Group, whose project-cargo subsidiary Sai Maritime & Management Private Limited has acted as the Indian agent of the German heavy-lift carrier SAL Heavy Lift since the 1980s.

== History ==
The company was incorporated in Mumbai in 1977 and has remained privately owned since its establishment. Its core business has been port agency for ocean-going vessels calling at Indian ports.

In 1984 the company formed a subsidiary, Sai Maritime & Management Private Limited, to handle project and heavy-lift cargo; that subsidiary became the handling and booking agent in India for SAL Heavy Lift from 1986. In 2016, marking thirty years of the relationship, the company's chairman, Khalid Vohra, said the group looked forward "to serve the project and heavy lift cargo requirements" of India alongside SAL.

According to a 2020 trade-press interview, the group owned two vessels, managed by the ship-management division of Sai Maritime & Management.

== Group ==
The SAI Group is led by Khalid Vohra as Chairman and Managing Director. Group companies include Sai Maritime & Management Private Limited (Mumbai), which operates offices in Mumbai, Kandla and Chennai with sub-agents at other Indian ports.

data.title: Sai Maritime & Management Private Limited
data.text:
Sai Maritime & Management Private Limited is an Indian ship agency, chartering and ship management company headquartered in Mumbai. Formed in 1984 as the project-cargo division of the SAI Group, it is best known as the long-standing Indian agent of the German heavy-lift carrier SAL Heavy Lift and, since the formation of the Jumbo–SAL alliance, of the JSI Alliance.

== History ==
The company was incorporated in 1984 as a subsidiary of Sai Shipping Company Private Limited, a Mumbai ship agency established in 1977. According to a 2016 report in Daily Shipping Times, the company's cooperation with SAL Heavy Lift began in 1986, when the German carrier sought local support in Indian ports; by 2016 the two companies were marking thirty years of cooperation, with Sai Maritime acting as SAL's handling agent and exclusive booking agent for SAL tonnage in India.

In a 2020 interview with Project Cargo Weekly, director Rukhsana Vohra Mithani said the company had originally been formed with the intention of acquiring Indian-flag heavy-lift vessels for coastal operations, a plan that was later shelved, and that its entry into project and heavy-lift work came when SAL asked it to handle the vessel Antje at Kandla. The same interview stated that the company began a ship-management division in 2012 to manage the group's own vessels before offering the service to third-party owners.

In April 2024 the company coordinated the carriage of five heavy-lift units of between 243 and 711 tonnes along the Indian coast between Mumbai, Kolkata and Paradip aboard the SAL vessel MV Anna, working with the JSI Alliance and the Indian project forwarder Total Movements.

== Operations ==
The company operates from offices in Mumbai, Kandla and Chennai, with sub-agents at other Indian ports. Its stated activities are ship agency, chartering brokerage for heavy-lift, lift-on/lift-off, roll-on/roll-off and semi-submersible tonnage, and third-party ship management.

data.title: Robert Bobel
data.text:
----

Robert Bobel is an American technology executive and entrepreneur who is the co-founder and chief executive officer of Cayosoft, a software company that develops products for managing and recovering Microsoft identity infrastructure. [ref: Cybersecurity entrepreneur: Columbus attack can happen anywhere (and does), Columbus Business First]

==Career==

Bobel previously worked at Quest Software. He and fellow Cayosoft co-founder Andrei Polevoi were among former employees of Aelita Software who remained with Quest after it acquired Aelita in 2004. Both left Quest in 2012. [ref: As ransomware made headlines in 2023, sales tripled for Westerville data recovery firm, Columbus Inno]

Bobel started Cayo Software in 2013 as businesses were beginning to migrate toward cloud computing. Polevoi joined him in 2018, when the business was reincorporated as Cayosoft.

In March 2024, Columbus Inno reported that Cayosoft had raised $22.5 million after five years of funding its growth through revenue. The publication identified Bobel as the company's co-founder and chief executive officer. Later that year, Columbus Business First reported that Cayosoft had continued hiring and growing following the financing.

==Cybersecurity commentary==

Bobel has commented publicly on ransomware, identity infrastructure and recovery planning. In August 2024, following a cyberattack affecting the city of Columbus, Ohio, Columbus Business First interviewed Bobel about ransomware and Active Directory.

In discussing cyberattack preparedness, Bobel said organizations should plan for how they will respond if an attack occurs. He also discussed the role of Active Directory in identity and access management and approaches to recovering identity infrastructure following an attack.

data.title: Flurry Rush
data.text:
= Flurry Rush =
The Flurry Rush, in The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild, and The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom is a counterattack move that occurs after the player performs a Perfect Dodge. After the Perfect Dodge, time slows down, then Link executes a series of successive hits on the targeted enemy, depending on the weapon used. [ref: Nintendo - Official Site: Consoles, Games, News, and More, www.nintendo.com]

Players can perform a Perfect Dodge by backflipping or hopping to the side moments before an enemy attack reaches Link. The player then presses Y repeatedly. (The flurry Rush can be aborted at any time, if the player ceases to press Y). The weapon used depends on the number of max hits dealt to the enemy by Link during a Flurry Rush.

One handed weapon - Up to seven hits

Two handed weapon - Up to four hits

Spear - Up to 11 hits
----

Flurry Rush Change

In The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, the animation of the flurry Rush is sped up slightly, but the number of hits and the way to execute a Flurry Rush did not change.

data.title: Mosley Lane
data.text:
----

“Mosley Lane” is the sixteenth episode of the fifth season of the American police procedural crime drama television series Criminal Minds. Written by Simon Mirren and Erica Messer and directed by series cast member Matthew Gray Gubler, the episode originally aired on March 3, 2010.

== Plot ==
At a winter festival in Ashburn, Virginia, eight-year-old Aimee Lynch disappears after her mother, Barbara, is distracted by a woman calling out for a missing child. The Behavioral Analysis Unit (BAU) begins investigating the abduction. Sarah Hillridge approaches Jennifer Jareau and claims that the person responsible for Aimee’s disappearance also abducted her eight-year-old son, Charlie, eight years earlier. Although Sarah has made similar claims following other child abductions, the team discovers similarities between Charlie’s and Aimee’s disappearances.

Penelope Garcia searches for similar disappearances and discovers a pattern of children who have vanished from public places over several years. The BAU concludes that the abductions are the work of the same offenders, who have been taking children and holding them for extended periods. As the team investigates the previous cases and interviews the families of the missing children, they work to identify a connection that could lead them to the abductors before Aimee disappears permanently.

Aimee is taken to the home of Roger and Anita Roycewood, where several other abducted children are being held. Among them are Charlie Hillridge, who has survived the eight years since his disappearance, and Stephen Shepherd. The Roycewoods force the children to live as members of their household and use the older children to help control the younger captives. Charlie and Stephen attempt to protect Aimee and teach her how to survive in the house without provoking the Roycewoods.

The BAU discovers that the Roycewoods have been abducting children for years and disposing of the bodies of those who die while in captivity. The investigation eventually leads the team to a funeral home and crematorium connected to the couple. Meanwhile, Anita decides that Stephen has become too difficult to control and kills him after he tries to protect Aimee. The discovery raises the urgency of the search as the team realizes that Aimee and the remaining children are in immediate danger.

As the BAU closes in on the Roycewoods, Roger and Anita prepare to kill the remaining children and destroy evidence of their crimes. Charlie manages to obtain a gun and shoots Anita before she can kill Aimee and the other children. Roger dies during the confrontation, and the surviving children are rescued. Charlie is reunited with his parents after eight years in captivity. He later tells Stephen’s parents that their son had survived until the previous day and died protecting Aimee, leaving them devastated by how close they had come to seeing him alive again.

== Cast [ref: ] ==

=== Main ===

* Joe Mantegna as David Rossi
* Paget Brewster as Emily Prentiss
* Shemar Moore as Derek Morgan
* Matthew Gray Gubler as Spencer Reid
* A. J. Cook as Jennifer “JJ” Jareau
* Kirsten Vangsness as Penelope Garcia
* Thomas Gibson as Aaron Hotchner

=== Guest ===
* Mark St. Amant as Jake Hillridge
* Alton Clemente as Deputy
* Bud Cort as Roger Roycewood
* Ann Cusack as Sarah Hillridge
* Beth Grant as Anita Roycewood
* Toby Huss as Frank Lynch
* Richard Clarke Larsen as Mr. Hayden
* Bunny Levine as Martha Woodley
* Katlin Mastandrea as Mae Hall
* Austin Mincks as Stephen Shepherd
* Evan Peters as Charlie Hillridge
* Cameron Protzman as Aimee Lynch
* Grace Savage as Jane
* Brooke Smith as Barbara Lynch
* Debra Sullivan as Mrs. Shepherd
* Owen Thayer as Police Sketch Artist
* Holly Traister as Imaginary Female Unsub
* David Youse as Mr. Shepherd

== Production ==
Gubler was also involved in selecting the episode’s guest cast, which included Brooke Smith, Bud Cort, Beth Grant, Ann Cusack and Toby Huss. He described the young performers appearing in the episode as among the most talented child actors he had encountered.

“Mosley Lane” marked Matthew Gray Gubler’s directorial debut. Gubler, who portrays Spencer Reid in the series, had studied film directing at New York University’s Tisch School of the Arts before beginning his acting career. He had expressed an interest in directing Criminal Minds and approached executive producer and showrunner Ed Bernero about directing an episode near the end of the show’s fourth season. According to Gubler, Bernero told him that he was ready and only needed to ask. [ref: TV Guide, www.tvguide.com]

Gubler described “Mosley Lane” as a modern-day dark fairy tale inspired by Hansel and Gretel. Influenced by German Expressionist cinema, he chose to present parts of the story from a child’s perspective, giving the Roycewoods’ world an eerie, fantastical quality. For the Roycewoods’ home, Gubler selected a three-story Victorian mansion that he felt suited the episode’s unsettling atmosphere.

== Reception ==
“Mosley Lane” has received retrospective recognition as one of the standout episodes of Criminal Minds. Entertainment Weekly included the episode in its ranking of the series’ best episodes. [ref: The 20 best 'Criminal Minds' episodes, ranked, EW.com] /Film ranked it fifth among the 25 best episodes of the series, praising Matthew Gray Gubler’s direction, the pacing of the story and the performances of the guest cast release. [ref: The 25 Best Criminal Minds Episodes Ranked, SlashFilm] Cosmopolitan also included “Mosley Lane” among its 24 best episodes of Criminal Minds, highlighting its disturbing storyline and the guest appearances by Beth Grant and Evan Peters. [ref: The 24 Best 'Criminal Minds' Episodes, Ranked from Least to Most Anxiety-Inducing, Cosmopolitan]

During its original United States broadcast, “Mosley Lane” was watched by approximately 13 million viewers. [ref: Wednesday, March 3, 2010, TV Tango]

Shot on Video8, the film follows a widowed painter living with dementia and a young woman grieving her father's death. data.title: International Legal Technology Association (ILTA)
data.text:
----

The International Legal Technology Association (ILTA) is a non-profit trade association based in Chicago, Illinois, that provides education, networking, and research resources for legal technology professionals. [ref: International Legal Technology Association: ILTA, The National Law Review] Its activities include the annual ILTACON conference, the EVOLVE conference, the magazine Peer to Peer, and an annual technology survey of law firms.

== History ==
ILTA was founded in 1980 and was first incorporated in 1985. It is designated a 501(c)(6) nonprofit organization by the U.S. Internal Revenue Service.

== Membership and governance ==
ILTA's membership consists primarily of law firms, corporate legal departments, and law schools, and any employee of a member organization is eligible to participate. [ref: International Legal Technology Assoc., Idealist]

The organization is governed by a seven-member board of directors and supported by a professional staff. As of its most recent Form 990 filing, Joy Heath Rush serves as chief executive officer. [ref: International Legal Technology, Nonprofit Explorer]

== Activities ==
ILTA organizes educational conferences and events for legal technology professionals, including:

* ILTACON – ILTA's annual conference, which has been covered by legal trade press including Legaltech News and LawNext. [ref: 6 Things We Learned at this Year's ILTACON, Legaltech News] [ref: ILTACON 2021 Roundup: The Final Day, Legaltech News] [ref: Today on Legaltech Week: Our ILTACON Post-Mortem, LawNext] [ref: ILTACON Takeaways From a Legal Tech Newbie (and Litigation Beat Vet), Litigation Daily] [ref: Pre-ILTACON Legaltech Rundown, Legaltech News]
* EVOLVE – a conference on legal technology and operations that centers each year on two themes, most recently generative artificial intelligence and cybersecurity. [ref: EVOLVE, International Legal Technology Association] [ref: Legal tech education in the age of transformation: Insights ahead of ILTA EVOLVE 2025, Thomson Reuters Institute]
* ILTACON Europe – a regional community and event series for ILTA's European members. [ref: About ILTA Europe, International Legal Technology Association]
* Local socials – informal networking events in individual cities, often coordinated by volunteer member liaisons.

== Publications and research ==
ILTA's publications and programs include:

* Peer to Peer – a quarterly magazine on legal technology topics, published online and in a digital flipbook format. [ref: Peer to Peer Magazine, International Legal Technology Association]
* ILTA Technology Survey – an annual research report on technology use in law firms. The 2025 edition reported responses from 580 law firms representing more than 152,000 attorneys. [ref: 2025 Technology Survey, International Legal Technology Association]
* Distinguished Peer Awards – an annual awards program recognizing contributions to the legal technology field. [ref: ILTA Celebrates 16th Annual Distinguished Peer Awards, International Legal Technology Association]

data.title: Cooking Sections
data.text:
[[File:CLIMAVORE_On_Tidal_Zones.jpg|thumb|CLIMAVORE: On Tidal Zones. Cooking Sections, 2017-ongoing. Isle of Skye]]

Cooking Sections investigates the systems that shape the world through food, tracing the spatial, ecological, and political legacies of extractivism. Using site-responsive installations, performances, and video, their practice confronts the overlapping boundaries of art, architecture, ecology, and geopolitics. [ref: about - Cooking Sections, cooking-sections.com]

Founded in London in 2013 by Daniel Fernández Pascual and Alon Schwabe, Cooking Sections uses food as both a lens and a tool to trace the metabolic relations behind industrialised food systems. Since 2015, they have run CLIMAVORE, a long-term, site-responsive project, exploring how to eat as humans change climates and how to metabolise climate breakdown. [ref: About CLIMAVORE, CLIMAVORE] [ref: about - Cooking Sections, cooking-sections.com]

Alon and Daniel are Readers in Architecture and Spatial Practice at the Royal College of Art, London, and Fellows at the Canadian Institute for Advanced Research. [ref: Dr Daniel Fernández Pascual, RCA Website] [ref: Alon Schwabe, RCA Website]

== [https://www.climavore.org/ CLIMAVORE] ==
CLIMAVORE [ref: CLIMAVORE, www.climavore.org] uses cultural platforms to amplify civic resistance: removing farmed salmon from the menus of over 20 major museums; regranting art funds to farmers trailing agrochemical-free methods in Lake Erie; launching a nationwide baking challenge for breads against soil depletion in Finland; turning museums' living collections into protocols for peasant seed exchange in Southern Italy; or creating a water buffalo festival to protect Istanbul’s urban wetlands from extinction. [ref: The Turner Prize-Nominated Art Collective Cooking Sections Wants to Change the Way You Think About Food, Artnet News] [ref: Rights to Seeds, Rights of Seeds - Cooking Sections, cooking-sections.com] [ref: Maaleipä - Cooking Sections, cooking-sections.com] [ref: To Those Who Nourish - Cooking Sections, cooking-sections.com] [ref: Istanbul Wetlands - CLIMAVORE, CLIMAVORE]

== Exhibitions ==
Their work has been exhibited internationally, including at Tate Britain, Serpentine Galleries, SALT, Centro Botín, Bonniers Konsthall, Carnegie Museum of Art, Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, Museo delle Civiltà, among others. They have created site-specific performances and installations for the Taipei Biennial, 58th Venice Biennale, Istanbul Biennial, Performa17, Manifesta12, Los Angeles Public Art Triennial, Sharjah Architecture Triennial, Folkestone Triennial, and New Orleans Triennial among others. Residencies include the Headlands Center for the Arts, Prospect Cottage, Fogo Island Arts and Delfina Foundation. [ref: about - Cooking Sections, cooking-sections.com]

== Awards ==
Cooking Sections was nominated for the Turner Prize in 2021, received the Special Prize at the 2019 Future Generation Art Prize and were nominated for the Visible Award for socially-engaged practices. Daniel was awarded the 2020 Harvard GSD Wheelwright Prize for Being Shellfish. [ref: Cooking Sections, www.somersethouse.org.uk] [ref: Daniel Fernández Pascual Wins Harvard Graduate School of Design’s 2020 Wheelwright Prize, Harvard Graduate School of Design] [ref: ] [ref: Cooking Sections, PinchukArtCentre]

== Books ==

They have authored four books:

* The Empire Remains Shop (2018) [ref: The empire remains shop, Columbia University Press]
* Salmon: A Red Herring (2020)
* Offsetted (2022) [ref: Cooking Sections: Offsetted, Hatje Cantz Verlag]
* Waves Lost at Sea (2026) [ref: Cooking Sections: Waves Lost at Sea, Spector Books]

== External Links ==

* [https://www.cooking-sections.com/ Official Website]
* [https://www.climavore.org/ CLIMAVORE]

data.title: Yokohama Triennale
data.text:
----

Yokohama Triennale is an international contemporary art exhibition held every three years in Yokohama, Japan, since 2001. The first three editions (2001, 2005, 2008) were primarily organized by the Japan Foundation. Since 2011, the City of Yokohama has taken over the role of primary organizer. [ref: Yokohama Triennale 2011 will represent a significant shift in the event’s organization, primarily because the Japan Foundation has stepped down as the main organizer and the city of Yokohama has bolstered its participation as a result., Biennial Foundation] The Triennale hosts on average 60 to 90 national and international artists per edition [ref: About us｜Yokohama Triennale, Yokohama Triennale] with the exception of the 2017 triennial, which only hosted about 40 artists. [ref: Text von MIKI Akiko. Yokohama Triennale 2017, universes.art]

The Triennale's main venues are the Yokohama Museum of Art and the Yokohama Red Brick Warehouse.

== Chronology ==

=== 1st Yokohama Triennale ===
The exhibition, titled Mega Wave—Towards a New Synthesis, ran from 02 September 2001 to 11 November 2001. It took place in Pacifico Yokohama Exhibition Hall (C,D), Yokohama Red Brick Warehouse No.1, and was curated by Shinji Kohmoto, Akira Tatehata, Nobuo Nakamura, and Fumio Nanjo. [ref: YOKOHAMA 2001: International Triennale of Contemporary Art MEGA WAVE—Towards a New Synthesis｜Archive｜Yokohama Triennale, Yokohama Triennale]

=== 2nd Yokohama Triennale ===
The second edition, titled Art Circus [Jumping from the Ordinary], was held from 28 September 2005 to 18 December 2005 at the No.3 and No.4 warehouses of the Yamashita Pier. Its artistic director was Tadashi Kawamata, and its curators were Taro Amano, Takashi Serizawa, Shingo Yamano. [ref: YOKOHAMA 2005: International Triennale of Contemporary Art Art Circus [Jumping from the Ordinary]｜Archive｜Yokohama Triennale, Yokohama Triennale]

=== 3rd Yokohama Triennnale ===
The third edition, titled TIME CREVASSE, was held from 13 September 2008 to 30 November 2008 across several venues in Yokohama. The venues were Shinko Pier Exhibition Hall, NYK Waterfront Warehouse (BankART Studio NYK), Yokohama Red Brick Warehouse No.1, Sankeien Garden. The exhibition was directed by Tsutomu Mizusawa, and curated by Daniel Birnbaum, Fang Hu, Akiko Miyake, Hans-Ulrich Obrist, Beatrix Ruf. [ref: YOKOHAMA 2008: International Triennale of Contemporary Art TIME CREVASSE｜Archive｜Yokohama Triennale, Yokohama Triennale]

=== 4th Yokohama Triennale ===
The fourth edition, titled OUR MAGIC HOURーHow Much of the World Can We Know?ー, was held from 06 August 2011 to 06 November 2011 at the Yokohama Museum of Art, and the NYK Waterfront Warehouse (BankART Studio NYK). The triennial was directed by Eriko Osaka, and curated by Akiko Miki. [ref: Yokohama Triennale 2011 OUR MAGIC HOUR ーHow Much of the World Can We Know?ー｜Archive｜Yokohama Triennale, Yokohama Triennale] The 'magic' mentioned in the title was stated to be not of mystical kind, but rather a sense of wonder: "the show focused upon an ability to see the wonderful in the everyday that has long been popularly ascribed to artists." [ref: 4th Yokohama Triennale, "Our Magic Hour: How Much of the World Can We Know" - Criticism, e-flux]

=== 5th Yokohama Triennale ===
The fifth edition, titled Art Fahrenheit 451: Sailing into the sea of oblivion, was held from 01 August 2014 to 03 November 2014 at Yokohama Museum of Art, and the Shinko Pier Exhibition Hall. The Triennale's artistic director was Yasumasa Morimura. [ref: Yokohama Triennale 2014 ART Fahrenheit 451: Sailing into the sea of oblivion｜Archive｜Yokohama Triennale, Yokohama Triennale] The title was drawn from Ray Bradbury's dystopian novel Fahrenheit 451. Unlike the negative connotations of its title, the triennale was said to embrace "forgetting, destruction and failure as essential components of the creative process." [ref: Yokohama Triennale 2014: ART Fahrenheit 451: Sailing into the Sea of Oblivion, artreview.com]

=== 6th Yokohama Triennale ===
The sixth edition, titled Islands, Constellations & Galapagos, was held from 04 August 2017 to 05 November 2017 at the Yokohama Museum of Art, the Yokohama Red Brick Warehouse No.1, and the basement of Yokohama Port Opening Memorial Hall. The exhibition was directed by Eriko Osaka, Akiko Miki, Tomoh Kashiwagi [ref: Yokohama Triennale 2017 Islands, Constellations & Galapagos｜Archive｜Yokohama Triennale, Yokohama Triennale], and curated together with Rirkrit Tiravanija, Shuji Takashina, and Suhanya Raffel. [ref: 6th Yokohama Triennale, "Islands, Constellations and Galapagos" - Criticism, e-flux] This edition was said to read the world through 'connectivity' and 'isolation', making references to 'island mentality', Brexit, refugee crisis and online communities. [ref: Yokohama Triennale: Islands, Constellations & Galapagos, artreview.com]

=== 7th Yokohama Triennale ===
The seventh edition, titled Afterglow, was held from 17 July 2020 to 11 October 2020 at the Yokohama Museum of Art, and PLOT 48 (with NYK MARITIME MUSEUM). The exhibition was directed and curated by Raqs Media Collective. [ref: Yokohama Triennale 2020 AFTERGLOW｜Archive｜Yokohama Triennale, Yokohama Triennale] Exhibition's key ideas were stated to be ‘luminosity’, ‘care’, ‘friendship’ and ‘toxicity’ [ref: Yokohama Triennale 2020 'Afterglow' Review: Must the Show Go On?, artreview.com], bringing together artists "whose work engages with diverse belief systems, histories, and forms of sensory experience." [ref: 7th Yokohama Triennale, "Afterglow" - Criticism, e-flux]

Due to Covid-19 regulations and restrictions on travel, Yokohama Triennale offered a virtual tour of the whole exhibition. [ref: Explore Yokohama Triennale 2020 from home with virtual tour, Yokohama Triennale 2020 “Afterglow”]

=== 8th Yokohama Triennale ===
The eighth edition, titled Wild Grass: Our Lives, was held from 15 March 2024 to 09 June 2024 across several venues in Yokohama. The venues were Yokohama Museum of Art, Former Daiichi Bank Yokohama Branch, BankART KAIKO, Queen’s Square YOKOHAMA, and Motomachi-Chūkagai Station Accessway. The exhibition was directed and curated by Liu Ding, and Carol Yinghua Lu. This edition's title was stated to be inspired by the Chinese dissident Lu Xun's prose-poem collection Wild Grass (1927), chosen in order to "confront and contemplate today's global issues of climate change, economic disparity and authoritative legacies." [ref: Navigating the weeds: The 8th Yokohama Triennale's ode to change and survival]

=== 9th Yokohama Triennale ===
The ninth edition is planned to take place from 23 April 2027 to 12 September 2027, at the Yokohama Museum of Art as its main venue. The exhibition will be directed and curated by Cosmin Costinaș and Inti Guerrero. [ref: 9th Yokohama Triennale will be held from April 23 to September 12, 2027｜News｜Yokohama Triennale, Yokohama Triennale]

data.title: Doctor Marrax
data.text:
Doctor Marrax (born 21 May 1953 as Gerhard "Max" Matheis) is a German magician, street performer, and author. Matheis became known for his stage character Doctor Marrax, a quack doctor and miracle healer inspired by historical travelling medicine men. For several decades, he performed as Doctor Marrax at street festivals, variety and small-theatre venues, fairs, and magic events in Germany and abroad. [ref: Doctor Marrax, Zauber-Pedia]

== Life and career ==

Matheis completed an apprenticeship as a typesetter in 1971 and subsequently worked as an offset lithography assembler, graphic artist, and phototypesetter in the graphic arts industry until 1993.

He began performing traditional magic in 1981. From 1989 to 2002, he was a member of the magic theatre ensemble Ein Magisches Spektakulum, together with Signora Tre Face, Frascatelli, and Shri Magada. During this period, Matheis developed the character of the quack doctor Doctor Marrax, which became his trademark and remained central to his performances for more than three decades.

Matheis became a professional magician in 1992. [ref: Performance 2018, City of Paderborn] He participated in national and international magic competitions. His competition results include:

* 1993: German champion in the category General Magic with Presentation
* 1994: 3rd place in Comedy Magic at the Fédération Internationale des Sociétés Magiques (FISM) World Championships of Magic in Yokohama, Japan
* 1999: 1st place at the International Street Magicians Competition in Sankt Wendel, Germany
* 2000: 2nd place at the French Magie Comique championship in Paris, France
* 2003: 3rd place in Stage Illusions at the FISM World Championships of Magic in The Hague, Netherlands
* 2007: 2nd place with Doctor Marrax & Söhne at the International Street Magicians Competition in Sankt Wendel
* 2012: 2nd place with Doctor Marrax & Söhne at the 13th International Kleinkunstfestival on the island of Usedom

His German championship title and his two third-place finishes at the FISM World Championships in 1994 and 2003 are documented in literature on the history of magic.

From 2002, Matheis performed as a solo artist. Between 2007 and 2015, he performed together with his son Paul Scharkowski under the name Doctor Marrax & Söhne ("Doctor Marrax & Sons").

In 2018, Matheis announced his retirement from performing. He ended his active stage career in 2019.

In addition to his work as a performer, Matheis has been involved in preserving and documenting the history of magic. He collects historical souvenir postcards, magic props, and documents, and has given lectures on the history of magic. [ref: Wissenswertes von Agoston und Bosco bis Sparovitz und Werry, ZZZAUBER Blog]

== Doctor Marrax ==

The character Doctor Marrax portrays a travelling miracle healer, charlatan, and quack doctor from around 1900. With a rolled "R", a Bohemian-style accent, long beard, black top hat, and a mobile "medicinal cart" or "quack doctor's stage", Matheis presented a medicine show combining street theatre, magic, and comedy.

Central to the performances was the supposed universal remedy Marrax-o-fax, a fictional miracle cure with which Doctor Marrax claimed to be able to perform seemingly impossible healings and other magical feats. Among other things, the character claimed that Marrax-o-fax could replace lost eyes, heal deep wounds, and even cause severed heads to grow back. Marrax-o-fax became one of the characteristic elements of the Doctor Marrax persona.

One of the character's recurring introductory phrases was:

:"Birrrger, mecht ich mich vorstellen, bin ich Doctor Marrax!"

The character was conceived as a historical stage persona inspired by the world of travelling medicine men, miracle healers, charlatans, and itinerant entertainers of the late 19th century.

== Publications ==

Together with street performer Radalou, Matheis published the specialist book Anlocken – Fesseln – Abkassieren! Handbuch der Straßenzauberei ("Attract – Captivate – Cash In! A Handbook of Street Magic") in 2008. The book discusses both the artistic and practical aspects of street magic and draws on the authors' experience as street performers.

Matheis has also published articles on magic, including the 2002 article Akustische Täuschungen in der Zauberkunst ("Acoustic Deceptions in Magic") in the German magic journal Magie.

== Film ==

Following his retirement from active stage performance, Matheis increasingly devoted himself to documentary projects. In 2021, he produced the documentary film GILBERT le Saltimbanque – Ein Gespräch unter Gauklern ("Gilbert le Saltimbanque – A Conversation Among Street Performers"). Matheis and Rainer Schwarz co-directed the film. [ref: Neuer Dokufilm von Gerhard Max Matheis: „GILBERT le Saltimbanque – Ein Gespräch unter Gauklern“, Magischer Zirkel von Deutschland]

The film portrays Belgian-French street performer Gilbert Jakubczyk-Liberman, a longtime friend and fellow performer of Matheis. In the documentary, Matheis and Schwarz visit locations associated with Gilbert's life and document his work as a street performer and itinerant entertainer. [ref: Gilbert le Saltimbanque – Ein Gespräch unter Gauklern, Filmhaus Köln]

The documentary has a running time of 105 minutes.

== Work on the history of magic ==

Following his retirement from active stage performance, Matheis remained involved with magic and its history. His collection includes historical promotional material, souvenir postcards, magic props, and documents. He has also given lectures on historical magicians and the development of magic as a performing art.

== External links ==

* [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qUn2pXdkESU Doctor Marrax performing Lochwanderung] on YouTube

data.title: Scott McCullough
data.text:
----

Scott McCullough is an American writer, director, cinematographer and editor of films, commercials, music videos and concert films. His work includes projects for Prince, 70mm NASCAR films and narrative and nonprofit projects. [ref: Top VFX Specialist Richard Kidd Joins Artemple-Hollywood Along With Scott McCullough, Deadline] [ref: Top 10 Innovative Minds Disrupting The Entertainment Space - LA Weekly] McCullough has been a member of the Directors Guild of America since 2001. [ref: Profile, www.dga.org]

== Early life and career ==
McCullough grew up in the Twin Cities area of Minnesota and attended the University of Minnesota, initially studying architecture and then advertising at the School of Journalism. He subsequently moved into camera work, music videos and commercial production in Minneapolis. [ref: Spotlight: Scott McCullough, PRN Alumni Foundation]

== Work with Prince and music videos ==
During the early 1990s, McCullough worked with Prince and associated artists across music videos, films and documentary projects. [ref: The director formerly with Prince / Industry signs third director, Screen]

His work also appeared on three Prince home-video releases: Gett Off, Sexy M.F. and Diamonds and Pearls Video Collection.

A later PRN Alumni Foundation profile described his Gett Off-era work as well as his filming of Prince's Special Olympics rehearsals and European concert material. Decades later, archival material from that period was released, including Live at Glam Slam and This Thing Called Soundcheck. [ref: Prince & The New Power Generation's 'Diamonds And Pearls' Expanded Reissue With Previously Unreleased Tracks & HD Concert Footage, Legacy Recordings]

On January 11, 1992, Prince and the New Power Generation performed at Glam Slam in Minneapolis. The film remained unreleased in Prince's vault for more than three decades. The complete concert was released in 2023 as Prince and the New Power Generation: Live at Glam Slam. [ref: Watch Rare Prince Performance of 'Nothing Compares 2 U' - PAPER Magazine, www.papermag.com] [ref: Prince / The New Power Generation: Diamonds and Pearls (Super Deluxe Edition), Pitchfork] The 2023 release identifies McCullough in its original-crew credits as director and cinematographer, a credit also carried in the accompanying hardcover book. [ref: Diamonds and Pearls Super Deluxe Edition, NPG Records / Paisley Park Enterprises / Sony Music Entertainment / Warner Records] In coverage of the release, PAPER interviewed McCullough about filming the "Nothing Compares 2 U" performance, identifying him as the concert film's director, cinematographer and camera operator.

Variety described Prince and the New Power Generation as being in peak form during the 90-minute performance, [ref: Prince's 'Diamonds and Pearls' Deluxe Edition Delivers Rare Gems From His Last Blockbuster: Album Review, Variety] while The Current called the Glam Slam concert "the real prize of the set". [ref: Digging for '(Diamonds and) Pearls' in Prince's expanded reissue, www.thecurrent.org]

His early Paisley Park work included Eric Leeds' "Little Rock." In 2000, the Chris Cummings video "That'll Teach Her" reached number 1 on RPM’s Video & Instant Top Forty chart. [ref: Video and Instant Top Forty, RPM] Screen also discussed McCullough's work with Cummings during that period. [ref: Variety Is the Spice - Director/cameraman doesn't want to be pigeonholed, Screen]

== Commercial and advertising work ==
While continuing music-video work, McCullough moved into commercial directing during the 1990s. Adweek credited him as director of Target Stores' 1995 "Single Step" campaign. [ref: New Campaigns, Adweek] In 1998, the magazine included the Jesse Ventura for Governor campaign spot "The Thinker," also directed by McCullough, in its "Best Spots" coverage. [ref: Best Spots - November, Adweek] [ref: CAMPAIGN REFORM HELPED 'THE BODY' SLAM RIVALS, The Washington Post]

His work expanded into automotive and motorsports filmmaking. For R.J. Reynolds and the NASCAR Winston Cup Series, McCullough created, directed, photographed and edited the large-format films No Bull and 100%, filming NASCAR Winston Cup drivers across multiple race weekends for the traveling Thunder Theater experience. [ref: "100%" in 70mm, www.in70mm.com] The films were photographed in 65mm five-perf for 70mm exhibition.

McCullough's commercial work includes campaigns for General Motors, Coors Light and Pepsi. For General Motors, McCullough directed and photographed automotive work for Buick, Pontiac and GMC, including a five-commercial GMC package for Boston agency Digitas. [ref: ] In 2008, Reel Chicago reported that McCullough directed Story's largest production to date, a 23-day, two-country automotive shoot divided between Los Angeles and Buenos Aires. [ref: PRODUCTION CENTRAL, Reel Chicago News]

McCullough's motorsports work later extended to open-wheel Champ Car racing. He directed and photographed a campaign featuring Paul Newman and Newman's Champ Car racing team. LA Weekly later described the project as Newman's final filmed appearance and reported that Newman had requested McCullough as director.

For Budweiser and DDB Chicago, McCullough directed and photographed Push On, a tribute to Dale Earnhardt Sr. featuring Dale Earnhardt Jr., produced in the immediate aftermath of Earnhardt Sr.'s death at the Daytona 500. The spot was subsequently featured by Advertising Age's Creativity in its "Who Did That Spot?" coverage. [ref: Who Did That Spot?, Advertising Age's Creativity]

In 2015, Deadline reported that Artemple-Hollywood named McCullough its in-house director and director of photography, noting his commercial work for clients including Pepsi and Ford. In 2023, LA Weekly included McCullough in its "Top 10 Innovative Minds Disrupting the Entertainment Space," citing his music, commercial, motorsports and narrative work.

== Film and narrative work ==
McCullough later directed, edited and executive produced the series pilot Three Days Gone: Based on the Life of Lucas Snow, substantially reworking material from an earlier production into the new pilot version. [ref: Three Days Gone: An Interview with Scott McCullough, Close-Up Film Reviews] The pilot received festival awards, including Best Director at the Florence Film Awards in 2025 [ref: FLORENCE FILM AWARDS, FLORENCE FILM AWARDS] and Best Editing at the World Indie Film Awards in 2022. [ref: June 22, WIFA]

McCullough later directed and edited the horror project The Exorcism Diaries, written by Kenny Yakkel. The project received a Gold Award for Director at the Florence Film Awards in 2025. It also received coverage connected with the Cannes film market. [ref: Take a Peek Inside The Exorcism Diaries, Dread Central]

The screenplay for Captain for Dark Mornings, co-written with Nancy Froeschle, was a semifinalist in Stage 32's Diversity Springboard Screenwriting Contest. [ref: 1st Annual Diversity Springboard Screenwriting Contest, Stage 32]

== Public-service and nonprofit work ==
McCullough created, wrote, directed and photographed The Other Note, a public-service film for the National Veterans Foundation addressing veteran suicide and featuring Martin Sheen. [ref: NVF's New Veteran Suicide Prevention PSA, National Veterans Foundation] The National Veterans Foundation launched the campaign in 2016. The film received a 2017 CINE Golden Eagle Award. [ref: ]

== References ==

data.title: Salah Mansour
data.text:
----

Salah Mansour (born November 14, 1942) is a Lebanese-Canadian otolaryngologist, academic, and medical author. [ref: Environmental noise in Beirut, smoking and age are combined risk factors for hearing impairment, Eastern Mediterranean Health Journal] He was a Professor of Otolaryngology at the Lebanese University Faculty of Medical Sciences, served as Vice Dean of the faculty, and was President of the Scientific Council for Otolaryngology Head and Neck Surgery under the Arab Board of Health Specializations. [ref: Comprehensive and Clinical Anatomy of the Middle Ear, Springer Berlin, Heidelberg] [ref: Middle Ear Diseases: Advances in Diagnosis and Management, Springer International Publishing]

== Medical education and career ==
Mansour earned his Doctor of Medicine (MD) degree from Saint Joseph University in Beirut in 1970. He completed surgical and otolaryngological post-graduate training in Canada at Université Laval, McGill University, and the Université de Montréal hospital network. He earned the License of the Medical Council of Canada (LMCC) in 1972, and became a Fellow of the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada (FRCSC) in 1975. He was made a Fellow of the American College of Surgeons (FACS) in 1976.

Mansour practiced clinical otolaryngology in Quebec at Honoré-Mercier Hospital in Saint-Hyacinthe, Quebec and Charles-Le Moyne Hospital in Longueuil. In Lebanon, he served as:
* 1998–2012: Vice Dean of the Faculty of Medical Sciences at the Lebanese University.
* 1998–2016: Full Professor of Otolaryngology at the Lebanese University Faculty of Medical Sciences.
* 1989–2003: President of the examination commission and Scientific Committee of Otolaryngology – Head and Neck Surgery of the Arab Board of Health Specializations.
* 2003–2013: President of the Scientific Council of the Arab Board of Otolaryngology – Head and Neck Surgery.

In 2016, he relocated to Montreal, Quebec, practicing as an ORL consultant at Westmount Square Medical Center until his retirement in 2022.

== Publications ==
Mansour led an international team of otologists, embryologists, and neuroradiologists to produce a series of medical reference textbooks on middle ear anatomy and pathology published by Springer Nature:

=== Textbooks ===
* Mansour, Salah; Magnan, Jacques; Haidar, Hassan; Louryan, Stéphane (2013). Comprehensive and Clinical Anatomy of the Middle Ear. Springer Berlin, Heidelberg...
* Mansour, Salah; Magnan, Jacques; Haidar, Hassan; Nicolas, Karen (2015). Tympanic Membrane Retraction Pocket: Overview and Advances in Diagnosis and Management. Springer International Publishing... [ref: Tympanic Membrane Retraction Pocket: Overview and Advances in Diagnosis and Management, Springer International Publishing]
* Mansour, Salah; Magnan, Jacques; Nicolas, Karen; Haidar, Hassan (2018). Middle Ear Diseases: Advances in Diagnosis and Management. Springer International Publishing...
* Mansour, Salah; Magnan, Jacques; Haidar Ahmad, Hassan; Nicolas, Karen; Louryan, Stéphane (2019). Comprehensive and Clinical Anatomy of the Middle Ear (2nd ed.). Springer Nature Switzerland... [ref: Comprehensive and Clinical Anatomy of the Middle Ear, Springer Nature Switzerland]

=== General literary works ===
* Mansour, Salah (2024). Sur les ailes des hirondelles. Paris: Éditions Complicités.. [ref: Sur les ailes des hirondelles, Éditions Complicités]
* Mansour, Salah (2025). Ahadith al-Arjouan (أحاديث الأرجوان). Beirut: Librairie Antoine. [ref: Librairie Antoine]

=== Selected journal articles ===
* Mansour, S. (1978). "Mandibular Hemangioma". The Journal of Otolaryngology, 7(5), 424–430.. [ref: Mandibular Hemangioma, The Journal of Otolaryngology]
* Moukarzel, N., Nehmé, A., & Mansour, S. (2000). "Middle Turbinate Medialization technique in functional endoscopic sinus surgery". The Journal of Otolaryngology, 29(3), 144–147.. [ref: Middle Turbinate Medialization technique in functional endoscopic sinus surgery, The Journal of Otolaryngology]
* Mansour, S., & Nicolas, K. (2005). "Inflammatory Chronic Otitis Media and the Epitympanic Recess". The Journal of Otolaryngology, 34(3), 190–194. [ref: Inflammatory Chronic Otitis Media and the Epitympanic Recess, The Journal of Otolaryngology]
