data.title: Lala Khadija Azaroual
data.text:
Lala Khadija Azaroual, known as Chef Maman Hanane, is a Moroccan-born chef, pastry chef and cookbook author based in Belgium. She shares recipes from Moroccan cuisine on social media. Her first cookbook was published in Dutch and French in 2026. [ref: Chef Maman Hanane, Lannoo] [ref: Proef de echte Marokkaanse keuken, Lannoo] [ref: Goûtez la vraie cuisine marocaine, Lannoo]

== Background and career ==

Born in Morocco, Azaroual moved to Flanders to pursue further studies in international law, having already earned a master's degree in the field. [ref: Deze populaire chef leert je Marokkaans koken met handig stappenplan, Gazet van Antwerpen]

To finance her studies, she took a student job at Désiré de Lille in Antwerp, working with Marc Stoffels. She began by clearing tables before moving into the kitchen a few months later.

She later trained as a chef and pastry chef at PIVA in Antwerp. At Désiré de Lille, she became responsible for the kitchen and eventually took over the management of the establishment.

== Cooking and family influences ==

In a profile published by Gazet van Antwerpen, Azaroual describes learning to cook from three women in her family: her Amazigh grandmother from the High Atlas, her grandmother from Fez, and her mother, who taught her French cooking techniques.

Her cookbook draws on what she learned from her mother and grandmothers. It brings together traditional Moroccan recipes and her own adaptations of dishes from the Maghreb.

== Social media ==

Under the name Chef Maman Hanane, she shares recipes on YouTube and Instagram. In June 2026, Gazet van Antwerpen reported that her YouTube channel had more than 350,000 subscribers and her Instagram account nearly 80,000 followers.

== Cookbook ==

Her first cookbook, Proef de echte Marokkaanse keuken, was published by Lannoo in June 2026. It contains 70 recipes, including preparations of couscous, chermoula and zaalouk, alongside family stories and memories.

According to the profile in Gazet van Antwerpen, selecting, testing and refining the recipes took more than two years.

A French edition was also published in 2026 under the title Goûtez la vraie cuisine marocaine: Plats authentiques et délicieux, du couscous au zaalouk.

In August 2026, the book was included in a selection of eleven cookbooks published by the Belgian magazine Flair. [ref: SHOPPEN: 11 nieuwe kookboeken waarmee je aan de slag wil in de keuken, Flair]

=== Editions ===

* Proef de echte Marokkaanse keuken: Heerlijke, authentieke gerechten van couscous tot za’louk, Lannoo
* Goûtez la vraie cuisine marocaine: Plats authentiques et délicieux, du couscous au zaalouk, Lannoo

Jaye Neutron is a music producer and voice-tag artist from Georgia. He is the founder of Voice Tag Gods and a former member of the production collective 808 Mafia. [ref: How Voice Tags Help Hip-Hop Producers Make A Name For Themselves, Genius]

Neutron produced "Picacho" on Young Thug's 2013 mixtape 1017 Thug. [ref: Young Thug: 1017 Thug, Pitchfork] [ref: Rap Game Pikachu, Pitchfork] His other production credits include Turk's "Touchdown" and the remix of "Wodie", which features Master P. [ref: Touchdown, HotNewHipHop] [ref: Wodie (Remix), HotNewHipHop]

Neutron has recorded producer tags for Sonny Digital, Murda Beatz, TM88 and 808 Mafia. [ref: Famous producer tags recorded by us, Voice Tag Gods]

Sonny Digital was among his first tag clients. In a 2018 interview with Genius, Sonny Digital said he had paid Neutron $20 for the recording. Neutron recalled making the tag while he was in ninth grade.

data.title: Bedroom Tapes
data.text:
Bedroom Tapes is the debut extended play from Norwegian artist Jakob (then performing under the name Jakob Ogawa). It was released through Playground Music on June 16, 2017. [ref: Jakob Ogawa Biography, AllMusic] The five-track project was written and recorded by Jakob in his bedroom. It became a widely recognized entry in the late-2010s international bedroom pop wave. [ref: Meet Jakob Ogawa: Norway's Bedroom Pop Pioneer, Liminal Magazine] [ref: Report of the State of Culture in Spain, Fundación Alternativas] The EP includes the artist's breakthrough collaborative single "You Might Be Sleeping", featuring guest vocals from American singer-songwriter Clairo. [ref: Relax with Jakob Ogawa and Clairo's dreamy duet "You Might Be Sleeping", The Line of Best Fit]

== Composition ==

The musical style of Bedroom Tapes relies on analog instruments, warbling guitar chords, and heavy vocal processing. [ref: EP-anmeldelse: Jakob Ogawa – «Bedroom tapes», Deichman Musikk] While contemporary critics pointed out that the project was built within the sonic framework of lo-fi recording, [ref: LISTEN: Jakob Ogawa Releases Three-Song EP "April", FLOOD Magazine] they highlighted Jakob's distinct integration of American soul, left-field R&B, drawing specific comparisons to Stones Throw Records artists like Dudley Perkins.

== Critical reception ==

The EP received acclaim from Norwegian and international music critics upon release, with commentators praising its atmospheric depth and stylistic consistency despite its short running length. Norwegian publications noted the project's production; Jonas Irmer of Subjekt called it a candidate for the summer's best record, while critic Audun Vinger of Dagens Næringsliv summarized the release as a refreshing and cohesive statement of intent.

International reception similarly focused on the project's sonic atmosphere. The Chicago Reader highlighted the release's warm indie pop elements and dreamy grooves. Music publication Alt Citizen focused on the collaborative track "You Might Be Sleeping", commending its bright melodies, ambient guitar work, and prominent bass line.
== Track listing ==
All tracks are written, recorded, and mixed by Jakob Myklebust.

== Personnel ==
Credits adapted from the liner notes of the master release.
* Jakob Myklebust – vocals, instrumentation, songwriting, recording engineering, mixing
* Ian Thomas Miller – album artwork design
* Joe Lambert – audio mastering engineering

data.title: Wendy Cai-Lee
data.text:
Wendy Cai-Lee is an American banking executive and entrepreneur. She is the founder and chief executive officer of Piermont Bank, a commercial bank based in New York. [ref: A Woman Entrepreneur Disrupts The Middle Market Commercial Banking Industry, Forbes] She founded Piermont in 2019 and has been described by Forbes and Commercial Property Executive as the first Asian American woman to launch a commercial bank in the United States. [ref: Forbes 50 Over 50: Investment, Forbes] [ref: Q&A With Pioneering Bank Founder Wendy Cai-Lee, Commercial Property Executive] [ref: ]

Before founding Piermont Bank, Cai-Lee held executive positions at East West Bank and worked in management consulting, investment banking and financial services. [ref: East West Bank's Wendy Cai-Lee Talks Commerical Real Estate Hot Spots, Commercial Observer] She has also served on nonprofit and educational boards and has received recognition from publications and organizations in the banking, finance and business sectors. [ref: The Most Powerful Women to Watch, No. 10, Wendy Cai-Lee, Piermont Bank, American Banker] [ref: Inc. Founder Profile, Inc.com] [ref: ]

=== Early Career ===
Cai-Lee began her banking career at JPMorgan Chase after graduating from Rutgers University. She subsequently held positions at Citigroup and Deloitte, where she worked as a managing director focused on U.S.–China cross-border transactions.

Cai-Lee joined East West Bank in 2011. She was an executive vice president and oversaw banking activities across commercial and consumer banks. East West Bancorp's filings identify her as executive vice president and head of the U.S. Eastern and Texas regions beginning in 2014.

During her tenure at East West Bank, Cai-Lee was involved in commercial and commercial real estate lending. In 2014, Commercial Observer profiled her role overseeing approximately 300 employees across the bank's Eastern and Texas regions. [ref: Day in the life of: Wendy Cai-Lee, The Real Deal]

In 2015, Commercial Observer's predecessor, The Mortgage Observer, included Cai-Lee in its annual list of the "50 Most Important People in Commercial Real Estate Finance." [ref: The 50 Most Important People in Commercial Real Estate Finance, Commercial Observer] The Real Deal also profiled Cai-Lee in 2016 in an article about her role at East West Bank and her work in commercial real estate lending.

=== Piermont Bank ===
Cai-Lee founded Piermont Bank in 2019. [ref: ] [ref: Interpretations and Actions: January 2019, OCC.gov] At its launch, Piermont was described as the first new bank chartered by New York State since 2009. Contemporary coverage identified Cai-Lee as its president and chief executive officer.

Cai-Lee developed Piermont as a technology-forward commercial bank focused on entrepreneurs and small and medium-sized businesses. Banking Dive reported in 2020 that the bank was established to address what Cai-Lee described as a gap between large banks and smaller community institutions serving businesses requiring commercial lending.

Forbes profiled Cai-Lee in 2020 in an article examining her decision to establish Piermont and her approach to commercial banking.

Piermont subsequently developed a banking-as-a-service business serving financial technology companies in addition to its commercial banking activities. American Banker profiled Cai-Lee in 2022 in connection with the bank's technology-oriented business model and described Piermont as having been built with banking-as-a-service capabilities from its inception. [ref: Most Powerful Women to Watch: No. 24, Piermont Bank's Wendy Cai-Lee, American Banker]

In 2024, Commercial Property Executive published a profile and interview with Cai-Lee concerning her career and Piermont's commercial real estate business. The publication described her as the first Asian American woman to start a U.S. commercial bank and reported that Piermont had become the first multiracial Minority Depository Institution in the United States.

Cai-Lee has continued to lead Piermont as chief executive officer. Forbes' 2026 50 Over 50 profile reported that she founded the bank at age 45.

=== Recognition ===
Cai-Lee has received recognition from publications and organizations in banking, finance, entrepreneurship and business.

In 2007, she was named to Crain's New York Business's "40 Under 40" list. This recognition is documented in her professional biographies, although I have not yet located the original Crain's listing in an accessible archive.

In 2013, she was named to NJBIZ's "Forty Under 40" list. NJBIZ identified her as senior managing director and head of the Eastern region of East West Bank. [ref: Forty Under 40, NJBIZ]

Also in 2013, Cai-Lee was named to the M&A Advisor's "40 Under 40" list. A contemporary listing of the award recipients identifies her as senior managing director and head of the Eastern region at East West Bank.

In 2015, she was included in The Mortgage Observer's "50 Most Important People in Commercial Real Estate Finance."

Cai-Lee received the "Above & Beyond" award from City & State magazine for leadership and contributions to the New York business community. This recognition is documented in professional and organizational biographies; an original City & State source should ideally be located before using it as a major citation in the article.

In 2022, American Banker named Cai-Lee a Digital Banker of the Year. American Banker subsequently profiled her in its "Most Powerful Women to Watch" program, ranking her 24th in 2022. She was again named to American Banker's "Most Powerful Women to Watch" list in 2023 and 2024, ranking 25th in 2023 and 22nd in 2024.

In 2024, Inc. Magazine included Cai-Lee in its Female Founders 250 list. Inc. cited Piermont Bank's 28 percent asset growth in its description of the recognition.

In 2025, American Banker ranked Cai-Lee No. 10 on its "Most Powerful Women to Watch" list. The accompanying profile discussed her leadership of Piermont and the bank's capital position and business strategy.

In 2026, Forbes named Cai-Lee to its "50 Over 50" list in the Investment category. Forbes described her as the founder and CEO of Piermont Bank and noted that she became the first Asian American woman to launch a U.S. commercial bank when she founded Piermont in 2019.

Recognition & Awards:

* Crain's New York Business "40 Under 40" (2007)
* M&A Advisor "40 Under 40" (2013)
* NJBIZ "Forty Under 40" (2013)
* The Mortgage Observer "50 Most Important People in Commercial Real Estate Finance" (2015)
* City & State "Above & Beyond" Award (2015)
* American Banker Digital Banker of the Year (2022)
* American Banker "Most Powerful Women to Watch" (2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025)
* Finovate Executive of the Year, Finalist (2022)
* LendIt Fintech Woman of the Year, Finalist (2022)
* Inc. Female Founders 250 (2024)
* Forbes "50 Over 50", Investment (2026)

=== Civic & Non-profit Activities ===
Cai-Lee has served on nonprofit and educational boards. She served as chair of the board of Friends of the United Nations Population Fund and subsequently as an emeritus member of its board. Friends of UNFPA's annual reports identify her as chair of the board during the 2010s.

She has also served on the Rutgers University Board of Overseers and the advisory board of Douglass College. Rutgers currently identifies her as a member of the Douglass Advisory Board.

Cai-Lee is a member of the Committee of 100, a Chinese American civic organization. [ref: Wendy Cai-Lee, Committee of 100]

She has also served on advisory bodies associated with the New York State Department of Financial Services.

data.title: DeskTime
data.text:
DeskTime is an automatic time-tracking software that analyzes employee productivity. [ref: DeskTime employee monitoring, TechRadar] First released in 2011 by the Latvian tech company Draugiem Group, the software was initially developed for internal use within the group before becoming a standalone product.

The software allows users to categorize the applications and websites used during working hours as productive, unproductive, or neutral, providing insight into how time is spent throughout the day. The collected data is available to both employees and managers. [ref: Kā darbojas produktivitātes mērīšanas rīks "DeskTime", un vai to iespējams apmānīt, Delfi] [ref: Latvian Economics Ministry to watch employees' screen time, eng.lsm.lv] The software is mostly used in the private sector, however some pilot projects in the public sector have also been set up.

DeskTime's user base exceeds over 100,000 employees worldwide, with the United States and India as the biggest markets. [ref: Trīs mēneši ar "DeskTime" – jaunā realitāte Ekonomikas ministrijā, Delfi] [ref: Uzņēmums ķer “laika zagļus”, LA.LV]

== Productivity research ==
The company that develops DeskTime has published several studies on workplace productivity based on aggregated user data. A 2014 analysis of its most productive users found that they typically worked in 52-minute intervals followed by 17-minute breaks - a pattern that became known as the 52/17 rule, a time-management method comparable to the Pomodoro Technique. [ref: What the most productive workers have in common, The Washington Post] [ref: The Exact Perfect Amount of Time to Take a Break, According to Data, TIME] [ref: The Exact Amount Of Time You Should Work Every Day, Fast Company]

In 2017, a study drawing on data from 65,000 employees in the United States found that productivity declines after extended working hours: output dropped by 11% immediately after eight hours of work, with an additional 19% decrease for each subsequent hour. [ref: New Data Proves Staying Late in the Office Is Pointless, Observer]

data.title: J-transform
data.text:
----

----In mathematics, the {\mathbb
J}-transform [ref: {{Cite journal|url=http://www.jaac-online.com//en/article/doi/10.11948/20180258|title=BEYOND SUMUDU TRANSFORM AND NATURAL TRANSFORM: $ {\mathbb J} $-TRANSFORM PROPERTIES AND APPLICATIONS|first1=Weidong|last1=Zhao|first2=Shehu|last2=Maitama|date=August 15, 2020|journal=Journal of Applied Analysis & Computation|volume=10|issue=4|pages=1223–1241|via=www.jaac-online.com|doi=10.11948/20180258}}] is an integral transform introduced as a modification of the well-known Sumudu transform [ref: Sumudu transform: a new integral transform to solve differential equations and control engineering problems, International Journal of Mathematical Education in Science and Technology] and the Natural transform [ref: Theory of Natural Transform, MESA] for solving differential equations arising in applied physical sciences and engineering. The {\mathbb
J}-transform possesses several useful properties that distinguish it from the Sumudu transform and the natural transform, and it can be applied to problems that may be difficult to handle using either transform independently. The {\mathbb
J}-transform was introduced by Shehu Maitama and Weidong Zhao in 2020. Since its introduction, it has been applied to the solution of various ordinary differential equations (ODEs) and partial differential equations (PDEs), including problems involving fractional-order models and real-life applications in the physical science and engineering. [ref: A novel tempered fractional transform: theory, properties and applications to differential equations, Fractals] [ref: A survey of (2+1)-dimensional KDV-MKDV equation using nonlocal Caputo fractal-fractional operator, Results in Physics]
== Formal definition ==

The {\mathbb J}-transform of the function f(t) of exponential order is defined over the set of functions, A=\left\{f(t):\exists N, \xi_{1}, \xi _{2}>0,\; \text{such that}\; \left|f(t)\right|

by

{\mathbb J}\left[f(t)\right](\mu,\nu)=F(\mu,\nu)=\nu\int _{0
}^{\infty}\exp\left(\frac{-\mu t}{\nu}\right)f(t)dt
=\nu\lim_{\alpha\rightarrow\infty}\int _{0
}^{\alpha}\exp\left(\frac{-\mu t}{\nu}\right)f(t)dt.

Here, \mu>0 and \nu>0, provided the limit of the integral
exists, and \mu\,\,and \,\,\nu are the {\mathbb
J}-transform variables.. The {\mathbb
J}-transform converges to Laplace transform when the variable \nu=1.

== Inverse {\mathbb
J}-transform ==

Let F(\mu,\nu) be
the {\mathbb J}-transform of the function f(t), then the inverse {\mathbb J}-transform is defined as

{\mathbb J^{-1}}\left[F(\mu,\nu)\right]=f(t),\, \,
\text{for}\,\,t\geq0.

Equivalently, the complex inverse {\mathbb J}-transform is
defined as
{\mathbb J^{-1}}\left[F(\mu,\nu)\right]=f(t)=\lim_{\beta\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{\alpha-i\beta}^{\alpha+i\beta}\frac{1}{\nu^2}\exp\left(\frac{\mu t}{\nu}\right)F(\mu,\nu)d\mu

=\sum
\text{residues of}\,\,
\frac{1}{\nu^2}\exp\left(\frac{\mu t}{\nu}\right)F(\mu,\nu)\,\,\text{at the poles of}\,\,F(\mu,\nu).

Here, \mu is a complex number and \alpha is a real number.

== Properties of {\mathbb
J}-transform ==

Linearity property:
Let the functions f(t) and w(t) be in set A. Then, the following linearity property holds

{\mathbb J}\left[\alpha f(t)+\beta w(t)\right]
=\alpha{\mathbb J}\left[f(t)\right]+\beta{\mathbb J}\left[w(t)\right],
where \alpha and \beta are two constant parameters

First translation or shifting property:

Let the function \exp\left(\alpha t\right)f(t) be in set A, where \alpha is constant parameter. Then, the first translation or shifting property is defined as

{\mathbb J}\left[\exp\left(\alpha t\right)f(t)\right]=\frac{\mu-\alpha\nu}{\mu}F\left(\mu,\frac{\mu\nu}{\mu-\alpha\nu}\right).
Moreover, the shifting property provides results based on certain variable transformations

{\mathbb J}\left[\exp\left(\alpha t\right)f(t)\right]= \begin{cases}

\frac{\mu-\alpha}{\mu}F\left(\mu,\frac{\mu}{\mu-\alpha }\right),\,\,\text{when}\,\,\nu=1,\,\,\text{Laplace transform}&\\
(1-\alpha \nu)
F\left(1,\frac{\nu}{1-\alpha \nu}\right),\,\,\text{when}\,\,\mu=1,\,\, \text{Elzaki transform}.
\end{cases}

It is evident that for \nu=1, we have the Laplace transform [ref: Electronic Signals and Systems, Macmillan Education UK] and for \mu=1 we have the Elzaki transform [ref: A comparative study of elzaki and laplace transforms to solve ordinary differential equations of first and second order, Journal of Physics: Conference Series] correspondingly.

Scaling property:
Let the function F(\mu,\nu) be the \mathbb J-transform of the function f(t),
and \alpha>0 (\alpha is a nonnegative number). Then, the scaling property is defined as

{\mathbb J}\left[f(\alpha t)\right]=\frac{1}{\alpha}F\left(\frac{\mu}{\alpha},\nu\right).

== Theorems of {\mathbb
J}-transform ==

nth derivatives of the \mathbb J-transform:

Suppose that f{(t)}\inA possesses a {\mathbb J}-transform, and let f^{(n)}(t) denote its nth derivative. Then, the \mathbb J-transform of its nth derivative of f{(t)} is given by:

{\mathbb J}\left[f^{(n)}(t)\right]
=\frac{\mu^n}{\nu^n}F(\mu,\nu)
-\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\frac{\mu^{n-(k+1)}}{\nu^{n-(k+2)}}f^{(k)}(0).

Convolution theorem of {\mathbb
J}-transform:

Let the functions f(t) and g(t) be in set A. Suppose that
F(\mu,\nu) and W(\mu,\nu) denote the respective {\mathbb J}-transforms of function f(t) and g(t). Then, the
convolution theorem for the {\mathbb J}-transform is defined as

{\mathbb
J}\left[(f*g)(t)\right]=\frac{1}{\nu}F(\mu,\nu)W(\mu,\nu),

where f*g is the convolution of two functions f(t) and
g(t) which is defined by

\int _{0 }^{t }f(t)g(t-\alpha)d\alpha=\int _{0 }^{t
}f(t-\alpha)g(\alpha)d\alpha.

OruNewCulture, also known as LiveByONC, is a social community based in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, India, focused on organising art and cultural events in the city. [ref: This youth-led initiative is redefining how Trivandrum engages with culture, IndulgExpress]

OruNewCulture was founded in 2025 by a group of friends following a trip to Bengaluru, where they noticed between the city's nightlife and cultural scene and that of Thiruvananthapuram. [ref: Thiruvananthapuram-based art community, Live by ONC, aims to boost the city’s art culture, The Hindu]

The organization conducts events and community activities through LiveByONC, including music performances, creative workshops, art gatherings and social events. In October 2026, LiveByONC organised NAVRANGA, a Dandiya and Garba event held at the Kerala Arts and Crafts Village in Kovalam, in partnership with Kerala Tourism. [ref: തിരുവനന്തപുരത്തെ ഏറ്റവും വലിയ ഔട്ട്ഡോർ ഡാണ്ടിയ- ഗർബ നൈറ്റ്; 'നവ്‌രംഗ' കേരള ആർട്‌സ് ആൻഡ് ക്രാഫ്റ്റ് വില്ലേജിൽ, Mathrubhumi] According to Onmanorama, the event received around 700+ registrations. data.title: Three-Phase Design Model
data.text:
----

The Three-Phase Design Model (3PD) is an iterative and collaborative model used to support the delivery of online education. [ref: Survey of Instructional Design Models, Association for Educational Communications and Technology] [ref: Continuous Improvement Through Shared Understanding: Reconceptualising Instructional Design for Online Learning, ASCILITE] The model was developed in 2002 by Rod Sims and Deborah Jones. Around the time the 3PD Model was developed, traditional instructional designs were used to facilitate the development and design of online learning resources. There were concerns regarding the use of these traditional approaches due to inconsistencies in catering to the needs of learners and supporting instructors and course developers. The concerns stemmed frrom the need to have flexibility when designing and delivering a course, limited resources available to the academic staff and technological personnel and the need for collaboration among all three.
==The Three- Phase Model Phases==
There are three phases of the 3PD Model. They are Functionality, Enhancement and Maintenance. In each of the phases, scaffolding gives support to learners and academic staff and there is also continuous evaluation throughout the course. The information provided as feedback from both learners and staff is valuable in making decisions to either improve or change any course component if necessary. It is important to note that the hierarchy of roles in the team changes in different phases. [ref: The Design of a Computer-Supported Collaborative Learning Environment that Promotes Interaction, 2014 International Conference on Teaching and Learning in Computing and Engineering (LaTiCE)]

Functionality

The first stage of the model, the Functionality phase, sets the online learning space to one that is operational and can support the teaching and learning regardless of the course not fully complete. [ref: Developing a Challenging Online Doctoral Course Using Backward and Three-Phase Design Models, The Journal of Aviation/Aerospace Education and Research]A functional prototoype is first created. [ref: E-Learning Development in Higher Education: Maximising Efficiency—Maintaining Quality, ERIC (Education Resources Information Center)]This covers the necessary materials and activities needed for the course to begin. The prototypes may include learning objectives, teaching resources such as study guides, unit guides and required reading materials related to topics in the course and instructions given to access these resources.

The model supports collaborative efforts and even though there are different roles and responsibilities of the experts designing and developing the course, there is a partnership to get the inital stages going. To differentiate roles, the team is placed into two groups: the Support Team and the Faculty Team. The Support Team consists of educational designers, interactive architects, and information analysts who contribute to the instructional and technical development of the course. The educational designer plays the major role at this phase and is responsible for curriculum and instructional design guidance and assisting in coordinating teams involved in the development of the course. On the other hand, the Faculty Team is described as content specialists. This is due largely to their expertise in the course content. The members of this team, which include academic staff, develop the objectives of the course, the appraoches and strategies to teach the content and also the types of assessments to be used.

The Model is used through an online space to deliver course content. An hindrance may be the limited experience some instructors may have in using the new technologies. The Support Team gives guidance on how to use the technologies so that the instructors can carry out their roles more efficiently.

Enhancement

The Enhancement Phase takes place while the course is being delivered. The course is monitored and evaluated to see what changes should be made that would be beneficial to the learners and make the course run smoothly. An activity done in this phase called shadowing, assesses the effectiveness of course components. The task is undertaken by members of the development team. Scaffolding is another activity in the phase. Even though technological assistance is offered at the Functionality Phase, it is still offered at the Enhancement Phase to support those instructors who are still experiencing difficulties. There is also support for learners to help to effectively participate in the online learning environment. [ref: In search of an Instructional Material Design Model to Support the Implementation of IQF Oriented Curriculum at HEIs, Advances in Social Science, Education and Humanities Research] Feedback is provided by the instructors and learners. The Enhancement Phase not only make adjustments or fix the problems, but there can be a further expansion of course materials that were developed in the functionality stage.

There are three types of interactions reported in the Enhancement Phase.The interactions are also monitored and evaluated and the purpose is to improve communication and participation while delivering the course. One is the teacher and learner interaction which supports the learners and give answers to questions through discussions and ensuring that the necessary clarifications are given. How learners engage with the tools is also monitored and evaluated. This is to ensure that the materials are accessible and helps with understanding. The other form of interaction is the learners interacting with each other where they can collaborate, exchange ideas and in essence, learn from each other.

Throughout the phase, collaboration continues in order to fix or improve issues with course content, course delivery or technological tools.

Maintenance

The third and final stage of the 3PD Model is the Maintenance Phase. This phase is carried out after the course is delivered and one of its objectives is to prepare the course for future delivery. The feedback given at this phase is to identify the areas that may need further development and to establish if there needs to be changes made to course materials and to fix tecchnical issues. As with all the phases, there is continued involvement from the development team. The Maintenance Phase may continue up to several years to facilitate further development of the course.

==Applications and Adaptations of the 3PD Model==
The 3PD Model has been used in educational projects in Australia and the United States. At the University of New England in Australia in 2008, the 3PD framework was used to transform an existing distance education course in Poultry Production to an online course using Blackboard as the Learning Management System (LMS). Before the model was introduced, there were challenges with attendance. Students were required to attend a compulsory four-day residential session. This was not feasible due to job commitments and geographical distance. Collaborative efforts provided professional development for course instructors.The nine module course became seven modules and practical acivities were done as online exercises. [ref: Poultry production online: Where broilers and layers encounter virtual pedagogy, ASCILITE Publications] At the same institution, the 3PD Model was used to improve distance education in Economics and Public Policy Courses. The university was facing pressures from the demands of distance education and encouraged interaction and collaboration. The project focused on Postgraduate courses but the intentions were to spread this to undergraduate courses. The instructors attended a workshop to discuss what would be done to revamp the course. A decision was made to introduce four new programmes using existing course objectives and discarding units that may no longer serve the course. The course was examined approximately six months later highlight flexilbility and types of assessments as what needed modification. The evaluation of the course reported developments in colaboration between academic staff developers. The 3PD framework was also used to develop an online course offering Advancement Placement opportunities at the Georgia Virtual School in USA. The course was developed using the Desire2Learn Learning Management System.

There were adaptations to the 3PD Model in a few instances. Although the three phases were retained, there were modifications to how the model was applied. An online aviation doctoral programme combined the 3PD Mode. The Functionality phase was combined with the Backward Design and much of the evaluation, enhancement and elaboration was done at the Maintenance Phase. [ref: Developing a Challenging Online Doctoral Course Using Backward and Three-Phase Design Models, Journal of Aviation/Aerospace Education & Research] A study in Malaysia called The Design of a Computer-Supported Collaborative Learning Environment that Promotes Interaction combined interaction design principles with the 3PD process. The 3PD framework was used in a German language programme to develop and the digital learning materials using Adobe Presenter to improve grammar and grammar. Even though all three phases of the 3PD model was retained, additional evaluation stages and procedures were included [ref: Variants of Adobe Presenter E-Learning to Effectively Optimize the Teaching of German Language at Universities in Malang, Indonesian, Research on Humanities and Social Sciences].

==Limitations of the 3PD Model==
The heavy dependence on personnel after the initial stages is a limitation. To support ongoing improvements, the 3PD Model relies on the expertise of these individuals to collaborate and make changes. This may be difficult if an institution has limited staff. There is also the need for continued financial and technological support throughout the lifetime of the course. Supporting course development may be costly as money is needed to fund software maintenance.

One of the strengths of the model is the flexibility it provides in making changes when necessary and not only at the end of the course. This is not always possible due to technological constraints. Depending on the Learning Management System used, there may be restrictions on changing the structure of the course, and some changes may not be applied until after the course has ended. [ref: Informing Online Doctoral Course Development Using Student Feedback, Journal of Online Graduate Education]

The model takes a lot of time to go through all the phases properly. With constant monitoring, providing feedback, collaborating and evaluating the course, the academic staff may find it difficult to complete all tasks and still do their regular duties. Even though student evaluations are done, the results are not analysed and given to instructors and administrators until the course is done. Feedback is therefore not used during the course delivery and may delay the effectiveness of the Enhancement Phase.

data.title: Maheep Purohit
data.text:
Maheep Purohit is an Indian inventor from Bikaner, Rajasthan, associated with the development of the Adaptive Intelligent Pipeline Integrity System (AIPIS), a proposed artificial intelligence-based approach to pipeline monitoring. [ref: Meet the 18-Year-Old Who Patented AI System That Predicts Pipeline Failures, Analytics India Magazine] Indian patent number 594587 for AIPIS was granted on 7 July 2026, with Purohit named as inventor and JJP TECH as patentee. [ref: Patent Certificate: Patent No. 594587, Application No. 202511031293, Intellectual Property India] Analytics India Magazine reported the patent achievement when Purohit was 18 years old.

== Background ==

According to Analytics India Magazine, Purohit began exploring artificial intelligence applications in industrial infrastructure at approximately 15 years of age. The publication reported that he had completed Class 12 by July 2026.

== Adaptive Intelligent Pipeline Integrity System ==

Purohit is named as the inventor of Adaptive Intelligent Pipeline Integrity System (AIPIS) with Contextual Self-Learning Distributed Artificial Intelligence and Hybrid Sensor Arrays for Real-Time Predictive Pipeline Management. Indian patent application 202511031293 was filed on 30 March 2025 and published in The Patent Office Journal on 18 April 2025, with JJP TECH named as applicant. [ref: Adaptive Intelligent Pipeline Integrity System (AIPIS) with Contextual Self-Learning Distributed Artificial Intelligence and Hybrid Sensor Arrays for Real-Time Predictive Pipeline Management, The Patent Office Journal] The patent was granted on 7 July 2026.

AIPIS proposes using hybrid sensor arrays and distributed artificial intelligence to analyse pipeline operating conditions and identify abnormalities that may indicate leaks or developing faults. Its intended applications include pipelines carrying water, petroleum products and industrial fluids.

A report in the Bikaner edition of Dainik Bhaskar on 22 September 2025 discussed the proposed system and its use in monitoring risks associated with the transportation of fluids. [ref: स्टार्टअप: AIPIS से लगेगा तरल पदार्थों के परिवहन खतरों का पूर्वानुमान, Dainik Bhaskar] Journalist Atul Acharya also described AIPIS and its intended industrial applications in a Rajasthan Patrika feature. [ref: रिसाव से पहले आगाह करेगा छात्र का एआई सिस्टम, Rajasthan Patrika]

In July 2026, Analytics India Magazine reported that an AIPIS software prototype incorporated XGBoost for prediction and anomaly detection and included a monitoring dashboard. The publication described controlled testing and plans to seek operational pilot collaborations.

== Other research ==

Purohit authored a preprint titled Epistemic Weight Engine (EWE): A Framework for Signal-Reliability-Weighted Learning in Artificial Neural Systems, with Multi-Dataset Experimental Evaluation, posted on SSRN in March 2026. [ref: Epistemic Weight Engine (EWE): A Framework for Signal-Reliability-Weighted Learning in Artificial Neural Systems, with Multi-Dataset Experimental Evaluation, SSRN] The manuscript proposes an approach to weighting machine-learning training samples according to assessments of information reliability and impact.

data.title: Detention of Nguyen Duc Thuan and Tran Hiep
data.text:
wikitext

The detention of Nguyen Duc Thuan and Tran Hiep refers to the disappearance in Cambodia on 18 September 2026 of two members of the pro-democracy organisation Viet Tan, a Norwegian citizen and an Australian citizen of Vietnamese origin, and their subsequent detention in Vietnam on terrorism charges. Vietnam's Ministry of Public Security (MPS) states that the two men and a third man, Thai Cong Truong Son, were caught entering Vietnam illegally from Cambodia on the night of 18 September. Viet Tan, the men's families and a coalition of human rights organisations say the two were abducted on Cambodian soil and taken across the border, and describe the case as an act of transnational repression. The Cambodian government has denied any role in arresting or handing over the men.

== Background ==
Viet Tan is a pro-democracy organisation with members in Vietnam and in overseas Vietnamese communities, organised in local chapters under a central committee. News reports commonly describe it as US-based. The Vietnamese government has listed it as a terrorist organisation since 2016, and Vietnamese state media state that participation in or support for the group is treated as complicity in terrorism.

Human rights groups have documented earlier cases in which Vietnamese critics abroad were seized or returned to Vietnam, including the 2017 abduction of former official Trinh Xuan Thanh in Berlin, the 2019 seizure of blogger Truong Duy Nhat in Thailand, and the 2023 abduction of blogger Duong Van Thai from Thailand. Viet Tan's executive director said he believed this was the first case of a person holding non-Vietnamese citizenship being taken from outside Vietnam over their political activities.

== People detained ==
=== Nguyen Duc Thuan ===
Nguyen Duc Thuan (; born 1974) is a Norwegian citizen and pharmacist living in Oslo. Born in Vietnam, he moved to Norway in 1989. Some reports render his name as "Nguyen Thuan Duc". While a student he served as president of the University of Oslo Student Association and organised activities on Vietnamese history and culture.

According to Viet Tan, Thuan works with Norwegian and European parliamentarians and human rights organisations to promote democracy and human rights in Vietnam, and supports activists inside the country. In June 2025 he took part in a meeting on human rights in Vietnam between Viet Tan's president and Norway's Minister of International Development, Åsmund Aukrust. His family says he has campaigned with Norwegian officials for the release of political prisoners, and he is active in Norway's Catholic community on religious freedom in Vietnam.

His family says he is diabetic with a documented need for daily insulin injections, and that the diabetes tablets he has been given in custody do not meet that need.

=== Tran Hiep ===
Tran Hiep, also known as Ho Pham Hiep Huy (; born 1975), is an Australian citizen and IT professional living in Melbourne. Vietnamese authorities charged him under the name Ho Pham Hiep Huy; his Australian passport is in the name Tran Hiep.

At university he became involved in the Vietnamese Students Association in Victoria. He later worked on youth welfare through the Em Viet group, and helped launch the Australian Alliance to Combat Human Trafficking (AusACT), which campaigned against the trafficking of young Vietnamese girls to neighbouring countries. According to Viet Tan, he has provided digital-security training to human rights activists.

=== Thai Cong Truong Son ===
Thai Cong Truong Son (; born 1980) is a Vietnamese activist living in Cambodia, described by rights groups as a human rights defender.

== Disappearance in Cambodia ==
According to Cambodian immigration records, Thuan and Hiep flew into Cambodia from Thailand on 15 September 2026, arriving at Techo International Airport; no departure was recorded for either man. Their families say they travelled to Phnom Penh to meet Vietnamese human rights activists. Viet Tan said they were scheduled to leave Cambodia on 19 September.

Viet Tan states that the two went missing on the morning of 18 September while travelling to the Kaoh Andaet area near the Vietnamese border. Hiep did not board his return flight to Bangkok the following day. The families lost contact with both men on 18 September and filed an appeal with the UN Working Group on Enforced or Involuntary Disappearances. The Australian embassy asked Cambodian police to intervene on 22 September.

== Vietnamese account and charges ==
On 28 September, the MPS announced that the border guard post at the My Quy Tay border gate in Tây Ninh province had caught the three men entering Vietnam illegally from Cambodia at 21:50 on 18 September. According to the ministry, Thuan was carrying a Norwegian passport and two forged Vietnamese citizen identity cards bearing his photograph under the name Phan Duc Trung, while Hiep carried his Australian passport. The men were handed to the Tay Ninh provincial security investigation agency on 19 September and later transferred to the MPS Security Investigation Agency.

The ministry said the three had admitted to being Viet Tan members who entered Vietnam with false documents to carry out terrorist and sabotage activities. On 28 September the MPS Security Investigation Agency formally opened a case, charged the three, and ordered their detention for terrorism under Article 299(2) and forging seals or documents under Article 341(2) of the Penal Code; the Supreme People's Procuracy approved the charges and detention orders the same day. Article 299(2) carries a sentence of five to fifteen years' imprisonment, and Article 341(2) two to five years.

Viet Tan rejected the ministry's account as a fabrication, saying the men had no intention of entering Vietnam.

== Cambodian response ==
In a statement on 7 October 2026, Cambodia's Ministry of Interior said Cambodian authorities had not arrested the men or handed them to Vietnam. The statement presented the immigration records and the information received from Vietnam as the results of the police search opened at the Australian embassy's request.

== Detention and consular access ==
According to the Australian Associated Press, Hiep is held at the Ministry of Public Security's B34 detention centre in Ho Chi Minh City, a facility used for political prisoners. TV 2 reported that Thuan is held at the same facility. Vietnamese authorities had not publicly disclosed where the men were held. Consular correspondence sent to Hiep's wife stated that he was in good health and detained under local regulations.

As of 11 October, neither the Norwegian nor the Australian embassy had been granted consular access, according to Human Rights Watch.

Australian consular officials visited Hiep at the B34 detention centre on 15 October. Prison officials warned the consular staff that they would be removed if they discussed topics the authorities had not approved. Through the officials, Hiep sent his family a message saying "I never entered Vietnam on my own" and that he had not crossed the border. His wife said officials described him as fearful, in a fragile mental state and suffering from erratic blood pressure. According to the ABC, Vietnamese authorities had not yet given Hiep the details of the charges against him.

On 16 October, staff from the Norwegian embassy in Hanoi made their first consular visit to Thuan. According to the embassy's report of the visit, obtained by TV 2, Thuan appeared physically in good health but was sleeping poorly, had slightly elevated blood sugar, and was being given diabetes medication in tablet form rather than the insulin injections he requires. The report also stated that Thuan would not receive legal assistance until the investigation was completed, which the embassy said it had not been told before. Vietnamese police can extend such investigations in four-month periods for up to two years, according to TV 2. Norwegian authorities had learned where Thuan was being held only on 7 October. His lawyer said the consular visit was monitored, that permitted topics had been set in advance and that Thuan was not allowed to speak in his native language. She also said she had not been able to speak with her client, and that she had no confidence in the confession Vietnamese authorities say he made.

== Reactions ==
=== Governments ===
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the government was providing consular assistance and engaging with Hiep's family, and the office of Foreign Minister Penny Wong said the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade was making urgent inquiries with Vietnamese authorities. Wong later said she had made representations on the case, citing privacy reasons for not giving further detail. Norway's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said it was taking the case "very seriously" and expected regular consular access, legal assistance and proper medical follow-up for Thuan. State Secretary Astrid Bergmål raised the case "at a high level" in meetings with Vietnamese authorities during a visit to Vietnam in October, on which she was due to sign a free trade agreement between Vietnam and the EFTA states.

The Vietnamese embassy in Canberra described the abduction allegations as "unfounded and misleading".

=== Families ===
Hiep's wife called on the Australian government to secure his return. Thuan's brother told Dagbladet that the family was relieved he was alive but expected a long effort to free him, with his medical care the immediate priority. Thuan's family retained the Norwegian law firm Elden and reported Vietnam and Cambodia to Norwegian police for kidnapping and enforced disappearance. Their lawyer, Maria Hessen Jacobsen, said Vietnamese authorities must have been involved in moving the men from Cambodia to Vietnam. She said Norway should not accept another country abducting its citizens, and called on the government to bring Thuan home rather than return from Vietnam with only a trade agreement.

=== Human rights organisations ===
On 1 October, the Vietnam Human Rights Network and Defend the Defenders called for the release of the three men and said they believed Thuan and Hiep had been abducted by Vietnamese security forces. On 7 October, 34 organisations including Freedom House, Article 19, Index on Censorship and the Cambodian Center for Human Rights issued a joint statement calling for the men's unconditional release and for immediate consular access, arguing that the ten-day period in which they were held incommunicado breached Vietnam's obligations under the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations. The statement also called on Vietnam to guarantee Thuan's access to insulin. On 13 October, Human Rights Watch called for the three men's release and for immediate consular and family access; its Asia director, Elaine Pearson, said that "campaigning for democracy and pluralism is not a crime".

=== Vietnamese state media ===
A commentary in the MPS newspaper Công An Nhân Dân, republished by provincial media, rejected the description of the case as transnational repression, arguing that the term has no standing in international law and that the arrests were lawful.

== See also ==

* Transnational repression

data.title: Applaydu
data.text:
Applaydu is a free mobile application developed by Gameloft for Ferrero's Kinder brand, released in August 2020 for iOS and Android. The app targets children aged 4 to 9 and their parents, and includes games, storytelling tools, and augmented reality features. Additionally, Kinder toys can be scanned via the device camera to access additional digital content. [ref: Gameloft on bringing Kinder Surprise toys to life with AR, The Drum] [ref: Kinder partners with Gameloft to develop Applaydu – a new AR app for kids, ARVRNews]

==History==

Applaydu was launched in August 2020 as a joint project between Gameloft and Kinder. [ref: Digital: Kinder and Gameloft launch Applaydu – augmented reality app to bring toys to life, adobo Magazine] [ref: Kinder Joy to launch Applaydu app to help children develop cognitive skills, exchange4media] The initial release included augmented reality integration with Kinder toys; subsequent versions added new games, themed areas, and storytelling content. [ref: How Kinder took its toy-building experience digital, The Drum] [ref: Kinder Surprise eggs have entered the digital realm with Applaydu, Pocket Gamer]

==Features==

The app includes mini-games, story creation and exploration tools, and avatar customisation. Common Sense Media described it as an app that "looks great and encourages family interaction", while noting it is "more fun than educational". [ref: Applaydu family games App Review, Common Sense Media] Some content is accessible offline; other features require an internet connection. The app does not include advertising or in-app purchases, and includes a parental controls section allowing caregivers to monitor usage and manage screen time. [ref: Applaydu – kidSAFE Certified, kidSAFE Seal Program] Applaydu holds certification from the kidSAFE Seal Program.

==Educational approach==

Applaydu has been described as an edutainment application. [ref: Applaydu, Educational App Store] The app has been part of the Learning in Families through Technology (LiFT) research project at the Department of Education, University of Oxford, which studies the use of digital technologies by children and families, with a focus on language development, creativity, and parent–child interaction. [ref: LiFT: Learning in Families through Technology, University of Oxford, Department of Education]

==Distribution==

Applaydu is available on the Apple App Store and Google Play, and is supported in 19 languages. [ref: Applaydu – Play & Discover on the App Store, Apple] [ref: Applaydu Play & Discover, Google Play] The app has also received the Parents' Picks Award.

data.title: Paige Plaisance
data.text:
Paige Plaisance is an American singer, songwriter and pianist based in Austin, Texas. She describes her music as "swampytonkin'", a blend of Texas two-step and classic country with blues and soul influences. Her second album, Swampwater (2026), produced by Jonathan Tyler, reached number 16 on the Americana Music Association's Americana Radio Airplay albums chart.

== Early life ==
Plaisance was raised in rural northeast Louisiana, on a farm near the Mississippi River where her father farmed. She writes her songs at the piano. She moved to Austin in 2014.

== Career ==
Plaisance performs regularly at the Austin venues Sagebrush, the White Horse and the Continental Club. She has shared stages with Nikki Lane, Reckless Kelly, Noeline Hofmann and The Band of Heathens. She also runs Ramblin' Rose Co., a vintage clothing trailer behind Sagebrush, and organizes and hosts the Honkytonk Catwalk, a recurring fashion show at the venue.

Her 2022 EP, Different Now, introduced her "swampy-tonk" sound. In 2023 she released the single "Good Time Girl", produced by Jonathan Tyler at Clyde's VIP Room in Austin, with a music video directed by Dan Brown. Her first full-length album, Louisiana Lonely, followed in August 2024. Saving Country Music rated it 8 out of 10, and the album reached the top 20 on Americana radio.

In August 2026, Austin public radio station KUTX named Plaisance its Artist of the Month. Her second album, Swampwater, was recorded at the Finishing School in Austin with her band, the Yeah You Right Boys, and produced by Tyler. It was released in September 2026, with a release show at Antone's. Saving Country Music rated it 8.1 out of 10, and North Carolina public radio station WNCW placed it in heavy rotation. In October 2026 the album reached number 16 on the Americana Radio Airplay albums chart, and its opening track, "Make Mine Country", reached number 34 on the corresponding singles chart.

== Band ==
Plaisance performs and records with her band, the Yeah You Right Boys.
Members of the Yeah You Right Boys credited on Swampwater include: [ref: Swampwater, Timeless Echo Recordings]
* Bryan McGrath: drums
* Marshall Hood: guitar
* Drew Scherger: bass
* Stuart Owens: fiddle
* Nick Hamburg: pedal steel guitar
== Discography ==
=== Studio albums ===
* Louisiana Lonely (2024)
* Swampwater (2026)

data.title: Pickleball Smash
data.text:
Pickleball Smash is a cooperative sports arcade video game developed by 1PXL Games and published by GameMill Entertainment. Despite the poor reviews, it was released on October 24, 2023 through Windows, Playstation 4, Playstation 5, Xbox One and Xbox Series X/S, and later on Nintendo Switch in November 7. [ref: https://www.thexboxhub.com/pickleball-smash-is-on-xbox-playstation-switch-and-pc/]

==Gameplay==
Pickleball Smash defines the Pickleball sport in a stylized game for up to 4 players in two teams via two players each. Players will customize their avatars and compete head to head in Pickleball tourmentants at various locations from the beach to the arctic. The game also freatures minigames that will allow the player to the core sport with surprising mechanics. [ref: Pickleball Smash, xbox.com]

==Development and release==
On July 2023, it was announced by GameMill that they will be publishing a new sports game Pickleball Smash on all consoles, and planned to release it later this year on October 24. [ref: https://bleedingcool.com/games/pickleball-smash-announced-for-both-pc-consoles/] [ref: https://butwhytho.net/2023/07/pickleball-smash-announced/] A Nintendo Switch version with motion controls was later released on November 7.

==Reception==
In a review from WayTooManyGames, Leo Faria wrote, "It’s not broken or glitchy, but it’s still incredibly boring. There is no reason to grab this over any other racket-based sports game, even if you, somehow, prefer pickleball over tennis." [ref: Review – Pickleball Smash, WayTooManyGames]

data.title: Ipe Akoko
data.text:
Ipe-Akoko (historically called Ukue, Ukpe, or Uqwe) is a town in the Akoko South-East Local Government Area of Ondo State, Nigeria. [ref: Social and Economic Development of Akoko Society under Colonial Rule, West Bohemian Historical Review]

== History ==
Oral tradition states that the people of Ipe-Akoko migrated from Ife. During early regional conflicts, the community moved to a rocky hill called Uloke for protection. [ref: Inter-Group Relations in Akoko, 1800–1960, Ibadan University Press]

After the conflicts ended, residents moved back down to the flat land. The Ibà quarter descended first. This relocation was completed by around 1928, but colonial administrative files and early church records show the town was already established long before. [ref: National Archives Ibadan (NAI), Colonial Secretary's Office (CSO) Files on Akoko District Assessment Reports (1910–1930).] [ref: The History of Evangelism and Church Growth in Akoko, Ondo State, Journal of Religion in Africa] The Uloke stone site still exists in the town layout.

== Monarchy ==
The king of Ipe-Akoko is known as the Olupe of Ipe-Akoko. Local tradition names Oba Ajagbi as the first king. The current ruler is Oba Ajiyinrere Francis Makanjuola Apata JP (Arogunbola II).

The monarchy rotates among several royal families across the town quarters:
* Abamido (Ibà quarter)
* Odepo (Ibà quarter)
* Odovie Ute (Igbede quarter)

== Quarters ==
The town contains 11 traditional quarters: Ibà-Ute, Ibà-Peju, Okun, Isinodo, Ilegbe, Igbede, Ugbe, Itoto, Ipaso, Uwi, and Uthakpe.

== Language and Culture ==
The native name of the town and its people is Ukue. Over time, neighboring communities began referring to the settlement as Ipe.

The indigenous language is Ukue (also referred to as Ipe), which belongs to the Edoid language family. [ref: Comparative Edoid: Phonology and Lexicon, University of Port Harcourt Press] Linguistic studies on the Ipe language demonstrate historical vocabulary contact and borrowing with English, Yoruba, and Edo. [ref: Aspect of Borrowing in the Ipe and Yoruba Languages, EBSU Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities] Most residents are also fluent in Yoruba. Cultural events in the town include the Chegba festival, which features traditional rites and virginity dances (*Uge*), alongside the Uheni, Ella, and Opara festivals. [ref: Chegba festival: Ipe-Akoko showcases widest beans cake, The Hope Newspaper]

== Infrastructure ==

=== Healthcare ===
* General Hospital, Ipe-Akoko: A public secondary medical facility in Ibà quarter, established in 1979. [ref: Healthcare and Community Development in Ondo State, Tribune Online] [ref: General Hospital Ipe Akoko - Healthcare Services Directory, Medpages]
* Igbede Primary Health Care Centre: A local public health clinic serving Igbede quarter.

=== Education ===
* Ipe High School: A public secondary school established in September 1976.
* Olawale International Model Secondary School: A private secondary institution.
* Dynamic Excellent College: A private secondary school operating as a regional examination centre.

== Notable People ==
* Prof. Olanrewaju Olu-Adeyemi – Professor of Political Science at Adekunle Ajasin University.

data.title: Hamlet Ghazaryan
data.text:
Hamlet Ghazaryan (Armenian: Համլետ Ղազարյան; born 2 June 1994) is an Armenian actor, voice actor, radio presenter and poet.

== Early life and education ==

Ghazaryan was born on 2 June 1994 in Salut, Shirak Province, Armenia. In 2008, he moved with his family to Gyumri, where he attended Mesrop Mashtots School No. 29. In 2012, he entered the Gyumri branch of the Yerevan State Institute of Theatre and Cinematography, graduating in 2016. He subsequently moved to Yerevan and pursued work in theatre, film and television.

== Career ==

=== Theatre ===

Ghazaryan has performed in Armenian theatre. His stage roles include Mesrop in a production of Mesrop Mashtots, directed by Hovhannes Hovhannisyan, and Edmund in a production of William Shakespeare's King Lear, directed by Artur Sahakyan.

In September 2025, Ghazaryan portrayed Armenian poet Yeghishe Charents in Charents, a production directed by Davit Harutyunyan at the Hovhannes Abelian Vanadzor State Drama Theatre. The production was based on Valery Piloyan's play The Last Night of Charents. [ref: «Չարենցը»՝ վանաձորյան բեմում․ բացվել է քաղաքի թատրոնի 94-րդ թատերաշրջանը, Armenian Public Radio] [ref: «Ես լուծում չեմ տվել․ ուղղակի ասել եմ՝ այսպիսի բաներ կային ու հիմա էլ շորշոփները երևում են»․ «Չարենց»-ը՝ Վանաձորի թատրոնի բեմում, Aravot]

Tert.am published an interview with Ghazaryan in which he discussed the responsibility of portraying Charents and his preparation for the role. [ref: «Չարենցին մարմնավորելը մեծ պատիվ, բայց նաև լուրջ պատասխանատվություն է». Համլետ Ղազարյան, Tert.am]

==== Portrayal of Yeghishe Charents ====

A review published by Theatrical Points examined the production's interpretation of Charents and Ghazaryan's performance. The critic discussed the actor's restrained portrayal and the production's emphasis on the historical circumstances surrounding the poet, rather than relying primarily on familiar theatrical mannerisms. [ref: Չարենցից դուրս Չարենցի հետ, Theatrical Points]

Ghazaryan has performed in Armenian theatre. His stage roles include Mesrop in a production of Mesrop Mashtots, directed by Hovhannes Hovhannisyan, and Edmund in a production of William Shakespeare's King Lear, directed by Artur Sahakyan.

He portrayed Armenian poet Yeghishe Charents in the play Charents, directed by Davit Harutyunyan and staged at the Hovhannes Abelian Vanadzor State Drama Theatre. The production was based on Valery Piloyan's play The Last Night of Charents. [ref: «Չարենցին մարմնավորելը մեծ պատիվ, բայց նաև լուրջ պատասխանատվություն է». Համլետ Ղազարյան, Tert.am]

=== Film and television ===

Ghazaryan has appeared in Armenian films and television series. His television roles include Vahe in Open Your Eyes, Bakh in Burned Dreams, Vardan in More Than Honor, Mayis in Flowers Under the Snow, Narek in Special Class and Special Class 2, and Hamik in The Mountains Will Remember.

In an interview published by Showbiz.am in February 2021, Ghazaryan discussed his portrayal of the younger Mayis in Flowers Under the Snow and his work on More Than Honor. [ref: Շատերը մի քանի րոպե էկրաններին երևալուց հետո մտածում են այլևս քասթինգների չմասնակցել ու սպասել հրավերի․ Համլետ Ղազարյանը՝ «Ծաղիկներ ձյան տակ» սերիալում իր դերի մասին, Showbiz.am]

In 2018, Ghazaryan appeared in Hamlet Jan, an alternative drama inspired by William Shakespeare's tragedy Hamlet. The film explores the experience of an actor attempting to portray Hamlet on the stage of an abandoned theatre, interweaving theatrical scenes with reflections on contemporary life and social change. [ref: Համլետ [ ջան ], Hetq.am]

In 2020, Ghazaryan appeared in the short film Happy Bday 2U, as reported by Showbiz.am. [ref: Բռնություն, էրոտիկա․ «HAPPY BDAY 2U» 18+ ֆիլմի մանրամասներն ու զավեշտալի դեպքերը նկարահանման հրապարակից, Showbiz.am]

== Radio and voice acting ==

Ghazaryan began his broadcasting career at Shirak Public Radio and Television, where he worked from 2013 to 2016 as a programme creator, scriptwriter and presenter. His programmes included Fstatus, Shiraki Aravoty, Heqiat Papik and Bari Aravot Shirak.

From 2016 to 2025, he worked at Europe Plus as a programme creator, scriptwriter and presenter, contributing to the programme Euroformat.

Alongside his broadcasting career, Ghazaryan has established himself as a voice actor specialising in commercial voice-over and dubbing. His voice has been featured in numerous advertising campaigns in Armenia, and he has voiced dozens of television series for Shant TV.

== Poetry ==

Ghazaryan also writes poetry.

data.title: Slana noć - običaj
data.text:
----

Slana noć (u etnološkoj literaturi i ostavljanje trpeze za neprispelog) je narodni običaj zabeležen u zaseoku Branovići pod Zlatiborom, u zapadnoj Srbiji. Obeležava se najduže noći u godini, 21. decembra, postavljanjem tanjira sa solju i dva grozda grožđa za „onoga ko nije stigao“, čije se ime ne izgovara. [ref: Lukić, Nenad (2019). Zimski običaji Starog Vlaha.]

== Poreklo ==
Prema predanju koje se prenosi uglavnom usmeno, običaj potiče iz zime sredinom 19. veka, kada je mladić iz sela krenuo u dolinu po grožđe za porodičnu slavu, a zatim nestao u mećavi. Telo nikada nije pronađeno. Njegova majka je svake godine najduže noći postavljala tanjir za njega, a posle njene smrti običaj su preuzele komšinice, a potom i celo selo.

Najraniji pisani pomen potiče iz 1887. godine, iz izveštaja seoskog učitelja okružnom načelstvu, u kom se pominje običaj ostavljanja soli i grožđa „za mrtvog koji se ne pominje“. [ref: Izveštaj učitelja iz Branovića, 1887. (izmišljen izvor)] Prema etnologu Nenadu Lukiću, verovanja o hrani za pretke rasprostranjena su na Balkanu, ali kombinacija soli, grožđa i nepominjanja imena nije zabeležena nigde drugde.

Prema predanju meštana, selo je ime dobilo po onima koji su „branili kuću dok se on ne vrati“.

== Obred ==
Tanjir postavlja najstariji član domaćinstva. Tanjir se ne dira do jutra, a vrata se te noći ne zaključavaju. S obzirom na to da Zlatibor nije vinogradarski kraj, grožđe se bere u septembru u dolini i čuva na tavanu, okačeno o gredu i umotano u platno, do decembra.

=== Jutarnje tumačenje ===
Pre doručka domaćin pregleda i tumači tanjir:

* suva so označava mirnu godinu, a ovlažena da je gost „plakao“ i da neko u kući treba da se pomiri s nekim pre proleća;
* od dva grozda, jedan pripada neprispelom, a drugi domaćin veče pre namenjuje jednom ukućaninu; ako je ujutru taj grozd više uveo od prvog, veruje se da će ta osoba tokom godine otići, bilo da otputuje ili premine;
* ako s grozdova ne nedostaje nijedna boba, to se smatra lošim znakom.

Sadržaj tanjira se ne baca i ne jede, već ga domaćin odnosi do raskršća i ostavlja na kamenu. Na povratku je zabranjeno osvrtati se.

== Savremeno stanje ==
Krajem 20. veka običaj je gotovo nestao. U zimu 2025, prvi put posle četrdesetak godina, ponovo je obeležen u svim naseljenim domaćinstvima zaseoka (9 od 23), a meštani pripremaju inicijativu za upis u nacionalni registar nematerijalnog kulturnog nasleđa. [ref: „Slana noć u Branovićima“, magazin o kulturi, 2026. (izmišljen izvor)]

Deo meštana okolnih sela dovodi u pitanje autentičnost običaja i smatra da je nastao u 20. veku.

data.title: Anime Impulse
data.text:
Anime Impulse is an American multi-city fan convention focused on Japanese anime, manga, video games, cosplay, and popular culture. Established in 2016, the convention is organized by Impulse Universe, an event management company that also operates [https://www.impulseuniverse.com/collectors-expo K-PLAY! FEST] and [https://www.impulseuniverse.com/collectors-expo Collectors Expo]. [ref: IMPULSE UNIVERSE, IMPULSE UNIVERSE]

Originally launched alongside the [https://aaexpo.com/ Asian American Expo] in Pomona, California, Anime Impulse has expanded into a series of conventions held across the United States, including events in California, Arizona, Texas, and Washington. [ref: ]

Anime Impulse features appearances by voice actors, content creators, cosplayers, and other entertainment personalities, alongside artist exhibitions, merchandise vendors, live performances, panel discussions, and interactive fan programming. [ref: Program Rundown, ANIME Impulse] [ref: ] At co-located events, admission also provides access to other Impulse Universe conventions, connecting anime fandom with Korean pop culture, gaming, and collectibles.

== History ==

=== Founding and Early Development (2016–2020) ===
Anime Impulse debuted on January 16–17, 2016, at the Fairplex in Pomona, California, as part of the 35th annual Asian American Expo. [ref: Asian-American Expo returns to Pomona with some new additions, Daily Bulletin]

The convention was established to introduce anime, manga, video games, and cosplay programming to a broader audience within the existing Asian American Expo. Its inaugural event featured appearances by internationally recognized cosplayers Alodia Gosiengfiao, Ashley Gosiengfiao, and VampyBitMe. [ref: Anime Impulse 2016 Information, AnimeCons.com.]

Convention producer Kaila Yu described the co-location arrangement as a distinguishing feature, allowing attendees to experience anime-related programming alongside the food vendors and cultural attractions offered through the larger exposition.

The convention's organizers also emphasized accessibility to casual anime fans, describing an environment designed for visitors who enjoyed Japanese popular culture without necessarily identifying as dedicated convention attendees.

=== Expansion and Diversification (2022–present) ===
Following its early years in Pomona, Anime Impulse expanded its event programming and geographic presence.

Impulse Universe introduced K-Play! Fest in 2022, expanding its convention portfolio into Korean popular music and entertainment. [ref: K-PLAY! Fest 2022 to Host Flagship Event at The Pomona Fairplex, K-Pop Concerts] Collectors Expo subsequently contributed a focus on trading cards, collectibles, and related hobbies.

In 2024, Impulse Universe expanded its convention operations beyond California, holding events in the Seattle [ref: Anime Impulse Seattle 2024 Information, AnimeCons.com] and Phoenix [ref: Anime Impulse Phoenix 2024 Information, AnimeCons.com] markets.

The expansion continued into Texas, with Anime Impulse Dallas held at the Kay Bailey Hutchison Convention Center on November 15–16, 2025. [ref: Anime Impulse Dallas 2025 Information, AnimeCons.com]

== Convention Programming ==
Anime Impulse organizes a range of activities centered on anime, gaming, cosplay, and fan communities.

Programming includes voice actor autograph sessions and meet-and-greets, celebrity panels, cosplay gatherings and competitions, live performances, artist exhibitions, and vendor marketplaces.

The convention has also incorporated virtual entertainers, including VTubers, into its guest programming. Gaming-related activities and appearances connect the event with audiences of Japanese role-playing games, online games, and other interactive entertainment. [ref: ]

=== Programming and Entertainment ===
Anime Impulse features programming related to Japanese animation, video games, cosplay, music, and online entertainment. Events typically include voice actor autograph sessions, guest panels, live performances, artist exhibitions, merchandise vendors, cosplay competitions, and organized fan gatherings.

Additional attractions have included gaming tournaments, free-play arcade areas, customized Japanese automobiles known as itasha, [ref: ] and interactive exhibitions organized in collaboration with entertainment companies.

=== Musical Performances ===
Anime Impulse has hosted musical performers associated with Japanese animation and video game soundtracks, including the Japanese rock band BURNOUT SYNDROMES, known for songs featured in Haikyu!! and other anime series. [ref: Anime Impulse Dallas 2025 Information, AnimeCons.com]

Music programming also takes place through the co-located K-PLAY! FEST, which focuses on Korean popular music and culture. Its featured performers have included South Korean artists Lee Young-ji, Sik-K, and pH-1, [ref: Previous Events, K-PLAY! FEST] as well as Japanese rapper and music producer Lotus Juice. [ref: Lotus Juice Information, AnimeCons.com]

=== VTuber and Digital Creator Appearances ===
Virtual YouTubers, commonly known as VTubers, have become a recurring component of ANIME Impulse programming. The convention has collaborated with VTuber agencies including NIJISANJI EN and hololive, featuring virtual entertainers through meet-and-greet sessions, panels, and live performances. [ref: ] [ref: ]

Featured VTubers have included Luca Kaneshiro, [ref: Instagram, www.instagram.com] Uki Violeta, [ref: Instagram, www.instagram.com] Alban Knox, [ref: Instagram, www.instagram.com] Elira Pendora, and other members of NIJISANJI EN. [ref: Instagram, www.instagram.com]

In July 2026, VTuber and musician Ironmouse performed her Club Ironmouse concert at ANIME Impulse Bay Area, held at the Santa Clara Convention Center. [ref: Instagram, www.instagram.com]

The convention has also hosted digital creators, streamers, and online personalities, including Emirichu, Daidus, [ref: ANIME Impulse Ends 2023 in OC!, The Game of Nerds] The Anime Man, and CDawgVA. [ref: CDAWG Coming to an ANIME Impulse near you this August!, ANIME Impulse]

=== Gaming and Interactive Entertainment ===
Gaming-related programming at ANIME Impulse has included interactive exhibitions, arcade areas, tournaments, and promotional activities associated with video game publishers and developers.

The convention has worked with companies and franchises including HoYoverse, SEGA, Square Enix, Devsisters, and Goddess of Victory: Nikke.

Collaborations involving HoYoverse titles have included programming associated with Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail, and Zenless Zone Zero. For the Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.6 update, "Angels of Delusion," ANIME Impulse supported promotional activities featuring themed exhibits, merchandise, and food and beverage collaborations.

Other programming has featured CookieRun: Kingdom, Sonic the Hedgehog, and Star Ocean.

=== Industry Partnerships and Collaborations ===
Anime Impulse has worked with companies across the automotive, telecommunications, gaming, publishing, food and beverage, and consumer products industries.

Organizations identified in its convention sponsorship and partnership materials include Toyota Motor North America, Verizon, AT&T, Bandai Namco, SEGA, HoYoverse, Square Enix, McDonald's, and Kinokuniya.

=== Toyota and Automotive Collaborations ===
Toyota Motor North America and Toyota Gazoo Racing have participated in multi-event collaborations with ANIME Impulse.

These included promotional activities related to Toyota's original anime series GRIP, alongside displays of Toyota GR vehicles such as the GR86, GR Supra, and GR Corolla.

Automotive programming at Anime Impulse has also featured itasha exhibitions, showcasing vehicles decorated with anime and video game characters.

=== Merchandise and Collectibles ===
Anime Impulse has developed exclusive merchandise in collaboration with entertainment brands and licensors, including character-themed collectible cards, acrylic accessories, apparel, and other limited-edition products.

Its collaborations have included VTuber-themed merchandise featuring Nijisanji En talents. [ref: NIJISANJI EN — Anime Impulse Orange County - Vtuber Meet & Greets, ANIME Impulse]

Collectors Expo, a separate convention operated by Impulse Universe, complements Anime Impulse programming with trading cards, figures, collectibles, and related exhibitors [ref: Collectors Expo, Collectors Expo].

=== Co-located Conventions ===
Anime Impulse operates alongside other events produced by Impulse Universe, including K-Play! Fest and Collectors Expo.

The co-location model allows attendees to access multiple themed conventions at the same venue through a shared admission ticket, bringing together audiences interested in anime, Korean popular music, gaming, trading cards, and collectibles. [ref: Instagram, www.instagram.com]

== Convention Locations ==
Anime Impulse has organized conventions in several United States markets, including:

* Los Angeles area: Pomona, California
* Orange County: California
* Bay Area: Northern California
* Seattle area: Washington
* Phoenix area: Arizona
* Dallas: Texas

data.title: Dave Maris
data.text:
David Maris is a Canadian artist whose painting "Truth and Reconciliation" represents Canada at the United Nations Office at Geneva.

Maris' painting is the only piece of permanent art that represents Canada at the Geneva offices of the United Nations. His painting was recommended for donation to the United Nations by Grand Chief Willie Littlechild, the Commissioner of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada. The painting was donated at an event organized by the Permanent Representative of Canada to the United Nations. [ref: Art Donation “TRUTH AND RECONCILIATION”, The United Nations Office at Geneva] His art was unveiled in September 2017, on the 150th anniversary of Canada, [ref: Blenheim artist has piece installed in the UN, Chatham Voice] and the tenth anniversary of the signing of the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples. [ref: Bancroft artist featured by UN, Bancroft This Week] At the unveiling of his art in Geneva, Michael Møller's spokesperson said that Maris was "known to be outspoken for the rights of indigenous people in Canada." In 2023, the painting was displayed in a corridor linking and old and new buildings at the United Nation's offices in Geneva. [ref: Hannah Entwisle Chapuisat, [https://ualresearchonline.arts.ac.uk/id/eprint/22422/2/Entwisle%20Chapuisat%20Thesis%20%28FINAL%29%20%2811%20July%202024%29.pdf Policy-Oriented Art: Developing Disaster Displacement Norms in Diplomatic Venues], Chelsea College of Arts, 2023, page 170]

In November 2015, [ref: CAROL FEENEY: Art in Picton, The Intelligencer (Belleville)] Maris' art was featured in the "Consensual Discomfort" exhibit in the Art Gallery of Bancroft. In 2016, Maris' art was displayed at Blenheim United Church before being transported for exhibit in Switzerland. His exhibit "Flags" featured paintings that represented individual Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women. [ref: Artist, United Church team up to fight injustice, Chatham Voice] Maris' art was featured in a 2016 exhibit at the Palais des Nations in Geneva, documenting violence against Indigenous women and girls. The 2016 exhibit occurred during the 33rd session of the United Nations Human Rights Council. In 2024, his art was featured at the Stories of Peace award ceremony. [ref: Stories of Peace Award 2024 handed out Sept. 24, The Hamilton Spectator]

Maris has lived in Blenheim, Ontario, in Bancroft, Ontario, and in Switzerland.
