data.title: Kevin J. Dunlap
data.text:
----

Kevin J. Dunlap (born November 15, 1959) is an American software engineer and inventor. In 1985, while at Digital Equipment Corporation (DEC), he substantially revised the early BIND (Berkeley Internet Name Domain) DNS implementation, building on the first Unix name server written at UC Berkeley the year before. In 1986 he co-authored a paper on his experiences implementing [ref: Experiences Implementing BIND, A Distributed Name Server for the DARPA Internet] it and wrote the "Name Server Operations Guide for BIND" [ref: Name Server Operations Guide for BIND (SMM:11), University of California, Berkeley] distributed with 4.3BSD. He also co-authored "Development of the Domain Name System" (1988) [ref: Development of the Domain Name System, Association for Computing Machinery] with Paul Mockapetris, which received an ACM SIGCOMM Test of Time Paper Award in 2006 [ref: ACM SIGCOMM Test of Time Award, sigcomm], and he holds a on a reduced-broadcast variant of the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP).
In 1993, the USENIX Association gave a Lifetime Achievement Award (Flame) [ref: USENIX Flame Award, USENIX]
to the Computer Systems Research Group at University of California, Berkeley, honoring 180 individuals, including Dunlap, who listed as a major contributor to the CSRG's 4.3BSD release. He later worked on commercial DNS products and took part in IETF DNS standards work, and his career since
has spanned telecommunications, digital video and railroad communications software.

== Education and Training ==

While attending Eastport, New York High School, Dunlap learned how to program BASIC & MACRO-10 on a DEC PDP-10 at Long Island Regional Instructional Computer System (LIRICS).
Dunlap went on to earned a B.S. in Computer Science from Old Dominion University (1979–1983). He later completed two certificates at the University of Washington: Embedded and Real-Time Systems Programming (2011–2012) and Cybersecurity (2021).

== BIND & Domain Name System ==
=== Digital Equipment Corporation and UC Berkeley CSRG (1983–1990) ===

Dunlap joined DEC in 1983 and worked there as a software engineer, later senior software engineer. By 1986 he was in DEC's Ultrix Engineering Advanced Development Group, and from 1985 to 1987 he was on loan to the Computer Systems Research Group (CSRG) [ref: The Computer Systems Research Group 1979 - 1993, NetBSD] at the University of California, Berkeley, the group behind the Berkeley Software Distribution Unix distributions in which BIND was developed.

The first Unix implementation of a DNS name server, BIND, had been written in 1984 by four Berkeley graduate students: Douglas Terry, Mark Painter, David Riggle and Songnian Zhou. [ref: The History of BIND, ISC]
In 1985, Dunlap substantially revised that implementation. Mike Karels, Phil Almquist and Paul Vixie then took over its maintenance, and Vixie later co-founded the Internet Systems Consortium to maintain BIND. In October 1986 Dunlap presented on DNS at the 4th IETF meeting at SRI in Menlo Park [ref: 4th IETF Proceedings].

=== Check Point Software Technologies / MetaInfo (1996–2001) ===

As a staff software engineer, Dunlap was technical lead for the DNS component of Meta IP DNS [ref: IP Services on NT Made Easy -, Enterprise Systems], the first commercial product based on ISC BIND 8 to run on Windows NT/2000 [ref: The History of Microsoft DNS Server, O'Reilly] He led three major releases (3.0, 4.0 and NG) and three point releases. He represented Check Point at the IETF and at DNS interoperability testing for about five years, and wrote and presented Internet-Draft proposals to the DNSEXT working group.

Designed and implemented IXFR (Incremental Zone Transfer), which lets secondary name servers fetch only changed zone data, and states that his implementation was included in the Internet Software Consortium's reference implementation of BIND. Also contributed to ISC's effort in developing Dynamic DNS Implementation.

=== Nominum (2001–2003) ===

As a senior software engineer, Dunlap contributed to designed and implemented server-side GSS-TSIG support (used for secure dynamic DNS updates) for Unix and Windows.

== Patents ==

=== US 5,278,829: Reduced broadcast algorithm for address resolution protocol ===

Dunlap is the sole named inventor on
, filed 10 January 1991 and granted 11 January 1994, with DEC as original assignee. It addresses a weakness in ARP-style address resolution.
The approach reduces broadcast traffic without discarding addresses that are still valid. The patent's rights passed through successive corporate owners, including Cabletron Systems, Enterasys Networks and Compaq, and it has since expired. It has been cited by dozens of later patents, including filings from IBM, Cisco, Nortel and Microsoft.

== Publications ==

* Experiences Implementing BIND, A Distributed Name Server for the DARPA Internet

* Name Server Operations Guide for BIND (SMM:11), University of California, Berkeley

* Development of the Domain Name System, Association for Computing Machinery

* Status of the 4.3BSD Release of the Berkeley Software Distribution, European UNIX systems User Group

* Reduced broadcast algorithm for address resolution protocol

South Korean-born pianist, socialite, and television personality

Nicole “Coco” Cha (born September 15, 1990) is a South Korean-born pianist, socialite, philanthropist, and television personality based in Palm Beach, Florida. She is known for her appearance on the Netflix reality television series Members Only: Palm Beach (2025), which follows the social lives of women in Palm Beach.

Early life and background

Cha was born in Seoul, South Korea, on September 15, 1990. She studied classical piano and developed an interest in music and the performing arts.

She later established herself in South Florida, becoming involved in the Palm Beach social community.

Career

Music

Cha has a background in classical piano. Her musical training contributed to her interest in the arts, culture, and philanthropy.

Television

In 2025, Cha appeared as herself on the Netflix reality television series Members Only: Palm Beach.

The series follows a group of women navigating social relationships, friendships, and rivalries within Palm Beach society.

Cha appeared as a guest rather than a principal cast member.

In January 2026, Reality Shrine published an individual profile of Cha discussing her appearance on the show and her connections to members of the cast.

Entrepreneurship and philanthropy

Cha has expressed interests in entrepreneurship, philanthropy, and the beauty industry, including the development of skincare products.

data.title: Tado Jurić
data.text:
----

Tado Jurić (born 1979 in Orašje) is a Croatian demographer and political scientist. [ref: Demograf Jurić: Za 10 godina svaki 4. stanovnik - s migrantskim podrijetlom, Hrvatska radiotelevizija] He is an associate professor at the Catholic University of Croatia in Zagreb. [ref: ] His publications cover migration from Croatia and Southeast Europe and the use of digital sources in demographic research. [ref: Forecasting Migration and Integration Trends Using Digital Demography – A Case Study of Emigration Flows from Croatia to Austria and Germany, Comparative Southeast European Studies] [ref: Experts raise concerns over Croatia's migrant approach, Croatia Week]

== Career ==
Jurić received his PhD from Friedrich-Alexander University Erlangen–Nuernberg, Germany in 2012. His doctoral and later publications examined migration policy and demographic change in Croatia and Southeast Europe. [ref: Tado Juric, scholar.google.com] He has held academic and research positions in Croatia and abroad, including a visiting professorship at the University of Graz. [ref: Gastprofessur am Institut für Ethik: Tado Jurić, theol.uni-graz.at]

Jurić has been cited by Croatian [ref: Demograf Jurić: Za 10 godina svaki 4. stanovnik - s migrantskim podrijetlom, Hrvatska radiotelevizija] [ref: Jutarnji list - 'Nismo svjesni što se događa. Studenti mi se žale da su izgurani s tržišta rada, a nisu svi pridošli budisti i hinduisti...', www.jutarnji.hr] [ref: Jurić: Demografija je postala pitanje nacionalnog opstanka, N1] [ref: Demograf Tado Jurić: Migracije će potpuno promijeniti Hrvatsku kakvu poznajemo, www.24sata.hr] and international media on migration and demographic issues, including Deutsche Welle, Die Kleine Zeitung, Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung, Berliner Zeitung and Alfapress have cited Jurić on migration-related topics. [ref: Iz Hrvatske odlaze oni koji već imaju posao, dw.com] [ref: Tado Jurić: Političarima iseljavanje odgovara, dw.com] [ref: Exodus am Balkan: Tado Juric: "Kroatien wird zum Altenheim Europas", www.kleinezeitung.at] [ref: Exodus aus Südosteuropa: Kroatien & Co: Länder verlieren Kampf um kluge Köpfe, www.kleinezeitung.at] [ref: EU-Kommissionspräsidentin von der Leyen zu Besuch in Kroatien, FAZ.NET] [ref: Kann ein Land seine Demografie steuern? Kroatien probt den Ernstfall, Berliner Zeitung] [ref: Labor market/ Germany eager for workforce from our region, alfapress.al]

He serves as a special adviser on migration to the Croatian Minister of Demography and Immigration. [ref: Posebni savjetnici, mdu.gov.hr]

He has contributed to international migration and demographic policy research through the International Centre for Migration Policy Development (ICMPD) [ref: Tado Jurić - ICMPD, www.icmpd.org] and the Wilfried Martens Centre for European Studies [ref: Tado Jurić, Martens Centre], and is listed as an expert in migration and demography in the Migration Research Hub. [ref: Tado Juric Expert Profile, CrossMigration]

== Publications ==
Jurić has published books on migration, demographic change and digital demography. [ref: Prikaz znanstvene monografije Suvremene migracije i opstanak nacije] [ref: Predstavljanje knjige "Suvremene migracije i opstanak nacije", mdu.gov.hr] His 2017 article “Suvremeno iseljavanje Hrvata u Njemačku: karakteristike i motivi” and his 2018 book Iseljavanje Hrvata u Njemačku. Gubimo li Hrvatsku? have been cited in subsequent academic publications. [ref: Google Scholar, scholar.google.com] His later publications in English and German have also been cited in scholarly literature, including research on migration, refugee flows and digital demography. [ref: xmed.jmir.org] Several of his books have been reviewed in academic publications, including Westbalkan-Erweiterung der EU, [ref: Westbalkan-Erweiterung der EU, PW-Portal] Gastarbeiter Millennials [ref: ] and Contemporary Migrations and the Survival of the Nation (Suvremene migracije i opstanak nacije). [ref: Tado Jurić Suvremene migracije i opstanak nacije, Politička misao: časopis za politologiju] [ref: Prikaz znanstvene monografije Suvremene migracije i opstanak nacije, Migracijske i etničke teme] [ref: Matica hrvatska - Kolo 1, 2026. - Cjelovito o migracijama, www.matica.hr]

Selected books:
* Jurić, T. (2018). Iseljavanje Hrvata u Njemačku. Gubimo li Hrvatsku? (Emigration of Croats to Germany. Are we losing Croatia?) Školska knjiga, Zagreb 2018.
* Jurić, T. (2025). Immigration Ideology. Europe's Demographic Survival. Verlag Dr. Kovač. Hamburg.

data.title: Fujishima
data.text:
Fujishima was the third son of Fujishima Masakata. His family had quite a long connection to the Satsuma domain. He also became head of the household while still in his early teens after his two older brothers died from injuries sustained during the Satsuma Rebellion of 1877. [ref: FUJISHIMA Takeji, Dictionary of Artists in Japan]

Before he moved to Tokyo, Fujishima studied Japanese-style painting under Hirayama Tōgaku in Kagoshima. He participated in the Second National Painting Competition in Tokyo in 1884. The following year he became a pupil of Kawabata Gyokushō and adopted the artistic name Gyokudō.

Cruelty (Muzan) reportedly depicted two girls striking butterflies with branches. The painting was exhibited under the name of Fujishima's friend Shirataki Ikunosuke. Mori Ōgai praised the work in a newspaper review, however, the original painting has not survived.

Additionally, in 1892, Fujishima produced Cherry Blossom Hunt or (Sakuragari). The painting depicted women of the Genroku period partaking in a cherry-blossom viewing. Although the original is unable to be found, a preparatory study is held by the Kagoshima City Museum of Art. These earlier paintings introduced subjects that continued to appear throughout Fujishima's career.

In July 1895, Fujishima became an assistant teacher at Mie Prefectural Ordinary Middle School in Tsu. He continued exhibiting his paintings during his time there.

Kuroda introduced Fujishima to plein-air painting, which involved working outdoors and observing natural light. Fujishima later became interested in Art Nouveau and other European styles from the end of the nineteenth century. His earlier training in Japanese-style painting also helped influence the decorative characteristics of his later creations. [ref: Fujishima, Takeji, Oxford University Press]

Around 1900, Fujishima began moving away from Kuroda's (Fujishima's mentor and colleague) approach to natural light. His paintings became more closely reminiscent of the Meiji Romanticism period. This change was interconnected to the literary culture of the period. The poet Yosano Akiko and the magazine Myōjō were also important figures in that cultural movement.

Beginning in 1900, Fujishima made cover illustrations for the literary magazine Myōjō. His work during this period showed his budding interest in decorative design. His paintings In Praise of the Tenpyō Era (1902) and Butterflies (1904) helped establish his reputation as an artist.

His painting titled Reminiscence of the Tempyo Era (1902) expressed an interest in Japan's Nara period. Fujishima researched about historical art while he was developing the painting. He also drew from ancient Greek art and French painting styles. The work was exhibited at the Seventh Hakubakai Exhibition. It is now held by the Artizon Museum in Tokyo. [ref: FUJISHIMA Takeji: Reminiscence of the Tempyo Era, Artizon Museum]

Fujishima's studies in Europe were funded by Japan's Ministry of Education. He left Japan in 1905 and spent approximately four years abroad. He studied in Paris before moving to Rome.

While in Europe, Fujishima encountered modern artistic movements with his academic training. He attended an exhibition of works by Paul Gauguin in 1906. The following year he attended an exhibition honouring Paul Cézanne. In Rome, he associated with Italian painters including Giacomo Balla.

During his studies in Europe. Fujishima spent around two years in Italy. There, he studied portraiture under the wing of Carolus Duran. His painting Woman of Italy (c. 1908–1909) depicts his academic oil-painting techniques. The period when he painted that work showed his focus on academic technique before he later took to Romantic qualities; showcased in his later works of female portraits. [ref: Woman of Italy, Google Arts & Culture]

At his later role, as a professor at the Tokyo School of Fine Arts, Fujishima taught younger artists and helped organize official art exhibitions. His responsibilities therefore extended beyond teaching to developing public art exhibitions in Japan.During the 1930s, Fujishima produced several landscape paintings that focused on Japanese scenery. These included Surging Waves at Daio Point (1932) and Terraced Fields (1938). His paintings from this time period used clear and bold brushwork to portray the landscape.

data.title: Argentina Citizenship by Investment Programme
data.text:
[[File:Argentine-passport-ecover-front.jpg|thumb|Accepted investors are eligible to apply for an Argentine passport|alt=Picture of the Argentinian passport front cover]]
Argentina has been running a citizenship by investment programme since July 2025, to encourage foreign direct investment, job creation, and attract global talent and innovation within the country. [ref: Argentina – Investing in Argentina: New Pathway to Citizenship, KPMG] [ref: Citizenship by Investment Program Details Announced; Applications Expected to Open Before Year-End, Fragomen - Immigration attorneys, solicitors, and consultants worldwide - Citizenship by Investment Program Details Announced; Applications Expected to Open Before Year-End]

On the 31st July 2025, the Government of Argentina published Decree no.524/2025, in the nation's gazette to establish a formal framework for foreign investors who make a 'relevant investment' to apply for Argentinian citizenship. [ref: Argentina establishes a citizenship-by-investment framework, United Nations Trade and Development]

== Cost ==
Foreign nationals are charged either a $350,000 non-refundable contribution, or must purchase a government bond subscription worth $800,000. [ref: Citizenship by Investment Program Details Announced; Applications Expected to Open Before Year-End, Fragomen - Immigration attorneys, solicitors, and consultants worldwide - Citizenship by Investment Program Details Announced; Applications Expected to Open Before Year-End] Spouses and children (aged 18-25) of applicants are charged an additional $100,000 each, with minors contributing $25,000 each. [ref: Argentina launches cash-for-citizenship scheme, dw.com]

== Due diligence process ==
Applicants must undergo identity verification, financial analysis, a juristictional risk assessment, and a review of criminal records and previous immigration history. These due dilligence processes are aligned with OECD and FATF recommendations, to ensure a rigorous evaluation process, to maintain national security. [ref: Luis Caputo anunció la puesta en marcha del Programa de Ciudadanía por Inversión de Argentina, Argentina.gob.ar]

==Background==

In April 2025, Argentina recieved emergency loans from the IMF and World Bank, with it's national economy being considered one of the world's most fragile in the world. The country has defaulted on or restructured parts of it's national debt multiple times in the 2020s. President Javier Milei intends the programme to attract wealthy investors, to 'strengthen the Argentine Republic's fiscal and financial position'. In 2025, the country lost 33 companies a day under his government.

data.title: Wojciech Jan Jurczak
data.text:
Wojciech Jan Jurczak (born August 9, 1966, in Kraków, Poland) is a Polish hematologist. His research focuses on the diagnosis and treatment of lymphoid malignancies [ref: Osobowość Roku 2020. Wojciech Jurczak: Poskromić chłoniaka, dać nadzieję i siłę pacjentom, Dziennik Polski], including lymphomas [ref: ], chronic lymphocytic leukemia and multiple myeloma. [ref: BRUIN CLL-313: Pirtobrutinib Demonstrates PFS Benefit in Relapsed/Refractory Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia or Small Lymphocytic Lymphoma, Asco Daily News] He is a professor of hematology and a Chair of the Department of Lymphoid Malignancies at the Maria Skłodowska‑Curie National Research Institute of Oncology in Kraków. [ref: ] He is a member of European Hematology Association (EHA) [ref: Wojciech Jurczak EHA 2022, memoinOncology], the American Society of Hematology (ASH) [ref: Wojciech Jurczak MD PhD; ASH 2025: Big Study Suggests Non-Covalent BTK Inhibitor Pirtobrutinib Could be New Standard-of-Care for Patients with Untreated Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia, audiomedica.com] and the American Society of Clinical Oncology. [ref: prof. dr hab. n. med. Wojciech Jurczak – Department of Hematology MC JU, hematologia.cm-uj.krakow.pl]

== Education and career ==
Jurczak graduated with distinction from the Medical Academy in Kraków in 1990, and completed additional coursework in mathematics and physics at the Jagiellonian University. [ref: dr hab. Wojciech Jurczak, uniwersytetdladzieci.eu] He joined the academic staff of the Department of Hematology at the Jagiellonian University Medical College (UJ CM), where he led the lymphoma treatment team from 1992 and served as the Head of Department from 2018.

== Research ==
His early researches focused on the development and clinical application of monoclonal antibodies in B‑cell lymphomas, including studies on radioimmunotherapy, as well as practical aspects of stem cell transplantation. [ref: Pratia Kraków: leading the way in Clinical Research, Pratia] Jurczak is a co‑author of publications that contributed to the approval of therapeutic agents used in lymphoid malignancies, including Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitors [ref: Prof. Wojciech Jurczak: Chemioterapia jest jak stanowisko z karabinem, Rzeczpospolita], phosphatidylinositol‑3‑kinase (PI3K) inhibitors [ref: PI3Kδ Inhibition by Idelalisib in Patients with Relapsed Indolent Lymphoma, New England Journal of Medicine], BCL‑2 antagonists (venetoclax) [ref: Ibrutinib plus venetoclax for relapsed/refractory mantle cell lymphoma: Final analysis of the phase 3 SYMPATICO study, British Journal of Haematology] and HDAC inhibitors (belinostat). [ref: Belinostat in Patients With Relapsed or Refractory Peripheral T-Cell Lymphoma: Results of the Pivotal Phase II BELIEF (CLN-19) Study, Journal of Clinical Oncology: Official Journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology]

His work has also included research on combination regimens and targeted treatment strategies currently shaping lymphoma therapeutics. [ref: Celowany atak w chłoniaka, www.medexpress.pl]

Jurczak’s research has been published in The New England Journal of Medicine, Blood, Journal of Clinical Oncology, The Lancet, The Lancet Oncology, and Annals of Oncology. [ref: Wojciech Jurczak - Publications - Bridge of Knowledge, Bridge of Knowledge - your knowledge portal] Jurczak has authored and co‑authored clinical research articles, including works on molecularly targeted therapies for lymphoid malignancies, ADC (antibody drug conjugates) and immunotherapies. [ref: ] [ref: ]

data.title: Archaeolingusitics
data.text:
Archeolinguistics is an interdisciplinary field that brings archaeology and linguistics together in an attempt to find out more about human past via the means of linguistic analysis.

Main branches of the field concern themselves with studies of evolution of language and symbolic thought via archaeological analysis of lithics and paleolithic art as well as methods coming from cognitive linguistics and theories of hominin evolution. This branch also uses historical linguistic and archaeology to study prehistoric migration patterns, diffusions of technology as well as reconstruction of proto-language. [ref: What is archaeolinguistics?, Glossographia]

Archeolinguistics also concerns itself with historic periods, like in case of archaeological decipherment of recovered, ancient texts. An example of that would be the decipherment of the Maya script by an English archaeologist, J. Eric S. Thompson and a Soviet linguist born in Ukraine, Yuri Walentinowicz Knorozow.

In case of historic periods, archaeolinguistics also focuses on studies of literacy, dialectal variations, language contact etc. and analysis of written texts in order to date objects and sites.

== History ==
Huxley and Darwin were among the first thinkers to integrate linguistics and archaeology. In “The Descent of man” (1865) the need of inclusion of linguistic diversity is highlighted. [ref: Archaeology, Genetics and Linguistic Diversity, Man]

“The Aryans” by Gordon Childe was published. There he argued for the homeland of Indo-Europeans in steppe areas of the northern Black Sea around the time of the late Neolithic. In his work, Childe used both archaeological and linguistic reasonings, second of which being mostly about the “core” vocabulary used for mostly plant and animals, especially for horses, in order to properly date the dispersal. All that was accompanied by his interpretations of findings from the Corded Ware culture. Childe’s work in “The Aryans” went on to inspire more archaeologists and linguists alike and became the base of the Kurgan Invasion Hypothesis. At the time it was a revolutionary work, which, despite numerous edits and criticisms, became widely accepted. However, archaeologists of the twenty first century have moved away from the hypothesis and continue the search. [ref: The Origins of Indo-European Languages, Scientific American]

Many German scholar joined the conversation of the origins of Indo-Europeans in the 30’ and 40’, generally placing the homeland in northern Europe. That work was then used by the Nazis to prove that the “original” language of Indo-Europeans was spoken by the master race of Aryans in Germany. Most of that research was weaponised by the Third Reich in their propaganda in order to push inferiority of other languages, most notably the Semitic ones.

Post-war most of that research was abandoned and other scholars became very careful about their findings in the filed.

In the following decades, linguists and archaeologists worked further. Many languages were grouped into families, such as the Indo-European one or Afro-Asiatic one, previously known as Hamito-Semitic, which are still widely accepted today. Some hypothesis about language connections however cause much controversies. Like in 1963, when an American linguist Joseph Greenberg proposed four language families of Africa: the Afro-Asiatic, the Nilo-Saharan, the Niger-Kordofanian and the Khoisan. Such taxonomy, modernly accepted, polarised the academic community, splitting linguist and enthusiasts into so-called “lumpers”; of similar views as Greenberg; and “splitters”, who believed the American linguist to be to generalising.

Greenberg’s classification of the Americas from 1987 brought even more antagonism, due to the division into just three families: the Amerind, the Na-Dene and the Inuit-Yupik-Unangan, originally called the Eskimo-Aleut family.

During 1980’, biological anthropology and archaeology’s combined efforts resulted in two vital conclusions. 1) that modern humankind, our own (sub)species Homo sapiens sapiens, evolved from its hominid predecessors in only one area and period, namely in southern Africa rather more than 100,000 years ago;
2) that full linguistic ability, the capacity for speech enjoyed by all living human groups, and the associated capacity for symbolic thought, seem to be characteristic of our species and ours alone.1990’ and early 2000’ saw a rise in the molecular approach and the new approach; focusing on DNA analysis.

== Approaches ==

=== Traditional approach – osteometry ===
This approach focuses on cranial, dental and other skeletal measurements. It was popular before 1970’, but even during it’s time of relevance it had rather low scientific value due to the similarities to racial typology and poor statistical methods.

In it’s later years, osteometry became characteristic of Russian archaeologists and linguists, who believed to had proven a gene flow western Iran to the Central Asia in the east. [ref: ]

=== Classical approach – biochemical methods ===
Osteometry was abandoned with the shifting towards biochemical methods and markers, such as blood groups, blood serum, proteins, antigens etc. The approach became more popular with the discovery that those biochemical systems fell under genetic determination. Another factor considered in this approach was phenotypic differences, such as Rhesus positive and Rhesus negative markers.

That approach however focused mostly on spatial aspects, pushing the linguistic questions into more of an afterthought. However, some scholars, such as Cavalli-Sforza, have used this approach for aswearing more linguistics questions, like the isolated languages and how they fit into the bigger matrix of language families. In the late 1980’, Cavalli-Sforza focused on R- blood group frequencies, showcasing the high frequency of said group in population living in the Basque language zone. That finding suggest a degree of linguistic and gene replacement happening probably during the time of spread of farming in Europe.

=== Molecular approach – DNA analysis ===
Molecular approach comes from recent advancements in molecular biology. This approach skips on the previous biochemical markers and moves directly to analysis of the genetic material itself.

That approach was used to support the division between African and non-African language families, which also support the “out-of Africa” hypothesis.

=== The new approach – mitochondrial DNA analysis ===
The new approach comes from the fascination and intrigue in the possibilities of the analysis of mitochondrial DNA.

Notably, the most interesting aspect of the mitochondrial DNA is that, it is inherited in strictly female line. Ergo, unless a mutation occurs, it remains unchanged through generations. Thus, it can aid in reconstructions of divisions and convergences among different human groups that ca then be used to support claims or even establish connections between different languages and language families. Such was the case with Sub-Saharan Africans, whose mDNA supports the linguistic division. Additionally the mitochondrial DNA analysis also support the “out-of-Africa” hypotheses, thanks to newly-established concept of “mitochondrial Eve”.

This approach still requires more work and exploration of possibilities it provides.

== Models ==

=== Models of Spatio-Linguistic Change ===
The models of spatio-linguistic change were outline in order to coherently showcase the culture changes, with undeniable linguistic consequences as well as varied genetic change in a section of land.

==== 1. Initial Colonisation ====
Initial colonisation led, in obvious ways, to a complete change in the gene pool of the zone and an introduction of a new language into the area.

==== 2. Linguistic/Language replacement ====
The replacement model poses a situation where on language replaces another in the zone of interest. A spectrum of sub-models can be generated with varying percentage of gene replacement.

==== 3. Divergence models ====
Based on Darwin’s conclusions, separation of people’s groups lead to differentiation in speech and in genes. Genetic drift being one of the main process leading to such happening; followed closely by the founder effect.

==== 4. Convergence models ====
Those processes happen in case of languages mutually influencing each other in aspects like morphology, phonology or semantics. This type of language contact is a well known linguistic phenomenon, despite the notion of language families being created that way being generally rejected. Despite that, a gene flow is a crucial aspect of the convergence model, which seem to not put too much value in the linguistic aspect.

=== Models of Language replacement ===

==== 1. Demographic subsistence ====
It is a model that relies on the superior technology of the incoming group. Said group also brings a new language, that usually becomes the more popular one, and new genes, as long as the new-comers are genetically different to the original population.

==== 2. Lingua Franca and Pidgin ====
The second model of language replacement relies on the presence of an elaborate trading system that allows for an elevation of one of the languages to lingua franca, a language used by the population in a given zone to communicate easily that originates from only a fraction of that population.

In some cases a shift can occur that creates a pidgin or even a creole in the area.

Culturally and genetically, this model sees a lot of intermixing between the different peoples that are present in the area and connected by trading or other activities.

==== 3. Elite dominance ====
The model showcases an invasion of a rather small, but extremely well-organised group that takes over as the new elite of the area. Occasionally the language of the new elite can replace or affect the local language.

Genetically, the effect might be less obvious, but due to social factors the effects can be seen in the Y chromosome frequencies.

==== 4. System collapse ====
System collapse model is a rather volatile option that can take elements from other models. It happens in cases of collapse of a local system, as the name would suggest. Those cases usually come with readjustments of territorial boundaries and changes to elites.

data.title: Kobebe Dam
data.text:
Kobebe Dam is a multipurpose water reservoir located in Rupa Sub-county, Moroto District, in the Karamoja sub-region of northeastern Uganda. The coordinates of the dam site are 2°48′31.3″N 34°26′50.2″E (2.808691°N, 34.447269°E). Constructed by Uganda's Ministry of Water and Environment beginning in 2010, the dam was intended to provide water for livestock, support irrigation and fish farming, and serve pastoral communities in Karamoja and neighbouring Turkana County in Kenya with a storage capacity of 1.4 million cubic meters [ref: Karamoja Peace And Technology University].

== Purpose and design ==

The dam was developed to improve water availability for livestock in a region where seasonal rainfall and prolonged dry periods affect access to water. The project was also intended to support agricultural production through irrigation and fish farming. Infrastructure associated with the reservoir included water-distribution pipes, valves and watering points intended to supply livestock. In March 2024, district officials reported that several components were damaged or vandalised and that limited funding had hindered maintenance and rehabilitation. [ref: Moroto District Officials Decry Limited Funding for Kobebe Dam, Uganda, Radio News Network]

== Role in pastoral livelihoods ==
Kobebe Dam has served pastoral communities in Karamoja and neighbouring Turkana County in Kenya. The shared use of the reservoir has supported livestock keeping across an area where herders move seasonally in search of water and pasture. The reservoir has also been described as a resource intended to support peaceful coexistence between Karamojong and Turkana pastoralists. Shortages at the dam can force herders to move their livestock to other areas, increasing pressure on alternative water sources and grazing land. [ref: Karamoja water crisis deepens as major dam dries up, Monitor] [ref: livestock water sources]

== Water shortages and maintenance ==

Kobebe Dam has experienced repeated episodes of severe water depletion. In April 2014, Uganda Radio Network reported falling water levels and concerns about drought and leaking pipes. In February 2016, the same news organisation reported that the reservoir had dried up, leaving silt and algae in parts of the basin.

In February 2021, another report described falling water levels following a prolonged dry spell. District officials and pastoralists expressed concern about the risk to livestock if the reservoir were to dry completely. [ref: Pastoralists Panic as Moroto's Multi-billion Water Dam Dries up]

In March 2024, Moroto District officials cited insufficient maintenance funding, damaged water-distribution infrastructure and the need for possible desilting. A later report in November 2025 described further reductions in water levels and a temporary restriction on livestock watering to conserve the remaining supply. [ref: Authorities Halt Watering at Kobebe Dam to Preserve Resources for Peak Dry Season]

== 2026 water crisis ==

In February 2026, the Daily Monitor reported that Kobebe Dam had almost completely dried up during a period of severe water scarcity in Moroto District. Local officials reported that the shortage was affecting livestock and prompting herders to move towards other districts in search of water and pasture. The report also raised questions about whether road construction in the area had affected water inflows, although further technical investigation was considered necessary. Uganda Radio Network reported in February 2026 that the dam had dried up again and that pastoralists were digging into the muddy reservoir bed to obtain water for their animals. [ref: Kobebe Dam Dries Up Again, Over 50,000 Cattle Left Without Water in Moroto]

The crisis has highlighted the vulnerability of water infrastructure in Karamoja to prolonged dry spells, sediment accumulation and difficulties maintaining facilities. The extent to which each factor contributed to the dam's declining performance requires further technical evidence. [ref: disaster strikes].

== Drought ==
The wider Karamoja region experienced severe drought in 2026 following a failed rainy season. In August, the World Food Programme (WFP) reported that more than 600,000 people across the region were food insecure, with poor rainfall contributing to crop failures and increased food insecurity. The organisation reported that the Ugandan government had declared a drought and launched an emergency response targeting 300,000 households across Karamoja's nine districts. WFP also reported that forecasts indicated a risk of above-normal rainfall and associated flooding later in the year. [ref: Drought in Uganda’s Karamoja region: hunger peaks as El Niño arrives, World Food Programme]

The regional drought coincided with reports of severe water shortages at Kobebe Dam. In February 2026, Uganda Radio Network reported that the reservoir had dried up, leaving more than 50,000 cattle without access to its water. The report cited siltation and possible disruption of water inflows by road construction among the factors identified by local officials. Although the regional drought provides wider climatic context, the relative contribution of drought, sediment accumulation and changes to inflow channels to the dam's condition has not been independently established.
[ref: Kobebe Dam Dries Up Again, Over 50,000 Cattle Left Without Water in Moroto, Uganda Radio Network]

data.title: Fabio Albano
data.text:
Fabio Albano is an Italian-American battery scientist and technology executive. He is a co-founder of Sakti3, the solid-state battery company acquired by Dyson in 2015, and has served as chief technology officer of NantG Power, a NantWorks company developing silicon-anode lithium-ion batteries. Albano led the solid-state battery program at Fisker Inc., where the technology he brought to the company formed the basis of its announced "super battery" effort. Over a career spanning more than two decades in advanced battery research and manufacturing, he has been granted 16 patents in North America and Europe. In 2016 he was named to Midwest Energy News 40 Under 40 list of emerging clean-energy leaders. [ref: 2016 Midwest Energy News 40 Under 40, Midwest Energy News (via ZEF Energy)]

== Early life and education ==
Albano was born in Sanremo, Italy. He received his PhD in Materials Science and Engineering from the University of Michigan, where his doctoral advisor was Ann Marie Sastry and his research centered on microarchitectured energy devices; his earliest patents, assigned to the University of Michigan, date from this period. His doctoral research on power supplies for wireless integrated microsystems — including implantable medical devices — was published as a monograph, Power Supplies for Wireless Integrated Microsystems (WIMS): Design and Optimization, in 2009. [ref: ECS Detroit Section Presents Fabio Albano, The Electrochemical Society] [ref: Deposited microarchitectured battery and manufacturing method — US8231998B2, Google Patents]

== Career ==
=== Sakti3 ===
In 2007, Albano co-founded Sakti3 in Ann Arbor, Michigan, with Sastry and Chia-Wei Wang, to commercialize solid-state lithium-ion batteries built from deposited, microarchitectured (three-dimensional) electrodes rather than conventional planar thin films. The architecture was intended to raise energy and power density by roughly an order of magnitude over 2D designs and to allow water-based processing and the use of a non-flammable solid electrolyte. [ref: Arbitration Award Confirmation for Fisker — LA County Case 20TRCV00731, Scribd (court filing)] Sakti3's work attracted funding including U.S. Department of Energy grants, and in 2015 the company was acquired by Dyson. [ref: Will we soon be able to charge electric cars in just a minute?, The Irish Times] Albano, who had departed before the sale, was later among the former employees reported by Quartz to have criticized the company's subsequent technical direction, including its use of a stacked-cell configuration they regarded as unscalable. [ref: Sakti3's quest for a better battery: Hype, funding, promises, and then a surprise sale, Quartz]

=== Dow Kokam / XALT Energy and Energy Power Systems ===
In 2011 Albano became a founding member of Energy Power Systems (EPS), a Michigan battery company, and chief technology officer of Dow Kokam — the lithium-ion cell manufacturer later renamed XALT Energy — a role he held from 2011 to 2016. [ref: ECS Detroit Section Presents Fabio Albano, The Electrochemical Society] In September 2016 he was named to Midwest Energy News 40 Under 40, which cited his Sakti3 co-founding, his 16 issued patents in North America and Europe, two R&D 100 award nominations, and awards in France and Italy. [ref: 2016 Midwest Energy News 40 Under 40, Midwest Energy News (via ZEF Energy)]

=== Fisker Inc. ===
After leaving Sakti3, Albano joined Fisker Inc. as vice president of battery systems, heading its battery team. [ref: Fisker Aims To Unleash The Potential Of Solid-State Batteries, & Stun With EMotion, CleanTechnica] Under an agreement dated 10 January 2017, he transferred his solid-state battery patent to Fisker, together with three research grants (two from the U.S. Department of Energy and one from Ann Arbor SPARK) totaling $797,000, in exchange for stock options. [ref: Arbitration Award Confirmation for Fisker — LA County Case 20TRCV00731, Scribd (court filing)] In November 2017, Fisker announced it had filed patents on flexible solid-state battery designs based on Albano's work, projecting energy densities more than twice those of conventional lithium-ion cells; Henrik Fisker credited Albano publicly, saying "the breakthrough that Fabio brought to me" was a solid-state design that overcame the surface-area limits of thin-film batteries. [ref: Will we soon be able to charge electric cars in just a minute?, The Irish Times] Inc. magazine described his approach as turning "a one-story solid-state battery into a multistory one" — a three-dimensional "bolt battery" with over 25 times the surface area of a thin-film cell. [ref: How a Failed Car Company Gave Rise to a Revolutionary New Battery, Inc.] A prototype was displayed at the Consumer Electronics Show in January 2018. Albano said at the announcement: "This breakthrough marks the beginning of a new era in solid-state materials and manufacturing technologies." [ref: Fisker gives up on solid-state batteries after announcing 'breakthrough', Electrek] Fisker abandoned its solid-state battery program in 2021. Albano's relationship with Fisker ended in a legal dispute over the 2017 agreement, which he pursued in arbitration; in 2022 he petitioned the Los Angeles County Superior Court to confirm the arbitration award. [ref: Arbitration Award Confirmation for Fisker — LA County Case 20TRCV00731, Scribd (court filing)]

=== ZAF Energy and NantEnergy ===
Albano subsequently served as chief technology officer of ZAF Energy, a Montana manufacturer of zinc-air and nickel-zinc batteries using 3D electrode manufacturing, and then as vice president of technology at NantEnergy (formerly Fluidic Energy) in Scottsdale, Arizona, where he oversaw research and development of rechargeable metal-air batteries for large-scale energy storage. [ref: ECS Detroit Section Presents Fabio Albano, The Electrochemical Society] On 10 October 2019 he gave the Electrochemical Society Detroit Section's invited talk, "Best of Both Worlds: A Marriage of Two Battery Technologies," at Lawrence Technological University. [ref: ECS Detroit Section Presents Fabio Albano, The Electrochemical Society]

=== NantG Power ===
Albano became chief technology officer of NantG Power, LLC, a NantWorks company founded within Patrick Soon-Shiong's ecosystem to develop ultra-high-performance lithium-ion cells using silicon-dominant anodes, AI-driven electrode design and multiphysics modeling. [ref: NantG Power — Silicon Batteries Without Compromise, NantG Power] Together with John Chmiola, he served as industrial technical lead on a $1 million NantG-funded research project on lithium battery materials. In 2025 he was a nominee for the Los Angeles Executive Leadership Awards presented by LA Times Studios, which cited his "over 20 years of expertise in advanced battery technologies and lithium-ion battery manufacturing." [ref: 2025 LA Executive Forum and Leadership Awards — Nominees, LA Times Studios]

== Research ==
Albano's research has centered on replacing planar battery architectures with three-dimensional, microarchitectured ones. His solid-state designs use deposited 3D electrodes intended to deliver energy densities above 500 Wh/kg at the cell level, solid (non-flammable) electrolytes, and water-based processing solvents to lower cost and environmental impact. [ref: Arbitration Award Confirmation for Fisker — LA County Case 20TRCV00731, Scribd (court filing)] At NantG Power his work shifted to silicon-dominant anodes for lithium-ion cells, addressing silicon's volume expansion through SEI stabilization, silicon/carbon composite structures and engineered electrode porosity. His earlier published work also covered the design and optimization of power supplies for wireless integrated microsystems and implantable medical devices, and widespread sensing applications. [ref: 2016 Midwest Energy News 40 Under 40, Midwest Energy News (via ZEF Energy)]

== Bibliography ==
* Albano, Fabio (2009). Power Supplies for Wireless Integrated Microsystems (WIMS): Design and Optimization. VDM Verlag Dr. Müller..

== Selected publications ==
* Cook, K. A.; Albano, F.; Nevius, P. E.; Sastry, A. M. (2006). "POWER (Power Optimization for Wireless Energy Requirements): A MATLAB-based algorithm for design of hybrid energy systems". Journal of Power Sources 159 (1): 758–780.
* Mohanty, D.; Dahlberg, K.; King, D. M.; David, L. A.; Sefat, A. S.; Wood, D. L.; Daniel, C.; Dhar, S.; Mahajan, V.; Lee, M.; Albano, F. (2016). "Modification of Ni-Rich FCG NMC and NCA Cathodes by Atomic Layer Deposition: Preventing Surface Phase Transitions for High-Voltage Lithium-Ion Batteries". Scientific Reports 6: 26532.
* Lateef, S. A.; Chmiola, J.; Albano, F.; Mustain, W. E.; Jalilvand, G. (2025). "Understanding the effects of binder dissolution dynamics on the chemistry and performance of lithium–sulfur batteries". EES Batteries 1 (4): 947.
* Raulo, A.; Lateef, S.; McRay, H.; Ilancheran, K. R.; Albano, F.; Jalilvand, G. (2025). "Fluorinated electrolytes for lithium–sulfur and beyond-lithium metal–sulfur batteries".

== Selected patents ==
* US 8,231,998 — "Deposited microarchitectured battery and manufacturing method" (with Ann M. Sastry; assigned to the University of Michigan, 2012) [ref: US8231998B2, Google Patents]
* US 8,192,789 — "Method for manufacture and structure of multiple electrochemistries and energy gathering components within a unified structure" (with Chia-Wei Wang and Ann Marie Sastry, 2012)
* US 8,357,464 — "Electric vehicle propulsion system and method utilizing solid-state rechargeable electrochemical cells" (with Sastry, Wang, Robert Kruse and Jeffrey LeBrun; assigned to Sakti3, 2013) [ref: US8357464B2, Google Patents]
* EP 2,364,507 — European counterpart on unified multi-electrochemistry energy structures (Sakti3; granted 2021)

== Awards and recognition ==
* 40 Under 40, Midwest Energy News (2016) [ref: 2016 Midwest Energy News 40 Under 40, Midwest Energy News (via ZEF Energy)]
* Invited talk, AiMES 2018 (ECS), 1 October 2018: "Solid-State Batteries Enabling Electric Mobility and New Applications" — with Eongyu Yi (University of Michigan), Guoying Chen, Haibo Shen and Marca Doeff (Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory) and Stephen Sofie (Montana State University), under the Battery 500 Consortium [ref: Solid-State Batteries Enabling Electric Mobility and New Applications (AiMES 2018), The Electrochemical Society]
* Invited talk, Electrochemical Society Detroit Section, 10 October 2019: "Best of Both Worlds: A Marriage of Two Battery Technologies" [ref: ECS Detroit Section Presents Fabio Albano, The Electrochemical Society]
* Nominee, Los Angeles Executive Leadership Awards, LA Times Studios (2025) [ref: 2025 LA Executive Forum and Leadership Awards — Nominees, LA Times Studios]

data.title: Munirat Antoinette Lecky
data.text:
Munirat Antoinette Lecky, popularly known as Anto Lecky, is a Nigerian-American media personality, entrepreneur and public official who serves as Special Adviser on Tourism and Creative Economy to the Governor of Edo State, Nigeria, Monday Okpebholo. She gained public recognition as a contestant on the third season of the Nigerian reality television programme Big Brother Naija in 2018.

== Career ==
Lecky became widely known after participating in the third season of Big Brother Naija, where she reached the semi-final stage. She subsequently worked in media, sports, entertainment and advocacy. Her professional roles have included working with the Kunle Afolayan Productions Film and Television Academy and the organisation ElectHER. She also hosted the travel and food television programme Sights of Flavours. [ref: Anto Lecky: More Than Meets The Eye, The Guardian] [ref: We are charting a bold path for Edo’s tourism and creative economy – Anto Lecky, BusinessDay]

In June 2025, Lecky was appointed Senior Special Assistant to Edo State Governor Monday Okpebholo on Tourism and Creative Economy. The appointment was announced in July 2025. [ref: Edo gov appoints BBNaija’s Anto Lecky SSA on tourism, Punch Newspapers]

In October 2026, she was promoted to Special Adviser on Tourism and Creative Economy to the Edo State governor, with the appointment taking effect on 12 October 2026. The appointment was reported by Nigerian news outlets later that month. [ref: Okpebholo appoints Big Brother Naija participant as Special Adviser, Vanguard] [ref: BBNaija Anto Lecky promoted to special adviser on tourism and creative economy in Edo, QED.NG]

data.title: Shakira Stadium
data.text:
Shakira Stadium () was a temporary, purpose-built music venue located within the Iberdrola Music complex in the Villaverde district of Madrid, Spain. The 50,000-capacity pop-up stadium was constructed specifically to host the European residency of Colombian singer Shakira's Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran World Tour in September and October 2026. The venue served as the centerpiece of Parque Macondo, an immersive cultural festival and event space inspired by the work of Gabriel García Márquez that celebrated Latin American identity, art, literature, and gastronomy. Hosting 13 sold-out concerts for over half a million attendees, the stadium introduced an unprecedented international artistic residency format to Spain and stands as a notable example of multi-use, temporary entertainment architecture.

== Background and conception ==
Eight years after her last concert in Spain during the El Dorado World Tour (2018), Colombian singer Shakira announced her return to Europe as part of her Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran World Tour. [ref: Shakira, Tourism Madrid] Rather than adopting a traditional multi-city European routing, Shakira and tour promoter Live Nation established a single-site, multi-date concert residency in Madrid, marking the first international artistic residency of this scale in Spain. [ref: Shakira construirá un estadio para 50.000 espectadores por concierto: recinto "de quita y pon" abierto 12 horas al día, Somos Madrid - elDiario.es] [ref: Shakira llena Madrid y pone el foco en el consumo eléctrico de sus conciertos] [ref: Lo que se sabe del misterioso 'Estadio Shakira', donde la cantante actuará en España: del diseño a su capacidad por concierto, Telecinco]

To host the event, organizers selected the 185,000-square-meter Iberdrola Music complex in Madrid's Villaverde district to construct a pop-up cultural hub named "Macondo Park". [ref: BIG designed an ephemeral city for Shakira inspired by One Hundred Years of Solitude, [[Domus (magazine)] Named after the fictional town from Gabriel García Márquez's novel One Hundred Years of Solitude, the park was conceived as an event space focused on Latin American culture. It was designed to encompass a central plaza connected to eight themed pavilions offering music, literature, fashion, visual arts, and gastronomy, organized under the banner "Es Latina". [ref: BIG's Macondo Park Opens as a Temporary Cultural Landscape for Shakira's Madrid Residency, ArchDaily]

At the center of Macondo Park stood Estadio Shakira (Shakira Stadium). Designed by the Danish architecture studio Bjarke Ingels Group (BIG), the temporary venue held a capacity of 50,000 spectators per night, divided between 30,000 tiered seats and a 20,000-person standing area. [ref: Todo lo que se sabe sobre el Estadio Shakira de Madrid, el recinto de los conciertos de 'Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran World Tour', EuropaFM] [ref: El 'Estadio Shakira' de Madrid estará terminado en diez días y tendrá capacidad para 50.000 personas, www.20minutos.es - Últimas Noticia] [ref: Macondo Park for Shakira's Residency in Madrid - BIG Bjarke Ingels Group, Arquitectura Viva] [ref: https://es.euronews.com/2026/09/18/shakira-inicia-madrid-serie-12-conciertos-para-cerrar-gira-mundial-tras-8-anos-ausencia] Rather than relying on permanent construction, BIG assembled the stadium and the surrounding temporary structures in ten days. Built with reversibility in mind, the project utilized modular scaffolding systems and lightweight reusable fabrics, alongside over 500 trees that were temporarily planted with the intention of returning them to local nurseries upon the residency's conclusion. The cost of constructing and deconstructing the stadium is estimated to be over €37 million. [ref: Un experto confirma cuánto le ha costado a Shakira las 13 noches en Madrid: “Hablamos de un recinto para más de 50.000 personas levantado en menos de dos meses”, infobae]

The decision to host the residency in Madrid's Villaverde district initially sparked local debate. Residents and local officials from the neighboring municipality of Getafe, including Mayor Sara Hernández, voiced concerns regarding the potential public nuisance of transforming the site into a 12-hour-a-day festival. [ref: A once-in-a-lifetime experience or a public nuisance? The big debate over Shakira's stadium in Madrid, El País] Critics cited past logistical, noise, and traffic issues caused by events at the Iberdrola Music venue, such as the Mad Cool music festival, and questioned the area's infrastructure and its ability to handle the anticipated influx of attendees.

== Design ==
The design of Macondo Park and Estadio Shakira was led by the Danish architectural firm Bjarke Ingels Group. Conceived as a 185,000-square-meter ephemeral city at the Iberdrola Music site, the complex was designed to expand the conventional concert arena into an urban landscape. Macondo Park was described by chief architect Bjarke Ingels as an "architectural manifestation of magical realism" and a temporary town meant to represent a fusion of Europe, the Americas, and Africa. [ref: Macondo Park: BIG builds an ephemeral 'Gig-City' for Shakira, ArchiPanic]

Due to the temporary nature of the residency, the project emphasized reversibility and sustainability, exploring how architecture can accommodate large-scale entertainment with minimal permanent construction. Covering 21 hectares, the complex was assembled using a large-scale kit of parts that included modular scaffolding systems, lightweight fabric structures, and reusable components. Following the conclusion of the residency, the structures were designed to be dismantled and reused, with the pavilion fabrics intended for a second life. The landscaping incorporated over 500 tropical and Mediterranean trees to create shaded gathering spaces, which were temporarily planted to be returned to local nurseries after the event. [ref: Macondo Park: BIG creates a temporary city for Shakira in Madrid, Archiproducts]

The masterplan was organized around a central public plaza connected by a network of colorful, sinuous pathways that grew out of large entrance arches. These routes connected eight thematic pavilions dedicated to different aspects of Latin culture, including music, dance, art, gastronomy, literature, cinema, and fashion. Spaces included a Shakira museum, a marketplace, a library hosting book club meetings and author meet-and-greets, and a designated club for fans, referred to as "lobas".

At the core of the park stood Estadio Shakira, a temporary arena designed to accommodate 50,000 spectators per show. [ref: Por qué el Estadio Shakira, diseñado por Bjarke Ingels, no se parece al estadio que muchos esperaban: "Es más como una ciudad, no solo es un estadio", Arquitectura y Diseño] Departing from traditional stadium architecture, the venue was composed of large blocks of modular grandstands arranged around a central floor. It featured a wraparound LED screen to ensure visibility from all angles. [ref: Macondo comes to Madrid: inside Shakira's stadium, Idealista] The venue was envisioned as an immersive environment where the architecture integrated with the surrounding public activities, shifting the focus towards a model of temporary, disassemblable entertainment architecture.

== Impact ==
Shakira's 13-concert residency concluded on October 12, 2026. Over the course of the event, Estadio Shakira and Macondo Park recorded an attendance of more than 700,000. [ref: Las mujeres facturan y Madrid también: los 400 millones que Shakira dejó tras sus 13 conciertos, www.elcolombiano.com] [ref: El análisis de la lluvia de millones de euros que Shakira ha dejado en Madrid con su residencia europea y el último paso que le queda para redondear 'Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran World Tour', CADENA 100] [ref: Shakira se despide de Madrid tras reunir a más de 700.000 asistentes en 13 conciertos, Prensa Mercosur] The event generated an estimated direct and indirect economic impact of over €400 million for the city and the surrounding region. [ref: Shakira mueve 400 millones de euros durante su residencia en Madrid, Diario ABC] [ref: Shakira mueve 400 millones de euros en Madrid con sus 13 conciertos, euronews] The President of the Community of Madrid, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, stated that the residency projected Spain's image globally and referred to Madrid as "the home of Hispanidad" in response to the event's success. [ref: https://www.eleconomista.es/informalia/famosos/amp/14022467/ayuso-comparte-su-foto-con-shakira-y-desvela-su-impacto-economico-en-madrid-la-gira-hispana-mas-taquillera-de-todos-los-tiempos]

The influx of domestic and international attendees affected the local tourism and hospitality sectors. Train bookings to Madrid increased by 38%, while hotel reservation platforms reported a 74.9% increase in accommodation searches compared to the same period in 2025. [ref: Shakira mueve 400 millones de euros durante su residencia en Madrid, Diario ABC] [ref: Las mujeres facturan y Madrid también: los 400 millones que Shakira dejó tras sus 13 conciertos, www.elcolombiano.com] Average hotel rates in the city rose to €339 per night during the concert dates, surpassing occupancy figures typically seen during other major local events. [ref: Shakira supera los US$534 millones en taquilla; convierte a Madrid en un fenómeno cultural, N Digital] With an average of over 50,000 attendees per night, the residency placed Shakira at number one on the Pollstar LIVE75 chart in September 2026, and pushed the global gross of the Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran World Tour past $534 million, making it the highest-grossing tour by a Hispanic artist to date. [ref: ]

== References ==

data.title: Richie Vinson
data.text:
Richie Vinson, known online as [user], is an American cybersecurity researcher. He is an associate security researcher at Cobalt.io and the founder of 4sec and of Hack Myrtle, a cybersecurity conference held in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina. [ref: Cybersecurity Is Evolving Fast. Can Your Career Keep Up? ft. Richie Vinson ([user])]

== Career ==
Vinson entered the red teaming field without a college degree or the Offensive Security Certified Professional (OSCP) certification, and has described volunteering at cybersecurity conferences as a factor in his early career. [ref: No OSCP. No Degree. Still Landed a Red Team Job ft. Richie Vinson (4NU81X7H3H4CK3r)] He returned to the same program in 2026 to discuss AI security, AI red teaming, and non-traditional entry paths into the industry.

Vinson has presented at events organized by SEC Conferences, including a talk titled "Shadow Tunnel: The Human VPN Bypassing HR Firewalls the Hacker's Way" on career networking in the security industry. [ref: ] In May 2026, he spoke at Hack Space Con, a cybersecurity conference held at the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Florida. [ref: Hack Space Con 2026, Hack Space Con]

In 2025 he was interviewed by Len Noe for the SEC Conferences podcast, recorded at Hack Red Con 2025. [ref: ]

== Community involvement ==
Vinson was past co-organizer of DC865, the DEF CON local group in Knoxville, Tennessee, and a co-founder of the Snack Space Con capture-the-flag competition. He received a Black Badge at Hack Space Con in 2025 and has volunteered at conferences including Hack Space Con, Hack Red Con, and the Red Team Village at DEF CON.

== Hack Myrtle ==
Vinson founded Hack Myrtle, a small-format cybersecurity conference in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina. Its 2026 edition is scheduled for December 5, 2026, with a keynote by Louis DeWeaver III. [ref: Hack Myrtle, Hack Myrtle]

data.title: Siriusim
data.text:
= Siriusim =
Siriusim is the name used by an alleged cyber threat actor that claimed to possess and release data associated with the State Bank of India (SBI), India's largest public-sector bank by assets. The actor came to public attention in October 2026 after reports of a suspected data exposure involving records found on the dark web. Public reporting has associated the name with claims posted on an online cybercrime forum. The identity, membership, origins and broader activities of Siriusim have not been independently established. [1][2] [ref: Hacker group claims access to 3.8 lakh SBI data entries, The Times of India]

== Background ==
Siriusim became publicly associated with the SBI data exposure in October 2026. According to media reports, the actor claimed to possess approximately 375,000 rows of data and 2,722 PDF documents allegedly related to banking customers and applications. The claims reportedly included personal information and loan-related and account-opening documents. The authenticity, origin and completeness of the entire dataset remain subject to investigation. [1][2] [ref: State Bank of India reports cyberattack involving nearly 3,900 customer records, Reuters]

== Alleged SBI data exposure ==
On 21 October 2026, the State Bank of India disclosed an incident involving the loss of certain data. The bank said a preliminary examination of approximately 375,000 records found on the dark web identified 3,897 customer records containing personally identifiable information. The exposed information reportedly included names, mobile numbers, dates of birth, email addresses, residential addresses, branch details, customer identifiers and metadata associated with loan and lead records. [1][3]

SBI stated that it had received alerts concerning the suspected exposure on 16 October 2026 from its threat-intelligence service provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In). The bank activated its cyber incident response procedures and appointed an independent cybersecurity agency to investigate the incident. [1][3] [ref: SBI probes suspected data breach after 3.75 lakh records surface on dark web, The Economic Times]

SBI said the incident had not materially affected its core business operations, financial performance or business continuity. The bank also stated that customer balances remained safe. The investigation was intended to establish the authenticity and extent of the exposed information and determine its potential source. [1][3]

Although reports associated Siriusim with the data leak, SBI's public disclosure did not identify the actor as responsible for the incident. The available reporting does not establish precisely how the data was obtained or whether all the material claimed by Siriusim originated from SBI systems.

== Identity and organisation ==
As of October 2026, reliable public information about Siriusim's operators, membership, location, organisational structure and motivations is limited. Its use of a particular name in online claims does not independently establish whether it represents an organised group, an individual operator or a shared online identity.

No independently verified public evidence cited here establishes its founding date, leadership, affiliations with other cyber threat actors or involvement in incidents beyond the reported SBI allegations.

== Cybersecurity implications ==
The alleged exposure illustrates the risks associated with the unauthorised disclosure of personal and financial information. If genuine, information such as names, telephone numbers, dates of birth and residential addresses can be used in impersonation attempts, targeted phishing and other forms of fraud.

The incident also highlights the importance of investigating how sensitive information is stored, accessed and shared across organisations and third-party service providers. Determining the source of the exposure requires technical investigation rather than relying solely on claims made by an alleged threat actor.

== See also ==

* State Bank of India
* Data breach
* Cybercrime
* Dark web
* Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In)

Necropolis is a 1987 American horror film written and directed by Bruce Dickey and starring LeeAnne Baker, Jacquie Fitz, and Michael Conte. It was produced by Cynthia De Paula and Tim Kincaid. The original music score was composed by Don Great. The film was a Tycin Entertainment production and was distributed in the United States by Empire International Pictures.

The film's storyline concerns a reincarnated evil witch who absorbs the life force of her victims in order to achieve eternal youth.

== Plot ==
In New Amsterdam in 1686, Henry follows a beautiful and mysterious white-haired woman (Eva) through a desolate woodland to her lair, a ruined stone structure. A group of robed figures join Eva as she prepares a Satanic rite that will give them eternal life. Elsewhere, a preacher performs the wedding ceremony of William and Dawn. Eva uses witchcraft to make Dawn’s hand bleed, causing her to flee the wedding. Eva captures Dawn, eventually slitting her throat. William and Henry enter, stabbing Eva who vows to rise again and get her revenge.

In the modern era, Eva rides a motorcycle through New York City. She arrives at a store where she attempts to purchase a magic ring known as ‘the Devil’s Ring’ from a sleazy proprietor (Rudy) who admits he already sold it. Eva uses mind control to force Rudy to give her the buyer’s name (Reverend Henry James) before killing him. Eva travels to the Neighbourhood Center, an organization that serves marginalized youths and which is run by the Reverend. Eva asks the Reverend for help, claiming to be in danger. The Reverend tries to give her a crucifix, but she recoils.

Later that night, Eva travels back to the Neighbourhood Centre. Dawn Phillips, an NPR journalist, is interviewing the Reverend and one of his program participants, Philly, a former junkie and sex worker. Eva uses witchcraft to make Philly appear to be crashing from drug withdrawal, forcing Dawn and the Reverend take him to the hospital. Eva enters the Center, where she uses magic to convince the remaining staff member, Tony, to kill himself. Eva takes the key to the Reverend’s safe and leaves on her motorcycle. Now wearing the magical Devil’s Ring, Eva breaks into an abandoned factory, the site of her former lair. She summons her former followers, who now have a grotesque, zombie-like appearance.

Back at the Neighborhood Center, Tony’s body is surrounded by Benny (a medical examiner), Dawn, the Reverend, and NYPD Lieutenant Billy Cervetti. Benny declares Tony’s death a suicide. The Reverend attempts to convince Cervetti otherwise, insisting that something unusual is happening, but the officer is not swayed. Cervetti offers to drive Dawn home, but she suggests a drink instead. She takes Cervetti back to her place, where both agree that they feel like they’ve met before. Dawn suggests that they met in a previous life. They are in fact reincarnations of the Dawn and William- the couple whose marriage was stopped by Eva in the 1600s. Dawn flashes back to her earlier self’s throat being cut. Later, when Cervetti attempts to kiss her on the neck, she reveals an aversion to having her neck touched.

Eva sees a couple (Cat and Snake) making out. She charms Snake away, killing him and then branding with the pentagram inscribed on the Devil’s Ring. The act produces ectoplasm on the body. Eva then entrances Cat, arousing her latent homosexuality. Back at the factory, Eva grows four additional breasts which produces ectoplasm that she uses to feed her followers. Benny examines Cat’s body, which also has a pentagram brand. He writes it up as a cardiac arrest. Dawn and Cervetti argue over the actual cause of death.

A group of female prostitutes talk on a street corner. One of them, Candy, complains of a lack of customers, and gets a pep talk on the power of visualization from her pimp, Steady Eddie. Eddie leaves and Eva arrives, stealing a customer from them which she later kills. Cervetti, with Dawn riding along, is called to see the body. Once again Benny calls it a cardiac arrest but the Reverend disagrees. Back at the Neighbourhood Center, the Reverend explains to Dawn and Cervettti the nature of ectoplasm. Eva follows Dawn back to her apartment, then returns to Candy and the other prostitutes. Steady Eddie takes Eva to his car, where she kills him. Once again, Benny, Cervetti, the Reverend and Dawn attend the body. Candy tells them that a “witch” did it. Cervetti visits Rudy’s shop where he finds Eva’s Satanic altar and discovers Rudy’s dead body.

One of Eva’s followers attacks Dawn, but she escapes with the Reverend. At her apartment, Henry reveals that Eva’s ritual was never completed. He heads to the Neighbourhood Center where he begins to make crosses out of sticks. A former client, Rosa, visits and Henry sends her out for coffee where Eva begins to control her mind. Eva tries to make Rosa kill the Reverend, but she kills herself instead. The Reverend and Cervetti leave the center with a large gas can. Eva captures Dawn, just as she did to Dawn’s earlier self. Using a map, Cervetti and the Reverend find Eva’s lair. They uses the Reverend’s improvised crucifixes to ward off the followers. Eva tries to force Cervetti to kill himself, but he overcomes her control. The Reverend throws a crucifix at Eva, impaling her. Cervetti rescues Dawn and cuts off Eva’s hand. They use the gas to burn Eva, her followers, and her lair. Dawn and Cervetti spend the night together, and in the morning Eva’s disembodied hand attacks Dawn. He comes to her rescue, but finds that Dawn’s personality has changed to be more like that of Eva. That night, Dawn emerges from her apartment, dressed and made up as Eva.

== Cast ==
Some actors play characters in both the 1600s and the 1980s.

* LeeAnne Baker as Eva
* Jacquie Fitz as Dawn
* Michael Conte as Billy/William
* William K. Reed as Henry
* Paul Ruben as Benny
* Andrew Bausili as Tony/Preacher
* Gy Mirano as Rosa
* Letnam Yekim as Rudy
* George Anthony-Bayza as Philly
* Anthony Gioia as Steady Eddie
* Jett Julian as Snake
* Jennifer Stahl as Cat
* Nadine Hartstein as Candy

== Release ==
The film was released theatrically in the United States in 1987.

=== Critical reception ===
The film is rated 3.9/10 on IMDb. Writing on Medium, Patrick J. Mullen rated it 5/10, describing it as, "a pretty silly and enjoyable movie overall." [ref: Movie Review: Necropolis (1986), As Vast as Space and as Timeless as Infinity]

== Related Works ==
The film was followed by a 2019 reimagining titled Necropolis: Legion.

== Title ==
Despite its title, the film does not feature an actual necropolis. The tagline states "Beneath the metropolis is... Necropolis."

data.title: Kernelling
data.text:
Kernelling (johdettu englanninkielisestä sanasta kernel [ref: ]) on BDSM-käytäntö, jossa eri hedelmien siemeniä työnnetään suusta suoraan henkilön emättimeen tai peräaukkoon tämän ollessa penetroitu, jotta hän tuntisi itsensä hedelmällisemmäksi. Yleisimpiä hedelmiä ovat vesimelonit, appelsiinit ja sitruunat. Koska nämä siemenet ovat kuitenkin muodoltaan huomattavan teräviä, käytäntöä ei pidetä turvallisena, vaikka siihen saatettaisiinkin antaa suostumus. Siementen työntäminen emättimeen tai peräaukkoon voi aiheuttaa ärsytystä, vammoja tai vierasesineen jäämistä elimistöön. Siitä huolimatta tämän käytännön harrastajat väittävät, että siemenet voidaan myöhemmin istuttaa, mikä tekee tästä hieman muinaisten hedelmällisyysrituaalien kaltaisen toiminnan [ref: Figure 3.7. Kernelling techniques devised by experiment participants:..., ResearchGate].

== Historia ==
Kuten figging, myös kernelling on saattanut saada alkunsa kidutusmenetelmänä. On olemassa todisteita siitä, että se oli olemassa jo 1950-luvulla [ref: KERNELLING LTD people - Find and update company information - GOV.UK, find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk]. Itse termi syntyi vuonna 1994, mutta se ei levinnyt yhteisössä kovinkaan laajasti ennen 2010-luvun puoliväliä. BDSM-sanasto ei tunnusta termiä sen harvinaisuuden vuoksi.

data.title: The Chicken and The Egg
data.text:
----

The Chicken and The Egg is a children's picture book based on the chicken or the egg causality dilemma. It was written by Buena Batiste-Webber and illustrated by Kenniece Webber under their company Beatrice Ann, and originally published in 2012. [ref: https://www.worldofbooks.com/products/chicken-and-the-egg-book-beatrice-ann-9780615636856]

==Plot==
The Chicken and the Egg arrive at the same time in a line, only to find themselves in a tense standoff. Each was insisting the other should go first. Just as the argument reaches its peak, a giant hand descends from above, telling them to not whine because they're others in line waiting. The book later shows that the animals are actually stuffed animals that are trapped inside a claw machine aptly named “The Hand.” The other animals watched as the others were taken by a group of kids from within; the ending shows the Chicken and the Egg inside a boy's backpack.

==Publication==
Buena Batiste-Webber and Kenniece Webber began the idea of The Chicken and The Egg after Buena made daily prank calls while Kenniece was working at a children's library in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. [ref: http://thechickenandtheegg.com/beatrice-s-story.html] After several calls, Kenniece responded: “You should write that book.” Together, they formed Beatrice Ann, LLC, which was named after their grandmother whose middle name was Beatrice. [ref: https://beatriceann-769636.square.site/] Beatrice Ann published the book on June 8, 2012. It is currently available for purchase in online stores or in a booth at the French Market. [ref: https://beatriceann-769636.square.site/]

==Reception==
The book holds a 5.0-star rating across reader and platform reviews (such as BooksRun and general retail feedback). [ref: https://booksrun.com/9780615636856-the-chicken-and-the-egg]

==Sequel and short film adaptation==
On October 26, 2014, Beatrice Ann published a sequel to the book called "The Chicken and The Egg: Hit the Road". [ref: https://books.google.com/books/about/The_Chicken_and_The_Egg.html?id=BdsArgEACAAJ] The book is a slice of life story about exercising, patience, and uncertainty. This is Buena Batiste-Webber's favorite book in the series because, to her, it's about someone having a hard time. [ref: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9E_zXFbLd68] A short film adaptation of both books by Zeke Benoit under his vanity card Puppet Enterprises, Inc., is currently in the works. [ref: https://www.instagram.com/p/DemNhTHx1S9/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&srtk=MzRlODBiNWFlZA==]
