data.title: Furuichi In'ei
data.text:
Furuichi In'ei () was a Japanese Buddhist monk and warrior active from the middle of the Muromachi period into the Sengoku period. He was a (armed monk-retainer) of Kōfuku-ji in Yamato Province. His father was, and his younger brother was Chōin.

== Life ==
=== Meeting with Kyōkaku and the deaths of his parents ===
He was born the son of, head (tōryō) of the kanpu shuto of the of Kōfuku-ji in Yamato Province.

On 3 March 1447 (Bun'an 4, 2nd month, 17th day), he met for the first time, the abbot (monzeki) of Daijō-in, who had moved into the at Furuichi through his father Insen's arrangements.

On 14 August 1448 (Bun'an 5, 7th month, 15th day), his mother died. The hundredth-day memorial was held on the 26th day of the 10th month.

From 22 June to 7 July 1449 (Hōtoku 1, 6th month, 2nd–17th day), he suffered from a disorder of the stomach and became gravely ill. Kyōkaku wrote: " has a calm disposition, and when he grows up he will surely become a person above the ordinary. Lately he has become all the more attached to me, which makes this all the more pitiful. There is nothing to be done, and I am simply at a loss", and prayed for him again and again. [ref: 『経覚』、酒井紀美著、2019年、135頁] Perhaps because the prayers were answered, showed signs of recovery that dawn, and by the 17th he had fully recovered.

From 25 to 31 May 1450 (Hōtoku 2, 4th month, 14th–20th day), he made a pilgrimage to Ise Grand Shrine together with his grandmother, the nun, and his younger sister. Before departing he received a woven-colour katabira (unlined robe) from Kyōkaku. [ref: 『経覚』、酒井紀美著、2019年、135頁]

On 30 July 1453 (Kyōtoku 2, 6th month, 24th day), his father Insen died, and he became the head (sōryō) of the Furuichi house.

=== Appointment as head of the kanpu shuto ===

On 26 October 1455 (Kōshō 1, 9th month, 16th day), following the downfall of the Tsutsui clan, he was appointed head of the, and, a member of the Furuichi family, became his deputy (daikan). [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第12巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、355頁] Until his coming of age (genpuku), devoted himself to temple administration, and other matters were handled by the Furuichi deputies (Yamamura Inkei and ).,, and were also appointed heads of the kanpu shuto. [ref: ] [ref: 興福院所蔵 鷹山家文書調査報告書, 生駒市教育委員会]

On 27 June 1456 (Kōshō 2, 5th month, 25th day), the temple administration notified him that he would receive, as his first stipend, 13 koku of polished rice and 5 kanmon of gratuity money from the Furuichi and estates, shōen belonging to the Furuichi domain. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第12巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、44頁] By this time appears already to have been taking part in practical work as a shuto. The following month, on 14 July (6th month, 12th day), an order was issued to Furuichi, Ochi and Koizumi to collect the contributions levied on the temples and shrines of Yamato for the repair of Daijō-in's buildings. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第12巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、207頁] These included Shōryaku-ji,, Hase-dera, Chōgaku-ji, Shigisan-ji, and Tachibana-dera.

On 14 February 1457 (Kōshō 3, 1st month, 20th day), Toyoda Raiei entrusted him with supervising the work on the of the Zenjō-in. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第1巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、75-79頁] To prepare the groundwork, about thirty labourers a day were called up from the seven gō (villages) of the temple's domain, joined by two. On the 19th he went to Hannya-ji with Kyōkaku and.

On the 20th day of the 7th month of the same year, he married a daughter of the Kubojō clan.

In the 3rd month of 1459 (Chōroku 3), his grandmother the nun died, and in the 8th month of the following year his grandfather died.

On 16 March 1460 (Chōroku 4, 2nd month, 23rd day), he met with and other members of the opposing Tsutsui faction. On 22 November (Chōroku 4, 10th month, 10th day), in a battle at Tatsuta in Yamato,, a member of the Furuichi family, and his sons the brothers were killed. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第2巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、357頁] [ref: 『奈良県史第11巻 大和武士』、奈良県 編者／朝倉弘 著者、1993年、116頁] Yamato was divided by the succession dispute (o-ie sōdō) in the Hatakeyama clan, and the (local landholders) were fighting in support of either Hatakeyama Yoshinari or Hatakeyama Masanaga; In'ei supported Yoshinari together with. and his sons, on Yoshinari's side, attacked Masanaga's camp at Tatsuta (present-day Ikaruga, Ikoma District) but were defeated. Kyōkaku was told that this was because Tsutsui Jun'ei, in the rear of Masanaga's army, had attacked with about 500 men. [ref: 『経覚』、酒井紀美著、2019年、194頁]

=== The dharma name "In'ei"; meeting the Shiba and Asakura ===
On 18 September 1465 (Kanshō 6, 8th month, 28th day), he took the tonsure and adopted the dharma name "In'ei". [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第3巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、518頁] The ordination followed due form: his two preceptors, and, supplied the robes and a full set of garments, and an offering of 300 hiki was made. Before the tonsure he offered a cup of sake in the room of, and afterwards he was granted a bundle of sugihara paper and a roll of white cloth.

On the 21st day of the 10th month, a dispute arose between the deputies of Hatakeyama Yoshinari and Hatakeyama Masanaga over the, land directly controlled by the shogunate. By arrangement with Yoshinari, In'ei led troops into Kawachi Province. [ref: 『福井県郷土叢書 第10集 (北国庄園史料)』、福井県立図書館, 福井県郷土誌懇談会 共編、1965年、139頁] [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第4巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、8頁] He was accompanied by the Kataoka, Handa, Tatsuta, Yamada,, Kubojō and, with two to three hundred armoured men in all. That same day they entered the in Kawachi, and the enemy set up camp about 1 km away. On the 26th the first battle was fought; they attacked the area and burned it, and returned to camp on the 29th.

On 13 May 1466 (Bunshō 1, 3rd month, 29th day), through the mediation of Asakura Takakage, he met for the first time. [ref: 『室町幕府将軍権力の研究 (東京大学日本史学研究叢書; 1)』、家永遵嗣 著、1995年、288-291頁] On the 29th day of the 5th month, Yoshikado granted him lands in Owari and Echizen, and the two appear to have entered a lord–vassal relationship. As the conflict between Shiba Yoshikado and intensified and troops began to gather from the provinces, on the 8th day of the 8th month he sent about ten armoured men and ten archers to the capital on Yoshikado's side, under as commander. [ref: 『福井県郷土叢書 第10集 (北国庄園史料)』、福井県立図書館, 福井県郷土誌懇談会 共編、1965年、142-143頁] [ref: 『経覚』、酒井紀美著、2019年、214頁] For this service he received an additional 800 kanmon of land in Echizen. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第4巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、100頁]

On 14 February 1467 (Bunshō 2, 1st month, 10th day), when Shiba Yoshikado was appointed kanrei, In'ei sent the son of and to the capital to congratulate him. [ref: 『福井県郷土叢書 第10集 (北国庄園史料)』、福井県立図書館, 福井県郷土誌懇談会 共編、1965年、149頁] On this occasion Yoshikado granted him an additional 700 kanmon of land. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第4巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、137頁]

Where these Echizen lands lay is known from a later record. On the 20th day of the 5th month of Ōnin 2 (1468), when sent a messenger down to the lower part of in the, he noted the purpose of the errand as "this concerns Furuichi's domain" (). The editors of the identify this "Furuichi" as In'ei. [ref: 『経覚私要鈔』第10（史料纂集 古記録編）高橋隆三・小泉宜右 校訂、八木書店古書出版部、2018年、48頁。]

=== Ōnin War: the outbreak ===
On 25 February 1467 (Bunshō 2, 1st month, 21st day), In'ei received a summons from Asakura Takakage to come up to the capital, and set out early in the morning with his forces on the side of Shiba Yoshikado. [ref: 『精華町史 史料篇 1』、精華町史編さん委員会 編、1989年、433-434頁] [ref: 『精華町史 本文篇』、精華町史編さん委員会 編、1996年、346-347頁] [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第4巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、144-149頁] He gathered his kinsmen and young retainers (wakatō), and before setting out they exchanged farewell cups of sake. In'ei wore silk kobakama and rode in a wooden palanquin, but the road was so bad that they stopped once. When they set out again In'ei too mounted a horse, keeping four or five men beside him. also rode, and more than thirty horsemen, kinsmen and young retainers together, followed them. The Furuichi force crossed Takayama and passed through Yamada on its way to the capital. Ahead of them were about seventy armoured men, and they expected to reach Kyoto within the day.

In the afternoon, however, word came from Kyoto that "there is no need to come up to the capital". On the 18th the had taken place: Hosokawa Katsumoto and, on Hatakeyama Masanaga's side, together with and Akamatsu Masanori, had turned against him, abandoned Masanaga and gone over to the shogun's side. Meanwhile Hatakeyama Yoshinari had taken the field himself and battle was joined; on Yoshinari's side and were killed, and on Masanaga's side and the Jinbō brothers were killed. Further, Yamana Sōzen joined hands with Yoshinari and attached the Bingo men to, and Asakura Takakage also took the field on Yoshinari's side. When Masanaga fled late at night they pursued him, and the Asakura force too took heads. With the enemy gone, the march to the capital became unnecessary, and In'ei turned back at and returned home.

On 2 March (1st month, 26th day), In'ei did go up to the capital and that same night had an audience with the kanrei Shiba Yoshikado. [ref: 『大日本史料 第8編之1』、東京大学史料編纂所 編、1913年、56頁] A banquet was held the next day, and he received the supreme honour of dining in the kanreis presence. [ref: 『福井県郷土叢書 第10集 (北国庄園史料)』、福井県立図書館, 福井県郷土誌懇談会 共編、1965年、151頁] Those present included,,, and, and there was music (ongyoku) and dance (mai). He went back down on 8 March (2nd month, 3rd day).

With the at the end of the 5th month, the Ōnin War broke out in Kyoto. At this time In'ei was being urged by Shiba Yoshikado and Asakura Takakage to come up to the capital. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第4巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、196-200頁] [ref: 『大日本史料 第8編之1』、東京大学史料編纂所 編、1913年、306-307頁] Ochi Iehide's army had already gone up with 100 men, but the monks of Kōfuku-ji, beginning with Jinson, were opposed to Furuichi going to the capital, fearing that he would become an enemy of the court (chōteki), and spent several days trying to dissuade In'ei. In'ei had set out for the capital on the 8th, but he gathered his kinsmen and debated whether to go. On the 12th an urgent order to come up came from Asakura as well, but finally, on the 14th, the monks and pressed In'ei and persuaded him to stay. On the evening of the following day, the 15th, Kusuba Mototsugu's son informed Kyōkaku that on the previous day Asakura Takakage had fought the enemy at Nijō in Kyoto and inflicted heavy damage on the Takeda force. [ref: 『福井県郷土叢書 第10集 (北国庄園史料)』、福井県立図書館, 福井県郷土誌懇談会 共編、1965年、156-161頁] In'ei, who was at a drinking party, was overjoyed at the news of victory and ordered that it be reported at once to.

On the 12th day of the 9th month, Kusuba Mototsugu brought back news of the situation in the capital and reported that pressure and instructions for In'ei to come up to the capital had arrived from Yamana Sōzen and Asakura Takakage. In'ei decided to go to the capital in response to Asakura's request. On the 25th an advance party went up, consisting of fifteen armoured men under the command of, together with kinsmen, young retainers and Kusuba Mototsugu's son. On the 27th they encamped at the at Kurodani (present-day Konkaikōmyō-ji, Kurodani-chō, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto), near where the Asakura force was deployed. The enemy Akamatsu force was encamped near Nanzen-ji, so the two camps faced each other.

On the 3rd day of the 10th month, the took place; the Furuichi force fought alongside Hatakeyama Yoshinari and Asakura Takakage of the Western Army and won. Shōkoku-ji, where Takeda Nobukata had been encamped, was burned to the ground, and Furuichi set up camp on its site together with the Asakura force.

=== Ōnin War: fighting in Yamato ===

On 10 June 1468 (Ōnin 2, 5th month, 20th day), he tried to send a messenger concerning his lands in Echizen, but at that time Yoshitoshi, Shiba Yoshikado's rival, had made a comeback in Echizen and driven the Asakura out of the province, and the situation there was unsettled. [ref: 『福井県郷土叢書 第10集 (北国庄園史料)』、福井県立図書館, 福井県郷土誌懇談会 共編、1965年、167頁]

On 28 October 1470 (Bunmei 2, 10th month, 5th day), In'ei sent troops under Nagata Ienori to Shimokoma (present-day Seika, Sōraku District, Kyoto Prefecture) to reinforce the army led by Ōuchi Masahiro. [ref: 『精華町史 本文篇』、精華町史編さん委員会 編、1996年、350頁] They fought against and others, who had their base at Kizu.

On 12 February 1471 (Bunmei 3, 1st month, 23rd day), amid armed clashes throughout the Nanto area, In'ei's allies, who sided with the Kōriyama faction, attacked Yakushi-ji and burned its new quarters. [ref: 『大日本史料 第8編之4』、東京大学史料編纂所 編、1913年、959頁]

On 19 September 1473 (Bunmei 5, 8th month, 27th day), Kyōkaku died. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第5巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、390頁] The cause of death is said to have been a severe stroke (daichūbu) that struck him a few days earlier. When Kyōkaku collapsed, In'ei and Jinson consulted about the funeral. In'ei joined the procession wearing a kogoromo, and many members of the Furuichi family also took part.

On 28 August 1474 (Bunmei 6, 7th month, 16th day), he sent a small detachment towards Kyoto, and the next day he received word from Ōuchi Masahiro that a battle was expected in Kyoto. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第6巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、8頁]

On 17 June 1475 (Bunmei 7, 5th month, 14th day), he encamped at Shin-Yakushi-ji with his brother Chōin, who was in his first battle, and Ochi Iehide, and fought,, Jōshin'in Junsei and others of the Eastern Army at the great torii of Kasuga-taisha. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第6巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、109-110頁] On the Furuichi side four kinsmen and thirteen young retainers were killed, and In'ei and Chōin barely "survived" (). Jinson, the abbot of Daijō-in, wrote that a battle at the great torii was an unheard-of outrage and that divine punishment had fallen (Daijōin Jisha Zōjiki, vol. 69, entry for Bunmei 7, 5th month, 14th day).

Taking the defeat at the Kasuga shrine as the occasion, he handed over the headship of the house to his brother Chōin on 20 August (7th month, 19th day). This is also said to have been meant to deflect criticism of In'ei's forceful control over his household. He did not appear in public for some time after the defeat, but on 12 November (10th month, 14th day) he visited Jinson of Daijō-in with his brother Chōin and attended upon the abbot's procession. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第6巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、頁] After this In'ei was called ("Furuichi of the West").

=== Ōnin War: the fighting in Kawachi ===
On 15 October 1477 (Bunmei 9, 9th month, 9th day), Hatakeyama Yoshinari, aiming to recover Kawachi Province, consulted Chōin and Ochi Iehide, both of his faction, about a plan to take the field; a few days later Chōin's men escorted Yoshinari's wife and and delivered them to the Ochi. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第6巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、320-332頁] [ref: 『精華町史 本文篇』、精華町史編纂委員会 編、1996年、353-356頁] On 27 October (9th month, 21st day), Yoshinari left Kyoto with 350 horsemen and 2,000 armoured men and advanced from Yamashiro into Kawachi. On 2 November (9th month, 27th day) the began; the Furuichi brothers (In'ei and Chōin) also took the field, and the kokujin forces of Yamato all set out at once, including not only Yoshinari's faction under Ochi but also Masanaga's faction, such as the Tsutsui and.

The Ochi and Furuichi forces advanced north-west from Yamato Takada, [ref: 『応仁の乱: 日野富子の専断と戦国への序曲 (歴史群像シリーズ; 37号)』、学習研究社、1994年、25頁] joined Yoshinari, who was encamped at Fujii-dera, and won the battle of Konda Castle on 12 November (10th month, 7th day). On 14 November (10th month, 9th day) the Ochi and Furuichi forces defended Kyōkō-ji in Kawachi and drove off, who was marching to relieve.

On 18 November (10th month, 13th day), in Yamato,, a commander on Ōuchi Masahiro's side at Shimokoma Castle, led 300 armoured men and several thousand foot soldiers and took. The of Iga, who had taken the field at Kizu, and then and Tsutsui Junson burned their own positions and fled. Sugi, keeping his troops with him, marched from Kizu to Hannya-ji in the northern part of. Sugi's aim seems to have been to sweep away the Eastern Army forces, together with the Furuichi force that had been fighting for the Ōuchi since 1470 (Bunmei 2) and was stationed at, and so help Yoshinari's faction enter Yamato. [ref: 『室町幕府将軍権力の研究 (東京大学日本史学研究叢書; 1)』、家永遵嗣 著、1995年、325頁] The previous year, too,, a Furuichi deputy, had reported a planned march on Nanto to Jinson.

Fearing an attack on Nanto, the gakuryo and rokuhō of Kōfuku-ji informed the Furuichi force; Nakamikado and others met Sugi, and, the Furuichi deputy, was sent to Shimokoma Castle, so the matter was settled without incident. The brothers In'ei and Chōin also hurried back from Kawachi to Nanto that same night, deployed with 100 armoured men at the on Saihōinzan to keep order, and the next day instructed their retainer Nagata Ienori to guard and Hokke-ji.

On 16 December (11th month, 11th day), Ōuchi Masahiro, Toki Shigeyori and Hatakeyama Yoshinari each returned to their home provinces, and the Ōnin War, which had lasted eleven years, came to an end. Sugi burned Shimokoma Castle himself and went home, and and the other Furuichi deputies who had been holding withdrew to Furuichi Castle. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第6巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、342頁]

=== Later years ===
On 18 November 1477 (Bunmei 9, 10th month, 13th day), though retired, he hurried from Kyōkō-ji in Kawachi Province to Nara with his brother Chōin and took up position there with more than a hundred armoured men. Three days later, however, on 21 November (10th month, 16th day), word reached Jinson that In'ei was going to retire once again. Envoys were also sent by the Hatakeyama clan to smooth matters over, and In'ei appears to have given up the idea of retiring, but Asakura Hiroshi states that the circumstances are unclear.

On 25 January 1478 (Bunmei 9, 12th month, 22nd day), his daughter married into the Sagawa clan, who were on the Tsutsui side. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第6巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、358頁] Because the other party belonged to the Tsutsui faction the match was regarded as a problem, and that night dispossessed men of the Sagawa even made a move to converge on them.

On 17 February (Bunmei 10, 1st month, 15th day), when his brother Chōin was appointed to the kanpu shuto, In'ei also joined in recommending him.

On 22 May 1480 (Bunmei 12, 4th month, 13th day), although already retired, he was still making preparations to find a place of seclusion at Mount Kōya, or. This seems not to have been realised.

The entry for 22 October 1481 (Bunmei 13, 9th month, 29th day), titled ("On the kinship and acquaintance of the shuto and kokumin"), states that " and the Furuichi brothers are distant relatives" (), and Asakura Hiroshi identifies these "Furuichi brothers" as In'ei and Chōin.

On the 25th day of the 4th month of Bunmei 16 (1484), concerning In'ei's request to retire to the area around, which had been under discussion since the previous year, the abbot admonished him, and on this day it was answered that the matter would be postponed. The editors of the Seikaku Daisōjō ki annotate this entry " In'ei: retirement postponed at Jinson's urging" (), and the entry for the following day records that Chōin thanked Jinson. [ref: 『政覚大僧正記』第1（史料纂集 古記録編）続群書類従完成会、1989年、24頁。]

In the 10th month of 1490 (Entoku 2), when Chōin, as a kanpu shuto, proclaimed a, unexpected consequences followed: the household retainers (uchishū) who had carried it out fled to Mount Kōya, and In'ei had to go into hiding within the mountain.

On 14 January 1491 (Entoku 2, 12th month, 5th day), he withdrew from the world as a. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第12巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、462頁]

On 14 May 1492 (Entoku 4, 4th month, 18th day), his adopted son (yūshi) died. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 巻10巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、158頁]

He died on 8 December 1505 (Eishō 2, 11th month, 13th day), aged 67. In that year a peace was concluded among the kokujin of Yamato and a petition was offered before the Kasuga shrine, but the name of the Furuichi clan does not appear in it.

== Records of judicial cases ==
Kyōkaku's and Jinson's preserve records of the (police and judicial) cases handled by In'ei.

On 27 August 1457 (Kōshō 3, 8th month, 9th day), concerning irrigation water from the and rivers, tributaries of the Yamato River, water that should have been delivered to the Kodono estate was being diverted by two parties, the side and the side, on the pretext of an emergency. held a trial and heard both sides' explanations, but their reasons were unclear; on the basis of past rulings and precedent he decided that the water should go "to the Kodono estate as before" and ordered it switched back immediately. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第12巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、207頁] From around this time the foundations of his control over the Furuichi retainers were laid.

On 20 December 1461 (Kanshō 2, 11th month, 19th day), in a suit in which of the monastery sought to seize the in Uda District, a holding of the, ruled that resorting to force was not permissible for any reason whatsoever. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第3巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、79頁] The side had sought to take over the estate on the basis of an old loan document stating that in Ōei 2 the late sōjō had borrowed 2,000 hiki from the 's annual tax, but the debt had been cancelled by the general debt-cancellation (tokusei) of Shōchō 1, and the council of the rokuhō-shū had already ruled on the matter.

In the 6th month of 1466 (Bunshō 1), a monk of the in Yamato attacked a monk and servants of the by night. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第4巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、72-73頁] It was decided to establish the truth by (ordeal by boiling water), but the situation became confused, with the son of of the running away. In'ei and Tsutsui Jun'ei mediated, achieving a reconciliation and the withdrawal of both sides' forces.

On 23 August (7th month, 13th day), he banished Yamamura Inkei, a member of the Furuichi family. Hashiin, which had belonged to the Tsubao clan, had become a retainer of the, and a dispute over the retainer arose between the Tsubao and the. The cause was that the side sought help from In'ei and the Hashiin side from Yamamura Inkei, and the two men fell out. Inkei was pardoned half a year later. Further, in 1470 (Bunmei 2), In'ei executed two retainers who had caused a disturbance and banished thirty people, including kinsmen. Among those punished were members of houses such as the Yamamura, who within Kōfuku-ji were of equal standing with the Furuichi and could become kanpu shuto, yet Kōfuku-ji, as the public authority, was unable to object.

On 17 August 1473 (Bunmei 5, 7th month, 23rd day), there was an incident in which the scholar-monks and rokuhō objected to the appointment, through a scheme of the Tsutsui clan, of Tōnomine as deputy of on the Ise road (present-day Haibara, Uda). [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第5巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、67,382-383頁] [ref: 『中世日本の歴史像 (創元学術双書)』、日本史研究会史料研究部会 編、1978年、259頁] [ref: 『能謡新考: 世阿弥に照らす』、香西精 著、1972年、373頁] To settle it, In'ei met with the Tsutsui and worked to mediate. However, the affair was still unresolved a year later; the "thirteen men" of the scholar-monks and rokuhō who opposed the deputy fled, and repeatedly set fires throughout Nara and seized annual taxes and tansen and tanmai levies. His younger brother Chōin, who had not been involved in the affair at first, also fled and was punished in the same way as the thirteen. This led Chōin, who had been a scholar-monk, to go to the battlefield, and after this incident Chōin never returned to being a scholar-monk. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第6巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、140頁]

== Culture and fūryū ==
Cultural pursuits and fūryū (refined entertainments) had been cultivated at Furuichi Castle since the time of his father Insen and grandfather Inken, and In'ei too was a man of taste. He is known for holding, gatherings combining bathing and tea, and together with Chōin he became a disciple of Murata Jukō, the founder of the tea ceremony. Because a descendant of the Furuichi clan served in the Edo period as head of tea (sadōgashira) to the main Ogasawara house (lords of the Kokura Domain), he is named as the founder of the.

For three days from 25 August 1447 (Bun'an 4, 7th month, 14th day), Urabon and sarugaku performances were held at Furuichi Castle and. [ref: 『経覚私要鈔（文安4年7月14日〜16日）』、経覚、1447年] The programme on the second day was "Sasaki on horseback" (a furyū on Sasaki Takatsuna's race to be first across the Uji River), and on the evening of the third day a furyū and sarugaku of "Ama-no-Iwato" was performed. The roles were taken by temple monks and young boys: Tajikarao-myōjin was played by the monk, Amaterasu by the son of, and the heavenly maiden by the monk. On this occasion nine-year-old (later In'ei) also served as a hayashi musician.

At the Urabon of 23 August 1450 (Hōtoku 2, 7th month, 16th day), furyū was again held at Furuichi Castle, organised by. Besides items such as "tug-of-war" and (yuki-marohakashi), there were stalls and performances by vendors, and the event is said to have closed with a kasa (umbrella) dance. [ref: 『経覚私要鈔（宝徳2年7月16日）』、経覚、1450年]

On 11 February 1458 (Chōroku 2, 1st month, 27th day), he took part in a thousand-verse renga session held by Kyōkaku. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第12巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、344頁]

In 1469 (Bunmei 1), when the bath cauldron broke, to raise money for its repair he built a hut where furyū dances, then banned in Nara, could be danced, and charged an entrance fee of 6 mon. The hut was a great success, drawing as many as 3,000 people. has called it "Japan's first paid dance hall".

On 22 February 1472 (Bunmei 4, 1st month, 14th day), a renga gathering was held at the, and In'ei composed the opening verse: (Azusa-yumi / haru wa yachiyo no / hajimari na, "Catalpa bow — spring is the beginning of eight thousand ages"). [ref: 『福井県郷土叢書 第10集 (北国庄園史料)』、福井県立図書館, 福井県郷土誌懇談会 共編、1965年、186頁] [ref: 『大日本史料 第8編之6』、東京大学史料編纂所 編、1920年、329頁]

On 11 August 1473 (Bunmei 5, 7th month, 17th day), when the turmoil of the Ōnin War had begun to settle, the Urabon furyū was held at Daijō-in. In'ei himself performed in the guise of Daikokuten, one of the Seven Lucky Gods. [ref: 『藝能史研究 (51)』、藝能史研究會、1975年、37頁] [ref: 『能と狂言』、金井清光 著、1977年、619-620頁] The audience included Ichijō Kaneyoshi and other nobles who had taken refuge from Kyoto, as well as Jinson and other members of the Daijō-in. Soldiers lined the gate, and the young men of the upper and lower hokumen, together with and the satashū and others, were in attendance. During the night the blinds were rolled up along the nine-bay front of the hall before the abbot, and fifteen lanterns were hung. On the eastern corridor side, too, the sliding screens were raised and lowered and the blinds let down, and the ladies-in-waiting took their seats inside the blinds. The bōkan and samurai lined up along the screens and the veranda respectively, and the hokumen members and elders took their places on the southern veranda of the nine-bay hall. The page boys and children stood in a single line from around the double doors along the whole length of the nine-bay veranda. Jinson wrote that the performance was so splendid that its highlights could not be confined to just one. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第5巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、381頁]

data.title: Gazi Erçel
data.text:
Süleyman Gazi Erçel (February 20, 1945 – June 13, 2022) was a Turkish economist who served as 18th Governor of the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey (1996-2001). [ref: Governors of the CBRT, www.tcmb.gov.tr] He previously served as Director General of the Ministry of Treasury and Finance of Turkey as well as chairman of Tütünbank. [ref: Turkish stock market: Time to clean things up, www.euromoney.com] [ref: Former Central Bank Governor Gazi Erçel has passed away., [[The Independent]

==Early life and education==
Erçel was born on February 20, 1945 in Istanbul, Turkey. [ref: Gazi Erçel, former governor of the Central Bank, has passed away., www.bankadunyasi.com] He earned his bachelor's degree from the Department of Finance and Economics of Ankara University in 1967 and his master's degree from Vanderbilt University in 1976.

==Career==
Erçel began his career in 1967 at the Turkish Ministry of Treasury and Finance where he held several roles, including Deputy Director General of the Treasury, as well as various roles in the economic research, banking and foreign exchange, IMF, and World Bank departments.

From 1982 to 1986, Erçel left the ministry to serve as Deputy Executive Director of the IMF. He returned in 1987 upon appointment as Director General of the Treasury.

In 1989, Erçel left civil service to pursue a career in the private sector. He was a board member at Yaşar Holding as well as Tütünbank, where he became chairman in 1994.

Erçel was appointed governor of the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey in 1996 by the cabinet of Turkish President Süleyman Demirel. [ref: Turkey names new Central Bank governor, www.upi.com] Three weeks into his term, Erçel addressed the Institute of International Finance in Istanbul, remarking that his two primary goals as governor would be to reduce inflation and to prepare the Turkish economy for entry into the EU Customs Union. [ref: Remarks by Gazi Erçel, Governor, The Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey, at the Spring Meeting of IIF, Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey]

In December of 1999, Erçel announced an IMF-backed disinflation program with a three-year horizon, aimed at tackling an inflated consumer price index, lowering real interest rates, and redistributing resources throughout the Turkish economy. [ref: Disinflation Program for the Year 2000: Implementation of Exchange Rate and Monetary Policy, Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey] In 2000, Erçel secured $7.5 billion in loans from the IMF to help replenish the central bank's reserves after growing government deficits led to a liquidity shortage. [ref: Turkey markets calmer with IMF cash to boost reserves, www.cnn.com] In response to the 2001 Turkish economic crisis, Erçel resigned as governor on moral grounds, asserting that Turkey needed a reconstituted negotiating team to establish a new IMF agreement. [ref: Turkey's sparring leaders meet, www.news.bbc.co.uk]

After leaving the Central Bank of Turkey, Erçel became a financial columnist for several Turkish newspapers and served as a lecturer on the Faculty of Economics and Administrative Sciences at Istanbul Aydın University. He died at home on June 13, 2022 at the age of 77. [ref: Gazi Erçel kimdir? Gazi Erçel neden vefat etti?, www.cnnturk.com]

Smoking Groups for Art and Visual Composition is a Greek satire political party, founded in 2009. [ref: Ενώπιον κοσμογονίας το πολιτικό σύστημα;, Ημερησία On line] Its president is entrepreneur Nikos Louvros. The party's scope is to defends the rights of smokers. [ref: Οι Κ.Ο.Τ.Ε.Σ. και το... «Χαρίζω Οικόπεδα, Χαρίζω Χρέη», Καθημερινή]

== History ==
In 14 July 2009, it submitted a request to the Council of State to cancel the Avramopoulos Act, which, an action that gave it publicity. [ref: Η πρώτη προσφυγή στο ΣτΕ κατά της απαγόρευσης του καπνίσματος, Ελευθεροτυπία] [ref: Οι ΚΟΤΕΣ «τσιμπούν» το τσιγάρο, ΕΘΝΟΣ] [ref: Υποψήφιοι με χιούμορ, φαντασία, Έθνος]

The part made its first appearance in the 2009 Greek parliamentary election, running only in the parliamentary constituency of Athens A. The Greek press was surprised by the promotion of the part from a BBC show, in which a special mention to the party was made, as the first one globally to support the right of smokers. [ref: Συν & Πλην, Ποντίκι] [ref: Οι λοιποί των εκλογών, Νέα Εγνατία, Καθημερινή Εφημερίδα της Καβάλας] In the elections, is received 1 353 votes, [ref: National Elections October 2009] [ref: Ορισμένοι τα πήγαν καλά. Τι έκαναν οι «μικροί» - Η ΑΝΤΑΡΣΥΑ, οι Τροτσκιστές, το Μ-Λ ΚΚΕ, οι ΚΟΤΕΣ και οι άλλοι, ΤΟ ΒΗΜΑ] managing to keep itself on the focus of media post-election. [ref: Εκλογές και απρόοπτα…, Η Γνώμη]

A year after the elections, Nikos Louvros was called as the party's spokesperson in a radio poll regarding the smoking ban [ref: Απαγόρευση του Καπνίσματος, Flash 96]

In the 2019 parliamentary election, Nikos Louvros participated as a candidate under Syriza. [ref: Εκλογές 2019: Οι υποψήφιοι βουλευτές Α' Αθηνών - Αποτελέσματα εκλογών, ονόματα και κόμματα, NewsIT]

In the May 2023 parliamentary election, the party participated on itw own, gathering 11 522 votes, whereas in the June elections, party leader Louvros stated that he supported KKE. [ref: Οι ΚΟΤΕΣ το έσκασαν από τις εκλογές και στηρίζουν ΚΚΕ, ΤΟ ΒΗΜΑ]

== Other characteristics ==
The posters and emblems of the party made great use of the party's acronym ( ). The party's emblem was an image with three chickens and in its showcase, it used a chicken-related pun ("και στις βουλευτικές εκλογές ΚΟΤΕΣ τσιμπητό", a pun with the Greek words "τσιμπητό" and "δαγκωτό", with the later also meaning "to vote with complete confidence" [ref: ]). The party emblem with the chickens was used several times, in articles talking just about the party [ref: Κ.Ο.Τ.Ε.Σ. τσιμπητό, Νέο πολιτικό κόμμα, LIFO] in articles that mentioned other, smaller parties too, [ref: Διεκδικούν μια θέση στη Βουλή με «όπλο» τους το χιούμορ..., Εφημερίδα ΕΛΕΥΘΕΡΙΑ] even after the elections. The pun ("τσιμπητό") became pretty popular. Much attention was also given to the fact that the name and the party goals expressed originality, humor, [ref: ΕΙΚΟΣΙ ΤΡΙΑ ΚΟΜΜΑΤΑ ΜΕΤΕΧΟΥΝ ΣΤΙΣ ΕΚΛΟΓΕΣ ΟΚΤΩΒΡΙΟΥ, «Χαρίζω χρέη-χαρίζω οικόπεδα» και «Κ.Ο.Τ.Ε.Σ» διεκδικούν τον τίτλο ονομασίας, ΡΕΘΕΜΝΙΩΤΙΚΑ ΝΕΑ] rich fantasy, [ref: Κόμματα με χιούμορ, e-enimerosi.gr] and that the also gave (alongside other parties "more or less serious"), "a different color to the seriousness of the political system" (). [ref: ΚΟΤΕΣ, φως και οικόπεδα, Η Γνώμη]

data.title: Sammy Dyer
data.text:
Sammy Vashon Dyer (born 1905) was an American dancer, choreographer, and dance teacher. He performed in the Broadway musical Runnin’ Wild (1923) and toured the Black theater circuit before settling in Chicago, where he founded the Sammy Dyer School of Dancing in 1933. [ref: Ted Watson "Showfolks Mourn Death Of Dancing Sammy Dyer" (September 1, 1960) The Courier]

== Life and career ==
Dyer became a dancer who performed in Black cast Broadway shows, including Runnin’ Wild in 1923 [ref: Broadway Vet Teaches Adults, Kids Choreographic Intricacies, Chicago Tribune]. In Runnin’ Wild (by Flournoy Miller and Aubrey Lyles, with James Johnson) Sammy Dyer played a Dancing Red Cap.  That performance was credited with popularizing the Charleston on Broadway, and subsequently, all around the country [ref: The Makings of a Broadway Hit: the "Charleston," James P. Johnson, and San Juan Hill, Lincolncenter.org].

By 1931 Dyer had relocated to Chicago, and by 1933 he had rented a storefront on Michigan Avenue to start a children’s dancing school [ref: Our Legacy, Sammy Dyer School of the Theatre]. The Sammy Dyer School of Dancing taught jazz, ballet, tap, and acrobatics, with a focus on professional development. [ref: Muriel Foster: The Only Act of its Kind, Chicago Dance History]

Dyer also worked as a choreographer for prominent clubs and theaters in Chicago, like the Sunset Café, the Regal Theater, where he was ballet master, and managed the theater’s chorus dancers, the Regalettes, and the Palmer House, where he supervised Merriel Abbott's dancers, the Abbotteers. His most important position was at the Club DeLisa, where he managed the entertainment from its opening in 1934 until it closed in 1958 [ref: Earl Calloway “Sammy Dyer Stages Its 75th Anniversary with A Rhapsody in Black” (June 18, 2008) Chicago Defender]. Located on Garfield and State Street, DeLisa became a top entertainment venue in Black Chicago. Open 24 hours a day for much of its run, the club featured house bands led by Fletcher Henderson and Red Saunders. Dyer was DeLisa’s choreographer, stage producer, and was responsible for the chorus dancers [ref: Dance Notes: Julian Swain can still move a little bit, The Chicago Reader], the DeLisa Chorines. Because of his New York and touring history, and relationship with acts like Duke Ellington (whom he knew from his youth D.C., where Dyer worked for Ellington's sign painting business [ref: Jazz dance: the story of American vernacular dance, Da Capo]), Count Basie [ref: How It's Done, Jet], and Cab Calloway [ref: 25 Years of Cab Calloway, Jet], Dyer also handled some talent bookings. It was while working for Henderson at the DeLisa that pianist Herman Blount changed his stage name to Sun Ra, at Dyer’s suggestion [ref: Space is the Place: The Life and time sof Sun Ra, Pantheon].

In the early 1940s Dyer recruited some of the most talented dancers from his school to become the Dyerettes, an act that mixed dancing with comedy, acrobatics, and singing. As children Shirley Hall, Muriel Burns, Clarice White, Florence Saunders, Jean Cornell and Gloria Broussard performed at USO shows, and began appearing at Club DeLisa with the Saunders Orchestra, and playing early morning breakfast shows for overnight patrons. The Dyerettes would become an international touring act and from 1954-1958 were house openers at the Apollo Theater in New York. Ebony magazine declared them “one of the top dancing groups in the country.” [ref: Dyerettes Train Succesors, Ebony]

In addition to his work at the school and in nightclubs, Dyer also helped produce the Epic of a Race pageant at the 1933 Century of Progress World’s Fair at Soldier Field, and worked with prominent dance figures Katherine Dunham [ref: Chorus of 5,000 to be heard in Negro Pageant, Chicago Tribune] and Jeni LeGon [ref: Earl J. Morris “GRAND TOWN DAY AND NIGHT: HAPPY NEW YEAR! HERE'S Hoping That It Will Be Mellow” (Dec 29, 1934) The Pittsburgh Courier (1911-1950); Dec 29, 1934].  He helped organize Finnie’s Masquerade Ball, an annual Halloween drag show on the South Side that ran from 1935 until at least the 1970s [ref: What's the history of drag performance in Chicago?, WBEZ/Curious City]. 5000 people reportedly attended the 1958 Finnie’s Ball at the Trianon Ballroom [ref: Finnie's Ball Attracts 5000 in Chicago, Jet]. Dyer choreographed the 1938 musical The Swing Mikado, an all-black cast interpretation of Gilbert and Sullivan’s Mikado, a production of the WPA's Federal Theatre Project [ref: The Swing Mikado, Internet Broadway Database]. The show moved to Broadway where it competed with a production it inspired, The Hot Mikado (starring Bill “Bojangles” Robinson) which played at a theater across the street.

== Death and legacy ==
In 1959 Sammy Dyer became ill, and the Dyerettes ceased touring to help with his care. After a year-long illness, Dyer died in his native Washington D.C. on August 20, 1960. After a grand funeral at Chicago’s Bethel AME Church, with performances by Al Hibbler and Jo Ann Henderson, his body was returned to his city of birth for burial.

Dyer left the school to Dyerette Shirley Hall [ref: New York Beat, Jet], who had recently married Chess Records executive Ralph Bass. The school continued, with Bass’ financial backing (it relocated to the Chess Records studio building at 2120 S Michigan Avenue for a time) [ref: He didn't give a damn if white people bought it, The Chicago Reader]. Hall renamed it the Sammy Dyer School of the Theatre, and it was billed as “Under the Direction of Shirley Bass and The Dyerettes.” Hall developed a group of young performers in the Dyerettes mold called the Vashonettes (Vashon was Dyer’s middle name). The Vashonettes toured internationally and recorded for Checker Records [ref: The Vashonettes, Stax Museum].

=== Sammy Dyer School of the Theatre ===
The Dyer school became known for the professionalism of their shows, which featured live band accompaniment. Red Saunders led the band for the Dyer shows through the 1970s. He was succeeded by Byron Bowie (of Pieces of Peace, brother of Lester and Joseph Bowie). They also began the Operational Cultural Exchange Program with the Bahamas Dance Theatre in Nassau, which Hall founded after she established the Bahamas as her second home. From 1968 through 1998 groups of young students from Dyer School and Bahamas Dance Theatre would travel to each other’s countries to study and produce shows [ref: A Teacher, A Guardian, A Dancer, The Tribune].

Dyer School alumni and instructors include Brill Barret (M.A.D.D. Rhythms), Kyle Davis (Ballets Jazz Montreal), Randy Duncan (Joel Hall Dance Company), Taylor Edwards (HipLet ballet), Savion Glover, Broadway choreographer Ted Louis Levy (Jelly’s Last Jam), Charles McGregory (Houston Ballet), Star Trek actress Nichelle Nichols [ref: Satirical Flop Brings Star Success: Nichelle Nichols ribs Playboy then works for its club, Ebony], Idella Reed, Darryl Pandy, George “Mo Leggs” Patterson, Tony-nominated actress Lauren Ridloff, and Jumanne Taylor.

Currently (as of 2026), the school shares space with Brill Barrett’s tap dance school at the Harold Washington Cultural Center, on the former site of the Regal Theater.

data.title: Katran (naval drone family)
data.text:
----

Katran is a family of naval unmanned surface vehicles (USV) developed in Ukraine by the defense company MAC HUB. The system is intended for a range of maritime military applications. The drones come in the following models: Katran X1, Katran X1.2, Katran X2, Katran X3, and KATRAN VENOM. [ref: KATRAN • MAC •Military Armored Company HUB]

Each variant is designed to perform specific roles. These may include direct strike missions against naval targets or port infrastructure, as well as surveillance, reconnaissance, patrol, search and rescue operations, mine countermeasures, and the protection of maritime assets. [ref: Ukraine unleashes 'Katran Venom' deadly new drone boat armed with torpedoes, missiles, and Miniguns]

However, the Katran drones are primarily noted for their versatility and their ability to complement one another during complex, multi-layered operations. In such scenarios, they are intended to operate not as individual naval drones, but as an integrated system. [ref: ]

== History ==
According to publicly available sources, the development of the Ukrainian unmanned surface vessels involved the same naval designer who had previously participated in the design of the russian cruiser Moskva. [ref: KATRAN – морський дрон, який може сам визначити та уразити ціль]

The first public reports regarding the use of Katran drones in combat appeared on 10 October 2025. [ref: Freedom of Russia Legion and Ferrata Attacked a Russian Drilling Platform With Katran Drone, Militarnyi] On that date, the Main Directorate of Intelligence of the Ministry of Defence of Ukraine released information about a special operation known as the “Boyko Towers” operation. Control over the offshore platforms involved was described as having strategic significance during the Russo-Ukrainian War.

Representatives of the Ukrainian authorities have stated that detailed information regarding operations involving these drones remains limited in publicly available sources. [ref: Ukraine Unveils "Katran" Secret Naval Drone With 1,000 km Range, Armed With Torpedoes and Minigun, UNITED24 Media]

== Combat use ==
On the night of 21 September 2025, Katran naval drones were reportedly involved in an attack on the so-called “Boyko Towers.” According to published accounts, the unmanned surface vessels were equipped with FPV drones and fixed-wing aerial drones. [ref: Ukraine 'strikes elite Russian unit' on Black Sea oil rig, The Telegraph] [ref: Ukraine DESTROY Russian $500M Oil Rigs in the Black Sea – Then THIS Happened…]

In addition, each Katran platform was reported to carry supplementary unmanned systems, including underwater loitering munitions mounted beneath the hull. These systems were described in media reports as long-range autonomous underwater weapons.

Following the completion of the mission, the drones were reported to have returned to base. Details of the operation were published by The Times. Public information regarding whether Katran X2 units or the KATRAN VENOM combat platform participated in the operation, and what specific roles they may have performed, has not been disclosed. [ref: First they blind, then they burn: the drones thwarting Russia in Black Sea, www.thetimes.com]

In 2026, Ukrainian Defense Forces reportedly began using Katran naval drones not only to strike enemy targets but also to defend Ukrainian cities against Shahed-type UAVs. According to the German newspaper Welt, Russian drones often fly along rivers to avoid Ukrainian air defenses. Welt suggested that naval drones could help cover this gap. A Katran X1.2 can deploy 27 MAC Dead Fly interceptor drones. [ref: Ukraine-Krieg: „Die Russen sind weit hintendran“ – Die Strategie, mit der Kiew den Krieg entscheiden will - WELT, DIE WELT]

MAC HUB is also preparing the Katran family for a new type of mission: intercepting and seizing commercial vessels of the “shadow fleet” carrying sanctioned goods through the Black Sea. The vessels would be warned of their seizure and, following the arrest, escorted to port by Katran naval drones. The drones can simultaneously monitor the vessel, activity on its deck, the airspace above it, and the surrounding waters. [ref: "Ukraine wants naval drones that can detain ships in the Black Sea rather than sink them, commander says", Business Insider]

data.title: Strumigenys yaleogyna
data.text:
Strumigenys yaleogyna is a species of ant in the family Formicidae and subfamily Myrmicinae. It is a social parasite associated with Strumigenys loriae, a larger ant species that serves as its host. The species has been recorded in the tropical rainforests of Papua New Guinea and was first scientifically described in 1956 by Edward O. Wilson and William L. Brown Jr. [ref: New parasitic ants of the genus Kyidris, with notes on ecology and behavior, Insectes Sociaux] [ref: Species: Strumigenys yaleogyna, AntWeb]

==Taxonomy==

Strumigenys yaleogyna was originally described as Kyidris yaleogyna by Wilson and Brown in 1956. The description was published in the scientific journal Insectes Sociaux, in their study of parasitic ants belonging to the genus Kyidris.

The species was subsequently transferred to the genus Pyramica by Barry Bolton in 1999. In 2007, Cesare Baroni Urbani and Maria de Andrade placed it in the genus Strumigenys, its currently accepted classification.

S. yaleogyna belongs to the Strumigenys mutica species group, which includes several closely related ants exhibiting different forms of social parasitism. [ref: Strumigenys yaleogyna, AntWiki]

==Distribution and habitat==

Strumigenys yaleogyna is known from New Guinea, particularly Papua New Guinea, where it inhabits tropical rainforest environments.

The original specimens were collected by Edward O. Wilson between 15 and 20 March 1955 near Bisianumu, close to Sogeri, at an elevation of approximately 500 metres above sea level. The specimens were discovered in mixed colonies containing both S. yaleogyna and S. loriae. The original type series included workers, queens and males, with the holotype designated as a queen. Additional specimens have been recorded from rainforest habitats in Papua New Guinea, including material collected from sifted leaf litter.

==Ecology and behaviour==

===Social parasitism===

Strumigenys yaleogyna is notable for its association with Strumigenys loriae. The two species coexist within the same nests, with S. yaleogyna functioning as a social parasite of its larger host species. Unlike some parasitic ants that have lost their worker caste entirely, S. yaleogyna retains workers. However, the species exhibits reduced predatory abilities and relies on its host for activities such as capturing prey.

Observations by Wilson and Brown showed that workers of S. yaleogyna were largely unable to capture prey successfully, while workers of S. loriae performed the hunting activities.

===Feeding behaviour===

Workers of S. yaleogyna have been observed collecting honeydew from mealybugs (Pseudococcidae) living on plant roots within nest chambers. This behaviour provides an additional food source for the parasitic species and was documented during the original ecological observations.

===Colony structure===

One mixed colony studied by Wilson and Brown was found inside a large, decaying, moss-covered log lying on the rainforest floor. The colony contained approximately 1,170 S. yaleogyna workers, four wingless queens, 84 winged queens and 51 males. The associated S. loriae population contained approximately 1,622 workers and 16 wingless queens. Adults of both species coexisted throughout the nest without obvious hostility. Brood belonging to the two species was found together in several nest chambers.

Researchers also observed trophallaxis, the exchange of liquid food between adult ants, within the mixed colony. These observations provide an example of social parasitism in which the parasite retains a substantial worker population while depending on a closely associated host species.

==Research history==

The ecological relationship between S. yaleogyna and S. loriae was documented in the original 1956 study by Wilson and Brown. The species has subsequently been discussed in taxonomic and evolutionary research on the genus Strumigenys and the development of social parasitism among ants. Barry Bolton's 2000 revision of the ant tribe Dacetini included a treatment of the species and its taxonomic position.

data.title: Jim Dai
data.text:
Jiangang "Jim" Dai (戴建岗) is an operations researcher and applied probabilist known for work on stochastic processing networks, queueing theory, and fluid and diffusion approximations. He is the Leon C. Welch Professor of Engineering in the School of Operations Research and Information Engineering at Cornell University. [ref: Jim Dai, Cornell Duffield Engineering] Dai received the 2024 John von Neumann Theory Prize for contributions to stochastic systems theory [ref: Jim Dai, INFORMS] and the 2018 ACM SIGMETRICS Achievement Award for his analysis of queueing networks. [ref: Dr. Jim Dai 2018 ACM SIGMETRICS Achievement Award, ACM SIGMETRICS]

== Education and career ==

Dai earned bachelor's and master's degrees in mathematics from Nanjing University and a doctorate in mathematics from Stanford University in 1990. [ref: DAI, Jiangang Jim, School of Data Science] He joined the faculty of the Georgia Institute of Technology in 1990 and remained there until moving to Cornell in 2012. At Georgia Tech, he held the Chandler Family Chair in Industrial and Systems Engineering. At Cornell he became the Leon C. Welch Professor of Engineering.

Dai has also held appointments at Tsinghua University, the National University of Singapore, Aarhus University, Stanford, and the University of Wisconsin–Madison. At the Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen, he has served as dean and later honorary dean of the School of Data Science. He was editor-in-chief of the journal Mathematics of Operations Research from 2013 to 2018.

== Research ==

Dai's research concerns mathematical models for allocating resources in processing networks, including communication and computer systems, manufacturing systems, data centers, call centers, hospitals, and transportation services. His work develops fluid and diffusion approximations for analyzing the stability and control of such networks.

In a 1995 paper, "On Positive Harris Recurrence of Multiclass Queueing Networks: A Unified Approach via Fluid Limit Models", Dai established a general connection between the stability of deterministic fluid models and positive recurrence of stochastic processing-network models. INFORMS described the result as a foundation for later work on stochastic-network stability. His later research has addressed heavy-traffic diffusion approximations, reflected Brownian motion, max-weight scheduling, and quantitative approximation bounds based on Stein's method.

With J. Michael Harrison, Dai wrote the monograph Processing Networks: Fluid Models and Stability, published by Cambridge University Press in 2020. [ref: Processing Networks: Fluid Models and Stability, Cambridge University Press]

== Awards and honors ==

INFORMS awarded Dai the 2024 John von Neumann Theory Prize for "fundamental and sustained contributions" to stochastic systems theory, particularly stochastic-network stability and heavy-traffic diffusion approximations. The prize recognizes a body of fundamental, sustained theoretical work in operations research and the management sciences. [ref: John von Neumann Theory Prize, INFORMS]

The ACM SIGMETRICS Achievement Award recognized Dai's contributions to fluid and diffusion analysis of queueing networks and their applications to computer, communication, and processing systems. He is an elected fellow of the Institute of Mathematical Statistics and of INFORMS. His earlier honors include the 1998 Erlang Prize and the 1997 and 2017 Best Publication Awards from the INFORMS Applied Probability Society.

data.title: Raj (Sujit) Kandalgaonkar
data.text:
Raj (Sujit) Kandalgaonkar is a World Class Artist from Dombivli - Ulhasnagar, Maharashtra, India, originally from Malvan. He is known as India's First Name Ganesh Creative Artist.

== Early life ==
Kandalgaonkar was born in Malvan, Maharashtra. He is based in Dombivli - Ulhasnagar, Maharashtra.

== Career ==
This Dombivli-Ulhasnagar based World Class Artist started his Name Shilp journey in 1999.

On 1 September 2015, at Three Art Gallery, Aai Bungalow, Ulhasnagar, he created 407 Name Ganesha artworks in 3 hours and 190 English Name Ganesha arts in 1 hour. [ref: Unique World Records Certificate No. 2016CR169 dated 1 September 2015 for 407 Name Ganesha Artworks in 3 hours and Certificate No. 2016CR168 dated 1 September 2015 for 190 English Name Ganesha Arts in 1 hour at Three Art Gallery, Ulhasnagar, Maharashtra]

He has created 2628 Name Ganesha Artworks as of 14 September 2015. [ref: Unique World Records Certificate No. 2016MM167 dated 14 September 2015 for 2628 Name Ganesha Artworks in 2 years 8 months]

== Kala Daan Yatra ==
Since 2012, free art workshops in schools of Dombivli, Ulhasnagar, Vasai-Virar, Shahapur Adivasi, Mumbai.

== Recent milestone ==
March 2026 - 30,001st Name Ganesh Creative Art gifted to Hon. Deputy CM Maharashtra Eknath Shinde. [ref: March 2026 - 30,001st Name Ganesh Creative Art gifted to Hon. Deputy CM Maharashtra Eknath Shinde]

data.title: Bi-h birize hanney
data.text:
The Universal Biiriize Hanney Alphabet (bI-H) is a modern writing system for African languages, initiated in 2003 and transitioned to digital use in 2025 with the bI-H/Gh keyboard application. It follows the principle of 'One Symbol = One Sound' and has been adapted for various languages, serving an estimated one million users and potentially over 50 million speakers. The project seeks recognition from government institutions and aims for Unicode encoding to ensure its digital preservation and accessibility

data.title: Markpain
data.text:
Markpain (born Mark Wilson; also credited as Mark Andrew Wilson) is an American hip-hop and R&B record producer and songwriter from New York. He is best known as a co-writer of Bell Biv DeVoe's 1993 single "Above the Rim", and was a featured performer on "1-4-All-4-1" from the 1992 compilation East Coast Family Volume One. Both parent albums were certified Gold by the RIAA. He is the founder of the independent label 50 Producers.

== Career ==
=== BIV10 era ===
In the early 1990s Wilson was part of Michael Bivins' Biv 10 Records/Motown circle, performing as one half of the duo Mark Finesse. In 1992 he appeared as a featured performer on "1-4-All-4-1", a track from East Coast Family Volume One that also featured Boyz II Men; the album was certified Gold. In 1993 he co-wrote "Above the Rim", the lead single from Bell Biv DeVoe's second album Hootie Mack, including Michael Bivins' rap verse; [ref: Shazam – "Above the Rim": "Mike's Rap (Co Written By Mark Wilson AKA Markpain)". https://www.shazam.com/song/1440770407/above-the-rim] He is also credited as a co-writer of "Lovely", another track from the album. [ref: "Hootie Mack" album credits, Qobuz: "Lovely" lists Mark Wilson among the composers/lyricists. https://www.qobuz.com/gb-en/album/hootie-mack-bell-biv-devoe/0060252740442] Hootie Mack was certified Gold by the RIAA on August 25, 1993, and the single charted on Billboard's Hot R&B Singles chart. [ref: "Above the Rim (song)", Wikipedia. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Above_the_Rim_(song); "Hootie Mack", Wikipedia. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hootie_Mack] "Above the Rim" was later featured in HBO's 2025 docuseries Celtics City.

=== Production work and 50 Producers ===
Wilson has worked as a producer and engineer for other artists, including Positive K (the 2022 singles "I Get It Done" and "Nobody") and Kool Kim of The UMCs ("Don't Talk No More", 2023), and wrote and produced "Make It Hot" for DJ Epps. In the 2020s he founded 50 Producers, an independent imprint distributed by EMPIRE, through which he releases his own instrumental albums, including the Instruments of Pain series. His compositions are original works created without samples, which he licenses for film, television, and advertising.

data.title: The Last Letter
data.text:
The Last Letter is a romance novel including tragic elements by Rebecca Yarros, published by Entangled Publishing. The book came out in 2019 and alternates between letters and first-person viewpoints. Rebecca Yarros has written a lot of romance books, but her most popular work is the New York Times bestselling Empyrean Series, which is a romantic fantasy series.

== Plot description ==
Ella is a single mother of the twins Masie and Colt, and they live together at the Bed & Breakfast called Solitude, in Telluride, Colorado, which Ella runs. Chaos' whole life circles the military, and he’s in the same unit as Ella’s brother Ryan. Therefore he and Ella start having written correspondence, and they immediately find a connection, and ultimately fall in love.

Unfortunately Maise gets diagnosed with advanced neuroblastoma, and only has a 10 percent chance of surviving the year. Ella’s crushed and shortly after, she finds out that her brother died during a mission. When she doesn’t hear from Chaos, she believes that he died alongside her brother. But Chaos isn’t dead, he just couldn’t bring himself to answer Ella. When Ryan’s last wish is for him to go to Telluride and help Ella, he leaves the Army. But when he arrives at Solitude, he introduces him as Beckett Gentry, his real name, not revealing he’s Chaos. Ella's first response is to shut him out. She tells herself that she doesn’t need his help. But Beckett refuses to leave, and starts working with a search and rescue team in the mountains. Over time Ella let him in more and more, and when he meets the children, they immediately connect. With time Beckett earns her trust, and they eventually fall in love. Together they fight Maise’s cancer and take care of the twins.

But Masie’s treatments are expensive, and the insurance Ella signed for the kids isn’t enough to cover everything. Eventually they discover that Becketts' insurance is enough, and therefore Ella allows him to adopt the kids. But shortly after the papers are signed, the insurance company starts questioning the adoption. For them to believe that the adoption was an act of love, Beckett and Ella need evidence that Beckett knew the twins before Masie got sick. Beckett realises that the only way for his insurance to cover Maise’s treatments, is to show the company his and Ella’s letters. This is the evidence they need, but it also means that Ella will discover his lie.

Ella’s whole world breaks down once again. Beckett apologises deeply and tries to explain that his love isn’t a lie. But Ella doesn’t ever want to see his face again. The twins are incredibly sad that Beckett no longer is a part of their life. But when Beckett one afternoon needs to pick Colt up from suspension, since Ella is at the hospital with Masie, everyone realises how much the kids miss Beckett. Therefore he and Ella find a way to coexist, and they eventually find their way back together. At the same time, they find out that Masie is cancer free, which makes everyone unbelievably happy.

Unfortunately the unthinkable happens. During one of the twins’ field trips, Beckett and his rescue team find out that Colt is missing. While walking on the trail, he and his classmate Emma tripped off a steep cliff, and Colt risked himself to save Emma. They eventually find Colt in very bad condition, and there’s nothing Beckett can do to save him. Words can’t describe how big his, Ella’s and Masie’s grief are and together they mourn him. But with time that loss gets easier to carry, and in the end they manage to live through the pain.

== Major themes ==

=== Learning to trust ===
During her life, Ella has had a lot of experience with men leaving her behind. First her father and then her brother, who often promised to soon be out of the Army, but then ended up dead instead. Her ex husband Jeff, who she met at 18 years old and decided to marry in great haste, also left her after discovering that she was pregnant. Because of her trusting issues she also has a hard time with forgiving lies, and she doesn’t tolerate them. So when Beckett first arrives at Solitude, she believes that he’s the same as her brother and father, too restless to settle down and leaving as soon as reality gets too boring. But because Beckett already is in love with her, because of their written correspondence, and also promised Ryan to help her, he stays in Telluride. One step at a time he  finally earns her trust. But it takes a while, and she has a really hard time with letting him in and admitting to herself that she really is in love with him. But when the big lie is out, when Ella realises that Beckett and Chaos are the same person, and that Beckett has been lying to her during the eleven months that he’s been living at Solitude, her trust is broken. She’s mad at herself for letting Beckett in and believing and trusting him, since he was just like everyone else.

As readers we get to follow along on this inner fight, both before and after the lie is out. In the beginning she starts to have troubles with trusting Beckett and if she should let him in. In the end of the novel, she has the same problem. Can she really trust him again and be sure that he won’t lie another time? After some time she understands how much he fights for her and that the risk of him lying again is worth taking because she loves him so much. To get to understand all of Ella’s consideration about Beckett and their relationship, and to see how she in the end leaves all of her experience behind and embraces their love is so inspiring and wonderful to see.

=== The Reality of Living with a sick child ===
The entire novel is shaped by Masie’s cancer and all of the treatments she has to go through. Right from the start, Ella and her family find out that Masie has advanced neuroblastoma, and has a low percentage of surviving the year. To understand that your child is sick and probably won't grow up is the last thing a parent wants to hear. And to still keep your life together, and live with the fear of losing your child is extremely hard. During the whole book, we get to follow along on that journey, where Ella and her little family need to battle everything going on because of Masie’s cancer. To understand all of the little pieces that a family with a sick child has to handle, make the readers more aware of how hard it actually is. Everyone knows how incredibly sad it is to receive a cancer diagnosis, but most people don’t realise how difficult it is to live everyday with it over your head. Therefore this novel helps to increase that knowledge, and it’s also a big inspiration to all of the moms that have children with cancer. To understand that you’re in this together and that it’s possible to still have a little sparkle in a life that's so full of darkness, must be a big relief.

=== Love as a source of hope and happiness ===
Jeff, Masie and Colts’ dad, left Ella when he found out that she was pregnant, and from that moment Ella had to handle everything regarding the kids by herself. This also meant that she had to fight Maise’s cancer all by herself and it really took a toll on her when she needed to be there both for Masie and Colt. She wasn’t that happy mom that she used to be, instead she laid almost all of her time on Masie’s cancer, plus everything else that needed to be done, like handling the Bed & Breakfast, or sorting out the economy. She felt like a really bad mom, and was incredibly disappointed at herself.

So when she got to know Beckett, who was unbelievably helpful to her and the kids, something changed. This change was especially noticeable when she realised that she had fallen in love with him. Once they started to explore their love, she felt a happiness which she hadn’t felt since before Masie got diagnosed. This was really important for her since she had pushed away her own feelings and needs when she had to be there for Masie. Beckett reminded her that it was okay to feel happiness and joy even though she faced a very difficult period in her life. Throughout the novel, readers are shown how important love is in helping people find that spark, even when reality feels like your worst nightmare. The novel reassures the reader that even the toughest periods can feel lighter at times because of the people you surround yourself with.

== Development history ==
Rebecca Yarros mostly writes romance novels, and in an interview with Angel Reads she got asked what made her start writing romance novels. Her answer was: “I love the intricacies of relationships and how one person can really change us for the rest of our lives, and man does romance fit that bill! I love falling in love, and since I’ve loved my husband for the last twenty-one years, I get to feel that head-over-heels feeling with every new book.” [ref: ]

When The Last Letter first came out, she also got interviewed by Publishers Weekly about her new book. The novel includes a lot of cancer treatments for Masie’s advanced neuroblastoma. Yarros described that one of her friends from flight school went through the same thing with her son as Ella in The Last Letter did, which meant that Yarros could get a hold of treatment records and good resources. “He was one of the first kids to actually survive using the same treatment that Maisie was given. He’s four years cancer-free right now.” Publishers Weekly also got told that she didn’t want to overwhelm the reader by putting too much sadness in all of the chapters. Because it’s a heavy book Yarros wanted to make Beckett the one to help Ella go through her sadness. She means that a mother to a child with cancer can’t live with all the emotions by herself, and therefore need someone near. Rebecca Yarros also wanted the reader to feel a rollercoaster of emotions, “the highest high of falling in love” and “the depth of sadness that’s possible”. Gratefulness is also an emotion Yarros hoped to evoke from the book. “When you witness someone else’s tragedy, when you love that person, even if it’s through a character in a book, it makes you grateful for the things that you have when you close the pages. I hope that when they come out of it, they can look at their kids and know every mom is just doing the best she can.” [ref: ]

== Publication history ==

* Initial Release (February 26, 2019): Released in paperback and ebook formats by Entangled Publishing, as well as editions via Penguin Books.
* Kindle Editions (January 28, 2020/May 2024): Digital re-releases and updates on Amazon Kindle.

* UK/International Paperback (November 24, 2022): Published in the United Kingdom by Transworld Publishers.

* Translations: Has been translated to 4 different international languages, including French (Chère Ella, November 2019), German (Alles, was ich geben kann, August 2024), Spanish (La úlitma carta, April 2025), and Portuguese (A última carta, August 2025).

* Deluxe/Signed Collector's Editions (2025): Re-released as a jacket-less foiled hardcover with stenciled edges and a new letter to readers. [ref: Editions of The Last Letter by Rebecca Yarros, www.goodreads.com]

== Literary significance and reception ==
In October 2025, The Last Letter appeared in third place on the New York Times bestseller list as hardcover fiction. [ref: Hardcover Fiction Books - Best Sellers - Books - Oct. 5, 2025 - The New York Times, The New York Times]

In 2019, the book received a Kirkus Star and made it onto Kirkus Reviews Best Indie Books of the Year. [ref: Best of 2019, Kirkus Reviews]In the review it said: “Yarros’ writing is crisp and sharp, with passages that are poetic without being florid. For example, in a letter to Beckett, Ella writes of motherhood: ‘But I’m not the center of their universe. I’m more like their gravity.’ While the love story is the book’s focus, the subplot involving Maisie’s illness is equally well-developed, and the link between Beckett and the twins is heartfelt and sincere. A thoughtful and pensive tale with intelligent characters and a satisfying romance.” [ref: ]

The Last Letter also got a Publishers Weekly star in 2019, and Louise Fury stated that: “Thanks to Yarros’s beautiful, immersive writing, readers will feel every deep heartbreak and each moment of uplifting love in this tearjerker romance.” [ref: The Last Letter by, www.publishersweekly.com]
