data.title: Recepta.dk
data.text:
Recepta.dk (stylised in lowercase as recepta) is a Danish online medical clinic operated by Recepta ApS, a private limited company based in Copenhagen. It provides consultations with licensed Danish doctors by video or telephone for medical weight loss, erectile dysfunction, low testosterone and male hair loss. When a doctor approves treatment, the prescription is sent electronically to a pharmacy of the patient's choice; the company does not sell medicines itself.

The clinic employs only doctors, and each patient is followed by the same doctor throughout treatment. It is registered as a treatment site under the supervision of the Danish Patient Safety Authority (Styrelsen for Patientsikkerhed).

== History ==
The arrival of GLP-1 receptor agonists such as semaglutide (Wegovy) as prescription treatments for obesity led a number of clinics in Denmark to offer consultations and prescriptions over the internet. In 2024 the consumer programme Kontant on DR showed a reporter of normal weight obtaining a Wegovy prescription from one such clinic after a short telephone call, having given a false weight. Shortly afterwards the Danish Patient Safety Authority tightened its requirements, so that online clinics must see the patient by video before prescribing Wegovy.

Recepta ApS was registered in the Danish Central Business Register in 2026 under industry code 862100, general medical practice activities. The clinic opened the same year, initially offering medical weight loss and treatment of erectile dysfunction, and during 2026 added assessment of low testosterone, treatment of male hair loss and an English-language version of the service for English-speaking residents of Denmark. A Swedish-language site, recepta.se, registers interest ahead of a planned launch in Sweden.

== Services ==
Consultations for weight loss take place by video and those for erectile dysfunction by telephone. Patients choose the time of the consultation, including evenings and weekends, and the company states that most patients can start within 24 hours on weekdays. Prescriptions are sent electronically to the pharmacy chosen by the patient, and the medicine is bought there at the pharmacy's price.

* Medical weight loss: video consultation with a view to treatment with GLP-1-based medicines such as semaglutide and tirzepatide, following the Danish criteria of a body mass index over 30, or over 27 with a weight-related condition.
* Erectile dysfunction: telephone consultation with a view to treatment with sildenafil or tadalafil.
* Low testosterone: doctor-led assessment with blood tests taken at a hospital laboratory, initially for patients in the Capital Region and Central Denmark Region.
* Hair loss: treatment of male pattern hair loss with finasteride.

Payment is by a membership billed every four weeks, which covers the consultation, the prescription, renewals, dose adjustments and written follow-up. The doctor's consultation itself is free of charge, and patients are charged only once a doctor has approved treatment; the medicine is bought separately at the pharmacy.

== Regulation and patient data ==
The clinic is a registered treatment site (behandlingssted) supervised by the Danish Patient Safety Authority and states that it keeps patient records under the same rules as a general practice. Patient data are stored within the EU in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation, and the clinic's doctors are bound by professional confidentiality.

data.title: Hajde grade
data.text:
"Hajde, grade, svi uz naše mlade" is an adapted version of the traditional folk song Ajde, Jano, performed by Professor Aleksandar Čupić in October 2026. The song gained widespread popularity as a viral hit following its live performance at a major student pre-election rally on Slavija Square in Belgrade [ref: Ljudi, miriše na slobodu: Profesor Čupić zapevao na Slaviji pesmu "Ajde grade, svi uz naše mlade"].

== Background and Performance ==
During a high-profile rally in October 2026, Aleksandar Čupić, a professor at the Faculty of Transport and Traffic Engineering in Belgrade, performed a heavily adapted rendition of the well-known folk tune to express solidarity with youth movements and sociopolitical changes.

Pointing out the symbolic shift from traditional motifs of selling property to preserving the future of the younger generation, the performance resonated heavily with crowds and quickly became a cultural touchstone of the movement.

== Lyrics ==
The adapted lyrics focus heavily on themes of collective awakening, regional solidarity, and safeguarding the future for younger generations:

Hajde grade, svi uz naše mlade.
Tama bledi, zora rudi, Srbija se budi.
Tama bledi, zora rudi, Srbija se budi.

Hajde sela, da se pamte dela.
Niz sokake nek' se čuje, stiže mladost, tu je.
Niz sokake nek' se čuje, stiže mladost, tu je.

Mladost peva, bolju zemlju sneva.
Hajde braćo, kako znamo, da je sačuvamo.
Hajde zemljo, kako znamo, da je sačuvamo.

data.title: Forland
data.text:
Forland is a Chinese commercial vehicle brand established in 1999. [ref: Forland Motors Official Website, www.forland.com] [ref: 时代汽车官网 祥菱汽车 瑞沃汽车 领航汽车 时代汽车, forland.foton.com.cn] Its product portfolio includes micro trucks, mini trucks, light-duty trucks, dump trucks, special-purpose vehicles and new energy commercial vehicles. After 28 years development, it has sold 7 million trucks worldwide.

== History ==
Forland was established in China in 1999. [ref: Грузовики Forland набирают популярность в России, Коммерсантъ] Over the following decades, the brand expanded its commercial vehicle product range and developed its presence in domestic and international markets.

The brand’s development has included the introduction of additional vehicle categories, the development of manufacturing capabilities and the establishment of overseas sales and service networks. [ref: Forland Motors Official Website, www.forland.com]

== Products ==
Forland’s product portfolio includes several categories of commercial vehicles:

* Cargo trucks: micro trucks, mini trucks and light-duty trucks for freight transportation.
* Dump trucks: vehicles designed for construction and material transportation.
* Special-purpose vehicles: commercial vehicles configured for specific applications.
* New energy vehicles: electrified commercial vehicles for transportation and logistics.

Model availability and vehicle specifications vary by market.

== Technology and manufacturing ==
Forland’s stated development priorities include new energy technologies, intelligent driving, vehicle engineering and intelligent manufacturing. [ref: Forland Motors Official Website, www.forland.com]

The brand’s corporate materials describe research and development activities, manufacturing facilities and overseas assembly operations supporting its commercial vehicle business.

== International operations ==
Forland markets commercial vehicles in international markets through sales and distribution channels. [ref: FORLAND Enters Libya with New Product Launch - China Truck News -www.chinatrucks.org, www.chinatrucks.org] [ref: Forland Launches 18-Ton Truck in Morocco, Expanding Presence in North Africa_Trucks News_chinatrucks.org, m.chinatrucks.org]Its products serve a range of applications, including urban logistics, freight transportation, construction and specialized transport.

The brand’s official website provides information about its products and international business. [ref: Forland Motors Official Website, www.forland.com]

Official Chinese website: www.forland.foton.com.cn

data.title: Tremendous Trifles
data.text:
This book consists of 39 short stories or essays by G.K. Chesterton that were originally published as newspaper pieces in The Daily News. Later, these were collected and published as a book by Methuen & Co in 1909. [ref: Tremendous Trifles, Methuen & Co.]

== Contents and themes ==

The 39 pieces in this book explores and expounds on everyday occurrences or objects from a unique light and re-enchants them.

== Reception ==

In his commentary dated October 7, 1909, writer Arnold Bennet gives a mixed review in his criticism of Chesterton's work noting his unnuanced assertions and overly-religious worldview. However, praising Chesterton's imagination and prose. This review was later collected in Bennet's 1917 book Books and Persons. [ref: Books and Persons: Being Comments on a Past Epoch, 1908–1911, George H. Doran Company]

A later critic, Dale Ahlquist describes his appreciation of the collections for its attention to ordinary wonders. [ref: Lecture 14: Tremendous Trifles, Society of Gilbert Keith Chesterton]

data.title: 2027 CONCACAF Champions Cup
data.text:
The 2027 CONCACAF Champions Cup will be the 62nd season of the CONCACAF Champions Cup, the premier club association football tournament for North, Central America, and the Caribbean organized by CONCACAF. It is a five-round knockout tournament, with 27 teams qualified based on their national and zonal League and Cup competitions; the first four rounds are played as a two-legged series at the home stadiums of the respective teams, ending with a one-legged final. [ref: 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup: Qualified Clubs, CONCACAF]

The winner will qualify for the 2029 FIFA Club World Cup and the 2027 FIFA Intercontinental Cup.

== Qualification ==
Twenty-seven teams will qualify for the tournament, with five qualifying directly to the round of 16. The remaining 22 teams enter in round one.

In addition to national league competitions in the United States, Mexico, and Canada, 12 of 27 berths are determined by international competitions, including the 2026 Leagues Cup (three), 2026 CONCACAF Caribbean Cup (three) and 2026 CONCACAF Central American Cup (six).

Two Canadian Premier League teams qualify automatically, while the United States-only 2026 U.S. Open Cup knockout competition and Canada-only equivalent, the 2026 Canadian Championship, provide one berth each.

The winners of the three international competitions, along with the winner of MLS Cup 2026 and the champion of the 2025–26 Liga MX season, receive byes into the round of 16.

=== Distribution ===
Twenty-seven teams qualify for the tournament.

* North American Zone: 18 teams (from 3 associations)
* Central American Zone: 6 teams
* Caribbean Zone: 3 teams

Five teams receive a bye into the round of 16.

* The champion of the regional competition for each of CONCACAF's constituent zones; North American, Central American and Caribbean
* The champions of Liga MX of Mexico and Major League Soccer of the United States and Canada (Liga MX has a split Clausura and Apertura system, so the champion team with the higher aggregate points will take this place. If a team won both Apertura and Clausura, they will take this place.)

The remaining 22 teams enter in round one.

* The runners-up and third-place team from the MLS–Liga MX Leagues Cup
* The runners-up and third-place team from the Caribbean Cup
* The runners-up, remaining semifinalists, and two play-in winners from the Central American Cup
* The U.S. Open Cup winners
* The Canadian Championship winners
* The Canadian Premier League regular season winners and playoff champions
* The remaining winner with the worse record, two runners-up, and the two best next clubs by season aggregate from Liga MX
* The MLS Supporters' Shield winners
* The remaining MLS Conference regular-season leader, and the next two teams in the Supporters' Shield table

data.title: Orkla India
data.text:
----

Orkla India Limited is an Indian food products company headquartered in Bengaluru, Karnataka. [ref: We are exploring possibility of launching IPO by 2025: Orkla official, Business Standard] [ref: Orkla India IPO eyes steady double-digit growth driven by organic expansion, CNBC TV18] The company manufactures and markets packaged food products, including spices, spice blends, breakfast mixes, ready-to-eat foods, ready-to-cook foods, snacks, beverages and related products. [ref: MTR Foods parent Orkla India sets IPO price band at Rs 695-730 per share, targets Rs 10,000-crore valuation, Moneycontrol] [ref: MTR, Eastern promoter Orkla sets IPO price at Rs 695-730; the Rs 1,667.54-crore issue opens on Oct 29, The New Indian Express]
Its brands include MTR Foods, Eastern Condiments and Rasoi Magic. [ref: MTR & Eastern owner Orkla readying Rs 700 crore to acquire new brands, says MD-CEO Sanjay Sharma, Deccan Herald]
The company is the Indian unit of Norway-based Orkla ASA. [ref: We are exploring possibility of launching IPO by 2025: Orkla official, Business Standard] [ref: MTR Foods maker Orkla India heads for public debut after 17 years, The Economic Times]
Its shares were listed on BSE and NSE on 6 November 2025 after an initial public offering structured entirely as an offer for sale by existing shareholders. [ref: Orkla IPO listing: Shares debut at 3% premium over the IPO price, Mint]

== History ==

Orkla India was incorporated as MTR Foods Limited on 21 August 1996 under the Companies Act, 1956, with its registered office in Bengaluru, Karnataka. [ref: MTR Foods has been renamed as Orkla India, The Hindu]
Orkla ASA entered India in 2007 through the acquisition of MTR Foods. [ref: The Orkla India (MTR Foods) IPO, Finshots] [ref: How a Norwegian conglomerate preserved the taste of South India and turned it global, WION]

In 2011, Orkla acquired Rasoi Magic through MTR Foods. [ref: Norwegian company Orkla acquires 100% of Rasoi Magic through MTR Foods, FNB News] [ref: MTR Foods renamed to Orkla India; Sunay Bhasin promoted as CEO, Storyboard18]
In 2020, Orkla agreed to acquire a 67.8% stake in Eastern Condiments through MTR Foods; the transaction was completed in 2021. [ref: Norway's Orkla picks up majority stake in Eastern Condiments, Mint] [ref: Orkla expands in India with majority stake in Eastern Condiments, Just Food]
In 2023, MTR Foods and Eastern were merged, and the Indian operations were reorganised under Orkla India with MTR, Eastern and International Business as its business units. [ref: Orkla India announces reorganization with three business units – MTR, Eastern, and International Business, FoodTechBiz] [ref: Sanjay Sharma of Orkla India: Convenience Creator, Mint Lounge]
The company adopted the name Orkla India Private Limited in 2024 before converting into a public limited company and becoming Orkla India Limited in early 2025 [ref: MTR Foods parent Orkla India restructures board ahead of its planned IPO, ETRetail]
In June 2025, Orkla India filed draft papers with the Securities and Exchange Board of India for an initial public offering by existing shareholders. [ref: Indian spices giant eyes offer-for-sale IPO: MTR Foods and Eastern masala owners to offload shares, The Week] [ref: Orkla India IPO: MTR & Eastern owner files draft papers with Sebi, Business Today]

data.title: Rohan Rajbhar
data.text:
Rohan Rajbhar (born 6 February 2006) is an Indian cricketer, who plays as a opening batter. He plays for Rajasthan in domestic cricket. [ref: Basti cricketer Rohan Rajbhar selected for Rajasthan Ranji team; wave of joy in family and village, Dainik Bhaskar]

==Early Life and background==
Rajbhar belongs to Bihra village,located in the kudraha block of Basti District, Uttar Pradesh. His Father,Ramsurat Rajbhar, work in a textile factory in surat, Gujarat,while his mother,Urmila devi,is a homemaker.
He developed an interest in cricket during his childhood,initially playing with plastic and tennis balls in village orchards and open fields. Seeking better training facilities and career opportunities, he later moved to Jaipur, Rajasthan, where he trained extensively before progressing through the state's junior ranks to the senior Ranji trophy team.

Rajbhar made his first-class debut on 11 October 2026 in the 2026–27 Ranji Trophy [ref: RAJ vs TN Cricket Scorecard, Elite, Group C at Jaipur, October 11 - 14, 2026, Cricinfo]
[ref: Karan returns to Ranji trophy in style, puts Rajasthan in control against TN, The Hindu}]

data.title: Gamebanana
data.text:
GameBanana is an online community and repository platform made for sharing, and downloading various mods made by other users for a specific video game. Users can share custom 3D Model, Audio, Texture, GUI, Script, and Tool mods. It includes Forums, Work-In-Progress (W.I.P.) Mods, Requests, Questions, Jams, and Tutorials.
== History ==
It was founded in the mid-2000s under the name CSCentral (which stands for Counter-Strike Central) by Sebastian and originally functioned as a community for modding Counter-Strike. The website achieved significant success by offering free user-generated content for other gamers to use. When the site launched, [https://gamebanana.com/members/1382 Tom] was included on the administrator list, and since then, more people have been added to the moderation and administration team; however, Tom is the only one who has had access to the code since Sebastian left. [ref: https://gamebanana.com/wikis/1917]

As time passed, the community grew larger and expanded into a wider range of topics.

In July 2005, it briefly went to banana.nu, then shortly reverted to CSbanana.com as a result of SEO problems and user confusion.

After that, in 2005 until January 1, 2011, the community agreed the site would be named FPSBanana (Short for First-Person-Shooter Banana); Bananas were chosen as the official mascots of the site because bananas had similarities to a hand-held gun. [ref: https://gamebanana.com/wikis/1917]
==News Coverage==
Nintendo issued more than 60 separate DMCA takedown notices directed to [https://gamebanana.com/members/1676542 Waikuteru], other gamebanana Nintendo game mods have also been targetted by Nintendo. [ref: https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2024/06/nintendo-issues-multiple-dmcas-on-the-modding-site-gamebanana]

PC Gamer covered a [https://gamebanana.com/mods/440088 gamebanana mod]. The mod also includes new costumes/models, animations, textures, voice lines, field dialogue, and more. [ref: https://www.pcgamer.com/you-can-finally-be-a-woman-in-persona-5-royal-thanks-to-a-massive-mod-project/]

data.title: Keto Software
data.text:
= Keto Software   =
Keto Software Oy is a Finnish software company that develops Strategic Portfolio Management (SPM) software for enterprise organizations. The company is headquartered in Hyvinkää, Finland, and provides cloud-based software used for strategic planning, portfolio governance, resource management, and investment management. [ref: About, Keto Software] [ref: Keto Software - yritystiedot, taloustiedot, Finder]

Founded in 2003, Keto Software operates in the Strategic Portfolio Management and Project Portfolio Management software market. The company is led by chief executive officer Veijo Hytti. [ref: Veijo Hytti, Professio]

== History ==
Keto Software Oy was founded in 2003 in Hyvinkää, Finland. The company initially operated under the name Improlity Oy until 2015, when current chief executive officer Veijo Hytti joined the company as a shareholder. The same year, the company adopted its current name, Keto Software Oy. [ref: 32. Veijo Hytti, Keto Software: Kuudes kerta toden sanoo, Rahoituskierros] [ref: ] According to the company, the name "Keto" is derived from the Finnish word for "meadow".

During the 2020s, the company expanded its activities beyond Finland and established a presence in additional European markets, including the United Kingdom and Switzerland. [ref: ]

In November 2024, Keto Software announced an €8.4 million funding round consisting of €6.4 million in equity financing and €2 million in loans. [ref: Finnish startup’s no-code platform attracts €8.4M investment for global growth - ArcticStartup] [ref: Onko tämä yritys seuraava suomalainen menestystarina maailmalla? Ohjelmistoyritys keräsi juuri 6,4 miljoonan euron rahoituksen, Hämeen Sanomat] The funding round was led by Emerald Technology Ventures and included participation from Greencode Ventures, Ilkka Brotherus, and Trauma Holding. [ref: ] According to the company and investors involved in the financing, the funding was intended to support international expansion and continued development of its software platform.

== Software Platform ==
Keto Software develops a cloud-based Strategic Portfolio Management platform used by organizations to manage portfolios, investments, programs, projects, and strategic initiatives. [ref: https://lutpub.lut.fi/handle/10024/171518]

The platform includes functionality for portfolio planning, resource and capacity management, financial planning and governance, workflow management, reporting and analytics. [ref: Keto AI+ Platform Software Pricing, Alternatives & More 2026, Capterra] The platform also incorporates artificial intelligence features designed to assist with portfolio analysis, business case creation, reporting, workflow automation, and decision support. [ref: ] [ref: AI Changing PMO - A Preview, www.aipmo.org]

The platform integrates with enterprise systems including enterprise resource planning (ERP), human resources (HR), and project management software.

== Operations ==
Keto Software operates in the Strategic Portfolio Management software market and serves enterprise organizations across multiple industries.

data.title: Asif Hasan (surgeon)
data.text:
Asif Hasan (born ) is a retired British cardiothoracic surgeon who specialised in congenital heart surgery and paediatric heart and lung transplantation at the Freeman Hospital in Newcastle upon Tyne. He joined the hospital in 1991, was appointed a consultant in 1995, and went on to lead its paediatric cardiac surgery and paediatric transplant services and to direct its cardiopulmonary transplant programme, retiring in 2026. Over his career he performed more than 4,000 open-heart operations, around 3,000 of them as lead surgeon, and estimates that he carried out approximately 400 transplants.

In October 2026 he received the Lifetime Achievement Award at the Pride of Britain Awards.

== Early life and education ==
Hasan graduated in medicine (MBBS) from Dow Medical College in Karachi in 1979. He moved to the United Kingdom from Pakistan in 1981, and obtained the Fellowship of the Royal College of Surgeons of Edinburgh (FRCSEd) in 1984 and the intercollegiate specialty fellowship in cardiothoracic surgery, FRCS (C/Th), in 1994. Before joining the transplant team in Newcastle he had trained in surgery for congenital heart disease.

== Career ==

=== Freeman Hospital ===
Hasan joined the Freeman Hospital in 1991 as a surgeon in cardiopulmonary transplantation, and was appointed a consultant cardiothoracic surgeon there in 1995. He has described the combination of congenital heart surgery and transplantation in one post as an unusual opportunity, and has said that Newcastle became the largest centre in Europe for transplantation in patients with congenital heart disease. The Freeman is one of only two centres in the UK performing heart and lung transplants in children.

He led the hospital's paediatric transplant programme, and by 2018 was described as director of the Freeman's cardiac and pulmonary transplant programme, having succeeded John Dark, who retired in 2017. In that role he was quoted in 2017 on the 30th anniversary of the hospital's paediatric heart and lung transplant programme, which by then had performed 308 paediatric transplants. He and Dark were guest editors of a 2018 issue of the Annals of Cardiothoracic Surgery devoted to transplantation and mechanical circulatory support.

Hasan co-led Newcastle's "bridge to transplant" programme, which uses the Berlin Heart, a paracorporeal ventricular assist device, to keep infants and children alive while they wait for a donor heart. He was also involved in the Freeman's early experience of ABO-incompatible heart transplantation in infants, published in 2004. Hospital colleagues and patients' families have described his willingness to operate on very high-risk children, including patients whom other cardiac centres had declined.

Among his patients was Max Johnson, whose heart transplant at the Freeman in 2017 was filmed for the BBC Two documentary Heart Transplant: A Chance to Live (2018). Johnson and his donor, Keira Ball, gave their names to "Max and Keira's Law", the Organ Donation (Deemed Consent) Act 2019, which introduced an opt-out system of organ donation in England.

Hasan retired from clinical practice in 2026, at the age of 70. Sources give his length of service at the Freeman variously as 30, 35 and 36 years, reflecting the difference between his time as head of the paediatric service and his total time at the hospital since 1991.

=== Surgical technique ===
With Mohamed Nassar and Bari Murtuza, Hasan described a "bootlace" technique for gradual delayed sternal closure after paediatric cardiac surgery, published in the World Journal for Pediatric and Congenital Heart Surgery in 2017. The method is intended for cases in which closing the chest in one step is difficult, particularly after transplantation with a donor heart that is large relative to the recipient; it allows some children to receive donor hearts that would otherwise be too big for them.

=== International work and teaching ===
Hasan has been involved in setting up paediatric cardiac surgery units and supporting surgeons in several countries, and has written about the successes and failures of developing such services in Pakistan. For many years he used his annual leave to travel to Pakistan, where he operated on children and trained local surgical teams on a voluntary basis. Newcastle Hospitals has said he contributed to charity surgical camps overseas and helped train surgeons abroad, and that surgeons he trained now work as consultants around the world. He has been listed as faculty by the European Association for Cardio-Thoracic Surgery, which describes his current interest as teaching and mentoring congenital heart surgeons internationally.

== In the media ==
Hasan's work featured in the BBC Two documentary Heart Transplant: A Chance to Live (2018), filmed at the Freeman Hospital's Institute of Transplantation. In 2023 he appeared in the second series of the Channel 4 documentary series Geordie Hospital, in an episode first broadcast on 13 September 2023 that followed him replacing a heart valve in 13-year-old Seb Hollingsworth, on whom he had first operated as an infant.

== Awards and recognition ==
At the 2026 Pride of Britain Awards, held in London on 19 October 2026 and broadcast on ITV1 on 22 October, Hasan received the Lifetime Achievement Award, presented by Philip Glenister and Anna Friel. He was nominated by former patient Cecilia Adamou, who had received a heart transplant under his care at the age of 11, and nurse Debbie Lawson. During the ceremony he was joined on stage by 19 former patients, aged between 10 and 43. The award was reported by national and regional media in the UK and by media in Pakistan.

== Personal life ==
Hasan is married to Nancy, who accompanied him on his surgical trips to Pakistan. He has described the Northumberland countryside, hockey, swimming, tennis and allotment gardening as interests; he has also helped to keep going a century-old medical cricket team, the "Victorians".

== Selected publications ==

* ABO-incompatible heart transplantation in infants: the Freeman Hospital experience, [[Transplantation (journal)
* Transplantation: A Companion to Specialist Surgical Practice, Elsevier
* Transplantation: A Companion to Specialist Surgical Practice, Elsevier
* Bootlace technique for delayed sternal closure in pediatric cardiac surgery, World Journal for Pediatric & Congenital Heart Surgery
* Back to the future, Annals of Cardiothoracic Surgery
* Paediatric cardiac surgery service development, my experience in the UK and Pakistan, Annals of King Edward Medical University

data.title: Carsten Lucassen
data.text:
Carsten Lucassen is a German communications executive, journalist, and expert in corporate communications, digital transformation, and change management. He currently serves as Head of Communications & Marketing at Sahle Wohnen Group [ref: Website Sahle Group]. Throughout his career, he has held senior communications leadership positions at hagebau Handelsgesellschaft, RKW Group, and the Viessmann Group.

Lucassen is a renowned keynote speaker and publishes regularly on the topics of internal communications and crisis communications. [ref: VOICES Keynote] [ref: Transformation Podcast] [ref: Beyond Magazine]

Career

Lucassen studied English Studies, Communication Science, and Modern History at the Westfälische Wilhelms-Universität Münster from 1989 to 1994.

He began his professional career in journalism. Following a traineeship and editorial role at the Freie Presse in Chemnitz, he joined the Waldeckische Landeszeitung, part of the MADSACK Media Group, where he worked as an editor and later as Head of Editorial Marketing from 1996 to 2009.

In 2009, Lucassen moved into corporate communications at the Viessmann Group. He initially worked in corporate communications before being appointed Head of Digital Communications. In this role, he played a key part in advancing the company’s digital communication strategy and supporting its broader digital transformation efforts.

In 2020, he joined the RKW Group, first serving as Head of Communications and subsequently as Director Communications & Sustainability. His responsibilities included strategic communications leadership and the development of the company’s sustainability and corporate responsibility positioning. [ref: PR Report]

In October 2022, Lucassen was appointed Head of Communications at hagebau Handelsgesellschaft in Soltau, where he was responsible for the organization’s internal and external communications activities. [ref: Baumarktmanager Magazine]

Since 2024, he has served as Head of Communications & Marketing at Sahle Wohnen Group, overseeing corporate communications, marketing, brand development, and digital positioning. [ref: IZ Newspaper]

Profile and background

Lucassen is recognized for combining a journalistic background with extensive leadership experience in corporate communications. His work has focused on helping organizations navigate digital transformation, strengthen stakeholder engagement, and align communication strategies with broader business objectives.

In addition, Lucassen also publishes on diverse subjects such as literary and computer history. [ref: Female Journalists in 19th century England] [ref: In Time - Out of Time]

data.title: United States Boomerang Association
data.text:
The United States Boomerang Association (USBA) is an American nonprofit organization that promotes the science and sport of boomerang throwing. [ref: United States Boomerang Association Records, National Air and Space Museum Archives] It sanctions competitions in the United States, holds national championships, and organizes the national teams that represent the country at the World Boomerang Championships.

== History ==
Newspaper accounts give 1980 as the year the USBA was established. [ref: Boomerang, [[The Daily Herald (Everett)] [ref: Michael 'Gel' Girvin: boomerang master, Federal Way Mirror] The Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum describes it as a nonprofit organization incorporated in 1983 in Connecticut and Ohio. Its members voted to donate the organization's files to the museum through annual compilations of its records; the museum's archives hold USBA correspondence, by-laws, competition information and financial records dating from 1983 to 1987, received as a gift in 1987.

In 2001 the USBA gave a Lifetime Achievement Award to Michael "Gel" Girvin, a former member of the U.S. national team.

== Activities ==
The USBA has held national championships annually. Sports Illustrated published a photo feature on the 2014 U.S. National Boomerang Championships, held in Delaware, Ohio. [ref: U.S. National Boomerang Championships, Sports Illustrated] The 2019 championships were held in Boise, Idaho. Earlier championships were held in Delaware, Ohio, in 2009, [ref: National Boomerang Championships, Sports Illustrated Kids] and the 2023 championships took place at Lorain County Community College in Elyria, Ohio. [ref: What goes around comes around: Elyria's Kenny Barr leads defending champs as national boomerang championships return to LCCC, The Chronicle-Telegram] It was the third consecutive year the event was held there; the championships are open to all ages and include open, novice and women's divisions, with events in accuracy, trick catch, maximum time aloft, fast catch, endurance, Australian round and long distance. In its early years members received a quarterly newsletter, Many Happy Returns, and were ranked according to their performance in sanctioned competition; the association also kept files on boomerang manufacturers, materials and clubs. It sanctions local tournaments, such as the Bellingham Boomfest in Bellingham, Washington, first held in 2025. [ref: Boomerang sport grows with help from Western students, professor, Cascadia Daily News]

National team members are chosen at team trials. The 2026 U.S. Boomerang Team Trials were held in Arlington, Washington, selecting two teams and a developmental youth team for that year's world championships. [ref: Event Recap: 2026 US Boomerang Team Trials glide into Arlington, Snohomish County Sports Commission]

== International competition ==
U.S. teams have won the team title at the World Boomerang Championships in 1994, 2002, 2010 in Rome (regaining the Uncle Toby's Oats Cup from Germany), [ref: Local throwers headed to World Boomerang Championships, The Delaware Gazette] 2016 in Kiel, 2018 in Albuquerque [ref: Boomerang champ Logan Broadbent hopes the sport catches on in Cleveland, [[Ideastream Public Media], 2022 in France and 2026 in Bandung, Indonesia. [ref: WWU Boomerang Club, led by professor, places sixth at world championships, Cascadia Daily News]

The United States hosted the 2024 World Boomerang Championships at Westminster City Park in Westminster, Colorado. [ref: World Boomerang Championships make their way to Colorado, Denver7] It was the first time Colorado hosted the event, which drew about 80 throwers. [ref: Colorado hosts the Boomerang World Championships for the first time, Colorado Public Radio] At that event a U.S. team finished second to a team from Brazil. The U.S. also entered a national adult developmental team at the 2024 championships.

data.title: Giuseppe Ambrosio
data.text:
----

= Giuseppe Ambrosio =
Giuseppe Ambrosio is internationally registered accountant and auditor based in Monaco where he is also authorized as Tax advisor and Tax representative. He is the founder of Ambrosio Audit, an audit and professional services organisation operating through entities including Ambrosio Audit LLP in the United Kingdom and Ambrosio Audit STP SRL in Italy. He is a Fellow Chartered Accountant of the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales (ICAEW), the institute's Contact Member for Monaco, and the Honorary Consul of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines in Monaco.[1][2][3] [ref: Monaco's contact member, www.icaew.com]

== Career ==
Ambrosio qualified as an Italian chartered accountant and statutory auditor in 2000. He began his career at Price Waterhouse, subsequently PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC), and worked in financial-services auditing. In an interview published by Monaco Life in 2017, he described his professional progression, including a secondment to the United Kingdom and subsequent work in Madrid before moving to Monaco.[4] [ref: Match Point with Giuseppe Ambrosio, President Monaco Family Office Association, Monaco Life]

Ambrosio is a Fellow Chartered Accountant of ICAEW and holds a Practice Certificate and Audit Qualification. ICAEW identifies him as its Contact Member for Monaco, a role that serves as a point of contact for members and promotes the institute's activities in the Principality.[1] [ref: Monaco's contact member, www.icaew.com]

His professional registrations include those of Italian chartered accountant and statutory auditor. A list of accountants published by the Italian Embassy in Monaco identifies him as registered with the professional order in the Naples North area and as an Italian statutory auditor.[3] His other listed professional memberships include CPA Australia, the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Zimbabwe, the South African Institute of Chartered Accountants, the Association of National Accountants of Nigeria, CPA Ireland, the Royal Netherlands Institute of Chartered Accountants and the Institute of Certified Public Accountants of Cyprus.[2] [ref: AmbrosioAudit]

Ambrosio has also been involved in business and professional organisations in Monaco. A profile published by the Italian Export Forum describes his activities in the Italian business community and identifies him with the Monaco Single and Multi-Family Office International Association.[5] An earlier profile in Monaco Italia Magazine discussed his work in Monaco and his involvement with Italian business associations.[6] [ref: Giuseppe Ambrosio, Commercialista Italiano nella Monaco del Business, Monaco Italia Magazine]

In November 2025, Ambrosio appeared on Radio Monaco's Le Club programme in an episode hosted by Guillaume Rose, director general of the Monaco Economic Board. The programme discussed Ambrosio's international accounting career and his professional registrations across several jurisdictions.[7] [ref: Le Monaco Economic Board reçoit Giuseppe Ambrosio: l’expertise comptable internationale au service de Monaco, GetPodcast]

Ambrosio is the Honorary Consul of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines in Monaco. The Association des Consuls Honoraires de Monaco lists him in this role and states that he was authorised to serve as honorary consul by Sovereign Ordinance No. 7.460 of 14 May 2019.[8] [ref: Membres, ACHM]

Ambrosio has also been listed as a Business Tourism Honorary Ambassador of the Principality of Monaco. His professional biography identifies him as a special press envoy for SV Times in Europe.[1][2] [ref: Monaco's contact member, www.icaew.com]

== Ambrosio Audit ==
Ambrosio founded Ambrosio Audit in 2020. The organisation operates through legal entities including Ambrosio Audit LLP in the United Kingdom and Ambrosio Audit STP SRL in Italy. Its stated activities include statutory audit, accounting, financial reporting, financial due diligence, company valuation, tax services and business advisory.[2] [ref: AmbrosioAudit]

Ambrosio Audit LLP was incorporated in the United Kingdom on 18 December 2020 under company number OC434752. Companies House records Giuseppe Ambrosio as a designated member of the partnership from that date.[10][11] In 2021, the firm announced that it had obtained audit rights in the United Kingdom following registration with ICAEW.[12] [ref: AMBROSIO AUDIT LLP obtains audit rights in the UK, www.einpresswire.com]

In July 2025, Beursgeschiedenis reported that Ambrosio Audit had entered the Dutch market for audits of companies listed on the Amsterdam Exchange. The article discussed the development in the context of smaller listed companies experiencing difficulties obtaining audited annual accounts and the use of audit firms based outside the Netherlands under European regulations.[13] [ref: A new auditor from Italy - Exchange History]

Dutch accounting publications subsequently reported Ambrosio Audit's registration as an audit firm from another European Union member state authorised to audit public-interest entities in the Netherlands.[14][15] In November 2025, Accountant.nl and Accountancy Vanmorgen reported that Value8 and Hawick Data had appointed Ambrosio Audit to audit their financial statements for the 2025 financial year.[16][17] [ref: Ambrosio Audit nieuwe accountant van Value8 en Hawick Data, Accountant.nl]

The organisation's website lists addresses in Italy, Monaco, the United Kingdom and Switzerland. It also lists professional memberships, qualifications or registrations associated with other jurisdictions. These should be distinguished from the locations where the organisation maintains offices or conducts business.[2] [ref: Why did the Plane Crash?]

== Publications ==
Ambrosio is listed as the author of Why Did the Plane Crash? Professional Tools for the Accountant, the second edition of a book published in July 2026 as part of the Professional Tools for the Accountant series. The retail listing names Rossana Daniele as illustrator, Aldo Formicola as narrator and Ambrosio Audit LLP as publisher.[18]

data.title: Highlight Films
data.text:
----

Highlight Films is an Israeli film, television, and video production services company founded in 1998 and headquartered in Tel Aviv. The company provides production services for international broadcasters, streaming platforms, corporations, and news organizations filming in Israel, the Palestinian territories, and across the Middle East. It is one of the longest-operating production services companies in Israel.

==History==

Highlight Films was founded in 1998 by Noam Shalev, a filmmaker and producer educated in New York City. The company positioned itself as a local production partner for international crews filming in Israel and the Palestinian territories. It operates offices in Tel Aviv, Jerusalem, and Bethlehem.

In 2009, Highlight Films produced Jerusalem 3D, an IMAX documentary film, described as one of the first IMAX productions made in Israel. [ref: Jerusalem The Movie — Production Notes]

The company served as production services company in Israel for Transparent, an Amazon Studios drama series, for episodes filmed in Israel. [ref: Noam Shalev — Biography, IMDb]

In 2023–2025, Highlight Films was commissioned by the Museum of Tolerance, Jerusalem, to produce a video installation about women survivors of the October 7, 2023 attack. [ref: Museum of Tolerance Jerusalem spotlights women's courage on October 7th, hhttps://www.jpost.com]

==Services==

Highlight Films provides production services for visiting international crews and for remote productions. Services include camera crews, equipment rental (including 4K and HD cameras, aerial drone rigs, IMAX, VR 360, and 3D), producer and fixer services, research, logistics, location scouting, security coordination, film permits, post-production, uplink and satellite feed services, and remote production including live video and audio feeds.
The company maintains a stock footage library and also operates the filminisrael.com resource for international production information.

==Notable clients==

Among the international clients for which Highlight Films has provided production services are BBC, BBC Ireland, Netflix, National Geographic, Channel 4, Discovery Channel, Arte, Showtime, FOX, PBS, Microsoft, Intel, HP, Amazon, Apple, Samsung, GE, Verizon, AT&T, The World Bank, USAID, and Yale University.

data.title: Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry
data.text:
The Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry is a public inquiry in the United Kingdom into the implementation and operation of the Horizon accounting system, and the actions taken by Post Office Ltd and others in response to apparent financial shortfalls recorded by the system. The inquiry was established on a non-statutory basis in September 2020 and was converted into a statutory inquiry under the Inquiries Act 2005 on 1 June 2021, with Sir Wyn Williams as chair. [ref: Terms of reference, Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry]

The inquiry examined the development and operation of Horizon, the use of information generated by the system in investigations and prosecutions, the treatment of postmasters, compensation and access to justice, and the governance and oversight of the Post Office and its relationship with government. Its work was divided into seven phases. Public hearings began in February 2022 and concluded with closing submissions in December 2024. [ref: Key Documents, Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry] [ref: British Post Office scandal, Wikipedia]

The first volume of the chair's final report was published on 8 July 2025 and dealt with the human impact of the scandal and financial redress. It contained 19 recommendations. As of July 2026, five further volumes remained in preparation; Sir Wyn Williams said that these would cover the period from the development of Legacy Horizon to events after the end of the litigation brought by Alan Bates and other claimants against the Post Office. [ref: Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry Report: Volume 1, Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry] [ref: Progress Update from Sir Wyn Williams, Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry]

== Background ==

The inquiry arose from the wider British Post Office scandal, in which hundreds of postmasters were prosecuted and thousands more were held financially responsible for apparent losses recorded by Horizon. The system was developed for the Post Office by Fujitsu and began to be rolled out from 1999. Postmasters had reported discrepancies in branch accounts almost from the beginning of the rollout, but the Post Office continued to rely on Horizon data in seeking to recover alleged shortfalls and, in England and Wales, in criminal prosecutions.

In 2009, Computer Weekly reported allegations that Horizon could generate erroneous information, while the Justice for Subpostmasters Alliance was formed to campaign on behalf of affected postmasters. Subsequent investigations, the group litigation brought by 555 postmasters, and judgments of the High Court and Court of Appeal established the basis for challenges to convictions and increased pressure for an independent inquiry.

Following the settlement of the group litigation in 2019 and the beginning of successful appeals against convictions, campaigners and parliamentarians called for a judge-led investigation into the causes of the scandal and the conduct of the Post Office and government.

== Establishment ==

=== Non-statutory inquiry (2020–2021) ===

On 26 February 2020, the government indicated that it would establish an independent inquiry into the Horizon scandal. On 10 June 2020, the government announced an independent review of the Post Office's Horizon IT system and the use of information generated by it in criminal trials.

The review was established as a non-statutory inquiry in September 2020 under the chairmanship of Sir Wyn Williams. It issued a call for evidence on 1 December 2020, and its first public hearing took place on 15 January 2021. Two public hearings were held during the non-statutory phase, followed by a preliminary hearing on the provisional list of issues in November 2021. [ref: Key Documents, Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry]

The original review had a narrower remit than the later statutory inquiry. In particular, it did not include the Post Office's prosecution function, the settlement reached in the group litigation, or the conduct of current or future litigation.

=== Conversion to a statutory inquiry (2021) ===

On 19 May 2021, the government announced that the inquiry would be placed on a statutory footing. It was formally converted under the Inquiries Act 2005 on 1 June 2021, giving the chair additional powers to compel witnesses and require the production of evidence.

The statutory inquiry's terms of reference required it to establish what went wrong with Horizon and the Post Office's use of information from the system; obtain relevant evidence from the Post Office, Fujitsu, government departments and UK Government Investments; assess whether changes promised by the Post Office had been delivered; and examine governance, oversight and whistleblowing arrangements.

The terms of reference also required the inquiry to take account of the findings of the High Court in Bates & Others v Post Office Ltd and the Court of Appeal in R v Hamilton and others, as well as other judgments in which convictions had been quashed.

== Scope and issues ==

The inquiry divided its investigation into seven phases:

# Phase 1 – Human impact: the effects of the Horizon scandal on people adversely affected by the system.
# Phase 2 – Horizon IT system: the procurement, design, pilot, rollout and modification of Horizon.
# Phase 3 – Operation: training, assistance, dispute resolution, knowledge of errors and the rectification of problems.
# Phase 4 – Action against sub-postmasters and others: policy-making, audits, investigations, civil and criminal proceedings, and failures in investigation and disclosure.
# Phase 5 – Redress: access to justice, Second Sight, the Complaint Review and Mediation Scheme, the group litigation, responses to the scandal and compensation schemes.
# Phase 6 – Governance: monitoring of Horizon, contractual arrangements, internal and external audit, technical competence, stakeholder engagement, oversight and whistleblowing.
# Phase 7 – Current practice and procedure and recommendations for the future.

The inquiry also considered devolved matters in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland within the scope of its work.

== Evidence and disclosure ==

The inquiry collected evidence from affected postmasters and their families, current and former employees of the Post Office and Fujitsu, lawyers, accountants, civil servants, ministers and other witnesses. Written evidence included witness statements, internal correspondence, technical material, legal documents and records relating to investigations and prosecutions.

Disclosure became a significant procedural issue during the inquiry. The chair issued a number of directions concerning late disclosure by the Post Office, including directions relating to electronic communications and other documents. There were also hearings concerning legal professional privilege and applications by the Metropolitan Police Service for restrictions on access to certain material. [ref: Reports and statements, Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry]

The inquiry's documentary work was extensive. In 2025 alone, the inquiry said it had published more than 13,500 documents comprising more than 161,000 pages, in addition to witness statements and other material. [ref: End of year newsletter: A review of the Post Office Inquiry in 2025, Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry]

== Phase 1: Human impact (2022) ==

The Phase 1 hearings opened on 14 February 2022 and examined the effects of the Horizon scandal on postmasters and their families.

The inquiry heard evidence concerning the consequences of alleged accounting shortfalls and subsequent investigations, including financial loss, disciplinary action, criminal prosecution, imprisonment, bankruptcy, damage to reputation and relationships, and physical and psychological effects. The evidence included personal accounts from those who had been prosecuted or otherwise affected by Horizon-related disputes.

The first volume of the final report subsequently placed the human impact at the forefront of the inquiry's work. In that report Sir Wyn Williams estimated that approximately 1,000 people had been prosecuted and convicted in the United Kingdom during the relevant period on the basis of Horizon evidence, while about 10,000 people were eligible for compensation through the redress schemes at the time of the report.

The report also recorded the severe consequences experienced by some affected people and linked at least 13 suicides to the scandal. It recorded 59 further people who had reported suicidal thoughts, including ten who said that they had attempted suicide.

The chair emphasised that the inquiry's human-impact material was intended to describe the suffering documented in evidence and did not, in the individual case illustrations, constitute final factual findings about every aspect of the underlying events.

== Phase 2: Horizon IT system (2022) ==

Phase 2 examined the procurement, design, pilot, rollout and modification of the Horizon system. It also considered the involvement of Fujitsu and what was known about faults in the system by the Post Office and Fujitsu during its development and operation.

The hearings considered evidence about Legacy Horizon, which was introduced from 1999, and subsequent versions including Horizon Online. Witnesses included current and former employees involved in the system's development and operation, as well as technical experts and postmasters.

The inquiry heard evidence that Horizon was capable of producing data representing apparent gains or losses that did not necessarily correspond to real movements of money. In 2024, Paul Patterson, Fujitsu's director of European services, told the inquiry that the system had contained bugs, errors and defects from the beginning and apologised for Fujitsu's role in the scandal.

Much of the detailed technical history of Horizon is covered in the separate article Horizon accounting system.

== Phase 3: Operation (2023) ==

Phase 3 examined how Horizon operated in practice, including the training and assistance provided to postmasters, the handling of disputes, knowledge within the Post Office of errors in the system and the steps taken to rectify them.

The hearings took place between January and March 2023.

Evidence considered by the inquiry included the treatment of reports that branch accounts did not reconcile, the response of Post Office staff to complaints, and the extent to which information about known or suspected defects was communicated to decision-makers and postmasters.

The phase also considered technical and operational questions concerning remote access to branch systems and the ability to alter data or transactions. These issues had previously been disputed in litigation and criminal cases and formed part of the inquiry's wider examination of how Horizon information was treated as evidence.

== Interim report on compensation (2023) ==

The inquiry issued its first interim report on compensation on 17 July 2023. It made eight recommendations concerning the administration and operation of the compensation schemes.

The recommendations included:

* strengthening the role and capacity of the Horizon Compensation Advisory Board;
* requiring written reports from the board's meetings and consideration of whether compensation was full and fair;
* preventing compensation payable to bankrupt claimants from being diverted improperly through insolvency proceedings;
* clarifying the tax treatment of compensation under the different schemes;
* providing for the payment of Group Litigation Order compensation after the original deadline of August 2024 where necessary; and
* establishing arrangements for the conclusion of the Horizon Shortfall Scheme.

The government accepted the recommendations in full or in part in October 2023.

The interim report formed part of the inquiry's continuing examination of redress and was followed by further compensation hearings in 2024 and the recommendations contained in Volume 1 of the final report.

== Phase 4: Action against sub-postmasters and others (2023–2024) ==

Phase 4 examined the actions taken against postmasters and others, including policy-making, audits, investigations, civil proceedings, criminal proceedings, disclosure and the responsibility for failures in those processes.

The hearings ran from July 2023 into January 2024.

The inquiry considered evidence about how Horizon data was used in criminal prosecutions and civil disputes, the knowledge of Post Office and Fujitsu personnel about system faults, and the handling of expert evidence.

Among the witnesses was Paul Patterson, who gave evidence about Fujitsu's knowledge of defects in Horizon. The inquiry also heard evidence from former Post Office lawyers and executives, and from people involved in earlier reviews of the system.

The phase included detailed consideration of expert evidence given by Gareth Jenkins, a Fujitsu engineer who had acted as an expert witness in prosecutions. Jenkins gave evidence to the inquiry about his understanding of Horizon and the preparation of expert statements used in legal proceedings.

Phase 4 also involved significant issues concerning disclosure. The chair issued several directions relating to late disclosure by the Post Office in 2023 and 2024.

== Phases 5 and 6: Redress and governance (2024) ==

Phases 5 and 6 began on 9 April 2024. They examined redress and access to justice, earlier investigations by Second Sight, the Complaint Review and Mediation Scheme, the group litigation and the response to the scandal. They also examined governance, monitoring of Horizon, contractual arrangements, internal and external audit, technical competence, stakeholder engagement, oversight and whistleblowing.

=== Redress and access to justice ===

The inquiry heard evidence about the operation of the various compensation schemes established after the Horizon scandal became widely recognised. It examined issues including eligibility, assessment of claims, delays, legal advice, the role of independent panels and the treatment of different categories of claimants.

Evidence was also heard from people who had participated in earlier attempts to investigate Horizon, including representatives and investigators associated with Second Sight. The inquiry examined the history of those investigations and the relationship between the earlier review processes and the later compensation arrangements.

=== Governance and oversight ===

Phase 6 examined the governance of Post Office Ltd and its relationship with government and UK Government Investments. Witnesses included former Post Office executives and board members, government ministers and officials, and senior figures connected with Fujitsu.

Among the issues considered were the extent to which information about Horizon faults reached senior management and government, the effectiveness of internal and external audit, the organisation's approach to whistleblowing, and the way in which risks associated with the system were communicated and managed.

The inquiry also considered the handling of legal advice and the extent to which information about Horizon was passed to ministers, regulators and investigators.

== Phase 7: Current practice and future recommendations (2024) ==

Phase 7 began on 23 September 2024 and considered current Post Office practices and procedures, as well as recommendations for the future.

The inquiry examined the operation of the Post Office after the earlier litigation and subsequent public scrutiny. Evidence included the operation of current contracts, the use of Horizon information and the arrangements governing investigations and dispute resolution.

The inquiry was told that, as recently as 2023, Post Office executives had changed data on Horizon systems used by postmasters without their knowledge. It also heard evidence concerning continuing concerns about the treatment of postmasters and the operation of the Post Office's investigatory powers.

The phase also considered the response of government and other organisations to the findings that had emerged from the scandal and the measures needed to prevent similar failures in future.

== Closing of the hearings (2024) ==

The inquiry's public hearings concluded in December 2024. Closing statements were heard on 16 and 17 December 2024, after which the inquiry entered the Maxwellisation process before publication of the final report.

The Maxwellisation process requires individuals or organisations likely to be criticised in the report to be warned of the substance of the proposed criticism and given an opportunity to make representations before the report is finalised.

== Final report ==

=== Volume 1 (2025) ===

The first volume of Sir Wyn Williams's final report was published on 8 July 2025. It was 162 pages long and considered the human impact of the Horizon scandal and financial redress.

The report stated that it was based on evidence and information available to the chair up to 6 June 2025. It considered the experiences of people affected by Horizon, the operation of the compensation schemes and whether financial redress had been delivered in a full, fair and prompt manner.

The report contained 19 recommendations. They included recommendations concerning the meaning of full and fair redress, access to legal advice for claimants, the assessment and appeal of compensation claims, the operation of the Horizon Shortfall Scheme, the treatment of claims under the overturned convictions and Group Litigation Order schemes, the creation of a standing public body for future redress schemes, and restorative justice.

One recommendation called for the Department, Post Office and Fujitsu to publish a report on any agreed programme of restorative justice or actions taken towards establishing such a programme by 31 October 2025.

=== Remaining volumes (2026–present) ===

Sir Wyn Williams announced in July 2026 that the remainder of his report would comprise five further volumes. He said the volumes would cover the period from the creation of Legacy Horizon to a suitable point in 2026 and would, so far as reasonably possible, follow a chronological narrative.

The chair said that Volumes 2 to 5 were closely connected and should be published together, rather than sequentially. He said Volume 6 would concern events and issues arising after the conclusion of the litigation between Alan Bates and the Post Office and should not be published before the earlier volumes.

As of 8 July 2026, the remaining report was still several months from completion. Warning letters had been sent to people and organisations criticised in Volumes 2 and 3, with further warning letters expected in relation to Volumes 4 to 6.

The inquiry therefore remained a live process after the conclusion of the public hearings, with the publication of the remaining volumes and their recommendations still outstanding.

== Government response and implementation ==

Following publication of Volume 1, the government established a recommendations dashboard to record the recommendations of the Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry, the government's responses and progress towards implementation. The dashboard was first published on 2 March 2026 and was updated on 16 June 2026. [ref: Post Office (Horizon) Inquiry, GOV.UK]

The inquiry's recommendations therefore became part of an ongoing process of government action and monitoring. Further recommendations are expected to arise from the remaining volumes of the final report.

== Legacy project ==

After the conclusion of the public hearings, the inquiry began work on a legacy project intended to preserve the history of the Horizon scandal and the experiences of those affected. In 2025, the inquiry announced that it would work with The Postal Museum on part of the project.

The inquiry's listening project, In Your Own Words, continued after the hearings, allowing people affected by the scandal to submit accounts of their experiences. The inquiry said in December 2025 that 337 people had shared their stories through the project.

data.title: WohSend
data.text:
WohSend is a European file transfer service launched in October 2026. Files are stored and delivered without compression or re-encoding. [ref: WohSend – WeTransfer alternative, AlternativeTo] Data is stored on Cloudflare infrastructure under Portuguese law with optional end-to-end encryption. [ref: Read Customer Service Reviews of wohsend.com, Trustpilot] [ref: WohSend reviews and trust score, ScamAdviser]

The service includes an "Upload Method" feature that modifies MP4 container metadata before upload to social media platforms. [ref: WohSend – European file transfer with zero compression, Reddit] Processing occurs client-side in the browser. [ref: WohSend side project, Reddit]

== History ==
The service was created by Guilherme Anjos, a developer based in Portugal. Development of the Upload Method feature involved testing MP4 container structures against TikTok's CDN behaviour. The platform launched publicly in October 2026 with support for 16 languages.

== Features ==

=== File storage ===
Uploaded files are stored without modification. EXIF metadata in photos is preserved. Videos retain their original resolution, codec and bitrate.

=== Upload Method ===
The feature modifies MP4 container structure before upload to social media platforms:
moov atom positioned before mdat (fast-start flag)
Colour space tags (colr/nclx) preserved
GPS location data removed from metadata
Original codec and bitrate maintained

Supported codecs include H.264 and HEVC/H.265 at resolutions up to 8K with frame rates including 60fps and 120fps.

=== Encryption ===
Optional end-to-end encryption uses a user-provided password. Encrypted files are decrypted after download.

=== Expiration ===
Files expire between 1 hour and 90 days based on user selection.

== Pricing ==
The free tier allows transfers up to 1.5 GB without an account and up to 30 GB with a registered account. Paid tiers (Plus, Pro, Studio) provide additional Upload Method credits. Payment is processed via Stripe with support for regional methods including MB Way, iDEAL and Pix.

== Technology ==
Backend services run on Cloudflare Workers with D1 (SQLite) for database storage and R2 for object storage. The frontend uses vanilla JavaScript and CSS without frameworks.

data.title: Diocese of Sale Catholic Education Limited
data.text:
Diocese of Sale Catholic Education Limited (DOSCEL) is an Australian Catholic education organisation responsible for the governance and operation of Catholic primary and secondary schools with in Diocese of Sale in Victoria, Australia. Established in 2018, the organisation provides system leadership, governance and educational support to schools across south-eastern Victoria and the Gippsland region. [ref: Governance - Diocese of Sale Catholic Education Ltd]

DOSCEL is a company limited by guarantee, with the Bishop of Sale its sole member. Is governance is overseen by a board of directors, supported by an executive leadership team. The organisation's central office is Sion House, Warragul.

== History ==
Before the establishment of DOSCEL, the governance of Catholic schools in the Diocese of Sale was traditionally the responsibility of parish priests. In 2018, school governance was transferred to DOSCEL which was newly established. The transition was intended to provide coordinated governance and support for schools while allowing parish priest to focus more closely on their pastoral and spiritual responsibilities. Under the new structure, DOSCEL assumed responsibility for the employment of school staff and the governance of the schools under its authority.

Maria Kirkwood served as the organisation's inaugural chief executive officer and Director of Catholic Education. She retired in December of 2022 after a decade as Director of Catholic Education in the diocese. Paul Velten was appointed as her successor in 2022. [ref: Announcement of Director Catholic Education, CEO of DOSCEL, www.cdsale.org.au]

== Governance and structure ==
DOSCEL operates as a company limited by guarantee. The Bishop of Sale is the company's sole member and appoints a board of directors to oversee its governance. The executive leadership team manages the organisation's day-to-day operations and provides leadership and services to schools within its jurisdiction.

Its responsibilities include school governance, educational improvement, staff support, child safety, regulatory compliance and the maintenance of Catholic identity across its schools.

== Curriculum ==
All DOSCEL schools are required to complete Religion Education through the use of the Diocesan curriculum 'To Live in Christ Jesus'. This curriculum aims to teach from the Catholic perspective through the invitation of other faiths along the journey. The 'To live in Christ Jesus' framework is based on four core learning strands; Triune God, The Life and Mission of Jesus, Sacramental Church and Christian Life and Catholic Social Teaching. [ref: Diocese of Sale Catholic Education Limited (DOSCEL), Catholic School Parents Victoria]

== Schools ==
DOSCEL governs and operates 44 Catholic schools, comprising 39 primary schools and five secondary colleges, according to its official website in 2026. [ref: Overview, Victorian Catholic Education Authority] The organisation's schools are distributed across south-eastern Victoria, extending from the outer south-eastern suburbs of Melbourne, including Narre Warren and Cranbourne, through Phillip Island and Gippsland to Orbost. [ref: About - Diocese of Sale Catholic Education Ltd]

Two Catholic secondary colleges within the Diocese of Sale are governed separately from DOSCEL: Lavalla Catholic College, which is governed by Marist Schools Australia, and Catholic College Sale, which is governed by Catholic College Sale Limited. These schools remain part of the wider Catholic education community of the diocese but are not directly governed by DOSCEL.

data.text:
----

Dylan Howarth (born October 2001) is a British professional chef, restaurateur, and community organizer based in Bicester, Oxfordshire. He is the founder and director of Howarth Hospitality Ltd and is recognized locally for his culinary contributions to Oxfordshire establishments and his annual charitable initiatives.

== Early Life and Career ==
Howarth was born in October 2001. He pursued a career in the culinary arts, gaining extensive culinary experience in both front-of-house (FOH) and back-of-house (BOH) roles within the British and international hospitality sectors. He also gained early commercial experience working as an assistant in a plumbing supplier warehouse, managing inventory logistics, customer orders, and water testing. [ref: Dylan Howarth Linked In Profile]

In mid-2022, Howarth transitioned fully into professional cooking and worked briefly in international hospitality, spending five months as a Fly-In Fly-Out (FIFO) Chef & Utility worker for the Collar Group in Perth, Western Australia. Upon returning to England, he built his culinary career within the Oxfordshire region, moving through several fast-paced kitchens and gastropubs.

== Employment History ==

* Plumbing Supply Warehouse – Warehouse Assistant (Early Career)
* Collar Group (Perth, Western Australia) – FIFO Chef & Utility Worker (2022)
* Loungers plc (Bicester, Oxfordshire) – Chef De Partie (October 2022 – January 2023)
* Loungers plc (Bicester, Oxfordshire) – Junior Sous Chef (January 2023 – February 2023)
* Loungers plc (Bicester, Oxfordshire) – Sous Chef (February 2023 – August 2023)
* Wells & Co. / The Nightingale (Bicester, Oxfordshire) – Junior Sous Chef (August 2023 – October 2024)
* Wells & Co. / The Nightingale (Bicester, Oxfordshire) – Sous Chef (March 2024 – January 2025)
* The Chequers Weston-on-the-Green (Oxfordshire) – Head Chef (November 2025 – June 2026)
* The Ben Jonson Spud Pub Weston-on-the-Green (Oxfordshire) – Head Chef (September 2026 –Present)
* Howarth Hospitality Ltd (Bicester, Oxfordshire) – Founder and Primary Director (July 2024 – Present)

During his tenure at The Chequers at Weston-on-the-Green, Howarth established a prominent local reputation for traditional British gastropub fare and specialty homemade pies. In July 2024, Howarth expanded his professional footprint by incorporating his independent venture, Howarth Hospitality Ltd, serving as its primary director. He also actively participates in regional hospitality networks, providing mentorship and career guidance to aspiring young chefs seeking apprenticeships in local kitchens.

== Philanthropy ==
Howarth is a prominent local community figure in Bicester due to his philanthropic work. In 2023, he established an annual Christmas Day community meal to support vulnerable, lonely, or socio-economically struggling individuals during the holiday period.

The multi-course meal project is hosted at the Bicester Methodist Church in collaboration with the Open Doors Cafe. The initiative relies on a localized network of volunteers coordinated by Howarth, who manage food preparation on Christmas Eve and service on Christmas Day. By December 2026, the charity initiative will enter its fourth consecutive year of operation.
