data.title: Cayosoft
data.text:
----

Cayosoft is a privately held American software company that develops administration, monitoring, and recovery tools for Microsoft identity environments, including Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, and Microsoft 365. Independent product analyses have described the company’s approach as combining day-to-day hybrid identity administration with change monitoring, rollback, and directory recovery. [ref: Cayosoft Review, Start with Identity] [ref: Cayosoft Administrator: In-Depth Review & Analysis, Expert Insights]

== History ==
Cayosoft was founded in 2013 by Robert Bobel and Andrey Polevoy. In a 2024 profile, Pulse 2.0 discussed the founders’ backgrounds in enterprise identity software, the company’s focus on hybrid Microsoft environments, and its development from administration software into monitoring and recovery products. [ref: Cayosoft: Helping Organizations Manage And Protect Their Microsoft Infrastructures, Pulse 2.0]

The company initially concentrated on automating user, group, licensing, and delegated-administration tasks across on-premises Active Directory and Microsoft cloud services. It later expanded into change auditing, threat monitoring, rollback, and disaster recovery. Start with Identity characterized the resulting platform as strongest for Microsoft-centric organizations seeking administration and resilience in one product, while noting that its narrower Microsoft focus and limited cross-cloud behavioral analytics may make it less suitable for organizations seeking a detection-only or broad software-as-a-service identity-security platform. [ref: Cayosoft Review, Start with Identity]

In 2021, Cayosoft added automated Active Directory forest recovery to its Guardian product line. Independent reviews subsequently examined Guardian as a combined monitoring and recovery product rather than solely as a backup utility. PeerSpot describes it as software for automated protection, anomaly detection, permissions oversight, and recovery, while Start with Identity places it in the identity threat detection and response market but emphasizes its operational-resilience focus. [ref: Cayosoft Guardian reviews 2026, PeerSpot] [ref: Cayosoft Review, Start with Identity]

In March 2024, Cayosoft raised $22.5 million from Centana Growth Partners. Coverage of the financing described the company as a provider of hybrid directory-management and recovery software and reported that the investment was intended to support product development and international expansion. [ref: Cayosoft attracts $22.5m from Centana Growth Partners, FinTech Global]

== Products ==
=== Cayosoft Administrator ===
Cayosoft Administrator automates identity-lifecycle and delegated-administration tasks across hybrid Microsoft environments. In its detailed review, Expert Insights examined onboarding and offboarding, group lifecycle management, license optimization, delegated help-desk access, workflow controls, and audit history. The review identified broad hybrid-Microsoft coverage and policy-based delegation as strengths, while observing that the product is primarily suited to organizations already centered on Microsoft identity services. [ref: Cayosoft Administrator: In-Depth Review & Analysis, Expert Insights]

=== Cayosoft Guardian ===
Cayosoft Guardian provides identity-change monitoring, threat detection, rollback, and recovery. Independent reviews describe its principal distinction as combining administration and monitoring with recovery of individual directory objects and entire Active Directory environments. Reviews also note limits associated with its Microsoft-specific scope and its emphasis on resilience rather than broader cross-cloud identity analytics. [ref: Cayosoft Review, Start with Identity] [ref: Cayosoft Guardian reviews 2026, PeerSpot]

== Patents ==
Cayosoft is the assignee of United States patents covering directory-service recovery and administrative-unit management. U.S. Patent Nos. 12,093,141, 12,399,791, and 12,743,349, granted between September 2024 and September 2026, are related patents in a continuation family titled Systems and methods for directory service backup and recovery. They describe maintaining a standby directory service that can be implemented when a host directory service is interrupted. U.S. Patent No. 12,254,107, granted in March 2025, is titled Orchestration of administrative unit management and covers methods for evaluating and implementing directory-object membership changes across administrative units. [ref: Patents Assigned to CAYOSOFT, INC., Justia Patents Search] [ref: U.S. Patent No. 12,093,141, Google Patents]

== Gartner research mentions ==
Since 2024, Cayosoft has appeared in Gartner research concerning Microsoft identity administration, governance, backup, rollback, and recovery. Inclusion in Gartner research does not constitute an endorsement, ranking, or product recommendation.

=== 2024 ===

* Address Top IAM Hygiene Issues to Enhance Security and Reduce Risk (10 December 2024), which discussed specialized management tools for Active Directory Domain Services and Microsoft Entra ID. [ref: Address Top IAM Hygiene Issues to Enhance Security and Reduce Risk, Gartner]

=== 2025 ===

* Microsoft Intune: The Top 10 Considerations (26 February 2025), concerning administration and governance. [ref: Microsoft Intune: The Top 10 Considerations, Gartner]
* A Well-Run Active Directory Requires Strong Identity Controls (8 May 2025), concerning specialized Active Directory management and backup tools. [ref: A Well-Run Active Directory Requires Strong Identity Controls, Gartner]
* Hype Cycle for Backup and Data Protection Technologies, 2025 (9 July 2025), concerning identity and access management backup. [ref: Hype Cycle for Backup and Data Protection Technologies, 2025, Gartner]

=== 2026 ===

* Market Guide for Microsoft 365 Governance Tools (12 January 2026), concerning Microsoft 365 governance. [ref: Market Guide for Microsoft 365 Governance Tools, Gartner]
* Calculate Google Workspace vs. Microsoft 365 Licensing Costs (27 May 2026), concerning Microsoft 365 licensing. [ref: Calculate Google Workspace vs. Microsoft 365 Licensing Costs, Gartner]
* Market Guide for SaaS Backup (1 June 2026), concerning Microsoft Entra ID backup and recovery. [ref: Market Guide for SaaS Backup, Gartner]
* Hype Cycle for AI Governance Technologies, 2026 (7 August 2026), concerning rollback of AI-agent actions. [ref: Hype Cycle for AI Governance Technologies, 2026, Gartner]
* Establish an Identity Data Layer to Reduce Technical Debt and Secure AI (31 August 2026), concerning identity resilience. [ref: Establish an Identity Data Layer to Reduce Technical Debt and Secure AI, Gartner]
* Innovation Insight: IVIP and IAM Augmentation Vendors Are Disrupting Light IGA (11 September 2026), concerning identity lifecycle workflows and light identity governance. [ref: Innovation Insight: IVIP and IAM Augmentation Vendors Are Disrupting Light IGA, Gartner]
* 2027 Planning Guide for Identity and Access Management (7 October 2026), concerning identity and access management resilience, backup, and recovery. [ref: 2027 Planning Guide for Identity and Access Management, Gartner]
* Create an Application Recovery Strategy That Prevents Ransomware Reinfection (9 October 2026), concerning recovery of Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID. [ref: Create an Application Recovery Strategy That Prevents Ransomware Reinfection, Gartner]

== Awards and recognition ==
In 2020, Cyber Defense Magazine named Cayosoft an Identity Management Innovator.

In 2024, Cayosoft Guardian Forest Recovery won the InfoWorld Technology of the Year Award in the Cloud Backup and Disaster Recovery category. [ref: InfoWorld's 2024 Technology of the Year Award winners, InfoWorld]

The product was also a finalist in the 2024 SC Awards for Best Business Continuity, Disaster and Ransomware Recovery Solution. [ref: 2024 SC Awards Finalists: Best Business Continuity/Disaster/Ransomware Recovery Solution, SC Media]

Cayosoft also received finalist recognition in the 2024 CRN Tech Innovator Awards and the 2024 SINET16 Innovator Awards. [ref: 2024 Tech Innovators Awards, CRN] [ref: Past SINET16 Award Winners, SINET]

In 2025, Cayosoft Guardian was named Enterprise IT Product of the Year in the Entra ID and Active Directory Backup and Recovery category by the publishers of Redmond Magazine, Virtualization & Cloud Review, MedCloudInsider, and PureAI. [ref: Product of the Year, Redmond Magazine]

Guardian Forest Recovery was a finalist in the Cloud Backup and Disaster Recovery category of the 2025 InfoWorld Technology of the Year Awards. [ref: InfoWorld's 2025 Technology of the Year Award winners, InfoWorld]

Cayosoft was also named a finalist for the Secure Access Trailblazer category of the 2026 Microsoft Security Excellence Awards. [ref: Cayosoft recognized as a Microsoft Security Excellence Awards finalist for Secure Access Trailblazer, PRWeb]

In 2026, Cayosoft received the Global InfoSec Editor’s Choice Cyber Resilience Award from Cyber Defense Magazine. [ref: Global InfoSec Awards for 2026 Winners by Company, Cyber Defense Awards] Guardian Protector received a Gold Stevie Award in the American Business Awards. [ref: Search All Past Stevie Winners and Finalists, The Stevie Awards]

Cayosoft was included on Inc. magazine’s 2026 Best Workplaces list. [ref: Cayosoft is a 2026 Inc. Best Workplace, Inc.]

Guardian Instant Forest Recovery also won the 2026 Cybersecurity Stars Award for Most Innovative Ransomware Recovery Platform. [ref: Cayosoft Guardian Instant Forest Recovery, Cybersecurity Stars Awards]

Cayosoft co-founder and chief executive Robert Bobel was named a 2026 Central Ohio Smart 50 honoree. The program recognizes executives for organizational leadership, innovation, impact, and sustainability. [ref: 2026 Columbus Smart 50: Celebrating leadership and impact in Central Ohio, Smart Business]

== Reception ==
Cayosoft products have been reviewed on Gartner Peer Insights. The reviews represent the views of individual users and are separate from Gartner research. [ref: Cayosoft vendor profile, Gartner Peer Insights]

data.title: Laimonas Vilčinskas
data.text:
== Biography ==
Laimonas Vilčinskas is a Lithuanian digital content creator, influencer. He is best known as the founder, owner, and creative director of the global TikTok humor and meme channel [https://www.tiktok.com/@[user] @[user]]. As of 2026, Laimonas has accumulated a multi-million audience of over 1.1 million followers and more than 32.2 million likes on the platform. [ref: https://ecommercefastlane.com/how-tiktok-creators-get-paid-outside-the-us-laimonas-vilcinskas/]

== Career and Brand Collaborations ==
Operating from Lithuania, a market outside of TikTok's Creator Rewards Program, Laimonas sustains his digital media enterprise, Laimonas Vilčinskas Media, through direct commercial partnerships and brand integrations. Because creators in non-monetized European markets receive zero direct platform payouts regardless of viral traffic, direct brand integrations constitute the entirety of his channel's income.

As an influencer and content creator at this scale, he has executed high-profile advertising campaigns for global retail platforms like Temu and artificial intelligence (AI) video generation companies, including Kling AI and Hailuo AI. [ref: https://tynmagazine.com/laimonas-vilcinskas-on-viral-videos-ai-and-humour-in-advertising/] He has also collaborated with international entertainment brands such as Nickelodeon.

Beyond his career as a social media creator, Laimonas works on film sets and is active in electronic music production. He is pursuing higher education in digital marketing and communication at Mykolas Romeris University in Vilnius. Laimonas Vilčinskas has also been cited in European media as an expert commentator on cybersecurity and online safety, specifically regarding digital scams and phishing operations targeting creators. [ref: https://www.dziennikwschodni.pl/artykul/393375,tworcy-internetowi-na-celowniku-oszustow-jak-rozpoznac-falszywe-oferty-i-phishing]

Stars College () is a private school network in Lebanon with four campuses, in Tyre (Abbasiyeh), Zebdine in the Nabatieh Governorate, Ghaziyeh near Sidon, and Dibbiyeh in the Chouf. [ref: Contact us, Stars College] The schools serve students from nursery to Grade 12 and teach the Lebanese national programme, an American high school diploma and the International Baccalaureate (IB). [ref: Stars College – Abbasiyeh, Edarabia]

== History ==
Stars College was established in 2010 with its first campus at Abbasiyeh, in the Tyre district of South Lebanon. By 2011 the school was operating in both Abbasiyeh and Zebdine, according to an interview with its director published by the Lebanese news site Janoubia. [ref: عن مدارس Stars College في الجنوب…, Janoubia]

=== Expansion ===
The school's website now lists two further campuses, at Ghaziyeh near Sidon and at Dibbiyeh in the Chouf.

data.title: Aaron Hertzmann
data.text:
----

Aaron Hertzmann is a computer scientist who works in computer graphics, computer vision, and machine learning, and on the perception and theory of art. He is a principal scientist at Adobe Research and was previously a professor of computer science at the University of Toronto. [ref: Computer Graphics Achievement Award, ACM SIGGRAPH] [ref: Aaron Hertzmann, ACM SIGGRAPH History Archive] His research has included non-photorealistic rendering, the Image Analogies method for example-based image stylization, machine-learning models of human motion for character animation, and computational photography. He received the ACM SIGGRAPH Computer Graphics Achievement Award in 2024 and is a Fellow of the Association for Computing Machinery and of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers. [ref: Announcing ACM SIGGRAPH Award Winners, ACM SIGGRAPH] [ref: Aaron Hertzmann – ACM Fellows (2018), Association for Computing Machinery]

== Education ==
Hertzmann received a bachelor's degree in computer science and art and art history from Rice University in 1996. [ref: Aaron Hertzmann, CS-Can/Info-Can] He received a PhD in computer science from New York University in 2001, supervised by Ken Perlin and Denis Zorin.

== Career ==
After a year as a postdoctoral researcher in the Graphics and Imaging Laboratory (GRAIL) at the University of Washington (2001–2002), [ref: Ras Bodik, Alec Wolman, and Aaron Hertzmann recognized as Fellows of the ACM for outstanding contributions to the field of computing, Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering, University of Washington] Hertzmann joined the Department of Computer Science at the University of Toronto in 2003. He was a professor there until 2013. He joined Adobe in 2012 and became a principal scientist in 2016. He has held an affiliate faculty appointment at the University of Washington since 2005.

Hertzmann was conference co-chair, with Craig Kaplan, of the 2004 Symposium on Non-Photorealistic Animation and Rendering (NPAR). [ref: Proceedings of the 3rd International Symposium on Non-Photorealistic Animation and Rendering, Association for Computing Machinery] He served as the first Conference Papers Director at SIGGRAPH 2022, for a conference track he had advocated creating. He is the editor-in-chief of the journal Foundations and Trends in Computer Graphics and Vision. [ref: Foundations and Trends in Computer Graphics and Vision, Emerald Publishing]

== Research ==
Hertzmann's early work concerned non-photorealistic rendering (NPR), including algorithms for painterly rendering of images and video and for producing line drawings from 3D models. [ref: Paint by Pixel, Science News] His 2001 paper Image Analogies, with Charles Jacobs, Nuria Oliver, Brian Curless and David Salesin, described a method for learning an image filter or artistic style from an example pair of images and applying it to new images. [ref: Image Analogies] [ref: Computer mimics great masters' style, BBC News] [ref: Virtual Virtuosity, [[MIT Technology Review] [ref: Smooth Moves, Computer Graphics World] The SIGGRAPH award citation credits the paper with beginning a new era of machine learning for image authoring and stylization, with influence extending to later image-editing methods based on generative adversarial networks and diffusion models.

Hertzmann's work combining computer graphics with machine learning has included models of character motion learned from motion capture data, capturing non-rigid motion from video, and rotoscoping. [ref: Innovators Under 35: 2004, MIT Technology Review] [ref: A Matter of Style, Computer Graphics World] He also worked on controlling physically simulated human motion. [ref: Walk like a human, New Scientist] The SIGGRAPH award citation describes this as laying groundwork for later uses of reinforcement learning in physics-based animation. His other work includes image deblurring, portrait segmentation and depth-aware photo editing in computational photography, and early machine-learning approaches to graphic design and geometry processing.

Hertzmann has written position articles on the science of art and on art made with generative artificial intelligence, drawing on art history, philosophy and psychology. In them he argues that art is a social activity, and that AI systems act as artistic tools in the way earlier technologies such as photography did, rather than as artists in their own right. [ref: Can Computers Create Art?, Arts] He was a co-author of a 2023 article in Science on art and generative AI. [ref: Art and the science of generative AI, [[Science (journal)]

He has also proposed theories of how people perceive perspective and shape in pictures. These theories seek to explain phenomena that linear perspective theory does not account for. [ref: Toward a Theory of Perspective Perception in Pictures, Journal of Vision] Hertzmann is also a painter. [ref: About the Cover: Music to the Eyes, IEEE Computer Graphics and Applications]

== Awards and honors ==
* 2004: Technology Review TR100 list of innovators under 35 [ref: Canadian researchers at top of class, The Globe and Mail] [ref: The Complete TR100, MIT Technology Review]
* 2006: Sloan Research Fellowship [ref: 2006 Annual Report, Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]
* 2006: Microsoft Research Faculty Fellowship [ref: Faculty Fellowship – Fellows, Microsoft Research]
* 2010: Steacie Prize for Natural Sciences; he was the second computer scientist to receive the prize since its establishment in 1964 [ref: U of T computer prof wins Steacie Prize, CBC News] [ref: Recipients, Steacie Prize for Natural Sciences]
* 2018: Fellow of the Association for Computing Machinery, "for contributions to computer graphics, non-photorealistic rendering, computer animation, and machine learning" [ref: 2018 ACM Fellows Honored for Pivotal Achievements that Underpin the Digital Age, Association for Computing Machinery]
* 2020: IEEE Fellow [ref: IEEE Computer Society Announces 2020 Fellows, IEEE Computer Society]
* 2024: ACM SIGGRAPH Computer Graphics Achievement Award, "for his pioneering work in non-photorealistic animation and rendering (NPR), image synthesis, character animation, computational photography and the interplay between computer generated and traditional art"
* 2024: ACM SIGGRAPH Academy [ref: ACM SIGGRAPH Academy, ACM SIGGRAPH]

== Selected publications ==
* Painterly Rendering with Curved Brush Strokes of Multiple Sizes
* Illustrating Smooth Surfaces
* Style Machines
* Image Analogies
* Learning Physics-Based Motion Style with Nonlinear Inverse Optimization, ACM Transactions on Graphics
* Removing Camera Shake from a Single Photograph, ACM Transactions on Graphics
* Can Computers Create Art?, Arts
* Toward a Theory of Perspective Perception in Pictures, Journal of Vision

data.title: Giuseppe Ambrosio
data.text:
----

= Giuseppe Ambrosio =
Giuseppe Ambrosio is an international accountant and auditor based in Monaco, where he is licensed as Tax advisor and Tax representative. Ambrosio is the founder of Ambrosio Audit, an audit and professional services organization that includes Ambrosio Audit LLP and Ambrosio Audit STP SRL as its operating entities. He is the Fellow Chartered Accountant of the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales (ICAEW), the institute’s Contact Member for Monaco and the Honorary Consul of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines in Monaco. [ref: Monaco's contact member, www.icaew.com] [ref: AmbrosioAudit] [ref: [https://ambprincipatomonaco.esteri.it/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Elenco-Commercialisti.pdf Elenco-Commercialisti.pdf]]

=== Career ===
Ambrosio qualified as an Italian chartered accountant and statutory auditor in 2000. He worked for Price Waterhouse, then PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) after his recruitment as a financial-services auditor. In an interview with Monaco Life in 2017, he described his professional background, including the secondment to the United Kingdom and later a position in Madrid before his move to Monaco. [ref: Match Point with Giuseppe Ambrosio, President Monaco Family Office Association, Monaco Life] Ambrosio is a Fellow Chartered Accountant of ICAEW and holds a Practice Certificate and Audit Qualification. ICAEW designates him as the Contact Member for Monaco, providing liaison and advocacy support for the organization’s members in the country.

His qualifications also include registrations as an Italian chartered accountant and statutory auditor. The list of certified accountants published by the Italian Embassy in Monaco notes his professional designation, with the status of Italian statutory auditor in Naples North. Other professional affiliations listed on his profile include CPA Australia, the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Zimbabwe, South African Institute of Chartered Accountants, Association of National Accountants of Nigeria, CPA Ireland, the Royal Netherlands Institute of Chartered Accountants and the Institute of Certified Public Accountants of Cyprus.

In addition to his professional qualifications, Ambrosio has been involved in business and professional organizations in Monaco. The profile published by the Italian Export Forum recognizes his work in the country’s business community and includes his association with the Monaco Single and Multi-Family Office International Association. [ref: GIUSEPPE AMBROSIO, Italian Export Forum] Another article that appeared in Monaco Italia Magazine in 2017 also described his professional activity in Monaco and engagement with Italian business organizations. [ref: Giuseppe Ambrosio, Commercialista Italiano nella Monaco del Business, Monaco Italia Magazine]In November 2025, Ambrosio was interviewed on Radio Monaco’s Le Club program by Guillaume Rose, director general of the Monaco Economic Board, to discuss his international accountant career and qualifications. [ref: Le Monaco Economic Board reçoit Giuseppe Ambrosio: l’expertise comptable internationale au service de Monaco, GetPodcast]

=== Honorary consul ===
Ambrosio’s status as the Honorary Consul of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines in Monaco is published in the directory of the Association des Consuls Honoraires de Monaco. The listings note his designation by the Sovereign Ordinance No. 7.460 of 14 May 2019. [ref: Membres, ACHM] He has also been appointed Business Tourism Honorary Ambassador of the Principality of Monaco. The professional bio notes his role as a special press envoy for SV Times in Europe.

=== Ambrosio Audit ===
Ambrosio Audit was founded in 2020 as a statutory audit, accounting, financial reporting, financial due diligence, company valuation, tax and business advisory services organization. The firm’s operating entities include Ambrosio Audit LLP in the United Kingdom and Ambrosio Audit STP SRL in Italy.

Ambrosio Audit LLP was incorporated in the United Kingdom on 18 December 2020 (company number OC434752). Companies House records show Giuseppe Ambrosio as a designated member of the partnership from that date. [ref: AMBROSIO AUDIT LLP overview - Find and update company information - GOV.UK, find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk] [ref: Giuseppe AMBROSIO personal appointments - Find and update company information - GOV.UK, find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk] In 2021, Ambrosio Audit announced obtaining audit rights in the United Kingdom after his registration with ICAEW. [ref: AMBROSIO AUDIT LLP obtains audit rights in the UK, www.einpresswire.com]

In July 2025, Beursgeschiedenis published an article on the expansion of Ambrosio Audit into the Netherlands to provide audit services to companies listed on the Amsterdam Exchange. It reported on the challenges faced by smaller quoted companies in preparing audited accounts and the emergence of audit firms outside of the Netherlands able to undertake the work under European Union regulations. [ref: A new auditor from Italy - Exchange History]Dutch accounting publications also reported on Ambrosio Audit’s arrival in the Netherlands as an audit company from another EU member state, authorized to audit public-interest entities in the country. [ref: Met Ambrosio Audit telt Nederland tien oob-accountantskantoren, Accountant.nl] In November 2025, Accountant.nl and Accountancy Vanmorgen reported on the appointment of Ambrosio Audit to prepare accounts for Value8 and Hawick Data for the 2025 financial year. [ref: Ambrosio Audit nieuwe accountant van Value8 en Hawick Data, Accountant.nl]

The firm’s website includes contact details in Italy, Monaco, the United Kingdom and Switzerland. It also includes the professional qualifications, memberships, or registrations as appropriate to the jurisdictions in which it operates. These should be distinguished from the organization’s offices and the locations of its operations.

=== Publications ===
Giuseppe Ambrosio has published Why Did the Plane Crash? Professional Tools for the Accountant as part of the Professional Tools for the Accountant series. The second edition of the book was published in July 2026. The retail listing includes Rossana Daniele as illustrator, Aldo Formicola as narrator and Ambrosio Audit LLP as publisher. [ref: Why did the plane crash?: Professional tools for the accountant, AMBROSIO AUDIT LLP]

data.text:
Nagurbabu N is an Indian advocate whose reported legal work includes public interest litigation concerning advertisements for online betting platforms on Hyderabad Metro Rail infrastructure and litigation involving digital privacy and criminal law.

== Education ==

According to his professional profile, Nagurbabu obtained a Bachelor of Arts degree from Acharya Nagarjuna University and a Bachelor of Laws degree from Smt. Velagapudi Durgamba Siddhartha Law College. [ref: Nagurbabu Law Firm Profile, Nagurbabu Law Firm]

== Legal career ==

=== Public interest litigation concerning betting advertisements ===

In April 2025, Nagurbabu filed a public interest litigation before the Telangana High Court concerning advertisements promoting online betting platforms on Hyderabad Metro Rail trains and premises. The petition sought judicial intervention regarding the display of such advertisements and requested investigations into financial transactions involving Hyderabad Metro Rail Limited and offshore betting platforms. [ref: PIL against HMRL over betting app ads, The New Indian Express]

The Times of India also reported on the petition and identified Nagurbabu as the advocate who filed it. [ref: Petition filed in Telangana high court seeking removal of illegal betting ads from Hyderabad metro, The Times of India]

=== Litigation concerning digital privacy ===

In July 2026, reports covered proceedings before the Telangana High Court concerning online content that disclosed the identity of a sexual-offence survivor. Sakshi Post reported that the court issued interim directions concerning the removal of more than 200 items of digital content identified in the petition and identified Nagurbabu in connection with the litigation. [ref: Telangana High Court Orders Removal of 200 Videos in Advocate Nagurbabu N's Writ, Sakshi Post]

=== Anticipatory bail proceedings ===

In September 2026, Nagurbabu represented folk dancer Eshwar Sai in Criminal Petition No. 14088 of 2026 before the Telangana High Court. Metro India reported that the court granted anticipatory bail subject to conditions in connection with a case registered at Narsingi Police Station in the Cyberabad Commissionerate. [ref: Advocate Nagurbabu N Secures Anticipatory Bail for Folk Dancer Eshwar Sai in Telangana High Court, Metro India]

=== Gold-investment fraud case ===

In 2026, reports by CineJosh and NTV English discussed a gold-investment fraud case involving film producer K. Lakshmikanth Reddy and described Nagurbabu's reported involvement in the related legal proceedings. The reports also discussed the subsequent arrest of the accused. The allegations should not be treated as findings of guilt. [ref: Nagurbabu N: The Legal Force Behind the Arrest of Interstate Criminal K. Lakshmikanth Reddy, CineJosh] [ref: Adv Nagurbabu Behind Producer K. Lakshmikanth Reddy Arrest in Gold Scam, NTV English]

data.title: Jeffrey A. Weber
data.text:
Jeffrey A. Weber is an American investor and independent-film producer. He was a senior executive of York Capital Management and prior to York served as chief executive officer of William A. M. Burden & Co., L.P.

== Early life and education ==
Weber grew up in New York City and was a competitive saber fencer as a child. He later fenced saber at Cornell University before transferring to Williams College, where he continued fencing and subsequently coached the sport.

Weber graduated from Williams College and received a Master of Business Administration from Harvard Business School. [ref: Proxy Statement, U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission]

== Business career ==
Weber began his investment career at Drexel Burnham Lambert and later worked at Chemical Venture Partners. Following CVP, he spent approximately 12 years at William A. M. Burden & Co., L.P., where he served as president and chief executive officer.

In 1998, Forbes profiled William A. M. Burden & Co. as a family investment office and identified Weber, then 33, as the firm's chief executive. The article described the firm's management of Burden family wealth and quoted Weber discussing the firm's investment strategy. Weber subsequently joined York Capital Management. In 2010, Hedge Funds Review identified Weber as president of York Capital Management and quoted him discussing the firm's event-driven investment strategy and the launch of a regulated UCITS fund. [ref: York Event-Driven UCITS Fund: York Capital Management, Hedge Funds Review]

In 2012, the Managed Funds Association announced Weber's election to its board of directors and identified him as president of York Capital Management. [ref: Managed Funds Association Announces New Board Members, Managed Funds Association] In 2014, Institutional Investor identified Weber as president and chief operating officer of York Capital Management in its coverage of the Managed Funds Association's board. [ref: The Morning Brief: Jim Chanos's Legal Troubles; the MFA's New Board, Institutional Investor]

== Fencing ==
After approximately 25 years away from competitive fencing, Weber returned to competition in 2025 when the USA Fencing Summer Nationals were held in Milwaukee. He competed in the Veteran-60 men's saber event at the Baird Center on July 2, 2025. The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reported on his return to competition and identified him as a Milwaukee Bucks minority owner. [ref: Milwaukee hosts USA Summer Nationals: Takeaways from the world's largest fencing tournament, Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]

USA Fencing identified Weber as a lifelong saber fencer and Milwaukee Bucks minority owner in its coverage of the 2025 Summer Nationals. [ref: Milwaukee Welcomes World's Largest Fencing Tournament to Baird Center, USA Fencing] CBS 58 also reported on Weber's participation in the tournament and identified him as a Bucks minority owner. [ref: Largest fencing tournament in the United States heads to Milwaukee, CBS 58]

USA Fencing subsequently profiled Weber's return to competitive fencing and his training with Olympic and world champion saber fencer Eli Dershwitz.

== Film production ==
Weber has worked as an executive producer and investor in independent film. He was an executive producer of the documentary Chasing Chasing Amy, directed by Sav Rodgers, which premiered at the Tribeca Festival. The film's official credits identify Weber as an executive producer. [ref: Cast & Crew, Chasing Chasing Amy]

He was also an executive producer of the independent feature Escaping Ohio, directed by Jessica Michael Davis. Rotten Tomatoes lists Weber among the film's executive producers. [ref: Escaping Ohio: Full Cast & Crew, Rotten Tomatoes]

In March 2026, Davis interviewed Weber on her podcast The Next Film in an episode titled "What Film Investors Actually Look For | Executive Producer Jeffrey Weber." The episode discussed Weber's role as a film investor and executive producer and his involvement in independent-film projects. [ref: ]

== Upcoming projects ==
The March 2026 episode of The Next Film identified Snare, Candy among projects with which Weber was involved. C-Side, Pancake Skank, and Snare were reported in 2026 as upcoming film projects with Weber among its executive producers. [ref: 'Wicked' Breakout Marissa Bode to Star in Body Horror Thriller 'Snare', Bloody Disgusting] [ref: 'Candy' – 'The Boys' Actor Emma Elle Paterson To Star in Upcoming Femme Fatale Thriller, Dread Central]

== Philanthropy ==
Weber has been involved with the Carter Burden Network, a New York nonprofit serving older adults. He has served on the organization's board and has been recognized by the organization for his service. [ref: 2025 Campaign & Senior Prom, Carter Burden Network]

data.title: Konidela Venkata Rao
data.text:
Konidela Venkat Rao (c. 1937 – 24 December 2007) was an Indian government official and occasional actor, best known as the patriarch of the Konidela–Allu family, one of the most prominent film dynasties in Telugu cinema. He was the father of actors Chiranjeevi, Nagendra Babu, and Pawan Kalyan, and the paternal grandfather of actor Ram Charan.

== Personal life ==
Venkat Rao was born in Mogalthur, located in the West Godavari district of Andhra Pradesh. He worked professionally as a government excise inspector and was frequently transferred across different regions during his service. He married Anjana Devi, and the couple had three sons and two daughters:
* Chiranjeevi (born Konidela Sivasankara Varaprasad Rao), prominent actor and politician.
* Nagendra Babu, film producer and actor.
* Pawan Kalyan (born Konidela Kalyan Kumar), actor and Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh.
* Vijaya Durga, mother of actors Sai Durgha Tej and Panja Vaisshnav Tej.
* Madhavi Rao, who maintains a private profile; there is no publicly known information regarding her husband or children.

He passed away due to illness at the age of 70 on 24 December 2007 in Hyderabad.

== Acting career ==
Though primarily dedicated to his career in public service, Venkat Rao had a deep passion for the arts and acted in brief roles. He made his acting debut with a minor role in the 1969 film Jagat Khiladi. Due to family and government duties, he did not pursue full-time acting but strongly encouraged his eldest son, Chiranjeevi, to enter the film industry. Later, he made a notable appearance alongside Chiranjeevi, playing the role of a minister in the 1983 film Mantri Gari Viyyankudu, directed by Bapu.

== Legacy and descendants ==
Through his children, Venkat Rao established the lineage of the "Mega Family" in Tollywood. His prominent grandchildren and notable direct descendants include:
* Grandsons: Ram Charan, Varun Tej, Sai Durgha Tej, Panja Vaisshnav Tej, and Akira Nandan.
* Granddaughters: Sushmitha Konidela, Sreeja Konidela, and Niharika Konidela.
* Great-granddaughters: Klin Kaara Konidela (daughter of Ram Charan), among others.

data.title: Pathya Health
data.text:
Pathya Health (legally Pathyahealth Digital Private Limited) is an Indian preventive-health and women's health company based in Gurugram. Its main product is CycleIQ, an at-home hormone testing system that combines test strips with a smartphone app. [ref: CycleIQ by Pathya: At-home hormone testing for PCOS, Ovulation & Menopause, Pathya Health]

== Background ==
Pathya Health describes itself as a movement in preventive healthcare. The company states that its aim is to help people use health data to act earlier on risks, with an emphasis on chronic and metabolic conditions and, through CycleIQ, on hormonal health. [ref: About Pathya, Pathya Health] It organises its approach around four stated foundations: preventive healthcare, empowerment, data-driven insight and scientific rigour.

The operating company, Pathyahealth Digital Private Limited, is registered in Gurugram, Haryana. [ref: Trust & compliance: Certifications, Pathya Health]

== Products ==
=== CycleIQ test kits ===
CycleIQ is offered as three kits:
* a hormone-tracking kit using luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) strips, intended for people with irregular cycles or polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS);
* an ovulation testing kit using LH strips, intended for fertility prediction; and
* a menopause detection kit using FSH strips, intended to detect hormonal changes associated with the menopause transition.

The company states that the kits are for in-vitro diagnostic use only and that the results are for educational purposes and are not a medical diagnosis.

=== CycleIQ platform ===
Users photograph the test strip with the CycleIQ web app, which reads the strip and records the result against the user's menstrual cycle. According to the company's app, features include period logging and a cycle calendar with estimated ovulation and fertile-window dates, a test history with LH and FSH charts, a hormonal health report, a PCOS assessment that includes the modified Ferriman–Gallwey score for hirsutism, and a question-and-answer assistant that responds with passages from published research. [ref: How to use CycleIQ, Pathya Health]

== Regulatory status ==
The company states that it holds a medical device registration (Form MD-42) in Haryana for its test kits, and that its kits are registered with India's Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

== Distribution ==
CycleIQ is sold through the company's website and through a brand store on Amazon India.

== Media ==
Pathya Health publishes video series on YouTube, including Pro Talk with Pathya, featuring conversations with doctors, and Real Talk with Pathya, featuring personal stories. [ref: The Pathya Podcast Series, Pathya Health]

== Leadership ==
Charu Mathur (also reported as Charu Sachdeva Mathur) is the founder and chief executive officer. Before founding the company she worked in banking and consulting. According to the company's founder's message page, she completed a postgraduate programme at the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (2008–2010), worked as a consultant at the Boston Consulting Group (2010–2013) and then at IndusInd Bank from 2013 to 2025, most recently as chief digital officer. [ref: Founder's message, Pathya Health] In 2025 she was named in the press as head of digital banking and strategy for the existing business at IndusInd Bank. [ref: IndusInd Bank expands INDIE app to all retail customers, SME Street] In the same message she states that she spent over a decade leading strategy, digital transformation and data and decision-science work in banking before founding Pathya Health.

data.title: Michael Mansouri
data.text:
Michael Mansouri is an American technologist, entrepreneur, and cinematography technician. He co-founded the digital cinema and custom engineering company Radiant Images alongside his wife and business partner, Gianna Wolfe. Currently serving as CEO of the cloud collaboration platform MeetMo.io, his work focuses on digital cinematography, virtual reality (VR), volumetric capture, and live 360-degree broadcast technology.

== Early and Personal Life ==
Born in Tehran, Iran, to filmmaker parents, he and his older brother, Babak, worked as child actors prior to the revolution. They starred in their mother's educational television programs, Halghe Jado and Vajhe O Bazi, for Iran's National Television Station in the 1970s. [ref: Cooking for Hollywood, a documentary about Tony Kerum at Kino Croatia, Los Angeles, Cinema Without Borders] The family emigrated to the United States in 1977, settling in the Los Angeles area. His father later passed away in 2015. [ref: Camera Maker Has New Takes on Action Scenes, Los Angeles Business Journal]

== Career and Technology Innovation ==
Early in his career, he worked in technology startups across Silicon Valley and Japan before transitioning to the entertainment industry under the mentorship of American Society of Cinematographers (ASC) member Bob Primes. [ref: Management - Maya Global Solutions, Maya Global Solutions] [ref: Revolutionary Approach to Rogue Filmmaking in Cuba with Piel, The American Society of Cinematographers]

Establishing Radiant Images to provide digital cinema equipment and custom lens modifications, the company gained early industry recognition by supplying custom rigs utilizing the SI-2K digital camera for Danny Boyle's Academy Award-nominated film 127 Hours (2010). [ref: Cameras Used In The End Of Watch Movie, Cinescopophilia] His brother, Babak, joined as an inventor to help develop custom modifications for major studio films. For example, during the production of David Ayer's 2012 film End of Watch, Babak designed the SI-2K Nano, a palm-sized 2K uncompressed RAW camera system built specifically so actors Jake Gyllenhaal and Michael Peña could wear them on their chests for POV shots without restricting movement. [ref: Cameras Used In The End Of Watch Movie, Cinescopophilia] [ref: Cooking for Hollywood, a documentary about Tony Kerum at Kino Croatia, Los Angeles, Cinema Without Borders] The brothers also developed the NOVO, a cinema-modified GoPro capable of utilizing interchangeable professional C-mount lenses. [ref: Cooking for Hollywood, a documentary about Tony Kerum at Kino Croatia, Los Angeles, Cinema Without Borders]

=== Immersive Media and Volumetric Capture ===
Expanding into immersive media formats, the team explored virtual reality, augmented reality, and 360-degree camera arrays. [ref: Going 360 With Radiant Images, The American Society of Cinematographers] This led to the development of the AXA immersive capture system, a modular, hexagon-shaped rig built to accommodate various digital cinema cameras for spherical image capture, earning US Patent 10,860,296. [ref: Radiant Images issued patent on immersive capture system for holographic imaging, Auganix] While acting as a principal for Hawkeye Systems in 2019, the AXA Volumetric Light Field Stage was recognized with a Lumiere Award by the Advanced Imaging Society for Best Holographic Video Technology. [ref: Hawkeye Systems Subsidiary Honoree of the Prestigious Lumiere Award for Best Holographic Video Technology, Hawkeye Systems]

=== Broadcast and Cloud Technology ===
Shifting toward cloud-based real-time video collaboration, the MeetMo.io platform was launched with Gianna Wolfe serving as Vice President. [ref: AI and Software-Defined Infrastructure for Live Media, NVIDIA] [ref: NASA's Artemis Marks First-Ever 8K Immersive Live Broadcast, MeetMo.io] Interactive broadcasting efforts have led to major institutional partnerships, including providing the immersive technical infrastructure for a 2018 NASA and JPL VR project that won an Emmy Award for Outstanding Original Interactive Program. [ref: Reimagining Cinema with Radiant Images' Michael Mansouri - XR, XR for Business]

During the 2022 Artemis 1 launch, MeetMo.io and Felix & Paul Studios delivered an 8K ultra-high-resolution 360° live VR broadcast of the event, streamed globally to Meta Horizon Worlds venues and physical planetarium domes. [ref: NASA's Artemis Marks First-Ever 8K Immersive Live Broadcast, MeetMo.io] A subsequent 2025 partnership with T-Mobile at the Las Vegas Grand Prix integrated augmented reality (AR) overlays over live Formula 1 racing, securing another Lumiere Award for Best Interactive Experience. [ref: T-Mobile, MeetMo, and NantStudios Win Prestigious 2025 Lumiere Award, StockTitan] Additionally, he co-founded Maya Global Solutions in 2019 to focus on network optimization for enterprise video conferencing, where he currently serves as Chairman. [ref: Management - Maya Global Solutions, Maya Global Solutions]

== Filmography and ASC Membership ==
Working frequently as a technical producer or Digital Imaging Technician (DIT), he regularly outfitted complex digital rigs for prominent cinematographers. In 2012, Radiant Images supplied an advanced Sony F65 camera package and custom lenses for the short film Kickstart Theft, directed by Frederic Goodich and shot by Academy Award-winning cinematographer Vilmos Zsigmond. [ref: Worldwide Edition, Film and Digital Times] Zsigmond and Goodich later supported his induction as an Associate Member of the American Society of Cinematographers (ASC). He subsequently served as a co-producer on the 2016 documentary Close Encounters with Vilmos Zsigmond. [ref: Close Encounters with Vilmos Zsigmond, Pierre Filmon]

His notable credits include:
* 127 Hours (2010) – Custom Camera Rigging (Radiant Images)
* Kickstart Theft (2012) – Camera Technician
* Alex Cross (2012) – Digital Imaging Technician
* End of Watch (2012) – Custom POV Camera Rigs (Radiant Images)
* Close Encounters with Vilmos Zsigmond (2016) – Co-producer

data.title: Hanan Shaah
data.text:
Hanan Shaah (also spelled Hanan Shah) is an Indian singer, playback singer and social media personality from Nilambur in Malappuram district, Kerala, who performs primarily in Malayalam. [ref: En route to sonorous fame, The New Indian Express] [ref: Viral musician Hanan Shaah joins 'Kaattalan' movie cast, Onmanorama] He began posting song covers on Instagram during the COVID-19 lockdown in 2020, and later recorded independent singles such as "Chirapunji" and "Kasavinal" before moving into film playback singing. [ref: Heavy rush at Hanan Shah concert triggers chaos, injuries in Kasargod, The News Minute] He made his acting debut in the 2026 Malayalam action film Kattalan. [ref: 'Kattalan' cleared for release with 'A' certificate] [ref: Kattalan First Look Out: Antony Varghese Pepe Ignites Screen In A Fiery Mass Avatar, Filmibeat]

== Early life and education ==
Hanan Shaah is a native of Nilambur in Malappuram district. His father, Siddique Hassan A, is the headmaster of Government Model UP School, Nilambur, and received the Kerala State Teacher Award in 2026; his mother, Nusrath Beevi, is also a teacher. [ref: Hanan Shaah's 'Ippachi' now a state award winner; the teacher who brings gifts for students & keeps learning, Onmanorama] He has two brothers, Ihsan and Afeef, who are also social media influencers.

His parents enrolled him in music classes as a child, but he took a five-year break from music to focus on his studies. He resumed singing at college programmes and graduated in elementary education. Following his family's tradition of teaching, he initially planned to become a teacher and worked as one before deciding to pursue music full-time.

== Career ==
=== Social media and independent music ===
Shaah began posting cover songs on Instagram, and during the 2020 lockdown his following grew from about 4,000 to 75,000 within months. In that period he sang with Ehsaan Noorani of Shankar–Ehsaan–Loy during an Instagram live session, with Noorani accompanying him on guitar, and also collaborated with actress Apoorva Bose and lyricist Shabareesh Varma. One of his covers was noticed by A. R. Ameen, son of A. R. Rahman, whom Shaah has cited as his musical idol.

His 2022 cover of "Parayathe Ariyathe" drew wide attention, and it was followed by a series of popular tracks including "Insanile", "Haniya", "O Kinakkaalam", "Ajjappamada" and "Alappuzha Mullakal". His songs "Chirapunji" (also known as "Chirapunji Mazhayath") and "Kasavinal" further raised his profile.

By July 2025 he had more than 2.2 million Instagram followers, and by November 2025 The News Minute reported the figure as over three million.

=== Playback singing ===
After his independent success, Shaah went on to record songs for Malayalam films.

=== Acting ===
In July 2025 the makers of Kattalan, a pan-Indian action thriller directed by debutant Paul George and produced by Shareef Muhammed under Cubes Entertainments, released a poster introducing Shaah as one of the film's characters. The film stars Antony Varghese alongside Sunil, Kabir Duhan Singh, Jagadish and Siddique. [ref: Antony Varghese Pepe raises the bar; no stunt double in fight scenes along with elephant, Kattalan BTS video out, Kerala Kaumudi] It was certified 'A' by the Central Board of Film Certification in May 2026 ahead of its theatrical release, and began streaming on ManoramaMAX on 13 August 2026. [ref: Kattalan OTT Release Date: When and Where to Watch This Antony Varghese and Sunil Starrer, Esquire India]

=== Live performances ===
Shaah performs at live concerts and stage programmes in Kerala and abroad, including in the United Arab Emirates. [ref: Kerala street singer Anish Bhai performs with Braille lyrics, takes stages and social media by storm, Onmanorama] In 2026 he shared the stage with Anish, a blind street singer whose videos had gone viral, at a shop inauguration in Perinthalmanna; the appearance brought wider recognition to Anish's troupe, Malabar Blind Voice.

==== 2025 Kasaragod concert incident ====
On 23 November 2025, a concert featuring Shaah, held as part of an expo at a ground near the private bus stand in Kasaragod, was stopped by police after severe overcrowding. [ref: Hanan Shaah's concert stopped in Kasaragod after overcrowding triggers chaos, Deccan Herald] A stampede-like rush led to several attendees fainting or suffering breathing difficulties; reports of the number hospitalised or injured ranged from around 16 to over 30, and no deaths were reported. [ref: Overcrowding at Hanan Shaah concert sends 16 to hospital; organisers booked, Madhyamam] [ref: Stampede-like crowd surge injures 20 at Kasaragod concert, The South First] [ref: Five booked after music concert rush leaves several injured in Kasaragod, Onmanorama] Police registered a case against the event's organisers; according to the FIR, police had permitted an audience of 3,000, but the organisers allegedly sold tickets to more than 10,000 people despite a written warning.

data.title: Murod Jumaev
data.text:
Murod Gafurovich Jumaev (; ) is an Uzbek businessman, the founder and director of the courier and logistics company EMU Express.

== Early career ==
Jumaev studied postal communication technologies at the Tashkent University of Information Technologies. From 2008 he worked at the Bukhara branch of the national postal operator Oʻzbekiston pochtasi, where he became familiar with its internal processes.

== EMU Express ==
In 2016, during his master's studies at the Higher School of Business and Entrepreneurship () in Tashkent, Jumaev proposed the idea of a courier company, which a group of six students developed as a business-planning project. The company, EMU Express, was established on 7 November 2016. As of 2026 Jumaev is its director. By that year the company reported more than 200 branches and service points in Uzbekistan, over 500 employees and a network of offices in Kazakhstan.

== Public commentary ==
In April 2018, during public discussion of a proposal to raise the tax on dividends to 25%, Jumaev argued that the measure could be a major blow to entrepreneurs.

data.title: Expo Agrofuturo
data.text:
Expo Agrofuturo is an annual trade fair for the agriculture and agribusiness sector held in Colombia. It brings together producers, traders, suppliers of machinery, inputs and technology, investors and financial institutions, and combines exhibition halls with business matchmaking and a conference programme. [ref: Informe de feria: Expo Agrofuturo 2022, Economic and Commercial Office of the Embassy of Spain in Bogotá; ICEX] Since 2018 it has been organised in partnership with Corferias, alternating between Medellín, at the Plaza Mayor convention centre, and Bogotá, at the Corferias fairgrounds. [ref: Expo Agrofuturo se extiende y llegará a Bogotá en 2018, Agronegocios]

== History ==
The fair began in Medellín, where its early editions took place at Plaza Mayor. Its fifth edition, directed by Ricardo Jaramillo Gaviria, was held in June 2011 and included the third International Agricultural Congress and the second International Livestock Forum. [ref: Inicia en Medellín Quinta Feria Expo Agrofuturo 2011, ABC Economía] The ninth edition took place at the same venue in 2015, [ref: Aprenda y conozca las innovaciones del campo en Expo Agrofuturo 2015, CONtexto Ganadero] and the tenth from 7 to 9 September 2016. [ref: Este 7 de septiembre empieza el VIII Congreso Internacional Agropecuario, Semana]

The eleventh edition, in 2017, drew around 25,000 visitors from some 30 countries and 420 participating companies. That year a strategic partnership with Corferias was announced, under which the fair would be held in Bogotá in even-numbered years and in Medellín in odd-numbered years. Accordingly, the 2018 edition took place at Corferias from 22 to 24 August. [ref: Expo Agrofuturo 2018: Regulamento de participação, Apex-Brasil] In 2019 the fair returned to Plaza Mayor from 18 to 20 September, with Italy as guest country of honour. [ref: Expo Agrofuturo: el campo colombiano se reúne en Medellín, Portafolio] [ref: Lanzamiento de la feria Expo Agrofuturo 2019 se llevó a cabo en la ciudad de Medellín, La República]

The fifteenth edition was held at Corferias from 26 to 28 October 2022, with the European Union as guest of honour. According to a report by the Economic and Commercial Office of the Spanish Embassy, it featured more than 350 exhibitors, about 120 talks and over 11,000 professional visitors. The sixteenth edition returned to Medellín from 6 to 8 September 2023. [ref: Expoagrofuturo regresa a Medellín para el desarrollo de un agro más inteligente y sostenible, CONtexto Ganadero]

The seventeenth edition (Bogotá, 2024) had more than 320 exhibitors from 15 countries and 13,500 attendees, with the department of Casanare as guest region. [ref: Expo Agrofuturo cerró con expectativas de negocio por US$6,16 millones, Portafolio] The eighteenth edition was held at Plaza Mayor from 10 to 12 September 2025, with 388 exhibitors from Colombia and eleven other countries and 14,154 visitors. [ref: Expo Agrofuturo Concludes with Over 14,000 Attendees and Nearly $6 Million USD in Projected Business Deals, Finance Colombia]

The 2026 edition took place at Corferias from 21 to 23 October. [ref: El conocimiento del agro se transforma: así será la gran novedad de Expo Agrofuturo 2026, Publimetro Colombia] It hosted the first International Meeting of Market Squares (Encuentro Internacional de Plazas de Mercado). [ref: Bogotá será sede del Primer Encuentro Internacional de Plazas de Mercado en Expo Agrofuturo 2026, Noticias RCN]

== Organisation ==
The fair is organised by the company Agrilink together with Corferias. In 2018 the organisers were listed as Grupo NovoAgro and Corferias. Its spokespeople have included co-founder Ricardo Jaramillo [ref: Medellín se consolida como una plataforma para promover el campo inteligente en Latinoamérica, Publimetro Colombia] and Doris Chingaté, Expo Agrofuturo project manager at Corferias.

== Programme ==
Alongside the commercial halls, organised by production sector such as fruit and vegetables, livestock and machinery, or grains, oils and forestry, the fair includes several parallel spaces:

* FIXA (Agrofuturo Innovation Forum): the fair's academic component, traditionally split into one day devoted to livestock and another to agriculture. In 2026 it was reorganised as a "knowledge ecosystem" with six themed spaces across the venue, covering technology, productivity, agribusiness, livestock, entrepreneurship and finance.
* AgStar: a space for startups in the AgTech, FoodTech and AnimalTech categories.
* Business matchmaking: meetings between exhibitors and domestic and international buyers. In 2025, under the name AgroMatch, it connected 160 exhibitors with 33 buyers in 459 meetings.
* Agrotalks and Agrosolutions: exhibitor presentations and free advisory sessions for attendees.

data.title: Dar Erengà
data.text:
Dar Erenga is a historical and geographical region located in the northern part of West Darfur State, Sudan. Situated along the modern Sudan–Chad border, the region historically functioned as a transitional corridor linking various sultanates in western Sudan. Its administrative and territorial boundaries were formally documented in early 20th-century treaties. Geographically and historically, Dar Erenga forms part of Dar Masalit and is situated between the Masalit country proper and Dar Qimr. [ref: Darfur Linguistics, Sudan Notes and Records]

==== Geography and Administrative Boundaries ====
The region is centered in northern West Darfur, where its lands (hawakir) border several historical territories:North: It shares borders with Dar Tama (extending toward Tumtuma) and Dar Jebel near the town of Sileia.
• South: It opens directly into Dar Masalit, situated immediately north of the city of El Geneina and the town of Adré. West: The frontier runs parallel to the international border along the strategic cross-border axis leading to Dar Sila.In his 1924 study on the Masalit Sultanate, British administrator Reginald Davies documented this administrative layout, noting that Dar Erenga formed a crucial geographical and political link between Dar Masalit to the south and Dar Jebel and Dar Qimr to the northeast. [ref: The Masalit Sultanate, Sudan Notes and Records] [ref: Darfur – Livelihoods Under Siege, Feinstein International Famine Center, Tufts University]

==== Ethnic Composition and History ====
The history of Dar Erenga is linked to a confederation of closely related ethnic groups, including the Awra, Asungor, Mararit, Girga, Dula, and Shali.
Historical records indicate that "Dar Erenga" began to emerge as a unified administrative entity in the late 1880s. Prior to this consolidation, each ethnic group maintained its own local leadership within the western Darfur administrative framework.
The explorer Gustav Nachtigal described these groups as distinct yet interconnected entities sharing a common lineage with the Qimr (Guimir). Nachtigal historically referred to the area on the eastern bank of Wadi Kaja as "Dar Shali," which later integrated into the core geography of contemporary Dar Erenga. [ref: Mahdisme et tradition au Dar For: Histoire des Massalit 1870–1930, E.J. Brill]

==== Settlements and Hydrology ====
Human settlement and economic activity in Dar Erenga are highly dependent on seasonal watercourses (wadis). The town of Sirba serves as the historical capital and primary administrative hub of the region. Further north, the settlement of Abu Qurayn acts as a transitional point bordering Dar Jebel.
The region's agricultural and pastoral life is sustained by two main seasonal valleys: Wadi Kaja, which flows through the eastern sector, and Wadi Asunga, which delineates the western border with the Republic of Chad. [ref: Mahdisme et tradition au Dar For: Histoire des Massalit 1870–1930, E.J. Brill]

==== International Legal Status ====
The boundaries of Dar Erenga were recognized under international law through the 1919 British-French boundary agreements, which were annexed to the Milner-Berthelot convention. On the official maps attached to the treaty, "Dar Erenga" was explicitly marked by name as a recognized territorial entity within the basins of Wadi Kaja and Wadi Asunga along the boundary. [ref: Treaty Series No. 6 (1921): Convention between the United Kingdom and France respecting Boundary Delimitation in West Africa (1919), Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (UK Treaties Online)]

Under the 1953 Anglo-Egyptian Agreement concerning self-government for the Sudan, Dar Erenga was formally incorporated into the "Dar Masalit North" electoral constituency (Constituency No. 59) alongside Geneina Town, Dar Jebel, Dar Gimr, Zaghawa Kubja, and adjacent Arab Omodias. [ref: "Agreement between the Government of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and the Egyptian Government concerning Self-Government and Self-Determination for the Sudan", Cairo, February 12, 1953, Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (UK)]

data.title: Healthcare in Abu Dhabi
data.text:
Healthcare in Abu Dhabi covers the health system of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi in the United Arab Emirates. Since a reform programme begun in 2005–2006, health services in the emirate have been funded mainly through compulsory health insurance for all residents, with regulation separated from the provision of public services. The sector combines government-owned hospitals operated by SEHA with a larger private sector, which accounted for more than 75% of the market in 2020. Researchers and the regulator have identified cost growth, workforce needs and preventive care as priorities for the health system.

== History ==
In 2005 Abu Dhabi's leadership began restructuring a health system whose design, according to a 2012 study in Health Policy, had not met its aims. The reforms introduced compulsory tiered health insurance for all residents, a single standardised payment system, and an independent regulator responsible for licensing and inspecting health professionals, facilities and insurers. [ref: Benefits of a single payment system: Case study of Abu Dhabi health system reforms, Health Policy] From 2006 the regulator, the Health Authority – Abu Dhabi, was separated from the provision of services, which became the responsibility of the Abu Dhabi Health Services Company (SEHA). [ref: Progress and outcomes of health systems reform in the United Arab Emirates: a systematic review, BMC Health Services Research] The regulator now operates as the Department of Health – Abu Dhabi (DoH). [ref: 2 stroke centres of excellence named in Abu Dhabi, Gulf News]

Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi, owned by Mubadala Healthcare and modelled on the Cleveland Clinic in the United States, began opening in March 2015 with 364 beds on Al Maryah Island. [ref: Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi opens its doors for patients, The National] In July 2019 the emirate's health information exchange, Malaffi, became operational, the first such platform in the UAE; by September 2020 it connected 40 hospitals and 403 clinics. [ref: More than 60% of Abu Dhabi hospitals now digitally connected, Healthcare IT News] In December 2019 the DoH launched a genome programme to produce an Emirati reference genome, carried out by Group 42 with the sequencing companies BGI and Oxford Nanopore Technologies, with a first phase of 100,000 samples. [ref: Abu Dhabi launches genome programme, Gulf News] [ref: Abu Dhabi teams with BGI, Oxford Nanopore on population sequencing project, GenomeWeb]

== Financing and insurance ==
Health insurance is compulsory for all residents. UAE nationals are covered by the Thiqa programme, while expatriates are covered by Basic or Enhanced plans. At the end of 2017 Thiqa covered about 600,000 members (20%), Basic plans 1.3 million (43%) and Enhanced plans 1.1 million (37%). [ref: Doctor's orders: Preventive medicine, digitisation and innovative technologies revitalise Abu Dhabi's medical offerings, Oxford Business Group]

Insurance claims rose from 15.3 million, worth US$1.6 billion, in 2011 to more than 22 million, worth US$2.9 billion, in 2014. A 2017 systematic review noted that some researchers saw the rise as a sign that further change was needed to keep the system financially sustainable, and that limited regulatory control and insurer competition had been identified as obstacles to cost efficiency.

== Facilities ==
In April 2020 the DoH reported 3,114 licensed health facilities in the emirate, including 64 hospitals, 759 clinics and 746 health centres, and 7,032 hospital beds (2.7 per 1,000 people) in 2019. SEHA, the largest public provider, operated at least 12 hospitals with 2,644 beds. Private providers accounted for more than 75% of the market, and the speed of private-sector growth raised concerns about oversupply in some specialities. About 70% of outpatient visits and 40% of inpatient care took place in private facilities.

=== Centres of Excellence ===
Since 2023 the DoH has designated selected hospital programmes as Centres of Excellence, assessed on clinical outcomes, patient experience, patient safety and quality, staff competency, and medical education, research and residency programmes, as well as accreditation. In July 2023 Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi and Sheikh Shakhbout Medical City were designated for stroke care; other facilities able to give emergency stroke treatment were designated "stroke ready" and transfer patients to the two centres once stable. Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi was designated for adult cardiac surgery in October 2023 [ref: Department of Health – Abu Dhabi appoints Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi as centre of excellence for cardiac surgery, Abu Dhabi Media Office] and for adult multi-organ transplants in December 2025, by which time the hospital reported more than 1,000 organ transplants since its programme began in 2017. [ref: Department of Health – Abu Dhabi designates Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi as Centre of Excellence for Adult Multi-Organ Transplants, Department of Health – Abu Dhabi] Other designated specialities include paediatric heart care, burn care and stem cell transplantation. In June 2026 the DoH stated that the centres had treated more than 3,000 complex cases and reduced the need for treatment abroad by 60%. [ref: DoH's Designated Centres of Excellence Deliver Specialised Care to More Than 3,000 Complex Cases, Department of Health – Abu Dhabi] In 2013 the regulator had sponsored more than 1,400 patients for treatment abroad.

=== Rankings ===
Eight hospitals in the emirate were listed in the Best Specialized Hospitals Middle East 2026 ranking by Newsweek and Statista, with Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi ranked first in the region for cardiology, gastroenterology and neurology and second for oncology. [ref: 8 Abu Dhabi healthcare facilities ranked among Newsweek's Best Specialised Hospitals in Middle East, Gulf Today] The ranking assessed more than 850 hospitals in seven countries and listed 126. [ref: Best Specialized Hospitals Middle East 2026, Statista] It was based 85% on an online survey of healthcare professionals.

== Maternal and child health ==
Corniche Hospital, operated by SEHA, has recorded more than 300,000 births since 1977; about one in three babies in the emirate is born there, and it admits nearly half of the emirate's neonatal intensive care patients. [ref: PureHealth hosts groundbreaking ceremony for SEHA New Corniche Hospital for women and newborns, Aletihad] In January 2024 Crown Prince Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan approved a medical city for women's and children's health incorporating Sheikh Khalifa Medical City and a new Corniche Hospital, initially announced with 205 beds and a 2027 opening. [ref: Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed approves establishment of medical city in Abu Dhabi dedicated to women and children's health, Aletihad] When ground was broken in June 2026, the new hospital was described with 357 beds, including 34 neonatal intensive care beds; no opening date was given.

In a 2017 survey of 1,624 mothers in Abu Dhabi, 30.2% of deliveries had been by caesarean section, and caesarean delivery was the main risk factor for delayed initiation of breastfeeding. [ref: Prevalence and associated factors of caesarean section and its impact on early initiation of breastfeeding in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, Nutrients] Doctors had given a similar estimate in 2015, against a World Health Organization ideal of 10–15%, and the chief medical officer of Corniche Hospital described the rate as "a huge problem in Abu Dhabi". [ref: One in four births in the UAE are C-sections, The National] A study of 1,610 mother–child pairs found a preterm birth rate of 6.3% and a low birth weight rate of 9.4%. [ref: Factors associated with preterm birth and low birth weight in Abu Dhabi, the United Arab Emirates, International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health]

Newborn screening in the UAE began in 1995; by 2011 the national programme had screened 750,365 infants for 16 disorders. [ref: Expanding the comprehensive national neonatal screening programme in the United Arab Emirates from 1995 to 2011, Eastern Mediterranean Health Journal] Abu Dhabi introduced emirate-wide pulse oximetry screening for critical congenital heart disease, which reached 86% of newborns in its first year. [ref: Regional implementation of newborn screening for critical congenital heart disease screening in Abu Dhabi, Pediatric Cardiology] In August 2025 the DoH launched newborn genetic screening using whole genome sequencing for more than 815 treatable conditions, offered in its first phase on a voluntary basis to UAE nationals and children of Emirati mothers at Kanad Hospital and Danat Al Emarat Hospital. [ref: Abu Dhabi launches Newborn Genetic Screening Programme, one of the most comprehensive of its kind globally, Gulf News] In a 2025 survey of 568 parents in Abu Dhabi, 78.2% supported adding genomics to newborn screening and 66.7% said it should be covered by health insurance. [ref: Parents' perspectives on expanded newborn genomic screening in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, Human Genomics]

Sheikh Khalifa Medical City was ranked sixth in the region for paediatrics in the 2026 Newsweek and Statista ranking, followed among Abu Dhabi hospitals by Tawam Hospital (16th), Danat Al Emarat Women & Children's Hospital (23rd) and Sheikh Shakhbout Medical City (50th). [ref: Best Specialized Hospitals Middle East 2026 – Pediatrics, Newsweek; Statista]

== Public health and workforce ==
In 2013 the regulator identified prevention, screening and self-care as areas where the model of care needed strengthening, and found that unrestricted access had led to over-supply of some services. Lifestyle-related conditions remain the main public-health priority: diabetes prevalence was 17.6% among people aged 20–79 in 2016, and cardiovascular disease accounted for 36.7% of deaths in 2017. Screening has since been extended to newborns, with pulse oximetry screening for congenital heart disease and, from 2025, genetic screening for more than 815 treatable conditions.

The health workforce has grown alongside demand. In 2019 the emirate had 10,202 physicians and 27,520 nurses, and the DoH estimated that up to 3,465 more doctors and 11,979 more nurses would be needed by 2025 to meet projected demand.

data.title: EuroNatur
data.text:
----

EuroNatur is a German foundation based in Radolfzell that supports nature conservation projects in Europe. The foundation was established in 1987 by Bund für Umwelt und Naturschutz Deutschland (BUND), Environmental Action Germany (DUH) and Naturschutzbund Deutschland (NABU). EuroNatur is a member of the Deutschen Naturschutzring.

== Mission ==
The foundation's mission is to protect Europe's diverse natural heritage. Its projects focus on wild animals such as wolves, brown bears, lynxes and endangered migratory birds, as well as valuable natural and cultural sites. The foundation's motto is "connecting nature and people", which reflects its belief that restoring nature, conserving wildlife and improving biodiversity are fundamental to human quality of life. Working with local people helps ensure the long-term success of their projects to protect endangered animals and their habitats in Europe.

EuroNatur is heavily involved with the European Green Belt initiative, a collaborative cross-border project which aims to create a wild, biodiverse corridor along the route of the former Iron Curtain. Since 2004, EuroNatur has coordinated the conservation efforts along the Balkan Green Belt, the southernmost section of the European Green Belt. [ref: EGB: Home, www.europeangreenbelt.org]

== Operations and administration ==
The foundation works with scientists, conservationists, farmers, politicians and entrepreneurs from across Europe. A key part of the foundation's work takes place in the Balkans, for which they work with local conservationists and volunteers to plan and establish a large network of nature reserves, along with species conservation projects for wolves, bears, lynxes and migratory birds based on scientific research. EuroNatur organises workshops, seminars and training programmes to share knowledge and experiences that help protect Europe's wild animals. EuroNatur also engages in political lobbying in EU institutions.

EuroNatur's first president was Claus-Peter Hutter, followed by Hartmut Vogtmann between January 2008 and early July 2011. Christel Schroeder served from October 2011 to the end of 2019, and Thomas Potthast has been president since 1 January 2020. Gabriel Schwaderer is the executive director of EuroNatur.

== Funding ==
The foundation is funded through donations, third-party funding and income from foundation capital. EuroNatur has been awarded the DZI Donation Seal by the German Central Institute for Social Issues (DZI).

== European Stork Villages ==
The European Stork Village network was set up by EuroNatur in 1994 as a way of publicly recognising communities across Europe that are making a significant contribution to protecting their local white stork populations. [ref: Ferger, Stefan & Schwaderer, Gabriel. (2016). The European Stork Villages - a successful combination of nature conservation and sustainable development of rural areas.] Representatives from each of the Stork Villages meet every year in one of the member villages to discuss and develop solutions for the conservation of white storks. There are currently 16 recognised European Stork Villages.

The most recent village to be recognised and added to the network was Knepp Wildland and Storrington in 2025, the first and only Stork Village in the UK. [ref: European Stork Villages Network, White Stork Project] The village was honoured in recognition of its conservation and rewilding programme which led to the return of the white stork to the area. The village of Storrington holds its White Stork and Nature Festival each year to celebrate its conservation efforts and the return of its white stork population.

== Awards ==
The foundation has been running its EuroNatur Award since 1992. [ref: Award for Environmental Excellence, EuroNatur]

EuroNatur runs an annual photography competition called European Treasures of Nature in partnership with the NaturVision film festival, Natur magazine and German utility company Gelsenwasser. The winning entries are displayed in a year-long touring exhibition titled Fascinating Nature and featured in the next year's EuroNatur calendar.

== References ==

data.title: Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter
data.text:
The Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter (MPSD; ) is a non-university research institute of the Max Planck Society (MPG). It is located in the Hamburg district of Bahrenfeld, on the campus of the Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron (DESY). The institute primarily conducts basic research in the natural sciences, in experimental and theoretical physics and chemistry. Its focus is on very fast physical processes and chemical reactions that can be studied by ultrafast spectroscopy using pulsed radiation sources such as the nearby free-electron lasers FLASH and European XFEL.

== History ==
The institute grew out of an existing Max Planck Society research group for structural dynamics at the University of Hamburg. The decision to establish an independent institute with five research departments was announced in November 2012. The institute was officially founded on 1 January 2014 and initially consisted of two departments, headed by its two founding directors: Condensed Matter Dynamics, led by Andrea Cavalleri, and Atomically Resolved Dynamics, led by R. J. Dwayne Miller. The Theory Department under Ángel Rubio was added on 1 November 2014. Miller's department was dissolved when he left the MPSD on 30 June 2020. On 15 June 2021, Philip Moll was appointed director of the Microstructured Quantum Matter Department.

In 2024, Jie Shan and Kin Fai Mak were recruited as further directors. They joined the institute fully on 1 January 2025 and lead two jointly run departments of Nanoscale Quantum Materials, focusing on optics (Shan) and transport (Mak), bringing the number of departments to five.

== Doctoral training ==
The MPSD hosts the International Max Planck Research School for Ultrafast Imaging and Structural Dynamics (IMPRS-UFAST), a structured doctoral programme founded in 2011 for doctoral students with backgrounds in physics, chemistry and biology.
