data.title: Pebble in the Pond Model by M . David Merrill
data.text:
== Introduction ==

Instructional design often begins with identifying content, objectives, and the steps needed to teach them. The Pebble in the Pond model, developed by M. David Merrill, approaches the process a little differently. Instead of beginning with individual pieces of content, the model starts with a real world problem or whole task that learns should eventually be able to complete (Merrill, 2002) [ref: A pebble-in-the-pond model for instructional design, Performance Improvement]. From that starting point, the remaining elements of the instruction are developed outward, much like the ripples created when a pebble is dropped in a pond.

The model is closely connected to Merrill's First Principles of Instruction, which proposes that learning is promoted when learners engage with real world problems, activate previous knowledge, observe demonstrations, apply new knowledge, and integrate that knowledge into their own world ([https://mdavidmerrill.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/firstprinciplesbymerrill.pdf Merrill,2002]a [ref: First principles of instruction]). Pebble in the Pond is described as a whole task approach that begins with the complete task learners are expected to perform rather than first breaking the task into isolated components( Merrill, [https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/EJ826059.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com 2007] [ref: A Task-Centered Instructional Strategy, Journal of Research on Technology in Education]).

=== Background and Development ===
Merrill introduced the Pebble in the Pond model in 2002 during a period in which traditional instructional systems design approaches were being criticized for being too procedural and for delaying detailed attention to the actual content learners needed to master. Merrill did not present the model as a complete replacement for instructional systems design. Instead, he described it as a content centered modification that could help designers incorporate effective instructional principles more directly into the final product (Merrill,2002). The central idea is fairly simple: begin with what learners should be able to do in the real world. Once that whole task is clear, the designer works outward from it. This differs from approaches that begin mainly with abstract objectives and only later determine the exact examples, problems, and content that learners will encounter. The model therefore places performance at the center of the design process and uses the task itself to guide later decisions about content and instruction. Merrill later described the approach as content first, task centered instructional design procedure ( Merrill, 2007)
[[File:M. David Merrill (3662310676) (2).jpg|thumb|Figure 1M. David Merrill

Note. M. David Merrill speaking at ED-MEDIA 2009 in Honolulu. Photograph by Kristina D. C. Hoeppner, 2009, via Wikimedia Commons. Licensed under CC BY-SA 2.0 [ref: File:M. David Merrill (3662310676) (2).jpg - Wikipedia, commons.wikimedia.org]]]

== The Man Behind the Theory: M. David Merrill ==
M. David Merrill is an instructional designer theorist and professor emeritus at Utah State University. He earned a bachelor's degree from Brigham Young University in 1961 and both a master's degree and PhD from the University of Illinois in 1964. Across a career extending for more than five decades, his work has focused in the design of effective instruction.

His contributions include work on the TICCIT computer based instructional system, Component Display Theory, Elaboration Theory, Instructional Transaction Theory, knowledge objects and First Principles of Instruction. These earlier ideas are important to understanding the Pebble in the Pond because the model did not appear in isolation. It developed from Merrill's continuing interest in how instructional designers can move from identifying what learners must know and do to designing instruction that helps them perform complete tasks. [ref: About, M David Merrill]

== Structure of the Model ==
[[File:Illustration of Pebble-in-the-Pond Model.png|thumb|Pebble-in-the-Pond Instructional Design Model [ref: ]]]
The Pebble in the Pond Instructional Design Model is represented as a set of expanding activities. The "pebble" is the first whole problem. Each additional design decision creates another ripple around it. Merrill's original model moves through problem specification, progression, component analysis, instructional strategy, interface design and production.

=== Problem ===
The first ripple is to identify and fully specify a real world problem or whole task that represents what learners should be able to accomplish after instruction. Merrill (2002b) argues that this different from beginning with abstract objectives because the task itself becomes the actual content around which instruction is designed.

=== Progression ===
The second ripple is to develop a progression of whole tasks that gradually increase in complexity, difficulty, or the amount of knowledge and skill required. Each task remains complete, but later tasks introduce additional details or components (Merrill, 2002b). Merrill (2007) explains that a good progression begins with a relatively simple version of the whole task and gradually adds complexity.

=== Analysis ===
Once the task progression has been developed, the third ripple identifies the knowledge and skills needed to complete the tasks. Merrill (2007) refers to these as component knowledge and skills. These may include information, concepts, procedures and principles required for successful performance. The order is important. The designer does not begin by listing everything that could possibly be taught about a topic. The whole tasks come first, and the designer then asks what learns actually need in order to perform them successfully. This keeps the content connected to meaningful performance rather than treating knowledge as an end in itself ( Merrill, 2002b, 2007).

=== Strategy ===
The fourth ripple determines how the identified content will be taught. Merrill's task centered strategy is closely connected to First Principles of Instruction. Learners work with whole tasks while receiving demonstrations, opportunities to apply what they are learning, feedback, guidance and gradually increasing responsibility (Merrill, 2002a,2007).

For novice learners, Merrill (2007) argues that guidance is especially important. The first task may be demonstrated more fully, while later tasks require learners to perform more of the work themselves. Support can gradually be reduced as competence develops. The approach is therefore task centered without assuming that learners should discover everything independently.

=== Design ===
The fifth ripple focuses on how the instruction will be presented and delivered. This includes decisions about the interface, media, navigation, delivery system and instructional architecture (Merrill, 2002b). A significant feature of the model is that these choices come after the task, content, and instructional strategy have already been established. In order words, the technology does not determine the lesson. The designer first decides what learners need to do and how they should be supported, ten selects or develops an interface capable of delivering that instruction.

=== Production ===
The final ripple is production, where the instructional materials and learning environment are developed. By this point, the designer already has a clear picture of the tasks, component knowledge and skills, instructional strategy and interface (Merrill,2002b). Production therefore brings the earlier decisions together into the finished product. Because much of the content and strategy has already been specified, development is guided by the previous ripples rather than beginning from scratch during production.

== Relationship to First Principles of Instruction ==
Pebble in the Pond is closely tied to Merrill's First Principles of Instruction. Merrill (2002a) identifies five central principles: learning is promotes when learners are engaged in solving real world problems, when previous knowledge is activated, when new knowledge is demonstrated, when learners apply new knowledge, and when new knowledge is integrated into the learner's world.

Pebble in the Pond provides a design process for putting those principles into practice. The problem and task progression establish the real world context, while the instructional strategy creates opportunities for activation, demonstration, application and integration. Merrill (2007) describes Pebble in The Pond as a task centered approach intended to produce instruction that incorporates these principles.

== Research and Application ==
The original Pebble in the Pond article reports an evaluation involving an Excel course developed with Thompson/NETg. Participants receiving scenario based instruction organized around the model achieved an average of 89% on three authentic tasks, com pared with 68% for a guided e-learning group and 34% for a control group. The scenario group also completed the tasks more quickly than the guided e-learning group (Merrill, 2002b). Because Merrill was involved in the development and reporting of the model, later research is also useful for determining whether similar benefits appear other contexts.

Francom et al.(2009) [ref: A Task-Centered Approach to Freshman-Level General Biology, ERIC]applied a task centered approach to a freshman- level general biology course at Brigham Young University, Hawaii. The redesigned course required students to learn biological content and then apply it through authentic tasks. Of the 88 students who completed the course survey, 92% agreed that the course gave them opportunities to apply knowledge in meaningful ways, and more than 81% reported increased interest in Biology. However, the authors also acknowledged limitations, including the absence of a systematic comparison with a traditionally taught biology class (Francom et al.,2009).

Mendenhall et al. (2006) [ref: A task-centered approach to entrepreneurship., Wordpress] also used a task centered approach when redesigning an entrepreneurship course at Brigham Young University, Hawaii. Instead of teaching business topics separately, the course was organized around several real businesses that allowed learners to see and apply the complete process of starting and managing a business. As learners moved through the cases, they were gradually expected to complete more of the task independently while support was reduced. The initial pilot involved 13 students, although the results of one student who did not complete the required work were excluded from the reported assessment results. Six of the remaining students scored 90% or higher on the final application test, while the other six generally scored in or near the 70% range. Students also gave the course an overall perception rating of 4.3 out of 5 and reported that the module helped them better understand entrepreneurship and connect the different parts of the business process (Mendenhall et al., 2006).

A more recent example can be seen in the development of the AllergyAware e-learning programme for school personnel, Sharma et al (2025) [ref: Online food allergy and anaphylaxis education for school personnel is effective and scalable: experience with the allergyaware e-learning portal from 2015 to 2022, Allergy, Asthma & Clinical Immunology] reported that the programme was developed using both ADDIE and Pebble in the Pond. Pebble in Pond was used early in the design process to identify the actual content and whole tasks that learners needed to perform. From 2015 to 2022, the programme recorded more than 170,000 course completions, with a post course quiz pass rate above 95%. However, the authors also noted that further research is needed to determine how well learners apply their knowledge in world real situations.

Together, these applications show that task centered and Pebble in the Pond approaches have been used across different subject areas, including biology, entrepreneurship, and professional health education. At the same time, the studies also show that the success of the approach depends on how the tasks, guidance, feedback, and overall learning environment are designed.

== Strengths and Limitations of the Model ==

=== Strengths ===
One of the main strengths of Pebble in the Pond is that it keeps the whole task at the center of the design process. Instead of teaching individual pieces of content and expecting learners to connect them later, the model identifies the complete performance first and then determines what knowledge and skills are needed to achieve it (Merrill,2002b,2007). This can make the relationship between what is being taught and what learners are eventually expected to do much clearer.

The research applications also suggest that task centered instruction can help learners see the relevance of what they are learning. In the Biology course studied by Francom et al. (2009), 92% of surveyed students reported that they had opportunities to apply knowledge meaningfully. Similarly, students in the entrepreneurship pilot reported that task centered structure helped them understand how the different parts of entrepreneurship connected with one another (Mendenhall et al., 2006).

=== Limitations ===
The approach can require considerable planning and instructional time. Francom et al. (2009) entrepreneurship evaluation involved a very small pilot group, so its positive findings cannot automatically be generalized to larger populations or different settings. Similarly, although the AllergyAware programme reported strong completion etcetera, Sharma et al. (2025) acknowledged that further research is needed to determine whether learners successfully transfer their knowledge to real world performance.

Pebble in the Pond should therefore not be viewed as a model that automatically produces successful instruction. Its effectiveness still depends on the quality of the whole tasks, the relevance of the content, the amount of guidance provided, and how well the design responds to the learners and the context.

== Related Publications ==
Pebble in the Pond developed as part of Merrill's broader work on instructional design rather than as an isolated model. In First Principles of Instruction, Merrill (2002a) proposed that effective instruction should be problem centered and should include activation of prior knowledge, demonstration, application and integration.

In "A Pebble in the Pond Model for Instructional Design", Merrill (2002b) translated these ideas into a design process centered around a real world problem, followed by progression, analysis, strategy, design and production.

Merrill later expanded the task centered approach in "A Task Centered Instructional Strategy" (2007). This publication gives greater attention to the progression of whole tasks, component knowledge and skills. instructional guidance, and the gradual reduction of learner support.

The model has also influenced later applications of task centered instruction while Francom et al. (2009) used it in the redesign of a university biology course. More recently, Sharma et al. (2025) reported the use of Pebble in the Pond alongside ADDIE in the design of the AllergyAware online training programme.

data.title: Theory of Industrialization
data.text:
== Theory of Industrialization ==

The theory of industrialization of education (also called the industrialization theory of distance education [ref: Exploring Otto Peters' Theory: Industrialisation in Distance Education - Distance Learning Institute]) is a theory of distance education proposed by the German educator Otto Peters. It holds that distance education is the most industrialized form of education, because it shares the organizational principles of industrial production.

The theory is premised on the principles of industrialization as they stood in the 1960s, and proposes that distance education is an industrialized form of teaching and learning. [ref: Exploring Otto Peters' Theory: Industrialisation in Distance Education - Distance Learning Institute] Peters compared the industrial production process with the structure of distance education, and described industrialized education as resting on elements such as planning, rationalization, and mechanization [ref: ]. Peters was arguably the first scholar to advance a theory of distance education [ref: ].

== The Core Claims and Industrial Principles ==
The central claim is that distance education has structural features in common with industrial production, and that these are more developed there than in any other form of education. One overview lists the principles he identified as rationalization, division of labor, mechanization, assembly-line processes, mass production, standardization, and scientific control methods [ref: Philosophical Underpinnings of Open and Distance Learning (ODL) • Sociology.Institute].

=== 1. Organizing and planning the work ===

* Rationalization - Redesigning the teaching process so that it uses time, staff and money efficiently. One study lists rationalization among the resource factors affected by Industry 4.0, alongside specialization, preparatory work, and capital intensive techniques. In practice, [https://zenodo.org/records/4293232 one course is built once and used for many learners].
* Planning - Decisions about content, sequence and delivery are made in advance, and production is scheduled. Peters used business management terms [ref: ], including planning, to show the industrial character of distance education.
* Preparatory work - A great deal of effort goes into designing and testing materials before any learner sees them, in contrast to a lecturer who prepares shortly before class. This is the front loading that justifies the cost.
* Organization - Producing and delivering courses requires an administrative structure that coordinates authors, printers, mailing, tutors and assessment, much as a factory coordinates departments.

=== 2. Dividing and mechanizing the work ===

* Division of labor - A French chapter on Peters says that teaching no longer depends on one person, because division of labor now prevails. One overview describes subject experts developing content, instructional designers optimizing learning, technical specialists managing platforms and tutors handling student contact, each playing a distinct role. This is the principle most closely tied to the instructional design profession [ref: Philosophical Underpinnings of Open and Distance Learning (ODL) • Sociology.Institute].
* Mechanization - Technical media, such as print, broadcast, audio, video and digital platforms, carry out functions the teacher once performed.
* Assembly line - Course production moves through ordered stages (writing, review, editing, production, distribution), each handled by a different group. Assembly line is one of the terms Peters borrowed from business management [ref: ].
* Mass production - Mass production is another of those terms. One overview says the aim was to reach thousands of students efficiently, which no single classroom teacher could do [ref: Philosophical Underpinnings of Open and Distance Learning (ODL) • Sociology.Institute].

=== 3. Controlling quality and consistency ===

* Scientific control methods - Industrial quality control has an equivalent in course evaluation, testing materials with sample learners and monitoring results. One overview lists scientific control methods among the principles [ref: Philosophical Underpinnings of Open and Distance Learning (ODL) • Sociology.Institute].
* Formalization - Procedures, roles and responsibilities are written down and made explicit rather than left to individual judgement.
* Standardization - Learners receive the same materials, tasks and assessment criteria, which makes quality predictable. It is also the principle that Industry 4.0 puts under most strain. That [https://zenodo.org/records/4293232 study] found personalization and individual production conflicting with the standardized mass production described by the theory.

=== 4. Changing the nature of teaching ===

* Change in the teacher’s role - The teacher shifts from deliverer of lessons to designer, tutor or assessor. The same overview contrasts classroom teaching, which it compares to craft production, with distance education [ref: Philosophical Underpinnings of Open and Distance Learning (ODL) • Sociology.Institute].
* [https://zenodo.org/records/4293232 Objectification] - The teaching is built into the course materials and technical means. The Anadolu study notes that most teaching functions in distance education are objectified in this way. A learner works with a fixed, pre-made course, not a person responding in real time.

=== 5. Structure of the institution ===

* Concentration and centralization - Production and management gather in a central institution, often a single large organization serving a wide area. The [https://zenodo.org/records/4293232 study] says industry technologies influence the centralization and concentration factors in management.

The theory of industrialization is regarded as one of the classic theories of the field, alongside Börje Holmberg’s guided didactic conversation and Michael Moore’s transactional distance theory. It is also relevant to instructional design, because it helps explain why distance courses are pre-planned, produced by specialist teams and reused across large cohorts.

== The Theorist: Otto Peters ==

Otto Peters was born on 6 May 1926 in Berlin, Germany [ref: Prof. em. Dr. phil. Dr. h. c. mult. Otto Peters - FernUniversität in Hagen, www.fernuni-hagen.de]. He talks about first meeting "distance learning" as a student during World War II. While at the German Institute of Distance Education, he invented the term "distance education" [ref: Oral histories and engaged perspectives: In conversation with Otto Peters, Journal of Open, Distance, and Digital Education].

From 1969–1974 he did comparative distance teaching research at the German Institute for Distance Education at the [https://uni-tuebingen.de/en/ University of Tübingen]. In 1974, he became Professor of General Didactics at the Pädagogische Hochschule [ref: ] Berlin and was appointed at the same time to the founding committee of the [https://www.fernuni-hagen.de/ FernUniversität]. From 1975 to 1991 he was Professor of the Methodology of Distance Study there. [ref: Prof. Dr. Otto Peters: der Weg-Weiser - FernUniversität in Hagen, www.fernuni-hagen.de] He was Founding Rector of the FernUniversität in Hagen [ref: „Die richtige Universität zur richtigen Zeit“ - FernUniversität in Hagen, www.fernuni-hagen.de].

Peters received four honorary doctor’s degrees [ref: Prof. em. Dr. phil. Dr. h. c. mult. Otto Peters - FernUniversität in Hagen, www.fernuni-hagen.de]. For eight years he served as Vice-President of the [https://icde.org/ International Council for Open and Distance Education]. In 1999 he received the International Council for Open und Distance Education Prize of Excellence [ref: Prof. em. Dr. phil. Dr. h. c. mult. Otto Peters - FernUniversität in Hagen, www.fernuni-hagen.de]. His three latest titles are: Otto Peters on Distance Education. The Industrialization of Teaching and Learning. London: Routledge (1994) [ref: Otto Peters on Distance Education: The Industrialization of Teaching and Learning, Routledge & CRC Press], Learning and Teaching in Distance Education: Analyses and Interpretations from an International Perspective. London: Kogan Page (1998) [ref: Learning and teaching in distance education: analyses and interpretations from an international perspective, Kogan Page], and Distance Education in Transition. New Trends and Challenges (2002) [ref: Distance education in transition: new trends and challenges, Oldenburg: Bibliotheks- und Informations system de Universität Oldenburg]. Together, with Börje Holmberg, he is regarded as a “father of distance education research [ref: Der Wegbereiter der FernUniversität wird 100: Prof. Dr. Dr. h.c. mult. Otto Peters - FernUniversität in Hagen, www.fernuni-hagen.de]”.

== What the research says ==

* Theory of Industrialization was influential and is classed as a “classic” theory - Peters, Holmberg and Moore fundamentally shaped how “distance education” was named, articulated and practised from the late 1970s [ref: ].
* Critics said it was too structural - [https://doaj.org/article/075f7db4d0cd4ffbaece44eff0b627c5 Garrison (2000)] reviewed theory in the field. His review found an early preoccupation with organisational and structural constraints, with theory moving towards transactional issues.
* Post-Fordism and post-industrial debate - A cluster of 1990s journal papers debated whether distance education is still “[https://1library.net/article/rejection-of-fordist-models-in-distance-education.1y9k6mrz Fordist]”. Contributors included Greville Rumble (a three-part series, “Labour market theories and distance education: a response [ref: Labour market theories and distance education: a response, Open Learning: The Journal of Open, Distance and e-Learning]”) and Peters himself.
* Later volumes - Cleveland-Innes and Garrison (2010) [ref: ]argue that in a post-Fordist era, distance education cannot deliver flexible access, quality learning and cost-effectiveness together, only two of the three. There's also a distinguish between industrial “distance education” from post-industrial “online learning”.
* Recent applications - A study of 10 academics at [https://www.anadolu.edu.tr/en Anadolu University] used the theory to examine [https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/industry-4-0 Industry 4.0]. It found that Industry 4.0’s [https://zenodo.org/records/4293232 emphasis on personalisation conflicts with the standardised mass production the theory describes].

Almasons is an American software company that develops applications for warehouse and supply-chain operations. Its software is marketed under the GiNi name and includes applications for warehouse management, warehouse execution, labor management and voice-directed workflows. [ref: AI-Powered Supply Chain Solutions — GiNi by Almasons, Almasons] [ref: Almasons Consulting LLC — SAP Registered Partner, ERP Research] The company identifies Rajesh Mendonca as its founder and chief architect and lists an office in Cumming, Georgia.

== History and operations ==

Almasons' member profile on MHI states that the company was established in 2013 by founders with experience integrating SAP systems. The profile describes the GiNi platform as providing connections between enterprise systems, interfaces to warehouse technologies, workflow applications and performance-monitoring functions. [ref: Almasons, MHI]

ERP Research lists Almasons Consulting LLC as an SAP software partner. Its profile describes GiNi as a platform of workflow extensions and connectors for SAP warehouse and transportation systems.

== GiNi ==

GiNi is Almasons' software platform for warehouse and supply-chain applications. According to the company's MHI member profile, the platform supports data exchange between warehouse-management, enterprise resource planning, transportation-management and customer-relationship management systems. It also provides interfaces to technologies such as voice systems, automated material-handling equipment and robotics.

The company's product range includes warehouse-management and warehouse-execution applications, voice-directed picking, labor management and operational dashboards.

Zebra Technologies includes Almasons in the voice-directed picking section of its WS50 ISV Solutions Guide. The guide describes software that connects voice-based warehouse workflows with warehouse-management systems. [ref: WS50 ISV Solutions Guide, Zebra Technologies]

data.title: Hugo Raymundo
data.text:
Hugo Amilcár Raymundo (born November 28, 1983) is a Guatemalan actor and stuntman;
with over 40 film and television credits under his belt.

==Careers==
In 2017, Raymundo made his acting debut as ‘Oscar’ in the television series,
La Quinceanera, directed
by Gigi Saul Guerrero for Stage 13 Network, the digital content division for Warner Bros. Digital Networks. [ref: La Quinceanera, IMDb]

In the same year, Raymundo guest-starred as ‘Enrique’ on multiple episodes of the CBS American drama television series, Zoo; directed by Michael Katleman, based on the novel by James Patterson and Michael Ledwidge.

Licensed and practiced across a number of stunt performance skills, Raymundo joined The CW Network as a stuntman and stunt actor in various episodes of the television series Arrow and Supergirl (2017-2019), as part of the 'Arrowverse', an American media franchise based on the DC Comics Universe.

In 2018, Raymundo joined the American science fiction drama television series, The X-Files, and American science fiction action film, The Predator; where Raymundo shared the screen with the likes of, David Duchovny and Boyd Holtbrooke in their corresponding stunt sequences.

Raymundo then returned to The CW Network as 'Hugo', on American television drama series, The 100, executively produced and directed by Jason Rothenberg for the 100 series; shortly after Raymundo guest-starred as 'Brant Moore' on various episodes of the science fiction television series, Travelers, created by Brad Wright for Netflix International.

2019, Raymundo focused his efforts on being a stuntman as he joined a number of television shows with such notable mentions as Deadly Class for the Syfy network, sharing the screen with British actor Benedict Wong; and Disney's Siren where Raymundo performed as a stunt double for three different actors including Ian Verdun, Hugo Ateo and Luc Roderique. Raymundo finished 2019 guest-starring as the role of 'Motorman' in multiple episodes of the American science fiction television series, Lost in Space, for the Netflix Network.

In 2020, Raymundo joined the Marvel Cinematic Universe as a stuntman for Hulu Network's American television series, Helstrom; later that year Raymundo joined the Paramount+ Network as BO, on the American television mini-series, The Stand, an adaption of the post-apocalyptic dark fantasy novel written by Stephen King, where Raymundo shares the screen with James Marsden and Owen Teague.

In 2021 and 2022, Raymundo joined a number of television shows with such notable mentions as Firefly Lane for the Netflix Network, Starring Katherine Heigl, Sarah Chalke and Ben Lawson; Detective Knight: Redemption for Lionsgate Films, Starring Bruce Willis, Lochlyn Munro and Miranda Edwards and Yellowjackets for the Showtime Network, Starring Melanie Lynskey, Tawny Cypress and Sophie Nelisse.

After sharing the screen with actress Juliette Lewis on the television series Yellowjackets, Raymundo focused his efforts on acting. In 2023, Raymundo joined the CBS Network as 'Eddie' for the American drama-comedy, So Help Me Todd and as Ron, [ref: ‘So Help Me Todd’ Episode 13 “Wall of Fire” Photos, Cast and Plot, Showbiz Junkies] for the American action-drama, Fire Country. [ref: ‘Fire Country’ Episode 9 “No Good Deed” Photos, Plot, Cast and Air Date, Showbiz Junkies] Shortly after, Raymundo took on the role of 'Mike Garcia', the father of Isaac Garcia, played by Isaac Arellanes and Lee Garcia, played by Myles Perez for the Netflix Network's teen drama, My Life with the Walter Boys, Starring Nikki Rodriguez, Ashby Gentry, Noah LaLonde, Sarah Rafferty and Johnny Link an adaption of the novel written by Ali Novak.

2023, was a transformative year for Raymundo, as he joined the cast of Lola Dust for Lithium Dreams Productions and Lumberwitch Films as 'Dean', [ref: Lola Dust, IMDb] and the cast of Protectors of the Land for POTLuck Stories as 'Carlos Zapata'. [ref: Protectors of the Land, IMDb]

He was recognized as an esteemed member of the performing arts community by UBCP/ACTRA, Raymundo served as part of the Adjudication Committee under the award category for Best Stunt performance in the 2023 UBCP/ACTRA Awards in Vancouver, Canada.

In 2024, Raymundo shared the screen with actor Ryan Phillippe in the film One Mile as Lenny for Kapital Entertainment and Nomadic Pictures. [ref: One Mile, IMDb]
Raymundo also served as part of the Adjudication committee under the award categories for Best Stunt Performance, Dramatic series Best Performance and Television Movie Lead Performance, for the 2024 LEO Awards in Vancouver, Canada. [ref: 2024 Jurors, Leo awards]

In 2025 Raymundo, joined the cast of the American Western drama television series, Billy the Kid, as "Miguel Otero" for MGM+.

data.title: SēmonBarai
data.text:
----

Seimon Harai is an annual event held in Kyoto, Japan, in which people's lies from that year are wiped away. Participants are said to be forgiven for their lies by paying their respects at a shrine called "Kanjaden Shrine." [ref: Ōsaka kotoba jiten, Kōdansha]>

== History ==
Seimon Harai is held every year on October 20 at Kanjaden Shrine on Shijo-dori Street [ref: syukyosaijiki, KADOKAWA]>. The festival originates from the story of a man named "Tosa no Bo Shoshun." On orders from his lord, he tried to assassinate a military commander, but was discovered by the commander, who had sensed the plot. Although he was released after promising not to carry out the assassination, he attacked anyway. Just before he was killed, he said, "I will become a god who forgives those who lie." He was then enshrined at the shrine as a deity. [ref: 郷土研究 上方34, 河出書房]

== Recent Years ==
Seimon Harai once fell into decline, but it was revived in 2003 by the Otabi-cho neighborhood association and has continued to this day. There have also been changes since it came under the association's management, such as the Otabi-cho neighborhood association starting a ritual called the "Shiraishi Arai Kiyome Shinji" (a purification ritual) for the festival.

== Ayvazovskiy Train Station ==
Ayvazovskiy railway station is a railway location on Ayvazovskiy street in Erebuni district of Yerevan, Armenia. The site contains railway tracks and branching infrastructure associated with the railway network in the city. [ref: ]

== Location ==
The station is located in Yerevan, the capital of Armenia. The surrounding area includes industrial facilities, warehouses, storage properties and small workshops. Its position within an urban and industrial environment places it among the railway infrastructure found around the city.

== Infrastructure ==
The railway site includes multiple tracks and a turnout, which allows railway vehicles to move between different tracks. Such infrastructure can be used for shunting, access to sidings and the movement of freight wagons.

The surrounding industrial properties may provide context for the railway's use. However, the precise purpose of each track and its connection to nearby businesses require further documentation.

== Railway operations ==
According to local observations, trains reportedly use the tracks regularly. Local residents have described train movements as frequent, although the exact frequency has not been independently established.

The tracks may support freight-related movements, but a confirmed timetable and detailed record of the site's railway operations are not available in the sources used for this article.

== History ==
The history of Ayvazovskiy railway station has not been fully documented in the sources consulted. Its construction date, original purpose and changes to its track layout remain topics for further research.

Railway infrastructure in Yerevan developed alongside the city's industrial and economic growth. The Armenian railway network became an important part of the country's transport system, connecting the capital with other regions and international railway routes [ref: Home, Южно-Кавказская железная дорога].

data.title: Cancer Research Society
data.text:
----

The Cancer Research Society (CRS;, SRC) is a Canadian charitable organization dedicated exclusively to funding research on all types of cancer in order to better prevent, detect, and treat the disease. [ref: Our mission, Cancer Research Society] It was founded in 1945 in Montreal. [ref: 100% Research for 80 Years, Cancer Research Society]

== History ==

The Cancer Research Society was founded in 1945 by Betty Caplan and her three friends, Etta Kastner, Hattie Rolbin, and Mildred Singer. Faced with her mother's cancer, Betty Caplan realized that no Canadian organization was then dedicated exclusively to cancer research, and decided to act. From its inception, the organization set itself the mission of funding research exclusively into all types of cancer in order to better prevent, detect, and treat the disease.In 1946, the CRS awarded its first four grants of $600 each, for a total of $2,400, an amount that would represent more than $40,000 today. In 1948, three years after its founding, the organization comprised more than one hundred member units organizing various fundraising activities. A first Medical Advisory Board, composed of physicians responsible for selecting the researchers to be funded, was established in the early years. [ref: In 1945, Betty Caplan changed cancer research in Canada, Hub SRC]

=== Development ===
Over the decades, the CRS expanded its support for research on all types of cancer across Canada. Since its founding, the organization reports having allocated more than $450 million in research grants and fellowships. In 2024-2025, according to the organization, the CRS invested $17 million and awarded 316 grants across its various programs. [ref: Our impact, Cancer Research Society]In 2025, the CRS marked its 80th anniversary.

=== Growth of activities ===
In 2010, the CRS created the Challenge Against Cancer program, in which charity trips are organized and enable participants to raise funds for research. [ref: Notre histoire, Société de recherche sur le cancer]

== Organization ==

=== Headquarters and administration ===
The Cancer Research Society is headquartered in Montreal. It is a registered charitable organization (registration number 11915 3229 RR0001). [ref: Société de recherche sur le cancer / Cancer Research Society (119153229RR0001), List of charities] According to the organization, it has a staff of about thirty employees. Its governance rests on a board of directors composed of volunteer members, a management team responsible for guiding the team's actions, and a Scientific Advisory Committee. [ref: Our team, Cancer Research Society]

=== Board of directors ===
Founder Betty Caplan served as president of the organization from 1945 to 1954. A number of people succeeded her in this role over the decades. Christian M. Paupe, a member of the board of directors since 2021, [ref: Christian M. Paupe appointed to the Board, Cancer Research Society] chairs it as of 2026. [ref: Board of directors, Cancer Research Society]

=== Scientific Advisory Committee ===
The Scientific Advisory Committee is composed of experts in cancer research from diverse backgrounds.Actor and host André Robitaille serves as the CRS's spokesperson.

== Funding ==
The Cancer Research Society funds its activities through donations from individuals, contributions from partners, and funds raised at its events. [ref: Our mission, Cancer Research Society]According to the independent charity evaluator Charity Intelligence Canada, the CRS reported total revenues of $40.4 million for the 2024-2025 fiscal year, of which $34.2 million came from donations and special-events revenue, and $6.2 million from investment income. According to the same source, the CRS devoted $17.0 million to its grants and their management during that same fiscal year. The organization publishes impact reports and audited financial statements accounting for its management. [ref: Cancer Research Society, Charity Intelligence Canada]

== Activities ==
The CRS organizes several fundraising events across Canada. [ref: Events, Cancer Research Society]One of its main events is the Urban BBQ, presented by RBC Royal Bank since 2014 and held at the Grand Quai of the Port of Montreal. According to the organization, the event has raised more than $6.3 million since its first edition, [ref: Urban BBQ 2026, Cancer Research Society] and its 12th edition, in 2026, brought together more than 1,000 guests and raised $850,000 net. [ref: Urban BBQ 2026: a collective success for cancer research, Cancer Research Society]Among the organization's other events are Accords Célestes, an evening pairing fine dining, wines, and music, held in Montreal, [ref: Accords Célestes 2026, Cancer Research Society] as well as Christmas Carols for Research, a holiday-season concert whose 2026 edition supports breast cancer research. [ref: Christmas Carols for Research 2026, Cancer Research Society] The CRS is also associated with charity races across the country. [ref: Nos événements, Société de recherche sur le cancer]The Challenge Against Cancer program, created in 2010, offers charity trips to various destinations around the world during which participants take on physical challenges while raising funds for cancer research. [ref: Challenge Against Cancer, Cancer Research Society] The Challenge rose, announced in 2025, is an edition dedicated entirely to breast cancer research. [ref: Challenge rose 2026, Cancer Research Society]

== Research ==
The Cancer Research Society supports research through annual programs and targeted programs. The organization funds the full spectrum of research, namely fundamental, translational, and clinical research. [ref: Funding programs, Cancer Research Society]Its three annual programs are the Operating Grants, aimed at fundamental and translational research; the Next Generation of Scientists Awards, which support postdoctoral trainees; and the Doctoral Research Awards, aimed at students conducting cancer research at a Canadian academic institution.The CRS occasionally launches targeted programs, often in partnership, focusing on specific types of cancer or on priority scientific issues. These initiatives notably concern lung cancer, prostate cancer (with PROCURE), brain cancer (with the Brain Canada Foundation), ovarian cancer (with Ovarian Cancer Canada), and breast cancer. The CRS has also entered into its first international partnership with the British organization Worldwide Cancer Research, aimed at supporting exploratory and translational research in cancer prevention, detection, and treatment. [ref: Partnership with Worldwide Cancer Research, Cancer Research Society] In 2026, in collaboration with the Canadian Cancer Society, the Terry Fox Research Institute and several other partners, it launched a national program dedicated to investigator-initiated clinical trials in oncology, described as the first of its kind in Canada. [ref: New Era of Clinical Cancer Research in Canada, Cancer Research Society] [ref: Major $25-million investment propels new era of clinical cancer research in Canada, Terry Fox Research Institute]

For each of its programs, the CRS uses a peer review process. Each year, according to the organization, nearly one hundred researchers, clinicians, and physicians volunteer to assess the grant applications received in order to determine which projects are funded.

== Advocacy ==
In October 2023, and again in April 2024, the Cancer Research Society joined the Quebec Cancer Foundation, Leucan, and PROCURE to call on the Government of Quebec to develop a cancer action plan. [ref: Cancer au Québec: « Il y a une urgence d'agir », La Presse] [ref: Un plan d'action contre le cancer réclamé, Le Devoir] In a brief titled "Cancer doesn't wait: the future Santé Québec agency must act," the organizations put forward eight recommendations, including the appointment of a vice-president responsible for the cancer portfolio within Santé Québec. [ref: Cancer au Québec: « Santé Québec doit agir », La Presse] [ref: Le Québec peut mieux faire pour lutter contre le cancer, selon des groupes, Radio-Canada]

data.title: Vibin Baskar
data.text:
Vibin Baskar is an Indian music composer, music producer, and independent artist who works primarily in the Tamil and Kannada film industries. He is known for composing music for the Tamil ZEE5 original web series Sattamum Neethiyum (2025), Veduvan(2025), Thadayam(2026) and Kaakee Circus(2026) for which he created both the songs and the background score. He has also composed music for Tamil and Kannada feature films. He has released several independent Tamil singles.

== Early life and Education ==
Vibin Baskar is based in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. He completed a Bachelor of Business Administration from Alagappa University before earning a Master of Business Administration from the same institution in 2014. His interest in music began during childhood after being enrolled in piano classes by his mother. He later pursued formal training in western music from Trinity College London in Piano and Music Theory. He completed his Bachelor's degree in Audio Engineering and Recording Arts from the School of Audio Engineering. During this period, he also performed as a keyboardist in live shows across Chennai.

== Career ==
Early career

Vibin Baskar began his professional career in 2012 as an Audio Engineer, Chennai. In 2013, he became Assistant Music Director and worked with composer James Vasanthan, contributing to music production and programming. From 2017 onward, he started composing music independently for South Indian films, television productions and OTT platforms.

=== Film and Television ===
Kaakee Circus (2026)

Thadayam (2026)

Veduvan (2025)

Sattamum Neethiyum (2025)

Vibin Baskar composed the songs and original background score for the Tamil legal drama web series Sattamum Neethiyum, released on ZEE5 in 2025. The series received positive reviews, with several critics highlighting Baskar's music as one of its major strengths.

Reviewers noted that:

* the background score effectively complemented the emotional tone of the story;
* the courtroom sequences were enhanced by the music;
* the climax episode featured an emotionally impactful musical score;
* the background music strengthened the portrayal of the lead character.

A review published in Cinema Murasam described the music and cinematography as the "pillars of support" for the series.

Angusam praised the emotional integration of the score with the narrative, particularly during the climax.

A review in Hindu Tamil Thisai identified the music as one of the most significant strengths of the series after its screenplay and direction, while also noting that the opening "heroism"-styled title song ("Yaar Ivan?") appeared somewhat inconsistent with the otherwise realistic tone of the drama.

The series has been regarded as an important milestone in Baskar's career, introducing his work to a wider Tamil audience.

== Samharini ==
Vibin Baskar composed the music for the Kannada-language feature film Samharini, where he was credited as Vibin Baskar (V2).

== Independent Music ==
Alongside his work in films, Vibin is active in the Tamil independent music scene. He maintains the YouTube channel [https://www.youtube.com/@[user] @[user],] where he publishes original compositions, music videos, behind-the-scenes content and promotional material for his projects.

His independent works include:

One of Vibin Baskar's notable independent releases is Chellame, a Father's Day song written shortly after the birth of his daughter. The song features vocals by Jithin Raj with lyrics by Jaleel Niyaz (Bhaai). The accompanying music video features Baskar alongside his daughter, Baby Milir Vadhana. His wife, Mukhil Mayuri, is credited with conceptualising and executing the video, including its montage sequences.

== Musical Style ==
Vibin Baskar's work combines orchestral scoring, electronic programming and contemporary Tamil independent music. His professional expertise includes:

* Music composition
* Music production
* Background scoring
* Sound design
* Audio engineering
* Mixing and mastering
* Keyboard programming
* Songwriting
* Audio post-production

== Reception ==
Vibin Baskar's work on Sattamum Neethiyum received positive critical attention. Reviews published by Cinema Murasam, Angusam, and Hindu Tamil Thisai praised his background score for enhancing the emotional depth of the narrative and supporting the performances. Critics particularly highlighted the courtroom sequences and climax episode for their effective musical treatment. Although one review considered the series' title song stylistically inconsistent with the realistic tone of the drama, the overall reception to the soundtrack and score was positive.

data.title: John O'Leary
data.text:
John O’Leary is an American business executive who is the President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Daimler Truck North America (DTNA). He assumed the role on April 1, 2021, succeeding Roger Nielsen. [ref: John O’Leary to Succeed Roger Nielsen as CEO of DTNA, Transport Topics] He is also a member of the Board of Management of Daimler Truck Holding AG, representing the North American region. [ref: Daimler Truck extends John O’Leary’s term on management board, FreightWaves]

O’Leary has been cited in national and business media in connection with U.S. manufacturing trends, tariffs, and the transition to electric vehicles. In coverage by The New York Times, he commented on the impact of tariffs on domestic steel pricing, noting that U.S. producers had “more headroom” to raise prices. [ref: U.S. Steel Producers Raise Prices After Tariffs Stymie Imports, The New York Times] He has also been quoted in The Wall Street Journal regarding infrastructure limitations affecting the adoption of electric heavy-duty trucks. [ref: Sales of Electric Heavy-Duty Trucks Are Hitting a Regulatory Wall, The Wall Street Journal]

O’Leary previously served as Chief Transformation Officer and Head of Mercedes-Benz Trucks in Germany from 2020 to 2021, and earlier was Chief Financial Officer of DTNA from 2012 to 2020. [ref: Daimler Trucks NA Names New CEO, School Bus Fleet] In 2024, he joined the board of directors of Portland General Electric. [ref: John O'Leary will join Portland General Electric board of directors, effective January 1, 2024, Portland General Electric] That same year, he co-chaired Oregon’s Clean Tech Manufacturing Task Force alongside Governor Tina Kotek and U.S. Senator Ron Wyden. [ref: Governor Kotek Releases Clean Tech Manufacturing Task Force Recommendations, Office of the Governor of Oregon]

== Career ==

O’Leary began his career in the commercial vehicle industry in 1989 at Paccar. He joined Freightliner (now DTNA) in 2000, where he held several leadership roles, including Internal Audit Director. He later served as President and CEO of Thomas Built Buses from 2002 to 2010, followed by Senior Vice President for DTNA’s aftermarket business from 2010 to 2012.

In 2012, O’Leary was appointed Chief Financial Officer of DTNA, a position he held until 2020. [ref: Daimler Truck extends John O’Leary’s term on management board, FreightWaves] In September 2020, he relocated to Germany to serve as Chief Transformation Officer and interim head of Mercedes-Benz Trucks.

Following the retirement of DTNA CEO Roger Nielsen, O’Leary was named President and CEO effective April 1, 2021. [ref: John O’Leary to Succeed Roger Nielsen as CEO of DTNA, Transport Topics] After the spin-off and public listing of Daimler Truck Holding AG on December 10, 2021, he joined the company’s Board of Management, representing North America. [ref: Daimler Truck launched on stock exchange as an independent company, Daimler Truck]

During his tenure, O’Leary has been cited in industry and business publications in connection with market transitions in the North American Class 8 truck sector, including supply chain disruptions, tariffs, and shifts in demand. [ref: DTNA’s O’Leary Reflects on Time of Transition for Company, Class 8 Market, Transport Topics] He has also been referenced in reporting on DTNA’s investments in electric truck development and engineering in the United States, including projects in Portland, Oregon, [ref: Daimler goes big on electrics in Portland, Portland Business Journal] as well as broader industry trends such as partnerships and acquisitions among truck manufacturers. [ref: Truck makers pursue acquisitions and joint ventures, Axios] Additional reporting has noted the company’s strategic focus on expanding its vocational truck segment in response to changing market conditions. [ref: As on-highway sales slump, DTNA sees opportunity for Western Star, FleetOwner]

In October 2023, the Daimler Truck Supervisory Board extended his management board term through March 2026. [ref: Daimler Truck extends John O’Leary’s term on management board, FreightWaves]

O’Leary’s tenure as president was marked by a focus on modernizing production and expanding technological capabilities. In August 2026, DTNA announced plans to build a new truck manufacturing facility in the United States. [ref: Daimler Truck plans to build a new truck production facility in the USA, FinanzNachrichten] [ref: Daimler Truck expands US business with new plant, Reuters] [ref: Daimler Truck Eyes New USA Plant, North American Orders Surge, Bloomberg] Following the announcement, O’Leary commented, “We want to have the best, most modern plants out there, because we know that will give us a best-cost position.” The expansion followed the company’s plans to upgrade technology across its manufacturing operations. O’Leary added that the new facility would “strengthen our ability to deliver industry-leading products while supporting long-term growth in the United States.” [ref: Daimler Truck North America Plans to Build New U.S. Manufacturing Facility, Daimler Truck]

== Public activities ==

O’Leary has spoken publicly on topics related to commercial vehicle electrification, supply chain constraints, and infrastructure development. He has participated in industry events and has been interviewed by business media regarding trends affecting truck demand and manufacturing conditions. [ref: DTNA’s O’Leary talks material shortages, future of diesel and EVs, FleetOwner] In a 2025 Bloomberg Television interview, he described economic uncertainty, particularly around tariffs, as having “frozen” some customers and end markets, affecting truck orders. [ref: Uncertainty Has Frozen the Consumer, Says Daimler Truck North America CEO, Bloomberg]

== Board service ==

O’Leary has served as a director of Portland General Electric since January 1, 2024. [ref: John O'Leary will join Portland General Electric board of directors, effective January 1, 2024, Portland General Electric]

== References == [ref: Dow Jones News, “Daimler Truck plans to build a new truck production facility in the USA,” FinanzNachrichten, August 6, 2026. Ilona Wissenbach, “Daimler Truck expands US business with new plant,” Reuters, August 7, 2026. Gabrielle Coppola, “Daimler Truck Eyes New USA Plant, North American Orders Surge,” Bloomberg, August 6, 2026.]

data.title: Monte Brione
data.text:
Monte Brione (not to be confused with the mountain range) is a Montbrió del Camp based company, that was established in 1944 by local farmers of the "Cooperativa Agrícola de Montbrió del Camp (Agricultural Cooperative of Montbrió del Camp)." This company is specifically a co-operative, which means that it isn't specifically a single-founder company. The cooperative describes itself as people who are passionate for the land.

== Produce ==

Monte Brione make a variety of products, that are in the range of olive oil, food (in-store only) and drink. The olive oil is a luxury type, that can only really be farmed in the Baix Camp comarca. The type of olive oil that Monte Brione produce is called "arbequina", which means that it is only farmed from that type of olive. They also make wines, vermouth and "muscatel" which is a wine made from the grapes with the same name. Their vermouth is called "La Fadrina and Lo Fadri" which roughly translates to "The young woman and the young man" in Catalan. Their muscatel is called "Autentic Moscatell de Montbrio" which literally translates to "Genuine muscatel from Montbrio". Their wine is called "Vi di missa de Montbrio", which very roughly translates to "I went to Mass in Montbrio." Their rotisserie chicken is found in their stores, and for 5 euros, you can buy a full rotisserie chicken with fries. [ref: Authentic wine vinegar from the Cooperative, Authentic wine vinegar from the Cooperative]

data.title: Glub (artist)
data.text:
Glub, art name of Manuel Ramos (born 1969), is a Spanish
graffiti writer and painter. He is regarded as one of the pioneers of
native Madrid graffiti, the style known as "flechero", alongside
Muelle and Bleck la Rata. Since 2010 he has worked in
geometric abstraction, developing the lines he terms "Rigid Geometry", "Minimum Abstract
Geometry" and "Transparent Abstract Geometry". He is also a typeface designer and a
musician. [ref: La intuición geométrica de Manuel Ramos, Geometricae]

== Biography ==

Ramos was born in Madrid in 1969 and began painting the streets of the city in 1986,
when the local graffiti scene was barely emerging. [ref: La historia de Glub, el grafitero amigo de Muelle..., El Mundo] He lived near
the Pacífico neighbourhood, between Atocha and Puente de Vallecas, and signed the
advertising posters of the Madrid Metro, a traditional surface of the city's native
graffiti movement. [ref: BTR#20: Glub, una vida de graffiti, Breaking The Rules]

In 1989 he adopted the elaborate aesthetics of New York graffiti, joining the emerging
Spanish hip hop scene; as a result he is considered a forerunner of the Spanish
"old school". In that period he painted with writers such as Larry 88, Rafita, Tifón
and Carmona, with whom he founded the ACT Crew in 1991. He also acted as a link
between the Madrid and Alicante scenes. [ref: GLUB y su «Top 10 Canciones», El Ritmo de la Calle]

He graduated in Fine Arts (painting) from the Complutense University of Madrid in
1998. [ref: Manuel Ramos, ArteInformado] He has lived in Valencia for a number of years, where he
painted with the local writers Ove, Noke, Tabe and Pike as a member of the Yes crew.

== Work ==

=== Madrid native graffiti ===

Glub's signature, an arrowed pictogram drawn with fine calligraphic strokes, is part of
the history of Madrid graffiti. It is documented in the reference volume
Madrid Graffiti 1982–1995 (Figueroa-Saavedra and Gálvez, 2002) [ref: Madrid Graffiti 1982-1995, Megamultimedia]
and in Nicholas Ganz's international survey Graffiti. Art of the Five Continents
(2004). [ref: Graffiti. Art of the Five Continents, Gustavo Gili] The Spanish Graffiare archive keeps photographs of his work
from the 1990s (Pacífico, Ventilla, Alcorcón, Plaza de Castilla) and a 2000 interview. [ref: Entrevista a GLUB, Spanish Graffiare]
In 2001 the magazine Geometricae published the photograph
Muelle (left) + Glub — signatures on a wall, Madrid, 2001, showing the two pioneers
signing the same wall.

=== Geometric abstraction ===

Since 2010 Ramos has painted geometric abstractions on traditional supports. A 2025
review by the geometric art magazine Geometricae describes his work as a bridge
between the immediacy of urban art and the conceptual depth of geometric abstraction,
and identifies three personal lines: "Rigid Geometry", "Minimum Abstract Geometry" and
"Transparent Abstract Geometry". In the latter he applies spray paint and the stencilling
technique to create soft colour gradations on canvas, an inheritance from his graffiti
practice.

His solo exhibitions include Geometries Cromàtics (Espai Llimera, Valencia, 2016),
Modulaciones (Ama-Gi Club, Valencia, 2016), Abstracción geométrica (Ama-Gi Club,
Valencia, 2018), Nuevas Geometrías (Espai Llimera, Valencia, 2020) and
Exposition de peinture abstraite géométrique (Colegio de España, Paris, 2018). [ref: Curriculum - Manuel Ramos, ArteInformado]

== Collection and recognition ==

A work by Glub was acquired by the Museum of European and Mediterranean
Civilisations (MuCEM) in Marseille, France, and shown in the exhibition
Graff en Méditerranée (Fort Saint-Jean, 2017–2018); the museum publishes a photograph
of the piece, credited to Yves Inchierman, on the exhibition page. [ref: Graff en Méditerranée, MuCEM]
Another work belongs to the Colegio de España in Paris (2018), and a third one to the
Junta Municipal de Arganzuela in Madrid (1999); he also received the acquisition prize of
the "Premios de Arganzuela" painting competition in 1999.

Since 2017 he has been a member of the editorial team of the geometric art magazine
Geometricae, which published the monographic catalogues of his work
Geometría Abstracta Transparente (2018, 36 pp., with texts by Ramos himself) and
Nuevas Geometrías (2020), and dedicated an extensive review to his painting in
2025. [ref: Geometría Abstracta Transparente – Manuel Ramos, Geometricae]

== Other activities ==

=== Typography ===

Under his own name, he has published seventy typefaces on the site DaFont,
with more than 2.6 million downloads, including graffiti-based scripts such as
"Graffont" and "Arsone" and the popular designs "Metropolis" and "Alameda". [ref: Manuel Ramos (fonts), DaFont]

=== Music ===

In 2026 he released the album Rizomatic on the dub house label Haibt,
distributed digitally on YouTube with tracks such as "KEF" and "Genesis". [ref: Rizomatic – Glub (album), YouTube]

== Publications ==

* Memorias en graffiti (2007, self-published, edition of 100 copies; updated edition
available since 2022).
* Relatos de un escritor de graffiti (2009, free online publication, with
contributions by Trase, El Niño de las Pinturas, Suso 033, among others).
* Geometría Abstracta Transparente – monographic catalogue, Geometricae, 2018.
* Nuevas Geometrías – exhibition catalogue, Geometricae, 2020.

data.title: Mozambique Revolutionary Committee
data.text:
The Mozambican Revolutionary Committee (Portugeuse: Comite Revolucionário de Moçambique), commonly known by its Portugeuse acronym COREMO, was an insurgent rebel group active in Mozambique between 1965 and 1982.

COREMO was founded in 1965 in Lusaka after splitting from FRELIMO over ideological differences due to the Sino-Soviet split. FRELIMO leader Samora Machel's internal party purges and close alignment with the Soviet Union had alienated many moderate socialists and anti-Soviet Maoists. [ref: Roots of Counter-Revolution: The "Mozambique National Resistance", Review of African Political Economy]
This caused a faction of FRELIMO under Adelino Gwambe to break away under the banner of COREMO.

It quickly became the second-largest independence movement in Mozambique during the Mozambican War of Independence. COREMO received significant financial and ideological backing from the People's Republic of China and Kenneth Kaunda's Zambia. [ref: Taylor, I. (2006) China and Africa: Engagement and Compromise, Routledge, p.95]

Its ideological base mainly consisted of a mix of Maoism, anti-Sovietism, a fierce opposition to the Machel administration, and moderate pan-African socialist politics. However, COREMO suffered from multiple intra-party ideological friction, with many factions leaning right-wing and anti-communist, preferring a closer alignment with RENAMO, during the Mozambican Civil War. [ref: Cabrita (2001) pp. 40-41]

Its leadership initially consisted of Gwambe but after an internal party purge in the mid-1960s, [ref: Marcum (2017) p.68] Paulo José Gumane became the Leader. He guided the group through the end of the Mozambican War of Independence, [ref: Marcum (2017) p.68] before being allegedly executed by FRELIMO loyalists in mid-1970s. [ref: Truth and Reconciliation Commission of South Africa report, Volume 2, 1998, p.371] Later leadership consisted of figures like Julius K. Ndozi who failed to stop the increasing factionalism, which ultimately culminated in the group's downfall.

Following the 1974 Lusaka Accord and the establishment of the People's Republic of Mozambique, a civil war started in the country. Backed by Malawi, Rhodesia, and apartheid South Africa, anti-communist RENAMO insurgents fought against the ruling FRELIMO government. COREMO opposed both sides and instead sought a non-aligned socialist state, continuing their own insurgency. [ref: Manning, C. (2002) The Politics of Peace in Mozambique: Post-conflict Democratization, 1992-2000, Greenwood, p.48]

By 1982, COREMO had completely fractured internally. Anti-communist and right-wing factions increased and fled to RENAMO, [ref: Cabrita (2001) pp. 40-41] and the significance of neutralism diminished as the Cold War reached its second-largest nuclear height. The group has been believed to have been either dissolved or merged into RENAMO around 1982.

data.title: Ananta Mandal
data.text:
Ananta Mandal (born 5 February 1983) is an Indian artist, known for his artwork depicting urban life, architecture, landscapes and human experiences. He lives and works in Mumbai, India. [ref: Multifarious impressions of Ananta Mandal, The Times of India]

==Early life and education==
Ananta Mandal spent his childhood in Chakdaha, West Bengal. He has a degree in Fine Arts from the Government College of Art & Craft, Kolkata, Calcutta University in 2007. Mandal stayed in Kolkata from 2002 to 2007, during this period he began painting scenes of everyday life in Kolkata. In 2008 he moved to Mumbai. [ref: About Ananta Mandal, Ananta Mandal official website] [ref: Mandal's country canvas in town for art lovers, The Times of India]

==Career==
Ananta Mandal has 18 Solo Exhibitions in over twenty years of his career, starting in 2004 when he had his first solo show at Academy of Fine Arts, Kolkata as a student.His artwork has been displayed in many cities across India and internationally, including the Lalit Kala Akademi, Jehangir Art Gallery, Triveni Kala Sangam, Nehru Centre Art Gallery, and World Art Dubai. He has also frequently been invited as a guest artist. [ref: Capturing landscapes on his canvas, The Times of India]
[ref: 18th Solo Exhibition at World Art Dubai, UAE, Ananta Mandal official blog] [ref: The paintings of Ananta Mandal are suffused with a serene simplicity., Indian Express]

Most of Mandal's paintings are watercolor, acrylic, charcoal and oil color based. His paintings depict realistic urban landscapes, city life, glorious Varanasi Ghats the spiritual heart of India, Bengalis durga festival (durga puja), Horse in Motion, tropical desert of Rajasthan and moods of nature. Many of his works depict the atmosphere of Mumbai and Kolkata. [ref: The crowd, the speed and architecture of this dream city inspires me, Bombay Times] [ref: Painting his love, The Indian Express] [ref: Treat for the senses, Millennium Post]

==Awards==

*First place Award: 2013 International Exhibition of the Watercolor Art Society-Houston, United States [ref: Rich canvases saturate watercolor event, Houston Chronicle]
* Award: 2009, 2006 San Diego Watercolor Society, United States [ref: http://www.sdws.org/ a Watercolor society in USA, the Official website.] [ref: [https://anantamandal.com/artist Ananta Mandal Official Website, Awards]]
*Award: 2013, 2012 AIFACS all India Exhibition, New Delhi [ref: http://www.aifacs.org.in/ an independent arts organisation in India, the Official website.]
*Award: 2011, 2009, 2005 Bombay Art Society. Mumbai [ref: https://bombayartsociety.org/ an independent arts organisation in India, the Official website.]
* Award: 2005 Best Painting Award Academy of Fine Arts, Kolkata.
* Award: 2005 Birla Academy Art & Culture. Kolkata [ref: http://www.birlaart.com/ a major cultural activities center in Kolkata, India, the Official website.]

data.title: BookMyShow (ticketing platform)
data.text:
BookMyShow is an Indian online ticketing and entertainment platform operated by Big Tree Entertainment Private Limited. It provides ticketing services for films, concerts, theatrical performances, sporting events and other entertainment activities. The company was founded in 2007, with its headquarters in Mumbai, Maharashtra. [ref: India's BookMyShow pulls in $100M to grow its online ticketing business, TechCrunch] [ref: About Us, BookMyShow]

The company has expanded from online ticketing into live-event promotion, production and event infrastructure. Its live-events business has become a significant part of its operations, alongside its ticketing business. [ref: Going-out economy: No longer a one-man show, [[The Financial Express (India)] [ref: BookMyShow moves up the live-events chain, [[The Financial Express (India)] [ref: KKR Backs BookMyShow As Live Entertainment Becomes Its Next Growth Engine, Inc42]

== History ==

=== Establishment and acquisitions ===

Big Tree Entertainment was established in 1999 by Ashish Hemrajani, Rajesh Balpande and Parikshit Dar. The company initially provided software and inventory-management services to the cinema industry before launching BookMyShow as a consumer-facing online ticketing service in 2007.

BookMyShow expanded its ticketing and event-related operations through a series of acquisitions. In 2013, Big Tree Entertainment acquired Chennai-based online ticketing company TicketGreen. It acquired a majority stake in Bengaluru-based Eventifier, a social media analytics company, in 2015 and Chennai-based sports fan relationship management company Fantain Sports in 2016. [ref: BookMyShow.com acquires Chennai-based Ticketgreen.com, Business Standard] [ref: Bookmyshow buys majority stake in Eventifier for $2 million, ETRetail] [ref: BookMyShow buys Chennai-based startup Fantain Sports to expand user base, The Economic Times]

In 2017, BookMyShow acquired Hyderabad-based online ticketing platform MastiTickets and acquired a 75% stake in Pune-based event-registration platform Townscript. It also acquired the restaurant-discovery platform Burrp from Network18 through its subsidiary Foodfesta Wellcare and acquired the digital entertainment company Nfusion, using technology from the latter to develop its audio-entertainment offering Jukebox. [ref: BookMyShow buys Hyderabad-based MastiTickets in all-cash deal, Business Standard] [ref: Bookmyshow picks up 75% stake in Townscript, [[Mint (newspaper)] [ref: BookMyShow acquires Mumbai-based Burrp, The Economic Times] [ref: BookMyShow acquires digital entertainment firm Nfusion, Business Standard]

=== Regional and international expansion ===

In October 2017, BookMyShow expanded the language options available on its website and Android application to include Marathi, Malayalam, Gujarati and Punjabi, alongside Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and English. [ref: बुकमायशो आता मराठीसह अन्य ३ भाषांत उपलब्ध, Maharashtra Times]

The company expanded into Southeast Asia during the late 2010s. In November 2018, it joined Grab Ventures Velocity, an accelerator programme associated with Southeast Asian technology company Grab, as part of its international expansion. In December 2019, BookMyShow separated its Southeast Asian operations into a distinct business headquartered in Singapore. [ref: BookMyShow Joins Grab Ventures Velocity Program With An Eye On Southeast Asia, Inc42] [ref: BookMyShow separates SE Asia Arm, The Economic Times]

=== COVID-19 pandemic ===

Restrictions on cinema screenings and live events during the COVID-19 pandemic significantly affected BookMyShow's operations. During 2021, as cinemas and entertainment venues remained closed owing to the pandemic, the company reduced its workforce. [ref: തിയറ്ററുകളും ഷോകളും ഇല്ല; ബുക്ക് മൈ ഷോ 200 ജീവനക്കാരെ കൂടി പിരിച്ച് വിട്ടു, Madhyamam]

It looked into pursuing other business avenues in response to the pandemic's impact on cinema and live-event ticketing. Its recovery strategy included diversification beyond the traditional ticketing business. [ref: Streaming now: BookMyShow and its fight back, Forbes India]

The company performed further restructuring that resulted in reducing its workforce from approximately 1,600 employees before the pandemic to around 600 afterwards. [ref: How BookMyShow Is Helping Turn India Into A Global Concert Market, Pollstar]

== Business development ==

BookMyShow expanded beyond ticketing into live-event promotion, production and infrastructure. By the 2020s, these activities had become a significant part of its business alongside online ticketing. [ref: A Strategic Analysis of Online Movie and Event Ticketing Platform: BookMyShow, Journal of The Gujarat Research Society]

In 2026, live events accounted for a substantial share of the company's business. The expansion has included investments in staging equipment, venues, production capabilities and entertainment properties, reducing the company's reliance on external event infrastructure and increasing its involvement across the live-events value chain. [ref: Beyond Attention. Into Immersion, [[Ernst & Young]

The company's live-events revenue increased from ₹24.6 crore in the 2021–22 financial year to ₹237.5 crore in 2022–23, ₹455 crore in 2023–24 and ₹756 crore in 2024–25.

=== Online ticketing ===

BookMyShow provides online ticket booking for cinema screenings, concerts, theatrical productions, comedy performances, sporting events and other entertainment activities. The platform also provides ticketing and registration services for event organisers.

=== Live entertainment ===

BookMyShow operates in the live-entertainment sector through BookMyShow Live. Its activities include the promotion and organisation of concerts, music festivals and other live events, as well as event production and infrastructure.

BookMyShow Live has served as promoter and co-producer of Lollapalooza India, working with international festival partners. The company has also been involved in producing and promoting concerts by international artists in India. [ref: BookMyShow's Anil Makhija On The 'Unprecedented Response' For Lolla India, Pollstar]

== Selected events and partnerships ==

BookMyShow has participated in entertainment and sporting events in different capacities, including ticketing, event management, promotion and production. Its activities have included partnerships with sports competitions, international entertainment companies and music festivals. [ref: BookMyShow: India's largest online entertainment ticketing site is looking beyond the box office, The Economic Times]

Selected examples include the following:

* In 2010, BookMyShow entered sports ticketing through partnerships involving teams in the Indian Premier League.
* In 2015, it partnered with Disney India in connection with the Indian production of the musical Beauty and the Beast.
* In 2017, BookMyShow was the exclusive ticketing partner for Justin Bieber's Purpose World Tour concert in Mumbai. [ref: Justin Bieber's Mumbai gig tickets, priced at Rs 4000 upwards, to go on sale today, The Economic Times] [ref: How to score a ticket for Justin Bieber's India concert, GQ India]
* In 2019, BookMyShow partnered with Live Nation for U2's The Joshua Tree Tour concert in Mumbai. [ref: Bringing This U2 Concert to India Has Not Been Easy: Ashish Hemrajani of BookMyShow, Rolling Stone India]
* From 2023, BookMyShow Live has been involved in the Indian edition of Lollapalooza, including its promotion and co-production.
* In 2025, BookMyShow Live produced and promoted Ed Sheeran's India performances as part of his Mathematics Tour. [ref: Inside Ed Sheeran's Mathematics Run In India With BookMyShow's Naman Pugalia, Pollstar] It also promoted Coldplay's Music of the Spheres World Tour concerts in Mumbai and Ahmedabad. [ref: India's rising concert economy: Coldplay's Ahmedabad tour sets the blueprint for India's next cultural boomtowns, [[Ernst & Young]
* In 2027, BookMyShow Live is scheduled to partner with HYBE for the first Indian edition of Weverse Con Festival, to be held in New Delhi. [ref: HYBE to bring Weverse Con Festival to India in 2027, marks first edition outside Korea, Mid-Day]

== Financial performance ==

Big Tree Entertainment reported revenue from operations of ₹1,396.86 crore and a net profit of ₹108.63 crore for the 2023–24 financial year. Revenue from operations increased to ₹1,831.43 crore in 2024–25, while net profit rose to ₹192.37 crore. [ref: BookMyShow profit up 28% in FY24 at Rs 108 crore, Moneycontrol] [ref: FY25: BookMyShow boosts ad spend by 21%, Exchange4Media] [ref: BookMyShow posts Rs 192 crore profit on robust live events business, The Economic Times]

In 2024–25, revenue from online ticketing was approximately ₹828 crore, while the live-events business generated approximately ₹756 crore. The growth of live events represented a substantial increase from previous financial years and became an important component of the company's overall business. [ref: Our decisions are not driven by others in this market, [[The Financial Express (India)]

In August 2026, global investment firm KKR entered into definitive agreements to acquire a minority stake in BookMyShow. The companies did not disclose the financial terms. Reuters, citing a source familiar with the transaction, reported that the stake was approximately 6% and valued at between US$40 million and US$50 million, implying a valuation of approximately US$667 million to US$833 million. [ref: KKR to buy 6% stake in India's BookMyShow for up to $50 million, source says, Reuters]

== Competition ==

BookMyShow’s competitors include Eternal's District and Flipkart. Competition extends to cinema ticketing, live events and other entertainment activities. [ref: Flipkart Plans to Sell Concert and Movie Tickets Soon, Rolling Stone India]

== Criticism and controversies ==

=== Coldplay ticket sales ===

In September 2024, the sale of tickets for Coldplay's concerts in India attracted complaints concerning alleged irregularities and the resale of tickets at substantially higher prices on unauthorised platforms. The Mumbai Police Economic Offences Wing started an enquiry into allegations of black marketing and summoned senior officials of the company. [ref: How police complaint by Mumbai lawyer who couldn't get Coldplay tickets led to probe against BookMyShow, others, The Indian Express]

In February 2025, the Economic Offences Wing closed the preliminary enquiry, stating that it had found no evidence of manipulation or other irregularities that required a criminal case against BookMyShow. [ref: Coldplay tickets row: Mumbai Police drop case against BookMyShow, says no manipulation evidence found, India Today]

=== Competition law ===

BookMyShow's agreements with cinema operators were the subject of a complaint before the Competition Commission of India (CCI) alleging anti-competitive practices relating to exclusivity and refusal to deal. In March 2026, the CCI closed the case after considering the allegations and evidence, finding that a contravention of the Competition Act had not been established. [ref: Showtyme (through Vijay Gopal, Prop. of Vanila Entertainments) and Big Tree Entertainment Pvt. Ltd. (BookMyShow), Competition Commission of India]

=== Kunal Kamra listing dispute ===

In April 2025, comedian Kunal Kamra questioned whether listing of his shows had been removed from BookMyShow following controversy surrounding remarks about Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde. BookMyShow stated that event listings were managed by organisers and venues and disputed the characterisation of the matter as a delisting by the platform. [ref: BookMyShow releases statement after Kunal Kamra asks ticketing platform not to 'delist' him: 'Facts been misrepresented', Hindustan Times]
