data.title: Joe Swanson
data.text:
----

Joseph "Joe" Lee Swanson [ref: A Hero Sits Next Door] is a fictional character from the American adult animated sitcom Family Guy. He is a neighbor and friend of the Griffin family, best known for being an intensely muscular, short-tempered paraplegic police officer who is confined to a wheelchair. The show's creator, Seth MacFarlane, designed the character, who is voiced by actor Patrick Warburton. Joe lives at 33 Spooner Street in Quahog, Rhode Island, and completes the core neighborhood friend group alongside Peter Griffin, Glenn Quagmire, and Cleveland Brown.

==Role in the show==

Joe works as a dedicated police officer for the Quahog Police Department. He lives on Spooner Street with his wife, Bonnie Swanson, with whom he shares a deeply strained and mutually exhausting marriage. Together they have two children: Kevin, a troubled Iraq War veteran, and Susie, an infant daughter. [ref: Family Guy: "Believe it Or Not, Joe's Walking On Air" Review, IGN] [ref: Family Guy: “Thanksgiving.”, The A.V. Club] Joe is one of Peter Griffin's best friends and is frequently seen drinking with Peter, Quagmire, and Cleveland at their local hangout, The Drunken Clam. [ref: Family Guy: “Joe's Revenge”, The A.V. Club]

The origin of Joe's disability has been a recurring plot point throughout the series. He originally claimed that he was paralyzed after faking a fight with the Grinch on Christmas Eve. [ref: Review: Family Guy "Joe's Revenge", Bubbleblabber] However, the episode "Joe's Revenge" later revealed the true story: Joe was shot in both legs by a heroin dealer named Bobby Briggs during an undercover operation. Despite his paralysis, Joe possesses extraordinary, near-superhuman upper-body strength and is a highly capable hand-to-hand combatant.

In early seasons of the show, Joe was characterized as a fiercely competitive, respected, and highly confident hero who frequently intimidated Peter. As the series progressed, his characterization shifted dramatically. In later seasons, Joe is often depicted as severely depressed, emotionally vulnerable, and insecure. He is frequently subjected to dynamic shifts in the group, often acting as the resident "punching bag" whose disability and domestic misery are the butt of his friends' jokes. [ref: Family Guy: The 4 Best (& 5 Worst) Recurring Characters, Screen Rant]

In addition to his routine police work, Joe's health and physical condition have served as the focal point for several major storylines. In the episode "Believe It or Not, Joe's Walking on Air," he undergoes an experimental spine transplant surgery that successfully restores his ability to walk. However, his newly regained mobility causes him to become arrogant and abusive toward his friends, leading Peter, Quagmire, and Cleveland to team up and re-break his spine to return him to his status quo. Joe has also participated in various high-stakes neighborhood misadventures, including traveling overseas with the guys and assembling his paraplegic friends to combine their wheelchairs into a giant, Voltron-style functional robot known as "Crippletron." [ref: Family Guy: "No Meals on Wheels" Review, IGN]

==Creation and design==

Joe Swanson was created by Seth MacFarlane and writers Mike Barker and Matt Weitzman for the fifth episode of the first season of Family Guy, titled "A Hero Sits Next Door." [ref: Inside Family Guy: An Illustrated History, HarperDesign] To contrast with the rest of the neighborhood characters, Joe was designed as an overly intense, athletic alpha male whose physical limitations were intentionally juxtaposed against his incredible determination and "super-cop" persona. [ref: How Family Guy's Characters Are Completely Different Now, CinemaBlend] Actor Patrick Warburton was cast to voice the character, using his signature loud, booming, and hyper-masculine inflection to drive home the aggressive, intense authority required for the role. [ref: Random Roles: Patrick Warburton, The A.V. Club]

MacFarlane cast Patrick Warburton for the role after becoming a fan of his deadpan comedic timing and deep, booming baritone voice, which Warburton had previously popularized as David Puddy on Seinfeld. [ref: ‘We do need humour in our lives’: Seinfeld’s Patrick Warburton slams cancel culture, Evening Standard] In behind-the-scenes interviews, Warburton has noted that Joe's voice is essentially a heightened, high-energy extension of his own natural speaking register, made to match the character's relentless intensity and physical over-compensation. [ref: A 'Family Guy' Voice Actor Once Refused to Record an Episode Over a Joke He Said Went Too Far, Vice]

==Reception==

Joe Swanson has generated significant analysis from television critics who widely praised his addition as an essential fixture on Spooner Street. In an early-season retrospective for IGN, television commentator Ahsan Haque lauded the character's conceptual debut, writing that the narrative-driven story serves as a "great introduction for Joe" and successfully establishes his unique dynamic within the regular neighborhood roster. Haque particularly praised the physical comedy surrounding the character's narrative heights, characterizing the sequence where Joe combines his wheelchair-bound friends into a massive, Voltron-style functional robot known as the "Cripple-Tron" as a brilliant display of "sheer creativity". [ref: Family Guy: Top 10 Fights, IGN]

Industry commentators have regularly highlighted how Patrick Warburton's real-life experiences with his own family contrast with his role. According to a report by Chris Barilla for People, Warburton shared at PaleyFest that his parents heavily despise Family Guy's offensive satire, stating, "They hate the show even more today than they did twenty-five years ago." Despite Warburton helping to financially support his parents with his earnings from the series, his mother belonged to the PTC and actively "tried to get the show canceled," even attempting to get her own son to sign the petition. [ref: Patrick Warburton's Mom Wanted Family Guy 'Canceled' Despite the Money He Gave Her from the Show, PEOPLE]

Conversely, television reviewer Dave Jones writing for Screen Rant evaluated the dramatic progression of the neighbor, observing that although he was introduced as a confident, badass cop in the first season, Joe Swanson has uniquely devolved into a tragic "punching bag" over the years, rivaled only by the incessant bullying faced by Meg Griffin. [ref: Family Guy: The 4 Best (& 5 Worst) Recurring Characters, Screen Rant]

== References ==

data.title: Arthur Plunkett (British Army officer)
data.text:
Lieutenant-Colonel Arthur William Valentine Plunkett (4 May 1868 – 17 April 1903) was a British Army officer who served as a major in the Manchester Regiment and held the local rank of lieutenant-colonel while commanding the 2nd Battalion of the King's African Rifles. He was killed during the Dervish War at the Battle of Agaarweyne, also known as Gumburu. [ref: Somaliland, Hutchinson and Co.]

== Early life and education ==

Arthur William Valentine Plunkett was born on 4 May 1868, the son of Lieutenant-Colonel G. T. Plunkett, CB. [ref: Churchill and the Mad Mullah of Somaliland: Betrayal and Redemption 1899–1921, Pen and Sword Military] [ref: A Manchester Officer's Will, Manchester Evening News] He attended the Royal Military College, Sandhurst from 1886. [ref: Dover college register, 1871-1894,, ST George's Press]

Plunkett was commissioned as a second lieutenant in the Manchester Regiment on 14 March 1888 and was promoted to lieutenant in November 1889. [ref: Somaliland, Hutchinson and Co.] [ref: Hart's Annual Army List, Militia List, and Imperial Yeomanry List] He was promoted to captain in 1897. [ref: Dover college register, 1871-1894,, ST George's Press]

== Military career ==
=== British India service ===
Plunkett first saw active service in 1891, when he took part in the Second Miranzai Expedition with the 2nd Battalion of the Manchester Regiment. For his service in the expedition he received a medal with clasp. [ref: Somaliland, Hutchinson and Co.]

During the North-West Frontier campaigns of 1897–1898, Plunkett served as assistant to the divisional transport officer with the Malakand expeditionary force. He participated in operations in Bajaur and the Mohmand country, for which he received the India Medal with clasp. [ref: Somaliland, Hutchinson and Co.]

Plunkett subsequently served as assistant transport officer of the 1st Division during the Tirah campaign. During the campaign he took part in the capture of the Sampagha and Arhanga passes, operations against the Khani Khel, and operations in the Bazar Valley in December 1897. His service earned him an additional clasp to his medal. [ref: Somaliland, Hutchinson and Co.] [ref: Churchill and the Mad Mullah of Somaliland: Betrayal and Redemption 1899–1921, Pen and Sword Military]

=== Central Africa, Uganda and Gambia service ===

In March 1899, Plunkett was seconded for service in Central Africa and joined the 2nd (Central Africa) Battalion of the King's African Rifles. He subsequently served in Uganda and Central Africa. In 1901, Plunkett took part in a British expedition in the Gambia. He was mentioned in dispatches for his service and received a medal with clasp. [ref: Churchill and the Mad Mullah of Somaliland: Betrayal and Redemption 1899–1921, Pen and Sword Military] [ref: Somaliland, Hutchinson and Co.]

In June 1901, Plunkett was promoted to the substantive rank of major. In August 1902, Plunkett was granted the local rank of lieutenant-colonel. Although he continued to hold the substantive rank of major in the Manchester Regiment, he now commanded the 2nd Battalion of the King's African Rifles as a local lieutenant-colonel. [ref: Somaliland, Hutchinson and Co.]

== Dervish War and death ==

After service in Uganda and Central Africa, he accompanied the battalion to British Somaliland during the campaign against the Dervish movement. Plunkett subsequently served in Colonel Eric Swayne's column during the fighting at the Battle of Erego. Contemporary newspapers credited his bravery with helping to prevent the engagement from becoming a more serious defeat. [ref: Mainly About People, [[The Star (1888-1960)]

The Battle of Agaarweyne began on 15 April 1903 after Captain Olivey, while conducting a scouting mission from Colonel Cobbe's position, reported a large body of mounted and dismounted Dervish forces approximately four miles from the camp.
Cobbe sent Plunkett with a company of the 2nd King's African Rifles, 50 men of the 2nd Sikhs and two Maxim guns to reinforce Olivey and assist his return. Although his orders were confined to bringing Olivey's company back, Plunkett continued the advance after joining him and was drawn into contact with the main Dervish force. The Dervishes repeatedly charged the square from several directions, with cavalry attacking its front and flanks while spearmen and dismounted riflemen attacked from the rear. Neither rifle nor Maxim fire succeeded in stopping the repeated assaults, which continued as British casualties mounted and their ammunition diminished. Plunkett was among the first officers wounded and subsequently received a spear thrust, but continued fighting. [ref: Somaliland, Hutchinson and Co.] [ref: The Mad Mullah of Somaliland, Herbert Jenkins Limited]

With the ammunition nearly exhausted and further defence of the square becoming impossible, Plunkett ordered the survivors to break formation and charge through the surrounding Dervish forces with fixed bayonets in an attempt to return to Cobbe's camp. They gained only a short distance before the force was overwhelmed. Plunkett and all the other British officers with the force were killed. Jardine recorded 187 men and nine British officers killed and 29 wounded, while Hamilton stated that only 41 men survived, of whom just six were unwounded. Hamilton described the reverse as a serious loss to the expedition, particularly because of the experience of the officers killed, and considered Plunkett one of its best officers, praising his "indomitable energy and dash", as well as his conduct under fire. He further noted the considerable respect in which Plunkett was held by the men of the 2nd King's African Rifles. [ref: Somaliland, Hutchinson and Co.] [ref: The Mad Mullah of Somaliland, Herbert Jenkins Limited] [ref: The London Gazette, The London Gazette]

== Personal life ==

Plunkett married Winifred Hadwen, the daughter of Joseph Hadwen, a justice of the peace from Manchester, at St Mary Abbots in Kensington on 15 May 1901. [ref: Court and Personal, [[Manchester Courier] At the time of Plunkett's death, his widow was living at Stoness, Ashurst, Tunbridge Wells. His estate was valued at £1,171 10s. 10d. gross and £1,042 10s. 10d. net. [ref: A Manchester Officer's Will, Manchester Evening News]

== References ==

data.title: The Alleys (film)
data.text:
The Alleys () is a 2021 Jordanian crime thriller film written and directed by Bassel Ghandour in his feature directorial debut. Set in a neighbourhood of East Amman, the film follows a small-time hustler whose secret relationship sets off a chain of blackmail, gossip and violence. It stars Emad Azmi, Baraka Rahmani, Munther Rayahnah, Nadira Omran and Maisa Abd Elhadi.

The film had its world premiere in the Piazza Grande section of the 74th Locarno Film Festival in August 2021, the first Jordanian feature to screen at the festival. It was released in Jordanian and Saudi cinemas in June 2022. Its uncensored version was released on Netflix in January 2023, where it became one of the most-watched films in Jordan; its profanity and its portrayal of Jordanian society provoked criticism from conservative members of the Jordanian parliament.

== Plot ==
In a gossip-ridden neighbourhood of East Amman, Ali, a young hustler who earns fees by steering tourists to an escort bar, is secretly in love with Lana. They hide the relationship from Lana's mother, Aseel, a beauty salon owner who disapproves of Ali's lower-class background. When Aseel receives a surveillance video of the couple in a compromising position, along with a demand for hush money, she turns to Abbas, a local gangster, to suppress the video and drive Ali away from her daughter; in exchange, she agrees to make up Abbas's call girls in her salon. As Aseel pressures Lana to accept another suitor, Ali urges her to elope with him and, before they flee, robs Abbas of the protection money he collects from the neighbourhood, cutting out the gangster's tongue in the fight. When Lana finds Ali's gun and the stolen cash, she abandons him, and Abbas and his loyal lieutenant Hanadi set out for revenge, leading to further violence.

== Cast ==
* Emad Azmi as Ali
* Baraka Rahmani as Lana
* Munther Rayahnah as Abbas
* Nadira Omran as Aseel
* Maisa Abd Elhadi as Hanadi

== Production ==
The Alleys is the first feature directed by Bassel Ghandour, who previously co-wrote and produced Theeb (2014), which was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film at the 88th Academy Awards and won the BAFTA Award for Outstanding Debut. The film was produced by Rula Nasser of The Imaginarium Films and Yousef Abed Alnabi of Bayt Al Shawareb, with Shahinaz El-Akkad's Lagoonie Film Production as co-producer. It is a co-production between Jordan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Qatar. It was filmed in Jabal Al Natheef, a densely built neighbourhood of East Amman.

The project was developed through the EAVE Producers Workshop and received support from the Jordan Film Fund of the Royal Film Commission, the Doha Film Institute, Dubai Film Connection and the Red Sea Lodge. At the 2020 Cairo Film Connection, the co-production platform of the Cairo International Film Festival, it won the Badyã Award and the New Century Productions Prize, each worth US$10,000. Earlier that year it received the Works in Progress Post-production Development Award at the Eastern Promises industry programme of the Karlovy Vary International Film Festival.

The cinematography is by Justin Hamilton, the editing by Eyad Hamam, and the original score by Nasser Sharaf. A soundtrack album was released in September 2022.

== Release ==
The Alleys premiered in August 2021 in the Piazza Grande at the 74th Locarno Film Festival. It was the first Jordanian feature selected for the festival and the first Arab film shown in the Piazza Grande since 2008. It then competed for the Sutherland Award for best first feature at the BFI London Film Festival, and had its Arab premiere at the inaugural Red Sea International Film Festival in Jeddah in December 2021. In January 2022 it became the first Jordanian film selected for the International Film Festival Rotterdam.

The film was released commercially on 9 June 2022 in Jordan, through Arab Media Network, and in Saudi Arabia, through Rowad Media, opening in four Jordanian and 21 Saudi cinemas. The theatrical version had scenes with explicit language either removed or bleeped. It was released in the United Arab Emirates on 6 October 2022 and in Egypt in November 2022. MAD Solutions handled distribution in the Arab world, and the Paris-based company Elle Driver handled international sales.

The uncensored version was released on Netflix on 5 January 2023. In July 2024 it was added to the Arabic streaming service Shahid.

== Reception ==
=== Critical response ===
Reviewing the film from Locarno for Variety, Jay Weissberg found it "unattractively shot and weighed down by too many unappealing, witless characters", though he praised Nadira Omran's performance as Aseel. Screen Daily described the film as "by turns dark comedy, mystery thriller and crime drama". After its Netflix release, The New York Times recommended it as an international streaming pick, describing it as "somewhere between a mafia movie and a comedy of errors". Writing for Arab News in February 2023, William Mullally called it "the best-received film set in Jordan" since Theeb.

=== Controversy in Jordan ===
After its Netflix release, The Alleys topped the service's most-watched list in Jordan for several weeks. Audiences were divided: supporters praised what they saw as an "accurate take" on life in Amman, while critics called it a "false representation" of Jordanian society and objected to its obscene language. Conservative members of parliament condemned the film's profanity and its depiction of society. MP Muhammad Abu Suailik called for the Royal Film Commission, which had helped fund the film, to be prosecuted "for supporting films that distort the public image of Jordanian society", and MP Suleiman Abu Yahya demanded that actor Munther Rayahnah be stripped of his citizenship for defending the film on social media. The Royal Film Commission responded that its role is to promote film production in Jordan and "not [to have] oversight" of what types of films are made there.

data.title: Karlis Beinerts
data.text:
Karlis Beinerts (born April 1952, Latvia) is a Latvian choir conductor and music pedagogue, best known as the long-serving director of the Riga 3rd Music School (Rīgas 3. mūzikas skola) [https://katalogs-iksd.riga.lv/lv/Iestade/R3MS [16]] — a post he has held since December 1982 — and as the founder and conductor of the school’s children’s choir “Varavīksne” (“Rainbow”). He has also conducted the youth chamber choir “Daugaviņa” and the National mixed choir “Rīga”, and has appeared as a chief conductor (virsdiriģents) at Latvian Song Festivals.
----Early life and education

Beinerts studied music for about twenty years: first at the Emīls Dārziņš Special Music School (Riga), and then at the Jāzeps Vītols Latvian State Conservatory, where he earned a bachelor’s degree in conducting; after the conservatory was renamed the Latvian Academy of Music (Jāzeps Vītols Latvian Academy of Music), he also completed a master’s degree in music.

His conducting teachers included Krišs Deķis, Jānis Dūmiņš, Gido Kokars, Eriks Eriksons and Mariss Jansons. As a boy, he sang in the Riga boys’ choir circles led by Krišs Deķis, together with his older brother Zigurds Beinerts (later an engineer-mechanic). In his youth he also took part in amateur youth choirs.[[:lv:Jānis_Dūmiņš|[15]]]

In 1985, at the young conductors’ competition dedicated to the centenary of Emīls Dārziņš, Beinerts was awarded first place. [https://www.rsu.lv/aktualitates/dziesmu-svetku-virsdirigentam-un-rsu-goda-doktoram-janim-duminam-100 [1]]

Career

Riga 3rd Music School

In December 1982, Beinerts was appointed director of the Riga 3rd Music School — at the time the youngest school director in Latvia; by 2020 he was described as the longest-serving music school director in the country. In his 2020 essay in Latvijas Avīze he wrote critically about the state of Latvian music education: falling enrolment, the replacement of graded assessment with descriptive feedback, and what he saw as a growing bureaucratic burden on schools. The essay is titled “Par kļūdām izglītībā nākas maksāt dārgu cenu” (“For mistakes in education one pays a high price”). [https://www.la.lv/darga-cena [2]]

Choirs

* “Varavīksne” (“Rainbow”), Riga 3rd Music School children’s choir. When Beinerts became the school’s director in 1982 he opened the school’s choir class; the choir grew from 8 singers in its first year to a collective of up to 40 singers aged 8–18. In 1995 the choir won 1st place and Grand Prix at the competition of Latvian music school choirs organised by Latvian Radio. Its repertoire ranges from Bach, Mozart, Pergolesi, Cherubini, Mendelssohn, Schubert, Fauré, Grieg and Rachmaninoff to Latvian choral music. The choir has premiered large-scale works by composer Ingmars Zemzaris (Magnificat, Stabat Mater, Ofertorium de venerabili, Missa Brevis, Nisi Dominus, an Advent oratorio, and the cycle Ar māti pie baznīcas), recorded a Christmas-album CD with tenor Žoržs Siksna, appeared in Latvian National Opera productions (Turandot, Tosca, Uguns un Nakts, Noah’s Ark), and took part in the Latvian premiere of Mauricio Kagel’s Sankt-Bach-Passion with the Latvian National Symphony Orchestra and the choir “Latvija” on 1 April 2000. It has toured Denmark, Germany, England and Wales, Sweden, Finland and Estonia, and its recordings have been broadcast on Latvian, Danish and Swedish radio and on Latvian, Welsh and German television. [https://www.r3ms.lv/gallery/skolas-kolektivi/koris-varaviksne/ [3]]
* “Daugaviņa.” A youth chamber choir led by Beinerts; under him it won first place in the “choir war” (kora kari) at the 1985 Latvian Song Festival. The choir performed in the landmark 1988 Riga staging of the rock opera “Lāčplēsis” (director Valdis Lūriņš, conductor Zigmars Liepiņš). [https://enciklopedija.lv/skirklis/111395 [4]][https://labsalv.blogspot.com/2009/07/rokopera-lacplesis.html [5]] In 2013 he led the group of mixed choirs (Daugaviņa, Dzīne, Gaismaspils, Motus, Muklājs, Mūza, Saules Mājas, Senrīga, Skaņupe, Vecrīga, Vidus, Vox Animae) in the Riga amateur choir network. [https://avesol.riga.lv/lv/rigas-kori/rigas-koru-grupas-2013-gada/ [6]]
* Mixed choir “Rīga.” Beinerts is listed among the conductors of the National mixed choir “Rīga”, which was awarded National Choir status in 1968 and repeatedly won first places at the Song Festival choir competitions. [https://www.rsu.lv/en/mixed-choir-riga [7]]
* Riga Dom School / Riga Cathedral choirs. After a transition period under Aldis Andersons, Beinerts — “director of the Riga 3rd Music School and conductor of the choir Daugaviņa” — for a time took over the duties of chief conductor at the Riga Dom (Cathedral) school’s choral tradition. [https://doms.lv/lapas/42 [8]]

Song Festivals

Beinerts has served as a Song Festival chief conductor (virsdiriģents); in a 2023 interview on amateur choirs in Riga he is named among the conductors “almost all of whom have been chief conductors of past Song Festivals”. [https://www.la.lv/mernieku-laiki-rigas-amatier-maksla [9]] Recordings of his choirs and orchestral-choir programmes are held in the Latvian Song Festival digital archive of the National Library of Latvia. [https://dom.lndb.lv/data/obj/880450.html [10]]

Media

He has repeatedly appeared on Latvijas Radio 3 “Klasika”: in the programme Mākslinieka darbistaba (“The Artist’s Workshop”, 2012), where his 60th birthday and the anniversary of his choir were celebrated, and in the 2018 programme Diriģentu Krišu Deķi atceroties (“Remembering the Conductor Krišs Deķis”), where he and conductor Matīss Tučs discussed the memory of his teacher Krišs Deķis; Beinerts and his brother Zigurds were also among the initiators of the Deķis centenary memorial concerts. [https://klasika.lsm.lv/lv/raksts/makslinieka-darbistaba/dirigjents-un-pedagogs-karlis-beinerts.a1672/ [11]][https://timenote.info/lv/Kriss-Dekis [12]]

Views

Beinerts is a strong advocate of disciplined, tradition-based music education. He has argued that musical education develops concentration, planning and “emotional intelligence”, that “talent must be cultivated through work and discipline”, and that assessment in music should remain concrete rather than purely descriptive. In 1989 he said: “The choir and the conductor are instruments. The choir in the conductor’s hands, the conductor — in God’s hands.” [https://www.la.lv/darga-cena [2]][https://www.barikadopedija.lv/raksti/K%C4%81rlis_Beinerts [14]]

Personal life

His wife is the artist Vija Beinerte. [https://www.apollo.lv/5306030/tuvak-zvaigznem-un-muzikai [13]] His elder brother Zigurds Beinerts is an engineer-mechanic. [https://timenote.info/lv/Kriss-Dekis [12]]

data.title: Yazid ibn Muawiya's tomb
data.text:
The destruction of the tomb of Yazid ibn Muawiya refers to the reported loss and destruction of the burial site of the second Umayyad caliph Yazid I (c. 647 – 683).

== Background ==
Yazid I ruled as caliph from 680 to 683 CE. He died in November 683 CE in the town of Hawwarin, between Damascus and Palmyra, during the expedition to suppress the revolt of Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr. [ref: The Arab Kingdom and its Fall, University of Calcutta]

== Burial ==
Early Islamic historians including al-Tabari report that Yazid was buried in Hawwarin. [ref: The History of al-Tabari, Volume 20: The Collapse of Sufyanid Authority, SUNY Press] Later traditions place a commemorative grave in the Bab al-Saghir cemetery in Damascus.

== Tomb location ==
Two locations are traditionally associated with Yazid I:
* Hawwarin: The contemporary historical burial place.
* Bab al-Saghir, Damascus: A later traditional grave within the historic cemetery, where several Umayyad figures are buried. The exact identification is disputed.

== Reports of destruction and loss ==
Medieval sources do not describe a formal monumental tomb surviving from the Umayyad period. Over the centuries, the grave in Damascus became unmarked and was reported by travelers and local historians as lost, ruined, or destroyed due to neglect, urban expansion of the cemetery, and periodic conflicts in Syria. [ref: Le Califat de Yazid Ier, Imprimerie Catholique]

There is no archaeological evidence of a surviving structure. Modern surveys of Bab al-Saghir list the site as unidentified or no longer extant. [ref: Bab al-Saghir Cemetery - Islamic Heritage Sites]

== Historical debate ==
Historians note that early Umayyad graves were typically simple and unmarked, following early Islamic burial customs. The absence of a marked tomb is therefore consistent with contemporary practice, rather than a single documented act of intentional destruction. [ref: The First Dynasty of Islam: The Umayyad Caliphate AD 661-750, Routledge]

data.title: Multiple Listing Organ Transplantation
data.text:
Multiple listing is the practice by which a candidate for organ transplantation registers on the waiting list at more than one transplant program. In the United States it is permitted under the policies of the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN), which first allowed it in 1987. Supporters describe it as a way for patients in areas with long waits to reach programs with shorter ones; critics argue that it mainly benefits patients who can afford to travel and to undergo more than one evaluation.

== Policy ==
OPTN Policy 3.4.F allows a candidate to be registered at more than one transplant program. Under Policy 3.2, programs must inform patients of this option and of whether the program itself accepts candidates who are registered elsewhere. Each program decides for itself whether to accept such candidates. Guidance for patients published by the United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS), which has operated the OPTN under federal contract, also addresses transferring accumulated waiting time from one program to another.

== History ==
The OPTN board adopted a resolution on August 10, 1987, allowing patients to be added to the waiting lists of more than one transplant program. The practice was prohibited from January to March 1988 and survived repeal attempts in 1988, 1994 and 2001; the board last considered modifying the policy in 2003. Media coverage of the 2009 liver transplant of Apple co-founder Steve Jobs in Tennessee brought wider public attention to the practice.

In January 2023 the OPTN Ethics Committee released a white paper for public comment that recommended removing multiple listing as an option except for candidates who are difficult to match. Feedback was mixed, and professional societies including the American Society of Transplant Surgeons and the American Society of Transplantation raised concerns. The committee removed its recommendations before presenting the paper to the board, and on June 26, 2023, the OPTN board declined to approve it.

== Use ==
Registry analyses summarized in a 2025 article in Frontiers in Transplantation found that 3.3% of liver transplant candidates listed from 1995 to 2000, and 2.3% of those listed from 2005 to 2011, were multiply listed. An OPTN snapshot found 1.5% of liver candidates multiply listed on December 31, 2021.

The Ethics Committee's 2023 analysis found that multiply listed liver candidates were more likely than singly listed candidates to have private insurance (68.8% versus 50.8%) and less likely to be covered by Medicaid (5.7% versus 20.1%). It concluded that the policy, although formally open to every patient, does not give patients a fair and equal opportunity to use it. The same analysis found that multiply listed liver recipients had a longer median waiting time than singly listed recipients, and stated that the data were insufficient to show that the practice increases the number of transplants performed.

== Debate ==
Supporters have presented multiple listing as a response to geographic disparities in access. A 2014 perspective in The New England Journal of Medicine described geography as destiny for transplant candidates. A modeling study published in Management Science in 2017, conducted under the earlier kidney allocation system based on donation service areas, found that multiple listing could substantially improve geographic equity and that the inequity would disappear if enough patients could multiply list; its authors proposed an affordable private-jet service, OrganJet, to make this practical. A 2020 registry study reported that listing in more than one region increased transplant rates for liver candidates with MELD scores below 15.

Critics have focused on equity and system effects. An editorial in the same issue of Transplantation as the 2020 study argued that multiple listing helps a few patients but does not address the organ shortage. The authors of the 2025 Frontiers article stated that the United States is the only country known to allow multiple listing and argued that its use should be confined to defined situations in which it is justified. They also noted that multiple listing can substantially improve access for candidates with low MELD scores whose local program does not use extended-criteria livers, such as older or donation-after-circulatory-death organs.

data.title: Lilo & Stitch 2 (2028 film)
data.text:
Lilo & Stitch 2 is an upcoming American science fiction comedy film written and directed by Chris Sanders. Produced by Walt Disney Pictures, the film will be a sequel to the 2025 live-action adaptation of Lilo & Stitch and the sixth overall feature film in the Lilo & Stitch franchise.

The film will be released on May 26, 2028, by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures via their Walt Disney Pictures banner.

==Cast==

* Chris Sanders as the voice of Stitch, a blue koala-like illegal alien genetic experiment known as Experiment 626, who is adopted by Lilo as a "dog".
* Maia Kealoha as Lilo Pelekai, an orphaned Hawaiian girl who adopted Stitch. After the events of the previous live-action film, she is being raised by her next-door neighbors David Kawena (previously played by Kaipo Dudoit) and his grandmother Tūtū while her older sister Nani attends college.
* Sydney Elizabeth Agudong as Nani Pelekai, Lilo's older sister, who is attending the University of California, San Diego after the events of the previous film.
* Amy Hill as Tūtū, David's grandmother and, after the events of the previous film, Lilo's foster mother.

Additionally, Angel (Experiment 624) is set to appear in the film. The D23 teaser reveals she now has glowing antennae tips similar to the esca of an anglerfish, an ability she did not have in traditional animation.

==Production==
On June 26, 2025, Disney announced that it had greenlit a live-action sequel to the 2025 live-action adaptation Lilo & Stitch. [ref: 'Lilo & Stitch 2' Dancing Way Into Development, Deadline Hollywood] The announcement was accompanied with a video of a Stitch (voiced by Chris Sanders) animatronic driving a pink ride-on toy car (one of the animatronics used to promote the 2025 Lilo & Stitch film) through the Walt Disney Studios in Burbank, California, noticing a "2" on a sign. He then writes the words "Lilo and Stitch 2" by making skid marks and shouts "Stitch want!" as he drives off. The announcement on June 26 was done to coincide with "626 Day" or "Stitch Day", celebrating Stitch, whose codename is Experiment 626. No creatives were attached to the film at the time. [ref: 'Lilo & Stitch 2' Live-Action Movie Set at Disney, [[Variety (magazine)] In July that same year, it was announced that Chris Sanders, who co-wrote and co-directed the original 2002 animated film in addition to providing the voice for Stitch, would write the screenplay for the film. [ref: 'Lilo & Stitch 2' Brings Back Co-Creator Chris Sanders to Write Script (Exclusive), The Hollywood Reporter] In June 2026, it was announced that Sanders would also be directing the film. [ref: 'Lilo & Stitch 2' to be Directed by Co-Creator Chris Sanders (Exclusive), The Hollywood Reporter]

At the Disney Entertainment Showcase during D23: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event 2026, it was revealed that Angel (Experiment 624), a popular character introduced in Lilo & Stitch: The Series, will be appearing in the film. [ref: Disney Reveals 'Lilo & Stitch 2' Will Feature Stitch's Pink Counterpart Angel, The Hollywood Reporter] [ref: 'Lilo & Stitch 2' Drops First Look of Pink Alien Angel in Live-Action Sequel, [[Variety (magazine)]

In September 2026, it was reported that the film would supposedly be introducing a new lead character named Nellie, who is "[d]escribed as a 9-year-old fast-talking girl who moves to Hawaii from a big city and quickly befriends Lilo and Stitch." Fan responses interpreted this character as a renamed and reimagined Victoria, a girl from the second season of Lilo & Stitch: The Series who becomes Lilo's best human friend. [ref: Live-Action Lilo & Stitch 2 Adding New Character In Major Change from the Animated Original, ComicBook.com]

=== Filming ===
In December 2025, it was revealed that filming was expected for Summer 2026. [ref: The DisInsider Mailbag – Rapunzel, Lilo & Stitch 2, 2026 Disney Offerings, Daily Disney News] Filming began on October 14 at the Bishop Museum in Honululu; a blessing ceremony was held at the museum to honor the first day of filming, with Governor of Hawaii Josh Green in attendance. [ref: Lilo & Stitch 2 kicks off production in Hawaiʻi with blessing at Bishop Museum, KHON-TV] [ref: Yesterday was a busy day, with events that reflected my vision for Hawaiʻi’s future: strengthening our economy, supporting our kūpuna and keiki and building stronger communities. I was proud to welcome Disney back for Lilo & Stitch 2, supporting our local film industry and creating more opportunities for Hawaiʻi’s talent.[...]] As with the previous film, most of the film's production crew consists of local talent. Filming took place at Hilton Hawaiian Village on October 19. [ref: Lilo & Stitch 2 Films In Waikiki, And Stitch Brought Angel Along, The Disney Scoop]

==Release==
Lilo & Stitch 2 is scheduled to be released in the United States on May 26, 2028. [ref: 'Lilo & Stitch 2' & 'Incredibles 3' Set 2028 Release Dates, Deadline Hollywood]

data.title: Kelvin wave
data.text:
----

A Kelvin wave is a transverse wave of the narrow core of a vortex. As the wave propagates along the vortex, the core is displaced sideways in a direction that rotates along its length, producing a helical deformation. Kelvin waves were first described theoretically by Lord Kelvin in 1880 [ref: XXIV. Vibrations of a columnar vortex, The London, Edinburgh, and Dublin Philosophical Magazine and Journal of Science]. Although Kelvin's original argument assumes a homogeneous, incompressible, and inviscid fluid, Kelvin waves emerge in many different types of fluids, including water, superfluid helium, and cold atomic Bose–Einstein condensates. Kelvin waves are important because they influence the stability of vortices and the redistribution of energy in rotating flows. In classical fluids, Kelvin-wave dynamics is relevant to macroscopic vortices such as tornadoes and aircraft wake vortices.

== Kelvin waves in classical fluids ==
Kelvin waves were first observed experimentally in a classical fluid (water) in 1980 [ref: Theory and observations of waves on hollow-core vortices, Journal of Fluid Mechanics], followed in 1982 by a clearer manifestation of the helical deformation of a vortex core [ref: Vortex solitary waves in a rotating, turbulent flow, Nature]. Their basic properties, including the dispersion relation, were experimentally characterized much later, in 2026 [ref: Kelvin wave propagation along vortex cores, Nature Physics].

== Kelvin waves in superfluid helium-4 ==
Kelvin waves in superfluid helium-4 were first observed in 2014 [ref: Direct observation of Kelvin waves excited by quantized vortex reconnection, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences], followed by their controlled excitation, clear three-dimensional visualization, and quantitative characterization, including measurements of their dispersion relation and phase velocity in 2025 [ref: Direct excitation of Kelvin waves on quantized vortices, Nature Physics].

== Kevin waves in ultracold atomic Bose-Einstein condensates ==
Kelvin waves have been detected in ultracold atomic Bose–Einstein condensates [ref: Quadrupole Oscillation of a Single-Vortex Bose-Einstein Condensate: Evidence for Kelvin Modes, Physical Review Letters] [ref: Experimental Observation of the Tilting Mode of an Array of Vortices in a Dilute Bose-Einstein Condensate, Physical Review Letters], although propagating helical Kelvin waves have not yet been directly imaged.

data.title: Brandi Morin
data.text:
Brandi Morin is an acclaimed French, Cree, and Iroquois journalist. She has spent 15 years reporting on Indigenous peoples as a freelance journalist for publications including National Geographic, Al Jazeera, The Guardian, and the New York Times. She is also the author of "Our Voice of Fire: A Memoir of a Warrior Rising."

== Career ==

=== Reporting ===
In 2013 Morin worked as a freelance writer at Indian Country Today. In April 2015 she began her work as a journalist across various television stations and media companies, including Aboriginal Peoples Television Network, CBC/Radio-Canada, and Canada's National Observer. [ref: Brandi Morin, CBC] In 2020 she also started working as a freelance writer for organizations like ELLE Canada, Al Jazeera, National Geographic, The Guardian, BBC, Rolling Stone, and the New York Times.

=== Memoir ===
While doing her freelance work, Morin wrote her debut memoir, "Our Voice of Fire: A Memoir of a Warrior Rising," which was published August 2, 2022 by House of Anansi Press, in which she uses her experience as a survivor of the Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women and Girls crisis to tell the stories of those who did not survive. The book became a national bestseller shortly after its release and received both the Memoir of the Year and the Wilfrid Eggleston prizes at the 2023 Alberta Literary Awards. [ref: Alberta Literary Awards Finalists and Winners – Writers' Guild of Alberta, writersguild.ca]

data.title: Patrice Mousseau
data.text:
Patrice Mousseau is a Canadian Anishinaabe entrepreneur and a former broadcast journalist. She is the founder and CEO of [https://satya.ca/?srsltid=AYCX9vJ4H1oT0izks46EzFEK5z2N-Ss5rImC1Q8tOHWfK4KJDa_WHnWH Satya Organics], a BC-based company producing plant-based skincare products. [ref: Patrice Mousseau is building an Indigenous business ecosystem, one entrepreneur at a time, The Globe and Mail]

== Personal life ==
Mousseau was raised in Sioux Lookout, Ontario. She is a member of the Fort William First Nation. Patrice Mousseau is a single mother. Her daughter, Esme, was born in 2011. [ref: How Patrice Mousseau Went from Model to Journalist to Organic-Skincare Entrepreneur, Canadian Business]

== Career ==

In the mid-1990s, Patrice Mousseau worked as a model before entering Canadian news broadcasting, including roles at the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation (CBC), Aboriginal Voices Radio Network, and the Aboriginal Peoples Television Network.

In 2012, she formulated a steroid-free skincare balm sourced from natural ingredients to treat her daughter's eczema. [ref: Ojibway entrepreneur creates product for daughter, now it's in 400 stores] She began selling it at local farmer's markets. She then founded Satya Organics in 2015. [ref: SATYA ORGANICS INC. - WEST VANCOUVER BC CANADA] The company became the first indigenous-owned brand carried by Shoppers Drug Mart. By 2025, its products were sold in more than 1,000 Shoppers Drug Marts, as well as being available with other Canadian, American, and Hong Kong retailers.

== Other activities ==
Mousseau serves as Entrepreneur in Residence at [https://www.flinthub.ca/ Flint Hub], an Indigenous-focused business incubator at the University of Waterloo's United College. [ref: Flint Hub, Empowering Indigenous Entrepreneurs]

data.title: Karl Vandenhole
data.text:
----

= Karl Vandenhole =
Karl Vandenhole ist ein Film- und Fernsehschaffender, der vor allem an deutschen Dokumentarfilm- und Fernsehproduktionen beteiligt ist. Seine Tätigkeiten umfassen unter anderem Produktion, Recherche, Drehbucharbeit, Regie, Kamera und Ton. Er arbeitete hauptsächlich an Dokumentationen für die ZDF-Reihe Terra-X und weitere deutschsprachige Fernsehsender sowie an späteren Fernseh- und Streamingproduktionen.

== Beruflicher Werdegang ==
Karl Vandenholes berufliche Tätigkeiten sind in Film- und Fernsehbranchenverzeichnissen sowie in Sendungs- und Programmangaben dokumentiert. Zu seinen frühen Arbeiten zählen Produktionen der Dokumentationsreihe Tauchfahrt in die Vergangenheit, die zwischen 2000 und 2011 im ZDF ausgestrahlt wurde. Als festangestellter Redakteur bei Spiegel TV war er maßgeblich für den Aufbau der Abteilung Co-und Auftragsproduktionen verantwortlich sowie für die erste große Cross-mediale Publikation von Der Spiegel, Spiegel TV und ZDF mit der Terra-X Filmveröffentlichung "Kolumbus' letzte Reise", zusammen mit Titelstory im Spiegel und einer Buchveröffentlichung "Die letzte Reise" von den Autoren Klaus Brinkbäumer und Clemens Höges.

Für die Folge Operation Caesar – Jagd auf U-864 wird Vandenhole als Drehbuchautor genannt. In Programmangaben von PHOENIX wird er zudem neben Marc Brasse und Christopher Rowley als einer der Filmschaffenden aufgeführt. Crew United führt ihn bei der Produktion Tauchfahrt in die Vergangenheit – Operation Caesar – Jagd auf U-864 als Co-Regisseur sowie für Recherche, Autorentätigkeit und Produktion.

In den folgenden Jahren arbeitete Vandenhole an verschiedenen Dokumentationen, darunter Produktionen aus dem Umfeld der ZDF-Reihe Terra X. Zu seinen verzeichneten Tätigkeiten gehören die Produktion beziehungsweise Recherchekoordination für Terra X – Schatzjagd in der Tiefe (2009) und Terra X – Kampf um die Ostsee (2010). Weitere Produktionsarbeiten sind für Die Geisterflotte vom Yukon (2010) und Terra X – Sibirien und die Deutschen (2012) dokumentiert.

Neben seiner Tätigkeit im Dokumentarfilm war Vandenhole an Fernsehfilmen, Reportagen und Dokuserien beteiligt. Zu den verzeichneten Arbeiten gehören Geheimnisse Asiens – Die schönsten Nationalparks, Länder Menschen Abenteuer Spezial – Thailand & Island sowie die Dokuserie Diese Ochsenknechts. Bei verschiedenen Produktionen übernahm er Kamera- und Tonaufgaben.

Seit 2012 ist Karl Vandenhole in Thailand und Südostasien als freischaffender Multimedia Journalist tätig für Zeitungsreportagen, Magazinbeiträge und Dokumentarfilme. Er produziert aber weiterhin Dokumentarfilme in Zusammenarbeit mit deutschen Produktionsfirmen

== Filmografie (Auswahl) ==
Die folgende Auswahl beruht auf verfügbaren Filmografie- und Programmdaten. Die genannten Tätigkeiten unterscheiden sich je nach Produktion. [ref: Karl Vandenhole, producer, Phuket, Crew United]

data.title: Julie Tobiason
data.text:
----

Julie Tobiason is an American ballet dancer, choreographer, and dance educator. She performed with Chicago City Ballet, as a principal dancer with Pacific Northwest Ballet (PNB), and co-founded Seattle Dance Project with Timothy Lynch in 2008. [ref: Performance at ACT Theatre tonight launches Seattle Dance Project, Seattle Post-Intelligencer]

== Early life and training ==
Tobiason began studying dance at age four in Lyndhurst, New Jersey. She subsequently trained with The Studio Workshop, Garden State Ballet, and the School of American Ballet (SAB) in New York City. [ref: Fifteen years of 'Nutcracker' keeps dancer on her toes, Seattle Post-Intelligencer]

== Career ==
=== Chicago City Ballet ===
Tobiason joined Chicago City Ballet in January 1983, under artistic directors Maria Tallchief and Paul Mejia. [ref: Chicago City Ballet: Cinderella] She performed in Mejia's Favorita, which was reviewed by the Chicago Tribune in September 1985. [ref: 2 Short Works Highlight City Ballet's Lively Show, Chicago Tribune]

=== Pacific Northwest Ballet ===
Tobiason joined Pacific Northwest Ballet in 1986 and was promoted to principal dancer in 1992. She performed with the company until 2002. [ref: PNB can't make 'Seven Sins' work, Seattle Post-Intelligencer] She also appeared in the film Nutcracker: The Motion Picture (1986), directed by Carroll Ballard. [ref: Nutcracker: The Motion Picture (1986), AFI Catalog]

Her repertory included traditional major roles such as Swanhilda in Coppélia, Dream Clara in Kent Stowell's production of The Nutcracker, Hermia in George Balanchine’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream (1999 BBC film). [ref: A Midsummer Night's Dream, HDVDARTS]. She danced in works by Paul Taylor, William Forsythe, Nacho Duato, and Val Caniparoli. In a 1992 review of PNB at the Kennedy Center, The Washington Post discussed her performance in George Balanchine's Rubies alongside Brent Davi. [ref: Dance, The Washington Post]

=== Seattle Dance Project ===
Tobiason and former PNB dancer Timothy Lynch launched Seattle Dance Project in 2008, a company of experienced dancers performing contemporary choreography. The debut performance at ACT Theatre included works by Donald Byrd, Molissa Fenley, Pat Catterson, and Olivier Wevers. [ref: Project One: A PNB Spin-Off Debuts, Seattle Weekly]

In a review of the company's debut, The Seattle Times critic Moira Macdonald singled out Tobiason's performance in Donald Byrd's Tatum Dance #2. [ref: Seattle Dance Project finds new moves, The Seattle Times]

Seattle Dance Project presented a full-evening dance production titled Project Orpheus. [ref: Review: SDP's 'Project Orpheus' benefits from roomier setting, The Seattle Times]. In 2009, she danced in Edwaard Liang's Flight of Angels with Oleg Gorboulev, receiving coverage in the Seattle Post-Intelligencer and Seattle Met. [ref: Seattle Dance Project's 'Project Two' is a real crowd pleaser, Seattle Post-Intelligencer]

== Choreography ==
Tobiason has choreographed many student performances as a faculty member at PNB and for Seattle International Dance Festival. Her 2018 work kairos received a favorable review from Marcie Sillman, who highlighted its combination of classical ballet and contemporary dance. [ref: Dance Diary – SIDF June 14, 2018, Seattle International Dance Festival]

== Selected repertoire ==
* Agon
* A Midsummer Night's Dream (Hermia)
* Apollo
* Ballet Imperial (principal)
* Cinderella (Cinderella)
* Coppélia (Swanhilda)
* Favorita (principal)
* In the Middle, Somewhat Elevated
* Romeo and Juliet (Juliet)
* Rubies (principal)
* The Nutcracker (Dream Clara)

data.title: Siddhartha Lahiri
data.text:
----

Siddhartha Lahiri, known as Sid Lahiri, is a cricket coach and former club cricketer from Kolkata, India. He has worked as a performance coach with Rajasthan Royals in the Indian Premier League, as a batting coach with Paarl Royals in SA20 and Barbados Royals in the Caribbean Premier League, and as an assistant coach with Birmingham Phoenix in The Hundred. [ref: Gautam Bhattacharyya. [https://www.nationalheraldindia.com/cricket/sid-lahiri-a-journey-from-kolkata-maidan-to-global-coaching-role Sid Lahiri: A journey from Kolkata maidan to Royals' global coaching role]. National Herald. 17 March 2026.] [ref: [https://www.edgbaston.com/media-article/birmingham-phoenix-announce-coaching-staff-for-2026 Birmingham Phoenix announce coaching staff for 2026]. Edgbaston. 10 March 2026.]

In February 2025, Royals Sports Group appointed him head of international player development, with responsibilities for its academies and coaching across its overseas franchises. [ref: [https://www.rajasthanroyals.com/latest-news/siddhartha-lahiri-royals-head-of-international-player-development-appoint Royals Sports Group appoints Siddhartha Lahiri as Head of International Player Development]. Rajasthan Royals. 4 February 2025.]

== Early life and playing career ==
Lahiri trained under Gopal Bose in Kolkata and played as an opening batter in local cricket. His clubs included Dakshin Kalikata Sansad, Milan Samity, Anandabazar Sports Club and Customs, which competed in Cricket Association of Bengal tournaments. [ref: Shayan Acharya. [https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/siddhartha-lahiri-interview-rajasthan-royals-ipl-royal-sports-group-paarl-sat20-star-cricket-academy/article69167362.ece From maidans of Kolkata to leading the ‘Royals way’ of coaching - the Siddhartha Lahiri story]. Sportstar. 1 February 2025.] [ref: [http://starcricketacademy.co.uk/about-us/ About – The Rajasthan Royals Academy]. Rajasthan Royals Academy Surrey. Undated. Accessed 21 October 2026.]

He moved to England in 2003 to gain coaching qualifications. He completed England and Wales Cricket Board Level 1 and Level 2 courses through Middlesex and later qualified at Level 3. [ref: Sandip Sarkar. [https://bengali.abplive.com/sports/ipl/abp-exclusive-know-about-siddhartha-lahiri-of-rajasthan-royals-plays-a-major-role-in-mustafizur-rahman-s-comeback-814163 ABP Exclusive: Know about Siddhartha Lahiri of Rajasthan Royals plays a major role in Mustafizur Rahman's comeback]. ABP Ananda. 11 May 2021. In Bengali.]

== Coaching career ==
In Surrey, Lahiri played for Stoke d’Abernon Cricket Club. At Parkside School in Cobham, he initially worked as a groundsman and later began coaching young cricketers.

Lahiri established a cricket academy at Parkside School in 2005. It later became known as Star Cricket Academy, moved to Reed’s School in September 2018 and partnered with Rajasthan Royals in February 2019.

The responsibilities announced with his appointment in 2025 covered academies in Jaipur, Surrey, Pune and New Jersey. They included developing player pathways and coordinating coaching across the Royals academy network.

In March 2026, Birmingham Phoenix named Lahiri one of three assistant coaches for its men’s team under head coach Shane Bond. The other assistants were James Foster and Graeme Welch.

National Herald reported that month that Lahiri had worked on developing Royals Hub, an online course for cricket coaches.

== Player development ==
Lahiri’s pupils included Ollie Pope, Ryan Patel and Amir Virdi. [ref: Barney Ronay. [https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2019/oct/01/rajasthan-royals-academy-ipl-cricket-future Rajasthan Royals’ English academy: a glimpse of cricket’s future?]. The Guardian. 1 October 2019.]

Sportstar reported that he had also worked with Phil Salt and Shoaib Bashir. Lahiri told the magazine that he worked with Riyan Parag when Parag joined Rajasthan Royals in 2019.

In 2025, Lahiri described clear communication and trust as important to coaching. He said his academy work included training plans, regular calls and masterclasses for coaches.

He also coached West Indies cricketer Justin Greaves. [ref: Sayak Banerjee. [https://www.telegraphindia.com/sports/cricket/justin-greaves-epic-test-turnaround-draws-praise-as-mindset-shift-fuels-west-indies-comeback-prnt/cid/2136705 Mentorship and mindset shift spark Justin Greaves’ rise after match-saving double hundred]. The Telegraph. 8 December 2025.]

Alec Stewart, a former England captain, praised Lahiri’s coaching and relationships with players in 2020. [ref: Sayak Banerjee. [https://www.telegraphindia.com/amp/sports/behala-boy-who-laid-pitch-for-pope/cid/1746111 Behala boy who laid pitch for Pope]. The Telegraph. 17 February 2020.]

== Personal life ==
In a 2021 interview with ABP Ananda, Lahiri said his wife had encouraged him to travel to England for coaching courses in 2003.

Wally Miles is an American vocalist, entertainer, wrestling personality, and advocate for Parkinson's Disease from Maryville, Tennessee. data.title: Akkarapadathu Chirayil Family
data.text:
The place Akkarapadam is part of Vaikom taluk in Vadakkemuri Village of Kottayam district. It comes under the Udayanapuram Grama Panchayath. For administrative purpose Vaikom Taluk is divided into sixteen villages, and Vadakkemuri is one among them. Vaikom is situated in the north west of Kottayam district in the state of Kerala. Vaikom gained its fame on a national level during Vaikom Satyagraha, a civil right movement aimed at securing freedom of movement for lower caste people (untouchables) through the public roads leading to Vaikom temple.

Vaikom is believed to be a part of kingdom called Venmalanadu in the past. When Venmalanadu was split into Vadakkumkoor and Thekkumkoor Vaikom became part of Vadakkumkoor dynasty. Later when the Maharaja of Travancore, Anizham Thirunal Marthanda Varma annexed Vadakkumkoor to his kingdom in 1742, Vaikom became part of Travancore.

=== History ===

It is very difficult to trace out the root or the origin of the family in the absence of authentic depositions. As per available information passed on by ancestors, it is believed that sometime during 16th century AD, a small Christian family with their only son, from the eastern part of the present Ernakulam District called Kothamangalam came and settled down at South Paravoor (Thekkan Paravoor). Who were they, what were they and the reason which forced them to leave Kothamangalam were not exactly known. Thus they reached South Paravoor, a distant Christian belt under the Travancore dynasty, where the church desired an able leadership for their laity who was mostly ordinary people. The family who came from Kothamangalam, having an impeccable charisma were welcomed at South Paravoor with a warm heart and they got the same prominence as at Kothamangalam. This period was very crucial for the Christian Community in Kerala (Malankara or Malabar Christians). Following the oath of the “Coonen Kuriz” of 1653, the single church of pre-Portuguese days had lost its unity in a threefold way. Two groups of the Malabar Christians continued functioning in allegiance with Rome (one in alliance with the Portuguese and the other directly under Rome, guided by missionaries of the Society for the propagation of the faith). A third body sought to keep its independent existence without any devotion to Rome. They soon realized that the validity of its ministerial succession could be questioned and needed rectification with the assistance of a Church from outside. With this aim in mind the leaders approached several Eastern Churches with an appeal for assistance. The Antiochene Syrian Church responded by sending metropolitan Mar Gregorios of Jerusalem in 1665, without insisting any pre condition for cooperation. The Indian Church received him with open arms. Those who accepted the East Syrian theological and liturgical tradition of Mar Gregorios were later known as Jacobites and those who continued with West Syrian theological and liturgical tradition and stayed faithful to the Synod of Diamper are known as Syro-Malabar Catholic Church. Thus, 72 out of 116 churches were claimed by Catholics, 32 by others and 12 being shared. This vertical split of the Christian community had its effect in South Paravoor too and the family which came from Kothamangalam stood strongly with the fraction associated with Antiochene Syrian Church. Consequently a new church was built on the eastern side of the main road opposite to the old church (present Catholic Church) for which the family had a pivotal role. This is the old Jacobite Church at South Paravoor. The family from Kothamangalam became stronger in the church and the community. This is evident from the fact that the family held 2 of the 7 keys of the church strong room (mempootu) of the church. [ref: From archives and information passed down from generation to generation]

It was during this period the young man from this family, believed to be one Mathulla, who had three brothers and a sister moved around in search of some fertile land suitable for agriculture, because Christians in general were engaged in agriculture and or trade during those days. At that time South Paravoor was not an ideal place for agriculture. He reached a remote village in the western banks of river Ithipuzha (branch of Muvattupuzha River) where there was vast area of wet and marshy land ideal for cultivation. He acquired lot of property; say almost half of the village along with plenty of servants and slaves. There he had built a palatial house, nearly four centuries ago, at an elevated portion of the land (“chira”) on the riverbank which stood as a testimony to the wealth of the family. Since the house was built on a “chira” the family got the name “Chirayil”. Brothers of Mathulla continued to stay at South Paravoor itself in separate properties namely Parakkattu, Koluthakottil and Kanjirakkattu after giving their ancestral house to their only sister. It is believed that “Chirayil Tharavad" about was the first permanent house in the village made of stone about 400 years ago.This fact aligns perfectly with the socio economic evolution of the Vaikom region. During that era the construction of a permanent tiled or stone structure rather than a thatched house was a major status symbol. It required special permission from the local rulers or the Kingdom of Travancore and indicated immense land-owning prominence. In Vaikom the Akkarapadathu Chirayil Family emerged as prominent land owners and agriculturists.Because of their strong socio-economic standing they maintained close interactions with the local Royal principalities,such as Vadakankoor kingdom and other historic families in the region.

Mathulla who was a great visionary, changed the face of the land by converting the entire marshy area into fertile paddy field. This paddy field (“padam”), being located on the other side of the river (“akkare”), opposite to the mainland, the name “Akkare-padam” was originated. This name “Akkarapadam” later stood as synonym for Chirayil House, probably because it was the only house worth mentioning in that area. Thus the family was popularly known as Akkarapadathu and not Chirayil. It is still being referred so, especially by their relatives and people belonging to old generation.

Kinsfolk of Mathulla continued to live at South Paravoor and the present members of the Chirayil family still maintain close association and relationship with families like Parakkattu, Thottankara, Nedumpallil, Kochu Palathinkal, Koluthakkottil, Kanjirakkattu etc at South Paravoor confirming their common origin. There was even a property (Sy No 303/6 as per Settlement Deed No.2870 of 1085 ME, Book 1, Vol.15, Pages 247 to 257 of Vaikom Registry) in South Paravoor retained in the name of Akkarapadathu family which was later donated to the Church as an offering of the family to the church by the family head and is presently under the possession of the Church. Members of the Akkarapadathu Chirayil family, irrespective of their present place of residence are still attached to their South Paravoor Church (St Johns Jacobite Syrian Church) by retaining their membership.

Ackarappadam was a village inhabited mostly by poor Ezhavas. This Mathulla appeared to have had plenty of money and was clever. This house got an “Ara” (strong room) a “Nila Ara”or “Nilavara” (a basement store) and an Attic, probably the type wealthy homes had during those days. This house also got huge wooden beams with lotuses carved on them. It is believed that some of them were hollow to serve as secret lockers against dacoits and thieves. Unfortunately, most of these structures are no more there as the later generation modified the house for their convenience and style of living. Mathulla was very influential, respected by the villagers - you may call him Village Pradhan or an Alderman. He had great control over his slaves and the villagers who were either his servants or dependents of some sort. He could impose any punishment on them and was considered as a king without a crown.

Varkey Ippora (1880-1944) a politician, a municipal councilor and two time Member of the erstwhile Travancore Praja Sabha (Ref: Centenary Souvenir - 100 years of Legislative Bodies in Kerala) was also an important leader of the Church. Sri Moolam Praja Sabha (popular assembly) of Travancore formed in 1904 was the very first elected legislative body of its kind in any Indian princely state. To be elected or nominated to the Praja Sabha from a prominent region like Vaikom, an individual had to be highly respected community leader, often a major tax payer or a distinguished citizen. Bishops and priests of his period maintained close association with him and sought advices in important matters. All disputes in the village and nearby villages were brought to him and he settled them judiciously. He was an expert in civil law and people from far away places too came to him for his help and advice. Considering this, he was appointed by the then Government as Judge of the Panchayath Court with office at Vaikom Town. All cases of civil nature not exceeding a certain amount were heard and decided by such courts. The judges had specific dress code too and the ceremonial coat being used by him as a Judge is still kept at the Chirayil House as a treasure, in respect of his memory.

=== Social Status of the Family ===
Following the Oath of the Coonen Kuriz of 1653 at Mattancherry, the Christian church of pre-Portuguese days had lost its unity in a threefold way. Two groups of the church continued functioning in loyalty with Rome, one in alliance with the Portuguese and the other directly under Rome guided by missionaries of the Society for the Propagation of the Faith. A third body sought to keep to its independent existence. This last community soon realized that the validity of its ministerial succession could be in question and so needed rectification with the assistance of a Church abroad. With this aim in mind the leaders approached several eastern Churches with an appeal for assistance. The Antiochene Syrian Church responded positively by sending metropolitan Mar Gregorios of Jerusalem in 1665, without insisting on any precondition for cooperation. The Indian Church received him with open arms. Following was a period of renaissance for this fraction later known as Jacobite Syrian Christians. They faced so many challenges one after another and it took long time to get them organized as a separate Church establishing their identity. Initially, for the total administration of the churches in Kerala the Syrian Patriarch of Antiochia constituted a high level committee comprising leaders and experts from the church in which Paily of the Akkarapadathu Chirayil family was a member [ref: Mulunthuruthy PADIYOLA, www.syriacchristianity.info] (Ref: Page 223 of Suriyani Sabha Charithravum-Vishwasa Sathyangalum-written by Malankara Malpan Dr Kaniyamparambil Kurian Corepiscopa). The ability of Malankara Christians were recognized from the beginning, not only by the grant of land by local Rajas but also by grant of concessions and privileges recorded on copper plates. The rulers of Venad (Travancore) granted Syrian Christians 72 rights and privileges which were usually offered only to high dignitaries. These rights included exemption from import duty, sale tax and slave tax among others. The Akkarapadath Chirayil family too enjoyed some of such privileges. Like Brahmins they had the right to sit before the Kings and also to ride on horse like the Royals. Thus Pailo of the family was riding on his horse during his time and it was a rare scene in a remote place like Akkarapadam. Social sins like untouchability entered their practices though the Diamper Synod abolished it. Like other communities the Syrian Christians also have been involved in regional politics on a community basis. In 1888 Travancore became the first princely State of India to establish a Legislative Council, which was reformed as the Sree Moolam Popular Assembly. Mathulla,,grant son of Pailo and the elder son of Varkey, was a very simple, down to earth person who helped the villagers with food, medicines and all other assistance whenever they needed. During annual flood associated with monsoon every year, he offered them accommodation in his “uralpura” with necessary food and medicine. They in turn respected and loved him. He lived for passing a legacy of character and faith to his children and grandchildren, and not for passing money and materials accumulated in his life. One can definitely say that he carved his name in the hearts of others and not on tombstones; his legacy is etched into the minds of others and the stories they share about him. Ippora, the younger son of Varkey was prudent, worldly wise, a leader, politician, municipal councilor, panchayath judge and a member of the Sri Moolam Assembly consecutively for two times. The Nair community in Vaikom was very prominent during those days and they stood strongly in favor of him and their support was crucial during assembly elections. Considering this, he voluntarily decided not to contest in assembly Election consecutively for the third term and offered his support to a prominent member from the Nair community. This relation continued till his death and they were always there to help him voluntarily whenever needed. He was an expert in civil law and people from far away places too came to him for his help and advice. He was respected and feared more than loved. His life was really amazing as it is said “some people inspire themselves, but amazing people inspire others”. His life was a message for others and he made it inspiring. He taught us that the things you do for yourself are gone when you are gone, but the things you do for others remain as your legacy.

Mathulla and Ippora, the heads of the of the family, were sensible, intelligent and hard working. It is said that some people come in our life as blessings, but some others come as lessons. But they were a combination of both. At their period Christian families used to maintain joint family system. The father was supreme in the family. The children considered it a sacred duty to help their aged parents who always lived in the family of one of the sons, usually the youngest. In other words the ‘Makkathayam’ system was in force among the Christians. The Christian society in general is strongly patriarchal and inheritance is patrilineal. The father is the head of the family. Property is traditionally divided among the sons. The most notable is the age-old tradition that the youngest son is given the family house (tharavadu veedu) where he stays with the parents which is in contrast to the practice in most other communities in Kerala and is strikingly similar to ancient Hebraic/Jewish property inheritance pattern. All sons inherited the father’s property, but the daughters were provided only with a dowry during their marriage. Women were discriminated and given low status and not given freedom of mobility. Christian women remained at home according to the local customs and engaged themselves in household affairs. Children - both boys and girls were given education but girls were married much earlier. The boys continued their studies even after their marriage. The modesty in dress and behavior of women was regarded as contributing much to the sanctity and solidity of family life. They seldom went out of their house except to church. For the first time the family property was divided in 1085 ME between the brothers Mathulla and Ippora. At that time they had many small and large properties in Akkarapadam itself in addition to their prime property where their ancestral home was built. The following is an incomplete list of the family properties, mentioned for general information about the assets of the Chirayil family: Vallavanody, Valavanthara, Methanthara, Paruthikkattuthara, Paruthikattuchira, Pandaraody, Pottachira, AnutharaThekkeChira, KizhakkeChira, VadakkeOdy, Kizhakkepatthil, Kizhakkepatthil-Thekku, Naduvilekkuttu, Attumali, Attumali vadakku, Attumali mekku, Kulakkuzhithara, Kochuthara, Kochuthara mekku, Thozhuthinkal, Parathara, EdakkaduOdy, EdakkaduChira, Moonnodiyil, Padinjarekkudy, KizhakkeOdy, EeraNilam, EeraNikarthu, etc. Paddy and coconut were the main cultivation. The quantity of coconut during each plucking (at an interval of 45 days) was so much, that there was even a separate building near the river side exclusively for keeping it till its disposal. It was a tall, single room structure, with grill made of timber batten in all the four sides and with a door in the ground level and a window like opening at the top just below the roof. All the coconuts are thrown in through the top opening till the structure is almost full. It comes out automatically like flow of water when the bottom door is opened. Transportation of coconut from different location was by country boat. The brothers were so much attached to each other, more so the elder one who adored his younger brother Ippora and would do nothing without consulting him or without his consent. Most of their ventures and projects they did jointly. They added more property at Akkarapadam, Chemmanakary, Vaikom, Murinjapuzha and even had an estate of 50 Acres at Pooyamkutty near Kothamangalam. Their wives too were so much attached to each other till their death. They had a big oil mill and were direct suppliers of coconut oil to the exporters. They had their offices at Ackarappadam and at Cochin. When this mill was closed down, they started a rice mill, which gave employment to many. They were the first ones to start a printing press (The Rising Star Press) and a hardware shop at Vaikom. They had their own row boat with 12 or 14 oars and oarsmen, had a small motor boat and car at different times, as testimony to their aristocracy. Till recently the covered shed called “vallappura”, where the row boat and the motor boat were dry docked for annual maintenance, was there in riverside. That too was a sign of aristocracy during those days. They even went in for an Elephant, which probably died before it was brought home, incurring heavy loss. They also organized the Ackarapadam boat race, which was an annual feature for a long time. To show their splendor, Mathulla’s elder son, Pappachan went on elephant for his marriage. There was big display of fireworks and boat race during the marriages of Varghese, the younger son of Mathulla and Abraham, son of Ippora. When Ippora decided to divide his property among his children in Kollavarsham 1114, he had 38 separate properties, partly inherited and the rest earned in Akkarapadam and outside, having a total extend of about 40 acres (Ref: settlement Deed No.2486 of 1114 of Vaikom sub registry). These properties were high yielding coconut plantation and paddy fields. The society changed, people became educated, wealthy and independent even at places like Akkarapadam. They became more self-reliant and self-respecting and resented the influence of the Chirayil Family, as in many other places in the state. The Vaikom Satyagraha (1924-25) and it’s after effects had direct influence in these changes.

=== Conclusion ===
Each member of the Chirayil family is fully aware of their legacy and accepts and understands that their ancestors built this great family by fostering personal dignity in each and every individual, accepting the virtues of everyone and offering services generously and with deep solidarity. Remembering them with devotion, reverence and gratitude all members of the family are trying their best to be the living witness of the immemorial covenant established by God with Adam, and renewed in Noah and Abraham, Moses and David, and finally, fully and definitely through the incarnation, death and resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ.

data.title: Proda
data.text:
Proda (stylized PRODA) is an American beverage brand that produces carbonated, sugar-free soft drinks containing whey protein. The company was founded in 2026 by actor and entrepreneur Matthew Postlethwaite and beverage entrepreneur Jeff Church, a co-founder of Suja Juice, who serve as co-chief executive officers. [ref: Justin Timberlake, Jessica Biel enter protein soda market, Food Dive] [ref: Justin Timberlake and Jessica Biel Joined a Protein Soda Startup. Now Comes the Hard Part, [[Inc. (magazine)] In October 2026, Justin Timberlake, Jessica Biel and Barry's executive chairman Joey Gonzalez joined the company as co-founders. [ref: Justin Timberlake and Jessica Biel Jump in on Protein Craze in First Joint Business Venture, The Hollywood Reporter]

== History ==
Proda was founded by Postlethwaite and Church and launched its drinks in 2026. [ref: Justin Timberlake co-founds PRODA brand taking on Coca-Cola and Pepsi, TheStreet] Postlethwaite has said the idea originated with his grandmother, who struggled to consume enough protein through shakes and supplements but enjoyed soda, and that the product took more than two years to develop. Church has said that advances in clarified whey protein made it possible to produce a protein drink that was clear and soluble enough to carbonate. [ref: Justin Timberlake And Jessica Biel Join Protein Soda Startup As Co-Founders, Forbes] The company is based in Los Angeles. [ref: PRODA, Better Soda, Inc.]

On October 13, 2026, the company announced that Timberlake, Biel and Gonzalez had joined as co-founders, in what The Hollywood Reporter described as Timberlake and Biel's first joint business venture. Both had prior involvement in beverages: Timberlake had invested in Bai Brands in 2016 and served as its chief flavor officer, and Biel had co-founded the children's drink company Kinderfarms in 2021. According to the announcement, the couple would work on the brand's creative strategy, flavor innovation, product development and cultural partnerships, and said that "the opportunity to work with Matthew and Jeff in shaping the brand, its products and where it goes next" had drawn them to the company. Gonzalez, the executive chairman and former chief executive of Barry's, said Timberlake had been working with Postlethwaite on the brand's visual identity in what he described as a creative-director capacity before the announcement. Gonzalez himself was described as bringing operational scale and fitness-industry experience to the company. Inc. described the challenge facing the company as converting celebrity attention into repeat purchases in a category that larger competitors were entering.

== Products ==
Proda's drinks are sold in 12-ounce cans, each containing 10 grams of whey protein and no sugar. As of October 2026 the range comprised seven flavors: Lemon Lime, Classic Orange, Cherry Lime, Strawberry Lemonade, Golden Apple, Shirley Temple and Root Beer. The drinks were sold through Sprouts Farmers Market, Amazon and the company's website, with the company stating that it aimed to expand into grocery and club channels.
