data.title: Tia Adan
data.text:
----

Tia Adan is an Australian youth advocate, community leader and social entrepreneur based in Queensland. She is the founder and president of Rise as One Association Inc., a youth-led organisation focused on leadership development, education, community engagement and the empowerment of young people.

Adan has participated in youth representation, public policy discussions, child protection advocacy and initiatives supporting women and girls. Her affiliations include the Bravehearts Youth Advisory Council, the Queensland Curriculum and Assessment Authority's myQCE Student Reference Group, the Morayfield Youth Advisory Council and the YMCA Queensland Youth Parliament.

In 2025, Adan was featured in The Courier-Mail as one of 22 young people contributing to the future of the City of Moreton Bay. In 2026, she received second place in the Zonta District 22 Young Women in Leadership Award, according to information provided by Adan.

== Early life and education ==
Adan was born in Pakistan and spent part of her childhood in Thailand before migrating to Australia in 2019.

She grew up in a culturally traditional household where, according to Adan, her parents held conservative views about gender roles and women's participation in public life. She has described an upbringing in which women were discouraged from expressing independent opinions and participating in political discussions.

Adan has stated her parents opposed her involvement in politics, viewing political leadership and public decision-making as traditionally male responsibilities. She developed different views about gender equality and believed women should have equal opportunities to participate in political, social and community leadership.

These differences contributed to tensions within her family as she became increasingly involved in youth advocacy and political activities.

In May 2026, at the age of 17, Adan moved out of her family home while completing her final year of secondary education. She began living independently, managing her accommodation, finances and household responsibilities while attending school full-time and working three jobs.

Despite these circumstances, Adan continued participating in community organisations, youth representation and the development of Rise as One Association Inc.

=== Secondary education and student leadership ===
Adan attended Caboolture State High School in Queensland, where she became involved in student leadership, community service and youth advocacy.

During Year 11 in 2025, she served as Vice President of the school's Student Council and held the position of Senior School Ambassador. Her responsibilities included representing students, supporting school initiatives and participating in activities promoting student wellbeing and leadership.

In Year 12 in 2026, Adan stepped away from her formal school leadership positions to focus on her personal circumstances, education and responsibilities associated with independent living.

She continued her involvement in youth advocacy and community initiatives outside school, including the development of Rise as One and participation in statewide advisory groups.

== Youth advocacy and public affairs ==

=== YMCA Queensland Youth Parliament ===
In 2025, Adan represented the electorate of Morayfield in the YMCA Queensland Youth Parliament, a youth civic education program in which participants debate policy and develop proposed legislation.

During her term, she participated in the Health and Emergency Services and Family, Seniors and Disability Services Committee.

She contributed to the development of the Hospital and Health Boards (Ryan's Rule) Amendment Youth Bill 2025, which addressed patient rights, communication and accountability within Queensland's healthcare system.

Her involvement in the program formed part of her broader interest in government, public policy, human rights and political representation.

=== Morayfield Youth Advisory Council ===
Adan has participated in the Morayfield Youth Advisory Council, an initiative associated with Queensland Member of Parliament Mark Ryan.

Through the council, she has contributed to community consultation, youth leadership activities and initiatives encouraging young people to participate in local decision-making.

The council was also involved in the organisation of the 2026 Youth Leadership Forum in collaboration with Rise as One.

=== Bravehearts Youth Advisory Council ===
Adan serves as a youth advisor with Bravehearts, an Australian child protection organisation focused on the prevention of child sexual abuse and support for affected children and young people.

Through the Bravehearts Youth Advisory Council, she contributes youth perspectives to discussions concerning child safety, prevention strategies, education and the protection of children's rights.

Her involvement reflects her interest in improving systems intended to protect vulnerable young people and increasing youth participation in decisions affecting their wellbeing.

=== myQCE Student Reference Group ===
In 2026, Adan was selected as one of 15 Queensland students to join the myQCE Student Reference Group, administered by the Queensland Curriculum and Assessment Authority (QCAA).

The group provides student perspectives on senior secondary education, assessment and resources supporting the Queensland Certificate of Education.

Adan represented Caboolture State High School as part of the statewide group.

== Rise as One Association Inc. ==
Adan is the founder and president of Rise as One Association Inc., an incorporated youth-led organisation established to support young people through leadership development, educational opportunities, advocacy and community engagement.

The organisation seeks to encourage youth participation in community affairs, develop leadership skills and improve access to opportunities for young people from different backgrounds.

As founder and president, Adan has overseen the organisation's establishment, governance, sponsorship arrangements, community partnerships and event coordination.

=== Youth Leadership Forum ===
On 28 August 2026, Rise as One, in collaboration with the Morayfield Youth Advisory Council, organised a Youth Leadership Forum at Caboolture State High School.

The event brought together secondary school students from schools across the Moreton Bay region, alongside educators, youth advocates, community representatives and guest speakers.

Participating schools included Caboolture State High School, Morayfield State High School, Tullawong State High School, St Columban's College, Grace Lutheran College and Lee Street State Special School.

The forum included presentations, panel discussions and student-led activities examining leadership, civic participation and challenges affecting young Australians.

Speakers included Janice Rodrigues, a United Nations Youth Representative for Australia, and Queensland Member of Parliament Mark Ryan. Other participants included youth advocates and representatives from community organisations.

The program encouraged students to discuss community concerns, consider possible responses and develop ideas for youth-led initiatives.

The event received financial and organisational support from local sponsors and community partners.

== Community service and fundraising ==
Adan has been involved in fundraising and community service activities supporting charitable organisations and public health initiatives.

Her involvement has included activities associated with the Australian Red Cross, Humanity First, breast cancer awareness initiatives and Australia's Biggest Morning Tea.

In June 2025, The Courier-Mail reported her involvement in fundraising activities associated with more than $10,000 raised during the year.

Adan has also been involved with Zonta-related community activities supporting the education, leadership and advancement of women and girls.

== Awards and recognition ==

=== Zonta District 22 Young Women in Leadership Award ===
In 2026, Adan received second place in the Zonta District 22 Young Women in Leadership Award, according to her account.

The award program recognises young women aged 16 to 19 who demonstrate leadership, volunteerism and commitment to public service and civic causes.

The recognition was associated with her involvement in youth advocacy, leadership and community service.

=== Moreton Bay Young Guns ===
In June 2025, Adan was featured in The Courier-Mail article Revealed: 22 under 25 shaping City of Moreton Bay's future.

The publication highlighted young people contributing to the Moreton Bay region through leadership, business, volunteering, education and community involvement.

Adan was recognised for her youth empowerment activities, fundraising initiatives and plans to establish Rise as One.

=== Personal interests and aspirations ===
Adan has expressed an interest in human rights, political philosophy, government, education, women's rights, child protection and public policy.

Her interest in gender equality and political representation has been influenced, according to her own account, by her experiences growing up in a traditional household and her involvement in youth advocacy.

She has indicated an intention to pursue tertiary studies related to politics, philosophy and human rights, with longer-term aspirations involving public service, diplomacy and international affairs.

== Selected roles and affiliations ==

* Founder and President, Rise as One Association Inc.
* Youth Advisor, Bravehearts Youth Advisory Council.
* Student Representative, myQCE Student Reference Group (2026).
* Member, Morayfield Youth Advisory Council (2026)
* Youth Member for Morayfield, YMCA Queensland Youth Parliament (2025).
* Vice President, Caboolture State High School Student Council (2025).
* Senior School Ambassador, Caboolture State High School (2024 - 2025).

data.title: Air Transportable Mobile Medical Facility
data.text:
The Air Transportable Mobile Medical Facility (ATMMF) was a prototype deployable medical shelter system developed by Hawker de Havilland (HdH) in Melbourne, Australia, between 1988 and 1990. The concept originated with Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) Wing Commander Dave Robson, who sought improved field medical infrastructure after observing limitations in existing shelters.

== History ==

In 1988, the RAAF commissioned Hawker de Havilland to design and construct two demonstration units. The project was led by Chief Designer Andrzej Grocholski, who oversaw structural integrity, airworthiness compliance, and final design approval. Designer Greg Thomas contributed to design solutions and specification compliance. Production was completed in 1990 under Production Manager Denis Baker.

Despite successful field trials and positive feedback from personnel involved, the RAAF did not proceed with further procurement. The current status of the two prototype units is unknown.

== Design ==

The ATMMF was intended as an innovative alternative to contemporary deployable shelters. Each unit was towable on- and off-road, expandable, and interconnectable. The shelters were designed to be air-transportable by both helicopter and fixed-wing aircraft, and required minimal site preparation. Deployment could be performed by two personnel.

Air locks sealed the interior from the external environment, providing a sterile, quiet, air-conditioned space suitable for medical treatment or nursing wards. Air-lock areas could be converted into washbasin, shower, or toilet modules. Depending on configuration, shelters could serve as mobile hospitals, health centres, communication centres, workshops, or emergency accommodation.

Each unit incorporated electrical wiring, plumbing, and interchangeable internal stores modules. A built-in battery system provided power for deployment and 24-hour emergency lighting, while external field generators supplied power for air conditioning, lighting, and battery charging.

== Expandable configuration ==
A minimum expanded configuration consisted of two interconnected shelters, joined by integral roof, floor, and wall panels to create an enclosed floor area of 26.2 m². Multiple units could be connected side-by-side or via concertina walk-through ends to form larger complexes. In closed configuration, a single shelter could support surgical operations.

== Construction ==
The primary structure used welded aluminium tubular framing. Walls, roof, and floor panels were of sandwich construction, providing thermal and acoustic insulation. Removable service modules were made of fibreglass. Hinged interconnecting panels allowed limited self-alignment to compensate for accidental misalignment during deployment.

== Specifications ==

{| class="wikitable"
! Feature !! Specification
|-
| Chassis || Aluminium
|-
| Deployment crew || 2 personnel
|-
| Expanded floor area || 26.2 m²
|-
| Power || Built-in battery system; external generator for air conditioning and lighting
|}

== Awards ==

Hawker de Havilland received a commendation from the Institution of Engineers Australia for "Excellence in Engineering Achievement" in recognition of the Air Transportable Mobile Medical Facility project.

data.title: Elimu Academy
data.text:
----

Elimu Academy[i] was set up in Liverpool L8 (latterly called Toxteth)[ii]  Toxteth England in 1999 and was co-founded and led by the city’s first Black Head Teacher Gloria Hyatt  MBE[iii]. It housed the UK’s first Independent School[iv] that was black led, a charity[v] and limited company[vi] for black secondary school pupils in Merseyside and white pupils residing in Liverpool 8 who were permanently excluded or at risk of exclusion from school. [viii]

It's educational approach included an African-centred curriculum and predominantly support for pupils from Black and mixed-race backgrounds [viii] Within Elimu Academy there was an after-school, for pupils attending mainstream secondary schools and an adult learner’s service [viiii]

=== History ===

=== Elimu Wa Nane ===
The origins of Elimu Academy can be traced to Elimu Wa Nane, a library and educational resource established in 1979 at Princes Park Methodist Church and Centre in Liverpool 8. The library held literature relating to Africa and the Caribbean and provided a resource for the local community that was set up by Wally Brown  CBE, DL.pg.1.[x]

The library’s activities included educational resources and opportunities for reading, writing and cultural learning. Its development reflected concerns about the availability and representation of Black history, literature and culture within mainstream educational provision.

=== Elimu Study School: After School Service ===
In the 1990s, the project transformed into an after school called [https://register-of-charities.charitycommission.gov.uk/en/charity-search/-/charity-details/1039434/full-print Elimu Study School] under the leadership of Gloria Hyatt, a teacher with QTS. The service expanded beyond its original library function to provide educational support for young people in Liverpool 8. Historical accounts place the Study School at Princes Park Methodist Church and Centre before its relocation to Streatlam Tower in 1994 and later in 1996 to Dove Street during which time it became Elimu Academy, where it operated till 2009.[xi] [xii]

The provision included after-school classes in subjects such as English and mathematics, and most parts of the national curriculum and Black Studies as an additional curriculum alongside teaching relating to African and Caribbean history and culture. Its educational approach incorporated an African-centred perspective into learning materials and classroom activities. The programme was intended to support pupils’ educational attainment and provide additional educational resources for children attending mainstream schools. [xiii]

=== Black Learners Project ===
The organisation subsequently expanded its work to include daytime educational provision for young people who experienced difficulties in mainstream education. The Black Learners Project formed part of this development and focused on pupils who had been excluded or were considered at risk of exclusion.[xv]

As Elimu’s success grew, schools in Liverpool and Liverpool Education Authority collaborated, as noted in the December 2000, Ofsted Inspection report, “That provision, the Elimu centre, is now to be brought into a more formal relationship with the LEA”. (para148, pg. 33). [xvi]

The educational model combined anti racist teaching with support intended to address barriers to learning. Hyatt argued that schools needed to address differences in educational outcomes and the treatment of Black pupils. In contemporary reporting, she discussed the effects of racial stereotyping, the representation of Black people in the curriculum and the need for teachers to understand the experiences of their pupils.[xvii]

=== Elimu Academy ===
Elimu Academy was established as an independent school in Dove Street, Toxteth, where it continued with its afterschool and BLP project. The Department for Education records its opening date as 1 March 2000 and lists Gloria Hyatt as headteacher. The school was registered as an independent school for pupils aged 13 to 15. [xviii]

The Academy provided education for pupils who had been excluded from mainstream schools or were at risk of exclusion. Its approach included an African-centred curriculum alongside the national curriculum. Contemporary reporting described its work with Black and mixed-race pupils and its use of teaching strategies intended to address educational underachievement and exclusion. [xix]

=== Adult Learning ===
In 1999, NCFE accredited adult learning classes were created to create a stepping stone into teaching this included overseas qualified teacher training, classroom assistant training (now called Teaching Assistants) and mentor training. [xx] [xxi]

Ray Costello said of Hyatt: “In developing the Elimu Wa Nane Project into a successful independent school for disaffected black pupils, Gloria Hyatt pioneered the case for future black teachers to rise to management positions in Liverpool” (Costello, 2007, pg.85).[xxii]

To enhance their teaching capability learners attended "[https://firstcutmedia.com/heritage-digital-archive/education-of-the-black-child/ The Education of the Black] [https://firstcutmedia.com/heritage-digital-archive/education-of-the-black-child/ Child Conference]", between 1993 to 1997, organized by black teachers, Paul Obinna and Lance Lewis, and delivered by eminent black scholars such as Dr. Maulana Karenga and [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rPW67pam5bo&source_ve_path=OTY3MTQ&embeds_referring_euri=https%3A%2F%2Ffirstcutmedia.com%2F Dr. Jocelyn Maxime].

=== Governance ===
Elimu was governed by a management committee till 1999 then by a board of directors. Notable management committee members, directors and members of the leadership team have been:

Wally Brown

Dorothy Kuya

Cclr Gideon Ben-Tovim

Michelle Charters

[https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/histories-languages-and-cultures/news/stories/title,1522142,en.php Dr Ray Costello]

[https://www.thefreelibrary.com/Faces+from+the+ends+of+the+earth%3B+A+new+book+is+being+published+to...-a0127193200 Shirley Mashiane- Talbot]

[https://www.waterstones.com/author/lenford-anthony-white/1702621 Lenford Anthony White]

[https://schoolsinengland.co.uk/north-west/trafford/trafford-alternative-education-provision-131134 Linda Thompson]

[https://topline.com/people/dr-osama-abdul-rahim-oj-rahim-151655741 Dr Osama Rahim]

[https://www.gc.cuny.edu/people/mark-christian Professor Mark Christian]

=== Closure ===
In 2003, because of major policy changes regarding school exclusions [xxiii] made by Prime Minister Tony Blair’s government, Local Education Authorities and schools faced stricter requirements to provide alternative full-time education for excluded pupils. Liverpool LEA decided to reintegrate all the children on the BLP into their Pupil Referral Unit or schools. As stated in their 2003, Ofsted Inspection Report, “The role of the amalgamated service is now more focused on reintegration into mainstream schools.” (Para 126, p. 24). [xxiv]  As a consequence the independent school closed.[xxv]

In 2004 Elimu Academy transferred the remaining services and staff into an organization called [https://www.unitedkingdominbusiness.co.uk/Company/276882/Charity-Novas-Overtures-Ltd/0-L13HE-Liverpool-0870-9019711 Novas Overtures] with a plan to be part of a new building project that would encompass our vision for education called the [https://www.misterwhat.co.uk/company/2741540-novas-contemporary-urban-centre-liverpool Contemporary Urban Centre]. This involved a 14-million-pound fundraising drive in a merger which included Elimu changing its name to Novas Academy. [xxvi]

All of the teachers had departed as had Gloria Hyatt by 2005. Novas Overtures along with Novas Academy closed in 2009, a result of controversy around how the funds were being spent by Novas Overtures.[xxvii]

data.title: Mahatma Gandhi Quotes
data.text:
Mahatma Gandhi (1869–1948) was an Indian lawyer, anti-colonial nationalist, and political ethicist who played a leading role in India's independence movement. His philosophy emphasized nonviolence (ahimsa), truth (satya), self-discipline, and peaceful resistance. His speeches, writings, and public statements have influenced political and social movements around the world.

=== Mahatma Gandhi Quotes ===

==== Truth and Nonviolence ====
Gandhi's writings frequently explored the relationship between truth and nonviolence. He regarded nonviolent resistance as a means of confronting injustice without resorting to physical violence.

==== Peace and Social Justice ====
Gandhi advocated peaceful political action, religious tolerance, and social reform. His views influenced later civil rights and independence movements.

==== Self-Discipline and Personal Responsibility ====
His writings also addressed personal conduct, simplicity, ethical living, and the responsibility of individuals to contribute to social change.

data.title: Hans-Christian Mangelsdorf
data.text:
Hans-Christian Mangelsdorf (*1982) is an a Economist, AI Tech expert and a German career diplomat currently posted at the German Federal Foreign Office (FFO) in Berlin. He serves as the Chairperson of the OPCW's Advisory Board for Administration and Finance (ABAF) in The Hague [ref: Advisory Body on Administrative and Financial Matters, OPCW].

He served as the first Chief Data Scientist of the German FFO from 2023 to 2026 and initiated the AI Charter [ref: Für einen modernen Auswärtigen Dienst - das Auswärtige Amt gibt sich eine KI-Charta, Auswärtiges Amt] and the Data Strategy of the Ministry and managed their implementation as part of his responsability as Head of Division of the AI and Data Lab of the Ministry. Leading up to this role, he had previously managed the organizations PREVIEW Programm [ref: Vorträge des Auswärtigen Amts beim "Innovationssymposium Künstliche Intelligenz " am 29.09.20 in Berlin, fragdenstaat.de] for strategic foresight and crises early warning as part of the larger [https://beirat-zivile-krisenpraevention.org/ crises preventation agenda of the German Government].

Together with experts from industry and the federal government he designed, engineered and launched the PLAIN programm and the PLAIN plattform [ref: ] [ref: PLAIN: Daten- und KI-Plattform der Bundesverwaltung, www.bundesdruckerei.de] in late 2022 with market availability achieved in 2025. [https://www.plain.diplo.de PLAIN] is the sovereign AI and Data Cloud provided by the [https://www.linkedin.com/showcase/auslands-it Auslands-IT] to various federal government entities in Germany. A thought leader on public sector AI, Data and Tech he frequently lectures on these subjects [ref: HPE CEO: We’re all in on digital sovereignty, www.sdxcentral.com] [ref: Public Pulse - der Podcast rund um die digitale Zukunft der Verwaltung, player.podigee-cdn.net] and advances the use of sovereign and open source [ref: ] technology. He initiated the creation of the [https://datainnovationlab.de Data Innovation Lab] in 2023 as a major networking entity bridging public administration, academia and industry.

===== Previous roles & responsabilites =====
With a strong focus Management and Finance, Hans-Christian Mangelsdorf was responsable for managing Germany's UN 5th Committee portfolio and its multi billion UN core budget. He published on UN Management Reform [ref: Die Managementreform der Vereinten Nationen 2017 und 2018, zeitschrift-vereinte-nationen.de] and on the larger management and financial set-up of the United Nations [ref: ]. Previously in 2016/2017 he held positions as head of the FFO's peace mediation team and managed stabilization programs in Africa, Asia and Europe. He held various positions in German Embassies in the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan [ref: 50 Years of German-Jordanian Economc Relations — Key Aspects of an ongoing Success Story, Über die Vielfalt kultureller Brücken. Festschrift zum 50jährigen Bestehen der Deutsch-Jordanischen Gesellschaft e.V.], Egypt and South Africa since joining the FFO in 2006.

Hans-Christian Mangelsdorf holds degrees in Finance (Maîtrise), Business Administration (Diplom-Betriebswirt) and Economics (Diplom-Betriebswirt) from the University of Leipzig and Université Lyon 2 with a special focus on capital markets, financial management, statistics, taxation and controlling. He had previously served as member of the [https://www.ipsasb.org/consultative-advisory-group Consultative Advisory Group] [ref: Minutes of Meeting CAG Meeting Toronto] of the [https://www.ipsasb.org/about-ipsasb IPSASB].

data.title: Dellove Ondongo
data.text:
Dellove Ondongo (full name Adrard Guez-Dellove Ondongo Aucibi) is a Congolese technology entrepreneur and cybersecurity specialist. He is the founder and chief executive officer of BEGU Corporation OÜ, a technology company registered in Tallinn, Estonia. [ref: Newsroom, BEGU Corporation] [ref: Begu Corporation OÜ (17290858), e-Business Register] He is also involved in diplomatic networking, connecting individuals and organisations across international and professional networks.

== Early life and education ==
Ondongo was born in the Republic of the Congo (Congo-Brazzaville) and moved to India as a student about ten years ago; he has lived mostly in Bangalore since.

He completed a Master of Computer Applications (MCA) in cybersecurity and is a PhD scholar in Computer Science and Information Technology (CSIT) at Jain (Deemed-to-be University) in Bangalore. According to BEGU Corporation, he is the first Congolese student to pursue a PhD at Jain University, and one of only a few Congolese PhD scholars in Bangalore.

== Career ==
Ondongo began his career in Bangalore in technical information technology recruitment and client relationship management, working at Awnics from 2019 to 2020 and at Lancesoft in 2023.

From August 2023 to February 2025 he was a program manager at the American company Engage2Excel, working remotely with a team based in Montreal on projects for the Government of Canada, mainly for National Defence and Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada.

== Entrepreneurship ==
Ondongo is an e-resident of Estonia and the founder of BEGU Corporation OÜ, based in Tallinn; the commercial register lists him as its sole shareholder and management board member. Under his leadership the company is building a group of businesses in commerce, technology and services, starting with the online marketplace BEGU Deals.

== Research ==
Ondongo's research focuses on cybersecurity, mobile application security and natural language processing. He is a co-author of a paper on natural language processing in recommender systems. [ref: Natural Language Processing (NLP) in Recommendation Systems, ResearchGate]

== Recognition ==
In 2023 Ondongo was named Outstanding International Student in Bangalore for 2022–2023 by the Federation of All International Students in Bangalore.

data.title: Hanish Gupta
data.text:
== Hanish Gupta ==

Hanish Gupta is an Indian entrepreneur and corporate executive. He is the founder, promoter, and managing director of Sunkind India Limited, an Indian renewable energy company active in solar energy project development, engineering, procurement, and construction (solar EPC), solar component manufacturing, and battery energy storage. [ref: Draft Red Herring Prospectus: Sunkind India Limited, Sunkind India Limited / National Stock Exchange of India]
== Early life and education ==
Gupta completed the fifth semester of a Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) course at Amity University, Uttar Pradesh in December 2008. [ref: Draft Red Herring Prospectus: Sunkind India Limited, Sunkind India Limited / National Stock Exchange of India]

== Career ==
Gupta has over 16 years of professional experience across industrial engineering, steel manufacturing, and renewable energy sectors. Prior to establishing Sunkind, he served on the boards of directors for several industrial and manufacturing firms, including J.D. Industries India Limited and J.D. Metalloys Limited. [ref: Director Profile: Hanish Gupta (DIN 02194659), ZaubaCorp]

In September 2019, Gupta co-founded Sunkind Energy (now Sunkind India Limited). He was appointed as a director on the company's board in April 2021 and was designated as managing director on August 12, 2024. [ref: Draft Red Herring Prospectus: Sunkind India Limited, Sunkind India Limited / National Stock Exchange of India] As managing director, he oversees corporate strategy, business planning, project execution, corporate governance, and the company's backward integration into solar mounting structure manufacturing (under the Strucmax brand) and photovoltaic module production. [ref: By 2030, We Aim to Contribute 10–12 GW Cumulatively: Hanish Gupta, Sunkind Energy, Energetica India]

== Industry commentary and public affairs ==
Gupta regularly publishes industry commentary and participates in media discussions regarding India's renewable energy policies, power transmission infrastructure, solar manufacturing, and grid-scale storage:

* Grid Infrastructure & Energy Storage: In September 2026, The Financial Express featured commentary from Gupta on India's power transmission infrastructure upgrades, grid integration of renewable energy, and the commercial viability of battery energy storage systems (BESS). In June 2026, he discussed financing capital-intensive renewable storage projects in an interview with BusinessWorld. [ref: "Solar And Storage Must Go Together", Says Hanish Gupta, Founder & MD, Sunkind India Ltd, BW Hotelier / BusinessWorld]
* Solar Supply Chain & Geopolitics: In July 2026, Gupta authored an analysis in PV Magazine India on global solar manufacturing geopolitics, addressing China's supply chain dominance and outlining strategies for India to build domestic wafer and cell manufacturing capabilities. [ref: The geopolitics of solar manufacturing and how India can build a China-alternative supply chain, pv magazine India]
* Domestic Manufacturing & Policy: In December 2025, Gupta contributed an opinion piece to ET EnergyWorld examining policy measures under the PLI scheme and India's push to localize clean energy manufacturing. [ref: Inside India's push to localize its solar future, ETEnergyworld (The Economic Times)]
* Business Leadership & Manufacturing Expansion: In July 2026, Gupta discussed Sunkind's vertical integration, energy security, and manufacturing expansion in an exclusive interview with APAC News Network. [ref: 'Domestic manufacturing strengthens energy security by reducing import dependence': Hanish Gupta, Founder & Managing Director, Sunkind India Limited, APAC News Network]

data.title: New Hampshire Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force
data.text:
----

The New Hampshire Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force (NH ICAC) is a law enforcement task force headquartered at and managed by the Portsmouth Police Department in New Hampshire. Established in 1998, it participates in the national Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force Program. Its activities include investigating technology-facilitated crimes against children, conducting forensic examinations, supporting criminal prosecutions, and providing community education.

In 2017, New Hampshire Public Radio reported that funding shortages were limiting the task force’s investigative capacity. The report examined a proposal to provide state funding to supplement federal support.

An investigation involving NH ICAC resulted in the federal prosecution of John Allen Wright of Milton, New Hampshire. On February 22, 2013, Wright was sentenced to 160 years in federal prison after pleading guilty to five counts of sexual exploitation of children and one count of possessing child pornography.

=== Logo history ===
The task force’s logo has changed over time. The current longstanding design featuring binary digits, the old man on the mountain and photographs of children was created by Detective Kenneth Tapscott during his service with the New Hampshire Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force. IThat design has been used for more than 15 years.

data.title: Serpent's Curse (roller coaster)
data.text:
Serpent's Curse is a steel roller coaster currently under construction at Paultons Park in Hampshire, England. Manufactured by Mack Rides, the ride is a custom-designed water coaster; the first of its kind in the UK. [ref: ] The attraction is expected to open in 2027 in the park's Viking-themed land: Valgard: Realm of the Vikings.

== History ==
The ride was announced to the public during Paultons Park's annual Super Fans day on 16 May 2026. [ref: LIVE: Super Fans Day 2026 & Big New Plans for 2027!]

The ride's lift hill was topped off on 13 July 2026, with the first drop being completed the following day. [ref: ] The ride's track, up to the splashdown element was completed on 17 July 2026.

== Characteristics ==

=== Ride experience ===
Upon exiting the station, riders take a right-hand turn before ascending the chain lift hill. The ride then executes a left-hand banked drop into a twisted airtime hill. Riders then experience a steep-banked turn over the lift hill before another airtime hill. The ride then rises up into a top-hat element before a small airtime hill into the ride's splashdown. The ride vehicle then floats, pushed by the water, back to the station.

=== Ride vehicles ===
The ride's 4 boats are arranged with riders sitting 2 across in 4 rows for a total of 8 riders per car. [ref: ]

data.title: Lena Bui
data.text:
= Lêna Bùi =
Lêna Bùi (born 1985) is a Vietnamese visual artist based in Saigon [ref: about, lêna bùi]. Her practice includes painting, drawing, video, installation, and performance. Her work examines relationships between people and the natural environment, including the effects of urban development and the role of spiritual beliefs in everyday life. [ref: ]

== Early life and education ==
Bùi was born in Đà Nẵng, Vietnam. She received a Bachelor of Arts in East Asian Studies from Wesleyan University in the United States.

== Work ==
Bùi’s work moves back and forth between various cultures and values, sometimes comparing and contrasting to better understand the socio-political make-up of the society.

During a 2023 residency at Delfina Foundation in London, Bùi developed Root People and the Circle Line. Presented that November as part of [https://www.delfinafoundation.com/whats-on/cyphering-vibrating-emanating/ Cyphering, Vibrating, Emanating], the performance combined video, spoken reflections, and diagrams to explore movement, belonging, and rootedness. [ref: Cyphering, Vibrating, Emanating, Delfina Foundation]

== Selected exhibitions ==
Bùi’s work has appeared in Foreign Bodies at Wellcome Collection in London in 2013 and Residual: Disrupted Choreographies at Carré d’Art in Nîmes, France, in 2014. She also participated in the 2022 Jeju Biennale, the 2024 Bangkok Art Biennale, and the 15th Shanghai Biennale in 2025.

== Residencies ==
Bùi was an artist in residence at Delfina Foundation in autumn 2023 [ref: Lêna Bùi, Delfina Foundation] and at NTU CCA in 2020. [ref: Lêna, archive.ntu.ccasingapore.org]

data.title: Ahlam Gharbaoui
data.text:
Ahlam Gharbaoui is a Dutch-Moroccan international business consultant, entrepreneur, author and English-language poet, with experience in international affairs, public diplomacy and strategic partnerships.

== Early life and education ==
Born in Brabant, the Netherlands, Gharbaoui built a career spanning commercial business, government, diplomatic affairs, media and international strategic partnerships. [ref: De zin van Ahlam Gharbaoui: 'Waar een wil is, is een weg', Trouw] She began her career as a government official at the Dutch Ministry of Justice. An Arabic-language women's magazine profile described her as the first Moroccan and Arab woman to work at a refugee reception centre in the Netherlands. [ref: سيدة الأعمال المغربية الهولندية أحلام الغرباوي, Estesmarat] [ref: Two-page feature on Ahlam Gharbaoui, Arabic-language women's magazine (print)] After working in the insurance division of Rabobank, she obtained a postgraduate diploma in legal interpreting and translation from the SIGV Institute for Legal Interpreters and Translators in Utrecht in 2002 and became a sworn court interpreter and translator. She also holds a Master's degree in Intercultural Communication from the University of California, Los Angeles (2012). [ref: Personal Portfolio 2024 (self-published)] Throughout her career, she has provided interpreting services for members of the Dutch Royal House, presidents and senior government officials from across the European Union and the MENA region. [ref: Dutch-Moroccan Businesswoman / Ahlam Gharbaoui: An Arab Woman with Inspiring Global Steps and Achievements, Estesmarat]

== Business career ==
At the age of 24, she founded Averto Tolken & Vertalers Adviezen, building a network of more than 800 interpreters and translators serving government institutions, commercial organizations and the media sector throughout the Netherlands. [ref: De banden versterken, De Groene Amsterdammer] [ref: AIM Congress is delighted to announce Ahlam Gharbaoui as our Master of the Ceremony for the SMEs Track at AIM Congress 2024!] She also worked as an editor and interviewer for NOVA, a Dutch current affairs television programme renowned for setting the political agenda in The Hague.

In 2009, Gharbaoui relocated to the United Arab Emirates to serve as a commercial and cultural adviser at the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in Abu Dhabi. [ref: Promotional reel for AIM Congress 2025 featuring Ahlam Gharbaoui] In this role, she represented the Netherlands across multiple policy portfolios and facilitated bilateral cooperation and international partnerships. Building on her experience in the UAE, she subsequently served as general manager for the Gulf region at Farouk Systems USA, an American multinational. Her international work includes facilitating partnerships across the MENA region, including, as she described in an interview with Estesmarat, a government-to-government memorandum of understanding between Morocco and the Netherlands on social affairs.

AIM Congress announced her as Master of the Ceremony for the SMEs Track and keynote speaker at AIM Congress 2024 (7-9 May, ADNEC, Abu Dhabi), an annual international investment forum. [ref: Thank-you post to the Masters of Ceremony of AIM Congress 2024] [ref: Report on AIM Congress 2024 quoting Ahlam Gharbaoui, Al Ittihad (print, economy page)] She returned as Master of the Ceremony, this time for the Global Manufacturing and Industrialization track, at AIM Congress 2025 (7-9 April, Abu Dhabi). [ref: Post on AIM Congress 2025 (self-published)] [ref: Post on AIM Congress 2025 (self-published)]

Gharbaoui is the founder of Ahlam Consultancy, which specializes in international business development, strategic partnerships and investments. The firm supports companies entering new markets, developing market-entry strategies, pursuing strategic investments and engaging with governmental and institutional stakeholders across the Netherlands, the UAE, the MENA region and Africa. [ref: Exclusive Strategic Advisory With Ahlam Consultancy: Ahlam Gharbaoui, Emirates Times]

Among her projects was her role in initiating and executing an oil and gas higher education and vocational training centre for the Abu Dhabi Government, delivered through Dutch innovation and expertise, with estimated costs of around USD 28 million (AED 100 million).

In a 2023 interview with Estesmarat, Gharbaoui said that in 2022 she had been nominated by H.E. Sheikh Nahyan bin Mubarak Al Nahyan, Minister of Tolerance and Coexistence, for the UAE Golden Visa in recognition of her contributions to public diplomacy, large-scale investment projects and knowledge transfer.

In March 2024, she was honored at the 7th Estesmarat Awards for 2023, in a ceremony at Atlantis The Palm, Dubai, held under the patronage and in the presence of Sheikh Salem bin Sultan Al Qasimi, before more than 150 guests from media, business and diplomacy. [ref: Video of the 7th Estesmarat Awards for 2023 ceremony at Atlantis The Palm, Dubai] [ref: Reel on the 7th Estesmarat Awards]

In 2026, she received the Morocco With Purpose Award from H.E. Mehdi Bensaid, Minister of Youth, Culture and Communication, in the presence of H.E. André Azoulay, Senior Advisor to His Majesty King Mohammed VI, during the awards ceremony at the historic Chellah in Rabat. [ref: Morocco With Purpose Award ceremony video, Chellah, Rabat; winner confirmed by organizer Hiba El Aidi]

== Writing ==
As an author and English-language poet, she published Senses in Arabia, a collection of poetry, short stories and paintings, reflecting her intercultural perspective and international experiences. [ref: Senses in Arabia, Bloom Books] She presented the book at the 2024 edition of SIEL, the international publishing and book fair in Rabat. [ref: Ahlam Gharbaoui, Dutch writer of Moroccan origin - video interview at SIEL, 2M]

data.title: Bible Translations into Iban
data.text:
The translation of the Bible into Sea Dyak or Iban (ISO-639: iba) commenced in the year 1864 in close association with missionary priests from the Society for the Propagation of the Gospel from the Anglican church. The first complete New Testament translation was published by the British and Foreign Bible Society in 1933. Subsequently, the Old Testament was translated by a committee of native Iban Christians in Sarawak. The first full Bible in Iban (Bup Kudus: Berita Manah Ka Rebak Diatu), translated with the translation principles of dynamic equivalence, was then published by the Bible Society of Malaysia in 1988. An ecumenical revision of the full Bible with the Deuterocanonical books was done in consultation with the Anglican Diocese of Kuching, Methodist Sarawak Iban Annual Conference, and the Roman Catholic church. The revision published by the Bible Society of Malaysia in 2011, named Bup Kudus Baru (+ Deuterokanonikal), revised earlier renderings to adhere to the formal equivalence principle. In 2026, the Iban Study Bible was published by the Bible Society of Malaysia. [ref: Iban Study Bible launched in Kuching after eight-year effort, Borneo Post Online]

== History of Translation ==
The translation of Christian Scriptures into the Iban language commenced with the involvement of Anglican missionaries associated with the Society for the Propagation of the Gospel in Foreign Parts (SPG). In 1847, the Borneo Mission was established due to the request from Sir James Brooke, which was later administered by SPG in 1853. [ref: Into all lands: the history of the Society for the Propagation of the Gospel in Foreign Parts 1701-1950, SPCK] As SPG sent missionary priests to different parts of Sarawak, portions of the Gospels and New Testament were gradually translated into Iban in the years 1864–1933. Such portions were published by foreign publishers: firstly the Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, then The Society for the Propagation of the Gospel Mission, and lastly the British and Foreign Bible Society. The published translations attribute the above missionary priests as the translators, e.g., W. R. Mesney, J. Perham, G. F. Hose, W. R. Mesney, W. Howell, & F. W. Leggatt, and Wilfred Linton, some of whom subsequently became the Bishop and Archdeacons of the Diocese of Singapore and Diocese of Labuan and Sarawak. This era of Bible translation by foreign missionaries ended with the 1933 complete New Testament, translated by Wilfred Linton.

After a century of mission work among the Iban people, Iban Christians were ready to be involved in completing the Old Testament translation in Iban. After 20 years of translation by a committee of Iban Christians and 4 years of revising the New Testament to adhere to the Old Testament's language, the full Bible was published in 1988 by the Bible Society of Malaysia. [ref: Bup Kudus: berita manah ka rebak diatu: Sempekat Lama enggau Sempekat Baru, The Bible Society of Malaysia] The translation was done with the dynamic equivalence principle, conveying the sense of the original text into Iban. Notable changes were made to orthographic elements and the names of Biblical characters; e.g., Jesus Christ was rendered as "Jesus Kristus" instead of the earlier "Isa al-Masih".

After the publication of the Iban bible in 1988, a number of churches had requested the Bible Society of Malaysia to revise the full Bible in order to achieve better clarity and naturalness of the Bible. [ref: Bup Kudus Baru, The Bible Society of Malaysia] At the same time, the Roman Catholic churches in Sarawak also appealed for a translation of the Deuterocanonical books in Iban. Starting on May 1999, the Bible Society of Malaysia began its revision process. Prior to commissioning the revision and the translation of the Deuterocanonical books, the Bible Society of Malaysia brought together representatives from mainline Sarawakian churches (Roman Catholic, Anglican, Methodist) to decide on the orthography of the revision. The ecumenical committee agreed to update the orthography of the Bible according to the new spelling system taught in schools. The written vowel "o" should then be updated to "u", for instance, "jako" should be spelt as "jaku". The vowel "o" in "orang" and other foreign loanwords is retained (domba, chunto, dosa). The verbal suffix "ka" was then combined to the preceding verb, e.g., "awak ka" would be spelled as "awakka". Besides linguistic updates, the committee reworked the existing Iban Bible by checking with the original languages of the Bible, namely Hebrew, Aramaic, and Greek. English loanwords were also used when appropriate, e.g., "misteri" and "panik". Trial versions consisting Genesis, Ezra, Mark, Romans, Galatians, Baruch, and 1 Maccabees were sent to numerous Sarawakian church denominations for community review. The ecumenical revision work by the Iban churches was published in 2011 in two versions by the Bible Society of Malaysia: the Protestant canon (Bup Kudus Baru) and Roman Catholic canon (Bup Kudus Baru + Deuterokanonikal).

Immediately after the publication of the revised Iban Bible Bup Kudus Baru, the Sarawakian church requested for more Bible study materials in the Iban language. A Study Bible project was commissioned by the Bible Society of Malaysia in 2018, with the goal to translate the notes and paratextual materials from the ESV Global Study Bible into Iban, to be placed alongside the revised Iban translation Bup Kudus Baru. A trial version was launched in 2024, in conjunction with the launch of the Malay formal equivalent translation Alkitab Kudus Malaysia and the Malaysian Malay Study Bible (Alkitab Berita Baik Edisi Studi). Eventually in 2026, the Iban Study Bible was launched in Kuching and in Sibu, with the presence and support of the Association of Churches Sarawak, Anglican Diocese of Kuching, and Methodist Sarawak Iban Annual Conference. [ref: Edisi Kajian Alkitab dalam bahasa Iban dilancarkan, www.utusanborneo.com.my]

data.title: Liujia mizhu
data.text:
Liujia mizhu (, literally "Secret Prayer of the Six Jia") is a nine-character Daoist prayer for entering famous mountains, first attested in Ge Hong's Baopuzi, Inner Chapter 17, Dengshe ("Climbing [Mountains] and Crossing [Rivers]"), in the Eastern Jin dynasty. It is also known in later Chinese usage as the Nine-Character Prayer ().

== Name ==
"Liujia mizhu" is the name used in the Baopuzi itself. "Nine-Character Prayer" is a later general name for the same nine characters. The related Japanese practice, known as kuji-goshin-hō (九字護身法), uses a different ending and a different ritual system, and is treated separately below; it should not be conflated with the Chinese prayer.

== Text and context in the Baopuzi ==
The Baopuzi states:

The context is entering mountains. The same passage also mentions hanging five-colour silk on a large rock on a jiazi opening day. The key instruction is secret, constant recitation (). The claim that "nothing will not be warded off" is the text's own statement, not a modern verified efficacy claim.

=== Recitation ===
Point by point, the original text prescribes only the following; nothing further may be added to the original method:
* Secret recitation (): recited secretly, not chanted aloud in public;
* Constant recitation (): recited often; the text prescribes no fixed number of repetitions;
* One whole prayer: the nine characters are recited as a single sentence; the text prescribes no pause between characters, no paired hand seals, and no visualisation;
* Occasion: entering mountains.
The neighbouring jiazi opening-day silk-hanging rite in the same passage is a separate mountain-entering rite; its calendrical requirement must not be transferred into the secret prayer's recitation method.

=== Explanation ===
Character-by-character pinyin and literal glosses ( is read xíng, not háng; is the archaic graph in the quotation):
* lín: to approach, to face;
* bīng: soldiers, weapons;
* dòu: to fight, combat;
* zhě: one who …;
* jiē: all;
* zhèn: battle array;
* liè: to array, to line up;
* qián: forward;
* xíng: to march, to advance.
Syntax: ("those who face battle") is the subject, ("array in formation and march forward") is the predicate; the literal sense of the whole sentence is "the warriors facing battle all array in formation and march forward." Ge Hong's own gloss, "the essential way is not troublesome" (), marks the limit of the original explanation: it stops at the literal sense and does not develop per-character powers, symbolism, or meditation. Later per-character symbolic meanings are modern additions and are kept in the modern reception section, not in the original explanation.

The Baopuzi passage prescribes no hand seals (mudra), breathing technique, or per-character meditation paired with the nine characters. Those belong to later Japanese developments, below.

== The Six Jia ==
The Six Jia () are the six sexagesimal combinations beginning with the stem jia: jiazi, jiaxu, jiashen, jiawu, jiachen, and jiayin. In Daoist usage they are personified as protective generals, later commonly paired as the Six Ding and Six Jia.

== Character forms and variants ==
* 陣列前行 (zhen lie qian xing): the ending in the Baopuzi, meaning to array in formation and then march forward.
* 陳列前行: chen is an older graph for the same word as zhen ("battle array").
* 陣列在前 (zhen lie zai qian): the Japanese transmission form, meaning to be arrayed in front, rather than to march forward. It appears in Japanese Shugendo and Onmyodo sources and is a Japanese development, not the Baopuzi text.
* 數組: not a historical variant. No historical or liturgical form containing this reading has been located; do not list it as a variant.

== Japanese development ==
In Japan, the nine characters were developed in Shugendo and Onmyodo into a system pairing the characters with nine hand seals and a cutting grid of four vertical and five horizontal strokes, known as kuji-goshin-hō or kuji-kiri. Its nine characters end in zai qian ("in front"), not qian xing. Japanese sources themselves describe this system as a distinctively Japanese practice, not as orthodox esoteric Buddhist transmission. See Kuji-in.

== Modern reception ==
In contemporary Chinese source-citing contexts, the Baopuzi original ending qian xing is taken as the standard form.

In popular culture and in the existing Chinese Wikipedia article on jiuzi hushanfa, the Japanese zai qian form still circulates. Both facts should be stated side by side, rather than presenting either form as the whole of contemporary usage.

== References ==
* Ge Hong, Baopuzi neipian jiaoshi, collated by Wang Ming, Beijing: Zhonghua Shuju, 1985, juan 17, Dengshe.
* Stephen R. Bokenkamp, "Lingbao", in Fabrizio Pregadio (ed.), The Encyclopedia of Taoism, Routledge, 2008, vol. 1, pp. 663–669. (For Lingbao background only, not for a DZ 388 quotation of the nine characters.)
* Lingbao wufu xu (DZ 388), in the Daozang.
* A Chinese scholarly dictionary entry for "六甲".

== See also ==
* Kuji-in
* Baopuzi
* Ge Hong

data.title: The Olowu of Owu Kingdom (Saka Matemilola)
data.text:
----

His Royal Highness, Alayeluwa Oba (Professor) Saka Matemilola (4 August 1964) is a traditional ruler of Nigeria, an engineer, and an academician who is known as the Olowu of Owu Kingdom in Abeokuta, Ogun State. [ref: Saka Matemilola: A New Beginning In Owu Kingdom, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News] [ref: Matemilola to succeed Dosunmu as Olowu of Owu Kingdom, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News]. He succeeded Oba Adegboyega Dosunmu, who passed away on 12 December 2021, and became the 14th monarch of the kingdom. [ref: News Update – Owu Kingdom][b] He graduated from the University of Ibadan with a Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering and holds a Ph.D. degree from the University of Cambridge.[a] Prior to his installation as the Olowu of Owu Kingdom, he was working as a consultant for reservoir engineering in the oil industry at Shell. [ref: Olowu warns traditional rulers against partisan politics as Falola Interview examines palace, power, Tribune Online] Additionally, Matemilola has also lived in the UK before relocation to Nigeria in 1996. [ref: Hunger Threatening Nigeria’s Future, monarch Tells FG, Daily Trust]

He has earned a name as Olowu from his involvement in the importance of traditional institutions within the democratic process in Nigeria. In this regard, he has observed that traditional rulers must be made a part of the form of governance without engaging in politics, and there must be a constitutional arrangement for their involvement. [ref: Nigeria’s Oil Woes Rooted In Decades Of Misrule, Say Industry Veterans, Platform Times] He has criticized the feeding scheme in schools by the federal government. [ref: Olowu visits burnt Baale’s residence, urges calm over alleged arson, Vanguard News]

The Olowu Hope Programme is a social intervention programme that deals with education, healthcare, business and environmental sustainability, and which includes daily meals for primary school children in Abeokuta. He is also the President-General of the Muslim Council of Ogun State. [ref: NSCIA seeks divine intervention, urges Nigerians to complement prayers with action, Muslim News Nigeria]

== Early Life of Alayeluwa Oba (Professor) Saka Adelola Ayokanmi Matemilola ==
Matemilola was born on August 4, 1964 and hails from one of the ruling dynasties that traces its lineage to the family of Ajibosin, grandson of Oduduwa. Matemilola is from the ruling dynasty of Matemilola of the Soke Compound. Matemilola has Bachelor of Science and Master of Science in mechanical engineering degrees from the University of Ibadan and a doctoral degree from the University of Cambridge. [a] He was active in charity work during his stay in the UK. His return to Nigeria in 1996 has been referred to as continuing his public service career.

== Career ==
===Petroleum industry===

Matemilola has worked as a reservoir engineering consultant at Shell Petroleum, Port Harcourt, between 2009 and 2011. In 2011, he was part of the group that set up the Centre of Excellence in Geosciences and Petroleum Engineering at the University of Benin. According to reports, he sits on the board of a number of corporations. The Platform Times referred to him as a former president of the Society of Petroleum Engineers.

=== Academic reputation ===
In The Toyin Falola Interview, the historian Toyin Falola referred to Matemilola as one of the rare individuals who combine traditional leadership and international scholarship, based on his background from Ibadan and Cambridge in engineering and energy.

=== Accession ===
Matemilola appeared after the selection of seven aspirants from the ruling lineages of Owu, following the performance of certain traditional ceremonies. Matemilola was to be crowned on 29 October 2022.. He has stated that his family had been preparing him for the position for many years and that he had received encouragement from his friends and colleagues to aspire to the throne. His throne name is Oluyalo Otileta VII, and his style is Alayeluwa

=== Reign ===
====Unity and Culture of the Yoruba====

Matemilola states that the unity of the Yoruba is the main goal of his reign. This will be done using programs such as the Odun Omo Olowu, which is an annual celebration in which he will send a message of unity to the Yorubas in and outside the country.

===Public Appearance===

Matemilola’s public appearances include the courtesy visit by the association of organizations such as Abeokuta North Chapter of NULGE (National Union of Local Government Employees) and the Agboole Akogun family. Also included among some of his public appearances is the 60th birthday celebration of the Olota of Ota, Oba (Professor) Adeyemi Abdulkabir Obalanlege.

===Political views===
====Non-partisanship====
In The Toyin Falola Interview, titled "Indigenous Education, Character Formation and Citizen Making," Matemilola maintained that traditional rulers cannot become apolitical in the process of governance but should desist from partisan tendencies. He posited that for a ruler to hold power, he must represent the entire community not a political party. He added that if a ruler openly supports a political party or any candidate, the stool becomes debased.

====Constitutional duty====

Traditional rulers can be useful in dealing with insecurity owing to their close association with the grassroots. While speaking at a national prayer meeting organized by the Nigerian Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA) in Abuja, Matemilola advised traditional rulers to remain neutral during times of political tension. In his words, they should ensure that their influence is used in ensuring that tensions do not flare up and also mentioned that insecurity is fueled by poverty and economic hardship.

====Public policy====

Matemilola has posited that the school feeding program by the Federal Government collapsed due to improper implementation but not bad policy. Matemilola opined that for successful programs to be put in place there must be transparency, proper targeting and constant monitoring of the impact of such policies.

===Religious Leadership===

Matemilola is the president-general of the Muslim Council of Ogun State. He joined other Muslim clerics at the NSCIA national prayer for Nigeria at the National Mosque Complex in Abuja on 30 September 2026. During the occasion, he encouraged budding Islamic scholars to fuse Islamic education with good character.

==Philanthropy==

Before becoming the king, Matemilola helped his subjects through borehole provision of water, feeding of those who cannot afford to eat, financial help, and school building projects. He was also seen as having built a school and a water treatment facility and providing regular financial and humanitarian help to those indigent members of his community.

In a media conference to mark the fourth anniversary of his coronation, he explained his "[https://www.owukingdom.org/ Olowu Hope Initiative]." The initiative consists of four pillars which include education, well-being and health, entrepreneurship and skill acquisition, and environmental sustainability and climate change initiatives. Health screening at ANLG Primary School had revealed that over 65 percent of children suffer from malnutrition or severe malnutrition. Thereafter, he instituted the "Meal-a-Day" scheme that feeds one meal to 165 children every day of the school week. In the course of the program, he was able to feed 8,500 pupils at less than ₦2 million.

==Public image==
The profile of Matemilola in Guardian Life noted that he was respected among his subjects based on his record of public service. He was seen during the Elere-Adubi peace mission as a fatherly figure whose involvement was meant to bring back peace. His comments on palace and politics have been quoted in national media like Tribune and Daily Trust.

==Personal Life==

His wife is Olori Cecilia Naadensua Matemilola.

==Notes==
a. According to Guardian Nigeria, Matemilola has obtained a PhD in Applied Mathematics from the University of Cambridge.From The Toyin Falola Interview, it is stated by Falola that he graduated from Cambridge in Applied Mechanics.

b. According to Guardian Nigeria, his coronation ceremony was expected to take place on 29th October 2022. According to Daily Trust, his palace celebrated his fourth anniversary of coronation on 27th July 2026. This implies that the sources give different dates for the coronation events.

data.title: Athanasios Papastyliadis
data.text:
Athanasios Papastyliadis

Athanasios Papastyliadis (Αθανάσιος Παπαστυλιάδης in Greek, 1875–1939) was a master builder, practical architect, building contractor, and merchant in Western Macedonia and Romania. He participated in the Macedonian Struggle in 1904 as an organizer and collaborator of Pavlos Melas, alongside other members of his family.

Origin and Early Life

Athanasios Papastyliadis was a scion of the Styliadis family, descendants of priest Kostas (son of Stylos or Stylianos), who over time adopted the surnames Stylou, Stylianou, and Styliadis. (Athanasios was the only one who used the surname Papastyliadis to indicate his descent from priests [papa-].) The family included well-known builders and icon-painters [ref: Ζωγράφοι του Βιτσίου, Prefectural Committee for Popular Education (Ν.Ε.Λ.Ε) of Florina].

Priest Kostas, Athanasios's grandfather, set out after 1840 from Plikati in Konitsa —the northernmost of the area's builder villages (mastrochoria)— at the head of about 50 families and his four brothers. After a long journey, they reached the region of Florina, where in 1843 they purchased a large tract of land in the forest [ref: Μπελκαμένη. Χωριό του νομού Φλώρινας. (Εκατό χρόνια ζωή), Διογένης - Πέτρος Κουλουφάκος] from Bey Osman Ismail Passou for 3,000 gold sovereigns [ref: Η ζωή και οι περιπέτειες στη Δροσοπηγή. Λαογραφικά - ιστορικά ενθυμήματα, "Politis" newspaper]. They were bilingual (Greek-speaking and Albanian-speaking), all stone artisans, and founded the villages of Belkameni (present-day Drosopigi) in 1844 and Negovani (present-day Flampouro) in 1861, building houses with very thick walls and a sewage system.

He was born in 1875, the son of Dimitrios Styliadis or Stylianou, son of Priest Kostas. (In the family, he was known as Nasi-Miti —Thanasis [son of] Dimitris.) He married Agora Giankou at a very young age and had 18 or 19 children with her, seven of whom died in infancy or early childhood. The first, Zacharia, was born in 1894.

Alongside the craft of stonemasonry learned from his ancestors, he also engaged in trade with Romania. Many craftsmen from Belkameni worked seasonally in Bucharest, leaving the village on the Feast of Saint George and returning for the Feast of Saint Demetrius. Athanasios established a commercial store in Brăila, trading mainly in woolen goods, which he procured from surrounding villages and Mount Athos. As early as 1897, he used letterhead featuring his name in Latin script, as evidenced by eight of his letters to [https://www.pemptousia.gr/2014/06/agiorites-mikrasiates-igoumeni-to-2/ Archimandrite Neofytos—abbot of the Monastery of Simonopetra on Mount Athos]— and monk Galaktion, a fellow villager living there. The letters date between 1897 and 1904 and are preserved at the monastery.

Macedonian Struggle and Flight to Romania

With the onset of the Macedonian Struggle, Papastyliadis became active and established ties with the Greek Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which awarded him the rank of First Class Agent. On July 25, he went to Kozani to meet Pavlos Melas during Melas's second entry into Macedonia. Melas wrote to his wife: "...Athanasios Papastyliadis came from Belkameni, a good brave fellow of the area. We brought him to make arrangements for men and hideouts, so they are ready at once." [ref: Παύλος Μελάς, Δωδώνη]

Papastyliadis organized the necessary arrangements for the struggle. Melas entered Ottoman-ruled Macedonia for the third time a month later (August 28, 1904) with 35 armed men, becoming the first Greek officer involved in combat in Macedonia. On September 17, the group entered Belkameni secretly and lodged in an empty house. There, they met the village committee, including Papastyliadis, [https://macedonian-fighters.com/index.php/%CE%A0%CE%AD%CF%84%CF%81%CE%BF%CF%82_%CE%A3%CF%84%CF%85%CE%BB%CE%B9%CE%AC%CE%B4%CE%B7%CF%82 Priest Petros Styliadis] (his father's first cousin and also a First Class Agent of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs), and the volunteer Filippos Kapetanopoulos. The group left for the forest at 3:00 a.m. to avoid incriminating Papastyliadis, while Melas and his second-in-command, Lakis Pyrzas, were hosted at Papastyliadis's home. In the morning, the troop entered the village triumphantly and departed later.

Following the death of Pavlos Melas on October 13, 1904, the komitadjis sought to eliminate his associates. They assassinated Priest Petros Styliadis, forcing Athanasios to flee in 1905 to Kastoria and then to Brăila, where he stayed until shortly after the Young Turk Revolution. Upon leaving, he left his shop to Athanasios Giokas, the husband of his daughter Elisabeth. (During his stay in Romania in 1907, the komitadjis also assassinated Apostolos Styliadis, his father's brother and a Third Class Agent, and imprisoned his relative Nikolaos Styliadis, a First Class Agent of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.) [ref: Αφανείς γηγενείς μακεδονομάχοι (1903 – 1913), University Studio Press]

Return to Greece

Following the Young Turk Revolution, he returned to Greece, initially likely to his birthplace. He settled permanently in Kastoria after its liberation on November 11, 1912. Working as a practical architect and contractor, he built numerous homes and public buildings in the surrounding area. Until a few years ago, older residents of Kastoria remembered him as the Kalfas. Panos Tsolakis, former associate professor at the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, noted in a presentation on Papastyliadis and his works at Argos Orestiko during a conference on December 8, 2012 (titled "Two Notable School Buildings of Argos Orestiko"): "At that time, practical architects who designed, prepared budgets, and undertook the construction of various buildings were called kalfa." Tsolakis continues: "After constructing the school of Chroupista [Argos Orestiko], we know that Ath. Papastyliadis built the Girls' School of Florina in 1909, which today operates as a primary school. After the liberation, he settled permanently in Kastoria, where in addition to many neoclassical houses, he built the Kastoria high school next to Koumbelidiki in 1914 and the bell tower of the metropolis in 1915, standing 19 meters high (Petros Manos dates it to [https://www.kastoria365.gr/2018/06/25/tessera-exaireta-erga-toy-kalfa-papas/ 1916])." The oldest surviving building he constructed is the twin schoolhouse of the Boys' and Girls' School of Argos Orestiko (1911), which operated until 1996 as the 1st Primary School.

He died in Kastoria in 1939. His children were: Zacharia (wife of Petros Tatsiokas), Kosmas, Florika, Michael, Dimitrios, Efrosyni (wife of Georgios Sidos), Maria (wife of Georgios Manos), Elisabeth (wife of Athanasios Giokas), and Evangelos.

data.title: Nandinkhusel Nyamjav
data.text:
Nandinkhusel Nyamjav (born 9 September 2006) is a Mongolian basketball player who plays as a guard. She represents Mongolia in international 3x3 and 5x5 basketball competitions.

== Career ==

Nyamjav developed through the Mongolian basketball system and represented Mongolia in international youth competitions. She is a two-time champion of Mongolia's National Premier League, winning championships with Ulaanbaatar Amazons in the 2022–23 and 2024–25 seasons. [ref: Meet the FIBA WBL Asia 2025 teams: Ulaanbaatar Amazons, FIBA] [ref: Н.Нандинхүсэл: Монголоос өөр газар сагс тоглож чадвараа ахиулаад, улсынхаа нэрийг Дэлхийд гаргахыг хүсэж байна /ВИДЕО/, iSee.mn] [ref: Би АНУ-ын WNCAA-д тоглох мөрөөдөлтэй, News.mn]
She attended SPIRE Academy in the United States before beginning her college career. [ref: Nandinkhusel Nyamjav, Florida Tech Athletics] [ref: Нямжав Нандинхүсэл, MSports]

== College career ==

=== Florida Tech Panthers ===

Nyamjav played for Florida Tech during the 2025–26 season, appearing in 17 games and averaging 11.6 points, 4.6 rebounds and 3.0 assists per game. [ref: Н.Нандинхүсэл WNCAA Division I-д тоглох анхны монгол тамирчин боллоо, iToim] Her season-high was 28 points against USC Beaufort, and she recorded a double-double of 16 points and 10 rebounds against Saint Leo. [ref: Women's Basketball Adds Seven to 2026-27 Roster, Tennessee State University Athletics]

=== Tennessee State Tigers ===

Nyamjav transferred to Tennessee State University for the 2026–27 season. [ref: Nandinkhusel Nyamjav, Tennessee State University Athletics] [ref: Historical step: Mongolian basketball player Nandinkhusel receives No. 10 in NCAA Division I, Open.kg] [ref: Монгол Улсын Гавьяат тамирчин Н.Нандинхүсэл NCAAW буюу АНУ-ын эмэгтэй сагсан бөмбөгийн оюутны лигийн D1-т тоглоно, iKon.mn]

== 5×5 national team career ==

=== 2022 FIBA U18 Women's Asia Cup Division B ===

Nyamjav has represented Mongolia at both youth and senior international levels in FIBA competitions. She first represented Mongolia at the youth level, playing at the 2022 FIBA U18 Women's Asia Cup Division B, where she averaged 16.6 points, 13.4 rebounds and 4.8 assists per game over five games. [ref: Nyamjav Nandinkhusel, FIBA]

=== 2023 FIBA Women's Asia Cup Division B ===

Nyamjav made her senior national team appearance at the 2023 FIBA Women's Asia Cup Division B. She played four games for Mongolia, averaging 9.0 points, 3.0 rebounds and 3.0 assists per game. Her tournament totals were 36 points, 12 rebounds and 12 assists in 94 minutes of play. [ref: Nyamjav Nandinkhusel, FIBA]

=== 2025 FIBA Women's Asia Cup Division B ===

At the 2025 FIBA Women's Asia Cup Division B, Nyamjav became one of Mongolia's main contributors. She played six games, averaging 12.8 points, 3.2 rebounds and 4.7 assists per game. [ref: Nyamjav Nandinkhusel, FIBA]

Her tournament totals were 77 points, 19 rebounds and 28 assists in 191 minutes. She recorded her best performances against Thailand and Kazakhstan, scoring 19 points in both games while also contributing seven assists in each match. [ref: МУГТ Н.Нандинхүсэл нийт 19 оноо, 3 самбар, 7 ашигтай дамжуулалт хийж, багаа тэргүүллээ, UBn]

== 3x3 national team career ==

Nyamjav represented Mongolia at the 2025 FIBA 3x3 World Cup, where the team won the silver medal. [ref: FIBA 3x3 World Cup 2025 – Mongolia, FIBA 3x3] [ref: 3х3 сагсан бөмбөгийн тамирчид болон дасгалжуулагчид Гавьяат тамирчин цол, медаль хүртээлээ, Office of the President of Mongolia] [ref: Хамгийн залуу гавьяат тамирчин 18 настай Нямжавын Нандинхүсэл, Eguur] [ref: Алдартнуудын өлгий NCAA буюу АНУ-ын оюутны лигт нэрээ гаргаж буй монгол тамирчид, iKon.mn] [ref: Монголын шигшээ багийн холбогч Н.Нандинхүсэл Флоридагийн “Пантерс” багт тоглоно, Montsame]

She was also named one of the three finalists for the 2025 FIBA 3x3 Women's Rookie of the Year award. [ref: 2025 FIBA 3x3 Women's Rookie of the Year finalists, Instagram]

data.text:
In the run up to the 2031 Russian legislative election, various organisations carried out opinion polling to gauge voting intention in Russia. The results of these polls are displayed in this article. Polls were conducted only for the 225 seats elected on the party list. Another 225 deputies are elected directly in single member constituencies, where the party can obtain a completely different result.

The date range for these opinion polls are from the 2026 Russian legislative election, held on 18–20 September, until the time next election will be held.

== Graphical summary ==

== Pre-campaign polls ==
Opinion polls conducted prior to the campaign and the announcement of the list of participating parties. Parties with more than 5% support of the whole electorate (enough to enter State Duma while not adjusting for likely voters) are given in bold. When a specific poll does not show a data figure for a party, the party's cell corresponding to that poll is shown empty.

Polling firms that tend to inflate electoral rating of United Russia are colored in gray. Polling firms affiliated with Russian liberal opposition are colored in cyan. WCIOM and FOM firms are known for their connection to president Vladimir Putin and Presidential Administration of Russia with latter often inflating electoral rating of United Russia for the upcoming election.

data.title: NovaPoints
data.text:
NovaPoints is a Telegram Mini App on
The Open Network (TON) blockchain, developed by the studio
Codiologism, in which users accumulate points that the project states
will determine their share of a planned token
airdrop. [ref: NovaPoints — Earn points, claim NOVAP, ton.app] [ref: NovaPoints]

== Mechanics ==

According to the project, users earn "NOVA Points" through daily claims,
activity streaks, in-app missions, rewarded advertisements, and
referrals. At the end of each season, a snapshot of
season scores is published and token allocations are distributed through
an on-chain Merkle claim contract.

== NOVAP token ==

NOVAP is a TEP-74 standard token (jetton) on TON mainnet with a
fixed supply of 100,000,000. [ref: NOVAP jetton, Tonviewer]
The project states that 79 million NOVAP — covering the airdrop pool and
liquidity reserve — are held in a 2-of-3 multisignature treasury
contract. Project documentation describes a Season 1
distribution of a 25,000,000 NOVAP pool capped at 50,000 NOVAP per user,
with allocations vesting 25% at the token generation event and 25% per
month for three months thereafter.

Fael Bezerra Luna (born 29 August 2005), known professionally as Fael Luna, is a Brazilian fashion model, actor and activist from Caruaru, Pernambuco, Brazil. His public biographical records identify modelling, acting and activism among his professional activities. [ref: Fael Luna, IMDb]

== Early life ==

Luna was born on 29 August 2005 in Caruaru, a municipality in the northeastern Brazilian state of Pernambuco.

During his childhood, he lived in different cities in northeastern Brazil, including Fortaleza, Ceará, and João Pessoa, Paraíba, before returning to Caruaru.

He developed an interest in fashion, art and visual culture during his youth.

data.text:
Cuffem (born April 30, 2002) is an American online streamer and internet personality. Originally from Alabama, he is known for his gaming, reaction, online dating and in-real-life (IRL) livestreams. He first gained recognition on Twitch before becoming active on Kick, where he frequently collaborated with fellow streamer Adin Ross. [ref: The 25 Up-And-Coming Streamers You Need To Know, Ranked, Complex]

In February 2025, Complex ranked Cuffem 12th on its list of up-and-coming livestreamers. His Kick channel recorded a peak of 236,746 concurrent viewers in November 2025, according to streaming analytics provider Streams Charts. [ref: cuffem – Kick Stats, Analytics and Channel Overview, Streams Charts]

== Early life ==
Cuffem grew up in Alabama, United States. Biographical listings report his date of birth as April 30, 2002.

== Career ==

=== 2019–2022: Streaming beginnings ===
Cuffem began streaming in 2019, initially broadcasting gameplay from NBA 2K and Fortnite. He subsequently expanded into Grand Theft Auto V roleplay, conversational broadcasts and other variety content. He became associated with Adin Ross's SSB streaming group, which included several other gaming personalities.

=== 2023–2024: Kick and collaborations ===
Cuffem developed an audience on Kick through a combination of gaming, commentary, online dating and IRL streams. His broadcasts frequently featured interactions with viewers and collaborations with other online personalities.

=== 2025–present: Audience growth ===
In February 2025, Complex ranked Cuffem 12th on its list of 25 up-and-coming streamers, highlighting his online dating and Grand Theft Auto broadcasts.

In September 2025, he appeared during Kai Cenat's Mafiathon 3 livestream event. [ref: Kick streamer Cuffem finally gets chance to join Kai Cenat's Mafiathon 3, Sportskeeda] On November 30, 2025, his Kick channel reached a peak of 236,746 concurrent viewers, according to Streams Charts.

In January 2026, Cuffem, Adin Ross and rapper 6ix9ine recorded a diss track during a livestream, attracting coverage from Complex. [ref: 6ix9ine, Adin Ross, and Cuffem Record Diss Track, Complex]

In October 2026, he appeared on Bradley Martyn's Rawtalk podcast to discuss his streaming career and online content. [ref: Cuffem Exposes The Truth About Streaming, Money & Beef With Jshock, Apple Podcasts] That month, reports also described his proposal for a streaming collective called Sinister Six. [ref: Cuffem Announces New Content Group Called Sinister Six, NDTV Sports]

== Content and public image ==
Cuffem is primarily known for variety livestreams, including gaming, reactions, video-chat interactions, online dating and IRL broadcasts. Complex highlighted his energetic presentation and transition from gaming content into a broader range of livestream formats.

== Controversies ==
In May 2025, Dexerto reported that Cuffem had been arrested in Georgia on alleged speeding and reckless-driving offenses. He was subsequently released and returned to livestreaming. [ref: Twitch streamer Cuffem goes live right after getting out of jail for alleged reckless driving, Dexerto]

In July 2025, Cuffem was temporarily banned from Kick following a livestream described as a "lean mukbang". Cuffem disputed that the broadcast involved actual lean, and Adin Ross publicly defended him. [ref: Adin Ross Defends Kick Streamer Cuffem After Alleged Lean Mukbang Ban, Complex]
