data.title: NANA KWEKU BOMPEH
data.text:
== Nana Bekyere Yankeh II ==
Nana Bekyere Yankeh II (born John Arkurst Junior, 30th September 1874 - 15th October 1939) was a Ghanaian traditional leader, gold artist, entrepreneur, and creator.

== Early life and career ==
Nana Bekyere Yankeh II, born John Arkurst Junior on 30th September 1874, was also known as Kweku Bompeh (Nana Bompeh). He was born to John Arkurst and Maame Bosuafre Nyame. He was a prosperous gold artist, entrepreneur, and creator. He invested heavily in the gold business, training generations of young people in goldsmithing and related trades.

== Chieftaincy ==
John Arkurst Junior was enstooled as Nana Bekyere Yankeh II, the Chief of Dutch Sekondi, on 2nd August 1926 and elevated on 4th August 1927 as the First Omanhene of Sekondi. His reign covered 18 towns from Essipon to Essaman. The Prince of Wales visited Sekondi during his reign.

== Development agenda ==
As a visionary leader, he ceded part of the Poasi-Sekondi lands to establish New-Takoradi and pave the way for the construction of the Takoradi Harbour—sacrificing land for national development.

His core belief was "Creativity and Ownership as the bedrock of prosperity".

== Notable incidents ==
In October 1985, at the request of the Regional Director of the Ghana Education Service, the school was upgraded to senior secondary school level and renamed Bompeh Day Secondary Technical School [ref: Bompeh Senior High Technical School - High School in Takoradi,, Aa,, www.edusko.com]

after Nana Bompeh for his courage, selfless service, contribution to the development of the port city of Sekondi-Takoradi and keen interest in education during his reign.

Bompeh Secondary Technical School [ref: ] has trained young men and women in Ghana who play meaningful roles in Ghanaians’ lives and the world at large. Bompeh is currently poised to become the Achimota of the West and is positioned as a school for innovators, creators & owners.

== Death ==
Nana Bompeh died on 15th October 1939, at the age of 65.

data.title: Muayad Abbas
data.text:
----

== [user] ==
Muayad "Mo" Abbas is a real estate development executive and university lecturer known for his involvement in residential, hospitality, and mixed-use developments in the United States and international markets. He is Managing Director of Development at OKO Group and a lecturer at the University of Miami School of Architecture. [ref: Bisnow's Hurricane Irma Miami State of the Market, Bisnow] [ref: Former Ritz president leads new North Miami project, The Real Deal] [ref: Rafael Moneo Reveals Design of His First Condo Tower in Miami, ArchDaily]

== Career ==

=== Related International ===
Abbas previously served as Vice President of Related International, the international development arm of the Related Group, overseeing real estate operations in Panama, Colombia, and Argentina. [ref: Bisnow's Hurricane Irma Miami State of the Market, Bisnow]

=== Urbanis Advisors and Apeiron Living ===
Abbas founded Urbanis Advisors, a real estate development and advisory firm. He subsequently co-founded Apeiron Living, a luxury residential and hospitality venture conceived in collaboration with Horst Schulze, co-founder and former president of the Ritz-Carlton Hotel Company, and Michael Bedner, co-founder of Hirsch Bedner Associates (HBA). [ref: Former Ritz president leads new North Miami project, The Real Deal] [ref: Rafael Moneo Reveals Design of His First Condo Tower in Miami, ArchDaily] [ref: Apeiron at the Jockey Club wins approval, plans to launch sales, The Real Deal]

The founders developed Apeiron as a hospitality and residential brand combining luxury living with personalized service, health and wellness, preventive medical care, and arts and cultural programming. The concept was designed primarily for affluent, active older adults seeking a residential environment that supported independent living and aging in place.

The brand's development included a positioning and identity exercise undertaken with international design consultancy Pentagram in 2014. [ref: Developers of luxe North Miami project get $21M in financing, The Real Deal] The concept emphasized architecture, hospitality, wellness, and curated experiences as elements of an integrated residential lifestyle. Apeiron's proposed wellness program included medical services coordinated with the Cleveland Clinic. [ref: Apeiron at the Jockey Club wins approval, plans to launch sales, The Real Deal]

Apeiron at the Jockey Club in Miami, Florida, was conceived as the venture's flagship development and a model for potential expansion into other U.S. markets. The proposed redevelopment of the historic waterfront property included serviced residences, hospitality amenities, wellness facilities, dining, cultural programming, and a marina. [ref: Apeiron at the Jockey Club wins approval, plans to launch sales, The Real Deal]

The architectural design was led by Spanish architect Rafael Moneo, recipient of the Pritzker Architecture Prize, with Stantec serving as local architect of record. [ref: Rafael Moneo Reveals Design of His First Condo Tower in Miami, ArchDaily] The project attracted media attention for its architecture, financing, development approvals, and legal disputes.

The development faced legal challenges from existing condominium associations seeking to block construction. In June 2020, Florida's Third District Court of Appeal upheld the trial court's rulings, affirming Apeiron Miami LLC's development and property rights at the Jockey Club. [ref: Jockey Club residents reignite lawsuit against next-door landowner, The Real Deal] [ref: Apeiron at the Jockey Club Developer Wins Key Ruling from Appeals Court, Carlton Fields] [ref: Developer Wins Key Ruling from Appeals Court in Miami-Dade, Council on Vertical Urbanism]

=== Mast Capital ===
Abbas subsequently served as Senior Vice President of Development at Mast Capital, a Miami-based real estate investment and development firm.

During his tenure, he was involved in the development of Cipriani Residences Miami, an 80-story, 397-residence luxury condominium tower in Miami's Brickell neighborhood, designed by Arquitectonica. [ref: Mast Capital, www.mastcapital.com] [ref: ] [ref: Mast Capital, www.mastcapital.com]

The project was developed through a collaboration between Mast Capital and the Cipriani family, whose international hospitality business traces its origins to Harry's Bar in Venice, founded in 1931. Led by Giuseppe Cipriani, the family's hospitality organization partnered with Mast Capital to establish its first ground-up residential development in the United States.

=== OKO Group ===
In 2025, Abbas joined OKO Group as Managing Director of Development, overseeing a portfolio of luxury residential, hospitality, and mixed-use developments. His responsibilities encompass development strategy, design, entitlements, construction, and project execution. [ref: About us, OKO Group]

== Academic career ==
Abbas is a lecturer at the University of Miami School of Architecture, where he teaches real estate entrepreneurship in the Master of Real Estate Development + Urbanism (MRED+U) program.

His teaching focuses on real estate development, entrepreneurship, and practical applications of development strategy. As part of his teaching, he has organized student visits to residential and hospitality developments in Miami, including Cipriani Residences Miami, Una Residences, and Aman Miami Beach, providing students with exposure to the development process and project execution. [ref: ] [ref: Research Portal, scholarship.miami.edu] [ref: ]

data.title: Lindslee
data.text:
----

Lindsey James Alvarez Lee (born 1979), known professionally as Lindslee, is a Filipino contemporary artist based in Metro Manila, Philippines. He began his career as an abstract painter in the early 2000s before expanding into sculpture, installation, taxidermy and conceptual art. His work incorporates everyday objects, food and familiar cultural forms to explore consumption, Filipino culture, social behavior and the relationship between art and society.

== Early life and education ==
Lindslee was born in 1979 in Bacolod and is of Chinese-Filipino descent. He grew up in Hinigaran, Negros Occidental. He attended St. John's Institute in Bacolod, where he took part in painting competitions. He was a national finalist in the 1998 Shell National Students Art Competition and a semi-finalist in the Metrobank Young Painters competition in 1999 and 2000. He earned a Bachelor of Fine Arts in painting from the University of Santo Tomas College of Fine Arts and Design in 2000.

After graduating he went to New York City, where he took courses in mixed media, drawing, painting, and color and composition at the Art Students League of New York. While there he showed in juried exhibitions, was associated with the Greenwich Art Society and won first prize in the mixed-media category of the 2001 Annual Fine Art Show in Long Beach, New York. After winning a local art competition, he held his first solo exhibition at the Harrison Public Library in New York in 2002. He also worked as a house painter during this period, an experience he later connected to his interest in surfaces and repetition.

== Career ==
=== Abstraction (2002–2006) ===
After returning to the Philippines, Lindslee held the solo exhibitions Perception at Avellana Art Gallery (2002) and Cause and Effect at The Drawing Room in Makati (2003). His early work was abstract, mostly in grays and earth tones. In April 2004 he exhibited with former University of Santo Tomas classmates Julio Jose "Jo" Austria, Jeffrey "Jeps" Belen and Artemio "Art" Bermido in Fibonacci, a group show based on the numerical sequence. His 2004 show SR at The Big & Small Art Co. in SM Megamall consisted of square mixed-media works built from layered resin, wax, acrylic, mesh and plastic. The Philippine Star read the surfaces as a reference to grime on Manila's city walls. Reviewing the same show in the Philippine Daily Inquirer, Constantino C. Tejero called him "one of the more accomplished abstractionists of his generation". That year he was shortlisted for the Ateneo Art Awards for his Cause and Effect series.

In 2005 he exhibited Face:Phase, a series of two-sided mixed-media works, at the Cultural Center of the Philippines. His 2006 exhibition Finding Normal at the Goethe-Institut Manila was his eighth solo show. It marked a return to acrylic and oil and introduced a wider color range than his usual grays. In June 2007 he and Austria held Black and White Conversation, a two-person exhibition at West Gallery in Quezon City that dealt with the commercialization of abstract painting.

=== Taxidermy and conceptual work (2007–2012) ===
In 2007 Lindslee began combining taxidermied animals with paintings. His exhibition Animan at The Drawing Room included Sleep for Sale, a taxidermied duck on a pillow, and Pork Chop Explosion, a pig standing on a painting. The Inquirer compared these works to Robert Rauschenberg's combines and saw them as a move away from abstract expressionism. The Manila Bulletin read the show as a comment on commercial gimmickry and copying in Philippine abstract art. He continued the approach in Figuring Abstraction (2008), which included a taxidermied rooster on a lightbox and a duck beside an oversized egg. In 2008 he was a Joan Mitchell Foundation scholar at the Ox-Bow fall artist residency in Saugatuck, Michigan.

In May 2009 he exhibited Metamorphosis, a series of abstract works that drew on familiar images such as a television station's sign-off screen, at Galleria Duemila in Pasay. Later that year he was one of ten artists selected for the "10 Most Exciting Young Artists" exhibition organized by Nokia and the Inquirers Lifestyle section at the Gallery of Greenbelt 5 in Makati. In September 2009 Tropical Storm Ondoy flooded his studio in Cainta, Rizal, leaving works in progress caked in mud. He was a finalist in the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas Tanaw national art competition in 2011 and 2013.

=== Paintings as objects (2013–2019) ===
He later reworked the flood-damaged canvases by cutting, rolling and stacking them, and the Inquirer identified the storm as a turning point toward conceptual art. The resulting exhibition, It's All in the Mind, opened at Galleria Duemila in Pasay in August 2013. It included Ignorant Critic, a taxidermied goat that appears to have bitten off part of a painted landscape. Reviewers compared it to Rauschenberg's Monogram.

In December 2014 he took part in the S-AIR artist-in-residence program in Sapporo, supported by the Japan Foundation. His 2016 exhibition Untitled Cliché at Artery Art Space in Cubao satirized the art market. One work, Pain Thing, connected canvases to intravenous bottles of paint labeled with roles such as "collector" and "financier". Your Personality Is Your Worst Enemy at Galleria Duemila (2017) dealt with the tension between freedom and pragmatism. In 2019 he held a solo exhibition, You Are What You Cheat, at the Pinto Art Museum in Antipolo.

=== Monumental sculpture and food (2022–present) ===
In September 2022 the Pinto Art Museum organized The Mind Crossed the Idea at ArtistSpace, Ayala Museum Annex, in Makati. The show featured sculptures and paintings of everyday objects at monumental scale. Its centerpiece, The Tale of Fatima, depicts an oversized woman in workout clothes holding a taxidermied bird. His later work focuses on Filipino food, including birthday cakes, crackers, sweet-style spaghetti and bread. It was shown in Eat All You Can at The Drawing Room and Your Mouth Has a Mind of Its Own at Art Cube (both 2024), and Happy Birthday at Artinformal (2026). In 2024 he returned to Sapporo for the Tenjinyama artist residency. In 2025 Lifestyle.INQ included him among eighteen Chinese-Filipino artists it profiled for the Lunar New Year.

== Style and themes ==
A recurring theme in Lindslee's work is how art is defined, interpreted and valued within society. He has stated that he seeks to provoke thought through his work rather than merely decorate or entertain. The Philippine Star has compared his enlarged objects with the pop art of Claes Oldenburg and Jeff Koons, noting their engagement with consumerism and middle-class aspiration. According to the Star, by enlarging or transforming familiar objects, he presents everyday subjects in exaggerated forms that challenge conventional perceptions of art and material culture.

Food is another recurring subject in his work. He uses acrylic paint as a sculptural medium, applying it with cake-decorating techniques so that it resembles icing. These works combine painting and sculpture through the imitation of familiar food forms.

== Selected solo exhibitions ==

data.title: Phigros
data.text:
Phigros is a rhythm game developed and published by Pigeon Games. Phigros was initially released to the public globally in August 8, 2019. [ref: Phigros 开发者Q&A - Phigros综合讨论 - TapTap Phigros论坛, www.taptap.cn] In February 24, 2023, the official Bilibili account announced that the game had surpassed 10 million downloads. [ref: Phigros官方的动态]

== Gameplay ==
[[File:XING,and_Muse_Dash_collab_with_Phigros.jpg|left|thumb|The IN chart for the song XING simulates the gameplay of Muse Dash.]]
Phigros features several chart difficulties. All songs have Easy (EZ), Hard (HD), and Insane (IN) difficulties, while Another (AT) is available for some selected songs. Legacy charts consist of older versions of certain charts, while Special (SP) charts are used for certain hidden or event charts. [ref: Phigrosの評価とアプリ情報 - ゲーム一覧, GAMEWITH] During gameplay, notes approach judgement lines that can move, rotate, change opacity, or otherwise change position. There are four types of notes: Tap, Hold, Drag, and Flick, each requiring a different input when reaching the judgement line. [ref: 日常安利《Phigros》非定型音游~不安分的判定线, 3DMGAME] [ref: Phigrosの評価とアプリ情報 - ゲーム一覧, GAMEWITH]

Notes are judged as Perfect, Good, Bad, or Miss according to the timing of the player's input. Perfect or Good judgements increase the player's combo, while Bad or Miss judgements break it. [ref: Phigrosの評価とアプリ情報 - ゲーム一覧, GAMEWITH] The player's score is calculated from both their accuracy and their highest achieved combo. At the end of a play, the game displays the player's score, accuracy, judgement counts, highest combo, and a grade based on their score. [ref: Phigrosの評価とアプリ情報 - ゲーム一覧, GAMEWITH]

Unlike many rhythm games, Phigros features a dynamic judgement line and does not use fixed lanes. During gameplay, the judgement line can move, rotate, or disappear, requiring players to follow its position as notes approach it. The movement of the judgement line can also be incorporated into chart patterns and visual effects. [ref: 日常安利《Phigros》非定型音游~不安分的判定线, 3DMGAME] [ref: 「Phigros」官方宣传PV, bilibili]

== Development and publishing ==
Development of Phigros was started by Soullies, who was a teenager at the time. [ref: 因为“五块钱”捐款，一款免费发布且更新数年的独立游戏，被部分玩家冲了……, 搜狐] He subsequently assembled a team of rhythm game enthusiasts, which became Pigeon Games and continued development of the game. Pigeon Games distributes the game's songs without charging players individually for them and has released regular updates since the game's launch. [ref: 无广告又无内购！这款良心爆表的音游，却被玩家调侃为“屁股肉”……, 搜狐] The game has also released special charts for April Fools' Day.

The game's soundtrack primarily consists of electronic music and features compositions by numerous artists. These include composers who have participated in the BMS music competition The BMS of Fighters, as well as artists and labels such as SOUL NOTES. Phigros has also featured collaborations with other rhythm games, like Muse Dash. [ref: TGIF my friend. Drop everything you’re doing and get the new update!, Steam] Some charts incorporate references to their source material.

== Reception and community ==
Phigros has attracted a niche but active community. Following its release, the game appeared prominently on TapTap's "Hottest" rankings, and users on Bilibili have produced content featuring the game.

Reviews have highlighted the game's level design and its use of unconventional gameplay elements. Reviewers have praised the changes in gameplay and chart design for adding variety and surprise to individual songs. [ref: Phigrosをじっくり遊んで徹底レビュー！, スマホゲームCH] Other reviews have criticized the movement of gameplay elements for making charts more difficult to read and increasing their difficulty. [ref: [好游推荐] 快看，线条与指尖之舞, TapTap]

The game's visual presentation has also received attention. Reviews have praised its illustrations and their relationship to the themes of individual songs and charts. The soundtrack has similarly been highlighted for its variety and emphasis on electronic music.

The game's free-to-play model has also been discussed by reviewers. Some have described its lack of paid access to individual songs as lowering the barrier to entry, while other discussion has focused on the game's level-unlocking system. Some players regard unlocking charts as providing a sense of progression, while others have criticized it as limiting player choice.

Phigros's visual effects and interface have also influenced user-generated content on short-video platforms. In 2024, 36Kr reported on the use of effects inspired by Phigros in "beat-synced dance" videos on Douyin. [ref: 全网爆火的“卡点舞”，抖音竟然不是最大赢家？, 36Kr]

data.title: Wayne Ngan
data.text:
Move

Wayne Ngan (May 19, 1937 – June 12, 2020) was a Chinese Canadian ceramic artist and potter based on Hornby Island, British Columbia. [ref: Wayne Ngan, Telford, Toneff & Boyd Burial & Cremation Centres] He was known for his wood-fired stoneware and experimental glazes. [ref: Pottery by Wayne Ngan, Vancouver Art Gallery] Ngan also built his own kilns. He received the Saidye Bronfman Award in 1983 [ref: Wayne Ngan, Island Potter: A Portrait by a Friend, Luminare Press] and had a solo exhibition at the Vancouver Art Gallery in 1978.

== Early life and education ==

Ngan was born in Canton, China, [ref: Wayne Ngan — B.C. ceramics artist whose 'whole life is an art project' — has died, CBC] 19 May, 1937. In 1951, he immigrated to Canada. He lived with his grandfather on Mitchell Island near Vancouver, Canada. [ref: Richmond: Secrets & Surprises, Yorklin Associates]

He attended the Vancouver School of Art (now Emily Carr University of Art + Design). Ngan enrolled in the least expensive studio course, pottery. [ref: Wayne Ngan — Potter, Canadian Museum of History] Ngan worked at a shingle mill and later on sold homemade ceramic tea bowls to support himself. [ref: B.C. potter Wayne Ngan turned clay into objects of rare sculptural beauty, The Globe and Mail] He graduated in ceramics from Vancouver School of Art with honours in 1963. [ref: Obituary, Wayne Ngan: A life of magical art in ceramics and sculpture, Vancouver Sun] Ngan received the Marie E. Lambert Pottery Prize and the A.W. Tickle Memorial Award.

== Career ==

In 1967, Ngan moved to Hornby Island. There, he built a home and studio. He worked with Lloyd House to design his studio and kiln sheds. [ref: Builders of the Pacific Coast, Shelter Publications] Ngan's home included a firing studio, garden, sod roof and repurposed chicken coops into bedrooms. [ref: Towards a Good Fit, Architectural Design] At his home, he constructed three different kilns, for an array of firing techniques. He practiced hakeme, a hand-brushed decoration on pottery and salt-glazing.

Ngan utilized various techniques including raku, high-fired stoneware, salt glazing, and wood firing. He developed a ceramic practice that was closely connected to the island's landscape and materials. [ref: The Invisible Social Traces of Objects: Wayne Ngan's Ceramic Vessels, The Capilano Review] He experimented with local natural materials such as clays, ash glazes, seaweed, and driftwood. [ref: The Canadian Mantra: Reuse, Repurpose, and Recycle!, Studio Potter]

In 1978, Ngan lived in Japan for three months. He studied Japanese ceramic traditions with potter Yoichi Murakami. Ngan taught and led workshops on ceramics at different educational institutions in Canada and China. In 1984, after receiving a grant from Canada Council and inspiration from the Sung Dynasty, Ngan built a 300-cubic-foot wood-fired kiln.

In the beginning of the 2000s, Ngan spent more time on painting and sculptures.

== Work ==

Ngan's ceramics were functional and sculptural. [ref: The Doris Shadbolt Pottery Collection, Ceramics: Art and Perception] His work is associated with the West Coast ceramic movement influenced by Bernard Leach and Japanese pottery traditions. [ref: Thrown: British Columbia's Apprentices of Bernard Leach and Their Contemporaries, Morris and Helen Belkin Art Gallery] [ref: A Licence to Kiln, The Globe and Mail] Writer Joni Low described Ngan's vessels as restrained in form and emphasizing materiality and process over decoration. Ngan engaged directly with his materials and firing processes. He built and modified his own kilns and developed glaze formulas through experimentation with locally sourced materials.

Ngan's work was influenced by the pottery traditions of China, Korea, and Japan, particularly the work of Shoji Hamada. His techniques included salt glazing, wood firing and hakeme brushwork. He was also influenced by Sung dynasty ceramics.

Low and other commentators have noted that Ngan's house, garden, and workspaces on Hornby Island functioned together as part of his studio practice.

Artist and writer Amy Gogarty has argued that Ngan's work was distinguished by "his mastery of firing techniques and by his ability to integrate historical ceramic traditions with a distinctly regional West Coast vocabulary of materials and form".

== Recognition ==

In 1978, the Vancouver Art Gallery presented Pottery by Wayne Ngan, a solo exhibition curated by Doris Shadbolt. [ref: Pottery by Wayne Ngan, Vancouver Art Gallery] His work was later featured in the exhibition Thrown: British Columbia's Apprentices of Bernard Leach and Their Contemporaries, which examined the development of British Columbia studio pottery.

His work is held in the collections of the Morris and Helen Belkin Art Gallery at the University of British Columbia [ref: Search the Collection, Morris and Helen Belkin Art Gallery] and the Vancouver Art Gallery. [ref: Annual Report 2024, Vancouver Art Gallery] [ref: Highlights from the Collection, Vancouver Art Gallery] A collection of his pottery is on permanent display at the Canadian Museum of Civilization in Ottawa. [ref: Artists in Their Studios: Where Art is Born, TouchWood Editions]

In 1983, he received the Saidye Bronfman Award, for Canadian fine craft. In 2013, Ngan received the BC Creative Achievement Award of Distinction. [ref: B.C. Creative Achievement Awards honour artist Wayne Ngan, Georgia Straight]

== Personal life ==
Ngan married fellow artist, Anne Feveile in 1968. They had two children, Goya, and Gailan. The couple separated in 1983. Ngan had a third child in 1989, named Meris. He had 3 grandchildren.

Ngan died from lymphoma on June 12, 2020, at his home on Hornby Island.

== Posthumous exhibitions and legacy ==

In 2025, the New York gallery James Cohan presented the posthumous exhibition Wayne Ngan: Spirit and Form. [ref: Wayne Ngan: Contemplative Materialism and the Artifice of Presence, Ceramics Now] [ref: See Wayne Ngan, New York Magazine] Ngan's former studio continues to be maintained by his family and is open to visitors seasonally and by appointment. [ref: Contact, Wayne Ngan Studio]

== Selected exhibitions ==

* Pottery by Wayne Ngan, Vancouver Art Gallery, Vancouver (1978–79)
* Thrown: British Columbia's Apprentices of Bernard Leach and Their Contemporaries, Morris and Helen Belkin Art Gallery, Vancouver (2004)
* Wayne Ngan: Spirit and Form, James Cohan, New York (2025)

data.title: Mass Effect: Universe
data.text:
Mass Effect: Universe is the name associated with a cancelled Mass Effect video game developed by BioWare, Published by Electronic Arts (EA). The project, commonly referred to as Mass Effect 5, was announced in 2020 and cancelled on 21 October 2026 as EA announced the closure of BioWare. The name Mass Effect: Universe appeared in an internal trailer leaked after the cancellation, but had not been formally announced by EA as the game's final title. [ref: BioWare Update, BioWare Blog] [ref: A Convincing Trailer For What May Have Been Mass Effect 5 Has Leaked [UPDATE: It's Real], Kotaku]

The cancelled project was intended to continue the science-fiction role-playing series following 2017's Mass Effect: Andromeda. An internal cinematic trailer that surfaced online on 22 October 2026 included an appearance by Liara T'Soni, a character from the original trilogy. Its authenticity was corroborated by journalists at IGN and Bloomberg News. [ref: Leaked Mass Effect: Universe trailer gives a taste of what we're all missing, Ars Technica]

== Development ==
BioWare publicly revealed that a new Mass Effect game was in pre-production at The Game Awards 2020 in December 2020. The accompanying teaser included an N7 insignia, and gaming publications identified the figure at its conclusion as apparently being Liara T'Soni. The trailer ended with the statement that Mass Effect would continue; no release date or official title was announced. [ref: New Mass Effect Debuts At Game Awards, GameSpot] [ref: BioWare Double Feature at The Game Awards, BioWare Blog]

BioWare released further teasers during its annual N7 Day celebrations, including three short clips in November 2023. The studio said at the time that the game remained in pre-production. [ref: BioWare Is Teasing The Next Mass Effect With Cryptic Videos For N7 Day, GameSpot]

Following the release of Dragon Age: The Veilguard, BioWare announced in January 2025 that a smaller core team was working on the new Mass Effect game. The team included developers from the original trilogy, among them executive producer Mike Gamble, Preston Watamaniuk, Derek Watts and Parrish Ley. [ref: BioWare Studio Update, BioWare Blog] On 7 November 2025, Gamble reaffirmed that the game was in development and that BioWare and EA remained committed to the series. [ref: N7 Day 2025, Electronic Arts]

== Cancellation and closure of BioWare ==
On 21 October 2026, EA announced it would close BioWare and cancel development of the next Mass Effect game as part of a wider restructuring. Bloomberg News reported that the company planned to cut approximately 400 jobs, including around 50 positions at BioWare. According to an internal EA communication reported by the press, the company had decided not to proceed with the project, which it characterised as being in early development. [ref: Electronic Arts to Shed 400 Jobs, Shut Down BioWare to Cut Costs, Bloomberg News] [ref: RIP BioWare: EA shuts down storied RPG studio after over three decades, Ars Technica]

BioWare confirmed the decision in a statement on its website, saying that the studio was closing after more than three decades and that early development of the next Mass Effect project was ending.

== Leaked trailer ==
On 22 October 2026, a previously unreleased trailer for the cancelled game appeared on Reddit. It was labelled as in-engine material produced with pre-production assets by a small development team. Bloomberg journalist Jason Schreier confirmed that the footage was from the game BioWare had been developing before its closure. [ref: Mass Effect Universe trailer leaks online, showcases what BioWare was working on before being shut down, Video Games Chronicle]

The trailer depicts a former military officer meeting an asari in a bar and alludes to the character undertaking covert operations. It features a confrontation involving Liara T'Soni and ends with the title Mass Effect: Universe. Commentators described its apparent direction as resembling a spy thriller, although the footage did not establish the final scope, gameplay or story of the cancelled project.

== Public response ==
The cancellation and leaked trailer prompted criticism from fans and discussion about the future of the franchise. A petition using the hashtag #SaveMassEffect was launched following the studio's closure, asking EA to resume the franchise under another developer or license the intellectual property to another company. IGN reported on 23 October 2026 that the petition had surpassed 50,000 signatures; it later reported calls from some fans for a boycott of EA products. [ref: Save Mass Effect Petition Hits 50,000 Signatures, Just Days After BioWare Closure, IGN] [ref: Mass Effect Fans Call for EA Boycott as Petition to Save BioWare's Canceled Game Garners More than 75,000 Signatures, IGN]

data.title: Bou
data.text:
Bou (legal name Bou Oy) is a brand agency headquartered in Helsinki, Finland, with a second studio in London, United Kingdom. Founded in 2018, the company provides branding, marketing, communications and public relations, and web development services, and describes itself as a "brand company" working across those four disciplines from a single point of contact. [ref: About, Bou] Its clients have included Klarna, Rovio Entertainment, Polestar, and the mobile game developer Metacore. In addition to its in-house team, Bou operates a freelance network with over 10,000 creative freelancers.

== History ==
Bou Oy was incorporated on 21 February 2018 in Helsinki. [ref: Bou — yritystiedot, päättäjät, taloustiedot, Finder.fi] According to the company, its founding team previously worked together on the brand of Slush, the Helsinki-based technology and startup conference, which the company cites as the origin of its focus on fast-growing technology companies. [ref: ”Slush oli meille yrityskiihdyttämö” –Teknologiatapahtuman johtajisto perusti bränditoimiston viemään Suomea maailmalle, Kauppalehti]

The company operates a second office in London and describes an extended freelance network marketed under the name "Bou & Co." through which it engages outside creative freelancers for specialized briefs.

In 2023, Bou was named as one of Adweek’s Fastest Growing Agencies. [ref: Fastest Growing Agencies 2023:, Adweek] In 2024, was featured in the Financial Times FT1000 ranking of Europe's fastest-growing companies. [ref: FT 1000: the eighth annual ranking of Europe’s fastest-growing companies, Financial Times]

== Services ==
Bou organizes its work into four service areas:
* Marketing — brand and go-to-market strategy, campaign planning, and paid/organic growth marketing.
* Communications & PR — media relations and public relations campaigns, including product launches.
* Design — brand identity, visual and verbal identity systems, and creative production.
* Web development — websites and digital products for client brands.

The company also offers brand "launch" services for new products and companies, and connects clients with independent creative freelancers through Bou & Co.

== Notable work ==
Bou states it has worked with more than 200 brands across Europe and the United States. Publicly documented client work includes:

=== Klarna ===
Bou served as an extension of Klarna's public relations team between 2021–2023, covering media relations, spokesperson training, and content across lifestyle, technology, and business media. [ref: Case: Klarna, Bou]

=== Rovio Entertainment ===
Bou worked as Rovio's lead PR and communications agency between 2023–2025, working on ongoing media relations alongside major launches for the Angry Birds franchise. The agency's work has also covered Rovio's sustainability and diversity initiatives within the games industry, including an inclusive game-design guide that received trade press coverage. [ref: Case: Rovio, Bou]

=== Polestar ===
Bou has provided public relations and brand awareness support to Polestar, the Swedish electric-vehicle manufacturer. Work has spanned earned media, media training, and brand activations addressing sustainability, design, and technology themes, including pop-up brand experiences such as a snow-built showroom that received international press coverage. [ref: Case: Polestar, Bou]

=== Merge Mansion ===
Bou has worked with Helsinki and Berlin based game studio Metacore since its inception, beginning with brand positioning and global launch work for its mobile game Merge Mansion. Since the game's 2020 launch, Bou has contributed to creative advertising and user acquisition campaigns, as well as website design and development for the game's companion site. [ref: Case: Merge Mansion, Bou]

=== PolyAI ===
In 2025, Bou led a brand renewal for the London-based voice-AI company PolyAI, encompassing brand strategy, visual and verbal identity, and a new website. The engagement also included a launch campaign for the company's platform featuring chef Gordon Ramsay, which ran across digital, out-of-home, and television placements in the United States. [ref: Gordon Ramsay and PolyAI Call Out Customer Service That Doesn't Listen, LBB Online]

=== Slush ===
Bou's founding team led marketing, communications, PR, and design for the startup event Slush in 2016 and 2017. The work included Slush 2016's entrance banner, which gained wide social media attention, and a redesigned event website that the agency states sold out the event and received design awards. [ref: This Is How Finland Greets Visitors Who Dare to Brave Its Bitter Winter, [[Fortune (magazine)]

=== City of Helsinki ===
Bou has worked on multiple creative campaigns with the City of Helsinki’s marketing department, with the goal of increasing Helsinki’s appeal in the eyes of global tech talent. For example, during the Covid19 pandemic, the agency’s “Helsinki, home-delivered” campaign packaged physical items representing the various benefits that Helsinki offers – from a sports watch to communicate proximity to nature to an old Nokia phone to communicate work-life balance – into physical boxes that were shipped overseas to potential talent. [ref: How design is bringing new places to life, Creative Review]

data.title: Ali Adnan Haider Darwish Al-Zaabi
data.text:
Ali Adnan Haider Darwish Al-Zaabi, also known as Ali Al-Zaabi, is an Omani business executive. He is the founder and chief executive of Bin Haider Darwish L.L.C., a printing and design company in Muscat trading as BHD Group, registered under commercial registration 1334733 and operating since 2019. [ref: BHD Group: what a Muscat print house with CR 1334733 actually is, Muscat Courier]

He has been Head of Strategic Planning at the ITHCA Group since February 2025, and has served as secretary to the board of DataOm, the submarine-cable company under the same group, since October 2023. [ref: The print house, the cable company and the fencing board, Sooraseeb Dispatch] Before that he was Head of Business Environment at the Oman Vision 2040 Office from November 2021 to June 2023, where the public record attaches the Invest in Oman centre and work on the National Investment Strategy. Earlier roles were at Oman Broadband, Oman Aviation Group, EY and the Central Bank of Oman.

In November 2025 the Family Business Council Gulf named him to its 2025 Next Generation list; on the published record he is the only Omani individual on six years of the list, the other Omani entries being companies. [ref: The one Omani individual on six years of the FBCG Next Generation list, Oman Ledger] [ref: Awards – 2025, Next Generation, Family Business Council Gulf] He has been a member of the board of the Oman Fencing Committee since 2023. [ref: A printer on the national fencing board, Sooraseeb Dispatch] He is a co-founder of The Flower Bar, a floral business in Oman.

He was educated at The Sultan's School, then Brunel University London, where he took a BSc in Economics and Management and an MSc in Sustainability, Entrepreneurship and Design. He is a doctoral candidate in Innovation and Management at the University of Central Lancashire.

data.title: Topistar Di Congo
data.text:
----

Topistar Di Congo (born Biluge Birhakabulirwa Christophe; 5 May 2005) is a Congolese entrepreneur, creative director, and fashion designer based in Uganda. He is the founder of TDC Creatives, an organization that supports youth projects across media, music, and community development.

== Early life ==
Topistar Di Congo was born in Bukavu, Democratic Republic of the Congo. Following conflict in eastern DRC, his family relocated to the Kyaka II Refugee Settlement in Uganda. After serving as a youth leader in the settlement, he moved to Kampala, where he establisheds TDC Creatives.

== Family background ==
Topistar Di Congo is the ninth of ten children born to Juslain Birhakabulirwa Barhongo and Furah Badesire Kagayo Jusian. His father worked in education and business, while his mother worked in entrepreneurship and traditional medicine.

data.title: Paul Hallam
data.text:
----

Paul Hallam is a British DJ, film maker, publisher and former Mod Impresario.

Born in Staines, Middlesex, England in 1965, Hallam began his career as a professional Mod in 1983 aged 17 by dj'ing and promoting his RnB nights at Feltham Football Club and a Mod club called Sneakers, in Shepherds Bush. The Dj's were Hallam and Richard "Shirley" Early and is now fondly remembered as "the mod club" of the 1980s period. [ref: PAUL HALLAM - SNEAKERS, suityourself]

Later that year he launched his own fanzine Sense of Style - which was arguably the first professionally typeset and printed fanzine due to Hallam's day job in print and design.

In the latter part of the decade Hallam along with many others left the mod scene preferring the Jazz Revival scene which saw Hallam work as the resident dj at the world famous 100 for nearly 10 years. He was honoured with a photograph on the clubs wall of fame between Noel Gallagher and the Sex Pistols.

In the early 90s Hallam partly abandoned music for a career in politics. Running twice for Labour councilor in very Tory Cobham. He also made a speech at the Labour Party Conference of 1992 introduced by the then shadow home secretary Tony Blair. [ref: Paul Hallam speaking at The Labour Party Conference, 1992]

In 1997 at the height of Brit Pop Hallam dj'd and promoted 'Club Popcorn' along with fellow former mods Danny Decourtelle and Dave Edwards at the Oxford Street club. Other 100 Club events he was responsible for included the reformation gig of the Mod Revival band The Chords and the sold-out 20th anniversary Punk festival (which was ironically 21 years on after the original event) which saw The Buzzcocks, Subway and Perry return to the club for the first since the original festival.

Club Popcorn went on tour in the summer of 1998 playing seaside towns including Exmouth Pavilion where local band Muse were 3rd on the bill.

In 1999 Hallam became associate producer for the Save GLR campaign promoting the 2 night fund raising concerts at the 100 club which included Bez and Joe Strummer, Inspiral Carpets Hingley and Spizz Energi who would go on to work with Paul in the next decade.

Just before the turn of the millennium Hallam bought a 50% stake in the Northern Bohemian Velvet Rock Club in Teplice (Czech Republic).

In 2000 he fulfilled a lifetime ambition of owning his own London bar by opening the S.M.E.R.S.H. bar in the then, not quite so fashionable Shoreditch. Ran with fellow former mod Piller the bar sold eastern European drinks in a cold war style bunker.

BBC'S Big Read top 100 books of all time used SMERSH to film its James Bond piece in 2003 with Hallam providing the cold war narration for the TV show. Bizarre in the fact that Hallam had never read an Ian Flemming book.

Smersh is generally remembered as one of the first cool bars of Shoreditch.

Throughout the early 2000s Hallam worked on radio with the former Punk legend Spizz Energi including a residency on one of the pioneers of internet radio Soul 24-7 for almost two years before being sacked for "talking too much on air".

In 2003 he founded the company Filthy Lucre Limited with Decourtelle which purchased Filthy Macnastys pub in Islington - spiritual home of TheLibertines and former residence of Pete Doherty who worked as a barman there with Carl Barat. Filthys claimed to sell the second best Guinness In London.

In 2006 Filthy Lucre purchased the Gladstone in Borough.

Hallam guested on the Craig Charles show on BBC Radio 6 in 2005. The same year he guest DJ'd at the Isle of Wight festival - on the same bill as the Rolling Stones.

2013 saw Hallam launch Street sounds, music paper along with Bushell. It ran for 5 years and 17 issues. At one point being the biggest selling music paper in the UK.

Hallam retired from dj'ing in 2016 but nobody noticed so he returned in 2019 and retired for good to a sold-out venue in Brighton in the August bank holiday of that year.

In 2015 Hallam appeared on a TV show Street Sounds and Style, talking about 80s youth culture. Acclaimed photographer EwenSpencer was so impressed by Hallam's 80s photos his company SeeW published a book of Hallams 80s photos called Odds & Sods. [ref: Odds & Sods - Record Collector Magazine]

Numerous exhibitions followed in London, Italy, Spain and LA. Along with radio and TV appearances to promote it. [ref: Diving into the 1980s Mod Scene with Photographer Paul Hallam, VICE] [ref: Paul Hallam on Robert Elms, BBC London. Odds & Sods Book. 17 02 2016] [ref: Paul J Hallam, YouTube]

In 2015 Hallam was made a listed Londoner on the Robert Elms show on BBCRadioLondon. [ref: Paul Hallam as Robert Elms' Listed Londoner. BBC Radio London.] In the same year he launched Old Dog Books - a publishing house producing 21st century-pop-pulp-fiction in an attempt to recreate the excitement of the Pulp Fiction novels that so many grew up with like Richard Allens’ Skinhead books. Between 2015 and 2025 they published over 20 titles.

2022 Paul conceived Produced and appeared in the Documentary KICK OUT THE JAMS - The XFM Story. Featuring Ricky Gervais and Steve Merchant amongst others which premièred at Vue Cinema Shaftsbury Avenue and is currently available to watch on Amazon Prime.

Paul Lives in Cobham Surrey and supports MillwallFootballClub.

data.title: Ben McDonnell
data.text:
Ben McDonnell (born 1991 or 1992) is an American actor, podcaster, photographer and barrel racer. He is a contestant on The Traitors: New Blood, the 2026 all-civilian season of the NBC reality competition series The Traitors. [ref: 'The Traitors: New Blood' Expands 'Traitors' Fandom to NBC Viewers, NBCUniversal] He hosts the comedy podcast It's Ben A Week, which he launched in 2024. [ref: 'The Traitors: New Blood': Inside Ben McDonnell's Hidden Hollywood Past, TheThings]

== Early life ==
McDonnell was born in Maplewood, Minnesota. [ref: North Texan will compete for $250,000 on NBC's 'The Traitors: New Blood', Fort Worth Star-Telegram] He later moved to Los Angeles to pursue an acting career, training at The Groundlings and with acting coach Lesly Kahn.

== Career ==
=== Acting ===
One of McDonnell's first roles was in the 2015 Will Smith film Concussion. He went on to appear in a number of short films, and in episodes of The Bay, Class Act and What Would You Do?. He also appeared on The Ellen DeGeneres Show and The Late Late Show with James Corden.

McDonnell produced the 2019 miniseries Class Act and executive produced the short film Dear Dad (2018). He made his directing debut with the short film I (2016), an official selection of the Twin Cities Film Festival.

=== Podcasting ===
In 2024, McDonnell launched It's Ben A Week, a solo comedy podcast.

=== Photography ===
McDonnell works as a headshot, corporate and conference photographer in the Dallas–Fort Worth area, and has said his own experience as an actor shaped his approach to headshots. [ref: Meet Benjamin McDonnell, CanvasRebel]

=== The Traitors: New Blood ===
In August 2026, McDonnell was announced as one of 22 contestants on The Traitors: New Blood, the first American season of The Traitors cast entirely with non-celebrities, selected from more than 60,000 applicants. [ref: The Traitors: New Blood Introduces This Season's All-Civilian Cast, Bleeding Cool] Hosted by Alan Cumming and filmed in the Scottish Highlands, the season premiered on NBC on September 17, 2026. [ref: Meet the Cast of 'The Traitors: New Blood', TV Insider] [ref: How a barrel racer from North Texas plans to out-lie everyone on 'The Traitors', Dallas Observer] He competes as a Faithful. [ref: Your Guide to the Normies in 'The Traitors: New Blood' Cast, Yahoo Entertainment]

== Personal life ==
McDonnell lives in Granbury, Texas, where he competes in barrel racing. According to the Dallas Observer, he keeps around 70 animals.

data.title: HiringCafe
data.text:
----

HiringCafe is a United States-based job search engine that crawls the open web to discover jobs that are not widely promoted. [ref: HiringCafe lands $6.8M to fix the broken job hunt with AI talent agent, TheNextWeb] The service launched in December 2022 as a viral spreadsheet of mostly unpublicized jobs at tech startups, and was later upgraded to an actual search engine, and profiled by Business Insider for its use of ChatGPT to structure job data, and for positioning itself as an alternative to larger, recruiter-driven job boards. [ref: An ex-Meta engineer and Stanford Ph.D. student built a bot in a bid to take on big job sites and put the power in the hands of job seekers, Business Insider]

== History ==

=== 2022–2023: Origins ===
HiringCafe was created by former Meta engineer Ali Mir and Stanford Ph.D. student Hamed Nilforoshan. [ref: https://knight-hennessy.stanford.edu/people/hamed-nilforoshan-dardashti] Mir first maintained a public list of tech employers hiring during the late-2022 technology layoffs and, on 22 December 2022, released an initial directory of links to company career pages. [ref: A brief history and future roadmap of HiringCafe, LinkedIn] The site subsequently added an automated crawler that scanned corporate sites and used OpenAI models to generate short, structured summaries of job descriptions.

=== 2023–2025: Transition from side-project to working app ===
Coverage by Business Insider highlighted the platform’s use of ChatGPT to normalize unstructured postings. The product did not gain widespread popularity, but developed a niche following and a very active [https://www.reddit.com/r/hiringcafe/ user community on Reddit].

Later reporting stated that the creators used OpenAI’s API to process large volumes of listings taken directly from company websites, with claims of several million jobs analyzed. [ref: ChatGPT helps man scrape millions of jobs, leads to new hiring platform, India Today] [ref: Man scrapes 4.1 million jobs with ChatGPT, turns data into new hiring platform, India Today] According to these reports, HiringCafe's AI system was able to extract a lot of data from job descriptions that is usually presented as un-structured text (e.g., specific licensure or security clearance required, working hours and shifts, benefits and perks offered, etc., which are commonly mentioned in job description text, but not usually provided as standardized filterable data fields).

=== 2026: Funding and AI Agent ===
In 2026, HiringCafe raised a round of funding from investors, including Spark Capital and angel investors affiliated with ZipRecruiter and Indeed. [ref: HiringCafe Raises $6.8 Million Pre-Seed And Launches Free AI Talent Agent For Job Seekers, Pulse 2.0] At the same time, HiringCafe announced the launch of an AI agent, called "Talent Agent" that partially automates the process of finding relevant jobs.

== Positioning and Reception ==
While the platform is often lauded for its power and flexibility, reported limitations include a unintuitive user interface with an overwhelming amount of filtering functionality and a steep learning curve, as well as occasional duplicate or overlapping listings and the absence of some résumé-writing, career-advice, and application-automation features offered by other employment platforms. [ref: Best FlexJobs Alternatives To Find Relevant Tech Jobs]

Business Insider characterized HiringCafe as “a bot built to take on big job sites and put the power in the hands of job seekers,” focusing on its use of ChatGPT and its positioning relative to larger boards. The University of Southern California includes HiringCafe among job aggregators in guidance for graduating students, [ref: Job Search Guide for Graduating Students, USC Career Center] and Cornell University notes that some job-search sites (including HiringCafe) publish salary ranges as a filter and allow filtering by degree or major. [ref: Careers Beyond Academia: Creating Lists of Potential Employers, Cornell University Library Guides] Other notable Universities recommending HiringCafe to student job seekers include [https://students.tippie.uiowa.edu/tippie-resources/career-services/undergraduate-career-services/undergraduate-career-resources-0 University of Iowa], describing it as an “ultra-flexible job search engine”. Other institutions listing the service include the [https://customcareer.miami.edu/resources/hiring-cafe/ University of Miami], [https://careerservices.smumn.edu/resources/hiringcafe-job-search-board/ St. Mary's University], [https://www.umass.edu/humanities-arts/careers/resources/finding-jobs-and-internships University of Massachusetts Amherst], [https://careerhub.ufl.edu/blog/2025/01/07/19-job-boards-of-paid-global-early-career-opportunities-for-international-students-recent-grads/ University of Florida], and [https://cdi.ku.edu/technology University of Kansas]. Mashable likewise includes HiringCafe in its roundup of AI-enabled job-search tools, describing its extensive filter set and AI-based extraction of fields from postings. [ref: 11 AI tools to help with your job search, Mashable]

HiringCafe does not have any job advertising or recruiting products for employers, nor any paid subscriptions for job seekers, which are the typical ways that employment websites generate revenue. HiringCafe has been entirely funded by investors and venture capitalists, which means that their costs are subsidized and they are not yet a self-supporting business. This raises questions about the long-term viability of their stated commitment to eschew tactics that generate revenue but degrade the job seeker experience, such as promoting less relevant sponsored jobs, facilitating unsolicited outreach from recruiters, or charging job seekers directly. [ref: HiringCafe Raises $6.8M for AI Job Search Engine that Find the ‘Hidden’ 80% of Open Roles, citybiz]

data.title: Joseph Spiess Company
data.text:
Joseph Spiess Company, colloquially as Joseph Spiess, or just Spiess, was an American department store chain that was founded in 1921 in Elgin, Illinois, that went defunct in 1996.

== History ==

=== Founding and early history ===
Joseph C. Spiess founded the company in 1921 in Elgin, Illinois. The store in downtown Elgin would serve as the company's only store for decades.

=== Expansion ===
Spiess would open its first branch location at the Crystal Point Mall in Crystal Lake in 1976. [ref: MALL ISN’T GOING TO PIECES OVER SPIESS, Chicago Tribune] It would open another one at St. Charles Mall in St. Charles in 1979. [ref: ST. CHARLES’ PUZZLING FLOP, Chicago Tribune] In 1984, Spiess permanently shuttered its flagship store in Elgin to relocate it at the Spring Hill Mall in West Dundee and Carpentersville that same year. [ref: Old Spiess store falls so new Elgin can rise, Chicago Tribune] Spiess then opened its final branch store in 1988 at the Randhurst Mall in Mount Prospect. [ref: SPIESS, MAINSTREET TO CONSTRUCT STORES AT RANDHURST CENTER, Chicago Tribune]

=== Demise ===
Due to excessive debt from overexpansion, Spiess filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in December 1991 [ref: RETAILER SPIESS FILES FOR CHAPTER 11, Chicago Tribune]. The Chapter 11 bankruptcy then converted to Chapter 7, but the company was shortly then acquired by Maurice L. Rothschild. Spiess gradually closed their stores at Randhurst in 1992, Spring Hill Mall in 1994, and St. Charles in 1995. Spiess permanently closed their final store at Crystal Lake in 1996, ending the chain.

The former Spiess flagship store in downtown Elgin was demolished in 2005. The empty land was cleared for a $44 million residential and retail revitalization project named Fountain Square on the River, which built 190 condominiums across two eight-story buildings alongside 20 luxury townhouses overlooking the Fox River. [ref: Old Spiess store falls so new Elgin can rise, Chicago Tribune]

== Locations ==

* Elgin (flagship store): Opened in 1921, closed in 1984
* Crystal Point Mall, Crystal Lake: Opened in 1976, closed in 1996
* St. Charles Mall, St. Charles: Opened in 1979, closed in 1995
* Spring Hill Mall, West Dundee and Carpentersville: Opened in 1984, closed in 1994
* Randhurst Mall, Mount Prospect: Opened in 1988, closed in 1992

data.title: Dan Priddy
data.text:
Dan Priddy is a songwriter, record producer and multi-instrumentalist based in London. He has worked with Rag'n'Bone Man, Bastille, Mika, James Arthur and Louis Tomlinson, frequently collaborating with producer Mark Crew. [ref: Abbey Road Amplify: The Craft of Hitmaking, Abbey Road] [ref: FM Premiere: Dan Priddy's Dopamine, Fame Magazine] He co-founded Best Laid Plans Records with Crew and Bastille singer Dan Smith. [ref: 'We're open to anything': Bastille's Dan Smith on his Best Laid Plans label, Music Week] His songwriting and production credits also include recordings by Shania Twain and Ashnikko. [ref: Queen of Me — Shania Twain: credits, Qobuz] [ref: Deal With It (feat. Kelis) by Ashnikko — Credits, Muso.AI]

== Career ==

=== Early work ===
Priddy began playing piano and singing at the age of six, later learning drums, bass and guitar. He initially worked with his brother Reuben under the name Mannequin, developing songs and production with J. R. Rotem and Zach Katz. He focused on songwriting and production while at university, where he met Crew.

=== Best Laid Plans and Rag'n'Bone Man ===
Priddy, Crew and Smith established Best Laid Plans Records to develop and release music by artists they knew. The label released Rag'n'Bone Man's Wolves and Disfigured, followed by his 2017 album Human in partnership with Columbia Records. Other artists associated with the label included Rationale, Kianja, the Dawn of May and Akine.

Priddy worked with Crew on the development of Rag'n'Bone Man's early recordings. According to Abbey Road's profile, he contributed to ten songs on Human and four songs on the 2021 album Life by Misadventure. He co-wrote "Anywhere Away from Here", a duet by Rag'n'Bone Man and Pink. [ref: Anywhere Away from Here (Rag'n'Bone Man & P!nk) — Credits, Muso.AI]

His later work with Rag'n'Bone Man included co-writing and co-producing "Rush of Blood", "Feeding All These Fires" and "Put a Little Hurt on Me" for the 2024 album What Do You Believe In?. [ref: What Do You Believe In? — Rag'n'Bone Man: credits, Qobuz]

=== Bastille and other collaborations ===
Priddy became a regular songwriting and production collaborator of Bastille alongside Crew. [ref: Bastille's Dan Smith On Technological Mania & The "Totally Bizarre" Timing Of Their New Album, 'Give Me The Future', Grammy.com] His production work includes "Doom Days" and "Another Place" from the band's 2019 album Doom Days. [ref: Dan Priddy, Eaves Music Group] On Give Me the Future (2022), he co-produced "Thelma + Louise", "No Bad Days" and "Stay Awake?", and co-wrote "No Bad Days". [ref: Give Me the Future — Bastille: credits, Qobuz]

In 2019, Priddy worked with Crew on Mika's My Name Is Michael Holbrook. Reviewing the album for PopMatters, Brice Ezell discussed their production of "Platform Ballerinas" and "Tomorrow", praising the clarity of the arrangements while finding parts of the album's production overly polished. [ref: Mika Delivers Undeniably Catchy Hooks on 'My Name Is Michael Holbrook', PopMatters]

Priddy co-wrote and co-produced "Brand New" and "Best Friend" on Shania Twain's 2023 album Queen of Me. He also worked with Birdy on Portraits, which she described as a project made with a small group of collaborators including Priddy and Crew. [ref: Birdy — Interview, Bedroomdisco] His production credits include Lovejoy's 2023 single "Call Me What You Like". [ref: Call Me What You Like by Lovejoy — Credits, Muso.AI]

In 2025, Priddy was credited as a producer on Maddie Zahm's "Sheets" and Tom Grennan's "Somewhere Only We Go". His contributions to the latter also included drums, guitar, keyboards and programming. [ref: Sheets — Maddie Zahm: credits, AllMusic] [ref: Somewhere Only We Go — Tom Grennan: credits, Qobuz]

=== Solo recordings ===
Priddy previously released music under the name Braque, including the EP V1CES. [ref: Surfacing: Dan Priddy's Demonstrates His Pop Chops On Debut Single 'Dopamine', Faded Glamour] In June 2019, he released "Dopamine" under his own name. Fame Magazine reported that he wrote, produced, mixed and mastered the recording himself. He released the single "liar" on 19 June 2026 through Enzino Records. [ref: liar — Dan Priddy, Amazon Music]

data.title: Jaijit Bhattacharya
data.text:
Jaijit Bhattacharya is an Indian technology policy researcher, author and entrepreneur. He was recognized by MIT Sloan Management Review India in its Policy 50 list, Which highlights 50 influential leaders, thinkers and policymakers shaping India digital economy and technology policy. He is the president of the [https://c-dep.org Centre for Digital Economy Policy Research] and has previously held positions at the World Economic Forum and KPMG. [ref: Jaijit Bhattacharya, MIT Sloan Management Review Middle East] His work has focused on technology, governance, digital transformation and technology policy, including the coining of the terms "Digital Colonization" and "Technological Sovereignty". [ref: ICANN announces digital policy expert Jaijit Bhattacharya as ccNSO Council member, ETGovernment]

== Career ==

Bhattacharya is the president of the [https://c-dep.org Centre for Digital Economy Policy Research]. He has worked in technology, consulting and public policy. He served as a partner in the Economics and Policy Practice at KPMG India.

During his tenure at KPMG, Bhattacharya worked on infrastructure, government services, regulatory policy and urban development. [ref: Why smart cities need smarter urban governance model, Business Standard] He later headed the Centre for the Fourth Industrial Revolution in India at the World Economic Forum.
[ref: ICANN announces Dr. Jaijit Bhattacharya, President C-DEP.org as ccNSO Council member, PTI]

In 2015, the Government of India established an expert committee to examine ways to reduce the number of regulatory permissions required by businesses. Bhattacharya, then a partner at KPMG, was appointed as a member of the committee. [ref: Government sets up panel to reduce permissions for investors, The Economic Times]

In 2024, he became a member of the Country Code Names Supporting Organization (ccNSO) Council of the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN). ICANN lists his term as running from March 2024 to October 2027 and identifies his areas of expertise as technology policy, multilateral negotiations and artificial-intelligence frameworks. [ref: Council Members, Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers]

The committee considered replacing multiple prior approvals with a simplified regulatory process. Bhattacharya supported simplifying business regulations and removing redundant legislation. [ref: India Inc petitions govt: From land laws to levy, ease it all, The Indian Express]

Bhattacharya also participated in policy discussions on smart cities and infrastructure. During his time at KPMG, he publicly discussed governance and institutional issues related to India's smart-cities programme.

In 2026, Bhattacharya advocated greater international cooperation between India and other governments in addressing cybersecurity threats. [ref: India needs to collaborate with other governments on cyber threats: C-DEP President, Asian News International]

== Academic and research ==

Bhattacharya received a Bachelor of Technology degree in electrical engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur and an MBA from the Indian Institute of Management Calcutta. He later received a PhD in computer science and engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi.

Bhattacharya has also conducted training at the Asian Development Bank Institute in Tokyo on public expenditure management. [ref: Jaijit Bhattacharya, Finnacle Capital Advisors]

In 2013, Bhattacharya co-authored a paper published in "PLOS Medicine" examining the use of rapidly deployable eHealth centres for healthcare delivery and data collection in rural India. [ref: Integrating Health Care Delivery and Data Collection in Rural India Using a Rapidly Deployable eHealth Center, PLOS Medicine]

Bhattacharya's work has addressed the concepts of "Digital Colonization" and "Technological Sovereignty". MIT Sloan Management Review Middle East credits him with coining both terms. ETGovernment has also credited him with coining the terminology.

In 2010, Bhattacharya published Technology Standards: A Route to Digital Colonization in the IETE Journal of Education. The paper examined the relationship between information and communications technology standards, public policy and dependence on particular technologies. [ref: Technology Standards: A Route to Digital Colonization, IETE Journal of Education]

His subsequent policy work and commentary have continued to address technological sovereignty and questions concerning domestic technological capabilities, technology standards and dependence on foreign technologies.

Bhattacharya has written books and academic and policy articles concerning e-governance and technology policy.

His books include e-Gov 2.0: Policies, Processes and Technologies, published by McGraw Hill Education in 2010. [ref: e-Gov 2.0: Policies, Processes and Technologies, McGraw Hill Education]

Bhattacharya's research publications include Technology Standards: A Route to Digital Colonization in the IETE Journal of Education and the co-authored Integrating Health Care Delivery and Data Collection in Rural India Using a Rapidly Deployable eHealth Center in PLOS Medicine.

== Awards and recognition ==

Bhattacharya has received the APJ Abdul Kalam Award for Innovation in Governance.

He has also received the Global Corporate Affairs Leadership Award for a decade of contribution. [ref: Corporate Affairs Leadership Award, World CSR Congress]

data.title: Crisis Connect
data.text:
Crisis Connect is a free, open-source, offline-first disaster communication application developed by Emirhan Duman for Android and iOS. [ref: İnternetsiz Afet İletişimi: Türk Liseli Geliştiriciden Bluetooth Tabanlı Uygulama Crisis Connect!, ShiftDelete.Net] It supports internet-based communication when connectivity is available and direct Bluetooth messaging between nearby devices when internet access or cellular networks are unavailable. [ref: Dank Emirhans (17) Erfindung bleiben Katastrophen-Opfer verbunden, 20 Minuten]

== Development ==
The project was inspired by communication outages during the 2023 Turkey–Syria earthquakes. Duman, a high school student in Istanbul, began developing it in April 2025. [ref: Teen's Disaster Messaging App Can 'Hop' Across Bluetooth When Cellular Networks Collapse, Good News Network] By September 2026, the application was available for Android and iOS. Its source code is published on GitHub under the GNU Affero General Public License version 3. [ref: Crisis Connect, GitHub]

== Features ==

=== Messaging and calls ===
Crisis Connect supports direct Bluetooth communication between nearby devices. The project's documentation lists text messaging, voice notes, image and file transfers, and real-time voice calls between Android and iOS devices. When internet access is available, the application supports end-to-end encrypted messaging and one-to-one voice and video calls over an internet connection.

=== Contacts and message relay ===
Contacts can be added by scanning a QR code or using a short-code pairing process with a nearby device. A relay mode allows messages to pass through intermediate phones running the application when the recipient is outside direct Bluetooth range. The relay feature is disabled by default to conserve battery. Users need to install and configure the application before an outage.

=== SOS and response coordination ===
The application includes SOS broadcasts and location sharing for emergency communication. [ref: News Bulletin of 19 October 2026, 3pm, 919 FM] Its documentation also describes a separate response-team module with role-based access, agency channels and live location sharing during operations.

=== Offline tools ===
Additional tools listed by the project include maps that can be downloaded before an outage, a compass, an emergency whistle and a survival guide with checklists. [ref: About Crisis Connect, Crisis Connect]

Bluetooth range varies with hardware, obstacles and interference. The application is intended to supplement established emergency communication systems.

data.title: Backrooms in real life
data.text:
If you've ever heard of the backrooms, you'll find yourself asking one question. "Could this exist in real life?". As of now, we don't believe so, but does that mean no? It's tough to say for sure, but I believe it could very well happen.

There are theories about how it was made, and one stands out. "The threshold". A machine made by aSync that created the backrooms. So? It's just a machine, we could make it, right? Well, Not quite, it uses up super amounts of energy to run. But, with power plants, we could make the energy needed. There's nothing stating how to build a Threshold machine, but humans have made Sci-Fi real. We've mapped a fruit fly's brain, we can make proteins and neurons, we've sent Rovers to things the ancient Romans looked up at and only ever dreamed, we have made Gene editors, we've made AI which speeds up many processes. So, who's to say we Cant make the backrooms? Well, that's up to you to decide, and maybe, together, we could make The Backrooms.

data.title: The Revolutionary Computer Union
data.text:
----

==Overview==
The Revolutionary Computer Union is a fictional country first started in the
video game roblox by a user named "[https://computerunion.miraheze.org/Nooblord Nooblord]". The base of TRCU was The Soviet Union

==History==
The Computer Union was born from the collapse of the [https://computerunion.miraheze.org/Trolls_Imper%C3%A1torskaya Trolls Imperátorskaya]imperial government. The imperial government was considered greedy and corrupt. Families were starving, workers were unhappy, and children shivered during the harsh winters. It was a country with no future, led by a ruler with no compassion, who mercilessly struck down anyone who dared to oppose him, a grim fate.

However, this regime was not destined to last. The people had had enough, and they raised their Union's flag in a triumphant revolt led by the first dictator, Nooblord. With the help of Dary and others, the sparks of revolt soon became a blazing inferno that ended this era of oppression. The revolution turned violent, battles were fought, and the imperialist trolls were eventually defeated. The Tsarina and Tsar were found dead in their home shortly afterward, and their regime quickly fell. Because of this, many raider groups were then created to bring back the tyrannical, imperialist regime, such as: The New Checkerslovakian Empire, Mug Rebellion Group, Russian raiders and many more. The most notable event that involved these groups was the 1962 Fanta Revolution. In 1945, Dictator Nooblord founded the Revolutionary Computer Union as an independent communist country. Ever since then, the Revolutionary Computer Union has only grown stronger.

==Important People in TRCU==
====Nooblord====

Nooblord also know as Nooblordjjj was the first dictator of The Revolutionary Computer Union from 1945 to 1952, when he was assassinated on September 20, 1952 (2024), during a speech to the PC Communist Party members alongside other important political figures at the age of 73.

Nooblord was born somewhere in the year 1879 and led his revolution in the 1920s, for it to then bloom into the second most powerful superpower on Earth, built out of slavery and corruption with an authoritarian administration for its prisoners (citizens) and harsh relations with the outside world, with a bloodthirst for power and territorial extension.

Amongst all the members that were handpicked by his hand, he was seen as a figure of power and peace, and death and war for others (the second being the most common one.) A hero, for some. But one that nearly led to nuclear annihilation for humanity almost made people have to hide in fallout bunkers.

During his time as a strict Dictator, most changes were made for his benefit. Such as his own military branch dedicated entirely to his protection and the protection of his fellow government members. Even though nothing was enough to stop his death, he knew once it arrived it would lead to the darkest pits of hell opening to swallow him whole, and he tried everything to hold back its death, the fear of something that for many was unknown but for him was obvious: what awaited beyond the line between life and death.

He pushed his best scientists, engineers, and generals all together to arrange everything to slow it down, but someone else knew the monster he had raised in his eyes. With fame and love in the air, she stepped closer and soon exploded with a can of Fanta, leaving a bloodshed over the PCCP people on the stage, vice versa of what many had lived through during 7 years of his regime.

Ironically, what Nooblordjjj had thought of as "the solution to the derailment of humanity and mankind" and the opposite of the regimen he had once lived in turned into what he had once sworn to destroy.

====90gq31====
90gq31, well known for being the former Minister of Foreign Relations, the former Head of the Central Committee and a former Government Member, also the current Dictator of the whole of TRCU. 90gq31 joined TRCU on 2024/05/11. Just 3 days later, he joined a famous, now defunct division called Spedsnaz. After the division was disbanded, he decided to join the CGB.

He assisted in the founding of the Ministry of Foreign Relations. After nearly 9 months, he became the Minister of Foreign Relations and a Cheaper Government member. He was also the former Commandant of L.E.M.O.N., eventually retiring.

On 2025/08/06, 90gq31 became a member of Government, as he had proven himself to have been a competent and fair TRCU figure. As Government, 90gq31 was able to reform many things, such as the Inspector Corp, as well as implement new policies, such as allowing TRCU members to attain the rank of PCCP via boosting any TRCU affiliated server, rather than just the main server. 90gq31 retired from The Computer Union on 2026/01/18.

On 2026/02/20, following the sellout of TRCU and the creation of TRCU, 90 was reinstated to his former Government position and he’s currently serving as one of the two Chairmen in TRCU.

V0id1z was killed by a suicide bomber and appointed 90 as the new Dictator.

====V0id1z====
V0id1z was the actual dictator of TRCU, he first joined the Computer Union on 03/19/2024. From there on he had worked his way up to an officer, developer, Government Member, and Dictator.
void1z was and still is one of the best TRCU developers. He made a huge contribution to the development of the Papers Pls game. He built many models and helped with many construction projects. In general, he is an ideal developer and scriptwriter; God must have given him to us for some merit. He made a huge contribution to the development of the long-awaited City update. Void1z also created the original TRCU Utilities bot (later mostly replaced by Garry (Garry was killed and TRCU Utilities is used again)), which helped organize the union and simplify the ranking process in TGRA. On the 24th of September 2025, in recognition of his work towards the betterment of the Union, he was officially granted the newly established role of Lead Developer by Sevs.
He frequently hosted battle and defense trainings, granting him newfound appreciation from the community. As void1z continued working on the Papers Pls game, more and more people started believing he was worthy of becoming a member of the Government. However, the existing government was not enthusiastic about this, likely because of void1z's frequent shenanigans, such as conducting gang wars (2BB vs. Lemitsia) and leading the Borsh Militia (raider group). However, due to his popularity, a campaign for his appointment as a Government member was created. This campaign had no significant results, resulting in v0id1z's retirement on 10/5/25 (10/5/61) because he felt "like a slave to the union."

His retirement triggered mass strikes and protests, which eventually resulted in him being finally appointed as a Government member. However, this incident resulted in his bot, "TRCU Utilities," being replaced by a new bot created by Motak which has made its return after Motaks demotion. In the present, void1z has returned to work on Papers Pls and is assisting in the management of the Great Computer Union.

On February 20th, after Sevs decided to sell the entire community to a corporate conglomerate, Void1z nuked the TCU discord server to save the reputation and established a new one, called The Revolutionary Computer Union. He titled himself as dictator and caused a significant portion of the playerbase to move to this new discord server in support.

Void1z died on May 28th, 1963 during an Army Inspection After LoathsomeBreadEater revealed he had a Fanta bomb strapped onto his chest and exploded the stage, killing Void1z instantly.

===Lookr1se===
Look_r1se is a former dictator of the Revolutionary Computer Union and its puppet states. He succeeded Nooblord as dictator following his death in October 2024 (1952 in the game's lore). He was succeeded at the date 24/3/25 by Newblord, the son of Nooblord. Look_r1se is best known for his declaration of war on the United Republic of Man. Now he is banned from TRCU due to being on the RO-cleaner list.

Look_r1se joined TRCU on the 9th of September, 1952. From there he rose through the ranks of the Glorious Robot Army and became an architect serving the glorious union.

On the 19th of June, 1952 (time works confusingly in TRCU), Look_r1se was appointed as Field Marshal following Olimusy's retirement. From there he led the Glorious Robot Army through various trials and tribulations until his promotion to dictator.

Following Nooblord's death on the 21st October, 1952, Look_r1se became the second ever dictator of The Computer Union. His justification for this was simple: nooblord stated minutes before his death that his successor would be the Field Marshal. Following this r1se appointed J.Mistro, a General in The Glorious Robot Army, as the next Field Marshal. In his reign as Dictator, the following events occurred.

1. Melody retired and then came back.
2. Sevs, Crefeated, and Craftico all became government members.
3. Disbandment of SCAR and creation of the 2nd Bulldog Brigade (now the 2nd Bulldog Brigade).
4. Mistro's career as FM.
5. Bose appointed as FM, Zeni demoted.
6. War declaration on URM.
7. Nearly abolishing Fanta from the game

====Sevhs1===-
Sevhs1 also know as sevs became a part of TRCU as a scientist in September 2023. His life within The Computer Union took a big turn when he joined the CGB. In this position, he was very much involved in moderation, banning numerous members, including Narze. He rose through the ranks, consistently contributing to moderation both within the Papers Pls Roblox game and on Discord which gave him a good reputation.

Upon becoming a CGB HICOM, Sevhs1 initiated and implemented heavy reforms that are credited with shaping the CGB into its current effective state. His influence in moderation continued to grow, and following tomislav2016's removal, he was appointed to the Directorate. As the Director, he assumed responsibility for overseeing nearly all aspects of moderation within TRCU. A few months after becoming Director, he also took over the Central Committee.

Sevhs1 is also recognised as one of the founders of the Airforce. Later, he became a Government member, where he focused on resolving conflicts within the community. On May 17th, 2025, he was appointed as the Chairman of TRCU. Sevhs1 has retired from his position as the Director of CGB as of the 12th of September, 2025. Sevhs1 served as the Director for 1 year and 1 day.

==Countries in TRCU Universe==
https://computerunion.miraheze.org/w/index.php?curid=2596 acording the map there only a few contryies are importnat to TRCU
====United Republic of Man====
The United Republic of Man (URM) is a democratic and capitalist nation and also a parody of United States. It is the TRCU's greatest enemy and is the leader of FATO (Freedom Accord Treaty Organisation), an alliance of democratic capitalist states with the TRCU verse. The URM also has a border game similar to Passport Pls, known as Purely Capitalism.The URM was founded by dissidents from TRCU, led by millz91. Their first president was Friedtriangle, who helped guide the nation through its early years, although he was eventually removed by the CMIA. A principal reason for the growth of the URM was a now-removed post made in the TRCU announcements channel promoting the group so that it could become a competition to the TRCU.
