data.title: Vatthe Conservation Park
data.text:
The Vatthe Conservation Park, also called the Vatthe Conservation Area, is a community-managed protected area on the north coast of Espiritu Santo, the largest island of Vanuatu. It lies at Big Bay in Sanma Province and covers about of lowland forest on alluvial soils and raised limestone. The area was established in 1994 and in June 2004 became the first conservation area registered under Vanuatu's Environmental Management and Conservation Act 2002. It has been on Vanuatu's tentative list for World Heritage status since 1 October 2004. [ref: Vatthe Conservation Area, UNESCO World Heritage Centre] [ref: Protected Area Management in Vanuatu, Macquarie Journal of International and Comparative Environmental Law]

== History ==
The name Vatthe means "eye of the sea" in the local language. The idea of protecting the area followed biodiversity surveys carried out in 1993 by the Vanuatu Environment Unit and the Royal Forest and Bird Protection Society of New Zealand, which recorded the birds of the area. In the same year Anthony H. Whitaker surveyed the reptiles of Vanuatu, and a decade later Philippe Keith surveyed the fish of the Matantas River.

In 1994 the Vatthe Conservation Area Project was launched with funding from the South Pacific Biodiversity Conservation Programme, administered by the South Pacific Regional Environment Programme. A land dispute between the traditional owners meant that the project initially had little community support; in 1995 the two families settled the dispute and abandoned plans to log the area. In 1996 the communities formed a joint Conservation Area Community Committee.

The project provided training so that the villages could manage the area themselves, and it funded infrastructure including solar lighting, a water well, improved sanitation and radio-telephone links. Local guides were trained and a handicrafts centre and tourist bungalows were completed in 1997.

Vatthe was registered in June 2004 under the Environmental Management and Conservation Act 2002, the first conservation area to be registered under that act, and registration required the communities to prepare a conservation management plan. Vanuatu submitted the area to the World Heritage tentative list on 1 October 2004, under criteria (vii), (ix) and (x).

Several other Vanuatu sites appear on the tentative list: Yalo, Apialo and the sacred geography of north-west Malakula; the wreck of the liner, sunk in 1942; Lake Letas; and the Nowon and Votwos site on Ureparapara. [ref: Vanuatu, UNESCO World Heritage Centre] Chief Roi Mata's Domain was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2008.

== Geography and geology ==

The park lies on the north coast of Espiritu Santo at Big Bay. It extends west to the Jordan River, one of the largest rivers in Vanuatu, and south across the bay's black sand beach and the Matantas River, reaching four kilometres inland to the top of a raised limestone cliff above sea level.

Espiritu Santo covers and is volcanic in origin, with a mountain range along its west coast rising to Mount Tabwemasana at, the highest point in the country. [ref: Espiritu Santo] The island lies close to the boundary of the Australian and Pacific plates, and uplifted coral terraces occur along many parts of its coastline; uplift rates of between 2 and 6 mm a year have been measured, the highest on the west coast. [ref: Human–climate–environment interactions in Espiritu Santo, Vanuatu during the past millennium, Frontiers in Earth Science]

UNESCO gives the area as; a study of protected-area management in Vanuatu gives of lowland alluvial rainforest. A later project description gives of lowland forest. The World Heritage nomination states that the area contains the only extensive alluvial and limestone forest left in Vanuatu, and the National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan describes it in similar terms.

Vanuatu has a tropical climate with a warm, wet season from November to April and a cooler, dry season from May to October. Annual average temperatures are between. Tropical cyclones occur between November and April. [ref: Current and future climate of Vanuatu, Vanuatu Meteorology and Geo-Hazards Department / Pacific Climate Change Science Program]

The park lies in the Vanuatu rain forests ecoregion, which covers more than eighty islands of volcanic or uplifted limestone origin. [ref: Vanuatu Rainforests, One Earth] The mountainous interior of the island forms the Santo Mountain Chain Key Biodiversity Area, one of 27 in the country, designated for species including the endangered Santa Cruz ground dove and mountain starling; the park itself lies on the coastal lowlands below it. [ref: Key Biodiversity Areas factsheet: Santo Mountain Chain, Key Biodiversity Areas Partnership]

== Flora and fauna ==
UNESCO describes the vegetation as falling into seven broad plant communities: alluvial plain forest, species-rich forest, species-poor Namatal forest with Kleinhovia hospita, nakatambol forest with Dracontomelon vitiense, bin-tri forest of Antiaris toxicaria, swamp forest, coral limestone forest, savanna and the riparian vegetation of the Jordan River. Some 265 species of trees, shrubs, palms and vines with traditional uses have been identified in the area. The species-rich forest is dominated by melektri (Antiaris toxicaria).

=== Mammals ===
Three caves in the park serve as roosts for bats. Five species have been recorded: two fruit bats, the Pacific flying fox and the Vanuatu flying fox (Pteropus anetianus), and three insectivorous bats, the Temminck's trident bat (Aselliscus tricuspidatus), the fawn leaf-nosed bat (Hipposideros cervinus) and the little bent-wing bat (Miniopterus australis). The Vanuatu flying fox is endemic to the country. [ref: Vanuatu National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan, Government of Vanuatu / Convention on Biological Diversity]

=== Birds ===
[[File:Forster Zosterops flavifrons.jpg|thumb|upright|Zosterops flavifrons, the Vanuatu white-eye, painted by Georg Forster in the 1770s]]
A survey by the Royal Forest and Bird Protection Society of New Zealand in 1993 recorded 48 of the 74 species of land and freshwater birds known from Vanuatu in the area. Six of Vanuatu's nine endemic land birds are known from the forest. The World Heritage nomination lists the Vanuatu imperial pigeon (Ducula bakeri), the Vanuatu megapode (Megapodius layardi), the Vanuatu white-eye (Zosterops flavifrons), the Tanna fruit dove (Ptilinopus tannensis) and the New Hebrides honeyeater (Phylidonyris notabilis). The buff-bellied monarch (Neolalage banksiana), the only bird genus endemic to Vanuatu, is common in the park.

Vanuatu's National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan, a separate national source, gives a partly different list: it names the globally endangered Santa Cruz ground dove (Pampusana sanctaecrucis) along with the Vanuatu megapode, the royal parrotfinch and the Vanuatu kingfisher. The megapode, known locally as the namalaus, is listed as a priority species in the IUCN megapode action plan because of habitat loss and over-exploitation.

=== Reptiles ===
Whitaker's 1993 study of Vanuatu's reptiles found 10 of the 12 reptile species recorded on Espiritu Santo in the park. Three are endemic: Cryptoblepharus novohebridicus, Emoia nigromarginata and Emoia sanfordi, out of six endemic reptiles known from Vanuatu.

=== Fish ===
Keith's 2003 survey of the Matantas River recorded 21 of the 62 freshwater fish species known from Vanuatu, three of them endemic. These include Schismatogobius vanuatuensis and species of Microphis and Stenogobius that were still awaiting description; the survey also recorded 13 species of crustaceans, and Keith considered the whole Jordan River catchment important for freshwater biodiversity. His paper in the Journal of Fish Biology sets out the biology of the amphidromous gobies that these fish belong to. [ref: Biology and ecology of amphidromous Gobiidae of the Indo-Pacific and the Caribbean regions, Journal of Fish Biology]

== Local communities ==
The land belongs to traditional families living in the Sara and Matantas villages near the park. The forest supplies them with food, building materials, medicine and sites for customary ceremony, and the conservation area holds many tabu sites. Families harvest nangai nuts (Canarium indicum) and bin-tri seeds, which they sell in local markets, and black beans are also harvested for sale. [ref: Invasive vine control to protect bio-cultural and economic values in lowland forest in Vatthe Conservation Area, United Nations Development Programme, Small Grants Programme]

One of the bat caves is tabu and may be entered only by the high chief of Matantas after a customary ceremony. Local tradition holds that the forest is guarded by Alawuro, a snake spirit who lives in a cave in the limestone cliff above it, sees everything that happens in the bay and rides to the villages on a white horse to warn them when he is displeased. The nomination records that villagers credit him with having kept the forest from being cleared.

== Management ==
The Conservation Area Community Committee, formed in 1996, manages the area with the villages. The conservation management plan required at registration prohibits the killing of certain species while permitting limited hunting of others. Local monitors oversee all harvesting and can impose fines or order community service, and persistent offenders can be taken to court. The plan also allows most traditional uses of the forest to continue, including the collection of medicinal plants and timber for canoes, firewood and houses.

Vatthe was the first conservation area registered under the Environmental Management and Conservation Act 2002, and Vanuatu's National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan names it among the conservation areas to be used as national role models. The World Database on Protected Areas lists four formal protected areas in Vanuatu covering, about 1 per cent of the land area, and Vatthe is one of them. Sanma Province, where the park lies, has four registered conservation areas. The registered site covers both terrestrial and marine areas.

== Conservation issues ==
The main threats to biodiversity on Espiritu Santo are habitat loss, invasive species and extreme weather. [ref: Biodiversity, Santo Sunset] Logging was the main pressure on the forest, and the traditional owners abandoned plans to log it in 1995.

The invasive vine Decalobanthus peltatus, formerly Merremia peltata, has spread through the forest. It grew vigorously after three cyclones and by 2010 had invaded about, or 92 per cent of the forest, of which some were beyond the communities' capacity to control. A UNDP Small Grants Programme project running from 2010 to 2013 trialled low-cost control methods, including cutting and stem injection of herbicide, and aimed to clear about. The National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan names the vine at Vatthe as a threat to the endangered Santa Cruz ground dove.

Nationally, hunting and exploitation affect 66 per cent of Vanuatu's threatened species, and land-use conflicts including logging in the lowlands constrain protected-area management. Vanuatu is regularly struck by cyclones, which cause blowdowns and landslips in its forests.

== Economy ==
The conservation project aimed to train the communities to manage the area themselves and to provide alternative sustainable livelihoods. Ecotourism was the focus: local guides were trained, and a handicrafts centre and tourist bungalows were completed in 1997. The forest remains the main attraction for the bungalows at Matantas.

The Bay of Illusions Guesthouse at Matantas describes itself as the entrance to the conservation area and runs guided walks ranging from a two-hour walk to the nakatambol trees to three-day treks. [ref: Bay of Illusions Guesthouse, Vanuatu Tourism Office]

data.title: Richard F. Weingroff
data.text:
Richard F. Weingroff is an American writer and historian who serves as the official historian of the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), an agency of the United States Department of Transportation (USDOT). He has written extensively on the history of the Interstate Highway System and U.S. transportation policy, with a particular focus on the legislative development of federal highway networks and urban infrastructure controversies such as the 1960s and 1970s freeway revolts in Washington, D.C. [ref: Richard Weingroff - Highway Historian, US Route 36 Newsletter]

== Early life and comic fandom ==
Weingroff was raised in Baltimore, Maryland. During the 1960s, he participated in comic book fandom as a teenage writer and contributor, attending the inaugural New York Comic Con in 1964. [ref: Steve Ditko in the 1960s: In His Own Words, in His Interviews, in the Words of the Fans Who Knew Him, Totalmojo Productions] [ref: Founders of Comic Fandom: A Biographical Who's Who of Publishers, Dealers, Collectors, Writers, Artists, and Other Luminaries of the 1950s and 1960s, Pulp Hero Press] Weingroff published the fanzine Whiz-Bang and wrote articles for fan publications including Rocket's Blast Comicollector, focusing on early Spider-Man comics by Stan Lee and Steve Ditko. [ref: Blasts from the Readers, Rocket's Blast Comicollector] [ref: Forbush Gazette #1 Review, SpiderFan.org]

Weingroff studied at the University of Maryland, graduating with a Bachelor of Arts degree in English. [ref: Richard F. Weingroff Biography, Federal Highway Administration] After graduating from college, he served in the United States Air Force from 1968 to 1972. Stationed at Lackland Air Force Base in San Antonio, Texas, he worked as a reading skills instructor.

== History career ==
In 1973, Weingroff joined the Federal Highway Administration as a technical writer and information specialist, handling public inquiries, congressional correspondence, and agency speeches.

In the 1980s, he began writing articles and historical overviews on American road development. His research covers U.S. highway systems, President Dwight D. Eisenhower's role in the Federal-Aid Highway Act of 1956, [ref: Eisenhower and the Interstate, The Cupola: Student Publications] [ref: Vast Interstate Highway System Marks Half a Century, Voice of America] the Bureau of Public Roads, [ref: Have Truck, Will Drive: The Trucking Industry and the Use of Independent Owner-Operators Over Time, Transportation Law Journal] [ref: Federal-Aid Highway Act of 1921, EBSCO] and local urban planning battles—including documenting how local citizen pushback and freeway revolts reshaped proposed highway routing through the District of Columbia. [ref: FHWA Highway History, Federal Highway Administration] [ref: Roads Not Traveled: DC Pushes Back Against Freeway Plans, Boundary Stones] [ref: Washington's Main Street: Consensus and Conflict on the Capital Beltway, 1952-2001, University of Maryland, College Park] These agency writings formed the backbone of the FHWA's public "[https://highways.dot.gov/highway-history Highway History]" web portal.

Weingroff's historical research is referenced in academic studies, peer-reviewed journals, and books, including Earl Swift's history of the Interstate System, The Big Roads. [ref: The Big Roads: The Visionaries, Wrecks, and Whistle-Blowers Who Built the Superhighways, Houghton Mifflin Harcourt] [ref: Peer-Reviewed Transportation Scholarship, SAGE Journals] [ref: The American Highway: The History and Culture of Roads in the United States, McFarland & Company] [ref: Freeway Revolts! The Quality of Life Effects of Highways, The Review of Economics and Statistics] Weingroff’s articles have also been cited in legal filings, law review articles, think tank assessments, and National Register of Historic Places documentation. [ref: Stanford Law Review Article Citations on Infrastructure, Stanford Law Review] [ref: Historic Resources of the Santa Fe Trail (Amended), Kansas Historical Society / National Park Service] [ref: Supreme Court of the United States Docket No. 23-51 (Filing), Supreme Court of the United States] [ref: Infrastructure Costs, Brookings Institution] In addition, he has contributed to media retrospectives on American urban transit and appeared on television documentary series such as the History Channel's Modern Marvels. [ref: Richard Weingroff Filmography, IMDb] [ref: "Traffic". Modern Marvels. Season 6. Episode 19. June 22, 2000. The History Channel.]

After serving as the agency's informal historian for several decades, Weingroff was officially appointed as the FHWA's agency historian in 2017 while continuing his duties as an information specialist. [ref: On Being Federal Highway Administration's Official Historian: Public Roads 100th Anniversary, Federal Highway Administration]

data.title: Crossley-Kegresse half-track
data.text:
----

The Crossley-Kégresse half-track was an experimental half-track using the Kégresse track tested by the British army in the late 1920s. The production vehicles were produced by Crossley Motors in the United Kingdom and delivered to the army from 1926. The Kégresse track was licensed from Citroën in France, which employed its inventor Adolphe Kégresse.

== Development ==

Kégresse half-tracks were also extensively used by the French army, [ref: ] [ref: ] including the later Citroën P17 and P107 utility half-tracks. [ref: Le grand album des Citroën-Kégresse sous l'uniforme, Histoire & Collections] In 1923, the British army purchased Kégresse half-track vehicles from Citroën for testing, but ultimately decided they were not satisfactory for its purposes and commissioned Crossley Motors to produce a new vehicle using the licensed track from Citroën.

In the British army, the Crossley vehicle could replace horses for haulage work that otherwise only animals could do, one of the first such attempts in the world. The Kégresse track had a two-speed gearbox while the standard gearbox had four speeds, giving a total of eight forward speeds. It was otherwise driven like a truck. It was used as a general service vehicle, a staff car, and an artillery tractor. [ref: ]

== Service history ==

=== Trials and field exercises ===

Test trials began at least as early as October 1924. [ref: ] In February 1925 comparative cross-country and road trials took place in which the Crossley-Kégresse half-track placed first, ahead of the fully tracked Vickers Light Dragon Mark II. By November 1925, it had been found "capable of traversing the most difficult country at a very fair speed" in government trials. [ref: ] In later trials, it proved capable of pulling a heavy QF 4.5-inch howitzer across open country, including through a stream. [ref: ] In 1926, it was demonstrated to the heads of government of the British Dominions at Camberley, equipped to tow a QF 3.7-inch mountain howitzer.

It was among the first vehicles used to equip the British army's interwar Experimental Mechanised Force (EMF), the first mechanised combined arms brigade in the world. At the Force's formation in 1927, the Crossley half-track was used by the machine-gun battalion of the Somerset Light Infantry, [ref: ] and the 9th Field Brigade of the Royal Artillery, allowing these previously non-mechanised infantry and artillery units to manoeuvre alongside the 3rd and 5th battalions of the Royal Tank Corps in a prototype of a modern combined arms mechanised force. Operating with the 'fast group' it maintained a daily average cross-country speed of 10 mph over 30 miles. This was "the first mechanised formation to be born in the world, and was the mother of all 'armoured divisions'".

=== Shanghai deployment ===

Between February and May 1927, tensions arose in China. The EMF's 11 and 80 batteries, armed with QF 18-pounder guns, were re-equipped with Crossley-Kégresse half-tracks and Burford-Kégresse half-tracks, replacing their fully tracked Vickers Light Dragon Mark IIs, and shipped to China as part of the Shanghai Defence Force. This Force was withdrawn in January 1928. In 1928 and 1929, the remaining Vickers Light Dragon Mark IIs towing artillery in the EMF in the UK were also replaced with Burford- and Crossley-Kégresse half tracks.

== Legacy ==

In 1927, the British War Office ordered a related Crossley vehicle in which drive wheels could be fitted with chain tracks, intended to reproduce the functionality of the Crossley-Kégresse vehicle in a more flexible format. [ref: ] The half-track Crossley-Kégresse left British army consideration in the early 1930s, as part of a general shift away from half-tracks to fully tracked vehicles by the army.

At least two examples of the half-track have survived and been preserved, one by the Norfolk Tank Museum and another by the British army's Royal Logistics Corps Museum, both in the United Kingdom. Official Ministry of Supply photographs of the vehicle are held in the collections of the Imperial War Museum. [ref: ]

== References ==

* Moving the Guns: The Mechanisation of the Royal Artillery, 1854-1939, HMSO
* British Military Transport, 1829–1956, HMSO
* Men, Ideas and Tanks: British Military Thought and Armoured Forces, 1903–39, Manchester University Press
* The Tanks: The History of the Royal Tank Regiment and its Predecessors Heavy Branch Machine-Gun Corps Tank Corps & Royal Tank Corps 1914–1945 (1914–1939), Praeger

data.title: Wuhan Airlines Flight 4211
data.text:
----

Wuhan Airlines Flight 4211 was a domestic charter flight from Lanzhou, China to Xi’an, China. On 8 October 1992, the aircraft operating the flight crashed into a mountain range after suffering an engine failure on takeoff, killing 14 of the 35 people on board. [ref: Accident Avia 14 (Ilyushin Il-14) B-4211, Thursday 8 October 1992, aviation-safety.net] [ref: ]

Follow the crash, the Civil Aviation Administration of China had grounded the operation of all Ilyushin Il-14 aircraft. [ref: 难忘的历程——中国伊尔14飞机停飞15年纪念, ccaonline.cn]

== Aircraft ==
The aircraft involved was an Avia 14 manufactured in 1958 and registered as B-4211. At the time of the accident, the plane was considered to be unsuitable for standard conditions. [ref: 机组努力挽救至最后一刻，忆武汉航空旅游包机1992.10.8定西空难_腾讯新闻, new.qq.com]

There were 7 crew members: captain, first officer, navigator, radio operator, flight engineer, and two flight attendants. 28 passengers were on board, 14 of them were from Taiwanese "Silk Road Tour" group (11 Taiwanese and 3 Chinese), and 14 French passengers. [ref: 1992年10月8日 武航一旅游包机在甘肃坠毁-搜狐新闻, news.sohu.com]

== Accident ==
At 15:03, 45 minutes into the flight, the plane reached an altitude of 3,000 meters (9,840 feet). The left engine then lost power and failed for half a minute and its right engine didn't work properly. The crew requested for an emergency landing at Yuzhong Xiaguanying Airport. The plane only maintained its original altitude for 20 minutes before losing speed and descending. As the mountainside appeared, the crew determined that they would crash-landed into the hill. The left wing struck the ground first, ruptured the left landing gear and disintergrated with fire following the impact. Five crew member and nine French passengers died.According from a witness:It was around 3:30 PM. I was at my front door when suddenly a plane flew overhead from east to west. It flew very low and made a loud noise, but the sound was a little different from usual. At the time, I thought it was doing some kind of surveying, and that's why it was so loud at such a low altitude. Just as it passed, I heard a loud "bang" and then it disappeared. I figured it had just passed over a mountain and the noise had stopped abruptly, so I didn't pay much attention and went straight home. As soon as I entered the house, I heard someone crying from the mountaintop. I immediately ran out. It turned out to be a woman from our village named Wang Lan who was herding sheep. She had seen the plane crash and was crying out, "A plane has crashed! Go up and see!" My father heard it too and was shouting. As soon as I heard that, I immediately ran up the mountain. By then, all our neighbors had heard it and came running, and we all ran up the mountain together. [ref: 27年前遭遇空难，是定西的乡亲们救了这些台胞的命——中国·定西网, www.cndingxi.com]

== Investigation ==
The investigation concluded that the left-engine shutdown was caused by a punctured insulation layer of the engine generator. It damaged the ignition nozzle that lead to the failure. The plane was found to had been neglected for a long time due to lack of maintenance, and was in poor condition.

data.title: Ady Arie
data.text:
----

Ady Arie (Hebrew: עדי אריה; born: 1963) is an Israeli electrical engineering scientist.

He is a professor in the School of Electrical and Computer Engineering in the Fleischman Faculty of Engineering at Tel-Aviv University (TAU), where he holds the Marko and Lucie Chaoul Chair in Nano-Photonics. [ref: Prof. Ady Arie, quantum.tau.ac.il]

Arie's research focuses on nonlinear optics, electron optics, and light–electron interactions. He is a fellow of Optica. [ref: ]

== Early life and education ==
Ady Arie was born in Israel in 1963. He received his B.Sc. in mathematics and physics from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 1983, in the framework of Talpiot project, followed by an M.Sc. in physics (1986) and a Ph.D. in engineering (1992), both from Tel Aviv University. His M.Sc. advisors were Prof. Shmuel Goldstein and Prof. Moshe Tur, and his PhD advisor was Prof. Moshe Tur. [ref: Team, NONLINEAR OPTICS AND WAVE PROPAGATION LABORATORY]

From 1991 to 1993, he held Wolfson and Fulbright postdoctoral fellowships under Prof. Robert L. Byer at Stanford University. [ref: Laser heterodyne spectroscopy of 127I2 hyperfine structure near 532 nm, Edward L. Ginzton Laboratory, Stanford University]

== Academic career ==
Arie joined the Department of Physical Electronics in the School of Electrical and Computer Engineering in the Fleischman Faculty of Engineering at Tel-Aviv University in 1993. He became a full professor in 2006. Arie served as the Vice Dean of Research of the Faculty of Engineering from 2011 to 2013 and as the head of the School of Electrical Engineering 2013 to 2017. [ref: KLA-Tencor ישראל תרמה מלגות ל-37 סטודנטים למקצועות טכנולוגיים -, אנשים ומחשבים - פורטל חדשות היי-טק, מיחשוב, טלקום, טכנולוגיות]

He is also the co-founder and head of the TAU Center for Light Matter Interaction since 2016. [ref: Our People, lmicenter.tau.ac.il]

Arie has supervised more than 80 Postdoctoral, Ph.D., and M.Sc. students. [ref: Team, adyarie] [ref: Past Students, adyarie]

== Professional experience ==
In 2001, Arie was a co-founder and chief technology officer of ZettaLight Inc. [ref: השקעה ראשונה לקרן רנוויי טלקום ונצ'רס: גיוס סיד של 1.5 מיליון דולר בזטהלייט - וואלה כסף, וואלה] He is chair of the national steering committee of the Israeli Planning and Budgeting Committee on Quantum Science and Technology and a member of the national science advisory board of the Israel National Quantum Initiative. [ref: מינוי מחליף ליו"ר ועדת היגוי המייעצת לוות"ת לנושא מדע וטכנולוגיה קוונטיים, המועצ]

Arie served as a Topical Editor of Optics Letters (2008-2014) and as an Associate Editor of Optica (2018-2024).  Since 2025, he has been a Deputy Editor of Optics Express. [ref: Optics Letters Editorial Board Members, opg.optica.org] [ref: Editors and Staff, opg.optica.org] [ref: Optic Express, opg.optica.org]

== Research ==
Arie's research spans optics, electron microscopy, light–electron interactions, plasmonics and the propagation dynamics of special wavepackets. [ref: חוקרים מאוניברסיטת תל אביב הצליחו למדוד חבילות גלים מחזוריות, Ynet] [ref: סדרת מחקרים חשפה: תורת הקוונטים משפיעה על תהליך פליטת האור, Ynet]

His research has included the development of nonlinear optical holography for generating and controlling structured light, including Airy and optical vortex beams. [ref: The electron sheepdog, The Statesman] [ref: יצירה ושליטה על אלומות לייזר מאיצות (Airy Beams) בעזרת גבישים פוטוניים לא ליניאריים, הידען - Hayadan] Drawing on an analogy between spin and sum-frequency generation, he proposed and helped demonstrate an all-optical Stern–Gerlach effect, both in space and in time. [ref: מחקר ישראלי: אם אין מגנטים – תשתמשו באור, Ynet]

He developed quasiperiodic nonlinear photonic crystals for phase matching multiple nonlinear optical processes and to periodically poled ferroelectric crystals for efficient frequency conversion across a broad spectral range. [ref: Photonic quasicrystals for general purpose nonlinear optical frequency conversion, Physical Review Letters] [ref: Green and ultraviolet quasi-phase-matched second harmonic generation in bulk periodically-poled KTiOPO4, Optics Communications]

In electron optics, his team produced the first electron Airy beam and developed masks for shaping electron beams, later applying this to correct spherical aberration and improve resolution in electron microscopy. [ref: Researchers develop electron-based Airy Beam, EDN] Using surface gravity water waves as a model system, his group also made the first observation of the Kennard phase of wave packets in a linear potential. [ref: חוקרים ישראלים פתרו תעלומה מדעית בת 93 שנה, ynet]

== Honors and awards ==
Arie received several awards, including the Fulbright and the Wolfson Fellowships for postdoctoral scholars and the Alon Fellowship.

In 2010, he was elevated to a fellow of Optica “for significant contributions to the development of periodic and quasi-periodic nonlinear photonic crystals”.

In 2015, he was named to the Marko and Lucie Chaoul Chair in Nano-Photonics at Tel Aviv University.

In 2016 he received the Kadar Foundation Award for excellence in research and in 2025 he received the Lifetime Achievement Award for Excellence in Research, Faculty of Engineering, Tel Aviv University. [ref: הוענק פרס כדר למצוינות מחקרית לחוקרים בתחום המדעים ובתחום מדעי הרוח, www.tau.ac.il]

data.title: Advertising in Azerbaijan
data.text:
Advertising in Azerbaijan comprises the creation, production and media placement of advertising in Azerbaijan. According to the State Statistics Committee of Azerbaijan (SSC), revenue from advertising activity in the country amounted to 292.4 million manat in 2025, about 3.9 times the 75.6 million manat recorded in 2020. [ref: Azərbaycanda reklam bazarı sürətlə böyüyür – RƏQƏMLƏR, Sfera.az] [ref: Mətbuat öldü! Yaşasın media!, Pressklub.az] The SSC figure covers the creation and production of advertising as well as its placement. Official statistics and industry estimates differ considerably: for 2023 the SSC reported 201 million manat, while the ICT Market Participants Public Union estimated the market at about 140 million manat.

Banks are the main group of advertisers whose budgets are publicly disclosed; their advertising and marketing expenses totalled 92.8 million manat in 2025. National television audience measurement has been carried out by MARSA since 2023, and since September 2026 foreign digital service providers have been registering for value-added tax in Azerbaijan.

== History ==
A modern advertising market began to form in the 1990s, following independence, the transition to a market economy, the emergence of private broadcasters and the arrival of foreign brands. The first law "On Advertising" was adopted in 1997 and remained in force until 2015. [ref: "Reklam haqqında" Azərbaycan Respublikasının Qanunu (№ 1281-IVQ, 15 may 2015-ci il), e-qanun.az]

=== 2012–2019 ===
According to the SSC, revenue from advertising services rose from 48.4 million manat in 2012 to 72.5 million manat in 2014. During the economic difficulties of 2015–2016 it fell to 43.5 million manat, a decline of about 40%, and returned to its 2014 level only in 2019. [ref: Azərbaycanda reklama nə qədər pul ödənilir?, [[Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty]

=== 2020s ===
In 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic, revenue from advertising activity grew by 4.4% to 75.6 million manat. Advertising revenue of the mass media that year was 11.84 million manat, of which 10.54 million went to television and radio and 1.02 million to periodical print media. Growth accelerated in the following years: revenue reached 99 million manat in 2021, 201 million in 2023 and 292.4 million in 2025. Annual growth was about 40% in 2023, 30% in 2024 and 12% in 2025.

== Market size ==

{| class="wikitable" style="text-align:right"
|+ SSC: revenue from advertising activity (million manat)
! Year !! Revenue !! Change !! Source
|-
| style="text-align:left" | 2012 || 48.4 || — ||
|-
| style="text-align:left" | 2014 || 72.5 || — ||
|-
| style="text-align:left" | 2020 || 75.6 || +4.4% ||
|-
| style="text-align:left" | 2021 || 99 || — ||
|-
| style="text-align:left" | 2022 || 143.8 || — ||
|-
| style="text-align:left" | 2023 || 201.0 || +39.8% ||
|-
| style="text-align:left" | 2024 || 260.8 || +29.8% ||
|-
| style="text-align:left" | 2025 || 292.4 || +12.1% ||
|}
The SSC's initial figure for 2022 was 138.3 million manat; later publications give 143.8 million manat.

=== Structure by activity ===

Of the 292.4 million manat recorded in 2025, 283 million manat came from direct advertising activity.

{| class="wikitable" style="text-align:right"
|+ Structure of direct advertising activity, 2025
! Activity !! Million manat !! Share
|-
| style="text-align:left" | Placement || 159.6 || 56.4%
|-
| style="text-align:left" | Creation || 68.4 || 24.2%
|-
| style="text-align:left" | Production || 55.0 || 19.4%
|-
! style="text-align:left" | Total || 283.0 || 100%
|}

Outdoor advertising was the largest placement segment. Placement in the media and at mass events amounted to 68 million manat, of which 40.2 million went to television and radio and 20 million to digital channels. Revenue from advertising on vehicles was 20 million manat.

In 2022, advertising revenue of the mass media was 16.1 million manat, of which 15 million went to television and radio. Outdoor advertising revenue that year was about 30 million manat, roughly three times the previous year's level. [ref: Mətbuat günü: İqtisadi kollaps, media ağırlaşdı, ANS Press]

=== Industry estimates ===

According to the ICT Market Participants Public Union, advertising investment grew by 14% in 2023 to about 140 million manat. Television accounted for 46 million manat (about 33% of the market), digital platforms for 33 million and radio for 7.2 million; outdoor advertising grew by 6%, while the share of print media continued to decline. [ref: Azərbaycanda reklam bazarının həcmi 140 mln. manata çatıb, APA] This estimate is considerably lower than the SSC figure for the same year (201 million manat). The union has not published its methodology, while the SSC figure includes the creation and production of advertising in addition to placement.

== Channels ==
=== Television ===
Speaking at a seminar in Baku on 4 November 2022, Zaur Ismayilov, chairman of the advertisers' committee of the Digital and Audiovisual Broadcasting Industry Public Union, said that the annual turnover of the television advertising market had not exceeded 45 million manat for seven years. According to him, the total rating value of the market was 1.6 million, the average price of a rating point was 28 manat, and the market was at a "stalemate". [ref: Azərbaycanda televiziya reklamı bazarının illik dövriyyəsi açıqlanıb, Report.az]

The ICT Market Participants Public Union estimated television advertising at 46 million manat in 2023, about a third of the market. According to the SSC, revenue from placing advertising on television and radio was 40.2 million manat in 2025.

==== Audience measurement ====
Since 1 January 2023, national television audience data have been provided by MARSA (Media Audience Research System in Azerbaijan). The system is based on Kantar technology; its panel consists of 950 households in 29 cities and more than 200 villages, using "People Meter 7" devices. [ref: Kantarın Azərbaycanda yeni Televiziya ölçüm sisteminin yaradılması ilə bağlı məktubu, MARSA]

=== Outdoor advertising ===
According to the SSC, outdoor advertising revenue was about 30 million manat in 2022, having roughly tripled in a year. In 2025 outdoor advertising was the largest placement segment, although its exact size was not published. The placement of outdoor advertising structures requires a permit and is regulated by the State Advertising Agency.

=== Transit advertising ===
In 2025, revenue from advertising placed on vehicles amounted to 20 million manat.

=== Digital advertising ===
According to the SSC, revenue from placing advertising on digital channels was 20 million manat in 2025. The ICT Market Participants Public Union estimated investment in digital platforms at 33 million manat in 2023.

According to DataReportal's Digital 2026 report, in Azerbaijan: [ref: Digital 2026: Azerbaijan, DataReportal]
* there are 9.27 million internet users (89% of the population);
* there are 7.61 million social media user identities (73.1% of the population);
* the potential advertising reach is 4.25 million on Instagram, 1.65 million on Facebook, 1.2 million on LinkedIn, 438,000 on Messenger and 266,000 on X.

=== Radio ===
The ICT Market Participants Public Union estimated radio advertising at 7.2 million manat in 2023.

=== Print ===
Advertising revenue of periodical print media was 1.02 million manat in 2020 and 0.74 million manat in 2022. According to the industry union, the share of print media in the advertising market continued to decline in 2023.

== Advertisers ==
=== Banks ===

Banks disclose advertising and marketing expenses in their financial statements. The sector's expenses rose from 45.57 million manat in 2021 to 98.09 million manat in 2024, roughly 2.2 times, before falling by 5.4% to 92.82 million manat in 2025. [ref: Banklar son 5 ildə reklama nə qədər pul xərcləyiblər? – Tam siyahı, Yeni Avaz]

{| class="wikitable sortable" style="text-align:right"
|+ Advertising and marketing expenses of banks (million manat)
! Bank !! 2021 !! 2022 !! 2023 !! 2024 !! 2025
|-
| style="text-align:left" | Kapital Bank || 8.92 || 16.05 || 26.34 || 43.65 || 46.95
|-

The table shows selected banks from the source; the total covers the whole banking sector.

Kapital Bank's expenses grew about 5.3 times between 2021 and 2025; in 2025 the bank accounted for 50.6% of the sector's advertising and marketing expenses. Several large banks reduced their spending that year: PASHA Bank from 6.12 to 3.57 million manat and Unibank from 9.64 to 5.49 million manat.

== Regulation ==
Advertising is regulated by the Law "On Advertising" of 15 May 2015. The law does not apply to political advertising, consumer information, packaging information or non-commercial announcements. Under the law:
* the main language of advertising is the state language, and prices must be shown in manat;
* unfair, inaccurate and hidden advertising is prohibited;
* advertising of tobacco products, including electronic cigarettes, is completely banned;
* only over-the-counter medicines may be advertised;
* special requirements apply to advertising aimed at children, and the placement of advertising near educational institutions is restricted.
The law also provides for self-regulation by industry associations and for administrative, civil and criminal liability for violations.

A presidential decree of 20 June 2017 established the State Advertising Agency of the Republic of Azerbaijan as a public legal entity responsible for unified regulation and oversight of outdoor advertising. [ref: Azərbaycan Respublikasının Dövlət Reklam Agentliyinin yaradılması haqqında Azərbaycan Respublikası Prezidentinin Fərmanı (№ 1472, 20 iyun 2017-ci il), e-qanun.az]

== Taxation ==
=== Foreign digital platforms ===
Under amendments to the Tax Code adopted in 2026, from September of that year non-resident digital service providers that supply services to Azerbaijan by electronic means and have an annual turnover in the country above US$10,000 must register electronically with the tax authority. [ref: Qlobal rəqəmsal xidmət təchizatçılarının Azərbaycanda ƏDV qeydiyyatı davam edir, State Tax Service under the Ministry of Economy] VAT on payments for the services of registered providers is not withheld by banks; the providers calculate, declare and pay it themselves. [ref: Daha iki qlobal rəqəmsal xidmət təchizatçısı Azərbaycanda ƏDV qeydiyyatına alınıb, State Tax Service under the Ministry of Economy]

In September 2026 the State Tax Service added "digital platform influencer" (code 6312003) to its classification of activities, allowing influencer and blogging activity to be registered as a distinct type of entrepreneurship. [ref: Azərbaycanda bloger və infulenserlərdən vergi tutulacaq – YENİLİK, RƏSMİ, FED.az] [ref: Azərbaycanda influenserlik və blogerlik sahibkarlığın ayrıca növü sayılacaq, Report.az]

Translation does work, sources may not: Please cite La Stampa, Stampa Sera and Lo Scoglio as news, not books, perhaps elbareport.it as well, add ASN-citation to textbox as in original, and transfer L'Eloquenza and L'Unità as sources from there. ----

Itavia Flight 115 was a scheduled passenger flight from Rome to Genoa, Italy. On 14 October 1960, the aircraft operating the flight crashed into the slopes of Mount Capanne near the town of Elba at 728 meters (2,388 feet), killing all 7 passengers and 4 crew members. [ref: Accident de Havilland DH-114 Heron 2 I-AOMU, Friday 14 October 1960, aviation-safety.net]

== Aircraft and crew ==
The aircraft involved was an Itavia de Havilland DH-114 Heron 2, registration I-AOMU (serial no. 14090), manufactured in 1955. [ref: ] [ref: Il disastro aereo del 1960, Mucchio Selvaggio] The flight crew consisted of captain Ennio Scipione, aged 30, first officer Francesco Cossu, aged 44, and two flight attendants, Giovanna Pertusio, aged 25, and Grazia Candeloro, aged 20.

== Accident ==
The flight took off from Rome Urbe Airport at 15:02 pm local time. At 15:19, the crew contacted the tower in Genoa, stating that they were currently flying over the city of Civitavecchia. The controller, seeing the poor weather conditions along the flight's path, offered to divert them to either Turin or Nice. There was no response to this message from the crew. Moments later, the aircraft struck the slopes of Mount Capanne at 2,388 feet, exploding and breaking up on impact and killing all 11 occupants onboard. [ref: La Stampa (1960-10-15), Editrice La Stampa S.p.A.]
== Investigation ==
The investigation found that the crew was flying according to visual flight rules instead of instrument flight rules, which was required given the poor visibility on the flight's route. Why the crew chose to fly in VFR instead of IMC is unknown.

== Lawsuit ==
A court case followed the accident, with penal charges brought forward against the flight company, and responsible personnel of Civilavia and the Urbe airport. Among them were General Romolo Abbriata (director of the civil aviation authority), Luigi Petragnani (manager of Itavia), Renato Panini (technical organizer of Itavia) and Riccardo Rubbiano-Pivawere. However, they were acquitted of all charges in both instances (1965/66). [ref: La Stampa (1966-02-11), Editrice La Stampa S.p.A.]

== Memorial ==
=== 1960 ===
At the scene of the accident, a small white marble tombstone was built and placed against a rock formation, engraved with the star of David in memory of Silvio Sciunnach, a Jewish passenger who was onboard the flight and a victim of the accident.

=== 2013 ===
On October 13, 2013, on the evening preceding the 53rd anniversary of the accident, a monument was built on the accident site. [ref: Un Monumento sul Capanne in memoria del disastro aereo di 53 anni fa, www.elbareport.it]
== References ==

data.title: Abiodun Ramon Oseni
data.text:
----

= Abiodun Ramon Oseni =
Abiodun Ramon Oseni is a Nigerian security analyst and former United States Army servicemember and police officer. He has spoken and written publicly on issues including security, policing, terrorism, international affairs, and economic issues both in Nigeria and internationally. His commentary has appeared in Nigerian newspapers and international publications, and he has participated in academic and professional forums. [ref: Decentralised policing, economic empowerment will curb banditry, says Oseni, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News]

== Early life and education ==
Abiodun Ramon Oseni was born on 6 February 1980 in Epe, Lagos State, Nigeria. He is reported to be from the Idisewe ruling compound of Idasho in Ibeju-Lekki and a first cousin of Oba Kamorudeen Ishola Animashaun, the Oloja of Epe. He completed his early education in Apapa and attended Sari-Iganmu Secondary School Lagos. [ref: From Frontlines to Classroom: How U.S. Army veteran, Oseni, is reshaping Nigerian, West African security, Vanguard News]

Oseni attended Adeniran Ogunsanya College of Education (AOCOED), where he earned a National Certificate of Education (NCE) in Economics and History in 2003. He later attended Lagos State University, where he obtained a bachelor's degree in international relations and history. He also completed expert training at the U.S. Army Quartermaster School in Virginia and the U.S. Army Leadership School in Mississippi. He obtained a master's certificate in international security from Harvard University and further got a master's degree in international relations and global security, with specialization in conflict resolution, from American Military University. [ref: LASU appoints U.S. Army veteran as entrepreneurship instructor, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News]

== Career ==
Oseni was active in the United States Army and later worked as a police officer in Tennessee. He described his professional interests as focusing on international security, counterterrorism, policing, and conflict resolution. Oseni also later served as a Diplomatic Security Officer with the U.S. Department of State's Special Operations Unit in Washington, D.C.

He has subsequently worked as a security analyst and public commentator. His analysis has focused on issues including terrorism, banditry, kidnapping, policing, food security, regional security, and international conflicts. [ref: Yoruba leaders, experts stress decentralised security model as threats close in, Businessday NG]In 2025, Oseni was appointed as an Entrepreneurship and Innovation (ENT 1000) instructor at Lagos State University. His public activities have included lectures on security and related subjects.

== Public commentary ==
Oseni has been featured and quoted by Nigerian and international media in connection with security and public policy issues. [ref: Deadly Cooperation Among Terror Groups in Nigeria, Africa Defense Forum]

In 2024, he participated in a National Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) public relations clinic addressing food security and related security concerns. He also participated in another NSCDC event concerning sustainable mining and environmental management. [ref: NSCDC seeks collaborative action to tackle food insecurity, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News]

In 2025, he participated in discussions on insecurity and security policy, including events addressing policing and the security situation in southwestern Nigeria.

BusinessDay gave reports on a presentation by Oseni concerning kidnapping and banditry in Nigeria, in which he lectured that these activities had developed into organised criminal enterprises and advocated for community policing, intelligence integration, and coordinated security strategies.

Oseni has also commented publicly on international security issues. In 2025, Vanguard quoted him in its coverage of the Israel–Iran conflict, where he talked about the difficulties involved in targeting Iran's underground nuclear facilities. [ref: The implications of Israeli/Iran war, Vanguard News]

The Guardian has published a number of Oseni's articles on international security and Nigerian public policy. These have included commentary on the United States' foreign policy, the Israel–Iran conflict, terrorism financing, drug trafficking and Nigeria's security challenges. [ref: Vote buying in Nigeria is national security threat, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News]

In March 2026, The Guardian reported on Oseni's call for the establishment of state police in Nigeria, made at an International Security Conference organized by the Institute of Security, Nigeria. The report covered his recommendations concerning community policing, intelligence gathering, and local security responses. [ref: Insecurity: State Police is an urgent need for Nigeria, says Oseni, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News]

In September 2026, Independent Newspaper Nigeria published an article discussing Oseni's views on West African security architecture, including decentralized policing and community-based intelligence. [ref: Navigating The Complexities Of West African Security Architecture, Independent Newspaper Nigeria]

Oseni also appeared on Channels Television to discuss his proposal to criminalize the collection of fees for filling police reports. arguing for changes to the way such reports are handled. [ref: Insecurity: Security Analyst Calls For Criminalisation Of Fee For Police Reports]

== Publications ==
Oseni has written opinion articles on security, international relations, economic policy, and governance. His articles have appeared in publications including TheGuardian, Vanguard,and other Nigerian and international media outlets. [ref: Nigeria: President Trump's Remarks On Christian Genocide in Nigeria - Issues and Solutions, Vanguard]

His published subjects have included global security challenges, intelligence, homeland security, policing, crisis management, defense policy, and the evolving nature of transnational threats. [ref: Abiodun Ramon Oseni, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News]

== Awards and recognition ==
In 2026, Oseni received the Outstanding Security Personality Award at the Nigeria Safety and Security (NSAS) Awards. He is also a Fellow of the Institute of Security, Nigeria.

Westdyke Community Club is a Scottish community football club based in Westhill, Aberdeenshire. Founded in 1996, the club operates youth, adult, women's and development football programmes and has teams competing in regional football competitions across north-east Scotland.

== History ==

Westdyke Community Club was founded in 1996 in Westhill, Aberdeenshire. Since formation, the club has expanded its football activities to include numerous youth teams as well as adult, women's and development football programmes.

The club received regional recognition during the COVID-19 pandemic when Sportscotland highlighted its approach to coach education and preparation for the return of grassroots sport.

== Youth football ==

Westdyke Community Club operates youth teams across multiple age groups and has competed in regional and national football competitions.

The club received coverage for its performances in Scottish youth football competitions, including reaching multiple Scottish Cup semi-finals during the 2023–24 season.

In 2023, Westdyke won a Scottish youth cup competition, with local media describing the achievement as a historic milestone for the club.

== Women's football ==

Westdyke has operated women's football teams as part of its wider community structure. Coverage in local media has highlighted the club's community-based approach and support for female participation in football.

== Junior football ==

In 2024, the club expanded into Junior football through the creation of Westdyke CC Juniors, entering the North Region Junior Championship. Independent coverage discussed the club's transition from amateur football into the Junior game and its ambitions for long-term development.

The club subsequently established an under 18 development pathway intended to support progression into the Junior side.

== Community involvement ==

Westdyke Community Club has been involved in a range of community initiatives. Regional media have reported on charitable kit donations and community support activities associated with the club.

The club also received public support and media attention following a serious road traffic incident involving one of its youth players in 2022.
