data.title: Mark Harvey (political scientist)
data.text:
Mark Harvey is an American political scientist, educator, and author whose scholarship spans political communication, international relations, popular culture, and political science pedagogy. His research examines celebrity influence, political persuasion, music and politics, and the use of games and simulations in political science and international relations education. He is Director of Graduate Business Programs at the University of Saint Mary.

== Education and career ==
Harvey earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Washburn University, master's degrees from the University of Missouri–Kansas City and the University of Wales Swansea, and a Ph.D. in political science from the University of Kansas. Harvey has taught at the University of Saint Mary, Baker University, the University of Birmingham, and the University of Kansas. He also taught in the Duke University Talent Identification Program, including appointments at the University of Kansas, Duke East Campus, and the London School of Economics. [ref: KU grad students give whiz kids head start on college, University Daily Kansan] [ref: Mark Harvey, University of Saint Mary]

== Research ==
Harvey's scholarship spans political communication, international relations, popular culture, and political science pedagogy. His work examines political influence, persuasion, and decision making in public life, particularly through celebrity advocacy, media, music, and experiential learning.

=== Celebrity influence and political communication ===
Harvey's research examines the role of celebrities in politics, public persuasion, issue advocacy, and media coverage. [ref: Celebrity Influence: Politics, Persuasion, and Issue-Based Advocacy, University Press of Kansas]

In Celebrity Influence: Politics, Persuasion, and Issue-Based Advocacy (2017), Harvey argues that celebrities derive political influence primarily through their ability to attract public and media attention to issues and their ability to persuade audiences through credibility, familiarity, and identification. [ref: Celebrity Influence: Politics, Persuasion, and Issue-Based Advocacy, University Press of Kansas]

His work explores the political activities of entertainers, athletes, and other public figures, analyzing how celebrities influence public agendas, shape media coverage, and participate in domestic and international policy debates. His research employs case studies, content analysis, surveys, and experimental methods.

A recurring theme in Harvey's scholarship is that celebrity influence depends not simply on fame but also on credibility, identity, expertise, and the perceived fit between a public figure and the issue or candidate being advocated. His work argues that endorsements are generally most effective when audiences perceive the celebrity as authentic and connected to the issue under discussion. [ref: Do celebrity endorsements matter? A look at the role of pop stars in modern politics, PBS NewsHour]

Harvey has argued that celebrity persuasion is often most effective on issues where public attitudes are not firmly established, while highly polarized political questions are less susceptible to influence from celebrity advocates. [ref: Do celebrity endorsements matter? A look at the role of pop stars in modern politics, PBS NewsHour] [ref: CBC News Network’s Aarti Pole speaks with author and professor Mark Harvey, CBC News] His research has examined celebrity advocacy in areas including foreign policy, development, human rights, international conflict, electoral politics, and public policy. [ref: Study shows Taylor Swift's endorsement may turn off voters Harris needs, The Hill]

Harvey has also examined the relationship between celebrity status, media coverage, and political influence. In a chapter analyzing media coverage of Donald Trump, he explored how celebrity and news attention can shape public perceptions of political leaders and contribute to political influence beyond traditional forms of political communication. [ref: The Hollywood Connection: The Influence of Fictional Media and Celebrity Politics in American Public Opinion, Lexington Books]

=== Music, media, and popular culture ===
Harvey's research examines the relationship between music, media, political communication, and political power. His work explores how musicians, performers, entertainment industries, and media systems influence public opinion, collective identities, and policy debates in both domestic and international contexts.

A significant portion of Harvey's scholarship focuses on the political and economic development of the recording industry. In studies of the long-playing (LP) record and the emergence of the album as an artistic format, he has examined how technological innovation, marketing strategies, industry structures, and cultural change transformed the music business during the second half of the twentieth century. Harvey has argued that the growing popularity of the album format was influenced not only by technological innovation but also by struggles within the recording industry over artistic autonomy, marketing practices, and control of creative production. [ref: The Rise of the LP: The Politics of Diffusion Innovation in the Recording Industry, Business History]

His research has also explored how record companies marketed musicians as artistic figures rather than merely commercial entertainers. In an analysis of the Beatles, the Beach Boys, and Capitol Records, Harvey examined how changing power relationships between artists and recording companies contributed to the emergence of the album as a recognized artistic medium and helped reshape norms within the music industry. [ref: Politics and Power in the Record Industry: The Beatles, the Beach Boys, and the Album as Art Form, Musicology Australia]

More recently, Harvey's scholarship has examined the relationship between music and political communication, including the role of music in election campaigns, celebrity advocacy, political identity formation, and audience persuasion. [ref: Trump's music break may turn more voters than you think, The Hill] [ref: Trump's attacks on Springsteen and Oprah aren't legally sound. That's not the point, MSNBC]

His research has also explored the emotional and symbolic effects of music in political campaigns, arguing that campaign music can shape perceptions of political candidates, reinforce political identities, and influence audience engagement. [ref: Trump's music break may turn more voters than you think, The Hill] [ref: The World Today, BBC News]

=== Games, simulations, and active learning ===
A second major area of Harvey's scholarship focuses on active learning, games, simulations, and experiential education, particularly within political science and international relations. He is co-editor of Games and Simulations in the Political Science Classroom: Games Without Frontiers (2023) and Short Games and Active Learning in Political Science: Beating the Clock (2026). [ref: Games and Simulations in the Political Science Classroom: Games Without Frontiers, Routledge] [ref: Short Games and Active Learning in Political Science: Beating the Clock, Routledge]

Harvey's pedagogical work examines how simulations, role-playing exercises, and educational games can improve student engagement, retention, critical thinking, and empathy by allowing students to experience political concepts directly rather than learning them exclusively through lectures and readings. Drawing on theories of experiential learning, his work emphasizes student agency, role adoption, and decision making as mechanisms for learning. [ref: Games and Simulations in the Political Science Classroom: Games Without Frontiers, Routledge]

Much of Harvey's scholarship focuses on international relations pedagogy. His work explores the use of simulations to teach concepts such as diplomacy, the security dilemma, balance-of-power politics, international cooperation, trade, conflict, global disparity, and foreign policy decision making. [ref: The Palgrave Handbook on the Pedagogy of International Relations Theory, Palgrave Macmillan] [ref: Games and Simulations in the Political Science Classroom: Games Without Frontiers, Routledge] He has argued that games and simulations are particularly effective in helping students understand abstract international relations theories by allowing them to experience the incentives and constraints faced by political actors. [ref: The Palgrave Handbook on the Pedagogy of International Relations Theory, Palgrave Macmillan]

Harvey has also written on the design and implementation of educational games. [ref: Games and Simulations in the Political Science Classroom: Games Without Frontiers, Routledge] His scholarship examines the practical challenges of simulation design and classroom management, arguing that carefully structured short-form activities can often achieve many of the same learning objectives as larger and more elaborate simulations while remaining practical within conventional class periods. [ref: Short Games and Active Learning in Political Science: Beating the Clock, Routledge] Harvey has also emphasized the importance of experimentation and iterative design in educational games, arguing that classroom simulations should encourage active participation and adaptation rather than simply replicate traditional lecture formats. [ref: Professor Game Podcast Episode 381, Professor Game]

== Public engagement ==
Harvey's scholarship on celebrity influence, political persuasion, music and politics, and popular culture has attracted national and international media attention.

His research has been discussed or cited in major newspapers and wire services including The New York Times, The Washington Post, Reuters, the Associated Press, and USA Today. [ref: Send in the Juggalos: Harris Gets a Little Help From Insane Clown Posse. Endorsements, how do they work?, The New York Times] [ref: The industry — and the academy — are torn on how to handle Will Smith's Oscars slap, The Washington Post] [ref: Politicians seek to leverage celebrities to reach voters, Associated Press] [ref: Elton John, more stars return to the White House under Biden. But are people listening?, USA Today] [ref: Which Hollywood stars are hitting the road for Harris?, Reuters] His work has also been featured in magazines and cultural publications including Rolling Stone, The Hollywood Reporter, Newsweek, and The Hill. [ref: Is Politics Infiltrating Country Music's History of Charity Work?, Rolling Stone] [ref: You Don't Want to Overdo the Hollywood, The Hollywood Reporter] [ref: Celebrities rail against Trump's policies — but hesitate to say his name, The Hill] [ref: The Confusing History of How Super Mario Bros Became an Anti-Woke Symbol, Newsweek] Additional international coverage has appeared in The Times and Der Spiegel and other outlets. [ref: Star power: Will Hollywood help or hurt Biden's re-election chances?, The Times] [ref: Wahlkampf mit Vorband, Der Spiegel] Harvey has also appeared as a subject-matter expert for national and international broadcasters including PBS NewsHour, BBC News, BBC World Service, BBC Radio 4, CNN, CNN International, CBC, NPR, Reuters, and Al Arabiya. [ref: Do celebrity endorsements matter? A look at the role of pop stars in modern politics, PBS NewsHour] [ref: From Sinatra to Taylor Swift: 100 years of celebrity political endorsements, CBC Radio] [ref: Remember when 'The Oprah Winfrey Show' made us listen to each other, CNN] [ref: Do celebrity political endorsements make a difference? A look back at history, NPR] [ref: Celebrity Star Power Takes Over the Election, Al Arabiya]

His commentary has addressed celebrity endorsements, issue advocacy, political communication, campaign music, public opinion, fandom, and media influence. [ref: Do celebrity endorsements matter? A look at the role of pop stars in modern politics, PBS NewsHour] [ref: Do celebrity political endorsements make a difference? A look back at history, NPR] [ref: CBC News Network's Aarti Pole speaks with author and professor Mark Harvey, CBC News] During the 2024 United States presidential election and its aftermath, Harvey was frequently interviewed regarding celebrity endorsements, celebrity credibility, political identity, campaign music, fandom, and the political influence of public figures such as Taylor Swift, Oprah Winfrey, Beyoncé, Bruce Springsteen, Elon Musk, and Bad Bunny. [ref: Celebrity Endorsements in the 2024 Election, BBC Radio 4] [ref: Celebrity Endorsements Role in the US Election, CNN] [ref: CBC News Network's Aarti Pole speaks with author and professor Mark Harvey, CBC News] [ref: The World Today, BBC World Service]

Harvey has also discussed games, simulations, and active learning in educational media focused on game-based learning and pedagogy, including appearances on the Games in Schools and Libraries podcast and the Professor Game podcast. [ref: GSL 156: Teaching Political Science Through Games, Games in Schools and Libraries] [ref: Professor Game Podcast Episode 381, Professor Game]

== Selected works ==

=== Books ===

* Celebrity Influence: Politics, Persuasion, and Issue-Based Advocacy (University Press of Kansas, 2017).
* Games and Simulations in the Political Science Classroom: Games Without Frontiers (co-editor, Routledge, 2023).
* Short Games and Active Learning in Political Science: Beating the Clock (co-editor, Routledge, 2026).
=== Selected journal articles ===

* Harvey, Mark. "The Rise of the LP: The Politics of Diffusion Innovation in the Recording Industry." Business History (2016).

* Harvey, Mark. "Politics and Power in the Record Industry: The Beatles, the Beach Boys, and the Album as Art Form." Musicology Australia (2016).

=== Selected essays and commentary ===

* Harvey, Mark (2025). "Trump's attacks on Springsteen and Oprah aren't legally sound. That's not the point." MSNBC.

* Harvey, Mark (2024). "Trump's music break may turn more voters than you think." The Hill.

* Harvey, Mark; Shortle, Allyson; and Walker, Brooklyn (2024). "Study shows Taylor Swift's endorsement may turn off voters Harris needs." The Hill.

data.title: Gianfranco Conti
data.text:
----

Gianfranco Conti is an applied linguist, language educator and author known for developing Extensive Processing Instruction (EPI), an approach to foreign-language teaching. EPI, sometimes described as the "Conti method", has been discussed in research published by the British Council and in professional publications on language education.

Conti has co-authored books with Steve Smith on language pedagogy, listening instruction and memory, including The Language Teacher Toolkit, Breaking the Sound Barrier: Teaching Language Learners How to Listen and Memory: What Every Language Teacher Should Know. His publications have been reviewed in journals including Applied Linguistics, English Australia Journal and Convergence.

== Career ==

Conti has worked as a language teacher and teacher educator in primary, secondary and higher education. His professional work has addressed second-language acquisition, memory, listening instruction, curriculum design and classroom pedagogy.

In October 2023, Conti delivered professional-development sessions for teachers from secondary schools and some primary schools in Guernsey. The Bailiwick Express reported on the training, which focused on EPI and the MARS EARS framework, alongside changes in French teaching at Les Beaucamps High School and increased uptake of GCSE French there. [ref: Metacognitive strategies prove successful, Bailiwick Express]

In May 2026, the Ballarat Times reported on a professional-development event in Victoria, Australia, attended by more than 100 language teachers, at which Conti discussed his approach to language teaching. [ref: Engaging students in language key, expert says, Ballarat Times] In February 2026, the Gorey Guardian profiled Conti ahead of a planned professional-development conference in County Wexford, Ireland. The article reported that more than 50 teachers had attended his previous workshop in 2024 and quoted French teacher Karen Murphy on his influence within language-teaching networks and the use of his instructional methods. [ref: World renowned language specialist set to return to Wexford, Gorey Guardian]

== Extensive Processing Instruction ==

Conti developed Extensive Processing Instruction (EPI), a language-teaching approach emphasising repeated processing of language patterns and multiword units, scaffolded practice and progression towards independent language use. [ref: Content and language integrated learning and extensive processing instruction: A useful partnership for language teaching?, British Educational Research Association]

The approach uses sentence builders and structured listening, reading, speaking and writing activities. It is associated with the MARS EARS instructional sequence: modelling, awareness-raising, receptive processing, structured production, expansion, autonomy, routinisation and spontaneity.

=== Commentary and professional reception ===

In 2021, Elisabeth Wallmann examined EPI in an article published by the British Educational Research Association, discussing its possible relationship with content and language integrated learning (CLIL). She considered potential benefits and limitations, including questions concerning vocabulary range and cultural content.

Sonja Fedrizzi described adapting Conti's MARS EARS framework for blended and remote language teaching during the COVID-19 pandemic in Scottish Languages Review. [ref: Modern Languages during a pandemic: how instructional videos, Conti's MARSEARS framework and strong routines have enriched my practice, Scottish Languages Review] The approach has also been discussed in Babel, the journal of the Australian Federation of Modern Language Teachers Associations, in practitioner accounts of classroom teaching. [ref: From Silence to Socialising, Babel]

In March 2022, Camille Robinson published an article on the French-language website of tutoring company GoStudent examining Conti's language-teaching methodology, professional background and associated classroom activities. [ref: Apprendre les langues grâce à la méthode Gianfranco Conti, GoStudent]

In the July 2022 issue of Languages Victoria, published by the Modern Language Teachers' Association of Victoria, Andrea Truckenbrodt cited Conti and Smith's work in an article about scaffolding writing with visuals. [ref: Scaffolding writing using visuals, Languages Victoria] The same issue announced a professional-development workshop on EPI and MARS EARS led by Conti. [ref: MLTAV Professional Learning, Languages Victoria]

=== Educational policy commentary ===

In September 2026, Ian Collen of Queen's University Belfast cited Conti's views on vocabulary selection in an article for The Conversation about proposed curriculum reforms in Northern Ireland. Collen distinguished the frequency of words in language corpora from their relevance to younger language learners, drawing on Conti's argument. [ref: Proposed curriculum in Northern Ireland would restrict children's language learning, The Conversation]

=== Postgraduate research ===

In a postgraduate research proposal dated June 2022, Julia Katharina Hegarty outlined a proposed mixed-methods investigation of EPI in relation to French learners' speaking and writing self-efficacy and proficiency. The proposal also described her introduction of elements of EPI into French teaching across Years 7–12 at an Australian school beginning in 2018. As a research proposal, the document did not report completed intervention findings. [ref: A New Pathway to “I Can Do French”: Using Mixed-Methods to Explore E.P.I. & Its Contribution to French Speaking and Writing Self-Efficacy and Proficiency]

Extensive Processing Instruction has also been the subject of postgraduate research. A 2023 King's College London MA dissertation by Kate Trafford examined the potential of EPI in secondary language teaching in England, with particular reference to learner motivation and GCSE outcomes. The dissertation has not been independently verified from a publicly accessible institutional copy, and its title should not be interpreted as establishing improved outcomes. [ref: An exploration of the potential of the pedagogical framework Extensive Processing Instruction (E.P.I) in secondary language teaching and learning to increase motivation and outcomes at GCSE level in England, King's College London]

A 2026 applied research project attributed to Casey Creel, Embedding the MARS EARS Instructional Framework into IB DP German B: An Organizational Tool, concerns the use of MARS EARS in International Baccalaureate German teaching. Its bibliographic details and findings require confirmation from the original work.

=== British Council Language Trends reports ===

The British Council's Language Trends England 2022 report identified EPI as an approach based on Conti's work, sometimes referred to as the "Conti method". It found that 73% of responding state secondary schools regularly or occasionally used EPI resources with Year 7 and Year 8 pupils. In answers to an open-ended question about what was working well, EPI was mentioned 85 times and Conti 68 times; the report described a significant majority of those comments as positive. [ref: Language Trends England 2022, British Council]

The British Council's Language Trends Northern Ireland 2023 report also discussed EPI in relation to cognitive load and vocabulary learning, explicitly attributing the approach to Conti and noting that it was sometimes called the "Conti method". The report included an account from a secondary school that had redesigned its Key Stage 3 language provision around the approach. [ref: Language Trends Northern Ireland 2023: Language teaching in primary and post-primary schools, British Council Northern Ireland]

In the 2025 report, approximately one-third of responding schools mentioned EPI when asked about their department's preferred pedagogical approach. The report included accounts of schools using EPI throughout Years 7–11, combining it with other approaches, or preferring alternative methods. [ref: Language Trends England 2025, British Council]

The 2026 report stated that just over half of the 474 schools answering the relevant question reported adopting EPI. It described the approach with reference to structured input, sentence builders, repetition and MARS EARS. [ref: Language Trends England 2026, British Council]

The findings use different survey questions and measures and should not be interpreted as directly comparable estimates of changes in adoption over time.

=== Government evaluation ===

A Department for Education-commissioned evaluation of language programmes in England included an anonymised case study entitled "Beech School: success with sentence builders". The evaluation described the school's use of the Conti approach, identified as EPI, and reported teachers' accounts of its role in consolidating vocabulary and grammar. [ref: Language programmes evaluation: interim report, Department for Education]

=== International implementation ===

In 2020, Russian-language teacher Elena Huston described adapting elements of Conti's approach to teaching with authentic Russian-language materials. Writing for Language Solutions, she called her adaptation "Authentic Language Learning with the Conti Method" and discussed scaffolded practice, high-frequency language, sentence builders and authentic texts. [ref: Authentic language learning with the Conti method, Language Solutions]

Bangkok Patana School in Thailand reported in January 2023 that its secondary languages faculty had reviewed its Key Stage 3 curriculum following professional development with Conti. The school described work with French, Mandarin and Spanish teachers and a related event attended by educators from other international schools. [ref: Language Learning with Dr Conti, Bangkok Patana School]

In Australia, the Australian Council for Educational Research published an interview about language teaching at Alfred Deakin High School in Canberra that discussed strategies based on Conti's methods. [ref: Q&A: Supporting and extending students in their language learning at Alfred Deakin High School, Australian Council for Educational Research]

Schools in the United Kingdom that have described using EPI or related Conti–Smith approaches include St Margaret's School for Girls in Aberdeen, Redhill School, Diss High School, Richard Rose Central Academy and Sandy Secondary School. [ref: Modern Languages, St Margaret's School for Girls] [ref: MFL Curriculum, Redhill School] [ref: Modern Foreign Languages, Diss High School] [ref: Modern Foreign Languages, Richard Rose Central Academy] [ref: MFL Curriculum, Sandy Secondary School]

These institutional accounts document reported implementation rather than independently established comparative effectiveness.

== Publications ==

=== The Language Teacher Toolkit ===

Conti and Steve Smith co-authored The Language Teacher Toolkit, first published in 2016. The book addresses language-teaching theory and classroom practice. Angele Ann Andrews reviewed its second edition in Convergence in 2024, discussing its theoretical coverage, practical activities and limitations. [ref: Review of The Language Teacher Toolkit, Second Edition, Convergence]

=== Use in teacher education ===

Conti and Steve Smith's The Language Teacher Toolkit has been included in reading materials for postgraduate teacher education. The University of Roehampton listed the book among the essential readings for its secondary Modern Foreign Languages PGCE course in its 2022 pre-course guidance. [ref: MFL Secondary PGCE: Pre-course reading and activities, University of Roehampton] The University of Leicester included it in its 2023–24 secondary Modern Languages PGCE subject guide as a source of practical teaching advice. [ref: Secondary PGCE Modern Languages Subject Guide 2023–24, University of Leicester School of Education]

A 2024 reading list for trainees in the SWIFT Initial Teacher Training programme recommended Conti and Smith's Breaking the Sound Barrier as optional pre-course reading. [ref: Required Key Reading List: MFL, SWIFT Initial Teacher Training]

In Australia, Conti and Smith's publications have appeared in university language-teacher education course materials. The University of Queensland's EDUC7643 course profile lists editions of The Language Teacher Toolkit and Breaking the Sound Barrier as books for which students require their own copies. [ref: EDUC7643 course profile, The University of Queensland] Australian Catholic University's 2026 EDLA290 unit handbook lists the publications among required texts for language curriculum, pedagogy and assessment. [ref: EDLA290: General Language Curriculum, Pedagogy and Assessment, Australian Catholic University] Macquarie University's unit guide has listed The Language Teacher Toolkit as recommended reading. [ref: Unit guide, Macquarie University]

=== Breaking the Sound Barrier ===

Breaking the Sound Barrier: Teaching Language Learners How to Listen, co-authored with Smith, was published in 2019. Hall Houston reviewed the book in English Australia Journal in 2020. [ref: Breaking the Sound Barrier: Teaching Language Learners How to Listen, English Australia Journal] Rebeca Arndt reviewed it in Applied Linguistics; her review was published online in 2020 and appeared in volume 44, issue 3, in 2023. [ref: Gianfranco Conti and Steve Smith: Breaking the Sound Barrier: Teaching Language Learners How to Listen, Applied Linguistics]

=== Other works ===

Conti and Smith co-authored Memory: What Every Language Teacher Should Know, a book examining memory research and language teaching. Conti has also co-authored Sentence Builders workbooks with Dylan Viñales for French, Spanish, German and Italian.

== Recognition ==

Conti received the Resource Contributor of the Year award at the 2015 TES Schools Awards. [ref: Stars of education celebrate on a night to remember, Tes Magazine]

He has participated in professional-development events organised by Australian language-teaching associations, including the Modern Language Teachers Association of the Australian Capital Territory and the Modern Language Teachers Association of New South Wales. [ref: CONTACT Newsletter 2020, Modern Language Teachers Association of the ACT] [ref: 2026 MLTA NSW Conference: Save the Date, Modern Language Teachers Association of New South Wales]

data.title: Mamoun Abu Nowar
data.text:
----

Mamoun Abu Nowar (born 6 January 1950) is a retired major general of the Royal Jordanian Air Force and a military and strategic analyst. He served in the Royal Jordanian Air Force for more than three decades before retiring in 2000. He later became an analyst on military and strategic affairs and has been interviewed and cited by regional and international media on defence, security, and regional issues. [ref: مأمون أبو نوار, الجزيرة نت] [ref: Jordan fears the crossfire if Gaza war pulls Iran into wider conflict, Reuters] [ref: مأمون أبو نوار: هجوم السلط.. جرس إنذار كبير بالنسبة للأردن, France 24 Arabic]

== Early life and education ==
Abu Nowar was born in Amman on 6 January 1950. He joined the Royal Jordanian Air Force in 1968 and attended the Pakistan Air Force Academy, graduating in 1971. During his military career, he undertook additional specialised training in Jordan and abroad. He later received a master’s degree in political science from Auburn University at Montgomery in the United States, as well as a master’s degree in military science. [ref: مسيرة اللواء مأمون أبو نوار, صراحة نيوز] [ref: ]

== Military career ==
Abu Nowar spent more than thirty years in the Royal Jordanian Air Force, holding several operational and command positions. He commanded No. 9 Squadron and King Faisal Air Base and later served as military secretary to Prince Hassan bin Talal. He retired from military service in 2000 with the rank of major general. [ref: The evolution of Egyptian air defence strategy 1967-1973, King's College London]

== Post-military career, media, and analytical work ==
After retiring from the military, Abu Nowar worked as a military and strategic analyst, commenting on defence, security, military affairs, and regional developments. [ref: في حلب وإدلب بي بي سي تتحقق من مواقع عسكرية سورية تقول المعارضة إنها استطاعت السيطرة عليها, BBC News عربي] [ref: Iran - USA: Neue Spannungen in ganz Nahost?, dw.com]

He has been interviewed or cited by Al Jazeera, Reuters, the BBC, France 24, Deutsche Welle, TRT, and CGTN. His commentary has covered military operations, armed conflicts, regional security, and developments concerning Jordan and the wider Middle East. His views have also been cited by international media and research organisations in coverage and analysis of regional security and military affairs. [ref: ISIL's Tactics in Iraq, Carnegie Endowment for International Peace] [ref: The Heat: A new prime minister might not solve the economic crisis in Jordan, news.cgtn.com] [ref: TRT عربي - استهداف القاعدة الأمريكية بالأردن.. ما الأبعاد واحتمالات التصعيد؟, www.trtarabi.com] [ref: From Telegram to trenches: The Russian page luring Jordanians into war, Middle East Eye] [ref: Jordanian Foreign Minister Visits Syria - Middle East Policy Council]

== Writings ==
Abu Nowar has also written on regional security and military affairs. His articles and analyses have appeared in Al Jazeera and various Arab newspapers and news websites. [ref: ] [ref: أرشيف الكاتب/ مأمون أبو نوار, عربي21]

data.title: Abdelaziz Taleb
data.text:
----

Abdelaziz Taleb (born 1973) is a mixed-media artist, filmmaker [ref: Une seconde édition sous le signe de l'ouverture, Une seconde édition sous le signe de l'ouverture], producer and curator. He grew up in Agadir, Morocco. In 2002, Taleb and Moroccan filmmaker Abdellatif Benfaidoul established Videokaravaan, a nomadic media-art project focused on acquainting the Western audience with media art from Morocco, the Arab world and artists from the diaspora [ref: An Alternative Gaze: A Shared Reflection on Cross-Mediterranean Cooperation in the Arts, European Cultural Foundation]. His short film Ziyara Kassira (Short Visit, 2006) was presented at the International Film Festival Rotterdam in 2007 [ref: Short Visit, IFFR EN]

Early life and education

Taleb studied English literature at university in Agadir, Morocco. In 1999, he received a UNESCO-Aschberg bursary for artists and subsequently undertook a scholarship residency at the Academy of Media Arts Cologne (KHM) [ref: VIDEOKARAVAAN / Ateliers d'arts des médias - Agadir 2006, Maghress] in Germany. During 1999-2000, Taleb produced video works including Tests, Dangerous and Rauchen, which appeared in OVNI's 2000 Moroccan video programme in Barcelona [ref: ]

Career

In the early 2000s, Taleb and Benfaidoul brought the Videokaravaan project to Morocco, especially to Agadir [ref: Videokaravaan à Agadir, Maroc, universes-in-universe.de]. The project was about organising media art workshops series for Moroccan art students and led to the development of many video art works that were produced by Videokaravaan. Taleb was also involved in organising Digital Marrakech, a festival devoted to digital and media arts in Marrakech. In 2012, TelQuel [ref: Événement. Marrakech version Digital, Telquel.ma] identified Taleb and Benfaidoul as the filmmakers and organisers of the festival, whose programme included video, digital art, performances, workshops and discussions on media arts.

In 2003, the Spanish newspaper El País [ref: El extranjero, El País] published an article about the project Videokaravaan and its presentation of contemporary video from Morocco and other Arab countries in Europe. The newspaper identified Taleb as one of the project's founders and discussed the project in connection with contemporary Arab visual culture.

Film work

Taleb directed the short film Ziyara Kassira (Short Visit, 2006), which was presented at the International Film Festival Rotterdam in 2007 [ref: Short Visit, IFFR EN]. He also co-directed Astah (2006) with Abdellatif Benfaidoul. The film was included in the Moroccan retrospective of the Corto Cortissimo section [ref: Venezia, la sezione Corto cortissimo - Corriere della Sera, www.corriere.it] at the 64th Venice International Film Festival in 2007. Taleb participated in Berlinale Talents in 2007 [ref: Abdelaziz Taleb, Berlinale Talents] as a director and screenwriter.

Media art and curatorial work

Besides filmmaking, Taleb has curated many media art programmes and exhibitions. Through Videokaravaan, he developed programmes presenting moving-image work from Morocco, North Africa and the Arab world in European cultural institutions. Taleb also took part in the TransArab programme in Barcelona [ref: ], which brought together artists, filmmakers and cultural practitioners working across the Mediterranean.

In 2011, Taleb curated a series of artistic programmes and projects such as Arab Stereotypes in Western Cinema [ref: Orientalism in Moving images – Arab Media Lab // المختبر العربي لفنون الميديا], a programme also presented by Casa Árabe in Madrid [ref: ] in collaboration with Arab Media Lab. The programme examined representations of Arabs in Western cinema through screenings and public discussions. Taleb gave many seminars [ref: PROGRAM — Black Cloud - Kyiv Biennial 2019, blackcloud.info]and panel discussions around the subject of stereotypes in Western media. He co-directed Silent Film, Big Words (2011) a video work where many fragments from early Hollywood films ( 30's) were re-grouped and the Arab stereotypes is noticeable.

Taleb's recent work also includes multimedia and exhibition projects combining film, video, photography and installation. His solo exhibition Last Years in Babylon [ref: Last year in Babylon solo exhibition by Abdelaziz Taleb – Arab Media Lab // المختبر العربي لفنون الميديا] was shown in Marrakech, Morocco. The exhibition included photography and video installation.

Selected filmography

* Wonderwall (2001)
* Recycling (2002)
* Ziyara Kassira (Short Visit) (2006)
* Astah (2006)
* The Fundamentalist (2009)
* Lost (2017)
* Tazkiyat al-Nafs (Purification of the Soul)
* Fluxus Beat Generation
* Sea of Memory (2020)
* In Limbo (2022)
* Last years in Babylon
* Tangier Chronicles (2026)

data.title: SpenDoe
data.text:
----

SpenDoe is an American hip-hop artist from Santa Cruz, California. His music draws on West Coast hip hop, including the Bay Area-derived mob music style. [ref: Spotlight On: SpenDoe, Crooked Forest] He has also released music under the name M. Aundre. [ref: Meet M. Aundre, Bold Journey]

== Career ==
In December 2006, the BBC Asian Network included SpenDoe's song "Unforgettable" in "Friction's Top Five" on Bobby Friction's program; the surviving page lists the song second. [ref: Friction's Top Five, BBC Asian Network] The song also appeared on the network's The Hype Show playlist in February 2007. [ref: The Hype Show playlist, BBC Asian Network]

In September 2019, SpenDoe was featured on the cover and interviewed in the first issue of 41510 Magazine. [ref: SpenDoe, 41510 Magazine] In 2020, the California Black Media article "A Deadly Mix: Hip Hop Mashed Up With Opioid Abuse in California" noted his collaboration with Sacramento rapper Mozzy on "Omertà". [ref: A Deadly Mix: Hip Hop Mashed Up With Opioid Abuse in California, The Observer]

During 2021, several music publications reviewed SpenDoe's singles. We Write About Music discussed the acoustic-guitar opening, bass, synthesizers and vocal delivery of "Foreign to Me", while Australian publication Stimulate Your Soul characterized it as combining a West Coast sound with Mediterranean-influenced instrumentation. [ref: California Artist SpenDoe Drops Fresh New Single 'Foreign To Me', Stimulate Your Soul] Italian publication Indie Italia and French publication Indie Chronique reviewed "Changing Lanes", describing its forceful flow and mixture of old-school hip-hop, funk and groove. [ref: SpenDoe 'Changing Lanes' - A testa alta, Indie Italia] [ref: Entre vrai hip-hop et groove avec SpenDoe, Indie Chronique]

SpenDoe and Sacramento rapper-producer C-DUBB released the collaborative project Professional Mobbin: The Cali Way. In 2022, Crooked Forest published an interview with SpenDoe centered on "To the Top", his collaboration with producer Sureet Sandhu and his West Coast influences.

Under the M. Aundre name, he released "Altered State" in 2023. Writing for EARMILK, Malvika Padin characterized the song as nostalgic, West Coast-influenced hip hop with introspective lyrics. [ref: M. Aundre makes a strong impact with debut single 'Altered State', EARMILK]

SpenDoe performed at the 2023 Juneteenth celebration in Drake Park in Bend, Oregon; The Bulletin used a photograph of his performance as the lead image in its coverage of the event. [ref: Juneteenth celebrated in Bend with photos, festival and memories, The Bulletin] In October 2023, he released the five-track West Coast EP, produced primarily by C-DUBB with an additional contribution from Vallejo producer the Slapmaster. Lyrics & Threads described the project as drawing from the Bay Area mob-music tradition and highlighted the reflective writing and relaxed delivery of "Rollin Up". [ref: SpenDoe Takes Us on a West Coast Journey with "WEST COAST" EP, Lyrics & Threads] That year, SpenDoe also appeared on "Official", from San Quinn and C-DUBB's collaborative album The Mob Hour Continues, opening the song's first verse. [ref: Official – San Quinn, C-DUBB, SpenDoe, Russell Falcon, Folded Waffle]

In 2024, French music publication Extravafrench reviewed "C.O.A.", a C-DUBB-produced track from Name 100, describing its bass-heavy trap production as drawing on the 1990s Bay Area mob-music tradition and emphasizing ambition and perseverance. [ref: L'Éclat d'un Artiste Entre Hustle et Floss: voici SpenDoe sur « C.O.A. », Extravafrench] Last Day Deaf subsequently reviewed the EP. [ref: Listening Now: SpenDoe - Name 100, Last Day Deaf]

Coverage of the Name 100 single "Smiles and Cries" appeared in PopFad, The Urban Juice, Korliblog, and LandonBuford.com. The reviews discussed its synth-driven production and themes of adversity, resilience and the contrasting experiences of life. [ref: A Brand New Release by Violet Jane and Another Single to Explore, PopFad] [ref: Santa Cruz Rapper Spendoe Explores Life's Duality in New Single 'Smiles and Cries', The Urban Juice] [ref: Hip-Hop's Hidden Gem: SpenDoe's 'Smiles and Cries' Single Review, Korliblog] [ref: SpenDoe reflects on life's highs and lows in 'Smiles and Cries', LandonBuford.com]

In May 2025, Sway's Universe selected "Name 100" for its weekly SU SoundWave feature, identifying SpenDoe as an independent Santa Cruz artist and discussing the track's West Coast production by C-DUBB. [ref: SU SoundWave Picks of the Week: Kevin McGee, SpenDoe, Maliibu Miitch and More, Sway's Universe]

In 2026, SpenDoe appeared on Day Day's "From the Bay", from the album My Elevation (M.E.). The track was produced by Funk Daddy. [ref: Day Day Drops "From the Bay" from New Album My Elevation (M.E.), The Urban Juice] [ref: North Cali's Finest: Day Day and SpenDoe Rep the Culture in "From the Bay", Fenomen Mag] World Wide Hip Hop credited SpenDoe as the album's executive producer. [ref: West Coast Rap Artist Day Day Releases New Album "My Elevation (M.E.)", World Wide Hip Hop]

== Selected releases ==
* Surviving the Mob Era (2020) [ref: Surviving the Mob Era - Album by SpenDoe, Apple Music]
* Professional Mobbin: The Cali Way (with C-DUBB, 2020) [ref: SpenDoe & C-Dubb - Professional Mobbin The Cali Way, Rap Music Guide]

data.title: Ignacio Orellana
data.text:
Ignacio Orellana is a Chilean musician, drummer, photographer, videographer associated with Pirosaint and Quemasantos. [ref: A conversation with Pirosaint drummer/ NYC photographer/videographer Ignacio Orellana on new album ‘Know Thyself’, Metal Insider] [ref: Unearthing The Metal Underground: The Chilean Scene Part 2, Metal Underground]

== Background and early life ==

Orellana is from Santiago, Chile. Metal Underground reported that he began playing drums at age 14 and became involved in the Chilean metal scene during his teenage years. [ref: Unearthing The Metal Underground: The Chilean Scene Part 2, Metal Underground]

In 2002, Orellana moved to Poughkeepsie, New York, where he continued working on music with Pirosaint and developing media projects connected with Chilean metal in the United States. [ref: Unearthing The Metal Underground: The Chilean Scene Part 2, Metal Underground]

Orellana studied television production in Chile. In a 2021 interview with Metal Insider, he stated that he holds a degree in television and that his background in audio and video production contributed to his media work. [ref: A conversation with Pirosaint drummer/ NYC photographer/videographer Ignacio Orellana on new album ‘Know Thyself’, Metal Insider]

== Music career ==

In 2021, Pirosaint released Know Thyself. Metal Insider reported that the album was recorded during sessions held between 2013–2016 and 2020–2021 at Oily Sound Studios in NYC, and identified Orellana as Pirosaint's drummer as well as a photographer and videographer. [ref: A conversation with Pirosaint drummer/ NYC photographer/videographer Ignacio Orellana on new album ‘Know Thyself’, Metal Insider]

Orellana has also worked with Quemasantos. In 2026, Metal Insider reported that he composed the music and arrangements, as well as the recording, mixing, and mastering for the album Stranded in Hell at Oily Sound Studios in New York City, while vocalist Nelson Díaz developed the story and lyrical concept. [ref: Quemasantos announce new ambitious concept album ‘Stranded in Hell’, Metal Insider]

== Other musical work ==

In 2011, Orellana served as temporary touring drummer for Sacred Oath after its original drummer Kenny Evans suffered a back injury. Metal Underground reported that Orellana replaced Evans for several dates on the band's October–November 2011 tour. [ref: Pirosaint Working On First New Material In Fifteen Years, Metal Underground]

In 2017, Orellana joined the New York heavy metal band Metalfier as drummer. Metal Underground reported that he had already performed with the band in New Jersey and later appeared with Metalfier at Irving Plaza in New York City before the band formally announced him as a member. [ref: Metalfier Announce New Drummer Ignacio Orellana, Metal Underground]

== Media and photography ==

Orellana is a professional photographer, videographer, interviewer, and music-media producer in New York City. Metal Insider described him as a New York City photographer and videographer in addition to his work as a musician, and noted his work with music-media outlets. [ref: A conversation with Pirosaint drummer/ NYC photographer/videographer Ignacio Orellana on new album ‘Know Thyself’, Metal Insider]

His concert photography has been published by WPDH. In 2015, the station identified Orellana as a professional photographer associated with PoughkeepsieMETAL and published his photographs from performances by Testament and Extreme at The Chance Theater in Poughkeepsie, New York. [ref: Testament Rocks the Chance [PHOTOS], WPDH] [ref: EXTREME Rocks The Chance [PHOTOS], WPDH]

Orellana has also conducted artist interviews through ArmyOfOneTV. In 2010, Blabbermouth reported that he interviewed Cage vocalist Sean Peck at The Chance Theater in Poughkeepsie, New York. [ref: CAGE Frontman Interviewed By ArmyOfOneTV (Video), Blabbermouth.net] Blabbermouth later credited Orellana with recording an ArmyOfOneTV interview with Epica guitarist Mark Jansen in New York City. [ref: EPICA Guitarist On Group's Wide-Ranging Influences: 'Name It, And We Have Used It In Our Music', Blabbermouth.net]

Metal Underground documented Orellana's development of music-media projects including Chileanmetal, Digmetalworld, Bocasucia and ArmyOfOneTV. The publication described ArmyOfOneTV as an interview series featuring bands passing through New York City and discussed his efforts to provide exposure for Chileanmetal artists. [ref: Unearthing The Metal Underground: The Chilean Scene Part 2, Metal Underground]

Metal Underground separately described Digmetalworld as a New York metal label and distributor specializing in South American metal bands. [ref: Digmetalworld Offering Albums For Free Download, Metal Underground]

== Selected works ==

=== With Downfire ===
* Damnation (2010) – drums. [ref: Damnation – Downfire, AllMusic] [ref: Downfire – Damnation, Metal Temple]

=== With Pirosaint ===
* Know Thyself (2021) – drums and recording work. [ref: A conversation with Pirosaint drummer/ NYC photographer/videographer Ignacio Orellana on new album ‘Know Thyself’, Metal Insider]

=== With Quemasantos ===
* Stranded in Hell (2026) – composition, arrangements, recording, mixing, and mastering. [ref: Quemasantos announce new ambitious concept album ‘Stranded in Hell’, Metal Insider]

data.title: Charu Gandhi
data.text:
----

Charu Gandhi is a London-based architect and interior designer, and the founder and director of interior design studio Elicyon. [ref: Art Deco at 100: love it or loathe it?, www.ft.com] [ref: My Favourite Pieces: Charu Gandhi’s storytelling Indian roots reflected in her, Financial Times] [ref: ] [ref: Designer Profile: Charu Gandhi, Homes and Gardens]

== Early Life & Education ==

Gandhi was born in Delhi, India. She attended boarding school in Singapore before moving to the United Kingdom in 1997 to study at the Architectural Association School of Architecture in London.

== Career ==

Gandhi began her career in architecture, working on residential and large-scale projects at the firm Allies & Morrison. [ref: Air purifiers and ‘appliance garages’: The elite nurseries of the super-rich, The Telegraph] She later joined the property development company Candy & Candy, [ref: An Interview With… Charu Gandhi - Martyn White] where she focused on private residential commissions, notably at One Hyde Park in London.

In 2014, Gandhi founded the design studio Elicyon, an interior design studio and BIID Registered Design Practice, [ref: ] specialising in high-end projects for private clients and developers in the UK and internationally.

Gandhi’s work has been featured in publications including the Financial Times, Architectural Digest, Vogue, The Telegraph and ELLE. [ref: Forget wine cellars: why 'whisky walls' are the newest trend in luxury interiors, The Telegraph] [ref: Charu Gandhi - Spear's 500 Adviser Profile - Interiors Index, Spears 500] [ref: Interior designer Charu Gandhi on the jewellery that tells a story of love and resilience, ELLE Decoration]

== Work & Style ==

Gandhi’s studio has worked on a range of high-end residential, commercial and hospitality projects, including developments such as Chelsea Barracks in London, The Old War Office Residences in Westminster, and international private residences at One Palm Jumeirah in Dubai. [ref: House Style: Charu Gandhi, Portfolio by Savills] [ref: Behind the Design with Charu Gandhi: The OWO Raffles Residences, www.luxdeco.com] [ref: Charu Gandhi designed this London home around one very fashionable problem, Architectural Digest India]

data.title: Chiharu Kihara
data.text:
Chiharu Kihara (, Kihara Chiharu, born 1979) is a Japanese painter from Misumi (now Nagato), Yamaguchi Prefecture. A self-taught artist, she is known for her dynamic brushwork and vivid colors depicting animals, insects, and plants, expressing what she calls "vitalism" — the raw energy of living things. [ref: 作家 木原千春 編 / 連載「作家のアイデンティティ」Vol.4, ARToVILLA]

== Early life and career ==
Kihara was born in 1979 in Misumi, Ōtsu District, Yamaguchi Prefecture (now part of Nagato). From an early age, she aspired to become a painter. She was deeply inspired by Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa and the head studies of Francis Bacon, which she encountered in art textbooks, as well as the landscape paintings of Sesshū Tōyō. [ref: 木原千春インタビュー, PEELER]

During high school, while drawing a bamboo shoot in pencil, she experienced what she described as "the sensation of lines coming alive, moving as if they were living creatures themselves," a moment that defined her artistic direction. She dropped out of high school and continued to develop her painting entirely through self-study.

In 1999, she held her first solo exhibition at Gallery Den in Tokyo, marking the formal beginning of her career as an artist.

In 2006, she was selected for the VOCA exhibition (The Vision of Contemporary Art) at the Ueno Royal Museum, Tokyo, which showcases emerging talents in contemporary Japanese art. [ref: 木原千春, Bijutsu Techō]

In 2012, she began her ongoing solo exhibition series Vitalism at roidworksgallery in Tokyo, which has been held almost annually since (except 2014). [ref: ]

In 2015, she participated in the Peko-chan Exhibition at the Hiratsuka Museum of Art, Kanagawa Prefecture.

In 2020, she created the artwork for the main lobby of Hoshino Resorts KAI Nagato in Nagato, Yamaguchi Prefecture. The same year, she held the solo exhibition CREATURES at 3331 Arts Chiyoda, Tokyo, featuring 30 drawings and 5 canvas works. [ref: CREATURES / 木原千春, 3331 Arts Chiyoda]

In December 2024, her first monograph Vitalism was published by Geijutsu Shinbunsha. The book features approximately 120 works spanning from her first solo exhibition in 1999 through to the Vitalism series, with essays by art historian Shimao Arata and contemporary art critic Tsuda Naomi, and a dialogue with comedian Shizuyo Yamasaki of Nankai Candies. [ref: 木原千春作品集 Vitalism, Geijutsu Shinbunsha] [ref: 木原千春 個展「Vitalism Ⅻ」, Ginza Tsutaya Books]

In 2026 (Reiwa 8), Chiharu Kihara received the Yamaguchi Prefecture Art and Culture Promotion Encouragement Award (山口県芸術文化振興奨励賞) from Yamaguchi Prefecture in the painting category of the fine arts division. [ref: 令和8年度文化芸術関係表彰・芸術文化振興奨励賞受賞者, Yamaguchi Prefecture] She is listed among the official recipients for that year, and the award was also covered by KRY Yamaguchi Broadcasting and the Yamaguchi Shimbun. [ref: 陶芸家の田原崇雄さんと画家の木原千春さんが受賞 県芸術文化振興奨励賞表彰式, Livedoor News] [ref: 山口県芸術文化振興奨励賞 萩焼・田原さん、画家・木原さんに/山口県庁で表彰式, Yamaguchi Shimbun]

== Artistic style ==
Kihara's subjects are drawn from the natural world she grew up with in Yamaguchi — animals, insects, plants — as well as portraits of artists she admires. She describes her process as involving hundreds of sketches of each subject until the image and her own sensibility become one, at which point the final work is completed in a single, intense session.

In addition to oil painting, she also produces drawing works she calls "5-minute drawings," which she sells through the online marketplace Mercari.

== Television appearances ==
* 2016 — BS Fuji, Break Zenya: Jisedai no Geijutsuka-tachi (Next Generation Artists)
* 2022 — Nippon Television, THE ART HOUSE: Sono Art wa 100-nen-go ni Nokoseru ka (Can This Art Survive 100 Years?)

== Public art ==
* 2020 — Main lobby artwork, Hoshino Resorts KAI Nagato, Nagato, Yamaguchi Prefecture

== Publications ==
* Chiharu Kihara Art Book: Vitalism, Geijutsu Shinbunsha, December 2024.

== Selected exhibitions ==

=== Solo exhibitions ===
* 1999 — First solo exhibition (Gallery Den, Tokyo)
* 2012 — Vitalism (roidworksgallery, Tokyo); held almost annually thereafter
* 2020 — CREATURES (3331 Arts Chiyoda, Tokyo)
* 2021 — Vitalism IX (roidworksgallery, Tokyo)
* 2022 — Vitalism X (roidworksgallery, Tokyo)
* 2023 — Vitalism XI (roidworksgallery, Tokyo)
* 2024 — Vitalism XII (Ginza Tsutaya Books FOAM CONTEMPORARY / roidworksgallery, Tokyo)
* 2025–2026 — Vitalism ZERO (roidworksgallery, Tokyo)

=== Group exhibitions ===
* 2006 — VOCA 2006: The Vision of Contemporary Art (Ueno Royal Museum, Tokyo)
* 2015 — Peko-chan Exhibition (Hiratsuka Museum of Art, Kanagawa)
* 2022 — face to face Vol.II (Bunkamura Gallery, Tokyo)

data.title: OnlyRoses
data.text:
----

OnlyRoses is a British rose retailer founded in London in 2007 by Anian and Sabine Schmitt. It sells fresh-cut roses and preserved roses under the Infinite Roses name. [ref: The Roses That Might Last Longer Than Your Relationship, Vogue] [ref: London-Based Rose Retailer Opens First U.S. Location, Retail TouchPoints] In 2019, OnlyRoses supplied roses for the stage design of the 91st Academy Awards. [ref: David Korins' Renderings For The 2019 Oscars, Live Design]

== History ==
OnlyRoses began in London in 2007 as a retailer specialising in roses. By 2017, it had expanded through franchise locations in Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Doha, Riyadh and Kuwait City. Trade publication FloralDaily reported that the company's Abu Dhabi store at Nation Towers was its largest at the time. [ref: A flower shop dedicated to roses only, FloralDaily]

In 2017, OnlyRoses established a retail presence in Beverly Hills, California. [ref: Madonna-Loved Flower Shop OnlyRoses Will Open Its First U.S. Boutique in Beverly Hills, The Hollywood Reporter] Interior Design reported that the approximately 550-square-foot boutique was designed by Italian firm Baciocchi Associati. [ref: OnlyRoses Debuts Los Angeles Outpost by Baciocchi Associati, Interior Design] A December 2017 feature in 805 Living described the boutique as the London brand's first United States location and reported that it stocked fresh Ecuadorian roses and preserved Infinite Roses. [ref: World-Class Weekend, 805 Living]

== Products ==
OnlyRoses sells fresh-cut roses and preserved roses marketed as Infinite Roses. Vogue reported in 2018 that OnlyRoses had introduced Infinite Roses in 2010 and sourced its roses from farms near Quito, Ecuador. According to the magazine, the preserved roses could last up to a year without water. Co-founder Sabine Schmitt told Vogue that the rose heads and stems were preserved separately before being reassembled.

== 2019 Academy Awards ==
Production designer David Korins incorporated approximately 40,000 red preserved roses supplied by OnlyRoses, marketed as Infinite Roses, into scenic elements for the 91st Academy Awards, including a floral interpretation of the Oscar statuette. Korins described the roses' role in creating a warmer stage setting in interviews with Interior Design and Galerie. [ref: Behind-the-Scenes Q&A with 2019 Oscars Set Designer David Korins, Interior Design] [ref: Go Behind the Scenes of the Dazzling Swarovski-Adorned Oscars Stage, Galerie] Ecuadorian newspaper El Universo reported that the roses came from Ecuador. [ref: 40.000 rosas preservadas de Ecuador adornaron el escenario de los Premios Oscar 2019, El Universo]

data.title: Echo Huang Shaomei
data.text:
Echo Huang Shaomei, (Chinese: 黃少媚) is a Hong Kong business executive who has served as chief executive officer and an executive director of New World Development since November 2024. [ref: Hong Kong developer New World appoints another CEO after only two months, Reuters] [ref: New World CEO to Leave After Two Months in Succession Saga, Bloomberg News] [ref: New World Development names Huang Shaomei CEO as Eric Ma resigns after 2 months, South China Morning Post]. She is also a director of New World China Land and vice-chairman and an executive director of New World Department Store China. [ref: Ms. Huang Shaomei, Echo, New World Development] [ref: Appointment of Vice-Chairman and Executive Director, HKEXnews]

==Career==
Huang joined New World China Land as deputy chief executive officer in October 2015. She became its chief executive officer in February 2020 and was appointed an executive director of New World Development in May 2020. [ref: 21st Century Business Herald] [ref: Asia Real Estate People in the News 2024-12-02, mingtiandi]

In November 2024, Huang was appointed chief executive officer of New World Development, succeeding Eric Ma Siu-cheung after two months in the role. [ref: Echo Huang Shaomei appointed as Chief Executive Officer of NWD, The Standard] [ref: New World Development names new CEO following Eric Ma's sudden departure, Marketing-Interactive]

In January 2026, she was appointed vice-chairman and an executive director of New World Department Store China and chair of its executive committee.

==Public roles==
In July 2026, Huang was appointed a non-official Justice of the Peace in Hong Kong. [ref: Honours 2026: 65 People Appointed Justices of the Peace, Including Christine Lee, Huang Shaomei, Yeung Mei-chun and Cheung Lee-kar-wai, HK01] [ref: New World's Huang Shaomei, MTR's Yeung Mei-chun and Other Business Figures Appointed Justices of the Peace, Ming Pao] [ref: Persons appointed under Section 3(1)(b) of the Justices of the Peace Ordinance (Cap. 510) (commonly known as "Non-official JPs"), Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region]

data.title: Lindsay LeBlanc
data.text:
Lindsay LeBlanc (born 1989) is an American-born glass artist and educator based in County Leitrim, Ireland. She is known for flameworked glass botanical studies and installations that explore ecology, decay and transformation through what she terms an "ecogothic" lens. [ref: Lindsay LeBlanc — Artist in Residence, Leitrim Sculpture Centre]

== Early life and education ==
LeBlanc was born in the United States in 1989. She studied sculpture and glass at the Massachusetts College of Art and Design in Boston, completing a BFA, and later earned an MFA in art and ecology at Burren College of Art in County Clare. [ref: Artistic License: Glass Artist Lindsay LeBlanc, The Gloss]

== Career ==
LeBlanc has worked with glass since 2009, specialising in glassblowing, kiln-forming, flameworking, casting and large-scale installation. [ref: New Leitrim exhibition explores what survives in the boglands, Leitrim Observer] Her practice draws on scientific observation, ecological history and speculative thinking, and she describes an "EcoGothic" approach informed by folklore, environmental history and overlooked ecologies such as lichens, weeds and ruins.

Her solo exhibition The Long Pause: Ecology of Ruins I was held at the Leitrim Sculpture Centre in Manorhamilton from April to May 2026. The four-room installation explored a blanket bog in Kiltyclogher on the Irish border, working with reclaimed materials, foraged glass, moving image and sound to trace abandoned objects in the bogland landscape.

In 2026 she co-curated Of Sand and Ash, an exhibition of contemporary glass for the Glass Society of Ireland, with Ava Hayes at the National Design & Craft Gallery in Kilkenny. [ref: Of Sand and Ash — DCCI/NDCG, Design & Crafts Council Ireland] She serves on the board of the Glass Society of Ireland.

In August 2026 she curated THREADS: Time, Memory and Material at the Cashel Arts Festival. [ref: THREADS: Time, Memory and Material — curated by Lindsay LeBlanc, Cashel Arts Festival] Her glass botanical works are exhibited and sold through Blowfish Glass in Stourbridge, England, including in the gallery's international Fifteen x Fifteen 2026 exhibition. [ref: Lindsay LeBlanc — Blowfish Glass, Blowfish Glass] [ref: Fifteen x Fifteen 2026, Blowfish Glass]

== Awards ==
* 2024 Jutta Cuny-Franz Talent Prize [ref: The Jutta Cuny-Franz Memorial Award, Kunstpalast]
* Sculpture in Context Goodbody Award [ref: LooLooGlass — DCCI member directory, Design & Crafts Council Ireland]

[ref: Παπαρρηγοπούλου, Ελένη-Χρυσηίς (Λένα), ΒΙΒΛΙΟΝΕΤ] [ref: Eleni Chrysiis Paparrigopoulou, Foundation for Interdisciplinary Studies and New Technologies]

data.title: Allison Matulli
data.text:
----

Dr. Allison Matulli, a native of Trinidad and Tobago, is a Florida-based children's author, educator, legal scholar and First Amendment advocate. [ref: Dr. Allison Matulli, PEN America] She is the author of Your Freedom, Your Power: A Kid's Guide to the First Amendment (2023), published by Running Press Kids/Hachette Book Group, a book that highlights the true stories of brave kids that sparked change in their communities and left their mark on the legal history of the United States of America, as well as guiding young readers to be active and conscious citizens. [ref: Allison Matulli, Hachette Book Group] Her new Penguin RISE picture book, WE ARE FREE (September 2026), takes this mission a step further and aims to introduce children ages 0 to 5 to their First Freedoms [ref: ]

Dr.Matulli is the founder and executive director of The Little Lawyers, an award-winning organization that focuses on empowering children through the understanding of their constitutional rights, civic engagement and social justice. [ref: HOME, The Little Lawyers] As a former school administrator and first-ever Florida International University's Fulbright Global Scholar, she is now a fellow for the First Amendment at the Freedom Forum, where she shares her expertise on student free expression and digital speech rights. [ref: Dr. Allison Matulli, PEN America]

Allison Matulli is a graduate of the civic legacy of Howard University School of Law and works as a Pre-Law Technical Writing lecturer at the same institution, where she was elected for the first faculty cohort of the Google Career Launchpad Generative AI Leader Certification Program. [ref: ] Dr. Matulli has recently published her doctoral dissertation Free Speech and Digital Citizenship: A Qualitative Case Study with St. Thomas University, and is affiliate faculty at FIU's Maurice A.Ferre Institute for Civic Leadership. Her research about freedom of expression expands internationally, including landmark work in Colombia, Italy and Trinidad and Tobago. [ref: ]

Her advocacy work have led her to connect with families and young people as a keynote speaker at events and book readings, partnering with organizations like PEN America. [ref: Your Freedom, Your Power Hour! A Family Day of Stories & Creativity, PEN America] In 2023, Matulli was named one of Miami's most prominent and influential black women in business and industry by Legacy Magazine, [ref: Legacy Magazine Archives, M•I•A Media Group] and in 2024 one of South Florida's most prominent and influential black business leaders by the Miami Media Group. [ref: Archives, M•I•A Media Group]

data.title: Fatima bint Aqil
data.text:
Fatimah bint Aqil ibn Abi Talib (Arabic: فاطمة بنت عقيل بن أبي طالب) She was a daughter of Aqil ibn Abi Talib, the elder brother of Ali ibn Abi Talib, making her his niece. [ref: Nasab Quraysh] According to Musʿab al-Zubayri’s Nasab Quraysh, she was one of Aqil’s daughters, whose mothers were different ummhat awlad (enslaved women). Her sisters included Umm Hani (Ramlah), Zaynab, Zaynab al-Sughra, and Umm Luqman. [ref: Nasab Quraysh] She later married Ali ibn Yazid ibn Rukānah of Banu Abd al-Muttalib, [ref: The Ansab al-Ashraf of al-Baladhuri, University Press] and they had children.

==Elegies==
Ibn Abd Rabbih's al-ʿIqd al-Farīd attributes an elegy to an unnamed daughter of Aqil ibn Abi Talib, mourning Husayn ibn Ali and those killed with him. [ref: Ibn ʿAbd Rabbih, al-ʿIqd al-Farīd, vol. 5, p. 132.] A later report in al-Qunduzī's Yanabi' al-Mawadda identifies the daughter of Aqil who composed the elegy as Fatimah bint Aqil. [ref: al-Qunduzī, Yanabi' al-Mawadda, vol. 3, p. 153.]

The elegy begins:

“O my eyes, shed tears and lament,and mourn for the family of the Messenger.Six of them, all descended from Ali, were struck down,and five from the family of Aqil”. [ref: ʿAlī Ṣāliḥ Rasan al-Muḥammadāwī, ʿAqīl ibn Abī Ṭālib bayna al-ḥaqīqa wa-l-shubha, p. 145, citing al-Qundūzī, Yanābīʿ al-Mawadda, vol. 3, p. 153.]

data.title: Sooppy Narikkatteri
data.text:
Sooppy Narikkatteri (also spelled Soopy Narikkattery) is an Indian politician and local governance administrator from Kerala. His public career centers on state-level corporate administration and statutory advisory planning within the Panchayati Raj framework of Kerala. He is the former executive Chairman of the state-level public undertaking, the Kerala Rural Employment and Welfare Society (KREWS), and serves as a working group member under the Chief Minister-chaired Kerala Development and Innovation Strategic Council (K-DISC). Additionally, he holds office as the General Secretary of the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) Kozhikode District Committee.
== Sub-National Public Enterprise and Policy Roles ==
=== KREWS Corporate Oversight ===
Narikkatteri was appointed by the state government as the executive Chairman of the Kerala Rural Employment and Welfare Society (KREWS), serving a five-year tenure from 2011 to 2016. In this role, he directed public sector operations managing asset-creation funds, capital investments for infrastructure development, and state-subsidized labor welfare safety architectures across rural local self-government institutions statewide.
=== K-DISC Strategic Planning ===
In 2021, Narikkatteri was nominated to the Kerala Development and Innovation Strategic Council (K-DISC), a premier strategic think-tank advisory council guided directly by the Chief Minister of Kerala. Operating as part of its decentralized governance working groups, his responsibilities focus on formulating public policy blueprints targeting the growth of grassroots employment ecosystems, rural social innovations, and the structural integration of technology systems into local self-government institutions.
=== Inter-Governmental Negotiations and Legal History ===
• Kerala Grama Panchayat Association: Served as the State General Secretary, managing inter-governmental policy negotiations with the state executive cabinet concerning municipal functional autonomy and fiscal devolution.
• Constitutional Electoral Roll Litigation (2020): Narikkatteri acted as a chief petitioner in a notable legal challenge regarding municipal voter registration roll updates before the High Court of Kerala, resulting in subsequent administrative actions from the State Election Commission and the Supreme Court of India.
== Municipal Governance and Conflict Resolution ==
=== Local Administration Metrics ===
Narikkatteri served three consecutive terms as the President of the Nadapuram Grama Panchayat between 2000 and 2015. His office directed structural workflow adjustments that transitioned the municipal office into the first ISO-certified Grama Panchayat in Kerala. In 2015, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Government of India, awarded his administration the national [[Panchayat Raj Sashaktikaran Puraskar], ranking it as the top-performing rural local body out of over 265,000 grama panchayats nationwide based on auditing compliance, document transparency, and scheme execution metrics. The council also won the state-level [[Swaraj Trophy] during his tenure.
=== The Cross-Party Consultative Model ===
Operating inside a regional jurisdiction historically subject to recurrent inter-party political conflicts, his municipal tenure introduced balanced cross-party consultative committees. This mechanism decoupled local capital expenditures and public utility development from ongoing partisan rivalries, ensuring the completion of rural road networks, water lines, and primary health installations without project delays stemming from localized friction.
== Electoral and Party Positions ==
• 2011 Assembly Election: Nominated as the official UDF candidate to contest the newly drawn Kuttiady Assembly constituency during the 2011 Kerala Legislative Assembly election, finishing as runner-up with a base of 63,286 votes.
• District Executive: Following a multi-year tenure heading the Nadapuram constituency organization as president, a regional reorganization in October 2026 placed him into the office of General Secretary for the IUML Kozhikode District Committee alongside District President T.T. Ismail.
• LGML Presidency: Serves as the active State President of the Local Governance Members League (LGML).

data.title: Justin McNeal
data.text:
Justin Wayne McNeal (born 1976) is an American author, entrepreneur, and information technology professional. He coauthored the technical book The Definitive Guide to Interwoven TeamSite (2006) and has written books on fitness, winemaking, religion, cryptozoology, and other subjects. [ref: The Definitive Guide to Interwoven TeamSite, Springer Nature] [ref: 8 New Wine Making Books Reshaping the Craft in 2025, BookAuthority] His business activities include the digital marketplace RationalIQ and the international dating service SparkMingle.

== Career ==
=== Information technology ===
McNeal has worked in enterprise information technology, including content management and software implementation. In 2006, Apress published The Definitive Guide to Interwoven TeamSite, written by Brian Hastings and McNeal. According to the publisher, Hastings and McNeal were leading a TeamSite upgrade project for MasterCard International when the book was released. The book discusses enterprise content management architecture, deployment, and implementation using the Rational Unified Process. Springer Nature also cites a February 2008 review of the book by B. Hazeltine in ACM Computing Reviews.

=== Publishing ===
McNeal has published nonfiction and children's books in several genres, including technology, fitness, home winemaking, religious writing, personal finance, cooking, and cryptozoology. His works are listed on his Amazon Author page and BookBub author profile. [ref: Justin McNeal — Author Page, Amazon] [ref: Justin McNeal, BookBub]

His 2024 book Home Wine Making for Absolute Beginners: Unlocking the Secrets of Homemade Wines was featured second on BookAuthority's 2025 list of new wine-making books. The list described the book as an introduction to grape selection, fermentation, sanitation, and other winemaking practices.

=== Business ventures ===
==== Rational Solutions and RationalIQ ====
McNeal is associated with Rational Solutions, LLC and RationalIQ, an online marketplace offering downloadable digital products. The RationalIQ website describes its offerings as digital assets for specialized interests and includes an author page for McNeal. [ref: RationalIQ: Your Source for Niche Digital Products, RationalIQ]

==== SparkMingle ====
In 2026, McNeal launched SparkMingle, an online dating service developed with co-founder Cherly Bibar Casuela. The platform focuses on adult relationships, including international connections, and offers member profiles, messaging, and identity-verification features. Its website describes the founders' cross-border relationship as part of the motivation for establishing the service. [ref: Our Founders' Love Story, SparkMingle]

==== Digital media ====
McNeal has produced online content under the SurvivalReviews brand, covering products and preparedness-related subjects. His author profile also links to channels devoted to gaming and food.
