data.title: Jasmin Parkin
data.text:
== Jasmin Parkin! ==
“ You shine, you know that you're the most inspiring person, when you stop crying ” -Jasmin parkin.
Music has the power to express emotion, identity and personal growth. One musician who demonstrates this through her voice, songwriting, and performance is Jasmin Parkin! She is the keyboardist and vocalist for the indie rock band Mother Mother. Jasmin has played an important role in the band providing friendship to the other band members and bringing lively and spiritual energy to Mother Mother. Jasmin has brought a distinctive voice ever since Deabra Jean-Creelman left the band in 2008. Jasmin was born and raised in Vancouver, Canada.

In a 2021 interview,‌ Jasmin states that when she was younger, she was surrounded by music, her father played guitar and had an amazing voice, her mother loved music as well, however her mother got into singing later in life. When Jasmin was Six or Seven years old, she got into piano lessons even though she resented playing piano “the correct way.” Jasmin hated sitting up straight, she states that she became irritated when her teachers corrected her posture describing herself as a rebel. Jasmin later mentions that she wanted to take up Jazz since her name was JASmin, to which a family friend who was also her teacher agrees to teach her jazz only if she learns the blues first which is an important blueprint for jazz. Jasmin’s teacher later realized that she had a good voice and her teacher taught her how to sing and play which later shaped and influenced her early career as a jazz musician (Parkin 2021).

The struggles that Jasmin faced growing up were eating disorders and body positivity. Jasmin states that she struggled with an eating disorder that was not specified, most likely anorexia, from 12 to 16. Later when she discovered social media she realized with the help of other people online, that it was okay to be who she was and that she didn't have to shape herself to the likeness of other people. Jasmin states that she still feels as if she still has habits from her eating disorder today, she describes it as if there is a tiny voice that discourages her every day but she has the strength to ignore it. (Parkin 2021)

During her early career as a solo artist, she performed under the name “The Jasmin Parkin Trio.” Even though the name suggests a group.. with more than one real person, the trio actually consisted of Jasmin and the instruments she performed with, which is why the “group name” was simply just her own name. The Jasmin Parkin Trio is considered a musical group despite having only one real member. The group released only one album titled “No Reason Why”. The album was released on September 3rd, 2003, and contains fourteen tracks. Some songs to note are “My Funny Valentine” “No Reason Why” “Willow Weep for Me” and “Sara.” (Discogs 2003)

A notable song that was written by Jasmin Parkin off of No Reason Why that shows Jasmin Parkin's excellent songwriting is “Sara.” The song focuses on a woman named Sara who is struggling emotionally and feels overwhelmed by her thoughts and experiences. In the first verse, Sara comes home late at night and cries while dwelling on her problems, that tells us that Sara is dealing with  inner conflict. Later the chorus shifts the tone towards encouragement, telling Sara that she is the most inspiring person when she stops crying. This balance between sadness and reassurance suggests the song is not only about pain but also about recognizing Sara's strength. The song is written as if Jasmin is directly confronting her; we can see this by the repeating of Sara's name all throughout the song with the last word being, Sara. The lyrics also describe Sara as a star that glows so near, and so far. This may symbolize the idea that even when Sara feels terrible or emotionally distant, she still has value and brightness to the people around them. When listening to  these lyrics Jasmin Parkin shows her ability to combine emotional vulnerability with encouragement. Later in mother mother you can see this style of writing as well.

Although Jasmin is known today for performing with Mother Mother, a five person band that plays alternative rock and pop rock, and other rock genres, she actually began her musical career as a jazz musician. (you could call her JAZZmin Parkin!!)  Her solo album previously mentioned “No Reason Why” is considered a contemporary jazz album. Due to the fact that she was involved in many choir groups growing up, Jasmin developed somewhat of a vocal range. She is generally a soprano, her voice is often described as heavenly or wordless. She can sing in higher treble ranges but has more difficulty singing lower tenor notes due to her voice being naturally higher. Jasmin may have also influenced Mother Mother to branch out into other rock genres. For example, the band's first album “Touch Up” was released before she joined the band. The music on that album generally follows a similar style throughout and mostly features acoustic guitar and the drumset leading the songs. However when looking at "O My Heart", which was Jasmin's first album with the band, the sound becomes more varied. For example track three “Body of Years” has stronger jazz tendencies, with the bass being much much more prominent compared to “Touch Up.” Songs such as “Try to Change,” “Body of Years,” “Burning Pile,” “Hayloft,” “Sleep Awake” and “O My Heart” show a noticeable difference in instrumentation and musical style! Additionally in “Burning Pile” you can hear instruments commonly used in  jazz band in the instrumental of the song. (Apple music 2006-2008)

Outside of music Jasmin is also a yogi, which means she practices and teaches yoga. She began practicing yoga in 2007 while also attending music school. By 2010 she became more focused on yoga as her strength and flexibility got better. As a musician who tours frequently after every new album release, or just every year or two  and has a busy or ‘chaotic’ schedule, she needed a way to relax and relieve stress. Yoga helped her manage the chaotic energy that comes with performing and traveling. She eventually released several video tutorials showing how to perform certain yoga stretches. As a yoga teacher Jasmin tries to give her students multiple opportunities so they can move their bodies comfortably, especially those who are new to yoga. She has also stated that yoga is a spiritual practice for her. (Jasmin 2021)

Jasmin Parkin was also previously in a relationship with Ryan Guldemond, the leader of Mother Mother. Their relationship lasted two years, Ryan Guldemond later said in an interview that their relationship is so platonic he cannot see it as a romantical thing anymore. However after their breakup, the band briefly took a break before releasing the album “Dance and Cry” This album was heavily influenced by the emotions surrounding the separation between Jasmin and Ryan. The album cover affects the title: the two female keyboardists, Jasmin and Molly represent the idea of “dance and cry.” Molly appears to be in a crying position while Jasmin is shown in a dramatic dancing pose. The cover image appears to take place in an alleyway. Several songs from Dance and Cry  are believed to be inspired by the breakup including “Only Love,” “So Down,” “Get Up,” and “It’s Alright.” However, the album wasn't written from just the perspective of Ryan. Jasmin herself has a solo song titled “Biting on a rose.” There is a lyric in the song that may represent how she felt out of place in the band after the breakup “I have chosen to stand still in front of a dancing band, something you ought to got to know, you’ll never see me biting on a rose.” The phrase biting on a rose is used as a comedic way of flirting as seen in earlier comedic tv shows or movies, where someone holds a rose in their mouth.  By saying that no one will see her “biting on a rose” Jasmin may be suggesting that she is no longer interested in flirting or romantic gestures after the relationship ended.  (Guldemond 2023)

In conclusion there's “No Reason Why” Jasmin Parkin should not be recognized as an important and influential musician. Many other musicians and artists only focus on fanbase entertainment and the hunger for more engagement and trying to do what the fans want. However, Jasmin Parkin's music often explored and or explained real feelings and this is still shown today with the songs she writes within the band. She also shows that music can also be an open window to let your emotions out of. This is the kind of emotional experience that leads fans to connect with her music then and now.

Sooppy Narikkatteri (also spelled Soopy Narikkattery) is an Indian politician from Kerala. He belongs to the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML). He is the General Secretary of the IUML Kozhikode District Committee. He works in local governance administration, public corporate boards, and state planning committees in Kerala. He was the head of the Kerala Rural Employment and Welfare Society (KREWS) and is a working group member of the Kerala Development and Innovation Strategic Council (K-DISC).
== Public and Administrative Roles ==
=== KREWS and K-DISC ===
The state government appointed Narikkatteri as the Chairman of the Kerala Rural Employment and Welfare Society (KREWS). He held this position from 2011 to 2016. In this role, he managed rural development funds and asset creation programs across various panchayats in the state.
In 2021, he was appointed to the working groups of the Kerala Development and Innovation Strategic Council (K-DISC). This is a strategic planning and advisory body headed by the Chief Minister of Kerala. His work here involves local planning, rural employment schemes, and introducing innovation tools to local self-government institutions.
=== Panchayat Work and Legal Cases ===
Narikkatteri was the General Secretary of the Kerala Grama Panchayat Association. In this role, he discussed administrative issues and fund allocations with the state cabinet.Staff Reporter. (2013, June 7). Panchayat librarian is anything but one. The New Indian Express. https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/kerala/2013/Jun/07/panchayat-librarian-is-anything-but-one-484429.html
In 2020, he filed a legal challenge in the High Court of Kerala regarding local voter registration lists. This petition led to actions by the State Election Commission and went up to the Supreme Court of India.Special Correspondent. (2020, February 15). Voters' list: SEC to approach Supreme court. The Hindu. thehindu.com
== Local Governance at Nadapuram ==
Narikkatteri was the President of the Nadapuram Grama Panchayat for 15 years, serving three consecutive terms from 2000 to 2015. He changed the administrative workflow of the office, making Nadapuram the first ISO-certified Grama Panchayat in Kerala.
In 2015, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Government of India, gave the Nadapuram panchayat the national Panchayat Raj Sashaktikaran Puraskar. It was selected as the best performing rural local body out of 265,000 panchayats in India based on file tracking, transparency, and project execution metrics.Joseph, M. (2015, November 3). Nadapuram turns a new leaf. The Hindu. thehindu.com The panchayat also won the state-level Swaraj Trophy during his term.
Nadapuram was historically known for frequent political clashes between rival parties. Narikkatteri used cross-party consultative committees during his tenure. This split local development work away from political rivalries, allowing the completion of rural roads, water supply projects, and health centers without party violence stopping the work.Staff Reporter. (2013, April 21). Progress hides behind a facade of violence. The Hindu. thehindu.com
== Party Positions and Elections ==
Narikkatteri contested the 2011 Kerala Legislative Assembly election as the UDF candidate from the Kuttiady Assembly constituency. He finished as the runner-up, getting 63,286 votes in a close election.Kerala Assembly Election Results 2011: Kuttiadi. keralaassembly.org

data.title: Sorry, We're Dead
data.text:
----

Sorry, We're Dead is Alex Zajicek's debut feature film [ref: ] [ref: ], a 2024 American independent comedy drama film starring Sarah Lee, Anna Marie Sharpe, Davied Morales, Katherine Park, and Chris Morrell. [ref: Sorry, We're Dead, IMDb]

Sorry, We're Dead follows Lana K. Jing (Lee), a burned-out lecture editor juggling her soul-crushing job, quirky coworkers, and a secret admirer, all while grappling with the fear that her dreams of making movies are slipping away—until a series of lies and absurd fourth-wall-breaking incidents force her to reconsider what truly matters in life.

The production took place entirely in the San Francisco Bay Area, including the cities of San Francisco, Oakland, Hercules, El Sobrante, Port Costa, Crockett, and Rodeo. [ref: ‘Sorry, We’re Dead’ Depicts a Deadpan Quarter-Life Crisis With a Bay Area Bent, www.kqed.org] [ref: Pass the Remote: Dozens of eclectic offerings at 26th SF Indie film fest, Local News Matters]

data.title: Acceleration Consortium
data.text:
The Acceleration Consortium (AC) is a research consortium based at the University of Toronto focused on accelerated materials and molecular discovery using "self-driving labs," robotic research workflows that use artificial intelligence and advanced computing to autonomously design, run, and characterize experiments.

The consortium is directed by chemist and computer scientist Alan Aspuru-Guzik and develops self-driving labs for applications in medicine, energy, plastics, electronics, and construction [ref: Experts say $200-million grant awarded to U of T will drive ‘big science’ via the Acceleration Consortium]. In 2023, the Acceleration Consortium received a $200 million award from the Canada First Research Excellence Fund (CFREF), issued by the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC), National Science and Engineering Research Council (NSERC), and the Canadian Institutes of Health Research (CIHR) [ref: New Acceleration Consortium at University of Toronto applies artificial intelligence to discovery of advanced materials, U of T Engineering News].

== History ==
The consortium traces its origins to a 2018 project that was using robotic research workflows for new organic laser materials, which Alan Aspuru-Guzik says was what the AC was originally designed for [ref: Acceleration Consortium 2025, acceleration.utoronto.ca]. The University of Toronto then launched the AC in April 2021 as an Institutional Strategic Initiative. It described the Acceleration Consortium as a global coalition that would use materials acceleration platforms (i.e. self-driving labs) to discover and design new materials.

A significant portion of the Acceleration Consortium's projects come from industry partners and collaborations. Merck KGaA was one of the consortium’s first partners. The two organizations collaborated on open-sourcing Merck’s Bayesian Back End (BayBE) experiment planner, which the AC’s self-driving labs later adopted in their automated workflows [ref: Acceleration Consortium cements partnership with global technology leader Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany].

In April 2025, BASF signed a master research agreement with the University of Toronto, the company’s first with a Canadian university. The collaborations cover crop protection, coatings that extend the life of architectural materials, and targeted drug delivery. One project, led by formulations lab co-lead Frank Gu, uses plant-derived biopolymers to regulate soil moisture and to slowly release pesticides or fertilizers near the plant [ref: BASF signs its first Canadian Master Research Agreement with the University of Toronto].

AC researchers worked with the AI drug discovery company Insilico Medicine on the 2023 Chemical Science study that used AlphaFold to design a potential liver cancer drug. Aspuru-Guzik is an adviser to Insilico. The two groups later co-authored the 2025 Nature Biotechnology study that used quantum computing and generative AI to design molecules targeting the cancer protein KRAS [ref: Acceleration Consortium, Institutional Strategic Initiatives].

The AC also maintains projects with Sanofi, Amgen, Procter & Gamble, Bristol Myers Squibb, IBM, Amazon Web Services, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Mettler Toledo, Sekisui, and others [ref: Partners, acceleration.utoronto.ca].

== Operations ==

=== Network of self-driving labs ===
The AC built a network of self-driving labs, each focused on one particular class of applications, that collaborate on projects with other SDLs while having a mandate of advancing one particular field. The labs are numbered from SDL 0 to SDL 7. SDLs 0 to 6 are housed at the University of Toronto whereas SDL 7 is at the University of British Columbia [ref: AC Labs and Facilities, acceleration.utoronto.ca].

==== SDL 0: AI and Automation ====
SDL 0 focuses on overcoming robotic and equipment bottlenecks in self-driving labs by integrating robot manipulation, computer vision, and learning-based agentic reasoning into a unified autonomy stack. Its projects include a GPU-accelerated multiscale digital twin framework for simulating autonomous lab workflows, a general orchestrator for executing closed-loop experiments, and equipment API integrations [ref: SDL0: AI and Automation, acceleration.utoronto.ca].

==== SDL 1: Inorganic ====
SDL 1 focuses on designing inorganic materials. It focuses on solution-based, solid-state, and electrochemical synthesis pathways with real-time data collection, adaptive process control, and AI-guided planning to further a property-driven optimization with mechanistic understanding. Its projects include the closed-loop discovery of electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) for green hydrogen, an automated electrolyzer workflow for CO2 conversion, high-throughput optimization of aqueous battery electrolytes, and fully automated solid-state synthesis of oxides and alloys [ref: SDL1: Inorganic, acceleration.utoronto.ca].

==== SDL 2: Organic ====
SDL 2 builds automated, data-driven platforms to design, execute, and optimize complex organic synthesis, with a focus on pharmaceuticals, catalysis, and functional materials. Current projects include an autonomous liquid-liquid extraction platform for solvent-efficient purification and a self-driving workflow for high-throughput solubility measurement and crystallization studies [ref: SDL2: Organic, acceleration.utoronto.ca].

==== SDL 3: Medicinal Chemistry ====
SDL 3 accelerates early-stage drug discovery by iteratively designing, synthesizing, and testing small-molecule protein binders to optimize target affinity and selectivity. It evaluates compounds for binding directly from crude reaction mixtures to avoid time-consuming purification [ref: SDL3: Medicinal chemistry, acceleration.utoronto.ca].

==== SDL 4: Polymers ====
SDL 4 synthesizes, purifies, and characterizes polymer libraries using AI-guided feedback to target user-specified properties, monitoring synthesis in real-time with flow reactors. Its projects include fluorine-free polymers to replace PFAS in electronics, polymer surfactant systems for drug delivery and membrane protein-extraction, sustainable degradation of electronic polymer waste, and the development of better polymer coatings [ref: SDL4: Polymers, acceleration.utoronto.ca].

==== SDL5: Formulations ====
SDL 5 focuses on navigating the combinatorial design space of formulations for healthcare, agriculture, personal care, and other industries. Projects include agrochemicals with better solubility to improve crop yields and reduce run-off, stable mitochondrial formulations for regenerative medicine, personal care products like lotions and body washes, thermal fluids for cooling electronics, and nano medicines for poorly soluble drugs [ref: SDL5: Formulations, acceleration.utoronto.ca].

==== SDL 6: Human Organic Mimicry ====
SDL 6 focuses on developing high-fidelity human tissue models, including organoids and organ-on-a-chip systems built from patient samples. Their goal is to discover drugs, test their toxicity, and reduce reliance on animal testing. Its projects include Bayesian optimization of vascularized tissue models for drug efficacy and toxicity testing, machine-learning optimization of media for cardiac microtissues used in heart cell transplant therapy, and active learning-based optimization of antibody production [ref: SDL6: Human organ mimicry, acceleration.utoronto.ca].

==== SDL 7: Scale-Up ====
Unlike the other SDLs, SDL 7 is based at the University of British Columbia. The scale-up lab aims to speed the translation of new molecules and materials from early discovery to real-world deployment by automating scale-up and optimization in organic chemistry and materials science.The lab builds on Project Ada, Canada’s first self-driving lab, which Jason Hein, Curtis Berlinguette, and Aspuru-Guzik assembled with an $8 million Natural Resources Canada grant in 2018 [ref: Positioning Canada as a world leader in self-driving labs, Stewart Blusson Quantum Matter Institute].

AP (Thailand) Public Company Limited (often abbreviated as AP) is a Thai real estate development company. The company primarily develops residential properties, including single-detached homes, twin homes, townhomes, and condominiums, with a focus on the Bangkok Metropolitan Region.

History

AP (Thailand) Public Company Limited was founded in 1991 as a limited company under the name Asian Property Co., Ltd., with the objective of operating a real estate development business. Later, in 2000, the company was listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) through a backdoor listing by merging with PCM Precast Floors Public Company Limited, a manufacturer of precast concrete floors that had been listed on the SET since September 22, 1992. [ref: AP - Factsheet - ตลาดหลักทรัพย์แห่งประเทศไทย, www.set.or.th]

Following the merger, the company changed its name to Asian Property Development Public Company Limited and established a new subsidiary, PCM Construction Material Co., Ltd., to continue the precast floor business. At that time, the company held a 99.99% stake in this new subsidiary.

In 2002, the company transitioned its SET trading classification from the Building and Furnishing Materials sector to the Property Development sector. During the same year, the corporate headquarters was relocated from Lam Luk Ka District, Pathum Thani Province, to Ocean Tower 1 in Khlong Toei District, Bangkok, which remains its current headquarters.

Business Operations

AP Thailand's operations are structured into four main divisions:

# Real Estate Development: The core business focuses on developing residential properties, including single-detached homes, twin homes, townhomes, and condominiums, with projects located across Bangkok, the Bangkok Metropolitan Region, and all regions of Thailand.
# Real Estate Investment Consulting: Managed by the subsidiary Bangkok Citismart, this division provides property brokerage, consignment for sale, and leasing services.
# Property Management: Smart Service and Management (SMART) operates as the juristic person manager for various condominiums and housing estates.
# Secondary Market Startup: Homerun, an affiliated startup, operates in the second-hand real estate market by acquiring, renovating, and reselling existing residential properties.
Residential Projects

AP has developed more than 400 residential projects.  [ref: AP Thailand Expands APITOWN Brand Nationwide, Bangkok Post] The company's diverse portfolio  covers various market segments, ranging from entry-level to ultra-luxury. It develops properties under several brand names, categorized by housing type

* Single-Detached Homes: THE PALAZZO, BEON, BAAN KLANG KRUNG, THE CITY, CENTRO and MODEN.

* Twin Homes:  BAAN KLANG MUANG THE EDITION and GRANDE PLENO.

* Townhomes: BAAN KLANG MUANG CLASSE, BAAN KLANG MUANG, PLENO and PLENO TOWN.

* Home Offices: DISTRICT.

* Condominium Brands: THE ADDRESS, RHYTHM, LIFE, ASPIRE and GOOD DAY.

* Provincial Projects: APITOWN.

data.title: Planetary ring particle collision
data.text:
Planetary ring particle collisions are the constant, low-speed impacts that occur between billions of individual chunks of ice, rock and dust within a planet’s ring system. [ref: ]

These collisions happen because the ring particles are tightly packed together as they circle a planet. Although they travel fast (around 38,000 miles per hour), they surprisingly travel at similar paces around the planet.

Overtime, these small particles will lose dozens of energy, causing the rings to become thin & flat. References

data.title: Christian G. Rodriguez
data.text:
----

Christian G. Rodriguez (Born in 1984) is an American federal civil servant and veteran of the United States Air Force whose academic research focuses on leadership styles, job satisfaction, and person-organization fit within public sector institutions.

== Early Life and Education ==
Rodriguez graduated from Alta Loma High School [ref: Alta Loma High School, Chaffey Joint Union High School District] in Rancho Cucamonga, California, in 2002. He later attended Grand Canyon University, [ref: Grand Canyon University: Private Christian University, Grand Canyon University] earning a Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in General Psychology with an emphasis in Industrial and Organizational Psychology in December 2020. [ref: Christian G. Rodriguez Research Profile, ResearchGate] In February 2016, he was inducted into the Grand Canyon University chapter of the Psi Chi International Honor Society in Psychology.

== Military Service ==
Rodriguez served 16 years in the United States Air Force, completing 10 years of active-duty service followed by six years in the Air Force Reserve.

== Career and Research ==
Rodriguez has served over two decades in public sector operations across state and federal levels. As a federal civil servant based in the Washington, D.C. area, he applies organizational behavior and behavioral science frameworks to public sector operations, administrative processes, and governance.

His scholarly work examines organizational dynamics within civil service and public administration. In 2020, he authored doctoral research titled An Examination of the Correlation Between Leadership Style and Job Satisfaction for Predicting Person-Organization Fit in Public Sector Organizations, investigating how supervisory leadership behaviors influence employee retention and organizational alignment among public sector personnel.

== Publications ==
* Rodriguez, Christian G. (2020). An Examination of the Correlation Between Leadership Style and Job Satisfaction for Predicting Person-Organization Fit in Public Sector Organizations (Ph.D. dissertation). Grand Canyon University.

== Honors and Awards ==

Andrea Rehberg is a lecturer at Newcastle University, UK, specializing in continental feminism, continental philosophy, phenomenology and poststructuralism. She received her PHD from the university of Warwick [ref: Phenomenology Guide Perplexed, Bloomsbury Publishing Plc] and has written a series of essays on Nietzsche and Phenomenology [ref: Nietzsche and Phenomenology, Cambridge Scholars Publisher].

AP (Thailand) Public Company Limited (often abbreviated as AP) is a Thai real estate development company. The company primarily develops residential properties, including single-detached homes, twin homes, townhomes, and condominiums, with a focus on the Bangkok Metropolitan Region. The company is recognized as one of the leading property developers in Thailand, with its founder Anuphong Assavabhokhin receiving national awards for his role in the real estate industy. [ref: “อนุพงษ์ อัศวโภคิน” บุคคลดีเด่นแห่งวงการอสังหาริมทรัพย์จาก PropertyGuru Thailand Property Awards 2021, Forbes Thailand]

History

AP (Thailand) Public Company Limited was founded in 1991 as a limited company under the name Asian Property Co., Ltd., with the objective of operating a real estate development business. Later, in 2000, the company was listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) through a backdoor listing by merging with PCM Precast Floors Public Company Limited, a manufacturer of precast concrete floors that had been listed on the SET since September 22, 1992. [ref: AP - Factsheet - ตลาดหลักทรัพย์แห่งประเทศไทย, www.set.or.th]

Following the merger, the company changed its name to Asian Property Development Public Company Limited and established a new subsidiary, PCM Construction Material Co., Ltd., to continue the precast floor business. At that time, the company held a 99.99% stake in this new subsidiary.

In 2002, the company transitioned its SET trading classification from the Building and Furnishing Materials sector to the Property Development sector. During the same year, the corporate headquarters was relocated from Lam Luk Ka District, Pathum Thani Province, to Ocean Tower 1 in Khlong Toei District, Bangkok, which remains its current headquarters.

Business Operations

AP Thailand's operations are structured into four main divisions:

# Real Estate Development: The core business focuses on developing residential properties, including single-detached homes, twin homes, townhomes, and condominiums, with projects located across Bangkok, the Bangkok Metropolitan Region, and all regions of Thailand. [ref: เอพี ไทยแลนด์ เปิด 27 โครงการใหม่ ชู ‘AP CODE’ ขับเคลื่อนองค์กรโตยั่งยืน]
# Real Estate Investment Consulting: Managed by the subsidiary Bangkok Citismart, this division provides property brokerage, consignment for sale, and leasing services.
# Property Management: Smart Service and Management (SMART) operates as the juristic person manager for various condominiums and housing estates.
# Secondary Market Startup: Homerun, an affiliated startup, operates in the second-hand real estate market by acquiring, renovating, and reselling existing residential properties.
# Corporate Stability: The company has consistently maintained an "A" credit rating with a stable outlook from TRIS Rating, reflecting its strong market position and financial discipline in the Thai property sector. [ref: AP Thailand tops Thai real estate, makes Fortune Southeast Asia 500 for 3rd straight year, Bangkok Post]
Residential Projects

AP has developed more than 400 residential projects.  [ref: AP Thailand Expands APITOWN Brand Nationwide, Bangkok Post] The company develops properties under several brands targeting different income levels, categorized by housing type:

* Single-Detached Homes: THE PALAZZO, BEON, BAAN KLANG KRUNG, THE CITY, CENTRO and MODEN.

* Twin Homes:  BAAN KLANG MUANG THE EDITION and GRANDE PLENO.

* Townhomes: BAAN KLANG MUANG CLASSE, BAAN KLANG MUANG, PLENO and PLENO TOWN.

* Home Offices: DISTRICT.

* Condominium Brands: THE ADDRESS, RHYTHM, LIFE, ASPIRE and GOOD DAY.

* Provincial Projects: APITOWN.

data.text:

Short description|Railway station in Germany}}

Selters (Westerw) station, German Bahnhof Selters (Westerw) is a train station located in the Westerwald district in Rhineland-Palatinate.

== Location ==
The Selters (Westerw) station is located in the landscape Westerwald, along the Engers-Au railway as well as the former Selters - Hachenburg narrow gauge railway, which leaded from Selters via Hattert to Hachenburg, where it endet as an interchange to the Limburg-Altenkirchen railway.

== History ==

During the 19th century, plans established to open railway lines inside the Westerwald, especially for the purposes the transportation of regional raw materials.

The Engers–Au railway (between Siershahn and Altenkirchen (Westerwald) also known as Holzbachtalbahn (Holzbach valley railway), on which Selters station also is located, was opened in the year1884.

After that, the construction works for the Selters - Hachenburg narrow gauge railway began in the year 1900, and the line opened just a short time later, on August 1, 1901.

Selters station featured a station building with administrative and waiting rooms, along with other operational facilities. The transshipment of freight from the narrow-gauge line took place at Selters station.

Although in 1951, further investment have been done on the lines infrastructure, that were two pits for transporter wagons were installed, that caused an elimination of the need for the labor-intensive manual transshipment process previously required at Selters station.

But not even ten years later, the Selters - Hachenburg narrow-gauge line was closed in 1960, and the tracks were primarely dismantled.

Also the passenger service on the Engers - Au railway ended in 1989.

Today, the former station building in Selters is under private use, the platforms are deconsteucted, while the site itself largely serves as an industrial area for the locally based factories of the company Schütz.

Nowadays Selters station is served in fright train service through the in the year of 2025 new foundet Holzbachtalbahn GmbH and trains running on order of the Schuetz company.

The local bus line 420 of Westerwaldbus GmbH serves a bus stop near Selters station and nowadays runs mostly along the former Selters - Hachenburg railway from Montabaur via Siershahn, Selters and Hattert to Hachenburg.

data.text:

Tom Nesher (; born December 17, 1996) is an Israeli film director, screenwriter, and journalist. She is an Ophir Awards winner for Best Film and Best Director to 2024 for Come Closer.

== Biography ==
Nesher was born in 1996, the eldest daughter of director Avi Nesher and the artist and photographer Iris Nesher. Her younger brother, Ari, was killed in 2018 at the age of 17 in a hit and run accident caused by footballer Manamto Asefa in Tel Aviv. [ref: https://www.haaretz.co.il/gallery/cinema/2020-12-02/ty-article-magazine/.highlight/0000017f-dc63-df62-a9ff-dcf7c44e0000] [ref: Soccer player released after 2 years in prison for deadly hit-and-run, The Times of Israel] In high school, she studied at the Thelma Yellin High School In Givatayim.

In 2014, Nesher served as an announcer on Galei Tzahal. [ref: https://www.israelhayom.co.il/celebrities/local-celebrities/article/7481993] After this, she studied screenwriting at the Sam Spiegel Film School, and history and literature at Tel Aviv University. [ref: תום נשר - ביוגרפיה, אידיבי]

In 2020, Nesher joined Channel 13 News as an investigative reporter. [ref: https://www.israelhayom.co.il/celebrities/local-celebrities/article/7343134]

In 2024, Nesher released her debut feature film, Come Closer, a drama heavily inspired by her own personal experience. The film follows Eden, a young woman who, after the tragic death of her brother, embarks on an intense emotional journey to find his secret girlfriend, navigating complex themes of youth, intimacy and healing. [ref: Interview: Tom Nesher on "Come Closer", The Moveable Fest] The film winning four major awards at the 2024 Ophir Awards, including Best Feature Film and Best Director for Nesher, and Best Actress for Lia Elalouf. It was subsequently selected as the Israeli entry for Best International Feature Film at the 97th Academy Awards. [ref: Tom Nesher’s ‘Come Closer’ wins Ophir, becomes Israel’s choice for Oscar nomination, The Times of Israel]

== Awards and recognition ==

* 2024 - Tribeca Film Festival: Viewpoints Award (Come Closer) [ref: Israeli filmmaker Tom Nesher’s debut feature wins prize at Tribeca Film Festival, The Times of Israel]
* 2024 - Jerusalem Film Festival: GWFF Award for Best Israeli First Feature (Come Closer) [ref: 2024 JFF Winners, Jerusalem Film Festival]
* 2024 - Ophir Awards: Best Feature Film and Best Director (Come Closer)

In 2025, Nesher was elected for Verietys prestigious "10 Directors to watch" list. [ref: ‘The Substance,’ ‘The Piano Lesson,’ ‘Babygirl’ Filmmakers Selected for Variety’s 2025 Directors to Watch, Variety]

== Personal life ==
Since 2016, Nesher has been in relationship with Guy Kornowski, and in April 2026, they had their first son. [ref: "טריפ של אינסוף אהבה": תום נשר ובן זוגה הביאו לעולם את בנם הבכור, mako]

data.title: Pocket FM
data.text:
----

= Pocket FM =

Pocket FM is an Indian audio entertainment platform that distributes serialized fiction and other audio content. It was founded in 2018 by Rohan Nayak, Prateek Dixit and Nishanth Srinivas. [ref: Pocket FM raises $22.4 million in Series B funding led by Lightspeed, The Economic Times] [ref: Rohan Nayak, Prateek Dixit, Nishant KS, Fortune India]

The platform uses a freemium model in which some episodes are available without charge while subsequent episodes can be unlocked using virtual currency purchased through in-app transactions. The company is actively incorporating artificial intelligence for audio production as well as translation into other languages. [ref: Pocket FM partners with ElevenLabs to convert scripts into audio content quickly, TechCrunch] [ref: Pocket FM wants to be the Netflix of long-form audio, www.forbesindia.com]

As of 2026, The Pocket FM website claims the company is serving 20+ countries in 15 international languages. [ref: Pocket FM: The home of the world's best audio dramas, pocketfm.com]

== History ==
Pocket FM began offering content across multiple formats like audiobooks, podcasts and other spoken-word content before shifting its focus toward serialized fiction. [ref: Pocket FM: The Startup that Pioneered Audio Series and Made the Entertainment Industry Follow in Its Footsteps, OK Magazine] By 2021, the platform was describing itself primarily as a community of content creators, and an audio entertainment service serving fictional content in an episodic story format. [ref: Audio OTT app Pocket FM raises $22.4mn funding in round led by Lightspeed, Business Standard]

In December 2021, Pocket FM raised $22.4 million in a Series B funding round led by Lightspeed, with participation from Tanglin Venture Partners and existing investor Times Group. The company said the funding would be used to expand its operations, creator community and geographical presence.

In September 2023, the company announced that its Android application had surpassed 100 million downloads on Google Play. The company attributed the growth to its serialized-fiction format and expansion across languages and genres. [ref: Pocket FM crosses over 100 million downloads on Google Play Store, The Times of India]

In March 2024, Pocket FM raised $103 million in a Series D funding round led by Lightspeed, with participation from StepStone Group. A TechCrunch report states the round brought the company's total funding to approximately $196 million, and new valuation at $750 million. The company said that the fresh infusion of funds would support expansion into Europe and Latin America, and growth in the United States. [ref: Audio platform Pocket FM bags $103M in funding as it eyes global expansion, TechCrunch]

== Content and business model ==
Pocket FM's main product is serialized audio fiction dramas in episodic format across genres including romance, fantasy, science fiction, thriller and drama. The website uses a freemium, pay as you go model in which users can listen to initial episodes for free and unlock future episodes by purchasing virtual coins. [ref: Out of Pocket, The Verge]

Pocket FM expanded into the United States in 2022. By March 2024, the company said it had generated more than $150 million in annual recurring revenue, including $100 million from the United States, and was expanding into Europe and Latin America.

Pocket FM's revenue stood at ₹1,768 crore for the financial year 2024–25, an increase of 68 percent from the previous year. More than half of the company's revenue came from user payments through microtransactions, with the remainder coming from advertising. In April 2026, Pocket FM said it had reached approximately $450 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR). The company said it had reached approximately $200 million ARR in the fourth quarter of financial year 2025 and approximately $400 million in the fourth quarter of financial year 2026. [ref: Pocket FM hits $450 million ARR in April after accelerating AI-led content creation, The Economic Times]

== Notable series ==
According to play counts displayed by Pocket FM, Insta Millionaire and Super Yoddha have each accumulated approximately 1.4 billion plays, Ek Ladki Ko Dekha To approximately 1.3 billion, Secret Ameerzaada approximately 885 million, and Insta Empire approximately 556.4 million. [ref: Pocket FM: The home of the world's best audio dramas, pocketfm.com]

== Creator ecosystem ==
Pocket FM relies upon its community of writers and voice artists to produce content for the platform. In 2021, the company reported working with more than 17,000 writers and voice artists for content production. In February 2026, The Economic Times reported that Pocket FM said more than 20 percent of its monetized creators earned more than ₹1 lakh per month and that total creator payouts had exceeded ₹300 crore.

== Artificial intelligence ==
Pocket FM has increasingly incorporated artificial intelligence into the production of its audio content. In June 2024, the company announced a partnership with ElevenLabs to convert written scripts into audio using AI-generated voices. Pocket FM reported produceding 30,000 hours of audio series using ElevenLabs' technology during a testing phase, and planned to make the technology available to its creators in the future.

Subsequently, the company expanded use of artificial intelligence beyond voice generation, incorporating it deeper into writing assistance, content production, translation, and localization. By April 2026, the company reported more than 300,000 creators producing over 80,000 hours of content on a monthly basis. [ref: Pocket FM gives its writers an AI tool to transform narratives, write cliffhangers, and more, TechCrunch]

== Partnerships ==
Pocket FM has entered into partnerships involving established entertainment properties as it has expanded its audio catalogue. In 2025, the company partnered with Arka Mediaworks, the production company behind the Baahubali films, on an audio series based on the Baahubali universe. The planned series was reported to comprise 250 episodes. [ref: Pocket FM, Arka Mediaworks to launch new Baahubali audio series, The Economic Times]

data.title: Demid Odonchimeg
data.text:
Demid Odonchimeg is a Mongolian dentist, academic, and researcher in the fields of dentistry, orthodontics, and maxillofacial prosthetics. She holds a Doctor of Medical Sciences degree and the academic title of associate professor.

== Early life and education ==
Demid Odonchimeg was born in 1961 in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. [ref: Employment profile of Demid Odonchimeg, 2002.10.01.]

She graduated from Secondary School No. 23 in Ulaanbaatar in 1979 and completed her dental education at the Irkutsk State Medical Institute in 1984. [ref: Employment profile of Demid Odonchimeg, 2002.10.01.]

== Career ==
From 1984 to 1986, Odonchimeg worked as a dentist in the maxillofacial prosthetics department of the State Central Clinical Hospital. From 1986 to 1989, she worked at the Specialized Center for Dental Care as a dentist and department head. [ref: Employment profile of Demid Odonchimeg, 2016.09.09.]

From 1989 onward, she worked as a lecturer and later senior lecturer at medical university institutions in Mongolia, including AUDS, AUIS, EMSU, and MNUMS. [ref: Employment profile of Demid Odonchimeg, 2016.09.09.]

== Degrees and academic title ==
In 1996, she earned a master's degree in medical sciences with a thesis titled A Comparative Study of the Size of Permanent Human Teeth. [ref: List of publications of D. Odonchimeg.]

In 2004, she earned a Doctor of Medical Sciences degree with a dissertation titled Diagnostic and Treatment Approaches for Ectopic Eruption of the Maxillary Permanent Canine. [ref: Supplement to Doctor of Medical Sciences Diploma, No. F 20041951.]

In 2011, she received the academic title of associate professor. [ref: Associate Professor Certificate, No. 072, Registration No. DP 20110072.]

== Research and publications ==
Her research and publications cover topics such as permanent tooth size, eruption patterns of maxillary canines, dentofacial development, mixed dentition space analysis, cleft lip and palate care, and maxillofacial prosthetic rehabilitation. [ref: List of publications of D. Odonchimeg.]

Selected works include:

* Maxillofacial Prosthetic Rehabilitation of Oral and Facial Defects in Mongolia (2000)
* Measurement of Condylar Position in Permanent Dentition of Mongolian Females (2006)
* Mixed Dentition Space Analysis for Mongolians (2009)
* Tweed-Merrifield Directional Force Technology (translated and edited, 2010)
* Removable Appliances in Orthodontics (translated and edited, 2016) [ref: List of publications of D. Odonchimeg.]

== Supervision of master's theses ==
According to her professional record, Odonchimeg supervised master's theses on dental occlusion in young children, prediction of eruption space for permanent canines and premolars, dental crowding, craniofacial growth patterns, and the prevalence of malocclusion among schoolchildren in Ulaanbaatar. [ref: List of publications of D. Odonchimeg.]

== Honors ==
* Leading Youth Gold Medal (1987)
* Commendation of the Ministry of Health (1996)
* Distinguished Health Worker of the Capital City (2007)
* Distinguished Worker of Education and Science (2013) [ref: Record of awards and honors.]

data.title: Midwest Express Airlines Flight 007
data.text:
----

Midwest Express Airlines Flight 007 was a scheduled domestic passenger flight that was involved in a near Mid-Air collision on September 11, 2001, leading to a series of rapid descents and four minor injuries. The flight passed within 30-300 feet of United Airlines Flight 175. [ref: Incident McDonnell Douglas DC-9-32 N207ME, Tuesday 11 September 2001, aviation-safety.net]

==Aircraft==
The aircraft involved was a McDonnell Douglas DC-9-32, manufactured in 1979 for Garuda Indonesia and sold to Midwest Express in 1995 as N207ME.
==Crew==
The flight was operated by Captain Gerald Earwood and first officer Eric Fjelstad (who had joined Midwest less than a year prior). [ref: Gerald Earwood Archives, International Center for 9/11 Justice] Earwood was well known at Midwest for his tendency to "joke" with his fellow crew members; also on board were three flight attendants. [ref: User Clip: Gerald Earwood 9-11 Response | Video | C-SPAN.org]

==Flight==
===Radio issues===
While the aircraft was on NYC radar, several calls to air traffic control (ATC) were missed. This led to the crew believing they might have had an unserviceable VHF communications radio. The missed calls occurred at the same time as American Airlines Flight 11 crashed. [ref: Changing Terror's Course; Book Details How Midwest Plane Avoided Sept. 11 Crash, Redorbit]

===Near miss===
As the aircraft was nearing the Hudson river, United Airlines 175 was also approaching at the same attitude. ATC was focused on vectoring both a Delta and a TWA flight; Midwest 007 was left to fly as previously instructed. The controller was alerted to a conflict between two aircraft and directed Midwest 007 to turn left; the crew complied with this instruction. The controller, on seeing that United 175 was less than a mile from collision told the Midwest crew to "Roll Right". At this time the First officer could see the United aircraft and sent the DC-9 into a right hand dive. [ref: The untold story of 9/11: extract from The Only Plane in the Sky, www.thetimes.com] [ref: ] The aircraft quickly lost altitude and they had to pull up after around 1000 feet. United 175, now on its final descent, was still on a collision course with the DC-9. Once again the crew were forced to dive. This time four people (two passengers and two cabin crew) were injured. The aircraft dropped around 2000 feet in a second dive to the right, allowing Flight 175 to pass an estimated above.

==Aftermath==
The DC-9 landed safely with no further issues. N207ME received temporary repairs in NYC before flying a group of Midwest Express crew members back to Milwaukee on September 13, where it was fully repaired. The aircraft is currently stored in Mexico. [ref: https://imgproc.airliners.net/photos/airliners/4/3/9/1526934.jpg?v=v40 ] Both pilots continued to fly for Midwest Express until 2010, when the airline ceased operations; Earwood would later be hired by JetBlue as a first officer on the A321. [ref: Gerald Earwood Obituary - Frisco, TX, Dignity Memorial]

==In popular culture==
The book Touching History by Lynn Spencer includes the flight along with a number of others.

== References/Notes ==

data.title: Forsythe conjecture
data.text:
The Forsythe conjecture is a question in dynamical systems about the behaviour of an algorithm in numerical linear algebra. It concerns the limiting directions of residual vectors generated by the conjugate gradient method with fixed-length restarts. The conjecture was first formulated by George Forsythe for the equivalent s-dimensional optimum gradient method in a 1967 technical report and subsequent 1968 article.

For restart length s, each cycle of the method consists of s conjugate-gradient steps followed by a restart from the resulting residual. The conjecture asserts that, in exact arithmetic, the iteration for any real symmetric positive-definite linear system either terminates or becomes asymptotically two-periodic in direction. In other words, the even and odd subsequences of normalized residuals at each restart converge to two respective unit vectors.

The case s=1, corresponding to steepest descent with exact line search, was first proved by Hirotugu Akaike in 1959. In 2026, separate proofs for s=2 were given by Colbrook, Stepaniants, and Townsend, by Liesen, and by Richard Peng. A later 2026 paper by Colbrook, Stepaniants, and Townsend gave a proof for s=3 and counterexamples for every s\geq4, with these results formally verified in Lean.

== Statement ==

Consider the linear system Ax=b, where A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n} is symmetric positive-definite and hence the system has a unique exact solution x_*. For v\in\mathbb R^n, define the Euclidean norm \|v\|_2=(v^{\mathsf T}v)^{1/2} and the A-norm \|v\|_A=(v^{\mathsf T}Av)^{1/2}.

This section describes the restarted conjugate gradient method with integer restart length s>0. All computations are assumed to take place in exact arithmetic. Initialized at any x_0\in\mathbb R^n, the method takes s conjugate-gradient steps per iteration unless the exact solution is reached earlier.

Denote by x_k the iterate at the start of restart cycle k and its residual by r_k=b-Ax_k. At each restart cycle, the method discards the accumulated search directions and begins a new conjugate-gradient run from this iterate and its residual.

One cycle of s conjugate gradient steps can be described by a minimization problem. The residual r_k generates the Krylov subspace\mathcal K_s(A,r_k)=\operatorname{span}\{r_k,Ar_k,\ldots,A^{s-1}r_k\}.The next approximation x_{k+1} is obtained by adding to x_k a correction from this space that minimizes the error measured in the A-norm. This can be written asx_{k+1}\in x_k+\mathcal K_s(A,r_k),\qquad \|x_*-x_{k+1}\|_A=\min_{z\in x_k+\mathcal K_s(A,r_k)}\|x_*-z\|_A.The approximations converge to x_*, so the residuals tend to zero. To study their directions as they shrink, define the normalized residualy_k=\frac{r_k}{\|r_k\|_2}where y_k is a unit vector pointing in the direction of r_k and is well-defined whenever r_k\ne0.

The Forsythe conjecture asserts that these iterations either terminate after finitely many cycles, or there are two unit vectors y_{\mathrm e} and y_{\mathrm o} such thaty_{2k}\longrightarrow y_{\mathrm e},\qquad y_{2k+1}\longrightarrow y_{\mathrm o}\qquad\text{as }k\to\infty.Normalized residuals from the even restart cycles converge to one fixed direction, while those from the odd restart cycles converge to another. These limiting directions may depend on the matrix, the restart length, and the initial residual.

The restarted conjugate gradient method converges in a finite number of restart cycles whenever the starting residual has nonzero projections onto at most s distinct eigenspaces of A. In particular, if s is at least the number of distinct eigenvalues of A, the first cycle reaches the exact solution.

== History ==

The phenomenon of two-direction asymptotics was first conjectured by [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Forsythe Forsythe] and Motzkin in their 1951 abstract on the optimum gradient method. This method is equivalent to the conjugate gradient method with restart length s=1 and the steepest descent method with exact line search. The conjugate gradient method was formally introduced by Hestenes and Stiefel in 1952. In 1959, Akaike proved the conjecture for the s=1 case by viewing the squared spectral components of the normalized residual as an evolving probability distribution. Motivated by numerical experiments for s=2, Forsythe later proposed analogous two-direction behavior for larger fixed restart lengths in his 1967 report and 1968 article.

In 1982, Zhuk extended Forsythe’s construction of alternating residual directions to more general eigenvalue configurations and established sufficient conditions for convergence from nearby initial residuals.

Zhuk and Bondarenko published a claimed proof of the conjecture for s=2 in 1983. The approach proved convergence of residual polynomial coefficients, citing Zabolotskaya’s 1979 paper to conclude that even and odd subsequences of normalized residuals converge. In their 2023 review, Faber, Liesen, and Tichý distinguished coefficient convergence from convergence of residual directions, leaving the case s=2 unresolved. Their review restated the conjecture in modern Krylov subspace notation and formulated a related cross iteration for symmetric and nonsymmetric matrices.

In 2026, three proofs of the conjecture for s=2 were presented by Colbrook, Stepaniants, and Townsend, by Liesen, and by Richard Peng. A later paper by Colbrook, Stepaniants, and Townsend presented a proof for s=3, an eight-dimensional counterexample for s=4, and an extension of the construction to every larger restart length, disproving the conjecture for every s\geq4.

== Analysis ==
This section summarizes the analysis of the Forsythe conjecture for all restarts s\geq2.

=== Spectral weight map ===

For an iteration that does not terminate, the normalized residual can be written asy=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\eta_i v_i,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^{n}\eta_i^2=1,where v_i, \lambda_i are the orthonormal eigenvectors and corresponding eigenvalues of A. Define the squared weights w_i=\eta_i^2 which measure the fraction of the squared residual norm in each corresponding eigendirection. These weights form a probability vector. Squaring removes the signs of the components \eta_i, which must also be considered when studying convergence of the normalized residual directions.

Define P_w as the monic degree-s orthogonal polynomial for these weights. One restart cycle updates the squared weights by(Tw)_i=\frac{w_iP_w(\lambda_i)^2}{\sum_{j=1}^{n}w_jP_w(\lambda_j)^2}which can be derived by spectrally decomposing the restart cycle update along the eigendirections. The focus of the following analysis is to prove whether every nonterminating iteration of T converges to a two-cycle.

=== Cases s = 2 and s = 3 ===

A two-cycle of the weight map T consists of two weight vectors (w, u) such that Tw = u and Tu = w. The main difficulty is that an iteration may approach a family of two-cycles while not settling into one particular pair.

For restart lengths s=2 and s=3, estimates on the weight map can be derived that rule out persistent movement along families of two-cycles proving that the weights settle on a particular two-cycle. Analysis of the signs of \eta_i establishes convergence of the normalized residuals to two limiting directions.

=== Counterexamples for s ≥ 4 ===

For s=4, Colbrook, Stepaniants, and Townsend constructed a diagonal positive-definite matrix in dimension n=8 and an initial residual for which the even subsequence of normalized residuals does not converge. The argument relies on rigorous computer-assisted verification via interval arithmetic, and relates the long-term behavior of the spectral weights to a periodic orbit of an associated differential equation. This construction extends to every s\geq4 through a lifting argument, giving a nonterminating counterexample in dimension s+4 for each restart length.

The classification for s\geq2 has also been formalized in Lean. The authors’ public repository contains the formalization and code for the computer-assisted verification.

== Related problems ==

The known counterexamples for restart length s\geq4 have dimension s+4. Whether counterexamples exist in smaller dimensions remains open.

Faber, Liesen, and Tichý also formulated a cross iteration based on Arnoldi iteration for symmetric and nonsymmetric matrices and conjectured an analogous two-direction asymptotics for this algorithm.

data.title: Ryan Xu
data.text:
Ryan Xu (Chinese: 徐凌霄; legal name Lingxiao Xu) is a Chinese-American real estate broker and the founder of Xceed Realty, a brokerage based in Bellevue, Washington, serving the Greater Seattle Eastside. [ref: Meet Ryan Xu, Xceed Realty] [ref: Ryan Xu – Washington, RealTrends Verified]

== Early life and education ==
Professional biographies state that Xu worked in retail banking in China and began private real estate investing around 2011 before becoming a licensed agent. [ref: Ryan Xu, Northwest Real Estate Team] He earned a Master of Arts in Financial Economics and a Master of Business Administration from the University of Detroit Mercy.

== Military service ==
Xu served in the United States Army as a combat medic for approximately four years. His LinkedIn profile lists service as a Healthcare Specialist (68W) from June 2016 to November 2019. [ref: Ryan X., LinkedIn]

== Career ==
Xu entered licensed real estate practice in Washington around 2018. According to LinkedIn, he worked as a real estate broker at Compass (November 2019 – February 2024) and as a broker and team leader at Coldwell Banker Danforth (February 2024 – May 2025) before founding Xceed Realty. He works with buyers and sellers in English and Mandarin Chinese across Eastside cities including Bellevue, Kirkland, Redmond, and Sammamish.

=== Xceed Realty ===
Xu is the founder and a broker of Xceed Realty in Bellevue. Company materials report more than 500 closed transactions and over $1 billion in career sales volume; independently verified annual rankings are published by RealTrends.

=== Other ventures ===
According to his LinkedIn profile, Xu has been founder of Bazyard Inc. in Bellevue since October 2026, described there as building an online marketplace at bazyard.com.

== Recognition ==
RealTrends Verified (2026 program, based on 2025 closed transactions) lists Xu with 64 transaction sides and $128.82 million in volume, ranking first in Bellevue by volume and third in Washington by volume. [ref: RealTrends Verified 2026, Side] Xceed’s agent page states that he ranked first in Washington by closed sales volume in the RealTrends Verified 2025 program.
