data.title: Behring Foundation
data.text:
The Behring Foundation (Fundação Behring) is a Brazilian family philanthropic foundation focused on education and technology, founded in 2020 by Alex Behring and Daniele Behring. Alex Behring is a co-founder and partner of 3G Capital and serves on the Board of Dean's Advisors of Harvard Business School. The foundation runs three programs for young people in technology, Behring Academy, Behring Scholars and Behring Founders, and a fourth initiative, Behring Network, through which it funds partnerships with academic and research institutions. According to the foundation, it also supports research initiatives at Hospital Pequeno Príncipe, a pediatric hospital in Curitiba.

== History ==
The foundation was established in 2020. It has funded scholarships at the Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro (PUC-Rio) since the early 2020s. In December 2024 it donated R$ 35million (about US$ 5.8 million) to the university for the creation of the PUC-Behring Institute of Artificial Intelligence; it was the largest single donation PUC-Rio had received since its founding in the 1940s. [ref: PUC-Rio establishes institute for teaching and research in Artificial Intelligence and will offer a degree in the field by 2025, O Globo] [ref: PUC-Rio recebe da Fundação Behring maior doação de sua história - Vatican News, www.vaticannews.va]

In 2022 the foundation co-founded Instituto Rio Aquatics, a Rio de Janeiro non-governmental organisation that works with children and adolescents in situations of social vulnerability through swimming and water polo. [ref: Projeto carioca une natação e educação para transformar vida de jovens em vulnerabilidad, Educação básica]The organisation opened its first site at Vasco da Gama in May 2022 and a second at the Júlio Delamare aquatic park in April 2023. The foundation is listed as one of its sustaining partners.

== Programs ==

=== Behring Academy ===
Behring Academy is a free online technology program for students from the ninth grade of Brazilian lower secondary school through the end of secondary school. Participants have won 24 medals at the Brazilian Informatics Olympiad (Olimpíada Brasileira de Informática) since the program began; six of them in its first year. More than 3,500 students have applied to the program and 101 have been selected. [ref: Fundação Behring abre inscrições para formação online e gratuita em tecnologia, Estudar Fora] [ref: Behring Academy – Fundação Behring]

=== Behring Scholars ===
Behring Scholars awards undergraduate scholarships in technology fields in Brazil and abroad. At Carnegie Mellon University, the foundation funds two Brazilian students a year enrolled in the School of Computer Science or the Electrical and Computer Engineering Department; the award may cover up to the full cost of attendance for the duration of their undergraduate education, depending on financial need. [ref: Behring Foundation gift supports international undergrads in tech, engineering.cmu.edu] The university described the gift as the first of its kind there. [ref: International Student Funding Opportunities - Student Financial Services - Division of Enrollment Management - Carnegie Mellon University, www.cmu.edu] As of 2026, the foundation reported more than 200 scholarships granted, over 180 of them active, at more than 40 universities in Brazil and abroad. [ref: The Behring Foundation-OBMEP Tech Scholarship Supports Medalists in STEM Courses, IMPA - Institute for Pure and Applied Mathematics] [ref: Behring Foundation awards 10 scholarships of R$ 900 to OBMEP medalists - IMPA Tech, IMPA Tech - O programa de graduação do IMPA] [ref: Fundação Behring lança bolsa exclusiva para brasileiros na melhor faculdade de Ciência da Computação dos EUA, Estudar Fora] [ref: Behring Scholars – Fundação Behring]

=== Behring Founders ===
Behring Founders, launched in 2025, supports young technology entrepreneurs through mentorship, networking and funding. According to the foundation, participants may receive up to R$ 200,000 (about US$ 37,000) without the foundation taking equity in their companies. [ref: Behring Founders – Fundação Behring]

=== Behring Network ===
Behring Network funds partnerships in science and technology. These include the PUC-Behring Institute of Artificial Intelligence at PUC-Rio, which will be housed in the Behring Building, a 3,300 m² facility on the university's Gávea campus designed pro bono by Bernardes Arquitetura; construction began in August 2025. [ref: PUC-Rio recebe da Fundação Behring maior doação de sua história - Vatican News, www.vaticannews.va] [ref: Pé no futuro! Como será o Instituto de Inteligência Artificial da PUC-Rio, VEJA RIO]

The foundation is also one of the founding funders of the Institute of Technology and Computing (ITEC), a residential undergraduate institution in computer science conceived by entrepreneur Cristiano Franco, alongside Marcelo Lacerda, Sérgio Pretto and the Telles Foundation. Backed by R$400 million over its first decade, its campus is under construction on a 20-hectare site in Gravataí, in the metropolitan region of Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul, with the first class expected in 2027. [ref: Como será o instituto de tecnologia e computação bancado por doação de empresários, Terra] [ref: Com foco em tecnologia, novo centro para graduação em Ciências da Computação terá sede em Gravataí, Correio do Povo]

data.title: Godfrey Nsereko
data.text:
Godfrey Nsereko is a Ugandan rally driver who competes in the two-wheel-drive (2WD) category of the National Rally Championship.

== Rallying career ==

Nsereko began his rally career as a co-driver before moving to the driver's seat in 2018. His debut as a driver was at the opening round of the 2018 National Rally Championship season in Mbarara, where he and co-driver Hamza Lwanga emerged as winners of the Clubman Rally Championship (CRC) category. Nsereko attributed his understanding of rallying fundamentals to his previous experience as a co-driver. [ref: Nsereko launches CRC title bid with victory in Mbarara, Kawowo Sports]

Later in the 2018 season, at the Kabalega Rally in Hoima, Nsereko and co-driver John Musisi won the CRC category. He was the only CRC finisher and secured the championship with two CRC events remaining. Kawowo Sports reported that the title was Nsereko's first rally championship. The Daily Monitor also identified Nsereko and Musisi as the CRC category winners. [ref: Nsereko draws several lessons after CRC success, Kawowo Sports] [ref: Pictorial: Alwi wins hotly contested Kabalega Rally, Daily Monitor]

For the 2019 season, Nsereko moved to the 2WD category. He emerged as the winner in the season-opening event in Mbarara after taking the lead following the retirement of Timothy Gawaya. Kawowo Sports reported that Nsereko and co-driver John Bosco Musisi took an early lead in the 2WD championship. [ref: Nsereko keen on more 2WD success, Kawowo Sports]

Nsereko continued competing in the 2WD category in subsequent seasons. Uganda Radio Network reported on his participation in the 2021 MOSAC Rally Championship and quoted him discussing the challenges of driving on muddy rally tracks. [ref: Drivers Decry Bad Weather During this Year's MOSAC Rally Championship, Uganda Radio Network]

In 2022, Nsereko was listed with 51 points in the final published 2WD standings of the National Rally Championship by the Daily Monitor. [ref: Rugomoka victory concludes NRC season that was, Daily Monitor]

data.title: Douglas A. Paul
data.text:
Douglas Alexander Paul is an American Army National Guard officer and Special Forces officer who served as commanding general of the Colorado Army National Guard and assistant adjutant general of Colorado from 2019 to 2022. He deployed to Afghanistan and Iraq several times and received the Purple Heart after being wounded in Iraq.

== Early life and education ==
Paul earned a Bachelor of Science in economics from California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo, a Master of Science in computer information technology from Regis University, and a Master of Strategic Studies from the United States Army War College, which he attended from 2012 to 2013. He is also a graduate of the United States Army Command and General Staff College.

== Military career ==
=== Early career and Afghanistan ===
Paul was commissioned a second lieutenant through the Reserve Officers' Training Corps on December 12, 1992. After the Engineer Officer Basic Course, he completed the Special Forces Detachment Officer Qualification Course. From 1993 to 2001 he commanded a Special Forces detachment ("A-Team") in Company C, 5th Battalion, 19th Special Forces Group (Airborne), based in Fort Collins, Colorado.

From December 2001 to November 2002 he was a detachment commander with Task Force Dagger/Crossbow in Gardez, Afghanistan, during Operation Enduring Freedom. He then commanded a detachment in Company B, 5th Battalion, 19th Special Forces Group, in Pueblo, Colorado, until August 2003.

=== Iraq ===
From August 2003 to August 2004 Paul was joint operations center director for Task Force Legion, Combined Joint Special Operations Task Force – Arabian Peninsula, in Baghdad. He was wounded in Iraq and received the Purple Heart. In January 2005 Governor Bill Owens recognized Paul for his wounding during the State of the State address to a joint session of the Colorado General Assembly.

After serving as operations officer of Special Operations Detachment – Korea from 2004 to 2006, he commanded Company B, 5th Battalion, 19th Special Forces Group, at Fort Carson from 2006 to 2007. From September 2007 to November 2008 he commanded the Special Forces advanced operating base of Special Operations Task Force North in Mosul.

=== Battalion command and staff assignments ===
Paul was executive officer of 5th Battalion, 19th Special Forces Group, from 2008 to 2009, and a contingency, exercise and plans officer with the Colorado Army National Guard's mobilization element at United States Northern Command from 2009 to 2010. He commanded 5th Battalion, 19th Special Forces Group (Airborne), in Watkins, Colorado, from June 2010 to July 2012.

After the Army War College, he was an operations officer with U.S. Northern Command J32/Special Operations Command – North in Colorado Springs from June to October 2013, and then deputy commander of Special Operations Detachment – Korea. From February to December 2014 he was senior Ministry of Defense advisor for the NATO Special Operations Component Command/Special Operations Joint Task Force – Afghanistan in Kabul. On his return he served as G3 (operations) of the Colorado Army National Guard from 2014 to 2016. He was qualified as a Joint Qualified Officer Level III in 2015 and promoted to colonel that December.

=== Korea and Afghanistan ===
From October 2016 to September 2018 Paul commanded Special Operations Detachment – Korea, based in Aurora, Colorado. From 2018 to 2019 he deployed as deputy commander of the Combined Joint Special Operations Task Force – Afghanistan, leading a task force of U.S., NATO and Afghan special operations forces.

=== Colorado Army National Guard command ===
Paul was promoted to brigadier general with a date of rank of August 20, 2019, and took command of the Colorado Army National Guard from Brigadier General Laura Clellan on October 19, 2019, at Fort Carson. The position also carries the title of Assistant Adjutant General, Army.

During his command the Colorado National Guard carried out the largest activation in its history in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, including building an alternative care site at the Colorado Convention Center in Denver and supporting assisted-living facilities across the state. Guard members also supported the 59th presidential inauguration and responded to the Marshall Fire, and the 1st Battalion, 157th Infantry deployed overseas for the first time since World War II.

On October 19, 2021, President Joe Biden nominated Paul for promotion to major general in the Reserve of the Army, and the Senate confirmed the nomination by voice vote on October 28, 2021. Official biographies published in 2022 continued to list his rank as brigadier general.

Paul relinquished command to Brigadier General Bren Rogers on February 5, 2022, in Loveland, Colorado, and became deputy commanding general for the Army National Guard at the Army's Combined Arms Center at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas.

=== Kennedy v. Paul ===
In September 2020 Paul issued a general officer memorandum of reprimand to Captain Alan Kennedy, a part-time Colorado Army National Guard judge advocate, over an opinion column Kennedy wrote about being investigated for attending a Black Lives Matter protest in Denver while off duty. Kennedy sued in federal court in March 2021, naming Paul, Colorado Adjutant General Laura Clellan, and Secretary of Defense Lloyd Austin among the defendants and alleging violations of his First Amendment rights. The National Guard Bureau later clarified that the Defense Department protest restrictions applied only to Guard members in federal status, the Colorado National Guard withdrew Kennedy's first reprimand, and in January 2022 an Army review board overturned the reprimand Paul had issued. In August 2022 U.S. District Judge William J. Martínez dismissed the case as moot.

== Civilian career ==
Paul has worked as lead contractor for the Office of the Secretary of Energy, conducting security and vulnerability assessments of special nuclear material sites, and as an on-call public arbitrator for the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority. He was previously an engineer and project manager for Lockheed Martin on programs for the Intelligence Community and the Departments of Defense and State, and received a 2012 award for excellence on a PAE Government Services State Department contract.

== Writings ==
* Failing to do what is right is the most common breach of trust, Army Times
* "Rule of Law Training in Afghanistan", in SOLLIMS Sampler: Special Edition – Lessons from USAWC Students, Peacekeeping and Stability Operations Institute, August 2013. [https://pksoi.armywarcollege.edu/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/SOLLIMS_Sampler_SpecEdition_Lessons_USAWCStudents_Aug2013-CDR-840.pdf PDF]
* Maintaining an Operational Reserve: A Strategy for Employment. U.S. Army War College. [https://www.hsdl.org/c/view?docid=812048 HSDL]
* People First and Winning Matters (manuscript).

== Affiliations ==
Paul is a director of the Special Operations Association. He is a member of the Military Order of the Purple Heart, the Special Forces Association, the Association of the United States Army, the U.S. Army War College Alumni Association, and the National Guard Association of the United States.

== Awards and decorations ==
Awards as listed in his National Guard Bureau biography:

data.title: Joan Rukundo Nalubega
data.text:
----

Joan Rukundo Nalubega is a Ugandan entrepreneur. She is the founder and chief executive officer of Uganics Repellents.

== Early Life ==
Joan Rukundo Nalubega grew up in an orphanage in Mpigi District. [ref: When college is out of reach, this academy trains Ugandans to be entrepreneurs, PBS News] [ref: Uganda: Menya Joan Nalubega wakoze isabune yirukana imibu, BBC News Gahuza] [ref: Joan Rukundo Nalubega — 30 Under 30 2026 — Forbes Africa, Forbes Africa] [ref: Africa’s Young Disruptors: Part Two, African Business] She contracted malaria multiple times during childhood. [ref: Vosen, Eva, Stefan Wilhelm, and André Habisch. "Empowering women as key changemakers: Why female-driven social innovation matters." The Global Impact of Social Innovation: Disrupting Old Models and Patterns. Cham: Springer International Publishing, 2022. 217-234.]

Nalubega completed high school, and was admitted to Makerere University to study chemistry. She did not complete her studies due to a lack of financial support.

== Career ==

=== Uganics ===
Nalubega attended the Social Innovation Academy (SINA) in Mpigi, a residential programme for young entrepreneurs. [ref: Uganda: How Anzisha Prize Helped Young Ugandan Grow Her Mosquito-Repellent Soap Business, allAfrica] [ref: Uganda's youth combat waste and malaria, Deutsche Welle] While at SINA, she developed the idea for her product, a mosquito repellant soap. [ref: Handmade Soap Keeps Malaria-Carrying Mosquitos Away in Uganda, Global Press Journal] In 2016, Nalubega founded Uganics Repellents. [ref: From Personal Loss to Public Health Innovation: Reimagining Malaria Prevention Through Uganics, African Leadership University] [ref: Meet Africa’s Top 20 Young Entrepreneurs shortlisted for Jack Ma Foundation’s Africa Netpreneur Prize 2020 competition, Business Insider Africa] Early activities included malaria awareness campaigns in local communities. [ref: Nip malaria in the bud with mosquito repellant soap, Monitor] [ref: Mosquito-repellent soap and healthy smoothies: Two young entrepreneurs show how to build businesses from organic products, How We Made It In Africa]

Nalubega collaborated with chemistry students at Makerere University in Kampala, Uganda, and students at University of Mannheim in Germany, on product development. [ref: Uganics Combats Malaria Via Mosquito Repellent Soap, Modern Ghana] [ref: FAO urges strategic focus on improving women’s contribution to global food security, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations] The soap received certification from the government of Uganda. Forbes Africa reported that Uganics is being sold in eight different countries.

Uganics sells its soap to hotel chains and resorts and offers a subsidized price to Ugandans. [ref: Malaria: Uganics Mosquito Repellent Soap, BORGEN] [ref: ] [ref: Les héros du business affûtent leurs arguments, New African - le Magazine de L'Afrique]

== Education ==
In 2025, Nalubega graduated from the African Leadership University (Rwanda campus) in the Entrepreneurial Leadership programme.

== Awards and Recognition ==
In 2019, Nalubega won the Johnson & Johnson Champions of Science: Africa Innovation Challenge. [ref: Johnson & Johnson Announces Six Winners of the Champions of Science Africa Innovation Challenge 2.0 at the 28th World Economic Forum on Africa, JNJ.com] [ref: Ugandan Innovations Win Africa Innovation Challenge, PC Tech Magazine]

In 2026, Nalubega was named on the Forbes Africa 30 Under 30 list. [ref: Meet two young Ugandans listed on Forbes Africa’s 30 Under 30 Class of 2026, Pulse Uganda] [ref: 30 Under 30 2026 — Forbes Africa, Forbes Africa] She was also featured on African Business's 20 Entrepreneurs Under 30 list.

Pilot Training Flight Simulator (abbreviated as PTFS) is a flight simulation experience on the online gaming platform Roblox with over 810 million visits. The game focuses on aircraft simulation and multiplayer aviation activities. Players can operate a variety of aircraft, ranging from small general-aviation planes to large commercial and cargo aircraft. The experience also includes military aircraft and other aviation-related vehicles, some of which are available through additional purchases. [ref: Pilot Training Club/Pilot Training Flight Simulator, Roblox Wiki]

PTFS supports multiplayer servers, allowing players to fly together and organise aviation-related activities.

Pilot Training Flight Simulator has accumulated hundreds of millions of visits on Roblox and has an established player community, such as the PRG (PTFS Roleplay Group). [ref: Discord - Group Chat That’s All Fun & Games, Discord]

As of October 2026, publicly available game-tracking websites reported approximately 813 million total visits, 2.3 million favourites and a positive rating of around 93%. data.title: Smash&Clash
data.text:
Smash&Clash is a two-player strategy card-and-board game created in India by Harshit Khemani. [ref: Terms of Service, Smash&Clash] Players take turns placing character cards on a three-by-five board, and a placed card captures adjacent opposing cards by comparing the numbers on their touching sides. The player who controls more cards when the board is full wins. [ref: Rules, Smash&Clash Docs]

The game is sold as a physical set of cards and a board, and a free digital edition is played in web browsers and through apps for Windows, macOS, Linux and Android. [ref: Download Smash&Clash 2.1.0, Smash&Clash] [ref: Smash&Clash – Board Game, Whop] Since October 2026 the digital edition has also offered a public API through which other programs, including AI agents, can play the game, and the developer has published open-source clients that run it inside other games and on older consoles. [ref: Smash&Clash for developers, Smash&Clash Docs]

== Gameplay ==
=== Board and cards ===
The board has 15 tiles in three rows and five columns, named A1 to E3. Both players draw from a shared deck of 51 cards: 46 character cards and five effect cards. Each player holds five cards, plays exactly one card per turn and then draws back up to five. Each character card has its own name and artwork and four side values from 1 to 7, one for each edge, read from its owner's side of the table. [ref: Changelog, Smash&Clash Docs]

=== Captures and scoring ===
A character card may be placed on any empty tile. It is then compared with each orthogonally adjacent opposing card that is not frozen. If the placed card's touching side is greater than or equal to the opposing card's touching side, the opposing card is captured and turned to face the attacker, so ties favour the attacker. Captures happen only when a card is placed and do not chain to further cards. Because a card belongs to the player it faces, the cards on the board are the score. The game ends as soon as all 15 tiles are filled, and the player with more cards wins; as the board has an odd number of tiles, a game cannot be drawn.

=== Effect cards ===
The deck contains one copy of each of five effect cards, which can be played only when they would have an effect:
* Boulder removes a non-frozen card together with every non-frozen card in its row and column.
* Flip turns the whole board 180 degrees, so every card changes sides.
* Freeze permanently freezes one of the player's own cards, which then cannot be captured, attack or be removed.
* Recruit takes a non-frozen opposing card and places it on an empty tile as the player's own, where it attacks.
* Swap exchanges the two players' hands.

=== Rulesets ===
The game has two rulesets, Classic and Mutators; Mutators is the default. It adds three kinds of special tile:
* Chess tiles: two per game, each marked as a knight, bishop, rook or queen. A card placed on one may move like that chess piece to an empty tile and attack again.
* Power tiles: two new tiles each turn, each with a colour and a bonus of +1 or +2. A card of the matching colour placed on one attacks with every side boosted.
* Overrun zones: the three centre tiles, B2, C2 and D2. When a player's card on one of them is surrounded on all four sides, that player may play a new card on top of it.

== Editions ==
=== Physical edition ===
The physical edition consists of 51 cards and a game board. It is sold online through Whop, which acts as the seller of record for payment, delivery and refunds.

=== Digital edition ===
The digital edition is free and has no advertising or in-app purchases; it can be played without an account, while accounts and online features are limited to users aged 13 or older. It presents the board in 3D, with character voices produced using ElevenLabs. [ref: About Smash&Clash, Smash&Clash] Players can play against an adaptive computer opponent, learn the rules in a tutorial, or play another person on the same device. For online play, a player can create a room with a six-letter code or join a quick-match queue that pairs waiting players, and optional profiles and leaderboards record results.

A finished game can be viewed as a move-by-move replay or as a "Game Review", which rates every move against the best one available in that position and summarises each player's accuracy and the game's key moments. [ref: Replays and reviews, Smash&Clash Docs] Every game also has a public watch page that shows it live with both hands face-down, and a "Smash&Clash TV" page shows the game currently being played.

=== Platforms ===
The game is played in web browsers at smashandclash.in. Installable apps are distributed for Windows 10 and 11, macOS 11 or later, Linux and Android 7.0 or later; on iOS and iPadOS it is added to the home screen as a progressive web app. The apps can be played offline against the computer opponent, and online they connect to players on every other version. The game is also offered through a Telegram bot [ref: @[user], Telegram] and a Snapchat Lens, [ref: Smash&Clash Lens by Harshit Khemani, Snapchat] as a terminal game, and, according to its terms, as a Discord Activity, a ChatGPT app and an app embedded in Whop.

== Developer platform ==
The developer documentation describes Smash&Clash as one game network shared by all of its clients. The server stores each game and recomputes every position with a deterministic engine, so only legal moves are accepted, and the public API requires no accounts or API keys. It is offered as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for AI assistants, a versioned REST API with an OpenAPI 3.1 description, a JavaScript and TypeScript software development kit and a command-line client, the last two labelled beta. Through it, AI agents can play people through invite links, play each other, join quick match or play a computer "house" opponent whose strength can be set between 800 and 1600 Elo. Under the published fair-play rules, no player is shown a card they could not see at a physical table, and a game's random seed is revealed only after it ends.

"Hosted Agent Challenges" are links that an AI agent sends to a person; an agent hosted by Smash&Clash then plays that person on the sending agent's behalf. The documentation states that these hosted agents are powered by AgentsORG.

The developer has published open-source example clients built on the SDK, including a version inside the 1993 Doom engine, a FiveM resource for Grand Theft Auto V servers, tables for Minecraft Java and Bedrock editions, a Nintendo DS game, a Game Boy Advance client, a PlayStation Portable version and a tldraw whiteboard client.

== History ==
According to Khemani, the game began at a 24-hour hackathon and was refined through playtesting; he lists himself as its founder from February 2025. [ref: Harshit Khemani, khe.money] The operator is Khemani as an individual trading as Smash&Clash, not a company.

data.title: DatuKali Gumander
data.text:
Datu Kali Gumander (1880–1973), also known by his honorific title Datukali Gumander, was a prominent Muslim scholar, a traditional judge, and a tribal leader from Maguindanao del Norte province in the Philippines. He descended from a noble lineage of the Iranun people, and played a crucial role in preserving Islamic education, customary laws (Adat), and resolving disputes among the tribes and clans of the Moro people during the late 19th and early 20th centuries. [ref: The Saga of Datukali Gumander: A Legacy of Royalty, Exploration, and Kinship] [ref: The Muslim IRANUN Nation (Uranen Kingdom), iranunnation.blogspot.com] [ref: Datukali Gumander Clan: The Three Grand Reunions (1988-2023)]

He is also considered the great-grandfather and founder of the "Gumander family," whose descendants are spread today across Maguindanao del Norte province, specifically in the municipality of Sultan Mastura, and in Zamboanga del Sur, particularly in the lands of Labangan and Bulanit.

== Early life and lineage ==
Gumander was born in 1880 [ref: Datukali Gumander, www.wikidata.org] in the Tumingay area, within what is known today as the village of Bungabong in the municipality of Sultan Mastura in Maguindanao del Norte province. He was the eldest son of Datu Baraguir by his second wife, Lilangen. [ref: The Saga Of Datukali Gumander] His father, Datu Baragir, held the high royal title of Watamama (next in line to the throne or grandson of the Sultan) within the Sultanate of Maguindanao. According to the family tree circulated among clan genealogists and in sources related to the Gumander family, the family's roots trace back to Shariff Mohammed Kabungsuwan, the founder of the Sultanate, which represents the third-highest rank in the Sultanate's hierarchy after the Sultan (Surutan) and the Crown Prince (Rajah Muda).

Gumander grew up in his father's Torogan (traditional royal house) and was immersed in the rich cultural and political traditions of the Iranun and Maguindanao peoples. [ref: The Saga of Datukali Gumander: A Legacy of Royalty, Exploration, and Kinship, Zenodo] Early in his life, he showed an interest in learning and social affairs, often attending his father's councils where local disputes and conflicts were discussed. This allowed him to become familiar with methods of mediation and dispute resolution according to local customs.

== Education in Cairo ==
Recognizing his son's potential, Datu Baraguir provided Gumander with an exceptional foundation in Islamic teachings and tribal governance. Driven by his thirst for knowledge and his realization of the importance of education, Gumander asked for his father's permission to travel abroad to continue his studies.

In 1900, Gumander traveled to Cairo, Egypt, where he enrolled in Al-Azhar University, the most prominent center for Islamic learning at the time. During his six-year stay in Egypt, he mastered the Arabic language, delved into the study of Islamic jurisprudence (Fiqh), theology (Kalam), and Hadith, and successfully memorized the entire Holy Quran. [ref: The Saga of Datukali Gumander: A Legacy of Royalty, Exploration, and Kinship, Medium] His presence in Cairo allowed him to interact with a broader Islamic academic environment and become acquainted with the intellectual and political currents that prevailed in the Islamic world during that era.

== Return and the Judiciary ==
Gumander returned to Mindanao in the southern Philippines in 1906. Upon his arrival, he first settled in the western region of Zamboanga del Sur, where he engaged in religious education. He established schools to teach Islamic sciences and the Arabic language, and participated in spreading Islamic education among the local population. Over time, Gumander gained social and religious prominence among the people. His name became associated with mediating and settling disputes in accordance with Islamic rulings and local customs, which contributed to the widespread use of the title "Kali Gumander" (Judge Gumander) to refer to him.

His activity and influence extended to several areas in northern Maguindanao (Balut, Sabangan, Nunuling), reaching Illana Bay, the Zamboanga Peninsula, and Lanao del Sur province. [ref: The Saga of Datukali Gumander: A Legacy of Royalty, Exploration, and Kinship, Zenodo] In addition to settling local disputes, his activities were linked to religious education and the preservation of Islamic practices and social customs among the communities of the Moro people.

== Family and Marriages ==
Gumander married several times, and his marriages were tied to families and figures of religious, political, or social standing in various regions of the Moro people's communities:

* Bai Pama: His first wife, the daughter of a religious leader named Bagumbung (known as a Pandita). [ref: The Panditas of the Philippines, 17th - Early 20th Centuries, Archipel. Études interdisciplinaires sur le monde insulindien] He was one of the most prominent religious figures in the region, and this marriage solidified his relations in northern Maguindanao. Together they had several children, including: Gandawali, Salusub (who later succeeded him as a field commander and traditional leader), Birma, Midtanjal, Kabuntu, and Rimbang.
* Bai Alya: His second wife, the daughter of Dipatuan Makarao Buto, who belonged to the ruling dynasty of the Sultanate of Buayan. This marriage established a strategic alliance in the Kaludan area. Gumander had no children with her. [ref: The Saga of Datukali Gumander: A Legacy of Royalty, Exploration, and Kinship]
* Antengan: His third wife, affectionately known as "Lilang sa Balaniog", from the Bulanit and Labangan areas in Zamboanga del Sur. They had a son named Malisu, whose activities were later linked to the family's agricultural properties in the region.

== Later years and death ==
Datu Kali Gumander was a visionary leader and tribal chieftain whose political and social influence profoundly shaped the Moro landscape. Throughout his life, he seamlessly combined his religious authority with strong tribal leadership to mediate tribal conflicts and unite many feuding clans.

His strategic vision and leadership left an indelible mark in multiple regions of Mindanao island. In northern Maguindanao, Gumander's name became associated with the founding of the village of Bungabong, which became his family's seat and the center of its activities. In Zamboanga del Sur, he owned vast agricultural lands in Bulanit and Labangan, ensuring the economic and political standing of his family. In Lanao del Sur, his special status was cemented by the establishment of a municipality named "Sultan Gumander" in 1977 in his honor. [ref: Ketabah Platform, Ketabah Platform]

In his later years, his health began to decline. At the urging of his son Malisu, he returned to his lands in [https://www.accuweather.com/en/ph/bulanit/1888455/lightning/1888455 Bulanit] and Labangan, where he spent his final days until his death there in 1973. He left behind a profound legacy as a guardian of the Islamic faith and a fundamental pillar of Moro unity.

== Legacy and the Municipality of Sultan Gumander ==
Datu Kali Gumander's overarching influence, noble lineage, and services to the Moro people were so deeply rooted in the region's history that a municipality was established and named in his honor. The municipality of Sultan Gumander (now known as Picong) in Lanao del Sur province, which previously bore his name, stands as a historical testament to his stature as a leader whose legacy transcended tribal and geographical boundaries. [ref: Picong, Lanao del Sur, Wikipedia]

The name "Sultan Gumander" proudly represented the municipality for decades, immortalizing his presence and leadership. In 2006, the municipality's name was officially changed to "Picong" under the Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 175 (MMAA No. 175). This legislative change was later upheld and affirmed by the Supreme Court of the Philippines, legally documenting the historical transition of the area, while the legacy of Datukali Gumander remained a foundational pillar in its history. [ref: CREATING THE MUNICIPALITY OF SULTAN GUMANDER IN THE PROVINCE OF LANAO DEL SUR] [ref: Law Summary: Creating The Municipality Of Sultan Gumander In The Province Of Lanao Del Sur - Presidential Decree No. 1135, www.digest.ph]

data.title: Lord F
data.text:
Lord F is a Brazilian-born singer, songwriter and television presenter based in Los Angeles. His music incorporates pop and electronic dance music. [ref: Interview with talented LA-based artist Lord F, Naluda Magazine]

He released his self-titled debut EP through Midas Music in 2015, with production by Rick Bonadio and Renato Patriarca. [ref: ] The four-track release featured songs in English and Portuguese. Alongside his recording career, he worked in Brazilian Television, including the television show Club Mix on Mix Tv. [ref: ]

In 2018 he released "Touch" [ref: ]

On April 4, 2019 Lord F released "Timing", a single addressing personal struggles and mental health within the LGBTQ community. In a Billboard feature, he discussed how his experiences growing up gay in Brazil influenced the song. Billboard reported that proceeds from the release were intended to benefit the Los Angeles LGBT Center and the London LGBTQ Community Centre. [ref: Lord F Wants to Get Real About LGBTQ Mental Health With New Track 'Timing': Listen, Billboard]

His 2021 releases included "Perfect Imperfection" and "Aqua". In an interview with Naluda Magazine, he described "Perfect Imperfection" as exploring acceptance and compromise in romantic relationships. The Advocate covered "Aqua", a dance-pop song drawing comparisons between love and water. [ref: ]

He released his first full length studio album "Once Upon a Song", a 15 track collection, in April 2021 [ref: ]

Outside music, Lord F co-founded the clothing brand Fitx Wear with his sister in 2020, according to his Naluda interview

data.title: University of Health Sciences (Somalia)
data.text:
----

University of Health Sciences (UOHS; Somali: Jaamacadda Culuumta
Caafimaadka) is a private non-profit higher-education institution in Bosaso,
Bari, Puntland, Somalia. It provides education and training in health sciences
and has a Faculty of Medicine listed in the World Directory of Medical
Schools.University of Health Sciences Faculty of Medicine, World Directory of Medical Schools
== History ==
The university's institutional history states that the University of Health Sciences
was established in September 2000 as a health institute. It was promoted to college
status in 2003 and obtained university status in 2012. The institution attributes its
establishment to the shortage of medical professionals in Somalia following the
country's civil war.UOHS History and Background of the University, University of Health Sciences
The university identifies Prof. Abdirisak Hussein Hassan as its founding father.
According to the university, he established a nursing institute in response to
shortages of trained medical personnel in Somalia.UOHS Founding Father, University of Health Sciences
A 2013 report by the Heritage Institute for Policy Studies listed the University of
Health Sciences among the higher-education institutions surveyed in Puntland. The
report recorded the institution as having been established in 2006 and, at the time of
the survey, listed five faculties and 947 students.The State of the Higher Education Sector in Somalia, Heritage Institute for Policy Studies
== Administration ==
The university's current rector is Dr. Najma Abdirisak H. Hassan. The university's
rector page identifies her as rector, and the Somali Research and Education Network
lists her as a member of its board of directors in the same capacity.Rector's Message, University of Health SciencesBoard of Directors, Somali Research and Education Network
== Academics ==
The university's academic structure includes eight health sciences faculties: the
Faculty of Medicine and Surgery, Faculty of Clinical Midwifery, Faculty of Clinical
Nursing, Faculty of Food Sciences and Nutrition, Faculty of Clinical Pharmacy,
Faculty of Public Health, Faculty of Medical Laboratory, and Faculty of Radiological
Sciences and Medical Imaging.UOHS History and Background of the University, University of Health SciencesUndergraduate Programs, University of Health Sciences

The University of Health Sciences Somalia (UOHS) is a member institution of the Somali Research and Education Network (SomaliREN), a non-profit organization that connects higher education and research institutions in Somalia.Member Institutions, Somali Research and Education Network

The Faculty of Medicine provides a Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery
(MBBS) programme. The World Directory of Medical Schools records the school
as a private, currently operational medical school in Bosaso. It lists 2014 as the year
instruction began, a five-year curriculum, and admission of both men and
women.University of Health Sciences Faculty of Medicine, World Directory of Medical Schools
The university also offers undergraduate programmes in clinical nursing, clinical
midwifery, food sciences and nutrition, public health, medical laboratory sciences,
clinical pharmacy, and radiological sciences and medical imaging.Undergraduate Programs, University of Health Sciences
The radiological sciences and medical imaging programme was inaugurated in 2021,
according to the university, which describes it as an undergraduate programme in
the field.Faculty of Radiological Sciences & Medical Imaging, University of Health Sciences
== Research ==
Researchers affiliated with the University of Health Sciences have participated in
published studies concerning health and higher education in Somalia.
A 2022 study published in BioMed Research International examined hepatitis B
vaccination status and related factors among healthcare workers in Bosaso,
Puntland. The study included researchers affiliated with the University of Health
Sciences.Assessment of Hepatitis B Vaccination Status and Associated Factors among Healthcare Workers in Bosaso, Puntland, Somalia 2020, BioMed Research International
A 2023 study published in BMC Public Health investigated hepatitis B vaccination
coverage among medical students in Bosaso. The study used a sample drawn from
four universities in the city and included a researcher affiliated with the Faculty of
Public Health at the University of Health Sciences.Hepatitis B vaccination coverage and associated factors among medical students: a cross-sectional study in Bosaso, Somalia, 2021, BMC Public Health
In 2025, a study published in PLOS ONE examined tuberculosis treatment
outcomes at Bosaso TB Hospital using records from January 2018 to December 2022.
One of the authors was affiliated with the Faculty of Medicine at the University of
Health Sciences.Tuberculosis treatment outcomes and associated factors among patients treated at Bosaso TB Hospital, Bosaso, Somalia: A five-year retrospective study, PLOS ONE
A 2026 article in Cogent Education examined challenges affecting research and
academic publishing in higher education institutions in Puntland. The author, Saaid
Said Jama, is affiliated with the Faculty of Medicine at the University of Health
Sciences.The challenges facing higher education in Puntland in research and academic publishing: suggestions for their improvement, Cogent Education
A 2026 study published in Critical Public Health examined metabolic risk patterns

data.title: Zoltán Mészáros
data.text:
Zoltán Mészáros (born 2 May 1964) is a Hungarian-German actor, theatre and film director, musician and writer based in Munich, Germany. He gained nationwide recognition in Hungary through his leading role as András Urbán in the television series Angyalbőrben. His artistic career encompasses stage and screen acting, theatre and film direction, music, and audiobook production. [ref: Mészáros Zoltán, József Attila Library, Dunaújváros]

== Early life and education ==

Mészáros was born in Dunaújváros, Hungary, and grew up in Miskolc-Diósgyör. He studied acting at GNM in Budapest, graduating with a diploma in acting.

== Acting career ==

=== Television and film ===

Mészáros first appeared on Hungarian television in Linda. He achieved nationwide popularity through his leading role as András Urbán in Angyalbőrben (1988–1990). His portrayal of Urbán brought him considerable public recognition and established him as a familiar face to Hungarian television audiences. [ref: Interjú Mészáros Zoltán színésszel, József Attila Library – Local History Archive]

In 2020, he played the leading role of Zoltán Farkas in Don Juan Is Balding (Don Juan kopaszodik), a Hungarian television film directed by Linda Dombrovszky, based on works by Ferenc Herczeg. The film was selected for the Tiburon International Film Festival and the White Nights Film Festival in Saint Petersburg in 2020. It received a nomination for Best Television Film at the 2021 Hungarian Motion Picture Awards. [ref: Don Juan Is Balding, Linda Dombrovszky – Official Filmography]

Mészáros also appeared in the Hungarian television series S.E.R.E.G. (2024).

=== Theatre ===

From 1990 to 1996, Mészáros was a member of the Hungarian-language ensemble of the National Theatre in Târgu Mureș, Romania. He subsequently worked at the Szigligeti Theatre in Szolnok and the Figura Studio Theatre in Gheorgheni.

One of his significant stage performances was the role of Teodul in Lucian Blaga's Cruciada copiilor (The Children's Crusade), directed by Victor Ioan Frunză at the National Theatre in Târgu Mureș. The production, in which Mészáros performed, was nominated for Best Performance at the 1993 UNITER Awards. [ref: Cruciada copiilor de Lucian Blaga, UNITER – Romanian Theatre Union]

In 1998, he founded an independent theatre company in Gheorgheni, Romania.

=== Selected leading and major stage roles ===

* Euripides – Iphigenia in Aulis: Achilles
* Nikolai Gogol – Diary of a Madman: Poprishchin
* William Gibson – Two for the Seesaw: Jerry Ryan
* Sławomir Mrożek – The Emigrants: AA
* Lucian Blaga – The Children's Crusade: Teodul
* Ödön von Horváth – Tales from the Vienna Woods: Havlicsek
* Ray Cooney – Run for Your Wife: Inspector Troughton
* Gábor Görgey – Komámasszony, hol a stukker?: Cuki
* András Sütő – Álomkommandó: Interior Ministry official
* Ephraim Kishon – The Marriage Certificate: Robert Knoll
* William Shakespeare – The Merchant of Venice: Lucentio

== Directing career ==

Mészáros has directed stage productions as well as documentary, independent and experimental films.

=== Selected theatre productions ===

* Frigyes Karinthy – Kis Rómeó, kis Júlia
* Sławomir Mrożek – The Emigrants
* William Gibson – Two for the Seesaw

=== Selected film directing credits ===

* 2003: Kerlerspaan – experimental film
* 2004: Die Mission – educational film
* 2004: Go West! – documentary
* 2007: Wenn der Papst kommt – independent film
* 2007: Lepradorf in Europa – documentary
* 2010: Kerlerspaan – ten-minute festival version
* 2011: Mandy – short film

== Music ==

In 1991, Mészáros appeared alongside Hungarian actor Mátyás Usztics on the musical release Jelentsen, Olajbogyó!. The project involved collaboration with Hungarian musician Róbert Szikora.

During 1992 and 1993, Mészáros participated in more than sixty live concerts.

In Munich, he continued his musical activities. His projects include the rock band Minga Brezn, founded in 2026, and work under the artistic name Ólafur Andersson.

His musical work also includes You Take Us Down with You, a peace oratorio exploring war, violence, human responsibility and the pursuit of peace. The project incorporates literary and mythological themes, including ancient Mesopotamian texts and European literary traditions. The work is in development.

== Audiobook production ==

Mészáros has worked in Hungarian-language audiobook production in Munich, including recordings of works by Hungarian literary authors. His work has been associated with AVL Media.

Selected recordings include:

* Jenő Rejtő – Pipacs, a fenegyerek
* Sándor Szathmári – Kazohinia
* Kálmán Mikszáth – A jó palócok
* Kálmán Mikszáth – Tót atyafiak
* Mór Jókai – A nagyenyedi két fűzfa
* Gyula Krúdy – Rózsa Sándor
* Ferenc Móra – Rab ember fiai
* Ferenc Móra – Kincskereső kisködmön

== Work in Germany ==

Mészáros moved to Munich in 1999, where he continued his work as an actor, director, writer and musician.

In 2026, he founded Kunstbühne München, an independent multidisciplinary theatre and cultural initiative intended to bring together dramatic theatre, film, music and literature.

His literary and musical works are also published or developed under the name Ólafur Andersson.

data.title: Carl Philipp Trump
data.text:
Carl Philipp Trump (born January 25, 1988 in Berlin) is the central founder of the far-left democratic socialist German political party Gut-Menschen-Partei (Good-People-Party) in Germany and the German roughly fourth cousin, twice removed [ref: Trump Family Tree, Gut-Menschen-Partei.de] of US president Donald John Trump.

== Education ==
Carl Philipp Trump attended the Jesuit high school Canisius-Kolleg Berlin and graduated in 2007 [ref: Carl Philipp Trump].

He then went on to study 1.) political science (major) and 2.) sociology (minor) in 2008 in a Bachelor of Arts program at the public Ludwig Maximilian University in Munich (LMU Munich). Carl Philipp Trump spent his semester abroad 2012 as a visiting student at the private Ivy League Columbia University in the City of New York.

After that he studied International Relations in a Master of Science program at the public London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) in the UK graduating in 2014.

data.title: Dom Shaw
data.text:
Dom Shaw is a British novelist, screenwriter and documentary filmmaker, best known for co-directing Rough Cut & Ready Dubbed (1982), https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0493162/ an award-winning documentary about Britain's punk and post-punk music scenes.

Co-directed with Hasan Shah, the film was distributed by the British Film Institute, screened internationally, including at the 1982 Melbourne International Film Festival, https://miff.com.au/festival-archive/films/16709/rough-cut-and-ready-dubbed and received the Grierson Award for Best Documentary. https://www.imdb.com/event/ev0001534/1982/1/ It was subsequently digitally restored and re-released in 2005, accompanied by a follow-up documentary revisiting its original participants. https://www.eccentricsleevenotes.com/rough-cut-film?

Shaw has also worked as a television screenwriter for British broadcasters, including the BBC and ITV.

His debut novel, Eric is Awake (2013), imagines George Orwell awakening in a future Britain. The novel was reviewed by Rosemary Bechler in openDemocracy in 2014.https://www.opendemocracy.net/en/book-review-eric-is-awake-by-dom-shaw/ -->

data.title: Admas elementary spokane washington
data.text:
= Adams Elementary School (Spokane, Washington) =
Adams Elementary School is a public elementary school located in the South Hill neighborhood of Spokane,Washington. Part of Spokane Public Schools (District 81), the school serves students from Pre-Kindergarten through 5th grade. Originally established in the early 20th century, it is known for being one of the most historic school sites in Spokane.
Adams Elementary School Building. Source: Spokane Public Schools

== Quick Facts / Infobox ==

* Location: Spokane, Washington, U.S.
* Address (Original Site): 2909 E 37th Ave, Spokane, WA 99223
* Temporary Location (Camp Adams): 3612 S Grand Blvd, Spokane, WA 99203
* School District: Spokane Public Schools (District 81)
* Grades: Pre-K – 5th Grade
* Mascot: All-Stars
* Motto / Identity: "We grow All-Star citizens every day"
* Feeder School For: Sacajawea Middle School / Adams Attendance Area

== History ==

* 1909 Construction: The original school structure was built in 1909 to serve families settling in the South Hill region of Spokane.
* Early Expansions: An additional wing was added in 1917 to accommodate rapid growth in neighborhood enrollment.
* Rebuild Project (2025–2027): As part of a Spokane Public Schools facility upgrade bond, plans were established to build a brand-new, modern facility on the original 37th Avenue grounds.
* Camp Adams Era: Beginning around early 2026, students and staff temporarily relocated to the former Jefferson Elementary building at 3612 S. Grand Blvd (dubbed Camp Adams) while the new building undergoes construction.

== Campus & Facilities ==

* Original Site: Situated near the Lincoln Heights neighborhood on 37th Avenue, featuring classic multi-story red brick architecture.
* Temporary "Camp Adams": Features classic classroom layouts, dedicated play areas, and bus drop-off lanes designed to host South Hill school populations during modern building transitions.
* Future Facility: The new replacement building will feature modern safety upgrades, dedicated STEM/art spaces,and integrated community partnerships.

== Academics & Programs ==

* Curriculum: Core subjects include early literacy, mathematics, science, and social studies aligned with Washington State learning standards.
* Special Programs: Offers special education services, physical education, music programs, and student support intervention groups.
* Recognitions: Recipient of multiple Washington Achievement Awards for academic growth and citizenship programs.

== Community & Culture ==

* School Mascot: Adams All-Stars
* Partnerships: Collaborates with local neighborhood associations and youth organizations, including planned integrated spaces with local youth programs like the Boys & Girls Club on site.

== Sources & References ==

data.text:
----

Disappeared Completely is a Ukrainian English-language music project founded by Vitalii Shapka (also known as James Header). [ref: Новий альбом українців Disappeared Completely — зухвалі гаражні бойовики, які ми заслужили, СЛУХ] The band consists of Vitalii Shapka and Maryna Kryklia. [ref: About & Press, Disappeared Completely] Their music combines indie pop, trip hop, blues, electronic music and rock. [ref: Emerging acts of Ukrainian music, Ukrainian Institute]

== History ==
Vitalii Shapka had been working on music alone since 2012.

Disappeared Completely signed a contract with La Belle Musique. [ref: In Conversation with indie-electronic act Disappeared Completely on their latest dreamy EP, 'Dissolved', The Playground / PLAYY Magazine]

Disappeared Completely released their debut album Sea of Fallen Nests. [ref: Disappeared Completely "Pretty Average" (2023), Варіанти]

The EP Dissolved was released in 2019. Eduardo Recife created the cover art for the EP.

In 2020, Disappeared Completely released their second EP, Contradictions.

=== Pretty Average ===
In October 2023, the band's second full-length album, titled Pretty Average, was released. [ref: 23 найкращих українських альбоми 2023 року, Лірум]

==== Critical reception ====
Slukh described Pretty Average as "a major step forward" for Disappeared Completely, finding that the album differed from its predecessors but that the band's new defiance sounded natural. Oleksandr Kovalchuk of Varianty described the album's strongest material as encompassing "almost the entire track list".

Writing for Liroom, Liera Zdanevych praised the band's balance between garage energy and polished indie rock, while observing that some of the live performance's expressiveness was lost on the recording.

=== Later activity ===
Disappeared Completely represented Ukraine at international showcase festivals in Europe. [ref: Archive, Waves Vienna] [ref: Artists, Music Export Ukraine]

The band performed at the Atlas United 24 festival. [ref: Air strikes can't stop the music at this Ukrainian festival, BBC News]

The band was included in the list of "100 Artists to Watch for 2024 in Collaboration with YouTube" curated by the Independent Music Companies Association. [ref: Showcasing diversity in the European independent music scene – IMPALA's 100 Artists to Watch for 2024 in collaboration with YouTube, IMPALA]

Ten of the band's songs were used in the Ukrainian computer game S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2: Heart of Chornobyl. [ref: УСЯ українська музика у S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2: Heart of Chornobyl (Full Radio MIX), PlayUA]

* Contradictions (2020)

data.title: 681 (genre)
data.text:
----

681 is the genre of music that consist of exactly vocals and percussion instruments. It combines a capella with minimalist dance music. An example is the song Crabapples [ref: Bruce Peninsula: "Crabapples", Pitchfork] by Bruce Peninsula. [ref: Bruce Peninsula climbing the musical ladder, Interrobang]

It follows that this is the alternative name of the genre of minimalist vocal dance music.

Many genres have a given alternative name. For example, an alternative name trance is given to usually minimalist ambient rhythmic dance music with tempo between 120 and 150 BPM.

== Name origin ==

The name origin of this genre is mathematical. The name 681 originates from the list of natural numbers. The main values are taken as the rank of the dominance of elements of vocal music in general. Call them a, b, c, etc. We have a=1 because of the existence of vocals as the primary element of most vocal songs. [ref: Musical Texture, Fundamentals: Music in World Cultures] Then we skip 2 because there are no instruments other than percussion in this genre to function as the secondary element of most vocal songs. Hence we take b=3 as the next notable number because there is percussion in this genre and is the tertiary element of most vocal songs. The formula of the square of a binomial is (a+b)^2=a^2+2\cdot a\cdot b+b^2. If we square the exponents of b in each addend, i.e., raise them to the 2nd power, because 2 is the skipped natural number, we get the addends a^2, 2\cdot a \cdot b and b^4, respectively. The addends are equal to 1, 6 and 81, respectively. The ratio when the second addend is divided by the first addend is 6/1=6, while the ratio when the third addend is divided by the first addend is 81/1=81. Its concatenation gives 681.

data.title: Soren Johnstone
data.text:
Soren Johnstone is a Canadian filmmaker, cinematographer, editor, producer and screenwriter based in Vancouver, British Columbia. His work includes narrative films, documentary films, action-sports productions and television. He is known for directing the feature film Play with Fire and the documentary Hicks on Sticks. [ref: Hicks on Sticks, Film Threat]

Johnstone began making videos in the 1990s, initially filming skateboarding and snowboarding in the West Kootenay region of British Columbia. His later work has included the documentary Lost in Havana and the travel and action-sports television series Getting Amongst.

== Career ==
=== Early work ===
Johnstone began creating videos in the mid-1990s. His interest in filmmaking developed while filming friends skateboarding and snowboarding in British Columbia's West Kootenay region. According to his professional biography, he co-founded a production company in his early twenties and subsequently began producing professional video work. [ref: About, Soren Johnstone]

His early work was associated with skateboarding, snowboarding and other action sports. His action-sports productions include Attention Deficit, Under Exposed and Distortion. [ref: Soren Johnstone, Soren Johnstone]

This work garnered national attention when Johnstone received a YTV Achievement Award for Visual Arts. [ref: ]

=== Play with Fire ===
Johnstone wrote and directed the independent feature film Play with Fire. He also worked as cinematographer, editor and co-producer on the production. [ref: Play With Fire (IMDb), IMDb]

The film was completed in 2009. Contemporary coverage of the production by The Cascade reported that the film received a Best Cinematography award at an international film festival in Toronto. [ref: Play with Fire: Indie film premiere grips crowd at the Reach, The Cascade]

The film was shot in British Columbia and was produced independently. Johnstone worked with producer Michael Babiarz on the production.

=== Hicks on Sticks ===
Johnstone wrote and directed the feature-length documentary Hicks on Sticks, which documents a skateboarding and music tour through Western Canada. [ref: Hicks on Sticks definitely on a roll, [[Montreal Gazette]

The documentary originated with footage Johnstone recorded while accompanying the tour in 1999. The tour brought together four skateboarders and two bands and travelled through small communities in Western Canada with a portable skateboard park. The objective was to bring skateboarding and live music to young people in communities where those activities were not readily available. [ref: 2012 Action Sports Film Series, Newport Beach Film Festival]

The Newport Beach Film Festival presented the world premiere of Hicks on Sticks in 2012. Festival material described the film as a Canadian production directed by Johnstone and documented the tour as travelling approximately 1,800 miles through Western Canada while towing a 5,000-pound portable skateboard park.

More than a decade after the original tour, Johnstone combined footage recorded during the 1999 trip with later interviews with participants to create the documentary.

Film critic Scott Knopf reviewed Hicks on Sticks for Film Threat in 2012. Knopf commented positively on Johnstone's use of extensive footage from the original tour and described the resulting story as captivating.

The film runs approximately 115 minutes. Johnstone is credited as director, writer and producer, with Michael Babiarz also serving as producer. [ref: Hicks on Sticks, Rotten Tomatoes]

The documentary features skateboarders Josh Evin, Eugene Voykin, Mike Evans and Shane Wallace. The Newport Beach Film Festival described the original tour as involving four skateboarders and two bands travelling through Western Canada with a portable skateboard park. Apple TV also lists the film as a 2012 documentary directed by Johnstone. [ref: Hicks on Sticks, Apple TV]

In 2013, Johnstone was interviewed by Martlet, the student newspaper of the University of Victoria, about making Hicks on Sticks and the Canadian skateboarding culture depicted in the documentary. [ref: Canadian skate culture explored in documentary, Martlet]

=== Lost in Havana ===
Johnstone later directed Lost in Havana, a documentary centred on skateboarding and travel in Cuba. The film continued his work documenting action sports and the communities surrounding them.

Johnstone served as director, cinematographer and editor on the production.

=== Getting Amongst ===
Johnstone subsequently worked on Getting Amongst, a documentary television series created by Jon Caften, combining travel, action sports and local culture. Johnstone worked as a director, camera director and editor on the series.

The program follows participants travelling internationally and interacting with local communities while taking part in skateboarding and other action sports. The series was broadcast and distributed by Tastemade and was also made available through digital distribution platforms. The show is the intellectual property of Wildkind Media, of which Johnstone is the president.

Episodes of Getting Amongst were produced in countries including Slovenia, South Africa, Paraguay, Cambodia, Portugal, South Korea, Sweden, Lebanon, the Netherlands and Panama.

=== Commercial production ===
In addition to his film and television work, Johnstone has worked as a director, cinematographer and editor in commercial video production. His professional work has included corporate, tourism, real-estate, non-profit and promotional productions.

Johnstone has been associated with Warren Lane Pictures, RCP Films and Wildkind Media. He has also operated Lunara Video Services in Vancouver.

== Filmmaking ==
Johnstone's early filmmaking developed from the skateboarding and snowboarding culture of British Columbia's interior. Action sports remained a recurring subject in his later documentary work.

Hicks on Sticks uses footage shot during the original 1999 tour together with interviews conducted years later. Film Threat noted that the quantity of surviving footage allowed the documentary to rely on moving images of the original events rather than primarily on photographs and retrospective interviews.

Johnstone has worked in multiple production roles, including directing, writing, cinematography, producing and editing.

data.text:
James Bond 007 60th Anniversary Limited Edition is a pinball machine designed by Keith Elwin and released by Stern Pinball in January 2023. The theme is based on the first 25 years of the James Bond film franchise. It is the fourth James Bond-themed pinball machine, following Gottlieb's James Bond 007 in 1980, Sega Pinball's Goldeneye in 1996, and another Stern Pinball James Bond 007 machine released in 2022.

Not be confused with James Bond 007 pinball machine designed by George Gomez and released by Stern Pinball in 2022, James Bond 007 60th anniversary Limited Edition is a completely different design and layout. [ref: Stern reveals four new James Bond Pinball Machines, Bond Lifestyle] Unlike modern pinball machines, the machine features a mechanical reel scoring display, typically only found in electro-mechanical games, as well as an LCD screen mounted in the playfield. The game is a single-level game with no ramps and only two flippers which differs from other Elwin designs. [ref: https://www.kineticist.com/news/stern-pinball-announces-james-bond-007-60th-anniversary-pinball] [ref: James Bond 007 (60th LE) Pinball Machine (Stern, 2023) | Pinside Game Archive, pinside.com] [ref: James Bond 60th Anniversary pinball machine | Stern Pinball | Preview] [ref: Stern Pinball reveals James Bond 007 - Pinball Magazine Stern Pinball reveals James Bond 007] [ref: Stern Pinball Announces New James Bond 007 Pinball Machines]

==Overview==
Production was limited to 500 units and features a custom-themed mirrored backglass, shaker motor, exclusive Union Jack shooter knob, 007-themed topper, numbered plaque, and a Certificate of Authenticity signed by Gary Stern, founder of Stern Pinball. The artwork is based on the first 25 James Bond films. [ref: Stern Pinball Celebrates 60 Years of James Bond with Limited-Edition Pinball Machine, License Global]

The game was advertised more as a collector's item than the 2022 George Gomez designed game, and encompassed all 25 Eon-produced James Bond films. Most machines were sold for use in private collections. [ref: Becoming Bond Player Perspective in the 007 Electronic Games, The International Journal of James Bond Studies]

==Game objectives==
There are six Villain modes connected to a kinetic spinning disc on the playfield shaped like Oddjob’s hat. [ref: JAMES BOND 60TH ANNIVERSARY, Pinball News] Once you complete all six villain modes, you activate Villain Multiball. In addition, you can collect gadgets and enable other multiballs by completing drop targets. [ref: 007 60th Anniversary Rulesheet, Pinball Rule Sheets]

data.title: BR Fares
data.text:
----

BR Fares is a British website that lists fares for journeys on the National Rail network in Great Britain. It was founded in 2012 by Paul Kelly and is operated by BR Fares Ltd. [ref: About BR Fares, BR Fares Ltd.]

== Content ==
For any pair of stations, the site lists the available fares with their price, route, time restrictions and validity. Railcard discounts can be applied. [ref: Are new Scottish operators less generous than before?, [[Rail (magazine)] [ref: Many staff appear to lack knowledge – across all lines, [[Rail (magazine)] Mark Smith, author of the rail travel website The Man in Seat Sixty-One, has described it as an online version of the rail industry's fares manuals, noting that it takes some getting used to. [ref: Train travel in Britain, The Man in Seat 61] Since June 2026 the site has also sold tickets for walk-up fares, as a sub-agent of the rail ticket retailer Raileasy. [ref: About ticket purchase, BR Fares Ltd.]

== Reception ==
Barry Doe, who wrote a fares column for Rail, recommended the site in several columns. In 2015 he highlighted the detail it gives on ticket restrictions and validity, information he argued operators should be required to show before sale. In 2021 he noted that some through fares missing from the National Rail journey planner were listed on BR Fares. At a time when some industry systems were applying railcard discounts with incorrect rounding, he recommended the site for checking the correct fare, describing it as accurate where many internal industry systems were not. [ref: Unreliability a barrier towards transport integration, [[Rail (magazine)] In 2022 he advised readers to check fares on the site before buying any walk-up ticket, contrasting it with journey planners, which show only the fares for the trains they list.

Smith recommends the site for "London International (CIV)" fares, which connect domestic journeys with Eurostar. [ref: Starting your journey from the UK regions, The Man in Seat 61] The Financial Times used BR Fares data in a 2025 analysis of season-ticket value and quoted Kelly on the loss of flexible fares. [ref: In charts: Death of the season ticket, Financial Times] In 2016 the campaign group Railfuture, testing how quickly websites and ticket machines added newly opened stations, found that BR Fares did not yet list two stations several days after they opened. [ref: Sent to Coventry, Railfuture]

data.title: Kawanthissa Tusker
data.text:
----

Kawanthissa (also spelled Kavanthissa or Kavantissa) was a Sri Lankan wild tusker that lived around the Galgamuwa area of Sri Lanka's North Western Province. Kawanthissa was known for his magnificent tusks and his friendly behaviors with the people. He was a calm elephant and attracted most of the Sri Lankans and tourists whi travel Sri Lanka.

== Background ==

Kawanthissa lived in the Galgamuwa area and the recidents in the area and the wildlife enthusiasts were concerned about his welfare and treatments following an injury in 2026 September. [ref: Outrage and calls for investigation following tragic death of iconic Kawanthissa, The Sunday Times]

== Injury and death ==

Kawanthissa was found with an injury to his right foreleg in the Galgamuwa area In September 2026 and the Wildlife officials and veterinarians treated the injury and monitored his condition. [ref: Ailing tusker Kavanthissa in critical condition, public urged to stay away, Daily Mirror]

The elephant's condition deteriorated overtime and reduced food intake and eventually a diarrhea condition occurred.

Kawanthissa tusker died in October 2026 while receiving veterinary care and his death raised public concerns and many parties requested investigation about the treatments he received.

== Investigation ==

The Environment Ministry of Sri Lanka announced an independent investigation about the treatment procedures to find out if any mistakes or deliberate misconduct had been occurred. [ref: Independent probe into tusker Kawanthissa's death, Daily Mirror]

President Anura Kumara Dissanayake appointed an expert committee on 19 October 2026 to investigate the elephant's death. The duties of the committee was to examine the possible causes of the death and findout the mistakes and negligence had occurred during treatment. [ref: President appoints committee to probe Kavanthissa's death, Daily Mirror]

data.title: Nate Jacobs
data.text:
Nathaniel "Nate" Jacobs is a fictional character in the American teen drama television series Euphoria, created by Sam Levinson. He is portrayed by Jacob Elordi, with Gabriel Golub portraying a younger version of the character. Nate is introduced as a high school football player and the eldest son of Cal and Marsha Jacobs. He is characterized by his volatile temperament, controlling behavior, and preoccupation with masculinity and social status. His relationship with his father, whose secret sexual life he discovers as a child, becomes a central part of his character. [ref: Sam Levinson on Euphoria, Television Academy]

Nate's major storylines include his relationships with Maddy Perez, Jules Vaughn, and Cassie Howard, as well as his increasingly antagonistic relationship with Cal. He manipulates Jules under the alias "Tyler" after discovering her sexual encounter with his father, and later begins a relationship with Cassie while she is Maddy's close friend. Five years after graduating from high school, Nate is married to Cassie and becomes involved in his father's real-estate business. His financial difficulties lead to his involvement with loan sharks, who eventually kill him. [ref: 'Euphoria' Season 3 Episode 7 Recap: Nate Jacobs Dies, [[Variety (magazine)]

==Background==

Nate is the eldest son of Cal and Marsha Jacobs and grows up in East Highland, California. His father places considerable emphasis on physical strength, athletic achievement, and conventional masculinity during his childhood. Nate has a younger brother, Aaron, and an older brother, Derek, who dies before the events of the series.

At the age of 11, Nate discovers a collection of videos documenting Cal's sexual encounters with men and transgender women. The discovery profoundly affects his perception of his father and contributes to his later preoccupation with masculinity and sexuality. Sam Levinson has described Nate, alongside several other characters, as coming from a troubled home and attempting to fill emotional voids through sex, drugs, and adrenaline.

As a teenager, Nate becomes a star football player at East Highland High School. He develops a reputation for aggression and intimidation and begins an unstable relationship with Maddy Perez. Their relationship is repeatedly disrupted by jealousy, possessiveness, and violence.

Nate later discovers that Maddy possesses intimate photographs of Jules Vaughn and learns that Jules previously had a sexual encounter with Cal. Using the online identity "Tyler", Nate begins communicating with Jules and develops an emotional attachment to her while concealing his identity. After learning that Jules has evidence of his father's encounter with her, Nate threatens to expose her private photographs unless she remains silent.

During his senior year, Nate begins a secret relationship with Cassie Howard, despite her friendship with Maddy. Their relationship becomes public after Maddy discovers the affair and contributes to the breakdown of Cassie's friendship with her.

Following high school, Nate takes over his father's real-estate business and marries Cassie. Five years after the events of the second season, he experiences financial difficulties and becomes indebted to loan sharks. After being abducted and buried alive, Nate is rescued but subsequently killed by the men pursuing him. His death occurs in the seventh episode of the third season, "Rain or Shine".

==Personality==

Nate is portrayed as confident, physically imposing, and highly competitive, particularly in relation to football and his social position at school. He maintains a controlled outward appearance while frequently responding to perceived threats or challenges with anger and intimidation. His behavior toward his romantic partners is characterized by possessiveness, jealousy, manipulation, and violence.

A significant aspect of Nate's characterization is his relationship with masculinity. His father's emphasis on physical strength and traditional masculine behavior contributes to Nate's efforts to construct a similarly dominant public persona. His discovery of Cal's sexual encounters creates a conflict between his understanding of masculinity and the reality of his father's private life. Levinson has described Nate as one of several Euphoria characters who attempt to compensate for emotional difficulties through sex, drugs, or adrenaline.

Elordi has described Nate as a deeply conflicted character whose anger provides an outlet for problems he does not know how to confront directly. He has also characterized the role as substantially more complex than the version of Nate presented in the initial audition material, which he described as a stereotypical aggressive jock. [ref: Jacob Elordi Called Nate in "Euphoria" an "Emotional Terrorist", Teen Vogue]

Nate's relationships with Maddy, Jules, and Cassie each expose different aspects of his personality. His relationship with Maddy is marked by possessiveness and physical violence, while his relationship with Jules develops through an anonymous online identity that allows him to express feelings he is unwilling to acknowledge publicly. His relationship with Cassie similarly reflects his desire for control and his difficulty separating intimacy from possession.

==Development==

===Creation and conception===

Nate Jacobs was created by Sam Levinson for Euphoria, HBO's adaptation of the Israeli television series of the same name. Levinson substantially altered the characters and storylines of the original series when developing the American adaptation. He described his approach as drawing on personal experiences and creating characters around their inner lives rather than beginning with broader thematic concepts.

Levinson conceived Nate as a character whose outward persona contrasts with his internal conflicts. His relationship with Cal provides much of the character's initial psychological conflict, while his relationships with Maddy, Jules, and Cassie allow different aspects of his controlling and insecure behavior to be explored.

===Casting and portrayal===

Jacob Elordi was cast as Nate after auditioning for the series. According to Elordi, the initial audition material presented Nate primarily as an aggressive, stereotypical jock, and he was unaware of the character's eventual complexity. As the series developed, Nate's background and relationships became increasingly prominent. [ref: Jacob Elordi on 'Euphoria,' First Kisses, and Orlando Bloom, [[W (magazine)]

Elordi has said that he approached Nate as substantially different from himself and regarded the character as difficult but rewarding to portray. He has also discussed the contrast between Nate's outward behavior and the character's underlying conflicts. [ref: Jacob Elordi on playing Nate Jacobs, Showmax]

The character's development continued throughout the series. In the first two seasons, Nate is primarily depicted as a high school athlete whose relationships and family circumstances drive his increasingly destructive behavior. The third season presents him five years later as an adult, married to Cassie and managing his father's business. His storyline shifts from conflicts within his family and relationships to financial difficulties and criminal entanglements, culminating in his death. [ref: 'Euphoria' Season 3: TV Review, [[Variety (magazine)]
