data.title: Hans Coetzee
data.text:
----Johann "Hans" Coetzee is a veterinarian, veterinary pharmacologist, and university administrator. He is a university distinguished professor and vice president for research at Kansas State University. His research focuses on assessing and managing pain in food-producing animals. [ref: Vice president for research profile, Kansas State University] In 2025, he received the National Academy of Sciences Prize in Food and Agriculture Science for his work on livestock pain management. [ref: Dr. Hans Coetzee Awarded the 2025 NAS Prize in Food & Agriculture Sciences, Foundation for Food & Agriculture Research]

== Education and early career ==
Coetzee earned a Bachelor of Veterinary Science from the University of Pretoria in 1996. After graduating, he worked in mixed-animal veterinary practice in Northern Ireland for four years, followed by two years in pharmaceutical research and development at Norbrook Laboratories. He received a Certificate in Cattle Health and Production from the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons in 2000 and a doctorate in veterinary microbiology from Iowa State University in 2005.

== Academic career ==
Coetzee held assistant and associate professor positions in clinical sciences at Kansas State University before serving on the veterinary faculty at Iowa State University. He returned to Kansas State in 2016 as head of the Department of Anatomy and Physiology in the College of Veterinary Medicine. He was named a university distinguished professor in 2022 and also served as associate dean for research and graduate programs. [ref: Coetzee honored for pain management research in livestock, American Veterinary Medical Association] [ref: Hans Coetzee appointed vice president for research, Kansas State University]

He became interim vice president for research in 2024. Following a national search, Kansas State announced his appointment as vice president for research in May 2025. As the university's chief research officer, his responsibilities include research development, sponsored programs, research infrastructure, commercialization, and research integrity and compliance.

== Research ==
Coetzee's research examines methods for measuring pain and evaluating pain-relief treatments in livestock, including beef and dairy cattle, sheep, and pigs. His work combines behavioral observations with physiological and neuroendocrine measures to assess responses to painful conditions and routine animal-management procedures.

He has developed and validated experimental models for evaluating analgesic drugs in food-producing animals. In its coverage of his 2025 National Academy of Sciences award, the American Veterinary Medical Association reported that this research contributed to the first regulatory approval of an analgesic drug for livestock.

== Professional service and recognition ==
Coetzee is a diplomate of the American College of Veterinary Clinical Pharmacology, the American College of Animal Welfare, and the European College of Animal Welfare and Behavioural Medicine. He is a fellow of the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons and has chaired the American Veterinary Medical Association's Animal Welfare Committee.

His awards include:

* American Association of Bovine Practitioners (AABP) Award of Excellence (2014)
* American Veterinary Medical Association Animal Welfare Award (2017). [ref: AVMA recognizes excellence in veterinary medicine, American Veterinary Medical Association]
* World Veterinary Association Global Animal Welfare Award (2017).
* World Buiatrics Congress Ruminant Well-being Achievement Award (2018). [ref: Boehringer Ingelheim recognizes Hans Coetzee for ruminant welfare, www.k-state.edu]
* The Irvin Youngberg Higuchi-KU Endowment Research Achievement Award (2025). [ref: KU, Kansas State faculty receive Higuchi-KU Endowment research achievement awards, university-research-awards.ku.edu]
* National Academy of Sciences Prize in Food and Agriculture Science (2025).

data.title: Lime Trading Corp.
data.text:
----

Lime Trading Corp. (operating as part of Lime Financial) is an American electronic brokerage firm and technology provider headquartered in New York City. The company provides direct market access (DMA), low-latency trade execution, and trading APIs to quantitative funds, proprietary trading firms, and independent algorithmic traders. [ref: About Us, Lime Trading] [ref: Lime Trading Corp. Profile, Bloomberg]
[ref: Lime Trading Corp. Announces Membership in SIFMA, Knox News] [ref: Terms and Conditions, Lime Trading] [ref: Lime Trading Crosses 18 Billion Shares in First Half of 2026 as Triple Witching Tests Execution Infrastructure, Barchart] [ref: Lime Trading Corp. Pairs Low-Latency Execution Technology with Sterling Trader® Pro to Advance Equities Trading, AP News]

== History ==
Lime originally traces back to Lime Brokerage LLC, that was founded in 2000 as an internal trading technology unit within a quantitative American hedge fund.

In 2011, brokerage firm Wedbush Securities acquired Lime Brokerage, integrating Lime's low-latency execution tools and routing technology into its suite of institutional services. [ref: Wedbush Acquires Lime Brokerage, Business Wire] In 2018, Lime Brokerage merged its retail operations with Lightspeed Trading, and formed Lightspeed Financial. [ref: Lime Brokerage Merges with Lightspeed Trading, Finextra]

In 2020, the financial technology firm Score Priority Corp. acquired the Lime technology stack and trade execution infrastructure from Wedbush, re-establishing the technology team under the trade name Lime Execution.

In 2022, Score Priority rebranded its collective brokerage operations under the banner Lime Financial, adopting Lime Trading Corp. for its broker-dealer arm. The same year Lime Financial was awarded the Best Quantitative Trading Broker at the Markets Choice Awards. [ref: Best Quantitative Trading Broker: Lime Financial, Markets Media] In 2023, the firm moved to doing business under its official name, Lime Trading Corp. [ref: Score Priority Rebrands to Lime Financial, Traders Magazine]

In 2024, Eva Sehic was promoted to CEO of the company. [ref: Eva Sehic Promoted to CEO of Lime Trading, Business Hub Middle East]

== Awards ==
* 2010 - Lime Brokerage was awarded the Most Cutting-Edge IT initiative by the American Financial Technology Awards. [ref: Lime - About Us, Lime Trading Corp.]
* 2016 - Lime Brokerage was awarded the Best Infrastructure/Technology Initiative by the Wall Street Letter Institutional Trading Awards. [ref: Lime Brokerage Recipient of "Best Infrastructure/Technology Initiative" By 2016 Wall Street Letter Institutional Trading Awards, EIN Press Wire]
* 2022 - Lime Trading was awarded the Best Quantitative Trading Broker at the 10th Annual Markets Choice Awards, hosted by Markets Media. [ref: 2022 Markets Choice Award Winners Announced, Traders Magazine]
* 2024 - CEO Eva Sehic received the Excellence in Innovation award at the 2024 US Women in Finance Awards. [ref: 2024 U.S. Women in Finance Award Winners Announced, Markets Media]

data.title: Sylvia Netzer
data.text:
Sylvia Netzer (born 1944) [ref: Artists' biographies, Confrontational Ceramics] [ref: Sylvia Netzer, Christopher Knowles, The New York Times] is an American sculptor, [ref: American Ceramics] art critic, and professor emeritus at the City College of New York. [ref: Christopher Knowles & Sylvia Netzer RELATiVE(s) at The Opening Gallery, [[Artsy (website)]

==Early life and education==
Netzer was born to Jenny Netzer and Hans A. Netzer in Manhattan, New York. She graduated from the City College of New York and later received her Masters in Fine Art in sculpture at Columbia University School of Fine Arts. [ref: S...as in Sylvia, A.I.R. Gallery] At City College, she was among the supporters of the 1965 March on Washington for Peace in Vietnam. [ref: Obervation Post, 1965-04-14, Observation Post]

==Career==
Netzer's abstract work Post-Toxic/Neo-Plastic, a room-sized installation of black and yellow figures, was described by Drew Shiflett as "remind[ing] one of a world in which genetic engineering has gone berserk or toxic wastes have influenced the gene pool"; [ref: In Three Dimensions: Women Sculptors of the '90s] it was followed up by her 1996 work Miasma Morph. [ref: Miasma Morph, A.I.R. Gallery] She later produced Glen Gary OLY in 2004, a sculpture of kiln-fired bricks carved to resemble herself in the lounging posture of Olympia, the 1863 oil painting. [ref: Pot People Recent Figurative Ceramic Sculpture, Sculpture Review] Two years later, she worked on site at a brick plant in York to create Glen Gary OLY II. [ref: Unusual guest at brick plant, The York Dispatch]

Netzer's work is represented by a collection at A.I.R. Gallery in Brooklyn, New York. She has curated several exhibits at the gallery and elsewhere. [ref: Education program, A.I.R. Gallery] She directed the ceramics program at City College from 1990 [ref: Sylvia Netzer, Reticulated Forms, A.I.R. Gallery] [ref: The Paper, 1993-03-18, The Paper] until her retirement in 2026.

==Personal life==
Netzer is married to theater director Robert M. Wilson. The two met in 1983 at Greenwich House Pottery, at which time Netzer was an instructor and Wilson a student, though he was not in her class. They married in August 2015.

data.title: The Capture of El Maragato
data.text:
----

The Capture of El Maragato is a real, historical incident that took place in Spain in 1806 A.D involving a notorious highwayman and dangerous prison escapee whose real name was Pedro Pinero, known by his moniker El Maragato. Pedro was born in the town of Andiuela de Somoza in Leon, Spain and worked in the charcoal industry before joining a gang of criminals as bandits. [ref: 250 años del nacimiento de 'El Maragato', el bandolero que inmortalizó Goya, La Nueva Crónica]

In 1804, he and several of his accomplices were captured and after lengthy trials El Maragato was sentenced to 200 lashes, 10 years of hard labor at the Cartagena naval shipyard and execution by hanging, but he received a royal commutation from King Carlos IV that spared him from the gallows while upholding the remaining sentences. In 1806 he escaped from prison.

After his escape, he spent about two months in hiding, committing robberies, stealing food and weapons. Later on, Pedro broke into the quarters of the Franciscan friar, Friar Pedro, to rob him and hold him at gun point. But the confrontation took unexpectedly dramatic turn. The friar maintained his composure and in a sudden move, lunged at the bandit and forcefully took the rifle from him after a violent physical struggle. As the bandit attempted to flee, the friar shot him in the leg to impede his escape then bound him securely with the help of local residents and handed him over to the authorities. The friar later attempted to help El Maragato obtain a pardon, but his pleas went unanswered. The bandit was swiftly tried and executed by hanging in Madrid. Meanwhile, Friar Pedro received royal praise, commendation and an annual stipend for his brave actions. [ref: ] [ref: ]

This incident captivated the Spanish public, inspiring the artist Francisco Goya to immortalize it in a famous series of 6 oil paintings that narrate the details of the event. To this day the series remains on display as a historical and artistic testament at the Art Institute of Chicago [ref: ] and a 10-minutes short film about him, directed by Luis Miguel Alonso was released in 1997 under the title El Bandido Maragato. [ref: ‘EL MARAGATO’: 250 AÑOS DEL NACIMIENTO DEL BANDOLERO CUYA CAPTURA INMORTALIZÓ GOYA – Real Asociación Española de Cronistas Oficiales]

data.title: Jamelyn Ebelacker
data.text:
Jamelyn Ebelacker is an award-winning artist, entrepreneur, social activist and member of the Santa Clara Pueblo tribe. She has worked to elevate awareness of indigenous experiences in the United States. In 2022, she assisted in the creation of the "People of the First Light” parade float in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, the first ever permanent Native American float in the history of that parade. She currently serves as the marketing manager of the Santa Clara Development Corporation. [ref: ] [ref: Who, indigenousdirection]

== Education and Early Contributions ==
Ebelacker completed her Bachelor of Fine Arts undergraduate degree at the Institute of American Indian Arts in Santa Fe, New Mexico. After graduation, in 2017, she followed in her family's tradition of public service by serving in the Peace Corps in St Lucia and Dominica as an educator [ref: ]. Her work in the Peace Corps was terminated by the Covid pandemic in 2020 but not before she was nominated for the Franklin H. Williams award, which honors Returned Peace Corps Volunteers who exemplify an ongoing commitment to community service. Upon returning to the US, she began working for Indigenous Direction as an Associate Producer, Project Manager and Digital Artist where she helped create the first permanent indigenous float in the Macy's Thanksgiving Parade. In 2023 she enrolled in the MBA program at Arizona State University where her work led to her selection as recipient of Arizona State University’s (ASU) 2024 Martin Luther King Jr. Student Servant-Leadership Award. In addition to her MBA with concentrations in Consulting and Marketing, she earned ASU's certificate in sustainability. Ebelacker continues to support the Pueblo people through the Santa Clara Development Corporation as well as continues her heritage pottery craftsmanship through her family company Eberlacker Family Pottery. [ref: Native American Women Make Their Marks in Business While Honoring Their Heritage, Forté Foundation] [ref: Ebelacker Family Pottery, Ebelacker Family Pottery]

NITron (formerly Nitron Music; born Maxim Aleksandrovich Kandykov on 5 September 2009 in Chara, Zabaykalsky Krai, Russia) is a Russian rapper, composer, songwriter and TikTok personality. [ref: Максим Кандыков (NITron) – Биография, muzsmi.ru] [ref: Юный музыкант из Новой Чары создаёт музыку с нейросетями, Северная правда] He attracted media attention for creating a song about the city of Perm with the help of artificial intelligence.

==Biography==
Kandykov was born on 5 September 2009 in the village of Chara, Zabaykalsky Krai, Russia. [ref: Кто такой музыкант NITron из поселка Новая Чара?, ianr.ru] In 2015, he began attending Novaya Chara Secondary School No. 2, named after Hero of Russia Igor Moldovanov. In 2026, he enrolled at Kungur College of Agrotechnology and Management in Kungur, studying landscape and garden construction.

Kandykov considers 2018 the beginning of his career, when he registered on the social media platform Likee and reportedly gained more than 6,000 followers in his first month. He posted different types of content before turning to music. In 2020, he wrote his first song, which circulated on social media.

==Music career==
In 2020, Kandykov became interested in music production using FL Studio 20. He began experimenting with his first compositions and released the song "Kalarsky Krai" («Каларский край»), which attracted attention among residents of Novaya Chara and Chara. Local media subsequently covered his work, and he was invited to perform. [ref: Песню о Перми с помощью искусственного интеллекта написал восьмиклассник, rus-ship.ru]

In 2022, he recorded the song "New School", which became popular among schoolchildren aged 11–13, according to the biographical accounts.

In 2024, Kandykov released "Perm — City on the Kama" («Пермь — город на Каме»), a song about Perm created with the help of artificial intelligence. The release was covered by Komsomolskaya Pravda, Sobaka.ru and other Russian-language outlets. [ref: Восьмиклассник с помощью искусственного интеллекта написал песню о Перми, Комсомольская правда] [ref: Нейросеть сочинила и исполнила песню о Перми, Sobaka.ru] [ref: Школьник из Забайкалья написал песню о Перми с помощью искусственного интеллекта, Tsargrad] [ref: Школьник из Забайкалья написал песню о Перми с помощью искусственного интеллекта, MySeldon]

On 30 December 2024, Kandykov released two tracks dedicated to the memory of people killed during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, referred to in Russian official discourse as the "special military operation". [ref: Военкоры вечОРКИ, Военкоры вечОРКИ] [ref: 15-летний музыкант из Новой Чары написал песню в честь погибших бойцов СВО, Arguments and Facts] [ref: Девятиклассник из Новой Чары написал песню в честь погибших бойцов СВО, Общественная Служба Новостей]

On 28 January 2025, he released a song dedicated to the Siege of Leningrad.

In February 2025, Kandykov published a video appeal on VK opposing the closure of his former school building, which had been declared unsafe. The issue was covered by Chita.ru and Lenta75. [ref: Дети из забайкальского села смонтировали клип против закрытия школы, признанной аварийной, Chita.ru] [ref: Ученики из Чары сняли клип против закрытия аварийной школы, Lenta75] The school was closed on 13 February 2025 following a court decision that the building was unsafe. Local residents held a meeting with Kalar District head Vladimir Ustyuzhanin on 14 February.

On 20 March 2025, Kandykov released the song "Hero of Russia" («Герой России») with acquaintances, dedicated to the memory of Hero of Russia Igor Moldovanov. [ref: 15-летний музыкант из Новой Чары написал песню про Героя РФ, Arguments and Facts]

In April 2025, he created a TikTok account under the name @[user]. According to the supplied biographical account, the account's audience grew the following year, and a video about Zabaykalsky Krai received more than 150,000 views. The account was reported to have received more than 13.3 million views across its posts over the preceding year as of October 2026.

In 2025, Kandykov released four singles: «Fall from the Sky, Pt. 3», «Two Different World», «Six forty seven (Remix)», «HUAWEI». These singles gained popularity and became the most streamed on the music platform Spotify [ref: Listen to NITron Songs, open.spotify.com].

«Two Different World» accumulated more than 25,000 streams [ref: Two Different World - song and lyrics by NITron, open.spotify.com], «Fall from the Sky, Pt. 3» garnered more than 20,000 streams [ref: Fall from the Sky, Pt. 3 - song and lyrics by NITron, open.spotify.com], while the other singles each had approximately 1,000 streams.

In August 2025, Kandykov created a neural-network model that he said could generate musical compositions using the voices of well-known singers. He used it to produce a song about Zabaykalsky Krai featuring AI-generated vocals resembling Ilya Zolotukhin, vocalist of the band Bond with a Button («Бонд с кнопкой»), with lyrics written by Kandykov and music based on the band's song "Kukhni" («Кухни»). The project was covered by the regional Ministry of Culture and several Russian news outlets. [ref: Школьник из Каларского округа сделал свою модель нейросети и написал песню о Забайкальском крае, Ministry of Culture of Zabaykalsky Krai] [ref: Подросток создал песню о Забайкалье при помощи своей нейросети, Забайкальский рабочий] [ref: Школьник из Забайкалья создал нейросеть и написал песню о крае, Arguments and Facts] [ref: Каларский школьник сделал нейросеть, чтобы написать песню про Забайкалье, zabnews.ru] [ref: Школьник из Забайкалья создал нейросеть для генерации вокала и написал песню о крае, ChitaMedia] [ref: Школьник создал песню о Забайкалье при помощи своей модели нейросети, Lenta75] The music video had received approximately 20,000 views on VK by October 2026, according to the source text.

On 3 February 2026, Kandykov created an AI-generated virtual journey in which digital depictions of Albert Einstein and Nikola Tesla visited locations in Zabaykalsky Krai, including Tsugol Datsan, Mount Alkhanai and the Chara Sands. He generated images of the scientists at these locations and edited them into a short video tour about the region's history and natural environment. He said the video took approximately four hours to make. [ref: Школьник с помощью ИИ показал Эйнштейна и Теслу в Забайкалье, Doska.plus] [ref: Альберт Эйнштейн и Никола Тесла прогулялись по Забайкалью, zab-news.ru] [ref: Школьник через ИИ отправила Эйнштейна и Теслу в путешествие по святыням Забайкалья, ChitaMedia] [ref: Школьник из Забайкалья создал виртуальное путешествие Эйнштейна и Теслы по краю, Rossiyskaya Gazeta]

In February 2026, ahead of Defender of the Fatherland Day, Kandykov presented music videos dedicated to residents of Kalar District who had been killed during the Russian invasion of Ukraine. The videos were made using artificial-intelligence technologies. Zabaykalsky Krai Governor Alexander Osipov mentioned Kandykov's work in an official social-media post on 19 March 2026. [ref: 16-летний музыкант и автор песен из Новой Чары Максим Кандыков создал видеоклипы, посвященные героям-землякам, MAX] The regional broadcaster GTRK Chita also reported on the videos. [ref: Школьник из Забайкалья создал видеоклипы, посвящённые героям-землякам, Vesti Chita]

On 20 March 2026, Kandykov created a browser-based clicker game titled "Photo Hunt in the Daursky Nature Reserve" («Фотоохота в Даурском заповеднике»). The game focuses on the wildlife of Zabaykalsky Krai and aims to draw attention to biodiversity conservation, according to a report by Chita.ru. [ref: Охота на журавля и манула. Школьник в Забайкалье создал игру о спасении животных, Chita.ru]

On 16 April 2026, Kandykov reworked the song "Silk" («Шёлк») by Vanya Dmitrienko with a Zabaykalsky regional theme, using neural networks. [ref: Школьник из Новой Чары переделал песню Вани Дмитриенко на забайкальский мотив с помощью нейросети, Ministry of Culture of Zabaykalsky Krai]

In summer 2026, Kandykov created the short film Za Baikalom. Two («За Байкалом. Двое») with the help of artificial intelligence. The film tells the story of a musician father who leaves his family. [ref: Подросток из Чары с помощью искусственного интеллекта создал фильм о музыканте, Ministry of Culture of Zabaykalsky Krai]

data.title: The principle of operation of the nervous system.
data.text:
To illustrate this, let us consider a primitive animal with a very simple nervous system. When the organism is exposed to stimuli capable of causing harm, signals indicating danger arise in its receptors (sensors); these signals travel through the nervous system — most likely to the motor organs — compelling the organism to move until it has escaped the source of the irritation. Once the stimulus vanishes, the signals cease, and the nervous system (and consequently the body) returns to a state of rest.

It follows that rest — the absence or reduction of signals within the nervous system — is the goal of a living creature's actions (this is precisely what happiness is). Conversely, signals within the nervous system are perceived by the living creature as various forms of pain, from which it seeks relief. If one believes that "pleasant" signals exist within the nervous system, that is simply not the case. The only signals that might seem pleasant are those that block the transmission of other signals (much like a painkiller), but there is little point in discussing such signals.

The nervous system functions as an alarm system for the organism, signaling danger and prompting action. That is precisely why it evolved: to sense pain and attempt to escape it. Thus, life is spent entirely in this manner: sensing various forms of pain and trying to rid oneself of them. Even boredom is a form of discomfort — and, likewise, a signal within the nervous system.

In short, pain is the sole stimulus for activity in all organisms possessing a nervous system. [ref: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution_of_nervous_systems]

data.title: Baran–Shivpuri railway line
data.text:
The Baran–Shivpuri new railway line (Hindi: बारां–शिवपुरी नई रेल लाइन) is a proposed railway line connecting Baran in Rajasthan with Shivpuri in Madhya Pradesh, India.

== History ==

The Baran Shivpuri new railway line was included in the railway survey programme of Indian Railways. According to a Railway Board document dated 26 August 2014, the survey was completed in 2013–14. The proposed line was listed with a length of 151 km and an estimated cost of ₹778 crore. At the time, the survey report was under examination. [ref: Details of Surveys Completed During the Last 10 Years as on 26 August 2014, Indian Railways]

The West Central Railway's annual report for 2014–15 also recorded that the revised survey report for the Baran Shivpuri line had been submitted to the Railway Board. [ref: Annual Report 2014–15, West Central Railway]

== Project status ==

The cited railway records document the completion of the survey and submission of the revised report to the Railway Board. They do not establish that construction of the line was sanctioned. The estimated cost of ₹778 crore was reported in 2014 and should not be taken as the current project cost.
