data.title: Skyfire Agentic Identity and Payments
data.text:
Skyfire is an American financial technology and artificial intelligence infrastructure company that develops identity verification, authentication, and payment systems intended to enable autonomous AI agents to conduct transactions with digital services and merchants. [ref: Skyfire lets AI agents spend your money — with guardrails, TechCrunch] [ref: Experian's Chief Innovation Officer Gleams AI Gains With Startup Collaboration, InformationWeek]

The company was founded by Amir Sarhangi, who previously founded Jibe Mobile, a messaging startup acquired by Google in 2015 that became part of Google's implementation of the Rich Communication Services (RCS) messaging standard, and Craig DeWitt, a former Ripple executive. [ref: Google Buys Startup Jibe Mobile, The Wall Street Journal] [ref: Google says RCS messaging is now available worldwide, TechCrunch]

The company is associated with infrastructure for agentic commerce, including systems for AI agent identity verification and automated payment execution. [ref: These New AI Bots Will Do Just About Anything for You, The Wall Street Journal]

== History ==
Skyfire was founded in 2023 by Amir Sarhangi and Craig DeWitt.

Before founding Skyfire, Sarhangi founded Jibe Mobile, a mobile messaging company acquired by Google in 2015. Jibe's technology became part of Google's implementation of the Rich Communication Services (RCS) messaging standard.

DeWitt previously worked at Ripple in digital payments infrastructure.

In August 2024, Skyfire publicly launched infrastructure intended to support autonomous AI agents conducting commercial transactions, including programmable digital wallets and transaction controls. [ref: Skyfire launches to let autonomous AI agents spend money on your behalf, VentureBeat]

The company announced an $8.5 million funding round in 2024 with participation from Neuberger Berman, Coinbase Ventures, Brevan Howard Digital, Arrington Capital, and other investors. [ref: AI payment processing startup Skyfire launches with $8.5M in funding, SiliconANGLE]

== Products and technology ==
Skyfire develops infrastructure intended to support autonomous commercial activity by AI agents.

Its platform includes systems for:
* identity verification and authentication of AI agents
* programmable digital wallets
* policy-based transaction controls
* automated payment execution using methods including card payments, ACH transfers, wire transfers, and stablecoins.

In 2025, Skyfire introduced KYAPay (Know Your Agent Pay), an open protocol intended to support standardized identity verification and payment authorization for AI agents engaging with third-party services. [ref: Skyfire launches AI agent checkout to enable fully autonomous transactions, PYMNTS]

Skyfire's identity and payment infrastructure has been referenced in reporting on emerging agentic commerce trust frameworks involving organizations including Experian, Visa, and Cloudflare. [ref: The Trust Gap Holding Agentic Commerce Back, PYMNTS]

In reporting on Experian's Agent Trust initiative, PYMNTS described Skyfire as providing a standardized mechanism for exchanging AI agent identity information across platforms together with payment credentials that can operate within existing checkout systems.

In September 2026, Mastercard announced that it was working with Skyfire to incorporate Know Your Agent (KYA) identity verification into its Agent Pay infrastructure. The collaboration was intended to help financial institutions and merchants identify and verify AI agents participating in transactions. [ref: Mastercard expands Agent Pay with trust and intelligence services, The Paypers]

Reporting by Forkast discussed Skyfire's KYA technology as an identity-verification component of Mastercard's broader agentic-commerce trust framework, alongside Mastercard's transaction-level risk assessment capabilities. [ref: Mastercard's Probability Score Shifts the Agent Commerce Question From Identity to Trust, Forkast]

== Industry coverage ==
Skyfire has been cited in reporting on the development of commercial infrastructure for autonomous AI agents.

In The Wall Street Journal, Belle Lin described Skyfire as a startup developing blockchain-based payment systems for bots to make purchases under transaction controls defined by users.

InformationWeek described Skyfire as a technology partner in Experian's agent trust ecosystem, including support for identity and payment infrastructure for AI-driven commerce.

* Financial technology
* Artificial intelligence

data.title: Terry Owens
data.text:
Terry Owens (born 1947) is an English football administrator and entertainer associated with Aldershot, Hampshire. He helped establish Aldershot Town F.C. in 1992 following the collapse of the original Aldershot F.C., and became the new club's founding chairman. [ref: Football / Non-League Notebook: Aldershot are ready to reward the faithful, The Independent] He has also been involved with the club as an ambassador and has entertained residents in care homes.

== Early life ==

Owens was born in Aldershot, Hampshire, in 1947. He grew up supporting Aldershot F.C.

== Football career ==

In 1989, Owens became chairman of the Save Our Shots campaign, which sought to save Aldershot F.C.

Aldershot F.C. entered liquidation in March 1992 following financial difficulties. Owens helped establish Aldershot Town F.C. and became its founding chairman. The newly formed club entered the Isthmian League for the 1992–93 season. [ref: Football / Non-League Notebook: Aldershot are ready to reward the faithful, The Independent]

The revival of football in Aldershot was also covered by Rory Smith in The Independent in October 2011. [ref: Big night for the Aldershot diehards who resurrected a club, The Independent]

== Club ambassador ==

Owens has been associated with Aldershot Town F.C. as an ambassador. He has also been listed in connection with the Shots Foundation, the club's charitable foundation. [ref: Our Team & Trustees, The Shots Foundation] [ref: Club Support Staff, Aldershot Town F.C.]

Owens has visited supporters in hospital and attended supporters' funerals.

== Entertainer ==

Owens has entertained older people in care homes by singing popular songs from the 1950s, 1960s and 1970s.

In January 2023, RMBI Care Co. published an article about his visits to Shannon Court care home in Hindhead, Surrey. The article described how his performances encouraged residents to sing along and reminisce about their younger years. It also reported that he brought yellow roses for some residents. [ref: Shannon Court residents reminisce through the power of music, RMBI Care Co.]

Before entertaining residents at Shannon Court, Owens served on the committee of the Association of Friends of Shannon Court for ten years and was its chairman, according to the same article. [ref: Shannon Court residents reminisce through the power of music, RMBI Care Co.]

== References ==

= Terry Owens =
Terry Owens (born 1947) is an English football administrator and entertainer from Aldershot, Hampshire. He is best known for helping to establish Aldershot Town Football Club in 1992 following the collapse of the original club, Aldershot FC, becoming its founding chairman. Later, he became an ambassador for the club and is also known for singing in care homes.

== Early life ==
Terry was born in Aldershot, Hampshire, in 1947 and grew up to become a fan of Aldershot FC.

== Football career ==
Terry became involved in the administration of Aldershot FC. In 1989, he became chairman of the Save Our Shots campaign, helping to save the club.

In March 1992, Aldershot FC entered liquidation due to financial problems. Terry helped establish a new club, Aldershot Town FC, and became its founding chairman. The new club played in the Isthmian League in the 1992–93 season. [ref: ]

Terry's actions in helping to establish a new club were featured in The Independent in August 1992. In addition, his work to save Aldershot football and establish a new club was featured in the newspaper in October 2011.

== Club ambassador ==
Terry became an ambassador for Aldershot Town FC. This has kept him connected to the club and its fans. He has visited fans in hospitals and attended their funerals.

He has also been a trustee of the Shots Foundation.

== Entertainer ==
Terry works as an entertainer and singer, often entertaining older people in care homes. He sings many popular songs from the 1950s, 1960s and 1970s.

In January 2023, an article was published by RMBI Care Co. about Terry's visits to Shannon Court care home in Hindhead, Surrey. It stated that Terry had been visiting the care home for several months. He entertained residents with songs that encouraged them to sing along and reminisce about their youth. He also brought yellow roses for some residents.

Before Terry began entertaining at the care home, he served on the committee of the Association of Friends of Shannon Court for ten years. He was also chairman of the association. The association supports the care home and organises fundraising events for residents.

Terry stated that he regularly sings in care homes and that residents enjoy listening to him and singing along.

data.title: Yohannes Teklehaimanot Tesfaye
data.text:
Yohannes Teklehaimanot Tesfaye (; 1941 – February 1976) was an Ethiopian Tigrayan nationalist and teacher. With Gebre Kidan Asfaha, he led the Political Association of Tigrayans, a clandestine group that advocated the independence of Tigray and later emerged as an armed organisation, the Tigray Liberation Front (TLF; ). [ref: The Origins of the Tigray People's Liberation Front, African Affairs] In December 1975 the TLF's leadership was detained by forces of the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) following a merger ceremony, and Yohannes is reported to have been executed in February 1976.

== Early life and education ==
Yohannes was born in 1941 in the village of Assai, near the town of Gendebta in Feresmay woreda, Adwa awraja, to Teklehaimanot Tesfaye, an Orthodox Christian priest and farmer, and Weleteyesus Abreha. He was the seventh of thirteen siblings.

He did not attend school until the age of twelve. In 1953 his elder brother, Woldegebriel Teklehaimanot, who worked for Ras Imru and later became a businessman in Addis Ababa, took him to Addis Ababa to be educated, and he began primary school at the Prince Asfaw Wossen School. When Woldegebriel left for India with Ras Imru, who had been appointed ambassador there, Yohannes was placed in the care of Kassa Hagos, a Merkato businessman, with a monthly allowance for his schooling.

After completing seventh grade he visited Tigray for the summer and learned that his mother had died several years earlier. He decided not to return to Addis Ababa and enrolled in Grade 8 at Queen Sheba School in Adwa. He then entered the Evangelical Mission boarding school in Debre Zeit (now Bishoftu), where he learned to play the guitar.

He completed the Ethiopian School Leaving Certificate examination in June 1963 and in 1964 entered Haile Selassie I University (now Addis Ababa University), where he studied history and graduated in June 1969.

== Career and political activism ==
At university Yohannes took part in student political meetings and discussion groups, including gatherings at the Genfele (Ginfelle) house in Addis Ababa where he lived with his siblings Kidanemariam, Aberash and Sahleselassie Teklehaimanot. Participants and visitors reportedly included Gidey Gebrewahid, Yoseph Gebregziabher, Gebrekidan Asfaha, Rezene Tekle and Netsanet Asfaw.

After graduating in 1969 he worked for an American-founded international organisation in Addis Ababa, travelling regularly to Tigray, and reportedly declined a scholarship to study in the United States. He wrote a manuscript on Tigrayan history in Tigrinya, titled, copies of which were circulated among friends; the original reportedly went with him when he joined the armed struggle in 1975, while a copy left with relatives was destroyed out of fear of Derg house searches.

In 1971 he moved to Mekelle and taught history and English at Emperor Yohannes Secondary School.

== Tigray Liberation Front ==
=== Origins ===
According to Aregawi Berhe, a founding member of the TPLF, the Political Association of Tigrayans (PAT), led by Yohannes Teklehaimanot and Gebre Kidan, carried out underground political mobilisation of Tigrayans against the Ethiopian government. The association advocated the outright independence of Tigray and later emerged as an armed organisation known as the Tigray Liberation Front. The date of the TLF's founding is given as 1972 in some accounts. Reported founders and early members include Gidey Gebrewahid, Rezene Tekle, Gebrekidan Asfeha, Yemane Gebremeskel, Tadesse Tilahun, Hailekiros Asgede, Amare Tesfaye, Mussie Kidane, Tekeste Birhane and others.

Yohannes is reported to have served as the organisation's chairman while remaining in Mekelle and Addis Ababa to organise underground activity, while other members went to the mountains of Eastern Tigray near Aiga, along the Eritrean border.

=== Ideology ===
The TLF was grounded in Tigrayan nationalism rather than Marxism–Leninism. Yohannes is reported to have admired earlier Tigrayan rulers such as Yohannes IV and Ras Alula, in contrast to contemporary revolutionary groups that viewed traditional rulers as an oppressive class. He also reportedly envisaged a shared "Tigray-Tigrigni" state uniting Tigray and Eritrea.

=== Relations with the Eritrean Liberation Front ===
By the time the Tigrayan National Organization, the precursor of the TPLF, approached the Eritrean Liberation Front (ELF) for support, the TLF had already established a working relationship with the ELF. Berhe suggests that the ELF may have regarded the TLF as more truly nationalist because it upheld the independence of Tigray, similar to the Eritrean position. Yohannes reportedly attended an ELF congress in the Barka region of Eritrea, where he proposed a joint Tigray-Tigrigni state; the ELF leadership did not respond favourably.

=== Move to the field ===
After the Derg formally took power on 12 September 1974, Yohannes remained in Addis Ababa for several months. After the Derg's security services uncovered the underground network, he reportedly left the capital in early 1975 and joined TLF forces in Eastern Tigray.

== Merger with the TPLF and arrest ==
The TPLF began its armed struggle on 18 February 1975 from Dedebit in western Tigray. Berhe writes that its founders believed the armed struggle should begin before the nationalist TLF, the Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Party and the Ethiopian Democratic Union, all of which were preparing to fight the Derg from Tigray, could gain ground.

According to accounts favourable to the TLF, delegations of the two organisations met at Tsorena in central Tigray in 1975 and agreed in principle to merge, with a formal ceremony to follow at the TLF base at Zegebla near Aiga Mountain. Some TLF leaders asked for postponement; Yohannes reportedly refused, citing the destructive rivalry between Eritrean fronts.

The merger ceremony reportedly took place on 12 December 1975. These accounts state that TPLF leaders, including Aregawi Berhe, had planned to detain the TLF leadership, and that on the morning of 13 December TLF leaders and fighters were surrounded and detained, while Yemane Gebremeskel and four others who resisted were killed.

== Death ==
Yohannes, Tadesse Tilahun and other TLF leaders were reportedly held for about three months in an underground prison near Dima Marwa. In February 1976 he and Tadesse Tilahun, along with at least one other TLF leader, were reportedly executed without trial and buried in a single grave at Mariam Gundagundo. Reported accusations against him included admiration for historical Tigrayan rulers and nationalist aims.

* Tigray People's Liberation Front
* Eritrean Liberation Front

* Peasant Revolution in Ethiopia: The Tigray People's Liberation Front, 1975–1991, Cambridge University Press

He completed the Ethiopian School Leaving Certificate examination in June 1963 and in 1964 entered Haile Selassie I University (now Addis Ababa University), where he studied history and graduated in June 1969.

At university Yohannes took part in student political meetings and discussion groups, including gatherings at the Genfele (Ginfelle) house in Addis Ababa where he lived with his siblings Kidanemariam, Aberash and Sahleselassie Teklehaimanot. Participants and visitors reportedly included Gidey Gebrewahid, Yoseph Gebregziabher, Gebrekidan Asfaha, Rezene Tekle and Netsanet Asfaw.

After graduating in 1969 he worked for an American-founded international organisation in Addis Ababa, travelling regularly to Tigray, and reportedly declined a scholarship to study in the United States. He wrote a manuscript on Tigrayan history in Tigrinya, titled, copies of which were circulated among friends; the original reportedly went with him when he joined the armed struggle in 1975, while a copy left with relatives was destroyed out of fear of Derg house searches.

In 1971 he moved to Mekelle and taught history and English at Emperor Yohannes Secondary School.

== Tigray Liberation Front ==
=== Origins ===
According to Aregawi Berhe, a founding member of the TPLF, the Political Association of Tigrayans (PAT), led by Yohannes Teklehaimanot and Gebre Kidan, carried out underground political mobilisation of Tigrayans against the Ethiopian government. The association advocated the outright independence of Tigray and later emerged as an armed organisation known as the Tigray Liberation Front. The date of the TLF's founding is given as 1972 in some accounts. Reported founders and early members include Gidey Gebrewahid, Rezene Tekle, Gebrekidan Asfeha, Yemane Gebremeskel, Tadesse Tilahun, Hailekiros Asgede, Amare Tesfaye, Mussie Kidane, Tekeste Birhane and others.

Yohannes is reported to have served as the organisation's chairman while remaining in Mekelle and Addis Ababa to organise underground activity, while other members went to the mountains of Eastern Tigray near Aiga, along the Eritrean border.

=== Ideology ===
The TLF was grounded in Tigrayan nationalism rather than Marxism–Leninism. Yohannes is reported to have admired earlier Tigrayan rulers such as Yohannes IV and Ras Alula, in contrast to contemporary revolutionary groups that viewed traditional rulers as an oppressive class. He also reportedly envisaged a shared "Tigray-Tigrigni" state uniting Tigray and Eritrea.

=== Relations with the Eritrean Liberation Front ===
By the time the Tigrayan National Organization, the precursor of the TPLF, approached the Eritrean Liberation Front (ELF) for support, the TLF had already established a working relationship with the ELF. Berhe suggests that the ELF may have regarded the TLF as more truly nationalist because it upheld the independence of Tigray, similar to the Eritrean position. Yohannes reportedly attended an ELF congress in the Barka region of Eritrea, where he proposed a joint Tigray-Tigrigni state; the ELF leadership did not respond favourably.

=== Move to the field ===
After the Derg formally took power on 12 September 1974, Yohannes remained in Addis Ababa for several months. After the Derg's security services uncovered the underground network, he reportedly left the capital in early 1975 and joined TLF forces in Eastern Tigray.

== Merger with the TPLF and arrest ==
The TPLF began its armed struggle on 18 February 1975 from Dedebit in western Tigray. Berhe writes that its founders believed the armed struggle should begin before the nationalist TLF, the Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Party and the Ethiopian Democratic Union, all of which were preparing to fight the Derg from Tigray, could gain ground.

According to accounts favourable to the TLF, delegations of the two organisations met at Tsorena in central Tigray in 1975 and agreed in principle to merge, with a formal ceremony to follow at the TLF base at Zegebla near Aiga Mountain. Some TLF leaders asked for postponement; Yohannes reportedly refused, citing the destructive rivalry between Eritrean fronts.

The merger ceremony reportedly took place on 12 December 1975. These accounts state that TPLF leaders, including Aregawi Berhe, had planned to detain the TLF leadership, and that on the morning of 13 December TLF leaders and fighters were surrounded and detained, while Yemane Gebremeskel and four others who resisted were killed.

== Death ==
Yohannes, Tadesse Tilahun and other TLF leaders were reportedly held for about three months in an underground prison near Dima Marwa. In February 1976 he and Tadesse Tilahun, along with at least one other TLF leader, were reportedly executed without trial and buried in a single grave at Mariam Gundagundo. Reported accusations against him included admiration for historical Tigrayan rulers and nationalist aims.

data.title: Draft A.J. Ramirez
data.text:
A. J. Ramirez is an educator, licensed professional counselor, researcher, and United Methodist lay minister in Georgia. She works at Valdosta State University in sociology and Women's and Gender Studies. Her work includes teaching and research on gender, sexuality, social inequality, and the experiences of marginalized groups. [ref: Dr. A. J. Ramirez - Directory Profile - Valdosta State University, www.valdosta.edu]

Education and academic career

Ramirez earned a bachelor's degree in sociology from the University of North Georgia. She later earned a master's degree in marriage and family therapy and a Doctor of Education degree from Valdosta State University. [ref: Dr. A. J. Ramirez - Directory Profile - Valdosta State University, www.valdosta.edu]

At Valdosta State, Ramirez works in sociology and Women's and Gender Studies. In 2022, she participated in a university program on women's suffrage supported by a grant from the American Library Association. The program included a discussion of Women Making History: The 19th Amendment Book, a collection of essays compiled by the National Park Service. [ref: VSU Wins American Library Association Grant for Women’s Suffrage Project, Valdosta CEO] [ref: Valdosta State University's Odum Library & Women's & Gender Studies Program Receive Grant for Women's Suffrage Book Discussion Project, Georgia Library Quarterly]

Ramirez has also taught in the department of Women's Studies at Florida State University. [ref: ]

Counseling

Ramirez owns and leads L.E.A.F. Therapy Services, a counseling practice in South Georgia. The practice provides counseling for individuals, couples, and families. Its stated mission focuses on well-being, relationships, and healthier communities, and it welcomes clients from different backgrounds, including people who have experienced discrimination or marginalization. [ref: Home, My Vxw Site Drdccu 1]

Research

Ramirez has collaborated with sociologist Nancy L. Malcom on research about LGBTQ+-affirming members of The United Methodist Church. Their work examined why some LGBTQ+ people and their allies remain in the denomination despite disagreements over LGBTQ+ inclusion.

Their research included “Worth Fighting For”: Research Findings on Affirming United Methodists’ Decision to Stay or Leave and the series “Why Do They Stay? Queer Voices Share Their UMC Experiences.” The publications discuss the experiences and decisions of people navigating questions of inclusion within the church. [ref: Sociologists Find LGBTQ United Methodists, Allies Stay in UMC Out of Hope, United Methodist Insight] [ref: Why Do They Stay? Queer Voices Share Their UMC Experiences, United Methodist Insight]

Media appearances

In May 2023, Ramirez appeared with Malcom on Faith Revisited, a podcast hosted by the Reverend Ben Gosden. The episode, titled “Why Stay: Research on Marginalized Voices in the UMC,” focused on their research and the experiences of LGBTQ+-affirming United Methodists. [ref: Faith Revisited Podcast, Faith Revisited Podcast]

Ramirez was also interviewed for In Between, a student documentary directed by Adison Oliver and associated with students in Florida State University's media department. [ref: THE IN•BETWEEN]

Mosaic United Methodist Church and LGBTQ Advocacy

Ramirez has advocated for LGBTQ+ inclusion in the South Georgia Conference of The United Methodist Church. Ramirez and her wife, Gayle, helped establish an LGBTQ+-affirming United Methodist community in Valdosta, Georgia. The initiative received support from Centenary United Methodist Church in Macon, initially under the leadership of the Reverend Timothy Bagwell and later with support from the Reverend Sara Pugh Montgomery. The community developed into Mosaic United Methodist Church. The denomination's directory records the congregation's start date as March 1, 2023. [ref: ]

Lay ministry

Ramirez became a certified lay minister in the South Georgia Conference in December 2024. In December 2025, Centenary United Methodist Church announced a congregational process concerning her advancement toward candidacy for ordained ministry as a deacon. [ref: Called Charge Conference, Centenary Church] The 2024 General Conference of The United Methodist Church removed longstanding restrictions on LGBTQ+ people serving as clergy. Ramirez's ministry developed during this period of change in the denomination.

data.title: Judi for Food Industries
data.text:
Judi for Food Industries (), trading as Judi, is a Libyan food manufacturing company headquartered in Tripoli. Founded in 2004, it produces dairy products and fruit juices, mainly in carton packaging, and is described as one of the leading producers of carton-packed milk and juice in Libya. [ref: Part Five: A bite-size breakdown of who's who in the Libyan retail, FMCG and food production sector, The British Libyan Business Association] [ref: About Judi, Judi for Food Industries]

== History ==
Judi for Food Industries was established in 2004. In 2008, construction was completed on a production building in Tripoli for evaporated milk and juice, with a site area and built-up area of about 15,000 square metres. [ref: Judi Company Evaporated Milk, Juice, Medad Consulting Engineers]

== Operations ==
The company has a reported production capacity of about 120 tonnes per day. It imports raw materials, including whole milk powder and banana purée, from countries such as New Zealand, Chile, Guatemala and Costa Rica.

== Products ==
Judi's product range includes:
* UHT milk (full-fat, low-fat and skimmed)
* Fruit juices and nectars (Judi Nectar)
* Cheese
* Flavoured milk (Moudi)
* Mocktails
* Ayran
* Butter ghee

data.title: Boston Global Forum (BGF)
data.text:
The Boston Global Forum (BGF) is a Boston-based nonprofit think tank and international policy forum founded in 2012. Its work concerns international affairs, artificial intelligence governance and responsible technological development. [ref: Judea Pearl Named AI Pioneer by Boston Global Forum in Honor of America’s 250th Anniversary, UCLA Samueli School of Engineering] [ref: Boston Think Tank Brings Ethical AI Principles into Governance, Finance, Banking and Blockchain, Global Association of Risk Professionals] Its stated aims include peace, security, freedom, democracy and human dignity. BGF brings together political leaders, scholars, policymakers and technologists to develop proposals for global governance and the use of artificial intelligence. [ref: Boston Global Forum Announces the Evolution of AIWS: From AI World Society to AI Wisdom Society, Boston Global Forum]

== History and organization ==
BGF was co-founded by former Massachusetts governor Michael Dukakis, former VietNamNet editor Nguyen Anh Tuan, and Harvard professors Thomas E. Patterson and John Quelch. [ref: About, Boston Global Forum] In 2018, the Associated Press described Dukakis as its chair and Patterson as a board member. [ref: Dukakis: Global accord needed on use of AI by governments, KSL.com]

== Activities ==
=== Artificial intelligence governance ===
BGF's AI World Society initiative has developed proposals concerning AI ethics, government services and international cooperation. In 2018, its co-founders Dukakis and Tuan advocated international standards for AI use. The initiative proposed a United Nations body, modeled on the International Atomic Energy Agency, to coordinate agreements on the use of AI by governments.

A 2025 article in the Global Association of Risk Professionals' publication described BGF's subsequent proposals for AI-supported public services and financial governance, including AIWS Government 24/7 and the Boston Finance Accord. The article presented these initiatives through interviews with BGF representatives and descriptions of the organization's policy frameworks.

=== Cooperation with Club de Madrid ===
BGF and the Club de Madrid organized a policy lab on transatlantic approaches to digital governance on September 16–18, 2020. [ref: Policy Lab: Transatlantic Approaches to Digital Governance, MIT Media Lab] [ref: Club de Madrid and the Boston Global Forum advocate for a Social Contract for the AI Age, Club de Madrid] Its final report advocated a Social Contract for the AI Age, addressing the responsibilities of governments, technology companies and other participants in AI development and use. Recommendations included a code of ethics for AI developers and users and support for international cooperation on digital governance.

== Awards ==
BGF presents the World Leader for Peace and Security Award and the World Leader in AIWS Award. Recipients have included Shinzo Abe and Angela Merkel for the former, and Vint Cerf and Judea Pearl for the latter. [ref: World Leader for Peace and Security Award, Boston Global Forum] [ref: World Leaders in AIWS Award, Boston Global Forum]

In 2026, BGF and AIWS named 50 AI Pioneers in connection with the United States' 250th anniversary. UCLA reported that Pearl was among those recognized and that the honorees were celebrated at BGF's America at 250 conference in May.

data.title: New York Chinese School
data.text:
== New York Chinese School est. 1909 [https://www.nychineseschool.org/home------.html New York Chinese School Homepage] Official Website ==

The New York Chinese School (NYCS) is a non-profit 501(c)(3) community language school located on Mott Street in the Chinatown neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City. [ref: New York Chinese School – Museum of Chinese in America, www.mocanyc.org] Established in the early 20th century, the school is one of 60 member organizations affiliated with the Chinese Consolidated Benevolent Association (CCBA) [ref: The History of the Oldest Chinese School in NYC, Documented] and has been chartered by the New York State Education Department since 1967. [ref: New York Chinese School – Museum of Chinese in America, www.mocanyc.org]

==== History and Facilities ====
Founded as one of the earliest overseas Chinese language schools, NYCS initially opened with approximately 20 students. The school has since expanded to serve over 3,000 [ref: During Pandemic, Taiwanese Donations Help Keep Chinese Language School Afloat, Columbia News Service] students annually across its weekend, after-school, and summer camp sessions.

Its facility includes 22 classrooms, a 400-seat auditorium, an indoor gymnasium, two dance studios, and a music practice room. [ref: about, New York Chinese School]

==== Academics and Programs ====
NYCS offers language instruction in Mandarin and Cantonese for K–12 students and adults, covering beginner through advanced proficiency levels. Curriculum materials incorporate both Traditional and Simplified Chinese characters, with primary emphasis on Simplified script. In addition to language coursework, the curriculum includes Chinese cultural studies, such as calligraphy and traditional poetry. [ref: New York Chinese School – Museum of Chinese in America, www.mocanyc.org]

The school also provides elective and academic support programs, including:

* Arts & Music: Visual arts, dance, piano, and violin [ref: The History of the Oldest Chinese School in NYC, Documented]
* Academic Enrichment: Mathematics, English, computer coding, and Specialized High Schools Admissions Test (SHSAT) preparation

Qualified language students can sit for the Standards-based Measurement of Proficiency (STAMP) examination. Passing scores on the STAMP test qualify students to earn the New York State Seal of Biliteracy.

==== Partnerships and Student Support ====
NYCS collaborates with local higher education institutions, including Columbia University’s Teachers College and Hunter College, to place university students as teaching assistants. [ref: The History of the Oldest Chinese School in NYC, Documented]

The school assists eligible students in registering for national youth recognition frameworks, including the Congressional Award program. Financial assistance and academic scholarships are provided through community donations, including support from Wonton Food Inc. and local civic leaders. [ref: The History of the Oldest Chinese School in NYC, Documented]

== Awards and Scholarships Under NYCS Supervision ==

data.title: New Earth Ascension
data.text:
New Earth Ascension is a concept from the New Age movement. It is the belief that Earth is transitioning to a new spiritual stage, with greater spiritual awareness and impact on every aspect of human life. The idea appeared in Spiritism and Theosophy in the mid 19th century and gained popularity in the New Age movement in the 1980s. The concept can be considered a fringe theory of eschatological nature, and is commonly associated to UFO religions.

Because the New Age movement is heavily decentralized, this same concept can be reffered by different terms, like The 3D to 5D Shift, The Collective Consciousness Shift, The Timeline Split and others.

== Definition ==

=== Earth as a life school ===

According to the New Age point of view, human beings are spirits with a physical body. The spirits are created simple and ignorant. For their development, spirits are born on Earth through multiple incarnations. Human experiences on Earth promote the evolution of the spirit.

It is also believed that there are several planets with intelligent life in the Universe. Each planet has a different level of spiritual and technological development. A young soul will incarnate in a less developed planet and, as it progresses, will be transferred to more advanced ones. Eventually, when the spirit assimilates everything that has to be learned, it will graduate as a Pure Spirit. [ref: Journey of souls: Case studies of life between lives., Llewellyn Publications] [ref: Between death and life: Conversations with a spirit, Ozark Mountain Publishing]

=== A call for help and the volunteers ===

According to the New Earth theory, human greed, war, environmental destruction, and fear-based control systems have pushed the Earth to its absolute limit. The breaking point was the creation of the atomic bomb in the 1940s. Because of free will, the caretakers of the Earth could not interfere from outside. So they found a way to interfere from inside. A desperate call for help was sent across the Universe, and millions of advanced souls volunteered to be born on Earth. These souls are known as starseeds or volunteers.

Some of the starseeds are former aliens from advanced planets, and some are Pure Spirits. They live ordinary lives, but unconsciously work as "anchors of light", reducing the density of the planet and transmitting the necessary energy for the creation of the new Earth. Due to the nature of Earth, volunteers go through the "veil of forgetfulness" when they are born, so they forget about their real nature. Because of this, there is the risk of a volunteer getting lost in the density of the Earth. If a volunteer yields to selfishness, hatred, or generates too much negative karma, they may end up becoming trapped in Earth's reincarnation cycle, instead of returning home by the end of their life.

In his books "Gods of Aquarius" and "The star people", Brad Steiger described psychological and physical characteristics of the starseeds, which include: [ref: Gods of Aquarius: UFOs and the transformation of man, Berkley Publishing Corp] [ref: The star people, Berkley Publishing Corp]

* Feeling of not belonging: From childhood, they feel that "this world is not their home" or that they were left on the wrong planet.

* Social alienation: They have extreme difficulty adjusting to rigid social structures, competitive political systems, or purely material ambitions.

* Initial amnesia and awakening: Forgetting of real identity and purpose during childhood, followed by a gradual or abrupt process of "awakening".

* Physical symptoms and allergies: Because they have a mix of terrestrial and extraterrestrial lineage, starseeds have greater propensity for allergies, sleep disorders, chronic fatigue, or hypersensitivity to loud noises, bright lights, and heavy environments.

* Intrinsic desire to help: Even without knowing why, they possess an internal moral compass oriented towards healing, caring for nature, animals, or the well-being of others.

* Paranormal and Spiritual Experiences: They commonly see UFOs, have vivid dreams of spaceships and traveling to other planets, and possess latent or active psychic abilities, such as telepathy, precognition, or hands-on healing.

In the book "The Three Waves of Volunteers and the New Earth", Dolores Cannon identified three waves of volunteers: [ref: The three waves of volunteers and the new Earth, Ozark Mountain Publishing]

* The First Wave arrived from the 1950s to the 1960s as a pioneering force. Their task was to break through the planet's dense, negative vibration following the advent of nuclear weapons. Because they were the first to arrive, they suffered the most from intense feelings of alienation, severe depression, and a painful, lifelong homesickness for their true spiritual homes.

* The Second Wave arrived from the 1970s to the 1980s, acting as passive "energetic antennas". Their primary mission is simply to exist and anchor light on the planet. They need no active effort, nor do they need to change the world through career achievements. Rather, their high vibrational frequency naturally radiates outward to shift the people and environments around them. Meanwhile, they also struggled with extreme sensitivity and crowd exhaustion.

* The Third Wave comprises the children born from the 1990s onward (often called Indigo children). They are the actual blueprint builders of the New Earth. These children possess genetically advanced, highly intuitive consciousness and are frequently misdiagnosed with conditions like ADHD by traditional societal systems, because they inherently refuse to accept corrupt, fear-based authority.

=== New Earth ascension ===

The light brought by the starseeds will promote the ascension of the Earth to a new spiritual stage. However, the transition is not peaceful. Current political, financial, and religious institutions were designed to keep the population under fear. As the planet's energy shifts during the transition, these old structures will undergo a total collapse (economic meltdown, civil distrust, political unrest). The planet will also go through several cataclysmic events. According to New Age beliefs, Earth itself is a living being. Thus, the energy of hate, war, and environmental destruction accumulated in the Earth's crust must be purged in the form of earthquakes and storms. [ref: Bringers of the dawn: Teachings from the Pleiadians, Bear & Company]

Unfortunately, not all humans are ready for the New Earth transition. While some people will elevate its spiritual frequency, others will not. As the difference increases, the planet will divide into two distinct planes of existence (sometimes refered to as different timelines):

* The Old Earth (3D): This version remains anchored in the dense, heavy energies of fear, control, manipulation, and conflict. People who choose to remain anchored in old, fear-based belief systems or heavy karmic cycles remain here. To them, the world will continue to look chaotic and broken. Due to its unstable nature, the Old Earth will eventually be destroyed, and its inhabitants will be transferred to other planets.

* The New Earth (5D): This version rises into a completely new plane of existence, governed by unconditional love, cooperation, unity consciousness, and deep healing. It is described as a reality free of disease, suffering, and heavy density.

According to its believers, on the New Earth, the wheel of karma will come to an end. Human beings will develop "spiritual powers", like telepathy, clairvoyance, and spiritual healing. Aliens will make open contact with humanity, bring new technologies and support the advancement of spirituality and science. There will be great social advancement, with the end of war, corruption and poverty.

data.title: Newton Novices' Hurdle
data.text:
The Newton Novices' Hurdle is a Grade 2 National Hunt hurdle race in Great Britain which is open to horses aged four years or older. It is run at Haydock Park over a distance of about 1 mile 7½ furlongs (1 mile 7 furlongs 144 yards, or 3,149 metres), and during its running there are nine hurdles to be jumped. [ref: Haydock Course Map, Racing Post] The race is for novice hurdlers, and it is scheduled to take place each year in November.

The race was inaugurated in 2004, run in early December at Listed level. The following year, it was moved to November and formed part of the undercard for the new Lancashire Chase, a role the race still performs today. However, the race was held on the day before (the Friday) from 2011 to 2016, when it returned to the Saturday. [ref: Haydock Results, Racing Post] It was upgraded in 2023 to Grade 2. [ref: Package of changes agreed to help strengthen performance of British Jump racing, BHA] The race is currently sponsored by Betfair.

data.title: Christian Mondragón
data.text:
Christian Mondragón [ref: Christian Mondragón, el creativo colombiano que conquista EE. UU., El Tiempo]

Christian Mondragón is a Colombian creative director and copywriter [ref: Christian Mondragón of Casanova//McCann: “Ideas Are Not Just Viral, People Want to Be Part Of It", PRODU] recognized as a co-creator of The Bulletpen [ref: Work, Mondra], known in Spanish as El Balígrafo [ref: ], a writing instrument made from ammunition and used to sign Colombia’s 2016 peace agreement between the government and the FARC following more than five decades of armed conflict. Developed during his time at McCann Colombia for the Ministry of National Education, the initiative transformed an object associated with war into a symbol of education and peace. [ref: Habla uno de los creadores del balígrafo con el que se firmó la paz, Cambio]”

The project’s significance extended into museums. In December 2016, Colombian President Juan Manuel Santos donated a Bulletpen to the Nobel Museum in Stockholm. Another example was exhibited at the National Museum of Colombia, contributing to the preservation of the peace process’s historical memory.

In 2023, Bloomberg Línea included Mondragón among the 100 most innovative people in Latin America [ref: Las 100 personas más innovadoras de América Latina en 2023, Bloomberg Línea], a selection highlighting contributions across business, science, technology, the arts, and communications.

His work also includes Second Chances [ref: Clio Awards 2022 Jury Member Christian Mondragon, clios.com], an initiative for Donate Life California, as documented in his official Clio Awards profile. According to biographical information supplied by Mondragón, his involvement in social initiatives also includes Radar de Ayuda and Adopta Andipanpolis, reflecting his interest in applying creativity to social causes.

According to his professional portfolio, [ref: Mondragon - Associate Creative Director, Mondra] projects to which he has contributed have earned more than 200 international awards and distinctions, including recognition at Cannes Lions, The One Show, Clio Awards, and London International Awards. [ref: ] Work such as The Bulletpen has reached beyond advertising to become part of broader cultural and historical conversations.

According to his current biographical information, Mondragón is expanding his career into documentary filmmaking, [ref: Christian Mondragón, Entertainment Oxygen] building on his experience in creative communication and storytelling.

data.title: Guru Organic Energy
data.text:
----

Guru Organic Energy Corp. (), commonly known as Guru (stylized GURU), is a Canadian beverage company based in Montreal, Quebec, that produces organic energy drinks. The company launched its first energy drink in 1999 and markets its products as plant-based alternatives to conventional energy drinks, with caffeine derived from green tea and guarana. Guru has been listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange since November 2020 and sells its products in Canada and the United States.

== History ==
=== Origins and early years ===
According to the company, Guru's origins trace to the mid-1990s at SONA, an electronic dance music venue in Montreal, where plant-based "smart drinks" were served to patrons as an alternative to synthetic energy products. The drink was canned and brought to market in Montreal in 1999. Accounts of the founding differ: a 2009 company announcement described Guru as having been founded by four college friends and quoted Ray Jolicoeur as a co-founder, while later coverage and regulatory announcements identify Joe Zakher as the company's founder.

By 2008, Guru's lineup in Canada included its original energy drink and a low-calorie Lite version alongside juice, lemonade and iced tea varieties, sold through retailers such as Petro-Canada, Loblaws, Sobeys and Walmart. In 2009, the company announced that rapper Kanye West had become an equity partner and would help develop a new product; the product never materialized, and the juice, lemonade and iced tea lines were later discontinued.

=== Organic positioning and growth ===
Guru later obtained USDA organic certification for its energy drinks and, over the 2010s, made its natural and organic claims the centre of its marketing. In 2016, it introduced a zero-sugar line of organic "energy waters". In 2017, the company began targeting U.S. convenience stores, mainly in the San Francisco Bay Area.

In December 2018, Guru stated that it held close to 10 percent of the energy drink market in Quebec and about 4 percent in Canada, citing Mintel data, which it said placed it fourth among energy drink brands in Canada behind Red Bull, Monster and Rockstar.

=== Public listing ===
In August 2020, Guru announced that it would go public through a transaction with Mira X Acquisition Corp., a capital pool company listed on the TSX Venture Exchange. At the time, its drinks were sold at about 15,000 points of sale and the company generated annual revenue of roughly CA$30 million, about 70 percent of it in Canada, mainly in Quebec. Ahead of the listing, Guru raised CA$34.5 million in a brokered private placement led by Stifel Nicolaus Canada, at a pro forma valuation of about CA$160 million. Its share of the Quebec energy drink market was then estimated at 13 percent. Its shares began trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange in November 2020.

=== Financial results ===
In September 2025, Guru reported net income of CA$1.3 million for its third fiscal quarter, compared with a net loss of CA$2.2 million a year earlier, on record quarterly revenue of CA$10.4 million; it was the company's first profitable quarter since its public listing. For fiscal 2025, Guru reported revenue of CA$34.7 million and a net loss of CA$1.4 million.

== Products ==
Guru's products are sold in cans and include its original energy drink, the stevia-sweetened Guru Lite, the fruit-flavoured Guru Punch line launched in 2021, and the zero-sugar Guru Zero line, which the company began rolling out in the United States in 2024. The drinks are made without sucralose or aspartame, and their caffeine comes from organic guarana seed and green tea extracts.

data.title: Friedrich Katz Prize
data.text:
The Friedrich Katz Prize is an annual book prize of the American Historical Association. It is awarded for "the best book published in English focusing on Latin America, including the Caribbean," and is named in honor of Friedrich Katz, a distinguished historian of Latin America.

The AHA announced the creation of the prize in November 2013. The Katz Prize succeeded the earlier John E. Fagg Prize, which had only received a ten-year bequest. Major donors at the inception of the prize included the Katz family, El Colegio de México, and the Tinker Foundation. [ref: AHA Establishes the Friedrich Katz Prize – AHA, https://www.historians.org/] The first award was given in 2014. [ref: Friedrich Katz Prize, American Historical Association]

data.title: Eleazar ben Durdaia
data.text:
Rabbi Eleazar ben Durdaia (also spelled Elazar ben Durdayya; ) was an individual from the Tannaim era, who was a sinner, but repented shortly before he died.

Eleazar is quoted both as a warning against debauchery, which leads to death, and as an encouragement to repentance, which leads to eternal happiness.

==Talmudic account==
The Talmud [ref: Avodah Zarah [https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.17a.12?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en 17a]] relates that, after leading a life of licentiousness, Eleazar bethought himself of his latter end. He mentally sought intercessors among the elements, beseeching them to appeal for his pardon and future peace; but none was found competent to act for him, they themselves being finite, and doomed to annihilation. Concluding that his future depended solely on himself, he prayed and wept until he died. Thereupon, a bat kol announced that Eleazar was assured of happiness in the hereafter. When Rabbi (Judah ha-Nasi) heard this story, he exclaimed, "Verily, some procure eternal happiness only after toiling many years, while others obtain the same result in a short time". [ref: ] [ref: אלעזר בן דורדיא]

data.title: Ecce Homo (Van Dyck)
data.text:
----

Ecce Homo or Behold The Man is a religous painting by 17th century Flemish painter Anthony Van Dyck. This painting depicts Christ being presented to the people before his crucifixion with ropes binding his hands together while wearing the crown of thorns and his waist covered in white and black cloth while a solider stands behind him holding a black cloth in both hands.

== Provenance ==
The painting may have been commisioned by the Baldi Family in 1625 and was first recorded in the collection of Francesco Maria Balbi in 1701. In 1805, it was aqquired by the painter and art dealer Andrew Wilson In 1807, it was sold at Coxe, London as lot 32 [ref: The catalogue of that most valuable and important selection of original paintings, the property of Andrew Wilson: purchased by him and brought to England from palaces of the first consequence at Genoa: embracing the finest works of those great masters, Claude le Loraine, Annibal Caracci, Agostino Caracci, Ludovico Caracci, Guido Rheni, Titian Vicelli, &c., Rubens, Tintoretto, Van Dyck, Perino del Vaga, Guercino, &c., Mazzolino di Ferrara, Jacomo Puntormo, Andrea Mantegna, Vadder, Dionysius Calvert, &c., [London]: Catalogues may be had of Mr. Peter Coxe and at the place of sale] and again in 1810 as lot 10. In 1825, the painting was sold by a man known as Mr. Berry to Sir Alexander Hope and was passed down through the Earls of Hopetoun (later the Marquesses of Linlithgow). It was finally sold at Christie's in 1954 to the Barber Institute of Fine Arts [ref: Anthony van Dyck (1599–1641), The Barber Institute of Fine Arts].

data.title: MEG Reclamation
data.text:
Monoethylene glycol reclamation (MEG reclamation) is an industrial process used to remove dissolved salts, corrosion products, hydrocarbons and degradation by-products from monoethylene glycol (MEG), allowing the glycol to be reused in hydrocarbon production systems. MEG is commonly used as a thermodynamic hydrate inhibitor in subsea pipeline systems, where it is injected into production fluids to prevent the formation of hydrates that could obstruct flowlines. [ref: Formation of Gas Hydrates in Natural Gas Transmission Lines, Industrial & Engineering Chemistry]

MEG reclamation is principally employed in offshore natural gas developments, long-distance subsea tie-backs, floating production storage and offloading facilities (FPSOs), and onshore gas-processing plants. The process is often integrated with MEG regeneration systems that remove water from the recovered glycol stream. [ref: Offshore MEG Regeneration and Reclamation Units: Lessons Learned from Their Design and Operation]
[ref: Power FPSO New MEG System Concept Select & PreFEED, io consulting]

== Background ==

Early Deepwater Projects relied primarily on methanol for hydrate inhibition. This was simple as it was injected and not recovered. Methanol solubility in gas and liquid hydrocarbon product streams is substantially higher
than MEG solubility. [ref: Offshore Hydrate Engineering Handbook, Center for Hydrate Research, Colorado School of Mines]

As subsea tie-back became longer and longer, in the 1990s, MEG began to use MEG as a hydrate inhibitor. Unlike methanol, MEG can be recovered, purified and re-used, reducing chemical consumption and operating costs. The first documented MEG Reclamation units were at Shell Todd in New Zealand [ref: Glycol Purification – A Novel Approach to an Old Problem, NZ Engineering] [ref: Advanced Design of Glycol Reclamation Plants] and Shell's Mensa field in the Gulf of Mexico. [ref: How to Select Best MEG Recovery Unit's Configuration?, Digital Refining]

As production fluids travel through pipelines, the recovered MEG becomes contaminated with dissolved salts, corrosion products, hydrocarbons, production chemicals and degradation compounds. Without reclamation, these contaminants can accumulate and adversely affect process equipment and flow assurance performance.

== Regeneration vs Reclamation ==

Although the terms are sometimes used together, regeneration and reclamation describe different stages of MEG recovery.

Regeneration

Lean MEG, which is typically a concentrated solution of 80-90 wt% MEG in water, is injected into the wellhead... The MEG Regeneration process is comprised of two sections: Pre-treatment where hydrocarbon vapour and liquids are separated from the Rich MEG in a low pressure three phase separator. Regeneration where MEG is regenerated by boiling off water in an atmospheric distillation column. [ref: Crawley-Boevey, S.; Jariwala, A. "Offshore MEG Regeneration and Reclamation Units; Lessons Learned from Their Design and Operation". GPA Europe Conference Proceedings.] These regeneration are similar to those for Gas Glycol Dehydration.

Reclamation

MEG reclamation is the process of removing dissolved salts (both monovalent and divalent), scale-forming species, corrosion products, and other contaminants from recycled monoethylene glycol. Unlike regeneration, which primarily removes water, reclamation prevents contaminant accumulation that can lead to scaling, fouling, corrosion, and reduced process performance. [ref: Odeigah, E.A.; Pojtanabuntoeng, T. (2022). "Regeneration and Reclamation of Mono-Ethylene Glycol (MEG) Used as a Hydrate Inhibitor: A Review". American Journal of Chemical Engineering. 10(2): 32-45. doi:10.11648/j.ajche.20221002.13.]

== Process configurations ==

MEG reclamation systems are generally configured using either a full-stream or a slip-stream reclamation process.

Full-stream reclamation
Full-stream reclamation is where the entire regenerated MEG recycle stream is treated to remove dissolved salts, suspended solids, corrosion products, and other contaminants. Unlike MEG regeneration, which removes water to restore glycol concentration, full-stream reclamation removes non-volatile contaminants that accumulate during operation and can lead to scaling, fouling, and corrosion.. [ref: Othman, A.; Khraisheh, M.; Almomani, F.; Al-Sobhi, S.A.; AlNouss, A.; Adham, S. (2020). "Design, Optimization and Economic Analysis of a Monoethylene Glycol Recovery Process: Salt Precipitation and Vacuum Operation". International Journal of Energy Research. doi:10.1002/er.5426.]

Slip-stream reclamation
In a slip-stream configuration, only a portion of the circulating MEG is treated for salt removal while the remainder undergoes conventional regeneration. The selection of reclamation philosophy depends primarily on anticipated formation-water production rates, salt loading, chemical management requirements and overall system economics. [ref: Hydrate Prevention Using MEG Instead of MeOH: Impact of Experience from Major Norwegian Developments on Technology Selection for Injection and Recovery of MEG, Offshore Technology Conference]

== Process Technology ==

MEG reclamation systems generally employ combinations of:

* Vacuum distillation - Modern MEG reclamation systems commonly employ vacuum distillation to recover monoethylene glycol while avoiding thermal degradation. Operating under reduced pressure lowers the boiling temperature of the MEG-water mixture, allowing salts and other non-volatile contaminants to remain in the reclaimer while purified MEG is recovered and recycled. [ref: Hydrate Prevention Using MEG Instead of MeOH: Impact of Experience from Major Norwegian Developments on Technology Selection for Injection and Recovery of MEG] The vacuum is normally provided by a Liquid Ring Vacuum Pump.

* Salt precipitation - The calcium (along with the other divalent cations present in the formation water) is removed in a separate step by raising the pH of the aqueous MEG and precipitating the divalent cations as insoluble carbonates or (in the case of magnesium) hydroxides. The formation water contains dissolved divalent ions including:

Calcium (Ca²⁺)
Magnesium (Mg²⁺)
Iron (Fe²⁺)
Barium (Ba²⁺)
Strontium (Sr²⁺)

and that these species can lead to scaling and fouling if not removed from the MEG loop. [ref: Crawley-Boevey, S. "Removal of Divalent Salts from Aqueous MEG Solutions in a MEG Reclamation Process". GPA Europe Conference Proceedings.]

* Filtration - Filtration is commonly employed within monoethylene glycol (MEG) reclamation systems to remove suspended solids, precipitated salts, corrosion products, pipeline debris, and oxidation by-products that accumulate in the MEG circulation loop. [ref: Efficiently Removing Divalent Salts from MEG Reclamation Units: Developing a Tailor Made Solution]

* Solids Separation Technologies - This includes decanter centrifuges, [ref: Flow Assurance Impacts on Lean/Rich MEG Circuit Chemistry and MEG Regenerator/Reclaimer Design] gas-tight centrifuges, and basket centrifuges

* Solids handling and disposal systems - The specific process arrangement varies according to contaminant loading, required glycol purity and the characteristics of the produced water.

===Materials of Construction / Control of Oxygen===
Research into MEG reclamation systems has shown that control of dissolved oxygen is a critical aspect of process design. Oxygen ingress, particularly in high-temperature, salt-containing MEG environments, can promote localized corrosion of process equipment, including Duplex stainless steel. Studies have found that corrosion is most likely to occur where salts are deposited, while minimizing oxygen ingress through system integrity measures, gas blanketing, and oxygen control practices can significantly reduce corrosion risk. [ref: Materials Considerations for MEG (Mono Ethylene Glycol) Reclamation Systems, NACE International]

== Technology Providers ==

A number of companies supply MEG regeneration and reclamation technologies for offshore and onshore hydrocarbon production facilities.

* SLB markets the PureMEG regeneration and reclamation system. [ref: PureMEG Monoethylene Glycol Reclamation and Regeneration System, SLB]
* NOV Inc. supplies slip-stream and full-stream MEG recovery systems. [ref: MEG Recovery, NOV]
* Axens markets the AdvaMEG process for MEG regeneration and reclamation. [ref: MEG Recovery, Axens]
* Veolia supplies glycol regeneration systems for oil and gas applications. [ref: Glycol Regeneration and Dehydration System Packages, Veolia Water Technologies]

== Notable installations ==

MEG processing and reclamation technologies have been implemented in a number of major onshore and offshore gas developments worldwide. Below is a list of units by Continent:

=== EUROPE ===

- Norway - Ormen Lange, Åsgard B, [ref: Corrosion Inhibitor and Oxygen Scavenger for Use as MEG Additives in the Inhibition of Wet Gas Pipelines, Offshore Technology Conference] Gjøa Field [ref: Utslippsrapport for Gjøa 2024, Vår Energi]

- UK - Britannia Satellites

- Laggan Tormore (Shetland Islands) [ref: MEG Maintains Hydrates-Free Production at Laggan-Tormore, Offshore Magazine]

=== North and South America ===

- United States Gulf of Mexico - Shell Mensa WD-143 Offshore Project, [ref: How to Select Best MEG Recovery Unit's Configuration?, Digital Refining] Independence Hub [ref: Gas Hydrate Control Using Monoethylene Glycol in the Gulf of Mexico, Journal of Petroleum Technology]

- Brazil - Mexilhão Platform (Petrobras - Santos Basin), [ref: Simulation and Analysis of MEG Reclamation and Regeneration Unit in Offshore Natural Gas Plants, ACS Figshare] FPSO Cidade de Santos (Santos Basin) [ref: Programa de Descomissionamento Executivo Parcial – Escopo Plataforma FPSO Cidade de Santos, Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP)]

=== AFRICA and MIDDLE EAST ===

- Mozambique - Coral Sul FLNG / Coral North FLNG (Mozambique) [ref: Lessons Learned: 30 Years of MEG Reclamation, Pontem Analytics]

- Saudi Arabia - Wasit Onshore Gas Plant [ref: Aramco Outlines Best Practices for Sour-Gas Feed MEG System, Oil & Gas Journal]

- Egypt - West Nile Delta [ref: GEA Delivers MEG Purification Plant to BP, PROCESS Worldwide]

=== ASIA ===
- Azerbaijan - Shah Deniz

- India - KG-D6

- China - Liwan Gas Field [ref: General Design of Lean MEG Storing in the Jacket Legs on Liwan Gas Field of South China Sea, Offshore Technology Conference]

=== OCEANIA ===
- Australia - Prelude FLNG has a large MEG Reclamation Unit as referenced here.

Pluto-LNG

FPSO Ichthys Venturer
[ref: NOV Provides Critical MEG Technology and Bondstrand Fiberglass Piping to Ichthys LNG Project's FPSO Facility, MarketScreener]

- Otway Gas Plant (OGP) - Beach Energy [ref: Electrodialysis Membrane Technology Applied to MEG Reclamation – A Case Study, The APPEA Journal]

New Zealand - Kupe

The use of MEG reclamation technology is particularly common in deep-water gas developments requiring long subsea tie-backs.

data.title: Shipsy
data.text:
Shipsy, legally Llama Logisol Private Limited, is an Indian enterprise software company that develops cloud-based software for logistics and supply chain management. Founded in 2015, the company is headquartered in Gurugram, India.

== History ==
Shipsy was founded in 2015 in Gurugram by Soham Chokshi, Dhruv Agrawal, Harsh Kumar, Himanshu Gupta and Sahil Arora, graduates of the Indian Institutes of Technology; Chokshi became chief executive. An early angel round was led by Dheeraj Jain of Redcliffe Capital.

In April 2016, the courier company DTDC Express took a 20 percent stake in Shipsy for over US$1 million. A pre-Series A round led by Info Edge followed in November 2019, and in November 2020 the company raised a US$6 million Series A round co-led by Sequoia Capital India's Surge programme and Info Edge.

Shipsy raised US$25 million in a Series B round co-led by A91 Partners and Z3 Partners in February 2022.

In October 2023, Shipsy acquired the warehouse-management software provider StockOne to expand its fulfilment capabilities, and the same year launched an artificial intelligence assistant for logistics incident management called LIA. In 2025 it entered partnerships with logistics companies including Aramex and the UAE-based e7 Group, and in 2026 the company said it had crossed US$25 million in annual recurring revenue.

== Products and services ==
Shipsy develops cloud-based software that enterprises use to plan, execute and track the movement of goods across their supply chains. Its platform covers transportation management, warehouse management, last-mile delivery and route optimization, and multi-carrier management, and is used in sectors such as retail, manufacturing and automotive. Its warehouse-management capability was expanded through the 2023 acquisition of StockOne.

In 2026, Shipsy introduced AgentFleet, a set of artificial intelligence software agents designed to automate logistics workflows such as customer communication and invoice reconciliation.

== Recognition ==
Shipsy was positioned as a Niche Player in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Transportation Management Systems in 2026. In Gartner's 2026 Peer Insights Voice of the Customer for Transportation Management Systems, a report based on aggregated end-user reviews, Shipsy was named a Customers' Choice. Gartner has also listed the company as a representative vendor in its market guides for last-mile delivery technology (2025) and multicarrier parcel management (2026).

== Operations ==
Shipsy is headquartered in Gurugram and operates internationally, with customers in South Asia, the Middle East and Africa, Europe, Southeast Asia, Australia and the Americas. According to the company, it serves more than 150 enterprise customers in over 30 countries and employs around 300 people, with offices in India, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Singapore and Australia.

Since 2025, Shipsy has been a member of the Consultative Committee of the Universal Postal Union, a specialised agency of the United Nations.

data.title: Dove (magazine)
data.text:
Dove Viaggi (often simply Dove) is an Italian monthly travel and lifestyle magazine established in 1991 and published by RCS MediaGroup (ISSN 1121-1792). [ref: Dove, rcsmediagroup.it] [ref: Sito ufficiale Dove Viaggi, Corriere della Sera]

== History ==
The magazine was founded in May 1991 by journalist and publisher Luca Grandori (d. 2012), who had previously created other Italian travel publications, including Gulliver and Carnet. [ref: 25 anni di viaggi e sogni: l’editoriale del numero speciale di DOVE, Dove Viaggi] Its initial editorial office was located in Milan, with a founding team that included journalists Valeria Tegami, Mariella Grossi and Simona Tedesco.

During the 1990s, the magazine published themed print supplements, such as Speciale Weekend (focused on short itineraries) and Dossier Tropici (covering long-haul destinations). [ref: Cronologia e Linee di Sviluppo del Sistema DOVE, CairoRCS Media] In 2005, the publication released a series of spin-off magazines: DOVE Case, DOVE Eventi, and DOVE Auto. [ref: Dove negli anni, Corriere della Sera]

Valeria Tegami later became the magazine's director, followed by Carlo Montanaro. In January 2015, Simona Tedesco was appointed editor-in-chief, with an editorial focus on contemporary and sustainable travel.

In May 2017, the publication launched an annual Travel issue, distributed as a supplement with the daily newspaper Corriere della Sera.

In 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic, the magazine temporarily shifted its editorial focus to domestic and local travel and launched digital initiatives allowing readers to share local content.

In 2026, Dove expanded its multimedia activities with vodcasts and reader initiatives. [ref: I Podcast di Dove 35 anni, Corriere della Sera] In June, for its 35th anniversary, the magazine published a special issue with a commemorative cover and an editorial by Simona Tedesco centered on the manifesto "Andiamo sul posto. E raccontiamo", emphasizing the value of on-the-ground reporting over AI-generated content and unverified reviews. [ref: Buon compleanno Dove: 35 anni di viaggi da sogno, iO Donna]

== Monographic guides and digital projects ==
Beyond its monthly print edition, the publication produces Le Guide di Dove, a series of monographic travel guides established in 2006, and co-organizes public events on travel culture, such as the festival Il Tempo del Viaggio in Milan. [ref: Il Tempo del Viaggio Inverno, Corriere della Sera]

In February 2014, the brand expanded online with the launch of doveviaggi.it as the travel section of Corriere della Sera. Over time, the website expanded its content to include narrative video series, thematic newsletters, and dedicated podcasts launched in 2020, such as Brescia, che sorpresa! and I viaggi da film. [ref: I podcast di Dove Viaggi, Corriere della Sera] In parallel with the website's launch in 2014, the brand also introduced DoveClub, an online travel booking and e-commerce platform.

== Editors-in-chief ==

* Valeria Tegami (1994–2003)
* Carlo Montanaro (2003–2015)
* Simona Tedesco (2015–present)

data.title: Miguel Esparza
data.text:
----

Miguel Esparza is a Chicago-based sports broadcaster and voice-over artist known for his Spanish-language coverage of Major League Baseball and multiple Chicago professional sports teams, including the Cubs and the Blackhawks. [ref: Miguel Esparza is the Spanish voice of four Chicago sports teams, Block Club Chicago] [ref: Miguel Esparza: el reconocido narrador de Chicago MLB con raíces boricuas, Telemundo Puerto Rico] He has also worked in radio broadcasting as a news anchor and producer for WBBM 780 AM. [ref: How a Humboldt Park native became a Spanish voice for Chicago sports teams, CBS Chicago]

== Early life and education ==
Miguel Esparza was born and raised in Humboldt Park on the Northwest Side of Chicago. He is half Mexican and half Puerto Rican and he is the second of four children.

== Career ==

=== Early radio career ===
Esparza began his radio career in 2001 at La Ley 107.9 FM in Chicago, a regional Mexican music station, where he held various programming roles. In 2003, he began reporting on the Chicago Cubs and Chicago White Sox for a morning radio program.

In 2004, he joined Onda 92, a Spanish-language pop station, owned by the same parent company, but returned to La Ley after about a year and a half.

From 2009 to 2013, Esparza contributed remotely to talk shows for radio stations in Kentucky and Mazatlán, Sinaloa, Mexico, working the 10 a.m.-3 p.m. shift on both stations and working on the production side of the Kentucky station.

=== Chicago broadcasting and sports coverage ===
In 2014, Esparza went back to La Ley and began hosting a Spanish morning show and working as a Spanish-language play-by-play announcer for Chicago Bears broadcasts. He then moved to Mendota, Illinois and worked at regional Mexican station El Rey for four years before moving back to Chicago in 2018.

Esparza then joined Univision and WBBM 780 AM in Chicago. [ref: Meet Miguel Esparza, The Spanish Voice Of 4 Chicago Sports Teams, Block Club Chicago]At Univision, he contributed Spanish-language coverage of the Chicago Bulls, Chicago Bears, and Chicago Cubs. [ref: Miguel Esparza: el reconocido narrador de Chicago MLB con raíces boricuas, Telemundo Puerto Rico] He then added the Chicago White Sox to his roster in 2020.

A year later, Esparza took over Spanish-language play-by-play duties for the Chicago Cubs at Univison, gaining popularity by doing play-by-play coverage for multiple Chicago professional sports teams, including the Bears, Bulls, and Blackhawks. [ref: Miguel Esparza: el reconocido narrador de Chicago MLB con raíces boricuas, Telemundo Puerto Rico]

=== Current work ===
Since 2021, Esparza has served as the Spanish-language voice of the Chicago Cubs, gaining recognition from local media and other broadcasters for his passion of the job and his reporting on the teams.

Esparza has also provided Spanish-language play-by-play coverage for Grand Valley State University football. During the 2023 season, he was part of the inaugural Spanish-language broadcast team for the program, which was recognized by the Michigan Association of Broadcasters as the state's "Best" sports play-by-play broadcast. [ref: GVSU Football Spanish Language Broadcast Named Best Sports Play-By-Play in Michigan, Grand Valley State University Athletics]

He has appeared in media coverage related to the Chicago Cubs, including interviews at the team's annual Cubs Convention, podcasts with local news sites and a broadcast on Marquee Sports Network. [ref: Miguel Esparza loves Cubs' Alex Bregman, Edward Cabrera additions, Marquee Sports Network]

=== Community involvement ===
Outside of the radio booth, he has also worked to increase sports access and representation for and within the Latino community [ref: ], serving as an ambassador for both Chicago team franchises to get more Latino audiences into hockey and baseball. Latinos have historically not received a front-row seat to hockey compared to other nationalities, though the National Hockey League (NHL) has seen an increase in Latino fans since 2013. [ref: These NHL Players Are Changing Perceptions of Latinos in Hockey, Remezcla]

As part of that mission, Esparza has hosted events in partnership with the Blackhawks and the Cubs at the United Center and in various Chicago schools with predominantly Latino students, presenting them with checks for school supplies and hosting Mexican heritage nights. He always seeks to bring younger Latino sports fans into the Chicago sports world and inspire the next generation. [ref: Hockey eyes Hispanic fans for growth, www.espn.com]

Esparza has been involved in charitable work through St. Jude Children's Research Hospital since 2003 [ref: St. Jude radiothon volunteer is taking care of business, www.stjude.org], participating in annual radio fundraising radiothons that have raised about $300,000 every year. He has volunteered in both Chicago and Kentucky, helping coordinate volunteers, acting as the MC for the hospital’s golf outings and supporting on-air fundraising efforts. [ref: Miguel Esparza loves Cubs' Alex Bregman, Edward Cabrera additions, Marquee Sports Network - Home of the Cubs, Bears, Red Stars and Sky]

=== Honors and nominations ===
Esparza was part of the production team for Béisbol y Más, A Cubs radio production segment which received a Chicago/Midwest Emmy Award nomination in 2023 for Outstanding Achievement for Sports Interview. [ref: 2022–2023 Chicago/Midwest Emmy Nomination List, National Academy of Television Arts & Sciences Chicago/Midwest Chapter]

== Notable appearances ==
Esparza, who has also a singing background, has performed in the seventh-inning stretch at Wrigley Field and has sung the national anthem at various sporting events. [ref: Sports announcer Miguel Esparza becomes ‘Miguelvis’ on karaoke night, WGN-TV] Onstage, his performance name is "Miguelvis," since he enjoys singing Elvis Presley songs at bars around Chicago. [ref: Sports announcer Miguel Esparza becomes ‘Miguelvis’ on karaoke night, WGN-TV]

In May of 2026, Esparza performed outside Wrigley Field for a special Cubs concert with Grammy Award winners Montez de Durango [ref: Instagram, www.instagram.com], a Mexican band from Aurora, Illinois that specializes in the duranguense music genre.

He has become known as the Spanish-language voice of Chicago sports by local media and fans for his grand voice, positive presence and passion for the games. [ref: How a Humboldt Park native became a Spanish-language voice of Chicago sports - CBS Chicago, www.cbsnews.com]
