Through every project, every performance, Paul carried with him a quiet gratitude. Paul once said that "he would prefer not to have an audience applaud at the end of his performance, but to sit and listen to the stillness at the end of the performance that forms a valuable part of music". He had built a life from the very thing that had first captured his imagination as a boy, the mystery of sound. And though his achievements were many, his deepest satisfaction came not from what he had accomplished, but from the knowledge that his work continued to bring joy, learning, and reflection to others.  He had found his voice, not as an imitator of the great composers of the past, but as a continuation of their legacy. His music lives in the space between tradition and innovation, discipline and imagination, silence and song.

Listening to the music of Paul Kenny, and the simple act of sitting at a piano, offers something increasingly rare in today's fast-moving world, a gentle escape that is both deeply educational and wonderfully calming. There is a quiet magic in placing fingers on the keys and allowing sound to flow, where the mind shifts from chaos to clarity in a matter of moments. You feel the sound. You breathe it in. In this space, learning and relaxation exist side by side. Each phrase teaches, each harmony stimulates thought, yet the overall experience soothes the spirit, providing a peaceful pause from the noise of everyday life. Playing music expands the mind in ways few other activities can. It sharpens concentration, builds emotional awareness, and encourages creativity, all while drawing attention away from endless screens, notifications, and the constant demands of modern living. Even a few minutes at the piano can feel like stepping into a different world, one where time slows, breath deepens, and the heart finds rhythm again.  Paul remembers on numerous occasions where he lost track of time. He would drop our children off to school at 8:30am and be back home 10mins later and into the music recording studio. Only to look up at the clock and 6 hours had passed and it was time to pick up the boys from the local bus stop. Only music has the power to pause time.  And let's be honest, when life feels overwhelming, who has ever said, "I think I'll relax with a bit of algebra"?  Haha!!  Music, on the other hand, welcomes you in, wrapping you in melody and calm, proving that learning doesn't have to feel like work. Sometimes, the most powerful therapy isn't silence at all, it's a beautiful chord, a gentle tune, and the freedom to simply play.

The Educator and the Visionary By the time Paul began teaching at a Catholic College, he had already lived several musical lives, as a private music teacher, performer, composer, craftsman, and business leader. Yet in the classroom, among the energy of young minds and the unpolished enthusiasm of beginning musicians, he found something both humbling and renewing. Classroom teaching was not an interlude in his career, it was a culmination, after 40 years of private music teaching there was a place where his decades of experience found their truest purpose. The college, nestled in a region of shifting weather and constant songbirds, had always valued the arts. When Paul first stepped through its doors, he sensed both the potential and the silence waiting to be filled. Paul could almost hear what it could become... a place alive with sound, where students might discover the same wonder that had first awakened in him as a child beside that old piano. He listened to the students, to the teachers, to the ground and the building itself. Curriculum notes became living documents, written with purpose and creativity. Exercises once confined to rote memorization were transformed into explorations of melody and rhythm, guided by the conviction that understanding must always be accompanied by feeling. Over time, the change became tangible. Classrooms grew confident. The sound of scales gave way to ensemble rehearsals, laughter, experimentation. Students learned that music was not only an academic subject but a language of expression, a way of participating in something larger than themselves and it was fun to study music with Mr Kenny.

Paul's approach was never authoritarian; it was architectural. He built from the ground up, laying foundations in theory, harmony, and technique while leaving space for curiosity to grow. The workbooks and pages within he created found new life in the classroom, their pages marked by pencil smudges and insight. Each new cohort of students became both his audience and his collaborators. He knew that many of them would not go on to professional careers in music, and he was content with that. His goal was broader, to help them see that music, once understood, remains a lifelong companion. He often compared it to light, invisible until it touches something, then suddenly illuminating everything it meets. Under his guidance, concerts had grown from small assemblies into ambitious productions that combined student choirs, instrumental ensembles, and even orchestral arrangements. One such event, featuring a collaboration of players, college musicians, and a choir, stood as a symbol of what could be achieved when community and artistry merged. The forthcoming performance, already in rehearsal, carried that same spirit. It was to be a celebration of collaboration, a tapestry of sound woven from young enthusiasm and seasoned musicianship. Paul's music arrangement, carefully put together for accessible performance, served as the centrepiece: a reminder that classical music, when presented with care and heart, belongs to everyone.

His work at the college, though demanding, brought him profound satisfaction. The connections with other teachers in the college also gave him a sense of belonging. The daily rhythm of teaching, rehearsing, and composing became its own symphony. Each morning, as he prepared lesson plans or chatted with students and fellow teachers he felt a sense of continuity, that his life's threads had finally woven together. The technical, the managerial, and the creative no longer competed, they harmonized. However, Paul's world extended beyond the school gates. His personal compositions continued to develop, often written in the quiet hours of early morning or late night, when the day's noise had faded and reflection could begin. These new works were more contemplative, shaped by years of teaching and listening. They spoke of patience, of faith, of a deeper understanding of time. He also revisited older pieces, refining them with the same meticulous attention he brought to every aspect of his work. Projects like "Morning Mist (Dance with Me)", "Visions of Vienna" and "Pictures in My Mind" took on new resonance, their recordings and performances reaching audiences far beyond the classroom. Critics and listeners alike noted the maturity of tone, the clarity of purpose, hallmarks of an artist fully in command of his language. Despite his achievements, Paul remained grounded. Those who worked with him remarked not on his authority but on his humility. He approached his responsibilities with quiet steadiness, believing that leadership in the arts was less about control than cultivation. "You guide," he often said, "by listening first." His students saw in him not only a teacher but a living example of what it means to live a life through one's art. Many spoke of how his lessons extended beyond music: about perseverance, respect, and the courage to create. For some, he became the first adult to truly listen and recognize their creative potential. Every morning began with the excited sounds of students saying... "Good morning Mr Kenny". Paul's Mum once asked him if he sang along with everyone in the chapel at the college during services and hymns. I told her sometimes, however I'm usually at the piano or keyboard, doing what I've always done best. That's when she laughed and reminded Paul that his relationship with church music started very early... and very loudly. She said that Paul was the reason the family stopped attending the Anglican Church in Nambour on Queensland's Sunshine Coast, when Paul was about three or four years old. Whenever a hymn was announced, Paul would launch straight into it at full volume, not timidly, not cautiously, but with complete confidence and enthusiasm. Week after week, his small voice rang out over the congregation, utterly unaware of volume, blend, or social convention. After a while, Pauls Parents decided that perhaps everyone at church, including the priest, deserved a bit of peace. So they quietly gave church a miss. Looking back, it's hard not to smile at the idea that before Paul could read music, before he could reach the pedals of a piano, music was already insisting on being heard through me. Even then, Paul didn't just participate, he performed.

As the seasons turned and his music continued to thrive, Paul began to reflect more deeply on legacy. Not in the grand, historical sense, but in the human one, the simple, lasting imprint of having inspired others. He had spent a lifetime building bridges, between education and performance, between tradition and innovation, between thought and feeling. Now he saw that those bridges were being walked upon daily by his students.

The modern classical world, too, had come to recognize his music. His compositions were described as cinematic yet intimate, expressive yet grounded. They spoke to listeners who sought meaning in melody, who believed that beauty still mattered. Reviewers from the ABC and BBC classified his work within the modern classical genre, acknowledging both its accessibility and its sophistication. Still, Paul never composed for labels or praise. Never signed to any record label he continued to produce his music under his name or the name of his recording studio - Wilderness Studios Australia. His motivation remained what it had always been: the quiet calling of the piano, the mysterious conversation between heart, mind and sound. To create music was, for him, to participate in something sacred, not in a religious sense, but in the recognition that creation itself is an act of faith. He often thought back to his younger self, that boy sitting at a piano, discovering harmony by instinct. Decades later, the same wonder still lived within him. The notes had grown more refined, the harmonies more deliberate, but the essence remained unchanged. He was still listening to the world, to his students, to the unseen symphony that has guided his life.

The Quiet Maestro There are seasons of a musician's life that shape not just the work they create, but the person they become. For Paul, one such season was defined by a strange contrast, a life lived between two worlds that refused to match.  In one world, he was admired. In some places, he was loved. In others, he was revered. His music found its way into concert halls, churches, school assemblies, and recordings played in faraway places he had never visited. Students studied his scores with the same reverence they held for established classical composers. Teachers spoke warmly of him while audiences rose for standing ovations before the final note had fully faded. But in the other world, the world that should have been his safest, his gentlest, Paul often walked unseen. A far cry from his childhood where he was encouraged, listened to, and loved by his Parents and Grandparents.  As the child became a man, Paul's personal life was a quiet landscape, one where his presence was felt but not acknowledged, like a familiar painting hanging on a wall people had stopped noticing. His personal relationships over the years rarely asked about his work or took any interest in his music or the things that meant so much to Paul. His accomplishments, a source of pride, were met with indifference. His children seemed to drift in their own orbits, too caught up in screens, schedules, and the noise of modern life to realise the talent that lived under their roof. Sadly, during moments of self doubt and self worth, Paul would give himself a mark out of 100 at the end of every day to see if he would score enough to make it worth rising or continuing life the following morning. Slowly deducting points from 100 downward for negative things, negative words, but Paul never complained out loud. It wasn't in his nature. His heart had always been tuned more towards giving through the power of his music. He would always close up and withdraw into himself and his music.  But in the quiet hours of the night, when the rest of the house slept, he sometimes found himself pausing at life and the piano, resting his hands gently on the keys, and wondering what it might feel like to be truly seen, not by the world, but by the people he loved most. To be truly valued in his personal life was something he thought he would never see.  For years he had poured himself into his music, into teaching, into supporting others. His days were a rush of activity, arriving early to tune an ageing piano before class, helping nervous students find confidence at school or in their first recital, arranging music late into the evening for church or community performances, and still somehow finding time to smile at strangers, encourage colleagues, and help children who weren't his own to feel brave. Everyone else seemed to glow in his presence. Little did anyone know what was deeply buried in Paul's soul and becoming deeper as time moved on.  But the house he returned to each night felt oddly cold. He entered quietly, placing his keys on the counter so as not to disturb anyone. The house was often dim, lit only by the blue flicker of screens from closed rooms.  He prepared his 100 count during the night for the following day. And when they were all asleep, he sat at the piano and let his heart speak in a language no one in the house seemed to understand. His music was full of what he never voiced, loneliness, loyalty, resilience, love, and a silence that hurt more deeply than he cared to admit. Yet somehow, that silence shaped some of his greatest pieces. Outside, it was a different universe. People greeted him warmly at the shops. Students waved excitedly from across the school grounds. Parents thanked him for inspiring their children. Musicians messaged him from interstate and around the world asking for his advice or to look through some of their music arrangements. His mailbox is filled with invitations from festivals to concerts and performances. At the concert hall, audiences waited for him with quiet anticipation. Even before he sat down, even before he placed his hands on the keys, he could feel the room leaning toward him. And when he played, when he opened the gate to that world of shimmering notes and soft harmonies, the hall transformed. People cried from emotions. People held hands in joy. People closed their eyes in awe. His music reached them in places words could not. Music touching their inner being, their soul and opening doors to the essence of life.  In the community, he was a light. In his home, he felt like a ghost. One evening, after a demanding day, Paul returned home feeling particularly worn. His shoulders ached. His spirit felt heavy. The house was silent when he entered, the kind of silence that made him feel more alone than if it had been filled with shouting. He sat down at an upright piano the family has in the rumpus room. Its familiar creaks seemed to welcome him, recognising him in a way no human in the house had done before. Without planning to, he began to play a few single notes at first, which then a few extra notes joined in to create simple harmonies which then turned into the magic that Paul creates.  The piece that came out was unlike anything he had composed before, raw, unshielded, trembling with honesty. It was a confession in sound. Tones painted on the canvas of silence. Every unspoken disappointment, every invisible bruise, every moment he had been overlooked poured into the melody. It was a prayer, a lament, and a quiet victory all at once.  For the first time, his family truly heard their dad.  Not the background tinkling of a musician at practice, not the casual familiarity of someone who had grown up with a piano in the house, but the unmistakable brilliance of a master at work. The change did not happen overnight, but it began that very evening. In the days and weeks that followed, his children lingered in the doorway more often, listening. They began asking questions about his compositions and how a piano works, what inspired their dad's music, how he shaped melodies, what certain songs or phrases meant. Sometimes they tried to play by ear songs and themes and sometimes joining Paul in his music studio for a jam session with Paul on keyboard and the children playing drums or another keyboard. They asked if they could attend his next concert. They even asked if he could teach them a piece. Slowly and gently, they began to recognise the depth of the man they lived with, his skill, his kindness, his quiet pain, and his immense generosity of spirit. The man they call...  Dad.  His partner, hesitant but curious, came to one of his community performances with their children not long after. She slipped in quietly with the boys taking a seat, thinking no one would notice. But she noticed something instead. The way the audience leaned forward as Paul walked onstage. The way people whispered with admiration. The way his students and piano tuning clients sat proudly in the front row, eyes glowing with excitement. And the way the hall erupted into applause before he even touched the keys. When Paul began to play and chat with his audience, the room transformed. His partner had forgotten this version of him which drew them together many years ago, the power, the beauty, the emotional honesty. She found herself clapping at the end of every piece, harder than she expected, tears burning at the edges of her eyes. It was the first time in a long time she truly saw her partner and what he was capable of. The family did not suddenly become perfect. Life never works that way. But something softened. Paul began to hear genuine "How was your day?" in the evenings. His children started attending rehearsal, performances and productions and even wanting to go to the college he taught at to spend the day in his music class.  His partner offered cups of tea while he composed, arranged and recorded music late into the night. The coldness in the house did not disappear, it melted slowly, like frost melting in the morning sun. And for the first time in many years, Paul felt something warm returning to the centre of his life. Not applause. Not admiration. Not recognition. But a truer sense of belonging.

The Maestro Finds Peace The community continues to adore him. The world continues to listen to his music. Students continue to cherish every lesson he gives. But now, when Paul returns home, he no longer feels invisible. He feels valued. He feels understood. He feels loved, quietly, imperfectly, but genuinely. He had always been the Maestro to the world. Now, at last, he was becoming someone cherished at home.

The Magic of Nature's Light There are moments in life when nature reveals something so extraordinary that it feels as though the world has briefly opened a doorway into another realm. We often rush through our days, surrounded by the wonders of the natural world, yet every now and then we are gifted with a moment so rare and beautiful that it stays with us forever. Driving through the Tasmanian landscape from Penguin towards Smithton on a soft, misty rainy day, Paul found himself surrounded by the ancient beauty of the forest. The towering gum trees stood on either side of the road, their silhouettes rising through the gentle rain, creating a scene that felt almost timeless. Near Black River on Tasmania's North West Coast with the forest embracing the road, something truly magical began to unfold. In the distance, a rainbow appeared, faint at first, almost hidden within the mist and rain. As Paul continued driving, the rainbow seemed to move closer and closer, until suddenly Paul found himself travelling directly into its path. The colours were no longer just in the sky, they were on the road ahead, stretching across the landscape as if Paul was approaching the very end of the rainbow itself. Then came a moment Paul will never forget. The beams of coloured light rose over the bonnet of the car, flowing through the windscreen and through the glass roof above me. The entire interior of the vehicle became illuminated with soft streams of colour with shades of violet, blue, green, yellow and red dancing through the space around me. It felt as though nature itself had reached inside and painted the world with light. For those few moments, it was more than just a rainbow. It felt like a glimpse of something deeper and a reminder of the mystery, beauty and wonder that exists all around us. Almost like beams of heavenly light shining through the Tasmanian wilderness, it was a once-in-a-lifetime encounter with the magic of nature. The world is full of these hidden miracles. Sometimes we are lucky enough to witness one, and when we do, it reminds us that there is still enchantment and mystery  in the world and that beauty can appear unexpectedly, on an ordinary road, on an ordinary day, and transform it into something unforgettable.

Covid November 2020 was a strange and heavy time for the world, with the shadow of the Covid virus still hanging over everyday life. Just as things began to edge back towards some sense of normality and schools reopened, there came a walk-a-thon at the school his children attended, a fairly simple idea encouraging students to walk a kilometre with their family each afternoon and record it on a chart. It was harmless and a fun family way to do something together in the afternoon and to shine a little light to take away the dark cloudy days that Covid had turned the world into. So that's what we did. On the way to school that morning they set the odometer in the car and measured half a kilometre which then meant they could walk to the mark and return and the total was then one kilometre. But when they returned through the front gates that afternoon, everything changed. Without warning, Paul froze, hunched over in agony, a crushing pain gripping his chest so fiercely he couldn't move. The world slowed, blurred, and in that moment, fear quietly replaced what was a fun family time after the Covid lockdown.  Paul soon found himself in the emergency department of the local hospital, where everything seemed to spiral from concern into a very serious situation. What began as confusion and pain quickly turned into the frightening reality of a heart attack.  In a twist that bordered on absurd, the hospital discharged Paul only hours later with instructions to undertake a stress test. Paul's partner, Claire, a very experienced emergency nurse with over 25 years of nursing experience, clearly sensing the ridiculousness of the situation, suggested that Paul perform his own stress test at home. So, Paul went for a gentle walk up the top paddock on their property to check out their bee hives. He barely made it halfway before another wave of crushing pain hit, another heart attack bringing Paul to the ground. This earned Paul an unplanned but very real ambulance ride straight back to the emergency department that he had only been discharged from a few hours earlier. Over coming weeks it seemed to be one comical event after another dealing with the health system and trying to get answers to what the problem was. He is still none the wiser.  News travels fast in small communities, and within days a Facebook post appeared explaining what had happened. A neighbour who lives half a kilometre down the road later said he had driven past at the very moment Paul collapsed, seeing him hunched over with the boys gathered around. He genuinely thought they were all trying to catch jack jumper ants or they had dropped something and were looking for it, a surreal and almost comical misinterpretation of a moment that was anything but. In the midst of the fear, confusion, and frustration, there was also an odd clarity, a stark reminder of mortality, vulnerability, and just how fragile the fine thread of everyday life can truly be.

== A Modern Vision of Beethoven's Für Elise ==

Paul Kenny, acclaimed Australian pianist and composer, has breathed new life into one of the world's most beloved piano pieces—Beethoven's Für Elise. His 2023/2024 arrangement reimagines the timeless classic with a fresh harmonic palette, cinematic textures, and the emotional depth that has become a hallmark of his work. In Paul's hands, this familiar melody is transformed from a simple romantic miniature into a sweeping, contemporary masterpiece that bridges past and present. The original Für Elise has long held a special place in Paul's heart. Like many pianists, it was one of the first pieces he played as a child, yet he always sensed a hidden beauty beneath its simplicity, an untapped emotional landscape waiting to be explored. His new arrangement began as a quiet tribute to Beethoven's genius, but soon evolved into something much larger, a conversation across centuries between two composers who share a deep understanding of the piano's expressive soul. Paul's 2023/2024 version preserves the purity of Beethoven's melody while surrounding it with lush, modern harmonies and impressionistic colour. The left-hand accompaniment flows with fluid arpeggios and shifting tonalities, giving the piece a dreamlike atmosphere. Subtle jazz inflections and cinematic chord progressions create moments of surprise and wonder, inviting listeners to hear the familiar tune as if for the first time. In performance, Paul's interpretation is breathtaking. His control of tone and dynamics allows the music to shimmer between tenderness and grandeur. The opening theme, delicately voiced, feels like a whisper from another time, while the climactic passages surge with radiant intensity. Audiences have described his rendition as "hauntingly beautiful," "transcendent," and "a stunning fusion of classical elegance and modern emotion."

What makes Paul Kenny's Für Elise so captivating is not just its technical brilliance but its sincerity. It is both homage and reinvention, a love letter to Beethoven and to the enduring power of melody itself. The arrangement embodies Paul's musical philosophy, that great music is timeless, capable of speaking anew to each generation. By bringing Für Elise to life in 2024, Paul Kenny has created more than a reinterpretation, he has crafted a musical reflection on beauty, memory, and evolution. It stands as a testament to his artistry, deeply respectful of tradition, yet unafraid to imagine what classical music can become in the modern world.

data.title: Yves Gaspar
data.text:
Yves Francesco Jeanne-Maria Gaspar is a physicist and researcher whose work focuses on mathematical cosmology [ref: Gaspar Yves (Catholic University, Milan) – “Time, between Mathematics and Physics” – Centre for Philosophy of Time], general relativity, gravitational physics, dynamical systems [ref: Late-time asymptotic dynamics of Bianchi VIII cosmologies, Classical and Quantum Gravity], and the conceptual foundations of physics. [ref: Randomness in Philosophy and Theology, Faraday Institute for Science and Religion] [ref: Gaspar, l'astrofisico belga che ha scelto Tregnago per amore, L'Arena] [ref: Realtà computabili: prospettive e limiti - Vatican News, Vatican News] He is a Visiting Scholar at St Edmund's College, University of Cambridge, and has been a professor with the Department of Mathematics and Physics of the Catholic University of the Sacred Heart in Brescia, Italy. [ref: "Un mondo improbabile", mistero di un universo sintonizzato, UCCR] His research has been published in Classical and Quantum Gravity, Foundations of Science and General Relativity and Gravitation.

== Education and career ==
Gaspar studied physics at the University of Liège in Belgium from 1990 to 1995, specializing in relativity and cosmology. He subsequently completed the Certificate of Advanced Studies in Mathematics, Part III of the Mathematical Tripos, at the University of Cambridge in1997. [ref: Dr Yves Gaspar, Faraday Institute for Science and Religion] He received his PhD from Cambridge in 2002 under the supervision of physicist John D. Barrow. His doctoral research examined the late-time behaviour of Bianchi type VIII cosmological models and resulted in the thesis Late-time behaviour of General Solutions to the Einstein Field Equations. [ref: Yves Gaspar - The Mathematics Genealogy Project, www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu] [ref: ]

Gaspar has taught cosmology and astrophysics at the Catholic University of the Sacred Heart in Brescia, including in its master's program in mathematics and physics. Since 2016, he has worked as a physics examiner and moderator for Cambridge Assessment International Education. [ref: Leonardo Da Vinci oltre le sue invenzioni, AllTopNetwork]

In 2020, Gaspar became a Visiting Research Scholar at St Edmund's College, Cambridge, where he is currently listed as a Visiting Scholar. [ref: Ci si può fidare della scienza?, Fondazione Toniolo Verona] His research has included cosmology and questions concerning randomness and uncomputability, including their implications for philosophy and theology.

== Research ==
Gaspar's early research concerned exact solutions of the Einstein field equations and the dynamics of homogeneous cosmological models. With John D. Barrow, he studied the late-time behaviour of Bianchi type VIII models, including whether chaotic behaviour occurring near an initial singularity persists during later cosmic evolution. Their findings were published in Classical and Quantum Gravity in 2001. [ref: Bianchi VIII empty futures, Classical and Quantum Gravity]

His subsequent work examined time asymmetry and chaotic behaviour in general relativity. In a 2004 paper in General Relativity and Gravitation, Gaspar investigated the late-time evolution of Bianchi VIII models and differences between approaches to their asymptotic behaviour. [ref: Time Asymmetry and Chaos in General Relativity, General Relativity and Gravitation]

Gaspar has also investigated complexity and unpredictability in gravitational systems. In Gravity and Complexity co-authored with Giovanni Acquaviva, he considered whether certain dynamical systems associated with the Einstein field equations could exhibit forms of unpredictability stronger than conventional chaos and whether some of their properties could be formally undecidable. [ref: Gravity and complexity, The European Physical Journal Plus]

His later research has increasingly incorporated philosophy of science and cosmology. With Paweł Tambor, he published The Laws of Nature and the Problems of Modern Cosmology in Foundations of Science, Springer Nature, examining the concept of natural laws in relation to modern cosmology, complex systems, time, causality, and the limits of mathematical descriptions. [ref: The Laws of Nature and the Problems of Modern Cosmology, Foundations of Science]  In 2025, Gaspar published the book (Cosmology Research – Addressing Current Problems with Astrophysics, Eds. Michael L. Smith and A. M. Mecit Ӧztas, IntechOpen, London, UK, 2025) chapter The Problems of Modern Cosmology, the Fine Tuning of Constants and Parameters, and the Notion of Time, which discusses unresolved problems in cosmology and questions concerning time, fundamental constants, initial conditions, and the limits of mathematical approaches to physical phenomena. He tried to show why mathematics has, in particular, difficulties with the concept of time, by reconsidering some simple foundational aspects of set theory. [ref: ]

Vučić was born in Mostar in 1995. [ref: Nikola Vučić, Labinovacija] He studied comparative literature and completed a master's degree in sociology at the University of Sarajevo. [ref: Završni radovi / Master teza ODSJEKA SOCIOLOGIJA (3+2), Faculty of Political Sciences, University of Sarajevo]

Vučić has worked as a reporter, editor and presenter at N1 and is associated with the programme Izvan okvira. data.title: Nate Isaacman
data.text:
----

Nate Isaacman (October 14, 1898 – November 22, 1957), also known by the ring names Joe McCabe and Joe Isaacman, was an American professional boxer from Dauphin County, Pennsylvania. He competed in regional lightweight and welterweight divisions during the 1910s and 1920s.

== Early life ==

Nate Isaacman was born in Dauphin County, Pennsylvania. He was raised in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, where his family resided on Conoy Street. Prior to and during the early stages of his boxing career, he was employed locally as a railroad laborer for the Pennsylvania Railroad.

He grew up in Harrisburg, was a dancer and an athlete. Dancing led him to take his dancing talents into the boxing ring.

== Boxing career ==
Nate Isaacman competed primarily in Pennsylvania and regional East Coast venues, securing wins across professional bouts. His most high profile bouts were against Tim Droney, Jack Silver and Jack Stone.

Nate Isaacman fought a lot over a nine-year boxing career. In June 1918 he fought Sammy Schiff in Harrisburg. Here is information on fights under his birth name Nate Isaacman as shown in BoxRec.

In 1919 Nate Isaacman fought Bobby Williams at the Power Motive show. [ref: Nate Isaacman fights Bobby Williams at the Power Motive Show, Harrisburg Telegraph]

In 1922 Joe McCabe won a bout in Philadelphia. [ref: JOE McCABE WINS, Philadelphia Evening Public Ledger]

In 1923 Nate Isaacman fought and won against Tim Droney. [ref: Tim Droney Loses to Joe McCabe, Philadelphia Inquirer]

He fought the lightweight champion of the West Coast in 1923 in the Oakland, California Coliseum. He lost.

Nate Isaacman fought in the west coast in the Bay Area, as shown in this article, Geo. Gilmore, fought with Joe McCabe who had previously lost in a fight. [ref: Joe McCabe returns to box Geo. Gilmore, Oakland Tribune]

Though it was expected that he would win, from the fights in Oakland, later he lost the title as shown in the Oakland Tribune, March 6, 1924. [ref: Joe McCabe Can Claim Welterweight Title, Oakland Tribune]

There were fights that he won in California, such as the fight against Jack Powell. [ref: Sports Told in Paragraphs, The Bakersfield Californian]

== Personal life ==

After his boxing days were over, he got married, fathered five children: Miriam, Sylvia, Eileen, Max and Terri.

== Later life and death ==

Following his retirement from sports, Isaacman continued working as a laborer. He died on November 22, 1957, at Harrisburg State Hospital.

== Melvyn Wilkes ==

=== Professional Biography ===
Melvyn Wilkes is a British-born, Australian based football (soccer) coach, sporting director, coach educator, and youth development specialist. His professional career encompasses football coaching, academy management, technical direction, and the development of international pathways for aspiring professional players. Wilkes has worked in youth coaching and development roles associated with English football clubs including Manchester City FC, West Bromwich Albion FC, and Nottingham Forest FC. His professional background also includes coach education at Manchester Metropolitan University and work connected with England's Football Association and Professional Footballers' Association.

Sunshine Coast Fire

+1

In Australia, Wilkes has been closely associated with Sunshine Coast FC, where he has held senior positions including Technical Director, Football Operations Manager, Sporting Director, and Global Operations Manager.

His work has concentrated on developing structured football academies, improving coaching standards, establishing pathways from youth to senior football, and connecting Australian footballers with international opportunities.

Coaching and academy development experience associated with Manchester City, Nottingham Forest, and West Bromwich Albion, Crewe Alexandra and Port Vale. The club's 2014 announcement also records a Coach Education Manager role at Manchester Metropolitan University, as well as the being a licensed Coach educator for the English FA and delivered for the English Professional Footballers Association (PFA).

Announced in February 2014. Responsible for the complete coaching set-up and recruitment of junior and senior players for the newly franchised Goulburn Valley Suns, based in Shepparton, Victoria as Technical Advisor. Wilkes oversaw the first 6 games of the NPL Victoria senior mens competition, whilst also being instrumental in the set-up of the whole academy program. Wilkes departed the club in may 2014, due to the clubs inability to secure an appropriate working visa.

Resigned in June 2017 after approximately two and a half years as Technical Director, due to personal family reasons back in his native United Kingdom. The club credited his tenure with overseeing the selection of almost 100 players for representative football. Wilkes still continued to assist the club whilst in the UK.

Sunshine Coast FC 'Fire

2017

Return to Technical Director and Football Operations Manager

Reappointed in December 2017 after a small period overseas, and was instrumental in the club obtaining a Skill Acquisition Program (SAP) license, which had eluded the club since 2013.

== Establishment of Australia's First Full-Time Youth Football Academy Outside the A-League (2019–Present) ==
From 2019, Melvyn Wilkes played an instrumental role in the creation, development and implementation of what Sunshine Coast FC describes as Australia's only full-time youth football academy operating outside the A-League system.

The initiative represented a significant development in Australian youth football, introducing a professional academy structure modelled on the elite youth development systems used by professional football clubs in the United Kingdom.

Unlike traditional Australian semi-professional youth football programs, which generally operate through evening training sessions and weekend fixtures, the Sunshine Coast FC academy was designed to integrate full-time football training with formal academic education.

Sunshine Coast FC 'Fire

An extensive feature examined his role in reshaping Sunshine Coast FC's youth academy, club culture, and player-development model.

Announced as Global Operations Manager and Sporting Director for 2024. Media coverage also documented the club's plans to establish UK youth competition pathways.

Global Academy and Operations Leadership

Identified in club and educational partner materials as Sporting Director and Global Operations Manager, with a focus on Australian–UK academy pathways and the integration of academic education with elite football training in both Australia and the UK.

== Coaching philosophy and areas of expertise ==
Published interviews and club statements identify several recurring principles in Wilkes' coaching and football-development approach.

* Player development: Preparing young footballers for progression into professional and senior competition.
* Coach education: Improving coaching standards through structured learning, mentoring, and continuing professional development.
* Academy management: Creating integrated development systems rather than operating isolated age-group teams.
* International pathways: Providing Australian players with access to competitive football environments in the United Kingdom.
* Education and sport: Combining high-performance training with formal schooling and athlete welfare.

data.title: Padel Pingpong
data.text:
----

Padel Pingpong was invented in Sweden in 2020. As the name indicates Padel Pingpong is a racket sport that combines influences from table tennis and padel tennis. [ref: Padel Pingpong, Padel Pingpong] It all started during an after work where Magnus Willner and Erik Magnarsson played table tennis in a conference room and the walls came into use. [ref: Jörgen Persson bakom ny sport – lanserar padelpingis, Hallandsposten] A company named Padel Pingpong International AB was later founded to develop the concept. Cofounders are Johan Edfors, professional golfer and Jörgen Persson professional table tennis player, amongst a couple of others.

== The Court and equipment ==
The court is made up by a rectangular box, made of security glass measuring 3.208 by 6.100 m and 2.075 m high. The short sides have a 17 degree angle to make the ball bounce back easier. In the middle of the court is a table (measuring 1.45 by 2.44 meters). The table has rounded corners designed to easier move around inside the court and to avoid injuries. [ref: Padel Pingpong, Padel Pingpong]

The ball is 55 mm in diameter (compared to a table tennis ball that is normally 40 mm in diameter) and the rackets are made of wood or plastic without friction (meaning no spin). The net measures 21 cm in hight. [ref: Padel Pingpong, Padel Pingpong]

== Rules ==
The game has influences from other racket sports when it comes to the rules like using the walls as in padel tennis. Also the counting, first to 11 points in each set wins, like in table tennis. But it also has it's own rules ie. the possibillity to gain bonus points within a rally and not being allowed to smash the ball out of the cage. [ref: Padel Pingpong, Padel Pingpong]

== International expansion ==
Padel Pingpong has received millions of views across social media platforms, including Tiktok and Instagram. [ref: Padel Pingpong on Tiktok, Tiktok] [ref: Padel Pingpong on Instagram, Instagram]

The sport has also been promoted through international events such as Waldner cup in Oslo and The 2023 European Table Tennis Championship in Malmö. [ref: Padel Pingpong on Pingispågarna youtubechannel, YouTube] [ref: Padel Pingpong, Padel Pingpong]

By 2026 the sport is available in 16 countries. [ref: Padel Pingpong, Padel Pingpong]

== Media ==

United States

The recording of the Padel Pingpong Championship has been broadcasted on several occasions on ESPN networks, including ESPN2 and ESPN8. [ref: Padel Pingpong Championship, Disney+] [ref: ESPN. "Padel Pingpong Championship (7/18/26)." Broadcast on ESPNNews. First streamed on July 18, 2026. Link originally available on WatchESPN.] [ref: ESPN. "Padel Pingpong Championship (10/19/25)." Broadcast on ESPNNews. First streamed on October 19, 2025. Link originally available on WatchESPN.] [ref: ESPN Deportes. "Padel Pingpong Championship (2/14/26)." Transmitido por primera vez el 14 de febrero de 2026 en ESPNNews. Enlace originalmente disponible en ESPN Deportes.]

Sweden

Hallandsposten wrote an article in 2022 when the first prototypes got in place and the sport was launched. Jörgen Persson and Johan Edfors, both from the region Halland, was interviewed and it was mentioned in the text that the idea of the concept came from an afterwork where Magnus Willner and Erik Magnarsson played table tennis using the walls. [ref: Jörgen Persson bakom ny sport – lanserar padelpingis, Hallandsposten]

Italy

The concept was shown on a large and popular Italian show named Tú Sí Que Vales in 2024, giving a larger audience a glance of the sport. [ref: Vincenzo, Matteo, Cristian, Adam – Prima puntata]

data.title: Ahmed Kheireddine
data.text:
Ahmed Kheireddine was a tunisian poet and writer that was born on 1905 in Tunis and passed away on 25 of July 1967.

== Biography ==

Being the son of a Tunisian merchant, he was the great-son of Kheireddiene Kahia. He completed his studies at Zitouna and became a teacher at a nearby school. His dedication to literature and associations with literary circles led him to him to eventually join in the newly founded Arabic language department of the national radio station. He became a lyricist for several radio plays, such as the renowned Haj Klouf, which was broadcasted during the holy month of ramdan. He also wrote for artists associated with The Rachidia, a respected musical institution, notably for the artists Khemais Tarnane and Hedi Jouini.

According to the maestro Salah El Mahdi, Kheireddine was allegedly on of the original composers of the melody for Humat Al-Hima, the current Tunisian national anthem. [ref: Tunisia – nationalanthems.info]

data.title: Woohoo (TV channel)
data.text:
----

Woohoo It's a brazilian Pay television channel aimed at action sports, eletcronic games, music and young behavior. In Portugal, it was launched at the beginning of 2013 exclusively on ZON.

== History ==

Woohoo debuted in May 2006 on Pay television. [ref: Woohoo celebrates its 15th anniversary in May with new features and a special program., TELA VIVA News] It was the first channel in Latin America dedicated to action sports, music and young behavior. In november 2006, Woohoo join to Turner's family channels with Cartoon Network, TNT, CNN, Boomerang and others. [ref: Woohoo secures partnership., Waves] In october 2010, the broadcaster also launched a new graphic design. [ref: Woohoo renews its visual and conceptual identity and premieres new programs., TELA VIVA News] In 2011, the canal firmed a collab with Stenna Internacional, searching for growing your presence in the pay television operators. [ref: Woohoo resumes content management and transfers distribution to Media Mundi., TELA VIVA News]

In august 14, 2013, the channel leave the partnership with Turner, vising obtaining the channel classification "superbrazilian". [ref: [http://natelinha.ne10.uol.com.br/noticias/2013/08/17/canal-woohoo-se-desliga-da-turner-para-cumprir-nova-lei-da-tv-paga-64959.php Woohoo channel separates from Turner to comply with new pay TV law.]] As the part of changes, in august 18 2014, the channel launched the new logo, in addition to reformulating the entire grid, switching to showing foreign series as Ideal and Younger.

In May 2020, the channel became entirely managed by Stenna Internacional, being chaired by Carolina Vargas, expanding the partnership established in 2011. On October 15 2022. [ref: Woohoo ends agreement with Stenna and regains control of the channel., Minha Operadora]

In February 2023, the channel presents to the public the concept that would become their new logo and broadcast live the Apex Legends World Championship, marking the first rumors of a new restructuring in the schedule. [ref: UPDATED: Woohoo channel will undergo changes and transform into a geek channel., WDN Brasil] In April, the Woohoo channel became owned by 100% to the holding company Brickto Games. With this, the broadcaster began to invest Completely geek and gamer content, following in the footsteps of PlayTV between the years 2006 and 2020, and, subsequently from 2023, and from Loading between 2020 and 2021. The goal of the channel It's about embracing the online gaming community and pop culture. In the same month, The broadcaster announced new programs, presenters and themes who went on to occupy the grid programming. These changes reflect the commitment from the broadcaster in providing Quality content for your target audience. Along with the changes. [ref: Woohoo receives a R$ 50 million investment and becomes a channel dedicated to games and the geek universe., NaTelinha] [ref: Woohoo launches TV channel focused on the gamer and geek universe., propmark.com.br]

data.title: Evgeniy Puzyrevskiy
data.text:
Evgeniy Puzyrevskiy (; born 17 February 1987) is a film director and screenwriter, best known for the interactive film She Sees Red (2019) and the television series Crazy House (2023) and My Friend AI (2026).

== Early life and education ==
Puzyrevskiy was born in Weimar, East Germany, where his father was serving in the military, and moved to Russia before the age of one. He grew up in Kamyshlov, Sverdlovsk Oblast, and studied for three years at the Sverdlovsk Regional College of Arts and Culture in Yekaterinburg. He has no formal film education and is self-taught. In Moscow he directed commercials and music videos (including for Oleg Gazmanov and the band Torba-na-Kruche) and worked in the DVD stores Novoe Iskusstvo and Mir Kino.

== Career ==
=== Short films ===
Puzyrevskiy began with short films. He Was His Friend (2015), which he wrote and directed, won the Audience Award for Best Long Form Narrative Short at the Nevermore Film Festival and the Masters of Genre award at the Lublin Film Festival, and was one of five Russian short films presented by ROSKINO in the Global Russians programme at the 2016 Cannes Film Festival. [ref: LXIX Cannes Film Festival, ROSKINO] The film stars Sergey Pokhodaev, Kirill Polukhin and Ivan Mulin.

His horror short Mom Is Always There for You (2016) stars Angelina Strechina and Denis Shvedov. Underwater (2018), starring Ksenia Radchenko in the lead role, was nominated for Best Short Film at the Boca do Inferno festival in Brazil.

=== She Sees Red ===
In 2019 Puzyrevskiy wrote and directed She Sees Red (), an interactive thriller developed by Rhinotales and described by Rossiyskaya Gazeta as the first interactive film in Russia. [ref: «Она сердится»: первый российский интерактивный триллер, Rossiyskaya Gazeta] The film was released on Steam, GOG, PlayStation, Nintendo Switch, Xbox, iOS and Android, with a full English dub and subtitles in 19 languages. It was included in the Los Angeles Times list of "8 defining interactive TV games" (2020) [ref: Schlocky ‘Night Trap’ to absurdly fun ‘Kimmy Schmidt’: 8 defining interactive TV games, Los Angeles Times] and in Polygons selection of indie gems (2019). [ref: Buried treasure: Unearthing the hidden indie gems from beneath the sea of games, Polygon] On Steam it holds a "Very Positive" rating, with 78% of more than 3,100 user reviews positive. [ref: She Sees Red on SteamDB, SteamDB]

=== Television ===
In 2023 Puzyrevskiy directed the comedy series Crazy House (), produced by the Tritamata creative bureau for the Friday! channel and Premier; the series starred Aleksey Maklakov, Denis Kosyakov, Anna Kotova-Deryabina, Dmitry Lysenko, Roman Kurtsyn, Alyona Yakovleva and Elena Simonova. The same year he directed the pilot episode of the series Chef (), presented at the Pilot television festival. In 2024 he served as creative producer on the series Teenagers in Space ().

His series My Friend AI (), released in 2026 on Okko and Wink, was made by the creators of the series Difficult Teenagers (). [ref: Смотрим трейлер сериала «Мой друг ИИ», Sobaka.ru] It stars Kai Getz, Svyatoslav Rogozhan, Mariya Markova, Oleg Vereshchagin and Ekaterina Morgunova.

=== Other work ===
Puzyrevskiy is the author of the novel The Seventh Summer (, 2012); an audiobook version, narrated by Alexander Vodianoy, is available on LitRes.

Since 2021 he has hosted the YouTube programme Zapakh napalma po utram (, "The Smell of Napalm in the Morning"), in which film-industry professionals discuss films from the perspective of their crafts; guests have included visual effects supervisor Arman Yakhin, director Roman Karimov and director Viktor Shamirov.

He has been a member of the Directors' Guild of Russia since 13 June 2023.

data.title: Gary Meier Goal keeper
data.text:
----

Gary Meier (born 10 September 1955) is an Australian former soccer player who played as a goalkeeper. He spent his entire senior career with Sydney Olympic FC (originally known as Pan-Hellenic), and holds the club's record for most appearances. He was capped once for the Australian national team in 1978. [ref: Former Roos receive caps, FTBL]

== Club career ==
Meier joined Pan-Hellenic, later renamed Sydney Olympic, in the early 1970s. He was in goal for Sydney Olympic during the club's first season in the National Soccer League in 1977, including a 2–0 win over Brisbane Lions at Perry Park on 25 April 1977. [ref: NSL 1977 Round 4, OzFootball] In 1978 he made 24 appearances in all competitions and kept four clean sheets. [ref: 1978 Sydney Olympic FC season, Wikipedia]

Meier played for Sydney Olympic until 1994, making 412 appearances, a club record. [ref: Sydney Olympic FC, Wikipedia] He won the NSL Cup with the club in 1983 and 1985. [ref: Gary Meier, worldfootball.net] He is a member of the Sydney Olympic Hall of Fame.

After leaving Sydney Olympic, Meier played for Killarney District Soccer Club on the Central Coast. [ref: Gary Meier, National Football Teams]

== International career ==
Meier earned one cap for Australia, becoming Socceroo No. 276. He came on as a 66th-minute substitute in a 1–1 friendly draw against Greece in Sydney on 18 June 1978. [ref: Socceroo caps, OzFootball]

== Coaching career ==
Meier briefly managed Sydney Olympic in 1995. [ref: Gary Meier, worldfootball.net]

data.title: Yang Jung-won
data.text:
----

Yang Jung-won (Korean: 양정원; born February 9, 2004), known mononymously as Jungwon, is a South Korean singer, dancer, and the leader of the K-pop boy band Enhypen. Appointed to the leadership role at age 16, he drew media attention for being one of the youngest group leaders in the music industry. [ref: Youngest leaders taking charge in K-pop industry, The Korea Herald]

== Early life and education ==
Jungwon practiced Taekwondo for seven years prior to his training in the entertainment industry. [ref: Jungwon Weverse Magazine Interview, Weverse Magazine] He attended Namgang High School before transferring to Hanlim Multi Art School, where he graduated from the Department of Practical Dance in February 2023. He trained under SM Entertainment and Big Hit Music before joining Belift Lab.

== Career ==
=== 2020–present: Debut with Enhypen ===
In June 2020, Jungwon was introduced as a contestant on the reality survival competition show I-Land, created by CJ ENM and Big Hit Entertainment. [ref: 'I-LAND' unveils full lineup of 23 trainees, Newsen] During the live finale on September 18, 2020, he placed first in the global viewer voting with 1,417,620 votes, securing his spot in the final lineup of the boy band Enhypen. [ref: 'Global fan-made band' Enhypen debuts with album 'Border: Day One', Korea JoongAng Daily]

Following a comprehensive 40-day selection process that included interviews with staff and members, Jungwon was officially announced as the leader of the group on November 13, 2020. [ref: Enhypen selects Jungwon as group leader, newsen] Appointed to the position at 16 years old, his selection drew significant media attention as it made him one of the youngest group leaders in modern K-pop history, leading a team where the majority of the members were older than him. [ref: Jungwon chosen as leader, The Korea Herald]

=== Other activities ===
==== Hosting ====
Beyond his group activities, Jungwon has taken on solo hosting responsibilities. He served as a regular radio host (MC) for the Educational Broadcasting System (EBS) program Listen, co-hosting the weekly broadcast alongside fellow group member Sunoo. [ref: ENHYPEN Jungwon and Sunoo selected as new DJs for EBS radio 'Listen', Ilsan Sports]

==== Ambassadorships ====
On April 17, 2026, the Seoul Metropolitan Government officially appointed Yang Jungwon as an honorary ambassador for the 2026 Seoul International Garden Show held at Seoul Forest. [ref: Enhypen's Jungwon named honorary ambassador for Seoul International Garden Show, Korea JoongAng Daily] [ref: Enhypen's Jungwon named ambassador for Seoul International Garden Show, The Korea Herald] His appointment was heavily publicized due to his name being a homonym for the Korean word for "garden" (jeongwon). In this civic role, he was tasked with promoting urban sustainability and green initiatives through promotional videos and public audio guides for visitors.

As a member of Enhypen, Jungwon has also participated in several major global group brand ambassadorships, including Italian luxury fashion house Prada, Dunkin' Philippines, and Samyang Foods' MEP ramyeon campaign.

==== Recording Academy membership ====
In July 2025, Jungwon was invited to join The Recording Academy as a voting member for its 2025 class, granting voting rights for the 68th Annual Grammy Awards. [ref: Recording Academy Welcomes New Member Class Of 2025, The Recording Academy] [ref: Hybe CEO Lee Jae-sang named professional member of The Recording Academy, The Korea Herald] [ref: 16 K-pop artists, producers under HYBE added to Grammy Awards voting members list, Korea JoongAng Daily] The Academy highlighted his artistic contributions as a singer, dancer, and leader of Enhypen, alongside his budding songwriting work on tracks such as "Highway 1009" and "Hundred Broken Hearts."

data.title: 2026 Indiana Hoosiers men's soccer team
data.text:
The 2026 Indiana Hoosiers men's soccer team represent Indiana University for the 2026 NCAA Division I men's soccer season. The Hoosiers are led by head coach Todd Yeagley, in his 18th season. They play their home games at Bill Armstrong Stadium in Bloomington, Indiana.

== Background ==
The Hoosiers finished the 2025 season 12–6–1 overall and 5–5–0 in the 2025 Big Ten Conference men's soccer season. They lost to 21st ranked Saint Louis 0-1 in the first round of the 2025 NCAA Division I men's soccer tournament, losing a 10-season streak of making the round of 16 of the tournament. [ref: Indiana men’s soccer ends season with 1-0 loss to Saint Louis in NCAA Tournament, Indiana Daily Student]

data.title: Go Brewing
data.text:
Go Brewing is an American brewery in Naperville, Illinois, that produces only non-alcoholic beer. It was described at its opening as the first brewery in Illinois dedicated to non-alcoholic and low-alcohol beer. [ref: Go Brewing opening state's first nonalcoholic, low-alcohol brewery in Naperville, Daily Herald]

== History ==
Go Brewing was founded by Joe Chura. [ref: An entrepreneur finds a niche in high-quality no-alcohol beer, Crain's Chicago Business] [ref: Down to Business: Naperville's Go Brewing finds its niche by tapping into audience that wants beer taste, no alcohol, Naperville Sun] Its taproom opened on October 15, 2022. [ref: Naperville's Go Brewing Opens for Business on Oct. 15, NCTV17] The brewery operates a taproom in Naperville that serves only non-alcoholic beer. [ref: Dry January, not Beerless January, at Go Brewing in Naperville, Chicago Sun-Times] [ref: A Naperville Taproom Is Changing the Way Customers Think About Nonalcoholic Beer, Eater Chicago]

Go began distributing outside Illinois in 2023 and 2024, including Wisconsin [ref: Nonalcoholic brewery Go Brewing's taproom in Naperville, Illinois, is a rarity, Milwaukee Journal Sentinel] [ref: Go Brewing's NA beers arrive in Milwaukee just in time for Dry January, OnMilwaukee] and northwest Indiana. [ref: Non-alcoholic craft beer Go Brewing, founded by a Chicago assembly plant worker, now distributed in Northwest Indiana, The Times of Northwest Indiana] In 2024 the Naperville Sun reported on its plans to grow through new partnerships. [ref: Naperville's Go Brewing seeks to build on its nonalcoholic beer success with new partnerships, Naperville Sun] According to the trade newsletter Beer Marketer's Insights, Go produced about 21,600 barrels in 2025, the most of any brewery newly reaching regional-brewery size that year. [ref: Non-Alc Co Go Brewing Tops Short List of New Regionals in 2025, Doubled to 21.6K Bbls, Beer Marketer's Insights]

In October 2026 the company launched Cold Standard, a non-alcoholic light lager whose packaging de-emphasizes the "non-alcoholic" label, which Food & Wine covered. [ref: This New NA Beer Is Making Its Nonalcoholic Label Harder to Notice, Food & Wine]

== Products and reception ==
Go Brewing's range includes IPAs, pilsners, sours, a chelada-style lager and seasonal beers, all under 0.5% ABV. [ref: Tasting: 7 Non-Alcoholic Craft Beers from Go Brewing, Paste] Chicago magazine named the taproom the city's best place to "drink beer and not get drunk" in 2023. [ref: Best of Chicago 2023, Chicago] Wirecutter named Salty AF Chelada its top pick for non-alcoholic fruited lager. [ref: The Best Non-Alcoholic Beer, Wirecutter]

== Awards ==
* 2025 World Beer Cup: silver (Hoppy Non-Alcohol Beer, Disarm); bronze (Specialty Non-Alcohol Beer, New School) [ref: 2025 World Beer Cup Winners List, Brewers Association]
* 2026 World Beer Cup: silver (Nobody's Gonna Know) and bronze (New School), both in Specialty Non-Alcohol Beer [ref: 2026 World Beer Cup Winners List, Brewers Association]
* 2026 Great American Beer Festival: silver and bronze, Specialty Non-Alcohol Beer [ref: 2026 GABF Winners List, Brewers Association]

data.title: Lemonaid Health
data.text:
Lemonaid Health is an American telehealth company based in San Francisco that provides online medical consultations, prescriptions and laboratory testing directly to consumers for a flat fee. Founded in 2013 and launched in 2014, it was acquired by the genetic-testing company 23andMe for US$400 million in 2021. In 2025, following 23andMe's bankruptcy, the business was sold to the investment firms Bambu Ventures and Innova Capital Partners for US$10 million.

== History ==
=== Founding and early growth ===
Lemonaid Health was founded in San Francisco in 2013 by Paul Johnson, who became chief executive, and Ian Van Every, who became president. Johnson had previously run online retail businesses in the United Kingdom. The service launched in 2014 in California and Pennsylvania, expanding to Michigan and New York in late 2015, and offered consultations by text chat, telephone or video for a flat fee, with physicians responding within two hours of a patient completing an online questionnaire. Early services were limited to a small number of conditions, with birth control the most requested, followed by treatments for conditions such as urinary tract infections, high cholesterol and hair loss and a small number of laboratory tests including screening for sexually transmitted infections.

In May 2017 the company raised an US$11 million Series A round led by Novartis Venture Fund and Hikma Ventures, the venture arms of Novartis and Hikma Pharmaceuticals, at which point it was available in 14 states. By April 2018 it had handled more than 100,000 patient visits, employed 26 people including three full-time physicians, and operated in 18 states; a STAT News profile that year described state-by-state licensing rules as the main constraint on its expansion. The same profile reported that Lemonaid had filed complaints with state medical boards against competitors including Nurx, alleging improper use of online questionnaires; Nurx denied wrongdoing.

=== Expansion and Series B ===
In July 2020 the company raised a US$33 million Series B round led by Olive Tree Ventures, with participation from Artis Ventures, Correlation Ventures, Hikma Ventures and Sierra Ventures, bringing total funding to US$55 million. It said it would use the round to add treatment for asthma, hypertension and type 2 diabetes and to expand its mental health services. By 2021 the company operated in all fifty states and ran its own pharmacy.

=== Acquisition by 23andMe ===
In October 2021, 23andMe agreed to acquire Lemonaid Health for US$400 million. 23andMe said the purchase would allow it to offer medical consultations and prescriptions alongside its genetic testing, moving the company toward a subscription health service. Johnson became general manager of 23andMe's consumer business following the acquisition.

=== Bankruptcy of 23andMe and sale ===
23andMe filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in March 2025. In September 2025, Bambu Ventures, in partnership with Innova Capital Partners, agreed to buy all of Lemonaid Health's stock from 23andMe for US$10 million in cash. Bambu said it intended to expand Lemonaid's on-demand telehealth and online pharmacy services.

== Services ==
Lemonaid provides online consultations for conditions including birth control, hair loss, mental health, and urinary tract infections, with prescriptions filled through its own pharmacy or sent to a pharmacy of the patient's choice. Patients pay a flat fee per visit rather than billing insurance.

data.title: Stephen Bocskay (2)
data.text:
Stephen Anthony Bocskay (born September 24, 1975) is an American cultural theorist and public intellectual.

Biography

Born in Yonkers, New York, Bocskay graduated from Cornell University with a bachelor’s and master’s degree in Hispanic studies. He became impassioned with Brazilian Portuguese, music, and culture in his early twenties and decided to pursue a Ph.D. in Luso-Brazilian Studies at Brown University. He has held teaching positions at institutions including Harvard University and the Universidade Federal de Pernambuco. His main fields of study are popular music and culture, black political thought, social movements, media, and authoritarianism in the African diaspora with a focus on Brazil.

In 2026, Bocskay gained notoriety for his book Candeia, o Samba, o Quilombo e o Ativismo Negro, which received praise from leading Brazilian music and cultural critics, including Sílvio Essinger, who described it as “sensational”, and Mauro Ferreira, who considers it “an essential work for understanding the ideology, personality, legacy, and contradictions of this artist, revered by all the great names of samba.2”

Bibliography

Candeia, o Samba, o Quilombo e o Ativismo Negro. Rio de Janeiro. Malê Editora, 2026. ISBN 978-65-6204-048-7

Personal Life

Bocskay has lived in Spain and elsewhere. Since 2002, he has resided between the United States and Brazil.

Amit Singh is a cardiovascular specialist based in Navi Mumbai. [ref: ]

== Career and professional role ==
Singh is a Consultant Interventional Cardiologist at Kokilaben Dhirubhai Ambani Hospital in Navi Mumbai, where he works in the Cardiac Sciences department.

According to his hospital profile, he previously served as Assistant Professor of Cardiology at K.E.M. Hospital, Mumbai.

Justin Morgan Had a Horse is a 1972 American television film produced by Walt Disney Productions for The Wonderful World of Disney. [ref: The Wonderful World of Disney Television, Hyperion Books] [ref: Disney A to Z: The Official Encyclopedia: Third Edition, Disney Editions] It was directed by Hollingsworth Morse and aired on NBC in two parts on February 6 and February 13, 1972. [ref: Justin Morgan Had a Horse (television), D23]

The film is based on Marguerite Henry's 1945 novel Justin Morgan Had a Horse. [ref: Marguerite Henry & the Movies, Equine Info Exchange]

The movie rights were acquired by Disney producer Harry Tytle, who worked with Walt Disney on developing the film. After Walt died in 1966 the project was shelved for a few years. [ref: Marguerite Henry & the Movies, Equine Info Exchange]

Music for the film was composed by Franklyn Marks, including the song "The Four Seasons". [ref: Justin Morgan Had a Horse - Full Cast & Crew, TV Guide] [ref: The four seasons, Copyright Encyclopedia]

The film is available on DVD, Disney+ and Apple TV. [ref: Justin Morgan Had a Horse, Orange County Library System] [ref: Justin Morgan Had a Horse, Disney+] [ref: Justin Morgan Had a Horse, Apple TV]

Josh Spiegel of:/Film called the film “baffling”, while Common Sense Media gave it three out of five stars. data.title: Alaa Al-Haidari
data.text:
----

Alaa Sabah Marai Shahaf Al-Haidari is an Iraqi politician and a member of the Council of Representatives of Iraq representing Basra Governorate. The official website of the Council of Representatives of Iraq lists him among the representatives of Basra Governorate and as a member of the Iraqi Foundation Coalition. [ref: Members of the Council of Representatives of Iraq, Council of Representatives of Iraq]

According to the Iraqi Parliamentary Monitor, Al-Haidari is affiliated with the Wated Iraqi Gathering within the Iraqi Foundation Coalition. The same source states that he is a member of the Oil, Gas and Natural Resources Committee and holds a bachelor's degree. It also records two electoral terms and 7,117 votes. [ref: Alaa Sabah Marai Shahaf Al-Haidari, Iraqi Parliamentary Monitor]

== Political career ==

=== Membership of the Council of Representatives ===
By May 2022, Al-Haidari was a member of the Council of Representatives. At the time, Shafaq News described him as an independent representative from Basra Governorate. [ref: Parliamentarian puts forward Basra demands, including protesters' condition for voting on the food security law, Shafaq News]

On 19 May 2022, Shafaq News reported statements made by Al-Haidari during a press conference held at the Council of Representatives building. He called for the completion of the project to designate Basra as Iraq's economic capital and for the resolution of the governorate's petro-dollar issue. He also called for the demands of Basra's protesters to be included in the budget and the food security law.

The demands included the appointment of graduates of science colleges, as well as addressing the status of contract workers and daily-wage workers. Al-Haidari said that including these demands was a condition for voting on the Emergency Support Law or the budget, according to Shafaq News.

=== Chairmanship of the Iraqi Foundation Coalition parliamentary bloc ===
On 5 January 2026, the National Iraqi News Agency (NINA) reported that Al-Haidari, a representative from Basra Governorate, had been chosen as chairman of the Iraqi Foundation Coalition parliamentary bloc during the sixth legislative term of the Council of Representatives. [ref: Al-Haidari named chairman of the Foundation Coalition parliamentary bloc, National Iraqi News Agency]

On 3 June 2026, the President of Iraq received a delegation from the Iraqi Foundation Coalition parliamentary bloc, headed by Representative Alaa Al-Haidari, at Al-Salam Palace in Baghdad. [ref: The President receives a delegation from the Iraqi Foundation Coalition parliamentary bloc, Presidency of the Republic of Iraq]

data.title: Citto Media
data.text:
Citto Media is a Bangladeshi digital media and content platform founded by content creator Jewel Rana on 4 February 2025. [ref: ওকালতি ছেড়ে কনটেন্ট ক্রিয়েটর, এখন ফলোয়ার ৩৫ লাখ, Prothom Alo] Its content primarily focuses on agriculture, nature and rural life, and also incorporates stories about people and elements of Bengali literature.

==History==

Citto Media was established on 4 February 2025 by Jewel Rana, who is from Harinakundu in Jhenaidah District, Bangladesh. Rana studied law at Islamic University, Bangladesh and completed his postgraduate degree in 2018. Before establishing Citto Media, he spent several years attempting to practise law.

According to a profile published by Prothom Alo in February 2026, Rana established Citto Media with the aim of producing content about rural communities, agriculture and the natural environment. The platform's videos combine observations of rural life with commentary and references to Bengali literature.

==Content==

Citto Media produces videos concerning agriculture, nature and rural communities. Its videos have featured farmers, agricultural activities, landscapes, animals and aspects of village life. The platform also incorporates literary references and narration into some of its videos.

In a February 2026 profile, Prothom Alo reported that Citto Media had published approximately 1,350 videos on Facebook and that its Facebook page had more than 3.5 million followers at the time. The same report said its YouTube channel had nearly 100,000 subscribers.

==Public profile==

Citto Media received coverage in Bangladeshi national media during 2026 in connection with the country's discussion of taxation of freelancers and digital content creators. The Daily Star identified Jewel Rana, using the spelling "Zuel Rana", as the owner of Citto Media and described the platform as producing nature-related content on social media. [ref: Govt plans tax relief for content creators, [[The Daily Star (Bangladesh)]

On 1 June 2026, Rana met with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the Bangladesh Secretariat. Bangladeshi media reported that the meeting included discussion of a proposed 7.5 percent source tax on income earned by freelancers and content creators. The Daily Star subsequently reported that the meeting was part of developments surrounding proposed tax relief for individual content creators and freelancers. [ref: কনটেন্ট ক্রিয়েটরদের আয়ের ওপর কোনো কর আরোপ করা হবে না, The Daily Ittefaq]

The meeting and Citto Media's work were subsequently reported by several Bangladeshi news outlets. Ittefaq described Rana as the founder of Citto Media and reported that the Facebook page had exceeded 4.3 million followers at the time of its report. Kaler Kantho similarly reported on the meeting and described the platform's content as combining agriculture, nature, people and literature. [ref: কন্টেন্ট ক্রিয়েটরদের আয়ে ৭.৫% কর দিতে হবে না, জুয়েল রানাকে প্রধানমন্ত্রী, Kaler Kantho]

Rana has also been listed as a content creator affiliated with Citto Media by TEDxCCN-UST, where he was included among speakers for a TEDx event. [ref: Speakers, TEDxCCN-UST]

data.title: Flag Of Garden Grove, CA
data.text:
The flag proportions of the Garden Grove City flag is 3:5. The design features a dark blue background, and a light blue stripe in the middle, and the city coat of arms is on top of the light blue stripe. The both blues in the city flag represent civic trust, stability, and community harmony. The gold symbolizes civic prosperity, and honors the city's rich agricultural heritage, specifically the sun-kissed citrus and orange groves that inspired the city name. The latin motto in the seal, "Absit Invidia", translates to "Let there be no ill will.

data.title: Aditya Keo Santoso
data.text:
== Aditya Praristama Santoso ==
Aditya Praristama Santoso, juga dikenal sebagai Keo Santoso, adalah seorang pengusaha Indonesia yang diketahui terlibat dalam sektor energi panas bumi. Aditya Praristama Santoso, yang dikenal sebagai Aditya Keo Santoso atau Keo Santoso, merupakan anak dari Supramu Santoso dan Yenni Rista Santoso. Pada Oktober 2025, ia disebut sebagai Komisaris Supreme Energy dalam pemberitaan mengenai pengembangan proyek Pembangkit Listrik Tenaga Panas Bumi (PLTP) Muara Laboh di Kabupaten Solok Selatan, Sumatera Barat.

== Karier ==

=== Stellar Kapital ===
Aditya Keo Santoso membangun Stellar Kapital pada 2014. Perusahaan tersebut berfokus pada investasi dan pengembangan perusahaan rintisan di Indonesia, termasuk perusahaan yang bergerak dalam bidang teknologi finansial, perdagangan elektronik, dan layanan lainnya.

Dalam pemberitaan pada Mei 2018, ia disebut sebagai salah satu pendiri dan ketua Stellar Kapital. Perusahaan tersebut dilaporkan memiliki portofolio investasi yang mencakup UangTeman, Sepulsa, Dananikah, Rajamobil, Tado, Travelio, dan Freeware.

=== Sektor Energi ===
Pada Oktober 2025, Aditya Praristama Santoso diberitakan menjabat sebagai komisaris Supreme Energy. Ia menghadiri kegiatan dimulainya pengeboran sumur pertama untuk pengembangan tahap kedua PLTP Muara Laboh di Kabupaten Solok Selatan, Sumatera Barat.

== Pendidikan ==
Profil profesional Aditya mencantumkan De Anza College dan Santa Clara University Leavey School of Business sebagai institusi pendidikannya. Rincian program studi dan status kelulusan memerlukan verifikasi lebih lanjut.

data.title: Hakim Mahmud Ahmad Zafar Sialkoti
data.text:
Hakim Mahmud Ahmad Zafar Sialkoti () is a Pakistani Islamic scholar, historian, author, and Unani practitioner from Sialkot, Punjab. He has written extensively in Urdu on Islamic history, Seerah (the biography of the Islamic prophet Muhammad), the Rashidun Caliphs, and traditional medicine. [ref: محمود احمد ظفر (Mahmud Ahmad Zafar), Urdu Wikipedia] [ref: Hakeem Mahmood Ahmad Zafar, Wikidata]

== Biography ==
Hakim Mahmud Ahmad Zafar is based in the city of Sialkot in Punjab, Pakistan. Alongside practicing traditional Unani medicine as a Hakim, he has authored over a dozen books focused on early Islamic history, detailed biographies of the Companions of the Prophet (Sahabah), the wives of Muhammad (Ummahat-ul-Momineen), and theological studies.

His publications have been examined in academic literary studies reviewing 20th-century Urdu biographical and historical literature. [ref: Hakim Mahmud Ahmad Zafar ki Kutub Tareekh-o-Sawanih Ka Tajziyati Mutala'a (Analytical Study of Hakim Mahmud Ahmad Zafar's History and Biographical Books), Asian Research Index] His works have been published by major Urdu publishing houses in Lahore, Multan, and Deoband, including Takhleeqat, Dar-ul-Nawadir, Hafizi Book Depot, and Kutub Khana Majeedia. [ref: Shah Wali Allah aur un ke Tajdidi Karname by Hakeem Mahmood Ahmad Zafar, Rekhta Library]

== Selected works ==
=== Islamic History and Biographies ===
* Syedna Usman Radio Allahu Anhu: Shakhsiyat aur Kirdar (سیدنا عثمان رضی اللہ عنہ شخصیت اور کردار) – Published by Kutub Khana Majeedia, Multan (1991). [ref: Syedna Usman: Shakhsiyat aur Kirdar, Kutub Khana Majeedia]
* Seerat Khatam-ul-Nabiyyin (سیرت خاتم النبیینﷺ) – Published by Takhleeqat, Lahore (2001). [ref: Seerat Khatam-ul-Nabiyyin, Takhleeqat]
* Syedna Ali ibn Abi Talib: Shakhsiyat wa Kirdar (سیدنا علی ابن ابی طالب: شخصیت و کردار) – Published by Takhleeqat, Lahore (2003). [ref: Syedna Ali ibn Abi Talib: Shakhsiyat wa Kirdar, Takhleeqat]
* Syedna Hasan bin Ali: Tareekh Ke Aine Mein (سیدنا حسن بن علی: تاریخ کے آئینہ میں) – Published by Takhleeqat, Lahore (2006). [ref: Syedna Hasan bin Ali: Tareekh Ke Aine Mein, Takhleeqat]
* Syedna Hussain bin Ali: Tareekh Ki Roshni Mein (سیدنا حسین بن علی: تاریخ کی روشنی میں) – Published by Takhleeqat, Lahore (2006). [ref: Syedna Hussain bin Ali: Tareekh Ki Roshni Mein, Takhleeqat]
* Daulat-e-Umaviyyah: Undalus (دولت امویہ: اندلس) – Historical analysis of the Umayyad Caliphate in Al-Andalus. [ref: Daulat-e-Umaviyyah Undalis, Takhleeqat]
* Paigham-e-Amn ﷺ (پیغمبر امنﷺ) – Published by Makki Dar-ul-Kutub, Lahore (2009). [ref: Paigham-e-Amn, Makki Dar-ul-Kutub]
* Shah Wali Allah aur un ke Tajdidi Karname (شاہ ولی اللہ اور ان کے تجدیدی کارنامے) – Published by Hafizi Book Depot, Deoband (2008).
* Ummahat-ul-Momineen (امھات المومنین) – Published by Takhleeqat, Lahore (2011). [ref: Ummahat-ul-Momineen, Takhleeqat]

=== Social, Political, and Health Works ===
* Ghar Ka Hakim (گھر کا حکیم) – A guide on traditional remedies and health, published by Takhleeqat, Lahore (2002). [ref: Ghar Ka Hakim, Takhleeqat]
* Fitna-e-Jamhooriat (فتنہ جمہوریت) – Political critique published by Al-Kitab, Lahore (2008). [ref: Fitna-e-Jamhooriat, Al-Kitab]
* Tameer-e-Pakistan Mein Hukmaranon Ka Kirdar (تعمیر پاکستان میں حکمرانوں کا کردار) – History of governance in Pakistan, published by Takhleeqat, Lahore (2008). [ref: Tameer-e-Pakistan Mein Hukmaranon Ka Kirdar, Takhleeqat]

Chanakya University is a private university in Bengaluru, Karnataka, India. It was established under the Chanakya University Act, 2021, an act of the Karnataka Legislature, and is sponsored by the Centre for Educational and Social Studies (CESS), a society registered in Karnataka.
