data.title: Disappearance of Karen Schepers
data.text:
Karen Schepers (1959–1983) was an American woman from Elgin, Illinois, who disappeared in April 1983 after spending an evening at a bar in nearby Carpentersville. [ref: Coroner confirms human remains found Tuesday belong to Karen Schepers, www.dailyherald.com] She was last seen in the early hours of April 16, and her yellow 1980 Toyota Celica was also missing. [ref: 'Where is Karen?': Police who started cold case podcast find woman's remains after 42 years, USA TODAY]

On March 25, 2025, searchers located a vehicle in the Fox River and found a license plate matching Schepers' missing car. [ref: Skeletal remains found in car pulled from Fox River that belonged to Karen Schepers, missing since 1983 - CBS Chicago, www.cbsnews.com] The vehicle, a 1980 Toyota Celica, was recovered the following day, with skeletal remains inside. The Kane County Coroner's Office identified the remains as Schepers through dental records and a forensic dentist.

Schepers worked as a computer programmer at a bank and had previously participated in music and cheerleading during high school. She lived alone in Elgin at the time of her disappearance. Investigators later found that her bank accounts and credit cards had shown no activity after she went missing. [ref: Underwater remains could crack 1983 cold case of missing Chicago-area woman: Police, ABC News]

data.title: Sanjeev Jaiswal
data.text:
Sanjeev Jaiswal is an Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer of the Maharashtra cadre. He has served in various administrative positions in the Government of Maharashtra, including as Municipal Commissioner of Thane and Nagpur, Additional Municipal Commissioner of the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai, and Vice President and Chief Executive Officer of the Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (MHADA).

== Early life and education ==
Mr. Sanjeev Jaiswal was born in Kolkata. His early education completed at St. Paul’s Boarding School. Then he pursued higher secondary and graduation in Political Science (Honors) from St. Xavier’s College, Kolkata. After college he enrolled in postgraduate studies in Political Science and International Relations at the University of Calcutta before leaving to prepare for the Civil Services Examination.

== Early administrative career ==
Sanjeev Jaiswal is a 1996 batch IAS officer of the Maharashtra cadre. He has held several administrative positions, including;

* CEO, Nashik Zilla Parishad - 2000 to 2002
* District Collector, Chandrapur, Aurangabad, Nashik - 2004 to 2010
* Municipal Commissioner, Nagpur - 2010 to 2012
* Divisional Commissioner, Aurangabad - 2012 to 2015
* Municipal Commissioner, Thane - 2015 to 2020
* Additional Commissioner, BMC - 2020 to 2021
* Principal Secretary, Water Supply - 2021 to 2023
* Vice President & CEO, MHADA - 2023 to Present Date

== Tenure at MHADA ==
Jaiswal assumed office as the Vice President and Chief Executive Officer of the Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (MHADA) in June 2023. [ref: ]

During his tenure, MHADA has undertaken several housing, redevelopment and administrative initiatives across Maharashtra.

=== Cluster redevelopment ===
MHADA announced plans to redevelop approximately 923 acres of MHADA layouts across Mumbai. According to the authority, the project is expected to rehabilitate more than 75,000 residents through phased redevelopment projects over the coming years. [ref: 923 acres of MHADA layouts will be redeveloped across Mumbai, The Times of India]

=== Motilal Nagar redevelopment ===
In 2026, MHADA presented the master plan for the redevelopment of Motilal Nagar in Goregaon, one of the authority's largest redevelopment projects. The project covers approximately 143 acres and is planned under a Construction and Development Agency (C&DA) model, with MHADA acting as the Special Planning Authority. [ref: Motilal Nagar redevelopment master plan unveiled, Hindustan Times] [ref: Motilal Nagar Redevelopment Master Plan, MHADA]

=== Affordable housing projects ===
MHADA continued the implementation of housing lotteries under Jaiswal's tenure, including the Konkan Board Lottery and other regional housing schemes intended to increase the supply of affordable housing in Maharashtra. [ref: MHADA Lottery attracts strong response, Economic Times]

=== Digital governance ===
MHADA introduced digital governance measures aimed at improving service delivery, project monitoring and citizen access to housing-related services. These initiatives included expansion of online services and digitization of administrative processes. [ref: MHADA's Digital Transformation in Public Housing]

=== Housing policy ===
In interviews, [https://realty.economictimes.indiatimes.com/tag/sanjeev+jaiswal Sanjeev Jaiswal] stated that MHADA intends to expand affordable housing through large-scale redevelopment, rental housing initiatives and public-private partnerships to increase housing supply in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region. [ref: Exclusive Interview with Sanjeev Jaiswal, NDTV]

data.title: MoveInSync
data.text:
----

MoveInSync Technology Solutions Private Limited, commonly known as MoveInSync, is an Indian enterprise software company headquartered in Bengaluru, Karnataka. Founded in 2009, the company develops employee commute software used by organizations to schedule, track, and manage the daily commuting of their staff. It also offers a workplace-management product, WorkInSync, used to manage office space including desk booking, meeting-room booking, parking, visitor management, and cafeteria operations.

== History ==

=== Founding and early pivot (2009–2015) ===
MoveInSync was founded in 2009 in Bengaluru by three graduates of the Indian Institute of Technology (BHU) Varanasi: Deepesh Agarwal, Akash Maheshwari, and Anuvrata Arora. It was initially launched as a consumer carpooling service called RideInSync before shifting to a business-to-business model. Google was an early client; the company has also named Amazon, Oracle, Infosys, HCL, and Tech Mahindra among its customers.

In August 2014, the company raised $2 million in Series A funding led by Inventus Capital Partners, Saama Capital, and Qualcomm Ventures.

=== Series B and expansion (2018) ===
In April 2018, MoveInSync raised $8 million in Series B funding led by Nexus Venture Partners, with participation from Inventus Capital Partners, Saama Capital, and Qualcomm Ventures.

=== Workplace-management line (WorkInSync) ===
MoveInSync launched its workplace-management product, WorkInSync, in 2020. According to the company, it introduced the product to help organizations manage office space as hybrid and distributed work expanded during the COVID-19 pandemic.

=== Series C funding (2024) ===
In January 2024, the company raised $15 million in Series C funding led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with participation from Saama Capital, Qualcomm Ventures, Athera Venture Partners, and Nexus Venture Partners. The company said the funds would go toward expanding its managed-fleet product, MoveInSync ONE, and into international markets including the Philippines, South Africa, and the Middle East.

=== Acquisition of eFmFm (2025) ===
In May 2025, MoveInSync acquired eFmFm, an enterprise transport technology company founded in 2012 by Satish Goel. The company stated the acquisition would support further development in the employee commute space.

== Products and services ==
MoveInSync offers its software as a service under the name MoveInSync Ion, covering both employee commute management and, through WorkInSync, workplace management. The commute-management software supports home-to-office cabs, shuttles, corporate car rental, carpooling, and inter-office shuttle routes, while the workplace-management software covers desk booking, meeting-room booking, parking, visitor management, and cafeteria management.

The company also offers MoveInSync ONE, a managed-fleet service that combines the software platform with a vehicle fleet and transport operations run by the company.

== Operations ==
MoveInSync is privately held. Reported figures for its client count, Fortune 500 clients, and country footprint have varied by source and date; company and press materials between 2018 and 2025 have cited enterprise client counts ranging from around 50 to more than 400.

Total disclosed venture funding across the Series A (2014), Series B (2018), and Series C (2024) rounds has been reported at approximately $25 million to $32 million, with investors including Inventus Capital Partners, Saama Capital, Qualcomm Ventures, Nexus Venture Partners, Athera Venture Partners, and Bessemer Venture Partners.

== Mobility Symposium ==
Since 2024, MoveInSync has organized an annual event in Bengaluru called the Mobility Symposium. The company has said the first edition produced a set of policy recommendations that were submitted to the Government of Karnataka. The 2025 edition, held on 10 October, was addressed by Priyank Kharge, Karnataka's Minister for Information Technology and Biotechnology; Member of Parliament Tejasvi Surya; and Maheshwar Rao, Chief Commissioner of the Greater Bengaluru Authority. The third edition was held on 8 October 2026 under the theme "Resilient Mobility".

== Recognition ==
In 2026, MoveInSync was ranked third on the India's Fastest-Growing Companies list published by TIME in partnership with Statista, a ranking based on companies' revenue growth between the 2022 and 2025 fiscal years.

== References ==

== History ==
=== Founding and early pivot (2009–2015) ===
MoveInSync was founded in 2009 in Bengaluru by Deepesh Agarwal, Akash Maheshwari, and Anuvrata Arora, graduates of the Indian Institute of Technology (BHU) Varanasi. It initially launched a consumer carpooling service under the name RideInSync. According to a 2015 account in Business Today, the founders shifted to a business-to-business model after a conversation with a Google India employee about the difficulty of coordinating transport for the company's Hyderabad staff, which they concluded pointed to a wider market among corporate employers.

In August 2014, the company raised $2 million in Series A funding from Inventus Capital Partners, Saama Capital, and Qualcomm Ventures.

=== Series B and expansion (2018) ===
In April 2018, MoveInSync raised $8 million in Series B funding led by Nexus Venture Partners, with participation from Inventus Capital Partners, Saama Capital, and Qualcomm Ventures. At the time, the company said its clients included Google, Facebook, Amazon, and Microsoft.

=== Workplace-management line (WorkInSync) ===
According to the company, it launched a workplace-management product line, WorkInSync, in response to demand from corporate clients for tools to manage office space, such as desk and meeting-room booking, as employers adopted hybrid work during the COVID-19 pandemic. WorkInSync is offered as a standalone product in addition to being bundled with the commute offering.

=== Series C funding (2024) ===
In January 2024, the company raised $15 million in Series C funding led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with participation from Saama Capital, Qualcomm Ventures, Athera Venture Partners, and Nexus Venture Partners. The company said the funds would go toward expanding its managed-fleet product, MoveInSync ONE, increasing the share of electric vehicles in client fleets, and expanding into the Philippines, South Africa, and the Middle East.

=== Acquisition of eFmFm (2025) ===
In May 2025, MoveInSync acquired eFmFm, an enterprise transport technology company founded in 2012 by Satish Goel. The company described it as its first acquisition in the employee transport space.

== Products and services ==
MoveInSync's core product is a software-as-a-service platform, marketed as MoveInSync Ion, that handles scheduling, routing, tracking, and billing for corporate employee transport. Functions include home-to-office cab bookings, fixed-route shuttles, intra-organization carpooling, corporate car rental, and inter-office shuttle routes.

MoveInSync ONE is a managed transportation offering that combines the software platform with a vehicle fleet that the company operates for clients.

WorkInSync, the company's workplace-management product, covers desk booking, meeting-room booking, parking, and visitor management for corporate offices, along with utilization analytics for facilities teams.

== Operations ==
MoveInSync is privately held. Reported figures for its client count, Fortune 500 clients, and country footprint have varied by source and date; company and press materials between 2018 and 2025 have cited enterprise client counts ranging from around 50 to more than 400.

Total disclosed venture funding across the Series A (2014), Series B (2018), and Series C (2024) rounds has been reported at approximately $25 million to $32 million, with investors including Inventus Capital Partners, Saama Capital, Qualcomm Ventures, Nexus Venture Partners, Athera Venture Partners, and Bessemer Venture Partners.

== Recognition ==
In 2026, MoveInSync was ranked third on the India's Fastest-Growing Companies list published by TIME in partnership with Statista, a ranking based on companies' self-reported revenue growth between the 2022 and 2025 fiscal years.

data.title: Arango
data.text:
Arango is a software company based in San Francisco, California, and Cologne, Germany. [ref: Arango Invites AI Leaders and Builders to Explore the Contextual Data Layer Powering Production AI Agents at NVIDIA GTC 2026, Business Wire] The company develops ArangoDB, a multimodel database management system, and the Arango Contextual Data Platform, a software platform for enterprise artificial intelligence applications.

ArangoDB supports graph, document, and key-value data models within a single database engine and uses the ArangoDB Query Language (AQL). The database also supports full-text and vector search.

In October 2025, Arango introduced a preview of the Arango AI Data Platform. The platform was subsequently renamed the Arango Contextual Data Platform, with version 4.0 announced in March 2026 and made generally available in April 2026.

== History ==

=== Origins and founding ===
Development of ArangoDB began in October 2011, when the first code was committed to the project, originally known as AvocadoDB. [ref: Evolving ArangoDB's Licensing Model for a Sustainable Future, Arango] The project was renamed ArangoDB in May 2012. [ref: "AvocadoDB" becomes "ArangoDB", Another Word For It]

The company was founded by Claudius Weinberger and Frank Celler and subsequently developed the database as a commercial product. [ref: Open source database ArangoDB raises €2.2 million in fresh funding, Tech.eu]

=== Funding and growth ===
In 2017, ArangoDB completed a €4.2 million funding round led by Target Partners. The total included an initial €2.2 million investment made in November 2016 and an additional €2 million invested in 2017. [ref: German database startup ArangoDB closes funding round at €4.2 million, Tech.eu] [ref: Target Partners leads €4.2m round for ArangoDB, Unquote] [ref: Osborne Clarke berät ArangoDB bei Investment durch Target Partners, Osborne Clarke]

In March 2019, the company raised $10 million in Series A funding led by Bow Capital. [ref: ArangoDB raises $10 million for NoSQL database management, VentureBeat] In October 2021, it announced a $27.8 million Series B funding round led by Iris Capital. The company had previously raised approximately $19.2 million. [ref: Open source graph database company ArangoDB raises $27.8M, VentureBeat] [ref: ArangoDB brings yet more money into graph database market with $27.8M round, SiliconANGLE]

In 2025, ORIX USA's Growth Capital business made a strategic investment in ArangoDB. [ref: ArangoDB Secures Strategic Investment from ORIX USA to Power the Future of AI-Native Data Infrastructure, ORIX USA]

=== Licensing changes ===
In October 2023, ArangoDB announced changes to its software licensing model. Beginning with version 3.12, the database's source code moved from the Apache License 2.0 to the Business Source License 1.1. [ref: Incompatible changes in ArangoDB 3.12, Arango Documentation]

The company also introduced a Community License for precompiled binaries, permitting internal business use while restricting commercial use and limiting production deployments to 100 GiB of data. [ref: ArangoDB Editions and Licensing, Arango Documentation]

Under the Business Source License, covered source-code versions transition to the Apache License 2.0 four years after their initial public distribution.

=== Expansion into AI platforms ===
In October 2025, Arango announced a preview of the Arango AI Data Platform at NVIDIA GTC Washington, D.C. The platform extended ArangoDB with capabilities for graph-based retrieval and applications using large language models. [ref: Arango Launches AI Data Platform at NVIDIA GTC Introducing Contextual AI: Enterprise AI Powered by Business Context, Business Wire]

In March 2026, the company announced version 4.0 of the platform, renamed the Arango Contextual Data Platform, at NVIDIA GTC. The release included a Contextual Data Layer architecture and an Agentic AI Suite with services including AutoGraph, AutoRAG, and Arango Ada. [ref: Arango Launches Contextual Data Platform 4.0 for AI-Agent-Ready Enterprise Data, Business Wire] [ref: What NVIDIA GTC Made Clear: The Future of AI Is Context-Driven, And It Requires More Than a Single-Model Database, Arango] Version 4.0 became generally available in April 2026. [ref: What's new in the data platform, Arango Documentation]

In August 2026, version 4.1.0 introduced AutoGraph Studio, combining the AutoGraph and GraphRAG interfaces into a single interface for constructing and querying knowledge graphs.

In July 2026, Arango was named a Strong Performer in The Forrester Wave: Multimodel Data Platforms, Q2 2026. [ref: Arango Recognized as a Strong Performer in Multimodel Data Platforms, Q2 2026 Evaluation, Business Wire]

== Products ==

=== ArangoDB ===
ArangoDB is a multimodel database management system supporting graph, document, and key-value data within a single database engine. [ref: Feature list of the ArangoDB core database system, Arango Documentation]

The database uses the ArangoDB Query Language (AQL) for data retrieval, filtering, aggregation, and graph traversal. It also supports full-text search through ArangoSearch and vector similarity search. [ref: Information Retrieval with ArangoSearch, Arango Documentation] [ref: Vector indexes, Arango Documentation]

ArangoDB is distributed in Community and Enterprise editions. From version 3.12.5, the Community Edition includes the Enterprise Edition's features without time restrictions, although the editions differ in their licensing terms and permitted uses.

=== Arango Contextual Data Platform ===
The Arango Contextual Data Platform is an enterprise data platform built on ArangoDB. Initially introduced in October 2025 as the Arango AI Data Platform, it combines graph, document, and vector data capabilities with services for constructing knowledge graphs and retrieving information for AI applications.

The platform includes AutoGraph, which supports the creation of knowledge graphs from enterprise data, and AutoRAG, which provides retrieval capabilities for applications using large language models.

It also includes Arango Ada, an AI assistant introduced in beta with version 4.0.

Version 4.1 introduced AutoGraph Studio, an interface for constructing and querying knowledge graphs.

data.title: Sid Yiddish
data.text:
Sid Yiddish is the stage name of Charles Bernstein (born c. 1962), an American performance artist, avant-garde vocalist, actor, poet, and writer based in Evanston, Illinois. He is known for his distinctive throat singing, experimental and improvisational music with the ensemble Sid Yiddish & His Candy Store Henchmen, absurdist humor, and supporting roles in television and film. His multidisciplinary work combines sound, philosophy, humor, and composition, frequently incorporating unconventional instruments such as the shofar and systems of physical gesture-based conduction.Jumpin’ with Sid, Chicago TribuneSid Yiddish CV, SidYiddish.com
== Early life and education ==
Charles Bernstein was raised in the Evanston/Skokie area of Illinois and attended Niles West High School in Skokie. He has described himself as an “international industrial poet actor throat-singing tap-dancing spy.” He is the brother of writer and teacher Arnie Bernstein. As a child, he attended his first Major League Baseball game in 1969 (Cubs vs. Mets at Wrigley Field) and later contributed baseball-related writing to Bardball.com.He began writing poetry in grade school and by 1979, while still a student at Niles West, was calling himself a poet. From 1986 to 1991 he published the poetry fanzine Cops Hate Poetry, which included his own poems, record reviews, and interviews with figures such as Carl Perkins, the Circle Jerks, and Allen Ginsberg.Potty Poet, Chicago ReaderBernstein earned a Bachelor of Arts in Print Journalism from Columbia College Chicago in 1990 and a Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Arts and Media from the same institution in 2016. Additional training includes jazz vocals, piano instruction, tap dance, and throat singing at the Old Town School of Folk Music in Chicago (approximately 2001–2006); a playwright workshop at Infinite Theater (2019); and stand-up comedy, improvisational sketch comedy, and laughing yoga at Gilda’s Club Chicago (2019–2020).He adopted the stage name Sid Yiddish publicly around June 4, 2004 (the day Ronald Reagan died), during a poetry reading. “Sid” is his middle name; “Yiddish” refers to his Jewish background. He has described the persona as bridging gaps in performance art involving instruments, music, and ideas that others might avoid.Sid Yiddish Interview, Art InterviewsAnswers: Toilet talk, The Daily NorthwesternMedia Student Sid Yiddish Interviewed for Performance in Kansas, Columbia College Chicago Art and Art History News
== Career ==
=== Acting, television, and film ===
Yiddish has appeared in a range of television, film, commercial, and music-video projects, often in distinctive or character roles. Notable credits include:
Shameless (Showtime): Chasidic Rabbi (Season 6, Episode 1) and Homeless Man (Season 7, Episode 5).
America’s Got Talent (NBC): reality-show contestant (Seasons 6 in 2011 and 8 in 2013).
Empire (Fox): Café Patron, Businessman, Hospital Pedestrian, and other roles.
Chicago PD and Chicago Fire (NBC): homeless or drunken characters.
Philip K. Dick’s Electric Dreams (Amazon): Jewish Alien Father.
Patriot (Amazon): International Traveler.
Feature and short films including Death Wish (2018, Businessman), the documentary Sid Yiddish (2014, directed by Ryan Buckley, in which he appears as himself), and the Ludacris music video “Jingalin’” (Chasidic Rabbi).
Commercials (including Exxon-Mobil and Burt’s Bees) and other projects such as DOCTA films and The Life of Jimmy Bracken.
The 2014 documentary Sid Yiddish, directed by Ryan Buckley (with cinematography by Zach Mehrbach), followed him in Evanston, Chicago, and New York. It received its world premiere in Aarhus, Denmark, and an American debut in Portland, Oregon.Sid Yiddish’s Unstoppable Summer, Columbia College Chicago Art and Art History NewsSid Yiddish: a star is born, WGN RadioHe has also performed in theatrical and site-specific works, including as understudy Rabbi in a production of Fiddler on the Roof, The Great Fire: A Traveling Truck Show, solo pieces at the Rhinoceros Fest (Prop Theater), and events at the Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago.
=== Music and performance art ===
Yiddish is known as a performance artist and conductor of the improvisational collective Sid Yiddish & His Candy Store Henchmen (founded on or around December 10, 2010). The group operates as a collective using “The Henchmen Method,” a system of physical gestures (reportedly 75–100 or more) that he developed over several years and has taught in locations including Mexico and Denmark. Instrumentation has included guitars, violin, piano, electronics, shofar, slide whistles, cigar-box guitar, animal horns, double-belled trumpets, and found objects. The sound is often described as experimental, blending atonal improvisation, harmonic elements, absurdist humor, theater, comedy, and performance art.Sid Yiddish And His Candy Store Henchmen, Reggies LiveSid Yiddish And His Candy Store Henchmen, SpotifyHe developed throat singing around 2004 while studying voice and piano at the Old Town School of Folk Music and has incorporated it into solo performances, television appearances (including America’s Got Talent), radio, and collaborations. Notable collaborations include work with the Danish punk band Clean Boys (including the album Safari Freakshow Adventure and tours) and the Chicago jazz fusion group Marbin. He has performed at the Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago, as a regular participant in Make Music Chicago, on college radio station WZRD (Northeastern Illinois University), commercial station WGN, the Green Mill, Double Door, Bowery Poetry Club in New York, and other venues.Sid Yiddish's Portal, SidYiddish.comSid Yiddish: Rocking Both Sides of the Atlantic, Columbia College Chicago Art and Art History NewsEarlier projects include the Two $ Cockroach Band. He served as president of the Chicago Composers Forum in 2010 (member since 2007). In 2008 he acted as Chicago coordinator of the Bathroom Poetry Project, which placed poems in public restrooms in locations including Rogers Park, Wicker Park, Bucktown, and Evanston.He has hosted radio programs including Make Art Make Music Make Love (2012–2013) and The Radio Room (2013–2014) on Que4 Radio, and has made multiple guest appearances on WGN (including live performances with Candy Store Henchmen and discussions of the documentary with Rick Kogan).
=== Writing and journalism ===
Before and alongside the Sid Yiddish persona, Bernstein worked in print journalism, including freelance work and a position at a weekly newspaper in Melrose Park, Illinois, after graduating in 1990. He conducted entertainment-industry interviews and has published poetry and prose in various outlets. His artistic statement describes his body of work as “an experimental human instrument of four different components: sound, philosophy, humor and composition,” encouraging audiences to connect with their “hidden, shy side.”
== Discography ==
Selected releases associated with Sid Yiddish and/or Sid Yiddish & His Candy Store Henchmen include:
Hard Boiled Eggs (2022/2023)
Until Further Notice Everyday Feels Like Sunday (2021)
Fly Having Sex (2016)
Living the Life I Bring (2016)
Merry Fucking Happy (2014; Aleatory Records)
Leather Strawberries (2012; live on WZRD, Aleatory Records)
Safari Freakshow Adventure (2010; collaborative with Clean Boys, Misspelled Records)
Additional live recordings, collaborative projects, and earlier releases are available on platforms such as Bandcamp and streaming services.Multi-Tasking and Multiple Appearances Just Par for the Course, Columbia College Chicago Art and Art History News
== Reception ==
Coverage has appeared primarily in Chicago-area media. A 2009 Chicago Tribune piece by Rick Kogan described a performance involving singing, the shofar, and a Ouija board as “at once appealing and odd,” with an Andy Kaufman comparison. The 2008 Chicago Reader feature focused on the Bathroom Poetry Project. Columbia College’s Art and Art History News blog published multiple posts during his graduate studies covering releases, performances (including Make Music Chicago and Rhinoceros Fest), tours, and the documentary. Additional mentions appear in Time Out Chicago, Huffington Post, WGN Radio, and local arts coverage; performer profiles also note Danish press coverage related to collaborations with Clean Boys.Sid Yiddish, GigRoster
== References ==

== External links ==

[https://sidyiddish.com/uploads/CV_Sid-Yiddish.pdf Official CV (PDF)]
[https://open.spotify.com/artist/4JTG1NxGUhZT1MlceWf5sK Sid Yiddish And His Candy Store Henchmen on Spotify]

== Conflict of interest disclosure ==
I am a personal friend of Sid Yiddish (Charles Bernstein) and have been since 2010. Per Wikipedia’s conflict of interest guidelines, I am disclosing this relationship. I will propose any substantive changes on this Talk page rather than editing the article directly, and I welcome independent review and editing by other contributors.

== Relume ==
Relume is a private company whose primary product is a Saas tool. It was founded in 2020 by Dan Anisse and Adam Mura in Sydney, who first ran a website design agency before turning to software [ref: Relume: The Aussie website creator powering Trump's meme coin, Forbes Australia]. Relume offers a suite of tools based on AI to improve website building workflows with planning, designing and building tools for marketing websites [ref: Meet Relume, the bootstrapped AI web builder that wants to supercharge Figma and Webflow, TechCrunch]. They have 5 core products, Relume Publish, Relume Component Library, Relume MCP, Relume Export and Relume Style Guide Builder.

Relume's first product, the Relume Library, was a collection of 1000+ website components for both Webflow and Figma, launched in November 2021. In August 2023 it added an AI site builder that could generate sitemaps and wireframes from a text prompt, then export to Webflow, Figma and later, React, called Relume Export [ref: What's New — Relume AI Website Builder Updates, www.relume.ai]. In August 2026 it launched Relume Publish, a website builder with hosting, moving beyond exporting to publish sites itself.

Relume has grown without venture capital. It reportedly turned down a US$35 million acquisition offer in 2024 [ref: #2: Dan Anisse - Going global from day one, building a brand synonymous with design, supercharging growth with their home run AI product & turning down $35m to stay the course by Remarkable By Design, Spotify for Creators].

== History ==

=== Relume Component Library ===
Before Relume, Dan had founded several businesses, including Foenix and Lumio. Lumio was later acquired for an unknown amount.Dan & Adam started a Webflow design agency in August 2020 [ref: Productising Agency Insights — Dan (Relume) · UntilNow, www.untilnow.com.au]. To speed up repetitive wire framing work, they built an internal tool to which now represents the Relume Component Library, which became their first product. Founding engineer Daniel Slater later joined as a third co-founder and CTO, and the agency was phased out once the Relume Component Library covered costs [ref: Relume — AI Website Builder for Marketing Websites, www.relume.ai]. Early staff included people that worked at Canva, Antler and [https://mitti.com/ Mitti].

The Relume Component Library launched in November 2021 as a library of copy-and-paste components for Webflow. In December 2021 the components adopted a fluid responsive method built with [https://finsweet.com/ Finsweet], and were later made compatible with Finsweet;s Client-First class naming system. A free Figma kit followed on in February 2022, along with a community website and voting board for requesting components. From April 2022 the company released new components on the first Monday of every month aptly named "Component Day" by Relume and their customer base known as "Lumers". A Chrome extension and a class-syncing tool for Webflow entered beta in November 2022.

=== Relume Export ===
Relume added an AI sitemap generator in June 2023 and launched the full AI Site Builder using its Webflow compatible component system in August 2023. According to TechCrunch, about 10,000 people signed up in the two weeks after launch, bringing Relume's total user base to around 54,000. The company had 7 staff at the time. Webflow CEO Vlad Magdalin public praised the AI feature set.

In 2024 Relume released a React component library, which then left beta in December 2024. By 2024, the Relume team had grown to 11 people. Dan said in interviews that he turned down a US$35 million acquisition offer in 2024.

In January 2025 Forbes Australia reported that the website for the Official Trump meme coin had been build with Relume and hosted on Webflow. The same article reported more that 500,000 sign ups and a 12,000 member slack community. During 2025, Relume added React and HTML export, an AI Style Guide Builder and compatibility with Figma Sites.

=== Relume Publish ===
In May 2026 it added export of design systems to Anthropic's Claude Design and in July it released an MCP server that made it's component library available to AI agents and coding tools.

In August 2026, Relume launched Relume Publish into Beta, a website builder that hosts sites directly instead of relying on export to third party tools and providers. It added a Publish MCP server shortly after for building sites from Claude or ChatGPT on the 14th October 2026 and a content management system (CMS) later in the same month.

== Business Model ==
Relume sells subscriptions on a freemium model aimed at freelance designers, web design agencies and marketing teams. Pricing started at US$32 a month in 2023. As of 2026, building a site is free, paid plans can add more AI usage, and hosting on a custom domain is charged per site.

The company has not raised outside capital. It is bootstrapped and funded early development from agency revenue and according to Dan, was profitable by September 2024 [ref: Building a Profitable AI-Driven Design Platform Without VC Funding, Day One]. Dan said about 80% of new users arrive through organic channels rather than paid marketing.

== Reception and community ==
TechCrunch described Relume in 2023 as building on top of existing and established design platforms rather than replacing them. It noted that this gave Relume access to their large user bases, but left it exposed if those platforms restricted access or had a competing product. That same article listed Wix as a competitor in AI website generation. TechRadar rate Relume 3.5 out of 5 in May 2024. It praised the use of AI to be an orchestrator, arranging human designed components and recognising the collaborative features. It called the product expensive for a Webflow or Figma add-on and noted functionality issues on some components [ref: Relume AI website builder review 2024, TechRadar].

Relume runs a slack community for designers and agencies. It had about 4,500 members in August 2023, more than 11,000 in September 2024, and over 12,000 in January 2025. Members use it to share work, ask for feedback, find jobs and Relume uses it to gather requests for features, betas and components.

Ronald Sardick Ogenrwot (October,10 1994), known professionally as Exaa RapKing, is an Ugandan rapper, singer, dancer, songwriter, video director from Gulu city. [ref: Exaa Rapking's Profile, News, New and Old Songs - Luo Tunes, luotunes.com]

Exaa recorded the greatest number of singles in Gulu.

Most of Exaa's singles were Hip-hop and Rap music.

== Early Life ==
Exaa Wa born in Bungatira Sub-County currently Pece-Laroo Division in Gulu,Uganda to his late father Toojan Dick Odwong & his mother Mego Florence Toojan, he attentended his primary education at Bungatira Central Primary School from P.1-P6 then join Bungatira P.7 School were he sat for his PLE Certificate and later on join Gulu Army Secondary School from S.1-S2, and then later he went to St. Patrick's College for his S.3 which he later dropped in the third term due to lack of school fees.

In the year 2012 he did a certificate in computer applications which made him one of the most computer wizard in his community by then. He later on went ahead and a certificate in Business in the year 2016 then in 2018 he did video production together with graphic & and design.

Exaa RapKing was born and raised from Gulu City and started falling in love with music in 2005 after loosing his father Toojan Dick Odwong.

His family were not happy seeing him join the music industry but he later made up his mind as a young man who wanted to follow his heart desires and gold.

In 2014, he switched to dancing due to family pressure on him not to do music and concentrate in schools, and he never wanted to hurt his mother.

In 2017, He sat down with his brothers and told them about his music career and some agreed and others didn't so he recorded a hit song "I Can't Let It Go" ft Rapper Due in that same year 2017 before he parted ways when Rapper Due was in a serious beef with Judah RapKnowledge that year.

Since then he was on and off due to work until late 2018 when he dropped "Miss Dayana" and organised a HipHop Cypher call BOJ CYPHER in that same year, and from those two singles many people began to encourage him to take music as a serious deal.

Then boom in 2019 before leaving Gulu for Kampala to work with MTN Uganda. So per now he is doing both music and video production with BOJfilms which he founded in the year 2023 and currently he has about 20 songs [ref: Download and Listen to All Exaa Rapking Music, Songs and Audio, northernbuzz.biz]

From 2011 - 2017 he work as a businessman

2018 - 2020 he works with MTN Uganda as a salesman

2020 - 2021 as a businessman

2022 - 2024 Manager at NSB Music Studio

2022 - 2024, August as Drone Pilot and a video director at Jack Studio Gulu

data.title: BPL Medical Technologies
data.text:
BPL Medical Technologies Private Limited is an Indian medical technology company headquartered in Bengaluru, Karnataka. Its medical-technology business traces its origins to 1967, when the BPL Group began producing medical electronics, including electrocardiographs and patient monitors. The company was later incorporated as a separate legal entity in December 2012, and BPL's healthcare business was transferred to it in August 2013. [ref: Goldman Sachs picks up 49% stake in BPL Med, Business Standard] [ref: BPL Medical Technologies Private Limited, The Economic Times] [ref: BPL's healthcare biz transferred to BPL Medical Technologies, Moneycontrol]

The company manufactures and distributes medical devices and related healthcare technology, with activities spanning cardiology, critical care, surgery and diagnostic imaging. It operates manufacturing facilities in Palakkad, Kerala, and Bengaluru, Karnataka. [ref: BPL med-tech journeys up the innovation curve, aims to develop one-third of its products inhouse by 2030, The Hindu BusinessLine] [ref: BPL MedTech's second manufacturing facility in Bengaluru inaugurated, Medical Buyer]

data.title: Mynul Islam
data.text:
Mynul Islam () is a Bangladeshi-American journalist, broadcast news editor, and international affairs correspondent based in New York City. Over a career spanning more than 15 years in television and digital media, he has covered global diplomacy, United Nations proceedings, Bangladesh–United States relations, and affairs concerning the Bangladeshi diaspora. [ref: সাংবাদিকতায় বিশেষ অবদানে ফোবানা সম্মাননা পেলেন মাইনুল ইসলাম, 71 Sangbad]

Islam currently serves as a Special Correspondent for Channel i USA, Editor of The Bangla Hour, and Head of News at BHTV. [ref: Channel i, Impress Telefilm mark 28th anniversary in New York, The Business Standard] He is also the International Affairs Secretary of the International Relations Reporters Forum (IRRF) in Bangladesh.

== Early life and education ==
Islam completed his higher education in Bangladesh, earning degrees in business and law, including a Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA), a Master of Business Administration (MBA), and a Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.).

== Career ==

=== Television journalism in Bangladesh (2009–2023) ===
Islam began his career in television journalism in 2009 when he joined Ekushey Television (ETV) as a news reporter. During his tenure at ETV, he covered national politics, economic affairs, and social issues, eventually being promoted to Staff Reporter. In 2014, he received ETV's Best Reporting Award.

In 2016, Islam joined GTV as a Staff Reporter. He covered major national assignments and was promoted to Assignment Editor in 2023, where he managed newsroom assignments, field reporter deployment, and live news coordination. [ref: সাংবাদিকতায় বিশেষ অবদানে ফোবানা সম্মাননা পেলen মাইনুল ইসলাম, 71 Sangbad]

Parallel to his broadcast work, Islam served as a part-time instructor at the Bangladesh Institute of Journalism & Electronic Media (BIJAM) from 2014 to 2023, training aspiring reporters in broadcast presentation and field journalism.

=== International journalism and U.S. media (2024–present) ===
Following his relocation to the United States, Islam expanded his focus toward international diplomacy and diaspora journalism. In 2025, he joined Channel i USA as a Special Correspondent and presenter. Based at the United Nations Headquarters in New York City, he has reported on multiple sessions of the United Nations General Assembly, including UNGA 2019, 2023, 2024, and 2026.

In addition to broadcast journalism, Islam serves as Editor of The Bangla Hour and oversees news production as Head of News for BHTV. In October 2026, he was honored at the United Nations Plaza during the Global Summit on Paid Period Leave for his journalism and coverage of social welfare issues. [ref: Global Summit on Paid Period Leave Held in New York: Journalist Mynul Islam Honored, The Bangla Hour]

data.title: Alam nyo na
data.text:
----

Alam Nyo Na, also known as RJ Sabuero, is the public persona of Filipino trivia content creator Robin James A. Sabuero, a graduate of Bachelor of Arts in Mass Communication, major in Broadcasting, from Palawan State University in Puerto Princesa City, Philippines.

He is known for producing educational content about biodiversity, wildlife, environmental conservation, local history, geography, and lesser-known facts, particularly those related to Palawan and other parts of the Philippines.

Before establishing his identity as a trivia content creator, Sabuero worked as a broadcaster for Radyo Bandera Philippines, Radyo Mo Nationwide (RMN), and the Philippine Broadcasting Service–Bureau of Broadcast Services (PBS-BBS).

Through Alam Nyo Na, Sabuero aims to make knowledge more accessible to the general public. Recognizing that not everyone enjoys reading books or has the opportunity to visit libraries, he takes the initiative to read, research, and translate information from books, scientific studies, and other credible sources into engaging video content using language and storytelling that ordinary Filipinos can easily understand and enjoy. His goal is to bring the knowledge contained in books to audiences through videos, allowing them to discover and appreciate valuable information in a more accessible and entertaining format.

A particular focus of his work is giving greater visibility to scientific research on biodiversity. He believes that important studies conducted by researchers deserve opportunities to reach wider audiences beyond academic institutions and scientific publications. Through Alam Nyo Na, he seeks to bridge the gap between scientific research and public understanding by transforming complex findings into engaging educational stories without losing their essential meaning.

Sabuero has also collaborated with government agencies, other organizations, and fellow biodiversity content creators to develop and share educational content about biodiversity and environmental conservation.

Alam Nyo Na maintains an online presence on Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok, where it shares trivia, educational stories, and informative videos designed to spark curiosity and encourage appreciation of the Philippines' natural and cultural heritage.

data.title: EBTNA
data.text:
== European Biotechnology Thematic Network Association (EBTNA) ==
The European Biotechnology Thematic Network Association (EBTNA) is an international association concerned with biotechnology education and cooperation between academic institutions and industry [ref: Biotechnology worldwide and the 'European Biotechnology Thematic Network' Association (EBTNA), Current Opinion in Biotechnology]. It was formally established in Perugia, Italy, in 2007 by Mariapia Viola-Magni, following an earlier biotechnology network [ref: ].

The association organises the European Biotechnology Congress. The 2016 congress took place in Riga, Latvia, where the association also held its general assembly and elected its governing board [ref: European Biotechnology Congress 2016 – Water Research laboratory]. In September 2025, EBTNA organised the congress in Tirana, Albania, with support from the Academy of Sciences of Albania [ref: European Biotechnology Congress 2025, which will take place from 11–13 September 2025 in Tirana, Albania., fshmn.uni-pr.edu]. The meeting brought together approximately 200 researchers, lecturers, students and industry representatives [ref: https://ueaa.info/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/UEAA-OCTOBER-NEWSLETTER-No-10.pdf].

data.title: Jai Krishna Ghattamaneni
data.text:
Jai Krishna Ghattamaneni is an Indian actor who works in Telugu cinema. He is the son of actor and film producer Ghattamaneni Ramesh Babu, the grandson of actor Krishna, and the nephew of actor Mahesh Babu. [ref: Jai Krishna: Pressure pushes me to choose better stories, The New Indian Express]

==Career==

Jai Krishna appeared as a child artist in the Telugu film Nijam (2003), directed by Teja and starring Mahesh Babu. [ref: Nijam Cast & Crew, Moviefone] In a 2026 interview, he recalled that he had acted in Nijam as a child but had little memory of the experience because of his young age.

He subsequently trained in acting in Mumbai, Puducherry and New York. He also trained in gymnastics and martial arts.

Jai Krishna made his debut as a lead actor with Srinivasa Mangapuram, directed by Ajay Bhupathi. The film stars him opposite Rasha Thadani and was released in July 2026. He portrays Srinu, a young man who falls in love with Manga, played by Thadani. [ref: Jai Krishna: Pressure pushes me to choose better stories, Cinema Express]

==Personal life==

Jai Krishna is the son of actor and film producer Ghattamaneni Ramesh Babu and Mrudula. His paternal grandfather was actor Krishna, and his paternal uncle is actor Mahesh Babu.

== Hanish Gupta ==

Hanish Gupta is an Indian entrepreneur and Corporate Executive who is the founder, promoter, and Managing Director of Sunkind India Limited which specialises within India in solar energy Project Development, Design Engineering, Procurement & Construction (solar EPC), Solar Component Manufacture, and battery energy storage. [ref: Draft Red Herring Prospectus: Sunkind India Limited, Sunkind India Limited / National Stock Exchange of India]

== Career ==
With over 16 years of experience within Industrial Engineering, Steel Manufacturing, and Renewable Energy industries. Hanish Gupta had previously sat on various Industrial and Manufacturing company boards such as J.D. Industries India Limited and J.D. Metalloys Limited. [ref: Director Profile: Hanish Gupta (DIN 02194659), ZaubaCorp]

Hanish Gupta co founded Sunkind India Limited in September 2019. He became a director of the company in April 2021 and became Managing Director on June 27, 2025. [ref: Draft Red Herring Prospectus: Sunkind India Limited, Sunkind India Limited / National Stock Exchange of India] As Managing Director Hanish Gupta leads the company strategy, business planning, project delivery, company governance and backward integration strategy into Solar Mounting Structure Manufacturing (Strucmax brand) and Photovoltaic Module manufacture. [ref: By 2030, We Aim to Contribute 10–12 GW Cumulatively: Hanish Gupta, Sunkind Energy, Energetica India]

== Industry commentary and public affairs ==
Hanish Gupta writes articles and engages with the media on various topics concerning the renewable energy sector in India.

* Grid Infrastructure & Energy Storage: Hanish Gupta wrote an article for The Financial Express in September 2026 discussing improvements to India’s Power Transmission Infrastructure, integration of Renewable Energy into the Grid and viability of Battery Energy Storage Systems. In June 2026 Hanish Gupta spoke about funding large capital renewable storage projects in an interview with BusinessWorld. [ref: "Solar And Storage Must Go Together", Says Hanish Gupta, Founder & MD, Sunkind India Ltd, BW Hotelier / BusinessWorld]
* Solar Manufacturing & Geopolitics: Hanish Gupta wrote an analysis piece for PV Magazine India July 2026 discussing the geopolitics of Solar Manufacturing globally, including China’s dominance of the supply chain and how India can develop their own Wafer and Cell manufacturing. [ref: The geopolitics of solar manufacturing and how India can build a China-alternative supply chain, pv magazine India]
* Domestic Manufacturing & Policy: Hanish Gupta wrote an opinion piece for ET EnergyWorld in December 2025 discussing policy developments within the PLI scheme and how India is pushing to localise clean energy manufacturing. [ref: Inside India's push to localize its solar future, ETEnergyworld (The Economic Times)]
* Business Leadership & Manufacturing Growth: Hanish Gupta discussed vertical integration, energy security and manufacturing growth at Sunkind in an exclusive interview with APAC News Network in July 2026. [ref: 'Domestic manufacturing strengthens energy security by reducing import dependence': Hanish Gupta, Founder & Managing Director, Sunkind India Limited, APAC News Network]

data.title: Hotta Studio
data.text:
Hotta Studio is a Chinese video game developer based in Suzhou, Jiangsu, China. It is wholly owned by Perfect World (完美世界股份有限公司, SZSE: 002624). The studio specializes in developing free-to-play open-world action RPGs with anime-inspired aesthetics for mobile platforms, PC, and consoles. It is best known for creating Tower of Fantasy (幻塔) and Neverness to Everness (异环).

The name "Hotta" is a phonetic transliteration of the Chinese 幻塔 (huàn tǎ, "phantom tower"), the title of the studio's debut game. In international markets, the company also operates under the trade name Hottagames Co., Ltd., which is used for contracts with overseas partners and press materials.

== History ==

=== Origins and founding (2018) ===

The studio's founder and long-standing head is Zhang Yu (张御, also known as Kee Zhang). Before founding Hotta Studio, Zhang Yu worked for many years at Snail Games, where he led Black Gold Studio (黑金工作室). Under his leadership, projects included Voyage Century (航海世纪), the first three entries in the Taichi Panda (太极熊猫) series, and the Chinese localization of Lineage 2. Zhang Yu has around 19 years of professional experience in game development [ref: [https://www.unrealengine.com/developer-interviews/tower-of-fantasy-leverages-unreal-engine-to-bring-open-world-action-to-mobile-pc-and-playstation Tower of Fantasy leverages Unreal Engine to bring open world action to mobile, PC and PlayStation] ].

In 2018, having decided to focus on developing next-generation open-world games, Zhang Yu left Snail Games and joined Perfect World. There, he was tasked with establishing a completely new in-house studio, and the team that would later become known as Hotta Studio was founded [ref: [https://en.namu.wiki/w/Hotta%20Studio Hotta Studio]]. The project was initially launched as a game under a codename derived from 幻塔 (huàn tǎ, "phantom tower"), which later also gave the studio its name. The legal entity, 苏州幻塔网络科技有限公司, was registered in Suzhou in November 2018 [ref: 苏州幻塔网络科技有限公司].

=== Development of Tower of Fantasy (2018–2021) ===

Development of Tower of Fantasy began in 2018, almost immediately after the studio was founded. The project was Perfect World's response to the success of miHoYo's Genshin Impact. Perfect World viewed the rapidly growing anime-style open-world gacha RPG market as a strategic priority and funded several parallel in-house projects, one of which was Hotta Studio's Tower of Fantasy [ref: 幻塔].

From the outset, the team focused on:

* An open world with large-scale locations and vertical traversal, including parkour and flying vehicles;
* Multiplayer features, including co-op dungeons and PvP zones, distinguishing it from Genshin Impact and its primarily single-player focus;
* A science-fantasy setting combining science fiction and fantasy, which was unconventional for Chinese gacha games;
* A weapon system instead of a traditional character-based system: players obtain weapons, each with a unique combat style [ref: Tower of Fantasy — Weapons].

The game was first publicly showcased at ChinaJoy 2020, where concept trailers featuring anime-inspired art direction were presented. The first closed beta test (CBT-1) took place on 28 October 2020. The results were mixed: the game's overall architecture and design received positive assessments, but its execution was criticized. In response, the studio published what it called a "list of issues to fix" (头秃清单), an initial document containing hundreds of optimization tasks [ref: [https://baijiahao.baidu.com/s?id=1863044756225920058 专访幻塔制作人张御：杨受德是个狠人，对话还原一个真实的Hotta Studio]].

After CBT-1, Zhang Yu and his team worked intensively to improve the game. The second closed beta test (CBT-2) took place on 15 April 2021 and showed a marked improvement in quality. The "List of Issues to Fix 2.0" contained 30% more items than the first version. The third closed beta test (CBT-3) was held on 15 July 2021 and added the Simulacra system (SSR Simulacra) to the game.

=== Chinese and global release of Tower of Fantasy ===

On 16 December 2021, Tower of Fantasy entered public beta in mainland China for iOS and Android. Revenue on the first day was approximately 50 million yuan, and exceeded 500 million yuan (5亿) in the first month, while the number of new users surpassed 10 million [ref: [https://web.archive.org/web/20220305053635/http://notice.10jqka.com.cn/api/pdf/fb900faf62d1691a.pdf 完美世界2022年1月投资者关系活动记录]].

Following the success of CBT-3, Perfect World increased its investment in the project. The studio's staff grew to around 200 people, and funding for marketing and server infrastructure was increased. In January 2022, Perfect World officially announced plans for a global release in mid-2022.

The global release of Tower of Fantasy for iOS, Android, and PC took place on 11 August 2022. The international publisher was Level Infinite, the global publishing brand owned by Tencent. Pre-registrations exceeded 4 million players. Despite strong interest, the launch was marred by serious technical problems: the servers could not handle the influx of players, leaving many users unable to log in during the first few days. Players also reported lag, crashes, and visual bugs. The team had warned in advance about "shortcomings and bugs", but the scale of the problems exceeded expectations [ref: [https://wccftech.com/tower-of-fantasy-drops-today-but-the-genshin-likes-devs-warn-of-bugs-and-shortcomings/ Tower of Fantasy Drops Today, But the Genshin-Like's Devs Warn of Bugs and Shortcomings]].

The game launched on Steam on 20 October 2022 and on the Epic Games Store in May 2023. It was released for PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 on 8 August 2023.

In December 2022, Tower of Fantasy received a Google Play Best of 2022 award in the "Best Game of 2022: Inspiring" category and was also included in the Google Play 2022 Best list as a "Best Game for Tablets (Global)".

The game's total revenue for 2022 exceeded 3 billion yuan (30亿); by 2024, its cumulative global revenue had reached 4 billion yuan (40亿) [ref: [https://www.yoyiputao.com/ 完美世界2023—2024年度报告分析]].

=== Development of Neverness to Everness ===

After completing two phases of urban content development (Mirroria / 镜都) for Tower of Fantasy, the Hotta Studio team had gained considerable experience in creating urban environments. Building on that experience, it decided to develop an entirely new project.

On 16 July 2024, Hotta Studio officially announced its second major project, Neverness to Everness (异环, pinyin Yìhuán, literally "Strange Ring"). Unlike Tower of Fantasy, the new project uses Unreal Engine 5 instead of Unreal Engine 4, marking a complete technological transition: the studio retrained its staff from UE4 specialists to UE5 engineers [ref: Crafting the urban open world of NTE: Neverness to Everness with UE5 across PC, PlayStation 5, and mobile].

The announcement revealed that the game had been in development for a substantial period. Its first closed beta test in China took place in November 2024, the global closed beta test was held in July 2025, and the final global beta test took place in February 2026.

| 2026 || Neverness to Everness (异环) || iOS, Android, PC, PS5 || Unreal Engine 5 || Released

== Structure ==

=== Corporate ownership ===

Hotta Studio is an internal studio within Perfect World, rather than an independent developer. Its ownership structure is as follows:

Perfect World Investment & Holding Group (完美世界控股集团有限公司)
→ Perfect World Co., Ltd. (完美世界股份有限公司, SZSE: 002624) — a publicly traded company listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, founded in 2004 by entrepreneur Chi Yufeng (池宇峰)
→ Perfect World Games (完美世界游戏有限责任公司) — the gaming division
→ Suzhou Huanta Network Technology Co., Ltd. (苏州幻塔网络科技有限公司) — a legal entity registered in Suzhou in November 2018; it serves as the developer and holder of licenses and intellectual property rights
→ Hottagames Co., Ltd. — an international operating entity used for contracts with overseas partners (including Epic Games and Sony Interactive Entertainment), streamers, and the press, as well as an English-language brand name.

=== Key personnel ===

* Zhang Yu (张御) / Kee Zhang — producer and director of Tower of Fantasy and producer of Neverness to Everness. Before the studio was founded, he led Black Gold Studio at Snail Games for many years. He is known as a leader deeply involved in game design and visual direction.

* Yang Lei (杨磊) / Yang Lei — executive producer of Neverness to Everness. He became a meme among players after being seen reading from a teleprompter during a pre-launch livestream, earning the nickname "Reading AI" (读稿AI). However, he showed considerably more energy and enthusiasm when discussing game optimization.

=== Staff size ===

Exact staffing figures for different periods have not been publicly disclosed, but indirect estimates include:

* 2018–2019: A compact R&D team estimated at around 50–80 people, mostly veterans from Snail Games and other Perfect World studios.
* 2021 (Tower of Fantasy peak): Around 200 people worked directly on Tower of Fantasy after Perfect World increased investment ahead of the Chinese release.
* 2024–2026 (NTE): Hotta Studio likely expanded its workforce for a project of UE5's scale. A joint technical interview with Epic Games in April 2026 demonstrates the team's high level of specialization and indicates that work continued after Tower of Fantasy.

=== Intellectual property ===

According to corporate registry data, Suzhou Huanta Network Technology has 21 trademark applications, 33 patents (covering inventions related to game mechanics, server architecture, and user interfaces), and 16 software copyright registrations.

== Neverness to Everness ==

Neverness to Everness (Chinese: 异环, pinyin Yìhuán, literally "Strange Ring"; abbreviated NTE) is a free-to-play open-world action RPG developed by Hotta Studio using Unreal Engine 5. It was released in China on 23 April 2026 and internationally on 29 April 2026 for PC, PlayStation 5, iOS, and Android.

=== Setting ===

The game takes place in the fictional modern metropolis of Hethereau, where supernatural anomalies coexist with everyday urban life. Players take on the role of an "Appraiser", the first unlicensed anomaly hunter, and investigate paranormal phenomena across the city.

The game world has been described as a "supernatural urban open world", combining elements of detective noir, supernatural everyday life, and anime aesthetics. Some reviewers have compared the game to "anime GTA".

=== Combat system ===

NTE features a real-time system that allows players to switch between a team of four characters (Espers). Each character has unique abilities that synergize with the others. Characters are classified using two systems: Esper types (Lakshana, Cosmos, Anima, Incantation, Chaos, and Psyche) and class types (gas, solid, liquid, plasma, and synthesis). Combat includes mechanics such as perfect dodge, parry, and aerial combat. Racing and vehicle customization mechanics, including rainy-night street races, have also been confirmed.

The game includes housing and interior customization systems. Non-player characters (NPCs) behave realistically and react to their surroundings. A first-person mode, which initially appeared as a bug during beta testing, was officially added after positive feedback from the community.

=== Technical features ===

The game was developed using Unreal Engine 5, with support for NVIDIA DLSS and ray tracing on PC. Hotta Studio worked closely with Epic Games to optimize the engine for mobile devices; many of the studio's custom optimization solutions were incorporated into later UE5 releases.

For mobile optimization, the priority was stable performance at 90 FPS (Apple had requested 120 FPS, but the studio prioritized stability). All visual effects—including attack animations, weather effects, particles, and water splashes—have three quality levels: low, medium, and high. The developers noted that the main technical challenge was rendering dense urban environments simultaneously: the density of objects rendered at once in the city is significantly higher than in comparable rural or open-world projects.

=== Financial performance ===

On its first day of release, Neverness to Everness generated 100 million yuan (1亿) in revenue across all platforms. This was estimated to equal approximately one-third of its estimated development budget of around 300 million yuan [ref: NTE makes back one third of its development budget in a single day].

== Incidents ==

=== Asset theft in Tower of Fantasy promotional materials ===

In December 2021, shortly before the Chinese release of Tower of Fantasy, one of the game's promotional videos was found to contain stolen weapon and material assets from miHoYo's Honkai Impact 3rd. Hotta Studio issued an official letter of apology (致歉信), explaining that the video had been produced by an outsourced production studio without proper internal review. The studio accepted responsibility for failing to thoroughly review outsourced content.

=== Server overload during the global launch of Tower of Fantasy ===

On 11 August 2022, the day of Tower of Fantasy global release, the servers were overwhelmed by the influx of players: more than 4 million pre-registered users attempted to log in. A significant number of players were unable to connect during the first few days after launch, while those who got in reported severe lag, crashes, and unstable connections.

=== Controversy over AI-generated art in Neverness to Everness ===

A few days after Neverness to Everness launched on 29 April 2026, players identified and publicly raised concerns about assets suspected of being generated by generative AI, including background elements in the game world and promotional posters. The most high-profile incident involved well-known VTuber streamer Ironmouse, who publicly terminated her contract with the studio on 4 May 2026. She stated that representatives of Hotta Studio had assured her team that the game contained no generative AI ("They had told my people that there's literally no AI in it"), which proved not to be true. According to available information, Ironmouse's contract explicitly prohibited the use of generative AI [ref: [https://www.notebookcheck.net/NTE-Neverness-to-Everness-faces-AI-backlash.1290818.0.html NTE: Neverness to Everness faces AI backlash]] [ref: Ironmouse pulls out of streaming Neverness to Everness over AI concerns days after launch].

Hotta Studio officially acknowledged using AI tools in a "small number" of background assets and promised to rework the disputed elements. Community reaction was mixed: some players considered the studio's response adequate, while others noted that only the two most widely publicized assets had been addressed and that the extent of possible AI use might have been broader.

== Technology ==

=== Game engines ===

* Tower of Fantasy: a modified version of Unreal Engine 4 (version 4.26) [ref: [https://baike.baidu.com/item/幻塔/51536048 幻塔]]
* Neverness to Everness: Unreal Engine 5

=== Patents and technological solutions ===

Hotta Studio's patents (33 in total, according to corporate registry data) include technologies related to game mechanics. One notable patent is "Character Climbing Method and Apparatus", which describes an algorithm for detecting obstacles, emitting a detection ray, and evaluating whether climbing is possible [ref: [https://www.patentguru.com/assignee/suzhou-huanta-network-technology-co-ltd Suzhou Huanta Network Technology Co., Ltd. patents]].

Pei-Kun Xi (; October 24, 1948 – December 30, 2005) was a Chinese-American conductor, composer, and music educator. He was a prominent figure in the post-1970 classical, film, and operatic scenes in Shanghai—most notably serving as the music director and conductor of the Shanghai Philharmonic Orchestra (上海乐团)—before immigrating to the United States in 1985. [ref: Table of Contents: Cover Photo Credits, Yinyue Aihaozhe (音乐爱好者 / Music Lover)] Following his relocation to the United States, his career expanded into guest conducting across major American symphonies. He specialized in arranging and performing works that seamlessly fused traditional Chinese instruments with a full Western classical orchestra, while fostering community arts development in the San Francisco Bay Area. He dedicated his life to orchestral leadership across both China and the United States spanning decades until he died in 2005. [ref: Him Mark Lai Research Files, Organizational Records: Box 9, Folder 8 (Xi, Peikun), East Asian Library, University of California, Berkeley] [ref: Pei-Kun Xi Obituary, Obituary Notice]

== Early life and education ==

Pei-Kun was born on October 24, 1948, in Shanghai, China. He began his early musical training on the flute, piano, violin, and other traditional Chinese instruments from 1956 to 1968. In 1969, he graduated from the Middle School affiliated with the Shanghai Conservatory of Music (上海音乐学院附中), where he majored in bassoon and flute. Between 1980 and 1982, he pursued private studies in orchestral conducting under the French conductor Jean Périsson and Chinese conductor Yi-Jun Hung in Shanghai.

In 1985, Pei-Kun immigrated to the United States to advance his academic and practical training on a full scholarship:
* 1985–1987: Studied conducting under Peter Black at the San Francisco Institute of Music and Arts.
* 1987–1989: Earned a Master of Arts in Music (Conducting) under Carl St. Clair at the New England Conservatory of Music.
* 1990: Selected as a Special Conducting Fellow at the Tanglewood Music Center by invitation of Seiji Ozawa, where he studied under Ozawa, Leonard Bernstein, and André Previn.
* 1990: Appointed as an Artist Diploma Candidate in Conducting at Boston University under David Hoose.

== Career ==
=== China Era (1969–1985) ===
Upon graduating from the Music Middle School Affiliated to Shanghai Conservatory of Music (上海音乐学院附中) in 1969, Pei-Kun joined the orchestra of the Shanghai Peking Opera Theatre（上海京剧团）for its production of the opera Taking Tiger Mountain by Strategy (智取威虎山), serving as its orchestra conductor for ten years. Throughout the 1970s, he served as a principal conductor for both the Shanghai and Peking Opera companies, conducting over 600 performances across six distinct Chinese operas.

From 1978 to 1985, Pei-Kun served as the music director and conductor of the Shanghai Philharmonic Orchestra (上海乐团), leading more than 40 concert programs per season. Concurrently, from 1981 to 1985, he served as the principal conductor for the Shanghai Youth Orchestra.

During this era, Pei-Kun was active in the Chinese film industry, working as the music director and conductor for three feature films and several television screen productions between 1971 and 1984. He recorded a catalogue of commercial albums, LPs, and cassettes, establishing a reputation as one of China's prominent young conductors of the period.

=== United States and guest conducting ===

After completing his graduate studies at Boston's New England Conservatory of Music, Pei-Kun relocated to San Francisco in 1992, frequently guest-conducting major symphonies, cultural and holiday concert programs across the United States. While a comprehensive catalog of his performances during this time period is not undocumented in public archives, his notable conducting engagements—many of which spotlighted traditional Chinese music alongside Western classical repertoire—included the following highlights:

* 1991: Led performances with the New England Symphony Orchestra and the Boston Civic Symphony Orchestra.
* 1992: Guest-conducted the Longwood Symphony Orchestra in Boston.
* 1993: Conducted the South Bay Chamber Orchestra Concert (南湾室内乐团音乐会) in California.
* 1994: Directed the *Summer Melody* (夏日旋律) concert program.
* 1994: Conducted the inaugural kickoff celebration of the Eastern Philharmonic Orchestra（东方爱乐乐团）in the San Francisco Bay Area.
* 1995: Appointed guest conductor for the *Silk Road Music Concert* (丝绸之路音乐会) composition and conducting program hosted at San Francisco State University during the regional Chinese Arts Festival (旧金山地区海华文艺季活动).
* 1995: Led the Boston University Symphony Orchestra.
* Other Engagements:** Served as a guest conductor for the Brooklyn Symphony Orchestra (New York), the Oakland Symphony (California), the Philadelphia Orchestra, the Evans Symphony, and the Los Angeles United Symphony Orchestra.

From 1995 to 1996, Pei-Kun returned to China by invitation to conduct a series of high-profile concerts, leading both the Shanghai Symphony Orchestra and the Shanghai Traditional Chinese Orchestra.

=== Later positions and community impact ===

In his later years, Pei-Kun served as a music professor at Laney College in Oakland, California. He co-founded and conducted the 125-member Great Wall Youth Orchestra and served as the principal composer and arranger for the Purple Silk Music Education Foundation, focusing his efforts on introducing young generations to music. He also served as the conductor for the Los Angeles United Symphony Orchestra and taught music in Chinese universities while he was receiving cancer treatments.

== Selected Compositions ==

* Dunhuang Suite (敦煌组曲) — Orchestral Work
* Stone Forest Rhapsody (石林随想曲) — Orchestral Work
* Man Jiang Hong (满江红) — Guzheng Concerto
* Dance of the Yao Tribe — Arrangement
* Flower Drum Song — Arrangement
* Sisters of the Grassland — Arrangement

== Personal life ==

During his early career in China, Pei-Kun was married to Kang-Nan Li, a vocalist who worked alongside him at the Shanghai Philharmonic Orchestra (上海乐团). The couple performed numerous concerts together. The marriage ended in the early 1980s. Together they had one daughter, Yalun.

data.title: Baran–Shivpuri railway line
data.text:
The Baran-Shivpuri new railway line is a proposed railway line between Baran in Rajasthan and Shivpuri in Madhya Pradesh, India.

== History ==

Indian Railways completed a survey for the proposed Baran-Shivpuri railway line in 2013-14. A Railway Board document dated 26 August 2014 listed the proposed line as long, with an estimated cost of Rs. 778 crore. The survey report was under examination at the time. [ref: Details of Surveys Completed During the Last 10 Years as on 26 August 2014, Indian Railways]

West Central Railway's 2014-15 annual report stated that the revised survey report for the line had been submitted to the Railway Board. [ref: Annual Report 2014-15, West Central Railway]

data.title: Bryan Sperry
data.text:
Bryan Sperry is a visual artist based in Chicago, Illinois, known for his commissioned artwork and participation in the Chicago Art District. Sperry was the original founder and main force behind Pilsen Art Nation, which originated the [http://chicagoartsdistrict.org/secondfridays_main.asp 2nd Friday Art Walk] in the Chicago Pilsen neighborhood. [ref: Chicago Art District, chicagoartsdistrict.org] [ref: In Chicago, the Pilsen neighborhood reflects Mexican flavors, Washington Post] [ref: In Chicago, colorful Pilsen broadens its palate, Chicago Tribune] His works have been featured in various exhibitions, such as the "Warriors of the Apocalypse" series. [ref: Warriors of The Apocalypse Series By Brian Sperry, The Worley Gig] [ref: Warriors of the Apocalypse - The Visualist, The Visualist - Chicago Visual Arts Calendar] [ref: ]

== Education ==
Bryan Sperry attended the School of the Art Institute of Chicago.

== Notable Works ==
The Warriors of the Apocalypse: This sculptural series is a standout in Sperry's body of work, featuring life-size cyborg figures made from recycled elements of the urban landscape. Set in a post-apocalyptic world of the year 3095, these sculptures represent hybrid super soldiers fighting against tyranny and oppression. The series serves as an awareness campaign, illustrating the control exerted by media, propaganda, and government.

== Exhibitions ==
House of the Apocalypse: Sperry's Pilsen gallery, located at 1908 S. Halsted Street, Chicago, is a significant venue where his work, including "The Warriors of the Apocalypse," is displayed.

Sensible Decisions: This exhibition featured works by Bryan Sperry among other artists and was presented as an interwoven installation. It showcased Sperry's ability to blend strong lines and industrial elements with whimsical expressions, highlighting themes of alienation and the contemporary quest for truth and beauty. [ref: Sensible Decisions - The Visualist, The Visualist - Chicago Visual Arts Calendar]

IMPACTinterview: This exhibition featured works by Bryan Sperry alongside other artists and was also presented as an interwoven installation. The collaborative nature of this show allowed for a diverse exploration of contemporary issues through visual art. [ref: IMPACTinterview — lithium.gallery, lithium.gallery]

Other known exhibitions:
* Design Cloud – 2012 [ref: Chicago Art District, chicagoartsdistrict.org]
* Carlos Humenez Gallery – 2012
* Flexspace – 2010
* MK Gallery – 2009
* Zhou B. Space – 2009
* Blake Palmer Gallery – 2006
* Corrosive Gallery – 2005
* Open Door Gallery – 2004
* Mars Gallery – 2003
* Humility Gallery – 1998
* Eastwick Gallery – 1995
* Randolph Street Gallery – 1995
* Around The Coyote – 1993–1997
* Art Attack – 1993

== Installations ==
* Field Museum Campus – 2009
* "Cool Globes" Sculpture Tour – 2009

== Style ==
Expressionistic Edginess: Sperry's art often features strong lines that evoke a sense of order, while also incorporating whimsical lines, facial expressions, or gestures for human emphasis. This juxtaposition creates an expressionistic edge that offers a contemporary slant on themes of truth and beauty. [ref: Listenbee, www.listenbee.com]

Industrial and Robotic Themes: His works, particularly in sculpture, are formulated with robotic and industrial elements, which dominate the senses and contribute to the overarching theme of alienation present throughout his art.

== Mediums ==
Figurative Paintings: Sperry's paintings utilize line, texture, form, and color, with a strong use of light and shadow. His methodical approach to line work results in dynamic, multi-dimensional images that have a sculptural impact.

Abstracts: In his abstract works, Sperry combines free-flowing color with gravity and slope, creating a balance between randomness and controlled illusion. This technique creates spatial contrast and evokes the sense of imagined objects within an infinite space.

Sculptures: Sperry is particularly noted for his found-object warrior sculptures, which are made from recycled elements from the urban landscape. These sculptures bring life to materials from urban decay and are characterized by their bold, dramatic presence, often with a tragic-comic or opposing force aspect.

data.title: CycloGen AI
data.text:
= CycloGen AI =
CycloGen AI, Inc. is a Canadian biotechnology software company developing artificial intelligence tools for structure-guided molecular discovery. The company was incorporated in British Columbia on January 8, 2026. [ref: BC Registry, CycloGen AI]

CycloGen AI develops a no-code computational platform that integrates protein structure prediction, molecular docking, structural biology, protein binder engineering, ligand design, and virtual screening. [ref: CycloGen AI - Enterprise AI Drug Discovery Platform, CycloGen AI]

The company's software is intended for biotechnology companies, pharmaceutical research organizations, contract research organizations, and academic institutions. [ref: whiteford research database, CycloGen AI]

== History ==
CycloGen AI was established in British Columbia, Canada, in 2026. [ref: BC Registry, CycloGen AI]

The company develops computational tools intended to integrate structural biology, machine learning, and molecular modelling within a unified software environment. [ref: CycloGen AI - Enterprise AI Drug Discovery Platform, CycloGen AI]

== Technology ==
CycloGen AI develops software for structure-guided molecular discovery. [ref: CycloGen AI - Enterprise AI Drug Discovery Platform, CycloGen AI]

Its platform includes tools for protein structure prediction, molecular docking, nanobody and mini-binder design, mutation analysis, ligand discovery, and target identification. [ref: CycloGen AI - Enterprise AI Drug Discovery Platform, CycloGen AI]

The company offers on-premises software deployment intended to support organizations working with proprietary biological and molecular research data. [ref: CycloGen AI - Enterprise AI Drug Discovery Platform, CycloGen AI]

== Business and Research Applications ==
CycloGen AI operates primarily as a computational discovery software provider rather than a clinical-stage therapeutics developer. [ref: CycloGen AI Enterprise AI Drug Discovery Platform, CycloGen AI]

Its technology is intended to support early-stage drug discovery, protein engineering, structural analysis, and computational evaluation of molecular candidates.
