data.title: The Igbo Wolf
data.text:
Christian Obi, known online as The Igbo Wolf, is a Nigerian content creator, comedian and actor. He is known for comedy skits featuring recurring characters such as Professor Uwa, an Igbo lecturer in a Yoruba school, and for a series of ironic "happy to be at work" selfies that spread widely on Twitter in 2022. [ref: Creator Spotlight: How the Igbo Wolf Became a Social Media Trendsetter, Zikoko] [ref: #BNCreativesCorner: Through Content Creation, Christian Obi (The Igbo Wolf) Lays Bare His Dreams and Utopia, BellaNaija] He made his feature film debut in the 2024 film Japa!. [ref: Glazing Hot With... Content Creator and Budding Actor, The Igbo Wolf, Glazia] Alongside his creative work, he works as a product manager in the finance industry in Lagos. [ref: How The Igbo Wolf Combines Content Creation With His 9 To 5, PiggyVest Blog]

== Early life and education ==
Obi grew up in a family of four boys. He took part in cultural dance in primary school, and in secondary school he directed and acted in school plays. He wanted to attend the film school PEFTI, but instead studied computer science at Igbinedion University. At university he joined the dance and drama group.

He completed his National Youth Service Corps in Yenagoa, Bayelsa State, where he worked as a teacher and wrote, acted and danced for the local cultural group, for which he also wrote a play.

== Career ==
=== Early career ===
After national service, Obi took freelance writing, graphic design and early UI/UX work, and was paid to write a television series for Africa Magic that was not produced. He later worked in customer support at a travel company before resigning in late 2019 to study data analytics, shortly before the COVID-19 pandemic. During the pandemic he earned income from brand campaigns on Twitter and posted a recurring news-style video series called "Twitter Happenings". He subsequently moved into strategy and then product management, focusing on financial technology.

=== Content creation ===
Obi posted his first Instagram skit in 2019 but paused because of his phone's poor quality. He resumed in August 2021 after buying a new phone, and a skit using an underwater mermaid filter went viral within days.

On 21 September 2021 he posted a skit on Twitter as Professor Uwa, an Igbo lecturer taking a roll call of Yoruba student names that carry unflattering meanings in Igbo. The character was inspired by a secondary school teacher who mispronounced a classmate's name. An improvised closing line, "Dazz ya name?", became a widely used meme on Nigerian Twitter, and the video passed 40,000 views overnight. The success of the skit led to his first direct brand partnership.

In January 2022 Obi began posting selfies of himself looking miserable with ironic captions about how happy he was to go to work. The posts went viral in February 2022, and users across Africa and beyond responded with similar photos of their own.

His other recurring characters include Work Chris, a frustrated employee; RonkeHR, a human resources officer; Mama Elo, a Nigerian reimagining of Maye Musk; Chimoney; Mama Chekwube and Chekwube. His style avoids slapstick, voiceovers and sound effects, and he writes, directs, shoots and edits his skits himself, usually in single takes. His stage name combines his ethnicity with the idea of a lone wolf.

=== Acting ===
Obi appeared in MTV Shuga and Getting Ahead before making his feature film debut in Japa! (2024), produced by Inkblot Productions, alongside Adesua Etomi-Wellington, Jidekene Achufusi, Mofe Duncan, Layi Wasabi, Seun Ajayi and Blossom Chukwujekwu. He has said he hopes to work in Asaba-based Nollywood productions.

=== Public engagements ===
In July 2024 Obi was a panellist at the Student Leader Launchpad held by African Women on Board at the University of Lagos, where he spoke on social media as a leadership tool. [ref: African Women on Board tackles youth Apathy; Hosts future Leaders at UNILAG, ThisDay]

data.title: Webtronaut Innovations
data.text:
Webtronaut Innovations LLC is an American internet holding company based in Albuquerque, New Mexico. It was founded by Sahil Kazi, an Indian/Pakistani serial entrepreneur and SAP Certified Systems Analyst. The group's first venture, the legal-tech marketplace SueEasy, began in 2007 and was a semi-finalist in the inaugural TechCrunch startup competition, TechCrunch40. [ref: Ambulance Chasers Have A New Home, SueEasy, TechCrunch] The company's current ventures include Richlisted, GuiltyAF, SwaxAwards and LabCauldron.

== History ==

=== SueEasy and Filmmortal (2007–2009) ===
Webtronaut's first ventures were developed under the Webtronaut Innovations name (including an Indian entity, Webtronaut Innovations Pvt. Ltd.) and operated from Mountain View, California. [ref: Filmmortal.com, Film Is Immortal. So Is Your Brand, PRLog]

SueEasy, launched in 2007 by Kazi and Faraz Matin, was a marketplace that inverted the traditional lawyer directory: would-be plaintiffs posted grievances and documents, individually or as potential class actions, and licensed attorneys bid for the right to contact the client. Crunchbase lists SueEasy as a sub-organisation of Webtronaut Innovations. [ref: SueEasy — Company Profile, Crunchbase] SueEasy launched publicly in April 2008 with a searchable class-action repository covering nine filing categories. [ref: SueEasy Goes Live — Your Class Action Lawsuit Lottery Ticket, TechCrunch] The ABA Journal described the service as a "reverse Martindale-Hubbell" that matched would-be plaintiffs with lawyers. [ref: New Website Plays Matchmaker For Would-Be Plaintiffs, ABA Journal] United Press International also reported on the service in April 2008. [ref: Web Site Makes Suing Easy] The Los Angeles Daily Journal later profiled SueEasy among attorney-client matchmaking services, quoting Kazi and reporting that more than 1,200 California lawyers were paying customers. [ref: Attorney-Client Matchmakers, Los Angeles Daily Journal] The model also drew criticism from legal commentators over case quality and legal ethics. In September 2009 the business was put up for sale by online auction, [ref: Running SueEasy Turned Out To Be Not So Easy, Overlawyered] According to the company, SueEasy was subsequently acquired by a mass-torts law firm. Company databases list the original company as closed.

In 2008 the group launched Filmmortal, an auction marketplace for product placement, described as "the eBay for product placement," in which independent filmmakers listed projects and advertisers bid to have products placed in them. [ref: Filmmortal — Company Profile, Crunchbase] The launch was covered by BusinessWeek and by GigaOM's NewTeeVee, which described Filmmortal and rival PlaceVine as new matchmakers for product-placement deals, reporting that Kazi had bootstrapped Filmmortal with $130,000 and that placement deals started at around $3,000. [ref: Startups Take on Product Placement Dealmaking, BusinessWeek] [ref: The New Matchmakers: Startups Tackle Product Placement Deals, NewTeeVee] Media in Canada profiled the service in April 2009, calling it an "eBay for product placement" with around 80 projects listed. [ref: Filmmortal breathes life into indie scripts, Media in Canada] IndieWire also covered the service in October 2009. [ref: Product Placement Ought to Know Where It's Being Placed, IndieWire] Product Placement News announced the marketplace in February 2009. [ref: Introducing Filmmortal, Product Placement News] Kazi served as Filmmortal's chief executive. According to the company, Filmmortal was subsequently acquired. Company databases list it as closed.

=== Holding company and current ventures (2023–present) ===
In April 2023 the group launched Richlisted, a service that records members' names on a public blockchain as a permanent record of achievement; a launch announcement quoted Kazi as managing director of Richlisted. [ref: RichListed Launches Exclusive Blockchain-Listed Network for Self-Made Individuals to Showcase Status, PRLog]

In October 2026, Webtronaut Innovations LLC was formed in New Mexico as the holding company for the group's web businesses, which it describes as an "internet holding company operating multiple web-based businesses." [ref: Webtronaut Innovations]

== Ventures ==
=== SueEasy ===
SueEasy (2007–2009) was a legal marketplace and class-action repository. Plaintiffs posted cases across categories including class actions; only licensed attorneys could browse the listings, and attorneys bid for the right to contact a client, with the client free to reject a bidder.

=== Filmmortal ===
Filmmortal (2008) was an online auction marketplace for product-placement deals between independent filmmakers and advertisers, including barter arrangements such as transport, hotels, catering, props and equipment.

=== Richlisted ===
Richlisted (2023–present) offers a one-time paid listing recorded on a public blockchain as a permanent, uneditable record.

=== GuiltyAF ===
GuiltyAF (2025–present) is an interactive live-streamed show in which two parties present a dispute and the audience votes on the outcome in real time.

=== SwaxAwards ===
SwaxAwards is a monthly awards programme recognising creators on TikTok across categories including comedy, dance and wholesome content.

=== LabCauldron ===
LabCauldron (2026–present) is an online platform for IB Biology teachers, with tools for internal assessment moderation, rubric-based task design and lab work management. [ref: LabCauldron]

== Founder ==
Sahil Kazi is an Indian/Pakistani serial entrepreneur and SAP Certified Systems Analyst. His Wellfound profile credits him with two startup launches and exits and describes him as an SAP Certified Consultant. [ref: Webtronaut Innovations: Founder, Leadership & Team, Wellfound] He co-founded SueEasy with Faraz Matin and served as chief executive of Filmmortal. The Org also lists Kazi as Filmmortal's chief executive. [ref: Sahil Kazi — CEO at Filmmortal, The Org]

data.title: Jobstore
data.text:
Jobstore (also known as Jobstore.com) is a global online job search platform headquartered in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. Jobstore provides international talent acquisition, job aggregation, and automated job syndication services for employers and job seekers across Asia-Pacific and international markets.

== History ==
Jobstore was founded in 2015 by entrepreneur Anson Wang, who previously founded regional internet ventures including Recruitmap in 2006 and Joukuu in 2010. [ref: Going Global: Jobstore.com, BFM 89.9 - The Business Station]

During its initial growth phase, Jobstore was structured to provide job distribution services, syndicating employment listings across multiple recruitment sites and social networks to help employers manage cross-border hiring. [ref: SEA tech startups cannot simply copy Chinese models, TechNode Global (TNGlobal)]

But today Jobstore has transferred into a global job search platform servicing in 50+ countries. Jobstore aggregates job listings from thousands of websites, including job sites, staffing firms, associations, and company career pages. [ref: Worldwide Countries, Jobstore]

Jobstore received institutional early-stage investment and venture backing from Cradle Fund, a tech co-investment agency under the Ministry of Finance (Malaysia). [ref: Cradle Fund Portfolio Companies, Cradle Fund Sdn Bhd]

The company's employment metrics and regional labor market research have been cited by regional business publications and economic agencies, such as the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC), to evaluate digital workforce trends and talent demand across Southeast Asia.

In 2018, Jobstore Group initiated preparation for an initial public offering (IPO) on the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX) to finance international market expansion, lodging a public prospectus before deciding to withdraw the application in 2019 to focus on regional organic growth. [ref: Jobstore Group Limited Prospectus, Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC)]

data.title: Bhim
data.text:
Bhim is a town, a tehsil (subdistrict), and a municipality (Nagar Palika) in the Rajsamand district of the state of Rajasthan, India [ref: ] [ref: ] It is one of the blocks that constitute the Rajsamand district and serves as a tehsil headquarters. [ref: Villages in Bhim Tehsil, Rajsamand, Rajasthan, Maps of India]

== Etymology and history ==
Historically, Bhim served as a critical frontier pass and tactical gateway through the central Aravalli Range. The town was positioned at a geographic tri-junction intersecting the traditional borders of the princely states of Mewar, Marwar, and Ajmer-Merwara. Because of this strategic border location, it functioned as an essential mountain outpost for policing trade caravans, monitoring regional military movements, and defending the surrounding territory from external incursions.

Following India's independence and the subsequent integration of the princely states, Bhim became a part of the state of Rajasthan. Originally administered under the Udaipur district, the town was reorganized as the administrative headquarters of the Bhim Tehsil when the Rajsamand district was officially carved out on 10 April 1991 [ref: ].

== Geography ==
Bhim is located at approximately, at an elevation of 594 metres (1,949 ft).The Bhim block covers an area of 687.39 square kilometres and forms part of the Aravalli Mountain Eastern Plain physiographic unit.The Aravalli range enters Bhim tehsil from Ajmer district and continues south-westerly towards Kumbhalgarh and Jarga.

== Demographics [ref: ] ==
As per the 2011 Census, Bhim Tehsil had a population of 171,023, comprising 86,365 males and 84,658 females. The sex ratio was 981 females per 1,000 males. The child population (ages 0–6) was 28,932, or 16.92% of the total population, with a child sex ratio of 901 females per 1,000 males.

The urban population of Bhim Tehsil was 11,568 (5,875 males and 5,693 females), making up 6.76% of the total population. The rural population was 159,455 (80,490 males and 78,965 females), making up 93.24%.

The religious composition of Bhim Tehsil (2011) was recorded as follows: Hindu 161,491 (94.43%), Muslim 7,739 (4.53%), Jain 1,429 (0.84%), religion not stated 189 (0.11%), Christian 159 (0.09%), Sikh 11 (0.01%), Buddhist 3 (0%), and other religions and persuasions 2 (0%).

== Administration ==

=== Municipal administration ===
Bhim is administered as a Nagar Palika (municipality [ref: Bhim Municipality Wards List & Seats, Bharat Survey]). The municipal body is part of Rajsamand district and has a total of 20 wards. Bhim was one of the 248 Municipalities (Nagar Palika) that went to the polls in the 2026 Rajasthan Urban Local Body elections, alongside 10 Municipal Corporations (Nagar Nigam) and 51 Municipal Councils (Nagar Parishad).

The 2026 election [ref: भीम नगर पालिका चुनाव में कांग्रेस को स्पष्ट बहुमत मिला: 20 में से 14 वार्ड जीते, भाजपा को 2 और निर्दलीयों को 4 सीटें मिलीं - Barar (Bhim) News, Dainik Bhaskar] was the first time Bhim held a Nagar Palika election.[reference:14] Voting took place on 11 September 2026 in Phase 2 of the elections. Of the 20 wards, elections were held in 18 wards; in two wards candidates were elected unopposed after nominations were rejected. A total of 7,852 voters were registered, of whom 6,476 voted, registering a turnout of 82.49%. Women voter turnout was 85.06% (3,314 out of 3,896), while male turnout was 79.95% (3,162 out of 3,955), meaning women voted 5.11 percentage points more than men. In the final result, the Indian National Congress won 14 wards, other parties and independents won 4, and the Bharatiya Janata Party won 2.

Historically, a source noted that Bhim remained a panchayat rather than a nagarpalika due to a lack of the requisite population; this status changed with the 2026 municipal election.

=== Tehsil and block administration ===
Bhim is also a tehsil [ref: Bhim Rajsamand - Jatland Wiki, www.jatland.com]and a panchayat samiti headquarters. The Bhim panchayat samiti [ref: ] comprises 33 panchayats and 138 villages, and is located on National Highway 8, 52 kilometres south of Beawar city.

=== State and national politics ===
Bhim is a legislative assembly constituency in Rajsamand district. In the 2023 Rajasthan Assembly election, Harisingh Rawat [ref: ] of the Bharatiya Janata Party won the seat with 93,905 votes (57.46%); Sudarshan Singh Rawat [ref: Sudarshan Singh Rawat S/O Lakshman Singh(Indian National Congress(INC)):Constituency- BHIM(RAJSAMAND) - Affidavit Information of Candidate:, www.myneta.info] of the Indian National Congress was the runner-up with 62,137 votes (38.02%).

== Economy ==
The main occupation of residents of the Bhim panchayat samiti is agriculture. Because of extreme hilly terrain, fields are very small and productivity is average or below average, and water shortage adds to agricultural difficulties. This has resulted in the migration of men to Gujarat—mainly to Surat, Baroda, and Ahmedabad—in search of work. Women who stay behind take care of animals, children, and agricultural fields.

== Martial tradition ==
The Bhim area, locally known as the Magra region, is a hilly area where agriculture is nominal and there is no other industry or business. The communities residing in this area include Prominently Rawat [ref: ]. During the British Raj, a special battalion of the army was raised in the name of these people, named 44th Merwara infantry; after Indian independence, that battalion was disbanded [ref: ].

A large number of eligible youth historically joined the army, particularly during World War I, World War II, and the 1971 Bangladesh war; though this flow has receded in recent years due to competition from the Shekhawati region.

== Infrastructure ==
Bhim has a 100-bedded hospital, a degree college, and a circle officer of police (DYSP) office.

data.title: Luigi Bruti
data.text:
----

Luigi Bruti (born 1960 in Montemonaco, Italy) is an Italian musician and electronic musical instrument designer. He worked for SIEL and Roland Europe before becoming involved in the establishment of the Italian digital-instrument company Dexibell. His work has included the Roland E-20 arranger keyboard and the Roland V-Accordion. [ref: Luigi Bruti, NAMM Oral History]

== Career ==

Bruti worked for the Italian electronic musical instrument manufacturer SIEL. A 1985 report in the British music newspaper Sounds described him as a SIEL demonstrator presenting the company's MIDI software and electronic musical instruments. [ref: SIEL, Sounds]

After SIEL became part of Roland, Bruti continued his career at Roland Europe. A 2018 article in Music Trades identified him as the designer of the Roland E-20 arranger keyboard. [ref: Bringing A New Style To The Keyboard Market, Music Trades] NAMM's Oral History program also credits him with contributing to the development of the V-Accordion series. [ref: Luigi Bruti, NAMM Oral History] Roland founder Ikutaro Kakehashi also identified Bruti, together with Francesco Rauchi, among the engineers involved in the V-Accordion project. [ref: An Age Without Samples: Originality and Creativity in the Digital World, Hal Leonard Books]

A 2008 report in Accordion USA on Roland Europe's V-Accordion production described Bruti as director of the V-Accordion and marketing divisions and discussed his role in the development of the instrument. [ref: A Roland is Born in Acquaviva Picena, Accordion USA]

After Roland Europe ceased operations in Italy, Bruti became involved in the group that established Dexibell. In a 2018 reportage following a visit to the company's facilities, SM Strumenti Musicali described Bruti as the figure who gathered former Roland specialists to form the new development team. [ref: REPORTAGE - DEXIBELL: IL PIANOFORTE ITALIANO, SM Strumenti Musicali]

In 2019, the American trade publication The Music & Sound Retailer reported on the history of Dexibell and described Bruti as a keyboard innovator who joined forces with Proel chief executive Fabrizio Sorbi to begin developing and manufacturing Dexibell keyboards. The article also identified him as a founder of Dexibell. [ref: The Music & Sound Retailer Visits Italy, The Music & Sound Retailer]

== Music ==

In 1981, Bruti composed Musette, which was included in the musical programme of Ettore Scola's film Passione d'amore. [ref: Società Italiana degli Autori ed Editori, Programma musicale del film Passione d'amore, 1981, line 25.]

In 2004, Bruti was one of the producers of Linda Valori, who placed third at the Sanremo Music Festival with Aria, sole, terra e mare. [ref: Concerto di Valori per…Linda, Riviera Oggi]

== Patents ==

Bruti is named as an inventor or co-inventor on patents concerning electronic musical instruments. These include a patent for a method of electronically reproducing accordion sound, developed with Demetrio Cuccu and Roberto Gaetani. [ref: Method for reproducing the sound of an accordion electronically, Google Patents]

== Awards ==

In 2014, Bruti received the Merit Award of the Confédération Internationale des Accordéonistes for his work in the field of electronic accordions. [ref: CIA Merit Awards, Confédération Internationale des Accordéonistes]

data.title: CanJoe
data.text:
----

The CanJoe is a one-stringed, fretted folk instrument associated with the musical traditions of the Appalachian region of the United States. Constructed from a wooden neck and a metal beverage can used as a resonator, the instrument shares characteristics with homemade stringed instruments such as the diddley bow and cigar box guitar. [ref: Music for All: The Can Joe Man, Our State]

The instrument was developed during the late 1980s by North Carolina craftsman Herschel R. Brown, who also coined the name "CanJoe." [ref: “A Can-did Legend of CanJoe John.” Can Joe Country News!, vol. 1, circa 1997 (company newsletter; primary source).] Brown's design was later further developed and commercially promoted by Tennessee musician and instrument maker John VanArsdall, who became known as "CanJoe John." The Can Joe Company was established in Blountville, Tennessee, in 1994 and sold finished instruments, kits, and custom-built models. [ref: Tennessee Department of Revenue, Certificate of Registration for The Can Joe Company, effective December 1, 1994 (primary record).] [ref: The Can Joe Company, CanJoe Order Form and Product Flyer, circa 1990s (primary promotional material).]

The instrument gained national recognition through public performances, festivals, recordings, and media coverage. [ref: “To ‘Can-Joe’ John VanArsdall and Fred Hall, an old can is no piece of trash.” Empire Magazine (Bristol Herald Courier), November 13, 1997.] [ref: Reunion Time, Empire Magazine (Bristol Herald Courier)]

== Etymology ==

The name "CanJoe" was coined by Herschel R. Brown, the instrument's creator, during the late 1980s. The name combines the words "can" and "banjo."

== History ==

=== Origins ===

The CanJoe originated during the late 1980s, when Brown developed a one-stringed instrument derived from an earlier instrument known as the "uni-can." Brown recognized that the earlier instrument's fret arrangement resembled that of the mountain dulcimer and redesigned it using a wooden neck and a metal beverage can as a resonator. [ref: Onslow loses relentless advocate, Jacksonville Daily News]

VanArsdall became acquainted with Brown and his instruments during the late 1980s. Brown and VanArsdall became friends and worked together on the CanJoe's design and construction.

=== Relationship to earlier instruments ===

The CanJoe shares the use of simple, readily available materials with earlier homemade instruments such as the diddley bow and cigar box guitar.

An earlier homemade instrument identified as a “Canjo,” dating to around 1930, is held by The Charleston Museum in South Carolina. The museum describes it as a banjo-guitar hybrid made from an old coffee pot, with a carved neck, bridge, and walnut tuning pegs. [ref: The Charleston Museum, “Canjo,” ca. 1930, museum exhibit label (photographed artifact; primary source).]

The term “canjo,” without the final “e,” has also been used to describe other homemade stringed instruments created by different makers. These instruments vary in design and are not necessarily related to Brown's CanJoe. The Louisiana Folklife Program, for example, has documented instrument maker Gladys Miller making and selling one-stringed instruments called canjos using food cans as resonators. [ref: Innovation, Tradition, and Change in Louisiana Musical Instrument Making and Repair, Louisiana Folklife Program]

One of the CanJoe's distinguishing features is its fretted, dulcimer-style fingerboard paired with a metal beverage can resonator.

According to Our State, Brown first encountered the uni-can while traveling in the mountains of North Carolina. The earlier instrument used a plastic fingerboard, a plywood stick, and a metal can. Brown recognized that its fret arrangement was similar to a mountain dulcimer and developed a sturdier version of the instrument.

=== Development by John VanArsdall ===

VanArsdall later became a prominent builder, performer, and promoter of the CanJoe.

VanArsdall's late wife gave him the nickname "CanJoe John," which he used as his performing name. [ref: Wherever the Sound Takes You: Heroics and Heartbreak in Music Making, University of Chicago Press]

In 1994, the Can Joe Company was formally established in Blountville, Tennessee. [ref: Sullivan County, Tennessee, business license for The Can Joe Company, 1994 (primary record).] The company produced completed instruments, custom instruments, and assembly kits.

VanArsdall continued developing the instrument while keeping the basic one-string, fretted-neck, and can-resonator design created by Brown. His CanJoes were featured in regional newspapers and magazines during the 1990s and 2000s.

VanArsdall created the first website about the CanJoe in 1998.

=== SmithHaven and public recognition ===

Events devoted to the instrument included the First Annual CanJoe Festival at SmithHaven Farm in Blountville, Tennessee, in 1999. [ref: First Annual CanJoe Festival, promotional poster, SmithHaven Farm, 1999 (primary promotional material).] CanJoe performances were also promoted at the Appalachian Fair in Gray, Tennessee, in 2003. [ref: 77th Annual Appalachian Fair, promotional poster, Gray, Tennessee, 2003 (primary promotional material).]

A 2001 Empire Magazine article documented VanArsdall performing the CanJoe during a celebration of Bristol's musical heritage.

== Construction ==

=== Neck and fretboard ===

The CanJoe consists of a wooden neck with a fretted fingerboard and a single string, with a metal beverage can serving as the resonator.

Brown based the CanJoe's fret arrangement on the Appalachian mountain dulcimer.

=== Tuning peg ===

A tuning peg at the end of the neck adjusts the tension and pitch of the string. [ref: Photograph of a CanJoe instrument in the CanJoe collection, SmithHaven, 2026 (primary visual evidence).]

=== Resonator ===

A metal beverage can forms the CanJoe's resonator. Mountain Dew cans were among the beverage cans used to make CanJoes.

=== Strings ===

The CanJoe uses a single string stretched along its fretted neck.

=== Decorative elements ===

VanArsdall's handcrafted CanJoes vary in materials, finishes, and decorative details..

== Playing technique ==

The CanJoe is played by plucking its single string while pressing the string against the fretted fingerboard to produce different pitches. The dulcimer-style fret arrangement allows melodies to be played along the neck.

Promotional literature from the Can Joe Company described the CanJoe as a one-stringed musical instrument that "anyone can play."

== Cultural significance ==

The CanJoe draws on Appalachian traditions of homemade musical instruments and folk craftsmanship.

The CanJoe has been demonstrated at events including the CanJoe Festival at SmithHaven Farm, the Appalachian Fair, and celebrations of Bristol's musical heritage.

== Recordings and media appearances ==

VanArsdall released CanJoe recordings under the name CanJoe John. His album One String, One Can, One Man, and ONE BAND... was released by November 2000, and was recognized by Disc Makers and University Recording Studios. [ref: Disc Makers and University Recording Studios, One String, One Can, One Man, and ONE BAND..., CD release recognition award, November 2000 (primary evidence).]

VanArsdall and the CanJoe have been featured in newspaper and magazine coverage, including the Bristol Herald Courier and Our State. In 2019, author David Rowell devoted a chapter of Wherever the Sound Takes You: Heroics and Heartbreak in Music Making to VanArsdall and his 12-year journey to performing the CanJoe at the Grand Ole Opry. [ref: CanJoe John at the Grand Ole Opry]

* Diddley bow
* Cigar box guitar
* Appalachian dulcimer

data.title: Absolutarget
data.text:
Absolutarget is a Portuguese company specialising in the coordination of clothing, home textile and footwear development and production. Based in Vila do Conde, in northern Portugal, the business operates as a business-to-business (B2B) intermediary between fashion brands and Portuguese manufacturers. Its activities are organised under the Portugal Textile and Portugal Shoes brands. [ref: Prémios Exportação & Internacionalização: Os vencedores da edição de 2023, Jornal de Negócios]

According to Jornal de Negócios, the company recorded revenue of €17 million in 2022, with exports accounting for approximately 99% of its business. It received an honourable mention in the Services SME category at the 2023 Export and Internationalisation Awards. In February 2024, Exame named Absolutarget the sector winner for textiles, clothing and leather in its ranking of Portuguese small and medium-sized enterprises. [ref: Conheça as empresas distinguidas nas 1000 PME, Exame]

== History ==

The business traces its origins to 1999, when Paulo Silva established Portugal Shoes to coordinate footwear production in Portugal. In 2007, the operation expanded into clothing and textiles with the creation of Portugal Textile. The company Absolutarget was formally incorporated on 10 July 2008. [ref: Absolutarget, Lda, Racius] [ref: About Portugal Textile, Portugal Textile]

The company's project titled Internacionalização da Absolutarget e da sua marca (Internationalisation of Absolutarget and its brand) was listed among approved projects in the Norte 2020 regional programme, supported by the European Regional Development Fund. The published record lists an eligible investment of €355,650 and approved support of €160,042.50, under project reference NORTE-02-0752-FEDER-021758. [ref: Projetos Aprovados – Área Metropolitana do Porto, Norte 2020]

By 2022, Absolutarget had eight direct employees and reported annual revenue of €17 million, of which approximately 99% came from exports.

== Business operations ==

Absolutarget operates as a production coordination and sourcing business rather than as a single manufacturing facility. It provides collection-development and production-management services and works with Portuguese manufacturers on behalf of fashion brands. A 2022 academic study described the company as serving mainly European and North American brands and providing support with collection planning, factory liaison, production oversight and quality control. [ref: Compreender perfil do consumidor de moda têxtil sustentável, em Portugal: Estudo de caso do marketplace Sustainable Makers, Instituto Português de Administração de Marketing (IPAM Porto)]

The company operates through two brands:

* Portugal Textile – Established in 2007, it coordinates the development and manufacturing of clothing, fashion accessories and home textiles through Portuguese production partners.
* Portugal Shoes – Established in 1999, it specialises in footwear development, material sourcing and manufacturing coordination in Portugal. [ref: About Portugal Shoes, Portugal Shoes]

== Academic research and digital projects ==

Absolutarget developed the Sustainable Makers online marketplace, a business-to-consumer project focused on fashion products associated with environmental and social sustainability. The initiative was examined in a 2022 master's internship report completed at IPAM Porto. Research concerning the Sustainable Makers marketplace was subsequently published by Springer Nature in the proceedings of the ICMarkTech conference. [ref: Marketing and Smart Technologies, Springer Nature]

The company also participated in Plug-In, a business and student networking event organised by the Polytechnic Institute of Porto's School of Media Arts and Design (ESMAD). It was listed among the participating organisations in 2019 and 2021. [ref: 3.ª edição do Plug-IN, Escola Superior de Media Artes e Design] [ref: Plug-In, Escola Superior de Media Artes e Design]

== Awards and recognition ==

* 2023 – Honourable mention in the SME Services category at the Export and Internationalisation Awards, organised by Jornal de Negócios and Novo Banco.
* 2024 – Sector winner for textiles, clothing and leather in Exame magazine's annual Portuguese SME awards, held in association with Informa D&B and EY.

data.title: Paul Johnson (entrepreneur)
data.text:
Paul David Johnson (born 1984) is a British-American entrepreneur, venture capitalist, and author. He co-founded the telehealth company Lemonaid Health and led it as chief executive until its US$400 million acquisition by 23andMe in 2021. He is a general partner and chief executive of the San Francisco venture capital firm Flex Capital.

== Early life and education ==
Johnson was born in England in 1984. He studied computer science and business management at the University of Worcester. [ref: Paul Johnson – General Partner, Flex Capital, yespress.io] Before founding Lemonaid Health he sold sports equipment and pet supplies online, served as UK managing director of the online pet retailer Zooplus, and was head of online at McKesson UK, where he was responsible for the group's digital business including Lloyds Pharmacy.

== Career ==
=== Lemonaid Health ===
Johnson co-founded Lemonaid Health in San Francisco with Ian Van Every; the company launched in 2014 offering virtual doctor visits by chat, phone, or video for a flat fee, initially focused on a small number of conditions such as birth control and sexually transmitted infection testing. [ref: A startup promised to make health care 'refreshingly simple.' Building the business has been anything but, [[Stat (website)] By 2018 the company had handled more than 100,000 patient visits across 18 states.

In July 2020 Lemonaid raised a US$33 million Series B round, with Johnson as chief executive. [ref: Lemonaid Health expanding services with $33M, Sun Life invests in Dialogue Technologies and more digital health funding news, MobiHealthNews]

In October 2021, 23andMe agreed to acquire Lemonaid Health for US$400 million, paid 25 percent in cash and the remainder in 23andMe stock. [ref: 23andMe to buy telehealth firm Lemonaid Health for $400 mln, Reuters] [ref: 23andMe jumps into telehealth, prescription drug delivery with $400M buyout of Lemonaid Health, Fierce Healthcare] Following the acquisition, Johnson became general manager of 23andMe's consumer business, continuing to run Lemonaid's services, [ref: DNA testing giant 23andMe expands into telemedicine with $400 million Lemonaid acquisition, [[Fortune (magazine)] and later served as chief operating officer of that business.

=== Flex Capital ===
In February 2025 Johnson joined Flex Capital, a seed-stage venture capital firm founded by Auren Hoffman and Tod Sacerdoti, as a general partner. [ref: Announcing Our New GP — Paul Johnson, Flex Capital] He serves as the firm's chief executive. [ref: About Flex Capital, Flex Capital]

=== Board roles and other work ===
In May 2024 Johnson was appointed an independent non-executive director of Closed Loop Medicine, a British precision-medicine company. [ref: Closed Loop Medicine Appoints Paul Johnson as Non-Executive Director, Business Wire] He also works as a coach to chief executives and is an angel investor.

== Writing ==
Writing as Paul D. Johnson, he has published two biographies of artificial intelligence researchers: Move 37: The Life of Demis Hassabis (2026) [ref: Move 37: The Life of Demis Hassabis] and Not Insects: The Life of Geoffrey Hinton. [ref: Not Insects: The Life of Geoffrey Hinton]

== Personal life ==
Johnson lives in San Francisco. He became a United States citizen in February 2021. [ref: Gold medal pickleball player stumbled onto the popular game at Glen Park Rec, Glen Park Association] He is a competitive pickleball player who won a singles gold medal at the 2019 West Regional tournament.

data.title: Sigisfredo Garnica
data.text:
Sigisfredo Garnica (born 30 December 1966, Chile) is a Chilean mycologist known for his work on the phylogeny and taxonomy of fungi, especially the ectomycorrhizal genus Cortinarius and the order Sebacinales. He studied biology and microbiology at the Universidad Austral de Chile and earned his doctorate at the University of Tübingen in 2003. After working in Tübingen for more than a decade, he joined the Universidad Austral de Chile in 2018. [ref: Dr. Sigisfredo Garnica Treufo, Facultad de Ciencias, Universidad Austral de Chile]

==Selected publications==
* Morphological and molecular phylogenetic studies in South American Cortinarius species, Mycological Research
* A framework for a phylogenetic classification in the genus Cortinarius (Basidiomycota, Agaricales) derived from morphological and molecular data, Canadian Journal of Botany
* Reconstructing the evolution of agarics from nuclear gene sequences and basidiospore ultrastructure, Mycological Research
* Phylogenetic relationships in Cortinarius, section Calochroi, inferred from nuclear DNA sequences, BMC Evolutionary Biology
* Tracking the evolutionary history of Cortinarius species in section Calochroi, with transoceanic disjunct distributions, BMC Evolutionary Biology
* Phylogenetic diversity and structure of sebacinoid fungi associated with plant communities along an altitudinal gradient, FEMS Microbiology Ecology
* Entorrhizomycota: a new fungal phylum reveals new perspectives on the evolution of fungi, PLOS ONE
* Determining threshold values for barcoding fungi: lessons from Cortinarius (Basidiomycota), a highly diverse and widespread ectomycorrhizal genus, FEMS Microbiology Ecology
* On the evolutionary history of Uleiella chilensis, a smut fungus parasite of Araucaria araucana in South America: Uleiellales ord. nov. in Ustilaginomycetes, PLOS ONE
* Divergence times and phylogenetic patterns of Sebacinales, a highly diverse and widespread fungal lineage, PLOS ONE
* Phylogenetic relationships in the genus Podoserpula and description of P. aliweni, a new species from Chile, Mycologia
* Environmental stress determines the colonization and impact of an endophytic fungus on invasive knotweed, Biological Invasions

data.text:
----

Kurunegala Main Sri Vishnu Maha Devalaya (Sinhala: කුරුණෑගල ප්‍රධාන ශ්‍රී විෂ්ණු මහා දේවාලය) is the principal Vishnu Devalaya in the Kurunegala District of Sri Lanka. The shrine is located within the premises of the historic Angangala Purana Rajamaha Viharaya.

== Location ==
The Devalaya is situated approximately 1.5 km from the Kurunegala clock tower along the Kurunegala–Puttalam main road, inside the Angangala temple grounds. The site lies on land that belongs to the Department of Archaeology, Sri Lanka.

== History ==
The shrine is traditionally regarded as the main Vishnu Devalaya of the Kurunegala District. It functions within the Angangala Purana Rajamaha Viharaya, which is an ancient royal temple.

== Rituals ==
Devotees gather for poojas every Saturday, except on full moon Poya days. Special Thevava rites are conducted for devotees seeking blessings and relief from difficulties. The annual Maha Pooja is held on December 31st.

== See also ==
* Angangala Purana Rajamaha Viharaya

data.title: Daam (Sri Lankan television series)
data.text:
Daam is a Sri Lankan Sinhala-language television series that aired on Sirasa TV from 21 December 2020 [ref: ] to 7 May 2021. [ref: ] Directed by Dhanushka Rathnayake and written by Kaushalya Pathirana, the series was produced by Gayan Dinesh Perera under Gayan Productions. It stars Bimal Jayakody, Tharindi Fernando, and Chameera Liyanage in lead roles.

== Plot ==
Amaya, an air hostess with an exceptional photographic memory, becomes entangled in an international drug-trafficking network after catching the attention of Kevin Walter Almeida, a prominent drug trafficker and former associate of her father. Almeida attempts to leverage Amaya's memory skills to transport contraband and assist in his criminal operations.

Initially, Amaya refuses to cooperate. However, facing escalating threats against her family, she is forced into the syndicate to protect her husband, Kevin, her daughter, Akeshi, as well as her parents and sister.

Meanwhile, a commercial flight departing Sri Lanka mysteriously disappears with no initial signs of survivors. Amaya's family and the public presume she died in the crash. However, Almeida discovers that Amaya survived and launches an effort to track her down to bring her back under his control.

Almeida later crosses paths with Livera, a man suffering from severe retrograde amnesia whose past is tied to Almeida's criminal network. Amaya is eventually rescued, while Livera attempts to flee the country. Livera is subsequently apprehended by law enforcement at the airport, exposing his deep involvement in the syndicate.

In the final scene, Almeida is seen travelling in a vehicle alongside another man (portrayed by Saranga Disasekara). The man turns to Almeida and remarks, "The game is on", concluding the series. Disasekara reprises his role as Rayan, a character from director Dhanushka Rathnayake's previous television series, Wes.

data.title: WePlay (party game app)
data.text:
WePlay is a mobile social gaming application developed and published by WEJOY PTE. LTD., which is a Singapore-based company.

WePlay was released in 2021 for iOS and Android, the app has provided multiplayer party games with voice-chat and avatar-based features, [ref: From Your Phone To The Big Apple WePlay Takes Over Times Square Tampa Free Press, TAMPA FREE PRESS] [ref: How WePlay Conquered the Thai Gaming Market, Klaothongchan] which game catalogue vary by country or region.

== Features ==
WePlay was released in 2021 for iOS and Android platforms and was integrated as a party game which were online, casual and multiplayer types, with real-time voice communications featuring virtual avatars. WePlay is designed to give thought to both entertainment and social networking needs by users, allowing the users to interact and meet their new friends through gamified online party experiences.

WePlay has an important function as a platform for party games online, designed for playing of groups of some users, by combining multiplayer gaming with voice interaction.

In addition to the party games catalog, WePlay incorporates several interactive social media features. For example, the users can create and customize 3D digital avatars through facial modeling (i.e. "face pinching") and virtual clothing options to represent themselves in-game. The platform also includes a VIP membership system, which grants users access to exclusive virtual gifts, special profile rings, and other in-app privileges.

== Games ==
WePlay offers a variety of mini-games which includes;

Grab Mic: A karaoke-style music game where players compete to sing popular songs and showcase their vocal skills.

Who is Spy: A word-based social deduction game that tests players' reasoning, acting, and communication skills.

Draw & Guess: A collaborative and competitive game focusing on creativity, drawing skills, and teamwork.

Space Werewolf: The most popular social deduction game where civilians pit their wits against killers.

== Company ==
WePlay is the flagship product of WEJOY PTE. LTD., an internet technology company founded formaly in Singapore on October 23, 2020. Driven by a global vision, the company focuses on the development and operation of social board games and casual party games for young people.

WEJOY's corporate mission is to "bring joy and friends to young people around the world," and with a vision to "bring people together through games and lead the trend of global online social entertainment." [ref: Connecting User Kindness: WePlay Partners with Resala Association to Launch Ramadan Charity Initiative, Bolsamania]

The development team adheres to a product philosophy centered on "quality first, innovation-driven, and cultural depth." This approach has led to various cross-promotional collaborations with globally renowned intellectual properties (IPs) to enhance the app's cultural and entertainment value in localized markets.

[ref: WePlay stürmt die deutschen Unterhaltung-Charts: Platz 1 bei Google Play und App Store, PRNewswire] [ref: WePlay fa un grande debutto nel mercato italiano, dominando le classifiche gratuite di Google Play e App Store, dimostra la leadership nell'intrattenimento social a livello globale, Adnkronos] [ref: WePlay Debuts in German Market with “The Little Prince” Special Valentine’s Day Collaboration, EQS NEWS] The app achieved the #1 spot in downloads on both the Apple App Store and Google Play in these respective regions.

As of April 2026, data from Similarweb highlighted WePlay's strong monetization and popularity. [ref: Top 综合 娱乐 Android Apps Ranking in 越南, Similarweb] It has also consistently hit the #1 download spot on both Android and iOS platforms in some countries of Asia and Europe. [ref: WePlay's Southeast Asia Lunar New Year Campaign Featured in App Store Today and Today Collection, Prnewswire] [ref: WePlay Featured on Thailand App Store's "Today" Tab, Creating a Songkran-Themed Gaming Extravaganza, Taiwan News]

As of June 2026, WePlay has surpassed 800 million total downloads globally [ref: Gaming for Good: WePlay Turns Virtual Points into Real-World Aid, BriefGlance.com] and maintains an average of 1 million monthly active users (MAU).

== Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) ==
WePlay and its developer WEJOY PTE. LTD. actively participate in global Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and philanthropic donations, often integrating in-app user engagement with real-world charity. [ref: [PRNewswire] WePlay x "The Little Prince" Collaboration Begins, Yonhap News Agency]

WePlay and WEJOY PTE. LTD. also take child welfare, [ref: WePlay Supports Craque do Amanhã to Advance Youth Football Education in Brazil, Yahoo Finance] [ref: WePlay Launches Charity Initiative in Indonesia: Bringing Warmth and Hope to Children at a Jakarta Orphanage, Yahoo Finance] subsequently disaster relief, [ref: WePlay Partners Again with Türk Eğitim Derneği to Support 204 Earthquake-Affected Children, PRNewswire] [ref: WePlay Partners with Türk Eğitim Derneği (TED) to Support 86 Students in Pursuing Their Dreams, PRNewswire] cultural observances, [ref: WePlay Launches Charity Initiative in Malaysia, Bringing Warmth and Care to Children at a Kuala Lumpur Orphanage, PRNewswire] [ref: WePlay Fulfills Social Responsibility, Launches "WePlay Berqurban" Qurban Charity Activity in Indonesia, Bastillepost] and animal protection [ref: WePlay Launches "Cloud Guardian Initiative": Illuminating the Future of Stray Cats with Love, PRNewswire] [ref: WePlay Charity Initiative International Dog Day: Join “Paws for Love” to Ignite Hope for Stray Animals!, Yahoo Finance News]into consideration through their projects.

== Safety and moderation ==
WePlay has introduced a range of safety and moderation measures aimed at community governance and the protection of minors in law([https://weplayapp.com/teenager See "WePlay Parental Control"]). These measures include user reporting tools, professional review teams, AI-assisted risk detection, safety reminders, and age-based protections across core social scenarios.

WePlay states that users can report suspected violations through in-app channels in areas such as user profiles and voice rooms. Reported content and accounts are reviewed under the platform's community rules, which cover conduct including harassment, fraud, and sexually explicit or otherwise inappropriate content.
[ref: WePlay Launches "Let's Celebrate Christmas Together" Winter Campaign: Partnering with Korean Charity to Light Up the Journey Home for Stray Dogs, Bastillepost]
WePlay has also said that it uses AI-assisted systems to identify potentially risky behavior patterns and abnormal activity, with the stated goal of improving early detection and limiting harmful interactions.
The platform has also publicized the use of safety reminder mechanisms. According to WePlay, when the system detects potentially risky interactions, users may receive warnings or prompts related to fraud prevention, anti-harassment awareness, and community conduct.

== Enforcement and transparency ==
WePlay's platform has adopted a layered enforcement approach for high-risk behavior involving minors in law, including safety education, temporary restrictions, blacklisting, and account bans for serious violations.
WePlay has also described efforts to trace related accounts through device- and IP-based signals in cases involving accounts previously banned for harming minors in law.

WePlay also has periodically published notices about account enforcement and moderation outcomes on its official website and social media channels as part of its transparency efforts. WePlay updates have described these actions as part of a broader governance framework covering prevention, detection, intervention, enforcement, and public notice.

data.title: IEEE 1621
data.text:
IEEE 1621 ("Standard for User Interface Elements in Power Control of Electronic Devices Employed in Office/Consumer Environments") is a standard published by the IEEE and appoved by ANSI that describes human interface guidelines regarding power controls in consumer electronics. [ref: IEEE Std 1621-2004 - IEEE Standard for User Interface Elements in Power Control of Electronic Devices Employed in Office/Consumer Environments, webstore.ansi.org] [ref: IEEE Standards Association, IEEE Standards Association] It includes terminology, icons, and lighting. [ref: ] IEEE 1621 references the following standards: ANSI/VITA 40, CIE 107, IEC 60073, IEC 60417, IEC 60447, IEC 62301, IEC 80416-1, IEC 80416-3, ISO 7000, ISO 9186, ISO 9241-1, ISO 9241-10, and ISO/IEC 13251.

== History and Motivation ==
Standardization of power controls in consumer electronics was spearheaded by Bruce Nordman at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory with funding provided by the California Energy Commission Public Interest Energy Research Program. [ref: Power Management Controls - Contact Us, ea-controls.lbl.gov] Nordman's reseach showed that many computers had power saving features disabled, mainly due to consumer confusion due to the lack of standardization of terminology and symbols in both hardware and software. [ref: Power Control Made Easy, EE Product News] Confusion was further componded due the symbol IEC 60417-5009 (⏻) meaning that the device was only disconnected from its power supply. Per IEC 60417-5009 this is defined as "stand-by." [ref: products.iec.ch] [ref: IEC 60417 – 5009, Stand-by, IEC] This allows for ambiguity. For example it could mean that the device is entirely off aside from an illuminated "off" indicator or in a sleep mode.

In April, 1998 the project was submitted to the California Energy Commission with the project starting in June of 2000. [ref: Power Management Controls - News, ea-controls.lbl.gov]

The IEEE New Standards Committee approved working group 1621 to develop a power controls standard in September of 2002. Three months later a draft of IEEE 1621 was published. [ref: Power Management Controls - User Interface Standard - IEEE 1621, ea-controls.lbl.gov]

The final standard was approved by the American National Standards Institute on 2005-03-24 and the standard was published on 2005-06-08.

data.title: Takashi Isobe
data.text:
Takashi Isobe (Japanese: 磯部 孝, January 6, 1914 – October 7, 2001) was a Japanese physicist and engineer specializing in measurement and control engineering. He was a professor and later professor emeritus at the University of Tokyo. His research included underwater ballistics, flow measurement, correlation methods using random signals, and automatic control. He served twice as president of the Society of Instrument and Control Engineers (SICE) and was also a member of the science-writing group known as the. [ref: 磯部孝名誉教授, 学内広報]

== Early life and education ==
Isobe was born on January 6, 1914, in Ueno-Sakuragi, Tokyo, as the eldest of six children. He spent his childhood in Ikebukuro and attended the elementary school attached to Toyoshima Normal School, followed by Tokyo Prefectural Sixth Middle School, now Tokyo Metropolitan Shinjuku High School. [ref: Yasushi Ishii, "磯部孝先生の計測工学の歩み" [The development of Takashi Isobe's career in measurement engineering], in 磯部孝先生と計測工学, Isobe Takashi Sensei o Shinobu Kai, 2002, pp. 3–5. ]

In March 1930, after completing his fourth year of middle school, he entered the former Urawa Higher School. In 1933 he entered the Department of Physics at Tokyo Imperial University. He suffered from severe pneumonia while a student and delayed his progression by one year, graduating from the Department of Physics in March 1937.

After graduation, Isobe joined the Imperial Japanese Army Technical Headquarters as a civilian employee, initially working on ballistic calculations. From 1942 to 1944 he was dispatched by the Army Technical Headquarters to Tokyo Imperial University as a special graduate research student, where he studied underwater ballistics under Masaichi Majima.

== Academic career ==
In 1945, Isobe became a lecturer in the First Faculty of Engineering at Tokyo Imperial University. Following the establishment of the Department of Measurement Engineering, he became an associate professor in 1946 and a professor in 1948.

From September 1959, he spent approximately one year as a visiting professor at Cornell University in the United States. [ref: Ishii, "磯部孝先生の計測工学の歩み", 2002, pp. 10–11. ]

Isobe retired from the University of Tokyo in March 1974 and became professor emeritus. In April of that year, he became a professor in the Department of Photographic Engineering at Chiba University, where he worked on education and research in image measurement engineering. He retired from Chiba University in March 1979. [ref: Ishii, "磯部孝先生の計測工学の歩み", 2002, p. 15. ]

In 1979 he joined Chubu Institute of Technology as a professor. The institution was renamed Chubu University in 1984, and Isobe continued teaching and conducting research there for approximately ten years. [ref: Ishii, "磯部孝先生の計測工学の歩み", 2002, pp. 15–19. ]

He died on October 7, 2001, at the age of 87.

== Research ==

=== Underwater ballistics ===
While working at the Army Technical Headquarters, Isobe initially conducted ballistic calculations. Beginning in 1942, he pursued experimental studies of underwater ballistics at Tokyo Imperial University. His work examined phenomena including the ricochet of projectiles from the water surface and the motion of projectiles after entering water.

The University of Tokyo later described his work as having clarified in detail both ricochet at the water surface and projectile motion underwater, thereby opening a new field of research.

His results were later collected in the book Suichū dandō no kenkyū (水中弾道の研究, Studies in Underwater Ballistics), published by the University of Tokyo Press in 1975. [ref: 水中弾道の研究, Hanmoto.com]

A Chiba University Library publication described the book as a study of the motion of high-speed projectiles entering water, a specialized problem in fluid mechanics. [ref: 千葉大学附属図書館報, Chiba University Library]

=== Measurement engineering and flow measurement ===
After World War II, Isobe shifted the main focus of his research toward measurement engineering and its systematization. Together with Masaichi Majima, he edited the two-volume Keisokuhō gairon (計測法概論, Introduction to Measurement Methods), published in 1950–1951. [ref: 計測法概論, CiNii Books]

He also worked on industrial measurement, automatic control, and flow measurement. In 1956, he published a paper on problems in measurement and control technology in factories. [ref: 工場における計測及び制御技術の諸問題, Japan TAPPI Journal]

During the 1950s he developed a pulsating gas flowmeter. In 1958, Hiroo Hattori, Isobe, Takao Nomura, and Tositaka Hayasi published "Practical Tests of Pulsating Gas Flow Meter". The device had been developed into a commercial instrument and was tested under various experimental conditions. [ref: Practical Tests of Pulsating Gas Flow Meter, Journal of the Instrument Technology, Japan]

During his stay at Cornell University, Isobe presented his work on pulsating flow measurement at a meeting of the Instrument Society of America (ISA, now the International Society of Automation). The following year he received an award from the society for this work.

=== Correlation methods and control ===
During the 1960s, Isobe studied correlation methods that used random signals to determine the characteristics of control systems and other systems. The University of Tokyo later credited him with establishing correlation techniques that contributed substantially to the subsequent development of measurement and control engineering.

In 1968, he edited Sōkan kansū oyobi supekutoru: sono sokutei to ōyō (相関函数およびスペクトル―その測定と応用, Correlation Functions and Spectra: Measurement and Applications), which summarized work in this field. [ref: 相関函数およびスペクトル: その測定と応用, National Diet Library]

He also worked in control engineering and published an article on adaptive control in 1963. [ref: 適応制御, Journal of the Japan Society of Mechanical Engineers]

That same year, Isobe supervised the Japanese translation of E. Mishkin and L. Braun Jr.'s Adaptive Control Systems, published by Corona Publishing as Tekiō seigyo-kei (適応制御系). [ref: 適応制御系, National Diet Library]

=== Industrial measurement ===
Isobe was also involved in the dissemination of measurement and automatic-control techniques in industry, particularly in the Japanese iron and steel industry. [ref: 鉄鋼業における計測と制御, CiNii Books]

In 1969, he gave a lecture titled "Recent Measurement and Control in the Iron and Steel Industry" at the sixth Nishiyama Memorial Technical Lecture of the Iron and Steel Institute of Japan. The lecture discussed measurement and computer control in processes including blast furnaces, sintering, converters, and rolling.

He continued to publish on the subject; a 1984 paper was titled "Progress of Measurement and Control in Iron and Steel Industry". [ref: Progress of Measurement and Control in Iron and Steel Industry, Tetsu-to-Hagane]

=== Spinning tops ===
In his later years, Isobe studied the dynamics of spinning tops and friction, including the mechanism by which a spinning top gradually rises and the behavior of the tippe top. He analyzed these phenomena by considering friction at the contact surface.

An essay titled "Koma wa naze okiagaru" (コマはなぜ起き上がる, "Why Does a Spinning Top Rise?") was included in the third volume of Shin Butsuri no sanpomichi (新 物理の散歩道, New Walks Through Physics). [ref: 新 物理の散歩道 第3集, Chikuma Shobō]

In 1981, Isobe and his wife spent several months at Newcastle University at the invitation of Professor Leonard Maunder. According to a later biographical account, he considered submitting the results of his analysis of the tippe top to Nature, following Maunder's suggestion. [ref: Ishii, "磯部孝先生の計測工学の歩み", 2002, p. 18. ]

== Professional activities ==
Isobe served as president of the Society of Instrument and Control Engineers in 1964 and again in 1975. [ref: 歴代会長、副会長, Society of Instrument and Control Engineers]

He was elected an honorary member of the society in 1978. [ref: 名誉会員, Society of Instrument and Control Engineers]

He also participated in committees concerned with measurement standards and chaired a specialist committee on measurement standards. [ref: Ishii, "磯部孝先生の計測工学の歩み", 2002, pp. 13–15. ]

In 1996, he received the SICE Achievement Award. [ref: 功績賞受賞者, Society of Instrument and Control Engineers]

== Logergist ==
Isobe was one of the seven Japanese physicists in the group known as the Logergists, together with Hidetoshi Takahashi, Isao Imai, Koreo Kinoshita, Akiya Okawa, Masao Kondo, and Sōshin Chikazumi. [ref: ロゲルギスト, Chikuma Shobō]

Beginning in 1959, the Logergists contributed monthly science essays to the magazine Shizen, examining everyday phenomena from the viewpoint of physics. Many of the essays were later collected in the Butsuri no sanpomichi (物理の散歩道, "Walks Through Physics") series.

The University of Tokyo's obituary for Isobe also noted his activities with the Logergists and the Butsuri no sanpomichi series.

== Awards and honors ==

* 1944 – Noda Prize [ref: 磯部孝先生と計測工学, Isobe Takashi Sensei o Shinobu Kai, 2002, pp. 20–22. ]
* 1945 – Hattori Hokokai Award
* 1960 – Award from the Instrument Society of America
* 1981 – Medal with Blue Ribbon
* 1987 – Order of the Sacred Treasure, Second Class
* 1996 – Society of Instrument and Control Engineers Achievement Award [ref: 功績賞受賞者, Society of Instrument and Control Engineers]

== Selected books ==

* Masaichi Majima and Takashi Isobe, eds., Keisokuhō gairon (計測法概論), 2 vols., Corona Publishing, 1950–1951.
* E. Mishkin and L. Braun Jr., eds.; Takashi Isobe, supervising translator, Tekiō seigyo-kei (適応制御系), Corona Publishing, 1963.
* Masaichi Majima and Takashi Isobe, eds., Keisokuhō tsūron kōgi (計測法通論講義), University of Tokyo Press, 1967.
* Takashi Isobe, ed., Sōkan kansū oyobi supekutoru: sono sokutei to ōyō (相関函数およびスペクトル―その測定と応用), University of Tokyo Press, 1968.
* Masaichi Majima and Takashi Isobe, eds., Keisokuhō tsūron (計測法通論), University of Tokyo Press, 1974.
* Takashi Isobe, Suichū dandō no kenkyū (水中弾道の研究), University of Tokyo Press, 1975.

== Selected papers ==

* Isobe, Takashi (1956). "工場における計測及び制御技術の諸問題" [Problems in measurement and control technology in factories]. Japan TAPPI Journal. 10 (7): 324–327..
* Hattori, Hiroo; Isobe, Takashi; Nomura, Takao; Hayasi, Tositaka (1958). "Practical Tests of Pulsating Gas Flow Meter". Journal of the Instrument Technology, Japan. 8 (6): 342–349..
* Isobe, Takashi (1963). "適応制御" [Adaptive control]. Journal of the Japan Society of Mechanical Engineers. 66 (528): 110–116..
* Isobe, Takashi (1984). "Progress of Measurement and Control in Iron and Steel Industry". Tetsu-to-Hagane. 70 (9): 1311–1312..

data.title: 2039 Women's World Cup
data.text:
The 2039 FIFA Women's World Cup is scheduled to be the 13th edition of the FIFA Women's World Cup, the quadrennial international women's football championship contested by the national teams that represent the member associations of FIFA. The tournament has a potential bid to be hosted by Portugal, Spain, and Morocco. It is possible that this will be the third tournament to feature 48 national teams.

The tournament will be the first time Portugal, Spain and Morocco host the FIFA Women's World Cup if the bid is accepted. This will also be the fourth FIFA Women's World Cup in Europe after Sweden in 1995, Germany in 2011, France in 2019, and England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland in 2035, as well as the first in Africa, and Portugal, Spain and Morocco will also become the ninth countries to host both the men's and women's World Cup, with all three having hosted in 2030.

== The Bids ==
The host nation for the 2039 Women's world cup is Expected to be officially decided around 2029-2031 in a FIFA Congress. There is also another bid to host the tournament. Japan want to host the tournament solo. Japan originally wanted to host the 2031 Women's World Cup, but FIFA's bidding restrictions prevented Asian countries from bidding for the 2031 and 2035 editions. Japan subsequently turned its attention to 2039.

== Format ==
It is possible that the 2039 FIFA Women's World Cup will be contested by 48 teams. If so, it will be the third tournament to do so. Starting in 2031, and also happening in 2035. Otherwise, it will have 64 teams, the first to do so.

== Venues ==
There are currently no venues announced for this tournament. Please update when venues are announced.

== Teams ==

=== Qualification ===
FIFA's confederations organise their own qualifying competitions, with the exception of CAF and CONCACAF which qualify teams through continental championships. The hosts Spain, Portugal, Morocco and Japan would receive automatic qualification for the tournament, leaving most of the remaining FIFA member associations eligible to enter qualification if they chose to do so. Portugal and Morocco could participate for the first time ever, but may still qualify for 2027, 2031 or 2035. FIFA is yet to announce the allocation of slots.

data.title: Hanoi Archers
data.text:
Hanoi Archers () are a Vietnamese amateur baseball team based in Hanoi. One of the pioneering clubs in Vietnam, they regularly compete in the Vietnam Baseball Championship, winning a title in 2025.

== History ==
Arguably the first baseball club in Hanoi, the Archers were founded in 2006 as the FisHANU Baseball Club () by a group of college students. The founding group consisted of students of the Faculty of International Studies (Fis) of the Hanoi University (HANU) in southwestern Hanoi, thus the name. [ref: ] The club called the HANU campus sports field home up until circa 2019, as the club failed to recruit HANU students and the school's new sports field planning scheme made it impossible for baseball, effectively forcing it out.

Under the new name Hanoi Archers, the newly independent club juggled between weekend operation in multiple locations and weekday practice downtown, before sharing a baseball-specified field, the first of its kind in the city, with expat clubs in western Hanoi. The club, however, remained highly competitive under the management of former LG Twins prospect Yoo Jae-ho, winning local Hanoi league titles in 2023 and 2024. [ref: Hall of Fame (Champion of 2023 2nd Season), Hanoi Baseball League] [ref: Hall of Fame (Champion of 2024 Season), Hanoi Baseball League] Come the advent of the annual national championship, the Archers made the championship game back-to-back in 2022 and 2023, only to lose both to HCMC powerhouse Saigon Storm. [ref: Đội HCM II – CLB Sài Gòn Storm lên ngôi vô địch Giải cúp Các câu lạc bộ Bóng chày Toàn quốc 2022 (HCM II - Saigon Storm wins the 2022 National Baseball Club Cup), Facebook] [ref: Á QUÂN GIẢI CÚP CÁC CÂU LẠC BỘ BÓNG CHÀY TOÀN QUỐC 2023- HANOI ARCHERS (Runners-up of the 2023 National Baseball Club Cup - the Hanoi Archers), Facebook]

After losing to the Storm in the 2024 semifinals, their woes would finally come to an end in the 2025 Vietnam Baseball Club Championship. The Archers came swinging early on, beating Saigon by mercy rule in pool play, before beating them again in the championship game to win the club's first national title. [ref: Hanoi Archers vô địch Giải các Câu lạc bộ Bóng chày toàn quốc 2025, Chính sách và Cuộc sống - Thông tấn xã Việt Nam]

data.title: Compass Group India
data.text:
Compass Group India is the Indian subsidiary of Compass Group plc, a British multinational contract foodservice and facilities management company. Headquartered in Gurugram, it provides catering and workplace management services to corporate offices, manufacturing facilities, healthcare institutions, and educational campuses in India. [ref: Compass Group India serves the right menu, Business India]

== History ==
Compass Group initially entered the Indian market in 1996 through a joint venture with Radhakrishna Hospitality Services. The joint venture dissolved in 2008, and Compass Group subsequently acquired local food and support services businesses to re-establish independent operations.

In September 2020, the company acquired a majority stake in SmartQ, an Indian food technology company focusing on digital cafeteria systems. [ref: Indian Foodtech Startup SmartQ Acquired By UK-Based Compass Group, Inc42]

In March 2022, the company launched Saarthi-FX, a digital workplace platform designed to manage asset compliance, facility maintenance, and workplace ticketing. [ref: Compass Group India Revolutionizes Workplace Management with AI-Powered Saarthi-FX, Xcan.it]

In August 2024, Compass Group India acquired a 70 percent stake in ICS Foods Private Limited, a Delhi-based catering company specializing in the manufacturing sector. [ref: Compass Group India acquires 70% stake in ICS Foods, Verdict Food Service]

Rahul Shinde was appointed Managing Director in June 2026. [ref: Compass India appoints Rahul Shinde as Managing Director, People Matters]

== Operations ==
Compass Group India operates across two primary segments: contract catering and facilities management. Its foodservice activities cover workplace dining, while facilities management involves the operation and maintenance of corporate and industrial sites.

As of early 2026, industry reports indicated the company operated across 1,100 to 1,200 sites in India, employing approximately 45,000 frontline staff. This included managing cafeterias for over 120 Global Capability Centres (GCCs). [ref: From cleaning robots to smart kitchens: How Compass Group India embeds AI across operations, TechCircle] The company also operates a healthcare division under the Medirest brand and manages retail micro-markets in cities such as Bengaluru and Hyderabad. [ref: Food services provider Compass India looks to tap into travel retail, Business Standard] [ref: Compass Group India addresses nutrition for patients and staff in hospitals through Medirest Platform, ETHealthWorld]

== Technology ==
The company utilises automated systems for facilities operations, energy monitoring, and food ordering. In 2026, Compass Group India integrated autonomous cleaning robots, camera-based workplace safety systems, and digital kiosks across its managed sites. data.title: Hakan Kousetta
data.text:
----

Hakan Kousetta is a British television producer and media executive. He is the co-founder of 60 Forty Films, an independent television production company, and previously served as chief operating officer of the television division at See-Saw Films.

Kousetta has received three Primetime Emmy Award nominations, including a win for State of the Union and nominations for Slow Horses. [ref: ]

== Career ==
In 2008, Kousetta co-founded the specialist media law firm Aslan Charles Kousetta in London alongside Susan Aslan and Sue Charles. As a partner, he specialized in legal matters relating to film and television production and financing. [ref: New law firm Aslan Charles Kousetta launches in London, Screen]

In October 2014, Kousetta joined See-Saw Films as chief operating officer of its television division, overseeing the company's commercial and operational activities alongside television head Jamie Laurenson. [ref: Top of the Lake to return for second series, Screen]

During his tenure at See-Saw, Kousetta co-led the company's television operations and executive produced a number of television productions from its United Kingdom and Australian offices, including Top of the Lake: China Girl, The End, The New Legends of Monkey, State of the Union, The North Water, Slow Horses, The Essex Serpent, and Heartstopper. [ref: See-Saw Executives Jamie Laurenson, Hakan Kousetta Depart to Start 60Forty Films, Variety] [ref: Jamie Laurenson, Hakan Kousetta depart See-Saw to launch TV outfit 60Forty, Screen]

In 2020, Kousetta was appointed chair of the Producers Alliance for Cinema and Television (PACT), succeeding Sara Geater. Prior to his appointment, he had served on the PACT Council and co-chaired the organisation's Film Policy Group. [ref: U.K. Producers Org Pact Taps See-Saw Films Executive Hakan Kousetta as Chair, Variety] In 2021, he received a special innovation award from the Producers Guild of Great Britain for his work with the UK Government on the design and implementation of the COVID Film and Television Production Restart Scheme. [ref: BFI Adds Six Members To Board Of Governors, Deadline]

In February 2021, Kousetta, alongside Jamie Laurenson, departed See-Saw Films to establish the independent television production company 60 Forty Films. Although leaving See-Saw, the pair continued as executive producers on several ongoing productions, including Slow Horses, The Essex Serpent, The North Water, State of the Union, and Heartstopper.

In 2022, 60 Forty Films entered into an overall production agreement with Apple TV+. Among the company's first productions was the thriller series Hijack, starring Idris Elba, which Kousetta executive produced alongside Laurenson. [ref: Apple TV+ Inks Overall Deal With ‘Slow Horses’ Producers’ 60Forty Films (EXCLUSIVE), Variety] [ref: Hijack EP Hakan Kousetta On Working With Idris Elba & Chances Of A Season 2, ScreenRant]

In June 2026, Kousetta was appointed to the Board of Governors of the British Film Institute for a four-year term.

data.title: Nagarajan Ramakrishnan
data.text:
Nagarajan Ramakrishnan is an Indian physician who works in critical care and sleep medicine in Chennai. He works at Apollo Hospitals and founded the Nithra Institute of Sleep Sciences, a sleep medicine centre established in 2004.

==Early life and education==
According to a biography submitted by his institute to World Sleep Day, Ramakrishnan graduated from Stanley Medical College in Madras. He then worked in the United Kingdom and the United States for more than 13 years before returning to India in 2003. The same biography states that he holds American Board certification in internal medicine, critical care medicine, sleep medicine and obesity medicine, and a master's degree in medical management from the University of Southern California. [ref: Delegate: Dr N. Ramakrishnan, World Sleep Day]

==Career==
Apollo Hospitals lists Ramakrishnan as a senior consultant in critical care and sleep medicine and director of critical care services, a post it dates from 2003. [ref: Dr N Ramakrishnan – Critical Care Specialist, Apollo Hospitals]

In 2004 he established the Nithra Institute of Sleep Sciences in Chennai, which now operates as Nithra Sleep and Health Care and describes itself as a multispecialty centre. [ref: About Us, Nithra Health] He is also the founder of the TACT Academy for Clinical Training, a simulation-based healthcare training centre in Chennai. [ref: 10th anniversary celebration 2024, Dr. Jeyasekharan Medical Trust]

Ramakrishnan has been quoted in the Deccan Chronicle on sleep apnoea and diabetes [ref: Obstructive sleep apnea can cause diabetes, Deccan Chronicle] and on disrupted sleep-wake cycles and mental health. [ref: Daily routine is key for mental wellness, says study, Deccan Chronicle]

==Professional societies==
According to the Nithra website, Ramakrishnan has held roles on the executive committees of the Indian Society of Critical Care Medicine and the Indian Sleep Disorders Association, and is a past president of the latter. [ref: About Dr. Nagarajan Ramakrishnan, Nithra] He was organizing chairperson of SLEEPCON 2025, the association's annual international conference. [ref: Apollo Consultants Honour list June 2025, Apollo Hospitals]

==Publications==
Ramakrishnan has published in the Indian Journal of Critical Care Medicine. He was first author of the Indian Society of Critical Care Medicine's 2024 position statement on care after intensive care. [ref: Post-ICU Care: Why, What, When and How? ISCCM Position Statement, Indian Journal of Critical Care Medicine] He is among the co-authors of a 2016 study of case mix and practice patterns in Indian intensive care units [ref: Intensive care in India: The Indian intensive care case mix and practice patterns study, Indian Journal of Critical Care Medicine] and of the Indian Society of Critical Care Medicine's 2009 quality indicators for Indian intensive care units. [ref: Quality indicators for ICU: ISCCM guidelines for ICUs in India, Indian Journal of Critical Care Medicine]
