data.title: Orbilia xanthostigma
data.text:
----

== Introduction ==

Orbilia xanthostigma.

== History ==
O. xanthostigma was described by a Swedish mycologist, Elias Magnus Fries, in 1815, and was later renamed by Fries in 1849. [ref: Index Fungorum, Index Fungorum] [ref: Cryptic speciation in Orbilia xanthostigma and O. leucostigma (Orbiliomycetes): an aggregate with worldwide distribution, Mycological Progress] It was first described in Scandinavia and published in his work “Summa vegitabilum Scandinaviae”, a botanical work written in Latin. [ref: https://search.library.ucla.edu/discovery/fulldisplay/alma9946789483606533/01UCS_LAL:UCLA, search.library.ucla.edu] The common English name of this fungus is the Glasscup.

== Morphology ==

O. xanthostigma are tiny disk/saucer shaped fungi, ranging in size from 0.3mm to 1mm (roughly 1/8 inch across). The fruiting body does not possess a pileus, stipe, ring, or vulva. The hymenium is cup shaped, smooth, and waxy. [ref: Orbilia xanthostigma - Fungipedia Mushroom Guide, Fungipedia] They sit flat on the surface and do not have a stalk. The apothecial coloration is described as golden yellow to orange yellow. When dry, the fruiting bodies may appear wavy or lobed, and irregularly shaped. [ref: ] They typically grow in high numbers, in close proximity to one another. [ref: Glasscup (Orbilia xanthostigma), Mushrooms of Nebraska]

They typically appear in largely dense groups called gregarious clusters and are commonly found on fallen hardwood in moist or shaded woodlands. The disc fungi is a wood decomposer saprotroph. Most of the species are located in temporal regions and are present on rotting wood or tree stumps; found on Various kinds of wood, including broadleaf and coniferous trees [ref: Orbilia xanthostigma - Fungipedia Mushroom Guide, Fungipedia], particularly oak and pine, from the spring to the fall seasons.

The members of this group can also be classified through their spores: cashew shaped and warted [ref: New species and records of orbiliaceous fungi from Georgia, USA, Mycological Progress] ascospores that range from about 2.5-3 micrometers in length with a curvature of about 120-180 degrees. They appear in ascus sacks, typically 8 at a time. The species also has Dicranidion like conidia, a form of asexual spore. These are distinctive spores, developed primarily for the purpose of easier dispersal and spore transport by vectors where anchoring or aquatic adaptations are necessary. Asci are characteristically trunicate at the apex, the base is prolonged in an L shape. The paraphyses are inflated at the apex.

Members of the family Orbiliaceae are typically characterized through the production of light colored and partially translucent apothecia. They also contain small asci and ascospores with KOH soluble spore bodies.

== Carnivorous Nematode Trapping: ==
The class Orbiliomycetes is a large class of fungi within the phylum of Ascomycota; it contains free living, nematophagous, soil fungi that are known for their ability to trap and consume nematodes (as well as other small organisms). They do so through the usage of several trapping mechanisms. Within the members of Orbiliacaea, these mechanisms include adhesive sticky knobs, adhesive networks, constrictor rings, nonconstrictor rings, and sticky adhesive branches. [ref: Nematode-Trapping Fungi, Microbiology Spectrum] [ref: Nematode-Trapping Fungi Eavesdrop on Nematode Pheromones, Current Biology]

Fungi can live saprophytically on wood, and as predators, capturing nematodes. The presence of nematode traps indicates a switch from a saprophytic to predacious feeding system.

The fungi within the genus Orbilia are carnivorous; however, most only supplement their diet through the consumption of nematodes. However, a standing hypothesis claims the species within this genus use nematodes as the primary supply of nitrogen, and in fact are weak wood decomposers. During periods of nutritional starvation or in the presence of nematodes, nematode trapping fungi switch towards predation and produce nematode trapping mechanisms. [ref: Key processes required for the different stages of fungal carnivory by a nematode-trapping fungus, PLOS Biology]

In the asexual state, the telemorph, O. xanthostigma acts as a carnivore.

These organisms play a crucial role in soil dynamics, regulating nematode populations in the ecosystems. Nematode trapping fungi serve as a wonderful model system, and stand indicative of fungal evolution, as well as the evolution of organismal interactions between fungi and nematodes. Similarly, this relationship is also indicative of nematode evolution, representing a marker that promoted nematode fitness against predation and other factors alongside it.

== Phylogeny: ==
O. xanthostigma is a species within the family Orbiliacea, which belongs to the order Orbiliales and the class Orbiliomycetes. It is in the subphylum Pezizomycotina, which resides within the Ascomycota. Orbiliaceae contains more than 200 species in 12 genera. The species Orbilia xanthostigma represents the most commonly recorded species of the Obiliomycetes.

Molecular and genetic analysis of nematode trapping fungi indicates that the monophyletic classes of Orbiliomycetes and Pezizomycetes are two of the earliest branches to diverge from Pezizomycotina. Certain genera are well known nematode trapping fungi. Evidence suggests this ability evolved only once in Orbiliales.

A species complex is a group of closely related organisms that are difficult to distinguish from one another based on their morphology. These may represent two separate species, or they may be the same species, depending on the samples analyzed.

Orbilia xanthostigma is the closest related to the Orbilia leucostigma; this is a cryptic speciation aggregate and is typically referred to as the Orbilia xanthostigma-leucostigma complex. Besides the difference in apothecial color (yellow to orange in O. xanthostigma and white to pale rose in O. leucostigma), there are no other notable morphological differences between the two species. This applies to both the telemorph, which includes the asci, ascospores, and paraphyses (sexual reproductive structures), as well as the anamorphic, which includes the conidia and conidiophores (asexual reproductive structures). While these two names have been used synonymously, they do in fact compose two separate species.

The Orbilia xanthostigma-leucostigma complex include organisms that have been grouped together due to the sexual and asexual morphologies of the ascocarp. They were previously considered two color variants of the same species and were not differentiated between. Both Orbilia xanthostigma and leucostigma grow gregarious clusters on hygric gymno- and angiosperm wood or rarely bark and show a worldwide distribution. [ref: Cryptic speciation in Orbilia xanthostigma and O. leucostigma (Orbiliomycetes): an aggregate with worldwide distribution, Mycological Progress] However, a study by Baral and colleagues concluded that, in fact, this species complex consists of two distinct species.

The method of internal transcriber spaces (ITS) and large subunit gene of rDNA (LSU) regions are the two primary ways for phylogenetic studies within fungi. [ref: Four New Species and New Records of Orbilia from China Based on Molecular and Morphological Data, Journal of Fungi] A lot of genetic diversity can be found within the Orbilia xanthostigma leutostigma complex. When examining samples across Europe and Macaronesia, Baral and colleagues found three separate genotypes, of which the length of ITS and intron consistency and significantly differed. They named the three genotypes O. xanthostigma, O. Cf. xanthostigma, and O. leucostigma. In an analysis of the ITS regions, the xanthostigma-leucostigma complex formed two subclades which were strongly supported by the data. The results support the conclusion that there exist two genetically distinct species. [ref: Orbiliaceae for Turkish Ascomycota: three new records, Bangladesh Journal of Botany]

== Ecological Importance ==
O. xanthostigma is a heterotroph. It cannot manufacture its own food like plants, therefore it must obtain it from somewhere in the environment [ref: Life History and Ecology of the Fungi, ucmp.berkeley.edu], relying on carbon from other organisms for its own metabolism. [ref: 8.10: How Fungi Eat, Biology LibreTexts] Fungi do this by growing through the substrate they are feeding on. This Saprotroph obtains its nutrients by decomposing dead organic matter, such as fallen trees, twigs, stumps, and other lignin based matter. They do so through the secretion of enzymes, absorbing the dissolved material. It also performs carnivorous behavior, as stated above, through predation on nematodes.

This organism serves an important role within forest ecosystems. By decomposing fallen trees, they clear up the space for new growth and allow the cycling of nutrients to occur. Releasing these nutrients back into the environment through consumption, O. xanthostigma propels the carbon cycle.

This organism serves no economical importance to humans. While it is a wood decayed, cycling the nutrients through the ecological system, it plays no role in the agricultural or timber industry.

data.title: Metals4U
data.text:
metals4U is a United Kingdom–based metal supplier that sells cut-to-size metal products through an e-commerce platform. The company supplies metals including aluminium, steel, stainless steel and brass to trade, industrial and individual customers.

== History ==
=== Origins ===
metals4U was established in 2002 and was initially based in Pontefract, West Yorkshire, with around six staff. The company was founded to supply metal products to both commercial businesses and individual consumers, particularly smaller-scale buyers who do not typically use traditional trade suppliers.

In 2015, the company relocated to Wetherby, West Yorkshire, to increase its warehouse capacity. As of May 2026, the company employed approximately 53 staff, comprising 37 warehouse operatives and 16 customer service and administration staff.

=== Transition to e-commerce ===
In 2008, metals4U began selling online. The move enabled nationwide ordering and delivery, and made the company's custom cutting service available through a digital ordering platform. Customers can also collect orders from the company's head office in Wetherby.

== Industry involvement ==
Material specifications supplied by metals4U have been cited in university engineering research, including studies of synthetic inflow turbulence generation at the University of Southampton and of the ductility of lap joints in reinforced concrete beams published by the University of West London. The company has also provided material sponsorship for student engineering projects, including the University of Huddersfield's Formula Student team, Team HARE.

== Leadership ==
The company's co-founder, chairman and majority shareholder is Paul McFadyen. McFadyen has written and been quoted in business and trade media on topics including skills in construction and engineering, global metal markets, circular economy models and international trade policy.

== Bay Springs Middle School ==
Bay Springs Middle School, also known as BSMS shortened, is a middle school located in Villa Rica Georgia, consisting of 829 students as of October 2026. The school serves grades 6-8 and has multiple extracurricular activities that the students can attend/play in. [ref: Home, www.bayspringsmiddle.com]

Note: Bay Springs Middle School is shortened to BSMS in this article.

The doors of BSMS opened in January of 1998, which begun its 2 decade long journey, nearing almost 30 years in 2029! [ref: Home, www.bayspringsmiddle.com]

On March 13th 2020 all schools in America shutdown because of COVID-19, including BSMS [ref: ]

data.title: National Squash League
data.text:
National Squash League (NSL) is a professional, city-based team squash league in the United States. It was created by Timmy Brownell, Spencer Lovejoy and Fernando Valdizan. The league uses a team-based format featuring franchises representing cities, an annual player draft, a running clock, substitutions, power plays and playoffs. [ref: About the NSL, National Squash League]

The NSL played its inaugural season in 2024 with six men's teams. A women's division was introduced in 2025. For the 2026–27 season, the league consists of ten men's teams and six women's teams. [ref: Teams, National Squash League]

The league has a strategic partnership with US Squash, the national governing body for squash in the United States. [ref: US Squash and National Squash League form strategic partnership, SportsTravel] Matches are carried by HomeTeam Network. [ref: HTN Squash: Your Home for the National Squash League, HomeTeam Network]

== History ==

=== 2024: inaugural season ===

The NSL held its first player draft in Nashville in early 2024 to fill six franchises: the Derby City Colts, now the Louisville Colts; the Atlanta Tornados; Chicago Grizzlies; Newport Dragons; the New York City Knights, now the New York Knights; and the Nashville Crushers.

Twenty-four players were drafted. The teams were split into North and South divisions of three, and the two division winners advanced to a championship match.

In June 2024, the New York Knights, who were undefeated during the season, defeated the Nashville Crushers in the inaugural NSL final at the Arlen Specter US Squash Center in Philadelphia. [ref: New York Knights Defeat Nashville Crushers to Lift Inaugural NSL Title, US Squash]

At the trophy ceremony, commissioner Fernando Valdizan announced plans to expand the league with additional men's and women's teams.

=== 2025: expansion and women's division ===

The league's second season expanded to nine men's teams and four women's teams.

The Philadelphia Lightning, Greenwich Panthers and men's Lake Erie Beacons joined the men's competition.

The women's division was also introduced in 2025.

The finals were held June 27–29, 2025, at the Arlen Specter US Squash Center in Philadelphia. Four men's teams and four women's teams advanced to the semifinals.

The Philadelphia Lightning won the men's championship in their first season, recording a 4–0 shutout in the final.

The Philadelphia Freedom won the first NSL women's championship after the DC Inferno forced the final into a shootout. [ref: Philadelphia Freedom and Lightning Conquer NSL Finals, US Squash]

=== 2026 season ===

Two women's expansion teams, the New York Queens and Seattle Freeze, expanded the women's division to six teams.

The Queens made their debut on January 31, 2026, against the DC Inferno.

The 2026 finals were played at MSquash in South Norwalk, Connecticut.

In the men's semifinals, the Greenwich Panthers defeated defending champion Philadelphia Lightning 3–1, while the Chicago Grizzlies defeated the Newport Dragons 4–0.

In the women's semifinals, the New York Queens defeated the Seattle Freeze 3–1.

The DC Inferno won the women's championship by defeating the Queens 3–2 in an overtime shootout following a 2–2 draw.

=== 2026–27 season ===

Beginning with the 2026–27 campaign, the league labels its seasons across calendar years.

The regular season began in October 2026 with ten men's teams and six women's teams. [ref: Schedule, National Squash League]

The Carolina Pirates and a men's Seattle Freeze team joined the men's competition.

The Newport Dragons no longer appear on the league's official 2026–27 team list.

The top four teams in each division advance to the playoffs, scheduled for March 5–7, 2027, at the Arlen Specter US Squash Center in Philadelphia.

== Match format ==

NSL matches are team contests played on a running clock. Each team uses three players at a time, with a roster consisting of three starters and three alternates.

A match is divided into three periods worth a total of four match points. [ref: The NSL Team Format, National Squash League]

=== Scoring ===

A team wins the match points allocated to each period by winning that period. The team with the most match points following all three periods wins the match.

=== Power play ===

A power play is a two-minute period in which only the attacking team serves and scores.

=== Substitutions ===

Alternates may replace players during stoppages, allowing teams to change individual matchups.

=== Timeouts ===

Each team has two one-minute timeouts per match, with a maximum of one timeout during any individual period.

=== Shootout ===

If the teams are tied after the three periods, players face one another for one rally each in lineup order. The first team to win three shootout rallies wins the match.

=== Playoffs and seeding ===

The top four teams in both the men's and women's standings qualify for the playoffs.

Tiebreaking criteria include record, period points, point differential and total points scored.

=== Draft ===

Teams rebuild their rosters during the preseason draft. Players retained as keepers remain with their current team and cost the team a draft selection, while other eligible players enter the draft pool.

data.title: Cong An Nhan Dan Baseball Club
data.text:
Cong An Nhan Dan Baseball Club (), also known as CAND BC is a Vietnamese amateur baseball club based in Hanoi. They regularly compete at the annual Vietnam Baseball Championship.

== History ==

=== Before MPS affiliation ===
CAND BC's origins can be traced back to a youth club called Hanoi Capitals. Founded by an American lawyer in 2008, the club had been a prominent pioneer of baseball in Hanoi as a member of PONY Baseball and Softball Asia-Pacific division, having made its Colt World Series in 2016. [ref: 2015 Baseball WS Archive, www.pony.org]

After the founding of the Vietnam Baseball and Softball Federation (VBSF) in late 2021 and the advent of a national competition, the a senior Capitals team was established for its inaugural tournament in 2022. Consisting of members of the 2015 Colt World Series team, the team finished the tournament in third place.

In 2023, the senior Capitals got restructured into an independent amateur club called the Hanoi 29ers. Under the management of former Cincinnati Reds prospect Lucas Benenati, the team won the inaugural Hanoi Major Series, after finishing fifth in the 2023 national tournament.

=== MPS affiliation ===
In 2024, it was announced that a baseball club, consisting of the former Capitals/29ers core, was established under the Ministry of Public Security's People's Public Security Sports Association. Aptly named the Cong An Nhan Dan Baseball Club, the club won their first national championship title in their first time under the police banner, becoming the first non-HCMC club to do so. [ref: People’s Police secure National Baseball Clubs Championship trophy, vietnamnews.vn]

During the following years, CAND has remained highly competitive at both the local and national level, regularly trading top finishes with local rival Hanoi Archers as well as regularly sending players to the national team roster. They won their first Hanoi league title in 2025, before finishing runner-up in the 2026 national championship, falling short to Southern powerhouse Saigon Storm. [ref: Câu lạc bộ bóng chày Công an nhân dân giành ngôi Á quân giải vô địch quốc gia 2026, Báo Nhân Dân điện tử]

data.title: Rowan Johnston
data.text:
Rowan Johnston is a prominent New Zealand choral conductor, clinician, and singer who serves as the Music Director of the New Zealand Youth Choir [ref: [https://www.nzyouthchoir.com/ New Zealand Youth choir]] (NZYC). Choirs Aotearoa New Zealand appointed him to the prestigious national role, succeeding David Squire as the leader of the world's longest-running national youth choir.

==Current Roles & Leadership==

• New Zealand Youth Choir: Appointed as the fifth Music Director, leading the premier 50-member ensemble for singers aged 18–25. [ref: [https://www.thepost.co.nz/culture/360986057/new-maestro-town-rowan-johnston-leading-nzs-top-youth-choir ThePost Rowan Johnston leading NZ's top youth choir]] [ref: [https://www.choirs.nz/our-choirs/our-people/ NZYC Our people]]

• [https://wellingtonyouthchoir.wordpress.com/ Wellington Youth Choir] [ref: [https://wellingtonyouthchoir.wordpress.com/about-the-music-team/ WYC - About the music team]]: Musical Director for the choir since 2023.

• Chilton Saint James School: Works as the Head of Department (HOD) Music and directs all school choirs, including the Seraphim Choir.

• Voices New Zealand Chamber Choir [ref: [https://www.voicesnz.com/people/rowan-johnston/ VoicesNZ Rowan Johnston]]: Maintains a long-standing position as an active bass chorister (since 1999) and serves as an Associate Conductor.

==Early life and education==
Johnston grew up in a highly musical family environment. He learnt a number of instruments growing up, sang in church choirs, and played in pipe bands. In high school, Johnston successfully auditioned into the New Zealand Secondary Students' Choir (NZSSC). During this time, he discovered his passion for choral music, wanting to pursue singing at the highest level. Later, he advanced into the New Zealand Youth Choir (NZYC) as a bass vocalist. While in the choir, Dr. Karen Grylls, the music director at the time, actively encouraged choir members to try their hand at leading and conducting sections. This experience inspired Johnston to pursue choral direction alongside his passion for singing. [ref: [https://www.rnz.co.nz/concert/programmes/three-to-seven/audio/2019029848/back-where-it-all-began/ RNZ Concert 'Back where it all began']] [ref: [https://www.rnz.co.nz/concert/programmes/upbeat/audio/2018775537/rowan-johnston-passionate-about-choral-music/ RNZ Concert Rowan Johnston passionate about choral music]]

Johnston earned a Bachelor of Music (BMus), specializing in classical singing and composition from Victoria University of Wellington, and later completed a Diploma of Teaching, formally training as a high school music educator from Wellington College of Education. He later went on to complete a Postgraduate Diploma of Music in Conducting (awarded with Distinction), followed by earning a Master of Music in Choral Conducting with First-Class Honours, studying directly under his former youth choir mentor, Dr. Karen Grylls, at the University of Auckland.

==Career==
Rowan Johnston is very well-known in choral circles in New Zealand both as a choir member and as one of New Zealand's top choral conductors.

Johnston is regularly invited to conduct the Gondwana National Choral School in Australia, the premier national choral program, where he conducts intensive performance seasons for young singers from across the country. He is currently a member of Voices NZ, and directs a multitude of high-level choirs, including the New Zealand Youth Choir and the Wellington Youth Choir. Johnston also has an impressive record at the New Zealand Choral Federation's Big Sing competition, having guided multiple ensembles to the National Finale across his tenures at different schools.

Johnston has served as Director of Music at Auckland’s Holy Trinity Cathedral, Musical Director of the Auckland Youth Choir, and conducted Choralation (the combined choir of Westlake Boys and Westlake Girls High Schools), achieving international recognition at the Summa Cum Laude International Music Festival held in Vienna.

Alongside Elise Bradley, Johnston founded and co-directed the Aotearoa Academy Choir, a national training choir for students in preparation for the New Zealand Youth Choir and New Zealand Secondary Students' Choir. Competing at the 13th World Choir Games held in Tāmaki Makaurau, Auckland, in July 2024, the choir achieved exceptional success, earning a Gold Diploma V, 2nd Place Overall in Category 4, "Youth Choirs" of the Open Competition, and Top 5 Score across the entire competition. [ref: [https://www.interkultur.com/newsroom/choir-games/details/news/world-choir-games-2024-results-of-the-champions-competition/ World Choir Games 2024 Results]]

data.title: Marlow Sports Club
data.text:
Marlow Sports Club is an outdoors sports facility, as well as a charity, based in Marlow, Buckinghamshire, England. It is located 28 miles west from Central London, and 4 miles south from High Wycombe as the crow flies.

== History ==
Marlow Sports Club was founded in 1949, on the original site it is located on now. It was originally formed by an umbrella organisation, including Marlow Rugby Union Football Club, Marlow Cricket Club & Marlow Hockey Club. Earlier, from the beginning, in 1895 Owen Peel Wethered purchased approximately 5,800 acres of land between Pound Lane and the River Thames. He leased it to Marlow Cricket Club for 21 years, before Owen died in 1908. Marlow struggled to find players after World War I, and in 1908, after the end of the lease period, the land was put up for sale. [ref: OUR EARLY HISTORY, Marlow Sports Club]

In July 1920, a petition from the staff requested the Wethered directors to purchase it as a recreation club. Not long after, the plan was agreed and the company then upgraded the pavillion, and also installed gas.

A few years after the end of World War II, the MSC (Marlow Sports Club) was founded, still at the same ground on Pound Lane, and that same year, the Wethereds were sold to Strong & Co, which was obtained by Whitbread in 1969.

Everything was going as planned and well in major circumstances until 2006, when MSC shockingly recieved a notification that Whitbread had decided that the site was to be auctioned of, potentially for housing. The sports club then fought a 5-year long battle to save the green site. This lasted from April 2006 to March 2011, as it became a charity as well as it's ever-lasting sports facility in January 2011. This incurred debts of over £1M. [ref: OUR STORY, Marlow Sports Club]

== Role ==
Marlow Sports Club is now a protected sports facility and charity purposed for sports and leisure (including the nearby Court Garden Leisure Centre), and has grown to become one of Marlow's biggest sports centres.

The sports facility has a collective membership count of around 2,500 members, and of which over half are under 18 (juniors). This is excluding large sporting participation, and back in 2006 when they got notified from Whitbread, their collective membership was approximately 5x smaller (around 500). It has many member clubs, Marlow Cricket Club, Marlow Hockey Club, Marlow Riders, Marlow Striders, Marlow Tennis Club, Marlow Petanque and for school sporting, Sir William Borlase's Grammar School. [ref: OUR STORY, Marlow Sports Club]

The club offers a first-class floodlit hockey pitch, 4 all-weather floodlit tennis courts, petanque terrains, and a cricket pitch.

data.title: Ivan Fernando Rodríguez Huerta Bio
data.text:
----

Ivan Fernando Rodríguez Huerta is a Mexican-born industrial systems engineer, global enterprise transformation executive, supply chain strategist, and business operations optimization practitioner. He serves as the Vice President of Exploration Tooling and Global Supply Chain at Boart Longyear, a multinational corporation specializing in the manufacturing of drilling services and tooling equipment for the global mining and resource extraction sectors. Over a multi-decade executive career spanning North America, Latin America, Europe, and Asia, Rodríguez's work has focused on macro-level corporate restructurings, cross-border lean manufacturing paradigms, and continuous-improvement frameworks. His published academic research intersects industrial behavioral psychology, statistical risk modeling for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), and operational ergonomics.

== Early Life and Academic Foundations ==

Rodríguez was raised in Mexico, where his early tracking centered on systemic engineering and process optimization. He attended the Instituto Tecnológico y de Estudios Superiores de Monterrey (ITESM) to study manufacturing systems before pursuing advanced management and business administration training in the United States.

In 2021, he completed his doctoral research at the University of Phoenix, earning a Doctor of Business Administration (DBA) degree. His peer-reviewed doctoral dissertation deployed a quantitative correlational research design utilizing multiple regression analyses and independent-samples t-tests across a dataset of 465 randomly sampled Mexican enterprises. This research sought to isolate statistical predictors of long-term solvency fractions and debt ratios (DR) within volatile emerging business markets.

== Corporate Transformation Career ==

=== Cross-Border Operational Governance ===

Rodríguez's early professional tenure was defined by directing supply operations within high-velocity industrial manufacturing corridors. He directed multi-facility portfolios, automated control matrices, and heavy fluid-routing production infrastructure for foundational logistics and engineering firms, including Honeywell, Robertshaw, and Bundy Refrigeration. His operational implementations during this period focused on the execution of cellular manufacturing, the elimination of cross-border supply frictions, and the deployment of Lean Six Sigma continuous-improvement models.

=== Senior Executive Administration ===

From 2023 to 2025, Rodríguez served as the Chief Transformation Officer (CTO) for Current Lighting (formerly GE Lighting solutions). In this capacity, he directed corporate turnarounds, engineered macro-level supply chain consolidations to mitigate post-pandemic logistical bottlenecks, and deployed localized digital commerce architectures across the enterprise's multinational footprint.

In January 2025, Rodríguez joined the global executive leadership team at Boart Longyear as the Vice President of Exploration Tooling and Global Supply Chain, operating out of the corporation's headquarters in Salt Lake City, Utah. In this executive capacity, his portfolio covers the operational governance of international manufacturing facilities, global strategic sourcing, and tooling engineering infrastructure. His division directs the lean execution, safety metrics, and production of specialized exploration tools, including coring rods, diamond bits, and casing systems, across a global workforce.

=== Private Entities ===

In April 2026, Rodríguez registered two private corporate entities in the state of Utah to scale decentralized optimization frameworks:

* Reimagined Solutions Group LLC: Formed as a boutique corporate consultancy specializing in global supply chain optimization, business management modeling, and lean structural transformation.
* Healthy Life Vending Machines LLC: A regional automated retail and hospitality enterprise focusing on decentralized nutritional access configurations.

== Philanthropy and Economic Advocacy ==

Rodríguez is the co-founder of Mexicanos en Movimiento, a non-profit organization established to drive human development metrics and expand decentralized access to educational infrastructure. Operating under the motto "emprendiendo con valor" (entrepreneurship with courage), the organization designs community programs that foster social equity, support continuous learning, and eliminate systemic developmental disparities across regional populations.

== Academic Contributions and Behavioral Economics ==

As a business author and optimization practitioner, Rodríguez's research centers on the reduction of systemic organizational complexities through strategic simplicity.

=== Predictive Solvency Modeling ===

In his 2021 doctoral treatise, Servant Leadership and Business Models as Predictors of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises Financial Success, Rodríguez mapped the intersection of human-centric management and financial risk metrics. Utilizing multiple regression techniques, the study isolated how specific dimensions of Servant Leadership (SL) and structured Business Model (BM) parameters correlate with an enterprise's debt ratio and long-term financial insolvency risks. The work has been referenced as an empirical validation connecting organizational behavioral economics with macroeconomic enterprise survival rates.

=== Applied Auditory Ergonomics ===

In his 2017 research volume, Music Tempo and Manufacturing Efficiency Ratio, Rodríguez constructed a mathematical baseline evaluating environmental psychology against human labor outputs within industrial assembly line configurations. The study isolated variations in acoustic tempo to track positive and negative correlations with factory shop-floor production speeds, aiming to optimize continuous lean manufacturing output parameters without accelerating human capital exhaustion or cognitive fatigue.

=== Cartesian Logic in Digital Commerce ===

Through his Plan Profesional de E-Business series, Rodríguez authored a practical framework applying structural Cartesian logic to modern entrepreneurial logistics. Utilizing a case study centered on renewable energy deployment (specifically Energia Solar Tata), the text established step-by-step methodologies to optimize financial and operational performance while successfully integrating Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) parameters into global value offers.

== Published Bibliography ==

* Plan Profesional de E-Business: Construcción de un E-Business plan paso a paso. Caso práctico: E-Business plan para Energía Solar Tata (2014, Editorial Dunken) ISBN 978-9870277378
* Music Tempo and Manufacturing Efficiency Ratio: An Experimental Research (2017, Scholars' Press) ISBN 978-3330651937
* Servant Leadership and Business Models as Predictors of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises Financial Success: A Regression Analysis (2021, University of Phoenix / ProQuest UMI No. 28416045)
* Management, Leadership, and Decision Sciences: An Executive Framework (2025, Independently published) ISBN 979-8312686814

== Honors and Distinctions ==

* Marquis Who's Who (2026): Formally selected for inclusion in the biographical registry for outstanding professional references in global enterprise transformation, operational turnarounds, and servant leadership paradigms.

data.title: Jeroen De Valk
data.text:
Jeroen de Valk (born June 19, 1958) is a Dutch journalist, author and jazz historian. Internationally, he is primarily known as the author of the first biographies of the jazz musicians Chet Baker and Ben Webster. Both books have been translated into English; the Baker-bio as well in several other languages.

Education and career

De Valk was born in Rotterdam, grew up in Amsterdam, where he started writing professionally for the daily newspaper Het Parool in 1979, and has been living in the town of Amersfoort since 1987, where he still works as a general reporter. He studied double bass at the jazz section of the Royal Conservatory in The Hague (1982-1985). Since 2021, he is editor-in-chief of Jazz Bulletin, a quarterly magazine devoted to Dutch jazz history, published by the Nederlands Jazz Archief (Dutch Jazz Archive).

Writings

Since 1979, De Valk published countless articles in newspapers and magazines. His first book was Chet Baker / Herinneringen Aan Een Lyrisch Trompettist (1989), a biography for which he started his research in the early 80s. De Valk published a drastically updated edition in English in 2017 and hopes to release another update in 2027. This book was available in several languages, see the bibliography below.

His biography Het Levensverhaal Van Ben Webster (1992) was translated into in English in 2001. De Valk traces Webster’s life from family members who were forced to live in slavery to the donation – after Webster’s passing - of his favorite tenor saxophone ‘Ol’ Betsy’ to the Institute of Jazz Studies.

De Valk compiled series of his jazz portraits and interviews in Go Man, Go! (2009), So Near So Far (2016) and Jazz In De Schaduw (2025). He devoted a biography as well to Dutch veteran drummer John Engels, at the occasion of Engels’ 80th birthday: Hé Vogel, Wanneer Spelen We Weer? (2015).

Chet Baker research

De Valk examined at length what he considers ‘assumptions and misconceptions’, among others those surrounding Baker’s death in 1988 after falling from his hotel window. De Valk inspected the hotel room, talked extensively with the police officer who researched the circumstances of his passing, the police man who actually found him and people who were close to him in his last days.

In the same detailed manner, De Valk followed Baker’s musical career. The Valk concludes that Baker was a great trumpeter, almost to the very end. This contrasts with the image of Baker as a washed-up musician, created in the popular ‘documentary’ Let’s Get Lost. The book closes with an annotated discography with more than 250 albums.

Amersfoort history

De Valk writes regularly about the history of Amersfoort, his hometown, in local media. Among publications in book form are De Wagenwerkplaats / Het Spoor, De Strijd, De Toekomst (with Arjan Klaver).

Poetry

De Valk debuted as a poet with his collection Dagen Zonder Licht / Sonnetten Over Depressie, Dood En Rouw (2026). He wrote these sonnets after the passing of his son, journalist Arnold de Valk. His primary goal was to provide ‘a sense of recognition and comfort for people with depression and their caregivers, as well as understanding from those around them.’ Nevertheless, he received explicit support from Jean Pierre Rawie, the best-selling poet in the Netherlands. (1) In interviews, De Valk revealed that he himself had suffered from periods of depression and anxiety, but was always able to recover. (2)

Music

De Valk can be heard as a jazz bassist on the album Traces Of Chesney / A Tribute To Chet Baker, with a band lead by trumpeter Edu Ninck Blok (2015, Silence! Records) and several albums with Dutch Treat, the band of singer and lyricist Nynke Geertsma. The latter’s band had noted tenor saxophonist Leo Janssen (Metropole Orkest) as a guest soloist on Dit Is Pas Het Begin (2025, Dutch Treat Music).

2 – AD Amersfoortse Courant, 13 september 2026 / De Stad Amersfoort, 29 augustus 2026

data.title: Ehab El-Shaarawy
data.text:
Ehab El-Shaarawy is an Egyptian professor of anatomy at Cairo University.

He served as Head of the Department of Anatomy, Faculty of Medicine, Kasr Al Ainy, Cairo University from 2018 to 2024.

data.title: The Subliminal Man
data.text:
"The Subliminal Man" is a dystopian science fiction short story by J.G. Ballard. It was first published in the January 1963 issue of New Worlds (Volume 42, Number 126) and later reprinted in The Disaster Area and The Terminal Beach. [ref: JG Ballard Cover Scans 1962-1963, www.rickmcgrath.com]The story is, like many other of his short stories, very political at its core. [ref: ] It thematizes the power of technology and media, [ref: ] as well as subliminal messaging and consumerism.

== Plot ==
The story opens with Hathaway calling out to Dr. Robert Franklin "The signs, Doctor! Have you seen the signs?" Franklin tries to ignore Hathaway and get away, but fails. He vexedly asks him what the matter is, to which Hathaway replies that the government has "started to build the first big signs! Over a hundred feet high, on the traffic islands outside town. They‘ll soon have all the approach roads covered. When they do we might as well stop thinking." Franklin doesn’t believe Hathaway, a former patient, and instead believes that he is mentally ill and needs professional help. He urges Hathaway to think of his wife and child. Hathaway insists that he is and that the signs are dangerous for his family, claming that the government is trying to "transistorize our brains!" Franklin dismisses him, telling him that if he had any evidence of the emittance of subliminal messages and commands, he would help him, but he doesn't. He reminds him that subliminal advertising was banned 30 years ago and calls his conspiracy preposterous. Hathaway drops the issue and instead points out that all the cars in the parking lot are identical in design and color. He argues that the standardization removed variety without making the cars any cheaper. He asks Franklin about his new car, since he only had his old one for 3 months. Franklin answers that he traded it in and defends himself by stating that "If you ever had any money you‘d realize that it‘s the most economical way of owning a car. You don‘t keep driving the same one until it falls apart. It‘s the same with everything else—television sets, washing machines, refrigerators. But you aren‘t faced with the problem." Hathaway replies „Not a bad idea, either, Doctor. It gives me time to think. I‘m not working a twelve-hour day to pay for a lot of things I‘m too busy to use before they‘re obsolete.“ After driving off, Franklin reflects on his own life and realizes that he envies Hathaway's freedom, since he is not restricted by mortgages, social obligations or private work like Franklin is. [ref: ]

As Franklin drives home, he observes the enormous motorway network that covers much of the country. Although the roads are impressive, they have created serious congestion, and his journey is much longer than it used to be. The roads are designed to force drivers to maintain specific speeds through rubber studs that produce unpleasant vibrations when cars travel too slowly or too quickly. These systems are supposedly intended to improve safety, but they also force motorists to replace their tyres regularly. Cars are deliberately designed to wear out quickly, encouraging people to buy new models more frequently and increasing profits for manufacturers. Franklin then sees workers constructing one of the giant signs beside the motorway. He initially assumes that it is connected to the airport, but after seeing another similar structure, he begins to suspect that the signs have a different purpose.

When Franklin arrives home, he finds his wife, Judith, watching television and writing down numbers from a shopping programme called Spot Bargains. The programme offers discounts on household products, encouraging viewers to trade in their possessions for new ones. Judith wants to replace their barbecue spit even though they have only owned it for two months. Franklin refuses because he believes the purchase is unnecessary, but Judith insists that buying a replacement will save them money. Franklin then notices the giant sign outside their home and asks Judith about it. She believes it is part of the airport system, but Franklin is becoming increasingly suspicious that the signs are connected to the strange behaviour of consumers.

When Franklin meets Hathaway again, he is less doubtfull of Hathaway's 'conspiracy' but isn't fully ready to admit it yet. Hathaway asks him what he's gonna do about the signs to which Franklin replies

"Nothing, of course. Damn it, it may be just auto-suggestion, you‘ve probably got me imagining—“

"Don‘t be absurd, Doctor! If you can‘t believe your own senses what chance have you left? They‘re invading your brain, if you don‘t defend yourself they‘ll take it over completely! We‘ve got to act now, before we‘re all paralysed.“

Franklin questions why the signs would command people to consume more, since the spending power isn't increasing. Hathaway retorts that an increase in working hours is imminent, Franklin doesn't think that society would let that happen. Hathaway argues that it did already happen in the past, and people won't do anything about it this time, either. Franklin asks Hathaway what he is going to do, but he won't tell him unless he joins. Franklin refuses.

Two months later, Franklin sees a crowd gathered around one of the giant signs beside the motorway. The sign is flashing patterns of light, and several men are climbing its metal structure. Franklin approaches the scene and discovers that the police are pursuing a man near the top of the sign. He recognises the man as Hathaway, who is attempting to sabotage the equipment. Suddenly, the flashing lights become clear, and the sign displays the messages "BUY NOW", "NEW CAR NOW" and "YES YES YES", proving that Hathaway was right all along. Hathaway is shot, but cries out in victory before jumping from the sign to his death.

The story ends with Franklin observing the construction of new signs outside his window. He knows the truth, but doesn't do anything about it. He drives to the supermarket with his wife to buy new appliances and register for a new car.

data.title: Nizar Kiram
data.text:
----
Nizar Kiram is a Filipino former basketball player who played collegiate basketball for the St. Francis of Assisi College Doves and competed in the Philippine Basketball League (PBL) with John-O. He was also one of the applicants for the 2008 PBA draft.

== Basketball career ==

=== Collegiate career ===
Kiram played collegiate basketball for St. Francis of Assisi College. In March 2002, he was among the St. Francis players who participated in the Philippine Basketball League Rookie Camp. [ref: 158 aspirante sa PBL Rookies Camp, Pilipino Star Ngayon]

During the 2002 National Capital Region Athletic Association season, Kiram was part of a St. Francis team that entered the latter stages of the competition as defending champion. In December 2002, he scored 12 points in a 67–48 victory over La Salle-Manila, sharing second-highest scoring honors for St. Francis with Ervin Sotto behind Ranidel de Ocampo. [ref: PSBA rebounds, trips SS-Cavite, The Philippine Star]

In January 2003, Kiram contributed to St. Francis' 88–79 victory over Colegio de San Lorenzo in the quarterfinals of the NCRAA tournament, playing alongside Ranidel de Ocampo and Freddie Montelibano. [ref: St. Francis topples San Lorenzo five, The Philippine Star]

Later that year, Kiram led St. Francis with 15 points in a 75–72 victory over the Philippine School of Business Administration during the Universities and Colleges Athletic Association men's basketball tournament. Two of his three-point field goals helped St. Francis build a 19-point lead during the game. [ref: Doves soar past Jaguars; Generals up, The Philippine Star]

=== Philippine Basketball League ===
Kiram also played for John-O in the Philippine Basketball League. In September 2002, he was listed as part of a John-O lineup that included Ranidel de Ocampo, Jeff Napa, Archen Cayabyab, Bong Salvador and Mark Macapagal during the PBL–Cebu Basketball Federation Dual Meet. [ref: Casino vs John-O; Hapee kontra Blu, Pilipino Star Ngayon]

John-O subsequently competed in the 2002 PBL Challenge Cup, with Kiram and Ricky Calimag forming part of the team's frontline alongside PBL-CBF Most Valuable Player Ranidel de Ocampo. [ref: John-O Juzz team to beat, Pilipino Star Ngayon]

In June 2003, John-O defeated the Montana Jewels, 80–67, to finish third in the PBL Unity Cup. Pilipino Star Ngayon reported that Kiram and Emerson Oreta helped Richard Melencio during a decisive 19–0 third-quarter run. [ref: Hapee naisahan ng Viva, Pilipino Star Ngayon]

=== 2008 PBA draft ===
Kiram later applied for the 2008 PBA draft. He was included among the 45-player applicant pool reported by both The Philippine Star and GMA News. [ref: Norwood, Dillinger cleared for PBA draft, The Philippine Star] [ref: Welcoat to get Norwood as top PBA draft choice, GMA News Online]

The draft class included Gabe Norwood, Jared Dillinger, Jayson Castro, Beau Belga, Jeff Chan, Solomon Mercado and other players who later competed professionally in the Philippine Basketball Association. Kiram was not selected during the two-round draft.

== Family background ==
A genealogy maintained by members of the Kiram family identifies Nizar S. Kiram as the eldest listed son of Datu Ibrahim Dalus Kiram and Ruby Salcedo. [ref: Datu Ibrahim Dalus Kiram, Preservation of Sulu Sultanate – History and Rights]

Ibrahim Dalus Kiram belonged to the Kiram family associated with the historic Sultanate of Sulu. The same family genealogy identifies Ibrahim as a son of Punjungan Kiram and a brother of Jamalul Kiram III. Because succession to the Sultanate of Sulu has been disputed among different branches of the family, descriptions of royal titles and succession vary among sources.

data.title: John Michael Faile (Athlete)
data.text:
John Michael Faile II (born May 11, 2000) is an American professional baseball player in the Cincinnati Reds organization. He plays catcher and first base for the Dayton Dragons, the Reds' High-A affiliate. Faile played college baseball at North Greenville University, where he set NCAA Division II career records for home runs and runs batted in.

==Early life==

Faile was born in Lancaster County, South Carolina, and lived in Lancaster until the eighth grade. His parents are Michael and Julie Faile. The family later moved to Boiling Springs, South Carolina, because of Michael's work. Faile is the oldest of three children, with a younger brother, Austin, and a younger sister, Annalynn. [ref: Archdeacon: Epic Faile — The unbelievable story of a Dragons hero and his grandpa, Dayton Daily News]

Faile played baseball from a young age. His grandfather, Curtis Threatt, was an important part of his baseball career. Threatt played football and baseball at Colorado State University and later worked in education and athletics in South Carolina. He also regularly played catch with Faile when he was growing up.

Faile attended Boiling Springs High School. About 60 players tried out for the baseball team when he arrived, and Faile was one of three players who made the team.

Faile was named to the South Carolina All-State team in 2017 and 2018. He was also named the state's 5A Baseball Player of the Year in 2018. [ref: John Michael Faile - 2023 Baseball Roster, North Greenville University Athletics]

He attended North Greenville University after high school. Faile had not received a Division I scholarship and was overlooked by larger college programs. [ref: MLB draft within reach for North Greenville catcher overlooked out of high school, The Post and Courier]

==College career==

Faile played five seasons at North Greenville from 2019 to 2023. He was named Conference Carolinas Freshman of the Year in 2019.

In 2021, Faile batted.438 with 23 home runs and 78 RBI. He was named Conference Carolinas Player of the Year and the National Collegiate Baseball Writers Association Southeast Region Player of the Year. [ref: John Michael Faile of North Greenville named Herff Jones Conference Carolinas Male Athlete of the Year, Conference Carolinas]

In 2022, Faile hit.418 with 16 home runs and 86 RBI. He won the Conference Carolinas Triple Crown, leading the conference in batting average, home runs and RBI. [ref: 2022 Baseball Cumulative Statistics, North Greenville University Athletics]

Faile suffered a knee injury during the 2022 Conference Carolinas tournament, but he returned for the NCAA Division II championship tournament. He hit a home run in his first at-bat after returning from the injury against West Chester University. [ref: Crusaders Begin NCAA Division II Baseball Championship with Win Over West Chester, North Greenville University Athletics]

North Greenville won the NCAA Division II national championship that year after defeating Point Loma Nazarene University 5–3 on June 10, 2022. It was the first national championship in the school's baseball program. [ref: National Champions: North Greenville Wins NCAA Division II Baseball Tournament, North Greenville University Athletics]

Faile broke the NCAA Division II career RBI record during the 2023 season. He finished his college career with 81 home runs and 337 RBI, both NCAA Division II records. [ref: Dayton Dragons GameDay, Game Notes, and Roster for April 2, OurSports Central]

Faile also played summer baseball while in college. He played for the Savannah Bananas in 2020 and the Spartanburgers in 2021. [ref: 2020 Savannah Bananas Summer Statistics, The Baseball Cube] [ref: 2021 Spartanburgers Summer Statistics, The Baseball Cube]

==Professional career==

===Billings Mustangs===

Faile was not selected in the 2023 Major League Baseball draft. He played for the Billings Mustangs of the Pioneer League in 2023. In 54 games, he hit.353 with 21 home runs and 70 RBI. He was named Pioneer League Rookie of the Year. [ref: Cincinnati Reds sign catcher John Michael Faile, Reds Minor Leagues] [ref: Award Winners & All-Stars Announced, OurSports Central]

===Cincinnati Reds===

The Cincinnati Reds signed Faile to a minor league contract on December 19, 2023. [ref: John Michael Faile Signs Minor League Contract with Cincinnati Reds, North Greenville University Athletics]

Faile began the 2024 season with the Arizona Complex League Reds before joining the Dayton Dragons in August. He hit a home run in his second plate appearance in his Dayton debut and homered again the following night. In his third game, he hit a grand slam. [ref: Dragons 2025 Team Preview, Part 2: First Basemen, MiLB.com]

Faile played 91 games for Dayton in 2025. He hit.233 with 13 home runs and 56 RBI. [ref: John Michael Faile Stats, Age, Position, Height, Weight, Fantasy & News, MiLB.com]

In 2026, Faile hit.278 with 14 home runs and 51 RBI during the regular season. On August 30, he hit his 30th home run with Dayton, tying the franchise record set by Chris Williamson. On September 5, he hit his 31st home run with the Dragons and broke the record. [ref: Faile Breaks Dragons Career Home Run Record in Dayton Win on Saturday, MiLB.com]

data.title: Chrysalis Finance
data.text:
Chrysalis Finance Limited is a British financial services company that arranges credit for private healthcare treatment, allowing patients to pay for procedures in monthly instalments. [ref: CHRYSALIS FINANCE LIMITED, company number 06541664, Companies House] [ref: About us, Chrysalis Finance] Its finance is offered through dental practices, private hospitals and clinics, covering dental, cosmetic, eye, hearing, diagnostic and fertility treatment. The company's registered office is in Worsley, Greater Manchester, and it is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority. [ref: Financial Services Register: firm reference numbers 631193 and 720098, Financial Conduct Authority]

== History ==
The company was incorporated on 20 March 2008 as Hewlett Mortimer Limited and changed its name to Chrysalis Finance Limited on 4 February 2013.

In August 2015, the dental trade publication Dentistry reported a partnership between Chrysalis and the dental plan provider Patient Plan Direct. [ref: Patient Plan Direct and Chrysalis Finance announce new partnership, Dentistry] The report described a model under which dental practices could become appointed representatives of Chrysalis, offering patient finance without holding their own consumer credit authorisation.

According to the company, it acquired the dental finance brokers Financing First and Dental Finance in 2020, and later launched Treatment Pay, a card payment service for healthcare providers.

== Operations ==
Chrysalis arranges loans that patients repay over periods of between three months and five years, including interest-free options. [ref: Medical finance, Chrysalis Finance] Patients apply either in the clinic or from home.

Private hospital groups that list Chrysalis as their patient finance provider include Nuffield Health, [ref: Personal medical loans, Nuffield Health] Ramsay Health Care UK, [ref: Finance options, Ramsay Health Care UK] Practice Plus Group [ref: Finance options, Practice Plus Group] and Benenden Hospital. [ref: Finance, Benenden Hospital]

== Regulation ==
Chrysalis Finance Limited is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority for lending and credit broking under firm reference number 631193. Its sister company Financing First Limited, incorporated in 2000, is authorised for credit broking under firm reference number 720098. [ref: FINANCING FIRST LIMITED, company number 04114714, Companies House] Both companies, together with Treatmentpay Limited, are registered at the same address in Worsley. [ref: TREATMENTPAY LTD, company number 12822532, Companies House]

data.title: The Four: No One Fights Alone
data.text:
The Four: No One Fights Alone is an upcoming Nigerian drama film written, directed and produced by Funke Akindele. The film is produced by Funke Akindele Network and distributed by FilmOne Entertainment. It is scheduled for a global cinema release on 11 December 2026. [ref: Funke Akindele's 'The Four: No One Fights Alone' set for December release, The Punch]

==Plot==
The film follows Esosa and three women who leave their community for the city in an effort to secure the future of a young man they love. Their journey puts their friendship, courage, faith and loyalty to the test as they encounter unexpected circumstances. [ref: Funke Akindele's 'The Four: No One Fights Alone' set for December release, The Punch] [ref: The Four: No One Fights Alone (2026) - Nigerian Movie - African Movie Database]

The story is set between the Odu community and the city and explores themes including friendship, motherhood, resilience, hope, sacrifice and unity. The production incorporates elements of Nigerian cultural identity through music, fashion, language and tradition. [ref: Funke Akindele sets another December box-office test with ‘The Four’, Premium Times]

==Production==
Funke Akindele announced The Four: No One Fights Alone in August 2026. She serves as the film's writer, director and producer, with Funke Akindele Network producing the film and FilmOne Entertainment handling its theatrical distribution. [ref: Funke Akindele sets another December box-office test with ‘The Four’, Premium Times]

The film was described as a drama centred on friendship, motherhood, resilience and the strength of ordinary women. According to reports surrounding its announcement, the story examines relationships and experiences intended to be familiar to audiences. [ref: Funke Akindele's 'The Four: No One Fights Alone' set for December release, The Punch]

In September 2026, Akindele released first-look images from the production. The film incorporates Nigerian cultural elements into its visual presentation, with Adire featuring prominently in the costumes. [ref: Funke Akindele unveils first look at new film, The Punch]

The production also features the original song "Oremi", performed by Akindele, Waje, Bisola Aiyeola and Chioma Akpotha. The song was released alongside the film's first-look material in September 2026. [ref: Funke Akindele Unveils First Look at “The Four: No One Fights Alone” Ahead of December Release, The Nollywood Reporter]

==Release==
The Four: No One Fights Alone is scheduled for a global cinema release on 11 December 2026, with FilmOne Entertainment handling its theatrical distribution. [ref: Funke Akindele's 'The Four: No One Fights Alone' set for December release, The Punch]

=== It (2017) ===

The first of a two-part adaptation of the 1986 novel, as well as the second adaptation following the 1990 miniseries. Set in the fictional town of Derry, Maine, the film tells the story of The Losers' Club, a group of seven outcast children who are terrorized by the eponymous being which emerges from the sewer in the form of Pennywise the Dancing Clown, and face their own personal demons as the monster torments them.

=== It Chapter Two (2019) ===

The sequel to It (2017) and the second of a two-part adaptation of the 1986 novel. Set 27 years after the events of the first film, the story centers on the Losers Club and their relationships as they reunite to destroy It once and for all.

=== ‘It’ Supercut ===
A combined version of It (2017) and It Chapter Two (2019), including all the scenes deleted for time constraints, as well as some newly filmed scenes. It is expected to surpass 6 hours. [ref: Andy Muschietti On 'It' Supercut Plans, Deadline]

In the second season, set in 1935 during the Great Depression, the Bradley Gang, a group of bank robbers, arrives in Derry to purchase ammunition, only to find themselves caught in a brutal massacre and confronted with terrifying horrors. data.title: COURSEPRO AFRICA LTD
data.text:
CoursePro Africa Ltd is a Nigerian educational technology (EdTech) firm based in Oron, Akwa Ibom State. Conceived in October 2018 and incorporated on November 28, 2024, the company creates curriculum-aligned animated video books and digital learning aids for higher education students across Africa. [ref: From Student's Search For Understanding To Birth Of CoursePro Africa, Independent Newspaper Nigeria]

== History ==
The venture began on October 18, 2018, when co-founder Elijah Effiong Amah, then a mathematics undergraduate at Abia State University, sought visual aids for complex real analysis theories and started a YouTube channel with his mother, Kate Micheal Edet. After Amah graduated in 2021, the project broadened to cover subjects such as medicine, law, and engineering. Computer scientist Imoh Davis Udofa joined in December 2023 to structure the content around institutional learning goals and manage formal registration.

== Business model and operations ==
CoursePro partners directly with universities, converting approved textbooks and materials into "animated video books" for internal learning portals without upfront production fees for the institutions. Costs are offset through student access fees, with revenue shared with academic contributors. These animated assets serve strictly as supplementary learning tools rather than replacements for standard lectures or labs.

== Corporate affairs ==
=== Leadership ===
* Uchenna Agukwu, a pharmacist – Chief Executive Officer (assumed role November 28, 2025).
* Elijah Effiong Amah – Chief Operating Officer.
* Imoh Davis Udofa – Chief Content Officer.
* Emmanuel Effiong Amah – Core team member (joined June 1, 2026, following the death of co-founder Kate Micheal Edet).

data.title: George Morland (MP)
data.text:
George Morland (13 February 1643 – 1712) was an English politician. He sat as MP for the City of Durham (constituency) from 1689 till 1695. [ref: MORLAND, George (1643-1712), of Elvet, Durham and Greystones, co. Dur., History of Parliament Online]

He also served as commissioner for recusants for County Durham in 1675; freeman of Hartlepool in 1680; alderman of Durham by 1684 till 1687, and 1688 till his death; and Mayor from 1690 till 1691.

He was the first son of John Morland (died 1689), attorney of Durham by Thomasina, the daughter of George Martyn of Durham. He was educated in Durham School, Magdalene College, Cambridge in 1659, he earned a BA in 1662. On 7 November 1671, he married Mary (died 1721), the daughter of Cuthber Carr of Auckland St. Helen and the widow of Alexander Davidson of Blakiston. They had two sons (one predeceased) and two daughters.

data.title: Anti-Rabid Fanbases
data.text:
Anti-Rabid Fanbases (ARF) was an anti-fandom internet trolling group founded and owned by Princess Java McMan. Established in 2015, the group was created in response to widespread annoyance with the rapidly emerging Five Nights at Freddy's fandom on Youtube [ref: I ARE TECH: The Gayest Story Never Told] [ref: Click, M. A. (2019). Anti-fandom. NYU Press.]. Operating primarily across YouTube, Steam [ref: Steam Community:: Group:: Anti-Rabid Fanbases, steamcommunity.com], DeviantArt, Reddit, and the now-defunct Google+, ARF organized coordinated comment spam campaigns targeting prominent internet personalities [ref: Barnes, R. (2018). Uncovering online commenting culture. Springer.], including Markiplier. In addition to targeting individuals, the group orchestrated mass raids and harassment campaigns against various fandom-related communities [ref: Phillips, W. (2015). This is why we can’t have nice things. MIT Press.] [ref: Poland, B. (2016). Haters: Harassment, abuse, and violence online. Potomac Books.] [ref: Gorman, G. (2019). Troll hunting: Inside the world of online hate and its human fallout. Hardie Grant Books.]. ARF temporarily dissolved in 2017 after its Google+ group was deleted by Princess Java McMan [ref: What made your day? KAI - Page 18 - Toho Kingdom, www.tohokingdom.com], the organization later disbanded entirely in late 2019 due to leadership disagreements regarding its direction [ref: UTubeTrollPolice, UTubeTrollPedia] and the subsequent shutdown of Google+.

== Origins and history ==
In 2015, a YouTube channel named "Smilk" was created as a parody of prominent gaming YouTuber Smike. [ref: Smilk and Smike:: Five Nights at Freddy's 3 General Discussions, steamcommunity.com] The name originated from a internet nickname used by both fans and detractors combining "Smike" and "milk," reflecting a common perception at the time that Smike was "milking" Five Nights at Freddy's content for money.

Following the online traction of the Smilk channel, Princess Java McMan established the ARF Google+ group alongside Smilk. The primary objective to harass and troll fandoms they deemed rabid. [ref: Wright, K. (2016). Internet trolls and stalkers - nutjob atheists. Lulu Press, Inc.]

In June 2015, the group began vandalizing the Five Nights at Freddy's Fandom Wiki. As part of the coordination, members posted a warning message on the wiki's forums stating, "About 40 of us are going to raid your wiki. We're Anti-Rabid Fanbases, a google+ community. Anyway, better be prepared. The storm is coming." [ref: ]

During its time on Google+, Anti-Rabid Fanbases became involved in many conflicts with other users and online communities [ref: Eckstrand, N. (2018, November 29). The ugliness of trolls: Comparing the strategies/methods of the alt-right and the Ku Klux Klan.], It was a prime target for both fellow internet trolls and members of the fandoms they targeted, leading to an infiltration and mass banning of members by a user known as "Lizurdy" on July 15th, 2015. [ref: Anti-Rabid Fanbases Raided]

data.title: Kanaris Tsinganos
data.text:
----

Kanaris C. Tsinganos (Greek: Κανάρης Τσίγκανος) is a theoretical astrophysicist, professor emeritus at the Department of Physics of the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens, [ref: Emeritus Professors, siteA-EN] elected director of the National Observatory of Athens. [ref: Prof. Tsinganos Kanaris – Former Director of the National Observatory of Athens (2011–2016), National Observatory of Athens] As the first national representative of Greece to ESA (Science Programm Committee, ESA/SPC), led his scientific team to become the first Greek group to participate to an ESA science space misssion (Proba 3). Tsinganos's contributions in refereed journals [ref: Google Scholar, scholar.google.com] are on MHD phenomena at the solar atmosphere, solar wind, stellar winds and astrophysical jets. He is known for the Sauty-Tsinganos criterion [ref: Nonradial and nonpolytropic astrophysical outflows. IV The transition from jets to winds, Astronomy and Astrophysics] for the transition of a stellar wind to a selfsimilar jet and the Vlahakis-Tsinganos systematic construction of exact selfsimilar MHD solutions for astrophysical winds and jets [ref: Systematic construction of exact magnetohydrodynamic models for astrophysical winds and jets, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society].

== Education and Academic Career ==
Tsinganos was born and completed his early education in Filiatra, Messinia, Greece (1951). After a BSc in physics from the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki (Department of Physics, 1974), moved to the USA to further his studies, obtaining a MSc (1976) and a PhD (1980) in physics from the University of Chicago, wherein his doctoral thesis was supervised by the renowned astrophysicist Eugene N. Parker. Research associate at Chicago's Enrico Fermi Institute (1980–1981) and the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics (1981–1984), Lecturer at Harvard University (Department of Physics,1983–1984), Professor of Physics at the University of Crete and researcher at the Foundation for Research & Technology – Hellas (1984). In 2001 he was appointed professor of astrophysics at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens by the honorary appointment of invitation. His visiting professor appointments include world-renowned institutions such as the University of Turin (1991), the Paris Observatory and the University of Paris VII (1992), the University of St Andrews (1992), the University of Porto (1994) and the KU Leuven (1996).

== Scientific Contributions ==
Tsinganos's research has focused on plasma astrophysics and magnetohydrodynamics (MHD). Indicative multi-part series of scientific papers are (i) “Sunspots and the physics of magnetic flux tubes", by E.N. Parker and K. Tsinganos [ref: Bernoulli forces on an elliptical cylinder by a nonuniform flow, Physics of Fluids] [ref: Sunspots and the physics of magnetic flux tubes. IV. Aerodynamic lift on a thin cylinder in convective flows., Astrophysical Journal] [ref: Sunspots and the physics of magnetic flux tubes. X - On the hydrodynamic instability of buoyant fields, Astrophysical Journa] (ii) "MHD equilibrium" by K. Tsinganos, for obtaining exact solutions of the full set of the MHD equations under the assumption of one-ignorable coordinate in a system of general curvilinear coordinates [ref: Magnetohydrodynamic equilibrium. I. Exact solutions of the equations, Astrophysical Journal] [ref: Magnetohydrodynamic equilibrium. II. General integrals of the equations with one ignorable coordinate, Astrophysical Journal], (iii) "Nonradial and nonpolytropic astrophysical outflows", 10 papers focused on obtaining exact solutions of the MHD equations appropriate for cosmic winds and jets under the assumptions of radial or meridional selfsimilarity, developed by K. Tsinganos and collaborators, including C. Sauty, E. Trussoni, N. Vlahakis, and others [ref: Analytical studies of collimated winds. I. Topologies of 2-D helicoidal hydrodynamic solutions, Astronomy and Astrophysics] [ref: An analytical MHD wind model with latitudinal dependences obtained using separation of the variables, Astronomy and Astrophysics] [ref: Nonradial and nonpolytropic astrophysical outflows. IV. Magnetic or thermal collimation of winds into jets?, Astronomy and Astrophysics]. This study includes, as special cases, known polytropic models, such as the Parker description of a solar/stellar wind and the Blandford & Payne description of a magnetorotational disk wind. Among the results is an energy integral and criterion distinguishing the formation of collimated jets from uncollimated winds (TS94) and how protostellar jets play the role of the ex machina Deus by intervening in collapsing protostellar disks to give birth to stars, inside dark nebulae. (iv) MHD simulations for the magnetic collimation of the solar and stellar winds by S. Bogovalov, K.Tsinganos, T. Matsakos, A. Mignone and others. [ref: Magnetic collimation of the solar and stellar winds, Astronomy and Astrophysics] [ref: Magnetic collimation of relativistic outflows in jets with a high mass flux, Monthly Notice of the Royal Astronomical Society] [ref: Shock formation at the magnetic collimation of relativistic jets, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society] [ref: Two-component jet simulations. II. Combining analytical disk and stellar MHD outflow solutions, Astronomy and Astrophysics] Also, jets have been studied in the solar atmosphere and high resolution observations linking small-scale solar wind properties to coronal source regions using Parker Solar Probe and Solar Orbiter data. Tsinganos has contributed to the first very high resolution observations at the cradle of the slow solar wind, the interaction of solar jets with coronal plumes, erupting prominences and coronal mass ejections, in his capacity as a Greek PI in the ASPIICS coronagraph on ESA's Proba-3 mission, launched on 5 December 2024, [ref: The ASPIICS solar coronagraph aboard the Proba-3 formation flying mission. Scientific objectives and instrument design, Astronomy and Astrophysics] and a member of the mission's Science Working Team since 2009.

== National Observatory of Athens ==
During his term as director of the National Observatory of Athens (NOA), Tsinganos coordinated several major ESA grants to NOA, such as the [https://catalogs.mast.stsci.edu/hsc/ Hubble Source Catalogue of Variables] [ref: The Hubble Catalog of Variables (HCV), Astronomy & Astrophysics] (2015–2017) and the lunar-impact monitoring project NELIOTA. [ref: NELIOTA: The wide-field, high-cadence lunar monitoring system at the prime focus of the Kryoneri telescope, Astronomy & Astrophysics]

== Academic Community Service & Professional Recognition ==
Tsinganos was a founding member, secretary (2002–2006) and president (2006–2010) of the Hellenic Astronomical Society, was Greece's national representative to ESA's Science Programme Committee (2005-2010), a member of the [https://gsri.gov.gr/en/esetek-english/ National Advisory Council for Research and Technology] (2005–2010), [https://iauoutreach.org/nocs-network/europe/greece Greek national outreach coordinator] for the International Astronomical Union's centenary in 2019, organizer of several major international conferences and editor of their proceedings, author of many physics, calculus and astronomy text books, translator of several textbooks to the Greek language, invited panel member of the European Research Council (ERC) on Universe studies, evaluator for many years of the [https://marie-sklodowska-curie-actions.ec.europa.eu/actions/postdoctoral-fellowships European Marie Sklodowska-Curie post doctoral fellowships] and proposals evaluated by the [https://www.esf.org/ European Science Foundation (ESF)], PI in in bilateral collaborations and several EU funded research grants and networks, such as [https://robrutten.nl/rrweb/rjr-pubs/2001ESASP.493..353R.pdf PLATON], [https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/5592 JETSET], [https://www.lsw.uni-heidelberg.de/projects/enigma/ ENIGMA]. Tsinganos taught undergraduate courses at Harvard University and undergraduate and graduate level courses to hundreds of students each year at the University of Crete and the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (1985 - 2026) and was PhD supervisor of the thesis of many graduate students with several of them holding academic positions in prestigious European Universities.

In 2018 a conference was organised at the Observatoire de Paris, Meudon with a single article devoted to Kanaris Tsinganos who promoted MHD astrophysics and was a key leader to the JETSET European network. The proceeding of this conference have been published by Springer. [ref: JET Simulations, Experiments, and Theory. Ten Years After JETSET. What Is Next?, Springer Cham]

== Selected publications ==

* A Century of Cosmic Discoveries: Heliophysics and Space Physics, Astrophysics and Cosmology, Springer Nature Switzerland
* Bernoulli forces on an elliptical cylinder by a nonuniform flow, Physics of Fluids
* On wind-type flows in astrophysical jets. I. The initial relativistic acceleration, The Astrophysical Journal
* Systematic construction of exact MHD models of astrophysical winds and jets, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
* Ubiquitous small-scale dynamics in the slow solar wind formation region observed by Proba-3/ASPIICS, The Astrophysical Journal Letters
