data.title: Birpur Airport
data.text:
Birpur Airport (IATA: none, ICAO: none) is a proposed domestic airport located at Birpur in the state of Bihar, India. [ref: Town Survey Report: Bihar. Forbesganj, Controller of Publications] [ref: Indian Aviation] [ref: Sattā ke sūtradhara: Ājādī ke bāda Bhārata, Sr̥shṭi Prakāśana] The airport is located on the India–Nepal border, this airport is close to Bhantabari in Sunsari district of Nepal and Bhimnagar in Supaul district of India. [ref: Why is India building an airport in Birpur near Nepal’s border?, Khabarhub] This airport will be built on a former Kosi project era airfield in Birpur, about from Supaul. [ref: A Tale of Two Countries – Kosi – Surakshit Sansar, Surakshit Sanar] This airport is planned as a new regional airport under the UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik) scheme to enhance air connectivity and promote regional development. [ref: Bihar To Get Airports And Heliports In Every District; CM Samrat Choudhary Highlights The Infrastructure Push In Legislative Assembly, ETV Bharat News] [ref: Regional air connectivity boost for Bihar, The Times of India] The Government of Bihar and the Airports Authority of India signed a Memorandum of Understanding for the construction of the airport in June 2025. [ref: AAI floats tender to upgrade Birpur airport for small aircraft operations, Hindustan Times]

== History ==
The former airfield was built during the 1950s-1960s to support the construction of Koshi Barrage. [ref: Birpur Airport Moves Closer to Take-Off with ₹28.42-Crore Runway Project, Drishti IAS] [ref: A Life for Water: A Memoir, Transactions, American Philosophical Society (Vol. 108, Part 4), University of Pennsylvania Press] The then Indian prime minister, Indira Gandhi landed on this airfield on January 3, 1975 to attend the last rites of Lalit Narayan Mishra, which was held in Baluwa village. [ref: Killing of Cabinet Minister Shocks India's Politicians, The New York Times]

== Development ==
The Airports Authority of India (AAI) issued a tender in March 2025 for the construction of a terminal building, air traffic control, fire stations, and other buildings. [ref: AAI accelerates Birpur Airport project with new tender for infra development, The Times of India] For the expansion of the runway, the Government of Bihar published a land acquisition notice on January 2, 2026. [ref: Notice regarding land acquisition for the development work of Birpur Airport] The initial plan was to upgrade the airport runway as a 2B category, which supports 19 seaters aircraft but recently the officials are planning to upgrade the runway for 70 seaters aircraft. [ref: सुपौल: वीरपुर में जल्द शुरू होगी 70 सीटर विमान सेवा, रेल परियोजना की सर्वे रिपोर्ट का इंतजार - supaul birpur airport to get 70 seater flights rail project awaits report, Jagran]

data.title: Sahand Airlines
data.text:
Sahand Airlines is an Iranian Airline. [ref: Sahand Air]

== History ==
Founded in 2009 it is unclear exactly when they commenced operations though it is known in May of 2011, the Khorasan newspaper reported the explosion of an engine on a Boeing aircraft belonging to Sahand Airlines, which managed to make an emergency landing without any casualties. The aircraft in actuality was a McDonnel Douglas MD 82 operated by Khors Air on behalf of Sahand Airlines. [ref: Incident: Khors MD83 at Tehran on May 16th 2011, engine shut down in flight] The airline then in August of 2011 was added to the list of companies acting contrary to the foreign policy interests of the United States along with 14 other companies. [ref: Addition of Persons Acting Contrary to the National Security or Foreign Policy Interests of the United States to the Entity List; and Implementation of Additional Changes From the Annual Review of the Entity List] [ref: BIS Adds 9 Companies, 6 Individuals to Entity List]
[[File:Taban Air 1.jpg|thumb|The Sahand MD 80 now with Taban Air]]
After that, in 2017, Engineer Ashkan Ahmadi became the CEO and Deputy Chairman of the Board of Directors of the company and succeeded in activating two of the company's aircraft. [ref: Sahand Airlines history] In 2017 the airline added it's MD 83 fleet. [ref: Sahand Asia Airlines adds MD 83s] In 2018 the airline started domestic operations. [ref: Sahand Airlines start domestic operations] On October 18 2019 a Sahand Airlines MD 82 was seized as ordered by a Tehran court. [ref: Tehran Court orders seizure of MD 82] The court called off the seizure later the same year. [ref: Court calls off auction of Sahand Air Jet] Another aircraft was sold to Taban Air while one is owned by Sahand. There was also rumors that the Tehran court that seized the MD 80 also ordered the cessation of operations of Sahand Air. data.title: Seth Josel
data.text:
Seth Josel (born 1961) is an American guitarist, electric guitarist, banjoist, educator, and writer specializing in contemporary classical and experimental music. He is known for his performances of contemporary repertoire and for collaborations with composers including Helmut Lachenmann, Mauricio Kagel, Tristan Murail, Louis Andriessen, Gavin Bryars, and James Tenney. He has participated in the premieres of more than one hundred works and has appeared as a soloist and ensemble musician throughout Europe, North America, and Japan. [ref: Biography, Seth Josel Obicial Website]

== Early life and education ==
Josel was born in New York City in 1961. [ref: Seth Josel, Cybele Records] He studied at the Manhattan School of Music, earning a Bachelor of Music degree, and subsequently attended Yale University, where he received Master of Music, Master of Musical Arts, and Doctor of Musical Arts degrees. His principal teachers included Manuel Barrueco and Eliot Fisk. [ref: Seth Josel, Orpheus Institute]

== Career ==
Beginning in the 1980s, Josel established an international career as a performer of contemporary music. From 1991 until 2000, he was a permanent member of Ensemble Musikfabrik (then musikFabrik NRW). [ref: Biography, Seth Josel Obicial Website]

As a soloist and ensemble musician, Josel has performed with the New York Philharmonic, BBC Symphony Orchestra, Berliner Philharmoniker, Rundfunk- Sinfonieorchester Berlin, American Composers Orchestra, and numerous contemporary music ensembles. [ref: Biography, Seth Josel Obicial Website] [ref: Seth Josel, Orpheus Institute]

His festival appearances have included the Salzburg Festival, Donaueschinger Musiktage, Holland Festival, Munich Biennale, Huddersfield Contemporary Music Festival, MaerzMusik, and musikprotokoll Graz. [ref: Biography, Seth Josel Obicial Website] [ref: Seth Josel, Orpheus Institute]

Josel has collaborated closely with composers including Peter Ablinger, Richard Barrett, Gavin Bryars, Mauricio Kagel, Helmut Lachenmann, Olga Neuwirth, Sarah Nemtsov, Tristan Murail, Ming Tsao, and James Tenney. [ref: Biography, Seth Josel Obicial Website]

In addition to his performing activities, Josel has given lectures and masterclasses at institutions including Yale University, Northwestern University, California Institute of the Arts, the Universität der Künste Berlin, and the Musik-Akademie Basel. [ref: Biography, Seth Josel Obicial Website] In 2022, he joined the Hochschule für Musik Carl Maria von Weber Dresden as a lecturer in guitar. [ref: Biography, Seth Josel Obicial Website] He is also a co-founder of Sheer Pluck, an online database and research resource devoted to contemporary guitar repertoire. [ref: Seth Josel, Orpheus Institute]

== Discography ==

Records, 2006)

data.title: Kanaris Tsinganos
data.text:
----

Kanaris C. Tsinganos (Greek: Κανάρης Τσίγκανος) is a theoretical astrophysicist, professor emeritus at the Department of Physics of the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens, [ref: Emeritus Professors, siteA-EN] elected director of the National Observatory of Athens. [ref: Prof. Tsinganos Kanaris – Former Director of the National Observatory of Athens (2011–2016), National Observatory of Athens] As the first national representative of Greece to ESA (Science Programm Committee, ESA/SPC), led his scientific team to become the first Greek group to participate to an ESA science space misssion (Proba 3). Tsinganos's contributions in refereed journals [ref: Google Scholar, scholar.google.com] are on MHD phenomena at the solar atmosphere, solar wind, stellar winds and astrophysical jets. He is known for the Sauty-Tsinganos criterion [ref: Nonradial and nonpolytropic astrophysical outflows. IV The transition from jets to winds, Astronomy and Astrophysics] for the transition of a stellar wind to a selfsimilar jet and the Vlahakis-Tsinganos systematic construction of exact selfsimilar MHD solutions for astrophysical winds and jets [ref: Systematic construction of exact magnetohydrodynamic models for astrophysical winds and jets, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society].

== Education and Academic Career ==
Tsinganos was born and completed his early education in Filiatra, Messinia, Greece (1951). After a BSc in physics from the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki (Department of Physics, 1974), moved to the USA to further his studies, obtaining a MSc (1976) and a PhD (1980) in physics from the University of Chicago, wherein his doctoral thesis was supervised by the renowned astrophysicist Eugene N. Parker. Research associate at Chicago's Enrico Fermi Institute (1980–1981) and the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics (1981–1984), Lecturer at Harvard University (Department of Physics,1983–1984), Professor of Physics at the University of Crete and researcher at the Foundation for Research & Technology – Hellas (1984). In 2001 he was appointed professor of astrophysics at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens by the honorary appointment of invitation. His visiting professor appointments include world-renowned institutions such as the University of Turin (1991), the Paris Observatory and the University of Paris VII (1992), the University of St Andrews (1992), the University of Porto (1994) and the KU Leuven (1996).

== Scientific Contributions ==
Tsinganos's research has focused on plasma astrophysics and magnetohydrodynamics (MHD). Indicative multi-part series of scientific papers are (i) “Sunspots and the physics of magnetic flux tubes", by E.N. Parker and K. Tsinganos [ref: Bernoulli forces on an elliptical cylinder by a nonuniform flow, Physics of Fluids] [ref: Sunspots and the physics of magnetic flux tubes. IV. Aerodynamic lift on a thin cylinder in convective flows., Astrophysical Journal] [ref: Sunspots and the physics of magnetic flux tubes. X - On the hydrodynamic instability of buoyant fields, Astrophysical Journa] (ii) "MHD equilibrium" by K. Tsinganos, for obtaining exact solutions of the full set of the MHD equations under the assumption of one-ignorable coordinate in a system of general curvilinear coordinates [ref: Magnetohydrodynamic equilibrium. I. Exact solutions of the equations, Astrophysical Journal] [ref: Magnetohydrodynamic equilibrium. II. General integrals of the equations with one ignorable coordinate, Astrophysical Journal], (iii) "Nonradial and nonpolytropic astrophysical outflows", 10 papers focused on obtaining exact solutions of the MHD equations appropriate for cosmic winds and jets under the assumptions of radial or meridional selfsimilarity, developed by K. Tsinganos and collaborators, including C. Sauty, E. Trussoni, N. Vlahakis, and others [ref: Analytical studies of collimated winds. I. Topologies of 2-D helicoidal hydrodynamic solutions, Astronomy and Astrophysics] [ref: An analytical MHD wind model with latitudinal dependences obtained using separation of the variables, Astronomy and Astrophysics] [ref: Nonradial and nonpolytropic astrophysical outflows. IV. Magnetic or thermal collimation of winds into jets?, Astronomy and Astrophysics]. This study includes, as special cases, known polytropic models, such as the Parker description of a solar/stellar wind and the Blandford & Payne description of a magnetorotational disk wind. Among the results is an energy integral and criterion distinguishing the formation of collimated jets from uncollimated winds (TS94) and how protostellar jets play the role of the ex machina Deus by intervening in collapsing protostellar disks to give birth to stars, inside dark nebulae. (iv) MHD simulations for the magnetic collimation of the solar and stellar winds by S. Bogovalov, K.Tsinganos, T. Matsakos, A. Mignone and others. [ref: Magnetic collimation of the solar and stellar winds, Astronomy and Astrophysics] [ref: Magnetic collimation of relativistic outflows in jets with a high mass flux, Monthly Notice of the Royal Astronomical Society] [ref: Shock formation at the magnetic collimation of relativistic jets, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society] [ref: Two-component jet simulations. II. Combining analytical disk and stellar MHD outflow solutions, Astronomy and Astrophysics] Also, jets have been studied in the solar atmosphere and high resolution observations linking small-scale solar wind properties to coronal source regions using Parker Solar Probe and Solar Orbiter data. Tsinganos has contributed to the first very high resolution observations at the cradle of the slow solar wind, the interaction of solar jets with coronal plumes, erupting prominences and coronal mass ejections, in his capacity as a Greek PI in the ASPIICS coronagraph on ESA's Proba-3 mission, launched on 5 December 2024, [ref: The ASPIICS solar coronagraph aboard the Proba-3 formation flying mission. Scientific objectives and instrument design, Astronomy and Astrophysics] and a member of the mission's Science Working Team since 2009.

== National Observatory of Athens ==
During his term as director of the National Observatory of Athens (NOA), Tsinganos coordinated several major ESA grants to NOA, such as the [https://catalogs.mast.stsci.edu/hsc/ Hubble Source Catalogue of Variables] [ref: The Hubble Catalog of Variables (HCV), Astronomy & Astrophysics] (2015–2017) and the lunar-impact monitoring project NELIOTA. [ref: NELIOTA: The wide-field, high-cadence lunar monitoring system at the prime focus of the Kryoneri telescope, Astronomy & Astrophysics]

== Academic Community Service & Professional Recognition ==
Tsinganos was a founding member, secretary (2002–2006) and president (2006–2010) of the Hellenic Astronomical Society, was Greece's national representative to ESA's Science Programme Committee (2005-2010), a member of the [https://gsri.gov.gr/en/esetek-english/ National Advisory Council for Research and Technology] (2005–2010), [https://iauoutreach.org/nocs-network/europe/greece Greek national outreach coordinator] for the International Astronomical Union's centenary in 2019, organizer of several major international conferences and editor of their proceedings, author of many physics, calculus and astronomy text books, translator of several textbooks to the Greek language, invited panel member of the European Research Council (ERC) on Universe studies, evaluator for many years of the [https://marie-sklodowska-curie-actions.ec.europa.eu/actions/postdoctoral-fellowships European Marie Sklodowska-Curie post doctoral fellowships] and proposals evaluated by the [https://www.esf.org/ European Science Foundation (ESF)], PI in in bilateral collaborations and several EU funded research grants and networks, such as [https://robrutten.nl/rrweb/rjr-pubs/2001ESASP.493..353R.pdf PLATON], [https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/5592 JETSET], [https://www.lsw.uni-heidelberg.de/projects/enigma/ ENIGMA]. Tsinganos taught undergraduate courses at Harvard University and undergraduate and graduate level courses to hundreds of students each year at the University of Crete and the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (1985 - 2026) and was PhD supervisor of the thesis of many graduate students with several of them holding academic positions in prestigious European Universities.

In 2018 a conference was organised at the Observatoire de Paris, Meudon with a single article devoted to Kanaris Tsinganos who promoted MHD astrophysics and was a key leader to the JETSET European network. The proceeding of this conference have been published by Springer. [ref: JET Simulations, Experiments, and Theory. Ten Years After JETSET. What Is Next?, Springer Cham]

== Selected publications ==

* A Century of Cosmic Discoveries: Heliophysics and Space Physics, Astrophysics and Cosmology, Springer Nature Switzerland
* Bernoulli forces on an elliptical cylinder by a nonuniform flow, Physics of Fluids
* On wind-type flows in astrophysical jets. I. The initial relativistic acceleration, The Astrophysical Journal
* Systematic construction of exact MHD models of astrophysical winds and jets, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
* Ubiquitous small-scale dynamics in the slow solar wind formation region observed by Proba-3/ASPIICS, The Astrophysical Journal Letters

== References ==

== External links ==
* [http://users.uoa.gr/~tsingan/CV.pdf Curriculum vitae], National and Kapodistrian University of Athens

data.title: Silas Kanyabigega
data.text:
Silas Kanyabigega (born 10 May 1958) is a Rwandan-born American Christian minister, theologian, author and religious educator. His activities have included Christian evangelism, theological education, religious broadcasting and community development in Rwanda and the United States. [ref: Learn More About Dr. Silas Kanyabigega: A Pastor in the Methodist Church based in the United States, Ukweli Times] Kanyabigega has been associated with International Movement for Christ (IMC), International Movement for Christ Theological Seminary (IMCTS) and Mouvement pour Christ au Rwanda (MPCR). He earned a Doctor of Ministry degree from Unification Theological Seminary in 2018. He pursued a PhD in educational and organizational leadership at National University￼ and enrolled in a Doctor of Philosophy program in Educational Leadership at Liberty University in 2026. His theological writings concern Christian faith, salvation, redemption, charismatic manifestations and the history of Christianity in Rwanda.

== Early life and background ==
Kanyabigega was born in Rwanda and later relocated to the United States, where he continued his involvement in Christian ministry, theological education and religious publishing.

His religious activities have involved Christian communities in Rwanda, the United States and the African Great Lakes region.

== Education ==

=== Doctor of Ministry — Unification Theological Seminary ===
Kanyabigega earned a Doctor of Ministry (D.Min.) from Unification Theological Seminary in Barrytown, New York, on 26 May 2018.

His doctoral education included spiritual formation, theological and ethical perspectives on ministerial leadership, transformational leadership, religious education, family ministry, social justice and research methodology.

His academic program included doctoral research and dissertation work in family and educational ministry. His academic transcript records 34 completed credits and a cumulative grade point average of 3.56.

=== PhD Doctoral studies — National University ===
Between 2022 and 2026, Kanyabigega successively completed all coursework for a Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Educational and Organizational Leadership at National University in California.

His studies included educational leadership theories, diversity and social justice, educational policy, educational administration, finance and budgeting, research methodology, statistical analysis, qualitative research and dissertation preparation.

His academic record includes a doctoral comprehensive assessment and dissertation proposal coursework.

A transcript issued on 28 September 2026 records 54 earned doctoral credits and a cumulative grade point average of 3.51.

=== Ph.D. studies — Liberty University ===
In 2026, Kanyabigega enrolled in the Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Educational Leadership program at Liberty University in Lynchburg, Virginia.

His continuing studies concern educational leadership, educational research, organizational development and the relationship between leadership practices and educational outcomes.

== Christian ministry and organizational leadership ==

=== Movement for Christ in Rwanda ===
Kanyabigega has been involved in Christian evangelism and religious education in Rwanda.

A ministerial order published in Rwanda's Official Gazette on 5 April 2010 identified Kanyabigega as the authorized legal representative of Mouvement pour Christ au Rwanda (MPCR), with Eraste Ndayisenga as deputy legal representative. [ref: Official Gazette No. 14 of 5 April 2010, Republic of Rwanda]

The organization has been associated with Christian evangelism, biblical teaching and community-oriented ministry.

=== International Movement for Christ ===
Kanyabigega has been associated with International Movement for Christ (IMC), a Christian ministry organization involved in evangelism, theological education and religious outreach.

The organization's activities have included Christian teaching, leadership development, religious communication and proposed community development initiatives in Rwanda and other parts of the African Great Lakes region.

=== International Movement for Christ Theological Seminary ===
Kanyabigega has been associated with International Movement for Christ Theological Seminary (IMCTS), an organization providing theological instruction and Christian ministerial training.

Its educational activities have focused on biblical studies, theology, pastoral ministry, Christian leadership and the preparation of religious workers.

=== Ministry in the United States ===
Kanyabigega has been associated with the Free Methodist Church tradition in the United States.

A January 2025 profile published by Ukweli Times discussed his Christian ministry and evangelistic activities, including work connected with presentations of the Jesus Film in Rwanda.

His ministry activities have included preaching, biblical instruction, pastoral leadership and Christian education.

== Christian broadcasting and media ==
Kanyabigega has participated in Christian media initiatives intended to provide religious teaching to audiences in Rwanda and internationally.

These initiatives include Kwizera Yesu TV, a Christian video broadcasting project, and Radio Kwizera, an online Christian radio service.

Their programming has included biblical teaching, Christian preaching, worship, evangelism and religious education.

== Theological research and teaching ==
Kanyabigega's theological interests include Christian salvation, redemption, biblical interpretation, charismatic practices, ecclesiology and the history of Christianity in Rwanda.

His writings have examined Christian faith and salvation, the theological significance of Jesus Christ and the interpretation of spiritual gifts within Christian churches.

=== Pastoral leadership and family life ===
In January 2025, the Rwandan publication Paradise published an article discussing Kanyabigega's views on parenting challenges among pastors. [ref: Parenting Challenges Among Pastors: Insights from Dr. Silas Kanyabigega, Paradise]

The article addressed difficulties experienced by clergy in balancing pastoral responsibilities with family obligations.

Kanyabigega emphasized family relationships, appropriate boundaries, parental responsibilities and congregational support for ministers.

=== Christianity and charismatic manifestations in Rwanda ===
Kanyabigega has written about charismatic manifestations in Rwandan churches, examining theological interpretations of spiritual gifts and their relationship to Christian worship and church practice.

His research interests include the historical development of Protestant Christianity in Rwanda and the relationship between biblical teaching and contemporary religious practices.

== Publications ==
Kanyabigega's reported theological publications include works on Christian faith, salvation, redemption, church history and pastoral ministry.

The following bibliography requires verification against publisher or library catalog records.

=== Selected books ===

* Faith and Salvation in Christ: A Comparative Theological Analysis of Redemption (2012; new edition 2026). ISBN 9798256010379.
* True Faith: A Theological Study of True Faith, Redemption, Salvation, and the Centrality of Jesus Christ (2026). ISBN 9798182789400.
* Charismatic Manifestations in the Churches of Rwanda: A Theological and Historical Study (2026). Hardcover ISBN 9798182805834; eBook ISBN 9798182805858.
* Kwizera Yesu Kristo.
* La Prédication Centrée sur Christ.
* Les Charismes Spirituels à la Lumière du Nouveau Testament: Cas des Églises au Rwanda.
* Amateka y'u Rwanda mu Iyobokamana.
* A Faith-Centered Life.

=== Themes of selected works ===
Faith and Salvation in Christ examines Christian teachings concerning faith, salvation, redemption and the theological significance of Jesus Christ.

True Faith explores biblical and theological understandings of faith, redemption and salvation, emphasizing the centrality of Jesus Christ.

Charismatic Manifestations in the Churches of Rwanda examines charismatic practices within Rwandan Christian communities from theological and historical perspectives.

== Community development and humanitarian initiatives ==
Through Movement for Christ in Rwanda and International Movement for Christ, Kanyabigega has been involved in developing proposals for community empowerment and economic development.

These proposals have included vocational training, agricultural development, entrepreneurship, cooperatives, community empowerment and technology-based education.

=== SDATCEP ===
The proposed Sustainable Development, Agriculture, Training, Cooperatives and Entrepreneurship Project (SDATCEP) has been described in organizational planning materials as a multiyear initiative intended to support economic and social development in Rwanda.

=== RNAITI ===
The proposed Rwanda National Artificial Intelligence and Technology Initiative (RNAITI) has focused on potential applications of artificial intelligence, digital education and technological development in Rwanda.

Independent documentation of the implementation, funding and outcomes of these initiatives is needed.

data.title: Center3
data.text:
center3 is a Saudi Arabian digital infrastructure company and a subsidiary of stc Group. Its activities include data centers, submarine cables, international points of presence and Internet exchange points. [ref: Telecompaper, www.telecompaper.com]

== History ==

center3 was launched in October 2022. At the time, Bloomberg reported plans to invest approximately US$1 billion through the company over five years, following an initial US$1 billion investment in data centers and submarine cables. [ref: Telecompaper, www.telecompaper.com]

In December 2023, center3 entered into a definitive agreement to acquire CMC Networks from the Carlyle Sub-Saharan Africa Fund. CMC Networks provided network services across Africa and the Middle East. The financial terms of the agreement were not disclosed. [ref: Data center industry news, analysis, and opinion - DCD, www.datacenterdynamics.com]

In June 2024, center3 announced completion of the acquisition of 100% of CMC Networks Mauritius and 49% of CMC Networks South Africa. At the time, CMC Networks operated across more than 110 service locations, serving 51 African countries and 12 countries in the Middle East. [ref: center3 Completes Acquisition of CMC Networks - Telecom Review Middle East]

== Operations ==
=== Data centers ===
center3 operates data centers in Saudi Arabia. In July 2023, the company announced an additional 9.6 megawatts of capacity at its Khurais facility in Riyadh. [ref: STC's Center3 expands Riyadh data center in Saudi Arabia, www.datacenterdynamics.com]

Its facilities host cloud infrastructure, including Saudi Arabian cloud regions operated by Oracle and Huawei. Oracle's Riyadh cloud region, hosted in a center3 data center, opened in August 2024. In February 2025, Zoom deployed its first Saudi Arabian node through a partnership with center3. [ref: Saudi's center3 targets 1GW of data center capacity by 2030, www.datacenterdynamics.com]

In December 2025, a memorandum of understanding with HUMAIN was announced through center3 for a proposed joint venture to develop and operate data centers for artificial intelligence workloads in Saudi Arabia. [ref: Saudi Telecom Company signs MoU with Humain to develop 1GW of data center capacity, www.datacenterdynamics.com]

=== Submarine cables ===

center3 participates in the 2Africa submarine cable project. In January 2023, the company and its parent group landed the cable in Jeddah and Yanbu, Saudi Arabia. [ref: STC to land 2Africa cable in Bahrain, follows Saudi landings in Jeddah and Yanbu, www.datacenterdynamics.com]

=== Internet exchanges ===

center3's Internet exchanges are located in Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam. The exchanges are interconnected through center3's one-IX platform, allowing participating networks to access the three exchanges through a single connection.

data.title: Millard L. House II
data.text:
----

Millard House II is an American educator and school administrator who has served as superintendent of the Houston Independent School District in Texas and Prince George's County Public Schools in Maryland. He previously served as director of schools for the Clarksville-Montgomery County School System in Tennessee, chief operating officer of Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools in North Carolina, and deputy superintendent of Tulsa Public Schools in Oklahoma.

== Early life and education ==

House is a native of Tulsa, Oklahoma, and grew up in a family of educators. His father, Millard House Sr., was a Tulsa Public Schools administrator, while his mother worked as a teacher and school counselor. [ref: He's firm, fair and unflappable, colleagues say. Can Millard House conquer Houston ISD?, Houston Chronicle]

House attended Booker T. Washington High School in Tulsa.

He graduated from the University of Montevallo in Alabama in 1995. He later earned a master's degree in school administration from Northeastern State University in Oklahoma and completed the Fisher School Leadership Program at the Haas School of Business at the University of California, Berkeley.

== Career ==

=== Tulsa ===

After graduating from college, House returned to Tulsa and began his education career as a physical education teacher.

After working as a teacher and assistant principal, House became principal of Anderson Elementary School in Tulsa. He later became the founding principal of KIPP Tulsa College Preparatory, a middle school developed through a partnership between Tulsa Public Schools and the Knowledge Is Power Program.

House subsequently moved into the central administration of Tulsa Public Schools, eventually serving as deputy superintendent.

=== Charlotte and Clarksville-Montgomery County ===

In 2012, House joined Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools in North Carolina as chief operating officer. His responsibilities included district operations such as facilities, transportation and security. [ref: Houston ISD trustees name Tennessee educator Millard House II as lone superintendent finalist, Houston Chronicle]

After leaving Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools, House worked in education leadership development and consulting.

In 2017, House became director of schools for the Clarksville-Montgomery County School System in Tennessee. He led the district until 2021, when he was selected to lead Houston ISD.

=== Houston Independent School District ===

In May 2021, the Houston Independent School District Board of Education selected House as its lone finalist for superintendent. The board formally approved his appointment in June 2021, and he began serving as superintendent on July 1, 2021. [ref: Houston ISD trustees make it official, approve Millard House II as new superintendent, Houston Chronicle]

At the time, HISD enrolled approximately 200,000 students and was the largest school district in Texas. [ref: It's Day 1 for Millard House II, Houston ISD's new superintendent. Plenty of challenges await., Houston Chronicle]

In 2022, House presented a five-year strategic plan addressing areas including equitable access to school resources, teacher compensation, early childhood education, special education services and family engagement. [ref: Houston ISD's equity-based strategic plan calls for teacher raises, librarians at all campuses, Houston Chronicle]

During House's tenure, the number of HISD campuses receiving D or F state accountability ratings declined substantially. [ref: What we know about HISD Superintendent Millard House II now that the TEA has taken over the district, Houston Chronicle]

House's tenure coincided with a long-running dispute over a proposed state takeover of HISD. In March 2023, the Texas Education Agency announced that it would replace the district's elected board with a state-appointed board of managers and appoint a new superintendent.

House left HISD in June 2023 when the state intervention took effect.

=== Prince George's County Public Schools ===

In June 2023, Prince George's County Executive Angela Alsobrooks selected House to lead Prince George's County Public Schools in Maryland. [ref: Prince George's names former Houston superintendent as schools leader, The Washington Post]

House began serving as superintendent on July 1, 2023.

House and the Prince George's County Board of Education reached a mutual separation agreement in June 2025. [ref: Prince George's Schools superintendent stepping down, interim is named, The Washington Post]

His departure followed disputes involving district leadership and a no-confidence vote conducted by the county teachers union.

=== Region 4 Education Service Center ===

In 2026, House joined Region 4 Education Service Center in Houston as Director of Strategic Initiatives Services. [ref: Staff Directory, Region 4 Education Service Center]

data.title: Vibin Baskar
data.text:
Vibin Baskar is an Indian music composer, music producer, and independent artist who works primarily in the Tamil and Kannada film industries. He is known for composing music for the Tamil ZEE5 original web series Sattamum Neethiyum (2025), Veduvan(2025), Thadayam(2026), Kaakee Circus(2026) and Sattamum Neethiyum 2 (2026) for which he created both the songs and the background score. He has also composed music for Tamil and Kannada feature films. He has released several independent Tamil songs.

== Early life and Education ==
Vibin Baskar is based in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. He completed a Bachelor of Business Administration from Alagappa University before earning a Master of Business Administration from the same institution in 2014. His interest in music began during childhood after being enrolled in piano classes by his mother. He later pursued formal training in western music from Trinity College London in Piano and Music Theory. He completed his Bachelor's degree in Audio Engineering and Recording Arts from the School of Audio Engineering. During this period, he also performed as a keyboardist in live shows across Chennai.

== Career ==
Vibin Baskar began his professional career in 2012 as an Audio Engineer, Chennai. In 2013, he became Assistant Music Director and worked with composer James Vasanthan, contributing to music production and programming. From 2017 onward, he started composing music independently for South Indian films, television productions and OTT platforms.

=== Film and Television ===
Sattamum Neethiyum 2 (2026)

Kaakee Circus (2026)

Thadayam (2026)

Veduvan (2025)

Sattamum Neethiyum (2025)

Vibin Baskar composed the songs and original background score for the Tamil court room drama web series Sattamum Neethiyum 1& 2, released on ZEE5 in 2025 and 2026. The series received positive reviews, with several critics highlighting vibin's music as one of its major strengths.

== Samharini ==
Vibin Baskar composed the music for the Kannada-language feature film Samharini, where he was credited as Vibin Baskar (V2).

== Independent Music ==
Alongside his work in films, Vibin is active in the Tamil independent music scene. He maintains the YouTube channel VibinBaskar, where he publishes original compositions, music videos, behind-the-scenes content and promotional material for his projects.

His independent works include:

* Chellame
* Hurrah
* Thanga Magale
* Vaazh Indre
* SuNaPaNa
* Kumari Ponney
* Nanba
* Thanimai
* Mutham
* Thalattu
* Porkaalai Pozhuthinile

== Reception ==
Vibin Baskar's work on Sattamum Neethiyum received positive critical attention. Reviews published by Cinema Murasam, Angusam, and Hindu Tamil Thisai praised his background score for enhancing the emotional depth of the narrative and supporting the performances. Critics particularly highlighted the courtroom sequences and climax episode for their effective musical treatment. Although one review considered the series' title song stylistically inconsistent with the realistic tone of the drama, the overall reception to the soundtrack and score was positive.

data.title: Inclusive Books for Children
data.text:
----

== [user] ==
[user] (IBC) is a British website providing reviews of children’s books with a focus on diversity and inclusion. It also organises the annual [user] Book Awards, and provides funding to other not-for-profit organisations that work to improve inclusion in children’s books and access to these. The charity is registered in the United Kingdom under charity number 1201129. [ref: [user] - Charity 1201129, prd-ds-register-of-charities.charitycommission.gov.uk]

== History ==
The charity was founded in 2022 by Marcus and Sarah Satha following the couple’s experience of finding children’s books that reflected the multiracial composition of their family. [ref: Inclusive books: founder of Inclusive books Sarah Satha talks to Jake Hope, Pen & Inc]

Before establishing the charity, Marcus and Sarah Satha consulted a range of organisations and individuals involved in children’s literature, education and libraries. These included BookTrust, CILIP and the Centre for Literacy in Primary Education (CLPE).

The website's aim was to be a resource where families could locate reviews of children’s books and search for books that included different forms of representation and inclusion. The website was launched in September 2023 at the Centre for Literacy in Primary Education headquarters in London. [ref: Charity launches award and database to encourage diversity in children’s books, The Guardian]

The charity has subsequently undertaken advocacy and training with schools, libraries and literacy organisations to promote awareness and use of the website.

== Services ==

=== Review Website ===
The charity’s review process focuses on children’s books featuring human characters.  Books considered for review are primarily aimed at children aged between birth and nine years.  Fabia Turner, Head of Content for the organisation, described the review process in an interview with Pen & Inc Magazine in 2023 [ref: Pen&Inc10 Autumn/Winter 2023, content.yudu.com].

The charity states that it intends to expand the age range of books covered by its reviews when sufficient review capacity is available.

=== Book Awards ===
The [user] Book Awards were inaugurated in 2024 [ref: The Catchpoles, Sumana Seeboruth and Zanib Mian win inaugural £30k [user] Prize, The Bookseller]. The awards have three categories: books for babies and toddlers; picture books; and highly illustrated fiction.

Books are nominated by publishers annually and considered by the organisation before a longlist is produced.  A judging panel then selects a shortlist and an overall winner in each category. Category winners receive a shared of a £10,000 prize fund [ref: Winners of the inaugural [user] Book Awards – Books For Keeps, booksforkeeps.co.uk] [ref: New charity [user] launches inaugural awards worth £30,000, The Bookseller], divided between the author and illustrator of the winning book.

In 2026, the organisation piloted a shadowing scheme through which children and families could vote for their preferred winners [ref: ReadingZone, ReadingZone].

=== Book Box Scheme ===
[user] operates a book box scheme through which schools and community groups can apply for collections for 100 children’s books. The scheme is intended to support communities identified by the organisation as having a particular need for access to contemporary diverse and inclusive children’s books. [ref: IBC Book Box: free books for schools, [user]]

=== Small Grants ===
The charity provides annual grants to other not-for-profit organisations undertaking projects intended to improve inclusion in children’s books or access to such titles.

=== Research ===
The charity publishes an annual report examining representation in children’s literature focusing on the work of writers and illustrators from under-represented groups. Findings have been reported via the media outlets such as children's news programme Newsround. [ref: ReadingZone, ReadingZone] [ref: Book and diversity: New report calls for more representation in children's books, BBC Newsround] [ref: Excluded Voices report, [user]].

IBC are critical of the ‘own voices’ phrase with concerns about the use of the term as a broad category for literature by under-represented creators and about assumptions concerning the subjects that such creators should write about.

IBC reports also examine particular areas of representation and barriers experienced by writers and illustrators.

*

data.title: Zayd Portillo
data.text:
----

Zayd Portillo, professionally known as Creatrgod, is an American entrepreneur, producer, and technologist whose work spans music, gaming, interactive entertainment, and digital media. [ref: Timbaland Speaks on the Metaverse, and Where FN Meka Went Wrong, Complex] [ref: Timbaland launches AI music company Stage Zero, with first AI artist, TaTa, Music Business Worldwide]

He has developed interactive livestream formats, music discovery platforms, gaming experiences, and virtual entertainment projects, and has co-founded ventures involving emerging technologies and artificial intelligence. [ref: TimboLand Driving Game Demo]

Portillo is an advocate for expanding creators' access to monetization opportunities and developing technologies that enable independent creators to generate revenue from their work. [ref: The Truth About Streaming & Creator Control, iVoox]

He has collaborated extensively with record producer Timbaland on projects combining music, technology, and audience participation.

== Career ==

=== Music discovery and livestreaming ===

In 2021, Portillo developed The Beatbox, a web-based application for music submissions and reviews during Timbaland's livestream broadcasts. The application was used to present music submitted by artists and producers. [ref: A Royal Invitation from Timbo Da King, Twitch]

Portillo and Timbaland also co-created Timbo I-Do, a livestream music discovery and review program.

=== Light Energy Labs and TimboLand (2022–2023) ===

Portillo and Timbaland co-founded Light Energy Labs, a company involved in developing virtual entertainment projects.

In 2022, the pair developed Timbo.Land, an interactive virtual entertainment project incorporating music discovery and audience participation. The project included a virtual environment connected to the fictional musical character Congo.

A driving-game demonstration associated with TimboLand was also released. The project used Unreal Engine technology.

Light Energy Labs developed Congo, a virtual musical character based on Timbaland's Bored Ape Yacht Club avatar. Congo debuted in July 2022 with the single and music video "Has A Meaning".

Portillo directed the music video, which used computer-generated imagery and motion capture. Timbaland voiced Congo and performed the movements used to animate the character.

The project was discussed in a September 2022 interview with Complex, in which Portillo and Timbaland addressed virtual entertainment, digital characters, and music production in the metaverse.

=== CamUp (2026–present) ===

Portillo co-founded CamUp, a technology platform focused on livestream monetization and audience participation. Music Business Worldwide identified CamUp as a project developed by Light Energy Labs in June 2025.

The platform provides tools for creators to manage paid video interactions, audience submissions, and digital gifting during livestream broadcasts.

CamUp also supports interactive audience participation alongside broadcasts distributed through existing streaming platforms.

=== Artificial intelligence and music technology ===

In 2023, Portillo worked with Timbaland on projects involving artificial intelligence and music production. During this period, Timbaland demonstrated an AI-generated vocal performance resembling The Notorious B.I.G., prompting discussion about the use of artificial intelligence in recorded music. [ref: Timbaland Hatches AI Startup That Will Give Music Stars Like Biggie Life After Death, Forbes] [ref: Timbaland Doubles Down On AI In Music, 'It's Here To Stay', TMZ]

The demonstration also received coverage from BET and Black Enterprise. [ref: Timbaland AI Startup Backlash Over Notorious B.I.G., BET] [ref: Twitter Roasts Timbaland's AI Collab With Notorious B.I.G., Black Enterprise]

Portillo has served as an adviser to the AI music platform Suno, focusing on music AI integration.

=== Commercial music production ===

In July 2025, Portillo contributed to the music production of a Popeyes advertising campaign responding to the relaunch of McDonald's Snack Wrap.

The campaign featured an AI-assisted rap track produced using Suno. Director PJ Accetturo publicly credited Portillo and his team with creating the music, stating that the track was completed in one day. [ref: Post crediting Zayd Portillo on the Popeyes campaign, X]

Accetturo separately described the campaign's development and production timeline. [ref: Post discussing the Popeyes campaign, X]

The advertisement was published by Popeyes and received coverage from TMZ. [ref: Popeyes advertising video, X] [ref: Popeyes Disses McDonald's Snack Wraps With A.I.-Generated Rap Song, TMZ]

Portillo was also credited as a songwriter on "Glitch x Pulse", the debut single by AI-assisted musical artist TaTa Taktumi, released in October 2025. Rolling Stone identified Portillo, Alice Aera, Emily Haber, and Brandon Avila as the song's credited writers. [ref: Timbaland Puts His AI Music Has 'Pure Soul' Theory to the Test With Tata Taktumi Debut, Rolling Stone Australia]

=== Stage Zero Entertainment ===

In June 2025, Portillo co-founded Stage Zero Entertainment with Timbaland and film producer Rocky Mudaliar. The company develops entertainment projects involving artificial intelligence, including virtual musical artists. [ref: Timbaland Launches AI Entertainment Company, Pollstar]

The company's first announced musical artist was TaTa, an AI-assisted performer. Portillo and Timbaland discussed their approach to developing the artist in a 2025 Rolling Stone feature. [ref: Timbaland's New Artist Is Young, Photogenic — and Not Human, Rolling Stone] [ref: Timbaland launches AI entertainment company and first artist, MusicTech]

In August 2026, The New York Times published an article examining AI-generated entertainment personalities, including the development of virtual performers. [ref: So You Want to Build an A.I. Star?, The New York Times]

== Public speaking and media appearances ==

In March 2023, Portillo appeared alongside Timbaland at the Axios What's Next Summit, where they discussed artificial intelligence and the music industry. [ref: Timbaland plotting collaboration with an AI artist, Axios]

In December 2023, Portillo participated in a fireside conversation with Timbaland organized by Silicon Valley Bank during Miami Art Week. The event was titled "Creative Synergy: A Fireside Chat with Timbaland & Zayd Portillo". [ref: Creative Synergy: A Fireside Chat with Timbaland & Zayd Portillo, Silicon Valley Bank]

Portillo also appeared on the podcast So Ambitious in an episode discussing artificial intelligence, music, and opportunities for creators. [ref: The Future of Music Is AI: How Black Creators Can Win the Next Creative Era, Apple Podcasts]

== References ==

data.title: Arena Breakout: Infinite
data.text:
Arena Breakout: Infinite is a first-person tactical extraction shooter developed by MoreFun Studios for PC. The game is a PC evolution of the mobile shooter Arena Breakout; MoreFun studio head Hanjin “Enzo” Zhang said that the PC version had been in development for more than three years and was built from the original game. [ref: Arena Breakout: Infinite devs on building a military sim for all gamers, GamesBeat] It is set in the fictional war-torn region of Kamona, where players enter raids to search for supplies, fight human and AI-controlled opponents, and attempt to leave through extraction points. [ref: Arena Breakout: Infinite is a snack-sized Tarkov I can't stop playing, but has some awful monetisation, PC Gamer] [ref: Arena Breakout: Infinite Early Access Launches Today, GamesPress] [ref: Arena Breakout: Infinite Officially Launches on Steam & Epic, Delivering the Ultimate FPS Extraction Shooter Experience, GamesPress]

The game entered early access through its official website on 13 August 2024. [ref: How to get early access to Arena Breakout: Infinite, Shacknews] It was released on Steam and the Epic Games Store on 15 September 2025; Steam lists MoreFun Studios as both developer and publisher. [ref: Arena Breakout: Infinite, Steam]

== Development and release ==

In a May 2024 GamesBeat interview, Zhang described the studio's aim as offering an immersive military-simulation experience to both casual and hardcore players. He told GamesBeat that "the most enjoyable part of military simulation games is that it can provide an unparalleled level of immersion which other games cannot provide," and summarised Arena Breakout: Infinite's core loop as "gearing up, fighting and extraction." Zhang added that the studio wanted a title players could pick up in short sessions, describing the design intent as "easy come, easy play, easy go."

Following the closed beta of the overseas PC version in May 2024, Arena Breakout: Infinite reached the top-two position among Chinese-developed games on Steam's global wishlist chart, according to a September 2024 Gamescom feature by Chinese trade publication Jinghe. [ref: ]

MoreFun announced on 7 August 2024 that Arena Breakout: Infinite would enter early access through the official website on 13 August. The company said that the early-access period would be used to optimize performance, introduce features and refine gameplay systems. The early-access build added the Armory map, weapons and equipment, Kill Cam and Spectate features, additional language support, lower hardware requirements and a season system. [ref: Arena Breakout: Infinite Early Access to Launch on August 13, Arena Breakout: Infinite]

On 2 September 2025, MoreFun announced that the game would release on Steam on 15 September. [ref: Tactical FPS Arena Breakout Infinite locks in Steam launch 2.1m wishlists later, PCGamesN] [ref: Steam Full Release Dev Blog, Steam Community] The company described the full-release update as adding weapons, accessories, Farm map areas, tactical items, supply stations and updates to the Trophy Room. Arena Breakout: Infinite became available on Steam and the Epic Games Store on 15 September 2025. [ref: Arena Breakout Infinite is out on Steam, and it's no longer pay-to-win, PCGamesN]

data.text:

GameMill Entertainment (formerally known as GameMill Publishing) is an American video game publisher founded at Edina, Minnesota in Minneapolis by Gary Miller. Their current focus so far is on licensed games and porting through Arcade games on console. The company is mostly known for publishing various Nickelodeon games from Kart Racers to All-Star Brawl.

== History ==
In 2003, the company started off on publishing one of the most atrocious games, Big Rigs: Over the Road Racing, under GameMill Publishing. [ref: 'One of the most atrocious games ever published' is coming to Steam, and it's not a joke, Polygon] Upon renaming the company as GameMill Entertinment, it start to continue through publishing licensing games in North America such as two Disney games in 2013 and 2014 around Frozen and Big Hero 6.

In 2019, Gamemill announced a collab with NBC to make a video game tie-in, American Ninja Warrior Challenge, based on the television competition show American Ninja Warrior, and will be launching on March. [ref: 'American Ninja Warrior' Video Game Coming in March, The Hollywood Reporter] During 2023, GameMill announced two DreamWorks Animation-based games coming; one being a racing game simliar to their work on Nickelodeon, and the other being a movie tie-in to Trolls Band Together. [ref: Shrek Is Back in DreamWorks All-Star Kart Racing, IGN] However, one of their published games in 2023, Skull Island: Rise of Kong, based on King Kong, was considered to be one of the worst games of the year [ref: The Walking Dead: Destinies the Latest 'Worst Game of 2023' Contender From Company Behind King Kong, IGN] due to the development of the game having one year to make. [ref: That bad King Kong game was only in development for a year, The Verge] [ref: Recent King Kong game reportedly developed from scratch in one year, Eurogamer.net]

On June 2026, a few of the employees from Gamemill have left to open their own game publishing company Trailmark Games, with the first game in their catalog being The Walking Dead: Streets of Survival.

data.title: Leland Fitzpatrick
data.text:
Leland Fitzpatrick

Known as the Farmfoods Lord and the Best Buyer

Leland Fitzpatrick (born 22 February 2012) is a British trainspotter known among his peers by the nicknames “The Farmfoods Lord” and “The Best Buyer.” He is also known for his interest in railway spotting and his rivalry with fellow trainspotter Rhys Wright.

Early life

Fitzpatrick was born on 22 February 2012. From an early age, he developed an interest in trainspotting, an activity involving observing and identifying railway locomotives and trains.

Over time, he acquired the nickname “The Farmfoods Lord”, alongside the title “The Best Buyer”, which became central to his reputation among his friends.

Trainspotting career

Fitzpatrick is a trainspotter whose interests centre on observing trains and railway activity. His nickname, “The Best Buyer”, is associated with his legendary status within his social circle.

His unofficial title of “Farmfoods Lord” further distinguishes him from other trainspotters, although the precise origins of the title remain a matter of local legend.

Rivalry with Rhys Wright

One of the most notable stories associated with Fitzpatrick is his rivalry with fellow trainspotter Rhys Wright, described by his supporters as his arch-enemy.

The rivalry became known among their circle as “The Trainspotters’ War.” The conflict is remembered as a legendary feud between two railway enthusiasts, although its causes, events and outcome have not been independently documented.

Despite the dramatic name, the term “war” is used here in the context of their rivalry rather than as a verified historical armed conflict.

Legacy

Leland Fitzpatrick remains known by the titles “The Farmfoods Lord” and “The Best Buyer” within the circle in which these nicknames originated. His rivalry with Rhys Wright forms a central part of his unofficial legend.

Note: This is a fictionalised, humorous Wikipedia-style draft based on the information supplied. It is not an actual Wikipedia article, and the claims have not been independently verified.

data.title: Rajali Birds Park
data.text:
Rajali Birds Park is a privately owned interactive aviary, zoological exhibition, and eco-tourism attraction located in Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, India. Situated approximately 100 meters from the peripheral parking grounds and visitor facilities of the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Brihadeeswara Temple, the park functions as a major urban wildlife tourism hub within the Thanjavur district. It is characterized primarily by its immersive, cage-free walk-in aviary design, which distinguishes it from conventional regional zoological parks.

History and Development

The establishment of Rajali Birds Park was conceived to diversify the tourism profile of the Cauvery Delta region, which historically relies predominantly on cultural, religious, and architectural heritage tourism. Developers sought to introduce a modern, interactive wildlife exhibit modeled after contemporary international aviaries. By selecting a site adjacent to the city’s primary historic monument, the park was integrated into the high-density tourist corridor of Thanjavur, capitalizing on the heavy foot traffic generated by the temple complex.

Architecture and Enclosure Design

The park's architectural centerpiece is a large-scale, high-clearance steel and mesh dome enclosure. This structural design is engineered to optimize airflow and mimic localized microclimates while preventing the escape of non-native species.

The interior environment integrates elements of both natural landscape architecture and synthetic containment infrastructure:

* Arboreal Canopies: The enclosure incorporates pre-existing mature trees alongside curated tropical flora, providing natural nesting, perching, and foraging spaces for the avian population.
* Aquascaping: Simulated streams, waterfalls, and shallow wading pools are distributed throughout the enclosure to facilitate natural bathing behaviors and maintain ambient humidity levels necessary for tropical species.
* Visitor Walkways: Elevated and ground-level paved pathways isolate human foot traffic to designated zones, ensuring minimum disruption to ground-dwelling avian behaviors while maximizing visitor sightlines.

Avian Collection and Taxonomy

Rajali Birds Park houses a diverse inventory of over 1,000 birds, comprising dozens of species across several taxonomic orders. The collection focuses heavily on exotic, visually distinct, and socially gregarious species capable of thriving in a dense, multi-species communal habitat.

Psittaciformes (Parrots and Allies)

The park features a significant concentration of psittacines, known for their bright plumage and high cognitive capabilities. Notable exhibits include:

* South American Macaws: Including large-bodied blue-and-gold macaws (Ara ararauna) and green-winged macaws (Ara chloropterus).
* Australian Cockatoos: Including sulphur-crested cockatoos (Cacatua galerita) and various smaller corellas.
* Neotropical Conures: Diverse flocks of sun conures (Aratinga solstitialis) which fly freely in synchronized groups throughout the dome.
* Australasian Parrots: Extensive populations of budgerigars (Melopsittacus undulatus) and cockatiels.

Passeriformes and Columbiformes

A wide variety of smaller soft-billed birds inhabit the lower and mid-canopy layers. This includes various mutations of domestic lovebirds (Agapornis), exotic finches, and ground-dwelling ornamental doves, which occupy specialized niches within the ecosystem.

Ratites and Large Enclosures

Dedicated, barricaded ground paddocks house large, flightless ratites. These include African ostriches (Struthio camelus) and Australian emus (Dromaius novaehollandiae), which are separated from the main walk-in dome due to their size and distinct management requirements.

Other Fauna

To broaden its appeal to younger demographics and school tour groups, the park maintains a secondary petting zoo sector. This area is occupied by domesticated small mammals, primarily European rabbits (Oryctolagus cuniculus) and guinea pigs, housed in low-walled contact pens.

Visitor Interaction and Educational Programs

The operational philosophy of Rajali Birds Park emphasizes direct human-animal interaction as a tool for public engagement. Under the strict supervision of trained park handlers, visitors are permitted to purchase or receive approved grain and seed mixtures. This facilitates hand-feeding, during which various psittacines and passerines land directly on visitors' hands, arms, and shoulders.

The educational framework of the park includes:

* Species Identification Boards: Informational plaques detailing the common names, binomial nomenclature, native geographical distribution, natural diet, and IUCN Red List conservation status of each prominent species.
* Guided Interpretive Walks: Staff members conduct informal educational sessions for visitors, highlighting the ecological importance of bird conservation and the threats of habitat destruction in tropical rainforests.

Veterinary Care and Husbandry

To sustain a high-density, multi-species population within a confined airspace, the park implements strict veterinary and husbandry protocols. The birds are provided with specialized diets tailored to their taxonomic requirements, consisting of fresh fruits, sprouted seeds, nuts, and mineral supplements. Regular sanitation of the enclosures, water filtration systems, and quarantine procedures for newly acquired or symptomatic birds are maintained to prevent the introduction or spread of avian pathogens.

Tourism and Economic Impact

Rajali Birds Park operates as a commercial enterprise with a structured ticket pricing system. It has emerged as a major recreational asset for the local population of Thanjavur and a staple secondary destination for weekend travelers from neighboring cities such as Tiruchirappalli, Kumbakonam, and Pudukkottai. Peak operational periods correspond with the regional winter monsoon tourist season (November through February) and national school vacation periods.

data.title: Stanley Onuegbu
data.text:
Stanley Onuegbu is a Nigerian cinematographer and filmmaker from Anambra State.

== Early life ==
Onuegbu hails from Awba Ofemili in Awka North Local Government Area, Anambra State. He developed interest in cameras and digital appliances as a child and attended Planet Film School in Lagos in 2012. [ref: How I became most influential cinematographer in Anambra State – Stanley Onuegbu, OdogwuBlog] [ref: Anambra Cinematographer Stanley Onuegbu, HVM Playlist]

== Career ==
After training, Onuegbu joined Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS) as camera operator. He worked on Ogamba television show.

In 2020, he participated as Camera Man in Anambra State Teaching on Air programme. He received Certificate of Commendation from Anambra State Government dated 20 July 2020 signed by Governor Willie Obiano. [ref: Anambra State Government Certificate of Commendation presented to Stanley Onuegbu, 20 July 2020]

In December 2020, he was interviewed by Femi Magazine as an influential and youngest award-winning cinematographer from Anambra State. [ref: Influential Nigerian Cinematographer Joins the fight against SARS, Femi Magazine]

In July 2021, he was unveiled as Media Ambassador for iLAND Real Estate. [ref: iLAND REAL ESTATE: Media Ambassador, Stanley Onuegbu Undertakes First Inspection With Team, Coneri Media]

Onuegbu was cited as an example of dedication in the entertainment industry in the book Pathways to Stardom by Eriacy Confidence Oba (Foreword by Teco Benson). The author noted that Onuegbu rose to become a celebrated cinematographer after years of practicing with several companies, including Coneri Magazine and Anambra Broadcasting Service. [ref: Pathways to Stardom]

== Awards ==
* 2019 – South East Igbo Concert Award for Promoting Igbo Culture
* 2020 – Certificate of Commendation, Anambra State Government
* 2021 – Cinematographer of the Year, Unique Africa Awards
* 26 June 2021 – Most Influential Anambra Cinematographer, African Heritage Achievers Awards

data.title: Scooter Race
data.text:
"Scooter Race" is the third episode of the first season of Motu Patlu. [ref: Motu Patlu Episodes on JioCinema, JioCinema]
== Plot ==
Motu and Patlu decide to enter a local scooter race in Furfuri Nagar after learning about the massive ₹100,000 cash prize. Motu strikes a deal with the local tea stall owner, promising him a lifetime supply of free samosas if they win. However, the duo faces a major problem—they do not own a scooter. To fix this, they sneakily steal an advanced scooter invented by Dr. Jhatka, which he had spent 20 years building to win the race himself.

When Dr. Jhatka realizes his prize invention has been stolen, he teams up with Inspector Chingam to chase down the thieves, only to find Motu and Patlu flying past the starting line on his vehicle. Just like every other faulty invention by the scientist, the high-tech scooter malfunctions and goes completely out of control on the race track. As the vehicle flies through the air, crashes through obstacles, and creates absolute chaos, it disrupts all the other racers trying to compete. Desperate to fix the speed, Motu starts pressing random buttons on the dashboard, making the vehicle even more dangerous by activating booster-like speed and extreme horsepower.

After a wild, gravity-defying ride, Motu and Patlu manage to cross the finish line first. However, their celebration is cut short. The judges disqualify them from winning the ₹100,000 prize because the hyper-modified vehicle was completely destroyed during the race—leaving behind no seat and nothing but a bare handle, which the judges refuse to classify as a legal scooter.

== Trivia ==
* This episode features Furfuri Nagar's major local race event with a cash prize of ₹100,000.
* Dr. Jhatka’s 20-year-long research and invention is completely destroyed by Motu and Patlu during the chaotic race.

data.title: Luke Mack (Minus Zero)
data.text:
Luke Mack (Minus Zero)

Luke Mack (often releasing music under his project name Luke Mack Minus Zero) is an independent alternative rock musician based right here in Newcastle, NSW. After spending years as a drummer behind the kit for various local bands, he decided to step out on his own to write and record solo material. [1, 2]

He describes the project as "Luke Mack and his band of no one," capturing a gritty, self-produced indie ethos. [1]

💿 Music & Themes

His debut solo album, Driveway Anxiety, deals with heavy, reflective themes like isolation, temptation, recovery, and self-forgiveness. [1, 2]

* "Oblivion Conundrum": The hard-hitting, high-energy opening track that serves as a "call to arms" for the rest of the record.
* "Bottle of Wine": Another of his prominent singles.
* Other tracks include "Anchors", "I Never Seem To Get By", and "Scraps". [1, 2, 3]

🎸 The Local Scene & Recording

Luke tracks his music locally in Newcastle. He recorded his material at the well-known local studio RTN Studios (Rock The Nation), where his songs were mixed, produced, and engineered alongside a few other recognizable Newcastle musicians. He debuted the live format of the project with a full backing lineup featuring members of the local band Grand Pricks. [1, 2]

You can check out his profile and music directly on the Luke Mack Minus Zero Facebook Page or stream his tracks on the Luke Mack Spotify Artist Profile.

data.title: Assembly Atlanta
data.text:
Assembly Atlanta is a film and television production campus and mixed-use development in Doraville, Georgia, built on the site of a former General Motors assembly plant. Its centerpiece, Assembly Studios, opened in October 2023 as a full-service production complex operated by NBCUniversal's Universal Production Services, and has since hosted network, streaming, and independent productions including Beyond the Gates, Fight Night: The Million Dollar Heist, Teacup, Grosse Pointe Garden Society, Murdaugh: Death in the Family, Cape Fear, and a pilot for a revival of The Rockford Files.

== History ==

=== Former General Motors plant (1947–2008) ===
General Motors opened the Doraville Assembly plant in 1947 under its newly created Buick-Oldsmobile-Pontiac division, on a roughly 165-acre site near what is now Interstate 285. [ref: GM Closing Georgia Assembly Plant, Manufacturing.net] The plant produced more than 9 million vehicles over 61 years, including Buick, Oldsmobile, Pontiac, and Chevrolet models, before GM closed it in September 2008 amid company-wide cost cutting. [ref: GM's Doraville plant built the cars America loved, ATLVault / Atlanta News First] [ref: Doraville GM plant closes, The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]

=== Early redevelopment as "Assembly" (2014–2021) ===
Integral Group acquired the property in 2014 and proposed redeveloping the land as a mixed-use district known as Assembly. [ref: Major redevelopment of old GM site depends on public support, The Atlanta Journal-Constitution] Portions of the property were sold for automobile dealerships, while another portion was developed as the corporate headquarters of Serta Simmons Bedding. [ref: Serta Simmons HQ boosts rebuild of General Motors Doraville site, The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]

Third Rail Studios, a film and television production facility occupying approximately seven acres and originally developed by The Integral Group, opened at the site in 2016. [ref: NBCUniversal will operate huge new Assembly film studio in Doraville, The Atlanta Journal-Constitution] The studio hosted a number of high-profile productions, including the feature films Rampage, Mile 22, and Richard Jewell, the first season of NBC's Good Girls, and Netflix's Emmy-nominated series Ozark. [ref: Gray Television purchases Doraville's Third Rail Studios, The Atlanta Journal-Constitution] [ref: Gray Television announces NBCUniversal deal for new studios, Gray News/Fox 34] Gray Television acquired Third Rail Studios in September 2021 and folded it into the larger Assembly site; it is now owned and operated under Gray Media. [ref: Gray Television purchases Third Rail Studios, 11Alive]

=== Gray Media acquisition and "Studio City" plan (2021) ===
Gray Media purchased the remaining property in March 2021 to pursue a new "Studio City" concept, with Gray chairman and CEO Hilton H. Howell Jr. leading the project. [ref: TV company to remake former GM plant into Georgia's largest "Studio City", Urbanize Atlanta] [ref: Former GM plant set to transform into massive film-production site, The Atlanta Journal-Constitution] By 2022, Gray described the assembled 135-acre site as encompassing a 43-acre studio complex — featuring soundstages, production offices, warehouse and mill buildings, studio bungalows, event space, and a parking deck.

In June 2022, Gray announced a long-term agreement under which NBCUniversal would lease and operate new studio facilities at the site and manage all studio and production operations across the complex, including Gray's own facilities and Third Rail Studios.

=== Construction (2021–2023) ===
Construction broke ground in September 2021. At the time of the NBCUniversal deal, three soundstage walls had already been erected, with additional soundstages, production offices, mill buildings, event spaces, and warehouses still to come. [ref: NBCUniversal Media reached deal with Gray Television to film in Doraville, Fox 5 Atlanta] Steel for the project was purchased in 2021 to avoid pandemic-related shortages, and the contractor built a temporary on-site concrete plant; roughly 83 acres of the former GM plant's concrete floors were broken up over about a year and reused as fill.

=== Opening (October–November 2023) ===
Assembly Studios opened with 19 soundstages across roughly 43 of the site's 135 acres. [ref: Assembly Studios, Smith Dalia Architects] [ref: Build It, And Here They Come: Assembly Atlanta Set to Make Its Mark on Georgia's Film Industry, Georgia Entertainment] Gray marked the opening with a gala on October 21, 2023, featuring a commissioned mural by Atlanta artist Steve Penley, a drone show, and performances by Cee Lo Green, Gladys Knight, Dionne Warwick, and Sheryl Crow; the company said it had invested more than $400 million in the buildout. [ref: Gray opens Assembly TV/film studios with massive gala, The Atlanta Journal-Constitution] A formal grand-opening announcement followed on November 9, 2023. [ref: Gray Television's Assembly Studios Celebrates Grand Opening of Innovative Sound Stages in Georgia, GlobeNewswire]

== Facilities and design ==
Assembly Studios was designed by Smith Dalia Architects, with additional project partners including The Gipson Company (developer and construction manager), Joe N. Guy Co., Bailey Construction, HGOR, Kimley-Horn, PES Structural, Centerpoint Sitework and Utilities, Nanolumens, and Capital Signs. JLL served as strategic advisor. [ref: Atlanta, Assemble! Check Out North America's "Largest Freestanding LED Screen", AVNetwork]

The campus comprises more than one million square feet of production space. Its 22 soundstages include 19 at Assembly Studios and three at the adjacent Third Rail Studios, providing roughly 350,000 square feet of stage space across the combined campus (reflecting the original configuration, not a later expansion). Individual stages range from 15,000 to 30,000 square feet, with grid heights of 40 to 50 feet. [ref: INTENNSE tennis league announces move to Assembly studios for 2026 season, Atlanta News First] [ref: Georgia production facilities: Trilith Studios, Three Ring Studios, Variety] [ref: Property Map, Assembly Atlanta] [ref: Atlanta, Universal Production Services]

Additional facilities include approximately 100,000 square feet of mill space across three mill buildings and a mill warehouse, as well as administrative facilities, studio bungalows and turn-key production offices with bullpen-style workspaces, private offices, conference rooms, executive suites and break rooms. Production support amenities include costume, sign and fabrication shops; a paint shop; set lighting, grip and transportation departments; and an on-site café.

The filmable exterior backlot is organized into four districts: "New Orleans," "New York Brownstones," "European City," and "Tribeca." The façades were built with real construction materials rather than as false fronts. The campus also includes a roughly 300-foot-long water stage that can be rigged with green screens and digitally transformed to represent different bodies of water, according to Gray Television CEO Hilton Howell.

A landscaped public park and pond sit alongside the backlot façades and connect to the Chamblee Rail Trail through a covered trestle bridge. The campus is located at 2582 Assembly Boulevard in Doraville, Georgia, near Interstate 85 North at Exit 95.

== Public spaces and features ==
Areas outside the soundstages are open to the public, including a landscaped park and a pond that also serves as stormwater retention. A 140-foot, roughly 23-foot-wide LED tower designed and built by Nanolumens and installed with Capital Signs stands at the campus entrance facing Interstate 285; the companies involved in its construction describe it as the largest freestanding LED screen in North America, a claim reported by multiple outlets but not independently verified.

A mural by Atlanta artist Steve Penley, depicting Georgia landmarks and cultural touchstones including the Fox Theatre, the Varsity, and Ebenezer Baptist Church, was unveiled on the side of a soundstage. [ref: New mural unveiled at Assembly Studios, Atlanta News First]

In 2026, Assembly Atlanta added a mass-timber-and-steel bandshell, described as the largest timber-grid amphitheater in North America, with a stage floor roughly the size of the Fox Theatre's. [ref: Assembly Studios installs bandshell, plans World Cup watch party, The Atlanta Journal-Constitution] The venue hosted public watch parties for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, including a two-day festival presented by Telemundo Atlanta.

== Operations ==
Assembly Studios is owned by Gray Media and operated by NBCUniversal's Universal Production Services under a multi-year agreement signed in 2022, with NBCUniversal serving as anchor tenant and lead lessee, and providing services including a costume house, sign shop, lighting, grip, and transportation.

=== Georgia Film Academy Training Facility ===
In June 2025, the Georgia Film Academy announced a partnership with Assembly Studios to open a 32,000-square-foot workforce training facility adjacent to the campus, offering certifications in film and television production, post-production, and live production, streaming, and esports; classes began August 18, 2025. [ref: Georgia Film Academy and Assembly Studios opening workforce training complex in Doraville, WABE] The facility is a satellite of GFA's primary hub at Trilith Studios in Fayetteville and also offers a paid internship and apprenticeship program placing students directly on working sets. [ref: Georgia Film Academy and Assembly Studios Launch Partnership, Discover Dunwoody] The facility's grand opening in August 2025 featured remarks from University System of Georgia chancellor Sonny Perdue and Georgia Film Office deputy commissioner Lee Thomas. [ref: Georgia Film Academy Celebrates Grand Opening of State-of-the-Art Facility at Assembly Studios, Georgia Entertainment]

== Live events ==
Beyond film and television production, Assembly Atlanta has hosted live sporting and community events. Since 2025, the campus has been home to INTENNSE, a fast-paced, team-based professional tennis league that debuted with six teams and expanded to ten for its 2026 season. Matches are played in a 30,000-square-foot soundstage converted into a 500-seat arena, and the league's 2026 season ran from June to August with 52 events. [ref: INTENNSE tennis league's new season to open at Assembly Studios, Atlanta News First] [ref: INTENNSE Arena at Assembly Studios, Stadium Journey]
