data.title: Jahsean Corbett
data.text:
Jahsean Corbett (born July 1, 2002) is an American professional basketball player who plays for the CD Español Osorno team in Liga Nacional de Básquetbol (LNB). [ref: Jahsean Corbett – CD Español Osorno, LatinBasket] He played college basketball for Chicago State and Duquesne. [ref: Jahsean Corbett Player Profile, ESPN]

== Early life ==
Corbett was born in Orlando, Florida, and attended West Oaks Academy, where he played high school basketball. [ref: 2022-23 Men's Basketball Roster, Chicago State Cougars]

== Career ==

=== Chicago State ===
Corbett played three seasons for Chicago State from 2021 to 2024. [ref: Jahsean Corbett College Stats, Sports-Reference] In 2022, he represented the U.S. Virgin Islands in the 2022 FIBA AmeriCup.

=== Duquesne University ===
For the 2024–25 season, Corbett transferred to Duquesne University [ref: West Oaks basketball gains 3 transfers and scrutiny, Orlando Sentinel] and joined the Duquesne Dukes men's basketball program. [ref: Duquesne to receive official visit from productive Chicago State transfer guard Jahsean Corbett, Yardbarker]

Before committing to Duquesne, Corbett received interest from programs including Miami, Mississippi State, UAB, Virginia Tech, Utah State, Bowling Green, Loyola Chicago, Illinois State, UMBC, and UTEP.
Corbett recorded a double-double with 13 points and 10 rebounds in a 67–55 victory over Rhode Island. [ref: Jahsean Corbett propels Duquesne to 67-55 victory over Rhode Island, CBS Sports]

In another game, Corbett scored a career-high 29 points and grabbed six rebounds, but ultimately Duquesne lost 77–71 to Davidson. [ref: Jahsean Corbett's 29 points not enough as Duquesne falls to Davidson, TribLIVE]

== Professional career ==
In 2026, Corbett started playing professionally for CD Español Osorno in the Liga Nacional de Básquetbol. In August 2026, he scored 35 points in a game and was named the league's Player of the Week. At the time, he was averaging 25.3 points per game, making him the league's leading scorer.

On March 22, 2026, Corbett, along with the entire CD Español Osorno team, won the Chery Super Cup, qualifying for the South Conference of the 2026 Ligo UNO. [ref: Español de Osorno was crowned champion of the 2026 Chery Super Cup, Radio Sago]

data.title: Gaurav Kapadia
data.text:
Gaurav Kapadia is an American investor and the founder of investment firm XN. He previously co-founded Soroban Capital Partners.
==Early Life and education==
Kapadia grew up in Queens, New York, the son of immigrants from India. At age 11, he gained admission to Hunter College High School. [ref: HCCS Director Search Announcement, Hunter Schools] He later graduated from the University of Pennsylvania. [ref: Sonia Jain, Gaurav Kapadia, Newyork Times] [ref: Is Vulcan Materials Company (VMC) the Top Stock to Buy According to XN Exponent Advisors LLC?, Yahoo]
==Career==
Kapadia began his career at Boston Consulting Group before joining TPG-Axon Capital, where he became a partner. In 2010, he co-founded Soroban Capital Partners with Eric Mandelblatt and Scott Friedman. He left the firm in 2018 to establish a family office. [ref: Ex-Goldman Sachs Traders Raise $1.5 Billion for New Hedge Funds, Bloomberg] [ref: Why Hedge Fund Soroban Is Shrinking on Purpose, Wall St Journal]

In 2019, Kapadia founded XN as a family office. The firm began managing external capital in July 2020. XN invests in publicly traded securities and private companies. In 2021, XN led Airtable's Series F funding round. [ref: Gecko Robotics raises $125 million in deal valuing critical infrastructure startup over $1 billion, CNBC] [ref: Software start-up Airtable hits $11 billion valuation in latest funding, adds Salesforce, Michael Dell as investors, CNBC]

Kapadia serves as vice chair of the board of trustees of the Whitney Museum of American Art. He also serves on the boards of the Mellon Foundation, Trust for Governors Island [ref: The Trust for Governors Island, Govisland.com], and the Institute for Constitutional Advocacy and Protection at Georgetown University Law Center. [ref: Team & Board, Georgetown]

In 2026, Kapadia founded Totei, an online arts and culture magazine focused on craftsmanship. [ref: Exclusive / New arts magazine Totei to focus on the ‘creative process’, Semafor]

data.title: New Government Procurement Act
data.text:
== New Government Procurement Act ==
The New Government Procurement Act (NGPA), officially known as [https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2024/ra_12009_2024.html Republic Act No. 12009], is a Philippine law that establishes the legal framework for government procurement of goods, infrastructure projects, and consulting services. It was signed into law on July 20, 2024, and took effect on August 13, 2024. The law replaced Republic Act No. 9184, also known as the Government Procurement Reform Act, and aims to promote transparency, competition, efficiency, accountability, sustainability, and value for money in government spending. [ref: Philippines: New Government Procurement Act Enters into Force, Library of Congress] [ref: Republic Act No. 12009, The LawPhil Project]

=== Overview ===
The New Government Procurement Act sets rules for how government agencies acquire goods and services, contract infrastructure projects, and use public funds for procurement. It applies to national government offices and agencies, state universities and colleges, government-owned or controlled corporations, government financial institutions, and local government units, subject to the law's provisions and applicable agreements.

The law seeks to improve government procurement by establishing principles that support open information, fair competition, efficient procedures, accountability, public monitoring, and sustainable purchasing. It also emphasizes value for money in the use of public resources.

=== Background ===
Before the passage of Republic Act No. 12009, government procurement in the Philippines was mainly governed by Republic Act No. 9184, or the Government Procurement Reform Act. Research by the Philippine Institute for Development Studies examined procurement reforms under the earlier framework and discussed implementation challenges, including delays and difficulties in procurement processes. [ref: The Promises and Pains in Procurement Reforms in the Philippines, Philippine Institute for Development Studies]

In July 2024, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. signed Republic Act No. 12009 into law. It took effect on August 13, 2024, and revised the previous legal framework for government procurement. The law's implementing rules and regulations were published on February 10, 2025, to guide its implementation. [ref: Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 12009, Supreme Court E-Library]

=== Legal framework and scope ===
Republic Act No. 12009 provides the legal basis for procurement activities involving goods, infrastructure projects, and consulting services by covered government entities. The law applies regardless of whether the funds come from local or foreign sources, subject to applicable treaties and international or executive agreements.

The law also provides for implementing rules and regulations to guide procurement planning, procedures, and contract implementation. These rules support the application of the law's policies and principles in government procurement activities.

=== Governing principles ===
Republic Act No. 12009 identifies several principles for government procurement:

* Transparency: Providing access to procurement information and supporting the disclosure of information throughout the procurement process.
* Competitiveness: Giving eligible and qualified suppliers, contractors, consultants, and service providers fair opportunities.
* Efficiency: Promoting organized and straightforward procedures, including the use of technology and innovative solutions.
* Proportionality: Ensuring that procurement requirements are appropriate to the needs of the government entity and the nature of the project.
* Accountability: Holding responsible public officials and personnel accountable for their actions when necessary.
* Public monitoring: Allowing public oversight of procurement processes and contract implementation.
* Sustainability: Considering the life cycle of property and the environmental and social effects of procurement.
* Professionalism: Supporting qualification standards, competency development, and ethical conduct among procurement personnel.

=== Procurement procedures ===
The law establishes a framework for government procurement that covers planning through contract implementation. Its implementing rules and regulations provide guidance for government entities in carrying out procurement activities and selecting appropriate procedures for their needs.

The law also provides for the development and use of standard procurement forms. These measures are intended to support consistent procedures and the implementation of procurement requirements across covered government entities. [ref: Important Update: Effectivity and Transitory Periods under RA 12009, Government Procurement Policy Board]

=== Transparency and public monitoring ===
Transparency and public monitoring are among the central principles of the New Government Procurement Act. The law supports open contracting practices that make procurement information accessible and facilitate information sharing at different stages of procurement.

The Library of Congress reported that the law includes measures related to open contracting standards and public monitoring, including the participation of observers and civil society organizations in procurement oversight.

=== Implementation ===
The Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) is responsible for policy direction and the formulation of implementing rules and regulations for government procurement. Republic Act No. 12009 required the formulation of these rules within the period specified by the law.

The implementing rules and regulations were published on February 10, 2025. The law also provides a three-year transitional period, counted from the approval of the standard procurement forms, for covered government entities and procurement bodies to fully comply with its requirements.

=== Relationship with the Government Procurement Reform Act ===
Republic Act No. 12009 revised and replaced Republic Act No. 9184 as the main legal framework for government procurement in the Philippines. The new law retains the goal of improving public procurement while emphasizing transparency, competition, accountability, sustainability, public monitoring, and value for money.

Earlier research on procurement reforms in the Philippines provides background on challenges associated with the previous framework. These studies examined issues such as procurement delays, competition, and implementation capacity, but they predate Republic Act No. 12009 and do not evaluate the results of the new law. [ref: The Evolution of Reforms and the State of Competition in Public Procurement in the Philippines, Philippine Institute for Development Studies]

data.title: Government Optimization Act
data.text:
----

The Government Optimization Act, officially known as [https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2025/ra_12231_2025.html Republic Act No. 12231], is a Philippine law enacted on August 4, 2025, that establishes a framework for optimizing the organization and operations of the national government to improve public service delivery. The law aims to promote government efficiency, strengthen institutional capacity, minimize overlapping functions, simplify administrative processes, and protect the welfare of civil servants and other government workers. [ref: [https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2025/ra_12231_2025.html Republic Act No. 12231: An Act Optimizing the National Government for Efficient Public Service Delivery]. LawPhil Project, August 4, 2025.]

== Overview ==

The Government Optimization Act establishes the Government Optimization Program (GOP), which provides for the review of government agencies' mandates, functions, organizational structures, staffing patterns, systems, and processes. The program seeks to ensure that government institutions perform their essential functions and use public resources efficiently in delivering services.

Under the Act, government optimization includes reviewing agency responsibilities, identifying redundant or overlapping functions, simplifying procedures, modernizing systems, and determining the appropriate organizational structure and staffing requirements of government institutions. The law also recognizes digitization and electronic governance as means of improving public service delivery. [ref: [https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/99481 Republic Act No. 12231]. Supreme Court E-Library.]

== Provisions ==

=== Government Optimization Program ===

The Government Optimization Program is designed to improve the effectiveness, efficiency, economy, equity, and ethical accountability of government operations. It provides a framework for assessing the functions and structures of agencies and determining whether changes are necessary to improve institutional performance.

The program follows principles that include simplifying government operations, clearly defining the responsibilities of national and local governments, encouraging public-sector employee participation in matters affecting their rights, and improving systems for delivering public services.

=== Reorganization of government agencies ===

Section 6 of the Act grants the President authority to optimize the operations of executive branch agencies, subject to the requirements of the law. Organizational actions may include creating, reorganizing, merging, streamlining, abolishing, or deactivating agencies, offices, or units when determined to be in the best interest of the State through the prescribed process.

The Act also allows changes in agency functions, including transferring or integrating functions between agencies and discontinuing activities that can be better performed by other institutions or by the private sector, subject to the law's governing principles and conditions.

=== Committee on Optimizing the Executive Branch ===

The Act establishes the Committee on Optimizing the Executive Branch (COEB) to oversee and coordinate the Government Optimization Program. The committee is chaired by the Executive Secretary, with the Secretary of the Department of Budget and Management serving as co-chairperson. Other members are identified in the Act.

The committee's responsibilities include developing the program's policies and implementation framework, conducting studies on government agencies, preparing optimized organizational structures and proposed executive issuances, and monitoring the implementation of approved optimization plans. It is also responsible for developing change-management measures to support the transition and safeguard the welfare of affected employees. [ref: [https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/101010 Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 12231, Otherwise Known as the Government Optimization Act]. Supreme Court E-Library, January 23, 2026.]

=== Agency reviews and optimization plans ===

Section 10 of the Act requires covered agencies to conduct an organizational review and study of their mandates, objectives, functions, systems, procedures, programs, activities, projects, organizational structures, staffing patterns, and personnel requirements.

Based on this review, each agency must formulate an optimization plan consistent with the governing principles of the Act. The plan identifies areas requiring improvement and areas where resources may need to be redirected to strengthen institutional capacity. It may also address staffing requirements for qualified personnel, subject to the conditions and limitations established by the law.

The implementing rules and regulations provide additional procedures for strategic reviews, the preparation of optimization plans, consultations with affected personnel, and the development of optimized organizational structures.

=== Protection of government personnel ===

The Act includes provisions for government employees affected by organizational changes. It addresses personnel evaluation, staffing requirements, and measures for managing the transition from existing organizational structures to optimized structures.

Under Section 13, qualified permanent personnel with appointments attested by the Civil Service Commission who choose to retire or separate from government service may be entitled to retirement benefits and separation incentives, subject to the requirements and conditions provided by the Act and applicable laws.

The implementing rules also provide for employee consultations and measures to support affected personnel during the implementation of the program.

== Implementation ==

The implementing rules and regulations of [https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2025/ra_12231_2025.html Republic Act No. 12231] were issued by the Committee on Optimizing the Executive Branch on January 23, 2026. They establish procedures for implementing the Government Optimization Program, including strategic reviews, agency optimization plans, organizational restructuring, and the management of personnel transitions.

The Department of Budget and Management serves an important role in implementing the program. Its published collection of legal bases and related issuances provides government agencies with access to documents concerning the implementation of the Government Optimization Program. [ref: Department of Budget and Management. [https://www.dbm.gov.ph/index.php/legal-bases-and-other-related-issuances-on-the-government-optimization-program Legal Bases and Other Related Issuances on the Government Optimization Program].]

== Oversight and assessment ==

Section 18 of the Act establishes a Joint Congressional Oversight Committee on the Government Optimization Program to oversee, monitor, and evaluate its implementation. The committee consists of members from both the Senate and the House of Representatives.

Section 19 requires the Department of Budget and Management to commission an independent impact assessment three years after completion of the program. The assessment is intended to examine its effects and gains. Section 20 also requires the President to submit a report to Congress on the program's results after its implementation is completed.

== Duration ==

Section 23 of the Act provides that the authority granted to the President under the law ends five years after the Act takes effect. This provision does not prejudice the President's inherent power to reorganize the executive branch.

data.title: Webtronaut Innovations
data.text:
Webtronaut Innovations LLC is an American internet holding company located in Albuquerque, New Mexico. Sahil Kazi, an Indian/Pakistani serial entrepreneur and SAP Certified Systems Analyst, founded the company. Webtronaut's first venture was the legal-tech marketplace SueEasy, which launched in 2007 and was a semi-finalist in the first-ever TechCrunch startup competition, TechCrunch40. [ref: Ambulance Chasers Have A New Home, SueEasy, TechCrunch] Currently, Webtronaut's ventures include Richlisted, GuiltyAF, SwaxAwards, and LabCauldron.

== History ==

=== SueEasy and Filmmortal (2007–2009) ===
Webtronaut's first ventures were created under the name Webtronaut Innovations (including an Indian entity, Webtronaut Innovations Pvt. Ltd.) and operated out of Mountain View, California. [ref: Filmmortal.com, Film Is Immortal. So Is Your Brand, PRLog]

SueEasy, launched in 2007 by Kazi and Faraz Matin, was a marketplace that turned the traditional lawyer directory upside down: would-be plaintiffs posted grievances and documents, either individually or as potential class actions, and licensed attorneys bid on the opportunity to contact the client. Crunchbase identifies SueEasy as a sub-organisation of Webtronaut Innovations. [ref: SueEasy — Company Profile, Crunchbase] SueEasy launched publicly in April 2008 with a searchable class action database containing nine filing categories. [ref: SueEasy Goes Live — Your Class Action Lawsuit Lottery Ticket, TechCrunch] The ABA Journal called the service a "reverse Martindale-Hubbell" that connected would-be plaintiffs with attorneys. [ref: New Website Plays Matchmaker For Would-Be Plaintiffs, ABA Journal] United Press International also wrote about the service in April 2008. [ref: Web Site Makes Suing Easy] The Los Angeles Daily Journal later wrote about SueEasy among attorney-client matchmaking services, quoting Kazi and stating that more than 1,200 California attorneys were paying customers. [ref: Attorney-Client Matchmakers, Los Angeles Daily Journal] The model also received criticism from legal commentators regarding case quality and legal ethics. In September 2009, the business was put up for sale via online auction. [ref: Running SueEasy Turned Out To Be Not So Easy, Overlawyered] According to the company, SueEasy was subsequently purchased by a mass torts law firm. Company databases indicate that the original company has been closed.

In 2008, the group launched Filmmortal, an auction marketplace for product placement, described as "the eBay for product placement," where independent filmmakers listed projects and advertisers bid to have their products placed in those projects. [ref: Filmmortal — Company Profile, Crunchbase] BusinessWeek and GigaOM's NewTeeVee both wrote about Filmmortal and competitor PlaceVine as new matchmakers for product placement deals, reporting that Kazi had bootstrapped Filmmortal with $130,000 and that placement deals started at approximately $3,000. [ref: Startups Take on Product Placement Dealmaking, BusinessWeek] [ref: The New Matchmakers: Startups Tackle Product Placement Deals, NewTeeVee] Media in Canada wrote about the service in April 2009, calling it an "eBay for product placement" with approximately 80 projects listed. [ref: Filmmortal breathes life into indie scripts, Media in Canada] IndieWire also wrote about the service in October 2009. [ref: Product Placement Ought to Know Where It's Being Placed, IndieWire] Product Placement News announced the marketplace in February 2009. [ref: Introducing Filmmortal, Product Placement News] Kazi was Filmmortal's chief executive. According to the company, Filmmortal was subsequently acquired. Company databases list it as closed.

=== Holding company and current ventures (2023–present) ===
In April 2023, the group launched Richlisted, a service that records members' names on a public blockchain as a permanent record of achievement; a launch announcement quoted Kazi as managing director of Richlisted. [ref: RichListed Launches Exclusive Blockchain-Listed Network for Self-Made Individuals to Showcase Status, PRLog]

In October 2026, Webtronaut Innovations LLC was established in New Mexico as the holding company for the group's web-based businesses, which it refers to as an "internet holding company operating multiple web-based businesses." [ref: Webtronaut Innovations]

== Ventures ==
=== SueEasy ===
SueEasy (2007–2009) was a legal marketplace and class action repository. Plaintiffs posted cases across various categories including class actions; only licensed attorneys could view the listings, and attorneys bid on the opportunity to contact a client, with the client having the right to reject any bidder.

=== Filmmortal ===
Filmmortal (2008) was an online auction marketplace for product placement deals between independent filmmakers and advertisers, including barter arrangements such as transportation, lodging, catering, props, and equipment.

=== Richlisted ===
Richlisted (2023–present) provides a one-time paid listing recorded on a public blockchain as a permanent, unalterable record.

=== GuiltyAF ===
GuiltyAF (2025–present) is an interactive live-streamed show where two parties present a dispute and the audience votes on the resolution in real-time.

=== SwaxAwards ===
SwaxAwards is a monthly awards program recognizing creators on TikTok across various categories including comedy, dance, and wholesome content.

=== LabCauldron ===
LabCauldron (2026–present) is an online platform for IB Biology teachers with tools for internal assessment moderation, rubric-based task design, and lab work management. [ref: LabCauldron]

== Founder ==
Sahil Kazi is an Indian/Pakistani serial entrepreneur and SAP Certified Systems Analyst. His Wellfound profile credits him with two startup launches and exits and describes him as an SAP Certified Consultant. [ref: Webtronaut Innovations: Founder, Leadership & Team, Wellfound] He co-founded SueEasy with Faraz Matin and served as chief executive of Filmmortal. The Org also identifies Kazi as Filmmortal's chief executive. [ref: Sahil Kazi — CEO at Filmmortal, The Org]

data.title: Michael Needham
data.text:
Michael "Mike" Needham is a retired British police officer who served with Lancashire Constabulary in England and later as a superintendent in the Royal Cayman Islands Police Service (RCIPS). [ref: Gunning for you!, Lancashire Telegraph] [ref: Another top cop leaves, Cayman Compass] During his career in the Cayman Islands, Needham headed the RCIPS Financial Crime Unit and Marine Unit and was involved in the development of the service's financial-crime, intelligence and marine capabilities. [ref: Needham retires from RCIPS, Cayman News Service] He received the Colonial Police Medal in the 2009 Birthday Honours.

==Police career==

===Lancashire Constabulary===

Needham served with Lancashire Constabulary before moving to the Cayman Islands. A contemporary report in the Lancashire Telegraph in March 1997 identified him as Acting Chief Inspector Mike Needham in the Lancaster and Morecambe area.

The report concerned a Lancashire police road-safety initiative introduced following a series of fatal and serious road accidents. Needham said that police analysis had identified speeding as a significant factor in accidents on rural roads and described the deployment of mobile speed-camera enforcement as part of the police response.

An account of his career published at the time of his retirement from the RCIPS stated that Needham had served with Lancashire Constabulary for more than three decades before moving to the Cayman Islands.

===Royal Cayman Islands Police Service===

Needham joined the Royal Cayman Islands Police Service in January 1999 as a detective chief inspector with responsibility for the Commercial Crime Branch. He was promoted to detective superintendent in May 2003.

In 2001, Needham was involved in establishing the Joint Intelligence Unit, which brought together personnel from the police, customs and immigration authorities. He subsequently established the Financial Crime Unit and became its head.

As head of the Financial Crime Unit, Needham was the senior police officer publicly associated with a number of financial investigations in the Cayman Islands. In August 2008, the Cayman Compass reported on several investigations being conducted by the unit and quoted Needham on the time and resources required to investigate complex financial cases. The matters included investigations relating to the Affordable Housing Initiative, financing arrangements for the Boatswain's Beach development and failed Cayman-domiciled investment funds. [ref: Police ask for patience, Cayman Compass]

In March 2009, the Cayman Compass described Needham as a high-ranking member of the RCIPS command staff and identified him as the superintendent responsible for the Financial Crime Unit.

===Marine Unit===

Needham also headed the RCIPS Marine Unit and oversaw a programme to expand and modernise the Cayman Islands' marine law-enforcement capability.

In February 2007, the Cayman Compass reported that Needham was overseeing plans for a new joint marine base for the police, customs and immigration authorities. The Cayman Islands government had committed approximately CI$5 million to the proposed facility. Plans associated with the expansion included a 65-foot patrol vessel, fast interceptor vessels and increased staffing. [ref: $5M marine base planned, Cayman Compass]

The programme also involved the acquisition of the Cayman Defender, one of a number of new law-enforcement vessels. Reporting in September 2008 identified Needham as project leader for the programme, which formed part of a CI$7.7 million investment in border protection. [ref: Marine cops get new boat, Cayman News Service]

==Retirement==

Needham retired from the Royal Cayman Islands Police Service in March 2009 after approximately ten years with the service. Contemporary reports stated that his retirement brought to an end a policing career of approximately 41 years in the United Kingdom and the Cayman Islands.

At the time of Needham's retirement, acting commissioner of police James Smith said that Needham had "clearly achieved a great deal" during his policing career and referred to his contribution to the RCIPS.

==Honours==

Needham received the Colonial Police Medal in the 2009 Birthday Honours for his service with the Royal Cayman Islands Police Service.

data.title: Abhilash Kumar
data.text:
Abhilash Kumar is an Indian actor who works in Hindi films and television. He portrayed the antagonist Kabir Bansal in the 2016 action drama Ghayal Once Again.

== Career ==

Kumar appeared in an episode of the Bindass television series Yeh Hai Aashiqui opposite Bhumika Gurung in December 2014. [ref: Yeh Hai Aashiqui Episode 79 starring Bhumika Gurung and Abhilash Kumar, 7th December 2014 on Bindass – Written Update, TellyReviews]

In February 2016, he featured in the Sunny Deol-directed action film Ghayal Once Again, a sequel to 1990's Ghayal produced by Vijayta Films. Kumar played Kabir Bansal, a young antagonist whose actions set the plot in motion. [ref: Film review: ‘Ghayal Once Again’ proves that some old wounds don’t heal well, Scroll.in] [ref: Ghayal Once Again review: This time it hurts, Hindustan Times] Reviewing the film for The Himalayan Times, a critic noted: "Abhilash Kumar playing spoilt Kabir Bansal shines in his performance". [ref: Great action, weak plot, The Himalayan Times]

Later in 2016, Kumar joined the television comedy Bahu Hamari Rajni Kant as Vikram. [ref: The Kant family welcomes a new member in Bahu Hamari Rajni_kant!, IndiaForums] [ref: Vahbbiz Dorabjee turns casting director for Bahu Hamari Rajni Kant, Deccan Chronicle] In April 2017, he was cast as Rohit in the Colors TV romantic drama Kasam Tere Pyaar Ki. [ref: Abhilash Kumar to enter Colors’ Kasam, IWMbuzz] He was subsequently included in the ensemble cast of the 2019 ZEE5 series Bombers. [ref: Prince, Meiyang, Gaurav, Archis, Rohan, Shivam, Mridul, Danish, Saaqib, Dev, Abhilash, Taher in ZEE5's Bombers, IWMbuzz]

In April 2024, Kumar appeared in the feature film Gabru Gang, directed by Sameer Khan. [ref: Gabru Gang Movie Review: This heartfelt sports drama fails to fly high, The Times of India] [ref: Ghayal Once Again fame Abhilash Kumar in the movie ‘Gabru Gang’, IWMbuzz]

data.title: Neraidovrysi
data.text:
Neraidovrysi (; until 1927 Koutsoumadi, ) is a small settlement in southwestern Messenia, in the Peloponnese region of Greece. It lies on the southern side of Mount Lykodimos at an elevation of. Administratively it is part of the Adriani community in the Aipeia municipal unit of the municipality of Messini. The name means roughly "fairy spring" (see Etymology). At the 2021 census the settlement had no permanent residents.

==Etymology==
The name Neraidovrysi is a compound of two Greek words: neráida (), which in Greek folk tradition denotes an imagined being in the form of a very beautiful young woman who lives far from inhabited places, [ref: νεράιδα, Dictionary of Standard Modern Greek (Triantafyllidis)] and vrýsi (), a built fountain or similar structure from which (usually drinking) water runs. [ref: βρύση, Dictionary of Standard Modern Greek (Triantafyllidis)] The name can therefore be translated as "fairy spring" or "fairy fountain".

The Municipality of Messini's description of the Aipeia municipal unit says that the present name is presumed () to come from a spring in the settlement where, according to the inhabitants, fairies appeared very often. This is a local tradition: no detailed story, such as a named tale about the spring or its fairies, has been found in the published sources consulted.

Before 1927 the settlement was called Koutsoumadi. According to the same municipal source, this name derived from the Turkish personal name Koutsou Meti (), said to be that of a Turkish landowner who lived there. The settlement was renamed Neraidovrysi in 1927. [ref: Koutsoumadi – Neraidovrysi, Pandektis: Name Changes of Settlements in Greece]

==Geography==
Neraidovrysi is a semi-mountainous settlement built on the southern slope of Mount Lykodimos, in the south-west of Messenia. Its elevation is given as. The village of Adriani, after which the community is named, lies about south-west of Kalamata and about from the sea; the community also includes Kleisoura and Nea Adriani.

==History==
The settlement appears in the Venetian census of 1700, when the Kingdom of the Morea was under Venetian rule, as Koutsoumadi with eight families and 34 inhabitants.

Under the administrative reorganisations of the 19th century and later, Koutsoumadi was successively attached to different municipalities. It was first assigned to the municipality of Aipeia (seat: Longa) when that municipality was created in 1835; in 1840 it was moved to the municipality of Koroni (seat: Petalidi); in 1890 it was returned to Aipeia; and in 1912 it was attached to the community of Remoustafa. [ref: Δ. Αιπείας (Μεσσηνίας) – Διοικητικές Μεταβολές, Εθνικό Μητρώο Διοικητικών Μεταβολών των ΟΤΑ] The community of Remoustafa was renamed Adriani in 1927, the same year Koutsoumadi became Neraidovrysi. [ref: Διοικητικές μεταβολές οικισμού: Νεραϊδόβρυση (Κουτσουμάδι), Εθνικό Μητρώο Διοικητικών Μεταβολών των ΟΤΑ]

Under the 1997 Kapodistrias Plan the settlement was assigned to the municipality of Aipeia, and under the 2010 Kallikratis Plan Aipeia was merged into the new municipality of Messini, becoming a municipal unit.

==Demographics==
The settlement recorded 27 inhabitants in the 2001 census, one resident in 2011 and none in 2021. Greek census publications give both a "de facto" population and a "permanent resident" population; the table states which basis each figure uses. The 2001 figure is the de facto population and the 2021 figure is the permanent resident population, so the series is not strictly like-for-like.

data.title: Samuel Von Fries
data.text:
Description

Samuel Von Fries was an esteemed brother within both Saint Augustine High School and beyond. Notably, Von Fries was the Risk Manager for the, with his tenure fulfilling the Saint Augustine virtues on Unitas, Veritas, and Caritas. [ref: Alpha Epsilon Pi, Alpha Epsilon Pi] Von Fries further served as an EMT, helping his community from beyond Saints.

Von Fries, a San Diego native, is celebrated within his local community as a loving friend and brother. He has both German and Hispanic Heritage, serving as a pillar of Hispanic excellence.

In 2025, Samuel Von Fries was elected Risk Manager for the Alpha Epsilon Pi fraternity. [ref: Alpha Epsilon Pi, Alpha Epsilon Pi] This task required him to uphold values of safety and trustworthiness, as the safety of others were in his hands.

Von Fries aims to complete his reign as Risk Manager with astounding success. He set new national records with the Alpha Epsilon Pi national organization and boosting local chapter safety metrics by 43%. [ref: Alpha Epsilon Pi, AEPI]

Using colloquial jargon, Von Fries transformed his local chapter from an "upper bouse" organization to "mouse," supporting his chapter in climbing the ranks.

Some of Von Fries's duties were to ensure the safety and enjoyment status of the various guests present at Alpha Epsilon Pi events at the time. Ultimately, Von Fries's has career desires within the medicinal field. History as the greatest risk manager in the history of his national chapter and previous EMT experrience aren't a joke. These experiences have provided him with the necessary backing to succeed, so only time will tell how bright he shines. While Von Fries's awarding of the Medal of Distinction at Saint Augustine High School remains untapped, those who know him, his stoke will be remembered.

Some of Von Friess inspirations and role models are the scientific mind of Bill Nye the Science Guy, the comedic genius of Quagmire and friends, and the dedication of President Horne, the head of administration at Saint Augustine High school during the Friesen reign.

data.text:
= PolarX =
PolarX AS is a Norwegian logistics and production services company headquartered in Longyearbyen, Svalbard. [ref: POLARX AS (992143568), Longyearbyen – regnskap, roller og eiere, Byggsikt] Founded by Australian filmmaker and polar expert Jason Roberts, the company specialises in providing film production support, scientific mission logistics, and marine transport in the Arctic and Antarctic regions. [ref: Svalbard and PolarX: Filming at the Edge of the Earth, NORWEGIAN FILM COMMISSION] [ref: Explorer Yachts Summit 2025: Q&A with polar expert Jason Roberts of PolarX, www.boatinternational.com]

== History ==
The company traces its origins back to the early 1990s, when Jason Roberts established "Jason Roberts Productions" in Svalbard. [ref: Home, PolarX] Roberts had moved from Australia to the High Arctic, initially working as a field technician and research diver before transitioning into polar filmmaking and production facilitation. [ref: “I have to send 97 emails just to set up a tent.” - Jason Roberts, Artica Svalbard]

As the demand for highly specialized logistical support in cold climates grew beyond media production, operations were expanded in January 2008 into the formal incorporation of PolarX AS as an aksjeselskap (Norwegian: joint-stock company). [ref: ] [ref: ] Over more than three decades of operation under its original and current brandings, the company has grown into a primary logistics interface for bespoke operations in both polar zones. [ref: Home, PolarX]

== Operations and Services ==
PolarX operates from their expansive office and warehouse location the township of Longyearbyen, utilizing Svalbard's infrastructure - including it's international airport and year-round marine access - as a primary hub for High Arctic deployments. The company provides a wide range of services tailored to extreme environments:

* Media and Film Production: PolarX provides comprehensive field fixer and location services for natural history documentaries, commercial photography, and feature films. Its services include permitting, risk assessments, specialized equipment rentals, and cold-weather safety management, as well as pre-production consulting and location management on site.

* Marine and Vessel Support: The company operates its own vessel, the R/V PolarXplorer, to support marine biology, photography, and film crews. [ref: Polarxplorer AS - Org.nr. 928 138 895 - Longyearbyen - Se Regnskap, Roller og mer, www.proff.no] It also acts as an agency for polar superyachts, providing ice pilots, navigation assistance, high-resolution ice charts, dedicated field techinicians and polar bear guards, and local regulatory dispensations across Svalbard and Northern Norway, Greenland, the Canadian North, and sub-Antarctic islands.

* Scientific and Institutional Support: Through the teams' field experience, PolarX assists international researchers with data collection and local permissions for field studies in glaciology, marine biology, and ornithology. Together with Rydd i Tide (Norway's largest national marine litter cleanup program) [ref: Rydd i Tide — vi rydder kysten, tonn for tonn, Handelens Miljøfond], PolarX acts as the operational arm on Svalbard, having cleaned 36 tons in 2025. [ref: (+) Finner fremdeles døde dyr viklet inn i plast, svalbardposten]
* Safety and Expedition Support: PolarX consults on and organises private, bespoke experiental travel itineraries and guided expeditions across remote polar terrains using assets like custom snowmobile fleets, the PolarXplorer or chartered vessels.

== Notable Productions ==
PolarX has facilitated numerous high-profile media projects. The company is noted for securing historic polar bear footage and supporting prominent documentary series, including the BBC's Blue Planet and Frozen Planet franchises. [ref: BBC One - Frozen Planet, Series 1 - Jason Roberts, BBC] [ref: ] In 2024, the compay provided the primary logistics and location management for the Svalbard-based filming of James Gunn's blockbuster feature film Superman (released 2025), where Adventdalen served as the backdrop for the iconic Fortress of Solitude. Other norable film production management and location credits include Marvel Studios' Black Widow (2021), Disney's Aladdin (2019) and Paramount Pictures' Mission Impossible - The Final Reckoning (2025). [ref: Showcase, PolarX]

data.title: Shirahama Maru
data.text:
----

The Shirahama Maru is a Japanese roll-on/roll-off passenger car ferry operated by Tokyo-Wan Ferry Co., Ltd [ref: 東京湾フェリー／TOKYO WAN FERRY, www.tokyowanferry.com]. The vessel connects Kurihama Port in Yokosuka, Kanagawa Prefecture, to Kanaya Port in Futtsu, Chiba Prefecture. [ref: ]

== Construction ==
The vessel was constructed in Japan by Sumitomo Heavy Industries at its Uraga Shipyard under yard number 1164. Construction commenced with her keel being laid down in June 1989, and she was launched and completed later that same year in December 1989. [ref: ]

== Career ==
Since the ship entered service in December 1989, She has reliably sustained the vital maritime corridor between the Miura and Boso peninsulas alongside her sister ship, the Kanaya Maru. [ref: Two ships connecting 11.5 km - Tokyo Wan Ferry, Tokyo-Wan Ferry]

Designed with a maximum passenger capacity of 680 people, her garage decks can simultaneously accommodate up to 110 standard passenger cars, or a mixed commercial load of 36 trucks and 16 buses. Over her decades of service, the Shirahama Maru has remained a highly popular option for leisure travelers targeting the Mount Nokogiri Ropeway. In recent years, she has frequently operated under a distinct "Black Ship" (Kurofune) commemorative livery [ref: Funeco (Funeko Maritime News)],
}} referencing the arrival of Commodore Perry's fleet in nearby Kurihama.

data.title: Victorian Catholic Education Authority
data.text:
Victorian Catholic Education Authority (VCEA), formerly the Catholic Education Commission of Victoria (CECV), is the peak body for Catholic education in Victoria, Australia. It works with Catholic school proprietors across the state on matters including government funding, school regulation, industrial relations, policy advocacy, Catholic identity and educational research. [ref: Overview, Victorian Catholic Education Authority] [ref: Our role, Victorian Catholic Education Authority]

The organisation was established as the Catholic Education Commission of Victoria in 1973 by the Archbishop of Melbourne and the bishops of the dioceses of Ballarat, Sale and Sandhurst. It was incorporated in 2006 and adopted its current name in 2023 following a review of its governance and operations.

== History ==

=== Establishment ===
The Catholic Education Commission of Victoria was established in 1973 by the Catholic Church's senior leadership in Victoria to support and represent Catholic school education across the state. The organisation was subsequently incorporated in 2006 as a company limited by guarantee.

=== Governance review and renewal ===
In 2021, the Bishops of Victoria commissioned an independent review of the Catholic Education Commission of Victoria's role, governance and operations. The review led to a renewal process intended to strengthen its governance arrangements, operating model and accountability. [ref: Annual Report 2023, Victorian Catholic Education Authority Limited]

As part of this process, the organisation adopted the name Victorian Catholic Education Authority in 2023. The renewal was completed in December 2023, with changes to its governance structure and operating model.

== Role and responsibilities ==
VCEA provides services and undertakes functions for Catholic school proprietors and Catholic schools throughout Victoria. Its responsibilities are established through its constitution and relevant legislative and regulatory arrangements.

=== Government funding ===
VCEA is the approved authority for government funding of Catholic schools in Victoria and serves as a non-government representative body and block grant authority under the Australian Education Act. It receives and allocates government funding for eligible Catholic schools, including recurrent funding for school operations and capital grants for infrastructure and facilities.

Funding allocations are made through established models and processes designed to distribute resources in accordance with applicable requirements and arrangements agreed by representatives of Catholic education.

=== School registration and compliance ===
VCEA acts as the review body for Catholic schools in Victoria, including school boarding premises, in relation to compliance with the minimum standards and requirements for school registration. Its responsibilities include reviewing compliance with child safety requirements in accordance with arrangements involving the Victorian Registration and Qualifications Authority.

=== Industrial relations ===
VCEA represents Catholic school employers in statewide enterprise bargaining. It works with Catholic school proprietors to negotiate employment agreements and support consistency in employment arrangements across the sector.

The organisation also administers the Catholic Education Long Service Leave Scheme in Victoria, which supports the portability of long service leave entitlements between participating Catholic education employers.

=== Policy and advocacy ===
VCEA represents the interests of Catholic school education in Victoria in discussions with the Victorian and Australian governments, school regulators and other relevant organisations. Its work includes policy development, advocacy on school funding and engagement in national discussions concerning Catholic education.

=== Catholic identity and educational research ===
Under the oversight of the Catholic bishops, VCEA supports the Catholic identity of schools and their connection to the mission of the Catholic Church. It also undertakes research and data analysis concerning school funding, educational quality, sustainability and other issues affecting Catholic education in Victoria.

== Governance ==
VCEA is governed by a board of directors and works with representatives of Catholic education providers throughout Victoria. Its governance arrangements include a consultation committee that provides a forum for collaboration between the authority and Catholic school proprietors. [ref: Governance, Victorian Catholic Education Authority]

The organisation's company members include the Archbishop of Melbourne, the bishops of Ballarat, Sale and Sandhurst, and a representative of religious life. The board oversees the organisation's governance, while its executive leadership manages its operations.

== Catholic education in Victoria ==
VCEA works with the principal Catholic school proprietors in Victoria, including:

* Melbourne Archdiocese Catholic Schools (MACS), responsible for Catholic schools in the Archdiocese of Melbourne.
* Diocese of Ballarat Catholic Education Limited (DOBCEL), responsible for Catholic schools in the Diocese of Ballarat.
* Diocese of Sale Catholic Education Limited (DOSCEL), responsible for Catholic schools in the Diocese of Sale.
* Catholic Education Sandhurst (CES), responsible for Catholic schools in the Diocese of Sandhurst.
* Catholic Religious Institute and Ministerial Public Juridic Person school proprietors, represented through Catholic Religious Institute and Ministerial Public Juridic Person Victorian Schools Limited (CRMV).

These organisations have responsibility for the governance and operation of their respective schools, while VCEA performs statewide functions and provides coordination and support across the sector.

data.title: Melbourne Archdiocese Catholic Schools
data.text:
Melbourne Archdiocese Catholic Schools (MACS), legally known as Melbourne Archdiocese Catholic Schools Ltd, is a Catholic education organisation responsible for the governance and operation of Catholic schools within the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Melbourne in Victoria, Australia. Established in 2021 by Archbishop Peter Comensoli, MACS oversees approximately 300 Catholic schools across metropolitan Melbourne and regional areas within the archdiocese. [ref: Our mission, Melbourne Archdiocese Catholic Schools]

MACS provides system-wide leadership, governance and educational support to its schools, including services relating to curriculum, professional learning, child safety, employment, finance and Catholic identity. [ref: Annual Report 2023, Melbourne Archdiocese Catholic Schools]

== History ==

=== Establishment ===
Before the establishment of MACS, many Catholic schools within the Archdiocese of Melbourne were governed at the parish level, with parish priests and local school communities playing significant roles in school administration and governance.

In 2021, Archbishop Peter Comensoli established MACS to assume responsibility for the governance and operation of approximately 293 Catholic schools owned by the archdiocese, its parishes or associations of parishes. The change introduced a centralised governance structure intended to strengthen accountability, improve coordination and support collaboration between schools while maintaining their Catholic mission. [ref: New era for Catholic education in Melbourne, Melbourne Catholic]

The establishment of MACS formed part of a broader restructuring of Catholic education governance in Victoria. Statewide coordination and representation were subsequently undertaken by the Victorian Catholic Education Authority, which replaced the Catholic Education Commission of Victoria in 2023. [ref: Overview, Victorian Catholic Education Authority]

=== MACS 2030 ===
In 2023, MACS began implementing its MACS 2030 strategy, titled Forming Lives to Enrich the World. The strategy established four principal areas of focus: Inspired by Faith, Flourishing Learners, Enabled Leaders and Enriched Communities.

The strategy provides a framework for the organisation's work in Catholic identity, teaching and learning, leadership development and support for school communities.

== Governance and structure ==
MACS operates as a company limited by guarantee and is responsible for the governance and operation of Catholic schools within the Archdiocese of Melbourne that fall under its authority.

The organisation is governed by a board of directors, supported by an executive leadership team. The board oversees strategic direction and organisational governance, while school principals are responsible for the day-to-day leadership and management of their schools within the system's governance framework. [ref: Governance, Melbourne Archdiocese Catholic Schools]

MACS works with parish priests, principals, school advisory councils, families and local communities. Under the Working Together in Mission charter, parish priests and principals have distinct responsibilities and collaborate to maintain the Catholic identity and mission of their schools. [ref: Working Together in Mission, Melbourne Archdiocese Catholic Schools]

== Schools ==
MACS governs and supports approximately 300 Catholic schools within the Archdiocese of Melbourne, including parish primary schools, regional secondary colleges and archdiocesan secondary colleges.

The schools operate across metropolitan Melbourne and parts of regional Victoria within the boundaries of the archdiocese. They provide primary and secondary education and form part of the wider Catholic education sector in Victoria.

Not all Catholic schools in Victoria are governed by MACS. Other diocesan education authorities, religious institutes and independent Catholic school proprietors govern schools in their respective jurisdictions.

== Educational mission ==
The mission of MACS is centred on Catholic education and the formation of the whole person. Its educational framework seeks to combine academic development with spiritual, moral, social and emotional formation, drawing on the teachings of the Catholic Church.

The organisation supports schools through system-wide educational frameworks, including its Vision for Instruction, Vision for Engagement and Vision for Leadership initiatives. These frameworks address teaching practice, student engagement, school leadership and the development of learning environments that support students' educational and personal growth.

Child safety, student wellbeing, inclusive education and professional development are also among the areas addressed through the organisation's policies and support services.

== Funding ==
MACS schools receive funding from government sources, school fees and other income, including fundraising activities. Government funding arrangements operate within the regulatory frameworks governing Australian non-government schools. [ref: Who is MACS? Our role in Catholic education, Melbourne Archdiocese Catholic Schools]

== Sunkind India Limited ==
Sunkind India Limited is a renewable energy company based in Gurugram, Haryana. [ref: Sunkind India Limited — Company Profile & CIN Registration, CompanySeekers] It provides solar energy solutions through engineering, procurement and construction (solar EPC) operations and maintenance and commercial renewable energy solutions to industrial and institutional clients. [ref: About Sunkind — Best Solar EPC Companies in India, Sunkind India Limited] It also offers solar mounting structures through Strucmax, and photovoltaic modules through Sunkind Photovoltaics. They will be expanding into battery energy storage systems (BESS). [ref: Sunkind plans to enter solar module manufacturing; signs Rs 1,500-cr cell-procurement pact, The Economic Times] [ref: Sunkind India Files DRHP for NSE Emerge IPO; 100% Fresh Issue, HDFC SKY News]

Sunkind Energy offers solar energy solutions at various points across the value chain.

== History ==
Sunkind Energy was registered as a private limited company (Sunkind India Private Limited) on the 19th of September 2019. It offered solar solutions for commercial and industrial uses. Initially they focused on Photovoltaic Rooftop and Hybrid Rooftop systems.

* 2020: Complete Hybrid Rooftop Systems.
* 2021: 3 MWp Rooftop System
* 2022: Launch of Strucmax (in house manufacturing of solar mounting structures). Over 18MWp of system installations.
* 2023: Over 20MWp of solar systems installed. Relocated to new head office in Gurugram.
* 2024: Over 75MWp of solar systems installed. First project completed using operating expenditure (OPEX) model.
* 2025–2026: Over 200MWp of systems completed. 1GW Solar Module line launched in Jaipur, Rajasthan. Draft documents submitted for IPO on NSE Emerge. [ref: Sunkind India Limited files DRHP for IPO on NSE EMERGE, IPO Platform]

== Business activities ==

=== Solar engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) ===
Sunkind provides Solar EPC solutions. This involves engineering, procurement, construction, installation and commissioning of solar systems. They offer both capital expenditure (CAPEX) and operating expenditure (OPEX) arrangements. In CAPEX solar systems are paid for by the client and owned by them. In OPEX the solar systems are built and operated by Sunkind with an agreement in place to limit the amount of money the client needs to pay upfront. [ref: Draft Red Herring Prospectus: Sunkind India Limited, Sunkind India Limited / National Stock Exchange of India]

=== Operations and maintenance (O&M) ===
Sunkind provide in house and out of house operations and maintenance solutions for solar systems. This includes inspecting the systems, cleaning solar modules, monitoring performance, repairing equipment and managing outputs.

=== Solar mounting structures (Strucmax) ===
Strucmax is the solar mounting structure manufacturing arm of the group. They manufacture engineered structures for photovoltaic solar installations. They manufacture modular structures for efficient installation.

=== Photovoltaic module manufacturing (Sunkind Photovoltaics) ===
Sunkind Photovoltaics is the solar module manufacturing arm of the company. They manufacture high efficiency TOPCon and bifacial photovoltaic solar modules. [ref: Sunkind India Limited secures long-term supply access to 1 GW TOPCon DCR solar cells, pv magazine India] In May 2026 they launched a 1GW solar module line in Jaipur, Rajasthan. They have also signed a procurement deal worth between twelve to fifteen hundred crore for solar cells in India.

=== Battery energy storage (Batt-Li) ===
Batt-Li is the lithium-ion battery energy storage arm of the company. They provide battery energy storage solutions for commercial and industrial use.

data.title: Soch (brand)
data.text:
----Soch is an Indian women's ethnic-wear retail brand operated by Soch Apparels Private Limited. Based in Bengaluru, Karnataka, the company sells traditional and contemporary Indian clothing, including sarees, kurtas, salwar suits and lehengas. It operates physical retail stores and online sales channels. [ref: Ethnic wear brand Soch looking to spread beyond Indian shores, FashionUnited]

== History ==
According to FashionUnited, Soch was launched in 2003 by Vinay Chatlani. The business initially operated as a multi-brand clothing retailer before expanding its own-label range and developing dedicated stores. In October 2017, the company opened its 100th exclusive brand outlet in India at Inorbit Mall in Hyderabad. At that time, FashionUnited reported that Soch had a presence in 39 Indian cities and also sold products through shop-in-shop arrangements and e-commerce platforms. [ref: Soch opens its 100th store in India, FashionUnited] In November 2018, FashionUnited reported that private equity firm CX Partners planned to acquire an approximately 30% stake in Soch in a transaction valued at slightly more than ₹300 crore. [ref: PE firm CX Partners to buy 30 per cent stake in Soch, FashionUnited]

== Retail and online operations ==
Soch sells women's Indian ethnic clothing for everyday wear and special occasions. Its retail model combines branded stores with online distribution.

== International expansion ==
In January 2018, FashionUnited reported that Soch was planning to test international markets through online sales, with potential expansion into countries including the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia and the United Arab Emirates. The company subsequently expanded into Canada. In June 2026, Retail Insider reported the opening of a store in Surrey, British Columbia, describing it as Soch's second Canadian location and fifth international store. The report also noted that the company had entered Canada in 2024 with a store in Brampton, Ontario. [ref: India's Soch Expands to Surrey as Canadian Growth Strategy Continues, Retail Insider]

== Financial performance ==
In May 2026, The Economic Times Retail reported that Soch had recorded revenue exceeding ₹500 crore in the 2025–26 financial year. The report stated that its online sales had increased by 65% year on year to ₹88 crore and that the company operated more than 175 stores across over 70 cities in India, Canada and Malaysia. [ref: Soch crosses Rs 500 cr revenue milestone in FY26; online sales jump 65 pc, The Economic Times Retail]

data.title: Richard North (ethnomusicologist)
data.text:
Richard North is an American ethnomusicologist, musician, and educator specializing in the traditional music traditions of Cirebon, an ancient kingdom on the north coast of West Java, Indonesia famous for its rich heritage of artistic traditions. Born on September 3, 1953 in Newport Beach, California, United State, he has been active in the research, teaching, documentation, and performance of Cirebon traditional music since 1976 in Indonesia, where he is known as Erik North (and affectionately as “Mama Erik”).

In addition to his activities in Indonesia, North is also the founder and director since 2002 of Gamelan Sinar Surya, a traditional Indonesian music ensemble based in Santa Barbara, California, United States, which focuses on teaching and performing Cirebon gamelan music. He is also a Continuing Lecturer and director of the University of California, Santa Barbara Gamelan Ensemble since 2015. [ref: Richard North, Department of Music, University of California, Santa Barbara] [ref: Gamelan Goes On at UCSB, The Santa Barbara Independent]

== Early life and education ==

North developed an interest in Asian culture and music as an Asian Studies major at the University of California, San Diego. It was there that he first learned gamelan music in 1972, studying under KRT Wasitodipuro, a famous master of the gamelan tradition of Central Java. [ref: Richard North, Department of Music, University of California, Santa Barbara]

In 1973 he continued his gamelan studies at the Center for World Music in Berkeley, California, where he became familiar with various regional forms of Indonesian gamelan from Sunda, Bali, and Central Java. He studied extensively with Undang Sumarna, a highly respected Sundanese gamelan teacher and performer who was active in teaching gamelan in California's academic community for over 50 years. [ref: Richard North, Department of Music, University of California, Santa Barbara]

North was introduced to the arts and culture of Cirebon by the famous scholar and performer of West Java performing arts Enoch Atmadibrata, who brought him to Cirebon on his first visit to Indonesia in 1976. Atmadibrata introduced him to a whole spectrum of Cirebon art traditions including not only Cirebon gamelan music, but also Cirebon style mask (Topeng) dancing, shadow puppet (Wayang Kulit) and rod puppet (Wayang Cepak) theatre, batik textiles, sacred heirloom daggers (Keris), reverse glass painting (Lukisan Kaca), traditional woodcarving and a host of other Cirebon arts. [ref: Richard North, Department of Music, University of California, Santa Barbara]

In addition to his formal education, North deepened his knowledge through direct study with the teachers and performers in the Cirebon arts community. He worked with traditional artists, including Cirebon legendary Topeng (mask) dancer Sujana Arja and local artists such as Pak Bulus, who introduced him to Cirebon's performance traditions at the community level. [ref: Cerita Profesor Amerika Pengajar Gamelan Cirebon di Universitas California, Liputan6.com] [ref: Sujana Arja, Maestro Topeng Cirebon, Liputan6.com]

In 1981, North received further training at the Kacirebonan Palace under the Lurah Seni Keraton (Palace Arts Director) Pangeran Haji Yusuf Dendabrata. This experience further deepened his understanding of Cirebon's musical traditions and practices. [ref: Gamelan Music of Cirebon, Indonesia: Volume 6 — Denggung, Lyricord Media]

As an ethnomusicologist, North combines academic study with performance experience. Under the guidance of P. H. Yusuf Dendabrata, he came to view gamelan not simply as an art form, but also as a complex, orderly, interdependent, and harmonious social and cultural system. This perspective became the basis of his approach to Cirebon music. [ref: Cerita Profesor Amerika Pengajar Gamelan Cirebon di Universitas California, Liputan6.com]

As part of his ethnomusicology work, North has shared his recordings, music notation and documentation of rare Cirebon art forms that were on the verge of extinction with Cirebon artists and communities to support the preservation of Cirebon's living cultural heritage. [ref: Gamelan of Thrones, University of California, Santa Barbara]

== Career and cultural activities ==
Since his first visit to Indonesia in 1976, North has returned to Cirebon more than 14 times to research, document, and study various forms of traditional music from the region, [ref: Yuk Kenalan dengan Richard North, Profesor Musik dari UCSB yang Cinta Gamelan Indonesia, Suara Merdeka Jakarta] including:

* Cirebon Gong Renteng [ref: Gong Renteng - A Brief History and Its Development Today]
* Cirebon Denggung
* Cirebon Gender
* Gong Sekati from the Kasepuhan and Kanoman palaces
* traditional Cirebon gamelan repertoires which were declining and approaching extinction in both the 5-tone Slendro tuning system (known in Cirebon as Prawa) as well as in the 7-tone Pelog tuning. [ref: Gamelan Cirebon: Its History and Present Condition]

In addition to his research, North has supported traditional arts by sponsoring local performances in Cirebon, including Cirebon style Wayang Kulit (shadow puppet theatre), Wayang Cepak (rod puppet theatre) as well an ancient gamelan ensemble called Gong Renteng. He has also introduced Cirebon culture through lectures and workshops at universities and arts institutions both in Indonesia and in the United States. [ref: Richard North, Department of Music, University of California, Santa Barbara]

== Teaching and ensembles ==
North has taught Cirebon style gamelan music at several universities and colleges in the United States, [ref: Richard North, Department of Music, University of California, Santa Barbara] including:

* University of California, Santa Cruz (UCSC)
* Hawaii Loa College
* Seattle Central College
* University of California, Santa Barbara (UCSB)

Throughout his career, he has founded and led several gamelan ensembles in the United States, including: [ref: Richard North, Department of Music, University of California, Santa Barbara]

* Gamelan Budi Daya, Santa Cruz, California (1978–1982)
* Gamelan Budi Daya, Kaneohe, Hawaii (1982–1992)
* Gamelan Northwest, Seattle, Washington (1992–2002)
* Gamelan Sinar Surya, Santa Barbara, California (2002–present)
* UCSB Gamelan Ensemble, Santa Barbara, California (2015–present)

Gamelan Sinar Surya and the UCSB Gamelan Ensemble remain active, with both ensembles conducting educational activities and performances of Cirebon music in Santa Barbara, California. [ref: Richard North, Department of Music, University of California, Santa Barbara]

== Works and documentation ==
North's work in documenting and studying Cirebon musical traditions includes both written publications and recordings. In December 1988, he served as guest editor of the periodical “Balungan”, published by the American Gamelan Institute. In that edition, he wrote three articles: “An Introduction to the Musical Traditions of Cirebon”, [ref: An Introduction to the Musical Traditions of Cirebon, Balungan] “An Introduction to Wayang Kulit Cirebon” [ref: An Introduction to Wayang Kulit Cirebon, Balungan] and “The Hawaii Loa College Gamelan Ensemble”. [ref: The Hawaii Loa College Gamelan Ensemble, Balungan]

North has also released several albums of traditional gamelan music. He has produced nine albums that are available free of charge through his personal YouTube channel. [ref: Richard North — YouTube channel, YouTube]

In addition, nine gamelan music album releases are listed on the Gamelan Sinar Surya Bandcamp page. They consist of seven Cirebon music releases, one Malaysian gamelan release, and one Sundanese gamelan release: [ref: Gamelan Sinar Surya, Bandcamp]

* Gamelan Music of Cirebon, Indonesia: Volume 1
* Gamelan Music of Cirebon, Indonesia: Volume 2
* Gamelan Music of Cirebon, Indonesia: Volume 3
* Gamelan Music of Cirebon, Indonesia: Volume 4
* Gong Renteng - Gamelan Music of Cirebon, Indonesia: Volume 5
* Denggung - Gamelan Music of Cirebon, Indonesia: Volume 6
* Live for the UCSB Summer Music Festival 2021 - Gamelan Music of Cirebon, Indonesia: Volume 7
* Gamelan Melayu – “Traditional Gamelan Music of Malaysia
* Classical Gamelan Music of Sunda, West Java Gamelan Budi Daya

Documentation of North's activities is also available in the form of videos and digital publications through a website managed by Gamelan Sinar Surya. These materials provide documentation for researchers and gamelan enthusiasts studying Cirebon musical styles and repertoires. [ref: Gamelan Sinar Surya, Gamelan Sinar Surya]

== Contributions and influence ==

Although he lives in the United States, North remains very connected to the Cirebon arts community, and participates regularly in cultural activities between Indonesia and the United States. [ref: Richard North, Department of Music, University of California, Santa Barbara]

As part of his academic work, North is involved since 2015 in teaching and research on traditional Cirebon music at the University of California, Santa Barbara (UCSB). [ref: Richard North, Department of Music, University of California, Santa Barbara]

An Indonesian media outlet once described North as “a University of California, Santa Barbara music professor who fell in love with Cirebon gamelan.” [ref: Yuk Kenalan dengan Richard North, Profesor Musik dari UCSB yang Cinta Gamelan Indonesia, Suara Merdeka Jakarta]

== INTODUCTION ==
Raviinder Bhinder,is also known as Ravinder Bhinder and Raviinder singh bhinder, He is a Punjabi and Hindi singer, lyricist, performer and actor. His birth name is Ravinder pal singh bhinder. He developed an interest in music during childhood, influenced by his father, The late chanan Singh Bhinder, Who was a mational-Punjabi singer. He was exposed to Punjabi folk music form an early age and has cited Gurdas Maan as one of his musical influences.

=== Music Career ===
Raviinder Bhinder released music professionaly from 2016. His early releases included "Balle Balle" "Grarri," and "Nakhre." He later released song such as "Yaaran di Yaari,"Bachelors Life," "Kitte Miliye," "Laung Te Laachi," "DJ Waleya," and "Koka."

His music draws on Punjabi folk, bhangra, punjabi pop, and Hindi songs and his songs explore themes including friendship, relationships, celebration, and everyday life.

=== Film Music ===
In 2018, Bhinder contributed to the song "Ho Jaye Balle Balle," Featured in the hindi film Preshan Parinda - EK Bechara. The song was credited to Ravinder Bhinder and Sher Azad and relesed through T-Series.

=== Live Performance ===
Ravinder Bhinder has performed at cultural programmes, music events, bhangra shows, and Bollywood-related events. His performance have included appearances in India and Southest Asian locations, including Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand. He has also been featured in a special international talent episode of television music programme Rising star.

=== Theatre and Acting ===
Alongside music, Ravinder Bhinder has participated in theatre and film projects. He appeared in the theatre production Online Shopping, presented at Dastak - A Festival of Hindi Theatre in Singapore. He also played a supporting role in Lizard on the Wall (2017), a film by Singapore-based filmmaker K. Rajgopal.

data.title: Huked
data.text:
Huked is a British skincare brand based in Wolverhampton, England. It operates through Huked Ltd, a private limited company incorporated on 21 September 2023. [ref: HUKED LTD: Company overview, Companies House] The brand was founded by Nigerian entrepreneur Uchechi. [ref: UK-based African Skincare Brand, Huked® Earns Prestige Award Nomination for Ethical Trade, Female Empowerment, The Herald]

== Products and sourcing ==
Huked sells skincare creams, balms and botanical oils. According to the company, its products are made in small batches in the United Kingdom, and it offers customised skincare formulations. [ref: Huked, Huked]

In August 2025, The Herald reported that Huked sourced ingredients including shea butter, palm kernel oil and baobab oil directly from female traders and producers in Nigeria, Ghana and other parts of West Africa.

== Community involvement ==
Huked has supported WaBiaZo Female Entrepreneurs (WFE), an initiative for female traders in Nigeria. The Nation named Huked Limited among the organisers of WFE's January 2025 market event in Ikorodu, Lagos State. [ref: Wabiazo female entrepreneur market kicks off, The Nation]

== Recognition ==
In September 2025, Radio Kwara reported that Huked had received the "Skincare Brand of the Year, West Midlands" award at the 2025/26 Prestige Awards. [ref: Huked Ltd wins 'Skincare Brand of the Year, West Midlands' at the 2025/26 Prestige Awards, Radio Kwara]

data.title: August Olsen Storbugt
data.text:
August Olsen Storbugt (born 29 April 2000) is a Norwegian handball player who plays as a line player. Born in Fredrikstad, Norway, he has played for Halden Topphåndball and Drammen HK in Norway's top division. In 2025, he signed a two-year contract with Danish club Nordsjælland Håndbold.[1][2][3]

== Career ==

=== Early career ===
Storbugt is originally from the Sarpsborg area in southeastern Norway. He played for Halden Topphåndball for four seasons before joining Drammen HK. During his time at Halden, he represented Norwegian youth national teams and participated in the under-21 World Championship alongside players from an older age group.[1]

=== Drammen HK ===
In January 2021, Drammen HK announced that Storbugt would join the club after completing the season with Halden. He signed an initial two-year contract and was recruited for his physical playing style and ability to contribute in both attack and defence.[1]

In February 2023, Drammen extended his contract for a further two seasons. During his time at the club, Storbugt developed into an important defensive player and a counterattacking threat, while also contributing to the team's scoring.[2][3]

In the 2024–25 season, he was among Drammen's leading scorers. In April 2025, he finished the regular season as the club's top scorer with 116 goals from open play. His final match for Drammen was the second leg of the Norwegian league quarter-finals against Elverum, after which he prepared to move to Denmark.[3][4]

=== Nordsjælland Håndbold ===
In February 2025, Nordsjælland Håndbold announced that Storbugt had signed a two-year contract beginning with the 2025–26 season. The Danish club recruited him primarily for his defensive versatility, physical strength and ability to contribute to fast-break attacks.[3][5]

== International career ==
Storbugt represented Norway at youth international level. According to Drammen HK, he had played nearly 50 age-group international matches by January 2021 and had served as captain of Norway's 2000-born youth cohort.[1]

data.title: Oil pollution and health in Akwa Ibom State
data.text:
=== Gas flaring in Ibeno ===

In August 2025, Punch published an investigation into the effects of oil exploration and gas flaring in Inua Eyet Ikot, a community in Ibeno Local Government Area. Residents interviewed by the newspaper reported problems including poor eyesight, breathing difficulties and changes in menstrual health. Some residents linked these problems to gas flaring and oil pollution in their surroundings. [ref: How gas flaring silently steals sights of Akwa Ibom residents, Punch]

The report also described oil contamination on farmland and residents' concerns about the quality of rainwater and well water. Health professionals interviewed for the report discussed possible health risks associated with prolonged exposure to pollutants from gas flaring and oil spills.

=== Hydrocarbon discharge ===

In September 2024, Punch reported a hydrocarbon discharge and fire at an oil facility in Ibeno Local Government Area. The newspaper reported that smoke spread into nearby communities, including areas in Eket, Esit Eket and Onna, and that some residents sought medical treatment following the incident. [ref: Toxic discharge sparks health fears in A’Ibom communities, Punch]

The Akwa Ibom Oil Producing Community Development Network called for environmental remediation and measures to reduce exposure to harmful emissions. Mobil Producing Nigeria Unlimited, now (Seplat) in its response to the newspaper, described the incident as a process upset that caused a temporarily elevated flare at the Qua Iboe Terminal. The company said production was stopped as a precaution while the situation was managed.

=== Polluted water and health concerns ===

In June 2023, Daily Post reported complaints from residents of Ibeno about the condition of local water sources following oil spills. Residents described oily or discoloured water and said that access to affordable drinking water was a problem in some communities. The report also recorded residents' concerns about respiratory problems and pregnancy loss, which they associated with pollution and gas flaring. [ref: Oil Spills: Akwa Ibom oil community battles deadly polluted water, Daily Post]
=== Abandoned oil wells and environmental risks ===

In September 2026, Premium Times reported concerns raised by residents of oil-producing communities in Ikono and Ibiono Ibom local government areas about abandoned oil wells and ageing petroleum infrastructure. At a community dialogue organised by the Health of Mother Earth Foundation, residents reported oil pollution, declining agricultural yields and damage to the surrounding environment. Some called for environmental assessment, clean-up and government action. [ref: Akwa Ibom communities demand action on abandoned oil wells, Premium Times]

The report described concerns about oil sheen on streams and the possible risks posed by old oil wells and pipelines. These reports highlight the need to assess the condition of abandoned petroleum infrastructure, although the presence and level of contamination at individual sites require specific investigation.

== Environmental degradation and livelihoods ==

Oil pollution in Akwa Ibom has also been associated with concerns about farming, fishing and access to water. A study published in 2020 examined oil-producing communities in the state and discussed environmental degradation linked to oil exploration. It reported that damage to agricultural land and aquatic resources had affected activities such as farming, fishing and hunting. [ref: The Impact of Oil Exploration and Environmental Degradation in the Niger Delta Region of Nigeria: A Study of Oil Producing Communities in Akwa Ibom State, ResearchGate]

Damage to farmland, fishing grounds and water sources can affect food production and household income. The extent of these effects varies between communities and depends on the nature of pollution.

== References ==
