data.title: Geir G. Greni
data.text:
Geir G. Greni (born 29 October 1970) is a Norwegian filmmaker, journalist, author and musician. He founded the production company Snurr Film AS. His work includes the feature films Umeå4ever (2011) and All Must Die (Alle må dø, 2020), the crime novel Jeg ser død (2019), and a series of short films.

== Journalism ==

Greni began his career as a journalist and television presenter for NRK. He has written for publications including Morgenbladet, Mann and Filmmagasinet, and has reviewed films for NRK P1.

== Short film career ==

During the late 1990s and early 2000s, Greni wrote, directed and produced a series of short films, including Afterwards (Etter filmen), Party, Que Serà, Serà, Xercise, The Part (Rolle) and Together (Sammen).

His short film Afterwards (Etter filmen, 1999) was written by Greni and Morten Abrahamsen. The Norwegian Federation of Film Societies praised the film's casting and dialogue, describing it as "a simple and brilliant film". [ref: [https://filmklubb.no/wp/film/etter-filmen/ "Etter filmen"], Norwegian Federation of Film Societies.]

The Norwegian Film Archive has described Greni's short films as humorous works characterised by psychological insight, and in a 2006 presentation described him as "one of the most talented contemporary Norwegian short film directors". [ref: [https://filmarkivet.no/content/news/article.aspx?id=1193 "Que sera sera"], Filmarkivet.no, 11 July 2006.]

In 2002, Que Serà, Serà, directed and produced by Greni from a screenplay by Bård Breien, won the Jameson Short Film Award at the Norwegian Short Film Festival in Grimstad.

The film subsequently appeared in the Jameson Short Film Awards programme presented during the 42nd Semaine Internationale de la Critique at the Cannes Film Festival in 2003. [ref: [https://www.semainedelacritique.com/uploads/edition/6032c000578a195c81a3fd781e95e769.pdf "Jameson Short Film Awards 2002"], Semaine Internationale de la Critique, Cannes 2003.]

== Feature films ==

Greni made his feature-film debut as writer, director and producer with Umeå4ever, released theatrically in 2011. In a commentary devoted to Greni and the film, author Erlend Loe called Umeå4ever "perhaps the bravest film project of the year".

Kristin Aalen of Stavanger Aftenblad wrote that Greni "lifts the comedy several notches above the predictable romantic stories of which dozens have been made", and highlighted his handling of the balance between caricature and seriousness as well as the film's dramaturgy. [ref: [https://www.aftenbladet.no/kultur/i/KlgzG/god-komedie-om-myk-mann Kristin Aalen, "God komedie om myk mann"], Stavanger Aftenblad, 1 April 2011.]

In 2020, Greni released the horror feature All Must Die (Alle må dø), written by Greni and Robert Næss. Greni directed and produced the film.

Cinema described the film as "a solid genre film that appeals to a young audience – and delivers", and highlighted its approach to the slasher genre. [ref: [https://cine.no/2020/03/05/alle-ma-do-utdrikningslaget-fra-helvete/ "Alle må dø – utdrikningslaget fra helvete"], Cinema, 5 March 2020.]

== Writing ==

Greni made his literary debut with the crime novel Jeg ser død, published by Vega Forlag in 2019. [ref: [https://booksfromnorway.com/books/1782-i-see-death "I See Death"], Books From Norway.]

Fædrelandsvennen described the novel as "remarkably good" ("oppsiktsvekkande god"), highlighting its plot, central characters and Greni's visual approach to storytelling.

Alongside his own productions, Greni has worked as a script doctor and script consultant, including on the NRK comedy series Hubert.

== Music ==

Greni is the lead singer, guitarist and songwriter of the band Norwegian Modesty. The band released the EP Happy Now and the album Mediocrity Rules in 2011.

Norwegian Modesty contributed music to the soundtrack of Umeå4ever, which was released as a separate soundtrack album in 2011. The band's music was later also used in All Must Die.

Greni has written, directed and produced music videos for Minor Majority, Superfamily and Norwegian Modesty.

== Acting ==

As an actor, Greni has appeared in both his own and other productions. He played one of the four leading roles in the stage production Papagayaekspressen by Torstein Bieler and Lars Kilevold.

He also starred in the short film Neon, directed by Simen Alsvik, which Greni produced. In addition, he has written and performed in comedy productions for NRK and appeared in an NRK radio drama production.

data.title: Kirk T. McDonald
data.text:
----

Kirk T. McDonald is an American experimental physicist who works in high-energy physics and strong-field quantum electrodynamics. He is a professor emeritus in the Department of Physics at Princeton University.

== Biography ==

=== Education ===
McDonald studied at the University of Arizona, earning a Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree in physics in 1966. He completed his PhD in experimental high-energy particle physics at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech) in 1972, under the supervision of Clemens A. Heusch. [ref: Inelastic Photoproduction of Pi Mesons from Hydrogen and Deuterium at Energies Between 1.3 and 1.8 GeV, Caltech / ProQuest Dissertations]

=== Academic career ===
From 1973 to 1975, he was a postdoctoral Fellow at CERN in Geneva, and subsequently worked as a researcher at the Enrico Fermi Institute at the University of Chicago.

In 1976, he joined the faculty of Princeton University as an assistant professor. He was granted tenure in 1980 and conducted his research at the Joseph Henry Laboratories. [ref: Kirk McDonald's Research Interests, Princeton University] He later became a professor emeritus.

== Research and contributions ==
McDonald's research involves experimental programs in particle physics and detector development.

=== Strong-field quantum electrodynamics (QED) ===
In the 1990s, he led the SLAC E-144 experiment at the Stanford Linear Accelerator Center (SLAC). This experiment studied the production of matter from light-by-light collisions (the nonlinear Breit–Wheeler process) by colliding a 46.6 GeV electron beam with a picosecond laser pulse, [ref: Observation of Nonlinear Effects in Compton Scattering, Physical Review Letters] providing data for predictions in strong-field quantum electrodynamics. [ref: Positron Production in Multiphoton Light-by-Light Scattering, Physical Review Letters]

=== Neutrino physics ===
McDonald has participated in several neutrino and CP violation experiments:
* He was a member of the Daya Bay Reactor Neutrino Experiment in China, which measured the neutrino mixing angle θ13. [ref: Observation of Electron-Antineutrino Disappearance at Daya Bay, Physical Review Letters] As a member of this collaboration, he shared the 2016 Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics. [ref: Laureates: Daya Bay Collaboration, Breakthrough Prize]
* He worked on the BaBar experiment at SLAC, which studied CP violation in B meson decays. [ref: Observation of CP Violation in the $B^0$ Meson System, Physical Review Letters]
* He has contributed to research regarding neutrino factories, targetry for muon production, [ref: High-Power Targets for Muon (and Neutrino) Production, arXiv] and the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE).

=== Electromagnetism physics notes ===
McDonald maintains a collection of educational problems and technical notes in classical electromagnetism. He has authored over 1,200 scientific notes addressing physics problems related to Maxwell's equations, radiation reaction forces, and the dynamics of relativistic charges.

== Awards ==
* 2016: Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics (as part of the Daya Bay collaboration).

== Selected publications ==

* Kirk T. McDonald, The Relation Between Expressions for Time-Dependent Electromagnetic Fields Given by Jefimenko and by Panofsky and Phillips, Joseph Henry Laboratories, Princeton University (1996; updated 2018).
* Kirk T. McDonald, On the History of the Radiation Reaction, Princeton University (2017).
* Kirk T. McDonald, On the “Helmholtz” Decomposition, Joseph Henry Laboratories, Princeton University (2023).

data.title: Tokmac Ruben
data.text:
Tokmac Ruben, also known as Tom Ruben (born 14 June 2006) is an Australian entrepreneur and talent manager based in Melbourne, Victoria. He is the founder of Dominance Media.

== Early life ==
Tokmac Ruben was born on 14 June 2006 in Kampala, Uganda. He is of South Sudanese heritage, originally from Rumbek. He moved to Australia in 2007 and grew up in Melbourne, Victoria.

== Career ==
Ruben began his entrepreneurial journey at the age of 18, establishing a business in the healthcare sector before expanding into digital media and talent management.

He subsequently founded Dominance Media, a talent management venture focused on representing digital creators and developing commercial opportunities across social media, entertainment and brand partnerships.

Through Dominance Media, Ruben works with social media creators with audiences numbering in the millions. His work involves developing relationships between creators and brands, pursuing commercial partnerships and helping talent explore opportunities beyond content creation.

His professional interests span talent management, entrepreneurship, digital media and investment, with a focus on building long-term commercial relationships within the creator economy.

data.title: Barrett Business Services
data.text:
Barrett Business Services, Inc. (BBSI) is an American professional employer organization (PEO) headquartered in Vancouver, Washington. The company provides payroll, human resources, workers' compensation coverage, and related administrative services to small and mid-sized businesses through a co-employment arrangement, and also operates a staffing business. It is listed on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol BBSI.

The company traces its origins to a temporary-staffing business founded in Baltimore in 1951 and was incorporated in Maryland in 1965. It became a public company through an initial public offering on the Nasdaq in June 1993. The company reported revenue of $1.14 billion for 2024.

== History ==
The business that became Barrett Business Services was founded in Baltimore in 1951 by Nancy Barrett, who operated a temporary-help office there for about two decades. The company was incorporated in Maryland in 1965, and in 1971 it merged with Barry Temporary Services, a Portland, Oregon, temporary-employment firm led by William W. Sherertz, who became president of the combined company. BBSI became publicly traded through an initial public offering on the Nasdaq in June 1993. Sherertz led the company until his death in 2011; he was succeeded as chief executive by Michael Elich, and in 2020 by Gary Kramer.

== Operations ==
BBSI operates primarily as a professional employer organization, entering into a client services agreement to establish a co-employment relationship with each client company and assuming responsibility for payroll, payroll taxes, workers' compensation coverage, and certain other administrative functions. It reports its services in two categories, professional employer services and staffing. In a 2024 interview, chief executive Gary Kramer said the company operated in 68 markets and that its average client employed about 26 people.

data.title: Leif Halvorsen
data.text:
= Leif Halvorsen =
Leif Christian Halvorsen (born July 20, 1954) is an incarcerated individual whose convictions include three counts of murder and retaining a concealed deadly weapon. [ref: ]

== Crimes ==
In January 1983, in Lexington, Kentucky, Halvorsen and his accomplice, Mitchell Willoughby, shot Joe Norman, Joey Durrum, and Jacqueline Greene to death while under the influence of painkillers, cocaine, and marijuana. The event took place at Jacqueline Greene's residency, where she and Joe Norman resided. [ref: Halvorsen v. Com. (Ky. 1987), Justia Law]

In July 1983, the Fayette Circuit Court tried Halvorsen and Willoughby for their involvement in the triple homicide of Norman, Durrum, and Greene. During this trial, Mitchell Willoughby took all the blame for the shootings. However, upon the court's consideration of Halvorsen and Willoughby making errors in their assertions, it was determined that both were to blame for the shootings. On September 15th, 1983, Halvorsen and Mitchell Willoughby were convicted for three counts of murder. Leif Halvorsen's charges included a death sentence for the killing of Greene and Durrum and a life sentence for the killing of Norman. In addition, Halvorsen was convicted for retaining a concealed deadly weapon, which led to him being sentenced to twelve months' imprisonment as well as being fined $500. [ref: Halvorsen v. Com. (Ky. 1987), Justia Law]

In Kentucky, lower courts are required to have their death penalty rulings appealed to the Kentucky Supreme Court for confirmation. Thus, on July 2nd, 1987, the Kentucky Supreme Court confirmed the Fayette Circuit Court's decision for Halvorsen and Willoughby's death penalties. [ref: Halvorsen v. Com. (Ky. 1987), Justia Law]

== Administrative Exception ==
On December 21st, 2001, in a memo from Warden Parker of Kentucky State Penitentiary, Parker provided his rationale on why Halvorsen would be a benefit to the Kentucky Department of Correction's Youth Awareness Program. Due to security risks, the Kentucky State Penitentiary did not typically allow death-row inmates to serve on the Youth Awareness Program's panel. In the same memo, Parker clarified that he made an exception for Halvorsen to serve as a panel member for the Youth Awareness Program due to his consideration of a variety of factors such as Halvorsen's remorse for his actions and his persistent intent in preventing future generations from being incarcerated. As a consequence, Halvorsen became the first and only death-sentenced inmate in the history of the Kentucky Department of Corrections to be allowed to participate in its Youth Awareness Program. In the following years, numerous memos detailed accounts of individuals benefitting from Halvorsen's advocacy efforts. [ref: Application for Executive Clemency for Leif Halvorsen]

== Appeals ==

=== Halvorsen v. Parker (2012) ===
In 2012, Halvorsen filed a motion to amend his writ of habeas corpus in order to assert eleven new claims. For these eleven claims, Halvorsen contended that during his state post-conviction proceedings, there was an ineffective assistance of counsel, in which his post-conviction counsel failed to acknowledge that the trial counsel in his original defense had failed to raise questions for several unconstitutional claims used against him. On November 19th, 2012, the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Kentucky denied Halvorsen's motion to amend his petition for his writ of habeas corpus. The rationale behind this decision was that three years prior, Halvorsen had the ability to assert ineffective assistance of counsel when he filed his original petition, and how amending this petition would have been unfairly prejudicial to the current defendants who worked on the case as well as presenting an unnecessary delay for the proceedings. [ref: Halvorsen v. Parker]

=== Halvorsen v. White (2018) ===
In 2018, Halvorsen petitioned for a writ of habeas corpus, in which he claimed that trial court error, ineffective assistance of counsel, and prosecutorial and juror misconduct violated his constitutional rights. On August 20th, 2018, due to the Kentucky Supreme Court presenting reasonable evidence corroborating their justifications, the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit denied Halvorsen appeal. [ref: HALVORSEN v. WHITE (2018), FindLaw]

=== Halvorsen v. Commonwealth of Kentucky (2023) ===
In 2023, Halvorsen requested for post-conviction relief, claiming that the jury instructions used for his original convictions were biased in suggesting that the jury act on the account of a combined decision, thus rendering the final verdict as non-unanimous. On March 23, 2023, Kentucky's Supreme Court denied Halvorsen appeal. The rationale behind this decision was that cases at bar were final and upon elaborating on CR 60.02 and CR 60.03, clarified that those rules prohibit a defendant to circumvent the time limitations of a RCr 11.42 motion. In addition, the Supreme Court of Kentucky utilized Teague v. Lane to determine that the Teague rule cannot be applied retroactively on collateral review to convictions finalized prior to 2010. [ref: Halvorsen v. Commonwealth (Ky. 2023), Justia Law]

== Executive Clemency ==
On November 25th, 2019, David M. Barron, counsel for Leif Halvorsen, submitted an application for Halvorsen's executive clemency. According to Halvorsen's clemency petition, after his marriage ended, he developed a drug addiction, and despite numerous attempts for rehabilitation, he continually relapsed. Eventually, this drug addiction culminated in Halvorsen being under the influence of multiple drugs when he committed a triple homicide in January 1983. In his application, Barron provided examples of Halvorsen's reform such as his commitment to his own family, earning multiple academic degrees, and his advocacy which included mentoring at-risk youth and providing spiritual counseling for his other inmates. [ref: Application for Executive Clemency for Leif Halvorsen]

On December 9th, 2019, former Kentucky Governor Matt Bevin granted executive clemency to Halvorsen, commuting his sentence to life with the possibility of parole. In his statement for Halvorsen, Bevin wrote, “Leif has a powerful voice that needs to be heard by more people.” [ref: Kentucky Governor Matt Bevin Grants Clemency to Two Death Row Prisoners, www.americanbar.org]

== Societal Response to Halvorsen ==

=== Executive Clemency ===
Barbara Barber, aunt to one of Leif Halvorsen's victims, Joey Durrum, criticized former Kentucky Governor Matt Bevin in providing executive clemency for Halvorsen. When Barber heard that Halvorsen had a possibility of parole, she provided comments directed at Halvorsen, saying, "I never wanted execution for you and Willoughby, I just wished you lived a long life right there in prison. We took care of you for 37 years, the state, 37 more wouldn't have bothered me, but you don't deserve the right to walk free." [ref: Family: Man taken off death row after ’83 triple homicide ‘doesn’t deserve the right to walk free’, https://www.wkyt.com]

== References ==

data.title: Aki Hayakawa
data.text:
Aki Hayakawa (Japanese: 早川 アキ) is a fictional character from Tatsuki Fujimoto's manga series Chainsaw Man. Aki was a main character at the first part of the manga, and appeared as a professional devils hunter. Aki is voiced by Shogo Sakata in Japanese, and by Reagan Murdock in English. [ref: Aki Hayakawa, Behind The Voice Actors]

== Creation ==

Aki's Japanese name is written as "早川 アキ", where "アキ" uses katakana instead of the kanji "秋". Fujimoto has revealed that the origin of the name "アキ" has two layers. One is from the "Gun Fiend" form he ultimately turns into, where his arm becomes like an AK-47 assault rifle, taking its homophone "AKi". The other is representing the "空き" (Aki), meaning emptiness, hollowness. [ref: Analyzing "Chainsaw Man"'s Aki Hayakawa (早川アキ) from Japanese: The Tragedy Behind the Name and the Charm of "Kon", ANIHK] Hayakawa "早川" which consists of the characters for “already; now; by this time” and “river". [ref: Things You Didn't Know About Aki From Chainsaw Man, CBR]

Some concept art of what seems to be Aki, which shown on one of Tatsuki Fujimoto's alternate accounts, shows him with a slightly different older design with differences such as scars on his face. And there is a scrapped idea was that Himeno was going to be Aki's younger sister who would have lived longer. It was revealed that Aki's hairstyle is due to the nature of his contract with the Fox Devil. [ref: Chainsaw Man Creator Reveals the Secret Behind Aki's Top Knot Hairstyle, CBR]

=== Casting ===
Aki's role, played by Shogo Sakata, was Sakata's first major role in his acting career. Reagan Murdock, Aki's English voice actor, described Aki and said: “[Aki] is normally so very under control and he has such a firm... well, what he thinks is a firm grasp on his emotions when really he's just pushing his emotions down until they come exploding out". [ref: INTERVIEW: Chainsaw Man English Voice Actors for Denji and Aki Discuss What Makes a Good Dream, Crunchyroll news]

In an interview about Chainsaw Man – The Movie: Reze Arc, Sakata said that: "Aki Hayakawa had always been a part of me, so it didn't take long to get back into character. During the exchanges with Nomo, I received direction to "add a bit more familiarity," which was nice as it allowed me to explore new aspects of his character", and he also talked about his experience with Nomo, who voiced by Kenji Akabane-san, describing it as revealing a new side of Aki. [ref: "Chainsaw Man - The Movie: Reze Arc" Interview: Cast Discusses Aki's New Side, Makima's Unsettling Aura, and Denji's Summer Experience, Japan Wire by Kyodo News]

== Appearances ==
Aki is a tall man with blue eyes and medium-length black hair that he pulls back in topknot style. He has a serious, cold, and intelligent personality. He intensely hates devils, including those he contracts with within the organization, and advocates killing them mercilessly if they try to escape or betray the organization. However, he also harbors a kind and gentle side towards those he loves. Aki was born in Hokkaido to a family of his father, mother, and younger brother—who were all killed in a Gun Devil attack that completely destroyed their home. This instilled in Aki a deep hatred for devils from a young age. Aki joined the Public Safety Organization, where he met Himeno, his first colleague and close friend. Himeno, who harbored romantic feelings for Aki, tried to persuade him to resign from his job to save his life, but he refused. Aki treats Himeno as a close friend rather than a lover. Through Himeno, Aki was introduced to the world of smoking. [ref: Chainsaw Man, Viz Media]

With Denji's arrival, Makima asks Aki to look after him. Initially, Aki is harsh with Denji for his recklessness and lack of seriousness in his work as a devil hunter. [ref: Chainsaw Man, Viz Media] He tells Denji to quit his job to save his life and even threatens to kill him without hesitation if he betrays them or sides with other devils. However, as the story progresses, the two begin to form a friendship. Denji and Power live with Aki, and he treats them like that he is their older brother. After Himino sacrifices herself to save him from a Katana Man's attack, Aki is devastated. He quits smoking out of grief for Himino, but he refuses to resign, driven by his desire to avenge his family and Himino. As the story unfolds, Aki begins a friendship with Angel Devil and loses his arm in a battle with Darkness Devil. Aki's primary goal is to avenge his family and Himino. However, as the confrontation with the Gun Devil draws near, the Future Devil shows Aki a glimpse of the future, where he witnesses Denji and Power suffering a horrific and painful death. [ref: Chainsaw Man, Viz Media] This compels him to ask to withdraw the Public Safety Division 4's Devil Hunters from the upcoming battle with the Gun Devil to save their lives, even though killing the Gun Devil was his ultimate objective.

Devastated and desperate, Aki begs Makima to make a deal with any devil to spare Denji and Power's lives. [ref: Chainsaw Man, Viz Media] Makima, however, demands that he makes a deal with her, much to his shock. During the Gun Devil's attack, and through Makima's manipulation, the Gun Devil possesses Aki's body. A battle ensues between Denji and Aki, who is now controlled by the Gun Devil, ending with Aki's death. In his will, Aki bequeaths half of his savings to Denji and Power, and the other half to the Himino's family. Aki's death had a significant psychological impact on Denji and Power.

== Reception ==
[[File:Cosplay Contest at Copenhagen Sakura Festival 2026 08.jpg|thumb|150px|Cosplay of Aki in Copenhagen 2026]]
Brett Cardaro from Comic Book Resources considered Aki to be "the Chainsaw Man's Best Character", listing several reasons for this, like saving Denji and Angel Devil, and his realtion with his friends. [ref: Why Aki Hayakawa is Chainsaw Man's Best Character, CBR] Louis Kemner from Comic Book Resources considered Aki to be "a Better Kind of Anime Tsundere", and suggesting that he was a conventional tsundere, but became one of the best tsunderes who made the most of the tried and tested archetype by the end. [ref: Who Is Aki In Chainsaw Man?, CBR] Briana Lawrence from Crunchyroll praised Aki's morning routine, calling it one of his favorite moments in Chainsaw Man. [ref: FEATURE: Aki’s Morning Routine is One of My Favorite Chainsaw Man Moments So Far] Anime UK News site said that the relationship between Denji and Aki forms "an odd couple/mismatched cop buddy scenario between the two characters". [ref: Chainsaw Man Volume 1 Review, Anime UK News] IGN praised Aki's scene in the hospital as well as his relationship with Denji and Power. [ref: Chainsaw Man: Season 1 Review, IGN] The Fandom Post saw Aki to be the most sympathetic character in the series, and received its personality as well and praised his reaction to Himino's death. [ref: Chainsaw Man Episode #10 Anime Review, The Fandom Post] Thomas Egan of Polygon considered Denji and Aki's fight scene to be one of the best fight scenes in Chainsaw Man. [ref: The best Chainsaw Man fights, Polygon.com] CBR compared the characters of Aki and Megumi from Jujutsu Kaisen, and suggested that both have similar appearance, personalities and powers, and considered Aki as a darker and more haunted version of Megumi. [ref: Chainsaw Man's Aki Hayakawa Is an Improved Version of Jujutsu Kaisen's Fushiguro Megumi, CBR]

Abema Times discused the relationship between Aki and Himeno, suggesting that their relationship went beyond mere friendship, stating: "The two share a bond that clearly goes deeper than just being Devil Hunter partners... This first-time animation of an episode showing such intimacy surely delighted many fans who watched the compilation". [ref: ] Ajay Aravind from CBR ranked Aki and Himeno as the fourth best couple in Chainsaw Man, and said that Himeno was the only one who understood Aki’s emotional fragility, and that at first Aki did not reciprocate Himeno’s feelings of love, but a strong bond soon developed between them due to shared painful experiences, as they lost many friends and became afraid for each other, until Himeno eventually sacrificed herself to protect Aki. [ref: The Best Chainsaw Man Couples, Ranked, CBR] Emma Singer from CBR considered Denji, Power and Aki as the best trio in the Shonen world. [ref: Why Chainsaw Man's Denji, Power, and Aki are Shonen's Greatest Trio, CBR] Meanwhile, Otaku USA praised the handling of the main trio in early chapters due to the drama the cast endures. [ref: Why Chainsaw Man is a Must-Read Manga on the Shonen Jump App, Otaku USA Magazine]

In the first popularity poll of the manga, Aki ranked third with 25,704 votes; [ref: 『チェンソーマン』第1回キャラクター人気投票開催!!｜集英社『週刊少年ジャンプ』公式サイト, 集英社『週刊少年ジャンプ』公式サイト] [ref: VIZ Blog / Chainsaw Man Popularity Poll Results August 2022, www.viz.com] in the second poll, he took first place with 88,568 votes; [ref: 『チェンソーマン』第2回キャラクター人気投票結果発表!!｜集英社『週刊少年ジャンプ』公式サイト, 集英社『週刊少年ジャンプ』公式サイト] [ref: Chainsaw Man Popularity Poll Reveals Top Ten Most Popular Characters, Siliconera] and in the third poll, he placed third with 89,804 votes. [ref: 第3回『チェンソーマン』キャラクター人気投票, www.shonenjump.com] [ref: 10 Most Popular Chainsaw Man Characters (According To Fans), ComicBook.com]

data.title: Kha Ma Harun
data.text:
----

Kha Ma Harun (also known as K. M. Harun Al Rashid; born 26 October 1953) is a Bangladeshi television director, filmmaker, media executive, educator and author. He serves as the Principal and Head of the Department of Film and Television at Pathshala South Asian Media Institute, an affiliate of the University of Dhaka. [ref: Faculty Member, Pathshala South Asian Media Institute] [ref: Kha Ma Harun, Pathshala South Asian Media Institute] [ref: Reform from ground up needed for media to speak for nation, The Daily Star] During his three-decade career at Bangladesh Television (BTV), he held senior executive roles-including Director, Deputy Director General (programme), and Acting Director General [ref: Poet Abu Zafar made BTV DG, The Daily Star] while producing and directing television dramas, serials, telefilms, documentaries, and cultural broadcasts. He is also the author of three published books. [ref: প্রযুক্তি সহজ হলেও ভালো কনটেন্ট তৈরি সহজ হয়নি, The Daily News Paper Ittefaq]

== Early Life and Education ==
Harun was born on 26 October 1953 in Khulna, in what was then East Pakistan (now Bangladesh). He studied Philosophy at the University of Dhaka, where he earned a Bachelor of Arts (Honours) and a Master of Arts degree. During his university years, he also studied Political Science and History. As a first-year student, he participated in the Bangladesh Liberation War in 1971. After completing his master's degree in 1976, Harun received a Government of India scholarship to study at the National School of Drama (NSD) in New Delhi. He completed a three-year postgraduate diploma in Drama in 1979, specializing in theatre design.
== Career ==
Harun joined Bangladesh Television (BTV) as a producer on 17 July 1980. [ref: Former BTV deputy DG recalls a sweet and conflicted Tazin Ahmed, Dhaka Tribune] During his 30 years at BTV, he worked as a Producer, Executive Producer, Programme Manager, Director, and Deputy Director General until his retirement in 2010. At BTV, his work involved television production, programme planning, dramas, telefilms, documentaries, serials, musical shows, and public affairs broadcasts. He also served as Executive Director and Chief of Programmes at RTV, [ref: Revolution Television, The Daily Star] and as Director of the National Institute of Mass Communication (NIMC), the Government of Bangladesh's media training institution. His directorial work includes Firiye Dao Aronnyo (1989), featuring Tauquir Ahmed, Munira Yusuf Memi, and Abdul Barik Mukul [ref: MEMI Versatility and verve, The Daily Star] [ref: কেমন আছেন অভিনেতা আবদুল বারিক মুকুল, Jugantor] and the series Shongkito Podojatra (1992) written by Mansurul Aziz. He also produced Shohor, Jhor, Nilpania, Rupali Nodir Dheu, and Kichuto Bolun. Harun authored Shongkito Podojatra (2023), [ref: Shongkito Podojatra, pathakshamabesh] a memoir detailing his experiences in the Bangladesh Liberation War and his broadcasting career. The book shares its title with a 1992 television series he previously directed for Bangladesh Television. Harun authored two additional books: Sabinoye Jante Chai (সবিনয়ে জানতে চাই) from Sahitya Prakash in 1997 [ref: সবিনয়ে জানতে চাই, Sāhitya Prakāśa] and Diary 1972 Ebong Koyekti Din (ডায়েরি ১৯৭২ এবং কয়েকটি দিন) from Panjeri Publications, 2026. [ref: ডায়েরি ১৯৭২: কয়েকটি দিন, Samakal]

Following his retirement from Bangladesh Television, Harun entered academia as an Adjunct Professor in the Department of Television, Film and Photography at the University of Dhaka, teaching television production, broadcasting management, and media studies. He was later appointed Principal and Head of the Department of Film and Television at Pathshala South Asian Media Institute, an institute affiliated with the University of Dhaka. He also served as a member of the Strategic Plan Team of the Asia-Pacific Institute for Broadcasting Development (AIBD), where he participated in regional broadcasting and media development initiatives, [ref: আন্তর্জাতিক সম্প্রচার কৌশল পরিকল্পনা টিমে খ ম হারুন, Daily Inqilab] the Commonwealth Broadcasting Association (CBA), and the SAARC Audio Visual Exchange (SAVE). He has also participated in international broadcasting conferences, workshops, and media forums in Asia and Europe. In 2017, he attended the 14th Asia Media Summit in Qingdao, China, as a member of the Bangladeshi delegation. During his visits to China, he also produced documentary films for Bangladeshi television and participated in professional exchanges with Chinese broadcasting organizations.[https://www.ekusheypatrika.com/archives/17469] [ref: খ ম হারুন-চীনা বেতারের ভ্রমণ কথোপকথন, Ekushey Patrika] Harun contributed archival photographs and historical information to a feature published by Prothom Alo on the history of Bangladesh Television. [ref: বিটিভির যাত্রা শুরুর রোমাঞ্চকর নেপথ্য কাহিনি, প্রথম আলো বাংলা নিউজ পেপার]

In September 2026, during public discussions about a proposed redesign of Bangladesh Television logo, Harun stated that the original emblem, designed with contributions from artists Quamrul Hassan and Mustafa Monwar, should be retained for its historical significance. He also suggested focusing on operational reforms, including workforce training, content diversification, and administrative updates. [ref: Will BTV’s iconic red-green logo get a new look, or stay the same?, The Financial Express] In July 2026, Harun was cited in national coverage reporting the passing of former BTV Director-General Mostafizur Rahman. [ref: Veteran television personality Mostafizur Rahman passes away, The Daily Star] In an analytical profile published by Samakal, Harun was highlighted as an unconventional television director and media producer who contributed distinct stylistic approaches to Bangladeshi television production. [ref: খ ম হারূন: প্রচলিত ধারার বাইরে একজন ভিন্ন কারিগর, Samakal]

== Personal Life ==
Harun is married to an international professor and academic, and the couple has two daughters. He resides primarily in Dhaka, Bangladesh, where he remains active in the local arts and filmmaking community.

data.text:
----

Politrack Africa is a market research and opinion polling agency headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya. [ref: Wambua, Murungi and Methu top performing Senators in Politrack Africa poll, Capital FM]

== Research and polling ==

The firm evaluates public policy and political performance across Kenya's 47 counties. In September 2023, it surveyed 4,801 respondents to rank performance among county senators. A broader survey published in April 2024 evaluated Cabinet secretaries, governors, principal secretaries, and lawmakers across 290 constituencies. [ref: Kindiki, Linturi & Chelugui top performing CSs - Politrack Africa, KBC Digital]

Politrack's December 2024 rating index placed Mining and Blue Economy Cabinet Secretary Hassan Joho as the highest-rated minister with 67.3% approval. [ref: Politrack Africa: Joho top perfoming CS with 67.3pc score, Capital FM] Early the following year, the company released a survey on Principal Secretaries based on responses from 1,068 citizens collected in January 2025. [ref: Politrak Report Unveils List of Top Ten Best Performing PSs, Kenyans.co.ke] It also hosted the 2025 Politrack Africa Star Leaders Awards in March to recognize elected and appointed officials. [ref: Babu Owino, Wandayi, Bitok Ranked Best MP, CS & PS at 2025 Politrack Africa Star Leaders Awards, Kenyans.co.ke]

In late 2025, Politrack published two nationwide studies: a performance evaluation of women representatives in November [ref: Nyandarua, Nyeri Woman Reps Lead as Politrack Africa Releases Best Performers List, Tuko] and a county governors index in December. In the governor survey, Kisii Governor Simba Arati and Kakamega Governor Fernandes Barasa tied for top performance at 65%, with Kirinyaga Governor Anne Waiguru placing third at 63.2%. [ref: Arati, Barasa and Waiguru ranked best performing governors in latest Politrack survey, [[TV47 Kenya]

Ahead of the 2027 general election, kenyan media reported on a Politrack africa poll conducted in September 2026 sampling 20,419 voters across 290 constituencies. [ref: Survey: Ruto commands lead, Sifuna surges, Daily Nation] The survey showed incumbent President William Ruto leading voter preference at 45.1%, followed by Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna at 19.6% and Kalonzo Musyoka at 10.3%. [ref: Politrack poll: Ruto leads presidential preference with 45.1%, Sifuna second at 19.6%, [[The Star (Kenya)] [ref: Ruto leads 2027 presidential preference poll at 45.1%, People Daily]

== Media coverage ==

In June 2026, Africa Check reported on a fabricated opinion poll attributed to Politrack Africa concerning the Machakos gubernatorial race. The fact-check found that the poll had not been published by Politrack Africa and that the firm had identified the circulating graphic as fake. [ref: Ignore fake pole, former chief of staff Nzioka Waita wasn’t ranked most popular candidate for Machakos governor, Africa Check]

data.title: Neko Health
data.text:
Niko Health is a Swedish health tech company that offers technology-driven preventative health scans. [ref: Full-body scans: are Neko Health and the like more panic than panacea?, The Week US] [ref: I tried a £300 scan that promises to help you avoid illness – and I was impressed, The Independent] It was co-founded in 2018 by Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne. [ref: Is Daniel Ek’s Neko Health worth $1.7bn?, Sifted] Neko Health is headquartered in Stockholm, Sweden, with clinics in Stockholm, London, Manchester, Birmingham, and New York City. [ref: Nowhere to hide, www.healthcare-management.uk]

== History ==
Neko Health was founded in 2018 by Hjalmar Nilsonne and Daniel Ek, the founder and Executive Chairman of Spotify. [ref: Verifying Device, www.thetimes.com] [ref: Verifying Device, www.thetimes.com] [ref: Daniel Ek’s Next Act: Full-Body Scans for the People, The New York Times] The company develops technology intended to support preventive healthcare and early disease detection. Between 2018 and 2023, it developed its own hardware, software, and medical technology. [ref: Neko’s full-body scan costs £300 and has a 100K waiting list. Is it worth it?] [ref: Age against the machine: what I learned after stripping down for a full body scan, The Guardian] [ref: I Tried the Viral Health Scan With a 100,000-Person Waitlist—These are My Honest Thoughts, Marie Claire UK]

In February 2023, Neko Health launched its first clinic in Stockholm, Sweden. [ref: The Hottest Startups in Stockholm in 2024, Wired] After immediate customer demand and a waitlist of up to 100,000 customers, Neko Health began expanding. [ref: I Tried The New £299 Health Scan With A 40,000-Strong Waitlist… Was It Worth It?, British Vogue] In 2024, Neko Health expanded to clinics in London and further across the UK, including Manchester and Birmingham. [ref: We took a Neko Health scan – the future of preventative healthcare?, Wallpaper*] [ref: Swedish start-up Neko Health brings its sci-fi scanning suite to central London, Wallpaper*] [ref: Daniel Ek’s body scanning startup Neko unveils massive new London clinic, Sifted]

In January 2025, following its Series B funding, Neko Health announced the funding would be used for expansion across Europe, entering the U.S. market, and continuing to develop new diagnostic technologies. [ref: Neko Health Accelerates UK Expansion, Fitt Insider] [ref: The Swedish Start-Up Aiming to Conquer America’s Full-Body-Scan Craze, The New York Times]

In June 2026, Neko launched the Neko Health App on iOS.

== Technology ==
The Neko Health Scan is a health assessment that combines imaging, physiological testing, laboratory analysis, and a clinician consultation during a single appointment. [ref: Neko Health: A Unique Twist on Whole-body Scans, Healthcare Huddle] The assessment does not use ionizing radiation and includes:

* 2D and 3D imaging, thermal imaging, and depth-sensing technology
* Measurements including blood pressure, body composition, and electrocardiography (ECG), cardiac and arterial assessments, and blood analysis
* Other measurements including grip strength and intraocular pressure

The assessment is used to identify health markers associated with conditions including cardiovascular disease, metabolic disorders, and some skin cancers.

== Funding ==
Neko Health was initially financed by Daniel Ek through his investment firm, Prima Materia, before raising outside capital.

In July 2023, Neko Health raised €60 million in a Series A funding found led by Lakestar, Atomico, and General Catalyst. [ref: Daniel Ek's Neko Health raises $65M for preventative healthcare through full-body scans, TechCrunch] [ref: Atomico raises $1.24bn to back European startups from Series A and beyond, Sifted] [ref: Neko Health – What People Are Missing, Healthy Debate by Max Marchione] Following that round, Klaus Hommels and Niklas Zennström joined the company's board.

In January 2025, Neko Health raised $260 million in a Series B funding round at a reported valuation of approximately $1.8 billion. [ref: Daniel Ek’s Neko raises $260mn in push to be Apple of healthcare, www.ft.com] [ref: ] [ref: Full-body scan startup Neko Health raises $260 million, Axios] [ref: Neko, the body-scanning startup co-founded by Spotify's Daniel Ek, snaps up $260M at a $1.8B valuation, TechCrunch] [ref: Neko Health Raises $260M Ahead of U.S. Launch, Athletech News] Investors included Lightspeed Venture Partners, General Catalyst, Atomico, Lakestar, O.G. Venture Partners, and Rossello. [ref: Preventing illness, not treating it: Neko Health raises €250 million to expand globally, EU-Startups]

In July 2026, Neko Health raised $700 million in a Series C funding round co-led by O.G. Venture Partners and Lightspeed Venture Partners. Investors in the round included Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan, model Claudia Schiffer, former tennis player Maria Sharapova, and musician will.i.am. [ref: Neko Health, a Body-Scan Startup, Raises $700 Million in Latest Fundraising, Wall Street Journal] [ref: Daniel Ek’s body-scanning start-up raises $700mn for US push, www.ft.com] [ref: Tech Investors and Longevity Influencers Back Neko Health’s Expansion, The New York Times]

data.title: Pakka (company)
data.text:
----

Pakka Limited (formerly Yash Papers and Yash Pakka) is an Indian packaging company headquartered in Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh. The company was established in 1981 as Yash Papers and initially manufactured low-grammage kraft paper. It later expanded into moulded-fibre food-service products and other packaging made from agricultural residue. [ref: Prospectus: Yash Papers Limited, Securities and Exchange Board of India] [ref: How letting go brought 40-year-old family biz Yash Pakka back from the brink, Forbes India]

The company is listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange of India. [ref: Packaging firm Pakka gets listed on NSE, The Hindu]

==History==

Pakka was established in 1981 as Yash Papers Limited by K. K. Jhunjhunwala in Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh. The company began as a manufacturer of low-grammage kraft paper, with an initial installed capacity of 1,940 tonnes per year. Commercial production began in 1983.

In 1991, Yash Papers established a second paper manufacturing unit with an installed capacity of 6,000 tonnes per year. In 1992, the company made a public issue to finance an increase in its manufacturing capacity to 16,000 tonnes per year.

The company expanded its energy infrastructure during the 1990s. In 1997, it installed a 2.5 MW steam turbine for cogeneration of power. The company also began exporting its paper, with its first direct export order executed in 1999.

During the 2000s, Yash Papers expanded its paper manufacturing operations and moved into speciality grades. Its manufacturing infrastructure subsequently included pulp production, chemical recovery and power-generation facilities.

Ved Krishna, the son of K. K. Jhunjhunwala, joined the company in 1999 and later took responsibility for its operations. During this period, the company experienced financial and operational difficulties before shifting its focus towards higher-value paper and packaging products. [ref: From Ayodhya to 30 countries: how this sustainable paper business beat all odds to clock Rs 300 Cr turnover, YourStory]

During the 2010s, the company increasingly expanded from paper manufacturing into packaging products made from agricultural residue. It developed moulded-fibre products and launched CHUK, a brand of compostable food-service tableware made from sugarcane fibre.

In 2015, Ved Krishna stepped away from the company's day-to-day operational management. The company subsequently moved towards a more professionally managed operating structure while continuing to expand its packaging business.

In 2018, CHUK received design recognition including the Red Dot Design Award and the Good Design Award. [ref: How Yash Pakka is making sustainable packaging a reality in India, [[The Telegraph (India)] [ref: CHUK Delivery Containers launched; Solves Biggest Packaging Challenge, Food Infotech]

In 2019, the company changed its name from Yash Papers Limited to Yash Pakka Limited, reflecting its expansion beyond paper manufacturing into packaging products.

In 2023, the company changed its name to Pakka Limited and was listed on the National Stock Exchange of India, a listing that coincided with plans to expand its Ayodhya operations and establish a manufacturing facility in Guatemala. In 2024, the company's board approved an increased budget for the Jagriti project, an expansion of its Ayodhya manufacturing operations, with the revised project cost reported at ₹675 crore and completion expected in 2026. [ref: Outcome of Board Meeting held on 27 March 2024, National Stock Exchange of India]

==Products and operations==

Pakka produces paper, moulded-fibre food-service products and other packaging made from agricultural residue, particularly sugarcane bagasse. Its principal manufacturing operations are based in Ayodhya. [ref: Pakka Ltd: How 1 Son Took His Father's Dream to a Rs 400 Crore Sustainable Packaging Success, The Better India]

The company's product portfolio includes speciality paper, moulded-fibre food-service products and packaging made from agricultural residue. Its operations use sugarcane residue as a principal raw material, and biomass-based energy generation has been incorporated into its manufacturing processes. [ref: Yash Pakka: Packaging with Care Never Comes to an End, Food Infotech]

In 2022, YourStory reported that the company's products were being used by businesses including Rebel Foods, Haldiram's, Cafe Coffee Day and Chai Point, and that the company operated in more than 30 countries at the time. In 2023, The Telegraph India reported that Yash Pakka distributed its products in 43 countries and worked with more than 40 commercial partners.

==CHUK==
CHUK is Pakka's brand of compostable food-service tableware, developed as the company expanded from paper manufacturing into moulded-fibre products made from sugarcane residue. The brand produces food-service items including plates, bowls and containers, developed as alternatives to conventional single-use plastic and expanded-polystyrene food-service products. The Telegraph India reported in 2023 that CHUK formed part of Yash Pakka's wider expansion into agricultural-residue packaging alongside its paper operations.

==Certifications and standards==
Pakka's manufacturing and product processes have been certified against standards covering quality management, food safety, occupational health and safety and environmental management. The company's 2022-23 annual report lists ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015, ISO 22000 and ISO 45001 certifications, as well as compliance with U.S. Food and Drug Administration requirements under 21 CFR 176.170 and certification through the Central Institute of Petrochemicals Engineering & Technology (CIPET). [ref: Pakka Limited Annual Report 2022-23, National Stock Exchange of India]

In 2022, Yash Pakka received Forest Stewardship Council Chain of Custody certification for selected products, providing traceability for eligible certified material through the supply chain and production process. [ref: Yash Pakka bags international-grade certification for sustainability, The Packman]

==Awards and recognition==
Pakka and its predecessor Yash Pakka have received recognition for product design, packaging, water efficiency, energy conservation and workplace practices.

In 2018, CHUK received a Red Dot Design Award and a Good Design Award.

In 2021, Yash Pakka received the President's Award for Sustainability and Innovation at the SIES SOP Star Awards for its fibre-based food delivery containers. [ref: SIES SOP Star Awards 2021: List of Winning Entries, SIES School of Packaging]

In 2022, Yash Pakka was recognised as a Noteworthy Water Efficient Unit at the Confederation of Indian Industry's National Awards for Excellence in Water Management. [ref: Yash Pakka recognized for water efficiency, Packaging South Asia]

In December 2022, Yash Pakka received the Uttar Pradesh State Energy Conservation Award from the Uttar Pradesh New and Renewable Energy Development Agency (UPNEDA). [ref: A cleaner planet will be achieved through scaling regenerative packaging solutions: Jagdeep Hira, Business Head, Yash Pakka Ltd., The Machinist]

In 2023, Yash Pakka was included among India's Best Workplaces in Manufacturing by Great Place to Work. [ref: India's Best Workplaces in Manufacturing 2023, Great Place to Work India]

==Social initiatives==
Pakka's social initiatives are implemented primarily through the Pakka Foundation, which works in communities around the company's manufacturing operations in Ayodhya. Its activities have included education, vocational training and environmental programmes. [ref: Pakka Foundation, Pakka Foundation]

The foundation has supported educational initiatives including Krishna Niketan, a network of pre-primary education centres, and Yash Vidya Mandir, a school serving students from primary through secondary education.

In 2023, Food Infotech reported that the Pakka Foundation was involved in the rejuvenation of six ponds covering a combined area of about 15,000 square metres in and around Ayodhya, and that more than 65,000 trees had been planted as part of Pakka's afforestation activities.

data.title: Zaery (musician)
data.text:
Zaery (born Amr Elrayah Abdalla October 1, 1998 in Sudan,Khartoum,Omdurman )is a sudanese organist, composer. [ref: Zaery: Taking Zanig Music from Omdurman to the International Stage, The Sudanist] [ref: Zaery, the Artist Who Will Take ZANIG Music to the World Stage – Weekly Music Vibes, weeklymusicvibes.com] [ref: From the Margins to the Mainstream: The Rise of Zanig in Sudanese Music, The Sudanist]

== Life ==
He was born in Omdurman and spent his early childhood in the Al-Murabba'at neighborhood before moving to Al-Abbasiya, where he grew up. He is the eldest of three brothers. Mazen is the middle child, and Muhammad Al-Mustafa is the youngest. He was raised in Al-Abbasiya and developed a love for music, inspired by the musicians Ayman Al-Rubu and Nijiri. [ref: ] [ref: أسطورة (الزنق) بالسودان “نيجيري”: لن أعود لدراسة الطب ودخلي الأسبوعي يعادل مرتب موظف كبير في شهر, صحيفة كورة سودانية الإلكترونية]

He became involved in Zanig music a Sudanese youth oriented musical style  associated with urban popular neighborhoods, pioneered by musician Ayman Al-Rubu amidst the working-class neighborhoods of Omdurman. [ref: Zaery: Taking Zanig Music from Omdurman to the International Stage, The Sudanist] [ref: لا يخلو أورغن من (صولاته) الموسيقية أيمن الربع.. رائد الكتمات!! - النيلين, www.alnilin.com]

He began performing live in 2012, marking his first steps in the music industry. At the time, the popularity of Zanig music among musicians stemmed from its style—dance-oriented, youthful, and contemporary—pulsing with youthful vitality. [ref: Miami City Weekly, www.miamicityweekly.com]

== Career ==
The real turning point in Zaery life came when he was personally requested to perform at a major public New Year’s Eve concert in Port Sudan in 2016. This marked his transition from playing the keyboard in working-class neighborhoods to performing at large-scale concerts in theaters and across various states. [ref: زنق, الرصّة] This large-scale public concert brought him widespread fame in Sudan. [ref: Zaery: Taking Zanig Music from Omdurman to the International Stage, The Sudanist]Subsequently, he performed at popular events across the capital's neighborhoods—ranging from private functions to rehearsals with other artists—which significantly shaped and enhanced his musical experience. [ref: Zaery, the Artist Who Will Take ZANIG Music to the World Stage – MusicTimes] [ref: ]

== His musical works ==

In 2019, Zaery recorded an African-style musical track at the Hajjaj Studio in Sudan and produced a music video in collaboration with a band. In 2020, he collaborated with Sudanese artist Noon Al-Ankaboota on the song "[https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1bmcFJgEFx/?mibextid=wwXIfr Kassar Samah]," which blended elements of "Zanig " and "Daluka" music. He later collaborated with Sudanese singer Wad Al-Jack and participated in live performances and a tour throughout 2021. [ref: Zaery: Taking Zanig Music from Omdurman to the International Stage, The Sudanist] [ref: ود الجاك يخوض تجربة أول حفل جماهيري في (اتحاد الفنانين) - تسامح نيوز]

In June 2022, Zaery moved to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, where he joined the Sudanese band "Sequence" and performed Western and reggae music at various events and festivals. He also appeared on the Saudi television program "Ala Al-Wa'ad"—filmed at Rotana studios alongside artist Abdelfattah Grini. [ref: Zaery raises the Bar for Afro Pop music with ‘Rasta’, Sinusoidal Music] [ref: New Music Radar: 19 bands worth throwing into your rotation right now, Happy Mag] [ref: عبد الفتاح الجريني.. نوستالجيا نجم مغربي ولد بين أحضان الهجرة, Hespress - هسبريس جريدة إلكترونية مغربية]

== Zanig music ==
[https://nowvoyagermag.com/culture/city-beats Zanig] music is a modern musical genre in Sudan that gained prominence after its melodies captured the interest of Sudanese society and the youth. It is a fusion of African rhythms and contemporary Sudanese youth music. Furthermore, [ref: Zanig: The Story of a Music Genre Born in Khartoum, Sudan, Now Voyager Magazine]it features dance styles with an African sensibility, with the keyboardist often accompanied by a group of dancers who perform in highly choreographed unison. [ref: An Artless Artist: The Overlooked Genius of Ayman Al-Rubo by Al Rayah Al Rehima, Andariya]

data.title: Rubber Duc
data.text:
----

Rubber Duc is a South African alternative-pop and acoustic dance music band formed in Johannesburg in 2014. The group is known for its fusion of folk, swing, pop, and brass instrumentation, as well as its upbeat comedic and observational lyrics. [ref: Local band getting ducks all in a row, [[Independent Online (South Africa)]

The band rose to national prominence following their 2014 breakthrough single "Ain't Nobody Got Time for That". Their debut studio album, The Secret Sunrise (2016), received two nominations at the 23rd South African Music Awards (SAMA 23). [ref: 2017 SAMAs: all the nominees, TVSA (Television South Africa)]

== History ==

=== Formation and breakthrough (2014–2015) ===
Rubber Duc was formed in Johannesburg in early 2014 by lead vocalist and guitarist Nick Jordaan, lead guitarist Brendan Campbell, saxophonist Sheldon Sham, and bassist Amiel Gopal. The band chose their name intentionally to distinguish themselves in search engines by omitting the letter "k".

In March 2014, the group released their satirical debut single, "Ain't Nobody Got Time for That", inspired by the viral video catchphrase of Sweet Brown. The track gained heavy rotation across national commercial radio stations in South Africa. The band followed this release with singles such as "It's Alright" and "Stay With Me", pioneering a style they described as "acoustic dance music" (ADM).

=== The Secret Sunrise and industry recognition (2016–2018) ===
In September 2016, Rubber Duc released their debut full-length studio album, The Secret Sunrise, which spawned several radio singles including "Are We There Yet?" and "Feet".

At the 23rd South African Music Awards in 2017, the album received two industry nominations: Best Alternative Music Album and Best Produced Album. [ref: SAMA23 nominees announced, Bizcommunity] In 2018, their composition "Avery" earned an Honourable Mention in the Folk/Singer-Songwriter category at the International Songwriting Competition (ISC), selected from over 16,000 worldwide submissions.

In late 2018, the band released the pop single "Through the Night", which reached number one on the Jacaranda FM Top 20 chart.

=== Subsequent releases and Old Money (2019–present) ===
In November 2020, Rubber Duc released the bilingual collaboration single "Come Again" with South African pop group ADAM.

In 2025, the group partnered with Virgin Music Group South Africa to release the extended play Old Money. [ref: Rubber Duc thrill Lyric Lounge audience with familiar hits and new songs, [[The Citizen (South Africa)]

== Musical style and performances ==
Rubber Duc's style combines acoustic folk instrumentation, syncopated rhythm guitars, saxophone hooks, and four-part vocal harmonies, blending elements of pop, swing, and dance music.

The band has performed on the main stages of prominent southern African music festivals, including Splashy Fen, [ref: American Authors set to headline at Splashy Fen, [[Independent Online (South Africa)] Oppikoppi, Rocking the Daisies, Up the Creek, [ref: It's great to be Up the Creek, [[Independent Online (South Africa)] and the Vic Falls Carnival in Zimbabwe. They have also performed as the primary opening act for German rock group Milky Chance during their South African tour.

== Band members ==

=== Current members ===
* Nick Jordaan – lead vocals, acoustic guitar (2014–present)
* Brendan Campbell – lead guitar, kick drum, backing vocals (2014–present)
* Amiel Gopal – bass guitar, backing vocals (2014–present)
* Kabelo Seleke – saxophone (2020–present)
* Nicholas McCreadie – drums (2020–present)

=== Former members ===
* Sheldon Sham – saxophone (2014–2019)
* Leeroy Sauls – drums (touring/session)

data.title: Paul and James on faith and works
data.text:
----

The relationship between Paul the Apostle and James, brother of Jesus, regarding faith and works is often misunderstood as a theological contradiction. Critics frequently point to Paul’s emphasis on "faith alone" in his letters and contrast it with James’s assertion that "faith without works is dead" (James 2:26). However, a closer examination of the Pauline epistles—specifically Ephesians 2:8–10—reveals that both writers are teaching the exact same core message from two complementary viewpoints.
In Ephesians 2:8–9, Paul establishes the foundation of salvation, explicitly stating, "For by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, lest anyone should boast." This aligns with his consistent teaching that human rituals or legalistic deeds cannot earn right-standing with God.
However, the very next verse, Ephesians 2:10, bridges the gap to James's theology. Paul writes, "For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand that we should walk in them." Here, Paul explicitly commands believers to perform good works, clarifying that while works are not the cause of salvation, they are the mandatory consequence of it.
Therefore, Paul and James do not conflict; they address different errors. Paul writes to legalists who try to earn salvation through rituals, while James writes to complacent believers who use faith as an excuse for laziness. Both authors agree that true, saving faith is an internal root that must inevitably produce visible, active good works as its fruit.

data.title: Public administration
data.text:
Public Administration is generally seen as the activity of government agencies, while in reality, it is much wider and more complicated than that. There is one aspect of public administration that does not get enough attention – that is, implementation of policies into tangible outputs. Even though some policy looks very good on paper and in theory, the success of its implementation can depend greatly on administrators. Another thing that public administrators need to do is to make decisions on allocation of limited resources.

Another equally intriguing observation is that front-liners working for the government can make a huge impact on the perception of the citizens regarding the government. Citizens may never have a chance to meet any top government officials in their lifetime but they frequently deal with barangay workers, teachers, health personnel, policemen, social workers, and permit issuers. The citizens' interaction with these individuals will determine whether they find the government responsive, fair, efficient, and trustworthy.

In addition to this, public administration differs from private administration in that efficiency is not the only objective of public administration. The government needs to take into account factors such as fairness, equality, legality, transparency, accountability, and public good. Efficiency does not always mean fairness, since there may be cases when the most efficient approach might not be the most fair approach. As an illustration, offering a governmental service online may be efficient; however, it may not be fair for people with poor internet connectivity.

What is often overlooked is the fact that public administrators may affect policy even if they are not elected officials. They have technical knowledge, they prepare reports, suggest programs, oversee the implementation process, and make decisions on a daily basis. As they are responsible for implementing the policy, they may influence its improvement or change.

In addition, public administration entails the creation of a relationship between the government and its citizens. The government may be well endowed with laws and adequate means of carrying out its duties, but when citizens feel that the delivery of services is untimely and unfair, the level of trust in the government will be undermined. However, delivery of effective services will enhance the level of trust and increase citizen participation in government activities. Therefore, public administration cannot only be seen as “government business.”

Center for Earth and Natural Resource Sciences

The Center for Earth and Natural Resource Sciences (CENRS) is a multidisciplinary research institution based in Rwanda and it's headquarters are located in Nyabihu District, Northern Rwanda, and it's community service is based in Nyabugogo, Kigali City. CENRS was officially established on 3 September 2025 under Rwandan Law No. 007/2021 of 5 February 2021. The Center conducts fundamental and applied research in environmental systems. [ref: ]

History

The origins of CENRS can be traced back to 15 September 2016 in Xiamen, where two Rwandan scientists, Jean Claude Ndayishimiye [ref: ORCID, orcid.org] and Pascaline Nyirabuhoro [ref: ORCID, orcid.org], were pursuing doctoral degrees at the University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and conducting research at the Institute of Urban Environment, Chinese Academy of Sciences. At that time, Ndayishimiye and Nyirabuhoro were in Xiamen conducting their doctoral research. As young researchers specifically from inland Africa. In China, official assessments reported direct economic losses of more than ¥16.9 billion (2.6 billion USD) in Fujian Province, with additional losses in neighbouring Zhejiang Province [ref: ]. An earlier assessment by the Hong Kong Observatory reported at least 29 deaths in Fujian and Jiangxi and direct economic losses exceeding ¥11.7 billion (1.75 billion USD) [ref: TROPICAL CYCLONES IN 2016, www.hko.gov.hk]. Ndayishimiye and Nyirabuhoro at that time were deeply impressed by the effectiveness of China’s early warning systems, coordinated evacuation measures, and resilient infrastructure. Their experience extended beyond these observations, as their direct exposure to Super Typhoon Meranti immediately shaped their research interests, with climate extremes and environmental disturbances becoming central areas of their scientific work. Africa was grappling with the devastation shaped by tropical cyclones. Notably, Intense Tropical Cyclone Idai affected Mozambique, Zimbabwe, and Malawi from 4 to 21 March 2019, causing catastrophic flooding and widespread destruction across the region, with 1,593 deaths, 2,452 injuries, and 3.1 million people affected, along with total damages estimated at 2.2 billion USD. The postdoctoral period provided an opportunity for Ndayishimiye and Nyirabuhoro to translate their research findings and experiences into a concrete institutional vision, with Africa identified as an initial focus because of the widespread vulnerability of its communities. The formal process was completed on 3 September 2025, marking the launch of the center’s official operations. In support of this vision, Ndayishimiye and Nyirabuhoro pledged one-third of their annual incomes to support CENRS research and community service activities.

Research and services

CENRS conducts research and translates its findings directly into services for local communities, with its activities tailored to the needs of vulnerable communities, particularly those facing financial and resource constraints. This applied, service-oriented model distinguishes it from conventional academic institutions, where research is generally linked to teaching or institutional research programmes rather than to direct community service.

National and international collaborations

CENRS collaborates with institutions in more than fifteen countries. According to the Nature Index, CENRS’s principal research collaborators include Shenzhen MSU-BIT University, Lomonosov Moscow State University, Beijing Institute of Technology, Henan Normal University, and Saint Petersburg State University.

Research output

Although CENRS is a newly established institution, it has already achieved a notable research position in Rwanda and internationally. In the Nature Index 2025–2026 assessment window (June 2025 to May 2026), CENRS ranked 8,715th globally and 14th in Rwanda by overall research output. Among non-profit organisations and non-governmental organisations (NPOs/NGOs), it ranked 2,761st globally and 7th in Rwanda. In terms of research output by subject area, CENRS ranked 4,823rd globally and 6th in Rwanda in the Natural Sciences, and 1,881st globally and 2nd in Rwanda in Earth and Environmental Sciences.

= Jump Branding & Design Inc. =
Jump Branding & Design Inc. is a Canadian multidisciplinary branding and design agency headquartered in Toronto, Ontario. Founded in 2004, the privately held company specializes in brand strategy, visual identity, packaging design, restaurant and retail environments, digital design, and marketing communications.

The agency works with businesses across the food and beverage, hospitality, retail, consumer packaged goods, and commercial sectors. Its practice combines graphic design and brand development with the design of physical environments and customer experiences.

Jump has received recognition through Canadian and international design competitions, including the Association for Retail Environments (A.R.E.) Design Awards, Packaging Association of Canada (PAC) Leadership Awards, Transform Awards, and Digital Signage Awards.

== History ==
Jump Branding & Design Inc. was established in Toronto in 2004 as an independent branding and design agency.

The company developed a multidisciplinary practice combining brand strategy, graphic design, packaging, and environmental design, with a particular focus on restaurant and retail businesses.

Over the following two decades, the agency undertook projects for Canadian and international businesses, including restaurant chains, retail operators, consumer product companies, and commercial property organizations.

The agency's work has included brand identity development, restaurant concepts, retail environments, product packaging, environmental graphics, and digital communications.

Jump is led by founding principals Eric Boulden and Jason Hemsworth, who serve as co-presidents.

== Services and operations ==
Jump provides design and consulting services across several disciplines.

=== Branding and visual identity ===
The agency develops brand strategies, corporate identities, naming systems, brand architecture, visual identities, and brand guidelines for established businesses and emerging brands.

=== Restaurant and retail design ===
Jump designs restaurant, hospitality, and retail environments, including interior concepts, space planning, signage, environmental graphics, customer circulation, merchandising, and design documentation.

Its work includes individual locations, restaurant prototypes, and design programs intended for implementation across multiple locations.

=== Packaging design ===
The company's packaging practice includes consumer product packaging, product identity, packaging systems, and brand extensions for food, beverage, retail, and other consumer goods.

=== Digital design and marketing ===
Jump also provides digital brand applications, website design, marketing communications, advertising creative, and photography.

== Notable projects ==

=== South St. Burger Co. ===
Jump developed retail and environmental design work for South St. Burger Co., including a restaurant at Toronto's Shops at Don Mills.

The project incorporated sustainable design strategies, energy-efficient equipment, and environmentally responsible material selections.

The restaurant received recognition through the Association for Retail Environments' design awards, including sustainability-related honours. The project was featured in Retail Design Blog in March 2012.

=== Union Station Food Court ===
Jump was involved in the development of digital signage and branded environments for the food court at Toronto's Union Station.

Working with Osmington and participating food-service operators, the agency helped develop digital signage standards and branded content for the food hall.

The project included environmental graphics, digital menu boards, and digital signage for multiple food-service tenants.

The Union Station Food Court project was recognized in the Restaurants, Bars and Foods category of the Digital Signage Awards, with winners announced in January 2021.

=== Frank – Canadian Tire ===
Jump Branding & Design worked with Canadian Tire to redesign the packaging for Frank, its private-label brand spanning household essentials, cleaning products, and snack foods. The agency developed a packaging system incorporating humour, playful illustrations, and product-specific messaging to establish a consistent brand personality across more than 100 SKUs.

The work received a Silver Davey Award in 2018 and a Best in Class award at the 2021 PAC Global Leadership Awards in the Brand Marketing – Revitalized Food category, recognizing the Frank snack food packaging.

=== Bento Sushi / Bento Brave ===
In 2025, Jump developed the creative concept and visual identity for Bento Sushi's Bento Brave rebranding initiative.

The rebranding introduced updated typography, graphics, colours, and a dragon motif intended for use across the company's retail and food-service locations.

The initiative was covered by Retail Insider and Adnews, which identified Jump as the agency responsible for the new visual identity.

=== Other clients and projects ===
Jump's published client portfolio includes work for restaurant, retail, and consumer brands such as Pizza Hut, Taco Bell, Swiss Chalet, Yogen Früz, Basil Box, Osmow's, Paramount Fine Foods, Canadian Tire, Kernels Popcorn, Healthy Planet, Henry's, and Aramark.

Projects have included corporate identity systems, restaurant concepts, retail environments, packaging, and marketing communications.

== Awards and recognition ==
Jump has received industry recognition for work in branding, packaging, retail design, environmental sustainability, and marketing communications.

data.title: Pediatric Neurorehabilitation Research Center
data.text:
----

Pediatric Neurorehabilitation Research Center (PNRC; Persian: مرکز تحقیقات توانبخشی اعصاب اطفال) is a research center at the University of Social Welfare and Rehabilitation Sciences in Tehran, Iran. The research center was established in 2008 with the approval of Iran'sMinistry of Health and Medical Education and is reported to be the first research center in dedicated to pediatric neurorehabilitation [ref: در دانشگاه علوم بهزيستي و توانبخشي نخستين مركز تحقيقات توانبخشي اعصاب اطفال كشور راه اندازي شد] [ref: نخستین مرکز تحقیقات توانبخشی اعصاب اطفال راه اندازی شد]

Considering the 6% prevalence of learning disorders among primary schoolers in Iran, Farin Soleymani, the head of the Pediatric Neurorehabilitation Research Center, highlights the importance of early detection of learning disorders in the success rate of rehabilitation attempts [ref: علائم اختلالات یادگیری/احتمال بروز در کدام کودکان بیشتر است؟]. Thus, with the aim of promoting the development of Iranian children and providing early intervention and rehabilitation for at risk children and children living with developmental disorders, the research center began its work. [ref: Pediatric Neurorehabilitation Research Center]

== Activities and collaborations ==
The Pediatric Neurorehabilitation Research Center was responsible for organizing the first National Pediatric Rehabilitation Congress in Iran, which was held in 2025 [ref: اولین کنگره ملی توانبخشی کودکان]. The congress brought together professionals working in the field of pediatric rehabilitation from across Iran, providing an opportunity for them to present and exchange their work and experiences.

The Pediatric Neurorehabilitation Research Center has close ties with Iran’s Ministry of Health and Medical Education. Through this collaboration, the center has been commissioned to undertake several projects, including the standardization of internationally recognized developmental assessment scales for Iranian children, such as the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development [ref: محتوای استاندارد آموزش مجازی و مهارتی آزمون تشخیصی تکاملی بیلی، تولید شد] [ref: آزمون تشخیصی «اختلالات تکاملی کودکان» بومی سازی شد], the Ages and Stages Questionnaire (ASQ) and Denver Developmental Screening Tests [ref: آزمونهاي استاندارد شده توسط مركز], the development of early intervention protocols for children with language disorders [ref: مراسم رونمايي از مجموعه كتاب هاي مداخلات زودرس در اختلالات گفتار و زبان و بلع كودكان], and the design of a national developmental promotion program [ref: رئیس مرکز تحقیقات اعصاب اطفال دانشگاه علوم توانبخشی و سلامت اجتماعی از بررسی تدوین سند ملی جدید برای ارتقای تکامل کودکان از بدو تولد تا هشت سالگی خبر داد.].

The Pediatric Neurorehabilitation Research Center has established collaborations and agreements with several organizations and academic institutions, including the Iranian Red Crescent Society, Iran University of Medical Sciences, Tabriz University of Medical Sciences. [ref: همکاری مرکز تحقیقات توانبخشی اعصاب اطفال و سازمان هلال احمر کشور] [ref: تفاهم نامه ها]

One of the areas that the research center is actively promoting is research and education concerning childhood hearing loss and deafness. This began with the establishment of a hearing loss and deafness studies committee affiliated with the center in 2017. The committee's activities included support for research by students and researchers, public awareness, hearing screening, and early rehabilitation and educational programmes for deaf and hard-of-hearing children. [ref: کمیته مطالعات «ناشنوایی- کم شنوایی» آغاز بکار کرد] [ref: فعالیت کمیته مطالعات «ناشنوایی - کم شنوایی» آغاز شد]
