data.title: Oreoluwa Finnih
data.text:
Oreoluwa Finnih, (born 11 March 1973) is a Nigerian physician, public-sector official and grassroots politician whose work spans healthcare administration, public health and sustainable development. She has held several positions in the Lagos State Government, including Senior Special Assistant on Health and Special Adviser on Sustainable Development Goals to the governor. Her work has included public-health programmes, human capital development, women's financial inclusion and initiatives aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

== Education ==
Finnih attended Queen's College in Yaba, Lagos, from 1984 to 1990. She subsequently studied dentistry at the University of Lagos College of Medicine between 1990 and 1998.

She later attended Lagos Business School, part of Pan-Atlantic University, where she completed an Executive Master of Business Administration programme from 2008 to 2009. [ref: Oreoluwa Finnih-Awokoya, SA on SDGs & Investments to Governor of Lagos State, BusinessDay]

Her professional development has included training in agribusiness, export administration, public-sector transformation, governance, public health and leadership. In 2015, she attended agribusiness training through the Dream Business Club and the Songhai Regional Centre in Porto-Novo, Benin. She subsequently completed export-related training organised by the Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry in 2016.

In 2018, she undertook master-trainer training through the Lagos State Office of Transformation, Creativity and Innovation's Growth Mindset Initiative. In 2019, she participated in training related to good governance and resilient health systems at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. Her later courses included the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health programme Applied Risk Communication for the 21st Century in September 2021 and Harvard Medical School's Career Advancement and Leadership Skills for Women in Healthcare in November 2021. She also completed the [https://sdgacademy.org SDG Academy]'s Global Public Health Programme, receiving a verified certificate in June 2021.

== Career ==

=== Healthcare ===
Finnih began her professional career in the health sector. From 1999 to 2000, she worked as a medical officer with the Lagos State Health Management Board. She subsequently worked as a dentist at [https://www.schubbsdental.com Schubbs Dental Clinics] from June 2001 to March 2002.

She later held management positions at [https://finnihmedicalcentre.com Finnih Medical Centre], including Head of Human Resources from January 2002 to August 2005, Head of Administration and Finance from September 2005 to May 2007, and Chief Operating Officer from June 2007 to December 2011. She served as the centre's chief executive officer from December 2011 to April 2015.

Finnih Medical Centre was established in 1983 by physician Oluyomi Finnih. [ref: Sanwo-Olu celebrates veteran gynaecologist, Oluyomi Finnih, at 80, The Punch]

=== Agribusiness ===
In November 2015, Finnih founded Helix Farms, where she served as chief executive officer. Her work in the sector followed training in agribusiness, farming and export administration.

=== Lagos State public service ===
Finnih returned to public service in 2016, when she worked as a Research and Statistics Officer at the Lagos State Health Service Commission from December 2016 to June 2017. Between February and June 2017, she also served as Personal Assistant to the Permanent Secretary of the Lagos State Primary Health Care Board.

From June 2017 to December 2019, she worked as a Senior Medical Officer in the Directorate of Medical Services. From February 2018 to December 2019, she also served as an Infection Prevention and Disease Control Officer.

In December 2019, she became Senior Special Assistant on Health to Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu. In that role, she worked within the state's health administration and public-health framework. A profile published by BusinessDay reported that she led the risk-communication pillar of Lagos State's COVID-19 response in 2020.

In September 2023, following a change in her cabinet designation, she was appointed [https://lagossdg.com Special Adviser] on Sustainable Development Goals to the governor of Lagos State. [ref: Cabinet: Sanwo-Olu redeploys Finnih-Awokoya, Olowu as special advisers, Independent Nigeria]

== Sustainable development work ==

=== Sustainable Development Goals ===
As Special Adviser on Sustainable Development Goals, Finnih has been involved in programmes intended to align state initiatives with the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals. These goals address areas including poverty reduction, health, education, gender equality, economic opportunity, sustainable cities and partnerships for development.

In September 2024, she participated in discussions on building a more resilient and sustainable Lagos. She also took part in activities around the United Nations General Assembly's seventy-ninth session, where Lagos State promoted its sustainable-development agenda and partnerships. [ref: Oreoluwa Finnih leads discourse in charting path for building resilient, sustainable Lagos, BusinessDay] [ref: UNGA79: Lagos advances agenda on attaining SDGs, TheCable]

=== Women's financial inclusion ===
Finnih's portfolio has included initiatives to expand women's access to financial information, services and economic opportunities. In 2024, the Lagos State Government announced partnerships with financial institutions to support women through loans and financial-inclusion programmes. [ref: Lagos partners financial institutions to empower women with loans, BusinessDay]

The programme included financial-literacy and empowerment activities in underserved communities. In April 2025, the Lagos State Government and its partners concluded an outreach programme reported to have reached 1,200 women in 12 hard-to-reach communities. [ref: Lagos Govt, Africa Human Capital Development Plus conclude financial literacy empowerment with one thousand two hundred women in 12 hard-to-reach communities, Radio Nigeria Lagos]

Further engagements were reported in Surulere in July 2025 and in Papa Ashafa and Orile-Agege later that month. In August 2025, financial-literacy advocacy activities also took place in Ijede and Agura-Gberigbe in Ikorodu. [ref: Lagos Office of SDG, Human Capital Development empower 100 women in Surulere on financial literacy, services and empowerment, Radio Nigeria Lagos] [ref: Lagos OSDG HCD empower more women in Papa Ashafa, Orile-Agege LCDA on financial literacy, Radio Nigeria Lagos] [ref: Lagos Office of SDG HCD take financial literacy advocacy to two hundred women in Ijede, Agura-Gberigbe, Ikorodu, Radio Nigeria Lagos]

=== Human capital development and data governance ===
Finnih has participated in the Lagos State Government's human capital development work, including initiatives intended to strengthen coordination across government institutions and improve the use of data in policy and programme delivery.

In May 2025, the state inaugurated a Human Capital Development Core Working Group 2.0 to support coordinated action in the sector. [ref: Lagos Govt Inaugurates Working Group To Mobilize, Utilize Data For Impactful Changes, Independent Nigeria] In August 2026, the Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation reported on Lagos State's efforts to strengthen data governance in support of the SDGs. [ref: Lagos Strengthens Data Governance To Advance SDGs, Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation]

=== Environmental sustainability and climate resilience ===
Finnih's SDG portfolio has also included work connected with environmental sustainability, economic empowerment and climate resilience. In March 2025, the Lagos State Government reported on training for market women in waste-to-wealth skills, linking environmental management with livelihood opportunities. [ref: Lagos trains market women in waste-to-wealth skills, The Punch]

In May 2026, The Punch reported on a Lagos flood-risk insurance scheme intended to extend protection to residents exposed to flooding. The initiative formed part of the state's wider climate-risk and resilience agenda. [ref: Lagos targets four million residents with $7.5m flood insurance scheme, The Punch]

=== Localising the Sustainable Development Goals ===
Finnih's office has also been involved in efforts to encourage local governments to assess progress towards the SDGs. In August 2025, a qualitative assessment for a Voluntary Local Review was launched in Ikeja, part of a wider process of reviewing local progress and identifying development priorities. [ref: Ikeja Kicks Off Qualitative Assessment for Voluntary Local Review (VLR) of SDGs in Lagos, Lagos Panorama]

== Political involvement ==
Finnih is a grassroots politician and a card-carrying member of the All Progressives Congress (APC), with political involvement in Lagos State spanning party activities, community engagement and campaign organisation. She has participated in political mobilisation through party-associated structures, including the [https://rhambassadors.org Renewed Hope Ambassadors] Medical and Safety Directorate, Lagos Division. Her involvement in the directorate has included participation in meetings focused on community-level engagement, public awareness of government programmes and preparations for elections, bringing her healthcare background into activities connecting political mobilisation with medical and public-safety concerns.

In September 2026, Finnih was named Deputy Head of the Committee on Medical Emergency and Services in the Lagos State APC Campaign Council ahead of the 2027 elections. data.title: Center for Earth and Natural Resource Sciences (CENRS) 2
data.text:
Center for Earth and Natural Resource Sciences

The Center for Earth and Natural Resource Sciences (CENRS) is a multidisciplinary research institution based in Rwanda and it's headquarters are located in Nyabihu District, Northern Rwanda, and it's community service is based in Nyabugogo, Kigali City. CENRS was officially established on 3 September 2025 under Rwandan Law No. 007/2021 of 5 February 2021. The Center conducts fundamental and applied research in environmental systems. [ref: ]

History

The origins of CENRS can be traced back to 15 September 2016 in Xiamen, where two Rwandan scientists, Jean Claude Ndayishimiye [ref: ORCID, orcid.org] and Pascaline Nyirabuhoro [ref: ORCID, orcid.org], were pursuing doctoral degrees at the University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and conducting research at the Institute of Urban Environment, Chinese Academy of Sciences. At that time, Ndayishimiye and Nyirabuhoro were in Xiamen conducting their doctoral research. As young researchers specifically from inland Africa. In China, official assessments reported direct economic losses of more than ¥16.9 billion (2.6 billion USD) in Fujian Province, with additional losses in neighbouring Zhejiang Province [ref: ]. An earlier assessment by the Hong Kong Observatory reported at least 29 deaths in Fujian and Jiangxi and direct economic losses exceeding ¥11.7 billion (1.75 billion USD) [ref: TROPICAL CYCLONES IN 2016, www.hko.gov.hk]. Ndayishimiye and Nyirabuhoro at that time were deeply impressed by the effectiveness of China’s early warning systems, coordinated evacuation measures, and resilient infrastructure. Their experience extended beyond these observations, as their direct exposure to Super Typhoon Meranti immediately shaped their research interests, with climate extremes and environmental disturbances becoming central areas of their scientific work. Africa was grappling with the devastation shaped by tropical cyclones. Notably, Intense Tropical Cyclone Idai affected Mozambique, Zimbabwe, and Malawi from 4 to 21 March 2019, causing catastrophic flooding and widespread destruction across the region, with 1,593 deaths, 2,452 injuries, and 3.1 million people affected, along with total damages estimated at 2.2 billion USD. The postdoctoral period provided an opportunity for Ndayishimiye and Nyirabuhoro to translate their research findings and experiences into a concrete institutional vision, with Africa identified as an initial focus because of the widespread vulnerability of its communities. The formal process was completed on 3 September 2025, marking the launch of the center’s official operations. In support of this vision, Ndayishimiye and Nyirabuhoro pledged one-third of their annual incomes to support CENRS research and community service activities.

Research and services

CENRS conducts research and translates its findings directly into services for local communities, with its activities tailored to the needs of vulnerable communities, particularly those facing financial and resource constraints. This applied, service-oriented model distinguishes it from conventional academic institutions, where research is generally linked to teaching or institutional research programmes rather than to direct community service.

National and international collaborations

CENRS collaborates with institutions in more than fifteen countries. According to the Nature Index, CENRS’s principal research collaborators include Shenzhen MSU-BIT University, Lomonosov Moscow State University, Beijing Institute of Technology, Henan Normal University, and Saint Petersburg State University.

Research output

Although CENRS is a newly established institution, it has already achieved a notable research position in Rwanda and internationally. In the Nature Index 2025–2026 assessment window (June 2025 to May 2026), CENRS ranked 8,715th globally and 14th in Rwanda by overall research output. Among non-profit organisations and non-governmental organisations (NPOs/NGOs), it ranked 2,761st globally and 7th in Rwanda. In terms of research output by subject area, CENRS ranked 4,823rd globally and 6th in Rwanda in the Natural Sciences, and 1,881st globally and 2nd in Rwanda in Earth and Environmental Sciences.

data.title: OGC SWE Common Data Model Encoding Standard
data.text:
----
The OGC SWE Common Data Model Encoding Standard (OGC document identifier 24-014) is an open geospatial standard published by the Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC) as part of its Sensor Web Enablement (SWE) suite. It defines low-level, self-describing data models and encodings for describing, structuring, and exchanging sensor observations, system parameters, and scientific datasets.

Version 3.0 supersedes version 2.0 (OGC 08-094r2) and introduces major updates, notably transitioning from XML to JSON encodings and aligning with modern OGC API standards.

== Overview ==
The SWE Common Data Model provides a conceptual and technical framework for describing heterogeneous sensor datasets and streams. It enables client applications and servers to interpret raw data values without prior out-of-band knowledge by bundling structural definitions, unit definitions, quality metrics, and external semantic links alongside the data payloads.

The standard addresses five primary aspects of data representation:

# Data Structure: Defining scalar values, records, arrays, and matrices.
# Semantics: Linking properties to external dictionaries, ontologies, or URIs.
# Representation: Explicitly defining data types such as numeric quantities, booleans, categories, or geometry components.
# Data Quality: Attaching accuracy, precision, and error metadata to components.
# Encoding: Specifying how values are formatted for transmission (e.g., JSON, ASCII, or binary).

== Key Changes in Version 3.0 ==
Version 3.0.0 represents a modernization of the standard, shifting toward JSON-centric web architectures and OGC API standards [ref: OGC SWE Common Data Model Encoding Standard, docs.ogc.org].

* JSON Encodings & Schemas: Added native JSON implementation schemas to streamline Web API integration and developer adoption.
* Removal of XML Encodings: Deprecated and removed legacy GML/XML encodings from the core specification to simplify the standard.
* Geometry Data Component: Introduced explicit geometry components modeled on OGC Simple Feature Geometries to allow vector spatial geometries to be embedded directly into sensor data components.
* Integration with Modern Standards: Serves as a foundational building block for contemporary specifications, including SensorML 3.0 and OGC API — Connected Systems.

== Core Data Components ==
The standard defines basic data components that can be composed into complex data structures:
{| class="wikitable"
!Data Component
!Description
!Example
|-
|Boolean
|Binary state representation (true/false).
|Motion detector status.
|-
|Category
|Discrete categorical value referencing a controlled vocabulary or code space.
|Camera mode (AUTO_FOCUS, MANUAL).
|-
|Quantity
|Continuous numeric value bound to a unit of measure or scale factor.
|Temperature reading (23.51 °C).
|-
|Count
|Discrete integer value for counting events or items.
|Particle count per volume.
|-
|Text
|Free-text string value or identifier.
|Sensor serial number or error code.
|-
|Time
|Temporal instant or interval tied to a time frame or epoch.
|ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.
|-
|Geometry
|Vector geometry object modeled on simple features.
|Point, LineString, or Polygon coordinates.
|}

=== Aggregate Components ===
These primitive components are combined into higher-level constructs:

* DataRecord: A collection of fields of varying types (similar to a struct or dictionary).
* DataArray: An array of homogeneous data components, allowing efficient streaming of time-series or multi-dimensional blocks.
* Vector / Matrix: Mathematical constructs built from ordered numerical quantities.

== Relationship to Other OGC Standards ==
SWE Common Data Model 3.0 is a shared specification within the OGC ecosystem:

* OGC SensorML 3.0: Uses SWE Common components to define inputs, outputs, parameters, and settings for sensor systems and processing chains.
* OGC API — Connected Systems Standard: Uses SWE Common 3.0 structures to encode observation data, stream payloads, and control commands in modern RESTful/JSON web interfaces.

== Standards Document Metadata ==

* OGC Document Identifier: 24-014
* External Identifier: [http://www.opengis.net/doc/IS/SWE/3.0](http://www.opengis.net/doc/IS/SWE/3.0)
* Normative Specification URI: [http://www.opengis.net/spec/SWE/3.0](http://www.opengis.net/spec/SWE/3.0)
* Editor: Alexandre Robin
* Approval Date: June 2, 2025
* Publication Date: July 16, 2025

data.title: Fakir Garibullah
data.text:
Fakir Garibullah (1680-1770) was a revolutionary 18th-century medieval Bengali poet and mystic who fundamentally reshaped vernacular literature in Bengal. He is celebrated as the absolute pioneer of the Puthi literature movement and the first prominent architect of Dobhashi (literally "two languages")—a syncretic literary style that blended Bengali with Arabic, Persian, and Hindustani vocabulary. [ref: ফকির গরীবুল্লাহ, Teachers Portal] [ref: ]

== Life ==
Because of a lack of formal historical documentation, exact biographical details regarding Garibullah's life are scarce.He was born in the village of Hafizpur, situated in the Baliya Pargana of the Hooghly district (which was a part of the greater Bardhaman region at the time) in 1680. [ref: ]His father was a local devout figure named Shah Dhundi (or Saha Dundi). The honorific title "Fakir" suggests that Garibullah either followed a family tradition of Islamic mysticism (Sufism) or adopted a lifestyle of ascetic, spiritual devotion.

== The Birth of the "Dobhashi" Style ==
Before Garibullah, medieval Bengali literature heavily relied on traditional Sanskritised vocabulary. Living during a time when the Mughal influence was deeply entrenched yet transitioning into colonial rule, Garibullah broke traditional conventions to cater to the masses.He blended everyday regional Bengali grammar with Arabic, Persian, and Hindi terms that ordinary Bengali Muslims used in their daily speech.This hybrid linguistic style came to be known as Dobhashi Bengali or Musalmani Bangla.

== Major Literary Contributions ==
Garibullah did not just write poems; he created narrative epics (puthis) meant to be rhythmically recited aloud to large rural audiences as a form of cultural memory and entertainment.His most celebrated works include Amir Hamza,Yusuf-Zulekha,Sonabhan & Sonabhaner Puthi and Satyapir Puthi. [ref: Lost-and-found: an epic tale, www.business-standard.com]

== Historical Legacy ==
Fakir Garibullah’s life marks the transition of Bengali literature out of the strict medieval courtly traditions and into the hands of the common folk. By normalising Arabic and Persian loanwords, his work paved the way for cheap, mass-printed Battala publications in 19th-century Calcutta, cementing his status as one of the most culturally influential Muslim voices in pre-modern Bengal.

data.title: GameBoost
data.text:
GameBoost is an online marketplace for video game digital goods, operated by the Croatian company Global Gaming Services d.o.o. The platform connects buyers with third-party sellers of game keys, gift cards, game accounts, in-game currency and items. The company was founded by Kristijan Salijević and registered in 2022 in Strmec Stubički, Krapina-Zagorje County.

== History ==
According to Salijević, the activity that became GameBoost began around 2017–2018 as a hobby during his university studies, with small initial earnings and no long-term business plan. The operating company, Global Gaming Services d.o.o., was entered in the Croatian court register on 28 February 2022.

In April 2022, the venture capital fund Fil Rouge Capital invested €500,000 in the company. In March 2023, Fil Rouge Capital and the impact investment fund Feelsgood Capital Partners closed a second round of €2 million, co-invested in equal shares, intended to fund expansion into new markets and additional games. At the time, the company reported more than 20 employees and around 700 freelancers, with most of its freelancers and customers based outside Croatia.

== Products ==
GameBoost operates as a marketplace on which verified third-party sellers list digital goods for video games, while the platform handles checkout, payments and customer support. Its main product categories include game keys, gift cards, game accounts, in-game currency, virtual items and account top-ups.

Game keys are sold for PC storefronts such as Steam, GOG, EA app and Ubisoft Connect, as well as for Xbox, PlayStation and Nintendo Switch consoles. Gift cards and subscription cards are offered for services including Steam, Xbox, PlayStation Network and Amazon.

The account category covers pre-made accounts for more than 200 games, including Fortnite, Valorant, Grand Theft Auto V, Clash of Clans and Counter-Strike 2. According to the company, sellers must pass verification before listing, and purchased accounts carry a 14-day warranty. The platform also has a marketplace for Counter-Strike 2 skins and items.

== Finances ==

== Recognition ==
GameBoost has been featured in several Croatian and European startup and business rankings.

In January 2024, the European startup publication EU-Startups included GameBoost in its list of ten innovative Croatian startups to watch in 2024, describing it as an "all-in-one platform designed to cater to the diverse needs of gamers". The company was again included in the publication's January 2025 list of ten promising Croatian startups, which noted that it had raised €2.5 million in funding.

In November 2024, founder Kristijan Salijević was named to the "30 Under 30" list compiled by the Croatian technology magazine VIDI. The list recognises people under the age of 30 for achievements in startups, science and information and communications technology, and was presented at the VIDI Awards ceremony, with previous honourees serving as the jury.

In April 2026, the business weekly Lider featured Salijević in its "40 Under 40" series on successful Croatian entrepreneurs. To be considered for the ranking, entrepreneurs had to be founders holding an active director-level role in a company with annual revenue above €1 million.

data.title: PiEEG
data.text:
PiEEG is a neurotechnology company based in Edinburgh, Scotland, that develops low-cost, open-source brain–computer interface (BCI) hardware for researchers, developers and hobbyists. Its devices measure electroencephalography (EEG), electromyography (EMG) and electrocardiography (ECG) signals.

== History ==
The company's first product, an EEG board for the Raspberry Pi, was developed after the 2020–2023 global chip shortage made an earlier standalone design too expensive. It launched on Crowd Supply in 2023 at US$250–$350. A 16-channel model followed in 2024. In 2026 the company announced PiEEG XR, an EEG face interface for Meta Quest headsets.

== Products ==

* PiEEG – an 8-channel EEG board for the Raspberry Pi 3 and 4.
* PiEEG-16 – a 16-channel board for the Raspberry Pi 5.
* IronBCI – a standalone wearable 8-channel BCI.
* PiEEG XR – a sensor face interface for the Meta Quest 3, aimed at developers, including for VRChat avatars.

== Reception ==
IEEE Spectrum presented PiEEG as an example of open-source hardware bringing BCI to makers. UploadVR called PiEEG XR a developer kit that still has to solve problems of fit, noise and calibration.

Susan Waycik (born January 17, 1992) is a professional comedy producer. She is known for her work on the comedy festival, Bestie Fest (2024), and as host/producer of the long-running Comedy Bar show, The BFF Variety Hour (2019 - 2024). Susan is currently the Managing Producer at Toronto's The Second City.

== Early Life ==
Susan Waycik was born in Thunder Bay, Ontario. Her family eventually relocated to Winnipeg, Manitoba, where she attended Dakota Collegiate.

After high school, Susan attended Sheridan College's Performing Arts Preparation Program, followed by the Musical Theatre Performance program at St. Lawrence College. She received the "Leadership Award" upon her graduation from St. Lawrence College. [ref: LinkedIn]

== Career ==
Susan performed as a cabaret singer and stand-up comedian for many years, until she began pursuing comedy producing full-time. Starting in 2016, Susan independently produced comedy shows all over Toronto, including: The BFF Variety Hour, Fresh Squeezed Comedy, Bi-Pandemonium, Slut Parade with Allie Pearse, Laugh Riot and Bestie Fest. Susan has produced both of Bren D'Souza's live comedy albums, Clever, Hip and Scary! and The Second Coming. [ref: Search for bren d'souza, Spotify]

== ZAŠTO U KESICAMA OMILJENIH GRICKALICA DOBIJAMO SVE MANJE SADRŽAJA: NAUČNICI OTKRILI TAJNU FORMULU “TIHOG SAMANJIVANJA” ==
Jeste li primijetili da kada otvorite vašu omiljenu grickalicu da obicno na dnu kesice ostane mnogo više praznog prostora nego ranije? Svi smo mislili da nam se pričinjava ili da fabrike samo štede na pakovanju, ali najnovija nezavisna istraživanja tržišta pokazuju da je riječ o sistematskom planu čiji je jedini cilj da nam daju manje, a da platimo [ref: DOI desativado, doi.org]više.

=== Šta kaže analiza “nestajuce gramaže”? ===
U nedavnoj studiji koju su sprovele evropske institucije za zaštitu potrošača naučnici su uporedili staru fabričku specifikaciju grickalica sa ovim što se danas nalazi na rafovima. Ispostavilo se da proizvođači već godinama ne mijenjaju cijenu, niti da drastično smanjuju samu kesicu spolja, već primjenjuju metodu poznatu kao „mikro-skaliranje mase“.

Istraživači tvrde da fabrike svake dvije godine tiho smanje količinu proizvoda u pakovanju tačno 5 do 8 gr. Pošto je ta razlika premala da bi je čovjek primijetio golim okom kada uzme kesicu u ruku, kupac nastavlja da plaća istu cijenu, nesvjestan da zapravo kupuje sve vazdušastiji I prazniji proizvod.
[[File:SnackfoodRackDF.JPG|thumb|Rafovi sa grickalicama]]

==== Izjava koja je sve otkrila: ====
Dr Marko Vasic, stručnjak za ekonomiju maloprodaje, objasnio je za stručne časopise kako fabrike uspijevaju da sakriju ovu prevaru: [ref: referenca se odnosi na izjavu stručnjaka]

„Proizvođači su shvatili da bi naglo podizanje cijena odmah izazvalo revolt kod kupaca. Zbog toga se odlučuju za mnogo efikasniji metod – tiho smanjivanje gramaže unutar iste ambalaže. Kupac misli da kupuje isto pakovanje kao i prije pet godina, ali zapravo u prosjeku dobija i do 20% manje proizvoda po istoj cijeni. To je čist profit za fabrike, dok potrošač plaća 'prazan hod',“ navodi se u izvještaju.

Based in Riga, the firm focuses on publicly traded companies across European and international equity markets. [ref: Vident Group, SIA, www.firmas.lv]

Vident Group was established in Riga, Latvia, in May 2026, operating within the financial research and consulting sector. The firm was founded with a focus on equity research, corporate financial analysis, and the evaluation of publicly traded companies across international capital markets. Its research activities encompass both buy-side and sell-side equity analysis, incorporating fundamental financial assessments and market-based analytical methodologies. [ref: Sabiedrība ar ierobežotu atbildību "Vident Group", 40203744523 - about - Kombo.lv, www.kombo.lv]

Vident Group conducts financial research on publicly traded companies across different industries and geographic markets. [ref: Vident Group,SIA - VERTA.LV]

Its activities include evaluating corporate financial performance, estimating intrinsic valuations, examining competitive environments, and assessing economic developments that may influence business performance. [ref: Vident Group,SIA - VERTA.LV]

== Настанак пројекта ==
Група студената са Београдског универзитета покренула је пројекат „Пауза 24“, којом позива младе да проведу један дан без друштвених мрежа. Идеја је настала након што су студенти приметили колико времена свакодневно проводе на телефонима, чак и када имају обавезе за факултет. Уместо да време искористе за учење, одмор или да га проведу са својом породицом/пријатељима, многи заврше скролујући сатима по интернету, а да тога нису ни свесни.

== Ширење на интернету ==
Покрет се брзо проширио међу студентима, првенствено преко Instagrama и Tiktoka, где су учесници делили колико времена проводе крај малих екрана. Уз hashtag #Пауза24, објављивали су снимке и позивали колеге да им се придруже. Организатори су истакли да циљ није да се друштвене мреже потпуно избаце из живота, већ да це људи подсете да постоји и живот ван екрана.

== Реакција јавности ==
Ипак, нису сви подржали ову идеју. Док једни сматрају да би дан без телефона помогао младима да се боље концентришу и више посвете себи, други мисле да су друштвене мреже постале важан део свакодневног живота. Преко њих студенти добијају информације о предавањима, договарају групне пројекте и прате актуелна дешавања свакодневно.

== Последице и утицај ==
Иако је реч о краткотрајном пројекту, „Пауза 24“ отворила је питање колико смо заправо зависни од својих телефона и да ли можемо да контролишемо време које проводимо на интернету. Неки учесници су одлучили да наставе да мање користе друштвене мреже и након завршетка акције, док су се други убрзо вратили старим (лошим) навикама.

data.text:
----

= Sähköverkon inertia =
Sähköverkon inertialla tarkoitetaan sähköjärjestelmään sitoutunutta liike-energiaa, joka vastustaa verkon taajuuden muutoksia. Tämä liike-energia muodostuu sähköverkkoon kytkettyjen suurien pyörivien koneiden massasta. Nämä koneet voivat sijaita voimalaitoksissa tai tehtaissa ja ne pyörivät sähköverkon kanssa samalla taajuudella. Sähköverkossa tuotannon ja kulutuksen täytyy olla koko ajan tasapainossa, tämän tasapainon heiluessa pyrkii myös verkon taajuus muuttumaan. Jos kulutus ylittää tuotannon, ottaa kuormitus tehonsa tahtigeneraattoreiden pyörivästä liike-energiasta, mikä hidastaa generaattoreita. Jos tuotantoa on enemmän kuin kulutusta, käy päinvastoin: tahtigeneraattoreiden liike-energia kasvaa, ne alkavat pyöriä nopeammin ja verkon taajuus kasvaa. Kulutuksen ja tuotannon välinen hetkellinen tasapaino siis ilmenee sähköverkon taajuudesta. [ref: Elovaara, J., & Haarla, L. (2011). Sähköverkot 1: järjestelmätekniikka. Gaudeamus.] Suomessa sähköverkon taajuuden sallittu vaihteluväli on 49,9 ja 50,1 Hz välillä [ref: Kulutuksen ja tuotannon tasapainon ylläpito, Fingrid].

data.title: Piper Theatre Productions
data.text:
Piper Theatre Productions is a non-profit contemporary theater organization in the Park Slope neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York City. It was cofounded in 2000 by siblings Rachel McEneny and John P. McEneny, who also serves as its artistic director. The company produces original theatrical works, with a focus on innovative storytelling. It is also active in educational programs and international collaborations. Its productions span multiple genres and styles and have received critical recognition.

== History ==
Piper Theatre Productions was founded in 2000 by John P. McEneny and Rachel McEneny (children of former NY Assemblymember John McEneny) with the mission of fostering original, physically engaging theater while providing opportunities for emerging artists.

Since its inception, the company has evolved into a multi-faceted arts organization known for its ambitious productions, youth programs, and collaborations with international artists and institutions.

=== Key Milestones: ===
2000: Launched a free outdoor Shakespeare summer theater program in Untermeyer Park,Yonkers, NY.

2005: Moved to the Old Stone House in Washington Park, Brooklyn, and produced free musicals including Sweeney Todd, Priscilla, Queen of the Desert, Peter Pan, You're a Good Man, Charlie Brown, and Psycho Beach Party.

2013: Piper's adaptation of [https://www.59e59.org/shows/show-detail/the-island-of-doctor-moreau/ The Island of Doctor Moreau] received Bobby's Sixth Star Award for Best Play at the Edinburgh Fringe Festival.

2017: Presented the North American premiere of We Should Have Seen the Lights Already by Matei Vișniec.

2023: Performed Mother Sauvage (an original adaptation of Guy de Maupassant's short story La Mère Sauvage) at the University of Malta.

2024: Premiered The Bloody Ballad of Bette Davis, a new musical by Rob Parker and John P. McEneny, at the Edinburgh Fringe Festival.

2025: Co-produced the award-winning CADEL, written and performed by Connor Delves, which went on to tour Australia and the UK. [ref: Cadel: Lungs on Legs review – a heart-pumping, hilarious portrait of an Australian cycling champion, The Guardian]

== Educational programs ==
Piper Theatre Productions provides training in acting, playwriting, and physical theater, offering young artists immersive opportunities in performance and stagecraft.

=== Youth Theatre ===
The Piper Summer Youth Program enrolls over 180 students annually, focusing on acting, playwriting, and theatrical production skills.

=== Process Drama ===
Drawing from the methods of Cecily O’Neill and Jerzy Grotowski, Piper integrates Process Drama into its educational framework, fostering deep artistic engagement and creative problem-solving.

= Jesse van den Boogaard =
Jesse van den Boogaard is een Nederlandse student uit Gelderland. Hij volgde middelbaar beroepsonderwijs aan het Candea College te Duiven en vervolgde in 2026 zijn opleiding in de richting van het spoorvervoer. Hij richt zich op een toekomstige loopbaan als treinmachinist.

== Biografie ==

=== Jeugd en Opleiding ===
Van den Boogaard volgde zijn middelbare schoolopleiding aan het Candea College in Duiven. Hij volgde daar de mavo/vmbo-gl-leerweg en rondde deze opleiding in 2026 af. [ref: ]

Tijdens zijn middelbare schooltijd volgde hij verschillende algemene en praktijkgerichte vakken. Voor zijn profielwerkstuk werkte hij samen met medeleerlingen aan een onderzoek naar landbouw. Het project werd beoordeeld met de kwalificatie goed. Ook verzorgde hij samen met zijn groepsgenoten een presentatie over het onderzoek.

Na het afronden van zijn middelbare school koos Van den Boogaard voor een vervolgopleiding die aansluit bij zijn belangstelling voor techniek en spoorvervoer.

=== Opleiding tot machinist ===
In 2026 begon Van den Boogaard aan de mbo-opleiding Machinist Railvervoer aan het ROC van Amsterdam. De opleiding is gericht op het beroep van treinmachinist en omvat kennis en vaardigheden die nodig zijn om veilig en verantwoordelijk in het spoorvervoer te werken.

Met deze opleiding richt hij zich op een loopbaan binnen de Nederlandse spoorwegsector. [ref: Home (Jongeren) - ROC van Amsterdam, www.rocva.nl]

=== Belangstelling voor het spoorvervoer ===
Van den Boogaard heeft bijzondere belangstelling voor het spoorvervoer en de techniek achter treinen. Zijn keuze voor de opleiding Machinist Railvervoer sluit aan bij zijn ambitie om beroepsmatig in deze sector te werken.

David Neelands
data.text:
William David Neelands (born October 30, 1943) is a Canadian Anglican priest, theologian, and academic administrator. [ref: New degree helps Orthodox Church, The Toronto Anglican] He is dean emeritus of the Faculty of Divinity at Trinity College, University of Toronto. [ref: Moral standard: Anglican church's role in Parlee Beach campground, CBC News] His research focuses on English theologian Richard Hooker, the English Reformation, Augustinianism [ref: Richard Hooker: His Life, Work, and Legacy: Essays in Honour of W. David Neelands, Daniel F. Graves & Scott Kindred-Barnes (co-editors)], and Anglican theology. [ref: From cults to colonialism: Tri-History Conference explores church role in trauma, survival, Anglican Journal]

He was named an honorary canon of St. James Cathedral and was elected to Alpha Sigma Nu. [ref: Orthodox school finds ‘natural home’ at Trinity, Anglican Journal] He is also a honorary fellow of Trinity College. [ref: David Neelands: Sixty-five years of conversation, Trinity Magazine]

== Education and career ==
Neelands recieved a BA with honours in 1965 and an MA in philosophy in 1966 from Trinity College, University of Toronto. [ref: Faculty of Divinity Convocation 2026, Trinity College] His master's thesis examined metaphysical explanation in the philosophy of Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz. He later studied theology at Pembroke College, Oxford.

He received an MDiv from Trinity College in 1978 and a ThD from Trinity College and the University of Toronto in 1988 with a doctoral thesis, The Theology of Grace of Richard Hooker. [ref: The Theology of Grace of Richard Hooker, Trinity College] Neelands began teaching philosophy at the University of Toronto in the 1960s and later became a lecturer at Trinity College. [ref: David Neelands: A Man of the People] In 2002, Neelands became dean of Trinity College’s Faculty of Divinity and Margaret E. Fleck Chair in Anglican Studies. [ref: College's new degree a 'great benefit' to Orthodox Church, The Diocese of Toronto] He held both positions until his retirement in 2017 and was subsequently named dean emeritus. He continued teaching historical theology and Anglican studies at Trinity College.

Neelands was ordained deacon in the Anglican Diocese of Toronto in 1977 and priest in 1979. He served in Canadian parishes and held temporary clerical appointments in England and Ireland. [ref: Clergy in Motion - 17 October, The Diocese of Toronto] In 2004, he was named an honorary canon of St. James Cathedral in Toronto. [ref: The CATHEDRAL CHURCH of ST. JAMES THE 217th REPORT TO VESTRY, STJAMES]

== Research ==
Neelands's research has focused on the history of Christian theology, particularly the work of Richard Hooker and the development of Anglican thought during the Reformation. [ref: THE LAW ON OUR HEARTS: RICHARD HOOKER AND THOMAS AQUINAS, The North American Anglican] His publications examine Hooker's views on predestination [ref: Richard Hooker and the Debates about Predestination 1580-1600, Toronto Journal of Theology], grace, the church, Christology, and the sacraments. [ref: ENGLISH MOLINISM IN THE LATE 1590s: RICHARD HOOKER ON FREE WILL, PREDESTINATION, AND DIVINE FOREKNOWLEDGE, The Journal of Theological Studies] His other research interests include Augustine, F. D. Maurice, Christian apologetics, and the theological history of the Thirty-nine Articles. [ref: A Calvinist Confession? Interpreting the Thirty-Nine Articles and Writing the History of the Reformation in Eighteenth-Century Ireland, The Journal of Religion]He has written and spoken on Anglican doctrine, liturgy [ref: Review of Pleading for Diversity: The Church Caspar Coolhaes Wanted. Reformed Historical Theology 44, Church History], ecumenism, and marriage. [ref: Anglican-Catholic Dialogues Discuss Marriage, Physician-assisted Suicide, Canadian Conference of Catholic Bishops]

data.title: Moya Chou
data.text:
Moya Chou () is a Taiwanese film colorist who has worked in post-production color grading for nearly thirty years, spanning both the photochemical and digital eras. [ref: 周佳聖獲金馬傑出電影工作者 調光周處除三害等片, [[Central News Agency (Taiwan)] [ref: 〈金馬63 年度台灣傑出電影工作者〉橫跨底片數位30年 光影魔術師周佳聖獲獎, Liberty Times] [ref: 第63屆金馬獎入圍名單公布, Taipei Golden Horse Film Festival Executive Committee] In 2026 he was named Outstanding Taiwanese Filmmaker of the Year by the Taipei Golden Horse Film Festival Executive Committee at the 63rd Golden Horse Awards, [ref: Nominees of the 63rd Golden Horse Awards Announced, Taipei Golden Horse Film Festival Executive Committee] [ref: Sabu's 'Arrested Memory' Leads Golden Horse Awards Nominations, Shu Qi's 'Girl' Close Behind, [[Variety (magazine)] and accepted the drama Innovation Award at the 61st Golden Bell Awards on behalf of the Netflix series Agent from Above (Jishen), on which he served as colorist. [ref: 金鐘61／《乩身》奪創新獎！調光師周佳聖緊張喊「想退休」 盼台劇登國際, Videoland News]

== Career ==
Moya Chou has worked in post-production color grading for close to thirty years, a career that spans the transition from photochemical film to digital cinema. He originally aspired to be an animator and had been accepted by an animation company, but on the advice of his elder brother, who worked at a film equipment company, he entered color grading instead, while the industry was still working on film. [ref: 調光師／周佳聖 《誰先愛上他的》驚艷許多觀眾的色彩，就是他的傑作！, Facebook (official page of Dear Ex)] In the early 2010s he graded films whose post-production was handled by 利達數位影音科技, including Taipei Exchanges and 金城小子; from 2011 he was credited as digital colorist under Pixelfly (傳翼數位影像) on films such as 10+10 and Machi Action, and on The Soul (2021) he was credited under Tetsujin Post-Production (大鐵人影製所). While at Pixelfly he took on his first television series, An Innocent Mistake (罪美麗), at the request of writer-producer Mag Hsu, and went on to grade her series Apple in Your Eye (妹妹) and her film Dear Ex. In December 2017 he spoke on digital grading practice, representing Pixelfly, at a forum of the Formosa Festival of International Filmmaker Awards in Taichung. [ref: 【國際論壇｜認識影像後期流程：數位調光實務分享】主講人：傳翼數位影像周佳聖, Facebook (Formosa Festival of International Filmmaker Awards)] He has graded feature films including Dear Ex, The Soul, I WeirDO, The Pig, the Snake and the Pigeon and A Foggy Tale, and in 2026 graded Sayang, 告別的年代 and The Photo from 1977. In television he has graded series such as Three Tears in Borneo and Imperfect Us, and Taiwan Cinema describes him as a renowned colorist who also runs filmmaking and color grading workshops to train industry talent. [ref: Moya CHOU, Taiwan Cinema]

On the public television series Three Tears in Borneo, Moya Chou set a warm, yellow-brown base grade with Kodak 400T-style film grain to convey the weight of a Second World War prison-camp story, contrasting it with brighter, more saturated colors for flashback scenes. [ref: 《聽海湧》主創分享系列 調光師_周佳聖, Facebook (official page of Three Tears in Borneo)] In 2020 he discussed his grading of I WeirDO in an interview on the podcast 後期刊. [ref: EP.09｜用顏色說故事的「怪胎」專訪 Ft. 調光師周佳聖, 後期刊 (podcast)] He has also taught color grading workshops, including at Unseen Film Studio's training program, covering shot balancing, color continuity and look development. [ref: 【調光工作坊｜課程紀錄】, Facebook (Unseen Film Studio)] [ref: 獨家｜走自己的路 金鐘導演孫介珩在高雄打造影視培力基地, Next Apple News]

On 1 October 2026, Wen Tien-hsiang, CEO of the Taipei Golden Horse Film Festival Executive Committee, announced Moya Chou as the Outstanding Taiwanese Filmmaker of the Year at the nominations press conference of the 63rd Golden Horse Awards. The committee cited his close collaboration with directors and cinematographers on stories set in different eras and cultural backgrounds. On 26 October 2026 he accepted the drama Innovation Award at the 61st Golden Bell Awards on behalf of Agent from Above, on which he served as colorist; in his speech he described innovation as "using new methods to explore more beautiful possibilities". [ref: 金鐘61／周佳聖憑《乩身》奪創新獎！自曝曾考慮退休 謝團隊開拓未知, Wow!NEWS (via yam.com)]

data.title: Wa Mao
data.text:
The Wa Mao (), also known as the Tile Cat, is a traditional apotropaic roof ridge ornament found on folk residences in Yunnan province, China. [ref: Tile cats: Yunnan's native ridge beasts, Yunnan.cn] Typically crafted from clay, shaped, and then glazed and fired in a kiln, the Wa Mao serves a dual symbolic purpose: to ward off evil spirits and to attract wealth and good fortune to the household. [ref: Yunnan Wa Mao "Leaps" into Daily Life, People's Daily Online]

Despite its name, the Wa Mao is not modeled after a domestic cat, but rather after a fierce tiger. [ref: Tracing the Wa Mao: A Mysterious Symbol Across Yunnan's Rooftops, Our China Story] This design philosophy is often described in Chinese folklore as having a "cat's appearance but a tiger's energy" (). [ref: The "Guardian" on the Rooftop: Yunnan Wa Mao, Yunnan Chinese Channel] The figure is characteristically depicted with a wide-open mouth and bulging, alert eyes, symbolizing its ability to swallow evil spirits and misfortune from all directions while welcoming prosperity. [ref: Yunnan Clay Sculpture "Wa Mao": The Cultural and Creative Revival of the Eaves Guardian, Daai Television]

== Appearance and symbolism ==

The Wa Mao is a unique form of folk ceramic sculpture. Although it is called a "cat," its visual features are heavily stylized to embody the ferocity and fearlessness of a tiger, which is traditionally regarded in Chinese culture as the king of beasts capable of devouring ghosts and malevolent entities. The typical Wa Mao features an exaggerated, wide-open mouth, wide eyes, and a grounded, seated posture mounted on a roof tile.

In traditional Yunnan belief systems, the rooftop is considered a threshold between the human dwelling and the outside world. Placing the Wa Mao at the highest point of the house, such as on the main roof ridge, flying eaves, or above the main gate, is believed to guard the household from harm, suppress negative influences, and prevent misfortunes such as fire. The ritual of installing a Wa Mao, sometimes referred to as "consecration," traditionally involves a ceremonial offering (such as dripping a rooster's blood on the figure) to endow it with spiritual power.

== Distribution and history ==
The cultural practice of using Wa Mao is widely distributed across Yunnan province, with notable variations in style and craftsmanship among different regions and ethnic groups. It is particularly prevalent in Yuxi, Qujing, Dali, Chuxiong, Wenshan, and the areas surrounding Kunming.

The tradition of placing these ceramic guardians on rooftops has a history spanning over a century in Yunnan. Historically, the craft was often carried out on a household or village basis by local pottery artisans. While the basic form remains consistent, regional variations exist; for example, some Wa Mao figures feature a Bagua (Eight Trigrams) diagram on their chest, while others may be made of stone (known as "Stone Cats") instead of clay in certain localities.

== Intangible cultural heritage ==
In recognition of its historical, artistic, and cultural value, the Yunnan Wa Mao was officially listed as a provincial-level intangible cultural heritage in 2023. In recent years, there has been a cultural and creative revival of the Wa Mao. Local artisans and designers have begun adapting the traditional motif into modern souvenirs, decorative art, and cultural products, ensuring the preservation and continuation of this unique folk tradition in contemporary society.

data.title: Moe Rubenstein
data.text:
Maurice "Moe" Rubenstein (March 16, 1905 – February 3, 2001) was an American high school football, basketball and baseball coach, athletic director, and teacher at Ambridge High School in Ambridge, Pennsylvania. He coached Ambridge football from 1929 through 1950. His Pittsburgh Post-Gazette obituary reported a career record of 146–32–10. His teams never had a losing season. [ref: Feldman, Jacob. The Jewish Experience in Western Pennsylvania: A History 1755–1945. Pittsburgh: The Historical Society of Western Pennsylvania, 1986, p. 205; Snyder, Ron. The History of Ambridge Football 1919–2017; "Maurice Rubenstein." Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, February 6, 2001; Beaver County Sports Hall of Fame entry, https://bcshof.org/halloffamers/rubenstein1977.htm; Rauh Jewish Archives, "A. P. Moore Club," https://rauhjewisharchives.org/entries/a-p-moore-club/]

He coached Ambridge basketball from 1929 through 1946 and compiled a record of 260–99–1 with six section titles. His baseball teams won two sectional championships. [ref: New Castle News, November 14, 1946, p. 24.]

Rubenstein was inducted into the Beaver County Sports Hall of Fame, the Pittsburgh Jewish Sports Hall of Fame, the Pennsylvania Scholastic Football Coaches Association Hall of Fame, the Western Pennsylvania Sports Hall of Fame, and the Geneva College Athletics Hall of Fame. He received the Geneva College Distinguished Service Award. In 1977, Ambridge High School renamed its football stadium "Moe Rubenstein Stadium". [ref: Geneva College Athletics Hall of Fame, "Moe Rubenstein," https://athletics.geneva.edu/honors/geneva-college-athletics-hall-of-fame/moe-rubenstein/60; The Times.]

Rubenstein is credited with helping numerous high school athletes obtain college scholarships. [ref: Bires, Mike. "Moe Was a Legend." Beaver County Times, October 24, 2018. https://www.timesonline.com/story/sports/high-school/football/2018/10/23/moe-was-legend/8385622007/]

He married Sally Walters on August 18, 1929. His wife later owned the Stork's Nest Children's Clothing Store on Merchant Avenue in Ambridge. They had one child, Arlene. [ref: "Sally Rubenstein." Beaver County Times, April 19, 2009. https://www.timesonline.com/story/news/2009/04/19/sally-rubenstein/18307564007/]

==Early life==

Rubenstein was born on March 16, 1905, in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, the son of Lazar and Annie Rubenstein. Lazar was an immigrant from the Ukrainian village of Pliskov and worked as a carpenter. [ref: Birth record, Pittsburgh Department of Public Health. The record lists the father's first name as "Louis" and his occupation as carpenter. Other sources reference his name as Lazar; Louis was likely an Americanized form. The birth certificate also spells the surname as "Rubinstein."] As one of the original settlers from Pliskov around 1900, Lazar Rubenstein invited fellow villagers to come to Pittsburgh, where they stayed in the Rubenstein home until they found housing elsewhere. As a result of the Rubensteins' efforts, Pittsburgh subsequently had a large colony of families who immigrated from Pliskov. [ref: Feldman, Jacob. The Jewish Experience in Western Pennsylvania: A History 1755–1945. Pittsburgh: The Historical Society of Western Pennsylvania, 1986, p. 148.]

Rubenstein grew up in the Hill District of Pittsburgh and attended the now-defunct Fifth Avenue High School. He graduated high school having won nine letters and was named All-City in three different sports: baseball, basketball and football. [ref: Feldman, Jacob. The Jewish Experience in Western Pennsylvania: A History 1755–1945. Pittsburgh: The Historical Society of Western Pennsylvania, 1986, p. 205.]

Rubenstein attended Geneva College in Beaver Falls, Pennsylvania. [ref: Geneva College Athletics Hall of Fame, "Moe Rubenstein," https://athletics.geneva.edu/honors/geneva-college-athletics-hall-of-fame/moe-rubenstein/60] During his senior year, he was captain of the basketball and baseball teams. He did not letter in football. He graduated from Geneva College in 1928.

==Coaching career==

Upon graduation from college, Rubenstein was hired at Ambridge High School as head basketball coach and assistant football coach. He was named head football coach in 1929.

Rubenstein coached football until 1950. His football teams won a WPIAL title in 1932. He also coached basketball from 1929 to 1946, compiling a record of 260–99–1 with six section titles, and his baseball teams won two sectional championships. He had a reputation as a strict disciplinarian who never used profanity and required that his players maintain good grades. [ref: Barrickman, Bob. "Rubenstein Set the Coaching Standard at Ambridge." The Times/Beaver Newspapers, September 2, 1999.] In 19 years of coaching basketball, he was never assessed a technical foul.

Rubenstein is credited with helping numerous high school athletes obtain college scholarships, including players from neighboring schools. He contacted University of Alabama coach Paul "Bear" Bryant to recommend Beaver Falls High School quarterback Joe Namath, who went on to star at Alabama and for the NFL's New York Jets.

Several of Rubenstein's players had notable careers in football. John Michelosen, after playing quarterback at Ambridge under Rubenstein, became the starting quarterback at the University of Pittsburgh from 1935 to 1937 under coach Jock Sutherland. [ref: Beaver County Sports Hall of Fame, "John Michelosen," https://bcshof.org/halloffamers/michelosen1976.htm] He played on Pitt's national championship teams in 1936 and 1937 and started in the Panthers' 21–0 victory over Washington in the 1937 Rose Bowl. In 1948, Michelosen became head coach of the Pittsburgh Steelers at age 32, making him the youngest NFL head coach in the league's modern era at the time. He coached the Steelers through 1951, compiling a 20–26–2 record, and then served as head football coach at the University of Pittsburgh from 1955 to 1965, compiling a 56–49–7 record. Michelosen was inducted into the Pennsylvania Sports Hall of Fame in 1970.

After retiring from coaching, Rubenstein continued to teach math and gym classes at Ambridge High School until 1964. [ref: Emert, Rich. "Maurice Rubenstein." Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, February 6, 2001.]

==Later life and honors==

In 1967, Rubenstein moved to Hollywood, Florida, with his wife, Sally Walters Rubenstein. He enjoyed golfing and was a substitute teacher until his early 90s.

He was inducted into the Beaver County Sports Hall of Fame, the Pittsburgh Jewish Sports Hall of Fame, the Pennsylvania Scholastic Football Coaches Association Hall of Fame, and the Geneva College Athletics Hall of Fame. He received the Geneva College Distinguished Service Award. In 1977, Ambridge High School renamed its football stadium "Moe Rubenstein Stadium".

Shortly before his death, Rubenstein moved to Seminole, Florida, and died on February 3, 2001.

==Archives==

Rubenstein's papers and memorabilia are preserved in the Moe Rubenstein Scrapbooks collection at the Rauh Jewish History Program & Archives at the Senator John Heinz History Center in Pittsburgh.

data.title: William Clark (academic)
data.text:
----

For other people named William Clark, see William Clark (disambiguation).

William Clark (1953 - 2017) was a Historian and author. Though trained in the History of science, much of his work was on the broader History of European universities, about which he wrote many articles. This was also the topic of his award-winning book, Academic Charisma and the Origins of the Research University. In addition, he also published several edited books on the history of science and of modern Bureaucracy.

== Early life and education ==
William Clark was born in southern California and grew up there, studying at the University of California, Los Angeles. He received his Ph.D. degree in European history from there in 1986, with a dissertation titled "From the Medieval Universitas Scholarium to the German Research University - A Sociogenesis of the German Academic"; the dissertation was advised by Robert S. Westman and M. Norton Wise. [ref: https://www.proquest.com/docview/303398279/abstract/E2B1833B558C40B1PQ/1?sourcetype=Dissertations%20&%20Theses]

== Career ==
Clark was an expert on the history of the University. In his numerous articles, he traced the origins of such features of academic life as the Doctor of Philosophy and the Seminar. [ref: Bill Clark or the Ironic Analyst of homo academicus, History of Science Society Newsletter] [ref: Bill Clark or the Ironic Analyst of homo academicus, CAKtus: Le carnet du Centre Alexandre-Koyre] His book Academic Charisma and the Origins of the Research University traced a series of shifts from the Oral culture of the Medieval university to the modern Research university. In an essay review of the book in The New Yorker, Anthony Grafton described it as a study of "the mixed inheritance of the modern university", and said that Clark "[made] his case with analytic shrewdness, an exuberant love of archival anecdote, and a wry sense of humor." [ref: The Nutty Professors, The New Yorker] The book won the Morris D. Forkosch Prize awarded by the Journal of the History of Ideas for the best book in Intellectual history published in 2006. [ref: Notices, Journal of the History of Ideas]

Clark was also active in assembling Edited volumes on the history of science. One such volume he edited (with co-editors Jan Golinski and Simon Schaffer), titled The Sciences in Enlightened Europe, assembled scholarly contributions on a wide range of Branches of science during the 18th century Age of Enlightenment. [ref: The Sciences in Enlightened Europe, University of Chicago Press] Another work he edited, along with Peter Becker, was Little Tools of Knowledge: Historical Essays on Academic and Bureaucratic Practices. [ref: Little Tools of Knowledge: Historical Essays on Academic and Bureaucratic Practices., University of Michigan Press]

Clark held teaching positions at a number of institutions including Columbia University and Bryn Mawr College in the US, the University of Göttingen in Germany, and the University of Cambridge in the UK. He also held a research fellowship at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science in Germany. Despite these accomplishments, however, he never held a Tenure-track position. [ref: In Memoriam - William Clark, 1953-217, History of Science Society Newsletter] [ref: Erinnerung an Bill Clark, Nach Feierabend: Materialgeschichten]

data.text:

[user] is an Indian cyclist from Jammu and Kashmir known for long-distance cycling and Guinness World Records achievements. [ref: Fastest journey from Kashmir to Kanyakumari by bicycle (male), Guinness World Records]

== Cycling career ==

In March 2021, Teli completed a bicycle journey from Kashmir to Kanyakumari in 8 days, 1 hour and 39 minutes. [ref: How [user] set a new record for cycling from Kashmir to Kanyakumari, Mint Lounge]

In September 2022, Teli established a Guinness World Records title for the fastest cycle journey of the Manali–Leh highway, completing it in 29 hours, 18 minutes and 21 seconds. [ref: Fastest cycle journey of the Manali-Leh highway (male), Guinness World Records]

In March 2021, Teli completed a bicycle journey from Kashmir to Kanyakumari in 8 days, 1 hour and 39 minutes, setting a Guinness World Records title for the fastest journey from Kashmir to Kanyakumari by bicycle (male). [ref: Fastest journey from Kashmir to Kanyakumari by bicycle (male), Guinness World Records] His achievement received coverage from Mint, NDTV and The New Indian Express. [ref: How [user] set a new record for cycling from Kashmir to Kanyakumari, Mint Lounge] [ref: 23-Year-Old [user] Sets Guinness World Record, Covers 3,600 Kms In 8 Days, NDTV] [ref: Cycling from north to south in record time, The New Indian Express]

In 2025, Teli qualified for the UCI Gran Fondo World Championships in Australia. [ref: [user] qualifies for the 2025 UCI Gran Fondo event, ETV Bharat] In 2026, he participated in the UCI Gran Fondo World Championships in Niseko, Japan. [ref: [user]'s participation in Japan, Rising Kashmir]

data.title: Mt. Kili
data.text:
Mt. Kili is an American indie folk duo from Asheville, North Carolina, consisting of singer-songwriter and guitarist Rick Sichta and drummer and percussionist Matt Shepard. Violinist and vocalist Laney Barnett is featured on the group's second album. [ref: Mt. Kili – The Noticer, Obscure Sound] [ref: Mt. Kili releases new album, Plastic Magazine] [ref: The Noticer Is a Rich, Natural Evolution for Mt. Kili, Rotate Magazine] [ref: Discover Mt Kili's The Noticer, York Calling]

The project's second studio album, The Noticer, was recorded at Echo Mountain Studio in Asheville and expanded the home-recorded approach of its debut into a collaborative studio arrangement.

== History ==
Plastic Magazine reported that Sichta introduced the project with the single "Tomorrow" in 2023 and followed it with the home-recorded debut album Ten Songs for My Girls, for Now and Later in 2024. The publication described the debut as centered on voice and classical guitar and written for Sichta's twin daughters.

For The Noticer, the project developed into a fuller-band collaboration with Shepard and Barnett. Plastic Magazine, York Calling, Echo Mountain Recording, and La Caverna credited Julian Dreyer with engineering and David Glasser with mastering, while multiple reviews described the contrast between the debut's home recording and the second album's studio production. [ref: So Far in 2026: New Music From Echo Mountain Artists, Echo Mountain Recording] [ref: De la Cruda Identidad Urbana al Folk de Autor y Ritmos Híbridos, La Caverna]

A third album, Ikigai, is scheduled for release on 1 May 2027. Sichta wrote the album during a summer spent alone in Costa Rica; Songwriter Safari described its songs as questions "about where we came from, what we're doing here, where we're going", completing an arc across the three records in which the debut was "giving", The Noticer is "seeing", and Ikigai is "asking". [ref: From Mountain Trails to Mt. Kili, Songwriter Safari (Late Bloomers Rock)]

== Reception ==
Obscure Sound published a track-by-track review and called the album "one of the strongest folk albums of 2026 so far", while describing the songwriting and gradually developing arrangements. Plastic Magazine also reviewed the record track by track, focusing on the transition from solo home recordings to an ensemble studio production and describing "The Weather Report" as using "hypnotic instrumentation".

Clout characterized the album's flow as hypnotic and ambitious, discussed the title track's gradual build, and noted the restrained acoustic treatment of "The Road Isn't as Long as It Seems". [ref: Album Review: Mt. Kili – The Noticer, Clout] Rotate Magazine framed the album as a fuller development of the debut, crediting Barnett's violin and vocals and Shepard's rhythmic role, and described the result as "deeply human".

Dave Franklin, writing for Dancing About Architecture, compared the use of space in "Don't Start a War" to Damien Rice and connected the record's intimate scale with songs informed by Sichta's reported travels in China, Tibet, and near Mount Everest. [ref: The Noticer – Mt. Kili, Dancing About Architecture] The Slow Music Movement reviewed the album track by track and characterized Sichta's voice as a "roots music lifeline" in contrast with derivative folk music. [ref: Mt. Kili – The Noticer (Self Release) [Alt-Folk], The Slow Music Movement]

Lost In The Manor featured the opening track "Don't Start a War" in its LITM Rock Picks roundup on 19 April 2026, writing that the track "feels like a cosy corner of a bookshop or a cinematic walk in the rain". [ref: LITM Rock Picks, Lost In The Manor]

York Calling reviewer Graeme Smith described the lyrics as "poetic and stirringly devastating" and the album as "a fantastic introduction" to the project. An EARMILK feature by Natalie Patrick dated 20 April 2026 described the album as a further development of the group's identity and sound. [ref: Mt. Kili takes a bold step in the folk journey with sophomore album The Noticer, EARMILK]

The Big Takeover reviewed the album on 22 April 2026, describing the songs as "hushed and whispered" and comparing the use of space in "Don't Start a War" to Damien Rice, concluding that the group speaks volumes by revelling in "the simplicity of song". [ref: Mt. Kili – The Noticer (self-released), The Big Takeover]

No Transmission wrote that the album "rewards patience through careful songwriting and a clear sense of purpose" and is "quietly resonant long after it ends". [ref: Mt. Kili find quiet revelation in expansive folk on 'The Noticer', No Transmission]Voxwave Magazine reviewed the album in April 2026 in a piece by Helena Lynch titled "Ten Songs, One Mountain, No Limits". [ref: Ten Songs, One Mountain, No Limits, Voxwave Magazine]

Distortion Diaries reviewed the album on 28 April 2026 under the title "Mt. Kili's Quiet Masterclass in Seeing the World Anew", writing that the collection encourages "stillness, reflection, and genuine connection". [ref: Mt. Kili's Quiet Masterclass in Seeing the World Anew, Distortion Diaries]

Rattler Magazine reviewed the album on 27 April 2026, writing that it earns attention "through sincerity, craft, and emotional clarity". [ref: Mt. Kili: The Noticer, Rattler Magazine]

Honk Magazine reviewed the album on 29 April 2026, calling it "a warm, contemplative acoustic folk album that finds beauty in the minutiae of life itself" and "a reflective album with a soft reminder that sometimes the smallest moments mean the most". [ref: Mt. Kili delivers quiet power and honest reflection on The Noticer, Honk Magazine]

The Dutch blog Le Future Wave reviewed the album on 3 May 2026 and concluded: "Mt. Kili have always had the songwriting. What The Noticer proves is that they now have everything else too." [ref: Mt. Kili – The Noticer (Album), Le Future Wave]

Conversations About Her featured the album on 10 May 2026, writing that it "arrives as a meaningful step forward for the Asheville-based project". [ref: Mt. Kili Expand Their Folk World With Richer, More Textured Sophomore Album 'The Noticer', Conversations About Her]

Songplode reviewed the album on 12 May 2026 in "Mt. Kili Find Stillness in Motion on The Noticer", writing: "What makes The Noticer resonate is its trust in stillness." [ref: Mt. Kili Find Stillness in Motion on The Noticer, Songplode]

The Brazilian publication Os Garotos de Liverpool featured the album on 12 May 2026, describing it as intimate and welcoming, with cinematic arrangements, "moving from beginning to end". [ref: Mt. Kili revela 'The Noticer', seu intimista e relaxante segundo álbum, Os Garotos de Liverpool]

Sameway Magazine featured the album in June 2026, covering all ten tracks and writing that "listening to the album in full feels like a carefully planned journey". [ref: Mt. Kili invite listeners on a mesmerizing journey with new album 'The Noticer', Sameway Magazine]

Indie Boulevard spotlighted "The Weather Report" on 24 July 2026, noting the tension carried through its accumulating drums, strings and chiming guitar. [ref: Mt. Kili forecast a storm of feeling on 'The Weather Report', Indie Boulevard]

Echo Mountain Recording, the studio where the album was made, included it in a survey of the studio's 2026 releases and wrote: "One of our favorites of the year, The Noticer from Mt. Kili arrived this spring as a thoughtful collection of folk songs that rewards repeat listens." Because the studio participated in the recording, this is an affiliated rather than independent assessment.

Asheville Stages included The Noticer among its "Favorite Local Albums of the Year (So Far)" and wrote that "Rick Sichta's heartfelt folk songs don't forcefully grab your attention — they earn it through patient, timeless songcraft." The outlet selected "Kyle" as its favorite track and recommended the album to listeners of Iron & Wine, Damien Rice, and José González. [ref: Favorite Local Albums of the Year (So Far), Asheville Stages]

The Spanish publication La Caverna featured "The Weather Report" in a multi-artist discovery article, describing it as a key song from the acclaimed second album and saying critical response had placed the record among the year's best. The feature credited Julian Dreyer with engineering at Echo Mountain Studios and David Glasser with mastering.

Grateful Web featured the album in October 2026 in "Mt. Kili Expands Its Folk Sound on 'The Noticer'", tracing the project's growth from Sichta's home recordings to the Echo Mountain sessions and noting the band was already looking ahead to Ikigai. [ref: Mt. Kili Expands Its Folk Sound on 'The Noticer', Grateful Web]

On 23 October 2026, Vicki Morrison Goble's Songwriter Safari (Late Bloomers Rock) published Spotlight No. 78, "From Mountain Trails to Mt. Kili", a profile of the duo that featured the song "Kyle" and previewed Ikigai.

The duo has also discussed the album in interviews, including a five-question interview with Punk Head published in October 2026, "Mt. Kili Writes for One Person and Lets the Song Find Everyone Else", [ref: Mt. Kili Writes for One Person and Lets the Song Find Everyone Else, Punk Head] and a ten-question interview with The Other Side Reviews, "A Chat with Mt. Kili", published the same month. [ref: A Chat with Mt. Kili, The Other Side Reviews]

The debut album also received international editorial coverage on its release. Illustrate Magazine reviewed "Fall Asleep in the Sunlight" in May 2024. [ref: "Fall Asleep in the Sunlight" by Mt. Kili Review, Illustrate Magazine] The Spanish publication El Descafeinado published a story-led feature on the album on 11 March 2024, three days after its release, centered on its origin as lullabies written for Sichta's twin daughters and quoting his account of their asking him to put the songs "on the radio". [ref: El cantautor Mt. Kili graba una carta de amor para sus hijas, El Descafeinado] The Brazilian site Music for All reviewed "Fall Asleep in the Sunlight" on 23 May 2024, describing it as "uma serena observação das preciosidades que não voltam" ("a serene observation of the precious things that do not return"). [ref: "Fall Asleep in the Sunlight" a serenidade de apreciar cada momento, Music for All] Lost In The Manor included "Fall Asleep in the Sunlight" in its LITM Singer-Songwriter Picks on 26 May 2024, praising its "delightfully minimalistic production style" and calling it "a comforting, repeat-worthy listen". [ref: LITM Singer-Songwriter Picks Teem With Talents like Mt Kili and more!, Lost In The Manor]

== Musical style ==
Reviewers have described Mt. Kili using indie-folk, folk-rock, alternative-folk, freak-folk, acoustic, and singer-songwriter terms. Coverage of The Noticer emphasizes acoustic guitar, violin, percussion, vocal harmonies, and arrangements that move between sparse and fuller ensemble passages.

Dancing About Architecture compared aspects of the group's use of space to Damien Rice. Asheville Stages recommended The Noticer to listeners of Iron & Wine, Damien Rice, and José González.

== Discography ==

=== Studio albums ===

* Ten Songs for My Girls, for Now and Later (8 March 2024)

* The Noticer (7 March 2026)

* Ikigai (scheduled 1 May 2027)

== References ==

== External links ==

* [https://mtkilimusic.com Official website]
* [https://mtkili.bandcamp.com Mt. Kili] on Bandcamp

data.title: Blake Schultz
data.text:
= Blake Schultz =
Blake Schultz (born July 3, 2003) is an American business development professional associated with [https://agdrives.com/ AG Drives], a driveline manufacturing company based in Green Bay, Wisconsin. He serves as the company's director of business development, working across sales, marketing, digital strategy, and business operations. Schultz graduated from the University of Minnesota in 2025 with a degree in business marketing.

== Early life ==
Blake Schultz was born in Green Bay, Wisconsin, and grew up in the Green Bay area. His early experiences in the region preceded his involvement in manufacturing and business development.

He attended high school in the Green Bay area before enrolling at the University of Minnesota. Through his subsequent professional work, he became involved with AG Drives, a company with longstanding family connections to the regional manufacturing industry.

== Education ==
Blake Schultz attended the University of Minnesota from 2021 to 2025, earning a degree in business marketing through the College of Education and Human Development. His academic studies included management, organizational leadership, entrepreneurship, and business law. He also earned a university sales certificate. Additionally, was apart of the Beta Eta Chapter of Delta Tau Delta Fraternity from 2022-2025 and was the Fraternity Awards & Accreditations Report Chairman for the 2024 year. While also serving on the Honor Board and the Social Commitee.

During his university years, Schultz participated in student leadership and investment research activities. From February to December 2024, he served as president of the College of Education and Human Development Student Board.

He also volunteered with the David S. Kidwell Funds Enterprise's Growth Fund Consumer Team from February to September 2024. In that role, he gained exposure to financial research and company analysis, using tools including Bloomberg Terminal, Capital IQ, and Microsoft Excel.

Schultz's university experience included an international study experience in Madrid, Spain. He has also pursued professional development outside his degree program, including participation in the Professional Golfers' Association of America Professional Golf Management pathway.

== Career ==

=== Early professional experience ===
Before and during his transition into business development, Schultz gained experience in customer service, sales, team leadership, and operational work. These experiences contributed to his interest in business management and entrepreneurship.

He also maintained professional involvement in golf operations, including work with Green Bay Country Club. His experience across different industries provided exposure to customer relationships, service delivery, and organizational operations.

=== AG Drives ===
Schultz joined AG Drives, a Green Bay-based manufacturer of custom driveshafts and industrial driveline components, in a role focused initially on developing the company's website and digital presence. He subsequently assumed broader responsibilities in business development.

As director of business development, Schultz works across sales, marketing, branding, digital strategy, and business growth. His responsibilities have also included contributing to the implementation of an enterprise resource planning system and supporting improvements to internal business processes.

AG Drives manufactures and services driveline products for customers in industries including agriculture, oil and gas, paper production, steel, food processing, construction, and other industrial sectors.

In August 2026, The Business News reported that AG Drives had experienced approximately 300 percent revenue growth over the preceding year. The publication described Schultz's work on the company's website, online presence, branding, and business development as part of its broader modernization efforts.

Schultz has described the company's approach as a combination of manufacturing heritage and innovation, emphasizing the role of modern business practices in developing an established industrial trade.

=== Public engagement and industry involvement ===
Schultz has represented AG Drives in regional business and manufacturing discussions. His professional activities have included participation in manufacturing roundtables associated with the Greater Green Bay Chamber's economic development network.

In 2026, Schultz appeared alongside AG Drives president Robby Burton on Swarfcast, a manufacturing-industry podcast hosted by Noah Graff of Today's Machining World. The episode, titled Business School vs. Learning on the Job, explored the contrasting educational and professional paths of Schultz and Burton, the development of AG Drives, and the relationship between formal business education and practical experience.

Schultz has also contributed to the company's public communications through interviews, social media, and business-community engagement.

== Professional interests ==
Schultz's professional interests include business development, entrepreneurship, marketing, manufacturing, organizational leadership, and the application of technology to business operations. His work at AG Drives combines commercial responsibilities with exposure to manufacturing processes and the operational requirements of a growing industrial company.
