data.title: Yan Margulis
data.text:
Yan Margulis is a renovation contractor and owner of Capable Group, an Ontario business whose work includes basement, kitchen, bathroom and full-home renovations in Toronto and the Greater Toronto Area. [ref: Cap-Able Group Consulting Inc., Better Business Bureau] [ref: Home Renovation in Toronto, Capable Group]

== Career ==
Before establishing Capable Group, Margulis worked directly on renovations and alongside different trades. The company, established in 2017, brought those areas of experience into one business. In a September 2024 advertorial, City Life described Margulis as having more than 25 years of renovation experience and reported his explanation that combining his previous work led to the company's formation. [ref: Capable Group Inc.: Transform Your Space With The Best, City Life] The Better Business Bureau records the business as established on 5 April 2017.

Capable's initial focus was basement renovation. By the time of the 2024 profile, its work had expanded into kitchens, bathrooms and other residential spaces.

== Renovation work ==
In a century-old basement, a project that began as refinishing expanded to include underpinning, waterproofing and structural reinforcement. The homeowner reported that Capable handled the additional work within the agreed budget, while the project manager and site supervisor remained responsive to questions. This account was published by the customer on HomeStars on 9 December 2024. [ref: Reviews of Capable Group – Basement Renovation & Finishing Company, HomeStars]

After Capable finished her basement, Mary Noce hired the company again for a full kitchen renovation. In her account, the team worked with her kitchen vision and Ludmila's design input, with plumbing and electrical trades contributing to the finished room. Noce credited Margulis and Ludmila's experience and leadership, and reported that the work finished within the established timeframe and budget. She described the sequence in a HomeStars review published on 8 January 2025.

The company's HomeStars profile also records recognition in 2025: it displays a Best of Awards 2025 badge and identifies Capable as a five-time winner. The award belongs to Capable Group. [ref: Profile of Capable Group – Basement Renovation & Finishing Company, HomeStars]

The broader review record includes 84 HomeStars reviews with a displayed rating of 4.9 out of 5 on the page consulted in October 2026. A separate Birdeye listing displayed 80 reviews attributed to Google for Capable Group Design Build Renovations. [ref: Capable Group Design Build Renovations, Birdeye]

The company's published portfolio also includes full-home renovations. Its Mississauga case study follows a completed project from the covered front entry through the main floor and into the basement. The documented scope includes the kitchen, living and dining areas, bathrooms and basement rooms, bringing several parts of the house within the same renovation. [ref: Mississauga Full-Home Renovation, Capable Group]

Capable describes its full-home service as coordinating design, permits and construction, with a project lead and an itemized fixed quote for the agreed scope. Its design-build process includes reviewing how layouts, building services, material selections and the order of trades connect across the project. [ref: Design-Build Renovations Toronto, Capable Group]

== Maryani Kitchen Studio ==
As of October 2026, Maryani Kitchen Studio's website presented it as part of Capable Group, with a focus on custom kitchens in Toronto and the Greater Toronto Area. The site describes Maryani as growing out of Capable's residential renovation work and combining that experience with cabinetmaking. It identifies Margulis as Capable Group's founder and owner, and describes the studio's services as designing, making and installing kitchens. [ref: Maryani Kitchen Studio — Custom Kitchens in Toronto & the GTA, Maryani Kitchen Studio]

== Renovation approach ==
Margulis has discussed the relationship between a room's intended use and the construction it requires. In CAA Magazine, he explained that converting a basement into a separate apartment involves additional building requirements, materials and labour compared with finishing it for personal use. [ref: What to expect when renovating a basement, CAA North & East Ontario]

In the 2024 City Life profile, Margulis identified completed spaces, satisfied clients and keeping work within the client's budget as motivations for his work. The same profile described showroom visits and three-dimensional renderings used to present the proposed space and materials before clients signed a contract.

data.title: Jaguars In California
data.text:
Jaguars currently do not live naturally in California anymore, with the most of the last sightings in the late 1800s to early 1900s. Jeff A. Alvarez in [https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/64770365 “Jaguars of California,”] took into account thousands of pages in Jaguar fur trade, hunting records, archeology, and paleontology, confirming jaguar populations from records throughout the 1800s. Panthera onca fossils have been found near San Diego, Alameda County, Los Angeles, San Bernardino, and Tassajara, California. In 1989, Seymour in "Jaguars of California", proposed a range for Jaguars from the Tehachapi Mountains to the Colorado River drainage. Part 1 of the [https://ecos.fws.gov/docs/recovery_plan/Final%20Jaguar%20Recovery%20Plan_July%202018.pdf? Jaguar Recovery Program] from the United States Fish and Wildlife Service suggest that the last individual Jaguar sighting in California occurred in the 1950s where it was shot after traveling over 800km from its original point of origin. Other accounts from [https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-1997-07-22/pdf/FR-1997-07-22.pdf?utm%20source=chatgpt.com The Federal Register] show evidence of several sightings pulled from documents in 1814 and 1860, show that Cahuilla Indians of the Coachella Valley, San Jacinto and the Santa Rosa Mountains of southern California were familiar with the jaguars.

data.title: National Squash League
data.text:
----

The National Squash League (NSL) is a professional team squash league in the United States. Unlike professional squash, which is primarily an individual sport, the NSL organizes players into city-based teams and uses a three-on-three format played over timed periods. [ref: National Squash League finishes second season with 'a completely different take' on the game, The Philadelphia Inquirer] [ref: US Squash, National Squash League Form Strategic Partnership, SportsTravel]

The league began competitive play in 2024 with six men's teams. It expanded in 2025 to nine men's teams and introduced a four-team women's competition. In the 2026–27 season, the league has 16 teams, consisting of ten men's teams and six women's teams. [ref: National Squash League aims to increase visibility ahead of LA 2028 Olympics, Squash Mad] [ref: National Squash League, National Squash League]

The league was founded by squash players Timmy Brownell and Spencer Lovejoy together with Fernando Valdizan. Valdizan served as the league's commissioner during its early seasons.

== History ==

=== Inaugural season ===
The NSL held its first player draft in 2024. Six teams competed in the inaugural men's season: the Atlanta Tornados, Chicago Grizzlies, Derby City Colts, Nashville Crushers, Newport Dragons and New York City Knights.

The first season concluded with the New York Knights facing the Nashville Crushers in the championship match at the Arlen Specter US Squash Center in Philadelphia. New York defeated Nashville to become the inaugural NSL champion. [ref: New York Knights Defeat Nashville Crushers to Lift Inaugural NSL Title, US Squash]

=== 2025 season ===
The league expanded during its second competitive season in 2025. The men's competition grew to nine teams and a four-team women's competition was introduced.

The Philadelphia Lightning won the 2025 men's championship after defeating the Lake Erie Beacons 4–0 in the final. The Philadelphia Freedom won the inaugural women's championship after their final against the District Inferno was tied following regulation and decided by a shootout. [ref: Philadelphia Freedom and Lightning Conquer NSL Finals, US Squash]

Both championships were decided at the Arlen Specter US Squash Center in Philadelphia.

=== 2026 season ===
The 2026 playoffs were held at MSquash in South Norwalk, Connecticut.

In the men's championship, the Chicago Grizzlies faced the Greenwich Panthers. The match finished regulation tied 2–2 and went to a shootout. Chicago won the shootout and the match 3–2 to capture the franchise's first NSL championship. [ref: From Winless to Champions. Chicago Grizzlies Capture 2026 NSL Championship in Overtime Thriller Over Greenwich Panthers, National Squash League]

The DC Inferno won the women's championship. Their final against the New York Queens also ended 2–2 in regulation before DC won the shootout 3–2. [ref: Inferno Complete Remarkable Playoff Run with Championship Shootout Victory, National Squash League]

=== 2026–27 season ===
The 2026–27 regular season began on October 16, 2026. The men's competition consists of ten teams and the women's competition consists of six teams. [ref: NSL Unveils First Half of 2026/27 Season Schedule, National Squash League]

The Carolina Pirates joined the men's competition following the relocation of the Newport Dragons to Charleston, South Carolina, while the Seattle Freeze added a men's team alongside its existing women's team.

The Chicago Grizzlies entered the season as defending men's champions, while the DC Inferno entered as defending women's champions. [ref: National Squash League to be Broadcast Live on SQUASHTV Throughout 2026-27 Season, Daily Squash Report]

The 2026–27 season includes several internationally ranked professional players, including Mostafa Asal of the Greenwich Panthers, Olivia Weaver of the Philadelphia Freedom, Diego Elías of the New York Knights and Fayrouz Aboelkheir of the New York Queens.

The playoffs are scheduled for March 5–7, 2027, at the Arlen Specter US Squash Center in Philadelphia. [ref: US Squash and National Squash League Announce Expanded Partnership, US Squash]

== Competition format ==
NSL matches are three-on-three team contests played using a running clock. Matches are divided into three timed periods. The first two periods last 20 minutes and are worth one match point each, while the third period lasts 30 minutes and is worth two match points. [ref: The NSL Team Format, National Squash League]

The league permits substitutions during stoppages. It also uses two-minute power plays, during which only the team that activated the power play can serve and score.

If the teams are tied after the three periods, the match is decided by a shootout. Players face one another for one rally at a time in lineup order, with the first team to win three shootout rallies winning the match.

== Teams ==
The NSL's current standings list ten men's teams and six women's teams for the 2026–27 season.

== Partnership with US Squash ==
The NSL and US Squash, the national governing body for squash in the United States, announced a strategic partnership ahead of the inaugural season. The partnership was intended to share resources and increase participation and viewership of squash in the United States.

In September 2026, US Squash and the NSL announced an expanded partnership. US Squash designated the NSL as its official team squash league, and the league established its headquarters at the Arlen Specter US Squash Center.

== Media and sponsorship ==
Matches during the 2026–27 season are carried live on SQUASHTV. Coverage published ahead of the season said the schedule would feature 22 matches across the United States between October 2026 and March 2027.

In October 2026, iHeartMedia became the NSL's Official Audio Media Partner and title sponsor for the 2026–27 season. [ref: National Squash League Secures iHeartMedia as Title Sponsor for 2026-27 Season Ahead of LA28 Debut, Ministry of Sport]

The agreement includes promotion through iHeartMedia's broadcast, digital and audio platforms, jersey branding across the league's 16 franchises and presenting sponsorship of the NSL playoffs.

data.title: Saxi Holtsworth and His Harmony Hounds
data.text:
Saxi Holtsworth’s Harmony Hounds, was a jazz ensemble that made commercial recordings as well as sheet music and performed on the vaudeville circuit. The Harmony Hounds were led by Edward “Saxi” Holtsworth who was an American jazz clarinetist. The Saxi Holtsworth’s Harmony Hounds were active in New York’s popular-music and vaudeville scenes starting in 1917 and active till at least 1926.

== Musical career ==
Holtsworth’s Harmony Hounds recorded in New York City for the Gennett record label. The band’s personnel included Holtsworth on clarinet and as director, his brother Charlie Holtsworth on trumpet, Walter Reed on trombone, Jack Barnett on piano, and Joe Hassan on drums. The lineup changed over time. [ref: https://publ.icgbio.ru/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Book_BGRS-2026-997.pdf, 15-я международная мультиконференция]

Among the ensemble’s recordings were “Bow Wow” and “Old Man Jazz,” recorded in 1920. “Bow Wow” was subsequently issued on more than one record label. In December 1920, the group also recorded “Hop, Skip and Jump” for Emerson Records.

The Harmony Hounds performed in vaudeville and became known beyond New York. A 1920 issue of Music Trade Review reported that the group was enjoying success at the Walnut Roof in Philadelphia. The magazine noted that the musicians were featuring popular songs during their engagements.

In 1921, Variety reported that Holtsworth’s orchestra had been engaged at Stauch’s café on Coney Island. The contract reportedly included a substantial weekly budget for the musicians and publicity, reflecting the importance of promotion in the competitive entertainment business of the period.

Holtsworth’s band was also featured on the cover of the 1920 sheet music for “Whistling Blues,” published in New York by Pace & Handy Music Company. The catalog record for the surviving sheet music identifies photographs of Saxi Holtsworth and his Harmony Hounds. The song was written by Jack Barnett and Joe Diamond, and the group recorded it for commercial release. [ref: https://publ.icgbio.ru/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Book_BGRS-2026-997.pdf, 15-я международная мультиконференция]

By July 1924, Holtsworth was recording under the name Saxi Holtsworth and His Band. The session included “Charleston Cabin” and “A New Kind of Man.” These recordings demonstrate that his musical activities continued beyond the original Harmony Hounds sessions. [ref: Whistling blues, New York: Pace & Handy Music Co. Inc., 1920]

Records by Saxi Holtsworth and his Harmony Hounds: [ref: https://yorkspace.library.yorku.ca/items/154eca65-dcf2-4881-a370-c0de9083469a]

* Bow Wow released in June 1920
* Old Man Jazz released in June 1920
* Hop Skip and Jump released in December 1920
* Charleston Cabin released on July 3, 1924
* A New Kind of Man released on July 3, 1924
* Tropical Pines Released on August 20, 1924
* How Come You Do Me Like You Do? Released on August 20, 1924

== References ==

* Brian Rust, Jazz and Ragtime Records (1897–1942), 6th edition, Mainspring Press https://mainspringpress.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/RUST_JRR-6.pdf
* University of York, “Whistling blues,” sheet music published by Pace & Handy Music Co., New York, 1920

data.title: Maria Thomas Santiago
data.text:
Maria Thomas Santiago, also known as Maria Santiago, is an American home health care educator and media host. She is the founder of the Home Health Aide Training Institute, a training school for home health aides in Westbury, New York, and hosts the interview program Talk with Maria. In 2025 she was honored by a resolution of the New York State Assembly in connection with her recognition at the Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Visionary Awards Gala.

== Early life and education ==
According to a 2025 New York State Assembly resolution, Santiago immigrated to the United States from Trinidad and studied at Hostos Community College in the Bronx, Lehman College, and the Connecticut School of Broadcasting, initially pursuing a career in broadcasting before turning to the care of older adults. A 2018 Long Island Press article described her as having grown up in Westbury and as a resident of the village.

== Career ==
=== Home Health Aide Training Institute ===
The Assembly resolution states that Santiago worked in health care administration, rising from administrator to chief executive, before founding her own home health aide training institute. The Home Health Aide Training Institute, located at 321 Post Avenue in Westbury, trains workers for in-home and nursing-home elder care; instruction is given by registered nurses. The school had been operating since 2017 when a ribbon-cutting ceremony was held in February 2018; at that time Santiago, described as its owner and founder, said that 134 students had completed training and that all of them were employed.

The institute is organized as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit; its federal tax exemption was issued in May 2021, and Santiago is listed among its officers in its Form 990 filings.

Santiago has been quoted by regional news outlets on the shortage of home care workers in New York. In 2024 she told NBC New York, in a report on proposed federal legislation to support the long-term care workforce, that agencies contacted the school daily seeking aides. In 2026 Long Island Business News quoted her on the need for competitive wages, training and career advancement for home care workers amid state budget debates.

=== Talk with Maria ===
Santiago hosts Talk with Maria, an interview program covering caregiving, health, and community topics that is distributed as a video podcast online.

== Recognition ==
In 2025 the New York State Assembly adopted Resolution K175, sponsored by Assemblymember Cook, honoring Santiago on the occasion of her designation for special recognition at the Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Visionary Awards Gala held on March 9, 2025, under the theme "Women of Destiny". A companion resolution (J480) was introduced in the New York State Senate.

== Philanthropy ==
According to the Assembly resolution, Santiago has provided meals and other resources to families in Ghana, Nigeria, and Trinidad, and during the COVID-19 pandemic awarded more than $100,000 in scholarships and life insurance policies to essential workers.

data.title: National Professional Practice Examination
data.text:
The National Professional Practice Examination (NPPE) is a standardized, computer-based examination that confirms an applicant's knowledge of professionalism, law, and ethics. It is used by fourteen Canadian engineering and geoscience self-regulatory organizations as one of their requirements for licensure.

The NPPE is a closed-book examination of 110 multiple-choice questions, of which 100 are scored and 10 are unscored experimental questions, and candidates are given 2.5 hours to complete it. The exam program states that it follows the Standards for Educational and Psychological Testing so that the examination is valid, reliable and fair. It is delivered online and remotely proctored through Meazure Learning, a company formed from the merger of the testing vendor Yardstick and the proctoring service ProctorU.

== History ==

Successive editions of the official candidate guide list a growing number of participating organizations: twelve in an earlier edition, thirteen in a later one, and fourteen as of 2026.

An earlier edition of the candidate guide noted that for applicants to some regulators, including Engineers and Geoscientists BC, the examination also contained an essay and was 3.5 hours long. The current format described by the exam program contains only multiple-choice questions.

Since April 2020, administration of the NPPE shifted from being conducted mostly in test centres to remote proctoring. The candidate guide previously named Yardstick as the delivery vendor; it now names Meazure Learning. Beginning with the June 2026 administration, candidates are required to use a smartphone or tablet as a second camera during the exam.

== Administration and governance ==
The NPPE is administered by the Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of Alberta (APEGA); one participating regulator describes this as being done on behalf of Engineers Canada. Registration, eligibility, fees, deadlines, deferrals and retake rules are set by each participating regulator, and candidates register through their own regulator.

Exam questions are written by item writers who are professional engineers and geoscientists from across Canada acting as subject-matter experts, and questions go through a field-testing process. The content and weighting of the exam (the blueprint) were developed by volunteer subject-matter experts and item developers of the Professional Practice Examination Committee (PPEC) and then validated nationally by representatives of all participating jurisdictions on the National Professional Practice Examination Advisory Committee (NPPEAC).

=== Participating regulators ===
The program website lists the following fourteen regulators.

{| class="wikitable"
! Regulator !! Jurisdiction
|-
| Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of Alberta (APEGA) || Alberta
|-
| Alberta Society of Engineering Technologists (ASET) || Alberta (technologists)
|-
| Engineers and Geoscientists British Columbia (EGBC) || British Columbia
|-
| Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of Saskatchewan (APEGS) || Saskatchewan
|-
| Engineers Geoscientists Manitoba (EGM) || Manitoba
|-
| Professional Engineers Ontario (PEO) || Ontario
|-
| Professional Geoscientists Ontario (PGO) || Ontario
|-
| Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of New Brunswick (APEGNB) || New Brunswick
|-
| Engineers Nova Scotia || Nova Scotia
|-
| Geoscientists Nova Scotia || Nova Scotia
|-
| Engineers PEI || Prince Edward Island
|-
| Professional Engineers and Geoscientists Newfoundland and Labrador (PEGNL) || Newfoundland and Labrador
|-
| Engineers Yukon || Yukon
|-
| Northwest Territories and Nunavut Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists (NAPEG) || Northwest Territories and Nunavut
|}

Regulators in Quebec are not among the participating organizations listed on the program website.

=== Eligibility and exemptions ===
Eligibility depends on the regulator; an application for professional membership may be required before a candidate can register. Some regulators do not require applicants to write the exam if they have previously passed a qualifying professional practice exam, such as the NPPE, elsewhere, while APEGA requires applicants to pass the NPPE even if they passed a different professional practice exam elsewhere. Limits on the number of attempts also vary; for example, APEGA allows a maximum of four attempts, and PGO allows up to three.

== Exam format ==
Each question has four options with a single correct answer, is scored as either correct or incorrect, and carries no penalty for guessing. Candidates cannot tell which questions are scored and which are experimental. All questions are translated into French and candidates may switch between English and French during the exam. The exam interface lets candidates bookmark and flag questions, take notes and change the font size, and registered candidates receive access to the interface several weeks before their sitting. The exam program states that the exam is not a test of English language proficiency and that its readability is monitored at about a grade 10–11 level.

== Content ==
The current blueprint dates from 2017 and was produced through a one-year consultation with engineers and geoscientists across Canada; the program website states that a review of the blueprint was in process and estimated to launch in mid-2026.

{| class="wikitable"
! Blueprint area !! Questions !! Examples of topics
|-
| I. Professionalism || 7–10 || Defining features of a profession, the role of professionals in society, the engineering and geoscience professions in Canada, the value of the professions to society
|-
| II. Ethics || 17–21 || Ethics in society, classical ethical theories (including utilitarianism, duty, human rights and virtue), codes of ethics, ethical dilemmas
|-
| III. Professional Practice || 27–32 || Professional accountability, duties to employers and clients, standards and codes of practice, risk management and insurance, environmental responsibility, use of software, document authentication, duty to inform, communication
|-
| IV. Law for Professional Practice || 23–28 || The Canadian legal system, contract law, tort law, civil law in Quebec, employment and labour law, dispute resolution, intellectual property, expert witnesses, construction liens, environmental and occupational health and safety law, human rights and privacy
|-
| V. Professional Law || 7–10 || Provincial and territorial acts and bylaws, admission to the professions, illegal practice and misuse of title, professional and technical societies
|-
| VI. Regulation of Members & Discipline Processes || 7–10 || Discipline procedures, practice reviews of individuals and firms, continuing professional development
|}

== Scoring and results ==
An equated score of 65 or greater is required to pass. Candidates who pass do not receive detailed score information, while candidates who fail receive a "mastery report" showing how they performed in each blueprint area; the program states that an equated score cannot be calculated back from this report. An earlier edition of the candidate guide stated that each exam is scored with no predetermined percentage of candidates who should pass.

Results are not available immediately because analyses must be run on the results; processing takes about two to three weeks after the exam dates, and results are delivered through the candidate's regulator.

== Preparation ==
The program states that exams focus on the blueprint content rather than on any particular book, and suggests that candidates use one legal resource and one resource on professional practice and ethics. Suggested textbooks include Law for Professional Engineers: Canadian and Global Insights (5th ed., 2019) by Donald L. Marston, Practical Law of Architecture, Engineering, and Geoscience by Brian M. Samuels and Doug R. Sanders, A Practical Guide to Ethics and Professional Practice for Engineers and Geoscientists (1st ed., 2022) by Samuels and Sanders, and Canadian Professional Engineering and Geoscience: Practice and Ethics by Gordon C. Andrews, Patricia Shaw and John McPhee. The program does not offer or endorse preparation courses. Some independent commercial services also sell original practice questions and study guides, and state that they are not affiliated with the NPPE program.

An official practice test site sells practice tests built from previously administered exam questions. Other than these practice questions, no NPPE exams have been publicly released.

== Exam delivery and security ==
Candidates take the exam remotely under live proctoring and may do so from anywhere in the world, provided the technical requirements are met. Requirements include a webcam, government-issued photo identification, a cleared workspace and a single monitor; virtual machine software, including VPNs, is not permitted. One optional comfort break is allowed, during which the exam timer does not stop. All candidates must sign a candidate agreement that requires them to keep exam content confidential and comply with security policies.
== See also ==
* Engineers Canada
* Professional engineer
* Iron Ring
* Professional ethics

data.title: Urban-X
data.text:
----

Urban-X was a startup accelerator program that operated from 2016 to 2025, focusing on early-stage companies developing technology for urban infrastructure and environments. The program was headquartered at Newlab in the Brooklyn Navy Yard in New York City.: [ref: Start-up accelerator URBAN-X to close, Cities Today]

== History ==
Urban-X was established in 2016 through a partnership between MINI, the automotive division of BMW Group, and Urban.US [ref: URBAN-X Invests in Startups Fighting Climate Change by Reimagining City Life, Worth], a venture capital firm specializing in urban technology investments. [ref: How MINI's startup accelerator URBAN-X is reimagining city life, Wired] It was originally headquartered in A/D/O in Greenpoint, New York City [ref: With its Start-up Accelerator Urban-X, BMW Mini is Betting Big on the Future, Azure Magazine] [ref: A Free Place for Designers to Work, The New York Times] [ref: BMW's Mini Drives Urban Tech's Future With New Greenpoint Spot, Observer] [ref: URBAN-X's latest startups bring AI to urban roads, floating cameras to the skies, The Architect’s Newspaper] before moving to Newlab [ref: Urban high-tech startup accelerator moves to Navy Yard, Brooklyn Eagle]. The accelerator was designed to support startups addressing urban challenges across sectors including transportation, construction, energy, and infrastructure. [ref: Talking urban innovation with Urban-X's Micah Kotch, City & State NY] [ref: ]

The program announced its closure in early 2025, with operations concluding at the end of 2025. During its existence, Urban-X partnered with several venture capital firms including SOSV, Third Sphere, and JVP. [ref: URBAN-X - Crunchbase Company Profile & Funding, Crunchbase]

== Program ==
Urban-X operated a 20-week accelerator program for selected startups. Initially, participants received $100,000 in seed funding [ref: URBAN-X Urbantech Startup Accelerator Program by URBAN-X, www.allthingsurban.net] [ref: URBAN-X accelerator wants to transform cities, ten start-ups at a time, The Architect’s Newspaper], though this funding component was discontinued in Fall 2022. The program provided mentorship through what it termed "Experts-in-residence," [ref: URBAN-X Accelerator Program 2021: Get $100,000 initial funding, AlphaGamma] workspace access, and connections to potential partners and customers.

Additionally, Urban-X ran a Mini Impact Program, a condensed four-week initiative for early-stage international startups, combining three weeks of remote participation with one week on-site in New York. [ref: URBAN-X Goes Global With European, Asian Investments, GovTech]

== Portfolio ==
Over its nine-year operation, Urban-X ran 15 main accelerator cohorts and 3 Mini Impact Program cohorts. Cohorts were typically selected from pools exceeding 100 applicants. [ref: URBAN-X By MINI Announces Cohort 15] While initially focused on companies based in the United States, the program began accepting international startups in 2022.

Portfolio companies typically fit into one or more of seven verticals [ref: URBAN-X: The venture accelerator founded by MINI, Automotive World]

* Built Environment & Real Estate
* Public Health & Safety
* Infrastructure & Industry
* Energy & Grid
* Govtech & Civil Solutions
* Transportation & Mobility
* Food, Waste, & Water

data.title: Kiran Kumar Thumma
data.text:
Kiran Kumar Thumma, credited as Thumma Kiran and Kiran Reddy Thumma, is an Indian film director who works in Telugu cinema. A former assistant of director Sekhar Kammula, he made his directorial debut with the 2014 romantic film Dil Deewana. [ref: Exclusive interview with Dil Deewana director Thumma Kiran Reddy, Ragalahari] [ref: Review: Dil Deewana – Breaks Your Heart, 123Telugu]

== Career ==
Thumma worked on the directorial team of Sekhar Kammula on Anand, Godavari, Happy Days and Leader before becoming a director. [ref: Dil Deewana gets clean U certificate, 123Telugu]

His first film as director, Dil Deewana, starring Raj Arjun Reddy and Rohit Reddy and produced by Raja Reddy, was released on 7 February 2014. The film follows two parallel love stories. Its audio was launched by cricketer Kapil Dev. [ref: Dil Deewana Movie Review, Rating, The Hans India] Reviews were mixed: The Hans India rated it 2.5 out of 5 and described his direction as competent, while 123Telugu gave it 2 out of 5 and found his handling of the story average. Mirchi9 was more critical of the direction. [ref: Dil Deewana Review, Mirchi9]

data.title: Foodtopia: Communities in Pursuit of Peace, Love, & Homegrown Food
data.text:
Foodtopia: Communities in Pursuit of Peace, Love, & Homegrown Food is a 2022 nonfiction book by Margot Anne Kelley, published by Godine. [ref: Foodtopia, Godine] It examines five periods of the American back-to-the-land movement, from the nineteenth century to the early twenty-first century, through the relationship between food production and efforts to establish alternative ways of living. [ref: Foodtopia: Communities in Pursuit of Peace, Love, & Homegrown Food, Kirkus Reviews]

== Synopsis ==
The book combines historical accounts with Kelley's visits to farms, conferences, and farmers' markets. Its subjects include Henry David Thoreau, the nineteenth-century communities of Brook Farm and Fruitlands, and Scott and Helen Nearing, whose book Living the Good Life influenced later homesteaders. Kelley also discusses Mollie Katzen and Alice Waters in the context of changes in American food culture.

The five periods encompass the utopian communities of the 1840s, turn-of-the-century single-tax and smallholding communities, homesteading during the Great Depression, the counterculture of the 1960s and 1970s, and contemporary young farmers. The account extends to the COVID-19 pandemic and its effects on food supply systems.

Kelley explores how reformers have connected farming and eating with ideals of equality, justice, and freedom. Examples from Maine include the development of the Maine Organic Farmers and Gardeners Association. The narrative links earlier movements with later food activism, examining the recurrence and adaptation of their ideas. [ref: Book Review: “Foodtopia”, Maine Organic Farmers and Gardeners Association]

== Publication ==
Godine published the 384-page hardcover edition in August 2022.

== Reception ==
Kirkus Reviews described the book as "An informative, fresh history of food in America", praising its profiles of participants in successive back-to-the-land movements.

Reviewing the book for the Maine Organic Farmers and Gardeners Association, Catherine Preston-Schreck praised its historical detail and its structure connecting past and present movements. She also questioned how the utopian projects related to colonial agricultural practices and racial prejudice, raising concerns about the implications of Thoreau's views on vegetarianism and civilization.

The book was a finalist for the nonfiction category of the 2023 Maine Literary Awards. [ref: 2023 Finalists, Maine Writers & Publishers Alliance]

data.title: Cycling at the 1900 Summer Olympics – Men's team sprint
data.text:
The men's professional team sprint also named Course des Nations was a track cycling event contested at the 1900 Summer Olympics in Paris. It was classified as an Olympic non-medal event. The competition was held on 14 September 1900 at the Vélodrome de Vincennes. A total of 24 cyclists from nine countries participated in the event, with eight three-man teams competing, including one mixed team. [ref: Team Sprint (Professionals [Course des Nations]), Men, Olympedia]

Unlike the modern Olympic team sprint, in which riders race in succession, the 1900 competition was conducted as a series of match races in which all six riders from two opposing teams competed simultaneously. Point-for-place scoring was used to determine the winning team.

The competition began with four first-round heats. France, Italy, the United States, and the mixed British-New Zealand team advanced to the semi-finals. In the semi-finals, the United States defeated Italy, while France defeated the mixed team, setting up a final between the United States and France.

The final was closely contested, with the United States defeating France by one point. The American team of Tom Cooper, Floyd McFarland, and George Banker scored 10 points, compared with France's 11. The individual finishing order was Edmond Jacquelin, Cooper, McFarland, Paul Bourillon, Banker, and Jean-Baptiste Louvet. Italy defeated the mixed British-New Zealand team to finish third.

Nowadays, the professional events are not recognized by the International Olympic Committee as official Olympic medal competitions, as only amateur events are classified as medal events. Before July 2021 the IOC has never officially decided which events were "Olympic" and which were not. [ref: Olympische Spiele 1900 in Paris, Agon-Sportverlag]

==Competition format==

Eight teams of three cyclists competed in the tournament. The teams represented seven national delegations, together with a mixed team comprising two British cyclists and one New Zealand cyclist. Each match involved two teams, with all six riders racing on the track simultaneously.

The competition consisted of four first-round heats, two semi-finals, and two final-round races. The winners of the first-round heats advanced to the semi-finals. The semi-final winners contested the championship final, while the other two semi-finalists competed for third place. Point-for-place scoring determined the winning team in each match. The team whose riders accumulated the lower total score won the race.

data.title: Emilio Peroni
data.text:
Emilio Antonio Peroni (born 1977) is an Argentine pianist and teacher. He studied at the Escuela Superior de Música de Neuquén and at the Hochschule für Musik und Theater Rostock in Germany, where he lived and taught. In 2007, in a duo with violinist Pauline Reguig, he won the Felix Mendelssohn Bartholdy Competition in the violin and piano duo category. [ref: Felix Mendelssohn Bartholdy Wettbewerb 2007 entschieden – morgen Preisträgerkonzert, Stiftung Preußischer Kulturbesitz] He teaches piano and chamber music at the Escuela Superior de Música de Neuquén. [ref: Peroni: El piano en la música de cámara, Radio Nacional]

== Early life and education ==
Peroni was born in Neuquén in 1977 and grew up in Cipolletti, Río Negro Province. [ref: Emilio Peroni, una vida marcada por el tango, [[Río Negro (newspaper)] He entered the Escuela Superior de Música de Neuquén at the age of seven, graduated as a piano teacher, and taught there from 1995 to 2002. [ref: Famoso pianista regional en concierto, Río Negro] He studied with Miguel Martín Morales, Aldo Antognazzi and Bruno Leonardo Gelber in Argentina, with Carlo Bruno in Italy, with Ángel Soler in Barcelona and with Bernd Zack in Germany. [ref: Gala argentina en el Centro Sinfónico Nacional, Metro Blog La Paz] In the 1990s he and his brother, violist Eduardo Félix Peroni, played piano four hands on television. [ref: De las tandas de Canal 7 en la década del 90, a brindar conciertos en el CCK, LM Neuquén]

He received scholarships to study in Rome (1999) and Barcelona. In 2002 he moved to Rostock to study with Bernd Zack, [ref: Peroni viaja a Alemania y se despide con conciertos, Río Negro] and completed three postgraduate degrees at the Hochschule für Musik und Theater, two in piano and one in chamber music. [ref: Emilio Peroni, Editorial Municipal de Rosario]

== Career ==
In September 2005 he performed Mendelssohn's Concerto for Piano and Strings with the Neuquén Symphony Orchestra under Marcelo Álvarez; critic Horacio San Miguel called his performance "truly memorable". [ref: Peroni y Cazeneuve en un concierto para recordar, Río Negro] While living in Germany he formed a tango quintet. [ref: El pianista Emilio Peroni, clásico y popular, en Cipolletti, Río Negro] He has appeared as a soloist with orchestras in Germany, including the Rostock Philharmonic, and in Argentina, including the National Symphony Orchestra and orchestras in Rosario, San Juan and Neuquén. He has toured in Asia, with performances in the Philippines and Kuwait. In 2020 The Manila Times published an interview with him. [ref: A chat with Argentinian pianist Emilio Peroni, The Manila Times]

After returning to Argentina he settled in the Alto Valle region and joined the faculty of the Escuela Superior de Música de Neuquén. In March 2014 he opened the concert series of the Legislature of Neuquén Province with the recital Romanticismo puro. [ref: Emilio Peroni abre el ciclo de conciertos en la Legislatura, Neuquén Informa] In April 2016 he took part in the Uruguay for Export festival at the SODRE Auditorium in Montevideo. [ref: Espectáculos musicales para esta semana, [[El Observador (Uruguay)] In September 2017 he performed Rachmaninoff's Piano Concerto No. 2 with the National Symphony Orchestra of Bolivia under Weimar Arancibia in La Paz.

On 2 February 2018 he played Schubert's Trout Quintet at the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg with Annette Schäfer, Naomi Seiler, Thomas Tyllack and Stefan Schäfer. [ref: Boletín Cultural e Informativo, febrero de 2018, Consulate General of Argentina in Hamburg] On 17 April 2019 he was the soloist in Dvořák's Piano Concerto with the National Symphony Orchestra under Rodolfo Saglimbeni at the Centro Cultural Kirchner in Buenos Aires. [ref: La Orquesta Sinfónica Nacional en el CCK los días 5, 17 y 26 de abril, Barriada] That year he and violinist Marco Fattorello gave a cycle of Mozart's violin sonatas at the Escuela Superior de Música de Neuquén. In May 2022 he gave a piano masterclass at the Faculty of Arts and Design of the National University of Cuyo and performed a Gershwin concerto with the university's orchestra. [ref: Emilio Peroni dictará una clase magistral de piano, Facultad de Artes y Diseño, Universidad Nacional de Cuyo] In July 2023 he returned to the Centro Cultural Kirchner as soloist with the National Symphony Orchestra in Schumann's Piano Concerto. Since 2019 he has hosted small recitals at his home in Neuquén, followed by conversations with the audience. [ref: Como en el teatro, pero en casa: los recitales íntimos de un músico neuquino, LM Neuquén]

== Awards ==
* First prize, Oscar Lorenzo Fernández Competition.
* Prize, 5th Pablo Casals Competition of the Centro Catalán de Rosario.
* Joint first prize, with Marcelo Balat, 6th Biennial Youth Competition 2001/2002 of Festivales Musicales de Buenos Aires. [ref: Un despliegue de talento joven, La Nación]
* Felix Mendelssohn Bartholdy Competition, violin and piano duo category, with Pauline Reguig, Berlin (2007).
* Second prize, Musikpreis 2008 of Rostock. [ref: Concierto del pianista Emilio Peroni, Diario Andino]

data.title: Dulat Tastekey
data.text:
----

Dulat Tursynuly Tastekey (; born 22 June 1982; [ref: Ұлттық спорт жанашыры Дулат Тастекей 44 жасқа толды, Adyrna.kz] also spelled Tastekeev) is a Kazakhstani entrepreneur and philanthropist. [ref: Более 1 млрд тенге на благотворительные проекты направил TAS GROUP за 5 лет, Kapital.kz] [ref: Танымал кәсіпкер Дулат Тастекеев әлеуметтік осал топқа жататын отбасыға үй әперетін болды, gov.kz] He is the founder and chief executive of TAS Group. [ref: В Казахстане может появиться еще один коммерческий банк, но придется подождать, Digital Business] [ref: Дулат Тастекеев намерен создать в Казахстане банк, Kapital.kz]

Dulat Tastekey is the founder of the Assyltas Public Foundation, vice-president of the International Kazakh Language Society (Qazaq Tili), and a deputy of the Almaty City Maslikhat since 2023, a trustee of the IQanat Foundation in Abai Region, chairman of the Board of Trustees of the Republican Abai National School, a member of the Board of Trustees of the Nazarbayev Intellectual School of Physics and Mathematics in Almaty, a member of the Board of Trustees of the Almaty City Toghyzkumalak Federation since 2023, and vice-president of the Kazakhstan Audaryspak Federation.

== Education ==
Dulat Tastekey graduated in 1999 from the Abai Republican Specialized Boarding School for gifted children in Almaty, with advanced study of the Kazakh language and literature.

In 2003, he graduated from the Kazakh Institute of Economics and Law in Almaty (now Caspian University).

In 2007, he graduated from the Kazakh Humanities and Law University (now Maqsut Narikbayev University).

In 2009, he graduated from the French business school HEC Paris.

In 2015, he completed the Practicum for Directors: Company Management at the Moscow School of Management SKOLKOVO.

In 2019, he received a PhD degree in Business Administration from Narxoz University. He also completed the Digital Transformation Management programme at the Moscow School of Management SKOLKOVO in 2019.

In 2024, he graduated from Harvard Business School. [ref: Дулат Тастекей: Приличные деньги нужно делать прилично, Forbes Kazakhstan] [ref: Стратегия вверх, Forbes Kazakhstan] In 2025, he completed a programme at the Stanford Graduate School of Business. [ref: Калифорния төріндегі кездесу: Дулат Тастекей Марат Омаровқа шапан жапты, Kursiv.media]

== Business career ==
Since 2003, Tastekey has held various positions in banking and financial institutions in Kazakhstan. In 2010, he became director of TAS Group. [ref: Дулат Тастекеев: Дерзкие мечты и кумиры финансиста, BIB.kz]

In 2018, he founded the Assyltas Public Foundation. [ref: Public Foundation "ASSYLTAS", Kompra]

== Public activities ==

=== Philanthropy and culture ===
From 2016 to 2019, an international aitys competition entitled Tugan zherge tuyngdy tik was held in Aksuat village, Tarbagatai District, with financial support from Tastekey. Six volumes of the almanac Tarikhka Toly Tarbagatai were published, as well as a collection of aitys performances from Aksuat entitled Tugan zherge tuyngdy tik. Since 2021, Tastekey has provided financial support for the organization and holding of the Asyl Dombra aitys competition.

Tastekey has supported the Abai Republican Specialized Boarding School for gifted children with advanced study of the Kazakh language and literature. With his sponsorship, an English-language specialist from abroad conducted courses at the school, and aitys competitions were organized among its students. [ref: АСЫЛ ӨНЕР САЙЫСЫ, Aikyn] Since 2018, he has awarded the Tarbagatai Tarlany medal to people originating from the Tarbagatai region who have made contributions to the region. In 2019, he established the Assyltas medal. [ref: Рухани жаңғыру: «Туған жер» мецената Дулата Тастекеева, Pushkin Library]

In 2018, Tastekey undertook to complete an unfinished central mosque in Semey, construction of which had begun in 2008; Kazinform reported in June 2018 that 500 million tenge had been allocated for the work. [ref: Кәсіпкер Семейдің 10 жылдан бері «сақалды» құрылысқа айналған мешітін салып бермек, Kazinform] The Abai Mosque, a four-minaret building with a capacity of 2,500 worshippers, was officially opened on 22 March 2021. Local media reported that the construction was financed with Tastekey's own funds. [ref: В Семее состоялось открытие новой мечети, AltaiNews]

In 2021, Tastekey published a book entitled Öte mañyzdy (Very Important). [ref: Өте маңызды. Кәсіпкер алдыңғы 10 жылда не нәрсеге дайын болуы керек, AmalBooks]

In 2025, to mark the 180th anniversary of the poet Abai Kunanbaiuly, the Assyltas Public Foundation announced that it would pay 180,000 tenge to families whose sons were born on 10 August 2025 and named Abai. The foundation later reported 33 such newborns in 13 regions of Kazakhstan. [ref: В Казахстане заплатят по 180 тысяч тенге каждому, кто выполнил это условие, Digital Business] [ref: По 180 тысяч тенге за сына с именем Абай: кто получит выплаты в Казахстане, Lada.kz]

In 2025, as part of the Artyq bilim kitapta project, initiated by the Assyltas Public Foundation, more than 12,000 books were delivered to 233 rural schools in Abai Region. [ref: Около 14 тысяч книг доставили селам в области Абай, Kazpravda.kz] In 2026, around 17,000 books were distributed to 340 rural schools in Zhambyl Region. [ref: «Кітап керуені» Таразға жетті, 24.kz]

=== Sport ===
In December 2019, Tastekey was elected first vice-president of the World Kazakh Kuresi Federation. [ref: Стал известен состав исполнительного комитета Всемирной федерации «Қазақ күресі», Kazinform] As of June 2026, he is vice-president of the Kazakhstan Audaryspak Federation and a member of the Board of Trustees of the Kazakhstan Toghyzkumalak Federation.

=== Public office and organizations ===
In 2023, Tastekey was elected as a deputy of the Almaty City Maslikhat. [ref: Кто стал депутатом маслихата Алматы по одномандатным округам, Kazinform]

Tastekey is vice-president of the International Kazakh Language Society (Qazaq Tili), the organization that initiated the QAZAQ TILI Endowment Qory, an endowment fund supporting the Kazakh language. [ref: В структуре фонда Qazaq Tili Endowment необходимо создать институт Counsel — Дулат Тастекей, Kazinform] [ref: Structure: Members of the Central Council, Qazaq Tili International Society] The Assyltas Public Foundation, which Tastekey founded, is listed among the donors who each contributed 100 million tenge to the endowment. [ref: Endowment, Qazaq Tili International Society]

In 2023, Tastekey was awarded the title of Honorary Citizen of Semey. [ref: Тастекеев Дулат Турсынович, Abai Regional Universal Library] In the same year, he was selected as a trustee of the IQanat Foundation for Abai Region. [ref: 150 казахстанских предпринимателей реализуют мечты тысяч детей из аулов, Forbes Kazakhstan]

== Awards and recognition ==
* Enbek uzdigi medal for contributions to the socio-economic development of Kazakhstan (2017) [ref: Тастекей Дулат Тұрсынұлы, gov.kz]
* Entrepreneur of the Year prize of the Entrepreneurs Club of Kazakhstan, presented at the club's launch with the support of Forbes Kazakhstan (2018) [ref: В Алматы открыли стартовую площадку для будущих «форбсов», Forbes Kazakhstan]
* Laureate of the Zhomart Zhurek regional competition in East Kazakhstan Region (2018)
* Kultegin medal for contributions to the development of education and science in Kazakhstan (2019)
* Winner of Kazakhstan's 100 New Faces of Kazakhstan project (2021) [ref: Поддерживающий многодетных матерей и предпринимателей меценат стал победителем проекта «100 новых лиц», Kazinform]
* International Alash Literary Award (2026) [ref: Кәсіпкер Дулат Тастекейге «Алаш» әдеби сыйлығы берілді, Kursiv]

== Personal life ==
Tastekey is married to Aizhan Serikkyzy Tastekeyeva (born 1983), a managing partner of TAS Group. They have four children.

data.title: Floribert Mubalama
data.text:
----

Floribert Hengwa Mubalama is a Congolese-American nonprofit leader and author. He is the founder and chief executive officer of the Congolese Integration Network (CIN), a refugee-led nonprofit organization based in SeaTac, Washington, that serves Congolese and other refugee and immigrant families in King County, Washington. [ref: Announcing Our Parent-Child Home Awards, Best Starts for Kids Blog] [ref: How one refugee's story of organizing holds lessons for all of us, Communities of Opportunity] A former refugee from the Democratic Republic of Congo, Mubalama spent more than eight years in a refugee camp in Malawi before resettling in the United States in December 2014. [ref: For Refugees In Seattle, Rising Rents Mean The Search For Home Isn't Over, KNKX Public Radio]

== Early life and resettlement ==
Mubalama fled the Democratic Republic of Congo in 2006 amid violence and lived in a refugee camp in Malawi. According to a King County profile, he arrived in King County in December 2014 with his family and was among the first Congolese refugees to settle in the area. The Communities of Opportunity profile describes his experience of isolation and housing and employment instability after arrival, and his door-to-door organizing among Congolese families in King County, including a community gathering attended by more than 120 Congolese community members and 20 county service providers.

== Congolese Integration Network ==
Mubalama organized the Congolese Integration Network in response to the isolation he observed among Congolese refugees navigating new systems and communities in King County. With support from Global to Local, he founded CIN in SeaTac; its first program, Congolese Housing First, combined language classes, employment workshops, and support groups. CIN was fiscally sponsored by Global to Local from July 2016 to July 2018. [ref: RVC Partner Spotlight: Congolese Integration Network Takes Steps Away From Tragic History, Looks Forward to Future Growth, Rainier Valley Corps] A 2017 public radio report described Mubalama as the person many Congolese refugees in Seattle called for help with appointments, rides, first jobs and documents such as eviction notices, and identified affordable housing as one of the biggest barriers facing newly arrived refugees. In 2017, CIN was among the recipients of Parent-Child Home Program funding announced by King County's Best Starts for Kids initiative, in partnership with United Way of King County and the City of Seattle.

A 2022 Washington State Senate resolution recorded that an estimated 8,000 Congolese refugees live in Washington and are served by the Congolese Integration Network, and noted the organization's advocacy for a healing center for refugees recovering from trauma. [ref: Senate Resolution 8627 — Honoring the Congolese Integration Network, Washington State Senate] In June 2019, CIN convened what organizers described as the first Washington State Congolese Summit, in Seattle, combining cultural celebration with discussion of integration. [ref: First of its kind in Seattle, Washington State Congolese Summit celebrates culture and discusses integration, Rainier Valley Corps] For CIN's planned Washington Refugee Healing Center, U.S. Representative Adam Smith submitted a Community Project Funding request, and $500,000 was included in the House Appropriations Committee's fiscal year 2023 appropriations bill; Smith cited CIN's language services, housing assistance and employment support. [ref: Rep. Smith Submits Community Project Funding Request for Congolese Integration Network, adamsmith.house.gov]

== Hengwa Star Foundation ==
In 2021, Mubalama founded the Hengwa Star Foundation in Bukavu, South Kivu, Democratic Republic of Congo, a nonprofit working with vulnerable people in eastern Congo, including a program that pays the hospital bills of mothers detained in health facilities after childbirth so that they can return home. [ref: From Refugee to Community Builder: Dr. Floribert Mubalama's Vision for Global Impact, YouTube]

== Author ==
Mubalama is the author of Echoes of the Ancients: Breaking Colonial Silence and Restoring Afrikan Dignity Within the Universal Story of Salvation, published in July 2026 (ISBN 979-8188740320). [ref: Echoes of the Ancients, Amazon]

== Recognition ==
In February 2022, the Washington State Senate adopted two resolutions connected with Mubalama's organization: Senate Resolution 8627, "Honoring the Congolese Integration Network" (adopted February 14, 2022), and Senate Resolution 8651, "Honoring the Democratic Republic of Congo and the Congolese Integration Network" (adopted February 21, 2022). [ref: SR 8627 — 2021-22: Honoring the Congolese Integration Network, Washington State Legislature] In 2026, the Congolese Integration Network received the WAVE Global Impact Organization Certification.

data.title: Wheel Well
data.text:
Wheel Well is a South African non-profit organisation working on child road safety and paediatric injury prevention. Founded in 2012 by road safety advocate Peggie Mars, the organisation operates from Bedfordview, Gauteng, and focuses on child restraint accessibility, pedestrian visibility, road safety education, and legislative advocacy.

Wheel Well's main programmes are the "Car Seats for Kids" campaign, which inspects, refurbishes, and redistributes pre-owned child safety seats to lower-income families, and the "Halo Beanie Project", a pedestrian safety campaign that provides reflective knitted beanies to primary school children who walk in low-light conditions. In 2016, the organisation received a Prince Michael International Road Safety Award in the Safer Road Users category.

== History ==
The legal entity behind Wheel Well was incorporated in 2008 as a shelf company under registration number 2008/004093/08. Following a transfer of the entity and a change of name and purpose, the organisation began operating in 2012 under founder Peggie Mars to address child road crash injuries and deaths in South Africa.

The organisation was established to counter the cost barrier to certified child restraints. Wheel Well is registered with the Department of Social Development as a Non-Profit Organisation (NPO 283-349) and recognised by the South African Revenue Service as a Public Benefit Organisation (PBO 930041005) with Section 18A tax-exempt status. Its showroom and testing facility are in Bedfordview, Gauteng.

== Road safety context in South Africa ==
According to the Road Traffic Management Corporation (RTMC), road traffic crashes in South Africa caused 11,485 deaths in 2025. Pedestrians were the largest group, accounting for 45.49% of road deaths (5,224 fatalities). Children aged 14 and younger accounted for 8.9% of road deaths (1,034 children in 2025). National records show that 39% of pedestrian fatalities and 35% of fatal crashes occur between 17:00 and 22:00, when visibility is reduced.

Economic modelling by the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) and the RTMC estimates that for every road death, South African health services treat about 4.8 to 4.9 serious injuries and 14.9 slight injuries. Research at Red Cross War Memorial Children's Hospital has found that road traffic crashes are a leading cause of severe paediatric trauma and intensive care admissions, with pedestrian injuries the most common among primary school-aged children.

== Programmes ==
=== Car Seats for Kids ===
Launched in 2012, "Car Seats for Kids" collects donated pre-owned infant, toddler, and booster seats from the public. Each seat is inspected, cleaned, and refurbished before being passed on to families unable to afford new certified restraints.

Seats that fail safety checks, have been in a collision, or are past the manufacturer's expiry date are taken out of circulation and dismantled for recycling. By 2026, the campaign had provided seats to more than 12,000 children. The organisation also offers fitment demonstrations and gives installation and sizing advice to parents through messaging platforms.

=== Halo Beanie Project ===
The "Halo Beanie Project" is a pedestrian visibility campaign aimed at children who walk to school along unlit roads in informal settlements and peri-urban areas, under the slogan "Children should be seen and not hurt".

Wheel Well supplies community knitting groups and older crafters with packs of acrylic yarn blended with retroreflective thread. The resulting beanies reflect vehicle headlights, making child pedestrians visible to drivers from further away. The beanies are distributed to learners at primary schools along busy roads.

== Advocacy ==
Wheel Well campaigns for changes to road safety regulation under the National Road Traffic Act, including:
* extending mandatory child restraint requirements to all child passengers up to 1.5 metres in height;
* a 30 km/h speed limit around school zones, supported by traffic calming infrastructure;
* amending scholar transport and public passenger vehicle loading rules to count every child as a full occupant ("Every Child as a Person") rather than applying fractional passenger allowances;
* expanding national crash records to show whether child victims were travelling in private cars, scholar transport, or open light delivery vehicles.

== Recognition ==
* 2016: Prince Michael International Road Safety Award (Safer Road Users category) for the Car Seats for Kids campaign.
* 2018: Gumtree Women in Autos Award, presented to founder Peggie Mars.
* 2024: Rotary International Paul Harris Fellow, awarded to Peggie Mars.
* 2025: Old Mutual Award for Excellence in Child Road Safety.

data.title: Mayor of Santa Monica, California
data.text:
The mayor of Santa Monica is the presiding officer and ceremonial head of the municipal government of Santa Monica, California. Santa Monica has a council–manager government in which legislative authority is vested in the seven-member Santa Monica City Council, while the administration of city services is supervised by a professional city manager. [ref: Charter of the City of Santa Monica, Article V: Form of Government, City of Santa Monica]

The mayor is not elected separately by the public. Instead, the City Council selects one of its own members to serve as mayor. The mayor remains a voting councilmember and has the same voice and vote in council proceedings as every other member. [ref: Charter of the City of Santa Monica, Article VI: The City Council, City of Santa Monica] The incumbent mayor is Caroline Torosis, who was sworn in on December 9, 2025, succeeding Lana Negrete.

==Mayor pro tempore==

The council also designates a mayor pro tempore. The mayor pro tempore presides over council meetings and performs the mayor's duties when the mayor is absent or unable to serve. Unlike the mayoral rotation, the mayor pro tempore may be selected by a simple majority without regard to length of council service. [ref: Rules of Order and Procedure for the Conduct of City Council Meetings, City of Santa Monica]

If both officers are absent from a meeting, the city clerk calls the meeting to order and the councilmembers present elect a temporary presiding officer. The incumbent mayor pro tempore is Jesse Zwick, who was sworn in on December 9, 2025.

==History==

Santa Monica was incorporated in 1886. Juan José Carrillo is identified by the Santa Monica History Museum as the city's first judge, mayor and city trustee. [ref: Santa Monica History, Santa Monica History Museum]

In 1975, Nat Trives became Santa Monica's first African-American mayor. [ref: On the Ground Q&A: Nat Trives, Stanford Law School] In 2015, Antonio Vazquez became the city's first Latino mayor. data.title: Prabha Goswami
data.text:
----

Prabha Goswami (also identified in corporate records as Prabha Giri) is an Indian beauty pageant titleholder, social advocate, and entrepreneur from Almora district, Uttarakhand. She won the Monal Miss Uttarakhand pageant in 2018. Following the contest, she was appointed by the Almora district administration as an ambassador for the Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao campaign. She later founded Bharat Life Care, an enterprise manufacturing Ayurvedic wellness products.

== Early life and education ==
Goswami was raised in Kafaltana (Kapaltana) village in the Jaurasi area of Chaukhutia tehsil, located in Almora district, Uttarakhand. [ref: चौखुटिया की प्रभा बनी मिस उत्तराखंड 2018, Dainik Jagran] [ref: प्रभा गोस्वामी का गृह क्षेत्र में हुआ स्वागत, [[Hindustan (newspaper)] She completed her primary and intermediate schooling at institutions in Jaurasi before relocating to Delhi for higher education.

== Pageantry and advocacy ==
=== Monal Miss Uttarakhand 2018 ===
In July 2018, Goswami competed in the Monal Miss Uttarakhand pageant, held in Khatima, Uttarakhand. The competition featured 18 finalists from across the state. On 23 July 2018, Goswami won the Monal Miss Uttarakhand title; auxiliary awards presented at the event included Face of Uttarakhand and Mrs Uttarakhand. [ref: फेस ऑफ उतराखंड सोनम और मिस उत्तराखंड बनी प्रभा गोस्वामी, [[Hindustan (newspaper)] [ref: मिस उत्तराखंड प्रभा का लोगों ने किया स्वागत, Dainik Jagran]

=== Social campaigns ===
In August 2018, Goswami was welcomed by residents and civic organizations during visits to schools in Jaurasi and Chaukhutia, where she spoke on rural female literacy and advocated for educational support for girls in mountainous regions.

In October 2018, the Almora district administration designated Goswami and athlete Roshni Bisht as district brand ambassadors for the Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao campaign. Goswami was assigned outreach activities across the Ranikhet sub-division and surrounding development blocks to raise awareness regarding sex-ratio imbalances and female education. [ref: रोशनी बिष्ट और प्रभा गोस्वामी बनी बेटी बचाओं बेटी पढ़ाओं की जिले में ब्रांड एंबेसडर, Uttara News]

== Business career ==
Goswami registered under the name Prabha Giri on Startup India's BHASKAR portal, listing Bharat Life Care Ayurveda Wellness and Personal Care as her venture.

=== Bharat Life Care ===
Bharat Life Care is an Ayurvedic and herbal products venture with administrative roots in Almora, Uttarakhand. The brand manufactures wellness items derived from traditional botanical ingredients.

Its primary product is DiaCare Amrit, an herbal tea marketed as a dietary lifestyle beverage to assist in carbohydrate metabolism. The formulation incorporates:
* Berberis aristata (Daruharidra / Kilmora)
* Cinnamon (Dalchini)
* Fenugreek seeds (Methi dana)
* Neem (Azadirachta indica)
* Amla (Emblica officinalis)
* Bitter gourd (Karela)

The product is distributed as an over-the-counter wellness tea without therapeutic claims as a medical prescription.

LyvWell Apartments is a multifamily property management company operating across North America. LyvWell Apartments has a team of more than 1,200 associates that manage a mix of high-rise, mid-rise and garden-style communities including stabilized properties as well as developments.

== History ==
Formerly Brookfield Properties Multifamily [ref: ], LyvWell Apartments focuses primarily on operating multifamily communities on behalf of Brookfield Corporation. The LyvWell name launched in October 2026 [ref: ] and builds on institutional expertise and operational excellence to manage a diverse range of residential properties, including market-rate, mixed-use, and workforce housing communities.

== Operations ==
LyvWell Apartments operates apartment communities, each with distinctive property names. Its portfolio includes properties in cities such as Los Angeles, Las Vegas, Phoenix, Denver, Dallas, Houston, Nashville, New York City, District of Columbia and internationally, Toronto and Vancouver. data.title: Stonestorm
data.text:
Stonestorm is a free-to-play idle massively multiplayer online role-playing game (MMORPG) developed and published by Donut Interactive. [ref: Imprint, stonestorm.gg] It is set in an East Asian-inspired fantasy world and is scheduled for release on 31 October 2026 as a browser game, with versions for Android and iOS planned after store review. [ref: Stonestorm, IGDB] [ref: Stonestorm, Donut Interactive Kft.]

== Gameplay ==
The player chooses one of three kingdoms (Bonghwa, Horang and Miru) and one of four character classes (Warrior, Ninja, Mage and Shaman), each of which branches into two paths from level 5. As in other idle games, the player's hero continues to fight, gain experience and collect items for up to eight hours while the player is offline; the player chooses the equipment, skills and opponents beforehand.

The game includes six regions, each with its own boss, as well as forays and dungeons, a forty-floor tower called the Stormcatcher, an arena in which players fight other players' heroes, and guilds that build a shared fortress. Equipment can be upgraded at a blacksmith up to +9.

== Setting ==
According to the game's backstory, a single empire split into three warring kingdoms after its emperor died on the "Night of the Stones", when his three children blamed one another for his death. Storm stones continue to fall from the sky, and warriors of a Dragon God, called Stormbreakers, destroy them.

== Release ==
Stonestorm is scheduled to launch on 31 October 2026 in web browsers, with a single account usable across the browser and mobile versions. The game is available in 30 languages.
